reviews.comment: Lectures often feel disorganized, and explanations are not always clear, which creates confusion among students. Overall, I believe the course could benefit greatly from clearer instruction and more supportive engagement with the students.

The good reviews feel like they were written by the prof himself. That alone says a lot about his teaching style, classroom, and what kind of “educator” he is when negative but constructive feedback seems unwelcome. A good educator should accept criticism, not hide behind exaggerated praise while students sit through boring, inefficient lectures.

Prof. Ajogbeje may be a nice person, but his lectures are painfully boring and poorly organized. He often drifts off topic and asks questions unrelated to the course material, making class feel inefficient and frustrating. The assignments are equally weak: repetitive, unstimulating, and mostly disconnected from the exams.

Professor Ajogbede is an outstanding professor who is not only good at what he teaches, but also very caring. I took his Applied Ai class and learned alot. Class can be tiring sometimes because it took place in the afternoon, but it is not the professor's fault. Overall, it is a fantastic class taught by a fantastic professor. I highly recommend it

Ajogbeje is bad. Students don't learn much from his classes. It's a waste of time. His lecture is dry and boring. All he does is pointing his long fingers at students and yelling them to pay attention to the low quality lecture he's delivering.
Prof. Ajogbeje is a great professor overall. He teaches a very fair curriculum and is easy to follow along with.
so-so class, so-so professor. Highly recommend, do you understand? SO
i took his AI class. it was pretty average. the class itself wasn't difficult but the professor was very difficult to deal with.

Professor Korede is an amazing professor. He is very lenient in grading while still giving you solid feedback on what you can improve. I received an A to A- on most assignments. As long as you show interest in the class and put in effort on the assignments, he is very forgiving. I once turned in an assignment late and received no penalty.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this class - it is not a 3000 level course in terms of sociology and was able to understand it well without having any background. All of the material covered in class was very applicable to the world and is referred to often by several other professors in other departments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Extremely good PROFESSOR. There is a decent chunk of work (you can still get an A without putting 100% in tho) but he leaves you kinda wanting to engage in the content. It's quite interesting and he does a great job presenting it. 1 test thats kinda hard unless you do the readings, 3 writing assignments, 1 big final project. Would recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Truly a wonderful professor! More work than a typical intro class, but very manageable (~20m reading before each class). Only 1 midterm, but easy to do well if you pay attention. After that, just a few 1-question pop quizzes on readings. Final presentation+paper on an interview instead of an exam. I took it for a premed req, but learned a lot!

Frenette is goated. He's knowledgeable about his field and enjoys teaching, making class interesting. Gives lots of feedback on assignments and grades easily. 20-page readings before each class, 3 1-page papers, 1 midterm, 1 interview project, and 1 6-8 pg final paper. Lots of work but the class made me leave my comfort zone and was very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Frenette was an incredible educator. His lectures were interesting and engaging. He made sociology exciting and relevant. He always treated students with kindness and understanding, and made himself available outside of class to offer help. His feedback on assignments was detailed and personalized. He is such a joy to learn from.

Professor Frenette has a really fun dynamic in the classroom. He cares about what he teaches and encourages classroom discussion. There are pop-quizzes, and the workload can be a lot if you don't get started early. Overall, I learned a lot from the class and look forward to taking another class with Professor Frenette!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Incredible professor, would absolutely take again if he secures tenure next yr. Genuinely cares abt his students, class is an easy A if you show up and participate. Study for the midterm but as long as you are paying attention you'll be fine. Easy grader and very accessible outside of class if you need feedback/clarity on grading. Highly recommend.

You can tell that Frenette is actually passionate about teaching and, although attendance is mandatory, I found that the lectures were interesting and easy to follow. He genuinely wants you to succeed and as long as you do want is required and attend class, you will do fine.

Professor Frenette is super understanding, supportive and clearly cares about his students. He explains material well and keeps class engaging. However, the pop quizzes and midterm were overly specific and felt like a test of memorization than comprehension. Despite that, the class had a positive, encouraging learning environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS. YOU WON'T REGRET IT.

Name me another professor who gives a 1-page pdf of feedback on your assignment. Literally the most caring and hilarious professor i've ever had. took this for pre-med soc requirement, enjoyed it very much. You will get good grades as long as you put in effort - this guy WANTS TO GIVE YOU POINTS. TAKE HIM OVER SOC1010. goated french canadian man

Awesome class. Absolutely take. Engaging and super interesting. The readings are 20ish pages but honestly not awful and you can take like 15 min to skim and be fine. Graded on response papers, midterm, final pres and paper, all of which he makes super doable. One of my fav classes I've taken at Vandy, definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Frenette is easily one of my favorite soc professors I've had. The class is super interesting, to do well on exams/quizzes you have to at least skim the readings/have a vague idea what they are about. Response papers are easy and final project & paper take time but are straightforward. Midterm is easy if you study for a bit the night before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hilarious & tbh kinda fine Canadian-French guy. Srsly cares about engaging w his students. Reading heavy for a 1000 course - I read all of them, but I also know ppl who didn't and still did well on tests. Go to class bc some stuff on tests are not in readings. Put effort and a good grade on the response papers/proposals is very attainable.

Prof. Frenette was great! The class was not insanely difficult. Attending lectures is very important because he emphasizes specific details that he wants you to know for his midterm and response papers. He gives great feedback and wants you to succeed. Participate and communicate with him, and you will be successful in this course. Would recommend!

I think this professor is great and he genuinely cares about sociology. The 3 papers are annoying but short, to prepare for pop quizzes just chat gpt a summary of the readings. I personally don't care or enjoy creative career stuff  so I found the class super boring, but if you are a music or theater person you would probably enjoy it. Easy grader.

Such a genuine, kind human! Very smart and engaging, and has a good sense of humor. I learned so much in this class, but I felt it was a ton of work for a 1000-level course. The midterm was oddly difficult and the research paper and presentation were time-consuming. It's a fairly heavy workload for an intro class, but very interesting nonetheless.

Prof. Frenette is a great professor. You are graded based on participation in class, 3 one-page response papers to certain readings, a proposal+presentation, and a couple of really easy 1-2 question quizzes. I found him accommodating and accessible outside of class, and his lectures very interesting. He's also hilarious. Lenient if you communicate!

Professor Frenette is so incredibly kind and understanding. He is extremely passionate about sociology which is clear in the lectures. 

The class was quite a bit of work, but Professor Frenette provides great feedback and all materials are very organized and accessible. If you put in the effort needed, you will definitely get a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Frenette was an amazing professor who kept everyone engaged with his funny lectures. There's one midterm, 3 short papers, and 1 big interview essay. The interview process seems daunting at first, but Dr. Frenette will make it manageable step by step. Very easy to access outside of class. I have learned so much about sociology from his class!

He is a very kind and caring professor and always encourages students to ask questions. The workload is kind of too much for a 1000 level soc course. There are many readings and writing in this course, but Dr. Frenette offers very clear and helpful lectures. If you can prepare those reading very well, it won't be hard to get an A.

Fantastic professor and class. Mine was about creative careers. Grade consisted of participation, a couple of pop quizzes, some response papers, a midterm, a presentation, and final portfolio. There were quite a bit of readings but they were all short journals. Great guy and clear and generous grading

The large research paper seems very overwhelming but is made manageable. Lectures arent the most exciting, but he does open up for discussion quite a bit, so it depends on the class itself. Material is super easy if youre a soc major. Its clear he is very caring and flexible!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very chill professor and a nice person in general. I learned a lot from his lectures and his assignments had clear guidelines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thought the class would be a lot more interesting than it was. It was very complicated when it really should not have been, and I found that he was slightly passive-aggressive. The concepts were so theoretical it made it really hard to ever really understand anything at a deeper level. SO MUCH JARGON. It wasn't hard, just not enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Frenette is one of the better professors I've had here. He tries to engage his students and guides them clearly through the work. The big final project and paper feels a bit overwhelming in the beginning but the smaller assignments throughout help make it manageable. His feedback is really valuable and helps you succeed. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Frenette is knowledgeable and gave good advice on the large project. The project was fruitful and designed in a way that we only did one part at a time. There was one mid-term exam and no final exam, just a short presentation and a final portfolio. Do the readings and pay attention in class, and you'd be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An understanding, standout character in the time of COVID and online classes. I was going through some really difficult circumstances during finals and when I didn't turn my final in on time, I got an email with a non-penalizing extension and words of encouragement, no questions asked. Great guy and he really values you learning over anything.

Professor Frenette is one of the nicest people I've ever met. Really wants you to learn the material in class, which is pretty interesting. He doesn't grade too harsh and gives amazing feedback. The final project is really important to the grade and there's a pretty simple midterm and a few response papers. Very easy to talk to out of class.

Professor Frenette is the nicest guy. He clearly wants everyone to learn and love the subject. If you do all the work its not hard to do well and hes very understanding and helpful in office hours. The majority of the work is for a big project worth 50% of your grade. Theres also a midterm and some reading quizzes, but theyre not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I'm not built for economics, but Professor Crockett is amazing nonetheless
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Crockett is fabulous. She's always so energetic and passionate, and she clearly cares about every single student. Although macro isn't the easiest class, she explains difficult contents very well. Her exams are slightly difficult so make sure you understand the formulas and concepts (don't just memorize them). Go to her office hours
She is a very nice professor that deeply cares about her students. The class itself was very logical and easy to work through.
Professor Crockett is awesome. Econ 3022 isn't the easiest class in the world, but she definitely helps in understanding the content. Would definitely take again.

Amy sticks closely to the slides and tries to expand, but often seems unsure of the material. Attendance isn't required but is extremely helpful—if you go, you'll be well prepared. Exams are fairly easy if you study, but expect to use the full time.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Crockett's class was super easy to understand. Her lectures were helpful and she was always super accessible during office hours and email. Definitely take her class for ECON 3022!

If you're about to take ECON 3022, definitely choose Dr. Crockett. Her lectures are very understandable and she makes it crystal clear which concepts would be on the test and how to study for them. Grading is fair, exams are fair, assignments are manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super friendly professor. She remembers people's names and chats with each one of us before class. The environment class is low-stress easy-A, graded on participation 10%, assignments 20%, midterm 25%, research reports (20%), and final paper25%. No FINAL! Very lenient grader and accessible through email. prob the best prof for 3000 econ elective.

She is one of the kindest professors I've had and genuinely cares so much about students. She is clear about what exams will look like and they are all very manageable. Gives practice exams. One short homework assignment a week, 2 midterms, and a final. She is accessible outside of class and is willing to help with anything! Highly recommend

I took her environmental course, she's the best! Like everyone is saying, she really takes the time to get to know students. Her classes were always fun, and she brought such a good energy to lectures. Her assignments are super manageable, and she let's you explore what you're interested in. Prof. Crockett is an amazing professor, take her courses!

Highly recommend. One of the best Econ professors I've had. Genuinely cares and takes the time to really get to know students. Good at explaining and relating Econ topics to the real world. Tests are very manageable and fair. Very accesible outside of class and really wants students to succeed. Lectures were also pretty interesting.

Professor Crockett is one of the nicest professors I've had at Vanderbilt. She makes an effort to get to know every student and is great at explaining concepts you may not understand. Graded on short weekly homeworks that help you understand course content, two midterms, and a final. Also very accessible outside of class through email
Whoever said weird vibes in the class nailed it. She's great at what she does and I really the class at first. After a while it felt like the class revolved more around her than the learning

Dr. Klyce is a sweet person. The structure is good—graded on many things. However, she is not lenient. You must be in person to turn in homework, or it's late. You're allowed to work together, but if your homework is too similar to others, you can get flagged for cheating. Overall unclear instructions and high maintenance for a 1000 level class.
weird vibe in the class

Great Professor! I did not take the lab, just the lecture. There are some quizzes, but as long as you do the problem sets, your grade should be fine! One of the best professors! Would highly recommend this professor if you need to take a science class as a requirement. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities!
Dr Klyce is amazing and if you have basically any prior knowledge of geology you will get an A in this class. It's called rocks for jocks for a reason.

Dr Klyce is absolutely amazing, and EES 1510 lecture is super easy. If you have basically any prior knowledge of geology, you will receive an A in the class. She's super helpful and I was extremely comfortable asking questions. The only thing is that there is a lot of reading but you don't have much homework outside of it, so it's a good trade off.

Class was very messy (changing field trip dates, changing attendance policy mid-semester). Labs were ridiculously long (took most of the class more than 14 hours on multiple labs). With that said, Dr. Klyce is a good professor (if you're looking to take 1510, ignore this. it's very easy and fun, which tricked me into taking this diabolical class)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is way too difficult and odee for a 100 level course.

I love Dr. Klyce, she's a fantastic teacher who is passionate about teaching Geology. But the amount of work for the 1 credit lab, and difficult grading of the problem sets have hurt my experience, too much work for a 1000-level science course, I will not be taking another EES class in the future.

The reason why recent reviews are so much worse is because she is actively trying to change the geology curriculum to reflect the difficulty of physics and chem, rather than oceanography or astronomy.

Not worth the lab credit. Dr. Klyce is on some ego trip and unless you're a carbon copy of her do not take this class. She's the LEAST understanding teacher I have ever had. Makes tests impossibly hard unless your an EES major. I actually really enjoy geology but bc of her I'm not adding a double major.

The lab was significantly harder than the actual class. The lab midterm was ridiculous but only counts for 15% of the grade. If you are looking to just fulfill the lab requirement, DON'T TAKE. It's not worth it unless you're really into rocks.
Bad bad bad - do not take if you care about your gpa and time!

From the class itself, I am traumatized, but deep down, but I do think Dr. Klyce does care for her students. I wish the grading rubric were clearer for lab reports and that the trips were more planned out in advance. The class is stressful, but Dr. Klyce does excel at explaining difficult content. Challenging class!
She makes it obvious when she has a bad day.

Dr. Klyce is one of the sweetest faculty on this campus! The class does sometimes feel like I'm being babied a little, but honestly, as a stressed college student I needed that breath of fresh air, and it balances out because geology is very vocab-intense so the constant reinforcement of concepts was helpful.

Dr. Klyce is the sweetest ever! She is so enthusiastic about geology and it bleeds into her students. There are weekly(ish) problem sets that are relatively difficult, but the LAs help. There are also weekly reading and reflections - easy. There are five exams and half the grade is a group exam. Would definitely recommend taking this class!

Dr. Klyce is one of the best professors I've ever had. She cares so much about all her students and the summatives are part individual and part group tests. There's readings and reflections due at the end of each week but they're super easy. The only thing I struggled with is the worksheets, but she and the LAs are always there to help if needed.

Didn't find the lab difficult, but workload was higher than expected for a 1-credit course. Took off 1 point for quality because the lab answer keys were not always accurate/helpful. Most labs graded on completion, TAs are accessible, and can retake lab quizzes. If you're not taking the lecture with the lab, you will be confused

Dr. Klyce is amazing! Her lectures are so clear and engaging with lots of demos/activities to help you understand the concepts. There can be a lot of "busywork" at times but the assignments contribute to your learning. Summative assessments are easy, p-sets are slightly harder but there's lots of support from LAs. One of my favorite professors!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I don't understand why there are any negative reviews. She is the most caring professor I've had at Vandy. She is very enthusiastic about teaching and it makes the class very fun. Only the lab is a little difficult. The lecture is one of my favorite classes I've taken though.

Honestly, simply the worst professor! She does seem knowledgeable about the topic and that's about it - the interaction, the way she structures the class, the belittle-ing of students. It is also impossible to get A without attending every single class. There are about 6 or so midterms, 100s parts of the grade, and so on. AVOID AT ALL COST!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This 100% should be everyone's science credit. I learned a lot about the world. Not a hard class if you pay attention and take notes. You're graded on so many things so nothing is high pressure (class isn't too much work though). Her research is on how to teach geology, so assignments and lectures are interesting and well designed.

One of the greatest professors at Vanderbilt. She is extremely caring, reaches out to her students, and tries to help them in any way she can. However, the class is a little tough and has a lot of laborious work and the grading on the summatives can be random and harsh. If you work a little, this class might be your fav classes at vanderbilt!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An incredibly difficult lab. There is a lot of work and quizzes every week. It takes up the entire 3 hours most weeks. So much memorization. The course has an emphasis on figuring it out yourself which led to so much frustration because you never know if you're right or wrong. If you just need a lab credit, don't take this. Run.
Quizzes and midterm are unreasonably difficult. Unclear expectations of prior knowledge for a lot of the labs. Does not answer emails.

Dr. Klyce is by far still the best science professor I've had at Vanderbilt University. She sets the benchmark for what I want to see in a professor. She has a very organized and structured learning environment. I couldn't believe any of the negative reviews; if you are disorganized and not interested in work, then this class is not for you.

Dr. Klyce is such a kind and understanding professor. People complaining must be disorganized or disinterested. You're graded on daily quizzes (easy, if you get ~70% right over semester you get 100%), easy summative tests, and very interesting exploratory assignments. Lectures are engaging and make clear what will be on the tests. Top notch prof.
Dr. Klyce is a great professor. It's quite easy to succeed in the class. The exams are easy and she cares about her students

The amount of work required for this class was absurd. Varied grading on the problem sets, she did not tell students how to study for summative assessments until the 3rd and she acts like she cares, but she has a passive-aggressive demeanor under this facade. It was nice of her to provide extra credit. I earned an A, but it was an awful experience.

A few instances of unclear grading due to the amount of vocab in geo, but I have very, very positive things to say about Dr. Klyce not only as an educator but as a person. Very accessible before, after, and outside of class, it's very clear she cares about her students, their learning, and their lives. Made geo interesting, applicable, and fun.

Assigns a portion of a test at 1pm the day of spring break. Every other class has an assignment worth a small amount of your grade to force you to go to class if you want an A. Inconsistent problem set grading to the point where the same problem set could get a 75 or a 100.

Great professor- problem sets are a bit subjective sometimes I got an A othertimes a C but she does drop your lowest grade on p.sets, reflections and homework! There are lots of mini assignments and an optional final that will replace your lowest exam grades. Expect lots of mini assignments- if you are not organized do not take this class!

Prof is really nice but like everyone else is saying, grading sometimes seems arbitrary. Best thing to do is to show up at her office hours & have her check over your work so you don't risk a random B-. Attendance isn't mandatory but SHOW UP. Participation questions usually cluster around one day a week, and if you miss it, your grade TANKS.

You could turn in an assignment the exact same as someone else and somehow get a completely different letter grade. The grading for this class seems completely random and inconsistent. Also she does not post any lecture slides or notes online due to "Creating a sense of community". Literally the most frustrating class I've ever taken.

Unrealistic expectations for the course material; slides are not posted. Actively talks down to students and treats us like children. Grading criteria are completely ambiguous, and no feedback is provided. Learn more in the lab than in the actual class. Klyce seems to believe she's better than her students and LOVES to belittle them. Do not take.

Dr. Klyce is sweet but the most frustrating thing about the entire class is the way her problem sets are graded. For a class that feels like you'll get an A as long as you put effort, grading feels extremely nitpicky esp on p.sets. Sometimes you'll confirm your sheet with an LA or her, get affirmations, and still get a bad grade. Super annoying.

Dr. Klyce was great because of how much she cares for her students. Her class can feel like busy work at times. However, if you attend class, complete all assignments/homework, and study a little for the six summative assessments, you will get an A. There are so many grades factored into your final grade that it's hard not to do well.

TOP 3 PROFESSOR AT VANDY! She made rocks extremely interesting by connecting your knowledge to real-world scenarios. You aren't learning to learn in this class, you're learning for long-term knowledge like where to buy a house and where not to. She understands most people take this for AXLE so she doesn't teach unnecessary information. Take this!
Lots of homework, and you have to attend class every Wednesday and Friday if you don't want to miss assignments/quizzes, but it's a pretty easy class and Dr. Klyce is a fun Professor.

This professor somehow manages to make a 100-person lecture feel personal and it makes me sad that I will not have her for any of my future courses. I would highly recommend taking geology with her regardless of your major.

LET ME TELL YOU. Annie Klyce is a gem. An absolute gem. I was lucky enough to take her class during her wedding season and it was super fun to get to watch her develop during this formative time in both of our lives. In terms of the material- it's rocks. I mean, how in-depth can rocks really be? I ended with an A, you probably will too.

Dr. Klyce's lectures are efficient and her expectations for the class were clear. There are many summative assessments, though. But the good thing is that they're just mini quizzes, which is way easier than midterm and finals. Definitely recommend her class if you're interested in Geology or just looking for a science class to fulfill AXLE.

Your entire grade is determined by 5 pop quizzes. If you fail these, you will see the consequences. There is no system by which this professor seems to grade. You are better off taking AP lit. I regret taking this class, I've learned little more than I can learn in a day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Would not do again
She is unclear in her grading, has no rubric or doesnt show it to students, and assigns pointless work. She emphasizes handwriting over depth in writing, and treats us like elementary age children.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Don't take her
Most of her "teaching" is just in-class discussion. Very little lecturing happens, and her subjective grading criteria are unclear. Very frustrating class

Whilst I initially enjoyed this class, it soon became the worst mistake ever. She is absolutely arrogant and honestly a nightmare. Her attitude towards students does not create a good learning environment in the slightest. Save your time, energy and dignity and stay far far away from taking anything she offers.

This professor is amazing. I got switched into this class because of the req but the course material was easy to follow. Participation also matters so make sure you do that. She is a great person, as well! Enjoyed her class & it's easy if you do as you're told.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Rest in Peace, Professor Olani
I didn't take this class, but R.I.P. Olani

the professor's tests frequently deviate from class material and he rarely gives enough resources to prepare. He doesnt really explain the questions during office hours. Outside of class, he is pretty inaccessible and rarely responds to emails. Good person buit bad professor.

came into this class w ap stats background (5) and still struggled. incredibly disorganized, never responded to emails, and wouldn't let us see our midterm exams. felt a clear gap between class slides and tested material. class averages were consistently in 70s, and he said during the final that he was done taking any more qs before time ended
irrelevant lectures, zero actual teaching, incredibly difficult tests with not enough time to finish them.
Didn't respond to 5/6 emails I sent, SO unorganized it's insane, genuinely feels like he's making it up as he goes. There is no structure.
Teaching style very unorganized. Expectations not clear, you will be teaching yourself

Amazing guy, super caring and funny, but a bad teacher. The lectures aren't relevant to the exam material, the tests make up 80% of your grade with no curve, even when he says he will. He's really nice and accessible, but getting help won't make a difference because the exams make no sense, and you won't finish on time.
Doesnt bother teaching, Formula sheet doesn't contain important formulas, Never clear what is on the test and what isnt, Nowhere near enough time to finish the tests
Unorganized and messed up the grading.

I'm still taking this class but there seems to be a lot of confusion btwn Olani and Andrade. Olani has bad reviews bc ppl say that he is disorganized. While i do think that his lectures might slightly be a bit disorganized, I think that he is less strict than Andrade. I recommend him and he cares for his students. He emphasizes what'll be on test!

Professor Olani is hard to understand and does not really teach, however, all his notes are clearly posted on slides which are easy to follow. Also, his tests always include a few questions that were in homework/practice tests/textbook so it is easy to do well.
Do not take this course if you don't have to

Highly dependent on whether you have previous statistics knowledge for not (ie: if you've taken AP Statistics, this class is relatively simple; however, without prior knowledge, this class will be difficult because his lectures aren't exactly helpful). Kind and funny man, but not a great professor in terns of teaching skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Olani is the absolute best! He is extremely helpful in office hours and genuinely wants each student to succeed. He loves when students ask questions and is hilarious. He makes class entertaining and really knows what he is talking about. I do not understand the negative comments here. Olani is a top professor at Vanderbilt. TAKE HIM.
Awesome professor. Best professor I have taken at Vanderbilt! No Stats background and did great job teaching! 10/10.

Class is tough, but if you pay attention you should be fine. Uses pop quizzes to ensure attendance, so be warned, but they're graded on completion more often than not. He was always excited in class, though that sometimes got him off topic. He worked with us to adjust course schedule to fit class and material needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sometimes, Professor Olani would say something wouldn't be on the exam, but I would later find it there. Additionally, I really struggled to follow along with his lessons, often wondering what the point was of attending class at all. I honestly found this class very frustrating, even though I tried really hard!
Hard to understand, and when you do, you get worse at what you're learning. I was better off teaching myself everything. Funny guy though

Olani is a funny professor who uses lots of random analogies, but the class is basically intro stats. Lectures aren't very helpful, so you'll need to study on your own. The class is curved to a B+ and has four problem sets, participation quizzes, two midterms, and a final, with a formula sheet allowed.
If you don't have a statistics base knowledge, never take this class

The worst professor I have met in Vanderbilt. Don't take this class. He puts off nearly all deadlines due to his inefficient class, and gives appalling bad formatting problems and solutions for midterm review. No need to say how he goes off topics during every class.
he is chill but ........

Easily the worst professor I took at Vanderbilt, and possibly in my entire life, and I'm so glad I took him. Here are some quotes from him:
“Suppose you are diabetic… God forbid"
“6 or 7 years ago, there was a lady that was sued. Does anyone know? Anyone?”
"If you want COVID or a cold, come to my office hours. You're welcome"

He definitely cares about his students and is a sweet person. Unfortunately, he's terrible at job - don't take this man unless you desire confusion and suffering. ESPECIALLY don't take him if you have no stats background.

He is very kind and funny. You can tell he cares about his students, and it is not difficult to get a good grade if you put forth some effort. He has an accent, but you can still understand him perfectly fine. I would definitely take him again. Your grade is based on 2 midterms, a final, and several problem sets.

Very kind in office hours, but he's a bad lecturer. If you are good at self-studying, just show up to classes for the occasional attendance check. I was pretty bad at self-studying, so I got a horrendous grade on the final. He does curve though.

Professor Olani is awesome. His class has a relaxed atmosphere and a manageable workload. He loves to get feedback from students and tries his best to improve. Also, if you go to class, he will tell you exactly what you need to prepare for the exam—highly recommended!

Professor Olani is actually a nice guy. He does his best to teach the class and usually goes over all the materials that show up on the test, even giving tips. Show up, participate, do your best, and trust me it will be more than enough.

Olani is a great funny person. He sometimes gets ahead of himself during lecture but he does good examples in class. You can learn a lot by studying the slides yourself if it doesn't make sense in class. Also tells us approximately what'll be on tests. He really cares about his students and rounded my grade to an A from a 91.7 without me asking

Professor Olani can be hard to understand in class sometimes since he gets caught up in random details but his lectures are overall good. He has an accent but you can still understand him. If you just show up to class, he'll tell you everything on the test and is extremely generous with grades. Also, he's just an amazing, funny guy.

honestly a really nice guy. lectures can be a bit unclear sometimes but make sense generally, and he is extremely lenient with exams (depending on how much he gets through, he reduces the amount of questions, topics, etc). despite saying he wont give alternative exam dates, he did just to work around students schedules. less work than other classes

Professor Olani is a very cute man with a cute accent. He sometimes gets sidetracked during lectures and talk about how he has to pick up his daughter but he cares about the learning of students. Can be sometimes a bit unclear during his lectures but he is super lenient with curving and the class average is actually quit high. FREE OROMIA
He is a really sweet guy, and he cares a lot about students. His exams were tough, though.
Great guy, and I actually enjoyed his class. You can see how passionate he is about what he teaches. It's inspiring.

Funny guy, super nice, don't need to show up to class. Super test heavy and he isn't great at covering content. Exams are such a gamble. Final got screwed up, but it was the department overruling his decision to do an online final.

Olani seems so sweet and kind but this class was so confusing and hard to get a good grade. Lectures are boring and just a repetition of whatever is in the textbook and your grade is dependent on three tests. The dept made him move our online final in person a week before it was supposed to be which frustrated a lot of students.

Kind and means well, but lectures are super confusing and disorganized. Grade is mainly determined by three tests which are difficult and very hard to study for. This class was painful to get through.

Very nice guy, not the best teacher. Lectures were unengaging. There were 2 exams and a final along w/ 8 quizzes with the exams making up a bulk of the grade. Tests & quizzes often had questions that weren't covered in class. He's fine if you felt like you understood macro, but if you struggled in macro Olani's class isn't gonna do you any favors
Worst teacher ever. Don't take class.

8 quizzes, two papers, two midterms, and a final. He doesn't respond to emails, skips over content during lecture, and goes completely around any questions you ask after class. Everything is very disorganized and the exam content and material is usually all over the place and isn't always relevant. Would definitely AVOID taking this class.
THEY MOVED THE EXAM A WEEK BEFORE FROM ONLINE TO IN PERSON. Have to change all my flights and moving times. Absolutely ridiculous.
Doesn't respond to emails. Many questions are incorrect. Avoid.

Olani's a really great guy. Very caring and understanding, even if you missed a quiz or midterm. His teaching is actually not bad-- yes he goes on tangent BUT he does explain things. the problem is the fact he doesnt make his own tests, so what we learn vs get tested on is different. he explains the basics and the test is far more in depth & harder

Honestly horrible class. Does not actually teach. Impossible to know how you are currently doing in the class and the quizzes and exams are extremely difficult for anybody who does not cheat. Avoid this class if you can.

Super kind professor, but seemed a bit disorganized. Grading criteria would change as the class went on. However he really wanted everyone to do well and curved the final grades a ton, so it was definitely possible to get an A. Not the best prof but you don't really need to avoid him
honeslty if you show up to class he tells you what's on the exam and most of the class is hw based don't trust these reviews I love Olani

He is passionate but new to teaching intro level courses, had heavy testing (2 midterms, 1 final, 8 quizzes with 3 dropped). Lectures sometimes confusing due to tangents, but he's kind at the end of the day.

Great guy, terrible prof. You learn from the textbook, but even that is not helpful. Many questions are wrong &he makes up grading, exams, etc. on the spot. Won't answer emails or show to extra office hours that he says he will. Tests & quizzes seem easy, but everyone does bad. FYI, I think he curved everyone by abt 10%. He is accommodating tho

He is a nice guy, but he's up there with one of the worst professors I've had. Doesn't teach; doing well in this class is 100% contingent on whether you read the textbook, and even then, the TopHat program is useless and unnecessarily hard. It might as well have been an online class, because he is 100% reliant on  TopHat.
His lectures are terrible, honestly not much of a point in going, you can just stay in and follow along on the slides online. Tests are kind of hard, but online

He will constantly be behind in the material taught in class to the point where we will have quizzes on material not covered. most of the quiz answers are impossible to answer. Not even he knows the answer to them but he refuses to admit it. On top of that, he does not even post the readings on time so you can't get ahead or even study.

Olani is a nice guy and he does seem to try very hard to be a good professor. He is accessible a lot outside of office hours and is willing to answer questions. But it was impossible not to space out during his lectures because he only uses slides and speaks in a very monotone voice. Tests were hard but the final grade is curved.

If I could have taken the class with a different professor I would have. Olani is a nice guy, but a terrible professor. He does not communicate expectations and he grades very slowly so most of the time you have no idea what to expect. Our final exam mostly covered material from the final 2 units (which we didn't cover in lectures). Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but not a good professor. Expect to teach yourself most of the material. Show up to class because he gives pop quizzes. Our class was constantly running weeks behind schedule and he's a slow grader so you have no idea how you're doing in the class until the very end.
I think he's good for an instructor. Very nice and easy going.
I had to say he was really hard to follow. I learned very few.
Absolutely the worst lecturer I have seen

Olani is genuinely nice and cares about the students. Lectures are pretty vague and I needed to review the book to do well on exams. Well intentioned but not the best teacher. Not hard to get above a B.
The worst

Genuinely a nice guy, but his exams are too difficult and you have no idea what you're doing. Rarely reply to emails (even if you have an urgent concern), which is very annoying. Terrible lecturer as well, I don't know why he is teaching classes here. Avoid if you can.

Classes are trainwrecks. His tests purposefully try to trick you. Often has to give back points because his multiple choice questions are flat out incorrect. Doesn't tell you how the grades are curved until the very end, so you're pretty much screwed in terms of knowing how well you are doing.

Don't take his class if you've got better options. Can't explain things to save anyone's life, let have any consistency with his lectures. You won't know your homework grade at all so you don't know what to fix.

While Olani is caring as a person, he is a terrible professor. His lectures go off so many tangents that he takes forever to get through the material. Better off reading the textbook and looking at slides than going to class. Also oblivious to what students need. Forgets about half the things he says, has zero accountability or reliability.
Exams are difficult and not related to the lectures at all. Self-study the textbook from the very beginning.
Nice guy, give extensions to HWs. Horrible lectures. You have no idea what you're doing on the HWs and exams. The exam questions are sometimes wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Olani is a nice guy who cares about his students, but his status as a 'professor' is laughable. Absolutely horrible lectures. You're on your own for material, and the only reason students do well on his tests is because they cheat.

Olani doesn't actually teach very much, he loves to go off on rants about random subjects that are only tenuously connected to economics. Just read the textbook; that's the only way to learn the material.

He is one of the most flexible and caring professors I've met, and an incredibly nice guy. However, struggled to learn a lot of the material necessary to do well in exams because this class is one of the most difficult ones in the Econ major. Without previous background in a programming language, you need to learn a lot on your own for homework.

Horrible lectures, lots of homework that is barely explained, difficult exams (online and ppl only do well by cheating) that you have no guidance for and you will learn basically nothing unless you are teaching yourself. That being said, he makes himself accessible during office hours and can be influenced to increase deadlines and stuff.

Prof. Olani really cares about his students. He is the nicest professor I have ever met. However, the class material requires hard work and a solid understanding of mathematic proof. Take the class if you want to challenge yourself. Otherwise, 3032 is a much better alternative.

Do yourself a favor and avoid him at all costs. Lectures were utterly useless. He covers the absolute bare minimum of each chapter -- you'll get to the homeworks and exams and have no idea what you're doing. Only reason I bothered showing up to class is to know when deadlines were because he changed them constantly without updating Brightspace.

the class material of econ1500 isn't bad, but olani himself makes the course difficult because of his bad planning and horrible lectures. just don't take him; he will make your life harder than it needs to be
He sucks, doesn't teach the material and just assigns you a grade at the end of the semester.
he literally missed the final grades deadline, along with teaching students how to code max twice the entire semester despite us needing it for every homework assignment

If you have no experience with stats (aka you didn't take AP Stats in high school), I would not recommend taking 1500 with Olani. He lectures on principle concepts but more complex applications show up on the tests. If you did take stats though, I *would* recommend! He's very caring and it should be straightforward if you have a good foundation.
really bad lecturer, nice guy but awful professor

Honestly pretty average, but sufficient to teach the class. You don't have to show up, there are like 3 or 4 homeworks, 2 midterms and a final. The class is chill asf, barely harder than AP stats. You'll be fine.

Honestly,80% of the content is stuff in AP Statistics. This is an extremely easy course itself, and one could self-study and ace the midterm (midterm is can be tough but it's open book). For a new learner, it can be tough to follow, but since he goes through the content very slowly, it is more efficient to study the content yourself. HW is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Knew less about the topic than some students, and the tests were poorly made with some questions not even having the correct answers.

I won't take professor Olani's class again. Econ 1500 is a good class, since I enjoy the process of problem solving. He talks in such a slow pace that I almost forget what he said before this word. Sometimes, he even cannot finish his class content and even required us to finish he homework even he hadn't talked about.

To say that I know what is going on in this class would be a lie. To say Professor Olani knows how to run this class, even more of a lie. Very nice and funny professor, but you will not learn the material. Doesn't really teach you how to code for homework assignments or anything of substance.

5 quizzes, 2 exams, and a final. Dropped lowest exam grade. Lectures were good; reading the textbook helped clarify. Definitely take Olani - he's a fantastic instructor. Cares SO MUCH about students learning and doesn't fixate on grades at all (he once said he was going to curve so most everyone had an A or B). 100/10. Great choice for econ classes

Professor Olani cares about his students. He would proceed through the material slowly, which was a little boring, but he made sure we understood the concepts. The homework is fairly graded and isn't much of a burden, and he is open to any questions you might have about the course materials or just the major in general.

Olani is an average prof. His lectures sometimes are disorganized, especially toward the end of the semester when he runs out of time without finishing the hard parts of each chapter. Quizzes and midterms are all multiple choice during COVID so make sure that you understand the concepts clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pretty average lecturer, yet very caring and funny. Grade is based on two midterms, final, and roughly 5-6 quizzes. Dropped lowest exam score since the class average was in the low 60s. Overall, above average in the Vandy Econ department.

Olani is very nice and cares about his students. He definitely cares more about you learning than your grades, which was refreshing. Lectures can be a bit disorganized but if you have questions he'll make sure to clear it up. Overall, great guy and professor for a difficult course!

Lectures were basically useless -- tests/quizzes are almost entirely based off textbook reading. He's a nice guy but the class is way too disorganized and definitely the worst of the econ classes I've taken at Vandy. I also felt like the tests/quizzes were hard to do well on because they're all multiple choice and conceptual.
Olani is a great guy, but his classes just don't do it for me. My other econ classes have been much better. If you can, look for other professors.

Professor Olani is a really nice guy. The class feels a little disorganized sometimes, but he wants all of his students to do well. Definitely one of the best prof choices for intermediate macro - take him if you can.

He's a really nice person and cares a lot about his students. His lectures are pretty useless though  I think I learned 90% of the material by reading the textbook. Problem sets from the homework were just textbook questions that took a while, but very representative of midterm questions. Very generous curve at the end, most kids got an A.

Really great guy, a funny professor, super caring, super dedicated. Just not a great lecturer at all. It doesn't help that the material is dry as well. That said, he curves a lot and puts homework questions on the test so if you go to class and keep up with the assignments and study hard you should be fine. Also, the TAs are not very helpful.

Does not care much about grades so gives lots of As. The material is easy so it's easy to slack off and fail a test later. He is a very nice guy so ask questions and talk to him in class if that is your thing. Accent to where if you arent paying attention you wont understand, but its a non factor if you pay attention and ask questions. Dry material

One of the most dedicated profs at Vanderbilt. Truly cares about his students and does whatever he can to support us. No question is a bad question, and stops to make sure everyone understands what he's teaching. Exams are similar to problem sets. Problem sets take a few hours but are doable. Take him.

FANTASTIC professor. Super caring, very funny, and a real pleasure to study with. I found myself looking forward to his class every single day, and I definitely want to study with him again in the future. Problem sets take a few hours each but are great indicators of exam questions - the two are very similar. Very fair overall, good curve.
Olani is not a good lecturer but he gives homework assignments that are extremely helpful for your midterms. As long as you understand how to do your homework, it is not hard to get an A.

Olani is probably my favorite member of the Vanderbilt Econ department. Absolutely hilarious during lectures, but still an excellent teacher who taught me a bunch about statistics. Sometimes people argued with him during class, but Olani was always right. Homework assignments and tests are graded thoroughly and he gives a sick curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: The content is super easy as it is basically identical to AP Stats. In addition, he is a nice guy that wants his students to succeed. It is not hard at all to get an A. However, despite all of this, I WOULD NOT take him again. As someone else said, he is a very mediocre lecturer and not well-organized. I don't think he should be teaching classes

he is one of the best people I have ever met. He is passionate about teaching and loves the classroom and his students. He will tell you what is on the tests. However, you will have to teach yourself the course. The homework assignments he gives are very helpful towards the midterms and you can drop one midterm grade.

He is not a very good lecturer; he could definitely be a lot clearer with his explanations of the material. But in the end, he is very caring and really wants the students to do well. In addition, he is very explicit about what will be on the tests, so the tests will end up being very easy if you're there to hear him explain them.

Olani is not a great lecturer, but his expectations are very straightforward and he's very lenient with grading. Also gives a sick curve at the end, so it's not that difficult to get an A if you go to class and do the homework. Helps if you've taken AP stats to get an easy A

Olani is awful at lecturing, I had to learn econometrics from the book almost exclusively. Seriously, this guy is so bad at teaching. Tests are mostly straightforward though and he grades pretty leniently. He's much better in office hours and is a really nice guy, I just don't think he should be teaching classes here.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Oof. He is absolutely horrible at teaching. One of the worst at explaining things and understanding students I've ever seen. Gets halfway through each lesson and runs out of time so you have to learn the hard stuff yourself. Gievs out problem sets very similar to tests, so no surprises, but it's still pretty hard and you learn literally nothing

Professor Olani is a great guy. His tests are extremely fair with no surprises and he makes it very clear what he expects of you. He may not be the best teacher, but if you can figure out the homework (which is never that hard) you will be fine on the tests. He loves to get students engaged and creates an active classroom.
My GOAT Alexander Jacobs. Great class to take for AXLE credit, study hard, take good notes and you will do well.

Conspiracy theories was probably my favourite class in undergrad. The lectures are very engaging, fun, and informative. Take good notes and make good use of your notecard on exams. The exams were all very fair and you can revise the 2 midterms to be one score category higher. The workload wasn't high but don't procrastinate on the poster.

Prof. Jacobs is great, but I feel there is too much work for a core class. We have 2 midterms and a non-cumulative final on terms in the course (not too difficult) and an assigned book + poster project. He's a fascinating lecturer and incredibly smart, but I just think there is a bit too much work.

Dr Jacobs is truly a gem. Vandy is lucky to have someone who cares as much about his students as Dr Jacobs does. Class is pretty easy, especially if you do the readings he assigns beforehand. My advice: Focus more on soaking up knowledge from Dr Jacobs than on a grade; he's brilliant, and you'll get more out of the class if you engage yourself.

Lots of readings for homework, but there were only 3 MC reading quizzes, 3 writing assignments and a final. Class is lecture only, but he explains concepts very well. he is a very nice professor and such a sweetheart!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved this class. Prof Jacobs is genuinely such a smart guy who offers impressive insights into the content you cover in class and makes the work very manageable. Sets up his grading rubric in a unique way that you will appreciate once you're in it. The amount of reading seems extreme at first, but the discussions make it easy to digest.

Professor Jacobs is amazing. Fascinating class. He does not lecture at you, and the class is very engaging. If you do the readings and participate in class, you will succeed on the exams. He doesn't try to trick you. Very creative and fun assignments. Very fair grader. He cares less about perfection and more about understanding main themes.

Professor AJ might possibly be the best professor at Vanderbilt. He is so generous with grading, prioritizing genuine learning over stress of grades. In class, he is always as hilarious and charming as he is knowledgeable. I suggest that everyone take a class with him if given the chance. Plus, some really fun yet unique assignments.

Religion Politics Culture with Professor Jacobs made me switch my major so that I could take more classes like Professor Jacobs'. He is one of the smartest and most engaging people I have ever met. Take any class you can with him!

Dr. Jacobs is a prof I will remember as one of the best educators I've had in my life. Extremely passionate, energetic, very eloquent. A type of person to talk to for hours and never get bored. Easy grading, nothing tricky. Gives you a token you can redeem if you get a bad grade. Makes it easy to become passionate with what he teaches. Amazing.

Amazing professor. Probably one of the smartest two or three people I've ever met. Unbelievably well read and has forgotten more about history than I will likely ever know. Great guy and just loved his class.

Professor Jacobs has the best-managed class at Vanderbilt. Your grade in AC consists of 5 quizzes, one midterm, a term paper, and a final. But, if you mess up on a quiz, he gives you a token to take everything but the final again. If you need AXLE American credit, TAKE THIS CLASS!

Professor Jacobs is one of the best professors I've had here. He really knows his stuff, and does his best to reduce the stress of graded assignments and exams. Participation in class was extra credit, so you could get full attendance points even if you don't like talking in classes. Highly recommend.

Jacobs is super smart and down to earth. He goes above and beyond to make the content approachable and enjoyable. He really wants you to focus on critical thinking and appreciation of the material rather than worrying about your grade. Has a points based system that lets you focus on growth & improving your writing instead of stressing over grades.

Professor Jacobs is amazing! He cares about his students and you will learn so much from him if you show up to class! He isn't a difficult grader (if you do decent work you'll get an A) and will go out of his way to make sure you succeed!
One of my favorite professors at Vandy! He explains things so well and his lectures are always very interesting.

This man is an amazing professor.  Super smart guy and makes basic topics very interesting.  Doesn't grade too hard, no busy work.  He uses a points-based system that allows you to focus more on understanding the content rather than just trying to get a high grade (if that makes sense).
Great professor

I love Jacobs! His class is pretty much a guaranteed A. His writing is graded pass/fail and his exams just test whether or not you did the readings. Just do the readings and watch the movies and there's no reason why you shouldn't do well. Entertaining and thought provoking teacher as well. Great experience!

Jacobs is a great guy and really cares about his students, and with any US history experience this class should be easy enough. Lectures were interesting and his clear passion for the subject made it easy to be engaged in the material. Really invested in his students' success; he is very accommodating and offered a few extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Jacobs is amazing! He is extremely passionate and knowledgeable when it comes to the subject matter. He is also flexible and understanding when it comes to mental health. The class does have a good amount of reading/participation, but there's extra credit and little homework. If you're interested in a history class, take one of his!
Funny and caring just put in the effort for readings
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Jacobs is one of the sweetest professors I've met on campus. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to do well in his class! He is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about American culture. If you are someone who likes to have more structure and direction in class, this class may not be the best learning format for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Jacobs is the best professor I have had so far at Vanderbilt. His lectures are fast-paced and entertaining, and he gives you every opportunity to do well. You MUST participate and engage in discussion, but it is not hard to do because he truly takes the time to make your questions feel validated. 10/10 recommend.

I took Professor Jacobs' conspiracy theory class last summer. It was a unique course, and I liked the use of Flipgrid. However, the readings were often long and slightly boring (others may disagree). The quizzes were challenging as well. I used my pass fail, but I ended up making an A. Overall, I liked Professor Jacobs, but the class wasn't my fav.

Jacobs is one of the most caring, best professors I've had at Vandy. During corona, he was understanding and shifted class to a very manageable schedule while I still learned a lot. Grades easy and definitely notices student participation. Some of the readings were challenging but still a must-take class for the US AXLE credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Jacobs is one of the best profs at Vandy. He makes class so entertaining and inclusive. I feel like I always learn something new with him and makes me view history in a different way. The class consists of weekly quizzes, a paper, and a final. It is very easy, and I highly recommend to take him to fulfill any axle credits!

Prof Jacobs is incredible. I've had him in other classes and every time he's just so fun. Best lecturer I've ever had by far, and when it's discussion he leads discussion well. Also one of the smartest people I've met in my. Cannot recommend enough - also he's great to talk to in office hours! Cares a ton about the students

I took his online summer class about conspiracy culture, and I loved it. I'm a STEM major, so I was just taking it as an AXLE requirement, but Jacobs made it genuinely enjoyable and interesting. His projects and assignments were fun and encouraged students to express their opinions-it wasn't a terrible workload considering it was a summer class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Jacobs is the best. This class made me interested in minoring in American Studies. It's also a pretty easy class -- if you do the work (not that much), you'll get an A. Definitely recommend for AXLE credit or if you're interested in American history/culture.

Super chill and understanding professor. Lectures weren't always the most interesting, but he cares a lot about his students and wants them to get As. Easy grader in terms of tests/papers. Would definitely recommend this class.

Intro to American Studies did not have much work, but it was still really substantive. I see concepts I learned appear in American culture on a regular basis. His lectures were long, but engaging (lots of thoughtful pacing). Maybe best of all, the grading criteria and the tests were straightforward--exactly what was called for.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really passionate about the subject matter. I enjoyed going to his class in the morning. He has very reasonable exams. He really wants participation and makes discussion sessions for that purpose that make up a significant part of the grade. Barely had homework. You must come to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Jacobs is great. He really cares about the material and is super knowledgeable. Easy A if you go to class and put in the work--he wants you to succeed. Little hw except for the exams and reading 3 short books over the course of the semester for one class discussion on each book.
Easily one of the best professors I've had. His lectures and discussions are very engaging and he's very accessible.
Great teacher, remembers everyone's name, easy class. It is very hard not to get at least an A- in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Jacobs is very interesting in his lectures. He is very knowledgable in his field but asks horribly unspecific questions to engage the class members. Essentially you can pass without ever saying a word in class. He remembers the names of every singe one of his students and genuinely cares about you. He will help anyone pass with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jacobs is an easy grader and professor. Mostly everything is given to you ahead of time for quizzes and tests. He is super nice and gives alot of extra credit. Lectures can be boring but he tries to make them as interesting as he can.

Very nice guy with pretty low expectations. He acknowledges that this is an intro class, so doesn't give too much work. You have 3 speeches that get longer over time and one 5 min science explainer video and that's it. Very light grader, cool prof, attendance is important. Didn't necessarily learn much but got great public speaking practice.

Dr. Morales is an amazing lecturer who knows what he is talking about. He is very respectful of everyone's opinions and is able to showcase nuanced aspects of arguments. I have learned a lot from the discussions in class and I feel more confident in my ability to make arguments. As long as you put in effort, you will have a similar experience.

Morales is the best prof I've had at Vandy. Extremely chill, content is interesting, and he is a super light grader. All you have to do is show up to class. Its clear he just wants people to find rhetoric interesting. I wish I could take another class w him. Anything below an A in this class is purely a personal failure on your end.

One of the best professor I've ever had at Vandy!! He is not only an excellent lecturer, but also very caring and interesting. Very helpful both inside and outside the class and gives useful feedbacks! Def gonna take his other class too!!
He is really nice and the content is super helpful for any field you want to work in or honestly just for life. Not a lot of work, but the work is all "meaningful" I'd say. Definitely recommend.

Honestly, Professor Morales was one of the best professors I have had at Vandy. I had him for science, rhetoric, and controversy. He has great discussions in class and is very open to all perspectives. He was genuinely great and as long as you put in some effort (just go to class), you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Morales is an excellent and entertaining lecturer who actually cares about what students have to say during class discussions. He is a super lenient grader and wants everyone to do well in his class. Definitely recommend him to anyone.

Blair could be a good school, but administrators like Prof Biddlecombe make it an unwelcoming place. Although he is an accomplished musician, he should not be in a dean position as he blatantly disrespects students and single-handedly gives students a negative view of the school. He does not have students' interests or success in mind.
Awesome professor and so passionate about music it is inspirational!
Professor Biddlecombe is too full of himself. The environment Biddlecombe creates in his class is suffocating and unbearable. The most unpleasant of all my hours at Vanderbilt.

I never took a class, but I took a choir clinic from this man. I was only in his presence for 1.5hrs, but i feel like my life is changed. Dr.Biddlecombe is an amazing professer and if I had the chance to take a class from him I would.

OK, if you're there to have some carefree experience this is not the class for you. Biddlecombe is INTENSE about music, and he's going to give everything he's got to get our performance to the highest level possible. He's direct and rehearsals are totally efficient - no wasted time. He understands singers, and is super specific about tone. Worth it

I took Dr. Biddlecombe's class simply because I enjoyed singing in a choir, but he was the sole reason that I developed a passion for choral music. I switched majors and have taken his class every semester since. He is a fantastic and talented director who asks only that you show up to sing with your best effort. Give him a shot you won't regret it
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: For a class that's only worth one credit hour-- despite meeting for 3hrs each week-- it's just too stressful. The material itself isn't stressful because it's just choir repetoire, but the environment Biddlecombe creates in his class is suffocating and unbearable. The 3hrs each week I spent in his class were the most unpleasant of all my hours.

Professor Biddlecombe is just too full of himself. I took this class only because it was required for me as Im a music major, and that is the only reason Id recommend someone take this class if its required for you. Thankfully Im a senior and dont have to sit in those seats anymore. He is cold, harsh and intense especially outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kindest professor I have had in a long time

Wonderful director who really engages with his students and tries to bring out the absolute best in the choirs. Loves to challenge the choral norms and uses innovative means to make choir concerts cool!
Dr. B is the man. like, for real. He's awesome.
Dr. Biddlecombe is easily one of my favorite professors, not only at Blair, but at Vanderbilt in general. A phenomenal musician,  an even better teacher.

This is Dr. Biddlecombe's first year at Vanderbilt, but I'm sure I speak for all of Symphonic Choir when I say he has far exceeded my expectations. Not only is he crystal clear in his instruction and overtly passionate, but he has a great taste in repertoire and a creative vision for his concerts. And he legitimately CARES about his students.

Prof Rokas is an incredibly thoughtful professor who genuinely takes the time to make sure his students understand lecture content especially during office hours. While his lectures can be slower-paced compared to Johnson, I did find them helpful (especially the math/calculation parts), and his exams are more manageable as well. Highly recommend.

Went to two of his lectures and self studied the rest. He goes extremely slow and does not say nor test anything outside the slides. Attendance is worth 0% of your grade. Youre better off spending lecture time doing something else and self studying lectures. There really is not much content and its quite simple (evolution, hardy-weinberg)

Overall, very good. Very knowledgeable and offers good help when asking questions. But content wise, his part of the course is much easier compared to Johnson but his tests can be tricky because the ease of the material makes you be less prepared for them. Read the lectures very well. But an A is very much possible with good effort.

Overall, good professor. Material is easier than johnson's section but exams caught my off guard because the perceived ease of the material made me prepare less for them. It is completely unnecessary to read the textbook for his half of the course. Do practice problems and memorize vocab (sometimes appears word per word from slides)
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Better than Johnson. Moved slower and less content in this half of BSCI 1511. Just like Johnson's exams, the questions are oddly specific. Though, Rokas provided practice questions after each lecture, so that's helpful.

I really liked Rokas. I thought he was passionate and did a great job of teaching new concepts. People are salty because they thought his part would be a lot easier than Johnson's, and it is not. Rokas's slides are very organized, which makes studying for his exams easy. He also only teaches material from lectures (unlike Johnson) which is nice.

Whole class graded on 4 exams (3 midterms and a final). Questions are unreasonably specific and often test on rote memorization rather than understanding. Content was not overly difficult in theory, but this class made me dread biology. Countless hours of studying were not enough to prepare you for exams as you never knew what to expect.

Everyone exaggerates how much easier Rokas is. All of our midterm averages were low 70s. The content itself is easier to learn, but the tests are challenging. You should consistently put in effort, especially since most ppl want to drop a Johnson midterm. His office hours and worksheets are helpful. Textbook also has good practice problems, def buy

Good bio prof but nothing special. Preferred Johnson's lectures as they were more engaging bio Rokas wasn't bad. Ecology/evo is generally easier so you don't have to study as much. More mem/vocab and calculations-based but if you passed high school math you will be fine.

easier half of bio2, most ppl do better on his exams bc it's less material than johnson's half. honestly might not have to go to class, just review notes and do lots of practice problems before each exam. make sure you slack off tho bc his third exam low key caught me off guard and was my dropped exam
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Why is his rating so high? He does not answer questions, and purposely confuses people. Do not take this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is unfair. People in Desantis's class have it so much easier. Do yourself a favor and avoid Rokas
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just take Hillyer/Desantis. Johnson and Rokas are worse in all ways
Very difficult. Does not prepare us for exams
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture's were not always engaging, but Dr. Rokas is very knowledgable in his field and the information he presented was very interesting. Don't sleep on Dr. Rokas' section of BSCI 1511. It still requires many hours of study and prep. Do practice problems early, and keep up/get ahead of lectures. Overall, I'm happy he was my Bio prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are a bit monotone but easy to follow and well thought-out. Provides practice problems for math questions and posts his lecture videos + weekly review sessions. Tests are exactly what you expect, and it's clear he is knowledgeable about the subject.

Don't really need to read the textbook (at best just skim), everything is on the slides. Content is mostly comprehension-based and a good chunk was review of AP Bio (which is pretty rare for this class). Make sure to do the practice problems

Great pick for semester 2 Bio. His tests can be very difficult though and personally I found the content to be far less interesting than Johnson. His tests are very difficult and require thorough understanding/memorization of his slides. Do practice problems multiple times!

Professor Rokas has well-structured lectures and provides a lot of practice problems and worksheets, with recorded office hours to go over them. His exams are difficult, but practicing and asking questions really helps. I would definitely take again.

Rokas requires far less content, but I find that his material could be more interesting. As a professor, Rokas was extremely helpful and would post additional relevant resources to help students practice. His exams were pretty fair, but several questions require clarification, as the wording does not always convey what he intends.

Rokas is an excellent lecturer and is clearly passionate about teaching. There isn't much information for his sections and he gives practice problems. However, his exams are quite difficult and require a deep understanding of the material. Other than that, Rokas is a solid choice.

I think Rokas is a good professor and is always willing to help if you have questions after class. I would say his questions this year were much harder than 2021's test. He will ask you questions in a format he did not previously so you really do have to understand the concept quite well. DO all the worksheets and practice tests ahead of time.

I really liked Dr. Rokas. He made the material seem manageable and not too difficult. That being said, it was definitely not an easy class; the exams were challenging and you're only graded based on exam scores so it's tough to do well in the class. But I feel like Rokas actually cared about his students.
