Dr. Rokas is truly a great professor. His lectures are clear and his explanations are fantastic. His exams can be very tricky, however, in that he tries to test how well you actually know what is going on. Study very hard and do all the worksheets carefully and you'll be fine. At the end of the day, he is a super fair prof. Take him if you can!

He is a very sweet guy with lots of patience- he will explain things 100x over to get you to understand concepts if needed. Disregard the review below mine- that person is just upset over their performance and wants to take it out on Dr. Rokas. Focus on lectures, reinforce with the textbook and you'll be fine. Highly recommend.
Sweet guy who is a really good teacher. Straightforward tests

He's a really good lecturer, and his passion for the subject is evident in how excited he gets in talking about the material. Furthermore, his slides are all you need to succeed in class (don't waste money on the textbook). That being said, his tests sure can be a doozy so make sure to buckle down and study really hard for them.

He seems like a really nice guy and was definitely a better, more organized lecturer than Johnson. Still, the test questions were purposefully confusing and tested you more on if you're a good test taker than if you knew the material.

He's a really nice guy who will be very helpful if you ask him, but his tests are hard.  Tests mainly on material in lectures, but a few things from the reading. It's a hard class, but if you take notes on each lecture and skim the reading, you can do well. Or go to office hours, he really wants people to do well and will help if you ask for it.

Dr. Rokas is a kind and caring professor. The lectures are long and sometimes hard to pay attention to, but that has more to do with the subject matter than Dr. Rokas. Exams require a thorough understanding of the material, but it's easier to manage than intro bio.

Dr. Rokas is an extremely nice man and truly makes an effort to explain concepts so that non-biology majors can easily understand them. His lectures can be dull and his tests are harder than you'd expect, given the difficulty of the material (basic Mendelian genetics). If you have to take the class, Rokas is a good choice.

Took BSCI 272 (computational genomics). This class is very interesting and not too difficult. Less stuff to memorize than most other bio classes because some class days are taken up by practicals. I'm surprised that so few people take the class. Perhaps the name of the class is too intimidating.

I had Rokas for Evolution and really liked him. Very focused on the quantitative aspects of evolution, and not for the easily bored. I work in his lab now and he is incredibly supportive without being at all coddling. Really cares for his students and wants them to succeed. One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt!
One of the best bio professors! His lectures were pretty clear and tests did focus on the math but wasn't bad at all. Also helpful during office hours.

This was the first semester of Computational Genomics. Rokas was great!  Easy to understand and he really wants his students to do well.  He's always available outside of class (even outside of office hours) if you don't understand something and is actually working on cutting edge computational genomics, so we got to learn from a real-time expert!

Taught the first part of the class. He's into the math of evolution and his tests reflect this. Its not too hard though. He is from greece but I didn't have trouble understanding him. I thought this was an easy B and an A with some effort. Not bad for a bio class.
Not the greatest lecturer. Definitely clear about the material though. Attendance not required

I had the joy of having Rokas in his first semester teaching. I don't feel as if I learned anything from his class -- all he did was work math problems for 75 minutes. He would present things poorly (and sometimes even incorrectly) and would only correct himself when someone asked him about it. Avoid this class if possible.

Prof is so nice and easy to talk to! Super understanding and kind professor and one of the best in the MHS department. Lectures can get boring but she tries to get group discussion and group work going often. Really good for MHS electives

Dr. Behague was a fantastic professor. I had never taken an Anthropology class before and was worried about this class but she gave clear guidelines and feedback. Lots of reading, but the readings are interesting and we have great discussions in class. She is also such a nice genuine person, loved her and this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Behague is one of the best and most interesting lecturers I've ever had. Her content is complex, nuanced, and pushes normal conversations on a topic into much murkier territory. Her grading is very easy and the class includes4 a big "thesis" type project, an excellent opportunity to explore whatever you are interested in. HIGHLY recommend!
SHE IS AMAZING. Take her.

I loved Social Medicine with Professor B! The class was a little reading-heavy, but she lightened the load towards the end of the semester. Overall, I learned a lot in the class without ever feeling overwhelmed. Would recommend!! The class was really interesting too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's outstanding as a lecturer and leads discussions with utmost regard for your opinion -- she respects you and will work with you when you need her help. Admittedly she did say "you'll have to try to not get an A" lol. No textbook but a fair amount of outside reading (grows increasingly anthro-heavy). Take this class.

Pr. Behague was an amazing professor who really care about her students. She is open-minded and considers new perspectives on psychiatry and mental health. Much of the class war based on research and a group project. Pr. Behague helps you through the research process, and it really invested in your ideas and success.

Dr. Behague. What an amazing lady. This class was an easy A. I took her Spring 2018 and can't take her right now unfortunately because she's gone for the year due to research. I absolutely loved her and she's my fav MHS professor. She literally does not believe in As. I, however, would make sure you do the work well; don't do absolute sh!!t

Good class. Such a nice teacher. Wants you to do well. Her lectures can get boring. Group presentation was easy and she graded nicely. I'd recommend her, but get coffee before class so you pay attention. Highly values class participation.
Difficult class with all assignments due online.
Funny guy, hard module.

He gives clear criteria for the work in this class. Though, this work felt somewhat tedious compared to the other modules! I personally hoped for more personalized feedback on my project to get a better idea of what the major might be like.
He grades pretty well; aligns with his standards and I think he really just wants his students to do well. I wish I could take this class again!!
i love this guy like he's hilarious!!!! super awesomesauce and he's splendid when it comes to conversation!!!!
He was a GREAT PROFESSOR! If you follow the rubric and don't cheat you will do great! He doesn't make you feel stupid and is so caring! Great class!

I think people are overly harsh on Dr. Bellan. He's honestly a really chill guy and as long as you hand in your work on time to a reasonable effort and don't plagiarise anything (duh) you'll be fine. I went into this course expecting him to be really strict and a super tough grader but now I'm just confused as to where all these ratings came from.

This module was pretty difficult for me - on the brightside it single handedly showed me that ME here might not be a wise choice anymore. Bellan was SO uninterested in the class it worried me that the entire department might be like this as a whole. Overall this module was bleak, boring, and hard - I dont recommend.

Lectures are not very interesting and feel somewhat disjointed from what the final project is. Funny guy and is well qualified. Start instrument early. Directions on assignments can be somewhat confusing.

This module was not as interesting as the other mechanical modules and was far harder. It sounded so fun yet Bellan grades super tough and it kinda stymied how much I could learn about mechanical engineering. Overall I would take a different module if possible!

Leon was honestly funny, but the class was just not very fun :( Many people in other modules got to do some really cool things but Leon's just wasn't interesting despite the neat idea of the class. I'd recommend other modules to avoid boring dry lectures.

Lab reports had clear criteria that was met but they could be pretty hard. Class as stated by others was very dull but that's kinda the point of this class I suppose. Overall not ridiculously hard if your lab group is good but can be super difficult if lab members don't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was very boring and overall quite dry. Bellan had the driest jokes ever - similar to the material. The lab reports are graded hard but manageable.

I don't really know what to say. I found Instrumentation Lab to be very interesting, and I wish I had more time to learn what I was doing. But, labs are never worth the time you put into them (Even for this 2 credit hr. lab). Lab reports were difficult, and didn't learn anything. There was only one midterm (it was ok), and a final project (ok too).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Bellan is very passionate about mechanical engineering and its principles. The class consisted of 2-3 homework assignments that took around 2 hours each to complete. There was also a fun group project where students had to create a musical instrument out of ordinary household products and record a video of them playing.

I had Bellan for the mechanical engineering module. He's a cool person and is definitely knowledgeable in his field. The mechanical eng. mod itself was lowkey a lot of work, especially because we had to write a total of 9+ pages for the progress and final reports at the end. Overall, not a bad mod and he is a nice guy. Start your instrument early!

Don't take it if you are not an ME major. Class time is filled with boring and dry lectures and he did not give us any time to work on our project, which is assembling a LEGO car. He is extremely tough in terms of car performance, way harder than the other modules. If you are an ME major, good luck.

Lectures are pretty dry, and Bellan doesn't do a whole lot to make it terrible engaging. Took the course during COVID, assume in-person lectures are slightly more interesting. Overall not a bad professor, but not a whole lot to make you be dying to get to class. Lab reports are also an absolute pain to write.

Bellan is a smart and nice guy but should probably stick to research. Lectures were dry and boring, lab was disorganized and did not allow everyone to participate. Lab reports are hellish to write and had everyone groaning into the early hours of the morning the night before they're due. I wish you luck if you take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grades far too harshly for a module. Lectures are boring and difficult to understand. Final project was unenjoyable.

The nature of the class is kind of tedious, and the lectures are sometimes boring, but I still liked Bellan. Dry sense of humor, good natured guy. The weekly lab reports take a lot of time but he spells out exactly what he's expecting. TAs do the grading and you have lab with them so it depends on that as well
Probably the least helpful engineering module out of the ones I took, but it was still fun and I think his grading system was fair.

This was hands down my worst engineering module. There are tons of long papers, a weird final presentation that no other group did, and his lectures are useless. Furthermore, Bellan isnt understanding or accommodating. He wouldnt accept homework late even if you were out of state. AVOID him and this module overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Your grade is determined by a few quizzes based on lectures, couple homework assignments, and the biggest part is the toy car that you build with your randomly assigned partners. Not the most exciting module, but the lectures do cover the basic mechanical concepts which can be interesting if you're into that, and racing toy cars is kinda fun.

This module had the most work. We literally had something due every week. The whole class revolves around the performance of a car. There is also an exam and a presentation. This felt like more than a 1-hour credit class.

One of my favorite MechE courses so far. You get to make things and learn useful engineering things which is fun. Lectures are kinda boring but useful. You get to do really cool things in lab although the weekly lab reports suck. Gives a lot of freedom for final group project. Didnt curve down this semester which I know previously was an issue.

The class only meets once a week and it's just to prepare you for lab. He's a somewhat boring lecturer but he teaches you what you need to know. He's a super smart person with a lot of interests, and I think if you asked him about the things he's interested in he'd be great. He doesn't usually go to lab so that experience will depend on your TAs.

He was a dull lecturer with litten charisma. The classes are somewhat unclear, but assignments and labs are not too bad. He often carries an attitude of arrogance and thus is not very approachable. At the end of my semester, he even curved grades down against university policy and showed little appreciation of students' effort on projects.

The module was much more difficult than the others. The class was surprisingly difficult and had a sizeable amount of work. The homework assignments were graded harshly and no late credit was given for assignments. This class made learning the material slightly unenjoyable. Would not recommend even if you want to be a mechanical engineer.

For an engineering module, this class was unnecessarily hard and unforgiving. No credit is given for late homework assignments, which are graded with a great deal of scrutiny. Lectures are actually somewhat interesting. There are waaaay better modules, even in the area of Mech. E. Do not take this unless you really love lego cars.
Not the course to take if you're just taking it for AXLE credit. The work wasn't difficult, but for a 1000-level, it was structured odd and changed throughout

Professor Bai makes class engaging and easy to follow. She's understanding of student's stress and flexibility if you notify beforehand. Exams and class projects were fair and didn't overlap with other classes. We had some changes in class activity but it's understandable considering we had severe weather disaster.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bai is a very engaging professor who clearly cares about her students. She worked hard this semester to accommodate students taking her class who are not studying STEM. I made genuine friends in her class because she had us doing group work every lecture. Content can be tough but nobody was worried about their grade. Highly recommend to all!

I thought Bond was a great professor, though I found 1101 to be very challenging as it was my first experience with programming. Granted, I skipped the majority of classes so that was likely the main culprit of my lack of success. All the content on the exams are taught to you, and he posts all his lecture slides.

Good professor overall. Tries his best to be engaging. The homework can get mind-numbingly tedious/repetitive, but overall the course isn't too difficult, and the exams are relatively easy given that you make a good cheatsheet

Really nice professor. More lenient about homework and other things. Ok lecturer, but new so maybe will get better. Class is also super boring. Random in class questions in class to take attendance. If you could get these questions from someone you probably don't need lecture. Is more comprehensive about what will be on exams.
Very kind. Let's you turn in stuff late. Opens assignments back up for you.
Honestly just a great dude. Very kind and enthusiastic.
This guy is the absolute boy. He's really nice and genuinely cares about the students. 1101 with him is awesome and I would absolutely recommend.

Not a good lecturer - students would literally correct him during class. Would kinda just read off the slides without really explaining, and I often felt I was just better off skipping class and reading the textbook. Attendance mandatory for 70% of the classes, and the exams were all pretty easy.

His lectures move very fast, but his slides are detailed and he always posts them after the lecture. There are lots of TAs with office hours throughout the week. Programming assignments were sometimes long, but you pay attention in class/take good notes then they're not too difficult (especially if you have previous coding experience).

Nice professor, good guy, just lectures are hard to follow when hes tracing by pointing around at the lecture slides, wish he wrote it out more. Had a tendency to go over the lecture time. The course itself has a LOT of tedious and mind numbing homework, very repetitive especially the zyBooks.
very confusing lectures, projects sometimes unrelated to the lecture contents
project always unrelated to the lecture, very confusing explanation

Lectures are very clear and engaging, he makes a lot of jokes. He is very easy to find outside of class and very helpful answering questions/with assignments. He wants students to succeed in the class. Assignments are difficult and time consuming but lots of resources are available to help. Exams are very fair.

Very down-to-earth professor with engaging lectures. Easy to reach by email and available after class for questions. Slides are posted and helpful for exams.

Highly recommend going to class since practice problems in class usually appear in some way on exams.

He also uses Counter Strike as an example when teaching OOP so he's goated.

Was a great professor for Discrete Structures. If you show up to class and pay attention in lecture you will be fine. I felt comfortable asking questions, and he made very abstract concepts easy to learn.

Very chill and down to earth, light hearted and made funny jokes.

Maybe 1101 is a very different experience but I had a good experience in 2212
Can he even teach?
Would absolutely never take this class again- I have never been more confused by lecture slides in my life.

Professor Robinson is fantastic, and I learned so much from her. Her lectures are super interesting. She is a fair grader and makes her criteria for an A clear and achievable. I am typically an A student, but my A- was well deserved (if not generous). Take her class!! She is among the very best professors at Vanderbilt.

Robinson will expect you to learn an incredible amount about architecture, and doing so will be very timely. So, steer away if you just want an elective credit. However, if you are interested in the topic, she is a romantic about the buildings she teaches, and you will also fall in love with architecture!
If you're a HART major, then get prepared for the exams. If you're not, then run!

One of the best classes I took at Vanderbilt. Robinson could be intense in her excitement for the material but was animated and engaging and brought Ancient Rome to life in class. Not the easiest, but I learned so much. Definitely go to her office hours. Robinson rocks!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is easy A if you do the work and readings and show up. Unfortunately I was major league struggling this year and tbh the B- was way too merciful I'm still shocked I didn't fail lol. She is so compassionate I honestly have no idea why she put up with me, and the content is super interesting and worth studying fully, not just for a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Robinson is awesome. Her classes are nearly entirely lectures, but they are really engaging. This class is a ton of work with readings, reading responses, and papers, but she doesn't grade too harshly. This is very much a get out what you put in class, and with Dr. Robinson, it's a lot of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Robinson is clearly very knowledge and passionate about the subject she teaches. Unfortunately this can lead to confusion about exact material and disorganized study guides as she sometimes forgets her students are not experts in the subject like she is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Robinson is awesome. She's clearly really passionate about the subject and goes over a ton of content in class. Theres a midterm a book review a project and final so not a ton of grades but enough different ones where it's not too bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was a great class! Robinson's a riot and kept class entertaining. Challenging class, exams were heavy but fair as long as we prepared well--find a study group!

This is the worst class ever. she thinks its the only class we are all enrolled in i guess because she requires WAY too much of us. worst, most chaotic lessons. feel like i didnt learn anything. and the tests are extremely anxiety inducing and a total free for all

Prof Robinson is a good lecturer and the class is fairly interesting; however, the class was very disorganized and felt inconsistent as we would rarely finish material meant for class even after consistently lecturing 3-5 mins over. Despite these inconveniences, Robinson cares about the material, and succeeds in bringing the past to life.

Robinson assigns a lot of reading and if you miss a lecture, you'll be behind. She posts recordings tho so it's not awful to miss here and there. More work than my other classes, but genuinely interesting stuff. She's funny and was helpful when I had questions. Tests are HARD. Doable but difficult.

This isn't my first art history class (if you haven't taken one before and you think it's going to be a bunch of pretty pictures, you're kidding yourself) but it's my first with Dr. Robinson. While there's a lot to pack in, she is clearly enthusiastic about her topic and knows her stuff. Use the office hours and the study guides and you'll be fine!
The tests are crazy hard.

Genuinely one of the worst professors I've had the misfortune of having during my time at Vanderbilt. Lectures are absurdly dense but incredibly disorganized and lacking in any discernible structure. You never have any idea what content is actually going to be on the exams, its just a huge free-for-all. Do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really have never taken such a difficult art history class in my entire life. The amount of work required is insane. She is so smart so she assumes everyone knows what she is talking about... you should see the powerpoint slides. they are completely anxiety-inducing with tons of random facts and no main point. it is too much work and pressure

Prof Robinson is great!She's passionate and knows a lot about the area.The class is energizing.Take notes even if she posts all her ppts. Memorizing everything is the key.She's super helpful outside class.Take this class with her!You won't regret it.

She's nice, passionate and knowledgeable. Take this class w/ her. Really really interesting stuff. She puts ppt on OAK so notes aren't necessary just write down what she's says and what's not in the ppt. You can print the ppt out later. Memorizing is the key. Not an easy class but just amazing and fun.

Prof. Robinson is amazing. She is brilliant, sarcastic, and engaging. You have to attend every class, however, she post lectures on OAK at the end of each week. I highly recommend anything she teaches. Also, go to her office hours.

Really nice, really helpful, and a pretty interesting class.  She is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about the material being discussed.  Side note: a lot of reading outside of class but you can get by in class without it.  Additionally, we were not tested on any of the information discussed in class. We weren't even tested at all!

Class is intense.  If you pay attention in lecture and take notes, you will do fine.  Requires a lot of reading outside of class but if you don't do it at all, you'll survive. She's a good professor-loves to teach and has a lot of fun with the material in class. Expects a lot out of her students.

Robinson can be rough if you don't keep up with the class, not necessarily the reading but the class. She's a great professor who really loves her field and wants students to do well.  She will push you but its worth the work.  even though the reading is required, if you pay attention and take good notes, its not necessary at all.

Bogdanovic is a fantastic professor. I took her seminar Meaning and Form in Architecture, and it is one of my favorite classes at Vanderbilt! She cares deeply about the subject, the class, and especially her students. The class is discussion-based, and she encourages students to think deeply about the material and develop ideas independently.
Amazing professor! Tailors class to students' backgrounds, gives plenty of time for papers, no exams, super easy to access. 100000000% worth taking, HART major or not!

super smart prof- you will learn a lot if you put in the work. Lots of opportunities for extra credit. If you are willing to work, you can get an A even if the material does not come naturally to you. She is caring and passionate about teaching and wants to see you succeed.

I would recommend the BYZ Art course to anyone as Dr. Bogdanovic structures this class so that anyone can succeed with most grades coming from 2 essays you choose from. However, she absolutely knows what she is talking about and has high standards that could make higher level art classes with her difficult for non-majors.

Very sweet and exceedingly knowledgeable. There are two mandatory papers and a third optional, all of which are short and graded very leniently. She also offers 10-30 points of extra credit if you submit 1-3 short written assignments. Overall, great professor and easy, interesting class

Dr. Bogdanovic is solid, it's clear she has a deep passion for the subject she is teaching. If you ask her a question about Rome, she will go on a 10-minute insightful tangent. But, she and her TA were ruthless and harshly graded the 4 papers. Bogdanovic provided plenty of opportunities for extra credit, but they are time-consuming. An A is hard.
AVOID ANY CLASS WITH HIM SUPER UNFAIR!
Avoid at all cost!

Dr. Bollen is a great professor who truly cares about your learning. He gives you all of the resources to do well in the class (TAs who will tutor you, office hours, an AI tutor for the class, a printed book of all of the lecture slides & practice problems). Finance is a tough class but he makes it as accessible as possible. 100% recommend!

BUS 1300 was the single worst class I have taken at Vanderbilt. He is a graduate finance professor teaching undergraduates for the first time, and it was completely unfair. He taught like we were third-year master's students, moved insanely fast, gave practice exams that barely matched, and made exams feel unfair instead of educational.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not recommend.
Great Professor. Lectures are extremely boring if you don't enjoy the subject material. His exams are fair but homework can be frustrating at times.

Dr. Bai's lectures were decent, but there really is a need for you to go through the content by yourself outside of class to grasp the entirety of it. She is very willing to help, but most of the time you'll need to meet her with a very clear question to get an answer. The exams are challenging and require content that is not always covered
Very clear grading criteria and many chances to submit good work. Very in-depth lectures and very open to feedback and questions on the presentations. Very passionate about computer science.

Professor Bai is well organized, and her lectures are easy to understand since she always makes sure students understand the material before moving on. However, some TAs have inconsistent gradings, and the PAs could also be time-consuming moving forward.

Dr.Bai is genuinely one of the most caring and accessible professors out there. Her lectures are easy to understand and she's always open to questions or discussions. I'm happy to have chosen to take her again in another course!

I loved this class with Dr. Bai! She is very open to questions. She frequently pauses during lecture to make sure the class is understanding the content. This class does have quite a fair amount of PA's (Java), but they were all directly related to the concepts in class. She is one of the sweetest and caring professors you will ever take!

She teaches well and makes it understandable because CS topics are just hard but she makes it conceptually easier to understand. Its a hard class and its dependent on you and your work . The tests are hard but you just gotta study.

She explained concepts clearly and offered lots of opportunities to ask questions if confused. She also provided many sample review problems before every midterm which were really helpful. Overall a very sweet and helpful professor.

First time taking a CS class, and she made the concepts very clear and easy to understand. Tests are not weighted heavily in the class, and she offers many opportunities to ask questions in class. Easily accessible during office hours and responds to emails fast.

Took 2201 with professor Bai over prof. Roth because the latter professor had no seats left. I was pleasantly surprised by professor Bai's enthusiasm in teaching and she wanted to make sure every student understood the concepts taught in class by giving good analogies and explaining many times to certain people. Just make sure to attend classes.

Dr. Bai is an incredible professor and if you have the chance to take her, you definitely should. If you aren't interested in CS, the class would be pretty difficult. However, as a CS major, I found the class to be super enjoyable and it has made me excited to continue taking CS courses. Dr. Bai's lectures are the best I've ever seen, by far.
The lectures are useless. I do not recommend her section.
She is a terrible professor! The lectures are confusing and the exams are hard. Not recommended.
Good teacher, helpful in class examples.
Blessing! I love you Dr.Bai

Great teacher, taking her again for 2201. Very accessible outside of class and will help you with the homework if you are stuck. If you take advantage of office hours, read the textbook, and follow along actively and ask questions, CS1101 will not be challenging. Tests are very fair. Great teacher, 0 complaints!
so regretful not to drop

After seeing more of her classes, I've realized Dr. Bai isn't as great as I first thought. Her explanations can be confusing, and she tends to act a bit arrogant when students offer legitimate request. CS is hard, yes—but good teaching should make it clearer, not harder.

She is a very nice professor but she has a noticable accent. As a person who does not have any prior experience in coding, this class is getting insanely hard and I can't catch up. She cares about the student's outcome, not the process.

This is probably the most GENUINE comment you'll see. Some students rate Dr. Bai low, but it's not because of her-- it's because CS itself is hard. CS is skill-oriented: you can't just understand concepts, you must use them. Each program involves many skills, requiring practice and creativity. Dr.Bai teaching is clear and neat, and she is caring!
Overall, great lecturer!

Lots of content, but she makes it easy to understand, and lecture slides are very well done so you can easily go back to reread later or if you miss class. She makes a strong effort to get to know and help students, especially if you participate in class and/or talk to her outside of class. Assignments are challenging but doable and you learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, makes sure to adjust the pace so that everyone can understand the material. Assignments aren't a walk in the park, but absolutely doable, and between her and the TAs there's plenty of opportunity to get help if you're stuck. Prof. Bai is really caring and kind and genuinely is one of the biggest reasons I switched to majoring in CS.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bai is extremely nice and caring. One time I submitted a regrade request for half a point on an exam question and she went back and fixed another 5 points that had been graded wrong on other questions. Slides are beautiful but lecture style is mildly robotic. Exams are a big time crunch but most of class grade is weekly programming assignments.

Lectures are mid, you learn mostly through zybooks, but you really learn how to code from the projects. About 2-3 projects per week and zybook assignments with challenge questions. I developed a good understanding of CS from this class.

this class is hard for someone without any prior experience. Her programming assignments feel practically impossible towards the end. Dr. Bai is nice and smart, but I don't think she is a good teacher for beginners. If you have prior CS experience than this class would def be easier
If you didn't learn any coding before please avoid this class. The pace of lecture is hard to catch and the PA is hard to reach outside classroom. OH didn't help much either

Dr. Bai is an amazing instructor. The class itself is pretty tough, but her lectures are clear, organized, and easy to follow. You can tell she really cares about her students, which makes it so much easier to ask questions. She is always willing to spend hours helping you outside of class. Definitely would recommend!

Gina Bai is truly kind and caring to her students. She does have a bit of an accent, which takes a little while to get used to, but she is significantly more personable to students compared to other CS professors. She is willing to slow down the lectures just to make sure everyone understands and presents info clearly and concisely.
Caring and always open to receiving questions. Just pay attention in lecture, do the homework, and make good use of office hours.

She is a pretty good lecturer and gives great advice about career and academic things. Guaranteed A if you just go to her office hours since she'll literally stay extra to help you debug your code. Overall a very caring professor and definitely one of the best in the department. Don't let the other reviews here fool you.

I took this class with no programming experience. Class was difficult but fair. Lectures got boring but were never a waste of time. I loved Dr. Bai, she let us out early, extended deadlines at the end of semester, gave warnings about test/PA difficulty. People who say they don't like her/the class just didn't work hard enough or weren't good at it.

I came into the class without much CS background, but everything was pretty much straightforward as long as you came to class. I don't think it was terribly hard, but the PAs did increase in difficulty at the very end.

The class was more challenging than expected but as long as you attend lectures and do all of the assignments you should be fine. PAs towards the end of the semester took a long time but they will help you in the long run when it comes to writing code on exams. Dr. Bai is a nice professor.

I don't know why people are leaving harsh ratings - I thought Dr. Bai was excellent. I had 0 coding experience before 1101 and found it to be quite easy thanks to her lectures. If you find it tough, do the Zybook before class so that lecture is your second time seeing the material. I had a disagreement about TA feedback on the PA, and she helped.

Atrocious professor. She is an extremely poor lecturer, is not friendly/nice whatsoever, and gives off vibes that you're worthless. Class is "hard" mostly because of the stupid PAs and the amount of content. Definitely doable, but if you have the opportunity to take with literally any other professor, do it.
I do no want to say too much about this teacher, terrible experience, RUN! The difficulty of the class will increase straight after midterm 2!  And she doesn't sound fluent.
very hard class go take someone else
She is awful! Avoid! Go take python!
Must pay attention heavily in class to do well otherwise will struggle in PAs and she places honor codes on PAs very easily
BAD attitude, she don't even know what she's talking about, homework heavy, would never take it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you have not coded before, don't take the class. PAs are awful, but office hours with the TAs are really helpful. Also, definitely do not start the PAs day of or day before if you have not coded before. This is the most honor coded class on campus btw and you find out at the end of the class. She also hates her students. Have fun with Gina.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class would definitely be hard with no coding experience, but not impossible. I left with a great understanding of coding and Java. Her lectures are fine, not boring and lots of content. She's very easy to understand. You're graded on a lot of things and it's a great class to see if you like coding.

Professor Bai is just fine. Her lectures are kinda dry and most of the time nobody was paying attention. The PA's can be a lot of work, especially if you have never coded before. However, there are so many TA office hours available. Lock in on the PA's because they count for almost 50% of your grade. Tests are fine, study slide examples.
not willing to have a normal human interaction with her students. wants you to fail and you will, she is out for anyone. terrible experience for a class that gave me no credit towards anything.
Horrendous teacher, 100% the worst I've ever had. Bad lecturer, doesn't care about her students, and wants you to fail. Avoid her at all costs

CS1101 itself is a difficult, work heavy class if you know nothing about Java. Dr. Bai makes it much easier than others though. Her office hours are accessible, and she really does help you 1-on-1. Her lectures are great. The only downside is that you have to be in class for TopHat questions that track your attendance, but they aren't weighed heavy

Prof. Bai did a good job teaching and responded quick to mails and Piazza. However, read of slides a lot so I started skipping lectures lol. However, if you truly understand the zybooks, PA's, and go over her slides to review before the test, should be an easy A. Totally fine if you have never coded before, just dont skip lectures!

Prof. Bai is by far the best professor I have had at Vandy. She cares so much for her students and she makes it so easy to get help. She stayed after office hours to help me on my code and encouraged me to stick with CS after doing bad on an exam. Even after taking her for 1101 and 2201, she still catches up and says hi to me whenever I see her.

Gina Bai is a good professor that actually tries. However, a lot of the assignments were either too easy or too hard. The tests weren't that bad, but the homework grading was definitely a little bit off. They grade heavily on style and I lost tons of points of projects that worked functionally well. Outside of that, I'd say she's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor taught everything clearly, and she constantly review materials covered before. I don't why so many people don't like her. I think many people underestimate the course 1101 and CS majors. This is course and major requires diligent. If you want to get A and you are a truly beginner, you must put 10 hours in this course every week.

Had Dr. Bai for both CS1101 and CS2201 (no option to put 2201). She really cares about her students. She once stayed an hour past the time her office hours ended just to help me with my code. These classes can be really hard but she's always willing to help. Read the guidance/spec ENTIRELY for PAs, those small missed details can add up

Can be stressful for ppl with absolutely no prior experience in cs (like me). The lectures are too fast-paced, probably because most ppl come into this class with some experience. Everything ties together by the end of the course, but can seem very confusing and random in the beginning. Definitely go to TA office hours if you struggle with PAs.
Average
super chill teach, never had any problems, could breeze by without attending class but she uses tophat, lectures were never difficult to understand
Gina bai is honestly a very caring professor who will go out of her way to help students. Lectures are very organized. Just make sure to do the zybooks and this is literally an easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very kind and accessible outside of class. Easy to understand lectures. I definitely would recommend her for CS1101.

Dr. Bai is super accessible out of class and always stays behind if you need help after. Lectures can get a little dry, but she often tells you exactly what to know for exams. The exams are the same throughout classes, but they're ok if you do the in-class practice. Sometimes she springs TopHat(attendance questions) on us, so show up if you can.
Go to her office hours, she is very nice and will remember you.

Professor Bai is very passionate about delivering the best introduction to computer science to both students majoring in computer science and not! I thoroughly enjoyed her class and thoughtful assignments. She is also very responsive outside of class despite the large volume of students. Definitely would take again.
Lectures were dull basically just read from her slides, homework took a decent amount of time but if you start the PAs early and do the zybooks is very manageable.

Lectures cover basic material, but are really not necessary.  The weekly hw takes HOURS.  Since working with others is prohibited, make sure to go to TA office hours.  These will get crowded, meaning that you often will wait up to 7 hours to not receive any help.  The class is poorly structured and needs a better way for students to receive help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loveeee Dr. Bai. Take her over Tiaras! If you are new to cs take her, she will help you before and after class, she will schedule meetings with you and go over her office hour time to help you. Plus her fashion is elite, and she is really nice. PAs suck but she is not the one that creates them, so you cannot blame her for them being hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is okay, the PA's just suck. Definitely would recommend her over the other professors, slides and examples were helpful. Just be prepared to spend hours on the PAs, but they're the same across all sections. Overall, CS is just very time consuming with the workload, but Gina is good.

Pros:
- Caring
- Possible to do well without going to class

Cons:
- Underwhelming lectures; I never understood the content until I did the homework.
- Overly complicated formats, such as length requirements and handwriting code.
- Up to 7 hours of HW/week

Survival tip:
- Focus your energy on PAs rather than lectures, and review heavily for tests.

Collaboration isn't allowed in any 1101 class, not just hers, so beware of that. Lectures were fairly dry and sometimes confusing, but you can just read zyBooks and learn the material anyway so it doesn't matter all that much. Last few PAs can get kind of hard. Midterms weren't terrible.

Any kinds of collaborations are not allowed on projects, and they tend to get very difficult toward the end of the semester. Would recommend Tairas over Bai if you are learning Java for the first time.
Take Tairas if you can

Probably a decent person, but a very dry lecturer who is sometimes not clear. I learnt most of the content by doing weekly Zybooks activities. Weekly programming assignments tended to be quite difficult towards the end of the semester, and it was very difficult to seek help from TAs and the professor at office hour due to very long waitlist.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Bai. Her lectures aren't always easy to follow, especially if you have no prior knowledge in coding.But if you read and understand Zybooks (the online textbook) this class is an easy A.

Dr. Bai made this class very manageable with clear expectations even though I had no CS experience. Lectures were confusing in the moment; the accompanying zyBook activities were far more helpful along with the programming assignments (although time consuming). Dr. Bai is highly accessible outside class and it's clear she cares for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For someone with no prior CS experience, I often left her lectures feeling super confused. But the weekly ZyBook homework made the content much easier to understand. Gina puts in the time to help students outside of class and she responds quickly to emails. She's also occasionally funny and you can tell she's a sweet and caring person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bai is very caring and conveys what she needs to, but there was nothing special about her lectures. She was a little hard to understand, and I mostly learned from programming assignments. You could never go to class and be totally fine. I really do like her as a person though, and the class is fine in general with or without her.

Although I only had Dr. Bai as a substitute for a month this past year, she was a good professor in my opinion. One time I was really struggling with my programming assignment and she stayed late and helped me work through it. I wasn't even her student at the time and she went the extra mile for me. Very nice professor, you'll do fine in her class.

Gina is such a queen. Everyone in my class loved her. This is definitely a hard class for people who haven't taken CS before, but she makes it so much more fun and easy. I've heard Dr. Tairas is a horrible and mean teacher, so def take Gina.

If you have to take CS 1101 at Vandy, take it with Bai. She makes even complicated topics very easy to understand, and her lectures are way more engaging than Tairas. Her office hours are genuinely helpful and she will take time out to explain the logic of the assignments if you need it. I would say definitely take notes during her lectures.

Professor Bai is a pretty good lecturer. Sometimes she is a little dry, but she explains things well and is good and answering questions/ clearing confusion. She is also super easy to reach for extra help. The work itself is pretty easy. Also, the exam questions are almost exactly the same as practice exams she gives on her Brightspace.
Gina isn't the greatest lecturer because she mostly reads off slides. CS1101 is fairly easy though, if you do zyBooks consistently you'll do fine.

This professor was hard and will always be hard. Not just in classes, but outside too. He helped me improve my grades privately in one on one office hours which I actually really appreciate, but lets just say that his office hours were hard to take. I also don't think he's had any real experience except what he calls "starting nine-month builds".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a funny professor. One class he started by saying that he really likes to play Grand Theft Auto Online and stealing cars and such and then immediately began lecturing about budgeting a construction project.

Sometimes he didn't even show up to office hours and would email later saying that he forgot he was holding them and to email him your questions. I've never had a professor this disorganized but it made me feel like I was wasting my time even asking him to help me.

I didn't like Dr. P. He was extremely disorganized and would cancel class randomly. He was often really tired and didn't want to teach at all but at least he graded our exams and papers easily. I wouldn't recommend this section.

Sometimes I wish Professor Paez were my DAD. I love this man. I mean, who else do you know that teaches difficult topics to a special education class? These comments on RMP are all from my special education classmates who are upset because they can't handle difficult topics. Anyway, if you are a student looking for a fun and easy class, take this.

I can't believe this is a real professor. He doesn't care at all about anything he's teaching and frequently goes off topic. I failed his class even though I went to all office hours and did great on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such is life.
I was having a medical emergency with a severe asthma attack and Dr. Paez told me too bad so sad you can't make up the final exam boo hoo

Lectures were terrible. But you need to do the TopHat in class for a grade, so go. Homework was so long every week, but it was free points at least. Tests were open book but extremely hard. You need to practice on your own but the online test makes things better. Do HW and you'll do good.
I changed majors because of this class. Don't take it with Dr. P

Very professional, excellent professor. I thought he was amazing all throughout the year but on the final he gave me a 0 even though I had taken the exam. He said he didn't see my exam with the others (he lost it).
RUN!!!! DO NOT TAKE
Dr. Paez emails people that don't show up to his classes and makes it very clear that attendance is strict. Don't take.

Even though this class was very easy for someone like me, Dr. P is politically biased and sometimes blurts out things that I don't think are appropriate. He feels strongly about immigration and even said he wished to "work on building the wall". I don't understand any of this because he seems to be of south American origin.
Rambles about his personal life instead of the material on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Paez is surprisingly clear even though he has a bit of an accent. Nonetheless, he wastes class telling us stories about his days in construction and his previous marriages. Didn't offer any help outside of class. You're better off switching majors.

Professor Paez is the greatest teacher to ever do it. Batman would betray Superman to be taught by Paez, and Goku would betray Frieza for a strand of Paez's hair. "If a hole in a boat leaks in water, the best solution is to drill a second hole into the boat so the water can enter through the first hole and exit through the second."

Even though some people think he's a hard grader and has difficult exams, Professor Paez is very caring. You can really see that side of him if you attend his office hours. Usually, they were empty and it was just me and him, but he was greatly interested in my life outside school and really cared how I felt. Nonetheless, the class is very hard.

He has years of experience in construction management so he is very knowledgeable about the work out in the field. However, he is very strict with attendance and will mark you absent even if you are minutes late. There is TopHat every class so come prepared! He keeps talking about his marriage issues and otherwise doesn't seem to care about you.

Required attendance. Professor P used to work in construction and was hired directly from the field which gives him a unique perspective on the work related to construction management. He's a fun guy that jokes about his numerous divorces but his lecture slides are really unclear and written in Times New Roman which is kinda weird. Grades very hard
Too much material to get through in a semester but crams it through anyways. More interested in getting through everything than actually teaching

Dr. Paschal is retiring; however, BME 2302 was an awesome class! Focuses on a majority of systems in just a semester so be ready to read. There are in-class exercises while you learn outside of class. Grading is what I would imagine medical school to be like, but it is easy to succeed in this class with appropriate effort.
Too much information. Not enough time. Felt rushed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She just read off the slide. No explanations, no teaching, just reading off lines and lines of a powerpoint slide.
Too much memorization and dry lectures that are just reading off a PowerPoint slide
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Now that I have taken more advanced BME classes and the MCAT, I finally understand what a good prof Dr. P. is.  She distilled the key physiology info, taught me to use engineering concepts to understand and retain it, and connected the phys to eng solutions.  I just didn't appreciate at the time and was pissed off about the B I got.

Course covers a lot of material and there is more reading than some other eng classes.  However, Dr. P. makes really clear slides summarizing the important stuff and posts those online so you can take notes on them. Test questions come from or are similar to in class examples, homework, or old exams that she posts.  I learned a lot. Worth it.

There is a LOT of material and class feels like drinking from a firehose at times.

She is really kind, and really does want students to succeed. 

Very available for office hours and office hours are really good.

She doesn't teach a lot of classes (shown by the ratings) because she is an Associate Dean in the Engineering School.

Classes are based off of PowerPoint slides that accompany the book. She typically goes through 20-40 slides per lecture which is ALOT of material. Lectures are just her reading off the slide. Very boring and dry class that is harshly graded

She's a very pleasant lady whose teaching just didn't work for me. Most of her lectures were reading directly from the slides which were verbatim from the book. I really wanted to like this class but she somehow made these interesting topics really dull.

Like many others say, she tries to cram too much info into one semester. The content is good and I enjoyed her as a person, but her lectures moved too fast. I would get behind almost every day and have to catch up after class ended. Her office hours were great and she really wants to help you if you ask!
Difficult professor who tries to cover too much material in a semester
Tough because of all the homework she assigns. Classic is heavily memorization based
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Difficult professor because of the amount of work she assigns. Homework is definitely not easy and takes quite a while to finish. Her exams draw almost entirely from her lecture slides so make sure to memorize them completely. She likes to test on the smallest details on her slides

Tests are extremely hard due to the amount of material covered. Weekly reading quizzes over a chapters of information and homework takes a very long time to finish. Unfortunately this class is more of a memorization biology course opposed to a practical engineering course.

One of the best professors in the department/at Vanderbilt. Covers what feels like a lot of information but explains it all in a very clear/logical manner, and does a good job of making the material relevant/applicable. Tests are not easy but are doable with studying. Would definitely take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There is a ton of material that she tries to cover and the exams are extremely difficult because of it

Bad lecturer because she only reads off the slides. Hard tests plus reading quizzes and hw are a waste of time. She purposely makes her homework takes 9 hrs a week because 3 credit hours  9 hrs of work outside the classroom. Ridiculous logic but she swears by it. Take the class with a better + logical prof who doesnt read off ppt slides
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult class because of the amount of material she tries to cover
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: all you do is memorize biology facts. doesn't seem like much of an engineering class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures are really helpful for the tests and are pretty much all you need. Homework is extremely difficult and not helpful at all but that is the same no matter what prof you take. She is definitely the more helpful lecturer and she really cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think its interesting how the 5 star reviews claim that Dr. Paschal is "enthusiastic" and "has energy", but none praise her teaching ability. This is because although she does seem to care about her students and is excited about the material, her teaching ability is not up to par. You will be stuck teaching yourself the entire semester
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. P is easily the most enthusiastic and caring professors I have ever had. While the material is undeniably difficult, she clearly cares deeply about her students and her energy is contagious. She makes herself accessible outside of class and will bend over backward if you are willing to make an effort in her class. I highly recommend Dr. P.
Not a good lecturer and tests are extremely hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: shes doesnt teach in class. rather she reads off the powerpoint slides to you so its up to you to learn outside of class. and its a lot of information to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Makes her students buy a $110 e-book whichforces them to memorize concepts that she rarely tests as everything important is on her lecture slides. Sure she is enthusiastic but all she does is read off of a powerpoint. Imagine an enthusiastic Siri that reads random facts to you really quickly. That is basically class in a nutshell. Take another prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Likes to assign hw over breaks
Tests arent too terrible. Just alot of info but all you need to do is memorize her slides. Weekly homework takes a long time though..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: assigns way too much work. she makes the class more of a biology/memorization based class rather than an engineering class so youre stuck memorizing hundreds of ppt slides for each exam. she makes the exams ridiculously difficult because she tries to cover 5-6 chapters of material in each one. highest exam score for the first test was an 83/100
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Do NOT take Sys Phys 1 with her. She requires you to memorize every concept on her lecture slides. Exams are worth 25% each and cover at least 300-400 slides of information. She specifically designed the class so that you HAVE to spend at least 6 hours a week on homework alone. Wait to take it with a more reasonable professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her voice is enthusiastic when she's lecturing, which makes her easy to pay attention to. Extremely helpful in office hours. Great at explaining things and giving examples to help you understand. Tests are tough because a lot of material is covered.

I also had her for 251, and she's a really good professor. She has a lot of energy and tries to make class interesting. There are a couple of easy homeworks and a semester group project. Exams are open book/open note and not too bad if you go to class and pay attention.

A great lecturer!  Makes real effort to make things interesting and bring in energy  and she succeeds. Very helpful. Great prof! Her tests: she often wants a certain detail and you'll feel like you're being tested on mind reading.  To ensure an A know every detail about everything.  Going over lecture notes helps. Read the text. You'll learn a lot.

Great professor in lecture, but sometimes she seems annoyed by questions, especially if it is something she has already said, which is understandable. Also, she seems condescending when "stupid questions" are asked or when she is challenged of being wrong or not knowing something. Most people would disagree with this review, I still recommend her.
Ok I dont know who said Dr. P was easy, but she isn't!  She's a wonderful, terriffic, great professor who teaches very well and is extremely interesting and you learn a lot, but she sure isn't easy!
very helpful in office hours -- also her tests are not hard and very straightforward. open book open note tests!!!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
great teacher, can be a hard class

Dr. Creutz is single-handedly one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. He fully understands what it means to be a student and absolutely accommodates any challenges you might face. He is super easy to reach outside of class time and will genuinely take the time to look at your questions (regardless of how silly they might seem). Great Prof!
Such a nice person

Really nice, knows the material really well and is great at explaining the concepts. I found the worksheets in class to be very useful. Lectures for 15-25 minutes and then goes around answering questions about worksheet. Is kind of a yapper but imo that only shows that he's concerned with students actually understanding the material

Understands what it is like to be a student and does not make the class unnecessarily difficult. He is very caring and likes to check in often to ensure classwork is going well. Best prof I have had so far.

Dr. Creutz is simply the math department GOAT at Vanderbilt. He will give incredible support during the classroom if you are struggling (and if you are not). He will make sure to hold enough Office hours for everyone in the class to be able to attend and ask questions if need be it. He genuinely goes out of his way to improve your math experience

he is so nice so good and teaches so well and cares about you and wants you to do good. like he gives in class paper notes like it makes me actually learn in class instead of doing everything on my own and making going to lectures not useless.
Makes the material very easy to understand and gives out a bunch of handouts to study. Actually the goat

I found that his lectures were too slow and didn't fully cover the content, and he yapped too much in response to questions. His posted solutions to review problems often contained errors which was really annoying. However, he definitely cares a lot about his students and offered a lot of office hours. Overall, not a bad prof, but a bit overrated.

Creutz is the best. I got an A in his class, and it wasn't a struggle after BC in hs with an absolutely heinous teacher. He explained everything much better. He cares about us. He clearly lays out what is expected of you on the exams. He teaches for about 15-20 mins, then lets you work through problems with your table as he walks around to help.
Creutz may just be the greatest of all time.

Bro. Best lecture style, best study materials, incredibly caring towards his students. He is so lenient on his grading, with very straight forward tests, which honestly made me want to try my best, as opposed to a prof who would purposefully run their students into the ground. I love you prof Creutz.
Great Math Prof. Majority of class is spent working on problems where he comes around and answers individual questions. He is great at explaining concepts both in his lectures and office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is so nice and actually cares about you as a student and knows u have outside stuff going on as well. He is very supportive too and will answer your questions really clearly and makes the lectures really engaging too with the in class packets . He tries really hard to make the class easy for us and for us to actually understand the content .

Explains basic concepts daily and then has us learn the rest through practice problem worksheets. Make sure you finish them though b/c the packet goes more in depth than he does. Sooo flexible with homework due-dates and making time outside of class to go over material. He tries to be funny every class with frequent bits and jokes. Very chill class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take Creutz. He wants his students to do well and makes class as enjoyable as it can be. You will do well if you ask questions and do the work. He is great, everyone loves him.

This guy is literally the goat. I had him for 1300 and 1301 and he always keeps it real. He knows the math department is silly so he does whatever he can to make the course as easy as he can within the department's restrictions. He kind, understanding, and explains things very well. Wish I could take him for every math class.
Creutz was great. He lectures for like 15 mins and then has you work through guided notes with groups while he goes around and helps. Tests were straightforward and his explanations are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Creutz is amazing, genuinely enjoyed taking his course. Explains the material really well and does not overcomplicate things. Also cares about his students and their success!

I have never learnt Calculus better than in Dr Creutz's class. His lectures are informative and he always is willing to take questions. Only con is that the final was hard and heavily weighted, but take Dr Creutz for your best shot!!

Creutz is the best professor I had this semester! You can tell that he knows what he's talking about and can help students understand the material well. I regret not attending his office hours more and taking the time to ask questions on topics I didn't understand (probably why I got a B+). If you struggle with understanding, Creutz is your guy.

I really like him he is so understanding, funny, and cares about his students. Probably my favorite professor. It was his first semester here and his classes got filled up so fast(waitlist too) for next semester because all the other students want him too.

Mr.Creutz is perhaps the best teacher I have ever had the pleasure of being taught by. He is extremely organized, has amazing lectures, and cares very much about the quality of education his students receive. If Creutz taught a tap dancing class to a school of fish, they would grow feet and become the best tap dancers in the world.

He changed Math 1300 for the better. Truly cares about students and their comprehension, amazing at explaining things without being too lecture-heavy. About 15 minutes of lecture per class, then distributed worksheets and could ask him questions in class. Very clear expectations and made a scary class very digestible. Highly recommend!

Calculus had always been challenging for me in high school, this was not the case in Creutz's class. He explained material simply and logically with very little lecture (about 15 minutes per class.) Majority of classtime was in-class work sheets where we were free to ask him questions. Very friendly guy and excellent teacher who truly cares. Take!!

Hard class but Creutz is definitely the best professor to take it with! Tests are tough (especially the last few questions on them), but manageable. Go to TA office hours/discussion for help and you'll be fine. Homework is mandatory, but helpful in boosting your grade! Creutz is great, and while calc is hard, you won't regret taking it with him.

Incredibly clear teaching, nice guy. This class is way too easy (you skip over any real math or formulas) and he knows it, but if you're looking for an easy A it's for you. It's actually difficult to get lower than a B. Dim room, boring subject, and early class time make it pretty easy to fall asleep, but that's not Creutz's fault
Homework is mandatory. Attendance is not.
Awesome Prof, go to office hours and do the homework and you'll be fine. Got A's on all the tests.
He is extremely clear and informative with his lectures, and a likeable guy. A very useful class, especially if you are a physics or engineering major.
sweet prof, really cool guy, incredibly laid back and understanding, makes hard concepts easy to understand
Very nice guy. One of the most sympathetic profs anyone will ever have. Tests were very fair as well as the homework and quizzes in recitation. Highly recommended.
Took him last semester. It was his first year here, but he still did a great job. Good teacher, tests aren't too difficult.
This is his first semester here. He takes weekly homework grades (half for completion). Gives a formula sheet on tests. Reasonable with regrade requests. No reason not to take him
Super nice, makes class easy just do the hw and its fine

I love professor Palacios! So incredibly sweet and caring. She is very knowledgable and wants to make sure everyone is actually learning. She proposed the idea of making 1102 a travel embedded class where we got the opportunity to visit Spain over spring break. Would definitely recommend taking her for any spanish class.

Very solid professor; really nice and brings a positive energy to class every day. Really easy to get a good grade in this course as long as you show up to class and do the tri-weekly online homework (tedious, and sometimes long, but not difficult).

professor palacios was one of the sweetest professors i had this semester! she truly cares about helping her students learn. beware that there is a lot of textbook reading and homework, but you get multiple attempts. this class is pretty participation and group project heavy so get to know your classmates. would recommend to new spanish speakers!

Prof. Palacios is the best if you actually want to learn Spanish. Her classes are very fun and engaging. There is quite a lot of homework, group projects, and one composition, but if you put the effort in getting an A is very easy. Attendance is mandatory and your grade will be dropped if you miss lots of classes (that goes for any language class).

Great professor, teaches concepts well. Only downside is participation is required, can only have three absences before points are taken off. Though at least she makes it required for sake of having us have more experience listening, processing, and responding to Spanish; she spends class time well.

A lot of busy work but that's to be expected for an intro language class. If you do the assignments and keep up with the class you will easily get an A. Very kind professor, really cares about your learning.

Dr. Palacios is literally the best Spanish teacher I have had. I dont know what the negative reviews are talking about. If u show up and do the work, easy A. If you want to learn Spanish, she will do her best to teach you. A lot of people get discouraged at Spanish which is why some people write negative reviews. No fault of Dr. Palacios. Take her
I dont feel her feedback is helpful. If you want to actually learn Spanish dont take it. If you want to just learn the conjugations/grammar and definitions she is for you
Doesnt care for her students well being...a lot of energy that I feel is misplaced. Not putting energy in right things
Profesora Palacios is one of the best and most caring professors at Vanderbilt. She brings a vibrant energy to every lecture and you can tell she wants her students to do well. Highly recommend!
Amazing professor! take her class. Easy A and not a huge workload. She is very sweet and funny!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Palacios wants you to do well! She's very clear on what she expects from you. While there is homework every night, you get 3 attempts so you can get a 100! All the effort you put into the class she'll reciprocate. Study for exams and participate, and it's an easy A!

She is a very sweet and funny professor who wants you to succeed. She is animated and speaks slowly when talking in Spanish to make sure you understand her. Class was an easy A and she is always willing to help. Would definitely recommend her.

Professor Palacios was a great Spanish Professor. She goes slowly and makes the class fun. The nature of the subject is repetitive but she has days where she switches things up again. Doing the work and simply keeping up with all of it will guarantee an A. I would take her again in a heartbeat.

Professor Palacios talks really slowly compared to other spanish professors, and it's one of the foremost reasons to take her class. She genuinely wants everyone to understand. She's not an overly generous grader, but she's fair. Work moderately hard and you'll come out with at least an A-

She is a good teacher, although a lot of times it feels like she is babying you as you learn the material. If you can get passed that, she is a very easy teacher and will guide you through the material very well.

I found her to be one of the most frustrating professors I have had at Vanderbilt. If you don't automatically understand things she can be rude and will certainly call out students if she feels they haven't learned something. I took her class because I wanted to learn spanish but it could not have been more unenjoyable.
Thoroughly enjoyed having this professor. She is a very nice woman, but she does expect you to do your work, as she should. I wish she was teaching 102 next semester so I could take her again.

I took her for Spanish 101 and 102.  She's extremely nice and fair.  If you keep up with the assignments and reading, it's not hard to do well in the class.  My only problem was that she didn't spend as much time as I would have liked on the grammar.  It was a very culture-focused class, but I think that's the department's doing, not hers. Recommen

I always found her to be nice and helpful.  Her first language isn't English, but she could answer all the questions about basic Spanish.  Her grading was always very fair and I'd recommend her to all my friends.  Just read the book and you'll get an A.

She is so nice.While she does speak primarily in Spanish, it is slow and clear, and it's part of learning.Simply hearing it every day and trying to understand and respond helps your listening comprehension A TON.She is quick to repeat if necessary and wants to make sure you learn.Participate & do your work, and have fun.No easy A, but very fair.

one of few teachers at vandy that i just couldn't [under]stand. every other class she went from being nice to just being a **** (and never any middle ground). the comment about just taking off points with no explaination couldn't be more true - WAY TOO SUBJECTIVE

She is a lenient Spanish teacher compared to most of the others. She tries to make sure that everyone knows what is going on and expected of them. This is a beginner's Spanish class and w/ a little effort it is not hard to make an A.

Poor teacher. Extremely hard to understand, constantly changes syllabus online often causing confusion. She doesn't understand more complicated English and is always right. Grading is very tough and class drags on. Not much actual teaching goes on, she just merely checks the previous night's homework. Steer clear if possible.

Has a poor grasp of English, which makes teaching "Spanish for True Beginners" a little difficult-she often doesn't understand English questions about Spanish grammar. Doesn't really explain why she took points off unless you ask her during her scarce office hours. You're stuck with her first impression of you. Seems nice at first, then she sucks.

Incredible professor with decades of teaching experience. Yes, there are plenty of assignments, but Lori's great feedback and teaching environment make all your work feel rewarded. Grading is more than reasonable. Very encouraging and kind.

The professor graded unreasonably unfairly for the trip responsibility grade, which was not established as its own grade until after the trip. This negatively affected many students in the class. The professor is a demanding and often cares about her students, but if she perceives you lack respect (even when she is wrong) she will punish you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Travel-embedded. Readings and discussion posts for all class meetings. Be prepared to have a 50-minute presentation in this course on a topic that you select at the beginning of the semester. Advanced Spanish skills are a must. Non-native Speakers may struggle in this course, and might not feel welcome. Tests (4) are difficult.

Lori is a great professor that cares about the wellbeing of her students. This is the best professor to teach 2000+ words of medical spanish to students. She is hard on students, but in a loving way, especially because she knows our ability to speak impacts the health of others. Easy grader and lots of homework. basically felt like med school, lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor in the Spanish department. Encouraging and really cares about your learning, especially speaking and will work with you outside class even on a call to help you practice, give ideas  or answer questions. Knowledgeable and super organized.

Learned so much vocab and business terms in Spanish. The class has a lot of assignments and grades which gives you a chance to improve and nothing counts for so much. the professor is very helpful and available. Creates a fun environment and loves participation.  my speaking got better in Spanish and presenting a few times  was a positive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class
