reviews.comment:
she was doing too much, most of the “learning” is dependent on you googling concepts and her just regurgitating that info

long vocab lists to memorize and manyyyy presentations w/ strict rubrics and spur of the moment guidelines 

she'd make inappropriate comments abt students personal lives and sexist

I've already taken two classes with Lori, and she's one of the best professors Vanderbilt has. She genuinely cares about all her students, and you learn so much in her classes. If you're thinking about taking her class, or if you already registered, just do your best and go in with a positive attitude. You won't regret it.
Fair amount of work but learned a lot. Great profe.

Lori is one of the most inspiring professors I have ever had. She truly cares about her students succeeding and is so encouraging. This course combines service in local clinics with a deep study of illnesses impacting the Latino population, along with a very strong foundation of medical vocabulary. She is very knowledgeable, but fun and funny.

Passionate prof, but her classes are SO work-heavy. My Spanish homework took up more of my time than my other 15 credit hours combined... expect nightly readings, vocab studying, and presentation preparations ON TOP OF spur-of-the-moment mini-assignments not on the syllabus. Learned a lot and easy grader, but sacrificed way too much time/effort.

Great professor that is super passionate in your learning, which means it can feel a little intense. Workload is alot but you chose your presentation dates for the 3 projects, so its up to you to manage your projects as you see fit. Demands alot but is always available to help, even if its a call outside of office hours. One of my fav professors!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This has been my favorite Vandy class so far! From day one, Lori was clear that this class will be intense yet rewarding. There is a LOT of new vocab to take on, but you will learn so many new words and what you learn will be so applicable in a healthcare career. Interpreting in a local clinic was inspirational as well. Take if it sounds for you!

Lori is the chillest and funniest prof I've had here at Vandy, shes very passionate about this class and gets very involved in making sure all her students understand whats going on. The 4 different projects in this class are a lot of work but you will learn a lot and you will basically get an A on every assignment if you put forth any effort.

Lori is inspiring and the best professor Ive ever had at Vandy. She definitely expects a lot out of her students, but she is supportive and encouraging at the same time. I learned so much in this class. Definitely recommend!

Professor Catanzaro definitely wants her students to learn but is extremely disheartening and overbearing at times. If you are not a native speaker, it is definitely hard to feel confident. While I did learn a lot and liked the class structure, the semester progressive got graded harder and she got less understanding and picked her favorites.

She is incredible. I loved this class and my Spanish improved a lot. Tons of business-related vocab so you definitely have to study to do well on the tests, but if you participate in class she's really generous with help and grading. I learned so much, and since we do a lot of partner/small group work I made new friends in her class too!

Out of all the spanish classes I've taken at Vandy, this one definitely taught me the most. There's 5 tests, papers, and you have an internship at a clinic in Nashville. LOTS of work, but the material you learn in this class will greatly prepare you to serve the Spanish-speaking population as a healthcare provider. Lori is a great professor!

Not difficult, but a lot of work at times. Exams include like 200 vocab words, so study early. Projects are time-consuming, but she gives very clear guidelines and is super helpful if you have questions. After you've done one project and one exam, you'll know how to handle the class with ease. Also, she's super friendly and chill. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Favorite class I've taken at Vandy. She really cares a lot about you learning. A lot of content, but it's doable, and everyone got an A in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: 4 tests that are vocab based and 2 presentations. The rest of the time class is so easy. She is hilarious and caring and will help with anything. Wants all of her students to get an A. Participation is so important because if she likes you then you are set. The final project is a group project. Include tons of details and she will be pleased.

Lori really cares about her students. Spanish for Business is a decent amount of work, especially at the beginning of the course. She decides who she likes towards the beginning of class, so bring your A game and you'll do great! There are 4 tests (none cumulative), two presentations, an interview assignment, and a final group project.

I really like Lori as a professor and I would definitely recommend her. However, Spanish 3345 is a LOT of work. It's nice because it's interesting and easy to get a good grade, but be prepared to put in many hours of work and learn an absurd amount of vocab.

This is my favorite class I have taken at Vanderbilt. She is absolutely amazing and cares so much about her students! The class did require work and you have to give a few presentations but it is extremely fun and interesting, so worth it.

Prof. Catanzaro is a great choice for an elective class. This class helps you gain a good grasp of business Spanish, it's not terribly taxing, grading is relatively easy, the class atmosphere is laid back, and Prof. Catanzaro is empathetic, accessible, and understanding. There may be a lot of busy work sometimes, but I still recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lori is the perfect kind of Spanish prof- she really cares about her students and is so good at teaching content through conversational Spanish. The class takes a lot of outside work sometimes, but it totally pays off in knowledge and practicality. Easy grader!

Lori is literally the BEST. Her class is a lot of work (tons of vocab memorization, lots of shorter papers/reflections) but you learn so much and the material is super relevant. I know that I'll be using the stuff we're learning in my career one day. She genuinely cares about students and is super personable, fun, and transparent. LOVE her.
Definitely my favorite professor.

Lori really cares about her students learning and wants you to do well.  She is pretty hard on your grammar and pronunciation but she overall is fair.  The amount of work is high, but you learn ALOT from these assignments and the material is so practical and relavent to real life.  Best Spanish prof and class I've ever had.

You have to work a lot in this class but Lori is encouraging and wants you to learn and especially to speak in class. There are a lot of projects and tests but the workload is not too much. Grammar is important and there is so much vocabulary, over a thousand words but very practical and I've already used it in a job interview.

Extremely easy grader.  Lots of work on individual and group projects (mostly presentation based) but no major papers.  She loves when students participate and is very willing to be helpful outside of class.

I have learned so much in this class.  Lori is the best Spanish professor I've had at Vandy, very supportive, kind and knowledgable. The  case studies, country profiles, company profiles, and current news are incredibly informative.  There is a LOT of work, but she is a fair and grader and makes us talk all the time and she corrects your grammar.

There is A LOT of work for this class - 4 tests, 2 presentations, a group project and a paper plus homework - but she's a very easy grader. The hardest part of the tests is the vocabulary. She's really passionate about the material, incredibly knowledgeable, and cares about her students. The work helps you learn, too, so it's worth doing.
This woman is simply AWESOME. Don't let the first few weeks scare you off. She is understanding and just loves it when you participate in class discussion.
best teacher i have ever had. she keeps everyone interested, and the assignments help give a better understanding of the subject

Literally my favorite professor so far at Vanderbilt. She is so kind, helpful and funny. Will do everything she can to help ensure you succeed in the class, and grades the tests/projects very fairly. Also smoking hot.

She is literally one of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. Because of her, I finally decided to major in Spanish. Class is easy as long as you go every day. Not much homework, but a lot of memorization, but its doable especially if you are premed. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND HER

The best Spanish professor at Vanderbilt.  Lori makes the subject so engaging and interesting and class time goes by so fast. She organizes class time with a balance of conversation, discussion, and presentations.  I have learned so much in her course, it is challenging, but the work is spread out and her grading is fair.

The best Spanish teacher I've had. She makes everything interesting and the subject is extremely engaging. LOTS of work, but nothing too difficult, and she's more than willing to help you at all times. My only complaint is her occasional habit of putting homework on the board in the last minute of class and you not noticing that it's there.

(Spanish for the Medical Profession) Lori is an excellent professor! Class discussions are interesting and usually include current news articles and videos. A lot of vocab memorization before the first test, but stick with the class - it lightens up into a moderate workload that's totally doable.

By far the best professor I've had at VU.  She is extremely helpful and really good at teaching.  She really takes an interest for her students.  The class is a lot of work, but if you put in the effort, you get a lot out of it.  Not too hard of a grader.
Lori's the best. Demanding but fair.  You will learn more in her classes than any other Spanish class at Vanderbilt.
Lori's awesome, very knowledgeable and enthusiastic, really organized and professional, helpful and really cares about her students
Lori is the best teacher in the span department. so knowledgeable and sweet..makes spanish fun. everyone who takes span should have her at some point!
She is a great teacher who provides an awesome foundation and isn't too hard either!

Great teacher...she made a boring class enjoyable.  She really cares about her students on all levels, so it's always easy to talk to her about class, life, whatever.  Take any class she offers!  You'll learn and have fun (amazing, I know)
Love her! Her classes are a lot of fun and not that hard. She's a fair grader and is so helpful. I would definitely recommend any of her classes.
Very helpful and passionate. Fun teacher!  She works you hard, but it's worth it and you definitely learn a lot! I def. recommend taking a class with her.  She is fabulous.

She is a wonderfully helpful teacher, always willing to tell you what you can do to improve. If you show effort she is a lot easier on you. She is very funny and makes learning about Spanish grammer actually pretty fun. Beware of surprise quizes, she loves to give them.

she is one of the best teachers to have for span 104.  if you take the time to show that you were interested, not only will you get a good grade in the class but she will also grade your essays easier.  i recommend her fully.

Definately Take her class! She is a great teacher and makes the class fun. I was worried that I would dread this 5 hour class, but it is by far my favorite class. She is willing to help you in any way possible and has a great sense of humor. The work load isn't that much. Don't show up late or talk when she is talking.

The best! A fair teacher. A's are possible, but you need to do your work. 201 is definately harder, but she makes the class much more bearible. Great sense of humor and GREAT resource. She has become a friend of mine. One of the few teachers that you can actually talk to. Take her classes!! She is absolutely wonderful.
It's a tough class, and Lori will challenge you, but she is also incredibly passionate about Spanish and about helping her students succeed. Take any class she offers!
Great teacher!  Not too hard but challenging and she makes it fun.  Very caring and understandable...just dont be late to class or talk alot while she is talking...that makes all professors upset.
She is the best spanish teacher I've ever had. It was not hard to attend her class everyday.
She is awesome! By far the best Spanish teacher I've had. Definitely take her class if you can. She makes the class really enjoyable and you'll actually learn a lot.
love this teacher, she made me love spanish!
Incredibly nice and helpful. She makes class entertaining and fun.
she's awesome- a lot of fun to have in class, and she reaches out to all her students.
She is really a great teacher. Has lots of energy and makes the class interesting and fun to attend. Not your normal boring spanish class. If you have to take Spanish, you will want to have her
Easy course, attendance policy sucks.  If you skip class, you'll do poorly in here.
No Comments

I loved Dr. Zepeda's Adolescent Development class. Her lectures and class activities were engaging, and she did a great job connecting what our learning back to our lives. Grade is based on a semester long infographic project, 3 multiple choice exams, homework assignments, and 4 reflections. Easy A as long as you pay attention and do good work.

Dr. Zepeda is a very nice and caring professor, and her class is enjoyable and interesting. Your grade is composed of participation (attendance), a semester long infographic project, 3 multiple-choice midterm exams, and several homework assignments. Easy A as long as you show up, pay attention during class, and do the assignments. Loved this class!

I truly could not say enough amazing things about Dr. Z. She is not only a great teacher who truly cares about your learning, but she's such a kind amazing person. There are 3 exams, no final, and one semester long infographic. I wish she taught other classes so I could take her agian.

For HART 2779. Dr. Chesney as a professor is a post doc fellow. His class is challenging, only in the sense that you have to put up with interesting views. Book heavy, unclear grading rubrics. 3 confusing midterm tests. He's a bit unaware of his privileges, thinks he's a very “based” anarchist.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: honestly a great prof, classes are very intimate and conversational and if you get to know him you will learn alot about architecture and do well in the class.

I'm kind of shocked Dr. Chesney has a low rating. I found him to be a great professor. You should be able to succeed in his class if you engage with the class and the content and show an interest. My personal qualm with him is that his organization can be somewhat loose, and will often send you the readings a few days prior
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Not sure why the review below says anyone who gets below a B is lying since I got a C in the course despite showing up to almost every class and turning in every assignment on time. This course is known for being one of the most grade deflated in all of Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Anyone on here saying they got lower than a B is LYING. He's just opinionated so some students get mad. very intelligent teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: very smart guy, learned a lot from him

reviews.comment: Grading metrics very weird, even if u get an A on all assignments, one B can result in an overall grade of a B. Course average sits around a C to a C+.
Sent out a spiteful email bc we were complaining that 2/3 of the class had B- or below.
i cry everyday, i cannot go to law school now

Chesney was irregular, but clearly an intelligent guy with lots of insights. Lectures & approach to studying the city were engaging but sometimes felt unorganized. 3 exams + 2 movies + participation for the grade. Split the class 50% A's and 50% B's. I enjoyed the class, but wouldn't recommend for those looking for an easy humanities class.
terrible professor...nothing else needs to be said

The lowest grade in this class he gave out was a B-. It's honestly not hard if you show up to class, and he provided about 5 extra credit opportunities throughout the class! The hate he's gotten is so not deserved, and I hope if you are reading this, don't be discouraged by the other comments. Show up, engage, and you will get a good grade, period

Dr. Chesney, though very informative and wise in terms of his knowledge of urbanism, is one of the most disorganized and confusing professors I have had at Vanderbilt. If you are not planning to major in urbanism or anything around this subject, please beware of taking this class. Altogether, I wish Dr. Chesney could change his grading system.
Man is talm bout how his life goal is to become a professor at Harvard LIKE DAWG U NOT EVEN GOOD ENOUGH FOR COMMUNITY COLLEGE GANG; and NO ONE CARES how u been to skid row and allat.

reviews.comment: REALLY goofy guy. Says some outlandish stuff and the lectures are just whatever he wants to yap about. Interesting grading where he gives top half As on tests and bottom half Bs but with presentations and extra credit you will probably finish with an A or A-. Strongly opinionated is an understatement but he's such a character its entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You could definitely tell that Dr. Chesney enjoys the topic that he is teaching to students. However, I want to warn that this class is very lecture and reading heavy, especially considering that most people take the class for AXLE credit. If you're not interested in the topic of urbanism, I recommend you find another class for Perspectives credit.
hardest course ive ever taken
just dont take this class
I am so lost in this class because of his super unorganized lectures

This dude is bizarre. Truly the best way to put it. From his lectures, to his tangents, to his grading, nothing makes sense. His lectures follow no pattern and his slides are incoherent. He ranks the class and the top half get As and the bottom half get Bs. Avoid at all costs if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chesney is a clearly knowledgeable, young professor with a unique experiential view of urbanism. He gives extremely interesting, well thought out lectures from memory, but they can be somewhat difficult to follow layout wise. The tests are difficult, but he makes it clear that the top 50% of tests get an a, and the rest get a b. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will either get a B or an A in this class, nothing less than a B. He's lenient grader and as long as you study, you will be fine. The lectures are somewhat disorganized but it's only because he is passionate about what he's teaching!

Lots of reading and lectures have mandatory attendance. Midterms are hard if you don't do the reading or show up to class, but are curved such that half of the class gets an A on the exam. Take this if you want to learn something new and ask questions about urbanism and history. The guy knows a lot. The class will be as enjoyable as you make it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm crying a day before my first midterm in this class. Absolutely clueless. He is making my first semester miserable
enough said

Lectures are super disorganized; he keeps going on rants. I have no clue whats going to be tested and whats not. (e.g. class is on urbanism but why are we talking about philosophy and randomly switching from ancient Greece to native American slaves to the crusades????)

Professor Russell is a fantastic professor who cares deeply about her work, her students, and the legal field. I am typically a straight A student, but had to work hard to achieve an A- in her class. Despite this, I would ABSOLUTELY take her again. I learned a lot from her knowledge and enthusiasm for the law, both in class and during office hours.

Professor Russell is a fantastic lecturer who cares deeply about her work, her students, and the legal field. I worked very hard to achieve an A-, despite typically being a straight A student. Despite this, I would ABSOLUTELY take her class again because I learned so much. Go to office hours!! She is knowledgeable and wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Russell was great, she was funny, and our class had great chemistry, which led to zero cold calling and good participation grades all around. The toughest part about her class is that a 95 is an A, but it is definitely possible. I highly recommend taking her class. I've never learned more about the law!

She was funny and charismatic and there's lots of extra credit opportunities to help boost your grade to that tough A (95) baseline so it's definitely doable. Didn't cold call but I had a really active section so if people are participating she won't just randomly call on someone else. Midterm was easy, mostly short response, final is fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Russell has been my absolute favorite professor at Vanderbilt so far. Her passion about the study of law and genuine interest in her students success is very clear. This class is a must if you are thinking about going into law school.

Professor Russell is the best. There are a couple low rated reviews for her from Covid years and I urge everyone to disregard them. She is so knowledgeable, very helpful, and super entertaining. She will work with you and go out of her way to make sure you are doing the best you can be. Also ties in current events when applicable which is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Russell is awesome. You can tell she is genuinely passionate about what she teaches and really wants all of her students to succeed, beyond the classroom especially. PSCI-3260 is great for anyone thinking about law school and I highly recommend it.

Most difficult class I've taken at Vandy—but worth it. Dr. Russell is so intelligent and this class covered many legal topics, including current events. Readings were long but manageable and she covered most in class anyways. The essay topics and moot court were interesting and very insightful. Recommend doing every extra credit opportunity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Russell's class helped me realize that I do enjoy learning about the law. She definitely cares about the issues at hand. Lectures were dry, and the feedback she gave on the 2 hypos and the moot court opinion felt a bit arbitrary. Worst thing is that she wants a 95 for an A - in my opinion, that's ridiculous and enough to steer clear from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hard to get an A (95+). Great professor but seems a little distant with freshmen who take her class. Really funny and usually engaging lectures.

Teaches out of the textbook for the most part. Readings can range from 20 to 100+ pages, so be ready. Doesn't cold call. Lectures can get a little boring but generally not too bad. Two hypotheticals, a decently hefty midterm, and moot court which r were pretty interesting. Generally a very nice, accomidating professor---fs take her if ur pre-law.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting and Thought-Provoking lectures, but the class was hard to excel in. Never skip and try to talk in class but do not need to do every reading. TA grades and it can seem pretty harsh, but she graded the final lightest of all which helped a bunch. Would take another class with her because the content really makes you think, but consider GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Despite the volume of material in this class, Professor Russell makes each lesson digestible and easy to follow. This class is quite fun if you're willing to speak up and really engage with the content. The hypotheticals and final project are intellectually stimulating and what you learn will really stay with you even after the class ends.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Russell's lectures are incredibly impactful. Her assignments are always relevant and grading criteria is made clear. She is very open to feedback and cares about the success of each student. Outside of class, she is always willing to give advice and guidance on pre-law/law school related matters. I highly recommend taking her classes!

You can tell she cares deeply about her students and the Constitution.  The assignments are fair and she provides a rubric before-hand as well as old exemplars from previous classes.  Strongly recommend.

Professor Russell is the type of professor that makes a Vanderbilt education worth it. She is exceptionally devoted to the success & learning of her students & makes a deliberate effort to get to know them on a personal level. Her classes are enriching, the expectations for success are made clear, & the lessons pay dividends far into the future.
I love constitutional law, so that's what allowed me to be excited about this class rather than Prof. Russell's teaching.

Dean Russell is a campus gem! An admired professor and inspiring leader, her presence elevates our campus. With more faculty like her, the campus would flourish. She's my role model, a fantastic person, a wonderful dean, and an excellent educator. She is so caring; she cares and advocates for those whose voices aren't heard.
She definitely cares about every student and wants to help you succeed- the final moot court project at the end of the semester was the best part.
She clearly loves teaching Judicial Process and knows a lot about the Courts.  She brought in lawyers and judges as guest speakers and helped us understand how the American judicial system works.

Dean Russell definitely makes you work to get the grade you want in her classes. Her TAs do sometimes grade assignments, which is problematic if they don't provide detailed feedback or grade inconsistently. Dean Russell is hyperaware of issues and works with her students to provide accommodations cognizant of problems. Just pop into office hours!

This class during fall 2022 is an exception to Prof. Russell's track record. She is respected in the poli sci department and people love her but this class was pretty disorganized and she apologized for it at the end. Participation is stressful and you're graded on a curve like a law class, which is also stressful so be prepared for that.
Ok professor if you're trying to go to law school, avoid taking her class unless you're willing to suck up.

I took five courses with Dr. Russell, and I can tell you that she completely changed my life for the better. Dr. Russell truly cares about shaping the next generation of lawyers and advocates. If you happen to be GENUINELY interested and passionate about law and politics, then you will succeed in her classroom. Do not be afraid to ask questions!
Not the best Poli Sci class by any means. Take another professor
"Extra credit" that's meaningless in the grand scheme of things. Grades are so subjective that it basically has no weight
Meh

I loved Professor Russell! The class I took with her was difficult, but there was a lot of extra credit towards the end to make up for some of the harsher grading on the papers. The majority of the harsh grading and feedback problems were not her fault, but the fault of the TA. I enjoyed this class, but would have enjoyed more with a better TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Incredibly disorganized. While you are assigned 5 reflection papers throughout the semester, expect to not receive any grades until the last possible minute.

She was a great professor who was super insightful. She offered lots of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Grade based on 5 short reflection papers and one final project. Would definitely recommend it for the political theory elective!

She's a great professor but the TA made this class awful with his arbitrary grading & useless feedback on all 5 papers. To make up for it, she offered plenty of extra credit at the end. Discussion heavy & comments could get repetitive b/c it was always a few people speaking on issues they don't have the range to. The topics were interesting though!

Very knowledgeable, you'll learn a lot of good material. Bases participation grade on how much you talk, which is problematic when you have 50 people trying to talk every class. If you don't suck up, good luck getting called on. Very disorganized with assignments.

Her assignment instructions literally contradict each other. If you're a perfectionist / organized / stress about school a lot-- don't take her class. Her disorganization will drive you crazy. If you're chill and don't stress too much, I guess she's alright. Unclear assignment instructions, a 94 is an A-, a lot of reading, hard to meet with.

Course content is very interesting! Readings were heavy with up to 60 pages per class (finished the entire textbook before spring break) & she does cold call in the beginning. 2 hypotheticals and 1 final brief/opinion  which were graded surprisingly leniently, imo. Only one midterm exam which definitely needs to be studied for. Great intro to law!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: very reading intensive. make sure you read and show up to class. cold calls but less frequent as semester goes on. make sure you study a lot for the exam and final presentation. might be a low 2-level but it could easily be a 3-level
really engaging professor. knows what she's talking about. is a good intro to law school, but be prepared for some big assignments. otherwise, a good class.

Professor Russell is a must-take if you're interested in law. You learn so much, and it's worth the work which I didn't think was an unreasonable amount. It's clear she's passionate about law and knows what she's talking about. Super caring and understanding outside of the classroom as she's also the pre-law advisor. A real gem and resource!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The only reason this was given a 3 was because an A- was quite achievable. However, the grading and expectations were incredibly unclear. Heavy on reading and can be randomly called on (though rare). Never knew the reason why I received the grades I did. Papers/short answer graded very subjectively. Very reasonable when it comes to extensions.

I have such mixed feelings about this. Russell often seems frazzled but she is organized and has a thorough syllabus with clear expectations. Grading inconsistent ( sometimes surprisingly lenient? ). Shes funny and cool, an interesting person. But not a super engaging lecturer. She didnt cold call much this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really great class if you're thinking about law school. Assignments can be a little vague, but she wants students to do well.
Amazing resource for everything pre-law. Class is very engaging and the assignments are interesting (if you like law). Decent amount of reading that you need to do before class (she cold calls)

Lady expects us to write a 15 page law school policy brief in 2 days. We would have had more time to think about it and write it, if not for her disorganized teaching style and procrastination! She procrastinates so much and never keeps to her promise. Its really hard to keep up with the class because of her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had a lot of good things to say about Russell, but they've been clouded by how she correlates eagerness to use quarantine productively with having all the time in the world. Course never had a set schedule (we don't know in advance what to read, when to meet, etc.) until 18 hours prior. Made life miserable & quarantine time even more uncertain.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not accessible outside class (and class was ONLINE!) Brings in a salesperson into lecture just so he can sell us LSAT prep material. I literally PAID to listen to an hour-long ad. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content is interesting but gets spoiled by the teaching. All the material assigned as reading is recovered in class in long-drawn-out ways. The rhetorical style is boring, causing most students to get sleepy until being cold-called in the middle of a class to answer a specific question. If you do a lot of work you'll do well, but it's a pain

Professor Russell has been my best professor at Vanderbilt. She not only makes classes interesting, but she validates all of her students as thinkers and workers. She wants you to succeed. She is very understanding about mental health issues and is more than willing to accommodate you. You need to put in the work but it does not feel like work

Constitutional Law was a lot less stressful than I expected. Good overview of the topic and intro to law assignments. 2 hypos (papers), short answer/essay midterm and really fun moot court exercise. Quite a bit of reading but super accessible outside class and fun stories during lecture. Helped spark my interest in law!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The most caring and approachable prof I've had. She can be biased at times and less knowledgeable about certain topics but the way she teaches her classes is very hands-on and enjoyable. Grading criteria for essays is sometimes unclear, but she's willing to help in office hours. An A is tricky (cutoff was 95). Highly recommend for pre-law students.

Russell certainly cares about her students, but doesn't know much and lets her political bias seep into her classes. She called all Republicans "Confederates," for instance, and when asked question about Shinzo Abe admitted she had never heard of him. She often got distracted in lectures, showing more Game of Thrones videos than actual material.

Dr. Russell's first year writing seminar was quite informative. I definitely learned a lot about the Supreme Court and the legal world in general. That being said, her grading criteria is not very clear. All the grades come from essays, and she doesn't always hand back feedback on the essays -- nor does she provide a rubric for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Russell is a truly helpful and compassionate professor, both inside and outside the classroom. In her classes, Dr. Russell sets reasonably challenging expectations, and her lectures are often both informative and enjoyable. I sincerely recommend Dr. Russell, especially for pre-law students (to whom she offers excellent law admissions advice).

Dr. Russell is by far the most popular professor in the PSCI department, and for good reason. She is passionate in class and really works hard to make sure her students are not only learning the material but appreciating it as well. Overall, Dr. Russell is amazing and I would certainly take her classes again. (Beware: lots of reading though.)

The vast majority of students seem to like Professor Russell, but for whatever my opinion counts, I feel that she lacks to proper knowledge to teach her classes. She consistently makes rather large factual mistakes and often teaches directly out of the textbooks; I would have learned more if I just read the books and never showed up to class.

Prof. Russell is a good lecturer, and she relies heavily on the textbook in this course (as in, we read the whole thing). Not great about returning graded assignments in a timely fashion, but you'll leave the class feeling like you learned a lot, and the material is usually fairly engaging.
Very easy grader, but an A is a 95 in this class so it offsets. Very nice, but sometimes a bit forgetful/wrong about trivial tangential details.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The best

Russell is awesome. The class was a little jumbled because it was her first time teaching it, but it wasn't that bad. Very little work and interesting discussion topics. Only criticism is that the TA grades papers and there's very little variance in grades regardless of quality--it's going to be a 90-92 regardless, which makes an A (96) difficult.

Professor Russell is the best professor at Vandy, in my opinion. I would recommend any of her classes to anyone interested in political science or law. She's really funny and knows everything there is to know about Constitutional Law. She is always willing to help students and it a really great person to talk to about legal careers.

I took this class (Law, Politics, & Justice) in Russell's first semester teaching it, so it wasn't very organized yet--but  it was super fun and low-stress. She picks hot topics to discuss each week (ex. gun control, death penalty) and you read and then discuss & write a short reflection paper. Most fun political theory class available.

Loved Russell's Con Law class. It's a ton of reading, but it's rewarding material, and she has fun and engaging lectures every day. She's approachable, super nice, and knows her stuff. I looked forward to trekking to Commons at 10 AM three times a week. Take her class.
Great teacher in all respects. Had her for multiple classes. Nothing but good things to say.

Carrie Russell is great. Her classes are the ones that at the end you feel so accomplished for what you have done and learned. However, they are a lot of work. You have to do the reading, and there is a lot, but her classes are completely worth the effort.

Professor Russell is hands-down the best professor at Vanderbilt. She cares about her students, is really funny and engaging, and knows the material inside and out. She makes Constitutional Law really interesting, and is a fair grader. I would HIGHLY recommend any class with her.

Dr. Russell is the best professor at Vanderbilt, in my opinion. This class is an Easy A, if you show up and participate and write decent papers, you will do well. Russell is funny and makes each lecture interesting. Overall a great professor and gives great advice.

I took the freshman year writing seminar on American constitutional law. Professor Russell is an incredibly nice and passionate individual. She is always there to help and is flexible with conflicts that arise throughout the semester. She makes constitutional law an extremely interesting topic due to her vibrant personality. One of my favorites.
Absolutely my best professor at Vanderbilt thus far. Kind, knowledgeable, and really wants to see her students succeed.

Love her. Great professor, really sweet and cares about her students. There is a lot of time-intensive reading and you need to be ready for class discussion (which means good attendance), but it was worth it. Only 2 papers and a brief at the end of the semester. Easy grader. Really supportive and always helpful in class and in office hours.

I LOVE CARRIE! She knows her stuff! Class is fun! This class is easier than her others like Con Law but its not an easy A. You still have to read a lot. Also you need to brief 2-3 cases every night.  We have 2 main assignments (a hypothetical and a trial). Other than that its the briefs and participatio in class.  You need to read to do well!

This class was literally my life this semester. Hands down my favorite class. Carrie Russell managed to take a very dry, complicated subject area (Constitutional Law) and present it in an interesting and clear manner to college freshman. I'm not going to lie- it's a lot of work if you want to really understand the subject. But I loved this class.
Great class, exceptional professor. Russell is helpful inside and outside of class, very accommodating. Her class was interesting and fun. Easy grader.

This is probably my favorite class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Prof. R is fantastic and truly cares. I didn't fully read the textbook at all, since there aren't any quizzes.  As long as you have a basic idea, and can answer at least vaguely a question she asks, you'll be fine.  3 assignments, all plainly laid out, and graded easily. Easy A.

Russell is one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt! I've had 3 classes with her.  If you're interested in law school, take her class. Attendance is mandatory, participation is important, and there's a lot of reading.  If you're willing to do all the reading you're fine. Her grading isn't bad; she's clear on what she wants.

Absolutely love her. She's harsh sometimes but she's a clear lecturer and she knows what she's doing. Make sure you do the reading-- it's essential. I'm looking forward to taking more classes with her!!!

Main problem with class: it is essentially you reading the textbook; every class period is simply a recollection of the reading for that day, with no critical analysis. I got nothing from the actual class itself. She also often deflects questions she doesn't know the answer to by saying, "Well, what do you guys think?" Really nice lady, though.

Professor Russell is one of Vanderbilt's best. If you're interested in law - take her class. The class is a great way to see if you're actually interested in law school. Her grading is fair, and she's very clear about what she wants. The reading is required, so if you don't want to do it, don't take the class. If you do the work, you'll do well.
Great class! If you have any interest in Law School this is a   Must take class! One of my favorite classes.

Frustrating class. She runs class by Socratic method which means reading is essential. However, it also means class is just a resuscitation of the reading with no additional knowledge provided. Also you have to read all 672 pages of the Constitutional Law textbook which is exactly as fun as it sounds. More work than its worth, take another class.

Professor Russell is awesome! She is very clear and straightforward, and super nice and helpful. She also has guest judges and lawyers which is cool. However, the class is pretty reading intensive.  Do the homework and show up and you'll be fine.

Professor Russell is one of the nicest professors I've had. She was very understanding and approachable. You shouldn't skip the readings because she may pick on you, and since participation is so heavily weighted, you probably don't want to get caught off guard. If you follow the directions, you will do well.

Really sweet lady, and genuinely nice. Class was VERY reading intensive, though, which required a lot of time outside of class. Also offers lots of in-class guests who come in that are lawyers/judges in Nashville - pretty cool. Class wasn't too difficult, although certainly not a complete blowoff. She's beautiful, too.

She's a good professor, and the material is presented in an EXTREMELY interesting manner. However, I dislike her grading scale, which makes it virtually impossible to make an A even after much work. She is very nice however, and is willing to look over your papers when you have questions.

She is a smart prof who still manages to be approachable and non-intimidating. Class expectations are reasonable and straightforward. Don't skip or half-a** the assignments, and you?ll do well. She is the clearest lecturer of the 7 PSCI profs I?ve taken.  Some readings can be difficult (even if they?re 5 pages) but are explained well in class.
she curves the grades down. not a difficult class but theres not reason for that

If you pay attention and read the lecture notes you'll do fine. The midterm/final were VERY straightforward.. almost all of the multi choice questions were on previous quizzes. If you've taken a US history course you won't learn that much.. but its okay for a basic polisci class.

The class is pretty straightforward.  Attendance is mandatory because she gives pop quizzes.  If you scan the readings and pay attention in class, you'll do fine.  However, if you're absent (even if you have an excuse), she won't help you.  Lowest quiz grade dropped, fairly easy midterm.  Good instructor, extra credit available if you work for it.

Class is book based. We discuss topics based on a book that explores current issues in the US. We use a text book for quizzes and exams. There is extra credit. There are pop quizzes. We do watch movies. She is fair and clear. She is willing to meet with you.

I took creative writing in high school and wanted to try this out and it ended up being such a fun class. We had to write two short stories and some exercises, most of it was reading though. Professor Dubrova was really encouraging and sweet. She gave me extra reading suggestions outside of class and made me want to take more fiction classes

This was the most enjoyable class I took last semester! Some days are reading heavy, but overall the workload is super manageable. Prof Dubrova is funny and caring, she loves talking about stories. The workshop was mostly discussion based, and I got to know other students super well by the end bc of reading their work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Warm and helpful with all students. Took her in her first year teaching, so she was a bit inexperienced at lecturing, but she clearly knows her stuff. Class readings were short and enjoyable. Much of the class comes down to reviewing others' work, which can be repetitive, but is easy.
bro your entire grade is based on four exams and not to mention he pulls the most niche things from his slides and expects you to remember them
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall great professor - some questions on exams included content outside of textbooks/lectures which made them difficult to anticipate, but Professor Johnson mostly helps students know what to expect on midterms. Final is comparatively easier and manageable

Very funny and engaging lecturer! He goes FAST though. Bio 1511 better be your hardest class bc it requires A LOT of effort to get a good grade. Grading is only based on the tests. average grade gets curved up to a b. no hw or attendance or anything bc grading is only tests

Extremely difficult tests, but if you get a B on at least one, Roka's other 2 are not so bad (imo). Extremely engaging, funny, and does a great job at explaining the infinite information he gets through during class. If you dont review you are indeed cooked.

One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Really good lecturer, EXTREMELY funny, and cares about his students. It is definitely a fast paced course and very content heavy but if you watch the online lectures he posts before class, the information during the in-class lectures sticks. Gave me a fist bump at the end of the semester :)
If you don't review outside of class, you will be cooked, and he goes really fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best biology professor. Extremely well thought out lectures and very entertaining to listen to (FUNNY). Lecture only class based only on exams. There is A LOT of material but if you watch the recorded lectures he posts and keep up with the material daily then the exams are pretty straight forward and very fair. He is not trying to trick you.

Dr. Johnson is a funny and engaging professor, so lecture was always enjoyable! Know that this course requires a lot of memorization by nature, but Dr. Johnson is a great choice to take it with. The recorded review/office hours sessions are really helpful and go over past exam questions which he explains very clearly.

I love Professor Johnson so so much. He is hilarious in class, he keeps things interesting and engaging. His exams are definitely hard, but it's a bio exam so what do you expect? My favorite professor so far.

There is no doubt that Dr. Johnson is a funny guy and passionate about his lectures, but his class is graded with another professor, Dr. Rokas, and it is made up solely of exams. If you are a bad test taker, stay far away. The exams are tough, but if you put in many hours studying, you can do well, but it requires A TON of effort outside of class.

I really liked Dr. Johnson. Class consisted of lectures but he was passionate and entertaining about it. His exams are kind of tough + some questions are in the textbook and not the lecture, but he admits that so you shouldn't be surprised unless you don't read the study guide. There are lots of readings but overall I liked his section.

I learned so much from Clocks. Keep up with the content as it comes and utilize the TAs/his office hours. Grading seems tough but he seems to be gracious with the final grade. You'll learn biology, practice public speaking, and sceintific writing - AWESOME CLASS!!!

Hands down the best prof. I've had at Vandy. Very passionate about what he teaches (more so in BSCI 3230). His tests are hard and often time is an issue but exams are very fair. You have to read the textbook because some questions might come from there. But overall, very knowledgeable and cares more about whether you learn or not.

This is an inherently difficult and fast-paced course- imo harder than gen chem. That said, Johnson tries his best to cover all the content while making lectures engaging. My only complaint is exams are unnecessarily difficult, but he makes up for it by curving grades at the end. Just wish there was some extra grade padding to go with the 4 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very informative and engaging lecturer! I really enjoyed his lectures but exams were difficult and detail oriented. On top of the crazy amounts of information from the lectures we had to memorize, he also expected us to memorize information from the textbook. But that's simply the nature of this course and if you put in the effort it is 100% doable
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A ton of content in little time. On top of going very quickly through 30+ slides per lecture, you're responsible for finishing the PowerPoint (on occasion) and reading the outlined chapters in the textbook. DO NOT TAKE if coming straight from BSCI 1509, you will not have enough background knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked the Johnson portion of the class, he was very engaging and made lectures fun. I highly suggest staying consistent with the textbook because thats what helped me with this class tbh. As long as you stay on top of content and study ahead of time you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked Rokas more than Johnson. I think it is ridiculous for a teacher to test material not covered in lecture, which Johnson does. Exams are fair. To get a good grade, you will need to spend a lot of time preparing for exams (which are entirety of grade). Material is super interesting!

Johnson's lectures were always incredibly content heavy. Despite the copious amount of content in lecture, he still felt he did not have time to cover everything he wanted and assigned 1-2 additional chapters of reading per lecture. Exams questions often had minute details from the book. Also consistently made inappropriate comments in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades come from four exams (final + 3 midterms). There are four midterms and the lowest is dropped. Dr. Johnson is clearly very knowledgable, so he expects his students to have a very deep understanding of the material - test questions are very specific and you have to know all the material in detail to do well. Lots of material also

Beware that your entire grade will be made up of exams: 4 midterms (lowest dropped) and 1 final. You must try your absolute best on every exam. I love this man tho he is hilarious and honestly gives fair tests, but it's just an overwhelming amount of content. Watch lectures before class, never skip. His biweekly office hours are also fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fantastic bio professor, best of the ones I've taken. Bio in general requires dedication but even if you are only slightly interested in bio Johnson will make you love it. Hilarious and interesting connections w/ outside topics. Must read textbook if you want an A. Not harder than other bio professors. Strongly recommend.

Professor Johnson was a great biology professor and I really looked forward to going to class because he kept it very entertaining. I would highly suggest reading the textbook before class, as it went in more detail than the lectures did at times.

hands down best prof at vandy, love this man. He's very accommodating for tests if you have any life stuff going on. but defo read the textbook bc his notes won't cover everything that he tests on. make sure you know all processes by heart, use anki/quizlet/write it out. bio is a lot no matter what, put in the hours and it'll show in your grades
Johnson is a bit of a strange person, but he's a pretty decent lecturer. I wouldn't take him again, but I don't regret taking his section instead of the other BSCI 1511 section.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take Hillyer. Johnson is worse in every way

yes his tests are (a little) harder than hilyer's. but at the same time he's so funny and so kind! he takes note to remember your name if you go to his review sessions and overall he just is very friendly. gen bio itself is a lot of reading and memorization but johnson was nice to take the class with :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall general biology is a tough class to take. But Dr. Johnson really has his way to teach the content in an easier way to comprehend. very caring and helpful. Definitely go to his office hour he will explain things with total clarity.

Dr. Johnson is a good professor, and you can tell that he cares about his students. However, this class is very intense. You are graded only on tests, and they require many hours of studying. The lectures are packed with a lot of information, but Dr. Johnson makes them engaging and fun. Definitely recommend his section if you have to take BSCI1511.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LOVE LOVE LOVE Dr. Johnson!! I had just come back from winter break stressed out because I wasn't sure if I wanted to continue on a pre-med track after the horror that was BSCI 1510, but Dr. Johnson truly helped me regain my love for biology and medicine and has been the best professor I have had in the biology department yet. Sooo funny in class
Vanderbilt version of James Watson
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is intense, covering a ton of material from the textbook and lectures. The professor moves quickly, but his recorded videos and review sessions help. Staying on top of the work is key. Unstuck ai was great for preparing for exams.

He is amazing! His feedback is incredibly helpful, provides detailed comments on your paper sentence by sentence. He is not only an excellent professor but also an outstanding researcher. Very accessible outside of class and always willing to help. While the exams can be tough, plenty of opportunities for partial credit. Highly recommend!
Best biology lecturer I've had at Vanderbilt. The rest are horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class overall. Not an easy A but probably more leniently graded than you would think. Johnson is one of the top researchers in the field and even though he pretends to be dumb, he knows basically everything about the topic. He also seems to genuinely enjoy teaching this class (unlike 1511), and he reflects that in his teaching.

i do not like his teaching style. i like him as a person but like it is an extremely dense topic and i feel like things could be explained clearer and with more detail. i felt like i was just thrown in in the beginning. he also grades based off vibes which i kind of like considering the tests are extremely hard. definitely an interesting man.

I loved Professor Johnson's class! Lectures were a bit intimidating but tests were all multiple choice and very straightforward. Straight memorization and understanding pathways is heavily required. He curves at the end as well. An A is very doable in this class, great professor and tests are not meant to trick you
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson was incredibly funny, kept things interesting, and made me excited to learn about bio. He was one of the fastest-moving profs I've had, and the amount of information was enormous. Nonetheless, this is just the nature of BSCI at Vandy. I certainly recommend Dr. Johnson as your bio lecturer. Exams were fair, and office hours were plenty.

Dr. Johnson is a funny guy, but he is an exceptionally disorganized lecturer who moves through content at the speed of light. Because of how fast he lectured and how all over the place it was, going to class was basically useless, and this was supported by an obvious decrease in the amount of students who attended. Funny, but legit very bad.

Best science prof I've ever had. It's a LOT of content and you're responsible for everything in the textbook as well as his lectures, but if you put in the time and effort, you can succeed. His tests are very fair and he posts all his lecture videos in addition to twice-weekly review sessions (also recorded on Zoom and posted). Highly recommend!

he's such a goofy little guy : )
Difficulty was similar to 1510, especially with the tests being very detailed and needing to memorize every little thing on the slides. However, he was such an engaging lecturer at times and likes to joke around a lot. I brought my HOD major friend once, and she said he's the weirdest prof ever (in a good way).
Great professor, the class is difficult with a lot of content, but you can do well if you put in the work.

Dr. Johnson seems like a nice guy, but sitting in his class getting lectured at is like being sprayed by a fire hose of information. So much info and he talks at the speed of light. Once you process what he says he's moved on 3 slides. Exams are also so difficult. If you have to take this class with him, be prepared to study a lot.

Dr. Johnson is an engaging lecturer with a kind, old-man-ish sense of humor. Be prepared, however, the class is A LOT of content. You must read the textbook and attend the lectures (or look at posted lectures) to do well on the tests. Memorize everything lol. Overall, it was the most I've ever learned from any class but it was worth.

A lot of material, but his lectures are very cohesive and office hours are everyday. Grading wasn't solely based on exams, and was a more comprehensive look at chronobiology in general, from experiments to research papers to applying the concepts. It was a very doable class and I learned a lot!

LOTS of content in his section. To do well, ONLY read the textbook pgs he assigns in his lectures your study time is best spent memorizing EVERYTHING in the slides. Draw things out. Everything anywhere on his slides may be tested. Try to stay on top of lectures daily, they can be a lot. Good thing is this content is super interesting stuff.

Professor Johnson has a lot of content to cover, so his lectures are a lot. However, he posts his COVID lectures, so if you put in the time outside of class, you can get all of the information. His exams are pretty difficult though, since they test a deeper understanding of how things work. I enjoyed his lectures, and it felt worth it.

Johnson is entertaining but requires a ridiculous amount of content. The final letter grade is based on the class average, so it's just about doing the best you can. I've never had to learn more material, which is why this class is so difficult. Luckily, Johnson posts recorded lectures, slides, and required readings, which simplifies studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend. Entertaining but near impossible to take notes in lecture, and expects an ungodly amount of textbook reading. He would speed over content in lectures then just tell us we were supposed to study everything. Tests are super tricky and MC vs. short answers were worth disproportionate amounts. I didn't learn anything. Demoralizing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every single one of his classes is a whole marathon of material in 50 minutes. There are about 400 slides (that he reads straight off of in lecture) that he expects us to know top to bottom for each exam. Even still, he doesn't seem to feel that those 400 slides are sufficient for 30 questions on a test so he requires outside reading. Funny guy tho

I loved his class. I loved how he read from the slides, told us to learn test material that wasn't covered in class, and gives us test questions not relevant to bio. I also loved hearing how it's my fault when I don't do well. My favorite part of the class was his demonstrations which were so cringy I wanted my cells to stop doing glycolysis.

Johnson is such an amazing, kind guy. He was very kind and sympathetic toward any extenuating struggles/circumstances I had and was always willing to answer questions. His tests are really hard and detail-oriented, but it's not impossible to do well. It just takes ALOT of time to master everything. Don't listen to these whiny premeds haha.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Johnson makes this course very hard. That could be a good thing if you want to be challenged, but his exams are hard and he moves light speed through content. Even with him flying through material, we still are expected to know textbook information that he didn't cover.

I enjoyed Johnson's section more because I found the material to be easier but it a lot of content. I had to start studying every day not to fail. Do not miss class! His online lectures are sometimes 2 hours long. His test can be super tricky and he loves questions that have "2 or 3 of the above is true" and one of his MCQ was A-H on the final.

Overall, BIO will be hard whoever you take it with but I think that Johnson could have moved slower. There was so much information on his tests and it was always very unclear what we needed to know. That being said, he was super funny and lectures were entertaining when they weren't absolutely confusing.

Dr. Johnson has been my favorite professor thus far- he has a charismatic personality and a great sense of humor to keep the class entertaining. Although his lectures are lengthy, he provides great explanations. Only downside is that some test material comes directly from the textbook, which are not necessarily covered in lectures. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson was an engaging lecturer, but moved too quickly between slides and relied heavily on recorded lectures to learn content. Tests were "based on deep learning," but ended up testing ability to recall obscure details and questions were made to trick you not test understanding. He Ignored the only email I sent him with questions.

Personality is amazing, but he talks SO SO FAST and gives you gargantuan amounts of material in lectures, and here's the kicker, a third of the material he still won't get to in lecture and makes you read out of the textbook. He cares, but for the exams you need so much precise detail. He's really good, don't get me wrong, but you've gotta be wary.

His lectures contain an insane amount of information and he definitely speeds through it (exams are very broad). It's very easy to fall behind if you miss a lecture or you weren't really paying attention. He does give you all the resources you need and if you have a question about something you don't understand, he's always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the most painful classes I've taken at Vandy. Johnson's half covers an absolutely absurd amount of material that you are expected to know with insane precision. Half the material on one test was over stuff we never talked about in class but was in the textbook instead. Know what you're getting into. Way better than Gilpen though

BSCI 1511 is definitely a difficult class, but professor Johnson brings so much energy and vivacity to his lectures, that it makes coming to class fun. He is available to answer questions every day of the week (even weekends!). Watch the lecture videos, study at least a week in advance, and take COPIOUS, DETAILED notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Johnson's as a person is amazing. He is very kind and wants you to do well however, BSCI1511 is very hard. It is not on him that the class is hard, that's just the nature of bio, but he does not make the class any easier. He does make you know things for the tests that aren't covered in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's a difficult class, but you learn a lot. Also, he is one of the leading scientists in this field, and I believe you can apply what you learned in this class to almost every field of science. Make sure you attend lectures and keep up with the materials, and you will be fine. If you get behind by more than 2 weeks, then you are setting yourself u
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hes a really charismatic guy and the material is hard but if u ask to clarify something hes good at doing that. Class is memorization but he taught the more anatomy part of biology so as a pre-med it was a lot more interesting . Solid bio prof and my favorite

Good teacher but hard class. Really need to study a lot for the midterm and the class itself is a ton of memorization. Definitely be ready to put your time into this class as theres no textbook for the subject matter so some of the topics are very confusing

My favorite BSCI professor so far, and probably my favorite STEM professor too. For a tough class, he made it much more enjoyable by connecting topics to art and pop culture. Definitely recommend for 1511. Love him!

Dr. Johnson is easily my favorite stem professor I've had at Vanderbilt so far. He is an amazing lecturer and makes them fun and entertaining with his awesome personality. He does expect a lot out of you and gives lectures that will take hours but they are very good and informative. Would definitely recommend for 1511!!

Speaks naturally at 1.5x speed so taking notes is hard. Dumb that he makes us read the textbook and listen to an hour-long podcast for like 1-2 questions on exams to be based on that content (enough to affect your grade but not enough to justify the time investment). Other test questions are straightforward, at least
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Much better, more chill experience than 1511. Dr. Johnson is so supportive, and his passion for the subject material shines through in every lecture along with his cheery sense of humor. The midterm is very fair, the final is a bit tough, and he can be a bit of a tough grader on the paper, but overall he wants you to succeed and is happy to help.

Dr. Johnsons' lectures were really interesting and full of knowledge. He assigns textbook readings besides class but honestly, you don't need the reading to do well on the tests. Most of the materials in the test will be on his slides. Nevertheless, there were still a lot of materials to memorize.

Dr. Johnson is the fastest lecturer I have ever taken. Additionally, his daily class saying was "make sure to read the book on this because I did not cover certain sections that may be on the exam". Also, little to no detail on his slides, instead there were pictures... with no descriptions what so ever. Personally, would take a different section.
An absolutely awesome professor who makes biology extremely interesting and fun to learn about in lecture. His tests are also very straightforward and clear. Would highly, highly recommend.

Probably the easiest professor I had among both semesters of intro bio! He's really hilarious and does a lot of hands-on demonstrations during lecture that help students easily grasp and internalize information and important concepts. His tests are straightforward and manageable to succeed on. All you need to study are the lecture slides, no book!
Just need to know the lecture material very thoroughly and a good/basic understanding of the assigned readings and youll find the class to be very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had a weird mix of "study the slides" and "study the book". Tested over things not covered in class. Super interesting material. Kinda weird dude who seemed to enjoy saying uncomfortable things? Was an okay lecturer and liked to tell stories, so that was cool. Not the end of the world if you have to take him. Just study a lot.

Dr. Johnson's exams require very detailed studying, but they're very doable if you prepare. (I would recommend recording the lectures to make sure you don't miss anything.) He's a nice guy, I would take his class again if I had to choose.

Johnson speaks really quickly, so be ready to take notes. Content can be dry, but he takes time to talk about interesting stuff outside the course's focus. Multiple choice is tricky, and some come exclusively from assigned readings. Short answers are typically lecture-based. Really interesting guy! His section is harder than the others, though.

Dr. Johnson is one of the few professors who truly balances his love of research and his love for teaching. He promotes learning, not memorization, and gives ample opportunities to make (and fix!) mistakes. His tests are difficult but fair. His enthusiasm and laugh are contagious. Go to office hours for the trickier topics. Woudl take again!!!!

Dr. Johnson is an overall awesome and engaging professor that is passionate about what he teaches with great jokes here and there. During lecture, he does a lot of reading off slides and he talks quite fast. Be sure to keep up on the reading assignments, as they show up on the tests. The class is passable if you go to lecture and read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson is definitely the most inspirational professor I have had. He is incredibly knowledgeable on the subjects and puts together clear, engaging lectures with hilarious remarks at times. He really cares about his students and always enthusiastic about helping you out during office hours. Reading the book helps. Overall amazing professor!

The professor makes uncomfortable comments throughout the semester that border the line of inappropriate. His lectures are dense and unentertaining. His expectations for the class are very ambiguous and this leads to difficulty on the exams. Would not take this class and rater do other classes to fulfill the Neuroscience requirements
Made really inappropriate, uncomfortable jokes during lecture. Tested on material from the book that he didn't cover during lecture.

His tests are hard, but he's an amazing lecturer. Super passionate, engaged, and expressive -- but he talks very fast! Tests are mainly on lectures, but he puts in a couple reading-based questions. Be prepared to take lots of notes and do a lot of studying, but you learn an insane amount and he makes the material really interesting.

Assigns reading and quizzes you on the reading. MUST read in order to pass the quizzes. The Final borrowed a lot of questions from the quizzes. Overall, Johnson makes the lectures interesting and is great at giving students the bigger picture. An A is manageable IF you keep up with the reading.

Profesor Johnson is a  wonderful and clear lecturer. He is engaging and hilarious. Class itself is not very difficult, but you really have to work for an A. I would say his section is harder than Rokkas's section. The book readings are helpful but not essential to doing well in his class. His mc questions can at times be absurd with 8 options.
You need to know the material REALLY well and in detail for the quizzes

I just took this class for AXLE credit and I'm not even passing. Even though it's specifically for non-science majors this class is insanely hard. Quizzes are extremely specific and over tons of material. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CAN POSSIBLY AVOID IT.

Dr. J is brilliant and an extremely engaging lecturer, but the fact remains that he's a very difficult professor. You need to know the material inside out and backwards to succeed on his multiple choice test sections. He doesn't write things on the board, and he zooms through his powerpoints quickly. It'd be helpful to look them over before class!

This class is incredibly difficult and frustrating. Quizzes do not test how well you know the material - you could memorize the textbook and classpak articles and still not do well. Lectures are extremely boring. Although Professor Johnson is extremely nice, it is very hard to do well in the class, even if you're good at Bio.

Where to begin? I felt like my expectations for this class were not met. As a non-science major I was really hoping for a solid, engaging synthesis of the material; instead, I felt like I was just jumping through hoops. Lectures are dry and not posted on OAK; quizzesthe final test your multiple-choice ability and not content knowledge.

I like Johnson as a lecturer. He's funny and pretty engaging, BUT if you are taking this class solely for AXLE lab credit, I would take something else. The quizzes are unreasonably difficult for "baby bio" and the bioethics paper is graded very harshly. There are plenty of more strategic options for AXLE

Johnson gives 5 quizzes, 1 of which is dropped, that occur during the second half of lecture of the indicated day. They're all out of 12 questions, which makes it easy to do poorly, and material is heavily focused on lecture, which often doesn't overlap with the textbook readings. He is passionate about his topic, but he is often busy with research

He's incredibly tough, just like every other 110B class, but it's not too bad comparatively. His tests are on par with the 110A classes, but not so difficult that you won't understand them. Not an absolutely exceptional professor, but he'll get you through the first half. You kind of have to skim the book, but not much.

Professor Johnson is great. He is a very engaging lecturer, and is very straightforward about what he expects from his students. The only downside was the paper, which was graded by a grad student. That assignment was less than clear and unfortunately worth a significant portion of your grade. Other than that though the class was easy enough.

I would not recommend this class. It is terribly organized and my grades did not align with my knowledge of the material. The grad student who grades the papers is unhelpful and abrasive. The quizzes are unreasonably difficult.

Straightforward lectures with most presentations later posted online. Study for quizzes and start working on the ethics paper far in advance. Both are significant parts of your grade. Professor is polite and friendly one-on-one.
if you did well in your 9th grade bio class and liked it, you will do well in this class
I took this class for AXLE and it was a huge mistake. The quiz questions are arbitrary and impossible. Unless you are truly interested in the subject, I would stay clear at all costs

Johnson has an eccentric personality and is awesome. He talks crazy fast and covers a lot of material so it's good to record his lectures since its hard to keep up with him when taking notes. Make sure to study his lectures and pay attention to what he says in class.
Great teacher. Tests are fairly difficult because they cover a lot of material, but are very straightforward if youÂ´ve been studying. Is always crystal clear and kinda funny in class.

After 110a, 100b is a breeze.  However, class attendance is necessary to pass the class.  Study lecture slides, and you can easily get an a.  Entertaining guy, but not as helpful as Stubbs.  Good teacher, and crystal clear.  Test format is much easier than the other bio professors.
Little secret to passing this class- he uses the same quizzes that were in the classpack 2 semesters ago. Get an old classpack and you got it made.

Attendance is not mandatory but make sure you go to class and take really good notes! As long as you skim over the textbook and pay attention you should do okay on the quizzes, although some of the questions are really tricky. But its not a huge issue because the final is easy and the lab will boost your grade up. He's also a great lecturer!

This class is not difficult if you take good notes and do the reading. You will get used to the quiz formats and the final exam is super easy. Professor Johnson keeps lectures as interesting as possible. He's pretty funny. Only downside to the class is the useless bioethics paper you have to write. I would recommend this class to nonscience majors.

Great lecturer. Awful quiz writer. Quizzes are vague and EXTREMELY difficult. Readings and attendance don't matter much for the quizzes because they're so difficult and random. Great guy, but I probably wouldn't recommend this class to anyone.
