Came into the class with heavy prior Bio knowledge and still did not achieve anything.  He puts extremely vague and useless questions on quizzes and is completely unhelpful.

A challenging class. Johnson makes some good effort to keep it interesting by bringing in guest speakers sometimes. He's clear and easy to understand. The quizzes are a challenge, but work hard and it wouldn't be impossible to get an A. You might learn some interesting stuff as well.

Dr. Johnson is an entertaining lecture who tries to make even the most mundane aspects of biology interesting.  While attendance is not madatory to do well, it definitely helps, and his lectures are quite entertaining (especially during the unit on sex!).  Tests are somewhat tricky, but getting an A is definitely possible if you study enough.

This class is extremely difficult because of the 12 question multiple choice quizzes. They ask questions about the small details of articles in the class pak any many of the questions are very tricky because of the wording. Do not take this class if you are not good at multiple choice exams. Be willing to work very hard.

He knows a lot about the material. Meeting with him in office hours didn't always clear up my questions. Sometimes I left feeling more confused. His 12-question quiz format means that one missed question counts for an entire point grade. He makes you take the test at the end of class which I did not like at all.

Do not use as a class to fulfill a liberal arts requirement. Great guy, interesting material (a random selection of which makes it on the absurdly difficult quizzes). Different approach to biology, don't take unless you have to.

Fun guy, good sense of humor. But its not enough to keep you coming when you realize he says nothing that isn't already on the slides. No use going to class at all. Memorize the slides as best as you can. Much better than Broadie/Patton last semester.

Great teacher. His notes on OAK are insanely detailed and leave little need to go to class. I went mostly because he does point out select things from the slides that you NEED to know (pathways and such). He's a great guy and tries to make class fun. If you like gary larson humor in context take this class.

Mult. choice quizzes determine almost half of grade. Miss one class means you miss at least one question on the quiz. Miss 1 question means an A-, miss 2 a B-, miss 3 and you have a C. Each question has choices A-H and often asks "Which of the following was NOT discussed in class." Pretty impossible to get right if you didn't write down everything.
awesome professor - great sense of humor makes the material really fun.  his quizzes can be hard, but not impossible if you study. take this class!
Good teacher who keeps it interesting with borderline dirty crude jokes.  tests are tough but I did better on them then 110A tests with patton/broadie
He is a great teacher.  Full of energy and he makes the material very interesting.  The class is hard mainly b/c of the huge amount of material covered.  Review the slides well, and you'll be fine.

Decent material, but INSANELY difficult! Quizzes are mc a-h and ask what was NOT discussed rather than what was. I spent more time on this class than for Econ 232...that's saying a lot. He knows people take the course b/c they have to, not b/c they want to, and so he makes it impossible. I don't want an easy A, just the opportunity to earn one.
THE easiest science class I've taken at Vandy so far--and Dr. Johnson makes it fun.  Pay attention during class, review the slides well, and it won't be hard getting an A on the exams.

You must attend class and take great notes to do well. Maybe even a tape recorder would help. His grading system relies too heavily on 12 question quizzes.  But, he is a great lecturer and manages to make the material interesting.

Like any bio class, there's a ton of reading. Johnson tries to make it fun, though. He brings in neat guest speakers and cracks some jokes. The quizzes need some work. 50% of the grade is 4 ridonculous quizzes, 24% is a 6-page paper, and the final is 26%. No attendance taken, but missing class is GPA suicide. Make sure u get notes for what u miss.

FOR THE LOVE OF GOD STAY AWAY! Hard, hard, hard cple class. Interesting material, but 12-question multiple choice quizzes each have choices a-h on them. Miss 1 question you have an A-, miss 2 B-, miss 3 C, etc. Grade based on 4 hell quizzes, paper, and final. Quizzes quiz you on what you don't know (i.e. Which of the following was NOT discussed?)

Not a bad lecturer for bio, its going to be boring anyway, but his MC quizzes are impossible; they ask what you DON'T know rather than what you DO know, so either go to class every day and read feverishly or stay away.

I took this for Science and the World.  He's a great lecturer, and he brings in really interesting guest speakers.  The quizzes are much harder than I expected though, and there's only 12 questions on each so you can't really miss many and still get a good grade.  Not a bad choice if you need it for a requirement.

Dr. Johnson is an AMAZING professor. He's funny, articulate, and gives and grades fair exams. After haveing taken 110A, his class seemed rather easy. I recommend everyone get a chance to be in his class-he's a great teacher. All his tests come directly from the powerpoint slides.

dunno about 105, but 110B was a piece of cake after 110A. tests aren't bad and lectures are very funny and interesting. def don't want to skip class though, powerpoints are helpful but don't replace notes!
This class is not easy at all.  The questions are very tricky on his quizzes.  If I had to do it all over again, I would not take the class.

really cool and hilarious and nice teacher. teaches really well and is really interesting. the best bio teacher i've had at vanderbilt. test are based on concepts taught in class--pay attention and you'll do fine. Really helpful in review session--will reanswser the question until you understand.
His lectures are very entertaining and hilarious. If you have to take a science class at Vandy take this one. The quizzes are hard, but the curve definitely helps.

Johnson is an awesome Professor. His lectures are really interesting and witty. The quizes can be tricky but are by no means impossible. If you pay attention in class and do the readings you can get a good grade.
The quizzes are entirely too picky and count for basically your entire grade. This is NOT an easy class for CPLE. Look for something else!

Carl Johnson talks and acts like Steve Martin. For a science prof he is clear, easy, and engaging. The guest speakers are amazing. Other posts are right about it being challenging, but it is honestly not that bad, and the workload is pretty light. If you gotta take a science at Vandy take this one.
He's a great guy and this class is really interesting!

Quizzes are hard, and tricky, but graded on a curve.  Study the notes and classpak (textbook isn't tested at all).  Guest lectures were VERY interesting.  You take lots of notes in class, but its very basic, info not difficult.  Would recommend.

UNLESS YOU ARE A SCI MAJOR, DO NOT TAKE THIS CPLE COURSE! The quizzes together are almost 50% of your grade, are incredibly hard, and loaded with trick questions. The paper is really the only lifesaver. Comprehensive final. Graded on a bell curve. Ouch.

His tests were entirely too hard... it was like he was out to get us!  He was also rude because he didn't offer an alternate exam... we had to stay til the VERY last day before we could move out.  The guest speakers were good.
This man is awful.  There is nothing good about this class.  His multiple choice ahs 10 options and the questions are extremely hard to figure what is being asked.
For a science and the world course, it was ok.  Could've been easier and could've been somehow different from General Bio.  I felt like I was in high school again.
Prof Dosser is awesome, he cares about his students and gives very clear grading criteria, assignments were easy to do and he always willing to discuss it with you.
Dr. Dosser is a gem! His class taught me so many life skills, taking his course and he is such a wholesome professor. A legend!
Dosser's the goat. Makes class very enjoyable.
Dosser is incredible. Cannot recommend taking a class with him enough.
greatest professor, highly recommend
Dosser is such a nice professor and super accomodating. Graded on 4 speeches and he grades very leniently. Impossible not to get an A as long as you prepare and try a bit.

Dr. Dosser is an incredible professor. He is so kind and is truly invested in his students' success and what he teaches. I'd recommend taking a class with him a million times over!! One of the best professors I've had at Vandy

Professor Dosser really cares about his students. He never uncomfortably forces students into conversation, but does a great job encouraging student input. One of the friendlier class dynamics I've had at Vandy, and I think it has a lot to do with the environment Prof Dosser creates. Great feedback on assignments. You get what you put in.

Dosser is exactly what a professor ought to be. He cares about the course content AND the students, and he fosters such a welcoming, thought provoking classroom environment. He has only been here for a year and is already much more accessible and invested in students' learning than any other comms prof at Vandy.

Max is the best prof I've had at Vanderbilt. Taken two classes with him and plan on taking two more. Grades are heavily based on effort. If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes, do it!!

TAKE CMST1500 WITH PROFESSOR DOSSER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! he's so nice and cares about students. 4 speeches with an optional final paper. you get to choose topic for each they just have to fit certain requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Dosser is so fabulous!! I'm definitely looking forward to taking more classes with him. He prioritizes learning and student wellbeing over lots of assignments and grades. I got better at public speaking in his class. The speeches get weighted more heavily as you go on so make sure you're implementing his feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Dosser is such a nice guy and an amazing professor!! I was so nervous for public speaking but he makes it so comfortable for everyone. The class is easy and really just graded off speeches (which are graded nicely). Great guy and great class highly recommend!!

easiest A and a super nice guy. Very accessible and will work with you to do well. only have to go on speech days but go to outline day where he will proofread and give feedback needed for an A. Speeches weigh progressively more as the semester goes on so beware. final paper was optional if you needed the points. love Dossie sm.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor for this course and a really nice guy. Grades speeches based upon improvement from the last speech, so don't worry if you are coming in with weak public speaking skills. You are graded on four speeches, ranging in topics, outlines for speeches and reflections afterwards. Approachable and will give feedback before and after speeches
she teaches at FSU calc 3! amazing professor that teaches a pretty difficult class. exams make or break your grade, but just make sure to go to her office hours because shes super helpful

My favorite math prof at Vanderbilt! So accessible outside class via office hours / email, and it was clear she wanted you to succeed. Would explain things so many times if you needed & encouraged you in OH. Tests were difficult, but class is graded on a curve. Really regained my love for math in diff eq w her.

don't let my grade scare you, semester was bad and by all means i should've failed. it's just a super hard class and i was otherwise struggling. i am confident in the right conditions i could've made a solid B with prof Diaz. she is wonderful and so, so helpful. i highly recommend her and ultimately i think she curved and it saved me from failing.
super sweet, very accessible and always willing to help! just an incredibly difficult class and her exams are not easy by any means. practice problems are the best study tool

SO AMAZING! Show up to office hours because there is no professor in the department that cares about her students as much as Rocio does. Do the optional homework and the grade should come, given the class difficulty.

(Math 2400, not 2300). Rocio is a kind, heartwarming professor. But, the class was bizarre. In theory, the concepts aren't that difficult to understand (unlike in 2300 and 1301). Yet it was very hard to do as well as you wanted to. A lot of points taken off over tiny errors, very unpredictable scores, strange final. Most frustrating class I've had.

*MATH 2400
I will say Rocio is a sweet person. But, I did not feel encouraged to succeed in her class, as I felt the work I put in to studying was never enough to actually do how I wanted to on exams. The final was bizarre. She gave no guidance on what to study for for exams, & your entire grade is based on just your exams, quizzes, and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Diaz Martin is super caring and will do her best to help you understand the topics. Class was pretty tough, but she makes it much easier by always being available and answering questions on email or office hours.

Excellent professor! She explained concepts extremely clearly with a good balance of practice problems and explaining the theory behind the formulas so it wasn't pure memorization. Exams are fair and are curved well, as are the final grades. She is very helpful in office hours in clarifying whatever questions arise.

Professor Diaz-Martin is always willing to help on even the simplest concepts and will never judge your accidental brainfarts. She's very good at explaining, and although the tests feel tough most of the time, they are manageable (plus she curves). To do good, you have to practice consistently. Not easy but it's definitely doable for most people

Professor Rocio is one of the best professor i've had here. She gives really nice lectures; and you can always find her after class. She will hold lots of office hours and explain every question carefully. However, every week, she will give homework, quiz, or test. Test questions are more difficult than others but if you work hard, they are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is one of the nicest teachers I have ever had. MATH 2300 is not easy, but she does a great job of explaining difficult concepts. She is super accessible outside of class and makes it clear that she wants to help you. Be prepared for some difficult tests. If you have the opportunity to take her class, take it.

Dr. Rocio Diaz Martin is very caring. She clearly wants all students to succeed. She is very accessible through e-mail, zoom, and office hours. The workload can seem to be a lot (including all optional practice), but it is definitely manageable. However, the exams were very difficult, but there's always a curve on exams, though!

Mutli is very hard. I have never had to work so hard for an A-/A in a math class. The tests are hard and lengthy, and the course is fast-paced, but I LOVE this prof. So genuine, caring, and kind. Will always help. Responds to emails fast with a ton of explanation. I love her. U will learn a TON from her, but be prepared to put in a lot of work.

By far my most difficult class, but Professor was extremely helpful during office hours. She cares greatly about her students, but her tests are definitely difficult and fast-paced. Struggled during this class even with additional office hours, studying, and homework. Overall wonderful prof, just a difficult class.

She really cares about her students and is always willing to answer questions. Office hours are very helpful. The tests are extremely difficult and impossible to finish in the allotted time, but she gives a curve. The material is very difficult. She does many examples in class and overall is a great professor.

Exams are very difficult and seem very long in comparison to how much time you have to take them, but there's always a nice curve that helps out. She sometimes has a hard time explaining complicated concepts, but really cares for her students and wants them to learn. Office hours are very helpful.

She's my favorite professor. The difficulty rating is of the class, not of her; although her exams are very tough, she ensures students still do well by reasonably curving/adding points. She also tries to alleviate the toughness of multi by holding many office hours and responding to emails so fast in great detail. Nicest and sweetest prof I've had

Really difficult class but Professor Diaz-Martin is so so so sweet and caring. It's easy to tell that she prepares for lectures and tries to make it easy to do well (lots of office hours, posts all the notes online, etc). Not a heavy workload, but lots of optional practice problems that help out. Tests are difficult but there's always a curve!

Incredibly sweet and helpful, you can tell she puts the time in towards helping every individual student succeed. Not an easy class by any means but she's super accessible both through office hours and email. A really great math professor

Multi isn't easy, but she does her best to make it better. It's clear she wants us to get high grades! SUPER accessible outside class. She's sooo sweet and funny. Tests are long and difficult but she is fair and curves/gives additional points. 4 midterms, 1 dropped. I really like her. Solid choice for 2300.
Hard to understand lecture style.TA did a lot of the classes.  Exams were difficult. Tons of homework.

Dr. Ravi's lectures were difficult to follow. He missed multiple weeks of class due to work trips (the TAs lead the lecture, but they were difficult to understand). Dr. Ravi gave no flexibility on grading or assignments despite missing class. The exams were very difficult and the homework was long (and due at 10pm which was irritating)
This is for 2205. Class is very difficult conceptually. Cares about students but exams are difficult and lectures hard to follow.
Great professor but terrible exams. Class averages were in the low 70s all semester, no curve and only one small extra credit assignment. TA and him grade out of vengeance
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for Statics and MOM and he cares the most about students actually learning by far. He cares about every student and is equally passionate about the material itself and the students understanding/wellbeing. Most clear teaching style of any professor I've had.

Super nice guy that genuinely wants you to learn. Takes the time to answer questions and make sure students understand with example problems. Homework does take a while but prepares you well for the tests which are pretty reasonable considering the content

Dr. Ravi is a very kind professor who really cares about our learning. He teaches in a variety of styles to work with different learning types. If you do the homework and pay attention in class, the tests are very reasonable.

Ravi is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He genuinely cares about each student and will do so much to help you succeed. He makes a lot of dorky jokes in class and maintains a very low-stress, laid-back, friendly atmosphere. He says he wants to be your statics "coach", not your teacher, and I think he embodies that really well.

Best professor I've had. I normally end up teaching myself the material in class, but I actually feel engaged when I am in Dr. Ravi's class. If you show up to class and pay attention you'll get a good grade. He's also the boy.

Great choice for Statics. He really really cares for his students and will help you as much as he can if you reach out to him. Lectures are important to attend. Tests are actually very fair and are similar to questions from homework/class problems/practice exams. Funny in class and teaches well. Put in effort and you will do well.

Dr. Ravi is a great choice for statics: he clearly cares about the student's learning and well-being, and his jokes and demonstrations made (in-person) lecture entertaining. As long as you put effort into this class all semester, you should be good.

Dry material, lectures don't make up for it. Duddu goes from very clear to bumbling later in the semester. Learning from the (lots of) homework helpful and a must. Tests fair but a time crunch and nitpicked for deductions. Two projects that feel pointless and unnecessarily difficult. Overall a slog, but Duddu genuinely cares and has some good jokes

I had him for statics and his classes were always enjoyable. Despite having him early in the morning he was engaging enough to keep me paying attention and he does a great job breaking down concepts and presenting them in an understandable manor.

Prof. Duddus lectures are solid. He has a pretty good mix of theory and solving problems. Sometimes he can get confused when someone asks him a question, but otherwise is very good at communicating his expectations and what you need to know. He has several group projects. His tests arent hard, but time can be an issue. Overall great guy.

Professor Lewis is the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. He cares about his students and wants us to succeed. He is always open during office hours, engaging in lectures, and there is no homework. Your grade is made up of 3 tests and a project, but he gives you a clear study guide of exactly what is on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lewis is great! Most of the learning will come from writing memos and case studies, but the lectures are helpful in preparing you for your major assignments. Grading is a bit harsh, but if you take advantage of office hours, you should do fine. There are also plenty of extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good lectures and very clear study guides for tests. Assigns lots of readings, but honestly it is worth your time to focus on in-class material and the study guides more.

You will learn in this class -- Lewis is a fantastic teacher and really cares. He will know everyone's name and face in a week. He applies the class to the real world and does case studies. That said, I wrote 9 pages for tests and got 3 words of feedback and averaged a B. This class is just not worth the grading scale.

Prof. Lewis is the best lecturer! I learned so much from his class. He always makes new presentation slides each class (never uses old ones). I truly admire his compassion, understanding, and respect. His class is very engaging and people never get bored.

Take at least one of his classes while you're at Vandy. It's a life-changing experience!

Professor Lewis is great, very kind and knowledgeable. His TAs grade everything and are quite harsh and provide little to no feedback. I learned a lot in this class but be prepared to read a lot. Two midterms, an essay, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lewis was a strong and engaging professor who I learned a lot from, but the class was poorly organized in my opinion. Felt rushed at the end with writing and is very hard to get an A. Heavy readings but can usually get away with skimming, and pretty much all grading is writing. Interesting class but not an easy A by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The most caring professor—his lectures are fascinating, and you'll learn so much! However, he's the toughest grader ever. Once you figure out what he looks for, you can earn high scores, but it still takes serious prep and effort. Totally worth it if you want to be challenged and grow!

His lecture is the best I have ever experienced! He is so knowledgeable and accessible outside class. Although you have to read a lot, it's worth it. You will learn so much from this professor. His grading is fair; if you work hard, grade won't disappoint you. He's a very humble person despite all the reputations, titles, and papers he published.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really kind and smart guy but it is true that he is a really tough grader. I wish he would've given more feedback on how to get more points. Definitely not an easy class, but came out of it realizing I actually learned a lot, and he is funny. Lectures are boring sometimes. Got by with dumping my lecture and review session notes into the exams.

Thought professors were supposed to lift students up and support them??  Not this professor!  If you are a hard working student RUN!!!  you will never be graded fairly.  All your hard work will get you a B- if lucky!  The most arrogant and uncaring professor I have ever had!!!!

If you take this professor you will
Watch all your hard work and your grade washed down the drain!!!  DO NOT take this professor he doesnt care about his students at all even if you work hard !!  Unfair grader,  see your gpa plummet.  Impossible to do well!  And not a nice guy.

Professor Lewis is one of the best professors and people I have ever met. He is well-respected by everyone that takes his class. He gives great, informative lectures and students are well-prepared to do well in the class. He is a tougher grader than most, but it is worth it to feel like you actually earned the work and learned in the class. 10/10

Professor Lewis is amazing and genuinely cares about each of his students. This class is pretty easy as long as you attend class and thoroughly complete the review sheets, which he will help you with in office hours. Two midterms, a paper, and a final. Highly recommend any class with Professor Lewis!

Prof. Lewis is a fantastic lecturer and super passionate about students' learning. Exams are entirely free response and his essay grading can be tedious, but prepare thoroughly and you will be fine. Great introduction to American politics for aspiring PSCI/PPS majors. Memorized everyone's names by the first day of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lewis is awesome, very simple material. Make sure to show up if you want an A, but the rest of your grade relies on a paper and the three exams, which are very easy. 10/10 would recommend

Prof. Lewis was so engaging and truly cared about his students. He learned everyones names and always made and effort to get to know us. His lectures are super engaging too. There aren't many grades for this class, so work hard on the things you get, but overall he grades fairly and gives you every resource you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at Vanderbilt and by far the teacher I have learned the most with. Lectures are engaging and actually interesting. There is reading, but you don't have to do all of it to understand it for class (read the conclusions and you'll be fine). He genuinely cares about his students and gives extra credit. A 92.5 is an A also.

Professor Lewis is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. His lectures are very interesting and interactive. He engages and challenges students. He also has memorized everyone's name on the first day which is so great. He is a tough grader but makes his expectations known from day one. Get to know him, go to office hours and you'll be great!

Professor Lewis is one of the best teachers I've had at Vanderbilt. He's fantastically caring, knowledgable, and invested into students' success. With that said, he's also by far the hardest grader I've seen. I do recommend this class, but don't say you weren't warned.

Professor Lewis is an incredibly kind professor and always willing to help. If you are genuinely passionate about poli sci and want to improve your writing then take his class. Test questions are selected from a list given before. He is a tough grader which is the only reason people rank him lower but he is an amazing professor.

Do NOT take this prof. The grading is completely arbitrary and nitpicky- they grade tough just to be tough. You will find your A-quality work is getting B's. Unclear criteria and he is shameless about it. He reminds me of a politician- smug, charismatic, but also underhanded. I have never experienced such arbitrary grading policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Maybe I had a bad TA this semester but this class was miserable. Though the material/lectures are interesting, the memos are ridiculous. They seem easy enough at first, but the grading makes it impossible to succeed. Very unclear criteria and feedback is usually too vague to actually help you improve. Avoid this professor if you value your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Does not care about his students at all. Tried to get help from him but was not open to helping me. Would not take again- beware.

This is my second semester with Professor Lewis and he is definitely one of the hardest professors (grading-wise) I've had. He's also absolutely phenomenal and he really knows his stuff. If he was teaching another class I haven't already taken with him I'd absolutely take him again! One of the toughest professors I've had but also one of the best!

Super nice guy, really accessible. However, class was difficult because of his high standards and criteria looked for on exams. All assessments were writing based and a ton of reading was required. Lectures were usually interesting but at times material could be dry and it was difficult to pay attention. Would take Lewis again but barely.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough class, especially the memos. He has high standards, but he's super helpful during office hours, and he's extremely knowledgeable about public admin. Really nice guy too. Highly recommend if you're thinking about working in government (or any other organization, honestly).

Professor Lewis is super nice and caring and definitely encourages you to meet with him during office hours. However, his lectures were incredibly dry and it was very easy to lose focus. You have to read a lot in the textbook, which is also very boring and long. He looks for very specific things to be included in test answers.

I learned so much in this class, but be prepared to read 100+ pages every week! Professor Lewis is so knowledgeable, approachable, and helpful for any assignment/test. But if you want to do well, you must interact with him and do as much work as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lewis' lectures are very engaging; he does a great job of breaking down concepts in an easy to understand way. Many test questions come directly from lecture slides, so definitely attend. Most grading is done by TAs, so things can get dicey (only reason for 4 stars; sometimes, feedback didn't even relate to my essays). Great teacher though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Lewis is a great lecturer, and I learned more in his class than any other class I've taken at Vanderbilt. However, if you are looking for an easy A, this is not the class for you. The TAs graded all of the tests and quizzes with unreasonable and ambiguous expectations. Overall, great content, but too tough for an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Lewis is very approachable and a great lecturer however, the harsh grading by the TA's in a 1000 level class makes this a course one to avoid at all costs. Nearly impossible to overcome the grading which is ambiguous and unfair at best. Too bad, as this should have been a class to celebrate Professor Lewis and his immense knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He has very high standards. It's a tough class, but his lectures are unbeatable, and he's a really nice, approachable guy. I might have learned more from this class than the rest of my classes this semester combined. If you're really into politics, you'll enjoy the class a lot and learn a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unless you need to take his class for credit, I suggest looking at other professors for an easier time. Prof. Lewis and the TAs have a high standard in terms of grading and it is not fun on the other end - especially for an intro class. He is a good person to talk to however.

Professor Lewis is a good professor, but the class was really difficult in terms of quizzes and exams that make up the class grade. Not only were the exams hard and full free response (no multiple choice), the grading was very harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lewis's lectures were in depth and interesting. I enjoyed his in-class activities during a mostly online semester. The midterms and quizzes were graded harshly and on details not always covered in class/textbook, requires a large understanding of all material. Lewis is funny and kind, would recommend for polysci majors but not really non-majors
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Lewis is by far my favorite professor I've had so far at Vanderbilt. The first day of class, he had memorized every single person's name from Brightspace! He genuinely cares about his students so so much. I also learned so much and the class made me want to pursue public administration. Would highly recommend.

Professor Lewis is an amazing professor who really knows about what he teaches. You can tell he cares about making sure his students are learning, and although the class is relatively difficult, that should not dissuade you from taking it. I learned more in this class than in any other class I took that semester.

Prof Lewis is one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He wants to make sure students learn material, not just memorize it, so get ready to work to receive an A. He is incredibly caring and is more than willing to talk to students outside of class. Also, be prepared to talk. Participation is 10% of your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If your goal is to learn from the best professors (and it should be), Professor Lewis's class shouldn't be missed. He makes you work hard (A's are rare in his classes), but he makes a point of being welcoming and accessible outside of the classroom. He pushed me to learn and improve this semester and was always willing to listen to my questions.

Probably the best professor I've ever had pushed me to think extremely critically and to constantly question if my answer was as good as it could be, but I learned a ton and a new way of thinking. Super interesting lectures and you gotta put a lot of effort in, but an overall great class experience

Professor Lewis is absolutely incredible--he's clear and his lectures are incredible interesting for American Presidency. Definitely a hard class and you're going to put in a lot of work, but I loved having him and would highly recommend.

Not taking a class with Professor Lewis is a huge mistake. He is a very tough grader, but fair. You can do well if you do the work. Lewis knows more about the presidency and politics than anyone and his lectures are clear and engaging. He is incredibly helpful in office hours and cares a lot about his students. By far my favorite class/professor.

Lewis is extremely clear during lectures. His class was enjoyable and fun each and every time, and he went above and beyond to create relationships with students, allowing for multiple extra credit sessions at his house. Grading was very difficult - expect A work to get a B+, B+ work to get a B-, etc. But, it's not impossible, and it's worth it.

Professor Lewis is a great professor and knows EVERYTHING about public policy. He is very helpful inside and outside of class. Pretty hard grader though. Take advantage of his expertise in writing papers. Great professor, recommended to hard workers.

Hard class, due to the fact that Lewis is a beast of a political science professor. Readings are long and technical, though you don't have to do all of them. Participation is key, and except for the 100 level courses, he'll know everyone's name in the class so he knows if you skip often and your grade will reflect that.  Fascinating guy though.
Professor Lewis is awesome. His lectures are clear and interesting, and he is very helpful outside of class.  He isn't an easy grader, but he is definitely fair if you put the time in.

He is the best professor I have ever had. He cares about his students and is super helpful. He is really passionate about the subject matter and, although he is not the easiest, he is no super rigorous as far as grading goes. You will have missed out if you do not take a class of his in your college career.

Take this class if you LOVE participation. I went to class almost every section and participated fairly regularly only to receive a 15/50 on my participation grade. After speaking to every other person I know in the class (about 10 people), this was no irregularity (everyone i spoke to got either a 10 or 15 of 50). Interesting class but very tough.

Professor Lewis is a wonderful resource to Vanderbilt. The 255 class is challenging, but incredibly helpful because he asks you to pretend like your're a consultant. Great class. Even better professor.

Challenging but very rewarding class. David Lewis is clearly passionate about the material, and his lectures are very engaging. Quizzes are open-note, papers are difficult, but as long as you don't start last minute you'll be fine.

He doesn't cover the secondary readings in class, but you can ignore them for the easy tests. The difficulty comes from the two papers you have to write; his standards are extremely high. Politically, he is absolutely neutral in class. This was the best-taught, most interesting class I've taken here, but also my lowest grade. Take it P/NP.

basic psci 100. Rough professor though. doesn't cover the immense amount of reading during class and expects you to know all of it. 1 of the top 2 toughest professor in the PSCI department. I'd recommend taking it with someone else.

CS3891 is possibly the most pointless class ever. Teaching is last on Hyde's priorities. He is often late and never prepared to lecture. The midterm was remarkably unrelated to class content. He normalizes grades opaquely at the end of the class, so you have no idea what grade you'll end up with. He is inconsistent with responding to emails, too.

This is for CS 3255. Hyde was a nice and funny guy, however lectures were dry and the class incredibly unorganized. He randomly cancelled at least 5 classes and hw was 50% of our grade but only were assigned 2 real hw assignments. I have no idea how this class ended up in the CS department its all math and studying for the exams was a mess.
He is good at motivating the story behind math. The lecture might seem dry. Wished he used a blackboard more when explaining things.
Love the side story or motivation part before each lecture. Great professor. The exams are a little tough, but he curves them.

Your entire grade in this class is based on a final project and a random assignment depending on if the professor feels like adding one. There is no concrete breakdown of your grade and he is incredibly unresponsive outside of the class. Do not expect a breakdown of any of your grades.

the course i took wasn't on here but he was very boring teacher. just stands at podium and lectures all day and that's about it. i saw people falling asleep in his class just because it was that boring.
I felt like his class was a social experiment and not the kind you want to be a part of. Kinda like squid game only your grades are on the line.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super flexible given COVID and was really nice to talk to during office hours. Main problems with the class stem from Vandy Algos itself (bad pacing, expects students to have prior knowledge, etc.) but David did a great job.

I loved Dr. Levin's class! He is super passionate about the content he teaches and his lectures are captivating. It is a lot of work--for exams be prepared to memorize a lot of information and the final project takes time. However, it is totally doable to get an A if you put in effort. You also don't need to do the textbook and he is accessible.

Worst class I have ever taken in my life. The fact that this course is offered at Vanderbilt is offensive – and he is 99% of the issue. His tests are easy, and the grading is impossible. He has expectations that are unreasonable such as grading down for not writing something that was not even asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can actually learn a lot from Prof Levin's class. He will place some test questions on PPT, just make sure you read them. He will hold review sessions before tests, super helpful. Just get ready to read and focus in class, as lectures only cover a part of readings and will go beyond reading, but exams will test you on both lectures and readings

The lecture slides cannot be understood. He takes attendance and marks whoever speaks. Grades are never updated, so you basically never know your grades. He's accessable outside of class, but not helpful.
PowerPoints were extremely difficult to follow. There was never a rubric provided. He doesn't share his PowerPoint presentations online. When you ask the TAs they never know what's going on either.
im sorry but this is a test
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of reading for this class. His lectures were interesting but did not cover all of the reading. Tests were sometimes weirdly specific and assignment's were vague. However the content was enjoyable and as long as you do all the reading/take notes you'll be fine. Final exam was open note and he sends out possible essay questions for all tests

PSYPC 2200 - Psychology of Thinking

This class was awful. Professor Levin is a harsh grader with vague expectations, and the TA grades just as tough. Feedback is minimal, and exams feel designed to confuse rather than assess understanding. The unclear guidelines and extreme grading make this course unnecessarily stressful. Avoid if possible!

PSY-PC 2200; One of my hardest non-stem classes. Do-able but I needed 1-3 days to dedicate to studying for the exams (I'd read the textbook+take note of all the studies & go to his review sessions and got As on them) & you won't get most grades back until the end of the semester. He's also difficult to reach outside of class & feedback is minimal

Interesting stuff to learn, however is is a very tough grader and it is hard to know what he is looking for. There are no helpful clear guidelines. He does seem passionate about his research, but not about his teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: (for PSYPC2200) energetic lecturer, but horrible about giving resources and clear guidelines to students. Not willing to give clear feedback on exams, cared more about catering to himself getting through the curriculum than catering to the students (not very well organized, would often teach content until the class before the exam)

Dr. Levin is a great lecturer, especially on topics that he's interested in, but tests are difficult and grading criteria for projects/papers are unclear. I've taken several psych classes prior to this course, so I had previous exposure to many of the topics covered. If this is your 1st introduction to psych, lectures may move too quickly for you.

Levin is a solid lecturer and cares about his students, but this class is so much harder than it should be. He assigns a lot of textbook reading and expects you to know every detail of it. His grading criteria for tests and projects is very unclear, yet he has specific expectations that he doesn't tell you about. He is a cool guy and loves psych.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Levin has a nice charm in his lectures and gets really excited which makes the topics seem interesting. However, outside the lectures, tons of reading for every class, tests weighed rly heavily based on niche textbook concepts, pretty harsh grading, hours of studying for tests. Final was open note tho W. Nice guy, but getting an A is rly tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is my rating for my second course with him this semester, I had very similar experiences with respect to being unreachable outside of class and having unclear grading criteria. No concrete rubric/description for any assignment, but it would be revealed later that he had very specific targets he expected you to know had to be included.

His grading criteria is very unclear and very harsh. He selects very niche questions to be worth many points on the exams; class averages have been low for every exam. He does not answer emails. I have perceived him to be rude and condescending in the times I have managed to track him down.

The workload and schedule aren't very reasonable. He expects a lot from students but doesn't cover all of the material in class, so he claims that you can ask him questions outside of class, but you can hardly reach him then. He relies heavily on lectures, but to me, his teaching isn't very clear. Don't take his class if you have other options.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS CLASS! He gives lectures that are engaging. However, he grades exams unclearly, forcing you to reach out to him. He does not explain his feedback well. Additionally, for the "projects," he doesn't provide adequate guidelines. For the amount of work I put in this class, the grades I've received so far aren't equivalent. I'm done.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Unlike a lot of other students on this page, I actually really enjoyed taking Levin's class. I think his lectures are quite interesting, and he uses lots of real world and hands on examples to help students understand content. The tests are difficult for sure, but it is very possible to get an A if you are willing to put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He grades his tests very very harshly and with a large degree of specificity, even though about 80% of test questions is content not covered in class. The expectation is to truly remember every statistic, sentence, etc from about 400 pages of reading for every exam. The class could've been grade if he had more realistic grading methods.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a decent lecturer but he is incredibly specific and harsh when it comes to grading. This would be acceptable if he gave us clear expectations or actually answered emails/showed up to his office hours, but unfortunately he does not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Levin is very passionate about psych and cares about his students. However, he lectures on a small portion of the unit, but he assigns textbook readings each night and anything is fair game for the exams - even things he never mentioned in class. You never know what he is going to ask on exams and the class is more stressful than it should be.

Dr.Levin is a captivating lecturer and weaves connections between the concepts. Reading the textbook is a must for tests (and engaging in the lecture better). Some might say it's too much lecture sometimes but it also depends on how much attention you're giving to him. Overall a great introductory class to the Cognitive Studies major and psychology
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TA grades the exams and she was a very tough grader. Lectures are very boring and unorganized. Half the time the students have no idea what he's talking about. Really interesting material but this class just made me lose interest in psych completely.

Very kind professor, you can tell he really wants his students to succeed and to know all the resources available to them. Definitely a little tricky for an intro course, but he brings a fresh perspective on topics that isn't present in typical psychology courses, making it interesting. Pay attention in class and put in effort and you'll be fine.

I took this class as a junior and felt like I already knew most of the content from upper-level courses. Yet, Dr. Levin taught the material in a way that was totally refreshing and relevant. He has a great respect for students and always welcomes discussion in-class. 3/5 difficulty but just because he has you do a lot (e.g. two projects).

Prof Levin is a great lecturer. Those navy blue slides haunt me a little, especially the ones that have pictures only, but everything on the test is discussed in lectures. The paper are graded easily. Would recommend but gotta put in the work.

Very engaging lecturer. His passion for his work and the whole field of psychology are really evident, and it made the class more engaging and one of my favorites to attend. If you do the recommended readings and take notes, it's pretty easy.

The class itself isn't terrible, he lectures for 75 min and you just sit there and take notes. He's definitely a bit quirky and tries to keep it interesting which is good, but the grading is very critical. I'm pretty sure most of the grading is done by the TA but still, some of the things they doc points for are unreasonable

Dr. Levin is a very kind and approachable professor and he does his best to make the lectures engaging. Overall the class is not very hard. There are plenty of opportunities to make up for poor exam scores (participation, attendance, extra credit research opportunities, other projects) and simply paying attention during lectures goes a long way.

Levin is such a sweet guy and really clear on what we need to know for exams. If you go to lecture, take notes, and go over the specific textbook topics he mentions, you will be fine. Midterm research project and final project are graded pretty easily and exams are fine if you put in decent effort. Not necessarily an easy A but definitely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Levin's class is a great introductory Psychology course. We covered the basics of introductory psychology thoroughly. However, this class had a bit of an applied psychology aspect, which made it all the more interesting. Overall, this was an excellent course that did not strain students.
class is easy and he's a fair grader but lectures were SO boring, especially over zoom.
An extremely caring guy and super passionate about psychology. His lectures can be hard to follow, but the tests given are extremely fair.

I really enjoyed his class, expectations were pretty unclear but tests were straightforward and if you just pay the barest amount of attention you'll get an A on all exams. Really boring lectures but a kind person

Dr. Levin was more organized than I expected going into the class. He is very knowlegeable about the field and exams and grading is ridiculously easy. The only work I put into this class was a few hours of studying before each exam.

You can absolutely tell that Prof. Levin loves his subject, that is clear. However, it can be difficult to pay attention. Stricter than you would expect grader, unclear expectations especially. Not an easy A, must put in significant effort to do well.

Nice guy but really dull lectures. Really disorganized class. Assigns a ton of reading but likes to pull a lot of test questions from lectures. Tests aren't bad, a couple easy projects that he doesn't grade very harshly, final is open notes. Take notes during the semester and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Levin's class. He is SO passionate about what he is teaching and you can tell that he enjoys being in class. It can get dry/boring at times, but overall, I am doing well in his class and feel as though tests cover the material we have learned in class. Read the book if you can because it is super helpful for tests

Prof Levin is really engaging during his lectures (one of my favorite profs so far). Most of his test questions come from lecture, but they're always engaging and the material covered is legitimately interesting so it's okay.
Prof Levin is a great lecturer and he cares about teaching, but the tests are pretty tough. I enjoyed the class, but it was a lot of work.  The material is interesting and he teaches it well though.
Really boring professor. Tests are moderately hard, but the final is open-note. Attendance is optional, and you can get most of the information for the tests from the book.
More interested in research than teaching. Has no interest in his students and makes no effort to help,
difficult class but he is very interested in his field and knows what hes talking about. not easy to understand, tests extremely hard, had to drop the class not very helpful when struggling

Nice guy and he tries to make class interesting, but none of that maters because the tests are so difficult. He is hard to get in touch with as he doesn't answer his emails. Find another professor and make your life easier

I really like Prof. Levin. Yes, it takes forever to get grades back, but he grades fairly for the most part. He is passionate about the field, and that passion translates into effective and interesting lectures. He is approachable and appreciates class contributions.

He is a really nice guy and you can tell he tries hard to keep class interesting. I don't think the tests are too hard, but he is very slow at giving grades back. I never read the text book and still got A's on the tests. This class made me want to be a psych major!

Nice guy, passionate about research, but not a good teacher for a psych class such as this.  The tests are difficult (half straight from text book/ half short answer and essay).  The written assignments are not difficult but he grades them for too hard.  This class was supposed to be an overview, but he didn't give us that.

He is more interested in his research than teaching, & he approached his class that way -- something that isn't wise in a freshman seminar. He rarely explained assignments & when he did, they rarely made sense. His TA did all the grading, but none of it was according to what he had told us to do. I learned little psychology & was bored all semester
Fantastic course, up to date lectures, great class discussions
Four amazing weeks in China with inspiring lectures as well as super insightful visits to research labs and companies. Highly recommended!
Amazing Maymester in China
Easy to reach after class and during office hours; he gave good feedback on my assignments.

3 quizzes (25 mcq and 3 EC) and 2 presentations. Quizzes are relatively simple if you go to class, but way more specific on the readings than expected. Presentations are only 2 mins, so they were easy to prep for. He was unclear about the projects, but graded nicely. Lectures can be boring, but he's a rly sweet guy who cares about the topic a lot.
Awesome readings and great in-class discussions; many extra credit opportunities with hands-on stuff like flying a LiDAR drone.
Amazing class with up-to-date readings and in-class discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Eberl is a fantastic professor who cares deeply about the topic that he is teaching and is a very engaging lecturer. I appreciate that he presents very balanced views surrounding the topic of AI and he gives you opportunities to learn more about the work he is doing. The class is graded by few things, but just read and stay engaged in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of readings required for this class, and participation is mandatory. Sometimes class gets a bit boring. However, he is a genuinely nice guy who is very interested in the material, and he does a good job of getting the students interested as well.

Readings are very long and dense. Class is all discussion-based, participation is like 1/3 of the grade. He is knowledgeable and passionate but boring. I honestly barely understood what was going on in this class. Assignment instructions are vague but he's a really easy grader, can get an A if you make an effort, even if you don't understand things
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely knows what he is talking but not my favorite grader. There was no final exam or paper though which is great. Grading is based on three papers, one presentation, and participation. Participation is loose he definitely has his few favorites. Lectures are boring.

Very chill class- discussion, participation, and 1 term paper. The topic "human landscapes" is very broad and topics of discussion often felt a bit vague. I think the class could have used a little bit more structure, but overall a very easy AXLE option.

Markus is probably one of the most interesting professors on campus. He has literally written the book on Mayan anthropology. Every lecture feels like a Ted Talk. In terms of class work, there were 5 assignments and one course-long paper that was only like 8 pages long. As long as you attended the lectures, the assignments were do-able--start early

The class was called AI and Material Culture and we were tasked with coming up with our own assignments... As you can imagine, it was a very easy class but I actually learned a lot about AI and I gained a ton of practice using AI and ChatGPT in different contexts. Attendance not at all mandatory and he's passionate about what he teaches.

Dr. Eberl is super passionate about Maya glyphs, and his excitement made the class a lot more enjoyable. Super interesting content, but towards the end, it was definitely over my head. The homework exercises were difficult but doable, especially if you started early. Be sure to discuss your thesis for the final paper w/ him to make sure it's good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Eberl mostly, but towards the end he began expecting us to decipher hieroglyphic texts and the events shown. I was actually losing my mind!!!!!!!!! The glyphs didn't appear in the catalogue he gave us, which is basically the only resource we have to decipher glyphs. When I asked him questions, he wasn't very helpful, so I was on my own.

I took this class for immersion, and it was definitely an easy and fun way to fill the requirement. Prof Eberl was understanding of students' circumstances and his lectures were easy to engage in. The readings were interesting, but it was easy to get through class lectures/discussions without doing them all.

You can tell how much Prof Eberl cares about the subject he teaches, but I will say the lectures were extremely boring. He's definitely a good professor but the class was rarely engaged and usually very few people showed up even though there's an attendance code for each class. But, very nice and understanding guy.

Very quiz heavy class. Take notes when you go to class and study the PowerPoints. He has a few activities but they barely count towards anything, and one essay. Overall though really enjoyed the class.

Such a boring class. Only took this for the writing credit, but class is so painfully boring. He has no clear grading criteria for anything, so you just have to guess what to get a decent grade to be honest. I participated in class a lot but still got mediocre grades for participation. The guy doesn't really know how to keep track of anything.

Found Dr. Eberl's lectures interesting for someone who knew nothing about archaeology before taking the class. Incorporated lots of cool field studies. Tests were kinda tricky, with very specific questions and multiple answers that seemed to be correct. Prompts for essays were very vague, and there seemed to be inconsistent grading among TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing lecture with super interesting topics
Super nice; helps a lot; many extra credit options

Prof Eberl is definitely passionate about archaeology and incorporates a lot of class activities into the lectures. No homework and gave extra credit. Grading is done by TA's, and some TA's grade way harsher than others. Easy to do well on essays but tests can be tricky. Low level of time commitment and you will learn about an interesting subject.

Do not take this class if you are not interested in archeology. It gets really hard to engage in the material if you are not interested. Professor doesn't give clear grading criteria so it's hard to write papers. Grading depends on your TA but is also harsh regardless & exams are time crunched, which doesn't help. Avoid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Eberl is very knowledgable, but relies on his own research. The course content is fine and the lectures are what you would expect, but the criteria for papers isn't very clear. Don't expect to ever feel prepared going into an exam, even if you reread/rewatch all content. He'll say the exams are conceptual but they're all memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Eberl loves his subject matter and it is very inspiring. However, his lectures are VERY dry. My biggest issue is that his grading is VERY HARSH. I memorized HIS OWN definition of a term and when I used/rephrased it on the exam when asked, I still got docked points. This proves to me that he grades hard just to grade hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Eberl is a great professor. Very reasonable workload, lots of class discussion time, and clear grading.
Dr. Eberl is a great professor. His class was mostly discussion-centered and very interesting. He brings in plenty of examples. Readings are assigned, but not the center of the class.

Professor Eberl is a really great guy who is really passionate about the subject of Maya Hieroglyphics. He goes very much in depth into the topic and I learned a ton about the calendar, verbs, and nouns of the ancient Maya language. However, his lectures are dry and his exercises difficult. Hard to stay involved in the end but loved him!
This course had amazing class discussion; everybody participated. It was fun jsut to come to class. Fantastic teacher!
Extremely responsive to email. The exercises he gives are like riddles. Very rewarding when you crack them.

Maya glyphs are a really interesting writing system and this class gave me a great introduction. Many handouts and in-class exercises. No tests but take-home exercises (some of them are actually fun).
Fantastic discussions in class; instructor makes even boring abstract topics interesting. I highly recommend it!
Super fascinating class on communities, both in the past and in the present. Great in-class discussions -- prof has great topics, often from recent news
Amazing class with tons of hands-on exercises like making your own ceramic vessel. Fun lectures with lots of examples. Great and helpful guy.
friendly atmosphere; makes readings interesting; helps with papers; quizzes keep you on track
great professor for a dull but required class; great class discussion; textbook is good (read the clarifying notes!) but you need to read. Nice guy, very approachable & responds quickly to e-mails

It's a required course and pretty abstract (theories of culture!) but the professor does a great job of explaining concepts and applying them to real examples. You have to read to keep up but it's worth it. Great class discussions
Great textbook - chapters are not too long; prof does a great job explaining the text in his lectures & adds lots of his own research
Very helpful and always available during office hours and by e-mail. great lectures

Erratic midterms, easy essays, useless/sleep-inducing lectures. Must attend to get the participation points which I anticipate will be the difference between an A and a B+ for people who actually try in the class. Worst thing to English major me, he doesn't seem to actually know Greek or Egyptian mythology at all. Mayan is his field of expertise.

I don't know what the first person was talking about, this is the most boring class I've taken at Vandy. I just took it to fulfill some credit and completely regret it. The questions on the exams are all over the place and the little "easy" tests each week are impossible to get 100% unless you read the book thoroughly. Avoid this if you can.

"Easy" B+ class if you attend for the participation points, but good luck staying away during lectures. Test/quiz difficulty varies drastically: I got a 100 on the first midterm and an 81 on the second. Over the semester, his questions become increasingly vague; at times it's very apparent that English isn't his native tongue.

never failed to greet and thank us (150+) for coming to class. knows his stuff only criticism is his reliance on HIS research. he compares everything to his work even though the books give examples that he doesn't always reference in class but will feature on a quiz. exams a breeze, field trips are fun, and his pleasantness is absolutely infectious
Informative course, I wrote some poems I'm really proud of. Detailed feedback from the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The sweetest professor I've ever had, she made our class engaging and informative! She gives amazing feedback for your poems and is so easy to talk to. 10/10 would recommend taking her class!!!!!!

Very passionate about teaching. Always ready to get our class going and goes the extra mile to help us become better writers and better people. Would 100% take any of her classes if I ever got the opportunity to again.
Such a fun and stress-free semester learning about and writing poetry. I walked out of our last class feeling like I was in Dead Poet's Society.
She is the best professor ever, cares so much about her students, super relatable, makes writing poetry fun (coming from a stem student), super easy class and best HCA credit out there
I just took the LSAT and thought about this class! Very useful knowledge and skills, very thankful!

I don't know where these angry freshman comments are coming from. I took Engelman's ethics course and loved it. The tests hard but I learned a ton. I still think about the abortion essay we read. Really fun and impactful class.

Prof Engelman is generally nice, but he just lectures on the chalkboard. During office hours, it was always a circular conversation of him not explaining anything. You have to understand the readings before you get to class. He is not flexible with extra credit or test corrections. Vanderbilt also just has no resources for logic. AVOID THIS CLASS.

I don't agree with the negative reviews... Prof Engelman is chill and accessible in class, and the lectures made the material easier to digest. He definitely challenges you with the exams and stuff but you get lots of feedback and room for mistakes. I'm not that mathy but I enjoyed the class a lot!

I'd really avoid taking Engelman. He's always on a crazy power trip. He's generally nice but unbelievably sarcastic and rude sometimes. Grading on the final was unbelievably harsh for a 20 point essay that he made seem was easy.

Engelman was often very passive-aggressive, political, and rude to his students. Unforgiving, and an extremely hard grader on the final, despite submitting solid work (many impressive students were given Ds). Fine if you put in work, but beware.

Professor Engelman is funny in class and very accessible during office hours. Assignments are just reading the textbook, which is lowkey optional since its a lecture-based class going over the textbook stuff. Grade is based on 110 and you only have to get 93 to get an A. Plenty of room for mistakes. Would recommend.

Super approachable. He replies to emails quickly and is always there, even if you are spamming him with your emails. He genuinely wishes to help his students improve at writing, and his feedbacks are very valuable. Robert's lectures are very engaging and fun, thanks to his energy and enthusiasm for philosophy and teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Robert does not know how to teach. Absolutely saturated with unbearable lectures to the point where students were falling asleep every single class. Unclear expectations for exams, poor directions, harsh and sarcastic when answering questions, and entirely inaccessible in that he requires handwritten notes (no tech allowed). Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You will likely never actually see Dr. G in the lab and will mainly be interacting with the TA. Aside from that, the in-lab assignments were really easy, but very tedious.

Took Prof. Grundstrom for core 1010, never want to take a class with her again. Very tough grader, lots of reading, and annoying about participation. My favorite class of the semester was the one we had a substitute teacher.

Dr. Gs incredibly nice and cares about her students, especially nonSTEM majors but made this class much harder than it needs to be. Right when you think it's easy, you realize you need to do endless reading since the lectures are all over the place. Tests became super hard, with mean being a 73 for one, but lots of extra credit which is generous.

Dr. G is so passionate about astro & willing to help! But, her class was like a middle school class. Lots of busy work & writing assignments. Exams have very random questions but she offers test rebates to get points back. lectures are useless and you have to read the textbook. lecture tutorials would be helpful if she provided an answer key.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Very chill professor, and is accessible outside of class. Probably one of the easier lab courses to take. Only issue is that it is at night.

Super easy lab, only downside is its at night. Made astro1010 lecture much easier to understand and succeed in. If you focus & grind you can get out an hour early most weeks. Dr. G is great, answers any and every question super helpful. Minimal work outside of lab, maybe 2 hours total all semester.

She's awesome, depending on your lab time, you might rarely see her and just be w a TA. You have to buy the lab manual and it's pretty easy even if it seems like the questions are trying to trick you. You have 3 big grades, in addition the weekly lab which are fairly easy to do.

This is my second class with her. It was a relatively easy A. Just put in the work by reading and studying a little before exams. She allows test rebates if you don't do amazing. Stay on top of her small busy work assignments and you will get a good grade but it can be pretty annoying if you don't format it correct. The work can be tedious.

Dr G is my favorite professor I've had at Vandy! She is kind, funny, and always willing to answer any question or explain any topic. It was annoying to have to show up and sit in a computer lab for ~3 hours/week, but for a lab that's kind of expected + I ended up leaving 1/2 hour early most weeks. Easy A as long as you show up

Dr. G is amazing at teaching astronomy. Only complaint was about the class itself. I would not have taken this class if I knew it'd be in a computer lab 7-9:30 PM and we wouldn't get to go stargazing that often. We always got out early by 9:30 instead of scheduled 10:30. Dr. G. gave us all the answers though, so easy A if you show up. Easiest lab.

This lab was the easiest class/lab at vandy for me. You would never do work for this class outside of class, and yes, 3+ hrs every week does sound like hassle but as long as you show up to class, you'll get an A

Feels like a high school class in a bad sense. Ruins my Tuesdays. If TA is nice, easy lab. But the entire lab design is straight up ridiculous. Most people know it's only for credit, so most if not all people put in minimum work to get by. Don't know why it exists. Also, barely related to the lecture at all.

I took the lab for ASTRO with TA Bill and he was amazing. This lab is extremely easy, show up and do the worksheets and you will be fine. The TAs walk around the entire time helping everyone with literally anything. The only downside is the time commitment. Highly recommend it for an easy lab.

Lab is basically run by the TAs with the exception of observations and the last project. A breeze to understand if taken with 1010. Basically show up and do 2-3 hours of work. TAs are very helpful and will help you find the right answers.

Dr. G is super sweet and nice but not the best prof. Tested on things covered in the txtbk and not in lecture, so going to class wasn't helpful if you read the book (which you absolutely needed to do to prep for the exams). Didn't teach - made us do worksheets to teach ourselves. Too many small homework assignments; felt like a high school class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I don't know why people gave low ratings for the lab. I thought that overall it wasn't too bad, and if you work with the right people you'd get out early almost every time. I guess each experience is different based on the TA you had though. The material on the lab wasn't too difficult if you put in the effort.

This is my second class with her and I LOVED it. She's so fun and caring, the content was super interesting, and she genuinely cares about her students and wants to see them succeed (will give accommodations, extensions, respond to you, etc.). Stay on top of your work, do the readings, go to lecture, and you'll be fine. Take her classes!!

The labs are graded and ran by the TA. There is a lot of work, but if you find a good group to work with on the labs, then you can knock out the labs and get out early. Granted I took this online. Dr. G sends out the labs and helps out for the first time during the final presentation. The lab is chill if you have a good TA that might be lenient.

The amount of work we have to do for a class that's worth 1 hour is absolutely outrageous. Weekly labs that take 3+ hours to complete, plus time consuming projects twice a semester and a final presentation that's extremely time intensive as well. The TA is nice and super helpful, but I wouldn't recommend taking this class for your lab credit.

This is an absolutely disgusting lab that ruins every single Wednesday for me. The prof and TA are all very nice and understanding, but there is just an ridiculous amount of work for a 1 credit lab. In addition to the hard and super-long labs, you have to do other projects twice a semester, and a end of semester presentation that is time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: There was no assigned textbook for class, so we were sort of on our own to clarify material we didn't understand. Took about half the semester for lectures to become comprehensible/ for her to work the kinks out of the course (but it was also her first time teaching the class). SUPER caring prof. Will be great next time she teaches the course!

Dr. G is extremely nice and down-to-earth but the lectures were entirely monologued and incredibly boring. Not to mention the course material was pretty inaccessible (she didn't start posting the lecture slides until at least halfway through the semester). We were often tested on things that hadn't been covered in class, which is always a bummer.

Astro lab with Grundstrom was an easy lab credit. The class was super disorganized, but the work was all really easy so the disorganization didn't end up mattering that much. She was easy to contact outside of class, and she's nice

Do NOT take this class. Excessive amount of work for a 1 credit hour class. No feedback. There is no clarity or direction throughout the entire work. She would post assignments, tests, test preps, labs, and everything else late. I learned nothing.

Don't pay too much attention to those other reviews saying her class is "brutal". You learn as much as you put into it and I thoroughly enjoyed the class. Although she was occasionally late posting the labs, if you have a later section you'll be fine if you manage your time well. She also encourages collaboration, which makes labs more manageable

Dr. G is definitely better than most profs in physics/astronomy, but not amazing. If you have taken lots of HS/intro physics you'll probably be fine, but if you just need a science elective another class might be better.

Every lab is a massive waste of time and the professor can't even get everything posted on the correct dates. 2 tests weekly labs and a final project is way too much work for 1 credit hour. Avoid at all costs.

I would not recommend this class to anyone. While I understand the transition to online classes is difficult, Professor Grundstrom continually ignores student and syllabus schedules, posting EVERY lab up to a week late and moving the due date max 2 days later. This is a one credit hour class, and she gives tests, a final project and labs. DONT TAKE

Grundstrom is super nice and a good overall prof. Her class is a little basic and the tests rely a lot on rote memory which is kind of annoying, but she has a very generous test correction policy so an A is very achievable. She keeps things pretty fun and light so it feels like a high school class. Overall would recommend as a manageable MNS class.

Since our lab was taught by a TA I think that I learned significantly less than I would have if she had been there all of the labs. She wasn't even there for review sessions and left the TA to literally give wrong information to us before the tests, tests the TA had never seen before. She's sweet and she is pregnant, but I wish she was there more.
