I don't understand the bad ratings for Dr. G at all. The subject matter isn't the most intersting in the world, but Dr. G is the sweetest and the absolute best. She does everything she can to help students and is super. There is extra credit, and as long as you show up, it is a pretty easy A. Class is consisted mostly of labs, and there's no HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class ruins every Thursday night for me. It is an easy A, but extremely boring and mundane. It helps a little bit with the lecture class, but really not that much. You observed three times and there is extra credit. Take it if you have to for the AXLE lab credit, but don't expect to have a good time.

They help you with the labs and the final project, so you can do well for sure, but the labs are brutal and super long and do not relate to the lecture WHATSOEVER. I had NO IDEA what I was doing for my lab tests AT ALL, I did badly but still got a good grade in the class, it's just extremely frustrating to not understand anything you're learning.

Grundstrom is lovely and clearly passionate. My lab was mostly instructed by and graded by the TA, so difficulty/leniency may vary. But for the most part its an easy lab credit and you learn a lot of interesting stuff. Only observe 3-4 times. No book or outside work besides studying for tests.
There are tests (midterm and final) and a final presentation, though this is a 1 credit course. Do yourself a favor and just take baby bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you're looking for a lab credit, Dr. Grundstrom is a great way to go. You will have very little work outside of lab, and getting an A is not hard if you just ask for a bit of help on the labs when needed. She walks around the room and is exceedingly approachable. There are two challenging tests, but they are not very important to your grade.

Prof. Grundstrom's lectures were not clear and I found myself reading the textbook instead of going to class to understand the subject. She seemed to genuinely care about her students and tried to be helpful during office hours. The tests weren't hard like some other reviewers said, but not having good lectures made doing well much harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof Grundstrom's lectures can be unclear, and when combined with hard material, can be catastrophic  for someone who struggles in physics. She doesn't always work out the example problems to completion, and the tests are very difficult; however, her lectures did get progressively better. She is also helpful and kind in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a seriously nice professor who will love you if you go to office hours. Hw is about 2-3 hours every other week.  Extra credit is given on tests and she curves them 10% to get the average around 80%.  She may not like calculus, but she goes over the exact examples that you will see on test frqs. Many students go into the final with 100%+
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I went into the final with a 95% in the class and got about the average on the final. Ended up with a B+ and I'm still mad about it.

May not be the best physics professor, but her passion for astronomy is immediately apparent. Great professor teaching an amazingly interesting subject. There is a lot of homework, but I didn't think it was an absurd amount. Probably 5 hours a week. I guess this perspective depends on your major?  :

I mostly agree with the reviewer below me. Dr. G is one of the nicest professors I've had, and she is a good teacher. But when I took this class, I was not expecting the almost absurd amount of homework that would be involved. Tests weren't that easy either, although she did give a ton of rebate points. I also have learned a lot about astronomy

Dr. G is one of the nicest professors at Vanderbilt. She is also incredibly passionate about Astronomy and at times her passion can be infectious. However Solar Systems is a ton of work. There are 4 tests plus a final and multiple blogs/hw assignments per test. Plan to spend several hours a week on the class. Class isn't hard; just alot of work

Dr. G's first time teaching E&M sucked for a lot of the class. Her lectures were confusing/often felt as if we were learning the material with her, rather than her teaching it. The exams ranged from "fine" to "we needed a 60 pt curve." However, VERY helpful/enthusiastic in office hours, so she was definitely supportive. She curved final grades too.
Dr. Grundstrom is an extremely nice professor but her tests are hard and her lectures are difficult to follow.
Someone needs to stop this woman from teaching physics. She's absolutely the worst.
Bad. Very bad.

Definitely the worst professor you will ever encounter throughout your whole life. Classes are useless, exam is the hardest with so many questions (trust me there are a whole lot of questions) with so little time. Worst. Avoid her or you will suffer.

Well, unless you're into "cool stuff", don't waste your time... I genuinely believe that she is passionate about astrophysics, and she is good at teaching that; however Gen Physics II is a long, difficult course, and you need someone who takes it seriously enough and is able to explain concepts concisely. She is not that person, I'm afraid.

To be honest, as a person, she's extremely nice and friendly. But as a physics professor, it's very hard to like her. Her tests are pretty tough for a professor who doesn't teach much in class. She might be a good astronomy professor, but for physics, please avoid her. You'll spend almost all of your time trying to learn this subject on your own
Its better to learn something than nothing. She the latter.
Not good at all
I don't think she had ever taught physics before this semester, but she is not clear at all and you will end up spending lots of time teaching yourself the material.  Don't do it.
Planning to take physics with her? Don't. You have been warned. DON'T. However if you like to listen to astronomy stuff or discuss clicker questions for half of the class time then go ahead.

If you are planning to take Physics with her, its a NO NO! Maybe she's a good Astronomy teacher, but not in Physics. Her lecture note is a magic! All the equations came out and she don't even knows what she's talking about. Plus, she took forever to set up the clicker and let you guys discuss. LOL.
Isn't able to convey points in understandable terms, especially when students ask questions.
Bad

If you aren't into astronomy, Dr. G's sheer enthusiasm and passion on the subject will get you excited about the subject. There was quite a bit of homework that was easy, but tedious "busy work." The tests are easy if you study, and she allows you to do rebates for points back. Overall, she is an extremely nice, helpful, and caring person.

Professor Grundstrom has a very well organized class and gives students every opportunity to succeed. There are a lot of graded assignments (ie: a fair bit of homework), but the material is interesting and Dr. G is an engaging teacher. Tests can be challenging, but depending on how the class does, you'll have the opportunity to earn points back

Possibly the easiest lab at Vanderbilt. As long as you followed all the directions on each lab, you got 100% on it. There were two tests, both completely made up of practice questions she gives you every week. Although lab could be mind-numbingly easy, she made astronomy so engaging and exciting that I couldn't help but thoroughly enjoy the class.

Awesome! So much fun! She is so engaging and can convince anyone to love astronomy as much as she does! Great class if you want to learn more about astronomy, or a great (and not very difficult) class for a science requirement.
My favorite professor!
LOVE HER best prof at vandy
She is very caring and tries to help in any way. The readings are long but its not her fault. Should for sure take.

Very chill, understanding if you have to miss class, super positive and kind in her lectures, creates very welcoming environment and super accessible. 10/10 Core teacher and perfect for freshmen. If you ever dont make expectations, she lets you revise and changes your grade.
She is quite literally the highlight of my week. Super funny, sweet, and good at conveying the material covered in class. I'm already trying to get her again for next semester.

I took her for CORE 1020. Absolutely love her; she tries to be relatable/silly and make your lives as stress-free as possible. CORE is already easy, you'll get an A with any prof, but she makes it SO easy. You need to put in below the bare minimum to get an A. Seriously a breath of fresh air, especially if you have other hard classes. Take her.

Easy A if you put in any effort at all. Readings before each class, and you can BS/chat your way through the discussions. 4-5 major papers, but all ~4 pgs, super easy grading. Desperately tries to get ppl to talk, so your classmates will make or break how fun this class is

Amazing professor! She really cares about her students and wants to make her class as beneficial for her students as possible. Her class was always full of engaging, interesting discussion, and she made all of our opinions feel valid. 10/10 recommend taking her class!

My favorite professors EVER. So caring and compassionate, the most supportive environment I've ever seen fostered in a class. She puts so much personality into her slides but has a healthy balance between lecturing + participation, which is very low pressure (talking in groups counts). Readings extremely light, can ask her for anything. TAKE HER!!!

I LOVE HER. If I could take Professor Covington every semester I would. She's such a caring individual and puts her all into the courses that she teaches. I looked forward to coming to this class every day and interacting with her. She never not had a smile on her face. 10 stars.

I took her for CORE 1010. Very entertaining and understanding - it was a morning class and she was sympathetic. Offered opportunities to get out of 1 lecture and assignment for going to a lecture outside of class. Loose due dates. High standards for papers but you can revise and they're short. If ur a decent writer the class is a free A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Covington is so good! Highly recommended!
Awesome and understanding professor. Her discussions are very fruitful. One of the best professors I've had at college.

Professor Covington was a really great professor. Our class was mostly discussion based, and she mainly facilitated the discussions then let us do the rest. Homework were short readings and the occasional response paper. Easy if you need AXLE credit

She is by far the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt and I enjoy going to class. Took this course for AXLE but so grateful I took it. She genuinely values her students and their opinions, and you can tell that she is passionate about what she says. It is a very pro-sex class though, and it can get pretty detailed.

What an amazing class! It was very reading heavy (sometimes reading 100 pages before class), but on some days you can totally get away with not doing the readings. Every class was just discussion where we talked about the readings and connected it to the world. Can rewrite every essay for full points and she is so kind and this was my fav class!!!

Professor Covington is fantastic! She is always so inspirational. She leads you to think and learn. Grading is really fair and you get unlimited revisions to boost your grade. If you read and participate actively, it will be an easy A. Great class and professor, definitely want to take her class again!

If you get the chance to take Professor Covington for a FYWS, seize the opportunity!! I took her Simple Art Murder course and it was simply incredible. The material is fascinating, I was always excited to show up to class, and the grading could not be any easier! She gives unlimited revisions on papers and provides comprehensive feedback.

I loved taking the Gendered Lives writing seminar class this semester. We had three papers this semester. Professor Covington is very knowledgeable and just a caring person outside of class. This course is pretty simple. The readings however are long in the beginning. She has an endless revision policy for papers. I recommend this class to anyone.

I love her. She made an 8 am class worth waking up to, and she made me want to speak in class even though I was always so tired. There are three major essays but they're all fun and easy, and it's an unlimited rewrite policy. TAKE HER!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: LOVED LOVED LOVED!! Absolutely an amazing person. There is an unlimited rewrite policy so it's pretty hard to not get an A. Prof Covington really cares about all her students and I can say that wholeheartedly. While the material was not my favorite, I loved her and her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very theory heavy class. 3 major papers (1 revision required per paper) and 2 smaller papers. You can rewrite the papers as many times as you want (most people got around 80s on first drafts and revised 1-3 times per paper) so if you are willing to put in the time its not hard to get an A.

Easy class if you've done any amount of literary analysis in highchool. Gives good feedback on papers, and allows regrades based on unlimited drafts, but was never really useful for me because she gave me >95% on all my first drafts. Still did the second draft beause she was nice and I didn't want to disappoint her

I took my first year writing seminar with Elizabeth and loved it! Super understanding, unlimited revisions make it easy to get an A as long as you put forth the effort to meet with her. Gives great feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE HER CLASS!! I love her. Genuinely cares about her students & wants us to be better writers. 3 essays, endless revisions :)
Unbelievable Professor. Very open and respectful to conservative students. Funny and does a good job making class enjoyable. Great instructor and helped improve my writing substantially.
I love Professor Covington! Took this class for an easy credit and ended up loving it! She is so hilarious and a great lecturer. Highly highly recommend you take a class with her
Great professor, really energetic and makes class interesting. You can also revise essays as many times as you want, making an A completely doable if you put in enough work.

Professor Covington is fantastic. Aside from being an awesome professor both in and out of the classroom, she has this energy that keeps even a slow day moving fast. I was especially appreciative of her system for paper-writing. If you're willing to put in the work to revise any of your papers, you'll get what you deserve from the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You will definitely become a better writer/reader in her class. You will also never be bored. She tells hilarious and sometimes personal stories about her life and makes you feel comfortable writing about your own experiences. I got 70s on most first drafts but edited them until I got As.
She is extremely helpful and very fair. Need to do the work and participate but pretty easy

Liz is great!! I took her and she was so helpful with all my essays and she loves what she does. She will definitely allow you to feel comfortable in her classroom and knows how to balance the class conversation and work. If you get engaged and give effort, you will pass AND make a new friend! :) very funny and considerate. TAKE HER CLASS!

I love this woman so much. She is honestly so inspiring and hilarious. She approaches this course in a way that is relatable to her student's lives, and she genuinely cares for everyone in the class. She is so honest and raw which is very refreshing. She is extremely passionate and overall, incredible. Everyone should take one of her classes.

She is the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. She was always available outside of class even to just talk. Her paper conferences were super helpful and rewrites were easy to get an A on. She doesn't care about deadlines (half my class submitted papers in a week late) and is very understanding if you have to miss class.

Elizabeth (she doesn't let you call her "Professor") is one of the best educators I've ever come upon. She really cares about the students' thoughts and participation is very important. Her humor makes class really fun and lighthearted, and she genuinely wants to see everyone succeed and enjoy their time in class. She is also very helpful w/ papers

Professor Covington goes above and beyond as a teacher and I truly feel like I've learned so much in her course. She is caring and truthful about what students need to work on as writers. I highly recommend!

Elizabeth (she doesn't let her students call her Professor Covington) is genuinely one of the funniest people I've ever met in my life. Also incredibly smart. Requires revisions on all papers so it's easy to get an A. Always willing to meet about papers, and very flexible with deadlines. One of the most fun and interesting classes I've taken here.

I absolutely loved this class - it inspired me to become an English major.  Elizabeth is so funny and interesting, I was never once bored/tempted to use my phone/sleepy in her class. I love her to death, but she IS kind of a tough grader, although she sometimes allows rewrites. One big perk: she's almost always down to have class at Ben&Jerry's.

I LOVED Covington's class. She is the most amazing English professor I have ever had. Have a bad day? Mention it and she just might take your class out to ice cream. She's not a fan of deadlines. She's as available as she can be. Just submit good work. She doesn't even care about the page count.

Prof Covington is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is energetic, hilarious, always willing to talk, and passionate about her work. You get as much out of this class as you put into it. She is a tough grader, but she brings the greatness out of you. If you want to improve and work hard, you will do well. Her class was my favorite.

Amazing. Always entertaining in class, and more willing to meet outside of class too. High standards, but plenty of thoughtful criticism and extremely fair grading. Planning to take her class (and Maymester) moving forward.

Elizabeth is one of the sweetest people I've met at Vanderbilt. She is incredibly smart, and she has pretty high expectations for students, but she is so supportive. She tries to pull the greatness out of people.
Elizabeth is probably the best English professor I've had at Vanderbilt! She is entertaining and absolutely brilliant. Take her if you have the chance!
Amazing professor. Grades hard but gives good feedback so you become a better writer. Took for AXLE but would take again.

I thought the class was pretty easy so long as you put in the effort. She lets you do re-writes, and you can email a rough draft to her to look at any time (even on the day it's due! lol but not just 3 hours before it's due of course)
She has really high expectations for your essays, but the class discussions are fun and interesting. If you're looking for a cupcake class, this isn't it.

By far one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. She is a harsh grader, but she gives you the opportunity to rewrite each of your papers after she initially grades them and counts your rewrite grade as 2/3 of your paper grade. She really knows what she's doing, discussion is always interesting and fun. Take her class!

Her sheer enthusiasm is enough reason to take this class. Working hard is a must, but she makes it easy to want to do well. She knows what she's talking about and wants you to do well, but won't compromise.

Definitely not a slacking-off kind of class; she's a pretty tough grader, but very reasonable and available to talk to during the week. Discussions are interesting and lively, and she knows her subject material. Come to class ready to discuss the reading pretty in depth. The class really improved my critical/analytical writing skills.

The material is very challenging and thought provoking, but Professor Covington does an outstanding job of thoroughly lecturing and interacting with students. She's extremely helpful and available outside of class. Her expectations demand that students learn more than the average standard by pushing them to expand their thinking and writing skills.

She was super nice/funny/passionate about what she is teaching, but is a ridiculous grader. Also, papers are due weekly and are expected to be very well written and a key knowledge of the reading is necessary (even with very little time to read the books). I recommend this class only if you are willing to work very hard on your writing techniques.

A self-proclaimed harsh grader, she is tough, but good. She really knows what she's talking about and cares about each student's success. It's a lot of reading at times, but it's an English class, so it's expected. Some books are really good, others painful, but she makes it all interesting. Very enthusiastic and funny.

Thank god I never have to walk into that lab ever again. All the random stuff you have to do for this class genuinely infuriated me every week. Nothing connects to course content, every lab is pointless, and it's all just busy work. Pray you get a good TA because I never met Brenda Enriquez not once.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of busy work but so much ec that almost everyone gets an a of some sort (only 8% of students get a b+ or lower according to her syllabus). Lab reports and lab notes were annoying and tedious so just hope you have a TA that isn't harsh at grading. I learned more about Excel than actual physics.

Doesn't care for students' wellbeing at all. It's a necessary evil to take her physics lab, which is generally a boring but easy A; just trust that if anything major occurs that affects your ability to succeed in this course, she will work overtime to make your life harder.
A 57 questions syllabus quiz? Are you for real?

The genuine amount of random crab and surveys you have to do for this class enrages me every week because it's the most pointless questionnaire of 60 questions where you just say how you felt about stuff and sometimes have to write a free response and you and her both learn nothing from it.

Not a difficult class, but a ton of busywork. Labs did not relate to the course content, and lab notes were extensive and tedious. Lab reports were unnecessarily long and repetitive, with unclear rubrics and expectations. Lots of opportunities for extra credit, but your grade mostly depends on your TA. I dreaded going to this class each week.

The lab notes are extremely lengthy, mainly consisting of busywork, oftentimes with unrealistic expectations. The lab report instructions/rubrics are unnecessarily wordy (8 pages) and different each time, making lab reports highly overcomplicated. Gives very repetitive homework assignments that are almost meaningless. Poorly ran class overall

lab content never related to course content, so everything was unfamiliar and made it difficult to understand. lab was very tedious and had us do irrelevant things(make presentations). TA dependent, can be harsh at grading. good amount of extra credit and can drop a lab unit.

I dreaded walking in every week. This lab is the worst I've ever taken, and that says something. The TA's do their best to make it tolerable, but the labs have nothing to do with what you're learning. It's like AI wrote everything and the lab reports are unnecessarily tedious. Only good thing is you can drop a lab unit and you work in a group.

This lab was an absolute mess. Confusing, not educational, boring BUSYWORK for 3hrs. I'm convinced she had an AI platform write all the lab formats and notes because of how oddly formatted and repetitive they were. Reminded me of labs I did back in elementary school with a notetaking load of AP lit. Biggest waste of time. Hoping 1602 is better.
Labs always depend significantly on your TA. Definitely did not look forward to going to lab every week. Lots of instructions and opportunities for extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: obv the grade u get depends on the TA but the labs themselves arent hard. lab took around 2 hrs per week on average. personally i hate physics but the lab wasnt bad
Made me switch my major. You can't avoid this course, thoughts and prayers

Very knowledgeable but incredibly rude and unapproachable. They dismiss questions as if you're wasting their time and make sarcastic remarks during lectures. It creates an uncomfortable learning environment where you're afraid to participate. Definitely not recommended if you value respectful communication and support.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My TA was really nice and helpful, but the overall lab structure was extremely confusing. The lab notes in every lab session were so redundant and difficult to understand. Even the easiest physics concept could be explained using a whole page. Also, the workload in lab was really heavy; homework, like lab reports, were really annoying.

a lot of work for 1 credit, but super caring. you can tell she's trying, and she was writing the syllabus from scratch so I get it. TAs make or break your experience though. Grading criteria (I think) have gotten clearer since I took the class, and she makes every effort to implement feedback/suggestions. Capstone & data analysis skills were useful

Dr. Fabela cared enough to help me work out class despite a bad medical emergency. I cried to her in fear of losing my grip on this class and she very easily helped me work out alternatives to dropping the lab. I finished with an A entirely thanks to her; however, normally 1502L is v dependent on what TA you get. Def know how to use google sheets

I frequently found myself confused as to whether this was a physics lab or a class on using google sheets to do statistical analysis. I don't think Dr. Fabela deserves all the hate necessarily, as your lab experience is almost completely dependent on your TA. That being said, the lab structure and content needs to be rethought. Easy but pointless.

Your experience in this class is HEAVILY dependent on the quality of your TA. Overall the organization of this class is EXTREMELY confusing and illogical. The emphasis on inquiry and "discovering" the science yourself is a nice idea, but a mess in practice. Also, unlike every other STEM lab, they make no attempt to align the lab with lecture. WHY??

Purely busy work and an enormous waste of time, as the labs do not supplement in-class material well at all. The labs themselves are not too difficult but she really increased the workload for each lab this semester, making each lab period literal torture to slog through. BRENDA WHY?????
Why did we spend an entire period making a 10 page rubric

Terrible pointless lab. Concepts are easy, but Brenda writes this lab manual with the cohesiveness and clarity of a fifth grader. TAs are confused, no concepts are taught well, and the material does not align with lecture (on purpose as well). Tons of pointless busy work and this class is a huge time sink.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I cannot stress how much patience she had with every student. She was extremely adaptable when we didn't have enough time to finish the lab. If you're there just to speed through the lab and get out of there, it's going to be frustrating because she really is there to teach you and help you understand the material (regardless if you want to).

Lab was just super confusing and you just have to follow instructions and put your head down to get through each one. It was relatively easy and the TA's grade nice. The Lab is just super tiresome. 3 easy takehome quizzes and some pre-lab quizzes. She drops lowest grades. It's easy to get an A just busy work really. No work outside of class rlly.

She is nice, but it being a lab you won't interact with her much.

Lab is a lot of work, but you can finish almost everything in class. Labs aren't very useful.

Pretty easy grade especially with the option of an excused absence and makeup lab options.
Its an easy A but there's a lot more work. Prelab quizzes are pretty tough unless you've taken physics before. labs are long. My TA sucked which made it worse.
Labs are basically useless but extremely easy A. Don't bother listening to the other reviewers who complained about their grade - they didn't work hard enough. Simple as that lol
if there is a heII I hope she's not there with me.

Brenda changed everything that was somewhat decent about an already abysmal physics lab system at this school. She thinks she is promoting collaboration by making "carefully selected" lab groups based on strength but that's a crock of shit. Labs are unclear and TAs are also unhelpful. There is no guidance or direction. Take if you need credit only.

Even though its a 1 credit hour class, the PHYS1601 lab feels like its taking more time than some 3hr classes. Labs are a mess. Not even the TA's know what to do and the pre-lab quizzes require you to read an obscene amount of work and most times are not even related to the actual lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ruined Physics 1601L through restructuring. I've taken labs for many difficult classes at Vandy, none of which are as ridiculous and time consuming Physics 1601L, a subject that hypothetically does not even need a lab. This lab has 5 papers and quizzes before every period, all of which is incredibly time consuming, poorly written, and unnecessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: While there has been improvements to the system, I still cannot say I enjoyed the lab experience. It's nice that the quizzes has 3 problems and you chose 2 to answer and the assignment amount has been streamlined. However, labs run for too long and certain sections can be really tedious. Overall it's just a poor experience that has muddled physics.

I'm taking the time to write this review so that when people read the other low ratings they know that they are entirely BS! Dr. Enriquez has completely changed physics lab to be a much more engaging, manageable, and enjoyable experience. + the easiest and smoothest lab experience I've ever had on campus. Ignore crybabies. Just follow directions.

Brenda seems to make the labs too long for a 3 hour lab time limit. There have been multiple labs where students cannot finish in the given time, and thus she makes one lab cover two days. Either she needs to be retrained or obligated to attend mock lab sessions before the scheduled lab to see if it will be able to be completed in the given time!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She makes the labs too long and has too much hw for it. Overall bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: For PHYS 1601L. Lab instruction was led completely by the TA. I liked this lab because there were no exams or quizzes, it allowed us to complete the lab without stress. No one likes going to lab but I do feel that the labs did help me understand the lecture content better, and I never had a lab last the full 3 hours.

Dr. Fabela is literally an angel. She has the patience of ten people and will explain difficult subjects with so much finesse and grace. She is super caring and immensely kind, and she is rejuvenating the curriculum from Charnock, so it is a million times better. You are in good hands with her and Starko FOR SURE.

Dr. Fabela provided the best lab experience I've ever had at Vanderbilt. She's replacing Dr. Charnock, and I think lab students will start enjoying themselves there. She was very helpful and caring at all times, and BIG BONUS was never afraid to remove parts of labs that were too hard or didn't make sense.

Dr. Spivey was a great professor and his class was really fun. My only issue was that some of the lab reports were graded too harshly, and it felt like him and the TAs were not on the same page with the grading standards. TAs would take points off for things we were told to do or would be overly critical of things that weren't stressed in class.
He is very helpful when you come with questions, and he also allowed AI-assistance for projects.

Dr. Spivey is great.
Main issue was the TA who did grading. Grades took forever and often you need the grades on the rough draft to work on the final draft. 
The class wasn't very organized and it was often hard to tell the scope of assignments. The class feels like a lot of work to do well just for a 1 hour class.

Spivey is a good guy but how easy 2900W is really comes down to the TA. My TA was nit-picking the hell out of every word I wrote and probably just hated my writing style. Way too much work for an 1 credit hour class but the last lab is kinda meaningful when you give your modified toys to the kids.

Spivey is an amazing professor that works on fitting your schedule to the class. He is very understanding if there are other things in your life that put you a little behind. Great professor but lectures can be a little boring but overall, amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BME Lab 1 - Spivey is easily the best choice for a professor in a BME lab at Vandy. He is a nice guy and isn't a tough grader. Overall, it was a enjoyable experience since is such a great professor.

Spivey will quite literally throw you in the deep end. I took his BME module the first block of my first semester freshman year, and I have never been more lost. He expects a lot of prior knowledge, which makes no sense for someone teaching freshmen.

Spivey was great for my first engineering mod professor. The hardest part about this class is just making sure your group does the work lol. Spivey is definitely the type to make sure that everyone does well, so don't stress if something goes wrong with your microfluidic device. Overall if you have Spivery for your BME mod, you will be just fine!

Prof. Spivey is a pretty good choice if you are interested in taking a BME module. There is pretty minimal homework and as long as you complete all the assignments you will get an A. You do have to go to office hours about once a week as the module starts ending to complete your project. But overall I had a positive experience in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer, but a tough grader! Get started on projects ASAP and utilize both his and the TAs office hours.
Dr. Florian is an incredible professor, however, be prepared to work. Start projects early, go to office hours, and you will succeed.

Dr. Florian is an awesome professor and it helps that he's so passionate about what he does. He can 3D print literally anything and encourages his classes to do the same. The class is very project-heavy and I think some of the material could be tough if you've never seen a circuit, CAD, or code before, but overall it's manageable and fun.

Really nice and enthusiastic guy. Seems to care about students' interests and careers and how the course content can apply to that. He is clearly passionate about the material himself and has 3D printed himself a boat!

Easily the most interesting class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Florian is an engaging professor as well. It's a very hands-on class with several time consuming projects, but if you go to office hours and get ahead it's very manageable. The final project is pretty difficult but very rewarding.

Awesome class- can't recommend it enough, super beneficial and applicable. 
I had absolutely no previous experience in any area of the course, and Dr. Florian did a great job making the content accessible. Projects were time-consuming but fun. Dr. Florian is an engaging teacher with a genuine enthusiasm for the subject and students' learning.

He provides vague instructions and grades with excessive specificity. The grading often feels arbitrary due to inconsistent expectations. This makes the class frustrating and more challenging than it needs to be. If the class wasn't required I would have never took it, It's a major waste of time.

Extremely harsh grader for the most part. Wants you to write exactly how he writes or he's taking off points. Homework can take quite a long time for a 1 hour class. Ambiguous grading criteria for most assignments. You can tell he is trying his best, but it ends up being a very frustrating class when it really should be a lay up.

Best class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Dr. Florian is kind and funny, and you will learn more practical skills in this class than any other ones. Class is NOT easy though, especially the final project. Go to office hours if you want to succeed.

The course is poorly designed. The workload is sometimes simply unreasonable and he did not give any heads up beforehand. Overall, he frames the class to be for all majors but in reality he is extremely unaccommodating to non-engineering students.

Dr. Florian is incredibly friendly and has the most extensive office hours out of any professor I know. I will say though that you have to go to office hours for most of the big projects in order to succeed in this class. I definitely recommend this class and professor to anyone who's interested, but beware this class is not as easy as it may seem.

This class was incredibly interesting, and I learned a lot. However, Dr. Florian can be a harsh and unfair grader. There were times when people turned in similar work and received extremely different grades resulting from unclear grading criteria. As well, he definitely favors some students over others, so be ready to convince him to like you.

Must-take class for mechEs. Beware, not an easy class even with prior technical experience. Workload varies greatly by week and can be as high as 7 hours per week (final project is higher). Don't recommend to non-engineers with little to no prior experience unless you are ready to put in the time and work. Quality class where you learn many skills.

One of the best classes offered for both engineering and A&S majors. He is very passionate about the material and is always accessible for help on projects/quizzes. The projects can be quite tough If you don't have a strong mechanical background but help is always available. The lecture slides are great; the lectures are engaging.

This was a really fun class! We got to work on cool projects, like making a phone case and then a syringe pump at the end. It's amazing how many skills we covered, like 3D printing, soldering, and programming LEDs with microcontrollers. Overall there isn't much homework but he is a harsh grader.

Professor Florian is genuinely passionate about digital fabrication and it shows in every class. The lectures are all extremely engaging, and the topics of study are put simply enough that any major could understand one--but he will go into detail if anyone wants to know more. I took this on a whim, and it was the best decision. Highly recommend.

His DF class covers a wide variety of topics in engineering, and the class was very hands-on. Most test grades in this class are thankfully project-based and very doable with little to no prior experience. The projects conducted in this class are very fun to complete and challenging. He is one of the most friendly and approachable professors.

He gives students all the tools they need to succeed. While there were a lot of areas that were entirely new to me, David did a really good job of teaching me the skills I needed to succeed. He was very available outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Florian cares a lot about the students and learning the content so the class is always enjoyable. The class bounces between lectures which instruct on fundamentals and practical learning days where you have time to work hands on with a skill set (CAD, wiring, etc) which really allows you to learn the content effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed this class and having Professor Florian as a teacher. Although I found portions of this class to be difficult he was extremely helpful and available for students.

Rapid Prototyping was a great class that applies engineering topics in relevant ways. Be prepared to learn a lot of new skills. Even non-engineering majors excelled in this class. Plus, if you take the class you can use the resources in the Digital Fabrication lab for the rest of your time at Vanderbilt to make some really cool things.

Anyone interested in digital fabrication should take a class with Professor Florian. He's lenient about grades and the material and teaching style is very engaging and fun. The workload varied a bit. On the low side it was maybe 2 hours per week of homework and on the high side it was 4-5 hours (though this was only for 2 weeks in the semester).

Great professor who is passionate about teaching this stuff to students. Also really cool guy with the projects he does. Puts in a ton of work into the course by bringing examples, recording videos, and having a ton of office hours. Homework can actually be a lot, but its actually useful to learning. Would reccomend if you're interested!

This rating is for psy-pc 2300. very sweet prof but she gives SO MUCH reading. every class there was a quiz on abt 60 textbook pages worth of reading hw. class was a little boring/repetitive but other than the hw it was pretty easy

She taught PSY-PC 2300 for the first time this semester, and the content was very research-based, which was very boring. She is nice, however the content is very research heavy. For exams, you have to memorize many studies to do well. You have to put in good effort to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I actually didn't take 1250 but didn't find the class listed here. Anyhow, Dr Fazio class is so, so boring. She just assigned a lot of readings and had no discussion structure. There were so many awkward silence moments. For the big assignments, she expected a lot but gave no instructions. It wasn't a hard class but I wouldn't recommend it.
Her teaching stye seemed desperate. She was pushing misinformation on many topics.

The class material was interesting and Dr. Fazio was very knowledgable, but the lectures were a bit dry/boring. The readings were mostly research which was painful but as long as you do them you do well on the reading quizzes. We didn't have tests, just projects. I like dev psych and she was nice - easy course just pretty boring

Dev psych with Fazio was a pretty laidback course. She doesn't assign tests which made things easier and the readings/reading quizzes were very doable (I skimmed most of them). Fazio is very knowledgeable and does a good job teaching, but goes a bit fast on slides in lectures. Highly recommend.

I really liked Fazio! As someone who doesn't take many psych classes, I really enjoyed how lowkey this class was. Big assignments are spread throughout the semester so you're never too overwhelmed by anything. Reading quizzes can be done well by skimming the text. She creates a really collaborative environment and allows lots of group discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Fazio is such a caring professor and makes lectures fun and engaging with cute, but educational, baby videos :) It is obvious that she wants her students to thrive - she covers all the important points from the reading in her lectures and she even gave us study guides which matched up perfectly with the test's content. 100% recommend.

Lectures are so boring and repeat the book reading that you have to do prior to class in order to succeed on daily quizzes. She is really nice but lacks empathy sometimes. It really isn't too hard if you just expect to study more than just the night before a test b/c they cover a lot of information
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Update since the last one was 2015. Dr. Fazio knows her stuff, and you do readings ever night for quizzes most classes. These are easy but yeah attendance is mandatory but she also drops 2. Test was soo easy and she gives study guides. Easy psych core class, recommend for sure over the other profs for these reasons. Lectures just go over hw reading

Dr. Fazio is a great professor for seminar style classes. She's happy to help you understand the material and discuss student interests. She's a great person to know, but her classes do require some extensive reading.
"Make it Stick" seminar. Discussion based class. Often got boring and talked about the same topics. Needed more information for discuss. Pretty boring.

LOVED DR. FAZIO! Easily my favorite class at Vanderbilt. Every assignment has clear guidelines, tests and quizzes are straightforward, plus she shows lots of cute videos in almost every lecture. Very approachable and clearly wants her students to do well. Also, no final!

Professor Fazio really cares about her students and is interested in getting them to learn everything they can. Her assignments are direct, she gives study guides (something unheard of at A & S, but maybe common on Peabody?), and she sets up her class to encourage discussions and group discussions.

Fazio has been my favorite prof so far. Her lectures are outstanding. She turns what could easily be something totally boring into what seems like the  most interesting thing ever. You'll find yourself uttering things like, "wow pre-operational kids are the cutest." In public. It'll be hella weird, but you'll love it. TAKE HER CLASS.

Very fun environment. He is a creative professor who makes his entire course an adventure. Throughout the course you complete three projects, so find a good partner at the begining of the course! He speaks mostly in French at this level which really helped me improve. He is always really helpful if you have a question, and is great to laugh with!
I adore his educational approach. He knows exactly what he is doing and why he's doing it. One of the best educators I have ever encountered.

One of the most unique professors/classes I've ever had. It's structured like a video game with levels and currencies. As a result, this was a joy to take. If you're wondering which language to take, take French with Alexis Finet

Interesting class set-up. You earn xp by participating in and outside of class which helps progress your grade. It's easy to get an A, as Alexis grades kindly and gives many opportunities to earn xp. As others have said, the online textbook is required for homework and it's very expensive. I had fun in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was the most unique class I have taken. He is a very eccentric person. The class involves a fictional story line about a french monster and grades by giving you "xp". There is never a dull moment in this class and it is very easy to get an A. But he does require external participation. The online textbook is expensive and annoying.
Dr Finet is genuinely awesome, I adore him! He makes the class really fun, the assignments are unique and not stressful. A ton of extra credit, too. Decided to do the French minor because of him.

Taking 1103 with & he's an amazing professor; passionate about linguistics and you can see it in the way he crafts the lessons. I would say the class is more review self pace, so you can def get behind. he is always willing to answer what ever questions you may have. As someone with limited French knowledge, I am glad to have him here.

I absolutely love Alexis. He's an amazing professor and makes every day in the classroom so much fun. He uses an adventure-based curriculum and makes it fun to work towards the grade you want. It's a flipped classroom situation and he gives great feedback and minimal assessments. There's no way to lower your grade, only ways to raise it!

This was my first French class at Vanderbilt and an amazing way to step my foot in the door to the French department here. He's very relatable kind, and hands-on. Trust me, you'll grow in your vocab and speaking quickly if you simply apply yourself in this class. Be prepared to do slightly more mini assignments here and there than other classes!

This class was super easy and Prof Finet made it really fun. He made an effort to create interesting assignments to get us to interact instead of just lecturing. It made learning a language a unique experience and I would def recommend. The portfolio was slightly tedious but if you paced yourself through the semester it was fine.

Alexis is a very nice guy, and I totally recommend taking his class if you have a chance. He grades easy but also gives good, detailed feedback. This class made French less stressful for me. The homework load and projects are pretty easy as well and up to you how much time you want to invest.

M. Finet is probably the most caring professor at Vanderbilt University and no I am not exaggerating. He will give you as close to individualized care as possible and seems like he genuinely cares about your development in the French language. The class is very interesting but be prepared to do a little more work that you would expect. MERCI!!

This was his first time teaching this course for the pilot version. He is a great professor, very kind, works with you and the grading is decent but this course was A LOT of work. Weekly discussion posts & vocab notebook (only 20 words), 4 group projects, attendance is graded and there is a final portfolio that you work on throughout the semester.

Alexis was mostly chill, he takes off points when you do not come to class but is very understanding of busy schedules if you need an extension or have a conference or something. Mindtap homework is due 3 times a week. He does not dock too many points on tests and presentations. Usually has a storyline plot with his classes which some people like.

If you are thinking about taking a french class, take one with Alexis! He cares so much about the class and his students. He makes it fun by having a theme of saving "Sonosia". He is very patient and understanding. He grades based on above satisfactory, satisfactory, in progress and unsatisfactory - where satisfactory is an A.

Alexis is one of the best professors I've had in Vandy. Smooth classes, helpful homework, and a fun grading system that makes you actually want to work hard for your grade. I wasn't planning on taking 2203 but I will because Alexis is teaching it.

Actually took him for phonetics but AMAZING class and professor. He truly cares, is funny, and the flipped classroom format worked really well so that we got maximum practice in class. Cannot recommend enough, a great French experience.

Dr. Alexis is really AWESOME. He designed a French Tree as our academic record. Everything we do for French counts as droplets to water our French tree. He is versatile, and he has really great slides. Take this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Alexis is a great professor. His class felt like a high school French course, which I liked. He is very tunderstanding and answers emails quickly. Most chill professor at vandy.
While this professor is new to Vanderbilt, I am glad I was able to take my language class with him. He truly cares about his students and it shows!
Great choice for an otherwise boring required class!

Professor Falconi made what was an otherwise exceptionally boring required class super enjoyable and added a lot of life. He also cared for his students outside of class as well, which was very appreciated.
Caring guy despite CORE 1020's weird curriculum

Attend class. Easily one of my favorite courses in the Spanish department. Professor Falconi keeps things interesting and puts in an effort to meet each student to cultivate an incredible learning environment. He is patient with those who are improving their Spanish proficiency, and cares about his students. I would highly recommend!!!

Falconi is genuinely hilarious. More often than not, his lectures turn into personal stories and tangents. He's forgiving in his grading of his writing assignments. His tests can be somewhat challenging, but they're not the end of the world. Take him for his personality. You won't regret it.

Prof Falconi was great, especially facilitating group discussions and getting everyone to feel comfortable speaking spanish in front of each other. He would often go on tangents, but they almost always related to class material and made it more engaging. We only had one paper and a presentation, but participation was needed in this course.

I loved Prof. Falconí and his class. Super great guy that is really easy to talk to. My Spanish ability skyrocketed in his class; really easy to understand and has tons of grammar practice exercises. The tests weren't walks in the park, but were very doable if you understand the MindTap concepts and do all of the practice work.

Dr. Falconi was an amazing teacher who really seemed like he cared about each of his students. He was very flexible with deadlines and extremely accommodating with any issue that arose. The tests are difficult but you are able to make up that grade through other assignments.

Professor Falconi is one of the kindest and funniest professors I've had. He was very flexible about turning in assignments, and his classes were engaging although most of his lectures went on tangents. Tests are difficult, but there are plenty of papers to balance and are extremely helpful in improving Spanish writing skills.

Prof Falconi was super caring, generously granting extensions on each writing assignment. His tests were hard, but if you did the review homework assignments he posted and studied the textbook, you could do pretty well on them. He went tangents in class, most of which were in English about politics or current events, which made class pretty chill.

Prof Falconi is awesome and funny, but he spends most of the class speaking in English and discussing politics. He goes on tangents (in English ) that last a while, which is nice if you want a lowkey class. He is also very flexible with deadlines, which is helpful, and he clearly wants his students to succeed.

He's really funny and chill, it's an enjoyable class to attend. I bought the paper copy of the book which was a mistake because altho it was way cheaper, a paper copy obv gives no feedback about when you're wrong, so I def didn't learn as much. He grades nicely so just put in the effort and it'll all work out. Do the reviews he posts for quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is so funny and really tries to get his students out of their shell and willing to talk. Be warned that he gets super behind on grading so you might not get a lot of feedback, but he's not a tough grader in general.
Prof. Falconi is amazing. His class is extremely chill and welcoming for all levels. He encourages participation and makes you feel comfortable speaking. One of the best professors I've had.

A welcoming and non-judgmental classroom, his students are encouraged to speak Spanish during discussions but not required. The tests are difficult, but higher grades on papers and participation help balance the tests out. He often goes on tangents during class but in a way that makes the language applicable to real life.

Professor Falconi made class very enjoyable. Some days were more productive than othersmost days we went over grammar/theory/homework in class. Other days we simply found an interesting topic to discuss and shared our opinions on it. Most of your work will be grammar hw and papers. Few quizzes but they can be tricky.

Really loved Prof. Falconi! He is genuinely one of my favorite Spanish professors I've had at Vandy. He does go on tangents during class and be ready for lots of smaller writing assignments. However, he is suuuuper flexible and really cares about you learning the language. Take him!

AMAZING professor. One of my favorites at Vandy yet. He is so caring and flexible. Goes on a tangent in class a lot and you end up not going through any of the material. A lot of busy work but super doable. He is the best.

Took SPAN 3301W freshman year and Profe Falconi was great. Always made class worthwhile and engaged students with interesting conversations that happened to be in Spanish. Tests are challenging but fair. There is a good amount of homework and essays so be ready to spend a lot of time writing.

The tests in this class are super difficult and given without much studying material. Classwork is manageable and the essays really boost your grade. Get ready to be called on during one of Falconi's thought-provoking class discussions. Very caring/understanding teacher; willing to adjust the class schedule to better fit the needs of students.

Get ready to write: between daily diary entries, three dense essays, three essays factored into the three tests, and a final essay, this class will make you a better Spanish writer if you put in the work. Falconi is hilarious and loves participation, he often starts interesting discussions and values your opinion. The tests are difficult so study!

Falconi is one of the most understanding and caring professors I have ever had. The tests are really hard but the papers help out your grade and he is happy to meet to help. He genuinely cares about his students in and outside of the classroom and gets we have other things going on. 10/10.

Heraldo is the man. Advanced Conversation with him was SUCH a great time - minimal workload and I feel like my speaking really did improve. He's such a gem - always understanding of students, helpful, remembers things about your life outside of class, etc. Take Heraldo!!!

I enjoyed Falconi's 3301W so much; as a professor, he is fun and pretty engaging. He was very understanding about turning in essays late, taking the time you need, and giving valuable help. His feedback was also great and I feel like I learned a lot of nuance. It is a lot of work, which is to be expected for a W course, but worth it in my opinion.

I would 100% encourage people to take this class. Professor Falconi is caring and very available to help students in and outside of class. Grades are based off of papers, which you can revise, and tests, which also have a writing portion. Make sure to speak in class! The discussions are always interesting and he values students' opinions.

Falconi gives great feedback and the essays are a great way to boost your grade. Tests are challenging so definitely study, but he gives you all the points he can. He is very flexible with deadlines and will let you turn in work late. I did not find him disorganized at all. Very kind professor who cares about his students a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fun guy, homework compositions w/ revisions help your grade, tests can be difficult and lectures can be a bit boring but with a solid foundation in Spanish (AP 5) the class is fine.
Prof. Falconí is am amazing professor, accessible, engaging, and funny, but also really genuinely cares for his students and their education in a way that most professor's do not.

Prof Falconi might be the funniest professor I've had at Vanderbilt. His classes are always entertaining, he speaks in English half of the time, and he gives great feedback on his grades. It is not hard to get an A in the class if you participate a lot and do the rewrites for each paper. The two quizzes/tests are not easy but just study for them.

Real G, funny & kind, great guy. However, did not actually learn much in class. You read/do hw then in class he goes on weird tangents. You do get to practice reading, speaking, and writing with several mini presentations. Tests very difficult and although clear what will be tested, it's all from the book on your own. More lenient on grading essays
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was a great class! Falconi truly cares about his students and his classes were always interesting. The tests were definitely heavy on book material. The grading for essay seemed harsh at times, however his grammatical feedback is great.

Falconi is such a sweet and cute man, but my biggest issue with him was his lack of communication and disorganization. He would always hand back our essays and essay rewrites weeks after we turned them in even though they were short. The online homework is not useful. Instructions for assignments were not always clear. Overall, the class was fine.

Falconi is great. He's funny and is good at teaching the material. If you're intimidated by classes 100% in Spanish you shouldn't worry; Falconi speaks almost exclusively in Spanglish. The two tests are very heavily weighted, so it's important to do well on them, but they're not super hard (do study though). He gives really good feedback on papers.

Prof. Falconí is well-liked and his SPAN3340 course is overall recommended.  It's a strange course in that there aren't many written/reading assignments -- it's almost all recorded conversations, presentations, etc.  Participation is key.  Go to office hours if confused -- he gives good feedback and wants students to improve.

He is absolutely the nicest guy. This class specifically is difficult in that the essays and tests are open ended but still require a lot of detailed knowledge and the lectures can be unclear. Grading isn't the easiest I have had but it's definitely fair. Participation and reading are very important.

Prof. Falconi is so awesome. He's the most chill professor I've met, and he's super helpful. He breaks out the Spanglish pretty regularly so if you absolutely can't function completely in Spanish, he's your guy. You'll need to really work for an A (or be a native speaker), but it only takes a little effort to get at least a B.

Falconi is such a bro. One of the best teachers I had in my first semester. Super laid back and extremely helpful. Hope to take another class with him in the future. Participate in class and go to him for help if you need and you will easily pull an A or B in the class.

Professor Falconi is the coolest. Very laidback class as long as you participate and do the homework. He's super lenient with due dates as long as you show effort. Like many language classes, it takes minimal effort to get a B, lots to get the A.
Heraldo is the best. You'll get a B even if you're awful at spanish and if you work hard you'll do really well.

He is really nice. The tests are hard, but if you participate, do well on the essays, and do your homework you can still do fine. He doesn't grade the essays too hard. It is hard to get in the A range though unless you get As on the tests

basically, you're going to get a b+ on you're papers if you put in work. the key to getting an a/a- in this class is doing well on the tests and pop quizzes, which is difficult to do if you didn't study. great prof overall, don't go to sportsmans instead of studying for the test on wednesday!

Professor Falconi is such a nice guy. He really cares about his students and how well they are doing. He is always willing to give extra help if needed. His class is fair and fairly easy if you put in some effort. Plus he makes class really enjoyable.

I've had Falconi for 207 and 202; he's extremely easy if you give off the right impression. Its near impossible to make lower than a B+, and near impossible to make better than an A-. He favors Spanish majors over minors. But, he is very approachable, understanding, easy grader, funny/interesting, etc. Take his classes for easier grading.

Falconi is an awesome. So down-to-earth and approachable. Loosens up very easily and if you put a reasonable amount of work into your assignments you can easily receive an A. Only complaint is that he talks in English the entire class--which can be frustrating in a Spanish Conversation class, but welcomed by some students....definitely recommend!!
Great professor. Keeps the class as interesting as it can be and is invested in his students' success. Doesn't just give out good grades, but is very fair and objective.

Fantastic Professor. He real cares about your success and will be available to help you outside of class whenever needed. I highly recommend taking his class. Also, his English is probably better than most of the native speakers in the class. Fantastic person!
Falconi is awesome. Definetly take him, he really cares. He's funny, engaging, always in a good mood. He really has turned my spanish experience around. Just a great, great guy.
No Comments

He is very helpful and approachable. He truly cares about the students. The class is challenging and demanding, but he can't do much about that. Mostly papers determine the bulk of the grade with a few tests.

Dr.Kola is an incredible human being. She can be a little disorganized but not in a stressful way or to the point that it negatively impacts students. All of the material is actually relevant & interesting to read. Incredibly insightful class and she provides good feedback. She cares about students and is accessible. Def take a MHS course with her!

Professor Kola is awesome.  She is by far the best Professor or Teacher I have ever had.  She is knowledgeable, kind, inspirational, supportive, interesting, and very compelling in her delivery.  I would recommend this class to all and I hope that I can take more classes with Professor Kola.  She is so knowledgeable and has enthused me profoundly.
Amazing lecturer. Her class was the highlight of my year

This is the best class I've ever taken at Vandy! Prof Kola is so smart and the class actually inspires you to want to read and learn. She's an incredible lecturer and person, so caring and kind. I wish I could take every class with her! Enroll in this class, you will NOT regret it.

Prof Kola is an outstanding Professor. I would highly recommend this class. The classes were intellectually stimulating and very interesting. I learnt so much and broadened my horizons profoundly. She is extremely brilliant, kind, caring and very respectful of students. Every medical student and Physician should have this knowledge. Excellent class

Dr Kola's course was a highlight of my semester. Her love for literature really came through in the lectures as did her care for her students. The classroom discussions were always lively and intellectually rewarding.

Dr. Kola is an amazing professor! You have to do a lot of reading but it's a literature class, after all. If you pace yourself it's not too bad. Really appreciated the document she gives out to help us keep track of our own assignments. It made me feel like she really sees us adults. As a prof, she's so smart, caring, interesting, and kind. 10/10.

i loved my class with her. she's so sweet and caring and very intelligent! a lot of reading, but it's a vanderbilt writing seminar, so that was expected. i learned a ton and thoroughly enjoyed class discussions. highly recommend taking her class!

I believe that it is very unusual she decided to allow students to form their own groups for class activities. If students have friends in class, good for them, but for others, it is awkward and you feel left out of many activities and discussions, wishing you made your friend enroll. It would be better if she assigns everybody groups to work in.
Please get a bigger room next year!! Loved your class

Super knowledgeable! Loved all the readings and activities, especially the chapbook. However, I think it's the professor's responsibility to hold deadlines accountable. Letting them fall like dominoes just opens the door for students to procrastinate. I know it is still technically our fault, but the delayed deadlines made moving out this year HELL

I love Dr. Kola as a person, she is amazing and kind and caring. I am just rating her teaching of the course. Being totally honest, it really sucked to have dealines continually pushed back and the syllabus schedule completely adjusted every day until everything was basically due on the last day. I understand having delays but this was out of hand.

For an MHS class, I feel like this class was unnecessarily hard. There's A LOT of writing, a lot more than other W courses I've taken. Readings go up to 60 pages, and because a lot of them are just pictures of a text, you can't have a program read it to you. Yes, this class was fun, but I stressed so much more than my actual core major classes.

Dr. Kola's class is fantastic. There is a bit of reading, but nothing unreasonable. She gives you feedback on each of your papers and a tentative grade before you resubmit them for a grade. A great W that is both easy and enjoyable. Couldn't recommend this class and Dr. Kola more!

Super sweet professor who cares a lot about her students. Very easy to get an A in the class since she gives great feedback for drafts and pretty much tells you exactly how to get each paper to an A. There are 3 papers and one project for the class which aren't difficult and there are many opportunities for extra credit. Great W class to take.

Professor Kola was so caring, and always went out of her way to make the class accessible, inclusive, and impactful for everyone. She was so accessible and supportive of her students. Attendance was important, but she was super understanding and provided ways to make up for missed lectures. I jumped at the chance to take another course with her.

Prof Finkelman is a great professor. He truly cares about his students and creates a good learning environment. He is extremely knowledgeable yet humble and, more importantly, personable so he is still engaging. Some of the best convos I ever had are with him. I took him first semester so I saught him out for CORE, that's how much I like him.

Really nice genuine guy and not very difficult. Definitely appreciates participation in his classes, but is not super strict about it. He provides really interesting insights for discussions and provides very honest perspectives.

Finkelman is an amazing professor! He teaches extremely well and his lectures are very engaging. He is very knowledgeable and loves discussing your questions and interpreations of the course content! He assigns a lot of reading but they are all foundational to the lectures. 10/10 professor and 100% recommend taking a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Finkelman is a great guy and a good professor. The class is pretty straightfoward and very interesting. All our work was take home and Finkelman was a good grader and he added helpful feedback. I'd take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very knowledgeable and always open to questions. I learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Finkelman is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about Jewish History. His lectures are very informative and give you exactly what you need to know for the debates and essays. There is a lot of reading, but reading it before class is a great way to be prepared for the lecture and participate (which is a big chunk of the grade). Take him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Learned so much from this class. It's actually a ton of reading that you need to do so I spent more time on this class than most, but it pays off. Only graded on a take home midterm + final paper, a film response paper, and 3 short quizzes. Super straightforward and prof is not a harsh grader. Only 8 AM i've taken that I was excited to go to.

Professor Finkelman is fantastic. He is extremely knowledgeable, has great lectures, easy grader, very accessible, and makes the class very interesting. Minimal work, mid-term and final are both take-home, 3 in-class easy quizzes with 1 drop. More focus on the actual material than on assignments, which I loved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of my fav history professor at Vandy. Extremely knowledgeable, amazing lecture, super accessible outside class, lenient grading, and offers detailed feedbacks to your works. But the class is a bit reading heavy. Participation 10%, quizzes 10%, film analysis 25%, take-home midterm (25%) and take-home final essay (30%), no real exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer, you can definitely tell he really cares about the course content and he makes it sound super interesting. Quizzes are fair, no tests, just essays. Lenient grader but gives good feedback. Lots of reading but the textbook and extra sources are interesting. Can't recommend this class enough
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Finkelman is great. His lectures are very organized. He follows a chronological approach, while also diving into different historiographical perspectives. He will tear your essays apart and still give you an A, so you get the best of both worlds. Can't recommend him enough for people who don't mind reading a fair bit for a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's just copying off notes he wrote years ago so when you ask him a question he has no idea how to answer because he's not locked in on what he's teaching. Also a lot of these reviews say he's a hard grader, and you might think you're immune to that - you're not. His tests are hard and only have 2 questions so if you mess up one you get a 50.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not sure he knows what he's doing - bumbles around and gets corrected by students often in class, grades tests strictly. Very nice guy and means well, though.
IT LOOKS LIKE HE WROTE HIS OWN REVIEWS. DO NOT TAKE DYNAMICS WITH HIM. TRUST

Great personality, he keeps class interesting with jokes and candy. Attendance is not mandatory and there is no honor code for the homework (all online). Had 5 exams but only 2 problems each, laid back class.

Class is an easy A. Attendance is nowhere close to necessary, but you go anyway for Frampton's personality. Great guy, makes pretty basic and boring topics interesting with random interjections of personal stories. Don't be expecting to actually learn anything though.

The exams aren't too hard for this class. Lectures are sometimes boring but you can't really make dynamics interesting so that's ok. I'd love to grab a beer with him sometime but I'd never want to sit through one of his classes again haha.

BEST PROFESSOR!!!! His dynamics class was one of the easiest classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. I highly recommend him over Dr. Dong because his lectures are much more boring. Frampton is really open in office hours and really willing to listen to feedback.

Professor White is really funny and a nice guy. He is super understanding. His lectures really show what consulting looks like in the real world which can be really helpful in comparison to "classroom learning." I would def take any class he teaches again.
Professor White is the best professor I've had in a long time. He is engaging, insanely smart, and really cares about his students. I would take any class he teaches.

Take this class! Great class for consulting. Meets for 2.5 hours but Prof White keeps it engaging with a lab/lecture approach and guest speakers. Having an external client helps learn how to apply concepts to a real client challenge. Prof White truly cares about us and often goes out of his way to help outside class w/recruiting and career advice.
great professor - group project that takes all semester but Prof White is accessible and also helping - you learn a lot but in a fun way each week

Prof White was great. Brings a lot of experience into the classroom with his professional stories. The class is centered around a group project so find good partners in the first week or so. Lectures are casual, weekly assignments are not hard, working with a real company client is interesting. Good class overall.

Applied Marketing with Prof. White has potential but is frustratingly disorganized. Expectations for assignments are unclear, feedback is almost nonexistent, and participation rarely gets above 4/5 unless you dominate class discussions. His changing expectations and lack of clarity make it hard to feel rewarded for your effort.

Had him for special topics business class: BUSA 3891-02: Digital Marketing and Social Media. He is the best business prof. and class is super fun and insightful. He is incredibly smart and had an amazing career. He cares about students and class is based on a consulting project, quizzes, and in-class projects. Little homework outside of class.

Brad White is a marketing genius. One of the smartest business profs I've taken. You get to do a marketing case project for a company and then present to their head of strategy at the end of the semester. The random group thing is annoying but good practice for the real world.

Be prepared to get 3/5 participation points every class. Doesn't matter how many questions u answer or how insightful your comments are. U will be randomly assigned in a group of 2 for the whole semester & have to complete enough work for 5 people every single week. Doesn't teach. Wastes class time. I've gotten absolutely nothing out of this class.
This course is not difficult. But it is not fun either.

The CS department is not known for being a social community. This class is a break in that pattern. Group presentations take up half of all classes and the discussions are interesting if you involve yourself. Prof. is kind and does a great job proctoring the class . The quizzes can be tough, but if you review the slides you will get an A.

She's not an amazing lecturer but she is clear. The content is just not all that interesting. She does participation quizzes but she gives an insane amount of extra credit opportunities to the point where you can do none of the quizzes and still end >100%. Allows AI usage on assignments. Everything is take-home.
