Very good professor. Not sure why the rating is so low. She really cares about her students and often asks for feedback to make the class more engaging, including choosing interesting datasets for assignments. The course is mostly basic coding, so a little boring, but it's simple and useful. She's very passionate. I would take her again.

Not the best professor but the easiest class you will ever take. Use AI (allowed and you are supposed to) and turn in assignments on time and there is no way you will get lower than a 110%. If you see this as the baseline for your future in data science, don't take. If you need it for credit and need an A, must take.

She is not that great of a teacher to be honest but the class makes up for it by being super easy. She does have a bit of an accent but it is not difficult to understand her at all. She really does try to make the class engaging but it is just coding so there isn't much you can do.
A lot of the class is taught by group projects overviewing a section of textbook. Overall a great brain break and easy A.

I honestly thought she was so funny and this class is very easy to do well in - idk why she has a low rating. As long as you show up and do the homework you will get an A. Very chill class and I learned a lot about current events due to the discussion assignments.
She gives everyone A if you just participate and do the million discussion posts and assignments which are like small papers every other week. it is just busywork but easy A.

Easiest class ever, but lowkey feels like a waste of time. Not the professor's fault, more so the university for forcing us to take ethics. Obvs gonna be boring if you stay silent the entire time, but if you actually talk and try to relax a little, or use it as a brain break, its actually fairly fun. HWs and discussion posts are annoying tho

Honestly, she's a passionate professor who cares about her students. I learned a lot about modern issues regarding computer ethics. She deserves 5 stars imo and I would take her again. She's funny, down to earth, sets clear expectations, and gives fair amounts of work
this class felt like experiencing a reboot of The Office. I've never laughed so hard while simultaneously wanting to d*e. Easy A

Advertised from the start as an easy A class. Very boring and lectures are hard to understand. Take home midterm and final. AI allowed on homework. Very easy class but I've learned nothing. Professor seems sweet but makes it easy to the point you don't learn.

This is an easy class. She doesn't allow you to use your phone, and you'll definitely fall asleep in class. But would you really rather have a class that requires effort? Take the free nap time. I write her biweekly papers in 30 minutes. Just write whatever comes to your mind, include one or two references, and you'll get full credit.

For such a poorly structured required course, she teaches it fairly well. Her policies, while annoying, are honestly fine. Y'all can last 150 mins a week w/o your phone. She doesn't teach, there are 9ish groups that present topics/chapters throughout semester. Basically a discussion class. Sometimes boring but decently interesting. She's kind too.

Professor Narasimham specializes in computer ethics, not data science. While she understood the field, sometimes her lectures were inconsistent and confusing, and she occasionally asked the students for coding help. There was a lot of homework and two exams but it was graded lightly. I learned more about coding in R than data science in this class.

boring lectures but easy class. tbh the other reviews are too negative. complaining about a docked point when you can lose 34 pts to still get an A is crazy to me. grading is slow but thats more on the TAs/graders. idk why ppl are complaining about a free A
Took DS1000 with her. Not problematic, but boring lectures and low attendance pay off. Material was recycled from previous semesters and is generally fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It seems like she knows very little about what she is teaching and the problem sets are assigned almost weekly but will not be graded until months later. I turned one in one singular hour late and I was docked an entire point. Its quite astounding considering that I had submitted it 2 months ago and it was finally graded now. Do not take with her.

Awful professor. Easy A, will bore you to death and say nonsense.

"The golden rule is to treat others as you want to be treated. But that can be difficult, because you don't know how others want to be treated. Some people want to be treated this way and others want to be treated differently."

Real quote by her. Feel smarter yet? What's your MBTI?
Very boring class, tedious discussion board and weekly assignments, one group presentation, online finals, very easy but class is not good

I took the online version of the class, most of the assignments are just busy work and there is a decent amount of reading to do. Quizzes seem more focused on the specific details rather than the principles which made it less enjoyable. Don't particularly recommend this class unless you're fine learning mainly from the textbook.

She's nice, but this class is really annoying. Her grading is good (thankfully), but her TA does it anyway. She is teaching in the CS department but barely knows anything about basic technology. If you care about CS ethics, this is a horrible class. If you only care about a good grade, just show up, do your assignments, and you'll be fine.

She reads directly from the textbook during lectures and knows nothing about R, less than what the students know. Lectures are mindnumbingly boring and she doesn't know what she's talking about most of the time anyway, but attendance is a big part of your grade. Tests are relatively easy and take home, but they're not even a huge part of your grade

Not a great lecturer, slides are unclear and the textbook is not super helpful. Avoid this professor if you can. Not necessarily difficult, but very stressful and not often helpful. The professor seems to know less about R than most students. Exams are take home, but the time limit is impossible. Avoid this professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Narasimham is caring and chill. The class is basically a statistics class using R. Attendance is mandatory, but she allows 2 unexcused absence. Homework weighs heavy. Midterms and Finals all open-book and take home.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are divided between group presentations (very fun; include debates, activities) and boring slides. Attendance is graded, so you should show up. Quizzes are nitpicky but pull directly from textbook; worth skimming for details. Prof. Narasimham is not super exciting but very nice, and the class is pretty straightforward. Recommend for easy A

Most boring class of all time. Attendance is mandatory and most students gaze off or do other work. Her slides are copied and pasted from the textbook. Easy class to do well in though because 50% of the grade is homework and both exams are take-home and open notes. If you confused use the TA. Gayathri's chill, but a tough class to get through.

Worst prof so far at Vandy. 

If you need DS2100, wait for Vandy to find another prof to teach this class.

She had ZERO experience with R and she was learning while teaching. 
Lectures were super confusing and boring. 
This course does not cover R syntax. 
Reading textbooks on your own is better.
Don't take if you don't know R and stats prior.

One of the worst classes I've taken at Vandy - the content, and her teaching, were equally terrible. Her lecture slides are useless, and I learnt better (if anything) by skimming the textbook. Unresponsive, grading is SO SLOW, assignments are unhelpful, she doesn't rly code at all either.

She reads from the textbook. I literally learnt nothing in this class. Lectures were confusing because she was also confused. This class would have been not only easy but at the very least manageable if there was another professor teaching it. Don't take her!

Narasimham gets a bad rep bc she "doesn't teach," but tbh CS1151 is basically a discussion class, so there's not much for her to be lecturing about. She's extremely accommodating w extensions or absences as long as u let her know beforehand. 

Quizzes & exams are online, material straight from textbook. She replies quickly to emails. Nice prof!

Terrible. She was learning the content as she was teaching it, and often gave incorrect info about R code, or skipped concepts because she didn't understand them. Unresponsive - never got back to me about a question I had. Taught from the book which made her lectures quite useless, with unhelpful lecture slides and annoying attendance requirements.

Easiest class i've ever taken at this school. everything is basically graded on completion, can do quizzes/final at home. prof can be a little snarky and lecture is boring but worth dealing with for the A.

Narasimham barely teaches, half the class is taught by student presentations. Participation grades, which sucks because otherwise no-one would show up other than for their own presentation. Prof has a lackluster tech knowledge. Grades SO SLOW, no presentations graded til the last week of class even though it was a decent % of grade. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She fine. Took it over the summer and received no feedback on papers for literally the entire course of the class. She grades the first two assignments and then proceeds to give you no feedback the rest of the course period. You simply don't know how you're doing beyond those first two assignments and your auto-graded quizzes. Still an easy class.

A LOT of writing each week (discussion+paper) which is annoying but more completion except a few weird rules like needing a citation/no contractions. One team presents a unit/week. Mostly common sense but some quiz q's were really specific. Kinda salty and opinionated but tries to be fun. I was surprised about her lack of tech knowledge at times.

Although this class is painfully boring, I've heard it's significantly easier with Narasimham than any other teacher, so take her for CS & Ethics if you have to. Grading is super arbitrary, so make sure you have a works cited and don't use contractions on all of your assignments, and make sure you don't repeat the 1st sentence of discussion posts.

Prof GN is one of the best professors I've taken till now. Her lectures are great and at the end of the semester, I actually felt that I learned something (which is not true for most writing heavy classes). I attended college remotely from the other side of the planet and she was very caring considering the time difference. I surely recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This was probably the most boring course I have ever taken. The first half is all common sense if you are under 50 years old. Dr. N rarely teaches if ever. This class is exclusively taught through presentations by other students. She is also very salty. I'd only take this if you have to.

Such a caring and understanding professor. Lots of weekly discussion posts and assignments but are not graded harshly at all. Quizzes are usually once every two weeks and there is one group project. Participation is part of the grade but you can easily earn those points.

This is the professor to take. She's hilarious and ridiculously nice/friendly. Cares about the students and makes class engaging with discussions every class. Class is an absolute joke grade wise- just weekly assignments and discussion posts and some quizzes here and there. Definitely this prof for good discussions and a nice professor.

A super nice lady! She doesn't really explain the material, but if you do the reading you'll be fine. Go to class and participate. Her exams aren't too hard. There are 4 and only 3 count towards your grade. The paper and projects are easy and interesting. Take psych 1630 with her! She's easy and fun.
HARD. not clear on what you want to write - confusing material. you do not need to go to class (not worth it to go) but a lot of confusing readings and all in all wrote about 50 pages.
Class is very easy--you get a cheat sheet or take home exams. Group work is encouraged on quizzes. Not the clearest teacher but it is not hard to get a B+ or A-

This woman is so sweet. She LOVES participation so speak up. It is not necessary to read the book but it will help greatly on the exams. There are only 4 exams and you only have to take 3 if you do well of the first 3. She is so easy. There is not homework other than reading and one group presentation and two essays (easy). fun topic too! good clas

Great class to take for an easy A. Low work load and she's a really nice lady. You get to choose 15 out of 20 multiple choice questions and 4 out of 10 short answer questions. Just take notes from the book and you'll be golden.
always showed up late to class. barely taught us. can't understand. study guides are way to vague, helpful, but extremely vague for the exam.

class is pointless, but attendance is mandatory. It's an easy class if you don't mind teaching yourself and reading a ton from a dense textbook. You can get a 100 by memorizing the study guide, but mine are usually 15 pages each, so that's a lot to memorize...

She is a VERY nice lady. However, she is the most boring teacher ever. There is no point in going to class, because she gives you a study guide that lists exactly what you need to know for her tests. However, attendance does count towards your grade. Simply filling out the study guide before the test will guarantee an A.

So easy. She gives quizzes in class, then answers them on the board. Tests are not much harder, especially if you keep up with the readings and do all the homework problems before the test. You get to bring a formula sheet to the tests with anything you want on the sheet. GPA booster

The sweetest woman in the whole world, but her classes are kind of pointless. she tends to just read off of her slides. however, her tests are pretty easy and she will often give away the answer if you ask her for help during the test!
She is a really sweet lady, but hard to understand and forgetful. She is however very understanding and pleasant to be around.

She was unorganized & inefficient. She often posted our readings the night before we were supposed to have them read & when it came time to discuss them, she hadn't even read what she had assigned. The class discussions were scattered at best & always ended up off-topic. Gayathri is really nice and all, but she just doesn't cut it as a professor.
No Comments

She is a really nice and caring person, but she is a little confusing to have as a teacher. She does not go over specifics for tests, just broad answers. She sometimes does not know the material. I do know, that her class was easier than the other courses and her final is optional if you do well on the two other tests.
Very difficult to understand (based on thick accent and knowledge).  There is no point in reading the texts because they serve absolutely no purpose in any of the assignments.

Gonzales is actually so caring and kind to his students, and even though the material seems intimidating, he does a great job explaining it and always encourages discussions. There are a few very short quizzes and debates in this class, but he's an easy grader. He's really a great person overall and this class isn't difficult.

Professor Gonzales is funny, incredibly caring, and personable! I also found the class material to be quite useful. He prioritizes learning and is understanding of people's circumstances. I also felt that we had some great discussions in his class. The only thing is that he is so busy that it can be difficult to reach him outside class.

Professor Gonzales is such a gem. He is the kindest, most understanding prof I have ever had. He genuinely just wants you to leave the class feeling comfortable in Stata and has no interest in making your life difficult. This class was a breath of fresh air. Very manageable class!
The best professor I have had a Vandy this far. He genuinely cares about the well being of his students. Loved the class.

Dr.Gonzales is deeply invested in your growth. This course involves Stata but for people with no experience, he guided them smoothly to the final deliverable of a policy-relevant research paper. Great mentor and person to chat with.

One of the nicest Professors at Vanderbilt; however, this class was super challenging for me compared to any other MHS class that I have taken. I think that he shifted his syllabus this semester to make exams/quizzes more serious which definitely caught me surprise. Tough class but nice guy,
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Gonzales is amazing! He is kind and caring. For example, he extended deadlines for assignments to relieve his student's stress.
One of the nicest people on this planet. Not even a PPS major and I enjoyed the class. Def take it

Dr. Gonzales is one of the best profs at Vandy. The class is easy, he prioritizes understanding class material over grades, and makes topics like insurance and policy interesting. He is incredibly kind, super flexible with deadlines, genuinely supports students through personal challenges, and makes mental health a priority. Take this class!

Prof. Gonzales is literally the best professor at Vanderbilt. He cares so much about his students, always willing to extend deadlines and accommodate students' needs. Additionally, he is incredibly knowledgeable and helps mentor students.

I cannot speak more highly of Dr. Gonzales nor this class. It was an absolutely wonderful class to just learn about health care and gain perspective on current events. The class is extremely chill; Dr. Gonzales really cares more that you learn something than the grade. Highly recommend this class to all who want to learn more about health care!

Healthcare Under Trump is a class that everybody who's interested in a career in health needs to take. It gives you an excellent, objective look a healthcare in the United States. Dr. Gonzales is the nicest and most caring professor I have had at Vanderbilt. He'll always listen to students and is available whenever needed.

Healthcare Under Trump is a must take for all MHS majors and anyone wanting to learn more about healthcare. Gonzales is probably the most caring professor I have had at Vandy. He'll give you extensions if you need them. You learn a ton, and if you put in work, you'll do well. He really just wants what is best for his students.
This guy is awesome. He's so passionate about music and so interesting, I loved attending class. Assignments and tests were easy. Offers extra credit. He's super fun to talk to in office hours too!

Easy, fun class. Professor Fry is incredibly passionate about music, and it shows in his teaching. I loved having the opportunity to learn about the history of rock music in his class. Just show up because attendance matters, write good essays, and you will do well!

Proffesor fry's class was very enjoyable. He wants every student to enjoy and appreciate the music he shows us in class. Although the readings are somewhat tedious, you can skim through them and get the bigger picture.

Free ass class, spent every lecture playing games or getting busy work done. You dont have to do any of the readings, tests are open note so you can prepare a great study guide... 4 papers are easy to score 90's on. How much time you spend on the paper is up to you. Offers hella EC. If you dont get an A in this class youre dumb.

attendance mandatory. 4 assignments. grading is unclear, limited feedback, so hard to know how you can improve. lots of busy work, and assignments take a decent amount of time to complete. dont take unless you have to. prof is kind and understanding, but boy can lecture drag on and feel pointless at times. He has some fun stories tho!
Pretty easy course if you just show up to class and do the assignments. The two exams are completely open note, so just prepare before the exams.

This class is super interesting and Fry is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable on rock history. There's 4 papers, but they're all personal and reflective. Class has readings but they're super interesting, often interviews with artists. His lectures are engaging and he really cares about sharing this music with students.
Robbie is a super great professor, only 4 essays over the semester and 2 open note exams. Very chill grader, would recommend any of his courses!

Dr. Fry is a great professor. I would recommend taking his courses! His grading standard is straightforward. In-class exams. He frequently references his passion for music and is a good reminder of what you are here for. He is always prepared for class and is engaged. A few papers to be completed throughout the semester. Off-campus solo trips.

I took Rock with Dr. Chase last year and compared to this guy she's so much better. We had fewer assignments, didn't have to go to a museum, didn't have any readings or hw, and learned a lot more actual historical content and facts. Dr. F just rants and goes on tangents about him meeting rock stars or talks about his kids and glazes Pat Boone.

Dr. Fry is beyond passionate about what he freeflows lectures with simple slides. If you pay attention in class, then the 3 papers and 2 non-cumulative tests are easy. Keep a detailed notes document, skim the readings, and then listen in class. But jazz was interesting, great TA, and enjoyed lectures for the most part.

took this for axle, this needs to be a W class ngl. ~4 essays, ~3 exams. each exam (+ final) has 5 Q's, one of them is given beforehand. all of them are long response Q's. i noticed he gave higher scores for longer/yappier responses...? i bought the txtbk, but tbh not needed. his slides have like 5 words, so pay attention and take notes in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Fry is so passionate about ethnomusicology and teaching, and his lectures show that. He is a bit slow with grading, and feedback is not very personalized. Do the readings, and you will succeed; skip them, and you will struggle. Make sure to go to his extra credit opportunities; they really do help out your grade a ton!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Got an A but would not recommend taking as an elective; I only took this course because of Blair requirements. The exams are oddly specific and based on weekly very scholarly readings that I gave up on doing. Professor Fry is very nice and enthusiastic, but is unfortunately slow with grading. Also, it seems like Miranda's section was easier.

Dr. Fry is a super sweet guy and very knowledgeable about music. However, his class is very boring. We listen to music occasionally, but it is mostly lectures. There are three relatively easy written assignments and two short answer exams where you get the questions before. Not a super difficult class, but pretty boring. Love Dr. Fry though

Fry is a good lecturer, very passionate about the subject, but unfortunately is too tough of a grader for a MUSL course- don't take if you're looking for an easy A. Also don't expect him to answer emails outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super caring about his students and absolutely loves what he does. Lectures are interesting and exciting, and he clearly wants his students to succeed. Only a few open-book online tests and some written assignments that are not graded harshly. If you read the material he assigns and use his study guides, you will be just fine in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fry is very passionate about his job and it shows in his lectures. He is very knowledgeable about music and I felt comfortable asking him questions during class. The class is not difficult but that doesn't mean you can slack off for an A. For the essays, there is a rubric but it is not very clear which is my only issue with the class.

Prof. Fry loves the blues and it showed in his lectures. We had 4 written papers (3-5 pages) 3 exams that were virtual and outside of class were all essay focused, no multiple choice. Attendance was mandatory but he only took it a few times.

robbie is an absolute homie, but the class is so boring. i dont really know what i expected with this class, but its fairly easy and you can tell robbie loves his job. its four 4 paper papers, and three essay tests (5 shorter essays). if you dont like jazz music, dont take it. if you do and need an American History credit, take it.

Very easy professor and an easy A. All exams are take-home and the questions are all from his study guides. As long as you do the work and answer all of the questions on his study guides, you will ace the exams. Attendance is mandatory.

As a person, Dr. Fry is great. Very enthusiastic and clearly cares about music & his students. However, a lot of what he discussed in lectures was not relevant to the exams. The four writing assignments were fine as long as you did the requirements, but the exams (which, in total, were worth 60% of your grade) were graded very harshly.

Professor Fry is a cool dude but he's a very tough grader. Do not expect to coast in this class or take it for an easy AXLE credit you will have to put in a lot of effort. I would never ever ever take a class with him again super hard. BEWARE!!!!!

Will never take Professor Fry's class again (sorry). He knows a lot and is passionate about teaching, but the only bad thing is he doesn't know how to teach. The course is reading intensive and most of the tests depend on if you read or not, but they somehow doesn't relate to the slides he provided and the stuff he talked about in class.

Hes very knowledgeable about what hes teaching, and it is quite apparent that he cares about his students. If you dont like writing that much, I dont recommend this class; however, if you dont mind it, then I 100% recommend it. Attendance is crucial for your grade. Overall, great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really love this guy. Like the class is incredibly lax -- a good bit of writing -- but it all goes hand in hand with the textbook he assigns. Tests were take home and were pretty easy, and if you didn't do well I believe he had opportunities to go back and look at your grade with valid criticism. Extra credit exists too.

Great professor. Class wasn't stupidly easy but got by with minimal work. I only read the specific readings that the papers were about. 4 papers and two open note midterms. Simple and interesting axle credit - would totally recommend. Fry is also legitimately cool, we talk about Thundercat and Kendrick Lamar.

I love Dr. Fry! He is, without a doubt, my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He gives great lectures and really cares about what he's teaching. He is extremely understanding and will help you out as best as he can (without being a pushover). Such a funny guy and an amazing teacher. I HIGHLY recommend him.
Prof. Fry is a nice, cool guy. Lectures are interesting but scattered. I showed up to class and took notes and I was fine. Write everything you know on assignments.
Robbie is very passionate about what he teaches. Lectures can be a little all over the place. Best way to thrive in this class is to keep up with the readings and participate in class.

Prof. Fry is a really chill guy and super passionate about music. He doesn't always know exactly how he wants his class to go, but it's mostly because he cares more about the material and learning than course logistics. Overall, very accessible and caring if you need to talk about the material or assignments. Three tests and four 3-page assignments

He's a great guy who knows a lot about jazz and music history. However, lectures are scattered and grading is very inconsistent. I've reached the end of the semester and have only received a fraction of my grades. You most likely won't have any idea what your grade is until it's too late. Do not miss class or turn in work late.

Professor Fry is freaking amazing. This was my favorite class during the semester and he made me care about the material. He cares and knows a lot about his content, he has a lot to say and interesting examples to get the class engaged. He tries to help you as much as possible and is willing to do whatever to help you succeed.

Robbie Fry is one of the most passionate professors at Vanderbilt. He really cares about the subject he is teaching and is so happy when students engage with the material. The class consisted of four essays (3-5 pages each), two exams, and a non-cumulative final. As long as you skim readings and include quotes in your essays/exams, you'll get an A!

Robbie is super passionate about music and wants to share that with students. Kind, compassionate and wants to support you. Tests and papers require a lot of writing (need quotes/sources!) but have may ways to give a "correct" or good answer. Need to do some work to get an A, but very interesting class with a cool prof

Professor Fry is very passionate about all kinds of music and Nashville so I learned many fun facts, but the "take-home" quizzes were quite challenging and sometimes on content we hadn't even discussed in class because he can be forgetful about what he has said in different sections. Work early on the final group project or you will have regrets!
Not hard at all. I put in maybe 10 hours of work total the entire semester outside of class, which was 4 papers and studying for the midterm and final.

Prof. Fry is possibly the worst lecturer Ive taken at Vanderbilt. Its not even that hes uncharismatic, but he cannot remember what he has previously discussed, which leads to constantly repeating himself. Learned at most 10 minutes of new content per hour. Tests are too hard, dont match the class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Robbie is an excellent professor. Extremely enthusiastic about the subject to the point where I, taking this class without much choice, feel confident and excited about the material. Lectures are interesting, so though he takes attendance, it's fun to be in class anyway. Easy and understanding grader/professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class will be very fun for those who like jazz. Papers are easily graded (just quote some from the book). Midterm questions are almost the same each year. If you make a study guide and study the tests are so easy (but the study guide will be like 15 pages). Just take notes from the lecture but you don't really need to concentrate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cool guy. I didn't go to office hours, but he seemed to be open all the time. We did some really fun stuff in class, very engaging lecturer. There are only 7 assignments the whole time, in addition to attendance, though, so be careful there. Make sure you come to class. Even though it was a well-sized lecture, he sent around an attendance sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My favorite class so far at Vanderbilt. Dr. Fry loves what he teaches about, and it is so fun to watch. I adore him. The content of the class is really cool. There is a midterm and a final which are all short answer questions. If you write everything you know with examples you should be fine. This class is easy and fun! TAKE IT.

Super passionate and knowledgeable. Very personable and caring. Make sure you take notes all semester long so you are ready for the midterm and final. 5 short papers about your personal encounters with music and a long paper/ethnography project due at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: @RobbieFry is a professor who absolutely LOVES geeking out about music with his students. He assigns several (fairly-softly-graded) papers a semester, along with a final project. If you do the readings (about 20 mid-sized pages a week) and go to class with an open mind- you will do fine. (test tip: they test your ability to think, not memorize).
Fry is an intelligent teacher who graduated from Henderson State University. However, this course is the most pointless class ever and the exams are unrealistically specific.

Fry is the absolute bomb. My favorite prof last semester, fry is funny, intelligent, crystal clear and willing to help any of his students. Because of him, survey of jazz was my favorite course where I really learned a lot of content that I didn't anticipate to retain. Absolutely recommend to anyone, even people who aren't musicians.

Super interesting class and Dr. Fry is definitely really passionate about jazz. You can get away with not doing the readings as long as you include them in your papers. Attendance at lecture is mandatory but it's interesting if you want to pay attention but not necessary if you want to zone out. Goes out of his way to find outside opportunities

Attendance is mandatory which is annoying because the lectures don't help all that much for the tests. I got an A without ever doing the assigned readings so ignore the "You must do the readings" posts. Show up, do other homework in the class, easy essay assignments, do the extra credit, and cram for the tests and you should get an A fairly easily.

One of the best classes I have taken. Dr. Fry is extremely passionate about music, so much so that I cared without any prior knowledge. Half of the lectures were filled with listening to great music, and he provided a comprehensive study guide before the midterm and final. As long as you pay attention to him, you will do fine. Highly recommend it!
DO THE READINGS

The material is interesting towards the end of the course, but the beginning is very tedious. The tests are really comprehensive, but if you fill out the study guide you should be good. There are 5 essays throughout the semester, but they're not too difficult. His lectures are scattered - be sure to take notes.

Fry really loves his topic and wants all his students to love it as well. Going to class and listening and taking notes is helpful. For the midterm and final, you have to know what Fry has been saying and talking about throughout the semester and you have to know the readings and music. Papers are easy.

Professor Fry is obviously really into the subject, but his lectures are impossibly long and boring. A good amount of my class would fall asleep during his lectures. The papers are super easy, but very mundane. Exams aren't too bad as long as you've gone to class and done most of the readings. If you know the study guide you'll get an A.

Be warned that THIS CLASS IS NOT AN EASY 'A''A-'! The relaxed atmosphere of lecture gives you a distorted perception of how involved the papers and tests are. If you want to get A's on these tests, you have to write out 16 pages single space (as prompted by his study guide) of random facts and memorize them.
Put in effort and you will do well.

He is awesome and passionate. It's also a big lecture so you don't have to pay attention. I learned a lot and did well even though I spent most classes reading my own novel for fun. Class is about 40% athletes so you know it's good.

Such as easy class (all the athletes take it!). A few BS assignments during the semester, and for the midterm and final he posts a review. He's very helpful during office hours and is very interested in the subject. Easy A.

He is the nicest and most passionate professor. Even in such a big class he keeps students interested. Wants people to do well and gives students many opportunities to boost grades. Very few assignments and midterm and final were straightforward

Excellent teacher; very enthusiastic! Encourages class-discussions, has high energy lectures, but laid-back personality. We read more articles than use the text book. Five interesting writing assignments, mid-term, final exam, and project. The tests are tough, so be sure to do the review sheets he posts online. Very enjoyable class.

Professor Fry is really enthusiastic and makes the class interesting. Not monotone which is a plus. The 5 assignments he gives are easy if you write thoughtful reflections; he doesn't expect perfect essay form or anything. Just make sure you take the first mid-term seriously, as you only have the mid term and a final to count towards your grade.

A very interesting class, especially if you're into music.  Five essays, but the grading is fairly easy if you do a good job.  The tests (one midterm and the final) are very easy and are basically just memorization.

Fry is a fantastic professor, and the fact that he's so passionate about the material makes the class all the more interesting.  It's definitely an easy A, but it can be fairly time-consuming between all of the small assignments you have to complete.  He's also strict with attendance, so go to class.  A fascinating course, definitely recommend.

Fry is the nicest dude ever and the class is super easy.  Study a little before the tests and you'll get an A.  The short writing assignments are super easy, make sure u do citations for 10/10.  Final paper is graded so easily.  Definitely take

One of the best professors at Vanderbilt.  Extremely passionate about the importance of music.  I took Survey of Jazz and was pleasantly surprised to find that it was so much more than music appreciation.  Fry uses the music as a lens with which to study the social and political climates throughout history.  Take Fry at some point.

I liked his lectures, and he clearly loves what he teaches. As the grades go, make sure to cite! He gave me an A+ on the final paper and I did it the day before. Very nice, interesting class (World Music). I got a C on the final but still got an A in the class.

Robbie is a pleasure to work with, and it's impossible to leave this class without developing a genuine interest in and respect for jazz. The man is so passionate, and his random rants really display his genuine love of his field.

Survey of Jazz. Very passionate about music. Must take notes. The book was unnecessary, everything was in his (boring) but well-outlined powerpoints. Gives extra credit. Takes sporadic attendance in his smaller lecture classes (esp. if it looks empty) and will dock your grade if you happen to miss those days. Not a heavy work load, either.

Such an amazing professor. Not the easiest material, especially if you aren't a huge music buff, but he lets you know exactly what is going to be on the test so one night of cramming is all that is needed. Also grades papers really easily. Definitely take any class with him!
If you don't like music, don't take this. Any music junky will thrive and easily get an A. Listen to the songs! K now the songs. It kills everyone on the first test. Overall very fun

NOT AN EASY A. He will cream you on attendance and some redundant listening journal sprawling over 60 pages. If you are not seriously interested in the Blues, do not take this class because it will come back to haunt you.

Class is interesting. Just copy notes from the slides he puts up in class and you'll fun fine. Have to know the songs from the textbook that he plays in class (title, artist, genre) and that's it. Other than that, don't read the text. Take advantage of the freedom he gives you for writing journal entries and papers- can make it interesting.
Great teacher. Go to class and take notes!! Study the notes, and you'll do fine on tests. A couple of papers graded very easy

Dr. Fry really makes this class very enjoyable and actually takes you to many different destinations.  The material is very interesting, and the class is definitely one of the best at Vandy. There are four 3-page papers, one term paper, and a travel journal (no tests!), so this class is very enjoyable and not very stressful, and you learn a lot!
Definitely not an easy A.  Tests were surprisingly detailed for a pop music class.  If you take this class, don;t sleep on it.

I've taken three classes w/ Prof. Fry, World Music, Jazz, and Music and Tourism. Jazz was really fun, World Music the tests were crazy hard but the papers were graded easily, and Music and Tourism is so legit. You get to tour places in Nashville like the Ryman and then write response papers and discuss it. Robbie's the best!

I had him for Jazz and World music. He is an absolutely fabulous teacher, mostly because he is so passionate about the subject. He gets so excited about what he's teaching that it's hard not to love it. Both are fairly easy classes, but I had some music background going in. Great teacher :)

This class starts out hard, the first exam you probably won't do too well. but it gets a LOT more interesting by the second and third exam. The material also gets easier. There are three papers that are graded reallyyyy easy. The final paper (7-10) pages is graded easy as well. I recommend the class.

I took the Blues this semester for an Easy A. He told me in office hours that he usually only takes attendance 3 times a semester, but everyone was skipping a lot this semester for some reason. He says that you don't have to be a music major to do well in this class, but I definitely felt there was too much music lingo for my comfort.

Great professor, incredibly passionate about the blues and pop music. Goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material and do well. He takes attendance if he thinks it's necessary (almost every day this semester). 3 easy response papers, 3 exams including the final - if you show up and actually pay attention, you'll get an A.

Professor Fry is the most passionate teacher i have had. His excitement is almost contagious. I took this class for the easy A and ended up getting into the material. His lectures are enjoyable not tedious with youtube clips and he allows laptop use. There are 3 EASYpapers and 3 tests that require some studying but as long as u go to class u do fin

I had Dr. Fry for Blues and World Music.  Fry is really passionate about the subject and is extremely dedicated to teaching.  The classes were both a nice 1-hour break to the school day, and I would definitely recommend taking them with him.  If you put in the work and are not a complete moron (like the person who posted below me), it is an easy A.

This Class in NOT an EASY A. This guy actually wants you to go to class. He will take attendance until everyone goes. I took this class for an easy A, not to learn about the Blues. NO EASY A. ATTENDANCE MANDATORY. 3 EXAMS WITH AN AVERAGE SCORE OF 80! ONE FINAL PAPER. 3 2 PG PAPERS. BORING SUBJECT.

He is incredibly passionate about what he teaches, and tried (and mostly succeeded) to make the subjects interesting for those of us not really interested in World Music. The class is not difficult if you put in at least minimal effort, but you do have to show up and at least skim the readings. My one complaint would be the ethnographic project.

He's a really chill guy. Just show up to class to take notes on his slides and you will be fine. He'll let you know before hand if you really need to read the book. He loves what he teaches and is a really cool guy. Great way to fulfill Intl. requirement

A terrific professor. Reasonable workload, generous grading, and interesting material. He's passionate about his subjects and is extremely well-informed. I absolutely recommend taking a class with Robbie Fry.

I am not a music person, and just took the class for an elective. Dr. Fry sometimes assumed we had more music background then I had, but was happy to answer any of my questions. HIs enthusiasm and command of the subject made the class fun and interesting.

Robbie is an incredible professor. He is extremely passionate about the Blues and expresses that through his teaching. The class is a nice break to your day--listening to music, watching videos, listening to Robbie's personal anecdotes. the best part? it's not hard. TAKE IT!

I think this class would be easy for a music major, but he definitely teaches like everyone already has a strong basis with music and has Blair-style expectations for papers, but he doesn't explain what exactly this is, he just expects you to use the first paper to figure it out. The class isn't impossible, but it's a lot harder than I had expected
Robbie was very clear in what he was expecting from the class. He has an obvious passion for music and is very laid back. Great class. Great teacher!!

Robbie Fry is really hard. He teaches this undergraduate class like he is teaching music majors. It is not interesting at all. You have to go to performances and write papers about them. I had a lot of music background before this class and I had no idea what he was talking about most of the time. I would take Wright instead of Robbie.

If you are into music in any way, this will help you come to better appreciate where it came from. He was really nice, and made it feel personal even though there were so many people in the class. I wish I could take this class every semester, but spread out and in more detail.
Robbie is a great, enthusiastic teacher, that really has passion.  The papers and tests don't require a whole lot of thought, and this class is overall quite easy if you go to class and do your work.
No Comments
Very very cool teacher!  Great class and he lectures so clearly.  He is passionate and it shows!

Very laid back, and understands the demands of other classes. Written work is very easy, and tests aren't to bad. Super understanding about being late with work or rescheduling tests. Loves what he is teaching and it shows.

Really cool, down to earth teacher, real easy tests and not very hard assignments, just a couple essays here and there. But he wont give you anything on the tests that you had to read just go to class and get notes
robbie is alright, easy papers you dont have to do everything in order, tests are kinda easy and you can cheat on the listening part. put a little effort in for an A

Even though this is not a Gordon Rule class, you still have to write 3-4 page papers. They are not that bad considering he grades them lenient. He will give notes in Powerpoint slides and give a review sheet that sums the notes up. He tries to make the class fun and plays video clips as well.
Awesome guy!
Very easy, fun class, easy to take notes and tests are clear. Makes class fun too. And the performances are cool too

He is chill and kind professor. His lectures are straightforward and easy to understand. Contents on his lectures are directly related to exam problems, so it is relatively easy to prepare for exams. It is easy to get an A if u attend the lecture and just take a note during class.
Ghandi is super kind and, in my opinion, a great lecturer. Exams are not difficult if you study the practice tests. He is incredibly smart and a great professor overall for the economics department.
Don't understand the bad reviews. Class was extremely straightforward, just need to show up to class honestly. Tests are what is expected from the practice materials.
Lectures are extremely informative and detailed. That said, you need to S T U D Y if you want to do well on exams, because you aren't allowed notes

Ghandi is a great guy and very knowledgeable about Microeconomics. The class is difficult and his lectures do not always explain the material in a manner that is easy to digest. Thankfully, he is very helpful during his office hours and is a solid option for 3012.

Very helpful during office hours and posts notes online. Tests are quite easy with sufficient practice and have curves; they do make up large part of your grade though. He also makes connections from class material to real-world matters during lectures (ex. Tariffs, collusion, etc).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ghandi's lectures tended to be a bit dry and on the boring side, but I felt as though I came out of each lecture understanding the material. He also really cares about students and is very open to questions and discussion regarding the material. Exams are manageable but they 2 midterms and final make up 90% of your final grade.

This class felt easy. The only problem with it is that it was a bit boring, since the content is pretty cut and dry. Ghandi is very nice and genuinely cares if you put in effort. Two midterms and a final and the grade pretty much depends on that. There is a decent curve, but Ghandi never posted any of the grades/ curves which was confusing.
Doesn't post notes or slides. On occasion that he does, the writing is extremely messy and unorganized. Additionally, he will take multiple days to respond to emails.

Ghandi was great, made the class super easy but only lecturing on the things he would test you on and made that clear. Also made material for exams clear so you knew what to study. Very accessible outside class and helpful. Very smart man too.

He's honestly a great lecturer and his exams are always very representative of the class content. One thing is attendance is mandatory because he doesn't use or post slides. His review sessions are so helpful and as long as you keep up with the content you should do well.
Gets the job done. Would not go out of my way to take/avoid. Its an easy class
Easy course, nice Professor, worst lecture
If only you attend the class and take good notes you will score well.
Rubbish
The worst professor I have never met! The professor never care about his students..
how he calculated the final grade is a puzzle for all the students. Never received any feedback of homework
He is so lazy that he never correct the homework and have no feedback. What he said was not on the test was on the test.

The worst professor I have never met! The professor never care about his students. He is so lazy that he never correct the homework and have no feedback. What he said was not on the test was on the test.
I got two midterms above 90 but he gives me F in report?

S
T
U
P
I
D

Not super exciting teacher, but overall pretty easy class. Does not post slides though so missing class regularly hurts really bad. If you go to class, and study for the exams (big chunk of the grade) youll be fine.

Overall I would say Professor Ghandi is a solid professor. It can be hard to understand what he wants from his lectures sometimes, but he is very accessible and willing to help you outside of class. The content of exams is not overly difficult, but they are worded in a tricky way that makes it easy to get questions wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ghandi is very caring and is always willing to help you do your best. However, his lectures are very unstructured but important since he does not have slides to upload. Test materials are easy and similar to practice tests, but not spending enough time studying before tests can affect your performance a lot (90% of the final grade).

There's little homework that counts for completion; the most time I spent was studying for tests which you have to study hard for bc he words questions tricky. To do well you have to attend most if not all lectures to get the info. He assumes students have already taken ECON class and skips steps when explaining stuff so I had to learn myself.
Very easy class, all information needed on tests and quizzes are given in lecture. Tests are a little but difficult, but just go to lecture and you do well on the test.

Ghandi is a nice guy but he's not very good at teaching. He makes micro way more difficult than it needs to be and often stretches out 10 minutes worth of course material into 50 minutes of explanation in his lectures. Rarely posts hw, and his exams (which make up 90% of your grade) are far more difficult than the HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you already have some experience with economics. I've never taken an econ class before and was very confused, but some of my friends who had taken econ before thought it was fairly easy. Ghandi isn't a great lecturer, but the TA's were generally helpful. Curve is pretty generous.

Lectures aren't always the most interesting. Will repeat himself a lot and sometimes important information gets lost, so try and pay attention. Sometimes glosses over important stuff that shows up again later. Tests aren't super hard or long but aren't easy either and are worth a lot. Sometimes will say amusing stuff in lectures.
The goat

Ghandi is an absolute despicable educator. He withheld test grades for our second test for 2 months and only released one score before calculating our final grades. The questions he asks are worded in the strangest possible way, potentially to trick students or simply because he doesn't know what he is even trying to ask. Take a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ghandi is overall a good professor but, lacks some structure in his class. Grading is made up of 2 midterms and a final which makes them very important. You must attend his lectures as he does not teach by a book but, mentions everything on the test in his lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ghandi is the WORST Professor I have ever had to date. He is not responsive and does not care about students nor their mental health as it regards to grades. Took over a month and a half to give us our test scores back and had everyone worried. Doesnt respond to emails. This class has me withered both mentally and physically. Please RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Funny and nice guy, but lectures are boring and needlessly complicated. He's not very good at explaining concepts, so be ready to spend time out of class teaching yourself. He is also horrible at getting assignments back in a timely manner, and tests are difficult and comprise the majority of your grade. His office hours are very helpful.

Prof Gandhi is accessible and very readily answer questions in and outside the class. However, lectures and dry and he struggles to be concise and meaningfully get the point across. This is worsened by the fact that he doesn't quite follow any book so you can't really study on your own. P.S. he takes absolute ages to return work.

I usually never write ratings for professors, but Ghandi needed a rating. The professor is a nice guy and cares for the students, but his lectures are the only source of information, which are numbing, disorganized, and hard to understand. His office hours are helpful for clarification, tests are hard, but on the plus side, he is flexible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Ghandi is a bad lecturer and is even worse at giving assessments. He expects everyone to have a deep understanding of topics but only teaches things at the surface level. He is bad at explaining topics and is unorganized. Assessments are extremely difficult and do not allow students to demonstrate knowledge. Doing homework does not help. RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take this class Pass/Fail or avoid it. Ghandi is a nice guy, but a poor lecturer. You have very few opportunities to practice the concepts so the tests are incredibly difficult. He takes forever to get grades back and there is very little feedback on what you missed. I feel SO lucky I took this during corona and could switch to Pass/Fail.
Great guy and good lectures but repeats the content a lot in lectures to the point where it's mind-numbing to hear him talk. Very little homework though, but tests are kinda rly tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Decent explanations but slow and boring lectures. Tests aren't a breeze but not too difficult either; major part of grade. Hardly any homework, though optional reading and practice questions probably would have made those tests easier!

Large lecture based class. It is easy to not pay attention in the class or stop attending and fall very behind. If you stop going to class it's hard to catch yourself back up. His test multiple choice questions are very confusing. He is a very nice man and gives generous curves though. Actually get the tophat if you take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Econ 1010 was hard especially if you do not have any background in Econ at all, but Prof. Ghandi is so helpful if you go to office hours (highly recommend going). def read the textbook if you haven't had Econ before and go to class - put in work and you can do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very confusing lecture. The midterm and final are very hard as well. However, they should not be hard if all the information are made clear in the lectures. Although professor Ghandi is a very nice person, I do not recommend his ECON 1010 class.
Professor Ghandi is a great person. Unfortunately, his class is the most boring one I had so far in Vanderbilt. The information is extremely unclear, which makes Economics a headache for me.

Professor Ghandi is a really nice guy who genuinely cares about his students. However, his class is very difficult even with relatively simple subject matter. His lectures are very scattered with minimal structure and the tests contain confusing and misleading questions. Overall, he's a great guy, but I don't recommend taking his class.
tests are hard. your best bet is to never miss a lecture and just keep up in the textbook which is short and semi-helpful
he is super sweet and likable but its hard not to sleep in class and he explains things very very poorly so if you dont have an econ background at all (in high school, etc) do NOT take ghandi

Lectures are honestly very confusing and disorganized at times. That said, Professor Ghandi is extremely accessible, helpful, and just nice outside of class, so if you are having trouble definitely go to office hours a lot. Know the homework and practice test problems inside and out and tests should be fine.

Truly relaxed professor. Very accessible and helpful. Very little work for this class. Only three tests including the final, some homework/quizzes which he literally won't let you turn in with the wrong answer, and a final project, which he is very willing to help with. It is a very low maintenance class, but material near end is difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Ghandi is amazing. Seeing all the negative comments here, I felt apprehensive about having him for Intermediate Micro, but he's been one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt so far. Don't get me wrong, the class is hard. Yet, he genuinely cares about his students and is very straightforward in lectures (even review sessions for tests).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: You should be okay if you have taken AP Stats and don't take this class as an 8 am. It was hard to focus that early in the morning, especially since he lectures the whole time. We rarely had homework, in-class problems, and there was no book required for the class, so it's pretty much on you to keep up outside of class. Tests are challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic and clear when teaching, and you will be tested more on conceptual things about statistics than equations. Quizzes and homework are infrequent but relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can either go to his lectures and take notes and never use the textbook or never go to class and solely rely on the textbook. You'll be fine either way. His accent takes some getting used to but it's not too bad. He repeats concepts several times to make sure you get it, so it's really easy to get distracted.
Really nice guy, interested in the subject. Tries to assign things that will help your grade and gives really helpful homework assignments. A very good professor

This is professor Ghandi's first semester teaching and with that being said it is a frustrating class because his lectures are boring and all over the place. But he does allow you to bring in as many "cheat sheets" into the test as you want so that helps tremendously. Tests are often not representative of class material but grades super easy.

Corporate Strategy is one of my favorite classes I have taken at Vanderbilt! The class consists of weekly quizzes over the lecture and business cases and two group projects. This class is very easy to get an A in if you do the work. It's also a great introduction into consulting and Slatton makes it very entertaining and engaging.

One of my favorite classes and professors I've taken so far at Vandy. Really makes you think, and cares more that you are learning and understanding the concepts than a grade. Absolutely loved the random anecdotes he'd tell throughout the class, too!

Clearly has a lot of experience and is passionate about teaching. However, if you are not one of his favorites forget it. Very argumentative, contradicts his own instructions and made some odd/rude comments in office hours/class. Class is also very consulting heavy so if that isn't something you are interested in do not take Business Management.

Corporate strategy is HARD, and Prof. Slatton makes it digestible. He's thoughtful, caring, and creates a course that will impact your life simply because you're crossing paths with him. He cares about you attempting to learn the content and applying the concepts, not perfecting it. A gem of a class, a legend of a professor.

Slatton is truly the best professor anyone could have. I took both of his courses and wish he taught more classes. He truly cares about each one of his students and is invested in their happiness more than anything. His classes were so helpful in preparing me for internships/careers. He is very "real" in what he teaches and how he goes about it.

Not too much work, weekly quizzes require doing the readings. Very nice guy, has great advice and is down to earth. Class was very helpful for presentation skills and very interesting.

Only con is that it seems he slightly favors former students or ones that are incoming at his old firm (bain)

Couldn't respect this man more. His class was probably the most entertaining of all I have taken at Vanderbilt, and you'll learn things that are actually very relevant for your career. For someone with a resumé as accomplished as his, he is surprisingly humble which makes him very enjoyable to be around.

Best teacher and class I've ever had. Doesn't waste your time on busy work and reading and case studies actually have utility within the course and enhance your business knowledge. Don't typically enjoy academics but actually had fun in this class. Only downside could be if your group sucks for the presentations but that isn't really on him.
Top 2 prof i had at vandy and he wasn't 2. Listen to his analysis/life lessons and you will learn as much as you're willing to
Goated prof for consulting hardos like me

This was an amazing class. Great practical lectures. His breath of knowledge is impressive. He truly care about us all. The group project was challenging because my group was not good, but that could happen in the real world also- crew projects to contribute a decent amount of your grade, but you can make it up on the individual work.
I exactly enroll his busn1100W class, he is a goat! Not only for his way of grading, but for everything he gives to us: love, trust, and help in career

Business management is definitely a class I recommend, and Slatton is very experienced on the subject. Case studies due every class and group project presentations requires real work and analysis. Even if you participate/post discussion every class you could still get duct points from participation! Generally not difficult but put in the work for A
da homie

Slatton was one of the best professors I've had at Vandy. His class includes a lot of daily work, but all assignments are worthwhile and I learned a ton from the semester. The group projects suck but the workload is pretty simple since there are no exams. Take Slatton for the business minor if you can.
prof slatton rocks, please take him if you have the opportunity. you will learn so much from an experienced professional in the consulting/business field! he will definitely challenge you tho lol

Did not expect to like this class, but ended up loving Slatton. Assignments are straightforward if you follow directions and try. Group presentations are hard and time consuming, but he grades fairly. Clearly wants students to learn and develop business critical thinking. Highly recommend.

Professor Slatton is amazing and so is the class! You have a Harvard Business School case every week, group and individual quizzes every week, and two big case study presentations. Great class if you are interested in consulting or just learning about several businesses. Slatton's experience makes the class great!
Slatton is the man. Knows strategy (refers to his past industry experience) and teaches with case method to teach MBA-level concepts. Wants you to succeed

Without a doubt the best professor at Vanderbilt by a mile. I have never met a teacher who cares so much about his students, and both his courses were super transformative for anybody interested in consulting or management in general. This year the class literally ended with thunderous applause and a serenade. Enroll.

Best professor I've taken in the business minor. I learned so much just by being in class and working through the cases. I wish I would've taken him sooner in college so I could have taken more classes. There is work due every class so thats a bummer but I think it was 1000% worth it-- highly highly recommend

Prof. Slatton is undoubtedly one of the best professors you'll ever have. Not only is he very very knowledgable and able to explain, he also goes the extra mile and expands class to a place where you talk about more than academics. He has the most sound life-advice. He's willing to explain things numerous times and is very clear with expectations.

Slatton's classes force students to think about what they're saying before saying it. He can be gruff (usually not)-and he's honest with you when you miss the mark- but he takes it as well as he gives it and lets students disagree with him too. Learned a lot about business and about life in the class. Group presentations are tough but rewarding.

Professor Slatton is one of the best professors I've had! He cares about his students so much and is very accessible to talk about course-related or personal things. Corporate Strategy is relatively easy if you put some effort in. The two group case projects were really helpful, and I have learned so much from this course!

I loved Professor Slatton! He is very caring, smart, and helpful. I like how he teaches you to write concisely; as opposed to pages of fluff, he usually requires only one page of writing per assignment. My only complaint is you have to participate almost every day. As a quieter student, I always felt nervous trying to get a word in.

Professor Slatton is an amazing professor, but more importantly, an amazing mentor. Throughout my time at Vanderbilt, Slatton has proven to be a valuable sounding board for personal and professional business endeavors. I can personally attest that he cares tremendously about his students and will reciprocate your respect, effort, and care.

I am a senior at Vanderbilt, and Professor Slatton has hands down been my favorite professor at Vandy. I learned so much from his Managerial Studies course, and I liked the material because it is mainly case study based and includes lots of real world knowledge. I highly recommend him as a professor to anyone interested in business.

Professor Slatton is a well-respected, straightforward, caring professor, but he also provides an example of the real world. Your answers are not always going to be right, but he takes the time to explain why and help you improve. This was one of my favorite courses at Vanderbilt thus far, and I would highly recommend it.

Slatton makes students feel dumb. He has an inflated ego and uses class time to brag about his career accomplishments. Worst of all, his "honest" responses to student contributions end up being his excuse to be incredibly disrespectful and dismissive to students who took this class to learn. Content is decent, but Slatton made it miserable. AVOID!

I did not enjoy my experience with Slatton. Slatton claims hes honest, but he's condescending and degrading. He will brag about his work experiences and dismiss class contributions at a rate three times that at which he'll compliment students. He is convinced that his ideas are superior and calls you out for disagreeing with him. Save yourself.

Professor Slatton goes above and beyond in everything he does! Not only is his class a very achievable A, but it is incredibly useful and transformative in providing career and leadership mentorship. He is flexible during extenuating circumstances and cares deeply about his students The bad reviews are ridiculous--he just says things as they are!

Slatton has a ton of great experience and is willing to share. While he'll call you out for any dumb ideas, you learn a ton of applicable skills and information. Participation and attendance make up 25% of your grade. He wants to help you learn and grow as a person.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Slatton is super cool. His experiences are incredible and lectures are awesome. Everything in this class has a purpose. That being said, he can be abrasive regarding participation. He will call you out for having a stupid idea.

Professor Slatton is wonderful! Easily one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. He is kind, funny, yet also frank and real. I learned an incredible amount in this class, both about business and life. It's not hard and is not much work, but, best of all, all of the work has a clear purpose. Do yourself a favor and take his class!

Professor Slatton is great. It is obvious that he is really passionate about what he does and genuinely cares about his students. Participation is extremely important in this class and the number of times you talk it kept track of. But you also learn A LOT about business. The class is essentially Consulting 101 and is helpful for recruitment.
Great Professor. Profound understanding. Rewarding class if you put the effort in and yourself out there.
Best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. Hands down. Cares about students, amazing lecturer, engaging class. A lot of work but no final.

Professor Slatton is far none the most amazing professor at Vanderbilt. He truly cares about his students and tailors his lectures to ensure that every class has meaning and has a piece of advice that fits beyond the classroom. If you participate, you will receive an easy A- all he wants is for his students to care about what they are learning.

Slatton is a true gem in the Managerial Studies department. His class was incredibly enriching and rewarding. Slatton is incredible at communicating the frameworks for understanding different business decisions. His ability to bring up insightful anecdotes from his experiences at Bain is something you can't get anywhere else. Take his class.

More honest than most professors; he will tell you if you have a dumb idea. 3 5-page papers on books, a reading quiz every week, and a group presentation on a company. Not that much work, learned a decent amount. Class discussions based on made up case studies.
Love this guy. Take anything you can with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Just showed up for the first hour-ish of class (it was once a week) to take the quiz and then dipped, got an A- based on the papers and final project without ever once participating

Slatton was great. He will actually call you out when you're wrong. There are three papers and a quiz every class, super easy if you read/skim the chapter and pay attention when he goes over the answers before the quiz. You have to make the papers personal to get good grades. Not available outside of class because he flies from Cleveland every week

Best professor I had this year. Learned a lot AND got an A. The type of lecturer that inspires movies. Beware of group members that choose not to contribute to the final project! A must take professor.

Classes are once a week. You start by discussing the textbook reading (just read the summary in the back of the book), take a short & easy quiz on the reading, and then discuss the week's case study. He also incorporates inspiring books into the course that I would honestly read even if they weren't assigned.

Slatton is the man. Class is largely case-based; he never gives formal lectures, so every day is engaging. I don't understand how he's rated so poorly... Maybe because unlike most profs in the 21st century, he'll actually tell you when you're wrong.

Participation matters A LOT. 2 papers which are really easy. Group project is one of the worst at Vanderbilt. He makes you rate how well each group member did on a scale which often creates a lot of stress within the group. Outside of class he acts like he doesn't have 3 seconds to talk to you. Take for an A but you'll learn nothing.

Prof. Slatton does a great job making business scenarios come to life with case studies that the class discusses. I found his lectures helpful and engaging and will carry those lessons with me after graduation. Assigns 3 great books to read and gives a quiz at the beginning of each class. I learned a lot. Would recommend.

Loved this class. Slatton is a fantastic professor that brings great real-world experience to this class. the 2 1/2 class goes by quickly because his lectures are great. Participation matters, you have to talk twice per class for it to count towards this 10% portion of your grade. Group project is graded easily but beware of bad partners.
Funds of Management might be the easiest class at Vanderbilt. An A is definitely attainable. No homework, only work is the group project at the end. Class participation is graded so you have to go

Slatton is  one of the best professors at Vandy. You'll learn so much from the class just from listening to his experiences because he's done pretty much everything  in the business world. The books and papers he assigns actually are relevant and interesting  unlike most college assignments. He's only available once a week but is super approachable

You must participate. The TAs keep track and if you aren't raising your hand at least twice a class, you're in dangerous territory. Never read for the quizzes, just review the summaries in the back while he takes attendance. You get to drop the lowest one. The papers are super easy and the TAs grade very leniently.

Slatton is a truly inspiring professor. His real-world experience is unmatched, and you can learn something applicable to the rest of your life in every class. The final presentation is vague, but understandably so; it's more about identifying and explaining what's important for a company than following a structured format. Highly recommend!

One of my favorite profs. The books are easy reads and interesting so your flow with the papers has the potential to be straight fire. Great lecturer. He shows passion in the subject, but if you get stuck with a bad group for the final project you will miss out on an easy A class.

Slatton knows his stuff, but the TAs who grade all of your work, however, are more difficult to deal with. The quizzes make up most of your grade and they aren't hard. The group project is a pain because it is very vague, but it isn't impossible. The participation reqs, however, are impossible. Overall, great class but bad grading system.

The class isn't that difficult. The class structure makes it hard for an A. You have a quiz every class period, with each question work 5 points or .5% of your total grade. It is easy to mess up on a few quizzes and significantly hurt your chances at doing well. The rest of class is all cases, so it's interesting to engage in class.

Simply memorize vocab for easy weekly quizzes. 3 papers are graded by TAs, I wrote all mine the day before they were due and my lowest grade was a 95. TAs are great, use them for help with the final. Slatton can be condescending in class and dismiss people's ideas, but you MUST participate anyway as its a huge part of your grade. overall good class

Interesting guy with great real world experience. Required reading each week with a short quiz in class (sometimes over very specific, random information). His grading is somewhat arbitrary and based heavily on participation so make sure to participate multiple times each class. 3 papers and 1 final project are reasonable. Not bad, but not great.
Slatton is such a nice guy. Papers are very easy and straightforward. Material is not difficult either.Participation is a huge factor in your grade though so make sure you participate!
He's self interested, just likes to hear himself speak. Grades are completely arbitrary. He's never available for students, he doesn't even live in this state.

Really easy class. Professor is a great guy, knows his stuff. Practically no studying needed. Three papers to write over books, but they're simple, just do exactly what he asks for. Books can be skimmed (he recommends it actually). Final project is vague, which was frustrating. Find past students to get an idea of what he really wants to see.

This is a easy class. Teacher like to hear himself talk.  Act interested and he will tell you what a big success he was.LOL  Just when you think it cann't get any worst and you want to laugh, you have to get up. Take this class it will show there are still great story tellers.Oh if you are lucky he will tell you the story on the bridge. Touching

Enjoyed this class. It is a good overview for business (sort of a taste test -- marketing, accounting, etc.). A bit annoying to fight for comments on the case studies and you can't just say whatever. Workload is pretty light. Get a good group for your project and start early!
