totally pointless class. follow the instructions for the papers exactly and you'll get a 100. not necessary to read the books. just go to class and make sure to talk because participation is a huge part of the grade. final project is just obnoxious. he selects your group, which makes it worse. not too hard of a grader though. nice guy, bad class.

If you participate in class and write the paper as he has outlined, then you'll get an easy A. You don't have to actually read the books and make sure you participate in class. He is a nice guy who has a lot of experience in the industry.
talking in class is a must, fight for comments even if they mean nothing. follow the instructions for papers EXACTLY.  also, get in a good group for the final project and start early.

Great guy! Really passionate about what he does, but not to where he is upset when you don't share that passion. He is very lenient grader, and want to help you get an A - he cares more about the effort you put in than what the final product looks like which is apparent in the way he grades. If you're worried to take this class, you shouldn't be.

All around chill guy. Easy to talk to. Class was interesting and useful. Mix of academic discussion and technical application. A few readings, two papers, two projects, and a few coding assignments - nothing hard. Best thing to do is show up and make a genuine effort.
Absolute goat, very understanding and is just an all around specimen. Could save the titanic

Daniel Genkins is a great professor. He works hard to make sure that people from all majors find his class digestible. You really do get out what you put in in this class. I wish that he made it slightly more difficult because there is no distinguishing between a little effort and a lot of effort, but he's probably too nice to change that.

Professor Genkins is one of the best professors I've had during my time at Vanderbilt. I don't think I could recommend someone more for anyone who needs an humanities AXLE course. This class was exciting, engaging, and thorough. The digital humanities part of the class is intriguing and unique, it was one of my favorite parts of the class!
The first prof I've ever had that genuinely tries to trick you.Try to get your hands on a test bank bc lots of upperclassmen have them and he doesn't change exams much so it's a HUGE advantage

Gave good lectures. Hardest CS core class, so exams and quizzes were very difficult. Exams/Quizzes curved to 85. 15 minute quiz nearly every Friday so be prepared to do extensive reading every week to prepare. Attendance is not mandatory, but recommended due to difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor and lectures. Talks like the 44th president peak lectures

Great lecturer and clearly engaged with the content. The quizzes/exams are a good challenge and curved. Wish he would shift more focus on the PAs and force application of the design patterns discussed in class. 4% extra credit is offered at the end of the semester (probably not great for inflation bwdik)

Overall tough class, very harsh deadlines for Friday 8am. Good lecturer and very helpful to go to class, but sometimes gets boring and his lecture slides are difficult to understand if you did not go to class. PAs are challenging, and biweekly quizzes force you to review content every week. Very nice guy but strict as a prof.

My favorite CS professor so far. I generally found the lectures engaging. While the quizzes are annoying, the questions and grading are fair. Assignments are relatively straightforward and provide an opportunity to bring up your grade if you struggle with quizzes/exams.

Once you get through ISD, Hemingway keeps his structured quiz/exams/PAs style and incredibly fast pace of going through the curriculum, but for Web Dev it's clear that he cares the most about individual success of everyone in the class. He consistently gives real-world examples and challenges students as much as he encourages them. Wonderful prof.

He clearly cares about his students and does a great job teaching a tough class. The lectures are engaging, and while the weekly quizzes, midterms, and coding projects are challenging, there's extra credit and he's always willing to help.
Love him! Definitely my favorite CS professor at Vandy. He really cares about his students, even though he can be tough at times. Highly recommend!

3rd course with him. I've had my issues with him but just follow deadlines! He is helpful within reason when things pop up but to me he has been the most practical CS prof. Vandy isnt as competitve with CS roles and Hemingways classes try to fix this issue by being challenging and practical. if you just do the assignments on time you will succeed.

I loved his class and he's a great lecturer and I was doing pretty well in it, but I stayed up all night working on a PA and only turned it in a few minutes late but he wouldn't let me get any credit and gave me a 0.
Don't take him for software design. Just stay at home every day and not go to any of his classes because you get nothing for going to class. It all just ends in despair, agony, and suffering.

It sucks that assignments are due at 8 am. I vowed to go to every lecture and thus would be a lot more tired than someone that skips all the lectures and eventually I ended up missing an 8 am deadline from all the burn out while someone I know that was NEVER in class and slept in every day gets to breeze past with 100.

Lectures are awesome, ask questions. Quizzes and tests are hard but curved and aren't weighted that high in your final grade. Focus on the PAs, those are the ones that matter. Barely got average on all the exams/quizzes and thanks to the PAs I needed less than a 50 on the final for an A. You'll definitely get an A if you genuinely try.

I played League of Legend in dorm instead of going to lectures and still get an A, which means lectures are not that meaningful and you can learn on your own after class. You will feel the pain when you get a tough TA grader who may get you 50% points off in an assignment mistakenly... Grade curves and this professor are good though...

A lot of people don't like this class cause of the quizzes, but in all honesty this was one of the most useful CS classes I took here at Vandy, and Hemingway is a big reason of that. A professor who clearly knows a lot and cares about you understanding/learning the material and challenging you to grow as a coder and a student. Also he's funny.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes that cause a lot of stress, exams are hard too but both quizzes and exams are curved up to 85%, class average is usually way lower. PAs are kind of hard to understand but if you follow the directions, they are very doable. Extra credit opportunities on assignments. Good luck.
Worst professor at school

Hemingway is a solid lecturer and always enthusiastic, he can be pretty passive-aggressive though. Quizzes and exams are very difficult but are curved to 85% average, coding assignments are even harder but have lots of extra credit. Decent class but pretty tough.

GOAT of the CS department. Hemingway gives thorough, engaging lectures, and can answer just about any question you throw at him. His quizzes are pretty hard, but all material is either in the slides or the reading. I'm a senior now, and I learned more in this than any other CS class by a large margin.
Usually leaves off a lot of stuff in class, and then you are screwed for quizzes and tests. Nice guy but really doesn't seem that great of a teacher.
Class is fine; quizzes suck; EC is great. You can get an A even with mediocre quiz grades if you do the EC. However, beware of making your coding style similar to his in the assignments.
Decently nice guy, but he lacks real-world experience and overall intelligence, making him unable to truly explain the course content. Might be best for him to stick to the humanities

Professor Hemingway I hope you are reading this. You are probably the best lecturer I have had at Vandy. I know I would not have done anywhere near as well without your teaching. You manage to make a seemingly difficult class really interesting and therefore enjoyable. Thank you :)
Best lecturer I've had

This class is hard, but great professor. He is always willing to chat/help in office hours or after class. I had to start HW early and go to office hours a lot (granted, this was right after CS2201 changed from C++ to Java, so he had to gauge how much knowledge we had). Study for quizzes like they're tests. HW is not bad with help and gets better!

The quizzes and exams in his class are the easiest I've ever taken. You can get an A+ without even going to one class. The professor will give you more than 20 extra credit in the end of semester without requiring any work.

Dr. Hemingway is a nice guy, but his class structure is super odd. He gives quizzes and exams that most students do poorly on, and then curves them to an 85 so most people get a good grade in the class, but have no idea what's going on. Assignments are easy but no one even knows what they're writing, you just have to pass arbitrary tests he gives.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I marked off pop-quizzes, but you know exactly when they are. Not even Batman with prep-time could get away unscathed. The homework descriptions are written in riddles even though they aren't that hard. If there is ever another professor for this class, take them. He's not a bad guy, but he'd rather curve than make it easier for some reason...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures are decently interesting. Quizzes can be tough due to time crunch and you can't really prepare that well for them. Exams are easier but grading schemes can be weird. Ok because those are curved to an 85. Decent prof but can seem like a douchebag sometimes re late policy, regrade, tech difficulties, etc. Otherwise alright dude

Hemingway is by far my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. BDE through the roof. Some people don't like him because he's strict about late assignments but they fail to realize that he is extremely caring and will give extensions if you communicate with him. He loves what he does and it shows. If you just listen you will learn so much

Weekly Friday quizzes were brutal and difficult but all tests and quizzes were curved to a class average of 85. Hemingway is super sweet and a good lecturer but you def miss info if you miss class bc he doesn't teach word for word from the slides. It's a difficult class but you get a fair amount of time to finish all programming assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable; will answer every question you ask. Big emphasis on absolute correctness. CS3251 is essentially memorizing the intricacies of C++

This class is difficult. Dr. Hemingway is a nice guy but super strict.
1st quiz - memorize everything he says.
Then, all quizzes before design patterns - focus on writing code snippets.
Design pattern quizzes - write down everything you can remember.
Tests are easier than quizzes.
Homework isn't too hard - start early and go to office hours.

exams and quizzes feel somewhat random and are graded strictly. lectures do not teach useful or interesting material. projects take some time. it's difficult to get help through piazza.
he also overcomplicates simple concepts in his lectures and on slides, which are from like 2012 or something. he's also bad at explaining

Prof Hemingway is one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. He gives amazing and informative lectures that are always interesting. He will spend as much time as necessary on trickier subjects. Quizzes are difficult but fair and projects are decent. The final project is really long but rewarding as you get to implement new features in a big app.

Material is too abstract to consistently do well on the 8 quizzes over the course of the year.  Final assignment is a never-ending nightmare.  Worst of all, the TA's and Piazza are no help.  Teacher and TA's answer questions more indirectly a politician.  Grading is outrageously strict.  This class makes you feel like you are suffering.

Knowledgeable, but a mediocre lecturer. Class slides are incredibly outdated, and over-complicated. Quizzes cover some hyper-specific, impractical details not present in lecture slides, making expectations unclear. Lectures themselves are unorganized, and frantically skip between superficial explanations of concepts. Little help outside of class.

I love Hemingway. He is more like a friend/colleague than a teacher. 3251 is hard, but manageable. The content is somewhat useless (except design patterns) and very outdated. The content can get boring but they're essential to understanding C++. Feels like he requires you to have overly-detailed understanding of the content.
go to class if you want a good grade

While Hemingway is one of the dept's best profs (low bar), & this class is the most applicable outside of school, it is extremely hard and fast-paced. His lectures aren't good & don't clarify much nor are they applicable to studying for quizzes or tests. He also isn't easily accessible outside class & even when you catch him, he is not helpful.
thumbs down

for all of hemingway's classes, expect heavy workload! but you will always learn much much much more than you will do in other classes. i took his isd and webdev and these 2 courses are definitely the best cs courses you can find at vandy
Chou Sha Bi Quiz zei ji ba nan
He is not at all a good teacher. Likes to almost prove his knowledge to students by creating over complicated slides. Don't bother.

Quizzes are quite challenging. PA's are not too bad, though. He is a decent lecturer, but he explains the patterns and algorithms pretty blandly and so nothing really sticks. His slides are lackluster and are hard to follow on your own time. Quizzes are pure memorization and don't provide much knowledge. It's an eh class.

I love Dr. Hemmingway! Great professor, amazing and easy to understand lectures, and meaningful PA's where I felt accomplished doing them.  They weren't overly difficult nor time consuming, unlike CS2201.  Quizzes started easy-ish and got harder the more theoretical they got, but still very doable.  Quizzes and tests are curved!  Take Hemmingway!

Prof Hemingway is incredible at teaching (provided that you pay attention and put in effort). He emphasizes the importance of writing maintainable code, approaches to tackling complexity and so much more. This is a class where you will learn a lot of valuable skills & lessons that will help you grow tremendously. 

Challenging but rewarding!

I did not think that the PA's in this class were as hard as the ones in 2201, but you definitely will spend some time on them. Hemingway is the only guy who teaches this, but I think he's a fine professor. It's very important that you attend class everyday, since quiz questions may cover stuff only mentioned in class and not on the slides online.

Prof. Hemingway is a pretty good guy. He connects well with students and usually always has a smile on his face. The programs can be long, but they're manageable. His quizzes are usually very hard, so study hard. Exams are tough but fair. Class takes a lot of work and can often become cluttered. Overall, is an alright professor, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hardest class I’ve ever taken (worse than data structures and 1301). Handwritten closed-note tests/quizzes are brutal. Projects due on most inconvenient days (same day as quiz, monday after spring break) and I think it’s on purpose. Very harsh. Late project? 0. 30 seconds late for quiz? 0. Lectures r boring but he knows his stuff and answers ?s

Hemingway is a really solid guy and easy to connect with - he did his undergrad at Vandy too! It's an upper division CS class, so I'm not sure what some of the other reviews expect. It's meant to be hard to prep you for jobs. To succeed you need to go to office hours, put in some long nights, grind before quizzes and get used to the class format.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable and answers questions but the strictest prof I've ever had. "I'm heartless. I don't accept late work for any reason. Maybe if you lose your arm, but then I'd probably say to use your other arm." Quizzes are difficult and very specific, often on the same day as projects. If you're late (even <1 minute) you don't get a quiz and get a 0
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He cannot explain anything. Clearly knowledgable himself but a god awful instructor.
Hemingway assigns are ridiculously hard. Lectures can also be too fast and kind of unfocused. Not a really nice guy either.
No. Just No.

Had the worst experience. Did not stay on top of the material for maybe 3 classes due to some personal issues in late fall and ended up never being able to recover. Hemingway did absolutely nothing to help, despite my willingness to complete extra credit.
Awful teacher. Just do not take him if you rely on a good teacher to learn well. His slides are unclear and his quizzes are ultra-specific for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible professor and perhaps even worse person. Be sure to stay connected with other students. Really doesnt care since nobody will do anything to him.

Projects very straightforward except for the last one where he doesn't provide you with any testing. The only reason quizzes and exams are difficult is because the instructions are unclear as to what he expects. Make sure to not only read the instructions carefully but also write down everything you can and hope to hit what he wants. Good luck

This class is such a refreshing relief after taking 2201 with Roth. Hemingway's grading is CRYSTAL clear, and he gives you the tests for all of the PA's. Only thing that is tough is that on a few heavier projects, the test scripts will get backed up on GitHub. Worst part of the class is that if you're even 15 seconds late on quiz day, automatic 0.

Quizzes are very very hard and based on pretty much anything he says during lecture. Slides were unironically made in the 90s. He seems like an okay guy, but the content is bleh and so is the format. Grading could also be better  takes 2-3 weeks to get quizzes back and sometimes obvious mistakes are made. There's a major assignment every week.

Hemingway's a great guy and professor. His class is EXTREMELY lecture heavy though. The quizzes are very very hard and based on pretty much anything and everything he says during lecture. The slides don't cover it all -- GO TO CLASS. The programming assignments are easy. The exams and quizzes are rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Literally the best professor in the CS dept. Teaches the most practical class for the whole major. The class definitely moves fast compared to other ones and can be a bit overwhelming at times but the knowledge and experience you can get from this class is unparalleled.

ISD is a notoriously tough class, but Prof. Hemingway teaches it well. He's a fair grader, although his quizzes were quite difficult (study lecture slides heavily). Programming assignments are quite lengthy, but TAs can help a lot if you start early. I appreciated that he was easy to talk to about course topics and more and was friendly
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, he's a cool guy but not a great teacher. His lectures diverge from the slides a lot, which becomes frustrating when you're trying to study. He often goes too fast in lecture for you to write down what he's saying. He answers questions well, but doesn't give students much material to study outside of class. Quizzes are unreasonably hard.

Hemingway is a great professor. The last programming assignment has a pretty unclear spec, but everything else is great. Beware of the quizzes, though -- they're tough and pretty much make class participation mandatory.

It's a tough class. Hemingway is alright, but the content itself can be very dry and I really didn't enjoy taking the class or learning the content as a CS major. Hemingway can be cold-blooded, but he knows his stuff well.

Here's the deal. For the average programmer, the first half of this class can be tricky. The second part is about design patterns and doesn't require much programming skill. That being said, the tests can be somewhat tough and the quizzes are annoying. I would take someone who says "This isn't hard to get an A in" with a grain of salt.

Hemingway is a good prof and was super accessible for remote students. PAs are generally not bad once you get started but the TRAVIS deductions are brutal. Other than that, quizzes get specific so you have to pay attention to what Hemingway says rather than what's on the slides. I would recommend re-watching lecture recordings for that.

Most of my problems with this class stem with the content itself (design patterns sometimes seem impractical and detached from real software development). Quizzes and tests test you on memorization more than coding skill which is an unfortunate byproduct of being a class based on design patterns. Homeworks are pretty easy and an A isn't difficult.

Hemingway is on of the best professors you can have here. He is passionate about what he teaches, gives great lectures, and is clear with the grading and what you should do to get a good grade. 3251 is not an easy class, but he just makes it a lot better.

Hemingway is one of the best professors at Vandy. I was fortunate to take two courses with him and in both, he was a great lecturer, passionate about both the material and his students' success, and a fair grader. Highly recommend for any CS or ENGM class or even to grab a cup of coffee with.

CS4288 with Dr Hemingway was my favorite class I've taken at Vandy. It's abundantly clear that Hemingway is passionate about web dev, and he teaches you real tools that are actually used in industry and are super up-to-date! Also gives really clear and insightful lectures, and is very helpful in office hours. Lots of extra credit esp near the end.

Prof Hemingway is just average. The biggest fault of the class is in its content, in particular design patterns. Basically Hemingway regurgitates Doug Schmidt's design preferences for 2.5 hours a week. There's not enough time to actually learn these patterns through practice, so memorization of unhelpfully abstracted concepts is the MO.

Web Dev is probably the class I learned the most in at Vandy. The class is definitely hard, but there is a lot of extra credit, especially towards the end of the class. Hemingway is a great guy and really helpful during office hours.

ISD with Hemingway is a lot of material that you have to make an effort yo understand... if you're not too strong with CS. Otherwise, this class isn't too difficult at all. Be ready for weeks and weeks of design patterns.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Professor Hemingway!! He is also super enthusiastic about what he is teaching and does a great job. While class isn't mandatory, his lectures are super helpful to doing well on the quizzes/hw/exams. That being said, the graders are kinda harsh on quizzes so you have to study a lot for them. overall, I love Hemingway and would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I learned almost nothing in this class, but that's not Hemingway's fault (the class itself isn't very useful). The programming assignments were rough occasionally and the tests were moderate. Hemingway's lectures were as good as they could be with the given material. He seems heartless (and kinda is), but can be very understanding and reasonable.
He's a phenomenal lecturer, but a cold heartless man
Extremely smart human being. Your only choice for CS3251. Not very responsible though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I've learned more in web dev than any other CS class since data structures. Hemingway is a great professor who has a lot of experience in this field and he makes this class more enjoyable than ISD but the projects are still a lot of work. What you learn is what you'll actually use in the industry so it's very useful. 6 assignments and 3 tests.

CS3251 with Hemingway is great as he is an amazing teacher. The quizzes can be tricky if you don't study for them, and there are many assignments. The assignments get a lot rougher after 4/5, so be prepared for that. Also, don't expect to get any help from Hemingway or TAs on weekends or over break, because they're completely unresponsive on Piazza
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: easy class if you do all assignments and start on them early. The quizzes and tests in this class are very straightforward. class picks up after midterm
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hemingway is much more bearable for 4288. He teaches you about the latest tools actually used in industry. But there is a lot of material in the course that he can't cover and expects you to do the work to learn it yourself. I must stress, this is a DIFFICULT course but it is most definitely rewarding and you will learn a lot if you make it out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hemingway makes assumptions. In other words, you should not be satisfied with what is given in lecture. Memorize the PowerPoint (By memorize I mean it), and search online anything that doesnt make sense to you. Furthermore, look through provided code and stuff. Overall it is an interesting class and he makes sure that you learn.

One of the best CS professors. Hes really friendly and personable. Programming assignments are difficult but manageable. Quizzes and tests are pretty straightforward. The lectures can be a bit dry, but overall a solid course.

Hemingway is one of the only CS professors at Vandy who focuses more on practical, relevant knowledge rather than raw theory. If you know how to program, the assignments are relatively easy but some of the criteria is occasionally vague (the TAs are improving it, however). The quiz/test material is straightforward and all of it is on the slides.

Embarrassment of a class. He's too lazy to write his own slides and just uses shorter, confusing snippets from lectures of past professors. If you take this class just know that Doug Schmidt has all of his lectures posted from 2011 that are far superior than anything provided by Hemingway. Character limits maxed.. just know this class was miserable

This class was translated from Java to C++ this semester and had some clear issues arising from the shift. e.g. Errors in provided files, TAs unclear on project specifications, etc. The homework wasn't graded all that hard, but weekly quizzes were tough. Hemingway is a straightforward teacher. Material can be dry, but worth learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The projects in this class were boring and irrelevant. Getting help was difficult because TAs would tell you incorrect info. Projects build on each other but weren't graded and returned for a very long time. The class felt unorganized, projects and READMEs had errors, and nothing compiled at first. Overall a lot of work and stress.

Fantastic professor. Really cares about teaching it seems, and although this class had a few organizational problems, I believe they'll be fixed as everyone gets used to using Clion anyway. I don't think there are any other options for 3251, but if there are, TAKE HEMINGWAY.

He's a cool guy, I found the material dry but he tries to keep it interesting. We had a a problem set due every other week, which were tough and consuming; and the other weeks we had quizzes that took the entire class time. THe quizzes really aren't bad if you do practice questions and study old quizzes. I found lectures helpful

Hemingway is the man. He makes lectures fun and enjoyable, but straight to the point. He makes the course as easy as possible without it being a walk in the park. You definitely learn a lot in the course. He has office hours, but it gets super packed because he has so many students.

Dr. Hemingway can explain tough topics better than any other CS professor I have come across at Vanderbilt. Comp Org is a tough class that is doable simply because he can explain it so well. Don't expect it to be easy, but expect to understand it.

Really irresponsible professor. There are lots of errors in his homework assignments, but he never accepts suggestions to correct them. Also, he is not very knowledgable on the subject he teaches. When students ask questions beyond the powerpoint, he usually has no idea how to answer them.

The WebDev class is the most fantastic class within the CS dept ive taken. The professor is a superchill guy, and he simulates the class as a real work environment. Could be alot of work, but the TAs super cool and will give out grades if you put in effort. All tests and quizzes are open laptop
Participation, quizzes, projects (hw's) and tests. Clear lecturer and organized class.

This class was on Python coding. It's a terminal course so there's no follow-up class. It was super interesting and Professor Hemingway is the man. He's very good at teaching Computer Science to non computer science people. Good mix of lectures and using the whiteboard. Occasional short quizzes and three tests. Really solid class and best Professor

My favorite professor at Vanderbilt. The class was Systems Engineering. It meets twice a week and you have a short quiz almost once a week  on one of the days. He is super interesting and insightful, always helps you out, and teaches some cool stuff. Has office hours in the FGH atrium and is super approachable. The man.
Fantastic guy. Very knowledgeable and clear lecturer. Reasonable, and a big-time Vandyperson.

Great professor. Very approachable, clear and excited to teach. Only problem might be that his quizzes were out of 3. You either get a 0, 1, 2, or 3. Which means 0, 33%, 66% or 100%. He changed this later, but by that time my average had already been damaged enough. Easy grader on assignments, which are pretty fun to do. Sometimes challenging.

Prof. Hemingway has been my favorite professor thus far at Vanderbilt. I love his approach toward teaching. He genuinely wants to get to know all of his students and be available for them. He hosts open office hours in the atrium of the engineering building before class so students can drop in and visit him without the intimidation of an office.

Gerard is a very hard grader and the lectures can get super boring, but he is the nicest professor, very passionate about his material, very smart, and the content can be interesting. He makes sure that students know what's on the test by giving great practice exams. He can grade a little tough but makes sure that students understand their mistakes
The nicest professor I've had at Vandy - very kind and straightforward to get an A

This is for ECON 3230, not ECON 2100. Gerard is a good professor and a great person, but the problem sets and exams are written and graded strangely, making the class more difficult than it should be. The class is manageable though, and he does care about his students.
2 midterms and a final that are pretty easy/similar to practice exams, drops 1/6 hw assignments. interesting class and super easy to do well.

Gerard is great. the class is incredibly interesting and I feel like I really learned a lot. Also, he just cares so much about the class and the students and really tries to create a great environment. Definitely one of the better econ professors.

Gerard is a breath of fresh air for the ECON department. He's clear in his lectures. He cares about his students. And, he asks for feedback to improve the class. His tests reflect exactly the PowerPoints and problem sets, so know those, and you'll be perfectly fine. This class is one of the easier ECON classes. Take him!

Professor Domenech-Arumi was one of the best econ professors I've had at Vanderbilt. His lectures were extremely engaging and grading expectations were very clear. I definitely recommend taking his class as it is very feasible to get an A.
Lecture seems tough in the beginning but you get used to it eventually. Easy Grader. Everything comes off of his slides. Great ECON Elective for a direct A!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ez to get an A
Gerard is such a witty professor. If you understand his humor, you will love his lecture. Other than that, the class wasn't bad at all and it is very doable to get an A
Lecture was not very helpful. The grading is confuse and you have to study outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Gerard is an amazing instructor who genuinely cares about his students. Provided the material is authentically understood (and it is presented very digestibly), the problem sets and exams are easy.

I'm glad that Professor Arumi joined the economics department at Vanderbilt. He is a really caring professor that wants to make his class material as digestible as possible. Works with students during office hours to make sure they understand the material. You will do well on his tests conditional on you knowing the material! So study his slides.
100% take his class. He cares about his students and is passionate about the material. The tests are fair and the homework is not overwhelming. I would take it again if I could.

The course content is super easy for anyone with some experience of Econ. His PPT is organized and clear. To do well in exams, all you need to do is to go over his PPTs and review the problem sets. He is a very nice person as well, consistently asking for students' feedback and explaining well both in class and during office hours. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Very kind and friendly professor. Genuinely cares about students. However, the exams are far more difficult than content discussed in class. There are problem sets, but they don't cover all material and are not similar to the exams which makes it difficult to prepare.
Genuinely cares about students and provides an interesting perspective on the content she presents. She wants you to bring in your own ideas and experiences
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: prof hao is literally one of the best teachers i've had at vanderbilt! she is soooo sweet and super intelligent, if you really want to learn more about gender in chinese society she does an amazing job of analyzing so many different texts and explaining many aspects of chinese culture and history. attendance is mandatory, but not difficult.

One of the best professors that I ever had at Vanderbilt, it is hight or nearly impossible get any grade less than A. AMAZING! take her class for credit or ALXE whatever, do not miss out on this course.
Excellent professor with so much knowledge. She also really cares about her students!
Pretty good professor. Would take again

Professor Hutton is an excellent instructor! I would highly recommend his Maymester 2120 course. It was fully online with 4 assignments. He used SAS which I was not familiar with but he provided a lot of help. He was available for questions and explained the concepts really well. The course was fast-paced but Professor Hutton made it manageable.

Super chill and pleasant guy! Class was very easy; HW twice a month and 3 online exams, no final. He curves exams that people do poorly on. I did HW during the optional discussion so TAs could check it and I could get it out of the way. I didn't really learn anything, but it is an easy addition to your schedule if youre taking other hard classes.

chillest man you will ever meet. all online, take home, open note exams. content wasn't too hard. he has detailed slides, so during exams I literally copied the exact steps on his slideshows. homework assignment once a week. super straightforward class. would recommend over any other professor.
Excellent class! Dr. Hutton made learning statistics a lot easier than my high school teacher. He is friendly and cares about his students.
Very very easy class. Tests are online. Just make sure you go to class (TopHat class), and you'll get an easy A. Weekly assignments take like 30-45 mins.

Dr. Hutton is clear, organized, and genuinely cares about his students. Lectures are straightforward. The exams are open note and fair. The pace can feel fast at times but if you keep up it's very manageable.
Dr. Hutton explains things very well and makes a difficult subject easy to learn. He's an excellent instructor!

Hutton is the absolute GOAT. Literally thanks you for coming to class every day. Every exam is online, open note, and you have plenty of time. Very straightforward and clear slides that give you everything you need. Weekly assignments take about 30 minutes and are graded lightly. He seems like the best choice for Peabody Stats.

Dr. Hutton is one of the best professors to take for Peabody stats. He's clear in his explanations and the tests are open book. I usually struggle with math but this class has been much better than previous math classes I've taken.

Despite the amount of asynch videos and slides he provides on a weekly basis, the pace is way too fast and very accelerated (especially if you have never taken stats before).  It was very hard to follow, process and understand.
Awful. Would rather have a root canal.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 4 tests. 8 assignments. Class is fine.

The TopHat notes are what you need for the exams! The homework doesn't exactly reflect what is on the test, and I think for me I have a harder time with online tests in general. I have a weaker math background than most and found this class to be harder than expected.

Absolutely loved Dr. Hutton! You can work with classmates on all assignments and the tests were all open-note take-home tests. As someone who really struggles in math, this is the math class to take. I learned a lot but it was not super difficult.

Attendance is not mandatory but there are tophat questions during class that make up your participation grade. Tests were take home on Brightspace, and they are reasonable if you review the lecture slides. Seven weekly homework assignments were fairly easy as well. Good intro course to statistics, I recommend taking Dr. Hutton.

Took stats for the first time ever and this class wasn't too bad. Tests (3) were all online and open-note but some questions still threw me for a loop. He posts all the slides and gives partial credit though so I managed to end with an A. I would recommend reviewing the slides heavily before each test. Cool guy who clearly loves statistics.

Tests are a bit hard because his lectures do not translate very well to it. There's a lot of knowledge translation you have do in between but that's expected in college. You have to show up to class ready to learn otherwise you will miss important points not shown in his slides. He does make stats simpler than it actually is so his course is good
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Test has three tests and 7 assignments and a grade for participation. Tests are challenging and since there are only three of them it can be a challenge to get an A. Great teacher very flexible and cares. He'll cancel discussions, is aware of breaks and participation is if you engage in the class. :)

Great prof! He cares about the students and the material that he teaches. His lectures are very clear and the assignments directly reflect the lectures. Tests are a bit difficult but overall it's not bad. He is great!

Dr. Hutton is an awesome guy. I'm glad I had him for my first Vandy statistics class. He is really passionate about the subject and gives great responses to any questions. The homework wasn't too bad (approx 7 assignments) and there are only 3 tests (all online/open note). As long as you pay attention and do the problems, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Professor Hutton is one of the most passionate, kindest stats professors here, and you can tell just by attending his lectures how much he loves this course. Three non-cumulative exams that are take home and open note, weekly homework that he'll be happy to help you on, no extra credit but the class is set up so you don't need it ever. 

Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Hutton's statistics class was about as good as statistics can get. The way he explained things helped make the material more understandable.

I was worried about taking stats online over the summer, but Dr. Hutton was adaptable, clear, and organized. His lecture videos were SO helpful and he connected abstract concepts to working examples to make them easier to understand. He was friendly and approachable during office hours- overall a great choice for Peabody stats, especially online!

Dr. Hutton is a solid choice for any statistics course. The workload is very manageable and he was always helpful in office hours. Correlation and Regression is a content-heavy course, but worth taking if you're interested in more intermediate to advanced statistical analysis.
The class had 3 tests all online. Weekly assignments that used SPSS. Instructor is nice and accommodating. Not a bad choice for Peabody stats.

I was a little unsure about taking statistics online but this class wasn't too bad. The interaction with the professor and TAs during class was helpful. The class is not that difficult as long as you watch the videos. Make sure you pay attention to how he wants things worded.

I was a little unsure about taking statistics online but this class wasn't too bad. The interaction with the professor and TAs during class was helpful. The class is not that difficult as long as you watch the videos. Make sure you pay attention to how he wants things worded

Professor Hutton is the worst Professor Ive had at Vanderbilt. I think his teaching style his especially maladapted to being online. He gives almost no feedback on assignments and leaves you in the dark on how to complete even the review. My experience left me constantly unsure if I was doing my work correctly. Do not take Professor Hutton online.

The lectures are on video and professionally done. Met weekly on Zoom to answer polling questions and work on assignments. Dr. Hutton put us into breakout rooms so we could work with other students. He is very accessible during and outside of class. The tests were manageable and open book. Definitely recommend for Peabody stats.

3 tests, 9 homework assignments, in-class participation, no final. Entirely a flipped classroom with pre-recorded lectures, so it was difficult to feel engaged. He's very understanding and responsive. Also very caring and knowledgeable, but sometimes I struggled to connect to the material on Zoom. He means well but is not the most effective online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Correlation and Regression was a helpful class! Dr. Hutton is very passionate about the subject and it's potential for understanding data. He is very accessible in office hours. No tests, just 5 homework assignments.

Dr. Hutton is a very caring and passionate person, which truly helped in a beginners stats class, where he never assumed that students knew stats concepts beforehand. The class was made easier due to the COVID-19 online switch, but he remained a very good lecturer and cared for our mental health. 3 exams, 7 homework, and tophat participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I was really worried about taking this class but I feel like Professor Hutton actually cared about making sure everyone understood the material. He covered a lot but if you go to class and pay attention then it is a manageable course. He was also very understanding during the transition to online because of COVID-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His tests are very doable, if you pay attention during lecture and also study the slides. Don't waste your time with the book his homework and tests are from his slides. He tells you exactly how to answer questions and gives you study guides for the tests. No final either
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hutton is very nice and helpful especially during office hours. I was disappointed after the first test but Dr. Hutton encouraged me and had faith in me that I could do better. I suggest going to office hours and asking questions if you don't understand something. He gives practice problems for each test which is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He is disrespectul. Does not respond if you send him an email. He confuses hisself when he lectures. He does not use the book. He contradict what the books says.

This is an intellectually stimulating class but not too hard. You have to go to class and pay attention to do well because it's lecture heavy. He also takes attendance and counts it in the grade. I do like how he goes into detail about the statistical concepts. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor! I didn't do that great on my first midterm so I met with Professor Hutton to see how I could do better. I've also been going to office hours which has really helped. I made an A on my second midterm and I'm so happy! I enjoy the class even though it can be a little boring sometimes but lectures are good and I love using Top hat.

I do not find Dr. Hutton's class to be difficult. He explains things in detail and the instruction is good. I took AP stats in hs and I feel like I never learned why we use the formulas. Dr. Hutton explains why and I enjoy that. He is extremely nice and always willing to help. My TA is great too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Literal worst professor at Vanderbilt. I learned nothing in this class. He is very unclear in lecture and doesn't make it easy to get help outside of class. He is very monotone which makes it difficult to pay attention when he lectures, but if you don't pay attention you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He cares about statistics and the class but teaches the intro stats class as if it was a graduate class. He is not clear about what he expects for exams and goes through material quickly, expecting people to already have a basic understanding of statistics. Very hard to get an A even if you study a lot.

Taking stats with Hutton is good choice if you are willing to work. His class is difficult. His exams are challenging and long. You must go to class because he takes attendance. I ended up doing better in the course than I thought and my final grade was fair. He is very nice and knows the material. He explains things well but not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hutton has good intentions, but his lectures are long and rambly and make the material more confusing. He makes his tests very challenging and the average for the tests was pretty low. He isn't trying to help by barely giving any equations for the tests. The homework took a long time. Overall, one of the hardest classes I've taken in a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures are clear and he gives a study guide for the exams. The exams aren't too bad if you do the practice problems. The textbook is useless because he relies on lectures. He is always available to meet outside of class and willing to help.

Really sweet, open to feedback, cares about students and their grades. Clear explanations with great picture representations on his ppts. He uploads everything and leaves room for review in class and has extra office hours before each exam. Go to office hours, keep up, DON'T SKIP CLASS. Only tests what he lectures, 10% of grade is from attendance.

This professor is a great person but a terrible teacher. His class is based entirely on lecture and there are very few grade opportunities. Although there are weekly assignments that are easy, they total to a tiny percentage of your grade. Your entire grade comes from three exams and he has no makeup policy. Avoid him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Be prepared to work. Class starts off with easy concepts but gets harder as the semester progresses. However, the material was presented clearly and he uses Top Hat to engage the class. You can ask questions through Top Hat during lecture. He is approachable and always willing to help during office hours. Overall, good prof.

Very awesome class for introducing me to statistics. His lectures were very informative and provided all of the information that was needed to do well on the tests. The tests are quite hard and long, but if you study all of the material, you should do well on them. He is very helpful and accepts feedback most of the time. Would take again!

Hutton isn't a bad teacher but rather a tough one. Grades are fickle in his class because he doesn't go by a particular grading scale everything depends on the exams' statistics. There are three exams and they are all relatively difficult. Takes attendance daily. Has weekly homeworks (easy) and quizzes is discussion. Prepare to work for an A.

Hasan is extremely kind. Sometimes he doesn't always explain things well or give students adequate info abt grading of proofs, but overall grades get assigned pretty accurately as related to effort. attendance was not mandatory, but rather counted for extra credit. fair amount of busy work, but cheat sheets on every exam + final

Professor Hasan is a great professor. He is very supportive and easy to learn from. In addition, he is super accessible, as he consistently provides office hours and is open to scheduling one-on-one time over zoom. It is clear that he has a passion for teaching and truly enjoys helping students reach their full potential. Highly recommend.

Prof.Hasan explains concepts clearly and covers all details in an engaging way. He makes his own slides, so the key points are easy to follow. Quizzes are not stressful because he reviews everything and gives you a second chance. Lots of chances to earn extra credit. He's very understanding and patient. A very supportive and approachable professor.
Good teacher overall, very accommodating with questions and responds to emails very quickly. Tests are significantly easier than the homework and is just a fun class overall. Would recommend

He is my favorite DS teacher I've ever had
Hes super understanding that we all have a lot going on and his grading is the best ever 
He basically sets up this class for you to succeed.

One of the best classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. Professor Hasan is incredibly accommodating, holds plenty of office hours, and is always willing to help students understand the material. The class is interesting, engaging, and you can really tell he cares about his students' success.Strongly recommend.

Prof. Hasan is very accessible outside of class, offering many office hours (both online and in person). Extra credit opportunities are offered for active participation, which makes the lectures more vivid and engaging. The final exam is challenging but fair!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If u have any sort of basic python proficiency this class should be a breeze. Sometimes lectures are all over the place but he provides online videos of him re-explaining things which are super informative and helpful. Even though it may be easy you will learn a lot that is applicable. Great professor who cares simple as that

Professor Hassan does not explain things thoroughly or efficiently. A lot of class time is wasted on worksheets that he goes around and checks individually or on a tangent. I had to learn most of the content from the Zybook. The final was disproportionally difficult compared to the midterms which made it difficult to prepare and know what to expect

Dr. Hasan is incredibly helpful during office hours even though the lectures might be boring but I believe that is simply due to the code heavy nature of the class. He is very supportive when you attend office hours and often pushes deadlines for the convenience of students. You might have to study a lot on your own though.

Nice person, funny during lectures to keep people engaged. However, the first part of the semester the lectures were clear but after the first midterm things started to get a bit confusing. The lecture also stopped aligning with homework and zybook which is bothering.

Professor Hasan is genuinely a teacher who cares about his students. He is very nice and accommodating, and he is well-receptive to feedback. If people complain about him, I can assure you they aren't putting in the work. He prepares you well for tests, too, with his practice problems, and you do get a cheat sheet for exams.

Absolutely loved prof Hasan! He was so upbeat, passionate about CS, and patient everyday with our class. Perfect class for anyone who knows nothing about CS or wants a slow review, easy A course. He has you code in class with him everyday while he lectures, so you can be actively learning as you go. He can be quite repetitive and slow, but so nice

This summer asynchronous course is well-organized and easy to follow. Professor Hasan is kind, approachable, and responsive. The class includes two midterms, a cumulative final, quizzes, programming assignments, worksheets, and ZY Books exercises. Highly recommended!
I loved his style of teaching, and I had a great time in his class. I looked forward to every lesson, as it was such an enjoyable and engaging experience for me.
Great proffesor and class.

He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He spends a lot of time preparing for tests and is very clear about what will be on the tests. Gives a lot of extra credit, so definitely show up to class leading up to the test.

Great and funny guy. He cares about students & is very invested in everyone's success. Participating during class helps you understand content & forms a helpful relationship. Go to TAs to check your HWs. Gives lots of material to ensure everyone understands content. Will make any changes to help your learning. Tests aren't hard & get cheat sheet.

He's a very kind professor who clearly cares a lot about doing the best he can to help you learn. Unfortunately, the best he can is, well, a little underwhelming. I tagged him as "hilarious" because my friends and I got MANY stifled laughs out of the daily mistakes made during lectures that we, the students, would correct. Great guy—not great prof.

Hasan is great. He prepares everyone very well for midterms and the final by working through reviews that are very similar to the exam questions. Additionally, there are plenty of extra credit opportunities. I would happily take another class with him.

Dr. Hasan is very kind and accessible outside of class. He sometimes doesn't have the best lectures but you'll never be tested on anything you haven't seen before. Midterm 1 is very easy, Midterm 2 was a little bit harder but still good. Final exam is pretty challenging but if you study enough and do all review worksheets you will score well

Professor Hasan cares a lot about his students and he's very approachable; however, I didn't find his lectures very engaging. I feel like I could have learned the content just by reviewing the lecture slides on my own. He tried to make the homework problems interesting and fun which I appreciated.

Professor Hasan is a very kind and thoughtful professor. He really wants his students to succeed and wants them to truly understand the course material. If you show up to class everyday, attend office hours, and put in work, you will receive a good grade and learn a lot. I highly recommend taking Hasan.

His class is easy as long as you stay engaged during lectures, which are fairly entertaining. He makes jokes and maintains a relaxed atmosphere. It's clear that he genuinely cares about his students, and overall, he's just a good guy. If you have the chance, definitely take his class.
Never take his class if you are actually interested in studying. All he does is make stupid jokes and never focuses on the actual lecture.
Great Professor. He cares about his students a lot.
Great professor! Super caring and amazing class

Overall a great dude who really cares about the material and presents very clearly. Not all lecture slides were posted which wasn't really a problem due to the volume of information available through the zybooks and HW. He also seems to have student's best interests in mind.

Professor Hasan was not a terrible professor, during his lectures he sometimes contradicted himself, which made proofs and other things where you needed a clear cut answer kind of confusing. Some of the topics covered are a little mind numbing but also logically confusing. Hasan tries to make class interesting & is accessible w/ email/office hours.

He responded to a lot of emails at night and was super kind and accessible throughout the course. The homework grading can be a little confusing at times, so spending your time in his office hours or at the TA is helpful.
Professor Hasan is an entertaining guy and is very accessible outside of the classroom.

CS 2212 is a very straightforward class. Do the ZyBooks & show up to class and that's 15% of the grade. Exams are mostly MCQ and very easy free response. 4 problem sets that are 4 questions each. Don't try to do it all at once. Provides extra office hours near exam/HW deadline. Funny lecturer, caring, and shows the real-life applications.
low key goated. i was sure i was going to get a F but this man pulled through. go to all the classes though

Professor Hasan seems like a nice guy, but lectures are a little hard to understand and often don't align with the homework. Office hours are super helpful when it comes to the 7 programming assignments. If you have coded before (especially in java) this class shouldn't be too bad, but if you have no experience I would chose a different professor.
Lectures are pretty boring, few homework assignments that are given weeks in advance, overall professor is kind but also boring
Easy Class. Lectures are terrible and you don't need to go but he gives top hat in class for credit to make you show up

Weak link of the CS department. He's a nice, funny guy, but doesn't prepare for his lectures. Will flip to a slide in a presentation he didn't make and say "Oh, I guess we're doing this now." Attendance, though mandatory, is often detrimental to your understanding. Will occasionally contradict himself and/or space out in the middle of class.

The material isn't super hard but his lectures are extremely boring. Homeworks can be pretty long but you get two weeks to do them. The class is very straightforward though and the grading policies are very clear. Cheatsheets are allowed for the exams.

Very straightforward class. 2 exams (you get a cheat sheet), a final, and 4 homeworks. Truly tries to help out his students and answers any questions you have. Minimal amount of work compared to other classes

Hasan is probably one of the kindest professors I've ever met. He truly cares for you, and he definitely seems to be trying his best to form a relationship with his students. I don't know what it is about his lectures, but I just don't learn anything from them. From other reviews, it seems I'm not alone. Hasan just can't teach well for some reason.

The textbook is straightforward enough that you can learn 80% of the content from there without much issue. Hasan isn't a great teacher but overall if you have a bit of prior experience in CS class isn't overwhelmingly difficult.

Prof Hasan will say he welcomes any type of question yet he'll ridicule q's that are eh. His accent makes it hard to understand at times so be prepared to do most of your learning from the zyBooks. However, if you do that, and actually understand the PA's and make good cheat sheets you should easily be in the 90+ range.

Bad lecturer. He always go discursive during lessons and seems to have a weirdly exaggerated ego. You'd probably have to learn through self studying the online textbook, which is much clearer than his lecture. Grading is inconsistent. Last semester many students shot him tons of emails complaining about grades, made him disturbed and changed grades

Dr.Hasan is a sassy man, jabbing at people in the back/students in general. As someone with basic Java experience, the course is straightforward and you can self-teach. Come to class to make sure you get the in-class worksheets- they're completion though. Assignments are straightforward, the 2nd exam was significantly more difficult than others.

Hasan isn't horrible, but he's very dry and boring, and the slides are basically the ZyBooks. Makes passive aggressive remarks towards students that you almost want to laugh at because of their absurdity. Grading is horrifically inconsistent, if you're taking this course without Python/general CS knowledge, the class is more like a 4 difficulty.

Dr. Hasan is a great guy and is very caring, would love to be his friend! Unfortunately, unless you come into this class with a previous coding background you will probably struggle. He intros this class by saying you will have to put in 10+ HOURS a week to get an A. Do not take his warning for granted - this is very true.

Horrible lecturer and frequently makes fun of students when they ask questions, but has the most well structured and clear-cut class I've ever had. Easy to do well, but you will not have a good time along the way. I would probably opt for another professor if you have the opportunity.

Prof Hasan was super unclear on the syllabus imo and a lot of us didn't understand what was supposed to be turned in for a grade or not until a month in. His lectures are pretty boring and redudant to Zybooks but office hours w him or the TAs are helpful. He is accommodating and try to get you a higher grade if he can, pretty nice guy overall.

His lectures are quite dry and boring, so it's really hard to pay attention. I think everyone just teaches themselves, which isn't so great when you have no programming experience and aren't a CS major. The PAs get pretty hard, and the exams are much harder than the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The tests aren't too hard as there's a cheat sheet allowed. All lecture slides are online as well.

He acts like he welcomes questions but then will respond with sarcastic, passive-aggressive remarks such as "we went over it in class :)" Do not recommend if you are actually interested in learning about computer science other than passing the class.

Cons: Homeworks take a while and are challenging, Zybooks are annoying

Pros: Homeworks prep you for the exam, cheat sheets on the exam, group worksheets in class that are super helpful, amazing professor and always willing to help, listens to feedback, responds fast, brings us KitKat, I can keep going. Can't recommend Prof. Hasan enough.

CS 2212 involves a lot of mathematical proofs that are difficult at times. It's definitely not easy for people who came from weak math background. However, prof. Hasan is a pretty solid lecturer and will give a lot of practice worksheets in class. Would take him again!!

Dr. Hasan is a nice guy but boring during lectures. Homework is much harder than class examples, but if you go to TA office hours early it shouldn't be a major issue. Tests are easy. Make sure to do the Zybooks and go to class. Dr. Hasan is also helpful during his own office hours as well.

Gives out insane homework assignments that are miles harder than exams or final or class examples, but they're very doable if you put some effort in

Gives easier exams than the other two discrete profs

Honestly a really nice and chill guy, kind of a shame he's pretty awful at lecturing and kind of wishy-washy abt the content when u ask him lol

Cares about students but fails to make lectures interesting; exams are doable but tough; homework is poorly worded questions that exponentially increase the time spent on simple topics. He provided very little advice for how to improve and change your performance.

He is a very nice guy and he wants his students to do well.  He is very accomodating with grades and tophats.  The lectures are kinda boring, but thats to be expected with most CS classes.  The PA's are not too bad and this class is easier than the other intro to CS classes.

His lectures are dry, but are generally useful and clear. 5% of the grade is attendance, so make sure that you attend his lectures. Workload for this course is also relatively light, so a solid choice if you don't want to spend too much time but still want to learn Python.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The first half of the course, Dr.Hasan's lectures were not very useful because they seemed to be exactly like the ZyBooks, and not worth the time. The second half of the course they were more useful. Unfortunately, he is very rude in class and office hours. I leave his office hours with a better understanding of material but demoralized also

Hasan loves computer science, but this class is mainly self-taught through zybooks, so people are typically working on them or programming assignments during class. This leads to awkward silences when he tries to call on people in a huge lecture hall because people are only there to do the tophat and are happy to learn the code through zybooks

Professor Hasan succeeded in teaching me the basics of Python and I feel prepared to take on higher-level data science courses. He lectures through the majority of class time but it's important to pay attention when he discusses content that will be on the PAs. He cares about his students and frequently asked for feedback on previous tests.

This is a good course to take when having no background in computer science. Expectations are clearly stated and it is easy to get help on the weekly programming assignments (these make up a big portion of your grade). This is the better computer science class to take, at least for engineering requirements. Very easy to get at least an A-.

This is a good introductory course for programming if you have never coded before, but the lectures are very boring. The professor would have trouble answering questions in class, but going to the TA's helps a lot. It was a fairly easy A.

Good class. Sometimes difficult to pay attention due to the classroom it was held in. Lectures were all posted online which was definitely very helpful. Also good accessibility of the LA & TA outside of the classroom for office hours which was helpful for the programming assignments. Exams are a little difficult.

Slow and boring, so you don't have to pay attention in class. Tests are straightforward and PAs are usually simple. Definition of easy A. Perfect class to take to get the credit if you don't like coding and he's a nice guy. But again: lectures are so boring and so painful.

Very confusing and bad teacher. This is definitely a teach yourself class. If you expected this to be an easy A, you are wrong. Be prepared to spend hours learning the material yourself. His course goals and grading expectations are very unclear. He does offer extra credit for in class participation.
Great guy and really wants you to do well in class. Not the best professor but gives easy tests and is quite helpful during office hours (gives a lot of hints for homework).

If you are looking for an easy class this is it. With that being said, his lectures were weak and he had trouble answering questions effectively. He seems to legitimately care but I learned everything outside of class.

Horrible lecturer. If I could skip class, I would, but there is TopHat attendance. If you ask Hasan a good question, expect, "That's a good question!" and "I will have to look into that and get back to you." Do Homeworks with your friends. Go to a TA. Don't go to his OH.

Everything was very easy up until the final, which i found to be 5x harder than both of the midterms. 

The programming assignments are worth a majority of your grade, but they're super doable.

Let's get this out of the way, he is not the best lecturer (go to Arena's section if you're looking for that), but he's the best choice for 2212 IMO. Hasan has easy tests, a decent amount of EC, and is a stand-up guy who puts in the effort to be a better teacher. 10/10 would take again!
Pretty easy class and cool prof, attendance is mandatory though
Best professor ever! His class in interesting and he is such a nice guy.

Professor Hasan cares about teaching his students and making sure they actually learn. He is very passionate about what he teaches. He tries his best to keep students engaged. The class itself is pretty easy. Just make sure to keep up with the assignments and participate in class because it is part of your grade.

Professor Hasan is a really good guy and cares a lot about his students. However, it is hard to do much with the 1151 material. Despite his best efforts much of it is very boring because the material itself is 99% common sense. Grading is extremely easy and he will help wherever he can just don't expect to be engrossed in the day-to-day lectures.
Really nice professor and cares about his students a lot! Great lectures and loved this course.

He is really nice and cares about his students a lot. Not great at lecturing (e.g., repeating things, spending too much time on stuff, etc.), but he is willing to take feedback and does everything he can to make sure you excel.

Overall Professor Hasan is a really great guy. He definitely cares for his students and wants them to learn. He is very understanding and offers ways for students who need a break to turn in assignments late. However, at times it can be difficult to communicate with the professor and if you are a beginner, this class can be a bit tough.
Great Professor! Really wants you to succeed :) Very doable to get an A if you put in some work, but not necessary to do a crazy amount.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The prof. Hasan is an amazing lecturer. His slides are clear and well-structured. His note is good. But the tests are a little bit difficult. The homework load is heavy but that helps you to understand knowledge.

Zybook assignments are the place where you really learn and apply the content as sometimes lectures can be a little boring despite Hasan is a good guy. The grading is great because PAs are 40% of your grade and they are easy to get a 10. Tests are not complicated but the time is limited and a lot of multiple-choice and open questions are presented.
Very understanding professor with easy-to-follow lectures. He is available outside of class hours for help and through email. 2 total exams with a cheat sheet and one final exam.

I really like Professor Hasan! He is understanding, grades fairly, offers a lot of help for programming assignments, and the coarse load is structured and manageable. Lectures can be boring but he tries to be engaging. My only complaint would be the exams and its time limit, but I will say he provides more than enough resources for success.
Professor Hasan is ok and tries to be understanding. However his lectures are not the easiest to follow and jump around a lot even within one topic.

Hasan clearly loves teaching, and he's super understanding. He's not a bad lecturer at all - I think the material is just hard to understand at first sometimes. Exams are easy. Homework is difficult but doable if you put in even an hour a day until it's due. 

Overall a great teacher. Think the earlier reviews were from when he was new.
Professor Hasan is generally a very funny lecturer, although sometimes his lectures are dry (that is also due to the course material).
not bad choice for 2212. some typos or confusing questions in hw but it is general for all 2212 sections.

For 2212, Hasan is a solid choice. The previous comments about him being a bad lecturer and not answering questions I think are from when he was new. I think he's gotten a lot better. Discrete isn't bad with him. His exams are easy and everything else is pretty much under your control.

Hasan is a nice guy and has great intentions but the fact that (I am assuming) English is not his first language is very obvious in terms of the connotation of some of his words. His lectures are not clear due to this and there are frequent typos in the assignments. The exams are fair. Attendance is more or less mandatory due to TopHat
good grader. bad lecturer.

Hasan is a super nice guy and clearly loves teaching, but he really doesn't know what he's doing. Exams had critical typos, lectures were really dry, and his answers to questions usually confused me more. I taught myself everything through the textbook. The final was not representative of what we had learned in class at all.

This class was very interesting and I really enjoyed it. I suggest taking this class but not with Hasan. He did a poor job teaching the material in class, and I learned a lot more from the online textbook. The final exam did not represent what we learned throughout the semester, and it was overall a lot harder to get an A than it should've been.

Hasan is fine. He is a nice guy and super friendly and approachable, but his exams have a ton of typos and he has a terrible habit of speaking constantly throughout every single exam which is really distracting. His lectures are pretty useless and I did the weekly assignments almost entirely by looking up the content.
CS1101 is a relatively easy class for Vandy, so I recommend taking it. Dr. Hasan is a bit unorganized in his lectures, but cares for his students.

Incredibly unclear, every assignment is riddled with critical typos, makes exams that are unnecessarily hard because of unclear and in some cases just incorrect directions.

Seems like a nice guy. Not good at answering questions.
Professor Hasan is a really nice guy, but his lectures are always quite unorganized and all of the exams have major typos on them that make it impossible to complete without major difficulty.

Professor Hasan was really accommodating of students' personal needs. His exams were in line with the course lecture content which helped establish learning objectives, outcomes, and expectations. It was particularly hard to complete the HW assignments because there were no similar example questions in ZyBooks or in-class lectures.

The class is graded mostly on the 4 homework assignments, which we had about 2 weeks to complete and were far more difficult questions than the ones we saw in class or on the exams. The Ta's were far more helpful than Hasan's office hours, but if you ever went and talked to him in person, he would try his best to put you on track.

He's definitely passionate about teaching the course, but he doesn't really know how to go about it. the way he lectures over slides is very quick, so zybooks is definitely what you should be looking at until he starts talking about the modules. idk GitHub is gonna be ur friend. Live programming is sometimes useful, but I wish it was more engaging.

Hasan is not the best lecturer, but he is a great professor overall. His lectures are essentially the zybooks. The homework problems are difficult (more difficult than in-class problems). However, the exams are easier than other professors and  much easier than the homework. Furthermore, Hasan is caring. If you need help, he 
 will accommodate you.

Prof.Hasan is a solid choice for CS2212. He is very caring and accessible outside of the classroom. Prof.Hasan, though not a strong lecturer, is helpful in explaining concepts. His tests are easy and do not require a lot of time studying. Homework is the same across all sessions and is totally graded by TA. Read zybook and go to lectures--A.

Hasan is an extremely funny and caring professor. The lectures get boring at times, but for CS/DS 1100 the material is easy enough that he does well lecturing with it. The PA's and tests are very easy if you pay attention. He's also a very nice guy. Recommend for cs/ds 1100.

Prof. Hasan is not the best but not the worst. He is not a great lecturer, but is a kind and funny person. Everything you need to know will be on ZyBooks, so if you want to take this class, just make sure you're willing to self-learn material. Tests are pretty easy compared to the graded homework!

The class is doable and you learn what you need to learn. But holy shoot Prof. Hasan can be kind of annoying at times. He likes to ask the class for answers and then gets flustered when a room of 70 awkward underclassmen don't want to speak up. I guess that probably sucks from his perspective but you've gotta know your audience. Still, good class

Prof. Hasan isn't bad, but isn't the best. His lectures are dry and basically repeat everything in the zyBooks textbook. ZyBooks will teach you everything you need to know without attending class. Tests are very fair and doable. Homework takes a long time and can be very difficult, often incorporating stuff you have not fully learned.

Hasan is a bad lecturer BUT still one of the best choices for 2212. Lectures are awful but you can easily self-study Zybooks, and he isn't good with questions but you can always use Piazza for that. The reason I'd suggest taking 2212 with him is bc his exams are 100% easier, and he is also a genuinely good guy, making the class quite easy overall

Prof Hasan is a really nice guy who is just not a strong teacher and lecturer. He reads off the slides word-for-word in lectures which are not very helpful; however, the ZyBooks textbook should suffice for studying and learning the content.
