He cannot answer questions well, so just don't ask them. Exams are much easier than the homework assignments.

Professor Hasan himself isn't a great lecturer, BUT that doesn't mean that he's a terrible option for CS 2212. His exams are EASY compared to the other professors, and he's a nice guy who will accommodate your needs. Just don't ask him questions because will won't give a coherent response. Reads directly off the slides, so reading Zybooks suffices.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hasan is a pretty bad lecturer. I only attended class because he occasionally had tophat questions. You should be able to teach yourself from the slides/zybooks. Exams are not too hard. The homeworks, however, are very hard. They will take you a lot of time and the graders can be really tough.

Dr. Hasan reads from his slides in all his lectures, which are then posted online. The lectures are pretty boring, and he sometimes cannot give clear answers to questions. The good thing is that much of this class can be self-learned from simply doing the assignments and reading the textbook.

Prof Hasan is pretty good. He rambles a bit, but tries his best to make sure you understand the content. He is very accommodating and will pull a few strings to make sure you leave well cared for grade wise and conceptually. He also adjusts assignment deadlines giving more time. Tests are also very reasonable and curved as needed.

Not very accessible outside of class (has three assignments due a week and only holds office hours once a week for one hour). TA is also not very easy accessible and do not offer enough office hours and also takes a very long time to respond to emails. Doesn't give clear enough background on assignments. Tests are easier than assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hasan rambles a bit, but he is very fair and tries to make this class as easy as he possibly can. All assignments and tests are designed to be challenging, but possible. He is very fair and adjusts deadlines and amount of work as needed.
Doesn't teach, just reads.

He doesnt know how to explain concepts well  every lecture consists of him reading off the slides. He is terrible at answering questions, to the point where he cant explain the definition of terms that are on the slides. The only positive side is that the class is relatively easy to self-teach with the textbook and other professors slides.

Hasan isn't great at answering questions or lecturing, but to be honest, he doesn't really have to be -- you can learn the entire class pretty easily from the online textbook and slides. Don't fret if he's the only choice left; you'll be fine, it's not that bad.

Professor Hasan's lectures were very clear and he definitely explained the concepts well. He genuinely cares about his student and if you seek him outside of class he can be very helpful. The assignments do take some time to finish but personally, I enjoyed working on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and a good teacher, just his section of the course is all the difficult stuff. It's definitely hard, but his tests are fair. He does rarely finish the content in class, but he posts videos for what he didn't get through, so expect to watch like half to one hour worth of videos per week outside of class.

Dr. Hillyer was genuinely the smartest professor I've ever had. He knows absolutely everything and has all of his lectures memorized. He is great at taking. His tests are slightly challenging, but very fair. The class is 4 exams and a final, all of which total up to 94% of your grade, with a dropped exam.

Professor Hillyer was an extremely dedicated and engaging professor. His lectures were very organized and he is very good at explaining concepts. His half of the semester is a lot more information and pretty difficult, but if you stay on task and listen to the lectures you should be good. There are no curveballs on his exams. LOVE Hillyer!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good lectures and slides. Fun, easygoing, but dedicated professor. His half definitely has a LOT more content than DeSantis but is still very manageable as long as you just show up to lecture regularly. Exams are straightforward. If anyone complains, it's probably more of a studying/content issue than a professor issue.

He's very nice and a great teacher, definitely take his section. His exams are the harder 2 compared to the second half, but the content is interesting and he explains super clearly. If you study hard and practice, getting a good grade is vey doable.

He does test on everything in the lectures - moreso than any other class I've ever taken, but if you study extremely hard able to get a good grade. Accessible in office hours, very kind, and willing to help.
He likes bugs, which is an immediate S-tier in my book.
He likes bugs, so that's an immediate 5/5 for me.

His lectures are dense and fast-paced but that's just the nature of the course. Lectures are posted online as well. He cracks jokes and seems to care abt the subject. The tests are HARD but fair and are same between all teachers. Not a lot of homework just study time. Many optional assignments he gives to help students with material. Flipped Friday

Hillyer is an amazing professor. His notes are incredibly detailed and they prepare you well for the exam. Exams are pure memorization, and the only reason they are difficult is due to the sheer amount of content we're learning. You don't have to go to lecture as he records them but I recommend going. He also has LAs. 4 Exams, 1 final. 1 exam drop

The Hillyer/DeSantis section is the best. Hillyer is the most caring and knowledgeable professor I've had. There is a TON of info you need to know for his very specific exams, but it is all very fair. Avoid cramming and memorize throughout the semester and you can pass this class. Average is a B, but with a little extra work, an A is attainable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hillyer is a decent lecturer and seems like a great person. His portion of 1511 has a ton of information, but he has far better slides. Exams are more difficult than Desantis' but fair. Def study throughout the sem rather than cramming before the exams. Homework is worth less than in 1510. Hillyer/Desantis is undoubtedly the better section of 1511.

Dr. Hillyer's exams may be hard due to the high volume of information, but he does his best to teach it well and make it engaging. You know what to expect for his exams. My biggest mistake was not studying earlier and more for his first exam. Do that and you're golden. Great teacher

Hillyer is a good professor and a good person. His slides are GOAT, but there are a lot of things to remember. His exams are hard, and you really have to study to get a good score. Your grade will not fail you if you put in enough effort.

Very genuine guy who is very passionate. Slides are organized and detailed, lectures recorded. Super fast paced and LOTS of convent, but that's just the class. Exams are super specific so need to memorize everything on slides so just put in time. Not much homework just memorization. His section is a lot more content than DeSantis but good prof.

Organized professor. Makes dad jokes. Lots of content. Hard content. An A is not impossible, but you need to put in the work. Came into this class with a sophomore telling me Desantis will be the harder professor. Inaccurate. Hillyer is. Desantis is easy.

While Hillyer is an amazing lecturer and is very helpful in office hours, you need to dedicate time and effort into studying for his exams. He gives you everything you need but you cannot afford to slack off in material. His exams are very fair and is only slightly difficult if you really review material. Plus, he is hilarious.
Very good. This is my favorite class ever.
Truly the best professor at Vanderbilt. Very smart, caring, and awesome. Made this difficult class enjoyable, and prepared us fully for exams.

I LOVE Dr. Hillyer! 10/10 would recommend. His slides are super well-organized and informative perfect for studying! He's amazing, hilarious, and one of those rare STEM professors who truly wants to inspire students to love science. You should take him! Oh and he's a total insect nerd, so be sure to ask him about that!

Dr. Hillyer is an amazing lecturer. He is very accessible and will go over anything you need during office hours. He makes lectures fun by cracking material-related jokes too. This class itself is a lot and can be overwhelming but go to his office hours!

Dr. Hillyer made A&P much more enjoyable. Not saying it was easy by any means, but his slides are amazing and you can tell he is extremely knowledgeable. His tests were hard but fair. I would definitely take him again.

Lectures are very straightforwards, all necessary information is on the slides, and there are weekly homework assignments that are very manageable. Tests are a little challenging, but nothing unexpected for the class. When he co-teaches this class, also consider who the other professor is.
All the info you need to know is on the slides. Super organized and easy to understand lectures.

Dr. Hillyer is THE GOAT. His lectures are great and so organized. Be prepared to memorize a TON of information, but everything you need for the exams is in his lecture slides. His tests were fair and he made lectures enjoyable with many bio jokes! Best bio prof I have had at Vandy so far!!

Hillyer was a bit easier compared to Desantis in my opinion. He has a lot of content, but he is consistently clearer and makes his tests fair. If you can memorize and apply a ton of concepts, you'll be fine. And if you ask questions, he'll actually help to the best of his ability instead of going, "everything is on the paper" like Desantis does.

Dr. Hillyer is an excellent professor. His lectures are very strong and engaging, with plenty of humor and thorough explanations. Exams are difficult, but completely fair if you read the slides carefully and do the optional worksheets. Very accessible and helpful in office hours. His and Dr. Desantis's class is excellent.

Literally the best man ever. Him as a person is so wholesome and he's so so so great. I loved his lectures more than 1510, and they were more simple to understand (personally). I highly recommend him. His tests are completely fair and understanding the topics thoroughly is the best thing you can do. Take him, no one regrets it!!!

Hillyer is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt so far. He has the best lecture slides in existence (you could theoretically skip all the classes and the lecture slides would be sufficient and clear enough). I have a list of his dad jokes from class and his lectures are so clear and I understand so much listening to him. He's also very hot.

The best BSCI 1511 guy you can get. His lectures were amazing and hilarious, he used scientific jokes to enlighten the lectures (what channel do ions watch on tv ? ion channels) . Take him if you can, 

P.S. DeSantis was a big plus too this time around.

He was unintentionally hilarious and his slides were amazing! It's not an easy class but always knew exactly what we needed to know for exams. We had Mastering which was very helpful for exam practice questions and counted as grade (buffer for tests)unlike the other section that wasn't offered it. I highly recommend taking Hillyer/Desantis section!

Normally I'd break down the pros and cons for a class, but there is seriously NO REASON not to take this class. Professor Hillyer is easily the best professor I've had during my freshman year; he's caring and has a lot of common sense in how he explains things. He's also very funny and doesn't give much homework.

Dr. Hillyer is a great lecturer who very evidently cares about his students and the material that he is teaching. The tests are very hard with lots of "one or more is true" answer choices and free response questions, however, they are the same tests given as the other bio class so take him.
Simply, the best

Dr. Hillyer is an excellent professor for the Biological Sciences Department. Yes, his lecture are content heavy but so are every other STEM course. One aspect about Dr. Hillyer that all of his students love is that he always throws in jokes to make students more engaged and follow along with the content. Overall, he is one of the best.

Hillyer is a great professor! He's so sweet and genuinely cares about his students. This course is very lecture heavy and he makes an effort to make them not boring by throwing in jokes. It's definitely a lot of material to learn, but if you memorize the lectures, you'll be fine for exams.
Hillyer tha goat, bro is just goated ong

Dr. Hillyer's lectures are boring since he just repeats the information on the slides and his exams cover very particular and obscure information. Matching is annoying and multiple choice is finnicky. Paying attention to the lectures is your best bet, but his class is honestly a hit-or-miss when it comes to the grade you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hillyer's section is difficult but clear. No need for the textbook, memorize his powerpoints (so much info!). A ton of work but a typical stem class. DeSantis's section is the opposite, little material but extremely unclear. It should be easy but it's not lol. Her tests are awful and she even gets confused by what she's asking. No dropped exam.
Accommodating in-person class but with recorded lectures to help those that got COVID. Clear lectures and expectations. Prof. Hillyer helped me during a difficult time. I recommend this professor.

Y'all are ripping on him but he's a really good lecturer. His slides are great and they're information dense, so the lectures are pretty tough and require a lot of memorization. He's always happy to explain further and answer questions and he actually makes sense

All of the information for Hillyer's exams are in his slides. You do not even have to attend lecture as long as you focus on the material on the slides. His exams were quite challenging and he graded tough and illogically on the free response questions. His half of the semester is better than the other half.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hillyer is an extremely useless professor. Lectures are completely unnecessary; if you literally memorize every single word on the slides, you'll be fine. Most of the questions on his exams are just pure memorization without any application or thinking. Study the slides and you'll be fine.

Honestly, he covered material in a perfectly fine manner. Not much to say about him--he made plenty of sense and did what he was there to do for an introductory course. I didn't have interaction with him outside of class, but he seems just like a dad-type professor, especially in his humor.

Dr. Hillyer is such an amazing professor! He is so passionate about teaching and biology, and it really shows. He is so helpful, kind, and very funny. His tests are quite reasonable, and test mostly concepts from the slides, not specific memorizational concepts. I would 10000000% take another one of his classes. I cannot recommend him enough.

He was really unhelpful in office hours and seemed annoyed that someone showed up to the zoom. He dodged every question I had and when I brought up concepts in lecture he was confused why I had questions in general. Don't hold office hours if you aren't going to use them productively.

This used to be a class that pre-meds used to boost their BCPM GPA, but it turned into another fast paced, stressful, GPA-tanking stem class. Nothing we learned was relevant for the MCAT either. unless you absolutely need this class to graduate, I would stay far away.
This is the second class I take with Professor Hillyer. Great Professor. There is quite a bit of work in this class (4 credits). Not fluff. Fair grader.
He says the tests come from lecture material, but he pulls the questions from the deepest parts of the textbook and expects you to know it. He is unhelpful and condescending during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This course has become yet another example of Vanderbilt wanting to lower averages in courses they believe should be harder for pre-health majors. It is a shame because this course should be taken by all pre-health majors, but I strongly urge you to stay away. Hillyer is so unhelpful and uncaring, and his exams are widely considered to be unfair.
Challenging exams but pretty easy grading at the end. Taking the intro bio classes before taking this class really helped me.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Hillyer is extremely unhelpful, does not give fair/reasonable exams, and made this class possibly one of the most miserable stem courses I have taken so far at Vandy. If my friends who are physicians or in medical school think our exams are ridiculous, you should take that as a sign to stay away from this joke of a course.
Great class with clear lectures. Comparing notes with my friends, this class was harder this year than last year.

Dr. Hillyer is such a sweet man and taught the material well but his grading was far too harsh. I attended lectures, took detailed notes from the textbook, and still did poorly on his exams. He was responsive to emails and seemed super understanding but ultimately did little to adjust grading standards when the class average was exceptionally low

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The test averages were the "worst he had seen in 14 years" and impossibly difficult. There is way more content to learn than you'd think, not to mention busywork assignments due every week that are graded harshly. save your mental health and stay far far away fro this class.
he just can't teach and hates when students challenge or ask him about the exam . AVOID

His notes are copied word to word from a poorly written textbook. In the office hour, he dodges all of your questions and gives you an impression that he does not know the materials. His lectures are basically him reading the textbook to you. Tests has many plausible answers and he tells you to choose best answer. Absolute nightmare.
One of the hardest most unforgiving professors at vanderbilt . student told him his test was too hard and he made the next one harder.

Nice guy, but he just reads off the slides. The only purpose of going to class is answering TopHat (10% of your grade). His part is harder than the second half of the class, but everything to know for the exam is in the notes, so don't buy the book. To do well, memorize/understand ALL of the slides (including details that may seem irrelevant).

Nice guy, but he only reads off the slides. Don't buy the book cause the exams only cover slide content, but it can be pretty specific. Only value in going to lecture is answering TopHat questions, which make up 10% of your grade. Other than that, just memorize the slides leading up to the exam if you want to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's genuinely super nice and makes funny jokes during lecture. Tests are straight from the powerpoints, but pretty specific and you have to know your stuff. Tests make up your entire grade.

Out of the 4 bio professors I've had so far, Hillyer is probably the most knowledgable and one of the more interesting. Super sweet guy, great lecturer, all good things to say. Only down side is that his tests were the most difficult 2 tests I've taken at Vandy, and it kinda screwed over my second semester bio grade. That's probably on me tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: hard class but good lecturer. sweet guy

Excellent teaching style that kept me engaged. Grading is via a mix of exams, quizzes, and writing assignments. All the information needed is in the slides and in what is discussed in class. This is my favorite bio class so far.

His lecture slides were clear but heavy with information. The class is mostly straight memorization with an ability to apply the concepts in other problems. He posted all the lecture slides, so there was no reason to attend class. As long as you drill the information and can apply it to examples, you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He reads off the slides a lot but the slides are well organized. He is a really nice man and makes jokes at times, but lectures get long sometimes. Exams are pretty straightforward, just study the slides well and you'll do fine. Solid choice for bio.

Professor Hillyer is great! His lectures are very clear, and he makes a great effort to help every student understand the material. The tests come directly from his slides so make sure you understand them well if you want to do well.

Hillyer is a really nice professor. He's willing to help but he was new. Since this was his first time teaching the class, he read off the slides a lot. The tests are really tough  (multiple choice options A-J) but all of the information is on the powerpoint slides and it's not impossible.

He is the best bio professor I've ever had. Awesome dad jokes and overall a very nice guy. His tests are kind of hard but not impossible (basically what you would expect out of a bio class). Take him if you can! You won't regret it. All the info is in the lectures so you don't need to read the textbook.
Great guy with an awesome sense of humor! Made the class fun to go to because of his dad jokes and his funny examples which helped clarify things.

Hillyer was the best!!!! He's hilarious and has so many dad jokes. His lectures are interesting and you can tell he's really into the subject. Always ready for help the day before the test and as long as you study and are good at memorizing, getting an A is not hard.

BSCI 236 is a great course. Dr. Hillyer gives crystal clear lectures that are well organized. People say he's a hard grader, but he curved the grade sufficiently in the end. So, I thought he was a very fair grader. The subject matter is interesting, but occasionally pretty graphic. The text book for this course is also very well written.
Dr. Hillyer was one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Really engaging, extremely willing to help any students that are struggling. Fair grader. Really interesting material.

Very tough grader. While the topic was semi-interesting, the amount of expected outside reading was absurd (multiple hours of scientific journals). Hillyer also is very poor at stimulating discussion, turning a very interesting topic into a dreadfully boring one.

Awesome Professor, one of the best. Great sense of humor, interesting lecturer, and extremely helpful. A lot of memorization, but tests are fair and not to bad with some studying. I would recommend taking any class he teaches!

This class was incredibly interesting, we learned about many different parasites from a tropical medicine perspective. Great for pre-meds. However there is SO MUCH memorization!!! This class is hard because there is really no understanding, it is all repeating back facts. There are three tests (average was usually in the 70's) and 7 pop quizzes.
He didn't seem to understand the material he taught very well?
If Reddit was a philosophy professor

I absolutely loved Prof. Kurun. Easily one of the best professors I've had so far at Vandy. He truly cares about his students' learning and is very passionate about what he does. Tests and cumulative paper were fair and very doable. Utilize his office hours and go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kurun is one of the most remarkable instructors in the philosophy department. He truly teaches you how to comprehend, argue, and write PROPERLY. Not many people in your life will pay such close attention to these vital skills. Moreover, Kurun is engaging, funny, and inspiring all while the grading is easy and he loves hearing feedback.

Ismail is excellent at explaining complex philosophy readings in a way anyone can understand and appreciate. I highly recommend you take him if you plan on taking a philosophy class. With reasonable effort, anyone can do well in his classes. He is also very available and helpful for office hours.

I took Intro to ethics with Ismail and he was great. The best part about him is that he will change parts of the class based off feedback throughout the semester. His lectures were interesting and he then encouraged us to use what we learned during discussions. Some topics were sensitive but he navigated them well. I recommend taking his class!

For some reason, wouldn't let me tag the course code as PHIL 1005, but this is the class I took with Kurun. He genuinely cares about his students and their success in his class. He asks for feedback and adjusts his class based on what his students need. Assigns readings per class that aren't too difficult. Discussion based class. 100% recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ismail is an outstanding professor and one of the best teachers I had at Vanderbilt. I took his class to fulfill a degree requirement, with no prior interest in philosophy. However, his lectures and passion for the subject made me deeply enjoy and appreciate it. He genuinely enjoys teaching and is great at it. I would love to take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall great class! Ismail really knows his philosophy and communicates concepts very clearly. His lectures were extremely informative, and he was always willing to meet with students outside of class, which was really helpful. Also, Ismail really cares about his students. HIGHLY recommend taking a class with him!!
Such a knowledgeable, kind, funny, great professor and human being. She truly cares about both her areas of expertise and her students

Took for AXLE; ridiculously easy. Got 100s on every assignment. Told us that we'd get credit if we showed effort and followed assignment guidelines. There are two exams, five small homeworks, and two projects. Offered an extra credit opportunity. Class/lectures are boring though.

Took this class for my freshman writing seminar, was bored out of my mind the entire time. Does not encourage student discussion so the class is silent. Writing assignments were fun and she is an easy grader. The energy in the classroom was just off.

I loved Professor Miranda's class, it was so fun and hilarious given the classroom participation. One thing I will say about her classes, she has pop quizzes at the end of class, so attendance is necessary. A few questions on the midterm/final are also pretty challenging as the textbooks are hard to navigate, luckily theres extra credit!

I really liked being in Prof. Miranda's course this fall. She is kind and approachable; you can tell she cares about her students. I didn't find assignments or tests too difficult. She's very knowledgeable about the (enjoyable) content she teaches, encourages you to explore further, and incites insightful class discussions. Awesome class!

Professor Miranda is amazing and so sweet. She is very caring and loves if you participate in class. Lectures can be boring at times, but the content is very interesting. She brings in guest artists and encourages you to explore outside of the school which I really enjoyed. Take her classes!
Pretty boring lectures, but easy grader. She does not really care if one is participating or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Run

Prof is a total sweetheart. However, no syllabus and no clue assignment weight. essays were ~500 words. final was a research proposal and a presentation.  Easy prof but be ready to read and participate. she LOVES if you talk, and you'll see it in your grade if you do. Easy A all the way. got away without doing some readings by participating.

She is by far the best professor at Vandy. Her classes are an easy A because she is so caring and loving and accommodates everybody. She gives good feedback and clearly outlines all her expectations in advance. She really wants everyone to do well in her class. Material is super interesting too. Love her <3

Solid class for AXLE purposes, just lectures with 5 quizzes, two "long" writing assignments (like 500 words), a few documentaries w/ responses, & a group final. Prof. Miranda was really sweet and seemed to really care that we thought the content was interesting. I feel bad that we almost never participated or had our camera on but she understood.

i love prof west! he is so nice, gives super engaging lectures where the entire class does actively participate. the content in the class is so interesting, he cares about his students and keeping ppl engaged so modifies syllabus based on class interests! frequent quizzes but not hard, he drops five of them, and interesting open ended essays!

Interesting class and good teacher. Come to class as much as you can, but participation and attendence is not required. Grade is dependent on three essays - most people get between a 90-94 on them - he grades pretty personally and it is not always reflective of how good/bad your essay is. Take him and this class though, enjoyed
He is a bad professor and grade you based on how he feels about you. Would never take his class again. If you ask him to explain his grading he takes it as disrespect.

CMST 2800 (Tag wasn't available). I LOVED this class. Professor West made it so interesting and lectures were always great. The topics are cool and he always loops them in to real world events. There were 2 exams which were very hard to study for, but I think the fun lectures and content makes it worth it. Take it!
class is a joke. Exams determine ur grade but he grades based off vibes. Would never take him again.

Professor West goes above and beyond in his classes. He is so knowledgeable about what he teaches and picks at your brain with insightful questions which spark discussion and a greater understanding of the material. His course materials are interesting and well selected. Office hours are helpful and he is very accessible.

Super accessible and understood how to do an online class well. This class is centered around one long essay to turn in, which felt like a very doable goal and he was helpful with his feedback throughout.

West is awesome! Lectures were engaging, super accessible, and allows you to pursue whatever you're interested in. The class itself is a lot of writing in comparison to my other W classes, but he breaks down the big semester paper (25 pages) into smaller pieces. Gives great feedback and challenges you to think critically and improve your writing.

Prof. West is awesome. He really cares about his students and works hard to make each class useful. This course involved a major (30-35 pg) essay, but he was always available to meet or discuss the project even after coronavirus moved class online. He allows his students flexibility in their topics and genuinely welcomes diversity of thought. 10/10

Professor West's courses are engaging and challenging, and he is not afraid to push back on your ideas to make you think. West cares about his students an is evidently passionate about the content of courses that he teaches. His classes will require you to put in work and do the readings, but the discussions are fascinating and rewarding. Would rec
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor West is hands down one of the best profs Ive had at Vandy. Actually makes you think about things and engages with student discussion and plays devils advocate so that you are actually grappling with real topics and not just trying to please him. Reading quizzes almost every class are manageable, and 3 papers total for the class (8 pages)

This was, BY FAR, the hardest class I've ever taken. Exactly ZERO people in the class got an A. The main problem with Dr. Igarashi is that the grading criteria are both impossibly high and ambiguous. There are no rubrics for the three essays (90% of the grade). I never understood how his feedback translated into a specific grade. But he is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took him for 3000W, so a lot of reading was expected. It was approximately 150-200 pages a week. He's a really great guy, and I found him to be quite funny. The class was a bit monotonous at times, but I would say he's overall really good at explaining concepts and making things engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 essays each worth 30%. good discussions which unfortunately don't serve any purpose besides being a small buffer of your grade. would not recommend this class if you're looking for axle credit

the issue i had with this class was that there was no clear grading rubric. it was purely based on vibes, making it quite literally impossible to achieve the grade you want. 3 essays basically make up your entire grade, and his policy is that attendance can only hurt your grade, but it cannot help your grade (if you take this class youll see)

AVOID THIS CLASS. Guaranteed non A grade. You could be a NY times bestselling author and not receive an A as long as he doesn't like your essay. Also will not curve the class. If you're looking for an easy intl cul class like I was, think again.

i have mixed feelings about dr. igarashi. he is sweet and passionate about what he teaches. but, the way he grades is so evil. this is an intro writing course and the average for the first 2 (of 3) papers was an 87.5 both times. if he doesn't like or agree with your argument (which happens very often), good luck getting an A.
prof igarashi was great. class was all discussions, so come prepared enough to attempt to participate. super understanding guy that seemed to care about his students. low pressure enviornment.

He is very nice and tries to make class engaging. Lecture slides don't have much written so pay attention. There's a decent amount of weekly reading (~ 50 pgs), 2 papers and 2 exams. Attendance counts heavy for a grade. Be prepared to talk but with such a small class it's chill. Grading on papers is ambiguous but you should do decent with effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Igarashi is a nice professor! He really cares about his students and give really detail instructions to students on individual meetings. Easy A class, and will definitely take it again!
Mandatory attendance class, but discussion questions and class vibe are pretty chill. Definitely easy A class if you follow the professor's instruction. Would definitely take it again!
Professor Igarashi is a really kind guy. He's one to one meetings help a lot. Easy-A class, would definitely take it again!!

Dr. Igarashi is a fun guy. He may be a good person but not a great writing professor. You need to come to the class, and he will force you to speak. The workload is not very much as a writing course. But it's hard to get an A in this course since you cannot get any useful feedback and you have no idea about how he will give you a good grade.

The quality of the lecture slides was very poor, leading to a lack of clear (and correct) information about the topics that were on the exams. Essay grading was pretty strict -- supposedly the grade is proportional to the effort put in, but he has no actual way of knowing how much effort you put in. I wouldn't recommend this professor. At all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cares about his students and does his best to keep lectures interesting. If you're into the material it's a great class, but I can understand how it could be dry if you don't already have interest in Japanese history. He'll make you work for a good grade on the papers and tests, but you'll get out what you put in!
pretty tough but good
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I will say, he's genuinely pretty tough, and you probably won't come out with an A.

However!! I feel like I've learned so much in his classes- I took one my first and second semester, and when he has classes available again I'll take them too. He really challenges you to think. I felt like I really grew as a person in his classes. 10/10 if I could
Harsh grader without constructive feedback. Does not give out A's. I'd avoid taking this class for a 1000 level W. Nice guy, but just not worth it.

Approaches the subject of history in a very unique way--lots of relation to sociology/media studies in lectures. Feedback on papers is somewhat vague, but prompts are interesting/creative and different that what you typically see. Some memorization-based tests and quizzes which seem a bit useless but they're fairly easy and don't count for much.

Friendly dude but his class requires heavy participation and he's a tough grader. He will readily call on you so don't take it unless you are interested. When it comes to our essays and essay tests, he seemingly takes off points for no reason. He will overall say your work is good but he rarely gives out A's
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Igarashi is a good guy, good professor, but he can also be a pretty difficult grader. He isn't difficult in the sense that he is overly critical (on papers assignments), but I sometimes leave his office hours with more questions than answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very smart professor who is passionate about Japanese studies. You definitely have to do the readings on time and participate in class discussions. The papers, however, are challenging. He allows you to write and receive feedback before submitting the final version, however the papers are graded semi-harshly.

Igarashi is a professor who cares about his students but is also a very tough grader. Very rarely does he ever give A's and his class requires more effort than your typical 1000W class. He goes above and beyond and meets with his students 1 on 1 but the books chosen were not super interesting. I would recommend the class if interested in Japan.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is good at creating an engaging class environment encourages deeper thinking into the provided readings. Prompts for papers are vague that allow flexibility for topics to be written about. One on one meetings about paper drafts are helpful but does not provide specific comments on how to refine paper's argument.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Igarashi creates very interesting, thought-provoking discussions on books that I personally enjoyed a lot. He has high standards for papers (3 per semester), and will make you push yourself in your analysis, but it's very rewarding, and I learned a lot in this class and genuinely enjoyed the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Igarashi's discussions were very engaging and I always enjoyed coming to class. Tough papers but Igarashi is a true senpai and you will do well if your drafts are solidish.

Really great class discussion - primarily in small groups. Writing is graded harshly, but he requires you to meet with him before each paper which is helpful for feedback. Difficult to get A-range papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Igarashi is a solid choice if you feel confident in your writing abilities. With that being said, he expects a lot out of you. His essay prompts and expectations really make you think critically and creatively. It's unsettling that the final grade is based mostly on papers, but it really encourages you to think about your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a good guy, but isn't always clear about what he wants from your essays. Still a great professor and would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Igarashi does a good job in creating engaging environment and gives everyone opportunity to share their perspectives on the matter. Lecture is not heavy at all. Expect intensive discussion on readings. Writings can be challenging since grading criteria is oftentimes vague. His feedback also hardly contains constructive recommendations.

Igarashi Sensei provides students with detailed feedbacks in their papers and journals. The lectures are generally clear, and in the discussion session he gives students inspirational prompts. Though a tough grader, he loves to leave comments that would definitely help with your writing every time he returns your paper.

Prof. Igarashi is excellent when it comes to creating an engaging environment and promoting critical thinking. Lectures are intertwined with discussions to create enlightening dialogues between everybody in the class. He encourages students to truly hone in on history instead of taking a broad viewpoint.  Take if you want to expand your horizons.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: It's teachers like Professor Igarashi that make me proud to be a Dore. His presentations have an almost cinematic quality. Unlike other history teachers I've had, Professor Igarashi gives you the knowledge as well as the freedom to share your thoughts on Japanese history. In his class, history flows like a great book. Yoshikuni is the man!

Great teacher, extremely knowledgeable about his subject. There are tons of readings, but relatively few essays. He requires you to take notes on the readings, and participation is mandatory. Good lectures, useful teacher, interesting class. Ignore the one guy in 2004 that griped about him, Igarashi is def significantly better than average.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Based on the effort that I put in to the class, the grade that I received was more than fair. In fact, I thought I would do worse. He is very interesting and willing to help. I don't think it'd be for everyone, but I really liked it.

Very tough teacher. He is easy to approach and talk about papers but the level of specificity he looks for is almost impossible. Some of the movies you watch are hard to go back and watch again for your paper. He is hard to follow in class sometimes for his accent. Unless you like writing about film and techniques, consider other writing seminars.
As Professor Igarashi would say when assessing my papers, "complicate things." His teaching style certainly does just that. The content of this class is interesting; its presentation, not.
He is surprisingly picky about the writing in the papers, so do your best work.  Exams are simple if you study.
No Comments

Should not be teaching. If that doesn't sum it up, then let me add: he is unclear in class, he grades oddly, and he doesn't make clear what he expects from students.  On the plus side: He is very smart, and he is nice, helpful in office.  Still, he leaves too much to be desired in the classroom.  Oh, did I already say that he should not be teaching
No Comments

Great teacher, enjoyed the class a lot. lectures may be hard to follow but interesting and draws upon many interesting points. a lot of reading, but very interesting. tests are managable, gives the essays beforehand. take good notes, go to class, tests very lecture intensive, the readings are merely
Lectures are very unorganized.  Hard to take notes.  Grades are random.  Id only take this as a pass/fail

Interesting teacher and lectures are fun if somewhat ambiguous, but grades don't necessarily seem to reflect how much you've learned. If you aren't great at writing this may not be the class for you.  If grades weren't an issue, I would highly reccomend this class; it was definetly a blast.
Not clear in his lectures or discussions or his expectations of assignments.  Helpful, though, outside of class and actually a nice guy and smart, just not a good teacher.  Grades seemed arbitrary.

Dr. Igo cares about her students, but she takes her class way too seriously. For a class that almost every freshman has to take, she acts like this class is meant to be more rigorous than it is. She gives a failing grade to well-done assignments, and the accompanying feedback is very knitpicky.
Take Dr. Igo for CORE 1010! She is amazing, and the discussions we had in class were more interesting & insightful than the other core sections I've heard from.

I had Prof. Igo for Core 1010 and she is the kindest professor I know. She can be a tough grader but it's because she wants you to do your best. She will occasionally bring baked goods to class and they are very yummy.

Igo gives great lectures and is such a caring professor. Her papers are really vague and she's a pretty tough grader, but if you're interested in the subject then i would definitely recommend taking a class with her because she's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the most delightful people I've ever met. Brilliant, sweet, momlike professor whose interest in the subject is contagious. The class was mostly discussion based, so I guess it depends a lot on the students in your class, but the readings are at least all interesting. Skipping the reading was common, but you'll get more out of it if you read.

This class was made very easy by Dr.Ivie. She is such an amazing professor. Just make sure you stay engaged and read the little passages she assigns, in order to participate in the class. I would 1000 percent take her class again! Make sure you stay on top of HOMEWORK or else your grade will not be the best, everything else is so so so very easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Ivie is an amazing professor. She makes classes fun and educational. I highly recommend you take her class. The readings are fascinating.

Dr. Ivie is an extremely kind professor who grades exactly according to the rubric that she provides. She allows many opportunities for extra credit and makes it known that she is available outside of class. The essay conferences that I've had with her were always helpful and pointed me in the right direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr.Ivie was an easy grader. I have to assume anyone who took my level class and says not to take her is being dramatic and didn't try very hard. Had reading homework between most classes, but it was extremely manageable and quick. Dr.Ivie was always nice, just didn't seem to care to get to know her students well.
Dr. Ivie was amazing all semester!

Professor Ivie is very understanding and flexible. She understands that we are college students who have a lot of work to do. If you ever want to speak with her she is available and class is easy to pass as long as you do the work assigned. She is very nice and kind I think the nicest teacher I had this semester.

Dr. Ivie was always very nice and willing to help! It was not hard to get good grades and as long as you show up you should be good. The class itself is a little boring if you took English in high school, but overall, a very easy and manageable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor was understanding and the class was very chill. The assignments that were assigned were clear, and the professor would gladly support and answer question if any students had any questions.

Professor Ivie is a good professor who is kind and understanding. There wasn't too much work considering it being a english class. It is very easy to talk with her and during class we would discuss with everyone as part of participation. It is better if you answer questions and ask them during class so that it runs smoothly.

90% of class time is spent discussing readings. The class was more time-consuming than difficult. However, she will frequently grade harshly on reading responses and essays and doesn't give good feedback on them. Found her grading to be very subjective and kind of annoying at times. She is responsive to concerns you may raise over email.

This course is graded on a project and two midterms. It is very easy to do well on these, as they are all based on just understanding the topics and being able to talk/write about them. Professor Izzo covers a lot of math and other things in the lectures, which can make them a little tricky to follow, but they are not necessary to know to do well.

Dr. Izzo is a great professor. She is very caring and really tries to keep students engaged during class. Attendance is optional but you will need to go to class everyday or you won't do well, because the class is only graded on the midterm, a group presentation, and the final. No graded homework either so you don't know how grading is until exams.

Professor Izzo wants to teach everyone the content, but she is not the best at explaining. If you ask questions and pay attention, you will be able to learn everything. There is no attendance requirement or homework and the class is graded on a simple project, one midterm, and one final. This means you need to study hard for the exams.

Prof Izzo is a very kind prof. Lectures are somewhat interesting. Definitely ask questions when you are confused, it helps the class flow at better paces (she will move fast otherwise). Two tests and a project, all kind grading but study well for those. Interesting content, the class is as good as you want to make it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Izzo is super kind and cares about her students. The exams are pretty easy and she is transparent about what will be on them. Homework is optional. All content comes from lectures, which are actually quite good and interesting. This is a great choice for a higher level elective, definitely easier and more interesting than alternatives.
My favorite class this semester. Put in the work easy A. Learned a lot.

Dr. Helderman is amazing!!! He truly wants the best for us and is very approachable and caring. I appreciated the balance between lecture and discussions. The films we watched were amazing. I would highly recommend taking any of his classes!

Dr. Helderman has genuinely been one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. He is very knowledgeable on the topics he teaches and is clearly very passionate. He is very helpful with assignments, and as long as you participate and stay on top of work you're bound to do well in the class. He is so awesome, take him if you can!
Great and engaging lecturer and most of your grade was based on two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The bad reviews must be old. Dr. G wanted us to learn as much as possible. Quizzes and assignments were easy. Most of the class was one big project that was easy to score high on. She grades super quickly and is super accessible in office hours and always values feedback on what we struggle with and is willing to adjust grading.

don't listen to other reviews! prof. g puts so much care and intention into her lectures-- while the class isn't easy, it's because she truly wants students to grow. if you put the work and the dedication that this class deserves, it is SO worth your while. these accent comments are insane, she's absolutely comprehensible. i've never had an issue.

Although she's definitely a harsh grader, Prof. Gauthier made up for that by being available outside of class, providing extra credit/hw and quiz drops, and listening to students' thoughts on the difficulty of quiz questions (dropping many of these if they were too hard!) She seems scary at first but an A is attainable if you put the work in!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I hated every waking moment of this course! It was the bane of my existence! Very tough grader and unnecessarily strict about participation. There's so many assignments too... I could scream. If you've got a busy schedule, DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE.

Gauthier made it out of her way to make this class a hellhole of an experience. Not only did she grade our assignments unbelievably harsh, but she was unreceptive to the challenges that students were navigating during COVID, assigning us up to six different assignments (quizzes, projects, tests, peer-reviews) in just one week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She assigns way too much homework and throughout the semester there are constant projects and tests. The work load was absolutely ridiculous and she showed little concern for her students mental health. If you have to take this class, please do it with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever had. It seems like she wants her students to fail, assigns pointless assignments every 2 days (literally), and pits students against each other. The course was online this year so she never actually teaches you- just made us do countless quizzes and HW. This class crushes spirits and makes you hate learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Multiple writings/week on Peerceptiv. The grading is partly based on your peers' review, which is not always objective. She breaks down the big assignment into small sections, but she grades on every draft so you have to be intense every day. There are 4 tests plus a final, 3 big reports, more than 20 completion quizzes, and more than 20 writings.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cannot agree more with former comments! She assigns readings and assignments for self-study only, and seldom gives lectures! She turned a lecture-based class into an asynchronous self-study class. I think her job is totally unnecessary for this class since we have to learn everything on our own. Her class doesn't deserve the tuition fee we paid.

Multiple large assignments per week. A large portion of the class is graded by consensus of peers and curved based on these peer grades. Assignments she actually grades had unclear directions and were graded harshly. Would not recommend if it is at all avoidable. Incorrectly calculated course grades and did not receive a correction for weeks.

This was the most ridiculous course Ive ever taken in my entire life. The workload was out of this world, the grading was harsh, and there was such a consistent lack of consideration. If youre a Psych major and have to take this class, Im praying for you. Be ready to have more work than you ever have in a single class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you are a cognitive studies major, heads up: Take PSY-PC 2170 as opposed to PSY 2150 with Dr. Gauthier. Avoid Dr. G at all costs. If you are a psychology major and can wait another semester to see if a different professor is teaching this course, do. Words cannot describe how awful this class is. It destroys and demoralizes your soul.

I learned, but only through working blindly on my own. The chapters in the books were not gone over lecture AT ALL. You learn by doing quizzes and writing MCs that receive confusing feedback. It's a lot of unnecessary work that other profs for the same class do not require.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever. Unclear grading criteria & an insane amount of busy work that has nothing to do with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hands down the worst professor I've ever had at Vanderbilt for Principles of Experimental Design. She has her students act as her personal TAs, gives zero rubric or guidelines for papers until AFTER they're graded, and completely demeans her students when they email her giving her feedback or asking questions. Completely inconsiderate during COVID.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far the worst class I have ever taken. Dr G has no passion for teaching. She says "there are no stupid questions" but if you ask her questions, she is condescending. She tried to turn a lecture class into a seminar. The workload is incredible and most of it is wasted on pointless assignments. Her instructions are unclear, and she grades harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the worst class Ive taken. The way the class is structured really ruins the content of the course. This class takes so much time and she is a really hard grader. One of my favorite things that prof G said was that she was very generous in grading class participation but the mean for class participation was a 76...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class was pretty interesting and covered all the basics of psychology. The grading criteria made it pretty easy to get an A since you could do test corrections on each test and drop your lowest grade. There were also some simple completion aspects to the grade. The tests werent meant to be tricky, but you have to keep up with the class to do well

Dr. Gauthier's first language isn't English, so sometimes the wording of her test choices is difficult to understand. The class itself isn't hard to do well in. There are 2 exams and a final, 10 short writing assignments, and required research studies. She posts all of her lecture slides online and offers a lot of opportunities for extra credit.

Gauthier's reviews are dismal at best, but I thought this class was okay. Thinking days are hit or miss, but there are extra credit opportunities to drop your lowest ones. And there are test corrections and extra research credit. If you show up to class, pay attention, take notes, and read the book, you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class. It was incredibly difficult for an intro level class, the multiple choice tests had two right answers for every question and were completely arbitrary, she is terrible at explaining anything in lectures, and barely tests on them but rather on super obscure facts buried in the textbook.

Defeniteily take this class! Dr. G is a funny woman and the class is super interesting and super easy. There are three exams in all (including the final) and you can drop one so the final doesn't matter. She lets you correct the exams and you take a practice exam before, too! She's the best.
Fair and generous grading policy. She's normally upbeat and funny in her lectures, which makes them interesting, even early in the morning.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gauthier was very down to earth and fun to get to know! Her Brain Damage and Cognition class was great because there are no tests, just a semester long project broken down into chunks. I found it manageable, as long as you started EARLY you had plenty of time to ask for feedback and get a decent grade. Class participation is technically required.

Dr. Gauthier is a nice person and all, but her methods are a bit unusual. For instance, she tries to make a lecture-type class a discussion-based class. She also has these special days at the start of every week called Thinking Days where you are compared to your peers--they are graded harshly in my opinion. Tests are hard b/c she is bilingual.

Professor Gauthier is a decent professor, but there is a language barrier on her tests. The questions can be incredibly poorly-worded. Coupled with a bizarre grading system, this class can be hard to get an A in. She does offer test corrections and 2 extra credit points though.

If you're trying to get an easy A don't take take her class. She is extremely unclear in her lectures and just plain boring. Her tests are also unclear and impossible to understand. The effort it takes to pass this class is beyond the scope of an intro class.

PSY 277 is a very interesting class set up that is engaging and interesting. There is only 1 lecture a week. One day is MC that students write (work hard writing these- it's not easy to get a 33 points), 1 lecture, and 1 day of talking about our brain damaged patients. Highly recommend.

She is not the clearest lecturer, but she is passionate about the subject matter and does try to help students outside of class. Keep up with the reading in the textbook and the tests are not too bad.
very very difficult class. tests are needlessly wordy. i studied my butt off and got Cs on both. not looking forward to final exam.

she's foreign. her tests are all multiple choice, but are often difficult to understand because of the language barrier. long textbook readings. tough tests. she gives you chances to save your grade by dropping lowest scores, but the tests are still hard and it's a lot of work. don't recommend it unless you're a smartypants

she's ok. lectures are super boring. writing assignment in class every monday (30% of your grade) = sucks. exams are hard, even with self correct. she has a drop1exam policy if you meet certain requirements which is GREAT cause the final covers so much material i can't imagine getting a decent grade. reading is key but it's not enough for an A.
She's adorable. It's not hard to do well if you show up to class.

Enjoyed this class. Tests are hard but you can self-correct for points. Must go to class to understand the pp.'s. MUST READ THE ENTIRE BOOK. if you don't read you won't understand the tests at all. If you already read, this won't be hard. She's nice. You can get extra credit thru psych experiments. I recommend her & this class
Studying for this class is HARD. She gives a study guide for exams but the info on the tests is primarily conceptual.
The cutest little Frenchy I've ever seen. Her accent is just adorable. Class is hard, though. Read the textbook thoroughly if you want an A.

Thoroughly enjoyed having this professor. Responded to emails quickly, never failed to take the time to answer any questions I had about the subject matter and had no problems meeting outside of class to help with the group project we had for the semester. It is a class that weeds out those who shouldn't be in this field, though.

She changed her class recently sot that here are no tests at all. However, the class is only out of 100 points, so each point deducted is a percentage off your grade. The material is SUPER interesting, but it actually is a decent amount of work. There are weekly clicker quizzes that are questions from students, which makes it difficult. Nice Lady.

I dunno what you guys are talking about.  Sure she has an interesting accent, mentions bears alot and in general requires students to do work outside the class but she is great.  One of the nicest professors ever.  If you don't think so then you have never gone and talked to her one on one.  Plus she is HOT

she may be a great psychologist, but she is the worst teacher ever. her impossible tests might have to do with the fact that she writes them in french first and then translates them. class is boring and worthless, just have somebody take your clicker to class

This class is not impossible. If you study the book and the lecture powerpoint (that she posts online for everyone), you will do fine. She makes the concepts more confusing than they really are on the tests, but if you study enough, you will be fine. Attendance is manditory though.

absolutely awful.  i studied 25 hours for her final and got a 76.  that shows how impossible and stupid her tests are.  do not take this class, if you are signed up for it, drop it.  you dont learn anything from her, its all the book. i gained nothing by going to class, you might as well just buy the book and read it if you want to know about psych

Ugh. Ok, no this class is not the worst one at Vanderbilt. But it's not a good one. Professor Gauthier is a nice woman who is definitely extremely intelligent, but it's obvious that she should not be teaching an intro course. The tests are picky, long, and convoluted. She makes easy concepts difficult. But her accent isn't that bad.

I'm sure Professor Gauthier is a very nice woman, but she should NOT be teaching an introductory course. Her lectures are long, boring, and incomprehensible, her tests are all multiple choice and absolutely impossible if you don't know concepts - which she is terrible at explaining - down cold. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER.

horrible class. going to class is pointless unless you are one of the 4 people that talk. attempts to make a discussion based class with 300 kids in it..tests are impossible-no matter how much you study

I'm sittingin this class, wondering why I am here! She has buchered my desire to major in psychology. Can't understand the testa at ALL! French Canadian is not my language! She doesn't answer questions at ALL! I despise this class now. And have plans to change my major because of her! AVOID THIS CLASS BY ALLLLLL MEANS!!!!!!!!

I really don't think she's that bad at all. It's not really an easy class, but she tells you what you need to know and she lets you drop you lowest test grade. I also think she explains things really well and she doesn't mind students asking questions at all and will take the time to answer them until you understand.

Stay away from this class at all costs. The tests are extremely difficult for an intro level course. If you take this class it will be a huge mistake, seriously avoid. This is my worst class and I hear complaints about its difficulty on a daily basis, all these people aren't wrong. AVOID AVOID AVOID

Prof. Gauthier is a very kind, energetic professor. HOWEVER, I would not recommend taking this class. The majority of lecture is spent answering questions on the "clicker" rather than actually learning/discussing the material. The tests are all multiple choice-- make of it what you may. If you do take the class, memorize the text book... all of it

She seems like a very nice professor - she tries to be funny and engaging in class. But I wouldn't recommend this class to non-majors. It's very difficult for an intro class. It might as well be a weed-out class like Gen Chem. If you do take it, read the book carefully and prepare for detailed exams.

By far the WORST professor I have ever encountered at Vanderbilt. Do NOT take this class with her. Gautier is absolutely miserable. Tests were all multiple choice and extremely difficult. Class is boring and you cannot understand her English.

She's a very fair teacher.  Read all the required assignments in the textbook, and know all of the highlighted vocab.  That's pretty much the whole test right there.  She also throws out questions if many people get them wrong.
Used an experimental class format that was a disaster. Only one of three days are lecture, the rest are useless but required attendance. The case study is a crapshoot; avoid this class.

Pretty hard to understand, both her and her TAs had english as their second language. Horrible review sessions, and her exams had a lot of really badly worded questions. However, her lectures were interesting with many video clips etc.

Gauthier's class isn't that hard. Yes, she has an accent, and yes, her test questions can be random, but she curves them, gives students opportunites to get points back, offers extra credit, and gives students an opportunity to drop their lowest grade. If you read (you don't have to go to class, lectures are all online) then you should be fine.
Terrible at lecturing. I had to teach myself the entire book outside of class. Plus the accent makes her difficult to understand in a large lecture hall. Everything in the book is fair game.

Class was soooooo boring. I didn't learn anything in class. I had to teach myself pretty much everything. She takes attendance, and if you miss too many classes, it hurts your grade. You have to do a certain amount of experiments too. Don't take the class unless you plan on majoring in PSYCH.

You either hate her or you love her. I was in between because she made the class really interesting, but then again, her tests are crazy confusing. You really have to understand the concepts cold to do well on the test. I dunno. She's cool, but after all was said and done....C for me :(

This class is very hard. I really didn't like it. The lectures are boring and don't explain very much. Dr. Gauthier seems like a very nice person but she does not lecture well to large groups. I had to kill myself outside of class to teach myself most of the material. I didn't really like this class and I wish I had taken something else.

This is by far the worst professor I have ever had.  She has no interest in the caliber of her class or the welfare of her students.  Her TAs are no help, and it seems their only job is to produce multiple spelling errors on each typed test.  I was very interested in taking this class and this teacher shot down my interest in majoring in psychology

Very boring class! Gauthier reads off of her lecture slides the entire time, which can be found online. Her tests are difficult and confusing, but manageable. Read the text, dont bother going to class.

I couldn't ever stay awake with this lady.  Her lectures were boring and just restated information from the book.  I thought psych was cool before, but now, it's whackarnolds.  Good nap time in class because I was put to sleep, but that didn't work out too well on tests, which had some crazy jargon.
This is the most amazing professor ever! I do think she is afraid of bear though.. Her test are difficult but its all word for word from the test. Makes for a very interesting class
No Comments

Prof. Gauthier taught class very well, but if you can't learn everything on your own, you're screwed. Also, her 'practice questions' in class are so simple, yet her test questions read like crazy French-Canadian speak.

Dr Gauthier is not an evil human being, nor does she deserve the plague; she is a very sweet person.  She genuinely tries her best to lecture to a large class and explain the material the best way she knows how.  However, most of the material you have to teach to yourself for hours and hours just to get a C on the tests, but you do get to drop one.
avoid her like the plague. if you already have the plaugue, please give it to her.

this was one of the easiest classes i've taken at vanderbilt-yeah, she doesn't curve her tests, but she always ends up taking out whole bunch of questions, so it actually ends up better than curving.  besides, you get to drop a test!
Hard and confusing tests. Which are not curved.
What an awful human being.
No Comments
Great Teacher. Great Lectures. Very Hard Tests. I learned a lot but got a C. Not good.
Hard class for intro, tries to cover too much material in her terrible French Canadian accent.  I wanted an easy intro to get some CPLE out of the way and jumped into a terrible class.

ms. g is a very nice lady. but her tests are very confusing. how can u answer a question in degrees? which one is most correct? it depends on how u feel about the subject. very difficult class to get a good grade in if u have not already taken psych. lectures are crowded with too much information and u generally have to teach urself.
No Comments
Wonderful professor.  Really knows her stuff, and I loved learning from her.  Yes, it was hard, but it's not meant to be easy.  She was excellent.
Tried to cover way too much in lecture so ended up actually communicating nothing.  Tests were poorly written and impossible.  Turned me away from my intended major.
this woman is awful. avoid her class at all costs. her tests are confusing because her diction is totally messed up.
No Comments

She was hardly in class and left all the work to the TAs who were horrid.  She was not helpful outside of class and did not have much contact with the students.  The tests were very confusing and unfair.

This lady is the devil.  I made a B+, but only because I made an A on the first test, which everyone did well on.  She then decided to make the MC tests extremely complicated and wordy.  Plus, her accent really blows.

Prof Gauthier seems like a nice lady, but her class is REALLY boring. Each class seemed like the same never-ending slide show with her narrating in a french canadian accent (that was kind of hot, i'll admit). The T.A.'s were horrible and , unfortunately, ran everything besides the lectures.

awful class, one of the worst i've taken...waste of time - classes are completely unnecessary b/c the powerpoint slides are posted online and the lectures dont contain any important info that isn't already found in the book...i'd never take this class again and i like psych. to begin with...
No Comments
No Comments

lectures are interesting, but she makes the MC tests really hard, all answers look right, she can be rather snappy if you ask her for help on something one-on-one and just refers you to a TA for the matter

intelligent and very respected in her field. the lectures are engaging and based around powerpoint, experiments, displays.careful tho cuz shes irked by the fact that vandy kids do well and wants to keep the average grade as low as possible with impossibly detailed tests and difficult thought papers.
Best teacher ever, definitely recommend! Really cares about his students and you won't meet a professor like him anywhere. He makes arabic very fun and engaging.
He is one of the best professors I've ever had. He actually cares abt you and wants you to learn Arabic and for it to be easy for you . And he is very certified and knowledgeable .

Dr. Eido is such an amazing professor. He easily connects with his students and makes class so interesting. His knowledge is so extensive and sometimes he would go into details about certain words and their backgrounds which I absolutely loved. I cannot wait to take many more classes with him.

Absolutely loved Arabic with Dr. Eido! Intermediate Arabic is very similar to elementary Arabic- online homework, several quizzes/tests, and required participation. He really wants his students to succeed. Also the most genuine professor Ive had.
Great professor who really knows his stuff, he really cares about teaching and making sure everyone knows what is going on. Also really nice and understanding. Highly recommend.

What more can we say about Baba Issam. This professor really takes great pride in the Arabic language, his Syrian heritage, and history in general. He is really going to be your Arabic father and he'll take an intimidating language and make it easy to digest. Just make sure you go over the grammar rules and vocab after class and you'll get you an A

Eido is super cool and understanding. Hell grade Hw and quizzes more leniently if he notices youre struggling, and gives pretty good feedback. Participation is really helpful and important to practice pronunciation/vocabulary. Highly recommend

Dr. Eido is an excellent professor. He makes a great effort to answer your questions if you're confused, and you can he is really passionate about Arabic. I would recommend showing up to every lecture, because you can easily fall behind.

Dr. Eido is one of the best professors you could take at Vanderbilt. Each class is fun, educational, and incredibly helpful. His grading makes sense, and he offers many opportunities for correction. He helped me learn more arabic in one semester than I thought possible. 10/10 recommend.

I learned more in one semester with him than years in Spanish. He cares about his students, is willing to work with you on due dates and test scheduling, and makes class engaging. That class is a lot of work, but if you're willing to put in the time, he will love you and you will do well. One of my favorite professors I've ever had.

Issam is the absolute greatest. He is a great professor, very understanding of his students, and, in general, enjoyable to be around. I think I probably know as much Arabic after one semester as I did in two semesters of Spanish-- and that's crazy considering it took us a couple months to even learn the Arabic alphabet. Would highly recommend.

Issam is the biggest reason behind my grasp of Arabic. He expects effort from his students - homework assignments around 3 times a week, and you need to show up to class about every day - but it is worth it. He is always helpful and presents Arabic in a way that is clear for an English speaker to understand. He is pretty funny, too.

quite possibly the best professor i have ever had in my whole life. i do not like accounting, finance, or math tbh however he made the content GENUINELY make sense & honestly interesting which balance sheets are not but somehow he made it so!!! tests are exactly what he says they will be. attendance optional but go bc it helps so much & hes funny
Professor Johnson is awesome. He is super organized and very good at teaching accounting. If you do the homework and the practice test, the exams are not bad. Great choice for accounting mod.

This guy's a beast. So straightforward, gives you a practice test that's pretty much exactly what you need for the exam. The lectures are pretty fast-paced and there's hw for each class, but as long as you don't fall behind it's fine. Material is lowk hard but perfect professor to be teaching it.

Professor Johnson is the best professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. He really cares about each of his students and understands that accounting isn't for everyone. He is patient and really wants to see his students succeed.

Dude is the GOAT. Makes accounting really interesting, and if you show up to the lectures (which are great) and do all the homeworks you'll be fine for exams. 

Sneaky lots of work for a business module, but it doesn't actually feel like a lot, which goes to show he's a great professor.

Thoroughly enjoyed how candid and honest this guy was. Smart fellow, made the concepts easy to understand and the exams were exactly as advertised (easy to study and use the practice exam for practice). No need to cheat! Awesome guy

Literally the reason I am thinking about going into accounting. He is easily the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt.
