Explains topics beautifully and gives students all the resources they need to succeed. The tests were not bad at all if you actually listen in class. He doesn't put anything on tests or homeworks that he hasn't explained in depth.
Very awesome guy and made accounting fun. Very attainable to achieve an A with extra credit and practice exams that mirrored midterm/final.
Tough material, solid lecturer, very fair grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super awesome guy, lectures are actually entertaining and you'll learn a lot from him. Accounting itself is hard and the exams are brutal. Very clear with grading and gives extra credit.
I loved the class; everyone should take this class. Still, I had to put much work and time into the content.

Professor Johnson is a great lecturer. He really takes the time to break down the material if it is needed. Exams are pretty easy to prepare for, as they are very similar to the practice exams. Very easy opportunity for extra credit. Keep up with the homeworks and do the practice exams and you should be fine.

Definitely take accounting with Professor Johnson. He is a great lecturer and breaks down the material well so you can understand. The homework assignments help you learn, and the exams are pretty easy if you study and pay attention during class. Material can be frustrating sometimes, but get over the bumps it should be fine.

this class wasn't beyond understanding from the lectures and assignments, but the tests were always stretched from the knowledge presented in class - able to get help in office hours but just had to know content backwards, forwards and upside down to do well
Personally thought he was a great teacher and taught concepts well, some friends would disagree. Grades class so that the average is a B, but many people just do the bare minimum in the class
Honestly, a pretty hard class based on three exams. A weed-out for those who are potential economics majors. Just push through it. He's very accessible during office hours.

The course material was manageable, but lectures were often disorganized and unclear, making them hard to follow. There was a disconnect between what was taught and what appeared on exams, which were challenging and included unfamiliar scenarios. Better structure and alignment would improve the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A chiller prof. Minimal work required if you are decently smart at econ. If your short on time just skip lectures, review slides and go to office hours (he is actually useful there).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stromme's class is mad chill just show up pay attention and you'll be good.

Nice guy, but the lectures moved way too fast and not a clear speaker. Your grade is mostly made up of exams, which are so much harder than the material taught in lectures and the practice exams. Even if you study to the max, don't expect to do well at all.

There is extra credit and a curve, but the class is still difficult. Professor Stromme is also not very good at explaining things and is incredibly monotone during lecture, I would stay away if you can.
Into level courses should not need to be curved this heavily. Im done.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: super boring lecture, get all the top hat points, super hard tests, bad questions on tests, if ur good at math you'll be fine, just get through the class cause ur stuck with him

Tests can be a bit tricky but for sure doable. Curve is ridiculous so dont worry about your grade too much if you got an A+ is Econ 1010 you can prolly get an A in this class with a small bit off effort. Participation mandatory but you can just do the tophats from anywhere so doesnt matter too much. Psets are easy to do as well

Lectures were mid. 80% of your class grade is tests, which were very difficult, but he curves insane. You can get F's on all exams and still end with a B in the class as long as you keep up with the psets and tophat extra credit. Not my preferred type of class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly really liked him and thought his lectures were very thorough and clear. Tests could be hard but he curves so much that it didn't even end up mattering. Tests all MCQ and attendance somewhat mandatory w/ tophats (3% of grade I think). Weekly problem sets that weren't too bad. He was forgiving too if you ever forgot to submit smth on time.

Solid lecturer and he prepares you well for the tests. Likes to challenge you on tests, but he curves a lot so in reality they are not very hard. Very funny guy, kinda has a depressed vibe. Definitely not a professor for everyone, but I really enjoyed his class.

When people say the tests are difficult in this class they mean it takes a lot of logical thinking to understand what the problems are asking. That being said he curves so much like a 70 can become an A so it doesn't really matter too much. Super great person as well
Tests are VERY VERY hard, making an intro level class extremely stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests can be difficult, but each test is curved. Very chill guy.
Tests unnecessarily hard although curved significantly still very stressful
Exams are EXTREMELY difficult, and lectures are very boring/unorganized. There is a curve, but it makes things unnecessarily stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The tests were extremely hard, and the lectures were very boring. He read of his terribly made slides, and his notes were all over the place and confusing. Impossible to study for the exams.
Test heavy class. The study materials he provided did not reflect the difficulty of the test

Genuinely such a nice person and definitely bright so I can't make this a 1, but he cannot teach big lecture classes. He doesn't make it clear what he's talking about and rushes through the slides. Assigns practice sets for hw and practices quizzes that don't reflect the actual exams (which make up 80% of your grade).

The homework is very helpful in understanding the content, but outside of that, good luck! Professor Stromme is not very good at explaining things and does not know how to lecture. The tests are way harder than they should be and are 10 times more difficult than what was taught in class, but there is a decent curve, and there is extra credit.

Dr. Stromme is a nice guy but he does not give great advice on how students could improve. I approached Stromme for advice on how to understand the material better but he could not provide any answers. The lectures are very boring and I performed better in the class when I just self-studied. For an intro class, Stromme gives the hardest questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stromme seems very knowledgeable, but if you're not an econ person, do not take him.  Students study so hard for his midterms and still struggle because there is little overlap between the examples given and his midterms. The practice exams have like nothing to do with the actual exams. Even going to office hours doesn't help.

Stromme seems like a nice enough guy, but I question his teaching abilities at times. His exams were harder than the practice he provided, and his slides were often wrong (math errors, etc). If you're good at remembering small details, you'll be fine. My advice: don't slack off just because it's intro econ; give it the time/respect it deserves.

Stromme seems like a super nice guy, I'll give him that. But his exams seemed to be unnecessarily difficult and often asked students to answer far harder questions than those provided in practice exams. Also, there were several instances where the handwritten math/work was objectively false. If you pay attention to details, you'll be fine

Such a caring professor who wants you to succeed both in his class and in life. Does a great job explaining concepts and giving examples. Makes his expectations for tests super clear and gives lots of advice on how to study. Overall, just such a great guy.

Stromme is an amazing proffesor and person. He truly cares about his students and makes his expectations very clear for test and your overall grade. Annotates slides for lectures and gives many examples to explain concepts. He even said he tries to give the maximum amount of A he his is allowed to give.
Overhyped as a professor but then again all the econ professors kinda stink. His teaching style is great for some but bad for others so good luck.

Chill class; weekly psets, 2 midterm, and a final. Each exam is around ~20 mcq and he curves generously, and also gives extra credit for attendance. His midterms are a little tricky, but he gives challenging practice exams. He also follows the textbook closely in his lectures, so I recommend buying it. Boring lectures, but I'd attend them all.

Relatively easy course, two midterms and a final. Most of the exam questions are straightforward. Lecture isn't mandatory, but he gives attendance points on TopHat. There are weekly problem sets, but they are short and TAs are helpful. Textbook is optional, but I found it helpful.

Professor Stromme is such a kind and caring professor. Go to his office hours!!! He is so supportive and is great at simplifying complex topics. To do well on tests you have to pay attention in class and make sure you don't fall too far behind, but his class is manageable and he is such a supportive professor. Definitely take 1020 with him!

Nice dude but def a disconnect between lectures/slides and test qs. Exams (3/sem) are heavily curved so its ok to walk out of the exam feeling lost. For me, concepts didn't click by attending class alone. There are weekly problem sets (hw is ~1hr/wk). Most ppl do fine cramming the night before an exam since he gives out as many As as he can

Do not take this. His course materials are not related to what's on the test and he's a bit too creative with test questions. He expects everyone to understand the concepts FULLY and don't give out enought practices

This class almost made me drop my econ minor. There was such a disconnect between the content we discussed and the exams. I ended up teaching myself the entire course. It took a lot of time outside of class to do well. His exams were unnecessarily difficult and even when you could argue you answer was correct, he would just shrug.

Strommes the boy. Hes such a gentle man he makes me warm and fuzzy inside.
Tests are hard if you dont study
Lectures are chill
there's extra credit

simply the goat. lets u out 15 mins early every class. no textbook and not mandatory participation. 3 tests and weekly problem sets make up the grade. I'm bad at econ but this was chill. W stromme so straightforward

Dr. Stromme is an underrated educator who explains concepts well. He could improve his time allocation to reviewing challenging concepts more clearly. Most complaints about him come from people who put no effort in and then expect to do well. Tests are fair with ~2 tough questions but he curves. He cares a lot and is approachable.
People need to realize that this is college—you are going to have to put in work outside of the classroom. The slides are posted, and he is always available to answer questions.
SOOOOO BORING, i never went to class cause i would just fall asleep. also uses weird sports examples on exams and that tripped me up. Thank god im not an econ major
chill class

On the lecturing side, Stromme has room for improvement, but it is clear that he cares about his students. He, especially in the intro courses, tries to set students up for success through brief conversations on college life and how to get to know professors/ his college tips. Would take it again.

I thought stromme was great. A lot of people thought he wasn't super engaging or would move too fast but he posts all his lectures and most people just sat on their phone during class and then complained about not knowing the material. I'd recommend him,

In terms of lecturing, he did a good job to present those ideas clearly but VERY BORING. But he's very sneaky in exams, he's going to ask sth you never had a chance to touch upon on and use those questions to trick you. Anything on the slides and mock exam are just for practise purposes, the real exam is much much harder, avoid him if possible
Stromme is great. He makes what can be boring material quite interesting. He's also extremely lenient with grades.
Great professor. Really good at explaining all concepts and giving examples.

This guy has no idea how to teach, but is definitely trying. He comes late to lecture and is unorganized but will help you in office hours if you go. Tests are pretty straight forward which makes up for this.

Super smart guy, but comes to class unprepared and doesn't really teach in lectures - you will get out early always, so do the readings. Homework is light but exams are rough if you don't prep beforehand or know Econ.

Prof. Stromme is super caring and accommodating. Lectures are not bad, and you can follow the content without extra work after class.  Exams are somewhat tricky, but they're mostly coming from lectures, and there will be strong curves curving your grade up at the end.
Super chill guy. Definitely was a breathe of fresh air compared to other Vandy Econ profs. He was super accessible, understanding, and really cared about his students.

John is no doubt the best econometrics prof you can get. There might be a slight learning curve at first when getting into econometrics, but once you get used to the pace of the content, then the class gets a lot more manageable. John is extremely accessible outside of class and always makes the greatest effort to help students prepare for tests.

Professor Stromme is really caring and accommodating. The class is just tough for Econ majors but he makes it really digestible. Most people struggle sitting through lecture because it is usually long, difficult proofs, but going to class and paying attention makes a big difference. He is the best (hope other Vandy professors don't ruin him lol).
Really enjoyed Professor Sauer - took his intro class and felt like he was genuinely curious in his students, always says hi or chats me still when I see him around campus almost a year later!
***Anth2101 and Anth1201****, the GOAT, cares about learning and not the grade. Everyone should take

Archaeology is a fun course. It is interesting, but rather predictable in the things you may learn. 

A textbook and workbook (for homework) are needed, and attendance is offered as extra credit towards the final. Dr. Sauer is understanding, thoughtful, and communicative, so if you have anything come up, feel free to let him know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, great stress-free class
The GOAT… enough said.

Amazing. No mandatory attendance but get extra credit on final if you go to class. Everything is open note and he is a great teacher. His lectures are interesting and the assignments are easy. Tests are open note

*Anth 2101 Easiest A of all time. Dr. Sauer cares so deeply about his students and our learning that the grade means nothing to him. He's so enthusiastic about what he does. Perfect elective if you like to learn and go to class to just sit/listen/engage and not have to worry about notes. 2 exams online open note 5 day window. Final paper 3-5 pages.

Class is super small so you have to participate, but Dr. Sauer guides the discussion and makes it easy to pay attention. All work other than the (very easy to write) paper, is group work, so one lead discussion and one final project.

Free A. The online tests are based on the lectures, but you can definitely just use the lectures he posts online. The attendance is non-mandatory and extra credit if you go. The tests can be taken in a four day window and it's online. The guy is caring guy and cares about his student's well-being.
Great guy as always. Easiest A you'll ever take, but at the same time you'll actually learn some cool stuff if you just listen in class. The world needs more Dr. Sauer

Dr. Sauer is the goat. I don't even feel the need to write more; he's so accommodating to those who can't always make class. If you do the readings and apply yourself to what you're learning on the exams, you'll get an A. Can't wait to take Dr. Sauer again, he's awesome.

Dr. Sauer is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt! He is very passionate about his work & the topics he teaches. There are two 10-page papers & you lead one class discussion over the semester. The papers arent bad: write about whatever as long as it relates to landscapes & he is flexible about grading & deadlines. Overall, highly recommend it!

Collapse and Sustainability is graded off one final paper, graded at the end. Throughout the semester, short chunks of the paper are submitted for completion grade. Attendance is extra credit and not mandatory. Highly recommend as this is a low work load class. Dr. Sauer cares about his students' well-being and is flexible with deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Core 1010 is generally a very easy class, but that doesn't mean it wasn't meaningful. Dr. Sauer did a great job with the class and my largest complaints are mainly directed towards the curriculum and not him. He leads a good discussion and was very forgiving with assignments/grading.
Love this guy!! He's super passionate about archaeology. Lectures are fairly interesting with a wide berth of content. Attendance is extra credit and exams are online and straightforward.

Professor Sauer is great. Attendance is optional but you get extra credit, so I went to most of them. He is a good lecturer and I enjoyed the content of the course. I think most people get an A, the exams are very straightforward if you go to lectures or look at the content afterwards on BrightSpace.

Professor Sauer is so easy I actually feel bad for getting an A. I kid you not I went to 4 classes. The exams are on brightspace and are very easy, your grade is 2 or 3 exams and a final. He is a really passionate professor and a gem of a human being. Attendance counts for extra credit, but he posts everything on Zoom.

Dr. Sauer is genuinely my favorite professor at Vandy. He is the most caring professor and extremely accessible to students. He is incredibly knowledgeable and a captivating lecturer. Everyone needs to take him at least once!
GOAT
A gem. Sweetest and most caring professor I've ever had. I cannot recommend taking a class with Dr. Sauer enough!

Best teacher I've ever had. Class was incredibly interested and very much discussion based. Sauer is so incredibly interesting. Also very caring and really just wants you to do well and learn. Super accommodating. Class is not a ton of work, but has its moments. Could not recommend the class more.

Dr. Sauer was amazing. He is the type of professor that genuinely wants you to 1) succeed in his class and 2) wants you to take away meaningful knowledge from his lectures. He is super caring and funny. His tests are super manageable and HW is very doable. Just make sure you stay on top of the due dates for the HWs, & refer to the syllabus.

This class was early in the morning, but Dr. Sauer's enthusiasm and kindness made me excited to come to lecture every day. All major exams are take-home and you can tell that he cares more about students being interested in the material above all else. Take anything with him for a fun, low-stress class!

Awesome prof and human being. Don't buy the textbooks as all the material for this class comes from lecture. I'd recommend attending lecture since some of his test questions won't be found elsewhere (although he does post recordings of lectures). Exams are open note, open book, and over the course of a few days. Easiest class I've taken at Vandy!

Dr. Sauer is an amazing professor who truly cares about his students. He makes sure to help us in every way: he records his lectures, advocates for rest days, and makes his tests online. He cares about us actually learning something. Grades consist of tests and a few homework assignments. Absolutely one of the best professors I have ever had.

As someone who has taken 2 classes by Professor Sauer, I have to say he is an incredible professor. He is very considerate of your time and doesn't assign busy work. His lectures are funny but filled with content, and he is a great person to take advice from. I cannot recommend Professor Sauer enough and I hope you enjoy his class as much as I did.

Professor Sauer was genuinely the friendliest and most accommodating professor I have ever had. He might have been too accommodating if that's even possible. He genuinely wants people to learn and doesn't care about heavily testing knowledge. This was a great class to take as a second-semester senior. If you want a breather, take a class with Sauer
Lectures and course contents are very interesting and Dr. Sauer himself is simply phenomenal. 3 short response papers & 3 research papers. Very fair grader. A great choice for a FYWS.

Dr. Sauer is a phenomenal professor who really cares about his students, and the class is really interesting. There are three response papers, as well as three research papers in this course, so there is a lot of writing but Sauer is a very fair grader. If you work hard and pay attention, you'll get an A. I'd recommend taking Sauer if you can.

TAKE A SAUER CLASS! He's just such a genuine guy and you can tell he really cares about his students. He did frequent check-ins in class and has pushed back deadlines when he knows everyone is stressing about another midterm. His lectures are super interesting too! Super amazing dude who's passionate about academia and archaeology.

Professor Sauer was amazing! Hands down the most inspirational and caring professor I have had at Vanderbilt. He truly wants all of his student to succeed. DO NOT pass up a chance to take any of his classes!

Sauer is super friendly & down-to-earth. Passionate about archaeology but understands that not every student in a summer course will be. Easy W course credit. There were Brightspace discussions for each lecture & 5 essays (not bad at all). I learned a lot about the field and came out with a new respect for archaeology. Take this class!!
Awesome professor who truly cares about his students and their learning. I started a minor in Anthropology just to have an excuse to take more of his classes.

The greatest professor of all time. He embodies what all good professors should aspire to be. Caring, bright, inspirational, moving, worldly, funny, professional- truly one of Vanderbilt's greatest treasures.

Professor Sauer is one of the most brilliant lecturers I ever had. He consistently was so engaged, had an incredible wealth of knowledge and was just overall likeable. Class was very participation based, and had some readings but supplemented discussion however weren't required to do well. Exams were online and open note over four days

Environmental Anthropology was one of the courses I looked forward to during the week- 2 papers and a few discussion posts and ended up with an easy A. Lectures were interesting and mostly student-led and Sauer is just an awesome person. everyone at Vanderbilt should take a class with him

Fantastic Professor. Very intelligent and personable. Interesting lore drops in class. His class has changed how I see the world.

Strongly recommend this professor! He really cares about the students and is always willing to help. Daily homework, four projects, and few grammar quizzes.

Professor Juntao is genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had. You can tell he really wants to see his students do well, which is very important when beginning a new language. I had no prior knowledge in German before and taking his really inspired me to continue taking courses at Vandy.

Prof. Li is hands-down my favorite Professor. He's so caring, engaging, organized, and always there for his students. I'd highly recommend him if you ever take a German class.

difficult to work with and passive aggressive from a lot of my interactions with her. definitely did not have the same experience as everyone else.

Malu is super interested in the subject and her class topics are extremely interesting.

Usually feels like he's compensating for things by using big words. example: "Many a neophyte researcher have the tendency to commit the grave error of..."
Almost everyone gets an A if they hand in their work.

Professor Pask is very uninvolved and doesn't seem to understand that he gives way too much work for a one-credit course. The lab directions are very convoluted and scattered all over the Brightspace page. The good news is that getting a good TA and lab partner can make this class much more bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Pask is such a sweet guy. He is the main director of 1511 labs so it is hard for him to always be around since he is in charge of so many things, and TAs are the main bay instructors. However, if you make an effort to get to know him, he is SO knowledgeable with questions and genuinely wants you to succeed. 10/10
It is hard to communicate how much a waste of time this lab is. It's incredibly time intensive for being 1 credit hour, ridiculously unclear, and flat out stupid.
Great class!
Nice guy
Super cool summer course!
You need to read

All these reviews are whiny lol. Pask is a really friendly guy and I personally really like him. Yeah, the TA you have determines your grade, but the homeworks aren't that bad. As long as you're willing to put the effort in, you'll do just fine. 1501L is definitely more boring than 1511L though. Overall could be better, but not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Pros:
- Having a generous TA can help your grade a lot.
- You often get to leave class early.

Cons:
- Unorganized/poorly worded homework.
- Little direct involvement from the professor.
- Content doesn't correspond to lecture.

Survival tips:
- Don't stress about understanding the content in lab; it's easier to learn in lecture.
- Get a good TA.

Bio Lab was a huge waste of time. Unfortunately, there's no way to avoid Dr. Pask's lab if you're taking biology, but I really wish he would put the effort in to rework the course to make it more relevant. None of the labs applied to or reinforced material covered in lecture, and labs were tedious with lots of sitting around and waiting.

This is the WORST professor I have ever had. He did not do ANYTHING the whole semester and just piddled around the lab. He did not help anyone, and his lab assignments are IMPOSSIBLE. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class made me question my sanity the night before the reports were due. The reports were overly complex with the way the questions were phrased. The labs were often frustrating and especially for the later half of labs did not even work (no result, non-analyzable results). Thankfully I got a TA that graded leniently and was accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Your grade in this class is determined solely by your TA. The homework is extremely long for a lab that only gives one credit hour. The labs itself were not that interesting, and the post-lab questions only made it less enjoyable.

The problem with this class is that there is so much work that you must do every single week. Despite this class being a 1 hour credit class, you must go to lab for 3 hours per week and spend even more hours outside of class doing work. The professor is nice but I strongly despise this class and has made me question whether I want to take Bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pask has never showed up to lab. His assignments waste so much time for an introductory lab. You can tell he copy pasted material because on Brightspace readings are in different fonts and formatting. His assignments are overly confusing. He is not even the teacher for this class whichever TA you get will be your teacher. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is well knowledgable, but the fact that he explains it SO BADLY is frustrating. He explains terms that are not well defined thinking that we know them but we are taking INTRO BIO. Needs to step back in the vocabulary sense and keep it a bit more simple. Clements on the other hand WAY better.

The formatting of the bio labs makes me want to scream. There are endless pages of irrelevant readings for labs and we had to watch a mandatory ten-minute video of Pask walking around talking about trees. If you get a good TA, you get an A. If your TA sucks....good luck.

Dr. Pask is super busy but comes out to the lab when he can. He cracks some pretty funny jokes and might seem intimidating cuz he can dunk a basketball with his height but he's really kind and genuinely cares about our experience in lab. The course seems hard because it's wordy but the answers are there. Just read the HW questions slowly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Pask... not my fav. He knows what he's talking about but he just isn't good at communicating it. There were multiple times where he refereed me to the prof that co taught summer bio to answer my questions. He's also not a real one. One time they put two correct answers on a test question, they admitted to it, and still didn't give point back

Absolutely terrible experience. I did not meet Pask once. You have to read his articles which are formatted terribly and overly-wordy and usually don't make sense at all. Useless lab. Learned close to nothing. You have to luck out with your TA. Everyone is constantly confused b/c it's a terrible lab with terrible readings.

Professor Pask himself isn't really present for anything and relies purely on undertrained TAs. The structure Pask sets up leads you to doing 2-3 hours of reading a week for a 1 credit hour intro lab. The readings are supposed to be instructional but are vague and actively avoid giving instructions. As for TAs, the one you get decides your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I never once saw Pask the entire semester. Your experience will be highly dependent on your TA, but imo they all were helpful, patient, and understanding. The course design however was a hot mess. The lab manual is actually gibberish, so half the people don't know what they're doing. Also, the lab content rarely aligns with lecture content.

I've never talked to or seen him, but the class itself takes up so much time, especially for a lab worth 1 credit hour. So much reading and disorganization that the labs just felt all over the place and it was hard to learn anything when the readings were confusing. How you do depends totally on who your TA is, but most are willing to help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. If you need bio lab for premed or something good luck. Way too much reading and busy work for a 1 hour intro lab. By the end I'd say maybe 20% of people knew what was happening, everyone else was just trying to get by.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Pask is a great guy and he does a great job organizing his students and getting them on the right track. Really easy to talk to and has the respect of faculty and students alike. Get to know him if you can because he truly is fun to be around.

Literally the worst class I have ever taken. Not even hard content, but makes you do the dumbest thing that takes hours to complete for each lab assignment due on a weekly basis. I'm a Vanderbilt student wanting to learn more about biology, not how to ctrl-F random research papers for irrelevant detail. This lab takes up more time than my bio class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The format of this class with Pask is all over the place. It is so difficult to understand and follow what the assignments want you to do. One assignment will take you several hours and will confuse and frustrate you. I am mentally exhausted after every lab and every assignment. If there is any other prof, take it with them instead.
The class has weekly assignments that must be completed as part of the class; they can be time-consuming but you can get lots of help from your TA's. Manageable.
Pask was significantly worse last semester than this semester. 1511L goes by quickly, and the tests got simpler. Tricky questions that often make no sense, but the assignments were all manageable.
He's really amazing, whenever I see him we talk about sports and what not. The assignments are pretty heavy and how you do depends on your TA, but Dr. Pask is extremely helpful via email and in lab.

I have only spoken to Dr. Pask once. It is clear that the in lab experiences take a lot of time, which is why I gave him a 2 instead of a 1. The out of lab assignments and quizzes are unreasonable and take an absurd amount of work for a one hour course. Also, how you do completely depends on what TA you get. It's not a great course.

I loved this class. It is clear a lot of work went in to making the in person labs go as smoothly as possible. Dr. Pask is more than reasonable, but if you are having issues things go better if you email before deadlines.

This class is all about setting you up for a research environment. The readings can be a bit lengthy, but I feel like I learned a lot. Dr. Pask a nice guy if you get know him even though it is hard during COVID times
A LOT more work and time spent on this 1 credit hour class than I had imagined coming into this. Your experience will probably all depend on which TA you get as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pask is an ok lab teacher. His assignments are formatted super weird and the reading get a bit confusing. He is somewhat understanding when it comes to missing lab for a valid reason. In lab he seems enthusiastic but I think its to keep the morale up because no one knows what's going on.

Your grade really depends on how nice your TA is. Pask is pretty understanding about some things but most things he is not. He is very unclear with instructions and does not seem organized. I feel like he avoided some of the emails I sent him when it came to serious or important things. This was pretty unprofessional.

Pask is a bad teacher. I literally did not learn a single thing from this class. The instructions are incredibly unclear. Things are not organized and he uses the pandemic as an excuse to make things HARDER!! He is not a forgiving teacher and should not be teaching this lab.

Not worth your time. He makes tests and assignments way harder then they should be and is unreasonable about things. If there is another professor take it with them or take it somewhere else and transfer in your credit.

While Pask isn't terrible, he isn't great. I'm not sure who writes the readings, but the readings are extremely convoluted and confusing at times. It's simple material that becomes difficult to read at times, which makes it frustrating to read. Furthermore, he can be passive aggressive at moments despite having unclear instructions.
Absolutely no care or empathy for their students regardless of what they are going through.

I've taken two courses under Dr. Pask. I can say a lot about him, but in the midst of a pandemic, when there was enough to worry about, he offered not an ounce of leniency or understanding. He's incredibly blunt and unhelpful over email, and I've seen no indication that he has any interest in developing meaningful student-mentor relationships.
He makes the tests and the tests are way too hard and annoying. Even if you read that boring material, the tests test you like you're a bio PHD for undergrad, give me a break.

Other than your effort, your grade in this lab will depend on how your TA grades your work. There are a lot of assignments and readings prior to the lab. Bi- weekly lab tests are very tricky in an annoying way. You will have to spend quite of outside time preparing for the lab tests and the labs.

Dr. Pask is great! Definitely try stopping by office hours and getting to know him, it'll soon become evident that he loves all his students and is passionate about helping undergrads explore biological research. Furthermore, the second semester of bio lab is much easier and less painful relative to the first. Look forward to it!

Dr. Pask is a total sweetheart. Sure, bio lab tests and homeworks can be tough and time-consuming, but it's an overall very positive experience. He's really caring and understanding and will do anything to make sure you get the help you need, such as help with make-ups for illness or go over your mistakes on tests. A real great guy!

Professor Pask doesn't really do anything except oversee the lab component of intro bio. He is new, so he kinda just uses what has been established (from what I heard) before. The tests are so extremely hard and are a big part of your grade, so memorize the online textbooks to prepare for them. HWs can be confusing as are the in class assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very supportive and caring. A clear step up from 1101

She is a great teacher. She is very understanding of your mistakes and helps you learn from them. She supports and encourages everyone in the class. Her projects were unique but not too hard. Definitely would recommend if you need a language credit.

She's a really pleasant person and will push you to do your best. Hardest part of the class was the in-class oral presentations. The tests and compositions were graded leniently. The atelier hw can be really time-consuming sometimes so stay on top of them. If you put in the time and effort into the class, your French will improve drastically.

Kevra is the GOAT!!!! The one difficult thing about this class was the homework was sometimes time consuming, but it was about 90% of the time it took less than 30 minutes and the other 10% took like 2 hours. Actually so kind though and a great person.

Pretty sure this is French 2201 next sem.

I really enjoyed the way she designed the curriculum to be instructed through a variety of media types. If I was curious about a specific topic, she would help me to dive deep into the topic. Just such a genuinely helpful person.
Professor Kevra was a very good professor who was very organized and clear with assignments. She really wants everyone to succeed in the class and progress in their French.

I had her for FREN 2203. A kind professor that really does want the students to improve their French ability. You should take her if you have the chance. She's very lenient on grading for in-person assignments, but tougher for assignments you do on your own time.

Four major papers and some grammar quizzes. Normally turned in two drafts and did peer reviews for the compositions. The writing is a lot of work but if you put in the effort, you'll notice an improvement in your French by the end of the semester. Understanding and granted extensions as burnout hit later on. A mix of synch and asynch classes.
The compositions matter a lot so really focus on grammar. Prof Kevra is very kind and wants you to succeed so please come to her with your questions!

Essentially, she is pretty stand off ish. When she grades, it feels like she tells you everything you did wrong, but rarely compliments you when you're right. Also, get ready to to be embarrassed because she likes to use your work as a "learning" experience so she often demonstrates your submitted assignments. I, personally, would not recommend her
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Kevra is very sweet but can come off a little standoffish at times. She is very fair in her grading and offers great comments in the first and second papers which can be resubmitted for a higher grade. Tests are very easy if you just review the notes and readings. Lectures can seem a bit trivial at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is pretty bad and rude. Also very hard with grading papers. Expects you to know everything but is not at all helpful outside of class.

(French 1111 - First Year Writing Seminar) Professor Kevra is a sweet, caring teacher who is very passionate about French culture. This course is not very difficult if you are willing to show up and pay attention, but there is also a lot to learn. Readings outside of class can be somewhat heavy, but the homework, tests and papers are not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kevra genuinely cared about improving each student's writing skills. At times, one could be swamped with assignments, but generally it was a reasonable workload. I would definitely recommend taking her class.

Dr. Kevra is really sweet and clearly cares about dance and its social implications/history. The dance workshops we did were a fun break from a day full of lectures. She really wants you to become a better writer, so the essays are not blow off assignments, sadly.

Kevra is so sweet! You do have to work really hard to get an A (which is a 95 or above). Try your best to have perfect grammar, because she marks off a lot if you don't. This was probably the most work-intensive french class I've ever taken, but I learned a ton, and the texts we read were very interesting. Study with your classmates for the tests.

Although most students find her difficult, she seems to be a pretty easy grader if you're good with grammar. I didn't do most of the reading, talked in class, crammed for tests and was fine. She's very interested in her subject matter and she's a super nice woman. Moved assignments when the class asked and occasionally brought food!
She is very nice, but very confusing when trying to explain how she wants you to write.

Kevra is a pretty decent professor. Her class is not east, and the small class size makes attendance mandatory. You have to write about 4 papers and there are several grammar tests, but if you legitimately study and try on the papers, it's not unreasonable to get an A or a B.

She's a decent professor. However, her grading on papers seemed inconsistent at best. Tests were ridiculously easy, just review the readings briefly, and you'll be fine. First half of the semester was really interesting, but the second half was dry, to say the least. The papers are the only thing you'll have to worry about in this class.
Great teacher!! Very very helpful. A little tough on grading, but definitely helps you a lot. Lots of reading, but most of it was enjoyable.
Very sweet and class is fun. I disagree with her writing style though, so I don't like the way she grades essays. Great professor though

Professor Kevra is such an understanding teacher. She really helped so much with my writing and understanding grammar. She is a fair grader for the 4 papers you have to write, however she has high expectations which will make you a better writer. The tests are pretty straight forward but make sure to study the "exceptions" from the textbook.

Great teacher!  Dr. Kevra knows her stuff and really cares about her students improving their writing. She is down to earth and willing to help.  She provides great feedback on essays which was very helpful.  However, she can be kind of a tough grader of essays though.

great professor! She 's very nice and passionate about what she teaches. She 's very down to Earth and easy going! You can tell she knows whats she's talking about! She is always willing to help if you put the work in. I would definitely recommend her:)

Very helpful professor, very well organized and put together class, very interesting subject. I highly recommend taking AMER 100W American social history through dance and I highly recommend taking classes with Professor Kevra.

Prof. Kevra is amazing! She is very enthusiastic about what she teaches and genuinely wants to help all students. Not only is her class very interesting and engaging, it also teaches strong writing skills.  Absolutely take this class; I highly recommend it!

I am not sure how she is as a French professor, but as a American Studies Professor with a class concentrated around dance, she was amazing! She was really helpful with improving your paper. And for a writing class, we only had 4 papers-1 2 pg., 2 5 pg., and 1 10 pg. !!! I would def. take her!!! And we actually go square dancing, do African dancing

Great lectures, readings, and hands-on Friday lessons. A difficult essay grader though. I worked for hours on one essay, changing and expanding upon the rough draft after a meeting with her, but I went from a B+ to an A- because it didn't have that "A spark." She was very helpful in trying to tell me how I could improve. Great teacher.

She was a very interesting writing professor. She uses many real world examples (movies, youtube, Quebecois dinner with the class), to rouse the interest of French Canadian culture. She is an amazing teacher and very helpful with writing and helps to understand the importance or rewriting.

This woman is completely useless. I was majoring in French before her; now I am quitting French. She runs class the way an elementary French grammar class is conducted, yet holds very high expectations for students despite the fact that she teaches absolutely nothing about writing. On top of that, she is insulting and elitist. Avoid at all costs!

Because of her I decided to drop my French minor.  Her class discussions were no more difficult than those I had in junior high french classes, yet she grades ridiculously harsh and tests and papers.  She's very sweet and kind, but because of her grading I would say avoid her for 201.
Did not care for the class once in it.

The best writing professor ever! Her class explores interesting aspects of food and culture. She gives pop quizzes and reading tests--do all the readings. She's very clear on instructions and reliable outside class. I recommend doing the rewriting.

Kevra is the worst teacher I have ever had at Vanderbilt. She is the first writing teacher I have ever had that offers test. The worst part of her class though is that it is about food! Who cares. We have to write 8 pages about food. Then read two other papers from people in class and write 1 page responses to what is wrong with them. Worst class.

I don't think she realizes that people take other classes other then hers. She gives out way to much reading and paper writing. She constantly gives pop quizes to punish you for one night of missed reading. She then makes you waste even more time by having to read other peoples papers and write one page papers on how to improve theirs. She sucks.

She is a very hard grader.  Not an "if you do the work, you will get a good grade" type class, but I did learn a lot and she is helpful and nice.  Everyone I knew worked very hard and spent a lot of time on the essays, and still got Bs and B+s.

Great gal, that Kevra.  Yes, she is a bit tough on the grades...but c'mon this is Vandy ya know.  She is more than fair and gives her students every opportunity to succeed.  Wish I had her every semester...
She is extremely energetic about what she teaches.

This class requires a lot of writing. The subject matter of the essays are not very hard, so you'll be fine as long as you put some effort into it. Kevra lets you revise each paper and keep the final grade, which is really nice. Kevra is sometimes a tough grader on papers, and her grading is very subjective. Tests are easy though.
she is a pretty hard grader, and her grading seems too subjective at times. she's really nice, but the grading was too hard.
she is fabulous! she had great class discussions and was a hard but fair grader. Her classes are never boring (i also had her for french 103) If you do the work you will get a good grade.
I really liked her. She gives really easy assignments each night and she really loves french. Her tests are a little harder, but not bad at all. She's very understanding and really nice.

Kevra is really nice and wants you to love French like she does, but doesnt do a good job of it. She had really odd discussions in class, and then graded really harshly on tests. Decided to drop my french minor based on this class.
A great teacher. Made me interested in taking more French classes at Vanderbilt. Extremely reasonable and works hard to keep the class interesting.
nice lady, but she only teaches by example, never by explanation, which is hard in french. tests were a lot harder than the class discussions and she is a tough grader.
I didn't really enjoy the class. The discussion in class was very elemetary and the tests were difficult.  I cant say that I took a lot of information from the course.
really easy course. she is very understanding and laid back. always have opportunities to improve our grades.

Professor Kim's course was not hard if you put in the work, his instructions were sometimes unclear, but he does want his students to do well. Much of the content in this class involve presentations and group work.
Hes literally the nicest guy in the world. Can tell he genuinely cares so much about students! He is a little hard to understand, but if you show you put in effort, you will get an a.

Professor Kim is very nice but not the clearest teacher. He is hard to understand and goes on tangents frequently. There is a lot of outside of class reading and he wants you to participate a lot. Even though there is a lot of work, none of it is that difficult, it is more just busy work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr Kim is very intelligent and loves what he does. He teaches content that he created himself, which is amazing. He also loves his students so much that he goes out of his way to ask how each person is. However, the class lectures are so disorganized that it is nearly impossible to tell what is going on. There is a lot of homework.

Professor Kim an incredibly caring and intelligent teacher. He fosters and environment where you can speak freely and often. If you are someone who enjoys thinking critically his readings are riveting. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit and as long as you show genuine effort you will get an A in this class! Would take again!

Prof Kim is a very passionate teacher but if you are looking to take an easy W class you probably shouldn't take his class. There is a lot of work in terms of presentations but it's not super writing heavy. Unfortunately, instructions are unclear most of the time and you'll have to rely on your class president who you elect to explain assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very unorganized lecture. You will read at least 4-5 books that are >100 pages long or read equally long poems. He will shift assignment deadlines randomly (in a bad way) and give group presentation projects almost every week. Syllabus for this class means nothing. Please don't take his class. Don't trust the ratings here. NOT WORTH IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is an incredible professor who has not only an incredible knowledge of the source materials but is also very caring about his students. However, this is a very heavy course load, sometimes many assignments each week. I recommend this class, but during a lighter schedule. As long as you put in work, you will get the grade you deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Great person and very knowledgeable but a ridiculous amount of assignments for a 1000 level W class. Posts confusing rubrics and difficult readings and posts assignments late the night before class expecting them to be done the next day.
Fun class, not hard to get an A if you do the reading and work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr,Kim really does care and keeps an open mind to everyone's perspectives. However, grading criteria was often unclear and he would notify us of HW assignments with pretty short turnaround. The learning curve for how he talks and comes up with ideas is insane-- first 3-6 weeks you will really struggle to understand him. It gets a little better.

I LOVE Professor Jeong-Oh Kim! He is so sweet, so smart, and truly takes an interest in his students having a good time learning the course material. I don't normally go to office hours but I typically met up with him outside of class a few times because a) he always gave constructive feedback, and b) I just wanted to spend time with him.

During the first few weeks, I had no idea what I was doing cuz the material was hard to understand. There was also a lot of homework at first, but afterwards, the class became a lot of fun with outside classes and group projects. Dr. Kim's a really lenient grader, and he offers so much extra credit too. He's also pretty funny

It's very evident that Professor Kim cares about his students very much, and I wouldn't be surprised if everyone in the class got an A. The class also really felt like a community. That being said, the amount of work assigned was way too much for this course, readings were sometimes quite difficult, and the expectations were often unclear.

Professor Kim is very caring and passionate about poetry/literature. His lectures are difficult to understand but with time you begin to understand his nuances. 2-3 writing assignments a week based on readings. If you don't like reading, this class is NOT for you, during the semester we read 5-6 books in their entirety.

Professor Kim is super nice and is not a hard grader. He wants his students to succeed and enjoy the class. However, he doesn't follow his syllabus at all and assigns so a lot read. Most of our homework assignments would be a lot of reading and 1-2 250 word responses, and he wouldn't post the assignment until the night before.

Kim is super nice and very lenient with deadlines, but his lectures are unclear to follow.  Unless you have an interest in the literary works, class is boring.  250-400 word prompts due after each reading (2-3 weekly), 2 Essays, a lots of group projects and presentations.  Take if you like to read/write, don't just take for credit

One of the most lenient and caring professors (also spontaneous at times). The readings and lectures can be difficult but he offers a lot of help outside of class. Pretty easy grader I would say, very generous with extra credit and extensions. There is quite a bit of homework but it buffers your grade. Most fun class I have taken.

This man is a gem. So kind, so caring, I truly felt like this class was a community. He is not the clearest on expectations for homework assignments and essays, but he makes up for it. He tries to make sure we have fun in the class. Sometimes a little confusing with his lectures but all in all a great professor

Though the class is reading heavy and lectures sometimes won't make sense, Dr. Kim clearly shows care for his students. very lenient grader and will reward you if you put in the effort and improve on homework and essays. Also very flexible with deadlines and willing to help students on essays. One of the best English professors at Vanderbilt!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Kim cares a lot about his students' well-being and is genuinely interested in their engagement with the course material. He provides a fun and welcoming classroom environment that makes everyone comfortable participating and sharing their ideas. One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt!

This professor is extremely confusing and frustrating. His grading scale is insanely high; in this class, a 91 is a B. Many times, his instructions simply made no sense and his grading criteria is very obscure. The workload goes far beyond what is expected for a 1000W level course. If you have the option, definitely take a different class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This guy is really confusing and his grading scale is very arbitrary. Don't take this class if you have the option.

Very lenient grader, focuses heavily on actual learning and improvement rather than difficult assignments. The lectures are challenging but interesting. He cares about all of his students and will ensure you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I literally love Professor Kim. Yea he gives a sh*t ton of work & it's sometimes hard to keep up, but he posts it all online. He's also really flexible. Easy A class, I mean he literally said "I don't believe in the grading system, i like to give my students As." And he is SO willing to meet you outside of class. Lots of extra credit opportunities.

Really nice person. He has an awful understanding of the language at a structural level. I had perfect attendance and turned in all assignments on time, but if you don't regurgitate what he says and praise every work you read in the class you won't get far. What he wants is very abstract and pointless. If you want to learn take a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is amazing! The lectures can be difficult, as theoretical English literature is not always so intuitive. But Professor Kim makes sure that he pays attention - academic and personal - to his students and really wants them to succeed! The workload is large, requiring responses several times a week. But the grading is not very harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is nice and well-intentioned. He can be hard to understand at times and his instructions are often confusing. The amount of reading per night can be high but you don't need a deep understanding for the class. For papers he won't like what you initially think and will tell you in a conference what he really wants you to write

Professor Kim definitely has high expectations of students but also really cares about them. He will meet you anytime you need and always willing to help revise on papers or give advice! Lots of homework but not unmanageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is a great professor, who always tries to engage the class on what he is lecturing on. There usually is homework every class, but it is very reasonable and he is very clear about what he expects. If you participate in class and do the work, you are able to take a lot away from this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While Professor Kim is extremely passionate about what he teaches, his unclear expectations and unorganized class structure makes you have to scramble to get work done on time. If you don't take the same stance on a topic, you will be docked points for it, so it's best to just agree with him. Also, his accent is really difficult to understand.

Dr. Kim is a very caring professor. What he wants in assignments is sometimes convoluted, but he generally rewards you if you put effort into the class. Lots of daily assignments, but not too difficult to get an A.

Please take Professor Williamson's class. It is, by far, the class I learned the most in and actually enjoyed going to class to. She is incredibly accomplished, well-respected, has a natural talent to make the lectures very engaging, and an impressive network that allowed us to meet so many interesting people. Highly recommend!

Professor Williamson genuinely wants you to learn and cares about the topics. She structures class very well and is veryyyy organized with her material. There are no "surprises" and if you stay on top of work and do what you are supposed to do, you will do very well in this course. Guest speakers are AWESOME and you learn lots from them!

Easy class overall. But do not take this class if you are not prepared to pander to her ego. She definitely has fairly clear preferences and creates a somewhat uncomfortable classroom environment with her interactions with students

Professor Williamson truly cares about her students and their learning experience both in and outside the classroom. Fun lectures, cool guest speakers, and real world learning. Can't recommend her or this course enough!

Prof. Williamson is the best! She is the most supportive professor I have had at Vanderbilt. She loves her students and wants to see everyone thrive. This class was also so interesting, and I learned so much from both the class and Professor Williamson's real business experience.

Professor Williamson is fantastic. She genuinely cares about supporting her students both inside and outside of the classroom. She's had an amazing career trajectory which makes her lectures interesting and her advice particularly helpful. This is one of the few classes I've taken that has prepared me for the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Williamson is one of the few professors at Vandy who genuinely cares about getting to know their students and wants to help them both in and out of the classroom. You have to participate, show up to class, and put effort into your work, but it is beyond worth it. The material, guest speakers, and projects are all relevant and interesting!

Amazing professor, life-long mentor and a gem of Vanderbilt's business department. Prof. Williamson has a very impressive background that actually translates into stories, life lessons, and invaluable advice. Plus, the group project is a great addition to the resume. Just show up, be proactive, and I guarantee that it will be fun and interesting.

I really enjoyed the format of this course. In the lectures, professor Williamson doesn't overestimate how much students know, and she gives students plenty of time to ask questions about concepts. While participation can be stressful for some, professor Williamson offers a multiple different ways to participate, such as anonymous TopHat polls.
Class is kind of a nightmare if you're shy because of participation grade. While she's obviously very accomplished, found her patronizing and rigid.
A bit stuffy of a classroom, a lot of the assignments are students larping around pretending to care. Very easy class to get an A on if you show up.

She's amazing and so caring! She teaches through real company cases focused on stakeholder groups and how to think about investing. The group projects are interesting and actually useful for any career, and she brings in great guest speakers. Definitely take it as a business elective.

Professor Williamson is the best professor I have taken at Vanderbilt hands down. Her class is amazing, as it combines so many tangible real world skills with business knowledge. I truly feel like I grew so much this semester due to this class. I could not recommend her more. PLEASE TAKE!!!

Professor Williamson cares a lot about her students and is a great person. There are a couple quizzes that are a little challenging, so recommend studying well for those, but besides that it is not a very demanding course load. She is a brilliant person who brings in tons of inspiring guest speakers. Highly recommend taking her class!

Super knowledgeable and clearly cares about the class and students, but the class can feel intimidating. She definitely prefers students who talk a lot, and it can impact your grade if you're not a hand raiser. Tons of group work, and her grading can sometimes be pretty harsh and hypercritical for a business elective.

Prof. Williamson deeply cares about and invests in her students, giving you every opportunity to succeed beyond her classroom. You don't need background in Family Business to gain invaluable lessons from the class. The course blends academic grounding with real-world insight from 7 highly accomplished guest speakers who you get to network with.

if you go to class and study for the quizzes its not that bad. new syllabus so changes probably coming but def was a little redundant at times. thought prof willaimson was mostly nice and understanding, has high standards for her students, but can come off a bit harsh at times. solid business class, don't know how much i would say i learned though.

This class is a super easy A but it was pretty time consuming. The whole semester is basically one big group project since she had to change the entire syllabus fall 2025 bc of Trump restrictions. 4 quizzes that you actually have to study for and a ton of group work that culminates in a final presentation. Big on attendance and laptop use in class.

A gem of a professor. Prof W. brings in amazing speakers, teaches you invaluable life skills, and is such a resource. She invests in her students. You get out what you put in for this course. Couldn't recommend more. Attendance is very mandatory, but much of the work is completion/for feedback, and the outside of class workload is light.

Professor Williamson is an extremely kind, knowledgeable, and thoughtful professor. She goes out of her way to get to know each and every one of her students on an individual basis. She leads her classes with an unbiased perspective and encourages participation of all kinds. I strongly recommend taking any of her classes.

Great vibes from Professor Williamson! Cannot stress how valuable the information I learned in this course was in my summer internship! I am eternally grateful for the professional training we got in our capstone project for this class. McKinsey has NOTHING on this class. 

She is also an executive coach outside of Vandy! Invaluable resource fs.

Best professor I've had at Vanderbilt!! Williamson is so kind and truly cares about her students. If you make the effort to ask a question, in or outside of class time, she truly cares about your interests, career, and about connecting. 

She connected me to my now-employer! So grateful for the confidence and understanding this course brought me.

Yes, both attendance and participation matter, but the claims of favoritism are entirely unfounded. If you are expecting an easy A without effort or skimming the readings, it will be obvious. She creates a safe and productive learning environment and gives constructive feedback. This course's grade is entirely comprised of your contribution/effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was not a great environment, saw some other ratings talk about her picking favorites and can absolutely confirm that it's true. She will dock your grades on arbitrary stuff if she doesn't like you & inflate them if she does. Overall just bad vibes, avoid if you can

Prof. Williamson was easily my favorite professor yet. As long as you try to engage with the material she teaches and complete your assignments, she'll be your biggest cheerleader. Don't miss any of her classes and don't be on your phone, but you honestly won't do any of these things because of how engaging she is.

Prof. Williamson's CSR class was incredibly enriching. Her dynamic teaching through application and inclusive discussions made every lecture meaningful. The consulting projects and guest speakers provided invaluable experiences. Her accessibility and passion for her students are evident; it is impossible not to feel inspired in her class.

Professor Williamson is well-connected and respected in the business world. This class is easy yet very applicable to the real world, which I liked. She cares deeply about her students, but my sense was she picked favorites despite claiming otherwise. To make a good impression on her, it's important to show up, come prepared, and participate.

THE BEST FOR THE SCIENCE/MATH CREDIT! . She made class amazing, and she cared so much about us students. The homework was all completion. You have to study a little bit, but it does not stress you out. Great to have in your schedule because it honestly is a mental break from your other classes.

Amazing. Her classes are very energetic, and she is incredibly professional. She has a very impressive educational and career backgrounds, and is always willing to help you outside of class as a mentor. If you show respect, attention and participation, she will love you and then it is almost a guaranteed A.

(Reposted her difficulty is a 2-3 not a 5)  Professor Williamson is absolutely amazing. I took two of her Special Topics classes and have learned more from her than any other class at Vanderbilt. She is always there for her students and perfectly balances structure and feedback. Take her class to have a mentor and a lifelong friend.

Professor Williamson is absolutely amazing. I took two of her Special Topics classes and have learned more from her than any other class at Vanderbilt. She is always there for her students and perfectly balances structure and feedback. Her strict requirements are because she cares. Take her class to have a mentor and a lifelong friend.

Professor Williamson is the best in the business. Plain and simple. You come to Vandy to take classes with professors like her. Makes a HUGE effort at getting her students to where they want to be. If you show up to class every day ready to work, you will have a great resource in your transition to the professional world. She is the GOAT. Brilliant

Professor Williamson is an amazing professor.  She cares about her students and is always willing to talk during office hours.  Her class is case study-based, with C-suite executives as guests.  She is always willing to explain any hard topics to completion.  She is truly one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt.

Overall, she is a very nice person, but her classroom was incredibly intimidating. She has a big ego and it is clear that a lot of people don't participate out of fear of her critical follow up questions. Going to class was a huge stress for me because of the excessive pressure that she places on her students. I wouldn't take this class again.

Williamson runs a tight ship but she prepares you for the business world and pushes you to achieve high expectations. She cares about her students, is approachable, and fosters an open classroom environment. As long as you show up prepared, don't ask stupid questions, and be a proactive problem-solver, you shouldn't have any problems getting an A.

Professor Williamson is amazing. She truly cares for her students and wants them to go into the real world prepared and ready to show up as their best selves. I don't think I have had another professor that has this thoughtfully designed their course. I couldn't recommend her enough. Lots of great guest speakers, and real world group projects.

Professor is great. Class itself is pretty interesting. I think the bigger benefit comes from the guest speakers (which are incredible) and from the semester long project you do with massive corporations which teaches you a ton. Strict attendance policy. Overall interesting and definitely would recommend.

Professor Williamson is definitely one of the best professors I've had here on campus. It's very clear that she cares about the content and about her students as well! She also brings in a number of guest speakers across the duration of the class, which makes attending class interesting, and the culminating project gives some real-world experience.

Professor Williamson is truly one of the best professors that I have had at Vanderbilt. She cares so much about her students, and it really shows. The content of Corporate Social Responsibility is extremely interesting, and all of the assignments in this class are meaningful. Everything has a purpose and there is no busy work. 10/10 recommend.

I loved this class. I'd say the only downside is that attendance is mandatory and you need to be on time. There are some incredible guest speakers (C-suite executives from places like Nike and Mars) which is super cool. Also the option to do a semester long project with a real company (mine was with Bridgestone). It was super awesome.

During my freshman year, Professor Williamson's CSR class was transformative. The real-world insights acquired through the consulting project, guest lectures from Fortune 500 executives, and her genuine mentorship have left a lasting impact on me. Recent office hours further highlighted her timeless commitment to student success. Enroll ASAP!!

I took Corporate Social Responsibility with Professor Williamson this past semester and absolutely loved it! Not only does she have am impressive resume to back her lessons, but she cares so deeply about all her students. I truly learned so much through this class that I know I will apply in my future career. Professor W is top tier at Vanderbilt!

Impressive person, and a good lecturer. However, she does have pretty clear favorites and least favorites in class. Group project grading is pretty arbitrary, and it's very clear that she has a pretty big ego. Fine class but would not want to be forced to cater to her again

Williamson is qualified and has an impressive resume. That being said, I found her patronizing and nitpicky. Participation is key, but because it's easy to tell who she likes  (and doesn't) in the class, it was hard to participate & not a place I felt emotionally safe b/c of constant passive aggression and lack of flexibility.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Williamson is AMAZING - I took CSR with her and we all got to participate in a semester long consulting internship with national companies. It was a super fulfilling learning experience and she is really dedicated to seeing her students succeed. She has a ton of knowledge in the industry and is really willing to help which I loved!!

Professor Williamson is by far the most helpful, caring professor at Vanderbilt. I have learned more from her in one semester than I have in the past three years of my Vanderbilt career. She educates you on the ins-and-outs of business that universities tend to lack to teach. Highly recommend taking this class.

Professor W is the BEST at Vanderbilt and I could not recommend her highly enough! Through CSR we heard from incredible guest speakers, worked on a consulting project with companies like the Preds, and always could meet with her for career advice, which were opportunities unmatched at Vanderbilt! Definitely take CSR and Professor W!!

Prof W cares so. much. about her students. She goes the extra mile to support them both in and out of the classroom (she gives invaluable career advice). Take any class with this incredible prof - CSR was my favorite class at Vandy. I  learned so much - awesome guest speakers, consulting project for a real company i.e. the Preds, Nash SC.

One of the best professors at Vandy. Interesting teacher, fascinating career background, and genuine care for her students. She is the only professor who has actually helped me with my career goals and invested into me.  Great class that really introduced me to new and thought provoking content.

Passionate about teaching; experienced; and engaging; she made this class worth your time & tuition money. Little assignments, quizzes, participation (20%), group project (30%). For the group project you get to pick a major company (The Predators; Tate's, etc) to do a real-life consulting project for. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Williamson is the most amazing professor. She cares deeply for her students and is a fantastic advocate for their needs and helps them develop themselves both in and outside the classroom. I loved the way she applied real world lessons and principals into the course and her passion (but also objective viewpoint) on/about the issue.
Really cool guest speakers, attendance and participation REALLY matter, very well connected and kind person who cares about her student- the class is a lot of work though. Overall, would take again.

Very easy A if you participate in class and don't do anything stupid (sleep, text). She cares a lot about attendance and punctuality. Tests are always open note and easy to ace. Group project grading can be a little subjective, but not too difficult regardless. She is very passive aggressive sometimes so make sure to get on her good side.
If you want a super strict professor, Professor Williamson is perfect. If you think you want to learn the material without all the stress, take a different professor.

Professor Williamson is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had at Vanderbilt. Not only is she an incredible instructor whose diverse teaching style keeps students engaged, but she is also an amazing human who takes a keen interest in her students. It was a privilege to be taught by her, and I would recommend her class to any student.

Participation MATTERS and she'll dock pts if you doze off a lil or are even a minute late to class. Journal entries are graded harshly so it's hard to get 100, 2 exams over the content and speakers (easy if you paid attention), one presentation (easy if you follow rubric). She is passive-aggressive sometimes. You can tell if she doesn't like you.

She is an amazing professor who goes above and beyond to help her students. Negotiation is probably the best and most useful class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. To get a good grade, you need to participate!!

Prof. Williamson is more than inspirational. She is always keen to connect with her students and has told us a lot of her stories in the business field. This class is more practical than I expected, which I really enjoy. Definitely will take her class again!
Professor Williamson really cares for her students and she brings lots of inspirational guest speakers. Just don't sleep in class :)

Great professor. Lots of learning with a sensible workload. 
Do not take if you cannot commit to attending every day without tardiness, though that may not apply to classes besides negotiations.

Absolutely awesome I think -- Professor Williamson brings so many inspirational speakers and her class is quite eye-opening to think about the future of business. 

But the classroom sucks.

Prof Williamson is very nice and accessible to students - she cares about everyone's success, not just in the classroom but career-wise as well. She has amazing connections and the class is largely made up of guest lectures and review of readings/cases. She will not like you if you refuse to participate or don't pay attention in class.
