Professor Williamson is by far the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. She cares about her students deeply, and at the end of the day, just ants you to learn. I've taken both of her classes, and have learned more from both of them than any other class at Vanderbilt. The work isn't too much, and it's all actually interesting.

Professor Williamson is hands down the best professor at Vanderbilt. She has strict attendance and participation requirements but makes her expectations clear from day 1. Professor Williamson cares deeply about the success of everyone in the class and isn't afraid to adapt her plans to incorporate students' interests. Take this class!!!

Professor Williamson's negotiation class was definitely my favorite class in the entire semester. I learned so many applicable skills and she is an amazing professor. She is always willing to give in-class and real-life advice and her experiences as a businesswoman make the class even better. I cannot recommend her enough!

LOVED Williamson as a person. Such a cool professional who has lot of very applicable experience. By far my favorite class I have taken at Vandy. Such a unique way to learn about ESG topics all of which Williamson is super knowledgeable about and presents multiple viewpoints on. She is great. You just have to do the reading and show up to do well.

My experience in Professor Williamson's class was incredibly positive, and it is a class I've learned the most from in my time at Vandy. I found the feedback and career guidance from her outside of class as the most impactful. One of the most influential professors I have met and she really made an effort to assist me along my journey!

Criteria to start the year is a little vague, but you get a clear sense of expectations through feedback on the first couple of assignments. Respect is reciprocated, and highly valued. Valuable asset outside of the classroom, want's the best for all of her students.

Super interesting class; even as a non-business major, I feel like I can now talk about CSR topics in interviews/jobs! Almost every session, we had insane guest speakers! She is a VERY successful businesswoman and knows her stuff. If you put work into your essays and participation, you'll learn a ton and your grade will reflect it. Take the class!!

Professor Williamson is amazing. (...and the one professor in the business department who doesn't mansplain and actually knows what she's talking about!) She brings in interesting guest speakers and is always willing to help students. Participation and attendance are SUPER important to her and to your grade.

This was my favorite class I've taken in three years at Vandy! Professor Williamson is genuinely one of the most caring people I've ever met and wants nothing more than for students to succeed. Her personal anecdotes are super interesting and useful. I also came away feeling so much stronger in negotiation. Not hard but learned a ton.

Corporate Social Responsibility was by far the most interesting class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Professor Williamson did an excellent job introducing us to the matter by combining amazing lectures with guest speakers, interesting readings, case studies, and group projects. I would definitely take one of her classes again.

Professor Williamson's BUSA 3105 class was one of my favorite courses! She is extremely committed to the success of each student. The coursework is very interesting, and Professor Williamson is able to connect the class material to relevant stories about her extensive experience in business and with amazing guest speakers. I definitely recommend!!

Professor Williamson and BUSA 3105 are absolutely awesome! She not only genuinely cares for the well-being and success of each of her students, but also was able to bring in tremendous speakers who furthered her lectures on the valuable skills to be a great negotiator! By far my favorite class at Vandy! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Professor Williamson is dedicated to her students success. Throughout the year we had guest speakers, CEOs and global leaders come in and talk. She helped us look inward and find what we can contribute to the world based on our passions. Professor helped us make so many awesome connections and helped us network.

Professor Williamson teaches an interesting class, but she is an unnecessarily difficult grader and is hard on her students. There is not a lot of work and most of the tests/assignments are not too difficult, but be warned, participation matters and she will find a reason to take off points.

Professor Williamson is one of the few professors at Vanderbilt that truly puts her students first. Her class is very interactive and engaging, without too much work. She is a huge asset outside of class and is definitely a great professor to have a relationship with. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, you will not regret it!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It is clear that Professor Williamson allocates 100% effort to everything she does. As a lecturer, she seeks to connect with each of her students the instant you step foot in her class, and provides high-quality lectures consisting of practical exercises and relevant guest speakers.

Loved Professor Williamsons negotiation course. It is one of the most practical learning experiences Ive ever had. Additionally, her office hours are not just for the course - she will help you prepare for actual job negotiations and networking connections. I cannot recommend her highly enough- take advantage of this amazing teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Williamson is an incredible teacher, one that genuinely cares about her students and their future. An *extremely* successful businesswomen, her negotiation class is not meant to be a textbook slog or an exercise in memorization. Rather, it is about practical skills- skills that I have used on a daily basis since her class. 10/10 course.

I absolutely loved her CSR course! She is very caring and wants all her students to succeed in the course (and professionally too, she has great advice/resources). Lectures consisted of interactive discussions on various CSR-related topics and interesting guest speakers. Highly recommend taking this class.

Show up on time and engage in the material and you will do well. Professor Williamson makes the coursework very hands on and really cares about students success. She makes herself available to answer questions / prep for exams and even offered professional development sessions throughout the semester. Recommend taking one of her courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her classes are challenging, yet very meaningful. She really engages her students and wants her students to learn practical skills for real-life negotiation. I learned so much that has become a part of my habit in my daily lives. I'd take her again, strongly recommended!

Professor Williamson is the best professor I have had at Vandy. She cares about students' success both in and out of the classroom. She is willing to meet with students to discuss the class, career paths, & more. Guest speakers are amazing. The material is real-world applicable. Easy A if you participate and do the work. Take her class!

She's the walking and talking version of cold corporate America. Her class is fairly bland although interesting, and her interactions with students are not the best to say the least. Would not recommend.

Professor Williamson is an incredibly caring and inspiring professor who empowers each of her students to optimize their personal (and professional) growth in her Corporate Social Responisibility course. Each lecture, including guest speaker visits, was informative, exciting, and highly interactive with reflective discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Williamson does a wonderful job of teaching the art of negotiation through applied practice. Her class is not meant to be difficult and everyone can get an A if they show up and put in the work. She is an established businesswoman who has real experience, so she knows what she's talking about. Great guest lectures as well. Must take.

Prof. Williamson is the best professor I've had. The material presented in her negotiation class is very interesting and the simulations she uses is a great way to learn the info. She truly cares about each of her students and is always willing to help with classwork and networking opportunities. Do not graduate without taking one of her classes!

Professor Williamson is the best. She sets clear and objective standards, and if you do the reasonable amount of work assigned you will do well and get so much out of her class. She is highly accessible during office hours and truly wants students to succeed both inside the classroom and in the business world. This class is amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Williamson is brilliant and one of the best professors I've had at Vandy. She's extremely knowledgable about the material and is a superb lecturer. She was always available to meet both during and outside of class to answer any questions or concerns. I HIGHLY recommend taking a course with her!

My class with Williamson was one of my favorite classes but she's one of my least favorite professors. Claims she encourages asking questions in class, but when someone speaks up she'll throw shade at them for "wasting class time". She made a mistake on a quiz that confused everyone and when I pointed it out she emailed me to stop talking in class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is amazing! She worked really hard to stimulate a real classroom environment even though the class was entirely online. More work than other sections of negotiation but really worth it because you learn so much applicable knowledge!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I graduated a long time ago and I just had a nightmare again about taking this guys classes in freshman year and he was chasing me around trying to draw on me with a red marker. I realized I never rated him on rate my professor. Here is my long overdue review. Do not take him. I hope he's changed but back then he was the worst
I have never stressed this much in my life and not sure why they do this to us, 50 percent of his exams are long answer and if you forgot one slide or one concept 10 points are gone just off the bat.

Professor Zwiebel has been rated very poorly in both 2201 (Cell Bio) and 1510. Coming into this semester, many of my classmates and I were worried about having him as a professor. By suprise, Prof Z has been very good (general consensus), contradicting what was previously said. Pay attention to ungraded quizzes and practice exams for his exams.

He dislikes teaching and does not like his job and makes it very clear I cannot believe he's allowed to teach if he dislikes it so much. Vandy please give this man a break he likes doing his research not teaching 18 year olds!!

Unclear slides. Doesn't cover the materials well. If unfortunately have to take him under extreme circumstances do attend the other sections as well or make a friend in there. Avoid at all cost. He kindly suggest I may go through my career with substances because I did not have a specific research focus with me when I asked him to be my advisor.

Made me cry in office hours. AT ALL COSTS DO NOT TAKE WITH THESE PROFESSORS. Grade based only on 4 exams + a final with the lowest being dropped. BE PREPARED TO FAIL. Lowest test average= 52 and highest= 63. The lecture slides are extremely dense and it is impossible to know what tiny little detail material you will be tested on from the slides.

If you need to take BSCI1510, take it with literally any other professor. All of his exam content comes from the textbook, with maybe a few things from his slides here and there. The exam averages are VERY LOW, usually around a 60, so if you feel comfortable with that, go right ahead. Overall, nice guy but a very tough grader and a very hard class.

I know someone who lost Summa Cum Laude because of his Cell Bio class, and I thought maybe I'd be up for the challenge of getting above a B in his notoriously hard class. I was MISTAKEN. Now the GPA that I toiled so hard for is ruined. Perhaps I should've spent 25 hours a week in his office and never slept if I really wanted that A so bad.

I came to Vanderbilt thinking that they would have professors of a higher quality and professors who taught better than those at other universities. Unfortunately, it appears that I was sorely mistaken. I'm glad that I will be transferring to another college to finish the rest of my undergraduate education.

His teaching does not reflect what he puts on the exams. He acts like he does not care for memorization, but will then ask specifics that are not even mentioned in the slides. Also has attitude with students for merely asking questions, not allowing for him to be approachable. The worst professor I have had in the bio department

His first year teaching this class and it's obvious that he just took the last professor's slides. Contradicts himself constantly. He says to "learn not memorize". He's lying. The only way too do well is to know everything on the slides. Even so, there were still multiple questions on his exams completely unrelated to anything we had discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Engaging lecturer; he doesn't prioritize bulk memorization and prefers a deep understanding of ideas. Exams at times have questions that are not intuitive at all, but he takes 20 mins after each exam to discuss any questions that students thought were unfair - he drops these questions and adds points to exams based on student feedback which is nice
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His tests aren't impossible by any means, but they aren't at all reflective of his presentation of the material. He seems like he genuinely just dislikes undergrads and becomes hostile out of nowhere for no real reason (i.e. yelling at students, getting offended by questions). Massive opp.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwiebel talks about something in class for literally 1 minute, has a single sentence about it in his lecture slides and writes 10-point frqs about it, plus 2-3 multiple choices. Super unpredictable exams, his lectures are fine and he's generally a funny person, but completely unfair in his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zwiebel translated from German to English means onion, which perfectly describes him. Hard, dry, and cold on the outside. Like biting into a raw onion, he is pungent, bitter, and makes you want to cry on the inside. He genuinely doesn't care about students (he says so himself), doesn't host regular office hours, and is mediocre at best at lecturing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man is NOT joking when he says he has Zoom OH bc ppl cry less (i cried after OH w him). The internet, any smart friends you've made first half of the sem, and chat will be your saviors for this portion. Ppl say he's the easier section but I was so mentally destroyed after OH with him it felt much harder for me and made me drop my bio major

Absolutely horrible professor. His first time teaching cell bio and clearly he knew nothing. Always sassy and rude to students, refuses to host regular office hours and generally hates teaching. Enjoys making students lives miserable. tests are incredibly hard and specific. Barley gives out partial credit.
Quite frankly I do not know where the few high ratings come from. Avoid him if you can. Cell bio was not taught by him last year, so take when it's not him!!!!

As a senior, I've never even imagined a professor could be horrible as this! He sees students as enemies. He takes pride in the class average for the exam being low, as if seeing us fare badly is enjoyable to him. Exams are absurd. He expects answers that he didn't even ask! With utmost sincerity, I suggest he resign from his teaching role.

Dr. Z does not care about you as a student, and he will say that to your face. His tests are significantly harder and not as fair as Graham's. Will be snarky and rude to students if they ask questions, and will randomly call people out in class for "talking" and humiliate them for no reason. Sadly, he is the only option for cell bio. Don't take.

Had him for the 2nd portion of cell bio, the most discouraging, mean, bad-temepered prof I've encountered. Unclear instructions on exams, very picky grader and tends to go on tangents in class about things that don't really matter. Gives sassy, mean remarks when students ask questions and point out unfairness. Extremely hard to approach
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever, do not even think about being honest on his exams because you will just fail everything. You NEED TO CHEAT. YOU WILL NOT SURVIVE OTHERWISE. He is not doing anything about it. Just treat AI subscriptions as your textbook cost and use it on all his exams. IF YOU DON'T PURCHASE AN AI, YOU WILL NOT DO WELL.

Dr. Zwiebel's half of the semester was significantly better than Broadie's. His quiz/exam questions made more sense and were easier to answer. The only downside is that the class is so used to cheating in Broadie's section that they continue to cheat in this half and inflate the class average.

he's knows alot and lectures well but I cannot get over the fact that he condoned cheating...like if your class has an average of 92 every test (with numerous people getting the same exact grade)you as a professor should look into why.

Worst professor I've had at Vanderbilt. 90k a year for a flipped classroom with no in-person lectures. I learned nothing from his boring videos. The exams were also take-home, so everyone cheated, and there was no curve. Therefore, you were punished for being honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwiebel's half of the course is easier than Dr. Broadie's, however, the open note exams encourages students to use ChatGPT. Those that do not cheat are punished since there is no curve due to the extremely high class averages on exams. I learned a lot from this class, but it is frustrating to receive a lower grade for choosing honesty.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zwiebel is a great lecturer and a sweet person in general. He really takes the time to help you understand the material during class. Compared to the first half with Dr. Broadie, his half has a much lighter workload and the exams are more straightforward. Definitely recommend!

Hybrid style: Prof. Zwiebel is great and funny lecturer but the recorded lectures are not as well organized. His tests are obviously not tailored to the online, open-note format given the astronomically high averages. Was frustrating seeing classmates use AI and collaborate openly at the library. Focuses on general concepts over minute detail.

Way better than Broadie. Polled us on what format of class we wanted and changed to regular lectures twice a week instead of all flipped. Good at lecturing, engaging, and his test questions are easier. Still very in-depth material for an intro class. Online, open-internet tests but probably changing to paper next year because averages were too high
avoid at all cost

I don't understand why Zwiebel has such bad ratings. He may not be the best out there, but his exams much easier than Broadie's. It also changed from a flipped lecture to a "hybrid" one for his section, which was a big improvement. As for his lecture style, it's really not bad and I like that he uses a lot of analogies to explain hard concepts.

Zwiebel is an underrated professor. Easily the best Biology professor I have had at my time at Vanderbilt. He really tries to make his lectures engaging and does a great job of explaining confusing concepts.

Very boring lectures -- he just reads off the slides and does not provide any extra information that the slides don't have. I stopped playing the audio recordings on each slide, and I got the same amount of information that I would've gotten if I spent an extra 3 mins on each slide listening to the recordings. He has easier test questions though.

I like Zwiebel a lot but I don't appreciate how everyone can just ChatGPT each question on each assessment and make >90% as it's not restricted by the professor to use AI tools. Finding out that using AI can get you good grades without studying at the END of the semester really sucks when everyone else who used ChatGPT has an A+ and you have a B.

Flipped classroom, knowledgeable as Broadie. Try to stay engaged, but I found it class easier with Zwiebel. He would try to make jokes, which was a nice contrast between Broadie. But still, the class was as difficult. Definitely come to the lecture with questions to avoid long moments of awkward silence.

I agree that Zwiebel is funny but I see reviews from 1 year ago claiming he is amazing and I don't get that. His lectures are so confusing and he talks slow and I just see students with other professors learning and understanding concepts while people in my class don't. The way his class is structured just doesn't foster learning as much as others.

Has quizzes over the entire week on Fridays. Fridays also happen to be held on Zoom. Lecture slides are very slow and he says "uh" A LOT. Slides are a little less organized than Broadie's but the content is simpler.

Similarly to Broadie, Zwiebel is knowledgeable but has trouble communicating content to students. His tests convered obscure details and expected us to make weird logic jumps. Ultimately, the class tested our ability to navigate slides and find obscure details rather than enhancing our bio knowledge. My tip is to be highly familiar with the slides.

Professor Zwiebel cares about his students and their success. He hosted review days outside of class, was available for questions over email or in person, and made fair exam/quiz questions that didn't try to trick you. Sure, he can be strict but that is overrided by now he is a nice guy and passionate biology professor.

Zweibel was the easier half of the course. Exam and quiz averages go from high 60s and low 70s to mid 80s. Zweibel's lectures are slower paced but longer than Broadie's. Zweibel definitely cares about his students, and he gives out tips on how to succeed in his section of the course. All exams are take-home and online but definitely study for exams

You will be pushed out of your comfort zone, but he is there to help you. He hosted a Q+A on his own time before every midterm/final. MUST read textbook (often test Q's will have direct wording from it) + watch lectures. Test Q's are written very clearly. It takes about 10 hr/wk to do well comfortably, (3x2hr lectures, 4 hr for reading textbook).
Learn the lectures.
Zwiebel gets a bad rep but he's really not that bad. Im doing better with Zwiebel than I did with Broadie. He's funny and as long as you watch the lectures you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is difficult but Zwiebel makes it feel a lot better. His lectures are comprehendible and quizzes/exams test less on pure memorization and more on understanding concepts which I prefer. He's also very considerate of his students and genuinely cares about us. The test average is also much higher than Broadie's were which is nice.

Professor Z was good as long as you learn the lectures. He recommends reading the textbook. The quizzes and tests are more straightforward than Broadie's. All tests are take-home, but know the material well as if you were not going to use notes on the tests.
I felt bad about his rate my professor so I thought I'd give him a good rating.

Professor Zwiebel is extremely intelligent and undoubtedly very accomplished. With that in mind, he wasn't the greatest teacher. He used recycled lectures from (I'm guessing) fall 2020 and there didn't seem to be much effort to ensure that the class was actually learning. Overall, he just didn't seem enthusiastic to be teaching us bio

I think professor Zwiebel gets more hate than he should. The class is less pure memorization than the first half, but this does mean you have to understand the concepts well. He says that you need to read the textbook, but if you review the slides enough you should be fine without it. Active recall is probably the best way to study for this course.

Even with in-person class, Zwiebel did a mostly virtual teaching format with classes being just Q&A sessions. We had to read the new textbook and listen to his pre-recorded ppt lectures. Overall it was just really difficult to learn anything for the class unless you did everything by yourself at home.

As you can see, all the ratings from Fall 2021 have been harsh. Context: we switched professors midway as did the teaching style (traditional to the flipped classroom). The flipped classroom made it much harder to stay on top of classwork and I agree it sucks. He does like it, so it might stay. IF! you were prepped for Q&A, his lectures were great.

The worst lecturer and often conveys material in a confusing manner. He does not provide background information, and often brings up terms without explaining. He listens to someplace for student learning rather than the actual students. He does not actually teach in class. I basically taught myself for his course

Genuinely one of the worst educators I've ever had. Unclear about what he wants us to know for the test and just awful at presenting information in a way that's interesting or easy to understand. It doesn't help that his lectures are so disorganized and that he often makes mistakes while talking or on the slides.
Zwiebel does not care for his students and his lectures are very disorganized. Avoid Zwiebel at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This guy is the worst professor possible. He cannot form sentences without going uh uh uh every couple words. He does not care at all about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Just not a good professor. His lectures are poorly organized and overall bad. He doesn't care about the success of his students at all. It's rather sad because the first half with Dr. Bordenstein was good, but avoid Zwiebel at all costs.
An absolute terrible professor and person
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had. Unclear in recorded lectures that are far too long but refuses to fix them or even edit out the parts where he coughs for 10 seconds straight. Makes students uncomfortable asking questions. Unclear exams, harsh grading policies with literally no partial credit. Sank my grade 8 points from the first prof. AVOID!!
He don't teach class in person and his tests are super hard. He coughs during his lecture recordings. He has 10 hours of lecture recordings per test. He is super tough. Avoid Zwiebel AT ALL COSTS.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Zwiebel gets a lot of hate but honestly his lectures were pretty easy to follow and he explained things well (maybe a few tangents), and his tests focus on you understanding the processes and concepts as opposed to Broadie's memorization heavy tests. If you pay attention in class you should be fine, he answers questions well too imo. Nice guy!

Avoid taking his class. He has absolutely no regard for his students . His lectures are terribly unorganized. He is also cold during class and outside of it. Going to his office hours is just not worth the disrespect from him. You have to read the textbook to succeed and success on his exams is hard because of how poorly written they are.

His class is a lot of work! Different from Broadie, his lectures require you to not only read the textbook but also rearrange and rework his slides because they are so disorganized. He did make an effort to improve this class by changing the testing styles. However, I would still try my best to avoid him.

He literally told the class one day that he tried to make the exam fun by making it challenging. His class is doable, but really tough. Don't cram for his class because it won't work. He puts a lot of information into one lecture, so by the time the exam comes it's a lot to study. Exams ask you to apply concepts, so you better know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer, hopefully you did well on Broadies tests so you still have a drop
reviews.rating_tags: LECTURE HEAVY--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Zwiebel is rude to students both in class and during office hours, and as such came across as very unapproachable throughout the semester. I would avoid taking him if possible.

Zwiebel does not write that much on his slides so you need to go to class to understand what will be on the tests. The tests range from really easy to absurdly difficult so be sure to know as much as you can about the course. You will learn a lot, but he is not as focused as Broadie.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Zwiebel is not at all accessible, and is often very intimidating. Asking a question takes a lot of courage because of his mannerisms. His tests are horribly structured, and draws from a small portion of the textbook. He also barely knows what he is talking about-don't expect him to be able to answer any questions. Boring lectures, horrible slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not that great of a teacher. Broadie was way better. Tests were a lot easier than Broadie's half though. Kind of mean to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is difficult, but if you show up to class, review the lecture slides for 30 min to 1 hour a day, reach out to Zwiebel if you have questions, and attend Zwiebel's weekly review sessions, you should do fine. Zwiebel is an okay lecturer, but he is willing to work with students to help them succeed. Overall, I enjoyed his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Rude. Disrespectful. No sense of organization. Horrible lectures. Makes lots of key mistakes and says wrong and contradictory things often. I personally thought Broadie's tests were easier because the frqs were directly from the lectures. His half of the final was so poorly written it was sad how little effort he puts into this class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: In my opinion, Zwiebel's lectures weren't as bad as I expected. However, he is an awfully rude person. He treats students like caged animals during exams. Moreover, his exams were unnecessarily difficult and filled with awfully worded questions and mistakes. The curve for this class is harsh. He made me hate biology. Avoid him.

Zwiebel was significantly harder to follow during his lectures than Brodie was. He can be blunt with you in office hours. His tests, while some multiple choice, were much harder to understand and to prepare for than Brodie's were.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His tests were MUCH more difficult to study for than Broadie's. None of his short answer or MC questions make grammatical sense but he refuses to provide useful answers about what his questions are even asking. Avoid at all costs. Useless, will tank your grade

Dr. Zwiebel's lecture's were not as clear as Dr. Broadie's (they switch over halfway through the semester), but his tests were much much clearer and easier to pass. Dr. Zwiebel is a very understanding, down-to-earth professor, and he is willing to go out of his way to help you understand the material.

Broadie is definitely the better half of the lecture pair, but Zwiebel isn't bad. He's not the best lecturer, but the tests are much easier than Broadie's and there are MC. His powerpoints aren't very clear and have a lot of pictures without words, so it helped to read for Zwiebel's tests, where on Broadie's I just memorized the lecture slides.

Lectures can be very long and boring but since his powerpoint slides have next to nothing on them you are forced to listen (something he tells you the first class when he also says you can't record lectures), and while he tries to be funny he is not always successful.
easy tests but this guy does not care at all about teaching and it shows. he is very paternalistic

Out of the 4 bio profs I have had so far, Zwiebel was my least favorite. His lecture slides have many pictures with few words so if you dont go to class you wont understand the slides at all. He can be rude in class and in office hours. Tests are MC and Short answer. Go over slides before class, TAKE EXCELLENT NOTES, and MEMORIZE ALL OF THE SLIDES!

Zwiebel was an okay lecturer (and it helped that I was more familiar with his material than Broadie's) but he would interrupt his lectures to call out people sleeping and wouldn't let his lectures be recorded. His tests were easier than Broadie's.

Didn't enjoy his half as much as Broadie's, mainly because he's not as clear with his lectures. Tests were harder to predict because he had mc, but overall weren't any worse than Broadies exams. Overall decent professor.

Not gonna lie, really tough class. Slightly better than the first half, but that's not saying much. Concepts can be confusing. I suggest meeting with the teacher very early just to introduce yourself for later on. Read BEFORE class. Makes things alot easier when it comes time for his god-awful tests. On the bright side he's pretty funny.

This professor ruined my first semester at college. He is extremely unclear, and his lectures are incredibly dull. He overcomplicates every subject. His tests are outrageous. You get marked wrong for writing the right answer using different words. Take another professor if at all possible! Save your sanity!!!!!

Zwiebel's half of 110A was the tougher portion for me; he reintroduced MC questions but focused on tiny details. There is supposed to be a generous curve but, as it turned out, it didn't help me. I had an 83 average after dropping a test and ended up with a B.

Zwiebel is probably the best professor I've had so far. He's extremely clear during lectures, telling you exactly what to and not to study. He's also very flexible in his office hours and responds quickly to emails. His tests are extremely fair and significantly easier than Broadie's. Take him if possible!!!

His teaching style is much more like telling a story than Broadie's scientific approach, and I don't think I liked it. He's definitely funnier and more interesting, but for Biology purposes, his methods are difficult. His part of the final was ridiculous as well, which I didn't see coming. Very nice, but very difficult.

A tad unapproachable and tests are unclear. They aren't as detailed as Broadie's but they're confusing. Zwiebel's a decent professor, but taking this section would cause you a lot of unnecessary stress. The Graham/Patton section is supposed to be easiest. And Stubbs is supposed to be extremely brilliant and straightforward. Take one of those.

He was pretty unorganized but a decent lecturer with the concepts. Pretty intimidating and can be condescending. Tests were completely random, easy MC but hard essays that were graded poorly. His half of the final was extremely difficult and a little ridiculous. Alright professor

Extremely unorganized; his slides rarely match up with what is posted online. Tests are extremely unfair and poorly written; he's usually **** when he writes them (he told us this). He goes over stuff in nauseating detail but then tests over the small parts he only spent a couple seconds on. Also, he says the word "essentially" way too much.

Awful. If I am going to spend days and days studying for your tests, I would appreciate a well written test that tests by understanding versus one while written when we was ****. If students put in the time to study so much, they expect to be properly evaluated.  I didn't even take one of his tests the material was so unorganized. I love Broadie.

Downright awful professor.  Take either of the two other sections (Graham/Patton is supposedly the best) b/c Zwiebel is not a good lecturer and gives poorly written tests that he wrote while **** (no joke...he told us this).  And this is coming from someone who got an A in his class!  I did like Broadie though for the first half.

Zwiebel is without a doubt the worst professor I have had at Vanderbilt.  His powerpoint slides are disorganized and he doesn't give a crap about teaching.  Broadie is the only reason why I'm doing well at all in the class.  And the tests have little to do with the material.  Zwiebel is just a lazy ass in general and should not be allowed to teach!

Very unorganized. He jumps around his powerpoint slides alot. Attending lecture is not necessary because his tests will be over both reading material and lecture material. Reading the book will cover everything that you missed in lecture. His MC questions are word for word from the book.
Awful professor. Awful to his students and tests are unrelated to material. Give me Broadie back!

Zwiebel is an arrogant SOB who has unclear lectures, disorganized powerpoints, and tests with very easy multiple choice questions but free response questions that have nothing to do with the class.  Don't hand in anything for a regrade either, b/c he will just take off points: The average on our test dropped from 81 to 78 after the regrade.  Avoid!

An arrogant man, who acts like his students should automatically understand the material. Difficult tests that have nothing to do with his notes, and although he says less is more for the short answers, you'll get counted off.
he mumbles constantly.  He uses way too big of words that really mean nothing at all.  Hard to understand.  Took this section cause i liked brodie.  unorganized.  Don't take him unless you have to.

interesting sounding, super unorganized lectures, very hard to get straight when studying for. decently hard tests, gave one the day after thanksgiving break. said he was going to make tests from the slides, but then said he took the test directly from the suggested exam from the textbook. lazy. hard.

He's a nice guy but he's not the best lecturer. he rambles and loves using elevated language when it doesn't make him more articulate. his tests are easy, but that only means there is practically NO CURVE. his lecture slides are ill-organized he's kind of lazy. he tends to scramble the order of stuff from the textbook
He is not a very good teacher. His lectures are rambling and he often does not know what he is talking about and makes mistakes during the lecture. His exams are not well worded but not to hard.

Excellent Professor.  Very organized and explains things well.  For those who think he's not approachable, they're mistaken! Very helpful outside of class.  He's from NY; so he has the cool NY attitude.

His lectures are interesting, and he teaches the meaterial in an effective manner. His tests can be something of a curveball. You have to be ready for any type of question. Fairly difficult, but a decent professor. Doesn't use the board enough.
Def. One of the best profs i have had at vanderbilt and has a good sense of humor,well organized good detail and gives a good basis for cell bio

His lectures are well-organized and exhaustive. They go into "nauseating detail." I liked his exams, too, because they were short answer. My only caveat with him is that he isn't very approachable because he is very curt and gets angry.
Great Lectures, Very helpful fair tests
Lectures are a waste of time. The last third of the semester I never attended, and still made an A. THe class is worthless.
When I had him for Cell Biology, he was really good and well organized.  Definately one of the better Biology/Molecular Biology profs.
great lecturer, concepts can be challenging but class is easy

amazing australian dude. open ai and open note everything with attendance quizzes (can drop 4), a midterm, and a final. lots of room for extra credit. easy to not pay attention, but course content has been super applicable to my other classes so highly recommend putting in effort. hes a joy to be around!

Incredibly nice professor. Good energy. Not the biggest fan of his lecture style which would involve like 100 slide power points with like a few lines of code on each. Random quizzes for attendance. Easy class overall.
Take Lilburn.
Easily my favorite professor. He's most energetic and funny professor there is, while being super competent and delivering engaging lectures every time. Will be taking him again for sure!

Couldn't say more good things about this professor! Extremely responsive outside the classroom and loves to make Garfield dad jokes during lectures that keep you somewhat engaged. Tons of extra credit meaning you might not even have to take the final. Makes you actually interested in coding and data science.
Cannot recommend him enough! Easy A with enough effort!

I don't have anything more to say than amazing! He's hilarious, very engaging class, so accessible and understanding outside of class. Ton of bright space quizzes but with unlimited attempts - you have to be in class to take them but you should be going to class anyways. It is a lot of content at some points but he is always helpful!

Prof. Lilburn is the best teacher I've had at Vanderbilt. He's fun, approachable, and always looking out for his students. There are weekly problem sets where AI is allowed. The take-home midterm and final are fair and also AI allowed, and his random quizzes are easy. I learned a lot and his funny backgrounds make class great. Definitely recommend

Chill prof, good lecturer overall although could present some of the material in a more structured manner (jumps around occasionally). The class is also structured in an easy manner, allowing for a lot of extra credit and 1 hw drop, with AI allowed. 1 take home midterm and 1 take home final.

Brilliant, original thinker. Passionate about teaching and understanding foreign cultures. She knows how to make people from different backgrounds share stories and truly connect, despite differences. As a non-US national myself, I appreciated her approach so much!

I looked forward to this required CORE class every day. Prof's questions and comments made me think and improve my analysis. She encouraged us all to participate. Her international background was a plus. Talking with friends in other sections made me see that the level of the prof matters in CORE.
Dr. Modena is the nicest professor ever. She cares so much about her students and always makes them laugh, which makes the class environment much more comfortable.
One of the most caring professors at Vanderbilt. Incredibly good interpersonal skills. Would highly recommend taking one of her classes.
A literal angel

Professor Modena is simply the friendliest, most caring, and most accessible professor at Vanderbilt University. She transformed the CORE required class into pretty much a debate class that involves everyones. She is quite supportive and gives great feedback, she is also very easy to reach by email or office hours where she will give immense help.
great class discussions!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's really gooooood !!!!!!! Take her classes!!
She expects consistent homework and class partecipation, but you learn a lot and the class is very engaging - recommended!

I LOVE HER. She is the sweetest lady and you just need to participate and you will do well. She speaks a lot in Italian so it can be hard to understand sometimes but she will go above and beyond to help you. She is so funny and I miss her already.
I loved this class! She's very kind and truly cares about everyone. It was also an amazing opportunity to really practice and get better at speaking in Italian.

One of the most funny and caring professors at Vanderbilt. Class wasn't super structured and we're never really aware of how we're doing because we haven't gotten any grades back, but she's super kind and flexible. Good class for the Italian minor and an interesting way to apply Italian to something outside a typical language learning class.

Pr. Letizia is passionate about the course and sets a good tone for each class. It's a small class where participation matters, and therefore it's a good chance to develop reading/speaking skills for the language. I recommend the course for Italian minors

Hilarious and amazing. Professoressa Modena is a great teacher, truly immerses you in the language and pushes you. Her classes often included lots of reading and critical thinking in addressing important social issues in Italian culture which is super interesting. Cares genuinely about her students.
Very funny. Great teacher :)

NOPE!!!!! anyone who says this class was easy is not telling you the truth. the class is unbearably boring, and i genuinely did not comprehend a single class lesson but had to go every class bc attendance SUPER mandatory. yet considering i knew less abt managing ops at the end of the course than i did before and managed a B it wasnt that bad.

Class was incredibly easy if you just pay attention. Attendance is mandatory, but you receive credit for going. Dr. Lapré is the best, he cares so much about his students. Start a conversation with him, he's a great guy!

Very engaging and really cares about the material and students. Quizzes aren't hard if you do in class work. Class is very organized and is more quantitative (use excel a lot). Topics are really interesting even if you aren't into sports

I highly recommend this class, it's fun and you learn a lot. Do not need heavy background in sports and Excel, but you mainly use Excel to complete problems. There are weekly quizzes that are take home and similar to class work. Attendance matters and helps a lot for quizzes. There is a final exam at the end.

Overall very organized class where expectations are clear. Professor clearly cares about the material and teaching it well. Just be ready class is very boring and sometimes he is not the most personable.
Very good professor. Clearly cares deeply about the subject and incorporates humor, games, and all kinds of examples into his lessons to keep it interesting and engaging.

Classes are boring and final exam is disproportionately difficult to class content. This class should not be a required business mod regardless, but since business minors have to take it, wait to take with a different professor - difficult to get an A since class is dependent on so few grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Should be loads of extra credit or something like that. quizzes very hard, one wrong and your grade tanks. chatgpt won't help you.

Lapre is a great professor and he does a great job of teaching the content in a way that is clear and understandable. Attendance is mandatory and you're not allowed to have tech in most of the classes, but he is very engaging. There are 6 quizzes and a final exam that is all multiple choice. Probably my favorite business mod I have taken so far.

Great prof, one of the better business modules. Prof breaks down the content clearly with full, printed slides. Do the practice problems before the quizzes, and those will prepare you for the final well. No tech in class, but if you spend the time listening, it makes the quizzes and such easier.
great class - if you show and do the problem sets and quizzes you should be fine - attendance does count so make sure to show up - final exam isn't bad
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was the hardest business mod for me. There's no midterm, so you have to study hard for an in-person final. The content is pretty hard and he gives weekly quizzes online (~9 questions) to check understanding. Missing a couple questions on each quiz can easily tank your grade. Attendance is required, no laptops, participation not graded tho.

Just pretty bad content and Lapre does an even worse job of conveying it in a digestible manner. Hard content so be sure to do the practice problems before attempting the quizzes which are worth a TON.

This class was surprisingly difficult and fast-paced, should be an elective instead of a fundamental course. Lapre is the best Prof to take it with, he's not the best at answering questions in class but is helpful if you reach out to him for help directly
Lapre is very nice and cares about the class. The class is just boring material so I dont see how he can do much more to make it engaging. Do well on the quizzes if counts.

Understanding of grade if you take the time to talk to him, but class was surprisingly hard. The final exam is only 20 questions with equal distribution. Homework is time-restricted and weighted for your grade. All aspects of learning in this class are graded, for better or for worse.
On time mandatory attendance was wild. 1 second late to class and the TA had to take off 50% of your participation for the day. Class was hard during lecture, but super easy when you study yourself.

He teaches well and is nice, but the grading structure does not support material. It's 5 quizzes and a test worth 80% of your grade -- all of which with few questions i.e. if you get one wrong, automatic B+. Also no partial credit on these questions and the quiz materials are distinctly harder than in-class examples.

I liked Professor Lapre and his enthusiasm, but his course was definitely one of the hardest classes I took at Vanderbilt. The content was fast paced. Additionally, the final had few questions; by merely missing one or two, I was unable to make an A. Not to mention, one of the questions was unlike any on the study guide. He is a nice man though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very well adapted to the online format. Expectations are clear and the practice problems are helpful for quizzes/exams. However, if you're not great at math, this isn't the class for you.
Online asynchronous course was very well run. Material can be hard, especially if you're bad at math, but not super hard if you stay on top of things.
I thought this was the best business module by far. Workload was pretty light, and adapted really well to the online format. Would recommend.

Professor Lapre is one of the most organized professors I've ever had. He makes it very clear what is expected at the beginning of the semester. His lectures are well organized and enjoyable to watch. The practice problems are fair and very helpful for the weekly quizzes. Would definitely recommend!

Professor Lapre is great! Managing Operations was the perfect balance of interesting, but not too hard. I felt like I learned a ton in a very short time, but Prof Lapre did not make it unnecessarily difficult. Weekly quizzes, one systems exercise, attendance, and final exam. Cool topic, great guy, good real-world applications. I really enjoyed it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very straightforward class. He's a very fun lecturer and seems to care about his students and not wasting their time with useless info. Homework is weekly quizzes, but practice problems are provided so it's not that bad. There was only one test (the final), which was similar to a practice test. Good choice for low-stress business module.

I did not think I would enjoy Managing Operations as a subject, but Lapre's enthusiasm is contagious. I ended up getting a lot out of the class. The homework quizzes take a lot of time, but they give you a good preview of what will be on the exams. He also gives you formula sheets for everything, so most of the class is just applying formulas.

Professor Lapré has more energy than most of Vanderbilt's professors combined. He is very enthusiastic and keeps the lectures entertaining. However, he moves very fast and it can be difficult to keep up. If you are interested in supply chain management or optimization, this is a very relevant course.

Although class was often a bit boring, Professor Ramey is super kind and really cares about her students. She tries hard to be engaging and doesn't assign too much homework. No exams and projects are definitely manageable and not excessively difficult.

I took this class thinking it wouldn't be stressful since it's a 1000-level: I was wrong. Ramey, while a sweet and caring person, is frustratingly disorganized & technologically inept. There was no syllabus, no clear due dates, & random assignments sprung on us at the last minute. Some concepts were interesting but overall stressful & not worth it.

Prof Ramey is the best professor at Vanderbilt! She is so kind and wants us to succeed. There is only one essay in the class and we discuss everything we need to write about. Each week there is one 250 word reflection that you pretty much get an A on. I've learned so much about Virtual Reality and its implications in the future! Taking DHUM next!
Extremely easy course, Professor Ramey was really nice, caring and helpful.

Definitely take DHUM 1100 with Ramey if you are interested in the Digital Humanities or are looking for an HCA AXLE Credit. I really enjoyed the project based learning approach that was used in the class, along with the emphasis on participation in classroom discussions. Overall, I strongly recommend. Prof Ramey is amazing!

Professor Ramey really does care about her students. I thought the class and what we learned were both very interesting, but it was a bit unorganized and pointless at times. However, the workload is very minimal, you get to learn a bunch of new and interesting software, and it is easy to get a good grade. I really liked the project-based learning.

She struggles to find ways to get the class engaged. I actually personally found the material VERY interesting, but she couldn't facilitate good class discussion or as good questions, and didn't incorporate texts into discussions enough. Also, avoided the cooler parts of DHUM for things like... tableu. Tho, readings she assigns are very interesting

Professor Ramey is an incredibly kind woman and a very easy grader. She even told us on the first day of class that she grades easily. However, I found the subject of digital humanities to be quite boring, but it didn't have to do with her teaching. I would only recommend taking this class if you are interested in DHUM. It might be better in person

This class was the best class I've taken so far at Vanderbilt. Professor Ramey is extremely kind and wants her students to learn and succeed. She is a virtual reality developer and a French professor and super interesting to listen to. She basically let us design the class and lead group discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Madame Ramey taught the first half of French 3101 for fall 2018. She was very textbook heavy (which was extremely expensive) and emphasized reading and the literature. Then there was a french revolution game that was okay. Lots of participation and constant preparation, but overall was interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Ramey is a good teacher, and she is very knowledgeable about the subject. The class is not too difficult, but she implemented a French Revolution simulation (entirely in English) with heavy writing and in-class participation that might not be suitable for some.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ramey is the absolute best! I've had her for a number of courses. She tells you exactly what is on tests, tests are not hard, and the material is super interesting. She really tries to make the material as relevant and fun as possible, and it shows. Missing class is fine as long as you have a reason.

Prof. Ramey really expects you do come to class doing your reading and participate.  If you do this, you will get higher grades.  Very clear study guides for exams, fair grading.  Great to talk to in office hours and can really help those in majorsminors and increase odds of you getting future classes you want since she is high up in the dept.

This class is a lot of work. You have to watch a movie each week and write a weekly paper on it, write two additional research papers, as well as a midterm and final. She's not a hard grader, so that makes it better. But if youre taking this class for a fun elective, then WATCH OUT. it's a lot of work, although prof ramey is very sweet and nice.

I LOVE RAMEY! she's such a great teacher and so incredibly nice...210 was a lot of work and it's a major pain to watch the films. Friday's with the TA are no fun, but Ramey's the best! (FYI-220 is way more interesting for French students than is 210)
extremely nice professor. she's very interested in the topic and it comes through in class. she's always flexible and quick to return e-mails and offer advice. very interesting topic to boot.

This professor changed how I view the world. They showed me that there's so much more to life than just living. And now I'm aware of the many struggles our genders face after centuries of patriarchy and now I feel enlightened and now I'm completely engulfed in the blissful embrace of that little light in the distance.

Dr. V is very nice and they always keep their word with regard to bringing surprises to class or making fun activities for us on particular days. They are a big fan of overwatch, which is cool because it was one of my favorite games growing up. They like to play Sigma. Other than that, Dr. V is always on top of grading and the exams are very easy.

They is one of the nicest people I have ever met! Office hours were always very fun and I felt very comfortable even though I was honestly a little afraid from their brutish appearance at first. Highly recommend!

Dr. V lets you skip their class if you aren't feeling well or just not in the mood, and I really respect that because they are committed to making you feel welcome and not forcing you to do things you don't like. I hope they teach more classes in the future!

I have nothing but good things to say about Dr. V. They is insanely nice and also added me on Clash Royale! They is at 10000 trophies which is very impressive too! Apparently all their cards are level 14 and 15 so they must've played this game a lot.

Professor Valle's class was quite easy. You give him a Pepsi, he gives you an A. Sometimes he wouldn't teach because he needed 50 Crowns on Clash Royale. He would play his screen on the projector and give us extra credit if our tips helped him win. Sometimes he would play Hollow Knight,which is by far the most boring game ever!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. V is really passionate about what they teaches. They is accessible outside of class and very passionate about feminism and women in general. I hope they gets to teach more classes in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: "Pinch poke, you owe me a coke" ahh professor

They call him

Babayaga

Dr. V is a very soft-spoken guy, and he has a very kind heart. He's very understanding and always open to feedback. Even if his lectures sometimes might be boring or if he sounds a bit monotone, his wonderful personality makes up for it all.

Dr. Vale was very open and accessible. I really enjoyed his assignments and research paper on the supernatural nature of sexuality, which required us to go out onto campus and conduct interviews. He's a very flamboyant and caring DIVA and I'm so glad I took his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr.V had it against me since the first day of lecture for 2 reasons. One is that I made a joke about women and sandwiches thinking it would be a funny Ice breaker but I was incorrect. The second reason was that we both said the same thing at the exact time and he said “jinks you owe me a soda”. I brought a him Pepsi. He likes mexican Coke :(

Dr. V was one of the nicest professors I've ever had. He was very soft-spoken and gentle and wanted us to do well. As long as you participate in class and ask questions, you will do well. Also, seek help in office hours, he gives great advice for essays and this usually translates to a good grade.

Prof. V is quite literally the best professor I've ever had. He clearly communicates his office hours and makes himself accessible outside of class. He has weekly assignments but they're so short and everyone always goes over word count anyway. Not harsh on grading and cares more about participation/effort than anything else.
He really cares about his students! He's great in office hours. He's one of my favorite profs at Vandy!

The material was very engaging and honestly the only reason the class was doable. However, he makes it clear that grades are a reflection of verbal participation. He puts students on the spot, creating an uncomfortable learning environment. He was often rude and unprofessional, yelling at students for minor issues.
He was incredibly rude to every student and would yell at people for talking to quietly and would personally attack students in class.

i had multiple courses with worsnick. he said i "act helpless to do good work". it was covid, i'd transfered, i was struggling mentally. all i did was school. i can't elaborate but things were *bad*. i got an a.

he continued to not remember me in future classes, and laughed through a retelling of the above to a class i was in.

it upsets me still.

Modern Architecture, my favorite class, showcased Worsnick's masterful grasp of architectural evolution. Lectures seamlessly intertwine broader themes, leaving you stunned in your seat after class. Weekly readings, brief quizzes, and 30 minutes of participation-based sketching and two exams make success easy and the lectures make learning easier.

I loved the class and the was largely do to worsnick! He's one of the best lecturers I've had at Vandy. Weekly workload is quite a bit and the tests aren't easy but I actually came out of this class learning something. You'll get out what you put in. It's not an easy A but if you work for it, you will get it. 100% recommend the class
DO NOT TAKE! Boring and unorganized
Super super unorganized, took forever to grade everything, quizzes twice a week. Overall boring, annoying, and so not worth all the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's super passionate about all the subject matter and very knowledgable. His office hours are limited but if you go they are very helpful. He is also the pre-architecture advisor and has been helpful in that regard as well. Probably the most knowledgable professor here about architecture as an industry. Does take a REALLY long time to grade exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Worsnick is awesome. Quite possibly the best professor I've had at Vandy. Attendance is mandatory everyday with in-class writings on Mon and quizzes on Fri, but his lectures are awesome, and I find myself excited about going to class. Cover some really cool topics, and he is very knowledgeable.

I liked the guest lectures- cool concept for the class, but some were boring asf. Worsnick has a lot of interesting things to say about all the art. Some of the discussions went over my head and I felt too dumb to actually say much. Office hrs weren't very accommodating- only once a week 8-10am and you had to schedule 24hrs in advance :(

I think Worsnick made everything sound harder than it would be. Pretty straightforward class. Guest lecturers once a week, then a discussion that followed. The semester project was fun and realistic. The tests were based on guests so just listen well to their presentations. The class itself was fine and engaging.

Prof. Worsnick is a great professor who pushes his students to go the extra mile. He is AMAZING one-on-one and helps you navigate through issues very smoothly and is just a very friendly, caring professor in general. However, his lectures can be unstructured sometimes and feedbacks can be a little harsh too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although he is a nice guy, you are penalized if you do not speak all the time in class. Sometimes interesting, but often goes off on tangents in class. I came into this class interested in architecture and left never wanting to take another architecture class. However, for a 1111 course, the course load was light compared to other 1111 courses.

I took Modern architecture, because this class previously had great reviews w another professor, and when I first checked ratemyprofessor Worsnick had good reviews so figured it would be same as before. Boy was I wrong. As someone passionate about HART, I hated how this class was taught. Worsnick also has a god complex and a big ego. Do not take!!!

Modern architecture with Worsnick was so disorganized. The lectures were boring and he would go off in tangents, and he also is very unhelpful in office hours. His grading criteria is vague too. He may be a good professor in other courses, but do not take Modern architecture with him at any cost unless you need to for some major requirement.

Professor Worsnick was passionate about all material and lead a discussion based class. I enrolled in his FYS, and it was one of my favorite courses. The lectures were loosely related to weekly reading, but often transitioned to elaborate on students interests. This Prof. made me consider a HART major and I look forward to taking his future classes

awful just awful. Most unstructured class I've ever taken. Expects you to draw every week, even though most people who took this class were not aware drawing was a requirement for it, and a good portion do not have the skills to draw. Does not answer questions directly and answers your questions with a question. Lectures are all over the place.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you enjoy listening to unstructured lectures that never cover the entirety of the material that you are still expected to know on exams and never having any content-related questions answered, take this class. As an art history major, I can tell you this is not how an art history class is done, a seminar, maybe, but not a 40 people lecture.

worst professor i have ever had. this prof thinks his class is the only thing you have to do with your life. in office hours/in class, he will never answer your questions or try to help you learn the material. he thinks he is god and demands a lot of students, and does not give any feedback/grades throughout the course.

easy grader/nice guy, but lectures are super boring. attendance in class and reading readings is mandatory, or you won't do well in class discussions. also weekly drawing assignment is a pain for non artists although it is basically a grade for effort not ability. if you are not super passionate about archicecture do not take this class for AXLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best HART professors. Passionate and always willing to talk with everybody about Arch. He could literally stare at a building and talk non-stop for half an hour. Lecture slides may be a bit disorganized in terms of chronology but I guess it's on purpose. Grading not tough. Emphasize: One of the best.

Professor Worsnick is regarded as one of the bes lecturers by the HART students. As a stem student, I don't really see it. His lectures are always rushed, poorly planned, and REALLY boring. You just stare at buildings while he talks about topics that are way too liberal arts for me, but if you're into that then you'll enjoy this class. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Worsnick's class is always enjoyable to attend! He is so knowledgeable about everything in the history of architecture, and sometimes link architectural movements with the poems and art of their contemporary. Professor Worsnick is also very caring and kind, and always willing to help. He also actively listens to the students' suggestions.

I loved having different lecturers come in each week! Worsnick knows some students took this class for AXLE credit, and he really tries to make each student engaged. You have to come to class to know the material for the tests, but you learn so much that I would highly recommend taking this class or any class with Worsnick!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hes a cool guy. He loves what he does (he changed careers because he loves art history so much!) and hes super energetic about what he does. Class is interesting, exciting, and dynamic, and he doesnt have crazy expectations for how much we should be doing outside of class. Fun to learn from. Different guest lecturing each week was fun and cool.

Really passionate about NY Architecture. Reading discussion is 20%, they get better as sem goes on. Prof. Worsnick's lectures clarify them as well. Grading standards aren't clear but he grades easy enough it doesn't matter. EC for using writing studio. No essay prompts, you have to research/decide a topic yourself. Short essay word counts are nice.

Prof. Worsnick has been super in my opinion in so many ways. Not only is he a wonderful professor in the classroom, but he's helped me a ton in my planning for grad school, choosing courses, and anything else I need. He is really accessible and is very kind and caring with his responses. He is my favorite prof by far at vandy. Definitely recommend.

Loved this class!! It wasn't what I expected it to be, but I mean that in a good way. It's clear that he loves what he's doing and it's easy to feed off his energy. Tuesdays are for lecture, Thursdays are for discussion. Had weekly reading HW accompanied by a quiz (super easy, just to check if you read), 3 papers, and a final. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super great professor - put in the effort in class and you will be just fine! Very friendly outside of class and truly wants you to learn, not just complete the course
Great professor! He makes the class so fun and is genuinely so respectful towards students. He is also a fair grader. Available to help students. Take him if you can!
He is a great professor and is very kind. He explains very well and also is very flexible to help students. I would take a class with him again!

Professor Murphy is the GOAT. He made Spanish class so enjoyable with group activities and keeping us engaged. Even with minimal Spanish experience, Spanish 1103 with Murphy should be sufficient. As long as you pay attention in class and participate, you will be fine. He is one of the best professors I've had at Vandy so far!

Professor Murphy is amazing. He teaches so engagingly and makes it easy to learn. He teaches the material so well, you just need to pay attention if you want to do well. In 1103 there are weekly quizzes, but they aren't very hard and going to office hours always helped so much before taking them if I wasn't confident. He is great! Take this class!

MY FAVORITE SPANISH TEACHER IVE EVER HAD! Such a good professor. He made the class super laidback and really just wants students to get better at Spanish, and takes the emphasis off the grade. He is a very kind grader and is super understanding in terms of needing an extension, missing class, etc.

Professor Murphy is a very good teacher. I was worried about taking a Spanish class since I don't have a lot of experience with it. However, I would highly recommend taking 1103 with Murphy even if your Spanish experience is very minimal. Do the daily and weekly hw on time, participate a lot, and try not to skip too many classes, and you'll be good
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Murphy is AMAZING! He is so incredibly kind and he makes spanish class so fun. He is very clear about what he expects from you. We have nightly homeworks online that are pretty easy and there are no exams, just some cultural assignments and a presentation recorded at the end. This is a great class to take if you need language credit!

Prof. Murphy is def one of my fav professors I've had at Vandy. I was really intimidated by taking a Spanish class because I thought I would be self-conscious about participating in a class in a second language. But it wasn't like that at all and a lot easier than I thought. He's super understanding and is really likeable.

Professor Murphy is one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. He wants students to succeed and is very accessible through emails and office hours. The class was super entertaining. He is a great option if you are looking to fulfill your AXLE credit.

Professor Murphy was fantastic. A fair grader and an excellent class overall. If you want to satisfy your Spanish language requirement, this is the class to take. I highly recommend it, and you will be happy that you took this class!!

Best prof at Vandy by far. Had him last year for 1103, and 2201 is harder but as long as you study for the tests then it is definitely achievable to get an A. Tests were fine for the most part but we go kinda fast. Murphy is the goat

If Professor Murphy taught all of the Spanish courses, I would definitely take them all. He is easily accessible outside of the classroom and is very understanding. As long as you come to class, participate, and complete the assignments online, it is difficult to not receive an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: take anything he teaches. if he taught every Spanish class here i would major

PROF MURPHY IS THE BEST PROF AT VANDY AND I WILL DIE ON THAT HILL! ALWAYS has engaging, fun lectures and is a super funny guy. Extremely understanding of what is going on in your life and truly cares about his students. Impossible to not get an A. I hadn't taken Spanish since freshman year of hs and still got an A. I love him to death pls take him

Professor Murphy cares for his students! Spanish 1101 is standardized throughout the Spanish department so you learn the same material and graded the same throughout the Spanish department. This professor is a gem! Overall, Professor Murphy is an excellent professor who cares and is accessible outside of class. Be prepares to work in groups!

Patient, caring, compassionate professor. Genuinely wants his students to succeed and tries to make learning spanish as enjoyable and un-intimidating as possible. Be sure to participate in class and actively engagedit doesn't have to be over the top, but be present in class and it should be an easy A.

I cannot say enough good things about Professor Murphy. He creates a welcoming classroom environment, which is extremely important for a language class. He does a great job engaging students and offering helpful feedback. He is always available for extra help and wants his students to succeed.
Professor Murphy is an excellent teacher. He primarily spoke Spanish in class which forced everyone to apply what they had learned.

Professor Murphy is one of the best. If you truly show effort, there is no way you get anything below an A-. The class is taught in Spanish so at first, it seems a little intimidating, but as the semester continues, it becomes a lot more manageable!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Murphy made learning Spanish super fun and straightforward. His teaching style is very engaging, and participation matters a lot. Grading is usually pretty lenient.

Professor Murphy is so kind and genuinely wants you to do well and learn in his class. Highly recommend him if you are looking at a Spanish class. 1103 is very easy if you have any experience in Spanish at all. Amazing person!

Prof Murphy is probably the best professor that I have had at Vanderbilt. He is so caring and really wants his students to succeed. You had to try to not get an A. Show up, do the work, listen to him, and you'll be fine. He was seriously so awesome. I hate Spanish but LOVED his class.

Fantastic professor - if you are looking to take a Spanish class, I would highly recommend Professor Murphy. Online class was synchronous on Tuesday and Thursday, asynchronous the rest of the week. Caring professor that you can tell truly loves to teach.
Prof. Murphy was one of my favorite professors! Gave an extremely fair amount of work and was extremely understanding. I recommend him to anyone thinking of taking Spanish!
He is great guy and the best Prof I have had

Murphy is amazing! Makes the lectures enjoyable, has a wonderful personality, and is very helpful. Workload was fairly moderate, and I felt like I learned a good amount during this class. Highly recommend!

Professor Murphy is the nicest professor Ive had. His 1103 class is taught all in Spanish, which helped with my comprehension. Youll have to tweet 2-3 times a week about a topic he chooses and write a couple papers throughout the year. There is online work, but it can be done on the one day of class each week that you wont meet for class. 10/10

First, if you are deciding between 1101 and 1103, take 1103 as you will not regret it. If you can take Murphy, do it. One of the most consistently well-liked professors at Vandy. Helps you actually learn the language, but not too difficult to get a high grade. Cares about student success. Makes you want to learn the language. Easy to understand.

Spanish 1103 is a really easy A as long as you have a decent Spanish background and participate in class. Professor Murphy is passionate about the subject and tries to always engage his students.
