You learn the material for homework and go over it in class with activities. Can be a bit boring but there's not much homework which is nice!

Wonderful professor... very kind and understanding and the class goes over a lot of material. It is only easy because he is so specific in his grading and what he is looking for- there are no tricks in his grading. Would definitely recommend even if you have poor Spanish background.
Makes Spanish fun to learn.

Professor Murphy is really caring and enthusiastic about teaching. He is nearly always smiling and genuinely wants you to succeed. There is a lot of daily homework (which isn't all that difficult) and talking in spanish in class is important.

The most caring and enthusiastic professor I ever had. He makes the class enjoyable and very possible to do well in. Tests are very easy with a little studying and he is very accommodating. Highly recommend. Definitely could have received a higher grade with more effort and proofreading.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. This class isn't a joke but it requires participation which ensures that you will understand the information. Murphy is very clear and grades quickly. There are many grades - none of which make up a majority of the course including book work, participation, short exams, video oral exams, and a 15% final.
Great attitude and creates a fun and comfortable environment. Pulled an A- pretty easily.

Pulling an A- is pretty easy, but making sure you stay above the cutoff for an A is pretty difficult. With that said, Murphy is a great professor and it's easy to pick up on what he's instructing you on. Participation also matters a lot, so make sure you're ready to talk in class. I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Simply the best.  You can tell he cares and prepares his lesson before every class.  I recommend planning your schedule around taking Murphy.  It is worth it.
GREAT PROFESSOR. just make sure you are comfortable speaking Spanish in front of the class. Also such an easy A if you have any Spanish experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Murphy is a fantastic professor.  He creates a very fun classroom environment and grades fairly.  If you put in the effort you will receive an A.

He is a great teacher and really wants his students to do well! It is clear he is passionate about the subject and cares about his students! He is super funny and kind and makes class fun!! 10/10 would recommend

He is hard and expects you to speak Spanish and conducts the class 98% in Spanish but its a Spanish class thats to be expected. He is understanding if something is happening but doesn't tolerate it becoming a habit.  Hes kind of a slow grader but all the tests and projects come back with helpful feedback. He makes Spanish fun.  Take him!
All around great professor and person. Makes the class easy to succeed in if you put in the work and is extremely helpful. He makes the class super interesting and is hilarious.
Very good and understanding teacher.

Professor Murphy is my favorite teacher at Vanderbilt so far. He is very helpful and personable. It is important to go to class and participate but he is very understanding and willing to meet with you to help. There was nightly homework and weekly projects, but the work is very manageable. If you can take a class with Professor Murphy you should!

Professor Murphy has very clear Spanish, and is not overly critical during class when students are speaking in Spanish. He is also very willing to compromise with assignments if he thinks the class isn't responding in the way he anticipated, meaning if he thinks students don't enjoy the assignment, he may consider changing it.
Prof. Murphy is great.  He is not a very tough grader and the fact that he is American makes him so much easier to understand!

Prof. Murphy cares a lot about his students. He was so understanding of my strenuous circumstances. His class was clear and a great blend of lecture and class activities. It is quite a bit of work for every class, which is 4 days a week. You learn a lot. I enjoyed his class and fully recommend it! I have no complaints whatsoever.

Professor Murphy is an awesome professor. He is very friendly, makes his expectations clear, and genuinely wants each one of his students to succeed. He speaks spanish in a way that everyone can understand. You will become a better speaker. Homework is daily, but helpful. The quizzes, essays, and tests are reasonable. Fair/Fun Class. Easy B+ or A-.
An amazing teacher! He is a very fair grader and very helpful. I don't have anything else to say, he's great!
Best Spanish teacher I have ever had. He is very nice and very friendly. Not too hard; it's easy to get an A-. It's very hard to get a flat A though.

Amazing professor who really cares for his students. Class is not that hard as long as you put effort into it and keep up with the material. Attendance is mandatory though, but it really does help and if you pay attention you will be significantly more fluent by the end of the class. There is homework on an almost daily business but its short

Class is much harder than Span 100 or 102 but Professor Murphy is wonderful. He needs to use more written examples however, instead of just letting the students talk the entire time, but then again it gets us the practice we need but sometimes some clarification with examples would be nice. He speaks spanish in a way we can understand which is nice

He actually speaks in Spanish the ENTIRE class but he does a really good job. I had never taken spanish before and i understood most of what he was saying. He's not a very easy grader but a very nice person. I would recommend him.

Prof Murphy was one of the nicest, most genuine professors I've had at Vanderbilt thus far. He's super reasonable when it comes to workload and is always willing to work with you if you have a probm or need to tun something in late. You can miss 5 classes with no penalty as well.

Best Spanish teacher I've ever had. Unfailingly clear, really wants you to understand and participate. Tough but very fair grader, wants you to put in the work and rewards you when you do. The class itself can be boring and repetitive but he obviously tries to keep your interest. Plus he's incredibly hot and a really nice, genuine guy.
HES THE MAN!... enough said.

He gets across the meanings of the word really well considering you only use Spanish in class. It's tons of fun and requires some participation, but you don't really mind. He makes the tests gradually harder, so it's pretty easy to keep your grades up! He's great, take him!

Professor Murphy is a wonderful teacher! He is kind, helpful, and patient. Willing to answer questions. Fair grader. Class is fun; I laughed almost every lecture. He uses visual and audio teaching tools. The class is entirely in Spanish, but he uses inflections and gestures to help everyone understand. TAKE HIM!!

Prof. Murphy is a great professor. He engages you in class and makes it easy for you to participate and feel comfortable even if spanish is not a strength of yours.  His activities may seem a little awkward at first but they really help you remember the material in the long run and thats the important part. TAKE PROF. MURPHY!

VERY active and interesting, often using humor and pictures to convey his messages.  I had little interest in Spanish prior to this class, however he presented the material in a very engaging and applicable way.  The class is taught in Spanish, but he is very clear. BEST! hands down.

My favorite professor this semester by far. This is a class I was least looking forward to taking and he single-handedly made it my favorite class. Just a great all-around teacher with a great personality.

Great professor! He's really helpful. He makes class fun and jokes around with the students in Spanish. I was dreading the language requirement, but it ended up being one of my favorite classes of the semester. You learn a lot, and class participation is really important, but he does it in an non-intimidating way. Take it with him if you can!
Highly recommended. He goes out of his way to try and make class more interesting. Always friendly, understanding, and encouraging.

Murphy is amazing!He doesn't intimidate the class with an "all in Spanish" lesson.He really wants his students to learn so he doesn't focus on picky grading with oral,written,&free write tests.He makes class fun&speaks in English from time to time to make sure everyone comprehends his lessons. Just make sure you study a bit. You can;t go wrong.
Such a great teacher. he is very helpful and funny. The class went by quickly and it was easy to participate
i love prof murphy, he is def an incredible teacher with a lot of enthusiasm for a language that could be taught very dully- he knows how to interest the class and teach what needs to be taught.
even though i've never taken spanish before, he teaches the class entirely in spanish, but it is completely comprehensible - i loooove his teaching style and his class.

He's one of the best Spanish teachers I've had, take him if you can, it's so easy to understand him and to get used to him speaking Spanish all the time. It was quite an enjoyable class and very structured.
this guy is one of the best teacher's ive had. easy (A-, no effort), fair, likes participation a lot and gives many opportunities for it. easily understandable. very nice guy.

Great guy and teacher. I was horrible at Spanish, but that wasn't his fault. I ended up doing OK even though the subject didn't interest me. If you are going to take Spanish, take Murphy. He is the best the department has to offer.
great teacher!  willing to help...very clear about what he wants...participation and attendence is important.  its great to have a spanish teacher without a confusing accent!
Professor Murphy is an awesome professor. He is easy to understand and he can teach the material very well. I recommend taking his class if possible.
Great teacher very helpful and open to questions
He's a great teacher. He doesn't have a confusing accent so its easy to understand him, but that does not mean you don't learn as much. Great class.
Nice guy. Good at explaining the various topics covered. Participation will help you, as will good attendance.
I love this guy! He really likes participation, so start volunteering from the beginning. He's so easygoing and really a fair teacher who's so nice and never condescending.
Very helpful and keeps class fun. Take him if you can.
Easy class, nice guy, very fair
Awesome professor. Nice Prof. Make sure to attend class and participate. Very helpful.

For FREN 1102. Very engaging class with very helpful teaching style. Always encourages trying to pronounce new words & getting comfortable speaking, which I think is the most important part of a language class for learning the language. Clearly very caring about her students' learning, would take again if I take another French course.

Prof. Porter is very kind and encouraging! If you engage in the class it's very fun and feels more like a conversation than lecture. Make sure to stay on top of the homeworks. Very welcoming professor!

The course can feel somewhat disorganized, and the assignments are sometimes unclear. There are multiple group projects. It is somewhat more demanding than other French classes at Vanderbilt, but most students will still likely get an A.

Unfortunately, I was unable to experience a full semester with Professor Porter since she had to stop teaching my section due to personal reasons. But in the time I was able to spend with her, she was a very effective teacher in a tough but fair way. I hope things go well for her

I would recommend having some sort of background in french to take this course. She was absolutely great and it was such a joy to attend her class. There is a lot of busy work and random assignments but she is a very fair grader and always gave me extensions when I asked.

Top French Professor at Vanderbilt! She goes above and beyond just explaining the material, ensuring each student feels comfortable in her class and confident in their abilities to communicate in French. She truly cares for her students, is very accessible for outside help, and gets to know her students individually. You will learn so much!!

Professor Porter is the best! She's extremely kind, passionate, and understanding. I had a great time taking this class and learned a lot. The content is pretty straightforward and easy to follow. She is also super flexible with assignments if you find that you need extra time due to an illness or other circumstance. Def recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would recommend Prof Porter to anyone looking to take a French class! She cares deeply about her students, is extremely kind, is very accessible by email to answer questions, and is responsive to student feedback and needs. I found the material of this class to be very interesting and Prof Porter taught the material very effectively.

Professor Porter is really cool and she is always willing to help students. She is very understanding, but the class itself an be annoying because a lot of the times the mindtap doesn't line up with that we are doing in class but that's true of every beginning language course at Vandy.

Professor Porter is the kindest, funniest professor you will ever have. She made going to class fun because she always brought the mood up. She has a lot of group assignments that have to be done outside of class, but she makes it easy for everyone to get to know each other in the class.

Mdme Porter is a great professor, but this class was definitely a little difficult. There are 3-4 papers that you write before class and then rewrite (from memory) during class time. I would say she was a somewhat tough grader for the writing assignments. Overall I would reccomend her as a professor

I ADORE Professor Porter, this was my second semester with her! A couple of times assignment criteria were a little unclear, but just because I'm overly anxious about specifics. Prof. is SUPER responsive to questions and def shows she cares! My French skills and confidence in speaking have grown so much. This class was so fun, definitely recommend!

Professor Porter is awesome. She is very kind and wants you to learn. She is receptive to feedback, so definitely bring up any questions/concerns you may have. Also, she is willing to help you find internships abroad.

Mme Porter is one of the sweetest professors I've had at Vanderbilt. The class is based on a lot of group work, and it's typically smaller in size so there's a lot of opportunities to ask questions and she is very helpful. She also offers many opportunities to improve work. Great to talk to outside of class as well, very clear that she cares !!

Professor Porter is amazing!!! This was my second class with her, and I learned so much. Professor Porter always wants to give her students as many opportunities as possible, and makes the course so engaging and fun. Definitely take a class with Professor Porter!!!!
She is really nice but be ready to do a lot of ready and group projects but she is very flexible in terms of assignments and quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she grades harshly, really nice though, and tons of textbook homework every class. I learned stuff but overall not worth it.v
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Porter was a pleasure to work with, and made very clear to students that her priority was our wellbeing. She had very clear expectations and consistently reinforced her availability to clarify anything we might have questions about. Could not recommend this course/ any course taught by her more!

This class had really unclear grading criteria, but the concepts are interesting. There were lots of group projects that were hard to coordinate. There was also a ten-page research paper that was a significant part of the grade. Good class, but more difficult elective than many of the French options

Is incredibly unclear with her directions. Assigns countless group projects and lengthy homework assignments, albeit with directions that are at times incoherent. Doesn't help that she won't respond to your emails for about 48 hours at best. She's nice but has no concept of time, and thinks she doesn't assign much HW when it can be 4-5 hours

Slams you with homework. Realistically, it's not hard to pull out an A-, but also there truly is about 2 hours of painful busy work and group projects that she will spring on you at the last second per night. Doesn't really understand how long things will take to do. That said, she's very nice and understanding. But it's a painful class.

TONS of group projects/presentations that aren't worth much points wise but are a pain to coordinate. Not a really work-heavy class but she's so all over the place and doesn't know how much time certain projects will take so sometimes you'll go a week without doing things and then sometimes youll spend 2 hrs on french a night. Smart and knows a lot

Great class. The subject matter was very interesting and applicable. Get to take a final test to certify you to work in French corporations. The class is very laid back and she is a very understanding and flexible teacher. Brings her dog and food to class sometimes. Lots of petty assignments/busy work at times but overall great teacher and class.

Dieu-Porter is a great professor who made me really enjoy Advanced Conversational French. The class is very fun to be a part of because she incorporates a lot of different types of activities such as you tube videos, online articles, textbook work, short presentations, and group oral exams. Overall I loved the course and it wasn't too hard as well.

Mme Dieu-Porter was a good professor. Exams weren't too tricky as long as you prepared the way she told you to. Class was interesting and she used a variety of activities (YouTube videos, online games, textbook exercises) to keep the class engaged. She does not stick to her syllabus whatsoever and sometimes dumps homework on you at the last minute.
Mme Porter is very nice and caring, but sometimes a little vague on what she expects from you. The class was fun and interesting, and the workload was light but sporadic.
A WONDERFUL professor with a sincere interest in her subject and her students. I thoroughly enjoyed her class and getting to know her.

Professor Porter is a cool person but only a decent teacher. Class is very much based on movies and the idea of identity. You have to watch a movie outside of class about every other week and then you'll have lots of class discussion, and relatively easy quizzes on them. Many short papers assigned. Lots of busy work but not a hard class overall

Very interesting and engaging professor. Fun and easy to talk to. I took her for French Conversation and Medical French and loved both of the classes. Contrary to what other people have said, I didn't find her that difficult of a grader...

Very kind and fun professor, but very picky with grammar. Does not grade very easily on papers, and there are lots of them. Four compositions, about weekly journals.  She assigns a lot of grammar homework that gets tedious and the tests can be challenging but overall I learned a lot.

Really nice professor, gives a lot of homework.  The homework's not too hard, but it's pretty tedious.  She grades papers kind of hard, but tests and quizzes aren't bad at all. I would take her class again

This class is challenging but Prof Porter is a nice and interesting teacher. Study a lot for the tests. Don't take this class unless you are very comfortable with french (I recommend not until after you've studied abroad). Best for people who are MHS/pre-med.

She's really fun in class, but a picky grader. She catches vocab and grammar errors thoroughly, so your grades might be a little lower than expected, but she's a fun professor and so is the class. She's also very understanding when it comes to other conflicts.

Nice as far as teachers go and easy to get along with. Although department attendance policies are somewhat strict, she'll let you get away with skipping quizzes, oral exams and class if you talk to her. However, don't let her friendly demeanor fool you - she's somewhat a hard grader and you'll almost certainly get half a grade lower than expected.

Porter is an awesome professor! Her class may be challenging but if you keep up with the homework and class participation, an A- shouldn't be difficult to get. It might seem like she gives too much extra work, but in the end it all pays off. I learned more in her class than I did after 4 years of high school french.
Gives too much work.

I had this professor for several classes between 01 and 05.  She ended up being my advisor because I loved her so much.  The "French for Business" class has come in handy in the real-world as I now work and live in Paris.  This professor is amazing.  You will LOVE her.

I love her....at first I was a little worried...STUDY for the vocab tests...some movies are good, others are...interesting...use language correcteur in Language Lab for cahiers...tests are easy if you're comfortable with your group members...
FANTASTIC teacher!! Don't expect to get an A, but expect to enjoy the class.  She always keeps things interesting and fun :)

Be ready to work in this class.  She will give you lots of work, but just know that it serves a purpose.  She is a good teacher (theres a reason why she was voted best teacher in A&S), and she will be very helpful inside and outside of class.  Take this class if you're at all interested in the business side of French.  It's worth it.

Intelligent conversation. Controversial issues discussed in her class. Obviously, she is the best. Too bad other professors do not learn from her! She is so helpful and my oral skills really improved. I should add that there is a lot of work though which is ok because the results show.

Great professor! the class was not as hard as i thought it would be. just speak a lot in class and youll be fine. besides the films we have to watch, there's not a ton of work and she's a very fair grader.

She's friendly and courteous, and I learned a lot. However, this was the most frustrating class I've had so far at Vandy, as you have to be superhuman to make an A. If you are at all concerned about making the Dean's List, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. The grades don't reflect effort.
A challenging course, but she does her best to help and too make things clear.

Her nickname is  la deisse  (the godess) for a reason, and not just because her maiden name was Dieu.  She's fun, laid-back, and uses lots of movies to keep the french conversation flowing. One warning: near fluency required to get an A.
such a good teacher!  funny too!  and its so cute when she tries to speak english.  she is very trendy and young and likes to gossip with the class.
Very in-depth and thorough lectures. The only issue is that tests aren't graded super clearly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love this professor, I highly highly recommend taking this class because she is absolutely brilliant and will change the way you view politics and give you an incredible base understanding of a lot of the theories. She is very caring, wants you to improve and is very helpful in office hours. Incredible lecturer, take a class with Dr. McMurry

She's very kind and wants to see you learn and succeed. Her lectures are very straight-up and she tells us what we need to know if you pay attention in lectures. She is very incredibly particular with grading, so make sure you know what her expectations are. 1101 is a great way to dip your toe into the world of political science.

McMurry is an ideal professor. She is incredibly passionate about the course material and gives an insane amount of detailed feedback for a class of 70. She also gives tons of extra credit and makes so much time to meet with students during office hours and not. Truly an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: takes off point for literally the smallest things, and doesn't give good feedback

Professor McMurry is one of the brightest faculty on this campus and this was proven through her teaching style. The class is reading heavy. Otherwise, each lecture was easy to understand and discussion-based, a nice change from all my STEM classes. Grading is a little harsh but easy to get used to. Exams are written. Cheat sheets are allowed.

She's really smart and passionate about her work, however, she grades exceptionally hard considering its an introductory course. Will mark you down for the smallest detail. Heavy readings for every class. One group project, a midterm, map quizzes, and a final. Does give a good amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super late review - She really is one of the most intelligent professors I have met at Vanderbilt. She has sooo much knowledge, and the material was interesting.

As an intro class, I think this class was a little too heavy in terms of being challenging. She is very nice and very understanding. Attendance is not mandatory but she offers map quizzes and if you label a certain number of countries correctly you can save up extra credit points to use towards test grades. I would 100% take her class again!

One of the best professors and courses I've taken at Vanderbilt. Super important to do the readings and go to the lectures/discussions but they are so worth it. She's really engaging and made the class so enjoyable. She is very accessible outside of class and clearly cares a lot about her students
Great professor, but little guidance on how grading works.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ross is overall a solid professor. He challenges you to critique your own ideas in discussion which shows that he actually does care about making you learn. Its important to note though that this class is less about learning about the anthropology of different world religions, but more the theory of why religion exists in the first place.

Great scuba diving instructor, not great with organization and classroom management. Honduras was amazing, and some discussions were fascinating, but hit-or-miss with discussions and lectures. If you like structure, organization, and not ok with dry days of learning, then wouldn't recommend. Easy A and great scuba, but that's Utila more than Ross.

You will read a LOT, and Norbert is not great at organization, but genuinely I've never met a smarter person, and he's funny! Just show up to class with an idea of what the readings are about. I don't agree with others re: belittling, he's nice he just corrects people when they're wrong.

Probably don't take this class if you're not a talker.
Please take literally ANY of other anthropology professor. Its pretty clear that he does not care , belittles students  and unclear directions for assignments.

Incredibly disorganized and unclear. Belittles often. Selects favorites. TA was perhaps the worst I have ever had at Vandy. Frankly, prof and TA was unqualified to teach this course. Very misleading and turned into a social justice warrior fest with everyone trying to be more politically correct than the other. Worst class I ever took at Vandy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was our Maymester in Honduras. It was a great time. We were slumming the first week, but future classes will be staying in a hotel the entire time. He gives A's to everyone in the class and it's a once in a lifetime experience. Let's just say that organization isn't Norbert's strength, though.

Overall nice guy, super laid back class. Literally just a single 6-page paper the entire semester. Only downside is 40-70 pages of reading per class (but you can skim). Attendance makes or breaks your grade. Overall, he's willing to help you succeed as long as you participate and engage in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is AWESOME. I've never been interested in religion before but this class was super interesting and engaging! Dr. Ross really cares about his students and wants them to succeed, and his lectures are very engaging. It is a pretty good deal of reading and writing but worth it (TA graded really easily). Participation is key. TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really interesting material and the class actually introduced me to a lot of ideas. Not well executed logistically, though. Dozens of required books and articles, many of which he doesn't post and you can't access online. Doesn't really respond to emails either, but engaging in class. Pretty easy grader but be ready to read 120 pages+ per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: really awesome guy who just cares about your learning. he really emphasizes the importance of discussion so if you do the reading and contribute, you make his life (and therefore your life) easier. overall really smart caring guy - would 100% recommend just be prepared to read a decent bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is a lot of reading but is very if you enjoy the content area or just want to question life. Participation is key and there are only a few graded assignments. Prof. cares about students and will gladly take any questions or continue discussions outside of class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you do most of the readings and come to class with questions, you'll be golden. There were maybe four graded assignments the whole semester, and they were really just opinion pieces on what we discussed in class. Participation is expected and graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: an amazing once-in-a-lifetime experience, there's nothing like getting scuba certified for a class grade. learned a lot about ecology and history w/o tests and quizzess, only one project great if looking for one of the cheaper maymesters and you probably won't want to leave Utila once you're there
Good guy, great guy, better class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Learning comes first for Norbert. If it is the same with you, you'll be just fine. The topic itself was confusing -contemporary middle east and kurdistan, but he broke it down ver well.  However, the assignments were a bit vague which became stressful at times.
Absolutely loved this guy.  class was interesting and the workload was OK.
I had to do a group project with the laziest student there ever was in Vanderbilt. Norbert gave us both an A-.  Other than that, the class was the only one I looked forward to that semester.

Norbert is the best. I think some freshman just got mad at him one day and submitted all the b@/@#it ratings below.  Have an idea about the reading, come to class and ask questions, let him teach you and direct your thinking. Done. Awesome experience.  Easy A.

Predecessor of ANTH2250 The only difference is that this is more work. I can confidently say that Norbert really improved my worldview for the better. Participation matters because for some reason not many people take his classes. I really don't know why he has such a low rating. Attend,  skim the readings, ask away bu don't fake it. Guaranteed A.

Norbert is a very down to earth guy. Me and a couple of other students regularly grabbed coffee by the central library. He is very understanding if you have difficulties outside of class. I felt that he was invested in me.  The class is a lot of reading. Yet if you show interest and do your best to attend regularly, you won't fall short an A-.

His students call him by his first name . If you are even remotely interested in the topic,  there is  virtually no limit to how flexible he can get with the grading criteria. HE WILL HELP AND BOOST YOUR GRADE! DO NOT LISTEN TO THE OTHER COMMENTS!  + if you are not interested in the topic and unwilling to learn, why are you taking anthropology?

Every class, you read 50+ pages from either his book or his research papers. I would read the summary of the papers and then say 1 or 2 things each class. You write 4 papers and do a graded rewrite, but he says that your grades will go up & they don't. Doesn't use OAK so no clue of grade until the end. There are a lot of better FYWS to take.

The most interesting part of his lectures was watching the sweat stains form under his arms while he babbled in his thick German accent for an hour and a half. His powerpoints were verbatim from the textbook. There are so many menial assignments. I skipped every class I could, studied very little, and still got a B. Dry, boring, easy, and unhelpful

Professor Ross is clearly not focused on teaching, and is just doing so for his research/grants. He is unclear, does not adequately engage the class, and is very boring. I was interested in Anthropology, but this class (Anthropology 101) destroyed any interest I had in the subject. I would strongly advise against taking one of Ross's classes!!!
Very interesting lectures, this professor seems to know quite  a lot.

Worst professor I have ever had.  He had us read all of his own paper (that were unpublished) and was completely full of himself.  Also felt uncomfortable during a meeting with him outside class.  Avoid if possible.

He is a very boring professor. He also makes up theorems and words like narture and the we cant help it effect. This class was waste of my time and although anthropology's subject matter had the potential of being interesting, Norbert Ross killed it. Stay away if you can. Also, your TA will make or break your grade.

He killed any interest I had in anthropology. His lectures are very dry & hard to follow; he seems to harp on things that aren't important. It takes half a semester to get used to his accent & tendency to mumble. The class is rather low maintenance if you actually pay attention. TAs grade all papers, so if you get a bad TA, you're out of luck.

He has a strong German accent that makes him very easy to tune out during lectures. He doesn't seem interested in how much you learn in his class; a good TA makes this class much better. There is a fair amount of work, mostly reading and papers to write. If you can actually pay attention to him and understand what he says, take the class.

Very boring class.  Ross is much more interested in his own research than in teaching.  He also has a huge ego, and doesn't respect udergraduates at all.  I have heard him say on several occasions that undergraduates are lazy and generally unintelligent.  Very unpleasant man.  Made me question the validity of the entire discipline of anthropology.
Worst class ever. Readings are confusing and uninteresting as hell. Class discussions are so boring that I had such a hard time trying to stay awake. Extremely unclear on instructions.

BORING!  He tries to make class interesting, but rarely succeeds.  Much of the time it seemed like he said the same thing over and over again.  He's often available outside of class, but never very helpful.  And he grades very subjectively; does not justify grades with points
I just knew this class was going to suck, but it was easy and I learned quite a bit.
The material for this class has the potential to be interesting but Dr. Ross's lectures are terrible and irrelevant. A good TA will make the class much better.

Dr. Ross is the weirdest professor of all time.  The readings are usually really long and tedious.  The TAs were awful and did most of the work, so it really depends upon that.  Ross would probably make a better higher-level Anthro teacher, but as an intro teacher he sucks!!!  DO NOT DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!

He's boring, real boring. I looked forward to the days the TAs would lecture. He really didnt do much in the class as the TAs made up the tests and quizes. He just kind of talked which was horribly boring. Id avoid him

he knows his stuff.  he will help you out of class for as long as you need. classes are a little boring at times, but i thought it was a good experience, thought i dont think i will continue in anthropology.
He's an interesting guy.  There are a lot of readings, but it's fairly interesting.  Dr. Ross is an approachable guy out of class as well.  I would enjoy another class with him.

BEWARE: Very boring! The readings are interesting if you plan on having Anthropology as a major or minor. However, the lectures suck the fun out of everything unless they are playing a movie. His german accent makes it hard to understand him. So, hope for an awesome TA so the class won't feel horrible. Also, you will FAIL if you don't read.
ugh...beware: STAY AWAY! boring, boring, boring!
he's very boring and the class sucks
He is the worst professor I have ever had... I refuse to take another Anthro class again.

If you get the opportunity to take one of her classes, do it! An incredibly layered and interesting woman with an absolute genius way of teaching. She may seem a little strict at first, but everything is planned and she means best.
The kindest woman I think I've ever met in my life. Makes it pretty clear what she expects out of assignments, allows redos, and super accessible outside of class. Looked forward to seeing her :))

Dr. Nelson is a dedicated and knowledgeable professor. She is passionate about the subject she is teaching---she truly wants her students to take the knowledge she professed to the rest of their life. She is an easy grader, always accessible during office hours, and is very caring about her students. Would totally take her class again and again!

(for CAL 3200) I love Dana!! She is passionate, well-read, and down-to-earth. Kind, no-nonsense professor. Good discussion leader. Quietly hilarious. She cares about her students and pushes you to be the best you can be. Strict no-electronics-rule which I didn't mind. Rewrites available. Reading was dense, but interesting. Truly one of a kind!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Nelson is my favorite college Professor to date. She is so passionate about the classes she teaches. She also emphasized feedback and helping students improve over just spitting out a grade. The principles she taught are translatable to general life. Lot of opportunity for students to be active in class and contribute.

Dr. Nelson is super knowledgable about the topic, and a great discussion moderator. She is tough on essay grading, but she offers unlimited rewrites, so you can definitely get an A if you work hard. Overall, interesting class and great professor -- would definitely take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was a great and thoughtful professor. We had unlimited rewrites and she was always very thorough with her feedback, allowing you to know what you did wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects
Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nelson is one of the most eloquent and experienced discussion moderators I've ever come across. She lectures with an open-mind and is very upfront with what she expects out of her students. Expect your opinions and reasons for those opinions to be tested.

Nelson is a tough grader, but the class is rewarding as she really won't let you slide by with a half-baked essay. However, this is mitigated by her very-generous test and essay policy: unlimited rewrites, and full test previews. If you're taking it for AXLE, look somewhere else, but work with her and you'll learn a lot about writing and history.

This class was supposed to be an English class, but it is taught more like a history class. If you like history lectures, this might be the class for you. If you like English discussions, this is not the class for you.

She's a great person, and I enjoy her personality, but she gives long lectures that seem wrong for an English class, and provides little time for class discussion. She's quite challenging, and I did not particularly enjoy her.
Great professor--really cares about her students. There is a lot of reading but it is manageable nonetheless. Highly recommend!
Was very unaccommodating. Was not flexible with illness or unforeseen circumstances. Blamed students for getting sick and missing class and then wouldn't meet to go over content missed.
Rude to students. Ruined my love for biology.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS
Professor Nordman is one of the best professors I have had at Vandy, and I'm a double major! I recommend taking his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Nordman is great
Professor Nordman is the best professor at Vandy

ALSO notice how all the positive reviews are from the SAME EXACT DAY like bffr there is obviously something going on. There is not way this professor would have a 3.3 rating and have a rating increase by 2.2 points without him teaching the class again.
Great course overall

Get ready to read and study. It is not a walk in the park, yet professor Nordman is a very incredible instructor. When I was having trouble, he would always suggest going to office hours. I ended up learning a lot from him and did well!

I recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Norman is seriously the best ever. I had a great time in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Please do not believe any negative comments about Dr. Nordman. He is incredibly caring and approachable.

This class is very difficult, but he wants people to do well. I was failing throughout the entire semester, and even then, he didn't give up on me. He encouraged me to not drop the class and helped me to do well.

Best professor for this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Nordman cares about each student. Despite other comments about him, I recommend taking his section with Dr. Brame. He is very knowledgable and although the lectures are somewhat vague, you can do well if you try.

Dr. Nordman exams were tough. The average for one of them was a 70, and he was proud of that. He does test based off exams and learning objectives. However, the types of questions he asks are in depth and require great application. One time, he asked an MCAT question, and the whole class basically got the question wrong.

Nordman gives good lectures and responds to student questions throughout. His portion of the class is less dense (still pretty dense though) but his exams are just as difficult. Don't have to participate in lectures but you should pay attention. Only real criticism is that his slides are slightly vague if you are trying to learn retroactively.

The Norman–Brame section completely ruined my interest in biology. The content is manageable, but Norman's exams are vague, misaligned with lectures, and unnecessarily confusing. He provides no practice exams because of his laziness & incompetence. He is often condescending when being asked and shows little concern for student success. Just avoid.

So friendly and passionate about bio! More difficult tests than Brame half, but also drops questions if everyone misses it. Only tests material right off the slides. An A is totally achievable in 1510 I just slacked on the final. Take this section!

Dr. Nordman is a chill guy but exams are way too difficult and go beyond what was covered in class. Would study for hours and still manage to get in the low 70s. Had to LITERALLY FIGHT for a B. If you have other options I would say register for those sections instead.

Chill guy! Lectures were informative but his exams were quite difficult, definitely more harder than Brame's. Still, he is very resourceful, he has AI podcasts for his lectures and even did IRL examples in class. BUT, he refuses to provide practice exams because "they wouldn't be good practice exams," do with than information what you will...

Good slides, good lecturer, and I believe respectful in class. I dont have experience with him in office hours however. He answered questions and was nice. His tests are tougher than Brames, study for Brame's test so you can drop one of his... If you study and lock in on critical thinking, his tests arnt too bad.
He is a horrible professor. A horrible horrible professor. As a fat kid, if I had to choose between running 100 miles or taking this class, I would choose running 100 miles.

Professor Nordman was the worst professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. He constantly talked to me like I was stupid, and made me feel bad about my potential in the STEM field. He doesn't care about his students one bit, and it is very clear through the way he conducts himself during office hours and when students ask him questions in class.

Do NOT take Professor Nordman for BSCI 1510. He is the most arrogant and egotistical professor I have ever had. His goal throughout the semester was to prove to the class that he is smarter than all of us, intentionally making the questions on his tests impossible to understand. I genuinely think he gets off on seeing his students fail.

Do NOT take Dr. Nordman for BSCI 1510. Please, please, please take any other professor. If you are in this class, and can't get off the waitlist for anything else. Just drop the class and wait until next year to take it... genuinely.
The only reason you would ever want Dr. Nordman as your professor is if you have shame kink and want to be punished.

This guy is the last professor you should ever take for BSCI 1510. Horrible professor, horrible at explaining what will or will not be on exams, and overall a complete douchebag. Going to office hours will not help your grade, but will actually somehow hinder it because he makes you feel like an idiot the entire time for bothering him

Nordman is byfar one of the worst professors ive had at vandy. some questions are open ended and confusing and he does not give partial credit for being partially correct. Additionally, he'd put questions that weren't talked about on his slide decks to intentionaly tank grades. i hope he never teaches 1510 again.

This was Dr. Nordman's first (and hopefully last) year teaching BSCI 1510. BSCI 1510 was an overall very rewarding class, and his lectures were informational. He has been the worst grader I have ever encountered. There are multiple times where I received 15%+ deductions due to mistakes on tests, and he does not care about student success.

Honestly the worst professor I've had at Vanderbilt by probably a mile. BSCI 1510 is split into two sections, and his section's content was not too difficult - but he is the biggest dick in the entire Biology department. He out right refuses to meet with students and regularly cancels office hours. If you meet him, he is very condescending

Took him for 1510. His lectures and slides are good. They're dense, but so are all 1510 ones. But his exams are so god awful. He writes them like he's trying to prove that he's smarter than you. Low 70s to 60s average on them. Asked a question once during one, and he gave the wrong answer dropping my grade by 5%. Take this class at your discretion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he is not awful. definitely do his past exams. you will not do good without them because his content is not as detailed as his questions. also in his answer keys for the practice exams, sometimes he puts the answers to his own questions wrong, which is extremely frustrating when you're trying to go over them. his tests are hard (64% averages)

when he smiles his lips curl into this shape that eerily resembles the joker. lecture heavy, seems to find enjoyment in our suffering. does curve to an 80, but i think he kinda convinced badgandi to not curve exam 4. avoid him, because his exams seem like it's more fit for people who absolutely love biochem and think about it in their spare time.

Dr. Nordman has resolved all of the issues that previous students commented about in regards to his character. However, Nordman is a dangerous professor to take. His course is very detail-oriented and there is a lot of information you are required to know. His exams are very difficult but he curves to 80. Good guy, just not easy at all.
Nordman is completely senile this year. Don't worry about the bad reviews from previous years. He gives me crime boss vibes and honestly I kinda had a crush.

I think they replaced the narcissistic Dr. Nordman from 2023 with some new AI because he just smiles and does his job now (completely sedated like a robot). I thought his class was structured pretty well and forced me to learn. I did alright on the exams just because I studied nonstop for a week so I guess if you wanna do good just don't slack off.

The worst professor I've had at vandy by far. Flipped classroom format is not conducive to anyone's learning goals. In class, rather than developing on lecture material, repeats parts of the online lectures verbatim and gives unfairly difficult exams which aren't even worth a huge chunk of our grade. Do not take.
Not a very nice guy to say the least...

DO NOT take Nordman for the biochemistry2 requirement (Molecular Biology). This class was completely self taught, he did not teach a single lecture in person. Exams were extremely vague, with only about 20% of the content learned showing up on them. The rest required you to be creative with no clear right answer. Partial credit wasn't given either.

He made a mistake with the beta-turn question on his exam. He refused to respond to emails, and refused to give the points back despite admitting that the question had a problem. Current students taking biochem, noticed the same error in his old exams. He put the same question in the makeup quiz. I lost 5 or 6 points in total and I lost my A-.

Nordman's tests were challenging, and relied on material from lectures and the textbook. He was standoffish in office hours and test review sessions, and answered more than one question with "it's in the lecture/notes, you already have the answer." There was a significant, positive change in energy when Brame's half of the semester started.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: decent professor. acted like a narcissist. His tests were very specific and very difficult. His grading is all or nothing which can really hurt you.

A really great person and prof. He does a great job of going over the main concepts in class. Exams are difficult but if you really grind hard you will be fine. Read the book! He won't admit it but some things on tests came straight from the text, not from class. Worksheets and quizzes prepare you well. Take him if you can!!

His content was usually pretty organized and his lectures were to-the-point. His exams always have questions that seem like they're meant to trick you though. He's helpful in office hours but sometimes it also feels like he doesn't really want to be there and can sound kind of annoyed, which ig you can't blame him for. An alright choice, hard class

Nordman? More like NordGOAT. Nordman was awesome, and I feel like in his section of the class I had a super strong grasp of the material. His exams are hard, but he gives you the tools to succeed in biochem. He is also super helpful in office hours and his in-class worksheets are very well-made and helpful for studying. I recommend him.

Dr. Nordman is a good professor, but sometimes, the explainations he gives is convoluted because of the difficulty of some of the material. He is great during office hours. His exam/homework is very application-based, which can make them hard. Overall, he is knowledgeable and very attentive to students' needs.

Nordman is a great proffessor and an even better person. He goes out of his way to make sure his students have everything they may need. It's a tough class regardless but he is very fair. Would highly recommend!
Dr. Nordman is a great professor. His exams are very detailed and wants you to write what he wants you to write or it is wrong. Just memorize everything you see on slides and you will be fine

Dr. Nordman's section was fine - you should skim the textbook and mainly focus on his lecture videos. I felt some of the test questions were unfair but overall a fine choice for biochem - lots of memorizing mechanisms and structures in his half of the class.

I think its quite ridiculous that he makes us read the textbook just for 1-2 random questions on the exam to be actually asked about them. Its also quite clear he himself doesn't know the material deeper than what the department told him to teach. However, overall him and Dr. Brame are the best choice for taking biochemistry.

Biochem is a hard class no doubt, but Dr. Nordman makes it manageable. He's personable and genuinely cares about the subject. He's extremely knowledgeable, but makes you work for it when you answer questions. Best advice - reach out to him individually. He can't know everyone in his class of 200, but he'll remember you.

Despite having to teach online due to COVID, I thought Dr. Nordman did a great job adapting to the needs/wants of students. His lecture videos were very clear and he took what students had to say to heart when structuring the synchronous classes.

Throughout this entire online class, Nordman failed to deliver anything good. His test questions include answer choices that don't even have the correct answer, what he says in lecture does not match with the textbook for various topics causing confusion, and on the final he proceeds to create more questions than promised in the announcement. Bad.

Here's the thing, biochemistry is one of the hardest subjects that I've taken at Vanderbilt, but it's just a hump that all pre-meds, prospective grad students have to take. I really enjoyed learning all of the material even though it was extremely challenging, in the end i'm glad I took Nordman/Brame and the tests really make you think hard

Dr. Nordman is an outstanding lecturer. He explains the material very carefully and helps students learn to apply what they learn in class to both work in the lab and other real-life applications. That being said, his tests are EXTREMELY difficult (probably the hardest section of the hardest class I've ever taken) and will require TONS of hard work
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Let me just start by saying while I was in his section, I thought it was hell. If you make it through to the other side you will be glad you took him and probably deserve a medal. To do well in his class, knowing and understanding the material is a minimum and you probably still won't do well on the tests. However, you will learn so much from him.

Dr. Nordman is one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. He does an incredible job explaining complex topics. On the flip side his tests are some of the most difficult I have taken. You really need to not only study extremely hard BUT also be an inherently good analytical thinker and problem solver otherwise you will struggle on exams

Dr. Nordman has been the best STEM professor I've had. The material is tough, but go to office hours/review sessions. The learning objectives really help to direct your studying, and exam qs always come from those, even if they seem less important in lecture. Also, don't read the whole chapter/do every hw q. Just use it to supplement lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nordman is super tough, but he's pretty fair. Lectures can get dry sometimes because of the material, and he goes over stuff pretty fast, but he's super accessible outside of class to help you. This is biochem, so it's not gonna be easy. Loved Nordman's way of teaching the material though. Definitely learned a lot.

Good: Good person, accessible outside class, hosts review sessions, pretty good at explaining the material, open to feedback, slides are good for the most part Bad: encourages textbook but it's useless, hard tests, things on test weren't always taught/emphasized, useless textbook problems
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Biochem is hard no matter who you have, but Nordman is pretty solid. He tries hard, and while it doesn't always translate, he is happy to meet with you outside of class to reexplain things. Plus, he brings his super cute puppy to every office hours!
Nordman really wants you to come to office hours so he can help you do well. His lectures are extremely organized and what you need to know for the exams is very clear. Plus, he has an adorable dog!

Good professor, gives good/entertaining lectures, really chill in office hours. Tests are kind of vague, and he goes over hard concepts in class but never tests any of them on tests.  Not a bad professor, considering its his first time ever teaching, but I do think he could(and will) get better in the coming years.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He speaks quietly you can't hear half of what he says. Recording lectures won't help since it's basically mumbling. The tests are too vague and he takes off points even if you get the answer correct if you happen to get the question before that incorrect. He also doesn't provide information about what to study. Would definetly not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The professor consistently shows up to class late, gives out almost no assignments, and when he does give out assignments, he does so later than promised. Additionally, he grades in the most random way possible. I have never, ever, seen a professor care so little about his class.

This course was very interesting. I really enjoyed when we went into the lab to view the current research being performed. There was a physical aspect of being able to manipulate particles that made it very enjoyable. It also worked well with the topic of the midterm essay and extended my interest in
the field.

Very caring professor frequently checking on the student's understanding. Very accommodating. Good pace of in class learning.
Concerned for the students and wants the very best from them.

I truly enjoyed this class! Professor Ndukaife is an authority in this area. I was amazed at how one person could be so knowledgeable and enjoyed transferring the knowledge to others in a clear concise manner. He is a very practical teacher and if you enjoy research you would love taking his class. Truly an inspiration to many young Professors.

Pretty theoretical class that can be difficult to comprehend. Dr. Ndukaife can be a little difficult to understand at times but if you ask for clarification he is very nice and will go back over material.

I enjoyed taking this course. It was engaging with plenty of opportunities to ask questions. I would have appreciated more heads-up on quizzes though as there were many quizzes. Overall, the professor cares about the class and tries to carry everyone along.
He is very knowledgeable of the subject and explains the concepts well. There were lots of quizzes, which helped me to understand electromagnetism better.

Lectures absolutely useless but still need to attend because of pop quizes. There's no homework for like half the semester so you have absolutely no idea what's gonna be on the test. Be ready to be completely clueless on tests and quizzes. But you may turn out fine. Think he must have curved the final. Have no idea how it was graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice guy, loves his optical tweezers, but he made the class harder than it needed to be, and electromagnetics is already a hard class. His lectures were derivation heavy and sometimes hard to follow, but he reads right out of the textbook 99% of the time so just read that. He had a tough time answering class questions and made a lot of mistakes.

Dr. Oster was wonderful at explaining complex concepts and moving through lectures well. If you do a bit of studying for quizzes and the midterms and participate on field trips and in class, it'll be a great semester.

Jessica Oster's paleoclimates class is a must take---you will learn a ton! There's a lot of material covered, and it's all very interesting. We had one group presentation, one midterm, homework assignments, and a final. We also got to go on a super cool field trip. I definitely recommend taking her class.

2510 is pretty lecture-heavy, and Dr. Oster is a fast lecturer, so be ready for that. That said, you learn so much in this class and it's a great time with the field trips. Nothing is weighted too heavily. The primary workload besides exams is prep for weekly scientific paper discussions. Her dog Wrigley is the GOAT

While Jessica is brilliant, she barely teaches in geochem. Most learning comes from reading ad super dense textbook with a difficult quiz for each chapter. Class time is mostly graded application problems. Lab at the farm was super fun and the content is very applicable, but be ready to work hard.

I definitely learned a lot of interesting and applicable things in this class, though a lot of the material was quite complicated and hard to wrap my head around. Prof Oster has high expectations, so I highly encourage doing the readings and putting in work to be prepared for class or else you will feel the heavy weight of her disappointment.

Dr Oster is a leading Paleoclimatologist, but teaching students is definitely on her back burner. She knows a lot about the topic she teaches about, but you have to read assigned papers to stay afloat in the class. The lectures are reviews of assigned readings, rather than the readings supporting her lectures. Pairs well after EES 2510.

Dr. Oster is a brilliant scientist, but the design of environmental geochemistry is especially hard to learn in. Its a flipped classroom, so you HAVE to teach yourself the material. There is a quiz on a new 30 pg VERY DENSE chapter every week. Its a really difficult class, but probably it is the class Ive learned the most in.

There is a large emphasis on groupwork which is both a blessing and a curse. There are weekly quizzes that are very difficult, but overall the grading for the course is very fair. Professor Oster is very helpful. I learned a lot and am able to connect what I have learned with my other environmental science courses. 8/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Ni is a great lecturer who cares about his students. He is passionate about teaching Organic Chemistry and his class becomes very rewarding especially if you take the time to develop a true interest in organic chemistry. His exams are well written and test understanding/application of the material rather than memorization. Attend office hours.

Had him for 2221 and took him again for 2222 because he's great. Yes, he is a little on the harder side but his ability to teach and the way he runs lectures make it so worth it. Great professor, and I will miss him. Content in this class is a little more difficult.

I absolutely love Dr. Ni. He is a very demonstrative professor and I always feel like he explains things clearly. He is very reasonable with what he expects you to remember and his test questions are always fair if you put in the work.The best STEM professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt and I always feel confident going into his exams.

Orgo is a difficult class, but Dr Ni is a great professor. I was not super happy with my performance overall, but I believe that is just the nature of the content. Ni's exams are LONG and the 55 minute class period often left me with unfinished exams, which brought down my grade significantly. The 3 exams and final is worth 90% of your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Taking organic chemistry with Dr. Ni was the best decision I made. Coming from someone who didn't do too well in gen chem, Orgo 1 was much better. While Dr. Ni's exams are difficult, I found them to be very fair. You will know what to expect on the exam. Dr. Ni teaches in a way that makes sense. Not to mention, he is unintentionally hilarious.

Dr. Ni is certainly an acquired taste. He is on the more difficult side of orgo professors, but he is very straightforward about what is expected on his exams and is highly, highly accessible outside of class. If you email him, he will respond within seconds. Can be awkward, but also funny if you get to know him. Overall, great dude

Ni is an absolute sweetheart. Attendance is mandatory with tophat quizzes everyday. He has great lectures and the tests are very straightforward. Go to pre test office hours and ask all the questions you have before the tests. Orgo is hard but Chi-Li makes it as easy as it could be
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ni is just ok. His exams are harder, which is why I really struggled. Two positives is he's pretty clear with what he expects from his students and has infinite office hours. However, he is dry and very stoic so I didn't exactly feel that comfortable coming to him with questions. Overall, not bad not great, so I will try out Clements next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ni is a solid choice for orgo overall, his tests are challenging but fair and everything you need for them is on the lecture slides. He has a lot of office hours and extra ones before every exam, and is generous with partial credit. Orgo is a hard class in general and requires consistent studying instead of cramming, but Ni is a good choice.

Dr. Ni the goat! He was a great teacher, able to simplify very complex mechanisms into basic steps. He made it really clear what was going to be on the exams and was very accessible via office hours. He gives really good tips on how to study orgo. You'll have to obviously put in the time to study outside of class, but it was really doable. 10/10

I believe Ni is very fair across all ranges. Yes, his exams are a little hard, but unlike gen chem, if you study his past exams, it is very predictable what he would put on the exam, and that alone is half the reason why I got an A- in this class. I think Ni can be a little dry, very straightforward about what we need to know and don't need.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ni is an ok lecturer, don't get me wrong, but his tests were AWFUL. I have received an A in every other pre-med class and am hoping for a B- in his course. The tests were significantly different from what we learned in class. Oh and don't let me forget about the fact that he does not share any test average because it is so low. Do. Not. Take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Ni is the GOAT in all caps. Orgo (particularly orgo 2) is tough no matter who you take it with. But Ni will tell you bluntly what you do and do not need to know for the exam. Just the same with other orgo profs, do yourself a favor and do the practice problems until your fingers bleed and you start having dreams about reaction mechanisms.

Ni is the goat. Yes it's hard and yes you will likely struggle, but that's just Orgo. He is so generous with partial credit and genially cares about his students and their success. He has infinite office hours and is always on his email. I took both Orgo 1 and Orgo 2 with him and am so glad I did. I feel so prepared for the MCAT. Take him!!!!

Not bad, not great. Make sure you write down what he says, not just what he writes. Exams are very long but partial credit will save your grade. Honestly orgo is a lot of memorizing so make sure you keep up with the class. Pretty nice guy, just a little boring but that might be just the nature of the class lol.

Ni is a great guy who really tries to make orgo as bearable as possible. Slides are very clear and they show you everything you need for the exams. Frequent office hours and a dedicated review class before every exam, so he answers all of your questions. The exams are difficult but fair, and he's very generous with partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great prof. He is very accessible with office hours like everyday and sometimes evenings. Everything he has on his slides are on the exam. His exams are tough and are harder than practice questions in the textbook, and the exams very application based, so you really need to know concepts and content.

really good prof, imo most orgo profs here are great. generous on partial credit. i'd rec go to OH if you're lost on anything, and draw out all rxn mech for exams 2+3 to study. txtbk q's help but are a bit easier than what ni uses for exam Q's. he's pretty stoic, but he rlly wants students to learn so don't let that stop you from asking questions
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy, but not a good prof. You are better off taking list

Ni is great in office hours. He really wants you to learn and the explanations he gives in office hrs are a lot more detailed than in lecture. HIGHLY recommend you go. A bit of a dry lecturer and his exams are hard, but overall I think he's the best Orgo prof. The first two exams are ok, but be prepared as the 3rd exam and final are really dense.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Between Hare and Clements I'd say Ni is a good medium. I really feel like he does what he can as a professor. He makes himself as accessible as he can. Some people do find him to be more difficult, but after the first exam he's fine as long as you learn to study for his style exams.

Orgo is difficult no matter which professor you have, but Ni is a decent choice. He is extremely generous about partial credit on exams. Also gives out a few extra credit opportunities. Tests were tough, and he is a pretty dry lecturer. However, he was extremely accessible outside of class (had question discussion boards and extra office hours).

Ochem is going to be hard no matter who you take, but Ni wasn't bad at all. He gives a bunch of partial credit for his exams and his slides are pretty good for having a sneak peek of what kind of questions he might ask. He also always brings a plushie to every class!! Always looked forward to see which ones he'd bring.

Complete honest review: Orgo is hard regardless of which prof you take. Class like this you just have to self study and I honestly think that Ni was one of the better profs this semester because of how lenient he is with grading. His lectures arent the best but he makes jokes here and there which is a plus. not easy but i recommend

During his first year of teaching he was considered one of the best Orgo profs at Vandy. However he has since changed a lot of things that worked for students and now he is in strong contention to be one of the worst Orgo profs.He does try to make up for the gaps in his pedagogy by offering lots of office hours.

He was good last year (supposedly). This year, he just talks at class. No engagement. Not helping anyone learn. People have no clue what is going on. Tests are very difficult especially compared to other orgo professors.

Do not take his class the exams are so hard for no reason much harder than other classes because he picks tiny parts out of the lectures to ask questions about. It is also very easy to mess up and lose many points. His lectures are boring and hard to keep up with you won't learn anything unless you do it by yourself.

Dr. Ni is one of the best choices for Ochem here. Had him both semesters and he is extremely accessible outside of class (even has night office hours before exams). He implements feedback from students.  However, lectures are dry, and exams are tough. Although he gives generous partial credit, I had to rely on textbook to learn most of the time.

I've had Hare and Clements for Ochem one and two and they were both...Mehh..not very caring overly difficult test givers. However, I retook Ochem 1 for a better grade with Dr. Ni and he truly is the best in my opinion in the chemistry department for this position. He's very nice, explains things very well, and gives so much partial credit.

TAKE THIS GUY!! Gave us surveys throughout the sem for extra credit on how he could make his class better and actually takes all inputs. He is VERY generous with partial credit. I have such high hopes for him as he continues to teach. He truly cares about the students and is clearly passionate about orgo. I really believe he's the best you can take

Dr. Ni was an amazing professor despite this semester being his first time teaching. Lectures were well organized and he was very accessible both after and outside of class. Exams were tough but he takes feedback from students and often reflects upon them. Also gave opportunities for extra credit and is a very lenient grader!
Genuinely kind and the best option for organic chemistry

As the other review mentioned, Dr. Ni is your best bet for 2221. It was his first semester teaching but he did a great job of going over material on slideshows and then highlighting what mechanisms we actually needed to know for the exam. He is very accessible outside of class before exam days. Exams are tough but they're tough for every section.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best organic chemistry professor at Vandy. Although his tests weren't easy he always gave tons of partial credit and was a very lenient grader. Made himself extremely accessible outside of class and would always hold nightly office hours on the days leading up to an exam. Highly recommend.

He is a great teacher in the sense that he knows the material and knows how to explain it well. However, lectures can be boring. Overall he is a great choice for organic chemistry and is very helpful to his students.

It's his first semester teaching, but he's an absolute chiller. He makes himself very available for office hours in the evening as well as right after class, so you can get all your questions answered before leaving if you're unsure of the material. Tests are difficult, but they are for every other section anyway.

This is his first semester teaching. I've had a really positive experience in his class - the class itself is pretty lecture-heavy, but so is every other orgo class. His slides are organized and he gives practice problems as well as weekly quizzes graded for completion. No graded hw, the tests are pretty hard but fair if you take the time to study.
Took him for abnormal psych, best lecturer I've had so far in college! Super engaging classes. Exams are multiple choice and questions are straight forward. Take this class!

Dr. Olatunji is an engaging lecturer with a clear teaching style and good sense of humor. Attendance is optional but lectures are VERY helpful. Exams are detailed and based on lectures AND textbook. The course includes two straightforward article reviews graded fairly, plus several extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Olatunji is an engaging lecturer with a clear teaching style and good sense of humor. Attendance is optional, but you need to attend lectures for your own sake. Exams are very detailed and includes textbook content. The course includes two straightforward article reviews graded fairly, plus several extra credit opportunities.

Dr. O is awesome!! Generally exams test based on lecture content AND textbook readings (each chapter took me about 2 hours to get through). Questions are multiple choice, but really fair and an appropriate amount of challenging. He doesn't post lecture slides  (only guidance for the readings), so go to class and pay attention!

I liked Olatunji when I took his class! I was put off at first due to what i've heard about his class, but it really wasn't that bad. he gave multiple chances for extra credit and getting a good grade was possible if you study the textbook and the lecture (take notes!). Attendance isn't mandatory, but you really do need to attend to pass at all.

He's great! So far my favorite class so far in undergrad and if you're interested at all in mental health / clinical psychology, this class is for you! It does take work, but Olatunji gives multiple opportunities to elevate your grade through extra credit. At the same time, exams are very achievable if you study lecture and textbook content.

3 exams, decently easy if you prepare properly and read the textbook and show up to class. This semester, he gave a substantial amount of extra credit for very little work, very invested in student success and overall just an interesting guy with good insight into the field of clinical psychology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Olatunji is deeply passionate about what he teaches, and it shows in the interactive way he teaches the class. The class is mostly graded on tests and 1 paper and 1 movie review so you have to study the textbook and attend lectures. I would take him again and he was 100% worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Olatunji is one of the best lecturers at Vanderbilt. He is notorious for giving difficult exams and being extremely tough overall. However, I feel that he is a great professor and is honestly underrated. Yes, his exams can be difficult but if you listen to the lectures and review the material you will do just fine in the course.

I may be biased, but I loved PSY3100 with him. People say it's super hard, but it really isn't if you keep up with readings and come to class (plus, having good note-taking skills helps). His lectures were some of the most entertaining I've had here, and although he can seem unapproachable, he's a nice guy who wants you to learn. I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Olatunji is not a bad person, but he's also not a good professor.
