He refuses to upload his lecture slides, dismisses most criticisms about his class, test questions are super trivial, and there are two papers only worth approximately 5% of the total grade (+ no feedback given on either paper). Do not take 3100 with him if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: so idk how the person before me got an A when grades arent even out yet...but anyways would not recommend this professor by any means. like other reviews said ur grade is mostly made up of exams which are trivia questions based off literally hundreds of pages of textbook reading. if you are a psych major take this class with Polyn instead!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. O! He's very funny and obviously cares about the topic, but lectures were long and sometimes hard to sit through. Grade is based only off of the 2 midterms and the final. There are 2 papers that only count for 5% of the grade combined. Some exam questions were hyperspecific, but go to lectures and read the textbook and you'll be fine.

I would not recommend this class to anyone. Your grade will be three exams and two papers but the papers are quite literally worth 2% of your grade. There will be no curves/exam corrections. Attendance isn't mandatory but you have to come to class because he won't post his slides and his exam is trivia based off something he mentioned once in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The entire grade is dependent on tests which would be fine, but it is not. He does not post ANY of his lecture slides and the textbook does not go over half of the things he says. The tests are also completely unreasonable. It is like he is wanting us to fail. Do not recommend and would never take again!!!

Professor O is great. He tried to make the lectures much fun. However, the composition of the grade doesn't make any sense. Two 3-5 pages essays each only weigh 2.7% of the total grade and other than that is only about exams. The exams are COMPLETELY NOT REASONABLE. For such close-book exam, it's too detailed and he seemed to enjoy testing trivia.

Tests are trivia based and extremely arbitrary. His lectures sometimes contradict the book, and he makes unsourced claims in lectures. 350 out of 370 pts are exams. Content isn't hard; it's hard to memorize many many meaningless/googleable facts. He brings up interesting studies, but is terrible at interpreting graphs/charts from said studies.

professor o is super funny, but the tests are incredibly difficult. tests count for 97% of the grade. the tests are multiple choice, but do not let that fool you- they are incredibly specific. attendance technically is not mandatory, but you wont pass without going. so, unless you dont have another option for PSY, dont take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. O is literally the top researcher in his field and it shows. All of the information presented in class is the cutting edge research, cited from primary sources. He also opens the floor for discussion on hot topics. Truly never learned more from a class than this one. Exams require preparation, but if you REALLY engage with class, you'll be good

The other reviews for Dr. O made me nervous taking this class, but it ended up being one of my favorite ones at Vandy. His lectures were so interesting/funny and made me never want to miss class. The tests are worth an insane amount of the overall grade, but follow the study guide, read the chapters, & go to the review session and you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor O is hilarious and I always found his lectures super interesting and interactive. Would occasionally get boring but super important to go to class in order to do well. You also HAVE to read the textbookThere's 2 midterms and a final that are all MC with super specific questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were tough. I recommend reading the textbook intensively, it improved my grade a lot. The two papers he has you write are not gimme grades -- plenty of people got C's and B's on them. I think I missed the cutoff for an A because I didn't know his dog was a labradoodle for EC which sucks. ("do NOT email me asking for grade adjustments" tho)

While the content of ab psych is interesting, the exams made it excruciatingly unenjoyable. Oluntunji is a smart guy, but the test questions are unnecessarily specific; he almost WANTS students to do poorly and even told us he himself got a B on the first exam. Exams are 94% of the overall grade but short papers were okay. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I thought that this was going to be my favorite class as a psych major but turns out all the fun is sucked out of the experience if tests are as unfocused and arbitrary. The whole class stressed me out and it DRAGGED on. The three exams were difficult and average was a low B but Dr. O still wanted scores LOWER and wrote tests accordingly. Forget it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the material in this class. It does take effort to do well. The tests can be specific and there are only 3, including the final. There is no homework, but there are two short writing assignments. Come to lecture and read the book to know the material for the test. The class length was a struggle, but it didn't meet on Fridays. Study alot.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 2 exams, 1 final, 2 papers (barely worth anything). Prof. O is an awesome lecturer. He definitely makes the class interesting and presents solid, evidence-based material from past research studies. He asks a lot of questions that make you think and question whether we're doing things right as a society and systemic flaws. Exams are based on notes.

This class was confusing and annoying. On one hand, the material is easy and enjoyable, and he is passionate and knowledgeable. On the other, he is pretentious, and the lecture covers so much unnecessary material and the textbook is so detailed that studying feels like roulette. Don't take as a blow off, must be able to memorize well to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Basically just tell you that drugs is inefficient and go with cognitive behavioral therapy instead for all mental diseases. Testing trivial details that you'll never get a chance to know.

You have to read the textbook thorougly, go to all of the lectures, and also look at the slides that he uploads online (which are different from those he uses in class). He discusses a lot of biology stuff (or rather neuroscience stuff) that is not in the textbook, and they will all come up in the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. O's lectures are interesting but fast-paced. Don't skip class if you want to do well. His tests are tough but get much easier once you figure out how to study for them. Very interesting and knowledgeable professor. He can come off as a little arrogant but if you talk to him 1 on 1 he's kind, remembers you, and cares about how you're doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Olubunmi was very knowledgable on the subject matter & lectures were always very interesting. However, his tests are difficult and he often asks about very specific and seemingly obscure details. He is also a pretty relentless grader, and final grades are comprised of mainly just the test grades, so it's definitely not easy to get an A.

Dr. O was a great professor. He is super knowledgeable about abnormal psychology and is engaging in his lectures. He really tries to get the class to discuss with him even though there are 100 people in the classroom. There are only 2 exams and a final, and a couple of papers for which the grading is pretty harsh. Great class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are only two tests and two 10 point assignments so study well. If you miss a lecture, you're out of luck because his P-Points online are not what he uses in class. Also, he is very arrogant in office hours and answers your questions with a question. The tests are multiple choice but often ask very specific questions. Wish I took pass/fail...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: My favorite class at Vandy. Hilarious and kind guy, don't be fooled. Tests are kind of hard but not the worst. Two 3-5 page papers, put some effort into them and should be fine, though the grades seem kind of arbitrary. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. Not an easy A, but an easy B+/A-. I loved this class so much.

He is great!! Very knowledgeable, helpful, and entertaining. There are 2 tests and the final-- none of them are that difficult as long as you read AND pay attention in lecture. Super interesting class

SO rude. Pretentious. Psych is my major and he is by far the worst Psych professor I've had. I would have liked the class with a different professor, but Olatunji ruined it for me. He is not nice or helpful, very full of himself, I went to his office hours and he was shockingly rude. He makes his class hard, trys to seem smarter than he is.

interesting class/material. grade based primarily on mult. choice tests that focus on rather specific questions but are totally doable if you attend lectures and skim the chapters. papers are good test boosters and there is ample opportunity for extra credit w/ psych studies. overall minimal effort req'd for a decent grade.

Wonderful lecturer.  Tests aren't too difficult - they don't cover anything that isn't discussed and/or in the book. He does expect you to know the material, but he tells you what to focus on. Has wonderful guest lecturers, as well as supplemental readings and videos. Also very available after class to discuss various topics related to the course.
Tests are pretty difficult for the average person, but it is a great class! Very interesting! Make sure you pay attention during class! The papers are grade boosters so make sure you do that as well.

Good lecturer, but tests were harder than expected. Almost the entire grade is based on multiple choice tests, but they aren't easy at all. A lot of the test questions were on very random, specific facts. It's not easy, and the grading system was very frustrating.

Topic: Clinical Fear & Anxiety (psych majors, take seminars - they're small, lots of discussion, no tests just papers) He can be a little intimidating one-on-one, but the class was fun. Good prep for grad school, and I learned a LOT. Dynamic lectures, great discussion. He's awesome. Don't leave without taking abnormal with him! Great professor!

Tests aren't too bad.  Grading is based on unfair extra credit policy.  He is very arrogant.   Easy B+, not too hard to get an A-, an A is a big accomplishment but is doable.   Pray that your cell phone doesn't go off in class or he will punch you in the ear.

AWESOME lecturer, good sense of humor. Didn't encounter him outside of class much (mostly TA's), but helpful when I did. However, I think they're trying to make this a weed-out class for PSY majors, as tests got increasingly harder - they were trying to get the average down to a C - kind of discouraging. But I really, really enjoyed the class.

He is a great professor with a very dry sense of humor. You need to go to class to take notes and read the text, but the material is interesting, especially if you're a psych major. There are only 3 tests which are not that hard. Definitely recommend him.

Bunmi has a lot of knowledge of the subject but tends to be sarcastic and can even be rude. you must come to class to take notes even though attendance isnt mandatory. class isnt bad but his attitude towards students could be better.

Very opinionated and somewhat of a smart aleck. However, he is a quality professor and a lot of fun. Bunmi knows his stuff and is easy to understand. He moves a little fast on power points, but if you read the text and go to class you will definitely get an A.
Hard class but I think it was worth it. You would probably enjoy the class if you are into econ research. He's a new professor so he'll get better over time. Also a really nice guy.

Extremely tough class, which isn't itself a problem, but the lectures made it difficult for me to enjoy learning the material. Very theory/academia based and I don't feel like I learned much about the real world. I didn't study too much for exams, but if you have a very strong math background, they aren't too bad. Curved heavily.

HARD class. Passionate teacher. Exams were too hard but heavy curve and I do think he calibrated towards the end. Learned a ton, glad I took the class, but I studied an obscene amount. Lectures sometimes lacked structure but good at explaining concepts. 

Class was worth imo but know what you're getting into.

Professor O'Keefe does not know how to teach undergraduates. He has difficult-to-understand lectures and is highly inaccessible outside of class. Homework sets were extraordinarily difficult and exams were quite tough. Classroom structure discourages collaboration and grading structure was illogical. I studied an unfathomable amount for a B. AVOID!
She's the best. Take her if you can.

LOVED her. Sweetest professor ever and very understanding. This class was a bit time consuming and had to learn a lot of grammar in a short amount of time but honestly didn't think it was hard at all compared to my other classes. 3 straightforward exams with grammar and writing sections + 3-4 papers. Easy grader. Definitely take her if you can.

My favorite professor at Vandy so far is awesome.  Very warm and fun energy, and is always laughing and having fun.  Cares a lot about her students.  Class was definitely the hardest I've taken, but definitely doable, and she is fully there to help.  Definitely recommend the class and her as a professor.

Professor Ortiz is amazing—super funny and caring! The only challenging part is the grammar, even for native Spanish speakers, but class discussions are engaging, and she really tries to make the material interesting for everyone.

Profesora Ortiz was wonderful! She has such a great spirit and she made class entertaining to come to even though attendance was mandatory. The work was not difficult and there were a few group projects. I would def recommend taking her.

This is a writing heavy class, but is overall very well done. you will learn a lot in a fast paced environment, so get ready to study outside of class, as well as complete daily online home works. She is very kind though, and will be sure to walk you through any trouble you may have.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Dra Ortiz! She clearly cared about each of our success and progress. There were 3 essays with ample time and required revisions (so it was hard to do poorly) and a couple of grammar quizzes for which she prepared us well (via MindTap and worksheets). I feel like my Spanish writing improved immensely. Take her if you can!!

I felt like I advanced immensely as a writer. We had 3 papers of different writing styles but we always received feedback on a first draft to know how to improve. The grammar exams are quite difficult but mindtap comes with a textbook and reading it helps a lot in my opinion because she does go through grammar quickly as it is mainly review.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Profesora Ortiz is an incredibly kind person and a great professor. She encouraged us to practice speaking Spanish and helped us have class discussions ranging from current events to literary analysis. Over the course of the semester there were three grammar tests and four essays. She provided detailed, thoughtful feedback on our writing.

She is truly the best 3301W professor. She is super kind and funny and class was honestly pretty fun if you have a good group. She is super nice and class is all based on papers and a few exams (which are easy if you prepare) which is expected for a Spanish writing class. Take her class!

Profesora Ortiz is marvelous. She is clear in her manner of lecturing and is extremely caring for her students. I am a native speaker, so I found the course to be easy; however, even then, she created a safe space for her students to express themselves openly and freely, which is very important for langauge learning.

I really enjoyed this class. Though it was lecture heavy I really enjoyed learning about the material. Professor Ortiz is one of the most caring and genuine people I have ever had the pleasure to be taught by. She is a very easy grader. The tests are tough, but the essays definitely make up for it.

Profa. Ortiz is one of the kindest people I've ever met, especially in an academic setting. At first, it almost seemed inauthentic, but throughout the semester I've come to realize that she's really just that nice. 3301 didn't require much effort as long as you went to class and kept up with the assignments. Would def take a class w her again!

Prof. Ortiz is one of the most caring people you will ever meet. She will always listen to you and wants her students to succeed. Brightspace was a little difficult to navigate at first, but it's easy to get used to. Highly recommend.

Profesora Ortiz is a hilarious, engaging hippie (in the best way). Prepare to be writing a paper once a week, on top of occasional vocab/grammar HW or assigned poetry reading. The writing assignments are usually open to creative interpretation, so they're as fun as you make them. In-class edits are common and she's super available for critiques.

Professor Ortiz is maybe one of my favorite instructors I've ever had. She always works to get everyone in class to participate in discussions, and it's clear that she cares about teaching. My only complaint is that grading criteria sometimes isn't super clear or accessible on the Brightspace page. Amazing professor, would highly recommend.

Professor Ortiz is a very straightforward and caring professor. We had lectures, in-class practice, online homework, multiple 2-page essays, a few tests, and a group presentation. As long as you  take the time to put in the work, you should leave with a good grade. One thing I wish I had done was participate in class more.

Profesora is great! The work itself is not hard. The papers are straightforward and she allows corrections to get points back. Her feedback is really helpful. The exams are very similar to the practice review sheets she gives in class.

Profesora Ortiz is one of the kindest professors I have had. She is very accessible outside of class and gives good feedback. Her lectures are organized and she teaches the material/grammar very well. The class itself is a good amount of writing and work in general, but taking it with made it more enjoyable. Would 100% recommend.
She's one of the nicest, if not the nicest professor I've had. She's so unintentionally funny. I loved having her as a prof.

Kind, genuine, sincere. You can tell her anything and won't be judged. She listens, asks questions and follows up. She is the first native professor I ever had, and hearing her talk about culture and literature in authentic Spanish makes me feel like I am in a classroom somewhere in Latin America . Her class convinced me to continue with Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Ortiz was amazing! She's super sweet and cares a lot about her students. She gives good feedback and isn't a super harsh grader. We got to watch a show in Spanish during class every Friday and then wrote discussion posts about it.

An absolute sweetheart. She's one of the kindest teachers I've had. She also gives good information and critiques for your writing. Be prepared to learn about Spanish grammar. With her as a teacher, you can't really go wrong.

Prof Ortiz is great! She makes class fun and truly cares about her students. Easy to get an A- in the class, but an A definitely takes a little work. Tests are grammar heavy but you will be fine with a base in AP Spanish. Lots of homework but nothing is too hard. Grade depends on tests and essays. Go to office hours!!!

Although she makes you work for it, in the end, it's totally worth it. She cares about each student and if you show up to office hours you are more likely to get a good grade in the class. Lectures aren't mandatory but super helpful.

Profesora Ortiz is awesome! She has a great sense of humor, provides constructive feedback on essays, and cares about helping you learn. Classes were mostly discussions with occasional lectures on grammar. Tests are grammar-heavy with short writing sections, and there are a few essays.
Such a kind and passionate professor. Gives very good feedback and class is fun. However, it is easy to get a decent grade but hard to ace. Lots of small assignments, but nothing terrible.

Prof. Ortiz is an amazing teacher. She is passionate about the subject and her students as well. In class, she encourages everyone to participate and practice their Spanish. One thing to note is that she often assigns a lot of work, sometimes multiple assignments a day, including podcasts, blog posts, and long movies.
Cares about students and their learning, makes you work but you get a lot out of it

Profesora is one of the most caring teachers I have ever had. She would always strike up conversation, and loved to start each class with some music and dancing to brighten our day. Although I loved the class, my only problem was with her grading. Instead of grading based on a set standard, it seems like everyone was graded against themselves.

She is the happiest professor I've ever had and really brightens my day every time. However, she is very unspecific in what she expects of her students and is a relentlessly tough grader. Her feedback is also vague. Everyone in the class has a different level of Spanish so instead of setting a standard, she grades based on individual improvement.

One of the most caring professors I've had! Even now, Prof. Ortiz will see me randomly on main and strike up a conversation with me in Spanish about how I'm doing. She's a tough grader on the essays but provides great feedback, especially if you go to office hours and ask for extra practice. Not an easy A, but she'll help you if you show you care!

Profe Oritz is one of the most caring professors I've had! I was a student the bottom of the class, and although she still graded tough, I went to her frequently and she offered a lot of resources and advice for me to improve. If you're willing to put some work in, you'll not only get a grade you want, but you will improve greatly in Spanish!

She is a great professor and is very passionate about the material. She is a hard grader on the essays, but she is very helpful during office hours and gives clear expectations for what she expects. The tests were fair and if you study hard for them, you'll do great. She really gets to know her students and class is fun.

Textbook used mainly for online homework--makes up test content for midterm and final. Read the syllabus to keep up with HW. Vague expectations given before papers are due but the essays are rigorously edited upon return. Work needs to be put in on the papers, go to her office hours to go over your drafts, even if you don't know what to ask about.
I would definitely take her again. She's super nice, genuinely cares about the students, and makes an effort to get to know everyone.
Easy to do ok, hard to ace. Tests are difficult, but papers (of which there will be many) are not. Be prepared to work very hard and do a lot of writing.

Profesora Ortiz is extremely sweet and enthusiastic and I enjoyed going to her class. There is a decent amount of essay writing, but she doesn't grade too harshly. As long as you put in the work and care about your essays, it's not hard to get a good grade in this class

Professor Ortiz is a super sweet lady and will give you helpful feedback, you just have to seek it out. She is an easy grader on essays. The tests are hard, but you can still get an A in the class even if you don't do great on the tests. She grades participation harder than you'd expect, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Profe Ortiz is the best! She is so helpful and sweet and clearly cares so much about her students' learning. The papers are manageable as long as you put in effort, and so are the exams but you need to study. Overall this is a great class, and Ortiz is definitely the teacher you want to take.
Complete sweetheart. Fast paced but easy class. Grades easy on essays and presentations.

She's really nice, expects a lot. As probably one of the only people in this class who didn't take Spanish all throughout high school, I sometimes felt lost, but most of my problems likely could have been solved with a better work ethic. I always felt like I was disappointing her if I used English instead of Spanish, but she appreciates any effort
Very sweet teacher. A tad disorganized--we often didn't know when things were due more than a week in advance.  But she's really helpful with explaining papers and passionate about the topic.

Ortiz is a very sweet professor who is a fair grader. You can get a good grade in this class as long as you actually try on the writing assignments and study for the quizzes. She's a great person overall.

Profe Ortiz is the most caring, loving teacher.  From what I've heard of other teachers who teach the same course, she's a lot less strict and requires wayyyy less homework.  For essays, she fully edits your papers and gives input. The department-wide tests are arbitrary however, and poorly made.  Not her fault though.
She is the best spanish teacher I have ever had. The classes are fun and interesting. She genuinely cares about her students, and is very relatable. She is the reason I am continuing on with spanish.

The best Spanish teacher that I have ever had. Incredibly enthusiastic and fun. She is incredibly passionate about her topic, and  you learn a lot too. Definitely bring out her goofy side in class. She is the reason I'm going to major in Spanish.

THE BEST SPANISH TEACHER EVER.  Seriously, I would be amazed if you found a better one.  So incredibly nice, cares about her students, is crystal clear when teaching and is young enough that she gets college life.  Even willing to bend some rules to accomodate students' busy schedules.  If you can, TAKE A CLASS WITH HER, she is the best.

Nicest teacher ever! Class is fun and easy, most of the time we just sit and discusss the material. She's incredibly helpful and funny, easier grader than most of the other Spanish profs. Definitely take her section if you can.
such a caring and awesome teacher!!!

Professor Ortiz is an incredibly sweet woman who really wants to help students out, if only they actually cared enough to go to her office hours. The problem is her class is easy and pointless so no one feels the incentive to come talk to her. I just wish she'd been a better teacher because she's a great person!
She is pretty easy. Makes it seem like the class will be hard in the beginning but grades papers easier as the semester goes on. Attendance is mandatory but it's a pretty easy class.

She is very sweet and has a great personality. Beware that she follows rules very strictly ad will not cut any slack. Other than that, she is very good with students and tries hard to make the class interesting. She can be a bit busy, but it is possible to see her outside of class.

Fun, enthusiastic woman who loves class participation. Do your work, and for essays the best thing to do is to write your first draft in Spanish right away, then revise it at least two-three times before you turn it in. Pretty demanding not only in good grammar but good arguments and theses. An easy and worthwhile class, and a remarkable professor.

Absolutely hilarious guy that made me laugh more than in any other class. The first half of this class was incredibly frustrating as you're bombarded by readings and the specific writing style he wants from you. Participate in class a little bit and ask questions in office hours and you'll do fine.

Lindsey is a funny guy. As long as you ATTEND office hours, do your readings before your class, listen to his feedback on your essays, and attend class, you will be perfectly fine. The essays are tough, and he does look for a particular essay style, which can make it difficult; however, he gives good feedback on essays, and office hours help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Lindsey was one of my favorite professors this semester! I always looked forward to going to this class, because he's such a smart and funny and quirky dude. My writing definitely improved over the course of the semester too. Prof. Lindsey is super caring and down to Earth, highly recommend him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I deeply regret taking this class. Prof. Lindsey is the definition of a professor who is looking for something unreasonably specific in his essays. I have never felt more forced to overthink my writing and complicate it to a point where it no longer makes sense. This class has added so much stress to my life. Take literally any other MHS course.

I might be a little bias because Prof Lindsey is also my advisor, but this was the first time I was able to take a class with him. He really is student oriented. Aims for each of his students to have success inside and outside of his classroom.

Lectures were unhelpful and off-topic. His requirements were SO ridiculously specific and forced me to write in a way that was unnatural and caused every essay to take me so much longer than it should have. You definitely have to do all the readings but they are interesting (the only part of the class I enjoyed). This class was time-consuming.

I have always hated writing but I LOVED this class! He makes class very engaging & interesting, and he clearly cares about his students a lot. Papers are pretty straightforward and not harshly graded. Just make sure to stay on top of your readings and participate in class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Lindsey was an incredible professor- the class was heavily discussion based and he really valued everybody's contribution even if he didn't agree with what they were saying. Incredible writing feedback! So passionate about writing and helping us improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall a very solid professor. He somewhat forces you to write in a style that he likes, but if you do that the grades will be good. The papers aren't long but he really pushes analysis so still takes time to do them right. Very good lecturer and he has a way of getting the class engaged. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor, great class. He is really enthusiastic and engaged, making it easy to get inspired by the course material. He expects quality work, but it isn't so much. I will say though, that this class is mostly about race, and a little about gender, which is fine but we barely covered how these topics connect to medicine (the class 'topic').

One of the craziest and most interesting prof's I've had at Vanderbilt.  He's really energetic, and lectures rarely stay on topic.  Really helpful in office hours and mainly focused on the depth of analysis in papers, so if you put in the effort you will get an A.

The most confusing professor I have ever encountered. He is very confused in his own mind and therefore does not come across clearly in lectures or assignments. His grading is tough and difficult to understand what he wants. He is very smart and always willing to talk with you. If you are not a very strong writer, do not take this class.
He's the man. Inspired me to take pride in my writing. Also is really hilarious in lecture, and the class had a lot of interesting discussions. Definitely recommend for all MHS majors
Good for CORE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Oliveira-Monte was great! I had little to no knowledge about Brazil whatsoever, but I learned so much from this writing course. There were 6 short papers and a final paper and project. Everything we talked about was fun and/or very interesting. The professor was incredibly nice and caring towards her students. Definitely would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Such an interesting and easy class. I learned so much about Brazil but never had to stress about my grades. The readings are manageable (about 15-20 pages due every class period). Each reading comes with discussion questions, so you can easily skim the readings but still understand the main ideas. Super lenient grader. Take this for your FYWS!

Great professor, you can tell that she cares a lot about her students. I learned so much in this class. Lenient grader. My only complaint is that we had to buy a text book only to use it once in class.

My FYWS very first semester and my memory is slightly foggy - basically all lectures with two presentations (1 group 1 solo). You gotta be invested/interested and participate or it will be boring. Lenient grader IMO. Really friendly, great smile and sense of humor. Go to office hours and she'll review your paper with you.

Professor Ornes is great. The class really cuts to the meat of what's important in science communication. His projects are really useful for building communication skills across different mediums. It would have been helpful to know earlier what the grade breakdowns were, since you get just a letter for each assignment: A = 96, A- = 91, B+ = 88, etc

The professor is a tough grader, and you have to put in a lot of work to get an A. Assignments take a while, and there are typically discussions due before every class. In this class, you are required to interview 4+ professionals in specific fields, which can be challenging. However, he is exceptionally knowledgeable on science writing and kind!

He is the GOAT of science writing but I will say some of the assignments are very difficult due to the fact you have to interview scientists. He will just give you a letter grade, so you won't know your final grade until the very end of the year. Overall though, your writing will improve

Prof knows a ton abt science writing and journalism. We had 5 pieces that were graded fairly and short discussion posts due before class w readings. You could def skim all readings, lectures are light and discussion-based. Had to make a podcast and interview random scientists which is outside of my comfort zone but valuable experience.

Although there was a lot of writing and due dates tended to sway quite frequently, the class was great. Ornes is very interwoven with the scientific writing field, and every class was enjoyable. He gave great feedback on the papers although grades were tough but fair.

Dr. Ornes will give you a really great overview of science communication in 2100, but you will have to do a lot of work for it. Some deadlines for projects that relied on interviewing multiple scientists were a bit tight, but Ornes will move them around if need be. This class was more writing intensive than my W class was, so keep that in mind.

I learned a lot in this class. Found the books on Library Genesis, but did not read. Very structured and you can tell he has been teaching for a while, yet still cheery and kind. Goes over types of science writing; news articles, research highlights, book reviews, then we go over the structure and write our own. Short discussion posts due weekly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is actually for CSET 2200, and the second class I have taken with Dr. Ornes. He is GREAT. He is understanding about deadlines but still excepts high-quality work. He will work with you, is very helpful, and has a background in science journalism. I would highly, HIGHLY recommend him.

Great overview of science communication from projects where you select the topics, and cool guest speakers (1 was the guy from Radio Lab!) However, Ornes is a procrastinator and often doesn't post stuff till the night before. He is very unclear about assignments and grading (no percentages, he'll literally just give a letter and your like... okay).

Cool guy with lots of experience in sci journalism. Lots of projects, which can be time consuming, but aren't difficult. Just make sure you don't procrastinate. Got to do some cool interviews and write about interesting topics. Will give extensions if you just ask about it. Clear grading criteria, but sometimes he over-emphasizes replicating style.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Ornes is really nice but expects a lot for this class. There are a total of 6 papers/projects so it's back to back the whole semester. He also expects you to interview researchers which can take additional time/effort so you can't procrastinate. Other than that, he grades pretty easily if you meet the criteria and is pretty accessible if needed

Professor Ornes' intro to CSET class wasn't anything remarkable. While he is extremely accomodating and likable, the 3 hour class period is simply too long for material that is relatively easy. It's an easy A if you're good at writing, making podcasts, and video editing. There's a ton of reading hw that he never goes over, but brings up randomly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a Cs major, I found this class boing. The Thursday 3 hour block class was a nightmare. I didn't feel like I was learning much new stuff in the lectures. Prof Ornes is super understanding and nice tho. He gives a lot of handouts, example articles. If you want to improve your writing and email him to get feedback, I'm sure he'll be responsive.

Dr. Ornes is a great professor and CSET2100 is an amazing class. I would highly recommend it to any person interested in science or science policy. I learned SO much valuable information in this class pertaining to communication as a career, improved my writing, and got to research such interesting topics. Would 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ornes is super passionate about science writing and about being there for his students and making us better science writers. He gives great feedback and does a good job of explaining assignments. The class is really interesting and engaging and my science writing skills have definitely gotten much better.

He is passionate about making us better science writers, but he sometimes focuses too much on having us emulate his preferred style. There is a decent workload with all the writing assignments because they are not normal academic papers. Additionally, get ready to have to interview people. Overall a solid class; be prepared to work for an A.

This class is once a week for 2.5 hours and it is so worth it. Ornes teaches the content super well and makes the class engaging so it doesnt even feel that long. None of the work is graded harshly enough so that you do poorly but you will need to put effort in for the full A. Overall great class and professor, highly recommend
An interesting class and professor for anyone interested in science/science journalism. His class isn't an easy A, but it's not much work for 3 credit hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Ornes is obviously enthusiastic about science writing and it really shows during his lectures. Expect to do a project almost every week, including essays, news features, videos, and podcasts. There's one big create your own project at the end of the semester in place of a formal final exam. If you love science, takes this class!

Took his AI and Society class which was mostly discussion-based. There was a paper and some projects here and there, but he's an easy grader and the class is really chill. Learned a lot about AI ethics and different AI tools. He really wants you to think critically about how we use AI to learn, not as a replacement for ourselves.
Very chill prof. Good choice for core

Dr. Molvig is an incredible professor. CSET 2100 is a fantastic class if you want to learn more about podcasting, video editing, AI, or VR. The best classes were those with strong attendance and good discussions, and Dr. Molvig is always ready for a discussion about almost any topic. He's a kind, funny guy who knows how to teach. Highly recommend.
Dr. Molvig's writing seminar was a joy to be in, and i'll be sure to take another class with him eventually. Easiest grader you'll find at Vanderbilt. Great lectures and trips around campus.

Dr. Molvig is an engaging lecturer and has a deep knowledge of the history of science. He makes the effort to help freshmen adapt to Vandy and explore cool places/topics (VU's data center, Einstein deepfake he made). Essays are alright and his comments help with revisions. Very flexible (canceled final paper for presentation due to time crunch).
Class discussions were so much fun! Professor Molvig was a great professor and obviously cares about his students. Projects were very open-ended.

As someone who had 5 majors in his undergraduate years, professor Molvig definitely knows a lot and has a lot to say not only about the class content but also just life in general. Class discussions are all over the place in the best way possible and assignments give you a lot of room to express your ideas. A pretty chill class overall.

This class was very difficult and I would not take it without prior knowledge of Unity or coding. It was very interesting and cool to work in VR, but the professors did not do a great job teaching us how to use Unity, so I had to rely on my peers and Youtube. I'm not really sure how I got an A, but it is not easy at all without experience.

Great class with the occasional big paper/project. You can tell he's here to teach history, not dates and names and events, and he strongly encourages student participation but not in a badgering way. Discussions/reading are straightforward in expectation, and the class TAs were easily the best I've ever had and could've run the class themselves.

Fantastic professor. I had him for a history of science W course, and the class was incredibly interesting. When everything went online for the pandemic mid-semester, he was very understanding and adapted well. He made class engaging, so I kept learning but never felt stressed. He cares about students and teaches well. 10/10 highly recommend

He's a really good guy. He cares about his students, and since we were a first-year only class, he takes significant time out of classes to talk about college in general. He made the topic interesting. There are 3 papers due, but he grades leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took Molvig for my first-year writing seminar and absolutely loved the class. Comprised of three books and three papers on them, with a few other minor grades. First two papers can be revised. Molvig is super knowledgeable on the topics he covers and he's an amazing person. Reading wasn't a lot until the last book on Einstein.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Molvig is awesome. He's super passionate about tech, as well as the value liberal arts can contribute to innovation. Participation and doing the (very interesting) readings is a must. Only other work is a 10 pg paper. The class also definitely changed my life like no other at Vandy, in terms of inspiring me to build a startup one day.

Ole is a good lecturer overall, but there are some caveats. He outlines the events in nonchronological order which can be confusing. Grading is based on two midterm take-home papers, a final project, and class participation. Class participation (25%!) is graded mercilessly and points are arbitrarily taken off papers, but the class is decent overall
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Highly recommend prof. Molvig. Lectures are extremely interesting if you're into the subject matter. Do the readings .

Dr. Molvig's class was fascinating. He obviously loves the subject material and shares an interesting perspective on it. There were  two papers, and weekly discussion posts which weren't at all difficult. There's a lot of reading though, and you should do it for the discussion, and also because it's just neat. Coolest professor I've had here so far
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite Vanderbilt professor so far. He's a chill guy, teaches really cool topics (in my opinion), and grades fairly. Expect to read a lot though.

Makes the class interesting, and it's not a ton of work. He assigns a lot of reading you don't have to do. The final is the only test of the semester and it's hard to gauge what will be on it, but he's a really nice guy and always willing to answer any questions.

Really nice guy with really confusing lectures. Mentions a lot of things you'll never need to know for the final and you have no idea what you're expected to know until he gives out the review guide. Overall the class was interesting with minimal work (2 essays, weekly blackboard posts, and a final). Not super easy, not hard.

Professor Molvig is amazing. He's really interested in what he does, and likes students who are involved in class discussions. There is a lot of reading, but I guess that is expected from a higher level class. Overall, highly recommend!

Prof Molvig is very good at what he does. His lectures are interesting and actually engaging, he encourages participation and discussion, and he understands his students. The readings assigned usually aren't too bad; when they are, he understands and goes over the difficult points accordingly. You can't go wrong with taking one of his classes.
Professor Molvig's class is the easiest class I've had this semester and the one I've learned the most from.  Course load is not bad, go to class and read and you'll be golden.
This was honestly the worst class. Prof Molevig lectures by reading what seems like an essay hes written at some point in his career. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. So painfully boring and not an easy A
Prof. Molvig is one of the best professors I've had at Vandy. He really cares about his students and makes class interesting. He is incredibly helpful if you go to office hours.
Volgy is amazing. He is very smart, great educator. He has a thick accent but v intelligent and reminds me of a Habsburg Emperor.

Very clear grading standards. He wants you to do well and not have to take his really hard final exam. The homework can be hard, but he is very helpful after class. Attendance is optional except for classwork days, but he really appreciates people being there (sometimes he gives us homework answers for attending lecture).

His modern programming class isn't super intensive but the material is pretty interesting. Homework and exams are pretty straightforward, and you can have a lot of fun with the final project and you get a lot of time. Highly recommend his class.

Professor Volgyesi is very knowledgeable and seems to greatly enjoy teaching his students. As others have mentioned, you can do the bare minimum and not learn much and still do okay in the class. However, if you decide to take it seriously and attend lectures, use him as a resource, etc, you will learn a ton. The project is also a cool experience.

This class is exactly as difficult as you make it. Volgyesi goes into great depth on Rust, and you can take away a lot from this class. His lectures are lovely, and he is literally the nicest guy I've ever met. It is not difficult to succeed in this course; anyone who has taken it knows why. But, there is no shortage of depth in its study of Rust.

A thorough class that teaches many important aspects of Rust. The majority of the course is dedicated towards learning Rust. The last few lectures are based around showcasing different projects that can be made using Rust (webdev, cli, etc.), and then you will build your own project. Homework and exams are straightforward. Excellent course.
80% HW, 20% attendance, only really have to attend class once a week for classwork days. Chill class, nice professor.
daddy

Volgyesi is the best. Super clear lectures that are easy to refer back to. Learns names of students that participate in class. Nothing on exams is suprising or designed to trick you; everything based on slides. Coding assignments are graded clearly with GitHub actions so you can know your grade as soon as you submit. Smooth and informative class.
Grade was 80% Programming Assignments and 20% weekly classwork assignments. PAs never took too long.

Dr. Volgyesi is what I wish all computer science professors are like. Optional final if do all hw and classwork -> easy A. He is really knowledgeable and is more than happy to help. He is a bit quirky because hes a stickler for formatted code but I have found it to only help. Hes also a funny dude with his phrases he uses. Really really great prof
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Volgyesi is a gem. He understands his students and understands how to make his students better at not only programming, but analytical thinking. Roughly 75% of the class is based on programming assignments (which can be tricky, but are manageable). The other 25% is the classwork grade, which is easy to complete if you show up to class.

Professor Volgyesi is an amazing teacher! I learned a lot from his class. Grading wasn't horrible and he's super clear about what is required. No tests, just classwork (completion grade), quizzes, and homework. Highly recommend this class for DS or SC minor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Volgyesi is fantastic. Took him for the scientific computing minor, and he made me glad to be pursuing the minor simply because it got me to study with him. SUPER accessible outside of class (always responds to emails quickly, even on weekends) and genuinely is a fun guy to study with. Grading wasn't too hard, and I learned a TON!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of Vanderbilt's best professors. Jump at any chance to take class with him.
Best dude ever
This class helps you learn a lot! The work is manageable and Peter is always willing to help. Take it and you wont regret it!

Volgyesi is a cool and funny guy, on top of being a solid prof. His lectures are very clear and he's helpful if you need it. The grading is very fair, and there are a few opportunities for EC as well. He certainly knows his stuff and you come away with a good grasp on Python. One of the most useful classes I've taken at vandy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 2204 might sound like another 1101, but it's far from it. Even though lecture slides are posted online and the majority of people skip class (sound familiar?) the online slides are nowhere near good enough to use as your only study resource. As someone who never went and payed the price I'll say it here - GO TO CLASS. Otherwise, kiss an A goodbye.

Dr. Volgyesi is one of the most helpful professors i've had at Vanderbilt. He really knows the material and cares that you learn. Tests were straightforward, 5 programming assignments were not bad except for one, final is all multiple choice. Overall pretty easy to get an A as long as you show up and put in some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I had at Vanderbilt! He cared about students understanding the material and applications of what we were learning. He also based the tests off of what we actually went over in class, so I would highly recommend going although its not mandatory. The grading is composed of a few programming assignments and 4 exams.

Professor Volgyesi knows what he is doing. His lectures are very good and bring the content in a easy-to-understand way. Together with the homeworks, both teach you how to become a good Python programmer. Even if you don't have experience with Python, I still recommend this class, as there are many intro classes in the beginning.

He is by far the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt! The homework was always enjoyable and really helped refine skills learned in class and you really get exactly what you put into the class back. I went overboard and sought out to learn every little thing I could in this class, but I don't regret it one bit. 10/10!! would definitely recommend.

Solid (and possibly the only) choice for the class. Really knows what he is teaching, is really enthusiastic about the subject matter, and is very upfront and to-the-point. A few programming HW that takes up a large chunk of your grade, three somewhat challenging exams and a reasonable multiple-choice final. Need I say more/

Good choice--class is majority based on homework, with 3 small tests and a multiple choice final. It's not too bad, especially if you have any background in Python (the first month or so is "intro python", followed by some very simple data structures and some scientific computing). Pretty easy, you'll learn a lot, Volgyesi is a chill and smart prof

Dr. Pardini is a really great professor who cares about knowing his students. The class is really heavy on watching movies/reading, so make sure you do that if it's assigned outside of class. He is clear in his assignments and all of his grading is very fair.

He's a great guy but doesn't really give you information about specifics for projects or papers. He either spends the whole class rambling and lecturing or expects you to participate but very easy class and minimal homework and assignments.
Pardini is really easy.  He is also a pretty good lecturer.  Take him over anyone else.

Samuele Pardini is just pretty awesome.  I feel fairly comfortable with the Italian language after just one semester, and it was a lot of fun each class.  He's helpful, funny, smart, and a clear speaker.  Unless you're terrible with foreign languages, you should enjoy the class and I strongly recommend it. it's also pretty easy comparatively

Professor Pardini is a great professor. He really breaks down the language and makes the learning extremely easy. He is a joker, which makes class really fun. The homework isn't too bad. If you want an awesome professor to teach you Italian, choose Professor Pardini.
Oh my goodness. Samuele is the best professor ever, and SO HOT.
Samuele was great! He's really helpful, his tests and quizzes are pretty easy, and the daily homework isn't too bad. Take Samuele, he's awesome.
Samuele is amazing... There aren't enough kind words to describe this man... He's the****
Samuele is such a great teacher, he is so much fun and makes the class enjoyable. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

Professor Quarry is an amazing lecturer. I enjoyed Reading Fiction and all the writing assignments that came with it. The novels we read were interesting, and class discussions were fun. However, very strict attendance. Overall, highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Quarry is a great prof; kind, and gives great advice for those who are new to writing fictional worlds. This class is not difficult, and the workload is incredibly manageable. This class is entirely analogue, but I never thought that was a bad thing. The assignments are reasonable and are often graded on effort. Take it if you need a W class.

A genuinely nice teacher and gives good feedback for the class. However, it's a no laptop/tech class so you have to print everything to the point everyone in the class ran out of money. Really strict with receiving hand copies of your written work. Other than that great guy but I'll try not to catch a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super chill class. Lots of reading at the beginning but the last month and a half is reserved for working on your final project where you write your own story and final presentations. Super caring prof who gives good feedback. Isn't looking for the best fiction writing ever, just looking for effort and improvement.

Professor Quarry is a wonderful professor. He leaves good feedback on papers and class time is not a total waste because much of the in-class discussions are very helpful towards how you will approach reading responses and papers.

Professor Quarry has my heart. I always looked forward to going to his class. I have since taken many of his upper level classes, and I seriously don't get tired of him and am always learning something new, even in his three hour classes. By far the best writing professor at Vandy. He's caring and gives great feedback!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Quarry is nice and wants to help his students become better writers. Our final grades were based on participation, 3 reading responses, and 3 essays. We read some strange books that I did not enjoy, but participating in class was easy. He graded harsher at the beginning of the semester. Glad I took it for my W!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I LOVE PROFESSOR QUARRY! this class consisted of critiques and participation, in class journals, and 2 essays that you edit after hearing critiques for the final exam. He provides a lot of insight into the nonfiction writing process and is the reason i decided to continue with english as my second major.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Quarry is one of my favorite professors at vanderbilt. He is very accessible, he can be a tough grader at times but he gives great advice on what to improve on in your writing. He gives many fair opportunities for assignments. The class consists of participation credit, reading responses and 3 essays. I 100% recommend taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Graded on writing critique letters to classmates, class discussion, two big essays, revisions of the big essays (final), and keeping up with journal prompts and writing activities. He gives a lot of time in class for feedback and thoughtful help and encouragement. He genuinely cares about your writing and facilitates good discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice professor, approachable if you have any concerns/questions for your essay. But his grading might be tough in the beginning, but he is willing to help you to improve your writing as the class goes on. Def not an easy A for someone who cannot write well (like me), but as you gradually know his expectation for your paper u'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You write 2 1500-2500 word essays that are reviewed by peers, and you review every peer's 2 essays. Low workload. JQ is caring but strict with participation. Easy A class as long as you care to attend and participate, but still is the class that has most improved my writing. He is friendly, hilarious, and tremendously helpful. Take this class.

Prof Quarry was a great person and awesome professor! Participation really matters and you have to do the readings. While the class was interesting, he was a really tough grader with papers. He had you relay heavily on the writing studio to get feedback, but if that wasn't helpful (and sometimes it wasn't) then it becomes very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Quarry cares about his students and is available for feedback. As long as you follow his instructions and guidelines, the essays aren't too difficult. Attendance + participation is mandatory for an A. Lots of reading at first, but then transitions into interesting comic books and short stories. Excellent professor, lots of interesting discussions.

Prof. Q, can be a tough grader. You need to be attending every class as it has a huge impact on you grade. Out of all my papers it seems like the last was easiest, but sometimes it is tough to know how much effort he wants out of you. Not an easy A, but easier in comparison to other ENGL professors. Make sure to participate and ask him questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thought this class was going to be easy, but it is NOT EASY. He is a tough grader on papers and he is not very clear in his grading criteria. Class is boring and he wants you to participate a ton. Graded heavily on participation and papers. NOT FUN

He's a teacher that will actually teach you how to write! The readings are cool (The Walking Dead, Dracula, etc.), and he's very accessible for writing feedback. Discussions really had me thinking differently about literature.

Dr. Quarry is a good guy and takes care in delivering a well-structured English class. He mixes discussion with telling the class what he thinks the story is about. I know that is not an easy task but he tends to the side of just telling us what he thinks the story is about. I appreciate that he is open to new ideas in our essays and readings.

Professor Quarry is a brilliant and compelling teacher. He genuinely empathizes with students and made class during COVID-19 unintimidating and enjoyable. He grades fairly, has clear expectations, and will tangibly improve your writing ability through workshopping. I finished his class on monsters genuinely thinking differently about society.

Easy intro writing class. Topic was on Monsters in Literature. Prof Quarry really nice and caring. Always goes over readings in depth in class making sure everyone is on the same page. Reading pretty much every day but not too much. 3 papers. Grades super easy

Never had this man as a prof, but wish I had--my entire college experience would have been changed. I contacted him after reading one of his articles, and his voice is one desperately needed at Vanderbilt. "Coming Out as Working Class" should be required reading for all members of the Vandy community and universities everywhere.

I took Quarry for Creative Writing: the craft of worldbuilding. This class was unfortunately just a Lit class disguised as a Writing course (but that may change going forward). Quarry is, however, a fun teacher and leads good discussions. He does care about you proofing papers more than some other teachers.

Professor Quarry is a truly incredible professor. I've taken several of his classes and decided to major in English because of them. If you want to take a class you're actually going to learn something in, and not just try to get an A (although that's completely do-able) take any of his workshops.

I liked Quarry for his monsters in fiction class a lot. That said, in his intermediate writing workshop, he leaves a lot to be desired. He lets his own personal biases reflect in your work, is harsh with his grading, and has expectations only hurt the motivation of aspiring writers. I'd wait for someone else to teach this class before taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Quarry is super into the craft of writing- students that care about writing and bring a fresh perspective are the ones he tends to focus on.  He's really clear with rules of class attendance and grading.  If you get less than a B it's because you didn't show up or turned stuff in late.
Sweetest guy ever. He really takes time to get to know his students and is young enough to be still going places. Vanderbilt is lucky to have him.

Most amazing and kind professor I have had at Vanderbilt. Pushed me to become a better writer. Interesting lectures and easy, captivating reading material. One of the best classes I have taken at Vanderbilt and a truly inspiring, awesome professor
Best teacher ever.  He cares, he ACTUALLY gives feedback, easy and interesting reads, he buys food, class flies by... what more can you ask for?

Professor Quarry is a genuinely nice guy and really cares about all his students. The class is discussion-based, so no lectures, just group conversations about the readings. Very willing to give feedback on papers before you turn them in. Readings are entertaining. Brought us food occasionally. Overall a really laid back, caring guy

Although my section was "the silent class", he really tried to get every student engaged and interested in what was being taught. He knew he had a bunch of premeds just taking a class to fulfill credit, but made it interesting and tried to get everyone to enjoy it. Great books, nice guy, clear grader and lecturer.

Forget seminars, take Quarry's Monsters in Fiction course for your writing req. His picks for readings are great, and his feedback on essays is always super helpful. Between the prof and the material, this is without a doubt my favorite course this semester.

Professor Quarry is awesome.  I'm in a class with only 9 students in it and it's so great.  He takes the time to get to know all of his students and he really wants the best for you.  He is super accessible and there are no tests in this class.  I would absolutely recommend taking this class!

Professor Quarry is the BEST as he gives personalized, typed feedback for essays to EACH STUDENT.  Expectations are crystal clear, he gives workshops and peer editing sessions.  Class FLIES by, he's super engaging, and his monster-literature based class is a wonderful shake up of the usual boring English.  Teacher of the year award.

Prof Quarry is a great guy.He really cares about his students and creates interesting class discussions. I feel like I learned so much in this class without being stressed about the work load. Also, the books are great and easy reads.

Favorite workshop so far and one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. Quarry challenges the limits of your imagination and gives thorough, super helpful feedback on your stories. Be sure to go to his office hours--he gives great advice one-on-one, too, whether about what you're working on or writing after college. Top-notch guy!

Professor Quarry is knowledgable, certainly, but the workshop didn't always feel like the most loving place. There was a lot of competition to seem "smart" and a lot of personal comments towards authors that Prof Quarry did not stop. If you're thick skinned then it probably won't matter to you, but any sensitive souls should beware.

Professor Quarry chose interesting texts, gave fair reading assignments, and was crystal clear about what he wanted in the (3) essays we had to write. He really tries to make class interesting and fun--he even brought cookies on halloween and pizza one day at the end of the year just to be nice. he rocks

This guy is the least understanding professor I've ever had. Doesn't allow for minor mistakes or corrections in your work, doesn't believe you when you have legitimate excuses for missing a class. I was really excited for this class, and I ended up hating it.

One of the best professors I’ve had at Vandy, maybe the very best.  He’s very relatable and treats everyone with respect, and you can tell he’s invested in his students not just as students but as people too, which motivated me to work even harder for him.  He’s entertaining also.  I don’t usually like English classes, but this one was a blast.
AWESOME CLASS, AWESOME GUY!! Very personable and great reads in class. Also, helpful when it comes to specific questions and great office hours. A MUST TAKE for AXLE!
Favorite class of my first semester at Vanderbilt.  Wish I could have him again.
He picks interesting books and is extremely helpful. Not a hard grader and takes into account what year you are.
He's a demanding grader, but his book selections are great, and class discussions are usually really interesting.  Take this to meet your W requirement!

His comments on writing pieces are not valid and he is very misleading.  He is not encouraging on papers at all whatsoever and does not choose relevant essay topics for the stories and novels read in class.  It is also frustrating that instead of actually teaching about English he refers directly to a grammar book.
So nice and approachable!  He really cares about his students and is easy to keep in touch with even after the semester.  He doesn't give many As, so but it's not impossible.  Favorite workshop!
Good professor, but he gives you a lot of work.  Understanding, good sense of humor, encourages you to come to office hours.

Quarry is one of the most approachable, most invested professors I've had at Vanderbilt.  He's also one of the most challenging, though getting an A in his class isn't impossible?however you have to make writing a priority if you want one.  Grading is somewhat unclear, but then so has it been in basically every workshop I've been in at Vanderbilt.

A truly nice professor. He's friendly, welcoming, and he really enjoys when his students participate in the class. He's also free in office hours. But his grading is horrible. He thinks a B is an above-average grade, and worst of all he doesn't give you you grades during the semester, so you don't know if you're failing. If you want an A, forget it
The LEBRON JAMES of Vanderbilt
Had him for my discussion and I wished attendance wasn't required because it felt like I was wasting my time and learned nothing every week.

I was enjoying my summer vacation and suddenly Quan Chen popped into my head and it ruined my entire mood and destroyed my rare day at the Jekyll Island resort and beach so I had to come here and warn the younglings.

The rudest, sassiest professor ever. It doesn't get worse than Quan Chen. I would go to his office hours to try and understand what was going on because his lectures were so complicated, and he would just laugh at me and tell me I shouldn't take any more math. He never taught how to do anything that was on the exams either, we had to figure it out.

I came to Vanderbilt thinking that they would have a better cohort of professors who provide a better learning experience compared to other schools. Obviously, this was not true. Glad to say I will be transferring to a different college for the rest of my undergrad.

I made an account to write a review about Quan. I have never been part of a worse course in my entire life. This professor shouldn't even have a job at a community college. I think my six-year old sister couldve taught this class (and she speaks english). She will be submitting her resume and I demand the school hire her as his replacement.

Terrible professor. Lectures are super boring. I didn't learn anything going there the whole year. Notes are really bad and don't help with the homework at all. Overall it would've been better if I just learned DiffEq through YouTube lectures. If he doesn't curve the final by at least 20% then I'm gonna crash out because I've failed all his exams.
I had Dr. Ying for multi and he was so much better of a professor compared to Dr. Chen. I think maybe if he gets a couple more years of experience, he'll be a better professor
His lectures are ok. I think he's a great professor that knows a lot of math. I think his exams are sort of structured unfairly and unnecessarily difficult though
i didn't wear my seatbelt on the airplane after coming back from spring break in hopes that I would die before having to come back to his class again.
I hate mathematics now that I took his class.

Interesting guy but my dead dog could teach diff eq better than this man. Only good part was when he pushed back our exam that one time but that's about it. I'd rather nose dive into a porta-potty and take a big bite of diarrhea soup than take his class again
Discussion was intolerable and most of the time seemed to not help anyone in the room. If attendance wasn't required, I wouldn't have gone at all.
jackie chan ahh professor
KWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOON CHENNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN
His English name shall be... Tim
He sounds like Kevin Hart if Kevin Hart was chinese
Such is life.
Chat is this professor real
i did all the suggested problems and Dr. Chen told me during office hours that they were all useless and pointless. WHY ARE THEY SUGGESTED THEN
I don't think Dr. Chen is as bad as what a lot of people here are saying. However, I guess I can't read most of the reviews, so who knows
what the heck are these reviews lmao. nevertheless, I agree with them.
My boy Quan Chen's got his own people hating on him dawg that's all i gotta say
I don't learn anything with this professor.
Don't take him. Please
He's not that bad I'm not sure why everyone is hating.
I think he's not too bad for someone who speaks English as a second language. Nevertheless Idk what he's saying.
His attendance policy is insane. You have to be there every class or you lose points.
Very fast when going over practice problems. It's like he expects we know them already. He reminds me of my abusive father.
Don't listen to the previous reviews, he's not that bad. He's worse.
i accidentally said he's Korean and he took 5 points off my grade.
I'm Chinese and I still don't like him.
He got really angry at me for pronouncing his name wrong. Apparently its supposed to be chyuan or something and not Kwan and it was my first time crying since my mommy spanked me when I was 7
I thought he was kinda hot but after a while I realized that he truly doesn't care about me. I think I'll go back to white guys.
He would rather take five big men up himself than let you turn in your test early.
This is the worst professor ever. Bad is an understatement.

Chen was the leader of my discussion section. You could tell he did not want to be there and was rude when questions were asked about the content. Going to discussion for 55 minutes every week actively lowered the quality of my day.

The professor primarily taught from the textbook but presented the material out of order, making it very confusing. Asking questions during lectures did little to help understanding. The discussion TA did a much better job explaining the material and answering questions, to the point of her office hours being packed with confused students. Avoid.

It was his 1st semester teaching, so he can improve, but this class sucked. For a class with only engineers, there was a lot of theory. No online notes, at all, we asked for them too. I think he cares and wants to improve but when you ask a question it is hard to get a real answer that makes sense. Followup questions are a fruitless attempt.

AVOID!! Professor Chen made it clear on day one that he did not want to teach this class and every day that was made more abundantly clear. Extremely difficult final exam with an average of ~65 and NO CURVE. The class itself is not bad, just take it with anyone else

So sweet, hilarious, and genuinely cares about her students. If you have never taken Chinese before (which was the case for me)-- beware for a tough first part of the semester as she doesn't give much context to how characters work within the language. However, I have seriously enjoyed her class so much and will always speak highly of her!

Wei laoshi is super sweet, engaging in class, and wants you to do well! The class itself involves a lot of memorizing characters and studying but it is doable if you put in the effort. Definitely take her class if you are looking to take Chinese.

I came into this class illiterate in Chinese which made me worried about my GPA. While this class is definitely a lot of reading and memorizing different characters (~400), Wei laoshi's amazing teaching makes it better. It takes 1-2 hours of time every class and tests are challenging but I've gotten way better at Chinese. Take it if you can!

Heritage Chinese is designed for Chinese-Americans. If you can't conduct a conversation in Chinese, this class will be difficult. Daily, easy memorization quizzes on vocab, essay + presentation every week. Classes are very chill, you basically just do the textbook. Tests are difficult for those inexperienced in Mandarin, but doable. Prepare well.

If I could have Wei laoshi every semester I absolutely would!  She is nice, caring, loves her students and her jobs, and so passionate about everyone doing well. Minimal homework but a decent amount of studying is required to recognize and write characters, and speaking practice.  I entered not knowing a word, and left holding basic conversations!

Wei Laoshi makes learning one of the hardest languages in the world seem manageable. I was really worried about taking an advanced Chinese course (I didnt want to ruin my GPA) but if you try in her class its not bad at all. Maybe a little extra work, but she really does care about practical use and understanding. Really recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Wei laoshi is excellent--she's been pivotal in developing my Chinese language skills, and I'm really excited to continue taking classes with her! The copious amounts of homework are necessary, but she and Guo laoshi are very considerate and plan the course in its entirety from the start. CHIN 2201 & 2202 were great experiences, and I'm so thankful.
love her so much. chinese in general is work and a time commitment, but she makes it more fun! definitely try to get her out of all the chinese teachers
love her so much. chinese in general is work and a time commitment, but she makes it more fun!

Lots of work, but that's mostly because of the Chinese language itself being a lot of work. Biweekly character quizzes, character writing, and workbook problems for homework. Professor Wei is a great teacher who explains things clearly and has a very relaxed class environment.
