Super sweet lady, who's fairly lenient with grading and definitely wants to help you improve your Chinese. Quizzes are a little harder under her than the other Chinese teacher (Liu laoshi), but they also help you contextualize the vocabulary so its definitely for the better. Overall, very nice and is there to help.

Definitely the best Chinese professor at Vanderbilt. Wei laoshi is super sweet and has a great sense of humor; she makes going to class enjoyable! That being said, it is a language class, so there's a lot of work involved to keep up, but it's not terrible.
Wei laoshi is by far the best Chinese professor. She is hilarious, sweet, and very understanding. I really enjoyed going to her class.

Professor Wei is so sweet! If you really think that something is too difficult or if you think she assigned too much work, she will adjust the course so that it really fits the level of the class. There is a good amount of homework each week, but it is doable and is not arbitrary unnecessary .
Doesn't teach the grammar well or how to use the vocab in a sentence, as if expecting us to automatically know how to idiomatically use the vocab, but still very nice and pleasant
Great professor. Wei Laoshi is very helpful and clear. Chinese is not an easy subject so you should expect a lot of work. But if you want to take Chinese, definitely take her.

Wei Laoshi is understanding, and always there to help; however, the Asian Studies professors treat this course like it is your only class, and it is A LOT to take on, especially if you are taking other difficult classes/ a lot of hours. I wouldn't recommend taking this class unless you have a background in the language. Tests are brutal.

Wei Laoshi is incredibly helpful! Definitely made Chinese class accessible and a lot of fun. This class is not for the faint of heart, though. You HAVE TO study, otherwise you're screwed. However, it's not overwhelming. If you even have a remote interest in Chinese, make sure to take Wei's class.

Great teacher! Helps students out when they don't understand. Daily quizzes can sometimes be tough, but it's doable. Just make sure you know the vocabulary and write out the essays before every test and you'll do well. Overall, fun class, very interactive, and you'll learn a lot if you work hard.

definitely top pick for chinese professors. extremely clear in class and is always entertaining. she is so willing to help and understands if you have any issues getting things turned in on time. the daily quizzes can be a little annoying but they're not hard

AMAZING professor.  SHe makes learning chinese fun.  She has a great sense of humor and wants everyone to do well.  Learning chinese is tough, but if you are up for the challenge, definitely get her! Quizzes are easy, tests can be pretty tough. Be prepared to do many oral presentations.

Awesome class!  She will make it worthwhile for you-always willing to help you and VERY lenient in terms of grading.  She also tries to accommodate to your schedule when it comes to quizzes/hw.  Overall and awesome professor!

Amazing professor, she really wants to see all  of her students do well. She is always willing to go out of her way to help you with extra time and provide extra practice. Tests are not bad, a lot of quizes on characters (most you can study right before and do fine). Oral exams are a little rough but overall grading is fair. Interactive class!
Sweet and helpful
She has a smooth manner and a great sense of humor. Makes practicing Chinese fun.

Dr.Quincy is an incredibly caring individual, and while the assignments could be quite difficult, going to office hours for only a few minutes makes everything so much more bearable. Her low ratings are definitely more of a reflection of student laziness, because while the class is definitely challenging, she is straight forward with what she wants

I love professor Quincy. Read the syllabus when its given and plan out your work. There are six assignments that are not graded on completion and while the final paper is hard if you have not run a regression before she will help you so much if you just go to office hours. She's super friendly and clearly super knowledgable in her field.

Graded relatively easily but assignments were very time consuming. No tests. Wouldnt take this class if you dont have a background in coding/econometrics. She is a VERY nice person, but she expected too much from us. The final project was way harder than what we learned in class so most people struggled but she ended up being lenient with grading.

Professor Quincy is one of the kindest professors at Vanderbilt. The class has been revamped since all of the poor reviews, so there are no exams which is great. However, the class is still very difficult. While there are no prerequisites, this course is VERY hard to complete without prior econometrics/data science/computer science experience.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Quincy is an amazing profess

Dr. Quincy is exceptional - she is so caring, and she is willing to help you outside of the classroom. The revamped class has zero quizzes and only papers/presentations (which she gives you so much time to work on). Take this class, it seriously wasn't bad at all. It helps that she made the classroom environment fun and enjoyable as well.
Dr. Quincy is a great professor with engaging lectures and meaningful assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The other ratings here are unfair and harsh. This is a good class and incredibly straightforward. Quincy is an incredibly nice person and she is so willing to help anyone outside of class. It is data science heavy which isn't great but you will do well in this class by showing up and completing things.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor really isn't as bad as the other reviews make her out to be. The lectures are fine and she's not boring, but she's just not very good at writing exams or making quizzes that are related to the actual material covered in lecture. However, they're all still pretty easy and getting an A is easy with minimal work and skimming readings.

You go to Vanderbilt. You're probably a smart kid to be taking a 3000 level Econ. You probably think that bad scores on RMP are from slackers who get Ds. You've probably dealt with tough professors in the past and gotten good grades. You have Quincy in your YES cart and are ready to study hard, show up to class, and get an A. Good effing luck

Do not take unless you have lots of knowledge about compute science and basically every upper level econ topic (Econometrics, Money & Banking, etc). She expects way too much of her students and thinks everyone has prior knowledge about all economic topics and how to code. Tests are extremely specific and obscure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Econometrics + History + Research Readings You'll do coding, read a ton, and the tests don't reflect the lectures The class is super hard to follow because she doesn't have a structured lecture. It can either go left or right but has no set direction Her handwriting is also terrible so good luck reading her lecture notes Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If this was some grad-level rocket science course with really challenging material, I wouldn't be upset by challenges. But Professor Quincy manages to turn what should be a straightforward course into something incomprehensible. And even if you manage to decipher what she's trying to teach, none of it will show up on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Just took the first exam in this class. To say that the material included on it was not covered in class is an understatement. Literally half of the exam was not even remotely related to content covered in class. Good luck to anyone trying to do well in this class.

Not good at all at communicating what is expected of students. Assigns way too much reading and quizzes are impossible. Just disappointed this was the only option left for so many students looking for an economics credit. Not worth it at all- just wait until next semester when you have different options of an econ class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She needs to be more structured in her presentations or provide better resources for out of class study, or both, but she does neither. Sometimes, though often enough where it's an actual problem, she's just wrong about definitions. Assigns way too much reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gives out daily quizzes that have literally no correlation to the content covered in lectures. Ridiculously unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The WORST PROFESSOR AT VANDERBILT. Not accessible nor accommodating. Rude. Doesnt know how to lecture. Quizzes on material she doesnt teach. Never take her class. Avoid, avoid, avoid.

Heavy workload, many readings, poor lecture (cannot explain things well enough), hard quizzes (include contents she never touches on in class), illegible handwriting. SHE DESERVES THE 1.1 RATING. DON'T TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Perhaps the worst professor I have ever encountered at Vanderbilt. There is a reason here Rate My Professor score is 1.1
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had at Vanderbilt. Relies on a premise of equitable and fair, yet lacks the empathy necessary to be a professor. The notes in class are not legible and the lectures are often filled with incorrect information.

Her writing is atrocious. Lectures were easy enough to follow but the exams and some parts of the homework assignments were nothing like we learned in class. Grading is very ambiguous because the feedback is so vague. It's hard to improve when you do not understand precisely what you're doing wrong. This class is much harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her notes were hard to follow. Several times she emailed the correct formula after giving the wrong formula in class. She did not seem to have a firm enough grasp on the material to give out challenging exams. In addition, several times I lost points on hw and tests for reasons such as "This is correct but explain further." Explain what further...?

Prof. Quincy should practice her handwriting. Her notes are illegible at best. Confusing lectures. Difficult midterms. Tiny font tests. The wording of the questions on the problem set is often ambiguous, and you get points deducted because you are unsure which value should be used in your calculation. Take it with a grain of salt :).

This class should be extremely easy, the content is simple and its a lower division elective. It is the professor that makes it hard. It is often impossible to understand what the questions in her problem sets are asking, and her lectures are hard to follow both because her hand writing is illegible and because they're mind-numbingly boring.
I cannot read her notes in class. Class does not teach what is on the homework and neither teach what is on the exam.

Hand writing illegible. She writes while talking so the notes she writes always have missing words or just incorrect. She has to write emails to us explaining the mistakes she made, several times! She also doesn't teach what she tests on problem sets and exams. She does not remember the basic knowledge she teaches. You gain nothing from her class.

I wouldn't take her, I'm serious. The notes taken in class are nothing like what is done on the exam- nothing. I mean if you are an incredible student who excels at grasping concepts quickly, go for it. The exams are very difficult and expectations are borderline unreasonable. We will see how midterm goes for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Quincy just doesn't know how to teach. Her class notes are a mess and her handwriting is illegible at all. Makes super hard problem sets and exams that have a lot of content she doesn't cover in class. I would rate her negative if there's a chance.

Her problem sets for ECON 2300 asked us about things we hadn't even covered in class. You can tell she's trying to be more accessible and understanding as a professor, but her expectations were way too high. Also, her handwriting is illegible which is why you need to attend class (her in-class notes are not going to be easy to read).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Professor Quincy's first semester teaching, and it showed. The disconnect between what we talked about in class and what was asked of us on exams was glaring, and it seemed at times like she thought we were PhD students. Expectations were really highhard exams, intense, lengthy readings, etc. Would avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most boring classes I have ever had. The class is not difficult, but it's a waste of time. She seems smart, but not a good teacher.

Chris is very kind, but the class is insanely boring. She lectured the whole time about unrelated things, so nobody paid attention. So much reading + reading quizzes that were actually hard. I didn't find the material, nor the way it was presented, to be interesting. She's a very nice lady who knows her stuff, but I wouldn't take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very dry lectures. So hard to stay engaged in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has changed her grading system, and in place of the midterm, she has opted to give her classes random reading checks instead. Although she claims they are easy, the class has done poorly on them overall. If she were to decrease the overwhelming reading load, people might actually do the reading and be able to perform better on these quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Quinn Trank!! She is so friendly, upbeat, and relatable. I could always tell she put a lot of effort into her lectures. Her midterm was challenging, but she is a generous grader (e.g., she gave points back on questions most people missed). One of my favorite professors ever!! A true gem at Vanderbilt. Loved her class.

Chris is very nice and serious about her material. The lectures are on org theories, but discussion is usually some application exercise. Tests & participation make up a big percentage of your grade, so you have to really study the theories, which can be hard when discussion is informal. It's a little tough but you learn a lot.
Shes well read and enjoys discussion!

I am so glad I took this class. She is a genius, so sweet and understanding. Also gives great feedback on the 3 short papers. Only issue with this class is that the expectations for exams are vague, but it's a small price to pay for an an otherwise great experience! The papers are creative and the group project is better than most.
quinn trank rules!
Best professor I've ever had. Amazing teacher, incredible engaging, absolutely the best I've had. And HOT!

very easy, no tests, one big research paper at the end of the year. Weekly journal entries (which your homework assignments can count as an entry) she is super nice and helpful! i really like her take her class!

Professor Quigley treats his students like adults, If you come to class prepared and ready to participate you will have an excellent time in this class as his discussion based teaching style leaves a lot of room for the development of complex ideas. If you show up unprepared however, Professor Quigley will eventually call you on your bull.

In my opinion, he is a really tough grader so if you're writing isn't already pretty strong, I wouldn't expect to get an A. Also, beware, his comments on your writing can be pretty harsh and comes off a bit condescending to me. Other than that, he's a pretty lenient guy and the actual class is really just a discussion.

Class isn't the most interesting, but Professor Quigley is extremely passionate about what he teaches.  Is very helpful, and lets you turn in essay drafts early so he can help you revise them to do better.  Difficult grader, but really smart guy who wants you to not just succeed, but really think critically.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great prof, super nice guy, loves to help students.   Gives lots of feedback and wants to help you do well.  Most of the grade is 3 essays, all pretty short and have the opportunity to submit a draft and rewrite.  Grades kinda tough, but work with him and use the draft and you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Incredibly helpful and passionate guy. Also very articulate. He assigns a very doable amount of reading and makes class interesting and fun. If you participate and spend some time on your essays you'll have no problems.

Not a bad class. It can be boring  and at 9 35, I often did not go (but still got an A-). Do the practice problems and homework problems as review. Don't bother buying the textbook (I didn't). Partner up with someone to do homework and studying with. Very math based, but it's simple algebra and calculus so not bad at all. Accent is annoying, yes.

After a few classes, not hard to understand. Make sure you can do his assignments and practice problems and you'll have no problems with the tests. If you don't understand something, go to his office hours. For being one of the hardest classes at vanderbilt, very manageable with Wen.

Tests are just homework and exercises with different numbers. Wen isn't THAT incomprehensible, but has a thick accent. Lots of office hours before tests where he is pretty helpful. Class is basically all math (through Calculus 3), so if you stink at math, stay away and take 231 with Conley.
He is an excellent professor. Very helpful, and wants his students to succeed. I definitely recommend him for 231
Simply a great professor. Extremely helpful

Great guy.Just shy of being totally incomprehensible.The class is powerpoints from the text.His examples are fairly helpful.Tests are basically the assignments,reworked.The workbook is,in my opinion,pretty useless.You can download the class books online,so thats nice.His office hours are helpful-so go.Get a study group together.Math ppl will excel.

I liked him a lot. Honestly, the class is considered one of the most rigorous in the department, so it is hard to love the class and professor. Initially he was somewhat difficult to understand. He was very clear and helpful during office hours. Very nice and caring. He posted class notes on OAK. The homework was helpful for the tests. Fair tests.
Not very easy to understand.  His English is very poor.
He is difficult to understand, but he is really caring and is very willing to answer questions.  You don't have to go to class. Going to TA office hours really helps for the assignments.

the class might seem intimidating at first, but if you ever need help with problem sets or any test material he is always willing to help. although the test are based off of the homework, the homework is by NO means easy. definitely take him over conley though!!!!!

the class will seem hard when he first hands out homework and the syllabus. but there is a curve and if you go meet with him then he is very willing to help you succeed in this class. during class he is hard to hear because of his accent and i would not take this class if you are not an econ major

If you have to take micro, definitely take him over Conley. You don't have to go to class because he posts all his notes on OAK. There are 9 homeworks, and if you just go through the slides they aren't too hard. There are only 3 tests, and they are basically the same as the homework, just with some twists.

His accent really wasn't a problem for me; stresses actual problems rather than multiple choice, so knowing pertinent models is quite helpful.  Is open to meeting with students and helped me, without hassle, when I had an issue regarding grading.  As micro professors go, he is quite good.

He's a very nice guy and wants to help. His accent can be hard to get over at first, however, he does send out his lecture notes so it's easy to study for tests. You have 9 assignments spread out over the semester with three tests total. They are moderately easy but you have to earn points when you can. Pray for an easy grading TA too.

a really nice guy, but the notes are confusing, and you need to know the subject matter perfectly for the tests. normal people shouldnt take this class because it is small and the people in it, are all really smart, so they do well and work really hard, which sucks. really interesting material
Has trouble speaking English well enough to communicate effectively.  Still, does his best and the material is very interesting.

QI rocks! He's awesome. No kidding, I would highly recommend taking his classes. I wish I can have him teaching all of my math courses. Tests are pretty easy. No hw,assignments etc. Great teacher overall!

He's a great professor. He likes to keep things simple and makes everything seems really easy. The best prof I've ever had. Tests aren't that bad, homework won't be graded. Just do the practice problems and it's an easy A course.
Best calculus teacher ever! He gives a bunch of examples in class and the tests are pretty easy as long as you look over your notes and do the homework

Very nice guy. He'll go over material until you understand it. If you have a question, ask him, he will give you big hints on what to do. Although his accent may be tough at times, he was by far the best math teacher I've had at Vandy. I'd definitely recommend him for this class.

Take this class! Qi Zhong is really nice. He's really funny and personable. Sit in the front and get to know him! :) His tests are definitely difficult/tricky, but if you review in class notes, hw, and examples from the book, you will do well. Stay on top of your work.
Great lecturer and goes through so many examples that makes the homework doable.

Great guy but not a great professor. Lectures are hard to follow and he isn't accessible at all outside of class. Disappeared for 2 weeks before the final. Test grading scheme is incredibly weird, where a tiny mistake means you lose 7% due to his "3-point system". Encourages you to argue with him, but shuts you down if you do. Needs to retire lol.

Homework after every class and due on the same day. Tests are doable if you grind decently beforehand and understand your materials. Sometimes he just disappears but overall if you try to talk to him he's willing to connect you to stuff. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very didactic. The material can be complicated, but is easily distilled, and exams were very very fair.

Great guy, good lectures, easy tests. The class was structed as 50 minutes of lecture, and then 25 minutes to do the homework due by the next day, which was usually easy to complete in that time. The class is not very hard (easier than Circuits 1), and if you want an A you can easily get it. He posts extra practice problems if you really need it.

He is a very nice professor, compared to the other EE faculty i met. The class is not hard, but his exams are somewhat random since there's no practice exams at all. Also the homework is hard and not that relevant to his exams. Overall, not too hard to get A, but you have to teach yourself to do it.

While he has a good attitude, his exams are very unreasonable. He expects you to do 2 hours of work on a 50 min exam. Studying more won't help because his exams tend to focus entirely on 1 random topic out of all the material he goes over. His lectures are over complicated and monotonous, so you are better off teaching yourself.
Easy class. Know mathematica like the back of your hand and you'll be fine. Tests are way easier than homework.
Easy tests, problem sets are a little too hard, nice guy, helpful with homework. Final is a little harder than the midterms

This class is much easier than 112, and Reed is just the man. Test questions are from homework. The night before homework is due he sits on his email ready to help. He wants everyone to do well and works hard to make it that way. If you dont like mathematica dont take the class.
Great teacher, explains everything well, tests are reasonable, nice guy. Nuff said

It was the first time Professor Reed taught this course, but it was hard to tell. Although a lot of the class was deriving the formulas we would use, he made it a lot less painful than usual. His lectures were very clear and his grading standards were very fair. The subject was difficult, but I still learned a lot and enjoyed the experience.

Great professor. Both him and Weller teach this class with different sections, and I'd recommend Reed. This class is a million times easier than 112 for lack of hand-solving problems - but you still end up learning quite a lot. Reed knows Mathematica well, and is a great communicator.

Dr. Rewers is an incredibly smart individual. Having taken him for a class with subpar content, he truly made it engaging. He goes far beyond the core content, expanding on concepts he teaches in his other classes. I have rarely learnt so much in a class. He also really accommodates students (extends deadlines and gives extra assignments, etc...)

Dr. Rewers genuinely cares about his students and wanted everyone to succeed in his class. Everyone had a chance to participate and he gave extra assignment opportunities for students to improve their grades.

Great prof. very funny and sweet. Attendance not required but pop quizzes for reading do occur sometimes. Class was pretty straightforward and not too difficult. Had the same prof for core: he is the GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Rewers is incredible, he is able to simplify all topics during lectures so it is easy to understand. Slides are a word and he just talks and knows everything. I will trust anything he says. All test and reading quizzes but are not hard at all.

Definitely take if offered again. Lots of guest lecturers, plus interesting case studies. Attendance is randomly taken, assignments are weekly mind maps. Cool to have Diermeier come to class. Kind of a unique class for Vandy. Was looking forward to it every week.

Professor Mario's class was the easiest class I took all semester. He had weekly assignments, a concept map with a recording 3-5 min long, then 2 bigger assignments, with a recording 10 min long. The main thing to note about this class is that you need to focus in class to complete the assignments correctly.Lectures were entertaining

It was a very unique class! Dr. Rewers did a good job presenting all of these different speakers and lecturing us about the dangers of free speech. The assignments were really easy, so more focus was put on the content of the lectures. Some were boring, but a lot had cool stories, topics, and made the whole class fun. It was a pleasant surprise.

You are graded on "mind maps" each week based on a different guest speaker that comes to teach. That's your entire grade, plus two "discussions" (ten min video reflections) and attendance which he takes 6 times randomly. It's a easy class, but it's also interesting and some of the speakers were awesome. They even had the chancellor come speak.

Needed an HCA for graduation credits, could not be happier with this class. Discussions are interesting and he gets everyone to participate, short writing assignments are super easy and insightful, larger essay is easy as well. Grading is also either meets expectations or doesn't and you get revisions
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Vandy prof. Cares about you understanding the concepts. Good discussion leader, makes sure everyone participates. Lots of interesting material covered. Will cold call, so make sure you do the assignments.
Chill class, now CAL1001. Some readings each week, plus response papers. Brings in interesting guests half the class. Definitely take if you're needing a 1 credit course.

This is the best class I've taken at Vandy. Prof Rewers is so kind and interesting, really good at engaging the class and making sure everyone participates. He cold calls at times to make sure you did the assigned reading but it is overall a low-stress class. Midterm and final exam are easy as long as you listen in class and take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I felt this class was lacking. The general concepts we learned about were interesting, but about half the readings were too theoretical and seemed irrelevant to the class at large. The final, an hour long oral exam, seemed to prioritize rote memorization rather than concept understanding in one part. Rewers is a good professor, but skip this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes at Vandy! Lots of reading but texts aren't too long. Graded by participation, an essay, and oral exam at the end. Material was super relevant. Definitely take if you have a chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Genuinely such an interesting class that has changed the way I think about Nashville. Graded by one 3-5 min (pretty informal) presentation on a Nashville influencer and one end of the semester interview with a Nashvillian. Easy class in terms of workload, brought in cool guest speakers, definitely worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't succeed in professor Rewers' class you are doing something wrong. Lectures are energetic and interesting and required readings are genuinely cool. Rewers himself is kind and thoughtful which makes it easy to earn your participation points, which are significant. 10/10 would take again, he fosters a great small class feeling.

The most I ever learned in a class. Rewers is incredibly intelligent, leads quality class discussions. and asks very good questions. The readings can get heavy and long at times but the topics are interesting and engaging. As long as you come to class and pay attention, the final exam is not too challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best class I've taken at Vandy yet. Rewers and a class full of genuinely curious people made for really interesting and relevant discussions. Participation during class is a must (he cold calls). Final at the end is an oral exam worth half your grade. Main critique would be that he called on certain students a lot more than others during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is super well spoken + being surrounded by generally conscientious and intelligent people made for good discussion-lecture. There are 2 short answers a week (each one is 2% of grade) and an oral final (50% of grade) so the big crunch really comes at the end. If you come to class and stay engaged, you should be fine.

Rewers is a very intelligent man. Class is entirely free discussion of the text, so the reading is a must. He has a frosty, impersonal demeanor at first, but after open enrollment, he's really nice to talk to. Only gripe is a grueling take-home final that felt unnecessarily long. Take if you are strong at writing and analyzing historical texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. Class discussions were always very interesting and content was extremely relevant. I have never learned so much in a class. Couldn't recommend more
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Well-spoken and knowledgeable who wants the best for his students. Readings were pretty difficult and long but grading is flexible in the class(2 very short responses per week and an oral final). However, He is a bit biased sometimes and calls on some students a lot more than others.
If you actually do the readings and study for the exams with flashcards, as well as participate, you'll do well. Interesting readings/professor as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, don't slack off though because the final grade is relatively subjective. Graded by participation and a few projects, lots of interesting guest speakers and very discussion based. One of the most fun classes I've taken at Vanderbilt, brought in some famous names to the seminar-style class.

This is a rating for AMER 1002, graded by one midterm and one final. Both exams are ten id questions that are impossibly hard, and final has a closed book essay as well. If you aren't an American studies major, take the writing section instead: a notable percentage of my section failed the course. Rewers is great, so take one of his other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent Professor. Really knowledgeable about his stuff. Class was mostly a conversation between students with minimal teacher involvement. Certainly my favorite class I've taken thus far at college.

I only had Rewers for a seminar but he has by far been my favorite professor yet. Such an amazing, caring, funny guy. I hope to take more of his regular classes in the future because he genuinely cares about making connections with his students.

Took his Welcome to AMER 1001 Nashville commons iSeminar. My favorite class I've taken ever. Probs about 30-60 minutes of reading per week. But honestly not that bad. We all just had good conversations, laughed, and vibed for a while each class.

I took his freshman commons seminar so it was different than his other classes but he made class so interesting every day, engaged every student, and was hilarious! you can see and feel his passion for teaching every day and i highly recommend taking him

Professor Rewers is absolutely amazing - I have never learned so much in a class. He is so interesting and leads the class discussions in the most engaging ways. Could not recommend him/this class more.

I'm a junior and this has been my favorite class I've had at Vanderbilt. It is a chunky amount of writing, but i appreciate that it is spread evenly throughout the semester, no massive final. Essay prompts are flexible, readings are interesting enough so that there is always something to write about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Grades are based on 10 weekly essays and participation. Readings are almost always interesting and the class discussions that follow are always thoughtful and interactive. Almost more of a philosophy class at points than a pure policy class. Rewers is wonderful and makes discussions flow really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rewers is amazing!!! I loved taking this class. He is so well-read and always chooses super interesting readings. Requires 10 weekly essays and calls on people at random in class, but always a cool discussion!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great guy, super insightful as well
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lots of work but an absolute king. Learned so much from this man
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rewers is one of the most intelligent and interesting faculty I have interacted with on Vanderbilt Campus. I left class every day having learned new things and found myself genuinely interested in the contents of the class. He gave lots of helpful feedback along the way for our one big paper. Expectations were clear. HIGHLY recommend.

Dr. Rewers made sure each person felt comfortable to participate in our discussions, creating a great learning environment & an appreciation for the course subject. He is not a harsh grader, so it's easy to do well overall. Go to class well-rested, well-read, and with some coffee; you'll succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Weekly 3-4 page papers on tons of reading (which he cold calls on) and 2 additional 8 page papers. At least 15 people have dropped this class and it is mandatory for the PPS major so that is saying something. While he is very intelligent, save your hard work for an actual writing course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Rewers assigned so much reading per class that I just stopped doing it. As long as you have two or three things to contribute and get the gist of the article/book you'll be ok. Weekly reflection papers weren't bad and final paper was broken up into multiple steps to be more manageable. He really cares about what you think and your growth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Rewers is extremely smart, and his lectures are very interesting. He actively encourages and enforces participation both during class with cold-call questions and weekly response papers on your own. His grading is fair with good feedback, too. Try harder than I did towards the end, and you will certainly get a good grade. Recommend.

This was a UGA course. Professor Barsky brought in multiple special guests with great insight. He himself brought great insight. I feel that I was extremely lucky to learn from someone as amazing as him. Professor Barksy encourages students to follow their own passions, applying what is interesting to them to the course he is treaching.

This is for EUS 2210. Professor Barsky is one of the best if not the best professor I have met in this school. He is so inspirational and passionate about the subject and infuses a feeling of passion for learning within me that I haven't felt in other classes where I have to care for grades. I learned lots in this class, and I hope to take another.

For FREN3891. Second class with this man, still adore him. Amazing, knowledgeable man who cares very deeply for all of his students and wants the best for them. Attendance isn't mandatory and an A is guaranteed, but for those who do care beyond the A, assignments are very interesting and worth putting effort into.

I LOVE THIS MAN. if you have the chance to take any class with king barsky, TAKE HIM. had him first semester freshman year and he genuinely changed the way i approach my college education. caring, enthusiastic, respectful, and an easy grader. he is probably the most interesting person i've ever met and knowing him has been an honor.

He is the best professor I have had so far. He is incredibly engaging and made my first semester in college so enjoyable. He genuinely cares about you and only wishes the best for you. If only he taught more classes up my alley because I would love to take another one of his classes.

Professor Barsky is an amazing professor who made an intro course that is (arguably) incredibly boring into the class I was most excited to attend. Discussions are great; they give plenty of unique approaches to the same topic (as well as how it relates to Chomsky) and breathe life into anything discussed, no matter how drab the topic.

Professor Barsky is truly a gem. He cares about every student and tries to get to know everyone individually. He makes the class extremely stress free and is flexible, allowing students to explore themselves and what they are passionate about. I highly recommend taking a class by him; you will not regret it.

Dr. Barsky is a wonderful professor with so many extraordinary stories and tons of knowledge to bestow upon his students. Any student would be lucky to take a class with him. He isn't fond of the usual grading-scheme and is willing to accommodate to his student's individual needs.
Best professor I have had at Vandy hands down. So passionate, extremely interesting, and very nice.

Barsky tries to make you think about topics in a different way than you've previously been taught. Every essay I wrote for this class was a first person narrative, even our research paper. He likes to add a fun spin where he can, and he supplements the class with stories from his life to build upon the concepts being taught. I highly recommend him.

He is a gem, in this class you are introduced to many popular classics: Odyssey, Inferno by Dante, Alice in Wonderland... You dont even have to read all of them (or even any) to get engaged during class. He also occassionally bring foods to class for everyone to enjoy. Final project was super fun personal quest and he gives everybody an A.

This is one of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures are so inspiring and he is so passionate about French literature/culture. There are three meaningful essays; no midterm and no final. He is very accessible and helpful.
I don't think you'll encounter a better or more interesting professor at Vanderbilt. He's an awesome and caring guy. I don't think I need to say anything else.
Super nice, gives automatic A on everything, good lectures, funny, definitely take his class!
Professor Barsky is one of the best!! You will not find a better professor at Vandy. I highly recommend taking ANY class with him as you will not regret it. The best!!!

Professor Barsky was an absolute gem! His class was super simple and only had a few grades but all were graded very easily (he believes in bringing out everyone's inner A by the end of the semester). Although the class was very simple, it gave me a better chance to sit back and learn and enjoy it rather than focusing on a grade the entire time!

Barksy is a legend. Writing sem is graded on 3 essays and he cares far more about your effort and making you a better writer than anything else. Very easy to do well in the course and he looks to help connect you on whatever career path you're interested in. Amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a great professor; he's so invested in every student and their interests. He cares more about your learning than your grades. He also has some really cool stories about his life and the way he explains the course material is pretty captivating. It was a writing class so we just had 3 papers for which he gave very helpful and specific feedback.

Barsky is so chill. Will gas up your paper no matter what you write about as long as you put a little effort and are passionate about your topic. I didn't read a single one of the assigned books for my writing seminar and was completely fine. He really wants you to succeed as an individual and in life, he's so kind and smart as well.
THE BEST PROFESSOR AT VANDERBILT! Literally a diamond in the rocks. He is amazing take him I swear to god you will enjoy his class

Barsky is a highly respected professor and he does give interesting lectures. Great for recommendation/networking purposes. He is also a very kind person and is always accessible outside of class. However, his class is very lenient and lax almost to the point of no responsibility (no hard deadlines, no one does readings). Very easy A. Overall, good
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A truly amazing professor. This class was all about refugees, and I learned so much and was constantly inspired. Professor Barsky is an expert, cares about his students, and has incredible stories to tell. Take any class with him.

Barksy is hands-down my favorite prof at Vandy. I went on his Maymester, then took a PSCI class, just because he was teaching it. I had no experience or interest in the material beforehand, but his interdisciplinary style really made me love it. He values participation & especially responds to students he knows well- get to know him outside class.

The world needs more professors like Prof Barsky. He leads you to think outside of your natural boundaries, challenge yourself, and raise new perspectives. Every student needs to take a class from this man. He is eccentric and quirky in the best ways. Easy grader if you engage and participate!

Barsky is free-spirited and incredibly engaging. I technically took a French class, but it was all in English. An easy grader as long as you engage in the material, grading standards are a little unclear but he's super helpful.

Bob Barsky is amazing! Best teacher ever, so understanding and so passionate.  I picked up this class late in the semester but he gave me all the information I needed and made me feel so welcome! He will make you interested in his class no matter what it is! Take it!
I had Barsky as a teacher while he was teaching in Montreal ( UQAM) in early 2000s at the master degree in litterature. By far, he is the best teacher I've ever had.

Best professor on campus, one of my favorite humans in existence. Barsky is extremely encouraging, clear, informed, and engaging. Take his classes even if you aren't interested in the topics - you will be soon enough. He integrates cross-disciplinary information and gives the best constructive notes on papers. For the love of God, take his classes.

Coolest professor I've had at Vanderbilt. Very understanding with deadlines and wants students to learn and be creative. He's also extremely intelligent and passionate about everything he teaches and can bake a great loaf of bread!

Wow. The best professor I've had at Vanderbilt--brilliant, focused on the learning above the grades, understanding, funny. The quintessential college professor...the type you see in movies. Charismatic and hosts dinner at his house at the end of the year. If you don't take from him you haven't lived.
So sweet...very easy grader! he knows so much about what hes talking about and really sparks interest! must take!
He is amazing and so inspirational!  by far my favorite professor!
No Comments

Barsky is by far the coolest professor I've met on this campus; he makes course material awesome and interesting, and just listening to stories about all the cool stuff he's done in his life is more than worth your time.  Definately take his class if you get the opportunity!!!
He is so nice. If you show up, do the presentations, and prepare a little for in class essays you can do super well and learn a good amount of hispanic culture as well.
Wenz is awesome. Cares about his students and provides plenty of opportunities for extra credit.

Wenz is the best ever not only is he an amazing teacher but he is so helpful and truly wants to help you learn. He is a very fair grader and gives helpful feedback overall he is the best as a person and professor and will miss him!!!
Professor Wenz is an absolute SAINT. He cares about his students, assigns meaningful yet manageable work, and wants us to have fun! I can't thank him enough for such an amazing year.

Professor Wenz is by FAR and HANDS DOWN the BEST professor at Vanderbilt University. I don't know a single person that has taken his class and dislikes him. In fact, anyone that takes any of his class sections raves about him. If you come to class, participate, and genuinely try - then he will do everything he can to give you an A
Outstanding teacher and makes the class engaging. Absolutely could convert someone into a Spanish minor or major. He is a must take.
Such a good option for 3302. Has such high energy and really cares about his students. Sends an email before every class of what homework is and what you are doing that day. Highly reccomend
Super caring!

Professor Wenz was fantastic. He cares so much about all his students and genuinely wants them to learn and succeed. He is very understanding and willing to work with you on anything, and he does a good job of keeping everyone engaged. Participation in group and partner discussion is essential and can get annoying but Wenz is the best.
Very good professor---flexible and caring and a pretty good spanish teacher. Grading is flexible and often gives second chances.

Wenz is the BEST language professor at Vandy, actually, the BEST PROFESSOR at Vandy. I usually hate Spanish class, but he made me look forward to going to class. There are quite a few quizzes, tests, etc. but he makes them so manageable! He is an amazing lecturer and an even better person. DON'T HESITATE to take his class! Also, he is a LeBron fan!

One of my favorite professors ar Vandy. He is so passionate and encouraging and is very receptive to questions. He grades very fairly. A good amount daily homework, but he is available for lots of office hours. Highly recommend taking Sr. Wenz!
Cares about his students, is very nice, very passionate about teaching the Spanish Language. Will make an effort to make a connection with you.

I took professor Wenz both first semesters of my freshman year and I really loved his class. He was so engaging. His class is an easy A if you keep doing works and completing them on time. He always there to help if you have any questions. I also love his class because of little snacks he usually give out :).

Dr. Wenz was an animated and engaging lecturer. Class participation was graded but Wenz made it low stress. The homework included minimal reading and online exercises that you had to keep on top of but were not time-consuming overall. He was easy to communicate with and was very understanding of problems.
By far one of the best classes, I have taken yet, super fun and laid back. There is a lot of homework but it all takes less than 20mins a day, if that.
Really honest professor.Really accessible and helpful outside of class. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. If you do the work you will do great in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Dr. Wenz is so unbelievably understanding and caring: he truly wants you to succeed in his class. 
For example, he provided office hours the morning of our final, just in case anyone had last minute questions. 
His tests are also fairly straightforward as long as you understand the grammar concepts. I cannot recommend his class more!!!
Wenz is the absolute goat. Love this guy. So accessible outside of class and really wants to see all of his students succeed. Couldn't recommend taking a class with him enough.

Professor Wenz is a king! He is extremely understanding and patient, which is great for a class full of people who have little to no Spanish,speaking experience. Even if you answer a question incorrectly, he will correct you in the nicest way. He always makes class interesting and I am sad his class for next semester is already filling up :(

This professor cared about personal things that were going on in my life that was why I wasn't in class. He truly cares about his students, there was a time when I missed an assignment and he let me go back and redo it without any questions asked. One of the best profs I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
most awful language professor I've ever met. the most terrible part is that he teaches so fast that the homework questions are way ahead of what he's teaching. I just started learning spanish and this guy ruined my experience. Would never take it again. 

Very heavy homework and teaches extremely fast that assumes everyone took spanish before.
My favorite spanish teacher by far. Knows his stuff but doens't show off unless its to help show you where you can be if you work hard. He is hilarious and loves to see you succeed
Really awesome professor. He's a grad student, but more organized and clear than most other professors, for sure. He grades very fairly, and is an incredibly reasonable guy.

Professor Wenz is a very good teacher. Spanish will definitely improve under him. B+ or A- is easily achieved if you show some effort - a true "A" takes a lot but if you are good at Spanish is not at all impossible. Highly recommend him.  Super nice guy.

Professor Wenz REALLY cares about his students and does his best to make classes interesting. Tests are tough but not horrible, and very easy to do extremely well on papers so it balances out. Not much time spent on homework or studying. Easy B+ or A-, a little harder to get an A.  Great professor and great class.
Very good professor!  He always explains everything fully and makes sure that you know the material without being a tough grader.  Also a huge sports fan!

Professor Wenz is one of the most caring professors I've ever had. He really wants you to succeed and will make sure you understand all the concepts. If you show him you are trying and want to do well, he will make sure you get there.

Steve was a really great teacher starting out. Very clear about what he wants from you. Doesn't throw curveballs on tests, written or oral. Great teacher when starting out. Extremely helpful in and outside of class. He shows a sincere interest in helping his students learn Spanish.
Pretty nice.
Professor Wenz is an extremely helpful professor. He gets to know all of his students, and is always available for extra help if you need it. Just go to class, do homework, and study for tests.

The content of his class was interesting, but every single class is just 50 minutes of lecturing. The lectures are all 40-60 slides long and he talks sooo fast. Theres also 150-450 pages of reading a week which is insane. Worst part is he grades you subjectively, with no clear criteria. Exams cover niche characters or happenings in readings

The nicest most passionate professor EVER. He loves what he does and I find it so inspiring. Took him for Roman law of delicts- I was terrible at it. This class was not my strong suit by any means and I lowkey thought class was extremely boring . But I love this man and would defend him till the death

This is a class where you really have to enjoy the topic to like the professor. He is clearly very passionate about his subject, but the readings are long and can be quite dull. He also lectures basically every class, which might not be everyone's cup of tea. The class is really easy however, and the workload isn't bad if you just skim the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a difficult class, and Dr. McGinn is an exacting professor. He is also extremely knowledgeable, helpful, and caring. 3150 is great for students who are willing to think hard about the cases, attend lectures, ask questions, and integrate feedback. Highly recommend if you fit this description and want to improve your legal reasoning/writing
Incredibly harsh grader.

Don't take this class if not interested in classics at all. You will be so uninterested and unmotivated to learn anything (seriously, I cannot recall a single thing I've learned this year). He's a tough grader - if you normally get As on papers, expect Bs from him. His lectures are paragraphs in a ppt. Nonetheless, he is caring and accommodating.

Professor mcginn is great, he seems to genuinely care about the material which makes an 8am lecture entertaining. He tends to assign a lot of reading but you can get by doing a lot less. Test are only hard because most people dont study until the night before, if you pay attention during lectures and study earlier youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. McGinn is very respected in his field, and it's easy to tell that he cares a lot about the material he teaches. Still, his lectures are fairly boring for non-Classics majors, and there are only two graded assignments all semesters. He's not a super tough grader, but he does take attendance. Definitely not the most engaging class I've taken.

Professor McGinn is obviously knowledgeable about Latin/ancient Rome, but this class was very dry. We mostly translated for homework outside of class and then went over it in class. There was only a midterm and final, so tests were very important for the grade. Work hard and you'll get an A but it's a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy and is very smart. Few assignments, 1 short paper, 1 long paper, and a midterm and a final. The class was boring but it was definitely a class that requires little work in and out of the class. Professor is really great, but only take if you need the credit or need a class that requires no work (but ok w not getting an A)

I highly recommend Professor McGinn and his Roman Law class, the best taste of law school one can get as an undergrad. All based on the class's case law text book, the papers can be a challenge, but Prof McGinn, extremely knowledgeable in his field, is a valuable resource to improving your writing and refining your analysis.

Dr. McGinn is incredibly understanding and is always there for you. The class involves a lot of reading, but the classes are generally just lectures, so it's not always really necessary. Beware: the only grades are two exams and a midterm paper. He's very lenient about grading essays, but vocab/identification sections of tests are difficult.
Hilarious professor, gives a lot of reading but he's by far the most entertaining professor I've had.

Dr. McGinn is a really fun teacher to have. Class is a standard advanced Latin course, taking turns translating material that was assigned. He's very understanding when it comes to issues outside of class interfering with performance or due dates. Tests are just translating a couple passages that were covered. Would recommend if you enjoy Latin.

Really energetic, and obviously enjoys the subject. Participation is a grade, but class consists entirely of translating Latin assigned at the end of the previous class. Might not be a good class for those with anxiety. Professor is more than willing to help with students and be accommodating when they're having difficulties. Typical Latin grading.

Amazing person, toughest grader ever. What's worse is that his handwriting is illegible, so no constructive feedback expected when papers are returned. Don't get me wrong , he's incredibly nice and more than willing to work with you, but don't expect an easy A, or an easy B+, for that matter.
Even a bad day with Professor McGinn is better than the best day fishing, unless you really, really like fishing.

Great professor. He's incredibly knowledgeable and suprisingly funny. His lectures are phenomenal and always interesting. I've heard he's becoming a softer grader than he used to be. Tests and essays are pretty easy, but it is a ton of reading to keep up -- I think it's well worth it, though.

He is clearly full of himself and thinks he's very charming and smart. He tends to dominate conversation and become upset, hostile even, if you disagree with him or offer a viewpoint different than his. He returns papers late an d with few comments. Those that he makes you cannot read because his handwriting is atrocious. Avoid if you can.

Very little work with this class. Assignments are short, only 2-3 papers, a midterm and a final. Only daily readings are a couple pages long, and not really mandatory. You spend the entire class going over court cases, very discussion based. It's hard to understand what he wants from you in the papers so it is hard to get an A but B to A- is easy.

He assigns a lot of reading but I think he understands that it's hard to keep up w/ so you can still get an A in his class if you don't read. His identifications on exams are all in the lecture. He gives you the essay question possibilities (1-2) to prepare for before the exam. He's really funny and knows his stuff. Just a wonderful professor!

Class is a breeze.  Very little reading required, just show up and listen.  There are only four assignments/test all semester. McGinn is great fun and extremely intelligent.  He'll tell you exactly what he wants if you go talk to him.
Very smart, but if you don't agree with his point of view, it can be detrimental to your life.  Seriously.  His calss was moderately interesting, and I was a classics major.

Definitly one of the better Latin teachers I've ever had. Sure he really does help your understanding of the language, but his immense bank of knowledge on Roman history, culture, and law allows him to spurt off as much explanatory context as you could ever want for just about any passage. So he's great for those more interested in history.

Easy teacher. Although he assigns insane amounts of reading, you don't have to do it. Just listen in class. Essays and IDs on tests are graded easily. His lectures are hit or miss. Sometimes incredibly interesting and hilarious, sometimes jumbled and incoherent. He is helpful outside of class and just an all around fun guy.

Don't take this class if you want to have anby sort of life other than reading 150 pages every night. He moves way too fast and his lectures are unclear. He gave us no real study guide for the test and expects us to have read 1200 pages in about 5 weeks which is ridiculous. One of the worst classes i have ever taken

He is a really nice guy, is incredibly smart, and is quite funny. However, his lectures move way too fast and there is way too much reading for a low 200 3 credit class. I am currently trying to read the 120 page assignment he assigned for us tomorrow. The subject matter is pretty interesting though and the paper is easy.

Knows his stuff really really well, but if you like to take notes in class you will find it difficult to keep up with him.  Just sit back and listen to him talk.  Try hard and you'll make a good grade.
ridiculously smart, and speaks a million languages.  Makes the whole class laugh at least once per class period.  but without a bkground in classics, his classes can be rough.

He is a genius and knows everything there is to know about classics.  But he requires tons of reading and lectures so fast you hardly get the notes down.  However, he is really interesting and passionate about the subject, and really nice and funny.
Exams are tough, but fair.  Read in advance, pay attention in class and go to office hours.

Fun class.  I got a B first semester and never got into the flow of the class.  Orgo 2 with Dr. T was a bit different - he was more clear on what the exams involved and was generous with extra credit and partial credit.  Some struggled, but seems like half the class got an A or A-. Read and do problems.

Great class. If you're looking for the easy A, this isn't it. But, I think I was challenged and learned how to solve problems in this class more than any other since I've been at Vandy. Dr. T has a high standard of excellence so you'll have to rise to the occasion.
Tough exams and very lecture heavy. Everyone I know in the class got an A or A-. So if you have a pulse, he's good.  If you want the easiest possible path to an A, not the right class for you.

First A in a chem class! I think Dr. T is great - his exams are very challenging, but he sets you up for success. He's fair.  Very approachable and willing to help. Only challenge is that he assigns too many problems and he expects you to remember everything from both semesters.

This was the first science class that I got an A in. Dr. T is great (and quirky). He really worked with me over the semester. Office hours are important - he will go over homework and problems with you. This was the first science class where I learned how to apply knowledge to solve problems. His test's are hard, but very fair.
Seems like a nice guy and a good researcher but his exams are a lot harder than the other sections. I would not recommend taking him if you are pre-med.

Dr. Townsend's lectures are digestible and easy to follow. He made an effort to get to know each and every student in his class. He wants everyone in it to succeed. He gives hundreds of practice problems and will sit and work through them with you. His exams are difficult, but reasonable for CHEM 2222.

I went to his office hours before a recent exam - there were at least 12 people in there and he handled it very well. He wants to help you, probably too much. Someone else said it, but he's a major researcher. So he expects everyone to take care of their business and will not stalk you about it.  Great teacher. Great to interact with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good class. Dr. T has a big brain and kind heart. He's full on OG / Uncle status at this point. I found the tasks challenging, but he does tell you exactly what's on it. Downsides - he moves at a blistering pace. He's also a researcher, so he is very busy. That said, I've been to office hours once a week and he's always helpful.

This has been such an enjoyable class. Dr T. is kind and patient.  I think he's rather funny and cool with a nerdy vibe. I've learned a lot. The material is very hard and dense, but I think he does a nice job making it digestible. He expects a lot. Lots of extra credit, doesn't grade homework. The mock exam should be in every class.

He's a major researcher, but is always at class and provides clear study guides for tests. He explains complex topics in accounting well - but better in office hours. Never avoids a question and tries to be helpful. He expects a lot but I think is fair. Not many assignments, which is good and bad.  Just 4 exams. Lots of extra credit, easy grader.

Dr. T is lecture heavy. Suggests and provides a large number of problems. This includes what he calls a mock exam, which is a duplicate of the real exam to show you the style and help with timing. If you do problems and read, you will get an A. But if you don't put in that effort, I can see how the class would appear very hard.

Heard that S-Class Steve was back in Orgo 2! Great organic chemist. He won't ever say it, but he's also famous. Super helpful office hours. Exams are tough, but fair. He legit goes over the topic of each question before the exam. He cares that you learn. Has lots of stories which kept me awake. Pay attn because you will see him in the gym and rand.

Orgo 3. He teaches it "Cal-Tech Style" where you get 1 month to complete the exams and can use any resources.  I like that he encourages working with grad students and professors to work problems. Very lecture heavy. Small class is cool. You will need to remember Orgo 1 and 2 as we learned 5-10 reactions per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. T, aka "S-Class Steve" created this seminar to teach the chemistry of drugs and how it plays into gangs and incarceration.  This was his first time teaching the class. Although it was bumpy (speakers canceling) it was very informative and interesting. I would take more classes from Dr. T just based on how much he cares about us.

I cannot express how much I adore steve. He is the king of vandy chem. Deeply cares about his students. Going to office hours will make your life brighter. Really emphasized problem solving. This was the first class where I felt like I saw the skills I had learned in orgo, bio, and biochem all come together in a meaningful way. A chocolate adonis.

This is the 2nd class I've had with Dr. T.  He normally teaches organic, but taught this as a one off. Tt was clear that this wasn't his speciality, but he battled through.  Said that the goal is to learn to analyze problems - and I've achieved that.  Take him for organic when offered as he's decent and cares about students.

Great instructor. Personable, funny. I appreciate that he went beyond the book to teach. 3 exams and a synthesis project. 1 exam was half in person / half group work outside of class. My complaint - he prints and copies everything! He gave nearly 350 practice problems, photocopied instead of PDF (in addition to the book)!!

This professor is amazing! I highly recommend taking this professor! He is very caring of his students. He cares more about teaching the material in an engaging way than grading students harshly. Truly, he is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt!

He is an absolute gem. By far my favorite prof of freshman year. I really struggled in orgo 1 (with rizzo), but townsend really made me fall in love with chemistry again. If you put in the effort, he will make sure that you get a grade you are happy with. Only criticism I might have is that his office hours are rather inaccessible. TAKE HIS CLASS.

Guy gave out like 400 problems (ungraded, in addition to the book)! You can judge for yourself whether thats overkill!  Hes a former athlete who believes in practing harder than you play (quote). I dont think the class was nuclear, but the competition among students is fierce. Work hard and you'll get an A/A-.
Dr. T was helpful. I was not prepared for this class and got a C+ in Orgo 1. Dr. T helped me figure out where I needed to improve.

I enjoyed this class most during my freshman year. His expectations are clear and he will make you think outside the box. My only complaint is that he only gives like 5 hours of office hours. If you email him questions, limit it to below 30 or else he wont answer.  Instead of office hours I sent him a list of 55 questions and he didn't respond.

Orgo 2 is hard.  The class should really be broken up into 2 semesters given the number of reactions.  Dr. T is dope, I enjoyed the class and he's super helpful in office hours. He spends about 3 classes per chapter, skips rote memorization, and introduces a lot of topics outside the book.

material is dense and high volume - Dr. T made this a nice experience - taking him again in the fall for Spec ID. expectations are clear. does problems every day and introduces a lot of content not in the book. only negative - he only offers 5-6 hours of office hours and its hard to catch him otherwise as he's constantly busy (literally).

After exam 1 he told me "perfection is the enemy of excellence". 1st prof. to ever tell me that its more important that i be bold than just regurgitate lecture or the textbook. Great class - his chemistry memory is amazing...i dont get how one person has that much information in their brain.

Material is hard, its so much. Dr. T is great - he could probably move faster, but likes to make sure we understand. He expects you to work most book problems and gives dozens that he's written. He's the only Prof. I've had so far who is approachable, I actually like talking to him. His memory is amazing.

Respect. Dr.T's strength is his accessibility (though its clear there are pulls on his time).  He's also a real human. Easy to talk too. Gives help. Gives a lot of problems outside of the book - nearly close to 300. He cares about learning outcomes and connecting the class to the real world. His shoe game and midlife crisis are amazing to witness.

Preface: We're 6 weeks into the semester. But this course has been a relief. This is the first class where I feel like I am prepared for the exams and know exactly what I'm facing. Dr. T cares that we learn the material and can problem solve. He knew my name when I showed up to his office without introduction. He is amazingly quirky. He cares.

He's an awesome guy. Orgo 2 is really hard in content and his tests are exceptionally hard. Good news is that he gives a ton of problem sets for you to work on. He seems to focus more graduate level orgo rather than undergrad shredded orgo, so don't be surprised if anything unusual showed up on test. Always to ask him questions is the key!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Rizzo/Townsend sequence is excellent. In the Townsend half, you will get an A or A- if you are excellent. You will get a B+ if you are average and a B if you realize you were not prepared for his class.

A few things. 1. Can't proceed like the 1st semester never happened. It all ties together. 2. Must read chapters in advance. 3. Must look for pattern recognition, do not memorize. 4. It sounds lame, but his class is representative of life. 5. This was the best class I had 1st year. 6. Class was a clear test of the best and the rest hang on.

I actually love the class, but I also don't think he's the best teacher for freshman. His tests are 100% application based and he assumes that we've read in advance and his role is to clarify tough concepts. He would be better teaching older students.

He's a great person and is hilarious, but I don't think he's a good teacher. Read and outline the textbook before lectures to make sure you understand what he's talking about. Tests are markedly different from Rizzo's (more application based) but if you understand what's going on, you'll be more than fine. For the love of god, don't try to memorize

Dr. Townsend will easily become you're favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He really cares about if you understand the material. Go to class, its hard! There's extra credit at the end of the year for attendance, even though its not technically mandatory. Don't be afraid to ask him questions and look for little hints in his emails for bonus questions.

Biased since I also worked in his lab. Great teacher a bit fast paced in class EXPECTS that you've read the chapter before hand. Test are nuclear and you'll receive it as fun, challenging, or demoralizing. You have to work for an A, but you have to work equally hard for below a B.

Attend class, he remembers and gives extra credit when/if attendance is bare. This class is an adjustment, exams are hard. Ignore book problems and focus on practice exams. Go. To. His. Office. You'll learn a lot about yourself here.

This. Class. Is. Hard. Dr. T. has high expectations and his tests, in hindsight are elementary. In the moment theyre an inferno. Odd part, I'm still thinking about the final and questions I got wrong are haunting me! Hope to have him again.

Here's the secrets. Come to class, he gives extra credit when attendance is low and somehow has names memorized on day 1. Read before class otherwise he'll lose you. Ask questions in class! When studying do not read anything he didnt cover in class. Everything is cumulative, so don't forget 1st semester. Go to his office!!!

As said below, ST makes this class bearable and hes accessible. This class has more info and is harder than 1st semester. 1. He teaches as if you've read the chapter in advance 2. He expects you to remember gen chem principles 3. He emphasizes hard problem solving 4. The entire class is cumulative All that said, I got an A.

Dr. Townsend makes orgo extremely bearable. He keeps classes interesting, is always in his office willing to help, and tries his best to make this class enjoyable. If you're deciding whether to take the freshman orgo sequence or to continue it, do it. It's extremely worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Can be a run-away train in class so you have to stop him to ask questions. Accessible for office hours. Class is tough, most assume that going in. No one drowns.

Better 1:1 than in class. But at least keeps your attn during lecture. Chill person, obviously under a lot of pressure, but maintains enthusiasm and effort. Exams are so hard, memory doesnt help. Super generous with grades.
First time I've ever had a real connection with a professor. Hardest class I've ever taken! After this course, I don't feel like there are many challenges ahead.

Lectures aren't too helpful, just a more in depth version of the book. Helpful during Off. Hrs. Gives a 30 min. lecture then stays after to do problems with people for 20 mins. Good format. Awful class time (right b4 lunch).

Great instructor. Hard class. Attendance not mandatory but if you don't speak to him in class or in office hours you'll be in trouble. Memory will not help you. Emphasis on using info to solve problems.

Good class. Hard. Attendance not mandatory but he seemingly remembers every person who attends or misses, where they sat, and what they where. Exams are a level 1, USDA prime butt whipping. Sad I won't have ST again in the future.

Only choice for freshman 2nd semester. Hes awesome. Incredibly helpful after class and in his office. Typically lets class out a bit early so we can get to lunch. Class time sucks (11-12). I didn't expect to have an emotional response to this class, but I am not pursuing chem.

Excellent. Dr. T is legit. I was terrified coming into his half based on reputation. His tests are among the toughest at VU. Looking back, theyre also not hard. Looking back, he's also the best teacher I've had through the first year. I'll miss his chill. His lectures are mostly hits. When its a miss, he knows and fixes it. Best class yet.

Great teacher. VERY lenient grader for how hard the subject is. Really nice guy, tests are extremely, extremely hard. People are gassing it on how useless his classes were, I thought they were helpful.

Great instructor.  His biggest weakness is utilizing classroom time.  Next year, we suggested he lecture 30 min and do 20 of questions at the end.  That way random questions don't take over lectures.  But, he's great, like the older brother i wish my brother were.

Class was close to a waste of time, only because he was battling trying to lecture with 2 dudes asking a ton of questions and a group of people who belonged in gen chem asking super stup questions.  BUT, best instructor i've had.  just wish some people werent around.

I got an unexpected and undeserved A.  Never worked this hard in my life.  Very tough exams, where he's looking for your thought process and logic, not 1 specific answer.  Negs- He should ignore some questions, some classes he was answering well over 30.  half were people trying to show him theyre smart.

He's dope.  Writes the toughest  exams ever, which are oddly fun/challenging.  Generous curve. Liberal grading.  Memorization is worthless here, he wants to see problem solving and application.   Great beard.

This is rate the prof. not the class!  But, great dude.  Tells you exactly whats on the exams.  Not interested in more trivial concepts, goes straight for application. Only prof I've visited for office hours and actually wanted to stay and talk chemistry and life.
