frshmn orgo.  maybe the most generous grader ever.  class isn't hard.  comments below are right, immature class.  i actually felt bad for Dr. T at times.

Dr. T is great.  The first "actual human" professor I've encountered.  Very chill and laid back and kinda gives no f's.  Only negative about his teaching style is that he doesn't police the class.  Maybe not his job, but sometimes it would help the class run smoother if he told people to shut up or ignore dumb questions.  But he's the GOAT.

Everyone gets murdered on the exams, but it's fine because the letter grade boundaries are super generous. Spends maybe 15-20 minutes of each class actually teaching, the rest laughing, and it's great. Ask him questions 1-on-1 and you'll be set.

He's great.  The first normal human professor i've had here.  Wicked smart, but not in an intimidating way.  I have a hard time focusing in class, no one can shut up.  So I find greater use meeting him for lunch or office hours.  Test are an exercise in humbleness.

Class has been cool so far.  Teacher is great.  The class is a bit obnoxious/immature so it takes a while to get everyone calm and ready to go...I think Dr. T would be better in an older sophomore class and I think if he slowed down a bit it might help, he's a runaway train.  Pretty good to look at.
Definitely one of my favorite professors. Very Approachable and humorous. Orgo is challenging, but he sure can make it fun. But you'll have to work hard for the grade. Not super hard tho

I loved the professors in the frosh organic sequence and I really enjoyed Dr. T.  Sometimes he will lose you in class, but interrupt him and ask for clarity, hes very receptive.   I only got a B.  I thought I was in danger of getting a C.  He helped drag me across the finish line.  Very supportive.
Awesome professor, super approachable.  Makes Orgo fun and as easy as possible.  Go to office hours, even if you don't think you need to.
Good, fair class.  Exams are hard.  Don't forget reactions from 1st semester, you'll need them.  Don't miss class unless he cancels, he knows!  I think he's too chill, but others loved that.

Dr. T is really laid back and approachable.  He makes attempts to be really clear in class.  When he misses, he comes back with an email or re-visits next class.  He's even better in office hours.  I took him to lunch for FEAST and we debated religion for an hour.

Good at explaining most topics in class. Read before class.  He aweseomly veers way off topic 2-3 times per class. Bernie bashing to taste of chemicals to the burgers with krispy kreme buns. Knows everyones name before first day of class.

Great class. Biggest critique is that he doesn't fill the entire class period. From what I gather, he comes in with a set of topics he wants to cover. Sometimes it take 45 minutes, sometimes 35. It would be better if he had back up materials for when time runs short.

I don't enjoy organic chemistry and I'm not good at it. That being said, Professor Townsend is such a passionate and engaging lecturer that he makes me want to go to class. While I find the tests incredibly difficult, he is willing to provide extra credit and support as long as he knows you're putting in the effort. So thankful I had him.

i wasn't prepared for either class in this sequence. Dr T kept me afloat.  Class was bumpy at the beginning, but Dr. T makes corrections as fast as we suggest them. He's really kind. Too kind actually. Lots of kids take advantage I feel.

One of the coolest professors I've had. Cares deeply about everyone and knows everyone's name very early on in the semester. Gave us his number so we could text him whenever we had questions and never makes you feel dumb for being confused. Tests are tough but he usually hints at the topics covered on them. Can't say enough good things about him!

Haven't spoken to him 1:1, but have emailed him. Always responds and tries to help. does a good job of breaking up lectures with banter. He's authentic. Negatives: doesn't stick to 1 lecture format. Doesn't yell at the rude kids who talk during class. Doesn't know lots of bio.

Cool teacher.  Mostly clear, but sometimes stumbles on his own words.  Very helpful.  Cares.  Gets visibly excited about certain topics (cool reactions, stereochemistry).  The best rambler I've seen.  Awesome shoulders.  Pretty easy exams aimed toward the median.

Highly supportive of Townsend in Frosh orgo.  His tests are real, but manageable (easy?) if you attend class. He's the type to be disappointed if his test aren't considered the toughest.  Hint:  He tips you off in a very subtle manner to exam topics and questions.

Easy class and tests.  Focus on reactions and mechanisms.   Knew everyones name the first week.  Will entertain any question.  If he doesnt know the answer he'll return with it next time around.  Brutally honest.

Dr. T is my favorite teacher so far.  His class is a ball buster, though.  If you take the class ask him to create practice problems. They're much better than the book homework which is useless.  Grading is really generous, but you have to earn an A.

Dr. T is the man.  This class is so hard I thought I was failing!  But Dr. T makes a pact with us at the beginning regarding grades and he holds true to his word.  My advice is to not worry about your grade, it'll be fine.  Just sit back and learn some orgo.  Downer is Dr. T is polite and won't crush the kids who talk during lecture. I want that!

Easy class if you read the chapters, do the homework, and ask questions during lecture.  I feel like he wrote exams to give the middle of the pack kids a shot.  Those of us at the top weren't challenged and had an A wrapped up by exam 3.

I was not very well prepared for the first or second semester of freshman organic. Professor Townsend saved my college career, by teaching me how to study, use knowledge to solve problems, and to not rely on memory tricks.  Very fair and generous with grades.  He somehow blends nerd with weird and cool  "owns it"!

Strengths:  Cares about teaching, students, orgo.  He has to be famous by now for rambling, streaming consciousnesses, and saying whatever he wants!  Writes helpful practice exams.  Weaknesses:  suggests a large volume of problems from the book, which in hindsight are much easier than the exams, voluntary and completely inadequate.

Townsend is a new teacher at the university.  His lectures are spot on awesome when it comes to orgo.  Sometimes they're awkward/off when questions come up regarding a non-orgo topic.  Overall, I've learned more about life in this class than chemistry (and I learned a lot of chemistry!).  I love how well he relates to the students.

I'll preface this by saying that I was incredibly unprepared for this class.  But, with that said, Townsend is a great instructor and really helpful during office hours.   A downfall is he is unfazed by the rude jerks who can't shut up in class and deserve to be hulk-slammed! Although noise doesn't bother him, its annoying to the everyone else.

Townsend is great.  I would say his class is the toughest I've ever taken.  At first I didn't understand why the exams were so challenging, but I realized he believes  exams are to demonstrate problem solving, not just memorization.   Due to the sheer volume of information, reading the chapter before class is a must.  My favorite prof this year.

Townsend is a g. Really chill and knows his stuff. I was initially thrown off by him saying "I don't know" to a lot of questions, but honest about what we know in science and what we don't. Good with partial credit on tests for showing some understanding of the concepts and pretty good on appreciating student learning instead of just the grade.
Great teacher! Gave his students his cell phone number in case they had any questions. Very helpful outside of class. Highly reccomend!

I took Prof. Townsend for a graduate level course in organic chemistry.  The course was very fast paced.  Since it was a graduate class, an emphasis was placed on reading and learning the material outside of lecture.  Exams were the toughest I've ever had.  On the flip side, I learned a lot about chemistry and life while in this course.

I thought this class was very manageable. There was a decent amount of homework, but the notes were useful and Dr. Rhoads was accessible outside of class. She provided plenty of study materials for the exams, which were much easier than homework and review materials. Lectures are okay, her notes are great.

If you just drill down everything from her notes, there is NO way you get anything lower than a B+ in this class. She is amazing at teaching, accessible outside class, has very clear grading criteria, has bonus points (if your final grade is higher than your midterm, she uses that instead), and is a very fair grader. Why is everyone so pressed?

She's friendly and truly makes an effort to get to know all of her students. Unfortunately as professor she isn't great. She makes you feel bad for asking questions about the content and isn't good at answering clarifying questions. Also she makes you feel bad for taking a risk and getting something wrong in class.
Excellent notes in class, tests were easier than practice ones, very accessible out of class

I think this class was pretty fair. I liked her teaching style with a lot of group work and printed out notes. The exams were hard but not impossible. A lot of webworks and written homework and quizzes every week. Overall good class but definitely had to study a lot.

Dr. Rhoads is a great professor. She cares about her students and is interested in who they are outside of class. She is patient and understanding whenever a student doesn't understand a concept. This page scared me about having to take her class, but honestly she is great. Don't understand why she has such a bad rating. Don't be afraid of her.

I feel that if you go to the lectures pay attention and ask questions you will be okay. I didn't go to class that often and didn't do my homework so I didn't get an A, but I feel that if I tried hard enough I could've. This class is a whole bunch of work, get ready to spend time outside of class if you want a good grade.

She's kind of nice, but this class kicked my butt. Exams were extremely difficult, and I felt like all my preparation didn't accomplish much because the exams were just that difficult. Thought she might take it easier on the final. Nope. I'd have an easier time trying to find a job in this economy than getting a C in that. I regret my life choices.

Fine professor. There is a significant amount of work between online homework, written homework, quizzes, and exams, and was manageable but fairly over the top. Rhoads is very nice and a good teacher, but didn't make the course any easier. The answer to a true/false on a midterm was neither one time. Final was brutal. Not easy, not absurd.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Rhoads was a great lecturer. The way she presents the information is very clear and her notes format is easy to digest. The class in general is hard. In this class, if you stay on top of all of the work and meet with her then you will be fine. The quizzes every friday are annoying but they can help improve your grade.
Awful experience. Grades super harsh and absolutely not worth it.
She goes super fast, grades harshly and makes this class a huge time commitment more than it can ever be. She's condescending and rude.

Dr. Rhoads is a very caring professor and is always available to help you. Her exams are extremely fair and there are no surprises on what questions she'd ask. She may be a bit strict with deadlines and grading, but she's FAIR. Office hours really help and she's genuinely a really nice person.

def is strict in her grading, goes a bit fast in class. for some reason, i couldnt understand anything she was talking abt; class was so hard i felt like n also sm new material being thrown at u everyday; a lot of notes as well.didnt like ca group. idk if these issues were js me, but she is willing to meet w u n wants to help u succeed in her class
The class is very reasonable for a Vanderbilt Math class. Prof Rhoads is very nice but can be strict grader
Great prof! The class is well organized and structured. Expectations are always clear and lectures are easy to follow. Tests and written HWs are graded quite tough though.

Professor Taylor is a nice person and she is sweet. However in terms of professor she is a harsh grader. She will knock down point for the silliest mistakes and even though sometimes it's a good thing she knocks down way too many. Homework is challenging and not enough time to complete tests. There are weekly quizzes as well as weekly hw/

Overall, Professor Rhodes teaching style may not be suitable for everyone, particularly those who value a supportive and approachable instructor. If you're considering enrolling in one of her courses, be prepared for a demanding academic experience with limited opportunities for assistance or understanding.

Great professor with excellent lectures. Good in-class notes for studying. Exams have difficult questions, but homeworks prepare you well for them. Attendance is mandatory and the class is tough, but u have to expect it with this class. Other reviews are hating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rhoads is a great choice for diffeq. She is a great lecturer who makes the content easy to understand. Her exams are tough, but if you put in the work you can do well. The final was especially difficult. She is a sweet person who is willing to meet outside of class. Do not listen to the other reviews. I would take her again.
Her lectures were awesome and super clear. Class was not that hard and she had a lot of office hours if you need her. Wasn't a fan of the CA groups though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A good professor, but a tough grader. Very tough, there is nothing to argue about, any mistakes will be considered. It's very easy to get a A- or B+. Have to be ready to anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't know why she has a super low rating, she's awesome! Was able to teach the content super well! My favorite math prof. Had office hours which was super helpful! Although she's super nice, you really want to make sure you know the content because the Math Department at Vandy is just rough in general. Love her!!!

A great educator and math teacher, Prof. Rhoads is very underappreciated!! She taught the best math class I've ever taken at Vandy (and we all know the math department here is awful), and she was wonderful at communicating information and explaining concepts. OBV hw & test heavy and u have to come to class but you were gonna have to do that anyway.

Great at teaching, though exams were tough. Provides fantastic guided notes. Try to understand the proofs on the notes/HWs and pay attention in class. She's really approachable and willing to help. Ask questions, go to office hours, send emails, whatever you need. Responds quickly and generally gives really good explanations. Would take her again.

She is the worst teacher I have had at Vanderbilt. Her grading is incredibly strict and she gives no leeway with homework and on tests. She is lecture heavy but is very bad at explaining what she is doing, skips steps and goes very fast. I had her two separate times and these problems stayed consistent in both and she was very bad. Take Mr. Haley.

I do not recommend taking this class. She is a very difficult teacher and can be quite condescending at times. She is a bad professor that ruined my love for math. She never seemed to have the time to help out regarding homeworks, and is a really hard grader. Run as far away as possible. Take Prof Hailey!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She definitely has a hard time connecting with her students. Frequently very awkward and passive-aggressive. Exams were super stressful and the class overall was dreadful. Sorry, but would not recommend.

Hard prof, but also just hard class. Lock in for the second exam. Textbook is good for some stuff, but all you need is to pay attention in class and heavily review the in-class notes. Most importantly really take time to do the HW and understand the problems. gg

Absolutely do not enroll in this class if you have not taken calculus, or choose a different professor. Professor Rhoads is unapproachable, condescending, and unprofessional especially for such students who may lack the experience of others. Want to utilize office hours? Go to another professor. Absolutely do not choose her for Calc1200.
Sometimes it's better to skip some stages in college. One of those stages is called Prof rhoads.
horrible.

Prof Rhoads is super organized and pretty good at lecturing. She provides a lot of practice and structures class time pretty well. 4 midterms across the semester is super stressful but she is accessible to questions and gives you the materials to succeed. Overall, good prof the content is just a lot

I found the classwork not too difficult. She does assign a lot of homework, but normally they aren't time-consuming, and she is extremely helpful during office hours. If you do the work and ask questions when you have them you'll be fine. She's also pretty nice and seems to want her students to do well (took 1201 but there's no option for that)
Avoid her for 1200 and 1201 worst class ive taken at vanderbilt

She is trying to change how she used to act, but it's not working at all. I don't feel like I am learning anything in her class because all she does is solve problems rather than explain how to solve them and when she tries to explain herself it's so vague. She's also very awkward to talk to, it just feels like she has no soul.

Very straightforward class and posts lecture outlines to fill in during class which is super helpful. If you need help with hw go to office hours and she will basically give you the answers. I took her for 1200 and 1201 and if you put in the work you should be able to get a good grade especially if you have calc background.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Rhoads made calc so much more difficult. Not only is she a really hard grader, she also frequently makes errors on her notes which makes studying for exam 10x harder. She is quite condescending in her lectures and doesn't seem to want to help her students. The exams are an absolute disaster and there are so many hws. Save yourself, RUN!

The lectures she puts out online are fine, but in class when she "teaches them" is when it goes downhill. As every other review has mentioned, she's very condescending. A majority of the students go to the other professors for office hours since we all don't want to deal with her attitude. She takes attendance very seriously unlike the other profs.
She is pretty clear with homework and explains things pretty well, though in a very condescending manner that becomes frustrating. She takes attendance and tardiness v seriously

Disagree with reviewers that said she was difficult and condescending. She was clear in lectures and concise with homework outside class at office hours. If you have questions, visit her and she'll give you answers. TA can tear up HW grades. I sat at back on phone every class, but could see difficulty for someone who's never taken Calc before.

I stopped asking questions cause her tone makes it seem like she thinks you're dumb. She talked too slow and I was literally fighting sleep every lecture. She talks about stuff that sometimes aren't on the tests. She mentioned this being her first job after finishing her PHD and you can tell cause she doesn't really know how to use the time well.

She expects us to understand everything that she's going to teach before she teaches it. During class, she'll ask a question and stare at us for a while for an answer and when we don't answer she'll start talking again with a shady tone. She loves to spend too much time talking to us, that she always ends up ending class late (EVERY SINGLE DAY).

tbh I agree w the reviewer who said she makes it hard to ask questions. she's very condescending: asked a question during class, & she proceeded to tell me (in front of the entire) "yeah..you definitely need to come to office hours." Like im sorry I didn't. grasp the concept of delta and epsilon in two seconds when I legit have never taken calc.

Literally my favorite professor my freshman year. If you actually put in the effort, you'll do fine in the class. She held office hours almost every day for kids that were struggling, she actually cared about the students got to know us, and she was just all around awesome. I signed up for her 1201 class next semester because I liked her so much.

definitely Wasn't as willing to help as other professors and doesn't create a safe place to ask questions, often in class someone will ask a question and her response will start by mentioning that this is material we should already know, making those who are really confused afraid to ask questions. She also equates confusion with a lack of effort.

just graduated and started med school, but i had to come back and support this GEM of a woman. truly one of the best stem profs and vandy- incredibly kind and also a great preparation for the mcat and med school.

I cannot emphasize enough...if she is an option to take biochem, or frankly any upper level class with...you should do everything possible to get in her section. Truly a highlight of being premed at vandy. She is the sweetest prof I've had here and shows she cares about her students through everything she does. Made me proud to be a bcb major.
Chill but informative class. Grade is entirely determined by tests and papers, but if you just pay attention in class you will get an A on everything. Very accessible and helpful outside of class.

I am a Dr. Tallman fangirl through and through. She is such an inherently kind and inviting person who genuinely cares about student wellbeing and learning. Exams always have averages >93 but the content is always super applicable to other classes/content in the biochem sphere. If you have the chance TAKE HER!!!!
One of the kindest professors I've ever had, lectures were always very good, never felt lost, really liked the exam style

Actually one of the best professors I've had at Vandy hands down. Genuinely one of the kindest people ever! She explains things so well and crams so much content into her exams, but somehow has the highest averages of any STEM class I've taken (~90s). Super accessible outside of class and honest about expectations. Take her!! She's amazing!

Genuinely my favorite professor I've had at vandy. Really cares about her students and makes an effort to learn everyone's names! Exams were not bad at all but I feel like I still learned so much in her section and I was able to focus on learning and understanding the content rather than just figuring out how to cram/do decent on the exam itself.

One of the most caring STEM professors at Vandy. Genuinely wants to see her students succeed and has straight up said her goal is everyone gets a 100 on her exams. Prepares you well for the MCAT too! Strongly recommend.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Really wants students to do well and learn. It is clear she cares about overall student wellbeing and was just an absolute delight to have as a professor.

This was her first time teaching and although she got off to a rough start she really hit stride about halfway through. She has a very different approach to teaching from most of the rest of the department, but not in a bad way. She really wants all of her students to succeed. She wrote extremely fair exams, and was transparent about expectations.

This is her first semester teaching, and tbh it shows. Course material feels watered down compared to other profs. She is constantly saying she doesn't want people to overthink questions, but the result seems to be that she doesn't want people to think critically about the material. If you actually want to learn biochem, look elsewhere.

Professor Triana is very nice, but the class is a little boring. It is 25% participation based and the participation rubric is ambiguous. Her final exam was difficult and had a lot that was not taught in the class. Also, there was a lot of reading HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Participation really matters, and is graded ambigously by her and the TAs. One final exam given with no help or study guide, poorly structured. Group project she grades fairly, maybe a little harsh. Class is basically if you can remember vocab and apply it the way she wants you to. Readings are not needed at all.

Nice professor, but the worst class I've taken  The 20% participation grade is evaluated entirely at will with 0 explanation. The exam is long and questions are very subjective with no help or study guide provided. It's so poorly structured no amount of studying would help. The course material is outdated and has no relevance to any modern career.

My biggest issue with this class is that 50% of your overall grade in graded at the level of a graduate student. She expects grad-level work out of your group project and you don't even know what you got on it until weeks after the final. The final was also 70 extremely difficult questions that were just not covered in class. So disappointing!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never had a professor or high school teacher as bad as Maria Triana. She does not hold office hours, she grades like it's a 3000-level class, and the final was 70 questions, some of which felt completely unfair. I would not recommend anyone take this class; it was the first class I have ever cried over!
While his lectures are not very interesting, he is a great guy, and his tests + homework were very reasonable. If you pay attention in class, the content is not difficult to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice guy, really chill. Great lectures that he is genuinely doing his best to make engaging. No mistakes on the slides, everything is clear. Exams are straightforward and actually easy (averages are in 80s) if you understand the models well. Idk what happened last semester with all the bad reviews, but he is a really solid prof

DO NOT TAKE CESAR!! By far the worst macro professor. His lectures are full of so many typos its not worth taking notes. Taught 95% of the material to myself. Class average on the 1st exam was 62% no partial credit. Office hours are a waste of time.
great lecturer, and although some concepts are challenging, he does a good job of trying to get everyone to understand. Getting an A is obtainable for everyone as long as you put in the effort

Difficulty of exams were disproportionate to classwork - filled with "curveballs" and averages were in 50s/60s. Exam curves were very helpful though to get an A in the class. Learned everything from the TA, who was great - you may do end up doing well in the class but prepare to go to stress out heavily exams. Overall way too challenging for Macro.

Professor Urquizo had engaging lectures and was highly accessible outside of class. He gave multiple grade boosters, partially because our class needed it and partially because he grades tough. You must be decent at math to do well. I enjoyed his class; negative reviews mostly stem from people who don't know math or didn't study or attend class.

NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS homework is graded on checkmark basis meaning only possible grades are 100 70 or 0, there is no partial credit and no error carry in multipart questions(mistake in part A results in a 0 for the whole problem) Mock exams were not even close to representative of exams, never covered exam materials in class. TAKE WITH ANYONE ELSE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor César gives lectures that are very difficult to follow, and the lack of a corresponding textbook for many of the units makes it very all or nothing if you can learn the material from the lectures/slides. It is difficult to pinpoint the difficulty of the course as the content and tests were difficult, however, the curves are very generous.

Do not be discouraged by the other reviews. Content was communicated very clearly. Professor César is a very intelligent guy who is very helpful in office hours/over email. Exams were not cake but were always curved significantly. The median final grade was an A.

The material is very challenging, but he is an easy grader who curves heavily and does a very good job of preparing students for the tests. Tests always have a curveball question significantly harder than the homeworks and practice exams, but he factors that into the curve. Median grade for the class was an A. Homework, easy 100, worth 25% of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Despite the exams being computation-heavy, lecture slides focused almost entirely on theoretical concepts and barely any review materials are posted. All of the professor's computational work during lectures is completed on a chalkboard with rushed explanations. Tests are unpredictable, with only a few total examples to study from for each midterm

Urquizo so frequently mess up his lecture slides that we spend the next class just going over and fixing his mistakes after he updated. He states that he doesn't want us to memorize formulas (then the TA tells us just memorize the formulas anyways) but to understand the intuition and proceeds to not build any intuition.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure why everyone is giving terrible reviews. Cesar is a great lecturer and is incredibly passionate - yes grading is heavily based on tests, but the curve on the exams are very very generous. You will get an A in the class if you put in some effort.

TAKE ANY OTHER CLASS if I could give him a 0 and a 6 I would. You know all those jokes about what's taught in class vs what's on the exams? This is that class, mock exams were misleading and he expected you to learn new methods and manipulate models in new ways for the first time on the exams which are 75% of your grade +no partial credit at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS HE IS TERRIBLE. 2 midterms, a final, and homework each made up 25% of the final grade. On homework he rounded your grades DOWN to a 100, a 70, or a 0, there was no partial credit or error carry meaning on multipart problems an error in part A gave a zero for the whole problem, which lost me 30% on a midterm. AVOID AT ALL COSTS

It is hard to understand what he is trying to teach, way too hard for an intermediate class. Averages for the midterm was in the 60s. He is a good / smart person, but definitely does not know how to teach properly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Very good guy but... DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

Learned everything from TA. His slides are essentially useless as they just are loaded with junk that he uses as examples, but includes very little of the math that we actually need to know for exams. 

The few times he uses the board he simplifies everything in his head making it impossible to follow.

It is evident that Cesar is very intelligent and knowledgable in the topic, however the lectures and mock exams he posts are not remotely similar to what we see in exams, which is 75% of your grade. There are "curveballs" on the exams that students have never been introduced to. Way too difficult for intermediate class

Very lecture heavy, do not take this class if you cannot pay attention to every single detail and be able to apply in complex situations that you have never heard about before. Test average was like a 65 on both midterms but he curves to have an average of 85. Lots of people still did poorly overall. Almost too smart of a dude which makes it hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall nice professor but if extremely unresponsive and unclear with instructions inside and outside the classroom. The biggest problem is that he makes it seem as if it will be the easiest class you'll take at the start of the semester but will mess your grade up at the end because he is in a bad mood. Most boring lectures I've ever sat through.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely unclear instructions about the grading. Providing grades with no feedback. Always have something happened at home that excused procrastination. Never replied emails and was hard to reach out. Not care about students. The class itself was easy, but the communication with professor was horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading criteria is unclear and he honestly didn't care about students at all. Barely reply to emails and won't help you with your grades even though he didn't explain them in advance and the grading is weird. Won't recommend to take.

Underwood is the complete opposite of strict. This class is pretty unorganized and you just have to show up to do well. Not a single person paid attention in class and I think everyone got at least an A-. Guy is a light grader. If this floats your boat then I would consider taking him. I will say he doesn't respond to emails and grades take a while

Not an impressive instructor. Disorganized and too laidback. Obviously knowledgeable but kinda doesn't matter when you don't expect much from your students. Maybe ok if you want a chill instructor but I care about school and it often felt like he did not

We primarily studied Daoism, reading fundamental texts like the Daodejing and the Zhuangzi. Professor explains etymology and historical context behind the texts, which is really useful. The class itself is very chill, focused around light, daily readings. Underwood is like the opposite of a stressful person. Definitely recommend.

Content itself can be confusing and sometimes he's not the best at explaining concepts but wasn't a super difficult class. Recommend to do practice problems from the textbook when preparing for quizzes/tests because sometimes he uses the problems not assigned for homework on the exams.

This class was easy enough but it could've been better.. Prof Underwood was very inaccessible via email and gave no feedback on papers, unless you planned a meeting with him (which he sometimes would not show up to). The content was pretty easy to understand and lectures were okay. Overall, nice guy and easy class but boring lectures.

Told us at the beginning of the course that his classes would mostly just be regurgitating the textbook. Worth going to class because he explains it more clearly than the textbook + credit for attendance. Really tries to get you to understand content, very accessible outside of class, held study sessions. Confusing at times but office hours helped.

I took 20th Century Cont. with Professor Underwood and this man deserves more reviews. The content in class was super dense and difficult (thanks Heidegger), but he was very understanding and he's a very fair grader when it comes to papers. Love the man and definitely take him if you're interested in philosophy or need to get rid of an AXLE credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Underwood is really chill and understanding. Always makes time to answer questions and go over areas of struggle. That said, he can sometimes struggle to explain complex concepts to students which can lead to some confusion. But overall, I would recommend this class if you are interested or need axle credit.

He's a nice professor and clearly loves to teach, but the class is incredibly disorganized. He covers good topics if you're interested in HR or consulting, but his lectures go on tons of tangents or have nothing to do with the module's content. It's tough to dislike him as a professor because he is so likable, but I can't say that I learned a lot.

I liked the class model of the folder of optional/some required Brightspace readings and the knowledge checks. Not a stressful class. If you take some notes too, you're really set. Prof Barzel makes an effort to make lectures engaging. Very relevant class for our futures in the workforce.

GREAT PROFESSOR! He is fabulous and clearly cares about the course content. He is so passionate about his course material and about the students' learning and is super relatable. He's the kind of professor that makes you want to read the material and participate even though attendance isn't required. Highly recommend

Ur was an awesome lecturer and made the coursework easily digestible. He was an awesome mentor outside of class, and I've gotten so much from his feedback and guidance in things related to business and career. Awesome guy! Highly rec!
Extremely easy class. Take-home quizzes and the final was a presentation. Professor Barzel is very knowledgeable, fun, and accessible outside of class.

Amazing professor. Even though the workload was light, I learned so much and found the class very helpful. Professor Barzel is very caring, the discussions are very intriguing, and he makes the class fun. Highly recommend as a HODL class or an elective.

Professor Barzel was one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. I genuinely felt excited to go to class because his lectures were so engaging. Not too difficult either, but still ended up learning a lot! Highly recommend taking any classes with him.

Favorite class this semester, one of my favorites at Vanderbilt. Learned a ton through in-class discussions , which he always kept very lively and interesting. Didn't overflow us with too much homework or out of class assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was my favorite professor this semester. He is really nice, and the workload is not too much.

Professor Usner is a solid professor as long as you do the bare minimum. He is very impartial, and if you do the weekly summary of the book (you don't actually have to read the book), then you should be fine. My two essays were definitely not my most inspired writing, and I still got A and A-. His lectures can be boring, and taking notes is smart.

Professor Usner is so kind and knowledgeable but classes were pretty slow. He takes attendance every day so definitely show up. The slides are not super helpful and you definitely need to take notes in class for the final and papers. You don't really need to read the books (I never did). He's passionate about his work and is understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty boring but it's clear he knows what he's talking about. Definitely won't be taking him again though. Take only if you realllllly care about the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. The lectures were a little dry but informative. Overall just a simple, "get through it" type of class. If you do the written assignments and are able to write a straightforward 5-page paper, I don't think you can get lower than a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: go to office hours !! this class was incredibly boring. make me realize that I don't want to be a history major. you must go to class to write notes about the lectures. he doesn't record it & the ppt usually only has pictures. 2 essays, weekly 1 pg single spaced, and a final
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are fascinating. Clearly cares a great deal about the subject matter. I try to read the weekly assignments when I can, but it's not necessary and the homework usually doesn't receive feedback. VERY easy grader, which is quite a relief at Vandy.

Usner isn't a bad professor; he's a very smart guy who's super nice, but my main issue is that he's painfully boring. He doesn't put notes on his PPTs, so you have to listen and take notes for the full 50 mins. Assigns a book a week but you don't really have to read them. If you're fine w/ boring lectures it should be easy, otherwise not the best.

Professor Usner clearly knows a TON about the class material. Assigns a book a week for discussion but you just need to read a few to write the essays. Only complaint: he lectures during class & doesn't put notes on the slides so you have to speed write the entire class. Come to class, take notes, follow the essay prompts and you'll likely get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took to fulfill AXLE. Honestly I just read the google books preview for the assigned readings and was able to do well in the class. Usner cares about his students and the subject material. His lectures are long and not much information is on the powerpoints so you need to take notes. Easy final, short papers, really enjoyed taking this class.

Professor Usner was very knowledgeable and was a super kind and approachable man. He assigned a book about every two weeks, but he was kind of a easy grader and was always willing to help (which means you don't really have to read all the books). Lectures can be long, though. Took attendance every day. Two 5-paged papers and a final exam.

The class can get boring at times, but it got better at the end of the year. Attendance and participation are a huge part of your grade. There are only two papers but they are ridiculously easy. He gives you all the information needed to succeed and he does his best to make the class interesting

Professor Usner is extremely knowledgeable and is very helpful if you go to his office hours. Grade is made of participation, two essays, and the final. The final is completely fair and won't be too hard if you take notes during the lectures. Lectures can be boring if you don't love the subject. Just go to class and take notes and you'll be fine.

I really enjoyed this class. Sometimes the lectures were a little dry, but other times I thought they were really interesting. Professor Usner is a very approachable professor, but he is so clear on his instructions and expectations that it isn't really even necessary to approach him. A  lot of reading is involved, a novel a week.

Loved this class! Attendance and participation are really important, as long as you take notes and he knows who you are, you're totally set. Two papers, final exam, and a hefty participation grade (attendance taken every day), so it's pretty easy to do well.

He is a very knowledgeable person, but his lectures are somewhat boring, although it might just be the topic. There are two papers, which are fairly easy, and a simple final. He checks attendance, though, so make sure you show up. You are also required to read one book a week and discuss it, but doing so isn't really necessary. Good for AXLE.
Solid professor. Pretty easy. He has an attendance policy. Go to all the classes, take notes, contribute, and you'll be fine. There are two papers. Work hard and them and you'll be set.

Don't get me wrong, Professor Usner knows his stuff. He is a very intelligent man with more knowledge about history than I can comprehend... but it is difficult not to fall asleep in his class. The lectures are very boring unless you are REALLY interested in the subject. Good class for AXLE requirement.
Solid history professor and lecturer.

Class meets once a week for two hours. You are 'required' to read one book a week, but nobody does. Attendance is half the grade, and a 20 page paper is the other half. Go to class, make half-baked contributions, and work your ass off on the paper and you'll be fine.

Classes were horribly boring. Never could understand what his point was or where he was getting at. No point in going to class- only grades were two papers. The papers you can do by looking at your textbook.

Dr. Usner is nice and really tries, but his lectures are boring as hell.  Probably due to the material (history of the US before 1865) rather than the teacher.  Class isn't hard at all.  Good for AXLE.  Easy to do well if you just read the book before the midterm.
He was a great professor; really cares about students. Would definitely take him again.

Professor Uhuegbu's class made me understand the difference between input and output when it comes to language learning. I realized I'm more effective in learning a language when using it practically in conversation or actively recalling words. He made us interact more often in class and I consider it useful since I improved more in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Led our discussion sections very well! An incredible TA who is very kind and engaging. His further discussion of class texts and ideas helped me understand the course better. I also really enjoyed his use of outside sources and personal stories to bolster ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super kind professor who was always extremely helpful and flexible. Sad to see him go.

This is just here to balance out my review from earlier in the sem. He prob deserves a 3.5 as a teacher and 3 difficulty. Super nice as a person and he clearly knows his stuff, but the class was very confusing. The hw's are insanely hard and the tests were not easy, but that is just the way 2212 is set up for all sections. They should change that.

Genuinely a nice guy, and wants you to get a good grade. He can get a little confusing during lecture and sometimes isn't the best at answering questions clearly. The class is easy enough to the point where that doesnt really matter though. Grind on the HWs and pay attention during class, you'll be fine.

Bruh. I heard from my friends who took this class last year that it'd be a breeze. This was definitely not the case. It's difficult to keep up in lecture and the Problem Sets are mad hard. Maybe if TA office hours were in person, this class would be easier but it was all online. Ghosh is not the move, sorry guys.

It's not so much Dr. Ghosh that's the issue. The homeworks for this class are literally impossible. I go to office hours and the TA's hint at the answers and then they're just wrong. Each homework is 10% and it's borderline impossible to get an A on any of them. The tests are so hard. See yall next semester when I retake it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: hes such a bad teacher. he puts stuff on the test that he doesnt teach. doesnt teach anything thats on the homework. take arena instead
terrible lecturer. can't answer questions. doesn't explain concepts thoroughly.
he is pretty terrible at explaining things in class. the homeworks are impossible unless you ask for help from a TA and the tests oftentimes have stuff that were not in the lectures.
Ghosh is definitely the best option for OS at Vandy. Ghosh >>>

Professor Ghosh is amazing and everyone I talk to in class absolutely loves him! He is super accessible outside class and will go out of his way to help you with homework questions. Quizzes are manageable. Definitely go for him if you have to take OS

I ended up taking 4 different classes at Vandy taught by Professor Ghosh because he is a very knowledgable professor who really wants his students to learn (even though the material can be dry). His powerpoints are thorough and detailed so you can use them to study, and his quizzes/tests are very fair. Not hard but learned a lot - def recommend him

Professor Ghosh is an amazing professor at Vanderbilt. He really cares about his students and this is the second time I've had him as a professor. The class isn't difficult as long as you pay attention to his lectures. Networking can be a difficult subject to learn, but Professor Ghosh is very patient with how he teaches. I would take him again.

Prof. Ghosh really cares about the course subject matter (networking is one of his main research areas), and that shows in his approach to teaching. Lectures are supplemented with PPTs, which make great study material. Hes very open to answering student questions and seems to take a genuine interest in our learning. Take networks with Ghosh!

Dr. Ghosh was very caring about students. He just wants everyone to do well. It took a bit of getting used to to his lecture style but once I did the lectures were pretty clear and solid. The class was super easy, at times even a bit too easy. Super approachable guy, great class if you want an chill CS elective.

Professor Ghosh is a really great guy. He's easily one of the most caring professors I've had at Vanderbilt; he really just wants everyone to understand the material and do well. He's really approachable and gives good help on lectures/homework. Some of the assignments are a little vague, but if you go to him for help he'll clear anything up.

Prof Ghosh is helpful in his office hours and will clarify specific confusions. The content is presented in slides, not a textbook, but attending class is still useful because he explains the sometimes confusing slides. Overall a great professor with lots of wisdom to share. Highly recommend.

Great dude and very helpful. The class material is dry but if there's anything you need to review, he'll walk it through with you very well during office hours. Although he is relatively new to the university, hope he moves up in Vandy.
Hes awesome

I love professor Ghosh. He is an extremely nice guy who cares a lot about his students. His lectures can be dry at certain times, but the powerpoints are so detailed and helpful. He is not a hard professor so long as you try and study, he doesn't try and trick you, he genuinely wants you to do well in the course and learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Funny guy, thick accent. Didn't learn a lot in the class and the material is inherently very boring, but he was a funny and caring professor. Curves all the grades a ton, with 60% of the class getting an A. Will give you back points if you email and reason with him. So glad I took him over Piot, whose class suffered under his regimen.

Some of the grades I received were suspect, but he was always open to talking through it. A very funny professor if you listen to him lecture. Quiz/exam questions sometimes unclear, but he is willing to explain what he wants if you ask during the quiz.
Really easy class. Sometimes the quizzes are hard but he'll curve them. His lectures are occasionally boring but other than that he's an excellent professor. Also very nice guy.

Professor Ghosh is extremely caring about his students and will go to great lengths to help as many people as he can, even if that means helping outside of class and his office hours. He will always make time and try his best to make sure his students understand the material.
Nice guy
Great teacher and cares a lot about his students
Nice person and caring teacher, but not great at writing tests clearly
He is a very hardworking teacher. He is very caring and I can feel that. However, sometimes his lectures can get a bit hard to understand.

Professor Uyanik is a fantastic lecturer and cares a lot about his students. He really wants his students to learn. His class is well organized, and he is available outside the class. Plus he is always in a good mood and he is super friendly. Too bad I can't take any more classes with him.

Caglar is a great professor. He is really nice and helpful, and his lectures are clear . Homework, quizzes and tests are all of reasonable amount and difficulty. Multi is not supposed to be easy, but he puts lots of effort into teaching and helping students understand difficult concepts. I wish I could take other math classes with him. Solid choice

Professor Uyanik is probably the best professor I've had so far at Vanderbilt. He genuinely cares about his students and is able to break difficult concepts down and make them understandable for us. During class, he really tries his best to make us understand the concepts and goes through many practice problems where we can ask questions. 10/10

Professor Uyanik is the best! His lectures are awesome, and his tests are fair (albeit tough). Do not be disheartened by the high difficulty score. Calc II is one of the hardest subjects, but Professor Uyanik does an amazing job explaining everything.

He is a fantastic lecturer and really wants his students to do well. Yeah, it's a hard class, but if you take 30 minutes a day to do the optional homework, pay attention in class, and go to office hours when you don't get something you'll be fine. Everyone I have talked to has said he is their favorite professor here. Also a very enjoyable guy.
Class is brutally hard, but Professor Uyanik does a very good job of explaining things and is especially helpful in office hours.

Professor Uyanik is a phenomenal lecturer and is very easy to access outside of class for office hours. The material is hard (as expected) and it may be easy to fall behind If you don't do the homework or go to office hours. His best feature is the clarity of his explanations of complicated topics.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I adored Prof. Urban. Although readings are dense for her Theories of Religion class, she is always very supportive of what undergrads have to add to discussion. She does not hold her undergrads to the same standards as her grad students and grades accordingly. She is good at facilitating discussion and creating an inclusive atmosphere for input.

I had such a great experience with Professor Urban in her Jewish Theories Class I took her Zionism Class the following Semester! If you put forth any effort at all in the course she will recognize it and is one of the most helpful professors out there if you have any problems. I highly recommend her and have loved both of her classes I have taken.

This class is horrible. She expects graduate work from students who have absolutely no foundation in Judaism. Extremely confusing, and very boring. Never taking a Vanderbilt Judaism class ever again. What a shame.

I highly recommend this class. The material is really fascinating, and Dr. Urban loves what she teaches. The readings aren't always easy to digest, but she's always willing to help if you go to office hours. Ditto for assignments--if you come to class and participate in the discussions, you'll be fine.

I recommend any class with her. She's very passionate and knowledgeable, encourages class discussion, and challenges you to think critically, write better and grow as a student. Very approachable and always available outside of class to help you in any way. Very fair grader-you'll do well as long as you show interest and do the assignments.

To be clear, her class is not easy. But, those who attend and who demonstrate interest in the material leave more informed than they might expect to be from an intro course. While her grading is not easy, she looks after those who are dedicated.

Professor Urban is definitely passionate about what she does, and it really comes across. Attendance is highly suggested because a lot of the grade is based on class participation, but it's never overwhelming. Definitely a class worth taking!
Demanding but engaging

Professor Urban was very intimidatin, demanding, and opinionated. I was scared to write papers after the class was over, when I really used to like writing. This class couldnt decide whether it was history or art/literature analysis, so it ended up being neither. Directives werent clear enough for a class intended for freshmen.
This course is not an intro level course, instead of basics Professor Urban delves into the abstract right away. Readings are dry, but there is only a midterm and a final exam.

As an introductory course in Jewish Studies, Professor Urban's class exceeded my expectations. Her knowledge and passion inspired me. Her clear and articulate presentation encouraged me to examine critically my biased views of Judaism. I thus not only learned a great deal but feel that I am now a better citizen of our diverse world. Great course!
No Comments
Great professor.  Friendly and knowledgeable, helpful outside of class.  A little shy, but great when you approach her.  Cute.
defintely do not take her intro classes...they are not intro at all

Umar is very clear about his expectations in class and does a good job explaining concepts.  If you're premed and want a physics class that will prepare you for the MCAT, take Umar. He won't bog you down with extraneous information, and his tests are easy.  Got an A with a moderate amount of effort.
Trust me, you will never find another course easier than this one.
great proff
Awesome....go to class, take notes, do the practice tests and practice HW and its an easy A
Completely easy, but teaches the basic concepts quite well.  Definitely get this guy if you have to take this for premed or something

His lectures are really boring, but go the day before a test as he tells you everything that will be on the exam.  The tests set up is the same as the year before and therefore they surve as a good study guide.  I highly suggest taking his course
See comment below.

Accent a little hard @ first. He realizes that the main concepts of the class are more important than difficult and tangent applications that would otherwise make the class hard.  Sometimes the lecture is slow but this is a really nice guy.  Tests have NO SUPPRISES and HW is strait foreward. Anyone can gat a good grade w/ marginal effort.

Gen chem 2 is by far a lot harder than Gen chem 1 and the tests are all the same so Dr. Todd is a clear choice. She gives the most practice problems and the most review of the content, and for a class like this the practice was extremely helpful. Just don't be late and don't talk over her and you're fine. Had her for both semesters and I love her!

Solid lecturer, but class is still very difficult. Be prepared to spend a lot of time studying outside of lectures. Exams are challenging. In lectures, students may be called on in front of the class, which can feel uncomfortable. Personally didn't feel very comfortable asking questions during lectures or office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She might be a decent teacher but she is one of the meanest professors I have had. Gen chem is a weedout class for sure, but she does not help at all. She enjoys belittling students and I have seen her discouraging people from future careers in stem because "I don't think you have what it takes." Avoid at all costs.

My advice to anyone taking Todd would be go to her office hours. She is very knowledgable and gives practical advice. She also knows a lot about medical school and the pathway to that and she will provide you with a lot of support and help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My biggest advice to anyone taking Todd would be GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS. I took her for chem 1601 and ended up not getting the grade I wanted so I met her after the semester ended. She is very knowledgable and gives practical advice. I regret not going to her office hours while I had the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Todd is a good professor, she knows her stuff and is very helpful, especially during office hours. She also provides a lot of resources to help you succeed. The class and exams are tough but there's no avoiding that. She can get very agro if you're late or talking when she is. Also flipped classroom style takes up a lot of time.
this class sent me into insanity. tara todd made me want to commit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Flip lectures ruin the life.

Flipped classroom-- it really does not work for me better than normal lecture style. The video's are a drag and oftentimes you end up speeding through them and getting stressed about the tophat's due at 10pm. Avoid if you have enough control to study on your own time and do practice problems outside of lecture before the test.

She lowkey gets a bad rep for having the flipped classroom w extra videos to watch outside class, but I think her method of teaching prepares you best for the tests. Gen Chem is going to take effort, but I think with Dr. Todd, you have the best chance of getting an A.

Dr. Todd, while always meaning well and being extremely helpful in office hours, teaches in a flipped classroom style and does not lecture, meaning you will be watching hours of videos every night to learn content.

Dr. Todd is amazing! She uses a flipped classroom style and even though the videos can be up to 2 hours sometimes, it really pays off. During class you work on practice problems the entire time with some lecturing here and there, but I found it really valuable to have practice every lecture and it really helped for exams and studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Bro don't do her 8am! She is doing a flipped classroom so she post a crazy amount of lecture videos for you to watch outside of class and they are due at 9pm. She does not teach in class and she is insanely passive aggressive. You can participate in class, go to office hours, and she still makes you feel stupid and is plain rude to you!

Lots of people complain about Todd and her flipped class method, but as I got used to her, I found it really helpful. While sometimes there were 2 hours worth of videos, I liked being able to practice in class, and that's why I did so well overall. She wants you to succeed, so if you put in the time to practice, it is very achievable to get an A.
Flipped classroom style, so be prepared for in class graded assignments and online lectures to watch for HW. Lots of HW and practice problems, but it prepares you well for the exam.

Since it's a flipped classroom, be prepared to spend at least an hour on lecture notes outside of class. Very obnoxious initially but once you get used to it you realize that it's lowkey more beneficial, especially since lecture time is used for practice worksheets with LAs. She provides lots of resources compared to some other professors.
great but I don't want to take it again.

Todd teaches with a flipped classroom style, meaning you have about an hour and a half of lecture videos to watch before every class. However, this means you'll spend the whole class period doing problems with LA's supporting you which really helps cement your understanding. It's essentially double the practice, so I think its definitely worth it.

Dr. Todd switched to flipped Gen Chem 1 for the first time this semester, which can be challenging, but if you put in the work, you'll do great. She's clear about exam expectations, super accessible, and offers tons of support—all her videos and slides, multiple office hours, quick email replies. Complaints come from those not trying. 5/5 prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a decent-ish teacher. Has a temper and will walk out on your class. Minor inconsistencies in how well she pulls off flipped classroom.

Tara Todd was an excellent teacher, the one everyone told you to get. Well, she went on a villain arc and now makes you watch every lecture before class in videos and answer quizzes, and doesn't teach you things that are as relevant as just reading the textbook. She is short and rude. Do yourself a favor, and take tainter.

Chem in general is difficult but Todd is a good professor. She is organized and offers the most resources for students to succeed. She is also genuinely caring about her students but can feel very passive aggressive at times when she gets mad and starts yelling at the class or during office hours.

Do as many practice problems as you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Todd is an amazing lecturer. The contents are heavy, but she tries to go above and beyond to ensure everyone understands the material. Read the textbook, complete the assignments, and attend her office hours. The pacing is challenging at the beginning, but Dr. Todd will support you learn the content through worksheets, videos, etc. Great class!

Gen chem is very difficult + exams are the same but Todd knows her stuff and is organized. She has an attitude and will be kinda hostile but her slides are good. Has LAs and coffee chats to get extra help and posts extra resources/review. Top hats in class are very fast/ hard to get points. I would personally prefer Tainter but Todd is a close 2nd.

gen chem is always going to be impossible but dr. todd made it somewhat manageable. she can be veryyyy passive aggressive at times (especially if you corner her with too many questions or move around during her lectures?) but she's not a bad professor whatsoever. the LA system she has is super helpful. i personally prefer tainter but todd isnt bad.

Todd was pretty great. She can be a little mean or rude at times but she also goes the extra mile for students that care. Go to class, read the textbook, do all the problem sets, and you'll do well. I think half the problem with gen chem is that it's a freshman class and we all just need to adjust.

Everybody gases gen chem up for being the hardest class ever. It simply is not, and Tara Todd is a really good professor. If you read the tophat textbook as she teaches her lectures are extremely clear and she posts SO many resources for you to learn and practice. Suggested problems, past exams, and great notes. She is quite sassy, but worth it!!!

Oh what to say about Dr Todd. She is quite helpful in office hours, but as far as her lectures are concerned, they are loosely related to the content that appeared on the exams this semester, and left most students quite underprepared. She also randomly crashed out and leaves the room so that's fun.

As a person who took IB Chem HL, this class was easy. Most content I've learned, the ones I haven't were extensions of IB concepts. The textbook is technically all you need, but Todd has these bonus attendance TopHat questions you want to be in-class for. Good slides, uploads optional questions. Aktiv questions forces you to not cram.

She's a good professor and provides so many materials and opportunities to do well in this class. She is hands down one of the best chemistry professors to take for CHEM1601. If she is an 8 am, however, I would recommend Daniels or even Tainter as well since an 8 am chemistry class can be rough.

CHEM1601 is a weed-out class and it is taught like one. It is difficult but doable. Dr. Todd is cut-throat and curt. However, it's worth it to take Dr. Todd if you are taking 1601 as she gives the most resources, has good lecture slides that are given for notetaking, and provides more opportunities of extra credit than the other professors.

I decided to tank the 7 AM wakeup to take Professor Todd over other chemistry professors. This proved to be a grave mistake. She often skipped lecture material during class, blatantly called out students for asking dumb questions, and had meltdowns which caused her to storm out of class early. Caused a very hostile learning environment for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ez material at first - gets way harder over time. Lectures & slides were confusing during tough material. Todd would jump back and forth, leave stuff incomplete, and sometimes just not explain things making it hard to take notes. My advice, READ THE TEXTBOOK FOR EVERY CHAPTER BEFORE THE EXAM, GO THRU OTHER PROFESSOR'S SLIDES (Tainter!), AND STUDY!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Todd teaches a hard class as well as anyone realistically can but here classes became harder and harder to handle throughout the year. On many occasions toward the end of the year she skipped content or review and stormed out of class early. She makes helpful materials available. She sometimes came off as abrasive during office hours.

Look, Gen Chem is designed to be a weed out class and as such, it's a very hard class. However, I really only have good things to say about Professor Todd. Her lectures and slides were incredibly helpful  (even though she did have a couple meltdowns during class) and she is a very kind professor.

Tara Todd constantly has meltdowns during lectures and will hold back material based on the way she feels. At times, I would fear going to class because of the sheer emotions. Her lectures were alright but nothing compared to Tainter or Daniels, try to avoid her (and gen chem) at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Todd is probably the best professor in the gen chem department, however gen chem is just an extremely difficult class. Only Todd and one other professor have LAs in class and Todd offers extra credit through weekly chem coffee chats. The thing is, she did have some like random meltdowns / freakouts? It was a bit off putting ...

Dr. Todd is a great lecturer and explains concepts really well. Sometimes, the lectures were slower paced, so we would end up cramming many slides to keep up with the other professors. Tests are difficult, so practice a lot from the textbook and aktiv. Coming from non-morning person, the 8am is not worth it, Tainter is a great professor as well.

Dr. Todd was a great professor. Yes, Gen Chem is hell, but she is the best professor you are gonna get. She is very helpful at office hours (don't be intimidated to attend), and although she can be harsh, she does so to maintain respect. Her expectations and demands are clear and reasonable, and she is actually quite funny and nice.

Tara Todd is the reincarnation of true evil. She is condescending and have daily meltdowns. The gen chem department is the reason I went to the Vanderbilt psychiatric hospital for a week btw. The department is incredibly toxic and these professors take pride in that (genuinely who tf finds pride in that???)
The class is unnecessary difficult. do not take this class.

Gen Chem is challenging, but Professor Todd makes it bearable. Attend class, do the Aktiv homework, and utilize unstuck ai for extra study prep - it's a game-changer alongside the textbook. She's tough but fair, and genuinely cares about student success.

Gen Chem is hard for anyone, but Todd made it genuinely bearable. Lectures were dense but useful when reviewing for exams. Stay on top of Aktiv hw and attend class (even though the 8am is tough, it's worth it). In-class TopHat & LA coffee chats give grade buffer points at end of sem. She's really nice once you get to know her (attend office hours!)

Gen Chem 2 is not easier than Gen Chem 1, so don't be fooled, but Dr. Todd is hands down the best professor for chem. She is thoughtful, caring, and provides her students with the most support and resources compared to other professors. Taking an 8am isn't easy, but Dr. Todd is 100% worth it. If you're unsure which professor to take, just take Todd

People love to overrate the difficulty of Gen Chem. Many people do not study enough and blame Dr. Todd. While there is a lot of material, the tests are very straight forward, and you just need to study. All of the test material is given to you in the form of slides and textbook. Do NOT freak out. Just study and you will do great.

Dr. Todd is a great professor. She knows how to teach the course content effectively to students and gives hard example problems in class to prepare students for the exam. For the top hat extra credit, make sure to read the group work as soon as possible. The professor may appear strict, but in reality, Dr. Todd cares about her students.

Coming from no chem experience, I was so nervous for Gen Chem but Dr. Todd and her class were amazing! She's got a lot of personality but really explains concepts well. Dr. Todd is the most organized gen chem professor and her section has the most incredible learning assistants who really help you individually. Could not recommend her more!

If you can get past her sense of humour and sass you should definitely be taking her class for gen chem! (Personally I thought she was hilarious) Although 8 am sounds terrible, you will truly benefit from her class as she writes all the exams and is an excellent teacher. Attendance is SO mandatory or you'll miss graded in-class questions.

Dr. Todd is a must for gen chem! Her lectures are very well organized and the group work in class is great practice. She is very accessible outside of class and wants to help students succeed. She also writes the exams and provides extra study materials for her students only. Having Dr. Todd as a professor was so worth the 8am!

Gen Chem is a tough course but Dr. Todd made the experience not as horrible. Her lectures were dense but very informative and were useful in reviewing for midterms. You have to stay very on top of the online homework assignments. In-class questions and coffee chats provided extra credit that helps give your grade a buffer.

Chem 1601 is a very hard class but Todd made it easier. She is very accessible outside of class and can explain concepts in multiple different ways until you understand it. She really cares about her students. I also found her lectures to be pretty enjoyable.

The course is unnecessary difficult. If you want to get a high GPA, try your best to avoid this course. Her PPT is confused. You can do review through her PPT. She teaches too fast and rarely highlight important points. She's not worth getting up early for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Take Professor Todd if you can. She writes the exams and her lectures are most similar to the exam content. She makes concepts easier to understand and although she can come off as a bit rude, she is still an amazing professor. Definitely go to class and read the textbook.
chem 2 was harder for me than chem 1; todd is the best gen chem prof though, so I recommend her over anyone else; very funny and knowledgeable, go to class and do your homework and you'll be fine

Best gen chem prof by far--hilarious, good lectures, accessible outside of class; no matter who you take, exams will be the same and fairly difficult for most; study daily, do your Aktiv assignments ahead of time, don't skip class, do the questions at the end of chapters in the textbook, and good luck!

Todd is a gem at Vandy. Her lectures are helpful, and she has guided notes if you want them. Office hours are always helpful and she really cares about student learning and success.

Take her class if you can!

Definitely the best gen chem professor. Although the class was challenging, you will be fine if you utilize office hours and do the recommended problems. Though she may seem intimidating and rude initially, she is extremely caring and helpful if you go to office hours and wants you to succeed. Take her if you are an incoming freshman!!!

Professor Todd's class was one of my favorites (I'm a chemical engineer and chemistry major). Although she could be condescending sometimes, she cares for her students and makes an effort to converse outside and inside of class. I would take her for Gen Chem if you're an upcoming freshman.

Take another chem prof. She is extremely rude, sassy, and will go on tangents in office hours instead of helping. She has an ego unlike any other professor. She is unresponsive to emails and will not help. Good luck because no matter how much studying you do, she'll make the test impossible. The questions are not similar to class problems.

cares way too much about getting students in trouble and is always irritated. makes attendance so incredibly annoying by requiring you to submit in-class questions and to submit pictures of your work separately but she always makes them close in the middle of class before everyone submits them and it's always a whole ordeal to just get your credit

Todd is the most amazing chem professor. She is extremely caring (and sassy) and wants you to do well. Study a little bit of material every day and go to office hours and you will do fine. The class is very difficult, but there are so many resources to utilize!

everyone on here said todd was worth the 8 am... she was DEF not. not only was i extremely sleep deprived, but the exams were also super stressful and hard. you really have to learn how to STUDY outside of the class for this course. the third midterm avg was in the high 60s yet no curve, and no easier final. good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Todd is a pretty good chem professor, but there's only so much she can do in her class time. She has in-class practice, offers review sessions, so it's not hard to find help for the course. However, it's obviously gen chem so it's a tough class, but she gives you all the tools you need to succeed.
i hate gen chem
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gen Chem is a very difficult class especially if you have not taken AP chem. I found her class to be worth the 8am. I would recommend going to office hours, she is very accessible and is looking to help you. She cares about her students in and out of the classroom and was very supportive of me during my first semester in college.

honestly would rather take tainter than todd. tainter has good slides that u can fill in but todd's slides aren't as good and her notesheets really aren't that useful because she goes by so fast that u wont be able to keep up filling in her notesheets. her slides have missing info and require u to read the textbook or watch videos which is annoying

I think that Todd is a good professor but CHEM 1601 as a course is very difficult, especially if you did not take AP Chem and even so, it still is. I think she and Tainter are equally good professors, nothing makes one better than other. I would say lectures do not elaborate well on material that is on test. Please review before semester begins

Prof Todd is the best gen chem professor of them all. She focuses on what is tested, gives lots of reviews, and is pretty funny (some people consider her rude but I think it's funny). I had a different professor for 1601 and there was a night and day difference between the two. The only downfall is that her class is at 8 am.
