Most amazing and caring professor at Vanderbilt! She is very receptive of students' needs and stress. Funny, engaging, caring, does not ask much of students. Take any class with her!!

Professor Valentine is very understanding when it comes to your personal life and if it conflicts. We talked a lot in class but I would rather talk than write tons of papers. The subject was mostly common sense so you don't have to read all the readings. I will definitely take her again and I recommend it to anyone.

Tough semester for her with COVID and some personal issues, but you will learn next to nothing. Very nice and easy, a great person, but will waste lots of time during lecture and ask questions with very basic answers, yet expect those to ignite long class discussions. If you want to learn, I'd try another prof

Professor Valentine is a 10/10 great professor and person. She is very approachable and makes you feel comfortable in the classroom. Assignments are not too hard, but you do need to do all of the readings or else you will be super confused. There were a lot of extra credit opportunities, and this class was an enjoyable experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Extremely nice person- got a bit behind but wasn't complaining. 10/10. Really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was great, very helpful and the class was straightforward.

She's a really nice person and the assignments are very manageable. Was always behind on grading and for the first essay, pretty sure she gave up and gave everyone an A (not complaining). Attendance is mandatory but lectures won't give you as much material as the readings will; readings are very easy to digest. Def take this class for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really like professor Valentine as a person. She is delightful and so much fun to talk to however she got really behind on grading and she seemed kind of unorganized. I believe that she has a lot of potential to be a great professor but because of COVID and it only being the beginning of her teaching career this semester was not her best.

Professor Valentine was one of my favorite professors that I've had in my two years at Vanderbilt. She was accessible, understanding, and had clear expectations set for her class. I appreciated her willingness to be flexibile (yet firm!) in a trying semester for all during the Covid-19 experience. Do yourself a favor and take her courses!

If you're looking for an easy A, this is definitely the class for that, but don't expect to learn much(or anything). Prof Valentine was all over the place, did not have clear guidelines, and barely graded anything until the very last day of the semester. I don't know if this was just a bad semester for her, but I was disappointed and frustrated.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Singh is very bad about communicating grading, expectations, exam material, dates, and other things to students. Our final is tomorrow and he has yet to even mention it once, let alone give a review. I will give him that he does answer questions well in class, his lecture slides are understandable, hw is helpful but also optional.

Absolute nightmare professor. Possibly the worst in the entire department. Reads off slides (that he stole) in a monotone, mind-numbing manner that induces a questioning of your life choices. He would struggle to teach addition to an 8th grader. After taking Singh, I wonder why Vandy hasn't fallen even lower in ratings. Nice guy tho.

He lied on his syllabus about exams being take home, and said exams are graded fairly randomly. The rubric on Gradescope is super vague and makes it very hard to argue for points back. The assignments are essentially a whole bunch of busy work. The material you learn in this class is all common sense. I don't recommend him for any classes.
Class was alright and a lot of lectures weren't very worthwhile, but he's a super stand-up guy and is very willing to help if you ask. Fair grader

(for Foundations of HCI) most disorganized class I've taken at Vandy. The syllabus given at the beginning basically meant nothing as quizzes/BIG projects were announced with days notices. Dr. Singh is knowledgeable but not a good professor, cares much more about getting through the curriculum than actually teaching content or giving project time

Not a good professor; he doesn't seem to care about what he's teaching or about his students, which doesn't help that the material he's teaching is inherently pretty boring. You'll need some prior experience building a project from scratch, because you don't learn anything useful for it in this course. I will say that he does grade pretty leniently

Personally, I think he is the WORST professor in the engineering apartment. He did not care about student, and he's teaching is very boring, feels like he's finishing his tasks rather than enjoy teaching and care whether student understand or not. Most CS professor is good actually, but he's an exception.

ALL things he taught is USELESS for project assignment, giving me a sense of he does not have a valid knowledge. Tests are all memory things. I can't understand he managed an advanced CS course's exam consists of all memory stuffs with no technical involved. it's a failure to design a course like that. I wish I chose the other section.

unpopular opinion but having taken all of Dr. Singh's class, i think Database is the best one. lecture and ICAs are actually helpful. SWE and Cloud Computing require a lot of self-learning and can be hit or miss depending on your teammates tbh. Dr. Singh gets more hate than he deserves, he's generally a chill guy and not a tough grader.
Professor is helpful, but the course and the way he taught is really bad.

Guys try to avoid this professor. He does not care about student, and has a tough attendance policy. After 3 absence, you will be deducted point directly on your final grade, and yet the lectures he gave is COMPLETELY USELESS. More importantly, he did not give you lecture slides to review until the last day before exam, which is ridiculous.
Unreasonable, with a complete lack of concern for students. Boring lecturer and takes attendance with in-class activities.

Good project based course to learn how to develop an app from start to finish. You do need to have some knowledge prior but everything can be learned during the class. Grade is heavy on group project so let him know if they don't do work. He seems like a harsh professor but that's because real jobs require you to produce REAL results on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures are very surface level so most things you learn are from "in-class activities" that he spends half the lecture time having you work on. Exams and homeworks often consist of things that he never mentioned and barely covered. He also gives very vague answers to your questions even if you go to his office hours.

TLDR: Good professor, AWFUL course (cloud computing).

Hopefully they redesign the course because it is incredibly outdated. There's a lot of content and the assignments are time consuming but it's a free A if you just turn everything in. Exams are dumb, straight info but you get a cheat sheet. 

As a prof, dry lectures but smart and good overall

lectures are informational to an extent but boring.
in class assignments are helpful.
but the exams contain content that is either not really taught or barely touched upon. he would briefly talk about something conceptually and then you would be expected to know everything about it, a whole bunch of stuff he didnt talk about.

This is a great project-based class -- as long as your project is interesting and your team is good, you'll have a good time. The class is planned and structured well, and although the exams are annoying, they're not too difficult.

This course should be a project course. His lectures only cover abstract concepts and he doesn't really teach you anything that is actually necessary to coding and deploying the project, even though the project is a huge part of your final grade. Without prior web development experience the project requires a lot of self learning.

I feel that Prof. Singh's lectures don't cover topics too in depth. In addition, the last two parts of the project were pretty difficult and time-consuming (they count for 12% of your final grade each). If you want to get a good grade, you have to go to office hours and self-study a lot in your free time!!

The worst prof I had in Vandy. Hardly replies to emails, busy office hours, exams test more conceptual knowledge than his slides. He rushes through every class, and explains the concepts poorly. He obscures project details and rubrics to make students lose points, and later contradicts himself during OH (also he didn't even do the project himself).

Professor Singh is ok at teaching his subject; when it comes to the projects he is quite awful. The lecture is surface level but I don't think that he does the projects or tests that he assigns. It's all very abstract and most students often find themselves trying to figure out the content. I like DB but Singh made me dislike one of my fav topics
Had him 2 times this semester. Awful in both classes. Surface level teaching and makes assignments and tests super technical

Did not teach a single thing relavent to the project. Feels like a project course because we completed the entire project without learning a single thing in class that was applicable. basically was told "if you dont know it its okay because you will learn it from working on the project". its exactly that your just going to have to learn itby urself

Bro just does not teach and gives tests thats extremely hard. During lectures he would talk about the subject. During tests and assignments it would be super technical much harder than what was explained

He is a very fair teacher.  Important concept to understand and pretty interesting stuff overall.  Lectures could be a bit dry, but the In class acitvies were very useful in reviewing for midterms and the final.  The projects were manageable, and answers questions clearly in office hours.

I've had Professor Singh for three classes while I was at Vanderbilt. I think he's quite a solid choice for most classes. While the lectures themselves can be a bit monotonous, try to reach him outside of class as he does a great job helping out when you develop a positive relationship with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definition of a mediocre professor. He isn't bad per say but isn't very approachable when it comes to answering questions outside of class and so forth. Only option for databases I think so you'll have to take it with him but other than the final the class is quite easy.

Professor Singhs lectures were not always the most interesting, but he really cared about students learning the software development life cycle. It was slightly odd that we had a project considering that this was not a project course, but our group did get to make a cool and useful tool. Would recommend Singh as long as you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Singh's lectures were extremely boring, he just reads from his slides. There were times when the homework included topics we didn't even cover in class. While the in-class activities were good, he often rushed through lectures to get to them. He also wasn't accommodating for those who had to miss class. Wouldn't recommend him at all :/
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Database management. Tons of work! Every class will have several in-class activity questions, and will have homework every week. And be prepared to have hw plus in-class activity plus projects at the same time for last few weeks. And though you have final project, you still have to prepare for the final exam. He's not bad but not great.

Lecturing is very boring, unfortunately. I usually just muted him while completing other homework since he requires attendance. Exams are extremely easy. We have discussions in class but they felt so forced. Grading for written discussions are annoying as the TA will take off 20% if you are one word below the word limit. You'll get 100% otherwise.
He's not bad but not great. He'll answer any questions you have and is glad to help.

Lectures very difficult to follow and understand. Doesn't treat teaching with any passion and seems like he is surviving each class. Assignments aren't impossible, but if you don't have any coding background this can be a grind.
The amount of busy work assigned in Dr. Singh's classes is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Take his Database Management. He is probably the best professor in database.

Generally easy class. Participation is mandatory (up to 3 absences before dropping half a letter grade) but there is no need to pay attention during the lectures so you can do other work. Busy work is 30% of the grade & it's pretty easy grading. participate about once per week to get full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: His lectures were super boring. I don't remember if I ever looked at his presentation during class. I just went to class for fulfilling attendance. I regretted taking class.
Coming to this guy's class is useless and you will learn nothing from it. And for the homework, you will always lose points as he will not tell you how he grades in advance.

The guy tracks class participation using tophat but compared to some other professors is really infrequent with giving questions on it. Therefore, missing a few classes early in the semester can be disastrous for your grade even if you are the one helping some other people get As!

Lectures are your typical, boring snoozefests (especially because the first half of the semester is really easy.) Nothing special, but his attendance methodology is messed up and can tank your grade because of his irregular attendance-taking schedule. If you've taken CS before, it doesn't matter if you go for him; but if you're new, just don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not take his CS 1101, but his CS 2201 is much better. I think his section is very easy, and you don't even need to come to every class because he posts his powerpoints.
His lectures are boring, but it is OK because this class is easy. If you go to class, you will be fine. He gives little homework and easy tests.

I took both his CS 1101 and CS 2201 classes. He gives much harder material in CS 1101, but his CS 2201 is much easier than the other CS 2201 sessions. Although he has an accent, I quickly get used to it after two weeks.

The lectures were insanely boring, but attendance is checked each class. He only lectures for the first few weeks, then it's primarily the class who teaches each other through presentations - so sometimes makes the quizzes hard. Just do the work and you'll be fine.

i'm sure he's an amazing programmer outside of class, but there is really no reason to go to class  he reads off the lecture slides (posted online) pretty much verbatim so you might as well teach yourself and skip class. there are lengthy weekly assignments that you should do because thats probably the best way to teach yourself
Lectures in class are very boring and it is more useful to just self-teach the material before each class.

Singh never went above and beyond and did not seem to especially care about the students. He showed up, read directly from lecture slides written by another professor, and left. CS 1101 is not an incredibly difficult course nor is he particularly strict, but take another professor if at all possible. If you're good at CS he won't be too bad

He is not exactly the best teacher, given the fact that his lectures involve him just reading from presentations. However, he will try to answer students' questions as best as he can, so I strongly encourage you to ask questions during class. Also, if you don't have previous programming experience, prepare to spend a lot of time outside class.

Since the CS 1101 classes have the same programming assignments and similar exams, I recommend taking a different professor if it's your first time learning how to code for more beneficial lectures. He has trouble coding in Java, but he is a nice person in general. He tends to just read off the lecture slides a lot.

CS1101 is extremely well-structured, with organized PAs and TA office hours. I think Vikash is a solid choice for the class. His lectures go at a slower pace to make sure everyone is caught up with the material, and he is always open to questions. Overall, the lecture isn't the most exciting but if you show up and pay attention you can learn a ton.

For starters, java is a dumb language to learn to code on. However, Singh makes it even more difficult. If you are able to, take it with the other professor. Overall, I would not recommend this class if you have no experience with coding. Practice it over a break or something first. There is too much work and you can't work with others. 0/10

He does not explain the concepts well. Class is a joke. Reading off slides doesn't equate to good teaching. He is not accessible through email. His teaching is just not good. And he should not at Vanderbilt. That's the honest truth.
Professor Singh tries to explain concepts well and is willing to answer your questions. CS1101 is interesting and you should try it.

CS1101 is a well-structured, challenging but fun class. You learn a lot if you're a true beginner. However, I'd not recommend taking it with Dr. Singh. He reads off exactly what's already in the slides, so most students just skip class.
Dude can't teach.

Dr. Singh knows the topics quite well, but it takes some effort to understand things fully in CS 1101. There is a big assignment almost every week that requires some time to finish, and it can get frustrating sometimes. This is not an easy class, but everything else is fine.

Dr. Singh is a solid choice for CS1101, especially considering it is an intro class. It is probably a good idea to show up for class since Dr. Singh is usually helpful in explaining the concepts if you are confused. Overall, this class is not a freebie, and you should expect to put in a decent amount of work for the PAs and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Singh does his job and that's it. Lectures straight from powerpoint slides created by another professor, and doesn't add anything else. Was unhelpful and confused/confusing in review sessions. Boring teacher and boring class, but okay for the intro level.
Vikash has a pretty heavy Indian accent. It's not too hard to understand him, but it causes him to talk slowly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Singh is a very subpar professor. His assignments lack relevance and the graders will drop you down to a 70% due to one typo. I would not have taken a class with him if I could go back and change the past.

Professor Singh has his class structured so that groups lecture on Tuesdays and do group activities Thursdays, so he only teaches maybe 10-15 minutes a week. Quizzes every two weeks, not terribly hard I only missed questions that were worded poorly. Honestly, if you have to take ethics take it with Singh, it sucks but its easier than other profs
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Straightforward lectures, writes out a lot of code, not the most engaging or thorough, but for CS it works!

CS 1151 is meant to be easy - just do your work and you'll get an A. Dr. Singh fulfilled his role as a professor but that's it. He was not enthusiastic about the subject and did not make class interesting. The class is structured so that student groups present most of the lecture material, which made class even less interesting.

Expect late nights until 3 A.M. on projects. The grading feels subjective and inconsistent — criteria are rarely communicated upfront, making it hard to meet expectations. The professor has very specific artistic standards that aren't always clear. Not ideal for those seeking structured, transparent feedback.

This professor and class made my semester miserable. I took this as a fun class, but instead, it was so time-consuming 3 hrs in class many outside of class late nights. The professor is unclear and has a bias. She only likes the art she picks out, not anything from your creative process. Grading doesn't make sense, and I had to pay so many supplies

Vesna is cool. I enjoyed her class and would 100% take her again. I learned so much about photography through this analog course. I will say that she has opinions and I did feel a bit pressured to alter my work sometimes. But she just offers advice. You take it or you don't. She knows what she's talking about. I 100% recommend this course with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: LOVED Vesna. Super helpful every step of the way, from learning how to use the camera to retouching finished photos. Very laid back and easy to talk to. She helps develop project ideas and finds ways for students to exhibit their work. The class was pretty relaxing for me, and the dark room is really cool. Makes the class seem like a little family.

Great professor! As long as you put in the effort, you will do well in this class. She is very accessible and tries her best to help students who are having trouble with their project ideas. Plus, dark room photography is actually a lot fun.
Excellent! You will do well if she feels that you are putting in effort and originality. Very laid back teacher! Love her

really really nice and helpful. can be unorganized and and unclear sometimes, but i think it is because she wants students to have more freedom in expressing their ideas. also tries to find every opportunity for students to show and exhibit their works, which is very nice. very down-to-earth as such a knowledgeable photographer.
Dr. Hensley is so sweet! She gives good feedback and genuinely cares about her students. The class is made by another professor so I can't complain about the workload but she made it so much better.
The GOAT. Best professor ive had

This is a required course for every A&S freshman to take; most people did not like it, I however all thanks to my AMAZING professor loved it. She is so much fun, caring, and so so sweet, but also knows the course well and is really good at teaching it. She is kind and understanding, and I looked forward to seeing her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring sweet professor. Extremely easy class where all we did was in discussion about readins and key definition. in the review sessions prior to midterm and exam she basically gives away 60% of the exam and tell you what to study for. lots of extra credit oppurtunities and one note card avalible for essays.
truly cares about her work. really easy class.

super sweet professor! all you do is read articles/sections of the book and come to class and participate in discussion. review sessions prior to midterm and exam, jeopardy style, got extra credit, one note card laying out your essays on midterm + final.

Professor Hensley is such a sweet professor! Class is led by students as discussion leaders, have to do it twice per semester but not hard at all. Lots of readings for homework but only 3 writing submissions and a final project/presentation. Easy A, just participate in class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly such an a amazing professor, the socratic seminar style class was super effective and fun. Everyone participated and Prof Hensley was super encouraging and kind. Always a class I looked forward to

Dr. Hensley is easily the sweetest, most amazing professor I have ever had. She continuously made a determined effort to spark students' intellectual curiosity, was highly understanding about extenuating circumstances, and truly made an effort.

She's the best, please take a class with her if you get the chance.

Professor Hensley is absolutely amazing and one of my favorite professors I've had here! Her expectations are clear, she genuinely cares about you as a student, and all she expects is effort and participation. As long as you speak up a few times in class and takes notes on the terms, you'll be set for the two exams (which are incredibly easy).

Very sweet, patient, caring, and appreciated every student's opinion. I'd take her again and again if I could! Grade expectation was very straightforward, as well. Definitely cares about your wellbeing before your student label.

Dr. Hensley is one of the sweetest professors I've had. The class is heavily discussion-based, and some of the readings can get a bit dense, but still enjoyable. Other than studying for the two exams, there isn't much work in the class. A lot of great topics are covered that are relevant to our lives. Highly recommend taking a class with her!

Prof Hensley is amazing, and I would highly recommend taking a class with her. The class was discussion-based and had 3 papers and a final project (no tests/exams). She's clear with her expectations, and wants her students to do well. But don't take this class if you don't plan on showing up and participating regularly.

Professor Hensley is passionate about her work and deeply cares about her students. The grading criteria for the class is clear and understandable, and the class is not too difficult if you put in the effort and show up for class.

Professor Hensley is very passionate about public history! In HART 2810W, we were required to submit weekly project updates, and a large part of our grade was based on participation in weekly roundtable discussions. This class only met once a week, so attendance was a must.

Professor Wisniewski is the most caring professor, and I highly recommend everyone to take his class. I had a wonderful experience learning from him, and his corny jokes will always bring a smile to your face. Highly recommend!! :)
Good professor. He is so passionate and caring for students. BEST PROFESSOR!!

Like any CORE 1010 class, there is a lot of reading. That said, take Dr. W for any class you can. He is one of the most understanding and thoughtful professors at Vanderbilt and makes every class enjoyable. You'll leave class smiling. If you put in effort and stay engaged, earning a good grade is very doable. I hope to take another class with him.
I think Dr. W does a good job at making a sort of drier content more interesting. He can be a bit more awkward but that could also be the fact that it's a quiet 8am.
We watched and read Flatland, and something connected in my brain
Dr. W is the most caring professor at Vanderbilt! He gives amazing feedback and he replies to emails really fast. I love his humor and I look forward to taking another class with him in the future.
I love professor W! He truly cares about his students and gives amazing feedback. He is clear abot what he expects from all his students and he is really funny. (I had him for CORE)
You learn a lot without having to do a bunch of work!

Mark is an amazing professor, and I would have him as a professor many times if I could! It is evident he is passionate about the subject he teaches, and he is very caring to his students. He takes students' feedback into consideration and is a very funny guy who often cracks dad jokes! Take his course, he is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I got lazy senior year and skipped taking the AP English exam. After hearing I had to take ENGL 1100 I was pissed. However, Professor W made this class actually enjoyable. He truly cares about his students and checks in with us often. While the class itself has some boring content, I highly recommend taking Mr. Wisniewski.

Dr. W is a really kind and fun person to have as a professor. As a Freshmen, he created a welcoming atmosphere for all who come. He gives amazing feedback and is often a generous grader.  You write 4 or 5 papers averaging about 4 pages, but that's pretty standard at Vandy. He helps you to build up your essays in steps through weekly assignments too

Dr. W is an amazing professor, and he makes sure to give freedom to his students in major assignments, which were 3 essays and final project. He made sure that class discussions were enjoyable and similar to Core 1010 so you wouldn't feel lost. He is very flexible, and he wants his students to succeed. Definitely recommend him!!
Amazing professor -- tries to be interesting and fun. Assignments gave a lot of freedom to students and could tailor class to what they find interesting. Very kind and understanding.

I took ENGL1100 with a CORE Focus, Dr. W is such a cool and genuine professor, you can tell he really cares about you both as a writer and a person. There are 4 major assignments, discussion posts, prior to class readings, and journals. It is a very, very structured class in a good way and he sets you up great for CORE and ENGL1100, def would rec!

Ignore the negative reviews (notice how they're all from the same day?) HOD 2500 as a course is not the most interesting or exciting material but Dr. Lowell is a great professor who is very kind and wants his students to succeed. Very accessible for advice during office hours, straightforward grading system, options for extra credit. Great prof!
The other reviews are not accurate. He is a kind person and wants you to succeed.
The ratings from January are about a different professor, clearly. Prof Lowell is extremely kind and knowledgeable about research.
The ratings posted in January are for a different person, clearly. Prof Lowell is extremely kind and knowledgeable about research methods.

so confused on these reviews. i took systematic inquiry (HOD 2500) and apart from the no technology approach, he is a sweet guy who cares about his students doing good. take the assignments serious, stick to the rubric, and you should have no issue.
Hes a nice guy. Exam a little challenging, study a week before youll be fine.
Wonderful class, very easy to work with, most assignments are essentially graded on completion
if y'all ever had one of those passive aggressive english teachers in hs this guy is 10x worse...pls don't get tenure

Lectures felt unstructured and often didn't match the assignments/tests. Grading seemed inconsistent, and questions were rarely answered directly. I put in effort but didn't feel supported or taught effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was extremely rude to his students and was very boring in lectures. Hard to sit through a class listening to his monotone lecture for so long, really didn't enjoy this class or this professor one bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It just seems like the professor doesn't really care about his students, nor the class. He comes across as cold and wildly uninterested. Would definitely not recommend this class, if you want a professor that explains the concepts well and cares. Overall, very poor experience.
He is Evil.

This class was frustrating and disorganized for most of the semester. Lectures often felt unprepared and jumped between topics without clear explanations, making it hard to understand what we were actually supposed to learn. Instructions for assignments were vague, and expectations frequently changed, which led to unnecessary confusion and stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Coming into the class, I was really looking forward to the course material. After taking the course though, I probably couldn't recommend a professor less then Professor Lowell. Not only is he rude and cold to his students, but he seems to not really care about your success in the class. Definitely would not recommend.

reviews.comment: Do not taie this class
Do not take

reviews.comment: Mean and unthoughtful guy

reviews.comment: Least chill professor I've had at Vanderbilt.

Love Dr. Wang!! Best class I have taken at HOD. She blends theory and case studies in her teaching. Really cares about the practical implications of our learning. Definitely would take another class with her.
such a sweet professor and cares a lot about students

This is for Understanding Organization. Dr. Wang is a fair grader. Her rubric is quite helpful navigating expectations. She is always accessible if you need feedback. I also really liked her class activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof. Wang brings the communication lens to her 2100 section, which is quite unique. A group project, an individual paper, and several short essays. On top of that, two exams that are fairly easy. Not hard to get an A. She is accessible if you need feedback. I am taking another course with her this semester, and really enjoys her teaching style.
Professor Wang is a great listener and going to her office hours is extremely helpful. She will challenge you to be a better student and person.

Professor Wang is a great lecturer and does a good job listening to class feedback. Her grades on essays are difficult to predict and she says she doesn't really use the rubric. If you go to office hours and ask for help, your life will get easier. Overall, she's a very good professor.

Very chill professor, good teaching style, and easy exams. There's homework nearly every class from the textbook, which can get annoying but it's not overly difficult. Overall he wants to make your life easier

I showed up to ECE 2112 a total of four times, and three of those were for exams. Everything you need is in the Brightspace and it is easy to learn alone. Really enjoyed his testing format and appreciated how nice he was with grading. Really chill dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He's ok, but lectures are him reading off the slides, clicking through examples so fast that they are meaningless.
Most of my issues are with the course, not the professor. 90% of the grade is exams, despite there being homework that usually takes at least an hour due every class period.
The entire class is graded by the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were just him reading off the slides. I opted not to go to class and just turned in my homework the night before since I would prob retain more information reading the slides myself anyway. Homework due before every single class almost and it's only 10% of grade. CRAZY. 90% rest is exams. Need to do like 2 practice exams before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest engineering class ever which is crazy since signals and systems is usually hard. Exams are open notes and he gives past exams. Lectures aren't super exciting but he tries to make it fun and short.

I feel so blessed that I took Digital Logic with Snake!! I came in pretty worried after having seen people struggle to even pass digital logic with other profs semester after semester.. and he somehow made it the easiest class I took that semester. Snake rocks
Snake turns one of the hardest classes for CS majors into the third easiest class Ive ever taken at Vandy...
If you're taking EECE 2116 he is THE MAN!!!

He goes by Snake. You'd never guess he's in charge of the honor council. Tests are open book, open note, open computer- you're an engineer, solve the problem. If you're in his classes you probably pay attention well so do that, it helps. Homework due dates and tests are totally flexible. Homework comes in bursts.

Professor Wilkes is really nice and funny, but the lectures can get a little boring and therefore you won't pay attention. Learned in this class, but wish the material was presented in a slightly more interesting way.
You'll learn a lot about classy music.
Really cool and helpful guy. Great class for graduate students, classes are very clear, and not much work is required outside class.
He curves a lot. So don't get frustrated after the quizzes and the tests.
Good professor for graduate students
Hard class great teacher. Lots and lots of notes but tests are straight forward and like the homework. I will take any class Snake teaches at Vanderbilt.
Good class, lots of notes, not much homework. tests are open book/notes.  pretty easy to get an A or B.
Boring and unfocused lecturer. Lazy person. Once was still photocopying the test after it had started. Cool guy if you don't have to learn from him. Killed my interest in the subject.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Lecture slides are a bit confusing but not a difficult class in general if you've taken stats before.
Take someone else if you can
Awesome prof and clear lectures, really cares about students. Very nice and had lots of extra credits opportunities. Would recommend!

She is an amazing professor. She always happily answered questions, her tests were fair, and she gave plenty of opportunities for extra credit. She's the nicest person ever, never putting people down for questions,

Addiction is such an interesting class for anyone in clinical psych. Watts makes 2.5 hr class interesting and engaging. Discussion questions each week that shape class discussion. Dr W gets to know each student, very personable. Papers have little guidance because of leniency; don't stress about grade as long as you participate! Fav class at Vandy!

Lectures were very dense and heavy in between each class. Her teaching style is not my favorite, and her way of explaining statistics was taught way more complicated than it should be. 

The way the TAs grade is very different from each other, and there were many instances where my peers got the same answer, yet I got points taken off.

I don't get why people would complain about this class. Watts said that if you come to class you will have a high odds of making an A. I came to class and made an A. There are a lot of problem sets but the exams are not worth a large portion of the grade. Try hard, you get an A. Watts is so nice and funny and really wants students to learn.

Her TA's / LA's are the biggest problem, Watts is a very nice person and worked with me to help me do well in the class. Wish I would've gotten an A, but had a rough start to the course tbh, TA/LA grading is super inconsistent but Watts is willing to regrade. Lowkey I think she will be a great prof with a better supporting cast, overall I fumbled

Although I loved Watts as a person, I can't say she was the best professor. She teaches the material almost as a review session and leaves multiple students who may have never taken stats behind. Questions on the exams are worded to where it is hard to understand what to calculate.

She's a really nice professor, but the grading can be kind of stingy because the TAs are not consistent amongst each other. LAs were nice (not condescending), they just come off more serious but they are awesome too. Exams are weighted small, but lectures can be dense. Learn the content, don't memorize it.

Watts is an alright person. The issue is her TAs and LAs. Yes, it takes one hundred years to wait grades back, and different TAs clearly have different grading criteria. Another issue is her two undergrad LAs. They may be good person and have good intentions, but they tend to be overly condescending when answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I agree with some of the comments; the TAs definitely have made the grading different and resulted in a lot of the inconsistencies with scores. However, getting an A is extremely doable if you put in the effort and attend lectures, complete assignments on time, and review slides. Don't just memorize, learn. Overall, an easy class and a funny prof.

Prof was very nice and genuinely wanted us to learn. The class covers a lot of material and so many tests. I wish the TAs graded more consistently but Watts was willing to re grade assignments and exams and wanted things to be fair. There are a lot of assignments but I learned a lot and the exams are not worth a huge portion of the final grade.

So unorganized.The textbook and lectures teach different ways of doing things.The TAs graded exams differently- my peers and I got completely different scores for the same answers to questions. There was an overwhelming amount of content and exam expectations were unclear. Watts is nice, but this class was not worth the stress.

Incredibly passive-aggressive. Inconsistent grading with little explanation. JASP is so confusing and she barely told us how to use it. The textbook is basically useless and she covers so much information in one class. You miss a day, you lose participation points and are miles behind. I don't recommend.

I don't agree with the negative comments about Professor Watts this semester and came here to recommend her. Professor Watts is supportive and kind and does everything she can to help. She reached out to me after I didn't do very well on an exam and we met and discussed the material I missed.

Don't take her! Assigned confusing JASP work with no guidance, just vague slide images. Heavy on formulas and vocab. Passive-aggressive and grades weirdly. No multiple choice, and exams don't match what she teaches. Only gives 10 minutes to submit attendance work after class and if you miss she won't fix it even if you were there.

I wish I could go back and take literally any other prof of get credit for this some other way, Dr. Watts is super inconsistent with grading. Literally had the same answers as friends for some questions and got 0 credit while they got full. Also there was a test where no one got this question right and instead of removing it she kept it. Awful.

all the tests are cumulative which is so much work. so many formulas and information and we basically get no guidelines or guide for what to focus/study for a a test. will test you on random concepts from the textbook never mentioned before. class is pretty boring, but she does explain the content fairly well. a little passive aggressive though.

agree w/ the low ratings; the class itself is fine. if you took ap stats, this is basically a repeat. the problem sets/hw she assigns strays away from lecture content a bit. she and the LAs are condescending when answering questions, which is crazy bc shes a clinical psychologist, so i would expect to feel welcomed but i hate going to her class.
Literally take any other professor, overall bad experience with waiting on grades, all her TAs grading assignments / tests differently from one another, and overcomplicating very simple things.

Takes forever to grade things, frequently messes up on practice problems, isn't super consistent with grading. Overall just not a great teacher and if you can take someone else I would, class is still semi easy but it is just a lot more painful than it needs to be
Dr. Watts is such a sweet professor and makes her slides very straightforward and organized. She makes her slides very similar to the homework and the tests usually don't have any surprises.

Engaging lectures with many examples. Extra credits are given if completing a design question to replace one lowest quiz. Dr. Dong is very accessible out of class to answer student questions. The response is quick. Overall, great experience.

At first, lectures made class seem pretty complicated. However, the 5 quizzes are all very easy and bear a strong resemblance to the practice test and homework. A short night of studying was enough to do great for me. He grades extremely generously. Super nice guy and very receptive to feedback. Best prof to get a good dynamics grade.

(ME 2190) New professor. Was very receptive to feedback and improved significantly as a teacher over the semester. Often hard to understand (partly because of the accent), but he teaches from the textbook, so having the textbook open during lecture is helpful. Limited office hours, but happy to schedule individual office hours upon request.

Professor Dong is a very passionate professor. There are 5 quizzes (midterms) throughout the semester, but you can drop one through a bonus question he posts towards the semester's end. He assigns a lot of homework and is not as accessible due to his heavy inclination towards his research, but he's always looking for suggestions to improve.

started off very strict with hard deadlines and lots of cold calling, but looked for lots of feedback from students and became much more forgiving towards the end of the semester. he is very blunt and has a funny way of answering questions, but he wants us to do well and was generous with extra credit and final exam questions.

Long story short, Dr. Dong is the goat. If you can do the homework well, then you will perform well on the quizzes. In other words, the quizzes are very predictable and Dr. Dong is not actively praying on your downfall unlike most other stem professors. Also, be ready to answer a random question that you have no idea what the answer is.

Professor Dong is an extremely smart and very caring man. He truly wants his students to do well in his class. That being said, his lectures were sometimes dull and he tends to move quickly over details that he doesn't think should be hard. Helpful Grader though

Class was pretty calm and prof Dong is top cheller. There's 5 quizzes throughout the semester which kinda sucks, but hw isn't too heavy and the quizzes were all pretty fair and similar to practice questions. Can be boring lecturer but pretty generous grader. Also he always says "cronk" instead of crank and that's just great.

No discredit to her, it was her first year when I took her class but the way she taught just wasent that all for what I expected. She would lack to fully clarify some topics and talk to herself to move on and not fully engage in some subjects leaving plot holes for questioning. Main reason I passed was from prior knowledge on a lot of the subjects.

Math 1300 is not a difficult course and Instructor Liu is very caring toward her students, but I honestly wouldn't recommend her. It is often difficult to follow along with what she is teaching and I feel like she sometimes tends to overcomplicate concepts. I also wish she would spend more time going over the problems in the daily handouts.

Hard to understand and follow in lectures sometimes, but helpful when asked questions and tried her best to communicate in a language that isn't her first. She doesn't write the curriculum, but stuck to it fairly well.
Great professor, pay attention in lectures. Slightly hard to follow sometimes, but always happy to answer questions. She does not make the packets or exams but teaches all the required information.

Dr. Jiang is a good person and cares about her students. Compared to other BSCI2520 classes, she is probably the most difficult, but she makes up for it with a 10% curve per exam, meaning the class averages are the exact same as the other classes. She works through difficult problems on her iPad, which becomes especially helpful during exam 4.

Not a single person I know actually enjoyed or liked her teaching style or her as professor. She is a nice person but not a good professor. Content is already difficult, and her accent makes the class much more difficult where she acknowledges she can't pronounce certain words cause according to her she is "learning Japanese" Joke of a professor.

For the people saying they are tired of " hearing complaints". The class is dense, and having an actual good professor that explains and is there when you ask would be great ant not much to ask at any institution especially at a T20 that costs $90K a year. Can't communicate , can't teach, not a real professor just a doctor in her field.

Bad professor, strong accent, " accessible after class" but was not helpful at all . She told me to breathe and interiorize the content and to read it again. Never once tried to explain anything. She knows her biochemistry but can't teach. No one understands her or her exam questions.

I'm rating the professor not the class contents. For a T20, this is the worst professor I've had. We ask for help during the exam we are only met with " read it again". What's the point of asking for help? Went to office hours, she told me to read it again, I was a total of 40 mins just for a "professor" to tell me to reach it again???

This class is a good indication of which Vandy pre meds will be successful, and which will spend the rest of their time at this school complaining. This class was in no way unfair, and is just a measure of who understands the content vs memorizes it. For a top 20, this school is filled with too many people who's primary skill is complaining.
She is smart, her issue is her inability to communicate. Her lectures are very unhelpful and you're better off memorizing everything on your own. Half the questions on her test don't even make sense.

I am tired of people complaining about this class. If you can't do this class, how do you expect to be a doctor? You do know you have the MCAT and USMLE steps 1, 2, 3? This class has a lot of content, but is extremely doable with a little bit of critical thinking and hard work. People do anything but prepare correctly.

Quite literally the WORST professor I have ever had. I figured the ridiculously low averages would mean there would be a curve — but no. She offered absolutely no help when I asked her how I could do better with my studying. Essentially told me that my energy sucked. Every other semester, there has been some curve, but not this semester. Avoid.
She expects you to be doing high level critical thinking on every exam question despite this being new content. Idk she's nice but just very upper level thinking exams.

Dr.Jiang is one of my favorite professors.  Her goal of proteins was for students to learn a lot and enjoy it.  She had us do 2 in depth group presentations on a book chapter.  She expects students to put in effort but wants you to focus on your interests.  She really cares about her students, she wants us to determine our true passions.

She claims that review sessions are a waste of time and that she does not have time for other office hours or individual meetings, despite many students asking for a more varied time slot. Claims she cares, but then says our low class averages are because we "don't embrace the material enough" and she refuses to take any sense of responsibility.

She's rude and inconsiderate of students. She's told us we have elementary-level intelligence, if she slept as little as us (because of her!) she wouldn't function, and promotes EDs with her hw assignments (recommended we eat 1x/day!?) It is also SO clear that if she didn't have information in front of her, she wouldn't be able to explain material.

She doesn't let you ask questions until the end when everyone just leaves anyway. When she does answer your questions, she makes you feel like you are incompetent. This class was harder than Orgo + Physics combined. She has made me very sad.

While sometimes a bit delusional, Dr. Jiang is a good professor with a good class. There is a lot of content, but she is clear with what will be tested, and gives a multitude of resources. IGNORE all bad reviews as these people would rather complain and criticize than put in any work. Take this class.
She cares very much about mental wellbeing but she make my mental unwell.

Exams are BEYOND unfair. You can study for weeks and still do absolutely terrible. When you ask for study advice, she essentially tells you to fix your mindset. Her accent also makes it very difficult to follow lectures. Take the other section--their prof gave them extra credit for wearing Halloween costumes, whereas we get absolutely none.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A high-content class with some complicated topics, but she teaches it well. Recorded lectures + lecture slides cover all of the content. In-person lecture isn't usually helpful. TopHat and Brightspace quizzes are much harder than in the first half of the class (Castiglione). Very responsive to Brightspace discussion board for questions.

Horrible. For lectures she says a whole lot of nothing and it's hard to follow. Exams aren't an accurate test of knowledge. She gives plenty of resources, and you can learn everything and still do badly on exams. To learn, expect to put in lots of hours that likely won't show in your grade. Unrealistic expectations with poor quality of teaching
Crazy accent, but outside of that, she is great. One of the most caring professors I have ever had.
Clear expectations

Great professor. Ignore the bad ratings, as these people spend more time complaining than studying. She gives a surplus of resources, and makes the class very doable even though difficult. I feel I have learned more in this class than any other. The combo of Castiglione/Jiang is elite.

I've had such a terrible experience in this class. Professor is rude and unsympathetic, has incredibly high standards, and doesn't take a shred of accountability for low class averages. Makes you memorize so much unnecessary things, and has incredibly difficult tests. Lectures are all fast paced and don't really make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes lectures very confusing and doesn't explain much. It was unclear what to focus on for the exams and her exam questions were hard to understand. She's not very nice either. Don't take this professor unless you have to.

She grades assignments and exams in less than 24 hours, but that is her only good quality. Her lectures are confusing and do more harm than good. She is rude. Her exams are not clear at all, and she makes you memorize many things that are not important. It's a shame her half of the class is so bad, because I know she puts in a lot of effort.
She takes attendance ON PAPER. Lectures are poor. Study materials are confusing. Exam questions make no sense. Dr. Castiglione was good, but the second half of this course is not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst lecturer I have had. She incorporated breathing exercises as part of the weekly assignments for a protein course, which was completely irrelevant. She was extremely irresponsible to make students give lectures throughout the course as part of the assignments. The only lecture she personally gave was in the first week. RUN
Amazing all around. Very caring
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Jiang is such a caring and kind professor. For BCB 2200, she was really flexible and worked with us most of the time. The class is graded by 3 exams and weekly homework. You'll do well on exams if you pay attention in lecture, which is mostly review from biochem and gen chem and lab techniques. I would highly recommend her and this class!
Very accessible after class and she cares a ton about the course and teaching in general. Not a great lecturer, but also not the worst. Her tests are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Jiang is one of the best professors I've had, especially in the bio department which tends to have meh professors. After a low exam 3 average she said that it was a reflection of her teaching, so she curved 10%. How many professors acknowledge that it is a combined effort? Not many. I highly recommend her, she genuinely wants you to do well.

I don't know why Dr.Jiang gets such a bad rep. She genuinely cares about her students, and goes over all content in class. If you pay attention in class and ask questions, which she highly encourages, you will do well. Her practice exams are very similar to real ones and she hints at questions in class. One of my favorite professors at vandy.

Biochemistry is difficult, but Jiang made it enjoyable. Be prepared to have to memorize reactions as you would in any biochem class, but Jiang provides every resource she can to help you succeed (recorded lectures, extra office hours, discussion board). Tests are extremely fair and she actively takes student feedback. Wonderful & intelligent prof

I had Jiang for biochem. She's not the greatest lecturer but she's very accessible after class, cares about being a good teacher very deeply, and has a discussion post that she responds to very consistently to answer questions. Her tests are decently hard but fair and she is open to regrade requests if you feel like mistakes were made
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Jiang gets a bad rep for being a hard professor but she's honestly not that bad. Lots of students weren't happy cause the content was confusing but she graded pretty generously (lots of partial credit) and gave plenty of resources to prepare for the exams. The classes may be difficult but she is still a good professor!

Nice person, can't coherently string sentences together at all, not very understanding, accessible at office hours if you wanna go but honestly its kinda useless. Would recommend just doing the practice questions and reviewing slides multiple times instead.

I really do love Dr. Jiang I think she is both an amazing person and professor and makes herself readily available to her students. Biophysical Chemistry is just really hard, I mean guys the name itself is daunting. Her exams are extremely difficult but I wouldn't say they are harder than any other professor's.

Jiang is a super caring professor. That being said, this had little effect of her understanding of course material. Her lectures were a faulty attempt to copy public MIT lectures, but often misunderstood these lectures and made frequent errors. Her standards were extremely high and she likely would not have succeeded in her own class. def Avoid

The worst professor I've had. She doesn't know what she's talking about because she expects students to fix her mistakes during lectures and her answer keys are constantly wrong. Thank god for a TA in this class who actually does the problems and gives full credit. I'm sure she would fail her own test if she were to take it.
brutal exams, ruthless professor.... kind and seemingly cares about her students in every environment except for writing and grading exams

Definitely a tough class, but I think Jiang did a solid job. I was her first year teaching at Vanderbilt and I think it took her some time to adjust to. That said she was very patient and listened to students. Once she found her stride, I think the course improved a lot. She's a sweet and funny woman and I hope she continues to grow as an educator.

While her class was rough. Jiang is a pretty good professor. She was very open to feedback and willing to change the class to help students. Yes, our grades weren't very good, but she does try very hard and cares a lot about your learning. She's also pretty funny which is some relief.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: run.

definitely a demanding class, but SO interesting. Liu laoshi gives unique and interesting perspectives and has taught me a lot about Chinese culture and U.S.-China relations. I wish more students outside of Chinese L&C department could take the class. there are a lot of papers and presentations, but that is expected for a 4000 level chinese course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A lot of project and papers (unclear rubric and expectation).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Liu laoshi is so sweet and she clearly wants you to succeed. Conversational class wasn't exactly what I was expecting since it was mostly her talking the entire time, and there wasn't really any vocab to structure the weekly papers off of. It was also surprisingly more work than expected but she provides good feedback.

I LOVE Liu Laoshi! She was organized and clear in her lectures, and also incredibly funny. There's a lot of material covered in this class, but she is accessible and also provides resources. Liu is clear about what will be on the exams, so getting an A is totally doable if you study properly!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Liu Laoshi is a wonderful professor. During lectures she will go through a PowerPoint containing all of the chapter section material for that day. She might sometimes go through new grammatical rules and concepts a bit quickly, but that can definitely be reviewed during drill or on the next homework assignment.

Professor Liu has profoundly deepened my knowledge of Chinese and the global economy. While this course was truly challenging, and I wish I had more time to thoroughly focus on the course content, Prof. Liu truly made the experience worth it. This is a fantastic course for anyone at this level as long as you are ready to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is very organized. If you have zero knowledge about Chinese, then you might feel confused for the first few classes. I would recommend you study Pinyin beforehand because the way they teach Pinyin is a tiny bit confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely love this professor. Honestly, she tries really hard at her job and she just really wants to help you learn Chinese. She is readily available for helping students outside of class. If you got a bad grade on a test or essay, ask her to go over it with you. Just by doing this she'll often find a way to help you earn back points later on.
Calligraphy. Easy one hour credit. No outside work, just show up and draw. Would reccomend to those that need a credit.

Professor Liu is pretty clear at explaining things and enjoys teaching. She's very strict on attendance (your grade goes down if you miss) and a bit sarcastic but overall she's solid and wouldn't have a problem taking a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: On the surface, Liu Laoshi appears to be very energetic and friendly. However, she picks clear favorites and tends to focus on those students. Other students are essentially ignored (especially if they are of a Chinese background). Furthermore, she becomes easily frustrated when students don't understand her.

Liu laoshi is incredibly fast-paced. Although she is really into the material and seems to love teaching Chinese, she tends to assume individuals have a background in Chinese. She speaks very quickly and is oftentimes hard to understand. However, I would still recommend her class! She is a sweet woman and a nice teacher.

Really nice woman, but learning Chinese is super hard. She speaks English well but the language barrier with the drill teachers is often troublesome. 2 character quizzes every week, a lot of memorization and recitation. Attendance is mandatory, and its a 5-day a week class which sucks. They reuse tests so find someone who has taken the class before
Professor Liu is very good and very helpful! However, this class is not for the faint of heart. You have to study and read, or your grade will suffer. It's not overwhelming in the least, though.

She is my favorite teacher. She truly wants and believes that everyone can learn Chinese. She has so much energy and is so passionate about Chinese that it draws you in, helping you learn as well. Take advantage of her office hours-- She'll love you and they're so helpful!
Very helpful. Goes out of her way to help students with study abroad programs and finding jobs. Very energetic teacher. Great class! (Not her fault the characters are hard!)

This class is torture. Seems to be a good amount of kids already with some proficiency in Chinese, so you are left to catch up. The workload is nonstop, she seems to think this is your only class, and she has a somewhat cold attitude towards your troubles. I do not recommend unless you are VERY interested in the subject.

I took intro Chinese back in 200 0 when there were only 19 students taking it.  Then 3 years of higher classes & independent study.  Excellent attentiveness to student needs, encouraged students who tried to study further, go abroad, helped get teaching jobs.  Really works her heart out for students and deserves great appreciation.

If you are taking this class to fulfill a language requirement, don't.  Liu  is a good teacher, but the class is way too demanding.  If you came to Vandy solely to learn Chinese, this is the class for you.  But if you want to have enough time for the rest of your schedule, don't take Chinese.
good teacher. youll learn chinese just have to get used to chinese being hard.

Liu Laoshi is a great teacher. She makes sure you understand all the grammar points in the text and makes comprehensive review sheets for the tests which are extremely helpful. Clearly Chinese isn't the easiest language to learn and the class does require a good bit of work, but if you keep up with it and study every night, its not hard to get an A

I took 201 and 202, and both semesters I ended up spending more time on that class than my other classes combined. She is a good teacher, but characters are so difficult and so much is covered in a short period of time that it really doesn't matter how good she is.
Hardest Professor EVER
It takes just a little effort to get an A.  Just make flashcards for the character quizzes and spend some time preparing for the tests.
Hard as hell. Chinese is a great language, but beware, you're gonna have to work really hard for a good grade. TIME consuming!
Incredibly straightforward and helpful, she really wants you to learn the language.  Class is interactive and interesting.
No Comments
Professor Liu does an excellent job explaining things.  She is enthusiastic and dedicated. Her tests are straight-foreward and don't require an unreasonable amount of preparatioin.

Professor was fine, but lecture was both totally useless and attendance was mandatory for some reason. In spite of that, I still regularly skipped because I couldn't be bothered, and still got As on tests.

This review is for CS2212 Discrete Structures. Koutsoukos was ok. Read off the slides and bored me so much that I'd skip class often even though attendance was mandatory. Learning content outside of class was doable but stressful so I'd still recommend you attend lecture lol. Cheat sheets and extra credit opportunities helped with the final grade.

This is for CS 2212. Good professor, cares about student understanding, overall good dude. Tests are straightforward, homework can be challenging but not impossible. Zybooks are essential because we don't learn too much in class but we do practice.

Koutsoukos is a good professor who cares about his students. He is very straightforward in lecture and with assignments. It sometimes feels like we don't cover that much material in class, but other than that, a very good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best professor i've ever had at Texas A&M. He truly cares about you as a student, and will go out of his way to help you with practice questions, after class reviews, and before test study sessions! I got an A and i'm terrible at math, if you dedicate some effort he will make sure you pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof Koutsoukos' Deep Learning class is very easy. The assignments are easy and straightforward to code. There is one midterm worth 30% and one project worth 30% of final grade but both are very easy. Overall a very easy subject and class. Koustoukos is a nice guy although his lectures can be dry. He is also an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This is a really good class to take for CS Depth credit if you're a CS major. The tests are very clear and not too difficult if you understand the material and go to the review session. Definitely recommend.

He is a great teacher, although his lectures can be boring, he makes it very clear what he expects from you.  Most of the grade comes from the homework.  And during the lecture (if you pay attention) he basically gives out the answers to the homework.  Very good experience, I highly recommend taking his computer engineering module.

Great teacher. He's never condescending when you ask him a question that you know is beneath elementary to someone as smart as him. Always respectful and he'll learn your name even though you're only in his section for a month.  Clearly lists out everything he requires. Glad I had him as my introduction to engineering, sad his section is over.

Had him for the freshman CompE module.  He's a fairly easy professor and knows his stuff, but like the other raters have said, he's extremely boring.  However, the homework he comes up with is rather practical and interesting once you get past his mundane lectures.

(Fall 2010) Had him for the CompE module of ES 140. Impossibly boring lectures, but if you pay attention, he literally gives you the answers to the homework. You have several quizzes, but none of them end up counting toward your grade. Incredibly easy A.
For CS majors this is a must.  Great class, so easy.  Tests are open book.  XK is awesome once you get to know him.

Nice guy, but very concerned with his appearance in front of the class. He won't admit he made a mistake.  If it is unavoidable, a mistake was made, but it was't his fault. Easy assignments, easy A, boring lectures. Won't post hmwk before it is assigned.
Didn't take attendance at 9:00am this semester--I liked the course and it wasn't too hard
takes attendance at 9am, oh yeah, boring as hell
No Comments

Super nice teacher with detailed lectures. Sometimes there are questions on the HW though that you have to learn how to do yourself. Detailed outlines for tests but the tests are still tough and you need to move fast. Final was very rough. Study and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get ready to not understand any concepts that she goes over! She does a lot of examples but the glides over the concepts, which I thought was the more important part of linear algebra.

She gives relevant examples and explains them well, doesn't teach proofs that we don't need to know, and she helps students in any way she can. Zhao is the best math instructor I've had during my 4 years at Vanderbilt. I am glad I took her class.

Update: Still a great prof for Vandy math, but made the final way harder than she said she would.
Best professor ever! She made MATH 2410 so easy to learn. She's also very open to student feedback. Take her class!

Dr. Zhao is such a caring and encouraging professor! She'll go out of her way to help her students in whatever ways possible. Linear algebra is not very hard conceptually, so I always surprised how Dr. Zhao managed to make challenging exams. The exams are a time crunch, but the good news is that she drops one of the 3 midterms.

Prof. Zhao is a great professor. Her lectures and notes were always good (although they followed the textbook closely). We were able to drop one of our three midterms which was nice. Tests were mostly very fair and were graded quite fairly. Always available outside of class as well for questions. Definitely take her in the future!
Great TA! Grades pretty easily and lectures really well.

Dr. Zhao is caring, kind, and a good lecturer. She grades fairly, if not a little light. As long as you go to her lecture and do your homework, you should do well with her. English is definitely not her first language, but you can understand her well enough. Definitely a good teacher.

Dr. Zhao was an absolute gem of a TA. She's very organized in her lectures (color coded chalk!) and super responsive outside of class (even at midnight the night before the final). She's also a genuinely funny and sweet person who really wants her students to succeed. I heard that she's teaching her own class next semester- try to take her!

Dr. Zhao is a wonderful TA, and I have heard she will have her own class next semester. She made a strenuous semester of calclulus much more manageable, telling what us what we need to know, opposed to things that we wouldn't need for the exam.

He's not the clearest during lecture but he's willing to help during office hours. He wanted the class average to be a B, which is high for a math professor, so he was willing to drop low grades/curve. Make sure to ask questions in class and you should be fine.

He is super smart! He made this notoriously hard class so much easier! I took this class with other teachers, and he also had some substitutes when he was out of town, and none of them can teach as clearly and quickly as he can! I was first annoyed by weekly quizzes, but they actually helped me prepare for mid-terms and final.
Smart guy and relaxed lectures, but his tests are absurdly difficult.

This professor is very smart, understanding, and so much fun. His delightful sassiness keeps a generally demanding course engaging and entertaining. Time-managment on the tests is crucial to doing well on the tests, as they are often longer than expected. He does offer bonus points though!

Very smart guy, moves fast sometimes so you have to pay attention.  It helps to skim the topic before class. Difficult class, but if you put in the work a good grade isn't too hard to get. 3 midterms, 1 final, and weekly quizzes (you can drop the lowest two quizzes)

He's not the best at explaining and his tests aren't too bad but you have to study its not an easy class but its not really hard either its just put effort in...get decent grade put more effort get higher grade. He made his first test wayyy too hard but he's getting better at it. he also takes off points too much sometimes....

Super merciful. If you don't do well on a test or quiz he tries to help you out and find some way to help your grade. Decent teacher, but goes really fast, you must pay attention. Lots of quizzes and 3 tests so you have lots of chances for getting points. Plus, he's reeeeeally hot. Awkward at first but can be really funny.

This is absolutely the most intellectually challenging class I have ever had at Vanderbilt, but Prof. Yang made it into an engaging and fun process. He made us realize how profound the concept of "equilibrium" really is, and showed the power of fundamental physical chemistry principles in modern biophysical techniques. Would take the class again!

Dr. Yang is a talented teacher who can make complex material so digestible. He asks insightful questions that challenge students for their understanding and keep everyone so engaged in class. The biophysical method part is my favorite.

Prof. Yang is the best. I initially felt intimidated by this course because of my weaker math background. However, Prof. Yang presents the material in such an engaging and accessible way that lectures became genuinely enjoyable. He is the professor who seems naturally meant for teaching, and the class material is so organized and logically clear.

I have never felt so stressed out in a class before. The lecture is very unorganized and mostly on a chalkboard. No study/prep material for exams, so you are forced to figure it out yourself from lecture notes. Homework is graded on completion/effort, which helps with grades, but leaves students confused when it's time to prepare for exams.

Agree with other ratings. Dr. Yang is the best professor I've ever had. His passion and knowledge for the topic make the class so inspiring and engaging. I would say the final was unexpected. There were no practice problems like that and the problems were very esoteric for me. I was extremely devastated to see my final grade as I loved this class.

Dr. Yang is the best professor I've encountered at Vanderbilt. His passion for the subject turns an abstract curriculum into an inspiring learning experience. He regularly calls on students during lecture, keeping everyone engaged. Dr. Yang links theory to real-world applications in chemistry and biology. I genuinely look forward to every class.

Dr.Yang is a good professor who takes time to know his students. The class is based on derivations of equations from thermodynamics to statistical mechanics but he focuses on intuition more. He can be a bit confusing at times and that causes the class to go really slowly. Watch out for the final exam which is much harder that the first 3.
Professor Xia is the man. Although he has some accent, but his notes on board is very clear. He would give some method to solve the tedious problem more efficiently.

I stopped going to class about 3 weeks in, never showed up except the day before the midterms and for the actual tests. You're going to teach this material to yourself. That being said, the material isn't super hard, you just have to memorize how to do each type of problem. He can't explain at all though and frequently makes mistakes during lecture
Professor Xia's class is a like a dream. One can compare it too floating on a cloud, an asian cloud. His melodious voice forces the differential equations into your mind. Overall class was okay 6/10.
Professor Xia's lectures are crystally clear! He is the best math professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt.

Yes, everything graded in his class is easy, but you would be in a rather passive position during lectures since he seldom interacts with students, but is helpful after class and during office hours. I am a Chinese so I understand his accent, though it might be quite exotic to you at first.

While his accent can be a little much at first, you get used to it within the first couple of classes and then it's pretty easy to understand what he's saying, although he's not the best at explaining some concepts. He doesn't really interact with the class so if you like to ask a lot of questions this is definitely not the right class.

I love his class!, and yes, tests and quizzes were both easy. He will review the materials before the quiz were given. Definitely take this class if want to improve your grade. The bad thing is that if there is about 70 people taking this class, there gonna be only 7 people show up. Lol. 3 tests, 6 quizzes (drop 1), 6 homeworks and one final.
