i hated his class!!!!... he's hard to understand and he'll write a lot on the board and then erase it because its all wrong (dont bother taking notes). i taught myself the material for most of the tests. get a tutor instead of asking him for help. his tests arent bad if you understand the material though

Definitely take this class if you have a choice between him and another teacher.  The tests and quizzes were both easy and everyone made it out with a good grade.  Although it is easy to get discouraged in the beginning as his accent is impossible to understand and you will have to teach yourself everything.

Horrible English although i liked the teacher..told you exactly what is on test...never made test harder then the homework and gave a surprisingly nice curve in the end...would take the class over again if i had the chance
Xia is the man.  Teaches straight from the book, easy tests, good class.

This guy is a complete farce.  He speaks english poorly, is extremely unhelpful, and had no TA when I took the class.  Buy a TI-89, learn to use it, and you will have an assured B+.  Teachers like this make me wonder why I pay to teach myself.  He is like a foreign robot.  Take Z and go to class!!!
This class is a joke.

Xia is a nice guy, but he does have an almost indecipherable accent.  The material is pretty hard, but the first two tests are pretty easy.  However, BEWARE THE THIRD TEST. Also, be SURE to have a TI-89 and know how to use it.  It makes the class infinitely easier.
This guy cannot speak english! his class sucks and he grades unfairly.

Extremely dull; virtually everyone does the crossword while suffering through his accent.  Sure the first two tests are easy, but you better ace them as more than half the class will.  Also need to do well because the last test and the final require twice as much time as given to complete.
Terrible english makes the course difficult to understand if you're not good at math.  Not willing to help outside of class, if you need it i recommend the help sessions offered in Featheringill.

Tests are generally easy but if you make one simple mistake he will take off tons of points. If you do not get it he will not help in office hours or in class. Very defensive. English is not cute, it is hard to understand.

REALLY easy tests. Class is twice as east with a TI-89.  I think his English is cute and very easy to understand.  I find his teaching methods very logical and easy to follow... not nearly as bad as the other comments made him out to be.
No Comments
Old Chinese dude. English needs work. His tests are easy -- just make sure you own a TI-89 and know how to use it....
No Comments
He needs to retire.  His tests are really easy so it's easy to get an A.
Hard to understand, but very easy tests
He cant speak english, he simply copies from the book, if you dont get it, F

Exams were a substantial amount of our grade. The final alone was worth 30%, but he provides ample partial credit when grading. His lectures were a little boring, but he covers the material effectively and I learned a lot.

Other than the fact that I found the lectures boring, I have nothing bad to say. Attendance is not mandatory, tests were pretty manageable to the material, he is responsive to emails, and always reminds you abt due dates. Weekly written hw and webwork but again wasn't too bad and got the lowest grade dropped. Group project at end of the semester
Found lectures to be pretty boring. Grading is pretty heavily based on exams.

Super nice professor. The first two tests were super easy, and the third was very hard. Attendance is optional; my roommate and I never went (totally our fault, you should go) because we're not morning people. Although we did receive midterm deficiencies, nothing else bad came of it, and linear algebra is relatively easy to self-teach.

Dr. Ying always responded to my emails quickly when I had questions. His lectures clearly laid out the strategies you can expect to apply to homework and exams. 

I think that the math department grades the 1301 exams very fairly, tons of partial credit if you show your work.

I chose Professor Ying because of how well respected he is in the math department; however he is very standoffish towards students. Office hours are very awkward and quiet. His lectures were pretty good, but I learned I did better in the class once I started using the textbook more since his lectures were straight from the textbook anyways.

Hard to understand and not very engaging. If you miss class it's hard to know what was covered, so always go. In class he delivers a lot of content in a clear and understandable way, so it's not hard to learn. HW problems are harder than class and exams lie in the middle. Never any review of what was learned. Not a bad option for 1301.

Such a nice guy who clearly knows the material well. A bit of a boring lecturer; his voice is so soothing I fell asleep during lecture a few times. Only goes over the basics in class, homework and exam questions are MUCH harder. Found myself using chat gpt to teach me beyond the basics. Not really his fault though, math dept here just sucks.

Abstract algebra is always difficult, with a lot of material covered in one semester. Dr. Ying had a very manageable workload, however, with only 4-5 HW questions per week, all taken from the textbook. For exams, we had 2 midterms and no final. A paper was due during finals instead. The midterms were doable. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lectures can be confusing because they're very theoretical at times, but overall good. Amazing during office hours, always willing to help and great at explaining. Sometimes hints at what will be on exams. You get a whole letter sized cheat sheet for every exam, including the final. Read the textbook if you're struggling even after office hours.

A very interesting lecturer and keep students engaged. I was unable to go to office hours but he was always free to make an appointment when I needed more help with certain topics. Even though the class is tough, he was definitely supportive. The class code is supposed to be MATH 2300 not 2410.

Great lecturer, able to write on the black board in the clearest way I have ever seen. Homework, quizzes and exams are harder than lectures due to the nature of 1301, but if you follow his instructions and do suggested problems it's likely that you will be fine. Gradings are merciful as long as you demonstrate your understanding of course material.

Lectures are super useful. I do not believe attendance is actually mandatory but this class is too hard to skip. The quizzes use textbook problems that were assigned so are easy. The graded HW prepares you for the tests very well. He has a lot of office hours, which are necessary. The class is hard but the best way to take it is with Dr. Ying.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ying's lectures are very clear and structured. However, just paying attention in class is not enough. The exam problems are exponentially more difficult than the ones covered in class. Dr. Ying is very accommodating with office hours, and they are extremely helpful. Be ready to study and practice a lot!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super caring and helpful! Very clear explanations in class, so don't miss any. Tests and homework are very difficult. Office hours are useful. Dr. Ying always offers extra exam office hours, and he does a lot for his students, but the course is very hard. Small grading curve at the end of the semester. Best professor for this course!

The lectures were not helpful at all.  They hard to follow and did not help my understanding of the course material.  Was ridiculously hard for no reason.  The HW sets and exam questions were no where near the level of problems in the textbook.  Pls do not take, I have heard other 1301 professors are better for this class.

He is extremely intelligent. Seems like just a real guy and not an academia-type. I would watch a movie about him. But his lectures are very boring. The hw was mandatory + graded. It was hard and not fundamental to what we were learning. If you must take this, get a pro tutor from day 1, instead of waiting until your grade is already bad.

Prof Ying is very organized with homework sets, lecture schedules, and in-class notes. He is always supportive and inspirational during office hours. He explains complex concepts clearly with rigorous logic. Though his hw set is much harder than others', you would be fine if you do the book exercise and go to his OH. He is really nice, take his!

Li is so precious. He is super nice, and his lectures are very very good. The exams and homework are very difficult and time consuming, but the more you go to office hours and ask questions the more you'll learn. The class is required to be very hard and have a certain number of people not get a good grade, but Li does everything he can to help you
The exams are very challenging. Bro is a walking math encyclopedia, he's very helpful.

I call him a "live version of the textbook" because his lectures are ridiculously clear and organized yet his personality is not the most exciting. Problem sets are tough. I had a study group and went to office hrs which made ps more fun and engaging. The tests are easier versions of ps but harder than hw and quizzes. Awesome prof. Great person.

Li was a great lecturer. Really didn't need to learn anything on my own because he basically went through each lesson from the book. He gives out optional hw problems but you need to do them since the quizzes are identical and the tests are just an extremely hard version. Watch out for the tests on the series. Just be prepared to work a lot.

Li is very intelligent and an excellent lecturer. His accent takes getting used to, but his handwriting is perfect. A cheat sheet is allowed on quizzes and exams, and quiz problems come from optional hw. Problem sets and exams were immensely more difficult than any practice available or problems done in class, and averages on both were pretty low.

Li was a pretty good lecturer. His teaching style is very clear and easy to understand. However, the practice problems are no where near representative of the exam difficulty. Even the graded problem sets were near impossible to do well on even though he allowed group collaboration. Get ready to study a lot because his exams are so difficult.

Prof. Li did was a fantastic lecturer, and was able to explain complex problems very clearly to his students. He was harsh, but also fair in all of his grading. Expect to struggle a bit in this class, but if you work hard, you will definitely finish with at least a B. (P.S. take full advantage of him allowing a 1-page formula sheet for the exams)
Very good, organized lectures with plenty of practice problems and worked examples

Professor Ying has a very deep knowledge of calculus, which is obvious in the way he teaches. He is good at breaking things down and getting into the details. He can be a little quiet sometimes but is still understandable. He teaches at a good pace and is a fair grader.
Professor Ying is really good at explaining things clearly and is very organized. However, this class is very hard and most exams have a low average.

Good lecturer and goes over as many examples as possible in class and light on proofs. Takes attendance maybe once a month. Only 3 homeworks, 6 quizzes and 2 tests. He lets you use a cheat sheet for each quiz/test and all the problems on quizzes are in the textbook. Also grades pretty lightly and is generous with partial credit on tests.

His lectures can be a bit inaccessible but compared to other staff lecturers, his exams are very fair and his syllabus is straightforward. If he sees that one exam was much too difficult (exam 2) he will adjust the later exams.

Li gave really good lectures. Though he has accent, it is not hard to understand. He is very willing to answer questions no matter inside or outside of class. But, the 1301 materials in general are too hard to get A. I went to every class and did all the homework questions, but the exams were still very hard for me. DON'T TAKE 1301 IF YOU CAN

Li is one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. He explains material clearly and is always willing to clarify hard concepts both in- and outside of class. Li is caring and kind person, and I would take any other class with him in a heartbeat!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Calc 1200 is a pretty difficult class. No matter what professor you will have, you will struggle. I personally would say that having calculus background beforehand will definitely help you do better than the other students. I would also say that you have to work your butt off to succeed. To be honest, this professor has easier tests and grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Math 1301 is an extremely difficult weedout class, no matter your math background. Professor Ying explained difficult concepts clearly, especially given that it was his first semester teaching at Vandy. Tests are hard but that's true no matter the professor. Office hours are helpful and he's overall a genuinely nice person. Don't skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Ling is definitely knowledgeable of all coursework. He answers questions until you understand and is very accessible outside of class. But you have to pay attention and go to class in order to do well. Accent is fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible professor. He makes simple concepts overly complicated and leaves students underprepared for quizzes and exams. He is also very unclear with feedback on grading and seemingly takes points off for no reason. His significant accent also makes it extremely difficult to understand him or ask questions. Avoid at all costs!

I mean I'm sure this class wouldn't have been that difficult if the professor was better. With an extremely heavy Chinese accent, he is unable to understand most students' questions as well. This leads to a student not even asking a question because he's just not going to understand it. I'm sure he's a nice guy, just don't know why he's a teacher.
Typical introductory calculus course. Professor is sufficient in teaching to learn the material. Basically if you study and pay attention in class you should be alright.
Dr.McDonald really cares for her students and the content. Lectures are repetitive and boring, however she gives fair grades and if you keep up with the progress it's easy to get an A.

She's clearly an expert and genuinely cares about the material, pushing you to think deeper. Not a harsh grader, but expect consistent reading and a few pages of writing each week. Attendance and participation are mandatory. Overall, just wasn't the most interesting course for me.

Dr. McDonal is kind and approachable. The class itself felt slow and repetitive with long lectures and a lot of discussion/group activities that did not always feel productive. Laptops are not allowed. fair grader, so it can be an easy A if you sit in the classroom 3 hours everyday.

The worst class I have taken in my four years at Vanderbilt. Really arbitrary and annoying deadlines, generally unclear instructions, and incredibly boring lectures that are drawn out to reach 3 hours. In the first half of the class, you do ridiculously long essays for no learning. The second half is a group assignment that could be done in a day.

Dr. McDonald is really nice though at times disorganized. Her lectures can be long (especially since this class met once a week for 3 hours), but she is very kind and funny. I didn't have any knowledge or interest in water justice before this class but she made me interested. Weird grading policy, but easy grader. Would recommend to others!

Condescending and rude to students. Teaches basic accounting but proceeds to give out exams that are harder than they should be. Considering that this class is beginner level and a 1.5 credit, Dr Yang has made the course an absolute headache.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst class experience I've had at Vanderbilt. He was very condescending in class and created an environment where students didn't feel comfortable asking questions or making mistakes while learning. Do everything you can to take BUS 1100 with a different professor

Professor Yang is definitely knowledgeable about accounting, but his lectures are very boring. Also, his tests are insanely hard and teaches basic accounting material, but puts high level accounting on the the tests. He also shows little emotion and kind of thinks he's better than his students. He is very easy to reach after class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough teacher, he really only talked to the first 3 rows. It was very tough understanding him and he went at the speed of light during lectures... he would usually leave 30 minutes on the clock due to just rushing through. If you have the option, do not take him (Save your GPA). Also tests were VERY hard.

He's not that bad. 3 points extra credit on final grade. Test averages were just below 80 which was tough and he can def be condescending, but an A is doable. Prob avoid if you can but if not can still do well.

yang is solid, he def can be condescending and move super quickly but there are ample opportunities to practice the material and study for tests. i see both sides of the argument here, i def benefitted from prior finance knowledge. still bombed final tho. id prob avoid if possible but not a bad professor

Yang is a decent professor who does explain the material relatively clearly. With that being said, exams were relatively challenging (he does allow the final to replace the midterm), and homework due both before and after each class was a lot of work for a 1.5 credit hour class
Very bad and inconsiderate, thinks he's above everyone because he went to colombia. Can't understand him at all. Cold calls and then makes fun of you for not knowing

Not a good lecturer at all, barely anybody even showed up to class. Nice enough guy but was way out of his depth teaching the course. The Midterm and Final were both far more difficult than the practice exams

I took this class without a prior accounting background and found the lectures very fast-paced and difficult to follow. I spent a lot of time outside class reviewing material to keep up. The midterm was especially challenging relative to lectures. I also found him hard to reach outside of class.

I found this class frustrating. Lectures moved extremely fast and often felt dismissive when students were confused, with little effort to slow down or clarify. It felt like you were expected to already know the material. I struggled to learn and would not take another course with this professor.
Not sure what everyone's problem is with Professor Yang. Exams were similar to content learning in class and very manageable if you studied.
With extra credit and homework, it is not difficult to get a good grade. He also replaces midterm with final if you do better on final. Not a bad choice.

I personally found Dr. Yang to be super cool. People here are way too sensitive. Yeah, his midterm was kinda dodo, but he made the final extremely easy. Just do the homework and pay attention in class, and you'll get an A. It was his first time teaching, so obviously the midterm wasn't perfect. Not a bad choice at all.

Do not take this class with him. Tests were much harder than homework, and lectures were a mess. Went over the midterm in 5 minutes with barely any explanation because he expects students to know everything already. Very condescending when students ask questions, and overall a bad lecturer. He's a new teacher, but still, take anyone else.
40% of this class is basically free with homework with keep the pace quizzes. the tests are fair and he gives partial credit.
Materials are hard compared to other business classes. But he was responsive to requests and questions in my experience. Learned a lot and helped me prepare for interviews.

I did fine because I had previous finance knowledge. Yang is a funny guy but he is the worst professor I've had in college. The tests are difficult and he is not accessible outside of class (I think the median was in the 60s). He also will make fun of you if you ask a question, so beware. I really would advise taking this with a different prof

He is a genuinely kind and down-to-earth professor with high expectations for the class. At times, the exams felt overly difficult compared to the study guides provided. Since it was his first time teaching, there's definitely room for growth. He's a great person but the introductory course may not have been the best fit for a newly hired professor

He apologized the last day of class, which made me feel a little bad. However, when people would answer questions incorrectly, he would be so condescending. He explains concepts like we have already learned them. This is his first time teaching, so I give him some grace.

Exams have unforgiving MCQs completely disconnected from HW/KP. The practice test is misleadingly easy. Yang's lectures are dry and sometimes unenergetic (understandable given it's his first time). He needs to fix his slides and actually walk through practice problems in class that match the real exam difficulty so students aren't blindsided.

I stopped going to class because the textbook was more helpful than he was. He expects everyone to understand difficult concepts the first time and looks down on those who can not. He speaks so quickly that the second you grasp one concept, he's already moved onto the next two. Don't register if you don't have to. At least attendance is optional.

Yang is condescending and unhelpful. Content can be challenging without a finance background, but should not be half as hard as it is. Talks about how students scored 50s and 60s on the midterm and doesnt realize it relates directly to his teaching. Its manageable to get an A in the class but not by attending his lectures. teach yourself everything

Professor Yang is extremely rude and will not help you at all if you have extra questions after class. While I expected accounting to be somewhat boring of a class, they way he teaches is incredibly horrific and will put you to sleep. Avoid him at all costs! Also, he does not offer partial credit on exams which is also a unique way of grading.
Good professor

Professor Yao was amazing and really cared about both her students and the Chinese Political system. Very laid back class with occasional projects that don't take that much time to complete. There's a final paper, but she's very accessible during office hours and gives great feedback on your papers. Would definitely take again

Professor Yao is very caring and thoughtful. She‘s always willing to discuss and help us any class related questions and did not grade very rigid. Didn't spend much time to study after class but still managed to have a good grade since she always have make-up assignment to revise grades.

Professor Yao was amazing!! I thoroughly loved this class and the papers I got to write. If you meet with her about paper topics or assignments, she is very helpful. Would recommend taking this course if you are Political Science.
Really enjoyed her lectures. Definitely recommend taking.

Professor Yao gives engaging and informative lectures. Being in her class was a blessing, as she was always there to help! Every assignment was graded reasonably with clear rubrics, and she was very understanding. I would definitely take her course again in a heartbeat :)
Amazing professor

Professor Whang is not just an effective teacher but a kind and understanding person. She genuinely cares for students and is deeply committed to their growth. She has high expectations but will meet you where you are to work with you towards your goals. She's receptive to feedback and wants you to take advantage of that. I absolutely adore her!

I love her class so much. She is very caring, humble, and approachable. Her drill activities are always fun and engaging. Her feedback is always helpful still not intimidating. I learned so much from her class and gained confidence in Korean.

professor whang was okay, but the drill sections of KOR1102 were just not helpful for my learning. sometimes she felt a bit condescending and didn't explain certain grammar points well. overall not a great experience, but it was an easy class.

This lady is my favorite. I look forward to her class every day. Makes it completely enjoyable, and everyone is a comedian. We made keychains one day in class and played ddakji game. TOO FUN! She is very bubbly and bright.
I LOVE HER SOO MUCHH. She's soo sweet and caring.

**Took KOR1101-1102** Professor Whang is so so nice!! One of the kindest and most understanding professors. Her classes are so fun and give you a good understanding of the course material through different activities. I will be taking as many classes as possible with her!
Shes so kind and patient with students, and is very helpful with the feedback she gives. Its obvious that she cares about her students and helping them improve in the language.

Dr. Z was great! I had prior experience with python, but her lectures helped clarify some topics I was unclear on. Attendance is technically optional, but there are occasionally geotagged tophat questions. She switched to a lockdown browser for the final exam of the semester, so the average on exams was finally not inflated by cheating.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is an amazing teacher! I came in with no python knowledge and limiting coding knowledge. Her tests are very predictable and she's not overly harsh on the homework. Uses lockdown browsers for quizzes and tests. You learn a lot and its not super difficult to get an A.

She was a clear lecturer and an easy grader. Lectures were a mix of slides and coding. Attendance was mandatory, but you only need 80% of the attendance score to get the full attendance credit. Exams weren't hard if you do all the homework and read through the slides. Offered many sessions of office hours. Highly recommend!

Challenging class for someone w/ no coding experience, but Prof Zhang was amazing. She adjusted lectures based on what the students were confused on. She and other TAs were knowledgeable. Pace moves quickly in class and exams were always a time crunch. Luckily some cheating was avoided this semester due to the lockdown browser. Attendance mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class moved a lot faster than I anticipated at first, and the lectures are hard to follow. In-class tophat questions are given little time and pretty difficult. The midterm exams were no cake walk either, but the final was open-note and PAs are weighted heavily which allows one to do well.

Professor Zhang is nice and encouraging! She was good at teaching the course material. I found the exams to be quite hard, like the multiple choice or typing code and manually indenting it in the Brightspace so you could not test it. 

Also people do cheat with AI and I wish that was monitored more because it brings up the class average unfairly.
Dana is wonderful. Very lenient to mistakes and understanding. She is a clear lecturer and makes the material easy to consume.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang is the best professor I have had at Vandy in one of the "gen ed" classes. She sets clear expectations for the class and as long as you do the practice exams, programming assignments, and pay attention in class, you will be fine on the exams. They are straight forward. Go to her office hours if you have questions because she is helpful!

Great lecturer and cares about her students. Personally, I thought the exams weren't a time crunch as some have stated. MCQ goes by pretty fast. Coding problems require some reading and thinking but there are hints given. Cheat sheet allowed on the exams. Attendance/participation through TopHat which accounts for 10% of your grade.

While the tests are designed with random questions to minimize cheating, the cheating using AI isn't monitored, which makes the average high, and unfair for those students who actually follow the honor code. Tests on Brightspace without a lockdown browser or a password allow this to happen freely. Weird.

Professor Zhang has been incredibly kind and accommodating to student needs. She was always going above and beyond to get our feedback and improved the class immediately according to it. She provides us with more than enough support to excel in the class, although the content can be pretty challenging. Def worth it if you wanna learn how to code!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is definitely the hardest course I've taken. The exams ruined my grade in the class. She makes them impossible to complete within the time & is very aware of that. It doesn't matter how much you know but how fast you can work. As someone who struggles to work quickly, this was a nightmare. You can only get a good grade if you're a fast worker.

Vandy's coding classes are unnecessarily challenging when there are plenty of YouTube tutorials available. I chose Python, thinking it would be easy, but after the first midterm, it got much harder. Prof. Zhang is great (hands down!), but the other one has easier exams. Ultimately, focus on your grades and take the easier option, if you can/want.

Dr. Z is the absolute best. If you're a DS minor who is concerned about coding for the first time, Dr. Z is the best professor to take CS/DS 1100 with. She is so kind and goes beyond to help students. By nature, the class is difficult, but Dr. Z is more than willing to give extra practice and fully caters the class towards whatever students need.

Professor Zhang is very nice and caring. She answered questions after class even though you could tell she had another one in fifteen minutes. Class was a little chaotic at the start, but once you settle in, it's pretty clear grading material. Only gripe would be that she goes pretty fast during lectures, so you have to lock in for note taking.

Explains things well, but the in class examples are a lot easier than things you are tested on. Exams are a time crunch and make you code in brightspace. Also, the class gets exponentially harder about half way through.
Love her!! Really nice online notes and always care her students as our elder sister!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang is the best CS professor I've had at Vanderbilt. She sets clear expectations and guidelines for how the course will be graded, and she cares about her students' learning. Your performance mainly consists of PAs, participation credits, ZyBooks readings, and exams. The exams, as others have mentioned, are a time crunch. Straightforward A.
Very nice professor and willing to help. However, her in-class examples are much easier than PAs or tests. The class starts off too easy and becomes difficult very fast.

Dr. Zhang is incredible! She's very organized, and her explanations are clear. She's always checking in to make sure we're coping with the material. Grading is generous. Deadlines are strict, but there is grace sometimes if you do the work. I didn't find this class too hard. PAs could be challenging but def doable. Caveat: I took AP CSA.

I don't know why everyone praises her, she is fake nice and doesn't care about any of the students actually doing well. She is extremely difficult to reach outside of class and doesn't explain things well in class at all which in an intro class is frustrating.
Very engaging instructor who tries to tie the material to practical application.  She grades fairly and provides good feedback on personal projects.

Professor Zhang is a great lecturer and clearly knows what shes talking about. Class is well-structured and well-paced. In class programming was easy to follow and helped a lot on PAs and exams. Tests were straight forward. PAs were also very manageable as long as you go to class or do the mandatory Zybooks. Highly recommend!

Definitely take her if it's your first coding class. She really takes the time to help you understand. If you put in the work, it's an easy A. The tests are a bit of a time crunch, though, so make sure you do it quickly. The questions are straight forward and there are no trick questions. PA's don't take more than an hour and there were 8 of them.

Profesor Zhang is super nice and very lenient. If you do your PA's and zybooks assignments you will follow. The tests are decently easy but they are long so you need to go fast to not run out of time. Also, she really wants you to get an A, at the end of the semester she tried her best to boost everyones grade up

Prof Zhang puts a lot of effort into her slides so you understand the concepts. She always does her best to make the content fun because she really loves to program. I found this class to be challenging because this was my first cs course so be sure to study and go to office hours if you have issues with past exam questions and PAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Zhang was a great professor. If you pay attention in class and work hard, you should end up doing relatively well, but the class still is decently hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: PAs were all easy. Tests aren't open note, but you're allowed a cheat sheet. She posted all of the lecture slides and any in class coding examples, so it wasn't difficult to catch up if you miss a class. Content was interesting, but I was falling asleep half the time because there wasn't much to do in class outside of listening and homework.

Zhang is great. She's young and understands her students. Her lectures are clear and correlate directly to the assignments and the exams. You get a cheat sheet on both midterms and the final is open book. If you go to class and pay attention as well as do the interactive textbook activities, you will get an A pretty easily.

Prof Zhang is fantastic. Every week, there's reading and an interactive text book. If you get >80% each week, you get a 100% in that area. Tests are pretty straight forward. For the second test, you get a cheat sheet, and the final was open book. She's caring, passionate, and her lectures were engaging. Highly recommend for an intro to CS!

Prof. Zhang is a gem. She genuinely cares about her students (curving when necessary, moving assignment dates following holidays, etc). She was always available for questions. Lectures could get repetitive, but they were interesting most days. Definitely take her if you can. The class itself is manageable, tests are more difficult.

The class is really hard and the teaching style isn't for everyone. But if you are able to learn everything outside of class and take the time to understand the concepts you will be set for every econ class you take. This class took a lot of time out of my semester but as long as you score in the top 40% you are guaranteed an A- at least.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly I think all the good reviews were written by the professor himself. Seriously, don't take his class.
DO NOT TAKE.

His lectures are clear and cover so much details that will for sure help me later on. He could just do the easy stuff like other sections have been doing but chose not to because he wanted his students to learn the essence of each concept (intuition and proof) which is so important for the econometrics classes later on. I appreciate his dedication.
Tests are way harder than the practice exams. Blamed the whole class for bad averages on exams and not his teaching
Goes beyond what the class should be and makes it much harder than it has to. DO NOT TAKE. Worst professor ive ever had
This guy sucks. do not take him will ruin your gpa
Not a good teacher. He seems passionate at least, but not great at teaching
Pretty sure the 1/5 ratings are just trolls... He's actually an excellent professor and deserves way better
Big fan of this guy! I will miss his lectures every single day :(

This guy is an excellent teacher, honestly. It seems like he has a great deal of teaching experience and really knows how to present the material. There's no doubt he explains the content far better than I ever could, even with a month to prepare!
not a fan of this guy
This is the best class I've ever taken! I learned so much from this class and his lectures. He has high standards but wants everyone to succeed and do well

I'm taking econ stats with him. There're five sections offered. His section is the toughest but most rewarding class I've ever taken. I've learned so much. Yes, it's the most difficult section out of all other econ stats classes. He's the one that teaches well. You won't like his teaching style in the first few weeks but will appreciate later on.

I have him for 1500 and it is just wonderful. Clear lectures at slow pace (and he makes a ton of good examples and has great handwriting). His tests both have easy questions and sufficient time to complete them. I see a lot of 1/5 reviews and I can promise you they are all from trolls. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

I have him for 1500. He is the worst professor I have ever had. He writes too fast and you can't read his handwriting, and he doesn't post lecture notes so there is no way to go back and try to figure it out yourself. His tests are completely different from the other 1500 classes and are exponentially harder. The average on our last test was
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have him for 1500 and it is just horrible. Unclear lectures at lightning pace (and he makes a ton of mistakes and has bad handwriting). His tests both have impossibly difficult questions and insufficient time to complete them. I see a lot of 5/5 reviews and I can promise you they are all from trolls. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS, FOR YOUR OWN SAKE.

To put it clearly, he's one of the best professors I've had. He speaks at a calm, engaging pace, writes clearly, and truly cares that everyone understands. The first midterm average was quite high. Enroll if you wanna raise your GPA and feel encouraged to ask questions :)

To put it clearly, he is the worst professor I have ever had. He talks extremely fast the entire class, writes illegibly, and does not care if people understand what he is saying. The first midterm AVERAGE was a 50, and he verbatim blamed the students for not trying! Enroll if you want to tank your GPA and feel belittled for asking questions.
Professor Zimran is amazing!!! He's the best econ professor at Vandy

I have him for econ stats. Zimran is truly the best. I learned so much from him and I can tell he geniunely cares about his students. He's super accessible outside of class and always willing to address any questions students have. He gives us lots of practice questions before exams and they're very helpful too. Take his class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Zimran is the best professor I've ever had at Vandy. I love his lectures and he always makes sure students understand the topic before moving on. He is super patient and cares about every student's success. He's also hilarious and tries his best to create a welcoming and collaborative classroom environment!
I have him for econ1500. He's the best professor I've ever had in my life. He's caring and accessible. Lectures are super engaging and interesting.

If your priority is landing on Wall Street or you aren't interested in the substance of econ at all (just for your "resume"), this is not for you. If you're here to truly learn economics, take his classes. 

His classes will challenge you rigorously, and in the end you'll learn more from him than from almost any other class at Vanderbilt.

I have this teacher forECON1500, and in all my years of school I have NEVER had a teacher seemingly go out of his way to tank kids' gpa's. His lectures move very fast and cover material that other teachers' sections of the same class don't even cover in the semester, and he grades the exams incredibly hard-- especially without proper allotted time.

If you want to die, take him. He doesn't care about his students. He came in and changed the syllabus completely and made us do things that was so much harder than what we were supposed to do. Other sections were doing the easiest things and he made us do such advance stuff. Please do not take him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I have ever had. Exams were incredibly hard and he was terrible at explaining things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Took ECON 1500. Worst professor at Vanderbilt.

1. No book, lecture slides, or notes provided. Assignments are not graded.

2. 85% of your grade is from midterms and finals (40%). No extra credit.

3. Doesn't matter how hard you study. Intentionally insufficient time to complete the exam.

4. Miss class? You WILL fail.

Please, avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was ECON1500 professor and I can genuinely say his class was the worst experience of my academic career. 1.) He assigned a textbook that was out of print 2.) He goes by the lesson so fast and undefiled 3.) class work does not match exam 4.) Grades are just exams and problem sets 4.) Even the tutors can't help us. Don't mess up your gpa.

Good: Reasonably interesting lectures & knows a lot. cares about the material. Not too much actual work (read 1 paper/wk, quiz every other wk). 

Bad: closed note quizzes suck. Final paper AND exam. No clue how you're doing in the class w/out asking. Super arbitrary grading. DO NOT recommend course unless you are highly interested in the material.

Don't agree with previous reviews. Class is difficult, but you will learn a lot and can do well if you are willing to put the work in. Professor Zimran is very helpful outside of class and is very passionate about his work. Wouldn't recommend taking it if you don't need it, but not a bad choice if you do.

Previous reviews are unfair, he's a good lecturer and very helpful outside of class. Week-to-week the class isn't bad, even though quizzes can be tough. The midterm and final suck though. Ambiguous questions, difficult material, extremely time-consuming. It's possible to do well, but I wouldn't take unless you need the course or love the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor is extremely strict and difficult to work with. Grading scale is completely arbitrary and students have next to no idea how they are faring in the class until they receive their final grade. 

Feedback on written assignments and quizzes is vague and unclear. 

Would highly recommend that students avoid this class, if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

Horrible person and horrible professor. Classroom is a hostile environment where he cold calls on students and humiliates them if they get the answer wrong.
