One of the worst professor I have come across at Vanderbilt. 

Guy is rude, dismissive, arrogant, brash, and hostile towards students. 

Final grade is based on a curve and the average on all of the assignments is between 50 and 60 percent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hard class. You need to pay a lot of effort, but professor Zimran is great. Lectures are detailed and you need to attend to do well.

Pretty solid prof. Cares about the results of students and is willing to go the extra mile for anyone who is trying their best. That said, class can sometimes be pretty dry/boring if you're not into 18th century British economic history. Pretty tough as well compared to other econ options, but definitely not impossible.
Horrible in every aspect

Great, respected professor, always very prepared to hold engaging lectures with interesting material. He is very willing to help you understand course material if you attend office hours. Covers a lot of material so easy to fall behind if you don't keep up. I learned a ton but be prepared to put in work and attend class if you want to do well.

Zimran is a great lecturer that explains economic history concepts really clearly, but his lectures are very fast and cover a lot. Quizzes are straightforward explanation of concepts for the most part, and exams were just analysis of papers, which you do every week in class. Great class if you want to learn, but requires some effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very organized and knowledgeable. But he expects an extremely high standard from his students. He's willing to help, though, and accessible. Don't take it if you're just looking for an Econ elective. If you take it, expect to put in lots of effort, and you can still learn something out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a really smart guy, but asks impossible standards of students. Quizzes were marked wrong unless they were word for word from his notes, even though they were closed book. Also grades whole class on a curve.

Got an A in the course and thought it was pretty straightforward. To do well you have to attend class though. Memorize the themes and strategies for each paper on the syllabus and it's fine. I learned a ton and thought it was incredibly interesting. He's a respected, published economist and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Absolutely ridiculous class with unreasonable grading expectations. An incredibly boring lecture-based class that is useless for learning Economics or History. He says that 30% of the class will get an A/A-, 40% will get a B/B+, and 30% will get lower than a B- but almost everyone seems to be in the latter category.

Extremely boring, 8am, outrageously unreasonable grading. I spent a semester waking up early to be bored out of my mind only to receive a grade that tanked my gpa. The amount of hard work didn't matter. Never heard of anyone getting above a B. Avoid this class and this professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Zimran is a legend. If you are academically curious and have an interest in U.S. history/economics, I'd highly recommend. Yes, you'll cram hard for tests/papers, but outside that, the workload is more than manageable. Zimran does his own economic research and is well respected on the Vandy faculty. I would definitely take him again if I could

lots of workload considering it's a lower level econ class. BUT, he told us that on the first day. I learned so much and how to view U.S history in economic perspectives. If you go to class, literally copy stuff on the board, and memorize you will be fine. HUGE curve. 1 quiz, 2 exams, and 1 paper which requires some work but go to office hour.

Do not take this class with this professor!!! No matter how much you love econ or history, it is NOT worth it. He makes the class ridiculously hard even though it is a lower level econ class. The final was cumulative and worth 40% of your grade. With that being said, he also goes super fast in class and puts in too much material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really great teacher. Cares about success and connecting the students to material. Weekly write-ups on readings that should not be done with AI. Wants the best for everyone, but lectures can get dense.
Nice guy very chill grader

Professor Zeller is such a great person. He is caring and understanding. He respects his students. The class is easy too as long as you do your readings. The presentation is fun and your final paper relates to your presentation's topic.

I really like the way Prof Zeller approaches assignments. It places an emphasis on learning instead of stressing about complete accuracy. Class goes by fast as he always has something to add, but he also encourages student participation. Some bumps along the road since this was his first time teaching the course, but overall great!

A really caring guy and loves his students. Funny too. Really easy A as well and helped me become a better writer and informed me of a lot about EU politics. He also really wants to learn from his students as well.

Dr. Zeller is a gem of the German department and Vanderbilt. His extensive knowledge, native understanding of the culture, and warmness towards students are all reasons why. The Avant-Garde course requires participation and interest, so make sure it's something you want to take. Overall, it was an amazing experience and course.

Zeller is a good professor. He really understands the field of Europe and history well. I learned quite a bit in his class. The class is super easy, requires minimal work, and has no final. He is a very respectable guy, but he tends to talk a bit too much in class. If you need AXLE credit, take this class and you won't regret it.

You kind of did have to do the readings for this class (I didn't though and it kinda worked out). There is one fat reading per week (70 pages ish). Dr. Zeller likes to hear himself talk which is good and bad. This seminar was about nature yet somehow we rarely talked about nature. I was very bored every class but it was an easy A. Little work.

Had Zeller for a FYWS and he noticed that I had read most the material in other courses before. He supplied me with a reading list that he thought fit my interests and invited me to meet with him and discuss the works on a regular basis. I very much respect his teaching style and belief on grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Zeller is big on participation, but he talks about 98% of the time. Most of the time he is talking too, it is super unimportant to the topic of the class. This semester (not sure if it is for every semester) there were no exams. He and his three TAs are not accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Zeller is a super nice guy really cares about the wellbeing of his students. Super manageable: 1-2 hours of reading and one response each week. Final project proposal is worth just as much as the actual project. He is very knowledgeable and can talk a lot but lectures can get kind of boring. Try to participate a little bit and you'll be fine

The class consists of weekly readings and 1-page double-typed journal responses. You don't have to do the readings and should easily get an A on these assignments. Attendance is mandatory and lectures are boring but participation and homework make up 60% of your grade. There is one project and one 4-6 page final paper. Super easy class!

He's a great guy and he's funny. His lectures are fun and he's easy to understand. If you take his classes, be ready to participate. His questions aren't hard, it's just some have a hard time with being vocal. German fairy tales was a great course and I recommend it because it doesn't require much (except reading) and it's taught well.

I took a Maymester with Professor Zeller, and it was awesome. He is so knowledgeable and wise, definitely talk to him about the class, or about life, society, global warming, anything. He's also incredibly caring and understanding about his students. Definitely take this maymester in Vienna if you like european art and/or culture!

Professor Zeller is clearly well versed in the subject, but the class and grading is based on his opinions. He is not very clear or helpful regarding major assignments. Attendance is mandatory even though there are no tests. The class is boring, but if you can deal with that and write a fairytalebuild a website that Zeller likes you're good.

The readings that he assigns are boring and long and only in PDF form. You have to read them to pass the weekly quizzes. Attendance is mandatory, which is frustrating because besides the weekly quizzes on readings, there is no point in coming to lectures since you won't be tested on them. Group project for midterm and final not explained well.

Christoph is a good professor but treats his students like middle schoolers. Unnecessarily long discussions in lecture about useless imaginary situations and excessive weight placed on blogs and discussion questions. One of those teachers that is offended when people use their phones on class, even if they aren't distracting. Boring material.

Mr Zeller was a guest lecturer at my university. Without any doubt, he's one of the most amazing teachers I've ever had. Very fair grading, great personality and incredibly intelligent with diversified knowledge. I've never had more lively discussions than during his class. Just ask him any question - his answers will amaze you!

very nice and always contributes interesting spins on the fairy tales he teaches. introduces ideas from fine arts, other literature, modern culture etc. very fun class that is informative and does not require a lot of work other than abstract thought. a nice break from the intensity of most Vanderbilt courses.

Professor Zeller's class was very easy and did not demand much work (maybe 2 or 3 hours per week).  The content was very interesting; we discussed many important global issues.  He's a really nice guy, and wants his students to succeed.  As long as you do the work, you should do well!

Prof Zeller is an extremely fair teacher, especially in his grading.  If you try, you will do well.  Although I wasn't extremely interested in the material I enjoyed coming to class for the discussions and the movies we watched were good too.  Definitely recommend his class.

It was always amazing how the texts were boring and senseless 10 minutes before class started and fascinating 10 minutes after it ended. Okay, not all of them--but considering the topic--! ...  If you are a lit person, you'll really like this class; even if you're not, you'll really like Christoph; so either way, take the class.
The course topics that Christoph chooses are always interesting, and he makes good selections of readings.  He's extremely fair at grading.  An A is given if you do the work and do it well.

THE BOMB! Always super positive and the class is structured well with clear grading criteria. You move through a lot of content fast, so it can be hard to build intuition. I took stats in high school, so it wasn't too bad, but I have.a few friends who struggled. That said, if you take an hour or two out of your week to review you can learn so much.

Faith is a lovely person. Problem is with the nature of the course, not her. For an upper level math course, it is way too easy. For example, I made 8 mistakes on the second exam and lost about 0.2 points for each. The grade inflation is insane. You get what you make out of this course, which is disappointing. Free A.
Love her. Although the lecture is boring, it's easy to understand, and she's caring and helpful at office hour. Also, practice exams are really helpful. Not a hard grader.

Prof. Zhang was one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. She encouraged us to keep trying and structured the class for you to succeed if you put in the effort. However, the content could be difficult and the WebWork homework got long, difficult, and tedious. Be prepared to spend lots of time on it but it makes up a large portion final grade.
She's really nice and caring. But make sure to put effort into this class. Homework ends up being really important.

Really caring prof who tries her best but struggles to explain more geometric conepts. Not very good at conceptualizing how long it takes students to do test problems and sometimes put things on tests that we hadn't gone over. Definitely think she can improve with more experience. Study examples to prep for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Great notes, cares, and easy to understand. Don't NEED to get the textbook if you don't typically learn better from them, just take good notes and review her's.

Approachable and very accessible outside of class; super helpful during office hours. Very lecture-heavy; if you prefer a more interactive style, take someone else. Found her tests to be slightly harder than some of the other professors. Not the best at explaining material sometimes.

She tries to make class as easy as possible within the requirements set by the math department. Posts all notes online, and creates reasonable tests. 
Also very helpful during office hours.

Really enjoyed having Prof. Zhang. Very nice, accessible in office hours, and cares about her students. Great teacher and wanted students to succeed. Math dpt just sucks here, but Prof. Zhang had very neat notes, posted in class notes, and made tests as easy as she could within the math dpt.'s restrictions. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice and wants you to do well in the class. Lectures are a bit unorganized and she spends too much time explaining derivations for theorems instead of just doing examples. But she is very helpful in office hours and will go through the exams with you if you come.

Weekly quizzes, class is really boring, don't have to take notes since it's all posted, homeworks take a good chunk of time. Exams are not too difficult. Made this class very not theory-based which made it easy

She has very good understanding of the content. Lectures are fast and dense. It might be a little to follow everything, but as long as you get the gist of it (and operational details of solving test problems), your grade be fine. Gradings are tough and sometimes careless, so do not hesitate to argue if you find grading mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class had quizzes every Tuesday and HW due every Friday(both pretty manageable). Quizzes were based on the previous week's HW, so it ensures you're keeping up with the class content. Overall the exams were medium difficulty. lectures on TR were a bit rough and not the most engaging. Extremely helpful at OH and very flexible to meet. Syllabus good.

Really time consuming class, weekly Tuesday quizzes, and if you miss a few minutes of material in class you'd be lost like a bird in Manhattan. Ashley is a super respectable professor and great person but she takes way too long to get to the crucial points. It's only lucky she shares class notes. Overall class experience not great.

Very reasonable workload homework wise. Quizzes were take home. Exams make up most of the grade, but you get to make your own formula sheet (full piece of paper front and back), and the questions resemble the questions given in lectures, homework, and quizzes. She was also generous with partial credit, and tests had bonus available.

Professor Zhang is a nice person at heart but tough grader. Her rubric is strict and partial credit is difficult to get. 2 midterms contributing 25% to the final grade. No curve. Midterms extremely difficult because they are out of 50 but spread across like 10 sections of the textbook. Avoid at all cost unless you already know multi.

This was Professor Zhang's first semester at Vanderbilt and she was fantastic. I would not recommend taking any Multi on the Tuesday/Thursday time block as it is an incredibly dense and difficult course, but Professor Zhang was great. Exams mimic lecture, quiz, and homework problems so review those heavily. Suggested homework/book was not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Professor Zhang's first semester at Vanderbilt and she was fantastic. I would not recommend taking any Multi on the Tuesday/Thursday time block as it is an incredibly dense and difficult course, but Professor Zhang was great. Exams mimic lecture, quiz, and homework problems so review those heavily. Suggested homework/book was not helpful.

Professor Z is the absolute goat. You will get a lot of reading, so don't take this class unless you're interested in the subject matter, but he is the best lecturer I have had at Vanderbilt. He always engages students and pushes critical thought. Super interesting and deeply philosophical. If I could take him again, I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Denis was actually the most entertaining professor I've had at Vanderbilt. I took this course just for credit and became so interested in the subject matter because of his lectures. Didn't get the grade I wanted and still would do it 100x again. Great experience and very interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Favorite professor this semester. Professor Zhernokleyev was very effective at leading conversations in Core 1010, which were highly fruitful and educational. I had my worldview and understanding of what it means to be Human regularly challenged, and had plenty of interaction with those who hold worldviews drastically different from mine.

Zhernokleyev is one of the best teachers you'll have. The novels are classics, and his deep expertise greatly enriches the reading experience. Lectures and discussions are thoughtful and engaging. He can go on tangents, but you always learn something. Participation matters and essays are graded hard, but the learning far outweighs the final grade.

Every word that comes out of his mouth is gold. Professors like that are why you want to study at Vanderbilt. He's a genius who is passionate about sharing everything he knows and welcomes your thoughts on every aspect of what he says and teaches. Incredible
The best professor at Vanderbilt. Highly recommend taking any class that he teaches, super interesting and class discussion is alway fun.

Read W&P over the semester, discuss in class. There are 4 short-essay responses (1 as presentation) and a final paper. If someone is not interested whatsoever in the material, this class could be tedious; if they like the reading, this class is amazing. Genuinely my favorite class; it will do wonderful things to your reading comprehension skills.

Dr. Zhernokleyev is an amazing teacher. He truly cares about his students and their understanding of history, literature, and the world in general. You might have to take CORE and that's annoying, but definitely take it with him, he's actually so smart.

Easily the most intelligent professor I've had at Vanderbilt. I went into this class having already read a fair amount of Dostoevsky, and I still took so much from his lectures, office hours, and feedback. A must-take for anyone interested in literature, philosophy, or theology

Russian Literature is not a breeze, but Dr. Zhernokleyev is your best bet for a thorough, quality class. He takes a lot of pride in the culture and ensures students have background in culture and history necessary to understand the works being taught. The lectures are a bit dry, but a good FWYS for those interested in the subject.
If you want to fail, just do it

Although very knowledgeable in his field, very tough grader on essay and expect too much for students. Comments for paper are similar even though students already make changes according to the comments. A very hard w course but you learned a lot.

This guy is a genius. He knows his stuff inside and out. However, I think it also makes him expect a bit too much for us. I did learn so much, though, and it makes me think about literature differently. 

Get ready to read, though. We read  ~1550 pages this semester. This was more than double than any of the two W classes I've taken in the past.
Have taken multiple classes with Dr. Zhernokleyev. Most interesting and engaging lecturer I've had at Vandy. If you're like me and had never taken a Russian lit class, definitely give it a shot.
Greatest Professor of All Time. Encourages you to speak and respect your thoughts. Extremely knowledgable.

One of the best classes I've taken as a pre-law undergrad. The lectures are well-paced and interesting, and he gives good feedback on papers & is very accessible through office hours. Loved class discussions over Russian literature. The readings can be dense but definitely worth the time.

DZ is truly a great professor! Hes very passionate about Russian literature which made the class enjoyable- especially for someone who knew nothing about Russia prior to the course. Dont miss class, utilizes his comments, and do the readings. 5 short papers, 1 long paper, and a presentation. Great course and great choice for an AXLE W.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Pr. DZ is passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches. I have enjoyed the 2 courses I have taken with him and plan to take another. Note - his courses are for students looking to develop reading, writing, and critical thinking skills. Reading Dostoevsky and Tolstoy takes time and has been worth it for me. Highly recommend for all VU students

Hands down one of the best professors I've had so far! Vandy is truly lucky to have Prof. Zhernokleyev on its faculty. I took his Russian Short Novels Writing Seminar last semester, and it was an amazing experience. He expands class discussions beyond mere literature, and delves deeper into religious, historical, and societal factors!

Prof. Zhernokleyev is extremely well-versed in Russian literature and he pushes you to think critically about all the readings. He's a tough grader but gives wonderful feedback and truly wants his students to appreciate the novels as much as he does. I only took this class for AXLE credit but I'd take another class with him in a heartbeat.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Anyone would be so lucky to take a class with this man. Best Vandy professor!!! This class wasn't my 1st choice because I don't really have a connection to Russia and it seemed like it could end up boring, but his lectures made it so interesting. He's really sweet and works hard to connect with each student and you will learn so much and have fun.

Professor Zhernokleyev is the best professor I have ever had. He is so passionate about Russian literature. I was in his Russ 1111 short stories class and he was able to relate the literature to aspects of Russian culture and even hit on deep philosophical ideas. Discussion based so make sure you read the books.
he's smart and passionate about what he teaches. He has great work ethics as an educator. I actually wanted to learn the Russian language after taking his class in English.

Denis is definitely a professor I plan to take again in the futurehis passion about Russian literature really translates into interesting lectures and thoughtful discussions. The reading is mandatory because participation in discussion is required, and it can sometimes be a lot but it's all pretty interesting stuff. Def recommend this class.

I took the Russian Short Stories first year writing seminar. Denis is beloved by most of his students, and is easily the most impactful lecturer Ive had out of the 11 instructors Ive taken classes from. He knows an incredible amount about the authors, Russian history, and philosophy. He can also be quite funny, though slightly rambly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice and intelligent. Make sure you do well on the papers if you want a good grade. Not too much writing for a FYWS. The reading was A LOT, but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Zhernokleyevs a good guy. Responds to papers with detailed feedback, but grading criteria can be unclear. Writing seminar was 3 papers and participation (make sure you read). Grading was more based on personal improvement than how your paper compared with other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Denis (he asks his students to call him by his first name) is one of the smartest professors I've had at Vandy. Very passionate about Tolstoy and Dostoevsky. He didn't give much feedback / grades, and there was a lot of reading (all of War and Peace), but most of us enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class of freshman year. Denis is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about Russian literature, and he led discussions about the assigned reading very well. There were a lot of stories to read, but they were all interesting and not too long.

Denis is a passionate intellectual who deeply cares about the development of his students. He gives excellent feedback and has challenged me to become a more analytical thinker and writer. I highly recommend his literature-based courses. I will definitely be taking classes with Denis again even though my major is completely unrelated to Russian.
Very difficult to get an A, harsh grader on essays and all other assignments. Too difficult for a first year writing seminar, not worth all the time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Denis is so insanely passionate about what he teaches that it's impossible not to get jazzed about 19th century Russian short novels (not something I was initially excited about). He's a tough grader but gives great feedback. Super sweet and adorable and a snazzy dresser. Assigns a lot of reading but it's mostly manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Denis is the man. He's obviously super passionate about what he teaches and I think that helps his students get into the subject. I was not at all interested in Russian novels before but now I love them and that's because of Denis. He grades papers pretty tough but he's always available for feedback. Take his class and you'll learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Denis is still new, so I don't know that he'll give any A's, but he loves what he does. His class makes you think. I did not originally want to take it, but I'm glad I did. If you ask for help he will give it. A lot of reading, but he is a nice guy. (and cute!)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great except I feel like he could have done more with access controls in cloud storage

I really got inspired to major in HOD after taking a class with Saydolimkhon. He is a wonderful human being and an amazing lecturer. Tests were fair, and his quizzes are not hard if you listen in lectures. Highly recommend.
He is an amazing lecturer and a smart man

I took the travel class to Spain with Dr. Absi. Absolutely can't recommend enough!! If you have the opportunity to take this course, by all means, DO IT! Minimal work outside of attending the lectures, and the whole class traveled to Spain for spring break. So much fun, easily the best course at Vanderbilt!
Very enjoyable class. Passionate about the subject area and very knowledgeable.

Genuinely the sweetest professor I've ever met. She actually truly cares about her students and tries to make sure everyone is keeping up. Details on assignments can be unclear but genuinely just talk to her, she's super approachable. Looking forward to taking statics with her this semester.

Highly recommend Dr. Absi for any course! Had her for eng module & statics, will take her for MoM. Super respected professor, makes extra efforts to meet outside of class and help you, strict grader but fair. Lecture heavy but so many resources and really cares about students' success and understanding. Great person all around -- loved her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher and really cares about her students. One of the more work-heavy engineering modules, but still fun.

This was my favorite class I have taken so far. You actually get to apply what you are learning to the real world, and you get to learn how to weld. The tests are only hard because of the time crunch, but I always felt like the questions themselves were fair. Shes such a great teacher and offers so much support.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible homework structure with uneven dates between deadlines.

Professor Absi did a fantastic job making Statics a manageable class. While I felt exams were a sprint and could rarely be finished on time, she gave a lot of partial credit and if you showed as much work as possible you would get a fine grade. The welding lab and final project were also highlights of the class for me. Hands-on experience is great.

I have nothing but praise fro Prof. Absi. She was such a good professor she made me want to switch from wanting to be an electrical engineer to a civil engineer. She is wonderful! One of the many amazing faculty that Vanderbilt has. Stay ahead and make sure to check brightspace for due dates as some assignments can be time consuming (1-2 hrs max).
not great. idk. sad.

Interesting module! A little more work than the other modules, but not impossible. The guest lecturers were interesting and I'd recommend to anyone a bit interested in Civil Engineering. Absi was kind and approachable, but with the structure of the class didn't get to hear from her much.

Dr. Absi is a really sweet and understanding professor! She wasn't the best at explaining the project, but she didn't grade anything too harshly. This module has slightly more work than the others, but it was pretty cool and I'd probably take it again.
Good Proff. She is understanding and easy to approach. Very smart, but has weird grading sometimes.

Dr. Absi is an exceptional educator who goes above and beyond . She explains complex concepts effortlessly and creates a supportive learning environment where asking questions is encouraged.
 She fosters critical thinking and creativity, preparing students for real-world challenges. Her passion for teaching is evident, making learning enjoyable.

One of my favorite profs at Vandy. The class is definitely hard, but she makes it as manageable as possible. She allows for extensions on all homework if necessary. She's very good at explaining content and accessible outside of class. Definitely study A LOT for the exams and be aware that the TA may grade the homework harshly.

Dr Absi is fantastic and her module is as well. Most class periods are in the lab building a wooden structure that will eventually be destroyed with string. A few lectures here and there as well. Grade is composed of three relatively easy hw assignments and a final report/presentation. Slightly more work outside of class in this module than others.

Absi is a very supportive professor whose sole motivation is to ensure her students understand the content. While the exams and final project are difficult, she effectively explains all material and is highly accessible via email and office hours. If you have the chance or are considering civ e or mech e take her classes. You will not regret it.

Dr. Absi is the nicest professor I have ever had. She is very approachable both in and out of class, and clearly makes a ton of effort to engage with her students and loves her job. Her classes are pretty difficult, especially the tests, but you absolutely will not regret taking a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Absi is a great professor for mechanics of materials. She has very clear lectures on all covered topics and ensures everyone understands the material. Weekly homework assignments that reinforce whats going on in class. This class is more difficult that statics but not impossible. Tests can be tricky.

I am excited to take courses from her in the future. The class is tough, but there are so many resources & she goes out of her way to make herself available to help. Professor Absi actually **teaches** the content and makes sure that the students understand (as long as questions are asked). She brought in props and did demonstrations.

Profesor Absi is an amazing profesor and woman. She truly cares about her students' success in and out of the classroom. She brought amazing lecturers in and also made really unique, engaging projects. Would totally recommend.

I took this module with barely any interest in Civil Engineering, and now I want to change my major to it. Dr. Absi runs this module so well. Half of class is spent in the lab building a fun structure (group project) and the other half is listening to amazing speakers from the CE field. 3 homework assignments. She's very sweet. TAKE THIS MODULE!
Nicest teacher at Vandy. Many people underestimate this class. Not that difficult if you study but easy to fail first midterm if you don't. Good lectures and videos posted online if you miss class.

Dr. Absi is the best! Her module was by far the most interesting and engaging module I took. She really cares for her students and assisted me when I was having trouble adjusting to the Vanderbilt lifestyle in the beginning of the semester. She singlehandedly made me want to take more civil engineering courses. The best for sure!

Dr. Absi's civil module was the most fun class I had my freshman year. It was split up into lectures which were guest speakers from the civil engineering field, and lab work where you built and demolished a structure with your group. There wasn't a lot of homework aside from some math related to your structure and some short writing.
CE 2200 is very easy is you have studied AP Physics C Mechanics or equivalent before. Prof. Absi is also very friendly and gives reasonable homework and tests.

Ghina is such a kind, caring, and genuine professor. Class covers some tough material, lectures can get confusing if you are not keeping up with the material. Instead of a final she does give a group project, which although difficult, is nice to have instead of another final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: if you pay attention and put in the work, you will do fine. She is very good at explaining the material in her lectures and is fairly entertaining/lively. Final is a group project where all of the concepts from the course get applied.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Absi's civil engineering module for 1401. She is awesome! So funny, so knowledgeable, and cares so much about her students and the material. The class had group work that was worth more than half of the grade, but she was a fair grader, making sure that at least everyone I know got the easy A that they should. More than available to talk

Honestly my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. Had her for fall 2020 and was the only prof I had who recognized we were in a pandemic. Super helpful and kind! I was going through a really rough patch of burnout and couldn't get a project for the class done, but was super available outside class to help and was incredibly leinient with deadlines.

Dr. Absi cares so much about her students. She is genuinely one of the kindest people I've ever met! Her lectures are super clear and she is always willing to elaborate on certain concepts during and after class if you need help. I seriously wish I could take her for every engineering class. Absolutely take her if you get the chance!!

Dr. Absi is an excellent professor, and quite possibly, the most personable professor I have ever had. She knows the material and will help you multiple times over if you ask. All that being said, her tests are very difficult unless you spend a lot of time studying. Also, set aside plenty of time (at least a week) for the final project.

Nicest professor i've ever had, she cares a lot about you and your success and is super accessible outside of class. Attendance is tracked in class and homework is due weekly. Lectures can be a bit confusing as she gets lost but overall not crazy hard.

Cannot recommend Dr. Bhandari enough! Great lecturer and even better curator of course material to make you learn so much in just one semester. Essays were actually fun to research and write. Readings were not very long. He brought in current events too, so the class felt very up-to-date.
Great professor. He's witty and definitely knows what he is talking about. Lectures are super interesting!

Love him! The class is lecture-heavy-- there are weekly discussion posts, 1 closed note exam, and 2 papers. He grades fairly and offers extensions. I learned a lot and it was worth the effort. The careers in African politics presentation at the end is great. Highly recommend taking a class with Prof Bhandari, he's a super nice guy and cares!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good. Nice too.

This is the hardest class that I have taken at Vanderbilt, and the only class I did not get A- or better in. The course just felt very difficult and hard to follow. She does care about you doing well and tries to make it better though.
Tests are quite easy and honestly overprepared for them. I believe that this class is honestly more straightforward than people make it out to be, but lectures are definitely something.

Prof Sahakyan is fashionable and sweet and likes to bake sourdough bread. The first day of class was a bit scary when she warned that you needed to have gotten A's in the prerequisite classes and be very good at calculus, but really all that insurance economics boiled down to was optimization. Tests followed homework closely and didn't need prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you hate yourself, take this course. Prof Sahakyan is a nice person, but the amount of memorization that she expects from students who are already juggling 3+ other intensive courses is unheard of. She doesn't seem to consider (or even care) that her students are undergraduates, rather than PhD level, and humans rather than perfect robots.
She is clear and organized. Although I was struggling with the HW, getting a good grade was not hard. I felt  that I learned a lot.

Zaruhi is a nice person but her lectures are pretty disorganized. She also gives a lot of homework that requires you to code. Her tests are fair and she wants students to succeed, but the content is hard and there isn't really a way around that. Overall, she was fine but I'm in no hurry to take another class with her.

Zaruhi is pretty funny but hard to follow. I had a better time teaching myself material from the slides and YouTube. Expect to spend 6+ hours a week on homework if you don't know how to code and an extra 2 for two extra credit points (it's not worth it) (maybe it is actually). Hopefully I got an A on the final to somehow secure the A from Yucatán.

Lectures are scattered and hard to follow, with slides that feel thrown together. The coursework demands a high level of technical skill with little preparation, and the exams focus on niche material barely covered in class or practice. There's a major disconnect between what's taught and what we're tested on.

low ratings for Prof Sahakyan's econometrics are so sensationalized. harder than other econ classes, but still straightforward. She's very personable and wants students to succeed, and she is very clear in lectures about what concepts will be on exams (like literally the exact proof). Pay attention, go to office hours if needed, you'll do great

I am thoroughly convinced Prof. Sahakayan does not know what she is teaching. Her lectures frequently jump around and her slides are very disorganized. There is a steep curve with the technical skills needed for HW. Tests are extremely narrow in scope and homework/textbook/TA practice not representative of what is tested. Otherwise she is alright.
i had a a 3.9 gpa. first b at vandy. bad lectures, easy hw, irrelevant exam qs.

Probably the hardest ECON class at Vanderbilt not only because of the content but because of the way she teaches. It's sad but you will have more success learning the content from YT or chat than listening to her lectures. Good luck

Zaruhi might be one of the most charismatic and caring professors I have ever taken, and she gives you clear guidance on how to do well in her class. With manageable homeworks, plenty of study material, and super accessible for office hours, she gives you all the tools to do well in her class. By far the best professor for Econometrics.

Zara is a very sweet professor. Lectures are not organized, but the material is all there. HWs are tricky with python but you get over the learning curve, they get much easier. Tests were not that tricky, just read through the slides well with a study partner. Lots of extra credit which makes buffer for A. Zara is still probably best metrics prof.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sahakyan is nice but an average professor at best. Her explanation of concepts is subpar in class, but she holds relatively regular office hours. Her tests are straightforward-ish, and she gives you the necessary materials to do well through her slides and homework. Python is included, but you don't need prior experience with coding.

She's very fine. She is a disorganized in class. A lot of problem sets that are python heavy, and she doesn't do the best job teaching python imo. With that in mind, the tests are manageable and she is pretty straight forward in what she expects from you. She clearly cares.

I honestly don't know why prof Sahakyan is rated so low. Her explanations of the concepts are very intuitive and her slides are super helpful. I didn't really study that much for this class or read the textbook and did well. Most people don't pay attention in class so maybe that's why they struggled.

Dr. Sahakyan is very sweet and clearly very smart, but she is not great at explaining the concepts. Her lectures bounce around, and the class is painfully boring. The math is straightforward enough, and there is a decent bit of homework, but it's not too hard. Gotta study for the tests, though. Kind of a run-of-the-mill ECON class but really boring

A simple class made much more difficult than needed by an incompetent professor. She is often rude to students and I often skipped class just to study for this exam. However, you're forced to take it so do what you can to pass through.

I think Prof. Sahakyan gets a bad rep because she teaches a generally pretty hard class. But she's a good professor! Her lectures are helpful, and honestly, if you go through the slides thoroughly, you should be OK for exams. TAs are helpful for homework, and they're graded very leniently, anyway. Didn't really read the textbook and was fine.

Lecture style is tough to adjust to since she jumps around (spend extra time reviewing PPTs), but she highlights what is important. Homework assignments are VERY useful for practicing programming. Exams, while time consuming, fairly assess the material and aren't arbitrary. She quite fairly calls out students for talking amongst themselves.

thinks this is students only class, bogus exams that take longer than the class time + 3 hr final, does not properly explain things, makes fun of students to their faces and in front of class. avoid her at all costs! the class is too hard and the TAs have no idea how to explain either

Idk what the hate is all about. She is a quirky chiller. Favourite econ prof by far. Walk into class, she has music playing. If you dont wanna go to class, just tell her beforehand and she will give a full participation grade. Mid to Easy exams. Easy hws, some of which are AI based. Might be dismissive sometimes but she really does care.

Strong professor. Insurance economics not everyone's cup of tea but Dr. Sahakyan is an expert in the field and wants students to succeed. Exams difficult but if you go to class you know what to expect, which is more than can be said of other econ electives here

I think she get's a little misunderstood in these reviews. The content is difficult and she is a little scatter-brained but if you try to understand and do the problem sets, an A is easily attainable (especially because she tells you exactly what is going to be on it before hand). Basic calc skills needed. She's super helpful during office hours.

Content is difficult, but if you read the textbook you will understand the material. Unfortunately, the professor is the worst lecturer in the whole department and requires students to attend the lectures for a grade. She is incredibly disorganized & I genuinely learned nothing in class, and instead, learned the material through the textbook.

Taking notes in class is not helpful but her powerpoint slides are extremely helpful. Know them backwards and forwards if you expect to do well on tests. Don't expect to do well if you didn't prepare for the entire weekend leading into the exam. Do your homework in latex...she gives you a free 2 points on your final grade and it's pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Attendance mandatory, she lets you out late frequently. Really not that hard if you pay attention in class, but she talks fast so it can be hard to stay on top of it. Definitely takes some studying but the material itself is fairly straightforward.
Hard stuff but overall way better than 2350. Very helpful PowerPoint. Exam questions are the same as HW. Just don't take 2350, take this.

Note: 90% of the 1-star reviews you see on her profile are probably from entitled students who do not come to class and have made very little effort. Dr. Sahakyan already warned at the very beginning of the semester that attending class can be the difference between making or breaking this class.
I just loved this class
Easy A
Avoid if you can't do high school math
She was very flexible with HW deadlines and the tests were very much like the homework questions
Manageable workload. Not an easy A but totally possible with the curves
I just don't get all the negative comments here. Zara is one of the best you can get for Econometrics at Vanderbilt
Solid class. The material was hard but her lectures made it possible.
Nothing on the tests was beyond what she taught. Maybe I got lucky but she did curve grades at the end and mine was boosted up a whole letter grade
Great class in general and it wasn't hard to get a good grade if you go to classes.

I think it's overall a difficult class but the materials are super interesting and you can really learn a lot from this class - about how the insurance works and how to calculate the risk aversion. Professor Zaruhi is really chill and nice and is willing to move the exam dates and give extra credits.

I doth stand here to say that my family ruined

Yeah the class is brutal but everything you need is on her slides. People decided class was not worth it and paid the price... hard to feel sorry for them. Tests are difficult but nothing impossible, contrary to popular belief. She is a super kind and caring teacher. You have to adapt to her teaching style. Ppl need to stop with their entitlement.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you come to class, she will give you extra credits and will go through what she taught previously. The exam contents should be fairly straightforward after completing all assignments and going through her slides. Good course and nice professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't understand all the good reviews here. Perhaps you lot are masochists. Though I am leaning more on the other end mate, I do perfectly respect your characters and opinions.

Zara is caring and teaches classes with humor. Idk why comments are saying she's awful - exams are similar to hw q but most of students did not go to her class this semester. Someone got a low score in 2nd exam is because they just pasted hw solutions and did not actually solve the problem themselves, and she DID GIVE CURVE on final overall grade.
Econometrics is definitely difficult, but if you actually review the slides and turn in all the homeworks, then the class is doable. Zaruhi also cares about her students and curves.

Yo I'm probably the not intelligent guy yall elitists talking about here but I go to class and can't understand a word. Maybe Im just dumb brah but I grad my hs valedictorian and I darn believe I fit for Vand but I still don't understand. Yeah it's deep stuff I get yall but it ought to be understandable for a good old hs valedictorian...

OMG she would literally teach when the class is about to take an exam and I literally learned absolutely nothing those days and I literally get a rubbish grade. I am now staring at the cold blue walls of my hometown's counseling center. OMG I really wanna cry...

Honestly, I think most of the comments here didn't get to the point. Yeah she might be a tough grader, but the true issue lies in the way that she teach. Instead of trying to make students actively understand the concepts, Professor Sahakyan sometimes would simply make students remember stuff. She remind me of a bad tutor I had in high school...
The worst
Horrible Professor and Arrogant students make the worst class ever

I do not know why there are so many negative reviews. Yes, the material is difficult but that is not her fault. The majority of kids do not even show up to class and then do terrible on the tests. Her tests are similar to the HW and overall I think she did a good job teaching the course.

Other reviews are honestly out of pocket and make me question my fellow students' intelligence. The class was manageable, and Zara was super accommodating. If you try on the homework you will know what's on exams. She mentioned caring about RMP, so I think some students have decided to be bullies. In reality, this was pretty laid back.

Econometrics is tough, but Sahakyan is an incredibly competent professor. The class has structure. You are tested on what you are taught (which can be a lot a times, but is fair). I feel like I've learned, retained, and will retain so much more of the content than I did in intermediate micro or macro. People hate on her because they are lazy

Pretty good class overall but the final was way too difficult, I am praying that she would give a curve in the end. Other than tough grading, it is an interesting class and the Professor is helpful and accessible outside of class.

Professor Sahakyan is a very kind person but exams are wayyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy too difficult (the average for the second mid-term is in the 60s range, NO CURVE). The Final was impossible (I prob got a 42...and idk if she's gonna give a curve, but HOPEFULLY, SHE WILL) Hardest class I have ever taken at Vandy... makes me wanna switch to HOD...

Her test makes me disabled. My finger has been chopped off because of cancer incurred from her test. I can't do any more tests. Professor Sahakyan ruined my test, my GPA at Vanderbilt, my whole career as one of the brightest scholars in the world and my entire life.

Lectures/slides, practice q's, and hw answers are posted on bspace, and tests are very similar to the hw. Class is curved. If you spend more than 5-10 mins a week reviewing material and figure out the hw instead of getting answers from somewhere else, getting a good grade is not hard. I didn't get a good grade, but I also didn't go to class.
When I was young, I wake up at 5 every day to study very hard. Yet I still didn't pass Professor Sahakyan's class. -- Barack Obama
No one knows economics better than me, yet I would readily fail this course. -- Donald Trump
Even I lose concentration/doze off compared to students in this class -- Joseph Biden

Professor Sahakyan takes material that is relatively dry - risk, and economic decisions under risk - and makes it interesting and understandable through clear lectures, practice problems, and ample support outside of class. Explanations of concepts are clear, lectures are engaging, and she teaches with a good sense of humor and positive attitude!
iskapes sarsap eli e, yes uzum yem lats linel

She makes an interesting topic very boring by translating everything into obnoxious mathematic theorems and abbreviations, when all of these are mere tools of application and everything, at the end of the day, should concern the human heart. Not grasping the importance of the human heart, she makes the material super difficult and unintuitive.
She is simply the most unaccommodating professor here in the department. Would teach new material at the last day of class and expecting you to do it well on the exam 1 week after it.
awful! just awful!
OMG Like literally I get chills from the thought of going to her class because it is so difficult and the knowledge is so impending and difficult for me. Sniff sniff I literally want to cry,,,
Her class is like when sugar hits the fan, a phrase which that idiot called Alex like to repeat.
Professor Sahakyan is a nice human being and very funny. Unfortunately, her classes are very boring and her tests are very difficult.

Professor Sahakyan is the most accommodating professor I've had at Vanderbilt. She is always willing to extend due dates, records lectures for later viewing, and provides study guides for exams. The lectures are not incredibly engaging, but she tries her best and genuinely attempts to give every student the best chance to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: it is a hard class and she knows that - so she tries to make it manageable and understandable. she knows people are afraid so she has the TA's grade in favor of the students. easy A on the homeworks and the exams are usually a B average. i had no clue how to use python before the class and im fine now. i would take it with her again

Sahakyan is much better than these reviews make her seem. She is funny, and you can tell she cares about her students. The course is tough, and her lectures can be confusing at times, but if you go back and review the slides and read the textbook to clarify, you'll be fine. Make sure to study for tests, they can be tricky if you don't devote time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Sahakyan is a very caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. Her lectures are fun and engaging, and her office hours are very helpful. If you are willing to put in the work necessary to learn the material, this class is rewarding and quite fascinating.

Sahakyan is underrated. Attend lectures and you will do more than fine in the class! She tells you what is on the exam as she goes through lecture. The exams are very similar to the homework, and often have a lot of theoretical and short answer questions with a mix of math, but she gives you necessary equations. Go to class and I get the textbook!

She is a way better professor than these reviews make it seem. Honestly, she is a good professor. The material is just hard. Lectures are okay, but, if you attend and REALLY pay attention, they are not bad and she gives you hints on what will be on the test. She is very understanding, respectful, and knowledgeable. 100% would take again.

Sahakyan is a very kind lady with a good sense of humor. The lectures aren't the best, but everything graded in the class is very fair and not unreasonably difficult. The content itself isn't super easy, but with a reasonable amount of time put in it's not bad. Attendance isn't mandatory and she also records lectures which is really nice.

Zara is so nice, and you can tell feedback has been acted upon. HW graded easy, tests are weighted heavily but are also not graded super hard. Seems like the TAs grade a lot and they're fair. Lectures are hard to follow, but slides and textbook are great (most test Qs very similar to HW or book). Gets a undeserved bad rap.

Her slides and TA are amazing, but her actual lecturing abilities are terrible. Python demonstrations were not helpful and she could not admit when she made mistakes. By the end of the semester only a handful of people still showed up to class.

Very sweet lady, not sure why her reviews are so bad. Lectures weren't the best but her slides are helpful and the TA is very good. Exams were very straightforward. Good choice for upper division econ elective

The class was an absolute rollercoaster, but I think it was just because Sahakyan is not the best lecturer. That being said, I do believe it's very possible to do well in the class through looking at the lecture slides and reading the textbook; I will also say that the TA's exam review slides are extremely helpful. Attendance isn't mandatory.

Much better than these reviews make it seem. Very clear slides, and a funny professor. You have to take this class for econ major, and I'd recommend taking it with Sahakyan. Utilize TA reviews, read the textbook if you need to, etc. She is very kind and willing to push back Homeworks/exams if needed.

The class is tough. No getting around that. Prof is nice, but doesn't explain lectures well. I only succeeded using outside tutoring. READ THE BOOK. Do not skip a lecture. Take good notes. Study for the tests 2 weeks in advance. The 3 tests are 80% of your grade, HW is 20% of your grade. Know Python, or take CS/DS 1100 or 1104 before this class.

Not a super difficult class--the tests are pretty heavily weighted though so that's something to be careful of. Zara isn't anywhere as bad as the reviews make her out to be--if you actually pay attention in lecture the class shouldn't be bad. The material itself isn't bad and can easily be self-studied. Would rec prev python experience.

Econometrics is very difficult to learn but Professor Sahakyan is trying his best . She is a cool and caring professor. Tests heavy and lecture heavy. If you want a good grade in this course, be sure to read the textbook and have some prior knowledge of stats and python.

Amazing professor that really cares about each one of her students. However, if you do not put in the effort to do well don't expect to be given an A at the end of the semester. The class itself is very difficult with lots of material covered, and studying outside of class is a must, but Zara and the TA's are super helpful if you ask.

Sarah is good for students who learn. Trust me, most of us taking her class loved her. Sure she has some problems sometimes but it is common for other professors too I've taken at Vandy. Her homework are useful and she gave good feedback. she is very enthusiastic too and she cares about her students. She is much better than a 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is the worst teacher I've ever come across and I really regret taking her class. Her exams are nothing like any other homework assigned, and she is extremely unorganized and all over the place with her notes. She makes an easy topic unnecessarily difficult. BUT she is a kind and understanding person. Still, I hated this class.

Econometrics is a difficult course. Zara understood the material and met outside of class time whenever I needed clarification on the course materials. Future students should understand that most of the class did not attend lectures. The people I know who went to class agree that she is a good professor (I doubt that they would give her below a 3).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I honestly don't understand the bad reviews for this professor. She is one of the kindest I've had in my four years at Vanderbilt. She was always willing to push back due dates and exam dates upon student requests. She was a good instructor and made the difficult content much easier to digest. She gives you everything you need to succeed and more.

Terrible class and even worse teacher. Lectures are extremely difficult to follow. Also her tests are very hard to understand and do not assess what is covered in class. She also assigns long homework assignments that have no application to the material that we are tested on. Overall horrendous experience in this class.

Would not recommend her because she makes a somewhat simple topic into a difficult one. The homeworks take at least 3-4 hours every week and there are 12 of them. She also actively tried to sabotage her class by putting a password on the hw solutions (to punish those who aren't listening). Not a good teacher. Only upside is her tests are very fair.

Zara is hands down the worst professor at Vandy. Lies to her students about grading scales, has zero clue had to properly run a class, and yet thinks her students are the ones who are lazy. She has no idea how to work Zoom effectively. If you don't want to learn and want to teach an entire course for yourself, this is the professor for you.

She doesn't want the best of her students. Takes points off for random reasons such as formating or naming issues. She doesn't respect students' efforts and will make you feel discouraged by her grading. Besides, she is not the type of professor that you would respect either for her knowledge or for her personality. Her class ruins my semester. Bad

Her lectures arent the best bc she jumps around a lot, but she provides comprehensive notes, practice problems & solutions, study guides, etc. Her exams are not hard at all & hw is short. She goes above & beyond to give students learning resources, but she does kinda care about attendance. If you know basic stats then Risk is easy

She cannot adequately explain anything, nor is she able to provide examples of any of the problems in which is expected to know for the tests. She often complains "people aren't taking the class seriously" when actually we are--she simply is a poor explainer. You are better off skipping the lectures and teaching the entire course to yourself.

Problem #1: Lectures are incredibly dry - makes u want to skip and u will most likely skip (or fall asleep in lectures) Problem #2: tests contained questions worth 25% requiring additional stats knowledge (if u want an A don't take unless ur coming off of stats) Problem #3: teacher doesn't make material much easier to learn. Zoom + Risk  Brutal

Zara is not a bad person, she tries to be funny and I know she means well. BUT! Her lectures are incredibly dry and confusing makes it difficult to concentrate. Exams are not what is covered in lectures. She also takes points off for really random things like not naming the files correctly. Just read the slides you'll be fine.

She is the worst professor at Vanderbilt. Actually I don't think she is good enough to be a professor here. I know that's mean but I have to say that her lectures only make the material more confusing. Her English is so poor that sometimes no one knows what she means. She makes mistakes frequently so that her lecture notes are not reliable.

The exams are hard and do not test what was covered in class. HWs are impossible, and the material is very dry. Also told us to "stop pulling the covid card" when people were asking for extensions. When 2000 people a day are dying and the only thing you do is school and sit in your room with 0 social interaction, she could show a little empathy.

Im a senior and this is the worst class I have had my entire university life. Zara is not a bad person, but her lectures SUCK. You inevitably lose attention because her lecture are confusing and just dive right into the equations. I learned 95% of content by myself and I know my classmates did too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She gave us way more homework than she said she would, class runs 10 minutes long everyday, the exams are really hard, and she breaks multiple school policies by assigning homework during reading days and making the exam 3 hours. She is really nice, but I would not take this class again.

Zara is my fav econ prof at Vandy. Unlike others, she's friendly, open, funny, and very considerate. she keeps lectures lively and fun with her corny but endearing humor. she's very available to talk and cares about her students' learning. she also has a very generous grading policy if you show improvement over the semester. great econ jokes too.

She doesn't cover in class what she asks on the homework and the exams. The homeworks are very difficult, and it is hard to know what she is expecting. Before a homework, more than half the class used to be at the TA's office hours and the TA had to literally solve it for us, because no one knew how to do it. Do not recommend. She doesn't care
Kind and caring professor. Encourages coming to office hours. Not too difficult if you don't fall behind.
Class was unnecessary/She seems to have a lukewarm grasp of concepts, rambling lectures. Bad. Avoid.
very slow grader, barely teaches

Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the content. Quite a bit of reading each day, but it's possible to skim them. Would recommend attendance because most of lecture is her talking; she posts slides, but they don't have very much content on them. 3 primary source analysis papers(700-900 words), midterm, and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Holekamp's film course on communism in Eastern Europe was an excellent course. The grading is heavily skewed towards participation, so make sure that you enjoy attending class if you are going to take it. Also, the class mostly consists of lectures, but I found them to be informative and helpful. Convenient office hours and custom appointments.

Professor Moncayo was so kind, but very disorganized and did not give much feedback. He is super understanding of circumstances if you talk to him about them, and this should be an easy A if you show up and do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy MHS elective. He works for the TN Dept of Health so he has amazing connections if you're interested in that field + tons of guest speakers are brought in. Class got pretty boring sometimes tbh but tests were easy and online. One major 12-15 pg paper due a couple weeks before finals but he grades super lightly. Very nice, cool guy!

Got off to a slow start but once we got past the first book, things really took off. Fantastic guest lecturers, especially if interested in public health or infectious disease. A lot of the class is more general social science ("Why does xenophobia exist?") Expectations were vague, but open note exams straight from book and overall a solid class.

He's disorganized like others say (late to class often), but it's because he's working for the Department of Health simultaneously... fair trade-off for an experienced prof imo. He responded to all of my emails. Lots of guest lectures that were mostly fantastic. A lot of vague discussion (e.g. "why does race matter"). Still recommend

A caring person but not that great of a prof. Very little feedback... still not sure how I did on quizzes/paper as he often delayed returning the grades. Also he liked to respond to questions w/ generality. Content wise, not very pub health oriented but a lot of general social science knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Very disorganized professor and does not respond to emails. While the content was interesting, it was unclear what would be on the exam, and we only had a few grades. The exams and quizzes were relatively simple if you did the reading and prepared for them. Easy class but prepare for a lack of guidance.

Dr. Moncayo is such a nice guy. He wants everyone to be successful in his class and even tries to offer career help to anyone who wants it. Not a lot of teaching in this class and a ton of guest speakers. Midterm is very reasonable and projects are insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor, really nice and definitely cares about the class. Exam was reasonable, but the quizzes are too hard/too specific. Overall an interesting class and a great professor.
Dr. Moncayo was one of the most awesome professors I've ever had, regardless of department. He's such a caring man, and he genuinely wants everyone in the room to do well.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Timing sucks but its worth it. Lots of guest speakers. Read 4 books throughout the year and those are the tests. One group presentation (easy grade). 10pg final paper on any topic you want. Nicest guy ever. Changed our due date when we needed more time. Highly recommend him as a professor! Felt like I learned a lot.
This course is overall well-taught. Beware of pop-up quizzes and make sure you spend time studying various logics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dubey is a good guy. He teaches well and the assignments aren't too hard. I learned a lot in his class. Grading is very slow and the assignments are poorly explained (setting up AWS stuff). Other than that, you will learn what you need to learn about databases. Grading is pretty generous and he is nice about it.

Grading is very ambiguous and they take forever to grade. Dubey does not run this class. The TA Pravesh runs this class and does all the grunt work while Dubey just lectures about useless stuff. The setup and the homework are pretty poorly explained and the example code barely relates to it.

Dubey is one of the best CS professors at Vandy. Definitely take this class over databases. Even though it is more work, it is much more useful and rewarding. He teaches you everything you need to know about so many technologies and grades very fairly. He's nice and actually cares about teaching this stuff.

Dubey's lectures are bland but the assignments are very interesting. We work with several different tools over the semester, such as Pandas, SQL, MongoDB, so you get a breadth of knowledge in the class. There are occasional pop quizzes, but are very easy. There's a group project at the end of the semester as well. Very nice Professor.

Information management systems is one of the most popular fields in Computer Science and Dr. Dubey makes sure we are on top of that. With readings that cover large-scale architecture design and homeworks that give us hands-on experience, Dr. Dubey prepares us for applying what we learn to the real world. The grading is also super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dubey is a very solid professor. Assignments and homework are clearly explained and fair, and the he is very in tune to the needs of his students. He is very good at connecting content to the real world, and introduced some very cool guest lecturers from the industry. I feel well prepared for doing this work in the real world!

Great lecturer who cares about both you learning the material and your grade. None of the assignments are hard if you pay attention in class, he also gives you examples related to the assignments. The quizzes are all straightforward material covered in class. Really nice professor too! Gave 2 makeup quizzes and a makeup assignment.
One of the best math professors at Vandy. I really recommend him

Not only is Dr. Abbrescia amazing at Math, but he is also an amazing teacher. He always tries to cater his lessons and class structure to what's best for the students. He is great at communicating the information in a way that makes sense. Easily the best teacher in the department. He's young so he connects better with students than older teachers.
GOAT, best professor I've taken at Vanderbilt by far.

If you can, take a class with Abbrescia. The material is difficult, but he explains it well and has very fair grading policies. If you work hard, you are likely to do well. Prioritizes students learning material and understanding it over timed tests and weeding students out. Also just an overall nice man who is reasonable yet challenges your skills

SUCH a nice, understanding, caring professor!! Actually cares so much about his students and their understanding, and emphasizes take home midterms to ensure that we have the time to think really deeply about important problems in diff eq. I had such a great experience in diff eq!

I don't think Abbrescia teaches this course anymore but I would recommend him for anything he teaches. Super friendly and caring, loves what he's teaching about, and wants students to really get the material. The class wasn't easy because the concepts are still super difficult, but he heavily encourages talking over material after class or at OH

Dr. Abbas is one of my favorite professors. He cares about us understanding, knowing, and enjoying the material, and it shows in the way he lectures. He guarantees that if you learn the material you will do well in class. Always takes time to make sure there aren't questions, and made me feel comfortable in class asking questions.

Professor Abbas is awesome. Teaches well, pays attention to students, gives a couple minutes of breaks in lectures and is really passionate about stuff which shows. He's also really fun in general and it's a good time overall.
Lectures are very clear and easy to understand. Examples on the slides and practice exams are very helpful for the exams. The instructor is thoughtful and easily accessible outside of class.

Professor Waseem was amazing to learn under--by far one of the most responsive/caring professors I've had the pleasure of taking. He makes discrete math, a typically daunting subject, very easy and approachable with his thought out lesson plans and clear explanations. Gave around 6% extra credit on each test putting averages into the B+ range.

TAKE DR. ABBAS!!! Best professor I've ever had here at Vandy. I don't care what the course is, but if this gem of a human being is teaching it, you can be damn sure that I'm enrolling in that class. Super clear lecturer-- and even if you miss out on a few classes, his amazing slides and practice exams will help elucidate tough discrete concepts.

I was shocked when Dr. Abbas told us that he's a research professor and that teaching isn't his "main job," because his lectures are so engaging and effectively communicated. Dr. Abbas taught me the most of any professor this semester, and he's inspired me to check out the more theoretical side of CS, something I never thought would interest me.

concepts are not too challenging, but you need to put in the work (ZyBooks & lectures). Even though the HW's are 5-6 questions, start early & use office hours as resources. Dr. Abbas is one of the most caring professors I've had at Vanderbilt- he goes out of his way to make himself available for help & really wants students to understand the course

Prof. Abbas has truly been one of my favorite CS professors yet. He communicates relatively abstract material in very accessible ways, aided by consistently impeccable slides (that he takes pride in!). He responds promptly to email, takes breaks during class to ensure students are tracking, and genuinely cares about his students. Take his class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 4 homework sets, 3 midterms, 1 final, zybooks. I really like Professor Abbas, he doesn't take himself too seriously and cares about his students a lot. I've found him to be one of the most accommodating professors I've had. The material can be a little confusing but the workload is fairly low. Can't go wrong taking 2212 with Abbas.
Professor Abbas is an awesome professor. Super nice and really cares about his students. Hard class in general but he does his best to explain everything in depth. One of the best CS2212 professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Abbas is a good professor who really cares about student learning. He takes the time to explain concepts so students thoroughly understand them. Just be aware that the material is, by nature, much to absorb over the course of a semester. Attending his office hours with homework is useful, and do practice quizzes to ace the actual quizzes.

This beautiful man really cares about each an every one of his students. He is super passionate about teaching, and isnt afraid of spending extra time to help you better understand a topic. He really encourages asking questions and working with classmates to better understand topics in class. We love Waseem Boii
He really cares about his students! He makes all his lecture slides super comprehensible. He also makes practice quizzes that are super helpful.

Professor Abbas really cares about his students and want them to learn. He's really passionate about teaching and the material and I wish there were more professors like him. He constantly asks for ways to improve the class environment and ways to help students learn. He's one of the best the Vandy CS department has to offer.
He is very passionate about teaching

Professor Abbas really cares about his students and that they get the concept. He's inspirational and wants us to really learn and gives different real life examples to the problems in class. He's accessible almost everytime we need him (in person or through email) and spends lots of time making his slides to make sure they're crystal clear. A gem!

Professor Waseem was brand new to teaching here when I took his class. He cares a lot about students understanding the material and is not afraid to fall behind the other sections if it's necessary. From what I have heard from friends, he is the best choice for 2212. Lectures can be a little bland and stray off topic, but it is worth it.

While he genuinely seems to care about his students, he doesn't do a good job of teaching.
