He never finishes his lecture slides and spends too much time focusing on things that aren't super important. I spent the entire semester teaching myself the material. this wasn't too bad and I just did the practice quizzes before the real thing and was fine
He is an excellent professor. He walks into the classroom every class prepared to teach his students useful stuff. He is always willing to help his students with any questions!
wonderful professor! definitely take his class!!

He does not really seem to care about teaching too much and does not make his own materials so he seems confused sometimes in class and has to figure out what is going on himself. But the quizzes are not difficult as long as you do the practice and homework is a helpful grade booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Abbot makes bio fun and interesting. Everything on the tests is from the lectures and the lectures are 10/10. No textbook use. He talks about current scientific research every class which keeps it interesting. Very helpful and encouraging office hours. Best professor I've had yet at Vanderbilt. Couldn't recommend him more.

Evolution of Behavior with Abbot was my favorite class I've taken at vandy. Abbot really knows his stuff and wants his students to care about it as much as he does. A great person to get to know outside class too! Exams in this class were very fair and could be easily passed if you just show up to class.

Really experienced teacher, very passionate about science and shares exciting cutting-edge science at the beginning of every class. Lectures are fairly entertaining. Cares about students and wants to help them learn. Exams can be a little confusing at times, but you can ask him for clarification. Overall solid choice for bio. Would give him a 4.5/5

Dr. Abbot is the best professor I've had in the biology department. He starts every lecture with something interesting that's happening in science. He inspires students to be interested in the subject. He explains everything incredibly clearly and makes sure everyone understands. His office hours are amazing.

Excellent professor lecture wise- inspiring, clear, and engaging. However, his tests were less than clear with a lot of errors relative to his teaching, but that could be due to the questions being written by the biology department as a whole rather than abbot himself. All in all the best choice for gen bio if you have to take the class.

Abbot is a really engaging professor. He was my favorite out of all of the bio professors. You can tell how much he cares about his students (he knows names in a lecture of 200 people) and wants them to be interested in the subject. The lectures are pretty clear and the tests are easier than the other half of the semester.

He was the best bio professor I've ever had. Awesome guy who clearly cares about his work and his students. He knew people's names in lecture and made a lot of jokes to keep us interested. His tests were easier than Hillyer's, but still not a walk in the park; that's just the nature of the subject. I wish I could take him again. Take his class!

Abbot is a great man and a great professor. He is very kind and helpful whenever asked for help. My only complaint would be his poor test writing skills. Some of his questions would test easy concepts but the wording was so vaguedifficult to decipher. Read slides before class, Take really good notes, and Memorize everything on his lecture slides.

Great lecturer, but very poor test writer.  If the questions and answer choices weren't vague, they focused on minutiae instead of testing our understanding. One exam asked to recreate a lecture slide as a short answer question, word for word. He was the reason why I didn't get an A in this class.

Professor Abbot is the best bio professor at Vanderbilt. He makes the class interesting and uses real life examples to make it more than just memorization of facts. Incredibly interesting to talk to outside of class as well. You will learn a ton and I cannot recommend his class highly enough.
Awesome prof. I was terrible at the class, as I did not take the prereq. Even so, I enjoyed myself! And he is SO good looking, he has great forearms. Take this class!

Abbot is an INCREDIBLY nice guy. He knew some people's names in a class of 150+, and really made an effort to pass on some life lessons through all of the biology. That being said, he was a terrible test question writer; I felt like many of his questions were worded fairly poorly. He also tests a lot harder than he teaches, as some already noted.

I don't know why everyone is complaining about his tests; they were the easiest of the whole sequence. I got my only 100 so far on a college biology exam during his half of the class. He's an awesome teacher and it's very easy to do well the class (especially if you've made it that far already).

amazing, amazing professor. I have really no strong interest in bio but he made the material really interesting. very helpful in his office hours as well. the test average for his sections was around a B. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND HIM!

I had him for BIO 110B and 238 . He was also my EEOB advisor. He was my absolute favorite teacher at Vanderbilt. He is extremely helpful and actually cares about you as a person (not just your grade in the class). Yes his tests can be tricky, but he gets you to actually apply your knowledge which is great.  Awesome guy :)
Abbot didnt teach much new that any good high school bio class wouldnt have covered already, but his tests had a way of being tricky. Covers the big picture then tests on details

Of all four biology lecturers I had, he was by far the worst. Nice guy, but tests a lot harder than he teaches. Teaching = rehashing basic concepts and philosophizing on the scientific world, meaning of life etc. Testing = memorized definitions, unnecessarily difficult genetic problems. Makes for pressure-cooker exams in the wake of poor instructio

Dr. Abbot is a miserable teacher. His subject matter is REALLY VERY SIMPLE but he decides to over-complicate the questions on his tests for no reason, other than to confuse and fail people that really have a good understanding of the subject matter. Dr. Page teaches the first section, and he's fantastic. Dr. Abbot isn't worth it. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Dynamic lecturer. Helpful to attend lecture- missing words on slides. Gives a very comprehensive overview of more challenging concepts and willing to put in time for office hours and (Friday?) review sessions. Approachable, remembers faces if you make an effort to see him- good option to keep in mind for letter of rec.

His lectures are helpful to attend and he is slightly easier than the other biology professors. With that said, this is a challenging class regardless of who teaches it. I recommend taking biology with him.

He's a horribe professor whose more interested in the greatness of Mendel than the actual work. He make his lectures fun and easy but his tests are completely different and he DOES NOT properly prepare the class for them. His preparation for  them was just utterly ridiculous.

he's a weird dude, but he's a good teacher.  focus on the slides in class (ppt format) and read the text.  if this is 110B, then you should be used to the workload. knowledgeable and sometimes can be pretty funny so just go to class.

I thought he was a great teacher. He'd put people on the spot with thought provoking questions making sure you really understood the material. He was really fun. Good note taking is an essential for his class because a lot of what he tests is based on the lecture rather then the powerpoint.
BEST TEACHER EVER HE IS DA****
did not like his teaching methods; did not effectively prepare us for what he tested us on

AWESOME TEACHER. He has made class a lot more intesting than the last 3 bio professors . His tests are easy and entirely off of his powerpoint presentations, which are online.  You don't need to go to class, because you have the online ppts. Reading the book isn't necessary either. I got a 100 on the first test and studied less than I did in 110A.
I had him for an undergrad seminar.  He's awesome and enthusiastic.. great teacher!
so awesome.
great
Very helpful and totally a tree hugger and family man.  Glad to hear he was good for Ecology!
This is a really fun class for bio majors.  It beats biochem any day!  If you like the environment, or want to know more about it, take ecology!

Abbot is a great guy and a spunky teacher.  His class can be boring though, and his tests don't exactly cover the big picture.  He likes to nit-pick and select small details from the lecture to put on the exam.  Overall, good class - I would recommend it to any bio major or environmental junkie.

Monsieur Abell is a great professor who really cares about his students and about the subject. He makes class fun and the workload is pretty light. There is weekly online homework and written assignments every few weeks, and the tests are all take-home. If you put in effort it is pretty easy to do well in his class.

Really enjoys the subject he teaches. Class (intermediate-level French) was taught entirely in French, and students were expected to respond in French as much as possible. Prof. Abell and the course material learned both help boost my confidence in speaking/listening in French. Students also got to watch 4 movies over the course of the semester.
Really fun guy, makes you want to participate in class. Lots of participation is required. Uses Pearson MyFrenchLab. Great introduction to french.

Guaranteed A! If you submit the assignment you'll get 100%. Loves to talk and will go on random tangents when teaching or explaining assignments but it gave me time to do my online shopping. She also includes some group work now and then to switch it up from the lonely writing but nothing an introvert can't survive.

Professor Ackerman is wonderful and so kind! She gives great feedback on assignments and is not a harsh grader at all. I greatly improved my writing skills and loved that she gave plenty of time to get assignments done in class! As long as you get your assignments done on time and show up to class you are pretty much guaranteed an A.

Prof. Ackerman is great! Her class is super easy and a guaranteed A as long as you complete the assignments. Very easy going and not harsh with feedback at all. Readings are very often but are usually short. Quite a bit of (easy) group/partner work in class and about 4 papers. Takes off points for tardiness and attendance is mandatory. Great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Lieberman is extremely smart and clearly passionate about his field of study. But, unfortunately it doesn't translate 100% into his teaching skills. His lectures were heavy and it's easy to lose track of his point within the first 30 seconds of him speaking. His grading is fair but there are only a few assignments during the semester.

Took his JS1002W class synchronously. He doesn't really care if you have your camera and mic off. Graded off of 2 papers, a midterm, and a final paper. If you payed attention to midterm prep and wrote well, he would give you a good grade. Lectures were long, but he clearly tries to engage you with material and is passionate about his field.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took a writing seminar with Lieberman, and he's a really nice guy who's incredibly knowledgeable about his field. Lectures can be kind of scattered/disorganized, but it's really only because he's super passionate. Kind of unclear at first on how grading would work, but he's very helpful outside of class, and gives great feedback on assignments.

Prof Lieberman is kinda like the quintessential kooky academic, but to be honest it only adds to the course. He is a super entertaining, animated lecturer, which really makes a difference at 9 am. The reading was challenging, but as long as you have it done, there is enough analysis and talking in class to make it a bit clearer.

Nice guy, cares about students, always willing to meet. However, seems so busy and scatterbrained that it really hurts the class. Sessions are typically boring rambling monologues showing little prep. Feedback is sparse and grades seem to be largely arbitrarily assigned. Often forgot about previous conversations, email exchanges, and arrangements.

I took an introductory writing seminar and the class was really cool, but also pretty tough.  Professor Lieberman is really interesting so class is engaging.  There aren't too many assignments (2 midterms that aren't bad) but a couple research papers that were graded tough.  He tells you exactly what he wants on everything.

Class was engaging half the time, off on odd tangents the other half. Good group feel as a seminar. One paper for the entire semester broken into four parts. Expectations were extremely vague. Indicated that grades were not an issue to worry about in the class, leaving at least several of us unpleasantly surprised with the final grade we received.

Literally the worst teacher that I have ever had. Her accent is completely horrible, and does the math in a way that managed to confuse a class of kids who have all learned the exact same material before in high school

Her tests were extremely straight forward and fair. The final was difficult but nothing impossible. If you actually pay attention and get your hands on a solution manual, this class is easily manageable. It should be noted she kind of calls you dumb if you ask a "dumb" question...

Very unhelpful teacher.  Lectures are fast and unclear, yet any questions you have will get an annoyed response with no help.  That said, the tests are fair and representative of the homework.  Read the textbook often in this class.
Decent teacher but moves quick in her lectures so it's pretty much necessary to read the textbook constantly.  Her tests are very fair and don't do anything to trick you.

Not spectacular, but not terrible either. I got an A just from reading the book and the internet. Tests are extremely easy though compared to the other professors for MATH 175. Read the book thoroughly and do all the homework/practice problems in the book. Homework is also a free 100 points if you have the solution manual.

Horrible class and professor. She covers all of the material, but her accent and her general method of teaching leaves one confused after class. Homework counts for 100/550 points. 3 Tests 100 points, 150 point final. Tests were very inconsistent in difficulty.. final was impossible. AVOID IF POSSIBLE!!

Major essays are pretty easy once you know what's expected. Thankfully, you can drop the one with the lowest grade if you opt to write an optional one towards the end of the semester. Seminars are overall good, but can sometimes turn into rambles.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You are not the exception to the rule. I got that A by the grace of God and her nonsense grading scale. Trust me stay away from her at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you need any kind of structure, this is not the class for you. Classes mostly consisted of the professor going on long tangents with no direction and very little learning. Instructions for every assignment are vague at best, and, on top of that, Ackerly is an unnecessarily harsh grader. Plus, a 4000 word final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: 4000 word research paper for final exam, wasnt in syllabus. Is extremely hard grader. Lectures are her just talking abt whatever tangent she feels like going on that day. STAY AWAY IF YOU WANT TO SAVE YA GPA AND GO TO LAW SCHOOL.

Ackerly is so intelligent and passionate about what she teaches. Her classes are insightful and it's usually half lecture half class discussion. It's a lot of reading with writing for each class, but it's the type of class where it's worth it. Midterm and a final paper with pretty unclear instructions but just show up at her office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Ackerly is super caring and you learn very applicable and relevant ideas. This course had weekly readings with a reading sheet due every Sunday, 2 400-word papers that used all the readings then a 3000 word final paper with broad guidelines and no specifics. There is never a prompt and you never know any grades, but good content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Ackerly was my most challenging class, but its rewarding. It's not like most political science courses because it focuses on political theory. There are some really challenging readings, and she expects a lot, but if you come to class and ask questions, you'll be able to succeed. I learned a lot, and she's impressive. Loves tangents tho

I've now completed every assignment and have absolutely no idea what grade I will get. Grading is as mysterious and random feeling as the assignments themselves. Learning comes from readings, which all seem to pretty much make the same overly complex points, but not from the lectures. Ackerly is clearly smart but rambles with no direction in class

Professor Ackerly is nice enough and the class isn't super difficult, but she gets easily irritated when people ask for clarification on the structure of the class or assignments. Very confusing and vague grading criteria and assignment instructions-got through it but everyone was confused most of the time. It's fine but wouldn't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The opposite of clear grading criteria or clear anything really. You have no idea what you're supposed to be doing or whats going on. Meanwhile she has tremendous expectations & is a ridiculously harsh grader for someone who gives awful guidelines and barely specifies what you're even supposed to be doing and ignores/fails to answer any questions
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Ackerly is one of the smartest people you'll ever meet. She's demanding yet accommodating. Gives heavy readings, but lets you choose the topic for your essay. She is not very specific on requirements for essays. But if you put in the work you do well. Great prof who cares about your learning.
Very knowledgeable in her subject area & it shows!! No complaints here :) Loved her

I had Climate Change with her this past semester. Although the class is challenging, she teaches you a lot. Ironically, this is the class where everyone became friends with each other over the struggle of it. I'll definitely take another class with her MAKE SURE YOU DO THE READINGS AND TAKE NOTES
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Ackerly is both approachable and knowledgeable. The implication is that you are best served by asking her questions (there will be plenty of time for this in class) to confirm and clarify any misunderstandings you have. Once you adapt to the challenging writing standards, you'll find that you've learned a lot and gained a good connection.

Ackerly is very kind and accessible outside the classroom, but nothing she says in her office or in the lecture hall is particularly clear. Her lectures are rambling, her readings are intense, and her feedback is strange  which is not helpful considering that she's a pretty rough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great lecturer but topics can be boring. Very nice and will give you extra attempts at papers. 3 400 word papers, 1 final project and attendance/participation.

If you want to have very little idea where the class is going and not feel like you're learning anything, take her class. She goes on a lot of tangents which can be interesting but overall this class was exhausting and unhelpful.

Ackerly is great but tough! As much as class and actually doing the readins is necessary GO to office hours. Office hours really spell out exactly what she wants, helps her understand where you and the rest of the class are in understanding the concepts, and help you with everything else. She's also pretty liberal and a leader in feminist theory :D

One of the best professors I had my freshman year. She challenges you constantly to look at things from a different perspective and participate in class. The more you put in this class the more you get out of it.

The class is very intellectually engaging. There is a very small graded workload in this course. There are daily readings however that can be time consuming and are very useful to understanding the material as the class time is generally spent discussing the concepts, with very little lecturing from the professor herself.

I went into the class thinking that I would be learning about the Justice system. However, all we did was read political theory. Professor Ackerly is nice, but her lectures didn't much help my understanding. Get a good TA! They grade 85% of your final grade (40% essays, 40% final, 5% paragraph). My TA was awesome. Misleading name, good class.

This class is not what you expect it to be. The class description is extremely misleading. There are no modern applications of justice, rather intense readings on political theory and lectures that lack clarity. The only positive aspect is if the TA grades your paper, but the class lacks structure. Do yourself a favor and don't take the class.

A great class if you chose to appreciate what it can be. Certainly encourages a higher level of thinking, but highly rewarding. Ackerly will not hold your hand, but you will be better off because of it. A positive attitude will go far.

Class requires a LOT of reading and the grading system is hard to follow.  However, Professor Ackerly is a very engaging and interesting professor who is very helpful both in and out of class.  If you put in the time, you can do well.

This class is tough and very demanding. I had a 4.0 at VU and this will be my first B. Professor Ackerly is extremely unclear and its difficult to follow her lectures. She is a very nice and brilliant woman...however this does not translate to a good professor. Lots of reading and class discussions.

Professor Ackerly is a fantastic teacher, she is extremely engaged with her students and is very willing to help you.  Her own work is very interesting and her ability to encourage you to look beyond the dominant worldview is invaluable.  The class is definitely based on reading, but all of the articles we read were extremely interesting!

Don't worry you aren't doing as bad in this class as you think you are. Still Professor Ackerly is very frustrating and talks SO much without really saying anything. There's no way of tracing your grade and really no way of knowing what she wants. The material is intersting but presented in a very difficult way.
A bit out there and abstract- no deadlines in the class, but ok if you like theory.

Great and talented professor...is willing to do whatever is necessary to help you, she just wants to know that you want to learn as much as she wants to teach. Take the class and learn something about politics!
this chick is crazy, possibly taking somethingmost boring course i have ever taken. every discussion, test, assignment is reading based so keeping up is a MUST.
No Comments

I absolutely loved this professor because she revolutionized the way I think about politics.  She is challenging, but that aspect of her technique is what has helped me to become a better student and more talented writer.  Awesome.

She is quite obviously left-leaning, but I don't think it effects the grading too much.  Lots of reading, but you can get by without doing it.  Doesn't take attendance.  Uses socratic method a lot, so if you aren't prepared to talk or bs, beware.  Grading seems a bit arbitrary but I still ended up with a B+ somehow

Is that last person on ****ing crack. Ackerly is one of the worst professors at Vandy. She needs to fired ASAP. She is incredibly condescending in class. Way too liberal and she makes sure you know that. I was interested in the class topics before I came in, but now just want to kill myself because of her. Please fire her!!!
best professor i have at vandy-- provides a thorough syllabus and grants "amnesty" when you are struggling-- really wants to engage in the text with you-- a must-take here
Very unclear. Not sure if I learned anything from that class. Repetitive and boring

I can't complain too much about Prof. Ackerly because I did the minimal amount of work and still got a B+. There is A LOT of reading, but the good thing about the class is that you discuss the reading thoroughly and therefore you don't have to read the entire assignment to understand the reading. She was a fairly easy grader on the journals/paper.
Great professor. I agree with the other comment: don't let "liberal" deter you. She really makes you think. Every student should take her.

She expects a lot, but if you keep up reading and journals, go to class, and participate in the discussion you will learn a lot. Yes, she is "liberal," but that really shouldn't deter you from taking a class from her. I am very conservative and I loved this class; I plan on taking more classes from her whenever I have the chance.
No Comments

Past ratings stressing her "femi-nazi" attitude are somewhat without merit. The class was very easy overall - there was a minor amount of reading and only 1 essay the entire semester. All she asks is a minor understanding of political philosophy. She is definitely liberal and unjustly values feminist thought, but overall a good teacher.

I'm a girl, but I'm still griping about her being a feminist nazi.  She is very unhelpful, rude, and critical.  Her class has loads of reading that often seems irrelevant and her lectures are as discumbobulated as the class.
No Comments

Horrible class and horrible professor. she is super liberal and used ever chance in class to make sure we knew she was a huge feminist. She is super condescending and just a bad teacher. Dont take a class with her at all
She is horrible and so is her class. I wanted to kill myself. No wonder no one except a few liberal loser GDI suck ups go to class. She hates men, conservatives, protestants, etc. She should be fired
She sucks. She is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. She is a femi-Nazi
Already boring subject matter is made more boring by her instruction.  There's a reason at this point in the semester that the class is averaging 50% attendance or worse.
Shes challenging but different than a lot of other professors, is every intelligent, and you can learn a lot from her if you put minimal work into the class.
I want to kill myself right now
not very clear in instruction

She is a challenging individual, but some simple-minded individuals may find her too judgmental. It is likely that they refused to open their minds and therefore had a bad class experience. If you're willing to be  engaged and thoughtful, you can succeed in her class. A generally enlightening prof.
No Comments

One of the most left wing profs I've seen. She even allows it to reflect her grading.  Completely insecure in her academic clout. Teaches Rawls as if Nozick never existed. Lucky for her most Vandy kids don't know he existed so the indoctrination continues. Only plus=hot short skirts and great legs
however said she was hot was completely riddiculous.

she doesnt care too much for the white protstant males in the class, she seems to think that we're all chauvinists that are responsible for the opression of women and minorities... but at least she's hot.
while political philosophy sucks, she at least tries hard to convey the main points. the work she expects you to put forth is pretty significant, but her grading is fair.
She IS condescending and unclear.  She offers little help to male students.  However she is HOT!
Do NOT take this class. She is a very intelligent woman but does NOT know how to teach worth her life!! She is not helpful, is condescending, and is incomprehensible.

Awesome and super caring professor, and she offers opportunities for extra credit. Nonetheless, tests are overly hard and worded in an extremely confusing way. If you miss class, you can't make up for in-class homework, which is a big part of your grade.

Dr. Seiffert is incredibly knowledge about the material and is a kind and effective lecturer. She truly cares about every one of her students. That being said, the grading scale is very test-based and it's kinda difficulty to get a straight A - I barely got an A-. Just show up, listen in lecture, study the study sheets, and do the research early!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Seiffert is really kind and into the material she's teaching. I don't know what some of the other reviews are talking about because all I did was read over the slides the night before tests (ignore the study guides) and I literally aced every test. Incredibly easy class and super interesting. I highly recommend it. Don't buy the textbook though
Honestly, she's a great professor, TRIES to be nice and does care, but is too hard for intro to pysch, does not curve enough and is way too fast and too much content.

She's honestly an angel, her lectures are just packed! Do digital notes, causing writing is not realistic. Get started with your research requirements at the START of the semester, don't make the same mistake I did and do them last second! She has a lot of opportunities for extra credit and is really nice. She has a textbook, but I never read.

GREAT PROFESSOR! She is clear about how to get all points and extra credit in her class, and it is very easy. Research requirement is free points if you keep up with it, and you can get 3 extra points added to your overall grade. Exams are taken directly from her slides, so if you study those, you will do amazing every time. Highly recommend.

She is a very kind person, but her lectures move so quickly that there is barely any time to write down what's on the slide, let alone anything she is saying. Her class is out of 100 total points. On each midterm, every question is worth 0.5 points. So if you get two questions wrong on an exam, your grade already drops 1%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chill and nice professor. Good lecturer and posts slides + classwork. Need to show up to class and do the reading sessions or research studies. Enthusiastic about psych which is neat. Tests are very similar to classwork and the study guide. Don't write everything down in lecture; focus on understanding the core concepts and you'll be good.

Very very nice professor, but the tests are mostly multiple choice and kind of hard. I enjoy the class, and attendance is mandatory to get points for classwork, but the tests are harder than they should be.

Professor Seiffert is a great lecturer and has a lot of knowledge about psychology. Her lectures are pretty fast-paced but she does take student feedback into consideration. Class is test-heavy but she gives study guides with concepts that are needed for the exams, and even offers review sessions. Overall I would recommend her class.
Hella lit and nice

My absolute favorite professor this semester!! She makes her lectures engaging by adding modern examples to all vocab and offers lots of extra credit. When grades are lower then expected, she gives surveys to the students on what she can do better and what the students need. She goes through lectures fast, but she posts all of them online after.

Although you could probably get an A by cramming for each exam the night before (she gives study sheets w/ all terms), Dr. Seiffert's fast lecture style and tedious MCQ exam questions were still pretty frustrating. However, this class provides a solid knowledge base that has served me well in other neuroscience/psych courses and MCAT prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't know where the other reviews are coming from on grading. Tests were quite easy if you just memorized the study sheet terms (I didn't even take notes) and Dr. Seiffert offered ~5% extra credit on the final grade for minimum extra work. The class itself was typical for psych, and it seemed better for learning MCAT knowledge than other sections.

This professor was the worst professor I've had at Vandy. The way she grades is horrendous. Everything she taught the class went in one ear and out the other. I would suggest taking legitimately any other professor for any other class before her again. She was horrible. Her tests were horrible. It was almost as if she was out to get her students.
Maybe stick to teaching quantitative methods 💜 this class was so random and difficult in its own way for no reason, hope no one has to endure her confusing self
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is fine, just be aware that the exams are a little random. It's honestly nothing crazy as long as you attend lectures and do the participation work, but it does require a little effort to at least keep on track with the material.

honestly pretty easy class ( i had some background going into it tho) but extra credit was offered when she saw students struggling and used mid semester feedback to ensure we understand content. grade is based on exams and class work and research requirement. it was her first time teaching the class but i enjoyed it tbh

Ok i like prof seiffert as a person, she's super nice and obvious very knowledgeable but taking her gen psych class was incredibly irritating. I've taken multiple psych classes at vbilt and took ap psych but her exams are so random and difficult. The study guides are given like days before the exam and are way too many words to actually study

I LOVE Dr. Seiffert! She is kind, organized, humorous during lectures. Her feedback on assignments is also thorough and personalized, shows how much she cares. Graded by weekly group work, 2 large homework assignments, 3 exams, and one final 3-page paper. The class is super doable and enjoyable and gave a lot of interesting insight about IO Psych.

Dr. Seiffert is a great professor. Very knowledgeable and cares that her students know the information. She is very clear on what is expected of students and what will be tested. She also answers any questions that you have about projects and such. It's not too hard to get an A if you pay attention.

Dr. Seiffert is a great lecturer and very organized. She briefly reviews old material at the start of EVERY lecture, and truly cares for each and every student, making sure to pass by Everyone to see if we need help on classwork. The cutoff for an A is high (180/190 points), but the class is fair. I'd certainly recommend her for your stats prof!

Professor Seiffert is one of the most caring professors at Vandy. The class was difficult, but she was always very accessible and made sure that no one felt completely lost. Very personable. I was also going through a really tough time and had to make-up some exams and she was very understanding about the whole thing. Would definitely recommend.

It's really clear she cares. Overheard her telling a touching anecdote about why she never wants to let anyone fail her stats course. Getting an A in this class can be tough, but it's doable if you meet with her outside of class when necessary. My only complaint is that she lectures too fast and doesn't upload slides before class for reference.

Stats is never going to be an interesting class, but Prof Seiffert did her best. She's a VERY fast responser and is very accessible. Her grading system is a bit tough (can only miss 10 points to get an A), but she's great with partial credit. There's weekly HW, group/indiviudal projects, and exams but it's all manageable. 0 complaints about her.
Generally is a rlly nice person and she is understanding, but the lectures go way too fast and you are expected to do a lot of reading and learning by yourself outside of the classroom.

There were a ton of assignments that didn't feel like the best use of time, but they did help to fill grades. The grading criteria was quite difficult - a point system where an A was 95%, making it pretty difficult to get an A with only a few extra credit opportunities. The final paper was graded easily, which helped. Exams cover a lot of material.

I went into the course hearing a lot of things negative things about Prof Seiffert. She was actually pretty funny at times, and when I missed an exam, she heard me out and let me make up for it. You do have to actually try and study for the exams, but she does give you a review sheet which helps a lot. Take it and work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took both quantitative methods with Seiffert in the fall and experimental design with her in the spring. I enjoyed both immensely and learned tons of useful information. Dr. Seiffert helps you navigate the vast statistical landscape and teaches what is necessary for understanding/conducting psych research. Uses creative metaphors for hard topics.
Entirely average.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course isn't terrible and you will likely learn a lot but the formatting of the course seems a bit off. There is a large amount of information that is covered in the course so there isn't much time spent breaking down and  each individual concept. Seiffert isn't unhelpful but it is really up to you to learn the concepts on your own.

I honestly really loved Dr. Seiffert and thought she was a great lecturer. She listens to her students and really takes into consideration their feedback each semester. I 100% recommend her. Also, when I took the class, there were 2 TAs and 3 LAs, so there was a ton of available help if you needed it.

I really enjoyed learning from Professor Seiffert. Princ of Exp. Design is definitely not an interesting subject, but Professor Seiffert was super engaging and approachable. Her grading criteria and feedback were super clear. She also gives a lot of assignments but they are not too hard so if you mess up on one, you will still be okay
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Seiffert is a really sweet woman that cares about her students. Her class is fairly interesting and lecture-heavy (which works for this type of information). Overall, an interesting class and a good professor. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You will not go wrong with Dr. Seiffert. Her lectures are very helpful and clear, and she posts the slides online so you can always review them later. There are problem sets that might seem like busy work, but they really help you learn the material. Show up and take good notes, and the tests will be straightforward. Study guides are also given.

Professor Seiffert is very caring and flexible to feedback. While lecture videos are repetitive and boring, an A is very achievable so long as you know the content either from class or the textbook. Exam questions are the same as the example questions but phrased differently. Time for the later exams was a little short, but extra credit helps.

Good news? She's open to feedback. She adapted her course in response to a mid-year survey. Bad news? She expects too much from her students (especially on exams). 3 out of the 4 people in my group couldn't finish the second exam on time. If you're someone who takes their time on tests (like me), avoid this professor.

Dr. Seiffert was my fav prof for undergrad! Had her for 3 classes and found that she has a clear grading style . You have to put in the work, but you can def get an A in any of them. Also saw a review saying she was demeaning--I have NEVER seen that in office hours or class over the 3 years I've had her. This was actually smth I admired abt her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took her statistics class and she did not seem very knowledgable at all (ex- she thought histograms and bar charts were the same thing). Her online class is extremely stressful. We have daily "assignments" due at the end of class, regardless of your timezone. I suggest you take that 8 am with the better professor if you need to take PSY2100.

Dr. Seiffert is one of the most professional yet approachable professors at this university. She remembers the names of every single student in her class, even if there are 60+ enrolled. She has high expectations and covers a LOT of material in her presentations, but she is thorough and will definitely help outside of class if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr Seiffert is clear and highly efficient with her lectures. I expect she could be a difficult prof for other courses, but I/O Psych is very relatable and the concepts are easy to grasp. You get a lot of points just for talking in class and putting a decent effort into participating. Lecture slides / taking notes prepares you excellently for tests.

She is very clear and concise, and the PPs contain a lot of information. She gives you a good study guide for each exam, and going back through the book for more information helps a lot in understanding. MC can be a little tricky so it's important to really understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've had her for three classes (#psychmajor), and have gotten used to her teaching and testing format. She's very clear and concise in what she wants and I really like that. If you go to her office hours, she's very ready to help. She cares about her students, and every once in a while is low-key hilarious.

This class is really terrible. Dr. Seiffert regularly makes mistakes in her math, rarely gives us opportunities to practice, and gives very unclear expectations for the problem sets. Furthermore, she treats math problems as speed races, and makes students feel stupid if they offer the wrong answer.

She was the worst professor I ever had. No chance for extra credit, extremely tough grader.  She didn't give back a single assignment until two months into the semester so you had no idea how you were doing.  Although I did well, her tests were ridiculously specific and tested the dumbest material. Horrible TAs. Horrible class, DO NOT TAKE

Fantastic Prof. Great Slides. Very clear and concise professors . One of the best. Her TA however, penalised for silliest of things and she was aware and told students he is wrong yet went ahead with his grades thus decreasing cumulative grade. You could make out the assignments graded by him and those by her by the grade that was given.

Professor Seiffert is my favorite professor in the Psych department by far. Her tests and homeworks really encourage a thorough understanding of the material. She is very responsive to student feedback and will slow down the course pace if students struggle; she really wants her students to do well.

Dr. Seiffert is an extremely sweet, caring and helpful teacher that does whatever she can to make things clear for her students. That being said, this course along with her teaching style is rather dry and boring, but she is still a professor that I enjoyed having.
This class was exceedingly dull. Class was boring, and her tests were way too difficult considering how easy the information actually is. She tests you on irrelevant information.

Technically she gets good scores because she does everything that Rate My Professor looks for. However, I have not particularly enjoyed this course. Her lectures are dry and boring, and the other students were reluctant to open their months for the first two months of the course. It's easy though I suppose
This course is a lot of work.

Professor Seiffert was great. When first walking into class I was nervous and expected the worse, and was pleasantly surprised when she displayed her awesome sense of humor to the class. She moves quickly and the lecture can be unclear at times but she is readily available to help and posts all of her materials online.

Dr. Seiffert is a fabulous instructor. She was always clear on what she expected from her students, made herself available to students for help, and very understanding and patient. She took great effort to make some of the oblique concepts in statistics clear and navigable for students who are new to the subject area. I am glad I took her class!

She deserves to be rated much higher on here. For the material she is teaching, she does a fantastic job of being engaging. She's also incredibly funny. Very specific sense of humor. Reasonable grader, little memorization required, if you have any inkling for problem solving or statistics, you'll do well. Even if you don't, study and you'll do well

Professor Seiffert dynamically conveys the underlying structure of modern psychological science in a manner that excites students. Her lectures are clear and interesting, and her style is definitely not boring.   Although getting an A in her course will be difficult, an A- is certainly in reach for anyone who tries. She will teach you much.

Research methods aren't the most interesting thing in the world. Despite this, the way that Seiffert taught the course somehow managed to make it much worse. The power points and readings are clear, and easy to understand. The group project is a time sink, but not bad. The biggest problem is the tests. Extremely unclear, and purposefully tricky.

Class is boring and pointless as she puts all of her slides online, but the class is easy. Weekly problem sets take 1-2 hours,"required" reading is unnecessary. Easy to catch up right before tests, and when you actually do pay attention Seiffert is nice and helpful
The class is interesting, but some of the topics can be dry... All in all the grading is very easy. If you are at all competent at writing, a night before is all you need to get an A.

seiffert clearly cares about the subject, but this class absolutely sucks. not only is it boring but a third of the class is dedicated to a group project. the multiple choice questions on exams are intentionally and unnecessarily tricky, they are also cumulative in addition to having a final exam

Seiffert is horrid, for lack of a better way to put it. She takes an already dull subject matter and manages to make it even worse. Unfortunate for the psychology majors who have to take it. The tests are harshly graded, and the multiple choice questions are practically riddles. If you have to take 208, take it in the spring with Sandberg.

Professor Seiffert is one of the most helpful professors I've had so far at Vanderbilt. She was always very clear in her prompts for papers, and she was always so helpful during consultations. She made it obvious that she really cared about the class and the students. If you work hard, you'll do well in the class. Plus she makes it interesting!

Both textbooks used heavily. A lot of reading. Attendance mandatory on Fri  for group project. HATED the group project that lasts the entire course of the semester. It's hard when evry 1 else has their own agendas. Tests are not too bad. Problem sets vary in difficulty. Started off  hard then got easier as she realized how hard they were for us.

Seiffert wants to help you as much as you want to learn. I would take her class again, but the students who don't engage in the class conversation definitely miss out. If you get in a good group for the group project and pull your weight, you should be set.
She always seems depressed when she is lecturing. Her exams are too long for the allotted time, and she writes ambiguous MC questions. I regret taking this course.

She was horrible. Yeah, she was clear in her lectures, but most of the information was useless. Her review sessions were not helpful at all. Also, a 95 is an A, a 94.9 is an A-. I would avoid at all costs.

2 rather difficult tests (READ THE TEXT!!), 4 long hmwks, a major group project (conducting an experiment - we had to get 100 participants within a week) and a hefty paper (around 20pg). Seiffert is extremely helpful, well-organized; all lecture slides  posted online, very thorough assgnmt guidelines. but most labor-intensive class I've taken here.
Mostly discussion-based class.  She knew a lot about the topic.

Probably one of the hardest teachers in the psychology department.  I would recommend taking the teacher in the other section over her.  Way too much reading and her tests are very hard with ambiguous questions for the multiple choice section.  Be prepared to put a lot of time in with this teacher.  Also a very hard grader.
No Comments

Although Dr. Seiffert was organized, she was a very tough grader. Not that you can't do well, you just have to pay attention to every detail, and be prepared to sit through the same confusing lecture three or four times. The work is very atypical of a college class, and involves a lot of question-asking to understand what she wants.

Professor Seiffert is the most organized professor I've ever had.  It's nice in that it makes the class very organized as well.  You always know what is expected.  She is very helpful outside of class and clear in her lectures.  The class isn't that hard if you pay attention.

This is for CORE1010. Didn't think she was a great professor and the class was so pointless + time consuming. She kept saying she didn't agree with some of the content we had to learn either but still was so serious about it with no mercy. Not a very engaging professor either and everyone was bored to death. Choose someone else for CORE1010.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. McNicholl was a great professor. She seemed interested in what she lectured and could answer questions. While there are a lot of readings for her class, normally you can get away with only reading part of it as long as it's not a reading quiz day lol. The paper topics were a bit vague but overall fine, especially if you ask for clarification.

Low reviews aren't explaining why they feel that way. She's very willing to talk about content and any follow-up questions you might have. You'll learn a lot about Buddhism if you're willing to engage. Participation and attendance do matter, but engage regularly and the assignments themselves aren't difficult to wrap your head around.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Unreasonable grading. Impossible to understand the grading criteria.

McNicholl is a great choice if you're a first sem freshman and really don't want some of the harder professors. Work was definitely high, but class was easy and most of the time, people would rarely participate because they didn't do the reading, and she wouldn't make it a big deal. She knows reading about technical religious vocab is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof is nice and content was more interesting than expected, although lectures can feel long. Easy A if you speak once in a while and turn in assignments on time.

If you hate exams, this is the class for you. But don't let that fool you, because the work assigned was heavy considering this was an introductory class. Grading was very generous but the readings, assignments, and papers were time consuming. Overall, not a bad choice, but this class definitely requires you to put in the work.

You will not regret a class with McNicholl. She is extremely caring, kind, and understanding of all students. She is incredibly knowledgable and genuinely interesting. Her class is organized, concise, and insightful. You'll love her and learn a ton. There is not a better professor.

If you have the slightest bit of interest in Buddhism/Asian Religion, take this class.  Professor McNicholl is one of the best and is extremely knowledgeable in this field, and the lessons on general writing will carry with me far beyond this class. You'll need to work a little bit for an A, but put in the effort and you'll be satisfied.

I have had few professors in my life who are as amazing as professor McNicholl. She is so smart, engaging, and sincerely cares about her students. Her lectures are very interesting, and she is open to student feedback. 13/10 would recommend. Even if you're a just little interested in her class' subject, I promise she will make you love it.

Dr. McNicholl is the best professor that I have had at Vanderbilt. I took her for two semesters (RLST 1111 and 1010), and I could not recommend her more. She is a caring professor, and you will learn a lot more than most other classes. If you have the opportunity, take her class. You will not regret it.

My favorite professor! So considerate and understanding, willing to extend deadlines if youre struggling or behind (no excuse needed either, she knows everythings tough bc of Covid). Also one one of the kindest professors Ive had.

Professor McNicholl is super knowledgeable and gives amazing feedback on writing assignments. She would adjust workload based on students' feedback in the survey. This course really sharpens my critical thinking and refreshed my understanding of religion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Extremely accessible outside of class, really cares about her students. She realised there was a lot of reading at the start and reduced it. Also really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor McNicholl is a great professor. She is very knowledgeable and cares a lot about her students. If you pay attention and do the readings, you will do well in the class.

Easy class, great teacher. No tests, just reflection type papers after each unit that were graded super easily (although this might change due to COVID). Teacher was super nice and very accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's amazing. I had her during COVID so it was online, and she was remarkably flexible throughout the semester. She puts so much work into the material- much more than any other RLST professor I've had. She gives thorough, encouraging feedback on everything. 100% recommend.
She is so funny and incredibly smart. Challenging but overall a great course.

Dr. Adler is great and led good discussions even with a group that was not the most participatory. Fantastic reading list with a solid mix of readings and films. Two graded papers are four pages, and one is 8-10 with a creative option. Great option for a first-year writing seminar. The timing of the final project during the exam period was strange.

Professor Adler is incredibly friendly and approachable. The topic of the course was quite dense, but she accommodated the range of backgrounds in the class very well. You absolutely have to complete the readings to keep up with the pace of the class. Discussion heavy course, but Dr. Adler did a great job at making the conversation feel natural.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite English courses I have taken here! Professor Adler is very engaging and clearly cares about her students and the material in class. I feel like I learned just as much from this class as ones that require double the work. Readings were interesting and relevant and papers were graded graciously w/ good feedback.
She's so nice and understanding. Her class was super fun and she makes lectures awesome. Would definitely take English classes with her.

the only english class i've ever taken that i actually enjoyed and learned from. dr. adler is so kind and knowledgeable, she makes you feel like every point you make is incredibly important. she's really accessible outside of class and absolutely hilarious in lectures. lots of reading, but totally worth it.

I liked this class a lot, and Anderson is a top 3 BME prof. He speaks really slow, but he is passionate about material. Exams are individually not worth that much, so consistent mid performances are acceptable. Go to class (attendance grade), do online reading grades (completion), and do WELL on projects. If you do that, guaranteed good grade.

Prof Anderson is great guy and really knows his stuff. Homeworks and in-class questions are big part of grade and easy to do well on. He let us take the average of our three exams in place of a final exam if we were satisfied with that outcome. Overall great professor, and doesn't place a lot of weight on exams.
At the beginning lecture might be tedious and slow but going on, programing projects are super helpful. Should have given out more quizzes to review concepts.

Dr Anderson's grading is amazing. Lots of things graded for completion and 6 simulation group project which you get in-class time for. Exams were HARD, most of it is multiple choice and some of it from the textbook and not the lectures. Lectures were pretty clear and the slides were good. Anderson is very kind but also disorgnized.

Sys phys is lecture heavy class but Adam explains concepts well and didn't rush through the material. Very little work outside of class and all simulation projects are explained well. Get to work with group on projects/exams, and his exams are very fair. Adam is a super interesting person, hope to take another class from him

great lecturer- explains the material so well and is extremely willing to help and take the time to make sure everyone understands what he's talking about. homework is not too complicated and he helps, tests are mostly fair, you should be fine if you pay attention in class and read notes carefully, but some v old concepts come up which is annoying

Blandin is a good guy and a good teacher. The problem sets are straight forward and there aren't any surprises on the tests. If you go to class and study some for the tests, and A is easily attainable. No reason not to take him.

Bread and butter econ professor. He teaches you everything he tests you on. There are no surprises in this class. He doesnt make lectures too exciting, but how exciting can macro really be? Can't hurt to take the class. Work for the A and you'll get it.

Professor Blandin was easily the best ECON professor I've had at Vanderbilt (had 5 or 6 teachers).  Lectures are pretty monotone but he makes it easy to understand is very willing to answer questions.  Homeworks are very straight forward and exams can be difficult, but if you study you'll do fine.  Seems like most of the bad reviews are old.

Was scared to take this course after seeing the low rating. He is one of the most solid econ professors I have had at Vandy. Very clear and comprehensive in his lectures. Has problem sets that help you understand material, rather than being a burden. Not a RMP guy, but his current rating does not do him justice at all. Would highly recommend.

Blandin is awesome and people are too harsh on him on rate my. His lectures are a bit dry, but they are incredibly clear, which is needed for this course. He is such a nice guy, his problem sets are similar to tests, and he gives a comprehensive study guide. His exams require understanding, but are not bad if you study. Overall, strong professor.

Professor Blandin is a good and solid lecturer. He's very willing to help in office hours and doesn't assign busy work. The content itself can be a bit confusing but so long as you do the problem sets and go over his slides you will be fine. He also pulls in real life examples like Trumps "DOGE" that just make the class more fun.

I don't get why he has low ratings. The content isn't riveting but his lectures are clear and his study guides go over exactly what will be on the exam. His office hours are great and he seems like just a nice person. Definitely by the book, don't turn in a late assignment but he also allows for drops to accommodate that. Great professor

Do not listen to the poor reviews, I am convinced that failure in this class comes from personal stupidity. Blandin has an extremely carefully constructed slide deck and walks through example problems constantly and slowly. Problem sets are extremely reasonable in difficulty and expectations for tests are clear. Learned a ton and would take again.

This was just about the worst class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Professor was completely unreachable for 3 days before the extremely difficult problem sets were due because he made it a rule to not help students past that point. Exams would introduce brand new topics to challenge you. Not worth the GPA drop.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this class was solid, largely because I did the problem sets with a group and went to office hours.  I think the class material is just trying to get us to be creative and solve novel problems. It can be a challenging class, but a good use of time.

This was a fantastic class! Material was challenging but not more than the typical Vanderbilt class. Tests were not bad if you worked to understand the problem sets. Lectures were long and required attention to really get the material. This was his first semester at Vanderbilt and he was very receptive to feedback and helping students learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst prof I have had in the economics department. Pretty dense homework that can be difficult to self-teach if you miss class. Tests tend to cover some tangential topics. During the final, we got a "challenge problem" that he expected most of us to bomb. Dull Lecturer but I appreciated the mathematical intuition behind the models he went over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material in this class is relatively hard but Blandin makes it worse. One main issue is that we have weekly problem sets that take up an inordinate amount of time and doesn't really to the tests very well. The other issue is that on exams he loves to include esoteric material from the slides that don't receive much practice or coverage.

Many fundamental assumptions and ideas are inferred by students during the exams instead of delivered and stressed during the class. Little or no practice problems are offered on the most weighted short-answer question in the tests. However, he is pretty reachable outside of class and is generally a nice person.

Will never take his class again. The only good point i like this class is that it offers me a high-quality 75-min sleep because lectures are monotone. Weird exam questions and weird grading.And be prepared for slides with typos and ambiguities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: List is the best orgo prof if you consider the whole package. Exams are MUCH easier than others profs'. You'll have to self-teach, but Klein problems prepare you well for his exams. He's a bit disorganized in class but carefully explains the material. 10 bonus tophat pts, and 25 pts each from activities and discussion.

He explains things very well even though he can be a bit all over the place. He is so helpful during office hours. He only tests what he teaches and he's very clear about what will be on the exams. I love Dr. List! Just because his exams are more straightforward doesn't mean you shouldn't study tho, if you study, you'll do well.

Sure, List's tests are "easier," but only take this class if you read the textbook chapters and can teach yourself a semester worth of material. If you actually want to learn from your professor, take someone else. He's a nice and genuine guy, just doesn't teach very well.

He is a bit disorganized but not anything absurd. He does get a little behind but he decides what is on the tests and the date so it evens out. He is really friendly and approachable Gives us practice sheets to make class more interactive. Orgo is just a hard course by nature.
Practice exams were practically identical to the ones given in class. Just memorize and you should be good.

So nice, but not a good teacher. Unorganized and distracted while lecturing. He's good for students who have time to read the textbook before each class, but not for busy students who don't have that much time and want to actually learn in class! Mostly reviews topics vaguely with few practice probs. Tests were difficult but some partial credit.

Funny professor and tries to keep class engaging. lots of self teaching and falls very behind. since he's behind, will sometimes speed through content to catch up. tophat questions help, but can be difficult. grading scale is harder than other professors(92=A). questions are more straightforward than other professors.

cons: list tends to be disorganized which can leave you lost in lecture. sometimes he throws curveballs on exams, testing on stuff we barely went over.

pros: list is definitely the nicest and funniest chem prof. also, his grading scale is very generous.

I enjoyed taking List! He has good office hours, silly jokes, and a nice grading system. His exams are also easier than other profs. However, he is disorganized and does not clearly state what will be on exams, which makes studying ahead hard. This is a majority self-study class, which is not a bad thing if orgo is your only difficult class.

List is really goofy and a great person. Is he a little disorganized in lectures? Sure. But he still provides a good understanding of the material, beyond what we need to know, just for our understanding. Importantly, his tests are far easier than those of other profs. Read Klein, do all the problems, and you'll do well.

I took Dr List for Chem 1 and Orgo 1, and he's my favorite. Yeah, he can get a little behind sometimes or make mistakes, but he is extremely responsive to emails and very helpful in office hours. He also puts very similar problems to the ones done in class on the exams. Love Dr. List!!

Definitely one of the easier orgo profs when it comes to exams, but not one of the better teachers. He's a little clumsy in lectures (forgetting things, making small mistakes), but he's a chill guy overall. Orgo is orgo though, and you're gonna have to learn a lot of stuff on your own anyway. Might as well take it w/ someone who gives easier exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is simply a really hard class, but Dr. List makes it more manageable. I can't imagine doing as well as I'm doing if I took this class with a different professor. He moves slower than the other professors, tests are "easier", and he gives the most partial credit. Yeah, he messes up sometimes but he's just so nice so who gaf.
Not good. Pretty poor at emphasizing what would be on the tests. Cool guy, just not great to take for the intro course.
Easiest orgo 2 prof.

He's a nice guy but a disorganized prof. Lectures are manageable but he doesn't hold reviews for midterms and didn't provide his old exams for practice. Exams are ~easier than other sections, but not reflective of how much each concept was covered in lecture. If you can self-teach, you'll be fine. Friday quizzes + extra credit TopHat questions help

I'm shocked to see others say he prepares you well for the exams bc I completely disagree. He told us we needed to know ~11 mechanisms for the final exam, and ended up putting none on it. He told us the multiple choice would be slightly more than prior exams but it was under 20% of the final (exam 2 was 46% and exam 3 was like 30%).

Very behind other sections and usually doesn't review for tests. Very nice and funny professor, dense lectures. His tests are easier than other sections but there is a lot of self teaching needed. Show up to lecture, the tophat points help!

pros: 
- easier exams- 92 is A (except our final was highkey foul but i think he curved) 
- humble- he will give points back on tests if its reasonable 
- very helpful in office hours

cons
- disorganized ish
- falls behind in lectures so some content was rushed but still on our midterm 
- not taught in a while so barely any practice exams

In terms of Orgo 2, it isn't easy. If you want to actually know orgo in depth for chemistry purposes, don't take List. But if you're premed, orgo 2 is barely on the MCAT, and Dr. List is your best bet of getting a good grade. If you can teach yourself, you'll be set.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not curve even being a disorganized professor. He seems like a good guy but teaching wise he is terrible

Dr. List is awful for Orgo 2. Despite not covering as much as the others, he is the only prof to not review before exams or go over what we need to know. His exams aren't awful but his communication abt them is abysmal. Finished writing the final the day of and lied abt what would be on it.  Feels like he prepares you for a completely diff exam.

First time teaching OChem 2 in like 6 years and it shows. We were behind the other class by like 2 chapters. But he's a good lecturer and hes clear about he expects on his exams. If you are stacked on other classes, this is the section to take. If you want a comprehensive coverage of OChem 2 maybe not the best prof.

List isin't awful for orgo 2 but I wouldn't say he is good. You will need to rely on self-teaching  A TON. His exams are easier than others but he doesn't prepare AT ALL. Sometimes it feels like he prepares you for the wrong exam (he told us we needed to know 4 mechanisms for exam 3 and put 1 on the test and it was one we didin't cover).

Though Dr. List hasn't taught orgo for a while, he is actually a good choice. His tests are more straightforward, and he tries to make the lecture more engaging and interesting by telling some jokes. He is also very caring and usually walks around to see if anyone has a question when doing tophat.

Dr. List is pretty average in lecturing ability, but he is really goofy. You'll have to self-study to get an A. Make sure to go to class for 15 bonus points (comes in clutch). Also go to coffee chats and do surveys for additional bonus points. Tests are the same between gen chem sections. Todd is probably better but grade depends on effort.
decent prof, but might want to rely on textbook for most of your learning. gets a bit more conceptual than first semester, so get lots of practice questions in before exams
He is the best orgo prof ever. Take him
GOAT Professor
Love this guy
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: BEST PROF AT VANDY. TAKE HIM
Great professor. Love everything about this class. TAKE HIM
Gen chem was best wit List. Great lecturer
Great guy. I love this class
First exam was easier than any professor
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Simple exams. Funny Guy. TAKE HIS CLASS
The highlight of my life is when he taught the class how to scissor on the first day. He is truly ahead of his time

Would not recommend if you've never taken chem before - with some background, his lectures aren't too difficult. However, he is not very good at explaining things so that someone with no background could understand. He makes quite a few mistakes during lecture and usually slaps himself across the face when he gets something wrong.

Not a hard teacher, just a hard class. Very funny in class but his lectures and slides aren't great, take Tainter if you can. You can do well with him if you just study a lot on your own, the LAs help a lot too and he is open for office hours.

Not horrible, but you'll have better success in his class if you had previous exposure to gen chem. Tends to lose the plot, and sometimes works out problems incorrectly. Sort of just states the concept then works out a problem. Doesn't really prepare you for the exams, which are 75% of your grade.

I don't think List is too bad. He's a little disorganized, but I still understood most of what was being taught. Tips: review the material by reading the textbook before the lecture. It's helpful because you can usually treat the lecture like a review. Study with friends who are also in gen chem and go to lectures for the TopHat bonuses.

Lets keep it real. As kind and funny of a professor he is, he is unorganized and unprepared for class. Oftentimes, he was caught using the wrong formula or calculating incorrectly by a student or LA. Although mistakes are common, I simply believe there were too many for such a hard class. I had to read every chapter of the textbook to self-teach.

He's an average professor. Great personality, is good to get along with and is accessible. As for teaching, he lands right in the middle. He regularly messes up on math in class. Slides are not as informational as professors such as Tainter. Chem 1601 is a difficult course and the first test material is more complex than what is given in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. List is a very caring and accessible professor; however, his lectures were not the best, and he often messed up example problems that were either corrected in class or had to be corrected later. General Chemistry will be hard no matter the professor, but taking a different one may be the best option for increased learning.

List definitely has a good personality and the most character out of the other Gen Chem professors. Honestly he wasn't that bad, most of the difficulties I had were mostly with the class itself.

Not a bad professor, but not a great one either.

List is a really good person, and you can tell he is well versed in chemical concepts. However, he is not the best lecturer. He tends to get lost working out problems, which can cause confusion surrounding major topics for the exams. He is willing to meet outside of office hours to discuss anything needing extra explanation.

Professor List is a funny and energetic lecturer, but his teaching style can be a bit unorganized. While the class is challenging, his approachable demeanor and willingness to answer questions make it more enjoyable. Utilizing Unstuckstudy and the free textbook alongside attending lectures is key to success.

Orgo lab experience completely depends on your TA. But you'll see List occasionaly walking around the bays. He's friendly and will nicely remind you of lab protocol if he sees something wrong. Semester 1 orgo lab lowkey harder than semester 2. But again, orgo lab experience is completely dependent on which TA you get. Reports are generally chill.
Orgo lab is set up really well. Everything is clear and not graded by accuracy, which is a nice relief from gen chem. It all depends on what TA you get with grading tbh. Taylor is the goat
Cool guy and very helpful lab instructor. Walks around and helps out kind of like a chef in a culinary school. Good instructions and videos. Lab is not terrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor List covers the majority of the basic material in class, and takes his time going over simple examples which can be helpful.  Overall, the class itself is difficult.  In order to be prepared for exams you have to devote a lot of time to practice problems from the book and Aktiv hw and fully understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly a great, understanding dude. Was sick a few times and he let me make up lab, tophat bugged out and he let me redo it, and my TA graded too harshly but I'm pretty sure List curved our specific section so I still ended up with an A. Seems intimidating at first, but funny dude and is very understanding of a student's situation. 5/5

Dr. List is such a kind, wholesome guy! I really enjoyed having him this semester and would definitely take him again. His lectures aren't the clearest, but some supplemental practice outside of class will fix up any confusion. I really like that we get to discuss his TopHat questions and understand how to do them.

Prof. List is very funny and energetic. He is behind on lectures but tries to make them make sense and answers any and all questions. Sat at the front and he would come up to make sure that we understood the practice problems. Would recommend sitting in the middle front! Chem1601 is itself hard but List makes it a bit enjoyable.

Prof. List was funny and overall nice guy. I've heard some criticism about him being behind the other lecturers but I really didn't think it was that bad. He's not the most organized, but I liked his lectures and overall it was pretty good. Fully understanding the homework is definitely an important part of being successful in this class.

Pros:
- Humorous
- Only 2 or so hours of work on non-test weeks.
- Attendance isn't mandatory.

Cons:
- Unorganized
- Often improvises examples, then gets confused and concedes that the example didn't work.
- Uses other professors' assignments, which don't fully correspond to his lectures.

Survival tip:
- Homework is key to understanding content.

Professor List is a nice and genuine person, but I found his lectures to be unhelpful because he dosen't explain concepts very well and barely does any practice problems. He was consistently behind the other sections because he took to much time doing Top hat questions rather than showing us test related examples.

I didn't take chem in high school and I found List to be a great prof. I learned so much and always felt prepared for exams. He is behind the other lectures usually, but that's only because he takes time to make sure we understand the content. Overall, I enjoyed his class, but it's definitely hard and requires a lot of work.

Dr. List is one of the nicest professors I've had at Vanderbilt, but his class is also one of the most difficult that I've taken. Your grade is almost solely based upon your exam scores, and the homework is nothing like the quizzes or exams. Take advantage of the practice tests, as they are quite similar to the actual exams.

Professor List was often behind other Chemistry professor in content. He doesn't really go into depth when explaining the content during his lectures making it hard to properly understand. His lectures are usually straight out of the textbook, so therefore, his lectures are pointless.

Professor List is great. He does tend to be a little behind the other professors in terms of content but I mean his lectures are hilarious(he's basically got ADHD so its fun to watch) and the one time I went in for office hours because I stopped paying attention in class he explained everything to me great.
