Dude is great would take his class again.
In honor of his last name being List I thought I'd make a list of things I like about orgo lab: ...

Adam List has anger issues. A dude took a bite out of a kiwi 10 minutes before lab and the man exploded. He yelled at the kid to get out of the bay and slammed the door behind him, making the walls shake. Other than that, he occasionally appears behind you without warning to help fix your lab setup. He's like a spooky, bipolar teddy bear.

Dr. List is a very nice and a great guy but isn't the best teacher. He always seems a little unprepared and is often behind the other professor's lectures. His lectures are exact copies of the textbook, so reading the textbook is super helpful to doing well in the class. The class is very hard so pay a lot of attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you take orgo lab, your experience strongly depends on your TA that you are assigned to. However, List makes the structure of the class relatively easy by having online modules to complete before class with notebook prep. Afterward is a standard lab report. He tries to help the TAs as much as possible and is generally funny.

Labs are run by TAs, so your experience will be highly dependent on what TA you are assigned. Reasonable workload for 1 credit lab. Reports were relatively straightforward, and had reasonable expectations. Procedures are well written and easy to follow. A word of advice, read the procedure ahead of time and learn to multitask: you'll get out early.

classic weed out class. tests are excessively hard and lectures are rushed. if you've taken ap chem, List is a decent option, but if you have minimal background knowledge, take someone like Todd who goes more in detail. study super hard for the tests.

The guy is a character but wastes an insurmountable amount of time saying the most out of pocket things I've ever heard. I learned more in my freshman year introductory high school chemistry course than I did this entire year. Material was rushed and List taught in such an unorganized fashion that concepts I USED to understand became confusing.
Dr. List is a good choice if you have taken AP Chem. He is funny and makes class enjoyable but because exams are the same for every class maybe not the best choice. Great guy, average professor.

Had him for orgo lab. Although labs are run by TAs, he did make a few videos for us due to covid so I did have him a bit more than those on an average year. Has an odd sense of humor but honestly, rather funny sometimes. Overall doesn't do much, but doesn't make the lab hard so I can't complain.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: For students who have already taken AP Chemistry, Professor List is a good choice. However, if you need a deeper explanation of the topics, it might be better to choose a different prof. He's super sweet and caring, but at times he seemed to be a little bit scatterbrained which could make it hard to learn.

Although I enjoyed having List as my professor, I would not recommend him if you are someone who needs in depth explanations for chemistry concepts. No matter who you choose as your professor, gen chem is going to be hard. Find the professor that suits your teaching style. List did not fit mine.

List is not the best choice for genchem. His lectures are a bit vague and not many in class examples. I relied heavily on the textbook, which is expected, but I wish that the lectures were more straightforward and informative. Do every single homework problem; it's really your only hope for the exam in this class besides understanding concepts

List's lectures are sometimes confusing and it's easy to get lost in the sauce because Chem 1601 covers so much. You definitely need to read the textbook to get a good grade, going to lecture is fs not enough by itself. But List is a good guy, such a dad and if you go to his office hours he's nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chemistry 1601 is by nature a challenging course. This definitely holds true, for there are standardized tests for all CHEM 1601 sections. These tests are difficult and make up the majority of your grade. However, Dr. List is a good professor who will cover the necessary material in lecture. At times he can be vague on expectations. You must study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is test heavy and the material is very difficult. Dr. List does his best to teach during class but he is much better during office hours. His tests were much more reasonable than other org sections and very similar to book practice problems. He is one the better chemistry teachers at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are the only thing that matter in this class. Also, List doesn't explain the material well, so reading the textbook is essential to passing. Very boring lectures and difficult tests. He at least tries to make the material somewhat interesting, but overall the lectures are pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. List is a fine lecturer for 1601. He doesn't write the tests so sometimes he misses stuff, but if you read the book you should be able to cover it yourself. Lectures are fairly standard, sometimes he'll make a good joke. If you put in the work as with any class you'll do fine with List.

Definitely the easier orgo professor. There will be a lot of self-teaching no matter what, but he gives good practice problems that are similar to what will end up on exams and the tests are easier than Hare's. He also has a pretty generous grading scale (88 for A- and 92 for A) and if you go to class, you can get up to 4% extra credit from tophat

Lectures seemed to go at a slower pace than Todd's, and were much easier to follow. However, he doesn't give print out notes or super detailed power points so you actually have to go to class and pay attention. He spends a lot of time on examples, which can be really helpful even if somewhat tedious. Super nice guy and great in office hours too.
Lab is mostly run by your TA but Dr. List will pop in at times. Very responsive and accommodating if you have issues or need to make up something.
Dr. List is the man. By far the best orgo teacher and a complete character.

When comparing him to another organic professor, I ended up doing much better in his class. Yes it's true you'll need to do a lot of self teaching but it was no different than in other chemistry classes. His tests were much more reaosnable and very similar to practice problems, no big surprises. He told jokes and made the lectures seem kinda fun.

One of the worst professors I've ever had in terms of teaching ability. Often confused, unprepared, and distracted in class. Doesn't seem to read his lesson plans before going through them. Sometimes he will skip entire slides and sometimes he will spend the entire class on one slide. Nice guy, but not a good teacher.

While List gave easier tests, his lectures were so boring that his class averages weren't that much higher than Hare. He had high standard deviations which means he wasn't teaching the material, students either knew it from previous studies/ their own learning or they knew none of it. My suggestion: do lots of practice problems, I didn't do enough.

One of the poorer scheduling decisions i've made. Incredibly nice guy but the lectures are very poor and confusing. His tests are fairly doable (many predict the product questions) and usually you get more time for his exams but prepare to study 100% by yourself. I suggest to take another prof. to be prepared for Orgo 2 or the MCAT.

List was clearly not used to teaching TR classes. He did not cover all the material that you are expected to learn in orgo 1. We were supposed to finish chapter 13 and barely got through chapter 12. His lectures are dull and uninspired. He doesn't really seem to care about students
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would highly recommend Dr. List. lectures are informative but must read the book out of class. Do all the recommended practice problems. Tests are easier than Hare's plus you get 1 hour 30 minutes for Lists exams instead of 50 for Hare. A/A- is doable
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 100% take List if possible for 2221. An A is only 92% and there is 4% extra credit plus points for recitation and a mechanism workbook. Exams are much more straightforward than Hare's. 70% predict the product, very little mechanisms and synthesis and some naming. Take advantage of the first test, it is super easy (average was 83 last year).
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. List is awesome! He was so accessible outside of class and he genuinely wanted us to learn and do well. He is also passionate about the subject which really helps. It is a very involved class, but if you study regularly, then an A is definitely attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was probably the hardest class I've ever taken, but Dr. List was still a great professor. He's really sweet and his fascination with organic chemistry is quite evident in lecture, yet he can make (and correct) the casual mistake from time to time. His tests are fair (easier than others') and Top Hat gives a HUGE boost to your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nice dude. Definitely is a better orgo professor than gen chem. Tests are relatively easy if you study and follow the lecture material. Only thing is that when he is in a rush to lecture or fit something in the exam he gets sloppy with his teaching but other than that good professor and would recommend

Lectures felt rather disorganized--sometimes entire slides would be skipped after he glanced at them. Was lost on days when he left his notes at home. Not great at re-explaining in a different way if asked. Very friendly during office hours, willing to stay extra long to get everyone taken care of. Not familiar with the online work (Dr. Todd is)

List really makes chemistry lecture interesting. He is such a character, in the best way, and he really seems to want everyone to succeed. General chemistry is tough, especially since the tests make up most of the grade and they're fairly hard. But List is a great choice for a lecturer and explains things really well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: List is honestly a great guy who is super funny and makes lectures interesting. He's not going to be super helpful in terms of teaching for what is going to be on the test but since all the gen chem tests are the same the professor really doesn't matter that much. Overall List is fine.

List is a great guy and entertaining in lecture. He covers the minimum of what you need to know. Overall, Gen Chem is tough but reading and minimizing silly mistakes allows you to do well. Beware the final, be sure to review at the end of the semester.

I had Dr. List for Gen Chem and for Orgo Lab. In orgo lab, I liked him so much more! He went through each bay at times, and he was very helpful when needed! My partner and I didn't understand a concept, but he explained it very clearly. I liked orgo lab so much more than gen chem lab, and the work wasn't too bad. It also depends a lot on your TA.

I wouldn't recommend Professor List if you have never taken chemistry before. However, if you are comfortable with the basics, take him because he does entertain and it makes that early morning lecture a little more bearable. He does get tripped up basic calculations sometimes, but he makes up for it by banging his head on the board in frustration
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: List is a dad with a UChicago degree. While he is enthusiastic about the material and sometimes funny in lectures, he skips half the material required to know for his tests which are impossible if you rely on the lectures only. The TAs are your only saviors should you take List's General Chemistry, which I advise you not to do. Pick another prof.

He's  a really nice guy, but a bad lecturer. He forgets to mention like half the material that the other chem profs teach, so you have to read the book or get notes from friends in other sections to be ready for the discussion quizzes and tests. He's very silly though and makes lectures entertaining, but you can't rely on them to pass.
Great professor! Very helpful.

Dr. List was a decent professor, but nothing special. He taught the required material, but often times he got confused by his own calculations. He was very friendly and was always willing to help. Clicker questions in his class are great for you if you choose not to go to discussion. The tests are standardized, but very doable if you read the book.

List is very accessible and very funny.  He wants to answer questions that students have. The class is too standardized to see how effective he really is as a teacher though.  Lectures are a bit helpful but the book is way better.
Professor List is a great teacher. He wants to answer questions so make sure to ask in class.
Good teacher and answers questions if you ask. Funny at times.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: List is a great teacher that has a great sense of humor and keeps his class both engaged and entertained. His lectures are straightforward and he is very helpful and receptive during office hours.

Professor List is a poor lecturer. He finds himself underprepared at times and struggles doing simple addition. Closely follows his lecture plans and also attempts to make jokes. He is mediocre at best.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor list teaches what is necessary for Gen Chem, but will get tripped up on his notes and go off on tangents during lectures. He was helpful during office hours, but the book was more valuable than his lectures. He is a decent professor, but Gen Chem is too standardized to tell how effective he really is.

He was a nice and entertaining guy. Towards the end of the year, I stopped going to lectures, but when I did, I thought he was pretty clear and understandable. I relied more on discussion for extra credit, but some test questions were very similar to his clicker questions. However, aside from his PPTs, prepare to read the textbook. You'll need it.

Professor List is funny and clearly knows a lot about chemistry, but he often goes on tangents about the history of certain experiments and derives equations, stuff you won't need to know for the departmentalized exams. If you don't know the material well you'll need to read the book.

By far the worst teacher I've had. Didn't learn a single thing in the lectures, only went because of the clicker questions. Had to basically teach myself General Chemistry, which is hard enough on its own. I wouldn't recommend taking from him.

He seems like a nice guy and tries to add some humor into his lectures. I think the biggest problem is that he isn't able to simplify chemistry enough to teach an intro class. He is knowledgeable, but doesn't explain the concepts very well. You will be better off reading straight out of the chemistry book during class than listening to his lectures

I found professor List to be very boring. He makes so many mistakes during class that it's hard to keep up. Never seems like he knows what he is doing, but he does get everything covered to some extent. Of all the chem professors, I'd put him somewhere in the middle.

Decent teacher and pretty entertaining guy. I only showed up to maybe half the classes because they weren't too useful as long as you went over the PPTs and clicker questions at home, which were great resources for tests. You'll also want to read the textbook.
Lecture didn't cover much. I hadn't taken Chem since sophomore year, so jumping back into it was struggle. Essentially learned everything from the textbook and my engineering friends.

List is a great guy and wants you to understand the material, but sometimes he doesn't explain the concepts in the most clear ways. You can expect clicker questions once or twice a week, and those are pretty helpful for conceptual test questions. His lectures don't cover everything but if you study, you'll do well. He's pretty funny, too.
He's very entertaining. Just show up, take good notes, and study and you should be fine.

He's ok. If you read the textbook, do the homework, and really put in the time to master the material you can definitely get an A. Todd is a better lecturer though (plus she writes the tests), so if you don't have any experience with Chemistry I would recommend taking her. Also he thinks he's a lot funnier than he is.

List was very confusing and he even confused himself a few times like he did not know what he was doing. Step into his office, it looks like a tornado came through, which reflects on his teaching style. He never finishes the material we need for a test and leaves out the concepts actually tested on. Take Todd, she makes the tests & gives notes.
Average lecturer. Gets the points across and is good at speaking. Encourages questions. Willing to help outside of class. Easy to understand but a little dry

He does A TON of examples in lecture, which is good for homework help but not great for the truefalse kinds of conceptual questions on the test. Reading the textbook can help with that. Tests are challenging. Expect to have to work for an A. This is a weed-out class, especially first semester so I don't recommend taking it unless you have to.

Awkward, unapproachable, unclear, & inefficient (ends 5-10 min early). Took attendance with clickers and it's a small part of your grade, but I stopped going halfway through the semester because he was more confusing than helpful IMO. Only thing I liked about his class is that he wrote out every step on the board when he gave us example problems.

Professor List is very passionate about organic chemistry, not so much gen chem. He doesn't make the tests, which are considerably difficult. Gets distracted and flustered easily in lecture with his own jokes and drawing irrelevant inorganic molecules. If you don't read the textbook you won't pass. Lectures don't help.

Dr. List was capable of teaching the material while throwing  in a joke or two.  He was available to his students if needed.  However, he is normally not the one who writes the tests, at least in general chemistry.

I loved List!  I'm glad I had him over Todd, who seems overrated to me.  List was always lively and laid-back at 9am and his notes are clear and prepare you well for the test.  I had never taken AP Chem and am not a chemistry genius and got an A- in the class.  Attendance is obviously not mandatory but its best to go and get notes.
Long, boring lectures. Sit in on other professors' lectures instead.

Stay away from List if you can. His lectures MIGHT cover 13 of what will be on the test. By the end of the semester, I wondered why I even went to class. Waste a lot of time making jokes and goes off topic. Take Todd if you can. She has the highest class average.

List is a pretty good professor but has a tendency to get off topic and talk about things that aren't covered on the tests. You'll have to read the textbook consistently if you want to do well since the tests are standardized. He's a friendly guy and sometimes tells cheesy jokes.

If you didn't take AP Chem, this class is going to be hell for you. He's not the least helpful professor I've ever had, but he's at the bottom of the list. His lectures are hilarious and will keep you awake though (even when he does suddenly announce that he doesn't care about gen chem).  You definitely need the text to keep up with what's going on
Hilarious

About as good as it gets for the first half of Chem. Can use clicker questions for extra credit rather than going to recitation. Tests are standardized across all sections so make sure to study the textbook and/or get your hands on past exams.

Loved him! Fun to listen and attend lectures. Class is difficult,studying outside of lecture required. Clicker questions were medium difficulty, and there were sometimes (~4/50 Qs) "easy" or "giveaway" questions to boost clicker score. Tests difficult and involved both formulas and concepts, but got easier with good studying habits.
He is a cool guy, but his lectures are very confusing and hard to follow. He jumps around a bit. I had to spend a lot of time outside of class reading the book to understand the material.

Cool guy. He has a dry sense of humor, and he tries to crack jokes. If you are annoyed by that, don't take his section. He's pretty clear in his explanations. Just read the book and do problems and you will do fine!

Extremely not clear, didn't know how to solve problems assigned. Unnecessary Useless work that didn't help for exams or understanding chemistry. Questions given for review and in class were childsplay in comparison to the caliber of exams. Take Phillips or Somewhere Else. Oh & the textbook sucks, get Chang Gen Chem if you want to learn.
Very confusing in class-did not explain things well or give adequate test preparation. very hard course if you did not take ap chem

This class was super easy compared with ap chemistry.  super easy.  you could sleep through class and get an a.  the book is very helpful.  study the book and do a lot of practice problems and you'll be fine.  this class is the easiest by far ive taken at vanderbilt.

Pretty good lecturer; jokes are pretty good, especially for being at 8 in the morning. Does a good job of preparing you for the exams. Clicker questions and online homework will do wonders for you though too.

Tries to make jokes in class. All of them are corny, but funny. He does a pretty good job of teaching. Never been to office hours but heard good things. He responds to emails. You may learn more from reading the textbook and mastering chem than actually going to class. The experiments in class are cool. If you can, try to get into Todd's section.
Lots of jokes (corny, but hey, he tries!) Really good about office hours; will take your questions pretty much anytime. Overall nice guy who looks out for his students.

Although I was not excited about having an 8am chem lecture, I am glad that I had List as my professor this semester. He's not boring or monotone, so it was easy to stay awake in his class, and for the most part, he teaches with clarity. He's a funny (in a cheezy way) guy, and I would take another class from him.

Three Words: READ THE TEXTBOOK. This guy is not good at lecturing and wastes too much time talking about things that are not on the exam. CHEM 102A is standardized so it doesn't really matter which professor you have. The textbook will be your best friend.

At first, you think he's cool. Then you realize that his lectures are pointless, the clicker questions are often ambiguous and unanswerable and he's incapable of spelling elementary words and doing mental math. He's a nice guy, but being in his lecture renders you woefully unprepared for the miserable departmentalized tests. READ THE TEXTBOOK.

List is an amazing teacher, and by far the best in the chem department! He was very clear in his lectures. He focused on the class understanding how to do the math concepts in chem, which is what the majority of the tests and exams are over. The tests in chem are hard, but I think he bests prepares you for them; he teaches 8 AM, but it's worth it!
He keeps it somewhat funny. Its an 8am class, i need to stay awake!!

He was hilarious and made the 8-a.m. classes worthwhile.  He definitely hates gen chem and probably should teach the chem kids who got a 4 on the AP exam and couldn't opt out of orgo at Vandy.  But I'd say he was fair .  Good teacher overall.  I had some good laughs.

8am classes are actually tolerable because of his energy-although still in need of a healthy dose of caffeine to stay awake. READ TEXT BEFOREHAND-extremely helpful. Problems done in class are VERY close to problems you'll see on exams. Go over exams with him, but get a tutor for concepts. LOTS of time needs to be put into this class. Decent prof.
He didn't seem very interested in teaching intro chem but he did know his stuff. I didn't get as much out of this class as I would have liked.

It doesnt seem like he cares about teaching gen chem and it shows in his lectures...hes more of an orgo guy. His lectures were very boring and hard to sit through especially at 8 in the morning. Take Phillips if possible!

Take Phillips, Phillips is definitely the best followed by List- NEVER take it at 8 a.m., I thought I'd go to every class but everyone misses it at least once when it's at 8 a.m., makes it much harder to pay attention

Professor List is a fun professor.  He has a lot more spunk than the other chemistry professors, but he is oftentimes more bumbly and mistake prone than others.  He should be a high school teacher, it seems more fitting.  I haven't done well on the exams, and I have had to put in a lot of work just to get the grades I have been having, class averag
He's engaging enough, but it's a boring subject.
Dr. List is very helpful and a really nice guy. He goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material and really simplifies it. His tests are pretty easy too.
this is for my wonderful TA

This guy is of shady(sketchy) character. Just look at him. Tests are skecthy (a couple problems could have several potential answers)His math is sketchy (can't add 25+273 in his head or on the board), and the TA's are sketchy in their grading. Experiments don't work(sketchy TA's fault.) This whole class is shady.  Cross over and use Prasad's notes.
yeah, your lab experience is pretty much TOTALLY dependent on your TA...I don't say how people can conclusively say orgo lab is hard or easy..it all depends on who you get
dr. list's labs are easy!  lab reports are pretty easy to write...but most of your orgo lab experience will depend on the TA.

really really nice guy even if he's not the best teacher in the world...It may not seem like much, but you'll miss him later, when you have to deal with other profs and realize that most science teachers here are just way too full of themselves.
Nice guy, decent teacher.  It's a difficult class no matter who the professor is.
i took orgo over the summer with him.super hard.i hate the third test and the final.too much question and too little time. he gets confused while explaining the material.
No Comments

Really nice guy who tries to help, but doesn't succeed.  Is never thorough enough. My notes from that class were basically useless on the exams, halfway through the semester I gave up going to class and just studied the book.
Cooky professor. Great person. Makes boring material into interesting material. The class is hard anyways.

I enjoyed his classes, partly because the demos were pretty entertaining. He pretty much skimmed through a lot though, and did not really prepare helpful notes and guides like Hanusa did. But other than that, he's a great professor. I am looking forward to taking orgo with him next semester.

Orgo lab with Adam is easy as pie.  The labs themselves are usually pretty quick and are hard to screw up on.  A lot of your experience will be the TA, so pray for a good one!  Other than that, the reports aren't bad.  Go see him if you need help on lab stuff or just anything w/ the chemistry dept.
he's a nice, funny guy, but not a great teacher.  his notes are disorganized and unclear.  has great demos to wake you up though.
nice guy. funny. can be hard if you havent already had some chemistry. keeps you awake most of the time especially if you have him for 8 oclock.
He gives occasional lectures that are nice and helpful. His lab notebook has some problems in it. Some of the prelab questions may be a bit difficult, but there are TAs to help you.
Easiest labs ever.  You think these are hard, don't take any more lab sciences.

List's labs were easy.  If you think they're hard, I cringe to think of what you'll think of upper-level chem/bio courses or med school courses.  You'll be wishing you had Dr. List's labs back.  This guy is incredibly nice and easy to talk to.  Take him!
he designs orgo labs from hell. therefore the labs and prelabs (not usually) are hard to complete.  just pray that you have an easy lab TA.  cuz list is no help whatsoever. he is evil

I did not like him.  Went to him once and was not helpful so I did not bother going back again.  I ended up not going to class for over half the semester, I thought he wasn't as good as cracked up to be.  I attended a couple sessions of other professors a
Well worth waking up at 8 AM.  Animated and likes his demos, though they might not always work.  Prepares you for the exams better than the others.
Good GUy, Good labs
He's great to keep you awake at 8am!!
No Comments
Absent-minded, nice guy, semi-difficult tests

Took him for CORE 1010. Fantastic professor, very passionate about the material. Gives great feedback on essays, and use him to go over your essay beforehand. Does talk a lot during class - became more of a lecture than a seminar but plucking at straws. Would take another class with him!

Class was pretty easy to do well in (5 short responses for completion and two papers). However, there was about 70-150 pages to read per class, and about 14 books over the semester and the material is quite repetitive. It is not the most engaging or exciting class but it is pretty simple and easy to do well if you complete the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, very flexible with deadlines. Class is structured really well. Lots of reading, but manageable and essays are relatively easy with very clear instructions.

Meyer is absolutely amazing. What a kind human being. A great writing course because he gives you a lot of time to write and is super nice about extensions as well as you have the chance to do peer reviews. If you are not taking his class what are you doing.

Professor Meyer really knows his stuff. He came very well prepared to every class and had clear grading criteria. The workload isn't overwhelming by any means, just four projects and 20 page readings. I would encourage you to participate as it is a discussion based course, but he won't do anything to mandate participation in class. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Meyer really cares about his students. He adjusted readings to help us avoid ones that were not that helpful compared to others. He also provided great feedback on our writing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. I took this class just for an AXLE credit but it quickly became my favorite class. Dr. Meyer is probably the most approachable and knowledgeable teacher I've ever had at Vandy. Regardless of your major/background his classes will teach you a lot without feeling like a burdensome grind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Meyer is the most caring professor that you will find at Vanderbilt. He usually will allow you to do late/makeup work. He also did not set strict word count limits on papers and did not take off points for papers being shorter than what was recommended. He keeps the class interesting and assigns interesting readings. He is a must take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: WOW. Simply wow. Dr. Meyer was the highlight of my freshman year. The class is reading-heavy though, so you should prepare for that. He is very chill though- he will help you with anything needed and often give you extensions. He is so understanding and caring. I am going to miss class with him. His essay feedback is amazing too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is super knowledgeable and a great lecturer. The class was fascinating. However, this class gave me the most homework of any class I have ever taken. The reading will take you at least a couple of hours a night. If you are willing to put in the work, the class is very interesting and rewarding, and he does make you a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was probably the most helpful professor I've had so far. Gives very good feedback on papers (but there are a lot). There is also a lot of reading so be sure to either read it or listen during class discussions. It's an easy class though and very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Meyer provides excellent feedback on papers and helped me grow as a writer. I took this as my FYWS and it was definitely a much larger workload than other writing seminars. There was a ridiculous amount of assigned reading as well as 3 6-8 page papers and 5 2-3 page response papers. If you work hard you should get an A no problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This course was very interesting but requires a ton of reading for each class. Class entails discussion on readings and weekly response papers which are difficult to complete if you dont read. In addition to participation and response papers, there are 2 large papers. If you show effort, Meyer isnt a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Black-Jewish relations was a really eye opening and intriguing class and Dr. Meyer did an excellent job of making the history we learned interesting and understandable. Reading can be heavy sometimes, but he gives excellent feedback & if you try, you will do well. It's evident that Dr. Meyer cares about his students, and he's a great professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Meyer is precious, knowledgable and wants you to care about his content. The novels he chooses are interesting and intriguing, and he does a good job of situating them in articles about the history. The weekly responses get boring but he does them to help you succeed on the papers, which are the true grades. Sweet guy and good Engl elec.

Nightly readings can get a little heavy but overall, it was a very interesting class. Dr. Meyer is very kind and wants to help you succeed and become a great writer. We had 15 short response papers (basically graded for completion) & three larger papers (6-8 pages). He makes it very easy to meet with him and gives helpful feedback.

Super organized. Well-curated readings--though difficult to finish them all. Extreme depth of knowledge. Lots of papers and he will mark every little thing. Really wants students to enjoy and understand the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Black & Jewish Relations as my first year writing seminar and loved it. The material was engaging, and I learned so much about something I never knew existed. Meyer was fantastic, gave amazing feedback on papers, and made class discussion meaningful. There was lots of reading, nightly 1-2 page papers, and 3 large papers. All reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this class just to fulfill credits, but it actually became one of my favorite classes! Meyers is so flexible and understanding and can make a dry topic interesting. You have a response paper due every single week, but don't be scared off because he literally just grades them for completion and you can write them in under an hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Dr. Meyer's first year teaching a writing seminar to my knowledge; it was a solid choice. Although he took up most of class time lecturing us on the readings without allowing for much discussion, the lectures were interesting, and he gave amazing feedback on the papers. An interesting class and great professor. Would definitely recommend.

Professor Meyer is very caring and is beyond willing to help his students be successful in his class. This class was only papers and on every paper he would provide detailed feedback on the draft and then allow you to edit and submit for a final grade. He provides a lot of resources to help students write. Very interesting lectures too.
Loved this class! He is really amazing, not too much work and he really cares about his students. Definitely take one of his classes if you need a W class.

I took Prof. Meyer's class on children of Holocaust survivors, and LOVED him as  a professor. He wants to see you succeed and engage with the material. He implements time off from class to do paper conferences in his office. You'll have reflection papers throughout the semester and two big papers as well, so it's not a blow off, but a great class.

Professor Meyer is great! Grading is easy and classes are usually interesting. Class is definitely an easy A if you commit to keeping up with most of the reading and putting effort into the 2 big papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Meyer is the man. He is a very lenient grader, especially if you meet with him during his office hours. If you can tolerate a good amount of reading and are a fairly decent writer, you will absolutely end up with an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I love this professor!!!! The class discussions are SO interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Loved the class. Super helpful outside of class, literally goes through your entire paper correcting everything (even commas) which is incredible. Get ready to read because the class is fairly reading heavy. Good books though that are good reads!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Professor Meyer for my first year writing seminar and my writing improved immensely. As a writing seminar, the class was writing heavy and a lot of work, but the readings are interesting and thus make the papers easier to write. Though he gives a lot of work, he values participation and effort and your grade will reflect that.
Professor Meyer is very helpful and gives great feedback. His lectures can be a little dry, and he could encourage more participation, but he gives students every chance to succeed.

Dr. Meyer is a great professor and definitely worth taking. I took his freshman writing seminar and the topic was interesting, but more importantly he was so helpful with improving my writing and it really paid off in his class and all my others. Definitely worth it.

Professor Meyer is a great guy and he really makes the subject matter engaging. He's a stickler for old school grammar rules on the essays, which can be slightly aggravating, but he gives great feedback. Participation matters, and you have to read a lot to be able to participate. As a non-Jew, I found the class to be insightful but somewhat dull.

Dr. Meyer is kind, but be prepared for a lot of reading and writing assignments. He also really values participation. Grading revolves around attendance, participation and writing - no tests. He is helpful outside of class and gives good feedback on papers. I took this class as a non-Jew and found it interesting, but not terribly exciting.

Prof. Meyer is super knowledgeable and knows how to communicate the material engagingly.  As a Jew, I found the class fascinating on so many levels.  I definitely recommend it, but beware: there is a ton of reading and paper-writing.  From what I can tell, grading is easy, but there's a lot of work.  Participation is big, too.  Recommended!

Prof. Meyer is great. This class is fairly easy if you put in the time to do the readings, and Prof. Meyer's instructions are very clear. Prof. Meyer also gives great writing advice and is grades things extremely quickly. Definitely take a class with Prof. Meyer if you get a chance.

I had the opportunity to be taught by Dr. Meyer while I was a Fisk University student. I had several classes with him and greatly appreciate all that he taught me. I echo a previous entry, he made me a better writer as well and instilled within me an affinity for reading. Bravo, Dr. Meyer. Hope all is well with you and the family.

GREAT PROFESSOR! Must go to class and complete most of the reading to participate in class to do well, but if you are hardworking its completely manageable. He writes back very helpful comments on his papers (only 3 in the semester), but the key to a great grade in this course is having him review a second draft. Wants his students to do well!

I absolutely recommend Dr Meyer.  The reading and writing are a bit heavy, but it is absolutely worth it for how much he helps you with analytical thinking and paper writing.  I'm relatively slow at reading/writing but it was still very doable. Favorite professor this semester. He keeps the class interesting and genuinely cares about his students.
Professor Meyer is great, especially for a first year student. He is extremely clear and understanding. He keeps his class interesting! I ended up in this class by accident and love it!

Professor Meyer is a great guy.  There is a lot of reading, but it is not really necessary for class discussions.  The three papers are very interesting to write and he is extremely good with giving feedback.  He truly helped me become a better writer.

Dr. Meyer was hands down my favorite professor this semester. He makes class real interesting and is unbelievably helpful with papers. Not a hard grader at all and will definitely work with you to make you a better writer. Lots of reading but it's not unbearable.

I have taken two classes with Dr. Meyer. He truly wants his students to succeed and to improve their writing skills. He always writes copious comments on paper drafts, and these are very insightful and helpful. He is very kind and approachable. Definitely consider taking one of his classes.

Great guy.  He truly wanted his students to become better writers.  3 papers in the semester, but Dr. Meyer takes the time to write page-long comments for each student in the class in addition to editing grammatical errors throughout the essay.  The class itself can get a bit dry, but Dr. Meyer makes the class worth going to every day.
Dr. Meyer is a good professor, really wants to make you a better writer and is really open minded in discussion.
No Comments

Just saw an email from Vicki that there were seats available in this section. It is literally no wonder there are only 6 students enrolled but if you're thinking about it, just don't. Cold calls, weirdest grader, you have to do the reading. Honestly the worst part is that I literally got no feedback for the entire semester just grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far harder than the other professors that teach this class. Our final essay was 10 single spaced pages while the other sections were 2-3. Exams were also significantly harder than other sections. With this being said Professor Soliz drives interesting discussions in her class. She is also very nice. Extra effort goes a long way with her.

Wow. Only professor I've ever had to do one of these for. So bad that myself and classmates often questioned if she was a legitimate professor or not. You will have to do a Bible's worth of reading each week, she'll call you out in class randomly, only had half our grades back from the whole semester, she's inconceivably lazy, etc etc. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this professor. Avoid at all costs, harsh grader, does not gives As out easily, slow grader
Horrible at providing feedback, no rubric, no grading. Its like torture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Don't you ever take his class online it would be a big mistake! Very hard for people that struggle in economics
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Easy course if you show up and do the practice problems
He is really helpful answering questions outside of class
He's such a boss!

I was taught absolutely nothing in 202, and then told that my work was terrible. Ron is an annoying old man who does not deserve the title professor. Ron teaches 202 like it's a baby sitting gig. Save your time, and dont risk your GPA. DO NOT take classes with him unless you already know the material. Either way you will learn nothing.

Prof. Porter is getting a little senile. He's VERY hard of hearing and can be pretty frustrating. That being said, he's really nice and is a great artist. Put in effort and show up, and it will help with your final grade. He likes hard workers. You learn a lot just by doing the exercises. I feel bad about the senile comment, but it's true!
Great professor.

This class has a leinient attendance policy and is fun to go to anyway. Ron is aloof and often goes on tangents, but knows more about painting than anyone I have spoken to before. Just search for his work, he's incredible. He will really improve your ability if you ask him questions, but be prepared to talk for awhile. That's as honest as I can be.

Ron's a great professor, but his class can get boring at times. I fell asleep drawing twice. Also, the class kinda sucked the fun out of drawing because we did nothing but life drawings day after day.
He is a good painting instructor... i only wish we did more paintings and spent less time on less significant ones.
Ron is very helpful, very knowledgeable, and can always make you laugh.  Low-key, relaxed, professional, an awesome teacher, makes you work hard while enjoying it.  You learn a lot with Ron :)!
One of the sweetest, most helpful people in the world.  Would do  anything to help his students.  TAKE HIS CLASS! You will not be disappointed.  Go Ron!
One of the nicest, most gentle natured professors I've ever had.  He knows more about mixing colors than is humanly possible.

This is a warning do NOT take this class if you want your final to be an 8-10 page paper. I'm saving you the stress and the sleepless nights now it's not worth it, unless you have fun with writing papers please go right ahead but don't set yourself up for failure. Easy class but atrociously boring to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Eh, he's okay...he never moves the discussion along so you end up spending way too many days on certain readings and not a lot of time on others. picks some pretty complex materials, likes class discussions, class doesn't take much effort and the only real work required is 3 papers a semester. if you're good at writing, it'll be very easy for you.
Good Teacher

He's a fine teacher.  If you put in a litte effort to the class you'll get at least a B.  Class is very boring, (maybe it's cuz i hate philosophy) but he's pretty easy grading papers.  The readings are not too hard nor too easy, but do require an OAK discussion board entry after each reading which gets old very quick.
He was great at showing me how the ideas in the class mattered in the world.  An interesting class, even if some of the readings are more difficult than would be expected in a 100 class.
This was my favorite class last semester.  He made the readings interesting without oversimplifying.  He was great to work with on my papers.  I loved this class!
He was great in keeping me interested and helping when was having a hard time writing.  He helped me a lot and is a good professor

This class was a disaster--he does not seem confident enough with his ideas to handle dispute well and does not encourage discussion. For a class of 20 there was way too much lecturing and not enough encouraged thought. If you like long, boring lectures instead of lively debate, take this class. If not, don't!

He is awesome.  At times he was hard to follow, but he spent as much time as needed in conferences to get through hard stuff (especially Nietzsche).  I have switched my major to philosophy after his class.

This guys class is about as cool as Barry Bonds enormous cranium.  Ahern is a pretentious non master.  He would be well served to learn a thing or two about capitalism.  HOwever, he is absolutely gorgeous and quite pleasong to the eye!!

He's a pretty hard grader if you put any of your own thoughts in your essay. Resay your notes from the class on your paper and youll probably do well. He didnt explain himself very well, and class discussion was limited to him talking to the class. It was very boring.

Like another poster said, it's hard to do well if you don't go to class.  However, even if you do, you're not guarenteed a good grade.  Take detailed notes during class and then rehash whatever he said in paper form to do well in this course.

This guy's class is very easy. All you have to do is write some **** papers and make it to class b/c he takes attendance. He is willing to talk outside of class pretty much any time. Going to class sucks because he is very boring, but if you don't your grade will suffer.
I took him for lab, and he did a good job logistically and in setting clear expectations. Also very interesting to talk to.
I like the dad jokes he makes during lectures. He is very knowledgeable about the material he is presenting and provides many opportunities to understand it. It was a really enjoyable class.

Dr. Daniel is the best professor to take for CHEM 1601. He is an anime nerd and is hilarious but also very knowledgable about chemistry and genuinely cares about the students. The class was a bit awkward as it was an 8am but still very good. Make sure to show up for TopHat bonus points. He can be a bit grouchy in lab though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty good class and prof, most I've ever learned in Chem. Sooo much homework beware of aktivs and tests are very high weight.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Daniel for lab, and he was good at communicating and graded fairly. Chem lab is challenging and time-consuming, but he made it somewhat easier to stomach.
Tough for no reason. This guy makes me not interested in Chemistry anymore. I got good grades in exams but it was too much pain.

Dr. Daniel is great, but the class just isn't that good. He is very nice and helpful, but this lab is just so much work for 1-credit. Long reports, hard final. An engaging professor in an unengaging lab course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof who explained things very clearly & prepared us well for the exams. Accessible in office hours to answer any questions. Always on track (while some other profs fell behind). Was definitely spoiled having him for my first pre-med class at Vanderbilt.

Daniel is a great professor. Chem is always going to be challenging but he truly cares about his students and wants to help them succeed. Loved the way he has fill in the blank slides (definitely recommend an iPad or something you can download the slides on to be able to keep up). Ask him for help and he will always help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel wants each student to succeed as an individual. Gen chem is hard as it is. He is willing to meet with students outside of class and office hours. Take Dr. Daniel for gen chem!!!!

hardest class ive ever taken in my life. so much work its insane. i didn't learn one thing in class i had to teach myself everything. the class is taught like I have already taken AP Chem which I hadn't.

Dr. Daniel is a funny and kind professor. Even though it can be tough to get up for 8:00 am class, extra credit opportunities are given at the start of every class. He posts lectures and notes in Brightspace in case you miss a class period. Lectures are definitely at a fast pace, but he makes sure to go over everything needed for exams.

Daniel made very clear slides for every lecture, and you can simply grasp all the information needed from his slides. There are also bonus credits from tophat and some surveys. The worst part is to get up at 7:30 am to get to his lectures. Definitely recommend this guy, and he is very smart.

Dr. Daniel is an amazing professor and very accessible outside of class. His office hours are extremely helpful and replies to emails very quickly. You can tell he genuinely wants his students to succeed.

hes actually pretty good. explains things in a way where you can understand things in a more intuitive way rather than through memorization. theres bonus points every class, which you can get up to 15 points of. they weigh pretty heavily to the final grade (if you get 15/15, you need 15 less points on the final to get the same final grade).

You can tell Prof. Daniel cares about his students and their understanding of the material. Very accessible outside of class and he makes sure you understand the concept rather than memorizing it. He gets through the material faster than the other chem professors which I appreciated. Don't skip class or you miss out on a huge amount of extra credit

Despite his section being at 8 AM, Daniel is probably one of the better professors to take for 1601. Todd has extra resources but can be mean at times, and the other professors are usually behind on material. Overall, he is a nice and approachable guy, just make sure to read the syllabus before asking him questions (he gets annoyed).
Dr. Daniel has been so helpful!! Definitely worth the 8 AMs :) Go to every lecture since he gives out extra credit!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel is great and more than willing to help students. Attending office hours helped tremendously. The lectures are relatively fast, but he is willing to explain things during office hours. There is extra credit every morning, so go to lecture. Gen Chem is difficult especially for those who didn't take AP Chem, but Dr. Daniel is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wants his students to do well. Kind and funny, would take him again nest sem if I could. Highly recommend. Goes a bit faster than other profs, but gives a review day before each exam and a free day after.

Prof. Daniel is a great teacher! I loved his class; his lecture and problems helped out a lot when it came time to take the tests and the final. His office hours are also very helpful and he genuinely wants you to do well.

Prof. Daniel is very kind. I never took chemistry, but his lectures and notes made it understandable. He is very helpful in his office hours and will take the time to teach the material to you till you understand it. He offers extra credit at the beginning of each lecture through TopHat. He is very engaging and wants you to succeed.

Dr. Daniel is an excellent professor. His slides and notes are by far the best of any of the Gen Chem professors, and his class is usually the only one to get a whole day dedicated to review before exams. TopHat questions for extra points at the start of each class, so going to lecture is worth it. Moves fast in lecture but is very helpful.

He's funny and definitely cares about his students (Todd can be mean). He does go fast, which can be hard if you've never taken chem before, but he can be slowed down by asking questions. There does seem to be a little bit of a communication issue between professors, so make sure you read the textbook before an exam, not just his lecture notes!

I loved Professor Daniels teaching style, he gives relevant practice questions and is engaging. If you read the textbook and show up to class, you will do well. He gives TopHat questions at the begining of most lectures so attendance is mandatory.

I personally think Daniel's the best Gen Chem lecturer at Vandy. (Todd's mean.) Daniel engagingly presents practice problems, both guided and unguided. Always starts the class with TopHat, so sadly you lose extra credit if late. Office hours are inconsistent (went twice, he wasn't there once) but he's a great one-on-one explainer when available.
Although he lectures fast, he can be easily slowed down by student questions in the lecture. If you have any questions, just ask him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Daniel is a great professor, funny, and relatable. He knows that the material is not easy and is always free to meet outside of class. His office hours helped a ton and I felt like he always wanted us to do well. Yes, he does teach faster but the way he teaches is more understandable than any teacher I've had for chem. Underrated

Professor Daniel is incredibly knowledgeable about chemistry and very available over email or office hours. People say he moves fast but he actually gets through the material covered on the exams and leaves room for an in class review day as opposed to other professors who finish exam content the day before or day of the exam. Take him!

Chem 1601 tests are the same for all students. Important to read the textbook before class so that you can answer the TopHat (Extra Creds) right. Drill down on the lectured material, as it is tested heavily. Also, you NEED to go to Dr. Todd's review sessions to review information. For tests, multiple choices are a killer tricky, so BE CAREFUL!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chemistry is a hard class; that does not change regardless of who the professor is.  Professor Daniel does teach faster than the other professors which can be difficult if you do not understand what is going on.  However, it is nice to have extra time to review for the tests. I would definitely take him again.

I don't get the Daniel slander!! He's such a wholesome and nice guy. He DOES go faster than the other profs, but that gives the class extra time for studying and review days. He's the most accessible teacher I've seen and will answer emails/offer a quick office hour SO fast. Gen chem is hard no matter which prof you have. Recommend him 100%!
Pretty good lecturer, very accessible outside of class and always extremely responsive to emails

He was honestly a great professor for chemistry. I know that his teaching style didn't complement a lot of other students, and I will say that he did kinda just read from his PowerPoints sometimes, but between the lectures, the readings, and the homework I was able to understand the concepts and the math pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content wasn't difficult because of the professor. It was more of a reflection of the Chemistry department as a whole. Prof. Daniel had lectures that were engaging and gave us the content we needed. He kept a good pace, but it was faster compared to the other professors.

If you're coming with no chem background, especially if you didn't take AP Chem, DO NOT take this prof. He assumes everyone has taken AP chem and never starts from the basics. If you don't already know most of the stuff, you'll be lost. He goes over content way too fast, so it's hard to learn in detail. Would not recommend.

One of the WORST professors I have ever had!!!!!!!!! Does not give out worksheets or support like Tara Todd does. Okay at explaining in office hours but in terms of lecture, he crams so much content in such little time. People who did well in this course spent HOURS studying a day. If you do not have a good chemistry background. GOOD LUCK CHARLIE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chem is just a difficult class regardless of who you take with. Reading in addition to going to lecture is very helpful and Daniel is a good prof. He does move quickly through material which can be difficult especially compared to a professor like Todd. If I could do it again I'd probably take with Todd, but Daniel is a solid choice.

This is the known scare of Gen Chem at Vanderbilt. Professor Daniel is a caring and kind professor. However, he does lecture fast and on one occasion I felt like I was being judge during office hours because I failed my first exam. He does seem like a genuine professor that cares for you! Be prepared to work for a good grade!

Professor Daniel is ok. He responds quickly to emails and makes his office hours well known. The problem is his lectures are WAY TOO FAST. We once started class 10 min late due to technical difficulties and we somehow still finished all of the lecture slides in the same 50 minutes. I haven't heard good things about his office hours. Take Todd.

I ended up dropping Gen Chem, but I really liked Dr. Daniel. He was always quick to respond to my emails, even with his hundreds of students. I found his lectures/powerpoints more clear and concise than Dr. Todd's. Dr. Daniel is a great guy.

I really liked Dr. Daniel. I will say that you have to do the readings he assigns to do well. It's a lot of self-study and self-teaching. The tests are extremely challenging and he could definitely give more examples of problems in class. That being said, I think he's a better option than many other of the 1601 profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely HORRIBLE! He doesn't know how to explain his own content but expects the students to understand. Stay away from his section or your mental health will be withered
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Reads off slides and not very engaging. Other professors went through many practice questions and gave many examples before the homework was due, but Dr. Daniel's class makes you mainly self study.

He is a good chem1601 professor, but his lectures do read exactly from the book and he reads from the slides, so the work for the class is mostly on your own anyways. He does answer emails and is helpful.
One of the nicest lecturer in the Chemistry department. Explains the materials super well and genuinely cares about your grade. If you see him listed in any classes TAKE HIM.
I had Dr. Daniel as my senior capstone lab instructor. He cares about his students, understands their situation(s), and is always willing to make himself available to help outside of class.

Dr. Daniel is an amazing professor! His lectures were always very clear, and he always made sure to answer any questions. Make sure to go to office hours! He was always willing to explain textbook questions, provide more examples, etc. He answered questions via email and the online discussion board as well. One of my favorite professors so far!

Dr. Daniel is a fine professor honestly. I didn't go to any office hours this semester, so I can't really say I got to know him very well. His lectures were typical and he gave information fine. He provided examples that were helpful and always answered questions even if they were dumb.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chem's tough, but Dr. Daniel is a competent and good lecturer. Assignments are clear and well communicated. Clearly understands the subject matter very well, and teaches it well too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Daniel was very accommodating for his students this semester and made gen chem bearable. This course is pretty standard between professors so with any section you will have a lot of homework to do and will need to put in the work, but Dr. Daniel definitely gave you the resources needed to be successful.

Dr. Daniel is a wonderful and caring professor who genuinely wants his students to succeed. As of 2020, there are extra credit pop-quizzes at the start of class to beware of. I really appreciated how Dr. Daniel consistently emphasized real world applications of the content we were learning!
Pro: good and kind prof, answers questions, cares about students Con: hard final, concepts don't really make sense, long and tough lab reports (think 10ish pages), hard weekly lab quizzes
Her ppt slides cover all the necessary materials, and tests are easy all tests have fun extra credit problems--just think with logic :) She is really caring and fun.

She's so nice and cool. One test was really hard but the others were easy if you studied and did the homework. It's not a super easy-A but it's definitely one of those classes where if you don't do well it's kind of on you.
Awesome class! Looked forward to it every week
awesome class.
Best engineering prof I've had at Vandy. Made Thermo seem easy if you do the work and a couple practice problems before each tests. Very fair tests and clear lectures.
Come to the class and you will make it. Believe me.
He is really great and cares about his student!!! Explain well and wants everyone to score his tests. Really helpful :)

Nasab is very nice however you don't learn much going to lecture.  Doing the HW is how you learn the material.  As attendance goes down he starts giving extra credit quizzes that add points to your tests.  He makes it easy to get an A and test questions are usually straight from HW problems.

Nasab is the nicest dude.  I had him for Environmental Control (ME elective).  He realizes its an elective so grades easy.  Very interesting and practical knowledge in the course.  Nasab knows his stuff and is passionate about it and very understanding.  Only complaint is that since no book, he comes up with HW probs and they are sometimes unclear.

Great professor, very easy class. Walks you through the weekly homework assignment during the lecture. If you have done any CAD before it is a BREEZE. If not, it takes a little to get comfortable with the software but still easy. Can't imagine not getting an A. Great for learning CAD basics, skills are mostly transferable to any CAD software

Great teacher who wants you to do well.  He usually doesn't take attendance but he pays attention and if people start skipping he'll randomly take it.  Teaches out of the book, very straightforward homework and tests.
The best Proffesor ever! He teaches the course really well and cares a lot about his students. Give extremely easy test, extra credit and great understanding of the material. Getting A is a must!

He is a  very understanding professor who really wants the students to do well.  For tests we got to use the textbook, our computers, and an equation sheet.  He made the final optional if you want to improve your grade.  Wants to keep the class interested and cares about how the class is doing.  Definitely worth taking even at 8 am.
No Comments

Lectures were really boring and hard to follow-- I learned by reading the textbook and doing the homework, so attending class was optional. Your final grade is based only on 3 tests and the final so you can't screw up on those. The tests were pretty easy-- very similar to the homework questions. 2400 was definitely a step down from 1301.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ahner is rude but can be pretty funny at times. Material is challenging but tests are relatively easy and very predictable. All your grades come from tests which normally come straight from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: For multi I would recommend because the tests aren't hard (compared to the other multi teachers I think) but you have to just teach yourself. Like his teaching really did not help just read the textbook, use slader and youtube to figure out hw, and the tests are exactly like the hw. Not a great prof but not a terrible class, just don't his help

Lectures aren't great and usually consist of him writing definitions from the textbook. I usually didn't even go. Your grade is solely based on exams, but the tests are super straightforward and exactly like homework problems. Not a bad choice if you're good at math and can figure it out on your own

As a teacher, Ahner is absolutely useless. He might know his stuff, but clearly is not the best in the pedagogical methods (i.e. he's trash). On the up side, however, his tests are all homework questions and calculators are allowed. On the down side, his tests are graded harshly, and account for 100% of your class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ahner is a smart man, but he definitely doesn't teach much in class. His lectures are nothing more than writing the definitions from the textbook up on the board, and then going over 1 example. Granted, that would be enough, if he explained anything further than that. But he doesn't. Just going off the book is just as good as going to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Your grade is only the tests but the tests really are not difficult. The test averages have always been a B or A but you have to do well on them because there is no grade boost here. As long as you do the homework which is not graded you will do well
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ahner is fine with lectures until he gets to the more difficult topics of Multivariable Calcalus. It was a fine experience, but the fact that your only grades are test grades is a little stressful. The final will bump your grade down.

He lets you use whatever calculator you want on exams, which is huge. Your average in class is just the average of your 4 exam grades. Attendance is totally optional, and he gives you all the HW assignments (all of which are from the textbook) on the syllabus. Overall, avoid 2300 if you can, but if you have to take it, Ahner isn't a bad option.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sweetest man you'll ever meet- make sure to show up to class and ask questions if you have them. One test is dropped, and it is clear that he wants everyone to succeed. Difficult to reach outside of class, but has not changed his tests in years and they are very predictable. Easy A if you can get old tests/study efficiently. Just go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I like Ahner. He's a good guy and genuinely wants his students to do well. That being said, his class is not easy to do well in if you aren't good at tests. You do get a drop, but tests are worth 100% of your grade (no HW and no quizzes). The tests are straightforward, but the format is such that a small mistake can totally screw your grade over.

Very dry lectures that honestly are not helpful at all. I read the textbook and I learned everything I needed to. Do the optional HW and understand the sheets he gives in class and you will do well ( tests are just copied from these problems). The class is 3 tests and a final and that is your grade. Typically a page of T/F and 3-4 open response

Lecture-wise, he's pretty straight to the point (though I found the material itself hard to follow sometimes). However, if you aren't a good test-taker, don't take him; grades are determined solely by midterms/final (though you do get to drop one). Test difficulty are roughly the same as (optional)hw and his in-class examples

ugh.. I definitely regret taking his class. I am not the type of person who's good at tests. So this class is killing me since it only has test grades. Also the tests r not hard, but u can not make any mistake at all which is like hell to me. Some people find it easy. But if anyone is like me, avoid.  I am a math major... but this is the worst .

Four tests and a final mean that you have nearly 0 margin for error in the course. Test problems themselves are not difficult, but the multiple choice questions are tricky and super easy to miss 10 or more points on.

four tests and the final make up your entire grade. tests are not very easy but you do get to drop one. class moves quickly. if you cannot make it to a test for any reason, you cannot make it up and that counts as your drop.
Do the daily homework and ask him about the ones you couldn't figure out. If you are consistent with this, you will definitely get an A.
He is a bit dry, although his jokes do bring a smile to the face. The class and tests are straightforward, and one can tell Dr. Ahner knows his stuff. A genuine guy and a nice class.

Did not provide intuitive explanations (e.g. geometric) of concepts like delta-epsilon proofs, partials, curl/divergence, etc., which are essential to understanding what the math actually means. Instead, focused on memorization. Tests were predictable, easy: 10 T/F, 4-5 free response from HW or handouts. He is fine if you already understand MVC.

His lectures are not very clear and are easily supplemented by reading the textbook because he follows the textbook exactly.  Tests are fair but they are easy to get a B or worse by making any mistake on a single free response question.  His non-mandatory homework is very helpful as test prep.  All that said, it was an enjoyable class.
Homework is not graded. Tests are ok but if you are wrong in 1 problem, your grade will be super low

Boring and annoying lectures. His jokes were pretty funny at first. But after a week, they became lame and extremely annoying. His tests are okay, quite predictable. You'll probably learn a little from his class though. But overall, he's a nice professor.

Class is too easy. T/F on exams sometimes throw people off, but if you pay attention to detail (definitions and theorems), they aren't bad. Actual problems on the tests are of equal difficulty to the hw, so you know what to expect. Doesn't like ppl who don't attend class, and he usually refuses to help you in his office if you miss class regularly.

Class is a joke. The tests are easy and based on memorizing the book.Dont count on Ahner teaching you anything though, he just spends his time lecturing you about the rest of your life. And should you dare to ask an interesting question will be shot down. Skip class and teach yourself. If you never need d.e. again take it. If you are a major avoid!
If you are a hard-working type A student, don't take this class.

Lectures are very dry, not much easier to understand than the book. No homework or quizzes. Tests are super easy. Calculators permitted. Good class if you just want an easy A and don't care if you learn anything. Otherwise, it's probably too easy.

Ahner gives lectures that are basically a repetition of what is in the book.  Do the homework, don't bother going to class, and you'll be fine.  It gets annoying though when he says "I can't give you an answer to that question." Only the annoying girl with the high-pitched voice ever got a straight answer from him the entire semester.  Easy A.
go to class, do the homework and it's easy
He's a straightforward teacher. His tests are no more difficult than the homework. Go to class. Do the homework. Ask questions if you don't understand, and you will do fine.

Ahner is a great teacher. Go to class, pay attention and if you have questions ask them, he'll answer without hesitation. Tests aren't that hard, make sure to study what he tells you to, plus you get to drop a test.

As it goes, Math 229 was a pretty easy upper level math course.  The first half is a repeat of 175 and the second is complex number analysis.  Calculators allowed on all exams.  There is no curve, but tests are straight forward and fair (you know exactly what to expect on them).  Homework is not collected, but you need to do it to understand...
Professor Ahner is an awesome math instructor and is truly hilarious.  If you disagree, then step outside and fight me!

Stay away.  I'm a straight A math student, but failed the first two tests.  I tried to learn the material by going to office hours several times a week, but he simply refuses to answer questions.  Horrible experience, horrible professor.
Good teacher...do the work, and you'll be fine...dont do the work and you'll be punished.  Fair grader and if you seek help out of class he will help.
Tests are based solely on class examples (no surprises).  He is a very straightforward teacher, but tends not to help outside of class so as to not give anyone an unfair adavantage.

One of the best DE professors you can get!  Go to class!  I wanted to kill him sometimes for always saying that we had to "drill, drill, drill" but his tests are based on examples done in class and they are easy.  I got 100's on a couple of the tests without doing any homework.

I lost count of the number of times I felt like jumping over my desk to strangle him, but all in all he wasn't that bad of a teacher.  He gives next to now partial credit and doesn't curve. He did a good job explaining the material, and his tests were the homework problems he assinged and was willing to go over in class.

No help outside of class, regardless of how often you go to office hours.  If you don't understand the material, you're screwed, because he doesn't explain it and the book definitely doesn't.  He doesn't like to answer questions and I've often felt scared to ask them in class.
No Comments
Learn alot if you put in the time and effort.
Great teacher! Makes sure you understand the concepts before moving on. He's helpful and his exams are very fair. Kinda eccentric, but kept me interested and entertained in an 8AM
He is the fairest teacher I have ever had.

he is too afraid of getting his ass sued to be a good professor.  he has office hours, but won't help you during them because he thinks it's not fair that the other students aren't getting the same help, so you leave angry and just as stupid as when you showed up.
Not helpful at all.  Actually discouraged me from taking classes I liked and never helped me in choosing a major.
No required homework, no quizes, and his tests are straightforward if you have done the work, often much shorter than other professors for the same class.
Best math professor I've had at Vanderbilt.
ugh.  boring.  and he tells us the same stories about playing the piano and the football team EVERY DAY!  and i don't think that he knows that he already told us the stories...
