This guy explains stuff as he quickly writes it on the board.  You can't listen and write down what he's putting on the board.  He moves so fast that you can't just listen and then catch up w/ what's on the board.  Didn't like him at all.

Ahner is great.  I specifically waited for him to teach advanced calc to take it.  Homework is optional, as it should be, and you learn the stuff.  All math classes should be like his.  Only problem is that I think he's a little depressed, but he's great.

Professor Ahner is an awesome teacher.  He is tough but fair.  He is willing to help any student who puts forth an effort.  Be forewarned, however, if you do not go to class (and do not have an excuse), he will no explain the material you missed.
No Comments
No Comments

Dr. Hamraie is a wonderful professor and kind human being. Their work in politics and activism brings a refreshing perspective to the lectures, and leads them to choose really interesting course material/readings.

This class was super fun and interesting. The class discussions are the most meaningful and important parts. Dr. Hamraie is super accommodating, flexible, and receptive. The class is based on a few short papers, group projects, and a journal at the end. The readings can be long but aren't entirely required and they are interesting.

Super interesting class with a lot of eye opening points and ideas. Would recommend this class to anyone. A few papers, some projects, and a final journal. Very accessible outside of class and very kind. Intriguing readings as well

I took Prof. Hamraie's class a year ago, and the things I learned in it keep coming back to me in other classes. They're one of the most unique professors I've had at Vandy, and their activist work outside of academia really added to the depth of the class. They're very accessible, and super kind. Your world view will definitely be expanded.

Dr. Hamraie is incredible and the assignments are easy if you put in the effort. They're super accessible when you need help, definitely don't hesitate to reach out to them. Theories of the Body is also super interesting for people who like to be reflective about themselves and society. The class is what you make out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Aidan is probably the best professor for Math 1300. His tests are fair and doable (especially compared to other Calc 1 professors). There are some graded problem sets, but textbook problems are optional. Aidan was always available outside of class and willing to help. His lectures go a bit fast, but this made us ahead of other classes on content.

As far as math professors go, Aidan is pretty much the best. He is a good lecturer, pretty reasonable, and quite nice. The tests were hard towards the end but he is probably the best math professor I've ever had. Wayyyy better than average Vandy math professor. Aidan is a gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Aidan was such a gem of a professor. He was approachable, clear and reasonable. He's a really cool guy as well! Fun to talk to! The tests are also very doable and within the scope of the class. Would 100% recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Valeriano Aiello cares a lot about his students. Since this is his first time teaching MATH2300 at Vanderbilt, he may seem a little nervous during classes. However, he is very well prepared with his class by providing very neat notes for understanding the course materials. He is also very accessible and very willing to answer your questions.

He's a quiet guy but he knows his stuff, sometimes he can't explain it very well though. His tests are hard but he lets you make test corrections and tells you exactly what you did wrong if you go see him during office hours.

If you don't want to read the textbook, don't take this class. He is an extremely new prof, that struggles to answer student's questions, and very awkward and nervous. very smart, and he wants to help you figure out the material. His lectures aren't too bad, he doesn't do a lot practice problems, just a few to get the jist. his test policy is great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Valeriano is a good choice for 2300. He gives a lot of extra credit and opportunities to compensate mistakes. His lectures are somewhat dry, so you'll need to read the textbook to get a good grade, but HWs and tests aren't very hard.

Professor Aiello is soft spoken and teaches the necessities before doing examples. Overall grade was based on take home quizzes, exams, and an optional final. Exam problems sometimes involved unnecessary algebra, but he graded leniently and allowed us to rework problems to get a few points back.

Multivariable in Vanderbilt is notorious. Department policy is to try force an average between 2.6 - 3.1. This guy helps you out relentlessly. He gives infinitely many opportunities to make up for missing work, gives more than fair exams and if per chance he makes them a bit harder than intended - you can fix your mistakes for next class for points

Professor Aiello teaches essentially nothing in class and your only hope is reading the whole textbook yourself in the two days before the exam. Expect a quiz every night on material he barely taught as well. He's very quiet and not super helpful in office hours. He also answers most questions by saying "I don't know." Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and makes lectures fun and interesting. Definitely take a class with Professor Aikin if you can.

HES AWESOMEE
Very funny in lecture, don't be intimidated by his pacing of the room its super engaging 
The grading is super chill and the TAs are awesome too. 
Hes very sweet

The class was more difficult than I expected. You really have to have a good understanding of the material for quizzes, but he does provide question banks to study prior to each quiz. You probably shouldn't take this class if you are just looking for easy AXLE credit, however, it is rewarding if you have any interest in the subject material.

Not bad but could have been better. Heard amazing things but got the feeling he was harder on students this semester. He isn't always the most approachable and not really receptive to feedback. Told us randomly a week before the final there was a new passage recognition section but never mentioned it before that, tougher course than expected
LOVE THIS MAN TAKE HIM. Took this class to fill a random liberal arts requirement and it was hands down my favorite class to go to. He is so funny and so interesting, you will NOT regret it.
Passionate and hilarious lecturer. Everything is graded off 3 quizzes and two papers. Don't need to come to class to do well but most do anyways. Fire emoji

Prof Aikin is an amazing lecturer who is passionate about philosophy and is great at breaking down complicated topics for beginners. Quizzes are easy to prepare for since there's a question bank to study and papers are pretty straightforward. Readings might be tedious to someone uninterested in philosophy but it's really not that much reading.

Professor Aikin is wonderful! I have taken 2 of his classes and I am about to take a third. He makes lectures more fun than you could possibly imagine and gets everyone so excited about the topic of philosophy.

He's genuinely so funny and nice. Although attendance is not mandatory, it helps immensely with understanding. He is also so sweet and approachable. The class is only based on 4 quizzes and 2 papers, and for the quizzes, he releases questions in advance! Papers are easier to write after knowing his expectations, but the class isn't hard at all.
It's not that easy
He's a cool dude just wish he stayed on topic more often. Definitely a harder class so make sure to study or don't take this class if you have a busy semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aikin is a great professor. I've had him before and the material was interesting, but if you do not go to class or keep up with the homework you will not succeed in this course. Tests were easy as long as you studied, but the final was difficult. It was hard to laugh at all of the jokes at 9:00 AM too. Love the man, take him if you can.

Aikin is a funny and engaging professor whose lectures are great. Unfortunately, the class is solely graded off of your performance on the 4 tests. Logic is difficult and the tests require extensive understanding. The tests were extremely difficult, especially the final, so I would only recommend it to those who are confident test takers.

Professor Aikin is a knowledgeable professor and enjoys joking about certain philosophers, especially those in the Hellenistic period. The class was never boring, and I appreciated his passion. Once you understand expectations, the papers are easy to write. The one con is he can fall days behind on lectures. Overall, definitely a great professor.

Dr. Aikin is energetic, humorous and enjoyable in the classroom. His Formal Logic class is difficult, but he put a lot of effort into ensuring students understood the concepts. The class is solely graded based off of exams, so that's something to keep in mind if you're not a test taker. The textbook could be better, but he's a great professor.

What a great prof. Probably the coolest, most energized, and most intelligent profs at Vandy. He loves the material and is insanely good at teaching it. Pretty cool material too. You need to take Aiken at some point at Vandy

Really fun professor if you're into his subject area. He takes his study seriously but not his class if that makes sense. He's really just here to have fun and help you learn. He definitely makes his quizzes and exams super simple, and his papers are equally effortless. If you just show up and listen, you'll be fine.

Aikin is the best. There's a textbook but if you just show up to class and listen (highly recommend going) you don't even need it. Tests have a test bank beforehand and are super straightforward. Class is 4 exams that you'll barely have to study for if you listen in class. He's very funny and makes it worth going to a 9AM.
Expectations are very well communicated. Enjoyable and funny lectures.
2 papers and a couple tests. The test material is given out beforehand. As long as you prepare for it, definitely a very easy A.

Easy A. Engaging material and very passionated lectures. He presented the material in a way that was easy to understand. The best philosophy teacher I had at Vanderbilt. Didn't really study but end up with a solid A.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. It's basically hyroglifics. I went to office hours multiple times a week and studied for hours and it was still so confusing I withdrew. He's a great prof though; material is just like a diff language I stg.

The course starts off pretty easy and then hits some really complex concepts, but Aikin is super accessible and wants to make sure you understand the concepts. He records TikToks and Podcasts where he does more practice problems and explains theories in further detail which makes his material that much more accessible. highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very clear with the grading and exam structures (he gives practice exams too) which is a big plus since final grade is determined solely by exams. Dr. Aikin is hilarious and always tries his hardest to get his students engaged with the class material. Not a super easy A but very doable. Def recommend going to class and doing the practice problems.
Chill class, Professor Aikin is pretty funny and the class is definitely an easy A. 10/10.

Grading is based solely off of two tests and a final exam. Aikin is a super engaging lecturer, but the course content itself is pretty heavy. Most times we don't get through all the objectives in class. Successful students attend lecture, do the homework, and go to office hours when necessary. Not an easy class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Aikin is one of the most engaging professors I've had at Vanderbilt, especially for a 100+ person MWF 9 AM class. He so obviously knows his stuff, and is very patient with his students - even when they ask and repeat questions throughout lecture. He makes the information as entertaining as possible and is super funny. 3003 is no joke though.

Professor Aikin is very intelligent while also being great at clearly explaining concepts. He's also funny and honest, which makes lectures interesting. You can tell he cares about his students. I recommend attending lectures because they made much more sense than the book.

Aikin is an extremely nice and easy going guy. He's a great lecturer and is easy to follow. Class is 3 tests (20% each) and a cumulative final (40%). Attendance isn't mandatory which is nice, but a double edged sword. The class really picks up in difficulty towards the end but if you go to class it's pretty simple and straightforward. Great prof.
Professor Aikins is super funny and makes his lectures interesting. Attendance isn't required but make sure to catch up cuz the material does add up at the end.

He's a great teacher. Attendance is not mandatory but his lectures are entertaining and will help you do well on the tests. Few things are graded and the essays are worth most of your grade but he's a fairly easy grader.
Great teacher overall. He was my first philosophy class at Vanderbilt. Helped me decide on becoming a philosophy major, can't wait to take another class of his
The most amazing philosophy professor I've ever met! He heated the class up and made those difficult concepts easy to understand. Highly recommended.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Would highly recommend taking a course with him.

Aikin is awesome. His class is challenging but you learn a lot and even if you feel like it's hard, it's still possible to do really well. He's a wonderful professor. I'm so glad I took his class and got to have him before I graduate.
humorous lectures that hold your attention. An amazing person and passionate teacher

Great guy, good class. Definitely gets harder as time goes on, and if you take it you should definitely do practice proofs from the book. Tests are straightforward (proofs at the end can be hard) and he even gives practice tests that are very similar to the actual tests. Class graded only on 3 tests and a final so the test grades are important.

Aikin is good at teaching and provides a lot of extra material like practice tests and podcasts on the textbook content. I took general logic prior to formal logic, so half the class was a review  GL isn't necessary to do well, but it helped a lot. This class really is easy if you put in some time to practice and stay on top of the schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you're a normal vandy student who doesn't study for tests until the day before, this class can get tricky towards the end. Sure, the first test is a breeze. But the material gets more difficult right after and if you don't read and do practice problems during the week then your cramming sessions will be stressful. Not easy A but attainable.

TAKE FORMAL LOGIC!! aikin is funny and brilliant and although rated as a 3003 class it's really not that difficult. perfect class for those who liked math in high school but got wrecked by vanderbilt calc. aikin is engaging and helpful and really helps hammer home the topics. he tries to keep tests around an 89% class avg so not too hard at all.

Wonderful professor! The lectures are inspirational, and tests are super easy. Dr. Aikin in fact tries every way to help you do better in this courses. He is also humorous and very accessible outside class. 100% worths taken. (The only thing I'm not crazy about is the textbook. I believe that Klenk's logic rules are way too superfluous)

Enjoyable logic class with this engaging professor. If you are looking to decide between this and general logic, you would profit much more by choosing Prof. Aikin's course. Lectures are generally straightforward, and if you do the exercises he assigns (but does not collect or grade), the path to high marks is easily navigable.

I had to take Aikin after hearing about him and I DO NOT REGRET IT. Scott Aikin is one of the most respected, well-known, kind professors at Vanderbilt. He's crystal clear and straight forward and wants you to do well. Formal Logic ended up being one of the most entertaininginteresting classes I've ever taken.  3 tests and a final, very doable A.

Prof Aikin is extremely enthusiastic and makes logic interesting! General logic isn't necessary for the course (I took it as a first semester freshman). His tests and grading are fair, and if you go to the lectures (which are usually entertaining) you can expect a pretty good grade

Ditto previous comment. Great teacher, knows his stuff and makes logic as interesting as you can possibly make logic. Tests are fair, there is literally no reading or work if you pay attention in class, so taking this class will help your other grades too. If logic is not your thing be careful, it can be a hard class.

Great class, great prof. If you're taking logic, esp. if it's just for a math credit, take Aikin. Formal Logic seems intimidating, but he makes it accessible. If you pay attention in class, you don't have to do a lot out of class to do well. 5 quizzes and a final, no attendance, participation, or homework grades.

Pretty nice guy, makes lots of bad jokes in class but he's fun to listen to. Don't make the mistake of skipping class - he doesn't take attendance, but everything is way easier to learn if you just take the time to sit there. Grade is four tests, with some built-in extra credit in there. Solid teacher, solid guy.
Incredible teacher.  Engaging and entertaining.  Attendance is not mandatory but it is helpful since his lessons are clear. Study/use the practice tests and you should be fine!
Great class. Don't need to go, very helpful. Study for tests and you will be fine

Absolutely brilliant professor.  Course structure is great as well: only 4 tests worth 25% each, and his teaching mirrors the textbook completely, so you really don't even need to go to class if you keep up with the reading.  The first test was challenging, but I finished with a 98 average in the class after only going to maybe 1/3 of the lectures.

Aikin was the ultimate man.  He gave homework but it was not graded and attendance  was not mandatory.  Not only did he give practice tests and hold review sessions before each test, but his actual tests were pretty easy as well if you study.  Plus, class is extremely entertaining because he's hilarious.

Amazing professor who is deeply passionate about philosophy and the use of good logic and really cares about his students. BTW the tests as of fall '10 are no longer open note/book/takehome. They are given in class bc of retards who cheated before. STUDY HARD for the first test on prop logic and go to REVIEW SESSIONS!Attendance is NECESSARY for A/B

there are 4 tests no other grades. he puts the test online and due the next time class meets, so you can use your notes and the book to complete. also he does not take roll. he even makes a podcast to put on oak summarizing his lecture. however, watch out for the first exam; all those resources and still bombed it; the subsequentexams aremucheasier
A beacon of teaching brilliance against the backdrop of my other, less competent professors this semester.

Great teacher, at first I thought philosophy would be an easy A, but Scott got me interested in it so much it'll be my minor. Willing to discuss thoughts, great sense of humor, and great reading assignments. I wish he were a full time prof at my campus. Scott, you are happily remembered and sorely missed...assuming my memory does not deceive.
Scott is awesome. His enthusiasm gets everyone excited about philosophy. Very fair, very entertaining.

He is a very passionate teacher, excited about philosophy, which is great!  I  came into the course, just needing to fulfill and AXLE requirement, but it has been a fabulous class.  I highly recommend him.  He is very willing to discuss philosophy or whatever with you.  He is very available, very intelligent, and he makes the material come alive.

He's very passionate about what he does, which makes his class more interesting. I highly recommend him, but he's not the easiest grader. He can be very picky, but don't let that turn you away from his classes. I give him two thumbs up.
This man is hysterical.  He gets so fired up when he's teaching that he sweats insanely.  Great teacher and he really loves logic...highly recommend the class!

Excellent TA. He made class very interesting and the work was not too bad as long as you read the materials. He was always very helpful whenever something in the big lecture didn't make sense. Overall, excellent class.

Chat is the only way to make it through this class because the homework and final project requires lots of functions he doesn't teach. He does encourage the use of AI on outside assignments but this makes tests difficult because you can't use AI on them. Akos is a fine professor but the class itself is pretty boring.

As someone with no coding experience, I really struggled in the beginning. Lectures are fast and can be dense, but he offers weekly recitations with the TAs every week. Homework assignments and project (can use ChatGPT) boost your grade a lot. Overall, not bad, just difficult for a beginner or if coding/logic isn't intuitive to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: He has an accent but still easy to understand. His tests are doable if you study (can use the class handbook during them), and we're allowed to use ChatGPT on homework and the final project. He's also nice, e.g. added 10% to a test for lots of participation and has an optional final exam if it helps your grade. (I had no CS experience before, btw)
Easy A. As someone who had never coded before, everything we learned was super intuitive and easy to follow. Plus, he now allows/encourages you to use ChatGPT for assignments and the final project.

He is the best Computer Science professor I have ever had. He would often tie concepts in MATLAB to real world applications that he helped in developing and was nice to the students. The first exam is the hardest since it is on paper, but the next two exams are easier. Optional final replaces worst exam score if you get a better score on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Akos is awesome, super nice guy who actually wants you to do well in the class. All the homework assignments are essentially completion (you can keep trying your answers until you get it right) and the exams are the same way, except you just have the class time to do it. Matlab being useful is also a plus.

Lectures are extremely boring. The assignments are of unrealistic difficulty and not explained well. The only way I have any idea what is going on is by spending 4+ hours outside of class per week in recitation with the TAs, plus more time on my own outside of class. If you don't have to take MATLAB, don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very boring class, but he posts lectures, and 2nd/3rd exams are open note, so you don't have to go to class. HW and tests are graded before you even submit. Final project is very difficult and did not relate to class topics much, but he was very helpful if you asked for help. If you have no CS experience- will probably be rough. Final is optional.

Excellent professor, lectures are not too fast and makes sure to answer questions. Exams are reasonable; he gives you plenty of practice to do well on them through homework, recitation, and in-class exercises. The two projects are the most difficult part of this course, but they are definitely doable. Dr. Ledeczi is kind and funny -highly recommend

Akos was great, sometimes hard to understand the lectures but there are also so many tutorials online. Class was very manageable coming from someone who never coded. 5 HW assignments, 3 exams, 1 big project, optional final to replace a bad exam grade

Dr. Ledeczi is funny and likes to have fun in class. The lectures are not very helpful if you just watch the take-home videos and understand them. The beginning of the class is easy, but it ramps up quickly. There are many homework assignments and projects, which take a long time. However, once you solve the problem, you immediately know your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was a hard class but Akos is a great teacher. He goes very fast and as someone who has never programmed before I struggled a lot. You just copy what he codes on the screen. He also has videos before every class that you watch. Exams are like 4-5 questions but 2 right is like a 70%. 2 projects. 5 HWs. Short codes overall. It's def hard to newbies

The class was really difficult. Office hours were very helpful for homework and projects. Introductory computer science is always hard, but I took this after having some other preliminary computer science knowledge, and it was still very difficult. There isn't too much work outside of class, but the work you do have is very difficult.

His lectures are kind of useless. The first test was a lot worse than the rest since it was on paper instead of a real programming test. Homeworks are tedious but very clear. There's one project with pretty unclear instructions. Many problems are worded very poorly is the problem.

In class all you do copy along whatever code he types himself, making it hard to actually learn in class. No code is really explained and even though this is considered an intro level course, it's expected that you already have a basic understanding of coding. Would not recommend if this is your first coding class ever.

If you are a complete newbie to coding DO NOT AND I REPEAT- DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! It is awful for students who struggle with coding or are completely new to it. He's overall a pretty nice professor and does give partial credit on exams(only really matters if you get at least in the 75% ).

Class is a little bit tough at first, but if you pay attention in class and watch the online video lectures, you wont be exposed to material that isn't explained in either of those. Definitely spend time understanding the homework and playing around with the functions of MATLAB and you should be good. He gives tons of partial credit on tests.

I enrolled in this class thinking it as an easy A based on these reviews- it's not. If u have no coding experience & don't think u would be good at it, ur probably right. Dr. Ledeczi as a person is amazing & wants his students to succeed, but it is quite difficult to follow along in class as he goes too fast. I blink and theres 6 new lines of code.

I thought that this class was very difficult and the only reason I got an A was that there were multiple extra credit opportunities. Prof. Ledeczi just types code all of the class and it isn't very engaging or interesting. The tests are hard, the homework is hard, and the projects are hard. Go to office hours bc the TAs are very kind and helpful.

Do not take this class. Even if you are told that you will need matlab later, taking python is much more worth your time. Lectures are just him typing in code on the screen and barely explaning what it means. Tests are moderately difflcult if you have previous coding knowledge but for those who don't I recommend doing anything else.

Not a cs person so the material was new but hes good at explaining problems and goes thru examples in class. Project is hard but he does offer good help during office hours. Overall solid choice for cs for non-cs ppl.

He kinda gives off dad energy. Overall, he's a great teacher however, there is a steep learning curve, so I struggled a bit in the beginning but then it was fine. he assigns a big project at the end of the year, but he and the TA's are more than willing to help you. He gives good coding advice during office hours, tho he might first come off rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Akos actually listens to students feedback and provides insane amount of help sessions and office hours. If you put decent amount of time, you will get good grades. He wants his students to get A's and actually understand MATLAB. This was my first programming/CS, but absolutely loved it. But, you have to start early on projects and studying .

Prof Ledeczi is the goat. I really struggled with this class at the beginning and ended up loving it. His grading is extremely generous and the exam problems are very similar to the ones done in class. 3 midterms, 5 hw assignments, 1 project in-class quizzes. Final was optional and replaces your lowest midterm. Take him, he is funny and understandi

My favorite class this semester despite not being a CS or engineering major! Super accessible and provides a great foundation for coding and MATLAB; starts off slow and easy and picks up toward the end, but in general very beginner-friendly. Not hard if you keep up, do the exercises, and read class highlights/keys. Funny and kind prof, fair grader

Loved his class. Watch the videos as there is quiz at the beginning of class about half of the days. 3 exams with a very generous scale (5 questions, 3 right is an 85). One big project towards the end is very time consuming but fair. Not bad at all for an intro class, and Akos is very knowledgeable and lighthearted. Very nice and fair teacher

Professor Ledeczi is super funny and cares about his students a lot. The lectures were somewhat boring because he mostly just reiterated what was in the assigned video lectures that we watched for homework. However, if you watch and understand the videos, the class should be pretty easy.
Great teacher for MATLAB, make sure to watch the assigned videos and read the class highlights, use the office hours/help sessions for problem sets and before exams.
I would highly recommend taking Professor Ledeczi. The exams were very easy and he truly wants his students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome CS professor. Grading criteria is super clear, and he does his exams on a strange grading scale that reward you for solving easy problems (2 out of 4 problems is an 85, for example). He assumes a little bit of CS background but overall if you go to class and office hours you'll get all the help you need. Definitely should take

Great, funny lectures, tries to add humour to sometimes dry computer science topics. Class has two projects, three exams and an optional final, plus 5 homework assignments. Very clear on due dates and what is expected, study outside of class by actually doing and learning on the homework's and the tests should be fine. Generous grader.

I had Prof Ledeczi for intro to MatLab, and I am so glad I did. He's got a personality to keep students engaged and does a great job explaining the material well. I had no previous programming experience yet felt totally comfortable using the software at the end of the year. He helps you learn by doing in class by following along as he writes code

Ledeczi makes concepts simple enough to understand and gives a lot of practice problems. Lectures can be a little dry and boring. Assignments aren't too difficult and there's a lot of help available if needed. Exams are literally designed to help students get good grades (easy questions worth a lot, hard questions worth very little).

Lectures are difficult to pay attention to, 90% doing practice problems that once you stop paying attention you're lost and its too late to jump back in. Easy enough to teach oneself if willing to put in the work outside of class. His office hours are a lifesaver for homework assignments

Definitely the easier professor, so get a good grade during his half of the semester. Class is a little dry, but he teaches concepts well and is really funny on occasion. You'll still have to pay attention in class and put in some effort, but he is very clear on what to expect on tests. Would show us cool CS research on Fridays which was fun.

Pretty straightforward guy; made intro compsci easy to understand for a first time programmer (though the class itself is pretty easy by itself). While the material is a little dry at times, he's a good lecturer overall. Definitely would take him again.

Akos was very straightforward in class, which was helpful for a first time programmer. His lecture pacing was good. He would also have little 5 minute study breaks that were for the most part entertaining. Would recommend for a first time programming student.

Akos is a pretty good CS professor. Accent is easy to understand. He is a little monotone during his lectures, but you don't have to come to class to make an A. Everything you go over in class is posted online. Overall a decent professor and pretty easy class.

Good professor. Clear in what to do, pretty interesting lectures, and very easy (although to be fair, CS103 is an easy class and we only had him for the first two weeks where we were working with Scratch and not even real programming..). but still, I could tell he is a good professor

This guy ROCKS. He's easy to follow, very helpful outside of class, and will look over your homework/projects and tell you what to fix. Tests are pretty easy, just know how to do the hw problems. He's pretty funny too.

Good teacher, is excited about the material and is pretty easy to follow in class. Good lectures but the real way to do well in his class is to read the textbook which he wrote himself. It's a great textbook and really itemizes what you should know for each test. Tests are fair and representative of the examples in both his lectures and the text.
SO much better than Hamm. Is kind of funny and explains the material thoroughly.
Nice professor, amusing. Tests are fair. Has a lecture summary document that has notes for the entire semester. Class is a joke for people with a background in CS, can get away with skipping often.
He's a really nice, funny guy. I thought I was going to hate this class and he managed to make the material interesting. His tests are almost identical to the practice problems he gives.
I think he is helpful.

I don't understand why he's rated low. I loved this class and learned a lot. If you do all the in-class examples the tests will be fine. I found Prof. Ledeczi to be a good teacher. If you're not interested in the subject it will be boring, but not so much for those who enjoy computer science.
Pretty boring, and fairly incomprehensible. That said, the tests and project in his section are introductory and werent too challenging
Excellent class, excellent professor.  He explains everything thoroughly & genuinely wants you to do well.    Tests are exactly like class, as long as you pay attention...I learned a lot.
No Comments
Extremely passionate and knowledgeable in the subject matter. Always clear and transparent about what to expect on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Aldroubi was one of my favorite teachers this semester. He is sometimes all over the place with lectures, so I relied heavily on the book to clarify concepts. However, he was always extremely helpful in office hours. He really cares about his students, and the tests were extremely fair. Lots of proofs and theorems, but nothing too crazy.
GOAT. Super fun and rewarding class. If you ask him to curve your grade he will at the end of the semester as long you put in effort throughout.

Prepare for a hard but incredibly rewarding class. HW is a lot and very difficult at times, but so much support is given. The class is as easy as it can be for the difficulty of content, and an A is very doable (probably easier grading than 2300). I have never had a more supportive prof, and if you like math and have Aldroubi I highly recommend.

at first may seem a bit overwhelming without any prior knowledge of mutli/linear but the class is laidback, really fun teacher, always super chill, hw is the main focus of the class so attend office hours for an easy a, tests arent hard just review of definitions + proofs from hw + textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very challenging but rewarding course. Collaboration is encouraged. Tests are fair but challenging. Mainly for math majors. Aldroubi is a great teacher, but office hours and discussion are crucial to full understanding of the material. Still my favorite course at Vandy so far.

He's the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. I previously never got above a B in Math, but I ended up with an A on this one. His lectures are fun, and the exams are manageable. The only downside might be that the exams account for 75% of the grade.

Super friendly professor who really cares about his students. However, his lectures can feel fast-paced! It helped me to go over each day's material for about an hour before and after every class. He was also very available and eager to help students during his office hours. Highly recommend Professor Aldroubi if you get the chance to take him!

(This is for MATH 2410) Aldroubi is great. Nice guy and the tests are straightforward. One downside is that tests are 80% of your grade so if you screw up one then you should talk to him. He is reasonable so if you show improvement he will bump your grade up.
He is one of the best professors in the Math Department. His lectures were clear, and the Homeworks and exams were easy. I would definitely suggest anyone to take his class.

Professor Aldroubi wants to see you succeed. He is approachable and loves questions which helps with the learning curve coming from Calc BC. Lectures move fast and can sometimes be unclear, so take thorough notes and heavily review the homework before exams. Form a solid study group since he lets you collaborate on homework. Favorite class by far.

Professor Aldroubi is probably my favorite professor in the Math Department at Vanderbilt. Advanced Linear Algebra with him was awesome, especially because he was so accessible and excited to help in office hours. Light grader, gives great homework help, and cares a lot about your personal/professional life. I sincerely hope I can take him again.

Towards the end of the semester, the lectures can be repetitive. However, this is still a rewarding course that generalizes multivariable theorems in 2300 to n dimensions (and more!). He gives out very easy exams because learning the content is more important. 2501 is easier than 2500 if you learned multi cal & lin alg before.

I learned multi cal and lin alg, and find MATH 2500 is not that bad, especially with a great TA. I feel like the grade, on average, is actually higher than MATH 2300, so it is a solid choice. Tests are mostly easy HW problems. The professor is bad at answering questions and crams everything to the end of the lecture, but overall very organized.

Aldroubi was easily my favorite prof this sem. 2500 is challenging, but not impossible. Aldroubi is a great lecturer  hard of hearing, but once you get a question across he will be sure to give u a good answer. He makes his exams easy. Weekly HW can be tough, but TA office hrs made that doable. Really nice, caring, and funny guy. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Aldroubi is very good at lecturing and getting the point across. He's reachable and caring (I asked him to grade an assignment for submission and he accepted). With that said, MATH 2500 is harder than what you would expect a freshman-level math class to be. This class needs WORK: I came with multi and lin alg experience and still had to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great prof. That being said, MATH2500 was extremely difficult. Came in with a 5 on BC, sought to major in math. Unless you're a god at math or have had prior multi or linear experience, this class will be a grind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Aldroubi is a great professor and by far the best I've had in the Vanderbilt Math Dept. He clearly loves what he is teaching and is very knowledgeable. He is very nice, cares a lot about his students' understanding of the material, communicated exam content well when asked, and is a fairly good lecturer considering the pandemic restrictions.

Prof. Aldroubi is extremely nice and his tests are very straightforward (unlike the rest of Vandy's math department). You can tell he really cares that we understand the material. He is a bit disorganized which makes the notes sometimes hard to understand and review. But other than that and his difficulty of hearing, he is a true gem.

As far as math professors go at Vandy, Aldroubi is as good as it gets. Complex Variables was tough, but he makes pretty straightforward tests with problems very similar to those on the homework. No final. Cares about students and focuses on major concepts. The class gets increasingly harder (but that may have been from the fallout from COVID-19).

Take 2500 if you can. It takes some work but is worth it. Difficult concepts and lots of proofs, but everyone works together so you learn more. Aldroubi encourages collaboration. Funny in lecture. Takes questions, bad at answering. Truly cares about student success. Crams everything into end of lecture. Doesn't test what he doesn't teach in class.

Professor Aldroubi's unique teaching style takes a little getting used to, but over the course of the semester myself and the rest of my class came to really appreciate him. He genuinely cares about your success and will take steps to help you. Overall a great guy, and I really enjoyed his lectures and this class!

Prof. Aldroubi is a great professor. His lectures can be a bit slow and unorganized on occasion, but hes a very caring and funny professor. Considering this is a class he doesnt normally teach, he did a great job. Homework was reasonable and the one time the test was too hard, he curved it.

Dr. Aldroubi becomes more likeable throughout the semester. He sometimes makes mistakes, but he's very open to our reminding. He explains concepts clearly and always emphasizes important ideas. Tests are the most straightforward ones I've ever seen, so you can get a good grade even with minimum efforts, but you can learn a lot if you're motivated.

I would agree with people saying that he's caring, but I don't think he's a very good professor. For analysis, halfway through the course he decided to let the students give lectures instead of teaching. He teaches straight from the textbook, so class is optional. Comes to class unprepared and wastes time getting lost in proofs. Wouldn't take again

Dr. Aldroubi is probably one of the most caring math professors you can ever expect. What he cares about is whether or not you understand the material rather than what grade you eventually get. The lectures are not perfect--they sometimes moves slowly and can be little disorganized--but at the end of the day, you can understand every concept.

Great teacher. Didn't like teaching Diff Eq & Lin Alg. He will help as much as you need outside of class and during class. His tests are very straightforward and his expectations are clearly highlighted in his review tests. Homework is very useful as a grade booster and as a studying tool.

Dr. Aldroubi is a wonderful teacher. He won't move on until everyone understands each concept. Homework is just enough to understand the material. Tests are not bad (study the practice tests). He said he would not teach 2400 (DiffEq + LinAlg) again because there was too much content for 1 semester,  and I agree with his choice. Highly recommend.

Was good teacher. Easier than what I could tell about the others, really cared about the students and tried to become familiar with us. Busy guy, but he does have office hours and loves to teach during them. Lectures are pretty nice, his hands are literally coated in chalk at the end of a lecture from how much he writes on the board.

Professor Aldroubi is extremely nice and helpful. He always started class by asking if he had any questions, which really shows that he wants his students to fully learn the material. He always emphasizes truly understanding the material rather than just memorizing tricks on how it work problems which some students may not like, but I preferred it.

Dr. Aldroubi is a really cool guy, and makes class interesting. Homework counts for 35% of the grade (pretty easy to make 100s on them). Tests are not too difficult, but minor mistakes will get lots of points off. Overall a great prof.
He is so so so nice and made the tough class so much easier. Love him so much

Aldroubi is a mathematical genius which sometimes translate into him assuming  students understand something when they don't. Nonetheless, he is very easy to ask questions of and super helpful in office hours. Takes the time to know each student's names and also provides extra help sessions right before exams. Great professor!
he is so so so so nice. I love his class and he gives really easy tests. He really tries to help you succeed and cares a lot about you. He is a very nice guy.
Best math teacher I've had at Vanderbilt.

This is my favorite math teacher to date. Aldroubi genuinely cares about teaching and coveys the material brilliantly. He covers exactly what is in the book but you won't even need to read it if you pay attention in class.

Professor Aldroubi is a rare exception to Vanderbilt's cryptic Math department. His tests are fair and based on class material. Homework is weighted heavily, and he'll help you with the problems if you go to office hours. Lectures are clear, entertaining, and get you interested in the material. Take this guy; he actually wants to give you an A!

Prof. Aldroubi is wonderful.  Only weakness lies in his typos during simple computations; these occur because he focuses on the big picture, which he strives to communicate to his students.  Besides these typos, he never once made a mistake.  The man knows math, and will teach you.  Linear is the basis for higher math. Glad I took it with Aldroubi.

Though the material was challenging, Aldroubi was very helpful - he's the only math professor I've had who will pause during a lecture to let the students work out a problem to make sure what he's saying is clear.  He's an extremely good mathmetician (he can graph anything in 3D in his head) and he genuinely likes to teach.
Weekly homework raher than tests. Helpful, very fair tests

I have had significant trouble with calculus courses. Prof. Aldroubi is quite the exception for the Vandy math dept: he cares about his students' understanding of the material and their performance in his class. He is extremely understanding and helpful. Go to class, do the homework, and talk to him if you have trouble.

TAKE 175 WITH ALDROUBI. Im ashamed that my grade is below an A right now b/c he is such a good teacher. There is 1 HW assignment every week instead of quizzes, covering exactly what will be on the test (except test problems are usually even simpler). Did very badly on one test (my fault) and he re-weighted the test and the final to help my grade :)

aldroubi is by far the easiest 175 teacher, i would recommend rearranging your entire schedule to get him instead of rafter. tests are just like the homework problems and he's really excited to teach you math. doesn't put up useless proofs.

Aldroubi is a phenomenal teacher. He really cares if his students understand what he is teaching. I would take a class with him again, easily. He grades easier than other sections, but at the same time he's worth it as a teacher because you end up greatly learning the material.

excellent teacher. really helpful. first test was a joke compared to everything we've done in class. unlike ALL other sections, there are no quizzes, instead he gives homework and it's impossible to get less than a 9.5/10 on the homework (not to mention he drops to hw grades). easy to understand, easy tests so far. highly recommended.

Overall, a very easy and moderately thorough DE class. Impossible to get below 95 on homework, and the tests are easier than the practice problems.  Aldroubi tends to make mistakes on the board, but otherwise he's pretty clear and helpful.  Class consists mostly of working on problems with his supervision rather than him lecturing, which iss good.

He could have made this class so much harder, but he managed to teach some fairly in-depth topics without screwing students' GPAs too much.  It's a skill most of Vandy's math department seems to lack. His grader does suck though. I ended up enjoying this class much more than I expected to.  Definitely recommended.

Aldroubi is pretty good. Nothing is too difficult and he is always very interested on whether you are learning or not. His grader was horrible though -5 pts for not being stapled, loses your assignments, and a problem in which you do 90% correct she gives you no credit.

A nice teacher who truly cares about his students, and probably one of the better members of Vanderbilt's incomprehensive, Bohemian math faculty.  That said, non-mathy people beware: this is not the high school calculus that was taught clearly and made fun.  You'll be teaching yourself from the book a lot and he's tough for non mathematical people.
No Comments
Aldroubi is kind of idiot and smells pretty bad, but hey his tests are easy and the extra credit is ridiculous.  Have fun laughing at his dress and mannerisms during class.

He's kind of a dork.  Don't expect anything too insightful.  most of the comments everyone else said is true but I feel this is a pretty important factor.  its so slow its hard to pay attention, if your at all into math don't get him
pretty good teacher, fairly easy, wants to make sure that everyone understands; very helpful if you go see him during offic hours. overall, a good teacher
he's really easy, and cares so much about making sure that everyone understands a topic that it almost becomes a drag.  the class is slow!
No Comments

best class i've ever taken, would take again if I could. assigned readings were tough at times (stem major things) but I still find myself pondering over the concepts we discussed to this day. truly changed my perspective on the social, political, and racial "otherness" of accents (including my own). discussion heavy, caring, easy grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: super nice! very discussion-heavy, readings were dense (I'm a stem major, words make me cry) but the topics were intriguing and honestly changed my outlook on linguistics and the way I think of accents in my everyday life. writing a 8-ish page paper was very difficult for me (again, STEM major things) but she was genuinely helpful and understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Saxena does an excellent job of facilitating discussion in class. The topics were all really interesting. She gives great specific feedback for papers and really wants you to succeed. Lots of reading and she will call you out if she suspects you didn't do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Saxena is brilliant and so kind. Her lectures and class discussions are really interesting and she cares so much about the class and material. Gem in the English Department!

Saxena is a great professor and did a great job directing discussions in our class and keeping them from veering off. She does call on people randomly to discuss the reading and will note if she suspects you did not do it but the books were all pretty great and easy reads. Final project was a lot of fun and she gave great feedback.

I liked her in the beginning but found her to have deep hatred for her own origin. A professor who dances on the grave of her ancestors but calls herself a "postcolonial literature expert". She has deep prejudice against India and Indians and has inherited the colonial lens to look at her former country. Deeply disappointed.

Definitely a solid choice for a 1000W!! She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. Manageable workload -- 2 short papers and 1 final longer paper, a short partner presentation, weekly journals (completion), and 4 super easy quizzes of which the 2 lowest grades are dropped. Sometimes boring though and MANDATORY attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Super caring, productive discussions, and fun content/material. Grading was very clear and she's a nice grader. Great to talk to one-on-one too, she's so smart. Overall, amazing professor and fun class.

Best class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt, and my favorite professor. Not only is Prof. Saxena caring and understanding, but she is more concerned about students' learning about the world around us. We watched films, wrote critically about them, and discussed. Amazing class, easy grading, and a great environment.

She is one of the most chill and caring professors at Vanderbilt. The discussions were thought-provoking and made me look at film in a completely different way. Grading Criteria: 8 Screening Journals (1 pg for completion), 3 papers, 4 Quizzes, 1 project . Very doable if you have a heavy load. If you put in the work, you can get an A.

Professor Saxena is really sweet, but there are versions of this class that exist that are far more interesting. If you're looking for an easy 2000+W class, take this, but you will be incredibly bored every single class period. Professor Saxena is so smart and cool, but it doesn't translate into a dynamic class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was pretty tough. It was 100% discussion-based, which I usually love, but the discussions could get pretty theoretical and/or theory oriented. It could make them difficult to participate in. I like Saxena, but when we did give her feedback on the class she would say "Yes, but" and then kind of explain it away. Solid, but frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her class discussions are incredibly thought provoking. She gives great feedback and assigns interesting readings. If you put in effort, it is definitely A-able. I took this as a writing course and we only had to do 2 papers the entire semester. Highly recommend.

Akers has a lot of experience in screenwriting and continuously shows samples from his own works in progress. The class is best for someone who intends on making it in the industry, but anyone who does the work can succeed. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he gives away perfect attendance pins at the end of the semester.
Akers is solid across the board. Get him to clarify things as quickly as possible in the semester.

Great professor. Attendance not mandatory, but the pin is worth it! A good amount of work, but it is all on your film, so if you enjoy filmmaking, take this class for sure. Infact take every class that Will has to offer. Hes a great teacher. He will even give you his cell and you can call if you need anything.
Akers is a great professor.  If you attend every class, you receive a perfect attendance pin.  Work tends to be heavy, but easy.  If you try and show an interest, expect at least a B.

Incredible professor.  Class attendence not mandatory, but he awards a perfect attendance pin at the end of the semester.  Actually class involves weekly writing assignments.  If you care about the class, it's an easy A.  If you get behind or stop caring, expect to do horribly.
All textbooks he gives you are suggested reading only. We had no papers and no tests. For our final exam he just said, "Okay now make a movie." Very time-consuming but sooo worth it.
fun class, with 99% of the work being on film projects

Easiest professor in the world to get along with if you're interested in the material.  Very engaging guy who doesn't force you to do anything.  If you do the work you'll get the grade you deserve.  He's flexible and real chill.  Loved all 5 of his classes that i've taken
The class is mainly difficult because it's so incredibly time consuming. But if you put in effort and produce a good product he'll give you a great grade.
Awesome, laidback guy, very practical and professional.  So laidback that I wasn't expecting him to shred my final paper like he did.
Great classes.  Loved it - hard as hell for someone without a creative bone in their body.
Will is amazing.
No Comments
No Comments
great teacher, funny, easy going.

Serkan is an awesome professor who makes it incredibly easy to do well. I got As on both my test and didn't feel like putting a lot of effort into the final project. He made it 15% of the grade for kids who wanted to pull up their grade but he let me make it only 5% of my grade so i didn't have to put in extra effort. Take him if you can
He's a great guy who really wants everyone to do well.  Extremely helpful and understanding. However, class is fairly boring.
Serkan is the best. I have never had a professor that cared more about the success of his students. He does everything in his power to help us succeed.

Prof Akguc is awesome. He lets his students to call him Serkan. He also provides his cell number for students to call 24/7 with questions. I think he really does want students to learn... he encourages learning with rewards like extra credit for answering questions in class. Take his class. You'll learn a lot, and an A isn't hard if you try.

Serkan is a good teacher and very nice! I found the class fairly easy. You should definitely take it.  Yes, you have to study. But it's really not that bad. And don't worry if you're not a math person, it's more memorizing and understanding the "language" of accounting. Serkan is very helpful in office hrs too.

Serkan is great.  To try and entertain the notion that he is "unprofessional" is absurd.  The problems from the Class Pak are essential to doing well on the exams.  Very nice guy and is always willing to help.

Horrible professor. He's less concerned with being a teacher, and more with being your friend, which is not only unprofessional, but kind of creepy.   Not very helpful in class and out, if you want to do well in the class you will have to teach yourself all the material.   definitely take Goodyear if you have the option.
Take his class.  Subject is not difficult and he is a very cool guy.  There is also alot of extra credit.
Serk is the man. Keeps accounting as fun and clear as he can. You just have to make sure you put in some effort and you'll get an A. Take the class!!!!
Serkan is simply the man. He is a great guy and actually wants everyone in the class to get an A. Class isn't that hard if you do the homework.  Take him.

He was helpful and the class is not that bad. 'Homeworks' aren't graded on correctness, but if you attempt them he gives you credit for 20% of your grade. Tests aren't difficult but he'll tell you what you need to know for them. Overall, this was not as painfully dry as i imagined accounting to be.

Absolutely one of the worst professors I've had at Vanderbilt.  He is hard to understand, and too busy trying to make himself look cool. He picks his favorites the first couple weeks of the semester. Homework is tedious, but necessary if you want to do well on tests.Tests=Difficult. Avoid if you can.

Class is not an easy A. You have to work through a lot of practice problems to get a handle on the material. That said, if you put in the work Serkan will give usually give partial credit back for redoing problems on tests even if the class average is a B+. Office hours way more helpful than class but extra credit for attending. Book=unnecessary.

He tries to make class interesting by joking with the frat stars, but the class is still boring and it was hard to make myself attend. The class requires a lot of work and the tests are challenging. His "practice tests" do not help at all. He also calls homework "homeworks" which annoyed me. Unless this is a requirement, avoid it.

Always willing to help any time you have questions. Responds to emails within a few hours. Accounting can be a bit dry, but he tries his best to spark interest in class, occasionally even with candy. He truly wants his students to succeed and will make sure you do well if you put for the effort.

Batra is the man. The content is super interesting and you will learn a lot, especially if you do the readings. The essays are graded kindly and there is not a crazy amount of writing. Highly recommend if you need a W course or are just interested in the topic.
Great professor, easy grader, and overall good guy. I had a great tine in this class and Batra was the best part!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Picks really interesting readings. I learned a lot about the period and improved my analysis and writing skills. Assignments are well designed. Interesting and not hard to get a good grade on. Participation is 20% of grade. Class isn't very engaging (boring lectures then surface level discussions).

Professor Batra is the best English professor I have had at Vandy. He gives very detailed feedback, and his lectures are very interesting. There were three paper assignments and 5 discussion posts we had to write. The workload is reasonable, and the material is very thought-provoking. We had very interesting class discussions!!

Professor Batra is a really good professor. He is very caring and gives very fair grades. The readings he selects are always an appropriate length to get done before each class, and he provided each reading for free on his brightspace. If you need to take a W I recommend him absolutely.
He was pretty easy-going and not that tough of a grader. Easy to succeed if you show up and are engaged. Graded on 5 discussion posts and some short essays. Nothing too bad.
take ENGL1260W with Professor Batra. he's so sweet and cares about what he's teaching! 4 papers and 5 discussion posts.

Took ENG 1260 with Dr. Batra, and found it to be one of my most interesting classes. I was initially relatively unenthused about the topic of the class, but now I am incredibly invested in prison literature as a result of Dr. Batra. He is incredibly kind, caring, and makes a clear effort to promote success in the class. 8am was rough but worth it.

Definitely one of my favorite classes so far. There is a lot of reading but it is all very interesting and relevant to the course. He really cares a lot about the course topics and does a great job at leading class discussions. He is not a very harsh grader and gives excellent feedback. Very inspirational class, would 100% take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Batra is the kindest, most understanding professor I have had at this school. His writing assignments are super interesting and unique, and he is genuinely invested in students' success. Highly recommend taking a class with him, especially if you need an upper level W credit.

Class was absurdly easy if you have had prior experience with Physics. As a professor, Ramayya isn't that great. His accent is thick and doesn't explain well. However, I still highly recommend his class. His tests are very easy and basic compared to Momchil's. Class average was a B, with a large amount of solid A's and C's. First test had 15 100%s.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not enough chances to earn grades. Three tests. One final. Cumulative HW. Tests are 20 questions, 5 points each, which makes things annoying. If you are a physics pro, you'll get an A. Would only take again if Duda isn't teaching the same class. Better than Momchill.

Tests are easy if you study old material from the course. Otherwise, some questions are thrown out of left field. Hope that there are no show your work, because those are graded absurdly. Don't go to class, read the textbook (if they changed it) and do old tests. Don't expect to learn from lectures.

Ramayya is an old, soft-spoken man and has a thick accent so he can be so it can be difficult to understand him, but he writes the lectures note by hand so its easy to follow him in class. His tests are not too difficult if you practice. The Final borrows a few questions from the previous tests. An an A is very manageable if you practice.

Do not take this class if you haven't taken physics before. Lectures are all over the place and not helpful for exams, which are loosely based on the homework. Exams may be stupidly easy for those with previous experience. Anyway, bad class, but probably still better than the others.

Prof R. is a nice man, but exams can be tricky.  20 multiple choice questions means 5 points per question.  So if you don't memorize some obscure facts that he may throw on the exam or just make small, silly errors, your grade drops by half letter grades at the drop of a dime.  Love the professor as a person, did not like the course
Threw random thermo on the end of our semester. All memorization. Ruined if you haven't taken physics before.

Take if you have had AP physics. If you haven't, like I haven't, I would recommend getting a different professor or help. He doesn't explain things clearly or teach at all. If you already know physics, his tests are very easy. If you don't, it's really easy to lose points & be below ave. He often doesn't cover principles on the homework or on tests
Easy and nice man

WORST Professor EVER...but take him if you've had AP physics in high school. You won't learn a thing in class, but his tests are a joke...a third of the class got 100's on the first exam and over half got A's. Slightly lower scores for second exam, but still over 10 100's. An easy A with a bit of prior knowledge and 2-3 hours a week.

Professor is really nice but very hard to follow. He definitely knows what he's talking about but cannot effectively explain it to someone that is lost. One on one has been no help at all to me. If physics doesnt come easily to you, I wouldnt take ramayya.
Prof Ramayya is very helping. His explanation is good. I would take his class for 116B too.

He knows what he's talking about, but is nearly unable to help students one on one. I don't recommend it if you havent' yet taken physics. He's reasonably easy to understand, but he doesn't explain concepts well.

This class is not all that great, but it's the best of the 116a sections. Ramayya spends the whole class deriving formulas using calculus, even though none of the tests or homework problems require derivations or calculus. Tests are pretty easy, but each question is worth 6 pts, so there's not much margin for error. He has cool demonstrations.

His lecture depends on his emotion highly. sometimes he is really lost, but in most of times, his lectures were good. However, he doesn't seem really interested in teaching. barely answers e-mails and left class in the middle of semester-it was aweful.

Ramayya focuses mainly on concepts rather than obscure details. His lectures are somewhat helpful, but definitely focus on the book. Tests are mostly multiple choice, fair, and moderate difficulty. Ramayya really cares about the class and is often available for office hours.  The class, while not great, is definitely the best section of PHYS 116A
I feel bad for the old guy, but it kind of seems like he lost it back in India decades ago. Very boring class and he's a very boring lecturer.

Prof Ramayya is just not cut out for teaching. He really lacks communication skills.  I liked physics when I signed up for this class. Now I don't. Clearly a researcher first; the students get whatever scraps of energy he has left. I would avoid him like the plague unless you're doing upper level physics.
has good intentions but his lectures are painful to sit through and don't really help.  This class is very difficult when it doesn't have to be.  avoid at all costs
glad to had this professor and good human being

Maybe it was just cause I was a newbie and hadn't taken any math and science in a long long time.. but I found this class extremely difficult. After studying through the book, and doing countless mastering physics problems, tricky multiple choice questions still got the best of me. I consider this a luck class at best for now. Will be retaking.

His tests are pretty easy. People do poorly on the test because he is not the best lecturer. He is really helpful outside of class, and he curves the class average to a B. Physics is a boring topic, so he's probably the best you will get. It's pretty important to read the textbook if you really want to know what's going on.
Very unclear, lectures are basically useless. Find previous versions of the tests and do the practice tests. The only way to survive.

20 question open notes, multiple choice exams. The questions are conceptual and require little to no calculations. If you had high school physics, the first two exams are extremely easy. The last two exams were a bit difficult but still manageable. Depending on the class avg, he will either drop the lowest grade or consider 87 to be A-.
Open note tests, still hard. Not great, but better than others

I thought that I was pretty good at Physics right up until I took this guy's class. He said it was going to be concept-based, and then he tested us on the equations. Don't let the open notes fool you, you can copy down every problem in that book, won't help much.

Very bad teacher with very confusing tests. If you actually try to work the homework problems by yourself without the answers you'll be screwed. The answers to most of the problems can be found online if you look hard enough and if you can find a copy of the solution manual to all the problems you'll be set. Clueless when it comes to giving notes.
The worst professor I've ever had. Horrible at teaching, horrible at making tests, and a horrible human being to boot. Never take him. Ever.

NOT THAT BAD.He's hard to understand and makes hard to stay awake in class when he writes on the overhead.homework assignments are due are weird times too.with all this said his tests are easy.he gives you a practice test that is similar to the actual test and in some cases he uses the same question. GOOD STUFF! EASIER TEST THAN THE OTHER GUY!

most of the days in his class were never boring because there's always a fun show from him, teaching us physics with application and stuff. I'm glad I got into his class, and his tests are not that hard, either! The ones who end up with bad grades are those who deserve them. He's not unhelpful; he just want us to understand it ourselves by thinking
Ridiculously awful class.  Smart guy, but he has no idea how to teach, speeds over important things and spends ten years on the easy stuff. He'll bore you to death, and his tests are poorly written.

This class sucks. Welcome to weed-out Engineering. Online homework was the bane of my existence. His tests were %80 multiple choice, and they were moderately difficult. Find some old tests and hope for the best.
worst teacher ever.  Incomprehensible,  gives homework assignments due on Friday and Saturday nights, and expects mastery of the material on the tests.  Tests are open note, but that doesn't help...
Probably one of the worst professors I have had. It is really hard to understand his teaching. He doesn't teach much physics, only does problems. Though the tests are open note, they can be hard.
Pretty awesome guy.  Tests are open note and not too hard.  The notes he gives in class are useful on the test, so don't skip too much. Read the textbook and you should do fine.

he might talk over the students heads, HOWEVER, it is by far one of the EASIEST fyw seminars you can take, you can be a horrible writer, and so long as you get your facts right, each paper is a guaranteed A (3total), plus your final is only a 25 m.choice test that takes 5 mintes. if you have remote interest in physics, youll be glad you took it.

When I took the FYS "what is matter" it was taught by Ramayya and his colleague Crowell. They both talked over every student's head the entire time but they could be mildly entertaining. Put time into your papers (3 papers, 4 pages each) and it's an easy A. Worth taking if you like cosmology.

I had Ramayaa for my first year writing seminar...he's horrible.  He seems like a guy who is at the school to do research; he's smart but he cannot teach.  Nice guy, but don't take any of his classes.

He's actually a really nice guy, but the class is horrible. There is NO partial credit on the test because they are multiple choice. In addition to that, there are only 2 tetst the whole semester (minus the final) which means less opportunity to raise your grade. Unless you're a physics genius or like to teach your self, take someone else.
terrible.  he knows his stuff, but his tests are multiple choice (no partial credit) and don't cover anything discussed in class.  Avoid him at all costs!
Means well, but often has trouble conveying his points. He honestly writes on an overhead projector for an hour and a half for every single class. Avoid him if possible.

Tends to talk over his students' heads... he's kind of too smart for his own good, and it's very obvious that he knows what he's talking about, but has trouble expressing it at times.  He means the best for his students, and gets big important points across very clearly in a way you will remember them, but details are iffy.

he was hard to understand, and he thought he was a cute little guy, but no one else did. his tests were  pretty complex because you have your notes. i would NOT advise taking his class. i went to him every week for help, and he was DEFINATELY not helpful
easy

He is an old guy that thinks he is funny in class when he really isn't.  Doesn't want to really help you outside of class, but with enough persistence he will give you the time of day.  Tests are hard, but you can use notes.

She's such a chiller. You get from this class what you put into it; if you want to learn helpful tricks to improve your art you'll learn them. Alex is very chill and nice. If you haven't taken an art class before, it might be way more work than you expect, but effort matters, so as long as you show up to class and try, you will be fine. Just a lovely person. She is very helpful and funny. Easy going and pretty lenient on all the deadlines. Portfolios are turned in twice a semester and holistically graded
