reviews.comment: Prof. Blau makes the classroom environment super relaxing and fun with music and conversations. Her feedback really helps hone the drawing skills. Class and homework are a little time-consuming, but if you like art/drawing, you will enjoy it regardless. Overall, it is very chill and works as a way to distress. Very lenient with grading.

The most difficult thing about this class was how much time it took up. There was the three hour class work time as well as homework over weekends. However, as long as you went to class, communicated clearly with her and show her that you put in effort on your work, she is pretty lenient and an easy grader. Very fun experience and freedom in art.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drawing and Comp was a great class; Alex was super cool. Though she focuses more on correcting rather than demoing, I learned many skills. She's an easy grader and understanding person--I have yet to find a professor as chill as her in the Art department. Highly recommend taking Drawing with her. You have to buy your own supplies but it's worth it.

Alex is really GOATED. At first I thought an A was impossible because the cutoff line is 96. But at the end, if you go to lectures and read textbooks, an A is very doable and the exam questions weren't as hard as I thought it to be.

Dr. Maier is a very engaging lecturer and explains concepts really well. He posts all the lectures. There are two exams in the course and weekly homework (based on completion). Although the exams are each worth 40%, the questions are not hard.

Dr. Maier is one of the best profs I've had at Vandy. He explains complicated topics very well and is an engaging lecturer. Grade based on weekly hw completion and 2 exams, which are easy if you pay attention in class! Seems harsh at first, but he genuinely cares abt students' learning!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There was a lot of reading and you had to go to lectures to keep up (slides posted but undecipherable if you weren't also in class), but Dr. Maier's personality made it worth it. My biggest takeaway was I wish I had taken it before self-studying for the MCAT, because there was a lot of overlap that would've been nice to not have to learn on my own!

Overall, this is a very interesting subject matter. This course is definitely not an easy A, and a lot of memorization is required. Your grade is almost exclusively based on two exams (1 midterm and 1 final). Each exam is 50 multiple choice questions and counts for 40% of your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have any interest in psychology or neuroscience, I highly recommend this professor! Attending his classes were the highlight of my week and he kept the class engaged. Tests consisted of topics heavily covered in class and readings. Easy homework, and while the readings were long, they helped to understand and give more detail on the topics.

Favorite Prof I have had at Vandy by far. Maier is one of the coolest and most thoughtful Profs at this school and his lectures are incredibly interesting. You can tell he has put tons of time into his lectures and research. Great course for premeds. An A is possible if you go to class and take notes and read the textbook pgs quick. TAKE HIM!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Maier is amazing. He is able to fit so much into his lectures while still explaining things well and including fun demonstrations that relate to the content, like magic tricks! Going to the lectures and reading the textbook makes the world of difference for this class. This class is so enjoyable, and Dr. Maier emphasizes that completely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Classes are lecture heavy but enjoyable since the professor likes to include magic tricks, demonstrations, illusions, etc. Homework is minimal but reading the textbook is helpful. Each of the two tests is worth 40% of your grade with 50 multiple choice questions that are mostly memorization. Take good notes and you'll love this class.

This is the best course I have taken at Vanderbilt. Prof. Maier is the most interesting lecturer and a pleasure to be around (he is really funny too) . He really cares about all of his students and most importantly, cares most about their quality of learning more than heavy work load. Take this class if you can, you will not regret it.

Excellent professor who teaches interesting materials and really encourages students to learn. Don't ever think about getting an A, unless your IQ is >180. Learned quite a lot during classes and he probably wants you to know that this class is hard at the beginning so that you can spend quite an amount of time. It's worth the effort nevertheless :)

Professor Maier is very smart and willing to help clarify anything that is confusing over email and in class. No computers are allowed, so trying to write down everything is really hard. The lectures are fast paced and stressful and then you read 40+ textbook pages to teach yourself before cramming for a 50 multiple choice question test.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Lecture heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Alex is a great professor (he goes by his first name). He makes lectures really interesting and engaging, and I actually enjoyed going to his class. reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take this class. Super interesting. He teaches enthusiastically. It's not that hard if you use the textbook and truly pay attention in class. You need a 96 for an A but an A- is totally doable (if you're willing to work).

Whoever said this would be an easy A must have been albert einstein. His tasks are pretty difficult and to get an A in the class you need a 96. There is a lot of content to cram into your head and regurgitate onto the 50 multiple choice question test, however he is helpful and willing to answer questions at any point.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class was pretty easy for a 200-level class. I did little work outside of class until the week before a test and I ended up with an A-. Now you see him; now you don't. He fails to deliver on office hours and student inquires. He makes classes mildly interesting, however.

He gives five incredibly easy tests and drops your lowest grade. Like you thought you knew easy tests until you took his tests. You need a 95 for an A, but it's more than manageable. Never more than 10 pages of reading per class--you have no excuse not to take this class.

Schuppe is 100% the best choice for orgo! So much extra credit/opportunities to improve your grade. He really cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. Difficult exams but extra credit helps a ton.
Take him and thank me later, the best professor ever

If you are a Vanderbilt student taking Orgo 2, I would get on the waitlist for Schuppe's section as if my life depended on it. Hands down the best professor of all time without a single question. I would take a bullet for this man if I had to because of how easy he made Orgo 2 seem. Genuine guy, incredibly knowledgeable, and sometimes can be funny

Schuppe is awesome! He cares about teaching. This class is tough but all 2222 sections are, prepare to work hard. Exams are a bit more tricky than Clements or Ni. Very generous grading, extra credit on every exam.
Schuppe is so nice but his section is harder than the other ones. Even looking at class averages, his are far lower than say, Clements. I think I would've done better taking her.

SHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOPY!!! This great man is the epitome of organic chemistry. He knows more than you ever will but he does try to spread his knowledge to the younglings. Amazing slides but treacherous tests (with EC so you can still get a good grade). Prepare for your life to be changed.

SHOOOOOOOOOOOPYYY!!!
Just take him
if you want to learn orgo, take him

Dr. Schuppe was probably the kindest, most caring professor I have ever had. Great teacher, always willing to explain concepts and answer questions, extremely smart, and very fair grader. Literally love this man. He cares so much about his students. You could schedule meetings with him whenever necessary and he had accessible office hours. Grading on the exams was SO fair. Alex is really good at being a professor despite him being very young and relatively new. It was his first time teaching this class; he was new to the throne. He is insanely good at teaching organic.

Dr. al-Wahish gave so much extra credit and her syllabus makes it really hard to fail. She is one of the most accommodating professors I've had in STEM. She encourages questions and is very helpful in office hours. If you paid attention and studied, the class was light for a pre-med req.

Dr. al-Wahish is one of the best professors at this school. If you attend class, study the notes, and understand her practice problems, you're well-equipped for the exams. reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are fast-paced, and if this is your first physics class, you won't learn much. BUT she REALLY wants you to succeed, and her syllabus is very accommodating. Please avoid for your own mental health
If you are looking for a class and professor to ruin your GPA and make your life hell, then she's your best choice!!

Not a good professor. Blames students for averages she set us up for (a 54 average should not be blamed on students). Does not handle criticism well. Her plenty of years of experience do not show at all in the classroom–overall a counterproductive and disinterested professor.

If you enjoy confusion, frustration, and the occasional existential crisis about your academic choices, this is the class for you!!! The lectures are essentially a bunch of "quizzes" thrown at you without any explanation of the actual material. The slides themselves are useless, and you're literally left flailing in the dark. Hope this helps!

She is extremely disorganized, reads off of the slide but says nothing of substance, has no continuity between the different aspects of the class, condescends students for asking questions and constantly complains about how much work she is doing. She is the most infuriating professor on this campus and the school does not care about our opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I have had yet. I don't know whats worse, her accent, teaching, exams, or the fact that her slides make absolutely no sense. We just do questions throughout the whole class without any explanation to the actual topics. Flipped Classrooms need to be abolished.

This is by far one of the hardest classes I have taken at Vanderbilt. Her lecture style is confusing/overwhelming and the exams are impossible. The homework on Pearson does not line up with the exams either. This class is the equivalent of trying to piece together a 500-piece puzzle!

This has been the worst stem class I've taken at Vanderbilt, even worst than gen chem 1. The lectures are extremely difficult to follow, and the professor's explanations often feel disconnected from the material we are expected to understand. The lectures don't add any clarity, if anything, they make the material feel more overwhelming.
I you want a class that will convince you to drop out, take this class!

Shes funny and kind outside of class but she is actually a terrible lecturer. Her lectures are very simplistic and then her exams are unimaginable. Her homework doesnt correlate with what she teaches. You can study so much and still fail her exams, she gives insane curves but at what cost.

Have an A in biochem but failed exam 2 (exam 1 was much easier). Took MCAT last semester and the physics was easier on that section than exam 2. No clear understanding on what topics will be tested. Constantly flexes that she holds office hours while holding an atrocious lecture (which is more accessible to everyone).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's friendly one-on-one but mean in lectures. She teaches super confusingly and way above what should be in an intro class. People who study hard still fail exams. She insisted the reason exam 2's average was in the 50s was because some students didn't study and decided to drop it. She says if you struggle with her, go to 1602. So terrible omg.

I have an A in orgo and I got a 40 on her second midterm. I aced the first. She curves them, yes, but it is still unbelievably tricky and tests you on reading comprehension. She is condescending, brutal, and acts like we are the problem when her terrible test writing and INCOHERENT lectures are not. I pray to god you see this and take 1601 instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor I have ever had in 3 years of college. Not only is she anxiety-inducing and calls people out, she makes every little trick possible to ensure that even the best students waste all their time and miss a multiple choice question. She has singlehandedly ruined my mental health and clarity. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS, please.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has prelecture homework, inclass quizzes & exams 60% of grade. Besides exams grades are scaled up. Most reviews are bullying as many were expecting a different professor at the start of the year. There is room for improvement but Dr. al-Wahish has listened to feedback, given a large curve, and is open to change. Not easy, but not "vile."
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have to pregame this class. That should tell you how it's going! (Horrible). The professor is condescending and does not effectively know how to teach.

I understand her words, but how she explains concepts does not make sense. I get that it's supposed to be a hard class, but I have to read the textbook daily to keep up with the content. Her practice problems do not match the exam difficulty (minus the first test, which was fair). This class was vile.

This is genuinely the worst professor I've had at Vanderbilt. The definition of disorganized. She is an extremely difficult exam giver who can't even teach students the basics. She continuously tries to guilt trip students into thinking their performance is their fault when clearly it's due to her incompetence. Please reconsider taking her class.

Dr. Al-Wahish is a horrible professor at Vanderbilt. She is funny but if this is an atrocious physics course for a pre-med. Her Pearson modules do not correlate with her classes. Her slides are so simple and everything else feels like a different world. Constantly rewards herself for holding office hours. This is her job!
She literally told students to take a different physics section if they disliked her so much. She literally farts on people. Avoid at ALL COSTS!

I'm not sure why she's receiving accolades for holding office hours or not blatantly turning away students when that's her job. She simply lacks the heart and compassion for teaching and is very particular about who she scolds and intimidates. She should not be teaching at Vanderbilt. Take PHYS 1601 instead.
She is totalitarian in her approach to teaching and tries to lie and say she's accommodating without acknowledging her blatant shortcomings. Do not take her.

Do not take this teacher. Words I would describe this teacher: rude, condescending, and above all a terrible teacher. If you don't have any basics in physics you will be struggling in this course. I have completely self taught the material, as her lectures are confusing and don't teach the material. She blames the students for her lack of teaching.

This is Dr. Amal's first-semester teaching at Vanderbilt, and obviously, there is always room to improve. I have a hard time understanding her lectures. If you see her class, make sure you have a background in physics. She expects us to know everything and gaslight students into thinking her class is manageable. This class makes me drink daily!

Sure, she does offer a lot of office hours and cares. She projects that, but it does not actually work/reflect. She is just bad at teaching as a whole and it's pretty evident with her first test average being a 67. Even with the "help", the class is still not by any means helping us nor improving us as students, it just makes many people dread it.

She made the semester hell for so many people. She makes her own TA's write good reviews about her. A comment on here made it seem like only one person really doesn't like her, but it's genuinely almost all her students. The only 5's she gets on here are from the people who are forced to give her good ratings.

Not sure why she's getting so many negative reviews -- honestly might just be one angry person. She patiently answers every question in class and has many office hour slots. She also gives us a free 20% of our final grade as participation. She genuinely cares for her students and is always available before and after class to answer more questions.
Her good reviews are literally from the TAs she forced to write good ratings that tell you everything you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You better pray if you do not have a background in physics. She claims to care about her students but will do anything to put her students on blast, a genuinely terrible individual who lowers Vanderbilt's academic reputation. Please take it somewhere else if you can!!

Worst professor I have ever had. If you take this class, be sure to get ready to self teach. She contributes nothing to your understanding during lecture. You could go to every single lecture, do every assignment and practice problem, and still get a failing grade on the midterm because of her terrible grading policies. AVOID at all costs.

Amal is the worst physics professor I have had. She does not clearly explain any material. She lacks empathy for students, often responding to questions in a condescending attitude. For students taking physics for the first time, STAY AWAY. It is almost impossible to succeed in her class without a background in physics. It is so easy to drown.

Considering this professor to be up-to-par with other Vanderbilt faculty is a true disappointment to the Vanderbilt name. Her teaching environment and methods are overtly old-school, and she feigns empathy when she receives her admonition from higher-ups. Do not take her if you can afford it; it's no reason to stress about this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Her only good reviews are from people in the physics department, herself, or bots. They are not perspectives from actual students, everyone I know dislikes her she is a 2/5 at her best.

She literally farts at people during class—quite a rude person with a horrible attitude. If you have no basis in physics, do not take her. She will only lead to your downfall. I feel like she has good intentions somewhere inside her, but her teaching and attitude do not reflect them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor stresses the importance of asking questions, but makes it difficult when she gives a passive aggressive and even sarcastic response. She thinks she's approachable, but she's not. This course really makes me second guess my intelligence but I know it's not just me that feels this way. Exam was heavily curved.

Be warned that all of the positive ratings on here she had her LAs write. If you don't understand something she'll call you out in front of the whole class and say "why don't you understand". And she always says you'll do well if you go to her office hours but I go almost every week, haven't missed a class, and still got a D on the midterm. AVOID.

I truly do not understand how others rate this professor at fives and claim she's inclusive when she has been anything but. It makes me question the integrity of these reviews honestly. She creates an oppressive and unwelcoming learning space that is increasingly unnecessary. She's best suited for a class in the high school setting, not collegiate.

Dr. Wahish puts tremendous effort into her teaching and is the best. I appreciate how she applies physics to our daily lives and connects current research to the materials we study. She is always willing to meet with students and work alongside them. Her exam is comprehensive and reflects about 90% of the class material. Go to her office hours.

Dr. al-Wahish is an amazing professor! I asked her to meet with me one-on-one outside her scheduled office hours, and she agreed. We spent over an hour working through problems together and developing a study strategy that works for me. She truly cares about her students and delivers fantastic lectures with many cool demonstrations

I've really loved being a student in Dr. al-Wahish's physics class. It's been such a rewarding experience, and I've learned so much. Her teaching style inclusive, and you can tell she truly cares about her students. She takes the time to meet with us one-on-one, offering plenty of resources and strategies to help us thrive.

It's amazing—just attend her lectures to see real-life applications of physics and science. She introduces the concepts and then gives us quizzes ranging from easy level to challenging  which are graded based on only participation. I really learn physics in her class! Don't miss her lectures and the demonstrations. Lectures are fun and educational!

Dr al-Wahish is very helpful during office hours and adjusts exam scores. Her lectures are highly engaging, and she often covers review problems that appear on the exams. From her in-class quizzes, pre-lecture reading quizzes, practice exams, and MYLab problems, I've seen over 80% of her exam content reflected, so make sure not to miss them!
Grading structure lenient so not hard to get a good grade but class is just really annoying and lectures are pretty bad. I rely on self study from textbook

Dr. Wahish's lack of empathy with students is glaring. Her grading policies are unnecessarily punitive, with each MCQ worth 5 points, leaving no room for even the smallest mistake. Despite this being an introductory course, she consistently fails to clearly explain basic physics concepts, making the class far more difficult than it should be.

She is way too intense and can be pretty rude and sarcastic. Please avoid her if you have anxiety or stress issues, as she only makes things worse. She has a good intention behind her attitude but is way too rude and mean for her first year here. I have no background in physics, and it just makes me feel dumb about it.

She is sooo passionate about the subject and cares about her students and their success! I put in average effort and still earned an A on the first exam with no physics background. She even offered 12 extra credit points to raise the class average. She has office hours every day, so if you're willing to put in the work, class is very doable!

Yikes. Probably the worst professor I have ever had. I get that she's new to the school, but despite her years of experience in teaching, she does not know how to teach! In lectures, we just do a bunch of problems, and she expects us to know how to solve them. RIP to the people who have no background in physics. Way too intense for an intro class.

Great teacher, sad that she has left Vanderbilt and is now in Georgia.... she has high expectations for her students but is helpful and cares about your success! Best French professor I've had out of the 4 french classes taken! Take her!! Sad s

Professor Stevens is a great teacher. Beware though, the whole class is completely spoken in french which is intimidating at first but is very helpful. She comes up with many fun activities to help you along and is always open to help you at any time. Definitely a great professor!
Great teacher. So funny. Not an easy A but a manageable and relaxing A-/B+
Madame Stevens is great!! Very very helpful, and the class is entertaining. Definitely easy to understand! Lots of homework, but it helps.
I think Madame Stevens does a good job teaching class. she is easy to understand which is especially important when speaking in french!

Dr. Hare is probably one of the smartest and most patient professors at Vanderbilt. Grade is out of 450 pts: 25 from quizzes, 25 discussion, and 4 100 pt exams. Reading the entirety of the chapter is not needed, but doing practice problems and keeping up with material is. Please go to office hours she is so kind. Live laugh love Dr. Hare. 10/10.

Dr. Hare is fantastic. Very accessible (4 office hrs/wk), clear/online-available lectures, and fair tests. Preview content prior to class, do the practice problems, ask questions, and you'll do stellar. Grades are curved one letter grade up. Partial credit is extremely generous. If there was one professor I'd make sure to take, it would be Hare.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare is amazing! She is very caring, supportive, and has plenty of office hours. Tests make you think outside the box, but doing the textbook problems will help with the skills. Go to class! It's easy to fall behind when missing a lecture or two. I feel well prepared for orgo 2 taking Dr. Hare's class.

I'm gonna be real- Hare's exams are HARD. But they're very doable with consistent practice outside of class. Lectures are great at introducing topics, but it's up to you to develop the skills presented in class for more complex contexts. She also has COVID lectures online in case you miss. This class almost made me lose my mind, but Hare is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare is a really good lecturer. The class was a little fast-paced but she provided good examples. She has office hours at least four days a week and is very accessible outside of class. The exams were hard because of the time crunch but the content was fair in hindsight. Do the practice problems and you'll do ok! Taking her again for CHEM 2222.

One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt, Professor Hare is so nice and wants everyone to succeed. Her exams are really tough, and it is a really hard class, but she makes it much more enjoyable! She is so approachable and office hours are great.

Hare is an incredibly thoughtful professor who goes out of her way to ensure students understand the content. Office hours are very helpful, try to go at least once a week if you can. Her tests are pretty hard. Memorize the mechanisms. Tons of outside work getting to know the content. Book is super helpful -- do all probs. This class is not easy.

Dr. Hare is a very good teacher, but be aware that her tests are also extremely difficult. You need to put in lots of time to keep up with the material, and you must practice on your own. Her lectures are very well-planned and there are Friday participation quizzes that give points outside of tests. She is a great teacher but will really push you.

Hare is MOTHER. She's so clearly meant to teach-- she explains thing really clearly and offers office hours 4 times a week. Her exams are definitely harder than others, but if you study the material, it's completely attainable. I don't think I would be as prepared for CHEM2222 or the MCAT if I took someone else. Genuinely the best.

Amazing and sweet person! She's very open to questions and explains things very well. Exams are very difficult (as everyone has pointed out), but they're doable if you study about a week in advance. Best tip I can give is to practice practice practice; you need to be very familiar with all of the content in order to stand a chance on her exams

Dr. Hare's test are genuinely so difficult. You have to go to office hours almost everyday and make Orgo your life to get an A in this class. It's possible but would not recommend if you are taking multiple STEM classes or have a lot going on. She is incredibly smart and a good professor but a lot of the class is self taught from the nature of Orgo

She was an amazing professor. Really worked to make sure that students understood the material. However, her tests were extremely difficult, so if you are good at teaching yourself material, it's better to have an easier test with a different teacher.
Hare is great professor, but Orgo 2 is really hard. Incredibly cumulative and she doesn't make the exams easy at all. You need to put in a ridiculous amount of time for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Organic Chemistry is very tough, but Prof. Hare is such a good professor. Get ready to put a lot of time into this class, but Hare will help you mostly. Daily office hours, guides/visualizations, participation quizzes on Fridays, 3 exams and 1 final. Taking her again for Chem 2222
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures, everyday office hours (hurray for the new couch), extremely caring. Exams are slightly difficult, but u will get good grades if u practice enough and go to office hours. Hare's the best!

She is the nicest person ever. As a lecturer/professor however, she will cook the hardest exam in her lab and hand it to you with a very honest smile. The students who liked her class were usually never in class and liked studying alone. Again, she is a nice person not a good teacher. If I had a time machine, I would pick the other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bottom line: You will hate yourself but love Alissa

The second semester of Orgo starts off strong with Spectroscopy, but the synthesis content on exams 2 and 3 get more difficult just due to the cumulative nature of the course. She always took the time to review a concept from 2221 if needed, and gave real-world application, which made the course much more engaging. Tests are fast paced, but fair.

Dr.Hare is an incredibly intelligent professor who is passionate about what she does. Her lectures are consistent and outline exactly what she is looking for when it comes to exams. Outside of class, she is just as amazing; she hosts office hours outside when the weather is nice, brings one of her pugs occasionally, and really tries to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare may very well be the best prof at vandy. Orgo is a BRUTAL class! But, Dr. Hare is an absolutely phenomenal teacher and person. She began offering office hours every day of the week to help us more. I can't explain how great she is. I'm taking her again for CHEM 2222 if that's any indication. 1000000000000% take her! Best decision I've made

Dr. Hare is awesome. Her office hours are super helpful (she holds them 4-5 times/week). The only downside is the 50-minute exams are difficult time-wise, but if you take practice tests as if they were real, you'll be able to adjust. She is definitely still worth taking despite the shorter tests. Also, she sometimes brings her dogs to office hours!

Hare makes coming to class worth it. She's very knowledgeable, and answers ANY question, no matter how basic. She makes office hours as available as possible and also has open discussion board questions that she replies to within 12 hours. I recommend her 100% for orgo. Her tests might be hard, but you will excel if you put in the effort.
A fine choice

Dr. Hare is an amazing prof-- hands down my favorite professor I've had at Vandy. She cares so much about her students and has office hours (which she sometimes brings her dogs to) very frequently. She explains the content really clearly and even though her tests are hard, she prepares you for them. Def my favorite class this semester. TAKE HARE!!!

Orgo is a tough class, but you have to take it with Dr. Hare. Her help outside of class is unmatched, and you WILL NEED HELP to do well in this class. You may think you're doing well at the beginning of the semester, but you can't let off the gas, as the content gets much harder. You gotta go to class.

Dr. Hare is maybe the most caring prof at Vandy. The absolute sweetest woman ever. Absolutely insanely great professor. The tests are super difficult but Dr. Hare prepares you incredibly well. She is an amazing teacher that breaks a very tough class into very approachable material. Commit your life to orgo and you'll do well. Take Dr. Hare!!!!

Dr. Hare is amazing. Orgo is tough, that's a no-brainer, but she is makes sure everyone has the chance to succeed if they work for it. Go to office hours, do the suggested problems, and stay on top of the class lectures. And if you have questions, ask her! You can tell she loves teaching and wants everyone to understand the content.

Dr. Hare is an amazing teacher. She explains things clearly and really tries to give you an intuitive understanding of what is going on in a class that requires a lot of memorization. It is a hard class, but doing the suggested problems from the book will really help you succeed.

Dr. Hare is by far my favorite professor I have had at Vanderbilt thus far. Orgo is obviously super hard, but she gets the material across so well and gives you the right practice to succeed to the best of your ability. 100% take Dr. Hare's section.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Orgo sucks but if you have to do it Dr. Hare is definitely the best choice. She's nice and tries to make her lectures enjoyable so you don't jump off the top of Stevenson.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Like many of the other comments, Dr. Hare is the right choice to make for organic. She has detailed lecture slides and her office hours are incredibly helpful. However, this class does require a substantial amount of effort on your part, but if you do everything she says (practice problems, read book and slides, etc.), you will do well. Good luck!

Hare is great at explaining concepts in simple ways and giving examples for everything learned, but it's easy to feel like you know what's going on when you don't. Also, not a lot of transparency regarding what will be on the test and grade cutoffs. Very difficult exams require lots of practice and memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a really good lecturer and makes you actually learn the material. She does go pretty fast. The tests are harder than other sections, but you always know what to expect. It's not impossible to do well on them if you do a lot of practice problems. The curve isn't huge, but it's not unreasonable. I had an 88 in the class and got an A-.

Dr. Hare is very accessible outside of class (basically has office hours every day right before a test) and has always been helpful and kind in office hours. I dont agree with prior comments that she came off snobbish at all. I think people were upset the class wasnt curved very generously, but its a notoriously hard class with few As.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good but goes through content really really fast, doesn't slow down when asked to politely so take that as you will.

It may have just been this semester but also felt here that Dr Hare was unnecessarily harsh and snobby sometimes if you talk to her outside of class as someone previously mentioned. She is clear and teaches well in class, although very monotone and not very engaging although that may just be the nature of the subject matter.

I highkey agree with previous comments this semester, Hare is decent at actually teaching - but outside of class can be kinda pretentious and inaccessible compared to other profs I've had. Still a fine choice but don't expect to enjoy the class necessarily.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good at lecturing, clearly knows the material herself. Found her passive aggressive especially on exam weeks and not exactly the most accommodating however, doesn't personally care about students as individuals.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is great at explaining the content, but especially towards the end of the semester, her lectures were way too fast to follow- never knew you could have too many examples, because then she rushes through them. Very nice in class, but me and others have experienced a bit of harshness and snobby-ness outside of class. A fine choice, but not best

Dr. Hare is probably the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. Of all the pre-med courses I've taken, her class was easily the most organized and well-structured. She genuinely cares for students and wants to see us succeed. At times, it can be frustrating because the other Ochem section seemed significantly easier than Dr. Hare's.

Dr. Hare is compassionate, accessible, & fair. She truly wants her students to succeed. I would definitely recommend hershe is supportive, intelligent, organized, and explains concepts clearly & patiently. My advice for her class: do all recommend problems, read the book, go to lecture, & go to office hours! Ask for help when you need it! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests were difficult. If you had her the for the first part of orgo, then you know her style. I wouldn't recommend her to anyone who hasn't taken her before because the change is drastic. She actually makes you learn chemistry and it isn't for the faint of heart. Loved her though
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare is one of the best professors I have ever had. She somehow made organic chem enjoyable. My best advice would be to go to office hours. She cares about her students more than any other STEM professor I have had experience with, so she is more than willing to help out if you're struggling. 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Hare is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. She is kind and cares. The class is just lecture and the grade is based on 4 exams, a final, and discussion. She is accessible outside of class but office hours are generally packed. It's still nice to go and listen to others' questions though. She is also very quick to respond to emails and grade.

Dr. Hare's tricks and accessibility made this challenging course manageable. During the final, I had to call her because my internet went out during COVID and she was very understanding. A great choice if you really want to learn your stuff and are willing to work!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Cares about her students so much. Orgo is a tough class and she expects her students to work hard, but she makes herself super available. She holds many office hours per week and is always available to meet one on one with students. Without a doubt the best STEM prof I've had at vandy

Orgo is hard, and Hare's tests may be harder than other professors, but I have learned the most in her class. She pushes you to really understand the concepts rather than memorizing mechanisms. Make sure to go to class, do the homework, and go to office hours/email her if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare genuinely cares about her students and wants them to learn the material, not just freak out about grades. The class is tough, but if you read the book & pay attention in lectures you can manage. Build a relationship with Dr. Hare - she's awesome.

Take Dr. Hare for organic chemistry! She has wonderful handwritten notes and is always open to answer questions either in class or in-office hours. Her tests are very straight forward and she gives you plentiful practice problems so you feel prepared. Orgo is difficult, but she breaks it down to manageable pieces and truly wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare is probably the best professor I have had at Vandy. I took her for both semesters of Orgo and it was amazing. Orgo will be super tough no matter what but Hare gives you tons of practice problems, diagrams of reactions, and super helpful office hours to make sure you understand material. Hare is a rock star

Dr. Hare is one of the best, most caring professors at Vanderbilt. She takes a difficult topic such as Organic Chemistry and makes it manageable to the students. Her lectures walk step by step through an entire chapter, and she offers even more assistance in office hours (at some point you will be confused). Tests are a bit difficult but manageable
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare cares SO MUCH about our learning. The class is notoriously difficult, but she gives the tools to be successful. She explains things well, class goes a bit fast, but her lectures are supplemented by the textbook. Her exams have a rep of being hard, but they are really fair and transparent. Also offers extra credit assignments to boost grade
Great professor  Go to office hours

Dr. Hare is awesome! She hand writes notes so make sure you go to class. Exams are hard but all pretty straightforward, as she is very clear about her expectations, and although the questions take more thinking than homework, there's nothing crazy on the exam. You just got to learn the material and do the recommended problems she assigns.
Go! To! Office! Hours!

Might come off at first as a tough professor (she is) but an extremely effective one at that. Class is useful for getting your notes filled in, but in my opinion office hours are where you learn the most, whether it's your own questions or listening to others. I came in with no organic chemistry experience and left the class rather confident.

Dr. Hare is the best. Orgo is a rough way to go, but her exams are very straightforward. She really makes an effort to get to know her students and her passion for the subject comes out in her lectures (sometimes there are memes!). I've learned more from her than any other professor, and I highly recommend taking her if you have the chance!

Super sweet woman, amazing prof! As long as you put in the work, orgo is easy and completely manageable. She is very encouraging and kind, marks super leniently and gives extra credit. Also curves when necessary. Great office hours, easily accessible. Lectures explain concepts well, but she could provide more practice problems.

Dr. Hare is one of the best professors I have ever had at Vanderbilt. No matter what, orgo is going to be challenging, but she with her encouragement, extremely helpful office hours, passion for teaching, and great lecture notes, it is completely doable- exams are difficult but curved well. Please take orgo with Dr. Hare, you will not regret it!
Really nice/engaging in class Moves fairly quickly through material so you need to keep up Tests are hard but curved fairly Very helpful and understanding during office hours

I've been out of her class for a year now and just came back to write a nice review. Literally the sweetest teaching woman Ive come across in some years. Some profs do tough love but she just does love and <3 amazing teacher. you may have to teach yourself but at least youll have an encouraging teacher to watch in class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I love and respect Dr. Hare so much. She is great at explaining material and her office hours are very helpful. Orgo is hard regardless, but the structure of Hare's class enables just about anyone to do well if they're willing to put in the work. Don't miss out on her section if you have a choice.
Professor Hare is the best professor at Vandy. Do anything to take orgo with her, she really wants to see her students succeed and it is very possible to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The best science prof at school hands down. People hate the memorization but part of learning orgo involves memorizing the things you need for reactions. She has clear, easy to follow notes. She also offers extra credit throughout the semester during lecture. Use the reaction maps and handouts from class, they will help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Hare for both semesters of Orgo, and she is one of my favorite professors at Vandy. She is so nice, and she is always willing to give help if you need it. She is definitely pretty hard though. Her tests are long and sometimes have hard ?'s, but they are fair and you get a nice curve. Definitely recommend taking her if you can.

Dr. Hare is simply the best option. One of the best professors I've ever had, and she's super good at helping you understand the topic and being available. Tests can be hard, but they are very fair. She won't pull any tricks on you. Take her if you can. Amazing person as well.
Was almost in the Johnston class, but got Dr. H instead. Shes great. I learned a lot. Previous comment is spot on. Easy exams, but long.
Best professor I've had so far. It is true, her class is easy and people shoot themselves in the foot more than she does. But I dont think she can ask difficult questions given class size.

Prof. Hare is great. She is very organized and kind. Her exams are pretty trivial as she uses long tests to force you to make mistakes rather than giving actually difficult problems. Its the chemistry version of bio-sci, you can memorize your way to an A.

Professor Hare is an excellent instructor. Her lectures are very clear, although sometimes she may go a bit quickly. She is extremely accessible outside of class, and sometimes even brings in her dogs during office hours to let us play with them. Tests can be difficult and require clear understanding of the material, but the curve is large.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Orgo is an extremely difficult class. Hare explains the material well by mainly giving examples of how to work different problems. She is very helpful during office hours and gives partial credit, but her tests are incredibly difficult. She is the better Orgo teacher, but her tests expect you to have memorized everything. Orgo is hard regardless...
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best teacher I've had at Vandy. Notes are very clear and tests are straightforward. She knows the material well & explains it very well to students. Very accessible outside of class and occasionally gives extra credit. Good curve. To do well, show up each class, take the notes, review notes, do recommended book problems. I love the class structure.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She really cares about the success of her students and is VERY accessible outside of class. Exams are very straightforward and easy if you do the homework. The final was kinda brutal, but she gave a nice curve at the end. Her notes packet is organized and, after lectures, has all the info you need. You just need to copy down her examples from class
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Doctor Hare is awesome. She really cares about us and comes across as an expert on all topics. Exams are straightforward (easy in hindsight), but the time crunch and pressure make things difficult. She sticks to the book and throws no unexpected punches.

Professor Hare is phenomenal. She is very approachable and really wants her students to learn the material and do well in the class. Her exams can be absolutely brutal but the class has a generous curve.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Hare is such a nice person. Gets to know her students if you let her and is always there to help. Hard exams because she wants to push you but find a kid who understands it and you'll be okay. Goes very fast in lecture so you should read before or after if you want to comprehend. 9/10 overall

She is a great option if you are trying to learn organic chemistry. Lectures are very thorough and well organized. She is very helpful during office hours. The class is wayyyy more difficult compared to the other section. There is a scale to even out the averages. I would highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Hare is an amazing professor. She is the choice for orgo 2 if you want to learn. She structures her lectures very well and is incredibly useful in office hours. The exams are more difficult than the other sections, but the curve is great. The tests are very easy to ace if you do all the homework. Overall, she's the best choice for orgo.

Her lectures are great and she provides notes templates, so you don't miss a thing. There's also a curve on the class which is really nice because her tests can be tough. More than willing to meet with students to help them out at any point during the semester. Sometimes brings in her dogs to office hours.
great lecturer.  cupcake exams that are more difficult versions of the homework.  similar to a bio course, lots of memory.  equal to woman sulikowski, both great options.
Dr. Hare is great.  Really kind, obviously into the material.  Exams are super easy.  If you can do the integrated/difficult homework section, should be able to coast here

Dr. hare is a great professor. She cares about her students and she takes time to really explain everything. Her office hours are a great source of information and were very popular. Her tests are hard, but her final is easy. She has an extended grading scale, so a 93 is not necessary to get an A. She is the best choice for orgo.

Dr. Hare is a great choice for organic chemistry. The class is hard, but her lectures are clear and she gives you tons of opportunities to work with her outside of class. Dr. Hare also genuinely cares about her students - a much-welcomed change from many of the STEM professors I've had at Vanderbilt.

Dr. Hare is amazing. She really cares about her students and her door is almost always open. Read the textbook, do or don't go to class, study, and you'll be fine. She gets major bonus points for bringing in her adorable pugs to office hours!!

Dr. Hare is one of the most helpful professor's I have had. She is always available outside of class and is willing to respectfully answer any question, no matter how basic. She definitely is the best Orgo professor to take, as she teaches several more concepts and techniques. Make sure you go to office hours! Best professor I've had at Vandy.

Dr. Hare is one of the best professors I have ever had. She truly cares for students shown by her accessibility outside of class, and helpfulness during office hours. She is also a great lecturer and makes it crystal clear what she expects from her students. The averages are lower, but she curves the class. Do yourself a favor and take this class!

Dr. Hare is definitely one of the best professors I've had so far. She's super nice and helpful during office hours and does her best to make sure students really understand the material. You can tell she's really invested in her students' education. Tests have lower averages than Sulikowski's but she also curves. Definitely going to take her again

Dr. Hare is one of the most caring professors that you'll ever have. The class is tough, as is any OChem class, but her tests are fair and she is always willing to provide students with extra help. The note packets she gives out are incredibly helpful as study guides. Utilize her study hours and get to know her. She is definitely worth knowing!
Love Dr. H.  Great class, not too difficult.  I think she'll be even better next year as she'll be settle in and comfortable.  Really clear and fair.

This is for the sophomore classes.  If you are a freshman see Townsend or Rizzo.  Dr. Hare is great.  Friends from the other courses were attending the Hare section instead of their prof.  Nuff said.  This was a great year for Orgo teachers.
Great lectures, always helpful, and very personable - honestly one of the best professors I've had at Vandy. She is organized and makes orgo much more friendly and doable.

The best orgo professor in vandy. Now that she's found her voice teaching (she was new this year) she's a great confident lecturer who is eager to help &clear at communicating. It's impossible to dislike her, she really cares for you &gives clear expectations. Also, grades very generously with partial credit. Orgo is orgo tho, so make sure to try.
Great class.  Pretty reasonable and straightforward exams.  I would've preferred shorter exams with more difficult questions, but test are fair.  Generous grading.

When I'm a professional, I hope to be like Dr. H.  This semester has been a great life experience and I learned a lot of chemistry. Beyond science, I was able to interact with a dynamic, young, woman chemist.  That has made all the difference for me.
No brainer for sophomore orgo.  I think she's way better than male sulikowski and goes a bit more in depth than female sulikowski.  Eye candy.

Everything about Dr. H is by the book and straightforward.  I learned a lot.  Her lectures always go over though and the test are always too long.  I'd rather face interesting and difficult questions rather than a never-ending amount of easy ones.

Hare is a boss.  Her lectures can be a little bit dry, but they're essential to doing well on test.  Emphasis is placed more on the lecture than the book.  Overall, she cares.  If you do bad in the class, its completely your own fault.

Outstanding teacher for orgo.  Very clear and you can tell she is prepared (almost scripted) for class.  Its only my 4th semester here, but from my experience there are only 2 competent orgo prof's available. Both are new, young, and into it. If you're a sophomore I advise you to take Hare!  You'll learn a great deal.  She cares.
Still a young professor, but very excited about teaching. She will do everything she can to help you understand the concepts. Highly recommend her.

Although it took me a while to warm up to Dr. Hare's teaching style (it is a little monotonous and boring), I came out of orgo loving her. Since she is a new teacher she is still working out the kinks in her teaching style, but her expectations are clear and as long as you understand the concepts in her Powerpoints you will be fine.

Organic chemistry is a tough subject, but Dr. Hare gives super helpful notes that outline what you need to know for the exams (you literally just have to fill in the blanks). She is really young, so she is still excited to be teaching and eager to help everyone succeed. As long as you study and pay attention in class, orgo isn't that bad.

Castillo seems like a nice individual at heart, but she speaks to students like they're little children.  She is not very flexible and takes the CORE curriculum extremely seriously. Like, no one else is that strict about it. Just take another CORE prof; she isn't really worth it.

She's a very very nice professor, who cares a lot for her students. She was graceful with grading and sometimes let us skip readings if she felt the course was too dense. Sometimes the grading could be a bit vague but overall was a good professor and did what she could with a class many people don't want to take lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Castillo is super passionate but a tough grader. Readings & film discussions were very engaging (weird books). I found any feedback I got to be vague & unhelpful. Participation is super strict but she grants extensions if u need them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Was one of the best teachers in my life. Caring, incredibly nice, offers TEA in office hours. Grading is fair. Material can feel dry at times, but there is breadth in form (movies, novel, stories, articles) & genre so you'll find something you'll love. But if you aren't experienced w/ grammar/writing be prepared to work hard, and go to office hrs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She is clearly very thoughtful as a professor and incorporates a lot of cool modern texts / open-ended projects into her course. Cares a lot about students too! Her grading criteria is not particularly difficult but there is a lot of busywork style homework for a 4000-level course.

Professor Castillo's class was interesting, and her passion for Spanish American 20th century literature was evident. You are graded on participation, essays, and fishbowls (like socratic seminars). Make sure to put in the effort to read the texts and put in effort into the essays. Her grading criteria is tough, but I thought that it was fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The best professor I have ever had. She's super intelligent and clearly cares about her students. Her lesson plans were very well planned and executed and her grading expectations super clear. She was such a joy to interact with twice a week, really looking forward to taking another class with her.

She makes this class an awesome experience because you get to discuss cool texts while still never feeling any pressure. Readings are never too long, grading is very fair/generous, and she loves making class as fun and engaging as possible. Even the final project isn't too bad with all the checkpoints along the way. Must-take for Spanish majors!

Castillo is a beautiful person. She cares about students and their knowledge of the topic. She challenges you and wants you to do well but the class isn't easy. The reading is sort of hard compared to other SPAN Elects but she guides you through it all. Papers are a little rough but again, she wants you to succeed. Go hang out in her office!!

Prof. Castillo was fantastic. She was super supportive from the get go and the class was really interesting. Actually do the work and it wont take too long. Super interesting, too. Will def take another Castillo class if I can.

Truly one of the best professors at Vandy and a MUST-take. Every class session is meaningfully engaging and interesting, and there's never a feeling of having too much homework or reading for the class. Furthermore, she's a very fair grader and really helps improve your writing if you go to office hours. Take for a balance between fun and learning!

Castillo is really an exceptional member of the department. Her grading is very fair, and because she's not a native speaker she's more lenient with grammar. Drop by office hours, she'll help you with your thesis. She's also the kind of professor who is understanding during personal tragedies, so don't be afraid to reach out if you're struggling.

4 essays, 2 presentations, one MLA quiz, final project(no exam). You read five novels and lots of short stories which are the basis for the essays, so it is a lot of reading but she is a really great professor. She is normally a Spanish/Portuguese teacher so much of what you will learn in any class with her will pertain to latin american studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Castillo is an incredibly caring professor, but her class is hard. Expect a lot of work and tough grading, but paper rewrites make it manageable. Small class size + her enthusiasm make it easy to be involved and up to date in the course, but the sheer amount of work is a lot. If you put the work in, and she can tell, you'll end with a fine grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took him for CORE 2500 Italy and Asia. Extremely chill and very knowledgeable, and he keeps the class interesting and laid back. Graded on planned reading quizzes, a presentation, film review, impossible interview, and midterm (same as quizzes). He does ask for very specific details in quizzes, so read the texts closely. Take him for an easy AXLE.

Dr.Mirabile is a great professor.  He really cares about Italian film and wants to inspire the same love for it in his students.  His practice quizzes are very similar to the actual ones, so as long as you know those you will be fine.  He regularly offers extra credit for attending other Italian events.
Andrea is such a great dude and one of the chillest professors you will encounter at Vanderbilt. Italian Cinema is pretty cool stuff and he makes it a great time.
sweetest professor ever! just watch movies and read articles with a few quizzes , super fun class

Professor Mirabile created a great environment for us to practice our new Italian, and he made it entertaining to talk about new things. If you show you care and try, he recognizes that and you'll do well.

One of my fav professors at Vandy. Class was an easy A if you study a little for the quizzes, go to class, and do the homework. He was so funny and caring and hope to take more classes with him! Definitely take him!
Prof Mirabile is the best. Class is super fun and really easy. Show up, participate, do the homework, and you'll get an A
Most fun class at Vanderbilt- super nice and funny dude who just gives u an intro look at italian and runs bits the whole year. Would take again every semester.
Love this class and this professor!! He's very funny and puts in effort to make class engaging and entertaining. There are a few quizzes throughout the semester, but they were not hard.
By far the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt so far. He's hilarious and makes the classroom such a welcoming, low-stress environment.

Professor Mirabile is one of the nicest guys at Vanderbilt. Class is based on a few quizzes, midterm, essay, and presentation, but he grades super easily. Not hard to get an A if you just show up, do the work, and study a bit for the quizzes/tests. Don't need to pay attention in class, just need to show up.

While Professor Mirabile is very funny and knows his stuff about Italian cinema, he is not a constructive grader for a writing course. His grading criteria is very unclear and inconsistent. The course consists of 4 papers (including the final), a midterm, participation (if he bothers to learn your name), and a group project. Little outside work.

Professor Mirabile is one of the best I've had at Vanderbilt. He is clearly passionate about the subjects he teaches and it shows in his lectures. The class was never overbearing on work. My one complaint is having a group project in a writing seminar but other than that the class was a lot of fun. It is also easy to get an A with effort.

Definitely take this writing seminar. One group project and 4 essays, totally manageable. If you love film, you'll love this class as you get to explore the world of Italian cinema. His grading isn't bad at all. I didn't feel stressed in this class. Andrea's a great guy too, really cared about our class.

Andrea is a fantastic professor. He is very easygoing, and the things he prepared for class are so interesting. You just need to watch all the films (only 2 of them are required to watch outside the class) and really think about the things he talks about. Definitely take his ITA1111, and you will survive the first year writing seminar.

This class is a hidden gem! Andrea is hilarious and very easy going. Little to no homework. Only 1 big group project & 4 essays (not a significant portion of the grade). Fantastic selection of films and analysis of italian history through film. The class is fun engaging and laidback, especially for a writing sem. He was my favorite prof this year.
Funny teacher, interesting class.

He's an awesome teacher, and a native Italian speaker, though he can communicate very well in English too. He is my favorite professor so far. The class is pretty easy, as long as you study at least some before the quizzes! It's also a fun class because most of it is conversing with other students in Italian.

He may be awkward at times, but he is very funny. He works on speaking skills with Italian. When he collects the homework you'll have once every month, (small assignments), he's very lenient on when you turn them in. The tests are particularly easy as long as you pay attention in class. I don't spend more than an hour outside class studying.

Took the "Italy Through Cinema" Freshmen writing seminar. Interesting class, most of it watching movies with a midterm and a few short papers and a final paper comprising your grade. Harder grader on papers than you would think, but very willing to help!
Great!!!

I could not agree less with the previous comment.  This professor was incredibly helpful, always available and I found his classes to be awesome.  His teaching style was amazing.  I can't see how someone would put such mean things about Professor Mirabile.  He's a great professor.

Disorganized. The most you will learn is from the book.  When I had to take a make-up quiz, he showed up 30 mins late n forgot to record a grade for that quiz. Failed to learn any of the vocabulary.  Only watched videos. The class suggested teaching improvements 2 him n he ignored us. No hw. no suggestions how to improve my italian.
She is the most unorganized professor I have ever had. Also, she does not know how to explain. I taught myself everything this entire class (stats). Take other professors if you can!!!
Does too much, rambles, not a good prof

Unfortunately, she is retiring, but she was a great professor who clearly cared about the subject material and about her students. The workload for this class was heavier than other classes, but I also learned a lot more in this class than other classes. If the course is offered again by another professor, I would definitely recommend taking it.

Andrade is all over the place, disorganized, and I hardly learned anything from her lectures. Fortunately, because she knows so little about what shes teaching, the quizzes and exams end up being very easy (especially if you do the homework she assigns)
Absolutely terrible lecturer. Does not adhere to the syllabus. Probably the worst teacher ive ever had in high school or college. Do not take.

Pretty sure she is retiring, so this probably doesn't matter, but this was a very interesting class, and she is clearly passionate about the material which is nice. Not a hard class once you learn what they are looking for in exam/quiz answers. However, there is a lot of reading and attendance is important.
She is a terrible lecturer and does not understand her own syllabus

She's a nice professor and this is one of the easier econ electives to take,but like others have said the class is poorly designed. Participation is 20% of the grade which is comprised of attendance and surveys in each module, however 60% of the survey points are in the first 2 weeks. Grading on the quizzes/tests (a sig. % of your grade) is vague

This was without a doubt, the worst teacher I've had at any level of schooling. Completely unorganized, lectures have no structure, weekly quizzes that you barely learn. Seriously my kindergarten teacher was more competent. If you had the choice between drop out and take this class, drop out.

Professor Andrade is so sweet and has structured the class that worked really for me. The group projects are annoying but are manageable. Quizzes every week seems like a lot but it comes in handy when studying for the midterms because the content is still pretty fresh. Overall, loved the content and interacting with her.

She is highly knowledgeable+intelligent in the subject. Her lectures are interesting+in-depth. She provides all slides and reading material–all you need to get an A in the class. Study the slides and readings for the quizzes and exams and you will be fine. Many group projects, occasional unclear instructions, just need to ask for clarification.

Dr. Andrade is very smart and a great lecturer. She takes the time to get to know everyone's names and this class is one of the most interesting I have taken at Vandy. The quizzes can be tricky but once you learn how to study for them, you should be fine.

Oh my god, when I say she is the most amazing, sweetest soul to have ever grazed Vanderbilt campus, I mean it! all the assignments and expectations were really clear. the class is also fairly easy to follow, definitely the easiest econ elective so far. she's also so passionate about the class and it really shows. absolutely take her

I don't understand why her rate my is not higher! She is SO sweet, and makes it clear that she wants to help us get a good grade in the class. She drops the lowest group assignment score, lowest quiz score etc. Attendance is mandatory, but thats a free 20% to your grade. This is one of the easiest econ electives to do well in. TAKE !!!

I took this class last semester and she is a really amazing professor and the class is very interesting. Just study the powerpoints and readings before the quizzes and you should be able to get a good grade. Go to lectures because she takes attendance some days.

This class is extremely straightforward - go to class, take notes, do the homework, skim the readings, do some review for tests. She explains everything you need to know in class. The only hard parts of this class is that there are a lot of details that she wants you to memorize, and the readings can be long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easily one of the hardest classes in the department, but well worth if you take the time to do the readings. Requires a-lot of studying for all of the quizzes, but exams become easier than expected. Very sweet person, and is so passionate (so show her the respect!). The TAs are hit or miss, but grading can be flexible.

She is an exceptionally nice professor, eager to share her passion for Latin American economics. The readings and quizzes are quite straightforward. Although the group projects can sometimes be annoying, the course overall is amazing. She is understanding if you miss a day and is always willing to offer support.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was very interesting and the professor is very nice, but it did require a lot of reading and studying to do well. There are quizzes every week which are easy if you read the material and study just a little the night before. The midterm and final are tough and group assignments were annoying, but overall I enjoyed the class.

I liked my Latin American development class this semester. Lectures were boring at times, and reading was heavy at the start, but the course was interesting. Group assignments are graded very leniently, quizzes are easy if you actually read. Midterms and final are hard but curved. Prof is responsive by email and seemed nice

Really cares about the subject and if you're interested in the topic it's a good class. As far as Econ classes go it'll be the easiest one you take, however it's still tougher than most. Quizzes are annoyingly tough tho

This class was infuriating. She took a topic I was interested in and made me dread it. Be ready to remember every number, percent, and stat, from every slide. Homeworks are insufferably long and took an entire weekend depending on the group. I kid you not, I spent more time studying for this class than my stem classes.

Very nice professor, but poorly organized assignments, quizzes, and exams. Questions on quizzes are unnecessarily confusing. TAs grade assignments way too harshly. Not a hard class, just overcomplicated assignments to make up for the relatively easy course material.

I am shocked that these reviews are bad. She is super caring and has pretty decent lectures. There is a fair amount of work for the class, but it is manageable and easy. If you show up, pay attention, and can answer the reading questions, getting an A will be easy. Also, her lecture slides are extremely helpful and she always posts them.

Completely agree with the previous review. She's better than lots of other profs I've had in the econ department and the class is super easy. Pretty heavy workload but none of it is difficult -- just things you need to complete each week. Don't let the negative reviews dissuade you -- take 2220 with her for a very doable A.

I truly don't understand the bad reviews. As long as you show up, ask questions, and do the readings, you're almost guaranteed an A. She is a kind woman who cares about Latin Dev. I don't usually leave reviews but I wanted to counter the other ones because I don't get them. Don't shy away from her because of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mandatory lectures for participation points, lectures kind of drag on when you can just copy from the slides. Has no concept of time management so classes always run over time. Homework heavy with readings, videos, and group assignments, quizzes and surveys every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awful professor. Rude. Can barely understand her with her accent. Has no sense of how to be a good teacher. Just rambles about random stuff that happened to her as a kid in El Salvador.

Quite possibly the worst lectures I've ever experienced in my academic career. 75 minute class also went 20 minutes over almost every week, which interfered with other classes and was very annoying. Class material is pretty interesting but the lectures are not.

Her course is a disaster, the professor(technically she is a senior lecturer but who claimed herself as a professor) is disorganized, very ealiy be misled by another stupid classmate(who only asked without learning or preparing for class), if you want learn something, never go to her course because she will ask silly questions on calss.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She means well and is a good person, very passionate about Latin America. However, the class is poorly structured and disorganized. She doesn't give quizzes or tests back and takes of for minor issues. The content is relatively easy, but dry. If you do the work, study, and show up to class, an A is doable. She also inaccessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Creates study guides that are supposedly based on the assigned readings, but sometimes asks questions that are not anywhere to be found. Hard to understand and does not explain the difficult concepts. Sometimes she'll teach a concept with one name and use another name on the test. Going to lecture makes material more confusing but factors in grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very difficult to understand. It is also hard to understand what is going on in class and she just lectures the entire time. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is a solid choice for an econ elective if you are prepared to put in the work. Her study guides are identical to the quizzes and midterms weren't too bad but you have to put in the time. The class was pretty boring but easy to get an A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super boring lectures full of information copied from other places. She doesn't give back any of the quizzes or midterms in class so you can't see what you lost points for unless you go to office hours. Quizzes are pretty easy but the true/false can be unclear.

It was meh overall. Lectures recount reading, but they aren't inclusive to what we are expected to know. So if you do the reading, then you are terribly bored, and if you don't then you are unprepared. Ambiguous grading at times as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory. There are seven quizzes and two tests with a final. Lots of info but easy to memorize. She gives you study guides for all of this. If you go to class and listen to lecture these are easy. She is not very engaging and has a Spanish accent but is very kind. If you go to office hours she will tell you what questions to expect.
Not difficult if you do the readings and go to the review session. She takes class participation to heart. Overall thought the class content was interesting. Friendly to talk to during office hours.

For my semester she hosted review sessions before tests, where she'd tell you the exact answers for test problems if the right questions were raised. Otherwise hunting for answers from readings would've been difficult. So try to go to those classes. Didn't enjoy memorizing dates & numbers as I don't believe it's the right approach to hist or econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It is as if her goal is to waste her students' time. I have never been in any other class with so much useless busy work. She takes attendance twice a class, so you are forced to sit there and listen to her ramble about topics that you already had to learn on your own to complete the homework.

Basically a history class, there's very little econ concepts. She is a very nice woman and if you go to her she will likely bump up your grade. Tests are very straightforward and curved, attendance is counted. If you do all the work/readings, which isn't that much, and study, you should definitely be able to pull an A (especially with the curve).

This prof has the right idea - teaching economics in a historical perspective, the way the discipline was meant to be. However, her disjointed organizational skills are clear, and it can be tough to follow along. Test material is extremely unclear, and the way she has you "hunt & gather" answers from academic articles is extremely disrespectful.

One of the easier Econ courses, but overall a bit stressful of an experience because its hard to gauge how well you're doing in the class. Curved tests and an end of the semester curve made everything work out in the end though.

Solid option--one of the easier Econ courses. It's really more of an Econ history course than anything.
