Professor Andrade is quite nice and really tries to make sure students learn the material, which consists of some memorization and lots of basic knowledge. The group project is very difficult--watch out for it. Kind of boring, but fine overall.

Tough, history material-heavy class with a really hard final. However, Professor Andrade is an exceptionally kind and caring person who is more than willing to work with you in office hours to improve your grades.

Latin Amer Development was more of a history class than an econ class, IMO. The exams were extremely reliant on memorizing events/dates/people/policy and consisted of T/F, 4 short essays, 2 long essays. The grading is very subjective, overall. Whom'st've graded the exams was brutal. I'm pretty sure there was an enormous end of semester curve, tho.

The class had little structure and did not follow the syllabus, but was easy for the economics department. Make sure that you attend class and skim the readings at the very least because participation (and showing up) matters in the end. Lectures could be drawn out at times but the content was kind of interesting. Tests were mostly straightforward.

Latin American Development is a great class. Andrade's lectures are super straightforward and interesting. Participation matters so don't skip class! Andrade provides study guides to go along with the readings that are very helpful for the tests. Overall, a great class!

Unclear syllabus . Grading was really strange - she dropped a bunch of quizzes and a project (which helped your GPA). Tests were hard, mainly because it was difficult to follow along in class, so you learn from her powerpoints. She often canceled office hours. But, there was not much work outside of class and she definitely curves grades A LOT.

Andrade's class isn't hard, and there are large amounts of past material available, but her voice is severely irritating in the morning. This class isn't as easy as other people make it out to be, but an A is very doable provided you put in the work.

I took this class before with another professor, and the difference was remarkable. Although this section was also plagued with a changing syllabus and unclear grading criteria (problem across all sections), prof Andrade made up for it with helpfulness and kindness in class. Best option for econ stats by far.

The class isnt ridiculously easy, but it's also a class that introduces statistics to economics, so that makes sense. She is super nice, and extremely helpful. Although she had to extend time on the final and some seemed to struggle, it's just how it goes, and it wouldn't make sense for a cumulative final (covering 10 chapters) to be much simpler.

Quite unclear and disorganized.  Test grading is fairly easy, but beware of the final -- it's absurd.  She is really inconsistent, and her final exam was totally unreasonable.  Very nice woman, to be sure, and she seems very knowledgeable, but she didn't stick to the syllabus at all and was unpredictable.  Take with someone else if possible.
It was very frustrating being in Andrade's class. She will get sidetracked frequently and completely ignore explaining concepts vital for understanding the material.
The class was very unclear. Grading was really slow. You know it is a problem when the day before the test a teacher uploads 4 study guides. Avoid at all costs

Easy class, especially if you have prior experience in Stat. Has a slight Salvadorian accent, but very understandable. Posts all lecture notes online. Class based in Excel, so you get lots of useful experience. An hour or two before the tests should be enough to get an A/A-. Projects can be a pain, and the grade depends on TA. Overall good prof.

Not a difficult class, but lectures are difficult to understand; I got a lot more out of just pouring over her posted lecture notes before tests. Helpful in office hours, though. Attendance isn't required, but that can be a downward spiral in terms of staying on top of the material. Easy A if you put in a night or two of studying before each test.

This class is not too hard but it requires a lot of independent study. Lectures are boring and hard to follow so you will probably end up learning everything from the textbook on your own. The textbook is good so its not a problem. Easy A if you prepare for every test and quiz. Tests are curved. She cares about how much you learn. TA is useless.

I found her incredibly hard to follow in class - I often left more confused than when I went in. The class is entirely in Excel, and it doesn't work very well with Macs, so beware of that as well. Maybe she's better with upper level classes, but I would not recommend her for an introductory course teacher.

Pretty easy class. Average test grades are in the low 90's. Group projects are relatively easy. Notes are given in a PDF and posted on OAK. If you took AP Stats in high school, then this class will feel like nothing.

This class is a must-take for any Econ major. The tests are a joke, and do not change much year to year. The project is annoying, but it is graded easily. 2 midterms. 1 exam. 1 paper. Easiest econ class you will find.

Pretty much a must take for Econ majors since your not going to get an easier Econ class. Andrade is really nice and tests are straight from your powerpoints that she posts online. Beware though, the group/individual paper is atrocious. Very lenient grader

Take this class (but with her, not the other professor). She genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. Go to class and take good notes because that is exactly what she tests you on. If you are an econ major and didn't take this class, that was a bad move.

Lectures are somewhat boring, reading straight from slides, and Andrade posts slides online before class. Attendance sheet passed around randomly though. Test questions directly from old tests and online sample tests. Andrade is a hard/picky grader, but if you argue her grading she'll bump up your score.
Boring lectures Easy class

This class was the easiest econ class I have taken at Vandy.  She values attendance, so make sure you go to class.  She posts all of her notes online, and the test questions are taken verbatim from her sample tests and power point notes.  As long as you review the notes and the sample tests, reading the textbook is unnecessary.  An easy A

This class is somewhat interesting but the lectures are mindblowingly painful and boring to attend. The tests are harder than they should be because of the way she grades them. Stay away from this class if at all possible.

insanely smart guy, like genuinely this is the class that i have learned the most from, but the reading quizzes felt excessive. you have one almost every day for 50-90 pages of content heavy articles. other than that, there's two exams and two homeworks. you also don't know what he's grading for in advance.

I absolutely LOVED Professor Coe. PSCI 2222 was one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. Expect lots of reading and frequent quizzes, but he offers a generous curve and drops the lowest quiz grades. He's an expert in the field and truly wants students to succeed in and beyond the classroom. I strongly reccomend taking his class

Professor Coe is insanely educated on WMD, and is very passionate in his lectures. This class is possibly the most difficult I have taken at Vanderbilt; however, the content is interesting and made me stay committed to the class. 3 HW, 2 Exams, but averages on assignments were ~ 70%. He curves at the end, but be prepared to get some poor grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Coe is an expert in his field, and it shows, so much so that he's intimidating. PSCI2275 was by far the hardest class I've taken content-wise, but you get a pretty generous curve. Between 3 homeworks, a midterm, and a final, sometimes the class average was in the 60s uncurved. Coe will make sure you know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: PSCI 2171 is a weird class because it only has lectures once a week and most of the grading is dependent on your research work. Dr. Coe is sweet and cares a lot about his students, but the lectures/textbook for the class component are somewhat dry (still interesting) and because there are no tests few people pay attention to the course content.

My favorite professor all-time. I took both of his undergraduate classes and they were my 2 favorite classes through all 4 years. Amazing lecturer, interesting material, etc. etc. If you think you'll be interested in the course content then you will love these classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 3 problem sets, midterm, and final. Psets are easy if you go to office hours. Assigns lots of reading, but I did none of it and got good grades on everything. Prof Coe is a fantastic lecturer, and the material is interesting. Take his course, and be willing to put in slight work. Not much, but enough to show you're actually learning. Well worth it.

Professor Coe is clearly very intelligent. He's nice but can unintentionally come off as condescending sometimes. The course material is super interesting but the assignments are graded pretty tough but he curves the grades at the end but you won't know until your last exam. You don't have to do the readings all the time cause he goes over them.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Homework assignments (3 of them) are graded very harshly. Class averages were usually about 70%, and he does this on purpose to "prepare you for real world". He does curve the class at the end, but overall pretty tough. Class also seemed more like a sociology class than political science. He lectures all class, is nice guy overall
Professor Coe is the man. My favorite classes at Vandy were the two he taught. If you get the chance to take either 2274 or 2275 do it, the material is interesting and his lectures are great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was probably my favorite class I've taken at Vandy. Very reading-heavy but it's all really interesting material, and you should be fine just skimming it, as he tends to go over it in class. He can be a difficult grader, but he gives a pretty generous curve at the end of the semester. Dude knows what he's talking about, helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Coe is the greatest of all time! He could explain paint drying and it would be interesting. His lectures are fantastic, he actively promotes student engagement/questions, and even the homework assignments are cool thought experiments. Can't recommend him enough, especially his Weapons of Mass Destruction class!

Professor Coe is the best Vandy professor I've ever had. He is crazy intelligent, funny, interesting, and great at explaining the material. He is a tough grader so initial grades seem scary, but says he will curve at the end. I will be taking every class of his that I possibly can!

Professor Coe had interesting ideas, but overall lectures were boring reading summaries. Homework was insanely difficult as you had to basically guess what he wanted. TA did all the grading and wasn't helpful with feedback. He graded on a curve so you had no idea what your grade was all semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Just started at Vandy and still adjusting (i.e. makes California jokes and assumed we were rich, smart, and lazy, etc.) Grades harshly, but whole class curved. 3 HWs (10% ea), 10% participation, 25% midterm, 35% final. Study guides for midterm and final, but still hard. HWs consist of 4 SA, but can only write 1500 words MAX per homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a solid teacher that listened to feedback. Extremely manageable class, extra credit, she is clear and moves at a reasonable pace. Great option for 1300.
She's demanding but great
Really hard class, had to teach myself the material basically because her teaching style didn't make any sense to me.

Reviews are harsher than they should be. Dr. Helmke is very receptive to feedback and made real improvements throughout the course such as slowing the pace down and pushing assignments back so students had time to master the material. She's corny, does her best to make a hard topic manageable, and curves exams nicely with extra credit. Solid option
Great Professor wants her students to do well.

People are too harsh because the class is hard and she can be corny. Regardless, she is a young, incredibly intelligent, and feedback-oriented professor. Many of the 1-star reviews on here were in her 1st or 2nd time teaching, and she has worked to accommodate student feedback and create a good class.

People are way too harsh on Professor Helmke. She is super nice and cares about students doing well in her class. She was super responsive to feedback and wants to continue to improve. She curved the midterm and the final was fair. The class is a bit harder than the other business mods, but Helmke is a solid option.
This is the worst class I've ever taken in my entire life.
So I gave her a bad rate my professor score but then she actually took our feedback and adjusted. You can tell she really cares. I just think this is a hard topic.

She's the perfect example of why not every finance professional should be a professor. She may have gone to Wharton and worked at Lazard, but she can't teach to save her life. She hands out harsh grades, puts in the bare minimum effort, and I honestly don't know why she's still allowed to teach here. Students deserve far better from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Dr. Helmke is one of the best teachers I have had. She is very smart, professional, and unlike many other professors, she is challenging us to learn new things. I wish every professor were like that. I definitely recommend taking her classes if you wish to succeed in your professional career.
This is the worst class I've taken in my entire life never take this ever.
Do not take Ever

I interned two summers on trading desks, so investments were easy, but the class's corporate finance and projects sections were extremely tough. Prof. Helmke a Wharton PhD, is crazy smart. Group projects are frustrating - groups of 6 are inefficient. Solo work would've been better. Still, I loved the content and the class despite the challenges.

Not as easy like other business classes, especially if you're not from a quantitative major. Midterm was challenging, final / quiz / problem sets very reasonable. There is lots of extra credit opportunities and fun projects, like watching a finance movie. If you're willing to put in the work you can learn a lot. Prof. Helmke is very knowledgeable.

Midterm was very tough but she adjusted by making the final easier. Not very accessible outside of class. Very knowledgeable about finance but she just kind of assumes that everyone else in the class understands what she is saying. Problem sets are done in groups but they are really tough. First time professor so she'll probably improve over time

Here's my thing - I think she is a super funny, cool person and I'd really like her if not for her insanely hard tests. She worked at Lazard, so is super smart, but not a great teacher especially when none of us know anything about finance. Final was MUCH easier than midterm and it's her first time teaching, so I think she will continue to adjust.

doesn't seem to know what students struggle with and how to approach teaching different subjects. Also don't you ever question her test questions or anything, she gets super defensive despite putting stuff on she didn't teach

This class was miserable. She is a very smart woman, probably too smart to teach college kids. She told our class that she wouldn't tell us what was on the exam unless 90% of the class filled out her course evaluation. Safe to say her evaluations were not pleasant.
She was too smart to teach this class. She acted like we understood it how she did and was just telling us what was on the slides instead of teaching it. Would not recommend.

Horrible-Her midterm was stupidly hard with stuff we hardly talked about. She also included topics we learned in the class before with no problem, hw, or anything to practice prior. Avg was so low she curved it by giving partial credit to the 3 free response questions even though much of the work could not be shown as it was typed on the computer.

Has such an attitude below the surface and is pretty horrible at teaching the concepts. Also very unclear at what to study and what is on the test. She didn't tell us what material to look at for the final until like a day before since she didn't get 90% of the class to fill out a course evaluation and then she comes in blaming the people in class.

Lectures were helpful, but this class is way too difficult for an intro business class. Of course the professor finds the questions easy since she has a PhD from Wharton, but for those of us with no previous exposure to finance, they are quite difficult. I took notes, was engaged in class, came from a math/econ background, and still struggled.

For an intro class, this course was ridiculous, and people who are literally working at top banks for IB/ PE struggled. She made all outside assignments incredibly difficult/time-consuming and not similar to the lectures as an "incentive to study for the final." Midterm was insane, she had to curve it because everyone would've failed otherwise.

Professor Helmke is SUPER smart, but she made this Intro finance course significantly harder than it should be. We have three take home quizzes and I spent 2 hours on the first one and still got a 60 after attending every lecture and taking notes. The problem sets are extremely complicated and nothing like we've done in class. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was an ok professor. My only issue with him is that he wouldn't put grades in a lot of the time which would not give us enough time to revise or inquire about any of our assignments. I got meets expectations for every assignment he graded and I come to find out after the semester ended that I had some does not meets which I had no idea about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a very collaborative class that doesn't consist of lots of lectures. However, he would go on tangents often. The class was very easy but that is just the nature of the class nothing to do with him. He is very lenient with late work. He first language isn't english however he was very easy to understand just occasionally misspelled things.

Prof. Taneja is a very caring and kind professor, but the class was very boring. The readings and movies we watched were great, but lectures were very mundane. He is an easy grader and is definitely passionate about what he teaches.
This class was honestly so boring. There is so much readings, and the lectures are so dry and boring. The professor cares and he grades pretty easily, but not worth the boredom of the class.

Intro to Islam was a very engaging and easy class. Films every week and you have to write a 2-page paper for 4 of them. Discussion posts and reading before every class, but you can get away with skimming over them. A different topic every week, which was a great structure. Dr. Taneja was incredibly nice and understanding, values participation a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've taken two classes with Prof. Taneja, and he is one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. Above all else, he's a caring professor, and he's attentive to the needs and situations of his students. The class is reading-heavy, but it's always interesting material and my friends and I often end up discussing it outside of class. 10/10 recommend.

Anand Taneja is one of the kindest people I have ever met, professor or not. In terms of the class, this translates to him being very accommodating, open to all questions, and assignments being graded with leniency. The TA, Austin, is also great. I learned a lot from this class and only wish it had been in person. Expand your horizons and take him!

Professor Taneja is a gem. His classes are interesting and he goes above and beyond for his students. His picks for textbooks are solid and the way he engages the class is next level. I didnt expect much taking the course, but honestly, it was a really good time. Id definitely take another class with Professor Taneja if given the opportunity.

Professor Taneja is extremely knowledgeable about Islam, and the class covers a lot of material. Each week consists of a film related to the lectures, and I found these to be very helpful and meaningful. Overall, the class deepened my knowledge greatly.

Dr. Taneja's class was great. The class is entirely discussion-based, and there are some writing assignments where you have to write a response to some films. I came in with little background on Islam, and I came out learning a lot. Very easy class too. Much of your grade depends on attendance, participation, and discussion posts. Great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Islam in the Modern World is an amazing class, we compare readings to films and those are our major grades for the semester. They are short papers only 2 pages and are actually pretty fun to do.

I took Islam in the Modern World and consider it to be one of my most valuable Vanderbilt experiences. Taneja leans left, but I am conservative, and felt that everything I contributed was deeply valued as long as I spoke articulately. The class is discussion based and very loosely formatted, which played to my strengths but might not be for all.

Absolutely loved being his class, Islam in the Modern World; it's an interdisciplinary and cross-cultural approach of such a complex issue. We had many different backgrounds in the class, and he handled it very well, opening discussion on controversial topics while offering facts during the lecture for background.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor with insightful lectures and discussions. Plenty of readings, but they're manageable and interesting. You'll come out with a much better understanding of modern Islam in the middle east and elsewhere; papers/blog posts are short and fairly open-ended. A must-have professor before graduating from Vandy.

Islam in South Asia with Professor Taneja is the best class I ever took at Vanderbilt. He has an amazing knowledge of South Asia, and our papers are literally based on classical Indian movies. For anyone passionate about the Indian subcontinent or just wanting to learn more, this is the class to take, and the professor to take it with!!!

It's pretty attractive to hear him speak in Arabic. He's very helpful and fun to talk to. His grading is to the point; just know how to explain yourself and dont make general claims in papers that you can't support. He is very understanding if you just talk to him. He's kind of blunt. Told me my paper was a mess (:'( ), but I fixed it and got an A-

He was great at facilitating class discussion and even when he stopped to just lecture it was very interesting. Probably one of the more important classes I have taken in terms of personal growth. Does not always have the most organized syllabus or clear rubrics but is very reasonable and will work with you to shift deadlines, etc. GREAT PROFESSOR

Professor Taneja is really knowledgeable about the subject matter and teaches from interesting and eclectic sources: movies, ethnography, philosophy, novels. I found the sources to come together in a profound and coherent way. I took Intro to Islam and Reformers of the Islamic Tradition with him. He's very helpful outside of class too.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He is new and has no idea what he is doing. Class is jumbled and makes no sense. If you voice an opinion different than his, he automatically shoots you down and makes you feel awful. There is absolutely no structure or clear guidelines on anything, even if you ask. Because of this, grades are arbitrary.
Excellent professor!

Prof Taneja is young, passionate, and enthusiastic about what he teaches. He really tries to engage and foster class discussion. If you go to class, pay attention, and participate in discussion (aka put forth some real effort), the class will be a good experience (maybe even enjoyable as I found it).

absolutely hated this class, worst class taken at vanderbilt. professor is rude, grades unnecessarily hard and class topics are random and dont seem to follow and cohesive order that would increase knowledge in the subject area.

Often has no idea where the class is heading. He expects you to respond in class but you can make your way through it if you throw around complicated, half-baked ideas. He assigns a lot of reading but if you're really interested in religion studies you would like them. Warning: CAN play favorites. You'll notice it in his class interactions.

She is such a nice professor, and while her expectations are clear, she just wants the class to be an intriguing experience for everyone. However, while there is little room to miss class due to the mandatory attendance, it is still very manageable to get a good grade as there is a decent extra credit boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I am currently enrolled in this course and am surprised to see any low ratings! She is an INCREDIBLY kind, understanding, and knowledgeable professor. Even at 8:40 AM, she makes class engaging and easy to follow. SO easy to make an A but mandatory attendance. I would highly recommend her to anyone needing a psych credit!
She is fantastic !!!

3 tests are 60% of your grade. The other 40% is basically from hw completion so it's an easy 100 there. The second test is pretty hard but the others aren't, take detailed notes during lectures bc notes will answer the majority of the test for you. Def do the reading if you want a good grade, easy A if you put in effort and take notes in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is really boring and very structured.  She's robotic and doesn't engage with the class at all really.  You have mandatory textbook quizzes for HW before every class.  Positives are that she's kind and the tests are open-note.  That being said, I'd avoid this class unless you really need a upper level psych class to fill a requirement.

She is really kind, I do not see why other comments are so negative. I like psychology so I loved the content she taught and did not find it boring. She did talk EXTREMELY fast and you have to get used to her speed but you can always raise your hand to ask her to repeat. Make sure to do inquizitive before class and tests are open note and open book

The easiest class ever. Not sure why other reviews are so low. Open note quizzes and exams. Quizzes on InQuizitive so you can answer unlimited questions til you get 100. On exams, you can use notes, google, textbook, etc. I think class exam avgs were As and Bs. You need extremely detailed lecture notes. Lectures were recorded. There is extra credit

If you're looking for an interesting psychology class this isn't the one. Every single class was the exact same-her going through the powerpoint while the entire class tries to note every word. That being said every exam is open-book and she records all of her lectures. Easy A if you take notes.

I am just genuinely disappointed in this class. I understand that covid made it hard to teach but it feels like she just pulled together a bundle of purchased material and useless assignments online for the sake of making this class. We don't get to engage at all except answering poll questions and writing reflections. It's just her lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Seriously, don't take her class. It's not going to be worth your time. Her homework is through InQuizitive which is very time consuming and useless. Exams are more difficult than what she teachers. Read the book very closely bec she expects you to know every single detail on it. She isn't very considerate of student's circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I've never left a negative review, but her class is truly bad. Not a Vanderbilt level class. No real engagement, lectures are dry, exam is ridiculously specific. Every detail is fair game. Personality was supposed to be such a fun topic but our cam and mic needed to be off at all times. Felt like I was in a grad student's class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I assume you're taking 3110 for reqs, not because you actually care about the economics of poverty. Lectures are boring – I barely went to any. There's 2 midterms, non-cumulative. Final is a presentation. My advice: forget going to class. Study problem sets / practice exams. Be warned, solutions are often incorrect. Not an easy A. A- if you work.

These ratings were super deceiving. Easy to get a B but definitely not an easy A at all, the grade cutoffs are very unclear. Problem sets are not bad but they are time-consuming. Tophat attendance is part of your grade so you must go to class. Exams are a large percentage of your grade so make sure you do well

Not sure why all the reviews for this professor are so positive. Lectures were very boring and attendance is mandatory for TopHat. Your grade in this class is fully dependent on midterm/final which isn't unusual for Vandy econ classes. This class should be guaranteed B for anybody, but getting an A was a lot more difficult than expected.

He is a super chill prof and clearly insanely smart. A great mix of theory and empirical examples of the concepts. Very interesting subject material, too. The concepts can be tough to grasp, but he does a great job of explaining them, and the psets are great practice. Great class with great proff.
He doesn't have the most interesting lectures, but his explanations in class are mostly clear and exams mirror problem sets and problem sets reflect his lectures.

Straightforward lectures that reflect what's on the problem sets and problem sets that reflect what's on the exams. Paper requirement wasn't hard. Nice guy who's willing to answer questions and clarify anything that's confusing. Interesting material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best 3000+ ECON classes to take. Non-cumulative exams and problem sets make up the entire grade. Tests are curved and class is curved. Tests aren't easy A's, definitely have to understand the material. Lecture notes are super important, the slides online aren't detailed. Really good guy who cares about students, even tho sometimes tough.

I highly recommend this professor. His lectures were straightforward and easy to follow, and the tests and problem sets reflected what was taught in class. There is no textbook, so you must attend class. Much of the material overlaps with the material from Labor Economics. He has a mellow, funny personality.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He can be a little scatterbrained during class, but he's overall a great professor. If you're really paying attention in class, his lectures are easy to follow and welcomes questions. Tests are fairly easy (if you study), as they are similar to problem sets and examples seen in class.

I never rate on this site but I feel so strongly that Moro does not deserve the rating he has. He is a great guy and is very funny in class, and he means well, but HE IS NOT EASY! I saw his ratings and took this class as an easy A. I am on the brink of failing now. His lectures are very scatterminded and unclear, and his tests are hard to predict

Most interesting econ class I've taken. Actual classes are kind of dry, but subject matter is interesting. Moro is a chill guy and will help you if you go to his office hours. With a little effort, you'll get a B fairly easily. Some of his test questions are sketchy, so an A might be harder to come by.

His class wasn't bad. Midterm and an Exam. 5 Problem Sets. Problem sets took maybe 1-2 hours. The Midterm and Exam had about 5-6 semi-easy/not difficult questions and 2-3 semi-hard/difficult questions. He curves the class at the end. Most classes are boring and pointless. Nice guy. Boring lectures. Easier and less work than most econ classes.
No Comments
Goat my goat what more can I say

It is nearly impossible to show up to Dr. Amat's class and not succeed. She has very clear expectations for exams and is not afraid to share them with you. Lectures are directly related to homework and exams. Great professor!
Very easy class, didn't grade hard and never gave questions that strayed at all from covered material
Dr. Amat is amazing! She is very clear about what will be on exams, and is always willing to answer questions. There is extra credit on each test. Take Dr. Amat for digital systems!

If you get one decision at Vanderbilt: Professor amat is the GOAT for circuits. Very lecture heavy but she kept it upbeat. Homework was hard and would take hours to finish but left me over prepared for tests. She's a fair grader and always available to give feedback or answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: ECE 2112: Dr. Amat is amazing. Despite how busy she is, she always seems to find the time to help a student out. Although her lectures were a little hard to follow at times, her exams were very straightforward.

FOR ECE 2112: Dr. Double A the woman you are. She is so nice and cares way more about student's mental health than their performance in circuits. The content of circuits is generally challenging but with Dr. Amat, you won't need to stress about performing well in her class because her exams use the simplest examples that are covered in class.
She's a great prof. Would recommend taking once at Vanderbilt !

Very nice professor who cares about the students' learning. her classes can get boring but ask questions to keep yourself engaged. She is good at answering questions and follows up with email if she finds a better resource. exams graded very generously.

super easy ece module. pretty boring lectures, 3 homework assignments, final project and quiz, all very easy and she tells you almost exactly what's going to be on the quiz. she definitely likes her students and is very approachable for help. nice grader and makes sure the class is an easy A.

Super nice professor. She posts slides for every lecture, but make sure to go to class especially near the end of the semester because the material gets confusing if it's not being explained properly. She's also really flexible about office hours if you ask.
Exams are super easy and she practically tells us what each question will be covering.

Prof Amat is super chill and nice. The slides can be unclear at times but if you ask her about content after class she is always happy to help and explain it fully. The class is graded on just a couple of things but the exams are easy because she posts detailed study outlines and has robust review sessions. Would recommend taking this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a very boring class. Professor Amat reads almost directly off of the slides and did not know how to explain the information from the lecture. There were many times where questions on the lecture slides would be answered "I don't know" by her. Not impossible but def will have to teach yourself.

3 tests, all got study guides she made based off of what we did in class. If you studied the vocab from the study guide and generally understood one or two readings (not mandatory to go to class, doesn't grade participation), you will get an A. Amazing person, super understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think the topics are interesting in this class but it is not really a discussion course so you kind of will just sit there and listen to her opinions on the topics, read the articles because she gives pop quizzes and just study all of the definitions she gives you

A lot of readings but the readings were very interesting. Participation does count towards your grade but it wasn't hard to participate at all. The discussions were always insightful and I learned a lot in this class. There are pop quizzes but if you stay on top of the readings, you will be fine. Exams were straightforward and the project was fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lovely professor. Learned an incredible amount but didn't have to break my back. Participation and attendance mandatory. Would 100% recommend.

Kinard is an amazing teacher & kind person. Her class mostly consists of discussing texts and her views, but she is extremely knowledgeable and well versed with words. As long as you participate in class and ask questions, you will do well. Also, seek help in office hours - she gives great advice for essays; this usually translates to a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Kinard is very well-versed in her subject and a nice, caring professor. Make sure to read the required readings and participate in class and you'll be fine. Most can be found online as PDFs so I don't know if the textbook is necessary. There are three essays and the first essay's revision counts as the entire grade for that paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Kinard is really easy to talk to, and the class itself is pretty easy. There are pop quizzes often, so you need to know what the main topics of the readings were. The final was fairly easy if you studied the vocab and readings and you need a basic understanding of how to identify particular material (ie. personification). Papers are doable.

Chance to revise 2 out of 3 essays, and all essay due dates were pushed back. Brought our class candy on Halloween. Occasional pop quizzes, but just do the reading and you'll be okay. Super sweet and understanding lady who provides easy, nonstressful introduction into college for freshmen. Take her and you won't regret it.

One of the easiest writing seminars, very little reading, flexible due dates. The professor gives great feedback for revisions and her grading is very fair. You can (thankfully) revise 2 out of 3 essays. Easy assignments and pop quizzes. Flexibility in devising your own essay prompt. If you are taking a first year writing seminar, take this one!
She is a nice and interesting professor. The course materials are very inspiring and insightful. I recommended my friends to take her class.

Dr. Kinard was a great prof and perfect for a first semester of college. If only I had taken the help she always offered, I would have probably earned an A, but at least an A-. Most readings for the class were short, which was really nice, and the topic was very interesting.

Very easy for a W course, but she really wants to get to your level and improve you from there. Classwork is easy to keep up with,and she is just a really nice lady. One of the first professors I had who understood teaching is not about huge volumes of impossible work.

Dr. Kinard is one of the nicest people I have ever met.  She cares about her students and is willing to meet with you.  Her expectations for her students are more than reasonable and if you take the time out to really understand the concepts you should do well.  I definitely want to take another class with her. She is a GREAT professor!!

Professor Kinard has been, by far, my favorite here at Vanderbilt. By leaving much of the class time open for discussion, the period flies by, and I always leave with new opinions and ideas about the poems. Not too much work, if you don't mind writing papers, but a very good choice for an elective!

Professor Kinard has been, undoubtedly, the best professor that I have ever had! She presents the material very well, challenges her students to think in novel ways, and goes the extra mile to help students inside and outside of class. She has a wonderful personality. I'm definitely going to take one of her courses again, even if it is an 8am!

Professor Kinard is hands down one of the best professors on campus.  She's so kind and truly cares about her students.  She's extremely articulate and knowledgeable about her subject topic (love & marriage).  She's realistic in her expectations and the class readings were really interesting! definitely take her class if you can, you won't regret i

kinard is one of may favorite teachers of all time!  She is extremely knowledgeable about almost every subject and is one of the most eloquent people i have ever meet.  She also has a very motherly feel, which is refreshing.  Our subject was very interesteing (love and marriage) and she gave me a new perspective!

love her! really inspiring.. picked great reading selections for class. included poetry, short fiction, and drama. goes over every reading in detail.. no tests but 3 essays and a few response papers that just reproduce class notes in essay form.. good requirement fulfillment for "w" course
Prof. Kinard is very helpful outside of class...I really wasn't interested in our class topic for the semester, but I came away w/ a new perspective...
she is so sweet and readily available!
She is my favorite professor of all time, wonderful, kind, so smart.
No Comments
No Comments

Take every class from her you can! She's such an amazing professor - very caring, funny, and passionate. Super flexible and understanding about assignments and due dates. The lectures are super clear and interesting, and the slides are well done. She also grades very generously and gives great feedback. Already great professor and person.

Took her fall semester of freshmen year and she was wonderful. the amount of material on her slides is a lot but because everything is open notes, not the optional final, you can use them on all of the quizzes. Drawings are really easy to do if you follow instructions, which are also clear. Bonus opportunities also help. Literally minimal effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was very easy and also entertaining. No test, no final, no attendance. Just a few online quizzes and some drawing assignments that are kind of tedious, but if you do all the work you will finish with an A. Attendance is not required but if you attend 80% of class you can get half points back on your quizzes. She is also entertaining.

dr. avona is by far my fav professor at vanderbilt! her lectures are interesting and comprehensible, and she is very accessible and helpful outside of class. if you have a chance take a class with her!

Dr. Avona is incredibly sweet when it comes to teaching. She empathizes a lot with her students and often gives extensions and extra credit when she feels like we are too stressed. The content is not difficult at all and is really interesting to learn through her slides. Her quizzes were never too difficult, but the content builds on itself.

THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER. If you're taking neuro, take this class with her. She's fun, engaging, cares about your learning, and her class is pretty easy grade wise. She's also just a nice person in general. I LOVE HER SERIOUSLY SHE'S THE BEST

Prof Avona is engaging, hilarious, and caring. She listens to feedback and adjusts accordingly. Lecture content can be pretty dense and sometimes hard to focus, but all quizzes and drawing assignments are open note. Go to class, take some notes, do assessments, and you'll be good. Final is optional and there are extra credit opportunities.
Dr Avona is a really accessible and kind woman who is really invested in her students and helping them to the most of her ability! I really appreciate her, 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor, easy class. Just go to lectures, do the assignments, and take the quizzes, you'll be fine. 100% recommend for psych major
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take all of her classes; she's amazing. Grading: 3 exams (review & practice done in class, one page cheat sheet allowed), in-class group work (mainly completion grade), one weekly paper w/ questions, and a final presentation. She's super caring and very flexible and her lectures are incredibly interesting/well done!

Grade is based on weekly quizzes and drawings. There is an optional final at the end and bonus points that can be earned through class participation. Class is pretty boring as the material is confusing and it is all lecture. However, Dr. Avona is awesome and really tries to make class entertaining (might be on me that I didn't like it).

Fun professor to learn from! Very kind and accomodating, and judging from past reviews, she strives to improve her class for her students since she has implemented some suggestions. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you get the chance for extra credit. Assignments and quizzes are sometimes extended when students feel overwhelmed with other classes.

Absolute best prof you could have for an intro neuro class. The content is dense, but she makes lectures engaging and assignments are completely manageable. If we were is too overwhelmed, she'd move due dates around to accommodate. Attendance isn't mandatory per se, but you get extra points for tophat q's in class. 100% take her for NSC 2201.

For NSC 3235. Only gripe with this class is that 30% of the grade comes from a group project and your group is chosen on the first day of class. Great if you take it with friends, not so great if you don't know anyone else. Dr. A is the best prof in the NSC department hands down. This class was informative and fun at the same time. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super easy science class for those who aren't STEM. Quizzes are open note and online. She made the final optional because she saw we were all stressed. Only have to go to 80% of the lectures to get full credit for participation.

drawing assignments and open-note quizzes. my semester she made the final optional bc she saw how stressed everyone was. she's very sweet and genuinely cares for students' learning and mental well-being. Easy A if you put in some effort and do topHat questions. She also has recorded lectues if you miss class, def take her for neuro classes
Best professor ever. Explains things so well and was very caring and understanding. If you're taking neuroscience, take it with Dr. Avona!!

Switched exams from in-person to online open note quizzes. Final exam was made optional. Attendance/participation through TopHat. Avona is very nice and caring. Drawing assignments aren't hard but require some thinking.

Professor Avona is wonderful. She cares for her students' wellbeing, and is extremely reachable. Quizzes are all application, but open note, so if you take notes in class, you should be fine. Very knowledgeable in her field. Not hard to do well if you pay attention and study. Her lectures are engaging and she loves a good interactive demonstration.

might as well skip her lectures and lose some participation points. I vowed to go to every class and ended up super tired from lack of sleep and thus forgot to submit some assignments. i know someone that just skipped all her lectures and wasn't as tired and got an easy A. doesn't feel fair.

such a wonderful professor and one of the two this semester that actually care about her students and their well being. she is so welcoming in her office hours and uses unique teaching style with drawing out mechanisms that really help. so supportive not just academically but emotionally too. love her in class demonstrations. wonderful

Dr. Avona is a wonderful lecturer and an even more amazing human. She takes the time to explain anything that may be unclear and is VERY accessible outside of class. She prioritizes the wellbeing and individual needs of her students. Any student would be lucky to take a class with her.

Dr. Avona is amazing. It is obvious she puts the well being of her students above everything. She is the most supportive and easygoing professor I have had on this campus. If she is available for any course I would highly recommend. It's like being able to accommodate is in her blood. I wish more would take after her..

Dr. Avona is very caring, supportive and THE BEST PROFESSOR! Her class is very engaging and fun. Lectures can be dense, so it's important to go to class. It's easy to fall behind because the content builds. Dr. Avona is always willing to help and assist with anything, neuroscience related or not! Take her classes, she's amazing!!

she totally changed around her syllabus from previous semesters: graded by quizzes and drawings and tophat only. made final exam optional after seeing her students stressed about other classes. genuinely cares about her students and always finds a way to make her lectures engaging (she LOVES halloween and her cats)

Dr. Avona is the best !!! My fav professor. Her in-class demonstrations are super helpful, her assignments include drawings & take-home quizzes, she made the final optional, and she provided extra credit. 
Take. This. Class.

I left a review earlier this year but now that she made the final optional, I completely change my mind. Amazing professor please take her. You won't be driven to hurt yourself like you will with other professors.
Such a kind professor. Truly cares about her students and makes everyone in a 200 person lecture feel like they matter. I will miss her and this class greatly!
The nicest most caring person ever. I love her and everyone should take this class.

Dr. Avona is a great professor! You can tell that she cares about her students & genuinely wants them to understand the content. There are 7 quizzes that are take-home & open note; There are some in-class tophat questions for participation & correctness. The final exam was going to be in person, but she made it optional. Overall, take her class! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ngl I was going to give her a lower rating but she just made the final exam optional because she cares for our well-being and that's really respectable. Good professor. Watch out for location based attendance though.
I LOVE SPONGGGGGGGGGGGGGGGEEEBOBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB

I love Dr. Avona! She is a great professor and truly cares about helping you gain a solid understanding of the material. Her grading is fair and her feedback is great; weekly assignments could get long but were not hard and we review them class. Participation is part of your grade and final is a group project.
Does not respond to emails from students. Does not care if the students learn anything

I love Dr. Avona!! She's a really good professor with fun, entertaining classes. But I really think she could try using location-tracking TopHat attendance instead of using tactics that feel like "traps" for students to be caught in. It just doesn't feel right to me. I think it would be more honorable to brainstorm ways to force people to attend.

she is not toxic at all, I've taken 2 classes with her and she is so so caring and is very accommodating. as long as you try to understand the material and put in the effort, this is possibility one of the best professors you can take a vandy

Some of her actions were a bit toxic. Made us switch TopHat answers to incorrect answers to catch people doing TopHat from home. It doesn't say anywhere that TopHat is used to judge in-class presence. People might be very sick and just want to do some practice problems from home and I don't think that justifies reporting them to the Honor Council.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are three tests, one final, and participation assignments. Dr. Avona is incredibly kind, caring, and extremely accessible outside of class. Her lectures are fun, and she makes neuroscience very straightforward. Non-neuroscience friends took it and loved the class! I HIGHLY recommend taking this class and/or Dr.Avona!!
It is one of the most interesting classes I have at Vanderbilt. Cute slides!! Concepts are all well-explained! Soooo nice!

Professor Avona is so caring, funny, and excellent at explaining. Don't even consider buying the textbook. Her slides are enough. Always attend lectures (in-class participation assignments). B/c there aren't many assignments, exams determine your grade. Don't worry, her exams always have clear guidelines. Highly recommend her.

Excellent upper level neuro course on pain as well as drugs that alleviate pain. The course had both a presentation component as well as 4 tests (including a final). This would scare off a lot of people, but overall, everything in the class is very doable. Prof. Avona is delightful, accommodating, and caring, would recommend her for any class!
Lectures were boring sometimes but exams were easy. Avona was super funny. Interesting material. There is a textbook but you didn't have to read it to grasp the material.

Neuroscience with Professor Avona was amazing! She is clear and engaging. Her tests are solely based off of the lecture slides, so don't waste your money on the online textbook. The test averages were pretty high at an 85%. She is very accessible outside of class so make sure to come to office hours it definitely helps!

She is so nice! I feel like people score highly on tests because they are studying a ton. I don't love how little things are used in the grade book. If you are not a good test taker, I would not take this class. But she is a kind person and I enjoy showing up!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Avona is engaging and clear. The tests are based on the slides; don't buy the online textbook - it's dense (save your money). Class test averages have all been around 85%. There are four exams - participation is 5%. Participation grades come from worksheets passed out at the end of class or short take-home homework assignments.

Professor Needham is literally the best. Classes were heavily discussion based, but she is mainly looking for effort and genuine reflection, so as long as you offer thoughtful ideas, even if you don't speak up every class, you're fine. Graded on weekly journals, 2 presentations, and a 10-page final. Highly recommend this class.

Class is only lectures with a weekly quiz based on that week's class. There is one final project at the end, which is a presentation based on a study you create. It is very easy, but attendance is mandatory. As long as you just go over the slides before the quiz, you will be so fine. Not the most entertaining class, but Dr. Needham is sweet.

If you need writing credit for Peabody take her seminar. Super nice. Don't really have to do the readings. Assignments are just informal weekly journals and one 10 page paper for the final. Final is just applying concepts from class to your own life. Not a tough grader.
so caring and sweet
this is my homegirl. Nicest lady and the easiest class ever. As long as you show you care even a little bit you will get an A.

Dr. Needham is the nicest professor I have ever had. She is so understanding and wants every student to succeed. Her class was easy and engaging. My class had great discussions and she was very lenient with grading. She is extremely caring and genuinely a very nice person.
The nicest professor every- really just wants to hear from her students! Not difficult to do well in the class.
She is quite literally an angel. Favorite class at vandy by far! If you have the chance its an absolute must take. Easy A, and enjoyable discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Needham is very sweet, but her classes tend to be very lecture-based. Nonetheless, still an easy A. Very little class discussion which could be kind of boring. Attendance is mandatory.

Pretty laid-back class and I actually enjoyed the content. Dr. Needham is very understanding and I liked how she tied lectures to real-world studies. Weekly quizzes; not too hard if you study a day in advance. Only complaint is the grading took far longer than it should've, so I was left in the dark about my grade for a while. Overall recommend.
Lectures got a little bit boring at times, but Prof. Needham is super nice and wants everyone to do well. I enjoyed learning about the studies we covered, and the class was pretty low-stress overall.

One of my faves! Dr.Needham is the best and recommend any class with her. She is so kind and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. Very manageable content, especially if you're interested in it, can be a little dry if you're not though. 2 small summary papers, no exams and weekly concept checks instead which are easy and low-stress

I can't recommend this course enough. The material, class discussions, and assignments are all very casual. Professor Needham is such a sweet and caring person. There's really no stress. Just show up, hand everything in on time, participate some, and you'll get an A without a doubt.

For a first-year writing seminar, we were graded on five 3-5 page papers and a 5-8 page final term paper. The concepts were interesting, so they were not too difficult, and she was not a harsh grader. In class, we didn't discuss our papers, but instead focused on weekly readings (which varied in length and depth) and held student-led discussions.

She gives helpful and interesting reading materials. She's an understanding and supportive professor. Discussions can sometimes be repetitive, but they are always open, respectful, and thought-provoking. A highly recommended class!

Professor Needham made this class very enjoyable by giving the students free reign of the discussion based class. We were able to share our stories and learn a lot about the world purely on discussions and a few papers and not a lot of homework.

So her lectures are definitely boring, but I think Prof Needham is the nicest woman ever. She is so accessible and caring. She genuinely wants every student to do well. The class is also not hard so even if you don't pay attention you can study and do well. If you put in a little bit of work you will easily get an A.

I honestly don't understand why she has such bad reviews. She's the sweetest, most kindhearted professor. Her lectures are definitely dry, but she cares so much about her students. Also, the class is SO easy. No need to read, and then just memorize her study guide and you'll ace the test.

Impossible to pay attention to because lectures are so dry.  Final project was creating an invention for new borns and we spent an entire month on presentations.  The final test was on other people's hypothetical inventions which is useless information and not applicable in any situation in the real world. DO NOT RECOMMEND.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's such a kindhearted, passionate professor, although her lectures can be kinda disorganized. Tests are fairly tricky, all short answer and fill in the blank, but she's very open to questions and very receptive if you don't understand something.  The research project is actually pretty fun if you choose a good topic.

Needham is thoroughly incapable of abstract and higher-level thinking. Answers on tests have to be exactly what she said in her powerpoint, she grades extremely subjectively, and her lecture style is immensely boring. She fails to promote interest in the material and addresses students in a very elementary manner. Not worth the money.

Professor Needham is one of the sweetest professors at Vanderbilt. She is pretty reserved but really cares about her students. The class is based on 3 non-cumulative exams and nothing else. The material is not too dense and she includes a lot of her and her colleagues research into her lectures. Love her.
Professor Needham is great.

Infancy was a great class with Dr. Needham because it's her area of expertise. She loves the subject and knows the material backwards and inside out. Reading the book isn't necessary if you want a B, but you definitely should if you're looking for an A. She is the sweetest lady and puts random cute baby pictures in the slideshows for fun.

the class is all tests and one project. she always says the tests will be on the broader ideas within the material but they then get very specific. her grading is horrible, if it is not worded perfectly, you won't get credit. do not take this class with her, choose another professor.

This class was terrible. If you did not word answers to questions on the test in the exact manner she would have (despite quality of answer) she would count at least half off. The material is a breeze. Her grading was ridiculous. Avoid if at all possible.

She is so sweet and is genuinely interested in the success of her students. She gives a review sheet a few days before each of her 3 tests and if you know everything on them, you will get a good grade. I never opened the book.
She is very nice and does great powerpoints, if that is your preferred learning style. Gives pretty clear directions, however, she isn't very apt for adjusting grades. Overall, very nice, though.

An extremely kind and thoughtful professor who is clearly passionate about her teaching. Covers a wide range of topics, from children's historical reasoning to climate justice and moon patterns. It's engaging and highly collaborative, with lots of work done alongside tablemates. HW directions can be a bit confusing at times, but she will clarify.

Pedagogy with Palmeri is great. She's sweet, knowledgeable, and leads interesting discussions. Class gets boring since its 2 hrs long/wk. Grades super easily, essentially completion. That said, there's a lot of work. 2 5ish page Field Notes, 2 2-pg interview reflections, 2 interviews, and a final 5-pg paper. Take 2330 with her if you can.

good class if your looking for an easy A, the lectures were kinda boring and the asingments were kinda weird at time but most of them were very fun. Very chill class with a very chill final project. She can be kinda a tough grader on some asignments if she think you didn't put in enough effort so you can just submit BS and get full credit

This class is so boring and seems pointless. There is a lot of 'busy' work and it does not seem to connect back to class material. Lectures and readings are pointless as there are no quizzes or tests. Therefore, this class is super easy but super boring. Dr. Palmeri is very sweet and caring though!

Pedagogy with her was as good as I could ask for. Seemed like she cared about the class and teaching well; however, didn't always feel like she wanted to engage with students on a personal level. Readings each week, a few short papers, and a chill final project. Not a bad option.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved prof Palmeri. Lots of her assignments are completion based, so if you put in some effort, you will do well. Very kind person.

Professor Palmeri was a great professor who really cares about her students. She definitely gave a lot of assignments and sometimes they began to feel tedious, but they were never graded too hard if you put the work in. She also was helpful in figuring out my schedule next semester and I look forward to having her again.

Dr. Palmeri is wonderful. She is very knowledgable not only about her social studies content but also about pedagogy as a whole. She truly cares about her students and is flexible with deadlines if you ask. My favorite professor so far. I can't imagine my teacher education without her.

Palmeri is a nice enough person, but her grading is not grounded in the essay prompts or rubrics. She will not adjust your grade, even if she made an error, and does not offer solid or constructive feedback. I wouldn't take this with her.

I was scared to take Anilkumar, but energetics was my favorite lab at Vanderbilt. He was funny and pretty friendly, and I learned a lot from the labs. He truly wants us all to be the best engineers we can be.

Technically, can you get the job done? I was basically with Dr. Anilkumar in space and for 50 years his refrigerator ran. We were the only team to do fluids in space correctly. You must account for thrust man or else that devil is gonna crap itself. I would hope you would be firing on all cylinders man but you have lost the plot.

If you try in this class you might be fine. Really pay attention to his lectures and do not be afraid to answer/ask questions. He will flame you (jokingly) if you are wrong or if it's a stupid question, but honestly it gets pretty funny after the first week. You will learn a ton, but it is very hard and there is very little curve. Highly recommend.

Review is for Energetics Lecture/Lab which is more of a reflection of the TAs. High-level ME course where participation is important and you are expected to be well-versed in the labs ahead of time. Weekly labs with 10-15 page reports. Graded kindly assuming proper lab preparation and understanding. Discussion/lecture sessions are very low key.

Probably one of the hardest professors I have ever taken. Emphasis on perfection and does not leave room for mistakes--to the point of being called out in class in front of everyone for wrong answers. Only take him if you want the challenge and have the self confidence to back yourself up.

Dr. Anilkumar teaches in the way you'd expect a drill sergeant to teach. He often poses difficult questions to maintain engagement and will act like random facts are just common knowledge (e.g. distance between Earth and sun of the top of your head). He knows his stuff and teaches well, but be advised that your best may feel insufficient to do well

Never got bored during lectures. Great professor, learned so much. That said, he's definitely intimidating and arrogant (one of those professors, talks about "real engineering"), shoots down wrong answer fast and harshly.
Hard tests, but teaches engineering the right way. Yes it will be hard and he can be harsh but he cares a lot about the students.
not easy to understand in class, way better to just study the book because going to class makes things more confusing
Lab teacher for energetics. Straight up mean. Disgustingly hard class. Mocks you for turning in reports late.
He was a good professor for fluid mechanics.

Very smart and understands how to ask the right questions to help you learn. One of the best professors I have had at getting you to learn the thought process behind the problems and the engineering way of thinking. Class is difficult, but I feel like I am learning a lot from him.

Has no office hours, very unwilling to help outside of class. Expects students to get it on the first time because he is so smart. Minimal work for the class. Four tests, four essays, and four homework sets. Heavily curves class in the end.

Professor Anilkumar is a good teacher.  He really understands the fundamentals of fluid mechanics. Sometimes he allows his lectures to go off-topic. If you work hard in his class, you will learn a lot.
He's a good teacher, but his method involves lots of interaction. Also, he curves the class at the end, so if you do well enough you will get an A. I also had him for ME 261.

Dr. Avison is clearly very passionate about addiction and addiction studies. He always references new papers and advancements in the field, but our tests are on big-picture ideas and processes. One question quizzes each class, but they're not hard and count for very little in the overall grade. Super fascinating class for pre-meds and neuro majors!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Avison is a little disorganized but very caring. Passionate about addiction. Once you figure out how he writes the tests, they're easy. If you're struggling, focus on the BIG PICTURE! He spends a lot of time on little details, but these aren't tested on. Show up to class and take notes, because the slides are messy and mostly have pictures.

He is exceptionally passionate about addiction and does an excellent job describing the neurobiology that facilitates it. His lectures can be quite complex, however, if you have taken any intro Neuroscience course, you should be fine. There is quite a lot of content, but he specifies which material is essential for quizzes and which is not.

Dr. Avison is a very nice man who is passionate about addiction, but the format of this class was kind of all over the place. He wasn't clear about what would be important on Block Quizzes (3, all short answer), and did not provide an answer key to questions. Also tends to get sidetracked about unrelated things. Can be condescending in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Extremely unorganized course with little alignment between lectures and exams. Tests frequently covered material not taught in class, making expectations unclear; Grading was inconsistent

reflected a lack of structure accountability that made learning secondary to managing confusion.

Raises serious concerns about the instructor's employment

Disorganized course with unclear grading expectations. Exams focus on obscure details barely discussed in lecture; one exam question had to be voided because no one answered it correctly. The required textbook is expensive but rarely used. When students raise concerns, and the professor is defensive, and explanations are confusing

This was by far the least professionally managed class I have taken. Homework was due every class with inconsistent time deadlines. Worksheets had frequent errors and repeated questions. Duplicate assignments were posted by mistake, and missing one upload resulted in a zero. Required $150 text was rarely used. Avoid Professor Benson at all cost.
Dr. benson is amazing and makes every class enjoyable. The assignments are often hard to follow but most grades are a completion grade or a test. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For the lab section, you go on hikes every week which is pretty fun and you're guaranteed to get an A. However, grading criteria is so unclear and she strays from the schedule like crazy so you have no clue what you're supposed to do. You just gotta trust you'll get an A and not tweak. Moral of the class: now I can identify like every tree!

Tbh very odd class. Benson is a really sweet lady and super caring, and the material is so free. But at the same time it's very unorganized. Felt like I was always doing smth for this class and most of the time just busy work. The lectures feel like ur learning nothing, but if youre fine with that as long as you get an A then it's whatever.

She is literally insane, cold calls and treats this course like a discussion when it is a 100+ person lecture, the exams are often fill in the blank with random details that were barely discussed, homework is tedious. She makes you buy an expensive textbook that you barely use. Not a hard class in terms of the content but difficult to survive

Dr. Benson is by far my favorite professor at Vandy. She is extremely passionate about plants and her passion is infectious. She truly prioritizes student well-being and learning over grades - once she even moved an exam bc we were overwhelmed. Classes are discussion-based, so come prepared and do the short readings bc she calls on people

Literally ignore those negative comments. This class is totally worth it if you want a fun baby bio course as a non-science major! She's quite wacky, which I loved, and you learn a lot of interesting facts in a low-pressure environment with easy exams. Also, if you need the lab credit, no reason not to take this if you love hiking and nature!

Dr Benson is incredibly passionate about what she teaches, and is very encouraging towards her students. Brings us sweet treats every class! You can get an A if you do all the homework, participate, and take the feedback she gives on your essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The Lab was so much better than the lecture (fun fields trips and activities). She's a really easy grader but all of the exams have little to do with the lecture. Quite the eccentric teacher, but definitely the better science course to take at Vandy if you're not into science stuff

A must-take for non-stem majors needing sci credit. Easiest and most fun lab out there (zoo field trip)! The class itself is manageable; some content is involved if you have no bio background (lots of memorization) but exams are predictable and fair. She's kind of a mess organizationally but an engaging lecturer. Homework graded for completion.

This is a must-take science class to satisfy AXLE. Stay on-track with weekly (very easy) assignments and pay attention in lectures and it's an easy A. She's also very caring and truly wants to see her students succeed and understand the material. Also take the lab! We went on hikes and learned to ID trees; very unique class indeed!

Prof Benson is hilarious and cares a lot about students. the class is mostly completion grades for homework along with three cumulative exams. attendance is definitely mandatory and there's a decent amount of work, but the content is not difficult. good for an easy science credit.

I absolutely adored Dr. Benson. The textbook is online and you don't even read it but you do need for assignments on there. Participation is a must and HW is all completion. 3 exams BUT she is such an easy grader and good about awarding partial credit. She is so understanding and believes in learning more than earning grades and being fearful.

THE BEST FOR THE SCIENCE/MATH CREDIT! . She made class amazing, and she cared so much about us students. The homework was all completion. You have to study a little bit, but it does not stress you out. Great to have in your schedule because it honestly is a mental break from your other classes.

DR. BENSON IS LITERALLY AN ICON. I LOVE HER SO MUCH. PLEASE TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU NEED AN EASY SCIENCE. You definitely should study for the tests, but she loves giving credit even if you only kinda got the answer right. I am not a stem person, and she made this class very enjoyable -- she's also just hilarious.
BEST TEACHER EVER

This has been my favorite class I have taken at Vanderbilt. This course is a science that makes it easy to understand for non-STEM people and science students. The class is engaging and interesting!  I would 100% take it again and cannot stress how amazing Dr. Benson truly is.

Dr. Benson truly cares about this class and her students. She encourages learning in engaging ways but also emphasizes the importance of taking care of yourself. Dr. B is very funny and keeps lectures light and fun. I learned a lot!

Dr. Benson is kind and you can tell she's passionate about what she teaches. Homework is due before class which is a doc with questions and sources to refer to for the answers, the workload is definitely manageable. Exams are heavily weighted in the class, with the final being worth 42%. If you study you should be able to do decent on these.

Dr. Benson is an incredible professor who strikes the perfect balance between challenge and support, making their science course both engaging and rewarding. The mix of lectures and hands-on components ensures a comprehensive and memorable experience. Would recommend 100% for anyone looking to gain a deep understanding and appreciation for science!

Dr. Benson is awesome! If you genuinely want to learn take this course because Dr. Benson has a plethora of resources to help you. Attendance is definitely mandatory, but Dr. Benson makes it a fun and caring environment so that it is a beautiful space to learn. Definitely take her class!
Really cares about her students. Highly recommend for a science class if you are non-STEM.

This truly has been my favorite class at Vanderbilt. Dr. Benson is an incredible professor and provides a positive for all students whether they are more science-focused or less STEM-driven. I learned about INTERESTING science! She is kind, engaging, and teaches meaningful science. The workload is very manageable and the exams are straightforward.

This is the best professor at Vanderbilt. She really cares about the well-being of her students and even plays a song in the middle of class everyday. Benson makes it hard not to learn the material. With the homework and lectures I feel like I've learned so much and I didn't know anything about this subject before. She seriously is the best ever.
She is the best teacher I have ever had. She plays music in class and is very understanding if you need to miss class for any reason. Homework is my completion and she really helps with exams.
Avoid if possible! Would not recommend this course or professor

Participation is MANDATORY! All homework is graded by completion. Tests are very specific but come straight from the lectures posted. She does cold call in class but you just have to try to answer. Have to buy textbook to do part of homework. Final is 42% of grade but you're fine if you study. Highly recommend if you need a science credit!
Awful. Do no take

Dr. B is great. Her class is wild but in a good way.  She simply never grades the homework- they're only for completion, so the only place you can lose points is attendance and the tests, which she grades leniently. She is super knowledgeable and relates the class to real-world problems like climate change. It's impossible to get below a C.

Dr Benson is not caring and is plainly rude. She cares more about her class and the plants than she does about the students. God forbid you come to her with a personal problem, she doesn't give a single f. Beware of this professor, find another baby bio course!!!!!

While the class was disorganized and the tests could be a little random overall it is a good choice for a science credit. Just pay attention in lecture and study her slides for exams.
