Also if you can get into the lab take it! It is hiking field trips every week and she wants you to get an A so much better than all the other lab options.

I LOVED her. As a non-stem major I was worried, but if you try in class it helps a lot. HW not hard. The final was for 42% of your grade, not fun. She's not perfectly clear about what you'll need to know on each exam which can skew what u study for. Despite perfect HW and attendance, I didn't get an A, but it was fun and my grade was good enough

1 quiz; 3 3 paragraph essays; 2 5 paragraph essays; 1 partner presentation; little easy hw assignments (5 min). SUPER EASY. Disorganized; she is confusing at times. Leniant on due dates. Understanding about life complications. Gave us food in class.

this class was way too hard for a baby bio course. there was so much content and she didn't link it together well. the exams had questions that didn't make sense. class was graded based on homework and 4 exams. you have to go to class to do well. it wasn't impossible, but there are probably easier baby bio classes.

Super nice and not impossible to do well but the class made no sense and the exams were brutal. She just pulled random facts that she might have mentioned in class and most of the study guide does not match up.

Never take this class! Her slides are barely legible, and she expects you to know extremely specific information on the test that doesn't support actual learning. On the final test, it appears she graded a lot harsher than the other tests. 10/10 would not recommend taking this class at all.

Took this class for AXLE credit and while I wasn't expecting an easy A class, it definitely didn't live up to my expectations. Crazy amount of content in one lecture, and if you miss a class you're out of luck since you can barely understand the slides. Had to buy a $100 online textbook for assignments that we used maybe twice, which was annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are all over the place and her slides are impossible to review with. Tests questions are hard to comprehend and draw from random facts. Do not take for AXLE credit.

Her only personality trait is that she previously taught at Harvard.
Her lectures are erratic and she only cold calls.
Her exams are barely legible and oftentimes do not align with course content. 

Avoid at all costs.

Benson is an engaging lecturer but there is SO much material covered in just one class. The lecture slides by themselves aren't helpful-- they're full of typos, pictures, random music videos-- which makes attendance mandatory if you want to do well on tests.

This is a MUST class for those needing to fulfill AXLE requirements. It was BY FAR the least challenging science class. The most important thing to do to excel in this class is to pay attention to her lectures and study the lectures for exams. Go to her review sessions before exams. Pay attention to what she emphasizes in the lectures. Great class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't get the book, I never used it. Dr Benson was super nice & the lab component was amazing with weekly hikes to learn about plants in person. She's so caring, homework is completion graded, lectures/notes posted online, & the major assignments were 2 midterms & a cumulative final. My fav prof in the bio department because of how she teaches.

The material seemed a bit random and it was unclear what was being tested. Organization skills were subpar. Having to memorize the name and year of random scientific papers for tests seemed pointless. Tests/presentations were graded without clear guidelines and rubrics. Hard to complain with an A; the class was easier than most biology classes.

Had no idea what my grade was all semester, and guidelines for assignments were kinda unclear. Nonetheless, she really is hilarious, quirky, and wants us to learn as our main goal, and the class was interesting and approachable compared to other bio courses. Had to know 50+ scientific studies for the class, but we really got a deep understanding.

Dr. Benson is definitely super quirky, but cares about her students and making sure that everyone learns and actually cares about the material. The tests are long but she is not a super tough grader so as long as you go most of the time and do the homework you should have no trouble getting an A, which I think she said at the beginning of class.

Dr. Benson is very kind and obviously cares about her students' success. She gives great feedback on papers and is passionate about the material. She is definitely quirky and takes some getting used to, but her classes are wildly entertaining. However, her communication skills via bright space and email need serious help. Overall, great prof.

Dr. Benson loves what she teaches, and will work to make you love it too. Some of the assignments are tedious, and the tests are a lot of info, but you have a study guide and in the end, Dr. B just wants to make sure everyone walks away caring more about the subject. Kinda quirky, but a great heart, I'd definitely take her again

Dr. Benson really tries to make class fun, encourages participation & even though there's daily homework it's really easy. Tests are long, but she gives a study guide before each one and gives a ton of partial credit. Green Earth is a great class to take to fulfill your MNS requirement if you're a non-STEM major and actually want to learn something
Dr. Benson really knows her material. I took her Biodiversity and Climate Change class and was immersed into primary literature. The class was fun and I learned a lot.

Dr. Benson is a very nice professor who really cares about students performance. I have taken plant bio as well as this course and both times she was extremely helpful and passionate about the subject being taught. She updates students with current scientific literature about the subject as well, which is really appreciated!
Really interesting class. Knew a ton about the material at hand and was enthusiastic to keep you awake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Benson is a really great professor who really cares about each student. Her lectures are really engaging and fun. I would definitely take it again. Go to her outside of class and she is super helpful as well.
Great teacher. Definitely recommend going during office hours. Really cares about students

Professor Benson is a fun loving and enthusiastic teacher who is passionate about sharing her knowledge. She can be scatterbrained but that just adds to the eclectic charm of the course.  Go to office hours and attend class. You'll love it.
Dope teacher, dope class

DIsorganized professor who filled her powerpoints useless information. The class was barely about plants, more about evolution. I'm sure she's a nice person if you really got to know her but as a professor, she really didn't do a good job of teaching. Beware, her tests don't really look anything like the study guides she provides. Lab is long.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Benson is a professor who cares about the students and makes sure that everyone is on the same page before moving on to the next unit. The class is lecture heavy but she does a good job with reviewing the material. There were 3 exams and they were all fair. Benson is an entertaining professor and makes the class enjoyable.

Dr. B is a very passionate professor.  She loves to see her students learn, however she can come off as scatterbrained a lot.  I would recommend visiting her during office hours, she was nice and provided helpful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Super passionate about the course material and very dedicated to making sure that you have everything you need to succeed in the course. Definitely cares about you, even if the class is a little tough!

Not the greatest professor... at all. Shes just really unclear in my opinion, and its stressful as a student. She also doesnt provide her notes, which arent even great in the first place. I definitely would never take another class with her again.....

A completely disorganized professor. She doesnt know the material, so her lectures are incomprehensible abridged versions of the textbook. Her assignments are all busy work, and are graded unfairly (like grading based on perceived effort rather than actual correctness), and you dont know how youre doing until you get your final grade. AVOID!

She is very nice and funny, and I like her as a person. However, she is not a very good teacher. She does not post her lectures online, and you can't ever read the print outs she gives you because the text is so small, so lectures are essentially useless. I had to learn everything from the book. Super unorganized not that knowledgeabl about materia

I had her for the "Genes & Society" First Year Writing Seminar. There was homework 3 nights a week (before every class), which was very erratic, unorganized, and really just wasted time. It would involve 2-3 paragraphs with lots of pre-reading. She tries to give good feedback but really just confuses everyone. Content of class was very interesting.

Professor Benson is a really nice person and seems to care about her students but she is so disorganized. She sometimes springs papers on you at the last minute with little to no instructions. The daily assignments due before every class period are tedious and unnecessary. 3 papers, 1 group project, 1 final paper. Fairly easy grader.

If any of you freshman are thinking of taking this class to fulfill your AXLE requirement, take anything else than one of Dr. Benson's 115F sections. All of her assignments and papers are poorly worded and extremely ambiguous; it is nearly impossible to tell what she actually wants from you. Take my word for it and do not enroll in this class.

Dr. Benson is a nice teacher. Although the class requires a great deal of work, the material is not particularly challenging. She is a fairly easy grader and is very willing to talk to you about your grades.

Dr. Benson is still my favorite college professor. She develops great relationships with her students, and this class is fascinating. She loves to play devil's advocate to spark discussion, and while she is a bit scatterbrained, she makes up for it with her enthusiasm for the class. Expect a lot of work. This class is tough, but oh it is worth it.

She is extremely scatterbrained and makes big project assignments up on the spot. The material is confusing but the tests are graded easily. However, she is harsher on the final and that is worth 45% of your grade so be ready to study for that.

She is completely scatterbrained and does not know her subject. One of the most unorganized professors I have ever had. We never knew what to expect for the tests and her lectures were not helpful. Take another BSCI class for sure.

This is one of the best classes you can take freshman year. Dr. Benson is an amazing professor that will show you how to approach scientific literature. It will be a lot of work, but so are all of the FYWS. She is awesome and worth every hour of work that she assigned! she might misspell things a lot, but she is smartest and most interesting person

Benson is AWESOME. Shes very enthusiastic and really cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. She doesnt take points off for grammar or citations which is great. You have to go to class but its only MW, and homework brings up your grade a lot so its very easy to get an A. Also so sweet and helpful outside of class. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

Horrible professor. She is very confusing when assigning her projects and grades only based on how much she likes you. Avoid at all costs. For people taking a freshman writing seminar anything else is better for your grade. The stress is not worth taking her class.
You will learn a lot in this class without stressing about your grade too much. Highly recommended for science people in particular. Dr. Benson is awesome and will help you with anything.

Dr. Benson is awesome, and you will learn a ton in this class without stressing about your grade. Definitely take this class, especially if you are a science person. Dr. Benson is always helpful and genuinely cares about her students. She is also just a great person to know.
Brightest Professor ever, she knows her subject and is very helpful

One of the best classes I have ever taken.  Dr. Benson is an exceptionally knowledgeable and enthusiastic professor. Her course was eye-opening for me, covering a broad range of fascinating topics that I previously knew little about. She really cares about her students and class discussions were very engaging.  TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

really enthusiastic about class and a pretty chill easygoing kind person. In fact, she pushed the class time to 8:40 instead of 8:10 just so everyone could get extra sleep. grades papers pretty leniently. not so clear about assignments sometimes though. still gets my name mixed up. Just attend class. very scatterbrained but intelligent woman

Possibly the sweetest teacher I have ever had. Tries to make her classes a "positive learning experience" and it works. She oftentimes is unclear and drops large (10 Chapter) tests on you that can be very surprising. However, if you learn the material and show her you are trying, she will reward you. Almost everyone in this class ended up with A's

Not a very difficult class. Only problem is that the readings are difficult to acquire (they are all over the place). Several papers and a final presentation. Book is not needed at all. Learned a lot and the professor, while not a very good teacher, makes class at least somewhat enjoyable (for an 8:10 class).

Botany: Easiest class ever.  I don't know what the comments below are talking about. She might be all over the place, but it is so easy and there is no stress in not knowing what she is talking about because you'll still get an A. The class is that easy. Oh yeah, don't buy the book, its a complete waste, for lab assignments go to the library.

Dr. Benson is so sweet and so interested in her field. The class is graded easily and buying the textbook is a waste, but she's rarely clear about what's expected in assignments and assigned very last minute papers. Stressful if you're the kind of person who needs to work ahead of time.

DO NOT TAKE HER! Seriously, she is all over the place. Major ADD going on. A lot of times she doesn't know what she's assigned and for when. She is a good and nice person but I have no idea what she's talking about half the time. Participation is a big part of the grade so reading should be done but not really necessary. She's whack!
Easy class but not worth taking. Most of the time you will not know what she assigns. The stress is just not worth it.

Benson's class wouldn't be hard except for the fact that you never know what shes assigning! The woman makes up assignments and due dates and the class itself is just all over the place. I don't even know what we learned. Brilliant woman but suchh a scatterbrain. If you're thinking this will be an easy freshman seminar, think again

Certainly one of the nicest, most helpful professors in the department. She is both passionate and knowledgeable about all subjects related to genetics and botany; the interest she shows in her students' thoughts and papers reflects this.

Probably one of the most unpredictable teachers I've ever had, and the only difficulty in her class is trying to figure out what it is that she wants.  She is really nice and very accommodating, loves her subject matter and has her student's best in mind. Yet she mixes up names and twists what people say in class into what she wants to hear.
Professor Benson is really chill and knows what she is talking about.  I would highly recommend taking her.
Very nice! She has been the kindest and most caring professor I've had here at Vanderbilt! I would highly recommend this class to anyone!
easy...she tells you what will be on the quiz...lab grade is almost all participation
I took the Human Genome frosh. seminar with her: easiest class EVER.
Very boring lectures and often goes on tangents but very knowledgeable professor. Very easy class however, graded on a couple big assignments that are relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As someone who grew up with stories of the Holocaust, Ari's class challenged me to analyze it in a nuanced way. There's a lot of reading for this class, but all of it is interesting and you don't need to have all of it memorized. Assignments are graded very leniently. He is a compelling lecturer and I'd leave class thinking about what I learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LOVED Professor Joskowicz. Lectures are super engaging/interesting, but discussion-based so depends on your classmates. The readings are long, but if you just get the general gist you'll be fine. Only a few assignments and they're all very easily graded. Seriously such a knowledgable and understanding professor, adds so much nuance to each topic.

An obscene amount of readings but you can kind of get away with only reading a little bit. Weekly discussion post on the reading. Lectures take forrreeevvverr but cover interesting material. Class is discussion based. No exams and essays are graded fairly easy. Long final project. Professor is sweet and understanding.

Professor Joskowicz is an amazing academic and learning from him was an enjoyable and rewarding experience. I'm a history major and I took this class as an elective because the content interests me, but I'd still recommend this class to anyone at Vanderbilt.

I'd recommend this class to everyone at Vanderbilt. Professor Joskowicz is very insightful and addresses the topic in a very respectful way. Be sure to do the reading because he has random pop quizzes before class starts; they're not hard but if you don't at least skim you won't do well. 10/10 would recommend if you want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. J is one of the best profs I've had at Vanderbilt. He seriously knows his stuff, is so passionate, and this class is SO interesting. Would take any of his classes again. Gotta read though bc he gives pop quizzes.

Professor Joskowicz is one of the best, if not the best, teacher I've ever had. He is so passionate and knowledgable about what he's teaching that it's inspiring. It seems like his main goal is to make sure his students understand-he doesn't grade the assignments harshly, he just wants to make sure that we are learning something. Take his class!
Really nice guy, fun class. A lot of reading and requires blogs every week but easy busy work. Easy overall grader and assignments are interesting and not too time consuming.

He's a generally nice guy, and this class had no tests, only papers. I would suggest at least skimming each of the readings, and participation plays a big role in your grade. It's not a terribly tough class, do a decent amount of the work and you'll end up in the B+/A- range.
Great professor. There is a lot of reading you need to do and talk about in class. participation is 20% so you actually have to read but the lectures are very interesting and he is not a hard grader.

Wonderful professor, extremely intelligent. Great class discussions, lots of reading but he can tell if you don't read. No tests, only discussions and papers. Takes everyone's comments seriously. Not a difficult grader.

He is an excellent professor. Class is very interesting, pay attention to the readings! He knows a lot about the subject, but also knows how to present it for those without background knowledge. Extremely helpful, and in general, seems like a great guy! Take his class!
Excellent Professor. Easy to understand, brings out interest in the class and stimulates conversation.

Joskowicz is an engaging lecturer, easy to understand, and knowledgeable in his field. He holds interest and encourages conversation in the class room. He's demanding in the readings you must prepare, but since the classes are discussion based, it's the best idea to read everything. Great Profe.

This class was awesome. I took it as an AXLE requirement, and I'm so happy I did. Caramanica knew so much about the course and attending the mandatory lectures was worth it. I learned a lot from the content and the hands-on activities. There's assigned reading for most classes, but it's supplemental and rarely referred to or needed in class.

Really loved Professor Caramanica, this class was really enjoyable, especially spending two weeks working in the Vanderbilt dining halls to make Cheese, Tortillas, and Pickles. She cares about her students actively participating in this class so if you aren't looking to speak this isn't the class for you. Definitely will be taking her again!

I learned so much in this class! Prof. Caramanica is extremely knowledgeable in the field, including much of her own research in lecture materials. Attendance is taken, but class is fun. 1-2 times a month we went on campus “field trips” or did a special group activity. Such an easy A, no exams, just a few paper-adjacent assignments and a few hw's.

Professor Caramanica made me genuinely interested in anthropology, and her experience outside academia made her lectures interesting and relevant. She definitely has high standards, but is very caring and understanding of students' needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Caramanica chose a more discussion approach than lecture-heavy. That means you have to come to class with an extensive knowledge of her 30-40 page reading from the night before. Her class discussions were often repetitive and got unnecessarily political. I definitely would not suggest taking this class if you get bored easily.

Not an easy gpa booster, lot of work esp reading. But this class is SO REWARDING. If you're interested in the topic, TAKE IT!!! Class was very small, deep seminar discussions, lots of interesting readings and conversations. Professor Bryen was funny and super knowledgeable. SO worth it! The writing experience is unique and feedback was invaluable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Instead of multiple choice test, Professor Bryen assigns essays instead. The essays are based on your interpretation of the texts and the lectures during class. Professor Bryen is a hard grader on the essay, so only take this class if writing is your thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Insanely knowledgable. True academic. UChicago born and raised. Makes you work for it, but extremely rewarding.

Professor Bryen is the best professor I've had at Vandy. I'm not even a classics major, yet he made this class my favorite at Vandy in 6 semesters. He is a classic "academic" type with an extremely endearing no-BS attitude. He embodies everything a professor should be. Knowledgeable, passionate, funny, caring, and a great communicator.

Respected Classics professor, very clever and well-read. Heavily focused on critical thinking rather than recounting history. Do take if you are a classics major, you will find him difficult if you aren't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Bryen taught me what's "being challenged academically". Highly knowledgeable and interesting, Bryen can teach you a lot about Roman history in his lectures and makes sure you learn through his styles. However, such an intelligent man is an extremely harsh grader and expects impeccable work. Take his class only if you love learning but not GPA

Although I was not particularly interested in violence in ancient civilizations, Prof. Bryen really opened my eyes to what history and writing about history was all about. I hardly ever read the assignments and just participated on a whim, and it usually worked. I did put lots of effort into my papers and visited him a lot

Professor Bryen is an excellent lecturer who can make pretty much anything interesting. He can be pretty snarky if people dont show up or read, but even so its usually funny. It shouldnt be hard to get a B but youll have to try to get an A.

Prof Bryen is the man. The subject material is intensely interesting, and he lays it out in a clear and accessible way. He's charismatic, so his lectures are engaging. Outside of class he is happy to meet regarding papers or tests. It's clear he has a great understanding of the Roman world, and he is very well suited to teach it.

Devilishly clever yet excessively conceited. If interested in the origins of the west (you should be), Bryen's lectures will undoubtedly be engaging. That being said, he thinks extremely highly of himself, and does not make himself available outside of class. Difficult to work with when it comes to papers/tests, etc. However, you WILL learn a lot.

Dr. Bryen is an amazing and super knowledgeable professor. His papers are difficult and are definitely harder than other First-Year Writing Seminars. Don't take this class unless you actually want to learn about violence in ancient civilizations or want to be a better writer. The readings are super long though and usually unnecessary for papers.

Professor Bryen is by far the best professor I've ever had. Two tests, two papers (one long one short). Really really good lectures, interesting subject matter, makes you want to learn. Available in office hours. Really clear expectations. Funny. I'd say it's an easy B, you'll have to work a littler bit harder for the A, he's fair in his grading
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Bryen is easily one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. The lectures were always extremely informative and interesting, and he had a way of weaving any questions or discussions into the day's topic seamlessly. Very funny in a dry, cynical way. Gives constructive feedback and is happy to help if you ask. Professor Bryen is great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Bryen was an excellent professor. His lectures were consistently engaging and informative, and the occasional days where we had discussion were well-guided and entertaining. He says he's a tough grader, but will provide helpful constructive feedback and make sure you learn a lot. Easy A if you put in 5 hours a week, but easy D if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was very supportive and showed interest in my paper topic when I went to his office; he recommended sources to look at that were extremely helpful.  Tough, but reasonable policies on due dates & attendance  Some unnecessary books  I enjoyed his sense of humor very much, and would thoroughly recommend taking a class with Professor Bryen!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Easy class, but there's a lot of complex material later on. Witulski is a really nice guy who is very lenient in grading. Homework is a bit tedious, but quizzes and tests were pretty light. The lectures are a bit dry, but what can you do? The content is dry in and of itself.

There is always something to do for this class, but Dr. Witulski is a super easy grader and this class was never too much stress throughout the semester. The beginning of the course is learning the ethical frameworks and the rest of it is applying them to different problems in the tech sphere. Love Arthur, gives great career advice!

Easy class, but lectures were very boring. There's a lot of writing involved in the assignments, but there's a rubric posted which is accurate. Had some projects (presentations, Ted Talks, debates), but you can just prepare the day before - may depend on your randomly assigned group. Skim through the textbook, don't read. Great choice for CS 1151
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures are sometimes cool, sometimes boring. There is a ton of writing involved in the weekly homework assignments, but he is a really chill grader so it's hard not to do well as long as you are doing the assignments. Quite a bit of group projects (debates, TED talks, and group presentations) but nothing too bad.

Ethics is an enjoyable class and Witulski is one of the kindest people at Vanderbilt. Get ready to write (2 papers every 2 weeks) but the prompts aren't difficult and the grading is very predictable. There are 4 group projects (presentations and debates) but they are honestly enjoyable. If you do the work, you will get an A.
Assigned a long paper for a 500 pg book. Other than that, love this guy. Super clear and open-minded. Can't ask for much more.
Interesting class. Didn't understand how much I learned in the class until I went home for the summer and could apply a lot of what I studied in real life.
Easy, but annoying, class. Lots of useles essays/presentations.
Excellent.
Had her for my history seminar. She always gave good feedback and made herself very accessible for students. She's very clear in what she wants to see in your writing. Also, she is super sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Professor Tuchman for the History Workshop. The class has many writing assignments, culminating in one final research paper, but the process she lays out makes the task much more negotiable for students. She is truly focused on improving her students as writers and as historians. I highly recommend taking her if you have the chance.

Professor Tuchman is extremely knowledgeable about the subjects that she discusses, and the lectures were very interesting. There were only 3 short response papers and a final paper, so each grade counts. The grading criteria are not very clear on them, but if you read the books, you can easily get a decent grade. Solid choice for an MHS course!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The good: good personality, cares about students, knows the material, gives good essay feedback, has interest in the material and loves when students discuss the material. The bad: would give unclear essay prompts and then modify them very close to the deadline, grading criteria was sometimes unclear. Overall, she was good. Would recommend for MHS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof. Tuchman is one of the smartest people I've ever met. Her lectures are insightful, relevant, and direct. Participation is a big part of the grade, and she will make you work for good grades on papers (two short, one long). Can be quite nitpicky with sentence-level concerns, but gives detailed feedback. Her classes are worth the struggle.

Took this class because I am interested in nursing and women's empowerment. Did not miss out on either of these things! Prof Tuchman is such a genuine, open professor who truly cares about her students and their ability to absorb information that's important. So thankful for this life-changing class!

Professor Tuchman is a great professor. While this class didn't have lectures on a specific time period, she gave incredible essay advice. She was so helpful in developing a good research question and gave great feedback on the work. She was very particular on the essays, and it was a lot of work. I would take this class again.

This class is not an easy A, but it by far the most interest MHS class I've taken at Vanderbilt. You have to do the readings to participate and write the papers, but she goes over most of them in class. She's a hard grader, but is very helpful in office hours.

She rarely gives above a B grade on papers. She was nice but I didn't really like the class. You need to read the books for the papers. There are 4 papers and you MUST meet with the TA in order to write what they want (it's unclear on the prompt). If you need this for an MHS Core, it's not that bad.

Professor Tuchman is an awesome lecturer who clearly tells the engaging story of medical history. While I usually find history classes quite dry, she was engaging and creative in her class content. There is a lot of writing, but the papers are pretty easy and not research heavy. Definitely take this class/professor.
She's a very engaging teacher, but a hard grader. I liked the class enough to say that it was worth the hard grading though.

The TA's actually have to double check with her before giving out an A on anything.  Apparently, to her, "History of Medicine" means whining about the treatment of women, minorities, and colored people.  The text she uses is literally called "Major Problems in American Medical History."  The class is full of girls who want to be doctors...
If you're a second semester senior just please come to class! She'll love you forever if you just attend.
way too hard a grader.
very interesting class, good speakers, good discussions, grading on papers, however, is really really rough.

the class has tons of work, but has been one my favorite this semester. lots of outside speakers come in and are all very passionate. discussion among the studnets encouraged. there are options to drop papers, etc., and the grading is stringent-- especially on history topics. she knows her stuff

Although topics are interesting, class discussions are pretty bland with no direction, just jumping from topic to topic...also insane grader on paper, almost unfairly...take the class if you have to but be warned
Very hard grader when it comes to papers, which comprise 90 percent of the class grade.  avoid at all costs
Rough, final exam was surprisingly easy with a week's worth of studying.  Tests are pretty acceptable, papers are graded harshly.

Dr. Armstrong is one of the best at Vandy in the LLO program. She provides an inviting space for students to stretch and grow the content covered. Her grading prepares you for success in writing papers as your progress in the program. She provided a safe space for students to share their personal experiences with the content matter. The BEST!

She butchered this class. The asynchronous part was given by a respected and knowledgeable professor but she could not translate this as a discussant. She acted insecurely and unprofessionally. Her discussion was shallow, rude, and limited. She focuses on how to write a reference page rather than think because she doesn't know how to.

Very strict on APA. Makes you a better writer. Covers all readings and gives great feedback. Very kind hearted and understanding. Very very hard class she makes you work for your grade. Make sure you apply her feedback to your papers will return them if you dont. Very laid back. Learns your name after 2nd class. Attentive. Hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The material is extremely boring, the lectures are very dry, and the class is not an "Easy A". With that being said, if you put in the work (including befriending the TAs who are very nice), you can definitely get an A. Would not recommend if you are uninterested in history/archaeology.

This class is a must-take before graduation and the easiest A you'll get at Vanderbilt. His lectures are fun, interesting, and easygoing. Even when he goes off topic he tells the most interesting stories of his excavations and journeys. Tests and quizzes require minimal studying and are extremely easy. Readings are all on Brightspace for free.

Dr. Demarest is good at what he does but not teaching. Objectives for assignments, quizzes, and tests are unclear. He and the course in general are very disorganized and the readings are long and there is way too much material to study for each assessment.
Demarest is pretty good. Sometimes he can ramble on, but it was a fascinating class.  There is reading for almost every class, but it's doable and worth the time.

Demarest is crazy. He's a pretty stereotypical old crazy prof but crazy smart. He knows a ton about archaeology, and wants you to understand. He has tons of cool stories from his field work and tells stories in class a lot. The class is really interesting and he's a fun professor. There's no textbook and "required" readings are all posted online.

Demarest is great. Even if you aren't into anthropology, check him out. He's hilarious and also knows a ton about archaeology. He loves the subject and makes it easy for you to understand it too. He's generous with grading and curving. Would definitely recommend taking him for an easy and fun A.

Demarest is very much the classic crazy genius professor.  Sometimes he can rant and forget what he was talking about, but his good lectures are incredibly good.  Good enough to where reading becomes optional.  Overall a great class and experience.

Demarest is incredibly knowledgeable, and sometimes his overwhelming knowledge leads him off on tangents that (may or may not) relate to the course material, so it becomes a bit tricky to know exactly what to know.  The class lacks structure, but when you can understand what's going on, his points of view are incredibly interesting.

Prof Demarest is extremely knowledgable about mayan archaeology considering he's dedicated his life to it. The class is very dense and the tests are pretty difficult, but he offers an extra credit paper at the end of the semester that can help bring up your grade. Overall a pretty interesting class

He is definitely one of the leading researchers in the field and absolutely brilliant. That being said, if you like professors that are organized and classes with clear structures, don't take this class! I personally will avoid his classes like the plague in the future. Also, to me, it feels like he only cares about his graduate students.

I also took his 213 on the Maya. Great class! Gained invaluable knowledge about the actual practice of anthropology and I really appreciated the perspective it gave me in considering a career in antrhopological fieldwork. This class should probably be required for undergraduates, though I think should be a pre-requisite.After class discussions inte

Great Teacher! A good bit of reading, but he helps you with it as much as you want in office hours and he lets you call him at home any time. Really challenging but actually fun. Rambles about the real field work and discoveries that he does every year. Thats the most interesting thing about the course.
Absolutely batsh*t crazy. University has tried to fire him for a buncha stuff, I heard, but he's got tenure. Big name in field, apparently, just ask him!
No Comments
No Comments

While very full of himself and often a bit scatterbrained when it comes to lectures, He is one of the leading researchers in his field.  His organizational style and the insane amount of reading material were actually a plus, as this class gave me a better understanding of the key concepts and debates associated with the Maya than any other class on a specific culture or group.
No Comments

He is responsible and knowledgeable. Although he only talked about two models in this class, his explanation for each model is clear and meticulous. He proved each model from the beginning. There are nine homework and three exams, and you need to work hard on each of them. If you want to learn a lot in econometrics, do not hesitate to choose it.
He definitely expected too much from us-a masters level course should never be that difficult
But you have no choice

4 textbook problems and 1 quiz each week, nothing too bad. Each lecture covers a lot but Atkinson is a great teacher who will go above and beyond to help you understand. The examples he shows in class are super helpful. Tons of exam prep is provided. Exams can be tricky, but class averages were always high. Atkinson made diff-eq a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Atkinson does a good job teaching Methods of Differential Equations. His lectures can be a bit long and heavy at times but the material itself that appears on his quizzes and exams is pretty straightforward. Make sure you do the homework questions and prepare for the weekly quizzes and you'll sure to receive a fine grade in his class.
Very fair professor, no graded homework, only quiz, midterms and final exams count for the grade. Tests are not hard but stuff can be messed if you do not put in effort.

Very fair, straightforward professor. Not the best linear prof for visual learners (he doesn't really touch on the visual representations of things at all) but he cares about making sure students understand the material. Tests were fair, and the class is very doable if you put in a reasonable amount of effort.

One of the best math professors at Vandy. He mostly lectures out of the book but hes really good at answering questions. The class is fairly straightforward: just do textbook problems. Hes also very helpful during office hours. Lectures can occasionally be boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Probably the fairest math professor Ive had. The class isnt easy, but he makes it as straightforward as possible. Lectures are dry but he explains things very well. Funny on occasion.

Overall very good teacher, lecture is clear, if a bit dry, and he goes into depth on the subject matter, depending on how well students are understanding it. Very accessible outside class. Homework every Thursday, Quiz every Tuesday  Mandatory attendance. Generally a good choice for your math class needs.
Tuesdays are for Quizzes, thursday are for homework submission... So Attendance is mandatory. His lecture is clear, with lots of examples if you didn't follow his initial explanation.

I agree with everything the person below said. Forgot to mention that the homework is OPTIONAL. He assigns "suggested problems". I spent more time on homework for this class than I would have liked. He assigns 3 problem sets that are worth 25% of your grade. Do well on those (office hours). Exams were hard for me, but I'm not great at math.

Class is mainly him reading straight from the book, and can be a little dry. Gives short, straightforward and easy quizzes everyday that are pulled from the homework the night before. Explains concepts well, but assigns a lot of homework that is computation heavy and can be tedious. You must study and put in the time to do well on midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: While the weekly quizzes are pretty simple, the assigned papers do not have specific criteria. Professor Tyree provides details on what she requires after you submit the assignment, and you are penalized for forgetting something. Definitely, go to her office hours before every assignment, or you won't perform well. Lectures are long and repetitive

Professor Tyree was without a doubt the most frustrating teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Her expectations for assignments are beyond unclear, and not even office hours can give you clarification. The content is easy enough to understand, however the assignments are impossible to satisfy whatever it is she thinks is the "correct" way.

People have overreacted to her teaching with these ratings. She is a fine teacher despite what others have said. The class itself consists of many papers. These papers can be very time consuming to write. The group projects are also fairly time consuming. The class is mostly busy work. As long as you show up and write the papers you will get an A/B
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I too think some of the other responses are not accurate descriptions of my experience with Professor Tyree. Her instructions can be confusing, but she is very willing to meet outside of class to help. You have weekly quizzes but you get the questions prior. Around half of the grading is done by the TA, so that will depend by the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I think that the other responses are inaccurate descriptions of Professor Tyree. She is a very genuine and nice individual and makes class easy and fun. While her instructions on papers can be confusing at first, she is very easy to access and will meet outside of class. Additionally she responds to emails within a couple of hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Tyree barely gave any instructions for the papers and is incredibly inaccessible outside of class. Do not take her for Small Group Behavior.

bad. like really bad. Have never done more work with less direction and such a lack of clarity. Class is an absolute bore because she reads off of the slides and you can clearly tell she doesn't know the material. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Not a single person in my assigned group enjoyed this class with her. She is a very difficult grader (given the course material) and frequently assigns "busy work." She read directly off the powerpoints and had a difficult time answering questions from the class. Very "cold" demeanor. Wish I would have taken it with another professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Competent professor, straightforward class. I found Atkinson to be very approachable after class and in office hours. It's a little writing intensive for an intro class but very reasonably graded. She clearly cares about the subject and her students.

This class is pretty writing intensive with multiple essays and a research paper, but I found she was a pretty easy grader. Neither of the exams were that difficult. Her presentations are good, but you still need to go to class because she takes attendance daily. She's very nice and understanding as a person, and was helpful outside of class.

Professor Atkinson is definitely tough, but she genuinely wants you to succeed and is very approachable and knowledgeable about the material. I would absolutely take another class with her! The class is a lot of work for an intro level course, but if you put the time in, it's definitely manageable to do well.
Nice person although lectures are pretty cut and dry. Also has a weird grading system where she offers extra credit but kids have to compete to receive it. Not an easy A but not too hard either.

Draws from her own experiences to add a military perspective to her teachings.  Very clear if not particularly personable or helpful outside of class.  Do the readings and the assignments.  Tests aren't too difficult.

I actually really liked professor Atkinson. She is not as uncommunicative as the other posts would imply. If you check with her TA, and then don't email her late at night and wonder why she didn't reply, she is extremely helpful and supportive. I learned a lot in this class, and it was informative without being overwhelming.

I disagree with previous posts. This was an excellent class. Prof Atkinson has a no- nonsense style. Her lectures are effective and to the point. Her powerpoint slides are some of the best ever!! You need to do the readings if you want an A.

She is honestly the worst teacher I have ever had. Not only are you not allowed to email her with questions (one student did and she sent a mass email out to everyone telling them never to ask her questions before her TA) but her grading scale is unbelievably subjective. I used to be a poli sci major... not anymore!

Somehow the interesting course material is made boring and tedious by Prof Atkinson. She seems to go completely against the grain of Vanderbilt's professor-student relationship by being as inaccessible as possible. She defers all questions to a TA who unfortunately is extremely nitpicky and not entirely comfortable with English. Good class.Bad Prof

In addition to being extremely boring, is extremely knitpicking. In class stresses small details at expense of teaching the big picture. Tries to institute a military style environment to the class in adidtion to a ton of bureaucracy. Defers almost all emails to the TA and is very hard to contact. Does not realize that Vanderbilt is not the AirForc

She is the most boring teacher you could ever imagine. Her tests are really easy if you can manage to stay awake in class. Three tests, one paper. Easy A-/A but I used to want to be a poli sci major and this class completely changed my mind.

Made an interesting topic of international politics unbelieably boring. Provides no insight and simply reads off of slides. Readings are NOT necessary as she simply reposts key facts from them in her slide shows. One of the most boring teaching styles I have ever encountered.

Her class is pretty good. Not too boring. I enjoyed parts of it. The midterms are mutilple choice, and then alot of essay questions. The exams are focused on the powerpoint and text. Make SURE you read!!!! Reading determines your grade. If you do well you will be on her good side. She's a nice lady but you can tell she has a military background.

I don't understand the negative reviews here.  I found the material to be very interesting, the tests very fair, and the professor friendly and accessible.  He does grade the hometown history paper a bit harder, but if you put some good work into it you should be able to make a solid grade.  Getting an A is definitely within reach, I recommend.
By far the worst professor at Vanderbilt. Avoid at all cost

Maybe this class was brutal back in the day, but if you're thinking of taking it now ignore the comments below me.  The tests are very fair, and as long as you put a reasonable amount of effort into studying you should be able to make an A.  Professor is a bit pompous and condescending, but he's a clear lecturer overall and the material is engaging

I love economics and I love history. However, I have dreaded this class ever since the first week of school. This professor is condescending, pompous, and totally bias. He is by far the worst teacher I have had at Vanderbilt. Don't believe the comments that say if you go to class and take notes, you will get a B or A- because you won't.

Great professor and great class. If you hate economics or history, don't take it. But if you want an easy-to-understand professor who makes his expectations clear, then take this class. Tests are straightforward and the term paper is the economic history of your hometown.

By far the worst class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Lecture is incredibly dense- have to take notes for the tests too. Book is almost as boring as the lectures. He is an incredibly hard grader. I could not manage to get above a B- on anything. Not helpful. Stay away from this class unless you are a joint Econ/Hist major.
Straight lecture. Essay tests. Nit picky grader. Chooses favorites.

Professor Atack is such a great professor. He really keeps students engaged in his lectures and makes jokes to keep the subject relatable. He wears a microphone so that he can improve his lectures in the future which shows he really cares about teaching. One of my favorite professors this semester -- such a sweet, funny man.

Attend class, take copious and detailed notes, know them inside and out,and the tests are easy. Textbook reading is unnecessary. Outside readings sometimes helpful on exams. Don't write an off topic paper, else your hard work will be wasted. Not an easy class, but certainly worthwhile: you learn a lot. Atack is really helpful in office hours.

Atack is really quite a good professor. Attending class daily is a necessity, but the tests are not hard. The essay is not graded as harshly as people have claimed. Office hours are really helpful before the test, and he is willing to answer questions unrelated to class. Don't do the reading, its his lectures again in unnecessary detail.

Not a gimme A, but worth it.  Not nearly as bad as the previous posts have made him out to be.  Attending class (at least a majority) and taking good notes are musts if you plan on doing well.  Tests are detailed, but you should be fine with one or two nights worth of cramming, which is not asking much, three times over the course of a semester.

The class is by no means easy. BUT, he isn't as bad as the previous posts suggest. He's a great teacher and he really knows his stuff . . . and he is always willing to answer questions. All and all, it's not easy, but not many econ classes are. oh, and you really should go to class... that's pretty much  what the tests are based off of.

Please for the love of god and your GPA do not take this class with Attack. Unless you love taking the most detailed notes and bringing a tape recorder to class I seriously recommend you pass on this. You will not get an A, thats a fact, unless you plan on spending every waking moment studying.
Stone Cold Fox.
Though Dr. Atack's classes seemed really hard at the time, I think in the end they're all worth it and it takes getting used to not having everything handed to you on a silver platter

Absolutely miserable. He is so full of himself, doesn't care to help students and is only here to do research.  He purposely goes out of his way to act condescending when addressing his students, and is such a hard grader on the hometown term paper.  Watch out, worst econ professor at Vandy.
Terrible

Very difficult grader, sometimes unfair.  He seems like a nice guy during lectures, but after speaking to him one-on-one, he is a prick.  I saw he was very friendly with a student, and was shocked...until I realized it was the TA.  He is here to do research, not to teach.  Frankly doesn't give a crap about his students, which is too bad.

Atack is a terrible professor with no concept of how to properly teach a course. The grading is far too hard, and he's no help at all when you ask him to explain a concept that he views as too easy to be worth his time explaining to you.

I have been consistently disappointed with this course.  Atack considers low grades solely as a failure of the students and appears to accept no accountability for his lack of teaching the material effectively.  He's very arrogant in his interactions with the class and seems to lack any compassion whatsoever. Worst class I've taken at Vandy. AVOID!

This class is way to hard for just a 209 rating. Despite the fact that you don't need 232 or 231 to get in it, the class, based on its difficulty should at least be above 260. Atack is boring, The TA grades way to hard on the homework and we were misled on the first test thus leading to  2/3 of the class getting below a C. Don't take this class.

Attending class and taking copious notes is the key to doing well in this class. The tests aren't bad if you take good notes. Reading the book is unnecessary unless you have tons of time on your hands. He's a hard grader on the hometown history papers, so beware of that. Otherwise it's easy to get an A- in this class.
This class is horrible. Avoid it like the plague! He will bore you to tears and give you a bad grade to boot!
Go to class, take notes, read the book for clarity (if needed), and you'll get an easy B
horrible
Great class, learned a ton.  He's not very easy, but if you go to class youll get a good grade.  I heard lots of horror stories going in, but they just werent true.  I really reccomend him.

Best/nicest lecturer I have had at Vanderbilt. Grading is 56% exams, 24% mock tech interviews, 20% HW. Could change later. Heard they are testing different curriculums in the sections. Attendance not required, but recommended and 70+% means you can get a boost if your are on fringe of a grade. Few points extra credit before the 3 exams.
Not a good prof :(

Great guy but only rating him so low because I wasn't a fan of his TopHat presentation teaching style. Probably the hardest CS class I've taken and the exams are very weird. Instead of asking us to walkthrough an algo he taught in class on the exam, he makes up a scenario that's difficult to understand and asks a what-if question about the algo

Funny prof, relates a lot of what you learn with the real world. Also really inspirational, makes me feel like AI truly isn't going to replace us. Lectures are really well done and digestible, he gives plenty of extra credit if you volunteer for participation or do well on exam reviews. Also will work with you closely if you go to his OH

Disagree with the review about not needing to hear about his daughter's life. I think it makes his lectures much more personal. Professor Arena, I hope you get your daughter some Jamba Juice over the summer by using a topological sort to find the longest path there, because you need the extra time to write an optimal substructure proof.

One of my favorite classes. I learned so much and Prof. Arena was always very encouraging and down to earth. He often stayed after class to go over questions or discuss the HW with me and was fast to respond to emails.

Arena is overrated imo. His lectures are quite good (albeit he is a bit annoying -- I don't need to hear your daughter's life story each lecture), but his slides are not: less focus on abstract ideas; only specific examples. The homework in this class is a bit ambiguously worded and graded too generously. It's not all trivially easy, which is good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Truly the GOAT. Most chill dude ever, decent extra credit, good at explaining difficult concepts easily, is very down to earth. If you put in effort you will do well.

The goat, if you have the opportunity to take a course with Dr. Arena absolutely do that. He is funny as hell, an extremely talented lecturer, exceptionally fun and nice. He even showed up to a student's music performance after promising to do so because he wanted to support his students. Great guy and prof.

Algorithms is a difficult class, but to pass a technical interview, you're going to need to know many of the skills taught in this class. The homeworks are quite long, time consuming, and challenging, so make sure to start early. Dr. Arena has some great slides, and tries his best to give as much help as he can at OH and providing extra credit.

Good, but not as life-changing as people make it out to be. Arena is great professor: cares about students, covers the material well, down to earth, relates the content to concrete examples. But frankly, half the students don't show up to lecture and just learn from TopHat.
Chill teacher but algo is kind of a lot of work. Just study a couple days before the exams and you'll be fine

All the reviews are real, I had Arena as an advisor and for algo this semester and he was great. I think people have to think the course is hard if they have other professors. Only graded by homework and exams with not extra credit but grade modifying assignments (can bump half a point or two). Lectures cover everything included in hws and exams
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Arena is the goat. Take him if you have the chance!! This class is hard but Arena makes it fun. Grading is fair and he gives extra credit a lot.
Best CS class I've taken and probably the best CS professor I've had, up there with Roth. Definitely not an easy class but it is intellectually engaging.

Arena is an amazing prof who truly cares about student success. The class is challenging but manageable with the help of resources like the free textbook and tools like Unstuck AI. Definitely worth taking if you can!

This guy is AWESOME. Truly one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. His quality of teaching is great (definitely a bit fast, but he made it pretty interactive and interesting so it was easy to follow). He also gives a ton of extra credit opportunities. Definitely, definitely take a class with Arena if you're pursuing CS!

I never write these but Professor Arena is by FAR the best CS professor I have had at Vanderbilt. He truly cares about creating a class where anyone can succeed and giving so many extra credit opportunities that honestly help so much in actively practicing the material. If I could take every CS class with this man I would.

Great prof. One of the most human in the department. Truly cares about the quality of his lectures and improving his teaching and it shows. Professor Arena I hope you're reading this so you know your students see and appreciate the effort you put in
Best CS prof in Vanderbilt.

Awesome professor. Difficulty of the class will vary by person, but I'd say its an interesting class that's not too stressful while still challenging your thinking. The homeworks are spaced out enough so that you have time to work on them and ask questions to improve your understanding. Opportunities to participate in class for extra credit too!
super great dude. always willing to listen and help out. lectures were easy to follow and clear. tests and homework are very fair
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: great teacher, always willing to help, homework are tough, exams are fair, gives extra credit, overall great professor

Arena is the absolute GOAT of the CS department. The best professor I've had in STEM classes. The most down-to-earth, hilarious, and caring professor you'll have. Lectures are incredibly entertaining, and he is always doing everything he can to be available for students. He genuinely wants to see everyone succeed.
Take it with Arena if you can!

If you can take Arena for any of his classes I would wholly recommend it. He has a great teaching style and his exams and assignments are all extremely doable. Easily best professor in the CS department
the chillest chiller who ever chilled.
He is solid good. Explain concepts so clearly. Love him
Awesome prof, class not too bad. Tons of in class extra credit, and attendance not required but he gives a tophat grade and gives questions every class. Easy if you pay attention.

Fantastic class and professor! I feel so much better prepared for technical interviews. The person who wrote that his slides on Brightspace have a mistake isn't looking at the right slides. He even said in class those slides come from his old online course. The current semester slides are on TopHat.
His brightspace slides contain a mistake

Professor Arena is a great teacher and really cares about this student. Algo is not an easy class but Arena wants his students to do well and is a great teacher who will help you if you go to him (you'll be fine in this class if you put the work in). Definitely take Arena for every class possible!
There is nothing more to ask for. One of the best professors at Vandy. very chill and very caring.
Good professor overall -- lots of room for extra credit, good slides, and actually cares about his students.

Professor Arena is by far one of the most caring CS professors I've had so far. Algo is a hard class, but Arena is always readily available for office hours and provides opportunities for a lot of extra credit.

Dr. Arena is by far the best professor in the CS department, no questions asked. Algorithms is obviously a very tough course but if you take it with Arena you WILL do well!! His tests are significantly easier than Johnson's and his lectures are easy to follow. The uploaded videos were a LIFE SAVER so if you miss class, just watch those!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Homeworks can be very difficult, but concepts and exams not bad. Start homeworks early and go to TAs for help.

Generally a good professor, although could provide more in-depth practice problems to questions, bc the lecture ones do NOT help with the guided homeworks, which are VERY difficult under a time crunch. But you will learn a lot. A lot of it pointless, but a lot that is not. Feels like he's along for the ride with ya. And he makes bidenxtrump jokes

Hard class but great professor. Discrete didn't make as much sense to me, but he made it manageable. Would absolutely take any class he taught. Genuine guy and best professor in the CS department, easily.

Professor Arena is the best CS professor here. Hes funny, genuinely cares, and looks for ways to help you succeed. The subject material was harder for me, but I believe, without him, I wouldnt have done as well as I did. Exams are easier than homeworks which is nice. And every Friday, he brought snacks for when you got a question right. Take him!
Arena is the GOAT. Nuff said.

Prof Dan is definitely one of the best profs I've had at the school! Besides being a kind, caring, and entertaining professor, he explains concepts in a very clear and structured way. Homework is great exercise but has never been overwhelming. Take him at all cost!!

Prof. Dan is hands down the best professor I've had at this university. Makes this class, which is difficult, as easy as he possibly can. Very understanding, truly cares about his students and about their success. Very personable and successfully relates the material to the students, uses good real world examples when applicable. TAKE ARENA!
Amazing prof who made going to class fun. Will take classes just because he teaches them.

Prof. Arena is an absolute gem. His lectures are super thorough and detailed, he goes over plenty of practice problems, and is readily available on Piazza to answer questions at nearly all hours. He uses Zybooks for the textbook; he tracks attendance through TopHat participation (5% of grade). If you get the chance, take Arena for discrete!

I generally don't like CS profs at this school but he is caring and open to explaining things in ways that don't feel condescending. He also has been the most understanding about mental health issues and genuinely wants you to learn and feel your best in the class
he is the best cs professor at vandy
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can't say enough good things about Arena. He cares, and you will see that. Discrete structures is very difficult and at times convoluted, but Arena makes it somewhat enjoyable and easier to understand. If you are confused about something, Arena WILL help you. Difficult problem sets (4) but easier exams and other grade cushions (participation).

Prof Arena is probably one of the best teachers in the CS department. He seems to genuinely want to see you do well(ie he doesnt purposely sabotage grades) and gives you all the tools needed to succeed. For this being an asynchronous class, I found it to be one my favorite classes to actually work on all semester.

This was my second time taking Professor Arena, and he did an exceptional job teaching 2212 in an asynchronous format. His lectures and examples are very clear and it is easy to get in touch with him. Highly recommend!

Prof. Arena is one of, if not the best professors in the CS department. He is a very nice person and extremely helpful to students. He truly has a passion for teaching. Take him if you get the chance!
Just a great professor. Take him if you get the chance. If you listen to his lectures, you will be fine. Homeworks can be tough, but he's always ready to help.
Amazing prof. One of the best I've had during my first year at Vandy

Dr. Arena is amazing. He responds to questions immediately and definitely wants all of his students to learn. I already knew java coming in, but I knew others that didn't, and everyone found the class not too difficult. Honestly, as long as you do the PAs, you'll be completely fine. Some do take a good amount of time though. 100% would take again.

Cares about students learning CS and learning to think. Programming assignments due every week, but he gives you the tools to do them in class, and if you are stuck the TAs will guide you through in office hours. I've had better lecturers, but I knew many people in the class and they all agreed he was great, which is rare. He also cares a lot.

This class made me fall in love with Computer Science. Truly a great and understanding professor. The weekly programming assignments got tougher as the semester went on, but if you get help from the TAs in office hours you will be fine. I thought the homework was kind of fun, and the tests weren't too bad. He wants his students to work to get As.

Dan Arena is the GOAT and the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. The class overall and programming assignments are challenging, but Arena is a great teacher who gives you every opportunity to succeed. If you put in the time and effort you can get an A.

I took this class pass/fail during the COVID semester. Math major, no prior CS experience. I wish there was a class for ppl who just want to dip their toe into CS, not an aggressive intro weed-out class like this. Definitely directed towards people with at least some prior CS experience. Insane amount of work (PAs took me about 6hrs/week).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: So great! His personality made lectures engaging and he explained concepts well. For a beginner coder, homework was difficult at first -- so if you have no experience, know it's not a breeze. Work hard and go to office hours and you will do well. Prof. once spent 40 minutes helping fix my code, and he responds quickly to questions posted online
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Didn't get to know him personally, but I loved going to lectures. He's very accessible, does the most to help his students, and tries to make his class as engaging and interactive as possible. Attendance isn't mandatory, but zyBooks count for part of your grade. Overall, 10/10 recommend; if he's teaching a course you need, take it with him.
Very good

Professor Arena is one of my favorite professors: he clearly cares about students, is very helpful with any questions you may have, and makes learning CS a challenging but very rewarding experience! If you put in the effort, a good grade is fairly easy!

Only take 1101 with Professor Arena. His lectures are clear and well structured, and he can explain the material to anybody - I had zero experience coming into this class. Every week consists of programming assignments and a bit of busy work. Two extra credit opportunities are provided.

Dan Arena is a great guy who genuinely cares about his students. The class is definitely work heavy, but since a lot of your grade is based on the programming assignments, as long as you put the work in, an A is definitely do-able, even with no past coding experience.

Professor Arena is phenomenal. You can tell he loves his job just through the effort he puts into his class as well as making sure all his students are understanding the concepts. This IS the CS class to take if you are interested in being a CS major. An 'A' is doable if you put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Dan is a really great guy who actually cares about his students and he does everything he can to make sure everyone understands the material. Definitely take his section if you can!! The class is a good amount of work, but office hours make it a lot easier.
It is a great introductory computer science course. The assignments take about 8-10 hours per week, but it gives you a good grasp of Java. Arena is a fabulous teacher who keeps lectures entertaining.

Only complaint is sometimes the Zylabs sample runs are off so you end up wasting submissions on the projects. His lecturing itself isn't great but his slides are really, really useful and if you learn them you'll do great on tests. Giving him a 5 more because he's a great guy who cares so much about his students' well-being, academic and otherwise.

The other reviewers aren't wrong  he is a very great lecturer and cares for his students. Definitely take his section of CS 1101 if you are on the fence about majoring in CS  I know a lot (myself included) who decided to major in CS thanks to professor Arena. An easy A if you already have background in coding
Arena is the reason I am majoring in CS

CS 1101 is a great class. Like the other comments say, it is a lot of work-- specifically with the programming assignments; however, Professor Dan makes these doable. I don't agree that this class is an easy A, I definitely think it is has gotten harder every semester, and requires more work. The tests are HARD: make sure to study for them!!!

He's an amazing professor who explains concepts really well. His slides are super clear and he will go over some concepts twice if he thinks the class doesn't understand them well enough. Easily the best professor you can take for 2212
Arena is the best professor for Discrete. Quizzes are all straightforward/fair and if you study his lectures you'll do well. Super funny guy who makes the class way more interesting than it could be.

I loved the course and if you do want to take 2212 I would recommend Dan Arena. An A is definitely attainable. He makes sure you understand concepts and will not test you on anything he feels he hasn't taught well. He is a very caring Professor and I am glad to have taken the class with him. Probably one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt

Professor Arena is one of the best professors I've had in the CS department here. He explains the material super clearly and thoroughly in class, and makes hard concepts easy to understand. Quizzes are graded fairly, and he is pretty accessible outside of class. I would definitely recommend Arena for discrete
He is a wonderful professor. He gives very good lectures. But if you want to get an easy A, I do not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The other ratings say it all. Great lecturer, posts each day's slides online. Obviously, going to class is the best way to ensure an A, but its pretty doable to miss a bunch of them and still pull it off, especially if you have prior programming experience. Most of the assignments are very time consuming, but not overly difficult.
1101 is a lot of work, but if you do the programming assignments well and actually go to class, it is not hard to get an A. His course convinced me to switch my major to CS

Dan Arena is my favorite professor so far at Vanderbilt. When you go to him during office hours, he knows exactly what to say to make you feel competent and respected. He was extremely helpful during office hours and his lectures are clear. Made me become a CS major and was always caring about his students. Truly a gem at Vanderbilt.

Arena is my favorite professor at Vandy so far. Extremely helpful, engaging, and knows what hes talking about. Lectures are super informative though not mandatory to go to. Class is naturally a lot of work but Arena is absolutely the way to go if you want to do well. Definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Arena is one of the most genuine, caring professors at Vanderbilt. Coming into this class with no programming experience I found the material of this class extremely difficult, but Prof Arena is so helpful in office hours and also responds to emails/posts on Piazza discussion board very quickly. His lectures are clear and he posts slides too.

Professor Arena is nice and available outside of the class, answering the email and piazza questions as soon as possible. Class's homework is time-consuming but it is more annoying than hard, and the tests are really straightforward and easy. Definitely an easy A and good experience with Java even though you have no experience in coding before.

Prof Arena made an introductory class a really special experience for so many people. He loves teaching and is so good about answering emails, etc. and helping out students with their grades or questions. Such a funny guy that you can tell really cares about his students, posts lectures so you don't have to go but you should for his explanations
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great prof. He really cares if you learn the material. Lot of work but it's totally worth it.

Umm it is easy to get A-, but you actually need to work hard for A or A+(if u want to get A+ u need to be perfect lmao) because your grade is determined based on how people do in class (btw if ur grade is over 90, then it is guaranteed A-). You can get A if u have a solid background. I think A+ cutoff >98. Well it is a fun class.
Absolutely awesome!

Professor Arena is so dedicated to helping you learn CS. He answers questions for everything, at almost all hours of the day. His teaching style is very helpful for anyone who knows nothing about this subject. This class can be hard bc CS is hard, but Arena really helps you get into it. Take him!

Professor Dan is an awesome teacher. His lectures are really entertaining and easy to follow. He really cares about how well you understand the material, and he's super easy to meet with outside of class. Definitely take him for any CS course you can.

Arena is the man!!! A great teacher, and sets it up where it is helpful when you go to class, but isn't essential to attend because lectures are online. You get out of the class what you put into it (the PAs are a huge time commitment) but i've learned so much over the past semester. Take this class if you have any interest in Computer Science!!

PAs are a lot of work, but they really do help a lot with understanding the concepts. Arena is definitely one of the best lecturer in Vanderbilt. I had no experience with programming before, but he teaches so well.

Professor Arena is very good at explaining concepts and its never a real mystery what are on exams. Dont really need to attend lectures since they are posted online but worth it if you end up having trouble. Very nice and answers all questions (through email or piazza) he receives.
Great professor. You can go to less than half the lectures and be fine - he posts all of them and they're pretty clear.
Cares about your learning and does everything he can to help you do well in a class that is not easy. Heard great things about him before taking the class and they were not wrong.
Dr. Arena is out to assist students and make sure they pass, often staying after classes are over in order to help students while also being available by email. Fantastic professor!
Arena is a great professor. Definitely the best for Discreet Structures. It can be a decent amount of work at times, but his lectures are entertaining and he explains concepts well.
