Probably the best professor in Vanderbilt Engineering. Always take his class if you can enroll in since so many people are trying to get into his session. The professor is so so so so nice but the class itself is challenging. Try to spend about 10 hours every week coding and debugging. The TAs are super strict on grading.

Dan just started teaching 2201 this semester, and he ROCKS, but it's a little more tough to be in his class rather than Roth's because Roth makes all the final decisions. Dan cares about you and your learning and will do everything to make you understand content. Great teacher, just make sure you are working to Roth's standards on PAs and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great professor, great stories, fabulous lectures!

Dan is a great teacher. This class isn't that hard and there are no tests, only quizzes. It's easy to get in the B range but really hard to get in the A range since so many things determine your grade in the class.

Dan is an amazing teacher. I had no programming experience coming into this class and he makes everything really easy to understand. It is a lot of work, but it's rewarding work. He is super helpful on Piazza and is good to go to for office hours if you have something the TA's can't answer. And he gives candy on Friday's for happy hour!

If you have any sort of programming experience and/or are good at logic, class is very easy. You can honestly show up to class maybe once every 2 weeks and still get an A. Just make sure you understand the lecture slides, which he'll post every day. Super helpful on Piazza too, and responds quickly.

Professor Dan is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is so helpful and really cares about his students' success. It's sometimes hard to go to lectures because they aren't mandatory, but if you go, you will learn and probably do better in the course. Some assignments are difficult, but there are TA office hours every day to help.
Made me work for an A. Didn't attend to many lectures, but if you read his slides and the textbooks, its do able

I love this man, he is friendly, accessible, and obviously very knowledgable and passionate about the subject. Inspired me to switch my major and made difficult concepts easy to understand. 10/10 the coolest dude

Professor Arena is an excellent instructor. Lectures are very clear, and he is always very willing to help. For example, on days where programming assignments would be due (Usually 11:59 PM), he would stay behind after class and help students who had trouble or questions. Tests are straightforward, assignments are easy but sometimes time consuming.

Professor Dan is easily the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt; he truly cares about his students' success. While this class definitely makes you work pretty hard, it is worth it-- you will learn so much. The tests are relatively easy, but the weekly programming assignments will typically take a few hours.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Dan was a great professor who had lectures that were easily understandable even if you've never programmed before. He explains things very clearly and is helpful if you ever have questions. Programming assignments are very doable if you put in the time and go to office hours if you have trouble.

Out of all of the professors I had last semester, Prof Dan was easily the best. Programming assignments are fair with a noticeable increase in difficulty a few times throughout the course. He is always on Piazza or email to the point where he will respond to questions at 10pm or later on the nights where assignments are due.
Great teacher, always available and replies his emails within a short time. He explains the material clearly and answers your questions. Difficult class though, I struggled to get an A.

Dan is a great teacher. Since 1101 is a big lecture hall intro class, a lot of people don't come, which I think is a shame because I learned so much from him in just one semester. Office hours are very helpful with programming assignments and as long as you don't start them the night before and put in time you'll be fine.

Definitely the teacher of choice for CS1101. Lectures are effective at teaching the material and also entertaining at the same time. Did an amazing job at fielding questions on the online discussion board we used, and is available for further help if contacted. If you start assignments early/attend office hours when needed, you should do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Arena is a great professor -- he has this vibe of "let's get through this together" in his teaching which is really inspiring. My only complaint was that we used TopHat for lecture, which is unnecessarily complicated when the powerpoint could just be posted on Brightspace.

Keeps the class lively and entertaining. Teaches the material in an understandable and relatable way that makes you want to learn more from him. Would prefer if he taught all my classes. There is a good amount of homework, but that should be expected from a CS class.
The professor is sooooo great, but the course does require a lot of work.
Professor Arena is one of the most fun and understanding professors I've had, yet he is also great at teaching students all of the material in a clear and interesting manner. He's super great!

Professor Dan was truly amazing! His lectures are quite fun. Attendance is not mandatory, but highly recommended. Programming assignments may sometimes take a really long time to complete, but are ultimately rewarding. It is not hard to get an A in this class, if you are organized and do your best on the programming assignments.

Pretty great dude. He has amazing lectures, teaches content well, and focuses on making sure you understand whatever is happening. He cares a lot about each individual student even though its a big class. If you're taking 1101, make sure its with Dan.
Always there to help, and his lectures really help with the exams and homework. Go to class and you'll do fine. #1 tip is start assignments early, so the TA's will be able to help if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very kind and wants you to do well in the course, hilarious and makes class and assignments fun

I took CS 1101 as a high school student, so it was both my first college-level class and my first formal Computer Science class. Professor Arena made the curriculum very clear and understandable with his excellent lectures, and though he assigns a lot of homework, the work done outside of class was extremely helpful and well worth the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: This class is pretty good at helping you learn Java. This class quite manageable if you have even a little coding experience. Otherwise, you'll have to work a bit. Professor Arena is very engaging and a good lecturer, and even a little funny, so I highly recommend taking it with him. The programming assignments take a long time, so start them early
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Dan was probably my favorite professor I've taken so far. Cheesy pop culture references, extremely helpful lectures, and nearly uninterrupted accessibility outside of class helped my understanding of Comp Sci a ton and made class really enjoyable. Definitely an extremely time intensive course, but it's totally fulfilling and worth it.

Prof. Arena is a highly competent and caring professor. He absolutely know his stuff, and he is able to teach it well too. The class itself is challenging and there is lots of homework, but it is manageable if you put in the effort. Prof. Arena and the TAs are very accessible and want you to pass, so if you put in the effort, you will succeed.

Loved the course but it is no joke. I had no prior programming background but I had no issue getting things done. The TAs and professor are super helpful on programming assignments. You have to be willing to do hours of work a week, around 10-15.

Prof Dan is a real solid guy. He is always willing to help with assignments and you get multiple submissions if you don't get it exactly right on the first try. Also, the test aren't necessarily easy but they're not killer by any means. The averages always lied around B to A-, and he does curve if it needs to be done.

I've already taken AP Computer Science before, so most of this class was a breeze. Despite that, Professor Arena still taught me a lot of new things because of how good he is at explaining the concepts and answered my questions perfectly each time. Would definitely take Arena again for Discrete Structures.

Professor Arena is awesome. The class is difficult for people who have never coded before, but after the first test it is not bad. Failed the first test, but then got As on the rest, so do not worry. Be ready to code a lot. Projects take a long time, but are super helpful for really learning the material.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: This is my first year at Vandy and no background in CS what so ever but Arena is the guy that made me want to become a CS major. He is super chill and funny in class. Obviously know what he is talking about and MWF 12-1 he has office hour and always helps his student on their program. Great professor. Course is challenging but doable.

Amazing professor and by far my favorite at Vanderbilt. Hard, hard class though. Even with Java and APCS background, you'll definitely have to work for an A. Roughly 15-20 hours a week of work outside of class, but very rewarding and fun once finished. Dan is very accessible and helpful. Go to office hours!
He posts the lectures online and is super helpful in office hours. I highly recommend using the office hours for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Arena is funny, helpful, and accessible. Don't get the optional textbook, it's useless. But he's very organized and overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lot's of very hard homework for the course but I went to his office hours and he helped me more than my actual professor! Obviously knows what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: His lectures are just so fun - he always has tons of cool real-life examples and case studies to go along with the boring textbook stuff (the mock trials/discussions of court cases on Fun Fridays are hilarious and really get the whole class engaged) The quizzes are not too hard if you review the slides carefully and he is kinda an easy grader too.
Great class. Great professor. Learned a lot.

CS1101 is a hard course. You definitely need to put a lot of time and effort into the course if you want to do well - there were times that I spent 20+ hours in office hours in a week. But Professor Arena was great! His lectures are clear and he is extremely helpful in office hours! If your gonna take 1101, take it with Arena.
Awesome, caring and the best professor I've ever had.

With weekly programming assignments, this class requires a lot of effort. Even for those who have some CS background and are CS majors (like me), the homework still takes a lot of time and can be tricky. Arena is a fabulous teacher though. He welcomes questions in class and is quick to answer emails.  I also took CS 1151 with him, which was good.

This year they reprogram all assignments and they are really challenging. I have no background and it is really hard at first. But I REALLY learned a lot. Prepare to spend a lot of time on this course. Professor Dan is the best!!! He is always there to answer your question and help you. If you love CS and prepare to major in it, definitely take it!

Vandy made this course harder than it previously was before Spring 2017. It is a challenging course but very interesting and you will learn a lot. Arena is a great teacher and he genuinely cares about his students. Great class all around if you're up to the challenge.
In short, Arena is a great lecturer and I was glad to have him. He's a gem in office hours and I'd recommend him to anyone.
He is a wonderful and fair professor.  Lectures always contain some humor, and he is very easy to work with and get in touch with outside of class.

Great professor, but one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. The sheer workload for this class dwarfed all my other courses combined. There are weekly homework assignments that really take quite a lot of effort to do. He's unbelievably responsive to questions, and is good at explaining the concepts. Seriously--Great professor, difficult class.
One of the best professors. Gives feedback so fast.... I asked a question on piazza and ten seconds later I received a response
don't buy the textbook. he's so great. love hte class. take ethics with him if you can. study for the quizzes
Hes great, love the guy.  Do the homework and youre fine

I've taken more than my fair share of traditionally difficult classes at Vandy, but none compares to CS 1101. It's a TON of outside work (10-17+ hrs/week). Prof. Arena is a great choice and very accessible outside of class, but Java is definitely not for the faint-of-heart. Do not take the class unless you are TRULY considering a CS major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Arena is phenomenal. Got through this course without ever opening the textbook because of how thorough & clear his lectures were. He is also very approachable when you have questions and seems committed to helping students succeed. Best advice for this class: Start assignments early and go to office hours if/when you get stuck.
Awesome. Professor Dan was really great and really cared about the students. I know it was his first semester teaching it, but I thought he did a great job with a tough subject.

Seriously one of the nicest professors ever. This course in particular was a bit rough because it was his first year and it contained a lot of reading off the slides and equivocal explanations of concepts, but the material isn't too difficult to begin with. But he still rocks.

Professor Arena is extremely helpful. He's patient with every student's every question. When you think you should get some credit back from any test or assignment, as long as your request is reasonable, he's definitely gonna help you. He takes the honor code really serious so you will always be rewarded for your honesty and hard work in his class

Professor Arena has been my favorite professor this year. He is very funny in lectures and extremely helpful in office hours. He definitely cares for all of his students and really does his best to teach us. The class itself is fine, some of the programming assignments can be difficult but you get a week to do them. Would recommend 10/10

Professor Dan is great. I went in with no CS experience, and he made it relatively parsimonious if I paid attention. Tests aren't too bad if you read the lectures and the textbook. The class had a few too many assignment that seemed only doable with LOTS of TA help or previous programming experience, when this is supposed to be an intro class.

He is a great, nice teacher. He knows the material. I definitely thought the course had way too many assignments, and the grading criteria was very picky. However, that isn't professor Arena's fault at all. I think he is the most interesting and funny out of all of the CS 1101 professors.

As a student who had never taken a CS course before, Arena really made me glad I did. Very personable and makes the lectures about as interesting as comp sci lectures can be. Weekly homework can be very challenging at times but it forces you to really know the material. Would definitely recommend.

Definitely one of my favourite professors at Vanderbilt. Office hours are a great time, and classes are fun too. Professor Dan genuinely cares about his students. Once, he stayed after class on a Friday for two hours to help me fix my mess of a program. He's the reason I'm considering a CS major. I wish I could take all my CS classes with him.

Professor Dan is very helpful from day one. He cares about how his students and this is demonstrated by him asking for feedback after every test about what the students thought. Assignments can sometimes get pretty lengthy but he gives ample time as well as 4 free late days. 10/10 would recommend. 12/10 with rice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The homeworks were hard and took time, but definitely paid off. My favorite class, such a funny guy.

Dan Arena is hands down the best professor for CS 1101. He is a good lecturer and is happy to help you outside class. I went to his office hours a few times and he was not at all intimidating. If you are able to take his class I would absolutely recommend him over any other professor.

The homeworks take time but the TAs are always available and Dan is really helpful during office hours. The tests are easy as long as you read the lectures. You don't need to go to class to do well but Dan is very entertaining.
THE BEST
Professor Dan is the best professor I have had at college. He is hilarious and insightful and knowledgeable and approachable.

intro cs is a weirdly structured class and the curriculum is kind of strangely ordered, so it seems like they brush off a lot of explanations saying we'll get to that later, but the class itself is pretty interesting and Dr Arena is good at explaining concepts so he's one of your best bets at not becoming frustrated by the curriculum.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are weekly discussion posts(300 words) due by midnight each Friday and biweekly assignments(500 words) due by midnight either Sunday, Wednesday, or Friday depending on the week. It is easy to receive a high A on all of these assignments that comprise the majority of your grade. 5 easy quizzes (3 at home online) (4 questions each) and a final.
She is very kind and great lecturer. Have been taking her class from sophomore to Senior. Would definately recommend her class to everyone

Prof. Nakano is really nice. There are LOTS of interaction during lessons, and she is always passionate about helping students to improve. Homework is somewhat heavy, but they are a part of the integrated learning experience and is graded leniently. If you love the subject and spend some effort, it is going to be a happy, easy A.
Very nice and kind Japanese professor. I'll definitely take her course again.

Nakano-sensei is a really really nice professor. Learning Japanese can be difficult, but she makes it instructive and fun at the same time. There is a bit of homework outside of class, but that is expected of a 5 credit hour course. She goes over the grammar and vocab in class so you get hands on practice. Tests/quizzes are straightforward.
She's so nice, and she explains the grammar very clearly. Just listen in class and do the homework and everything will be just fine.

Really nice person and is super knowledgeable about the course material. Pretty hefty on the readings so coming to class prepared w/ a few talking points is a good idea. Fun activities like teaching a class as a group & other things to help understand concepts surrounding technology. Most of grade is comprised of essay based midterm & final project

Nice guy. Really nice guy so I feel bead writing this, but  not worth it. Too much of a stingy grader (never gives 100), biased graded and and dumb content and lextured . Just avoid if possible, not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Carse was great! You can tell that he really cared about the course material and genuinely wanted everyone to succeed. I would recommend this class to everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Carse is one of my favorite all-time professors. You could tell he really cared about what he was teaching about and wanted his students to feel that same passion. Doing most of the readings (at least skimming) and participating in class is definitely helpful for your learning. The class discussions are some of the most interesting I have seen.

Two medium-to-long essays. Fair amount of reading. Super interesting class, great lesson plans, lots of discussion/activities instead of lectures. Prof is super cool and wants to hear your thoughts on the content. A participation-based class but I think most people felt comfortable and I looked forward to it every day. I would say an easy A-.

Prof Carse is kind of awkward and can be apathetic sometimes, but his class isn't too difficult as long as you do the work. Pretty interesting material, just beware he loves to cold call on difficult questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Was my first course in HOD and I felt it was not for me, but Dr Oberoi was a pretty great teacher. She brought in engaging speakers and always taught the content well. Easy, well structured and a decent class, and Dr Oberoi did manage to communicate pretty well.

2 short papers, one group essay, 2 exams, one final group presentation. The class is a great intro for consulting, and Dr. Oberoi is incredibly kind and prioritizes student well-being. She's a very fair grader and gives helpful feedback. Could not recommend more.

WOULD NOT RECCOMEND. Nice ish professor. Difficult class. The TA was not the most knowledgeable when I took it and that was extremely frustrating. She has some good policies like 2 free absences and an automatic revision but the course itself is harder than other 2100 classes by far. rubrics are unclear, I did not like this course.
2 tests, 1 final consulting presentation and 2 papers (1 paper is team of 2).

At first, Professor Oberoi was tough, but she took our feedback and incorporated it thoroughly. She did not have to put in the extra time to help us succeed, but she did. She teaches to help you become a consultant, not for you to memorize terms. She is fair and continues to make sure that you are putting in your full effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A sweet and kind professor who makes her class super easy to follow. You can either pay attention in class or skim through the textbook. Her lectures are basically repeats of the chapters in the book. As long as you put in some effort to know what's going on, this class should be easy and enjoyable.

Prof. Oberoi is such an amazing lady! Most of the 2100 teachers out there are such a disappointment, but she truly is a hidden gem. She's kind, knowledgeable, and never overwhelms her students. Best option for "Understanding Organizations" by far!
the best.
show up to class, sit towards the front, and get to know the guy! he's such an awesome and caring person and will help you succeed if you just ask for help.

Dr.Choudhoury is a really caring professor. His lectures are good and he does his best to ry and give his students funny stories to remember important material for the tests. However his tests are difficult, read the book and put the right UNITS, HE WILL DEDUCT IF YOU DON'T DO THIS. He is a caring professor and will try to understand you.

Material science is a difficult class but Dr. Choudhury gives you more than enough resources to help you succeed. Even though he doesn't have fixed office hours, he'll grab breakfast with you and will leave his afternoons open for Q&As. His slides are really good so it's easy to catch up if you miss class. He also learnt everybody's names :)

He's an amazing professor and amazing lecturer. You can do well in the class but you also need to put in the work. Cares so much about you and will go out of his way to meet you outside class hours. He has amazing slides. Recommend going over them before class because he does add on to them during the lecture and these additions are important.

Ashok is truly an amazing person who cares deeply for his students and the material. However, he doesn't go over any calculations in class (HW and exams= mostly calculations).

But, the exams in this class are SO fair. No surprises. If you know how to do all the HW problems well and understand the big conceptual topics, an A is within reach.

One of the nicest professors at Vandy, but does not teach to the test AT ALL. All of class is conceptual and the exam is genuinely 90% math. He definitely is the better professor than Rogers, but rogers makes the test and has participation points. If you want to learn Material Science, take Ashok, if you want a good grade, take Rogers.

Dr. Choudhury is my favorite professor at Vandy so far. His lectures are a bit dry and the homework is a bit difficult, but the exams are pretty fair. He is such a great person and goes out of his way to learn everyone's name even with over 70 students in class. He is super accessible and always answers questions and hosts reviews outside of class.

Professor Choudhury does not provide study guides for exams, does not go over calculation problems in class, & his lectures can be boring (mostly just because of the content). However, he cares about his students, is always willing to answer questions, & knows the content. If you can help it, he is the only relevant choice for Materials Science.

Professor Choudhury is a great Professor. He really cares about his students and will go the extra mile to ensure that they are able to succeed in his class. His office hours are great and honestly a required part of the class. He cares about what he teaches, and while lectures are confusing, he is more than happy to clarify afterwards.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students. The class requires some outside learning and the lectures are boring, but he's definitely the best MSE prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Choudhury is a solid choice. Not easy, there's a significant amount of material, and this class is pretty boring, but Prof. Choudhury is pretty funny and you can tell he cares that you learn. You will have to spend time outside of class just to understand the lectures, and exams are kinda difficult.

Ashok is a really good professor that explains the materials (no pun intended) super well. He is also extremely helpful outside of the lecture if you actively seek help from him. Make no mistake, this class is NOT "easy", you have to put in hard work if you want an A (i.e. study at least 8-10 hours per week and be on top of anything).

Fun guy, lectures are interactive and he does his best to keep everyone's attention but his slides can be boring after a while. Material overall is a bit dry but Ashok's always able to meet and further explain things... he will even boost test grades if you meet with him. Learning outside of the classroom is needed for a good grade.
He is arguably my favorite professor so far at Vanderbilt. He is extremely helpful outside of class and legitimately cares about his students. Choudhury is the best!

Caring teacher that does try his best to make the class interesting. His lectures are often not related to any material that is tested on, and he primarily focuses on theory, while the tests are largely calculation based with many equations that aren't covered in class. His grading rubric for tests seems random and takes off random number of points

Choudhury is super caring and wants the best for all his students. He is really into his field, and is always willing to meet with you. Reading is not necessary, but can be helpful. Weekly quizzes, so make sure to show up on quiz days, and short weekly HW. His lecture are mostly theory, but his tests are more math-based, which is frustrating.

Choudhury is SO GREAT. His lectures are a bit dry, but he knows his stuff, he's the nicest guy, loves to help students, and he uploads lecture notes. The review sessions are helpful. One thing- he likes to call on random students in class for answers, so you have to pay attention.

Prof. Choudhury is an amazing teacher and really involves the class in his lectures. People say that his class is more difficult than Wittig's but that is because he doesn't reuse tests. The course is very doable and it isn't too hard to get a good grade. He is also extremely approachable and helpful. Final not necessary is you make all A's.
He's so amazing. If you really pay attention in his class, you'll definitely get an A! He's always willing to help everyone even outside the class. The best  instructor ever!

This professor is super amazing. The best instructor I've ever had here at Vandy. Super helpful even outside the class. He showed his interest in helping students. Explained things very well and clearly.You should choose him or else you'll regret.

In class, pop quizzes were easy, and Cengage hw's were easy. The issue was that you had to be in class on time, not even 1 min late, which made it a little stressful. She also doesn't like computer screens and moved everyone to the front in the last month. She's a funny prof. I didn't learn a lot, but its a really easy A.

Maxcey is an interesting lecturer and makes the class engaging with videos, examples, and interactive stuff. She made all 200 of us move to the bottom few rows because of people using screens which made class extremely uncomfortable for a month. Graded on daily in class quizzes (easy) and Cengage textbook homework (also free). Take for a free A.

Take the class if you want a free A. Interesting lectures about different Psych applications (AI, self-care) but little coverage of core MCAT topics outside of the HW. More small-group conversation/activities than most large lecture classes. Her lecture style/language is a bit casual for me. Must arrive on time to take quizzes.
Easy A, but she will not continue class if she sees you on your computer.

Dr. Maxcey is too worried about the things that take place in the classroom.  While some people who use computers for things unrelated to class that sit in the back are not great, she obsessed over them too much and punished the whole class for it.  She is too easily distracted, and it took away from learning.  Easy A though.

Maxcey is so sweet. No exams, long and frequent homework assignments, and in-class activities. Wonderful person, but large lecture format makes this course less for the people who love stats, more for the ghosts in the classroom If your goal is to take a stats class where you can get an A but have no obligation to learn, Maxcey stats is your dream
Maxcey is wonderful! No exams, just grades based on attendance, readings, and SONA. she wants this to be a low stress class. she's super sweet and we have engaging class discussions.
This class is light work. No exams in the class, and the grades are based on SONA, homework, attendance, and MMB. Other than that, just enjoy the class and get that A

Super easy A. Just attendance, homework and SONA research participation. Class was so fun she's hilarious and makes it very engaging and interesting. Maybe not the best if studying for MCAT because you don't need to study but I really enjoyed and all material is posted on PPT slides, plus great for GPA.
You can tell she really cares about what she's teaching and is good at getting people interested in the topics.
just show up to class. No exams. No papers. No nothing. just sona credits and online questions. Easy peazy
Easiest A ever. There are no exams in the class and grades are based on attendance, homework, small assignments, and SONA credit. She is an amazing person too.
She is the best professor I have ever had. Nobody will beat her. She is an amazing professor.

Maxcey's psychology class is a breeze! No exams, just easy homework and fun, engaging lectures. I loved how she tailored the material to what we wanted to learn. Definitely take this class - unstuck ai was a big help for study prep too.
Loved the class structure and formatting, had a good time w Maxcey and she was really accommodating at various points.

i remember vividly when she once said, "I don't know why anyone would take anything other than psychology, it's the most interesting/best thing" (something like that) and it just kinda turned me off from the class tbh bc it's like why would u disregard ppl's interests, not everyone is interested in psychology and wants to do something in it..

took this class for a few days n dropped out a while ago bc she didn't give me good vibes tbh; was kinda rude n i didn't like it. also feels like she thinks she's a lot better than everyone else. idk abt the new assessment structure ppl r talking abt since i dropped but it seems better ig, idk? personally i took a diff psych class n i'm glad i did

After lots of turmoil regarding the assessment structure for the class, she took action to restructure the assessments and make life easier for her students. You can tell she is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about psychology, and cares a lot about her students.

I LOVEEEEE Prof Maxcey, she's an amazing lecturer, doesn't give exams, and is literally so funny. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her definitely do it, she's my top psych professor. The only thing is the homework for quan methods was tedious but the no exams makes up for it.

Professor Maxcey is the best professor at Vanderbilt! She is so cool, so knowledgeable, and will always take the time to answer any questions I have. I am taking every class she offers. 

The class was not challenging (as long as you put in the work and attended class). There were (very easy and short) in-class quizzes for attendance!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was the easiest class I've ever taken at Vanderbilt. HALF of the grade is homework and there are no exams or essays. Professor Maxcey is a wonderful person too, I never personally talked to her but she made me feel like she was someone I could always talk to. Really nice and funny in my opinion.

Maxcey is amazing. Not stressful and a very interesting class. She really cares about her students and doesn't want to add to their loads. She bases her lectures off of what her students want to learn most. I definitely recommend taking her class or probably anything she teaches.

Maxcey's General Psychology is a fantastic class that does not add substantial stress to an academic schedule. Grading was homework and participation based as opposed to tests, but pop quizzes are given at the end of class based on the subjects discussed. A pleasure to listen to during lecture and interact with.
Her class was one of the most fun class I've taken!! The topics were so interesting and she made lectures so fun, applicable, and interactive. I felt comfortable participating in class.
No final exam, or any exams at all and classes are really fun and engaging.

I love her so much! She has a talk-style way of teaching and allows us to absorb as much information as we see benefitting us. Although the class was super chill (no real quizzes, tests), I was able to learn so much about myself.
This is the easiest and most interesting class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. I highly recommend even if you do not need to take this class.

Dr. Maxcey cares about her students, and she is a kind person. Lectures were more like conversations, which is rare in large classes. However, the class was unstructured in terms of curriculum. While I enjoyed the course, I don't think it would be helpful for MCAT/grad school prep or when a firm understanding of traditional gen psych is required.

Dr. Maxcey obviously wants her students to succeed, as evidenced by her decision to completely restructure her course after a lot of students complained after the first paper. Her lectures were always interesting and interactive, and it honestly didn't feel like a stereotypical lecture; rather, it was like she was holding a conversation with us.

Easily the best professor I had this semester!!! The bad reviews are from those who were dumb enough to ignore her instructions for the first paper. The grading was very fair throughout and the guidelines were clear. She goes out of the way to make the class engaging and teaches in the most unique & interesting way. Learned the most in this class.

Maxcey truly cares about her students and their learning experience. This class is not a typical course where you learn terms and definitions, but she makes the class an engaging experience! In the beginning, the course started out rough due to low grades on the 1st paper, but she completely restructured the course and made it SO easy for everyone

Professor Maxcey was easily my favorite professor this semester, and I loved taking her Gen Psych class. Her passion for the field of psychology shines through in all of her lectures and she deeply cares about her students. Highly recommend taking this course.

She truly cares about her students, is an amazing teacher, and makes her lectures relevant AND interesting! Please ignore the bad reviews; when her previous class structure wasn't working out, she completely reorganized everything to make her class easier for all students. I'd recommend taking her class :)
Great person and teacher. Cares about her students

She's hilarious and cares about her students and it's obvious she loves what she does. Grades are just in-class quizzes that are open note and mostly common sense. I fell asleep in some lectures but still got a 100 on them. This class was interesting and gave me a good buffer for my harder classes. Would definitely take her again!

Gen Pysch with Maxcey was awesome. When students expressed concern with the class format she changed it to make it an easy A for all students. Just show up to lectures, take notes and you will pass the in class quiz that is open note. She's hilarious. Highly recommend.

Please ignore all of the bad reviews for PSY 1200 in the last few months - they are because grades on papers were extremely harsh, but Professor Maxcey has switched around the entire class. It is fairly easy and you will receive an A if you take good notes during class. Professor Maxcey is hilarious and truly cares for her students.

Professor Maxcey is my favorite teacher by far! She is an amazing lecturer and her classes are really interesting and engaging not to mention she is absolutely hilarious! Don't listen to all of the negative reviews, they were because of the first paper grade and Dr. Maxcey addressed this issue and completely restructured the class. Very easy class

For anyone looking to take 1200 be wary of recent reviews. She intially had a bad paper-based class setup but has radically changed it to basing grades off of pretty easy end of class quizzes based on the lecture each day. She doesnt follow any set curriculum so prob bad for premeds who need the knowledge but easy enough to get a good grade now.

Maxcey is nice and does care about her content, but I wouldn't recommend her class. This semester had a big grading change, it's hard to say what grades will look like. However, it is clear that she will only teach what she wants: no format, no clear grading, no formal content. Difficult for pre-meds, and who's to say what grades will look like.

Most of these reviews are written by people who were angry over the first essay grade. Her essay structure of the class was very fair. However, after hearing the uproar from the people who got poor grades, she changed the whole structure of the class. She cares about her students. Don't listen to the negative reviews, she is engaging and fabulous!

After receiving grades from the first essay of the semester, students panicked: scores were low. However, Professor Maxcey made it apparent that she cares for her students and swiftly restructured the entire class in roughly 48 hours in order to ease her students' worries. She clearly loves what she does and, not to mention, she is hilarious.

Professor Maxcey is a great lecturer with a passion for the study of psychology. After encountering a bit of a challenge in regard to grading, Professor Maxcey was quick to listen to the input and concerns of her students, changing the course style and making sure that each student gets a fair opportunity at receiving a good grade in the class.

When we received our first grade for our papers. Papers that were insightful received Fs. As the TAs graded based on numbers of terms that none of us knew because we were not a coherent rubric. She then spoke to us condescendingly and did not listen to any of our concerns, even leaving her LAs confused, as they had no idea what they were doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Maxcey's intro course feels needlessly tough after changes in her syllabus this year. The material's simple, but grading is harsh because of her weird rubric, making a perfect score or an A nearly impossible for 5+ 8pg papers. She doesn't believe in having grades yet makes grading hard. Also, contacting LAs is forbidden too though they do nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Maxcey is a very hard grader even though the material is easy to understand/interesting to learn about. There are many long papers that my classmates and I spent 8+ hours on and asked her for help and then she failed many students- the class average was a C. Lots of people have withdrawn and I am almost failing so I may be forced to.

Terrible. There are six 8-10 page papers and she grades very hard. I am good at Psychology and spent hours on the paper and got a C. So many people are withdrawing from class since we already missed the drop/add period. She gave little to no feedback and will not reconsider grades. I do not reccomend taking any class she teaches.

DON'T TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!! The worst professor I have every had and I am a psychology major. Extremely hard grade on papers and not empathetic or available outside of class. I took very detailed notes, seeked extra help, and read assigned readings then she failed me with no feedback. If you need Gen Psych, transfer it in over summer

Dr. Maxcey claims to be empathetic towards her student and often goes on and on about having her own kids and hoping they will get treated kindly and with respect by their professors. However, she speaks to her own students with a very condescending tone and spends most of the class ranting about her controversial, borderline political, opinions.

she does not give clear explanation for what is expected. 5 long papers due and no rubric. She was rude to meet with and had no empathy towards students who didn't follow the rubric that she wouldn't give us. I got a F and put real effort into the paper.

The grading scale is very unclear and relies more on students' abilities to write down every detail said in lecture instead of a fluid and insightful understanding and engagement with the course material. Maxcey attempts to apply an objective grading scale to essays, which are inherently subjective (like comparing apples to oranges).
She's on a power trip and takes it out on students.
DON'T TAKE HER CLASS!!! She is very petty and speaks down to her students. Paper grades have a very unclear grading system with many flaws and discrepancies.

Class now is different to past reviews. Grades are 20% attendance/SONA and rest is five papers that are 8-10 pages each. Mandatory attendance to "check in" with LAs who do literally nothing. Class was mostly 1st sem. freshmen and she tries to scare them often. As a junior it was patronizing. She just rants the whole lecture, no actual psychology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class attendance was not mandatory, but it was helpful to attend class with the assignments done in class that would be due a few days later. She did 2 kinds of categorized classes, a lecture about statistics and then a more tech-savvy one for you to incorporate the statistics you learned in excel.
She's a horrible person. No empathy. I took her class a few years ago and a friend passed away. The exam was a few days after and she refused to let me receive an extension. DO not take her class.

Most of these good reviews are from the TA's. She has unfair grading policies towards specific students. There are also "grading policies" that are not listed in the syllabus. Loads of Mindtap homework that is unrelated to exam material. Unreasonable and unfair is what you get with Professor Maxcey, do not recommend.

Do not take this course, mind tap heavy, unrelated lectures, and short deadlines for everything. You will spend hours trying to complete the homework which is given every day of class. She doesn't care about her students. You would think that a professor in the Psych department would care more about student's mental health and well being.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class but I really admit it was a lot of work primarily because of Mindtap (do them early!). I liked the Data Viz assignments and found them helpful for the future. I was shocked that she had 6 exams but they were not too bad. Also, go to class if you can despite what anyone says.

Prof. Maxcey is probably passionate about teaching and a very good professor, but do not take this class. She changed the structure this year to be much worse. Easily my most hated class. Hours and hours of mind tap homework every week and incredibly nit picky grading on assignments/exams. Barely learned much.
She was single-handedly the worst professor I have had in my life. Unfair grading polices and doesn't care about your mental health. STAY AWAY FROM MAXCEY.

It was fine- I learned a lot, homework was pretty heavy but for a stats class I thought it was reasonable and she offered fair and plentiful grade opportunities. Adjusted deadlines and work as needed and it was nice that she generally rewarded going to lectures but it wasn't super necessary.
Horrible.
The class itself is really easy and I think everyone got an A. However, the teaching was lazy and unfulfilling. Definetely recommend self studying psych extra hard for the MCAT

This class is super easy. Weekly data viz activities which only took 20 minutes. Make sure you don't procrastinate the Mindtap activities because it's long and tedious but I was able to grind them out in 3 days. Very flexible and caring about student's mental health. I only had to attend lecture once a week. Take her if you need a stats credit.

If you want to fill your Stats requirement and get an easy A, then this is the class for you! I enjoyed the Data Visualization activities, as they're applicable to the real world. The online homework was very tedious, and it's easy to procrastinate since there's no set due date. But overall, Dr. Maxcey makes this course very flexible/accessible.

Prof. Maxcey values student mental health above all else and told us that she wouldn't even give us grades if she didn't have to. Gen psych with Maxcey was super relaxed and non-stressful while still being very interesting. Take classes with Maxcey when you can!

Very, very easy class and interesting lectures. Take her psychology class for your gen psych credit while you can. Grade was based on attendance/participation and textbook assignments, all of which could be completed at any point through the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PSY 1200 with Maxcey is a 100x better than taking this class with Sandberg. I am not sure how someone could not get an A in this class if they just showed up for attendance and worked through the online modules (which were basically completion). Not the best learning experience if you are trying to get ready for the MCAT, but Maxcey is a gem.

Take her class!! This class is amazing and not difficult at all. She forms it in such a fun way, I loved it! Most of the work was online through mindtap and you could do it at your pace, it is just due at the end of the year.

Professor Maxcey is a gem! She genuinely cares for her students and wanted the best for them. She was the only professor to reach out to me and check up on me when I had medical problems occur and I was not able to attend class. If you see her courses I would recommend taking her! Her lectures are more discussion vibes and like feedback! 1000/10!

It's probably very easy to chalk up Maxcey's teaching style this year as "lazy" and "underchallenging" but in reality I think she did a perfect job. There's a pandemic and for people like me, intro to psychology doesn't need to overtake my workload. I learned what I had to learn and at the end of the day, isn't that her job? a bit odd but sweet

I LOVED my general psychology course with Dr. Maxcey! She was super considerate and really accommodating about the fact that learning during the pandemic has been challenging. She shows that she genuinely wants us to care about the material and learn in an effective way. Fair amount of reading, but definitely one of the best courses at Vandy.

Took PSY1200 with her, and it was ridiculously easy. 70% of grade came from the online homework and the other 30% came from attendance that you could make up by watching movies. Very laid back and understanding of how hard the Vandy work load is.

PSY1200 with Maxcey was honestly somewhat of joke given how easy it was. She gave the option to complete 70% of your grade outside of class through MindTap and the rest was just showing up for like 2/3 of classes to enough attendance credits. So much better than Sandberg. Very caring lady too. Take her!

Review for PSY 2100!!
Maxcey is so so sweet and would reach out to the whole class to make sure that everyone was doing mentally okay. Only really had to go to class on Mondays then hand in the Wednesday and Friday assignments on time. Besides that, there's a ton of cengage hw due at the end of the course (just do a chapter/week).

Prof Maxcey is genuinely one of the most caring people I have ever met. She is also very entertaining and her lectures are easy to listen to. There is a decent amount of out-of-class work, but it is not super challenging. Highly recommend.
Nice, never have to prepare for lectures, you can do basically everything online and sometimes come to class and get an A. A low stress class

Her 1200 class is pretty easy. Do some online homework or some reading and come to class 60% of the time to get an A. She's very entertaining during class. only complaint is that a lot of students are taking pysch for the MCAT and without a structured course I feel like I didn't learn much for the MCAT

Professor Maxcey is the best Professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. She genuinely cares about her students. While there is consistent work every week, this work is meaningful and creates a desire for students to engage in it. Her grading system also shows that she understands students are human beings and can't be perfect all the time.
The least I've ever learned in any class. If you want an easy A, take this. But if you want to learn, take another class.

Dr. Maxcey is the best professor I have ever had at this school. She is literally an angel from heaven. Please take this class if you want to learn more about Positive Psychology and about life in general. This class changed me for the better both as a student and as a human.
Dr. Maxcey is the most kind and caring professor Ive ever had. She genuinely cares about her students and her classes reflect that.

Professor Maxcey cares deeply for her students. I would definitely recommend taking her Positive Psych course if you can. I looked forward to class every week and the material covered was engaging and useful. Definitely my favorite class I have taken at Vandy.

I took her Positive Psychology class and loved it! I can't say that I've genuinely been sad to be done with any of my other classes at Vanderbilt but that's certainly true of this one. The workload was light and incredibly interesting and the class discussions were my favorite I've had so far at Vanderbilt!

I took Dr. Maxcey's Positive Psychology class in the fall. It consisted of listening to one or two podcasts as homework, participating in class, and performing activities that made you happy outside of class. She is the most down-to-earth professor at Vanderbilt and this class felt like therapy. Highly recommend.

Dr. Maxcey made this class super flexible. Your grade is based on a learning contract. There are weekly CogLab activities and homeworks. No tests at all. Just come to class as much as you can. If you miss class you can still turn in assignments and won't lose points. Classes are not boring. And she is the best!!! Would recommend.

Lectures' mostly just her perspective on the field or her own stories. It may be enjoyable if you're following her. Otherwise, it's best to do the labs on your own, or else you may want to suffocate yourself in Wilson's toilet. Somedays I just go to class to hear what she has to say and then punch myself for doing that. Cengage hates procrastinator

I took her Positive Psychology course last summer. I really enjoyed the class at first; it was easy, fun, and personally rewarding. However, on the final paper, I randomly received an F. It was so unexpected and didn't make sense. I still received an A overall, but it was a strange ending to a class supposedly focused on fostering one's wellbeing.

Has very specific grading contract policy, she ended up failing multiple people who had "unsatisfactory" papers at end. Acts caring but is not willing to truly help and support students like other professors. Even if I got an A I would never recommend this class to those who want their self-esteem intact.

Our grades depended solely on group work. We were graded harshly and given unclear feedback. Although we were given the chance to revise for an A, I thoroughly hated the class. The entire experience crushed my self-esteem as a student. I recommend taking a course from any other professor.

Easily the worst professor I ever had at Vanderbilt. Super demanding coursework and very picky about paper format and contents, even though she is absolutely helpless in providing clear instructions of what she expect us to do. The course is about positive positive, but her presence and rude feedback add nothing to my happiness if not destroying it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In the two classes I have taken with Dr. Maxcey, she put up a front of being kind and caring but her actions prove her to be uncaring and lazy, e.g. students not being able to see what they got wrong on exams since she uses copyrighted questions, and blaming students when most of them failed an essay on which she gave very ambiguous instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Maxcey goes above and beyond to help students who reach out to her. The grading difference between her and the TAs was drastic and many times students felt in the dark about her intentions/goals with major assignments. However, as these issues became apparent, Dr. Maxcey did an excellent job of adapting to the needs of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Professor Maxcey was warm and friendly, her decision to convert all of the course's assignments to group papers really wasn't the perfect solution to mitigating the challenges of online learning.

Extremely harsh grader with rude feedback. Grades are based on group papers which are hard to get a good grade on as she and TA's grade extremely subjectively. Anthology exam is ridiculous and she is very condescending. Do not recommend.

This class had weekly meetings and several papers that were really tough to get a good grade. Our group determines how well you do in the class, which is randomized. The TAs are super tough graders and not accommodating. Would not take this class again, also was annoying of a class.

The most stressful class Ive ever taken. The content itself is not difficult, but 60% of our grades were based on group papers, where feedback is so harsh and not helpful. I felt like I lost my sanity taking this class. So much frustration to never be tested/assessed on knowledge of cognitive psychology. Would never ever take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Maxcey teaches you a lot about cog psych and her lectures are pretty engaging. The problem is that the grade for the class is 20% material and 80% ability to write scientific papers for children (kinda bs). This class was really frustrating at times but Maxcey seems like a caring person. I'd stay away if you're looking for a stress-free class

Covid plan kind of a mess, but she's super accessible and kind. Her TAs suck, and there is a lack of communication between her, the TAs, and the class which where lots of the problems arise. Too nitpicky about essay formatting. I think it would be a lot better a normal year, but right now this class gives me a lot of anxiety. TOO MANY ESSAYS!

You can tell that Professor Maxcey really cares about her students and this class as a whole. Compared to other 3000-level psychology courses, I think that the work load is very manageable for this class and Maxcey/the TAs are available for feedback and if you have any questions. Overall, I am enjoying the class as a whole.

Take her only for in person classes. Do not take her during Covid for online classes. I can tell that she's a really good person with work ethic and care for students, but she is strict, and her online class design is poor. I'd definitely take her during regular class time.

I had high hopes for this class but it's easily the worst class I've taken. Papers and online recorded meetings are graded under a vague but demanding rubric. She seems considerate but that falls very quickly given the harsh feedback and little room given for students to learn, improve, and demonstrate what they know of psychology, not writing.

Words cannot describe how much I regret taking this class. Maxcey is one of the worst teachers at Vanderbilt. Her grading and feedback is very inconsistent and harsh. She acts like she's kind and caring, but she's super rude, unhelpful, and unsupportive. So many students did horribly on papers 1 and 2, which speaks volumes to her teaching ability.

If you value having a good GPA, sanity, and happiness, do NOT take this class. Her instructions are ridiculously unclear and frustrating. There is no way to get a good grade on the papers because her rubrics don't make any sense. The feedback comments on papers were confusing, rude, and unhelpful. Please do not take this class with Maxcey. fml

Worst class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Maxcey was a horrible teacher: her expectations for assignments were inconsistent and unclear, and she grades harshly without valid explanations in the feedback. A majority of students received Cs-Fs on the first paper, which is a statement on her poor teaching and communication skills. DON'T take PSY 3120!

Taking this class is literally the worst decision I have ever made. The requirements for the papers are ridiculously vague and over 60% of your grade is group work with people you don't even get to choose! She acts nice and like she cares, but her feedback is always really nasty and she expects you to know things she doesn't even teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took this class because of all the good reviews, but her covid plan is just a mess. Most confusing, useless, and disorganized class I've taken this semester. We watch videos every week and then have to discuss them in small groups when we don't even have tests on them, what's the point?!. Super unclear grading and guidelines on last paper. Awful!

For an online class of over 120 students, her COVID plan is to have mandatory group meetings every week with close to zero help, and she asks those meetings to be recorded and sent to her. Really ineffective and stressful to all. Also the least flexible and understanding professor I have this semester towards internet issues/remote operating.

One of the nicest professors I've had. Her online positive psychology class was a literal gem! Not only do you learn a ton, you also get to apply the knowledge you gain to your everyday life. Her feedback is always sweet and personalized; you can tell she cares a LOT about her students. Her syllabus is also super clear - she checks all the boxes!

THE ABSOLUTE BEST PROFESSOR. She has handled the switch to online classes so well, and she truly truly cares about her students. You can tell she became a professor because she actually cares and wants to teach!! She is also such a good lecturer and she makes material even more interesting than it already is. Take as many classes as you can w her!!

Maxcey is amazing!! She loves psychology, but more than that she loves teaching! She's a fast talker but PowerPoints are easy to follow and she explains things really well. We never had outside work except reading a popular book for a book-based exam, and if you attended class you didn't need the textbook. She made it easy to learn a ton!

Dr. Maxcey is an amazing teacher. She is very clear with what she expects you to know for exams and she has been extremely accommodating during this time of COVID-19. Her lectures are not straight from her powerpoints, she does a good job of incorporating outside material and encourages class participation despite the large lecture style.

This class wouldn't be as amazing as it was without Professor Maxcey. She encouraged critical thinking and class participation during her lectures and didn't just come and talk over a Powerpoint. Her passion for both teaching and for the study of psychology has inspired me to take more courses in this field.

Took her for Gen Psych. Really amazing professor. She made the material interesting and clear. Tests were straight forward. highly recommend. We are finishing the course online, and she has done an amazing job continuing to provide creative opportunities to learn the material without adding stress to our lives. much respect.

Thanks to Dr. Maxcey, Cog Psych is probably one of the best classes I've taken at Vanderbilt yet. She is truly a hilarious yet super clear and helpful lecturer, and all you need is to take notes and pay attention to get an A. Beware that Journal Article Exams require a lot of work the week before and a purchase of a workbook. Super easy A and fun!

Knowledgeable and nice, but the weekly homework assignments take away from anything positive. Be prepared to spend hours upon hours on the behemoths of homework that she gives weekly. And it is graded incredibly harshly too - you aren't getting higher than an 80 unless every line of work is meticulously checked. Tests are easy at least!

Basically, Professor Bowden is so smart, but she is so out of touch with the class. She definitely doesn't understand half the things that are going on. There's never enough time for the tests which sucks because she doesn't offer any advice for that but also doesn't really test you then on what you know. The homework takes a long time to complete

This is the worst class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. I got an A, but she is the worst teacher I've ever had. Take this class with DB. I've taken it with Bowden, that doesn't mean you have to. If you choose to ignore me, your loss. You can to avoid her. She is the worst teacher and person I've ever met. Save yourself, I didn't. Trust. Me. Avoid.

Clear grading criteria, unclear literal grading (of assignment) criteria. Drops 4 lowest homework + 2 lowest quizzes, requires participation, not so accommodating, makes you work for an A. She's a newer teacher so I'll give her some slack, but be prepared to complete work fully and on-time always. Be wary of her class, but take if you need BME cred

shockingly unhelpful. frustratingly unclear at every possible opportunity, NEVER marks anything but expects improvement. he handed back the midterm and essays, all done 2+ months ago btw, after we'd finished the final. repeats your question back to you 5 times never gives a straight answer. class discussion felt redundant. just so disorganised

Very unclear expectations and hard to get an A. He provides no feedback, making it very difficult to improve enough to raise your grade. Smart professor and brilliant lectures, but no structure and stressful, confusing assignments. I didn't receive a single grade the whole semester I don't know what I will end up with, but I can only assume a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really good discussions. Pretty hard to get a grade and feedback, but could be because his role in the office. Wanted his students to succeed and was very accessible.
very kind and amazing professor. passionate in class topics as well as encouraging other students' success. offers a lot of feedback in order to improve your writing. a fantastic class overall

Pav is a great professor. He's very understanding and lenient with some deadlines. However, the class itself was not my cup of tea. The class is pretty much all discussion, and the material was really boring and abstract to me. It was one of my harder electives content-wise, but still very feasible to get an A if you stay on top of readings.

Absolutely wonderful Professor, incredibly supportive and you can see that he has a passion for literature. A lot of reading and papers to do or this class, however revisions are available for nearly everything. Super accessible outside of class as well and checks in with students to see how they are doing. He is incredibly caring and supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pav is a wonderful professor. He is really engaged in his subject and made Chaucer fun, and is also really kind and encouraging to students. I learned so much in this course. I love that he assigns theoretical and historical texts to supplement the core text. He clearly spends lots of time thinking about pedagogy and it really pays off.

Prof. Aulakh is one of the kindest professors I've had at Vanderbilt. I learned so much from his class, Race and Early Modernity, and he truly cares about the success and mental health of his students. He's a bit of a slow grader and a little tough when it comes to papers, but he really makes you into a better writer. Definitely take his class!!

look. he is a good prof, in that his classes are fun, and the material isn't bad but an unnecessarily harsh grader who i feel like has a high expectations for a class filled with stem majors. maybe only 2 people in class actually majored english and i think the prof should adjust his expectations proceed w caution
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Pav is so well-learned and analyzes Shakespeare in such brilliant ways, but that makes it hard to keep up with him. He is a pretty harsh grader because he wants you to keep digging deeper into the themes and hidden meanings of the stories, which can get frustrating. However, if you reach out to him, he will help you in writing your papers.
Fantastic professor take if you can

This class has lots of reading, but Pav is one of the most understanding professors. He made discussions interesting and gave solid feedback on assignments -- your writing will definitely improve. Office hours were helpful, he genuinely cares about his students, and he often checked in about our workloads in general and adjusts deadlines as needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Pav cares about the subject and wants to make sure that his students understand the text. He spends discussion really discussing the intricacies of text, which makes the passages that much more interesting. However, it can feel hard to do well in his class because you don't know what he is looking for in your paper, so I suggest office hours.

Professor Pav is definitely a good professor  he knows his content well and is caring to his students, but he expects a lot. Definitely talk to him if you need help with something because he's super helpful and caring. Would take his class again if I ever needed it for AXLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: AMAZING prof. I loved him! There is a good amount of reading and there are a few mini essays and two long essays, but he really gives great feedback on your papers and you get rewriting opportunities. He really wants you to become a better writer, but also wants you to get an A. If you have the opportunity, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Just an all-around great guy. Pav really cares about his students, and he fosters a sense of community in classroom discussions. The readings are consistent but manageable, and he's always aware of the workload he assigns. Based on previous ratings here, I'd also say he's gotten a lot better at grading things in a timely manner.

Professor Pav's Intro. to Poetry course challenges you to think critically and take perspectives outside of your typical purview, which makes this course seem a little more difficult than your typical "Introduction" course. HOWEVER, this class will truly teach you how to be a better writer, a skill needed in whatever industry you go into.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Pavneet is a great lecturer and fosters good discussion. He will help with papers but does expect a good amount for a freshmen seminar. Just do the readings, participate in class and ask for help on papers. He wants you to succeed, you just need to prepare to work a good amount on weekly responses and longer critical analysis essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Pav is one of my favorite English professors at Vanderbilt, and his Canterbury Tales class was a lot of fun! While there is a lot of reading, Pav gives clear guidelines as to what to focus on while you read. He is incredibly smart and dedicated, and clearly cares about his students. His paper feedback really helped me improve my writing skills.

Very nice and understanding. Pretty flexible with deadlines and seems to care about his students. Passionate about the content. I signed up mainly because I heard the class was easy, but I ended up really enjoying it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pav was great! He was funny, engaging, and invested in students' learning. The relaxed atmosphere really helped The Canterbury Tales come to life.

Pav is a great lecturer and he really cares for his students. He gives great feedback, but I feel like his grading is too harsh from necessary, considering this is only a introductory class. While you can definitely improve & learn a lot, find another course if you are just looking for easy AXLE credit.

Pav is a great guy and a pretty chill professor. Day to day, the class is pretty easy as long as you do the readings. However, the actual paperwriting (there are 2) is very difficult unless you're really into poetry and start planning weeks ahead of time. Take this all with a grain of salt, especially since this is coming from a STEM major.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has you read a lot of poems and his papers require you to put effort in, but he is a great professor. He loves students in his office hours and a lot of his assignments require you to meet with him. He is enthused and encourages class discussion. He normally has a set idea of what a poem means, so either find that one or defend a new idea well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Pav is a very sweet, and caring instructor. Clear expectations (updates 2x a week)and plenty of constructive comments. He was willing to guide you through the process of learning new things and teach you. (He hosted 3 office hours for just an essay+revision - not many do this) You might not end up with the best grade, but you learn a lot. Worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Pav is a really nice guy and has great intentions, but his grading is wildly difficult. Unless you're an english major that is truly a gifted writer, this class is not for the common man. His grading is exceptionally nit-picky, especially on top of the fact that there's so so so much reading in the class every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Funny, caring guy. Very kind and has great feedback on papers. Lots of reading but only a few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Pav is a great professor that will challenge you to think deeper about the readings he assigns. His poetry class was a good course and definitely recommended especially if you need a writing class. Very approachable and lenient.

What's great about Pav is his enthusiasm and deep understanding/appreciation for the subject provides an incredible learning environment. Though I am not much a poetry fan, I grew immensely as a writer from his course, and I have gained more respect for poetry thanks to him. Super approachable and friendly as well. Another great Vandy professor.

Pav is the best. His lectures bring totally disparate texts together brilliantly, and he was constantly blowing the classes mind. I've been told he grades on the tough side, but I haven't had any problems; as long as you put effort into your work, you'll be fine. The class grade was mostly made up of two five page papers and one longer final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Pav's Shakespeare class is great! I came into the class expecting it to be super boring, as I was not at all interested in Shakespeare, but the class really sparked my interest. There are just a few papers and presentations for grades, and he is kind of a tough grader, but he offers a few revision opportunities, and is very helpful outside of class

Very harsh essay grader - his feedback was often not clear and he definitely had his own view and interpretation of Shakespeare that he attempted to force on students. He was also an incredibly slow grader - I never received any grades or feedback for assignments I turned in during the second half of the semester.

Pav (he asks students to call him by his first name) is a great professor, if a little disorganized. I took his Shakespeare class and was impressed by his knowledge about the time period and his willingness to run with student comments. You'll definitely be reading and writing in his class, but it's worth it for interesting discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Mostly interesting lectures... tough essay grader
Great prof, really cares about students and he's pro at fostering discussion in class. Comprehensive feedback on essays, not easy but fair

She was available for any and all questions I had in a timely manner. She offered feedback on assignments. I enjoyed the class and the only complaint I have is that I wish I had some feedback on the quizzes so I know what I missed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Shes the worst professor I've ever had. don't even waste ur time taking an online class.  If u have a tech issue that even tech support can't fix but gives you a ref # so she can call them AND you screen shot the error screen, she will email u back 2 weeks later and tell you that its ur fault that u did not finish it& tell u that ur irresponsible
RODP class of Social Deviance. Very accessible, just do your work.  Answered questions quickly and was eagar to help.  Highly recommend.

i agree with everything everyone else said-she is a good lecturer, the topic is interesting.she likes it when you speak up in class,so feel free to participate.she's not a very warm person,but good at getting her point across and good at leading a class.i'd definitely recommend her, even at 8 in the morning.

A great lecturer, teaches straight from the book.  Non-cumulative final.  Many people had problems with the group project.  You must work in a group of four people which makes it hard.  Attendance does count.  Four misses and a grade is lowered.  Great lessons and messages for an Intro course!

She gives you all the answers for your tests in her lectures.Plus, she like to cancel class alot and you really don't need to read to pass her tests.There is one paper and it's with a group.Can't get much better!
Super nice and helpful. You write 3 essays and can rewrite them for better grades. No tests and pretty easy reading material.

One of the most devoted professors, and easily one of the most respected persons I encountered in life. Her expectation on writing is realistic and clear. Very approachable in and outside class. If you genuinely want to improve writing, Romero is your best bet.

Romero is awesome. She manages to balance actually teaching the material well and maintaining an ultra chill atmosphere. There are weekly tests, but it's more a blessing than a curse because they're all really easy, so their effect is that they dilute out any bad grades you might get on other things. Essays etc are allowed to be revised for credit.

Professor Romero's entry level German class was a breeze. She is very patient with everyone and wants you to understand the material, not just memorize it. She gives you plenty of opportunities to improve your grade (regrades, primarily), but there are a lot of quizzes and assignments.

Auer isn't necessarily a tough professor, but this isn't really that tough of a class. If you raise your hand 1-2 times a class, and attend 80% of the listed classes, you'll receive an A. As a professor, Auer is knowledgable and enthusiastic about his subject matter; if you have interest in the topic the class is a must-take.

This teacher used to be very easy, and when I heard this, I decided to choose him as a teacher.  Little did I know, the class was made much harder this year.
