It is not as easy to get an A in this class as it used to be because the school is cracking down.  If you are taking this class just to get an easy A, I would advise against it.  I got a b mi

Great class especially if youre looking for a non-language international credit. Easy A-/A with minimal work/effort. Probably requires 10-15 hours attention over the entire semester. Quizzes really aren?t that tricky and midterm/project is all but a joke. Still he?s very smart and makes it pretty interesting. Even at 8am its still worth it
Sea Power, a Navy class that he supervises, is the best! Highly recommend... very interesting.
Navy Power is a chill class!
definitely an intelligent man but needs to clarify his quizzes. other than that, great class and easy if you put minimal time into it.

Quizzes can be pretty difficult, given the ambiguity of some of Dr. Auer's questions, but overall, the midterm and the exam make up for the points lost on quizzes.  Dr. Auer might have his biases (strictly towards the right) and it shows in class.  Otherwise, a great course.  You'll learn a lot.  Just don't skip any quizzes.
A Great Class. I recommend it to anyone who can get into it.

Auer's class is set up in a very methodical fashion and it is very easy to keep up with the reading. He has daily quizes, but if you even skim the reading you'll be fine. The essays are a joke and so were the exams.

A pretty good professor; it's fun listening to his anecdotes.  Plus, it's pretty cool to get taught by such an important man.  I give him a 3 for clairity, though, because his quiz questions are sometimes ambiguously worded.

This isa fun and easy class and you learn a lot about international relations.  Daily Quizzes are annoying but way easy if you did the readings.   Plus, Dr. Auer is an interesting guy and a value to Vandy due to all his connections from his time in DC.
Great professor and inspirational professor.  He does have some goofy jokes but a great guy
Not hot at all and ****. He flirts with all the girls and makes stupid jokes. Other than that, he is a smart guy and a creative artist.
One of the most inspirational professors I have ever had. We need more of his kind in the art department. Makes me think in a way I never have before...
Hottest non-Gentile on campus.
No Comments
No Comments
Great man very smart and friendly chooses interesting subject matter.

This professor is one of the most fair and non-discriminatory individuals that I know. By no means is the previous statement true. He was set up by a TYC group on campus who manipulated his responses to questions asked at a forum about the military.
No Comments

This class was too easy for a college course, but it was his first time teaching sustainability at an introductory level so I don't blame him too much. Relied heavily on the online textbook. A more diverse set of class materials would have made the class much more engaging in my opinion.

Although most classes were lectures, Dr. Ayers was engaging and really connected the course material to the real world and to our lives. I truly learned so much in this class and would recommend it to anyone in the environmental sphere, not just STEM majors. Midterm, final, and homework were easy. One big project and a few presentations.

Professor Ayers wastes class time by talking about things not relevant to the course content. Many of his sources are also 10+ years old which is unacceptable, especially in a sustainability class. Do not take this professor or class. Easy but felt like a waste of time and money.
Prof. Ayers is an awesome teacher and intelligent man. He's super quirky and funny and seems to care about the students.

I took this class on sustainability for my freshman year seminar and I was excited about the subject. However, the class was not good (I went to about half the classes even thoug it wasn't lecture) and even though professor Ayers is a nice guy, he made us read his terrible book. Not knowledgeable about sustainability-- don't bother.

Really nice human being.  I loved his class.  He is writing his own book which is not half bad.  He really loves the subject matter that is addressed, and his enthusiasm is contagious.  I will bet my life this class converts anyone who takes it into a liberal.
Nice helpful professor, grades relatively leniently on tests.  Attendance is a must.
Class is simple, other than the fact that he curves down. I made a 90.5, which was a B+.
Knows what he is teaching. The class is an easy A. Listen to everything he says because they will likely be covered on the exam.

Ayers is a little nerdy, but hes a good guy. Tests are easy and predictable if you look at the old tests. go to class take notes, and study them and its certainly an easy A. I never went to class and still think its an easy A
Sogabe sensei is ridiculously funny and is a great teacher.  Love her!!
She. Is. Awesome.

Even though daily class is a challenge, Sogabe presents a great learning environment. She always tries to help & builds on your weak points. Also love talking about Japanese celebrities/dramas/etc. in class~

Sogabe-sensei was easily the best professor I had at Vandy. All the other comments are true. Her exams are tough and long. You will use every minute allowed to complete an exam. You gotta bring your A game every day. Yet, her classes are so fun that you're happy to do it. She's great in the class and out. I'd visit her office just to chat at times.

Sogabe-sensei does not mess around. You'll get a lot of points shaved off your grades on tests for forgetting to make vowels long and the like, but her tests are always fairly straightforward. She's always there to help, even at night via e-mail. Oh, and did I mention that she says really ridiculously funny things in class?

Sogabe-sensei is probably one of the best professors that i have had at vanderbilt. she has so much energy every day in class & her antics make japanese HILARIOUS. her grading is HARD enough incorrect character strokes & you can fail a test, but you can talk to her every day after class if you want to improve. she's always available & insanely nice
This class involved a lot of work and memorization, but then all language classes do.  Sogabe-sensei was very helpful and approachable in and outside of class.
She is willing to meet and help you with any questions you may have.  Lots of memorization, but by far the class I have learned the most in.

I loved Professor Azzoni! When a student would come in sick, she would insist they go home for their health even though the class had mandatory attendance. Overall, a very understanding professor and a great first professor to experience at Vandy.

If you want an easy class to boost your gpa and fulfill a requirement. I would definitely choose this one. The professor allows the students to make adjustments to the grading criteria based on their comfortability. It was an easy and fun course; however it was very long (about 2 hours).
If you like the subject, you'll love the class. I took the class to get my humanities out of the way, and I was so bored. However, it was incredibly easy with minimal work.
Very sweet and knowledgeable. Lectures were easy going and very discussion based on the readings.

Far more interesting class title than actual class experience. Class time is VERY lecture heavy and focuses too much on her specialty, the ANE. Didn't really learn a lot or enjoy the class but it's easy if you show up and occasionally chime in.

Prof. Azzoni is amazing! She is eccentric, but so, so sweet. She honestly wants to help each of her students find individual meaning out of her course. Classes are discussion based, but make sure you read the material beforehand. Talk to her outside of class, you will not be sorry! I wish she were staying at Vanderbilt, but she is moving!

Bless her heart. Prof. Azzoni is the cutest thing ever. She's very, very enthusiastic and very knowledgable about her subject. She's also VERY feminist, so if you're not into that kind of thing, prepare yourself. She's Italian and has an accent, but it's not distracting.

Honestly, she is a great professor, who really wants to get to know you!  Read the text for sure, participate, and go to office hours.  Her accent is a little difficult to understand at first, but it becomes easier as the class goes on.  She's definitely a feminist, and gets most excited about the Goddesses section of the course.
Professor is engaging and intelligent, but works best with smaller groups. She has an accent, but it's not hard to understand her.

Everyone had told me THIS was the professor to take. I was thoroughly disappointed with her lectures--very boring, she's difficult to understand, and rarely agrees with the pieces you read for class. She isn't very clear on what she expects from students, either. I tried to meet with her, and she was less than helpful every time.

She is nice and means well but it is almost impossible to understand her and the readings are unbearably boring. There are no tests which is nice but the papers are confusing topics but she is very flexible. Do not take this class unless you have a lot of interest in religious stories from the bible.

There is no text book for this course, but still be prepared for a lot of reading. No tests, grades are based on reflection papers and research papers, but she is a fair grader and flexible with due dates. This was the first time this class was offered, so she was adapting it as she went, but overall a good course and wonderful professor.

great prof. lectures are really interesting. she's an expert in her field and knows a great deal. easy going personality a plus, too. attendance mandatory, fair amount of reading and writing, but she's a very fair grader and will do anything to help you succeed. definitely take her!!!
Amazing class. Should be required for all students to take.

This class was life–changing in the sense of helping me view others in a completely different light. Now whenever I see someone do something I normally would not accept, I look at the situational factors. Also, whenever I have a disagreement, I use the strategies we learned it class so I don't experience the backfire effect.
He does not respect for his students
I spend over 40 hours for his final project, doing a 42 page presentation + 18 page appendix for the presentation and still got a B. Avoid if you can

His class was fine, but I didn't care for Balch as an individual. He made a lot of odd remarks throughout the class that my friends and I would side-eye each other for. We were also in a large lecture hall and he forced us to get out of our seats constantly. Exams and Projects were easy, just make sure you get a good TA.
Amazing all around! Really great attitude!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! (I was in 2210) He is a great teacher and passionate about Social Psych, but the class is graded off 4 projects with horrid criteria (ex, for a commercial, if he would share with a friend it's an A, if he would only give it a like, its a B). The average on projects is a B, and the TAs are very harsh for no reason
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Balch is the most wonderful and engaging lecturers at Vanderbilt! I have never been so excited to go to class. The workload was decent: a discussion post before every class based on the readings and 4 extremely enjoyable and open-ended projects (including final). If you're hesitant about taking his class, don't be! It's a pretty easy A too.
Super fun professor, super engaging content and useful coursework! take him!!

He is one of the most genuinely caring and kind professors I've met at Vandy. The coursework is average, and the classwork was never a big concern for me. The lectures were so fun, we are constantly doing activities and applying psychology topics outside of class! Take him if you can!

Great guy. Class is project and discussion heavy. Some open-endedness to assignment descriptions that could be improved. However, a very engaging and interesting speaker. Clearly cares about the subject matter and makes it fun to learn. Relatively relaxed in most areas (participation, attendance, grading) but makes you want to succeed.

Wonderful guy, really. He clearly is incredibly passionate about social psychology and is in it for no other reason than pure passion. EXTREMELY engaging class where you are setup to make close friends with your peers and the people around you. I recommend this class to all psych majors at vandy for a distribution course, its worth it.

I loved this class! Super interesting content, and Balch is very clearly also interested. Really fun in-class activities that make you think, and as other people have said, I think I've learned a lot about myself/daily life after taking this class! Projects were not too bad as long as you dedicated time to them. I would seriously recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was genuinely my favorite class I've taken at Vandy. My friend and I were in it together and we would always reflect on the things we learned, and we actually applied them to our real life. Such an engaging lecturer. He removed all tests, and the projects were time-consuming but overall not too bad. Would DEFINITELY recommend!
No midterm or final, fun (but time-comsuming) projects. Hard to slack or hide in class.

It's been a while since I was truly excited to go to class. The class was really fun and thought-provoking. I particularly enjoyed the aspects that made us reflect on our own behavior. Weirdly enough, I feel like a better person after taking this class because I can not only point out my imperfections but improve them.
Loved it! He goes above and beyond to make the class relevant and interesting.
I found this to be one of the most engaging and well-designed classes I've taken at Vanderbilt.
This has been a fantastic and enjoyable class! I apply what I've learned every day, and I do feel that this course has added to my lifelong toolbox.
Attending class was actually worthwhile (and he takes attendance). Learned a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: No more midterm or final. The projects are hard but enjoyable. Don't take this class if you want to totally slack off or not engage in class.
Easy to get a decent grade if you keep up with the reading. Such cool activities!
I now understand people so much better after taking this class. The content will have you look at life different and the prof is an incredible Lecturer.
The class is mostly projects, with the big one being a policy change project. Always helpful and got a bunch of folks who mostly want to go into consulting care about public policy.
The best class I've taken in college. Period. Cool projects and great lectures.

It's crazy seeing some of these reviews (mostly from one person?). I don't think those students learned the lesson about using blame to justify. 

You call tell the guy cares a ton about creating great classes. Great activities and super cool projects. There's no longer a midterm and it's a bunch of really fun projects. Take it!

Lots of assignments that seem easy but end up being graded very strictly. He cares about class but he grades towards ideas that he likes so make sure your ideas match his. Also you are forced to attend a council meeting out of class.

Some of these reviews are crazy. Yes, the midterm/final were tricky to work through because the format is very situation-based, but we had full practice exams where we could ask questions for most of the next class period. Got an A on both with minimal studying, just paying attention in class and taking the practice exams seriously. Great lectures!

This is truly one of the worst profs I have ever had at Vandy, the entire course has NOTHING to do with the midterm and final. both are essays that are graded on the personal beliefs of the TA's, and he provides the vague "rubric" only a few days before. He also INTENTIONALLY tells the TA's to grade harshly so the class avg can be low... AVOID!!

Your grade is completely dependent on the opinion of 1 of 2 graders, and one of the graders is not even present in the class. Expectations for the class are UNREAL: 5 journals, discussion due every class, readings for every class, midterm and final that ruin your grade, 2 quizzes, and participation/attendance required for each class. Good luck.
Super stupid exam format. Your grade depends entirely on the personal opinion of the grader. Rubric is useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I have taken at Vanderbilt! Professor Balch is amazing and cares about his students. The content is relatable and applicable to real life, and his lectures are engaging and amazing! Final and midterm make up the majority of your grade and if you study and do practice tests you'll be fine. Attendance and participation matter.

So subjective for tests, lectures aren't relevant for the tests. Doesn't even grade the exams himself. Wants his averages to be like Gen Chem and Bio which is bull for a PSYCH class. Joke of a class. Don't take.
Crazy subjective grading. Only midterm and final really make up your grade. Had to argue for 10% back on test which is ludicrous. The lectures are entirely irrelevant for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ridiculous grading system and vague rubrics, everything is based off his own beliefs and "going above and beyond" what is expected... also there's an unreal amount of readings and other assignments... will also hover over you when you are discussing with other classmates

AVOID AT ALL COSTS, Balch has unreal expectations for this class when it should be an easier class in the psych department.. he also let everyone know at the beginning of class that the class average was an 80... lower than bio and chem??? take abnormal instead

Nice guy who genuinely cares but INSANE expectations for a psych class. Unclear rubric. Easy to get a B, difficult and unclear how to score higher. Nothing is graded by him, all by the TA. Rubrics provided are useless and you are graded entirely subjectively. Definitely would not recommend.
He is passionate about the subject. However, the expectations for the class are ridiculous. The tests aren't even graded by him, and it is instead graded by a grader. Take your 3 credits elsewhere.

Professor Balch is truly an exciting lecturer and cares about his students. The class itself requires a lot of discussion both in person and online. The midterms are pretty difficult and require outside of the box thinking. Overall, this is a very interesting class with a very good professor, but you are gonna have to work for the A a bit.

Dr. Balch is very friendly and cares a lot about Social Psych. Overall, this was not my favorite class, but it definitely is engaging. I found the midterm and final to have very ambiguous grading, which is tough because they are 50% of your grade.

This class is great.  You learn a ton about psych and life. It's fairly discussion-based and interactive. Tests are more than fair. The readings were fairly interesting. There's not much HW. The lecture portion of the class is engaging.  Balch puts a lot of effort and passion into the class, and it shows. This is one of the best classes I've taken.
Explains concepts clearly, grading is fair, and assignments aren't outrageously difficult. Definitely take for HOD 2700

HOD 2700 with Dr. Balch is an incredible opportunity for a bunch of business majors to start thinking about important problems that exist in the real world. Dr. Balch is incredibly knowledgeable about the public policy process and works hard to present it in a way that is interesting to relatively uninformed college kids. A great guy all around!

Balch is such a great prof. Easily my favorite class to attend and do work for. He makes public policy super interesting for a bunch of HOD majors who have never touched the subject. People added public policy double majors just because of how great the class was. Take Balch if you can, everything taught is relevant, he is a fair/easy grader

Cannot recommend Professor Balch enough! Social psych was engaging and I came away with knowledge that is highly applicable to real life. Classes include a lot of group discussion, but you warm up very quickly. Take Dr. Balch for a class you'll look forward to every week.

I loved every single bit of this class. Professor Balch's teaching style is amazing. I have never learned so much from a class at Vanderbilt. His lectures are engaging, fun, and applicable to real life. The midterm was a little challenging - it mad me think outside of the box. However, I do think the course is very manageable and fun!
One of my favorite courses taken for HOD- super interesting, work was kinda fun to do, and a pretty easy A. Would definitely recommend

HOD 2700 with Balch was a really interesting and engaging class- one of my favorites taken at Vanderbilt so far. Wasn't a super difficult class (a few papers, video project, and long term semester project) I ended up with an A overall and didn't put an insane amount of work in

Best psych class I've taken at Vanderbilt yet. He doesn't grade too tough, and there aren't a lot of assignments to work on. The reading and lectures are interesting and applicable outside of class. Lots of small group discussions, and you can tell he is generally interested in all of us as students and people.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is easily one of the best classes I've taken at Vanderbilt, but it's not one of the easiest. So worthwhile, I never felt the walk to Commons was a waste of time. If you're going to take this class, absolutely take it with Balch. Heavy emphasis on written assignments, great course topics, lecture-discussion hybrid class (really effective style)
Incredible Prof, amazing human, gives good advice
His teachings about religious groups like mine made me extremely uncomfortable, and it is not a safe space to be able to express a contrary view without retribution.

I took SOC 2321, not SOC 3312. Professor Bandy is a fantastic professor. This is one of the few classes at Vandy where I felt like I truly learned new and important information that help me to understand the world. The workload is very manageable.

Absolutely loved Bandy. Truly believe he's one of the best CORE teachers. Super engaged, cares about his students, and very in tune to busy parts of the semester. One of the other reviews on Bandy is wildly inaccurate, the class is easy if you submit your assignments and participate 1-2 times a class. Papers are graded fairly and can be revised.

Professor Bandy was awesome -- easily the most relaxed CORE teacher that I have heard of. He was always super caring and available for Office Hours and worked super well at allowing all people to contribute in class discussion while avoiding awkward silence and not just teaching to fill class time.

Easily the worst professor you could take for core. What should have been my easiest class was anything but due to Bandy's grading and demeanor. Papers are graded harshly with rude feedback, and participation is not measured equally for each student

a really nice guy. the class has a lot of reading, but discussions were always interesting. students are graded on two long papers, weekly discussion posts, and participation. while the class is demanding, Prof Bandy is understanding and flexible, and not a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: (This is for SOC 2604 his Social Movements class) I absolutely loved Prof Bandy and this was genuinely a class that I found myself learning so much from. Really thorough lectures even if a wee bit long. Readings are pretty heavy each week but he lightens the course load when he assigns papers. Also a much more lenient grader than you'd expect!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A super nice professor! He genuinely cares about his students and provides help. There is a lot of reading each week and a personal project at the end of the semester. You would get an A if you put in the work.

Bandy was so sweet and very smart. Lots of readings each week, but really interesting topics. Weekly blogposts + final project + attendance for the grade. Not much participation from students, and I really felt the class could've been so amazing with more :(

Dr. Bandy is a very smart very kind guy. He assigns a huge amount of reading but as long as you skim and get the basic ideas you'll be great. Bandy cares a lot about student engagement in the topics he teaches about because he cares about what he's teaching. I liked him a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite class this year. Bandy is such a gem - super intelligent and a great lecturer, also caring and funny. There is a lot of reading, some of it a bit dense and a lot of it unfamiliar, but it really enhanced my understanding of environmental justice issues, along with the invigorating class discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: SOC 3314 is probably my favorite class that I've taken at Vanderbilt. Prof. Bandy is an incredible professor who  encourages participation and opens your eyes to a lot of nuanced and important issues surrounding environmental justice. Quite a bit of reading, and you can't get away with not doing it - but all the readings are worth diving into imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Joe is absolutely amazing. He's the head of the Center for Teaching so he knows how to be a good professor. His class is discussion based and these can often get off topic, but are still informative. He really cares about his students. There is QUITE a bit of reading. Grades include weekly discussion posts, a 7 page and 15 page paper. Worth it!

Profe is a truly caring professor, but expectations on major assignments are often confusing or ambiguous. He makes himself available outside of class and is willing to help with grammar and essays but I only felt supported occasionally despite the large amount of work I put in outside of class. Lectures were always exciting and Profe was engaging.
Aznar is a character. Very funny and friendly in class, and he fostered a good participatory environment. He speaks a little too quickly for a beginner level class.

Great teacher and very energetic. Grades off of mini-quizzes and some take home and in-person essays. Fun and inclusive lectures and if you pay attention and do the light homework you will get a good grade.

This man is an absolute gem. He's hilarious and engaging and wants all of his students to succeed. Don't let him scare you on the first day of class: lectures are mostly in English and assignments are mostly online and not graded harshly at all. My Spanish definitely improved too!
Amazing professor with clear grading, make sure you stay on top of homework and actually study for the weekly quizzes.

Profe is amazing! He is super caring, wants his students to understand the content and succeed, and is pretty funny too. Class participation is huge in this class, as well as the small assignments assigned, but a low workload. There are small quizzes that you will need to prepare for. Overall, a great and simple introductory class for Spanish!

Professor Aznar's class is absolutely incredible. He ensures that everyone understands the difficult material. His lectures are based off of textbook content. He is also available outside of class a lot. He is a harsh grader in terms of participation and will embarrass you if you're late. Lastly, be ready to be cold-called.

Professor Aznar is the funniest guy out there. He really cares so much about his students and makes class so fun. This class is fairly easy if you put in the work and study, and profe makes it easy to access him for any questions. A lot of short quizzes, but not bad and only a few major assignments. One of the best classes I chose this semester.

Prof. Aznar is an amazing teacher, and he is able to convey class material in the most engaging and funny way. Classes involve a lot of participation, and he tries to include everyone in discussions. I learned so much Spanish with him and would definitely take his class again.
He makes grammar actually fun, overall class isn't that hard just be prepared to study minimally.

Profe is HILARIOUS!!! He makes class engaging by cold-calling. He is enthusiastic in his teaching and wants students to succeed. The quizzes are really easy. Sometimes he will make people say embarrassing things in spanish to keep class entertaining so always be ready. He is always excited to give extra help to those who need it.

Always looking to help students do their best, asks for feedback from his students to improve his class and students' understanding, and makes class very exciting. Very funny and caring guy, 100% recommend

Aznar is awesome. He's super nice and funny. You can tell he cares about his students. He's not the most organized guy, and he never answers his email, but other than that, he's a gem in the Spanish department.

Super nice and funny. Took fall 2023 and we had no tests or quizzes, so you needed to do well on the timed writings. Must practice writing and speaking at least every week to do well. Very eager to help w. office hours/ zoom meetings/ whatever you need. Overall solid choice prof & practice or your grade will make you regret your choices

Lectures in basic spanish but fast because he is a native speaker. My listening improved a lot. Quizzes are mid. HW before each class but it is easy. He is very funny and tries to keep the lectures entertaining. He does call on students randomly to answer questions so if that is not something you would enjoy I would not recommend him.

Profe Aznar is a must take if you plan on taking a Spanish course. He's so incredibly caring for each of his students, treating students more like extended members of his family. The class has daily homework, but it's all very easy. Just be careful because he does not take any late credit. He has given zeros for work turned in 45 minutes late.

As someone who really struggles with Spanish, Profe Aznar was the perfect professor. After the first day of class, he emailed me about meeting outside of class for any necessary support. The combination of his accessibility and jokes throughout class made the learning experience comfortable. Profe is very fair with his grading.

I really did not enjoy 1103 with Aznar. He values participation heavily, but more often than not I felt like his cold calls were him testing me rather than trying to teach me. His grading was pretty unpredictable and he was hard to reach out of class. People love him though, so I may have had a rare bad experience.

Profe is amazing. Will kind of force you to speak only in Spanish in the classroom, but it becomes so much easier, and your speaking will improve a lot with him. He is also very caring and offers anything he can to make it easier for students to suceed.

Profe is really kind and caring. Participation is really important for this class, so he does cold call a lot which can be stressful, but overall he just wants you to try your best. Homework assignments are pretty easy. He can be a harsh grader when it comes to quizzes and tests.

Aznar is a very nice man who genuinely cares about teaching his students. He's very animated which makes for interesting lectures which can sometimes come off as unplanned or unstructured. I learned quite a bit but the course could def use some revisions. Also, he's a very fair grader and the workload is very light for the most part.

The GOAT, he is super funny and actually cares about students. You will learn a lot from him in an easy class and the class is actually fun. I took his Maymester in Alicante and it's been my favorite class at Vanderbilt. One of my favorite profs, TAKE HIS CLASS!

Lectures in basic spanish but fast because he is a native speaker. HW before each class but it is easy. He is very funny and tries to keep the lectures entertaining. He does call on students randomly to answer questions so if that is not something you would enjoy I would not recommend him.

Profe cares about his students so much. He emphasizes what he wants his students to learn before they leave his class and will spend time reviewing subjects the class struggles with. You do have to participate every once in a while. He is accessible and makes Spanish a joy to learn. I highly recommend him!

Profe is great! He truly wants you to succeed and be confident in your abilities. He is extremely funny and tries his best to make class fun. Participation definitely helps your grade so be sure to speak every now and then! HW (MindTap) is manageable and projects/writing assignments are not difficult. I 100% recommend him.

Profe was hilarious and engaging during class. there is a participation grade at the end of the semester so make sure to speak up during class. There is mindtapping homework before every class but its easy. Definitely take Profe Aznar he is great!

This is such a good class to take with Prof. Aznar. You will actually jump up a level in Spanish by the end. He is so passionate and engaging while teaching. He is pretty funny. He's actually from Spain, too, which is a plus for me. Obviously, you will have to write a lot. Overall, I highly recommend this class for intermediates.

El profe's class was great. I knew a lot coming in as I had taken AP, which definitely helped out a lot, yet I still learned so much about the intricacies of the Spanish language's grammar and syntax. The tests were pretty tough, but el profe truly supported us and if you put in the work, you will succeed. Also, incredibly funny. HW is manageable.

This professor was alright. He cares for his students. I never felt that personally but he states he wants everyone in his class to learn and become a better Spanish learners. I truly have mixed feelings about this professor's hate and like at the same time (mostly hate tbh).

He really cares that his students learn spanish. Super energetic (borderline chaotic at times). Gets annoyed when students are off task/on their laptops during class, so be careful about that. He will get confrontational/up in your face if you're not 100% paying attention. As long as you show up, participate, and do the work, it should be an easy A
I definitely was not good enough at Spanish to be in this class, but it ended up being fine. The essays aren't bad at all, but the exams are really hard. El Profe is that guy tho.
EL PROFE!!!!!!!!! LO MEJOR

El Profe has been my favorite professor at Vanderbilt so far. He comes into class with a smile and has great energy. He genuinily wants his students to learn the materal and makes sure you know you can speak with him out of class whenever. He is really funny, and if you have the choice to take Aznar I would highly recommend it
Profe is great. A lot of work and can be difficult at times, but you will get out what you put in. He cares a lot about the students and has a lot of enthusiasm. Highly recommend

Profe Aznar is an energetic guy who cares about his students and their progress in Spanish. There is a lot of homework, papers, and tests, but he lets you make corrections to the papers to improve your grade. The hardest part is the grammar, but his lectures are really engaging which makes going to class fun. Attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: El Profe is the best

El Profe is the best!!!! He is so enthusiastic and is a great teacher who really cares about his students. He wants everyone to learn and is very passionate about what he does. He is always available to help his students. He is one of the best Spanish professors that I have ever had and strongly recommend taking his class

Profe Aznar is truly the best. He is very caring and wants students to learn Spanish, not just pass the tests. The weekly homework is pretty time-consuming but the tests are easy. If you show up and make an effort you'll get an A.

Spanish is not a subject I enjoy, but Profe made it a lot less painful. He's very energetic, caring, and funny. Your grade is spread across a lot of categories, so it's not hard to get a good grade. Beware, though- the Mindtap assignments are tedious, and he loves to cold call on people. Overall, he does care a lot about his students.

El Profe somehow managed to make an online class talkative and fun, which after over a year of this mess is even more impressive. He's a genuinely friendly guy who gives you lots of opportunities to practice, study, and succeed in his course. Even though the class is laid-back, the format improves your speaking skills drastically. Great choice.

I took Prof Aznar's class online, which made it difficult for students to understand what was expected sometimes. The workload is not too bad for a five credit class. He grades fairly, but usually gives A- on assignments. You will need to put in extra effort to get an A, but he does make it possible.
Please ignore the previous review. She is salty about receiving an A- for not completing half her assignments!

I just finished this class and I think Aznar is a pretty standard Spanish professor. He makes an effort to teach and really wants you to understand Spanish and be good at it. The one thing I take issue with is his grading. It's completely subjective, and he refuses to give full points on an assignment even if you did everything he specified.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think I entered the class just to fulfill AXLE and left with a lot more Spanish than I expected. He's fair, energetic, and really wants you to learn. Just try your best to work on your speaking skills from day 1 because it'll help you in the long-term. Do you work on time and with effort and you shouldn't get anything other than a thick A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Aznar's class is decent. It's a pretty standard language class. If you pay attention in class and take time to make sure you understand the concepts, you'll be fine. That being said, he's also slightly crazy... he's VERY energetic, makes lots of jokes, and actively works to set the students up with each other. It's pretty entertaining.

Profe is really engaging and cares about his students! The online work was sometimes frustrating as it did not correspond to the unit we were working on. Grading was also very slow. Overall this was a enjoyable class!

I had Profe Aznar for 3301W, and I really disliked him and the class. However, taking 3302 with him made me really like him and has encouraged me to continue learning Spanish. He is disorganized and late to class a lot, so I recommend making a group chat with the entire class so everyone is on the same page about HW and stuff. He is awesome, though

El Profe is one of the most caring professors on campus; his encouraging us to only speak in Spanish and his constant feedback have really helped my speaking improve, and he's the reason I'm continuing with a Spanish minor. He is so passionate and his class is the best Spanish one I've been in. Highly recommend, he's an inspiration to learn from!

Love Jose so much! He is so understanding and truly cares about his students. If you dont understand something, he will take as much time needed to fully explain the concept. He'll like you if you only speak in spanish!

Aznar is a nice man overall. However, he falsely accused several students of plagiarism because they were the "best papers" he had ever read. Once realizing he was in the wrong, he gave those students Bs even though they were the "best papers". Extremely frustrating situation.

Professor Aznar was one of my favorite teachers at Vanderbilt! If you show up, participate, do the homework, and don't speak in English, it is pretty easy to get an A.  He really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well.  I mainly just used the book to do the online homework.

Profe Aznar is the most enthusiastic professor I've ever had.  He made a basic spanish class engaging and fun.  He is a bit overwhelming with his enthusiasm, but he really cares about his students and wants them to improve.  He's slow to give tests, or grades back, so go to office hours or ask him in class for them back.

Professor Aznar was a great teacher. Definitely my favorite in my first semester at Vanderbilt. Material for the class was relatively easy, but he always pushed us to work harder & learn more because he cared more about our learning than our grade. He always brought excitement into the class, and the class went by much faster than others. Take him!

I've never seen anybody get more excited about commas, but he makes grammar pretty interesting. The daily homework isn't usually collected, but he notices if you don't do it and it'll impact your grade. Get on his good side early on and you'll do fine if you just do the work.

Aznar's a great guy- he really does want you to do well. You have to really show him that you do care, though. The class is a little bit unorganized and sometimes assignments were unclear, but he'll always help if you need anything. Super animated lecturer which helps to make the dry grammar stuff less of a drag.

Aznar is such a great guy. He often adjusts the course curriculum to fit the needs of his students and really seems to care about all of them. Attendance and participation is important, but if your essays are good he won't give you a hard time about anything really.

Aznar is hilarious, especially in a small-class setting. But sometimes he gets really moody and starts randomly yelling at kids which is pretty awkward. But if you write good papers and spend a decent amount of time studying for the TWO TESTS, you'll do fine. Definitely pick him over the other professors for this course, but expect some moodiness.

Profesor Aznar really cares about helping his students learn and helping students that are struggling. He offers "Cafe con Prof." twice a week where you can grab coffee with him and discuss anything you are struggling with. He is hysterical and makes learning about grammar entertaining. I learned more in this class than in 3 years of high school.

Tempermental professor. Will give you bad subjective grades if he feels like you don't participate enough. Also, expects you to put his class before all other classes. Is not flexible if you have to come late from another class.
He's great. Makes your spanish a lot better.

Yes, he is very passionate about the classes, but also VERY manipulative. I would highly recommend NOT taking the class, but if you do:  1. Set the bar (for ability, not input) LOW! He decides how much you progressed--not how you did the asmt 2. Asmts aren't graded systematically but are based on your 1st grade and how many weeks have passed.

This man was by FAR the best Spanish professor I've had at Vanderbilt (and I've completed a major, so I've had a few). I had Aznar for a Maymester in Spain, and this was the best decision I made at Vandy. This class made my mind up on pursuing the major. He was extremely helpful. His passion for the class was amazing to see. TAKE HIM!!

Professor Aznar is by far my favorite teacher so far. He truly cares about his students and will help them in any way possible (even meeting after hours to assist) The class is an easy a if you do the homework and participate in class. His passion for teaching is inspiring and makes you want to learn the language more. Amazing professor!!

I've never seen a teacher care more about his students. I took this class with him as a Maymester in Spain, and it was incredible. If you have a chance to do this, do it! Admittedly, he is a tough grader and he really pushes his students, but it's because he wants you to actually learn Spanish and not just check the class of your list. Take him!
He really cares about his students. He makes the tests crazy easy but he really expects more of people in class. Great teacher. Always enthusiastic. Class passes by in the blink of an eye.

Aznar is one of the funniest profs I've ever had. He is clearly not that used to teaching lower-level Spanish, but he's been very good at making himself understandable. He definitely cares more about whether students are learning than what their grades are, so the tests but be an easy A, but he'll challenge you to go further.

Professor Aznar is a great, helpful teacher who's not afraid to challenge his students to improve. He's not big on written evaluations; almost the entire grade in 207 comes from your in-class presentations and oral exams. Part of your grade comes from recording Spanish conversations with friends in your free time, so get ready to do a lot of those!

Aznar is a really nice guy. We just talk in Spanish the whole class. The homework assignments are kinda time consuming (especially the movies). He doesn't grade the major assignments very hard and it is very unclear what your grade is most of the semester, but it turns out fine!

He is without a doubt one of my favorite teachers ever. He is always trying to help his students succeed in any way possible. However, he's a harsh grader and he's nit-picky. He's so sweet and energetic! He truly cares about his students. You should take this class if you want to improve your Spanish rather than just wanting to improve your GPA.

I have take a lot of Spanish classes, and he is by far the best teacher I have ever had. The amount he actually cares about his students is unbelievable, and his theatrical personality keeps class interesting. He is by no means easy, but it is supposed to be a hard class. Take him!

Prof. Aznar is one of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. He legitimately cares that all of his students learn Spanish and why it's important. His tests and quizzes are fairly easy, but the oral grades require a bit of advanced preparation. Spanish 103 is definitely the best way to fulfill the AXLE language requirement! A must take class!

Professor Aznar is definitely one of the best professors that I've had so far. He sincerely cares about his students and wants them to do well. He also makes class really interesting, especially when he starts talking about Spain (he was raised there). For sure a must-have professor!!

A theatrical, lively professor, who is very passionate about the subject matter of the class. This carries over to his concern for the students, and he is greatly helpful if you ever need a paper proofread. Definitely go to office hours and have your compositions read, as he will point out the strengths and weaknesses. Excellent professor.

Aznar is extremely invested in his students and really works to make sure his class is a "family". You can tell that he is very interested in the subject and wants his students to learn. He is a hard grader but as long as you put the effort in an A- is very possible. In the class you watch spanish movies and learn about different spanish countries.

Prof Aznar is one of the best I have had at Vandy. He is incredibly kind, invested in his class, and constantly attempts to make his students feel comfortable. Go to class and participate and an A is definitely realistic. He's awesome!!!

There are several considerations in taking this class with Aznar. He truly cares about his students and wants his classes to feel like "family". He wants his students to learn and improve. That being said, he is one of the most rigorous and difficult graders. Not the teacher to take if you want a grade to boost your GPA.

I cannot think of a professor who cares more about his students and who loves teaching more than Sr Aznar. The class, however, is NOT easy at all. He doesn't really believe in giving As in the beginning as he wants to see improvement throughout the semester. Though my gpa suffered because of the class, I know his class will help me in the long run.
Amazing professor. Always energetic in class and it would be impossible for him to be any more helpful.

I have never had a teacher who genuinely wants his students to learn and do well more than Professor Aznar. He's always looking for suggestions from his students for how to improve his class, and he wants to help you outside class too. Not an easy A by any means, but you learn a lot. Definitely take anything you can with Professor Aznar.

This was my first Spanish class, so I cannot compare him to the other professors, but I cannot imagine anyone else being more enthusiastic and well-meaning. He radiates a pride for his heritage and, accordingly, wants his students to excel in Spanish.

The BEST!  Prof. Aznar is probably the nicest professor I've had at Vandy -- had him for both 201W and 202, and was excellent both times.  Neither were "easy A" classes, but he wants you to do well.  Very interesting and engaging in class and available outside of it.  Would recommend to anyone!

My favorite professor thusfar. First day of class he says (in Spanish), "If my students do poorly, I feel like I'm failing." The most important thing to Aznar is that you make progress. You don't have to be perfect, you have to try. He's willing to set up times for the class to meet at Starbucks and practice before recordings. Makes class fun.

Fabulous teacher, incredibly enthusiastic and helpful.  He truly cares about the success of his class and is very approachable.  His lectures are easily understood and interesting.  He fully teaches the material, and adds a little fun in as well.  A must-have for Spanish 102.

So enthusiastic!! keeps the class interesting but he is very demanding. This class has a lot of written work and recordings and is NOT an easy A whatsoever. My spanish has improved leaps and bounds in only one semester!

I went to Spain with Sr. Aznar back in 2005 and I had the most amazing experience of my life.  He is absolutely wonderful! He is such a passionate person and a fantastic teacher.  He is very eager to get his students involved in Spanish and love it as much as he does. I would 100% recommend him to anyone and everyone.

Professor Aznar is fantastic! He wants us all to be comfortable in the classroom, which is really important for a speaking class. He genuinely cares for his students. We even have weekly "coffee dates" to practice conversational spanish! He's the best 202 teacher, hands down.
The worksheets he hands out with the lectures are very helpful for understanding the material. There are weekly quizzes, so stay on top of the material.

Bat-Od is a lovely guy and such a kind person. He's a really good lecturer, and puts a lot of thought into giving good lectures. He doesn't just copy down textbook proofs, he is prepared to sit and think through the proofs as he lectures, which results in some silence but always a good, intuitive explanation of all the proofs. Great course too.

though a wonderful and friendly person, dr. battseren is definitely not the best lecturer that i had a vandy. there are times i am left more confused and i honestly learn better on my own. he follows guidelines given by dr. hollingsworth (who made the course super confusing and unstructured), which leaves his lectures confusing as well.
Very welcoming to all students and extremely accessible outside of class.  Very knowledgeable about the content and can break tough concepts down into every single small individual detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were ok, but goes way over time almost every class because of some unrelated story. Class involves so much busy work, and honestly if you have zero knowledge of Korean coming into the class, its pretty hard to prep for the exams. Wouldn't recommend unless you know some Korean already and have a light courseload.

Caring and dedicated professor. A bit awkward but funny in a very dad-joke way. Puts in effort to get to know his students. Will call randomly on you, but it's not that big of a deal even if you don't know an answer. Lots of turn and talk to your partner activities.
Great teacher, super passionate. Be aware that attendance is huuuuuge in this class, received an A- due to my own fault of missing too many classes. Also soooo much busy homework in this class.
Very interesting Korean class.

Jang is a funny professor who cares about his students. However, the class setup is harder this year. It's weird, but Korean was easier when it was 5 credits, not 4. The daily class setup had just 1 quiz + 1 homework due weekly. Now, as a 4-credit class, we have 2 quizzes + 1 homework due weekly. Nothing to do with Jang, but I hope that changes.

A very nice and caring teacher but can be intimidating sometimes. It is a fast pace class since there is a lot to cover in a 50-mins class. It's a small class so it's easy to find friends and form study groups.

His lecture is well organized and explanations are clear but it's too boring. He always goes over time while wasting time on unnecessary stories. He is very impatient with students making mistakes which makes me scared too speak in Korean. I learned a lot from his class still but wouldn't take his class again

Prof Jang is really humorous and caring. He is super organized with notes, class schedules, and vocab lists. He explains complex grammar clearly. He is always supportive and gives valuable feedback. Really enjoyed the vibe of his class, you always learn something but in a chill mode. Highly recommend his class!

You would have to be trying so hard to fail this class. He tells us what he expects from us on the tests and posts study guides which are the test the week before. Very lenient with grading. He is also very funny and is always willing to help.
Awesome class. Really made me appreciate Korean language and culture. Jang is super passionate and wants his students to do well. What a great learning atmosphere!

Freshman-Tbh Jang easy to like. He is ecstatic about learning the language and presents the information really interestingly. However, after completely bombing my midterm IK the problem was the initial structure. The course starts off as being flipped classroom like. (we're expected to memorize A LOT of vocab w not much guidance/structure)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Korean for two semesters last year and taking intermediate Korean this year. He is so funny and caring. There is so much work in this class, but if you do your homework on time, you'll be fine.

Professor Jang is very nice and very passionate about the Korean language and Korean culture. Is not the best at time management during class-- will sometimes go on tangents about something small and rushes through grammar/harder material or goes over time. By participating in lectures and drill sections you get a decent understanding of Korean.

If you are Korean American he can kinda be a little smug towards you. Does chastize you a bit if you don't know Korean as well. A little unfair if you are Korean-American versus a person from a different ethnicity as there are a slight grading standard. Ex: White guy pronounces terribly still has the same grade or better as a Korean American.

My views have changed since 1101. The class is not as bad as I thought it was, but I still feel like there are other language options. His tests often contain typos and it is hard to understand what the test is asking and for some, they were missing instructions completely. It is an alright class, but lectures can get boring.

Highly recommend Professor Jang. It is clear he cares about his students and he truly wants you to do well. He works really hard for his classes and his teaching style is great. Super educated and well-liked by all his students. There aren't enough good things I can say. If you are thinking about taking Korean, definitely do with Professor Jang.

He's a nice guy, but he isn't very accommodating especially during COVID. And he doesn't explain his lessons in enough detail. He always takes too long on the easy part and then zooms through the hard parts because we run out of time every class period and we go over time.

Professor Jang is the most sweet professor I have encountered at Vanderbilt. He cares so much about his students and it really shows. He has a clear schedule for the semester and straightforward grading criteria. He grades generously on oral exams too, which is really helpful for those of us who are non-native speakers. Definitely take this class!

Dr. Jang's Korean class is very manageable regardless of your background in Korean. His class will makes sure you know the contents for the exam. As long as you focus in class and do the assignments, class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I learned so much useful Korean. He's really funny during discussions and makes sure to create a welcoming atmosphere. The assignments and quizzes are challenging in just the right way; they prompt you to remember the phrases for later use. Also glad I got a primer on Korean literature!

Prof. Jang is a great language teacher. This class is easy and great for learning if you really want to learn Korean. The tests are thorough and there's speaking parts so you have to stay diligent to study everything. Recommend!

I have taken professor Jang for 2 years now, and I would recommend his class to anyone that wants to learn Korean. There is homework 2x a week with quizzes on Fridays. He wants his students to do well and to learn Korean.

This is one of my favorite classes I've taken at Vanderbilt so far. Professor Jang's teaching style is incredibly effective and he's super nice. Grading criteria is super clear. Korean is a tricky language so staying on top of the work is important. Just show up to class, do the reading, and do the homework and you will do well and learn a lot.
Professor Bateman is a genius, I could listen to him explain Mergers and Acquisitions all day. If I don't mishear him, that is.

Patrick is an amazing professor. We walked into class one day and he stopped to give us a talk on how we should care for the homeless, and more importantly encourage a return to traditional moral values. Tests are a bit hard, but I think it's widely known how Paul Allen's tests are harder.

Patrick Bateman is the best professor I've ever had. His insight into the murder & execution business is the most helpful to my career. Also, do not listen to Paul Allen's review; he does not know what he is talking about.
Expert in finance (especially mergers and acquisitions), just don't get on his bad side.
Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh

Take this guy's courses.  He is a true American hero and is inspired by many.  A lot of video tapes will be watched, with you being forced to return many.  Course materials including chainsaws and axes get relatively expensive but still worth it.
Don't touch his watch.
He is hip to be square!
Often goes into tangents about 80's music.  His keen insights, especially about serial killers, are incredibly detailed.  I don't know how he knows so much...
No Comments

Betz is the best! He's very passionate about the material and cares about his students, and that's evident in his lectures. Loves participation, but is very encouraging, especially when students who don't often speak up want to share. Lenient grader, really just wants you to try and to learn. Highly recommend!

Betz is the best! He is very passionate about what he teaches and caring about his students, and that energy is evident in his lectures. Loves participation, is very encouraging when you share in class, especially when the people who don't talk often want to contribute. Lenient grader, really just wants you to try and learn. Highly recommend!!

Both 1550 and 1551 were the best classes I've taken here. Betz is engaging and cares about his students. Readings before each class but short. Weekly discussion posts based on course readings, but short and graded on participation. Clear on grading criteria. The midterm was in-person but gives prompts beforehand. Take-home final! Take him!

Do not be scared during the first class when you think the guy is on crack- he just genuinely is passionate about the material, which made him one of my favorite professors at Vandy. I WILL SAY- the lectures move insanely fast, and your fingers will feel like they're falling off towards the end, however if you take notes, the exams are super easy.
Love this man. He is incredibly passionate about teaching, and it shows with the way he comes to every class. Reflect his energy, and you will find yourself being equally as passionate.

Amazing and hilarious professor. He shows up to every class with fantastic energy and passion for Brazilian culture. He organizes classes directly around the textbook, making it very easy to follow. At the same time, his group discussions make the class very interesting. There are lots of quizzes and small assignments to be aware of, though.

Best professor in the Portuguese department. He cares a lot about students and their learning. He is hilarious, and after one semester, I can speak Portuguese with Brazilian friends and family. Take a class with Prof Legg!

Honestly a really good teacher if you want to learn, class was interesting and thought provoking. He makes weird jokes and is too witty. Class is all participation, pop quizzes, and HARD papers. Take him if you want to learn, but be prepared for homework, exams and very interesting class sessions.
He is such a good lecturer and actually cares about your wellbeing. He's super open to any doubts you have about assignments and has great class structure. I hope to take more of his classes!

I thought this class would entail watching movies in class, which is not the case. there's a lot of reading outside of class/movies which is time-consuming. participation in lectures is also very important. the few papers aren't too bad, make sure to submit and REWRITE because he gives a lot of points back. he's also a super nice guy who cares.
Very annoying. Super disorganized class, never knew what to do. Papers were fairly easy just hard to write when you don't know the prompt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's an amazing professor. He really cares about his students' learning and all the work he gives is useful. He gives great feedback on assignments which really helps one get better. I definitely recommend this class.

Prof. Legg is the heart of Vanderbilt's Portuguese language program. I am so grateful for having had an opportunity to learn with him and to continue taking courses with him. His passion is inspiring and it motivates you to learn deeply about the Lusophone world. What an incredible professor.

Professor Legg really enjoys teaching about Brazil and Brazilian culture. That said, there is a lot of reading often assigned between class sessions. He is a very kind professor, who also teaches upper-level Portuguese courses, which may be more interesting than Brazilian Cinema. He grades somewhat tough in papers, but he lets you fix mistakes.

Dr. Legg's passion for this course quickly made it one of my favorites at Vandy. He wants all of his students to do well and is willing to provide any resources needed for you to consistently improve your writing. A class that is very film heavy, it was a great break from various dry science courses. All in all, a great guy.
Awesome First Year Writing Seminar. Knowledgable, very engaging lectures with clear expectations.

Legg was an awesome choice for a first year writing seminar! He gave three short essays with one longer final essay, giving the chance to rewrite each essay with clear expectations. He also adds a buffer to your grade by giving credit for one page reflections to films that are automatic 100s. Not a lot of work and incredibly interesting lectures.

Professor Legg is incredible. Super passionate about Brazil and its fascinating culture. He makes class engaging and interesting. For a Freshman Writing Seminar, there is not that much writing (4 papers, a final paper, and weekly response posts). The films watched in class were great as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: A while back we named the loading dock bin after her.  It's amazing how the name has remained after so long. "I'm taking a trip down to BethAnn, can I grab anything from you on my way?"
You can't spell Bethann McLaughlin without the word laugh. And boy-oh-boy is there plenty to laugh at.
Almost a decade since Zald et al booted her out and yet BethAnn is still the source of half of our happy hour amusement. What a legacy!

Just google her. No review I could give her is more scathing than what's already been said about her. Truly a deeply misguided and sorry individual. I will say though that no one was or is sad to see her go.

Professor B is very precious. I had him for core 1020 and it was such a fun class. I learned a lot while also having fun. I love that he is very responsive to his emails and also accessible outside of class. Communication is a big thing for him if you are experiencing any issues talk to him he is happy to listen and help.

Always had thoughtful insights about the readings and designed engaging class activities. He truly cares about his students and encourages participation without being pushy. Explains everything clearly, and as long as you follow instructions, you'll do great. Gives excellent feedback on papers and discussions. A perfect professor for CORE!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Easily one of the most helpful and knowledgeable professors I've had the pleasure of taking a class under.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This man is such a wonderful teacher and human being. He's so gentle, kind, and caring towards his students, and it feels like he's so passionate about everything he teaches. In general, he's pretty adept at using technology, which helps facilitate class. Take it if you're okay doing a bit of reading! Easily a solid A if you're involved.

Trigo is a nice guy who very obviously cares for his class. He is also incredibly intelligent but this means that sometimes his interpretations were very obscure and hard to understand. Readings are long but he explains them if you don't understand. Essays are short but there wasn't a very clear way of grading. Go to his office hours for help!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory and he will take off points if you miss even one class. Stay on top of the reading as he keeps the class discussion lively and includes all students. He is a very sweet man and women in Latin American literature is his area of expertise, so you will learn a lot on the subject.

Great professor! thought-provoking discussion in class, lets you rewrite the 3 papers he assigns. takes a special interest in every student. all around nice guy and the books we read were all very interesting. highly recommend this class/professor!!

I would HIGHLY recommend this First Year Writing Seminar with Prof. Trigo. He is this really cute, funny man who is able to lead incredibly thought-provoking, interesteing discussions every day. There are only 3 papers and you can rewrite them to gain a grade and the novels and topics are really interesting. Plus, he brought us brownies and coffee!
No Comments
Extremely informed about his field of studies. In well prepared for every class and shows interest to helping students learn the material. Assignments and exams are in a medium level of difficulty.

Class is good in that you get to do real good and its unique in that you get to choose what nonprofits to donate to. Hated the fact that she milked the entire 3 hours and made us read random philanthropy readings that had nothing to do with our work. She is nice and assignments aren't too bad, but she is just really boring and hates laptops.

Bess gave a decent class. She's the only 2100 instructor with exams, but they were fair. Lectures were long and tech isn't allowed, which may be tough for some. She tries to engage, however grades are returned at a glacial pace, meaning that you won't know if you're doing something wrong/right in the many quizzes and reading assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most boring class I've taken. If this wasn't mandatory no one would take it. I've never dreaded going to a class more. Unhelpful professor & useless TA. Avoid this professor at all costs. Thank god there is only one exam bc it was the most difficult thing I've ever done at Vanderbilt & was 30% of my grade!! Ruined my 4.0
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bess is a kind lady, albeit a bit bland. This course is unique: Students are given a large sum of real money and tasked with allocating it to deserving nonprofits. It's all one big group project, consisting of several group papers and presentations. Discussion boards every week. Glance over readings and participate, and you'll be fine.
Simply horrific

THE WORST ! she is actually the most boring and dreadful professor then gets mad when no one participates or answers her question, so she banned technology and asked all students to physically print out 25 page readings and bring to class. the other profs for this class are so easy and give no exams, yet she gives 2 exams only writing. DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: simply the worst professor ive ever had at this school

I took away nothing from this class. Teaching style consists of reading off meaningless slides and case studies. Exams and reading quizzes are deliberately meant to trick you. It is framed as a "consulting" class but much emphasis is placed on esoteric theories and frameworks. 

avoid. This class is one of the reasons I'm dropping out of HOD

So many better options for 2100. Her class is severely outdated and has 2 very long open response exams worth 30% each, whereas every other professer has no exams. The class has hints at being a consulting preview, but is once again outdated. If you're not getting 94s on your exams, good luck getting an A. Also lockdown quizzes that are not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolute dread. Content is fine but all she did was read off slides. Gave us assignments over breaks and didn't give us details on the final until the very last week. NEVER responded to our emails so depend on your TA. She assumed a Korean-American student was from China and never apologized. Never seen a prof so removed from their students/content

I would say that her readings can be lengthy and boring, but if you do all of the readings you should do well on the quizzes. Actual class attendance is mandatory, but not as beneficial to your learning. Make sure to understand application of course concepts.

Bess wasn't bad she was just very boring. She also assigns a ton of homework that isn't necessary and could be reduced and have a bigger impact on students. She does seem to care about her students' wellbeing and is willing to give extensions and help if you just ask. The main issue with her class is that it's too much work for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Kind and easy A. She can be boring at times and breakout discussions can be a lengthy but overall solid choice, good readings discussed, as long as you do the work it's easy to get a good grade. She isn't amazing at technology and zoom though, lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Can be Boring but a solid option for 2100. Kind and accessible with good feedback. Getting a good grade isn't that hard.

Excessive reading with no relevance to the big picture of topics discussed. Discussions were boring and readings were long-winded with no explanation or discussion of its relevance to the big picture. Never had papers so subjectively graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bess is very nice, approachable, and accessible. Papers are long but she really helps you do well on them before turning them in. I liked the class but most of her lectures were hard to sit through because some of the material was boring and difficult to engage with.
She's a little boring, but the class is pretty easy. Couple of exams, a bunch of easy quizzes, and some pass-fail assignments. The final paper is annoying, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Bess is so nice, but not a good enough lecturer to make the material seem less boring. It'll be that way for most non-Van Schaack professors, though, so if you need to take the class and Van Schaack's section is full, she's not a bad call. The course includes weekly quizzes, several pass/fail assignments, two exams, and one 6-8 pg paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Bess is very kind and accessible, but unfortunately the course I took on Community Psychology was pretty bland. Most of our readings were from a mediocre textbook and lectures were fairly uneventful. Even though the papers and final project were interesting, the class quickly became disengaged, defeating their potential.

This class is beyond boring. I did not personally learn anything. If you're looking for an easy A and a pointless semester, go for it. If you are looking to put your thousands of dollars in tuition to at least some good use, stay away.

Bess is a Saint, and this class was honestly the best I've taken at Vanderbilt. The material is actually practical and useful and you can apply it later on in life. The class was very centered around case studies along with learning the textbook material. You definitely have to study and prepare for the testsquizzes, but if you do you can get an A
Professor Bess was much better at leading this class than 1000. She is very nice, but discussion isn't always the most interesting. She is a fair grader.

She is very nice, but doesn't always have a clear concept of what's going on. Class isn't the most interesting. For assignments it is best to talk to the lecturer or your grader because she isn't grader you and doesn't know all the guidelines. Attendance and participation are parts of your grade so go to class and participate.
She has no concept of how to teach a class. Most boring class I've taken at Vanderbilt thus far. Awful professor. Switch out if you can.

So nice, go to office hours she's really helpful.  Not always clear, but she gets back to your emails super  fast.  Slow grading.  Easy class.  Sometimes hard to sit through, but she definitely likes you (and gives you a better grade) if you go to her classes. Talk to her after class, attend class, say something during class, you'll get an A. Easy.

She has no concept of how to manage or instruct a classroom. Her comments on papers are not helpful and you can fail a paper for not having "strong topic sentences" which she....long story short, she is a bad teacher, a subjective grader, does not know how to actually teach a class...unfortunately I'm stuck with her for the rest of the semester.

she is sweet and means well but is an idiot. its painful to sit through this class. grading is extremely subjective and it takes her forever to grade papers and get stuff back to you, really annoying.

Really nice teacher, but the grading is so subjective. Nearly impossible to get above a B on any written assignment (which is all of them). You can do all the reading and understand the concepts and still not do well. Very frustrating class grade wise.
This is not a tough class, its just painful and slow and pretty useless. I like most HOD classes but this one is a waste of time. Shes very nice and easy but just doesnt grab you at all

very cut and dry class. she gives you the material in interesting ways and expects you to integrate it into a few presentations you make in the class. not too bad all around. her case study analysis are fairly straightforward too, just make sure you know what she expects.

Professor Bess is not nearly as bad as this website makes her sound (maybe she improved?). Her syllabus was clear cut, and she provided us with very specific guidelines to papers, quizzes, and tests-all strait-forward.  I enjoyed the class and Professor Bess

Nice, but doesn't have a great understanding of the material. Not helpful, has no idea what she's looking for on papers, but tests are relatively easy. does not line up at all with any other 1200 class. take it with someone else if you can.

Doesnt really know what shes doing. You can tell by the way she "asks" what we think and has a difficult time coming up with answers to questions. Doesnt really seem to know what shes teaching, and grades as if we should somehow just know what we should have done.

Kimberly Bess ruined HOD for me. She puts the tiniest details on the really hard tests (aka "just a little quiz!") while completely ignoring the main topics just so the tests will be hard. She hasn't been teaching long and doesn't really know what she's doing--speaks straight from the textbook.

I think she didn't know what to expect by teaching this class. She drastically changed the syllabus about 5 times, and it ended up being totally different from what the other classes are doing. It doesn't align with 1210 either so there's alot more work involved. Take this class with another professor.

This woman is insane. She just began teaching and thus feels like she needs to prove something by giving the most difficult tests (which she markets as "short quizzes") and really boring assignments. All other HOD1200 classes love their curriculum--I recommend taking another teacher.

I would recommend this teacher or class to anyone. Professor Bess is an incredible teacher and you can tell he really cares about his students. The class was very reading heavy but extremely rewarding.
As advertised. This is not a class on WW2, but a class on how to think, how to analyze, and how to disagree. Def a must take. Lot of reading if you do it all. Great TAs too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Bess is an incredibly interesting and entertaining lecturer, and reading his works throughout the semester was also really helpful for the course. There is a lot of homework, but it honestly waters down the essay/final grades a lot which I liked. Definitely take a Bess class if you can!
