Bess is very passionate & knowledgeable about so many topics. His lectures are engaging & information-dense so make sure you go. There are weekly reading & homework assignments & sometimes movies to watch/review. Two 5 page papers and a written, in-person final. Some readings are boring, but Bess always makes the topics interesting. Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: look up "the boy" in the encyclopedia and you will find a picture of this man
Take the class. It transformed my life in many ways. Throughout the course, Bess offers perspectives you may not have realized you were missing.

This class was amazing. It really gets you thinking about life and how we choose to live through it. Bess is one of the greatest lecturers. He is engaging, mindful, and so open to discussion. You have weekly reading responses which aren't difficult a few film responses. discussion section has mandatory attendance.
One of the only classes where you look forward to listening to the lecture. This class will definitely have you pondering, take it while you have the chance because Bess really is one in a million.
Great professor who teaches a wide variety of interesting content in his Human Flourishing (2790) class. Very accessible in office hours, and class isn't too hard either.

Human Flourishing was great! Fair bit of reading each week, but follow instructions on the weekly assignments and do them on time, and you'll get a good grade. Attendance at his lectures is optional, but I highly recommend (I felt I didn't go enough); it's a great opportunity to hear his stories and expand your understanding of life. Def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Michael Bess is the reason I fell in love with history. He's probably the most inspiring professor you could get at Vandy. Took his WW2 class and Human Flourishing and loved both. Not a cakewalk but def not too challenging. Just difficult enough to get you thinking a lot about the material outside of class, but not too much to stress you out.
TA is extremely awful! Who pose those good comments! Lecture is boring as hell. Materials are boring. Rather Drop five times this class. Dont take this one.

Bess already gets his flowers in this rating section but just to reiterate, he's the man! Obviously cares about students so deeply and if you take a class with him you'll leave improved wholly as a person, more intelligent, and better able to understand, interact with, and think about the world. Reminds you what university level education is for.

As a senior who just graduated, I can say that he is probably the best prof Vandy has to offer. I learned so much daily that I was truly sad when the class was over. He knows everything about everything and gives the most awe-inspiring lectures that make you sit back and just say, "damn, he is good." Take him if you can, you won't regret it!!!

Absolutely one of my favorite classes and professors at Vanderbilt. The class is structured and organized well, so there is never any confusion about what needs to be done. The only real downside is that there are a lot of readings, but they are engaging, so it isn't bad. Bess is definitely a professor I would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Bess completely changed my view on history. I came into this class as a psychology major and left as a history major. Bess is an amazing lecturer and such a kind guy. I went to office hours pretty much every week to shoot the shit since he's wicked smart. Def a lot of reading but so worth it, and the reading responses make up a bulk of the grade.

this class is what you put into it- lots of little assignments, engaging lectures and ways to participate and engage. he had optional extra credit discussion sections and projects that you get to choose how to enhance your own flourishing! lots of reading and films but its worth it. one of the best classes!

Prof Bess is truly the best Vandy has to offer. His WW2 class is the most interesting course I've taken in all my years here. Bess's lectures are so interesting and he makes the class into more of a story than a history class. Really intelligent historian and kind individual who actually cares about his students learning something. A must take.

I LOVE professor bess! He's such a kind man who's also clearly brilliant. I took him for human flourishing and I loved it! He puts so much effort into each lecture, and he genuinely wants his students to do well. You get out of the class what you put into it, and I honestly found this class to be very impactful. Highly recommend!

The other reviews on Dr. Bess are accurate, though hyperbole. He is a kind man, a great writer, and the topic of this course are interesting. However, I do find that his lectures could be slightly monotone, without much visual aid. He could also be slightly polarizing, and let his political leanings taint his material. Other than that, he is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Vanderbilt is lucky that they have Professor Bess. He's wicked smart and does an amazing job at engaging his students in discussions. I personally loved his interdisciplinary approach to teaching as well as his practice of frequently bringing in guest lecturers from other departments. His class exposed me to so many new topics and perspectives.

Professor Bess is crazy smart. He's a great teacher but he really impacted me just on the fact that he cares so much for his students. I separate him from every other professor I've had for this reason. He makes an effort to really get to know everyone. Lots of reading but it's all interesting and he offers so much during discussions. Recommend!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bess is probably my favorite teacher I've taken at Vanderbilt. His WWII class was extremely interesting and I genuinely enjoyed listening to his lectures. It's definitely not an easy class and you have to do work, but in my opinion it was extremely work it. Highly recommend taking one of his classes.

One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Amazing lecturer, makes every aspect of the war interesting. Truly one of the best professors you'll find at Vandy. I do not have a single bad thing to say about Professor Bess.

Outstanding WWII history professor who really knows the material and finds unique ways to teach it to the class. Our class had 90 students and he still took the time to know who I was and what interested me in the subject matter. The best professor I have ever had. Would recommend him as a must have.

Absolutely brilliant, World War II with Bess was probably the best class I've taken at Vanderbilt. It was less of a military history class and perhaps somewhat of a philosophy class at times--but in the best possible way. Definitely take any class you can get with him!

Bess is arguably the best professor I have taken at Vanderbilt. Lectures are engaging, and he does a great job of tying them to the real world. His experience (30 years) of teaching at Vanderbilt really shows. Lots of reading, but readings I enjoyed completing. Take him.
Good class.
Michael Bess is the wisest man I have ever met. I took his WWII history class and it changed me. Great guy and teacher

I absolutely loved Professor Bess. His lectures were captivating and engaging, they made you want to listen. His lectures tie very nicely into the weekly readings. Readings are supposed to be finished before lectures begin every week which is not hard to do. Discussion sections were also very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. If you can get into a seminar with him you must take it at all costs. He's a genius who cares about his students. You should expect to reciprocate work however.

Bess is maybe the best prof I've had at vandy. His lectures are heads and shoulders above anything else and his knowledge about ww2 is supreme. He just comes off as a kind, engaged prof who cares about the subject matter and his students.

Bess is VERY smart and engaging. The assignments are creative and the tests are fair. The readings can seem like a lot but skim; essay questions and ID's are given in advance (he picks from them), so you know exactly what will be on the exams. Not an easy A but *best* class I've taken. Significantly improved my thinking and writing skills. TAKE IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bess is the best lecturer at Vanderbilt by far. His organization and emotion are incredible. I learned more about the moral intricacies of WWII than I thought was possible and it was all thanks to professor Bess.
Best class at Vandy hands down. Pretty easy too, an A is definitely doable. Bess is absolutley inspirational.

Best teacher I have had at Vanderbilt.  My time at Vanderbilt would not have been the same without taking this class.  Lectures are amazing and he's honestly a genius.  Its really not hard (not a guaranteed A but if you put in some effort an A should not be hard at all).  Might seem like a lot of reading but readings are not really that necessary

I didn't understand what everyone saw in him at first and thought he was pretty average. Then he gave the final lecture of the class, and it was the most moved I've been in any class I've taken at Vandy. He's a guy that truly cares and wants to see his students address critical issues.

Bess is the man, he is a really down to earth guy who makes history a fascinating subject. European History was not my favorite subject but his lectures are powerful and go beyond the normal views I had of history which was great. Hope to take another class with him!

Bess is an awesome guy. He's a great lecturer and has an impressive knowledge base. Really interesting professor - would definitely recommend any of his classes! One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt.

Professor Bess is the best lecturer ever and this is a great class.  There is quite a bit of reading and weekly reading quizzes.  Only 3 essays, none longer than 5 pages.  Tests are ID's and essays. Attendance is not mandatory in lecture, but you miss too much if you don't go.  Grading standards are high, but A's are easy if you study hard.

Superhuman Civilization: Lectures follow the class-pack word-for-word, but attending and hearing his storiesanecdotes is what gets you 100s on the exams.  Weekly readings for credit are great grade boosters.  TA's do almost all grading, but it's a really unique concept class cross listed for MHS.

300 person lecture negatively affects the class but Bess is fantastic. Really makes you reconsider everything you thought you knew about WWII in terms of the events themselves, their moral significance, and their consequences. Lots of readings but they were a highlight of the course. One of the best profs out there. Definitely recommend the class.
Bess, simply put, is fantastic. Lucid, entertaining lectures. Challenges you to learn more than just the military history of WWII. Best prof I've ver had. Simply brilliant.

He has an excellent understanding of what's an acceptable work load (it might actually be a little too easy). The syllabus shows a lot of reading, but the trick is to SKIM! The papers have a very short page limit, and his grading criteria are very reasonable. His lectures are enjoyable, but sometimes they seem irrelevant and too idealistic.
The best lecturer I have had so far. Readings are not necessary but are helpful. Midterm and Final are a lot of memorization, but are not hard. Definitely would recommend this class.

Prof. Bess is a great lecturer. You'll need to have attended lectures to prepare for the final and midterm. Discussion sections are based mostly on his book about WW2 and really engaging. Very helpful outside of class in office hours if you have questions about the material or history in general. Really enjoyed this course!

Professor Bess is awesome!  His lectures are really interesting and looked at WWII from a different perspective than I had previously considered. Midterm was kind of challenging/there are weekly quizzes but he offers lots of extra credit to make up for it.  I highly recommend him.

The class itself is OK, the work is not. Imagine having to memorize every single person/place/thing about World War II, well that's what the midterm and final is. Way too much work for a 100-level as mentioned. He's a good lecturer but fundamentally clueless about what is an appropriate amount of information to test you on.

Bess is an above average lecturer, class can be interesting. This is not really a typical history class, moral issues/lessons, not battles, are the primary focus of the class. Way too much reading. Midterms and finals test you on outrageous amounts of information. If you like to read history books, then take this class.

Do not take this class if you are not taking it pass/fail. The reading is a ridiculous amount and confusing since it does not go in chronological order. For the midterm and the final his expectations are ridiculous. He is brilliant but completely unfair in his requests for this 100 level history class STEER CLEAR.

all you do for this class is read his book, which i found to be terrible. i wouldnt be surprised if 99% of his book sales come from vanderbilt students. that being said, class is boring, lecture topics are chosen at random and in no way follow a chronological time line of WWII. the final is also VERY hard for a history class.

Easily my favorite class at Vanderbilt. Bess is extremely interesting and makes you think about parts of the war that you never would have considered. It is a lot of writing and probably should be a W course. Grading is a bit arbitrary. I got an A but worked really hard for it.  If you go to class and take good notes, its not too hard to do well.

Bess is an incredibly engaging and helpful professor. He genuinely cares about his students and what they are learning. However, the class is a lot of work and the grading is tough. I ended up with an A- in the class, but I spent three times as much time on this class compared to any other.

Prof Bess is great, works very hard to make sure that his lectures are clear and well-written so the class stays engaged. But in terms of the workload and grading, it is EXTREMELY difficult considering it is a 100-level and not a W course. Take it pass/fail as a senior so you can really enjoy it. Learned a lot, worked a LOT.

Great prof, hard class. Grading on essays (which you write a lot of) is arbitrary and inexplicably tough. As has been said, almost as much a philosophy class as a history one. If you're cool with a B, I would reccomend the class, you learn a lot. Unless you are very willing to work, I think an A is a stretch for most people.

Professor Bess is an excellent professor! I took History of World War II (172) with him. He makes World War II extremely interesting, and he knows his stuff! If a student studies what is in the class pack, he'll easily get an A. I highly recommend this course to anyone! You can't go to Vandy and not take History of World War II with Professor Bess!

Bess gives great lectures but his class is pretty tough.  I don't know many people that ended up with an A in the class.  World War II is an interesting subject and Bess does a great job.  You actually learn a lot.  Should be a W course, though, considering all the writing that is assigned.  Good class but make sure you're ready to do a lot of work

My favorite class at Vanderbilt.  Bess is one of those rare professors who understands the importance of actually teaching, and he does it to a higher level than most Vanderbilt students.  You won't do well unless you challenge yourself.  But this is the sort of class I came to college for and would highly recomment it.
He's nice and he'll help you out.  Plans lectures out like speeches.

Bess lectures are excellent - always well thought-out and written before hand. He doesn't simply ramble on. However, your grade depends on the TA and the books aren't really necessary to the class since they are mostly fact based. Also: the class-pack has basically everything you need to study for the tests.

I see many reviews talking about how awesome his lectures are, but I and many of my friends found them to be shallow and based on extremely simplistic arguements.  Questioning moral dilemmas does not always make for relavent discussion when war is the subject.  His lectures and book are useless when it comes to exams.. they are purely fact based.
An amazing lecturer, probably the best I've had at Vanderbilt.

I took WWII Fall 2005. It was an ok course, but we used the book he wrote. He makes some interesting points, but some of his arguments are facile. There is too much focus on nuclear warfare (not as important as genocide to our generation). He doesn't teach about the actual war. I was disappointed.

AMAZING AMAZING AMAZING professor, man, and teacher.  I would highly recommend him for any class, to anyone.  Compassionate, intelligent, and humble are only the beginning of a long list of his noble attributes.

Bess is an AMAZING guy!  Lectures seem more like a doctoral speech than a dry lecture, looks at sides of WWII that I never thought of considering.  Very nice guy, approachable outside of class.  That being said, it IS a difficult class and requires a lot, but it's worth it for this class and this guy!

Amazing lectures, although a lot of his ideas are not exactly in the mainstream. But he's still an incredible teacher devoted to his students and receptive to points of view other than his own. You can tell he loves to teach.

While I found the class very interesting and Bess to be an engaging professor, my problem was that he actually doesn't teach you anything about WW2.  You discuss random issues dealing with morality of decisions like the atomic bomb, and while that is all well and good, you do not get the details of the war.  It was more of a philosophy class.

GREAT PROFESSOR! Your grade depends on the TA, but Bess was engaging, hilarious, and genuinely cared about the students and their learning.  I strongly recommend this class to anyone!  He will be gone until spring 2007, but take this class then!
Simply the best - very committed to his students.

still is one of my favorite professors.  His lectures are very informative, but very focused.  sometimes he gets into a story and you think, like other professors, he's rambling, but he always seems to have a point.  his tests weren't terribly hard, as long as you do the reading.  Definitely a professor to seek out.
WWII class.  My favorite class at Vanderbilt.  Someone needs to get him a show on the History Channel.

Bess is an incredible professor.  He incorporates multimedia into his lectures, reads poetry, plays music, movies, shows artwork, etc. from the time periods he is talking about.  He puts things into a social/cultural context and makes things interesting.

This guy is the man, and his class is amazing.  I just graduated, and I can honestly say his class is the only class that I made it to for EVERY lecture. He makes classes interesting, and he can teach you more about the subject than you can imagine.  A pregnant TA may get in the way of your enjoying the class, but if you ignore her, you'll be set.
Awesome teacher, tough grader, but one of the best at Vanderbilt.

This is absolutely the best course I have had the pleasure of enduring at Vandy.  Bess is the only professor I have ever felt not only is passionate about his material, but loves to teach it as well.  A standing ovation on the last day of class proves the entire class' opinion of this great teacher.

I loved Professor Bess.  His class was so good that on the last day we all gave him a standing ovation.  I even almost starting crying, it was so good.  The only hard thing about the class is the TA though.

Such a great professor.  I learned so much from his course and highly recommend him to anyone.  He makes you work hard and think, but its refreshing to have a teacher who challenges you intellectually.
Pretty good teacher, but kind of one-dimensional. Class was exciting at first, but it's kind of repetitive now.
Helpful, and clear.  Great teacher.
No Comments
He is absolutely one of my favorite teachers-so excited about the topic. I didn't mind doing all the work required because the class was so great.
Great teacher. I always make up excuses to go to his office hours just to hear him make really intellegent points.
The finest professor I have ever known.  Thank you so very much.
Quite possibly one of the most inspiring, interesting and generally good teachers I have ever had. Class is tough, but actually....fun.
Extremely knowledgeable and an interesting class.  Not difficult if you do the reading.
He is so incredibly nice and has a great sense of humor. The class is very interesting and enjoyable.

incredibly nice, v. personable prof. class pak outlines all lectures for the semester, including ids for midterm and final. good course to strengthen writing skills. dont let the fact that he is a hard grader keep you from taking this course.
great teacher, great lecturer, class isnt too hard but they grade hard.... a fair amount of reading, but really interesting class.... great guy and always willing to help

WWII history with bess has been my favorite class at vanderbilt this year. bess's lectures are great and intriguing. the TA that grades my papers and tests is one hell of a hard grader, though...overall great class, but hard too.
awesome stories, REALLY interesting, only 2 midterms, 2 papers...definitely worth taking!  my favorite class at vandy!
interesting and informative lectures, helpful and nice, but hard grader
Goes off on tangents often, fails to finish lecture material, but he's a nice gy

Piyali is the sweetest and most caring professor you'll ever have!! Her 1260W class is focused on exploring south Asian culture through film and literature. The books/movies are carefully selected and are things that you will most likely actually enjoy! As long as you keep up with the readings and put some work into your essays, you will get an A!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Piyali is one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Her stories and experiences are incredible, and she is so inspiring as a person. It's extremely clear that she cares deeply about all of her students. 2 essays for the whole semester, which she gives you detailed feedback for to revise before you submit them. Not a stressful class at all!

Piyali was fantastic! I absolutely hated writing, but over the course of one semester, I have learned to love it. She genuinely cared about my growth, and wanted to see me and my classmates engage in the classroom. She is also super accessible and gives A TON of feedback. Workload is perfect and stays consistent so there aren't any curve balls.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I love Piyali! I took her nonfiction writing seminar, and it was one of my favorite classes. We wrote two essays and one short piece. There are also readings due every class, but it's never overwhelming. The final was a portfolio of our work, and was very rewarding to complete. And her life stories are amazing and super interesting.

Piyali is truly amazing, and she only has good intentions and really wants the students to learn much from this class. Only negative side is that the writing style has to match the style she wants. But definitely take this class if you are considering it! Interesting topics, discussions, and amazing classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bhattacharya is helpful and inspirational. She really wants her students to succeed and is willing to do anything for them. The course is manageable if you keep up with the readings and participate in class discussions. She always provides her student with new perspectives and you will definitely learn a lot by the end of the course.

Dr. Bill goes out of his way to try to explain the lectures in new ways. He is clear with his exams about what is going to be on them, and they are similar to his quizzes. He does give in class assignments that are participation. He genuinely cares about the student, and you can tell he is extremely passionate about the topic.

I took the class two years ago so the class format may have changed. But he is a really kind and nice person, still remembers me even that's the only class I took with him. He cares about your well-being alot. Lectures can be fast-paced but would not be a problem if you do your work. Love him!

I think this class is very straightforward. Homework assignments that were always started in class, online exams, and everything open note! Just read the slides and do your own research if you're confused. He reads the slides to you in class, does several demonstrations, and clearly cares about your well-being. LOW-STRESS!!

Good lecturer and you can tell he puts in effort. Found the class to be easy if you've had previous background in general biology. Exams are open note & take home but can be tricky. Attendance not required, multiple attempts on quizzes & HW assignments.

very friendly guy, but the class itself is very disorganized. he skims through 100+ slides in one class period, so it all ends up self-taught and hes really unclear about grading (we never got our exams back and he ghosts emails a lot). I feel like def has the potential to be so amazing but way more stressful than I expected.

Very hard to understand his lectures. He tries to go through 75 slides in one 50 minute lecture, so I'm stuck trying to teach myself the curriculum. Very kind person so it's hard to give him a bad review but I can't seem to do well on any of his exams. They also don't give you the option to get feedback from exams.

Dr. Bill was my first professor in any STEM class at Sandy and he gave me such a great experience. He was hilarious, the notes he gave during lectures were clear, and he didn't expect anything that he knew we couldn't handle.

I really enjoyed the Parasitology course. Dr. Bill does a great job of being accommodating to the busy semester. There were 4 exams, 3 of which are mainly diagnosing patients with parasites. The unique grading of the exams where you get to drop your three worst case studies was very helpful. He is also such a nice guy and cares about his students.

ECE-6343
The slides are a bit boring, he does warn that it'll be sleepy. Professor is very knowledgable. Exams are take-home, we have 1 week to submit, they are not terribly hard, however some questions are not "publicly available" so don't just ask ChatGPT, it'll get a lot of things wrong, read the slides and attend class.

He is an ok lecturer, however he is very unorganized and it makes it difficult to work outside of class. He is very funny and is entertaining during lecture and cares about his students understanding. Exams are incredibly difficult to complete during the time provided. The average exam grade in my section was a 57, but he curves final grades
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: To be very clear, this is a tough course. However, it's an extremely rewarding course. This is the 1st courses that I've taken at Vanderbilt that has truly re-taught me how to think and solve problems, and for that, I'm grateful. Oh by the way, Bhuva seems stern but he's an extremely nice, flexible guy. Get to know him; he really wants you to learn

No one cares more about his students' success than Professor Bhuva. While this class is definitely challenging and has a reputation for being one of the most difficult classes at Vanderbilt, Bhuva has open office hours and is always happy to help his students with any questions. His lectures are both informative and entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took this class in the Spring of 2018 and it was terrible. You basically don't know how you are doing in the class until the end.

This class is hyped up to be too hard, in reality, it's very doable if you pay attention and do the homework. He does open office hours, so if he's not teaching or doing research and then he will sit down and help you. Great guy, highly suggests going to class and engaging in class and you'll be fine. He also lets you decide when you have the tests
An amazing prof! Cares so much about his students. Difficult class though
Great guy, knows his stuff. Really takes the time to listen and talk to his students. Tenured but don't let that scare you.
Great teacher and really cares for students. Very accessible outside of class. Material is a bit tough but he will try his best to help you understand it. 10/10 would take again.

This man is brilliant and cares deeply about his students. The class's difficulty is overhyped because of unprepared freshmen. Exams may be long, but not terribly hard, provided you don't panic. The class/lab gets messy/disorganized sometimes, but as long as you keep up by doing textbook problems, you'll be fine.

Very engaging lecturer. Hilarious. Acts condescending but at heart is a really nice guy. Cares about you genuinely learning the material & not just trying to attain a grade. Not the best prof if you want someone organized who explains the material clearly and easily to help you. A great prof if you enjoy learning challenging things and funny lectur
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Insanely good lecturer, will challenge any student regardless of their natural ability.  He is also hilarious and it is hard to NOT pay attention in his class. The HW in VLSI is EXTREMELY time consuming (easily more time than any engineering course). However, the HW and project grade should be an automatic A.

Professor Bhuva is knowledgeable and cares about how well students learn the material. Unfortunately, those qualities are overwhelmed by a completely disorganized class. His lectures ramble and he blindly assigns homework without looking to see whether the problems are relevant or solvable. Tests are too long and they test speed over understanding.

Would say Dig. Logic is one of the hardest classes for CS majors here, with either prof. Grade was determined by wkly hmwrk (wildly inconsistent grading), three midterms (all avgs 60), and final (3 hrs long). One of those classes where the material is difficult enough by itself, but the grading makes it 10x worse (many students withdrew to retake)

50% of the HW is doable and the other is random jank that was never taught in class. Graders are harsh on HW. For multipart test questions, if you mess up part A you'll lose points for remaining parts even if it was done correctly afterwards from part A. Midterm avg were 70%, 48%, 60%. Final avg was 69%. Curve was big-85.7% gave me an A somehow.

Good lecturer, knows his subject very well. Unfortunately, graders are very inconsistent, on homework and tests. Book is terrible, and homework problems from the book are often very different from the midterms. If you pay attention though, you will learn Digital Logic, even if your grade suffers a bit.

Dr. Bhuva is an excellent lecturer. Go to lecture and take good notes if you want a good grade.   The material is different (number conversions, K-maps) but he tries his best to explain it clearly.  He is extremely helpful during office hours.   Finally, he is a funny lecturerer with a bone-dry sense of humor.
Dr. Bhuva is very professional. He will teach you how to critically, and thoroughly think about the topic. He is inspirational. Hard class, but very essential.

Bhuva is really on top of digital logic. He explains things clearly and won't move on until everyone is clear. He is always willing to give more examples if you ask. Prepare for his condescension but don't be scared by his snide remarks( or jokes). He wants you to LEARN more than anything else. Hang in there after 1st exam, it'll get better.

He can be obnoxious, but I love this guy. He's got a very sarcastic sense of humor and can seem unapproachable, but if you ask for help he'll give it.  Will give points back on tests if the graders made a mistake.  Extremely clear lectures with hilarious one-liners thrown in.  Lectures go really fast unless people ask questions.

Bhuva may be the better instructor for Digital Logics, but I recommend taking another class if possible. Our class average on the first two tests were a 51 and 52, and he waits until the very end of the year to scale. In class, he teaches well but is derogatory towards many questions. The pre-labs are awful and the TA's are useless.

Bhuva is the most condescending professor, perhaps human-being, on the planet. He is unwelcoming and any question you may have will be struck down with a sarcastic rhetorical. He does not prepare you to review the tests in any way. He is no help with clarifying the lecture, assisting with the lab, or anything pertaining to this lab.
He's a good lecturer, he makes the concepts seem easy in class. The hard part is finishing the tests in time, they are too long for a fifty minute test. Not to mention the lab; the lab is horrendous.
The best.

Bhuva was great! Funny guy and keeps interest levels high. But you need to keep up with assignments and take help regularly as travels frequently. His grad research student Nihar taught 4-5 classes.get hold of him if you cant find Bhuva.TAs weren't much help
Not a good option. Test average is around 60~70. He curved final grades by 9 points.

He was very unhelpful initially, when I did poorly on the 1st test. However, after I scored highly on the remaining tests he suddenly became very patient and helpful whenever I asked questions. Averages of all tests were b/w 60-70, and the final curve was small (I had a 90% and was curved to an A). Also, the TAs were useless.

He didn't explain things clearly at first but his clarity improved over the semester. I don't like the way he teaches.He always wants to keep the average around 60~70. Although he draws a curve in the end, it is not a huge curve at all (no way to be curved from F to B-)

It is undeniable that he doesn't care much about this class. In spite of this, he teaches it very effectively and does want students to do well. He did make a significant mistake in writing one exam, but he gave the points back, and is always fair. He won't test you over anything that he doesn't cover. He's one of the best professors here.
Too difficult.

He is definitely smart. He flies through the material during lectures, and sometimes this can cause confusion. Tests are poorly made and can contain mistakes. It seems that he made it in a hurry. You will need a lot of work and luck to get a decent grade.
Stay away.

He's a good lecturer, but he cares so little about this class, and it shows. He is never in his office nor does he reply to emails, he and the TAs are absolutely useless when you need help, and the tests are so poorly written that he had to omit an entire problem on our 2nd test. Most of all, THIS CLASS IS HARD. Be prepared to teach yourself.

He is one of the most clear teachers you can have at Vanderbilt, so you must attend lectures. That being said, the book is too bad, and he can be very condescending if you go to his office. He is also careless about homework assignments and tests. He made a test problem wrong in our 2nd test so people got stuck and couldn't finish the test.
Great professor with a great sense of humor. Don't become discouraged by the low test averages -- he curves a great deal.

Bhuva is a great professor. Tests are very challenging for some. (Average of all the tests was <65). He is fair, and likely curves a great bit. He also really cares about students and wants them to succeed.

Best professor I had my freshman year. It's incredible how clearly and logically he explains the material. At the beginning of the year he pretends to be really austere but it's just an act; he seriously cares about his students and will NEVER move on if you don't understand. Class is very hard, but he's a great guy. Trust me, Bhuva's worth it.
I really love his teaching style, though the material is really challenging. Make sure to preview everything before the class as he will go extremely fast.I learned a ton.
Great teacher and very clear. The homework and pre-labs are fairly difficult and time-consuming, but overall the class is worth the time. It will be hard, but definitely take this class!
This guy's legit.
This class is a weed out class.  But stick with it. My final grade was a high F. It was curved to a B. :)

Some people give up in his class. Don't..there is always a curve at the end.  He is extremely busy all the time so it is hard to get help immediately. Just email him and he will tell you where he is if you need help. This guy helps a lot too -> www.youtube.com/user/nptelhrd#grid/user/803563859BF7ED8C

Very difficult teacher, but he's very funny his class was my favorite I've taken. The material is really interesting, but if he says something in lecture that you don't understand say so immediately, he WILL go back over it otherwise he just assumes you understand. he genuinely wants his students to do well and has a generous curve

Makes students think that he's very unapproachable (on purpose). Has a very good sense of humor. Moves very quickly. If you don't keep up, you're dead. Very interesting guy once you get to know him. The homework and lab are very time-consuming. The test aren't hard if you understand what he's teaching and if you work quickly.

Totally not as bad as everyone says. Tests are hard and you probably won't do too well on the first one but after that you'll be fine. Go see him if you don't understand something, he's very helpful outside of class. Pre-labs SUCK and take hours so be ready.
Now you can do ANYTHING in digital logic!

Not bad at explaining things, but makes himself very unapproachable.  His tests (80% of your grade) will be unclear and he won't be there to clarify the questions, even if he says beforehand that he will.  If you do things a different but equally functional way, you'll still get it wrong and you're not going to be getting any points back.

I know this guy seems like he is going to be hard and not helpfull from the rating but he is a good teacher he is funny and keeps class interesting. I think it is the subject he teaches that makes him hard and confuzing try to take this class if you can

Hilarious guy, funniest prof Ive ever had. Pretty good teacher, if you don't get something, stop him in class and he'll go back over. The class is easy at first and gets hard at the end. The book is terrible, and the homework makes little sense, but has nothing to do with tests. Grades are very easy and with minimal effort you should get an A or B.

If you're trying to decide which class to take for EECE 116 (Sztipanovits or Bhuva), there shouldn't even be a question.  Bhuva is 10x better than Sztipanovits at stimulating your interest in the subject. He works more examples but also moves more quickly.  It helps to go to both teachers' review sessions though, if you can find out when they are.
sometimes unclear on what he wants you to do, but approachable and he will help you if you seek him out.  class not too boring because of his personality.

Bhuva is great.  Some don't like this class because it is "hard" but if you are prepared you'll do fine.  Be aware that the tests that Bhuva makes are harder than the ones that Stapanovitz (sp?) makes.  Both sections take the same test, though so it's fair.

Very nice guy and very brilliant. Don't let the accent fool you. He is very nice during office hours and willing to help. He talks and writes on the board very fast so take notes quickly. Tests were reasonable and I got a A- with some work.
Good class, a pretty fun guy. Sometimes he doesn't really make it clear what he wants you to do or how he wants you to do it but if you talk to him one on one he's really nice and helpful.
He is a pretty cool guy, he kind of makes the class fun with his little jokes here and there. I didn't think he was that difficult to understand, either.
He is much better than Stipanovitz at teaching Digital Logic.  It is sometimes hard to understand him, and he moves really fast.  Since he covers a lot of info, you will do better on the tests.
Intimidating and hard to understand, but it gets better as the semester progresses.
Talks as fast as he writes on the board. Good sense of humor. Very nice outside the class. The tests are kinda breezy but too short so u miss one u miss a lot.
Awful, awful course.
No Comments
No Comments
really knows his stuff but is at times difficult to comprehend

I really liked Professor Bils! The class has 2 midterms and a final (all open notes), a take-home quiz, and online textbook quizzes (multiple attempts). While attendance isn't mandatory, its super helpful to go cause he does examples on the chalkboard that aren't posted, which are EXACTLY like the exams.

He made intermediate micro into one of the easiest classes at Vanderbilt. He gives extremely thorough lectures and does numerous example problems. Midterms are open note, plus he gives a practice midterm before each that is very similar to the actual midterm. Same is true for the final. Definitely take 3012 with Bils if you can.

This class is super easy if you show up and pay attention. Material is super straight forward and every test is open notes. He also gives practice midterms before the tests that are almost identical to the tests. Great professor and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, not bad at all. All tests were open-note and the class averages have been very high. As long as you go to class and take notes you don't really have to read the textbook, other homework (all on an online platform) were fairly easy to complete and not very time consuming. Though boring at times he is a clear lecturer.

Bils is an excellent professor with clear lectures. If you understood lecture, did the problem sets, and went into office hours for help, you were well-prepared for the tests. This was a basic game theory course, and anyone who found it dry perhaps expected something else. Would easily take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is a tough class, but Bils does a good job and is very helpful. Go to office hours for the p sets.

The most boring lectures you will ever be forced to sit through in your undergraduate career... you will come out of this class knowing nothing new about politics. Painfully slow grading, one midterm did not match anything he taught in class, and extremely inaccessible professor. My worst class at Vandy to date. DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR BILS!!!!!

A saltine probably has more of a personality than him. He stands there and writes on the whiteboard for 1hr and 15 min straight, sometimes just copying the textbook. The textbook is supposedly required by he never mentioned it once in class. No answer keys to hw or exams, and takes literal ages to hand them back. Also not helpful with feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To be fair to Professor Bils, I had never taken a game theory class before. However, he made it seem like an intro course and it did not feel that way. When I asked to meet with him about my declining grades, he told me to "study differently" and would not give any tips to that effect. He drones on in lectures and the tests do not match them at all
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy class, but clear expectations. Grade based on 5 problem sets, two midterms and final. Attendance not mandatory but you should definitely go. Hard subject matter though and do not take unless you really want to learn about Game Theory or Economics. Common misconception is that is fulfills poli sci theory requirement- it does not.

This is kind of a weird class and is hard for lots of people. I didnt find it too bad; its really just person to person. Bils is nice enough; clear lectures and grading criteria. First test was STUPID hard, but it got better afterwards. I recommend; I have heard Wiseman is better, but Bils does alright for 2259. Solid choice.

This dude gives you the world's easiest problem sets and lectures at a high school level then turns around to give you the hardest exams you've ever taken. Avoid at all costs and pray for a curve if you have no other choice.

Excellent econ professor. Tests represented the material in lecture. Bils is a clear lecturer that teaches you what you need to know, provides real-world case studies, is very accessible, provides practice exams, and holds in-class review before each exam. Grades very fairly. Im excited to take his game theory course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was somewhat interesting but Professor Bils is pretty hard to keep up with. The bar is high and you need to study on your own a good amount to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I feel like I was teaching myself the material the whole time. Compared to the other professors, it seems you have to work way harder just to get a lot less out of the class. Try to get someone else for micro if you can but it's not the end of the world if you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great guy, but the lectures were sometimes confusing and I feel like overall the class was harder than it really needed to be.

I think this was his first time teaching 3012 and he's a really nice professor but his lectures were confusing and he didn't give as much practice as other profs did. We even skipped the last chapter completely. Exams were over zoom while other classes had takehome. Thankfully, he curved a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is the first time Professor Bils teaching undergraduate courses at Vanderbilt, and so far he does a fantastic job. Lectures are clear with examples and details; tests are fair and represent what is covered in class. Looking forward to his political science classes in the next semester.

Reinforcement learning is the worst class I've taken in Vandy. The lectures are extremely dry, even the slides are poorly organized. The assignments are outdated and full of typos and mistakes, and they deduct points for stuffs not mentioned in the questions. The TAs aren't responsive and grades are released at really late.

Professor Biswas is a nice professor, who is knowledgeable about the topic. The problem is not with him but with his TA. 50% of the grades were returned on the last day of the semester. The professor asked him to take over for 5-6 classes, and the TA did not know what he was talking about, we had to correct his work in the example problems given.
Reinforcement learning was incredibly hard. Projects that aren't really solvable, pop quizzes, chapters of textbook reading per week, the whole nine yards.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Weirdest class of my life; Biswas is extremely accessible, explains concepts multiple times, and is very clear, but the other students constantly decided to not submit easy assignments. Really low energy, dry lectures, it was hard keeping attention. Class was fine, but I didn't get what I was hoping out of it, mainly bc "coding" was in Simulink.

He is a very kind professor who is very helpful when answering questions you have on anything, especially homework. While his lectures can be dry, overall the class is easy. 4-5 well explained homeworks, 4-5 quizzes that weren't too bad, and one class project.

His lectures can be a little dry, but for Advanced ML, you can learn most of the stuff on your own or by going through his slides. No tests, although there are final projects and participation counts towards your grade.
Does not explain things at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is a good teacher and very knowledgeable person. I took his graduate class and it required a lot of prerequisite knowledge. He did not explain basic things but went deeply into details.
He is a below average teacher with poor teaching skills. A lot of the students in the class seemed to share my frustration. I will not take any of his classes from now on.
Was disappointed by the class.

Purcell is one of the best. An amazing storyteller and a kind, intelligent man. Good class for improving writing, speaking, and argumentation skills. Weekly reading and discussion of famous historical speeches. Engaging guest speakers. A few assignments with sometimes picky grading.

Purcell's aura is infinite, and his lectures were super interesting. The class lasted two and a half hours at night, but it didn't feel long. However, he can be hard to read and is a bit of a picky grader. He also seemed to value quantity over quality participation. Still, this class is a must-take for anyone interested in municipal government.

Purcell is the gold standard of Vanderbilt professors. He's passionate, intelligent, engaging, and the 21st century cities class feels relevant in a way other classes don't. I felt honored just to be in his class the way it impacted me. I can't recommend taking Purcell more; he's an amazing professor, and person!
He was amazing!
He is amazing! Definitely take his class. Very insightful!

I LOVE MAYOR PURCELL! Genuinely one of the most intelligent, well-spoken, and caring people I've ever met. 
I feel like I learned such an insane amount in such a short amount of time. Workload is super minimal (3 short essays, final paper, one presentation, and participation) and he's an easy grader. Very supportive guy. TAKE HIM!

Professor Purcell is one of the most knowledgeable and compassionate professors I've had during my four years at Vanderbilt. Vanderbilt is lucky to have him, and if you're remotely interested in state/local politics, this class is a must-take. Even though this class is late at night, it is 100% worth it, and I look forward to it every time.

The class meetings are well planned and and a joy to be in. My only gripe is that the written assignments lack specific guidelines, and there aren't that many, so there's more pressure on each assignment. Purcell is brilliant and very available to answer questions though. Graded on participation, 3 policy memos, and one final paper/presentation.

Class is amazing. Once a week, couple hours, and very useful content. Different from any other class, not much work and Purcell is an awesome guy. Really helpful and wants everyone to succeed. Highly recommend

Professor Purcell is the greatest man alive. Although the course is 2.5 hours once a week, he makes it interesting by dividing class time up into weekly news, a speaker, and then discussion. He's a reasonable grader and wants everyone in his class to do well. I wish I could work for him after graduation.

Amazing professor. I learned SO much. Readings are very interesting, but take a while. Lectures are engaging and fascinating. Tests are very hard so take good notes on readings and lectures. He wants the best for all his students in life. It's a lot of work but every bit taught me so much and I loved learning from him. Take him if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Collins is an expert in what he teaches and does a good job teaching what are all things considered pretty abstract concepts. His quizzes are kind of hard so make sure to do the readings, but he is always actively helping his students - for sure reccomend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is obviously very sma

Professor Collins is a great lecturer! I learned so much from his class. We do need to read one assigned paper before each class, but it doesn't take very long. He is always accessible outside of class. His final is not cumulative! One midterm, one final, some easy homework. Take a class with him if you can. He is a very intelligent person!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a superstar in the econ department, and teaches undergrad only once in a while. If you ready to work and learn, there is no better choice than him. He is amazing in every single aspect, and I guarantee you will probably learn more than in any other class at Vandy. His intelligence, expertise, and passion shine through. Very caring, respected.

His class was RLLY TOUGH but he is definitely one of the most knowledgeable professors at vandy. There's a LOT of reading and the articles you read every class will be asked about on the midterm. Grading is made up of article responses, a long essay, 3 exams, and PARTICIPATION MATTERS. He's super nice and chill but his grading was the death of me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Absolutely great class. Hard to get a good grade, though.

Collins is an awesome professor. The class is not easy by any means, but one of the most interesting econ electives and feel like I learned a ton. Collins himself is unbelievably knowledgeable and writes leading research in this field, which is insanely cool. Don't think he's teaching undergrads for a bit but such a worthwhile class.

Professor Collins is fantastic and incredibly caring. The class is a little bit more abstract than some other ECON classes/electives and the material has the potential to be incredibly dry, but he does a great job of making it interesting. If you take him, start the paper early! Don't rush to finish it the week before it's due -- it won't work!

Absolute gem--Dr. Collins passion shines through in his lectures and pedagogical style. He's very easy to engage and will help students explore their own ideas in the term project. That being said, the class (despite being a lower level elective) isn't easy. There's a decent amount of reading (research paper each class + discussion response).

Definitely recommend taking a class with Collins, especially if you need a US credit. Very clear lectures, Collins knows the material inside-and-out (and has had a hand in creating a non-negligible amount of it). Fairly easier but not the easiest option-- exams are kind of weird and worth 60% of the grade, but definitely fair. Best EconHis here imo
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: An extremely nice guy! We read a research paper per week and are expected to know them well for in-class discussion, essays, and exams. It's definitely a good amount of work, but Prof Collins is always willing to provide extra help thru email/office hours. Would definitely recommend ECON 3150 for an upper-level ECON elective.

Read an academic paper each week to discuss in class but wasn't too bad (you don't have to fully understand it all, just know the general concepts). Topics were all very interesting. Professor Collins appreciated all students' opinions and was very easy to talk to. Very organized class structure and clear assignments. Would take again!

This class felt like a graduate level class. You read one research paper a week and are expected to know it inside and out for the tests. The research papers are at least 30-40 pages and very dense and difficult to understand. Group paper is extremely challenging but he helps you as much as you need it. Curved at the end though and he's super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He must be one of the best and cleverest eecon prof at Vandy! Take his class if you really want to learn a lot! you need to read lots of papers for this class and take notes of the lectures. Grading is fair, and he curves.  very helpful. His TA also very helpful.

Probably the best Economics professor at Vandy! His lectures are interesting, informative, and detailed. His tests are fair, but require preparation. He is very approachable - I learned a lot in this class and recommend it. He knows a ton about the topics discussed in class.

Expects lots of difficult reading. He makes up for it by giving notes so go to class. He is very intelligent and serious...very helpful during office hour. Tests are fair but the final research paper might give you a hard time. Challenging but great class.
Great class and professor. Prepare to work..lots of reading. He gives valuable notes in class so attendance is mandatory. Overall, one of the most difficult class I've taken at vandy.

This is a great class, but the most challenging one I have taken at Vanderbilt.  The course work is very demanding and the final paper takes a great deal of work.  Professor Collins is one of the most approachable professors I have ever had, but this class is also the lowest grade I have recieved at Vanderbilt.

Very difficult class that I was determined I would get a B or below, but he grades completely based off of the class average. If you can beat everyone else, you'll do alright and learn from one of the best in the field. Ended up with an A-, but that final paper was hard and should not be written at the last minute.

This class is very demanding-you're required to read a lot of dense econ research papers and memorize some complicated econometric models for the midterm/final.  Go to class, Prof. Collins notes are really thorough and helpful for exams-this is a difficult course but Prof is really helpful and an added bonus, he's the cutest econ prof at vandy!

Genius.  Class is demanding because you will be reading professionally published econ papers - a first for most students.  Bill is very knowledgeable on this subject and will guide you through any problem you have as long as you show the effort.

THE most interesting class I have taken at Vanderbilt! Collins is brilliant and really conveys the material well. For the final paper- you really have to work on it on your own initiative, but at the end you will feel very accomplished. Midterm and Final are difficult so prepare to study!!
Very intelligent and academic but doesn't mean he has unrealistic expectations for his students.  Overall an excellent teacher, though an A in the class is hard to come by.
No Comments

Collins really knows his stuff.  I did find this class tough, even though I got an A in 231, which is supposedly the tougher of the two intermediate weed-out classes (taken with another prof).  He was very prompt in answering emails, looks like a econ prof (wardrobe, check!).  I would recommend him.

This guy is impossible. He expects the class to average Ds on his tests.  Sometimes i dont even think he knows what he is talking about.  Take it if you really wanna push yourself, otherwise steer clear!
This guy has literally the hardest examinations I have ever taken in my life.  Good teacher? Perhaps, but be prepared to work harder than most classes you've ever been in.

This dude is brilliant, BA and PhD from Harvard.  Class is tough, but if you go to the TA's for help on problem sets you're set.  He doesn't hold official office hours but is very helpful and nice when you set up an appt.  I recomend

Easy A if you just mildly pay attention in class. As someone with no coding background, I struggled to keep up slightly after the midterm but Chat GPT (which he allows us to use) was helpful in explaining concepts. If you do all the psets and extra credit, you don't have to do the final to make an A. Great skill, highly recommend course.
Bisbee is a very good lecturer. As long as you follow his work in class, you will be able to learn R very quickly!

loved his lectures, especially since I took it election year so he'd talk abt data related to the election. easy A class, but i got lost halfway through the semester so chat came in clutch. he's really helpful in OH, so I'd recommend you go if you're stuck on a pset

This class really wasn't difficult at all. Bisbee is super funny and understanding when it comes to grading. He's very clear with his lessons, and you will do well as long as you at least somewhat pay attention in class. Learned a lot in ds 1000!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A great professor especially as a student who never had experience in coding. Was easy to follow along and helpful to visit TAs during office hours online throughout the week if needed.

Awesome class. Very clear grading criteria from the start which helps you plan out your time. The problem sets took me a decent amount of time, and started getting harder by the end. My advice would be to really pay a lot of attention in the beginning to learn about the fundamentals of R, which will actually help. He's a great professor!

Bisbee is great. He runs the class with people who have never coded in mind. If you don't get an A in this class, you must have been trying to fail. Additionally, I learned enough in this class to skate by some technicals in an interview which is all you can really ask from such an introductory course.

I went into this class not knowing anything about coding and came out of it knowing so much. This class uses R studio which is harder than other languages but Bisbee makes it so easy to follow along in lecture. He also gives A TON of extra credit to the point where some people don't even need to take the final. Overall a super caring and good guy.
One midterm, one final, PAs are easy. Class is easy

Professor. Bisbee does an amazing job introducing students to R and RStudio. This is a great class for people with or without coding experience. He is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about his field. I would highly recommend this course for people interested in Data Science or for an easy AXLE SBS credit.
awesome professor
Prof. Bisbee is a great lecturer. As DS1000 is an intro-level course, go to lectures, do homework, and this will be the easiest A to get at Vanderbilt.

Dr. Bisbee is an incredible professor who will give you a great overview of what Data Science is and help you learn R Studio in just a semester. I came out of this class understanding how Data Science can shape my further careers and how it can be applied to ethics. The problems sets can be challenging, but Dr. Bisbee offers extra credit.

Super chill class. Pay attention in lecture & use campuswire and you'll do so well you won't even need to take the final to get an A. Personally I didn't pay attention at all, took the final, and ended with over 100%. Loved it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy but boring. Great for math credit but the class is so mind-numbing and he doesn't teach how to code all that well.
BEST ever. Genuinely cares for students, which is rare for a big class. Easy A- Many students could skip the final and still end with an A

I loved Bisbee!! He was a great professor even though he went at the speed of light at times. The problem sets are difficult but manageable (don't leave it til the last day like I did and spend 7 hours on Friday doing it!). He often gives a lot of answers to tests and problem sets during class. Also lots of EC opportunities so its a grade booster.

I love Bisbee. First half of the class is super easy but then difficulty spikes. However you can still get an A in the class because the tests are extremely easy and they're always open note. The only con is that Bisbee types way too fast. You end up just copying what he's typing but not understanding why he's coding anything. Lot's of coding.

Course material is super interesting. Bisbee himself is a kind and cool guy! While there is a lot of extra credit, (My tip is to do all of it so you don't even need to take the final.) the problem sets can be difficult to solve and take around 10+ hours on super hard ones. CampusWire and TAs are super helpful and there is help everywhere for you.
There're lots of extra credits so it was easy to get an A. He had great lectures that keep me focused for the entire one-and-a-half hours. You will definitely learn a lot from the course.

you can tell that bisbee is truly passionate abt his field and cares abt his students! there's soooo many extra credit opportunities that it seems virtually impossible to leave without an A. the course itself was a bit tough at times for me, but it was manageable. the only critique i have for bisbee is that he goes a bit fast at times

Lectures are generally interesting, but can be boring at times. The homeworks directly correlate with the material taught during class making the assignments extremely doable. The midterm is also super easy as the practice midterm is spot on with the actual midterm. He is super generous and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Professor Bisbee is a great lecturer and so intelligent in his field. The class was a little confusing at first esp if you dont have a CS background. Pretty much everyone finishes with an 100 or above in the class because he gives so many opportunities for extra credit.

If you have any CS experience at all, this will be a very easy class, but Bisbee still tries to make it engaging. Interesting data sets (elections, sports, hollywood, twitter, etc) helped keep it lively. So much extra credit (most people were averaging like 130% on Psets) so you can focus on learning and enjoying the material rather than your grade

Great professor, obviously passionate about data science, but has a habit of going fast in lectures. Taught in R, but it's easy to pick up if you have CS experience. Graded on two tests (20% each), problem sets (40%) and attendance (20%) ChatGPT was allowed for this class if you give credit, but the class is totally doable by yourself.

Great intro class you can focus on learning and not worry too much about grades. Lots of resources like posted slides and access to prof via Campuswire. Midterm and final were take-home but should be pretty doable with resources provided. Lectures were a good mix between coding and introducing interesting data sets (college admissions, politics).

Good lecturer, attendance is mandatory though. For every class you dont attend its 1% off final grade essentially. Problem sets are easy enough since they are take home. The midterm and final are hard so get those started early instead of turning them in late.

I had a great time in this class. If you've never programmed before, it might be a little more difficult, but even then, you can copy-paste code from the slides for pretty much every assignment and exam (and they're take-home). The datasets and analyses are really well-picked, especially later in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was my second coding course and I thoroughly enjoyed it. I went to almost every class and found Prof Bisbee to be a great lecturer, everything in his lectures prepares you for the problem sets and the exams. Some sets were very hard so I went to TA office hours and they walked me through my code effectively. Encouraged me to continue DS minor.

This class is time consuming. Class is mandatory with quizzes. PAs assigned each week. They aren't difficult, but to do well, you need to put in a good bit of time. There are many opportunities for extra credit, but again, these are often time consuming. Overall more work than I was expecting for an intro class, but it's not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Bisbee is very accommodating - he adjusted the course grading/structure in line with student feedback and really cares about student success. However, his lectures are useless and this course can be very time consuming and frustrating, since you're never taught the syntax of R itself. Exams are take-home and similar to problem sets.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: lectures like a monologue. does not have idea on the actual pace of student learning. types r code way too fast and does not explain them

To be fair Professor Bisbee is a new professor at Vandy. At first the class was challenging because the psets were very long. Towards the end he was very receptive to student feedback and shortened the psets. We never learned a lot of the syntax of R but the class became easy towards the end. Good class to take if you're looking for an easy A.

Professor Bisbee was very receptive to student feedback throughout the semester. He truly cared about making the class accessible to students of all coding backgrounds. Like other reviews have mentioned, I did not like how the class didn't cover the basics of coding in R. Everything else about the course was excellent.

This class sucked on its own, but Prof. Bisbee was very accommodating and made the class a lot better. He was very understanding and kind with everyone and offered chances to make up grades and gain a lot of extra credit. This class wasn't very good at actually teaching you how to code using R, but it's very easy to get an A if you put in effort.
Great professor, lectures were super helpful and very similar to problem sets. Lots of extra credit and support available.

Very understanding of students' feedback; was continually adjusting the course, and made it easier when he got feedback on the difficulty at the beginning of the semester. If anything, the class became super easy near the end, especially the problem sets. You won't regret taking him. A solid choice
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Bisbee is a great lecturer and very knowledgeable about the subject. There is SO much extra credit, lots in each problem set and on the midterm and final. Professor Bisbee is also very kind and open to student feedback.

Professor Binkley and this class are fantastic. This class is by far the most useful class I have taken at Vandy, and everyone else in the class agrees. Professor Binkley walks through everything with you in class and makes everything you need to know very clear. I will be taking more of her classes in the future.

Def one of the harder BUS electives but useful. There's easy weekly HW + 3 long assignments using Excel and data gathering concepts learned in class. Also a midterm and final exam (one is Excel skills test, other is paper exam). Long final group project that took a longgg time. Class is lots of work but rewarding and she's a pretty easy grader.

I loved professor Binkley! She definitely is not the easiest professor at Vanderbilt but she is passionate about accounting and really helps you through the material. Her tests aren't bad if you understand the material but you need to spend time with it to understand the nuance.

Usually wouldn't write one of these but Professor Binkley absolutely deserves one. She's super understanding, has good experience in the business world, and always gives grades back in 1-2 days. The course helps you a ton with excel and the projects were very similar to work I did in my summer internship, so highly recommend for job preparation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: great professor

Dr BJ is a caring professor who wants her students to do well and grow as writers. She allowed us to resubmit our 2 papers and podcast for a higher grade. If you actually take Dr. BJ's feedback and apply it to your resubmissions you'll be set for an A.

I took this first year writing seminar to get an GOOD grade because people said it was easy. She purposefully admitted to scoring our papers lower the first time to force us to resubmit and get the higher grade. I put hours every week leading up to podcast submission and got points taken off for BS.
Can't believe this class lowered my GPA (A-).

Dr. BJ is a caring professor. Easy A as long as you show up in class and do everything as instructed. You're probably not going to learn a lot though, but what would you expect a FYWS to be? Considering its light workload and lenient grading, this could be the best option for FYWS.

ANTH 3890 utilized two professors. BJ added nothing to my experience or academic learning. Perfectly fine human but would've rather had the other professor teach this course alone instead. When disagreements arose in class BJ acted as if she had never taught on a college campus before. When she did talk she had valuable insights - this was rare.

She's great. Take her writing seminar. Content is truly meaningful, and I learned a ton. Two essays (around 4-5 pages each), one podcast, and weekly discussion posts. Very easy load, especially compared to other FYWS. Also gives more than enough extra credit and allows for essay resubmissions for up to 10% boost. Take her!!!

Some reading, but content's interesting so didn't feel like too much "work." Grade dependent on a few assignments, but she gives lots of feedback & allows to resubmit for higher grade. Overall cares about students a lot & teaches with the intention of having students become better thinkers/writers, rather than earning a good grade. Definitely take!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class for a first year writing seminar. Definitely pretty interesting, despite the fact that there is a good bit of reading. Lots of discussions in class. I definitely became a much better writer as a result of the class.

Best FYS class. Climate Change is so prevalent in the world today. Having to take her class won't just open your eyes to the problems we face but will also enhance your writing skills. She is accessible outside class and will give you 1-2 page feedback on your paper. You can also get 10% back on your papers. Books she chose are amazing! Take her!!!

Prof Bjork-James is amazing and clearly cares about her students' wellbeing. She was super open to meeting with students outside of class and the course itself was also super interesting. Weekly readings/discussions were graded easily as well as the book report. The final project is a lot of work but you get plenty of time to do it! 10/10 recommend

Professor Bjork-James is probably one of the nicest professors I've had at Vanderbilt and she cares about her students. There were weekly readings with discussions, but the readings were interesting and pretty easy. It's an easy class about an interesting topic with an interesting final project that's a good distraction from tests and essays.

She is the best ever! She is so clear with grading and gives a ton of extra credit even though her class is super easy to begin with. Also, lots of positive reinforcement from her and she'll listen to what you have to say during discussions very intently. Take her.
Super nice woman who really cares about her students. Loved her. she was totally accessible and was flexible with students. a fair/nice grader
The AI expert who has zero publications on AI—let alone any works in progress. Good luck being a role model for future AI experts. I'd rather talk to my smart vacuum cleaner about AI.

Professor Blocher won't provide a grade breakdown on his syllabus, but know that only the project and the final count towards your overall grade. I turned in 20 assignments over the course of the semester and none were considered in my overall grade. I would have prioritized my time differently had I known, but he intentionally keeps it unclear!

Blocher's class is fine but his style is what makes it awful. He is an EXTREMELY tough grader and doesn't like contrary opinions. Also nothing in the class really matters outside of the final, did great on the group projects and 100s on quizzes and still got a Pass because the final was so strictly graded. Do not take this course with him.

This is a horribly structured class that teaches you how to use ChatGPT to code (you do not even learn how to code). Jesse acts approachable and yet he is extremely condescending and passive aggressive. It truly baffles me how a computer science professor somehow doesn't know how to work a F string and has to consult chatGPT. The worst class ever.
The professor grades the final exam harshly, making it count for 50% of the course grade. He rarely shared genuinely helpful business insights in class.

MGT 6534; awful class if you do not know how to code already, basically teaches you how to use ChatGPT to code. Relatively easy until the final individual project which basically determines your grade in the class regardless of your other grades.

Lots of reading is required!! Attendance and participation in class matters. But I would say Jesse is hard-working and willing to offer help. You can find him whenever you want through slack or email. And for case you wrote, he would carefully read through it and give feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He runs a flipped classroom model with readings before class and exercises in class. I'm not the biggest fan of this model, especially for this class. The class material doesn't do a good job bridging between theory and real life valuation models. Good comprehensive and intuitive explanation of corporate finance theory, however.

(MATH 2820) Dr. Hollingsworth cares about the subject and it shows in his lectures. They are sometimes hard to follow, but only because the content is tough. Problem sets are hard, exams are fair but not easy, but he is willing to help. Classes were poorly attended but going consistently and asking clarifying questions helped me earn my grade.

He is a nice guy but his tests were very unfair in my opinion. Very unclear expectations unless and tests are just a slap in the face. Tells you to study class notes more than the PSETs he gives and then the test is nothing like what he gives you to study. No practice exams or anything for tests. Unless you already know prob/stats I wouldn't take

Took him for 2820. Although class can get kind of awkward due to a lack of participation, he really wants you to learn and it shows. He does a good job of going over material and I thought all assignments/tests were fair. Not getting the hate at all tbh

Professor Hollingsworth is a genuinely nice person and fun to talk to. If you approach the lectures with a positive mindset, they become pretty interesting. You get out of them what you put in. Also, gotta love the guy's shirts.

Homework is not graded for understanding. 
Don't go to his class, just spend class time self studying and making sure homework is correct (according to notes)
