On tests you won't remember a single thing from lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are a genuine waste of time. I couldn't remember a single thing from any one of his lectures on any of the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Professor Hollingsworth is terrible at teaching Calculus. As a student who took pre-calculus in high school, I thought this would be a great starting point to introduce some new calc concepts, but you need prior knowledge!

The way he teaches made it very unfathomable for me. He shouldn't be at this prestigious university for his mediocre teaching.

Poor at teaching but expects everyone to catch on. Deserves to be teaching at a community college, not a top-20 institution. Not a bad person, but regularly acts like it's his first time teaching. Do not take this class if you do not have prior experience in calculus---he says that you dont need experience, but you definitely do if u wanna do well.

Approachable, caring, and funny. Students complain that his lectures only cover the basic concepts, while HW and tests have much more difficult applications. BUT, I think it's hard for a prof to cover everything in a 50 min class, when many students are still stuck on the algebra while others have already taken AP calc. Not a bad option for 1200.

I don't get the negative reviews, he's a really chill professor and you can tell he wants his students to do well. Make sure to actually study pretty regularly, and if you don't understand the concept his office hours is really accessible.

Hollingsworth is an interesting professor. The Class Notes and Homework provided by the math department covered the necessary things for the exams, but he would only cover what HE thought was important. Read the textbook as a supplement because he wouldn't cover some material on the exams, or he would only teach the basics of a topic.

i found myself having to self-teach a lot just bc i feel like hollingsworth's lecture style isn't for me. also, he went a bit fast at times but i think that's just how the course is. if you have to take him, he's a pretty solid option for math 1200.
Class consists of lectures of practice problems, very little teaching of concepts.
The class was really boring and I had to draw heavily on my knowledge from high school calculus to understand the material from the course.
For Math 1200, I think he is a solid professor. He really wants us to be clear of the course concepts. Really nice guy, and definitely recommend to just get the calculus requirement done.
Solid professor, but often struggled to convey certain challenging math concepts. Classwork was not comparable to the homework, and the homework was not comparable to the exam.

This class is legit one of the worst class I've ever taken. Only 3 people show up for class and the professor reads off a slide. This explanations are so bad that you might as well just read the textbook. The textbook does a better job than him. Just show up for the exam, waste of my time.

The class is literally boring though BH is very helpful and responsive person either after class or via email. The content is not hard and the midterms are gradually easier. Totally good to go if you can self study and the only thing is to make a comprehensive cheat sheet that covers the formulas and examples.

He is by far the worst professor I have had at Vandy even though I really enjoy math. He only reads through class notes, which explains why only 4 people show up to class, and not understanding at all. The class average is always 10-15 points below other classes and he still thinks that's a good average.

This was probably my least favorite class ever. It is so poorly taught. The entire class is just formulas that you write down and regurgitate, and Dr. Hollingsworth simply reads them off a slide. He seems like he was no experience teaching. The class itself is incredibly easy but I struggled to motivate myself because it was so boring.

-so disorganized -talks in monotone and goes on so many tangents you never get what the point was -super unclear about grading criteria, few instructions but never gives 100s -he's super excited about what he's talking about but bad at engaging class -notifies about changes in assignments/due dates/class times/expectations randomly
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Carwil was just ok. Really wouldn't take him if you get bored easily. Spews nonsense a bunch.

I struggled a lot with my mental health while I took his class. He was incredibly patient with me and worked with me so I could do well in his class. He is genuinely very caring. He told me he was in my corner and wanted me to succeed. His readings were not the best. He was hard to follow in class at times but very nice professor to work with.
not worth your time

TRUST me when I say skip taking class with BJ. Expectations and deadlines are unclear, he provides no feedback on assignments, and lectures are just a series of dry rambles -- not to mention the fact that there's a ton of reading, almost none of which is relevant. Has a HUGE ego and loves to stroke it, makes his class hard for no reason. Hard pass.
Inconsiderate of your time and assigns things last minute
Extremely dry to the point where lectures become awkward

Unclear grading criteria and does not explain things well during class. He also assigns a ton of reading that takes hours that you really don't need to do. One of the worst and least enjoyable professors in the anthro department tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please take literally ANY of other anthropology professor, the way he teaches is awful and is even extremely unhelpful during office hours. Its pretty clear that he does not care about his students
Gives no feedback at all, rambles on in lectures and class is very disorganized with unclear instructions

Very easy class. About 4 papers and 10 blog posts in total. Heavy readings and he doesn't really explain them so it's easy to get confused but you can probably get by with doing minimal reading. Lectures could get boring at times and awkward if nobody talked. Didn't really know how I was doing until the end because there was barely any feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You'll get as much out of his class as you put in. Most assignments can be done without doing the readings, which there are a lot of. A few essays, a ton of blog posts, and a group panel discussion. Only lectures during class, but you don't need to take any notes. Class would be much better in person, didn't feel at all connected on Zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bjork-James' class forced me to think. Most of the class is based around either exploration of your ideas or analyzing the ideas that influence you and the world around you. The class is easy, but if you want to learn, you will. Furthermore, he genuinely cares about the wellbeing of his students -- he's the kindest professor I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Attendance definitely not mandatory. Could easily write papers without going to class, but it would probably help if you did. Pretty easy class. Really nice guy, but class was a little awkward at times.
Claimed attendance was mandatory but didn't go to class for a month and still made an A. Only major grades are a few papers that are pretty straight forward and graded fairly.

Prof. Bjork-James is a very nice and knowledgeable person, and he knows the topic quite well, but the class can sometimes get slightly boring because of the topics and lack of engagement of the students .
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I enjoyed all of the course content, especially the readings. That beign said, I had no idea how I was doing in the class until finals had already finished up for the semester, and the lectures did not seem to particularly meld with one another. This class was like an anthology, rather than a novel, and I'm still not sure what the moral was.
Awful. Literally the most boring class ever, and the tests are incredibly difficult. Avoid at all costs.

Pretty easy teacher. Really benefitted from going to his office hours. He would literally walk through the entire review sheet with you. A lot of reading but you can skim them and do fine. Essays are easy and is a very lenient grader when it comes to participation and blog posts.
He's a great teacher if you pay attention and is extremely knowledgeable. There's a lot of reading, but if you're interested in the topic, it's not bad. One of my favorite teachers at Vandy.

The class was pretty awkward, participation is supposedly graded but I did fine without saying a word. A lot of reading, try not to fall behind because you'll need to know it for the midterm and final tests and the occasional blog posts. A few papers but they weren't very hard. Carwil is meh.
Class felt very awkward.  Took anthropology expecting an easy A and did not get one.  Don't think I would take him again

Professor Bjork-James is a very nice professor. You can tell that he wants his students to actually understand the material. All we did in class was discuss the readings. It's up to you to participate. There were specific guidelines for papers and study guides for the exams. You're required to write blog posts throughout the semester. Not hard.

Professor Bjork-James's lecture is not bad, though sometimes it's a little boring and I get sleepy. Review sheets are very clear and useful.  Prepare for a lot of readings. Some of them are essential for tests don't skip the reading assignments. Writing assignments are abundant too but rubrics are clear. If you pay efforts an A is not that hard.

Super sweet, accommodating, and easy to learn from. If you want to be a front row demon and learn accounting to pass the CPA exam, she's the goat. If you want to sit in the back and do work for other classes and pass the exams, she's still the goat. Always quick to respond to emails, flexible with deadlines, and wants her students to succeed.

no attendance but she's heavily on participation on guest speakers dates, also in class just give her answers on the practice problems if you had them cuz she's kinda not happy when no one answered her lol. Besides that, she cares a lot about you, ur knowledge and ur grades so easy A if put in at least 70% of ur efforts. love her sm!!!!

4 projects (2 groups and 2 individuals, the last one is replaced for final exam). This semester she changes so no more notecards or cheatsheet but her exam (2 exams) are mimic to the practices questions sheet (a bit longer and long but she allows to come an hour early to start on the exam. Dont skip the reviews class session!

Easiest business elective I've taken thus far. First half of the semester you review basic BUS1300 and have an exam (notecard allowed), second half you do basic budgets and formulas and have an exam. HW is light and graded for completion. Four projects done in class that she gave everyone 100s on. Easy content and chill, sweet professor.

I highly recommend taking this class-- Professor Blandford is a very lenient grader, and most of your grade is completion. Lecture content is very clear and organized, homework is light. She's a great lecturer and lots of what you learn will be relevant to anyone interested in a career in finance or business in general.
This class is such a nice break from my other classes. We do a lot of in class speaking and fun activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class does require work.  Professor Blomquist doesn't make up the syllabus, homework, or the exams.  Those are the same in every section of FREN 1101.  If you stay on top of your work, you'll get a good grade.  She grades pretty easy on most assignments and curves when she can.
Too much for French beginners. She is trying to make you get to a level that is a bit unattainable if you do not put in a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 6+ hours of homework each week. Too advanced for beginners. This wasn't an easy class nor was the professor very helpful.
You have to complete 6 hours of homework each week. The course is too accelerated for French beginners. The professor is not understanding when it comes to difficulty level.

Lisa is great! She is very caring and understanding. Class isn't hard as long as you keep up with your work. She always curves. This class is stress-free and you will learn so much by the end of the semester!
Professor Blomquist has fun classes and I'm amazed at how much I've learned in two semesters.
Prof. Blomquist is the best! Her grading is beyond fair. If you work hard, you will succeed in her class.

Professor Blomquist cares a lot about her students and can be very helpful. It's an easy A if you show up but every class you miss is 0.5% off your final grade so it can add up and lower you to an A- very easily. 94% for an A. She can sometimes nitpick/look over your shoulder to help. It's her style but some might not be comfortable with that.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I like Prof Blomquist, she is very nice and has great lectures that were very helpful in bettering my French. However, there very many times when I felt overwhelmed by the amount of work she had for the class. MindTap was tedious but actually did teach me a lot. Exams/Quizzes were not too difficult though. Final exam is a simple group presentation.

Prof Blomquist is really nice but her feedback sometimes comes off a little rudely but she does genuinely care about you and your French speaking skills. Sometimes the class did start to get heavy because of almost weekly quizzes, frequent homework, and MindTap exercises as well as the two module exams. Overall, a great choice for FREN 1101.

Lisa is one of my best professors. She is so supportive and patient. She always tries her best to help you learn. This class is not so hard as long as you finish all assignments and pay attention to class content.
Dr. Blaha is approachable, and the grading in his class is reasonable. As long as you put a solid amount of effort in, you get rewarded.

He is just the best. Fav prof ever. He makes me look forward to coming to his class every day, and when I was having a bad day, his smile, jokes, and demeanor made it so much better. Wish I could take every class with him. Sad the semester is over.
I did not enjoy this class very much and some of the assignments can be graded to harshly but overall esay A just make sure to attend every class lecture as he takes attendance very seriosuly

Caring, easygoing professor who understands he's teaching core classes and just wants you to get something out of them. Very accessible and always willing to meet. Grading is lenient—just follow the rubrics. There is a textbook most people don't read, but it does supplement lectures, so skipping it can make things confusing.
Looked up in dictionary "the boy", and Blaha came up. He's a one-of-a-kind professor at Vanderbilt. Great as his job and so down to earth. Would take him over and over if I could.
Really easy class and nicest professor ever.
He is the absolute man. Cares about his students. Loved the class.
This class is free
Dr. Blaha is so sweet and cares so much about each student. His lectures can be a little boring but its a very hands on class and he wants everyone to succeed.

Dr. Blaha is not only one of the best professors I have ever met but one of the best people. Even though the topic at hand could be a bit tedious, he always seemed happy to come in at 9am for our section. In regards to the class, show up and do the work and it should be an A course. Genuinely cares for his students and wants them to do well.

Dr. Blaha is probably the nicest professor at Vanderbilt. He is really so kind and understanding and he is always smiling. HOD 2700 was a little boring, but he did his best to make it fun and interactive. The class was an easy A as long as you submit everything on time, go to class and do your best. I would recommend taking HOD 2700 with Blaha!

Professor Blaha is funny and caring! He is super understanding and helpful. I enjoyed the engaging simulator lab classes. He also gives us lots of opportunities to direct our own learning through our policy paper. He is also super understanding and accessible outside classroom. I hope that everyone appreciates Professor Blaha and all that he does!

Best HOD prof, took 1300. Class lectures are knowledgeable and helps for easy papers. He is super helpful too and funny. Lab sessions are interesting and fun. No exams, just go to every class for participation.
this class is actually a joke

Run-of-the-mill intro HOD course. Dr. Blaha has a very chill, easy demeanor, and frequently lets out class 30-45 minutes early. To do the reflections and observations you will need the textbook, but as far as I can tell, the class is graded pretty easily. I know I won't be an HOD major because it is very dull to me, but this class was an easy A.

I love Professor Blaha! He is so kind, funny, and cares about student learning. He is straight forward with his expectations. I recommend taking him! To be honest, you don't really need the textbooks, maybe just the one about the policy roadmap.

He also has a really cute dog that he should bring to class, not just office hours!

Funny dude. Honestly don't see how you won't get an A in this class unless you're a bad writer. But even then, Prof Blaha is insanely understanding. Class is super chill and he's just a genuinely great guy.
Absolute clutch! Take him

Dr. Blaha is the best choice for 2700. He is a great professor and is very nice. He tries to make lectures fun and engaging. As long as you hand in the weekly assignments on time you will do well in this class.

Love this guy. So sweet and made public policy a fun and engaging topic. His assignments are weekly and spaced-out really nicely, not too overwhelming at all. Great person and professor! Take his class!

Take this man if you want the best option for 2700 and also a father figure. This man is so friendly and wonderful and his class is the perfect example of one that gives just the right amount of work without being tedious. All the assignments are easy but also teach you what you need to know for your final paper. Blaha is the GOAT

Dr. Blaha is a great professor. He is genuine, funny, and always brought energy to our 9AM. There are weekly, very straight-forward writing assignments, one midterm that is open-note, and a final policy brief paper + debate. He is super helpful answering any questions and is just a good dude. Do not take anyone else for 2700.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Blaha is the most wonderful Professor I've ever had. He is kind, funny, and fair in his lectures and assignments. He has an emphasis on learning and wants you to be successful. Don't worry about your grade because he makes sure you understand the criteria. Best Professor for 2700 and everybody should take him for any class that they can.

Professor Blaha is the best HOD teacher at the school. There is a lot of material in the class but his lectures are engaging and he uses fun group activities. There are weekly writing assignments that range in difficulty but are easy to get A's on. He is a caring professor that will accommodate your needs as long as you show up to class.

Blaha is awesome! The class content is actually a little complex, but he does a great job walking you through the policy analysis process and stays focused on that for the entire semester. If you meet with him, he'll help you out with grades. He's very animated and funny during lectures and an overall down-to-earth great guy. Highly recommend.
Take him for 2700 if you can, he is really great. Assignments are clearly defined and not too overwhelming. Lectures are interesting and group in-class activities are fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Blaha is the nicest professor I've ever had at Vanderbilt. He is caring, extremely friendly and personable, and loves to crack jokes. The class is set up with lectures and weekly one-page assignments that are extremely doable and graded very leniently. One midterm that he lets the students create. Best option for 2700 and it's not even close.

Not the worst class to take for credit but certainly not the most interesting. Lots of weekly homework. Logic Labs helped to understand the concepts even though the attendance for them is not required. Dr. Boyce clearly cares about her students and is really accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Allows notecards on exams, even the final exam. The homework is also easy and attendance is not required on the logic labs, however the labs assist greatly in understanding the material and provide extra credit. Overall super easy course

Dr. Boyce was an amazing professor and cares about making sure all students understand the material and helps us work through it in class. 1 logic lab a week, but you only have to attend 4 throughout the semester; extra credit if you attend all of them. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was very nice, but the class was terribly boring. The homework feels like busy work and always takes hours to do. They are repetitive and don't really contribute to learning after the first few problems. It is honestly just a waste of time. I honestly don't think there's any reason to take this class. It is too much work for an easy A.
This was a very easy class, and Prof Boyce gives extra credit and note cards for exams to make it even easier. She is nice, caring, and is willing to help you succeed.

Dr. Boyce is an adequate professor but I wouldn't take her class again. Her lecturing style is very rote and she would assign a boatload of homework that wasn't super helpful. She could also be quite rude in face-to-face interactions. However, she did allow us a notecard cheat sheet for exams.

Do not take Dr. Boyce for Logic. Taught myself entirely from the online textbook but attendance is mandatory for some reason. Cold calls. She is disorganized and difficult to follow when the whole point of logic is to simplify. Unfortunate because she's very kind and accessible outside of class but I hated this class baaaaad. Take someone else.

Gen Logic: Very straightforward class. Material is easy as long as you just do the weekly homeworks and don't fall behind. 3 exams and you get a notecard. The material isn't particularly interesting but Boyce is a very caring prof, super understanding.

I thought Dr. Boyce was great, allowed notecards on exams (which made life easy), although her lectures could get pretty boring. All in all, pretty solid class. However, I wouldn't recommend it to a non-philosophy major/minor.

Do not know my final grade, but hopeful it will be an A. She is kind, values participation and she is easy to talk to in office hours. The biggest issue is inconsistent grading and a lack of clear instructions. She is new to Vanderbilt, so this will probably be improved in future semesters. I recommend her, but not the easiest philosophy professor.

Professor Spieth is a very respected businessman and he has lots of high-level experience in business. Professor Spieth understands education and students, making his class very intriguing. He makes sure that every student learns in this class by doing weekly in-class negotiations. The class is not very hard but the most useful class for any major

It is very clear that he is passionate about the content in this course, and it makes students buy into his teaching. The class style is also very engaging, with negotiation simulations in every class. Homework is a maximum of one hour a week and is pretty easy. One of those classes you have to take before graduating from Vanderbilt.
Easily one of the most useful classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. Spieth is an incredible teacher and the class is pretty straightforward. Not that much work. But incredibly value skills learned.

Professor Spieth is super smart, caring, and funny. He genuinely wants students to enjoy his class and learn something valuable. Quizzes are easy if you do the readings, and the in-class negotiations are fun. This is my absolute favorite class; I could not recommend it more. Great for real-life skills even if you are not interested in business.

Professor Spieth was incredible. I learned so much every single week. Each week, we'd talk about the reading, have a quiz, then do an actual negotiation. I genuinely think this was the most I've ever learned in a class. The assignments are easy and the negotiations are completion-based, but there are a lot of them. Easy A if you put in the effort!

Spieth is a great prof, but the grading can be very nit-picky and feedback on presentations is given live. Quizzes and exams aren't too bad if you read the textbook. Very nice guy, and he brings in solid speakers.
This guy is a gem. Wants his students to succeed, very smart, funny, and caring. I cannot recommend his class more. You will also learn a ton about real-life negotiation skills.

Class is viewed as a way to practice your skills, so you're graded on your reflections, not outcomes. It helps alleviate a lot of pressure and grading is really transparent. Participation is MAJOR. There's a group project that is a decent chunk of your grade but not too hard. Overall, really fantastic prof that obviously cares about his students!

loved spieth he's great. learned more in this class than most of my major classes put together. Everyone in the business minor should take a class with him. Also makes an effort to set you up with business connections post college if you ask him

an AMAZING choice for negotiation @ vandy. was not too difficult, but was challenging enough and I learned so much. really fun simulations and discussions. he is one of the only profs I have personally walked up to and thanked after the course was over... really felt that I came out of this class with a newfound skill set!

Great prof and his lectures aren't bad if you're following for all his real life examples and try to participate in discussions. However, he assumes proficiency in both math and econ theory (macro and micro), doesnt explain that stuff at all. Interesting content and very applicable to the real world. Knows his stuff inside out.

Although the content of the class is interesting, Professor Bond is a horrible lecturer and makes everything very difficult to understand. Homework assignments are impossible and goes way beyond the content in the lectures. Class is very test heavy, yet the homeworks don't apply to the tests at all. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very passionate about the topics he teaches! Very accommodating and understanding as well.
this class had its hard spots, but overall was super fun and learned a lot of stuff that is applicable to many different things
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy, but the lectures are super boring and he makes it really difficult to understand the concepts - I ended up having to teach everything to myself. Very test heavy with 3 homework assignments as your only other grades.
Awful lectures. Noting makes sense
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dope dude. Like fr. But class is so tough. Does anyone actually know what's going on in lecture?

Favorite econ class I've taken at Vandy so far, Bond's lectures are really interesting and the textbook is actually not painful to read. Theres not a lot of things you're graded on which means less work overall for the class but also that every test is worth a ton of points, but the grading is really lenient.

If you go to lectures and office hours, this course is equally as hard as other upper-level econ courses with a lot less homework. Bond is a super smart and nice professor. I learned more in this class than I have in pretty much any other econ course here. The tests and problem sets align well with the content of the course.

This is the worst econ elective I have taken at Vanderbilt. Lectures make no sense, problem sets are extremely hard, and PowerPoint slides are useless. There were 3 exams and the averages were pretty low. Would not recommend taking this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beyond boring lecture. entire course is 3 exams (that everyone fails) and 3 hard problem sets (that no one knows how to do). would absolutely never take this class again and i am going to have to take it pass/fail. no one ever knows the answer when he asks the class a question and everyone seems to be very lost. take another elective not this one.

This is a pretty subjective class. You can get solid grades on papers (I got a 96% on the 2 papers we're graded on that's 80% of our grade), but ended up with a B because prof didn't see me as an "avid participant". Super subjective, hard to please.. but not the worst econ prof choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is experienced and well-versed in what he teaches. The class was relevant to the current world situation and an interesting one. He tried very hard to make this class more of a discussion-based class which I appreciated. 2 problem sets that are hard and 2 essays which are graded more leniently than the problem sets. Good choice for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Bond is more of a leader than a teacher. However, I highly recommend him overall. You are graded solely on two problem sets (quite difficult) and 2 papers+presentations. You are given ample time to do the papers (10 pages each) and they are graded quite fairly, so an A is possible. No final which is nice and the lectures aren't tested at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class. The lectures are really good, and he's a nice guy. Problem sets are challenging and you will need to use the textbook, tests are not too difficult. You should attend class, and you will probably learn something. Don't know much about the other 263 professors, but my guess is that Bond is the one to take it with.

Very nice and smart guy. Class could have been more interesting, but it balances out due to the fact that he does not burden you with work. Very reasonable professor. Overall, not imperative to take this class, but I do recommend it.

Professor Bond is a very nice guy who is knowledgeable about his subject and seems to really enjoy teaching, though lectures can be boring.  Be prepared to teach the material to yourself before tests though, since there are hardly any practice problems.
He is what I aspire to be someday.
No Comments
Eric Bond helped me understand economics.  He is the man.

To take Dr. Boles class is both a privilege that every single person regardless of their major should take. This class did not change my semester – it changed my life. Her brilliance and over qualification makes her the best professor I have ever had in my life without a doubt. Do not miss the opportunity I pity those who do not know her.

Dr. Boles is by far my favorite professor at Vanderbilt! I have taken multiple classes from her. She is so knowledgable on her subjects and very accessible outside of class. She is also super caring and hilarious-- she leads class with a deep understanding that college students are human may sometimes be tired or need an assignment date adjusted.

I have taken multiple courses with Dr. Boles. She cares deeply for everyone and is always willing to help in any way she can. Dr. Boles exemplifies what it means to be an incredible instructor, role model, and human being. If you are considering taking any of her courses: do it! You will learn a great deal and have a fun time doing so.

Unbelievably sweet, caring, and accomodating. Easy assignments that are based on your interests and connect back to the real world, no exams during any of the courses I have taken with her. Doesn't dock you for being shy and participating less often.

Really interesting class and important subject matter but definitely at a graduate school level in terms of difficulty. Very complex and abstract discussions and there's an expectation that you show up to each class with enough knowledge to lead discussion. Cool professor but probably hardest Advanced Topical Seminar out there
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jessika is one of the best professors I've had during my undergrad! She has tons of real world experience in pediatric healthcare and incorporates lots of stories into her lectures. Every class is engaging and assignments are all relevant and interesting! She's always available to support you if you need help, are struggling, or want to learn more.

This is the second hardest course I took at Vanderbilt, but also my favorite. It requires a lot more independent thought and figuring things out than typical, which I loved. Bonneton cares about making the course manageable and grades on curves and asks for feedback to accomplish that. Attendance is not mandatory, but you must attend to do well.

Nicolas is a really nice guy and I do think he wants us to do well. I genuinely enjoyed showing up for class and he made it enjoyable. He's pretty funny also. However, the class is incredibly difficult. The exams are very challenging and it is a bit disheartening to walk in knowing you are going to do poorly. Curving is very unclear.
Best econ class ever! Learned a lot and topics are interesting. A lot of extra credits for exams so super easy to get a good grade.

This was definitely the strangest class I've taken—the tests are really hard, but the professor is aware of this and grades VERY nicely. He also makes his assignments out of more than 100 points, so even if you're struggle, just know you'll probably be fine. Lectures sometimes were confusing, but he is funny and makes them interesting.

Bonneton is a super nice guy. With that being said, not the greatest professor. All the content comes from lecture and he moves extremely quickly. The exams and quizzes are very difficult and rely primarily on memorization, a fact that he is well aware of. Avoid, difficulty up there with econometrics for me. Taken 4000 game theory electives easier.

If you are taking this to fulfill CS Project, take another project class as there are much easier/less stressful project classes. If I knew what I knew now, I would've chosen a different project class. You have been warned.

Professor Bodenheimer is quite unhelpful in terms of the projects. All of the work is on the TA's, and they're the only ones who can actually help you. His lectures are boring and completely irrelevant to your project. Unless you have Unity experience and will love working on a game, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Dr. Bodenheimer's Game Engine Design revolved around Godot Engine, with 5 assignments that used Godot's features and modified them in C++. Physics engines, 3d shaders, etc. The content is esoteric at first glance, but the examples in class made them straightforward. The final project was a group game. Great grading with plenty of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bodenheimer was an awful professor through and through. Lectures are wildly irrelevant and useless, completely unrelated to VR development. He is not easy to reach, and is as unpassionate about helping students as he comes across in lecture, and at times is offensively condescending. Rely on the TAs and hope your partners are good. He will NOT help

Lectures are so useless for a project class and they go too fast even when it is related to the actual development of your VR project. Bodenheimer knows less than his TA's and expects you to have everything done despite providing as little resources as he possibly can.

He never respond to any of your emails. I had to email him five times over two months to get him sign some paper. When I finally asked him in person, he told me he usually don't get bothered by students' emails.
His class is a waste of time too.
Bobby, come on... care more about your students...

Wastes a lot of time in lectures, and doesn't have a great overall class schedule for getting students to make games of any quality. That being said, if you have a decent group and self-regulate throughout the semester, you'll get an A without too much hassle.
bobby is clearly not interested in teaching. if you see this bobby, a word of advice, you should just focus on your research and stop teaching. It'll make everyone's life better.

Bodenheimer's reputation is unearned for how he currently is in class. This class was straightforward and assignments were pertinent to the field. Take this class as it's a nice intro course and a relatively easy A, even if you have to work for it. Lots of extra credit.

The projects for this class are really long, but he gives you a few weeks to do them and offers lots of extra credit. Lectures often have nothing to do with the projects but they are pretty interesting and it is obvious that Bobby is passionate about graphics. Definitely take his courses if you are willing to do some work.

Easily one of the least inspiring and disorganized professors I have had at Vanderbilt. Despite the easiness of the class, I was thoroughly disappointed at how little I learned about the field of Scientific Computing. Grading was horribly untimely despite giving us dates when he would finish grading.

Dr. Bodenheimer ended up being the worst professor I had at Vanderbilt. The skills and materials required to be successful on the projects (which are the only grades in the class) are not sufficiently supplied by the lectures, leaving students in the dark. He is a prime example why Vanderbilt's CS department is not up to the caliber it should be.

(Fall 2010) I had Bobby B for the CS module of ES140 - without a doubt the most boring class I've taken. Reading the textbook was required, but the lectures were pulled straight from the book - making attendance pointless. Used software called Alice - one of the most non-user-friendly programs out there. TONS of extra credit though. Easy A.
His graphics class is hard, but it is great.  He is very smart and up to date in the field. The best teacher I've had here.

Bodenheimer is the worst teacher ever.  His class consists of him reading directly off of Powerpoint slides then showing us Disney movies.  He does not teach us anything about how to do the final project, which is worth your whole grade.  Pretty useless in general.
Might as well not go to class because he's not very helpful there.  Same applies for office hours.  He's fairly condescending in most conversations.  Needs to get down off his high horse.

Dr. Bodenheimer, though knowledgable in his field, is quite possibly one of the worst undergrad professors i've ever had.  His smug indifference for his students' understanding of the subject makes even visiting his office hours a loathesome chore.

Bobby B is the absolute worst professor that I've ever had.  His lectures were extemely unhelpful, assignments unreasonable, and worthwhile help outside of class was nonexistant. I've sworn never to give money to Vanderbilt until Bobby B is history.

This is the only class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt where it hurts to attend lecture. All she does is read off the slides word for word and answer every question as "anatomists don't really know the answer." Tests ask questions on super obscure details, so I highly recommend anyone who wants to spend at least a week self-studying anatomy!

Anatomy with Bosma is very average. Most people don't go to class since attendance isn't taken and you basically just have to memorize the slides to do well on the exams. Exam avgs were low 80s. Her lectures aren't that engaging and she isn't as funny as she thinks she is. Overall, not a bad course. The projects are annoying but easy As.

Yes, this class was difficult - but that's kind of the whole point of A&P. Dr. Bosma was a great professor who is very knowledgeable and helpful. Super reasonable class - just put in the work to memorize the information. The class prepared me well for anatomy portions of my dental school curriculum.

Anatomy is just brutal. Her exams are difficult, and minor details that aren't emphasized in class show up on the exam sometimes. Memorize the slides. You can pretty much self-teach yourself this course with the slides tbh.

I think Bosma is a great prof. Her lectures are a lot to absorb and her exams are challenging but you can do well in her courses. Just memorize everything on her slides and do your best to pay attention in class.I didnt find her passive agro like others did I feel some exam questions are on very minor things that she doesn't emphasize much in class

Dr. Bosma is not a professor I would recommend taking A&P with. She expects students to have all information completely memorized (even a decent amt of info not taught in class). It also seems like she isn't very confident on the info she is teaching as she reads off her slides in class. She's very nice and approachable outside of class i will say
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's a little ridiculous how she expects us to memorize every little detail in the course, when all she does is read off very wordy slides; you might want to change your teaching style or provide information that will actually be on the exam

Other reviews touched on this, but her exams are hard, and she grades pretty unreasonably. She tries hard in lecture, but she doesn't teach everything that will be on the exam; she expects you to memorize it a ton and self teach using the textbook for most of the content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is definitely a very passionate and smart lecturer, but Bosma can come off as very passive aggressive when you try to get help after class. She also makes her exams INSANELY difficult with short answer, no one can memorize everything :(

Definitely has a quirky and positive energy but sometimes can come off as passive-aggressive. She can be nitpicky when it comes to spelling and grading on exams. Her exams were almost entirely short answer or fill in the blank and sometimes were really specific topics with so much content covered. Her lectures and slides were also incredibly dense
This woman is insane and I love her
Dr. Bosma is so amazing! She's so funny in lectures and makes Anatomy fun! Get ready for group projects, but she loves creativity put in them! I had a blast taking her class, such an ICON!
Literally the goat. Great subject matter and one of the kindest professors you'll have. I could not recommend her more.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice lady, easy class just make weekly discussion posts.
Best professor ever and class super easy. Highly recommend

Dr. Bruce is super nice and chill. Took her class on Death and Dying in America, and it was mainly book clubs, films in class, and discussion posts. Her stories from past experiences with working in healthcare were really interesting to hear.
She was the homie. Take every class you can with her because they really aren't that hard. Just gotta do the work

Whenever Dr. Bruce teaches a new course, I sign up for it. She is an incredible person and wonderful professor! All of her classes follow a similar basic format with discussion posts, film/book reviews, and in-class activities. You will learn a lot and never feel too stressed. Take her!

I've taken a few classes with Dr. Bruce, and I adore her. It is clear that she cares for her students. The classes are graded on a few papers, book reviews, discussion posts, and attendance. There really is not a ton of work to get done here and minimal stress. The content is super interesting so I didn't even mind doing those written assignments.
Best professor I have ever hard. MILF

Dr. Bruce was wonderful for "Death & Dying" class. She is so down to earth and funny, which makes the heavy subject matter easier to digest. There are no exams in the class which was also really nice. Mostly written assignments, but she is a very lenient grader. Lectures were interesting and made me do a lot of self-reflection. Definitely take!
Dr. Bruce is wonderful! I have taken multiple of her classes, and all of them have been wonderful. I have learned a lot, and she is a very caring person

MHS 3890 classes are super hit or miss, but "Families in Turbulent Times" in Dr. Bruce lands in the "miss" category for me. She is a very nice and very approachable professor, but the class itself is just too much work for what most people taking it expect. Make sure you do every reading because every single sentence is fair game for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Bruce but her "Families in Turbulent Times" course is no joke. Make sure you have a solid understanding of the 50+ pages of reading she assigns each class because pop quizzes get really specific. I feel like I learned a lot but this was one the hardest MHS classes that I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Love love love Dr. Bruce. Took mental health in adolescence with her and the class was structured super well and was very chill. We have modules based on mental illnesses and watch a movie and have a guest speaker for each module. Grades are from a very straightforward 2 page movie review and thank you notes for the speakers.
not a great teacher

Dr Brame is amazing. She is the sweetest professor ever, and I would highly recommend taking her for CORE 1020, just be on time for class. There is a good amount of reading, but every CORE class has the same amount.

Very nice professor with good lectures. Gave learning objectives that were relevant to test material but had harder exams than Dr. Nordman and her final section was also harder. Super nice and accessible outside of class, but get ready to memorize lots of small details and spend a long time on her lecture slides. Would recommend if you are premed

I took her class in conjunction with Dr. Jared Nordman. Her tests are slightly challenging, but if you really study, you can succeed. She is a great teacher, and I heard worse things about other teachers, so I suggest taking her class.

Professor Brame is an amazing professor. Her lectures are very dense in content, but she explains them very well in the slides and has lots of office hours available. Her exams are difficult as they involve application and lots of memorization. I hope to take Dr. Brame's class again in the future.

Pretty great professor. She has effective lectures and explains everything pretty well. She is clearly invested in students learning and wants to help them if you are willing to approaching her. Exams are difficult and very specific on content (expect to apply the information as well as pure memorization) but not unfair.
So happy and friendly! Only tested on material off the slides in class. One test drop and some extra credit for tests.

Such a sweet and caring professor! Always did her best to help us understand the topic, visit her office hours! Difficult class but great STEM professor at Vanderbilt. Averages were higher than the other sections, practice exams available, don't expect clear cut study guides for what will be on the exam

Great lecturer, if you like Bio you'll find it interesting, if you dont like Bio its cooked either way. Tests are tough and require more than just rote memorization, but everything on the test is in the lecture slides (no textbook needed). Her test averages were better than Brody's and the same as Clemons. Very nice and caring person.

Dr. Brame is such a thoughtful and deliberate professor. She was a tough grader but her tests were fair, and it was interesting to learn from her. Definitely better than Nordman (beware!) but so easy to get in touch with.
Tests could be a bit difficult but her lectures and practice tests really prepare you
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best STEM professor I've ever had!!! She puts a lot of effort into her lectures and organizing the material so they are easy to understand, which not a lot of professors do here. Her tests are straightforward, and I always feel very well prepared. I wish I could take more classes with her!
My favorite professor at Vandy! Made genetics so much easier with her course design. Other STEM classes should follow this one's structure. Super personable and reasonable with test questions.

She is nice, but not a good professor at all; much of what is taught in class does not really pertain to the exams at all, as only previous practice tests / problem sets do. I would save yourself before taking this class, as there is no set structure to study.

Dr. Brame was a great professor for biochem. While her and Dr. Nordman's tests were "harder" than other sections, she was very kind, understanding, and willing to help. Grades are based on attendance, quizzes, homework, and 5 exams (but 1 gets dropped). They're difficult so be ready, but she offers lots of help.

Challenging class, but Dr. Brame was excellent. Participate in class and office hours and you'll form an excellent relationship with her. Tests are memorization-heavy (obviously), but no textbook is needed, and she clearly outlines what you need to know. She was also very good at answering questions on the discussion board.
She's a very kind woman and is always willing to help. Her exams are difficult so be prepared

Relies very heavily on her pre-recorded lectures. Many classes felt like there was essentially no teaching at all. Her material is a lot more depth than Dr. Nordman's and is very detail oriented. Know every detail of everything and exams will be okay. Super nice person, just wished she actually taught more instead of relying on old lecture videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brame has pre-recorded lectures, and she has homework to do for biochem. The tests are relatively easy, but the concepts are very difficult for memorization. She holds office hours, and both her and TA Cole get back to you on Brightspace discussion boards quickly. She's such a great, inspirational teacher, and she is up to date on current research.

I loved Dr. Brame - she connected metabolism to clinical examples and I felt that I had a really good understanding of metabolic pathways after taking her section. Do not read the textbook and focus on understanding everything in her lecture videos.

Biochem sucks and is really hard but she is probably your best option. Explains things well and is helpful outside of class. Exams are hard and require you to really understand the material and be able to connect the topics and information.
Biochem is inherently hard, and the tests are harder. Great teacher tho. Really wants to see you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice professor who cares about student learning. Better teacher than Nordman and makes easier tests, however I can see the class being much harder without open notes that we got for COVID-19 semester
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Brame cares about her students; she's a great person. Unfortunately she wasn't such a great professor. She was unorganized. Her teaching style was very different from Dr. Nordman. She expects you to know all the structures, enzymes, reactants, products, and more. I never would've passed the class if it wasn't open note. Unrealistic expectations

Brame is the best! Used case studies to demonstrate concepts we learned and was always looking to clarify any questions we had. Teaches things well the first time but super available to help if you're struggling. Relied a lot less on us memorizing the textbook and more on pathways taught in class. The class IS memorization heavy but it's biochem.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Brame is one of my favorite professors. Not only is she extremely helpful in office hours (more so than the other biochem professors) but she makes it clear what you need to know for exams-only the learning objectives. Her lectures can be confusing at first; however, the tests are straightforward with a few tricky questions.

Dr. Brame teaches a super hard class yet manages to make it both very exciting and easy to grasp. Her teaching style is truly aimed at working at the students' level of knowledge, and she makes it VERY clear what will appear on her tests. TopHat, homework grades, and a generous curve along with her amazing teaching really help everyone survive.
She teaches at a good pace, and gives lots of time for questions. Pretty clear in learning objectives, and what you need to know. Very helpful in office hours, and she's really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Brame. She is my favorite professor ever. I learned so much from her and I will always miss taking her biochemistry course. I took her class two years ago . Still thinking about how great it was!

Dr. B is honestly the sweetest lady ever (she uses name tents). She is often unclear, but all you need to do is raise your hand and ASK. If you ask her, she will not hesitate to answer your question and clarify any details. Her exams were very fair, but the lack of curve at the end is harsh. Make a study group, bc her office hours are inaccessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've never written a ratemyprofessor rating and I'm two years into med school now and wanted to come back because of how grateful I am for Dr. Brame and how she taught her class. It makes biochem in med school basically a breeze because of how well she taught things and how she has you actually understand material. I still reference her ppts!

Her section involves lots of memorizing pathways, but Dr. Brame tries her best to make metabolism exciting. AWESOME at teaching- loved her class interaction (kept me awake in lecture) & practice qs. V caring,accessible, clear w what u need to know for exams in learning objectives (listed on each ppt) & if u ask upfront. Helpful to record lectures

Didn't like Brame at first, but she really grew on me through the semester. Super accessible if you have any questions. Material is definitely really hard, but her test was pretty easy, although the final was kinda insane. Pretty much have to take her anyway since she teaches 2nd half of both sections, but I really like her now. Solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. B is accessible outside of class and really wants students to apply their knowledge. Engaging lectures with challenging material but still doable. Textbook not helpful b/c no answer key. Blindly reviewing lectures is not enough; you have to understand pathway interactions, enzyme cofactors, etc. not explicitly covered. "Select all" MC format.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Brame is a very good teacher. However, content IS hard (it's biochem after all). Make sure you understand integrative metabolism (towards end of lecture). Final is cumulative. She explains material very well during office hours and responds quickly on the Brightspace discussion board. Sometimes, test questions can be interpreted in diff ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: EXTREMELY hard class, but Brame is an excellent teacher and clearly cares about her students. Study constantly because there's a ton of things to memorize - if you try to cram or even study a few days in advance you'll fail.

GREAT lecturer. Makes you think and somehow engages a class of 150 students. I thought her portion was easier than Eichmann's, mostly because she makes the material MUCH easier to understand and breaks it up into manageable chunks. Breaks down any complex ideas into simple terms, and tells you precisely what to know.

Dr. Brame is a great teacher with high expectation. She reviews the material as she goes, asks thoughtful questions, and explains material very well. Yes, you have to memorize a couple of pathways, but this is Vanderbilt. You can handle it. If you come to lectures and pay attention, you can do really well.

Brame's part of biochem is a lot harder than Eichman's.  Memorize EVERYTHING. Tests are really specific.  The final is a cumulative final plus a whole test of new material and just as hard as the midterms.
Full of himself

Doesn't consider opposing ideas to his. Narrow minded. Grades very subjectively. Gives bad feedback. Hard to access outside of class. Has a solid lecturing style and is engaging, but not worth it based on these other things. Would never take again.

The class is structured to make you read and write a lot, but he drops a substantial amount. Professor Byrd is an engaging lecturer, and while he does not track attendance, I would avoid skipping as it will pay off big for the open-note exams. I took for a W US history class and would do it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class isn't easy but so worth it, in my opinion! Since this is a writing class, there are a lot of papers, but if you attend class, you will be fine. He is extremely intelligent and has high expectations for you as his student. I really enjoyed his inspirational lectures. Although this class was difficult, I would do it again.

Petty grader. Unhelpful in feedback. Very knowledgeable in the course and gives good lectures. 3-hour midterm and final are brutal enough, on top of weekly responses is very heavy workload. There are much better history W's.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you are a pre-med or a stem major, I would avoid him only because his class is a lot of work. Weakly reading responses with 200+ pages and a 3 hour mid-term and final was just brutal. Professor Byrd is a genuine caring person who wants you to do well and enjoy history. I found his lectures quite boring but non-stem majors found him interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Byrd was very insightful. He's very passionate about the material he teaches, and this shines through in his lectures. Although the weekly reading responses were a bit of a hassle, the grading was fairly lenient, and he would often give extra credit based on the strength of your response. Absolutely AMAZING class and professor!

Brandon Byrd is an articulate man who really loves what he teaches. Personally, I'm not a history person but if you are, you likely won't be disappointed with the class. Go to class, and actively engage with the material and you'll do great. The course readings and lectures can drag on at times but that's the only real con.

AMAZING lecturer. My class was on African American History to 1865, and his lectures brought the course content alive. His lectures generally covered the whatever was available in the book, but the lectures were far more interesting than the text. Really engaging in class and has good banter with students.

A great professor to have to fulfill your FYWS credit. You can always tell that hes truly engrossed into what hes teaching, and the content that he covers is applicable to real life. Not as many writing assignments as other FYWS classes, but get ready to turn one in at the end of every week. Asks a lot of thought-provoking ?s in class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Caring

reviews.comment: I learned a TON in his class. Very smart and always wants to know about how we feel on any particular topic. Kind of a harsh grader but it honestly helps in the end, and he gives extra credit opportunities to help you out. I don't know what the people below are talking about in terms of his abrasiveness - maybe it depends on the class?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Definitely the best class I took this semester! He's a tough grader and it's more to your benefit than you think. He encourages his students to voice their opinions during discussion and is always helpful after class or in office hours. I'd recommend completing the reading throughly because he may give a pop quiz. Would take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Course is geared towards intellectual history, with a micro focus on concepts of community and identity among enslaved peoples. Dr. Byrd sets very high expectations for students, and has very specific ideas for how writing should be done. He is, however, well-versed in his field and an encouraging presence for those trying to get into the academy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I would say Brandon Byrd did not make my schedule any easier. I found it hard to make good grades in the class even though I was trying my best. I utilized every resource available to me and still received subprime grades. I had As in all my other classes, so I was baffled why I was struggling in an intro level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awful feedback on papers and lack thereof . Makes students stay late after class and makes them late for the next class. Additionally, is condescending towards students during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I have ever had. If he likes you, you'll do well, but he assigns favoritism so weirdly. He is never available outside of class, and he gets defensive when you ask questions. DO NOT TAKE ANYTHING HE TEACHES!! SAVE YOURSELF!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Byrd's class. On Mondays and Wednesdays he would lecture while on Fridays we would go over primary documents in small groups. The lectures were always narrative based, which I found much more interesting than typical history lectures. He's a good speaker. There was a lot of work. Heavy focus on women/race/minorities.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Compared to other history courses I've taken, the grading was pretty lenient but the workload was insane (9 two page response papers, a 5 page essay, a midterm, and a final). He's a nice guy and a decent lecturer, but it was a pretty boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Byrd is an extremely tough grader. If you aren't perfect, you won't do well. Grades include attendance, weekly responses, midterm, and final. The responses are a hassle and you have to read so much to prepare. Midterm and final are ridiculously hard and not enough time. I do not recommend taking this class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Extremely passive-aggressive, both in person and over email, and judgmental when you ask her questions. However, the slides and content were somewhat easy to follow, and the exam questions (calculations section) were similar to the homework. Gives a decent amount of partial credit on exams as well.
Enjoyable lectures, very similar to the textbook. Assignment deadlines are mid-day, so it can be easy to forget. Overall, one of my favorite lectures this semester.

Appears friendly, but very impatient with students, losing her temper or speaking in a patronizing way. Not helpful nor happy when you ask her questions. REFUSES to give an actual answer key for any assignment despite the class being entirely computational. Weekly hw that takes sooo much time. Tests and final very close to hw and class probs tho.
Extremely unkind and judgmental. If you ask a question or do something she doesn't like, she gets extremely angry. Often made me more confused when I asked questions.
Will laugh at you in office hours.
It's a hard class and she def does not make it any less difficult. This is my only every rating for a professor which I guess says something. Made me want to drop chemical engineering.

Yes Professor Rogers can come off as passive aggressive, but I absolutely loved her! Her lectures were easy to follow, and she always graded fairly. She was sometimes difficult to reach outside of class hours. However she was always willing to answer questions during and after class.

Made what could have been a fairly interesting class pretty boring. Lectures consist of her reading slides word for word, sprinkled in with a few TopHat questions graded for participation which is nice. Exams were fairly straightforward with a decent amount of partial credit. Minimal amount of HW.

Most people complain about this class but it is really not bad if you make an effort. If you pay attention during class and GO TO OFFICE HOURS, you will do well. Prof Rogers is very kind and wants to help her students. I learned so much during office hours. She gives lots of partial credit on exams and they are similar to HW. Take Prof Rogers.

Class was somewhat interesting; she was awful to deal with. Was angry in class, adverse to questions,  slides weren't helpful for tests, 10-15 pt. test questions w/ limited partial credit, and passive aggressive in emails. Lab was light but reports were entirely on Word skills. Dreading taking her again. Easy to pass, gotta work for an A.
Such is life.

This woman is the worst professor I have ever had. She gives terrible lectures that cover nothing related to the test and then whines when people ask questions or come to office hours. The crazy thing is the course material isn't even that bad, prof Rogers is just horrific. If you didn't completely fail chemistry I would advise to take chem 2.
The lab is just an excel and word formatting simulator. Lab reports are practically unrelated to the actual course material. Most busy work I've ever had in college.
She complained her students grades on the exam were too high so she made the second one harder.
Dont take her please. She is so bad
She's a nice person but I just don't like her.
I went to office hours and asked her for help on the lab report and she was not eager to help me at all.
I was in the hospital for a fractured cranium after a car accident and she said too bad so sad you fail lab 4
I was sick and she wouldn't let me make up my lab quiz.
RUN!! Do not take this section!
Prof Rogers is great! Make sure you go to office hours. I don't know why other people are so mad.

I like Professor Rogers but I think she's a little strict with grading. Also, she might be copying and pasting grades and feedback because I once got the same grade and same feedback on a lab report as 4 other people I asked….
I watched a couple dudes singing hymns, blues and freedom songs during our class. If this is what freedom entails, then put me back in my chains, oh Lord.

Have you ever had a dream that you're falling and you suddenly jolt up in bed because you hit the ground? This class will do the same with you jolting out of bed because you realized YOU MISSED YOUR 12 PM QUIZ ON A MONDAY THATS WORTH 10%!!!! (Happens every week)
Rogers likes to rail her class's lab grades and make us beg for mercy. I feel much safer with Sean Combs and I'd trust him to teach me material sciences rather than her.
DONT TAKE HER FOR MSE LAB!!!! It'll be your deMiSE.
Steve  rogers is such a bad professor Im gonna transfer dawg

My friends and I have missed 4 quizzes so far because they're set to no notifications and due at a very strange and confusing time of day that's easy to miss. Don't take her if you can. Purposefully sabotages your grades.
Complete L. I'd rather have my boyfriend hit me every day than go to her class because it honestly is pretty much the same but my boyfriend is nicer to look at.

One of the rudest professors I've ever had the displeasure to interact with. I always try to be respectful and polite when interacting with professors but every single one interaction I've had with her she's been unnecessarily rude.

The class itself isn't hard, but her lectures were pretty unhelpful. If you asked Dr. Rogers a question she didn't like, she was often unnecessarily rude in her response. Answers to homeworks, exams, and in-class problems were not posted, so you pretty much have to go to class and/or office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader, and she wouldn't admit any mistakes she made. There is NO rubric for the exam, everthing is grade according to her feeling on your work and her impression on you. But there is no way to avoid her, so make sure you do well in other courses to balance your GPA.
she is extremely strict with deadlines and extensions, denies accommodations straight up.

This class is very straightforward. The tests are all problems from lecture slides or homework, so if you understand those you're chillin'. The labs do take forever, but the lab sessions are low-stress and kinda fun! I am glad I took this over chem. She is sweet, answers emails fast, and is very accessible outside of class.

Very straightforward rubric with straightforward exams and homework. The lectures taught me pretty much everything I needed to know to do the homework and perform well on my exams. Overall great professor and great class, the structure of the course worked well with me!

Dr. Rogers often fails to deliver clear lectures and regularly makes simple errors that students must correct. After falling ill, she forced me to make up the exam at 7 am the following morning, or receive a 0. I was unable to take the exam because I was still sick and received a 0. The class is easy, she is just horrible, avoid her at all costs.
Took Rogers for her Elective and CHBE 2100. I think her rating is low from Material Science, because she is great for the ChemE classes. Highly recommend.

Prof. Rogers has a lot of fluff in her lectures and is extremely unaccommodating for basically any make up assignment, test or absence. On the other hand she is very accessible and tests are very reasonable.

She lectures way too fast and has too much information on slides. I end up spending the whole class trying to keep up on writing things down. If you don't have an iPad, it's more difficult. Things are not explained well and seem unconnected. I had to go through the textbook to piece things together. Considering this, the tests were reasonably easy.

MSE 1500 itself is a fairly easy course. Most straight forward exams I have ever had for a course that strongly mimic the homework problems. There is a lot of content, and the lectures feel extremely overwhelming. You must also attend every day for Top Hat participation. The lab is not great and reports are tedious 5-hour work.

The worst professor I've ever meet at Vanderbilt. The grading is very very harsh. Do not feel surprise if you take 8 hours to do the lab report and still got 50/60 or even worse(if you do not follow her formats, do not feel surprise if you can only get 20/60). If you can avoid this class, do not take it.

Beware of lab reports. She will not answer any of your questions, and is rude in her responses. MSE1500L is just a 1 credit lab course, yet takes up 70% of my school problems and 70% of my time here at Vanderbilt. She is unclear in many ways leaving students constantly in the dark. Good luck.

Not good. Subtle rude remarks when answering questions regarding confusing and unclear labs. Lab reports will be very vague in terms of what to do but will be graded harshly on the smallest of things that were unclear in the assignment. Do not take if possible.

Please ignore these comments. I took her class and was honestly the best class I'm taking this semester. Her midterms are the most straight forward midterms I have ever taken. She is so sweet too, and is willing to help outside office hours. Do not regret taking her. Plus, 35% of the grade is just homework and participation, which are easy 100s.

Really Harsh Professor. Your grade doesn't depend at all on how well you do your experiments, or whether your analysis makes sense, but depends entirely on whether you follow her FORMAT in writing your lab report. You MUST follow his guidline for the lab report, if not, your scores will be really bad.

This is by far the heaviest 1-credit-hour class I have taken so far at Vanderbilt as a Junior. Although the class is mandatory, it has not been optimized and the lab reports are tedious for those unfamiliar with excel projects. If professor Rogers grades your assignment rather than the TA, you should expect no lenience in grading.

For CPP you really don't have a choice, but she's not that bad. She will teach you what you need to know, but it's boring. She also makes a lot of mistakes in her work in class. At the end of the day if you go to class and do all the homework you will get an A.

Not the best lecturer nor the kindest professor, but she does make concepts clear and gives guides on solving problems. She sometimes makes silly mistakes (like simply identifying the limiting reagent) when solving examples, but you don't have any other choice for ChBE 2100, so just go to lectures, do homework and you'll do fine.

While getting an 'A' isn't impossible, the labs for MSE 2205 made me question my major. The first few labs are very time consuming, easily taking around a day to complete from start to finish. Do not procrastinate and never skip lab.

You dedicate 10-15 hours of work for a weekly report and consistently get 10-15 points off for formatting because they want you to. Taking this lab will genuinely hurt your grades in other classes with how much time it demands. I have never met Ms. Rogers but she is very hostile when replying to emails and absurdly unempathetic. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took both MSE 1500L and MSE 2205 with Prof Rogers with identical experiences. Lab reports take 10-12 hours, most of which is busy work. Reports are so convoluted that TAs must do constant Q&A on the class page. Rarely grants extensions & condescending to students. The big takeaway is how to fudge data and write excel formulas. Avoid if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class this semester, and also the most fair class I think I've had. The tests were very straightforward with no trick questions intended to make you crumble; if you can do the homework you can do the test. I was also pleasantly surprised by how quickly Prof. Rogers replied to emails; she always helped out when I needed it!

Not sure why this lab/Rogers gets so much hate but I loved MSE 1500 Lab. I learned a ton about Excel, had a knowledgeable TA, and Prof Rogers responded to my emails almost instantly. Beware, some lab reports took like 10-15 hours, but you have 2 weeks to do them. The classroom sessions also helped solidify calculations/equations from the lecture.

Somehow Prof. Rogers has managed to make MSE1500L the hardest class I've taken at this school. Ridiculous grader - enforces a personal style guideline (which she conveniently NEVER provides in writing) with fascist intent. Don't be surprised if you regularly get 70-80% on reports that are completely correct but don't follow her format preference...

I couldn't tell you a thing about Dr. Rogers' personal life, and she doesn't know anything about me other than my name. But all things considered, she had a very clear, fair grading policy (with generous extra credit); her exams covered exactly what was mentioned in lecture and on homework problems, so there weren't any surprises. Fair class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I certainly wasn't a fan from the start, but Dr. Rogers teaches content well and her lectures are well formatted. While she can easily come off as harsh to students, she isn't trying to, and being nice to her goes a long way. If you have a choice for CPP, this is certainly the better choice. Gives LOTS of partial credit on exams.
Do not take. Very unwilling to help you outside of class.

Terrible professor. Unwilling to work with her students *at best*. Thankfully she's been relegated to labs, however, the apparent lack of oversight led to massive disparities in lab quality between sections. I would avoid anything spearheaded by her if given the opportunity, as she seems utterly uncaring and unwilling to put in any work herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Rogers can sound cold and sarcastic whilst teaching and in office hours. She does not seem particularly caring towards the students. The textbook material and its examples are much more important than the lecture material as the lectures are basically Rogers showing equations.

She's not even a chemical engineer apparently. Her classes are very disorganized and she's extremely unavailable to her students. There have been so many instances where she made a mistake but would rather send her students on a goose chase than just fix and upload a new one to brightspace.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rogers was a pretty good professor- cpp is a tough class but she explained things well if you asked her directly. I didn't get a lot out of lectures and in class stuff but she was helpful during office hours
GET OUT. IF YOU TAKE HER YOU'LL HAVE A HORRIBLE SEMESTER. BY AND FAR WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE HAD

This class was extremely difficult which is why I am giving her a 3 for the rating.
