If she expects this much from her students she should have said so in the beginning and she should have more practice material prepared. In terms of lectures, I think Professor Rogers is great. She really explains the material clearly and defines each step.

Rogers was ok for Material Science. The course itself is kinda boring but she doesn't try to make it interesting or engage her students--most people did other homework during lectures. There is only one homework assignment per week, three tests, and a final. The tests weren't too difficult as long as you know the material. Not difficult to do well.

Rogers might actually be the worst professor I've ever had. Her lectures made zero sense and it was really hard to tell what in the lectures we actually needed to know. She is also extremely unhelpful in office hours and often can't even answer my questions. I wouldn't have even shown up to class if she didn't use Top Hat so much.

I had Prof Rogers for Material Science, and had a nice time in her class. I think she does a solid job explaining the material and the homework never got out of hand. Likes to do Top Hot questions in class so you need to show up. She can be intimidating to approach but isn't mean to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ignore these reviews. She speaks clearly and precisely, doesnt mind answering questions or going over old material, no matter how dumb the question is. Her tests are very fairly written, accurately accessing content from class and homework. Shes the sweetest lady ever, I want her as my mom. Shes very calm, and shes always willing to help out!

Prof Rogers is terrible. Makes fairly simple content extremely difficult and is terrible at explaining things intuitively. She's extremely condescending and doesn't care about having her students succeed . I got an A in gen chem and this class was nearly impossible. Definitely one of the worst professors at Vandy.

There is a lot of content in each lecture and it's tough to keep up. Class time is often used to work through problems similar to homework and exam questions. Multiple-choice conceptual questions are also discussed in class and often re-used on the weekly quizzes or midterms. Not the best teacher, but excellent at discussing problems/solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rogers is awful at holding down a classroom. Definitely takes favorites. Constantly condescending, and very hostile. She rarely actually answers questions, most of the time she just dodges them, and then gets angry when students are confused. Sometimes outside of class she can be helpful but you have to be very careful how you approach her.

Rogers does not make it clear what she expects of you. Especially on the tests and quizzes. There were so many quizzes that I failed because it was one line on a lecture of 30 slides the answer was from. Also she doesn't provide the reference sheet ahead of time and honestly does not make sense why not. Do not recommend.

I dont understand why Rogers gets so much hate. Her lectures are very to the point and you can pay attention or not, she doesnt care. Homework is huge % of grade and is super easy. Tests are predictable. She ends lecture like 30 mins early everyday. Highly recommend if you want an easy class and you prioritize doing well over learning the material.

She was very unclear on what material would be on exams. When someone would ask, she would give a snarky response. It was extremely unclear and it caused a lot of confusion for many students. Also, everyone cheats on quizzes which are worth 15% of your whole grade! So if you have some morals, then your quiz grade is below average and youre screwed.

She is really boring and a very poor lecturer. She just reads off the lecture slides which often have mistakes on them. When she is solving example problems she can't remember how to do them and often needs help solving them.
Dr. Rogers is not good. She is rarely ever helpful and seems to not have a firm grasp of the content she is teaching. Furthermore she is often rude and condescending.
Straightforward class. Lecture is bland and material is self-teachable. Prof is not very helpful and will mostly likely refer you to textbook or lecture slides for any questions.

Dr. Rogers is overall not a great professor; she oftentimes cannot seem to communicate what she wants you to know or what her tests and quizzes will cover. The online aspect of the class is extremely intensive and almost unrelated to what you learn in the actual class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The lectures were too boring for me to ever go. However, prof rodgers has very fair tests that can be passed easily as long as you go to class. i recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Inside, I think she's a nice person, but there's something missing from her in lectures. Doesn't quite have the ability to explain things conceptually / intuitively. Literal mountains of homework. Exams very long and difficult. Although you'll come out of the class learning what you needed to learn, the class itself is a frustrating struggle.

Her lectures are boring and discourage student engagement. Nobody asks questions because we all know she can't answer them. Tests are easy to make up for how little of the content is actually absorbed.

She is not familiar with the materials and can not explain concepts or answer questions clearly. All she tries to do is going through the powerpoint, by reading the text printed on handouts she provides, so the lectures are very boring and you won't learn much. There is no deriveation so it's more about memorizing. Wouldn't recommend.

Teaching is just kinda average. She goes over problems in class but tends to focus on concepts more than strategies and sometimes glosses over essential details assuming student will be able to connect the dots. Problem sets and quizzes weekly,and tests are like harder versions of those two.
not helpful at all... many explanations are based on facts and not on why or how those facts came about. Sarcastic and rude.

Easy class for ChE, tests are short so dont mess up or you lose a lot of points. HWs and quizzes are simple and straight from the notes. Final project was graded rather arbitrarily and she refuses to give anyone a 100. She isnt very enthusiastic about the content either

ChBe 161 w Mrs Rogers  you have to put in effort to do well in. Three tests each with simple-ish problems based on the homework. Bi-weekly quizzes. Final is really tough, not very similiar to the tests, its based on the problem solving techniques that you pick up if  you DO THE HOMEWORK   slowlyadvance & dont look solutions. This is key to class.

Unlike some other CHBE professors, Rogers doesn't seem to know the material like the back of her hand. She is still clear and helpful. She works several examples in class, and those + the homework are very similar to the exams. Exams are open book + note sheet and were all very fair/straightforward. Basic weekly quizzes.
She's not really helpful but the class is too easy.
it was actually listed as es 140, i think i sat in the wrong class

Clear & helpful professor, but very dull subject matter.  Lots of work involved, but homework is done in assigned groups making it bearable.  Tests aren't hard, but you have to be moving FAST to get them done in time.
Was not helpful in class at all. Mandatory attendance. Very easy but not fun nor do you learn much.

Nice professor, tries her best to engage the class, although the material itself is pretty boring (due to structured curriculum).  Don't back out of you have her for your chem module, she's pretty decent about grades, and the amount of work is bearable.
very good teacher! enjoyed her class and everyone i talked to liked her as well!
tough subject yes, but she tries her best. not a great teacher but she makes it up by giving easy tests. the kids who did bad probably deserved it.
She had absolutely no interest in teaching the class and really didn't want to be there.  She was sarcastic to students and went over the material very vaguely.

This class was extremely difficult, but Dr. Buchanan was an incredible lecturer. Problem sets are very time consuming, but worth 20% of grade. Exams are often near impossible, but she provides a generous curve (an 80 is an A-). In addition, she provided an extra credit opportunity for the class after an exam average was lower than expected.
Buchanan is clearly very smart and knows what she is talking about, and her lectures and slides are organized and clear. BUT if you don't have any of the math background, prepare to go through war.
consider doing some easier, like becoming a billionaire.

PChem is the hardest class I've ever taken, but Dr. B is an amazing professor. Extremely helpful in office hours and makes additional time if needed. Homeworks are hard but challenge you to think about the material critically. Tests are unbelievably, brutally difficult (almost to the point of discouragement) but the whole class is curved by 10 pts.

P-chem by nature is really difficult, but Dr. Buchanan is iconic. She is super helpful in office hours and explains concepts well, just don't be afraid to ask questions. Start homework early and really try to understand it to do well on tests, which are pretty difficult, but fair. There is a 10+ point curve for the class overall.

This class was single handedly the worst experience I've had at Vanderbilt. A person after reading through the second exam got up and left and never returned. Exams are '50 minutes long' and she says she can do them in 14 minutes but I call cap as it is physically impossible, class average was a 52 with a 17 point standard deviation.

I love Dr. B with my whole heart. She's by far my favorite prof I've had so far, and while getting through this class was the hardest thing I've ever done, I somehow still looked forward to going to class, just because of how much she made me love chemistry. She is so easy to talk to in office hours and genuinely helpful. Can't recommend enough.

Buchanan is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt hands down. However, to fellow Chemistry majors: quantum is truly a math class, not a chem class. If you don't have a strong math background, you will need SIGNIFICANT help from the engineers to have a fighting chance. Multivariable should be required - if you haven't taken it, better take 3310.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Buchanan is an amazing professor. The class material is really tough, but she does a great job explaining everything and guiding you from scratch. Great logic and teaching. She also sincerely cares about her student so if you reach out for help she's always there. Exams are tough (avergae around 70) but predictable. Textbooks are kind of useless.

You will need to read the book and listen to lectures 3 times over to barely follow, and she jumps from the book and her own material making it more difficult that it already is. She is one of those 'genius' people that assumes you know everything and is too stubborn to change small aspects in class during this pandemic so that students can relax.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The first third of the course is about kinetics (which was deceivingly easy), but the rest of the material is all about quantum mechanics. Since I have a strong math background, the class wasn't conceptially difficult but occasionally cringy watching Dr. Buchanan trying to squeeze differential equations and linear algebra into 50-minute lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Pro: explains material very well, accessible outside of class, cares about students, wants you to succeed, straightforward Con: material is incredibly difficult, tests are hard and all open-ended questions, homework is difficult, textbook is not really helpful, little resources for practice questions provided
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Buchanan is amazing. The material in quantum is crazy hard, but she explains it really well. She also really cares about her students and is willing to spend a lot of time with you outside of class. Make sure to go to office hours and get a good grade on all the homework. It's worth more of your final grade than most people realize.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's new at Vanderbilt but is one of the most caring and dedicated professors I have ever seen. Quantum mechanics was a pain in the ass and class average was around 50-60. The material was obviously hard, but she's very accessible outside of class and held many review sessions that are CRUCIAL if you want to do well. Would take her again anytime.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Buchanan was teaching for her first time so the test averages were really hard. I attribute that to the difficulty of quantum mechanics because I believe she does an excellent job trying to teach it to you. She cares so much and goes through detailed explanations of concepts. Those tests and homeworks are v hard, but if you talk you can do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Students say SPAN 3303 is boring, but not with Bunsen. His lectures are engaging, and I began appreciating the subject material. He wants you to participate, so as long as you prepare the readings and put some effort into papers, that's all that matters. He doesn't log grades, but if you do what you're supposed to, you'll get an A no problem.

Cardenas is my favorite professor I've taken at Vanderbilt, and not just in the Spanish department. He's incredibly kind and funny and knows the material he teaches like the back of his hand. You can see his passion for the subject while he lectures. I didn't envision myself taking another Spanish literature course, but he makes it worth it.

Great professor! Honestly did not expect too much out of students, but attendance and participation was definitely considered for the grade. As long as you participate in conversation and talk about readings you'll be perfectly fine!

If you have to take 3303, def take this section! Prof. Cardenas-Bunsen was funny, engaging, and encouraging. He truly cares for each and every student. I was hesitant to take this course, but I found myself enjoying the readings. This may not have been if not for C-B. Due to the small class size, expect to participate in every class multiple times.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Cardenas is incredibly kind. Lectures are a tad boring at times but just show up and follow instructions and you'll get an A.

My favorite Spanish professor that I've had at Vanderbilt! Classes can get boring but are definitely way more interesting if you at least skim the readings. He is such a wonderful professor who cares so much about his students and you can tell he is so knowledgable about what he is teaching.

Professor Bunsen's a gem, he's engaging with lectures and makes some tough readings clear and interesting in class and connects the works back to other art and history. Great guy, it's evident he really cares about his students and is passionate about the material. Flexible with assignment dates. Only graded by a few papers. 10/10 recommend.

Such a kind professor who cares about the material so much. He is also very funny. Lectures can be a bit boring, but he does not grade harshly at all. If you do the papers on time and participate now and then you should get an A. Definitely will be taking one of his classes again.
Great professor, easy grader. Class discussions were at times difficult to follow but very accessible. Readings were also dry at times, but for a literature class this is definetely a great option.

Professor Cardenas is truly one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Though the subject seems dry & pretty history-heavy at times, he truly knows his stuff and will always be willing to lend a helping hand. Reading assignments every class are mapped out on the syllabus so you know what's coming, very doable class overall.

One of the best Spanish professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He is incredibly accommodating and clearly cares a lot about the course material. I was dreading taking Spanish Literature, but I really enjoyed the class. You'll be reading a lot, but there are only 5 written assignments (2-4 pages), so not a heavy workload.

Professor Cárdenas-Bunsen is one of my favorite Spanish literature professors at Vanderbilt. He is an exceptionally well-read, attentive, and insightful academic who will help you learn about Spanish and Spanish-American literature. There is plenty of reading, but all of it is carefully chosen and truly worth it. I will miss being in his class.

Great class for spanish lit. Most of the readings are online and actually interesting. Graded by 2 papers and participation. Super engaging and e-mails questions ahead of time so it's easy to prepare for class. Very clear about papers and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: He's probably the best Spanish professor I've had at Vanderbilt- he explains the concepts well, genuinely passionate about what he teaches, and is a very nice grader. Would recommend taking- he really fosters a really great class dynamic and highlights untold stories of latin america!

Bunsen is a really nice professor and gives a pretty fair amount of work. Small reading and a few questions prepared for each class. Occasional longer homework assignments, with 2 small exams that aren't difficult to prepare for and a final paper. Not a tough grader, just show up to class prepared and participate and you will earn a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a nice and intelligent professor.
Really sweet guy, just teaching a terribly boring subject. Not too much work, lenient grader

He is really nice but bro is ancient. He really needs a TA because he takes forever to grade things and gives minimal feedback. He constantly forgets about assignments and just makes up the classes as he goes. He is nice and funny but definitely has favorites and is biased towards Arab people.

There is no structure to this class. No syllabus, prof assigns tests and projects with less than a week's notice, and he will not clarify what tests are on until the day before the test (he has done this three times so far this semester). He never fully taught the alphabet and moved straight to advanced phrases without teaching basic vocab.

Dr. Bushra is rude if you don't understand the material or if you need him to reexplain. He is so unorganized, not tech savvy, and rarely teaches grammar. It is so difficult to feel welcomed in his class and productively learn Arabic without an outside tutor. I am dropping my minor, and I know many who have also dropped because of him.

Professor Bushra is very helpful in class, makes sure everyone feels welcome, and is highly knowledgable on Arabic language and Islam. However, it was unclear at the beginning of the semester what the assignments would be, which led to stress regarding how we would be graded - luckily in the end he was actually very fair and we learned a lot.

Bushra is a caring professor, and he truly wants you to succeed. Besides studying for quizzes and tests, homework exclusively consists of biweekly online assignments. Understanding when it comes to absences and doesn't have strict quota. However, he is disorganized and class can be boring.

Dr. Bushra is the best Arabic professor there is. He calls on everyone in class, which is a bit scary at first, but you get used to it and it helps you learn the material. His tests and quizzes are very straight forward and he has the best sense of humor and demeanor. You will regret not taking his class.
Busha is the best teacher ever - he really wants you to succeed (really willing to help outside of class) and makes class fun and interesting
Best professor ever!!
Great class to take.  Highly recommended.
Prof. Bushra is a good guy. But he is not answering the emails. I can say he is very lazy and not organized. You may end up with a B if you do minimal work. easy grader!
genius, amazing, best guy ever, so smart, really wants you to suceed, even if you get everything wrong youll still get a b for trying
Awesome professor who is very reasonable. If you try you will learn something and get an A. He is always there if you need help.
I <3 Professor Bushra! He is sooo nice. Take his class, he will make you laugh! =)

I think Bushra is a GREAT teacher. True his is not so clear sometimes, but he is extreemly helpfull and will see you at any time of the day. Arabic is a tough language but if you go to his office hours he will help you out b/c he knows you are trying. TAKE THIS CLASS

Profesor Chase and this class get way too much hate. The class is relatively easy if you just pay attention in the lectures. Her lectures are interesting and shes engaging, lots of fun material and stories. I will say the grading on essays is a little weird and the tests are timed, points taken off for small mistakes and questions can be confusing.

Extremely stressful for a music class. Tests are take-home but extremely rushed, so you need to take great notes. The grader is very picky about what earns full credit. Papers are graded super harshly, and they don't really give feedback explaining the grade, so it's hard to know what to improve. Be prepared to spend more time than expected.

Participation is mandatory. Class isn't that hard the tests are exactly like the notes. Personally didn't enjoy the teaching style, took a long time for tests to get back which was frustrating. Pretty easy to get a good grade if you go to class.

Now that I've seen the other rock professors, I know I was too harsh on Dr. Chase. Her class was super easy and we never had any hw and barely any assignments. She taught history from an unbiased POV and hit all the interesting tea. She made us listen to songs that were catchy and left an impact on me. The new professor is terrible compared to her.

Prof. Chase was actually a pretty okay prof. She has a bit of a temper. The online exams were pretty extremely rushed despite getting 2 hours to take them. With that being said, the class was pretty easy. Tips to succeed: Transfer all of your notes to a google docs to be able to search up answers during test and don't waste time on the hw readings.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun content but way too much work for an MUSL course. Tests involve recognizing songs, memorizing artists, producers, managers, and historical backgrounds. You also loose points for spelling which didn't help. She also seemed to not be too interested in the content. And spent too much time talking about hip hop in a rock class.

I enjoyed Dr. Chase's class; it was refreshing as a STEM major. Make sure to be in class every day because she sometimes does attendance checks and top hat quizzes. Also, make sure to write all the notes in addition to conversations/details because those will appear on the exams. Exams are open note & non-cumulative (research paper/ extra credit)

I took this class so you don't have to. Please don't make the same mistake. The grading was very subjective and my first orgo exam had the same average as the first test for this class. Explain to me how that makes sense. But I guess everything happens for a reason, and now I know that my reason for taking this class is saving all of you from it.

Don't waste an elective on this, it's too much work and no fun for a basic level class. They need to restructure the grading or get a different professor because I don't think a c average on an exam for a non stem class is acceptable.

The exams require exact memorization, and if you don't interpret the material as she expects, you lose points. The grading is inconsistent, and there's no clear rubric. As a stem major, this was the most time consuming class I took. It sucked the fun out of the subject. She is also unreachable and very condescending outside of class.

Go to every class and take notes: WORD FOR WORD, of the slides. Tests are online & open note, and the final is NOT cumulative. There are one or two papers, but it's all about music, so it's not horrible. If you can attend every class and stay awake... you're good! No technology. Extra credit available. Try to participate to avoid her attitude.

People (and myself) don't like her personality...she just yearns for class participation. You DO have to study for her exams... pure memorization of LITTLE details. MUST come to class and MUST take notes...but the content is fun. For me, this was a good break from STEM classes...but you still have to study to do well.

Dont take this class if you're looking for an easy axel. It used to be with the previous prof. not with Chase. Slides are insanely dense almost like a chemistry course. Slides are not posted only available in class. Studying is reliant on your notes and tests are okay but be expected to be asked very deep rooted questions based on slides.Overall No

DO NOT BRING YOUR LAPTOP TO CLASS: she WILL rant about how she is the only woman of color you will ever have as a professor at Vanderbilt and reprimand you for not respecting her the same as her white counterparts. She also does not give feedback on papers, she just grades them, and the tests are INTENSE. But they're online, so just prep well!
God. It's hard to even summon the words to describe this class. Tests are SO HARD. How am I supposed to memorize so many things. I can't. dont do this to yourself

I had her for hip hop and the class was fine because all exams were open note. But DO NOT take rock music with her. Does not care about the content, and exams are impossible because there is so much to memorize. Papers are also a pain. This is just way too hard for a music class that should be for enjoyment.

Dr. Chase is passionate about what she teaches and returns the respect you show to her. Exams are open note+not cumulative. You'll do well if you pay attention in lecture.
They hire graders to look at your exams. If you miss a lot of points, be diligent about asking Dr. Chase about it so 1. you can see what you did wrong or 2. she can look it over.

Avoid taking at all costs. It might look fun and easy but it is not. Content is fine and kind of interesting. Professor Chase is terrible, the tests are terrible, the grading is terrible. Class needs a complete rework because it has potential. Please listen to my advice when I tell you that this is NOT the easy/chill humanities credit you think

Do not take. All bad reviews are 100% true. Do not make my mistake and ignore them. Rude, inaccessible outside of class, arbitrary grading that takes months, not a fun class at all. Would not recommend to anyone.

she might be the worst professor ive had at Vanderbilt. 
I was stripped from my sleep because of her insane memorization 
I was stripped from my happiness because she is so painful to listen to
I was stripped of my GPA because she makes the tests so impossibly hard 
be warned.

Very fun class I loved it, and Professor Chase is so interesting. The random attendance and no technology are kinda annoying, but it's okay because the course material makes up for it. I'm sad we never touched on Hamilton though. Whoever is the grader is insane and very picky when you miss the tiniest bit of information in an essay.

Prof. Chase is honestly just rude. Not accessible before/during/after class and is extremely passive-aggressive toward her students. Not understanding and quite honestly judgemental. Doesn't post lecture slides, takes random attendance, no technology. If you want a professor that cares, don't take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: OH MY GOD LITTLE RICHARD UGGGHHH I LOVE LITTLE RICHARD OH MY GOD I SAW HIM ONCE YOU KNOW TUTTII FRUTTTIII OHHH RUUDIIIIIII

She's a bit on the spectrum but that's ok. I think she's a little harsh and moody though (cancels or ends class when she doesn't feel like doing her job). Make sure to check out her Highland Quad 2011 spotify playlist though.
Her history of rock class is literal hell for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing class. 2 papers, 1 midterm, 4 quizzes, and a final. All assessments open note. No technology is allowed in class, so you have to handwrite notes and type them up after class. Beware that the graduate grader grades the papers (NOT the professor or TA), but other than that super fun class even tho prof Chase was not always excited to be there

Professor Chase is definitely a bit odd - makes it very clear that she does not care about her students in a way that is surprisingly honest. She  gave up on the last two weeks of class because she didn't want to be there (openly stated). The content is pretty interesting. The essays are graded more harshly than in any of my English major classes

Terrible instructor. Her lectures were outright awful. The amount of content that is required to know for the exams is more than my organic chemistry class, how is this possible? Everyone around me had to cheat. This is not what a 1650 level MUSIC class should be like. She kind of just gave up at the end, honestly, with this class, I would too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She makes rock music very woke in a way that is offputting to students who just want a fun class. Also weirdly tough grading on the essays. She taught hip hop and rap in the later part of the year and ignored actual rock music for some reason. Always in a bad mood and will make it your problem. No phones/laptops. She's awful compared to Gunderman

Class is copying off powerpoint (not posted) and listening to music. No homework and open note tests. 2 papers, 2 exams and 4 quizzes but pretty hard. Points taken off papers for things not on rubric. Prof would be passive aggressive abt lack of participation, but otherwise ok. Pretty low effort/fun class but not as easy to get high grade as hoped.

content: memorize slides to ace exams, mandatory attendance and she is NOT remorseful, no essay rubric, lecture slides are never posted

professor: I can't tell if she enjoys teaching or if she can't tolerate students, which explains condescending tone and limited student participation. You feel like an inconvenience when asking her a question.

Should be an interesting course, but she makes it all memorization because of the slides that she just reads off of. Not posting them isn't even the issue, it's the fact that she can't teach the material and just says what she wants to say and expects us to memorize all of that.

Professor Chase is a solid professor who has incredibly knowledgable in her field. This class was so easy. Just make sure you take notes in class because she doesn't post her lectures online. There's two tests (open note), a 5 page research paper, and a final. Listened to tons of cool music. Can be a little passive aggressive but super nice overall

brother, go to class for this one. you have to. take notes and pay attention and you will be fine, but i would rec taking history of rock with the other prof that teaches this. she gives out the test bank and she lets you take notes on your laptop. 
sometimes she would be a bit passive aggressive but understandable bc no one pays attention

Kind person, but the grading is tough... instruction of the quiz are sometimes unclear, paper mostly rely on outside-class resources, tests are notes needed,  can be very hard if you are not fully concentrate in class.
I really hope she's still single I'd love to live in Gillette with her ;)

I brought one of my out-of-state psych major friends to this class and she pointed out that Dr. Chase might be on the autism spectrum, so don't be too creeped out when she gets a little weird sometimes. I really liked this class and it's basically take notes and study and you'll have an A; do nothing and you'll get an F-.

I loved this class, definitely take if you are interested in the music industry or even if you just want an easy history credit. Professor Chase a great teacher and tells her students how to succeed from the beginning. As long as you show up to class (she takes random attendance) and take good notes, you will do great!
Although the class material is not very hard, attendance is mandatory (random attendance check) and the grader grades very strictly, taking many points off when grading the essays and midterms.

She is unreasonable and annoying. She constantly tries to be funny, but she is not. No electronics are allowed. Mandatory attendance. Take the class, but be prepared to have an insufferable professor.

Professor Chase is great. The class isn't very hard because all you have to do is copy her slides (which she does NOT post online) and then the tests are pretty easy. We listened to a lot of cool music and learned about really interesting history. There was minimal homework and the class was really fun. Highly recommend.

I think Professor Chase is definitely an energetic/nice prof. However, there are very few assignments/grades, so you have to do well on each one or else you are screwed. Furthermore, the midterms can be graded in a very nitpicky way sometimes, taking off points for small details. Also the quizzes make you remember the most random details.

Tests are online and are pretty easy. Need to attend class to take notes since she doesn't post slides online. Papers are not too difficult either as long as you finish it a little earlier and have her look over it.

This is probably my favorite class I've taken in college. Prof Chase makes lectures super interesting, and I feel like I learned a lot! Not too many readings, but make sure you do them. Random attendance quizzes throughout the semester, three exams that are mostly open ended, and one essay. As long as you pay attention in class, you should do great
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Chase is a decent professor, but her bluntness can seem rude. Major assignments are graded by an unresponsive and overly nitpicky outside source, impacting grades. An A is possible, but requires some work due to the random bits of knowledge that show up on quizzes/exams. Take good notes, because slides are NEVER posted for any reaon. No technology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're looking for a really cool professor who is incredibly knowledgeable in her field, Dr. Chase is the one for you. She communicates expectations very clearly, and if you attend class and take decent notes, you'll be fine. Do what she says, because she tells students exactly what to do to set themselves up for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting lectures, but make sure to get all your notes because reading and listening quizzes will focus on really niche topics. If you don't like your grade, Chase is usually pretty sympathetic; don't be afraid to ask for a better score.

Professor Chase is not bad. Her class can be entertaining and interesting. I would recommend it for a humanities credit. Some assignments are annoying but it is nothing difficult. 4 quizzes + 2 papers + midterm and final
fun prof for History of Rock; take the class if you need HCA credit; we just listened to music and talked about amazing artists; go to review sessions; easy grading for tests and papers
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor but more importantly a super easy class. If you go to every lecture and take decent notes you'll be completely fine. Two exams, a paper, and a final comprise the entire grading but they're graded very generously. GO TO LECTURE, notes/ppts are not posted online for any reason ever.

Dr. Chase is nice and seems down-to-earth, but is a lil snippy at times.
1 paper, 2 exams + 1 final, all graded very generously. The class content is interesting, and we listened to a lot of different music (not just hip-hop). Make sure to attend every class, because notes/PPT will not be available ever. Just take good notes and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is very easy. If you're interested in rock music, this often has nothing to do with it, so don't get your hopes up.

Pretty light class. Notes have to be taken on paper. Some of it is interesting. Get to listen to music which is cool. She's kind of annoying though and condescending. Very strict about deadlines, which is understandable, but she comes across it in a very rude manner.

Her courses for AXLE requirements are majorly overrated. The class has very interesting content, but the Tuesday/ Thursday class feels like it's 4 hours long. Professor Chase has an unusual vibe that's kind of mean and the test grades in this class are way too nitpicky considering the course content. Im taking another class of hers tho #hypocrite

Chill class; easy A given you go to class and take notes. Tests (including the final) are open note and easy if you do any amount of review beforehand, and theres 1 paper the whole semester. Only gripe is that she doesn't post lecture slides, but if you get a buddy to send notes when you miss class its fine. easy class for AXLE or eng libarts core.

Super fun and relaxing class. Fairly easy grading but most test questions did not seem to have a "correct answer" that we ever talked about so be ready to throw everything at a question and hope something sticks. You have to write down what she is saying in class, not just the bullet points. Do the readings, they always come up on the test

Prof. Chase was a great professor that was very engaging with her lectures and the class was actually very enjoyable. Super easy to get an A in this class if you go to class and take notes and the papers are graded very leniently. Take this class for AXLE credits if you have the chance

Prof Brittany is a very passionate and dedicated teacher. Her lectures are always engaging. Beware that it's more like a "history" class and she's very demanding for your work (2 papers, 2 exams, 4 quizzes, no slides posted), but the exams are open-note and she grades essays fairly (sometimes deduct points for minor grammar errors tho). Recommend!

Interesting and enjoyable laid-back class. Easy AXLE credit as long as you show up to class everyday and take good notes. If you skip class, you wont do well. 3 open-note exams and a paper. Prof Chase made the class fun; overall I'd recommend it.

Prof. Chase changed the structure of the class this semester, adding annoying reading/listening quizzes and not offering any sort of EC. The class isn't really hard so much as it is annoying. Your grade consists of two papers, two exams, and the quizzes. Very little feedback given on any assignment. Not very responsive to emails.

This elective music class is far more annoying than it should be. Prof. Chase is probably nice as a person, but she comes across as incredibly condescending and pompous for someone who is teaching an intro level music class that most people take to fulfill AXLE. With that said though, would not say this class was an easy A due to nitpicky grading.

This class was super fun. Dr. Chase realized it was supposed to be enjoyable and made the essays and tests not impossible. Lectures were fun when people participated. This was a great AXLE class to take if you're willing to not skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Chase is so enthusiastic and fun  I learned so much in this class and it was very easy. 2 papers, 2 exams, NO HOMEWORK the entire semester. You must go to lectures because otherwise, you don't know the content on exams, but they are so fun because you mainly listen to music and take notes. Take this class!

Prof Chase is the best! She is so funny and really cares about her students. You can tell she is passionate and it comes through in lectures. I've received 100s on the two papers and a 96 on the first midterm. Very easy class so long as you take good notes and refresh before exams. Class is what you make of it! Very fascinating.

Amazing, hilarious teacher. Class is quite lecture heavy but super engaging and interactive. Be sure to take notes - exams are ripped word for word from them. Some people were upset they got low grades on their papers/exams, but if you just read the instructions carefully and actually do everything that's asked of you, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing, hilarious teacher with great lectures. Even though the class was lecture heavy, it was also super fun, engaging, and interactive. Some people were upset because they got low grades on papers/exams, but if you just read the guidelines carefully and actually do what's asked of you, you'll be fine. Be sure to take notes!!!

This class is honestly one of my favorites. I typically do not like history classes but I found this class to be very interesting and engaging. Grades are based on two tests and two papers, the papers at 5-7 pages long and if you put in the time and follow the rubric you'll be fine. The tests are open-note and online, very easy if you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Chase is very unclear about her expectations with papers and exams, and she is strict with her grading policies. For an intro music class that many students also take for an AXLE credit, Professor Chase makes this class way too difficult and grades way too harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was truly so easy-- definitely take it for US His credit. The quizzes quote directly from the notes, & the tests are graded extremely generously. It was a T/R class, but we never had a lecture longer than 30 minutes. The only difficulty is the papers. They're not hard (I never got lower than an A-), but the criteria are somewhat vague.

Survey of American Hip Hop is an incredible class . Professor Chase makes the lectures interesting and engaging. Go to class, take notes, participate some, do the work (minimal workload), and you'll get a pretty easy A. Plus, you get to listen to a lot of music which is fun!

Async for Spring 21. Quizzes SUPER easy, exams fairly easy and open note. Two research essays might be more daunting if writing isnt your strong suit, but I found them easy. Unfortunately didnt get to know Professor Chase personally, but based on her lectures she is pretty animated and adds some interesting commentary/stories to the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Chase is amazing. Could not recommend her class more. As long as you show up and take notes during her lectures, you will get an A. She engages the class is such interesting discussions and I enjoyed every single second. Could not recommend more.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was asynchronous so there were online video lectures. If you do all of the assignments and take good notes, it is a very easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Survey of American Hip Hop is easily the best class I've taken and Professor Chase is the best professor ever. She really teaches the material in a way that engages the students. She doesn't post lectures so be sure to show up and pay attention but as long as u do that its an easy A. class is 3 tests 1 essay on a hip hop album super chill class.

Would definitely recommend taking this music class for an easy A. Weekly quizzes straight from the lecture videos. Exams are graded a little harsher but still easy and doable. you write two 5-7 page papers related to the material that are graded nicely. Took it asynchronous.

Chase is great! I loved the history of Hip Hop. She's super friendly and helpful and the lectures are super interesting. Only weird thing is that she uses hired graders which can make things a little confusing. But it's an awesome class!

I really loved taking Professor Chase's class. The material was very engaging and interesting to learn. I feel like I gained a whole new appreciation for music and history from her class. Her essays seemed to be hit or miss between students. I did well on them as an engineering student, but I know several writers/english majors who didn't.

AMAZING class and she is a really engaging lecturer. She is brilliant and deeply cares about the material, which made it enjoyable to learn from her. The content of the class is also really interesting! She randomly checks attendance and it's factored into your grade. Other than attendance, there's only 4 grades (2 tests and 2 papers).

Prof Chase is very excited about the material she teaches, and she is very knowledgable as well. She also makes class discussion interesting. However, there are only two papers, two tests, and a final, and everything is graded by a third party. She is not very flexible about deadlines or giving points back. Overall, a fun class though!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Chase is fun and passionate about the courses she teaches. She's a true music lover, and can give insight into many styles and genres. Tests are doable if you take good notes & pay attention in class. She is responsive over email but does not tolerate B.S. Overall, a great learning experience and an easy A if you do what you're supposed to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She made this class so much harder than what it had to be. During the pandemic she graded us so hard on the smallest things. She was so inconsiderate. she didn't want to hear people excuses on what they were going through at home or nothing. I regret taking this class.

Take Pop Music! It's a great learning experience and I can't imagine a better professor. It's super enjoyable and interesting, some of my friends not enrolled in the class came anyways because of how fun it was.
Easy A, chill class, funny discussions
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Overall, a pretty easy class. Papers take time, but the exams, if you study the stuff she goes over in lecture, will be a breeze. Take for an easy humanities class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best profs I've had so far here. She's incredibly nice, supportive, and encourages great class discussion. Tests are easy, and papers are fine if you go in and get help during office hours. A really interesting class, and her passion for the subject made it even more enjoyable.

Your grade is 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. Papers are given with vague prompt yet graded with expectations that were not clear. No sample paper, no rubric, and sometimes she doesn't have time to meet or answers emails too late. I enjoyed the class, but the grading and unclear expectation made it regretful.

Professor Chase is very passionate about music, but your grade only comes from 2 papers, a midterm, & a final. The papers are given with vague prompts, no rubric, & with little guidance, but they are graded in a very specific way. The expectations are unclear & the professor uses a grader so the grades given are inconsistent with little feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I was told by Apple Care this was an easy A class and it certainly is not. She has 4 grades for the whole course, which would be fine for an upper level course but not for an elective. Professor is passionate about music and material is interesting, but setup of the course is trash. No rubrics for essays and subjective grading, highly detailed exam
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Chase is very enthusiastic about the subject matter, which makes the class enjoyable. However, attendance is required because she does not post the notes online. Also, the tests mainly cover material from the lectures. But, if you study and write good essays, you'll do well in the class. Once you get to music from today, the class is fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Chase is average, but she expects a lot of work from a 1000 course that most are taking for AXLE credit. Grade is based on 2 5-7 page papers, a midterm and final exam, and attendance. She doesn't post lecture slides online, so you have to be in class to take notes or you'll miss information. Never bought or used the book and got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: SHE IS AMAZING. She is so caring and it shows. My favorite professor at Vanderbilt so far. Wish I could retake this class.

Great professor. Attendance is practically mandatory everyday (read other reviews) despite what the syllabus may say so keep that in mind. Lectures can be tedious at the start but it really ramps up towards the second half of the class. Decent amount of work, but it's doesn't feel like much if you're good at time management. Overall very fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's more enthusiastic and passionate about her class material than most Vandy professors. You can tell that she genuinely loves to talk about music! She was very nice to me when I had personal problems and came to talk to her. She even put me in contact with other classmates for a study group. I've never had another prof do that - she cares!
so passionate and knowledgeable, truly cares. would definitely recommend if youre willing to memorize the notes for the midterm and final. amazing professor

If you miss a class, you're basically ruined for that topic on the exams. She doesn't post the slides on Brightspace, the TA isn't going to tell you (she'll just tell you to look it up), Prof Chase might tell you if you're lucky. Best bet is to not miss a class. Note: exams include an essay component.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her class is so fun! She has personality and loves it when you speak up, so don't be afraid to. The only thing that hurts people's grades is the harsh grader she uses on the paper, but she allows you to submit for a regrade. She's notorious for handing back tons of points. People who got 85s will resubmit and get As. Study the lecture notes!!
An amazing professor--so knowledgeable and truly wants the students who actually care to do well. Interesting class too, especially if you are already familiar with a wide variety of genres.

Dr. Chase is awesome. She keeps the class interesting and she really wants the students to enjoy the subject. She's really clear about what she wants from assignments and what will be on tests. She's also super chill and the class I have with her is more like a discussion than a class.

Class is super easy. The exam questions are pulled straight from lecture and the readings are super short. The only downsides are the tedious papers (2 5-7 pagers in the semester) and the fact that she refuses to post the lecture slides on BrightSpace. At any rate though, if you need to knock out a humanities requirement, take this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super chill woman. Unlike what some people will tell you, there is work you gotta do in this class. Even so, it's not much: just a couple papers and some exams. Plus, she gives great lectures. Take this class! It knocks out a Peabody humanities requirement and AXLE
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Butt is a great professor but definitely not the most engaging during lectures. Tough grader but his feedback sessions are helpful and his grading criteria are clear. Three speeches, an exam, "Flexpoints" and "speech exercises" compose your grade, the latter two being essentially completion grades.

Professor Butt was good! but boring.Three speeches and one test - in which he gave a study guide. Small class and he talks 90% of the time, getting distracted on my laptop was a problem. I found the book on Library Genesis but hardly ever did the readings, there is a summary at the end of each chapter. Plus he goes over everything.

Professor Butt is not the nicest or most interesting professor I've ever had. He seems to care about his students, but his demeanor can vary by the day and he is usually fairly strict. Lectures are pretty boring but clear and you don't really need to do the readings. His grading criteria is super clear, but, be warned, he is a tough grader.

Take advantage of a grade boosting class. Grades on the easy side with clear criteria and offers plenty of feedback. Nice guy, class is pretty boring and another teacher could probably go through his 6 slides in 30 minutes instead of 75, but definitely helps your GPA. A lot of freedom to write about a topic of your choosing and not a time sucker

Gives a LOT of feedback. He attributes this to not having hundreds of students. This is two-edged. 1) You get specific feedback on what to improve on, 2) because there's a lot more feedback than you'd regularly have, expect to put in more work to address that feedback.

Professor Butt is so nice and eager to help. The class is confusing at first and the one test is very hard but he really wants everyone to do well and the class is enjoyable. Grade is based on one long assignment and four debates. I would recommend the class.
One of the nicest people I have ever met in my life. He is super encouraging and I am going to be his new best friend in the future.

He is actually extremely boring and his lectures are SO awful. If you have never done debate before, this class can be really difficult. Also, he piles on a lot of work at once and is not very clear with what he wants. If you don't have to take this, I wouldn't...

Super easy class! He's hilarious and keeps things interesting. Most of the grade comes from the debates that you prepare for the entire semester, and he has experienced debaters there to help and give lots of feedback

Arbitrary grading, boring lectures, gives off aura of inexperience even after having taught for many years, I barely learned anything in class. Don't be fooled: he barely teaches any "argumentation theory". He rewards mindless rhetoric and a substantial portion of your debate grade is determined by 4 debates on a Saturday, graded by students.

Nicest guy on Campus. I honestly thought the class was going to be a disaster after the first couple of class periods, and considered dropping, but I am glad that I didn't. Quite possibly the easiest grader ever, dude understands that it is an intro level course and genuinely just wants people to enjoy his class.

Andrew was the BEST TA I could've asked for this class. He did an amazing job explaining the philosophy concepts and did so in terms we could understand. Super helpful for papers. Truly a hilarious guy, super caring, and all-around awesome. You can tell he loves the topic and wants everyone to succeed and find at least some interest in philosophy.

Andrew is the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt and it is not even close. He teaches like he understands whats its like to be a student because he was a student a year ago. I can not say enough good things about this man and am lucky to have been in his discussion. Hes the kind of guy I would want to have as a friend. Take this class

Andrew is one of the best TA's I've ever received at Vanderbilt. Coming from someone who took this class just because I had to get rid of my philosophy requirement, Andrew made the subject much more enjoyable and engaging in comparison to the actual professor. He is truly a talent and I hope Vanderbilt keeps him for the future.

The grading in this class was completely arbitrary. The numbers assigned to participation, composition, and oral assignments were completely random. All of the grades (except for the take-home tests) were completely surprising. You may think you're doing really well, your classmates may think you're doing well, but everyone is probably wrong.
She's a very rude and hard Professor. Do not take her.

Not a bad professor at all. She's not always the most on-topic, and the composition grades can be rough, but she is fair and engaging. Not an easy A class, but if you put in the effort you'll do fine.
Gandy has no idea what shes doing. You will get a bad grade because participation counts for a lot and she gives you a bad grade no matter how much you participate.
HORRIBLE!!! dont do it. Class is so boring and the only things graded fairly are exams, everything else is assigned a random number and kills your grade. Gandy Fails.

Dr. Byers was a bad professor. The power points used in lecture were made years prior and all he does is click through them. He only introduces concepts, never solves examples. The textbook used is only for homework and won't explain the topics covered. Also, he tells you things that should've been said on the syllabus at the end of the semester.

Byers often came to class with powerpoints he made during his lunch break that were full of errors, but it was nonetheless enjoyable to try find the actual correct answers with him. Byers is very experienced with the material and wants his students to get A's, he's always happy to help and is very fair with grading.

Don't let his gruff, unemotional personality fool you, Dr. Byers is a really nice guy and a really great professor who cares a lot about his students. He does a fantastic job of making some really complex material very understandable, and he never gives you more work than you need. He's got some fantastic insight from many years of practice too.
One of the hardest classes I have ever taken. The material is incredibly difficult but if you go to office hours, he will help you out. If you can take another class, take that one.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great lectures and design of homework problems so you really learn something after finishing them. A lot of hands-on MATLAB stuff that extends beyond the theory. Overall great experience!

Dr. Byram is excellent. Biostats is a tough class and the homework is hard, but if you go to officer hours, he will really help you out and help you learn the material. The tests were not bad and open note. His lectures are good and he really covers the material well. My biggest advice is to ask questions. He is very responsive and happy to help.

Dr. Byram is exactly what a professor should be. He's always looking for feedback, always willing to help, and is incredibly accommodating. He returned emails to me at 2am to help with project questions and has met with me the morning of tests to go over concepts. It would be a shame if you had the chance to take him for any class and didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof Molineux is awesome. She cares a lot about her students and the material she teaches. It's clear that she is very well-versed in her field. Definitely recommend taking this with her, but do not miss class since attendance is a large portion of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is generally pretty easy, however, grades are determined mainly by your TA. But, you better hope nothing bad in your life happens because this professor does not care about her students. I received a dean's note for some things happening in my life that impacted my attendance. She disregarded the dean's note and I went from an A to a B+

The class was pretty straight-forward. The lectures can be boring, but the work load is manageable. She is a pretty fair grader. There are smaller writing assignments, but you only do 4/9. There are also two longer papers due at the end of the semester. Not very many readings. Sometimes passive aggressive. Attendance is taken every class

The class was quite boring, lecture had nothing to do with the papers. You get to choose to do 3/7 papers (could do a fourth one for a higher grade). Final is a paper that's basically a topic of your choice on the topics the class covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Molineux was great! Although this FYWS was not my first choice, I am glad to have taken this class. Prof. Molineux gives good feedback on every essay, so you will likely be a better writer by the end of the course. Be prepared to make time for a one-page paper every week and two 3-4 page essays. Fairly easy A-, hard A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sometimes hard to stay zoned in, prof Molineux is more quiet/introverted than some profs and can ramble. But super kind, helpful, and passionate about history. Class is SO EASY though, assignments are all intuitive she even lets you use AI to help with your research, but i didn't cause it's just that easy. Little boring, but good class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I basically did nothing all semester and got an A.  Definitely take this class if you need the US History AXLE.
This Professor is pretty easy. Just submit decent quality work and your going to blow this class out of the water tbh.
The class is boring. Assignments are heavy. Definitely not recommend.

This class is very interesting.  Professor Molineux is very nice, a good lecturer, and often ends class early.  She is sometimes a little picky when grading, making it difficult to get an A on many assignments.  I would definitely take this class again though.
Dr. Molineux is a great lecturer. She typically ends class early and is very kind. However, assignments are graded by the TA who is also very nice, but can be tough.
Interesting lectures, efficient and ends class early, graded by TA though who can be tough. Assignments are reasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a great lecturer, very engaging, and all assignments are very aligned with class material. Graded off of a few participation activities, weekly short writing assignments, and a few longer papers. She is very helpful outside of class and willing to answer any questions. Pretty easy grader and most assignments have draft and final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was kind of a joke and I definitely suggest it. The professor lectured most class days and most classes ended significantly early. The class was canceled multiple times for different reasons and the workload was easy. It only entailed of 7 micro-research projects, a primary source analysis which was the midterm, and a take-home final.

I used this class as a study hall, and you could do the same. Prof only lectures (but ended class early every day), easy homework assignments, and midterm/final were easy to complete with little prior knowledge. There is an attendance grade. Honestly don't even really know what we learned, but I got an A.

One of the better options for FYWS. Honestly, it was pretty hard to get an A and I really had to try but it is impossible to get less than an A-. But to get an A is pretty hard but she is really nice and I loved her lectures and I thought the content was really fun. Great Choice if you like History. Work is light as well.

Great choice for a FYWS. Grades fairly, light on the reading in comparison to other courses, helps you grow as a writer. Gives out mostly 88s, 90s, 92s, and some 94s on assignments and papers. Easy A-, hard A with A range being 94+.

Molineux is a really good lecturer! The course was quite interesting and the workload was pretty low. There's a fair amount of homework, but it is all pretty simple. Would easily take again. Fair grader.

Prof. Molineux is the only professorI had this year that recognized how burned out we all were without any breaks. She is extremely accommodating and altered the class structure to lighten the load a bit. Sometimes the prompts can be a little ambiguous but she is a generous grader. Participate and do the homework and you will be totally fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Molineux is a wonderful, passionate, flexible professor. She is a great lecturer, explaining concepts much better than the readings. I am not really into history, but the format of this course was manageable and enjoyable. She was extremely helpful during office hours. Some grading expectations seem unclear or inconsistent, so talk to her about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very dense and hard to understand if you solely look at the powerpoints, so show up to class. Other than that shes okay and grades reasonably. Papers are not too crazy. Take the class if the subject interests you or lectures will be hard to sit through.

Great class! Lectures contain lots of information and it's obvious that Molineux is very knowledgable about the subject material. Gives plenty of feedback on essays. Most assignments are a mix of lecture and reading material.

She is a good professor with obvious expertise in her field. The key to this class is doing well on the various writing assignments. She is super helpful when it comes to answering questions about essays at her office hours. I would recommend taking good notes during the lectures, as that information will be helpful on future assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! Very reasonable work load and she is so intelligent and a great speaker. If you do everything you're supposed to you should be completely fine.
Her descriptions of assignments are very vague and unhelpful.  She also grades incredibly hard.  She is a nice lady but her expectations are extremely high.

Molineaux knows her stuff, but she's not the most personable professor I've had at Vandy.  Her class is good if you're interested in U.S. history; if you're not, pick something else.  Her lectures are good, some of the readings make you want to pull out your hair.  It's not really a fun class, but it hones your critical analysis skills.

I found hist139 fairly interesting, because I like U.S. history, but the reading bored me to death.  Also, Molineaux seemed pretty unapproachable.  Unless you really enjoy history (specifically this time period), I'd suggest a different social science or humanities class.  However, it did improve my critical analysis skills...

Worst class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Professor is unorganized and unhelpful. Gave 10/20's consistently on weekly questions. Gave me a 3/10 on the extra credit. Graded impossibly hard throughout the entire semester. Lectures are incredibly boring. Stay away at all costs. Don't know who possibly liked this class below me.
Professor Molineux is a great professor and the class is pretty easy.  However, attendance is mandatory

Dr. Jones is by far one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. She is always full of energy and actually cares about her students. The class is structured in an unorthdoxed way that makes it immersive and collaborative. Truly the biggest benefit of the class was access to Dr. Jones who has tons of office hours and provides countless opportunities.

Drug Discovery is the most unique course I've taken at Vanderbilt. While the 4-5 group presentations require strong commitment, the skills gained make it well worth it. What sets this class apart is Dr. Jones' dedication. Her guidance makes it more than just discovering drugs - it's about discovering how to think, adapt, and lead.

Drug Discovery was one of my favorite classes. It's a group project across the semester and if you pull your weight you will get an A. Definitely a different format than other classes and takes a second to get used to, but Dr. Jones is so caring and really wants you to succeed. There are 4 big presentations, no tests, can't miss more than 3 classes

Class is an easy A with time and effort. No tests and you pretty much dont need to learn random info. But you will need to meet outside of class constantly and put in a lot of work in the group project. This class is manageable if you have a good team. I really enjoy the way she has structured the class and talk about it in my med interviews

I did not have fun in this class. It was difficult information that I honestly was not interested in. Only take this class if you are interested in how a drug is made from having thousands of targets to passing clinical trials.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is basically a bunch of group work. Its pretty easy to coast if you do the easy parts and have a good group. Everyone gets an A but it is a ton of work and reading papers. Also the groups are expected to meet with Dr. Jones around 6 times outside of class but sometimes at the most inconvenient times such as Saturday morning.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: There are four 25 minute group presentations, one four-paged single-spaced book report, and a final 2 hour group presentation. This class is hard. The material is grad school level but if you follow her revisions for the presentations, you will get an A. You can only miss up to three classes. You won't be allowed into class if you are late!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The whole class is pretty much just group projects. You have 2 books to read + a paper to write for each but she's just checking to make sure that you read them. Pretty much everyone gets an A, as long as you are not late to class (BE THERE BY 8:00AM SHARP) and contribute to the group project. Learned a lot in the course! Def take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones is a baller. She does so much and cares a ridiculous amount about this class. Its an easy A if your group is solid and the class is so cool. She has 10 years in industry and really intimate knowledge about the topics. The presentations are pretty intense and she'll hook you up with all sorts of opportunities. A rising star for sure.

This class is essentially just one large group project with a few fairly tedious book reviews and blog posts along the way. Carrie cares a lot about her students and will give you ample guidance to make your presentations as good as possible. A decent amount of work, but if you have a good group, you'll be fine. Also, basically everyone gets an A.

Carrie, as a lecturer, is very good. She requires participation, and she helps make sure you understand the material (Easy A). However, she is not very accessible outside of class. She is very busy, and she offers you many things. But she can be tough to get a meeting with or get an email back from. Just stay on her, and she will be fine!

Carrie really cares for her students. This commons seminar is super easy, the only grade comes from weekly blogs, showing up to class, and a 5 page single-spaced book review. She lectures for about half the classes, and she takes us to different labs for the other half. Would definitely recommend. Easy A
Dr. Jones cares immensely for her students and it shows- great class and a great teacher.
He is very helpful, and the class is great! Just prepare and show effort and it will pay off.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed taking Professor Carlone's class. You can tell that he loves the subject that he teaches and wants us to succeed. The topics we learned in class were also quite interesting. We did have a group project, so beware of that, but other than that, great class.

Literally didn't learn anything and was the easiest class ever but the very few assignments and presentations we had were graded incredibly harsh with barley any comments making it impossible to get a good grade. HOD1300 is supposed to be a super easy A. He also is just creepy and made me uncomfy AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst dude I ever did meet. Absolutely zero grading strategy, will dock you if he doesn't like you. Lectures are basically senseless and rubrics mean nothing to him. Grades basically on vibes and opinion and if he does not like you he will make it clear through your grade. Extremely strict on attendance. He does have a good extension policy.

Paper-heavy course. Expect very few comments on your paper, but can email for further comments. If you follow the instructions to the T and check off all the rubric requirements, you'll get a B. Attendance is quite strict: if you're 3 minutes late you're at a 50% for the day. Nice person, but life is not that serious. Good extension policy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Carlone is a very nice guy but you could follow the rubric perfectly and still get a B+/A- on the paper. Attendance is mandatory but he makes the class engaging and creates a good classroom community. Email him/TA for tips on how you can improve the paper before you turn it in to get a better grade.

Seems like a pleasant guy, but he's a wolf in sheep's clothing. Grading is incredibly tough and ambiguous. You can follow the rubric to the tee and you'll still lose points. TA replies to all the emails for him. On top of that lectures are boring. Would never take again.

I'm really upset about taking this class(HOD2100). The TA won't reply to emails, it's hard to learn anything useful, and their grading is extremely strict. I'll never take another course with this professor again. I hate HOD.

Took 2100 w him. Super tough grader, no feedback on papers, unclear how to improve. Way more writing than other sections: case briefs, long reflections, consulting report, infographic. Most ppl got B+/A-. Only know of 1 A which is insane for AN INTRO HOD CLASS. Also ghosted my emails for like a month straight. Nice guy, but brutal class. Be warned.

This professor is simply terrible. You can not rely on anything that he says. He could tell you one thing and then expect something else on the assignment. Getting an A is a miracle. Least structured class. Other sections of HOD 2100 worked with Vandy Dining or did something actually applicable to the course content. AVOID!
terrible. dont take this class.
don't take corleone he will and wants to ruin your gpa
no doubt the hardest hod prof here, doesnt respond to emails or offer support and just slashes ur grade for no rsn
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless you want to tank your GPA, do not take Carlone. There is no reason for less than 20% of the class to get an A in a HOD intro class, which is generally supposed to very easy. Takes off points for the smallest thing, getting a 90 plus on a presentation is a miracle.
Professor Carlone was a nice professor, the work wasn't too difficult. The subject matter just got a little boring.
I've taken multiple classes with Dr. Carlone. He is easily accessible and provides great feedback. Take him if you can

Dr. Rizzo moves at an absurd pace, often 3 chapters ahead of others. Final exam was unfair. Lectures don't match the exams, and little practice material is provided. In class, handwriting is ILLEGIBLE and explanations are poor. Outside of class, he rarely answer emails and office is VERY hard to find.Tests have ruthless MCQ w/ zero partial credit.

Incredibly kind professor and genuinely cares about his students' understanding of the material. If you want to learn orgo I would 100% recommend taking Dr. Rizzo's class. He will explain concepts to you in office hours as many times as it takes for you to understand them and he's very kind to his students. Amazing professor all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rizzo is the best choice for orgo. His content has a big conceptual component (10 MCs per exam). I think this really helps you to do well in orgo, and I understood content way more than my friends in other classes. Class is graded on 3 midterms, a final, and discussion. A is doable if you put in the work. Super nice and really wants to teach.

Orgo is a hard subject on its own, but Rizzo is one of the best profs to have. He goes pretty fast through the lectures and sometimes his answers to questions weren't clear, so I really had to learn how to teach myself. Overall though, his exams are manageable and he's generous with free response. (His attempts at jokes are also really sweet.)

The MCQ on Rizzo's exams is a double-edged sword but he is very generous with short answers. I found myself having to self-study as he moves very fast, but it drove me to keep up with Vanderbilt's rigor. This class is fast-paced, has a lot of information, and will take up most of your time. But, if you're taking Orgo at Vandy, take this one!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly a great professor. He really cares about students and his lecture style is really easy to follow. He provides tons of examples, but you have to do the work outside of class. If you read the textbook and do all the recommended problems, you will be okay.

I think Professor Rizzo cares about his students, but I found him to be a terrible lecturer. The pace was fast and I could never read his handwriting. You should always read the book ahead of time.
