The tests are objectively easier than the other professor's. I think I would have done better in another professor's section based on teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rizzo is an excellent professor. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is lenient in grading, and he gives a curve at the end. The tests are easier than Clements or Hare. I find his lectures engaging, but they move at a swift pace. He's a very experienced chemist. Highly recommend for orgo

Dr. Rizzo is a fantastic professor. He uses the textbook, has video recordings of his lectures available, and also lectures in class time. He provides SO many options for office hours (like 3-4 times per week). His tests are more straightforward than the other orgo prof's exams. He also grades very leniently. I think this is the best orgo section.

Everyone says Rizzo is great, but I find him to be so boring and his handwriting to be so illegible that I can't understand anything. His tests are really challenging, and you really have to study the textbook. He makes me genuinely hate chemistry and I hate showing up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have credit for AP Chem, TAKE THIS CLASS! Rizzo's lectures are clear and followable, despite the tricky subject. He occasionally lightens the material by discussing things like "Breaking Bad." For exams, reading TB and doing practice problems is necessary to do well, but Rizzo gives generous partial credit on frq's. Much better than gen chem

You have to read - Rizzo is not the type of professor to give standalone lectures w.r.t. the textbook. Having said that, if you do read textbook and do problems, his lectures will clarify the key points, and he is always willing to answer questions during and after class. The tests are hardish, but grading is fair and the class is curved at the end

Orgo is going to be hard no matter what, so you might as well take it with someone who is generous with partial credit/curving. I found Rizzo to be a very dry lecturer, while simultaneously moving at an extremely swift pace. You will not be successful in this class if you do not dedicate a significant amount of time to the optional TB problem sets
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although Orgo has very hard material, Dr. Rizzo did his best to explain the difficult topics in an easy to understand way. He is also a very lenient grader and probably gives more points than we truly deserve. Additionally, he tends to curve so most students have a B- or more. If you are a freshman with a 5 on AP Chem, Rizzo is your best choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rizzo is nice and wants to see his students succeed. You can tell that he loves chemistry and teaching. It is a difficult class however and very test heavy so I would keep that in mind. He offers resources to help you succeed but there is little to no homework so it is completely up to you. At the end of the semester there is a significant curve

Rizzo is a nice guy but tough class. Doesn't take attendance but lectures are helpful. Definitely suggest reading the textbook and doing the suggested problems. Office hours are accessible but he is kind of awkward and not the easiest guy to chat with. He definitely does care about his students' performance and the class was interesting. Recommend

If you are a freshman with AP credit, you should take Rizzo hands down. I really enjoyed the way he taught this class, but his tests are definetely tough. The way he teaches orgo is amazing. There is a generous 3-6 point curve at the end of the semester. I highly recommend doing the textbook problems. He is socially awkward though.

Really cares about student learning despite the hard content. Amazing guy to interact with during office hours, wish I did it more. Tells random chemistry or art-related stories during class to break up the monotony. Wish he was my dad.
Organic Chemistry is hard but Rizzo is an excellent lecturer -- he gives a pretty generous curve at the end of the semester too.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Decent teacher but awful and insensitive human being. Asked for extra/outside class help at least 10 times and he was unwilling even though he promised to be accessible. Really good at explaining concepts but very very insensitive
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rizzo is a great prof and really nice guy. Doesn't take attendance but lectures are clear and helpful. Test are pretty straightforward (be careful of multiple choice they're worth a lot). Orgo is obviously difficult but if you do all the textbook problems you'll be fine. If you have the AP credit would definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He's genuinely such a nice guy & he's so smart. Super willing to help you outside of class. Lectures aren't mandatory, but I found them incredibly useful. They can be a little dry, but he does his best to make them funny and engaging too. Do all of the recommended textbook problems and you should be fine for the exams.

Still not easy, but million times better than gen chem. Rizzo is a nice lecturer, is willing to answer ?s if it means repeating info, and is very accessible, even holding office hours in commons once a week. Class is still difficult and you should be confident w/chem knowledge and test-taking skills to take the class. Read TB+office hours+lecture

Attendance not taken but lectures are clear and helpful. Try to read textbook before class add then work through homework problems after lecture. Grade based solely on 3 tests and the final, but tests are straightforward and easy if you know what you're doing. Rizzos a really nice guy and super helpful. If you have AP credit definitely take!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Good lecture notes, reading the TB, and doing the suggested problems are key to doing well in this class. No graded HW/quizzes. Work heavy and challenging but very manageable. Exams are difficult but fair-know material conceptually. He is very accessible and cares about students. A sense of humor if you get him talking. Much better than gen chem!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The key to this class is doing all the homework problems and meeting with Professor Rizzo when questions arrive. He makes a considerable effort to make himself available for review sessions and with his office hours. Lecture can sometimes get a bit dry, but Professor Rizzo does hit you with the occasional funny joke.

Professor Rizzo is an overall average teacher. He's mellow, teaches material thoroughly, and helps you out (curves you) if you work hard. If you can take this class, definitely do it. It's much easier than gen chem. Overall good experience for freshman organic chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He really wants you to do well: his lectures are helpful and he has lots of office hours. His exams aren't nightmarish, but to do well its good to do all the problems he assigns and take the class seriously. His lectures were funny for me, but his humor is a dry variety. He's really sweet and helpful even though the subject is a bit difficult.

Rizzo is a caring professor - he wants you to succeed. He's available during office hours and sit and answer every question even if it's past office hours. Tests are fair and doable but it's easy to lose points on the MC. Easier class than all the craze organic receives.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Solid Professor. Lecture was very boring but somewhat helpful, although reading the textbook and doing the problems is way more helpful. Tests are fair but still pretty difficult, probably an 8/10 difficulty especially since the MC is worth a lot of points. He is a very helpful and knowledgable guy though and will help you if you seek him out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Rizzo's lectures are easy to follow even if the topics are complicated. As long as you take good lecture notes and look at the textbook, you'll be able to understand the content pretty easily. Doing his suggested HW problems really helps. Tests are hard but fair. Beware of MC questions! They're tricky and worth 4% each. He's also a hilarious chap
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Rizzo is really nice. He is definitely a great organic chemistry professor  he knows what he's doing. He also tries really hard to be accessible to students. He doesn't always give the best advices, but his lecture is well planned. Super funny. Take lots of notes, and review regularly. Be prepared, though, because it is not at all easy.

Professor Rizzo is great! If you got a 5 on AP Chem, take orgo with Rizzo.  He is super helpful and teaches difficult material well!  Homework problems aren't mandatory but do them and you're ready for the tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: All around just a great guy. Tests were very doable, and very fair. Final was very comprehensive and challenging, but manageable. He is extremely kind, helpful, and never gets mad, even when some kids ask ridiculous amounts of irrelevant questions each day in class. Really enjoyable guy, and overall great experience.
Class is fair and manageable. Didn't go to class much but read the book thoroughly and did all the problems and ended with an A-. Be sure to read and do all the problems and you will get good grades.
Excellent professor who made material that is traditionally considered to be difficult easy to understand. Tests were quite fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Super nice guy, got us candy. Everyone loves him, but his lectures can be a little dry. The key to this class is reading the book and doing the problems that he suggests on his website. Very easy class for the hype that organic chemistry gets.

Had him for first-semester orgo. WAY better than taking genchem, for all you incoming freshman to Vandy reading this who got a 5 on the AP absolutely take this class. Doesn't give lower than a B unless you completely don't try, no mandatory homework, optional weekly review sessions. Rizzo also brings humor to the class every so often.

Prof. Rizzo is just a genuinely friendly guy, and the whole class liked him. He actually brought candy bars for everyone on Halloween. The material is dry and there's a lot of it, but he explains things clearly and throws in funny little sidebars sometimes. Definitely not an easy class, and the only grades are 3 tests, final, and discussion session

Professor Rizzo taught my first semester of freshman orgo and I would highly recommend him. Each lecture was the same but he made fairly difficult material easy to understand. He gave helpful examples and the tests were very fair. Read the textbook and do the practice problems and you will do fine.

Rizzo is a really cool guy, and is a pretty good lecturer. He covers all the mechanisms very well, and is always ready to help (he has extra study sessions every week and right before tests). Throws some humor into the class to make it palatable. Tests were kinda tough, but not too bad. Do the homework and you'll be fine

Very good at explaining various mechanisms in organic.  Classes are always the same, and there are basically no other grades besides tests and finals. Tests aren't confusing but easy to make mistakes on because of how complex the material can be. I went to office hours lots, and he was extremely helpful then. Also makes jokes every now and then
Great professor! Had him for freshman orgo and hes fantastic. Tests are a little tough but not someone completely unmanageable.

Rizzo taught my freshman-only Organic Chem class for one semester and did a great job making sure we understood everything. He stops regularly for questions and always sticks around after lecture for any remaining questions. Tests are straightforward, no curveballs. He can be pretty funny sometimes too. Take him if you can get him.

It was a TR 9:35 class so the lectures were going to be long. He spoke for the whole hr and 25 min without stopping to break up the lecture briefly with jokes or stories, something that other orgo professors do. He covered the material, but showing up or staying awake was nearly impossible because his lectures were so monotonous and boring.

So glad I took him over Sulikowski. His tests were easier (3 not 4) but a pretty tough final.  Extremely boring lectures but explains the mechanisms well. Nice guy and super fast grader. Its easy to do poorly so be prepared to keep up! You know what is expected if you go to lecture so no surprises.
Teaches straight from the notes - most boring lecturer of all time. Study hard for his quizzes, they're tough. Curves to an 80.
YOU'RE AWESOME.

Great guy, really into his research. Never went to office hours, took this class freshman year. Managed a B in first semester AP organic. Got an A in this class. Keeps everything simple, just study notes and read before you come into class, and always do the optional problems. Stay on top of the work, don't slack off and you'll get an A.

Rizzo is easily one of the best professors I have ever had.  He gets to know his students and, if you ask for help, will identify the weaknesses you need to work on and explain things in such a way that O'Chem seems easy once you've left his office.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
Everything you need to know is on the slides, so there's no need to attend class; just do the recommended problems and memorize slides. Plus, his tests are easier than Sulikowski's. Take him.

Rizzo is best described as somebody you can take where you can succeed and not have to go to class everyday. I went to class everyday and got a B, but then again that's the highest I ever got in Chemistry. Just do all the suggested problems in the book and you'll be fine.

Everything is from slides, which makes class attendance mandatory. The problem sets he gives are an important key to doing well on the tests. Don't simply study the slides or problems, understand the basics of the mechanisms and how they can be applied broadly. You'll do fine, just be prepared to work.

Hes a great professor, really cares about your future even if you dont plan on majoring in chem. His tests are now straight forward, but the material is hard. He reads off the power point slides, but he is willing to help you during offce hours until you understand the material.

i didn't get an A in the class either, and the class was ridiculously hard, but i don't blame that on rizzo...in all honesty, he tried hard to get the material through to his students and his slides were organized and helpful.  a lot of students dropped out and people complain about rizzo being a bad teacher, but it's just a hard class.  get over i

HORRIBLE!!!!!!!!! You basically have to memorize hundreds of powerpoint slides, and in the end it doesn't even pay off on the tests. Take another section!!! If you must take this one don't even bother going to class, spend that extra time studying. He is boring and hell. The only thing he is good at is ruining GPAs!

OMG, so so bad, my GPA sucked this past semester b/c of him. I usually get all A's in my premed classes, and with him? no way. basically, he goes way too fast and expects you to memorize all these obscure mechanisms. he also seems really pissed off if you go into office hours for help. so PLEASE TAKE THE OTHER SECTION, for the love of god...
bad news

Rizzo taught way ahead of the other sections, leaving his class with much more work and memorization.  Tests were impossibly nitpicky, asking you to name reagents and obscure reaction intermediates.  I had no trouble with 220a with Hess, but this class was impossible.
this guy is bad, got an A in 220, struggle in this class...he is a nut...hadn't taught since the 1990s and does not know what he is doing, horrible powerpoints
Straightforward, tests not too incredibly hard.  Be sure to know your stuff before going into office hours!
Prof. Rizzo was very clear and fair...this guy ate alot of chalk dust to teach us and I appreciated his hard work.  If you study, the exams should be straightforward.
seemed arrogant, never really available for office hours...tests were okay

Dr. CK has no breakdown of her grading policy, syllabus is constantly changing, doesn't tell or post when assignments are due, and is just horribly unorganized when it comes to her class. Avoid at all costs

I don't have anything personal against Dr. CK. She does try her best to be understanding, but I genuinely have never been more stressed out by an MHS course. From pop quizzes, no syllabus posted for weeks/months (?), Brightspace miscommunications, very few if any grades put in at all over the semester, and getting bomb dropped with a HARD final.

Dr. CK is a great individual; however, her teaching style is absurd. From no syllabus in the first week of classes to an impromptu final project being announced during the last four days of classes, it would be a disservice not to let you know what you are in for if you decide to take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: CK has no clue what she is doing. She knows the course content but has the most ineffective teaching methods I've ever seen. This class was beyond disorganized, nothing was graded on time, I've literally NEVER gotten any feedback. The interviews and readings you do are complete bs. Only took accountability when she asked us to write course evals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I second the other comment on the lights. I don't like to be told how you want the lights in the room and get out of my chair to fool around with them when you can LITERALLY turn them on and off yourself from next to the blackboard ;/

I think she's a great person even though her lectures are completely boring and useless and I don't learn anything! At least she's a little fun and gives very easy grades. Someone should really tell her that she can control the lights from the wall behind the lectern so she doesn't keep asking people to do it from the back of the room.........
Ngl I had my doubts at first cause she's hard to get in touch with, but once I did, she was actually really nice and genuinely cares a lot about her students.
She definitely takes a long time to respond and get appointments but she grades easily so I guess it's not too crazy

She's a great person and very nice! I don't think I've ever worked in a group during class where every other student doesn't complain about her in great detail. There's widespread awareness that something is wrong with her class unfortunately. I wish she just had concrete deadlines and timely feedback or numbered grades. That would make it awesome!
A lot of craziness, but I like her mostly because of who she is as a person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you want to submit tons of assignments and homework and get NO feedback whatsoever, NO grades back, take her!! I interviewed someone in my dorm for an assignment and ran into them this week when they asked if I did good and I had to tell them that we don't get a grade back on it! She gave memo feedback to only half the class and not the other.

Dr. CK is beautifully chaotic and cares more about you just doing the reading and participating than actually grading harshly. She can be a bit disorganized but she's flexible with deadlines and just wants students to learn.
She's genuinely a sweetheart and is trying her best given her chronic condition and life.

SO extremely disorganized. Nobody ever knows what's going on. When asked for clarification on her unclear assignments she answers in the most confusing way that doesn't even answer the question. Assigns LONG readings before every class that are completely irrelevant to each other. Classes are so random. Can't tell you what we learned or did so far.

I DARE YOU to take her class if you do not believe how messy and disordered this class is. I can't believe I had the luck of choosing her section out of 6 other sections. If an admin would come sit in her class for a single day, she would be fired.

99% of the class is figuring out what her instructions mean. "I'll send an email out with more details". Email never sent. If it is sent, the instructions don't make sense. You can have an entire writing assignment due someday and the instructions are "details in packet" JUST FOR THERE TO BE NO PACKET. It takes a LOT to even get started on work.

Calling her disorganized is like calling Epstein flirtatious. Uses different names for a single assignment to the point where you think theyre different, and there's no standard place where you can check either because "living syllabus" and 3 different dropboxes for the same thing or no dropboxes at all for stuff all due on a particular day.

Every assignment we have is a mental gymnastics exercise. Homework with contradicting instructions, assignments with multiple overlapping submission dropboxes, instructions to turn something in during class and it never gets collected, promises that a worksheet will be returned just to never be seen again.  You also don't learn ANYTHING in class.

Dr. CK is a a fun person. But it is so extremely frustrating when you're given an assignment and her "instructions" leave you with no clue what you're doing and you just guess your way through. In class she gave instructions for an assignment and was somehow SURPRISED when the whole class was confused, saying she "thought [she] was clear" (?????)

She is genuinely really accommodating and helpful. She did have a rough time with teaching this past last semester, but she was experiencing health issues. Give her a chance the readings and discussions make the class an easy A.
I have some words I can say about her and her class, but I will probably get censored. Don't waste your time with her, she's not worth it.
All of the reviews about her being unorganized are 100% true. I wouldn't recommend her to others and her expectations on assignments are very unclear. Class was interesting but avoid her if you can.

There's really not I can say positive about her. The content was somewhat interesting, but she was extremely unorganized and it was at the expense of the students. Pretty lazy when it came to grading and actual teaching as half of your grade comes from busy work like watching guides. Simply not a Vanderbilt level professor, truly a let down.

I absolutely loved this class and Dr. CK. I will admit, the class requires a fair amount of reading and you really do have to participate. She is a bit unorganized so in terms of deadlines/assessments, that's not optimal; but she truly is so passionate and wants everyone to do their best. I couldn't recommend this class more!

Our section's expectations were confusing only because she was changing the course structure to be easier on students. Yours won't be. Dr. CK is super real and passionate. The content is super interesting but you'll be reading a good bit.

Overall the class was very interesting but Professor Callahan-Kapoor is extremely unorganized. She says she wants to help and give feedback but responds to emails after days which is always near the assignment due date. I was constantly confused about what exactly she wanted for assignments because there were three different guidelines posted.

She's one of the most caring professors at Vanderbilt. She has an impressive memory - she tries to remember at least one personal detail you've shared during class. Very approachable and open to feed back - take her whenever you can :)

Dr. CK is an extremely caring professor, who genuinely wants to know who you are outside of class. Her feedback on papers is extremely thorough and generally has high expecations. She likes challenging ideas and having thoughtful discussions. An interesting class to begin with but even better with Dr. CK.

Professor CCK was very nice and understanding. She let our class have a lot of agency during our time. Lot of readings. Can't say for sure but would assume CCK is one of the best people to take Core1010 with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Callahan-Kapoor was one of the most supportive professors I've ever had. She worked to make the course guidelines work for me when I was struggling, and helped students finding meaning and personal interest in the content/theories she was teaching. She is wickedly smart but not intimidating and embodies true kindness and empathy for her students.
super easy grading scheme, every assignment is basically pass fail. decent amount of work but CK is a great professor would highly recommend
LOVE LOVE LOVE HER! I love all of the class discussions and she is so approachable as a professor. TAKE THIS CLASS IT IS THE BEST ONE I HAVE TAKEN AT VANDERBILT!

One of the most intelligent, kind, and awesome teachers I have had. Does an amazing job facilitating class discussions. Created a great environment for discussion. Available for Office Hours to discuss feedback. Overall, an awesome teacher.
Amazing professor; cares about what her students think and wants you to do well

This class would go off the rails every time but in a good way- never dull with all the WTF moments. Prof CK is caring, intelligent, loves class participation, and is a great human and teacher overall. Take this class for the tangents into every MHS sector and crazy moral debates. Lots of little assignments and reading/videos but they're doable.
Pretty straightforward when it comes to tests and written work. Shes very knowledgeable about the subject, but a bit disorganized. She did cold call in online class, and for that reason, Im out.
Laziest most unorganized professor Ive ever had. Doesnt reply to emails, course was easy but almost impossible due to her lack of organization. Most frustrating academic experience
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was a little disorganized online, but the readings, documentaries, and podcasts were all amazing. You will learn so much in this class if you spend time to do the assigned readings before class. Super easy grader but takes a long time to get things back to you. She cares a lot about students and is flexible on deadlines.

Really enjoyed my COVID & Society section under Prof. Callahan-Kapoor. She's really understanding of students' mental health needs and doesn't give too much homework. She loves Peerceptiv (students read/grade each other's papers) which is the MOST annoying platform ever, but the class made up for it.

This was a COVID special topi class. The class was very interesting with guest speakers every week and the discussions in smaller groups. Prof Callahan was very understanding with deadlines/assignments, and genuinely care about our well-being and our input in the class. She really values participation. Short papers every week sometimes peer-graded

She's a great teacher and very specific with what she wants out of you. Participation is crucial; if you don't speak in class you get docked points. Also, if there's a lag in the discussion she'll usually cold call on someone and ask specific pointed questions from the readings. Realistically like 30 hours of work a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. She explains the material well and when she notices the class struggling, she's really flexible with her grading and willing to go back to different concepts. Reading heavy!! Assignments are doable there's just a lot of them. Definitely learned the most this semester from this class. Do the assignments and get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: By far my favorite class I have taken. Extremely interesting topics covered and she clearly cares so much about it. Lectures are interesting and usually fairly interactive. Definitely a lot of homework, but as long as you skim you should be fine. She gives many opportunities for extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The material is ambiguous and sometimes hard to interpret. None of the assignments should have been difficult but the expectations were never clear. If you're okay not having any idea what's going on or what your grade is for the entire semester then go for it.

Made the class more difficult than it should be. Very ambiguous, ambitious goals for discussion that ultimately failed in accomplishing what she intended. Course content interesting, but poorly taught; she is a very confusing lecturer. Sweet lady, bad professor. Also makes you write your own exams(??) Assignments change all the time, disorganized!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Callahan-Kapoor is very sweet and the class is interesting. However, the assignments are often ambiguous and obscure in meaning. Even after seeing her in office hours, I wasn't clear on what was expected of me. In addition, the overall class seems a bit unorganized. Multiple choice on exams often seemed subjective as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. CK and her caregiving course are wonderful. She made the material interesting and tailored our readings, assignments, etc to our interests/input. She really respects her students and is always available to help with coursework and understanding the material. Students are held to a high standard and she's a hard grader, worth it though.

I LOVE Dr. Callahan-Kapoor. She's my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. You will definitely have to put in a lot of work for her class. She has very high expectations and is a very tough grader. BUT, she makes it all worth it. So caring and is there for you outside of her class. I've spent hours at a time in her office. EXTREMELY intelligent lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Callahan-Kapoor has been my favorite MHS professor so far. I had little to no expectations for her Caregiving seminar as it was my first MHS class and the only one I got into, but I've never enjoyed such a thought-provoking class. She really considers you her equal, and expects you to contribute to the class as much as she does.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Callahan-Kapoor is an amazing professor and her Theories of the Body class was fantastic. Between the frequent journal assignments, final paper, long reading hw for every class, and the tests, this class was A LOT of work(I felt like it should be a W course). The material was very interesting and you can make an A if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She takes a very long time to grade things and has a specific thing she's looking for in each assignment. She can be very picky when grading, but if you discuss the grade she usually will give partial credit. Readings are long but not really required. She's very open to discussion and bases most of class on in class discussion. Solid choice for MHS

Professor Callahan-Kapoor is WONDERFUL, easily one of my favorite professors yet. She's a tad disorganized but she's new at being a professor. She is so caring and understanding, she humanizes profs. Participation is the single most important part of the class, but not the hardest. It's easy to get an A if you participate and show genuine interest.

Very tough grader (and takes a long time to grade), not very responsive to emails and sometimes felt kind of condescending. Some assignments had very clear grading criteria, and others were extremely vague. Discussions/participation huge part of class; also had final sprung upon us right before class ended. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Theories of the Body with her is a great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing at leading vibrant discussions (makes the classroom comfortable for everyone to speak), caring, and passionate about her subject and expanding student's perspectives. Reading, podcasts-fascinating and informative. However, the class should have been a W-course: 300-500 weekly blog posts, numerous essays, and a written midterm and final!

Dr. Callahan-Kapoor is very knowledgeable in her subject, and she takes class time to make sure the students also understand the material. There  is a lot of reading, but she is flexible with the assignment due dates. From my experience, she was fairly generous with grading written assignments if you explained your argument and what you understood.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A knowledgeable teacher, but by far the most unorganized professor I've ever had to deal with. Every student I talked to in the class (and I'm not being hyperbolic) was always confused about assignment due dates. Lot of reading, which is sometimes interesting, but your grades will sometimes suffer just because of her disorganization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: While Dr. Callahan-Kapoor is extremely knowledgable on her subject and shows a genuine interest in teaching the class and making sure her students understand the subject matter, the workload was extremely intense for an intro class. Readings for every class, three days a week, that were often extremely long and intensive scholarly writings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great class!! Professor Callahan Kapoor really knows her stuff. Readings weren't too bad; the amount was average for a typical MHS class. Definitely recommend anyone to take this! Interesting topic, and she's an easy grader (Just be aware of grammar; she can get picky). Earned an A by just skimming the readings.
The class was interesting and she is very knowledgeable about the subject and cares about the students, but the workload was much more than any other class I have had
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: It is admirable how much she cares about students, but it was too much work for an intro course. I would bet that she will change the final because it was by far the most work I have done for a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Very reading-heavy and required a solid understanding of the articles and their authors by the end of the semester. Although the class only had 1 paper and 7 mini-essay things, the final was very tough. It required tons of time since it was a take-home test, plus there was an in-class portion. If you take this class, you better like MHS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Kapoor is very knowledgeable and is very committed to her students. THERE IS ALOT OF READING! The assignments are not easy either! She is a tough grader but your reading and writing skills will definitely improve!  You will also learn a great deal! DO NOT PROCRASTINATE! Beware of the final! I would not recommend taking her class your 1st year
Celso is so passionate about what he teaches and will help you succeed in his class. Definitely take a class with him if you can!

I took Castilho's Futbol-Soccer class as someone interested in sports. We got to go to a Nashville SC game to observe fan behavior. It was really cool. Looked more into contemporary issues than history but he is passionate about the topic, which translated well to the content we explored. Assignments and essays graded fairly.

Professor Castilho's Gender, Law, and Slave Emancipation in Latin America was an easy LHS credit. While his expectations for assignments were not always clear (often reiterates/clarifies expectations leading up to the due date), he is a lenient grader. He was very accessible outside of class and one of my favorite professors!
Celso is an awesome professor who clearly knows a lot about the subject. Lectures can sometimes be a little bit boring but he's very accessible out of class.

Professor Castilho is a very kind and knowledgeable professor. He knows a lot about the subject, which makes the lectures interesting. Not an extremely difficult class, but you do have to show up to class and do the readings to do well. Somewhat lecture-heavy at times, but highly recommend Professor Castilho.

Great course, made the final paper a lot less scary and doable. Super helpful feedback and the readings/discussions are interesting! Toward the latter half of the semester, you'll get days off sometimes so you can work on your paper, but I mostly used them to catch up on sleep :) He schedules 1:1s to make sure you're on track, really nice overall
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good choice for the required 3000w class for majors. Most of the class is focused on a long research paper, so be sure to pick something that interests you. A lot of weeks with no class so you can research, which requires self-discipline. Liked the guided paper process. He gave good feedback, and the class definitely improved my research skills.

I was nervous about this class, but he made the research paper way less intimidating. He lets you choose any topic in history for the paper, but also gives a good amount of guidance & advice. The first third of the class discusses confederate memory & identity, which was super interesting. He also has a lot of "research days" without class meetings
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was very hesitant to take this class because my interest in Modern Latin America was little to none.  But Celso is so passionate about what he teaches that I found myself engrossed in it as well.  Super caring, fair grading, very organized, interesting, and easy to talk to.  Class participation is important, so make sure you do the reading.

Celso is one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. He has clear lectures, and all tests and quizzes are open note and open book for the most part. His lectures are engaging and make you think, and he's a very fair grader overall. If possible I would take more courses with him.

Professor Castilho is probably the most eloquent and intelligent lecturer I've had at Vanderbilt. A semester after finishing his class, I find myself using phrases and ideas that I picked up from him when discussing things completely unrelated to Brazil. The class is easy: weekly reading quizzes and open-note essays. Show up and participate

Really nice guy, lot of reading, but if you do it you will do well in the class. Class isn't too boring, and he does a good job of keeping the class engaged. If you try pretty hard, you can definitely get an A- or A.
Great professor who is really approachable.  He gave us really useful ways to improve our writing and critical thinking skills.  If you must take HIST 200W, take his section!

This class (modern latin american history) has an enormous amount of reading. Be prepared to print lots of articles. I learned a lot and enjoyed the lectures, but I'm still not sure how to write papers that he would like.

Interesting class but a lot of the reads are classics you may have read before. Heavy on the reading and discussions are just summaries basically. I think there were 3 short papers and some outlines. Tichi is not afraid to call you out for anything. Once you get past that its an easy class, especially if you express your grade expectations to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's super lenient about grading papers. If you're looking for in-depth or critical discussions about books or social issues, this isn't the class for you. I felt like I was in a middle school english class sometimes - we didn't go much further than summarizing the books we read. She has some odd personality quirks, but overall an easy A.

She is a terrible professor, just in that the lectures do not bring more to the table than you could have easily gotten on your own; very base knowledge. she is extremely unorganized and speaks down on students. Class was interesting due solely to my fellow students. Otherwise, the class was snooze-worthy. Papers are elementary. Bad attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's actually a really awesome professor. Kind of scatterbrained at times, but has good intentions. Will call you out for not doing the reading. She is super straightforward about what she wants on her papers. Just be engaging with her and she will definitely show how much she cares. Pretty much an easy A, and the topics were all very interesting

I liked Tichi a lot.. She was always willing to help! She really cares about your abilities as a writer. I definitely improved! Not too much writing, a lot of reading. Take her for your writing class! The subjects were interesting!

Professor Tichi was amazing and this was my favorite class of the semester. She is super laid back and energetic. You can tell she really loves teaching & I think that makes all the difference. This class is heavily discussion based so come ready to talk. Don't skip class. Also papers can be unclear so make sure you ask for help and you'll do well

Prof Tichi is extremely knowledgable and personable. She takes the effort to get to know her student, and all the readings she selected were about real world issues. It takes a considerable amount of effort to get a good grade, but it's totally doable -  in the end all the effort is so worth it!

Love Professor Tichi - she is an amazaing instructor.  We read awesome 19th century novels and she really gets the wheels turning in your head.  I more than enjoyed the class discussions.  She requires weekly papers.

Professor Tichi is one of the best English professors I have had. She chose great books with a variety of themes and kept the discussions interesting. She does assign a lot of writing, but the assignments were honestly so fun I enjoyed writing them. Also, she is very understanding of students' schedules and was accommodating to the whole class.

I took a special topics course with her: Jack London and Edith Wharton. It has been an amazing course, and I have learned a lot about some of my favorite books. She is very approachable and is very friendly. I loved her application of the literature to real-life events. Her class has definitely been one of my favorites so far.
AMAZING professor. If you are an English major or not at Vandy, Tichi has a way of captivating your interest while improving your critical thinking and writing skills. I highly recommend her classes.

Pretty easy grader, plus you can revise a paper.  Hates people who don't go to class- refused to let one kid speak b/c he skipped so many classes, so go to class and talk some and you will get a good grade.

you would not believe how laid back a prof she was...VERY nice grader if you show you have genuine interest in the subject i am even surprised by my level of interest in the matter even though the class has ended...i would DEF recommend her class!!! she puts the material into real world context its VERY worthwhile

Most of the time, a very kind woman; she's very passionate about what she teaches. She genuinely wants her students to learn and to care about today's society and knows that the change that goes on in our minds is the most important thing. She's very knowledgeable about a lot of issues.

I took this class because a 118W was recommended for first year English majors. Unfortunately, the class did absolutely nothing to advance my learning of English. She is a fairly interesting professor and I enjoyed learning about current issues, but I felt like the class was kind of a waste of my time.

Love her. Shes pretty liberal and her books are great. There were a lot of them and she expects you to do a lot of reading a week. We had the total of 6 papers, but she made the last two pretty simple. Very smart, and she doesnt want her students to graduate naiive. Not that bad grader. Gives opportunity for extra credit. Office hours help alot!!

The textbooks she picks out is so much more intereseting than other 118W coures. Refreshing change from the VandyBubble- actually get to talk about REAL LIFE, REAL Issues. Fair grader just talk to her. she is a sweetheart.

She definitely makes you work for your grade.. expect to write a paper a week in response to the reading. But she is a fair grader and keeps class very interesting with videos, handouts, pictures, current events discussions etc. Vibrant would probably the best word to describe her!
No Comments

She really makes you think about issues. She pushes you to think and actually learn something, not just memorize and learn nonsense. I totally recommend her.. She's just a really nice professor too.. She really cares about her students...

I took her because I heard she was easy.  It wasn't worth it.  Her class was so pointless.  I learned nothing.  It's a waste of time to go, but you have to.  She doesn't care about helping you write better or the study of literature.  Take 118 instead.
awsome teacher, does voice her political views but who cares, fun class

If you're a gifted writer or an avid reader, don't waste your time here.  She doesn't care about literature - she just uses English classes as a forum for various conspiracy theories and political rants.

Pushes the liberal, democratic agenda all class, every class.  Does not promote political dialogue; patent that *her* views are the right ones, end of discussion. Definitely not for serious English students.
She may be easy, but she's full of herself.  Don't ask questions or talk in class, because she won't listen.
very intelligent, funny, interesting! love the class
she is one of the most intelligent professors that i have ever have.
she is so cute and eccentric, extremely knowledgable and with-it, and ridiculously understanding.  great class/interesting readings.  i highly recommend any class she teaches.
The easiest 200-level course I've taken, and interesting too.  Go for a small class with her, you'll have fun and learn quite a bit

Cecilia is the most wonderful person on the planet. She curates her teaching style to specific student needs and genuinely cares about her students' learning. She connects with students on a human level and goes out of her way to address individual weaknesses without embarrassing students or being condescending. I could not recommend her enough.

Professor Mo is very knowledgeable in her field. I took her for a FYWS so the structure was much different. She focused a lot on the content of Human Trafficking but didn't address the writing process as much, which was the sole part of our final grade. She's an extremely tough grader but the final paper will usually boost your grade a full letter.

Way too much reading (don't do it, just BS your way through). She's helpful outside of class. A super tough grader and very nit-picky when grading papers. It's not an easy class so you should be interested in the subject if you want to take it. The topics got repetitive about halfway through the semester. I wouldn't take the class again.

Professor Mo is an outstanding professor who truly cares about her students. Reading requirements can be rigorous but doable. She acknowledges and rewards improvements on written assignments. She is always willing and able to assist after class or during office hours. Take Professor Mo's classes if you can!

If possible, avoid this professor. She's nice, but her expectations are absolutely ridiculous. We often had 50-100+ pages of reading per class (all of which she  expected us to complete), had pop quizzes with obscure details on them and the final exam was horribly long.  If you work hard, an A or a B is possible, but finishing everything is not.

He's probably past his prime. Lectures are dry, random, and not very helpful. Plus, sometimes he will just say something that is wrong. His textbook is very good though, and honestly far more useful than lectures. Everything on tests is worded weirdly so you're never totally sure what he's asking. Curves are pretty nice though.

This is an excellent class to satisfy a W-level requirement. There is not a single lecture. You just sit down and Buckles guides a lecture. Super great to bounce ideas around as a small class and he helps you really understand how the history of economic policy and what we should do now and in the future. Don't let his intro reviews scare you away

Lectures are unnecessary, but his online textbook is brilliant. It completely removes the need for you to ever show up. The content is pretty simple. As long as you read and do the practice in the online textbook, all of his exams should be pretty simple.
Prof. Buckles's lecture helped me to review what I had learned before in macroeconomics and link everything together by applying the theory in daily news. Thank you Prof. Buckles.
Hard. Unhelpful. Awful. If you can get another professor, do it. Otherwise, delay the class a semester if possible

Overall not a good professor at all. Bad lectures, doesn't explain the material on the test, you literally study only from his textbook. Honestly, I learn much more from youtube videos than from his boring lectures. Weekly quizzes, two essay papers, midterms, and final. Sucks. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS.

DO NOT TAKE BUCKLES FOR MICRO. He gets extremely confused about what he is teaching and his exams are unnecessarily hard and contain content that he never covered in class. His lectures make absolutely no sense and he rambles on and on about irrelevant content or stuff he doesn't even understand. He gets points kind of friendly

absolute hell. Never take a class with him. You will learn absolutely nothing. Super boring lectures with quizzes and tests full of tricky questions. I WISH I trusted the feedback of other students. It was my only option and I had to take it but I wish I never did. It's time for him to retire. I want him out of my life and I f.... hate him.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures were so confusing and disorganized that I learned more from reading the textbook and got more confused going to class. For an intro class, the concepts were easy yet his lectures and tests made even the simplest concepts crazy complex. This INTRO class made me doubt my major. DO NOT take!

Stephen Buckles is like my grandpa. I love my grandpa, but idk if I'd wanna learn microeconomics from him. Lectures have a lot of tangents, not a fan, and maybe 1 or 2 things can be taken from class. Easy to read textbook- vv useful. Does not deserve the hate he gets, kids are lazy and his curve is wild, but ur likely gonna get shafted on frq.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy who wrote a fantastic textbook but is sadly pulled down by useless lectures and stingy TAs. A is achievable if you just read the textbook and learn how the TAs grade free response. You can still get points off for them if Ben's having a bad day though, sadly. Weekly quizzes, a couple of papers, two midterms, and a final.

He's a nice guy but is way too old to still be teaching. He doesn't know how to use lecture slides. He prints out notes and projects the paper notes onto the board using a camera. I took micro in high school and figured this would be an easy A but ended up having to do quite a bit of work to do ok in the class. Buckles wrote the book so its helpful

DO NOT TAKE AT ALL COSTS. I ignored advice that other students had given me to avoid Buckles because I was just taking him to fulfill an econ requirement and it was the worst decision I've made at Vanderbilt. He's decent if you ignore ~everything~ about his teaching. If a single student enrolls in Buckle's intro course, society has failed

There is no point in going to class, his lectures are boring and he mumbles gibberish. His quizzes and tests are very hard but he has a very nice curve so it is very hard to get below a B- in this class. I would recommned just reading from the textbook during his class time to replace lectures and for the weekly quizzes be strategic ;)

Professor Buckles is undoubtedly the worst professor I have ever had. He is a nice man but his classes are utterly useless and the quizzes/tests he gives are full of trick questions. He teaches many incorrect things in class and then gives quizzes on the material expecting students to know answers to questions about which he taught incorrect info.
Bad lecturer. Very boring, making it hard to pay attention. Tests are hard but he curves everything SO MUCH.
Buckles is very much like a grandpa. He's adorable and kind of iconic, but is constantly a little confused. Would you want to learn microeconomics from your grandpa? Me neither.
Hilarious professor, very anecdotal, and super cute...
Hes verbally and mentally slow

I love Buckles. Brilliant teacher who wants his students to truly understand economics. His intro classes provide a solid foundation for future learning. Trust the guy - Go to class or at least take an hour out of your week to read the textbook. Tests are straight out of the book and pretty easy if you don't skip class and cram. Heavily curved

One of the worst experiences ever. An easy class made difficult by an incompetent professor. Buckles clearly did not know how to use technology with graphs done on paper being held up to the laptop camera. His test questions were difficult to understand, even if the concept was easy. Buckles also wrote the textbook which is poorly written.

I really struggled with a class that would be relatively easy for me if I had another professor. My advice, just don't take him. Everything is unclear, from grading, lectures etc. He makes us purchase his own textbook which is not even that great at explaining concepts. Absolute worst class and I'm not even kidding.

By far the absolute worst class I have ever taken, and I went to a pretty trash highschool. After tests and quizzes I was ALWAYS left wondering how we were expected to know the answers. I read his book very carefully but he would ask things that were never discussed in class or his book. Tbh a total trainwreck of a class. GPA buster. Avoid! :(

He still did not know how to share his screen after an entire year in a pandemic  fine, some people have a hard time adapting to new technology. However, when he blames confusing test questions and poor class performance on online school instead of accepting the blame for being an incompetent professor  it is completely unacceptable.

Do not take this class for intro to micro. Tests and quizzes were so unnecessarily difficult and you have no idea what your grade in the class is because he just gives letter grades. We also never got our grades from the final back. If you have to take micro and he is the only option, wait a semester and take it with someone else. Seriously.

The lectures were incredibly difficult to follow, and it got to the point where I stopped going altogether and read the textbook. The tests were massively curved and somewhat confusing, along with the weekly quizzes. If you already know micro, take him and don't go to class. If you don't take someone else.

Pretty sure the pandemic and the transition to online learning have done a number on this guy's ability to teach. Clear that he cares a lot about students' learning, but the class is extremely disorganized (barely makes use of Brightspace), it takes forever to get grades back, and honestly I have no sense of what grade I will get in this class.

Terrible Professor. Maybe is accomplished, but cannot teach an intro-level class for his life. Grading criteria for exams is extremely unclear, lectures are useless (he spends more time on tangents than actually explaining class material), and TAs are god awful. Spend time memorizing his textbook, as that's all that seems to work for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: gotta be the worst class ive taken here my man doesnt communicate at all, and no one ever has any idea what specifically he's looking for in his essay questions. would drop a 0 if i could

I can't really put into words how much I dislike this class. The lectures will actually confuse you more, and his questions are so badly worded that a 50% on a test is often equal to an A or B. You would learn just as much if you just read the textbook on your own time. The only thing this class will accomplish for you is giving you unneeded grief.

Buckles's macro policy seminar is a great option for an upper level econ class--people are turned off by their memories of buckles in the intros, but the seminar is where he really shines. The whole class consists of discussions of current events, two in class essays that are essentially policy recommendations, and a final paper, so not too bad.

Did not have a good experience. His lectures are boring and didn't help me in the slightest. I relied on his textbook mostly. He isn't accessible and provides shaky direction at best. Totally oblivious to the needs and experience of his students. Not only that, but he messed up many of the final grades and now won't discuss it until August.

Maybe he was once a great teacher and economist as the other reviews say. Maybe he once could teach a class without forgetting/messing up all of the material. Not anymore. He repeatedly loses tests, gives incorrect grades, and does many other careless actions. Avoid at all costs.

Unclear grading criteria. Lectures are dull and move too slowly. Attendance is mandatory but I feel like I got more confused by going to lecture. Read textbook and do practice questions. Tests try to be tricky, but not in a good way. Questions can be extremely unclear. Short answer criteria are specific so its possible to fail with the right answer

Professor Buckles is one of the kindest professors out there but I wouldn't recommend taking his class unless you have to. His tests are insanely difficult. He takes forever to give you your grade back. The quizzes are okay but you essentially teach yourself and I'd skip lecture because he rambles and goes on tangents.

The course itself is quite interesting, but it should not be taught by Buckles. Very nice and genuine guy, but his lectures are awful. The way he grades quizzes and tests are obscure, and will not explicitly tell you what your average is. Terrible at responding to emails. You are better off just reading the textbook, and not going to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Super nice dude. Really cares about the students. But, he is not clear, confuses everyone (including himself) during class, and only answers emails half of the time. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is helpful for the 10 minutes of class that he explains the concepts.

Professor Buckles is extremely hard to follow while lecturing. He rambles on and on about asinine tangents that are unrelated to the Economic chapters. The required online textbook for the class is extremely hard to follow and very disorganized, while it must be used for the class since he cannot teach the materials. Quizzes are extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: People are too concerned about grades when it comes to Stephen Buckles. Yes, his test/quiz questions can be ambiguous (as econ often is), but if you read the textbook and understand it you should be fine, there are HUGE curves. All Buckles wants to do is get you to think like an economist, and that is more valuable than you think.

Buckles is really bad in lecture. Avoid going to class if you can. I found his tests to be difficult and filled with tricky wording. A lot of times a multiple choice question would require you to know two different things, which really gave me a bad time.

Buckles's intro econ classes are not too hard, but his lectures are dreadfully boring. His TAs and office hours are not very helpful either. Ghandi is teaching the class next year, but if Buckles comes back, take him and read the textbook (which is good), but don't expect much else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A nice guy but he absolutely can't teach. He is all over the place and going to lectures is pretty useless. If you read the textbook you should be okay, but he and the TAs just are not good at teaching the material. Wish vanderbilt would do better.

Just 0 intuition and practical understanding of economics from Buckles. TAs aren't much better. I had hoped Vanderbilt had more to offer than Neoliberal garbage in their econ departments. As far as a grade, if you know an iota of economics, getting a B is a joke. If you want an A, memorize his stupid textbook and regurgitate it on the tests.
Buckles is a legend, use his textbook and if you don't understand go to lectures. His tests aren't very difficult but you have to work a little. Buckles a sav

These are the keys to this class. 1. Show up to class 0 times unless it's a test day 2. Read the book as he assigns it, very, very carefully. 3. Study a decent amount for the quizzes or tests. If you do these things, an A is extremely, extremely doable.
Buckles is a very insightful teacher. You get what you put in for this class, so you have to put in the effort to see results. He is very helpful if you go to office hours.

This class is probably the best upper level econ one can take. Not too hard. Learn a ton about relevant topics. Not many graded things. Grade more based off being in class and adding to the discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The professor does not know how to teach. There was one day where the TAs went up, and it was painfully obvious that they were better than the professor. To be frank, the professor's classes are boring. However, passing the class isn't that difficult as long as you do the practice questions for each chapter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His exams and quizzes are usually tricky and wordplay. His lecture and test questions tend to be confusing and playing around your thoughts regardless of how much you study and learn. His textbook does help! I would recommend not to take his class if you want to find inspiration to fuel your econ interest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I don't think I quite ever learned how to take his quizzes/exams, or how to think exactly like him, which feels like the expectation sometimes. Read the book, go to class and take notes, and then read the book like four more times and you should be good to go. Sometimes, the lectures are pretty entertaining, and he is clearly passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Buckles is a good guy with humor and very knowledgeable about economics. But he is definitely not a good teacher. He has no idea what he is teaching. You need to read textbook yourself for tests. He uses his own textbook which has a lot of flaws and typos. Tophat attendance counts for small percent of grade. Three test and quizzes every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not going to lie, it's hard to get an A, but an A- or B+ is doable. GO TO OFFICE HOURS to ask for points back on open responses. Textbook teaches you most things, but he's a very nice professor who tries to keep the class engaged. Attendance is part of the grade, but not a huge amount.

This man has been teaching for so long that he is bored with the material and fails to teach an intro-level class effectively. The lectures are ineffective because he often gets side tracked by unnecessary concepts that are difficult to understand. The textbook is good and straightforward but is not reflective of material covered on tests.

Professor Buckles is a nice professor. However, the content in his class is confused and quite different from his exams. His exams are tricky and difficult. A knowledgeable professor but maybe not suitable for basic economic classes.

Buckles is a great guy. Very charismatic and knows what he is talking about. Unfortunately, it will be difficult to understand this class unless you have taken some sort of econ beforehand. His lectures are confusing and he explains things in a way only he can understand. Would not recommend if you have not taken econ before.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but his lectures are so confusing. He mostly asks questions and leaves you to figure out the answer during class. Plus, the textbook is written by him so it doesn't help much. The curve on every quiz/test is VERY generous though, so not hard to get a solid B with minimal effort. Do not take if you actually want to understand econ.

Why Buckles is still teaching at a top 15 school is beyond me. Oh wait, it's because he's been here since the 70's and has tenure. Buckles is senile, and barely understands the economic concepts he teaches. He cannot write test questions for his life and seems to condone widespread teaching (phones out, taking tests outside the room) in his class.

Buckles is the best professor I had in the economics department. Not sure why there are some negative comments on here, but probably those are mostly from people who just didn't do well and are entitled. Buckles is clear, memorable, and funny. I remembered a lot of his stories and examples well after the class was over. Absolutely would take again.

Horrible teacher. You can go to every class, study for days, understand the textbook and information inside and out, and still completely fail the tests and quizzes due to terribly worded questions, completely arguable answers, and inconsistent/unstructured short answer grading from the TAs. He is not helpful in office hours. Don't take.

Not a huge fan of his teaching style. Lectures aren't all that helpful and a bit dull, and you're better off reading and re-reading. Quizzes can vary a lot in difficulty. Tests aren usually fine, and there's usually a curve. Overall, the class is fine and not super hard but you probably aren't going to fall in love with econ or anything.
His lecturing style is not for everyone and his tests and quizzes are worded kind of bad, but beyond that, great teacher with charisma and knowledge.

Not until you go through the whole semester that you'll realize how good Buckles is. His lectures may not be that effective or clear, but the textbook and online quizzes should be enough for you to grasp the picture of prins of macro. Tests are doable with enormous curves. He is your best choice for 1010 by far if you care about how much you learn.

his lectures helped me understand the material much better, even though sometimes theyre a bit dry. pay attention though because he says exactly what the essays will be. also, definitely do the multiple choice questions at the end of the section because they help a ton on the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: I ended up reading the textbook like 8 or 9 times through by the time the final came around. Reading and rereading and memorizing the what he says in the textbook is key to doing welll. have to put in a LOT of independent work

Buckles's lectures barely help you understand what you are tested on. Read the textbook and fill in everything, and if you do not understand something go to office hours. Do not need to go to class but answer all top hat questions. Tests are difficult and you really need to understand the concepts to do well. Very specific grader on writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The textbook is really important for this class, so read it and do the problems. His lectures range from very interesting to average. Overall, he is funny and he will answer all questions you bring to him. I cannot recommend him because 75% of the questions are tricky (worded weirdly or requiring topics not yet learned). Take Luea if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Students taking ECON 1010 with Buckles should consider his lecture as an emphasis to the reading assignments that are supposed to be read prior to be coming to class. If you complete and understand the assigned reading, you should do fine in this class, considering the generous curves. Relying on lectures to spoon feed you and you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Buckles lectures are really confusing and not very helpful at all. The textbook is basically your only way of passing the class. He does curve generously though
I've taken Econ before, so this class was pretty easy. He uses Top Hat, so I came to class when I didn't need to probably
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Textbook is great! But Buckles' lectures are very confusing, he spends most of class talking about one small topic and were left to learn the more difficult topics on our own.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Boring and useless lecture. Really need to read the book to do well.

Some ratings here are not honest at all. Indeed, the course relies heavily on the textbook (you will want to read it for at least three times), but Buckles' lectures can be very good emphasis on the material. He is passionate and also very willing to help. A perfect performance is almost impossible, but he gives generous curves. High recommend.

Buckles is the guy in charge of weeding-out prospective econ majors. If you want to truly learn the basics and principles of Economics, he's your guy. However, if you think your GPA's more important, you probably shouldn't take him.

Buckles is a well-liked professor, but what he teaches in lectures and what he tests students on is very different. He has to generously curve every quiz and exam so it's not terrible, but the textbook is definitely more important than the lectures. Attendance is only 3% and he doesn't teach much in class, so definitely not mandatory (recommended).

Professor Buckles is great! Really smart guy. Quizzes/paper are easy but make up a small portion of your grade. Participation is 3% (clicker q's) so go to class. Everything's based on the book, so read it and fill it in. Tests are tough, and questions are confusing. Generous curves somewhat make up for difficulty. Go to office hours, it might help.

Buckles may have once been a great professor, but his mind is starting to slip. Makes clear errors during lectures. Often has to reassign credit on tests because his questions are incorrect. All test questions are "trick" questions that are worded in an incredibly confusing way. If you can avoid Buckles, do it.

Buckles is awesome. He is VERY clear about his expectations and if you read the book and listen to lectures you can get an A. Go to class to answer the clicker questions because they are more important than they seem.
Buckles was the most inspirational professor I have ever had. Enjoyed his lecture every single time.

Professor Buckles is a respected professor at Vanderbilt. Some people complain about his class but it is not that bad for an responsible Vanderbilt student. If you do the readings and self-quizzes, a B+ to A- is attainable, and an A is attainable is you are really on top of this class. His curves are generous.

Buckles is a great professor. Really makes you understand the material to do well. Tests are tough. Quizzes are easy, but aren't worth that much. Go to TA hours. Read his textbook thoroughly and carefully, because the class revolves around it. Attendance is only 3% (through clicker questions), but skip and you won't do well. Buckles is awesome!

Buckles is one of the most well-known Vanderbilt professors, and he is great at what he does. His lectures are engaging and generally quite clear, though sometimes he will struggle with more difficult concepts or in answering questions from the students. If you're willing to work for it, you can do very well. I would highly recommend his classes.

Buckles is an amazing professor that really cares about his students learning. His wrote his own textbook that is pretty clear and gives all the information you will need for the class. The tests are tough, but reasonable. Improved performance throughout the semester will be rewarded by him bumping up your letter grade at the end of the semester.

He's often unclear about what he wants in questions on tests & TAs grade tests inconsistency & too harshly. But Buckles is brilliant-the way he teaches econ gets to the heart of things & really helps you understand what's going on. Going to class isn't necessary (40% of class doesn't) but it's difficult to do well if you skip (lots get Cs &Ds)

His lectures are definitely very helpful to understanding the material. He wrote the textbook, and you can get by with just that, but it's very dense and very dull. He can be kind of confusing, but overall it's okay. He stays after class to answer questions. Curves are ridiculous, but tests are still difficult. Papers are easy though.

Buckles is great. You'll have to work for it but if you do, your grade will reflect the effort you put in. Attending his office hours (not TA's) will bump your grade up and also make you like the class more.

The class is hard, but if you read the book (Buckles wrote it) and show up to class you should be fine. There are clicker questions every class that count for credit to give you more incentive to show up. Buckles can be kind of confusing but I personally enjoyed the class and the way he explains things.

Buckles is generally either hated or very well-liked by students depending on if you can see past the specificity of accepted answers for test responses or the generally confusing wording of his questions and lectures. Makes you view econ as how people think. Textbook is definitely required. Tests/everything else curved A LOT
Nice guy, tries very hard to be helpful whenever he can. Questions are frequently poorly or confusingly written. Focuses almost entirely on understanding and intuition rather than actual formulas.

Buckles is an incredibly good teacher making sure that not only do you understand what would happen in the economy, but also why it would happen. Listen to his examples in class and use these on the tests. Tests/quizzes are very specific to what he wants so make sure you pay attention to exactly what he wants you to say. This is usually in the book
This class is definitely doable but you'll have to work for the good grade. Work hard and it's yours.

Professor Buckles is a really well known professor at Vanderbilt. His Introductory Microeconomics class is difficult for some, but doesnt have to be. The TA's are very helpful and always provide clarification to any questions you might have about one of Buckles' lectures or readings. To do well in the class, you'll have to rely heavily on the book.

Buckles is a really nice guy who knows a ton about economics, but isn't the clearest in lectures or office hours. He also uses his own textbook. Tests aren't impossible but often very confusing in the way they are written. Definitely possible to do well but it won't be a super smooth ride, especially if you didn't take econ in high school.
Avoid if you can

I took 100 and 101 with Buckles, and I will say that he is a great lecturer, but the TA grading of essays can be a bit random.  Tests, however, are heavily curved, making A's possible, though still not particularly easy.  I would recommend his class if you are an Econ major, as he really knows his stuff!

I don't know why people are saying that Buckles is an Econ master. He certainly does not prove that by the way he incoherently rambles on in class. His tests would be straight forward if he did knew how to write coherent sentences and did not give you multiple answers on MC that were correct.

Buckles is an economic genius, and his lectures are intriguing, but he can sometimes be confusing, and he has some idiosyncrasies that make his tests difficult -- especially the essays, which are graded arbitrarily and harshly.  Grading seems random, but the B-range is easily attainable.  A's are hard to come by.  Great textbook, useful office hrs.

A hard intro level course. Essay questions are graded harshly and tough, and some MCQs can be tricky. Read the book several times and take notes during class. ALWAYS pay attention to his clicker questionsreview questions in lectures. Not an easy A but I learned so much even though I took micro in school. You'll never get bored in Buckles' class!

Great professor, difficult class, but not impossible. If you put in the work, you can get by with an okay grade at the very least. Tests are curved, and Buckles can be very entertaining. Don't be scared off by him.

Very difficult class, but it is doable. He does curve every test, so that is helpful. Lectures are pretty interesting. While you may hear terrifying things about Buckles, I promise if you put in the work you can handle it. I had never taken an econ class before and made it through with a B+.

If you think the practice questions in the textbook and questions on the quizzes are hard, wait until you get the test. This class is not about learning economics, it is about learning Buckle's contradictory and seemingly random train of thought. He writes the book himself but, it is written as confusingly as his lectures. TAs are useless

He is clearly very knowledgable but has trouble clearly expressing himself, let alone at a level an introductory course requires. He requires that you use a textbook he wrote for the class. It is written in the same unclear and contradictory as his lectures are. He is notorious for not answering his emails. Helpfulness of TAs varies greatly.
