Buckles is tough, but this class will challenge you and help you be a better student. If you're into actually learning, take him.

Dr. Buckles is a Vanderbilt legend. While I know a lot of students who would say that Buckles is unnecessarily tough or only gives Cs, this is not true. If you read the text and study a lot for each test, it is possible to do very well in this class. Buckles is funny and interesting, although lectures are by no means mandatory.
often contradicts himself, tests are brutal study textbook

Buckles sometimes isn't clear, and if you haven't taken econ before, its difficult to understand the connections he makes. The tests and quizzes are a tough, and you have to plan ahead in terms of office hours because of the lines. It's an ok class to take if you're interested in the subject, but if its not required for your major, don't take it.

Buckles is interesting but there's nothing in lectures that one can't get out of the textbook. Weekly quizzes help to boost your grade if you keep up with the reading. Taking old practice tests (as he suggests) was the best thing I could have done for my grade. Papers are easy - going to TA sessions for help with the papers typically ensures high A
Not an easy A by any means but very doable if you do your reading and attend lecture

ECON100 with Prof. Buckles is good, but a mixed bag in some ways.  Buckles explains material pretty clearly, but then asks somewhat vague multiple-choice questions on testsquizzes.  Grading isn't too hard but is indecipherably arbitrary on essay questions.  Buckles is very helpful and friendly outside of class.  Class is enormous so rely on TAs.

His essay questions are graded by T.A.'s who seem to take points off randomly.  He has insane curves, mostly because his tests are pretty difficult.  Non-econ majors should think twice about taking this class, as it is definitely not a walk in the park.

Really nice guy and willing to help if you need it. Long line for his office hours so get there early. He is incredibly smart, but definitely hard for an intro level micro-econ course. Expects a lot of his students but I feel smarter after his class. Difficult  because he writes the textbook and then uses the same words in class to explain.

I was debating whether or not to use my AP credit and skip Macroeconomics because of its rumored difficulty. I am absolutely glad that I didn't. You will have to work in Professor Buckles' class, but it will be worth it. After you're done with his class, you will understand economics like you have never before. I strongly recommend it.

Prof. Buckles is a great lecturer: engaging, funny, and clear. His textbook carries this voice and is very helpful and a great foundation. It's unfortunately not enough. TAs grade the assignments, and unclear grading standards will lead to knowledgeable students failing for simply not explaining with enough detail. Go to class!

Buckles is notorious for a reason. His class is tough and he's not just going to hand out good grades- you have to work for it. That said, this was one of the most rewarding classes I have taken at Vandy. His lectures can be unclear, but if you go to class and read the textbook thoroughly you will do well.

Buckles's lectures are always pretty interesting and he really gets his students to know macro concepts well. However, Short answers on essays are often worded very weirdly and have nothing to do with class, and they are graded very harshly.  Buckles seems to try to make easy material unnecessarily hard. avoid this class if you can.

I got an A but even after having taken Econ before, this class made me work hard. NOT AN EASY A! The best way to study is being thorough with the textbook, sample exams and online quizzes. Be sure to keep notes for long and harshly graded essay questions. MCQs are not that bad. Econ majors-take this class as Buckles drills concepts into your brain

If you do not ave to take Buckles Econ, I would skip it, or take it PF later on. That said, this is a great class. You learn a ton, Buckles is the man, and his textbook is amazing! Know the  textbook well and you will have a good knowledge of Macro Econ. That said, lectures are sometimes boring and often useless. Tough Grading, Tough Class.

Buckles is a good lecturer, but the class is terrible.  The material isn't too hard, but  it's almost impossible to get full credit on the tests' essays because of how harshly the TA's grade, so it's hard to get above a B. You won't know your exact overall grade until the semester ends; everything is curved.  Don't take if not an econ major

I absolutely love econ, but this class is very difficult. Despite the grade I received, it was one of my favorite classes. Be prepared to work hard. There are weekly quizzes (sometimes a short paper instead), 3 midterms and one exam. Go to class in order to figure out how Buckles thinks, and read the book to understand the concepts.

If you took AP econ in hs & got credit for this class, do not take it thinking you will get an easy A out of it. AP is graph based and Buckles is all verbal (making it hard to understand if you learned it graphically). Very specific with short answer questions on exams. Weekly quizzes. Understanding guy and interesting though! Go to his offie hours

This class takes a lot of effort. You have to do the work outside of class and attend class consistently. Lecture is most based on the textbook he wrote. Tests are very hard, especially in the given amount of time. Essay question grading is very tough, MC questions are difficult. Overall, not an easy class, but you know what's expected going in.

I know I'm in the minority here, but I cannot stand Buckles as a professor. Because he wrote his own textbook and what he says in lecture is pretty much a repetition of the textbook, you only hear things one way, which sucks if you dont understand the way he teaches. Test questions are confusing, so are quizzes. Funny guy, but confusing as hell.

Buckles is an extremely knowledgeable and humble man, and he is clearly passionate about his class. Participation credit (which is about 3%) is obtained from attending lecture and using clickers, and there are weekly online quizzes that cover 1-2 chapters of material, and there are three exams and one final. While exams are tough, the curves help.

Buckles is very enthusiastic about economics but he does a poor job of being clear about concepts. He often presents questions and never answers them. The exam are tough and essays lose arbitrary amounts of points. I recommend taking it passfail to save your GPA.
Doesn't set you up to fail. Curves al tests. You don't try, you don't pass.

Professor Buckles seems to really enjoy Economics. Although the lectures are large, he does his best to keep the class actively engaged. Test questions may be unclear and confusing, but he gives a large curve.
great  to the gut
Really good professor. Help me a lot. Choose this professor and you will never regret.

Buckles is the man. It was truly a joy to attend his lectures. Make sure to really know the textbook material - this will go a long way to helping you on the tricky multiple choice questions. Make your essay answers as detailed as possible (again, using textbook info) and you will do fine. Exams are graded on a curve.

Do the work (practice problems/online quizzes) and you'll get a good grade. I loved Buckles, and he was super helpful during office hours. Give DETAILED essay responses like the samples in the book, and you'll do fine with grading. He closes polling for clicker questions too fast, which is annoying because clicker questions = attendance points.

This class was incredibly easy however professor Buckles is the worst professor I have had. He is boring and unclear on many concepts. It is best to just read the text book and the test questions are from the book and he barely changes tests from previous years.

Buckles makes Economics come alive in lecture and often provides hints for exam free response, so go to class (attendance points too). Exams are progressively weighted, so you're rewarded for improvement. However, if you don't study properly, you'll likely to do worse on other exams. If you read and ask questions in office hours, you'll be fine.

Phenomenal professor who is so passionate about economics. The class is hard but you learn so much which makes it worthwhile. Lectures are unclear but the textbook is amazing. He is a great guy who is willing to help his students. You can read the textbook thoroughly and still do poorly bc his questions can be vague and essay grading can be unfair.
Good class, but tough for non-majors. He's a great lecturer, but a little intimidating to ask questions. Three tests, one-page papers.

Death! Extremely hard. Attendance 3%. Don't bother going because he's super unhelpful in class. Doesn't answer emails, email TAs. Very helpful in office hours though, I lived there. There's no way around him... Everyone wants to be an econ major. Hardcore weedout. Must memorize his textbook. More useful than class. No math in the class.
super hard class but interesting for those interested in economics. he never answers emails and is not very helpful but if you study a lot it is fine.
Lectures can be boring and hard to follow, but quizzes/tests aren't horrible if you read the book.  Not hard to get a B, but you need to put a lot of work in to get that A.

If you can avoid taking this class with Buckles as a teacher, I would recommend it. The lecturing isn't clear, and although Buckles does know economics very well, he explains it poorly in lecture. The grading is very picky as well.

Not difficult to get an A/A-/B+ if you put in the effort and do the problems in the textbook/online quizzes. Buckles is a great professor and is very helpful during office hours if you are unclear about the material. Go to office hours; your grade will reflect it. Buckles gets a bad rep sometimes, but he's a great professor and really knows econ.

Definitely not an easy class, but it is very possible to get an A- or A if you put the time and effort into the class. Buckles wrote the book, so reading and doing the practice problems are essential to doing well, as the exams are very similar. He is a great professor who knows econ inside and out, and office hours are very helpful.
The class is interesting and Buckles definitely knows what he's talking about but the test questions are ridiculously vague and grading is really inconsistent

Buckles can be tough, but you will leave his class knowing Economics inside and out. Treat his book like the Bible, do not fall behind on the readings, and be obsessed with knowing the step-by-step processes. It is certainly possible to get an A or A- in his class, but by no means easy. The only reason I went to class was for the clicker q's,
Make sure you read the textbook! He wrote the book, and it helped me in class significantly more than his lectures. Never went to lecture, just read the book and ended up doing well in the class.

Professor Buckles undoubtedly knows what he's talking about, but that doesn't always translate over to the students. He often asks questions and then never answers them. His lectures can be intriguing, but it is usually hard to pay attention. The book is a better source.
Exams are tough, but curve is generous. Relies on book. Class lecture is interesting/entertaining but not mandator
Humorous and interesting professor. Smart, wrote our textbook. Some problems can be confusing, but doesn't need a lot of time to figure it out.

Professor Buckles is a genius who likes to hear himself talk. His class was difficult to concentrate in although he covers all necessary material. Depending on the TA you get grading standards vary widely. The textbook is helpful if you can overlook the masses newspaper articles he includes. You must do the reading and homework in this class.

Buckles is just great. I'm actually feelIng sad when I finished my last class with him today. I wish he is gonna teach some upperclass-level classes so I could take his classes again. Anyway, some people  might find his lectures vague or hard to follow, in which case I would definitely suggest reading the textbook, which is so clear.

A hard class, but nonetheless, you will learn so much.  The textbook is your biggest ally here.  Buckles is a professor who is passionate about the subject and a really nice guy, but can struggle with being too vague in his lectures and on tests/quizzes.  Go to office hours with him when you can!!

Buckles is a decent lecturer but is not very clear.  The lecturers don't really help and the exam essays seem to be graded differently based on the TAs.  The TAS are worthless and not helpful at all.  I would not recommend this class to anyone unless you have to take it.  This has been the worst class I've taken at Vanderbilt

If you don't enjoy Economics and/or have no plans in majoring/minoring, don't take Macroeconomics. Buckles is an outstanding lecturer, but at the end of the day, if you don't understand economics, even his accessibility can't help you. Tests and quizzes are challenging but fair if you  think intuitively. Memorizing will not help you in this class!

Buckels is fundamentally useless. He is a charismatic lecturer but he is almost never clear. The quizes and tests are confusing. When giving feedback on examinations he often says that he could have made the questions more clear. Do not take unless you have to.

Professor Buckles is really helpful and passionate. His textbook is fantastic. However, the quiz and test problems have ambiguous answers. And the grading of essay questions are inconsistent and horrible. If you get a bad grade on essay you will never get that grade back from Buckles, find T.A. instead!

A lot of people flame Buckles and it's really unjustified. Buckles is a brilliant lecturer and is incredibly accessible for help considering that he teaches about 1000 students a semester. The textbook is good and if econ is your thing, the lectures are honestly fun. Do the work and you'll get a good grade. Rewarding class.

All logic and application: "if x changes & y stays the same, what happens to z?" Allow the TAs to be your best friends; they help. The subject is very nuanced so you must consistently practice being able to look at the puzzle from all sides. The book gives the rules; the prof gives the exceptions and details. Concepts are tough; grading/testing not

Buckles and this class are absolutely horrible. I have never been so bored. He is extremely unclear on material and is incapable of giving you a straight answer to a simple question. He relies way too much on the textbooks and the TAs, but even if you pour over the text, anything higher than a C on exams is next to impossible. DO NOT DO NOT take!

I really enjoyed this class.  Buckles is a tough teacher, but if you go to class and do the work, it's not that bad.  Make sure to do the practice tests to get used to the type of questions he'll ask you!

Buckles is a fairly difficult teacher. Questions on tests are often ambiguous and grading of essay questions is very inconsistent. Going to class isn't really necessary, the textbook is the most important resource.
Really nice guy. The tests are absolutely unreasonable, though. You can understand all of the material and still get a C. You do come out knowing a lot more about econ than before, though.

Horrible class. Extremely unclear and ridiculous questions both in class and on exams. Really set up for failure. Has to give out massive curves just to get the average to a reasonable level. I would consider taking econ at a different college in the summer and transferring the credit to Vandy.
He's a nice professor, but relies too heavily on TAs outside of class.  Also he never responds after the final.

Economics is my major and I heard great things about Buckles.  I enjoyed his class but he is sometimes vague and his teaching style is... interesting.  You will have to work for an A. 3 Tests, 2 extremely short papers. Final was kinda hard. I still recommend him though, he is one of those classic Vanderbilt professors everybody has.
Very engaging lecturer. Always keep his class of 300 on their toes and excited. You learn so much in his class. Tests arent too bad just read the text.

Dr. Buckles is a great, intelligent, personable guy.  That being said ... he's a poor lecturer.  He poses clicker questions for the class to answer, but he expects you to come to the answer yourself.  He does not say the correct answer after everyone weighs in on the question.  Those questions usually end up on the tests.

This class is pretty difficult. It's nearly impossible to get full credit on the essay questions on the tests, and he takes off a huge number of points for seemingly small mistakes. However, he definitely knows the material and is helpful if you ask. It's not really that important to go to class because he restates everything in the reading.
He is very difficult, unclear in lecture and only somewhat helpful in office hours. He is so nice and a great guy but this is not an easy class at all.

Everything has already been said about this guy, but to sum up he's a great teacher, extraordinarily helpful in office hours, and you will learn more in this class than probably any other at Vanderbilt. That being said, it's difficult. Take it anyway and treat the textbook as the bible and you'll be alright.

Buckles is by far the most overrated professor on campus.  Cheating exists in this class due to the huge lecture hall and oblivious TAs.  Many of the TAs are also unhelpful.  Buckles uses his own book, which has an embarrassing amount of typos.  You will learn more than your grade reflects, but it is possible to get an A.

attending class is optional. reading & answering all mult. choice/essay questions in the textbook (that he wrote) is definitely the best investment of your time. if you do 100% of the textbook, through and through, it's reasonable to get an A/A-. his tests are hard and his mult choice ambiguous.

You really don't need to go to class to do well because he says the same things that are in the book (that he wrote), but be sure to read. I went to class just because Buckles is a great speaker and has real life application. Not at all an easy class, but you learn a lot.
Class ll be hard if you dont study. If u do then A or A- is definitely possible. Seriously even if you get a B or something like that, you will not regret for taking him afterwards.

Prof Buckles is a really popular professor. He's a good lecturer and very smart. Make sure you answer all the questions in the textbook. His multiple choice can be tricky and he expects very specific answers for essays. Overall a very manageable class.
Very nice, interesting and the nicest professor on campus. Class is only hard if you don't do the reading. Attendance is optional but it's worth going just because he's such a good professor.

He is a very good professor. His lectures are good and his teaching style is great. You will learn a lot in this class. However, the testing material is poorly structured. What he wants from you is vague, you can read a question and go the completely the opposite direction if you don't understand him. His book has clarity isses mking it hard at tim

Buckles knows his stuff.  You can take other teachers (Vrooman) and probably get by easier, but it's not worth it.  If you want to be an Econ major, TAKE BUCKLES.  The amount you will learn is absolutely worth a little more work. If you go to class and study the book well, you can get an A. He is incredibly helpful at office hours too. TAKE BUCKLES

Buckles is amazing.  His class is completely doable, thanks to the curves.  You can go to class and learn from him, or read the book and its the exact same stuff.  Either way you learn alot. HE IS AWESOME.
Just study from the textbook. Class is pointless except for clicking in

He definitely knows the subject very well.  It's necessary to read the textbook, as most of the lecture and test material is straight out of the book (Buckles writes the book).  Picky grading on essays.  It's definitely possible to get a good grade.
Great professor, really got me interested in the subject. Interesting lectures, enjoyed class. TAs are usually harsh graders but office hours are all week and they are really helpful.

Professor Buckles sometimes gets the title of "Best teacher at Vanderbilt" and he deserves it.  His interest in his own subject is outstanding and his help out of class is superb.  On top of that, he is a very reasonable person in terms of handing in work.  The class is hard, but completely worth it.  Clicker questions in class make it interesting.

Prof. Buckles has driven me to the airport 3 times. An amazing guy. His class is too big and his TAs are at times overwhelmed and unhelpful. Use them as best you can. Knowing the text is not enough to get an A.

His tests and lectures are straight from the book, which makes his class run smoothly. You always know what to expect. The final is pretty difficult, and the tests during the semester aren't easy, but you can tell he really loves econ, which is refreshing. MUCH better than Vrooman.

Need a lot of efforts to get a good grade but that's probably because it's a comprehensive class. Definitely do the sample exams online before the exams and read the textbook carefully before finals(you'd better start reviewing early!)

Great professor, incredibly smart guy. You'll learn a lot from the class, but he does grade kind of hard. Not unreasonably at all though. A lot of people get upset and say that his class is impossible to do well in, but as long as you listen to what he says when you go and read the book he writes, then youll do great.

Buckles is the man!  He is definitely not going to give out an easy A to anyone but does a great job making a somewhat boring subject interesting, relevant, and easy to understand.  I learned more in this class than in any other this semester and am looking forward to taking Micro with him in the Spring.

Great Professor. With some work, its definitely possible to get an A/A-/B+ in this classes. Buckles and his team of TAs are very helpful during office hours and willing to help you understand the material. Between the practice exam and his lectures, he pretty much tells you all the essay questions on the exam (just listen very closely).

This professor will kill your GPA. He writes his own textbook every semester, so if you do not understand his teaching style, you will also not understand the book and are doomed to make a bad grade. Although he and his TAs are accessible, he does not do a good job of explaining economic principles. In short, teaching FAIL.

The class isn't too hard if you actually take the time to read the textbook. The text is definitely more useful and informative than the lectures. Also, be sure to study the practice tests he posts online. They're very similar to the actual exams. With some effort an A is definitely possible.

Buckles is, I would say, the most knowledgeable professor at Vanderbilt. Knows everything about the subject matter, ties it in to the real world and makes sure people get it. Extremely approachable at office hours, which is the best way to understand how he wants you to think. Tests are hard but hey everyone's taking them and they are curved hugely
Greatest professor at Vanderbilt.  Hard tests but they are manageable.
Amazing.
Great lecturer. You really need to know the material to hope to get a good grade. Do all the practice stuff and learn the textbook.

Fabulous teacher, obviously one of the big names at Vanderbilt. He is a fascinating lecturer and is careful to show you real-world applications.... The class is a LOT of work though. Weekly proctored quizzes and essays, that kind of thing. But Buckles makes it worth it. Do take ! you're wasting an opportunity if you don't!

HE IS THE MAN!! great class and great professor!! you will learn a lot about econ  after the semester! The work is challenging but if you stay on top of your readings and studying ... and to the TAs if you need help it is possible to pull a low A!!  GREAT CLASS GREAT PROFESSOR!   BUCKLES IS THE MAN

Professor Buckles is extremely versed in Economics and is very passionate about the subject.  Attendance is three percent of the grade.  The lectures are mostly based on the classpack, but mostly enjoyable.  The exams are extremely difficult and even with the curve it is difficult to score well.  Weekly quizzes are also curved he drops lowest 2.

His lectures and the book are the same. No extra dimension there. His tests are EXTREMELY unreasonable. Very difficult to prep for the tests. Everyone I talk to is struggling even with a curve. Other than that, he's passionate about the subject and aways willing to help. Just PRAY your TA's speak English, otherwise office hours are useless.
Best lecturer I have had at Vanderbilt.

Buckles is a really good lecturer and you will learn a lot in his class if you are willing to try. However, don't expect your grades to reflect how much you work or how much you know, that will remain frustrating. That said he is engaging and a good teacher.

Tests are graded unreasonably.  If you are a good student and you want to be humiliated by rediculously low grades, take this class. Calculus was much easier.  If you like passing tests with 40% (on the curve) then this class is for you.  I think there is something wrong with a professor who makes tests so much harder than the practice questions

He is really no the material and knows how to teach it. His exams are EXTREMELY DIFFICULT He curve them but still almost impassible to get an A. But in the end you will know econ but it will lower ur gpa.
Extremely smart guy, has poured himself into his work. Knows everything there is to know about microecon. Absolutely take if you have any interest in econ, mandatory for majors.

An excellent teacher any way you put it. Is the material hard? I don't think it is, but there are more than a few low grades in the class. Everything revolves around the textbook, and also attend every lecture, even though attendance isn't mandatory. You will enjoy this class and you will learn a lot. Great personality, brilliant teaching approach.

Such an amazing professor. He knows his material inside and out, but the class if difficult. The tests are extremely frustrating because you must know the "Buckles' Answer" to the essay section. Definitely take if an Econ Major. You might not have the grade you want, but you will leave with a true  understanding of Economics.

Frankly, I think his lectures are overrated. That said, the material isn't as difficult as people make it out to be. He says he doesn't want you to memorize, but you do have to essentially memorize his thinking process to do well on the free-responses. Tests can be frustrating at times, but the generous grading policy makes up for them.

Not an easy A by any means. You have to make sure you understand every step in the train of thought he uses to explain concepts, but by the end you will know micro inside and out. TA's tend to lowball you on quizzes and not change the grade even if you're right. If this happens, go to Buckles. He'll listen to reason and fully explain any questions.

Such a knowledgable professor and is a great lecturer, so his classes are usually interesting. No doubt about it, it's a tough class, but if you put the time into reading the book and go to his office hours, an A is reachable.

Buckles is one of the best teachers I've ever had.  His class is difficult and he wrote the textbook himself so he knows everything.  He demands more than simple memorization.  You have to be able to analyze a great deal of info.  Very difficult, but definitely a class worth taking.

you will learn the most in this class.... but you won't necessarily have the grade to show for it. he's one of the most knowledgeable professors i've ever had at vanderbilt.... and he's hot for an old guy too.
Hard grader, but learn a lot.

Wow! Buckles is an amazing teacher. He's an absolute genius, but unless you are an ECON major, and you know for sure you are...then take the class. He's one of those teachers that while in the process of learning a lot, you will do poorly. Study hard and manipulate his office hours. A "C" is the equivalent to an "A" in his class.
Buckles is a hard teacher.  You will work the week of tests, but besides that it's not bad.  Once you get to used to his style it is not terrible. Don't be afraid of taking it, it will be worth it.
learned a ton.  killed my gpa
I learned a lot in econ 100 but it was one of the most miserable classes I've taken at Vanderbilt.

Buckles, Objectively. 1st - I admit, I learned a lot in class. However, I wouldn't rec. taking this class for a grade if you are not an econ major. Why? A) The class is 150+ people so office hrs are always full (6 A's given). B) He gives extremely difficult exams, w/ Buckles logic required. Myth: He was Reagan's economic adviser.
good professor but you have to be able to essentially memorize the book in order to do well on the free response questions, unless you're really good at econ, avoid this class

Buckles made my sophomore year miserable. I am sorry that I did not think in the same way that he did. Its not that i did not understand micrecon, it's more that i didnt undersstand his overinflated value of himself. He just likes to flaunt his supposed superiority.avoid avoid avoid like the plague and i am sorry if youre an econ major.
Good teacher. Hard on his tests but you will learn a lot. Buckles really is the man.
very smart guy, applies concepts to real life situations
you must take buckles before leaving vandy!!!! hard class, got my first B, but def worth it. i learned a whole lot, and Buckles is the man.

Professor Buckles is perhaps one of the best teachers at Vanderbilt. This class was not easy, but he is an amazing lecturer. I had very little interest in econ before taking this class for a requirement, but  Buckles' class has inspired me to minor in it. You may not get the grade you want, but if you let it, this class may just change your life.

he's awesome... but i think it's a you like him or you don't. he's fair. go visit and ask questions during office hours- very helpful. for tests, look at sample exam distributed and short answers in the book and memorize those because he likes to see exact wording.

You have to study for Buckles, because the class is hard and not that helpful.  Grading is very hard.  The syllabus is clear about the assignments and the text is gold, so study it.  In class, Buckles put me to sleep - almost impossible to pay attention and it didn't really help even if you did.  Study the textbook and you'll do fine.

I'm certain that any positive review of Buckles is from a member of his facebook fanclub, as someone wrote this: "On ratemyprofessors.com Buckles has a low rating. We need to remedy this terrible injustice. Please go and give him all 5's!!! He should have the highest rating of any econ professor on the face of the earth." He is awful. Bottom line.

He's an amazing lecturer, but his exams are very hard. Sometimes questions seem to be worded very awkwardly. And also some things seem to be more subjective than they should be. What you and others may think be right may not be what he's looking for, and this is especially true for short answer/essay questions.

This class is very hard.  I feel like I have to study for it way more than any of my 200 levels.  He knows what he's talking about and explains everything pretty well, but the grading on the tests is absurdly difficult.

What are the reasons for coming to my class? A. You might ask clicker questions which attribute to 1% of my grade. B. There is no reason, i'll just fall asleep. C. The class is typically pointless and i don't learn anything D. Everything for the test is in the book so there is no reason E. All of the above F. None of the Above is Logical  a
Very intelligent professor. I think he's pretty overrated. Although he is very good at what he does, it was hard to stay awake in his class. Tests are ok, study for the essays.

Buckles is an amazing prof who could one of two things to you if you put forth an honest effort in his class: either a pretty good lecturer who has tough tests, or a man who will literally change your entire world-view by opening you up to the beauty of economics.

Buckles is definitely hard, but his class is completely worthwhile. Don't be scared out of taking this class just because you may get a poor grade. After having Buckles you will have an extremely comprehensive knowledge of Macro/Microeconomics, although a high grade won't neccesarily correlate.

I did not at all enjoy this class. It allowed me to discover my extreme hatred for the subject of economics. Buckles is okay, but not the amazing professor that I've heard people make him out to be. His quizzes are reasonable, but the exams are awful.

Great teacher, pretty exciting I'd say as far as economics professors go. He is a bit tough on the tests, but that's probably a good thing for Econ majors. After you adapt to his class it's really not bad though, and you learn the stuff pretty well.

This class made me really depressed for a long time. I don't know if I'll ever recover, it probably changed my life. Buckles himself is a good, easygoing guy, but this class just destroyed me. If I studied I did poor, when I didn't study I did just as good as when I did. Eventually I just gave up and accepted the apocalypse that was this class.
Very very hard. He is a great teacher and knows what he is talking about, but it is nearly impossible to do well even if you know the material.

Its no secret the man likes to hear himself talk, and for good reason.  He is a very dynamic speaker and can hold an audience.  However, if he is as good as he is hyped up to be his textbook should have a hard cover.  overrated

Know the exact language of his book and you'll be fine.   Coming to class helps too, as his explanations clarify the stuff he wrote in the book.  Tests are hard, but due to the curve its not that hard to do well in his class. Because of the size of his classes, his office hours are very busy. Excellent lecturer

Amazing professor. He wrote the textbook and it's a great tool that clearly explains everything and he uses the lectures to really drive home what the textbook says.  The grading in this class is very tough, though.  You need to know the logic of everything. Know the details.  Great teacher, tough class, but definitely worth taking.

Professor Buckles is the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt, but not to be confused with the best grade or the easiest class. It is a challenge for sure, a 100-level course that is for weeding out. If you have a slight interest in Econ, like I did, I highly suggest you challenge yourself and take advantage of why our tuition is so high.
This class is pretty difficult, but you'll do okay if you put in the time and the effort.  Buckles definitley knows his stuff and makes sure his students will too.
I would rather die a slow and miserable death than take this class over. Proceed with caution.
Buckles is simply the man. I've never learned more in any other class. It is definitely one of the hardest 100 level classes, but not impossible. Everyone at Vandy should take him.

Interesting lectures, but if you're not interested in economics you'll probably find them boring.  Tests are harder than average for a 100 lvl class.  Attendance isn't recorded, but you can't really skip a lot since tests are difficult and it's hard to learn the material right from the book.  Luckily many test q's come from lecture.
The opportunity cost of taking this class is an A in another class. Remember that.
Very hard, very hard to understand, class is worthless, if you have to take the class dont bother to go to class and try and understnd the book very well. Avoid if possible.

Best professor I've had at Vanderbilt.  Amazing knowledge of Economics and will make sure you learn the material.  Tests are tough, but the amount of stuff you realize you've learned after having him as a professor makes the class worthwhile.  Very helpful, friendly, and approachable.

He's an amazing, intelligent professor. He expects you to know the stuff well and is more difficult than Vrooman. He's definitely worth taking if you want to know econ or go on with other econ classes.
Tell me WHYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY.... hahaa
Buckles isn't very good at explaining things clearly sometimes.  You will probably be reading the book a lot.
Gotta love him

Amazing professor.  Goes out of his way to help you learn.  The class is difficult but he gives you all of the materials you need to get an A, you just have to put time into it.  Probably the best prof. I've had at vandy and he's so smart its ridiculous.

Terrible. I agree that he thinks he is God's gift to earth. his tests are unfair due to the fact they contradict everything in life. he asks questions in class, discusses them, but leaves you in the dark on the answers. not worth the pain, please take vrooman...you either love him or you hate him due to your learning style

Quizzes every week, some which test on info not covered in class.  Extremely hard tests.  Use Buckles's exact jargon to get credit.  He also has MC ?'s that are meant to be confusing/contradict his book & lectures.  I hate this man.  He is condescending and thinks he's God's gift to humanity.  I learned a lot, but it's not worth it.  Take Vrooman.

Simply the best professor at Vandy! His tests are very hard, and you need to memorize past exams' answers to make a decent grade. He just knows so much, and is so passionate about the subject. Def take him for both 100 and 101 if you want to be an econ major. He drills the basics into your head, and make sure you never forget it.
Regurgitate EXACTLY what he says in class on the exams and you'll do well. Otherwise it's tough.
yeah, he TOTALLY loves being called Bucks

Great Professor. Extremely helpful during office hours. My only complaint is that his test questions can be very ambiguous. Often I knew the answers to the questions, but because his questions weren't specific enough, I did not write everything I needed  to for full credit. Studying his past exams is a must!
Not as hard as people say he is. The best professor at Vandy.

Do not listen to anyone who says Buckles is unfair or a bad teacher.  He is quite simply the best professor in this university.  Knows everything, teaches it well, very nice in office hours.  He is the man, the myth, the legend.  Take everything he teaches.

I thought this class was very hard and definitely did not help my GPA at all.  Either you understand the stuff or you don't...whether I studied a lot or not at all didn't really change my grade.  I'm sure he would be a great teacher if you could understand what he was saying though.  He acted out relevant and good examples in class.

Do you: (1) Not have much experience with economics? (2) Really wanna get an A? DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. It was more frustrating than any 200-level class I've ever taken in any other subject. Buckles is great, but mere earthlings are not welcome here.

I heard many bad things about him going into Econ 100. Yet, he really is not so bad and the class is totally worth taking. You will learn so much and his lectures are interesting! He knows his stuff so well- one the best professors at Vandy.

Wow  so easy.. i'm in school of engineering and i barely put any effort into this class and i'm getting a B..  buckles is extremely interesting, makes you think an entirely different way about everything.. good class, well taught.. although you have to do the reading
Love him as a person but his lectures are pretty worthless and boring as hell. Hard tests
HORRIBLE class, lectures are not helpful at all you have to completely teach yourself from the book. i wish someone had warned me against taking econ 100 with him.
Great professor, really into his subject - I'm not an econ major and the class wasn't too hard, but reading the book (that HE wrote) helps a lot.
Man his class is hard, but I really enjoyed it. He's funny and extremely knowledgeable. Take it if you're up for a challenge.
dont take his class

Buckles is the man. Both of his classes are weed out ECON majors. It's not supposed to be hard, but Buckles will give you a run for your money. He twists questions in ways that make you have to think carefully because THAT'S JUST HOW GOOD HE IS AT GETTING YOU. You walk away learning how to think inductively.
Best teacher. Great advisor.
Buckles is the man.  His class sure isn't easy, but he knows exactly what he's talking about.  Even if you aren't an econ major, definitly take at least a class with him.
Quizes every Friday. It's a bad idea to go to happy hour before taking said quizes.
No Comments
Good teacher. More detail and a for me, the book, was very helpful.

It's a no-brainer that all Vandy students must take his class.  I recommend sitting in the front row lest you get lost in the masses.  Whatever you do, DO NOT get behind on assignments or your grade will never recover.
professor bucles is the best teacher at vanderbilt

its sure not like econ 100 at most colleges, which is an easy A. Buckles is hard, and he knows his stuff. You gotta write exactly what he wants on tests and quizes or your screwed. id stay away from buckles if i could

BOTTOM LINE:  You have to think like Buckles and do the reading to do well. PEOPLE CHEAT ON QUIZZES, WHICH SCREWS THOSE WHO DON'T. PAPERS ARE THE SAME. Class is not essential if you do the reading/ understand it.  There will be lots of hot girls in  his intro classes, but take Vrooman if possible.
Teh test suck and the qusetions are worded so you really have to think about it.  As long as you go to class, and really study the book you'll be okay.  He is very, very knowledgeable

I studied my butt off for a B, but I learned more than in any other class.  Taking any of Buckles' classes requires a lot of dedication, but it is definitely worth it if you are interested in economics.

He's an economic genius.  This guy knows what he's talking about, but doesn't always explain it in the best way.  Go to the TAs office hours for help, not his.  If you can find previous tests, that's the best way to study for his exams.
so many econ majors at vandy...he knows this is a weed out course...he doesnt like to give As.
This class is really difficult! Quizes once a week aren't so bad, but the tests are!
Tests and quizzes are hard, with short answer questions requiring you to have to guess at what he wants you to write.  His lectures are not bad, but not nearly enough to do well in the class.
Buckles is very unclear. His book is horrible and contradictory.
He's a really good teacher but the tests are ridiculously hard his questions are curveballs

Professor Buckles is an extremely smart man, but he does an absolutely terrible job of conveying what he knows in a simple, coherent manner. He writes his own book, which is hard to follow and poorly written. Test questions are absurdly difficult and he rarely gives enough time to completely finish.
The man is an economics GOD.

Fire Vrooman - Buckles has it covered.  Smarter, fresher, and he tells better stories.  One of the best professors at Vanderbilt.  Weekly quizes are annoying, but keep you on your toes.  Would have been ten times better if I could have taken them in my room.
It seems like he does not want students to do well.
Buckles is a great teacher and will give you an advantage going into future econ classes.
My favorite profesor ever! Made me think I wanted to be an econ major. He is extremely helpful too, just make an effort. Buckles is just so great!!
Take Vrooman.  Buckles doesnt teach, wrote a vague book, and still is the highest paid teacher at Vanderbilt.  I think hes a great "economist" but a horrendous intro-econ teacher
the best teacher I've ever had in any subject
extremely nice and always willing to help outside of class. he's great.

His tests WILL**** you.  He is an economic genius and his passion shows.  I learned a lot in the class even though it was unbelievably hard.  Read the class pack and do the problems in it, don't skip class, ask questions, and get a decent grade.

Buckles is obviously brilliant but his lectures can be hard to understand. Go to class and pay attention. Multiple choice on weekly quizzes can be tricky even if you have studied. He is not very helpful during office hours. Work hard, but you may not do well in the class because of tricky questions.

Buckles is an excellent teacher. I highly recommend taking his class, especially if you are thinking about majoring or minoring in economics. The class is not easy and you definitely need to keep up with the reading but you will learn a great deal.

Buckles is an excellent teacher. He is challenging, insightful, and very well read. He frequently supplements his classes with news from the day of the lecture and employs novel ways to make 200 person lectures interesting, intellectually stimulating, and fun.  His class demands hard work and focus.
dropped econ and i switched majors
very smart man

I thought I was an econ major til I took this class.  The lectures are dry (if you take the class, glance around and see all the people sleeping), the TAs arent helpful and Buckles is a good guy outside the classroom but tests and quizzes are completely based on the reading and are ridiculous.

Buckles is a good teacher, but he is too ambiguous and does not get across to all of his students very effectively.  He ends his classes with questions that he does not answer.  The tests are very difficult and the weekly quizzes are ridiculous.

Go to class, read the book carefully, take the on-line quizzes.  do all of the multiple choice questions in the book b/c they're similar to test questions, and just write as much as you can for the test essays.  the TAs can't speak english or draw curves

I had Vrooman for Econ 100 and really enjoyed his class, it catered better to my learning style.  Buckles is a smart guy and he wrote a very clear book but I didn't feel like I got much out of his lectures and the tests were impossible.
msot awful class of my life.

I took Econ 100 with him and am going to take him again in Econ 101- read into that what you will. Do and UNDERSTAND all of the practice material in the study guide, sample quizzes, and practice tests or it will be a rough class. Don't overlook this one

Tests take every minute of time alloted to finish.  Definitely have to teach yourself a lot of the information.  Book is written by him - there are a lot of errors on it.  It helps A LOT to get old tests and study them, they help.

THIS IS ONE OF THE WORST CLASSES AT VANDERBILT. TAKE VROOMAN IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE. THE TA'S ARE AWFUL AND THE CLASS IS HUGE. IT MAKES NO SENSE TO HAVE FOREIGN TA'S TRYING TO GRADE ESSAYS FOR A CLASS AS HUGE AS THIS ONE.
Best teacher at Vandy by far. Challenging class, but reasonable. Buckles is very clear and interesting.

Buckles is a pretty damn good teacher in my opinion, but some of the negative comments here are on point.  A lot of questions on the quizzes and tests are not worded well and the grading is much to strict for a lot of things.  Overall a good class though,

Challenging, definitely worth the time and energy for econ majors.  What you put in to the class is what you get out.  Even with strict grading, the TAs are very helpful in office hours and are more than willing to do what they can to help students.

I think Buckles is a great teacher.  He speaks very clearly and has a very helpful class packet.  His exams are difficult, but they aren't too bad if you've been keeping up with the reading and lectures.

Not a fan of this class.  His tests have some poorly written, very tricky questions.  And the essays are such that they can often be answered in more than one way, but only one answer is accepted as being correct.
TAs tend to grade really strictly, lots of time pressure when you're taking the tests.
tests graded way too strictly.  prepare to do alot of self-teaching if you want to do well.

He's very boring -- a spoiled brat who flies in for class every day from NYC.  If he wasn't such a snob who decided to write his own lousy textbook I might give him more credit becuase he is very smart.  Also the TAs suck and grade hard.

ahhhhh, this course is hard! ! ! he is not straightforward when he teaches, you have to do a lot of reading, learning and studying on your own! the tests are very very difficult, and i dont think the tas speak english

The material is boring, but thats not his fault.  Buckles is a great teacher.  The class is always large and that makes interaction hard, but thats not his fault.  His is insanly helpful.  He's teaching because he loves it, and that's why he's so good.

My worst grade in econ was in this class. I did horrible in his class, and I got an A in intermediate micro. Just do whatever it takes to get through this class and you'll be fine.
dreadful lectures and arcane textbook... the only thing more worthless than his lectures are the tests.  he's a great guy and very helpful, but the class is just a pain
Flies through lectures, but willing to sit and teach you during office hours. Take advantage of that, he's probably the best teacher for this class.

i think he's a great teacher. the campus copy textbook he makes for the course do a great job of explaining the material. the weekly quizzes blow, but you get to drop 2 so its not that bad.

class can be confusing and dry sometimes, but he's very nice and helpful in OH
Not too bad... but the quizzes are annoying and the lectures should be optional.

great professor, everybody loves him
Good lecturer, easy to talk to, will help you out in any way possible.
Very sweet and flexible with deadlines, given adequate notice. Lots of hands-on components to the class. Very good lecture slides, and the assignments have very clear, well-defined rubrics.

Dr. Sappo is really great for DF2100. She's knowledgeable about the course content and has done some cool personal projects. She's super flexible and understanding about deadlines. Course expectations are clear and grading isn't tough. She gives helpful feedback. Lectures are scarce and discussion-focused. Easy to talk to and find outside class.

I wasn't interested in medical imaging at all before taking this class, but the way she guided us through the MRI project was truly inspiring. She held brief workshops on CAD and Python programming prior to the project, which turned out to be incredibly helpful for the main project. I would definitely recommend taking!

very laid back but very disorganized. can be confusing whats due when, but its quite hard to not get an A in the class. participation is optional except for fridays. grade is made of weekly 250-word discussion board posts, a midterm project and a final project.

I love her. She is definitely neurodivergent &has a dry humor.. but a fun personality. No exams, no homework. Just listen to her lectures so you can do the in-class activities. You'll have a group presentation and a final project of your choice. She makes you talk to your classmates :) All life-relevant information in her course!!

Dr. LJ is really trying to give her students a great learning experience. There is a good amount of homework, and weekly in-class group work. But it is super easy to get good grades and learn too! No tests, everything is a project.

Dr. LJ was awesome. She wants you to succeed. This class was manageable. There were discussion posts, class activities, and a final project where I created a podcast. Overall, very informative class that I would take again.
She is the best professor I've had!!! So kind, understanding, hilarious, and inspiring.

Her class is not very difficult, but some of her comments can feel inappropriate and make the class uncomfortable. Overall, the coursework is manageable and most students find it easy to earn a good grade.

The content honestly isn't that hard, but I never rlly learned in lecture. Get ready for a lot of pointless algebra. If you can self study and learn from the HW and practice problems you will be fine. If you're not comfortable with that though, do not take. Prof is really smart though and willing to help you out.

Professor Li is a very nice and extremely intelligent person, and he is very willing to meet with you outside of class to help you understand things. That being said, the content in this class is HARD, and the exams very much reflect that. They have unnecessarily hard math, and in his lectures he will often skip math steps which makes it confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are often very confusing, and he skips over complicated steps that make learning new content incredibly difficult. The exams are near impossible. Almost all exam content is twisted questions that you have never seen before, full of complex algebra. It makes studying for exams a guessing game that you're likely to lose.

I wouldn't recommend this professor, to be honest. He skips steps all the time when doing class examples, which is the WORST when we have just learned a new topic. Additionally, he only does like 1 example of very complicated topics! He kind of talks to students kind of patronizingly, though he is 100% well intentioned. Mixed but overall negative.

Not bad, not amazing. I found the lectures boring and ended up self studying a lot of this class. He usually posts online note pdfs before exams, which essentially cover everything you need to know. The homework problems are also good practice for tests. You'll get a good grade if you can self study the concepts (just a lot of algebra slop tbh).

Christopher Li is a good teacher, and he has good notes. He was patient, receptive to students, and explained ideas clearly. The main downside of his class was that the test covered more than just what you learned in class and on the homework. But if you are a good test taker and thoroughly understand the concepts, you will do fine.

Rising senior here - this is the easiest Econ class I've taken thus far but unsure how new B+ average policy will affect difficulty. Exams cover a lot of material so make sure to study. They're short answer so no trick questions. Not the most riveting lecturer but Dr. Li is well-versed in his field. Would recommend for an upper-level Econ elective!

Classes are pretty boring and lecture heavy. He shows clear favoritism in which topics are covered – Chinese institutions are given the most attention, even moreso than American ones. However, the class is very easy, and besides from 6 homework assignments that take 30 minutes max there is only a few tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most boring classes and lecturers I've taken, but this was a pretty good option for easy upper level Econ credit. I missed class most of the time, but was able to succeed from studying the lecture notes for the two free-response exams, completing the easy reading assignments, and doing well on the group debate.

Lecture was pretty boring, workload wasn't too terrible, grading criteria is a little unclear/arbitrary, exams only 40% of final grade, readings aren't necessary except for the ones for the assignments, most people skipped even though participation is a part of your grade. Not a terrible option for an ECON elective, but not the most engaging.

This was a high-quality, informative class. Prof. Li takes a more nuanced approach to examining economic history through a mix of theoretical mathematical and empirical applications. It's not a very challenging class, but it is very focused on free response homework assignments and exams. There are also a lot of readings, so be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Li is nice, but his class rules are very unclear. There are only 2 tests including the final, which isn't cumulative, and a handful of short answer homeworks and one group project. His lectures are the exact same as the readings, so the class is really boring, but it's not difficult. If you need an upper level ECON this isn't an awful one.

Rennhoff is very sweet, which is totally deceiving as a student. Her tests are built to trick you and are weighted very weirdly — where True/False questions are essentially worth the same as math. Her lectures cover about 10% of whats on the exams, and she expects you to memorize slides to a tee. The class was way harder than it should have been.

Tests are worth 75 percent of your grade. She tests on niche topics related to microeconomics, so if you have not studied this area in a while good luck. The math areas are quite complex her explanations rarely go in depth. For a 2000 level class this has more work than my 3000s...
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was very interesting. Professor Rennhoff is very helpful and accommodating. It is of the difficulty you would expect from a 2000 level course, where it gets you connected with the subject matter if you are interested, but is not particularly strenuous.

I loved Dr. Rennhoff. She is super helpful in class and in office hours, incredibly caring, and the class is super interesting. Lectures are basically mandatory because of small in-class questions and a few easy quizzes, but honestly, I would go to lectures anyway. The exams are not too difficult as long as you take notes in class and study.

Prof. Rennhoff is great. Everything in the course is very straightforward and pretty interesting. If you take good notes, reviewing for the exams is easy. This is pretty much as easy as it gets for econ electives, so take it if you can. I also loved her southern accent.

She's the sweetest professor ever! The material she teaches in class is interesting that it motivates me to go to class everyday. There's no homework to turn in just quizzes (exactly like hw), the only thing is that if you miss class you should probably get notes form someone else since she spells everything out for you in class.

Very caring person! Super knowledgeable on Econ and Healthcare. Makes the class interesting. Learned a lot. Feels like it is easy to get an A-, but very tough to get an A. Test can be challenging. However, nothing is cumulative. Grades fair on assignments and tests. Many True False questions on the Exam, which makes it clear if you are wrong.

Prof Rennhoff is amazing. She is so kind and supportive and really gets to know students. Her lectures are interesting. Go to class and take good notes and you'll be set for the exams. There's one short writing assignment and a group presentation. She does quizzes (you're told ahead of time) and in-class group questions. Great class.

Great lectures. Knowledgeable about the subject and shares her interests with the class. 3 tests non-cumulative, yet attention to detail from lectures, so studying is quick but detail-focused. Participation matters, but if you listen in lecture, then studying is straightforward. Quizzes roughly every other week, no graded hw, one group presentation

Rennhoff is incredibly nice and decent at explaining concepts, and the material is straightforward. Your grade almost entirely consists of quizzes and exams, but her questions are fine. Attendance is basically mandatory since she gives pop in-class questions and quizzes. This is one of the easiest ECON electives, so take it if you can wake up.

Sweetest, kindest prof! Learned a lot about insurance, healthcare, big pharma, etc. Clearly knowledgeable about econ and explains things very well. 3 tests worth 23% of your grade each with some trick questions on there, so not the easiest econ/MHS elective out there. Would def recommend if you have a genuine interest in the topic and go to class.
Great professor and a great class. Super interesting class material and goes at a comfortable pace, making sure no one is left behind.
Super nice, expectations are clear, class is interesting

I loved this class and working with Prof. Rennhoff. The content can get complicated but she explains it a really simple way that made sense for me. Tests were tricky bc of wording but office hours were really helpful. Class content is a perfect mix of math and econ graphs and memorization content. This was one of my fave classes at Vandy.

Nice prof, good lecture. Not that hard to get A-, but quite difficult to get an A (Quizzes15%, in-class questions 5%, group presentation 5%, grading others presentations 1%, 3 noncumulative exams 23% each,1writing assignment 5%). MUST be at EVERY class since you dont know when she assign in-class questions, test can be hard due to tricky wording.

Dr. Rennhoff is nice but it was difficult to understand the material at times. The tests are a major part of your grade and sometimes confusing. I would take another course if you are just looking for an easy A econ elective. Pretty interesting class though and def recommend for pre law.

I don't know if it is just me, but this class is unnecessarily hard. I went to almost every lecture and it felt like the material on the exam was barely covered in class. The lectures weren't great, and the in-class presentations had barely any material on them. If you don't go to every class, you're pretty much guaranteed to get less than a B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! One of the best in the Econ department. Clear grading criteria, no annoying weekly submissions. We do not have to turn in the homework. Most of the class are graded on quizzes as well as exams.

Anyone who doesn't like Rennhoff or her classes has got to just be lazy. If you go to class and have notes on everything she teaches, you have all you need for the test. Hands down the BEST choice for 2000 level elective for Econ
Professor is okay, grading is clear. In class questions are annoying because you don't know when they are so you have to go to class every time.
The BEST professor, she makes everything digestible... just MEMORIZE the notes for the exams and they will be from everything she says in class

subject is simple and should be a fun elective, yet with the grading structure it was needlessly difficult to do well. You could understand a topic very very well and get unlikely with her tough exam grading and then be screwed for the rest of the semester. participation is basically mandatory for this 8am but exams are 75% of the credit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took it online so not sure how similar it is to in person, but I loved the class. Learned a ton, not just about econ but actually about our healthcare system in America. Rennhoff is great and was super open to any questions. Would definitely recommend.

Make sure to memorize everything. The material itself is easy, but the exams are worth so much that you have to make sure not to mess up on any of the questions. Fyi, the average on most of the exams were around 87-88, so getting an A- is not hard. Bar for an A is 94 though. Show up to class and you'll be guaranteed to get minimum B+.

I did enjoy this class. She is very nice and is willing to help you learn. With that being said, the tests had some tricky problems which I found unfair. It is very easy to get an A- but extremely hard to get an A. The level of content in this class is rudimentary. Just make sure you memorize all the slides word for word.

This course was very unfair, boring, and graded by tough memorization based exams. She seemed to be nice towards the start of the semester but was not as such towards the end. Didn't learn much, as you are expected to cram and memorize many useless/specific points for exams. It felt as she definitely played favorites. Take a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a fine person, but her class is unorganized. No Powerpoint. Lots of BORING-AS-HELL reading. Didn't read at all. Unnecessarily specific exams. I am a good student alright, but the class average is unreasonably high. RUN!!

The best class I have taken at Vandy and probably the best professor in the department. Walked away every day with so much valuable knowledge. Tests are more specific than you may think, so make sure to commit enough time; otherwise, they are super straightforward. Rennhoff is simply the best there is. Take this class or one of her other ones!
Great and easy. Could have taught us more.

Pretty easy class towards the beginning of the semester and towards the end it becomes more like a standard class. About 6 homework quizzes throughout the semester, in class questions that are guaranteed 100s but essentially force you to show up everyday, and 3 non cumulative exams. 

Best part about this class is how amazing Prof Rennhoff is

Rennhoff is probably one of the kindest professors that I've ever met at Vanderbilt. I loved taking Health Care Policy with her, and the class has been really informative regarding the U.S. healthcare system.
Didn't learn jack in her legal class. Boring as hell and she isn't that knowledgeable. Had students do presentations for like 1/3 of her classes because she probably ran out of material. Yawn.

Dr. Rennhoff is a very nice professor. Her class is very standard and fair. The content is interesting in my opinion. You definitely need to study for the tests but they are very indicative of what was gone over in lecture. I would take her again in another class if possible. The class has a great balance in terms of lectures and group work.

U have to show up to class because usually 1 a week there are group problems u do in class and get credit if your names on it. the tests were very straight forward if you show up to class. helpful to go to class bc u learn a lot, but I skipped a few and was fine. she was nice and great at answering questions

Kind of boring/unorganized lectures. Often learned concepts in 10 mins on my own after class despite her teaching them for 75 mins. Exams sometimes gave questions about methods/concepts not covered in class/textbook/HW. Graded by few things so one mess-up = tanked grade. But, she is kind, accessible, and not work-heavy, so a good choice for stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An excellent choice for ECON 1500. She provides you with all of the resources you need to do well in this course. Just pay attention in lectures (take good notes) and do the homework problems. If you do this, you will be prepared for quizzes and exams (although make sure to spend ample time studying).
One of the best options for ECON 1500. If you took AP Statistics, it's super straightforward and simple.

2 midterms & a final, with the lower midterm grade replaceable by the final. SUPER clear lectures & accessible in office hours. All questions on the exams/quizzes are very similar to the weekly optional HWs. Be sure not to make too many mistakes on the midterms as 1 multiple choice question is worth 1% of your final grade. Overall a solid choice
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Rennhoff is definitely the best Economic Statistics professor you could have. She gives detailed outlines about what the midterms will be on. Weekly quizzes consists of 1 question which is exactly like the optional HW. Super clear notes, allows you to collaborate on in-class questions, and SUPER straightforward if you took AP Statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 1. ur final exam is basically 50% of ur grade 2. always available for office hrs 3. a lil hard to talk to but a nice person u can tell 4. exams r much harder than practice problems + HW + quizzes 5. not much studying unless u cram b4 exam 6. very firm on grading, will not change / listen to args 7. explains concepts well in lecture 8. POP QUIZZES!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Fantastic lectures that, if you attend, you'll understand the material easily. I felt like I learned a lot, and she was always willing to answer any questions. Exams aren't hard as long as you follow the study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Don't buy the book. Do attend lecture. TA review sessions are pretty helpful. As long as you do the basics in this class, you'll be more than fine.
The class was not too difficult, but I still feel like I learned a lot. Professor Rennhoff's lectures were easy to understand.

Professor Rennhoff cares about students and wants to see them succeed. This special topics class was interesting, and really easy to do well in. The tests were pretty simple math-based and definition based problems, and the lectures were very interesting. Quizzes are just like the homework.
Interesting class. Reviewing posted lecture slides and her review sheets are the best ways to study. Quizzes are very similar to homeworks. She's always willing to help during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Rennhoff is hands down one of the best Econ professors at Vandy. She is so caring and kind, and her lectures are really clear and engaging. You can tell that she's really passionate about the subjects. Exams are really manageable as long as you go over the lectures, and homework sets are not too bad at all. Loved this class.

Professor Rennhoff is great. This class consists of 2 case write-ups, 3 exams, and a group presentation. Lectures are incredibly important to attend and you don't need to read the textbook. Study details about articles and important concepts because they can be more specific than you'd think.

This class was really clear and easy to understand. It's more math based instead of theory based, but pretty simple and well explained math. Lectures are amazing and are the way to go. You don't really need to read the textbook but definitely take notes on lectures. Truly a gem in the econ department.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rennhoff is the best Econ prof I've had at Vandy. She is incredibly caring, accessible, and truly wants her students to succeed. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about US health policy, and she made learning about it fun and engaging. Class is not difficult if you attend lectures, and you definitely don't need to read the textbook.

Don't be intimidated by the 94% A. The tests are not that difficult, but you would have to go to class and take good notes. Attendance is not essential, but she also doesn't post her slides so COME TO CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a great lecturer and while an A is a 94%, if you do the work, a good grade is definitely possible. Make sure you go to the review sessions held by TAs before exams & take good notes in class. Don't buy the book

Quizzes every week are easy bc she gives the q's ahead of time. Question bank for exams so if you do those you will do very well. Super nice professor. Definitely one of the best econ professors in the department. Dont need textbook, especially if you listen in class. Sometimes offers extra credit for going to class

She is the sweetest, cutest professor ever! Very easy, as long as you show up to class, take notes on everything, and do the homework/questions provided. Quizzes every week, but are based exactly on homework and she lets you ask questions on it before taking. Gives a question bank for each exam. She tries to learn everyone's name, will call on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Go to every lecture and you won't need the text book. Quizzes are easy points, tests are relatively straight forward. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best I've had in the Econ department. Her lectures are super clear and she's very kind and approachable. The grading was exam-heavy but exams weren't very difficult if you did the practice problems she posted. Not a ton of work. Highly recommend.

Dr. Rennhoff is by far the best Econ professor I have taken at Vanderbilt. She is very clear and explains things really well. She is very good at helping you understand the basics. She makes you work on problems in groups in class which was annoying, but that strategy actually helped me so much. Final is definitely harder than the two midterms.

I really like Dr. Rennhoff. She is incredibly sweet and knowledgeable! ECON 2350 is not difficult if you attend every lecture and take good notes. The tests are detailed, but you just have to write down everything she writes on the board. Dr. Rennhoff is very clear and very caring about all of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GREAT professor. I am not particularly interested in Health Care but she made the subject really interesting. The class is relatively easy within the econ department, but felt by far the most worthy of coming to class and listening of any ECON class I have taken so far. Professor Rennhoff is great, and makes the concepts extremely clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There were only three exams, weight 89%. 5% goes to presentation and 5% goes to in-lass question. Each exam has 50 point, so if you lose 1 point on the exam, you lose 0.6% of your course grade. As a result, it is really to get a B. Also, she takes points off easily. Be aware, arguing with her is a waste of your time, she won't give points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 1.) while she may be very nice and explain things in class it does not correlate to what you are tested on or even given practice problems for 2.) math based and a decent amount of calculus and equation solving, micro tends to be boring not as cool and relatable as macro 3.) you won't use this stuff in any business job lol unless u become an econom
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Renhoff tries her hardest to make sure that everybody gets the content. The tests are straightforward and mostly multiple choice, along with a free response question. Although the homework in this class is optional, it's a good idea to do it. If you're going to pick an intermediate micro teacher, Prof Renhoff is by far the best choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Rennhoff is pretty straight forward. Class is easy enough as long as you keep up with the class and don't get too far behind. Lectures are really helpful so you don't need to read the textbook. There are quizzes most weeks, but they are pretty easy and she tells you beforehand.

Easily the best micro prof at Vandy. Rennhoff explains things very clearly, to the point where I almost felt like the material was being dumbed down, but she's one of the only professors I had who presents practice problems in class and then forces you to work them out on your own - it's super useful. Make sure you do the hw to understand concepts

Don't buy the book, you won't need it. This is an econ class in which 100 on an exam is attainable simply by attending and studying lecture. The material is interesting, and it helped me get acquainted with simple health care terms and learn about HC policy history. Rennhoff is very clear, writes everything on the board, and is very nice.  Do take!

89% of the final grade was based on three three non-cumulative tests. They were pretty easy after going to pretty much every class and taking decent notes. No homework. Group project worth 5% of the grade. Pretty good prof and easy class, but don't screw up the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Rennhoff is a good lecturer, which is important because the course material is pretty much 100% lecture-based.  Attendance is essential.  Her 2350 class is a solid applied econ class, learned a fair amount.  Tests weren't difficult, but you need a 94 for an A.  Text isn't really used.  Rennhoff lived up to her reputation of being a good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I hate Econ, but I loved this class. Very interesting and nothing too intense in terms of econ or math. 3 non-cumulative exams, a group presentation, and some in-class questions (basically pop quizzes). A little hard to get an overall A (94) b/c the exams are out of 50 and she grades the presentations more harshly, but an A- is very doable.

Very interesting and useful class, especially if have any interest in HC system. So sweet and helpful. If you study for the tests, attend class (for in class questions), and have a good project, easy to get an A/A-.
The exams are not hard, but 50 for total test grade makes you easily go below A.

Tests are exactly like the study guide she gives you. Final is not cumulative. Pretty solid Econ elective. Easy A- but for some reason an A is a 94%.. Pop quizzes once a week but you do them as a group.

Her healthcare policy class is pretty easy. Go to class, write down the notes on the board, and know how to do the in-class questions, and you should be good to go. The tests cover a lot of material, but it's mostly memorizing things from your notes. She's really nice, and the lectures are interesting if you get into the material they cover.

Rennhoff is an excellent professor. You really learn material well, and she is super clear in class. There is little to no outside work, and quizzes are a joke. However, her tests are very difficult. The class is fair, but the time constraints are a killer and most students think their grades don't reflect how much they know.
50 point tests are killer, one mistake and you got a B.

I don't know how anyone can say this is an easy class. While yes, she teaches the material very well, is helpful during office hours, and is a great professor, none of that matters when every single one of her exams asks questions you could not possibly have prepared for, no matter how hard you studied or how much work she put in. Not a fair class.

She explains health care in the US and internationally in a very clear, unbiased way (particularly important for me, as an ultra-Conservative).  Class was 4 essays and a final (nothing too difficult).  I would definitely take her for whatever class you can!
So helpful and nice, her class was the best I've taken. She's extremely helpful and good at teaching the material and class is pretty easy. She's also a dime piece

Really sweet woman.
