Her lectures are crystal clear; repeats everything multiple times, everything goes on the board, etc. My only complaint was with some of the test questions; I felt like I knew the material incredibly well before each exam, but would sometimes get B's because of ambiguously-worded T/F questions.

Professor Rennhoff really sparked my interest in health care.  She is so sweet and very helpful!  Learned a lot!  Workload is manageable and readings are very easy to get through.  If you put effort into papers, you can definitely get an A/A- on them.  Participation is 25% and an easy A.
Professor Rennhoff is very sweet and helpful. Doesn't give out a lot of As and A+s but more A-s and below. Very engaging and a good professor. I recommend taking her class!

Professor Renhoff is tied with Buckles for best Econ professor.  It is the one class where I don't feel the urge to pull out my laptop because it is interesting and engaging.  If you go to class, you don't have to study that much for the tests, but you still learn a lot. Definitely take Health Econ with Renhoff!!!
The final exam is much much harder than the homework or the midterms.

I love Prof Renhoff! She is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. I'm not a stats/math/econ person at all, and I still did fairly well in this class because she was always willing to help. Also, she let us use formula sheets on all of our tests/exams which was great!

Definitely take Professor Renhoff for Microecon...she is by far the best option! Lectures may drag on, but her tests are fairly easy, and she is very helpful in office hours! She genuinely wants to know her students' names also, which is refreshing in a large lecture class.

Her micro class wasn't bad. Weekly problem sets that don't take too long. You take 3 reasonably easy tests and she drops one. I saw another prof's tests and they looked more difficult. The cumulative final is pretty hard though. She's helpful in office hours.  She goes over everything in class, so you don't need the book.

Very interesting class and relevant to the current Health Care situation in our country. Class is comprised of approx 6 reasonable problem sets, 2 midterms, presentation, paper, and a final. You must come to class to do well but it is engaging.

you have to go to class because she doesn't use the textbook.  you can pretty much guess what is going to be on the tests based on the problem sets and examples she does in class. she is very helpful outside of class during her office hours.  231 is not an easy class but she is probably the easiest out of them all. she is also pretty hot

Shes a really nice professor. Everything you need to know comes from what you learn in class, no need to read the book. Shes extremely helpful and if you go to see her, she will work through the homework problems with you. The class will be easy if you go and take notes, thats where all ghe tests and homeworks are derived from.

Dr. Cizmar is amazing! I'm currently taking her class this semester (Fall 2025), and she's already one of my favorite professors. She is very caring and provides detailed, encouraging feedback that has really helped improve my acting skills. She's also incredibly genuine. Definitely take her if you have the chance!

Truly a great professor who cares about what she is teaching. Class has 5-500 word reflections and 2-750 word responses on two productions. The midterm is a monologue and the final is a scene with a partner. 20% of your grade you choose!! It can be an easy A if you attend class (you get 2 drops) and just participate. Such an easy and fun class.

She is an amazing professor and I would recommend her to anyone! Participation does matter because it's an acting class, but her teaching style makes you want to participate. I learned so much both as a person and as an actor in her class.

Cizmar is such a caring professor and makes class super fun to be in. She really knows what she's talking about and can easily jump in at any moment and help you exactly where you're at. She also is incredibly human and relatable.

I took two classes with Dr. Cizmar this semester, and can't wait to take another in the future! She cares deeply about each of her students, is understanding of life circumstances, and gives good detailed feedback to your acting. 

No theatre experience required to succeed - the only way to do poorly in her class is to refuse to participate at all
Not sure what this negative rating is about. This class was a great way to fill my comms credit and Dr. Cizmar was awesome. Not difficult at all as long as you show up.
Her class is rigid and need students have preference for acting major. Tough for beginner.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Cizmar is the best professor I have ever had. She cares deeply about her students and truly pushes them to be the best version of themselves. Her feedback is extremely helpful and you learn so much during class time. She is absolutely hilarious and I wish that this semester with her never ended.
Absolutely love Prof. Rouse!! Literally nothing bad to say. All you really need to do is participate and follow her feedback for a good grade. Content is interesting too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is more like an AP English class under the guise of medicine. If that's your thing, go for it. But it's not mine, so I ended up sitting through this class every day feeling like I was wasting my time. But the main reason I wrote this is to point out that the trips DO cost money (transportation).

Easy assignments due every Tuesday night. 3 big papers total. We take notes on all readings because some days, she will ask us to upload them. Outside trips had to be taken, but they didn't cost anything. She's amazing. Really helpful and nice to talk to. Literature heavy class with medical elements, like poems/books about HIV and mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you're taking this class because you're interested in medicine, don't do it. It's 95% literature and 5% medicine, and most of the assignments feel like a waste of time. If you're taking this class because you're interested in literature and writing, then it might be a good choice. If you dislike poetry, definitely not.
Prof Rouse is a really cool person and I enjoyed the perspective she provides as a new professor. Would definitely recommend her and her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: only have to take 3/4 exams, graded extremely easily, have to attend class to do completion attendance worksheets.

I don't know why so many people are saying she's not a good professor. This class is super easy. She gives you so many opportunities to succeed and you don't even need to do super well the exams to get a high score.
Just do the practice exams and show up to office hours once or twice and you'll get an A
Very easy course she gives you many opportunities to do well. Her exams are weighted by the questions so you can miss half of the questions and still get an 80 or 90% on the exam,Super easy A.

People are complaining for no reason. She does give in-person exams, but they're very easy. She drops the lowest one, and the study guide is about 95% the same as the exam. Grading is also pretty forgiving since it focuses on understanding. She's very nice and sweet too.

Not a good teacher, teaching style makes no sense, she makes exams so heavily weighted for the class. She gives no real sources of preparation for the exams, her practice test, which says that the study materials are 20-30% related to the exam, so you study using the practice exam for no reason, cares 0 about students' grades or helping them.

Not a super engaging lecturer, but is very knowledgeable and passionate. Attendance isn't technically required, but beware of missed in-class assignments (they add up quick). Content can be hard, but exams are insanely easy in comparison. Grades best 3/4 exams, so no final if you do well early.
easy class to get an A but I wouldn't expect to learn anything. drops lowest homework and test grade so I didn't even take them. good person, mid teacher

I don't know why she has such a low rating. As long as you go to the lectures and pay attention, you'll be just fine. I had never taken stats before and found the class to be occasionally confusing, but Li genuinely wants you to pass and will help. She can be a tough grader, but she also offers to look over assignments prior to submission.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was scared going into the course because I'm bad at math and the low ratings, but after taking it, I'm not sure why they're so low. I had no background in statistics, but with just a little studying, I got back pretty decent grades. Lectures have lots of concepts so you will have to study and you can drop one quiz + homework grade.

Dr. Chen was such an amazing professor! She wants to help you succeed and is accessible via email. I had questions about an exam the morning of,  and she was super helpful even though it was very last minute.  I had no stats background, but the organization of class makes it super do-able to receive A, just do your work and pay attention.

I don't know why her rating is so low. I had no problem in this class, and statistics was not my strong subject. Her lectures could be more entertaining, but she gives you the information you need for the exams. Getting an A in this class should be easy if you put in some effort. She is also very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor. Chen is very hard to understand and the classes tend to be boring and unhelpful. I figured out everything on my own, but the concepts of PSYPC 2110 are pretty easy. I would say to only take this class with Professor. Chen if you have taken stats in high school. If you haven't, the class might be harder but still doable to get an A.

If you can take another professor for Peabody stats I would definitely do that. She was hard to understand and put no effort into teaching. Consistently ended classes early and homework/quiz grades weren't returned until there was no time to utilize feedback. She may have boosted grades for final but was a headache of a class. Would look elsewhere.

This class is only easy if you put in work like other classes. Use the TA and email them with all questions because she can't answer them clearly. Homework is long and doesn't help. However, if you study the powerpoints, memorize the bullet points, and come to class to get class credit then you'll be fine

I'd taken advanced stats in high school and another stats class here at Vanderbilt before hers. She talked so quietly and slowly that it was hard to even concentrate. Then she only gave us 20 minutes for the quizzes, which felt impossible after the first few. She confused me on many terms I had already learned and felt successful at.

Li Chen was absolutely amazing! Although her lectures were not the most interactive nor engaging, they were very informative. If you go to class every day and pay attention you will do well. The homework is graded for accuracy (which can be a tad annoying), but it causes you to actually understand the material instead of blowing it off. She's good!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: you can barely hear her talk in class, and her accent makes it even harder to understand her. the class starts really easy, especially if you have taken AP stat or any other stat class. once you get to like quiz 5, the level of difficulty spikes and the final screwed everyone over. if you need to take psy-pc 2110, try not to take her class.

Don't take her unless you have a strong stats background (like really strong). She is nice but a terrible professor. Incomprehensible lectures as she speaks quietly and just writes on a small portion at the bottom of the board. You will likely have to teach yourself. 5/6 homework assignments & quizzes each, which are graded at the discretion of TA.

Professor Chen was a really nice person, but her instruction is unclear and unhelpful at times. I was only able to pass because of past stats classes, which I don't think might have been the case otherwise. If you can, take another professor.

Professor Chen is an incredibly sweet and wonderful woman, but not the best professor. Her class is extremely confusing and complicated despite stats being an easier math class. Your grade in the class also depends heavily on how hard your TA is, so hopefully your TA grades leniently.

She is a really nice person but I can't say the same in terms of her ability as a professor. I know she really cares about us, but her pedagogical ability is not very good, and the class, in turn, seemed more difficult for a lot of student despite its easy nature. TA does a lot of the grading, and if they are harsh, good luck.

Simple one - super nice lady but horrible professor. ONLY take if you have taken stats in high school. Dont even need to go to the first 7/8 of the class if you have taken stats. She talks so quietly that it is impossible to hear her. However, I have a soft spot for her as she really cares about her students.

Prof Chen is super nice and great at responding to emails. But, I only got an A in this class because I've taken AP stat. Quizzes and final aren't hard, but her explanations are unclear and applicability is rarely (if ever) explained. You can get through this class with a fine grade, but you're going to have to work if you haven't taken AP.

Really nice individual, however, she doesn't explain the concepts in detail and is vague in her descriptions on the whiteboard. Very challenging if you haven't taken a prior stats course. Please avoid and find a different professor for Intro stats

This experience has been by far my worst with a professor. She explains no applicability for anything, and instead will just say this is the t score because you use this formula. That explains why the only people in my class that arent lost have taken AP Stat before. Seriously feel dumber every time I leave her class

The course itself does not compose of overly-complicated material, but the way it was taught made it very difficult to do well with no prior stats experience. Super harsh grader and does not make the effort to get to know students / give extra assistance if needed. If you aced AP stats this may be your prof but if not, try elsewhere

The lectures were ok but there were millions of things to do toward the end of the semester whose grades were never released. At least 30-40% of the grade we didn't see and never got feedback. No one (and there was no time to) was accountable for this huge chunk of our grades. Do not take her.

I liked Dr. Kam at the start of the semester - engaging lecturer and assignments have very clear directions, plus she makes herself super available to her students. Group project as majority of grade, my group was awful and she did not step in. Got A's all semester but she gave me a much lower grade than I earned because I didn't talk every class.

Dr. Kam is an amazing professor and I adored her class. She is one of the most organized and straightforward professors out there and lectures, as well as class expectations, are clear. The tests were pretty reading based (pulling from the reading) so make sure you listen to her lectures and at least skim the readings. Great class overall.

Professor Kam truly cared about her students succeeding in her class. There are readings before every class but also long as you skim them you will be fine. I wrote nonmandatory because you can skip a few classes here and there if you engage the times that you are there. She's not a hard grader and she is very understanding. You will learn a lot.

Professor Kam is a very motivating person. She always made class feel comfortable and interesting. We did A LOT of reading, two or three research articles for each class, but she reviewed and filled in blanks in class. She does take attendance. We did a huge research project with a national survey; the whole class and every assignment led up to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Kam is great!! Very reading heavy class, but you can tell that she is very passionate about political psychology. Class is centered around two exams and a large final group project. Sometimes has trouble articulating concepts in lay terms, but good class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Mediocre class. Interesting topic but felt like I didn't learn much about it after a semester of work. 90% of assignments are centered around one group project. She's nice but a bit unclear about instructions. Posts rubric AFTER grades are released.

She's very nice, although she can be a little bit unclear with she wants of us in assignments but she gave good feedback and overall it is a course with taking. She is also very helpful outside classroom.

Professor Kam is an amazing professor! She is so passionate about political psychology. The class itself is not that much work until the final project at the end. Be sure to take notes on the readings!

Kam is literally one of the most wonderful profs you will meet, so incredibly kind. The class is well organized and expectations are always clear. Most of the class is structured around a group research project that we all had a ton of fun with. The workload is manageable, just be sure to outline every study you read. Cannot recommend her enough!!

Worst teacher I have yet encountered at Vanderbilt, readings are ridiculously long and tedious and grades are heavily based on tests that are made up mainly of data analysis. You will have to memorize hundreds of pages of readings for each test and assignments are incomprehensible and can heavily affect your grade. Avoid her at all costs

She seems very sweet and she is but she will test your ability to memorize and analyze an incredible amount of information. Midterm 25%, Final 35%, Participation 5%, Assignments 35%. If you do better on the final it is with 40% and the midterm is less.  This class has an absurd amount of reading every week, but you can do REALLY well! GO TO CLASS!!

Worst polisci teacher I've ever had. Assignments are tedious & terribly worded sometimes incomprehensible. midterm study guide included 120 terms you must study but only 10 MC on exam. large portion of exam is data analysis & essay. the class basically turns into a STATS class. american public opinion seemed interesting before kam, now I cringe
TJ is awesome! Super chill and takes into account schedules when assigning work. I'm not usually a big fan of English classes, but actually liked coming to class

Not a course with a heavy workload. A little frustrating. It was like you could do nothing and be fine. I did well on the assignments after rewriting them, yet I did not end up with the grade I wanted at the end. I asked him about it, but he refused to show grades on the last few assignments. I was definitely shocked by my final grade. Nice guy tho

TJ IS AMAZING!!!!! He is the sweetest and most understanding professor of all time (would bring muffins/bagels for the class and has extensions on papers)! He also gives you great feedback on assignments, has clear expectations and instructions, and is all about helping you improve. Can't say enough good things-- would definitely recommend!
Super laid back and easy going... learn a lot too....

I was terrified to take this class (Philosophy is not my thing) but I am so glad I did. Great teacher. She actually makes you think so if you just want an easy A, don?t take this class but if you?re a moderately intelligent person and a good student you'll do well. If you don?t understand something, go to office hours! She is super nice one on one.

cisneros is a sweetheart. not a difficult teacher at all. pretty fun laid back class. you just got to get her to like you, she one of those. pretend to show an interest in her class (because few do) and shell give you the grade you want!
Do your work. You're at Vanderbilt. She expects you to act like it.

Very easy class. She expects you to attend class and do your assignments. These comprise a majority of your grade. Maybe not always as clear as she could be but your effort is always noted and appreciated. Put forth the effort and you can generally expect to do well in the class. Do your work. Easy A.

This professor was extremely helpful in understanding the material, and i found her lectures quite interesting and insightful. she expects a lot but is always happy to give extra help if needed. she has a great personality and pushed the class to think outside their comfort zone and understand things beyond their own priveledge. wonderfull teacher.

Natalie was the worst professor I've had at Vanderbilt. She knows very little about philosophy, or if not she is awful at teaching. I learned NOTHING in this class and was graded on absurd parameters. She recommended that someone begin their paper with a Merriam-Webster definition... I think that speaks for itself

What a nightmare! She was HORRIBLE! totally unfair grader. If she doesn't like you, just drop the class because you have no chance of doing well. She ruined my GPA and I really tried. other people read my papers and thought they were good and she still gave me a C. very unclear expectations.DO NOT TAKE HER SECTION! never had a worse teacher.
ok, this prof is a ridiculously hard grader, boring, not that intelligent, reading is easy but grading is ridiculous for a 100 level class, no tests, sucks as an individual

Cannot say enough good things about Dr. Clinton. By far one of the most caring profs at Vanderbilt and is genuinely interested in seeing students succeed. Class was extremely interesting with multiple exams where the lowest is dropped.

Best prof in the department! The class was really early but I still came even though attendance was optional because he is so engaging to listen to. It's exam-heavy, but they are graded fairly and he drops the lowest one. He also gives a lot of prep material to help. There are also simulation activities which can be chaotic but also really fun!

Professor Clinton is quirky as hell (basically I just mean nerdy) but like in a good way. He's so fun to listen to when he lectures about polling because you can just tell he's so (overly) passionate about the subject. He does talk really (and I mean really) fast but just learn to accept that about him. Highly enjoyable nevertheless!

Professor Clinton is such a nice guy and so understanding as a professor. Took him for intro to quant. poli sci--the quizzes you can retake as many times and exams are all very doable. Super into content and just a great, nice guy. Really recommend him

Took him for the first-ever Intro to Data Science class. Prof. Clinton knows SO much about polling, statistics, and data science. Actually maybe too much at times for an introductory level class. He was super accessible for office hours and is very passionate about Trump-Biden polls. Grade was based mostly on 4 group projects. Sometimes difficult
Professor Clinton is a super nice guy, and he knows a lot about the content. Clear grading criteria and not too many assignments.

Professor Clinton is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. Granted, being a member of an 800 person online class, I did not get many one on one interactions. However, he is extremely passionate about his subject, and his jokes make me smile every time. This class was a rather easy A as long as you put in then work (which was minimal).
Prof Clinton is top notch concerning political data science. Seems like a good guy too.
Great professor. A true gem

Clinton is the man! This class often feels more like an interactive seminar than a class but definitely opened my eyes to some really cool concepts. Prof Clinton is passionate about what he teaches and definitely take him if you get the chance. The class was all code based and had some interesting assignments, but often felt really unstructured.
Great class and truly an amazing professor. His class is actually worth the tuition. Not difficult to get an A as long as you put some effort into the problem sets and ask questions

Professor Clinton is a really great guy and undoubtedly knows the subjects he teaches. However, he claims to be accessible outside of class and willing to work with students, but I didn't find that to be the case necessarily. The course schedule was mostly unpredictable, and the final ended up being like 8 times longer than any other assignment.

It is so rare these days to find a professor who not only knows the material taught like Prof. Clinton does, but also has the patience and communication skills to teach it. Professors like Clinton are the ones who you really attend college for.

Engaging, humble, absolutely brilliant professor, and easily one of my favorite at Vanderbilt. Knows the material like the back of his hand, and has a real passion for it. Class is primarily based around in-class lectures and assigned readings. Grading seemed difficult during the course, but class is definitely curved at the end. Learned a ton.
Assigns way too much reading. The class itself was not as bad as it could been given that the subject is so boring. Really nice guy though.
Great professor.  Made me find a subject that is terribly boring to be somewhat interesting - that took some serious skills.  He does assign WAY too much reading though.
The first exam was unexpectedly hard, but beyond that, all exams were really okay if you study. Dr. Clements is also a good lecturer. Take her you won't regret.

I loved Prof. Clements for Orgo. I personally struggled in Ni's Orgo I, but Clements was the first chem class I felt prepared when walking into the exams. She is so caring and her practice exams are very similar to the real thing. Lots of office hours and some opportunities for extra credit. She does talk quiet in lecture, so sit in the front.

3 midterms (125 points each) and a final (150 points). Technically flipped, but I didn't watch any lectures and only went by the book. She covers all the important info in class anyway, with very helpful worksheets. The BEST part about her is that she gives 6+ practice exams for each midterm + extra review sheets, so you will always feel prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements is a great orgo prof. She provides so many resources to succeed. She gives tons of practice exams which are rly similar to the real thing. Her class is flipped, but you don't need to watch the videos you can supplement with the text book. In-class she goes over the more important concepts and gives a lot of practice. Take her!

DO NOT TAKE KATIE CLEMENTS, SHE IS THE MOST EVIL ORGO PROFESSOR OF ALL TIME AND I HAVE HAD NIGHTMARES EVERY DAY FOR THE LAST 3 WEEKS OF HER FACE !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! NEVER EVER TAKE HER FOR CHEM 2222

Yes, orgo is hard, but she is such a sweet professor.She really helps explain things in simple ways, though I did find the exams to be difficult sometimes, you still knew what to expect. You definitely need to study extensively before the exam, rather than cramming information. Very accessible and understanding with office hours! do NOT miss class!

She's a great option for ochem. Her lectures go at a very digestible pace and she'll always answer your questions on the discussion board + in class. The exams were all fair and her practice exams prepare you well. The discussion quizzes were open-book, internet, and collaboration. The aktiv hw's are very reasonable lengths so workload isn't high.

Dr. Clements is a solid choice for orgo. It's a tough class regardless, but she makes the content very approachable. Lots of in-class practice + LA collaboration make lectures engaging and helpful. Exams are tough but fair and are very predictable. Focuses more on problem-solving than conceptual stuff, so great if you like a practical approach.
AVOID her class at all costs! my biggest regret in undergrad
Do everything you can to not take her for orgo!! She is one of the worst professors I have had in my entire life.

Dr. Clements is a knowledgeable instructor, but there is a pretty heavy out-of-class workload. Her tests are (relatively) predictable. The final is a mash-up of all her exams w/ predict the products, drawing mechanisms, and ranking things (for acidity/carbocation stability/etc.). Overall, the best advice I got was to do the Klein textbook.

Clements is the best professor you can take for Orgo 1. All of her exams are fair for the rigor of the content. Plus, she gives tons of extra help (videos on concepts, practice exams, practice worksheets). Just do not underestimate the exams. Make sure you do practice problems and study a bunch, as the average on exams was around 75%.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements's lectures are fill-in slides and can self-learn to a certain extend, but dont fall behind! Supposedly reading can be helpful. Organic Chemistry is much harder than chemistry. For tests 2/3, you memorize a ton of mechanisms for how reactions occur and then utilize those logical mechanisms find a pathway to turn one compound to another.

Orgo is hard but professor Clements does her best to set her students up for success. She posts in-depth videos online explaining all the topics we briefly cover in class. She is really helpful in office hours and never talks down to confused students like I've seen some other STEM professors do. She puts her cat on her slides, so cute!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is hard and there is a ton of information that she expects you to know inside and out. However, she is very kind and cares about the success of her students. She provides a ton of resources for test prep and to supplement the lectures. The LAs in her section are also very helpful. Her tests are fair, and she offers a lot of partial credit.

Orgo is difficult, there's no way around it. Yet, Dr. Clements does her best to provide us with the materials to succeed. She hosts 4 office hours a week, and had one every day leading up to the final. She posts other prof's practice exams, her COVID videos as extra review, & very little if anything was on the exam that wasn't taught. I'd recommend

Professor Clements is truly a great and caring professor. She wants you to succeed and is always willing to help during and out of the classroom. Although she can make mistakes here and there, she takes her time with the lectures to make sure we know the information. I think she is the best option for starting out in orgo

Clements is a great lecturer and her class is very clear on expectations. Her exams are generally straightforward although some questions can be difficult. If you study each reaction and do practice problems, this class should be a breeze.

The amount of heart this woman has is incredible. She's super kind and gentle and makes it easy to ask questions at any time. Never be afraid to ask for help! Dr. Clements is very open minded and tries to see from many perspectives that aren't just her own. Makes Orgo super clear and explains why electrons are being "pushed" a certain way.

Professor Clements is one of the sweetest professors there are. She is very understanding and always open for input. Her lectures cover all the material that will be tested, and doing the assigned textbook problems will guarantee you an A. Some problems on tests can be very hard, but they only tend to make up around 5% of the test.
I think Clements is the best choice for chem2221. Her tests are reasonable and her lectures are clear.

Professor Clements is actually spectacular at teaching the material! I know my post doesn't have my final grade listed, but that's because I blame myself over the rigor of the class. Exams are very fair. Her explanations keep everything simple and manageable. You have to work, but with her teaching quality, anywhere from a B to an A is very doable!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A solid option for orgo- gives very reasonable exams, and gives lots of practice problems in lecture. She expects you to watch lecture videos before class, but I never did and was fine- she would go through the stuff you actually need to know in the first half of class and gave examples the second half. Very helpful learning format. Loves her cat!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Clements! She is super organized, color codes things and gives detailed steps for each rxn. She created a new office hour for a few students in the class that couldn't make it to the other options and answered all of my 10 question emails! I studied an insane amount outside of class and I loved being able to rewatch the lecture videos

Professor Clements is super sweet and caring as a professor. She is also really accessible outside of class for help. However, for me, the lectures and video recordings do barely anything more than the book to help you learn the material. Tests are not too difficult or tricky, but prepare to self study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a little rough in terms of the class format. What made it so difficult is that it was flipped, so you were responsible for learning the material on your own through videos. Class was office hours where we sped through a few problems and then were dismissed. Oftentimes, it felt like you're teaching organic chemistry to yourself.

This was her first year teaching organic chemistry (except for a summer class) and honestly you can kinda tell. She's a super nice person, but the class was structured so you watch lectures as homework and just sit in class doing practice problems. I hated the format for the class and didn't go to class hardly ever and still eked out an A minus.
She doesn't ever lecture during class, just does 5 practice problems and calls it a day. She's nice but annoyingly strict with grades. Take someone else if you can.

She was very helpful and wanted to make sure everyone got an A. Made ample time for meetings with everyone about papers and made sure that everyone was able to make the transition to online post-COVID without any hangups. Helpful and accommodating when I had personal life problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements is a very caring and kind professor who's super accessible outside of class. She explains things clearly to make things easy to understand and is very receptive to students. If you do the work and pay attention, the class is very manageable. Take her if you have the chance!

Dr. Hendrix is an amazing professor and an even better person. In core, he made sure that all students understood the material. Also, he seeked feedback from students a lot about the course. He is a really nice guy, super funny, and cares a lot about his students. Whether it's for a language class or core, take Dr. Hendrix.

Clint has been the best professor I have met at Vandy. He is funny, welcoming and understanding. He makes an effort to meet you where you are at if you are struggling. The class is heavy in grammar, but Clint helps you make the jump from an intermediate to advanced Spanish speaker. I am taking him again this semester, and nothing but good things!!

Prof. Hendrix is the perfect professor for someone with beginner or intermediate Spanish skills. He's kind, professional, and funny and doesn't make class difficult either — if you show up and do the necessary work, you shouldn't have a problem getting a good grade. He makes up for a relatively dull class with his personality.
Hilarious and kind teacher! My favorite Spanish prof at Vanderbilt so far. He prepares you well for all of the tests/quizzes and explains concepts well!

Prof. Hendrix was my favorite professor this semester! He is extremely personable and kind. He answered his emails very quickly and hosted office hours three times a week. The class is grammar-heavy, but if you enjoy learning Spanish, I highly recommend it. Also, if you speak Portuguese or have a Spanish background, this is a great class for you!

This class is entirely based on grammar, so I would not recommend if you have't received a lot of grammar practice in previously. You will learn every single Spanish tense, and it will be necessary to study in this class. Clint is very nice, open, and willing to help, but he is strict in what he expects and will not be lenient on grading.
Nice guy, very funny, provides helpful and understandable explanations of the content. I'd have to imagine that Dr. Hendrix is one of the best options for 2201

Clint was by far my favorite teacher this semester. He truly cares about his students and he made me enjoy spanish for the first time in a while. There is a lot of verb conjugation work, but Clint is understanding and knows it is difficult. I'm not super passionate about spanish, but I loved class because of this professor. I 10/10 recommend!!!

I LOVE CLINT! He is such a great professor! Very personal and funny. He incorporates lots of interactive activities into class every day and makes sure that every one has a chance to participate. This class is very grammar-heavy and fast-paced, but he manages to make it not too hard as long as you do the homework and study. Prof Hendrix is awesome!
Very understanding, funny, and keeps the class super interesting and entertaining. Not very available outside of class time but sticks around a bit after class for questions.
I was not originally planning on having him, but his class was great.  he can sometimes be a bit quiet, but the learning environment is great

Professor Hendrix is funny, down-to-earth, and cares a lot about his students. He encourages participation and really helped us improve our Spanish skills. We learn a lot of grammar in this class, but the tests are doable. There is online homework before every class, which is tedious but not hard.

Great option for Spanish. This class does take some effort but Hendrix makes it very easy for you to succeed. You will have to study for tests but if you do decent on your tests its pretty much an A or at min A-.
Chill professor but still made class very interactive. Kept students engaged so class periods felt like they went by very fast.

Great prof! He really cares about his students. This class is a LOT of work. Youre gonna learn a TON of verb tenses and conjugations. He does his best to help you understand, but its just a lot of content in a short time span. Do all the homework and try to score well on the first tests and trabajos escritos, bc the final and midterm are hard.

Prof. Hendrix is an amazing professor. Cares very much about his students' success and is very accommodating. Always willing to dig deep into questions and come up with researched answers about grammar, etc. if we're confused. While it could be a lot, all online HW served its purpose. Class discussion was always fruitful, lots of speaking practice.

I LOVED Señor Hendrix (who had us call him Clint). He's a super nice and funny guy and very understanding of late assignments, etc. The grading was very straightforward and not too difficult. His lectures were clear and organized, and he does a great job teaching the material and making it interesting. Would 100% take again, he's the best.

I don't know where to start. Professor Hendrix is an amazing professor as well as an amazing guy. He is caring, and he is the type of professor that everyone should strive to be. He not only teaches the content very well, but he makes you feel welcomed in his class and at Vanderbilt. This class can be work heavy at times, but it's manageable.

Señor Hendrix is a great professor and a great dude in general. Class was always fun, and he kept lectures quick and to the point. He was always helpful when something was confusing for me. Make sure you participate as much in class as possible so it's more fun for everyone.

Great reasonable professor. Extremely understanding about circumstances that may cause an assignment to be submitted late and has a good understanding of the concepts he teaches and can convey them well.

Clint made my first semester here amazing. Super understanding right now (mental health days, lightened assignments, etc.) Theres HW, but its not excessive or hard. He makes sure to cover everything in class multiple times and makes it fun. I didnt need to go to office hours, but he does have them. Im going to miss having his class.
the best!

Prof. Hendrix made Spanish super fun. Even without a great background in Spanish, I felt super comfortable. He is relatable and shows funny videos and the assignments are fun. Class 4 days a week is a little rough, but the 5 credit hour A is nice.

Man, I love Clint. Had him for 2203 and spent a lot of time watching funny cat videos and talking about current events. He gives great feedback and even though the class is 4 days a week (you get Wednesdays off), he's a riot and makes the commitment totally worth it. Put in the effort and you'll see the results

Clint is the man for 2203. His class is difficult to get an A in, but a B+/A- is not hard to come by. He will give a lot of feedback and he's just a hilarious person in general; if you care about the content he'll care about your grade and help you make sure its a good one. Grading criteria is really clear but showing up and being friendly is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love Clint! We spent a lot of class talking about cats, but he also tied in current events and pop culture references to make Spanish more interesting. His class wasn't too difficult for a B+/A-, but an A requires a bit more effort since foreign language courses require a 94. He's an incredible professor though who is always there to help

Good guy who just wants to hang out and help you learn Spanish. You'll have to work a little bit but if you care and want to learn the language, its a very doable A. Works with you to make sure you can get credit for as much as possible

Uncle Clint was the man; hilarious professor who always made class a good time. Definitely one of the goofiest professors you'll have. Knows the material really well and cares a lot about it. Be prepared for a B+/A-; A's are very hard to come by but B's are easy. Would definitely take a class with him again.
Professor Hendrix is quite funny. He's very good about editing papers over office hours, which more people should take advantage of. Overall, he's a very good professor.

incredibly personable, and occasionally even hilarious.  allegedly grades harder than the other 104 professors, you'll have to work pretty hard if you want an A, unless you're naturally a spanish whiz, but a B/B+ is pretty easy to get in his class, if you do the work and put in basic effort.  i feel like i learned a lot of spanish in one semester.

Extremely personable and funny. Eager to help students any way he can. Encourages conversation in class which keeps it interesting. He is the best 104 professor but the hardest grader. It is tough to get an A but easy to get a B.

Extremely personable and funny. Eager to help students with whatever they need. He is the best professor for 104, but he grades much harder than the others. Hard to get an A, but easy to get a B if you put in enough effort.
Hendrix rocks. He's so easy to understand and is very receptive to the needs of new learners. Definitely take any class he teaches, you won't be sorry.

He is an extremely reasonable teacher and an awesome guy. Definitely the one to take for 201W. He doesn't care if you don't do the daily work. He grades the essays hard, but that's expected since it is a writing course. He's the man.

Great professor. If you're taking Spanish, try to get in his class. Very helpful, funny, and makes class fun. Not easy or difficult. Fair grading. You'll get the grade you deserve. Does a good job of keeping the class engaged and interacting.

I literally adored Professor Hendrix. There was not a day that I didn't laugh in his class. I had him for 104 and I thought the way he spoke was perfect for the level. He grades fairly so you will get the grade you deserve. The work isn't too intense. Definitely try and get him if you can!
easy to get a B+, harder to get an A-
Hendrix is awesome.  Really funny and helpful.  Not the easiest grader, but I learned a lot.
He's very funny and really nice. Not the easiest grader but very fair. If I were to take this class again I would definitely take it with Hendrix. He's awesome.

Prof. Hendrix was very nice and funny. You can only miss five classes but thats because of the Spanish Department. I actually liked coming to his class. If you are taking a spanish class and he's teaching him try to get him!
Classes were always fun, and he was very helpful outside of class.  He's a fair grader and always honest with students when asked, even if the assessment isn't as 'nice' as one would like.

LOVE Hendrix!! The class itself is not that interesting, but he makes it fun. He genuinely wants his students to do well and will help you with whatever you need. Definitely the best professor in the Spanish department!!
Hendrix has a great sense of humor and never lets class get too boring. His speaking is easy to understand and I am so glad I took from him this semester. I highly suggest any of his classes
He's friggin cool

Hendrix is by far my favorite Spanish prof in the department. He's verrry funny and helps with those tricky aspects of the language that are more difficult for American students. He's also a really fair grader. He made me want to continue with the language past the intermediate level. Wish I could have fit it into my schedule.
Hendrix is a great teacher, funny, never too serious.  There are pop quizzes but thats not him, its the department.  My writing has definitely improved!
Hendrix is awesome and hilarious--not to mention a great teacher. My spanish writing improved significantly this semester.

Compared to other classes I've taken in the Spanish department, 201 is a difficult class, but for the most part Clint makes it bearable.  He tries to keep a sense of humor to lighten the mood a bit, but watch out for pop quizzes and random collection of homework on Fridays.

I hate Spanish and am only taking the class for a requirement. This guy made the experience more bearable. He speaks more English in the class than he probably should. I literally did not open my textbook for a month until the night before the midterm, and I somehow still passed. This guy is young, easy, and funny at times. I really recommend him!
This class isn't hard, Clint's a young, laid-back, American professor (read: no difficult accent) and is lenient with grading and attendance. Very relaxed, easy class.
He's American and knows how to speak English. Nice guy, too.

2 exams (index card cheat sheet) + final project, weekly reading reflections (due Sundays), attendance and participation matters. I would highly recommend taking this course. Dr. Clark keeps things interesting and engaging at all times. Guest lecturers were excellent. Late work not accepted no exceptions. Don't use AI.

Weekly reading reflections due Sunday (500 words or less), 2 exams (one index card cheat sheet) + final project. Dr. Clark makes the class extremely enjoyable. I would highly recommend her to any of my peers. Things must be turned in on time with no exceptions. Frequent guest lectures (AMAZING)! Extra credit is available. AI is prohibited.

Incarceration, Policy, and Health is one of the best classes I have taken. The course consists of weekly reading reflections, two exams, and a final project on a topic of your choice. Grading is very fair. She frequently brought in guest lectures. The material is super engaging, so participation is easy. Highly recommend, Dr. Clark!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross was a great professor for an early sociology course. There are readings assigned for every class, but they can be skimmed instead of read. (Some will have pop quizzes though!) Class is very easy, the content is almost too common sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very nice, wants class to engage. He assigns a lot of readings, but you really don't have to actually read them, just skim them and make sure you have the main points down. Definitely try to participate, as you have a participation grade and it is really easy to get involved in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and the class is easy. 2 multiple choice exams (just read over the lecture slides) and 2 written exams (given the questions beforehand and a 1 page cheat sheet). Readings are interesting but you just have to skim them. 1st lecture of the week is a lecture presentation and the 2nd is usually a group discussion about a reading.

This an easy class if you just listen through the lectures and skim through reading. Graded on participation, pop quizzes on reading, 2 exams, and a midterm and finals( 5 essay questions to you beforehand with 1 cheatsheet). The class is not interesting with relatively boring lecture reading and discussion. I recommend 1020 which is more fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is a very new professor who just got his PhD last semester, but he's very nice and kind. I would take this class again.

Black Girlhood with Dr. Taafe was the most enriching and eye-opening class I've taken at Vandy and if they offer it again, TAKE IT!!! Class was always an open discussion based on themes in our readings/films and personal experiences. As long as you're engaged, skim the readings, yap a bit in class, and do your assignments on time, you'll get an A.

Dr. Taaffe is an amazing professor. Her facilitations help us get into profound thought provoking topics that have the ability to change the world. She bring positive energy and you can tell how passionate she is about the work that she does. I feel grateful to have been in two of her classes, and will be taking another next semester.

Dr.Taaffe is honestly one of the best professors at Vandy. She truly cares about her students as well as the content she teaches. The lectures are amazing, as are the discussions but that might depend on who's in your class. If you do the assignments, it's not diffcult to get a good grade. She offers a lot of EC. Attendance is necessary though.

I LOVED this class and learned so much! Dr. Taaffe is a great person and treats her students very kindly inside and outside of the classroom. The extra credit events were fun, and I enjoyed getting to know her and the other people in this class. Highly recommend!

She has to be one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. Her course is very discussion-heavy, but no matter how crazy of a stance you might have, she will consider it with open arms. She is also very passionate about the well-being of her students. Overall an amazing professor.
She's awesome! Very clear on what is being tested on. She will literally tell you the questions that will be tested on. Take her if you can!

Does a perfect job teaching survey (Intro to AADS). Teaches basic historical and sociological facts. About 50 pages of reading a week. 2-3 films. Very kind and intelligent person. Taaffe is super passionate and provides a foundation for further thinking and research on topics like racism, colonialism, intersectionality.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Taaffe is an incredible lecturer: relatable, open, and engaging if you are at all interested in history or sociology
Intro has a lot of reading in my opinion (about 70 pages a week)
The readings are relevant and diverse (academic, fiction, essays, historical documents)
Taaffe is a Professor I have seen act with very genuine kindness towards ppl

Amazing lecturer. I learned way more in this class than I have in any other, and the class is relatively easy. Lots of reading outside of class, but the assignments are graded relatively easy and the final is take home.

Dr. Taaffe is an extremely caring and understanding professor. Most of the class time was structured as a discussion rather than a lecture but she was always clear about what specific topics would be on midterms and quizzes. Sometimes a lot of reading was assigned but the accompanying writing assignments were not difficult and graded leniently.

many people dislike taaffe classes due to 'difficulty' but really she tells you exactly what to study from each reading for each quiz/test. however,if you dislike reading to the point of not doing the readings beware of this class as you NEED to do the readings to get a good grade. other than that taaffe is such a fun and thought-provoking teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Taaffe was a pretty good lecturer and the material is super interesting. LOTS of reading. VERY disorganized and the TA was available half-of-the time.

She does not give feedback on tests. Tests are not clear and always have two answers that can be right. I have emailed her and my TA on multiple occasions asking for help and got no answers. I tried. Not much I could do after a certain point.

If you like to read 50 pages a night, this class is for you! One of the most time consuming courses Ive taken and it was for AXLE. She grades pretty fairly but thats only if you go to class and take good notes in addition to the hundreds of readings she assigns.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is very reading and text heavy but Professor Taaffe's class was the highlight of my day. Her class was a nice break from my stem classes and the discussions were always intriguing. She can be a little unorganized at times and you need to email her if you want feedback on some assignments but overall I love her as a professor.
Awful teacher and never responds to any emails. This class could have literally been taught by a 12-year-old and there would be no difference. Taaffe needs to learn some communication skills
Professor Taaffe is one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt so far. She's so caring and flexible and makes her class really welcoming and comfortable. I learned SO much through this class.

One of the worst professors at Vanderbilt. Seemed to have completely given up on teaching during Covid. Tried to introduce students to some pretty radical things and blatantly lied in some cases to try to make her case. Least respectable professor I have encountered at Vanderbilt. That being said, the class is VERY easy.

Professor Taaffe is probably the coolest professor I've had at Vandy. Her expectations for tests are very straightforward as long as you pay attention and take notes during the lectures. There are lots of papers, but as long as you complete them in a format that mimics the examples she provides, you will get full credit. Take her class if you can!

Taaffe is very caring and knows a lot about AADS, but she does not set up her class well. It feels a bit like high school where she assigns lots of readings and busy work that takes up your time but barely talks about everything. And the writing assignments add up (40 pages total) but are mostly reflections. Very easy A, but kind of a waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Literally definition of meh. She's nice enough but she doesn't respond to emails or update her syllabus so you're always reminding her about stuff. Material is interesting but there are so many due dates.

Incredible. I took 1010 with her and thought it was the best class I'd have at Vanderbilt until I took this Black Power class. She is more caring than probably any other professor I've ever had and opens your eyes to so much. She runs discussions so so well and connects what's happening today to whatever we're covering in class. Absolutely take her

This is the worst professor I have ever had. She starts every class with her political opinion. She never grades any assignments so it is difficult to know how to improve on your work. The material is interesting but her laziness makes it difficult and unenjoyable.

She is incredibly opinionated and shares her political views any chance she gets in class. When we switched to online in the spring of 2020, she stopped teaching and responding to students. The rest of the semester consisted of student-led discussions that took place of her lectures. She didn't even bother to comment on students' discussion posts.

I gained so much perspective from being in Taaffe's class. HOWEVER, when classes switched to online, Taaffe was horrible. She failed to respond to emails and gave up. Times are hard for everyone, but Taaffe turned an amazing class into a terrible one. I was so disappointed; I continued to want to learn but Taaffe no longer provided that opportunity

Taaffe is a very sweet woman and genuinely cares about her students. She has so much knowledge about the content beyond what is assigned. However, she really struggled with the switch to online class, and our Zoom meeting was unproductive. There were a lot of papers assigned over long readings, but they were simple to complete. Take her in person!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: The easiest A at Vanderbilt considering that she tells you what specifically what will be on the test with about 95% accuracy. As far as enriching your learning experience, she won't. When we went to Zoom lectures she used it as an opportunity to do little to no work. HW graded on completion, student run discussions, little email correspondence.
The Intro to AADS course is known for opening your eye about the racial history of entire diaspora and Taaffe just makes it all the better.

Enjoyed a previous class with Taaffe. However, this course was one of the worst I've been in, a sentiment expressed by most members of the class. Taaffe only taught for three weeks and was not only absent the rest of the time, but would not know what was being taught by the grad student or took responsibility for his behavior. Bizarre midterm
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Taaffe is absolutely unbelievable. Literally took this class as a way to fulfill an AXLE requirement, and I'm now minoring in AADS. She takes important pieces of history and makes them so relevant in today's world. She cares so much for her students and the world and is truly one of the best professor's I've ever had. TAKE HER!!!

Dr. Taaffe is one of, if not the best professor I've ever had. Literally went from taking the class as an axle requirement to majoring in AADS. Cares so much about her students, the issues on hand, and is funny, kind, and everything you'd want in a professor. Easy class as well, if you participate and read you can get an A. Incredible Professor!

I don't know what to say about this phenomenal lady other than to take her class! She makes learning about the diaspora so interesting and the class is actually fun. 3 unexcused absences before participation deductions so take that how you will. Taafe genuinely cares about her students so you will do good. Listen and it's hard not to get an A.

I recommend taking one of Professor Taaffe's classes to everyone. She understands AADS classes are all about self-growth, so most of what is talked about in class are conversation-like versus lecture. If you pay attention in class, the quizzes and tests are easy. She respects the topic more as learning experience rather than pushing information.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fun core professor, very chill. Take him for a fun core that doesn't stress you out.

The entire class is flipped: most kids are busy outside of class and do not have the time to have to do all of the videos and take notes outside of class. This is very inefficient, and I would much rather have a professor who actually teaches during class instead of just linger in lecture.

flipped model classroom style but the videos are not super long and are very informative so helpful when studying for exams. His frq is more conceptual and not memorizing which may help or hurt you. Gives a ton of partial credit. Really nice guy and great teacher even if the videos include lots of coughing. Hard class is just bc lot of content.

This section was definitely the better section to take this year. However, Clements portion of exams contain a lot of mutations that make no sense and awkward wording. I enjoyed his flipped classroom as I was able to repeatedly watch his videos when reviewing, though.
Textbook definition of BOSS QUEEN

dr. clements is a nice person, but his teaching style didn't resonate with me. he moved fast to cover a ton of content, so you have to do a lot of independent study, but even then you can get very lost. i put a ton of effort into his section and still didn't do well, and not even patton's section could bring me back up. harder than gen chem imo.

I genuinely don't understand all the hype around him. He is a sassy man who doesn't understand that part of his contract is to TEACH the class, not through some videos on Brightspace and expect us to become masters at it. His exams are unnecessarily hard and unfair, and as someone who got an A, Patton carried this class without a doubt

Overall good professor who cares about his students learnings. He isn't a great test writer, though, as his questions can be poorly worded and confusing, and reach into niche applications of topics. His half of the class is definitly the harder half, but he's nice.

Dr. Clements is very caring and approachable. Content is covered for about 20 minutes in class(flipped) and the worksheet is completed the rest of class. I found this style to be difficult since the content was sped through and required previous understanding. The test questions were extremely out of the box and were advanced for an intro class.
He will grade you on the most minute detail on the lecture. For the final, the majority of the lectures weren't even covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: professor doesnt care about students and makes tests too hard

Dr. Clements is a nice person who seems to care about his students. It's a flipped classroom, so videos before class, which wind up being a few hours of work. Did fine, but certain exam questions and lectures just did not belong in an intro course.

His content is hard, but Clements has lots of office hours. He provides a lot of content due to the flipped classroom, so be prepared to do a lot of work outside class. It is annoying that he covers a lot of topics in greater depth than we need to know them, but he doesn't test a lot on things he doesn't teach. Tests weren't awful but not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice enough guy. The exams are really brutal in a non-constructive way. Preaches "application" of content but tends to get insanely in the weeds and far-fetched with exam questions, such as his little stint over CRISPR. Did well in the class but had to literally live and breathe the content, which shouldn't be the case for a 1000-level class.

I personally did not enjoy the flipped classroom, where we had to watch lecture videos before coming to class. We did not do anything in class other than ask questions, which did not help me learn the material.

Based on practice exams from previous semesters, it seems like without Dr. Clements, genetics would've been hard. He's a fun guy and wants you to do well. He gives a lot of partial credit. I once gave a bogus answer on a test question that asked why a technique can't be done by just saying maybe the lab has no funds and got it marked right.

Genetics is a strange class, I feel like the averages are low but I seemed to do ok even without studying a ton and I don't consider myself to be a genius or anything at all. Maybe there are a lot of seniors that don't care as much in their last semester. Otherwise, I think DC's tests are really easy and straightforward. Practice to do well.

Dr. Clements is a Vanderbilt gem and a really great person. Loves interacting w/ and guiding students. His portion is flipped however and videos sometimes take >2 hrs to watch + take notes. Great lecturer/explainer. Review and LA sessions saved me on test questions. Everything you need for exams is on the slides. Easily the better 1510 section.
My dawg. Made one of the hardest STEM classes at Vandy easier than most. Very friendly, engaging, and willing to help. Just needs to stop burping in his flipped classroom lectures.

This class is naturally hard due to the content covered and the really hard exams. However. Dr. Clements is so incredibly caring and supportive during and outside of class. He does really advocate for mental health and is always here to listen and understand. The flipped structure is not personally for me, so be aware of that.

This class is flipped, meaning you'll have to watch videos before each class. Memorize the videos and their slides. 4 exams, 1 drop, and homework grade (easy) gives like 6%. Class time is spent on worksheets covering material learnt. Dr. Clements is a fantastic person, wants to know as many students as possible. Have to take this section of 1510.

DC is one of the best professors I've ever had. He's super friendly and caring and he's just like a big brother that knows just a little more bio than you. If you give a reasonable answer on a test he'll always give you credit, there's not a set, mandatory answer for many questions. Be sure to rate his cat, Dr. Kevin on rate my (5 stars)!
I'm very concerned about Tom Clements' relationship with his cat. Gotta be illegal in some states fr.

Clements portion of the class is entirely flipped lecture style which made it so you have to spend a lot of time outside of class in order to learn the content. It is a high time commitment, but the videos do contain most of the information you need. The tests however require you to apply the information not just recall it which requires more.

I wish Dr. Clements was as good at lecturing as he is at cracking jokes. I found the LA teaching days on Fridays more helpful than the worksheets done in class for test preparation. I understand condensing lectures, but pausing every 5 seconds gets old quickly. I like the idea of learning the material before class, but the execution was lacking imo
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements was a great professor and made learning the content very simple. Was flipped classroom which I enjoyed, but it can be hard for some. It's a lot of content to memorize and understand, but the application was not that difficult. His exams are hard but you have all the information needed. He uses the LA's a lot! Hard class, great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements does flipped classrooms, and the videos he posts are pretty dense. Though it may seem like they are only an hour long, it does take like five. The tests are also pretty hard since he likes to do mutation questions. The best advice would be to condense your notes from each lecture because BSCI 1510 is a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements definitely knows what he's doing both in regards to the teaching the material and educating students effectively. He uses his LA's well, and his classroom is flipped. That didn't matter too much for me, but if you don't like lots of recorded pre-lecture videos, then you're in for a tough time. Exams are hard, but he's a great guy!

If you're taking notes on the videos, it takes a good 3 hours. He also burps and makes crazy mouth noises in lecture videos, which honestly should be edited out. He often reads off the slides in the videos and sometimes doesn't explain what that means. It makes some concepts super-confusing, but he does have discussion posts for questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom is not a great method to teach biology. It is quite difficult for bsci 1510. Tests are in person as well.

BSCI 1510 is difficult because it is like drinking from a hire hose for the amount of information you need to memorize. There is also lots of extraneous information that you do not need to know, but is hard to tell which is which. Dr. Clement's section has flipped lectures and has LAs that can help you with in-class practice questions.

Dr. Clements is probably one of the most likable professors at Vanderbilt. I enjoyed the class overall, but his lecture style didn't quite fit with mine. I like the idea of going through a worksheet for class, but only every now and then. I feel like it's hard for me to retain everything if that's done every class.

Dr. Clements is very caring, but the tests were difficult for many because of how much content was presented in little time. I wouldn't retake him because I hate flipped classroom and the videos got long sometimes, but he's a great guy. PSA: HE BURPS AND MAKES MOUTH NOISES IN HIS VIDEOS!!! If you have a pet peeve of mouth noises, be warned.

Dr. Clements is awesome and probably the strongest professor in the introductory biology courses at Vanderbilt.
He really cares and puts a lot of effort into helping students.

He does mostly flipped classes, where you watch videos before class and work on worksheets during class. It's a different style, but he makes it work.

flipped classroom is extremely ineffective and difficult to follow. he is a nice person but not a good professor. way too difficult for an intro class. your LA is VERY important, because professors don't really do much. he assigns 3-5 videos at 18-25 minutes each per night, but it ends up taking 2-3 hours because you have to write down everything

Dr. Clements is a really cool guy, and a really great teacher too. Unfortunately, his exams were so difficult they left me wanting to change my major. Would still recommend him just because he makes class fun and is better than the alternatives, but be prepared to really grind for his exams.

His flipped classroom did not work well, as many of his videos contained errors. Students learned false information and would have to change misconceptions at a later time, damaging learning. Test questions were either trying to be funny or trying to relate to students which distracted from the actual material being covered.

If you're a first-year, this is the move. There is a lot of content, and the questions can be challenging, but Clements provides a ton of practice. In addition, there are a few cushion grades, such as online quizzes and attendance. Regardless, go to office hours; he incorporates students' questions into his exams and explains concepts well.
As long as you study the worksheets he gives you. You'll be fine. Pay attention to lectures because he only goes over things that will be on the exam. Also I love Dr.Kevin.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best bio professor to take class with!

Clements is super nice and caring. He's really not trying to fail you but it is a hard class with a lot of content. He has a bio meme instagram page and I think he wants learning to be fun and enjoyable.

Dr.Clements is an amazing prof. He uses memes to explain the complicated biological processes and his lectures are typically concise. He cracks jokes here and there, sometimes it's funny sometimes it's not, but that's okay. I feel like he really tries his best to motivate us to learn and not want 1510 to be a weed-out (tho it is by nature)

Clements is nice and explains concepts well. His exams are well thought-out and he is by far the best biology professor. Just be prepared that the content of his lectures is not in what he says, but what is written in the slide notes. He tries hard to be cool but it falls flat. Still the best of the professors and the most approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Clements during his first year teaching and it was truly great because he showed me that he cares about empowering students to ask questions about science. There's a lot of material but go to office hours or ask an LA so you can learn before the exam and not complain about your grade! DC is smart, supportive, and super friendly, so ask!

Nice but kind of annoying. He wasn't willing to change grades for incorrect test answers he wrote which was annoying. His lectures were super boring. He tried to crack jokes a lot but they just aren't funny. They were giving science teacher trying to be funny with biology puns but nobody laughs. Not the vibe at 9 am, Dr. Clements. Id pass on C dog.

Dr. Clements is an amazing professor and is truly dedicated to helping students, being accessible and inclusive, and promoting quality learning! He holds office hours on weekends, has a whole class discussion board, has test corrections, and is great at science communication. The LA program really enhances learning and connects you to peers!

Prof Clements is a wonderful and engaging teacher. He is very nice and understanding but makes you work for every bit of your grade. He is helpful in office hours and his recorded lectures are well organized. Tests are very fair.

Clements is fine. His lectures and homework were briefer than Friedman's, but this often led to a lack of depth. His tests are not extraordinarily difficult. My main gripe is that he doesn't answer questions. He'll dance around an answer but never fully explain or have a fellow student give a convoluted answer. Tries very hard to be liked.

Incredible professor. Class is taught flipped classroom, and in person time is used for small group discussion of HW with Learning Assistants. I loved the format of the class, but some of my peers felt differently. Clements loves to add meme/jokes to his slides, and makes the class enjoyable. Genuinely does not want BSCI 1510 to be a weed out.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements is amazing. He teaches complex topics using memes. He taught his class this year as a flipped classroom. His lectures were fun to watch, although they were a bit disorganized. His test questions are sometimes confusing, but he is a lenient grader.

Dr. Clements genuinely cares about his students so much. He breaks down topics in a way that makes it easier to understand and reminds us that this isn't a weed out class. He wants everyone to succeed and will help in doing so with memes and metaphors! Highly recommend him; he gives great lectures as well

Dr. Clements is such a nice guy, really. He's funny and wants to get to know his students and will admit when he doesn't know something, which I appreciate. However, I will say that the tests were EXTREMELY hard and the information was not taught in a way that made it easy to understand. A lot of it has to be done on your own.
The class is harder than the professor. Regardless of what professor you get for BSCI 1510, it's going to be hard but Dr. Clements tests and lectures make him the best choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Clements is a gem. His online lectures were easy to understand and 15 minutes long. I attribute much of my success in the class to the LA's and the flipped class. Honestly, his part of the class felt like my high school bio class (most people didn't agree with this). I'm not sure if this trend will carry over to in person classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Clements was great to take online. He was a really caring professor who is willing to explain anything to you as long as you ask. His lectures online can definitely jump around a little bit, but as long as you watch the lectures and do your work and study, you'll be fine. He's a good teacher!

Dr. Clements is the absolute best professor I have ever had in my time at Vandy. The expectation of any intro to bio class is that you won't really get close to your professor but Dr. Clements is always available to chat and provides amazing feedback and advice. Enjoy pics of his cat, Dr. Kevin, and chat him up at any time because he's a g
He's a really cool dude who is trying to change the current status quo of intro bio being a weed-out class. Really fun to hang out with outside class, I've kinda befriended him that way.

Dr. Clements is a great professor to have for intro bio. He made an effort to come to LA meetings frequently, even when it wasn't his turn for giving lectures. He loves his biology memes, and he's equally great at making lectures interesting. I would take another class of his in a heartbeat.

Dr. Clements made bio lab so much fun and really packs a lot of information into each lab period. He also is very accessible outside of lab hours and is great at describing complex ideas in simpler terms (I especially love his analogies). Didn't have him for lecture but would definitely recommend having him as a prof!

He definetely wasn't a great lecturer and I had to take advantage of office hours and youtube to fully understand the material, BUT he has the easiest most straightforward tests I could ever ask for. If you want to make it out as a premed, TAKE HIM.

Although I've had Professor Clements this past semester in a lab setting, he's been the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He genuinely cares about his students, and wants them to understand the content thoroughly. He's very detailed in the information provided, and also gives incredible feedback. Easily accessible, and a great person overall.

Best Professor and the sunshine of bio department! Deeply care about students! Office hour was helpful and full of joy! Dr. Clements and his TA, Dr. Kevin, write email to students every week about this week's goal, which is extremely helpful that everyone would read until the end!

Dr. Clements is a great professor. He clearly loves teaching biology, and really heightened my passion for it through his lectures, even being online this semester. He likes to include memes to keep you entertained, and will even take memes made by students. His tests aren't over arbitrary material. If you pay attention, you will do well.
