I took BSCI 1510 this summer and it was all online. I thought Dr. Clements did a great job with this transition and he made every effort to give us feedback and meet with us often. Definitely come to the zoom meetings and participate! Would recommend for the fall online semester highly! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's genuinely a super nice and funny guy - he wants to see you succeed. Takes attendance with Tophat every day. Lectures are sort of useful, but tests are based entirely of the powerpoints, and are super straightforward (the averages on his tests are in the 80s).

Dr. Clements is a hilarious professor that believes that everyone should be able to succeed -- that biology is not a weed out class. He presents class material very clearly and provides in-class notes that help students study and prepare for the exams. His exams are fair and he makes it as straightforward as possible.
One of the best Professors hands down! He's very accessible and answers his emails very quickly! Come to Office Hours because there's usually a big group and it's a great way to find study buddies!

Dr. Clements is an amazing Professor! He gives us time in class to think out things for ourselves rather than just spoon feeding us everything. The use of LAs was good and sometimes the activities went too long. I really liked how most of the LAs were women when the course was taught by two men.

Wastes a lot of time in class doing TopHat, trying to utilize the LAs, but then rushes through the material. His tests are very straightforward though which is misleading after Graham's more difficult exams. Dr. Clements is definitely passionate and a good choice for intro bio. It feels like a high school class with "in class assignments"
Professor Clements even has LAs in his Office Hours! Really take advantage of all the opportunities to help you understand the material!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Clements is an amazing Professor! He tries to really hard to make class engaging and often peppers in jokes. Pay attention to the in-class activities because he takes mostly from them on the exams. Would recommend!

Professor Clements doesn't really know what he's doing and wastes a lot of time in class on TopHat. You need to study the slides (don't buy the book). Tests are straightforward and he cares a lot about his students. You want to do relatively well in Graham's half, but this will raise your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wow! This professor is THE guy to take for intro bio, and don't let anyone else tell you otherwise. Nowhere else will you be able to find someone as caring and passionate about the material who is also able to teach it in a fun and memorable way. His slides have everything you need, so don't buy the textbook! Tests are straightforward and fair!

Clements is a new professor still getting his groove (as of 2018 Fall) and I feel like a lot of students (pre-meds) are giving him a hard time for it. Sure, he makes some mistakes during lecture, but a student with the smallest amount of motivation to learn would seek him out in office hours. Just use your brain, and you'll be fine. Solid choice.

Dr. Clements is an amazing guy. He really cares about his students and their success, which is hard to do in a 200 person lecture. He puts a lot of memes in his lectures and none of the exam material is really a surprise. The class is difficult but that's just the nature of biology at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements is super invested in his students and does everything to help them succeed. He tries to make lecture super engaging with memes and jokes and explains topics as many times as students need. His exams were super fair but it is Bio so you have to put in a lot of time with the material. His slides have everything you need, don't read book!

Dr. Clements is an amazing and caring professor. He is super helpful in office hours and truly cares about students. The material is hard but that is just the nature of the course. His lectures are interesting and he makes them fun. You get to drop one test too which is huge.

Clements is super helpful and funny and puts jokes on his tests - it's definitely not an easy class but he really takes the time to try to help you understand and hosts review sessions that clear a lot up. All the information is in his lectures which he posts online and you never have to read the book at all.

I loved having Dr. Clements as my professor in BSCI 1510. He cared about us. He had a lot of review sessions outside of class. He made the effort to learn as many kids' names as possible. His tests are not easy but if you work extremely hard, you will definitely do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Clements is super nice and cares about students learning biology. However, he's still new, so he's still figuring out his teaching style and how to best explain certain concepts. Overall, he's so funny and tries to make the class useful and interesting. Would recommend if you're willing to teach yourself some of the material

Dr. Clements is one of the most caring professors I've had and is very accessible. However, he is still new to teaching and doesn't have a solid of a grasp on the material. Use the book to double-check him because he takes diagrams from the book. Read these descriptions to help with understanding the processes since tests are process-heavy.

Dr. Clements cares more about his students than any professor I've ever had. He is incredibly accessible outside of class and clearly wants his students to succeed. His lectures can sometimes get too specific and it's hard to discern what's actually important. But even then tests were pretty reasonable as long as you take good notes during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Probably THE best STEM professor here! Not only does he teach the material clearly, he does so in a fun way while providing students with ultra-detailed slides that are great for review. His tests are much more direct and to the point than average, and he will do ANYTHING to help his students understand the material, especially in office hours.

Ask him to do extra review sessions! He generally obliges when asked. Love his memes to connect material. Hell post them on the VandyBio Instagram. Class is test heavy, but youll be fine if you attend lecture and ask questions!

Dr. Clements really cares about his students in the extra effort to help out everyone. If you don't understand concepts, just go to his office and he will gladly help you out if even it's not during office hours. His memes and jokes are solid too. The other BIO professors at Vandy really don't care, so take his section if you can!

Some of the content in the lectures was very confusing, but overall really great bio professor who really wants his students to succeed. See him for extra help and go to the review sessions- he drops lots of hints about the tests. I believe test averages were higher than some of the other bio teachers, so if you study hard you should do well.

He is very accessible outside of class and cares a lot about the success of his students. He is a new professor so his lecture style is not very clear and refined yet, but if you learn/understand every detail in his powerpoints you will do well on the tests.

He seems to care about his students, but that doesn't translate at all into how he teaches. He includes too much random information, and his tests are incredibly nit-picky. You could technically put the right answer, but get no credit because you didn't use the exact words they were looking for. AVOID IF POSSIBLE!!! Really nice guy, though.

Though a nice professor who seems to really care for his students, he includes way too much information in lecture, and a lot of it you don't even need to know. Yet he also won't tell you what is important, and what is just an FYI kind of thing. He also wastes lots of class time with Top Hat questions, and uses Drake references way too much.

Dr. Clement is a good professor who likes to incorporate Drakes and meme into his lectures. He explains the biology concept well and smooth. Like other biology lectures, the test is full of details and you should be prepared to know all of the details that he puts in lecture slides. Review session is very helpful outside of class.

He spends a lot of time on his slides and his Drake/Spongebob memes (totally a G though). Tests are hard and his class feels more like an intro biochem/bio-orgo class than a regular biology course, but at lease we'll be prepared for the future. Feel bad for those who are not premeds or prescience
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: New professor in his late 20's. Tests are EXTREMELY specific  make sure you memorize those slides (and their notes!) and the very nitty-gritty details about what Clements says. He sometimes says that you don't have to memorize something, but then it pops up on the test, so be sure to just memorize (and understand) every and all concepts.

If Dr. Stauffer's offering a class, you should take it! This class had 2 papers & 1 speech, with 4-5 readings you could skim (though I enjoyed reading them). His priority is clearly that his students become better human beings. This class was a breath of fresh air; I looked forward to weekly talks about life/goals/values/commitments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely recommend Religion, Politics, and Culture. Class was super interesting and I learned a lot. Graded on attendance/participation, 2 papers, and a presentation. There is a lot of reading but none of it is really necessary tbh. No exams or anything like that and he was very accomodating of extensions.

Dr. Stauffer offers special classes every fall. Take them. I learned more in this course than in most 'standard' classes. He lets the students do most of the discussion, and adds his own insight as a pastor and professor. Weekly readings are easy and insightful and lively discourse in class made this my favorite course. Would highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really nice guy, the final is a 15+ paper (short story, article, etc) which can be difficult to write, but other than that great class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor! Truly cares about his students and was willing to adjust the difficulty of the quizzes. The class itself is genuinely fun: you get to play video games and the workload is reasonable. Lectures don't always seem relevant and the syllabus isn't always accurate, but as long as you do the work and show up to class you'll be fine.

A passionate and caring professor who makes excellent choices for readings (and video games in the case of this class). When the students were critical of his quizzes he accepted feedback. However, as others have pointed out he can be arrogant/won't accept other interpretations/pushes an agenda. Lots of time spent outside of class on readings etc.

Clayton brings a unique love for the arts to policy discussion. Extremely well-versed in media across the board, the class hinges on participation and reading/watching the course content. Ultimately a pretty cool class with low work load and caring professor. Take for sure w/ an interest specifically in sci-fi or the intersection of art + policy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Great Professor. He's very knowledgeable and truly invests in the well being of his students. This class is very interesting and a nice break from the super heavy typical Vandy course load. He takes attendance and timeliness VERY seriously so don't be late! And be sure to participate in class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jay Clayton is the sweetest most adorable professor ever. He cares so much about the subject and his students and he's wicked smart.

I loved the lectures and discussions, analyzing both classic and new works in sci-fi. You get the chance to revise your final paper TWICE. The work wasn't too much: 5-6 blogs, and a final paper. I didn't like how heavily weighted the paper was (60%), and the peer review for blogs. Some readings were too long. But I recommend this class to everyone.

Class is amazing and the readings, while numerous, are interesting. You'll want to do the work for this class. Clayton really knows his stuff and bends the syllabus to the students. Definitely recommend.

He definitely is enthusiastic about the subject, which makes class more fun. His grading is very subjective. He is extremely helpful if you want to talk to him outside of class. He values students´opinions and listens carefully. His grading is a little tough, but the class is great.

Grading system is extremely subjective and rather unbalanced. Interesting class and readings, but I hated his participation system and he'll mess you up if you don't format papers just like he likes 'em.
Great readings but lots of them.  Teacher seems enthusiastic about the subject.  The digital media projects or movie making option gives you freedom, or you can write a 15 page research paper.
A lot of reading. The readings are well selected and his class structure allows for creativity. However, he is a pompous, self-promoting, irritating professor who seemingly grades on a whim.
Pompous and unreceptive to ideas offered in the classroom.  Has an agenda, but difficult to see what it is.

Good discussion, grade is decided by what you want to do- either papers, project, or research paper. You read about a novel a week, which for a non-english major can be sometimes challenging. Good class.
best vandy professor hands down love that lady

I am obsessed with her. Literally the most interesting, smartest teacher I have had at this school. She is so kind and actually just wants you to learn life skills. Easy to do well if you show up to class.
easiest class ever bruh. its sooooo freeee. take her.
So sweet and wants you to get an A, best class ever, basically no work, take her if you can!

This class is so cake. There is weekly take-home bright space quizzes, a weekly journal, and 2 group presentations the whole semester. All the stuff is so applicable and truly interesting. Never felt stressed
Best professor ever

GOAT of the engineering department. She is a super nice professor and very reasonable about grades and even extenuating circumstances. Class is very easy but also interesting and we do fun stuff all the time. She is also super super cool as a person and has lots of relevant experience in engineering.

Professor Cooper is a gem at Vanderbilt and if you have the chance to take a class with her DO IT!

Weekly journal assignments and readings can be annoying and time-consuming, but they are a pretty easy grade.

She is super caring and really wants students to succeed in class. She puts lots of effort into preparing students for their careers.

Easy class for an easy A. Attendance counts towards your grade but you can miss some classes. Can opt out of final if you have an A which almost everyone did. Super caring lady and doesn't care if you don't pay attention in class. 2 group presentations and weekly online quizzes and 2 page double spaced journals

Best professor I've had here.

Very caring, accessible, and understanding. Material is great for engineers as it focuses on soft skills that a lot of awkward engineering kids desperately need. Assignments are straightforward, easy, but still teach you a good amount. 

100% recommend. Love her. Did I also mention she worked at NASA for a long time?

Professor Cooper is one of my favorite professors here! You can tell that she really wants her students to learn instead of regurgitating information. Her lectures are fun because she brings in different activities and leads a lot of fruitful discussions. She is very down to earth and really cares about the things that her students care about.

Professor Cooper is awesome. She has interesting lectures that are very applicable to the real world. She also has a ton of experience and shares her stories. There are group discussions or activities every class that are always super engaging. Weekly quizzes and journals on the readings and some presentations, but very manageable. TAKE HER!!!!
Professor Peterson is very caring and invested in the subject matter!
Easy A but incredibly disorganized and did not learn anything
Basically no work. Chill class. Didn't learn much. Would think easy A but grades not out yet, we have no clear guidelines or assignments so who knows.

DO NOT BE LATE! Very strict attendance/late policy. But if you show up on time and participate regularly, it is not difficult at all to do well in. Readings are pretty much optional as they are not needed for assignments or discussions. Very little work (5 ~250 word discussion posts, a 20-30 minute presentation, and 4 short in class worksheets).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Peterson is so kind and caring and this class is enjoyable and a breeze. Yes it meets once a week for 2.5 hours which is draining but she tries to make it engaging, Super easy grader. Just read the books enough to answer her questions and you'll do well. I highly recommend this course to anyone looking for a low-workload MHS class
Kind of boring. Just participate and use common sense on assignments and you will do fine. Do NOT say anything controversial that can be perceived as offensive. Easiest A at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Peterson is a great professor for a core MHS class. The class itself did not have many grades, and the grades that were given were very reasonable. There were no exams during my semester. Grades were based on attendance, participation, discussion posts, in-class assignments, and one group presentation. Overall, very easy to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class simply for the Perspectives AXLE credit and was able to receive a relatively easy A. I was not very interested in the content, but I enjoyed how little work there was. I didn't participate once in the class, but made sure I completed all assignments including the 4 "daily work" assignments and the group presentation and was fine.

MHS 1930 was a great class with the grades mainly being participation, discussion posts, and class presentation. Dr. Peterson is a very kind and knowledgeable lecturer, but I wish there was a better rubric for the grading system. I think this class is great for pre med students, as it really educates you about the flaws of the medical system.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is really nice, but sometimes hard to follow along. It can get quite boring at times, but she does bring in guest speakers a lot. You have two tests which are both take at home and a presentation. As long as you participate and do your work, you should do just fine.
Easy A. Two online take home exams, one group project and discussion posts make up most of your grade. She shows a ton of interesting movies in class and brings awesome guest speakers.
so disorganized.

Mental Illness Narratives is an amazing class. Group presentation. We read a book for each unit and then answer 10 questions she sends us. Light workload. Interesting class. We watch movies for each unit and have guest speakers. I would recommend it to anyone interested in learning more about mental illnesses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Peterson is an extremely caring and knowledgable professor. I deeply enjoyed every lecture and every guest speaker she brought in. If you put in the work, she grades you well for it. She truly cares about her students and it is obvious through her actions and the way she treats her students.

The class was not too bad. To do well, you HAVE to attend all lectures and participate; I think it's 20% of the grade. Be prepared to write fast as she talks a mile a minute and can do 50 slides in 60 minutes. Nit-picky for the final presentation. Lastly, she is nice, but HATES when people are late. She can get pretty rude about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Costa really cares about his students learning, is super knowledgeable, and does a great job at facilitating classroom discussion. I'll miss this class.

I did not mind this class however i did not think it was very interesting. Professor Costa would review the readings we had for homework. He ioffers some extra credit opportunities however can be a tough grader on exam responses.  You are graded on attendance, participation, and the midterm and final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Costa is very caring. He holds 3 hour-long office hours, and makes his expectations clear. There are MANY E.C. opportunities, which is great as 80% of our grade is covered by a midterm & final. I hadn't taken a philosophy course before and struggled initially. It's an adjustment, but if you put in the effort and ask for help, you Will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy. Lots of extra credit opportunities and automatic bonus points. Professor was caring, took the readings spoke about them from perspectives you might not have even thought to go down. Emphasizes need for discussion, tries to lecture less when possible.
Professor Costa is very responsible and cares a lot about his students. His teaching approach emphasizes dialogues and participation. He is also very easygoing.

One of the more passionate professors from my experience of the philosophy department. Discussions strayed a bit from topic (and some of the major modern philosphers were given less attention than would be ideal), but overall it was a fun experience. Give the class a reasonable amount of effort and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Costa is a great guy, really friendly, understanding, and always accessible with questions. My one qualm with the class was that the discussions always seemed to stray far from the readings--I think with a subject like modern philosophy, spending a little more time explaining the material would have been helpful.

The lectures are not mandatory (I don't think) only the discussion sections are but they're once a week. He was honestly fine, the class is very Econ/histroy and very little democracy so beware you're taking this for the LHS major and are more Law and Society leaning that History. The TA Zack was really nice and not that harsh so take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great class! Although there are a lot of readings, he is an incredible lecturer... super engaging! I would 100% recommend this class. I learned an incredible amount of really formative history!
Awesome prof, insanely smart, and lectures are super great and interesting. Tho for CRM, HIST-2690, all the grading is done by TA's which can be harsh at times. Overall fun and interesting class.

Best professor at Vanderbilt. His lectures were amazing, and the class brought together so many primary sources to immerse everyone in the 70s. The grading was tough since it was mostly based on the papers, but I learned so much and it was an immensely enjoyable class.
Professor Cowie is amazing! He is a brilliant lecturer and makes learning so fun and engaging. TAs can be tough graders but don't let that scare you off! Take Cowie if you can, you won't regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cowie gives one of the best lectures of any professor at Vanderbilt. He is brilliant and it is a blast to just listen to him ramble, let alone present intense historical arguments. The class is hard. It is a lot of reading and challenges you to think outside of a normal history structure. The grading is hard. However, I can't recommend him enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt- really funny and caring, incredibly knowledgeable in history, and incredibly interesting and relevant lectures that make you understand why we learn about history. 3-4 papers a semester that are worth most of your grade. Provides pdfs of all readings, grading can be TA dependent, incredible guy

Cowie is a fun, engaging professor. The class was quite interesting and flowed well throughout the course. 3-4 papers, nothing crazy and extremely manageable if paying attention during lectures/discussion. The papers also had multiple prompt options so the class caters to student's interests. A great class to take and highly suggested.

Best professor and class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Makes me want to work hard and clearly cares for his students/how much they learn. I understand the concern regarding the grading, but I think it's worth it. 10/10 recommend.

I really enjoyed this class!! It's obvious that Professor Cowie cares about his students' well-being. Homework is assigned with built-in flexibility, there's opportunities for extra credit and turning in late work, he's very willing to explain topics more in-depth or find extra resources if necessary, etc. Would highly recommend :)

Incredible professor and labor historian, HIGH grading standards. Reading assignments can also be absurdly long. Not impossible to get an A, but it definitely takes some effort (i.e. going over outlines and rough drafts with the TAs). For the workload and standards, it should honestly be a writing course and not 1000 level. Very rewarding though!

Cowie has really exceptional and interesting lectures. They were very thought-provoking and the class was structured very well. However, his TA's grading is probably the harshest I have seen in my entire life. Like it's insane. I wish I could take another of his classes again but it literally isn't worth it with his TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, knows a ton on the topic and makes it really interesting. Probably not the class for you if you're not a good writer and/or a history major. Regularly read 100+ pages per week and yeah, the TAs are very strict in grading discussion posts and papers.

Cowie is great, and I feel bad saying this, but do not take this class. TAs are insufferable when it comes to grading. Papers and discussion posts are graded VERY harshly, and in my opinion, sometimes unfairly. Save your GPA and do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cowie is a great professor with really interesting lectures, but his TAs are absolutely brutal. I truly have never had papers graded so harshly in my entire life. It's an interesting class but the grading makes It worth not taking his classes at all. Will hurt your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cowie cares about the subject, and his lectures were entertaining. However, his TAs made the class very annoying. Lost points on discussion posts and papers for vague comments like "you could've mentioned the Kennedy article here." When asked for clarification on their comments they were not helpful and did not give answers that justified them.

This man is truly incredible. He only got a 4 because his TAs were harsh graders. His lectures are interesting and hilarious. He engages in conversation with students and will talk about anything with brilliant insight. Lots of reading but who does them and 4 hard papers with a take-home final. Loved the class despite how much work it was.

Absolutely brilliant, really interesting as well. But be ready for 100+ pages of readings on some weeks, paper expectations are really high, and the questions he asks of you in assignments can be really hard to confront. Take if you really care about the topic and you will learn a lot, but definitely not for AXLE or anything like that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Loved his lectures! Super funny and kept my interest. His TAs were a little harsh on papers in my opinion. Lost a lot of points for comments like "you could have mentioned the Coates article here." Still a solid choice. Learned a lot even though I didn't make it to every lecture. Good choice for AXLE!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Cowie is incredible. As a widely-respected expert on labor relations, he brings a passion and nuance to the subject that seamlessly moulds it with the supplementary topics of capital and democracy. Brilliant professor who is always happy to talk outside of class and provide advice. Beware though: the TAs grade papers extremely harshly.
Cowie's lectures are really incredible and he clearly is very knowledgeable. A lot of reading and his TAs weren't the easiest graders, but his class is very worth going to.

Cowie's lectures are simply amazing. Sadly he's going on leave next year :( If you get a chance, absolutely take him. The readings and papers are not too bad, and participation and extra credit help out your grade. Another option is to just audit his lectures and get the best part of the class without worrying about everything else. Take Cowie!!
great professor with engaging lectures and a good grasp of knowledge. his teaching assistants grade the papers strictly, so the class isn't an "easy a". the content is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Papers were graded a little too harsh in my opinion. Tons of reading but most of it was discussed in lectures. Overall, he is a very knowledgeable and cool professor. If I could do it over though, I would have taken country music since this was just taken for the axel credit, I wasn't really interested, and there is an above average amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Cowie is SUPER knowledgeable and an amazing professor. He's a fair grader and cares about his students. Although the class is on a very niche topic (or topics, I should say), he encourages students to make connections to topics outside of the class. There is a lot of reading, but it's worth it for the discussions. Awesome class and prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cowie is so passionate about his area and so lowkey about the fact that he is widely renowned for his knowledge. Assigns a lot of long readings but the discussions are the best part. Really critical on essays but will still give you a fair grade and good feedback. Such a funny guy and awesome teacher, makes everyone love the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor, but he makes you read too much.

Professor Cowie is great and his lectures are always energetic and interesting; however, he is a very tough grader on both tests and papers. Also, the TA was not good, and was an even worse grader. Even if you put a great deal of effort into the class, it is extremely difficult to get an A or A-.

Awesome guy that really inspired class, but a lot more work than should be expected out of a 1000-level class. Don't take this or any class with him unless you care a lot about the field and are ready to work.
Cowie's course is lecture heavy, but I found him to be super engaging! TAs graded everything-  Sarah was tough but fair. Would definitely take a class with him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Cowie makes you wrestle with issues that matter in our society now. If you came to college to establish your values and the way you see the world, this class will certainly help. His class is hard but not as hard as people claim. If you're on the fence, take it. You won't regret it!
don't take his class unless you are a history nerd
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Cowie has been my favorite professor I've had at Vandy. Cowie assigns great real books, not textbooks, and brought in an author and skyped another in class. He  cares a lot about the subject and his passion is contagious. Grading consists of 3 papers, a midterm, and a final. Talks about real world problems in class. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Something that was frustrating about this class was all the students that were disentaged and clearly doing other things on their computer. However, if you're looking for a mangeable class, I would recommend! She gives really engaging assignemnts, and I could more or less see the connections to my own life. She's such a sweet and caring professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Travers is great every time. Gives great feedback on papers, super willing to work with students about deadlines/assignments. If you're a comms major, taking lots of her classes and building a relationship will serve you well.

LOVE HER! She is so accommodating and so nice. her lectures are really interesting, and i genuinely feel that my life was enriched from the material. no joke. she moved around many deadlines if we were stressed because she is so caring!! her feedback is also really helpful on essays. she also laid out the schedule rlly nicely. definitely take!

Special topics on Space & Media: she is better in 3000-level courses than intro comms. 10 page paper + she gave super targeted feedback for each paper checkpoint. Super helpful and made editing easy. Canceled class a lot and made our final project optional. participation goes a long way and had to watch movies for midterm, can't really study for it

Professor Travers is very kind and knowledgeable; however, much of the exam information is orally lectured, and the posted slides are not very helpful when attempting to review. 2 midterms, 2 short papers, and a final exam.

I did not enjoy Prof Travers' class. Exams are tough (MC, fill-in-the-blank, and SA) and rely heavily on lecture attendance and assigned readings. She's not very helpful in office hours, so you're often left figuring things out alone. The course content is dull, making it hard to stay engaged or motivated to study. Not a great experience overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Travers!! I took intro to comms with her but I've since taken other classes too. She definitely grades progressively harder as you move into higher-level classes but 1002 is a breeze if you remotely pay attention in class. Essays were graded by TAs. She's a great professor but also a really fun/nice person!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: may not take attendance, but you CAN'T skip. slides are mostly useless and you need detailed class notes to do well on the tests. TAs grade everything (which is only two papers) and the rubric is not specific. Three tests are bulk of your grade but you can cram and get an A. she appreciates any participation a lot, so speak up. lectures were boring
Good professor. Grades include some discussion posts, 2 papers, and 3 exams. Very doable if you just memorize the slides. Professor Travers is nice and cares about students.

Take Travers if you can! Lots of people say she's a tough grader but being a good writer helps. 2 exams and 5 speeches, including one "impromptu" about the day's reading and a terrible group speech for the final. Fun class, definitely recommend for the CMST credit you need.

Professor Travers is a really engaging lecturer and encourages discussion. Speaking in a 75 person lecture is usually really intimidating, but she makes it comfortable. The readings can be long at times, but they aren't difficult. Pay attention to the vocabulary. It WILL be on the exams, and you just have to memorize it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the most high school-like class ever. Tests are straight flashcard memorization, and you need to know tiny details to do well. Go to office hours for papers, and you will do well on them. Class is mid at best, but she tries her best to make it engaging by including real-life examples. Overall, not the easiest A, but it's def manageable.

This was a very very chill class. She is a super nice professor who explains everything you need to know to do well on the exams. The exams are super straightforward, but you have to know tiny little details and all the vocab. If you know those and listened to class discussions about the readings, this is an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Travers is one of my favorites in the Communication department. The readings were short and the lectures were really interesting. Was pretty easy (2 papers, 3 exams-all take home). She is such a caring and kind person. Take her! I really loved this class
Professor Travers is so caring and always is such great vibes, loved this class! Definitely great for improving public speaking skills.

The tests are exactly from the notes. If you memorize the notes and vocab you'll get an A. Don't procrastinate on the papers though bc she's a tougher grader than you'd think. She is super caring and actually talks about life with the students though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. She has super interesting lectures with lots of connections to current events and I learned a lot.

Prof Travers was one of my favorite professors my first year. She genuinely cares about her students. Pay attention in lectures though because the tests are based solely on lectures. Fair amount reading/writing for a communications class, idk why people are complaining.

You kinda need come to class & take notes bc she answers all the test questions in class if you pay attention. Grade is based on two papers, which she will give you feedback on if you ask before you turn it in, and 3 exams that are open note and all can be answered easily if you pay attention. She is kind and wants you to succeed

Doctor Travers is an excellent professor. She seems to really care about the progress of her students, and this seemed to pay off. Taking Fundamentals of Public Speaking is a valuable experience for anyone, and I recommend doing so with her.

Public speaking wasnt the easy A I had hoped. Professor travers is super sweet and accessible but a much harder grader than I would assume. Shes so great but dont take the class unless youre seriously interesting in communications or need the credit

Professor Travers is so sweet and very clearly cares about her students. She is very willing to meet any time after class to help with speeches and is not a harsh grader as long as you put some effort in. A very chill class with essentially no work other than the primary speeches

Professor Travers did a great job of teaching this Into to Communications class. She definitely sets out high expectations but a good grade is achievable with hard work. She makes the class interesting by tying in real-world examples with rhetorical concepts. I would completely recommend her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'd definitely recommend her if you're new to Communications like I was. Make sure to study the terms and pay attention in lectures, and you'll do fine on the tests. Papers could be difficult but she was super helpful during office hours. Overall a very sweet, relatable prof

Second class with Prof Travers. Super nice, makes class fun and pretty lax on grades when you follow instructions and put in a little effort. 3 free absences, 2 major/3 minor speeches, short self-assessments on each, no midterm, easy final. Choose your own speech topics, some interesting guest speakers. Great way to practice public speaking skills.

Dr. Travers is really hilarious and succeeds in bringing the (pretty boring) course material to life. 3 individual speeches, 1 group speech, 2 papers, a midterm, and a final (not cumulative), so it is a BUNCH of work, but its managable if you plan ahead.

Important things to note: Travers is friendly and open to questions at any time Pop quizzes - do the readings well There are flexible essay due dates Tests are easy enough if you study. I learned a lot; the class discusses both historical and modern day theories and examples and is very interactive. I would recommend Prof. Travers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This class was pretty tough. Professor Travers' class is mainly lecture based and there is A LOT of information to be learned. The class is based off of 2 tests, 2 papers, & participation/quizzes. The quizzes are HARD. Tests are almost IMPOSSIBLE. Gives good feedback on papers, but I recommend this intro class with someone else. Attendance strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Super nice and is very clear with her lectures and what's going to be on tests and quizzes.  Take notes and study and it'll be fine.  Tough grader on essays, but she's very clear and very understanding.  Supplements lectures with interesting and current videos such as presidential debates and commercials.

Favorite professor at Vandy so far. The class was mainly  lecture based, but if you write down all the notes on the slides and cram them in the week before the test, you should do fine. Travers was very helpful in office hours and spent time getting to know each student's name. Excellent essay feedback. There were 6 pop quizzes of medium difficulty
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Not a Vanderbilt quality education.  Very nice but I learned ZERO. For such easy material, she only gives terrible grades. She gives so much affirmation when presenting or during office hours but never follows through.  Just do yourself a favor get the requirement over with through a different class. Really big bummer overall. 100% regret taking.

This class was easily the worst class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Not only did she not provide ANY helpful feedback on speeches, she even wrote things like "great job" while still giving less than a B. Pretty sure no one in my class got higher than an A-. She seems sweet but massively unhelpful and please if you care about yourself don't take it!

She seems helpful, but the lectures don't translate into actual use for the speeches. She will give you the same grade for every speech, even if she says that you improve. Her feedback seems helpful but even if you follow it, you can't improve your grade.

She gives bad grades to prove she's tough, but gives no helpful feedback, so you get stuck to one grade all semester. Be kind to your GPA and don't take this class. Didn't learn much, not at all an easy A.  Would not recommend.
Do not take if you are expecting an easy public speaking course grading is tough and you will get pigeon holed into a grade that you will receive constantly on every speech.

I took her Intro To Cultural Anthropology class and she was a helpful professor. The topics we covered was interesting. The 2 midterms given were fair and grading is fair. Just know the content and you will be fine. Learn to communicate.

Super nice and cares! Lecture could sometimes be a little boring, but not too bad. Some of the readings are super interesting, though some are a little long, and you need to do them to do well on the exams. Only 2 exams and 2 essays. Grading not too harsh, though doesn't give a ton of feedback on essays. Overall interesting course would take again!

I absolutely loved this course. Professor Conklin is very enthusiastic and I especially liked how she melded her own research into the course content with our readings and discussion on the Wari tribe. I didn't find any of the assignments or course content necessarily difficult, but I still felt like I learned quite a bit about the subject. 10/10

professor conklin is so nice and all she wants is for you to succeed! she is very passionate about what she does, the material is also interesting! she gives very detailed study guides that if studied, will get you an a on the exam. class is very reading & writing intensive also. participation sorta required, you can afford to miss a couple.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: so so nice and found class very interesting, she's super accommodating and wants everyone in the class to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content was super engaging and interesting. Professor Conklin is extremely passionate about her work and gives exceptional feedback on assignments. It is obvious she cares about both the material and her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The grading is hard. If you're not an Anthro major/minor, don't take it for AXLE. There's going to be a lot of writing.

Prof. Conklin is super sweet. She really wants her students to succeed and the class isn't very hard. However, there are weekly portfolios that are graded pretty harshly (depending on your TA) that take up a lot of time. By far the worst part about this class. If you need an easy A, take this class though.

Easiest class I've taken at Vanderbilt (for AXLE). Minimal studying, min. work. Teaches out of multiple books rather than one boring textbook, and provides lecture notes that has everything you need for the tests. Paper was graded harder than the tests, but you could rewrite it. Lectures kept me engaged through the whole 75 minutes. So interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Intro to cultural anthropology w Beth has by far been my fav class. I can't promise you'll learn much but it will be an easy A and its very entertaining. We had 2 papers and 2 tests and all were easy As if you do the study guide and email her questions. One of the most understanding professors I know.

Prof. Conklin is such a sweet teacher and definitely cares for her students, and she is very accommodating if any of her students need extra time on a deadline. Quizzes are simple - skim the reading and you should be fine. Her love and passion for anthropology is evident, and she encourages her students to alter their worldview. 100% recommend.

Most memorable, most impactful course I have taken. Professor Conklin taught creatively through various sources instead of using a generic textbook. All of the readings and topics were incredibly interesting and relevant to life on an individual, societal, and worldly level. Loved this class, loved Professor Conklin!

Food Politics was a really interesting class.  Professor Conklin is a decent professor and a very likable person.  Expect to do all the reading, because you have to submit weekly notes for a grade.  There's a few papers and a group project.  Overall, an enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Never got a single graded paper back from Prof. Conklin so receiving a final grade was a complete surprise a the end of the semester.  Lectures are long and repetitive, but she has some interesting stories.  Grade was 40% reading responses submitted weekly, plus a few 3-5pg papers.
She is the most enthusiastic professor I had ever been with. The topics discussed in class are really interesting..
Professor Conklin is very clear about what to study for tests and quizzes.  It is also  very clear how enthusiastic she is about her subject.

very nice but repeats herself quite a bit so the lectures are pretty boring. there are weekly quizzes so doing the heavy reading is pretty much required for a good grade. tests are essay/short answer based and are graded fairly harshly. overall not that bad/too much effort aside from being slightly disappointed with what could be an awesome topic.

I've never rated a prof on here before but had such a great time in her class I had to give her a review. She has had some incredible experiences and loves to share stories. She puts more emphasis on learning and less on specific grades. As long as you are present and make knowledgeable comments in class you will do well. I highly recommend her!

complete airhead, but very lovely. class is a joke if you know how to bs well. 2 papers and presentation are joke grades; midterm and exam are challenging, but easy if you bring in good info on cheat sheet. lectures painfully boring and she repeats her ideas a lot.

she's really nice and wants her students to do well.  Her tests are super easy. the readings are boring, but if you go to class they are not necessary.  also don't have class if you just do the readings and go to the reviews.  i would definitely recommend the class...the workload isn't bad either (2 exams, 1 paper, 1 research project)

I had considered majoring in Anthro, but after this class that's out. It was sooo boring and I had the hardest time going to class. The TAs were really bizarre and seemed to grade arbitrarily. Unless this class is a requirement for you, avoid it.

If you're not an anthro major, stay away.  5 required books for the class (including Conklin's own book), quizzes every week, and tests that are absolute monsters.  I feel lucky I got a B- after getting a 65 and 75 on my first 2 tests.  She lets the TA's do too much in the class, so you're always asking them questions instead of her.
I really loved Beth Conklin! A breath of fresh anthropological air in my otherwise stale schedule. Vandy needs more classes like this.
Delegates most of her work to her TA's, who grade encredibly hard to try and impress her.  Blatantly fudges facts, and lectures are so boring you can count on falling asleep in class.
No Comments
No Comments

Conklin is super smart and interesting.  I loved the 101 class and would recommend it to anyone; her book is fascinating.  Her lectures are interesting and she's always really excited about the material.
somewhat bitter person, not a very good teacher with horrificly hard grading standards for many who just take the class to fufill cple

Ive taken professor three classes with professor conklin and have enjoyed them all. While lectures can be slow at times the class as a hole is fantastic.  Exams are very easy, the questions come straight from the study guide.

conklin is very knowledgeable about the wari, the group she studied, and has interesting stories.  however, her lectures run long and are fairly dry (even t.a.'s fall asleep).  her tests also contain a lot of vague questions, although she looks for specific answers. all in all, not too bad for cple.
I really like this class and I think Conklin did a good job.  Lecture could get dry sometimes, but it wasn't too bad.  Reading her book was cool since she was obviously well versed in the topic.
Conklin was a difficult professor, she was unclear and while friendly, i was not pleased with her having us read her book.
Cornfields lectures are extremely boring but must attend because there are no slideshows. He literally stands in front of the class and talks for an hour. But he is nice and gives easy A.
Lot of readings that were discussed in class. Essays are doable if you take notes in class. He's very nice and knows what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Cornfield is awesome. You're graded on 4 papers. If you attend lecture which is required, the papers write themselves with the notes you take. Definitely take his class!

Cornfield is genuinly such a sweet man. He is very funny and makes you feel like you want to have good discussions in his class. The class is only graded on 4 papers so make sure you attend the discussions or else its harder to write the papers. 
Overall loved this class.

Cornfield is beyond kind and respectful. He's passionate about his work and a great beginning class for freshmen. The content was interesting, class was a little slow, but papers were straightforward and easy. It was exactly what you would expect from a beginning freshmen writing seminar. Definitely go say hello to him in office hours

Prof. Cornfield is just a super nice guy. Really cares about students, is always there to support you if you need help with the papers or just are going through personal hardness. Easy A, probably the right class if you wanna skip a bunch of them, but I would recommend going to class just to bond with classmates and prof and see new perspectives

Probably the best FYWS at Vanderbilt. Prof is extremely sweet and caring, and it's an overall chill class. Attendance is pretty optional and only about 4 people show up to class, but it's useful because it will help you write your papers. Take this class if you can!! Sweetest prof @ candy

Professor is so, so nice but his class is so boring. Def one of the easiest writing seminars out there, would recommend bc his grading is light and there's no need to do the readings if you go to class at least once a week bc he goes over everything important and you can reference those notes in papers. Summary: lowkey boring but easy and nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: kinda boring but super easy. sweetest professor at vanderbilt. super easy class. you should get an A. go to class even though its not mandatory bc taking notes will write your papers for you

Cornfield genuinely cares about the material and has a lot of knowledge on activism. The only thing I didn't enjoy was the heavy readings, but he made the concepts really interesting to learn about. TAKE NOTES. everyone says it but TAKE. NOTES. they will write your essay. go into detail on concepts and you'll get an A. Really great guy.

Pretty spot on with other reviews about him. Phenomenal guy that you want in your corner at Vanderbilt. If you take minimal notes they will write your papers. Definitely an easy A and attendance is not mandatory, but definitely show up. Super caring professor. Don't be intimidated by the four papers that make up your grade. As I said, take notes.

Professor Cornfield is one of the most caring professors at Vanderbilt. Class is not mandatory but the lectures and notes you take will write the papers for you. As long as you follow the paper outlines it should be an easy A. Class is mostly discussion-based with some nongraded group presentations. Highly recommend for a FYWS!

Such a sweet and cool professor. Prof. truly cares about what you do on campus and how that fits in with future activism. This class encourages you to think about your past, present, and future roles in fostering social change and upholding democracy. Papers are mostly theory applications from the course, but take notes in class. He says it all.
Awesome professor who really cares about his students. Grade is only four papers, but if you take notes then your papers will write themselves. Definitely take if you can! Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really solid choice for FYWS. He is extremely caring and accessible both inside and outside the classroom. Truly wants the best for his students. Take this class!

Cornfield is probably the sweetest (and easiest) prof you can take at Vandy. 4 papers, 3 are 5pgs and 1 is 10pgs. You don't need to take notes, but if you do then your papers will write themselves. Engaging teacher, he pours into every student. Connect with him, he's the kind of teacher you want in your corner. Office hours made my day.

Graded by four papers. Literally the nicest and sweetest guy ever. Really accessible and easy to talk to. Gives good feedback and genuinely cares about his students. Lectures can get dry, but as long as you have a decent understanding of what's going on it's an easy A. Cornfield is truly a great guy.

Such a great guy- very passionate about what he teaches. 4 papers throughout the semester, and as long as you know what's going on in the class, you will get an A. He's super helpful during office hours and wants you to succeed.

Our semester had four large papers based off weekly guest lectures. Dr. Cornfield is a super chill and understanding professor, who encouraged critical thinking and facilitated great discussions. Sometimes class seemed a little boring or slow, but it was a TR class, and it ended up being worth it for how much I learned.

Super easy class for FYWS. Amazing professor and you only have to write 4 5 page long papers total, which is the bare minimum for a FYWS. I honestly believe if you just write the papers, you will automatically get an A. You can't get below an A-. You just can't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Cornfield might actually be the cutest human being on planet Earth. This class is easy if you just do some of the readings and participate. It's very manageable, low stress, and an easy A. I've gotten the impression that it's much easier than other writing seminars, but it's very interesting and he's just so sweet.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy professor and kind. If you make anything less than a B+, what are you doing??
The best educationer I've ever met. Cares about students. Super helpful in office hours. Inspires us to think at a higher level.
Best sociology professor. The writing seminar is chill and easy. Grade is all based on papers. Helpful after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Amazing prof who genuinely cares about his students and helping them succeed. Really funny guy who is also extremely knowledgeable.

Dan is terrific. Great lecturer who incorporates a lot of discussion in class. Super receptive to new ideas and encourages innovative thinking. Good amount of reading, but his exams are rather straight forward; he just picks two questions from his review session and you answer one of them. Three exams and a term paper make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Good guy, good class. Lecture-based where he goes through the text readings. Don't have to do the text readings though, just take notes on it in class. This means though you have to go every class. Also literally gives you test questions before the test and you go through answers in class. Good class for easy A and you learn cool stuff. Take it.

He cares a lot about his students and takes the time to get to know everyone. While the class is about "art" it also touches on government, businesses, and society. He's a very accommodating and engaging professor. The class is almost all discussion-based, but you're only actually graded on your papers. This was my favorite class this semester.

Excellent person, really cares about all of his students. Definitely would recommend this class even if you're not that interested in the arts, as it ties in well with relevant real-world concepts in business and isn't very much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Cornfield is a great guy and wants to see his students succeed. He walks you through the test questions the lecture before the test. The class is theory based, but he tries to get you to connect it to your life. He really looks to students for what's happening on campus that could be incorporated in class. I really liked him and the class!

Cornfield is a super nice, funny guy. His lectures just bored me to death. This is the stupid easiest class you'll ever take, because Cornfield walks you through the test questions every time. I was just so bored during every class, and that's brutal for a 9 am.

Prof. Cornfield is a caring and invested professor! If you attended class and took notes during his lectures and the class discussions, you are very likely to do well! If you ever get confused, he is extremely helpful and willing to help you understand during office hours. Plenty of time to finish the term paper and  prepare for any midterms.

This class is super easy and fun! He is friendly and funny, and his tests are just 1 essay question each and he gives you the question in advance (in a list of questions, but one of them will be the one on the test). Take for an easy A and a fun time!

Great person, the sweetest guy! Super helpful! Like the comment before said, there's no need to read, just take good notes in class. Easy grader, gives review sessions before tests with sample questions and answers. Very easy to make an A, just take good notes!

Don't have to read the books before class- just get a general understanding.  Grades are based just off of examinations (that are just one essay for each of the three tests).  Attendance not mandatory.  Take strong notes in class- especially on the day before the test when he goes over the practice questions (they'll be the test)
I love him! He was so sweet. Class wasn't very hard, you do 3 essay tests. He takes time to get to know you personally & wants to see you succeed. Take his class!

Friendly, knowledgeable, open to discussion and debate. A lot of fun to talk to. Lectures are usually interesting. Class participation valued. Work load not bad and fairly graded. Great professor, great guy.
Amazing professor, absolutely take her if you can. Clear grading criteria and gives thorough feedback on speeches and writing. Cares so much for her students too!
I love Prof Johnson! Sweetest professor ever, so kind and caring. Class is very easy and she tries to make it fun and interactive
Super chill class. Quizzes are kinda random but aren't worth too much. Fair expectations and useful info for the real world for all engineers. Good professor overall.

Class is pretty chill for most of the year, one 10 min solo presentation and one group presentation towards the end, takes a bit of time to prepare for. Class content is pretty useful outside of class. Professor is caring and extremely nice
So cool and caring, would recommend everyone to take this class by her. She is an understanding and straightforward professor

Work in this class fluctuates -- there are periods where there is little to do and some periods where there is a good bit of work. Grading is pretty lenient. It is evident that she is more interested in your development as a communicator than just evaluation. I highly recommend her office hours, she's very accommodating and is willing to help.

Very useful class to take for every engineer. Some of the assignments and presentations can be tedious but it is all necessary. Johnson is very kind and conveys the material clearly. Highly recommend.
Best prof ever!! She is so kind and genuinely cares about her students. Everything we learned in class was very helpful/applicable to the outside world.
Very friendly. Course is of good pace and assignments and activities are almost always useful, rewarding, and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Johnson is extremely nice and caring. Class is quite easy but does cover a lot of useful topics and information for your career.
Professor Johnson is an angel and I would take a bullet for her

One of the most useful classes I have ever taken! Teaches you how to write reports, give presentations, make a resume, and more, with clear grading guidelines and fantastic feedback. This class has helped me in so many ways, and interviewers loved hearing about it. Any STEM major, in A&S or Engineering, would benefit. Take this class!

Professor Johnson was great this semester. Her help with resumes/presentations/writing skills were useful for several factors of my job search. I went to her several times outside of class to ask for help and she always provided great feedback. She made the class accessible and students comfortable with feedback.

Professor Johnson is a great resource for anybody looking for experience with technical presentations and the career search process. She is an extremely fair grader, and the workload is not bad whatsoever. Great class for an A and to gain experience giving presentations in front of peers.

Professor Johnson is extremely sweet and caring. The class is actually very interesting and helpful in interviews and presentations. Very easy A and meaningful content. Definitely take Johnson at some point at Vandy she is by far the best.

One of the best teachers I've had at Vandy. Extremely helpful and gave great feedback that improved my public speaking and presentation skills more than they ever have in my life. Encourages peer critiquing which also helped.

Cannot say enough good things about Prof Johnson. Class is great for working on your writing and public speaking skills. She is helpful and kind, and she provides great feedback on all assignments. Take this class no matter what you are majoring in. Mix between written papers, presentations, and other basic assignments.
Best class and teacher I've had at vandy. You learn really useful things and is almost a guaranteed A if you finish your work.

Professor Johnson is not only a wonderful person, but you also learn an incredible amount about professionalism and public speaking in her class. This course changed the way I will build powerpoint presentations in the future, and also helped me gear up for the job search. No matter your major, I HIGHLY recommend that you take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The best

Go to office hours for every big assignment and she will help you get an A. Watch out for the resume/cover letter assignment,  go to office hours for this one. She will find things you should change with your assignment. Easy to do well only if you are aware of the exact specifics and requirements for each assignment.

Johnson is awesome. Fantastic teacher, knows her stuff and practices it in the classroom. Really wants her students to succeed, very fair grader, always available for one-on-one help. Wonderful disposition, too. No tests, few short papers. The class is interactive in nature, show up and what you learn will stick. Engineering students take it ASAP.

Excellent teacher. Really wants to help you and is willing to answer any questions. Loves to hear feedback and will do different workshops depending on what your class wants to work on. Pretty easy grader, but you still need to practice your oral reports.

Professor Johnson is fabulous. For a professor teaching communication, she really gets it. She is also very fun, helpful, and encouraging, so take some time to get to know her outside of class. It's a great idea to take this when you want to prepare a resume and find an internship, as those are class assignments and she will help you polish it up
She's really nice and you do less work than with Sharp. Very fair grader too

Prof is nice and approachable but not the best at lecturing. PAs are incredibly annoying at the end. Take Bai bc she is more engaging and has better lectures. Make sure to truly study and do the work-if you have this prof rely on learning from zybooks and not really from lecture. If you put in the effort you def can get an A in this class though.

Class is lowkey hard. Everyone says if you have cs experience you'll be fine but it was hard for me. The PAs are easy at first but later they get rly hard. He does not understand the material he lectures about. He just simply reads off the slides that is created by the other professor. this guy will honor code you for no reason. thick accent so you cannot understand. VERY VERY tough grader and is not available outside of class at all. do not take.
THE WORST PROFESSOR DO NOT TAKE

Professor Csaba is really knowleadgeable, and quite approachable. He is more than willing to discuss anything about computer science in general. Poor dude needs to retire. Lectures are pointless, and even though attendance is required now, most people get the login code at the beginning of class and leave. A is definitely super easy to get, if you want a GPA booster take this class, at the expense of barely learning anything.

While Csorna is a sweet man, he does lack teaching skills. Going to his lectures are absolutely pointless and you will do better teaching yourself. Not a great lecturer. Will need to read textbook/self-teach. Exams were take home online however. Not sure if this has changed.

reviews.comment: Sweet old man, but not a good lecturer. Oftentimes, I'd leave his lectures even more confused.

The exams are easier than the homework. Lectures are not all that relevant for working the problems, but are a good conceptual supplement. He is very sweet, and I really don't know what people's issue with him is.

Can't tell if he's more out of touch with students or reality—asked if the ISS is still in orbit & expects MultiVar skills. Reads off slides he doesn't make or even review. Lectures so incoherent you'll contemplate if it's unethical to not call 911 to report a stroke. So scattered, perfunctory, & tech-illiterate that text-to-speech is more valuable
Steven Csorna is so old and technologically illiterate that we NEED him in Congress NOW!!!

We had an exam today, but due to the snow, class was canceled. Csorna did not email or put anything on Brightspace in order to communicate what would become of our exam and apparently it opened today and I missed it. Extreme lack of communication, he probably sent a pigeon out of his house with a letter or something and it froze on the way here.

Lectures were just reading off slides and few people showed up. Better off using textbook to self study and just show up for tests. Sometimes has funny demos, but just reads off slides that are posted online before class that are screenshots from textbook.

Worst professor ever. The only reason he has anything above a 1.5 is because he's an “easy A,” which WILL change next semester. Incoherent, unmotivated, technologically illiterate, disorganized, among other things. Lectures are pointless (reading off slides). There is no correlation between lectures, HW, and exams. No extra resources.

Csorna is the worst professor I have ever had. He doesn't create his own course material so he often gets confused in lectures. He isn't clear about what content is covered in the course. It was a fun and easy class if physics didn't matter for your degree, but if you're in engineering or need a strong physics foundation, I would not take him.

Terrible professor that can't teach. Spends half the lecture figuring computer settings and other half reading ppt notes and deriving equations. Had to self study everything. reviews.comment: he cannot teach, but he makes up for it in personality and grading ig

This class is way too hard! I've been trying to do everything for real but I'm gonna have to start just googling everything because my grade is too low! I really hope the final is also online or else I'm screwed
He is so sweet. Easy A and everything is online.
basically a self-taught class

If you want to learn physics, don't take him. If you want to never go to class and have an easy A, this is your guy. Tests and final were online, a TopHat code every once in a while for attendance. Super sweet and silly guy, understanding but just old af. Even he forgets how to do physics
Don't take him.
My friend attempted to off herself because of how stressful and difficult this professor was. DONT TAKE.

Dr. Csorna is genuinely the best professor I have ever had in my entire life. he is so sweet, kind, and caring for all of his students. I do not understand the negative comments people have written about Dr. Csorna because he is genuinely my favorite and best professor ever. I love physics now because of him and he changed my life. Lowkey slacked off, got a D. Only attended twice (ik, bad) but saw one guy shamelessly sleeping—prof saw and said nothing. Presents slides and says stuff like "so he is trying to tell u..." chillest guy ever. told us the first class that he forgot his debit card pin and the atm ate his card. I actually feel so terrible that nobody goes to lecture but he's soooo sweet and kinda funny.

reviews.comment: bro was the most wholesome teacher ever known to grace the school, always cared and wanted people to ask questions, but you gotta teach yourself + read from textbook to fully understand the material, not the hardest class but need to memorize a lot of formulas

I am in *1602 with Csorna and he is by far my favorite prof. this semester. His lectures are a little boring but he tries to make them funny and just truly cares about the students. He is such a sweet man who just loves to chit chat. His lectures are a tad boring but he explains things well and all the tests are take-home online. Definitely take over other 1602 options.

Lectures are useless, as he covers less than half of the topics. You MUST read the textbook or SELF-TEACH from the WEEKLY long Mastering Physics homework. reviews.comment: Couldn't care about teaching. 50% of the classes are student presentations which are 80% of your grade; make of that what you will.

Good guy I could talk to recreationally but in terms of teaching, my dead dog could teach physics better than this man. Homie straight spends the entire class writing a proof for two equations that are already given to you. Only good parts of the class were when he performed his lab demonstrations for proof of concepts. All in all. I hate physics.

Most of Dr. Csorna's lectures were quite boring and uninformative except for an occasional demo. However, there isn't much homework and all exams are online, so if you are willing to read and do practice problems on your own the class is not very difficult.

really nice guy, but probably the worst lecturer i will ever have. online textbook/program used is far from helpful. lecture isn't very accessible unless you're well-versed in physics. i respect the guy, very smart and knows his way around the subject, but would rather jump in sewage than take him again
Do not take if you don't already know physics. Lecture has nothing to do with homework or tests.
Just a cool guy, loves physics

Definitely a solid choice for any physics-major eligible class. Does not go super fast and tests are more reasonable than most. Homeworks took longer than they look though, so don't procrastinate and set out plenty of time to do them.
Showed up to class solely to get the attendance code... terrible teacher, cannot explain anything to introductory physics students. Don't waste your time, take ANY other physics professor!!!!!!

Unless youve taken a physics class before you will struggle. Does not explain concepts well, spends most lectures doing complicated proofs and examples that you wont need to know, I had to teach myself from the slides/textbook. His emphasis on timed testing favors memorization over a larger grasp of context or creative ability. Having tests where one small multiple-choice wrong could result in a letter grade drop for that test created extra stress for students.
