reviews.comment: Prof Csorna doesn't put much effort into his class. For our online class, all of the exams were auto-generated through mastering physics. Class sessions were pretty pointless and unrepresentative of the exams.

Uncommunicative, awful professor. The amount of laziness on display is truly astounding. All of the homework is ridiculously tedious. He doesn't understand how to use technology, which would be fine if he at least understood how to teach. He also consistently made changes to his prior announcements without warning. Avoid at all costs.

In my time at Vanderbilt, Csorna is probably the WORST professor I've had at Vanderbilt. His first and third exams were impossibly difficult, and the transition to online has made this class 50 times harder than it should be. DO NOT TAKE CSORNA FOR PHYSICS.

Have to self learn and study, lack of course structure and materials. I do think at one point and time he was a good prof, but not anymore. Don't get me wrong he's smart, but a terrible teacher and has trouble explaining.

You have to self study with him. Luckily for me, highschool physics really came in clutch and allowed this class to be much easier than it should've been. But still, his lectures are beyond useless and he has zero teaching ability.
lectures are useless. Have to self-study which is extremely frustrating and time consuming.

Typical vanderbilt case of super smart guy with no teaching ability. Class isn't too hard, but you could honestly skip all the lectures and your grade would be the same. The only problem is, attendance is mandatory.

Very smart guy, but he is an awful lecturer and all of the course content (including exams) is based on Mastering Physics by Pearson. Pearson has an uncountable number of issues that makes being successful in the class nearly impossible due to simple syntax errors caused by Mastering Physics and its "quirks" no matter how well you know the content.
Dude's smart but has 0 teaching ability.

Professor Csorna is a really nice guy who wants students to learn and succeed. I went to his office hours and he answered all my questions, but he is unfortunately a rather dull lecturer. This class is hard only because self-studying is needed and all the tests are less than 20 multiple-choice questions. With prior knowledge, this is a fine class.

Dr. Csrona is a really nice guy. He's very helpful during office hours, cracks good jokes during lectures, and gives good demos in class. However, he's not the best lecturer. Take him only if you already have a good understanding of Physics.

Csorna is very good at responding to in class questions, and will say hi if he sees you outside of class. The course is hard, but he makes it more manageable. Physics can be extremely hard, but Csorna tries to make sure that everyone is coping.

Dr. Csorna is a really nice guy and he genuinely wants you to do well. However, he is one of those professors that definitely knows the material well but just cannot teach it. Avoid this professor if you want to gain a clear understanding of physics. His tests are only easy for people that came into the class with a solid understanding of physics.

Dr. Csorna is a great professor. He teaches well & actually cares about how you're doing in his class. Go to his office hours if you think you need help, or to just establish a friendship w/him. He's motivated, but can be monotone at times. I had him for 121A & 251A & had to work very hard (this is Vanderbilt) & spend time in office to do well.

If you are not interested in physics, but only in getting good grades and fulfilling your science requirement, then avoid him. But as a physics major I really enjoyed his class. He is so helpful and organized. The material is tough, but I feel that I learn new knowledge in every lecture. I definitely recommend him!
Csorna does not know how to teach physics. I think he should teach Maths because he keeps doing useless derivatives in class.

Csnora clearly favors boys over girls Second, he is terrible at explaining things. He simply says the same thing over. third, we do 50 minute long derivations that we never use and do not help our understanding.

Csorna is actually one of the worst professors I have ever had. He is dull, boring, unorganized, plays favorites, etc. PHYS 116B is an awful class, no matter who you take it with, but Csorna should certainly not be your first choice.

He's willing to help you if you are willing to show some effort. But, he has very high expectations. So work hard to get good grades. He uses projector and rarely use chalk and black board, so the class is a bit boring.

boring, bad at teaching and absolutely no point in going to lectures. Physics 116A is not a hard class so just doing the homework and doing practice tests should earn a good grade. I only went to class 2 times besides the 4 tests and still did well

If you have to take Csorna (and your other option, Ramaya isn't much better) you should a) read the book b) go to lecture so you can know what is on the test (this will help you soooo much when you are teaching yourself. you dont have to know what he doesnt go over)c) go to his office hours and have him reexplain whatever he explained in class

Avoid this man at all costs. He is TERRIBLE at teaching. He just mumbles about how to derive equations. If you've never had physics before, just read chapter summaries and work practice problems like your life depends on it. Going to class is a waste, just go to tutoring and learn how to work the practice tests. Class avg on tests usually ~50%.
completely useless. 20 point curves on tests should indicate something. avoid at all costs.
Bring a pillow.

There is really no point in attending the lecture. He mumbles a lot and just reads of the notes on transparencies, which are often illegible. Requires a LOT of self teaching and study. Tests are multiple choice, but no partial credit hurts more than helps. If you have the option, take another section.

Unless physics is your thing, his lectures don't make much sense. He spends the whole class discussing equations and concepts - not much time spent on actually solving problems. Tests range from pretty easy to nearly impossible, and are about 12-15 multiple choice... he does [have to] curve a lot (our 1st was curved 20 pts) & drop your lowest test.

Lectures are pretty much useless. Figure out what chapters and sections are on the test and then study the book. to do well just do ALL the practice problems in the end of each chapter. his test well all 12 multiple choice questions but class average was curved up to a 80

His lectures are not coordinated well with the readings and labs; to make matters worse he mumbles a lot and goes off on tangents. I honestly felt that the lectures were worthless and the tests were hard. You have to read the book and understand everything very well to succeed in this course.

useless lectures, u learn everything from the book on ur own, tests are only 20 questions ALL MC & all 5 answer choices are like +A, -A, +A/2, -A/2, & none of the above so if u miss 1 tiny calculation u miss the whole question, meaning u automatically don't get A on test. terrible writing, moves way too fast, bluntly refuses to hold review sessions
Tests are all multiple choice, he's much easier than the other sections. Go to the review sessions!
Do not take.

Dr. Crawford is caring and a fair grader. I enjoyed how we worked to build our own exhibition at the Curb Center, but I felt like the segment of the class where we studied the history of portraiture was irrelevant to the exhibition project, and the readings were long and mind-numbingly theoretical. Less writing than you'd expect from a W course.

HART 1105 was an amazing, interesting class lead by an incredibly interesting lecturer. I couldn't imagine a better intro to HART. Exams were open note and graded fairly. Readings were a little boring, but only 10 were assigned throughout the whole semester. Extra credit and revision opportunities.

Made me love art history even more! Must take if you are even remotely interested in art history. Lots of readings and discussion, but definitely think it made me a better reader, writer and critical thinker!

Professor Crawford is so nice!! She is very accessible outside the classroom and willing to take her own time just to help us improve the essays. She is very supportive while students are discussing.

My course is 2710, but they don't give this option.
stay away if u want to maintain your sanity

reviews.comment: Dr. Crawford is simply wonderful! She picks the most interesting and compelling topics, readings, and works of art to discuss in class, so participation is critical. We had two very engaging guest speakers come in to discuss their work. She is so caring and respectful and is easy to reach outside of class. I definitely recommend taking her class.

While Crawford's class is generally easy to get an A in, you can tell if she dislikes you as a student. Besides that, all of her work can be resubmitted for higher grades and she allows extensions on some of the more lengthy assignments. In terms of it being a writing seminar, she doesn't provide a lot of resources to improve outside of the subject
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

Not very organized with due dates and what to have prepared for class, but easy to get to know the class flow. Overall, easy A if you do the readings and add to the discussions.
prof crawford is great. love the seminar we had.

This was such an amazing FYS with an amazing professor! The material was extremely interesting and lectures were engaging. reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Crawford is one of the funniest professors I've ever had. She makes the classroom a space where students can show up with their personalities and engage on many levels. Professor Crawford is so fun and this class genuinely changed my life and perspective. Amazing. She is not a tough grader but be ready to write. Pop quizzes every week so you have to do the readings, but they are interesting!!
Prof. Crawford teaches those classes that you walk out of and say, "hey, that really changed my life." Take her. She is fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Incredible! Crawford is hilarious, genuinely cares about her students, and wants to help everyone improve. One of the kindest and most down-to-earth, tell-it-like-it-is people I've met at Vanderbilt. Cannot recommend highly enough

Crawford was my favorite professor this semester. The lectures make you care about the material regardless of your grades on the assignments (she can at times be a tough grader) You get quizzed on the weekly readings, write 5 250-500 word essays, and a final essay. She got me interested in GSS and I would take a class with her again in a heartbeat!

Professor Crawford is seriously awesome. She highly values students opinions regardless of perspective and creates a fun and engaging atmosphere. Readings are well selected and make for a coherent course.

Professor Crawford is one of my favorite professors she's hilarious, super knowledgable, cares about students and isn't too tough of a grader, but you HAVE to do the readings to do well on essays and the reading pop quizzes. Read the material, come to class and you'll do well. Definitely take this class if you get the chance!

Western Civ with Professor Crawford was great. She's one of the few professors who's actually hilarious, and she's also very nice. Grading is lenient with incredibly easy reading quizzes and participation adding up to half the grade. The other half is essays, which aren't graded harshly.

She is AMAZING! So funny, really interesting readings and lectures, made a class that sounds super boring on paper (western civ) so fun. I can only imagine how great she is when she's teaching a class she actually wants to be teaching. Pop quizzes about once a week to make sure you did the reading and two 7 page thought papers.
She's incredible, take her class

Professor Crawford is absolutely hilarious. The class had multiple short quizzes really just to make sure you read - no tricks. There was a midterm and a final paper. The class was dynamic and I definitely learned something new every day - fantastic class!

The best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. Stay away if you're super conservative and easily offended but otherwise TAKE HER CLASSES if you're at all interested in gender or sexuality. She really knows her stuff and is super interesting and funny. Quizzes on the reading so attendance is basically mandatory, but it's also fun so it's not a chore.
She is literally my favorite professor at Vanderbilt! Brilliant, engaging, and helpful in office hours. Pop quizzes, and 3 papers, no tests. Definitely take her class!

Prof. Crawford is an amazing professor. She is so nice and so helpful. Just go to her office hours before a paper and she'll basically write the whole thing for you. She makes dull readings interesting and is extremely funny!

AMAZING! Best professor at Vandy. She is hilarious. No weekly quizzes for my class. Rated R discussions, but very entertaining. I plan on taking all of her classes she is so great! Brought us candy multiple times "just cause" Participate in class & show up & you'll be fine. Paper grades depend on the TA

Funny teacher, but I hated it when she would shove her disgustingly liberal political views down everyone's throats. Also not a bad grader as long as you cite the texts in your papers enough. Weekly reading quizzes. Sometimes she has more than one. Not difficult but not easy.

I've never had a better professor. KC is a brilliant academic, a true friend, and a wonderful confidant. She has always been incredibly accommodating, and provides all that she can for her students to succeed. On top of it all, she is hysterical. I highly recommend her.

An absolutely hilarious class. I definitely recommend it if you have absolutely no interest in history whatsoever, because she makes it bearable. TAs grade the papers (3 of them) and there are no tests. Quizzes on reading once a week (EASY).

Dr. Crawford is an amazing scholar and a good teacher, but her interest in the particular class determines its quality, although I had her for Western Civ., and I'm not sure any history teacher enjoys teaching that class. Her specialties are gender/sexuality and French history. And she's definitely hot, especially if you're a lesbian (I imagine).

easily the best professor i have encountered at vandy.  she is more than helpful and does everything she can to make class interesting.  she encourages and rewards participation in class and will not make you feel stupid for not having an answer.  make sure you keep up with your work though, she does not assign things just to ignore them in class.

Challenging class, but definitely worth taking because Professor Crawford is brilliant and absolutely hilarious. One of the funniest people I've ever met in my life; she makes even the most boring material come to life. Highly recommended.
No Comments
her**** class is the worst class I have taken here yet.  I dreaded going to it and only did so because she insists on giving pop quizes (25% of grade)

Even with potentially boring material, she finds humorous and saucy readings which engage and excite. I recommend the "Crawford Experience" to any Vandy student. If you aren't intellectually sophisticated, you may not appreciate her. Otherwise, you'll laugh in every class. Enjoy!
Took french hist. Got a B (my lowest grade yet) but it was worth it because she was really entertaining.

Crawford is the the best teacher I have had at Vanderbilt. Her classes (especially 187) are always entertaining. But I must warn... her classes are not easy. If you want a fun but challenging class, take any of Crawford's classes.
No Comments
Definately take this class! She is great at explaining, has a very open mind and good at making things interesting. Funny and helpful too!
No Comments
SHE ROCKED! I really enjoyed her class and she's very interesting. DOn't take her class if you're easily offended
One of the most fun and interesting classes I've taken here.  Crawford is very engaging in class and has a great sense of humor, given her subject matter.  Everyone should take this class!!
I really appreciated that the class was effectively all tests, no BS at all. The tests are reasonable as long as you read through the slides a few times

The class itself is all exams and lectures. If you're into that (and I am) this class is amazing, interesting, and very easy. Prof. Creanza is an excellent lecturer and person; I can't recommend her enough. Took this class as a non-Bio major and still succeeded and enjoyed it. Enroll!

Such a sweet person! Very encouraging and makes lectures pretty chill. We also had a quiz every lecture that served as attendance, but they were easy. Would recommend!

reviews.comment: Creanza is one of the nicest and most caring professors in the biology department. This class is really straightforward. The three tests are about moderate in difficulty, the pop quizzes in classes are easy and worth more than a test, and the final is very easy. Creanza tests more on fundamental principles of evolution rather than random facts.

reviews.comment: Creanza's section of Evolution was way easier than Rokas'. She's super sweet and knows her stuff, although she's really soft-spoken and easy to tune out. Lectures are participation-heavy (as in, she asks questions and encourages discussion) but not mandatory. Exam questions are very similar to textbook questions and practice questions she gives.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good guided notes, although not that engaging. Good top-hats that sometimes show up on the test. He's probably the best option for general chem. I think his notes are rather sparse when it comes to conceptual stuff, and I had to learn some of it through just doing the homework problems.

I had him for first semester, where I thought he was a fantastic professor. This semester was definitely worse. I found he spent the majority of class time on easy algebra during the calculations, but would move very quickly though the setup/reasoning behind calculations or key ideas. This definitely made the multiple choice on tests harder.
Tainter is a pretty decent lecturer and helpful during office hours. Tainter is a good option to get through gen chem.

He is a very chill person and lecturer. If you are more of follow along slides person when it comes to learning, he is definitely the best choice. His explanations are clear and easy to understand. If you go to his office hours come with questions ready or if you are confused he will clarify he always say hi when you wave or when he knows you!

It's a standardized course, so all the homework/tests are the same across all of the gen chem classes. That said, Dr. Tainter is a pretty good lecturer (although it becomes pretty fast-paced, especially towards the end of the semester). Having AP Chem experience will help a lot. Taking Chem 2 so we'll see how that goes...

Dr. Tainter is a great professor if you already have a background in chem, as his lectures are fast-paced and can sometimes skip over explaining high school-level chem concepts. If you don't, you're better off with Dr. Todd. I took AP Chem, so he was a great choice for me. Gen chem is not a bad course, just make sure to lock in from the start.

GOAT great lectures that touched nearly every concept in great detail. His notes are fill-in, so you can download them to your tablet and take notes as he lectures. In class TopHat for extra credit. Office hours are good, he'll explain homework concepts to you. I felt really prepared for exams, and he was really kind during office hours.

tainter is a nice guy. responds to emails quickly and cares about his students. the class moves at a fast pace, and he doesn't record lecture, so if you miss something ur screwed. in hindsight i would have picked todd for her lecture style.

Very nice, cares about students learning. It's a hard class regardless and his lectures can definitely move fast, but among your options, he is likely the best general chemistry professor at Vanderbilt. Good luck getting him!
Best use of class time. Goes over slides in class. Made an office hours appointments once and he was kind of rude but his lectures were helpful.

Best chem professor at vandy. Attendance is not mandatory but if you miss a class, you miss in-class questions that count as extra credit, which could boost ur grade if needed. Homework was very straight forward and he gave you plenty of time to do it. Lecture slides were simple and he explains them well. His lectures+reading textbook=good grades
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: If you actually do the work, gen chem is not that bad, tainter is the best with excellent lectures where he introduces and explains all the concepts you will need to know while still working and explaining examples which prepare you very well for the exams, he is very receptive to questions and takes his time with every student

IMO the best gen chem prof for visual learners. He has AMAZING lecture notes, and students in different sections always comment on how organized and thorough they are. Unlike other profs, he's never cranky and always very kind during lecture. The tophat textbook fills in any gaps in your understanding if you miss lecture.

Best gen chem prof you could have at Vandy. Lectures were informative and interactive, and his notes are top-tier. Occasionally I got the impression that he's a little unsure of himself; he's probably naturally more shy/reserved, but he really does know his stuff and does a great job at lecturing. Take his section if you can.

Words cannot describe how much I love Dr. Tainter! He is one of the best professors at this school, and his notes are amazing. He has mentioned to me multiple times how the greatest joy of his being a professor is seeing his students grow and succeed. Vandy is so so lucky to have him! If you take him, you will love him too :)

Dr. Tainter was great—he is consistently kind and funny in class, and he truly wants you to learn the material. He really draws the focus away from exam scores and just teaches you chemistry. His in class reviews were super helpful and overall I enjoyed his lecture.
1601/1602 are awful, but Tainter was helpful. His lectures are more “follow along” style. He responds to emails quickly and is willing to work with you.

1602 is hard but Tainter makes it bearable. He has good slides and posts the completed notes after class. He explains clearly and works through examples well. He allows questions and tries to help the class understand as best he can. I would definitely choose him again if I were to take this class again. His office hours are helpful as well!

Tainter is probably the best of the 1602 profs - he teaches the material very well but doesn't ask questions that are impossible. Gen chem 2 is a hard class with a lot of material, so you definitely have to spend outside time going over Aktivs and using other resources (organic chemistry tutor is great) to learn the material for tests.

Tainter is my FAVORITE professor. I took him for 1601 and picked him again for 1602 (like many others); his averages were always slightly higher than others. He makes himself available for office hours weekly. Gen chem tests are very fair IMO, and if you just do a lot of practice problems and go to EVERY SINGLE LECTURE, you will do great!

Dr. Tainter is great, but the class just isn't that good. He is very nice and helpful, but this lab is just so much work for 1-credit. Long reports, hard final. An engaging professor in an unengaging lab course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 1601 is notoriously a difficult class, but Tainter makes it reasonable. Lectures were engaging and prepped you well for exams. He explained material extremely clearly, and though I did not take advantage of office hours as much as I should have, friends who did said he was super helpful. If you can take him for 1601 I would definitely recommend.

He is truly a fantastic professor. His lectures are easy to understand, and he breaks down complex topics into simple ideas. If you attend lectures, earnestly do Aktiv and discussion, and read Tophat, you will excel. The chem department is highly organized at Vandy, and all the professors provide great support. 100% recommend Tainter.

Gen Chem is just a pain, but Prof. Tainter was pretty good. He's slides were helpful with diagrams and example problems. While I was too scared to ask questions in the giant lecture hall, many other students did, and he was always happy to explain. Not perfect, but his slides give you a good idea of the test material.

Chem 1601 is obviously a very notorious class at Vandy and no matter what professor you have, it's gonna be rough. However, professor Tainter tries to make it as approachable and easy as possible. His slides are very thorough, he's always willing to answer any questions, and his office hours are super helpful. Would 100% recommend.

Chem 1601 is a tricky class in general, but Professor Tainter is one of the best lecturers here. While he moves fast, his slides make it easy to prepare for exams, and he is very willing to answer questions during class. He has fill-in notes, so it works best to use an iPad and annotate the blank slides he provides instead of typing or using paper.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Taking Tainter's CHEM section next semester too. The CHEM 1601 curriculum is standardized for all professors, but Tainer's lecture slides and textbook tables made it much easier to prepare for exams. Todd and Tainter probable have the best slides of any professors, which is super important for test prep.

Dr. Tainter is the best gen chem lecturer in my opinion and he often has the highest test averages which can be attributed to his lecture style. He is pretty accessible outside of class and is very open to answering questions during lecture. For CHEM 1601 in general, exams are tricky and sig fig/units are annoying but doing Aktiv helped a lot.

Tainter provides good notes templates for lecture and is generally very clear when explaining concepts. A hard, fast-paced course in general, especially without AP chem experience, but going to his lecture was very helpful for me; I relied a lot more on just going over his slides rather than reading the textbook and ended up doing fairly well.

Hard class in general, but not Tainter's fault. In general, things seemed best for Todd's class (extra worksheets, access to LA's) but Tainter was a close second. Clear slides and a good lecturer, willing to answer questions and used class time well. Still, did most of my learning outside class. If you can't bear the 8am, take Tainter.
Teaches tough material at an understandable pace. Stops to allow for questions and is very well spoken. Highly recommended.
Gen chem is a difficult class no matter who you take but his powerpoint lectures were easy to follow, he was always prepared and knowledgeable and he seemed like a genuinely nice guy.

Tainter makes taking General Chemistry fun. He puts in the extra effort to make sure we are engaging with the material and more importantly, that we find the information fun! Additionally, the way he organizes his lectures makes it far easier to study, with clear topics on the lectures that each take up one slide.

Dr. Tainter is genuinely the best professor and overall person I have met at Vanderbilt. He is not going to sugarcode anything or pat you on the back but he will be realistic and help you answer your questions during office hours. He is willing to give you the effort if you put in the effort. He is him... overall love him.
Not the nicest guy when approaching him. Class is fully lectures and exams which is your entire grade other than a few homework assignments. Best gen-chem teacher during my semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tainter is very caring, and I wish I had taken him for Chem1601. He has fill in notes but the content is def. relevant. Course structure is very similar to 1601. He always answered questions I had and is a great prof. to have. I say aim to get him or Todd for both semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tainter is a solid choice for gen chem. Dr. Todd writes the exams, so being in her class will probably be the most ideal. However, if you struggle to wake up for her 8 am time slot, Tainter is a great choice as well. He's good at explaining more conceptual topics, and his class is overall very enjoyable. Office hours are awkward but helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tainter is genuinely so sweet and cares about his student's success, especially those who actively make an effort to succeed (office hours key). Gen Chem is tough no matter who you have, but Tainter makes it bearable/engaging with fun facts before class. He goes fast, especially on math/prac prob, so read & come to class prepared ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tainter is an AMAZING Chem lecturer. Gen Chem is going to be rigorous for a lot of people, but he cares about understanding the information and being able to succeed. He's very organized and can explain things extremely well in-class and outside of class in office hours. Definitely one of the best Gen Chem professors!

Dr. Tainter is by far the best teacher to take for Gen Chem. He's caring, knowledgeable, and his lectures are clear and engaging. He'll answer questions and wants his students to succeed. Although it's an inherently difficult course, he makes it manageable. If you take him, you're set up to do well, and have a good chance in a really tough class.

Gen chem is going to be unnecessarily hard no matter what, but definitely take this professor. His lectures are the clearest and he provides the most information. While he goes fast and gives a little too much detail sometimes, students in Professor Tainter's class seemed to have a better understanding of what was generally happening.

Professor Tainter is a solid chem professor. His lectures cover everything, but he goes a little fast. However, he's always willing to answer questions and clarify anything he went over too quickly. We usually finished content early enough that we could review in class for the exams. A great choice for gen chem!!

Tainter is a good lecturer and teaches well. This class requires a lot of work, and reading the textbook is highly recommended. Go to class and try on the TopHat questions because doing so helps you learn and potentially get 3% extra credit. The Aktiv assignments are long, so starting early is best. Ingrain topics because the tests try to trick you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gen. chem sucks, but Dr. Tainter makes it as bearable as he can. Lectures are well-planned and cover relevant material. He offers plenty of practice problems to help you learn concepts. Definitely go to class because the tests are not fun, but he does offer review sessions and old exams to look at. Great professor in a rough course.

Dr. Tainter is actually amazing. Like hands down the absolute best choice you can take for Chem. The tests are literally the same no matter who you have so trust me take him! He's the kind of professor you could do bad on an exam and still be like I fully blame myself and not him in anyway. He is so nice and made freshman year chem so much better.

If you're signing up for Gen Chem at Vanderbilt, prepare to be in for a wild, extremely difficult academically, and draining ride. Dr.Tainter was very helpful in offering tips for studying, exams, etc. He also is a good lecturer, and genuinely cares about his students that are trying their best (aka attending office hours)

Dr. Tainter is (in my opinion) the best gen chem professor offered at Vanderbilt. I actually enjoyed going to his lectures, however, do not solely depend on his lectures to get a decent grade like I did. I messed up big time by doing that but I recognize it as my own fault- I will be taking him for 1602 and I am excited honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gen Chem is a hard class regardless of the professor but Dr. Tainter prepared his students the best. He moves quickly and sometimes gives too much information, however I never had to read the textbook once during the class because he gives you everything you need to know for the test. He is very understanding and accessible outside of class.

Prof Tainter is a very funny and kind chem professor. He teaches gen chem very well and will always be open to answering any questions you may have. Gen chem, in general, is extremely difficult here at Vanderbilt, but he makes it a little less daunting.

he was an amazing professor for gen chem. the class itself was very hard even if you have a chem background. he's very chill and welcoming, so you could ask him just about any question you have. He gives fun facts before every class which is also cool.

Professor Tainter is a good option for Gen Chem if you took AP Chem in high school. If you didn't, he might confuse you a bit, so just refer back to the textbook for help. He gives fun facts before every lecture and is overall a super nice guy.
The teacher is great. He's a very respectable guy and teaches well. He cares about his students and can be pretty funny at times. Class is very hard but that's expected with a chem class.

Tainter is a horrible professor. He complicates simple topics in General Chemistry and I learned more from watching Youtube videos than I learned from him in class. The course is very challenging and my high school, unfortunately, didn't have AP Chemistry. I would prefer Todd over Tainter because she makes the course more digestible for students.

Tainter is an excellent professor who gives very clear lectures that cut out fluff so you can focus on the important stuff. Powerpoint notes can be downloaded and reviewed for ease of studying. Good sense of humor and very approachable. Teaches by the exam, which is helpful. Highly recommend. Difficulty rating is based on the class, not the prof.
Same thing as Chem 1601 if you liked him for that you'll like him for this

I had both tainter and todd.his lecture-style notes were more suited to my learning and I think that's the biggest difference between them. If you learn better from example problems tainter is your guy (he makes the discussion q's) but if you learn better thru textbook summary, do todd! depends on ur learning style not who's "easier"! gl with chem!
literal DILF.

I took Professor Tainter’s class for both Chem 1601 and 1602. Both semesters he has been amazing! He provides the slides to you before class so you can take notes with him which really helped me understand the material better. Instead of scrambling to write everything down I could really process what he was saying and do all of it with him.

He's a pretty solid lecturer and you don't really need to read the textbook. Tests though are kind of messed up because they put weirdly specific questions on the true/false & <  >. Overall a nice guy and solid choice but be ready to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gen Chem is hard regardless but Tainter really makes it more breathable. His lectures are SUPER well-structured. Make sure you understand the materials as you go along and you'll be fine. He does a good job picking out the materials that will be on the tests. His office hours doesn't really help but you'll be ok doing problems on your own.

Professor Tainter is an awesome choice for Gen Chem. I never read the textbookonly attended lectures + office hours, and I always felt prepared for exams. Chem took a ton of practice problems, but that's how it is for any teacher. His lectures often had examples of exceptions that other professors didn't cover and would often show up on exams.
Tainter makes things too complicated, only does lectures, and barely reviews material. Save yourself and go with Todd.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gen Chem will likely be difficult regardless of your professor, and if you struggle with chem or don't have much experience, you should probably not enroll in a class that only meets twice a week. I found Tainters lectures to be very engaging and thought they prepared me extremely well for the exams, and I will be taking his class again for 1602.
Favorite Chem Professor, I love how he gives us notes to write one so we are not writing everything. He writes the discussion and top hat so thats a plus too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Tainter is your best choice (up there with Dr. Todd) for Gen Chem. TopHat is very helpful to make sure you're learning concepts and Dr. Tainter is always available for help in office hours, after class, or in a separate meeting. Tests are VERY difficult without a strong chem background. Be ready to put in a lot of work and time to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I pity the person who takes this class without having taken AP Chem. Tainter is very knowledgeable, and you can tell he cares about his students, but this is easily the hardest class I've ever taken. Exams are absolutely brutal, even with lots of studying. The class itself is extremely difficult, but it's not a reflection on him personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tainter is a very good professor. His class is primarily lectures, TopHat questions and discussion quizzes which are very difficult. Exams are brutal but with constant work and practice you should be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: People say Todd is the best but I really think its Tainter. I'd compare my lecture notes with other students and Tainter's were the most in depth and comprehensive. He gives very difficult topaht questions after lecture each day that are honestly harder than exam questions a lot of the time. He prepared us so well for exams! Tainter is the man!

Gen chem is hard no matter the professor, but Tainter has Powerpoints for every lecture and does a fantastic job explaining concepts. I really feel like I got a much deeper understanding of each topic we did. Fast paced class and extra credit on Top Hat. Prepares you really well for the tests, be prepared for an extremely difficult final
Great at explaining things. Really nice too.

Dr. Tainter is very knowledgeable and his lectures are well thought out and organized. He has powerpoint slides that you can print out that serve as guided notes with blanks and example problems. This is very helpful during lecture and makes the material very clear. His lectures are easy to follow and I really felt I understood the material.

Professor Tainter does a really good job of explaining chemistry, so he is definitely a good option for students who have not taken AP chem. He moves fairly quickly through the material, but he gives lots of practice problems, which are very helpful. His lectures are also helpful.

Chem is a tough class no matter who the professor is. However, Dr. Tainter does a great job to make it as easy as possible (its still very hard). He's helpful during office hours, and is a super friendly guy. Very organized but fast-paced lectures. If you have to take chem, take it with Dr. Tainter.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tainter was not a great professor. His lectures went super fast and he barely did any practice problems. If you have no background in chem this will be a challange. Office hours are helpful though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Considering Todd teaches a 8am, I would argue Tainter is the best option for gen Chem at Vandy. At the end of the day, the work you do outside of class is what will dictate your grade. With that being said, Tainter is a good lecturer that starts off each class with a fun fact - he even works in important exceptions to his PowerPoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: he's a good lecturer and explains stuff clearly; prob the best option other than Dr. Todd. gen chem is super hard no matter who you take it from so success is just based on work done outside class. reading the textbook is useful to really understand the concepts

Dr. Tainter is my favorite professor so far at Vanderbilt. His lectures are amazing and he covers every topic in great detail in a straight forward way. The class in general and tests are fairly difficult but if you put forth the effort a good grade is very attainable. Definitely taking Dr. Tainter again.

This is a very difficult class that requires a LOT of work on your end to succeed. However, it is not impossible. I would say most people get C's in this course. Tainter is a great guy and a solid lecturer. He's friendly during office hours, just come prepared with questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is passionate about the topic and truly cares for his students, even though it might seem like it at first. His is very thoughtful about giving students time to ask questions. He apparently put effort into making lectures more interesting and understandable. Glad to have taken his class this semester!

The best chemistry professor I've ever had. He's always prepared for lectures and does answer questions well. He prepares you well for the tests. Overall a great teacher despite the nature of the class.

Dr. Tainter is a great professor and a nice person. His lectures are very clear and he frequently pauses in his lectures to ask if anyone has any questions, and takes care to answer questions asked by people on zoom. I feel that he does want students to succeed and I never felt him coming across as condescending. His lectures are kind of fun too.

He is such a mean person. He pushes you to come to office hours and when you do ask questions he looks down on you for it. Compared to the other gen chem professors, my friends who were also in his class were way less prepared than our friends with other professors.
good professor. hard class but he explains well and is very helpful during office hours

Lectures are very clear and understandable, although the pace is quick. Aleks online can be a B**** but you gotta get through it. Tests are tricky and class pace would be challenging for anyone who has not taken AP or does not have a solid foundation in chemistry.

Super nice guy. The class was really small because it was an 8 am, but it's worth taking Dr Tainter. Really loves chemistry, teaches at a good pace, and even gives fun facts at the beginning of class each day.

Tainter is a great choice for 1601. Lectures are engaging and he works at a much more reasonable pace than other professors. He is accessible outside of class, and definitely get the sense he wants you to do well. Definitely an easier class if you have AP chem background,( i didnt and office hours helps). Ill get an A- or B+ depending on final.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took chem 1601 twice with Dr. Tainter. The first time, I thought he was intimidating and a horrible professor but I realized I was just frustrated with the material. He is actually very clear during his lectures and really helpful in office hours! Chem 1601 is a major weed-out class so you MUST do all the readings, problem sets, etc to succeed!

Pro: clear grading expectations, responsive to e-mail, overall good and kind person, sometimes responsive to student feedback Con: write-ups for labs are tough and extensive (usually 10ish pages), concepts don't make sense in class, hard final, doesn't really answer questions directly

Dr. Tainter is great. He is a clear, engaging lecturer that makes sure the material is understood. He is extremely accessible outside of class. Gen Chem is a very difficult course, and it really helps to have previous chem experience, but Dr. Tainter will work with you to get you the grade you need.

I really enjoyed Dr. Tainter's class! He presented all the topics we needed to be successful very clearly and answered some questions in class. His office hours were also very helpful. I also read each chapter of the textbook. Although the tests were still incredibly difficult, it was a fair class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Tainter's lectures made 8 a.m. gen. chem very bearable. He starts every class with an interesting couple of facts before jumping into material. He is very neat with his notes and makes very good use of diagrams and drawings. Overall, his lectures are very simple and very clear. He is open to questions and very helpful with his answers.

Tainter is a good lecturer. He is helpful outside of class, but he wants you to have good questions. Homework is not too bad, but you definitely should work more problems outside of class. I feel that reading the book is optional, but still have it for charts and practice problems. Remember that this course is completely designed by the department

Dr. Tainter is the man. I never once opened the textbook, I only went to his lectures and took notes. I found his teaching style to be very clear and straightforward. Everyone I've talked to who had him last semester is sad he wasn't an option for this one (that's only four people but still).

He is a solid lecturer, yet some simple questions asked were either met with blank stares or dry answers as well as practically glossing over the information. In order to succeed well, you will need to read the textbook alongside his lectures, as he does not provide some information in lecture found in the book needed for tests and the online HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had him for his 1st ever class and this was my 1st ever college class. His lectures go along with the book, but you really need to work a lot outside of class to understand it. Departmental exams, online hw, and recitation quizzes are the only things for grade. For being a new lecturer, he does try his best and I'm sure will get even better.
Good lecturer- funny, and engaging as well as knowledgable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Tainter is an amazing professor, especially for being so new. I really appreciated his lectures and advice. You can tell he really does care about his students and that they not only succeed but also fully understand basic Chemistry. His tests are uber-hard but it's totally worth it. He will prepare you for the rigor of upper level STEM classes

His lectures were basically outlines from the chapter, but he presented all the information clearly.  His in-class examples were fine, and he did a good job answering questions. However, the tests are institutional and meant to be tricky. You will need to put in a lot of extra time to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For his first semester, Dr. Tainter did a great job lecture-wise. He was willing to answer any questions during class and put a lot of effort into making the concepts as clear as possible. The tests in this class are institutional and purposefully difficult, so you will still have to put in work outside of class, especially if you haven't taken AP.
Extraordinary pianist and inspirational mentor. Dedicated to his work and very responsive to student's questions. Recommend!
He is my teacher this summer. I feel like study with him for each of the following summers. He is a teacher with many stories. I also like his performances.

Great pianist!!! He's so knowledgable but never arrogant in his teaching! People talk a lot about his tough grading but he emphasize more on students' consistent progress. It's such a loss not to take his class!!:p
They said it... this guy is incredible.  If you're going to take piano lessons at Blair, Take Him!!!  That is all (:
My hero!
Amazing pianist

I really enjoyed the class and its material and would def recommend. GIS is such a good tool to know and this class definitely taught me enough to where I feel comfortable using it even outside of class. Dr. Curry-Johnson was nice and personable, she encourages asking questions and loves class engagement.

Curry-Johnson is clearly passionate about GIS and mapping. Kind and accommodating, willing to work through issues you have. Cool hands-on/technical class with a reasonable load for homework, projects, etc. Limited exploration of the software--sometimes felt like we were doing the same thing for weeks. Final group project allowed for exploration.

Great professor and class, thoroughly knowledgeable on anything and everything related to GIS. Awesome lectures and doesn't hesitate to elaborate on anything that isn't clear from the get go, extremely caring and will accommodate your learning style and timeline, great feedback on assignments. Big final project at the end, choose your group wisely.

Class was fine. Definitely learned how to use QGIS, and it was minimal work, but class time is pretty useless. VERY long hard to parse lectures, mostly containing information you don't end up using. She was clearly very excited to be teaching this class, but grading criteria was rather unclear at times.

Professor Cusomato is one of the kindest professors I've had at Vanderbilt. She's very understanding about late work/missing assignments/extenuating circumstances, and she's also a really good teacher. There's a lot of assignments, but they really help you grow as an artist

Farrar is the best! I wish I got to know her better. The class is well-designed, she gives all students lots of attention, and she truly appreciates everyone in the class. This class is demanding time-wise, but you will leave with tangible pieces that you are proud of as well as a new skill you can carry with you for the rest of your life.
She is a very nice person. Class is interesting as long as you enjoy it and like drawing, otherwise it becomes a bad choice.

AWESOME class. I came in with some art background, but I was not at all confident in my art ability. After taking this class, I improved more in one semester than in 3 years of art classes in high school. Farrar is an incredible teacher (and artist) and as long as you put effort into the in class drawings, easy A. Hardly any work outside of class

Farrar was an awesome drawing teacher! Some people in my class didn't do as well, but I think she really looks at how much effort you put in. She'll help you if you're trying to get something right, but she'll probably dock you if you just slap something down. Make sure to participate in critiques too! Drawing was an awesome class too.

Professor Currey has been an amazing professor. Class is always fun and productive, and you get a lot of hands-on poetry experience. All the readings have been really interesting, and even as someone with little poetry background, I have found this class to be very enjoyable.

Professor Currey (who also simply goes by Joanna, if you like) was an outstanding professor. I had no academic experience in writing poetry prior to her class but am leaving feeling really engaged and excited to continue writing. She's receptive to input (taught us more about form and pentameter when we said we wanted more). Highly recommend.

Professor Currey is great! I really enjoyed the one-on-one sessions where we corrected pieces of writings I turned out and discussed how to improve it. There were times when my writings seem lackluster, but she is always encouraging! I like her unbiased attitude towards writings, but I kind of hope that she will shed some personal insights, too.

Craig is an amazing and incredible professor. His lectures could sometimes get boring and hard to follow but overall this class was easy and taught well. The mindfulness course was a fun element and there was only 1 paper for the class. Take a class with Craig before he retires !!

I just want to say that if you're reading this, enroll in his next class before he retires. I don't know how else to describe how caring he is as a professor. Don't let the writing you have to do for this class scare you, he will give plenty chances for feedback

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Super cool guy and I love hearing his stories. 

Super understanding, I loved the assignments in his class, and I want to take more of his classes in the future. 

If you're on the fence about taking one of his classes, DO IT! You will love it :)

Craig is a very sweet professor. He is very understanding about mental health and personal challenges, so if you need an extension, just ask! As long as you do all the papers and Padlet posts required for this class, you'll do well.

His class is undoubtedly the better choice out of the two intro classes for the Cog Studies major. No exams at all, just three papers and a final project which can all get a little tedious but aren't too bad in terms of difficulty. He is incredibly knowledgeable about what he is teaching although lectures can sometimes drag. Great guy overall!

1117 was the most amazing freshman seminar. The class is low stress & a great transition into Vanderbilt. The stress management portion was beyond helpful. 1 essay, 2 projects, weekly reflections. Lectures can be long, but what you take away from the class is well worth it! Take Craig's class. He's cares so much about each and every student.

This class is perfect for anyone getting started with the Cognitive Studies major. There are 3 papers (that are easy to do well on if you follow directions), weekly discussion posts, and a final project. There is a lot of assigned reading but you just skim through them and be more than fine. Prof Smith (goes by Craig) is quirky but very kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Craig was the kindest and most interested in his field professor I have had this semester. The classes were very interesting and I learned a lot. I took PSY-PC 1117 as my writing seminar and it was such an amazing class. I would recommend taking any class with Craig as it was such a great experience!!
Craig is a great professor. He is very kind and understanding. You will learn a lot of meaningful stuff in his class. I highly recommend!

Craig is one of the nicest, most understanding and caring professors I have ever had. The assignments are meant to help you grow, not to harshly critique you. Great writing credit for Peabody and introduction to cognitive studies. Lectures can get long winded, but the class is easy workload. 3 papers and a final project. Would recommend!

super accessible, very chill with extensions, cares a lot about well-being of students. grading makes sense, and A is obtainable. that being said, lectures are incredibly boring and you may fall asleep, but it is an easy A.

Craig knows what he's saying really well, lectures well, and facilitates class discussion well. The class is four papers, a final project, and participation. The papers are fairly easy and he gives good advice and feedback on those papers. Really cool guy, really conscious and aware of what's going on in the world. Good dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Craig is the best professor I've had so far. His lectures can get tedious but he generally recognizes and calls it a day. Definitely utilize office hours if need be. Grade is based off of 4 8 page papers that are very formulaic (but helpful in understanding the material), discussion posts, and participation. Interesting content, A is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Craig is a sweetheart and very accessible for help. The structure of the class is logical, a paper due at the end of each topic unit and a final project, but the lectures can be a bit disorganized. The readings he selects are fascinating and relevant to the units, but they are long and numerous. Overall, I highly recommend Craig and this class.

Craig is a nice guy who really cares about his students. The readings were interesting, though sometimes class discussion was unproductive and we didn't get to discuss them in depth. 4 thought papers that you can send to him ahead of time for helpful feedback and a fun final project. Overall a good class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, and clearly of unreal intellect, but class discussions can get somewhat all over the place. There's a ton of reading (several books + a bunch of articles) and a fair amount of writing (four 8 page papers), but as long as you stay on top of it all and plan ahead, it's not awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Craig is a great professor, but can be a bit rambly. He really cares about his students and wants to help you learn and think critically. The only assessments are 4 6-page papers. (No tests!) There is assigned reading, but you only really need to read what you need for the papers. If you do your work and put in the effort, you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Craig seemed to have no clear direction for the class, made comments that were sometimes uncomfortable. Not a bad man, but not a great professor. He had lofty goals for what he wanted the class to learn but got derailed by conversations that were somewhat interesting but ultimately led to me learning nothing the entire year.

I love this class because he creates a comfy environment in which you learn how to think. You really get in the mindset for thinking critically and creatively- applicable to any field, not just psychology. The "thought" papers reflect scientific thinking and how scientists chew on and develop ideas. We learn about and discuss many different topics.

Craig Smith is a great professor who is very distinguished in the realm of psychology. Instead of tests he assigns Thought Papers for most of his classes (1207 also) but they're not difficult and he gives very helpful feedback.

Craig is an awesome teacher, although sometimes leans towards the crazy side. SPITs are hard work, and I've consistently lower grades than I believed that I deserved. Slow on the grading front, so don't expect getting your papers back in a timely fashion. Other than that, an awesome class that really sparked my interest in cog studies!
His lectures are often too rambly for my taste, but he is a great guy in general and makes everyone feel welcome.

Super easy class, no exams, the only major assignments are 3 thought papers and a group project. Extra credit given for participating in psych research. Craig is very accommodating but he is a frustratingly slow grader.

No tests! He's an enthusiastic lecturer and keeps people engaged for the most part. Sometimes can get a bit ranty. Papers amount to rambling but it's generally interesting, constructive rambling. Interesting readings for sure! Pretty easy class, good psychcog science Intro. Take it! It's a good class with a good prof.

Craig is a cool guy, he takes attendance so you have to go. Class participation and the 4 papers will make up your whole grade, but he even says his class averages are higher than other Peabody classes. Overall very easy class, no need to take notes. Just make sure you say a couple things every class so you get participation points.
Readings are interesting, and it's easy to do well. But, there's a lot of work and a lot of papers...that unfortunately don't actually teach much classes aren't worth the time, but are mandatory.

Incredible professor/researcher/advisor. He will bend over backwards to help his students out, and is about the clearest explainer of any professor in recent memory. He really wants to see his students succeed and is very approachable. He responds to emails quickly and thoroughly, and makes himself easily accessible outside of class.

I've had him for 1200 and 1700. best teacher i've had a vanderbilt. His lectures may get to be hard to follow, but if you just pay attention then writing the papers is NOT hard. He is so helpful and is willing to work with you. the only bad ratings that craig has are probably of students that didn't pay attention and tried to bs the papers.TAKE IT!

Craig is one of the most kind and helpful professors you'll ever have, and he's easy to get in touch with. All papers, discussion-based (often rambling), much easier than A&S classes. Definitely geared towards freshman so sometimes I got a little bored, but you do talk about a lot of really relevant and interesting topics.  Craig's a great guy

Craig is a really nice guy, and he's willing to work with you if you have any issues.  However, this class was sort of pointless. I didn't learn anything and wasn't even sure what we were supposed to be talking about most of the time. It's just discussion-based which got very hard to follow. Not hard, but not an easy A.

SUCH a nice guy. He stresses participation, but he mostly takes it in the form of attendance. you'll have to do a lot of writing, but it's worth it with no final, and just combining reading into the form of 5 or so papers. No tests, just papers and an entirely "discussion" based class.
Fun guy, though their is a lot of writing for a non-W course... still enjoyed the subject.

Craig is a nice guy, and the class is pretty easy albeit slightly boring. There were no tests or homework just 5 papers on "required" readings. As long as you write the papers, expect a C+ minimum, but don't expect to get an A unless you actually put a decent amount of time on them. I spent about 3 hours on each of them and averaged about a B+.
The class is really boring at times.  He's also not as fair of a grader as everyone says that he is.  The discussions can be interesting, but when they're not it's painful.
Such a nice guy!

Craig is a smart man who knows his stuff, but if you want the class to be more than just the lectures, you have to ask good questions and get a good discussion rolling. Craig is funny + will sometimes go off on tangents while trying to answer some questions. Good stories and and a dry sense of humor. I liked his class structure and grading style.

As many people said before, the class material is very interesting. Class time can range from boring when the professor just sits and speaks the whole time to very engaging when we have discussions. Only assignments are 5 6-8 page papers that end up being pretty easy and sometimes interesting to write based on their structure.

He was my VUceptor during my freshman year. He's a really nice and funny guy who knows how to make something as horrible as Vanderbilt Visions a little less painful. He would take us out to free dinners in lieu of discussing the weekly topics. I was lucky to have had possibly the best possible VUcept group EVER!!

Most interesting class I have taken in my whole life. It's interesting b/c is very applicable & relevant to life. Craig is nice, encouraging, helpful, fair,& knows his stuff. If you pay attention & take good notes in class you might not even have to do all the readings to write your papers. Sit at the front of the class since he is a bit monotone.

really nice sometimes funny guy. subject material was really interesting even though his lectures were a little boring at times.most papers were opinion papers so as long as they were well written it was fairly easy to do well. helpful outside of class and knows a lot about this subject. only recomend however if truly interested in the subject

Very kind professor. I have had him for two classes and have not really had to sweat either. His two ways of evaluation are participation (classroom and message board) and several essays. Take him for 1200, but unless you are into the psychology of emotion, only take 1600 if you don't have a better option (a little boring)
I hated this class.  The discussion groups were extremely aggravating, and tended to center around entirely moot points.  Not as fair of a grader as every one says...
This guy is so nice. He knows his stuff and is geniuinely happy about teaching. Three papers and a project? Done and done.
lectures are boring because he is monotone, but the material itself is really interesting; the papers are easy to write and he is a pretty easy grader--good class all around
Craig is awesome.  His classes are great, trust me.
Very interesting class. He's a great professor and he knows his stuff! Your grade is from 5 papers that you write throughout the semester. Fair grader. Really interesting topics.
No Comments
Also teaches: PSY 1700 and PSY 210: Emotion and Adaptation

The course is overwhelmingly fast-paced. There's a quiz every class from the hw. Lectures include examples from the book, which helps for homework. The solutions manual = life-saver. His office hours are stressful and intimidating, but helpful. The evening exams are too long/complex for the allotted time - SO HARD. Fun material, though!

daily quizzes on the hw are a good grade booster. besides that, its a difficult class and requires a lot of work. tests were way too long and difficult in the beginning and it showed in the very low test averages. finally made the last test easier and more doable. don't take just to fulfill a requirement

It is a hard class but he is a very fair grader. You absolutely have to go and work really hard, but he is more than willing to help. Go to office hours and do the homework really well and you will be fine.
Tests are much harder than any problems you see in class. Skips over a lot of material that you are expecte to know and only goes over new topics once.
if you are extremely self-motivated and very good at math take his class...if not good luck its hard

I would definitely recommend taking this course. Dr. Curwood makes the topic very interesting and is extremely helpful. The workload isn't extensive and it is not hard to get a good grade. Take this class, you will not regret it!
Super nice and knows what she's talking about. Essays were short and simple and she grades pretty easily. Readings are actually extremely interesting.

She is great, knowledgeable, really sweet and very flexible. Your grade is based on three papers, participation (on seven books) and attendance (although not explicitly mandatory, it is). She expects much from your writing and will allow re-writes. Only qualm: Discussion-based class got a bit boring if people were unprepared. NonReaders: Beware.

dr. curwood isn't horrible, but i wouldn't say she is the best here at vandy. she is extremely monotone, but she knows her stuff. she expects a lot out of your writing, but she is not an extremely hard grader at all.

One of my favorite classes at Vandy! Dr. Curwood is very knowledgeable and an overall sweetheart. We had great class discussions including watching a Trina video to analyze her feminist values. take this course!
Nice, very helpful. The class is discussion based which got very monotonous. Papers are not graded very hard and she is very communicative about your strengths and weaknesses.

Personally I did not care for Dr. Curwood's course this fall semester. I did not feel as if the class was valuable to my education and it became very mundane and repetitive. She needs to improve on her teaching style to further capture the attention of the students in class. I did not care for how she basically force fed the information. I did enjo
No Comments

Dr. Curwood is an amazing professor.  I enjoyed every aspect of her class, and looked forward to attending every meeting.  I praise her teaching style, and strongly recommend taking one of her courses.
Worst CS professor I've had. Uses a large curve to compensate for his inability to teach or speak clear English.
Difficult class.  Class average on the tests ranged between 55-65 for all.  HW is 40 percent of grade though

3 programming assignments, 1 test, and a project worth 50% of your grade.  An easy grader on everything except for the final deliverables on the project.  I'm slightly retarded at C++ and ended up with a 92, but he gives a nice curve (A was 90-100).  Bonus project worth up to 10% extra. attendance never taken

You will have to read to understand sometimes, and it can be hard to understand what he is saying, but if you go to office hours he will be very helpful and you will get your work done. You will come out with a deep knowledge of C++

somewhat hard to understand in class. book is extremely helpful in determining code, but if you go to office hours he is really helpful. i didn't go to class for a month and still got an A. big grade curve he defines at beginning of class. tests are difficult but not overly taxing.
No Comments
No Comments
Overall, a great professor and lecturer. She is very understanding and will help you improve your writing no matter what background you are coming from.

Dr. Cyrus has a great approach to teaching an introductory writing seminar. She chunked the writing process for the big research paper into approachable sections and made tackling the assignment less intimidating. She gives great feedback and is very supportive. The subject material was fun to learn about because of Cyrus' engaging lectures.

Dr. Cyrus is an *interesting* character and took some getting used to, but by the end of the year I liked her. The class was low-stress but the amt of homework she assigned was pretty unreasonable with multiple things per day, some of which she expected us to spend multiple hours on. But you can definitely get by without putting that much time in.
Dr. Cyrus is great. Her papers are a lot of work but she gives great feedback and ultimately will make you a much better writer. She's extremely flexible to student needs as long as you communicate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr Cyrus rambles off topic constantly about things that are not only irrelevant to class but to life in general. We once spent 30 min listening to her talk about the social hierarchy of nuns in the 1300s. Class is disconnected from the writing assignments which leaves you doing a ton of outside research for papers and wasting your mornings in class

Very helpful, well spoken, and knowledgeable. Class is a lot of work, but that's because it's a writing seminar. Also, don't be afraid if she starts talking about music theory, because you don't actually have to know it to succeed.

Cyrus knows her stuff, and is overjoyed when her students are actually interested in the topics. My best advice is to make her KNOW that you're working. She has the best mercy with office hours I've seen so far at Vandy, and she LOVES you if you actually use them. TAKE GOOD NOTES.

I can agree with most of the previous comments.  Her teaching is creative, eccentric, but she does present the material achronologically, which is very confusing considering that by the end of the semester, you're supposed to be able to label materials, visual and aural, according to time period.

Dr. Cyrus is a good teacher. Most of her lectures are engaging but she should work on consistency. Still though, she has a load of office hours, and is pretty creative with the interactive stuff. Incredibly smart but her class just shouldn't be on TR, because it drags on.

has too much on her plate...shouldnt' be allowed to teach considering she's head of the dept, has about 5 kids, editing a few books, and her husband is  in irak.  come on lady, you're smart, don't teach!

class is impossible and not clear at all. she jumps around chronologically, doesn't define terms, refuses to give anyone an A, and is honestly one of THE weirdest people i've met. she appears willing to help but you're obviously low on the priority list
No Comments

It's a writing course, which is pretty self-explanatory. As long as you attend class, the pop quizzes that come up won't seem that bad. The prof makes class enjoyable, but she often responded to my emails with questions 5+ days after I sent them, and is incredibly late (like, over a month late) to return paper grades to you- so just a heads up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was a really nice teacher, super funny and easy to talk to. Participation matters, and she'll pop quiz you pretty frequently, and right when class starts so don't be late. Also really odd/inconsistent grading some papers most of the class would do really really well, others the majority would do horribly. No tests which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Devereaux is by far the most chill professor I've ever had. She's very hip and funny, although the reading and assignments do pile up at times. If you put in the work and are active in class, she will like you and reward you accordingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Devereaux is a fun professor who makes the class fun. This class focused on death and dying and Professor Devereaux was very insightful. The class was 3 papers, a presentation and one revision. Occasional pop quizzes on the readings were tough.

Don't listen to other people. She's a great. She can come across as a bit dry and intimidating at times but her orgo knowledge is unmatched and she wants to see you get an A and the syllabus is structured around ample extra credit opportunities.

You could tell that Dr. Kim is a knowledgeable person, though this often made lectures a bit more challenging due to her vocabulary. Discussion quizzes are helpful, and she helps out with the grading scale and extra credit. Study and go to office hours, and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally the worst professor and person ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: - Trust take Daria. This is the most reasonable and individual professor. She cares about her students as long as you show that you care. Do not be afraid of past reviews. She has cleaned up the class - her averages are 75s like the other sectioms
Not good. Stay away
does she write her own reviews on this site?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dr. Kim's class! Lecture-heavy, but that's to be expected in Orgo. I liked her mechanistic explanations for organic reactions, and they helped me understand the fundamentals of organic chemistry better. You definitely have to like chemistry to like Dr. Kim's class, but if you don't like chemistry, why take the class to begin with?
I truly got an appreciation for how reactions worked taking Dr. Kim's class. Yes, it was challenging but I came away from the class with a much better understanding of Ochem

I love MOs!

Wish we covered the last 3 chapters though.

Don't take Kim if you only want to get past orgo, or only learn HOW a reaction happens. She teaches molecular orbitals which explain WHY an organic reaction happens. This class is only for those who want to do orgo research or simply want to learn the real thing.

Definitely would not recommend taking Orgo II with Dr. Kim. Her grading criteria was confusing for tests, and she was the only professor to not let us take participation quizzes in groups. Overall, very tough class, didn't learn the last 3 chapters, and she wasn't very accessible outside of class.

Least accessible, rude, does not take feedback, and seemed to constantly have her foot out the door. Her lectures were a mess, and did not reflect the textbook or other sections. Weekly, incredibly dense quizzes graded for correctness. Exams near-impossible, grading was not transparent and you never knew where you stood. WILL RUIN YOUR SEMESTER

DO. NOT. TAKE. She made her own curriculum which heavily emphasized molecular orbitals and gave us near-impossible quizzes every other class. We did not cover the last three chapters like other sections, and she had TAs that could not help explain her content! The average of the first test was so low that by writing your name you could get a C.

DO NOT take Kim for Orgo II. I went from a B+ in Orgo I to barely passing her class. She was hyperspecific about what she was looking for in exams and barely gave partial credit. Went to every office hours and only got more confused by her convoluted answers. Wish she could have structured her class more similar to Hare/Clements.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First exam averages ~ 40%, she curved it pretty significantly though. No other curves at all but the averages got better. Offers significant bonus points on her exams but they're stuff that aren't really taught, just connections that you can only really make between topics if you truly understand them. Grading is at times are all or nothing.
Very risky

I'd avoid taking Orgo 2 with Dr. Kim for now. This was her first semester teaching undergrads orgo. Dense PowerPoints, often used complex vocabulary, and quizzes for accuracy which made the class harder than it should've been. Class was heavily MO-theory based and often asked to reason our answers. Didn't finish last 3 chapters. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!

Bad course experience. Content is severely inconsistent with the other Organic Chemistry sections. little focus on mechanisms and synthesis and instead is very heavily based on MO theory. Pacing was terrible. Some days got out 20 minutes early with nothing learned and others were grueling 75-minute info dumps. Never got to the last 3 chapters.

DO NOT TAKE! Her lectures put you to sleep and are incomprehensible, I could never understand a word she was saying. She teaches more in depth than any of the other professors (MO theory of reactions??) and it does not help you understand the material. The textbook doesn't have most of this MO stuff so you can't even teach it to yourself.

David is probably the most caring professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He's truly one of the best and knows so much about what he's teaching and is definitely very passionate about it all, too. I cannot recommend him enough if you're thinking about starting a Russian class. He is AMAZING.
