Great Professor, can not recommend David enough! He is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt and cares about how much students learn. Definitely take this class if you need to take a language class or are interested in the Russian minor/major.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Happy to be another addition to David's 5/5 streak. If you take RUSS1101, you will love it, and you will get an A, but you'll do work for it. Every day it's somewhere between 30 and 90 mins of homework, but David is generous with exceptions for almost any reason, and you can always revise for full credit. I really encourage you to take Russian!

David is one of the kindest humans to have existed. He is very enthusiastic about the Russian language and puts in a lot of effort to make sure we know what we're doing, and even if we don't, he never makes us feel incompetent. He is awesome! If you're considering taking Russian, DO IT!!!
AMAZING! He will make you wanna learn russian
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: David is a phenomenal professor with a contagious enthusiasm for the Russian language. He cares so much about his students, always making time for extra help and allowing us to correct our work. Class time is filled with interactive activities that encourage us to practice speaking Russian. The homework can be a lot, but none of it is busy work.

The G.O.A.T.! No professor is as engaged and aware of his students as David is - truly an unparalleled learning experience. Lots of work though, but it is worth it, you signed up to learn a language, after all...

David was an amazing professor, so fun and caring!  Class participation is important and immersive. The homework is heavy, but it really helps you learn. Each test is cumulative. I loved this class, it was really fun and I learned so much more than I thought I could've!

David is great. He is extremely energetic and cares a lot that everyone learns the material, but he is not at all harsh with grading. As long as you do the homework and go to class you will get a good grade.

David is by far the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. I was really struggling with Russian when I came into his class, and I've turned around into understanding it much better. I love going to the Russian events outside of class as well! If you're unsure of who or what to take, take Russian with him!!!

Professor David shaped my Vanderbilt experience more than any other professors! He is a phenomenal instructor, and genuinely cares about his students as people, and is so passionate about Russian. He genuinely wants his students to do well, and will help you and is very accessible. He is an incredibly kind person!

David is a gem - absolutely one of the best professors I've had the fortune of interacting with at Vanderbilt, and he made learning Russian feel extremely easy and spiked up my general interest in Russian culture too. Would absolutely recommend him to any and every one.

Absolutely AMAZING. David is always super willing to help and super engaging and enthusiastic in class. Makes potentially boring material fun and made me really take an interest in Russian merely one week in despite having never taken it before. Hands down would not have survived the class without him.

Like every other review says, David is the best professor I have ever had and probably will ever have. He always comes up with activities in class to engage us instead of reading from the textbook, and he always is willing to help outside of class! He is also the reason I was inspired to pick up a Russian major!

David is easily the most energetic professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He knows to effectively learn a language you need to actively engage with it, and devises many (often humorous) ways to get the class involved. Very kind and helpful, definitely recommend taking a class with him.

David is the best language teacher I've ever had, any language. He makes it so easy to pick up. He makes class fun and interesting and submerses you in the language. An absolutely fantastic professor. He made me want to major in Russian and become fluent, and I'd never taken Russian before this year.

David is AMAZING. Super kind and patient, fantastic teacher, very caring and understanding. He's passionate about Russian and will pass that on to you. If you have interest in the Russian language, take it with David Johnson. Vanderbilt would be stupid to ever get rid of him.
You need to participate a good amount but the class is so fun. She is an amazing professor and very caring. I would take this class 100 times because of her teaching.

Professor Wasick is THE BEST professor I have met at Vandy so far. She is the most caring human you will ever meet. Her class was so educational yet fun. As long as you attend her class, turn in your assignments on time, and do well on the quizzes you will do great. This is an easy A if you take this class seriously.
Wasick is a really fun and entertaining professor. You can tell she loves teaching! Fair grader and overall a good experience.

¡Profesora Wasick es FENOMENAL! 

I love Profesora Wasick and her class! She is hilarious and our class was always so much fun. Participation is mandatory, but there are many opportunities to do so and it helps build your Spanish skills.Great teacher and the reason I'm taking another Spanish class next semester.

I took her for 1101, and I only wanted to take her for 1102! She is amazing. Very funny, kind, and considerate. As long as you participate and demonstrate an interest to learn the content, you will get an A in the course. Make sure to keep up with daily assignments and practice when given the opportunity in class, as this will help you do better!

Dr. Wasick wasn't terrible, but she wasn't great. Didn't get grades back for months after quizzes, content was essentially cut in half halfway through the semester. She is very accommodating, however. It's clear she doesn't want you to stress over her class.  Overall, very easy A, though I definitely could've gotten much more out of the class.

Prof. Wasick is amazing! Her lessons were always entertaining and easy to follow. She's very relaxed and understanding. Super easy A. Make sure you consistently do mind tap & review textbook in preparation for quizzes. Overall, a great class and a great professor. Completely stress free.

I'm dumbfounded that her rating isn't a 5. She is probably my favorite professor this semester. She is hilarious, super patient, and kind to everyone. Some people had trouble speaking Spanish in front of the class, but she was never condescending and instead helped everyone improve. Stay on top of her work, participate, and this will be an easy A.

Very good professor. The Spanish course is quite decelerated, so if you want to learn Spanish, you have to go the extra mile and learn it yourself. The course covers pretty much everything you need to know in Spanish (tenses, scenarios, etc.)

I love Professor Wasick! She tried to make every single class exciting and encouraged participation. Lots of homework, but it is all pretty easy to complete. She gives great feedback on written assignments and didn't give a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Wasick is a very kind and funny teacher. Definitely one of my favorite classes this semester. Some busy work with homework, but she grades on completion. Not all of her classes have tests, but if you study some they are fine. Definitely participate in class too but it's very easy to talk. She does not grade harshly. Easy A and fun class!

Prof Wasick is a hilarious teacher and keeps the classes engaging and fresh. There is a lot busy work to complete throughout the week and sometimes the assignments can be easily forgotten about. If you keep up with the tedious work you should be good. She is a little hard to reach outside of class and doesn't respond to emails but that's it.

SPAN 1101 was my favorite class this semester! There were lots of small assignments/projects throughout, along with daily textbook activities, but nothing was too time-consuming or difficult. When students would make mistakes in class, Wasick was kind and patient. She really cares helping students learn.

I have taken like four classes with her now and I love her classes. They're all really interesting but she is a very easy grader so I feel like I actually learned. Cancels class for religious holidays which is also nice.

Pretty unorganized semester. Some topics were interesting but couldve learned on my own, class time was not always well thought-out. Didnt receive feedback or grades on our midterm until the final was assigned. But an easy A I guess?
Cancelled class often. Participation in discussion was a big thing, but it wasn't a grade killer if you didn't do the reading or otherwise couldn't for a day

Prof. Wasick's class was super chill. Definitely take if you're looking for an easy A and not looking for a ton of work, but if you put some time into the readings, you'll still learn interesting things on translations. You rarely get feedback on assignments and most assignments are reflections and some translations.

Profesora Wasick is really nice. I've taken two classes with her, and both were very easy As. Tests are take home and open note, and she is flexible if you need to miss class. She is the easiest professor I've ever had. You don't learn as much, but she is very knowledgeable about phonetics.

Prof. Wasick is super nice, but she's pretty inaccessible and takes a while to answer emails. We only met live on Zoom once a week, which meant that no one really learned anything. Not a lot of homework and easy enough to get a good grade, just felt like a waste of time. YOU NEED THE TEXTBOOK to complete the exams and homework.

Señora Wasick is so nice! Her internet connection was not the best, but she was very helpful and understanding over email. The class relied mainly on the textbook reading, which included homework from each section (graded for participation).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A but you only learn about linguistics if you read the textbook. Because it was an online class and her internet was bad, she typed most of what we needed to know in the Zoom chat. We also only met once a week rather than 3 times a week like the syllabus indicated (and sometimes not even once a week). She's nice though.

Not an interesting class but not hard either. Occasional worksheets for homework but it's never actually checked in class, so you're really only graded by 2-3 tests. Wasick is nice, cancels class a lot, and is easy going in class. Pretty easy to get an A as long as you study a little before the test and pay a bit of attention in class.

Professor Wasick is super sweet and really helps you learn to appreciate all that translation and interpretation have to offer! She offers tons of extra credit opportunities, but you probably won't need many since the class and its assignments are very easy and straightforward. You'll learn a lot and have fun doing so, too! No textbook needed, ever

If you want an A, take her class. If you want to learn anything, don't. Rarely grades assignments, so don't expect feedback. Cancels class often. Speaks (almost explicitly) in English. Has a hard time explaining concepts in Spanish.

She knows her stuff about phonology, but it was a little difficult to take her seriously discussing the topic given how poor her own accent is. If you go to class and skim the textbook, the tests should be a breeze. She ended up giving us a participation grade on the oral assignments so I'm not sure how tough she is on them, but probably not very.

If I'd known what phonology was before I signed up for this class, I wouldn't have taken it.  Prof. Wasick knows her stuff mostly, but I found her American accent problematic when trying to understand the different pronunciations in class.  There are many better electives in the Span. dept., and if you want to take phonology, maybe try someone else

Easiest, least substantive class I've taken since middle school PE. Lectures were an absurd waste of time but attendance is mandatory. The professor had nothing meaningful to say about the topic and conducted most classes in English.  No tests, but we never got any graded work back, so grades at the end of the semester were a complete surprise.

Professor Wasick is very kind and helpful. Ample opportunities for extra credit, and the class gets easier over time. Somewhat unclear - the syllabus changed multiple times. But, she clearly knows her stuff and I felt I learned a lot about a field (linguistics) that I was completely unfamiliar with before. Would recommend, but don't think it's easy

Interesting class on translation. Didn't get to interpretation as much, but lots of extra credit opportunities and her as a hilarious professor who really knows her stuff make this a great linguistics course to take!

A teacher who drills it into you-- I barely had to study for the final because we had been taught the material so well. She's not good about handing work back. If you put in the effort and go to class and absorb the information, you can get an A-

probably one of the easisest Spanish classes you can take. Profesora Wasick is very helpful and goes over everything in class with PowerPoints. As long as you look over the powerpoints and do the test reviews you will be fine!

Professor Wasick is a quality Spanish professor because she has clear demands, is very adept in the Spanish language and knows her stuff. I would not recommend challenging her knowledge of the subject matter or her if you have hispanic background (or not) because she will use it against you when grading your ish!

If you do the reading and pay attention in lectures, this class is not too difficult.  Be sure to participate.  Heads up - the book is in English, but lectures, tests, etc., are in Spanish, so be sure to note the Spanish terms for things.  Don't miss class!

I really enjoyed this class. Wasick knows pretty much everything about Spanish culture and history and she makes learning about it fun. There are daily "temarios" and 1-page papers twice a week but they help a lot in reinforcing the reading. I personally think she's really funny and she's also understanding and helpful. Just get on her good side!

I really like Wasick. There's a ton of work and it's really important to keep up with it daily. But she really knows her stuff and her grading is fair... she isn't an easy "a" but she's do-able. I had no interest in Spanish for Business before this semester but I have learned a lot and the material is very useful. I would recommend her for sure.

Wasick is an odd one.  If you work hard, she will give you the grade you deserve--but it is harder to get an A in her class than many others at Vandy.  Honestly, the key to being liked by Wasick is to go into her office hours and to participate during class.  I'd recommend that people take her classes but be prepared to work for your grade.
her tests are ridiculously hard, and i've heard the same for other courses she teaches. If AT ALL possible, DO NOT TAKE HER CLASSES.

this woman is the worst professor I have had at Vanderbilt.  She is lazy and takes forever to hand back exams and papers, yet expects the students to keep up with an unreasonable amount of work.  She is bitter and unpleasant and obviously doesnot enjoy working with young people.  She seems unhappy in general and seems to take it out on the students

Why anyone still takes classes with this woman is beyond me. She's confused, she's confusing, and she shouldn't be teaching. 1) Doesn't stick to the syllabus 2) Assigns homework LESS THAN 12 HOURS BEFORE CLASS 3) Hands out pop quizzes when she still has 3 of your papers and 2 of your tests to grade.

What an AMAZING professor! She is so entertaining- it's almost impossible to be bored in class. She is relaxed on late work, and will answer any question you have. Drawback: the tests encompass a lot of material- make sure you study vocab as you go through the chapters, NOT the night before. But I'd definitely recommend any class with Wasick!

Picks favorites, is outright rude in class sometimes to those she doesn't absolutely adore. Horribly inconsistent grader on papers and projects. Takes about a lifetime to ever hand papers/tests back to you.

Wasick is awful. No one will deny that she picks favorites.  She also takes it personally if you are EVER late to class or absent - and don't think that verification will help you out.  Unless you are on the lady's good side, you are in trouble.  I discussed her with many peers and they admitted she definitely favored them.  BEWARE!
Great teacher, very engaging.  Makes class interesting and if you are willing to do the work you will get a good grade.

Really liked her-- very engaging and helpful all the time.  I agree-- she's the only teacher that I've had that can make 8:00's fun!  I hear she's better in lower-level classes, so take her for those and cash in.
Much better than the Span 206. My only gripe is the slow turn around time for her to hand back graded assignments.

really like her. relaxed class atmosphere, she keeps things funny and straightforward. we work mainly out of class pak and just correct hw exercises. 2 tests, 2 short papers, all easy but got handed back months later. v. accesible by email and always willing to help

she's awesome. she is so helpful and always there to answer questions in e-mail. she's always willing to help in office hours or after class. this class wasn't too hard, but requires a lot of work. she makes it so you can do well if you work hard. she's fair and funny in class.
She is the only teacher I've ever had that successfully made class fun every day at 8:00 in the morning. Great sense of humor and ability to relate with students.

She is very judgemental, chooses her favorites, and grades unfairly - especially with attendance (even if you participate tons and turn in great work). She takes forever to get back assignments, and piles on the work; she also has difficult tests.

There are daily assignments, If you do work your work everyday there is no reason why you shouldn't get an A or B. She goes out of her way to omit sections from tests that are not fair or sections that most students do no do well on.

Everyone in my class didn't like it. It's like a high school class.  Do the daily work, read, write out excercises, talk and succeed.  You need to get to know her.  A lot of work though, don't take if can't commit to be prepared daily.

Easily the worst Spanish class I've had here and probably the worst class overall. She didn't really teach anything, we always did exercises from the book in small groups and she takes forever to return assignments.

Dan is very approachable and a great professor and mentor. That said, be prepared to follow up on grades and assignments, as many things change from the syllabus throughout the semester, so attendance is important to keep up with any important announcements and changes.
He is amazing!!!!!!

While you have to parse through some (very interesting and fun) sideplot storylines during lectures, if you take good notes and ask questions, the class will go just fine for you. He genuinely cares about his students and is just overall a fun professor.

Dan is super knowledgeable about glaciology and is at the forefront of the field. His lectures were so engaging and the field trip was incredible. He truly cares about and gets to know all of his students and is one of the most down to earth and chill professors. I would take any class Dan teaches and any EES major should take one with him.

Dan Morgan is an extremely unprofessional and disorganized professor. Grading is unclear and he never posted the last few labs or final, and he has clear favorites and makes no effort to hide it. His exams were impossible and nobody could complete them alone. He has no respect for time and class always ran over. I don't know 1 person who got an A.

Structural geology is a difficult class. Dan gives a lot of examples but does not do the best job at explaining some of the concepts. I heavily relied on the book for the tests, but it could not help with the more abstract questions. I was confused for most of the semester, yet ended up with a good grade, so if you put the work in, it works out.
Awful class, boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really charismatic guy (who I've befriended) who is just really disorganized. Be ready to be confused about grading criteria until the day before submission, before he explains himself and extends the due date
Tests are much more difficult than needed. Some topics are made more complex than they actually are.
WASN'T VERY UNDERSTANDING OF PERSONAL CIRCUMSTANCES AFFECTING MY GRADES
Dr. Morgan is a very well-known, involved figure on campus. I had a freshman seminar with him that was super interesting (field trips, discussions, little HW). Any class with him is a solid choice.

Professor Morgan is so passionate about the subject. He made me excited to go to class and it was a lot of discussion which was pretty easy to get involved in! You can have a lot of fun in class if you choose to. Tough homework, but he let us work together.
Loved my commons iseminar! It wasn't much homework, was an easy A, and we got to see cool things all over campus. He even took us into the tunnels below Vanderbilt. If you can, take this isemminar!

Professor Morgan is very nice and funny but a bit scatterbrained. This class was a pretty easy A if you gave any effort at all. Textbook and lectures are unnecessary, questions are from old tests he posts online. Lots of busy work, felt kind of like a high school class. Taking the lab helps you understand the material better. Takes attendance.

Professor Morgan is a great guy who truly wants to get to know his students. He recognizes and knows by name every student in a large lecture class, so you are never anonymous. Tests are literally 80% recycled questions from online old tests and 20% new questions, but he does not post answer keys to old tests. Best way to study is to do old tests.

Professor Morgan is funny and nice, but a bit scatter brained at times. The material is almost all memorization, so it's not a great class to take if you're more inclined to problem-solving types of science. Study his old tests rather than the material itself to get good grades on the midterms. (I figured this out too late.)

Overall not a bad class, but I felt Professor Morgan didn't really cover too much of what was on the tests in class. You have to read the textbook to get the full picture.  Participation is collected randomly (most days) so go to class.  Easy homework assignments and reading quizzes every week. Some tests were much harder than the material was.

One of the best classes I have taken at Vandy. Dr. Morgan is probably the most caring professor I have had over the past two years, he will do anything for his students. Great class, great professor, not hard to do well. Take it if you can!

Dan Morgan is an amazing guy.  He's so nice and passionate about what he teaches.  I took this class to meet my science requirement and I would definitely recommend you take it. He makes his lectures fun and makes the material relevant.  He posts his lectures and past tests online, so as long as you study you should do well in the class.

Took him for the Antarctica commons seminar. Great class, learned a lot. Entire grade is on one Antarctic presentation and a 3-page paper which is pretty straight forward and easy. Class had a field trip and was capped off with dinner at the professor's house. Best commons seminar out there
Dan is a rock star.

I came into this class with absolutely no interest in Geology, but was pleasantly surprised by Prof. Morgan. He is always enthusiastic about the course material, understands that many are just there to fulfill a requirement, and makes every effort to make the class lively and enjoyablce. Very helpful, very knowledgable.

Professor Morgan is fantastic! Great lectures and very helpful. He does take attendance through participation turned in after each class, but you can miss three so it's not a huge deal. The tests are no big deal: mostly questions from old exams posted online. The lab component is time consuming and more difficult, but definitely manageable.

Professor Morgan "rocks"! He lectures well and makes the material interesting. Go to office hours: he'll help you with homework assignments, provides extra credit, and is a great conversationalist. Prepare for the tests by practicing old exams online--make sure to check your answers with him or the TA's! No answer keys online for practice exams.

Great teacher. He is super nice, interesting, and helpful. Lecture isn't too boring. If you go to office hours he gives you the homework answers. Tests are mostly questions from old tests (which are posted online), homework questions, and only a few new questions. Can easily get an A if you put in the work and go to class

class topics are generally easy. very easy with a background in a class like environmental science, etc. take notes on your computer b/c he posts all his powerpoint presentations. that alone will get you an acceptable grade without reading the textbook. reading the textbook on top of this will get you an A. attendance mandatory- he takes attendance
Absolutely the man. Crystal clear lectures, incredibly helpful, interesting, and the tests are just like the sample tests. Don't take anyone else for 101

I'll get it out of the way: the class is hard as hell. And you may sometimes take exception to his strict grading, but Dan is one of the most helpful, not to mention knowledgeable, professors you'll ever have. Rarely will you go to his office and not find him, ready to spend as long as you need to figure something out.

Here's the scoop...before I took this class I thought Professor Morgan was terrific. However, his level of compassion from EES 101 and EES 240 is night and day! I still think he is great and is always willing to help.  However, you may have some animosity towards him the night before labs are due...but you'll do it and get through it. He's a GREAT!
What a dreamboat!

Professor Morgan is very knowledgeable and is readily available during office hours.  I learned a lot in the class, however, its not a complete breeze.  It's important to grasp the concepts and if you want to do really well I suggest reading the textbook, though many students just review the slides (which you must fill in yourself during class).

Thermodynamics is hard, but Professor Li made it accessible! He expects a lot from his students and can be a bit of a strict grader, but he cares to explain topics in depth and it's clear he is very knowledgable about this topic. If given the choice between him and Pitz, definitely take Li.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and good teacher once you get past the accent. With that said, lecture notes are not posted online which makes studying/missing class difficult. Tests are pretty tough but graded leniently. Study more than you think.

The MEMS/NEMS class is probably more targeted to graduate students, who made up the large majority of the class. The lectures were relatively dry, theory/research-based, and they went over my head a lot. I would only recommend this course to undergrads who are truly interested in the field. He did grade very generously to at least undergrads.

Between Pitz, Li, and Dr. Y., Deyu is firmly the second best thermo professor. Exams are very similar to practice exams. Lectures are dry and consist mainly of deriving equations with a few practice problems sprinkled in. Some people found his accent hard to understand but I had no issues. Homework sneaks up on you and can be tricky.

In attempting to make this review I actually had to go back to the syllabus because I could not remember the professors name. Now don't let this drag you down because I'd still say to take this guy. Class is lecture heavy and top tier boring but he gives very fair tests, does practice problems and does give you what you need to know.

Thermo isn't a fun class, but Professor Li doesn't make it worse. Lectures are pretty dull and content heavy, but he gives you all the relevant information and equations for the tests. 85% of your grade is the midterms and finals, but he holds an exam review session where he covers an old exam the lecture before the test. Lenient grading scale too!

Class is pretty chill, lectures can get monotonous and are sometimes hard to understand, 1-2 homework's per week which are all online + gives out practice tests that are nearly identical to the real exam. Stopped going to class half way through the semester.

He gives you practice exams that are nearly identical to the actual tests, and he is very explicit in the things you need to know. He gives out on average one homework assignment per week that is around 2-4 questions and does not take much longer than 45 minutes to do. English isn't great but also isn't hard to understand, just copy the board.

tries to make jokes during class but fails because everyone was asleep, hard to understand sometimes but writes everything on the board, homework can take awhile even though its only a few problems, worth it to go to class at 8 am because he curves a lot and if you only miss a few classes you can get 2 points added to your overall grade

It's worth waking up at 8:00 to take this class, he is SOO much easier than the other Thermo prof.  He speaks in very broken english so the lectures are boring but understandable.  Homework is due once a week, its hard but not impossible. Get a solutions manual and you'll be fine.  He grades fair on tests and is helpful out of class.

Very sweet professor and is very passionate about the content. This half is way less dense than the first half but is somehow made more difficult. Lectures are just reading off of slides and they are often out of order. Content was easy to understand but exams did not reflect that; tested on things we were told not to know
If the martians had the death beam pointed at earth, I'd rather have Iguodala take the game-winning shot than her lecture any more future doctors.
True or False: The first early humans appeared 6 to 7 million years ago.

She is so bad. She cannot teach for her life and reads directly off a script. Because the content is so easy she makes the most ridiculous exam questions, expecting you to know the smallest details or even an example she gave that's not even on the exam slides. She is NOT a biology teacher. Somebody send her back to earth sciences.

Her section of the course has the easiest content ever. But she somehow manages to make the tests harder than the first half, because her questions are so poorly worded and hard to understand what she's asking. And she completely neglects to teach what she actually asks on exams, and instead spends class time on pointless demonstrations.

DeSantis was a good prof, but honestly I found her section more tedious. The content was definitely easier, but it was harder to go to class because I was not interested in the content. She's a nice person and I don't get all the reviews comparing her to Satan 😭

She's a decent lecturer, easy exams, nice person

DeSantis has improved a lot. She is super kind and cares about her students. The content is way easier than Hillyer's section, and even though she can go off topic, she manages to get her point across. Exams are easier, some practice questions were copied directly from the practice exams. Hillyer/DeSantis over Johnson/Rokas any day of the week.

Desantis is a nice person but not a great lecturer. She reads straight off a script, and the slides aren't informative + give distracting info. She said not to memorize dates, but tested them on the final. Her wording on exams is vague. That said, her exams are MUCH easier than Hillyer's w/ far less content. She's worse but still take this section.

While the material may be easier and the averages higher, I found her questions to be overly ambiguous. She is without a doubt the weaker professor of the hillyer/desantis pair. Her lectures are boring and not informative of what content she expects you to know. Study hard for hillyer so you only have to take 1 of her exams
Incredible professor. Amazing lectures. Very fair exams. I feel like I learned a lot. Much better than Rokas from what I've heard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Desantis gives really easy exams. If you got to lectures and do the practice problems, you will be totally fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet and passionate. Slides are sometimes just photos but recorded and pretty easy. She goes at good pace, exams match practice. Homework is light. Her section is much easier than Hillyer.

WAY EASIER COMPARED TO HILLYER. There is absolutely no reason not to get a 90+ on her exams if you put in the effort. The FRQs are literally THE SAME as the ones she puts in the practice exams. The people who don't do well in her half simply just lack effort.
Literally the best

I don't understand where some of these reviews are coming from. Her lectures are straightforward and while she does move a bit fast, she records and posts all her lectures. Her exams are very similar to the practice exams she gives us and office hours are very helpful. Compared to Hillyer, the information was verryyy light.

She is so sweet and caring. She is an angel. Exams are straightforward and not confusing at all! She loves to use hilarious mnemonics and interesting demonstrations and videos rather than speak herself. She is definitely the most responsible professor at vanderbilt!

Lectures are not helpful because she reads off script. The slides contain a lot of pictures with few words, making it hard to review before exams. She often uses complex terminology (such as scientific names of animals) without writing them down. Content is easy, but she makes the exams hard because the wording is extremely confusing!!!
Such is life.
Exams are easy, and lectures are good.
Very nice professor. The most caring person ever. Amazing lecturer, and she records them. Truly a gem of the bio department.
Awesome. Don't listen to old reviews. She has improved a lot
Very sweet. Cares about students, and helps in many ways. Definitely the strongest option for the course.
Very good. Both DeSantis and Hillyer are stronger than their Rokas Johnson counterparts.
Idk where the bad reviews come from. She is a great lecturer, absolutely prepares you for the test, and gives straight forward exams.
I wish she was an unnamed geochronologist at the start of Jurassic Park who gets immediately stomped on by Indominus Rex so I wouldn't have to take this terrible class of hers.

Every day I sit in lecture, I feel like this class is fine, but when the exams come around and she doesn't care to answer your questions during the exam and gives out very unreasonable questions, you start to rethink!!!
If I was a fossil and Desantis came to study me, I would be glad that I'm a fossil and don't have eyes.

Despite the content and workload being manageable, my main issue was DeSantis's lecture style. Often it felt like we strayed from the main focus of the content that was necessary for any assignments and tests, and, even with recorded lectures, then it felt difficult to focus back in on the primary information.

Lectures were boring but the content was a fraction of Hillyer's. Very stingy with the regrades though- once submitted a regrade for a question, got the point back, then lost another so my grade was the same. Overall she's not terrible but also not the best.

The content of Dr. DeSantis' section was much easier compared to Hillyer's section. She made the lectures engaging through fun demonstrations that I enjoyed. That being said, she is not a very good lecturer, as she reads off a script that is copied directly from the textbook. Exams had many typos, but were doable and similar to in class questions.

she is a very good lecturer. i feel like some of these reviews about her slides are unfair as her lectures are all recorded & posted online. yes, some slides are just images but just watch the lecture vid. however, be warned that her practice exams look nothing like the actual exams in class. the wording of some questions can cause confusion

DeSantis fails to be coherent during much of her lectures. Lots of time is wasted to demonstrations that could be conveyed in a clearer manner. Questions on exams tend to be poor and very vague. She has a negative attitude and seems to want to penalize students rather than help them on regrade requests. I recommend Johnson and Rokas.

She is a very nice woman. She actively tries to engage and know her students, which is nice. She is absolutely terrible at writing tests. She said she'd be consistent and close to Hillyer, but that was a straight LIE. They are way too vague sometimes and her slides are literally just images sometimes, which isn't helpful when trying to review.

Very unorganized class. Her lectures don't help with understanding the material, and her slides are insufficient if you want to self learn. Exam questions are confusing with vague wording and unfair grading criteria. Mastering questions do not resemble test questions at all and are a waste of time.

DeSantis is definitely the weaker when compared to Hillyer. DeSantis is super boring in class, her slides are bland but have the info you need for the exams. She was worse from last semester but not nearly as bad as the ones she got during Covid. This is still the better section for 1511. Median of exam scores: 76,86,86,82.
IGNORE 2023 Ratings!!! DeSantis's clone was teaching the class that year!!! She is back!! RUN!!!!!

DeSantis's half is terrible. At the start of the final class of the year, she threatened to go through the exam of anyone who submitted a regrade request and find places that should not have received credit and take off points. I don't know if this was just a bluff but what a way to say you're lazy and don't want to deal with any regrades......

The content is braindead easy. She is unfair. The test questions sucked, and she was nothing but defensive when asked to reconsider her incorrect keys. If you're a good mind reader, take her class; you'll do fine.

I liked Hillyer's half more. I also think its a little strange that she has policies such as not being willing to talk about exam questions over email- you have to schedule a meeting. If I just have a quick question to clarify why this test answer is correct I shouldn't need to go all the way to your office for a 1.5 minute meeting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Last semester DeSantis did switch up and make the class very easy... BUT this semester she definitely went somewhat back to old ways because this class WASN'T super easy like people last year claimed it to be but she also is definitely BETTER than she was >2 years ago. The exams are fair, and the slides are good. She tries to be funny but isn't.

Dr. Desantis is a great professor, the bad reviews from before must be outtdated. Her slides present all of the information understandably, she includes engaging demonstrations and interesting outside videos in the lectures to make real-world connections, and her exams are very reasonable. The Hillyer/Desantis 1511 section is definitely ideal.

She literally changed everything this semester around. Much better than what we anticipated from the reviews, take this section over johnson/rokas you won't regret. Exam median on one of her exams was a 90 so you know that it is easy. She was amazing and nothing like what the earlier reviews said.

She really changed her teaching this semester. Her lectures were always entertaining, a clear reflection of what's on exams and she made an effort to get to know everybody's names (very caring) We had Mastering which was very helpful for exam practice questions and counted as grade (buffer for tests) unlike the other section that wasn't offered it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best teacher I have ever taken!

Professor DeSantis is one of the most unreceptive teachers I have ever met. She does not respond to student emails and takes no feedback. Her tests were online and not necessarily difficult, but they were the types of questions where should would nit pick. I loved Professor Hillyer's half of the class but hers was terrible. AVOID HER at all costs.

Dr. DeSantis' lecture content is sparse and boring. Her exams are all online and are easy, but time management is a big issue and the test content is at times quite confusing. If you are blindsided by even one of her exams you can kiss your A goodbye. She is a nice person but she has no business teaching biology. Avoid her class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: nice person, horrible professor. did not give clear feedback. exam questions were written poorly. got confused by her own questions. online exams only, not on paper even though there was a lot of math involved. took off points on regrades without adequate explanation. material itself was easy, but her test questions made it unnecessarily difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Desantis is one of the most disorganized & lazy professors I have taken at Vandy. She sets her students up to fail and ignores feedback. She has no concept of how to create appropriate tests & did not take accountability for the mess-ups that she made, resulting in our grades being negatively affected. Do NOT take her if you hope to succeed in Bio.

Has the most ridiculous/unfair grading rubrics for FRQs that do not fairly assess knowledge or award partial credit. Never answered emails even though I later learned she read them. Gave math-heavy exams online and didn't care that everyone hated it, no practice exams that matched actual test format, unclear questions. Worst professor I've had here

Avoid taking biology with her at ALL COSTS. She is the reason why I am dropping pre-med. She talks through the exams, so it's impossible to concentrate. Makes the exams on brightspace because she thinks COVID can pass through paper... (she doesn't even teach with a mask on, so she doesn't care about COVID). Doesn't give any practice problems.

She is inaccessible and an unclear grader. She is unreceptive to students' ideas and defensive when her methods don't work. Her exams are nothing like what is covered in class, and she does not provide sufficient review materials. I loved Hillyer's half but sadly do not recommend you take him if it means you have to take Desantis. Avoid.

She's very passionate about what she teaches, and the material wasn't the hardest thing I've ever learned... but the lectures were just generally unorganized and the test questions didn't really make sense a lot of the time. She was super nice, but I just would have liked a straightforward lecture and cut-and-dry questions for gen bio
Professor DeSantis is definitely your best bet for BSCI 1511. She's super nice and clearly loves what she does. Tests are straight forward and everything is from the powerpoints.

DeSantis is truly the most incoherent professor I've ever had here. I was going to be a bio major, then I took her class and realized that this was something I never want to do again. Grades tests unfairly, isn't accessible, writes incoherent questions. DO NOT take. She actually writes test questions like a fourth grader.

At my time at Vandy, Desantis might be the worst prof I have ever taken. She is ill-prepared, makes us do activities that do not make sense for the class, and makes exams that do not properly test what we learn and the questions are incoherent. I do not recommend her for any class, especially BSCI 1511.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Got me interested in fossils!
Not easy but fair. Excellent lectures and makes u think.
Excellent professor!  Made me want to major in EES!
Very interesting, liked the outreach project.
She expects you to be prepared for class which forced me to learn a lot.  I really enjoyed outreach event.

She has high standards for students but I do not think it was unreasonable.  There were a few too many weekend field trips that conflicted with school activities, but many students did not go on these and there were not issues.  Interesting class, could have a better format.
She has the most unreasonable teaching methods and pc af. Probably cuz she just started teaching this class or smth
Lots of work in both lab and lecture. In total, there are 4 exams and 3 lab practicals, which is much more than most other bio classes have. Also assignments and presentations here and there.

You definitely have to study a good amount for the last 3 quizzes to do well. Tophat for our class ended up being extra credit points so you don't really need to attend lectures-just use the textbook to study. If you study and do the homeworks you will get an A.

If you have previously taken bio or pay attention in class, this is a very straightforward course. Homeworks are over half the grade, and are usually quick, so make sure to do all of those. All quizzes and the final are multiple choice. There are some TopHat attendance checks in class, but for the most part, lectures are skipable.
She is a very nice person, I just don't think Baby Bio was as easy as people made it out to be. You really had to try for a good grade and everybody I knew in the class that wasn't premed struggled.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are brutal. Not enough to follow slides, have to listen to every word. Difficult as she rambles and the material is very uninteresting. Bad class if you don't like science or haven't taken a bio class for years. Quiz questions are application based and purposely tricky. Avg 80-85 with a 20 point curve, and she removes curve for the final.

Not sure what the complaints are abt difficulty. A lot of topics are just general knowledge. Hw is 50% and participation based. Quizzes are curved by ~20% and all mc. Due is an alright lecturer. Tends to ramble a bit and doesn't break up the time well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is indeed not baby bio, realized it too late in the sem. The first quiz was easy, the second and third were horrible. For an AXLE, you need to have basic knowledge of chem and bio, not worth the time. This is harder than my other major-related class. Good luck taking this. (On another note, she is actually caring but good luck)

I took this class thinking it would be “baby bio,” but it was far from it. The quizzes are frequent and detailed, and the exams make up most of your grade. The material is complex and overwhelming for non-science majors. If you just need a science credit, take something else—this class is not fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Took last sem. She seems very very nice but is just not that great of a teacher. The tests are hard when the material isn't actually that challenging. You aren't doomed since the class average is curved to a B but is a very stark contrast to hillyer
Dr. Due is a very caring and an amazing professor, but it is really hard to stay focused on her lectures.

She was all over the place. She would go on long tangents, and I often lost the point of the entire class. Got so much work done for other classes in these lectures though! I would say the class is fairly easy, but I had good biology classes in high school, so that helped. She is a super sweet person though! If you're a type A, however, avoid her.
Dr. D is amazing and this class was honestly not bad at all, mostly based on completion of homework assignments. She really cares about her students and is very understanding.

I took three classes with Dr. D this semester and I do not understand her low rating. She is AMAZING. She is so willing to give extra credit when the class isn't doing well (she gave us an assignment that could REPLACE an exam grade) and is a good lecturer. She is also a great human being, an actual angel. She has helped me regain my love for bio!

She is an extremely caring person. However, her classes were tedious consisting of 1 hour 15 minute lectures. I had to learn all of the material on my own time, and the tests often included material we didn't even discuss in class. This is NOT "baby bio." I had to work extremely hard to succeed in this class and the labs were painful.

Dr. D's tests can be difficult and specific but as long as you apply yourself, you should be fine. Lectures can sometimes drag, causing you to have to teach yourself some topics (not ideal). However, she offers extra credit at the end of the semester which boosts your grade a ton. Contrary to popular belief, Dr. D. does want you to succeed!!

The class is terribly structured. Material is basically random and there's too much info. Dr D just puts whatever she wants on the quizzes and the material is obscure and oddly specific. She's made the class really bad because her assessments are uncoordinated and difficult to study for because there is no structure. For AXLE, take another class.

Dr. D clearly cares about her students and does everything she can. She holds review sessions before quizzes and literally sends out a document telling you what will be on the quiz. As long as you actually apply yourself this class is very doable.

Lectures covered core material well, and following assignments reinforced those points. Homework was 35% of the grade but has very forgiving policies. Guest lectures were scheduled to break up course content and tied it together in an impactful way. Quizzes are the other bulk (40%) but are not that difficult (memorization) + you get a drop.

For an intro non-major course, the content was very difficult and overly specific. Dr. D is a very sweet person but not a very great professor imo. When asked a question, she either doesn't know the answer or explains for 10 mins. You have to study A LOT for the quizzes but even then they were too difficult. Would not recommend the class.

Professor Due cares about her students doing well, but the class is very lecture based. The lectures are just very boring. The quizzes are also really hard. Professor Due will say something will not be on the quiz, and then there will be three questions about that topic on the quiz. She is very sweet, but the class is harder than it needs to be.

Dr. D is incredibly kind and really does care about her students and the content. However, the class is far more difficult than it should be for a non-major intro bio class. I wouldn't take this class to fulfill a core requirement. There's a good amount of reading and work, lectures are hard to follow, and the quizzes are hyper-specific.

If you're taking this class in the fall just know IT'S NOT BABY BIO. Sadly learned that too late. You can definitely finesse a good grade on the quizzes, and the homework are not tough, but the final is what got me because I didn't learn a thing in class. You don't have to go to lecture but there are a few in-class participation grades you'll need.

Dr. D is knowledgeable and very caring, but did not do a good job teaching the course in an online format. Modules were often posted very last-minute, forcing you to scramble to cram in the info before tests. Course materials were all over the place in brightspace and the lectures didn't have much structure, which made them feel pretty pointless.

Dr. D is very sweet but disorganized in an online setting. The TA Mason often had a better ability to teach in lecture than she did. Homeworks were long, and lectures unhelpful, so I had to teach myself most of the material. The TAs also graded the short answers on the tests harshly. This class was an easy enough A but also bored me to death

Professor Due-Goodwin is great! She cares about students and knows a lot about her topic. I didn't do well because I didn't care but it is do-able for non science people to do well in this class. Just be ready for multiple choice exams and reading the textbook.
Do not take this class in the online format. There is no correlation between the homework and what is on the test. Completely unorganized to the detriment of learning.

Definitely would not recommend taking this class, especially in the online format. Leaning "modules" are extremely disorganized and lengthy, and you have to do lots of piecing together between long videos, readings, and rare lectures to feel like you are getting any type of understanding. Modules are assigned days after scheduled.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I believe DDG took critiques of her online class to heart and really responded to student concerns. She changed up the format and reached out to students often to see if it was working, even went so far as to adapt to more note access during exams. Wish there were more lectures for clarity. Lab was interesting and fun for non-science majors
The assignments/homework do not correlate to what is on the exam. The online course is disorganized to the detriment of learning.
This class was so unorganized. The format is constantly changing which is extremely unhelpful in terms of preparation for the exams, which do not reflect the homework at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is one of the most disorganized classes I have ever taken. Content is often not posted until days later and deadlines are constantly being shifted. The homework content does not match at all what is on the exams, which are way too long in length for the time allowed on the exam. One of the worst classes I have taken.
The homework readings are super long and not helpful at all. Exams are hard. Professor doesn't teach on Zoom.

Avoid. The class is super disorganized given the online format. Frequent exams but only lectures once every two weeks or so. Homework is tedious and not helpful for exam preparations. Unclear on what is expected of us.

DDG is the best. Her lectures can be boring but she's kind and helpful, especially if you go to office hours. I hate science courses usually but the guest lectures for this class were fascinating (jet lag, living with HIV, etc.) The lab component is not fun, but manageable. As long as you study a little bit for the exams you can get an A!

DDG is the cutest human. She cares very much about answering questions her students have that may be beyond what she's lecturing on that day. The lab component of class can be challenging somedays, but others you will get out early. 3 exams and a final+ online textbook questions semi-regularly make up your grade. Relatively slow grader.

Love DDG. Took this class for fun, and I really ended up enjoying it. She can run long in lecture sometimes, but usually the material is pretty interesting. She is very caring, and she is so invested in the class and our learning. Grades are distributed among tests and other assignments, and her tests aren't too bad if you study the slides well

Dr. Due Goodwin is super sweet and caring. Kind of a southern mama type. Lectures were over more boring content, but I thought her section was a lot easier. Just like any other bio class, study and memorize. She's not too bad (:
Really boring lecture. The test are really random and specific. Book doesn't help. Just read powerpoints

I learned so much more in Zoology compared to other bsci courses I have taken so far. Study early for the tests, it's easy to get behind. Tests are very straightforward, but easy to not go into enough detail for the short answers. She offers extra credit on each test. She usually spends a lot of time talking before lecturing, but is super nice.

Dr. Due-Goodwin really cares about her students! She makes herself available if you can't come to office hours. Her part of the course requires textbook reading. Her exams are not as challenging as some of the other Biology professors in my opinion. She's a great choice for Bsci 1511!

I loved Dr. D! She is a really cool professor, and Zoology is a really neat class. It was an 8Am on T/R, but I genuinely liked going. She is always willing to talk to you more about the material or your own interests too. I really enjoyed the lab portion too, very interesting. Tests can be extensive, but she gives you advice on how to study.

I did not enjoy DDG's lectures. They seemed to focus on minutiae and were not exciting in content or presentation. Much of the important material was also left for self-study without being covered. However, she was very accessible and was caring and genial. Tests are hit or miss: not impossible but annoying. Would recommend the other 1511 section.

I found the lab component and tests to be especially in-depth and challenging, though this class was designed for non-majors like me. Dr. D is very nice, gives good lectures, and brings in several awesome guest speakers. Lecture slides and study guides are posted online. Not an easy A, but a fine choice to satisfy the lab requirement.

Class is really boring, but you only have to show up on days when there is a guest lecturer. She posts the slides for all of her lectures online along with her notes for information to discuss. Tests aren't terrible, but require some studying.

The lectures were very boring and on a superficial level, her voice was super grating, making them hard to listen to. The tests are difficult, but fairly straight forward as long as you keep up with the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lecture and Lab are one class for Zoology, so study hard for the lab practicals. Her Powerpoints have all of the information you need for the tests, though, so just study those. she's a really engaging professor; I found myself wanting to actually go to my 8AM class. Lab might actually be harder than lecture, though, but it's always interesting.

Definitely take for AXLE lab req. Sweet professor who wants you to succeed. Excellent communicator, always keeps students in the loop. Tests aren't that difficult, co-req labs are a joke. Sizeable portion of your grade is basically completion. Only need to go to class for four pop quizzes and the timing of them is somewhat predictable. Easy A.

Her Ecology Lab feels like another class compared to Ecology, because they don't really corroborate at all. Still, she's a really nice person who doesn't make you do a whole lot outside of class. The projects are really interesting, and I love her as a person. Still, she really loves to talk, a lot more than needed for lab, but it's worth it.
Professor Due-Goodwin is a wonderful lecturer and makes a true effort to get to know each student. Despite requiring lots of memorization, Zoology ended up being my favorite class at Vandy.
Such a sweet lady. She makes labs fairly interesting, just pray you get a good TA because thats who you mainly see/deal with.
An excellent lab instructor. She is obviously well-informed about the subject material and genuinely shows interest in how her students perform. Quick response to e-mails.

Pretty easy class and wonderful professor!three tests, and a two part final (cumulative part is take home). Skip anything in the book that is not mentioned in the class ppt slides.She is really understanding and flexible (even with exam dates!). You have to take the lab, but it is actually pretty fun(compared to 110B). Def take for a BSCI/EEOB majo

Nice lady, but don't bother going to class. Study the slides and supplement with the textbook. Very quick to respond to emails and willing to help in any way she can. The class is very difficult, but so is every other section. I'd recommend her to anyone taking 110B.

She changes from the other profs in intro bio. All the others make sure their notes are where tests come from, she chooses to go the book route. Print off her slides and review the book you will be fine for all tests.
She is great!
Never have to go to class just read the textbook.  One of the easiest classes I've taken at Vanderbilt.  She's a really nice lady and will do anything to help you out too.

Very friendly which is nice.  Lectures are not too bad.  Attendance not required.  Tests are pretty tough for a 100 lvl class.  You will have to spend a good amount of time studying and using the book if you want an A.  A B is easy though.  I'd suggest going for geology if you want easy science CPLE credit instead.

Due-Goodwin is an amazingly nice woman, and is one of the most helpful professors at VU. However, her tests are crazy. My average dropped significantly from above a 96% (w/o curve) from Page's section to in the eighties from her tests. Super unclear/unorganized with her lectures and notes. She just isn't clear AT ALL.

Most helpful Professor I have encountered yet at Vandy.  Shows genuine interest in students.  Very easy to talk to in and out of class.  Very helpful in Office Hours.  Husband who also works in the Department is a riot!!!

Very easy class.  Dr. Due-Goodwin is very helpful.  All I used to study for tests were her posted lecture notes.  She is also very personal and helped me jumpstart a new major.  In study sessions, she is very vague.  That just means that you study the shorter versions of lecture notes posted on Blackboard.
This was an easy class! The prof. posts detailed outlines of the text and lectures online, which is amazing! I never even opened my textbook.

It's always sad when the textbook to a class is more interesting than the teacher.  READ every word of the text; you won't get much out of class.  When it comes to grades, she is the epitome of vagueness.  She'll tell you to know general stuff and then her questions will be really specific.  Definitely don't take it your first semester, freshman yr
I hate her. She makes me fall asleep every class.
Sucked, avoid her, doesn't teach the material.  Don't get me wrong, she's nice, but not a good teacher.  Honneger, Broadie, and Patton are all better, in my experience anyway.
Bio with Due and her xeroxed lecture notes is a piece of cake, mmkay.
No Comments
Great teacher who knows the possibilities and limitations of her non-bio major students. willing to help you with anything in and out of class. tests pretty straight-forward

The sweetest and most understanding professor.  She really wants to work with you and help you any way she can.  To make a good grade you gotta keep up with the material and go to class though. NOt an easy A or B
She is extremely sweet and will help you with anything.  You know that she really cares about the students and wants to do what she can.  Tests and grading are kind of hard though.
Her class does require some work, but she is willing to help you through it every step of the way.  She is very kind, warm, and approachable.
Alright class.  Nice person. Definitely a morning person. Lots of material, not to hard if you put work into the class.  I didn't, and it burned me.
very clear in class lectures, helpful, but grading and tests are difficult
Take him for CORE, super chill guy and makes the class interesting.

I have mixed feelings. I do not like that we are only given one overall grade. No individual project grades or individual participation grades. There was a specific piece he complemented in person with minor criticisms, but later criticized harshly in an email to justify the grade. Which is fine, but felt a bit deceptive in my opinion.

Patrick is an incredible professor. I felt inspired and intrinsically motivated to create good work in his class and even cared less about my final grade. He places a large focus on the creative process, but if you show up, work to release your inhibitions, and are respectful and open-minded, you will do great in this class.
Really cares about the students and is a great professor!

Patrick was an amazing professor! I was a bit nervous coming into the class since I'm not an art major, but Patrick was incredible about making me comfortable and by the end I felt like I could explore art and be creative. I had a lot of fun. This class did, however, require some time out of class and was my most expensive because of materials.

I took Patrick's sculpture 1 last semester and he is so caring and inspirational, so I continue to take sculpture 2. The course is not merely about sculpture, but about more general installation art. Sculpture 1 is the class to build the techniques and sculpture 2 offer you a place to make you own art.  Really enjoy this class.

Patrick is such a nice guy. He really inspires you with your projects and gives you good feed backs. This class is not only about making works but also explore different artistic notions. Recommend for those who like messing around and like installation arts/ sculptures.
Attendance is not taken, but the posted slides don't cover everything, so make sure to attend classes.

Dr. Benton is super engaging and incredibly knowledgeable. There are no out-of-class assignments except for three papers (super short) and two of the three exams. The last exam is the final and is open note, but taken in class. He gives points back if you meet with him during office hours and gives exceptional feedback. (PSY-PC 1250)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: (For Neural Networks). Great, passionate, and understanding professor. The lectures were pretty stellar and the homeworks/projects were designed to challenge you in a relatively safe space to make mistakes and learn on how to fix them. Learned a lot in this class while not being too stressed out about the class structure, despite the material.

The tests and workload was very fair and made me feel like I was learning a lot without being overwhelmed. Can tell this class is set up for students to succeed, while still being sufficiently challenging.

Dr. Benton's engagement with the class and his passion about Developmental Psychology is truly what contributed most to my learning. I genuinely was always excited to go to class because of how great he was as a teacher.

Dr. Benton is caring and an easy grader. The exams are based on lecture notes and are take home, open note and you can do corrections on them, and there is no homework. There is one group project at the end of the semester, and if you do well on the first two exams you don't have to take the final!

Professor Benton is a pretty nice guy, This class is harder compared to the other dev psych classes available in Peabody, but it's not impossible. His test can be a little confusing but at the end of the year, he started allowing us to use a cheat sheet. The homework is also very useful if you have an interest in research.

the hardest PSY-PC course you will ever encounter. the graduate students struggled a lot. grading was weird and unclear, but he did give second chances. not sure why he didn't make changes to the course until after grad students failed his midterm. made the class harder than necessary, but I understand that this was his first semester at Vandy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His reading quizzes were annoying otherwise good class

His reading quizzes for more difficult then his exams tbh lotta difficult class and he's a great person and a professor. It's just a little bit hard to get in A. This course can benefit a lot if he would add an extra credit project. Overall, he's a really kind guy. The exams aren't very hard and he allows a cheat sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the most real and refreshing professors I have had here so far, he is honest and will crack jokes in class but we always cover the material for the day and sometimes get out early. He is very wise and knowledgeable, class is not mandatory but you are going to want to go every time because he is very passionate about what he teaches.

beware he changed the class up so much then what it used to be, no long easy A. the guy is completely rude and shows no respect to anyone. quizes every class and 50% of the grade is 2 exams he barley prepares you for take gupta instead

David is great. The class is really easy if you do the work. Grades are based on daily readings where you create 2 questions each per article (pass/fail), weekly short lab reports, attendance, a take-home midterm, and a take-home final (group or individual). Easy A and he gives helpful feedback before final submissions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is the sweetest guy ever but the daily reading quizzes were a lot. Beware that you have to read what's assigned or it will drop your grade by a lot. His tests are also difficult but the final group presentation makes up for it. Overall, he's very very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Diehl is a genuine professor who knows what he teaches. He's a super nice guy. Class has daily quizzes but they are designed to be simply just checking if you've completed the readings - not intense at all. He sets you up really well for both the midterm and the final. I would definitely take him again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Diehl is such a good professor for 2100. He is so caring and will make sure you get all the help you need to succeed. The work is very manageable. 6 reading responses as online quizzes on different case studies and book concepts, two take-home quizzes, and two policy briefs.
Good class. It is mainly papers and reading responses, and exit tickets for participation. Whole class is basically about looking at companies from different perspectives.

Professor Diehl is very knowledgable and passionate about this topic. He's great at explaining the concepts and as long as you pay a little bit of attention in class, and use the TA as a resource, you should be able to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures and not too much work to turn in. Readings are usually pretty short as well. Easy quizzes, policy briefs take more work. He's probably the best choice for 2100.
Work you do in class is actually helpful for assignments and gives you extensions. A lot of the work is basically completion and then two take home quizzes and two essays.
He is the best. Super understanding and although the class content isn't riveting he tries his best to make it interesting.

Very nice guy. Class is boring but that is to be expected given the content. A lot of class is discussion based which is great. Attendance is "mandatory" but you get 3 (? maybe 2) skips without having to do any makeup work which is decent. Class is pretty easy with grading but you have to try. 2 big papers that count for 20% each of your grade
felt like I could take a nap every class, either the content was just extremely boring or the professor was just not able to teach. Maybe a different professor for this class would be better.

Class is rather boring, but he makes it as interesting as he can. More of a class to sit and listen to him talk like a podcast almost. You do group work every class which is just answering questions or coming up with connections to class material. Very understanding and supportive outside of class. He has a stuff happens mindset which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just read these reviews, and although I feel that the most recent ones are a little bit harsh, I do agree with the fact that diehl acts all nice, but really isn't wanting to explore different viewpoints. Seems to be extremely self-centered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was hesitant to write this review at first because I thought that it could have just been a single experience, but after reading the past rmp review, I've decided to write one. Diehl was really unsupportive of my needs while I was going through some mental health issues and was considering taking a leave of absence. He didn't seem to care at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Diehl seems to care about his students on the outside but really does not care at all. I tried talking to him beforehand about a few circumstances that I couldn't control, and instead of helping, it felt like he was blaming those circumstances on me. I felt extremely unheard, and won't be taking another class with him ever again.

Prof. Diehl is a nice guy with a boring class to teach. Weekly tophat reading quizzes are annoying but pretty easy. Midterm and two papers, the test is easy and you will ace the papers if you follow the rubric. If you have to take 2100, he's a good prof. I just found the class boring and very centered on working in corporate America.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not good but not awful. His assigned work was not interesting at all, though.

There is quite a bit of busywork, including weekly modules of activities to complete but none of it is particularly difficult or graded harshly. Two 6-8 page policy briefs and a group project with different components due each week which was easy. He is very accomodating and listens to class feedback, particularly in the online format.
Great guy but is kind of disorganized especially with an online class. lots of busy work but tends to grade pretty leniently. Overall would recommend him for 2100
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Diehl! He was very friendly and caring. The work consisted of 7 case studies (each one took me like 8 hours), two papers (midterm and final), group projects, readings, and daily quizzes on the readings. No tests! Everything was easy, just time consuming. Great class!

Professor Diehl really seems to care about his students and is very accommodating and understanding. Lectures were pretty boring and class is mandatory but there were sometimes engaging activities. A lot of group work graded easily, about 7 case studies (kinda tougher grading but follow rubric), and easy daily quizzes. Definitely recommend!

He genuinely cares about his students, which is awesome, but the amount of work that seems to have no point whatsoever is overwhelming. To me, it felt a little like a high school class with the amount of busy work we had. Professorawesome. Classthe most boring thing on earth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Diehl seems to genuinely care about his students! He's willing to be flexible with assignments and deadlines to fit student needs and is a pretty easy grader! Mostly group project based class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Diehl is a really nice, genuine guy. Attendance is mandatory but his lectures are interesting and funny. Most of the class is based on a group project. He often has moved back deadlines if too much was assigned in one week, and he even moved up our final so people could go home earlier.

Very good class to take, I do not recommend taking freshman year, but despite that he made this class fun and enjoyable. Do not let my grade trick you, I'm just bad at languages, but the professor is genuinely great and makes French enjoyable, If I were better I would take his class over again. Be prepared to do homework and put in extra work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This was prof Dize's first semester at WashU, but I hope he sticks around for a while. I had terrible experiences with French prior to this class, but he completely changed my perspective. While the course is difficult, he is more than willing to meet outside of class and help however he can. One of the most caring professors I have ever had!

Wonderful Class! Nathan makes so many awful yet wonderful jokes, and he truly wants to help you learn. The class is fast, so you have to learn a lot of vocabulary and grammar really fast; however, Nathan makes it really enjoyable and understands

It's an easy introduction to French and Nathan doesn't want anyone to be left behind or lost. He is willing to change a few things up to best work with students and is always making time to be able to help students outside of class. Is passionate about the language and tries to make learning it fun. Lots of partner speaking activities in class

TAKE HER CLASS. Her workload is manageable and predictable, so you get into a routine quickly. Be prepared to participate in class for credit! She always has fun and engaging lectures, so you'll never be bored.

Professor Deng is one of the nicest professors I have had the fortune to take a course with. She's very flexible with grades/deadlines as long as you let her know. Class can get long with lecture, but she usually spaces it with fun activities. She does a good job at conveying the content, and the assignments and reading are pretty well aligned.
One of my favorite classes and professors I have had at Vanderbilt! Professor Deng is so incredibly sweet, and her class is very engaging and easy to get an A in.

Dr. Deng is the best teacher I've had so far at Vanderbilt!!! I thoroughly enjoyed her class, she has really interesting lectures and it's not stressful at all if you show up to class and do the really easy assignments. The material is a nice and applicable change from regular engineering classes, and I loved coming to class everyday!!!
I had a great experience in this class. The workload is not too heavy, and the content and lectures are very engaging! Dr. Deng was a great professor, and highly recommend taking her class.
Great class!
Very kind and understanding, you can tell she enjoys teaching. Just be involved and you'll be totally OK

I would 100% recommend Professor Deng to anybody thinking about taking this class. The work is extremely doable and a nice break from other vigorous classes at Vanderbilt. As long as you go to class on time and submit your work on time, you will get an A in her class.
She is an absolute sweetheart. You get what you put into the class. Very easy, but interesting material.
Professor Deng is so sweet and the class activities are fun! I would recommend this class
Very nice prof

Professor Deng is really chill. Class is fun with group activities so she won't talk at you the whole time. Only downside is there are a lot of quizzes and journals due every week but other than that good course.
