Professor Deng is very kind and will help you to get an A in her class. It is a decent amount of work/group projects, and you do not learn a whole lot, but it's a nice break class for engineering students

She incorporates a lot of activities during class time thus making it more engaging. You only have to attend in person once a week, the other lesson is on zoom. It is an easy A class, but attendance is very crucial.

Professor Deng's lectures are engaging and informative. She truly cares about the success of her students and was willing to be accommodating. The out-of-class work is manageable and relevant to what is taught in this course.

Great professor teaching one of the best classes at Vanderbilt. I really had the time of my life coming to the lectures and would not miss them for the world. Will miss this class thoroughly and the great friends I made here.
The best class I took at Vandy. Would recommend it for all engineering majors.
The workload is manageable with weekly journals, quizzes, and fewer than 5 group projects. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities, and if you do well enough throughout the semester as well.

great vandy professor! very encouraging of students and expressing ourselves. there are weekly journals based on the readings/your personal experiences. it is also a hybrid class which makes it easier to balance as a vandy student. workload is manageable, and she is very understanding of personal circumstances. would def recommend.
The BEST Vandy professor. Enjoyed her class!
The BEST Vandy class!
The professor was chill but her materials were quite relevant and important.
she is fantastic so take hers if you can

Dr. Deng is indeed very different from other professors so she might not be someone for everyone. She trusted to let us take the lead and to own our own learning. She has a rigorous structure and she sets high standards. She is also caring and supports us from every level. I do not know about others but I learned more this way.

Prof. Deng is absolutely amazing. She is very different from other professors. She cares about her students not only doing well in her class, bu actually understanding the material to its entirety to practice and implement the principles in their individual lives.

I loved this class! It was a great end of the day with interactive activities and interesting theory. Just be ready to be active, and the good grade is yours! Professor Deng is a really sincere person, and a good professor!
Great professor, caring towards students, course is very easy. Some activities are fun, and stimulate thinking.
One of my favorite classes! Professor Deng is very sweet, caring, and easy to work with. Do your work and she will have high respect for you.
Good class👍
Very polite.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very understanding and easy to get along with, goated teacher. I just slacked off too much in class, so I didn't get an A, but there's no reason not to. You get what you put into the class. She's always willing to engage with you; you just need to respond to her.

Prof. Deng truly cares about her students, and she clearly wants everyone to exceed. She emphasizes the application of the material to the work force, so overall it's very relevant to our future careers which I appreciated. If you participate in class and do the weekly assignments expected of you then it's pretty easy to do well in the class.

Professor Deng is the sweetest person ever. I don't think my learning experience would have been the same if it was taught by anyone else. She cares so much about our learning and goes the extra mile everytime.
Genuinely one of the sweetest professors ever. She wants to see you succeed and has a legitimate care for the well-being of her students. Highly recommend!
Prof Deng creates a great learning environment. In-class activities are engaging.
The Goat, really flexible with anything if you have any problems. Super nice and understanding of students.

Prof. Deng might be the kindest person ever to step foot on campus. She genuinely cares about you, not only academically but also as a person. I recommend that any freshman take this class, especially since it double-counts toward the liberal arts credit. There is a weekly writing journal, but she's a lenient grader and provides helpful feedback.
Professor is very passionate and invested in this course. I felt supported while taking this course, and professor is very understanding if you have any concerns.
Very kind to all her students!
Professor Deng is awesome!
Passionate professor, lots of in-class activities
Had to take this summer online version and it turned out to be surprisingly smooth and pleasant. Learned a lot about teamwork. Professor is very supportive throughout.

Dr. Deng is great. Out of all of my professors, she has been the most invested in me academically and personally. Applied Behavioral Science is the type of class where you get out what you put in. I really enjoyed my time in this class and would recommend it to any engineer at Vandy.

Professor Deng genuinely cares about her students and creates a safe environment to speak your own opinions. Overall the class is not the most difficult but you do gain a lot of valuable lessons and I really encourage showing up to get the full grasp of the lessons.

The professor was very well demonstrating what was to be expected in the class. More emphasis on being able to put yourself out there and build your own character. Very useful and definitely a must take for tops classes at Vanderbilt. She is very caring, respectful, and engaging with her students, making sure each and every one is successful.
lovely and easy a class if you just do the journals and quizzes.

Took 2440 to satisfy my module classes, ended up being one of my favorite classes I've taken in 4 years CS & Neuro. Prof. Deng is incredible. Work is enjoyable to do, guidelines are clear, lectures are discussions, and I feel I'm already benefiting in the real world from the class. She is also incredibly nice and caring. Highly rec the course.

Professor Deng is amazing! She's super kind and caring and she wants all of her students to succeed. She gives you multiple opportunities to improve your grade if you're not happy. Not to mention the content highly relevant to everybody not matter your major

An amazing professor with the willingness to help students with career and personal development. It was a pleasure to come in everyday and be greeted by her even if we were late. Overall a very insightful class, but also at the same time not stressful to add to your classes for the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Deng really cares about her students. This class is a really nice break from all of the "technical" engineering information learned in other classes and instead focuses on soft skills that actually matter.
We love Prof. Deng
Prof. Deng is not like any other professors because I feel valued in her class. I also feel more comfortable to challenge myself. Great professor!
Final was tough. She did not teach us anything but we still learned a lot.

Actually to be fair, I think she is pretty fair. She is not a typical hands on detailed oriented engineering professor. But she created a great learning experience for what project management is really like. You will have to get used to that way of work to very much appreciate her.

The sweetest lady ever. Very kind, caring and understanding. I love her she is so nice and sweet. Would easily take again. Could have gotten an A if I tried harder, her class was not very difficult it was very doable.
The sweetest women ever and such a great teacher!! Learned so much about management, super informative class. TAKE HER SHE IS THE BEST EVER TEACHER CANNOT SAY ENOUGH GOOD THINGS!!!!!
every assignments are vague, half class were useless online, talking about rules and syllabus

Dr. Deng has a lot of love for what she teaches and for bringing groups of engineers together! We had such a small class, but I feel like she connected us and engaged us with the material. She also threw us a holiday party with cookies to end the semester because that's just the kind of person she is. 10/10 would recommend!
Dr. Deng respects and cares about her students a lot. She also says she learns a lot from working with us. Mutual respect and appreciation.

I was worried to be in a small class at the beginning of the semester. I soon realized that Dr. Deng is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. Totally unexpected. She has made our small class the most engaging learning environment on earth. We had great discussions and enjoyed our class learning together. Incredible.

This class teaches the most simple, fundamental, and powerful management and leadership concepts and techniques. A lot of class interactions and many opportunities for public speaking. Writing is also essential. Amazing that Vanderbilt School of Engineering was able to hire and retain such a great management professor!!
Very kind, very helpful, genuinely cares about our success and learning. The class isn't hard, which gives you space to actually learn without being overwhelmed by due dates.
Great professor, would highly recommend taking this class
Greatest teacher at Vanderbilt! Biggest takeaway from her class is her kindness and how empathetic she is for her students.

Professor Deng is a really sweet professor, and the class is pretty easy if you can set aside a couple hours a week to write 4 paragraphs and complete an open book quiz (I'm guilty of putting it off until the due date, and it worked out well). There's a group presentation and a personal presentation/essay, but they were chill and she grades nicely!

Professor Deng's class was an amazing experience. Heavy focus on learning and understanding as most work was graded for completion or graded very easily. Lots of opportunities to share opinions and discuss with pears. Amazing professor.
Don't be fooled - Dr. Deng is tougher than she appears. You may think it is easy. She has high standards. And she does not bend to pressure. Great professor.
She did not lecture us much. The class was mostly group work and class discussions. Really liked it in my senior year. I had to work harder. But I learned more and better this way.

Prof. Deng is nice and accessible - easy and enjoyable to work with. She encourages the class to give her feedback over a range of platforms, both formally and informally. She shows grace and commitments to our learning experience. She is receptive to our comments but she also holds us accountable with the right amount of pressure and challenge.

Dr. Deng taught us very well - one of the most valuable lessons is how to face ambiguities and uncertainties in the discipline of project management. It was quite a stretch from what I am used to as a Vanderbilt student. But I think I will appreciate it later.

Prof. Deng is very kind and cares about students and their experience, but the execution of this class needs work. Assignments and grading are vague, communication was poor, and we had to repeatedly ask for clarification with conflicting information. She knows the material well, but lecture time was often wasted on tangents and transitions.

Professor Deng is a very caring teacher who wants all of her students to succeed. The ENGM 3700 course was not particularly challenging; however, sometimes her instructions and expectations were unclear. Overall, she was great.
what a mess of syllabus
Really nice professor. Engages the class and connects with her students

Prof Deng is the sweetest woman, she not only cares about how you want the class to be ran, but brings in a lot of simple participation credit to make your grade better. Group Projects are typically given way in advance and you know what you are graded on. Really enjoyed this class, simple concepts that are easy to talk about.

Super sweet professor! Material and workload is not difficult at all compared to other classes, but the content itself is very interesting and more insightful than any other course I've taken at Vanderbilt. Professor Deng is also very accommodating and understanding that students have busy schedules.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hybrid schedule is nice! Group assignments require a fair amount of time, but peer feedback forms are helpful/reassuring. Grading criteria is often vague, but Prof. Deng is willing to clarify and offer feedback when asked. The opportunity to receive feedback from "check-ins" before submitting the final assignment for DMAIC was very helpful.

Prof. Deng goes out of her way to ensure that students are engaged with each other and the class material. Be aware -- this course is mostly group projects with random groups. Assignment criteria can be vague, but she encourages creativity. If you already like the subject matter you will like this course, but it's not for everyone.

The course materials were organized thoughtfully and purposefully by Dr. Deng. It was a great class to learn about self and others on the subject of applied leadership. Be ready for challenges and critical thinking. It might look easy and simple in the first place. But I know what I have learned in this class will have a lasting impact.

Dr. Deng is super understanding of your personal situation and provides tons of extra credit opportunities. Everyone can and should end up with an A in this class, and while the topics covered throughout the semester are varied and broad, there are a few that will stick with you for sure. It's not a difficult class content or even work wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Deng is super personable and will do all she can to help you succeed in her course, there is a lot of reading but group discussions each week help you understand the main points.
Dr. Deng is super personable and will do everything she can to help you succeed in this course!
Good class to take as an elective or for major/minor requirements

With this being the first year Prof. Deng has taught this course, we encountered many technical difficulties. However, she was super adaptive and really cared about students' success and negotiated with students to find workable solutions. This course was one of the most memorable and informative courses I had taken in the past semester.
I have never seen a professor working this hard to come up with solutions for our learning experience. No one is perfect so we all understand. I respect her efforts a great deal!

Professor Deng is amazing and cares a lot about her students. The class had very mundane assignments which were graded harshly but she was open to feedback and adjusted everything favorably. She is a great professor overall and if you do all the assignments you will get an A. The class also inspires a lot of reflection!
Really great class and a great prof, felt like she cared so much about us and very open to feedback

If you're not an engineer you'll probably complain about this class. If you are an engineer, then this will be the nicest class you have ever taken. Prof. Deng's teaching adds a 'human' element to most of an engineer's workload and she is a lovely person.
Prof. Deng cares about her students a lot. I have found great values in her class activities and topics. I appreciate that Prof. Deng took our comments and made thoughtful adjustments.

The class overall was incredibly simple, but the lectures were meaningless and mandatory to attend. Group projects had no real rubric and overall the class was very disorganized. It was abundantly clear the professor never read the syllabus for her own class (the other teacher used the same one) nor conduct activities. Overall awful.

Fall 2023 is Prof. Deng's first semester at Vanderbilt so sometimes the class feels a little disorganized due to her adjusting. But other than that Prof. Deng is super nice and caring and doesn't make this class very difficult. If you do all the assignments you will get an A.

Professor Deng is new to Vanderbilt so she was still adjusting to how to run this course. I enjoyed her class; the grading criteria for homework and projects are very straightforward. Very approachable and understanding. You get an A if you put in the work.

Lectures meander and are regularly wrong/unclear. All assignments are group projects which just adds layers of stress to the class because the turnaround time is usually like a week. Entire class graded by "points" rather than assignments so you don't know what your grade is. Lots of arbitrary headaches. Couldn't pay me to take this again. Avoid.
Genuinely the best professor I have taken. Class was easy, with the only out of class work being like 10 minutes of homework. If you can take this class TAKE IT!

Divya Ji is just such an amazing professor. Her experience in teaching languages shows in her teaching every day, and I am so grateful. Her teaching really helps students understand what they are learning, and she makes learning fun with engaging activities. I learned so much within one semester, even when I thought I would be so behind.

Divya Ji is by far, the best professor I have ever had. Through her immense dedication and compassion, she always finds a way to make learning enjoyable. Aside from being a phenomenal professor, Divya Ji is just a phenomenal person. She cares for you and will always put your first. She is my second mother, older sister, and best friend all in one.
Best professor I've had at Vandy. Super caring and understanding. Wants you to succeed.

Divya Ji has definitely been one of my favorite teachers at Vanderbilt. She is caring, thoughtful, funny. The class is so engaging and makes a student actually want to learn Hindi. Definitely recommend taking this class and her.

Divya Ji is the best. Seriously. I can't think of a more supportive, caring professor. She's so kind and so fun to be around, and she allows your class experience to not only be super informing, but also very fun. Take her class.
Amazing Class, could recommend more, Divya-Ji is a wonderful lecturer, and wants you to succeed.

What a fantastic, caring, extremely organized professor. She is so knowledgable about the linguistic aspect of Hindi and will adjust her lectures to suit everyone's needs. If you have no background at all in a foreign language, that's ok. She WILL 100% help you excel. Try your best and she will recognize your effort. 1000000% recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is the mother I never had., she is the sister everyone would want, she is the friend nobody deserves, I don't know a better person. She's what professors should be. She's a mentor and everything done in class is aimed at you learning the material . She's so caring, gives 100's on homework as long as you do it, quizzes have lots of extra credit

Divya Ji is the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt so far. She is such a caring and skilled professor and genuinely loves her students. I highly recommend taking Hindi with her because you will learn (even when you think you aren't).

Divya Ji is without a doubt the best teacher I have had at Vanderbilt. She realizes that Hindi is a tough language to learn, especially for those who are not native speakers, and runs her class as such. Divya Ji is an amazing teacher in the way that she personally invests herself in her students lives, becoming their friend while remaining a mentor
Grading criteria were unclear, and feedback often felt aggressive. Late (and harsh) grading and lack of remediation opportunities made this class stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: SHE IS SO UNCLEAR WITH EXPECTATIONS. she seems so chill on syllabus day/before the drop date then after will post harsh grades out of nowhere that feel incredibly unfair. i could have sworn i got at least a 95 on 1 of 2 tests and got a 70. have no idea how or why considering she didnt pass them back. she also makes aggressive comments do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very interesting class, but harsh grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor added assignments abruptly, used class time for personal projects unrelated to the course. Group projects were unbalanced. Constant changes to project requirements added unnecessary stress. Attendance is key in this class!!! Show up or end up like me. She also has terrible grading rubrics and grades based on how she feels.

Dr. Dine is a very fair grader and is accessible to students who aren't already knowledgeable about art history. Not necessarily an "easy A" but 100% an attainable one if you show up, learn, and put effort into projects.

She is compassionate and cares a lot about museum studies. Unfortunately she expects the same passion from her students, which can be annoying. A lot of woke/left leaning material. Museum field trips are fun and the class is very easy. A group project + final project make up most of your grade. She will grade tough if you dont put in effort.
Run! The grading criteria is very unclear and harsh. The workload is really unreasonable for an AXLE course. Don't take her class if you have other options.
Super nice professor. Two written assignments, and one podcast group project. Gives great feedback. Not hard to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wonderful Professor! Highly Recommend!

Lectures are dense but great—full of valuable info, so go. She's approachable but can be intimidating or slightly demeaning. Lecture participation is minimal; discussions matter more. Tests are long and graded tough, but fair if you're prepared. She learns everyone's name and pays attention, which is a nice touch.
Overall great but hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Lectures are dense but great—full of valuable info, so go. She's approachable but can be intimidating or slightly demeaning. Lecture participation is minimal; discussions matter more. Tests are long and graded tough, but fair if you're prepared. She learns everyone's name and pays attention, which is a nice touch.
Overall, great but hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Heney really deserves a higher score on here. I took Ethics and Mental Health with her, and the class was very informative. She grades participation with weekly writerly check-ins, so you can't skip. The midterm was tricky, but the exam was the study guide she gave so you had to study properly. She is so caring and kind, I recommend her.

Overall glad I took Ethics and Mental Health with her, but it was not an easy class by any means. I may just not be a philosophy major, but I definitely put a lot of work into the course. Of course, I came out with a lot more knowledge. She clearly cares about the material, but I've felt that she can be a little condescending/unhelpful one-on-one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my favorite class that I have taken at Vanderbilt. Professor Heney is awesome and she really cares about the material. The readings were rarely more than 10-15 pages per week and they were all super interesting. If you engage with the readings and come to class, an A is totally attainable.

Dr. Heney is very good at teaching her specialty. I took death and dying (PHIL 2608) with her and I learned so much. The course readings address interesting philosophical questions, especially for pre-med students. The midterm and final can be thorough, but easy if you study. I highly recommend to anyone who is pre-med or interested in philosophy.

This class is heavily dependent on who your TA is. They grade everything, so if you don't choose the right one you could be screwed. The material is very interesting and so are the discussions, but there is vague feedback on major assignments. Nothing went in the grade book all year, so prepare to constantly calculate where you are at grade-wise.

Avoid this class. Your performance seems to be heavily dependent on who your TA is. Dr. Heney was pretty condescending in office hours at times as well. I was missing points on tests for reasons even she and the TA couldn't explain; grading criteria is not clear at all. One of the hardest classes I have taken at Vandy, I only got an A by luck.
Incredibly rough grader. Feedback wasnt too specific and no chance for rewrites. interesting material but didnt

Professor Heney really cares about her students and is super accessible/flexible. Class only met once a week and we only had two papers that were the majority of the grade. Super interesting topic and as long as you do the readings, participate, and put forth the effort on the papers you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Heney is amazing; she's so kind, understanding, and helpful. Class is really engaging, interesting, and not like other classes because she really takes time to show that she cares. The material is interesting and enlightening; the majority of your grade is on papers but they haven't been graded yet. I recommend her as a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrific professor that truly cares about his students. He makes a topic that is inherently very boring actually bearable to learn, and he provides you with everything you would need to get and A with a very fair amount of effort. He curves generously, and this should be the top priority for upper level econ courses!

would not recommend this class - lecture makes complete sense but then when it comes to exams, they're not straightforward and unnecessarily difficult - interesting class though nonetheless but if you care about getting a an easy A, avoid this class I think there are other higher level econ courses that are easier

Professor Dillender is a great teacher! He truly cares about the success of every student in his class. You take a midterm and a final, have a group presentation, and a few very straight forward quizzes or in class questions. I recommend this class highly for an upper econ elective! It is very chill and the professor is so nice.

Professor Dillender has been the best economics professor I've had at Vanderbilt. Grading was very lenient and there's a variety of things (not just tests) included. He explains difficult concepts in a simple manner and is very accessible. Highly recommend taking his economics of health class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He would always skip class during our semester because of the Kirkland Hall riots and campus protests (I mean I guess he is the chancellor but still). Didn't release any grades until after Finals Week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Diermeier is a funny guy and he's obviously super accomplished in his field of study. But, he assigns a crazy amount of reading (sometimes 150 pages per class) and his essay grading is HARSH (since he's so busy the TAs do the grading). He can be really strict about attendance so don't skip class or else he might lecture you on oil investments
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Diermeier is an icon on campus, but in the classroom he is even more engaging, a solid lecturer, and witty. Readings can be long/tedious and he takes participation very seriously (25% of your grade). Four papers and a final which are graded by TAs (sometimes tough). Sometimes goes on tangents about the benefits of the fossil fuel industry.

I enjoyed MATH1320 with Professor Sonkin. His lectures definitely clarified the material in the textbook, and he was extremely patient and helpful during office hours. I'm not much of a math person, but I would take his class again.

This professor is simply amazing. He used to be at Vanderbilt but now is at UVA. He is the most kind, caring professor I've ever had and truly is passionate about all of his students doing well. If you're having trouble, he will go out of his way to help you. 100/10 professor. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I couldn't tell you if he's a good teacher or not because frankly you can not understand a word he says. If you can, avoid this teacher. His tests are pretty hard and you won't learn a lot from him. Maybe a little from trying to figure out his notes but you would have to rely heavily on the text book if you took a class with him.
extremely hard to understand.. very boring.. extremely unhelpful
go to class and office hours - he's a great professor if you put in the effort. the material is just hard though
He is really hard to understand and the grading is really tough. He's helpful if you go to his office hours though.
No Comments
No Comments
He is Russian and at first is kind of hard to understand, but once you get past that he is definitely one of the best math teachers I have ever had.

Professor is good and lecture is pretty good but this course is way too hard for undergrads to take, especially students without physics-related background. Much harder than any other courses I took above 3000.

Prof. Disconzi is a great pick for 2610. Class is very lecture heavy like most other math classes. Offered extra credit test re-dos with open solutions that would give you a boost if your overall grade was on the cusp. Would definitely take again.

Professor Disconzi was a good professor but the online nature of the course made it difficult to completely understand the lectures. By going through the textbook sections and doing examples you can kind of teach the course to yourself. Disconzi was very accessible outside of the classroom and gave extra credit to help round up students grades.

If you've done well in math in the past you should be fine. Lectures are okay but you can tell Prof Disconzi is not particularly interested in teaching. I don't recommend skipping class, especially in the later part of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Disconzi is a gem at Vanderbilt. His lectures are insightful, and he is very good at explaining things. Tests are straightforward.
Heavy accent.

I didn't really think he was a very good lecturer. His handwriting was hard to read and his lectures were often very unclear. I ended up learning most of the material from the textbook, which was surprisingly easier to understand than Disconzi himself. The tests are very similar to the practice test, and they're pretty hard IMO. Overall difficult
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Disconzi is a super good teacher and explains most concepts really well. He also wants you to do well if he sees you put in the effort. However the class material is still super hard and he doesn't let up on the tests. If you put in a lot of work and go to his office hours, you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Disconzi is a good teacher. There was no textbook for the class, so it was decently difficult to find additional sources that lined up with the notation he taught, but he started posting the class notes which made it a lot easier to study. His tests were long and difficult, but all of the work was outlined in the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Disconzi was great! His tests were very challenging but he was super clear in his lectures. He was always willing to meet even outside of office hours if you asked him. I think there are probably easier professors but if you want to understand the material Disconzi is great and he really seems to be there to TEACH. I highly recommend him
Test are similar to practice test. He teaches the material in a clear way. There is a group project that helps your grade too. I think he is one of the best math teachers i have had at this school
Assigns outrageous amounts of homework, gives extremely long tests
Good teacher, tests are hard algebraically, but he's helpful. Misgrades tests often.

155a is extremely difficult no matter who you take. Disconzi had lots of good reviews before I took this class, so I signed up for it, but it really doesn't matter. The class's test averages were in the 60s and the final was terrible.
Prof. Disconzi is helpful and wants you to succeed. He holds review sessions, office hours, posts practice exams, and even teaches recitation on occasion. His tests are hard though.
Really straightforward. Bases his lectures off of the book and explains the concepts very clearly. Make sure to do the hw and the practice tests and the tests should not be difficult.

Professor Disconzi is a very nice guy and cares about his students a great deal. He would have been my favorite professor if his tests weren't so unreasonably hard. So far we've had 3 tests and the averages have all been around 60s.

Marcelo was the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt thus far. He always wanted the students to succeed and made the class as easy as he could while challenging us as well. He was very helpful during office hours and was an all around great guy. Take any of his math courses if you can

Professor Disconzi is new at Vanderbilt and is great. His accent really isn't a problem. He explains concepts excellently and loves to help. Prior to every exam, I would go into his office (not even during office hours) and ask him questions to make sure I understood the material. He always helped. He cares about students who care about the course.

He really is a great teacher. Though sometimes it's hard to understand him through his accent, after a while you get used to it. If you need help he is more than willing to work with you on certain problems and will explain it very clearly. He writes everything word for word down on the board so it makes things easy to follow. Definitely take him!

Disconzi is awesome. He really knows what he is talking about and gets his point across clearly. He goes through steps that many teachers would just skip and assume that you know what they are talking about. He really wants you to do well in the class and is great in office hours. The class is hard, but if you actually do HW then you should be fine
He is coooooooooool! Take his class and you will get easy tests, easy quizzes, good grades.
Disconzi is the man. He explains things thoroughly and clearly in class, and challenges you enough in the tests, but doesn't go over the top. Math 155b is always hard but he's always willing to help.
Tests and quizzes were both easy. He gave us an assignment every two or three weeks. He was very helpful during office hours.

Probably the best 155B professor you can get (as far as I know). He is really good at explaining things, very helpful, and he keeps an up-to-date website with everything you need to know about the course, including extra examples, quiz keys, etc. I love his Brazilian accent.
Very helpful teacher. He always welcomes students to ask questions. He can explain every question clearly.

Dr. Hardin's lectures are sometimes difficult to follow, but he welcomes clarifying questions. I needed to attend his office hours around twice a week to fully understand concepts and get clarification on homework questions (homeworks were often really long). He is highly accessible outside of class, which led to my success. Straightforward exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult to follow in class lectures. Content is hard and proofs can be tricky but his exams are pretty fair and straight from the homework
Caring and nice professor but jumps from concepts to concepts making them hard to track. Things could be better explained. Don't take this class if you absolutely hate proof based questions.

The absolute mf boy. He cares so much about your learning. His tests are fair, homework is pretty long/difficult but it helps you learn a lot. Hardin is the goat, people who complain prolly just didn't show up or go to OH.

So unorganized. His lectures are impossible to follow. He messes up halfway through each time and has no idea what he's doing. My recommendation is to just read the textbook, all of the problem sets and exam questions are taken straight from there. He is a really nice guy, but seriously has no idea how to teach this material

I took 2600 with professor Hardin and he was absolutely amazing. He cares so so so much about his students and evidently wants you to succeed in the class. Go see him at office hours and he is amazing at explaining material if you are struggling with anything in class. I would 100% take him again and would actively seek him out for future courses.

Hardin is a good guy but very disorganized. About 1/3 of our HW and 1 exam were cancelled bc he couldn't keep track of things. IMO lectures were chaotic and very difficult to follow, but the HW was reasonable. Reading the book definitely helps. Exam questions came directly from HW, so study that and you should be fine. Felt like I learned a lot.
This class was very difficult imo. Dr. Hardin was very accessible outside of class but the material was still very hard to understand.

Doug is an amazing prof and a stand up guy who really cares about his students (esp. during covid). I took his data science courses (3670, 3890). His lectures are phenomenal, and the content isn't easy, but he makes it accessible. If you're unclear or lost he will help in class or office hours for as long as it takes to help you figure it out.

Very caring professor. His lectures arent the best Ive seen but easy to follow, and hes very willing to help you. HWs are essential supplement, and you do sometimes have to teach yourself so definitely read the book. Tests arent bad if you have studied your HWs thoroughly. Recommend to CS majors if you dont want to suffer 2810/20s instructors

Brilliant professor. Can be disorganized as said, but only because he's constantly busy researching, working with graduate students, and helping his undergrads, whom he seems to put first in priority. Class is a must and office hours are essential but amazing. He's nearly always in his office with the door open. Re-inspires a love for math.

Really great math prof - one of the better I've had at Vanderbilt. He's pretty easy-going with deadlines and due dates. Lectures are pretty good - good mix of theory and examples. Tests aren't too bad - there are some basic proofs but mostly straightforward computation.

He's super helpful during the office hours. If you read the book before, you could fairly understand what he's talking about during the lecture. Finish the review sheet, it's super helpful for the test. Also, we have a final project, which means no final test! It's rare for math classes.

Prof. Hardin is one of the nicest guys, even though he's kinda all over the place in class. But he's super-helpful during office hours (which you need to go to or you'll be done before the first midterm). The tests are fairly easy, and the homework ranges from mildly difficult to boringly tedious. You do a lot worse with math profs.

He is somewhat disorganized in class, but extremely helpful during office hours. He assigns weekly homework which is collected and there are often short quizzes at the beginning of class which together keep you on top of the material. 204 was the hardest class I've ever taken, but luckily he's a super nice guy and a lenient grader on tests.

Hardin is such a nice guy. It's up to you to stay up to date with the material but he'll do what he can to make sure you understand what's going on. His tests are very fair and he grades them leniently. Homework is due before each test and there are daily quizes (a problem or two from the short, ungraded nightly assignment). Highly recommended.

He assigns alot of homework and there are quizzes nearly every class period, but its all to make sure students are keeping up with the material. Doing so will earn you a good grade. He is disorganized in class, but extremely helpful in office hours. Being able to do proofs is a must, but he's very good at explaining how to proceed. READ THE BOOK.

Hardin is a really nice guy!  His tests are hard at times b/c he makes you know proofs and recite theorems but overall getting an A/A- is definitely possible.  Go to office hours because he is really helpful and kind.

Nice guy but incredibly disorganized and often confusing.  The averages on the four tests were usually in the C range.  He also gives tons of homework.  I would definitely avoid Hardin and 155A, unless you're premed or an engineer.  It's really hard and an absolute GPA killer.

Decent teacher, consdering the subject. He moves pretty quickly, but tells you specifically what you need to know for the tests - take good notes, do the homework, and you'll be fine. He has exact requirements for proofs, so make sure you pay attention.
Professor Hardin is AWESOME.  He's such a nice guy and his tests are really easy, also very helpful during office hours.  He's a little spacey but very entertaining!
He teaches alright, but his test dont allot for enough time!!
Really great guy, will definitely help you out if you go to his office hours, couldn't recommend anyone else, I thought he was terrific
He's a really nice guy, I definitely recommend his class over any 155a or 150a class.

Professor Hardin is a really sweet guy who's willing to work with you if you have problems.  Homework is a big part of the class though, so if you don't like to put too much effort into homework don't take him!  But I would recommend the class just because he's so amazing!
Very tough to follow in class because he confuses himself. The homework is difficult and takes a while but the tests and quizzes are ridiculously easy. Very good class overall.
No Comments
this guy doesn't know what he's doing and he doesn't want to be here. people are dumber for listening to him lecture
No Comments

WHAT?  I saw some people say his tests were hard.  Must be another one of those worthelss Peabody majors.  OH NOES YOU NEED TO KNOW HOW TO USE A FORMULA... please.  This class is a cakewalk.  I slept through every class and still got 97 as my final grade.  He is a little disorganized, but easy.

He is nice and all, but his teaching style is messy to say the least.  He somehow manages to take an hour's worth of lecture and only be able to touch lightly on 15 minutes worth of material.  His tests are not that friendly either.

I always felt like teaching this course was Hardin's last priority.  He seemed disorganized and confused, which made the class much harder than it ought to have been.  Lots of homework, some that even he doesn't seem to know how to do.
Excellent introduction to a very difficult topic.  Though tangential from time to time, Dr. Hardin managed to always bring it back to the subject at hand.  Overall this was a wonderful experience.
Very helpful, very nice and understanding. I hate math but he made it OK.
Always up front and helpful
No Comments
He is a nice guy but can't teach.
easy as pie but as nice as california weather
He is a really nice guy, but sometimes goes off on random tangents. Easy math class...and he is very understanding.
No Comments

This class was very interesting. He was very knowledgeable and seems to really love this topic. At first, it seemed very overwhelming, but his exams are not as hard as they may seem. He offered extra problems to get some credit back. He really wants us to understand, constantly asking for questions if we did not get it.

Cellular Neurobiology is a pretty interesting class. There were 5 homework assignments, that were fair, and 2 midterms and a final that were pretty difficult. However, he curved generously at the end. He's a great professor, really wanted us to do well in the class and very accessible outside of class. Would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class covers some great material, but the execution could be improved. McMahon clearly knows his stuff but his slides can be incoherent and unorganized at times and it's hard to know what to study for the test because we never use the textbook. He will hold review sessions and answer questions. Part of the grade is monitoring your own clock.

I enjoyed McMahon's class.  The class is pretty interesting....but because it's at an awful time in the afternoon, you may get a little sleepy.  Book isn't necessary but study the lectures carefully and McMahon is very helpful outside of class.  Easy A if you put in the work

Lectures are somewhat unstructured. Plus, he doesn't post quiz scores regularly, so it is sometimes hard for you to know your standing. Not a bad choice as an easy elective, but there are some better options if you are serious about econ.

Professor Dolezal is a great person who cares a lot about his students. He is very friendly and will try to get to know people personally and talk about things that he cares about and likes. A lot of people say that the class is disorganized - the class I took did not have a lot of the issues other people are describing.

Super nice guy and is very knowledgeable and passionate about sports. However, this is the most unorganized class I have taken at any level of schooling. One time he didn't even cover the information that showed up on one of our quizzes. Midterm average was a 68% w/o curve and the final didn't seem much better. Way too hard for a 2000 elective

I really like Prof Dolezal, but I wouldn't recommend for anyone to take this class. Even though the class average was only a B+, it felt a lot harder than a 2000 level elective should, especially for such a trivial and enjoyable topic. If you do take this, expect it to be a priority at times.

Professor Dolezal spends time ranting about random topics in class and purposely doesn't cover the material on exams. The midterm average was a 68 and he chose not to curve it. Office hours are a waste of time- he gets distracted and doesn't answer questions directly. He doesn't respond to emails and is incredibly unorganized. DO NOT TAKE

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! This year the Econ Department requires the average to be 'B+'. However, the average of the Midterm is 68%, which transferred to letter grade is D+. The quiz level is completely different from the practice problems he provides, and the midterm is even harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're an athlete, you might surprisingly do well somehow. Outside of that, the class is absurd, designed a test that no one in the class could finish but later told the class there were a surprising amount of people that did "finish" and because of that, didn't have any curve. Terrible teaching, but alright person.

Kent Dolezal loves sports but those are his only pros.His exams are nothing like what he covers in class and he refuses to go over material on exams students have failed.He only teaches material well when the Econ department shows up and besides that will ramble on personal life.Besides Kent is a GOAT and I will destroy anyone who slanders his name

Prof Dolezal is an awesome guy. Classes are typically relatively engaging discussions. However, quizzes and tests are on concepts we do not practice often. Questions are often broad, confusing, and very different from what we have seen. The content is not hard but is presented and tested in a way that makes it more difficult than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kent is a disorganized mess of a professor who tests on things that he never properly teaches. in fact, he never properly teaches ANYTHING. such an awful class, stay away

Seems like a fun class right? It might be: limited outside work, barely any solid material. If you're into sports, you might even enjoy his rants. His grading, however, is nothing like his teaching skills. He barely formally teaches topics, and he once taught us a lesson the class FOLLOWING a quiz we had on that material. Pass.
Makes so many mistakes and is so confusing and unorganized. Trying to study with his materials or answer any of his questions is impossible when you can't trust whether anything is written correctly.

Least organized lectures and materials ever. Almost every quiz, assignment, solution key, or test will have multiple typos or mistakes, leading you to lose your mind trying to figure out why you don't understand the concept when you actually do.
definitely avoid probably worst class I've taken at Vandy

Prof Dolezal is a great guy, but this has been my least favorite class at Vandy so far. The practice problems given in class or as prep often did not resemble what was asked on the tests or weekly quizzes. I often spent more time reading a question on exams to just interpret what it was asking than solving it, despite knowing the techniques needed.

This class was extremely difficult for a 2000 elective. I like math, but was still pretty lost. Lectures are very all over the place and he makes lots of mistakes. Weekly quizzes and midterms are very challenging. There is final presentation, paper, AND exam. Avoid.

This is not to bash prof Dolezal, he is very kind & funny! However I would not recommend taking this class unless u like math & it comes to u naturally. The biggest problem with this course is that it is too difficult to be a lower level elective but Dolezal makes many mistakes while teaching & goes too fast. A quiz every Friday even if not ready.
Dolezal is a great guy and very passionate about sports. Easy to get an A in this class since the econ concepts are very basic and its a lot of T/F questions about sports leagues.

Professor Dolezal is a great guy and I loved sitting in his lectures. He is very passionate about sports and he loves to talk about literally any sport. I would recommend doing a quick refresh of micro before the class, but otherwise most of the economic concepts are pretty easy to grasp.

I found this class to be tremendously disorganized. There's a lot of busywork, and the professor is never exactly clear what's due when. Doesn't use Brightspace very well either. One group project through most of the year will take some time. The economic concepts themselves are pretty elementary.
KD the goat

Dolezal is the best, he cares about his students and the class material. There is a semester long group project which is enjoyable witha good group. I would honestly recommend this class to people who are actually interested and know sports though

Micro is a boring and hard class but dolezal does a good job of explaining it. The quizzes and tests are fine but most questions have multiple parts so if you dont know the first part good luck with the rest.

Super nice and laid back. Lectures aren't the most interesting and helpful, but his practice walkthroughs online give you everything you need to get As on quizzes/exams. What he teaches is exactly what you see on tests and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: H is a very nice man and the class is pretty easy to get a good grade in. However, feedback is almost nonexistent. Expectations for assignments, quizzes and tests are never explained, so the only way to prep is to do the problem sets online. However, they are riddled with errors, to the point where I am pretty sure if he has never checked them.

Professor Dolezal is a great professor. If you put in the time and do the work you will be fine. Available outside of class and is a nice person willing to help if you ask. I would recommend the class to people genuinely interested in Sports Economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dolezal was overhyped in how easy his class is, definitely a more formidable class after covid. Show up, study the textbooks, know how to do the sample problem sets on Brightspace, and you'll be fine. Very nice guy as well, but definitely loved to make the class his own (with tangents as others said) rather than follow the textbook exactly

Dolezal seems like a good person, but he goes off on tangents SO MUCH. His writings on the whiteboard are confusing. He would start off from one side, move to the other opposite and come back to the original spot. His slides are unorganized. but the quizzes and exams are not difficult if you memorize the sample quizzes he posts on BS.
Dolezal is nice, but can go off on tangents and be a bit dry in his lectures. The quizzes can be difficult--make sure to study beforehand. Final project is not very well-structured.

Kent is a boring lecturer, goes on tangents a lot, and doesn't give much help in studying for his constant quizzes. This class is much harder than it was last year since he made everything in person again.

Kent's exams and quizzes are not too difficult. He has big problems when it comes to sharing his personal beliefs. Near every class he goes into something unrelated to economics and voices his belief. He shares way too much and it's very apparent what side he lays on. if this doesn't bother you then his class is fine.

Super nice, really wants students to succeed. Very understanding and always goes the extra mile in trying to make things as easy on students as possible. Also great at dumbing down concepts and making them very digestible. Can't recommend highly enough for Macro

The absolute best option for your first year writing seminar. Dolezal meets 1:1 to discuss every paper and offers multiple options for revision. 1 book to read and 3 papers the entire semester. Makes a great class environment. 87 is an A and that's not because it's hard. Truly wants each student to succeed.
Super nice professor, gives tons of material and is very organized with his notes/quizzes and overall class organization. Love him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Literally the best. Super funny, always makes me want to show up to class, a fair grader, very chill assignments, jokes around with us, and literally connected me to his friend to help me find an internship this summer. He's one of the best professors here, and I highly encourage taking his classes!

Dolezal is a g. Super easy to access outside of class, understanding of the issues with group assignments, and has lots of cool stories to tell. 2160 isn't bad at all. A range is super low at 90%, and as long as you do the labs and take homes you'll be fine on the exams. Just be careful to not make dumb mistakes with calculations and you're good.

Freakonomics was such an amazing class. Although we only end up reading a couple chapters of it, it's still worth it. Kent cares about his students so if you put basic effort into the class and participate, he won't let you not get an A. The papers are simple and he really empathizes with freshmen. The final group paper took some effort but easy A.

Prof Dolezal is a cool guy, but his class was very disorganized, so get ready to ask a lot of questions before you fully understand what the heck you have to write for a paper. That being said, he gives really good feedback on papers and lets you submit a draft to get comments before submitting the final copy. Super easy fyws (plus an 87 is an A)

A solid choice for a first-year writing seminar. He is a very laid back guy who is not the most organized but at the end of the day he wants you to learn and succeed. Class discussions are not the most interactive but he gives you plenty of time for the papers, which are graded pretty easily. As long as you put in the effort, you should get an A.

Kent is amazing! Super helpful when going over papers one on one. Also he helps students utilize the writing studio. One final group project/presentation and 5 small papers throughout the year. Very nice professor and was glad to have taken his class.
Kent is a great guy, and will grade fairly. If you are struggling in his class reach out to him, he will help you prepare for tests, and be upfront with you about what it takes to improve your grade.

Dolezal is kind and his grading is fair, but it is easy to fall behind in lectures when he goes quickly. Econ 2160 is difficult without a background in game theory or a lot of time dedicated to doing the (countless) practice problems. Like a math class, this class requires that you learn problem-solving processes, not facts. Do go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: For some reason they made 2160 harder this semester. Lots of calc which makes no sense for a lower level econ. Professor is always trying to fix his mistakes. Most people get very lost

Great professor. Makes one of the harder classes at vandy not bad at all. Teaches well in class and follows organized structure. Super nice guy who you can go to for help all the time. Very willing to work with students regarding missed stuff/poor grades. At the end of semester, does all sorts of grade boosters like dropping lowest quiz etc.

Very relaxed and informal first-year writing seminar. Three short papers during the year where he grades the paper during a 1 on 1 appointment where he discusses the whole paper with you. Final is a group project that you have plenty of flexibility and time to work on. Very open and relatable professor.
Super cute.
There is genius in his teaching. Take his class. Dolezal cares about his students and has a great sense of humor. One of the best econ professors I've had at Vandy.

Kent is a super nice guy. He's always accessible outside the class and he's humorous. However, you should teach yourself through textbooks and homework problems now and then, because his lectures are not always super clear. Make sure you did some previews before attending the class, or you'll be confused for 50 minutes. Not a hard class though.

Idk why his reviews are so great, you do not learn that much in this class. he often won't come or just gives out a worksheet in class to work in. i go to all classes and still do not learn much, i have to do most on my own to understand stuff. beyond that, it is not that interesting. if you like calculus, math, algebra and solving equations
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hard class but he's a super nice guy. Definitely try to take him for intermediate Macro, as he's a pretty easy grader and a super nice guy. I would definitely take him again.
Probably one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. While lectures can be a bit hard to follow at times, he makes a tough class enjoyable and relevant. Highly recommend
Dope class, dope dude.  Strategic Analysis was one of my favorite Econ courses that I took at Vanderbilt.

Great professor, funny and engaging.  Sometimes a little hard to follow in class, but review sheets are super helpful and tests aren't too hard, plus he's accessible outside class.  Multiple options for final, which was very easy.

Great guy, easy A. Unless you are straight dumb or just lazy and don't follow the requirements you'll get A- or A. But he's a new professor, very disorganized and the discussions were boring and not engaging at all. Most of the essays we wrote had nothing to do with Econ nor Freakonomics.

Kent is like the funny Uncle you see around the holidays who always cracks jokes and gives you gifts your mom hates. The kind of guy to buy beer for you despite you being underage because he knows you're just a teenager trying to have some fun. Kent's lectures aren't always the clearest, but he has a big heart and he wants you to succeed.

Professor Dolezal is fantastic. While his Strategic Analysis course is difficult, that is largely due to the subject material. He is very helpful during office hours and you can tell he cares about his students. His classes always seemed to fly by, often making me wonder whether the clock on the wall was correct. Great Professor- very engaging.

This class is great. Attendance is tracked so show up, also class is very interesting. Tests are not hard, do the  review questions he gives and you'll be fine. He is really a nice guy, answers questions outside class. I love this class. TAKE HIM !!!

Phenomenal Professor and a great guy in general. He really cares about his students and is extremely accessible outside of class. Provides real life examples that make the material relatable and provides endless practice problems for tests. Tests are extremely fair and similar to reviews.

Dr. Shadle is the best!  He is charismatic and has great classroom presence -- knows how to make the class laugh but also how to engage with serious topics. We had a fair amount of research to prepare for class discussions, but he is very organized and always gave clear instructions on our assignments.  Would 100% take any of his classes again.

Great professor. Engaging, shows up and ready to talk about the topics. Try your best to participate, Dr. Shadle prefers students who are active in-class and show interest in the readings. He may be lenient with some students. Submit papers on time and use his feedback to improve on your musicological writing! I would recommend to take him.
Took Dr. Shadle's Program Music class last fall. Discussions were intellectual and also fun. Highly recommend for the musicology elective

Dr. Shadle is genuinely the greatest professor I have ever had. I was not the most participatory student in this discussion-heavy course, but his endless passion for the subjects which he lectures on inspired me to become more engaged as the semester progressed. No professor cares more about his students and the subject he teaches than Dr. Shadle.

Dr. Shadle is very passionate about what he does and it makes you interested in the material. He makes class very fun, engaging, and the work isn't too much every week. Very chill class and he's very supportive of his students. Take his classes!

Prof. Shadle's class is exactly the kind of thing to look for as a Blair major - Super interesting but also really easy and never enough work to actually remove you from what you're here for (performance, composition, etc.). Assignments were all super easy and he's very accommodating. Take this class for MUSL core. You will not regret it.
Very kind and understanding professor. Awesome course that student who don't have too much experience with music can easily take. Highly recommend.
Lectures are pretty interesting, essays are pretty easy plus you get a lot of freedom with what you want to write about. An excellent choice for an HCA or W credit whether you're in Blair or A&S.

Dr. Shadle is awesome. He's a great lecturervery engaging, inclusive, and funny too. This class is a great choice for a W if you're an A&S kid, but also super interesting if you're in Blair too. The assignments are easy, not too much writing, and allow you to have fun with it if you want.

Shadle is absolutely awesome and this class has been my favorite at Vanderbilt so far. The course content is wicked interesting and Shadle does an amazing job at presenting it to students. Assignments are breezy and allow you to get really creative if you want to. Super good pick for an easy and interesting W course

Loved taking this class with Dr. Shadle! Material was very interesting and the class was discussion-focused. Dr. Shadle is hilarious, gives great feedback, and truly cares about his students. There were 3 papers, but all had interesting prompts and were graded fairly. Would definitely recommend taking a course with Dr. Shadle.

Prof. Shadle is amazing! He knows so much about classical music and makes it accessible to people who aren't familiar. Also, some really cool guest speakers come in. Graded over three papers, but a fairly easy grading scheme.

Must have some sort of musical experience to enroll in this course. Professor Shadle is by far one of the best professors I have encountered. He is hilarious and his passion for music is very evident. If you show up to class and engage in material with him, you will definitely pass.
Classes with Professor Shadle are great and laid back. He knows his subjects and just cares about his students. The class is heavily discussion based, though, so be ready to talk.

If you email Dr. Shadle, he will respond in like 5 minutes (no joke). Really tries to connect with his students and structures his class very well. Writing was not bad at all for a W class (most amount of pages you had to write was 3-4). Definitely a very good class to fulfill AXLE or for the music minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing. Must take. Very good for AXLE because it's a writing course and it counts for HCA. Discussions are great if you participate and he is sosososo supportive of everyone's ideas. Highly recommend.

Professor Shadle is a great professor who seems to really enjoy his subject. Occasionally class sessions include a bit too much of "Guess what professor Shadle is thinking", however, every discussion was very interesting and helpful. He has a great sense of humor, and is very helpful outside of class.
Professor Shadle is a great teacher and he really makes his students think critically without you even being aware of what he's doing. I ended up taking 2 more classes with him.
he is chill, exams are easy if you can gain some intuition for the theorems. solid lecturer. cares & wants to make it easier for you.
Decent lecturer. Nice guy and cares A LOT. Exam grades got back and class did well. Boring material and hard to teach I think but he tries.

I do not advise him. The first exam today (no cheat sheet) wasn't unreasonable, but the questions felt like the reverse of what he emphasized. What should be asked conceptually is vague—he just wants you to write explanations without saying so.

His lectures are fast and confusing, and his grading is very harsh. He may single-handedly tank my GPA.

This class, like many BME classes, was an absolute mess. The lecture does not equate to the lecture notes which does not equate the homework which (guess!) does not equate to any exams. Does makes the content way too confusing. There is 0 rubrics or grading expectations. He is condescending and rude to students. Avoid!!

He gets hate because people are bad at stats
Very great lecturer and very engaging!

Does gets quite a bit of shade thrown at him, but the class isn't that bad at all. he's pretty comparable to other bme profs. you'll be fine as long as you keep up with work. tries to be funny (and is acc kinda funny), super accessible outside class, wants students to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
He is one of the best professors at Vandy. While his material is fairly difficult --- he has the best notes ever to review class material and goes over everything so you know how to do stuff. 

He does not care about terminology and wants to see you can apply what you've learned. Pay attention in class and go over notes and you'll be great
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His rating does not properly reflect Dr. Does. He is engaging and funny during lectures and is very fair with homework and exams. Beyond that, he genuinely cares about his students. I would heavily recommend Dr. Does.
Dr. Does is a great professor, don't listen to the hate. It is very hard, though, but you'll be okay

DONT NOT TAKE THIS COURSE unless you really hate your life and want to hate it more!!! His lecture is tedious and you have to figure out bunch of stuff by yourself. The TA office hour is very helpful but there are many helpless students already waiting there. Imagine that OMG.

Avoid! I have never seen any professors bring such an inexplicable sense of superiority into the classroom before. His lecture is outdated and harsh. Midterm is a disaster. I SPENT A LOT OF TIME STUDYING BY MYSELF and I had to go to TA's office every week to make sure I understand the lectures correctly and set things right.

I'm gonna get drowned out by everyone else but he was one of the better profs I have had. The PDF notes were actually some of the best I've seen, and you can miss a few classes and get caught up mostly with the notes, plus he is SUPER open with office hours and really does care. 
Exam averages were low for sure, but ~33% made an A and ~33% made a B

AVOID!! RUN!!! Lecture heavy with only pdf format notes. Homework, test questions, and the final group project are confusing with no rubrics. Two midterms with averages both around 70, and a course average of about a B - almost impossible to get an A in the class. Trust me BME majors, there are plenty of other options for BME 2400.

Majority of lectures reading off his notes and sometimes MATLAB problems. Never went over problems that would be on written exam. Everything was very Matlab based and then we went to the written and were like huh! Coding exams in class should be take home especially if barely any partial credit is given. Graded harshly. Superiority complex

My friends told me to avoid this course at the beginning of this semester but I didn't listen lol. The exam averages are around 60s.The tests are hard and there are 10 assignments. He is kinda harsh on grading but thanks to my TA, he helps me a lot on the notes and assignments, I can't imagine if I lost more than 20% on hw.

Definitely AVOID Dr. Does' quant class BME majors... First midterm with mean ~60s and standard deviation of 25! STD of 25!! That's no better than a random number generated, and he seems feel not bad with that. Lecture's are unclear and confusing and I spead most of my time study by myself.

This class definitely lived up to its hype BUT Dr. Does is actually a really good lecturer and super funny person if you pay attention and put in the effort to actually understand the concepts. The MATLAB portion of the test can very easily tank your grade - hence the bad reviews - but other than that this class is very doable and interesting

If you can, do not take quant with Prof. Does. Seems like a decent enough guy, but has absolutely no forgiveness on test grading (first exam averages were ~60s and he was completely okay with that). No partial credit on MATLAB test portions (and yes even though this was a 50 min class, exams were 2 hours long IN PERSON with written/coding parts).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Condescending and rude teacher. HARD TESTS!

Avoid. at. all. costs. Saying exams are tough is an understatement, no homework grading rubrics, unclear lectures in pdf format, basically go into the first exam blind with no review material provided and averages around 60%. No final exam! just a month-long project worth as much as two homework assignments yay. Again. Avoid. - sorry BMEs
harsh
Prof. Does is a nice guy but this class was super difficult for no good reason. Harshly graded homework, and difficult exams, and is overall very unclear when telling us what he wants on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unclear grading, unclear project requirements, unclear notes, lectures with the most worn out marker of all time on the whiteboard, most of class content is delivered orally, smug, seems to make things unnecessarily hard, accused class of cheating on first exam (average was a 70 something), gave a much harder test everyone failed, bald

Does is very kind and cares about his students' learning. He is extremely accessible outside of class. Weekly assignments were fair and tests were tough, but final is a group project helps boost grade. He is a very good teacher and I learned a lot, but you get out the work you put in.

2 midterms (half in-class, half takehome), 1 HW every week, final group project (no final exam). His notes were helpful but his lectures were useless. Fair midterms, especially the take-home portion. Go to office hours for the assignments, as they are not hard and a big part of your grade. He answers by email v quickly and always tries to help.

He really cares about his students and was super helpful whenever I talked to him one on one! I personally had a difficult time understanding his lectures since he was pretty heavy on verbal explanations instead of using slides or writing everything on the board, but I know not everyone had that issue. Just depends on how you learn

It's just frustrating how I'm a BME major but still ruined my GPA due to this class. The content itself is interesting but the teaching sucks. Just wait to get more points deducted than expected in every test if you take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Does is a funny guy and a good teacher.  Helpful slides, easy assignments, fair midterms, and fair grading.  He likes hockey and medical imaging, so talk about either and he'll be happy.  Overall great professor.
RIP Dr. Kevin, you are dearly missed 😿💔🕊️
Dr. Kevin is so helpful and answered all my questions when I went to office hours and even let me pet him, which usually earns me a mean stare and a "get out of my office!!" from other professors.
Whoever gave the 1.0 not only likes dogs, but probably is one.
Whoever gave a 1.0 review definitely likes dogs.

Dr. Kevin changed the trajectory of my life. I was a mere pre-med, battling existential crises and humbling weed-out courses, when I had the incredible fortune of taking Dr. Kevin's course. His engaging lectures, ardent passion for the science, and compassion helped me realize that biology is a glorious path. We
I'm very concerned about Tom Clements' relationship with his cat. Gotta be illegal in some states fs.
Asp, Arg, Lys, Glu, Val, Ile, Asn!!!!!!! GOAT

Dr. Kevin is not only the best professor I've had at Vandy, but my favorite teacher of all time. He is super caring, has great style, and brings good vibes all around. His class is graded on # of purrs, how well you can throw his toy, and an essay on hating dogs. Overall, I could not recommend Dr. Kevin enough.

Dr. Kevin is by far the best professor to ever teach at Vanderbilt University. He lays on the table and purrs all day. Easy A if you listen to his amazing and insightful lectures. His amazing science experiments are referenced in his tests, with all the mutations he's discovered he deserves a Nobel prize.

Dr. Kevin is the most fabulous biology professor that I have ever had. Some might even say he was the cat's meow of the bio department. I would say that there is no need to claw one's way to success in this class- there is an equal chance for everyone to succeed.
10/10 lectures with amazing material. I feel so motivated and inspired. #we love Dr. Kevin
cat :)
I am forever loyal to Dr. Kevin.
I would sell my soul for Dr. Kevin
Great cat

Wow... Just wow. Dr. Kevin is by far the most unique and caring professor I've ever had! Bsci 1510 can be daunting at times, but Dr. Kevin makes it easy. He can explain CATabolism like no one else in the bio department. Never before have I had such a PURRfect professor. Take him if you can! He'll keep you feline good about yourself.
the GOAT

Dr. Kevin is the Coolest of All Time! He always seeks to make class a paws-itive experience and is inclusive of everyone. He even has an Instagram account so that he can be accessible outside of class.
Dr. Kevin purr-fectly conveys all course content in a paws-itive manner. He is very detailed and purr-poseful in his descriptions of sun spots—best explanation I’ve ever heard. Take his class!

Dr. Kevin is easily the best of any Professor I've ever had at Vanderbilt. Part of his class was really just listening to his whimsical ramblings about trying to teach biology in a human reference-frame while being a cat. His stories are truly motivating and make you want to do your best no matter what or who you are. He's also AMAZING at O-Chem!
Best professor ever!
Dr. Kevin is the best professor at Vanderbilt, paws down. He always comes prepared for classes and is the highlight of the class
Sad, stressed, depressed? Dont worry! Dr. Kevin has your back.
I love him :)

Wow! What can I say... Professor Kevin is the highlight of my courses this semester. He always reminds me to stay PAWsitive. Although I ask a lot of questions, he never makes me feel inFURior. He also helps me feel motivated after FELINE discouraged. Love his motivational pictures on Brightspace <3
Dr. Kevin has been my favorite professor BY FAR! I absolutely love him, and I will definitely take him again.
The PURRfect professor <3
Dr. Kevin is the light of my life and was so helpful in BSCI 1510L. He is purr-fect and I will never fur-get my experiences in lab with the wonderful Dr. Kevin.
A real gem in the Biology department.

Dr. Kevin played a large role in maintaining my mental well-being over the semester. He genuinely cares about his students, and is always there to cheer us up with a silly pose or smile. Very well educated on the subject matter and gives wonderful feedback. Also does a great job of reminding his students when assignments are due!

Sucre was my favorite teacher this semester. Although the reading is a lot, it is very rewarding to be able to engage with the content in class as he discussed it. Very important to take notes on pretty much everything he says because he highlights the most important themes of each text, which he subsequently tests over. Great intro to philosophy!

Prof Sucre is great and really cares about the material and teaching it. If moral philosophy is of any interest to you, this is a great (and very easy) class to take. If you engage with the material, you can get a lot out of it.
Very easy if you participate in class and engage with him. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and the reading is minimal for a humanities course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Sucre is such a chiller, reading pop quizzes that you generally could guess what questions he would ask. Also super unintentionally funny sometimes, which makes him even better- favorite prof at vandy by far.

Professor Sucre was great! Lectures could be boring at times but he was, but if you are interested in the topic you'll be fine. Doing the readings is not crucial, but definitely try to read as many of them as possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hes the best

He's chill but not as nice of a grader as people are saying. Don't have to go to class but if not you should get notes from someone else.
