Likes answers that match up exactly to what he said in class and if you leave something out you lose a good amount. Very manageable though if you just memorize what he says.

Dr. Sucre wants all his students to do well and is very upfront about it. The content is difficult if you are unfamiliar with ethics, but he goes through all the readings during class. There's definitely a learning curve, but he's aware and tries to make it as interesting and simple as possible. Not a low-effort class, but he's a smart professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Final was 50% of your grade so that was pretty stressful, but he claims(and I believe him) to be a generous grader. There were like 10 pages of readings before each class but he explains them during the class. Pretty solid and nice guy but as a non philo major it could get a little difficult to understand/differentiate between the philosophers.
I think Sucre is a good guy but this class was hard! I don't get why people rave about him. if you need it for your major it's doable but if youre doing it for axle take someone else

Has super high ratings because he's really easy. Most kids getting an A and you don't have to do any homework. Grade is based on the midterm and final. More of a lecture class rather than discussions even though it's capped at 30 people. If you're genuinely interested in philosophy I'd try something else, but if you just need a req he's good.

Dr. Sucre is a great professor. You can read the material but he fully explains everything in class. There was a midterm, a final, and a basic presentation to understand one reading. He is a gracious grader and clearly explains what he will be testing you on. This guy rocks and I would recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sucre is a fantastic teacher. I took the Introduction to Ethics course and really enjoyed it. There is a lot of reading, but you do not have to do it as long as you submit the reading responses before every class (they take around 10 minutes). He is an extremely witty and funny person and I highly recommend going to office hours!

First time writing an RMP because I liked this guy so much- The daily reading responses are extremely manageable (I can guarantee he doesn't even look at them) and attendance isn't mandatory. He's a super chill and funny guy- he acknowledges that the content isn't always "fun" but does a good job making up for that. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't need to do the readings (use ChatGPT/Spark notes), but you will need to submit daily reading responses. Though attendance isn't mandatory, all his exam questions come straight from lectures. Literally curved our midterm and final because he wants the average grade to be an A. My class' final average grade was a 95. This guy is the GOAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Great professor. Two exams and a final. Each exam was 4-5 short essay questions based off of assigned readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sucre is a great guy and an excellent teacher. He makes an effort to explain concepts in a simple, digestible way and is always willing to engage with students. Highly recommend if you are interested in philosophy, law/law school, or religion

Great lecturer, I didn't understand the content at first and he had a way of explaining things so they stuck- good examples. Very kind to students who were nervous to participate and clear requirements. Reading responses for each class that you just had to do, a midterm, and a final worth a LOT of the grade.
Great professor, very available and approachable. Show up and do the readings to get the most out of the class. Very discussion based. Also is very easy to get an A if you just show up.
Great teacher, easy A for this class. Just do the (short) readings and come to class. Caring professor and interesting guy.

Dr. Sucre is a pleasant professor. He assigns daily readings to base the class on organized discussion. Reading responses and a paper are the only two assignments. Discussions were sometimes hard to follow, probably because of his level of intelligence. He is willing to chat one on one, and seems to be a good guy apart from a good lecturer too.

Probably my favorite professor and class ever at Vandy! He's hilarious and makes some really dense and difficult readings easy to digest in class, so attendance is important. Discussion based. Really illuminating if you're interested in law school and legal theory, and he obviously cares about helping his students explore the material further.

Absolutely love him. A lot of good readings, some of them might be dense tho. Classes are discussion based, and he is very funny and clearly explains things. He does not go through the reading point by point so you might get lost if you dont read. He is very accessible outside of class and willing to talk about life and food and law school.

LOVE him. Very funny and down-to-earth- vocal about thinking u shouldn't go to law school. A lot of reading but he is very willing to answer questions (in and out of class). Its discussion-based and he loves if u participate (even if not profoud). Had a test and a midterm paper you expanded on 4 final- gave best feedback I have gotten undergrad
The discussions were extremely aimless and uninteresting. I think part of the problem was that Professor Sucre didn't have much experience with asian philosophy.

He is very disorganized and doesn't care that the majority of students aren't paying attention and aren't doing the readings. He just have discussions with 5 students and that's how the class runs. He is very picky about what he wants on the midterm and final essays, so he will deduct points for no reason.

"Discussions" during class were just him and like maybe 5 people talking. The content is difficult to grasp as it is & him having no other materials to help us was very frustrating. He was not receptive to our feedback about his exams. Midterm was rough & the final was even worse. Made me never want to take another philosophy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unlike the previous PHIL 1004 rating I would disagree on a number of claims. First of all, a small (30-sized) Asian philosophy class is not meant for a professor to lecture, but rather information is shared through discussion. Not sure if he will be teaching this course again, as he was assigned it last minute, but overall I thoroughly enjoyed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wonder why his rating is so high. I'm taking his PHIL 1004 this year and honestly this is the worst class ever. He has no slides prepared and we simply had a lead-no-where discussion each class. Overall, he is not a harsh grader. HOWEVER, if you really want to learn some Asian Philosophy from 1004, please choose another prof/ another class.

Professor Sucre is awesome. Huge fan. The readings could get pretty confusing, but his grading is really easy and he's so accessible. If you show up to class and stay engaged, you will get a good grade. Awesome guy to talk to about philosophy, careers, or life in general.

One of the easiest and most interesting classes I've taken. You need no medical knowledge to do well, but you just need to pay some attention in class and do the readings, which are fairly short and simple. The class is filled with interesting discussions and you'll get an A if you put forth some effort. Take if you can.

Sucre is the man. While he does give pop quizzes, attendance is not mandatory. Participation is 10% of your grade, but if you try and contribute or ask questions, you'll get credit. Super nice, both as a person and as a grader. Material is fascinating, and he creates good discussions. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I took PHIL 1008 without any medical knowledge. This class is all discussion based, with daily reading and sporadic (easy) reading quizzes. Dr. Sucre is very caring and poses interesting discussions that really make you think. This class was never really boring, he is super cool!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Bro does not give a crap about class. He is in lalaland

The class is pretty much a sequel to Digital Systems but different topics covered. Sternberg himself is nice and helpful. Lectures aren't super exciting but usually to the point. Grade is mostly based on 3 average difficulty exams and a long final. Lab sucks though because it's long but rewarding when things work. Start the final project early!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gives inconvenient busy-work assignments with very little explanation. Class is in general very easy but be ready to sit at your computer trying to figure out what the hell youre supposed to do.

Sternberg is passionate about what he teaches, but his lectures are dry and don't relate to assignments. Additionally, all of the homework assignments were really obscure and took hours to figure out how to even get started using the technology (IDEs, command prompts) to complete the homework. Avoid his module if you can, there are more fun ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sternberg freestyles his lectures, and I believe the topic changes each year. I like the lectures as a tech-savvy person, but others might find them hard to follow. Also the HW could be hard for students with no previous experience in Machine Learning basics, but actually could be completed if you follow the instructions
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Sternberg teaches the computer engineering module and while he isn't a bad teacher there is a steep learning curve for those who have never coded before. The instructions to assignments are very vague and Prof Sternberg lectures the entire class without really explaining what we are doing or how to do it. Overall, not the best experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty nice guy - the class material is a little dry if you're tech-savvy, but he does cover a couple of decent topis. Participation is encouraged and there were some amazing discussions. He kinda freestyles his lectures, but that's okay because the homeworks and the final test were both ridiculously easy if you paid attention to the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lab component is heavy in the labs, but it's very interesting. I really liked this prof, he really tried to help the students. I don't think the rating here justifies him well. I had a good experience with this prof. He really cares about his students!

This is just a module and I could tell that he came to class and just freestyled his lecture. With the addition of his monotone voice, I can not recall a single topic I learned in here. I don't think he is the best person to represent the field of CompE.

Dr. Sternberg is a decent lecturer. He tries to go over a lot of topics in a short time. This gives you a good idea of how CompE is as a major, but sometimes you will have no idea what's going on in class. The two homeworks are very easy and the exam will not be much trouble if you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Talks about the topics on a very high level. The topics are interesting. No final project unlike other ES modules.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the gems in Vandy's HOD department. Some of the most engaging lectures where he is so passionate about community change and planning. Teaches students to constantly think about the why when it comes to societal structures. Essay length req can be a bit long but he lowered the page req for the final essay when the class asked. Tenure ASAP.

Professor Nalani is the best! He is the most engaging and dynamic professor I have ever had. He cares about building community, truly believes in all of his students, and wants to give them the kind of knowledge that helps them navigate the rest of their lives. He also gives students and groups many chances to edit before final submission.
NAlani is the best. Hes cares so much and he actualkly listens to what the class wants. Topic was so interesting. Papers are long but as long as you try youll be an A

One of the best lectures I have ever had. He is inspirational and works diligently to ensure that all his students feel engaged. He also personally incorporates the concepts you learn into the class which helps enforce the concepts being taught.

Professor Nalani is one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. It is very clear that he genuinely cares about his students and their learning. The class consisted of 4 10-12 page group papers, a 20 min presentation, a midterm, and reading reflections. Grading was not hard at all, and he is very receptive to feedback! 10/10 class :)

Professor Nalani is a great person and professor. He genuinely cares about all of his students. He is a great balance between being fair and challenging. The class is an A if you put in the effort, show up to class, and complete assignments.

Such an amazing person, and truly cares about students. The class HODC 3342 was assignment-heavy at first, but he changed the syllabus to make it easier and more doable for students. Great prof and person

The most caring prof I've ever had. He is also an insanely talented lecturer and you'll learn so much from his lectures. The majority of class is group assignments (4 10-12 page group papers), 5 500 word individual reflections, attendance/participation, and a 20-25 minute final group presentation. He's a very nice grader. Only downside is A=95%

Cannot recommend enough. Nalani is inspiring, passionate, and the only HOD professor with experiences that are actually relevant and valuable to understanding human and organizational development. Invests SO much into students and is an insanely good listener. he's very actionable and can help you through anything, whether class or career related.

A very honest and kind human being. Was very flexible and personable. Always listened to what students had to say and facilitated classroom discussions. Also included real-life examples for content. Great class and great guy.
Best professor I have had so far at Vandy. He is super kind and wants his students to succeed. I cannot wait to take more of his classes.

HOD 1250 is the hardest course I've taken at Vandy due to how structured the course is. Sometimes Prof Finch wasn't able to go over all the tested content during lecture but he was easy to reach out to and was very understanding. Shoutout to Samuel, very good TA and did a really good job going over exam material during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take the class with him, there is no study guide for any exam. The review session is a joke he does not go through anything with you. there are about 15 readings each with 25-35 pages and also the concepts that he goes through during his lectures. he just throws all these to you before midterm/final and not tell you what to focus on. awaful!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very interesting guy. Really knows his stuff and does a good job explaining course concepts. The TA's do most of the grading so you won't interact with him much unless you go out of your way.

Professors are kinda useless in the course, since TAs lead discussion and grade everything, but Finch seemed like a nice guy. Lectures are typically full of nothing, a big chunk of time gets taken up by mindfulness activities and Peabody advertising at the start of most lectures. Not useless stuff, just felt like a very inefficient use of time.

This class was co-taught with another Professor, but I tended to prefer Dr. Finch's lectures. The content itself is sort of interesting, but a lot of days the lectures feel exactly the same. A decent amount of work and effort is required if you want to do well. Tons of assignments so nothing is worth more than 15-20% of your grade, which was nice.

I took a HODH seminar on Alcohol and Drug Use and found it pretty interesting. It was co-taught with Dr. Perkins. Class was straightforward, lectures were a bit boring at times but the content and assignments are decent. Prof. Finch is a nice guy, would recommend.

I took Professor Finch's HODH 3650 seminar thinking it would be an interesting class, but looking back now, I wish I had dropped it during open enrollment. The assignments are super ambiguous and you don't get any feedback until the end of the semester. Most people walked in expecting A's and left with a shocking C on their transcript. Avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Finch essentially just gave lectures (since everything is graded entirely by TAs), but I preferred him immensely to the other professor who co-led the class. He knows his stuff and comes across as someone who wants all of his students to succeed. HOD 1250 has a ton of assignments, but luckily they are all worth a small chunk of your grade.

HOD 1250 is entirely dependent on your lab TA (they do all the grading, answer your questions, etc). Dr. Finch was a super nice guy who knew how to give an engaging lecture, but I can't say he did much in terms of actually interacting with students. Get your TA to like you and 1250 will be relatively carefree.
Amazing lecturer if the content was relevant to what we were tested on. Tests were so unclear and just not comprehensive whatsoever. Study guides were useless.

Make sure to answer the online questions during class- they are graded but very easily. Attendance is mandatory and make sure you study for the open note tests. They seem easy but are not as easy are everyone thinks. The final was challenging. Still an easy A and the typical HOD1250 curriculum.

Finch is a great guy and a solid professor.  If you're interested in management consulting this class will definitely provide you with some of the tools you'll need when you enter the workforce.  Not a hard class either, but the fact that there are so many small assignments can make it a bit time consuming, so be aware of that.  Good class overall.
Great professor! He is demanding, fair, and very pro student.

He speaks really clearly and he presents current events every day that have to do with the subject of public policy for the day. He is a fair grader and makes the class interesting. He used to be a basketball announcer.

Professor Dustan is a great professor. His tests are very straightforward based on the problem sets, and he is very accessible outside of class. Intermediate Micro is just a hard class in general no matter the professor, but I recommend taking it with Dustan. He does not go through a lot of examples in class, but the problem sets help with that.

Prof Dustan is the man. The class is not too difficult but not a cakewalk either. You always know where you stand -- assignments are reflective of the exams and the lectures are cohesive (he also posts annotated slide decks, which is a huge plus). Dustan is clearly passionate about the subject and manages to sneak in hilarious quips during lectures

He genuinely wants his students to gain more from his class. Problems sets are easy if you go to office hours. The final was a lot of memorization just cuz it's cumulative, but questions were more like check marks to test if you have paid attention in class, no hard questions. Easy grader in terms of the 6-8 page essay.

Prof Dustan was awesome - definitely recommend. Made the class super straightforward with weekly (challenging but doable) problem sets, one pre-recorded presentation and a final paper. Made the content really engaging and it really shows that he cares about both the content he's working with and his students. Really kind, smart professor

Great professor and great guy! He is an excellent lecturer, lectures are super clear and concise, has an obvious passion for dev econ and knows his material. Weekly problem sets, presentation, essay, all very leniently graded. Accessible outside of class/in office hours. Look out for the occasional dad joke. One of Vandy's best econ classes/profs.

Professor Dustan was a great professor. His classes were very engaging and his problem sets were related to the material and were actually interesting and thought provoking. Grading was not too harsh, he is willing to chat with you if there are any issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors you can find in Vanderbilt. Inspiring, brilliant, helpful, kind etc.

I enjoyed his lecture, super clear and organized with some interesting examples. Helpful during office hour. He really cares and loves about development economy.  The class does not require lots of work (usual workload). I think for anyone who goes to lecture and likes this topic, you should be able to do well in this class.

He's a great teacher and explains things in a digestible way, but expects so much when it comes down to it. A paper based on reading 2 books, tests with more formulas than you've ever had to memorize, and he follows the book but picks and chooses what to cover making it impossible to follow the reading. Also the final is cumulative.

Professor Van Schaack runs a structured class. The midterm is challenging but fair, and the final paper is manageable if you stay on top of it. Unstuck study can be a helpful study tool alongside the textbook.

Van Schaack is a great professor and even better person. His grading guidelines are very clear- if you simply do what he asks and check your work you can get an A. Midterm did have a lot of content, but I felt it was very fair. There were no surprises or trick questions. Very approachable, kind, and funny! Totally recommend.
He is a good guy, I do not think he talks about himself too much like some others have written. The hardest thing in this course is the 10 page paper at the end but it is not too bad.

grades tough and not really approachable about correcting the grades bc it's all TAs. only offers 10-minute office hours appointments which isn't super helpful for getting feedback on papers. repetitive during lectures but still worth taking, he's engaging and the material is interesting. if you do the readings and show up you should be fine
Never NEVER TA for this man!!! Worst mistake of my life.

Van Schaack is a cool enough guy. Probably a narcissist but his lectures were interesting enough if you can listen to him treat ChatGPT like its the second coming of christ for a couple hours a week. Unlimited AI use policy so take advantage of that. Like people have said he's strict w APA formatting, so just double check.
Great guy who will be there to help you as needed

There are reading quizzes at the beginning of each class (not hard, you know the questions before, and it allows the use of chatbot) and an exit ticket at the end about the lecture content. There is a midterm but no final; the average is about an 85. The final is a literature review. Compared to other HODs this class is more difficult.

Very arrogant prof. with nothing better to do than sit there and go thru each and every one of your citations cause God forbid you put a hyphen rather than the specific dash he is looking for. Not lenient on anything and loves to talk about himself. Good luck Charlie.

Fun and entertaining. Midterm is tough and lit review takes a lot of time. Everything else is decent. He allows AI which is super helpful and preps for use in future jobs. People say he's full of himself which I understand but don't agree. With that much experience and stories to tell, u can tell he's living an amazing life. Great prof rec taking!

People don't like Van Schaack because they don't follow directions. He's a stickler about APA and formatting, but as long as you follow the assignment directions and are a decent writer he's not difficult. No final and the midterm was quite manageable.

This page is all memes. If you want a class that makes you think in HOD, this is it. His lectures are not all fluff and actually prepare you to think in the real-world. People say he is a tough grader, but he just makes you detail-oriented. When you go into a career and miss some things, it's not just going to be a little mistake. Top 3 at Vandy.

I DO NOT LIKE THIS DUDE Super easy class as long as you turn stuff in. It's required for HOD core + he's the only one who teaches it, can't avoid He is very full of himself Loves talking about whatever is on his mind with no connection to class (would be fine if he was more interesting) Tries too hard to be hip/chill with references Just not my fav

Professor Van Schaack is super strict on specific detailed things (APA citations, format of assignments, etc) and grades harshly on those little things but he does tell you everything you need to know during lecture and in the syllabus and is responsive to emails. As long as you follow the detailed instructions, he wants you to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He took away my snack time privileges and would often prevent me from going out for recess. Class was okay tho.

This class is basically a free A if you know how to follow directions. Just do everything as he instructs on his syllabus and things will go smoothly. Attendance is unfortunately necessary, but paying attention during them is not (Although it would make things easier if you did.)

Van-Schaack is the absolute best professor at Vandy IMO. Don't get me wrong he is a stickler for grading (you'll find there's a good reason for that), but he cares about his students, and his lectures are funny and engaging. Genuinely looked forward to his lectures every week. There are quizzes at the beginning of every class so beware.

I loved this class and Professor Van Schaack! His lectures are amazing and truly interesting. You can tell that he really cares about the content he is teaching and also about his students. He is picky when it comes to assignments, but just follow the directions & you'll be fine. I wish he taught more classes. Best professor I've had so far

Best professor in HOD department. Funniest and most engaging professor I've ever had. Had everyone laughing everyday and makes himself relatable. Made me actually care about the class as he truly believes in what he teaches. Teaches you content that is actually important and applicable, unlike 90% of other HOD classes. Wish he taught other classes

Dude is a hard grader, but an awesome lecturer. Very funny, clearly cares about his students. There are enough guaranteed A assignments that tough grading on two papers won't hit too hard. The midterm was psychotically nitpicky, but he offered extra credit after and tbh if you memorize the slides you'd be fine

This class was more work than I was expecting from ENGM... BUT this is the most helpful class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Van Schaack cares about this class and we spent a lot of time talking about upcoming technologies. This class gave so much clarity for the future. We has quizzes once a week and we also had 3 papers (you can use ChatGPT!!)
The worst ever. So disrespectful and difficult for no reason

Van Schaack's great, no clue why people bash him sm here! He's so engaging and the class is useful esp if you're into research. He does grade tough and the papers take forever to do, but if you get started early and communicate with him and the TAs, it's not difficult whatsoever. Otherwise the class isn't a huge amount of work. Highly recommend!!!

In 2500, biggest thing is to turn everything in on time and use perfect APA format. His assignments take a lot longer than expected. His class is also lecture heavy and you can miss three classes during the semester. Not my favorite class but is doable if you stay on top of everything. Midterm was super hard and nit-picky so good luck with that.

Decent lecturer, cares about students. Like other raters have said, he's strict about APA formatting, but if you go to office hours, it's nbd. There's 1 midterm and 2 big papers. The midterm was based of the study guide he provided, and he didn't count questions where everyone had issues. Go to TA's office hours way before due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Least favorite class at Vandy so far tbh. Work isn't overly difficult just tedious w/ nitpicky grading so follow directions closely. Boring lectures that drag out mundane basic concepts but there's a reading quiz almost everyday so you're forced to show up. Van Schaack is a decent guy just pretentious towards students & needs his ego to be checked
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Van Schaack was okay. He is a tough grader and extremely precise as to what he is looking for. You will succeed in his class if you attend class, do the class readings, take the quizzes, do the exit tickets, learn APA, take notes, and make sure to connect with your TA to ask any/all questions- DO ASSIGNMENTS IN ADVANCE TO GET FEEDBACK
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever.  350 characters is not enough space to express my hatred for this man. He only cares about himself and will spend half the class just bragging.  Pretty much every lecture could be an email and also is stuff you learn in 5th grade.  If there ever was a 8th level this class is a prime candidate.  Yes I got an A but I don't care.

The midterm was a bit harsh, as some of the questions were tricky, and the final paper deadline could have been more distanced from the final exam so that it would be less stressful for students around finals week. However, Van Schaack made lectures interesting, was thoughtful of students' requests, and was a solid choice for HOD 2500 overall.

While I really enjoyed the content of this class and Van Schaack's lecture style, his expectations in grading were extremely nit-picky. He does give detailed instructions, but you must do everything perfectly in order to get an A on assignments. He will take off points for stupid stuff (like the color of links in citations). Nice prof, though.

Systematic Inquiry is not for everyone, but Van Schaack makes it extremely clear what he expects from students in exams and papers. Lectures can be boring, but he makes research methods as interesting as they can be. He is a very practical professor, and accessible if you contact him during office hours.

Van Schaack may be the worst teacher I have ever had at Vanderbilt. Every single class he reads straight from his PowerPoints, which is quite possible the laziest method of teaching possible. He takes points off of assignments for things he never mentioned, is VERY nit-picky about APA and just over-all is rude and uncaring towards students.

Van Schaack is a professor who acts like he is above every student. Get excited for a class where basic stats and experimental design are mansplained to you every lecture and where your grades are dependent on knowing the right dashes to use in APA (which you are not taught). I legitimately learned nothing.

He is just not the move. If you have the chance to avoid him, do it. Everyone thought they nailed the midterm but a majority ended up with a C. It is an extremely boring class. There is a quiz on the reading every single class. Additionally, his writing assignments take forever and has nit-picky grading criteria. 10-15 hour lit review before final.

Van Schaack is a funny guy but he tends to assign way too much work. Most lectures were just him reading off the power point slides and adding in a few jokes. We also had a ton of assignments and they were all extremely time-consuming. He also doesn't give a lot of grace to students or show much concern for their needs and is not lenient at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Van Schaak has been uncaring, inflexible, and condescending to multiple students this semester. Besides the quizzes, whether you go to lecture or not WILL NOT MATTER for your grade (unbelievably boring). Study guides hold minimally difficult information (literally just research methods), however the midterm has nothing to do with it. AKA: He sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The regrade policy was discouraging and unfair for students to make a case and point for their own work. Sure, he might say the grading policy is "inherently unfair," but discouraging students to not even try to gain points back when the grader is clearly in the wrong is not helping the system. Otherwise, the course is not that difficult.
He is full of himself and mansplains constantly. Content is ok but he is not very nice to his students

literally the worst prof at Vanderbilt I genuinely hate him so much... he mansplains everything and it so incredibly cocky which makes learning the material incredibly difficult because you just have no motivation to try.

If you work you can get an A but you have to be sure to get full points on the easier assignments. Exams are 100 multiple choice questions and can be frustrating but generally doable. One huge paper at the end with the final exam only 2 days later. He knows his stuff tho and if you pay attention you can learn valuable information.

Makes expectations clear, but still a very nitpicky grader. Can be quite arrogant and paternalistic at times. I learned a lot and he was definitely more engaging than the TA, but they seem to take pleasure in taking off points for the little things or putting tricky questions on exams. Go to class and office hours and you'll be fine.

If there's a different option, DEFINITELY take it. Van Schaack is the most persistent nit picky professor I have had at Vanderbilt and any moment you stop listening to a small APA formatting piece of advice, expect 5-10 points off your grade. The midterm was non-sensical and asked questions with no relationship to class and there's a quiz everyday!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I don't understand how Dr. Van Schaack has such high ratings. He spent class rambling, mansplaining, and making generally uncomfortable comments about race and gender. He also took the pandemic as an opportunity to be as brutal of a grader as possible. He does not care about teaching, but rather inflating his ego and trying to make you lose points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 2500 is not the most exciting course but Dr. Van Schaack does a good job keeping the energy up. This really helped me stay engaged. The assignments are lengthy and time consuming but not difficult. You have 3 allotted absences that do not impact your grade so you get to sleep in some weeks.

Van Shaack is hilarious. Truly a great guy and because of this his lectures were never really boring. He is super productive and there are no "pointless" lectures. Start the papers in advance of the night before and you'll be golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HOD 2500 over Zoom. Lectures were fine but grading is too dependent on TAs. Everything is very formulaic.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: hod 2500 over zoom. hated this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: HOD 2500 over Zoom. very poor. TAs not helpful. hated this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was one of those classes that is hard but doesnt have a ton of work. When there is work, give it a lot of effort. But a good chunk of the time there isnt a lot of work and you always know whats coming workwise which is nice. Go to class, TAKE NOTES which a lot of people didnt do for the async lectures, and youll be in good shape
Van Schaack is a nice guy but class/grades are super TA dependent which sucks. The reviews also take quite a bit of time but he's overall super chill and clear about what the class entails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you do the readings, it's really easy to get an A.

Van Schaack is one of the best professors in the HOD department. For those that complain that he is arrogant 1) you need a better sense of humor and 2) he is a very accomplished man and deserves to be so. He is so clear about what he expects from you and gives you every resource and opportunity to do well, so if you don't that is on you. 11/10

Super chill professor. He creates phenomenal study guides, and as long as you study those and his printed notes, you will do well. Attendance is not always required, but I would still recommend going. He often hints at test questions and his lectures are entertaining. I thought it was so cool that he knew everyone's names. Van Schaack is great!

The content is useful, but lectures seem to drag on for an unnecessary amount of time. The grading criteria is strict for the midterm and final, so you may feel like you get points taken off for the smallest things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Currently getting an A- in the class. But to reiterate what the person below me said, he is so boring and extremely arrogant. What I really hate most about this class is its not understanding concepts - its memorizing exactly what he wants and regurgitating. He takes off points for the dumbest things. Sorry HOD majors as its required with him.

I literally don't have the motivation to attend his class because he is super arrogant and talks about boring things constantly. His test has an incredibly heavy amount of detail, that is literally impossible to remember.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: really easy to get an A if you do the readings.

His grading is really clear, and you only have to come to class when there's a quiz. It's a lot of work for a few big assignments/exams, but other than that it's easy. He's pretty annoying and arrogant though.

Ugh. Some people like him, but honestly his arrogance is too blatant for me to see past. Wastes class time by making lectures a performance to hype himself up. That said, class and grading is extremely straightforward. Put time into studying and you'll be fine. Lectures completely unnecessary(just go 13 of the 16 days there are quizzes-he drops 3)

Don't see the hype around him. He does making a boring subject interesting, but he is extremely arrogant, and he lectures more about his life than the actual material. Wide variety of grades so getting an A isn't hard, but his lectures are pointless; however, you have to attend to take the 16 quizzes given throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a caring and knowledgeable teacher. He tries to help you understand the material with analogies. There's a lot of info to learn, and you can lose points on things you didn't expect, which can make this class hard. To get full points, he and TAs are looking for lots of things, so you have to put in a lot of effort to get an A.
His lectures are so engaging and exciting. He is an expert in his field. I wish he could teach every course at Vanderbilt.

Van Schaack is by far the BEST professor I have had at Vanderbilt. He makes the entire lecture hall laugh. He was presenting on APA citations and he still made everyone hysterical. He gives good feedback and engages with students during lectures.
hands down one of the best professors i've ever had at vanderbilt. take him for any class he teachers. always gives very clear grading material. can't go wrong with van schaack

Van Schaack is one of the best profs I have taken. He is also just one of the best people I have met at Vandy. You barely notice that attendance is mandatory b/c his lectures are just a joy to attend. He's extremely funny and very easy-going. Most importantly he's a generous grader. Write a few papers but put in some effort and you can get an A

Van Schaack makes a terribly boring subject much more interesting. He gives daily reading quizzes, but gives the questions beforehand so very easy, basically attendance points. His tests and papers are not easy, but he is VERY clear about what he expects so if you follow directions you will do well. He knows all students by name and truly cares.

Van Schaack is easily one of my favorite professors! Not all of the reading materials were interesting but he could make them interesting in his lecture. It was entertaining listening to him talking about the syllabus for the 2nd time in HOD 2500. It takes some effort to get an A but doable. He teaches things that are actually useful in our future
Van Schaack is a legend, not only for his personality and jokes but also because you can feel that he really cares about his students and their learning.

Earning an A is not hard, you literally just have to do the work he clearly assigns on time. His midterm is not that hard, just go to class and use his Pencast as a tool to study because the midterm is based on it. Final project is a guaranteed A- or above if you give a little effort, and he is always accessible to help. Go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This man's tests are from hell. I would study for a week and still barely pass them. Overall, would recommend if you can get to EVERY SINGLE CLASS because attendance is based on your quizzes. You only get to miss two quizzes. God forbid you've already missed 2 and need to miss more - you're screwed. Don't take it if you dont need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Andy's the man. Readings are required but very interesting. Attendance is mandatory for most classes because of daily quizzes, but the lectures themselves are engaging. He knew my name and called on me the first day of class before I ever introduced myself, which was a bit surprising but also shows he's interested in his students. Take him.
He works hard to make lectures interesting even when the material is boring. He looks for pretty specific answers on midterm and final, but he is very clear about what he expects.

Nice guy and pretty funny/engaging during his lectures. Course content is pretty dry, but he does a good job adding stories and such to make it more entertaining. There are daily reading quizzes, but they are easy. Unfortunately, I had this on WF at 8:45am so that was rough as half the class was hungover. Very enthusiastic person for that early.

Van Schaack is an engaging lecturer who makes a not-so-interesting topic much more relevant to students. The class is not necessarily easy--tests and papers are graded with an eye for detail--but if you are willing to put in the time/effort, it is completely doable. Overall very positive experience and you will learn a lot about scholarly research.

Pretty easy course. Easy subject material, all the lectures are provided up front, he gives study guides for every exam, and he's crystal-clear about his expectations for every assignment. No textbook, and less than 15 minutes of homework (reading for in-class quiz) most days.
The syllabus is very straight forward and he makes it very clear what he expects of his students. There are long papers that he grades pretty hard, but an A is definitely manageable.

Dr. Van Schaack is probably the best prof I've had at Vanderbilt. His ability to turn a subject that can be particularly dry, research methods, into something fun and engaging only speak to his ability as a professor. Additionally, there is no doubt that he cares about his students and wants each to succeed in his class. 100% take him if you can.

Dr. Van Schaack is literally amazing- one of the best professors I have ever had in college. He is hilarious and is super accessible outside of class, and the organization of his class as well as his clarity of expectations is amazing. He makes a topic that could be really boring SUPER interesting- that's the sign of an amazing professor

Very knowledgeable, good lecturer. Very, very harsh grader on major assignments/tests though. Have quizzes almost every class that ensure attendance. He's funny and knows every single student by name which is cool.

Took him for HOD2100 as a maymester. While it was incredibly demanding (a paper per week with a midterm and project in one month), he was an amazing professor. Not only was he easily accessible out of class, but he gave great feedback and was just an awesome guy. After this course, I requested him to be my advisor, he's that great.

VS is hands down the best teacher I have ever had. His class is difficult do not get me wrong, and as always with HOD some of the material is difficult to assess, but he does an excellent job and is constantly looking to improve. Sure he is a little cocky, but who wouldn't be when you are as good at what you do as he is. Take for HOD 2100 and 2500.

The best professor I've had. Made what could've been dry information extremely interesting with his sense of humor and engaging lectures. Learned a ton. There are weekly quizzes and the papers are a lot of work, but he's clear about what he wants. He is super helpful in office hours and you can tell he really cares. Take this with him if you can!

Doctor Van Schaack is funny and he is an engaging lecturer. He also truly cares about his students. Although he can come across as cocky, he is extremely knowledgeable and experienced. I would absolutely take any course he teaches.

Dr. Van Schaack is one of the best professors I have ever had.  If you want an A or A- in the class, you'll have to work hard, but it is attainable.  Dr. Van Schaack is a great lecturer and I looked forward to going to his class each week.  Definitely take this class with Dr. Van Schaack!

You do learn a lot in this class, but quizzes at 8 am that you actually have to study for sucked. End of the semester is very work-heavy, last 3 weeks consist of 3 huge papers plus final (75% of your grade). Papers are graded harshly. Both tests are hard. It is hard to get a solid A. Do a final project if he likes you -- graded MUCH MUCH easier

Every lecture with Van Schaack is amazing. One of the smartest, most interesting professors out there. He is better at keeping everyone in a large lecture feel involved than anyone else, and he is very likely the best professor I've had. The material is alright, but Van Schacck makes it seem awesome. Straight-forward guy, A or A- is very attainable

I honestly loved Dr. Van Schaack. He was incredibly helpful when I was sick in the hospital and had to miss class. Though he can be cheesy, he really makes lectures interesting and easy to understand. The second half of the semester is hellish because that is when all the papers are assigned, but he was always available when I had questions.

I absolutely loved Van Schaack's Systematic Inquiry class. It was by far the most interesting and practical class I have ever taken and I can honestly say that it has changed the way I think. Everyone should take his class. He is hilarious, fascinating and engaging. He is a tough grader, but he is clear with what he wants. I highly recommend him.

One of the best teachers I've had at Vanderbilt, period. Very enthusiastic about the material, be it HOD or ENGM. He was the major reason I decided to pursue an engineering degree after taking his Technology Forecasting and Assessment Class.
Great lecturer and useful learning material.
Really cool professor who gives very engaging lectures. Super helpful in office hours, and he has done a lot of cool things professionally. Would recommend him for 1700 for sure!
Great prof teaching an interesting class. Lots of little quizzes and 4 short papers but they are easy once he explains them and he grades easy as well. Would definitely take a class with him again.

Great Teacher, cares about his students and wants them to do well. Class is important but is also interesting. As long as you make an effort to show up and do the reading you will enjoy the class and get an A.

This guy is suspiciously smooth. About half-way through the semester you realize it's his sales background bleeding through into the lecture. What's he selling? Why himself of course. The bulk of each lecture is occupied by egomaniacal bragging on his own career. Quizzes and assignments are simple, should be easy to swing something in the A range.
The class is all mindless busy work. It feels like a class you would take in the beginning of high school. Also, Andy loves to talk about himself. a lot.

Van Schaack means well and keeps a potentially boring class interesting, but struggled to keep the class afloat the second half of the semester. Was impossible to meet with as its clear he's an adjunct professor and picks favorites right off the bat. Good teacher, but far too self-involved.

Guy below me is right. And he's a stickler. Seems so "new age of education," so cool, but he's so self-involved. At least you don't have to go much the 2nd half of the semester. The quizzes are breezy, gives you the questions. Skim readings for answers. He gives you the midterm and final questions. Writing assignments take a while. Easy to get B+

You like him for about the first half of the class and then you realize that he's a total cheese. He loves to make you think he wants to go the extra mile for you but when pressed, he never follows through. Not a fan.

Van Schaack is extremely clear about what you need to know and what you have to do. Class is very well organized. The material is interesting and useful, though he tends to drone and repeat himself. Daily quizzes. He gives the questions in advance. He posts/conducts extensive reviews for the midterm and final. The TAs can be really anal on grading.

Van Schaack is a great lecturer and he is very clear about what you have to do to get an A in his class.  He's a stickler about rules, deadlines, and random stuff, but as long as you hand stuff in on time and don't plagiarize you should be fine. The Critical Review sucks though...

Interesting instructor. The material taught is considerably different than in other sections of the course, for better or worse. While the extra things included are generally pretty practical, it would appear to come at the cost of the core material. My recommendation would be to consider taking this instructor in the event that you're not a major.

Van Schaack rocks. He is so engaging in class. The only frustrating thing is it can be hard to meet with him outside of class. Reading quizzes every week are graded pretty easily. He tells you exactly what you need to know and everything is applicable to real life

Van Schaack ROCKS! I had it at 8:45 and it was well worth getting up that early. He makes the topics interesting; definitely take this class no matter your major or prior interests. It is well worth it.

Van Schaack is the man! By far the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. He is so straightforward with what is on the tests and how to do the projects. Easy A as long as you pay attention and do the readings, and his lectures are so interesting that it's not even an issue. I would recommend this class and any others he teaches.

Van Schaack is literally the best proessor at Vanderbilt and surely top in the country. HOD 1700 is extremely useful and class is hilarious because of him. Take this class no matter your major or interests. You will absolutely walk away a much more capable person. I would go to class on Saturday that's how much it rocks.
He tells you what he wants.  No tricks.  The class applies to real life.
GREAT professor. He's so hilarious, and genuinely wants the class to help you in the real world. Takes the time to learn the names and faces of all his students. Definitely take his class!
Van Schaack is definitely my favorite professor I've had at Vanderbilt. HOD 1700 is extremely practical (not to mention interesting), and he is hilarious, helpful, and fair. Take this class!

Extremely funny. wants you to do well, and helps as much as he can.  grading is a little difficult so be prepared. 1 point quizzes in almost every class-be prepared. class is out of 100 points. extremely nice guy, readily available.
Andy is awesome, extremely engaging, reminds me of Steve Martin a little bit. No textbook. The class readings are useful and interesting, and he is the fairest grader I've ever had.
Van Schaack is the man. hilarious and engaging. no textbook. straightforward grading. interesting and useful class.
This class is a must. Even if you are not an HOD major, take this class. Material is very useful, and Van Schaack is hilarious. Classes are fun. No textbook, minimal reading, easy quizzes.
Best teacher ever!!! Most useful class I have taken at Vanderbilt. He is a comedian and  makes the material interesting. He is extremely helpful. Do your work and you will get an A

Van Schaack is the man! Take 1700 with him for sure. He makes the class interesting, and doesn't use a textbook because he puts all the assignments online. He's pretty easy and willing to help you with just about anything. He's super nice and pretty funny too. One of the best profs at Vanderbilt hands down!
Take Van Schaack. Only one assignment during the semester requires any sort of time commitment. He is very engaging in class and easy to understand. Makes boring concepts interesting.
BEST TEACHER AT VANDERBILT. absolutely take this class. he is an unbelievable teacher. so helpful, extremely successful, smart, interesting...i could go on and on
Van Schaak is an absolute legend.  He is very clear and understanding and he has a very good teaching style.  I definitely recommend taking his class.

Great professor. He does everything he can to make a boring topic as interesting as possible. He makes a big effort to get to know the students in this lecture-style class and be relevant to us. The only imaginable complaint against him is he might say something offensive if you hold strong traditional values. Take this class.

I LOVE Andy! Offers you help outside of class, such as with resumes, even with jobs and contact information! He has lots of interesting anecdotes to offer you--so he connects otherwise boring statistics with the real world. Realizes his class material is dull, so he does everything he can to make it not so dull...Take it!!!
Brings a lot of experience to the class. Makes a boring topic more interesting. The topic itself is not thrilling, but if you have to take 1700 with somebody, take it with Van Schaack
Amazing. I wish I could take this class over & over again, sad it's over
He is what every HOD professor should be. He is also the most helpful and available professor I have ever had. Wonderful, caring person.
Cool Guy

Makes a dry subject (basically research methods) fairly entertaining and funny. Expectations are very clearly laid out, so if you do the work, you should get an 'A'. He gives you all the material on the tests beforehand. Lots of small assignments here and there. I would highly recommend taking him. He's the best HOD professor I've had so far.
One of the best professors at Vandy. Extremely helpful, esp at office hours. Makes it clear what he wants. overall great class and prof.
THE BEST TEACHER EVER and the smartest guy i've ever met!
Van Schaack is an awesome teacher.  Go to class, and it really pays off.  If you pay attention, you will do well!

Van Schaack is the most pretentious man I have ever met. He is cocky and extremely unprofessional. He is unfair and not understanding in the least. His class is not worth having to deal with him all semester.

AMAZING TEACHER!!! my favorite at vanderbilt. do anything you can to take any of his classes. he gives you more than half of the questions on the tests the class before and is a really fair grader. makes super boring subject material pretty interesting. really easy to talk to outside of class.

Overall, he is better than most professors because he teaches the material well. However, he encourages you to e-mail him all the time but then he never responds to e-mails and is tough to get a hold of outside of class when you really need him even though he advertises himself as very available. He's also somewhat nit-picky about his grading.
Don't take 1700 with anyone else or you are just an idiot. Plan and simple...Van's the man.
Amazing teacher!! Keeps you engaged with class material. Friendly, understanding, & intelligent. MUST take 1700 with him!!

you are choking if you don't take 1700 with the van man. I bombed the first two tests and with all the extra credit he offers, ended up doing well. The only way to do bad in this class is to make a concerted effort to do so. Plus, he is by far the coolest teacher at Vanderbilt. Also, will tell you exactly what to study for his tests if you see him.
1700 isn't the most interesting class, but Andy makes it practical and interesting.  He grades fairly, helps you out, and is an overall great guy.

This class (1700) is awful, but is a major req. I can't imagine taking it with anyone but Van Schaack. He is the quintessential Peabody professor: well-known in his field of study, but more importantly, has REAL life career experience. He always talks about his job(s) and it makes it interesting. He doesn't spread assignments out very well.

He is the best teacher I have ever had at Vanderbilt.  He takes a boring topic and makes you think about it and makes it apply to your life.  He cares so much about his students.  If you have to take 1700, take it with Andy.

I love Andy Van Schaack!  He is the most caring, sincere, and humorous professor I have ever had.  He makes the class as easy as possible-it's hard to get below a B+.  There are two exams (SO easy) and 2 papers (not bad).  He brings us brownies and donuts on occasion and is an overall great guy.  Take him for 1700!

Boring class, but it is required, so Van Shaack does his best to make it interesting.  He brings us food, lets us out early, tells funny stories.  He wants us to do well, and is not out to get us.  If you have to take 1700 take it with Van Shaack.

Andy is so funny and interesting. It's a computer class and we make our own web site. There's no homework and he's extremely helpful and available. He brings us food to class. Reccommended for everyone...even non-education majors.

Class is not mandatory just get the notes and study them well, she is very kind and understanding, the course schedule seems very structured and overwhelming but as long as you are on top of everything you will be fine. Just do your assignments, she will not track you down if you don't turn something in or warn you about dates
Kind professor and really simplifies the topic. Tests and quizzes aren't difficult. She and her TAs are always accessible if needed.
sweetest teacher i've ever had. super caring, wants students to succeed. tests are very easy, she doesn't try to trick you. only math class i've had where i didn't stress about exams or homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dunbar was great! She's super sweet but make sure you turn in your work on time because she takes off a ton of points
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterm and final are not that bad as long as you study content from the slides and can apply the concepts. Assignments are also easy as long as you follow the instructions and look at the rubric. Lecture can be dry because she lowkey reads off the slides but still enjoyed the class.

sweetheart of a lady. for exams, just read the slides, no need for the txtbk. dry lectures, but participation is mandatory. Had some cool guest speakers. very forgiving in terms of grades → only 40% of grade was determined by midterms. Has like 1 assignment a week, all v doable not too time-consuming compared to some other classes

Dr. Dunbar is amazing!! Highly recommend her for dev psych. Her lectures were always engaging, and she is one of the most caring professors I have had. The tests were pretty easy after studying, and she is very understanding. This class taught me a lot, and I found it really interesting.
Passive aggressive at times and refuses to answer emails; course is organized terribly and slides have way too many words.

Jenni is super nice and her class is very easy. The exams are not bad at all if you just pay attention. She does just read off of her slides and could never answer students' questions, but I still learned a lot from the class despite that. She has many independent projects, but they are all pretty fun and easy. Good guest lecturers too

Jenni is easier for Stats than for Dev Psy, but it was still a great experience. It's a very content heavy class, but she does a good job with her exam review highlighting the most important concepts to review; if you just review from her exam-prep slides, you will do fine on exams. Attendance MANDATORY. Readings not required

She's not the most knowledgeable on dev psych (would often not be able to answer additional questions by students), but it didn't affect my experience too much. The grading was easy in 1250, but that may be TA-dependent. Would recommend her to anyone looking to take dev psych with a kind and unharsh prof, although there are a lot of assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am not sure what the other reviews really are saying, she is an extremely boring lecturer and reads off slides that have so many words; she also grades pretty harshly and will ask very specific questions on tests about the slides.

Very easy class but lecture heavy.  A few assignments worth large percentages of your grade and a couple of minor homework. 2 non-cumulative midterm exams. She really cares about her students and their success in her class.

The lectures were quite information-heavy. Which is okay, but I felt like she frequently read off the slides (word for word). This made lectures boring. 

The tests themselves were based off of the class slides (which was nice since it narrowed down the large amount of information we had to know), but were challenging at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I actually took PSY-PC 2700 but there wasn't a way to add that. Jenni is super nice and wants everyone to do well, but the class itself is kind of dull and tedious. I'm grateful that she posts her slides online, but every class is essentially just her reading them off the screen. The two exams for the class require a ton of memorization. Kinda meh.
Amazing professor. Easy class. Tests were very straightforward, and she always clarifies topics in class if you ask. TAKE HER CLASS!!!!

Dunbar is the sweetest professor I have had at this school. She cares so much about her students and their learning. She made class very easy to understand. The exams and quizzes were straightforward. There are random problem sets in class, so make sure you are there most days. They aren't graded but you do have to be in class to get credit.

Stats with Jenni = Automatic A. She's really sweet and caring. She tells you exactly what you need to know for the exams. And on the exams, you can skip multiple problems. 2 exams=50%, 4 quizzes=20%, 4HW (she assigns 6, but doesn't collect them all)=20%, Attendance=10%.

She is the sweetest professor I have had! She cares about her students and tries her best to make lectures engaging and entertaining. The work isn't hard and she grades easy. The exams are not too bad either and she tells you everything that will be on it.

Dunbar is awesome. Grading criteria was always clear, and she formats the exams so that you can choose a couple questions to not be graded. Do practice problems from the book and the homework and you will be fine for the exams and quizzes. All of the information that you need to succeed is right in her slides.

Easiest class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Takes some practice to get the swing of different statistical tests, but Jenni is a great professor who made it easy. Neither of the two exams were hard. Great class.

Jenni is the nicest professor I have had the entire time I have been at Vanderbilt. She was so incredibly sweet and understanding of outside circumstances. She was very generous with grading and deadlines - she pushed assignments back if she felt like we didn't have enough time to complete them. Exams were very fair and had plenty of preparation.

Peabody Stats can be a total nightmare with a lot of the other professors out there, but Jenni is an undisputed gem. This class is super manageable even if you have no previous experience in statistics. Lectures are super easy to follow, and she is always willing to go the extra mile to help her students! You won't find a better option than Jenni!

Jenni (as she encouraged us to call her) is the nicest Professor that I have ever had at Vanderbilt. She makes a point to ensure that her class isn't too stressful. Some of the lectures can be a little slow paced sometimes, but that's not really a bad thing. If you're looking to take Peabody Stats, there is no one better than her.

I loved Jeni she was so kind to all of her students, but I still learned so much. I was sick and out of school for two weeks and she accommodated my needs perfectly. The layout of her tests are incredible -  you get to pick one or two questions you don't want graded. It was easy to do well by completing homework assignments and attending class.
prof dunbar goes out of her way to help you succeed. very little homework and easy tests compared to other prof teaching the same class.

Professor Dunbar is so sweet and makes lectures fun, relatable, and engaging. She also takes plenty of time to let you take notes and is always open to questions. It is important to actually study and memorize for the 2 exams, but the assignments are very easy and if you follow the instructions and put in a small amount of effort you will get 100s.

She is a nice person, but a bad teacher. She needs to make her lectures more engaging and teach the material better rather than just putting slides up and reading off of the slides. An idea for how she can improve is hand write the notes herself during class for the class to copy instead of using her PowerPoints.

Professor Dunbar is genuinely one of the kindest Professors of all time. I was going through a lot  this semester and lost tons of motivation. She worked with me around my situation and deficiencies. There's also the fact that her PowerPoints are so well-made that I got a 90 on our first exam only showing up twice. Psych is just better with her.

Jenni is amazing. Her teaching style is clear and concise, and she always encourages questions, never shaming students for being confused. She is incredibly understanding when it comes to potential student hardships. Grading criteria was clear, tests were never curveballs, and she just made things make sense (and I had never taken stats before)!
Professor Dunbar is super sweet and you can tell she really cares about her students. Not a difficult class, especially if you have taken AP stats in high school.

I LOVE JENNI sweetest woman I've ever met. Her lectures were so fun, the class material was interesting, and the assignments are super easy. She's very accessible and creates a welcoming environment. Absolute GEM
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jenni is one of the kindest professors I've had! She admits when she does not know the answer to a question and has our TA write them down so she can look into it later. She talks about her toddler to give personal examples about developmental psychology as well as her experience as a counselor. She is so caring, accessible, and intelligent!
Such a sweet teacher. I loved having her and would highly recommend taking her classes.

Great professor in all aspects! She lets her students breathe and doesn't assign too many readings at once - perfectly timed out. She is very passionate and is always willing to help out with any assignment. Lastly, you can tell she really cares about her students. The pop quizzes werent too bad; try to read but skimming usually can get u an 8/1
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Super sweet professor. Easy A, but material starts to pick up midway through the semester so just be prepared to study for quizzes. All assessments straightforward. She only tests material she knows we understand.
Incredibly caring & helpful professor. Makes the content very understandable and provides formula sheets for all assessments. It is very possible to make an A in this course.

super sweet and nice lady... really knows a lot about this subject... easy A definitely take her if you can... tests are literally her powerpoints and those are super easy to follow and she posts them online as well... some in class activities so being present for that is important but not hard motivating self to get to class b/c interesting stuff.

Professor Dunbar is awesome. Her lectures are powerpoint and very easy to follow. There is almost no homework, except for a few papers, and a percentage of the final grade is based on easy in class partner assignments. If you've taken any psych classes in the past, a lot of the material is review. Wish I learned a little bit more but great prof
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great class. Jenni is super nice and really really likes discussion. She is a great person who genuinely cares about her students and will give you the benefit of the doubt on tests and rounding up. 10/10, Take her class!!

Best lower-div physics prof. Says he doesn't curve and give ec but each exam essentially has 1 ec problem so everyone automatically gets a ~5-6% boost on each exam. Hw could be tedious so do them as the chapter progresses in class. Use your notecard well and getting an A should not be difficult. Do the practice exams at least a week before the exam

I took Dr. Dutta for PHYS 1601 and took him again for 1602. His lectures were just as engaging, and the class is structured very similarly. I found this course's content to be significantly more difficult than that of 1601, so it took more work for me to earn my grade. Attending lectures is super important to understanding the content and problems.

dutta is AMAZING. test questions were all taken from slides and practice exams, so as long as you review those you're good. his lectures were easy to understand, and he was very willing to help and answer questions and always got so excited during his demos. would definitely take again and was definitely worth the 8 am.

Great lecturer that made tough physics concepts seem digestible. The masteringphysics can be annoying so do them as you progress through a chapter. Questions on exams were almost all pulled from slides, past and practice exams, and the homework (heavy emphasis on slides and past+practice exams). Use your notecard wisely and an a is very possible.

I loved Dutta! He made me love physics for the first time! So happy to teach and so gifted at teaching! I loved the real life applications! Super organized and you are solely tested on material off the slides and homework problems. It's time consuming to study for the tests, (dont wait until the night before!) but a B-A is achievable. Worth 8AM!!!

I have praised this man before and I'll do it again. One of the best profs on Vandy campus. He really cares, but the class 100% relies on the work that you put in. If he allows you one test drop for this class, by all means, rely on the third test as your drop. Don't mess up the other ones.
1602 is much more difficult than 1601 but the tests are either the hardest thing you've ever seen or the easiest. Much more calculus involved.

1602 is a different beast compared to 1601 with Dutta. Although he is a great professor, he purposely tries to trick you on some of the exams. The content in 1602 is generally harder than 1602 so try not to miss lectures. For exams, he takes questions from: 1.) the lecture slides, 2.) MasteringPhysics, and 3.) exams from previous years.

First time Dutta teaches this class. Clear explaination, and answer any questions during lecture. First test was hard with an average of 78% (with curve) but the 2nd mid term and final were much better. Despite having lots of homework, he gave generous extra credit.He even wrote a quantum story that is very accessible to non-majors.

Bless this man and his family. An outstanding lecturer who would have the most memorable physics demonstrations. You will never get a question on an exam that you haven't seen before (questions are pulled from Mastering Physics, lectures, and practice exams)

This class was very large, so professor Dutta put a lot of effort into making the lectures engaging and entertaining with in-class questions and demonstrations. The homework was relevant to the content and exams. I had already taken classes in high school with similar content, so it was very easy for me; not everyone shared this experience.

Dr. Dutta is amazing! He is very passionate about physics and helpful in office hours. The slide problems and mastering physics can seem overwhelming, but make sure you complete all of them. Attend lectures, it is easy to fall behind and not understand the content, it's fast paced. Take Dr. Dutta, he's the best!
take dutta if you can! by far the best physics prof for gen physics courses. explains concepts clearly and offers lots of help. workload is beyond manageable and he's also pretty funny
Good professor with excellent study material.

I love this man. Such a gem. Class isn't that hard if you've taken physics so I skipped a lot. When I did go to class tho I loved watching Dutta teach, you can tell he loves his job and cares about his students. Slide problems, mastering physics, and sample exams are your friends.

Professor Dutta is easily one of the most passionate teachers at Vanderbilt. He gives incredible lectures and really wants to see you succeed. However, the tests are challenging, though fair, and a very high weight of your grade. Use office hours and other resources and you will be fine. Definitely don't miss out on taking him, just study up.

Office hours are recorded on Zoom and posted for whole class. Very hard to work with to reschedule exam due to extenuating circumstances. That said, it is evident that he wants his students to succeed. Lectures are engaging and he gives real-world connections. Do the practice problems and watch his videos for clarification, and you will be fine.

Professor Dutta is excellent at explaining physics concepts and frequently uses demonstrations in class. Make sure to do ALL of the slide problems, as you will likely see a few on midterm exams. His office hours were helpful as well. The class has 3 midterms and a final. He grades everything on a slight curve.

i have never taken physics before. he cares and his lectures are nice. but i just wish he answered his questions on the slides or with the questions visible. i did not do the best but i feel like thats partly my fault. but if you have never taken physics before, it does get overwhelming and i feel like some steps could've been walked through more
Three midterms, one dropped. Final exam online. Annoying homework problems, overall not too difficult but not easy

Dr. Dutta has mastered the art of teaching. He explains concepts so well and is very engaging. Most challenging part of the class is all exams are multiple choice (so not a lot of leeway for missing questions if you want a high grade). However, most questions are from homework or slides, so go to class and review notes and you will do fine.
Just Don't. he's a good teacher but the worst professor
Very interesting lectures and very good professor
One of the best professors inside Vandy.

Professor Dutta might be the best teacher that I have ever had. He is an expert at making notoriously difficult concepts extremely clear. He is extremely knowledgeable of everyday applications of the physics concepts that were discussed in the class. Demonstrations were frequent and always applied directly to the material.

Professor Dutta makes a challenging physics course manageable. Engaging lectures, plenty of practice problems, and helpful office hours. Even if you're not math-inclined, the course is doable with diligent studying using resources like Unstuck ai. Overall, a great learning experience!

Professor Dutta is really good at explaining complicated physics concepts and equations. His tests are all easy to get high scores if you listen carefully on classes and do the homework (not heavy at all!). Recommend to anyone who want to study physics!

[PHYS 3200]. Great class! Started with a in-depth review of statistics, which was very helpful. The text was hard to follow, but Dutta's knack for clarifying difficult proofs helped a lot. Lectures were very engaging and full of fascinating stories about Stat Mech OG's. Problem sets were long but quite interesting. Learned a ton and had a blast!

Physics will always be a more challenging class, especially for those not as math-inclined, but Dr. Dutta makes it manageable. There is a lot of homework, but it is also manageable. Best thing to do to study for tests is use the practice test he provides. He does lots of demonstrations, and is overall a pretty funny guy. Would recommend for 1601.

Even though class is not mandatory, his lectures are really engaging and worth attending. The tests are hard because they are only multiple choice with no partial credit. You have to study hard to do well if you've never taken physics.

10/10 would recommend. took this last sem, amazing prof. taken for formality so it was easy but he made studying really fun. he started the semester by saying there won't be any extra credit and ended up giving around 7+ points of extra credit. basically all the tests had extra credit except the last midterm, so it's easy to end with over 100%

Dr. Dutta is AMAZING! Best Vandy professor I have ever had. This course is essentially just a faster, more difficult version of AP Physics, so if you've taken it, 1601 will be a breeze.
