Dr. Dutta is extremely helpful during office hours and curves exams. Lectures are ridiculously engaging, and he often covers exact exam problems, so don't skip!!
I love his lectures and the interesting demonstrations in class. You can easily get an A if you do all the problems on the slides and in the hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super, super nice professor and person in general. Very generous and fair grader for the exams. The exams consist of the homework and slide problems, so it is very easy to get an A or A+ in his class. His lectures are also very interesting and entertaining.

Professor Dutta has probably been my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He is funny and engaging which is helpful because lectures are important. Most of the tests are based on lecture questions or homework questions which makes them pretty straight forward. This class is a breeze if you've taken AP Physics and still very doable if you haven't.
GOAT Professor. Go to lectures and do the practice problems and it's an easy A. No curve, but each midterm is scaled an extra 7% and can drop 1 midterm. Final is online.
Introductory Physics is hard. But Prof. Dutta makes it fun and exciting. Lots of extra credit. Lots of work to do outside of class.

Prof Dutta is one of the best instructors I've had at Vandy. I can tell he's really passionate about the subject and teaches it really well. There's a lot of homework, but you get multiple attempts and he's really good about going over the problems during office hours. Test problems are often similar to problems he discussed in class.

Professor Dutta makes physics very enjoyable for his students and is good at keeping everyone's attention. However, all exams are 15 multiple choice questions, so every wrong answer (sometimes just choosing negative instead of positive or vice versa) is -7 points. Mastering physics takes forever and most of the problems were not taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: LOVED DR. DUTTA he was the best. He made physics really understandable and he was very accessible outside of class. He is a must have for physics! I am a pursuing a minor in physics because of him. 10/10.

Professor Dutta was simply the best option for PHYSICS. MAKE SURE TO TAKE HIM!!! His lectures are simple and he has a lot of demonstrations. Holds a lot of office hours and will work the problem out with you!!
Had to work really hard but feel like my IQ went up a few points

Attendance is not required, make sure to go to every class.  Dutta goes over examples in class that could be on exams, and he never posts the worked out examples.  Understand all examples and mastering physics well, as all exams are mc and are quite difficult with time constraints, making it very hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dutta is the best professor ever. As long as you go to the lectures, do all the slide problems, and mastering physics, you will do fine on the exam since he uses same problems. Lectures aren't mandatory but you have to go because the stuff he teaches is on the exam. No textbook. Drops lowest midterm. Great office hours & records it. Very clear.

Dutta is simply amazing!
Good lectures, fun demonstrations, office hours are amazing, etc.
Exams are multiple choice with a generous notes sheet policy.

Worth the 8 AM!
I had his 8 am Gen. Physics class, and honestly, his teaching made the class for me. He's so funny and also explains seemingly complicated topics with ease to help students understand them well.

He's a really good professor and can explain tough concepts well. He also went viral (search "me failing physics meanwhile my professor" on TikTok) which was fun. Downsides are the tests are all multiple choice and are worth a lot and can be quite tough. Upside is though that many questions are from slides and homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Though PHYS 1601 can seem daunting, Dutta made it incredibly doable. His tests are all multiple choice, but he curves each test grade. He also has an incredible formula sheet policy: you can bring sheets from past exams and end up with 4 full sheets for the final. Go to lecture, take good notes, and make thorough formula sheets and you'll be set.

physics isn't the most interesting subject, but prof. dutta made it fun. his lectures can be a bit slow at times (i was in the 8am so that might be why) but he explains things very very well and provides lots of resources outside of lectures as well.

Dutta is a great professor. His tests were in-person but he often gives extra points, and you get to drop your lowest midterm. His exams are easy if you keep up with the material and study the practice test. He sets you up for success. You will do well if you actually put in the work: definitely take Dutta!

Really solid choice for 1601. Not super exciting but pretty good teacher. Tests are a big part of your grade though and the multiple choice format is super unforgiving so study hard for those, but not too much homework and quizzes are pretty easy. Take him if you can.

With the tests now in person, I would not recommend taking Dutta. He definitely knows physics but he is condescending when you do not understand something and spends too much time in class on proofs instead of practice problems. He requires you to do too much out of class to succeed/understand and the homework was unnecessarily difficult.

I had Prof Dutta for 1601 and 1602 and I thought he was a great physics teacher and most likely your best option at Vandy. It is impossible to teach every aspect of the course in class and you have to learn the small details by doing the homework. But overall, the exams are straightforward and are based on homework and in-class problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, I really enjoyed this class. It took a few weeks for me to figure out how to succeed, but I got it down and did really well for the rest of the semester. All it takes is paying attention to the lectures (you'll see many similar problems from the lectures on the tests) and doing the homework. Dr. Dutta's office hours were a big help too.

Tips: I learned after taking both 1601/1602 that getting a good grade in this class comes down to having all the information ready in front of you went taking the test. I printed out all of the slide problems and made sure everything was organized and I improved significantly from 1601.

He is very kind and wants us to learn. My favorite part of his class was how he connected the concepts we were learning to the real world. My least favorite was that the tests are 14 multiple-choice questions, so if you make a few mistakes your grade drops a lot. If you pay attention to the slideshow problems and homework, they're not too bad.

His lectures are very good, but very fast. Homework is a lot of masteringphysics problems. There is no curve or extra credit, but if you do all the homework the exams are pretty reasonable. It's a big class so it can be difficult to get help on problems. He does come off as a bit intimidating, but he is thoroughly and completely fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Dr. Dutta. All exams are online, multiple choice, unproctored. This format is condusive to academic dishonesty and does little to prevent honor code violations. Also, there's no way to get partial credit by showing your work. The tests are 85% of the grade and there's no attendance grade (or any sort of buffer besides HW).

It is obvious Prof. Dutta is very intelligent and is very fascinated by physics, however, this class is very fast paced and leaves him little to no time to throughly teach the content, which often leads to lots of homework and not a lot of in class examples.

Class is really full so it's difficult to get individual attention unless you go to office hours, but Dr. Dutta handles it well. He always answers emails quickly, his lectures are clear, and he provides a lot of demos and examples. If you do the homework and understand example problems from lectures, you'll do really well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Dutta is one of the best professors I've had at Vandy. His lectures are very clear and his office hours were so helpful I didn't need to get a tutor. I didn't think I would like physics, but Dutta changed my mind!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Everything you need to know he'll explain in lecture super well and clearly. Homework takes forever and is pretty hard but most of the exam questions are taken straight from it. Exams are online but only 14 questions so if you get one wrong that's like 7% down. Dutta doesn't seem to care about his students, though, kind of mean and unavailable.

If you have to take physics take Dutta. His lectures and examples are very clear. Exams are MC and usually straightforward questions that are mostly from homework. The homework takes a long time though.

Dutta is super funny and very clear in lectures. He does demonstrations a lot (he rode across the room on a fire-extinguisher-powered bike once) and drops your lowest midterm. Very fair w/ his grading and accessible outside of class. Maybe avoid if multiple-choice questions are not your strength. Stay on top of hw and studying and you'll do well!

Do not take anyone else for PHYS 1601! Dutta is the absolute best. Lectures are very engaging; he does a demonstration almost every class and is very funny. Tests are open book online (all multiple choice), and he drops the lowest midterm.

Prof. Dutta's class is very straightforward. 3 tests (one gets dropped), 50 minutes, 14 questions, all multiple choice. Most of the questions are from the homework and his lectures. Tests are usually curved by a few points. As long as you understand the notes and how to do all of the homework problems this class shouldn't be too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Dutta is an incredible and very fair instructor. His lectures are clear and his tests are straightforward if you've understood the problems in class and on the homework. He also supplements the lectures with demonstrations...like a rocket cart that he rides across the classroom. If you need to take physics, take Dutta.

Dr. Dutta is an amazing lecturer, his method of teaching is great (he shows lots of real world examples with videos and demonstrations) and captivates you attention throughout the whole lecture. The only negative aspect of this class is that you only get 50 minutes to do the midterms, which didn't feel like enough time. Stay ontop of HW/PWP probs.

Prof. Dutta teaches fast, but he knows the material, his explanations are clear, and in-class demos are helpful. Exams are solely multiple-choice, but all open note with questions ripped from homework/class. Go to class but don't count on a lot of help from office hours. Overall, a much better choice than the other prof options!

I have not had a class that I felt was more fair. He tells you exactly how to prepare for the exams and you get a drop on your lowest one. His lectures are clear and have fun demos. So many exam questions are just taken from problems done in class, lecture slides, and homework problems. Go to class and actually do the problems and you're good.

Dr. Dutta is the best professor I've had at Vandy. He's passionate about physics and cares about students. Understand problems from lectures and homework well, and you'll do well on tests. He also drops the lowest midterm grade. I hated physics in high school, and was dreading it in college, but now it's one of my favorite subjects as a pre-med.

reviews.comment: Great prof! Really cares about making sure his students understand the material. Easy to access after class and during office hours. Extremely organized. Test questions are based on the slide problems and Mastering Physics, so do those and you'll do great. Most of the grade is tests, but you get to drop one midterm. Really nice dude.

Dr. Dutta is the best. He makes a hard class fun and is super passionate. Just make sure you start the MasteringPhysics HW ahead of time and go to office hours if you can't do some of it. Midterms are online, open note, not proctored. 14 MC very similar to class problems and HW. Go to class even if it's just for the demonstrations.

reviews.comment: Dutta is great. Awesome demonstrations in class. Very fun guy who enjoys teaching Physics. Watching lecture in class is good, but also reading the textbook will help solidify the knowledge. Don't fall behind in Mastering Physics

reviews.comment: The classic teaching-an-intro-course-might-as-well-make-it-fun college prof. Professor Dutta makes the Physics 1602 material really manageable. He moves quickly in his lectures, but stops to do cool demonstrations occasionally. Best physics professor I ever had. His exams are basically the same as the homework and in-class questions.

Dutta is amazing and made a dull intro physics class way more fun than it should have been. Always super accessible and helpful with my questions. Dr. Dutta is so nice and willing to help. The exams were challenging but very much like the class examples/homework. Make sure you keep up with the material and do not leave the homework until the last minute and you'll be fine. If you have to take PHYS 1601, take him.

reviews.comment: His tests are pretty difficult and all multiple choice, aka no partial credit. If you pay attention in lectures and study you'll be fine.

reviews.comment: Great choice for physics, really cares about you learning the content and has lots of office hours that are so helpful for problem solving questions. Dr. Dutta is THE BEST! Even though the class wasn't easy, I'm so glad he made me work through the problems and was always available to help understand concepts because I did really well on the physics portion of the MCAT and I owe it all to him! Take his class if you want to actually understand physics and handle any problem on the MCAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Super sweet and hilarious. I wish I had him in a normal semester, zoom classes with Dutta doesnt do him justice. Tests are 14 MC - difficult, but doable. Based off concepts in class. It's possible to recover, started with a C, recovered to an A. Watch all lectures and do all the homework.

There are so many excellent reviews here that this one seems unnecessary. However, I would like to reiterate that Dr. Dutta explains concepts extremely clearly and with real life examples. This class is accessible to everyone, including those who are not STEM majors. You also don't need to be good at math contrary to what you may think.
Great teacher. If you have somewhat of a brain you'll get an A. I showed up to class every day and paid attention and somewhat studied and I literally got above a 100 in the class. Take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dutta is hilarious and his class is very fair. It's not even worth taking Physics with anyone other than Dutta.

Truly an amazing guy. Knows his stuff in and out, and takes his lectures seriously but not too seriously. He even makes an effort to learn names in a lecture hall of 100+. He has a great teaching style, and is always there to help his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dutta is the best intro science prof hands down. Super sweet guy, gives very clear and engaging lectures. His class is VERY fair, if you put the work in and pay attention in class you will do well. Test questions are very similar to practice exams, so if you have old exams too you are set. Do anything you can to take physics with him.

Dr. Dutta is a great professor and has a great reputation among students; he is a really clear in lectures, but you still need to do a lot of independent HW and studying to do well, cramming will not work

If you can, TAKE PHYSICS WITH DR. DUTTA! He's one of the kindest and funniest professors I've ever had - so willing to meet with you outside of class and go over problems in office hours. Lectures are SO HELPFUL - even though attendance isn't mandatory, DON'T SKIP. Tests are all multiple choice, and usually straight from the homework problems.

Dr. Dutta is a great instructor; he is very good at explaining physics and is super accessible when you get stuck. The class is a lot of work, and keeping up is key. You should work on physics about once a day if possible to succeed.

Dutta!! This man is the best professor I have ever had. He is pure genius and is just incredible at explaining material. He really wants his students to understand and has frequent office hours where he makes sure to explain in careful detail whatever your question is. Do not pass up the chance to have him as your professor.

Dutta is really good at explaining the content but the tests are unfair. Only 3 of them and they are all 14 questions so one little mistake can cost you a letter grade in the class. That being said, you know what to expect going into them and he does drop your lowest exam so he's there to help. Dutta is probably your best option in this department

I am a physics god so I thought it was an easy A, in fact I even got a 100. I won the international physics olympiad for 9 years straight so I thought it was kind of easy but I still had to work hard #dutta4pres2020
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Dutta is the best science professor I've ever had at Vanderbilt. Go to lectures - he explains difficult concepts in the book extremely clearly. 3 tests, all MC which makes it impossible for partial credit. Final grade is mainly the tests and final - there is no curve at end. Lectures are essential to doing well - go to class and you'll probably do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

Dr. Dutta is one of the best physics professors at Vanderbilt. Try to take him by any means. He wants his students to succeed and is very helpful in doing so!

reviews.comment: Dutta is the man and by far one of the best professors I've had in my short time here at Vanderbilt. His lectures are easy to understand and if you pay attention in that class and do just a little extra work outside, you will get the grade you want. #Dutta4President2020

Dutta is probably one of the best profs I've had at Vanderbilt. Problems are explained pretty thoroughly in class, and if you do all the problems in the powerpoint, exams are doable and fair. I highly recommend Dutta over all other prof. For you pre-meds, take 1601 with Dutta over any other professor for 1501. Make sure you do all the Mastering Physics problems and problems on the slides. reviews.comment: Dr. Dutta is a great lecturer. There's a lot of material to cover but he explains it well and is accessible if you need him. There's a big grade cushion with the homeworks and having a drop test is nice too.

Professor Dutta is so funny. He tries to show some cool videos sometimes to make lectures more interesting. He does clicker questions, so go to class!! Easily the best professor I've had so far at Vandy. He goes out of his way to make his lectures engaging and actually cares about his students' learning. His tests are pretty fair (doing the homework and reading the slides will get you a good grade). I highly recommend him.

Dr. Dutta easily earned his reputation for being the best Gen Phys professor. His lectures were clear and easy on the eyes, though take note that he will pass some examples for the sake of time. Very funny guy, passionate about physics. Class is exceedingly fair, and old tests are available online to study from, which is great because questions are often repeated.

Dutta is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. I had never taken physics before, but Dutta is such an great lecturer that I was able to understand the concepts and keep up with the rest of the class. Dutta is a fantastic lecturer, truly one of the best I've had. He explains concepts very well and clearly loves the material. reviews.comment: Dutta is awesome. He is really great at explaining physics and making hard concepts seem easy. He also gives a lot of extra credit through tests. He is also really helpful and nice during office hours. He even gave us brownies on the last day! One of the best profs I've had.

Dr. Dutta is amazing. Probably the most organized professor at Vanderbilt. His lectures are clear and easy to follow and he is great at explaining physics. The content is not difficult, but show up to class to see how he works out the tough questions. Very generous with extra credit. I got a 107, 74, 67, and 100 on his three midterms and got an A.

This class ranges in difficulty based on your prior physics experience. I had only taken algebra based physics in high school so all of the material I had learned before was easy for me but when it got to the new material it was very challenging. If you go to class and do your work you'll be fine. Dr. Dutta is very nice and very funny.

If you have any Physics background this class is very easy, as it only goes into the basics in each section covered. Additionally, the test questions are always the easier versions of the concepts discussed, and almost every test question is either from prior tests, the homework, or a clicker question in class. Dutta explains everything needed well

Professor Dutta makes every one of his lectures entertaining and engaging. His tests are fairly straightforward and he his lenient on his free-response grading. He's terrible in lectures, never finishes problems he starts

Dr. Dutta gives really helpful lectures, and if you keep up with the homework and make sure you understand everything you'll do fine. reviews.comment: He is very passionate about what he teaches and makes sure that we understand the material conceptually, and thoroughly. I had never enjoyed Physics as much as I did in this class. reviews.comment: He's sassy, and it's a huge lecture, and he calls people out during lecture for talking. The material is hard, he goes fast, and we just don't learn the correct things for lab. I was unsure if I still wanted to major in physics after taking 1901, but taking a class with Dutta absolutely made me want to continue. He is very, very (very) passionate about physics and often deviates from the material to talk about miscellaneous physics things, but always makes it interesting. He's also really funny.

One of the best teachers at Vanderbilt and probably best in Physics department. Challenging class but if you follow along in lectures and know how to work all the problems he shows in class and on the homework, you can get an A with no prior experience. If you have the chance to take him, take him, simple as that. Also, he does lift.

Dutta is the man. He's super into helping his students. People may be scared by him not curving anything, but he goes out of his way to make sure that as long as you're as invested in learning as he is in teaching, you'll get plenty of points thrown your way. Getting over 100 is definitely possible. Also this guy lifts

He probably responds faster than your significant other when you send him an email. You don't have to come to class all the time but the lectures are really interesting and inspirational. Do all the homework and make a real effort to understand physics rather than just try to plug in the numbers, then you can get more than 100%.
Dr. Dutta clearly cares about his students and wants them to learn. He does a very good job with explaining difficult concepts and is helpful during office hours. Tests are fair.

I loved Dr. Dutta. Very inspiring. Lots of hw, but not as difficult tests as everyone says. Yeah, they are still pretty hard (esp free response), but it's pretty fair based on how much you know. he grades out of 50, when the actual test is out of 55 (if you get 45/55, then he "curves" as if it's 45/50). Our all-multiple choice final was pretty easy
The tests are hard. Do the Wiley BEFORE the week of the test (at least 3 days in advance) and go over it a bit each day leading up to each test.

Professor Dutta is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is extremely good at teaching and despite having very little time to teach so much content, manages to do so successfully. Very interested in making sure he is doing everything to help students learn. HW isn't too hard. The tests are pretty reasonable. Final was very easy.

I breezed through physics 1 at vanderbilt, but had a very very difficult time with passing physics II with professor dutta. The material is much harder. Professor Dutta is extremely helpful outside of class, but his test are very very difficult. Dont take dutta unless you are obsessed with physics.

WileyPlus is horrible and will quickly become the bane of your existence, especially the weekly quizzes, but they are good practice for the tests. He tries to remember the names of everyone in the class, which never actually works, but it's a nice touch. You get to drop one test, so the grades aren't as low as it sounds. Go to office hours.
Great professor. Had to work really hard though!

Physics is hard. DON'T try to take it unless 1) you abosolutely have to 2) you are crazily obssessed with it just like Dr. Dutta is. The class is hard, dry and requires tons of work put into it (but you can't blame it all on Dr. Dutta). Textbook is kind of necessary because you won't learn much in class. He gives out extra credits so take them.

physics in general is a tough subject, he was way better than my 116a teacher. wish i had kept up with the homework because once you fall behind the wheels really come off the bus. besides dropping 1 of 3 exams, he doesnt have extra curving. strict grader (u cannot fake short answer trust me), but final was fair w repeat questions from exams

I never write reviews, but I wanted to let other students know how amazing this professor was! Dr. Dutta was really helpful during office hours, very patient, and made the subject more interesting. You will have to put in A LOT of time on the  homework, but it's worth it for the tests. I never thought I would get an A in physics! Great professor!

I am not sure why this guy is teaching at Vanderbilt. Plenty of WileyPlus homework that is not useful. DO NOT TAKE

gives no partial credit, doesn't curve anything, very poor teaching skills, entire class is clueless, feigns that he cares about each individual by trying to memorize names while he gives exams that average in the 40-60's.

Physics is like hell for me and professor Dutta makes it worse. POP QUIZE+RANDOMLY CALL PEOPLE TO ANSWER QUESTIONS+TONS OF HW. But he is pretty helpful, illustrates questions clearly but the questions are soooo hard. I spent almost 2h everyday on it.

Wonderful class. Dr. Dutta absolutely loves physics and was ecstatic to discuss it beyond the scope of the course. Clear lectures, lightning fast email response. Tests were 5 free response each. Partial credit is stingy but extra credit 8-20 pts every test. Generally an awesome guy! Homework's extensive, online and Powerpoint Problems.

Sourish is the best lecturer I have had at Vandy. He made every topic covered in 121 (basically faster paced 116) crystal clear. He was always excited to help students. He gives homework that is due on the day of the test. Tests are tough but fair. If you understand the material, you can get a 100. If you dont, you can easily get a 50.

Great professor, very helpful, answers emails promptly, has office hours daily and review sessions before the tests. He drops a test and keeps only your highest two which helps a lot in the end. I took this class over the summer, it was an excellent choice for physics. I'd highly recommend Dutta!!!
Great experience taking 116A over the summer. highly recommended!
Great guy! Helpful in and outside of class. Totally approachable. Knows the subject very well.

I've always hated physics, but it wasn't too bad with this professor. Assigns a take-home problem every day, and uses Wiley Plus for HW. I wish he showed more demo's in class though.

like so difficult. graded notes every lesson, but unfortunately the most interesting class ive taken so far. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class was extremely hard for a 1000-level writing class, but Prof Dubilet really cares about helping students improve their writing. Go to office hours!
At first I was a little intimidated by Alex, but he's actually a great guy. I really enjoyed this class and Alex is always willing to help. I would definitely take this class again.

Alex is a great professor! He expects the best from you and requires you to be well prepared for discussions, but as a result you become a much better writer/analytical thinker. He is extremely intelligent and overall a great guy.

CSET2560 Science for Supervillains. Dr. Durst is a great professor; the other reviews for 2550 are not true. im not really sure what anyone on here is talking about. I took science for supervillians, and he was a very kind a caring professor during this time. This class is genuinely awful. No consistent grading and piss poor communication.Unnecessarily low graders.
The professor has no proper grading criteria. He does not care about your well being. If you want to save your gpa i dont recommend this class.

He's a great professor. I'm sure all the other reviews are from people who didn't  actually show up to class because he was clear about homework and was always ready to clarify any questions and explain exactly what's expected.

(For CSET2500). Ironically, there was not effective communication from the professor to the students regarding reliable grading criteria, attendance policies, and expectations for the class. You can tell he's passionate about the class, but it's not a very effective class for learning anything or doing anything else than getting a science credit.
Creepily stares at you during class until you answer. He talks about his opinion too much. Harsh grader for absolutely no reason.

This is NOT a communications based class as advertised (despite the professor saying there is little science). The prof does a poor job communicating material, very slow grader, and unhelpful with questions. This class was not hard to do well in, but felt hard based on the lack of instruction, information, communication, and guidance.

Seemed kind of checked out from the class at times, very disorganized. I'm not sure why this class is in the CSET department because there was very little on the communication of science, and the vast majority of the class was on the science itself. Extremely slow grading.

VAGUE hw instructions, tough grader, disorganized, posts grades months (& lecture slides days) late, syllabus has no assignment deadlines on it--he chose due dates randomly (except w/weekly reflections) no latework/absence policy so u don't know how these issues impact your grade if an emergency occurs. Low workload but class structure WILL get you

Incredibly disorganized. Hard grader for, quite literally, no reason (and to make matters worse, you won't know that grade until two weeks before the semester ends). Nice guy, but un-inspiring lecturer. Easy-ish MNS credit, but something about this class and his expectations/assignments led to constant frustration. Take oceanography instead.

Dusan is amazing. One of the nicest professors I've ever had. Even not coming from a sciency backround this course was very interesting. The course was lecture heavy so as a note taker myself I enjoyed jotting everything down. We would do lectures M/W and discussions on Fridays where I quickly learned how knowlagable Would 100% take again.

Dusan is a great person, and his class is very interesting. If you do not pay attention in class, you will not learn anything and will be lost on the assignments. He is a very fair grader, and there are two papers and one other assignment across the entire semester. He is extremely smart, and it shows. Be sure to ask him a lot of questions.

super chill professor, lecture heavy but not much work outside of class except 1 assignment that he gives over 1 month to turn in. other than that, relatively easy (if you come to class and pay attention even a little bit) take home midterm and take home final. super caring about students and learns everyone's names and background very quickly.

He's lecture-heavy, which is great for note-takers. Jotting down the main ideas will ensure a perfect exam score. His classes are structured this way, possibly due to his physics background. His Galileo class was particularly interesting in understanding modern science because he presented a unique perspective. Thank you

2nd time taking Danilovic and once again, very easy course, lectures could sometimes be boring but everything was super simple. workload was also really light. barely thought about it until exam time, and even then, if you showed up to class, everything was self-explanatory. still felt like I learned a lot. def take if looking for an easy A

His accent is very hard to understand. Class is also very dry and boring. He doesn't make any effort to engage with students. He makes you buy blue books for class. There are much better professors at Vanderbilt for communication courses.
Really wants to teach and make the class engaging; really wants students to get best grades; lectures can be a boring; tests are sometimes very difficult.

It became clear to me about 2 weeks into this class that Dusan is the smartest professor I have ever had. His passion for this subject matter is effortless, and his knowledge is immense. He can recite in perfect detail the history of modern Europe with no notes in front of him which is breathtaking to see in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is probably one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. Dr. Danilovic truly enjoys teaching AND learning from others on a variety of topics (it pays to talk to him after class). The grade is made up of two papers and one presentation that requires you to read two novels. It's not too much work unless you leave it to the last minute.

Would not take again. Lecture and slides are hard to follow. Lots of grading discrepancies with TAs. Get questions for exams beforehand, although not clear with what is wanted. If any concerns regarding the class, difficult to get a response or dismissed directly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, class material is not that difficult. Make sure to actually read the lecture slides. Only issue: the TA tends to grade very differently from the professor which is good and bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: fun professor, he try to make the class less boring by making jokes sometimes- can be hillarious or not- it doesnt matter cause at the end of the day attendence isnt mandatory. He gave out 10 possible exams question for each midterms so just memorize all of the answer and you should be good.

Dusan is a king. Very silly guy, loves astronomy, tries his best to make it interesting. He goes off on random tangents in lectures which can be super funny or mind numbingly boring. Pop quizzes, none are dropped. Tests seem easy but the grading is all over the place and u never know what u will score even if u know the content.

Danilovic is one of my favorite profs thus far. He is knowledgeable and passionate about the material and it shows in lecture, which I actually looked forward to despite expecting to hate this class because I am not a science oriented person at all. He is funny, nice, and even remembers names if you go to class enough and says hi outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dusan is a quirky fun guy who really knows what he's talking about. Sometimes lectures are a little confusing, but he is willing to explain things to you 1:1. 10 pop quizzes with just 1 question and 3 exams which he guives you all the questions before. Although big grading discrepancies between him vs TAs who are a lot harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Danilovic tries to teach. Personally, I do not like his lecture slides. Moreover, I get that he tries to be fair and gives all the questions in advance. This makes the class apparently easy. However, the TA's grade super harshly. Depending on who's grading your tests, you will either get an A or a B. People do try in this class and still do bad

Dusan is awesome and so funny. He is also very knowledgable and considers students' questions very thoughtfully. If you're looking for an easy lab & class, this is the one. Attendance isn't mandatory but there is a pop quiz every week on the material. Super lax class, midterms and final are simple for the most part. no hw ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't miss class. Dusan gives no homework -- take his class trust.

Dusan is a great professor and I loved his astronomy course. All the material was super interesting and he obviously loves and cares about the material. All the tests he gave us the questions before hand and I never stressed about work. He does give difficult pop quizzes every week but if you were there you instantly got 50% would take again.

Professor Danilovic is a great guy and is very knowledgeable. He makes it easy to schedule office hours and I would suggest utilizing them. He gives you the potential test questions so scheduling meetings with him to discuss the questions is important. One of my favorite professors I have had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Danilovic is amazing, and people that complain are perhaps not showing up to lecture or not putting in the very doable amount of work to get a good grade on the exams (he literally gives you the possible questions beforehand, all you have to do is prepare). He is incredibly passionate about astronomy and genuinely cares about his students.

Religiously read TB, took notes, went to every lecture. Class was still hard af. Heard other professor teaching astronomy was pretty chill and much ezier. The pop quizzes are ridiculous and exams are difficult. Wish slides and lectures were much more useful in which professor gives more info on what we should study. Overall: :(

He's clearly very passionate about astronomy. However, his lectures are quite dense and disorganized. Multiple choice on tests sometimes feels like random trivia from class, so pay attention. He does give you the prompts to the FRQs beforehand. A few homework assignments which are free points. Very open to student feedback.

chegg is practically a necessity if you want to get through the homeworks in any reasonable amount of time. Pretty bad/unremarkable lecturer too. Often was at least 5 minutes late to class. Assigns way too much homework. Only upside is his tests are pretty easy. Take Dutta instead

Prof. Danilovic is a very caring professor. His lecture is clear and the sample questions on the slides are similar to the exam question. I've taken AP Physics before and take this class solely for AXLE lab credit, so Mastering Physics is very unnecessary for me. Homework is boring and TOO MUCH for the second half of the semester.

Nice guy, awful professor. He assigns way more homework than he thinks he does, and the homework is HARD. If you do it honestly, it will take you about 10-20 hours a week--cheating is pretty mandatory to get through the homework. Tests are super easy if you know the content fairly well though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest tests ever, but give the most insane amount of useless HW ever. You will get an A. You will hate every minute of his boring lectures and the 5 HOURS of mastering physics assigned EVERY WEEK. He doesn't understand what is good for his students. 40% of the grade was HW and the tests were so easy, which sounds nice in theory, but it is hell.

Any of his CSET courses (not astr) are fantastic. He is a feminist, liberal, personable, and so fricking funny. The course structure is mostly lectures and papers, very very minimal work. One or two papers/projects for the entire semester and you do not need to take notes. He is extremely underrated and deserves more love!

Class Taken: CSET 3890  [not an option on here]
Professor Danilovic is the most interesting, engaging, thoughtful, and compassionate professor I have had at Vanderbilt University. To succeed in his class: attend classes, be transparent about your workload and other deadlines, time management, submit your best work :). P.S: Talk to him after class

Professor Danilovic is very passionate about astronomy and makes his students want to be passionate, but with his dense, unorganized lectures and overly hard tests, it's hard to be passionate. Not good at giving feedback and helping people prepare for the exams. Goes on random tangents and if you miss one thing he says, you risk failing. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Danilovic is phenomenal. He expects that you work on the homework problems assigned and correspondingly are ready to ask questions in class. Although, he might be a boring lecturer at times, he does not force attendance and really cares for his students. Just make sure to reach out to him outside of class for extra help to build a connection.

Tbh this course let me know that Astronomy is not for me. His lectures were hard to follow and boring. Dusan is a nice guy and you can tell that he really cares about the subject but I think he fails to realize that the majority of the class is only there for AXLE. Tests are hard but doable. Don't recommend but good luck if you do take

Tests were hard if you didn't write down every word he said in lecture -- otherwise, fairly easy. Danilovic is a sweetie and really wanted all of us to succeed. A nice curve at the end, too, and he loves it when people show up to lectures. (Bonus: if you go often enough, he starts to remember you and says hi when you run into him around campus.)

I highly recommend this professor to ANYONE at Vanderbilt. This was by FAR the best professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. Very intellectual, cares about students, etc!

P.S. Ignore the bad reviews, these are essentially students who did not work with the professor to improve their grade OR never attended lecture OR just didn't try.

*I took MATH1301 not ASTR1010* Lectures are just him reciting definitions, theorems, and example problems from the textbook. His handwriting is hard to read. Sometimes you do 1 section of the textbook, other days you do 5. Very particular about grading exams (-1 point for missing abs val bars while working on exams, etc.) Exam Qs from textbook/hw.

Professor Dusan is WONDERFUL. I would highly recommend taking his class, all you need to do (like any college course at Vanderbilt) is to study for the tests. He gives you 30% of the test before the exam so you already know 30% of the material on it. I would recommend attending all of his lectures.

Professor Dusan deeply cares about his students.
avoid this class

The subject matter in astronomy can be a bit daunting, but I can really tell he cares about what he is teaching and makes an effort to prepare us for the tests. Barely any homework or work outside of class. The tests are not bad at all, mostly just information from lectures and if you read the textbook they will be easier as well.

Professor Dunlap may be the most disorganized and unprepared professor I've ever had. He seemingly was not prepared to teach the class, is an incredibly boring lecturer, and the structure of the class was disorganized to the point where half our cohort has complained to the dean. I do not recommend him as a lecturer or professor.
Lectures are boring but he tries his best. Its Patho. Review your notes, fill in the holes with Kahn Academy and youll be fine.
Good professor
No Comments

Tests on things that are kinda specific but he does a great job on telling you what to expect on the exams. Manageable amount of homework (5 response papers throughout the year) and grade is mainly comprised of 2 exams and 4 speeches. Not the toughest grader on speeches if you can show that you prepared beforehand. Super nice professor. Recommend

Do not take this class if you want an A. The grading is primarily exams and speeches. The speeches are pretty easy but he doesn't believe in A+ so a perfect speech can never get a "perfect" grade. Exams are so hard for reasons people already mention but the worst part is there aren't many questions so if you get 1 wrong your exam grade is cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great class set-up (often ends early), genuinely good guy and cares for his students, always willing to talk about grades or even just about life, is kinda a harsh grader, but has enough filler points for making an A still very attainable

Professor Wood was absolutely terrific. I understand he made adjustments compared to last year's class, and I am thrilled to say those improvements were absolutely phenomenal. I genuinely enjoyed this class, be it manageable homework, fun speeches, or engaging class activities. I couldn't recommend this class any higher.

This was the only class not for one of my majors this semester and ended up being my hardest. Wood has really high expectations for speeches, very strict on late work, and makes impossible exams containing incredibly niche things he mentioned only once or small details from videos watched in class. Way harder of a course than it should be. Avoid

Professor Wood is great at teaching public speaking. There are quite a few projects and he grades super fair. Classes are pretty boring when they aren't speaking days, but generally not too bad. He grades pretty soft on the presentations most times, but the exam is hard if you don't read the textbook which is otherwise unnecessary in this course.

I don't know how a communication class with Professor Wood ended up being harder than my engineering courses, but it did. You have to memorize every word he ever says, and the questions barely connect to what we learned. Somehow, I spent more time studying for that class than all my others combined, and I still left every test feeling confused.

OMG, this class was a nightmare! The professor is a super hard grader, and even if you're a great communicator, you'll fail if you don't memorize every little detail about random theories of organizational structure. Like, how does knowing four theories help me write an email? 😤
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs!!!! Seems like a good man but the class is ridiculously hard for no reason. Get ready to memorize a bunch of stuff you'll forget the next day. My worst grade since freshman year and it was probably the easiest class lol

This guy seems nice at first. But his grading criteria is terrible. I mean, he is a masterclass in making a terrible exam, and the exams are a huge portion of the class. Any little detail, any little tangent, it can all be on the exams. Go for a bathroom break? Hope he doesn't choose that small 5 minute period you missed. No, he won't help you.

Good professor and a very nice guy. Tests are impossible and must remember every minor detail from his lecture and test questions are on things we could have discussed for less than a minute in class. He does not post study guides or notes but does give relatively good grades on papers.

First com class at Vandy and not what I expected. Super nice guy with good lectures, you have to remember every word for exams so take good notes. Participation matters and not super understanding. Makes up for it with papers and feedback. You will learn a lot from him and the class is super interesting but can be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Everyone, make sure you do not take this professor. I have now taken him in two classes, and those two classes are ironically the only two C's I have had at Vanderbilt. His exams are incredibly unfair to the students. I have nothing against him, but I am trying to be as direct as possible. Do not take his classes if you want to have a high GPA.

Incredibly engaging class but unfortunately the >50% of class time you spend on great discussions doesn't count for anything because participation isn't graded and exams/essays don't touch on it. Must write down every word he says in class to do well on exams because there's no study guide, no slides and the obscure stuff will be on the test.

I took the first amendment class with Wood and it was by far the hardest class I've taken at Vandy. Any detail from the textbook could be on the exams. The class average for the exams was in the C range. You get to makeup points with essays though. The class is basically only lecture, and you're super behind if you miss a day. He's nice though!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is for CMST 3050. Prof is fine as a lecturer but there are 3 exams and they are unjustifiably difficult. He will write a question on legitimately ANYTHING that leaves his mouth during lecture and you have to be accountable for everything. There are no study guides for the test, there is no review day, no slides posted, nothing so good luck.

Gives clear grading criteria and is pretty lenient when it comes to speech grades, as long as you hit all the points in the criteria. Grades fast (usually same day) and his lectures mostly come from the textbook. The exam is almost impossible to do well on, so do well on speeches and try to study textbook and lecture notes leading up to exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I take Wood's classes whenever I can. Tests are notoriously difficult but As are possible if you memorize what he says in lectures. If you miss class often the tests get very hard. Generous with curves at the end of the semester. Interesting and engaging lectures, you'll leave the class actually having learned something.
Best professor ever. The course is designed to make you want to drop it at the beginning, but it gets so much better as the semester progress. Plus, Professor Wood's curve is very generous.
Very good intro class, I don't really know why people give him such a low rating. He literally curves two letter grades.

After reading reviews on rate my professor I was scared to take this class, but it turns out that his tests are not atrocious. Lectures are very interesting. Just memorize the terms he goes over in class and you'll get As on the exams. I highly recommend.

I've taken two classes w Wood, so here's what I've gotten; class material is interesting, non-exam grades are normally easy As, but the exams are atrocious. With this class, follow the speech outline and memorize your speeches, you'll be fine. The final is awful and there's nothing you can do about it, so use your speeches to cushion your grade.

In the grand scheme, this course is pretty easy but it's one of the classes that if you shove it off for later it'll make your life harder. Attendance is mandatory and will kill your grade if you don't come. There's nothing on the boards in class and everything he says in class will be on the tests. Focus on class time rather than reading the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just not good. Doesn't let student do actual public speaking.

Sticks by a very stringent speech outline that leaves little room for students personality in speeches. Grades are detracted from 100% instead of added meaning it is difficult to get a good grade unless you go strictly by formula which does not always create the best speeches. Textbook was mind numbingly wordy and rudimentary. Huge time commitment
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fun public speaking class. In general, the class did not require much work day to day but there were 2 minor and 3 major speeches that required lots of preparation. As long as you prepare enough you'll do fine and there is pretty clear grading criteria. Final was hard but was generally just memorization. Great guy and made class fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you are looking for an intro level, easyish communication class, don't take 1002 because his tests are really hard to do well on. His classes are fun but you really have to grind hard for the tests and the results are often not worth the time.

Dustin wood is a great guy and really cares about his students. The speeches are all really fun, and not too difficult to do well on. The on drawback is that his final exam is extremely specific and irrelevant. He takes very esoteric one-liner facts out of the textbook and expects you to remember them - basically wants you to memorize textbook.
Great professor- makes the class fun while challenging you to think critically. It's easy to do well as long as you follow the assignment instructions. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Wood is very passionate about this material and it shows through his lectures. While class was always engaging, tests are impossible. It is incredibly frustrating when the grade does not reflect what you have learned. Additionally, I missed one day of class for my 21st and it cost me a letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took CMST 1500 with him this past spring, and he is by far one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. He gives out A's like they are nothing, yet he inspires all his students to work hard and become better public speakers. Make sure you pay attention to the grading criteria closely, and if you do, you should definitely be on your way to an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Wood's class. His slides did not have very much info on them, so be prepared to take a lot of notes. I had to be typing the entire time, but he is a good lecturer so I was always engaged. The syllabus is detailed and he is very accessible outside of class. I will definitely be taking more classes with him in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't think this professor understands that this is an intro class. His tests are extremely hard. Not only is most of it short answer, but some of the questions are from the smallest details that he mentions during lectures, and the amount of information you need to know is absurd. Don't take this class if you have a choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wood was a very tough and subjective grader in that he took off points for items that the thinks you should have added to make it stronger even though you adequately answered the prompt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't know how this guy got a job at Vanderbilt. He's very opinionated and refuses to admit when he's wrong. His "quizzes" are made up of minutia no one could remember. He specifically said students would not need to memorize dates for a quiz, yet dates made up 20% of that quiz. His attempts to be "hip" are cringeworthy and he is often very rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Public speaking is a great class to take (unless it's online kinda lost it's purpose cuz of corona). Woods a nice guy we had good class conversations and he's a pretty easy grader. As long as you put in some effort and follow directions you'll be fine. There is a final exam so make sure you take notes during the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class, not too much work. Speeches aren't hard, and he's an pretty laid-back grader and prof overall. Lots of class discussion (not graded, but interesting). Solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dustin Wood is an interesting lecturer. I genuinely enjoyed going to his class; it was extremely engaging and interactive. However, his exams are impossible. He covers a fraction of the info on them in class, making it imperative you do the readings in great depth. I had never in my life failed an exam until this class. No study guides either.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wood is very accessible and friendly both inside and outside classrooms, though he is very very attentive to details and nitpicky. I work SO HARD and you don't always get rewards (grade wise) regarding your efforts put in. He is responsible and helpful overall, and I do learned a lot. It was frustrated to work hard without getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Really cares about his students and rewards hard work. Lots of the info taught feels very common sense, making tests feel kinda difficult and odd to study for (they aren't bad though, like other CMST tests). Provides clear expectations for speeches and usually lets you use whatever speaking notes you want. Most straightforward CMST prof I've taken.
The exams weren't difficult if you put in effort to study and the speeches are fairly graded. Your grade truly reflects how much work you put in.

Wood has the most nitpicky details on exams I've seen. After explicitly stating years of court cases did not need to be known, the most valuable question on our midterm had - you guessed it - years of court cases. Despite assigning copious readings, he expects students to memorize the most insignificant things. Textbooks also ludicrously expensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wood is very nice and receptive to his students, but mostly teaches intro level comm studies classes. Because of this, you would expect some level of easiness compared to upper level classes which he does not afford. Other reviews say don't expect an A and I have to agree with that completely. Not much hw, but expect extremely hard tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Wood is very receptive during his office hours. I literally come in at random times during office hours, and he is always willing to have a short chat. He is very helpful both inside and outside the classroom. I learned so much in this class. He made me want to be a Communications major! I'm so glad to have him as my professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wood is at times passive-aggressive, and is generally not open to discuss much during office hours, but is a great speaker and knows how to teach speechmaking. I became a much better public speaker and his feedback helped, but his "quizzes" made up huge parts of the grade and were based on minutia in large readings. Very tough to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great guy, class is always interesting and my public speaking has really improved- definitely take Wood, just don't expect an A because it won't happen.

Super interesting guy who makes class easy to look forward to.  Consists of three big speeches and two smaller ones that make up most of the grade.  Two quizzes that are very hard and nit-picking.  Very tough to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The quizzes are deceivingly hard. They're more like exams because they are sheer memorization and regurgitation of textbook and in class material. He is super nice and class is interesting, but it is difficult to get an A in the class.

I absolutely loved Professor Wood's public speaking class. His lectures are engaging, he truly cares about his students and gives great feedback. This was one of the best classes I've taken at Vanderbilt and I highly recommend taking it with Professor Wood. Make sure you study for the 2 quizzes- they are more difficult than you expect.

Have learned SO much about the judicial system and 1st Amendment. Class discussions were engaging and Prof. Wood does a good job of relating topics to current events. That said, as someone new to reading cases and law-texts, I initially found the reading assignments to be dense and hard to parse through. Tests are tough so prepare to study hard.

Prof Wood was by far the best,  and most dynamic professor I had this semester. He did a great job of varying his teaching styles and keeping class interesting. He also did a great job of creating a constructive and collaborative class culture, which I found greatparticularly in a class where public speaking is key. I'd take another class w/ him.

His senior seminar was the hardest class I have ever taken at vanderbilt. the reading was dense and boring and his tests consisted of memorizing minute details of over 150 court cases. Avoid this class at all costs.

A lot of work for a 100-level class, but your speaking skills will noticeably improve.  Really pay attention to lectures and readings if you want to get above a C on exams.  Speech topics are personal choice and his grading criteria is extremely clear, but he grades harshly for source bias and grammar.

Wood is such a nice professor. Definitely wants to relate to his students and make them passionate about the material. Only drawback is that he's not as charismatic of a lecturer as others in the department, but he's very understanding and compassionate. He uses a lot of powerpoints that make lectures helpful and definitely strives to help.
Dwayne Sagen gives people Chicago Symphony sound advice whenever they're in trouble. How cool is that?

Sagen is a bit underrated. He's a good guy and means well with the marching band, it's his life, but he's a much better administrator than a director. Also, he's really let it slip these past few games. It's not as though he's stopped caring about the band, but I don't think he really gets the band anymore. He's just kinda disconnected from it now.
Sagen is such a politician, this is the only thing that he is really good at. He is a horrible marching band director and does not care about his students...only about himself.

Dwayne Sagen is an absolute nut.  He is ridiculously crazy, and has no idea how to run a rehearsal.  The band works and works, but NEVER improves.  Warning: he is a great salesman: he'll hook you into the band program, but will cut off all contact with you if you quit.

I was in Marching Band with Sagen as the director.  It was wayyyy more fun that my high school band, mainly because it was more low key and not all strict. But since the band is not a rigid and disciplined band, it shows on the field.  We are okay, but not awesome.

Sagen is extremely two-faced.  He pretends to act all concerned, but all he cares about is marching band, which, by the way, is terrible.  He is an awful conductor and music reherser as well as field instructor.  Stay away from band.
i find sagen critical and difficult to work with.  as admissions counselor, he's slimy.  this is one person blair can live without.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
One of Vandy's greatest faculty assets!
What will the band do next?!
Straight forward class, professor is super passionate and content is mildly engaging. Final project is a group pitch, graded nicely. Overall great class and prof

JD is an awesome professor. He's such a nice guy and genuinely cares about seeing students succeed and learn. This class taught me a lot of real world knowledge and was not very hard. There is a decent amount of homework, but none of it is difficult. Highly recommend.

JD is awesome. He's smart, well-connected (guest lectures are awesome) and brings a lot of real-world experience to this class. There's a fair bit of reading for this class, but you can skim it and still do well. Mock negotiations are interesting and useful. You're basically guaranteed an A, but I think engaging in this class is actually worthwhile

Dyke is great! You get what you put into the class, so I suggest having fun with negotiations and participating. Dyke is also great at helping students with career advice and getting guest speakers, so make the most of that aid. Lots of small assignments, but easy to knock out. Test and presentations are easy.
Absolute Star of a proffessor

Truly an amazing prof with so much valuable real-world experience to share. He wants you to do well in the class and cares a lot about his students. Prof. Dyke encourages the best from all of us, as well as free and original thinking.

Prof. Dyke is incredibly bright and caring. He taught me so much about negotiation but also life. Throughout the sem, he told fascinating stories, drew from a neat class textbook (Negotiation Genius), plus brought in great guest speakers. I'm truly grateful for the time I got with him and hope that I can take more classes with Prof. Dyke soon :)!

Review is for BUSA 2205: Professor Dyke is a great professor. Take his course if you are looking for a laid-back, stress-free class that will still be a valuable use of your time. Lots of guest speakers from all industries. Assignments are all very clear and easy to get done. Quizzes/exams are open notes, so just stay organized for an easy A.
This was an amazing class. It teaches skills that are applicable to everyday life as well as business. Great guest speakers. A must take type of class !

Professor Dyke is amazing!! He is so caring and understanding for his students. The class is a lot of fun with a lot of simulations. He tries his best to make his students understand the key points and make them do well in class. One of my favorite classes by far. Highly recommend taking it!

Professor Dyke is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt so far! He is a great lecturer and constantly tells you about his business experience. As a business professor, he is teaching you just that: business. There are guest speakers and the class is revolved around real experience. This class teaches you a life skill more than anything else.

Professor Dyke is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt so far. He cares a lot about his students and has a lot of very interesting personal stories that he tells the class. He is very down to Earth and very approachable as well. This class was very easy and and the workload was not bad at all. Definitely take this class if you have the chance.

Professor Dykens is one of the best people I have ever met. She is so knowledgeable about the disabilities field and loves to share her knowledge with others. The class is not too hard and I couldn't recommend it more.

Just like the other comments say, Dr. Dykens is very sweet, and she is very passionate at what she does and teaches. Each "Quizzes" - they are EXAMS - are content heavy and you will need to put work into it. Highly recommended for people who are interested in clinical psychology or other mental health field, but if you not, don't take it.

I would take a bullet for professor Dykens. She is the sweetest and most understanding professor I have had and genuinely wants her students to learn and succeed. Take notes and study for the tests and you will be totally fine. Highly recommend this course.

Overall would highly recommend this course! Prof. Dykens is very nice + caring and I found her lectures engaging. The class is graded on a few assignments, a midterm, and a take home final. The midterm was the most difficult part of the class, but she ended up giving lots of partial credit/points back. The final was very doable and graded easily.

I love her so much. So sweet, caring, and knowledgable. I have been recommending this class all semester long! There are not many assignments- a few short reflection-like papers, an op-ed, in person midterm, and a take home final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although Elisabeth Dykens is nice and genuinely wants her students to succeed, her lectures are a bit boring and her exams are tough, especially for her multiple choice questions.  If you are not really interested in clinical psychology, please do not take this class.

If you have the chance to take a class with Dr. Dykens, do it. She is so knowledgable about developmental disabilities and really encouraged respectful, inspiring discussions. She was also very accommodating with due dates (she gave everyone an extension on the main paper) and generally is a generous grader. She is such a gem.

Prof. Dykens is a very sweet professor that genuinely cares about students and lecture material. Very flexible especially if you talk to her beforehand. Attendance suggested but not mandatory. Assessment material can be very specific so study carefully.

Professor Dykens is by far one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. She never fails to bring a sense of great knowledge and pride in everything she lectures on. While it is important to take any class with her seriously, she is very caring and flexible if anything is hindering you from doing your best in her class. 10/10 would recommend

Dr. Dykens is without a doubt one of the best professors at Vanderbilt -- she cares passionately about her students and about the subject she teaches. Her perspective and work with individuals with IDD is inspiring, and she makes the subject easily accessible for people with any academic background. Cannot say enough good things about her!

Professor Dykens' lectures are so interesting. She includes her vast first-hand experience in the field as well as tear-jerking videos. She is understanding if you cannot meet a deadline and gives you plenty of time to complete them. Lastly, she completely changed my perspective on those with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

I had Professor Dykens for my first year writing seminar (controversies in disability). Her background is SO interesting and she is a truly kind and inspirational woman to be taught by. Her assignments are fair and she gives class time to review and meet with students to talk about what they can do better. She helped me improve my writing a lot!

Dr Dykens is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had. She was so passionate about what she taught and wanted to engage with students and hear what they had to say. outside classwork was very easy and she grades very kindly. The mid-term was a little difficult but she will give credit to multiple answers if students do badly. Loved her!

Dr. Dykens introduced a lot of topics about developmental disabilities, which can be a lot of information to handle. This makes the lectures sometimes dragged on, but she is the sweetest and kindest person ever. None of the information is tested except on the final paper, where you will write about topics that you enjoyed throughout the semester.

I really enjoyed Dr. Dykens in Clinical Psychology! It was her first time teaching the class but she presented all the material very clearly and her lectures were engaging. There weren't may assignments (probably due to COVID), but she was clear with expectations and I learned a lot.

Writing was not overwhelming for a writing seminar, she was extremely reasonable about due dates and things like that. Lectures can drag a little, but she is super knowledgeable and extremely kind. Would encourage anyone to take this class

Elisabeth is very knowledgeable and passionate about the field of developmental disabilities. She cares about her students and is flexible with deadlines. She is genuinely interested in what you have to say and designs all assignments to assess and challenge your perceptions, not solely to evaluate your writing techniques. Great choice for FYWS.

Professor Dykens is extremely caring and flexible. She has engaging lectures, and is passionate about what she teaches. She is also an extremely interesting person and has an interesting background. She is flexible on due dates and relies on student feedback.

3640 is a cool class if you like probability. Definitely some review from 2810/2820, but cements important concepts and expands into new interesting areas. Prof. Domel-White gives great lectures and the tests/homeworks were fair albeit sometimes time-consuming. Also (surprisingly) the textbook for the class is a great read to supplement lectures.

Prof. Domel-White is a great choice for 2420. Lectures are clear and he is super accessible outside class. Expect a lot of homework that can vary drastically in the time-commitment and also tests which require a solid understanding. That being said, he is a very fair grader and gives you tools to succeed you just have to put in the time.

MATH 2420: 
Very clear lectures. Doesn't spend excess time on useless proofs that will not be tested--gets straight to the practice problems most of the time! Very friendly and happy to answer questions in class or office hours. Grading criteria and expectations for exams are incredibly straightforward. Overall highly recommend for any math class.

The lecture is dry. Directly read off the note. No derivation of the mathematical equation. Most of the time you are just expected to plug in equations without understanding. The exam is unnecessarily long, it tests how quickly you can solve the question, not if you understand the theory behind it. Average 6-8 hours of homework per week.

RMP won't let me select it but I had him for MATH 2810. Pretty good compared to other vandy math profs. Lectures were clear, problem sets take a while so start them early. Hardest part of the class are exams, they can be pretty long and tricky. If you show up to class and don't procrastinate on the homeworks you should do fine

Fantastic! Math at Vanderbilt is particularly difficult in introductory classes like 1200/1201 and 1300/1301, but I believe Prof. Domel-White does a good job with helping us prepare for the concepts. Also gives some extra credit points on Written HWs and curves the final semester grade. Textbook questions are optional, but HIGHLY SUGGEST DOING!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had him last year (Spring 2021) for MATH 1301, and he was amazing! His class was unnecessarily difficult because the math department made his class super hard (specifically the test questions), but he was as fair as possible. I highly recommend him if you have to take a math class at Vanderbilt.

Professor Domel-White is by far the best math professor I have ever had. I was failing his class within the last month of the semester. He was willing to let me still turn in all the missing homework I had. He also extended this offer to the rest of the class. He was very understanding and he made concepts very easy to understand.

Domel-White is a solid choice as a math prof here, just know he tends to spend equal time on the easy and hard material, so you'll get slammed with a few very difficult lectures before the test. Really nice professor, and he'll meet you for office hours to talk about problems or your grades. Make sure to do more than the homework b4 the test!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Calculus 2 is a really hard class, but he makes class time enjoyable. It's really important to go to every class because he will drop hints about what is on the tests. The tests are mostly straightforward but the timing was definitely difficult. He is available outside of class and is great in office hours. He will explain anything again for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Really great professor!! He is accessible outside class, makes hard material much easier, and doesn't assign a lot of homework compared with other sections.

I think MATH 1301 in general is a really hard class, but I think that professor Domel makes it easier. He is always available outside of class and will answer and explain things clearly. Make sure to do the suggested homework too if you want to do well on the tests. Otherwise, you have one problem set and WebAssign hw due every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Previous review removed. I will clarify. Save yourself the frustrations and avoid this professor. I was very interested in the material before this class. Unfair and arbitrary. The absolute worst.
Previous review removed. I will clarify. Save yourself the frustrations and avoid this professor. I want very interested in the material before this class. Unfair and arbitrary. The absolute worst.
She's a really good teacher and a lot of fun. Her grading is fair, and the assignments are managable.
An inspiration for scholars of any discipline.  (And yes she is totally hot!)

Ebner really cares about his students and is a generous grader, but the class is hard to stay awake in. Focus on the slides and don't waste your time with the awful textbook. This class starts off very intense (5 of the 10 chapters covered in the first 6 lectures), but it becomes much more manageable as the semester progresses.

This course will definitely challenge your skills at reading scientific papers and articles.  The work load is heavy at the beginning, but then lightens up after the first couple of weeks.  Ebner usually does a good job of explaining things, but can be a little unclear sometimes.  Be sure to start on the research project early and pick a good topic

Though this class may seem difficult at first, it is actually pretty interesting. The material is pretty intense, but he has a thorough study guide, and his TA, Ayan, is really helpful. Also, he throws a lot of questions out. There is no final. He speaks in a pretty monotone voice, complete opposite of Leslie. I find him to be very nice though.
