Required summaries of text chapter or scientific paper for each class. Helpful study guides for test. Three tests and presentation/paper.

dear god, could this man be any more boring?  i found it really hard to pay attention in class or even just make it to class (he does 8 o'clock classes)...but it doesn't matter, because the tests are based on the review questions which he goes over during review session.
The class was interesting, and the tests were as easy as the subject matter would allow.  It was rather engaging for an 8am class.

I absolutely LOVE Professor Earley. He's an incredibly good writer with amazing ideas. He is introverted (like me) so make sure to take the time to really listen to what he has to say. 

Participation in class is really important, but pushed me to become more confident in providing feedback to others. I really grew as a writer and student!

50% participation + 50% via 3 essays make up grade. Don't be fooled into thinking easy A... It's not. Earley is a good writer but an AWFUL teacher and he wastes so much time in class. Of our 75min class, only abt 45-55 mins were actually spent talking and the rest silently staring at each other. Also, terrible communicator/never responds to emails!
I enjoyed his workshop a lot. Recommend

I took Intermediate Fiction Workshop hoping to improve my writing, but I left the class feeling like I learned nothing. Prof. Earley wastes so much class time, the syllabus made no sense and wasn't accessible, and the course guidelines were confusing

This first year writing seminar (ENGL 1111) was by far the strangest class I've ever taken - basically we just explored ghost stories and folklore. Ended up being super fun though - discussions with Tony were pretty entertaining and the class was the easiest class ever. Fantastic choice if you're looking for something -different-
Great guy who really cares about his students. Relaxed atmosphere in class. Unconventional teaching methods - but solid gold advice. (A good writer, too. Read his stuff.)
Swivels on dowels.

Mostly, gives grades based on how much he personally likes you/your writing, not so much on how hard you try or how much time you put in.  I felt the grades were quite random, really.  Knows his stuff but doesn't go out of his way to help students.  Wouldn't take him again. Take another professor if possible.
Toady Squirrelly is about right.  Glorified children's literature.
TERRIBLE!! I got a B- in this class and I've never received this bad a grade in upper level english courses.  Pompous, not helpful--miserable!!

Overhyped.  Call him Toady Earley, as he cares more about his office furniture and the fittings of being a "chaired professor" than he cares about thinking in any discernible way.  Same category as some of his colleagues (Daniels!) in creative writing.  Give him even more of a sinecure and get him out of any attempt at the life of the mind.  Please
Witty, but unfocused. He went off on tangents i.e. how perfect the title "Spring Break Shark Attack" was.

Such an original!!  Earley will thoughtfully and honestly help you move from writing like a reader to writing like an author.  Don't mistake his quiet demeanor for disinterest.  I took three of his classes and would run back to take another one any chance I got.  Don't miss out on this experience!

If you want to endure an ego trip from someone who thinks he's a famous writer (his colleagues think otherwise), then take this class. If you want to learn fiction writing from a good teacher, take Lopez's 205. Earley's class is a study in awkward silence
No Comments

Expect a B or B-, gives one A. Great writer, great comments on completed work, but not a good teacher. Funny and genial in class, but class is not structured well. Take him once if you're a major (just for the experience). Try Lorraine López instead!!
He's gruff at first, but very nice once the class gets going.
Arrogant
Challenging but overall an excellent teacher
Fitz is by far one of the most caring and laid back professors at Vanderbilt. I highly recommend his class.
He was a gem, so glad I took his class. Funny and personable. The class was almost entirely discussion, no lectures. It requires a lot of work but he's not a hard grader.

Great professor, one of the only classes I enjoyed going to. Rambles a lot about random stuff but it's fun. Not too much work, just participate in class and try your best on projects. Not a clear grading criteria, but if you try your best you'll do fine and he gives good feedback to go off of. Him and his wife are cute together also. :)

Not much work, especially in the second half of the semester, but when you have to do the (fairly short) papers, they basically have to be flawless to earn an A. Super interesting class and he's a really nice guy.

Professor Fitz is one of Vanderbilt's invaluable gems. I wouldn't be surprised if he were named one of the most talented literary translators in the U.S. His class is engaging, he cares about his students more than anyone, and he helps you gain beautiful insights into a world you will know well by the time you leave his class.
Prof Easley is a great teacher if you are in his class to learn.  It takes some time to get used to what he is looking for but if you try you can do very well.

Professor Easley is a nice guy, but I've never been so frustrated by a professor in my entire life. Lectures are nothing like the exams or the homeworks. He changed the grading of the course halfway through the semester is constantly sending unbelievably complicated emails notifying us of errors he made during the previous class. Do not recommend.

Easley is a really nice guy who wants his students to leave with a strong grasp on the world of investing. He has an fascinating background in finance, which shows in lectures. The class isn't much work, and if you go to his review sessions and office hours to understand what to expect for the tests, exams aren't bad but they are long.

I took her at UH. She took way too long to return graded assignments, retests you on things that she thinks is necessary which puts the class behind and literally waits until test day to cover material that you'll be tested on that day. At the end of the semester she lost half of the classes final test grades, so there's that.

Really easy class, if you just try and know some french, you can get an A. Prof.Early is really nice and helpful. Only problem is that it is every day of the week at 9 AM, and you are only allowed 5 absences during the course of the semester. But thats the only drawback to this class, along with it sometime being boring.

She was a cool teacher. I did not have to do too much work and still got a B in the class. Study a little more than I did and you will be fine. Oh, class is usually pretty boring- but then again, it was a M-F 8am

The best professor I've ever had. LOTS of work; but extremely lenient grading. Emphasis is CLEARLY on learning and retention of information, and the Prof seems to go to great lengths to teach a lot without being a GPA killer. And the subject matter...wow. Amazing, amazing professor. The best part is that the man is objective. No favoritism.
He is an intimidatingly smart dude. You'll learn a lot in his class.

VERY INTERESTING CLASS CONVERSATION! He is SO helpful and very understanding when it comes to late assignments (with good excuse). He is young so knows how to explain novels in a way we understand. Helped with my writing skills

Topic is "what is British", so you read British books. You can miss three lectures w/out penalty. Three papers. No tests/quizess. One group presentation. Very helpful in thnking of paper topics and making a good outline. Pretty easy grader, I got an A with reasonable work.And he rides a motorcycle which is pretty cool!!
Great prof, interesting subject. I really enjoyed taking his classes.

Lectures were a little boring and lots of papers but you can choose which ones to do and he lets you send it to him for feedback. Overall it was a lot of work on a niche topic just for an international cultures credit but he was nice and I got an A once putting in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof. Eakin is a phenomenal professor who really knows his stuff. His style of lecture makes the material interesting and clearly displays his passion. Only gripe is that you have to write 5 papers, totaling ~30 pages - which is annoying for a class that is not a W course. Don't take if you don't like writing, otherwise 100% recommend.

second time with him, love all of his courses! genuinely loves what he is teaching! lots of books and optional papers, skimmed some and was fine! those that i did read were lifechanging! if you miss class, powerpoint are vague but his book is the best way to succeed in the class! definitely would recommend taking as an easier class, he is the best!

I love Dr. Eakin -- he is super intelligent, fair, and respected. His lectures are very interesting and the class is not too much work comparatively. You are only graded on essays, so beware if you are not much of a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His slides have like 3 words per slide which are not helpful to refer back to and he makes you read 5+ books for the class. HOWEVER, he lets you choose which essays to write and allows you to rewrite them. Also a good person!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Eakin was a wonderful professor. His lectures and course content were interesting and his passion for the subject was obvious. The readings he picked for the class connected well with the course material and he was always willing to read any drafts or outlines for essays and wasn't a harsh grader. Attendance counts for participation.

Professor Eakin is extremely caring about what he teaches and makes lectures easy to pay attention to. If you miss a class you will miss important information that he only gives during class. Essays you can choose from over the course, easy take home tests, readings from his own books make it easy to know exactly what hes looking for, clear grading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Eakin is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about Brazil, but I would've liked to see a different class structure or at least more variation. We only watched pre-recorded lectures and discussed them in class which got old a few weeks in. Overall interesting class but be ready to write because he only grades on essays and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Participation counts for 15% of the final grade so you have to go to class and actually talk. He's a good prof who cares about students and the subject that he teaches. A nice perk is that he's always willing to read and edit drafts for papers/exams a couple days ahead of time. Basically all the grades are essays so beware if you don't like writing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Eakin is nice enough, although his emails/grading can seem a little blunt. However, this class was horribly labeled. We were not graded on anything other than papers and a large portion of the class was history/latin american studies majors. Looked like an easy liberal core requirement, it's not. Should be a 200-300 level writing class.

Professor Eakin's History Workshop was one of my favorite classes I've taken at Vandy. He makes the material accessible for students and gives great feedback on papers. Keeps the lectures interesting and doesn't grade too hard. Loves music and movies.

Professor Eakin is well-read, smart, and an engaging lecturer. He is able to put the class material in a global and historical context that helps his students make sense of history. This class--Reform and Revolution--was great, although it required a lot of reading and writing. Best teacher I've had here.

Interesting material, but I learned a lot more from wikipedia than I did class.  3 weeks on a given country will recycle the same 9 slides.  Lots of discussion, but I never felt like Eakin listened to students, just waited until the end of class to give his  interpretation and that was it.  Paper topics are equivalent of junior high book reports

Eakin is a great professor who truly cares about his students.  If you put in the time and go to class, you will do well and learn a lot.  I would highly recommend him to anyone needing an INT credit or additional history class.

I wonder how he got a job here, because he is not a very good teacher.  He absolutely picks favorites and will grade you much harder if he doesn't like you for some reason.  He may seem nice, but he will administer grades based on the person and not the work, ridiculous.  Dont take this class
The best professor I have had so far! He is an excellent lecturer and very easy to listen to. He is also a very fair (and not too difficult) grader.

Great class taught by probably my best professor at Vanderbilt thus far.  Eakin is passionate about the subject and although there is a good amount of reading, it is often enjoyable and very informative.  Attendance is mandatory but you will find yourself wanting to go to class.  If you do the readings and work, it is very possible to get an A/A-.

A lot of reading but a great class if you have the interest and the time.  Eakin's a very reasonable grader (expect to work for an A though), knowledgeable and helpful. Not sure which actions the below user is commenting on, although if he likes you (going to office hours/showing interest is probably enough) it helps.

Do not take this class with Eakin.  All the grades are subjective and writing based.  If you are one of his favorites it is really hard to get a good grade.  His grading is unfair and im shocked that his actions are tolerated.  So suck up to him and you can pull off an A.

Marshall Eakin is the best. He absolutely loves his subject which makes the lectures interesting. His requirements aren't bad either: you have to write two papers all semester and can pretty much hand them in whenever.

LatAmStudies majors take an Eakin class at least once!! He knows his stuff. Friendly, fun, extremely knowledgeable. We read really cool books (if you like Latin American history) and the exams weren't bad at all. Learned A LOT from this guy, still contact him for help with Brazil research.
Awesome class! Eakin is a great professor! Definitely recommend if you are looking for a relatively easy, but very interesting AXLE class. You will really learn a lot, but your GPA will not suffer.

Eakin is fun & enthusiastic. I don't like history too much, but he made it a fascinating subject. Granted, some classes were boring, but overall they  were very good. Not too hard of a teacher. Remember detail, and DEFINITELY be able to come up with an overriding argument with those facts, and you'll be fine. A great class and a better teacher. :)
I really like history, and I've done pretty well in here. I liked him more as the semester went on. No complaints!

Great class! Prof is so much fun, so knowledgeable, and so interesting.  Really knows his stuff, and makes class interesting.  not too hard, either.  Only a midterm, final, and 3 5-6 page papers on books(he lets you choose which 3 out of 6 books to do).  Vandy always advertises this class for visiting students to sit-in on  because he's so awesome!
Expects detailed answers to test questions, but covers all material thoroughly in lecture.
Good guy. Interesting. Great perspective.

I struggled to learn to write papers for Marshall -- my high school English teacher encouraged the kind of ornate prose that he loves to prune out! -- but once I did, I knew that I had really learned a lot about how to write.  Few professors convey their l
Marshall is one of the best professors I have had at this school.  Definately the best in the history department.
Very smart, personable prof. Challenges the students, esp. in this class, to write the best paper of their lives. Goes by Marshall, instead of Prof. Eakin.

Dr. Wright-Rios is a truly insightful, caring human. Don't be intimidated by the reading volume, it does take some getting used to, but it's not that bad. Our class had super interesting discussions about the readings. It beat hearing a professor yap for an hour. And he recommends books/articles based on your conversations outside of class.

Extremely passionate about his class and its a joy to hear him teach. Downside: this class is based on completing the reading before class, and then having a class discussion on it. It is a lot of reading! It's manageable though. There are 3 papers and a project at the end. He loves participation since this class is more discussion based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Cares a lot about his students and spends a lot of effort making us better writers and historians. There are assigned readings before every class, but they are very manageable. He expects a lot of his students, but he is a very fair grader and is always willing to help you make your paper better. Overall an amazing professor.

Very discussion-heavy. Hefty workload (two papers for a midterm, one analyzing a film, and two for the final), but the worst part of the class is the reading. He assigns 50-80, sometimes 100 pages a night, though we all knew nobody was completing them. I managed an A- even though I skipped half the readings. Nice guy, but unnecessarily demanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of reading. Don't take if you are trying to satisfy axel. Very interesting class though. No tests just papers which are graded very harshly.

Extremely long readings and videos (movies). He wants you to dedicate more than three hours of your time a week for his class. Class is extremely dry. He just goes over the readings for the day and then opens the floor for others to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: WrightRios is a phenomenal professor who is incredibly passionate about his courses/material and is genuinely invested in your success. He is so easy to talk to and can be such a good resource if you go to his office hours. The class does require a lot of reading, but it's so worth it, as I don't think I have ever learned so much in so little time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class taught by a professor who is deeply invested in the topic. The class will show you why drug-trafficking has become prolific across Latin-America. Take this class if you have a genuine interest in Latin-America and/or drug-trafficking. Readings are necessary to truly understand the topic. Grade is comprised of 3 papers and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This course was not what I was expecting. Unless you are a history major or really interested in Latin America, I would suggest not taking this class. Every class, we would get assigned multiple readings and Dr. Wright-Rios would just summarize them during class and that was it. I felt like he relied on the readings way too much in order to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I highly recommend this class from Dr. Wright-Rios. The man is a walking textbook but despite all of his knowledge, he allows for student discussion in a course with sensitive topics. The information in this course was very interesting for me so it wasn't difficult for me to stay engaged but it didn't seem like anyone else zoned out either.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most knowledgable people in his field. A ton of readings to do after every class, but not the end of the world if you don't do them because many people get through the class without doing the readings. He is a reasonable grader and an overall nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He has high expectations for the essays, but talking about them with him during office hours before you start writing is a great way to get ideas for what he would like to see in the paper. He assigned a lot of reading, so unless you're interested in the material, it'll be a grind, but if you're interested, he's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wright-Rios is very clear and enjoys discussing lecture topics with students. He has a genuine interest in the coursework and provides plenty of first hand experience and anecdotes to supplement the texts.

I  loved this class and did really well, until the final paper. I tried really really hard (harder than the papers I got As on that semester) and answered exactly the question he wanted. I had another vanderbilt professor read it, who said it was superb. Despite my near perfect grades the professor gave me a B on this paper for an A- overall

I found him not helpful and the quizzes every class tedious. His exams are essay based and pretty broad. Very lecture based, no discussion even though participation is an aspect of your grade so be prepared for that. Not someone I would take if you didn't have to.

Professor Wright-Rios is an excellent professor! He makes class fun and interesting, and makes the material relevant! Its a lot of reading, one has to read the assigned readings, and a lot of papers. He has high expectations, but if you go to his office hours he is more than willing to help! If you put the effort, you will pull out an A!
Class is a bit of work, and reading can become slightly tedious, but overall interesting and grading is fair. Should pull off a high B with moderate effort and an A with high effort.

Wright-Rios' freshman seminar was a good choice.  He grades pretty tough, but once you get the hang of what he's looking for, it's a ton easier.  Be prepared to read a lot.  He expects a lot from his students, but he's easy going and very helpful.
He is just flat out boring, not to mention harsh when grading papers.  He made want to never take another history course at Vanderbilt.
A wonderful man, brilliant, great communicator--one of the last of the really great minds in academia.
Read a play every week and write a two page response to it. Class is spent discussing the plays and he typically picks some really interesting plays. Changed the way I look at theater

If you get the chance to take the Don Quixote FYWS, take it. It 's an easy A if you go to class and read the book. Professor Friedman is not out to trick you and he wants you to succeed. Also, Professor Friedman is the most wholesome man I have ever met in my life. He continues to be a resource for all of his students after the class finishes.
Professor Friedman is so positive and passionate about teaching. His eyes light up whenever a student has something to contribute. It's a real joy to learn from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Can't say enough about Prof Friedman. Even though I only took a commons seminar with him, he put so much energy into it and is so kind, helpful, and down to earth. Gave everyone a personalized gift at the end of the class and emailed us 3 months after class ended just to say he hoped we were having a good summer. Amazing man

I looked forward to Dr. Friedman's class every week; the discussions are incredible and the homework is easy (he does assign a lot of heavy reading). Dr. Friedman really cares about expanding your literary horizons; every class an open-forum for opinions on the day's reading so you do most of the talking. I'm taking every seminar he teaches!

Dr. Friedman is without a doubt the best professor at Vanderbilt. I looked forward to this class every week. As long as you submit proofed, intelligent essays, you will get an A. His courses require a lot of reading (in HONS 184, a book each week) but you will learn so much in-class discussions. If I see Dr. Friedman is teaching a class, I take it.

Dr. Friedman is the man - one of my favorite professors! He is one of the nicest, most down-to-earth people you will ever meet. Always enthusiastic to meet with students outside of class. Class discussions were always interesting, and you truly learn a lot about theater and U.S. culture. Highly recommended.

Professor Friedman is the greatest!  He has the biggest reputation of anyone in the Spanish department, but you would never know talking to him - he's incredibly humble and respectful to students.  He assigns a lot of work but has no problem giving As to anyone who completes it, and he genuinely cares about every student. Take his class!

SENOR FRIEDMAN IS THE COOOLEST!!!!! he is seriously the SWEETEST, MOST ENOURAGING, NICEST professor ive ever had at vandy and he REALLY cares about his students!! and hes a VERY easy grader! (trust me i do not get good grades very often!) hes the BEST teacher ive had and your a FOOL not to take him!!
Very helpful outside of class. If you make the effort, he will appreciate it.  Loves what he is teaching and it shows.

Best prof Ive had at Vandy- a fair grader on written work and very engaging.  big on class discussion/participation. take any class from him- hes just an all around great, nice man who cares about what he is teaching
Fabulous professor! The most intelligent, gracious, polite, kind, passionate professor -- he inspires learning in all.
I love this professor!  I would take any classes he teaches.  He really cares about his students and it shows.

It is very clear that Prof. Friedman wants the whole class to succeed -- while the class is somewhat intensive on a reading amount (60 pages+ of Don Quijote en español each session), the book is very good and the discussions make it even better. RECOMMEND
Dr. Stringfellow's class is quite easy. Only graded on a few quizzes, and many are dropped.
Incredibly easy, funny lectures, quizzes are beyond manageable. Nothing at all to worry about.

Completely subjective multiple choice quizzes based on opinions given in lecture. Never went because didn't think I'd get anything out of it based on the amount of subjective/just wrong questions on the quizzes.
Classes were mostly just guest lecturers. While you could get away with missing some of the lectures and still get an A, Id recommend attending as a lot of them were very interesting.

Very knowledgable about the law. Brought in the authors of some of our readings for us to ask questions and hear from, which was really cool. As the former dean of Vanderbilt Law, he knows a lot about law school and has connections everywhere.

Turned an entire course on administrative and regulatory law into a class on history. Even when we got to study important information, he was incredibly dry and boring, and absolutely terrible with technology. He didn't even realize his PowerPoint wasn't up for the entire class one day.

Rubin is an excellent professor who was clear about the course expectations (related to the one paper) from the onset. If you read and pay attention, you will learn and enjoy it. If you are uninterested in the long Zoom lecture, you may not. Any poor feedback here reflects laziness and entitlement, not poor instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rubin is a passionate instructor that will expose you to classical and modern scholarship about democracy and critical theory. Opportunities for feedback on paper were made before due date. If interested, dont hesitate to take this class, but do make sure to understand the readings and participate in discussion to be best prepared for the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rubin was knowledgeable and passionate about the material, but he did a very poor job of actually teaching. His lectures were long, boring, and relatively disorganized. The class only had one grade  a 20 page paper  for the entire semester, and he graded it harshly with little to no feedback. Nice guy but would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The entire class was graded on one paper. The deliverables on the paper were confusing as best (not to mention the ultra boring lectures). A terrible class by any measure with no teacher effort coupled with unfair grading that was dependent upon one assignment. To add insult to injury, he delayed submitting grades by over two weeks!! AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid taking this section. Too much memorization of facts that others sections get to use a formula sheet for. Minimal partial credit. Little information about what to expect for tests, gives example problems/answers with no supporting work. Does not post homework online, only on T and TH lectures, and both are due on T, weekly.

This professor is very difficult and challenging to work with. He does not care about his students and will call our on them in class for doing the smallest of things. He called me out for eating a granola bar and said I was being disruptive in class. His handwriting is very messy so it is hard to follow along in class.

DiffiQ is already a hard class, and Saff makes it even harder because he doesn't seem to care about his students' success. More so focused on his own research and doesn't provide lots of assistance, extra material, or help. His tests are kind of tricky because he just assumes that we've memorized a bunch of very specific identities, and theorems.

Professor teaches material well, in a very straightforward manner. He doesn't expect you to prove things too much, though he does expect you to know theorems to determine whether methods can be carried out. Homework easy A's if you put the time into it, exams are easy as long as you study the types of questions in hw and practice exams.
Avoid Saff if possible
Math major. Good course. Hard online but learned a lot
Great lectures. He cares but won't coddle. Just do the practice exams

In terms of grade, this class is doable. However, Saff is the least caring math professor I have ever met as a math major. He shows little respect for the students: his phone kept ringing in lectures, and he forced everyone to turn on webcam. His lecture is clear though, but the exam counts 80% to your final grade, absolutely miserable.

The content was easy enough and he was a decent lecturer, but Prof. Saff doesn't really seem to care about his students. He forced remote international students (15% of the class) to attend the synchronous online lectures (with cameras on), by not making lectures available separately, and sometimes taught like we were in high school.

Saff is a good lecturer. He is not accomodating. The tests are exactly like the study guide except for the difficult true-false. Lots of time on tests. Seems to care more about his research than teaching. Some homework took way too long and others were super quick. Be careful as many people in the class seemed to really dislike him as a professor.
Do the practice exams and you'll be fine. The optional project adds 3 extra credits to your final grade.

Very long and difficult exams but if you understand all of the notes from class you'll be prepared. I didn't find office hours very helpful at all. Really got the vibe that he doesn't care much for his students.

Clear lectures. Wrote the textbook so he knows what he's talking about. Pretty clear on what you have to study. Didn't get the impression that he loves all his students and sincerely wants every one of his students to succeeed, but still very helpful in office hours. If you do the weekly hw (which is graded btw) you'll be fine.
Solid
Worked hard but my best class so far!
Great teacher!  Expects a lot but learned a lot!  Highly recommend it

This class was a lot of work at times. His class was not enjoyable. His lectures went 3-5 minutes after the class ends every day, which was extremely annoying, and you have to stay because he gives out the homework assignment only after he finishes his lecture.
Tough but learned a lot more than I have in any other math course.  A lot of homework and great lectures.

Excellent lecturer but don't think you aren't going to work for your grade.  Missed some class because lecturing internationally but is willing to help if he sees you aren't afraid of the work.  High standards but learned more than I have in a lot of other courses!!
Good lectures, but clearly does not care about teaching. Missed at least two full weeks of class, unacceptable. Inconsiderate amounts of homework. Exams are okay.

Great lecturer.  Terrible grader, huge workload.  I mean seriously, parial credit?  Who takes off 8 points on a test because a kid missed one negative sign?  And assigns so much homework, it's crazy.  You understand it after 2-3 problems, but you have another 12 to do.  At that point, it's just about the grade, not about learning stuff.

Ted is the man, easily one of the best professors on campus. You can definitely tell that he cares about his students in and out of the classroom. As long as you do the work you will do fine in the class.
Excellent, nice professor who wants his students to both learn a lot while having fun. I strongly recommend him to all!

SO AWESOME! Absolutely incredible. Will go to any length to ensure that you learn the material. Also, the class is very easy if you just do the work, the grading is extremely reasonable. Intro German is a great way to get that foreign language requirement.

I took Professor Fischer's coffee seminar class. Fischer is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. His willingness to understand his students on top of his knowledge makes the class very intriguing, not to mention he brings in coffee from different regions in the world for the class.

Coffee seminar class! Cares so much about students learning. Met with us individually about each paper we wrote. Made the 3-hr block time pass quickly with a very welcoming environment. Very knowledgable about coffee. Brewed specialty coffee every class!

Fischer is probably my favorite professor at Vandy so far. He's super interesting in general, keeps you engaged, and really focuses on keeping his course relevant to what's happening in the world. The readings got a little long and esoteric towards the beginning of the course, but just power through and don't worry about understanding every word.

I had him for Anthropology of Globalization, and he could not have been better. He truly cares and is passionate about what he teaches. If you are a humanities major or are passionate about non science things, you will love him. He really goes out of his way for his students. One day he brought free coffee for us to taste test! Participation is key

Great guy. You don't have to read any of the books as long as you go to class and take good notes, but attendance isn't mandatory. 2 quizzes, a midterm, and a final. Online blog posts count as your participation.  Overall, moderately easy/interesting class to fulfill AXLE behavioral science req.

Professor Fischer is amazing! He tends to jog around when thinking really hard, which is really funny! He does expect a lot from students, including five books and weekly 200 words online responses. But he is extremely helpful and I learned a huge amount from this class! TAs are all very nice! I want to major in Anthropology after this class!

Very engaging and animated. reinforces a lot of the material in his assigned reading. most of the material that he presents will end up on the tests. the one paper he assigns is pretty easy, you just need to integrate sources into a case study (you don't really need research). fairly easy class all things considered.

ONE OF MY FAVORITES. He comes to class and gives a lot thus he expects a lot of you. You have to take excellent notes, but he is one of the most stimulating professors here. He obviously loves his job and that makes you appreciate the subject material. You do have to study a great deal for the tests if you want an A. GREAT CLASS, GREAT TEACHER.

Fischer is very animated and lively...plus he always laughed at his own jokes which I thought was funny.  The tests and quizzes are not difficult as long as you go to class and are able to remember details.  The paper is the hardest part of the class...be sure and get lots of feedback from your TA on it.

He's pretty wierd and kinds funny! But you HAVE TO GO TO CLASS EVERYDAY and take really good notes because you will be tested on it. Tests an quizzes aren't hard at all you just have to recall all the info he stressed in class. The class was slightly interesting but it's really an easy A for CPLE and AXLE!

Prof. Fischer is entertaining and engaging and is really able to maintain your interest every day. I came in with a mild interest in anthropology and am now contemplating pursuing it in grad school. You MUST go to class and take detailed notes. Tests cover a lot of material but it's all in the lectures so they're not that difficult.
AWESOME teacher.  A little weird and even creepy at times, but he is incredibly knowledgable and wants everyone to do well. Plus, the topic is really cool.

first anthropology class i took and he got me hooked into the major.  He is an excellent teacher and lecturer, his readings are well selected to give an interesting overview of anthropology, and he is exceedingly helpful outside of class.  well worth 3 hours of any semester.
enthusiastic teacher. not a bad class, lots of reading but I never did them and did alright.

Very interesting!! Did not want to take anthro, but ended up being one of my favorite classes. Do go to class though, or you may miss specifics, all tests are on SPECIFIC DETAILS, so know them! Each and every one! He's a really nice guy and is obviously well versed on the subject. Loves to teach!
He's a really nice guy, and is an excellent teacher.
Awesome, very excited & passionate Prof.
This is a very interesting class. Fischer's own field work and enthusiasm make the lectures very enjoyable. The books were also well-chosen. Hard vocabulary on the tests, though.
Lively, interesting lecturer; Grading was NOT bad at all... he'll reread the stuff if you disagree with the TA!  You should take him!!!
Fischer is the best! Hands down! You have to be crazy not to love him!
So nice! And cute too!
fun class, if you take notes and study the quizzes arent bad. very charismatic
great class for CPLE - not boring
quizzes are too specific but tests arent bad, lectures are entertaining and well presented, not a bad course to take for cple

I really didnt like this class. My TA was an impossible grader. Fischer is a good lecturer and attendance is not mandatory but you are tested on so many specifics that you need to come to all the classes and even then you may miss important details
interesting class, cool and funny prof...i definitely recommend this class for cple reqs.

Lectures are long, boring and repetitive.   Professor is largely inaccessible and unhelpful - seems more interested in securing tenure and promoting his own banal research than teaching students. No matter how very interesting the class might sound on paper, he will effectively render it the most mind-numbingly boring experience you can imagine.

I enjoyed the class and subject was interesting. It wasnt the most exciting course I've ever taken, but lecture powerpoints were clear, concise, and all posted to Blackboard, which made it easy for papers. Grading was based on attendance/participation (15% w/2 free skips), two 4-6pg papers (25% each), & at-home essay final (35%). Pretty easy grader
Subject of the class and some of readings were interesting but his lectures were disappointingly pretty boring. Zoned out pretty consistently every class. He is cute, though.
Very easy to get an A. Paper topics are interesting. Dr. Perez is very interesting to talk to during office hours, but the content of his lectures can be a bit boring

The title of the class and the articles are interesting, however, the professor talked about his own research in lectures a majority of the time and did not help explain how the concepts applied to politics as a whole. When asked questions in class, he often went on tangents that were hard to follow and didn't really answer the question.

His lectures are extremely fast-paced, so be ready to move quickly through material. The readings are immensely helpful, so definitely use those to your advantage and cite them in the few papers you'll have to write. Very reasonable workload.

Perez is a very smart guy, but seems more interested in his research than in teaching. Some of the course content seems irrelevant, but interesting. His grading expectations are unclear, but he respects quality writing. There is not a ton of work throughout the semester, overall a manageable class and decent professor
Avoid at all costs.
Doesn't make his grading standards all that clear, especially for his (rather unique) short papers.  Overall, a rather tough grader...prepare to be potentially disappointed with your grades.

Eichman was a clear lecturer but his tests are very specific. Lots of the material is similar to Intro Bio material, and there is a lot of memorization. I enjoyed Brame's section more because I enjoyed her teaching style and cared about her students. I would choose Eichman over Jackson. He goes into more detail whereas Jackson covers more content.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his half of biochem. He goes pretty quickly but he has clear examples and doesn't make you memorize any more than you need to. His exams weren't terrible either, but skipping class is not an option. I would take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Eichman's part of biochem is much easier than Brame's portion.  Don't need the textbook.  Memorize everything and study straight from the powerpoints.

Biochemistry is always very hard, and it requires a lot of studying. Still, most of the stuff you need to know is on his slides, which is nice, and the book is mostly unnecessary. Show up to class and you should do fine. Eichman is a nice person, and I have no complaints other than the ridiculous amount of memorization.

Dr. Eichman's half of the course, although challenging, was more manageable than the latter portion. Exam material comes directly from the lecture slides and every detail is a possible test question. Best to start memorizing the slides at least a week before each exam.

This class is not easy and takes a lot of work, but Eichman is very clear about what you need to know.  His section was easier than I expected. He is not readily available and has skipped office hours before and doesn't email back readily however.

Pay attention in lecture because he is good at showing you what you need to know for the tests. He stresses that you need to read the book. You don't but it definitely helped me understand some concepts better. Overall, he has been one of my favorite professors. Tests weren't too bad. He likes to test concepts over brute memorization.

Dr. Eichman is reasonably clear in what you need to know, and basically anything in his slides is fair game for the test.  However, on the first day of class, he made a big deal about how you need to read the book and do practice problems to do well, but this is NOT true.  I didn't ever use the book and got an A in the class without too much effort

This is a weed out course. To prepare for exams, he recommends reading all chapters in the textbook (4-6 per test) and doing all of the chapter problems around (30 per chapter). In reality, studying from the book will NOT help you do well! He only tests on what he covered during lecture. However, his tests are very long and confusing.

Many are put off by his scatterbrainedness, but he is actually really clear about what you need to learn if you listen to what he says. He really understands that we're going to have to take a test on this material so he doesn't make you learn ridiculous stuff for the hell of it. Really helpful in office hours and easy to get to know him.

Outstanding teacher. He really cares about how everyone does and does not grade hardly. If you've survived Biochem I, you should definitely take Biochem II with him. It's a walk in the park by comparison.
Great Professor.  She makes class interesting, and is understanding if you accidentally miss every once in a while.  She's very helpful outside of class as well, and is a fair grader.

An absolutely amazing professor. I have had her for two classes now and wouldn't mind having her for a third. She is a great lecturer and has a way of looking at things in a new way. She shows a lot of movie clips in her classes. She is a hard grader though. However, her class is totally worth just be willing to put in a lot of work.
she clearly loves teaching, sometimes kind of intimidating. she makes things really interesting but hard

I took for CPLE credit, glad I did.  She is very good, and take home tests are great.  They aren't necessarily easy, but a lot less stressful.  Lots of reading.  GO TO CLASS ON FRIDAYS, you will be rewarded when half the class skips.  Thank me later.
No Comments

dry lectures, INSANE amounts of reading. but, class is one takehome open book midterm and 1 5pg paper, with a takehome final. eigen is brilliant and soft spoken, but commands the complete and total attention of her class at all times. did the hustler crossword in class a lot
He made every discussion amazing and interesting no matter the topic.

He is the most interesting and engaging professor I've ever had. He's always asking questions that push you to look at ideas from new perspectives. He turns even the most boring readings into genuinely interesting conversations and consistently brings up counterpoints that challenge the way you think. I 100% recommend taking Professor Grossman.

Professor Grossman is the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. He is not only incredibly kind and helpful, but he truly pushes students to become better critical thinkers. He is extremely smart and always prepared. He knows how to make a discussion meaningful/interesting and I always look forward to his class. He is the best professor for CORE!
He is the nicest and most interesting professor I have ever had. If you are selecting a core professor, Mr. Grossman is your guy.

JS 1002W. Amazing course, amazing guy. Could not recommend him more, and he genuinely cares about everyone's learning and appreciation of the material. One of the coolest, smartest people you will meet on this campus. Take him.

Dr. Grossman is amazing!!!! He is so knowledgeable and always helpful. The topics were super interesting and he was always looking for our input. Discussions were always interesting and well guided and I really learned a lot. Paper grading was fair and feedback was good. Lots lots lots of readings but they're interesting and often skimmable. Take!!

Dr. Essin is the most thoughtful and caring professor I have had. She is an incredible person who makes her class so much fun. I 10000 percent recommend taking a class from her; you will be more than lucky to be taught by her. She would bring in cookies, bring in a cute dog, create such a healthy classroom community ect.

Dr. Essin is a phenomenal instructor! She is very kind, caring and goes out of her way to make genuine connections with her students. Her assignments are straightforward and she sets clear expectations on what she is looking for. She also gives great feedback. My favorite class first semester. Highly recommend

Dr. Essin is one of the best professors I have had. When I took her class, it was her first time teaching the new Vanderbilt course "Science, Technology, and Values". She was very knowledgable about the material. She even did the assignments with the students. She is truly one of the most kind and caring teachers out there, and makes class so fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers at Vanderbilt.

she is AWESOME. You can get away with not doing hw, but it makes the class a lot more fun if everyone does. Besides, most hw is just watching musicals. If you don't like musicals, why are you here lol. She's very funny and I had a blast. She doesn't grade hard. As long as you try, you'll get an A
She is the mother I never had, she is the sister everybody would want. She is the friend that everybody deserves. I don't know a better person.
Dr. Essin is wonderful
Super great experience in this class. Got to meet a lot of new people and passed easily while also learning stuff. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Essin is so sweet and caring!! I absolutely loved her class and she always made class fun and interesting. Mostly, the class consisted of asynchronous assignments that involved readings and discussion posts. Essin really cares about her students, and I'm so glad I found her class as a first-year student, she's a gem!

The assignments are very open ended (i.e. final paper prompt was "craft an argument about a show's cultural relevance..) but not necessarily difficult. I say a teacher that can make me laugh at 8 am and assign Fiddler on the Roof for hw is a good teacher. Also yea I learned a lot from her, she's good at teaching and engaging students

Christin is the best!! She tells the funniest stories about her life during lecture to keep you engaged. She's incredibly understanding about how much stress is put on college students already and is careful to balance her classwork accordingly. Tests are pretty easy and if you read the plays you'll get 100 on quizzes. Good AXLE class.
She's overrated. Her class is not easy. Not a good choice for AXEL
Not an easy class, tough grader. Don't take it if you are not a theater major.

Prof Essin is the best professor I've had. She teaches you a lot without you realizing it. She is downright hilarious and is one of the coolest people around. Definitely take her class. I would take it again and again if I could.

Don't take this class unless you are passion about reading playwrights. Her grading is very random and unclear. It's very hard for you to find the points on exams on everyday lectures. BTW, don't expect your take-home exam will be easy, because it takes a whole week to finish.

Really great class if you love theatre or just have a passing interest in it. Covers a lot of stuff in one semester but nothing ever felt rushed and everything tied in well to the class. Definitely worth taking.
THE BEST PROFFESOR EVER!!!!!!!

This class was a lot of fun and we had some good lectures and discussions. Several creative projects/papers, but not too difficult if you put the work in. She's very entertaining and incredibly helpful outside of class.
Easy class, not as challenging as you might hope for an upper level class at a place like Vandy, but you get the grade in the end.

Dr. Essin is amazing! Take Thtr 100. She is funny and fantastically brilliant! She is so full of LIFE! (loves to laugh and makes others laugh) She is always smiling and her powerpoints are so well-organized and full of youtube videos! :) TAKE THIS CLASS!
Dr. Essin is AWESOME! She's hilarious and the class is really interesting and not hard at all. Take this class!!
The best Professor you will ever have. Recently moved to Vanderbilt. Inspiring and fun.

Great professor. Lectures are very entertaining if you're listening. Talks quietly, but is funny if you're tuned in. Grades very lightly, and she will show appreciation if you participate in class. Answers emails quickly even if it's a weird time. Lots of points just for participating/being attentive. Tests are all similar.

I'm not an Art History Major. This class was super easy with barely any homework until tests come around. She is a boring lecturer because she has a monotone voice. With the one class essay & the essay responses on the tests, she grades very subjectively and somewhat harshly.
NOT AN INTRO CLASS!! If you do not have a lot of experience with art history courses DO NOT take this class!! Very hard grader on quizzes!!

The best professor I've had at Vanderbilt hands down. I wasn't sure I'd be into art history, but her style of lecturing is great.  She's also great at providing assistance outside of class that goes beyond all other professors. I strongly recommend taking any class with Prof Moodey!
Professor Moodey is wonderful. Perfect lecture voice and loves the subject

Professor Moodey is by far the best I have encountered! Great lectures, amazing sense of humor, and an overall lovely person. She is very passionate about the content of the class and her knowledge is unparalleled. The assignments are perfect for the class and are very fulfilling to complete. Please, if you are considering taking this course,DO IT!

I LOVE Professor Moodey and I am not even a HART major. This class was so interesting and I learned so much. There were no exams just 2-3 assign. and a book project (this is time-consuming but fun). She is honestly just a lovely person. She loves what she does and is so excited to teach other people about it, which makes for a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Moodey is so knowledgeable and passionate about her content! While the class was lecture heavy, she truly made it so interesting. I took this class solely as an art credit but ended up loving it. Beware of few tests that are very memorization-heavy. However, Professor Moodey makes what to expect on each exam abundantly clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Moodey is so intelligent! She knows her material so well and expresses it in a way that engages all students. Her tests are pretty straightforward and the expectations are well articulated from the start. Would certainly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you are not good at a TON of memorization. There are no projects really or homework assignments (except for a few participation grade assignments). Three very challenging tests that rely on memorizing a TON of art pieces (30-50 per test) and you have no clue which of the pieces you'll actually be tested on (total gamble).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: make sure to go to lectures and take careful notes. very accessible outside of class. lenient grader

Prof. Moodey is so knowledgeable about this course and makes the lectures really interesting most of the time. If you are looking for a HCA axle credit you should know that there are only 3 tests and a paper. BUT the tests are actually sneakily really hard because you have to memorize so many pieces of art. Interesting class though.

I enjoyed my class with Dr. Moodey. The textbook readings are mostly the same material as the lectures so it's not imperative that you get through every chapter of the book. Make sure to start working on the essay early in the semester. I felt that Dr. Moodey was able to teach effectively in an online format, and graded easy on the essay and tests.

Professor Moodey is really sweet and makes art history interesting even if you don't like the subject. Her class consisted mostly of three tests, with slide IDs and essay questions. Participation is important, but she appreciates your input even if it's not always right.

Never cared about medieval art, but she made it engrossing through her lectures! So knowledgeable and engages her students well but won't force you to participate if you're not as educated on it as others. Graded by 3 tests, a paper, and attendance; tests are memorization and analysis based, and she is a lenient grader. Her enthusiasm rubs off.
Medieval Paris! I didn't think I would like Medieval Art, but Prof. Moodey's enthusiasm and sly humor rubbed off on me and I ended up really enjoying the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed her class. Really interesting/engaging lectures. She does a really great job of getting people to discuss and work through concepts without just telling you the material outright, super effective teaching style. Tests require memorization but really aren't bad. I would absolutely take another one of her classes.

She's very passionate about her material, and grades easily which is great because the subject matter is not confidence inspiring, though not outright hard. three tests and paper. She requires a great deal of memorization but seems to understand that and places more importance on other aspects. Clear lecturer, great teacher for required class.
straight memorization. study hard!! she is arrogant and class is boring

I found the class interesting, but I agree with the post below. A-/B+ is very possible but don't expect an A. Tests are all of the same format and she gives a practice quiz, but there is a lot of material to memorize. Not a bad axle option.

As it's a beginners' class, it covers all art from 30000 BCE to 1400 AD. So she finds it difficult to move coherently from chapter to chapter & connect dif periods. This is really confusing when studying. Grading is easy if you're happy with a B/B+/A-. Impossible to get an A:in tests she takes off 5-6 pts from 50 for an "excellent/brilliant" essay.

She refuses to tell you anything she went through in lectures during office hours. She also grades unfairly, taking off 5-10 points from your exam essays for no reason, and when you ask her she will say "this is a good score", and tell you to read the sample essay on OAK, which is usually not as good as yours.

The material itself is straightforward memorization. But she, as a teacher is awful. She's overly religious and turned it into a religious course. She called us all heathens for not knowing our scriptures well enough. She let's you out late everyday, and has a stuck-up demeanor. I'm moving to have her fired, she does not represent the school well.

Professor Moodey is wonderful! She really cares about helping her students in class. Tests are all the same format and they're not cumulative, so as long as you don't mind memorization they're not too hard. I  always read the textbook for class, but I'm sure you could do well without keeping up with the reading. Highly recommend this class!

I wasn't interested in art history at all but I really liked the class. Professor Moodey tells you everything you need to know in class. The biggest time commitment is memorizing the works of art before each test (there are 3 plus the final) but the tests all have a standard format which makes it easy to study.

I had no interest in medieval art before this course, but she made it very enjoyable. Prof Moodey is very quiet, but she definitely knows her material, and if you come to class and study for the three tests, her class is not bad at all! She does take a long time to grade, and she never handed back the paper that was worth 30% of the total grade.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS TO FULFILL AXEL!

I took the AP for the same class and didn't do well, but retook with Prof. Moodey.  She was an excellent teacher and very interested in the subject.  The test material was clearly laid out in class and the 4 tests were very reasonable.  I ended up doing much better in here than I did with my previous teacher.

The class was really straightforward because all the tests are the same format. That being said, she is maddening to have as a teacher. She let us out late almost daily and had no regards for how far over her lectures were going. She is not helpful at all in office hours so don't waste your time going.

Moodey is an incredible teacher! She's very quiet but knows everything about medieval art.  She wants her students to succeed and is very helpful! You need to go to class but i almost never used the textbooks. Her tests are very reasonable and i highly suggest this class!

I feel that this class would not have been as enjoyable as it was if Prof Moodey had not been teaching it. She clearly loves art/art history. Also, she prepares you for the four tests that make up your class grade (plus attendance taken on random, unannounced days) by giving a not-for-credit practice one. She cares about student success.

Prof. Moodey is seriously one of the best-kept secrets at Vanderbilt. As long as you go to class and take good notes, (and listen to what she's saying, because it's always brilliant and/or hilarious), you will do well. I went from not caring about medieval art to being obsessed.

Ive taken two classes with Moodey...and im seriously obsessed with her. At first she comes off a little intense and she speaks very softly. She also does not change her exam days or offer alternate exams in any circumstance.  However, her tests are always reasonable and she's hilarious if you really listen to her. Shes also really sweet. TAKE HER

Talks very quietly, but very knowledgeable on the subject matter. Personally, medieval art is not my favorite subject, but it was bearable. Lots of memorization for tests (midterm and final), but fairly easy for papers.

I took this class to fulfill an AXLE requirement. Big mistake. I don't really care about ancient art. The class was boring. And the amount of memorization that was required for the two exams was ridiculous. There was one paper that she graded way too hard. If you are not obsessed with are, stay away from this class!
No Comments
Eleanor is my goat. Well prepared, fair, extremely competent, and very helpful outside of class. Takes the extra effort to build a warm environment. Take her classes!

This course was my favorite math class at Vanderbilt so far. Eleanor was totally dedicated to the students, and her passion for the material was tangible in class. She did a great job explaining difficult subject matter in a digestible way.

Eleanor is a fantastic math teacher. She is fair, clear, and organized, and also truly cares about her students. Number Theory can be a difficult subject at times, but she does a great job at explaining it. Also, she writes pretty easy/fair tests even if the problem sets are difficult. 100% would take for any math class

Overall, she has a great way of teaching students and really meeting them where they are at in the course. Office hours are a must because it can help you further understand the content which can be relatively harder than traditional calculus 1 taught at high schools.

Professor McSpirit is probably the most organized professor that I have ever had. Expectations are clear, problem sets are posted well ahead of time, tests are graded quickly, and lecture notes are posted on Brightspace. She is a patient and straightforward lecturer and very accessible in office hours.

Her approach to teaching mathematics is definitely different from high school! If you are taking this class straight out of high school, I would recommend McSpirit as your #1 choice. 

She even helped me with scheduling out my math degree during office hours. Truly just wants to see her students succeed.

McSpirit is a great addition to the Vandy math department. She has a strong format for her lectures, so you know what to expect each class. The exams are the same for every section of the course. She's also super accessible via email. If you do your homework and attend the occasional office hour, you should be fine.

Dr. Filosa is sweet and caring, and very accommodating. She's a whimsical person and makes class discussions very fun and enjoyable. She's can be a bit unclear on expectations, and confusing at times, but she's generally great and a lax grader. Would recommend.
Dr. Filosa is the sweetest, kindest, and funniest professor ever. Even though the content of the course was a little iffy (out of her control), the course was always fun with Dr. Filosa.

Dr. Filosa is kind, humble, and funny. She knows a lot about the material (for our writing seminar, it was Dante's Inferno), and she presents information in a way that makes you feel excited to learn more. Her class was a unique one and totally worth it. I'll definitely think about it whenever this book is brought up. Take her class!!!!

**for Core 1020 Ela was a true ray of sunshine and a kind lady. Would often reminisce on old stories and friendships-- she's lived a good life i can tell. Participation and attendance were technically mandatory for core, but she didnt care. You can always get an extension for an assignment. Easy grader and we had a snowball fight at the last class.

Professor F made class fun and funny every day. She's such a joy to have as a teacher! The only frustrating parts is that she wasn't very clear on what would be on quizzes — I would often sit in front of a comprehension quiz and I didn't know we had to prepare for an entire section (and I'm organized). She's also pretty slow to return work.

Dr.Filosa is hilarious and a great professor! Her classes is definitely harder than the introductory italian classes, but as long as you pay attention and take notes in class, do the homework, and study for the tests you will be fine. She makes class super fun and is very open to any questions you may ask.

If I could describe Dr. Filosa in one word it would be "nutty." She is awesome. Super funny and caring. Also really respected in her field.

Her class is difficult and she expects a good amount from you, but If you pay attention in class and review before the exams you'll be fine.

Absolutely loved Professor Filosa! She's so considerate and is willing to adjust assignment deadlines in order to accommodate students. Tests were difficult, but study adequately and you'll be fine. She creates a fantastic classroom environment and keeps the mood uplifted. Highly recommend!

Impossible to get a read on this prof, in a good way. Tough but fair perhaps? Class had a LOT of assignments (hw everyday, 4 quizzes, 2 short papers, 2 oral exams, 2 written exams, 3 "extracurriculars"). Not hard to do well in but you have to work for the grade. Caring professor and very funny in a uniquely Italian way (great fashion sense too).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Elsa is passionate about the Italian language and wants her students to succeed. In addition, she set the tone to create good energy in the class. I recommend the Italian minor for Econ/Business/others looking to diversify their course load.

I absolutely love Elsa. Her class is probably a little more challenging than the ordinary intro-language class, but that's just because she pushes you and wants you to actually learn (and you will). She is such a funny and kindhearted person, and easy to contact outside of class. I'm so excited to take more classes with her in the future.

Prof Filosa is absolutely my favorite professor this semester. She is a loud hilarious Italian lady that loves her students and genuinely wants to help them learn the language and culture. I hope she teaches a more advanced class in the future so I can have her again.

Professoressa Filosa is an incredible professor, very caring towards her students, passionate about her work, kind, empathetic, interested in your improvement, exciting, funny, knowledgeable, engaging and has lots to teach to her students. It is definitely recommended to take her class and you will surely learn a ton & enjoy her warm presence.

Dr. Filosa is the nicest teacher I have ever had. She begins class by asking how everyone is doing and cares about everyone in the class. The class I had with her was taught in English, but all work she assigned was very reasonable and tests were straightforward.

Professor Filosa is the sweetest and most charming professor I've ever had! She cares so much about her students and it makes you really want to do well. That being said, her tests and quizzes are really hard and if you don't want to learn Italian, don't take her class. If you do want to learn, you'll do very well and enjoy her cheerful presence!

Clearly very knowledgeable about her subject, which makes the lectures interesting and time just flew by. Homework in the form of having to research a character per canto was too much work and tests emphasized trivia way too much. Lively and interested in her students. Loved the accent.

The class on Dante's Divine Comedy is only actually about the Inferno; we barely glanced over the rest. Her tests are on random information and are confusingly worded, to the point where she normally takes five minutes before each to explain what certain questions meant. Too much of the class is just her re-explaining what the book says.

Elsa is a nice lady with an entertaining personality. Overall, the class was a nice break from traditional academic classes. The book we read had some good ideas, but I do wish they were taken a bit further. Do be sure to not take the class too lightly. It's not hard, but it isn't graded much easier than a writing class. Nice accent and good pizza!

Elsa was amazing!The class was super interesting.Although challenging,it was reasonable to get an a if the subject was approached correctly.There are a lot of grades in here which can balance out one bad grade.She was extremely helpful,funny and kind.The class was small,and the teacher really got to know us.I appreciated that she was genuine.

awesome CS. nicest lady of all time, very casual, knows its just a 1 hour class and doesnt care. sign up, you get an A. one page writeup a week that takes about 10 minutes, she gives A on each one. 1 little book about civility. final paper is great. few pages about the semester. TAKE IT. not most interesting CS at all, but nice mini gpa/hour boost
She's so awesome. Hilarious, sweet, and a great teacher. Makes class really fun. Weekly quizzes, sometimes a tough grader. Love her to death.
Elsa is the best teacher at Vanderbilt and I'm really proud to give her the first chili pepper.
She was incredible.  It was an absolute pleasure to take her class.  I love her more than Rafaella Carrà.
Elsa is so entertaining, and she makes me look forward to this class! She gives quizzes often, but they are not too difficult. Also, the class size is small, which is fabulous for a language class.

Absolutely wonderful. You learn so much so quickly with Elsa. She has a great, engaging personality that lends itself well to teaching. There's a lot of daily completion homework online, which actually turns out to be really helpful in staying on top of new topics and preparing for quizzes.
Elsa is such an amazing teacher! makes the class fun and is so likeable. By far the best language teacher at vandy
By far my favorite teacher at Vanderbilt.  She is extremely likeable and funny. She also grades fairly easy.
So Funny

Professor Filosa was a great professor in terms of keeping the class interesting, fun, and not too difficult. However, when it came to grading written assignments, participation, the oral exam, etc.. she absolutely chose favorites and did not grade fairly.

Elsa is fantastic. I would recommend her Italian class to anyone. I had her for a full year, and I loved it. You learn so much, but the pacing is good, and she's really fair. Also, she's really nice and funny and cares a lot about her students. GREAT class.

I love Prof Filosa! She has a great energy and sense of humor. Also, she truly wants her students to succeed in and to enjoy learning a new language. Her grading system is very fair. Classes are always enjoyable. She is a wonderful teacher and this is a wonderful class!

Elsa Filosa is THE BEST. She is so nice, lots of energy, cares about her students. She runs a very democratic classroom. This class IS TOUGH cause it moves so quickly but she makes very clear what you need to know for tests/quizzes and does a good job of highlighting the important material in the book.

Elsa was one of my favorite professors during my first year at vanderbilt. she was extremely energetic and excited about italian. she also has a lot of fun stories that make the class a lot more interesting. i strongly recommend taking her class.

Elsa is one of the nicest teachers I have ever had. While the class does have a ridiculous amount of work (its a first year language!), you do learn a lot and Elsa is willing to work with the schedule. She wants you to well, and if you're nice and talkative, she'll love you! If you want to learn Italian and enjoy your 4 day a week class, take Elsa.
interesting and non-stressful. take it with house
Syllabus makes her seem a lot more strict than she is. Lectures are great, relaxed class, really emphasizes empathy in public policy. Could not recommend Dr. House more.

Phenomenal person. Really gets you thinking about the subject and application, and super interesting career. Insanely low workload, three assignments the whole year and the first two take like an hour, and the 3rd is a group project. Lectures are amazing, but you don't need to take notes to succeed. I can't recommend her more, my favorite HOD core

Amazing and hilarious lecturer and awesome person. Really cares about her students. Strict on attendance but that's about it. Very few assignments and a final group project. Use her as a resource to get feedback on the assignments and you will do well in the class. Very knowledgeable about the subject matter and encourages class discussion.

Live, Love, Laugh Emily- her class was my favorite this semester! Grading: Attendance (25%, 2 free absences), Short Policy Paper (20%, 6 pages), Midterm (20%, take-home, manageable), Final Group Paper/Presentation (35%, 20 pages + 10-15 min presentation). She offers thorough feedback and creates a relaxed, supportive environment. Highly recommend!

Dr. House was very knowledgeable about Public Policy- especially the higher ed side of things. Her syllabus makes her seem very strict, but that's rlly not the case. Show up to class and engage, and you will get a good grade. She cares about her students. 100% recommend.

Lots of writing in the class, but all group-based on a topic you select. She is very passionate and down to Earth. Brings cool guest speakers. Very open to feedback and very nice. Her syllabus makes her seem a lot stricter than she is--she's very nice, understanding, and a great resource overall. Plus, she's very funny. Definitely recommend her!

I enjoyed this class with Dr. Pendergrass and Dr. Peterson. The main draw was the spring break class to France, yet they did a fantastic job as a team to show how compelling the class topic was. The assignments were tailored to be thought-provoking and also very easy. They were so fun to be with on the trip and I'd definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Pendergrass is amazing. She is kind, thoughtful, and overall a wonderful person. She is amazing to learn from - she has done so much in the education world that I enjoy hearing of her travels and time spent in schools. She puts students first and pushes us to do our very best. She is a mentor and wonderful person to have in your life.

Pendergrass is a lot of fun and great to hang out with during the traveling part of the course. The work for the Harry Potter class wasn't meaningful and did not engage well with the topic of social justice, and sometimes grade oddly tough, but for the most part was chill.

Professor Pendergrass is super sweet and caring. You can tell that she genuinely enjoys the class are cares about her students. The workload was very manageable and it was easy to succeed if you put in effort.

Emily is an angel. She cares about students and the content. She wants you to succeed and hopes that you get a lot out of the class AND the assignments which is beautiful. She will be a friend, colleague and connection forever. You will get so much out of this class.
She has all the qualities that you would want in a good professor: engaging, caring, and fun. The coursework was pretty simple and not too time-consuming. Easy grading. Good at working with students.

I have never had a professor that genuinely listens as much as Prof. Lordi. It is very clear that she genuinely cares about what each and every student has to say and she thoughtfully responds each time. I love this class and the readings taught me so much.

She is by far one of the best professors here at Vanderbilt. She is so passionate about what she teaches, and while I actually took another class from her not on here, I can tell by how she is in this class that this is very normal for her. She is super sweet, an easy grader, and honestly, quite funny, as well

I loved Prof. Lordi's approach to this course. Her readings are super light and essays can be written primarily off of discussions. She's a great resource to go to when writing papers and trying to understand key themes in the readings, and the discussions themselves are super interesting. Great for Engl. majors & non-Engl. Majors!

She is AMAZING. So intelligent and respectful of students - I felt smarter just being around her (lol) and she really helps you develop your ideas through class discussions. This class was very light on homework (only readings), but the readings are so interesting. One of my favorite classes I've taken at Vandy!

She is caring and a good grader. If you need any help, go ask her. But she is not really into teaching. She seldom replied emails and provided limited feedback. Sometimes even checked her phone during class.

Such a sweet human and cares for her students a lot. She made the final project easier by having you work on it throughout the course of the semester. She is lecture-heavy, but it gets slightly broken up with group discussions in class.

The best professor!! So understanding and truly wants you to succeed in her class. The final project is a doozy, and it definitely helps to work on this throughout the semester. She offers so much support for the project and it is split up into 3 different parts across the semester. Love her so much
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A literal fairy princess of a professor. She is extremely compassionate, and genuinely cared more about her student's success than anything else. The project was larger than I anticipated, but the way the elements of the final paper are distributed throughout the semester makes it not overwhelming. Would take again!

Professor Phillips-Galloway is a great person! The class is mainly focused on one big project which can be overwhelming but she will take you through the whole process and make sure you understand what you need to for the class. It's a good introductory ELL course and Emily is the kindest professor ever.

Contrary to a lot of these comments I actually really enjoyed this class! Dr. Ritter is very bright and gives great lectures. I genuinely felt that I learned a lot from this class.
