You can get an A if you work your ass off, completely understand her confusing grading criteria and don't slip up ever. A big part of doing well in her class is getting lucky with your group members. Take another professor, if you can.

I had Dr. Enyedy and I enjoyed this class, but there are a few things to note. 
1. It is HARD to get an A. You have to fight for an A, but if you keep showing up, being on top of everything, and communicating with her she will help you get an A.
2. She cares about all her students.
3. She cares about honest effort into the work you produce.

Prof. E, is a joyous professor. She cares a lot about students mental health. Unfortunately, she also cares a lot about how much effort you put into assignments. In general, this class required a lot of hard work and due diligence to succeed on papers and group projects. You need to clearly understand all expectations and ask questions.

Prof E's incredibly unclear grading metrics make it virtually impossible to do well in this class, no matter how astronomical your efforts are. Despite praising the quality of my assignments, she docks excessive points for things never stated in the guidelines. I've never met a prof who tries to act so empathetic and be the complete opposite.

When you first enter the class, Enyedy will give you the illusion that she'll help you get an A. However, she hands out so many bad grades for no reason. She doesn't even grade with a rubric, which makes me question how she got a PhD and got to Vandy. Don't take her, I beg you. I would rather get drafted to fight WW3 than be in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUN! She is the toughest and honestly meanest prof I've taken at Vandy. She is trying to prove something by virtually giving no A's and saying "grades don't matter" . This is a course that used to be easy but now you get graded so harshly (it seems like she finds joy in it). Genuinely think this woman is evil.
Avoid. This class withered my patience and my grade was battered at the end of the semester!

She was kind of a hardo. She took the class really seriously. The class itself isn't difficult especially if you get a competent group. The expectations for your work are high but not impossible. The hardest part about this class is that you group members will probably be dumb and bring you down. Grade VERY strongly tied to group members.

Enyedy is great for 1300. She realizes that the nature of this course is to improve small group work skills so she doesn't feel the need to pile on excessive readings or individual work. This class provides an incredible opportunity to make new friends from your small group. I highly recommend 1300 with Enyedy.

The class is really pointless but super easy and Dr. Enyedy cares about students and wants them to succeed. Suck up a bit and meet with her before presentations and you will be fine. The lab group days you rarely stay for even 1 of the 2 hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She cares about student well-being and she's a nice professor with kind intentions. But, her lectures are super boring and obfuscate textbook material that I found interesting. She gives detailed presentation rubrics but then grades on whimsical observations that don't reflect her initial guidelines. Often left me feeling bored and frustrated.

Class was mostly comprised of group projects (2 really big ones spaced out throughout the semester). Other than that, just weekly reading quizzes and participation are your grade along with a final project. Enyedy really cares about students.

While Karen is a very sweet, caring lady, this course was a glorified trainwreck. I'm not sure if HOD 1300 is always this way, but there were arguably no guidelines for any assignments, which was often frustrating. Her Tuesday lectures with Dr. Smith were unbearable at times. Pray you get a good group (I did)! They were my saving grace.

Professor Enyedy was very sweet and genuinely cares about her students. Lecture is mandatory but quite useless and feels like more of a group therapy session at times. Assignments can be graded quite harshly but grading is usually done by TA's.

I loved Enyedy. She always checked in with us about how we were doing, was really responsive when she asked us for feedback about the class, and the work felt really meaningful. Definitely a class some people slacked in bc the work wasnt too bad, but do the work and youll get so much more out of the class and itll make the bigger stuff easier.

She cares about her students and gives great feedback on papers. Make sure you ask about criteria and specifics when working in group projects. If you connect with her on a personal level she will help you out. Long lectures but she tries to make them as fun as possible. Best HOD1300 teacher for sure.

Karen loves group projects. I hate them, but that's because I'm the one who winds up doing all the work. Will you get an A? That depends on your writing abilities and fellow group members. If you're a strong writer, you'll do well on the essays. Otherwise, PRAY for competent group members! And if it matters to you, her lectures are extremely dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not that hard to get an A- but Hard to get an A because no clear guide lines that screw you over in the beginning. Generally boring but kind but kind of annoying. She loves Marvel comics and talks about it all the time so good way to impress lol. Lectures pointless.

Tough grader in the beginning, but with feedback easy to do well. However, vague guidelines and you really need to ask questions and specifics because she won't tell you. Caring, but lectures kind of boring. The class got more interesting, beginning quite boring. Heavy on group projects and essays, with super easy quizzes.

Very nice and caring; weekly reading quizzes, two group projects, and a few individual writing assignments; grading criteria can be vague but is willing to talk and adjust things if asked; very understanding and reasonable; she used to be a counseling psychologist so she is good at talking with her students

Professor Enterline is incredibly knowledgable about her subject. Her lectures are really informative and give a lot of interesting background on authors whose works tend to overshadow their lives/historical moments. She is very down to earth and easy to talk to. This class is not very difficult, with just 3 writing assignments. The texts are fun.

Wonderful professor (I took Classical World Literature)! Incredibly knowledgeable and passionate. She is super kind, and class was very engaging and interesting. Lots of reading but not too much; try to stay on top of it and you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Enterline is a gem in the English department. She is SO knowledgeable, real and cares about her students. She will help you improve your writing if you ask for the help and she will expect you to try in discussions, but accepts any interpretation you may offer. Listen to her interesting lectures, read & TRY and you will love the class.

SO much reading. So little interaction with students. All lecture and Lake spoke so much more than Enterline when her material was more accessible and interesting about the readings. Enterline is sweet and knows a lot about her subject. Theres too few assignments to ever feel solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Enterline is the best! Definitely a top Vandy English professors. She is brilliant at her subject -- classical world lit isn't necessarily the easiest to understand (imo), but her lectures are amazing and she makes class very engaging. She grades/assigns work about average for Vandy English dep't (not super easy), but very accommodating!

This is an amazing class for anyone looking for a strong background in the classics. I learned a ton, and the workload was super manageable. Professor Enterline is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had--her lectures as well as our in class discussions were always interesting & engaging. She is a fair grader and very helpful with papers!

This was my first literature course at Vanderbilt and I found Prof Enterline to be very welcoming and encouraging. I was frankly blown away by her knowledge of literature, language, and history. Definitely learned more in this class than most, and the reading list was fantastic! Some weeks there's a lot of reading, but it was always manageable.

Very good class - wasn't a ton of submitted work (a few papers and a midterm) and was very lenient due to COVID-19. Enterline has a frankly ridiculously wide breadth of knowledge, and though there's a bit of an overemphasis on relatively niche literary theories, overall her lectures and discussions are well done, and the reading list was phenomenal

Professor Enterline is wonderful. She is incredibly knowledgeable in course material, and does a great job making readings accessible and engaging for all students. Professor Enterline always makes herself available outside of class and is super helpful and understanding. I will definitely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Enterline is yet another English professor at Vanderbilt that I absolutely adore. World Lit was one of the best classes (if not the best) I have taken throughout college. The sheer amount of knowledge Enterline possesses is awe inspiring, but I never felt as if she was talking down to me. She definitely cares about her students and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Enterline is really knowledgable about literature and literary history. She prefers to conduct classes half lecture style and half discussion. She's really understanding regarding adjusting deadlines if we're behind on reading. You'll definitely learn a lot in her class, but be prepared to read!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I can't believe how much I learned in this class. I was a little intimidated by Professor Enterline at first because she knows so much. But she is approachable and cares -- gives good feedback too.

I was intimidated by Professor Enterline when I first stepped foot in her class because she is one of the most knowledgeable people I have ever met. However, she is an incredibly caring professor who truly wants to hear new opinions and ideas and have interesting discussions. I learned so much in her class and had a great time doing so.

Professor Enterline is incredibly knowledgable in her field of study, and she inspires her students to really love Shakespeare's works. I went into this class with little knowledge of Shakespeare and experience in writing close analysis papers, but I feel like she has really helped me improve throughout the semester. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Really caring professor who makes class interesting! Participation is important but Prof. Enterline made me feel comfortable speaking up which I usually don't do a lot. Papers (of which there were only a few) were on interesting topics and discussion went deeper than just plot details so I appreciated the plays more than I thought I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: If you read and participate, you will enjoy the class! Prof Enterline is super open to participation and makes you want to participate. I have not done very well (as well as I would have liked to) on the papers, but I think if I were to meet with her I would get better help before submitting, but I have procrastinated. Overall, take the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Enterline's passion for Shakespeare is contagious and introduced me to a whole new world of literature that I didn't know existed. She goes beyond simple comprehension of the texts and films and engages every single person in the class in a way I haven't experienced at Vanderbilt yet. Read each of the plays -- they're not that long!

Professor Enterline is a great professor! She is an expert on Shakespeare and makes literary analysis super easy and intuitive. She's very dedicated and is always open to meeting to talk about papers. Class discussions are super interesting and really helpful when you start writing the papers. This is a really good W course regardless of your major
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor! By far, one of the best authorities on Shakespeare! Take her course, you won't regret it.

Professor Enterline made me re-fall in love with Shakespeare--this class was so entertaining and the in-class discussions were incredibly interesting and thought-provoking. She is super caring about her students and one of the most knowledgeable professors I have had so far at Vandy. 10/10 recommend this class for any type of student!!
Teaches very tough foundational texts, sticks to her own rigid interpretation of them. You shouldn't leave college without taking a class on the Virgil, Ovid, Dante, Shakespeare though. Worth it.

I don't normally love shakespeare but professor Enterline made the class extremely enjoyable. She's a fair grader but grades for improvement so it's easy to raise your grade. Would recommend this class for your W, work load is easy to manage and I like the small class discussions

Professor Enterline is the best!!! She is so knowledgeable and cares about making sure her students succeed. This class reignited my love for Shakespeare and made me excited to read and come to class. The workload was completely manageable and the materials were interesting, 10/10 recommend this class/Professor Enterline.
Great professor! Extensive knowledge and thought on Shakespeare and all of literature! Write literary papers in her courses and you are golden! PS attendance is a must, so show up to class!

I LOVED Professor Enterline--I seriously have never met another teacher with such a breadth or depth of knowledge. She jam packed my brain with knowledge. By far one of the smartest teachers on campus, and you are truly missing out if you don't take her class.
Professor Enterline was wonderful - she's brilliant but accessible, and discussions are lively. She really does care about all of her students opinions and ideas. Definitely recommend taking her.

Professor Enterline is a fantastic professor. She is extremely knowledgeable on her topics and works to promote this same passion in her students. She is always available to meet and go over paper topics, and her feedback on assignments is extremely helpful on improving writing as well as a enhancing understanding of the material.

Dr. Enterline is hands-down the best English professor Ive had at Vandy. (Ive intentionally placed myself in her classroom three separate times.) Shes incredibly knowledgable about her subject, clearly explains concepts, and always engages the class in interesting (often funny) discussions. Do not graduate without taking one of her classes!

Don't take a class with Enterline. She shouldn't be teaching discussions, because she just lectures AT the class and shoots down peoples' ideas. Her classroom isn't welcoming or comfortable. She is also pretty boring unless you like classics/olde and middle english.

Enterline is not a very good teacher. Although she is clearly a knowledgeable woman, she is very closed minded and tells you you are wrong if you do not agree with her. Definitely should not be teaching a discussion based class. She basically lectures all class and it's boring. Boring reading materials too. She's nice but avoid her if possible.

Enterline tends to dominate class discussion too much, and too often tries to relate everything to her area of research no matter how much of a stretch it is. She was a bit difficult to meet with out of class and didn't seem like she really wanted to help. She did, however, give me an unsolicited extension on a paper, so she can't be that bad.

Grades are decided from two medium-length papers, two exams, and a simple participation grade. Her lectures aren't always the most exciting, and she focuses too much of what we read on our texts' relationships to her area of research (Ovid), but she really knows here material, and it can be a really good class at times

Listening to Professor Enterline is more or less a religious experience.  She knows her subject matter so well, and is so passionate about it, it's hard to imagine her turning anyone off to English.  She turned us on, that's for sure.

I had her a while back.DO NOT TAKE THIS WOMAN. She completely turned me off of English, which was my passion, by reading only the first three pages of a twelve page paper and telling me it was garbage. Meh.

I took her freshman seminar, Writing Lives, and I loved it. She made everything very approachable and brought out a lot of insight about Shakespeare and the other authors we studied. She focuses a lot on those who participate and encourages students to explain things to one another. One of the most influential classes I've taken.

I love English but she kind of turned me off of it. She is smart and you will learn things, but I don't think she is as helpful as she could be. I would ask for help on revising my papers and she would only say things like "just go a little deeper"- not very helpful. I didn't enjoy it as much as I thought I would.

This class is AMAZING. I'm a science geek so anything englishy makes me cry, but prof enterline made shakespeare SO interesting. she knows a lot about the subject & its fascinating how the discussions related shakespeare to our everyday lives.Class is difficult and time-consuming (she expects a lot), but one of the best classes i've taken @ vandy.
I sat in on her class, but she is overrated.  She seems full of herself and does not seem approachable.
No Comments

Very interesting class.  Very knowledgeable about her subject - Shakespeare.  She likes to focus on issues of gender and sexuality.  Sometimes passes off as laughable something that may not be very obvious to students.  I'm in eng. and got a good grade.

This class had so many engaging conversations that stemmed from the content. She really wants to see her student succeed and does not want grades to affect how they interact with the class. She has us make discussion posts on the reading which allowed me to interact with how others thought. Most of it was turned in for completion not a grade.

Dr. Epstein-Levi's course has been the least stressful one I've taken at Vanderbilt and it's one that's inspired me to minor in GSS. Truly helped me learn a lot! HIGHLY recommend taking this course!!!

GSS2234 was a super easy class, albeit somewhat boring because people were reluctant to participate in discussions. Prof. Epstein-Levi's grading criteria are clear, and she's very flexible when it comes to deadlines and late work. You have to do a few quick annotations and reflections weekly (by quicky I mean 25 minutes) and 2 creative projects.

She is a great professor. She makes the class easy, so you can do what you want with the class. You don't have to stress over your grades in this class and she is very passionate about what she talks about. If you pay attention in class, you can learn quite a bit without having to worry about your final grade.

Professor Epstein-Levi is a great teacher and a great person. The class has got to be one of the easiest at Vanderbilt. I took this class for AXLE credit and didn't go in expecting to learn a lot, but I did learn quite a bit. It was a nice breather from my harder classes. It's probably like 30 minutes of work a week other than the paper and final.

Asynchronous, very helpful and understanding of students. Would take again for sure, learned a lot and used creative mediums to teach this class (podcasts, Netflix show, her own rap song, etc.). Definitely appreciated her as a teacher this semester.

One of the most understanding professors I have had and really understood how COVID is impacting us as students. Concepts were very interesting and she works hard to make assignments and papers engaging.

She is such a kind professor and grades very easily. It was online and very easy. Attendance was optional and we were only graded on 3 easy homework assignments a week. Definitely recommend taking her class if you need an easy GPA boost. She is also just such a kind professor and will always be understanding.
She is an amazing Professor and really cares about her students. She focuses on projects and gives amazing feedback and plenty of help on the projects.

I really enjoyed his course on Victorian England. He is absolutely hilarious, and gives good feedback on papers. He is very understanding and not too tough of a grader. I highly recommend prof. Epstein, and I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Epstein deeply cares about his subject, and he wants his students to do the same. This sometimes shows through aggressive emails when you miss a day of class, but far more often he brings crumpets to class or has movie nights at his house for assigned films. His lectures tend to ramble, but he knows his stuff and gives good feedback on essays.

Epstein is one of the nicest profs I've had. He cares about his students on a personal level. As a teacher, he knows his stuff and is pretty lax. I never felt strained, but the lack of pressure meant I didn't put as much effort in as I should have. Great guy, though, and I'd recommend him for sure.
Great guy. Definitely recommend taking his class. The only grades come from 3 papers and the classes are discussion based.

epstein is a really cool guy. his lectures seemed kind of arbitrary/disconnected, but at the same time he always kept my attention. his class was somewhat difficult but i enjoyed him as a teacher and would take a course with him again.
the best professor I had freshman year...he really cares about his students and is always willing to let you do a rough draft. he is awesome!
He is awesome!  Definitely knows what he's talking about, and very interesting to listen to.  Good sense of humor.

Professor Epstein is one of the best english professors. Although he is a tough grader, especially for a FYWS, he actually teaches you how to write. His classes are mandatory and your grade is based heavily on if you attend and are outspoken in class. Before his class I could barely write a paper, now I am able to and do not dread writing a paper.

The class was difficult, no doubt, but interesting as well. I learned a lot about writing and even though I didn't get the best grades on papers, I'm glad I took the class because Josh taught me a lot.
He used really helpful handouts and was easy to follow.
He's a tough teacher but you do learn how to write better.  Make sure you are active in class and ask him for help if you need it.

Josh is a really interesting person. If you happen to take this class, make sure you speak up cause he will mess up your grade if you don't. Say anything, he'll always respond with "that's interesting". Oh, don't skip his class cause his attendance policy will kill you if you miss a lot.
No Comments
No Comments
He is a good Professor but lowkey overrated.

actually the GOAT. love him. even though there were annoying ppl in our class he would still be so patient and kind to them bro i love him. there will always be something due before class (discussion or  a quiz) but theyre chill. i always thought the quizzes were pretty fair and you get a drop. + presentation, paper, couple of assignments.

Professor Wilkey is one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He is extremely thoughtful about implementing student feedback, and very receptive. His classes feel safe and he does a great job practicing what he teaches in terms of learning and teaching techniques.

Prof. Wilkey has lots of scholarly research papers, chapter readings, chapter quizzes, and group work integrated into this class. Participation is very important and things can definitely pile up if you let them. Overall he is a super great guy who is extremely knowledgeable and passionate.
Just an amazing and understanding proffesor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilkey is very entertaining and makes class fun. There are no exams, so you can zone out during lessons. Weekly quizzes on the reading, but easy if you read. Weekly article discussions that are also easy. Multiple projects and a final paper, but nothing is too bad. Overall a pretty easy class.

Prof. Wilkey is very caring and available outside of class. Lectures and reading could get dense and advanced. I appreciated how there were no exams, just (very) short quizzes. Some projects and papers but the expectations were clear and so was the feedback. Wilkey was always willing to go over grades too! Overall I was pushed and learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Instead of a actual textbook, he uses a psychologist's book for the course which was way more palatable. Every Tues, you read a chapter for hw, take a short quiz, and discuss. Every Thurs, you complete an article reflection and watch a group presentation. Overall I learned a lot and did not stress about my grade at all! Dr. Wilkey is awesome!

Dr. Wilkey might be the funniest professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt, he literally gave a Mariah Carey all I want for Christmas is you Vinyl away as a prize for best presentation in our class. The class is a good amount of work, but he wants you to do well for sure. Highly recommend.

Dr. WIley is one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. He genuinely cares about his students, is funny, and makes class engaging. Feedback is clear and there are no tests, only short article discussions, a few projects, and a final paper. Highly recommend. The textbook is an actual book with weekly quizzes, but they are easy if you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilkey is awesome. It is clear he really cares about students' learning, and he is overall just a great professor and a really nice guy. Class consists of weekly reading quizzes (easy if you read) a few short papers and a presentation. Grading criteria was clear and you will do well as long as you put the work in. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There were lots of homework (but honestly ChatGPT and Grok does 80% of the work for you). Exams are basically the shorter version of homework, so if you understand your homework, exams is not that hard. Professor cares about the student, class is easy going. Almost got Rick Rolled.

Dr. Barth is prob one of the best profs for control theories out there. Hes a great lecturer who can deliver clear and concise explanations on abstract ideas/concepts. Also, hes hilarious and actually cares about students learning experience; of course, very knowledgeable as well! He Rick rolled the entire class on 04/01 which was great lol!

Your grade is almost all exams, and they're not great. The homework is just time consuming, and usually needs you to read a week ahead to do any of it. Don't ask him any questions it seems like he doesn't know the answer to. He got real angry with a student for asking questions about homework. Overall, doesn't feel like he or the TA really care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had professor English 20+ years ago but am writing this review because I liked him so much. I probably took 4-5 classes plus an independent study with him. He was my favorite professor in 4 years in Vandy. A great lecturer and a tough grader but gave me the tools and inspiration to get good grades in his classes. Also very funny and personable

Don't take this class if you can avoid it. I took it for fun and regretted it immensely. The speeches are fine if you prepare and cite sources. His cross examination is intimidating, but he's a decent guy. The tests suck. It's 40 "name the 5 components of___" type questions. All free response and from the book not things covered in class. Dont skip

He is willing to help and gives a lot of useful feedbacks. He can provide you with good ideas of speech topics, but still you have to make a LOT of effort. All the speeches and exams follow each other so you might be stressful the whole semester. Lectures are clear and most of the stuff presented will show up in the three non-accumulated exams.

Didn't think that English was as clear as everyone mentioned here. Didn't give the clearest instructions when I went in with outlines, and in cross-examination sometimes didn't ask pertinent questions. This class is  A LOT of work -- research takes up a lot of time and there are exams. Didn't think it was super helpful overall.

Without a doubt the most beneficial college course I took!  Seven years after graduating, I still review the principles that Professor English instilled from this class.  Echoing what others have said and just good advice in general is to spend extra time with your professors.  Only critique, the tests made up way too much of the grade...

This class is what you make of it.  The syllabus is essentially non-existent and he comes off in class as being very harsh, but when you go to him he is quite helpful.  Taking public speaking is useful, of course, but if you can take it with another professor your grade will thank you.

CMST 100 with Professor English has been the best and most helpful class I've taken since I've been at Vanderbilt.  English is a tough grader and tries to intimidate you, but if you listen to him it will pay off.  Pro tip: Go to his morning office hours, he loves to see you go that extra mile beyond the extra mile by waking up early.

Great guy and a great teacher. Do plan on working a lot, and make sure you STUDY HARD for the written tests. You might not think a written test is a hard thing for a class like this, it is. He's very helpful outside of class and really just wants to see us succeed. I'll be taking his advanced class, though my GPA will not thank me.

I can't express how important this class is, as well as its teacher. Take the class, you won't regret it. Make sure you get your speeches done ahead of time, go to office hours, show interest, and you will be fine. Professor English tries to come off as scary, but he really isn't. He is the reason I'm a Communication Studies major now. TAKE HIM!

The best professor I had in at Vanderbilt. If you reach out to him and meet with him outside of class, you can receive a good grade. Go to his office ask for topic ideas, bring him your outlines; if you do this he will give you clear instructions on what he is looking for. One of the most interesting professors on campus and a great mentor.

Without a doubt, you will become a better public speaker after taking his class. He'll find all the holes in your argument, so prepare for cross examination, but his grading isn't that hard. Tests are straightforward as long as you pay attention to his lectures, handouts, and outline the chapters. Great professor. Highly Recommend.

After this class you will have confidence in public speaking, credible research and valuable critical thinking skills.  Prof. English makes attendance mandatory and has students write a 1-2 page paper to review and critique their own speeches which encourages self reflection and growth.  You will take away so much from Prof. English and this class!

I heard a lot of talk about him before taking his class, but I definitely recommend it. I took it first semester freshman year, and I think the skills I learned will help me through the rest of college. Yes cross-examination sucks, but he's so nice when you talk to him outside of class. Your grade definitely reflects the amount of effort you put in

Yeah, the class was hard. But it's definitely possible to pull off a good grade if you put in the work. Cross-examination is AWFUL but it doesn't actually count for anything. He's a big softie, and if you go to his office hours, you'll see that. Take this class if you're interested in communications! Non-CMST majors beware...

He is very scary when it comes to cross examination (I teared up once...). Very strict on his expectations and is really really strict about attendance and assignments. Tests are pretty hard too and require a lot of studying/reading out of the book

Professor English will make you an amazing public speaker. BUT, there are some negatives. His grades are incredibly deflated (one or two kids each class pull off an A-), and he refuses to even think of the possibility that a student could be right. He could use a class on acting much more humble. Became a great pub. speaker but not without a price.

If you don't take this class you are an idiot. Professor English is an amazing professor who will challenge you initially and if you heed his advise and put your heart and soul into your speeches you will not only becoming an immensely more capable public speaker, but also an immensely more capable student.

This guy is the man. He's a great teacher who will push you to do well and is willing to help you if you need it. Tests are tricky but not impossible. I've never taken a public speaking course before this and now I love it. Take this class if you come to Vandy.
Honestly the best professor I've ever had. You will have to work extremely hard on all 5 speeches if you expect to do well on them

Absolutely phenomenal.  Professor English makes his insanely high expectations very clear.  DO NOT take anything he teaches for an easy A.  Take his courses if you want to drastically improve your public speaking, debate, and research skills.  He is very critical and gives intense cross examinations. Meet with him during office hours when possible.

Challenging and tough, he knows how to push your buttons.  He's always willing to take time to talk about your speeches and he definitely pushes you because he wants you to succeed.  Very difficult class, but well worth it. Go to class and be on time - he takes points off for absence/tardiness.

Prof English really is cool... especially for his age. He expects a lot out of his students, but that's because he really wants to see them succeed. His lectures were always liberally slanted, which I didn't care for. If you don't like to work hard, avoid his class. If you want to become a great public speaker, don't settle for anyone else.

He's a doll if you work hard and make sure he recognizes that. He expects a lot from his students but respects hard work and is willing to work with you always. If he respects you you're golden. You gotta have a backbone for this class. Tests are tons of material but very clear what he expects. Speeches & cross -examination are hard but manageable

He certainly keeps you on your toes (he takes points off your overall grade if you're late/absent). Tip: be ten minutes early for his class. Also, he can really give you a hard time. This class requires a lot of work if you're not a huge public speaker.

Hard class but great teacher. Tests are purely memorization. Speeches are fun to prepare for but cross examination sucks. Really has an interest in his students and their skills. Has a great sense of humor... totally an old boy. Highly recommend the class even for non CMST majors. Definitely learn a lot that can be applied to any subject.

John English is amazing.  He is so sweet (tough love kind of class)...and you learn SO much. If you put in the effort, he sees, and he helps you improve. Anyone who says he loves failing students just didnt try in the class. Great skills for the "real world". Definitely take his class if you have the chance, you'd be missing out if you didn't.

I don't care what people say, I think he was a great teacher. He made us all into incredible speakers and was unbelievably kind and helpful outside of class. He knows what he's doing and, while most people hate how he does it, it works. You MUST take him if you're taking public speaking, otherwise you are just cheating yourself.

English is one of the most challenging teachers I have ever had. He pushes each of his students.  He puts on an act in class and comes across as a really tough guy but in reality he is great and really cares about his students. Tests are direct lists from book and notes. You HAVE to be on time. Probably will get an A-/B+ if you put in effort

Difficult, but as difficult as you think. If you previous speaking experience/good research experience you can prepare your speeches 2-3 days before and still come up with a B/B+. The test are kinda tempermental. I made a B+ on the first one, and I studied like 2 weeks for the other and made a C. Go figure. Good class though.

English loves to exert his intimidating, take-charge personality: From the first day of class, he greets you with "Welcome to Hell." Though demanding and never satisfied, he will teach you immensely about the subject. Every year, his students win the Houston speech contest because he is that good. I highly recommend him!

Tests are 90% memorization 10% guessing what he's going to ask about from the reading.  He takes off points for every class you miss with one grace day and points for every day you are late.  Grading on speeches is tough but you are graded on content as well as presentation so you can still get B's even if you aren't great at speaking.

Though every day in class felt like a rally for liberal Democratic Party, Professor English is the best person in the department teaching this course.  You will become a terrific public speaker, but unless you already are one, you will not make an A.  He will pick favorites early, so be confident, assertive, and postive.

3 words..he loves himself...condescending, rude, not a good teacher, everything is memorization, he picks favorites, prides himself in failing students...how the greek community voted him best teacher i have no idea...

I've ony been in this class two weeks and I already dispise him. He's very unhelpful and he caters to certain students (i.e. people who go an entire season only winning four games). He needs to relate to students better. He's extremely arrogrant and conceited. I'll give you a full evaluation when I'm finished with the class.

Definitely a good idea to keep up with the reading. The tests cover a lot of material, and is pure memorization. It's definitely a good idea to take 100 before taking this class especially since he makes a lot of mention of it in the beginning and points out people hes had before. But, overall, he's one of the best professors I've encountered here. Really will make you a better and more aware speaker.
Great class. Very direct. Hard nosed. A lesson in tact or compassion would do him good.
English picks favorites.
Really a nice and honorable man, but more disinterest in his students then one could know, and too much of a showman.  The most over-rated professor since Vrooman.

JE will make you a better public speaker.  No doubt about it.  He will be prepared with tough follow-up questions.  The tests are a waste of time, merely memorization of terms.  Class would be much better with just speeches, no tests.
very strict, not the most friendly professor.  you learn a lot though
I loved this class. All you need to do is memorize every list in the book for the tests, and for papers start early and practice! He has taught me more than any other teacher.
for 100 he's the best and the most difficult.  If you procrastinate you will end up beating yourself.  Keep up with reading because the tests are a ****.

English may be tough but I'd say he's also the best. For speeches, don't mess around- start early, and pick off the wall topics (he loves that). For tests, know the notes and be prepared to read the entire book.
He favors students who have already taken his other classes. The exams are straight memorization, and a ridiculous amount of content. He is extremely arrogant

Ridiculously hard tests and kind of intimidating, but a really funny guy and great to get into discussions with, if you can get over the intimidation.  I learned a lot, and improved my speaking skills, but the exams were the hardest I've ever taken.
Hard class, tough teacher but a really good one.  He's not their to hurt you or make you do bad, just pushes you to the next level. No tricks or games, but he is funny as hell.
This boy is tough, no doubt about it - but he's hilarious and you need to take his class for 100.  Period.
He's hard as Hell, and can be intimidating.  But if you get to know him he's an amazing guy, and he'll make you a much better public speaker.
very good knowledgable professor.  helpful.  learned a lot.
English is hard, but fair.  Probably the best you'll get for CMST 100.  Practice a lot and watch out for the tests.

The class wasn't engaging because all he did was talk to us. He made us read articles and excerpts everyday for omewrok, which isn't a problem. However, in class all he did was talk about them. he didn't really teach us anything.  He is still young so hopefully he grows as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very unprofessional and condescending in office hours and in emails. Absolutely irrational grading, and was unable to explain his own rationale for grading. I highly recommend staying away from Eric.

I dont understand why the reviews are so bad. Hes a nice guy and is obviously interested in philosophy. Very heavy workload and and often annoying grading scheme. However, he awarded a lot of extra credit and let us redo papers.

He is, bar none, the worst professor I have ever had. I took 5 years of philosophy before (with more educated and better teachers), and as a STEM major I just took this class thinking it'd be easy credit and it's the furthest thing from it. Be prepared for 2x 500-1000 word essays every week and the harshest/most irrational grading imaginable. -/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor often snaps at students and changes the class at will depending on his mood. The class is dead silent except for the hour long droning of his voice because we fear that expressing a different idea about the text than he does will lead to a more critical grading of our assignments. Short temper, hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the hardest class I've ever taken in Vanderbilt. I am one of the few if not only person who received an A but was only able to achieve this because I have taken upper level philosophy courses that provided me with the knowledge that the professor expects us to have. He dislikes questions or any ideas that conflict with his own. Hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hands down the hardest class I've ever taken in my life. If you are an HOD major do not for whatever reason take this class. The professor is fine but the content is incomprehensible. The workload for this class surpasses the combined workload for all my other classes combined this semester...

Professor MacPhail is lenient and occasionally pushes back due dates, but the work required of us is still unrepresentative of an introductory class. There is more work required in this class than upper level STEM courses. The readings are difficult to understand but he summarizes the content after quizzing you. Bad for grades, Good for Philosophy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is a must take course for any philosophy majors out there. This class covers the writings of all the important philosophers and the daily quizzes and worksheets require you to scour through the readings, forcing you to understand the material or risk failing. Very difficult for an intro class, but learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures can be dry because it is philosophy after all, but he does occasionally sprinkle in humor, making the lectures endurable. Would rate him a 1, but he definitely knows what he is talking about and just doesn't know how to teach a class. There are no clear grades in the class, but he does give a vague range that our grades may fall in.

This class has around a hundred pages of heavy weekly philosophical reading, along with brutally difficult weekly quizzes, and two extremely long and critically graded essays. The syllabus has changed dramatically since the start of the course, but it is too late to withdraw from the class so I am stuck with an extremely difficult course...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although his intelligence is clearly visible, his teaching ability is severely lacking. He does not follow the syllabus and decides to change the entire course depending on his mood. The readings are much too complicated for an introductory philosophy class, but if you want to learn about the most famous philosophical papers, this class is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is so much reading in this class, and the syllabus changes every day it seems like so you never really know what is due, what the grading policy is, or what you are supposed to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're planning to major in philosophy, this class is a good choice. You have weekly writings (2 pages), and two big papers. You get to pick the topic for all the essays, so if you like being told what to write about, it might not be a great idea to pick this class. He provides all the textbooks and is helpful out of class (reply might be late)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor York is evidently passionate about public policy research. While the content covered may be complex at times, she excels at making a class accessible to all levels of experience in research and statistics. I will acknowledge their final research paper takes time so please DO NOT PROCRASTINATE. Get started sooner than later.

Encourages you to think deeper into some of the course topics. Can be challenging at times, but the course is rewarding if you are passionate enough about it. Enjoyable class to attend and participate in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor York is talented and her lectures are okay, but her final paper is really tough. You need to go to office hours to ask for help; take it if you love to challenge yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework was pretty difficult, but Prof. York was accessible to answer questions and lecture slides helped a lot. Class discussions were helpful, and it didn't feel like we wasted time in class.

Prof. York is difficult but knows what she's doing. The final project is worth 40% of your final grade and the assignments are time consuming. The class lectures are interesting but hard to keep up with at times.
Great professor!

She is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. You have to go to class to understand what is going on so don't skip! As long as you do your work, attend class, and participate in class discussions, you will be fine. The assignments are also engaging and encourage you to think critically!

Super subjective grading and little helpful feedback to improve on future papers. Had a participation assignment with no available grading criteria, but graded it from a very explicit rubric that we did not have access to? Country Report as the final project, graded it as if it were a PHD dissertation. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Words cannot do Dr. Erving justice. She is the BEST professor I have ever had. If you can land a class with her, DO IT! You will not regret it. Vanderbilt got real lucky with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Literally one of the best professors, her lectures were so engaging. Lot of writing that piles up at the end, but it's just one research paper. 1000/10 recommend her.

Dr. Erving is truly a gem. Interesting and engaging lectures and such a kind person. You can tell she knows what she's talking about. Show up to class and do the readings (they're always a manageable length and interesting) and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor. Class is super interesting and if you do the work you will do well. Definitely one of my favorite classes at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: BEST class I've taken at Vanderbilt so far. The material itself was fairly easy but I learned a lot from it. Classes were engaging and interesting. Grades come from easy quizzes (if you do the reading), three exams, and a paper that was fun to write. A good class to take if you want a meaningful yet not overwhelming AXLE class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Erving is a gem. If you do the readings and pay attention in class (which is easy since she's so engaging) you can easily get 100% on the exams. She really wants you to learn the course material and she really wants you to do well. Def take her class if you have the opportunity- you'll learn a lot and get a little GPA boost in at the same time
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Erving. She's the best prof I've ever had. Genuinely cares about her students, and she is VERY reasonable in terms of class/student expectations. Do everything she wants you to do, and you'll be fine. Learned so much too. She's the reason why I'm a socio major.
Grade is three tests, three papers, and a few quizzes. She hands out As if you do the work

Professor Erving is excellent and her lectures are very engaging. She doesnt just spew out information, but she ensures that is is comprehensible and interesting for students. Be ready to read though; the readings are interesting although there are a couple of boring ones. Also prepare for quizzes, which are fairly easy if you read.

I loved Dr. Ritter! He is very caring, smart, relatable, and funny. I was amazed at his ability to connect different philosophy literature. All the readings were interesting and purposeful. I was kind of nervous to take Philosophy, but this was truly one of my favorite courses at Vanderbilt. I will definitely never forget Dr. Ritter and his class.

I took philosophy with Professor Ritter a while back now and can honestly say his class was one of the single best classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. This class tangibly improved how I think. Anybody looking for a strong introduction to Philosophy should try to get into his section. I HIGHLY recommend him.
Great guy and gives good explanations to difficult concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ritter's intro to philosophy class was one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. Before taking this class, I knew nothing about philosophy and received an A with minimal stress. I generally did my best to engage with the texts, and I learned a lot that I was able to apply to other subjects. He's super cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: honestly his low ratings dont make sense especially bc his rating was a 5/5 last semester so im guessing people assumed they could slack off but its still a class! you have to do minimal work and its very easy but at least skim the reading! he understands most people cant read all the assigned reading and he grades very easily. just do the work!

Cares a lot about his students and knows the topics well. I did not have a background in Philosophy but Dr. Ritter was able to introduce the concepts in an approachable and understandable way. He really wants you to get better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great guy
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He assigns an unreasonable amount of reading (we read 6 books this semester, with 6 more printed out readings) so we rush through readings that need to be delved into much deeper. Class discussions often get erratic and go on for the whole class period, and he dodges questions and often goes on convoluted tangents that don't make sense. Easy grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The course agenda changes very frequently so it is hard to know exactly what we will be doing the following class. There seems to be a lot of making up stuff as we go, but it is slightly irritating because we are given two days notice of a test. Other than that, content is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly this class was much harder than most classes I've taken. He is very soft spoken and appears to be very nice, but is in reality pretty strict with grading and assignments, regardless of a student's individual hardships (athletics, family problems, illness). Overall, the course is well created, but is a kind of scary professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I felt that this class was far more difficult than necessary. Although he says the class isn't graded on a curve, the tests and assignments' difficulties would increase or decrease based on the classes' average grade. Other than that, he is a very nice person and super easy to talk to. Easily reachable through email and he dresses veyr nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chill as hell Tiny class so its hard to skip A- with pretty minimal effort, and it fulfilled my goal of expanding my thinking

He gives a lot of papers and reading, but the reading is extremely relevant and he makes class discussion easy to follow. If you pay attention in class and follow along it shouldnt be hard to get at least an A-. He's also a really nice guy and easy to talk to (also super lenient with due dates).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Estes was great - he's spent his entire career in industry and brings in a lot of great guest speakers. The class wasn't easy but if you study and work hard an A/A- is definitely attainable. 1 Midterm, 1 final, and a couple projects make up the overall grade.

Investment Analysis is a class where you will have to work, but you will learn a ton. Similar to Financial Management in reward, and if you take these two classes you're probably good for FNEC. Estes has had an incredible career and a wealth of knowledge, so higher expectations are warranted. 100% worth taking.

Prof. Estes is a great guy and you'll enjoy lectures with him, but Investment Analysis is a lot of work. Not sure how other profs compare, but this class was unreasonably time-consuming.  Other than that, Prof. Estes definitely cares about his students, wants to help us learn, and brings a wealth of interesting real-world experience. Not a bad bet.

Lippman is the guy. Refreshingly normal, great lectures, just enough HW, accessible outside of class, straightforward tests with no surprises at all, very fair through and through, and he is just a reasonable person which is so nice. He's very busy so he just wants everyone to do well since it's less work for him, which I support.

Dr. Lippmann does a great job of writing out all necessary material and making it clear what concepts are important. He wants students to grasp the subject and does helpful examples and shows how to use all equations/formulas/graphs!
I don't know who thinks this was a good class but it was awful.
Dr. Lippman teach's one of the more tedious classes but he does an exceptional job of engaging students and making the material clear.

If you have the chance to, take Lippmann for Separations. His notes are well-organized and applicable to the course material and he does examples in class as well as Aspen tutorials which are both //extremely// helpful for homework. He has a relaxing voice. Solid guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The only thing bigger than Dr. Lippmann's biceps is his passion for teaching.  Great teacher and a great person.  Nothing but respect.
Very clear explanation, and a super-nice guy!

This is from Columbia, not Vanderbilt. Dr. Kim is the antithesis of pedagogical standards. I am deeply regretful of taking her course, Persuasian at Scale. Her lectures are superficial, and her communication with students is subpar.
Professor Kim is young, talented, and always passionate about teaching. Her feedback is amazing and she is ready to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is absolutely fantastic. Her lectures are clear, the material is super interesting, and she is willing to help after class.

Professor Estrada-Belli is really amazing.  You can tell how passionate he is about what he teaches, and it makes it so much more fun to listen to him.  As long as you go to class and put a little effort in, you can get an A.  He is very considerate when grading, as he understands not everyone in the class is majoring in anthropology.

He is so nice! Took this class for a core requirement at Tulane. Went to class everyday, and did great on the tests. His tests are extremely straight-forward and he is very generous about grading them. Definitely take, he's probably even more interesting if you actually like anthropology!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Estrada-Belli is a great anthropology and archaeology professor for majors and "just interested" students alike. He is amiable, extremely knowledgable and really wants to help people who want to know anything or everything about the subject. Also a great teacher in the field!!

This class has the potential to be really interesting, but Dr. Estrada-Belli makes it an incoherant jumble of random facts.  The correct answers to exam questions are voted on by the class.  He has no real plan with his lectures and the class just lacks structure.  If you've got other options, avoid this class.
I would like to add that I think Dr. Estrada-Belli is far less scatterbrained than Dr. Janusek

This class is awesome!  Definitely different than anything I have taken before...Prof. Estrada-Belli really lets you take it wherever you want...if there is something in particular that interests you...he is happy to discuss it.  I highly recommend this class! :)

really nice, funny guy, easy class, but definitely one of the most disorganized people i have ever seen....randomly instituted an attendance policy 4 weeks into the class, etc....overall, pretty easy for CPLE
Great guy! Entertaining lectures, easy straightforward test (2 midterms and a final), and one easy 6-8 page paper.  Based on this class, I'm taking his Old World class next semester

This class was very interesting,and since there wasn't much pressure to do well, you could sit back and enjoy learning. He had colorful, engaging slideshows, non-boring group discussions and reasonably easy midterm and final exam. Presentations were fun too, instead of boring lectures. He's very friendly and makes class interactive and engaging.
Very cool course. Only take it if you are really interested in GIS & Remote Sensing.
Very interesting class! He can get very scatter brained at times.
most def'ly easy on the eyes, the class was unclear and boring though
wow, soo full of himself, even if he is a nice guy. easy class.

Fairly easy class, just make sure to take notes because the notes posted online are worthless.  However, note are impossible to take because the material is so boring and the Hustler crossword puzzle is a good MWF distraction.  However, if you do the work, the class isn't too bad.
BORRRIINNGGGGG!!!! Though tests were ridiculously easy....most boring class in the world....i feel as if i didn't get my money's worth!!!!
too hot to handle...

While anth 104 was a good intro class, anth 217 left something to be desired.  The content barely scratched deeper than anthro 217, and EB left it up to the students to present almost half of the material for lectures.  as well, as a major with an archaeological focus, i say that the word "archaeology" in the title was a gross overstatement.  Strict archaeological interpretation never came into play.
Egotistical and too disorganized, but easy grader.
Awesome when it comes to passion, but very disorganized. He will help after class, very nice guy.

While he may be easy on the eye he is so BORING and disorganized and not at all clear.  Yes, he loves archaeology, but he also loves himself a bit too much.  I'll take organization over easy grading any day.
he's great, he knows his subject and loves anthropology
Great prof., covers interesting material well and with lots of visual aids. Relatively easy tests based almost completly on lectures. Grading done by TA's. Take for Soc.Science CPLE req.
If you want to talk mayan go to this guy, but make sure you appreciate his good looks.
Hot?  Not even a question.  Also very interesting. Worth any boring moment just to gaze at him.
No Comments
Taking this teacher would be a terrible mistake. Avoid her at all costs if you want to save your sanity, GPA, and time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Heo is just not a good professor. She fails to explain things in a conceptual way, instead relying on graphs to do all her lecturing for her. The curve was generous, but Heo mentioned at the end of the semester that it won't be that way for future ECON 3012 classes. If you can avoid her, do so.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Heo is one of the best professors that I've had in the at Vanderbilt. Some material that professor Heo teaches might be above the heads of some Vanderbilt students, but if you actually attend and pay attention, she makes it as easy as it can be.
Professor Heo is obviously smart, but she has trouble giving that info to students. She's a bad lecturer and makes little sense. The tests also made no sense and feedback was not helpful.

I had this class in its first year in existence. Avoid it if you're allowed to (i.e. if you started at Vanderbilt before the Fall of 2018). I got an A- because she gave a very generous curve, but she indicated that she'd be getting rid of that, so.... She just can't explain things well at all; she's brilliant, but not an effective professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pretty darn tough course. Heo's class is more difficult because she expects more from you as a student. Certainly learned more in this class than I would have in another section. Curve is generous.

I have no idea why ratings for Heo are so negative. In my experience she's a solid professor. Lots of people find her tests hard (the last one had a median of 59 before a curve), but with the curve, only two people had anything below a B. She gives practice exams and pertinent hw; read the book, do the hw, go to class, and an A is totally doable.

Aside from murky grading scales and dry lectures, this class was pretty decent and not very difficult. Heo is quite helpful during office hours, and gives practice tests before midterms. If you put in the work, a good grade is very achievable. Also, her accent is very understandable.

Excellent teacher. Super nice and understands the material well. Sometimes this leads to her teaching over students' heads . But if you have any problems, go to her office hours. She's very patient and will take time to clearly explain the concepts.
Really good.
Avoid her class!! You will learn nothing from her course. I would not recommend Heo to anyone. Absolutely horrible. very arrogant!!

theres a reason why this person got these horrible reviews lol. Apparently i cant give her 0 so i gave her 1, but zero is what she deserves as an instructor. I'm a decent student with a nice gpa, still struggled because the class structure and the instruction was awful. Just dont take her, there are many other good professors you can have.

AVOID AT ALL COST. She doesnt know how to lecture, period. Probably a nice person, but a terrible professor. There is a reason why everyone is telling you not to take her. Thank god the TA is helpful.

The syllabus for this class is in broken English. Her teaching ability is SEVERELY restricted by her inability to adequately communicate in English. Be warned, she has a significant language barrier. As a result of this communication issue, the lectures were virtually impossible to follow.

Professor Heo seems to have a solid understanding of economics , but her teaching ability is SEVERELY restricted by her inability to adequately communicate in English. Be warned, she has a significant language barrier. As a result of this communication issue, the lectures were virtually impossible to follow. I would not recommend Heo to anyone.

As much as I want to say positive things about Heo, the reality is that her lecturing was very unclear. Some of this is excusable due to the language barrier, but she also gave almost no example problems to help us understand the concepts. The whole class did horrendously on both the midterm and the final... At least she curves. Avoid if possible.

The syllabus for this class is in broken English. In lectures I often wondered if I was taking Econ 231 or introduction to Korean language.  Unlike Drake, this professor was quite literally the worst I've ever had. So bad that it made me resent Econ and question my decision to major in it.
Absolutely horrible. Literally do not even ponder the thought of checking this box on your YES account.
worst teacher i've had at vanderbilt. does not care about students' success and has very unclear lectures. very arrogant and takes it out on her students. tests are nothing like the class material.

Dr. LeBoeuf has high expectations but leads a high quality class. Homework is time consuming. Exams are very fair in both content and grading. He is accommodating to students and wants everyone to succeed.
Do not go late to class, do not let your cellphone go off during class, and do not turn your hw in late. Don't do the above and you'll do pretty well in this class

interesting introduction into civil engineering. didn't intend to be a civil engineer and still do not plan to be one. project took alot of work, but fairly easy concepts with some practice. TA was really easy grader, so just BS your way through the class.
Nice guy. Attempts to make Civil Engineering interesting. Work is simple math and using Excel. Like all other ES140 classes just BS your way through with some effort and you'll get an A

Very nice guy. Definitely is a bit naive sometimes. You don't take notes...just stare at slides (which doesn't work for an 8 am class). The TA for this semester is terrible though. If you did not get a homework problem completely right, the TA rolls two(or three)dice, and whatever the sum is, that's how many points he takes off.

He is a model professor. He cares about his students but doesn't let you slack up. If you go to class and study you will surely get an A. He sometimes can be naive about how much work he is giving you, but just talk to him and he will be more than accommodating. Classes are informative but pretty chill.

Large homework load, tests are harder than posted years' past.. but seem easy when you go over them.  He typically drops a hwk grade, and you can exempt the final if you make an A before the final. He is out of town alot, but his TAs are typically pretty good.  Go to class and get to know him, and he'll like you - always a perk.

This class was SO BORING. He just read his slides to the class. Also, he held us 5-10 minutes late EVERY SINGLE CLASS DAY. "Sample tests" from year before are really simple; the test you will actually take is really hard.
He will thank you for coming to class, which makes no sense.  Maybe he thinks he's awful?  Well, he isn't.
This was the most boring class I have had at Vanderbilt.  Made me not want to be a civil engineer for fear that I might have him as my professor again.
Real chill guy, interesting and easy class on engineering ethics
No Comments
I loved him!!! he is a super duper professor, fun to talk to!! you defininely must take him! and.. really hot ;)
Had him for a seminar... he was super boring
Excellent professor.  It's too bad so few of us get to be his students.

Pretty good class. No big issues. Got questions answered right after lectures. Only went to office hours right before the exams, and it was pretty useful. Just pay attention to the lectures, and you don't have to study for that long.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Game theory is supposed to be fun. However, lecture examples are a bit repetitive and presentation is not too engaging. Nonetheless, you will get all the FUN questions during EXAMS (might not be fun if you see ur grades though). Also, practice sample exams doesn't mirror difficulty of actual exams :(

Kirill is awesome. Class was inherently a bit challenging, but he wants to see you succeed. Lectures aren't the best, but I expect them to get better as he gets more experience. For a required class like 3012, Kirill is a great prof to take it with.

Solid professor. Genuinely nice, chill and funny, but needs a lot more experience to make lectures more structured and engaging. That said, the exams and grading are fair, and he is very clear about what to expect with practice exams. His notes are great too. Goes out of his way to explain concepts

Class structure was 25% HW / 50% 2 midterms / 25% Final with cheat sheet. Compared to other profs he's probably a good choice, but I agree that lectures sometimes felt erratic and I had no idea what was going on. He is a nice guy, pretty funny in a Russian way, but the class is hard and you do have to study and seek help. Class is curved to B+ avg
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Game theory is awesome with him, a bit of an erratic lecture style but content is so fun if you like math. Tests are hard but graded fairly.

Really chill guy, brought us cookies as motivation for the final. Helps you build intuition and does not hesitate to slow down lecture to ensure everyone truly understands the concept. If you actually attend lectures and take notes, it's not too difficult to do well in the class. Only downside is that syllabus is pretty test heavy.

DO NOT TAKE MICRO WITH KIRILL! Not only will you be set up for failure in his class, but for all the classes that build up on micro. He was all over the place during lectures. He made a lot of mistakes that ended up confusing me so much I stopped going to class and used his notes to teach myself the material. First midterm class average was a 74.
Legit best econ prof I've had, willing to work with students with deadlines, exam weights, etc. Super funny too and he brought homemade cookies to the last day of class

Professor Evdokimov is one of my favorite professors based on all the courses I have taken so far. He cares about his students and explains things clearly. People who are complaining might just be lazy and don't want to put time and effort to learn the materials. I find the lecture notes to be clear. The university needs more professors like him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very approachable professor. You can even reschedule the final if you want. The attendance is highly recommanded because the reasoning taught would be used in exams a lot.Tests are not easy if you are  not good at reasoning and thinking out of the box. Not a hard grader and your grade is negotiatable if attending his OH and letting him remember you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was his first semester at Vandy and he took every opportunity to improve the class. However, I found his lectures hard to follow and disorganized, though his notes were better There were often mistakes in his lecture/notes that made things confusing. I taught 90% of the content to myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Evdokimov is genuinely a good professor. Not perfect, but this was his first semester teaching, and he improved a lot. His lectures are good, but I found that it was still necessary to review the lecture notes myself. If you have strong mathematical reasoning, you'll do well. Tests are very similar to the practice tests he gives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On the first day, he said his class would be harder than the other sections and more calc heavy. His lectures are hard to follow and expects you to have taken a high level calc course even if you only took 1200 & 1201. He gives a practice exam before the exam that is very similar to the actual one which is helpful. You just have to teach yourself.

Lecture notes are really helpful and he gives so much practice with homework problems and the practice exam so it is not hard to get an A (though 80% of your grade is exams). He's also a very nice and chill person and wants to make sure students understand. It's only his first sem teaching but he's probably the best Econ professor I've had

Professor Evdokimov is a really nice professor. He cares about his students and gives amazing lectures. Easy A class. The exams are pretty much based on assignments. Will definitely recommend people to take this course!

dude is a chiller. cares a lot, exam content incredibly clear (basically a mirror of the practice midterm he provides). first semester teaching and rate of improvement was astonishing. lectures a bit messy at first but pretty clear now.

Dr. Goldberg is one the most well-respected men in all of Nashville. Taking his class was enlightening. He tried flirting with my girlfriend at a frat party but other than that he has been nothing except kind to me. I still stay in touch with him. he is a caring person
Best professor at vandy loves his students and hangs out at frat row on the weekends

Goldberg is a fair, yet stringent professor. He really wants everyone to succeed and is accessible outside of class, but his exams are very difficult. If you do all the practice tests and go to his office hours you should be fine. In my opinion, hes the best professor for THTR 3891 especially if you get to know him.

Dr Goldberg is the sweetest man god ever made. He saved my building from a burning cat child before completing his PhD in indefatigability, snake oil sales, and perfunctory illusions. I distinctly remember an autumn evening in his gazebo of a lecture hall when he gestured like a school boy to his crush and made a subtle crows chirp warming my soul

Dr. Goldberg is very intelligent and displays strong expertise regarding makeup. He is unclear of the guidelines and when you ask how to prepare he just says "kitty cat". For the eyeliner assignment, we had to use protractors so make sure you have the proper materials for this course before taking it. Take this class but be ready to work hard.
Just saw Dr. Goldberg rizzing at a party. Tough grader tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Saw Dr. Goldberg do an impressive keg stand last weekend. It was one minute fifty four seconds. I do remember seeing him sit in a lawn chair for the rest of the evening. 
Though grader. He's super specific about how he wants you to do cat eyeliner so make sure you go to office hours.

Professor Goldberg is such a gem! He's incredibly thoughtful and caring in class to his students. Giving him an overall rating of 3 because one time he threatened to break a students knee caps for asking how tall he was. What he lacks in height he more than makes up for in lecture. If you get the opportunity please, please, please take his class.

Dr Goldberg is one strange boy! He made us refer to him as Prince EVAHN, or he would put is in the corner of shame during class.
I took his class called "Hair and Makeup" and he taught me how to slay a cat eye and how to properly line my lips. One class he got so angry a student didnt refer to him as prince, he threw his dyson airwrap at his face.

Prof Goldberg is a harsh grader. One time I went to his office hours and he laughed in my face when I asked for a curve. DO NOT INTERACT WITH HIM unless you want to be absolutely ridiculed!!! Don't underestimate him because of his height, he can get quite angry!

There once was a prof named Goldberg, quite short,
Whose teaching style some did purport,
He loved pop quizzes,
With acting, he's the bee's knees,
Outshining The Rock in every retort!

Dr. Goldberg, a Vanderbilt Theatre sage, though stature small, knowledge vast, tech-savvy in the modern age. With humor akin to Shakespeare's jest, his pop quizzes put us to the test. In makeup class, we found our muse, a professor whose wit did amuse!

Dr. Goldberg, oh what a marvel to behold, In the world of theatre, he's pure gold. Though not very tall, his talent does enthrall, A giant of inspiration, he stands so tall. A legend in the making, With every performance, the audience is quaking. Master of his craft, a true sensation, In the world of theatre, he's our inspiration. tough grader.

DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR GOLDBERGS CLASS!! there are genuinely some sicknesses that I would rather contract than attend his class. DOES NOT CURVE GRADE AT ALL (avg. was a 69.42 :////) he is the meanest grader i have ever met and does not teach the material at all (be prepared to learn eevrything yourself!) proceed with caution!!!!
