Allow me to share a memorable anecdote: One day, Dr. Goldberg spontaneously transformed a fellow student into an elderly character. We were all amazed by his incredible talent and artistic flair. It was a moment that inspired us to push our own boundaries in the world of hair and makeup. Waittttt this made me miss him, guess I'll stop by his office

Dr. Goldberg was an exceptional professor during my time in the theatre department, specifically in the area of hair and makeup. His teaching style and expertise left a profound impact on me and my fellow students. However, there was one thing that always kept us on our toes - his infamous pop quizzes!

Professor Patterson is actually amazing. Her classes often have a lot of assignments however on multiple occasions she gave out extensions or adapted the assignments to be easier. She cares about her students deeply and as long as you participate and do your work this class is an easy A. Everyone should take a class with her.

Was a tough grader overall and very unclear with what her grading criteria was. She gives enough feedback after the first few assignments so that you'll eventually know what to expect, but she should be more upfront about what she wants. Slightly condescending towards her students and doesn't really make it a comfortable space to ask questions.

The worst class I have ever taken. I rate 1 just because there's no 0 on rmp. Her class is very confusing, and the grading is not fair. It's hard to communicate with her. She makes students feel anxious and insecure, which I feel of being targeted in her class.

Thought the class was interesting, but she does not respect students, is not considerate, and clearly picks favorites. If you disagree with her, good luck, she doesn't forget. She targets certain students which makes for an unsafe and uncomfortable learning environment. Her grading is so arbitrary and based on her opinion of you and not your work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is an expert in her field. A great amout of readings and they are sometimes it's hard to finish reading before class. However, you can definitely learn a lot from the course, both from readings and lectures. Also, she cares about her students very much and would postpone the ddl if most students cannot catch up. She does grade harshly, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the most researchers in the area of criminology nowadays. You can definitely learn a lot in her lectures and the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Patterson is a very kind person and an excellent professor. She is extremely willing to help outside of class and prioritizes learning over grades. There's a decent amount of reading and attendance is mandatory, but the class was overall easy and if you make an effort, you'll get an A.

Professor Patterson is a very caring person. She prioritizes learning over grades. That being said she will slow the course down if the class is confused by certain topics. Definitely go to class, its a good mix of lecture (a little boring) and lab (learning to use SPSS). Do the reading. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! She will work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Funny in a strange way. Bit odd but in a good way. Tends to ramble about whatever crosses her mind, but I thought the course material was very interesting. It's not necessary to read all of it, but it is pretty eye opening. Somewhat of a tough grader but visit her office hours and show her you care.

Professor Patterson is an interesting professor. Lectures are usually interesting but she has this habit of just voicing EVERY thought running through her head and will sometimes just flat out talk to herself in front of the class. Sometimes funny, sometimes weird. Kinda tough on grading but the class was fun and I actually learned a lot.

Professor Patterson's class was by far the most interesting of all my classes, and it was very eye opening.  There was a decent amount of daily reading, but most of it was interesting.  She was always pretty flexible with due dates and very understanding of the stress that students face.  It is clear that she cares about her students and the topic.

Professor Patterson's class opened my eyes to things I had never considered concerning how people's lives are influenced not just by individual choices but y social forces. Her knowledge is endless and you really feel like you are being taught by an expert who also is totally down to earth. She has high expectations for herself and students.

Professor Patterson is one of my favorite professors I've had at Vandy. She does a great job at getting students interested in what she's discussing. She is very knowledgeable and makes the subject easy for students to understand. We wrote several papers, but her feedback on them was very helpful. I would definitely recommend taking this class.

Professor Patterson is one of the most enlightening and informative professors at Vandy. She delves into some of the most relevant and sensitive topics we deal with in society, while shedding a comedic light that makes the class pleasant to attend. Professor Patterson may be critical, but she always emphasizes learning over academic success.

I took criminology with professor patterson and the class is pretty relaxed, there are only two tests and after that its basically just student led discussions and short papers on readings- lots of reading assigned- they are interesting but no sweat if you don't do it since the student led discussions summarize whatever reading is due that day.

Very dry and boring lecturer, but promotes class discussion. Class is an easy A if you just do the work, she grades very fairly. She is ambiguous for the midterm and final, but it's not hard stuff. You don't need to read, just skim and you'll be fine. Nice person, extremely interesting class material. Definitely a class to take.
I feared this class and Dr. Patterson actually showed me that not only couldI learn the materials but they were relevant and even interesting.

I don't suggest taking Patterson for Stats. She teaches straight from the book but quizzes you on the book material BEFORE the lecture, so class is pretty pointless--but you have to go anyway for the pop quizzes. Problem sets are tedious. I'm not great at math but the class was SUPER easy (content-wise), and I barely learned anything.

Evans lectures were by far my favorite lectures. He lectures super well, explains things well, and covers content in an interesting manner. He is an incredibly tough grader though which is reflected on his homework and exams. You just have to show a good understanding of the content and apply it at a high level to the question being asked.

Evans is awesome, clearly cares a lot about the material and makes what would be an otherwise boring class quite interesting and relevant. Class is lecture-heavy but he's more than happy to stop and talk about questions for half the class period. Assignments aren't bad, exams are graded kinda steeply but class is curved. Participation encouraged.

Professor Evans is honestly exactly what you what from a professor. He's passionate, excited to answer questions, constantly makes real world applications, and is honestly just a really nice guy. Assignments are graded by accuracy but given there's only 4 the entire semester, so the time commitment is pretty light. Curves whole class up at end.

I have no background in Econ but find Prof. Evans' lectures and the course content to be incredibly engaging and relevant, making participating in-class easy. You are evaluated on 4 homeworks (10% each), 2 tests (one 20%, one 30%), and a subjective eval (10%). Assignments are straightforward and graded reasonably. Highly recommend!

Professor Evans' class was unexpectedly my favorite this semester. He works hard to make material interesting, challenging, and relevant to his students. His teaching style and assignments are engaging and make you think in positive ways. I highly recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Evans has great lectures but is not clear at all in his expectations. For example, you'll complete your first assignment with no instructions as to what he expects in your answers and will probably get a low grade. There are only 4 homework assignments, midterm, final exam, and a "subjective evaluation" (participation and attendance combined)

He explains everything really well and will answer your questions very clearly. Homeworks are harder than actual tests. Difficult concepts at times but it is all very interesting. Would definitely recommend.

Evans is pretty notorious for being a bad lecturer, which I do not deny. However, he makes up for it with his generous grading. It's not an easy A, but as long as you study how to solve the problems in the textbook, you will be fine. The group project is also graded generously, based on effort more than anything else.

Really nice guy, wants the best for all his students. That being said, the class is pretty brutal. It's not that hard (most exam questions from the book), but he just does not teach very well. His class is one of those that just seem to never end. Material isn't that difficult, but hws can be obnoxiously long. Group projects are dry

Evans has a good personality and will try to help with questions. However, he doesn't seem to understand the material fully himself, and will often struggle to answer questions raised. Additionally, the lectures are virtually pointless and students usually just do other work. I would find a good study group because it will definitely help.

Evans is super nice and very willing to help but he doesn't seem to understand the material enough to help you. Class periods aren't productive because he doesn't seem to plan them ahead of time. The homework each week takes forever and then is graded super harshly. If you haven't had experience with a similar software, this class will be hard.

Evans seems like a great guy, he just shouldn't be teaching at a collegiate level. He doesn't seem to know the material before he comes into class and is often scrambling to figure out for himself what to do in the modeling software he teaches (Creo 4.0). That being said, the material itself isn't too difficult, so his class is definitely doable.

The homeworks are too time-consuming and are graded harshly (by an external grader). The material isn't taught clearly and many lectures are spent doing tutorials that could easily be done in other time. Class can be spent more productively.

Evans is a nice guy and cares about students... But, he should not be a professor. He would be better off as a 2nd grade teacher. Seriously. He doesn't understand the class material and (obviously) can't explain it. Didn't learn a thing. Attending the lecture will allow you to do other homework. Mechanics of Materials with Professor Mazita helps.

She's fun and interesting and very chic. I would definitely recommend taking a class from her but not necessarily Phonetics. Phonetics is hard because French doesn't really have a standardized pronunciation system- it's regional. Thus, her grading on tests is inconsistent. The amount you study doesn't correlate with how well you do.

Eva is a great teacher. You will learn more in her class than in any other professor's class for introductory French. SHe is very helpful and really knows what she is talking about. If you make an effort in class and have good attendance, this class is great.

Wonderful! It was my favorite class & I feel like I know so much more of the language even though I took some in high school. Don't be tardy & be sure to come every day but she is very nice & wants everyone to do well.
Never prepared. She rambles on about stuff and smiles if you ask a question, but she has no idea what she's talking about. She's friendly, but it's scary to see how she's wasting our time.
She is extremely nice and helpful! Not the easiest grader, but if you keep on top of your work you will learn a lot and most likely end up with a good grade.
Great professor! Loved it..
No Comments
No Comments

Mlle Eva Dessein is a great teacher!! She is young,easy going and a lot of fun and HOT !!! Being french she knows what she is talking about, and is very clear. Eva is always ready to help out and will makes time for everyone. there are a ton of assignments in this class and she is not an easy grader, but everyone loved her!!!!

Honestly, she's a great teacher, although tough grade-wise. As a senior who only needed this one class to graduate, the workload could be intense. However, over the course of one semester with her, I improved my writing more than I had in all four years at vandy. She's also very accessible as a prof and person.

As previously mentioned, the workload is atrocious.  Having papers due Friday at 8pm is a great way to put a damper on your Friday night.  That having been said, she gives you tons of comments on your writing and is generally very helpful.

Professor Hunter is definitely not an easy grader, but you will likely leave the class as a better writer.  She allows you to do corrections on all of the papers and she grades the final website project much easier than all of the essays.

Worst class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. Each text is dense, paper due every week, had to create a web page, had to do multiple peer reviews, was graded on participation, and had to write 3 big papers. Sound fun? Absolutely miserable, I start convulsing whenever I see her on campus again.

Amazing! Course is entirely paper based with one single page paper due a week. She's a hard grader and makes you work for the grade, but she also allows you to correct any paper you get below a 90 on and literally resubmit it for a new grade. Such a wonderful and fun teacher. She really knows her stuff and likes teaching.

Great class! I'm so glad I took orgo 2 with her in fall instead of spring. She's very nice and helpful during her office hours. She printed out the notes for us and made study guides that helped me prepare for the test. Take her section if you are able to!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy class. Enjoy her class a lot. She is really helpful. Try to talk with her during office hour will definitely help you a lot.

Eva Harth is genuinely amazing. Organic Chemistry is always going to be a tough subject but she is willing to help you if you show her that you're committed to working. By far the best science class I've taken at Vanderbilt, over gen chem, bio, and physics. If you have the opportunity to take chem with eva- do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She's a great teacher. I'm so glad I took organic 2 with her this semester instead of taking orgo 2 in the spring. The tests aren't too bad. The study guide and looking over class notes helps. She is very helpful during office hours. There are moments that she appears a little scatterbrain, but I really loved having her as my prof. highly recommend

She is one of the best teachers I have had so far at Vanderbilt. She seems a bit unorganized at times, but it is part of her charm. You need the book. You need the notes. All of it helps. She is also easy on the eyes  (even from a girl's perspective.) I learned a lot and would take this class again. Highly recommend.

Harth is firstly very kind and always helpful. Her class is not as challenging as the other section and does not prepare you as well for the next semester. If you go to class and office hours, getting an A is not difficult. Lectures are often unclear and repetitive. I found myself very dependent on the textbook.
Awesome professor and one of the nicest ladies you'll ever meet. Know the material you're expected to know and you'll do great. Made chemistry fun and always willing to help!

Dr. Harth will help you and give you all the tools to success. Her tests are a bit unclear, but her study guides allow you to prepare very well. Attending lecture isn't mandatory, but by doing so you will know exactly how her tests are written. Easy quizzes every Friday. I recommend Dr. Harth if you want a decent grade in Organic Chemistry.
You would definitely get good grades in her class if you understands the material well.
Gutte

She has a bit of a rough accent and makes mistakes writing on the board..  but she gives super easy quizzes that she will literally give you the answers to, and the tests are straight from the notes. Easy to get a good grade if you just memorize the notes... dont really need the book except to correct a few of her mistakes. good class to take

Nicest.Professor.Ever. Take notes in class and memorize those notes and you will get an easy A. Try to learn on your own and you will fail. She is very unprepared and jumps around sections a lot, but what she tries to teach, she teaches it well.
Professor Harth was always willing to help! She's an excellent teacher and made organic chemistry actually fun/not unbearable. I would definitely recommend her!!

Can't speak english, can't teach, totally unclear, comes to class unprepared.  She also grades subjectively based on how much she likes you, and her grading scale changes on a daily basis (no joke!).  She screwed over 2 of my friends by giving them a B+ when they clearly had a 90+ average in the class b/c she felt like they "did not deserve an A-."
She's nice, but sometimes unclear and taking notes is confusing.

Not recommended if you're serious about a future in chemistry, as understanding her lectures may be somewhat difficult.  Otherwise, this is a great class and a great opportunity to take off a little bit of the edge that comes with the typical weed-out orgo class.  Very nice lady with a very nice grading scale.
She's a very good person, Im not good in organic chemistry, but she's very helpful and always willing to go out of her way to do things for you! I would highly recommend taking her!

Awesome professor! The most helpful, concerned teacher I've ever had! Sometimes unorganized, but putting forth the effort will make you really learn the material. Tests can be stressful to prepare for, but, like I said, just make some effort and you'll be fine. Incredibly nice lady and fun to talk to. She knows her stuff!

Nice person, but horrible professor. Unorganized, boring, & unclear. Can't understand her train of thought when taking notes b/c she can't explain things clearly at all. She's very confusing - you don't learn anything from her, you have to teach yourself. Only consolation is that her tests are easy. Just glad I never have to be in her class again.

One of the best profs I've ever had at Vandy. Nicest lady ever, really fun, and makes a dry subject enjoyable! She is so helpful outside of class and really wants you to do well. Her tests are tough but fair. Take her class!!!
She's pretty disorganized and her lectures can be hard to follow, but it gets better as the year progresses. Tests are too easy with an insane scale, if you study you'll do great.
Got to love her grading scale.
Very engaging, a little reading/lecture heavy but discussions are so enjoyable I hardly notice.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fay is AWESOME! She encourages original thinking, helping you generate novel thoughts and never-before-heard connections between films and literature. You will learn so much in this class that no other class at Vandy covers. Grade consists of 13 discussion posts, 3 papers, and class participation. Class participation is really important to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fay is an incredible teacher. Even though the course is a little bit writing and reading heavy, it is all necessary work and it didn't feel like busy work at all. She engages with the class and really takes the time to get to know us. If you are considering taking the class just  go for it!

Fay is one of my favorite profs at Vandy. She runs a spectacular lecture and discussion, and always has amazing insights for weekly screenings. Fay has great energy and enthusiasm, and she's always open to hearing you out. She's very considerate and fair about assignments, and definitely cares about her students. If you're in CMA, don't miss out.
Professor Fay is very nice, but I found the class itself quite boring and she was difficult to learn from because it seemed almost as if she played favorites.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The face of the film studies department, Professor Fay is knowledgeable, passionate, and can come off like a cat lady. Her classes will teach you an incredible amount and if you put in the necessary work, you will have an unforgettable experience. She tends to take heat as she is tough (not what some expect for intro film) but she is a real gem.

Professor Fay is a wonderful, enthusiastic professor. She teaches with such excitement and joy, which really gets students more interested. She is engaging and very intelligent - you can tell she knows what she's talking about. Great class, not easy though she's a pretty tough grader.

Clinical Ethics is SUCH a cool class. Professor Fanning brings in guest speakers every week to talk through complex case studies and share perspectives from the field. Readings and discussion posts each week, but you can skim the readings to respond to the lead post and it's basically a completion grade. Three papers throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you're unsure about this class- take it! Completely changed my perspective on death and dying and allowed me to talk openly about a difficult topic. Dr. Fanning's lectures are excellent and he brings in guest speakers who are motivational and impactful. Lots of opportunities to do well and papers are actually interesting and fun to write.
Favorite class at vandy so far! Super nice guy and a really interesting subject area that we don't talk about in academia enough - definitely would recommend it.

Prof Fanning was super sweet and the class is very interesting. The guest speakers were definitely the highlight for me. There is an outside of class volunteer component to the grade so keep that in mind. Overall, a unique class- I just found it a bit boring at times. Few grades determine your final grade.

I enjoyed this class. Unless you totally hate math, the class is fairly easy. Ezell's lectures can be hard to follow, but he is very helpful during office hours and will explain things until you understand it.

I LOVE EZELL! he cares about you more than you could ever comprehend, tries his best to teach a difficult subject, and does all he can to ensure that even the worst students end up with a decent grade. LOVE HIM
Not too bad, if you understand statistics. The tests are hard but he curves them VERY generously. Problem sets arent bad either, I would definitely take this class

Ezell is goofy, fun, and really intelligent. BUT, this stat class was not easy. Problem sets suck, tests pretty challenging, but he is AWESOME about curving grades. Very generous grader. Helpful in office hours. OK for AXLE math req. If you study and go to class you can probably get an A. Works on prob sets with a partner.

Basically had to teach myself everything in this class. He is not very good at explaining things. In class its as if he is speaking another language and then if you ask a question he makes you feel like an idiot. Don't take this class if you are trying to fulfill a math requirement, its not worth the extra work you have to put in.
Professor Ezell is a really nice guy and extremely funny. He is a good grader and generous with points. More importantly he is always available to help. I think he is a great teacher.
Horrible.  He doesn't use examples, which makes learning impossible unless you're already good at math.  Makes you feel like you're an idiot and seems to get angry when you ask questions.  NO-GO.

HE IS AWESOME! I am not kidding, nobody in the world is less interested in math/stats than I am, but I loved this class. He is one of the most helpful professors I have EVER met, and is so accommodating. I would take stats again just to have another class with him.

He wants you to do well, and is always available--like he's in his office at like 6:30pm. He makes stats fun, even at 9am--which can't be said for most professors. Highly recommended. Awesome. Go to his office hours--that's the difference maker, and will set you apart from someone just passing and someone who gets an A.

Ezell was a great teacher.  He is such a nice guy and he was so lenient when it came to grading papers.  He really taught me how to become a better writer and was really interested in how his students were doing during their first year in college.  I would def. advise that freshman take this class for their writing seminar.  No quizzes or tests.

Incredibly nice guy. We watched some videos, and he was always very helpful. He is pretty lenient on grading papers, and even lets you rewrite a few. If I would have tried harder, I could have got an A. You don't have quizzes, but he will see if you are reading every once in a while with worksheets.

I don't know why everyone seems to have such a problem with him, either.  I took Juv Del with him, so maybe he's a lot different in the stats classes but as long as you do the work and go to class you'll do fine!
You have to go to class and take notes...his tests are really hard but he has a HUGE curve.  He's VERY helpful outside of class!

Ezell is great! His class is interesting, but also challenging. If you put in the work, you will be rewarded with a fair grade. I would definitely take a class with him again. For those who had a problem with him, it must be because they did not do all the work, which he cannot be blamed for.
Be scared. Very scared.  You may not fail...but you might not pass either.  He is very confusing and cannot be trusted to teach you squat!
We need more professors like him. I did pretty well in the class and I'm going to medical school. Thanks Ezell for thinning the herd...that's the way Darwin would have wanted it.

The rumor was that this guy wrote STATA. Truth be told, I think he was married to STATA. Overall if you did the work ahead of time, you could get through the course but if you waited until the night before you were screwed.
AWFUL. Completely not helpful. Gets mad when you dont understand. Hardest class Ive ever taken. Stay away seriously

I've taken Ezell for Soc127 (statistics), Soc232 (juvenile delinquency), and Soc212 (social research).  The subject matter of the courses he teaches is very technical and difficult.  But, Ezell is a very nice guy and is always available for extra help.
I regret the day I signed up for his course.  I will never take another class with him again.  Everyone I know who has taken him feels the same.

Hated this class!  This was my least favorite class I have taken at Vandy.  The test questions were ambiguous and related to minor details that were barely mentioned in class.  The amount of reading was overwhelming.  Overall:  Terrible!

Hilarious guy! Always trying to make us use Stata when it's clearly for professionals. SPSS works just as well!!!!!!!!! Assignments aren't always clear. If you explain them before hand we won't have to ask all the time.
Not helpful in or out of class. Not nice, and not understanding.
Very brusk and rude with students.

This professor has absolutely no idea how to teach at the undergraduate level.  He has violated the dead week rule by giving us a huge problem set due on reading day.  He has also violated us by giving a take home and a regular 2 hr exam.  Be scared.
No Comments
Maybe he's okay in the non-statistics classes he teaches, but for this class, RUN. RUN LIKE THE WIND. Seriously, avoid him if at all possible. He is not nice, and he refuses to help students.

Faulk is an awesome professor. He was so funny and nice! The class is very understandable and it is easy to do well if you put in the effort. The weekly homework really preps you for the tests and the extra credit opportunities help a lot. Faulk is super accessible outside class so definitely go to office hours before tests. He is the best!

Faulk is the best teacher I've had in the math department. His lectures are very organized and give you a good working grasp of the material. Very accessible for homework help in office hours, and also very understanding about my illness during exam season. Nice guy, solid professor for only his second year teaching. Would take again.

Professor Faulk wants you to understand the material, but isn't out to give you a bad grade. He has weekly homework that is only around 10 problems of ranging difficulty. His tests are very difficult, but he gives a generous curve that makes it hard to get worse than a C on an exam. Test averages are usually around an 85.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is mostly lectures, most yanked from the textbook. The take home midterms took hours to complete and have some moderately confusing questions.

Very nice and friendly person, lecture are also great. Tests are VERY hard, usually with class average of 60. However, he curves the grade into a perfect normal distribution with mean 80 and sd 10, so you can still get an A is you did relatively well. There is also weekly group problem sets, which if you got bad teammates, it can be VERY annoying.

He made a take-home portion of the test that counts for 25% of the test grade but literally takes at minimum 12 hours to complete and 30 pages of JUST explaining math. He teaches content extremely well but the problems have literally barely any relevance to the content as he makes the problems extremely geometrically based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: professor faulks class was a rollercoaster, but in a good way. his take home tests will both make you feel enlightened after solving a question and then make you want to rip your hair out when you see the next one. start those early. while the tests are difficult and lengthy, he grades fairly and is accessible outside of class for help.

Faulk is an ok choice for diffeq. He's not the best lecturer; I often had to learn from the textbook because his lectures are hard to follow. Faulk's main strength is that he's not a tough grader. The last couple midterms and final are take home, but he puts a pretty nice curve on them. The take home exams take a lot of time, so start on them early

Too hard to grasp. A tough grader who cares too much about the details. The lectures are not clear so I must study on my own. What taught on the class is basic but the tests are too tough, with a lot of extra content. Hard for a student to follow.

I think all the negative comments are just freshmen who took the class after doing calc BC and weren't prepared for college coursework. While the class is extremely diffcult, faulk goes out of his way to ensure conceptual understanding, grades fairly, and curves so the grade distribution is exactly fair. The homework is really hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hardest tests out of all the professors that teach 2300. Average grade is around a 50 for each quiz he gives but he applies a massive curve. His group homework is near impossible and incredibly complex, which he grades for accuracy. If you haven't taken a multi class before and just want the credit his class is not worth the struggle/migraines.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would only take this class if you already have knowledge of multi var because he still does not know how to lecture. His curves are by far the biggest but that's only because the averages are usually in the 50's without it. There are weekly group challenges that are basically impossible and weighted too heavily. Tests are way too long and hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: He makes super hard tests. Avoid Faulk at all costs for 2300

Made what should be basic concepts complicated and confusing. Group projects were way too difficult, especially during a COVID semester. Tests are hard and too long for the time given, with raw average scores often in the 50s or 60s. The curve will help your grade, but it won't make you feel any better about still not understanding anything.

Would not recommend Faulk for Math 2300. Seems like a nice guy but his lectures are extremely confusing and he makes little sense when explaining things. Tests are crazy long and extremely difficult. He also introduced group challenges on top of long homework assignments that took hours to complete and extremely difficult material beyond the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests were difficult but he was very generous with partial credit and there was a curve. Emphasized conceptual understanding instead of just throwing formulas at you which I liked. Also helpful in office hours. I could tell he was still getting the hang of lecturing (it was his first semester teaching) but that didn't hinder my learning at all.

Tests are the hardest out of all MATH 2300 professors. Nice person but sometimes fails to explain some concepts clearly or even understand them. Homework takes a long time as well. Midterms are 50% of grade and final is 25% of grade but both have small curves.

Problem sets/ homework takes forever, but they're helpful and generally and easy A which is nice cause HW is 25% of the grade. He's a really nice guy and extremely smart, but the tests can be really difficult. Tests are generally curved out of the highest score. The class is not impossible, but it's definitely a lot of work.

Half the class took 1301 so it goes quickly. HW is graded for accurary-grader sucks-and very long, due weekly-work ahead! Tests are long and much more difficult than other prof but if you do hw and pay attention you'll be fine and he also gave partial credit. His lecture was good and he explained things well but near the end hardest part he just eh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst professor ever at Vanderbilt. After getting an A in 1301 and 1300 I am going to get a C in Mitchell's class because he has no conception of how to teach. He never gives good answers to questions and awkwardly laughs things off. Most freshmen in the class have taken multi so he makes the tests really hard. He just sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong, she cares about her students and what she teaches, but is sometimes passive aggressive and isn't very good at teaching. Every other class follows the same notes, but she does her own thing which makes it hard to follow along with the guided notes. She messes up on her own examples sometimes, which can get very confusing.

Thought she was a nice person and cared for students. The class is not very difficult because there are opportunities for grade revision. The lectures are very disorganized. She often starts an example, then gets confused by the example, before finally giving up on it without telling anyone.

Would not recommend her if you have alternative choice. Super nice, super supportive, but awwwwwwwwful lecture. Simply read the textbook instead of wasting time in class. Grades are easy A, but I learn almost nothing :(
Challenging content but very easy grading; Prof. Fernos is very nice to students but no one understood her lectures so be prepared to self-study for an entire semester

Took Professor Fernos for Math 3200. The lectures can be very sporadic at times and will often drift away from the intended content, but have the potential to be very interesting nonetheless. Her tests are very easy and she does an excellent job at preparing you for the questions you will see with the homework and practice problems.

Talia was one of my more caring professors. With that said, sometimes the lectures would get confusing and carried away. Questions asked by students also seemed to be often left unanswered. Allows for test corrections and is very accessible in office hours.
Great at teaching the intuitive and formal basis for linear algebra.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor does not know how to teach linear algebra! She will make mistakes during lectures and students will point out the mistakes before she even notices she has messed up. She does not have patience for questions and does not answer questions clearly.

JUST STUDY THE HOMEWORK AND PREP PROBLEMS SHE POSTS. Every test the questions were taken straight from the homework or straight from the midterm prep she posts. It's straightforward once you accept that it's not that deep.

Fernos lectures from her notes, but gets confused easily, sometimes derailing class for a while, confusing everyone else, only to realize her mistake later. Exams are hard, and you have to mostly self teach from the textbook as she expects you to know everything. If you want to understand content and listen to good lectures, take someone else.

Class: New, interesting concepts. Weekly homework, lots of proof reading. Regret not going to math cafe.

Professor: Helps a lot in OH. Lectures can feel disorganized, it partly on me for not doing the pre-readings. She's lenient when making the exams given the topic. Exams are close to the practice problems. Plenty of bonus on homework & exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Every class with her goes like this:
1. She attempts to lecture from her notes
2. She gets confused by said notes and makes an error
3. She gaslights herself and the class that there is no error and tries to continue with the proof
4. It doesn't work, so she tells you to convince yourself that it's true.
5. GL self learning abstract Linear Algebra!

Professor Gutierrez is excellent! His lectures were by far the most interesting of any Econ class at Vandy--possibly of any class I've ever taken. I learned SO much and actually felt engaged. His tests did seem tricky at first, but he curved a lot in the end and offered extra credit. Would recommend.

Professor Gutierrez is a nice guy, and clearly tries to make the class fun, but the semester was such a trainwreck. His lectures are incredibly dry and unorganized, and his exams were simply way too long to do well on. The final exam had more to do with random last-minute readings than anything we talked about in class. Really weird.

He is very knowledgeable on the subject and his lectures are very clear and thorough with many examples that really drive his points home. However, lectures are dry sometimes so it can be difficult to follow along and some of the problem sets can be difficult. He posts the slides online from lecture.

Learnt more about Stats from his course than I did from 2 other courses combined. He is an extremely nice person and teaches to the point. Starts out from basic before getting to the core of each concept. Even brings dice to the class to help explain some statistical concepts. Shows how passionate he is to explain things as simply as possible!

Once you get past the accent, he's not a bad professor, at least in Development Econ. 2 tests, a final, homework, participation with occasional quizzes (so be sure to show up to class), and a group project. Tests are over lecture slides and homework - isn't too hard if you study those. He doesn't try to trick you. Easy class.
I  liked his classes very much. Be ready to work hard but classes are interesting and you will learn a lot.

He is a very good professor. He explains the material and he is very clear when explaining new concepts. He provides good examples for each new topic. Exams are long, but he is fair when grading and gives extra points for participation in class. I would take this class again.

He explains very little in class but expects the students to know a lot. He focuses on very simple concepts in class but makes the exams extremely long and difficult. The TA was a Chinese guy named Nam, who was even less helpfulknowledgeable than the professor. None of them deserved to teach at Vanderbilt.

I don't know if we attended the same class as the previous graders but the Professor is one of the most helpful and has the most thought out class material. If you put in above average effort, you can walk away with atleast an A-
Incredibly boring class and very unhelpful professor. I would stay away.
Terrible professor. He barely speaks English and refuses to help students whatsoever outside of class. Do not take this class whatever you do.

He is really smart, however since he is transferring to another university next year, he seems a bit lazy and demotivated. Still, the examples he gave were much more clear than those in the text (which is horrible). Tests were easy if you understand the material (basic concepts of linear algebra) and do practice problems.
He's horrible at explaining concepts and makes tests disproportionately hard compared to homework. Also gets off topic a lot.
Good professor.  Relatively probably one of the easier math professors.  His tests are hard, but if you do the homework, you should do fine.  Also, he curves a lot at the end of the course.

Easier than some of the other professors. Do all your homework and you will be fine. Daily quizzes which are just one of the homework problems, great grade booster. 20% quizzes, 80% tests. Tests he wrote were just like the homework. Highly recommend.

this class made a subject I love feel like a chore. She is a really, really difficult grader and it seems like if you don't write exactly what she wants to hear and already believes, you'll come out with a C. Felt so defeated after repeatedly getting bad grades on writing I was proud of. Also hard to keep track of grades and how she calculates them

Lots of reading and writing. If you don't like writing about books, avoid this class. If you love literature, then this class is for you. I cant stand writing on novels, so this class was a challenge for me to put myself through.

I took the first year writing seminar. She facilitates great discussions on the books that really go in-depth on the  material. There are quite a few novels and plays to read, but you are given adequate time to do so. The class consists of only three essays, so make sure you put a lot of effort into them. Great class.
Great teacher! She is unfailingly kind and generous, and she gives prompt feedback on all papers.

No not take this class unless you are prepared to spend 4 hours on reading in preparation for each class. Tests are hard and on very very specific details from the reading. Class itself is very interesting and discussion based.

She knows what she's talking about, however material is presented in a very confusing manner and discussion topics bounce around way too much.  There are many articles and books you have to read to be able to pass the exams and write the essays and you have to have a high level of analysis on these works.  Loved the professor, hated the class.

Dr. Fesmire is amazing! I've had her for two classes, and she does her best to keep them centered on discussion focused. She also provides in-depth comments on papers that have done wonders for my writing.

One of my favorite teachers at Vanderbilt. Attendance not strictly enforced, but going to class will let her get to know you which helps. Grading can be tough, but the subject matter is interesting and she is incredibly knowledgeable and willing to meet outside of class to meet with students.

Professor Fesmire made me fall in love with WGS. I was scared to take the class after reading this site, but she is amazingly kind and cares about her students. She lets students contribute a lot to the supplementary material as well. 150 is the prereq for the WGS major, so it isn't the easiest. But a great class! She also loves when guys take it.

I had Professor Fesmire for WGS and really loved her and the class. She's an intelligent and passionate woman so that made the class all the more exciting. WGS really changed my perspective on a lot of things (lol axle pun.) She may pick favorites a little, but she doesn't force you to speak if you learn better by listening like me! Great class! :)

Professor Fesmire teaches a good class - 100% class discussion. The book selection is great. Plus, she bakes brownies. However, she is very subjective, opinionated and definitely picks favorites. She is a tough grader but does allow for re-writes.

The reading selections in Classical World Literature were very interesting.  She explains the material well, and the class discussions were good.  Her grading isn't the easiest, but if you pay attention then once it comes time for the paper it's not so difficult.  She lets you revise if you're not happy with the grade.  Plus, she bakes brownies!

Fesmire has a dry, sarcastic sense of humor, which I love. She bakes us brownies and doesn't mind digressions from the reading. Grades tough, but truly cares about her students. Not sure about her Gender studies classes, but this W class is a lot of fun. Several major papers and lots of reading responses to boost your grade.

Assigns a crap load of reading that is completely ridiculous. Don't have to read it all... but the 3 tests are mainly identifying and analyzing the hundreds of passages read. So your choice. The tests are hard. The papers, however, aren't too bad. The class is over all okay but requires way to much work for what is for most an elective.

Fesmire is great at leading discussions in class and definitely favors those who talk more. A lot of reading and writing is required for this class and the grading can be confusing and intimidating at times; however, she offers a lot of help in office hours. She is passionate about her subject and enjoys students who do (or pretend to do) the same.

She is a very nice professor who gets to know her students and makes class interesting. However, her grading is very subjective and tough. I had all A's or A-'s going in to my final paper, yet my final grade was a B+. She doesn't keep a paper trail of grades that is accessible to students, so good luck with your grade, but she is a good professor

There is a lot of work for her class (at least one reading assignment for each class usually and quite a bit of writing), but she is a great professor and she knows her subject very well. The readings were interesting for the most part, and I was usually excited to go to class. She is a bit of a tough grader, but she will often allow for rewrites
She is very helpful and genuinely interested in both her topic and her students!

Very good professor, interesting and you can tell she loves the subject she was teaching about. However, it is VERY hard to understand exactly what she wants (what she wants is very specific) and very hard grader.

Professor Fesmire is very knowledgeable about the subject, and you can tell she's enthusiastic about the subject. However, the class is a LOT of reading, but as long as you read and pay attention in class you'llknow what she's looking for and do well. I'd take another one of her classes.. I think.

I'm still trying to figure out why I took this class. I was a feminist until I had the information crammed down my throat 100 different ways. The world is not always as she sees it, but unfortunately if you don't act like it is her way...your grade drops...just agree with everything she says and you will do well!!

it is not a very difficult class to get a B. if that is what you are looking for than it is extremely easy. But if you are looking to get an A it is pretty hard. I found that she has a very narrow mind on what she is looking for on her tests. You practically have to read her mind to get full credit on the questions or to get an A even if you study

Prof Fesmire is fun to take.  She is interesting, open-minded to any stance you take on any of the readings, sarcastic (but not in a derogatory manor) and  very hepful.  My only advice is to speak up in class and have strong opinions because those type of students are the ones she warms up to best.
some interesting books, however, there were a lot of obscure handouts that were a bit tedious to get through.  the class was not really waht i had expected.

Prof Fesmire is a great teacher, she keeps the class interesting and allows for alot of open discussion. She's a very nice lady and if you have problems very open to discussion. Freshman: this is a great class for you! Males dont be afraid of WGS you may just learn something!

She kinda reminds me of a English/Humanities version of Econ's Steven Buckles.  She's quirky and funny, but you can tell she thinks highly of herself and is used to having her butt kissed.  Be prepared to do things her way, but the class was interesting and worthwhile.
Dr. Fesmire is awesome.  Western lit was really fun, especially the class discussions.  I encourage everyone to take her classes whenever possible.

A great professor and lovable person-generally very friendly and interesting in an upfront, flippant way.  Sometimes goes on tangents expressing her views on political issues and/or celebrity gossip, but allows the class to participate.  A fun and worthwhile teacher.

Shakespeare Film was my favorite of 5 classes. HW was to watch movies, how can it get better? Fesmire, that's how. She loves talking about any topic, debating and analyzing anything and everything. Very open-minded and a great sense of humor. A lot of writing (some difficult), but it is a W course.

Fesmire is really great.  If you are concerned with a grade you received and really want to redo because you know you have something better in you, she might just let you.  Also, she encourages you to sit down with her and work out your thesis statements until they are well crafted and smooth.

She is a very difficult grader, especially for a CPLE class. The exams and essays are complex topics that are guaranteed to make your head spin. She's entertaining, but when you're pre-med you can't afford 3 hrs a day to dedicate to her class & its assignment load.
Definitely my best professor! I would recommend her class if you like a lot of discussion!
She's an excellent teacher with an ability to make even the most tedious topics scintillating.  I'd recommend her to anyone.

Prof Fesmire is funny and witty and makes the material come to life. Essay topics are challenging but you can use your notes and go to her for help. I definitely recommend this class, its a great overview of western literature and she has great insights into the texts. SHE's GREAT!

She was a difficult grader and her essay topics were probably the most convoluted things I have ever read.  She types two whole pages as a prompt for 1 essay. Although she is really cool and her class discussions are interesting, the course is lacks focus
Although the class was a lot of work, she's a very fun professor.

I really enjoyed this class.  The reading load was heavy and some of the books were slow, but Fesmire always keeps the class upbeat.  She is a fair grader and is really engaged and interested in the material.
Reading heavy class, but Professor Figal is very knowledgeable and a super nice. You can tell he loves what he does. He was a somewhat tough grader, but class is always super chill

So much personality. Really made me enjoy the curriculum. Never read for the class and still got A- on almost every paper. Not too tough of a grader. Really recommend him. Only huge problem was the zoom discussion at 8pm on Thursdays. Really inconvenient timing.

Figal is a great professor. Very fair grader and engages in discussion. Definitely go to his office hours. Class consisted of 4 smaller papers and two larger papers (midterm and final). Lectures can feel long some days. I highly recommend taking his class if you are looking for an interesting social science credit.

Would definitely recommend taking this first-year writing seminar over any other. You watch a ton of anime with little reading and write 3 papers with rewrites over the course. Was not difficult at all and rather enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Figal is amazing. He is very knowledgeable and passionate when it comes to Japanese culture. You will have the chance to not only learn the big important chunks in lectures but also very cool trivia bits from his own study abroad / travel experiences in Japan. He does go on a lot of tangents, but then again, even those are pretty interesting.

Pretty notoriously awesome teacher on this campus. Course is extremely interesting and beneficial no matter who you are and he does an excellent job of guiding you along. Readings were very reasonable. Class is worth going to and by the end of the semester it was the only class I still attended.

Figal is incredibly smart, but this is a cause of some of the issues in this class. He rattles all the lectures off of his head and doesn't have a powerpoint or anything. Hard to take notes when he is very scatterbrained and skips around time periods. He expects too much from his students in terms of grading, but is a very genuine and caring guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's not very good at actually teaching. In lectures, he spends very little time on specific points in time and skips 50-100 years at a time. There's no real theme to each lecture; he just talks. The tests cover some information that isn't covered in class or in the online text. I found myself having to rely on wikipedia for studying a lot of it.
By far one of my favorite classes/teachers

Self and Cyborg was a really awesome Freshman Writing Seminar. Prof. Figal is fun and his discussions are always interesting. He can be a little blunt at times, but I really loved his class overall. The movie screenings were a lot of fun. Take this class if you have any interest at all. You won't be disappointed.

Prof Figal's anime class is an eye opener. You will find the animes as bizarre as they are exotic. 2 books assigned but are optional, mandatory screening every week. Generous grader and spends time helping students on writing. I wish I could take his class again but alas I am afraid I won't have another chance since I am an engineering student.

He is really funny and although sometimes a little awkward, he will make class worth attending. He taught the Pre-modern Japan class and made it really easy and interesting esp since I hate history. Very easy grader as long as you kind of know what you're talking about. Making a A-, B+ is very easy. Definitely worth taking his class.
Generally easy grader but you really need to be interested in Japanese Animation and watching a film every week is kind of tedious. A B is easy to pull off but an A will take much more effort.

Prof. Figal is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about teaching. He always has a joke on hand to help explain an idea, or just for fun. He grades reasonably and is always upbeat. His FYS class on Japanese Animation is awesome and he makes Premodern Japan about as fun as it can be. Take his class!

I took his Honors seminar, and the class was interesting. He is a very enthusiastic professor who is always willing to help you outside of class. The only fault I can pick with him is that he grades rather unreasonably. He doesn't give 100% for anything even if it's perfect, which really screws your chances of getting a solid A. Harsh grader.
fantastic, fun, really loves teaching, spends time helping students
Figal knows a lot about his subject, is enthusiastic, hilarious and awesomely awkward.
Very energetic about Japanese History!  Great Professor all around.

Professor Figal is wonderful! His class is interesting and intriguing, yet the workload is not unreasonable at all. You have to work hard around test time and when writing assignments are due, but it doesn't require an insane amount of time otherwise. You come away with a thorough knowledge of Japanese history. Professor Figal makes class very fun!

Ok, I smoked this guy's class.  His grading is horrid, but if you play to the left he loves it.  The worst thing about him is his total arrogance.  Anyone who has his class and has to read his blog, etc. will recognize this.

Prof. Figal's a great guy and knows lots about Japanese Popular Culture, though I and others might feel his grading to be a bit random.  Caution, however.  Many many many outside viewings of J-pop films required, which can be a pain.
No Comments

She requires a ton of work outside of class and really values participation and showing up. Sometimes it's hard to know what exactly she is looking for, but effort and participation matter a ton. Fun class, but deceptively difficult and time consuming
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Filsoofi is very kind and understanding. Sometimes the assignment guidelines are a little vague, but if you contact her, she is willing to clarify any misunderstandings. She grades mostly off of perceived effort rather than the quality of work, but obviously she still expects you to try your best. She makes the class feel like a family.

Dr. Filsoofi is by far the best professor I have ever had. There is a lot of time you have to spend outside of class to finish projects, but it was a nice break from tests and was very relaxing. She is a very sweet woman who is willing to work with you if you need accommodations.

Super sweet and kind professor. Really fun class and a nice break from lectures and other classes. Raheleh does expect you to spend a decent amount of time in the studio outside of class but is very reasonable. Expectations and assignments are not always super clear but easy enough to figure out and get an A in the class.

Class lectures don't really help, but they're fine. She is kind, fun, and insightful based on her experiences. Class is a few online exams that can work with in group and a few APA papers that require some work. Not much work outside of class but fairly easy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was entertaining and interesting and Prof. Fike is great! One day a week with Fike and one day a week with a TA. The class material is easy to follow and the final grade is composed of papers, tests (open note and take home), attendance and a few easy dicussion posts. I would recommend this class with Prof. Fike it was great and easy!
Very chill class overall. Test questions were confusing but the course content was easy and straightforward. Everything graded by TAs, so if you have a chill TA you'll do great.
If youre trying to take 1250, she is the best!

TAs grade everything. A whole bunch of reading if you take it all face-value, but learn to read efficiently and it won't be an issue. Take lecture notes and the tests will be easy, but they're open note/book anyways. Lectures were hilarious and made meaning of the readings. Dr. Fike has such a rich personality, and I'm glad my 1250 was with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Arbitary grading, irrelevant reading assignments and boring lecture. Do not recommend

This is a joke of a class who should not be taught in any college classroom. The content was jumbled and I feel like I've learned nothing after the class. Test questions are designed intentionally to trick you, lectures consist of slides-reading and assignments are extremely time-consuming.

Professor Fike was the best professor I have had at Vandy so far. The class is super engaging and she really allows each of the groups to have fun. She is very knowledgeable and contributes a lot to student discussions. Grading was pretty fair and she made sure you knew what she wanted on each assignment. Some of the group project grading was tough
By far the worst class I've taken in 3 years at Vandy. Stay away.

Class isn't even taught by fisher -- he just sits in the audience as his grad student struggles to get through often incorrect slides/information, with quizzes that have mistakes genuinely every time. how is this allowed man.
Not too bad but don't expect to learn anything from lectures. Slides are disorganized and not a good resource.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Group projects and homework quizzes are easy but exams, especially online part, have a lot of tricky conceptual questions

Class is very dry and Professor Douglas is clearly not a great professor. Did not understand his explanations in class. Only take this class if you are somewhat interested in the material. Other than that, he is clearly passionate about it.
Side note, he is very passive aggressive in his emails. Made a stressed out student feel incredibly bad.
Nice professor, but wouldn't recommend the course if you're not interested in automata theory at all - course load is above average and quizzes and exams are hard
The tests and quizzes in this class are like one multiple choice worth 100% points, so it's 0 or 100. In the end, you either get an A or get a F.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only take this course if you are actually interested in the course material, if you are then you'll enjoy it and won't have too much trouble with it. The professor is passionate about this class and teaches it well, though can get off track sometimes. Office hours can significantly help you out if you need it.

Very dry lectures, unclear grading criteria for projects, students generally learn everything from the textbook. Do not recommend this class. Highly encourages us to use ChatGPT, but somehow I learn more from GPT than from this class.

Professor Fisher is a good guy and quite accommodating. 
The material is incredibly boring, useless, and complicated, coupled with a lack of effort or inability of Professor Fisher to explain it well, makes for a super rough class. The saving grace is that the grading and assignments are quite reasonable. I strongly recommend you to avoid it.

2.5. Tough course, okay lecturer, not okay enough for this course. The Final is super detailed, and the professor did not cover everything. Good thing is he seldomly ask TopHat in my year, which allows me to audit Roth's section. He is sometimes humorous, and clearly not focused enough on teaching this course.

2201 is a very difficult class in general. Only programming experience going into the class was 1104 so I struggled on the first exam and first few projects. The projects take anywhere from 5-15 hours per week. Take professor Roth if you can, Fisher is alright but his lectures are harder to follow and he doesn't get through all of the content.

Had for Computing & the Environment, liked him a lot, and got an A in the class without too much effort. Near-weekly readings and quizzes, and the quizzes were hard--often asked about minor details in the readings. Group project wasn't graded too hard. There was also extra credit opportunity. 4 absences allowed.

Fisher is a genuinely nice guy and a solid choice for 2201. Some of his lectures were a little unclear, and he didn't seem to know as much about the programming assignments as Roth. However, he offers Extra Credit and definitely rounded my grade up, so that was really nice. Overall, Fisher is very chill, but the class itself is quite difficult.

Unclear grading criteria. The class was pretty useless, the project turned out to be just two search algorithms that we implemented. Instead, the 90% of the class was student presentations about mostly stuff that was barely related to AI, regarding a made-up game that wasn't even fully implemented. Avoid if possible.
Horrible professor, awful assessments, changes the course requirements every week without telling students. Overall, hopelessly unaware and useless teacher.
terrible textbook, but definitely an easy class
Sometimes he has trouble explaining things in class, but he gives good grades to everyone in his CS2201 class. So if you want to get an easy A, definitely take his CS 2201 class.

Professor Fisher's course is organized poorly and he does not curve grades. He expects students to watch video lectures and come to class yet he rarely teaches in class. The Racket programming assignments were terrible. He's also very inaccessible outside of class. His test count for a lot, make sure to do well on them. He is friendly though.

He barely teaches anything and expects us to read almost everything from e-books and online videos. Its fine that some teachers in colleges do less and put more heavy load on students, but its NOT OK to simply put the "teaching" task itself on the hands of the students.

Not a great professor. He barely teaches in lectures and expects you to learn through online courses. His homework assignments are very vague and convoluted. He takes a simple subject and make it overly conceptual. You barely learn how to code in SQL. His grading criteria is confusing and very specific. Test are not too bad but not great either.

Doug uses an open textbook available online for free. Though some of the material is a bit dated, it's an intro class. Tests are based on being able to do the problems discussed in lecture. Whatever you do, do not procrastinate on the final project, it semi-killed me. Doug is a great guy -- he wants you to succeed but you also have to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Perhaps the worst class I've done at Vanderbilt overall.

Okay, so you learn less than nothing in class. You're forced to watch online videos of other colleges. Tests are multiple choice only. And extremely difficult. There is not one positive thing I can honestly say abut this class.  You're better off looking at the online video yourself, because those are good. I can't figure why he teachers this class

He's a very nice guy, but you will have an A until the last week of class, and then he'll screw everyone and you'll end up with a B. He's never there when he says he'll be in office hours, and if he is there, he'll tell you to post your question on the message board. It's frustrating

He is an alright guy, but the class seems easy until about the second to last day of class when everyone finds out they have a B-. He always says he'll have office hours but he isn't there and even when he is he says to post whatever question it is on the discussion board. Don't take this class if you can avoid it

I like the guy, but I just don't think he teaches things very clearly.  He always asks questions but never has answers.  A lot of it has to do with the fact that databases suck though.  201 was much better.

Quirky, funny guy. The material is horrible though. Go to class or you will get lost for the whole semester. Tests ranged from hard to simple, but the programs were the hardest assignments I've ever had. Jesus... a HUGE step up from 101. Nice curve at the end, but overall the class is pretty forgettable and the book is terrible. Good luck.
Boring lectures coupled with excruciating tests and programming assignments makes this teacher a piece.  He is a nice person and all, but he should try NOT being a teacher.
Great guy who is a good professor, but teaches two of the hardest CS classes material-wise.  That's a tough thing to do
Lectures are B-O-R-I-N-G! Nice guy but bad subject material.  CS101 is not enough background and is the only pre-req.  Test averages for the year was a 53.  Good curve at the end of the class though.

His lectures were very unhelpful and taxing.  Tests were tough (probably because the lectures were so unhelpful). Assignments were vague and any help given was purposefully incorrect.  A shining example of why tenure is a BAD thing.
No Comments

Worst class ever. Tries to be funny but is not at all. Horrible at providing examples and provides erroneous code as help for programs and claims it wasnt a mistake but to make you work hard on the programs. Test are extremely hard. Most averages were 40
No Comments
he's a nice guy when you talk to him outside of class. pretty cool, rides a harley :) but his lectures are BO-RING!! nearly died when i took 201 with him...
Nice teacher, but boring lecturer
Very funny and very passionate about her field. The class was very enjoyable, and I would love to take another class with her. Great professor.

She is super passionate about concrete (the subject of the module) and loves to teach. 100% take the module if you are at all interested in civil or if you just want a free A. Grading is very easy and she assigns very little hw. She is awesome and there is so much she will teach you if you are curious to learn!

Dr. Sanchez is SO passionate about concrete and she'll share that with you. The class is fun and focused on the group project of designing a block within her guidelines. She'll teach you about 3D design and efficient construction designs. The class is graded easily (because she wants you to do Civil), and you get to 3D print your block and test it.

Dr. Sanchez is very funny and passionate about concrete lol. She's super cool though. The engineering module is very easy. It's heavy on group projects though (if its the 3-D print cube one again) and attendance is taken + many activities for grades are done in class. But she sets assignment deadlines to an hour before class for some reason...

Dr. Sanchez is my favorite! She reminds me of Dr. Troxel a bit. Her lectures are extremely clear and although her tests can be challenging at times, if you do all your HW, pay attention in class, go to her office hours for help, and do all the problems on the handouts she gives out every lecture, you will be more than fine! She ROCKS!

Fantastic professor.  I'd take Fluid Mech with her again in a heartbeat.  Her lectures include a little bit of derivations, explanations of how to use the material, and practice problems.  Homework due once a week is manageable, and we had 4 tests and a final.

Similar teaching style to Troxel, but doesn't play favorites as much. Since Sanchez is fully aware of her superior teaching skills when compared to other CE professors, she gets away with being annoyingly picky about the littlest things. The final was a 3 hour marathon. The average was a 69. She didn't curve it.
Does an excellent job teaching the class.

There's homework due every day, it's a pain. But when it's time to work for your test, you will already know all the material without even noticing. Amazing class, amazing teacher, and you can be sure not to score less than a B.

If you can get her, do it! I have friends who got other teachers that were very boring and loved when she subbed for their class. She gives daily handouts with problems that we do IN CLASS that are just like the homework. Bottom line: you will learn without even noticing it and be fine for tests.
No Comments

Wow. Do not take her section. The classwork is unnecessary and unclear, and she really seems to have no idea what she's doing. This is an HOD core class, but if at all possible TAKE THE OTHER SECTION.

Flores is great.  Her class is very involved, there is a lot of reading, but you will do OK if you skim the main points.  You will definitely learn a lot more in her 1800 section than other teachers.  She is very helpful, especially to students who aren't very politically minded at the start of class.

I was not expecting to like this class, but I learned so much and Prof. Flores really challenged us.  Each day we talked about relevant issues and it was great to have an understanding of what's really going on.  There was a substantial amount of worth, but nothing unreasonable.

You may have problems understanding her thick French accent. Relatively light workload but pop quizzes are difficult. It's hard to sit through her lectures and take notes because it's somewhat disorganized. She seems to have the attitude that Americans and Europeans are worlds apart (case in point: first reading is 'EU Guide for Americans').

Brutal, brutal lecturer. But not very time consuming class. Easy book review-3 pages double spaced. short quizzes on lectures that can be difficult because she asks RANDOM questions. a very, very boring class but I would take it again because of the low workload.
Very nice prof, very easy class. 4 relatively easy assignments/projects and 4 quizzes, no final, and she grades pretty fairly. Knows what she's talking about.

She is one of my favorite professors.  The class had 3 major assignments throughout the semester (and a lot of smaller ones) and no final.  The workload wasn't unbearable at all.  Those who put in a moderate amount of work did fine.  She's really nice and helpful outside of class too.

treats her class as if it is the students' only one.  has a ridiculous amount of expected reading, but not doing it will not kill you.  very unhelpful and unclear and VERY defensive about her teacher and France. avoid her!

I have taken 2 classes with FFK.  If you are willing to put in a moderate amount of effort(i did about 1/3 of reading), you will do well in her class. She is very intellegent and is passionate about politics(esp. europe and environmentalism). She encouraged us to pursue topics we were interested in and apply them to what we learn. She's great.
While she clearly knows a lot about European politics, she gives grades based upon her personal political leanings when it comes to papers. It is quite absurd.
difficult grading and does a poor job conveying the material. probably the worst teacher i have ever had. AVOID!
Although she knows the subject matter very well she is extermely hard to understand and is VERY intimidating!  Do not get on her bad side!

At first, I hated the class, but it grew on me.  Although the lectures are often confusing and unclear, they are sometimes helpful and she is always willing to help out of class.  Typical French woman though -- stuck up and hates American students...makes stide comments about them.  Overall, eh, okay -- intelligent and excited about topic

She's kind of intimidating at first, but give her a chance. Shs is really knowledgeable and can answer most questions. If you show interest and put in a moderate amount of effort, you will do well. She's not as bad as people make her out to be.
Super-helpful and is keen to share her passion for the subject. Comes from the top Pol Sci department in France and really knows her stuff. Not an easy class but fairly marked. Very cute too!
If you like extremely left-winged teachers and arbitrary grades….you are home
Lectures are disorganized; reads from notes. Fails to convey material well and readings are a nightmare. I would not recommend this class.

She really wants the class to learn - her enthusiasm is clear and her discussion is usually interesting. There is a ton of reading from several books that you have to go to the reserve room to get, which is horrible. Tests are essay and theme based, term paper has lots of room to choose a good topic. If you work you'll probably at least get a B

Ok, so maybe I was a little extreme before.  She's very nice, and the tests aren't as hard as we all thought they would be.  Definitely not a blowoff class.  TONS of reading.  Unclear lectures.  But generally makes sure there is a lot of good class discussion.

I could write a 300 pg book about how much I despise her. She's the worst prof i've ever had. Forutnately she's a visiting professor. But if she's around for Spring 06, DONT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER.  Lectures are so disorganized, acts like this is the only class we're taking, unreasonable demands.

Free class, although kind of boring. Only take if you're actually interested in the topics. Small GPA boost and attendance is not taken so you could also take it for that reason. Teacher is funny and a good lecturer but material is intro level and dry sometimes. Nice to have just once a week.

Some of the lectures were honestly really interesting, and others were confusing. He is so sweet and obviously cares about the material, but sadly most of the class did not (many would skip every class). To me, it was a good way to learn about the topic without having to stress about the grade! Thanks Prof Fleetwood :)

Fleetwood is a super nice guy, but the class itself is not very interesting. He clearly cares a lot about the subject, but students tend to not care and skip class. The only grades are weekly homework assignments which are super short and easy. This is a good class for an easy A and an extra credit hour.

This was one of the most boring classes ever. He is super dry. I went to class maybe 3 times all semester. However, he is super easy for grading the homework and it is basically just graded for completion.
Great professor! Very considerate. The class is easy and you will get an A as long as you are submitting all the homework. Lectures can be very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Fleetwood is amazing, but the Quantum Engineering class can quickly get dry, especially if you have a physics background.

Prof. Fleetwood is great. His lectures about diverse areas are interesting, and the HW is really easy and entertaining to do. Also this course doesn't really have much group projects--you only need to meet with some classmates for choosing stock and that's it. I highly suspect this seminar is used to soothe Freshman who got destroyed by courseload

Dan Fleetwood is a great guy. He is so interesting and has so many stories to tell. He provided us with advice that will applicable throughout our entire lives and made a pretty confusing and foreign topic understandable and interesting. If you can get into the Moore's Law seminar take it. One HW assignment a week that you get 100 on for submitting

Homework is one weekly assignment that you turn in at the start of the next class (so attendance matters). But there's no final or any other assignments so the class is an easy A. Lectures were really try and boring. Most people just did other homework during them.
Prof. Fleetwood is a really interesting guy and I learned a good bit from this class. As long as you do the homework and show up for class you should be good!

One of the best professors on campus for me. Learnt so much about Moore's law and the financial and engineering world - every lecture was amazing. The guest lecturers were pretty good too. No final exam, just easy weekly homeworks and a decent stock market competition which was fun. Insane class, would love to be taught by him again.
