Great lectures. Very interesting class as a whole. Super easy class and helps with the GPA while still being a class I want to go to. Definitely recommend

Dr. Fleetwood's seminar is very interesting and fun. He personalizes his lectures around current world events and is always willing to answer questions about anything. The only grades are a short homework assignment each week and showing up to class. Fantastic professor!

His range of knowledge and conveyance of the various aspects of Moore's Law makes showing up for class very pleasing. There is homework for every week, but most are easy. He occasionally has amazing guest lecturers over. Worth every while for an easy A.   Bonus: Look him up on Wikipedia!
Fleetwood is a god on earth.
Vastly knowledgeable, he is a good professor. Extremely well-known all over the US for his work in Radiation effects.

Very good lecturer. Brilliant guest lecturers. Easy class. Everyone got an A. But the grade is not important. The amount I learned about the engineering industry is tremendous. Lots of research into the financial sector of the industry, new inventions, history of the growths, decline of some sectors, and future prospects. Fascinating.
LITERALLY.  THE. BEST. CLASS. OF. MY. LIFE.  This beautiful man makes my Wednesdays.  Take this class.  It will make your life.
Take him for this class if you can. Tests are identical to whats covered in class, and completely fair. It is a tough class but he makes it do able.
Very easy A! Take if interested in technology and engineering. A few guest speakers, no tests, no quizzes no final... just 1 hw assignment per week that takes about 30 min to do. great prof!
He's a really good professor, but electromagnetics is a really hard topic. He's a fair grader and has clear lectures. Make sure you go to class.

Just had him for my freshman seminar, but it was a lot of fun, and he did a really good job at keeping us focused in a class that didn't really matter.  he even bought the team that won the stock market game daily dilbert calenders!
Terrible material.  Good Professor.  He's nice if you actually go talk to him.

Sort of a frustrating class at first but turns out to be pretty good. The importance of E-mag to EE becomes increasingly important through the course (as upsetting as that is) Glad we have to take it. Not very helpful for questions, mainly because he is so used to the material it is hard to bring it down to our level. Enjoy it, and he curves, a lot

For CS 4260 AI. Best lecturer at Vandy. Super interesting class, fair homeworks, but challenging exams. No final, just final project. One of my favorite overall course experiences. Unfortunately he is no longer teaching at Vandy after this semester.

lass moves fast but lectures are clear and questions are answered well. Midterm was pretty hard under short time, but curved very generously. Forrest always available to help out on HW and project. Good guy.

Hard class, but very interesting. Got kinda crazy. You learn to code in Julia, but it gets confusing because you don't know if your code is wrong because of your syntax or because you implemented logic wrong. Would recommend this class, but it is quite mathematically dense.

Mathematical programming is a very interesting topic, after taking the class a lot of game theoretic situations that occur in real life stand out to me. Dr.Laine is very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. It's certainly not an easy class, but attending the weekly study sessions can be very helpful. Assignments are in the Julia language

Forrest is awesome, created a 6 hour office hours on a sunday to help with final immersion project. Will do his best to make sure everyone completes to project and will help you understand autonomous vehicles. Honestly one of the best profs ive had in CS

There's no other word for it, Dr. Laine is simply amazing! Class is *very* tough but equally interesting and rewarding. Midterm + Assignment + Finals. Extra Credit assignment but was not easy. No Textbook because EMP is a relatively new field. Classes were recorded but don't miss lectures! And never, Ever, EVER miss Office Hours!
Unprofessional weirdo. Very condescending and expects his students not to succeed. Grades tests way too hard.

Charnock will make you feel bad about not understanding complex topics the exact way he expresses and understands them which hinders learning and diminishes any interest in the field. The lab manual he wrote is gibberish at times and has little direction.

Dr. Charnock may be the single most condescending person I have ever met. His lab manual is an utter mess and frankly, the state of the lab under his direction is embarrassing for the school. Physics lab was was one of the most painful and frustrating things I have come up against. Vandy needs to do better.

Your grade depends entirely on the TA. However, the lab manual, which he wrote, is very confusing at times (even to the TAs). Basically no work outside class though; you turn in your lab at the end of class.

The grade depends on TAs, so the rating is based on my (very nice) TA. The lab is more conceptual based so you need to understand what you are doing. At times it gets confusing and you need to ask TA for help. Overall it's not hard to get an A for this course.

As others have said, your grade is based entirely off your TA. My TA graded a bit harsher than others, so I ended up getting curved to an A I suppose. Labs can be a bit weird, and with this class being online, troubleshooting problems can be a headache. At least the expectations were slightly relaxed because of this.
Your performance will depend on how good your TA is. The workload is bit less compared to other science lab courses, but applying uncertainty and sig fig rules can get annoying.

He doesn't really do anything with Phys 1501L. Your experience is based entirely on your TA and mine was fairly easy. In the online lab, there are no quizzes and you can easily finish the "lab reports" within the lab period. Definitely easier than gen chem, orgo, and gen bio labs.

HIs labs really just depends on your TA. I had a great TA and he was very simple with his instructions and made the labs easier than they should be. All he asked of us were to the point responses to our lab findings and results as well as showing our data. Never have seen or heard of Charnock in my life. Try switching sections if your TA is bad.

Although he doesn't really teach the 1601 or 1501 labs, he's very involved in the 1912 lab. Clearly a smart guy, but super weird and cringey (not in a good way). We never got to see how we did on each lab. The only grades we got were from homework, which he took off points for the stupidest reasons, like not having aligned equations. Avoid.

Dr. Charnock runs the Physics labs, but he is not too involved - your TA is going to determine most of your experience and your grade. The labs themselves, in my opinion, are confusing and not well designed to help understand the material. The class was definitely the thing I dreaded going to most each week, but hey, at least no outside lab reports

Dr. Charnock writes the lab manuals for the introductory physics lab sections. While physics lab is probably the easiest lab of Bio, Orgo, and Gen Chem, it is still annoying because of the labs themselves. Rarely do you get out early and several labs have nothing to do with lecture material. As for your grade, it totally depends on who your TA is.

The class is taught entirely by a TA, but Charnock makes the lab manual that the class follows as a guide. There's no homework/lab reports, only 2-3 question prelabs, and the grade is half quizzes that are based on the material from the previous lab half labs that are filled out with mostly data. Overall very good supplement to the lecture and easy

For the most part, the lectures were extremely boring, but if you ask questions he has tons of great stories to tell. Super knowledgeable about archeology, less so about the internet. Has tons of specific rules for writing papers, but if you follow them you will get 100 on all 3 papers. Also you don't need to read anything outside of class.

Fowler's lectures were boring, and I often dozed off in them. But guess what, he grades really easily and that's all that matters. Participation is graded by weekly reaction statements that are only 100 words and all exams are take home. If you want an amazing, fun professor, go somewhere else. But if you want an easy A, feel free to add it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fowler was great this semester and he helped me learn the basics of archaeology. The three papers are straightforward and not too hard, although the final paper took me a long time to write. Participation is large percentage of grade. Good feedback on paper.
The teacher is funny and very nice, and the class is a pretty easy A. However, the class is extremely boring. Unless you like archaeology or like writing, I wouldn't recommend.

One of the best professors ever at vandy, will answer any questions that you have and always asks how we're doing. Not super hard class either, weekly reading responses, 2 essays, and a midterm and final (all essay based)

Bill (what he likes students to call him) is an absolute sweetheart! We only had 3 papers and the final was a 5-10 minute presentation on the research we did for our papers. Bill does love to talk a lot during the class which kept us from covering majority of the articles on the syllabus. However, for an 8 am class, it was pretty chill.

A basic understanding of archaeology going into this class is extremely helpful, but not necessary. He enjoys what he teaches, laughs at himself, and cares about his student's opinion. Its an easy A if you're not lazy and have the time to read, deadlines are suggestions which is very nice. Lectures can be boring, but the material is online
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bill is a great guy. He's super understanding and pretty lenient on deadlines (most of the time). Of course, you cannot take advantage of him with deadlines, but he sometimes pushes due dates back by a few days or so to be nice. His class is pretty straightforward, and it is in your best interest to do the reading. It's easy to get an A if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Bill (as he asks students to call him) is a pretty friendly guy, but he tends to takes like 10 minutes to answer a yes/no question, and is pretty monotonous. However, his class is so chill that the easy A makes the boredom worth it.  Readings in this class (first year writing seminar) were not required, but the textbook was interesting anyway.

He's funny in a sort of awkwardly endearing sort of way. The amount of reading can be ridiculous at times, but overall the class is fairly easy. He's a genuinely nice guy who cares about his students, and definitely makes the class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Even though it's an 8am, ANTH 1111W is a solid choice. Between the clear grading criteria, little (and not entirely necessary) readings, and relatively straightforward assignments, this class is not structured to stress you out. Archaeology isn't my thing and I admittedly didn't love the material, but I definitely don't regret taking the class.

He is extremely interested in his field and it really shows in class.  Sometimes he will ramble and the class kind of zones out but if you listen he is actually saying some pretty cool stuff.  Fair and pretty easy grader.  Meet with him about your papers and he will give good feed back. Overall a very like-able guy.

Not sure what everyone else is talking about, but, whether or not he realizes it, he's very condescending. I know not one person in the whole class who likes the class or him. Do not take, even if it sound cool-it's awful. You're not going to fail this class, but he's not very clear in his expectations, and he's nit-picky about the papers.

Dr. Fowler is the man. He loves what he teaches, and it shows. If you actually go to class and do (skim) the readings, it's hard not to get a good grade. Exams are all take-home essays. Final paper is 10 pages. Easy grader. Great guy.

Wonderful professor whose love of teaching and passion for the material comes through in each class.  Lots of reading but the workload is overall very manageable.  No drafts on papers but you could schedule to meet with him and he'll give great feedback

Dr. Fowler is one of the nicest teachers I have ever had. He truly cares about each student doing well! He takes any amount of time to help you in the writing process and gives countless resources and insights during class. Class can be a little boring, but worth the interesting topic:)

Bill is a wealth of knowledge and a renowned scholar in the study of Mesoamerica. Although the structure of 115F is somewhat mundane, the content is interesting. Expect many reading assignments, and plenty of assistance from Fowler IF YOU SEEK IT.

Easiest class ever. Everything in this class is either 5 or 10pts. If you write anything, you're guaranteed to get at least a 4/5 or 9/10. If it's related to anthropology in any way, you'll likely get a 5/5 or 10/10. If it's related to the topic, you'll get bonus points. Weekly quizzes are incredibly easy even if you don't read the text.

personally, i think Prof. Fowler is a great person with a lot of experience in the fields of anthropology.  I've taken 4 of his courses and look forward to the take-home midterm and final exam.  He is so helpful and just a good guy.  A lot of experience with archaeology and ethnography in Mesoamerica.

Horrible course.  I learned absolutely nothing and had to read hundreds of pages of boring readings.  He doesn't return any grades to  you (probably doesn't grade your work) and then pulls out a random grade based on how much he likes you.  He forgot to come to class twice!  Class was a total waste of time, one of the worst that I took at Vandy!

Class is very easy.  Painfully boring though.  Weekly reading quizzes suck though.  Exams are take home (midterm and final).  Three 250 word essays that are graded fairly easily.  TAs are interesting, but Fowler himself just loves to hear himself talk.  It also takes him about an hour to get out an entire sentence.
Not as bad as they say unless you expect a jock-oriented snoozefest. My only qualm is that he lets the TAs write quiz questions so they're usually incomprehensible.

The class is somewhat interesting, and he knows much about the subject. The readings can be long, but usually it isn't necessary to do them. He does get off topic very easily, and he can be a little absent-minded at times. The class is basically 3 papers: a book review, a short paper on whatever topic, and a final paper than expands on the second.

Absolutely terrible class. I am surprised to see all the higher ratings below. He is extremely boring in lectures and goes off on tangents about absolutely nothing. He is extremely unhelpful to his students even though he seems available a lot of the time actually going to talk to him will do nothing. STAY AWAYYYY!

I hate this class and the teacher is the worst I've come across at Vanderbilt.He is more interested in what he has achieved as a scholar than in what the class is reading at home. Homework assignments are basically a division the total pages in two books by the number of classes, so it's sort of discontinuous because the author jumps around.Stayout

Class was kind of boring but easy and the final paper was interesting (grade consists of only three papers and paper three is just an expansion of paper two)- He's a fun guy, really loves the material and tries his best to get to know his students (aka optional dinners at his house, outings, etc.) Bill is amazing!

Easy class, I took it pass/fail and never had to worry about it.  Subject is interesting, and some of the class lectures were excellent, but Bill lets students ask too many dumb questions and tends to get off on a tangent at times.
His lectures are pretty dull, but he loves the subject and his enthusiasm really comes across. Easy weekly quizzes...only one 10 page paper. Not bad at all.

I love this guy. If you have any interest in archaeology, and want to have a good time learning about it, I would highly recommend this class. Bill is a great guy. He's always willing to help you out when you need him. And the class itself is relatively easy. It's good stuff.
honestly this professor made me want to leave vandy
Not good!
Lacked an ability to educate
I put inspirational ironically because I was inspired to drop the major after this class
Material wasnt covered adequately. Lecture was all but useless. Sign in and leave because you wont learn anything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute awful class. Of the info that wasn't obvious, the professor did a terrible job of explaining it. The TA's carried the class. Oh and the grading scale was absurd. Stay away from this teacher

Dr. Forber Pratt was awful. She can't lecture at all, giving hour long boring monologues, which exactly 0 students listened toeven the front row ones. This very well may be the worst class I've ever taken. Do yourself a favor and stay away from this professor.
There should be some criteria about being a good teacher before you get your phd. forber-pratt doesnt know how to teach AT ALL. Seriously needs some coaching.......
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pretty unclear about grading criteria. There are definitely easier 1300 sections. Final grade is based on quizzes, papers, and two group projects. No tests.

Forber-Pratt was a first time teacher and it was clear that she had no idea what she was doing. She does not explain any of the assignments and operates under the assumption that you just know what to do. She also does not provide understandable instructions online. Would recommend taking this class but taking it with anyone else but Forber-Pratt

Great professor. So much passion for the subject and has the ability to communicate concepts clearly. I took his course on Well-Being - it is not easy but if you put in the effort, you'd realize how fascinating it is. Loved every lesson and would take another course by Prof. Forcehimes if I can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, one of the smartest people I've met!

Andrew is one of the smartest guys I've ever had. He is hilarious and makes class fun and interesting. He doesn't require attendance but you'll want to go to class anyways. Great dude and loves to talk philosophy

Andrew is a great teacher. I had a hard time understanding the material (just because Logic isn't my thing) but when you go to him for help he seems excited to explain it and not at all frustrated. He's also hilarious and super attractive. I would deifnitely recommend taking any of his classes!

Andrew is the bomb. He is very energetic and makes a lot of little jokes...is entertaining and a good public speaker/teacher. Highly recommend. I've never bothered to take the time to rate another teacher, but this guy is worth the recognition.
Andrew is the man.  Brilliant, helpful, and inspiring.  Highly recommend the class.

He gives a test every 2 weeks and a big paper due during Thanksgiving break. He gives handouts of all the readings so you don't need to read, but the handouts are very dense and they make it difficult to understand the material. He does not treat this class as an intro class. I do not advise you to take his class.

I also took him for 105. He is great, he's pretty easygoing and really explains the material well. He grades fairly and quickly, and he really doesn't care if you come to class, but you will want to go anyways. He is really interesting and very tolerant of opinions other than his own. Take him if you can!

Good teacher, has a talent for expressing difficult concepts in a refreshing way. He's energetic and funny which helps breed enthusiasm for the subject matter and is a pretty easy grader when it comes to most assignments. Highly recommend taking a class of his.

He's a grad student but he really knows his stuff.  He doesn't require participation, but you should go because he'll explain everything you need to do and he teaches the material so that you don't have to do the reading at all.  He is pretty lax on a most things (including late grades), and he's hot too.

Profe Foster was my favorite professor this semester. He obviously loves what he does and will help in any way he can to make sure you understand. Very kind and likable. Tests were easy if you study at all.
Not a hard class at all! Profe Foster is very understanding, and is always willing to help. Do not wait until the last minute to go to office hours though!
Not a tough grader and wants you to learn. Nice guy and very helpful. I would definitely take another course with him.
Very clear cut spanish class. He wants you to succeed and is willing to go the extra effort to get you there. Average amount of work. I learned a lot. I recommend him
great class, Fox is a real world marketing success and an all-around great guy

Professor Fox is one of my favorite professors at Vandy. I learned a lot in his class and he is extremely helpful if you've missed class or if you're just behind. The class is not necessarily difficult, but you need to study for the quizzes. The final project is what makes up the majority of your grade. Take this class!
Prof. Fox is the best.  He is great at what he does and he brings in awesome speakers. If you are planning to take Marketing, definitely take it with him.

Professor Fox is an awesome teacher, makes class very enjoyable with real world applications. 3 tests, a couple homework assignments, and the group project. TAs are helpful and studying for tests is easy with the powerpoints and review session. Lots of great guest lecturers. TAKE!
Best marketing teacher in the department. Would take his class over and over again. TA reviews are really important they help you a ton on quizzes. Class has no tests.

If you are taking marketing, you definitely want Fox. He is awesome, uses lots of videos, quizzes are easy, TAs are helpful, and he is so cool. He knows everyone and brings in awesome speakers. Definitely a teacher you want to get to know who can really help you in the future
Awesome, cool professor. Go to class and you won't need to buy the textbook. Go to TA reviews before tests because they are very helpful.

It is so rare to find kind, loving human beings like Prof. Folgarait. Throughout the semester, he has taught with utmost excitement and treated everyone with endless respect. His lectures were so engaging and in-depth that I lost track of time in every class. He set the bar high for what professors should be like. Such an invaluable experience!
Just an amazing person. This was his last semester teaching, but I'm leaving this comment because I am very thankful that I had a chance to take his class. Recommend him if he ever teaches again.

Professor Folgarait is the kindest man alive. No hyperbole. Whatever you expect, expect more. He is gracious and caring. He is never frugal with his compliments and his entire teaching philosophy is to encourage willing participation, learning, and excitement. He more than succeeds. It is a privilege to have been able to take his class.

Without a doubt the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. Caring, understanding, will work with you no matter what. He is incredibly intelligent but explains the material so that anyone, even an art history beginner, can understand it. Soft-spoken, witty, engaging lectures without being too complex. Many reasons his classes are hard to get into.

Prof. Folgarait is the kindest person in the world and his class was genuinely a joy to go to. He is incredibly understanding if you have to miss class but makes the subject matter very interesting. The grade is also basically one final paper that he allows you to rewrite until you've reached an A.

He is literally the nicest professor ever. Grandfather vibes- he genuinely cares about students. It consists of three papers, but only the last one is graded. The final paper is presented in class, but it is read straight from paper. He gives you an imaginary grade and you can edit until you get an A. He expects every student to end with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Folgarait is the GOAT. You cannot hate him. He is the best professor in Vanderbilt period and he will make your day brighter. All the professors at Vandy needs to learn how this man treats his students and learn from him. He makes HART easy and interesting. More importantly, he makes you feel good about yourself and respected. TAKE HIM!!!!

Professor Folgarait is literally the nicest human being I've ever met. Sometimes I wish I waited to take his class in person just to interact with him more. HART 2710 is graded on 2 non cumulative tests that are two open ended essay questions. Spend a little time before each test preparing and take good notes every class, and you will do great.

Professor Folgarait is one of the most caring and kindest professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He is extremely knowledgable about his area and his lectures are very engaging. I enjoyed all aspects of this class and am now very strongly attracted to the art history major. Definitely would recommend!!

Professor Folgarait is such an amazing professor. It is clear that he is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches. I have been struggling a lot mentally this semester because of Covid and he was the only professor who actively worked to make accommodations for me and genuinely cared about how I was doing. I highly recommend him.

This man is truly deserving of all of the praise he gets on here. Dr. Folgarait is a great professor and one of the most genuine, caring, intelligent, and inspiring people I have ever met. I took this course for an HCA credit and loved every minute of it. Definitely try to take a class with him before you leave Vanderbilt -- you won't regret it!

Kindest man I've ever had the pleasure of interacting with. Showed a genuine interest in both the student's learning and well being. Sent unprompted encouraging emails. Graded our essays insanely quickly. if you take good notes in lecture and do the reading and you will get a good grade in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Super nice and friendly  you only get one paper to write and you can rewrite it as many times as you want! Easy A.

Professor Folgarait is the best. Extremely caring of his students, very knowledgeable about the material and good at stimulating discussion. Workload is very manageable and he provides great feedback. Take him if you can.

Phenomenal professor. As a non-Art History major, I was very appreciative for his clear lectures and passion for the topics. He is one of the kindest professors on campus. Only 2 exams - but both are very fair and he gives great feedback. Took this course for AXLE, and I loved it so much I hope to take him again. 10/10 recommend

This man is one of the most intelligent, caring, and thoughful professors you will ever meet. All of the previous reviews are accurate; you should definitely take him for any class he offers. He's incredibly accomplished but humble at the same time, and this translates into the way he interacts with students. He grades easily and is very flexible.

Spots in his class aren't gone within the first day of registration for no reason. Best professor I've ever had at Vandy. A mentor, an intellectual, an inspiring intellectual who really teaches you to think and push your limits. I literally thought about graduating one semester late just to take a few more of his classes.

He is the BEST Art History professor I've had so far. He really knows what he's talking about and makes every class engaging! He also cares so much about his students and really wants you to do well. He taught my writing seminar and we only had one graded paper but it was super easy and you could choose your topic. Take any class he teaches!!!!

Folgarait is one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. He cares about his students and engages everyone in learning. His teaching and grading methods enable students to learn a lot without feeling the pressure of getting a bad grade. If you pay attention in class, do the reading, and review a reasonable amount of time it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Cares so much about the students' well-being and academic performance. This writing seminar taught me a lot and changed my perspective on modern art completely. Take this writing seminar if you have the chance!!!!

He is an incredible person that cares about the health of his students. If students came in sick, he would excuse them from class to rest and feel better. He has interesting lectures and connects it to modern events. Success is based on a research project at the end of the semester and easy to do well. Easy humanities class for STEM majors.

Hands down one of the best professors at Vandy. Must take even if you have no art experience, like me. It's only a midterm and final, with no other work at all. He doesn't take attendance, but it's extremely important to attend class, since there's no other way to get good notes to prepare for the tests. Super nice guy who wants you to succeed.

Professor Folgarait is amazing. He genuinely cares about each of his students and he does everything he can to make sure you get the best grade possible. His lectures are interesting, but be prepared to talk a lot.

Despite his soft, soporific voice, Folgarait's enthusiasm for the subject keeps you alert and interested. The material you learn in lecture is unique, and this is one of those classes where you learn random facts and stories that you can tell to impress colleagues. Not a lot of d2d work, but I did prepare extensively for the exams.
The BEST professor I've ever known.

Words do not do this man justice. Folgarait is simply the BEST! His passion for architecture is awe-inspiring. He is an extremely compassionate prof who loves it when you speak in class. Not to mention he's a generous grader. 2 short exams, that's it. If you attend lecture, you'll get an A. Go for the grade, stay for the best prof on campus!

As a STEM major, I was weary of taking a liberal arts class, but Professor Folgarait makes the content accessible and interesting to every student. Study for the midterm and final (the only two grades for the class) and you will succeed. Everyone should try to take his class. If you don't like art history now, believe me, you will after his class.

Professor Folgarait is amazing!  He is kind and caring and knows everyone by name.  He gives fascinating lectures and is very easy to understand.  Instead of requiring you to memorise dates and facts he cares more that we understand the concepts and movements in art.  I wish I could take a class with him every semester!

Folgarait is an awesome and well respected professor. He is extremely thoughtful and passionate about the art he teaches, which conveys itself through lectures. I didn't have to read the book once - his lectures are superb. Would highly recommend this class or any others that he teaches.
Great professor with interesting lectures. Two tests, no homework whatsoever. Just need to study some before each midterm to know some specifics for the essays.

Professor Folgarait is adorable in class and a great lecturer. He's very clear and willing to entertain any and all comments. He's also willing to joke around a bit, which is awesome. His workload is very reasonable and manageable.

THE BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD IN VANDERBILT. He is so nice, cares for each student and respect everyone's opinion. The material is interesting and mind blowing.  Very soft-spoken. Lectures are always amazing and I'm kinda sad that it is over. It was the best summer class I've ever taken. TAKE HIS CLASS, you won't regret it.

Best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. If you have any opportunity to take him, you must! He is such a wonderful man, who is very invested in his students' success and well-being, and his lectures are fascinating.
Nicest man, AMAZING professor. Guaranteed A if you put in the work and have good notes. Only 2 tests, no participation. Must take a class with him at Vanderbilt.
Amazing lecture. Always respect students. Also is very serious about plagiarism. he said that the work he checked by plagramme  plagiarism checker.

Folgarait is hands down the kindest, most knowledgeable, most intriguing professor I've had at Vandy. He wants each student to do well and puts all of his effort into lecturing. I went to office hours just to chat because he knows so much and loves to talk about it. Take his class!!! I've steered a lot of people to his classes and they loved it!

AMAZING LECTURER. He is so soft spoken and kind, he cares so much about his students. I don't like modern art but I LOVED this class. No homework as long as you go to class (you will want to, its so enjoyable and relaxing), only a midterm and final, no attendance taken. One of the best teachers at Vandy, every student should take a class with him!

Folgarait cares so much about your success and makes you feel special. You can revise your papers an unlimited number of times until you get the grade you want, and he always pushes you to go for the A. Makes the material relevant and interesting, makes art history easy for newbies, and encourages thinking outside the box.

Leonard Folgarait changed my life.  Literally.  17 years ago, he saved me from the hell of Pre-med and organic chemistry with his enlightening lectures, clarity of ideas, and non-judgmental nature. He is a gentle man who lets his thoughts and ideas make the impact. Thanks, Leonard. Because of you, I have pursued a career in ideas.

Very, very nice and intelligent man. Lectures are interesting, however, he offers theoriesinterpretations that I have never seen before, historical background on paintings is sometimes confusing due to errorsomissions (especially on Guernica), and spends way too much time on minor artistsworks (includes Jetelová but no de Chirico or Ernst).

LOVE FOLGARAIT!!! I'm not a big HART person but Folgarait made class interesting and fun. His lectures could not be more clear and only two essay tests (midterm + final). Fairly easy grader and as long as you study his lecture notes an A is pretty easy. If you need to take HART for axle, take him!!!! almost no rote memorization also like other hart

Leonard is the best teacher I've had at Vanderbilt. The material is interesting anyways but he nevertheless does an unbelievable job of bringing together the artistic styles with the history and psychological components, which are key to understanding the art. Leonard is just an awesome dude and one of the kindest you'll ever meet. Take the class.

Best professor at Vanderbilt. Life changing class, even though it was my fifth time learning about many of the -isms. He's remarkably methodical in his lecturing and doesn't proceed until everything is crystal clear. He's stimulating, mind-blowingly knowledgable, and makes you WANT to be class. Two tests, easy grader, best class I've ever taken.

This class is awesome and Leonard is a gifted teacher. I'm an Econ major, but I leave this class with an inspired interest in art. You don't have to go (but you should because his lectures are amazing). Two tests: mid-term (40%) and final (60%). You only need to study the night before, and he grades easy. This is a must-take for anyone.

I took Leonard's classes in the 80's.  Now, I'm a landscape designer.  The 20th c. Euro class I took spring of 1982 as a Freshman (had to get permission) is the rock I push off of daily in my work.  It's not about landscaping people; it's about Kandinsky.  Leonard's class has stayed with me f o r e v e r.

Inspired an interest in art in me (im econ) and gave me a knowledge base I put to use when I go to art museums.  Easy class, go to most of his lectures (youll enjoy them) so you know what to write on the essay tests.  Only a midterm and final; no work in the class except studying several hours for them the night before.  Definitely reccomend taking
Prof. Folgarait is THE BEST. There's so little work in this course, and he allows rewrites on everything. Absolutely amazing :)
Amazing professor.  His lectures are interesting and always have a twist ending where everything starts to make sense.  Grades based on what he thinks you deserve, which is usually very high.
Great professor. The class is easy, but you will learn quite a bit. It's less about learning the subject than it is about learning how to be a student and about developing critical thinking.

Definitely look forward to this class each week. Mind blowing discussion that pushes the limit of what art really is. Grade based on 2 5-page subjective papers and 1 12-page research paper, opportunities for regrade. Very helpful and insightful on all topics. Class is solely discussion and analysis of different art forms. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Professor Folgarait is the best teacher at Vanderbilt. Whether you like Art history or not, you will love this class. He challenges you to think and perceive the world in a way that you wouldn't usually see it. The book is 100% unnecessary. There are 2 tests so just study hard but no work besides studying. So go to class and enjoy the best teacher!

One of my favorite professors and one of my favorite classes. I'm considering majoring in art history thanks to Dr. Folgarait. Incredibly knowledgeable and super helpful. He wants everyone to succeed and he's willing to work to make you do well. I hope I have another chance to take a class with him

This man will change your life. You will look at the world differently. His lectures are brilliant, eloquent, and he carefully plants seeds of art historical curiosity in your brain. Magic. Not only is he highly intelligent, but also caring and passionate about his students. You're a fool if you don't take AT LEAST one of his classes. HURRY! NOW!

Dr. Folgarait conducted a very interesting and entertaining class. Most of our time was spent experiencing and discussing various works of political art. He is very good at leading discussion and encouraging each participant. His class put less emphasis on learning facts and more on learning how to look at art.

GREAT professor. He's a great lecturer and throws int he occasional semi-funny art history joke. Don't buy the text- it's 100% unnecessary. Go to class, take notes, and you'll get an A. He puts only a few slides online that you'll need to know for the test. There's just a very straightforward midterm and a final.

Even if Art History isn't your cup of tea, take his class. I'm in another one of his classes now- I can't say enough amazing things about him. Don't buy the book. If you go to class and take good notes you can easily do well. His classes are either: midterm, paper, final or just midterm and a final. With minimal effort it's an easy A-/B+

Professor Folgarait is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt.  This class was amazing. Don't buy the book- go to class and pay attention to what he says and you'll do fine. Trust me- you'll want to go to class- he's that great of a lecturer.

The ABSOLUTE BEST teacher I have ever had.  He is insightful, encouraging and so intelligent!! Plan your semester AROUND his class- it doesn't matter if you are a major/minor, you NEED to take his class!
best professor at vanderbilt hands down. absolutely amazing - his lectures are brilliant. if you get a chance, take him.

Prof. Folgarait has been my favorite teacher out of all my classes in high school and college. He makes art history extremely interesting and truly worth studying. There is no attendance but you go anyway because the lecture is so interesting. I highly recommend anything he teaches. Midterm, paper, final. All reasonable if you go to class.

Professor Folgarait is incredible!! His lectures gave me goosebumps because they were so fascinating. You must attend regularly in order to do well, because the mid-term and final are timed essays based on the lectures. but by the end of the first lecture you won't -want- to miss class...EVER!

Love him! Always looked forward to class. He's a dynamic lecturer with a contagious passion for the subject. Not a difficult class, but challenges you to think deeply. He infuses his discussion with a soft-spoken, dry sense of humor. Also extremely helpful outside of class - so kind and sincerely interested in his students. Take one of his classes!

Please take this class! It is phenomenal! Folgarait is probably the nicest man you'll ever meet, and the way he views the world and art is inspiring. Your grade is based on one 12 page paper that you work on all semester, and he gives you feedback before you turn it in. Classes are a dynamic lecture/discussion format. What college should be!

This class is great!  Folgarait makes the lectures interesting and he is a fair grader.  Only a midterm, final, and one paper.  You know what he expects and he is willing to help his students.  Definitely my favorite professor i have had a vandy!  Take one of his classes

He and Michael Rose (music) were the 2 best professors I had at Vandy (back in the mid-1990s). I learned more in FA111 than any other class there.  He is hilarious with a dry humor, yet inserts a serious amount of knowledge into each lecture. If I still lived in Nashville, I would sit in on his classes just for fun--they were that good!

Sometimes I go sit in on his lectures, even though I'm not in any of his classes anymore. I can't say enough nice things about him ... he is what I think college should be about: being passionate about learning.
I LOVE THIS CLASS!!!  He is a great teacher and the class is so interesting.  Such a sweet man!

AWESOME!  Probably the best professor I had at Vanderbilt (back in 1995).  His lectures were so good that I was disappointed when the class ended.  Even if you don't care about are, you'll love it when the class is over.  I can't say enough good about him.
Clear lecturing style but sometimes doesn't get to some of the material
The most helpful, intelligent professor at Vanderbilt. Hands down. TAKE ANY of his classes and be amazed at the multitudes you will learn.  A wonderful himan.

He's really smart, and really nice.  He just wants everyone to do well in his class.  If you go, don't do the crossword while he's looking, and put a little effort into the tests, it's definitely an easy class.  He's pretty soft-spoken, though, so it's sometimes hard to hear what he says.

he is a really intelligent man who teaches more than art history, he also is extremely kind and funny which makes him different from vandy's many pompous profs. his lectures are interesting but he is extremely soft spoken and sometimes it is easy to fall asleep.  p.s. beware of your cell phone ringing in class
He is the best professor at Vanderbilt.  I absolutely recommend any of his classes. His lectures are really interesting and clear, and he is extremely helpful and friendly with students.
I LOVE LEONARD FOLGARAIT! He is THE best teacher at Vanderbilt! He is so helpful and kind to everyone. Take at least one class with him before you graduate!
One of the best people I have ever met in my entire life. I am constantly enthralled by his lectures, and wish class would last all day long with him!!

I LOVE LEONARD!!! without a doubt the best art history professor on campus, and maybe the best at Vandy! he makes the class fly by and you'll learn so much from him! TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE THE CHANCE! ps-go talk to him if anything's wrong...he'll fix it!
I love Dr. Folgarait.  He was my thesis director, and he and his wife are great friends of mine.
He is fantastic!!! I LOVE him and think he's the best A&S teacher to ever step foot onto Vanderbilt's campus. And plus his humor is fabulous!

Made the 2 hr summer class go by quick, a helpful prof who makes class interesting.  As far as difficulty goes, I think it's pretty easy to regurgitate what he says in lecture for the essay tests, so i definitely recommend this course or any course he teaches.  111 with him is an easy A

As an egineering student looking for humanities courses, I was a little afraid of walking into an upper-level A&S course for my first A&S class.  Dr. Folgarait was tremendously helpful in helping me adapt, and his class was thoroughly interesting as well.  I couldn't have asked for a better professor.

Folgarait is great! Unlike most art history professors, he doesn't require unnecessary memorization of dates or artists for his tests. He seems genuinely interested in your actual knowledge of the material, rather than useless facts. I highly recommend him, he is a sweet man and great professor.

Leonard Folgarait is the best professor in A&S at Vanderbilt. His assignments and exams are very thoughtful and very thoughtfully evaluated.  He's engaging (if a little soft-spoken), but he challenges everything you know about the world and forces you to live/experience life actively.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had, soo knowledgeable about the subject matter, so enthusiastic and helpful.  His assignments are wonderful, they make you think more about art and about yourself.  TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM!! You won't regret it.

He's the most helpful professor at Vanderbilt. Really cares for his students and is super sweet.  Take his classes, very enjoyable!!!  You'll have a new perspective about the buildings around you when you're done!!
Quite possibly my favorite person in the world
TAKE ALL HIS CLASSES! He is an incredibly inspiring and sweet individual.  Has utmost trust in all his students and very understanding. WONDERFUL WONDERFUL WONDERFUL

As a graduating senior, he is the BEST professor I've had at Vanderbilt.  I feel I learned so much from him and have gained a new appreciation for art and architecture.  Whether an Art History major or not, I highly recommend taking one of his courses.
HE IS HOT!!!!!!!
Great human and professor and hot hunk of a man in this weird dort of way.
FABULOUS, my absolute favorite professor. He is very inspiring and forces you to think. Class is always entertaining and I leave knowing I learned something everytime.
so cute, very mellow, i LOVE him!

Very cute, quiet, quirky little man. Straight-forward with what he expects, fair grader. Not exactly dynamic in lecture but he seriously grows on you..I even have started laughing at his little lame jokes.
Very interesting, nice guy.
Extremely sweet and caring. Goes above and beyond for her students to ensure they succeed. She makes sure you understand the course material. The class is not demanding at all.

Dr. Frierson is one of the most compassionate people I have ever met. She cares deeply about her students and their well-being, both in and out of the classroom. Her lectures are engaging, she is very clear about grading and the content of exams, and she gives thoughtful feedback on any work done in class. She's a great professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor for sociology and a nice class to take for premeds needing the sociology requirement. Very clear about what will be on exams, very flexible with work as well. Highly recommend.

Amazing professor, class is pretty easy so if you want an A and also learn about sociology it's a great fit. She's always avaiable and LOVES when students come to office hours. Would be a miss to not take her.
Great professor!! Very nice, caring, and understanding. She makes it very easy to do well because she is a great teacher.

Professor Frierson is extremely compassionate and cares a lot about seeing her students succeed. She is very knowledgeable and open to feedback from her students about what they want to see in her class. No exams, 2-3 very short papers, encourages class discussion/participation, and loves finding ways to make the topic engaging and applicable.

Dr. Frierson is my favorite professor ever, very understanding when it comes to extensions + she is SO kind. This class is digestible and interesting, consisting of, one midterm, two projects/papers, one final, and readings for every class. Even though this was her first year teaching, her lectures are engaging and her discussions interesting.

I am a freshman who took Dr. Frierson's class (it's her first year here), she is the KINDEST professor ever. One midterm, a couple projects/papers, one final, readings for every class that you aren't quizzed on but are beneficial to read. If you are looking for a relaxing, easy, and still interesting class (imo), this is the one for you.
Class had few assignments, but all felt meaningful. Be prepared to write notes upon notes though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chiller. Awesome stories. Talks in circles sometimes, though. Easy enough grader.
I really liked his lectures. Insanely easy class too if you put in expected effort. Interesting material as well

Fav prof, so knowledgeable and friendly. Class is low-stress easy-A, but you still learn so much about Latin America. Graded on one midterm (27.5%), 3 film discussion posts (20%), one 7-10-page research paper (25%) and one final (27.5%). Exams are in-class essays (he gives you the prompts a week before, so not difficult at all) Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable about the field, but can drone on and run off on tangents, which would then keep us in class a couple minutes late. Interesting material, but lectures can be difficult to stay focused on. One paper (7-10 pages), 3 discussion posts on films, midterm, and final.

Prof. Robinson is a great professor who is extremely knowledgeable about course content. He really shines when he is talking about personal experiences and how it intersects with the course content. Lectures are dry but the assignments and tests allow you showcase your knowledge in different ways and Robinson will get you to where you need to be.

Very kind, understanding, and fair grader. Tells you exactly what you need to review prior to the midterm/final, making it very possible to do well. One 7-10 pg paper, but outside of that workload is pretty light
such a chiller
Lectures are dry but he is very knowledgeable. Never read a thing and did fine. Just pay attention and study the day of. Super nice guy that was very open to questions and discussions in class.

Dr. Robinson is very knowledgable, but it was SO hard for me to sit through his lectures. Idk how it's possible, but it felt like every sentence he said was jam-packed with information. However, prior to exams, he basically gives the prompts and reviews, which is great. Also, be prepared to do a presentation, paper, AND final exam at the end.

Robinson is such an awesome professor and a really nice guy. He really cares about students and he just wants to see you learn. He is super old-school and his lectures are pretty dry, but he really has a lot of interesting experiences to share from his time in Panama/Latin America. If you come to class and take notes, you will be fine for exams

I LOVE Prof. Robinson. Funny, friendly guy and very passionate about the Caribbean. 3 HW assignments, 2 exams, 1 paper - all doable if you pay attention in class. Never read any of the assigned material and still got an A. He lectures the whole class but likes questions and tangents. Overall, great quality prof and highly recommended!

Absolutely loved Robinson he was awesome! Super old-school prof with lectures and essay-style midterm, final, and assignments. He really cares about the material and this is clear through his lectures, though they can get a little boring at times. As long as you show up for class and do a good outline for the midterm and final, you are golden.

I've taken two of Prof. Robinson's classes, both were very similar. The classes are almost entirely lecture-based, and his style is very traditional. That said, the lectures are fantastic and interesting. Workload is light, grading is very easy.

Prof. Robinson is a great professor who is extremely knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. He is pretty boring and lectures very slowly, but it is still easy to succeed. The only grades in this class were in-class midterm essays, in-class final essays, a research paper, and 3 discussion posts, but he gives the essay prompts before
Honestly, it was not a fun class at all, and his lectures were pretty awful, but he is so nice. Like genuinely so nice. The class is super easy too, so I would 50/50 recommend it.

Not a 1, probably more like a 3, but his current rating is far too high. He grades on a curve, and quite arbitrarily at that, so watch out! Not a fundamentally difficult class, but Professor Robinson makes it hard to get an A without luck. I've taken six history classes at Vanderbilt and this was by far the hardest. Interesting material though
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Robinson is an amazing lecturer with an ability to make Latin American history accessible to all! Clear instructions, he basically tells you the questions for the midterm and final. Emphasizes clear and concise writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved the class and loved the lectures. He's got very interesting stories from his time in Latin America. Some really cool projects/readings, great class and great professor.

This is my 2nd course with Prof. Robinson and I am excited for my next one. His courses drive you to learn in-depth profiles of Latin American countries and historical themes. He is really is the heart of my Latin Am. history major concentration, as he does justice to the region by representing its history well. Vanderbilt is better for having him.

Super nice prof, easy class, lectures are just long and dry. Midterm and final are in-class essays, plus one research paper on a topic of your choice. Super chill and good to learn about the broad themes shaping Central America.

Prof. Robinson has vast knowledge of Latin America and he's an expert on the history of the countries that he's done archival work and research in. His class is lecture-based by nature and may be a bore for somebody who's not interested in Latin American history, but I thought the class was excellent and I'm really glad I took it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Robinson is really passionate about the material and gives out the prompts ahead of time. He's a very fair grader, but the material may be tough to sit through if you're not interested in the subject since the class is 100% lecture. Though he posts the powerpoints, attendance matters and it's in your best interest to take detailed notes.

Robinson is an awesome lecturer and gives out essay prompts on the tests about a week before them and the only grades come from 3 tests and a final paper. Class is interesting, but focuses more on Spain than Latin America. Robinson is extensively literate on the subject and really loves teaching about it. Take it if you're interested in Spain
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Long lectures, lots of reading and note-taking. Nevertheless, interesting class and a great professor. He clearly loves his subject and sharing it with students, and he's a fantastic lecturer, helpful in office hours, and basically gives you the essay questions before the exam. Not an easy A, but if you prepare responsibly a good grade is doable.

None of the readings are necessary except maybe the mini-novella on the History of Brazil. Class is extremely enjoyable and he makes it a cake walk. Essay questions for exam told in advance and are easy ..interesting guest lecturers, but sometimes I wish he would just lecture since he was just so dam good. I am now minoring in LAS because of him.
He's the man.  Very clear lecturer, not too difficult, helpful outside of class, and generally a cool guy.  History/LAS major or not, take classes with him.
Boss. If you don't like this guy something is wrong with you. Good lecturer, very straight forward, an easy A. One of my favorites.
Robinson is great. If you put in effort, you will do well and he will be super helpful. Tells you the essay questions before the test, and was always available to look over stuff outside of class.

The class encompassed a lot of information but he taught it very straight forward and I learned a lot. He tells you the subjects of the essays before each test so you can prepare. He's also always available outside of class and extremely helpful. OVerall, he's a great teacher who clearly cares about his students.

I took this class to fulfill axel and it was pretty good. I agree that if this is not your thing it can be a little dull,but isn't that true of all history classes? He tells you EXACTLY what the essay questions on the test will be; prepare well and its an easy A. He is very easy to talk to and will also read your paper drafts. Overall a great class

A tough class.  The lectures can be boring, but you learn a lot from the class.  He is very interested in the subject matter, but I wouldn't recommend the class unless you're interested in the subject.  2 papers, a midterm, and a final.  Not a very easy grader.

Professor Robinson is amazing.He really knows his stuff. Tends to show up to class a little late. He tells you what is going to be on the exams. Definitely take any class he teaches. You will actually learn something instead of just memorizing and forgetting. Weird right?

Brilliant lecturer who really knows and cares about his material, making class enjoyable. Will tell you what you need to know for essays on tests. You have to do the readings and be prepared to write everything on tests, but if you put in the work you can get an A. Would highly recommend it to anyone for AXLE or major/minor credit.

He is SUCH an amazing teacher. He's so passionate and really cares about his students. This semester, he took the class to hear the former president of Chile speak at Blair! It's easy to do well because he tells you what he expects. He makes the subject interesting because he loves it so much! Definitely take this class and anything else he teaches
he is outstanding. Robinson is an amazing teacher and is great to students.  he appears tough, but really cares, and his assignments are challenging but straightforward.  HIGHLY recommended.

This class is extremely interesting.  There are guest lecturers 3 out of 4 classes.  Two papers, two tests (final and midterm.  Lets you know exactly what you need to know for the tests.  Also, when he lectures, it is extremely interesting.  Great class overall and not too difficult.  Good liberal education class.

He's great! His class took a really complex look at the intricacies of the subject matter clearly and completely. He lets you know what to expect on exams. The papers are pretty short (3-5 pages). It seems like he wants his students to be interested and successful.
He makes the material absolutely fascinating. The papers and exams are very straightforward. I felt like I learned a lot from this class.

He is great!  He tells you exactly what is on the tests and never tries to fool you.  The papers are not too bad either.  He is very helpful in office hours and he really wants his students to do well.  He talks about history from many different angles and makes it very interesting.
He's a cool guy. He makes his class very interesting, and he's helpful. He was my advisor too.

Robinson is the man, so straight forward and tells you exactly what you need to know for the test.  Also very funny and has relatively interesting lectures for how boring some of the material is in real life.  Recommend this class

Robinson is one of my favorite professors because he tells you exactly what you need to know.  His lectures, while sometimes mechanistic, are driven and give insight into the area of study.  I was never confused after leaving a class and his tests are fairly straightforward.  He is a fair grader, and is a nice guy under his tough-guy facade.

Prof. Robinson was a great lecturer.  His way of speaking was so colorful and made me want to listen to what he was saying.  He gave out the test question subjects before the test and was a fair grader.  He's always willing to help out.  He rocks!
Great prof, tells you exactly what to expect and doesn't throw curve-balls. It takes some work, but if you've earned an A, you'll get one. Interesting lectures, very smart! Take his classes!
This guy kicks ass! He is a straight shooter and would rather us learn than worry about grades! LOVED HIM!

well-travelled and versed in iberian history, robinson brings a sense of humor and insight into the material he teaches. he is straightforward and no-nonsense; breaks down major movements into simple smaller themes so everyone can understand them. ive taken 2 of his courses and would rec him to ever

Prof. Robinson was a joy to have in class!  He was extremely enthusiastic about the subject matter (as well as knowledgable) and eager to help out outside of class.  His tests are straightforward; he gives you the topics beforehand!

robinson is a great guy. tests are short essays which are graded very fairly. papers are graded the same. lectures are dynamic - although he gives 20 minute answers for some simple questions, the notes are always on the overhead. classes are NEVER boring
yay for professor robinson!  three cheers! Straight forward, down to earth, and very good at keeping things interesting!  also very helpful outside of class!

Good professor. Makes it clear what you need to know to do well.  Has three volume levels...loud, louder, and loudest.  Funny at first, then just becomes monotomous.  Is like a football coach. But, good guy who wants everyone to do well.
Loved him. Lectures dramatically. Does not take attendance, gives outlines for all lectures and study sheets for exams. You have to know the stuff but he makes it very clear what you need to learn.

Sienkiewicz is super knowledgable and really cares about his students. You're pretty much guaranteed an A in this class if you submit everything. Some of the PAs can be pretty tough, and there is quite a bit of work, but honestly super worth it for the skills you develop in the end. Would recommend!

Professor Sienkiewicz is the most inspiring professor in the main music core curriculum. He cares deeply about his students and assigns the large workload only because he knows how valuable the content is, even if the singular course credit doesn't reflect it. He won't accept anything less than musical artistry, but you learn that artistry there!
He's a nice guy and he's willing to help out one-on-one if you're having specific issues.

He is honestly one of the most positive people I have ever met. He is extremely encouraging and cares a lot about his students, personally and academically. His class is somewhat difficult, but you will get a good grade if you participate in class and show effort for the weekly assignments. He also gives opportunities for re-dos on assignments.

Weird, weird experience for me in Dynamics. Frampton is genuinely one of the funniest professors I've met in college, but in terms of teaching was subpar. Lectures consist of him writing down solutions line by line from a sheet, and people often caught errors from him copying things down wrong, so lectures were very dry. Tough exams
AKA the boy.
DO NOT. I repeat... DO NOT

Lectures are actually pretty solid—he explains things clearly and keeps it interesting. But the exams? Kinda rough. The first two hit way harder than I expected. The later exams were easier, but if you're aiming for consistently high grades, you might want to think twice before choosing his section.
DO NOT TAKE DYNAMICS WITH HIM. I REPEAT. DO NOT TAKE DYNAMICS WITH HIM.

Super fun guy. Lectures can be quick for some but he posts the lecture notes. There were only two midterms (3q each) and both had low averages which upset some, but the final was easy and graded generously. My biggest issue is that the labs and HW need to be reevaluated, as both had issues, especially lab. Overall, difficult class but not too bad

Had him for my engineering module where we built a ukulele from relative scratch. Good professor, keeps his lectures on concepts relatively short but also interesting and focuses heavily on hands on experience and group work. Supportive to your ideas and a helpful mentor when engineering something. He was also pretty funny with a great personality!

Almost impossible to reach outside of class hours. Provides very little feedback on exams and no explanation of where you went wrong. 85% of your grade is based off of 5 tests (2 problems each). Expressed disappointment in class due to low average but didn't suggest any way to improve.

While he seems like a likable guy because he throws lollipops at you, his exams are extremely unfair and difficult compared to the homework and in-class examples. All other sections people had As, while in Frampton's class very intelligent students were struggling to pass.
Rude to students and cares more about his job in administration than his job as a professor

For system dynamics, Dr. Frampton does not teach as easily as other classes. The material is pretty difficult, with a large amount of mathematical manipulation for modeling systems. I think he goes through the material in a very understandable manner. Attendance is not mandatory at all, notes are posted.
Frampton was a great professor for the MechE engineering module where we built a ukulele from scratch. I thoroughly enjoyed his class. It is very hands on and a lot of fun!!

Frampton's ukulele module was super fun! We spent the full class in the design lab designing, fabricating, and building our ukuleles. It was all hands-on group work and it really gets you comfortable using tools, CAD, and 3D printing. Definitely one of the best options for the engineering modules.

Hilarious guy I would love to grab a beer with but hope I never have to sit through another class. System Dynamics has been the worst course I have taken in the ME dept. thus far. Lectures are writing equations non-stop for 50 minutes which no one follows. The majority of your grade is based on two exams and a final with a 65% average on the first.

Frampton is actually the nicest guy ever. He cares so much about getting kids hands-on experience. The class is an easy A, he even says as long as you turn in something that you basically get an A. The class is there to give you a taste of MechE not make you hate it. Attendance isn't mandatory, but its so fun that I never skipped. Take Frampton!

Class is an easy A. Attendence is nowhere close to neccessary, but you go anyway for Frampton's personality. Great guy, makes pretty basic and boring topics interesting with random interjections of personal stories. Don't be expecting to actually learn anything, though

Great personality, keeps class interesting with jokes and candy, attendance is not mandatory and there is no honor code for the homework (all online). 5 Tests but only two problems each, laid back class.

Spends the entire lecture shifting between either just writing out the terms in super long numerators or denominators while everyone just sits there, or telling flat jokes/stories that just waste your time. When he's not writing super long num/denoms, he scrolls so fast that it's impossible to write down notes. Textbook is helpful.
I took Prof. Frampton for the MechE module and it was by far my favorite class this semester. He assigned one assignment per week and had funny lectures with guest speakers. Very easy A.
Very easy module, the final project was fun and made sense. Highly recommend.

In this module, we just had to build a ukelele. It didn't matter if it was held together by duct tape or the most beautiful piece of work, he just wanted the students to learn something along the way. He also gives Dum-Dums whenever someone asked a dumb dumb question. Great guy.

I had so much fun in this class (building a ukulele)- Prof. Frampton is really helpful with teaching students about what resources are available through VU's engineering department. Focuses on the positive when giving feedback about our ukuleles.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Is very cool and funny. Class is light and fun. He is pretty laid back.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's really laid back in class but then exams are surprisingly difficult. There are five exams and each one only has two problems. They are usually graded out of 30 points, and he'll take a couple of those points off for a small mistake, so even though the content isn't that hard, it's hard to do well on the exams. Other people loved him.
Good teacher.

Wonderful teacher. Design studio was absolute best engineering seminar and I'm not even considering mechanical engineering. Regardless of your majors, the class is crazy fun and you learn a lot. Super easy to get an A of course, take this course. Does work wonders on getting you familiar with the design studio.
Prof Frampton was super nice to talk to and willing to help in/out of class. The modules were met for fun mostly and therefore were easy: we showed up, followed instructions, and basically all got A.
Professor Frampton is great. Tests are hard, but he's a good teacher and cares about his students. Make sure to participate and that he knows you.
A prince among men. Don't pay attention to the chili pepper, that was just a joke

Interesting teacher. Makes jokes in class to keep you interested. Test rage from easy to doable. A lot of the test problems come directly from the homework so make sure to always do the homework's and you will do fine. Or put the homework problems on your equation sheet.
Terrible.

The grading is weird. He has hw, graded out of 9. He gives grades of 6-8 to ppl who had almost identical hw essays. Each hw is around 20-25% of the grade. This caused me to get a B+ in a nonsense class where I learnt nothing,lost all interest in MechE,& I am planning to shift to Electrical as that module, despite being tougher,was fairer & more fun
Great dynamics professor.  Tests can range from doable to easy.  Always do the homework.

Take the MechE Module from him! He's very nice and funny and explained concepts well. Not a lot of HW, but what we had was easy, and he graded our reports very easily. The lego car project is kinda fun and doesn't require a significant time commitment. I enjoyed this module and it was easy to get an A, so I'd definitely take MechE from him!

Very enthusiastic about teaching; The class project is building a LEGO vehicle, which requires a very creative mind. Also he has a sense of humor; He jokes on how integrations in calculus are dark magic to him and how they serve as nothing but tools beside screwdrivers and wrenches for engineers.

I would definitely take a class from Frampton again. He has a sense of humor, and his teaching is very clear. He uses hw problems from the book as test questions. He talks about sports and Napoleon Dynamite in class. The class itself is statics on steroids. In class, everything makes sense then the hw is much more complicated. Not impossible though

haha definitely one of the most normal professors i've known. sense of humor. plus, he's leaving in a semester, so his classes resembled Office Space. He's pretty much checked out: 'thats all i have for you today.' Homework is rough, and the book is horrible, but just take notes of his examples. Test policy is cool - cheat sheet, 1 drop, 1 lab drop
Systems is not super easy, but he makes it bearable. He goes through stuff really fast, but if you take good notes, you'll be fine. He grades pretty fairly and tests aren't terrible

BME 3890 - Special Topics: Hardware & Firm. For the love of everything, don't take this class, especially not with Baudenbacher. Don't get me wrong, he's a nice guy, but nothing about the class was clear. No syllabus was ever posted and everything was just vague. The assignments are coding heavy and oftentimes felt impossible. All love though.
avoid taking any class with this professor. he won't tell you about guidelines and then will penalize you when you don't meet guidelines. he's also super unorganized and will make it your problem.
BME 3860/3861 - Research for credit. Essentially all you need to get an A in this class is to turn in all assignments and go to the presentations. Just do what is asked of you and it's pretty easy.

Franz is genuinely one of the smartest and kindest people at this university. His class is not easy, but it is because of the material. He teaches it quite clearly and does his best to ensure student comprehension. His jokes frequently kept the class entertained and you can tell he genuinely cares about our education.

Great guy, kinda hard course.

BME3890: Hard/firmware.
His lectures are all over the place. They vary wildly in difficulty, even within the same lecture. It's very hard to follow what he's talking about most of the time. Class didn't have pre-reqs listed but you really need to have taken physics to understand the circuits and a bit of coding to understand structures.

His way of presenting lectures is not very interesting, which can make it hard to learn, and the lack of textbook for 3300 makes it extra hard to catch up if you missed anything. If you're able to really pay attention and take good notes, you'll be okay, but the class will still be hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I honestly disagree with the ratings here. He def isn't the best lecturer I've ever had (a bit dry), but his lectures are helpful if you actually listen. His tests are very difficult and long, but he's a very lenient grader. He just wants to make sure you understand the process. Averages are usually in the 70s (pretty normal). Extremely nice guy.
All other comments seem to describe this class pretty well. I am only have one more thing to add: I hate bubba.

This class is truly impossible. You are taught none of the material. The HWs are not on material from the slides frequently. The tests are insanely hard. The only good thing is no one does well, so there is a curve. Do not take this professor.
Great Guy.

Dr. Baudenbacher really tries, but he doesn't accomplish much in teaching. Stuff covered in lectures wasn't indicative of what would be on the tests. He wasn't there to proctor two of his own tests. Averages are horrible, but if everyone fails nobody fails. Take this version of instrumentation if you want an A but don't want to learn.
Mentally absent. Inconsistent. Detached from reality
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fun class which consists entirely of discussion of readings on different topics relating to evolution and society. Grade is mostly based on participation and writing assignments along with a presentation. Definitely a nice change of pace if you are looking for a BSCI class that is more discussion rather than exam oriented.

Very poorly taught. He made no syllabus and notified us of tests less than a week in advance. No brightspace page, showed up 5-10 minutes late to class almost everyday. Absolutely no effort to engage students, lectures were boring, unrefined word dumps you copy verbatim. I was excited to take this class, thinking it was for passionate students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sci & Soc was an amazing class in terms of material. If you're into evolution or meta-science, you will love the readings. But grading is brutal. Seminar class but with a B average. Weekly readings (100ish pages) / responses, participation (2+ hours discussion each week), term paper, and you deliver a 25/30 min presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Funk is a very nice man who cares about his students. Science and society mostly involves reading and doing questions and discussions on interesting topics in biology/evolution. For some reason, a lot of people dropped after the first class, but I would recommend it as a fun elective

Dr. DJ Funk is an awesome dude. Unfortunately, his portion of the class is very boring and not engaging. Lecture is essentially him reading off the power points, but you have to go because he leaves some parts blank. He is the hardest grader I have ever experienced at Vandy and barely gives any partial credit. Avoid if you can!

He's the man! His class is tough and detail-oriented, but it's definitely manageable if you give yourself enough time to study.  His exams come straight from the class notes.  Probably the nicest professor I've had at Vanderbilt; he really makes an effort to get to know everyone's name.

It sounds like the last two posters are just bitter. I liked this part of the class better than rokas's. We learned about macroevo., like dinosaurs and human evolution, which I really liked. Yea, the test were detail oriented, but its a BIOLOGY class. Do study the practice tests, he reuses questions. Overall this was an easier bio class.

As suggested by the post below, he is ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE. One of the worst. Very boring, gets off track easily, and never returns tests.  I received 93 and 96 on the first two tests (Rokas), and 73 on his test. He asks very detailed questions. He used 50% of questions from previous class's test, unchanged. No key for practice final.

Dr. Funk is the man. His name is daniel j. funk... DJ Funk, sounds like an mc to me... that's no coincidence. He puts a lot of work into preparing lectures; he doesn't just regurgitate the book. If you are interested in the subject (evolution) you should take this course.
He's probably one of the nicest teachers I have met in the bology department.  Extremely helpful out of class as well.  His tests are very straight forward and relatively easy for a BSCI course.
Dr. Funk is a goofy guy and makes the lectures fun. This is a really interesting class, espeically for Biology majors.

Do not take this class! Gives unclear feedback, grades harshly with vague guidelines, going to office hours does not help. Thinks highly of himself and his own knowledge base but is terrible at teaching it. Be prepared to spend hours and hours each week on group projects outside of class. Tons of work without learning a thing.

Furse is clearly very experienced in Entrepreneurship, but for that reason he assumes his way is the only way.
