His advice is vague, doesn't answer your questions directly, and then he'll change his advice from week to week. This class requires a presentation every single week and doesn't offer a lot of chances to actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Entrepreneurial Challenge is both the hardest and best class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Highly recommended. Furse is very difficult but loves to see his students succeed.

Furse teaches a challenging but rewarding class. As a CEO of a group, this class challenged me in a way that no other class in college has, and has stimulated my interest in pursuing Entrepreneurship and changed the way I think about business and management. Working in a group like this is a truly unique must-have Vanderbilt experience.

Followed project criteria and made every correction suggested.  Met with him to discuss corrections so feedback was understood. The only problem?  He changed directions and the feedback each time was 180 from the previous time's.  Gave the same lecture several times.  Cursed at me following my presentation for following his directions.

Professor Furse was extremely frustrating to work with. From week to week the professor's advice would change drastically, which made our work much more difficult and time consuming.  This is an intense course that already requires more work than any other class I've taken and I'm a senior. I would NEVER recommend this course to anyone.
He's pretty inconsistent with his feedback on your businessplan.  Overall he knows a lot about marketing but am pretty sure he didn't actually know what half the class's projects were.
How will gonna disagree that he is one of the greatest professor in Vandy?? He is perfect. Take his class for your interesting and good grade.
Professor Furse is very helpful, has incredible insight into growing a profitable business.
No Comments
This is a great class.  He really knows a lot about building a business.  He's a teacher at Owen so he has high expectations but is very helpful.  Great guy!

I was really impressed with Shannon. I learned a ton in this class and without feeling like I was getting overworked, which is hard to do and surprising given she has been only teaching for a few years. Would definitely recommend.

Shannon was a great professor.  I am not interested in Philosophy, but she related everything back to our lives to make concepts interesting and easier to understand.  She gives out her notes each class, so as long as you attend class and study her notes for the tests, you will do well.

Shannon is a great professor for being a grad student. She brings a younger, more vibrant teaching style to what can be a boring class. She gives out notes in each class so you have to be there to get them or have a friend get them for you. Memorize those and you will make an A in the class without reading one page or article although reading helps

Professor Pursley is super funny and understanding. Your grade is pretty much just the midterm and final exam, but they are open-note, and he is pretty clear about what is going to be on the test, so it is easy to know what to study. You can tell that he really does care about students grasping the material. Don't be nervous to take the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is pretty simple, graded on the midterm and final, just have resources prepared, and it's chill. He is knowledgeable and good at explaining things, but he can get long-winded at times, and class can be boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pursley is a nice guy and I can tell he cares about his students success and wants to help. That said, this class is almost entirely made up of two exams that are very difficult and content heavy. There is barely enough time to use the open notes benefit and most of the questions require advanced legal reasoning beyond an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very hard. This class only had a midterm and final that make up a large portion of your final grade and the lectures are very long.

The content is really easy, but the midterm and final are a little tricky. Professor Pursley is not good whatsoever; he does not know how to teach and goes on frequent tangents. Only take the class if it's not Professor Pursley.

Very smart guy but he goes through A LOT of content in the course and the lectures can be confusing. Definitely a hard intro course but if you put in the work it's worth it for Legal Studies Minor or Pre-law Students. Also the class is graded on one midterm an a final (just a 2nd midterm) which is daunting but doable as they're online & open-note
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Pursley is extremely intelligent as he is a JD, has tenure, and teaches real law school classes. If you want to try out the high-paced, reading-heaving environment of law school this class is for you. 75% of the grade is based on 2 pretty difficult tests. Pursley includes things on the tests that he doesn't put in lectures but talks abt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The main complain I have about this class is the fact your entire grade relies on a midterm and a final. Although Prof Pursley really cares about what he's teaching, DONT take this class if you want an easy A. Only take this class if you aren't going to grad school. Overall nice guy, not a nice grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although I found this class to be very interesting, it was unfortunate that the two exams (midterm and final) primarily determined my grade. There were almost no other factors for your grade. The tests were challenging, with unreasonable depth and detail for each question. I decided not to pursue the legal studies minor after taking this class.

Professor Pursley was very approachable and passionate about the material. However, the midterm and final (which amount for 75% of your grade) are incredibly hard for an intro course. The people that do well are the ones who cheat (which is a large majority). If you want a high GPA for law school and are not willing to cheat, don't take the class.

Took class for fun and ended up adding a legal studies minor. Lectures can get lengthy/boring but he's funny and so excited about what he's teaching. He cares more about understanding than anything else, and loves when people come to office hours. The class makes much more sense if you do the readings. He will cold call, but it's not serious.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a fun class! She is such a kind and approachable professor. Easy 100 point group assignments each week. 10 question open book quizzes at the end of each week and can be taken 2-3 times. I suggest picking your group members very wisely for the end of semester video project, don't pick people that don't show up to class or do any work
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Fusco is a great professor! History is my worst subject, but she made the topics easy to understand. Clicker points are a big part of your grade and as for tests, there is only a midterm and a final. There were 5 essays, 3 of which are only a page long. There is a lot of reading for the class.
Fusco is one of the best professors I have every had.  She is enthusiastic and her lectures are never boring.

A WHOLE LOT of reading.. (And you need to do it in order to do well on the in-class participation quizzes.) Also, a handful of short papers and several major essays. Time consuming, but you'll get a good grade if you put in the work. One easy quiz and final test (multiple choice). Very sweet, enthusiastic professor who cares about her students.

Fusco is not only the sweetest and cutest thing alive, but is also an extremely good professor. Her lectures and discussions are almost universally interesting and relatable; she's not the type to get up + drone on for the whole class. Constructive comments on assignments and always willing to help! Her class is my favorite, period.

Great teacher, takes a genuine interest in her students. She is a tough but fair grader. Make sure to talk to her in her office hours. Fun and cute, I'm a fan. She likes it when you speak up in class.

Fusco's class is awesome. She is so funny and the conversations are never lacking.  You only have to write 2 essays and take an exam plus do a weekly post, but it's pretty easy compared to other english classes.

I don't know what these other posts are talking about...Prof Fusco is nice and cares so much about her students. She works really hard to make sure we stay interested and learn a lot. She is always willing to meet and is in general just a great person! I definitely recommend taking 118W with her.
do not take!!!

absolute garbage. if you want to sit through the most boring class you have ever attended and get a grade that doesnt reflect upon the amount of work you put into the worthless assignments she assigns, take this class.
awfully boring

I have to disagree with the previous few posts.  I hate english classes and was dreading taking this class but Katherine made it worth while.  She is adorable and super friendly and very willing to help outside of class.  She isn't a tough grader if you actually do the work.  Personally, I loved her and totally recommend taking her class.

I appreciate challenging classes that actually have substance, but that doesn't mean you have to destroy the subject entirely with useless assignments and boring lectures.  I was thinking about adding English as a second major, but after Fusco... I'm sorry to say that I never want to take an English class again.
I wish the comments were more accurate when I signed up for this class! don't do it. she's terrible. extremely boring. hard grader. more work than any other section. TERRIBLE...
Terrible.  I don't even know where to start.  Don't take any of her classes!
one of the most boring professors of all time... and a tough grader. avoid at all costs. she thinks she's a good teacher too, which makes her even worse. again, avoid.

DONT DO IT! ...unless of course you are HOD and have nothing else better to do than to slave over 3 papers and a scrapbook that you're going to get a garbage grade on anyway.  young teacher on a powertrip, basically. she'll also bore you out of your mind. one of the worst teachers i've had. THERE ARE EASIER SECTIONS OUT THERE. you have been warned.
This class was a GREAT way to improve your writing.  She is also the most helpful teacher outside of class i have ever encountered.
Probably the worst teacher i have ever had.  I would rather castrate myself than sit through that class.

when i first signed up for english 118W i was somewhat dreading taking the course. however, i lucked out with prof fusco and loved it! she really tries to pick engaging material and keeps her classes interesting. also, very fashionable and well-dressed.
She is the best!
Ms. Fusco is one the best teachers I have ever had in English. Write 3-4 papers on the short readings you do. Topics are interesting. Grades fairly. Participate and you'll get extra points!
I loved her! She is so sweet and helpful. Her office hours were the best, definitely take advantage of them, she's such a fun person to get to know and so helpful with brainstorming ideas.
Great Teacher and is always willing to help.  If you can take this class. And then take it again because its thats great!

Katherine is a great teacher and I love her methods of teaching. This was a required class for me and I thought I would not enjoy it but she made it worth it. It's the writing class I have learned the most in. This is class is also pretty easy so take it!

Exams were really easy and had plenty of extra credit. Lectures were fine but the terminology slides he gives are all you need for the exams. Removed our final and changed it to attendance points. The GOAT if you want to boost your GPA.

Gary just kinda yaps about whatever for an hour, but the exams were easy so it's hard to complain too much. By the middle of the semester, only like 20% of people were coming to class. Not really sure I actually learned that much about drug design.

His class was much easier than M. Sulikowki's. Tests usually taken from practice exams. Going to lecture is important b/c he always told us what he would/wouldn't test. Uses the chalk board so his notes are unorganized and all over the place. You WILL need the book. He was very considerate on exams and gave extra credit. His curve was amazing.

He knows organic better than he knows his kids (his words).  On the low end for challenging classes.  I agree that you should avoid 1:1 interactions.  I didn't get racially insulted like others have, but had to hear stories about his music interests.
Great professor for Orgo 2. Classic chalk talk lecturer. Goes beyond the book for his lectures, which is cool.  Great stories. Exams are easier than expected based on his lectures.
He's a great organic teacher. Uploads slides online, always has review sessions before the exam, and has easy exams. Definitely recommend
Great professor with a quaint sense of humor. Not one of those profs that just regurgitates the textbook. He knows his stuff cold and tries hard to teach the material at a conceptual level.
Great teacher; very considerate of students and always willing to help

Indeed, his class is reasonable in that his tests are easy.  But that does not reflect his effort as a teacher.  He is, in fact, probably the laziest and least concerned teacher I've ever had.  Mrs. is far better, and Rizzo is actually worse.  Bottom line: Most Organic Chemistry Professors at Vanderbilt are inescapably terrible.

I took his class for the first semester of organic chemistry. I actually preferred him for teaching style than his wife( but Michelle was still great ). He may give you lots of information which are not necessarily important but for the sake of learning. I did not think that his tests were hard at all for me, but you may hold a different opinion.

TAKE MRS. SULIKOWSKI INSTEAD! Your grade will be drastically better. Organic chemistry is a very difficult subject, but the teacher can make or break the class. Mr. Sullikowski does not teach so that the students can understand, despite his superior knowledge of the subject. Avoid at all costs!

Sulikowski is as good as it gets for orgo. As long as you put in the work and are reasonably intelligent you will do fine.  Anyone who says he is unreasonably hard obviously does not want to put in the effort that it takes to do well in orgo, because Sulikowski's tests are EXTREMELY reasonable.  Good luck in med school if you can't get through him.

Guys... I prefer this professor over his wife because... 1. His tests and quizzes are mostly from textbook. Also, make sure to read textbook to understand some theories. 2. Unlike what other people say, he is organized. 3. His explanation is very helpful to understanding reactions. 4. His tests are hard but not impossible(like Johnston's).

Horrible professor.  He clearly knows his stuff, but can't teach  at all.  His wife is way better.  He is extremely unclear and unorganized.  He thinks if 1 person can understand him in class, the whole class gets it.  Pretty much if you're in his section, you're screwed.
Don't bother going to class. Very unclear about tests.
It's Orgo, so expect it to be hard. And also no Curve... WTF?

It's a decent amount of work and you need to do the readings but he is an amazing prof. The in class negotiations and debriefs are really impactful and he does a great job making sure everyone feels comfortable and prepared. One of my favorite classes at vandy and a great professor, you just have to do the work. Would 100% recommend.

Professor McClure is great. It does require a lot of effort, especially reading and preparing for the negotiation simulations. Quizzes are lowkey hard, even as a good student.  I will say that Prof Leddin does not grade negotiations based on outcome but completion, making her class easier imo. Participation matters a lot!

Professor McClure is an incredible professor who goes above and beyond to ensure that his students are well equipped to not only learn about negotiation, but how to apply it in everyday life. The class is designed with many parts, so even if you're not a good test taker, you can succeed by doing well in negotiations and vice versa. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took his M negotiation class and it was super helpful and insightful. Class is lectures, quizzes, simulations, and group project. Goes on tangents that don't matter and wont let you out one minute early. Good class for hands-on learning and not too difficult. Quizzes are rough so do readings but fun class overall. Super smart guy.

Perhaps my fav prof I've had yet. McClure is so good at what he does and manages to fill a 3hr w/o boring students. Negotiation requires lots of prep and post-work, but if you put the effort in, you'll get good grade. Presentations are relatively easy if you put the time in. Get to know him because he's really smart and fun to chat w/. Highly rec!

Phew this class is quite a ride. I had to put in so much effort before every Monday to think about how to "combat" those negotiations, but it's worth it isn't it? Of course the message is integrative negotiations are generally "better" but definitely this is not a place for leaning back. Work hard and succeed!!!!!

OMG Professor McClure is so nice and like I learned so much in his class compared to other classes. But like literally his quizzes could be so difficult some times. Like I got good grades cuz I am literally a great student who works very hard hahaha/

This is a class that throws you into the battlefield and, sometimes, is a process of how to meet (and deal with) jerks. While after this class I am not super certain how to deal with them, the inspiring speeches of Professor McClure and the message of the class -- integrative is often better -- will stick with me as I step into the business world.

Professor McClure is inspirational and urges you to learn. The class actively encourages you to learn through quite some load of work -- there is the closed notes quizzes and some writing reflections after each negotiation. But nothing helps one succeed more and learn more than doing all of these work.

Gives non open book quizzes that you have to study for and you have to write a prep sheet for negotiation simulations so there's a decent amount of HW every class. Still fairly easy and laid back but other professors could be easier. Final is open note. Dr. McClure is a nice guy.
Professor McClure is brilliant -- the class helps me understand many concepts of negotiation very well.

New topic every week, quiz every week, textbook and article readings, 4 assignments/projects, and cool guest speakers. A lot to learn in this class and McClure teaches it really well. He's a great lecturer who does well to make things interesting and engaging. If you want to learn the basics of business, totally recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Few chunky homework assignments. His grading isn't very specific. Quizzes every week and you have to really study to do well on those. Class is not always interesting, but the information is relevant. Open note final, and overarching big group project and paper. The material is easy but you have to put in some effort to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Material was interesting and straight foward. McClure is so nice and made an effort to get to know his students. There was a quiz each week that aren't hard if you review the material a little. The final was open note so print out the slides for the final and you're set. I did every paper the day before and got A's. Interesting and easy, loved it.

I really don't Gary for several reasons. First, even though he gave inspirational speeches, he still failed to do a good job to make the content delivered interesting. Second, lots of unnecessary guest speakers. Third, the quizzes are super hard and covers minor details that you wont even have the interest to read. Fourth, so many written homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Gar is amazing. Great guest speakers at least once a week. Perfect overview of everything in business in a single class.
Not a big fan of ol' Gar. Calm down on those weekly quizzes bud. And we get it, you're Southern. Other than that, material isn't too bad. Chime up in class and you should be walkin pretty.

Super nice and knowledgeable dude. The quizzes are a little harder than they should be, but not awful. The papers are super easy, and graded very easy as well. There is a major group project which, as long as you plan ahead, is not hard at all. Take this class if you want to learn about business!

My favorite class this semester. Work is pretty easy and fun, McClure is an interesting professor with lots of real world, applicable experience. Plus, if you want a solid overview of all aspects of business from legal to HR to marketing, this class is the best at Vandy. As a bonus, the textbook is pretty readable. Take this class!

Easy A and a great overview of business if you want to get a feel for it. The readings and textbook can get a little dry and oversimplified sometimes, but that said, McClure incorporates a lot of real-world case studies and guest speakers to keep you engaged. Study for the reading quizzes!

The class is very applicable to the real world, although none of the material is covered in too much depth. To succeed on the quizzes just reread the powerpoints and read the chapter summaries, because that's where most of the questions are from. The class is a very easy A-, but you need to do well on the quizzes to get an A

Really interesting guy with a lot of experience, but he does spend most time on lectures that are based on basic book material and it can get boring.  Weekly reading quizzes more difficult than they should be.  4 major assignments graded super easy, as is the group project.  Attendance is taken every class and you can only miss a couple.

Absolutely loved Professor McClure's management class. He is able to speak from a wide variety of business experience and makes lectures useful and engaging. The class was extremely reasonable- weekly quizzes, 4 assignments, a group project and open-note final. I also recommend getting to know him outside of class. He is a great guy.

Prof. McClure is one of the best professors I've had at Vandy. He is extremely knowledgeable with great industry experience and incredibly passionate. Not a hard class at all- 1 group project, weekly quiz, 4 assignments. I've learned a lot in his class and he's also a super super nice guy so I recommend getting to know him. Take this class!

Probably one of the best classes to take early on at Vandy. Easy professor who takes an accessible topic and makes it really interesting. Quizzes are once a week on the reading, there are a few easy papers and a group project.
Really good professor and brings in awesome guest speakers. Without prior background material can be confusing but he does a good job explaining.
super nice, understanding guy. learn a lot and class is not too hard. phenomenal.

Best business professor at this school and all of his classes are excellent. You learn so much about the business world and it is not hard to get an A as long as you put in the effort. Everyone must take him at some point at Vanderbilt - great speakers, inspirational speeches in class, and all around good guy.

Prof. Kimball is simply the GOAT. Incredibly knowledgeable and an expert in things like Real Estate, very well-respected and high up within the business programs at Vanderbilt, and his class is both (nearly) a free A and you will learn very interesting stuff. I took his class in Private Capital Markets with Scott Carter, it was 10/10.
Kimball is the man. This is the class to take if you have an interest in finance.
Nice guy, you can tell that he is very passionate about teaching students and helping them get jobs/internships. Class is also a great balance of being challenging but not overwhelming

Very cool guy with lots of business advice. 2 cases are worth 66% of grade, other 34% is HW completion and attendance. He walks you thru the 2 big cases multiple times and gives great advice before grading so no need to stress over grades. Def a learning curve for those who haven't taken accounting in a while and aren't comfortable w excel tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The GOAT. Best in class and real world advice

This class is extremely helpful and relevant if you want to develop a foundational knowledge of topics in finance. All class content was relevant to current events and the weekly case studies/guest lecturers were really helpful for engaging with the material (also easy As). Kimball is super nice and approachable.
Best professor I've had at vandy. Kimball is a must take
Easily my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. Cares a ton, as long as you get your work done on time and ask questions when you need help rather than at the last minute you'll be golden.

Hands down my favorite professor at Vandy. He is wise, insightful, and cares about his students. You learn a lot in the class, but there are no tests and you can get a good grade. I cannot stress how good of a Professor he is.

This guy is seriously incredible. If you have the chance to take a class with him, you absolutely should. He is funny, knowledgeable, and extremely sincere. Regardless of the subject matter, or class, you should enroll. He creates actual bonds with his students and made it impossible to skip because of how much I enjoyed it every time I went.

Prof Kimball is a great guy that really prioritizes his students. Grades are mainly made up of 3 big financial models that take some time, but he walks through them in depth so you know what to do. Other grades are some homework assignments, but they're graded on completion and effort. Extra credit is also offered on some of the big projects.

Prof. Kimball is very clear, open to communication, and always accessible. Which is good because you will not pass without going to office hours. A majority of the grade is 3 projects, which take a lot of time (do not leave until the last minute). I learned an incredible amount though, and an A is 100% attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is a tough class, but you learn a ton and it helps you prep for finance interviews. 80% of your grade is based on 3 cases, which will take you 100-120 hrs to complete. 20% is based on participation, which is largely dependent on you going to office hours.

Professor Kimball is very smart and helpful. Taught me more about finance and Excel than any other professor/class at Vandy. Your grade is basically determined by 3 very challenging and time-consuming cases. Make sure you go to office hours regularly, use the TA's as a resource, and meet with Professor Kimball. He really is a wealth of knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Kimball is one of the best at Vanderbilt. Extremely nice and friendly, always available to talk about the course and jobs, and provides very good feedback. Like others have said, grade is based on 3 very time consuming cases. He allows one re-do and one late submission, so if you take advantage of that and go to office hours, A/A- is possible

Best professor I've had at Vandy and as far back as I can remember.  Could not recommend more highly.  However, be advised that Financial Management is a lot of work (an unreasonable amount sometimes), but make no mistake: you will learn more in this class than in any other in the FNEC minor if your experience is like mine.  Take Kimball!

Kimball is the best professor I've had here. Super nice guy who wants you to do well. 3 cases that are very time consuming and can be difficult - get an early start and go to office hours and you'll do fine. I learned more in this class than any other FNEC class here. Class models help with the cases, so go to class and pay attention.

Fin. Mngmnt. under old course #'s. Kimball is my favorite professor at Vandy. This class is tough, but you learn A LOT. It is the only class I've taken that you truly cannot get away with putting off the projects until the week before. Give yourself time for working on the cases (spread out over 2-3 weeks) and you can get in the A range no problem.
Awesome professor. Great preparation for jobs - hard work that is interesting and pays off.

Kimball is hands down the coolest professor I've had at Vanderbilt. I learned a ton in his lectures and he facilitated a really laid-back classroom atmosphere. The class was also ridiculously easy, but to be fair it was a one-credit Commons Seminar. Really approachable as well; he took the entire class to his house for dinner on the last class day.

Tough class but totally worthwhile if you are going into finance. Kimball is the man and makes class interesting. The cases are a ton of work, but there are only three of them and you don't really have to do any work outside of that.

Professor Kimball genuinely cares for his students -- he's always willing to meet, and he takes his classes out to Sam's during the semester -- and is great to talk to about anything, be it related to his class or not.   He's also a great lecturer. Would recommend for him for both FNEC 240 and 275. He's really just an awesome guy all-around.

This class is hard. However, Kimball is the man, and if you put the work in a B+ or A- if definitely attainable. The class is 3 financial models with an option to redo one for the final and some participation points. It's a great class and learning opportunity, but again, it's hard.
An unbelievably reasonable Professor. Manages to make a relaxed environment in which you still learn. Cares deeply for his students and is always accessible. I recommend taking his course.

Kimball is a straight up G. He knows finance well and makes the class pretty easy and fair, considering how hard the material is. His lectures are pretty interesting and funny and he's worth getting to know

Kimball is a great professor for anyone who has an interest in building a business. His discussions on his experiences really set him apart from many of the other professors at Vandy. Sure the class may not necessarily be difficult, but I walk away from the class everyday feeling like I enhanced my knowledge base and entrepreneurial skills.

Easy class, lots of memorization from a book that I never opened. Straight regurgitation on the tests.Class presentation is easy if you actually try. Way too many stories from his work experience, but he made it a laid back class and an easy A. Good prof.
Uses real world experience to teach the class, rather than basing it off the text book. Irrelevant though, he's leaving.

He doesn't give back graded work, he doesn't teach, his lectures are dry and he mainly just talks about himself. Do not take his class. He canceled three classes this semester, since each class is the equivalent of one 40 minute class, that's like canceling 9 classes. Worthless professor.

We spend literally 30 minutes watching youtube videos every class, he just talks about himself when he's not showing us youtube clips and he has canceled three classes (we only meet once a week, for 3 hours).  He seems like a nice guy, but it's a terrible teacher. His assignments are ambiguously written. Don't take this class you will learn nothing

Kimball is a very good teacher and actually cares about his students.  The class is easy.  I would also recommend him for FNEC 275.  He knows his stuff, as he was the CEO of a logistics company for many years, so you'll learn a lot of real world experience through his class.
Truly cares about the students and bring real world experience.

Prof Kimball is a really cool guy, really funny and nice. This class, however, is pretty hard. I think he is overestimating our knowledge of finance and as a result its hard to really learn much. Kimball is a stand up professor, but I would avoid this class
Boring and pretty worthless.  Didn't learn anything.
Great teacher!!! Fun class!!! We did a Lion King exercise. One final paper 12 pages long, 4 class exercises. PowerPoint presentations on selected readings. He has real world experience.
Absolutely take this class. Get off ratemyprofessors.com and sign up for his class. He's an awesome guy and the class is very enjoyable

Great teacher. He makes class enjoyable. For the class you need to do outside reading for about 2 hours a week. The class exercises are tougher than you would expect, but the daily extra credit helps. He has business experience and KNOWS what he is talking about. This is my favorite class at VANDY.
Ngl this class is so light. If you love sports, this is a great class for you! All you have to do is reflections, open-note quizzes, and show up.

Dr. Torres is the GOAT. He is such a nice guy and tried to make an effort to talk to everyone in the 200 person class at least twice during the semester. The content of the course itself is a little hard to get behind as the lectures are pretty boring and the content is pretty unsubstantial. He brings in guests and encourages self-grading.

Really easy and chill class. You self-grade your reflections and the quizzes were really easy as well. Extra credit for speaking in class and attending events. Prof. Torres is really chill and the class teaches you a lot about sports that you didn't already know. Putting in grades took a while though.
This class is a joke

Such a nice guy. Encourages in class discussion (lecture), randomly will create in class assignments and surveys for attendance. Easy assignments and self graded. Didn't put grades in until thanksgiving break.
He is a good professor.

Amazing professor with chill vibe and have super interesting ideas each class, but get ready to read a lot because he discuss a lot of the reading in class. It can be unneccessary sometimes to come to class if you have exams from other class or if you just want a break but if you email him in advance you should be good.
Professor Torres is on a whole nother level of chill. Assignments are pretty easy and the class is genuinely interesting too. Take his class for A+ vibes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very laid back and chill, but make sure you come to class. As long as you turn in your work on time you will be fine. He is actually really smart and he brings about some thought-provoking points. Amazing class lots of room to study what you want.

Dr. Torres Colón is one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. GPUS mostly consists of a lot of reading and many (short) reading assignments, but the professor is extremely helpful and always available in his office. The class is early, but waking up is worth it, especially for those who are interested in global relations and politics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: GPUS was so interesting and he's great at bringing in perspectives from everywhere. On another note, despite weekly reading responses(easy but annoying), the class turned out to be heavily graded by about 3 different papers. He allows for edits on the papers as he doesnt believe in grades, but be prepared to do some work doesn't seem to count much.

Gannon is a great professor because he makes it easy to get a good grade while also ensuring his students learn a lot. Weekly quizzes are 40% of your grade and 3 mid-terms are the other 60% (20% each), with an OPTIONAL final exam. Also, the questions for ALL OF THE ABOVE are posted beforehand. Still, I learned so much. 100% recommend taking

I LOVED this class. Would genuinely reccomend to everyone to take. It covers super important global themes in an easy-to-understand way and Gannon is awesome. He makes it easy to do well and genuinely does care about the students. There are quizzes every week but they are easy to do well in if you put in fifteen minutes of effort.

Dr. Gannon is a great lecturer. The class is easy with opportunity to retake quizzes until you literally get an A. The prompts for essays for exams are given in advance. The attendance is not mandatory. Dr. Gannon is friendly & cares about his students. For final, you can retake up to 2 exams if you are not satisfied with your grade. Loved class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 3 essay-style exams with prompts given a head of time (hated studying for these but accesible). weekly quizzes but he gives you the questions. can take in office hours so you can do the class with never going.

Awesome professor. Lots of quizzes but unlimited retakes and you have the questions for the quizzes and midterms beforehand! Recommend you book office hours with him before the exam and ask him what he wants you to tackle for each question.

Best professor I have ever had. He knew so much and made it seem so simple. Grading structure was 12 quizzes with infinite retakes and 3 tests that we had the questions before hand. Very good guy who did a great job. Take his class if possible.

weekly quizzes but u get the questions in advance, 3 exams u get the essay topics in advance but handwritten. He is such a fun professor, and the class is so interesting i feel like i learned so many important things about a variety of topics, super foundational.

Prof Gannon is amazing. He gives all the exams and quizzes beforehand making it a really easy class to get an A in. Although the weekly quizzes can get annoying, you can retake them as many times as you need in order to do well. Super kind and down to earth. Definitely take his class!

In addition to being the best professor I know, he is also probably the best person I know. Do whatever you can to take his class. Change your major if you have to. Genius-level smart, sweetest person ever, genuinely hilarious and cares about his students probably more than he cares about himself. We don't deserve him.

Professor Gannon is an incredible professor who cares about preparing his students for what the future may bring. Attendance is not mandatory, but I highly suggest attending each lecture. His class will change your perception of data science as a field, and how it can benefit you personally. His lecturing style is engaging yet full of wisdom.
Great guy, great teacher. Puts the emphasis more on learning than grades (you can retake almost anything until you ace it)

Gannon is by far my favorite professor I've ever taken. On the first day of class he said attendance was optional. There were quizzes frequently, but you could retake them an unlimited amount of times. He offered extra credit just for watching movies and reviewing them (like Oppenheimer). He also brought his adorable dog to class often.

Prof used to be a high school teacher, so knows his stuff on the teaching side, and is very clear with questions and overall lectures. You will enjoy your time as he also is extremely knowledge and will build your interest in this entry level class.

He's a super chill professor that grades fairly and is really flexible. Attendance isn't mandatory and all quizzes can be made up and you know all of the quiz questions before even taking it. He gives extra credit for watching movies with a short summary too. His office hours are super helpful and going to class is actually fun so go if you can.

Very intelligent professor who breaks complicated topics down into very simple concepts. Super lenient grading requirement with infinite quiz retakes and essay topics released beforehand. Missing a class is hardly punishing.

Amazing professor! I loved the class. He taught the content in such an easy-to-understand way that made it accessible and engaging. He knows a lot about the subject and can answer any question! He has lunches and office hours open to ask questions as well as extra credit opportunities and you can retake quizzes. He also may bring his dog to class:)

Considering the fact that he releases all of the quiz and test questions in advance there is no reason for you not to get an A in this class unless you're not putting the work in. Not even accounting for quiz retakes, extra credit opportunities, and optional final. You don't need to show up for lectures but they're insightful and fun! 10/10 class

He is one of the best lecturers I've ever seen. Was able to relate to students in a 110 person class. Easy grade with 40% of the grade being quizzes shown ahead of time with infinite retakes. The other 60% are 3 exams with an option to retake and he gives the prompts ahead of time to. I genuinely enjoyed coming to class to learn from his lectures.

Gannon is the boy. There's weekly quizzes and 3 tests (+ optional final to improve grade) but he gives you all the questions before hand so studying is so easy. This was my favorite class. Also he sometimes brings his dog to class so that was lit

Dr. Gannon is an amazing and caring professor. His class was super fun and I really enjoyed going to class each day. Attendance is not mandatory but I genuinely looked forward to going to each class. He makes it really easy for his students to succeed and it is easy to do well without too much effort.

Dr. Gannon is the BEST!!! TAKE HIM for any PSCI classes he teaches. He is knowledgeable about his field and truly enjoys teaching students. 60% of the grade was 3 exams spread out, and the rest was weekly quizzes that you could retake anytime, as many times as you want, regardless of your grade. Exams can be difficult, but that's mostly bcs of TA's

This was by far the best class I took this semester, lectures are fantastic, easy to follow, and so interesting! Grade was based on quizzes (with unlimited retakes) and 3 essay exams (with an optional final to replace one) with questions for both given in advance, so easy to succeed if you put in the effort. Best professor at Vandy so far!!
Professor Gannon is awesome. One of the best professors I've had so far. Really cares about his students and opens up his office hours to everyone. Lectures are never boring and always makes jokes.

Lectures really were informative and interesting. He does "front-page explained" where he uses class time to discuss current events for purely informational reasons. Super low stress class. Quizzes are gimme, essay prompts are given beforehand for exams. Extra credit options available. Sometimes he brings his dog to class! TAKE THIS FOR AXLE!!
Very understanding with students. Actually learned something in data science for the first time.
Class is basically a repeat of DS 1000. Good lectures, but I really wish this class wasn't completely redundant.

Very funny guy. You can never go to class or lab as long as you take the quizzes and complete the labs and psets. You get 2 tries for every quiz. One complaint is that things weren't graded until last week of the semester. He canceled the final exam, though.

Loved this class. Lots of assignments, but they are graded quite generously and he gives the quiz questions ahead of time and allows you to take it multiple times for a higher grade. He makes the material really easy through funny real world examples. Lab attendance is optional as long as you submit the work online

Easily the best prof at Vanderbilt. Literally the dream professor. Doesn't care about attendance, quiz and exam retakes, interesting lectures, the whole shabang. If you need 1102 and don't take it with this guy you are making the worst mistake of your college career. Class is an easy A and he knows it too. Do it.

Professor Gannon is the most amazing, caring, and accomplished lecturer I have encountered at Vanderbilt. He only teaches one PSCI class yet with his lengthy credentials and passion he should teach so many more. The prompts for the midterms are given in advance but they are very challenging with unclear grading done by TAs.

amazing professor and great class! attendance is optional, but I suggest going, his lectures are fairly entertaining. There's weekly 5 minute quizzes and 3 midterms. the TAs grade but there's opportunity for retake. theres really no reason you can't get an A. would def recommend to fulfill AXLE.

Dr. Gannon is one of the best professors I've had this semester. He's a super nice man and is very passionate about what he teaches. He's concise, teaches his students so many things, and wants to make everyone feel welcome. Your grade really just depends on the TAs, it was hard to know what they exactly wanted on exams. Extra credit is offered.

Very approachable with easy-to-understand and engaging lectures. Quizzes can be retaken. For the exams, it's very difficult to understand what the TAs want to see in your answer, especially because no rubric is given - it feels very subjective and arbitrary. The TAs weren't very helpful in office hours and seemed almost frightened of the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. He is crazy accomplished and knowledgeable, which usually mean professor like that would be a bad teacher, but he genuinely cares about the quality of his teaching. He was really available outside of class.The lectures are funny and chill. he brought his dog to class a couple of times and is always comfortable to joke and chat.

Dr. Gannon is an absolutely fantastic professor. It's obvious he really cares about his students. Lectures aren't mandatory, but most people go anyway because his class is just generally enjoyable. Quizzes and test questions are provided in advance, so prep is fairly easy, and there are opportunities for retakes and extra credit.

Dr Gannon is a great lecturer, and sprinkles in a lot of jokes and humor throughout the class. The class was 60/40 between in class essays and quizzes (which you can retake), and you get both ahead of time. The tests are graded by TAs and pretty harshly, and there isn't an actual points rubric. Helpful in office hours, book them early. A = 92.5
The best professor you can possibly get at Vanderbilt. Great lecturer and makes jokes that always hit hard.

Absolutely amazing lecturer/teacher. Very very accessible outside of class, gets lunch with students, opens extra office hours before exams, and is very accommodating. Lectures are interesting and helpful. Weekly quizzes are not difficult, he goes over the answers, and you can retake them. Exams aren't too difficult if you attend lectures. 11/10!!

He is an amazing lecturer. The grading is also chill. Quiz questions are given before the class and are taken every Monday. Quiz took up 40 percent of your total grade. However, exams are a bit difficult, requiring you to write an essay. Prompts are not easy and your really need to prepare for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: FANTASTIC lecturer. Totally understands his audience. Grade based entirely on weekly quizzes (qs provided in advance) and 3 essay exams. Final is an optional retake of 2 previous exams. A good grade requires a good essay (and a lot of reading) but quizzes and retakes lighten the load. Take him if you get the chance, you won't regret it!!

Tsikalas is the goat. I have nothing bad to say about him. He is really nice and incredibly organized. His lectures have note packets and are incredibly well delivered. Tests are fair and he gives a lot of partial credit. Simply, the model for what a professor should be.

The best professor at Vandy. Lectures have printed notes and are incredibly well done. Super nice guy and incredibly good at teaching. I looked forward to attending his class every day and would recommend anyone to take one of his classes. Tsikalas is the goat.
Amazing prof, clearly wants students to succeed and gives handwritten notes on the material at start of each class. A lot of busywork but content is manageable and exams are fair.
Super helpful in office hours and very clear and organized explanations during lectures.

He is AMAZING!!! Super helpful during office hours and really just anytime you need him! Definitely one of the best math profs I've ever had! The exam reviews were super useful, and just by studying them, you could definitely get a 95+

im ngl the class was a lot of busy work but omg HE IS THE GOATTTTT. im telling u he can teach, hes super nice, actually funny, and office hours is literally a hack like. TAKE HIM!!! most striaghtforward teaching ever. wish i could take him for all maths ever.

The absolute man. Young, relatable, and most of all cares about his students. Very accessible outside of class. Organized lectures, he provides structured notes at the start of class and goes through them on his iPad. Top 3 math professor at Vandy.

Lectures are always very organized with notes posted to bright space; he tries his best to help you prepare for the exams and makes everything super clear for you. Very responsive in e-mail (I got immediate replies for more than half of the times). And indeed a very very nice person that is willing to help students.

He is the best math professor I have had at Vandy. Great lectures, pauses to take questions regularly and answers carefully, and very clear about expectations/deadlines. Super helpful in office hours, very responsive to emails, and willing to go out of his way to provide extra help and ensure his students are successful.
Very Organized lectures and makes maths enjoyable, all you need to do is pay attention in class and you are good.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Midway through the semester, but I can definitely say that Tsikalas is a breath of fresh air in the math department. Incredible guy, very chill, almost like on ashwaganda. Easy to understand, VERY organized lectures, notes posted, quizzes are announced in advance. One of the few profs in math department who makes class enjoyable
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: good class. No tests. Gives good feedback and really cares about the students.

Dr.Woodman is fantastic; he really cares about the material and teaching it. he will definitely make you laugh and for grades there's 9 weekly assignments ( 40% ) and 2 papers(midterm & final) based off NSF proposals that are both fairly simple, just go see him in OH once for each paper and both of them become really easy.
great & funny lecturer. u can tell he genuinely cares about his students and his class. class consists of 1 weekly assignment and 1 grant paper.

Dr. Woodman is a fantastic lecturer and is super passionate about the material (which can be a little bit dense sometimes)! Your grade in the class is composed of two papers (60%) and 8-10 weekly homework assignments (40%). Attendance isn't mandatory at all. There were numerous peopl who never went to class and did just fine on assignments.

Woodman is chill and just wants people to appreciate cog psych. Classes are lectures where he'll point out helpful things for the HW readings or about papers. 40% of the grade is weekly HW on readings, 30% paper 1 30% paper 2 which are modeled after NSF grants. 2nd one was a little tricky for me to get right but GO IN TO SEE HIM and you'll do well.

Woodman is a great guy who really understands how our society is changing. He's steered away from MC exams and more towards being concise with writing. The course material is super interesting and he focuses on what's actually useful. I think past ratings of him don't reflect the change in his teaching.
He's the man. Will make you laugh. Grades consisted of a short weekly homework assignment and 3 papers. Easy class and pretty interesting. Covered a wide range of topics.

Was actively unhelpful and not understanding when dealing with difficult extenuating academic circumstances . The lecture content is boring, but it's an easy A so it's probably worth taking the class if you're not going to be interacting with him directly much.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Woodman clearly knows what he is talking about, but no one I have talked with LOVED his class. The powerpoints were sometimes boring, and the tests focused heavily on application. While I feel like I learned quite a bit, I wish Woodman would have made more of an effort to connect with his students. Overall, not a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really hated this class. Lectures were boring, tests were poorly worded and too difficult, and the professor was extremely rude and unhelpful to myself and others I talked to. Dropping one exam and 3 extra credit points is the only reason I didn't get a C in the class. I'd never take him again--not worth it in any way.

Honestly just reads off his lecture slides, but at the same time makes it very confusing. Is so unhelpful during his office hours. Allows students to make "rebuttals" on things they got wrong, but even then still won't change the grade. Don't take this class if you can help it.

Professor woodman's lecture is amazing. easily one of the best classes I've ever taken at Vanderbilt. He is funny and makes the lectures really engaging. The workload isn't heavy at all: it's just 9 readings and answer 3 questions to show him that you did the work. Tests can be a little bit hard if you don't go to class and listen carefully

A lot of students are unhappy about his MC tests that require application of the material. However, if you go to class and pay attention, he explains the information in great depth, ordered really logically, and with obvious passion. He's also really funny with stories of famous psychologists! Hw is reading journal articles to supplement lectures

Tests were harder than previous semesters but still not a hard class if you try. Average was like a BB+ but As are doable. He is super funny, albeit inappropriate at times. Really helpful with grad school advice and such. Material was interesting to me, less so for many. Attendence required. In-class quizzes can be kinda tricky. Easyish homework.
Funny, laid back, generous grader, morning lectures tended to put me to sleep because some of the material in Cognitive Psych just isn't very interesting.
great prof, interesting guy, fair assessments. definitely recommended.

He's so funny and his slides clarify any confusion a student might have.  Attendance was not mandatory, but I loved coming to class because he's so funny. Really, there isn't anything to hate about this class.  The book he uses keeps my attention!
Coolest professor I've had at Vanderbilt.  Great sense of humor.  Classes are enjoyable.  Tests are easy.  What is there not to love?

He's very knowledgeable abt the subject, but honestly, I could pay attention for about 40 minutes before my brain would just zone out - a tendency shared by fellow classmates. He's a nice guy though, and from what I've heard, cognitive is just a boring class. Know that it's more "science-y" than other psych classes. READ THE BOOK to study for tests

Professor Syunyaev is very knowledgeable regarding Eastern Europe. Lectures were interesting, and all the resources to do well were there and easy to find. The research paper was a bit tedious, but the guidelines were clear and he was accessible and even encouraged us to come speak to him about the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ignore the negative reviews! Professor Syunyaev is a great guy with wide knowledge on Russian history and the methods/creativity of social science research. Lectures are engaging, especially if you do the readings beforehand. There are only a handful of assignments, his expectations are clear and concise, and he is accessible in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So much hate, but Professor Syunyaev is not bad at all. He goes on some tangents in class, but lectures aren't bad if you're interested in political science research. He is super knowledgeable about the topic and the class is pretty easy, you definitely don't have to do the readings. Overall not a bad course and he is a kind and caring professor.

I don't understand the other comments because I found Professor Syunyaev to be great. He cared about everyone in my class, even after we were no longer taking the class. He was really helpful during office hours and gave clear feedback on assignments when talking to him. I didn't find his lectures or the way he expresses himself confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The guy cannot communicate what we are supposed to understand for the tests and papers, and does not give any clear criteria for how they are graded-- overall, your grade in his class will be a gamble. I can't help but feel that he's given up due to having a class that is not riveted by his drawn out lectures on Russian history.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
"Discuss the professor's professional abilities including teaching style and ability to convey the material clearly." 
I'm sure he knows all about political science and European history, but the guy can't teach, and it's apparent. He talks about the same thing every week, in a repetitive and confusing manner. Nice guy, poor professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are boring and tend to feel very repetitive. He goes over concepts and makes them feel much more complicated than needed. Overall difficult class with lectures that do not matter and feel like a waist of your time to go to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elections was probably the worse class I have taken at Vandy. Having to take quizzes on the most minute and tiny details was a huge hassle. On top of that, the midterm was insanely difficult. With over 1100 students, they boasted about how so many people did well in their class. The reality? Every single person I know needed to cheat to do well.

Really enjoyed Dr. Geer's humor, the class not so much. 1000 people in the same building makes taking notes impossible. They only marked attendance ONE TIME and it was on the day before thanksgiving break. The midterm was way harder than it should have been as well.

Elections is a must-take course for anyone at Vandy. Super interesting course content and speakers that range from super influential (Pelosi) to just plain brilliant (Walter Isaacson). Not to mention, grading is very lenient, with quizzes/exams always being open-note. Technically, attendance required but Tophat didn't work well enough to record it.

First of all: definitely dressed better than Meacham I'll give credit where credit is due. Second of all: great lecturer, learned a ton from the class. He and the other elections professors definitely do quiz you on some really minute details from lectures and readings so those quizzes were a hassle. Also obsesses over sending emails
Professor geer in elections was the best - so understanding and easy. Only problem is this is the type of class where you must cheat to get a good grade
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lectures are sort of interesting; not a bad speaker. He tends to make very general statements; most learning was done from guest speaker's comments. Inaccessible outside of class (I waited 2 weeks for a 15 minute meeting for exam/essay feedback). TAs grade, so essays and exams will be graded harshly without uch specific feedback on why. Frustrating

Geer is very knowledgable and bring a lot of cool speakers to the class (ex. VP Al Gore, TN Gov. Haslam). The class is relatively straightforward. Class is a lecture (by lots of different people) with questions and discussions by students. 3 short essays and 3 in-class essay exams are your grade. TAs do all of the grading.

Super intelligent and knowledgable professor. TAs do all of the grading though. Grade based on tests and short papers. Just make sure you study for tests. Little work except for studying for tests and the three short papers(750-1250 words). Would definitely take if you get the chance. Not super hard at all and very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: PSCI 1150 is a great course; its only offered during election years, so its a solid choice to take. Midterm and Final exams plus three assignments spaced throughout the year make up your grade.

Presidential Leadership was taught by Dean Geer, former Tennessee Gov. Bill Haslam, and Pulitzer winner Jon Meacham. So obviously, it was interesting. The three spent lectures discussing important topics on leadership. Exams were written, but not too hard. I don't know if this class will be taught again, but I'd recommend Geer if you can get him.

Professor Geer is an amazing lecturer and I really enjoyed his class. His assignments are all essay based which forces you to finish the readings and really understand all the material. Grading is pretty much determined by the TA's. He doesn't teach much as Dean of A&S but definitely take his class if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives pretty interesting lectures and brought in some really cool guest speakers like a former congressman, former governor of TN, nytimes correspondent, campaign strategist, etc. Tests are in-class essays which are really annoying but they're very straightforward

fun lectures, cool guest speakers like the mayor of nashville and former vice president al gore. really tough to get an A, but easy to get a B come to class, take notes, and read as much as you can most difficult part is writing the essays, extremely vague expectations, or none at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Geer is funny and insightful. Class needed more organization, but it's interesting just to hear his ideas. He respects students and their thoughts, however vapid. Class was large, so TAs did grading, which was erratic on tests, but fair on papers. Tests are free response; you choose which questions to answer, but they're tough, so do well on papers

Professor Geer is an extremely knowledgeable, smart, engaging professor. He truly cares about the work he does, along with student feedback. He really wants to make sure us students are interested and learning from the material. Has great connections and brings a lot of cool speakers to class. Take anything he teaches!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Geer is an engaging lecturer and knows his stuff. Attending lectures is not only interesting, but helpful in being prepared for exams. However, tests and papers are graded by TA's, so the grading expectations become less clear.

Geer is a relatively interesting lecturer, worth it to go to class as lectures are on exams. Class not an easy A, but if you put your work in, go to review sessions and revise papers with TA should get at least B+. TA has grading power, so make friends, unique thought rewarded in papers
Political Advertising Honors Seminar- it was so interesting though it was a bit difficult

College Professors are not to teach opinion, instead Factual and clearly balanced for an educational knowledge. Therefore allowing free agency to choose individual opinions of context taking the class.
Hard to get a good grade. 3 papers due, 3 midterms, and a final. Don't need to go to class, but you should.

Geer gives great lectures and is very helpful outside of class. Attendance isn't mandatory but it will help a lot on the exams, because he draws straight from what he says in class. Grades largely depends on the TA though.

Geer is a great teacher! interesting and not hard. just go to class and take notes and you'll be fine! He's funny and personable. Learned a lot even though I just took class for nonmajor elective.  He also had awesome guest lecturers who were very interesting. Geer knows his topic and is prominent in political science world.

Professor Geer is helpful outside of class if you seek him out. This is a huge lecture class so attendance is not taken, but go to class. He is an interesting lecturer and brings in really interesting outside speakers. The outside speakers will be on the exams! Three exams, three papers, and one final big question. Not hard.

Amazing class!!! I would absolutely recommend it. Professor Geer is fantastic! As long as you do the readings and take notes in lectures, tests and papers should be fine. Very interesting material, as well.

Professor Geer's course was a lot of fun. His lectures were always great, and he did a great job incorporating current issues into the requisite American history. The reading is substantial, but most of it is reasonably interesting. I switch to a PSCI major because of him!

Professor Geer is a great lecturer, always brings in interesting speakers (ex. Tim Pawlenty, Anne Kornblut, etc), and explicitly tells you at least one question you can expect on each upcoming test...but that means you have to really plan out your essays beforehand in order to get full credit. Also, get to know the TAs! They grade your papers!
Knows his stuff. Not a lot of work, but tests are kind of hard. Lectures are interesting though and you'll learn a lot. He brings pizza sometimes too.

GREAT GUY! Brings pizza to class on rare occasion, very interesting lectures, knows his stuff. There is a lot of reading and the tests are not easy but are as hard as should be expected. TAKE THIS CLASS! It will give you a great perspective on American government.

Geer is an awesome professor with tons of connections so there are great guest speakers/callers. Grading can be tough on the papers, but they are fairly reasonable. He just knows a ton about the subject so definitely take him
Real easy class.  Enjoyed it because we always had influential people calling in.  Basically just talked about the 2010 midterms all the time.
One of the leading political scientists in the nation. Definitely knows his stuff. If you are a PSCI major you should take at least one class with him. I liked his lectures better than Oppenheimer's.

Great class. The workload isn't overwhelming, and you'll learn a lot. Better yet though, the class allows you and encourages you to form your own opinion, which is very fulfilling. The lectures are very well structured and very interesting. Take this class.
It's important to go to the lectures and really plan out essays before the tests but the class is great!

Awesome guy who gives incredible lectures. Tests are complete essay, and not that easy, but if you take good lecture notes they aren't bad at all. Papers can be tough, but if you know what he's looking for you'll be fine. Incredible work experience and great stories. Lectures help. Looks and sounds like the Mayor of Beverly Hills from Entourage.
My favorite teacher at Vanderbilt. He knows what he is talking about and makes class interesting. Very funny and an easy grader as long as you skim over the lectures before the tests. TAKE HIS CLASS.
One of the BEST teachers at Vandy, definitely take his class if you get the chance- not much effort needed to get an A as long as you attend class

Prof. Geer is sort of mixed. He's very informed on a lot of issues, but clueless on some important ones. Makes first third of the course seem like an Am. Hist. class. Name drops a lot about impt politicians he's had drinks with. Overall good professor. Rocks his chain in class. The man.
Great teacher. He is really passionate and knowledgeable, but grading is hard.
No Comments
very superficial lectures. not helpful, self-serving. wouldn't take again.

full of himself and his grading is very inconsistent. Does not appear to have mastery of subject matter. not approachable outside of class or after/before class. tests make your hands feel like they are going to fall off. Easy B Very hard A- or A
Geer is the best professor at Vanderbilt.

Gere is the best professor Ive had yet. He keeps lectures interesting even for those who have little interest in polisci. He is very clear on what he expects on exams and papers. Your hand will fall off on his exams (which are essays) but as long as you read and take good notes in class, there will be no surprises and you will do well.

great professor. stimulates interesting, and extremely knowledgable about the field.  however, be forewarned: he does not grade easily, and this class is NOT an easy A. You will have to read to stay on top of things, AND show up to class in order to do well on the midterms.  The essays (a large part of the grade)are graded harshly.
Another self righteous political science prof. Egotistical, full of himself, and generally states the obvious. Not the most insightful or intellectual prof, but he certainly thinks so.
don't take
Geer rocks.  Excellent lectures, pretty funny.  He cares about his students even in large classes--will always email you back.  A must take while on campus.

Grading standards in Geer's class are simply ridiculous.  In my 200 person class the highest score on the first paper was a 92!  The material is interesting and Geer knows his stuff, but the way his TA's grade is absurd.  If you are expecting an A it will probably be a B.

Very Overrated!  I think most people who give him good ratings have not taken many other polysci courses yet.  There are much better teachers in the department; Geer is basically a decent high school government teacher with a good reputation.  He should step off his high horse.  Take Oppenheimer.
Great prof!  Excellent lecturer who is one of the foremost experts on presidential politics.  And he makes class interesting!

A great lecturer that keeps class intersting by discussing salient issues. I definitely recommend taking a class from him at some point because he has absolutely incredible knowledge of presidents, elections, and government.

Easy grader on the beginning Psci classes. Not very friendly or approachable outside class. Keep up with readings. Put thought into the paper topics and talk to the TA for guidance. Class was interesting and not very hard.
Great professor.  Not very approachable out of class, though.  But in class, he's entertaining and it's easy to see why he's regularly on CNN, FoxNews, etc.
Very clear, tests are not terribly difficult but theyre no cakewalk.

Tough class.  Neel's lectures were much easier to understand and more informative.  Geer has interesting information, but the tests, papers and grading standards simply ruin the class.  It was not fair at all!

geer is awesome. he makes me want to come to class. his class is challenging and it makes you think, but its so interesting. the tests are difficult, but its well worth it. hes the best teacher ive had here!
wow
Great lecturer.  Good sense of humor.  And kinda of hot too.  I even like the reading.
A very good teacher.  Presents the material fabulously, keeps the class upbeat throughout his lectures, and very fair on grades.  A little more to the left than I would normally like, though.
One of my favorite classes and favorite professors at Vanderbilt.  He made the topic exciting and was very helpful.
He is the best professor I ever had--he quite literally made me change my major.

Everyday I looked forward to coming to class.  It was easy to do well, if you read and paid attention in class. Tests were challenging but fun. BEST class at Vandy and by far the BEST Professor at Vandy. We are lucky to have such an amazing Professor.

Great course.  I learned a ton.  The relationship between Geer and Neel made the class so much fun.  The tests were a bit hard, but it was well worth it.  The best class by far at Vanderbilt.  Make sure Geer and Neel team up again!

The class is interesting, but the grading standards might as well not exist: no one gets fair grades on papers and the tests are poorly written and even more poorly graded.  If you want a decent chance at anything above a B, stay away.
PSCI 245

Dr. G is an insightful and supportive professor. Her classes are engaging, innovative, and intellectually rewarding, though they do require real time and effort. If you put in the work, you will gain a great deal from her course. I also highly recommend reaching out to her—she offers thoughtful guidance and truly valuable advice.

If you truly put in the effort, you're not going to get a low grade. But if your expectation for this class is to show up, do nothing, rely on your group members to do all the work, and still get a high grade, then this probably isn't the class for you.
She will mess up your grade if she doesn't like you or someone in your group. And your whole grade depends on your group. Don't take her!!

Dr. G is very disorganized, making it hard for students to understand expectations. Instructions for assignments are often unclear, yet grading is harsh. Your grade depends on your group, which she claims are personality-based, but they rarely work well. Even with strong effort, your grade will suffer due to group performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I spent a lot of time going to classes and completing work. I was never late or missed any deadline. I stayed up late prepping for projects and consulting her as well. However, her grading was extremely subjective and totally depends on whether she likes you or not. There is no point in trying hard for this class or treating it seriously

After reading some of these, I feel inclined to leave my own. Dr. G. is a one-of-a-kind professor here at Vandy. There is not a single professor who cares more genuinely about the well-being of her students. I wholeheartedly recommend anyone to take at least 1 class with her. As for grading, I found her to be fair & wants everyone to succeed.

It really depends on which small group you had. My group was good but objectively speaking, the class was a disaster. The activities lacked purpose and the only people who got high scores in assignments were the ones who chatted with her after class. I spent hours on my response and got a 85%. I don't think this class actually teaches anything.

If you don't want to waste your time, then don't choose this professor. 
The grading is really vague and totally depend on her mood. Even you worked super hard you can still get a bad grade, which will make you feel very frustrated.

All the feedback she gave me was a joke. She focuses so much on pointless details like the dress code (color of the suits) in our final presentation. She thinks WAYYY too highly of herself as a social scientist, but in reality her class is 100% pointless. The funniest thing is she set herself a judges' table during our presentation.........what....

Avoid this teacher!!!! Took this class a while ago, but definitely the WORST one in my HOD classes. She doesn't seem like she knows what she's talking about, and the class is very unorganized. Class is very boring.

Many students frequently complained about the class but no one felt comfortable speaking up because the professor cares too much about her reputation. Overall, this class was disappointing and honestly pretty sad. All of the activities felt absurd. There was zero practical value or meaningful learning that can be applied in any real world context.

The professor was extremely frustrating to deal with, and grading felt inconsistent and unfair. Class lacked real substance and I learned nothing. She seemed to view the course as incredibly important. A lot of effort was put into flashy, surface-level activities rather than anything genuinely educational. Class is awkward and borderline ridiculous

Genuinely nice professor. Heinously disorganized BrightSpace. Major grades are group projects, and she is hard to meet with outside of class. Assignment criteria is often unclear and feedback takes 3+ weeks. Also has randomly due reading quizzes (middle of week; never mentioned in class). Has extra credit activity but doesn't end up giving the EC!

Dr. G is great! She is such a sweet and kind lady who genuinely cares for her students. Given the nature of the class, you are constantly doing group work. It is a lot of reading and writing, and in order to do well, you have to have a very nuanced understanding of the readings. There are reading quizzes, 4 papers, and two lengthy presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Gilchrist is very passionate about what she teaches. That being said, she is not very good at conveying her passion to her students. Class is very unorganized, multiple assignments are given that are not very clear, and she seems to have a bit of a superiority complex. Do not recommend unless necessary.

Dr. G is great. I'm not HOD but loved her class. Your grade is entirely dependent on the small group you get assigned to for the sem. Class time was oftentimes used ineffectively. Learned the most from doing the PO papers and quizzes. Nonetheless, she is very kind and is very obviously invested in students' learning.

Dr. G is one of the nicest and most knowledgeable professors I've had, but the class is incredibly disorganized. The topics covered are interesting and important, but the assignments are disjointed from lectures, vague, tedious, and difficult. She is somewhat of a harsh grader, and she is also hard to reach outside of class if you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. G is very passionate about her teachings. Participation matters, and as long as you do the readings and stay on top of group projects, the class isn't that difficult to manage.

I love Dr. G! I feel like my life was truly changed after taking this class. It was harder than the other 1300 classes, but everyone in those classes found them very boring, and we all found it fascinating. I feel like I look at the world and people completely differently now than I did before taking this class. She made me love the material.

Dr. G. is an amazing professor. Do not take HOD 1300 with any other professor. Her passion for and knowledge of groups is unrivaled. The small group design of this class is unique and is a great change of pace from the usual lecture classes.
