Best math prof I've had so far. She makes the material very accessible, takes AMAZING lecture notes, and specifically avoids putting weedy calculations on her tests so they're about the actual calculus rather than making you lose points for arithmetic/calculation mistakes. Highly recommend going to her office hours too, they're very helpful and fun
She is amazing!!!! The best math prof I've ever had! Grading were super lenient and lectures are amazing and  easy to understand! Would post notes every week and office hours are really useful!!!
Great choice for multi, lectures can be a little confusing and she tends to make arithmetic/silly errors a lot, but she's very helpful in office hours, and tests are fair.

i went into math 1100 having never taken calculus before and it was an ok experience. professor giannitsi could be unclear at times during lecture and TAs were not helpful at all, so i went to tutoring very often. she spends a lot of time on easy problems and not enough time on harder ones, so lectures can feel long. overall, not terrible or great.

I figured I'd just give my 2 cents considering I noticed that the professor has a 5 star rating. The professor is great, but this class is still difficult. Multi will always be difficult, so I just felt like it was misleading seeing a 2 and 3 star for difficulty. This is a very difficult class that you will have to dedicate a lot of time to.

One of the nicest and easiest multivariable calculus at Vandy Math Department. Tests are easier than the other professors, though HW can be tricky sometimes. If you ultilize office hours then the HW shouldn't give you too much trouble though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Christina is very caring and wants students to succeed. She can sometimes be confusing during lecture and not cover all stuff needed on the HW so reading the textbook helps. High test average, but quizzes can be hard.

Besides BI in Higher Education, I had Capoeira. We went to Bahia, Brazil. I worked in his summer research lab with gifted students--paid internship! Faculty get lots of emails. Ask for a one-on-one after class. He'll meet you anywhere. He rewards effort all day long. So, lean in.  Sleep on, Dr. G, and you'll miss out on amazing opportunities.

AADS 4851: If you are looking for an AADS class to take, AVOID THIS PROFESSOR. This course has by far been my worst experience in any course under the AADS department, let alone any course at Vanderbilt. This man does not respond to any emails, does not provide any forms of a syllabus, and does not provide any structure to any of his courses.

The topic of his class was important and interesting, but he has you write a lot for this class alongside reading articles and a book, watching movies and doing reviews, and doing group presentations. His expectations are unclear, and unless you are majoring in AADS, I do not recommend taking this class in particular. The final ends up being LONG.

Really interesting class & you'll be well read on the topic by end of semester. However, expectations are crazy. 4 presentations, 6 papers, weekly discussion post about a book + other weekly readings. Very strict about APA, formatting is 60% of the rubric for the papers. Final project is a dissertation as in ends up 50-100 PAGES. Seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. G is a cool professor who loves Capoeira but I found myself getting frustrated at times with poor communication and unclear/varying expectations. Offered hybrid in fall of '20, easier if you're on-campus. More reading (PDFs) than expected and the quizzes sometimes focused on specific/minor details. The Capoeira itself was fun, good for AXLE.

Dr. G is a good man and cares greatly about his students. Make sure you talk to him outside of class, READ, and PARTICIPATE. He will call people out who slack off and your grade will reflect your effort. Grading is unclear, no rubrics for papers, you won't really know your grade until the very end. Good experience if you're okay with lower grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilman is a great guy but I have no idea why he doesn't answer his emails. Throughout the semester, I have emailed him several times and have yet to receive one reply back, even during the end of the semester when I'd like to discuss important things like my grade. It's very frustrating.
Good Professor but he straight up just doesn't answer emails. His lack of communication was by far the hardest thing I've had to deal with this semester in an otherwise pretty chill class.

Creative course. Dr. G. took us places that normal classes fear to go. This class engaged us in a real life death row case. We work in a real courtroom and played roles of the lawyers, jurors, and judges. We adjudicated two cases and it was so real. This course changed the way I think about black masculinity. About justice and injustice. Must take.

Dr. G is off the hook funny and serious at the same time. really interesting readings and you must participate. I really enjoyed this class. You must take but be ready to work for it. You need the books, be on time, and take advantage of the extra credit. visit him during office hours it counts and is very helpful...

Dr. G.'s Black Masculinity class was the most interesting class.. taken in four years at Vandy. The variation throughout - right down to the last class was so creative. Attendance is important, participation expected. Don't get caught up quizzes,just read. if you do poorly - extra credit available. I feel i have learned so much... if you can - take

Capoeira because it  fit international requirement, but Dr. G. made it interactive an  interesting. I am now taking classes in AADS  and Portuguese language class.   So kewl, i can't imagine any profs I've had or will have who is more there for us. 3 papers and a two days final on technique, songs, history, and Roda. Excellent

I did well in Dr. G's course and will look for him in the future. To be successful take notes always, be on time, read ahead (he will touch on everything assigned even if you think, like i did, he forgot) and v. important participation is crucial. Very informative class and learned how to write for the next level.
Read and participate. stay on top of your work Dr. G. won't do it for you.

Dr. G (as he is called) knows his stuff. He makes you create. Often frustrated me because I was used to getting so much more direction. Dr. G. made us think of our own research project while infusing current events dealing with race and sports. I enjoyed the class and will be taking his Black Masculinty F2015. B ready to read and be asked questions

Fun and amazingly interesting class. Dr. G made the most difficult things easy. I was just taking it for a requirement I think Capoeira and BrazilAfrica will be a part of my life forever.  I am taking a beginners Portuguese class in the fall as well as Dr. G's 3 credit course on Capoeira.  Good class - he will allow you just to drop in if you like
One of the best to talk to about your future. Resonable amount of reading. Group work important. As well as participation.  Would def rec

I never knew what Capoeira was until I saw it in the course offerings.  Dr. G. (Lobo Cinzento) opened my world up to my new favorite hobby. We met on Sunday afternoons and trained hard. I grew to look forward to the hard work. I feel challenged by getting up side down  not anymore. I am taking his AADS 1706 course in the fall. Cool Prof.

Dr. G. Makes you work for it, but he is awesome and will be there for you after the semester is over. He met w any student at anytime. He was always available not only during office hours but if you could not make them he would come in. We met one Sunday at 5pm. Awesome .....

Dr. G. is the coolest. He made me work, but he was so helpful and gave out books to students who did well on all assignments during the semeseter. Like 7 or 8 new books. He cares about his students. He cares about Race, Sports, and American Culture. Be ready to ready and learn...

I took the class because I needed to fill a requirement, but am so happy I chose this one. Prof. Whiting is more than just a person in the class going through the motions as many of my teachers in the past. He cares that we got not just prepared for this class, but for any class we would take in the future. Two things Read and Communicate.

Dr. G. is the most insightful professor i've taken here. If you read and are prepared to having hard discussions, you do well. You have to read and work at learning writing for publication, which means APA, or MLA, both that I now know we all need. I am enrolling in his class in the fall on Black Masculinity. Already reading the books. Great Prof.
I really enjoyed this class! The instructor was very clear about his expectations and this class always felt like more of a fun study break workout than a class.
Great class, Awesome professor.

Instructor is challenging and demanding. The reading material was always interesting.  He is organized and helpful outside of class. Would come and meet you even if you couldn't make office hours.  He will push you.  You won't pass if you don't read as participation is critical in any of his courses from what I've heard. Would take him again.
Iconic Prof. needed in my professional development

This research methods course is a must take class. The requirement to construct my own research problem, have it reviewed by four published professors is the real deal. I feel prepared to go on to a graduate level of methods. Dr. G. can be intense about class participation and attendance, but then it is bad when someone misses a once a week class.

Very knowlegable. Very nice, and loved his passion. Class informative and great first year course for anyone interested in learning how to write for college level. Def. will take another class with him

Take a course with this man, he'll change your life. A brilliant thinker, speaker, and professor, his classes aren't work, they're fun. He grades fairly, will ALWAYS offer help out of class. Seriously, if you have the opportunity, go for it. You won't be dissapointed.

very interesting class with a very knowledgeable guy/ I am thinking about joining the military and professor Whiting has better prepared me for the transition while teaching an outstanding course. Do take and DO READ and Participate. Then your assured the grade you EARNED/

Professor Whiting made us work on Research Methods to develop our own ideas. While he supported us he help me to become a better reseacher. I know im prepared to take this to the next level and this course prepared me to think i can compete. He is intense sometimes, and doesn't like excuses or laziness. I wish i had another class w him.

I took this class "only" as a upper level writing requirement. Dr. G. made me want to major in AADS. His interest and passion for the subject, and our effort was like no other that I have had at Vandy. He relates well to students and understands the demands on us. He has impacted the way I think about Race and the Military. serious students only...

First professor to make me feel like i am not in high school. He is approachable, gave great/timely/detailed  feedback, encouraged taking responsibility. Looking back he always had a plan. Great experience, VGood Prof., Highly recommend taking his classes if you can be focused.

I have taken three classes with Dr. Whiting, including AADS 115. I worked real, real hard. But I learned a lot, lot, lot. It's worth it. Prepared me for classes in History and English (writing component as well as historical materials covered). Plus he is fun to talk to in office hours.

Had class in spring. I am looking for another Whiting course this year. The keys to acing his classes (got an A-): read and participate (he places a premium on these); learn APA and read that manual (it will be on midterm but it also helped me write a better paper); and go to the writing studio. He is a tough grader. So another reader never hurts.

As someone who plans a career in teaching, I found Prof. Whiting's Black Issues in Education course to be a must. I didn't know the history of educational inequity in this country or much about the achievement gap. I learned about cultural competence and other concepts in education. It was eye opening. He is passionate about the subject.

Haters and skaters have been out in full force. Took this class as freshmen in 09. Prof. did not mess around with those of us who didn't read. READ PEOPLE. Otherwise, he was chill. Liked class participation aspect. Took another upper level course. learned a good deal. Have to work though.

Took this class last spring. Prof. Whiting was fun. Readings were interesting. He is a tough grader. Makes you think out the box and pushes you to do your best. You won't do well if you don't read. You will have to participate. And yes, you will learn APA. Helped me in my other classes. But class was always rigorous and stimulating.
took class in spring 11, great professor. you will have to work for your grade though.

Dr. Whiting is one of those professor who can truly inspire you to think critically about the world and education.  Not only was his class useful in helping me to TRULY master APA (beyond simple HOD apa) , but he and the class was helpful in guiding me toward my career path.  Dr. Whiting is a great resource if you are willing to reach out to him.

I def would not register for this class.This dude is out of his mind. He talks about his self most of the time as if he's an olympic winner.NEWSFLASH, YOU'RE NOT RUNNING THE 800 METER ANYMORE!Unclear about things, will not help you directly.Try to make you feel bad, the list goes on.Learning how to do apa is the only thing from this guy.Dont do it!

I disagree with most of the comments about Professor Whiting! AADS 210 was a GREAT class taught by a GREAT professor, who is very knowledgeable about the subject matter. To do well in this class, make sure you keep up on your readings and participate in class discussions. Also, do not hesitate to ask questions! I would recommend taking this course

He was rude, very negative, and disinterested in his students.  Class time was spent attacking us for our incompetence while glorifying himself.  I honestly learned nothing about writing other than how to cite using APA format and write abstracts.

As a student who has taken two of Professor Whiting's courses, I disagree with many of the prior comments posted.  While many may label him as UNFAIR,the truth is that he only pushes his students to be the BEST students they can be! He is a very knowledgeable, personable professor who constantly strives for  excellence from himself and his students

In my opinion, the statements made against Professor Whiting are both inaccurate and grossly unfair. I took his Black Masculinity course my junior year, and it was one of the most rewarding experiences at Vanderbilt. The reading assignments were pretty long, but they were necessary to understand the lecture and also engage the guess speakers Whitin

Law School done!  I watch 30% of my class wash out 1st yr. they couldn't think for themselves. I've understand now why he is a stickler for detail. It's because Prof. Whiting totally knew critical original thought works. He was looking into a future i did not understand. Fun person who cares. If your serious, he's the man. Not GPA booster.

THE WORSE TEACHER AT VANDERBILT BY FAR!!please avoid this professor at all cost.he is unclear, disorganized, arrogant, and hardly ever responds to emails.You do not know where you stand as far as grades until they have RUINED YOUR GPA!!!i thought if i did the work and went to class i would do ok but this is FALSE.TRUST ME AVOID HIM!!!!!!!

Worst prof I've had here. Anal about APA style but other than that fails to give feedback about papers. Thinks he is much cooler than he really is. Never talk about readings inclass. When we do, he jumps from topic to topic. Very condescending. Never answers emails. Thinks our inability to follow his incoherence a reflection on students not him.

Prof. Whiting is a cool guy to just talk to, but as a professor he sucks!!! I had little interest in the class to begin with, but he has further dampened my interest in the subject matter. His directions are extremely unclear, and he is anal about APA style. He does not respond to emails and will rarely show up for class the week a major assignment
I thought I had a decent grade all semester but Whiting is so disorganized that there is no way of knowing where you stand in his class. I don't recommend taking this seminar.

In AADS 115W, you get a lot of work and the reading is very intensive, but atleast it's interesting.  You only write about 4 major papers, and the class mainly focuses on reading, watching movies, discussion, and APA style.  Whiting can sometimes be very unclear and confusing about assignments and deadlines though. You just have to learn how he is.
He is very unorganized and he does not tell tou his expectations ahead of time.
most unclear professor ever imaginable.  you are never aware of where you stand on your grade.  the class sounded interesting BEFORE i took it, but turned out to be a nightmare.  AVOID THIS CLASS.

Whiting is a great guy. I really liked his class and he's a fun prof. to have. I learned a lot in his class. It is true though that he does assign a lot of work and def. doesn't really give you deadlines about when its due. He's also a REALLY tough grader. He will def. make you work for your grade but as long as he sees the effort you'll be ok.
No Comments

This guy loves to embarass people in class and make you feel dumb as hell. He gives you tons of work without any clear deadlines so you never know when work is due and then you get punished for not being prepared. I withdrew from this class last semester and it was the best thing I did last semester. Avoid Prof. Whiting AT ALL COSTS!!!

The class is challenging, but if you put in effort, it's definitely possible to succeed. Professor Simonett cares a lot about his students and making sure that we understand the content. I would highly recommend taking him!
This coming year will be his last one, so 100% take him if you can. The class is very hard, but it is not graded hard, and Professor Simonett is easily the most caring Professor I have taken.

This professor is truly a great person and genuinely cares about his students. He teaches extremely difficult content, which makes it difficult to find this class easy, however if you go to class, office hours, and do your homework, you will find it possible to succeed. He encourages collaboration on homework, which helps immensely.
Very good and nice professor. Doesn't grade hard, but that doesn't make the class easy. Lots of work but definitely worth it.

very caring prof who truly cares about the well-being of his student. a good option to take if you're taking 2300. not very accessible outside of class so try to ask questions in class and make some friends u can go to

Prof. Simonett's lectures are very clear and he lets you know exactly what he wants you to master. The course itself is not easy and definitely takes a lot of time to learn, but Prof. Simonett can give you a very clear direction. He is very kind and caring.

2500 is a rigorous but very rewarding class if you are interested in pure math. Homework consists of one proof-based problem set per week, and collaboration with classmates is encouraged. Simonett is such a nice professor. He gives great lectures and tells hilarious stories. His office hours are very helpful.

While MATH 2500 may seem daunting at first, I would encourage anyone interested in the more rigorous side of math to take the course. Professor Simonett is a great professor and is very helpful in his office hours. I would also highly encourage anyone taking MATH 2500 to work collaboratively with their classmates as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: 2500 is incredibly hard, but incredibly worthwhile. Simonett gives great lectures, but still expect to read from the textbook A LOT. His office hours are very good, and grading wise the class gives you a ton of cushion with HW being 55%. Don't be scared to take this course but be ready to put in more effort than classes like gen chem require.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Simonett has a calm and collected demeanor. He is a good teacher and is very patient. This class is difficult if you don't keep up with homework (which is not graded). The consolation is that the final exam score can be used to replace one of your previous midterms. Prof. Simonett will always make time for you and address your needs.

Professor Simonett was excellent and knew the material. He was accessible to students and wanted to see every student succeed. The class contained three midterms and a final, with optional homework questions integrated into the exams. Professor Simonett was fair with grading and provided study guides for the tests. I highly recommend him for multi.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Multi is a tough subject, but Dr. Simonett makes it really manageable. The tests questions mostly come straight from homework so just study the homework to do well. It is clear he really cares about his students and wants the best for them!
Writes on board so fast and runs very mid office hours

Prof. Simonett is great. The classes he teaches are tough so naturally not the "easiest" professor but he does a great job lecturing and assigns only necessary homework. If you dedicate yourself you can do well in his class. I would say to take advantage of his study guides (they're typically very representative of the tests) and the homeworks.

If you're a freshmen able to take 2500/2501, its an amazing opportunity that will literally change how you think about math and prepare you for any challenge thereafter. Gieri Simonett is definitely the right professor to teach the class.

I took the 2500/01 freshman track and although it was a rocky path at first, it was definitely a worthy challenge. The material is very packed and abstract, but Dr Simonett did his best to set me up to succeed. In terms of grading, you need to earn the points but he is generous overall. Is accessible and really cares about his students. Take him!

2501 is a very challenging proof-based and content-heavy class. A lot of people, myself included, had trouble adjusting to the quick yet rigorous pace of the course, but Professor Simonett made this transition possible. He was always very helpful during every office hour and clearly cared about his students well-being. Take his class if you can!
This class is really hard. Be careful lol don't get stuck in it like me

Professor Simonett is an amazing math professor. All of the lectures are clear and he makes complicated concepts easy to understand. The class is also pretty generously graded (50% of the score is based on HW). The weekly problem sets teach you as much as the lectures. He's not very accessible for office hours, but the TA's office hours are great.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Simonett's expectations are very straightforward: for every test, you are expected to memorize every theorem, proof, and definition from the chapter. Weekly problem sets are extremely difficult. Made the class way harder than it needed to be-- the other 3100 prof gave take-home tests and let students redo HWs for a higher grade.

Overall good professor. Class material is tough but he generally explains it pretty well. Reading the textbook will help with understanding but is probably not that necessary since he explains stuff decently in class. Definitely do the optional homework because you'll fail otherwise. He's very clear with what he wants you to know for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Simonett is really an amazing professor! He makes his lectures really easy to follow and he gives super helpful study guides before each exam. He gives a lot of optional homework (sometimes even before he finishes the material) so studying outside of the class is also very important!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 2300 was super hard for me, but Simonett is definitely the best professor to have for it. The class is crazy difficult. Do the homework problems to study for the tests. Simonett is the nice prof I have ever had. He is so invested in his student's learning and met with me every week in office hours. So so kind. Great guy, horrible class/material.

Simonett is the sweetest prof I've had and genuinely cares about helping his students succeed, but he expects you to work incredibly hard to get there. PAY ATTENTION TO STUDY GUIDES for exams, go to office hours. HW is not graded but necessary to pass exams. You'll come out of the class with a good understanding of multi.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hard prof, nice but difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Simonett brings an amazing attitude to class. He cares a lot about students but requires significant work from them as well. Four tests determine your entire grade, so there isn't any room for error. Homework is optional in name only. Always had an A+ in Calc 1 and 2 but multivariable was much more difficult and I got my first B or C ever
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: This was a very difficult class for me as a freshman, yet despite not doing well in the class, it is clear professor Simonett is a great professor. Definitely go through all the ungraded homework and give the study guide an in-depth look. His exam averages were all usually in the high 80s, so most students do pretty good.

Great professor - my favorite math professor so far! He is helpful, his lectures are clear, and he says what to expect on tests. He never tries to trick you, and his grading is very reasonable. Multivariable calculus is not easy math but if you do the homework and pay attention in class you will be fine. Professor Simonett wants you to do well!

Best MATH2300 professor! Homework is optional, but you should do it because a lot of the test questions are really similar. Go to office hours because Professor Simonett is really helpful. (I had no multi experience before)

Professor Simonett is extremely caring and passionate about Multi. Do the homework and stay on top of the material and the tests will be fine. Lectures are great but very conceptual so the hw is important to get practice doing problems. Go to office hours because he is super helpful and is also a really nice guy! -Freshman with no prior Multi class

Professor Simonett is a great lecturer and cares about his students. He gives clear proofs on the concepts in class and grades his exams loosely. HW is not required and the final grade depends on 4 exams. Also don't listen to those who say you need previous experience--Multivariable Calculus is hard but manageable if you attend class and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Simonett is such a caring professor, but you can't expect to just show up to class and get an A. The homework is optional, but definitely a necessity if you want to succeed in the class. Go into office hours often with any homework questions, or even just to check the answers for even numbered problems. Get to know him - he's so kind!

Definitely the best professor for 2300. Hw is not graded but prepares you well for tests. He posts a study guide for each test outlining what you need to know. Lectures are clear and he doesn't move at too fast of a pace. As long as you study for the tests and have some interest in math you can get an A. -Freshman who never took multi before.

Any negative reviews are definitely just people who do the bare minimum in class and still expect an A. Simonett cares abt his students are wants them to succeed but u do (obviously) still need to work hard. Tough class great prof
100% best Professor for 2300
Simonett makes me love math. Nicest most caring Professor while also (rightfully) expecting the best from his students
Hard class but fantastic Professor
FAVORITE TEACHER

1 of best teachers Ive had! 2300s tough but hes by far best prof for it. Great person, really cares abt his students. Hw s optional but dont be lazy- tests resemble the hardest hw probs. GO TO OFFICE HRS. He is v accessible to students. If you like math u will love his class. PS Im a freshman. Nobody in my class had taken multi before.

His lecture is clear. Homework workload medium. Definitely not harsh at grading( calculation errors weigh 1 point on test or so). Test question types are specified and practice question demoed in class. Only issue is that you have to go to proof for theorems urself: he only addresses the most critical ones. Do the HW and I think A is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Simonett is a really passionate teacher who cares about his students' success. The expectations for the class are very clear and tests are hard but very doable. Homework is optional, but required to do well on the tests. Thus, if you are not very self-motivated/organized and don't stay on top of the homework, you may struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Simonetts class is very difficult but he is there to help you through it. Test are the main component of grading and although there arent many curves, they are fair and give you the chance to succeed. Very caring, very personal
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Simonett is a decent lecturer, though he spends too much time on proofs and not enough on practice problems in class. His study guides are pretty useful. He bases exam questions almost directly from HW questions, so DO THE HW (even tho it's optional). Don't show up to class late consistently or else he will call you out in front of the class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the best choice for MATH 2300, his study guides are extremely helpful and I do recommend looking over them thoroughly. It is important to pay attention especially if this is your first mathematics class at college. The homework is a lot but it is very useful for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best choices for 2300. Really helpful inside and out of class, and he is very straightforward in what he expects for each test. Paying attention in his class is more important than other math classes, however, as he highlights different methods for sketching/parameterizations than the textbook that he expects us to follow on the test.

Prof. Simonett was an inspiration for this difficult class, willing to curve tests if they were too difficult, and made the final optional for those content with their grades. Truly cares about his students and their learning. Highly recommend, may be more theoretical in MATH 2300 than strictly necessary.

Professor Simonett was amazing. I genuinely think having him as a professor is the reason I didn't drop the class during the first week. He makes 2300 extremely manageable and genuinely wants his students to succeed. The homework he gives is also extremely helpful.

You can tell he really cares about his students. This class isn't necessarily easy, you definitely have to put in the work however, he is a very organized and clear lecturer and easily accessible outside of class if you ever need help.

Professor Simonett is easily one of the kindest people at Vanderbilt. His lectures are easy to understand and he genuinely cares if students understand the material or not. He gives lots of homework but his tests are straightforward and he wont try to trick you.

Dr. Simonett is the best math professor I've had at Vandy, and it isn't even close. Exams are straightforward, and he gives study guides outlining topics to look over for each of them. He genuinely cares about all of his students, inside and outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Gieri Simonett is the man. Lectures are pointless to attend. I ended up losing knowledge compared to when I entered on some days. But he gives you everything you need to succeed. Just follow his study guides and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing and Caring prof. Hard class but he genuinely wants you to learn and understand the material. I had some special circumstances this semester and he was willing to meet with me outside of class and office hours to help get me back on track. Best math prof ive had at vandy so far

The best, and nicest, professor I have ever had. Goes over concepts slowly and deliberately, and makes an effort to make sure everything is understood before moving on. I never felt like I was playing catch-up. He cares about YOUR success, and he is always willing to go over HW/tests and sometimes give extra points here and there.

Prof. Simonett is a very kind man who clearly cares about his students. He is also a pretty good lecturer. That said, the course is very difficult and a lot of the material is proof-based and abstract, even though the course title hints at applications (of which there are few.) 3 midterms (75%), homework (25%), no final. Overall, solid choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Unreasonable amount of proofs for a methods-focused class. Spends too much time in class on proofs instead of going through practice problems. Weekly homework takes a while, but is worth 25% of the grade, which is nice. Tests are tough (he thinks a class average of 80 is good), but he provides helpful study guides (study them religiously).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Simonett is extremely organized and caring. The lecture follows the textbook, but beware of alternative proofs and some extra materials he throws in. He tests you on how familiar you are with the course materials and does not ask for too much ingenuity. HWs are intensive, but reasonable. One of the best 3100 instructors at Vandy so far.

Prof Simonett gives you a TON of homework but its OK because its worth 40% of your grade. He is great because he gives out these study guides before each test and if you know each topic you will do very well on the tests. He doesnt try to trick you and teaches the material in a super accessible way. Hes also really nice! Will take again for sure

No final, four midterms, which are heavy proof-based, but you can drop the lowest one, which means that if you do well on the first three, your grade is guaranteed almost one month earlier before the end of semester. He gives a lot of homework and grades them strictly, and homework counts for a lot. In general, it is not hard to get A in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No final, so the three midterms count for a lot-- and they're hard. this prof practically only tests knowledge/memorization of proofs/theorems. Gieri is an extremely nice and understanding guy, but he is definitely not a great professor. Even my friends in my class who were math majors struggled to get anything higher than a C in this class.

I enjoyed being in Dr. Simonett's class. He gives a lot of homework and his tests are lengthy for the time given, but he taught the material well. He is a bit soft spoken and has a foreign accent, but he's easy to understand nonetheless. He was always very nice and obviously cares about his students.

Dr. Simonett loves teaching and you can definitely tell by his teaching quality. His tests are straightforward and he wont test you on any concept that wasnt in the homework. He is one of the nicest professors Ive had.

Professor Simonett really cares about his students. He is very organized and I thought he was very easy to understand despite his accent (he's from Switzerland).  This class is definitely hard but he is extraordinarily helpful. He gives a lot of homework but that helped me learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: He teaches in a very standard lecture style where he covers one or two chapters of the book. Attending his lectures are not necessary (read the textbook), but he assigns a large amount of homework. The professor is very straightforward with his expectations on tests and won't throw curveballs. It may be a little too straightforward for some.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is heavily based on lectures and homework problems. His lectures are interesting and well taught. He assigns a few hours of homework a week, but the homework problems are almost exactly paralleled on the test. Go to class and do the homework and the class should be easy.

He gives pretty clear lectures and tries to focus on concepts rather than memorization, which is nice. His tests are always just a little to long to finish in the amount of time we have. The biggest downsides are that he assigns a few hours' worth of mandatory hw every class, and stops class to interrogate anybody who walks in even 5 minutes late

At First I put my focus in class on note taking on his lectures. I used these notes for the first test to study and got a D. It was after this I realized how unhelpful and incoherent his lectures were, and that studying online and the textbook was the way to go, and got a 90 on the next test. Also not helpful in office hours. Have to self teach.

Ordinary differential equations are not fun, but Simonett very clearly enjoys the subject and teaching it. His office hours are very helpful and his grading is very fair. I always felt that I got the grade I studied for. His lectures are very coherent and focused and the homework actually helps you practice the processes he presents in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Simonett is one of the better math profs at Vandy. If you seek out help even a little, he's there. Tests are pretty straightforward, but definitely not easy. That is, you'll know exactly what you need to study for each of the three tests and final. There' not much of a curve. The homework is really time-consuming so DO NOT start at the last minute

Clearly enjoys teaching and wants to help his students. Approachable during office hours as well. That being said, his explanations can sometimes be unclear and it was difficult for me to do well in this class because I did not get a solid foundation of the material at the beginning of the semester. Tests are challenging.

Attendance is absolutely mandatory (this goes for any Multivariable class, not just Simonett's). His quizzes are usually straightforward; tests emphasize theory and are more challenging. He was very approachable during office hours and he genuinely wants his students to learn a lot about calculus. He's a kind professor and will try to help you out.

Simonett was a fantastic teacher. The material on the test was difficult, but if you take notes and study, then you can get A's. The people who struggled were those who didn't come to class. All the test questions are from notes or homework. Sometimes he brings donuts... so that's nice

Professor Simonett is one of the rare professors who truly cares about how his students are doing in and outside of class. He explains things well and will do anything to help you understand the material. His tests and quizzes can be difficult, but they are also fair. He is definitely one of the best professors in the math department and at Vandy.

Prof Simonett is one of the best math teachers at Vanderbilt. He explains the material well, and provides good examples in class. His quizzes and tests are kind of rough, but he is an extremely easy grader and gives a lot of extra credit. He does ask us to memorize a few proofs, but he always clearly tells us exactly which proofs to know. Take him!
Simonett is a very good teacher, but his tests are impossible. The book is relatively useless, and Simonett likes to focus on proofs. The other 175 professors are  easier.
He knows his stuff. He has a slight accent, but overall he's a good lecturer. He gives quizzes every Wednesday which are moderately hard. The tests are manageable. He's helpful outside of class.

Simonett is very sympathetic to undergrads and willing to help.  However, his lectures aren't very well organized and he isn't very good at guiding students along to understanding.  He can be kind of boring in class and the accent is a little distracting.  The class itself isn't hard if you are decent at math and do homework occasionally.

Let me convince you of something....This man, the Greek god ZEUS, is absolutely amazing.  His tests arn't that hard, but he makes the quizzes too long and hard.  He drops two quizzes.  He also says squrred, instead of squared.  His stories are hysterical!

Dr. Simonett is a fantastic professor, and really nice! He makes sure that you understand everything in the class and the concepts behind it. He moves faster than other classes, but I learned more than my friends who had diff. professors. Sometimes he does random stuff, like bring in donuts or have people draw dragons on the board.

you might wanna skip out on this one. while you hear other 175 classes breezing through the course a few people can be seen studying on monday night stressed out beyond anything. avoid him at all cost even if it means sacrificing your electives.

this is an excellent prof. The course is hard so you have to do the work but his tests/quizes are reasonable. His lectures aren't all that bad (not borinig even at 8:10AM) for math.  He adds quirky things to class to keep students interested and he tells stories that are halarious.
He will do whatever it takes to make sure his students understand the material.  He is very clear in his lectures, and he is a big fan of partial credit.  A great professor

Difficult material, difficult tests, but Simonett does whatever he can to help you understand.  His lectures are very good.  Also, very nice and interesting to talk to in an out of class.  Brought donuts on several occasions.
Really tough tests, but entertaining to listen to and brings in treats for you! Helps you out so that you do well in his class.

He is pretty much the definition of HARD. His tests are extremely long u wont finish it in time, and on top of that its HARD. The man is super smart, i think that's why he expect his students to be as smart as he is..AVOID AVOID
Shami is a wonderful professor and really tries his best to help you.
Avoid this teacher if you can. The class is hard as it is (harder than 155A somehow), and with Shami as your teacher it just won't be good. Avoid avoid avoid.

so i def dropped this class. if u can't understand him, i advise you do the same. the class is exceedingly difficult [well, the quizzes at least] compared to other sections. office hours are helpful, but he may get stuck on a student, and forget about u. knows his business, and teaches as if u do too. test him quickly, & get out early if ur unsure
Really nice guy, not a good teacher. He is very difficult to understand. Class is pretty much useless. He is only good one on one in office hours You are better off with a different teacher
Hard but not too bad if you go to tutoring and office hours. Shami is helpful but has a thick accent.
Shami is a cool dude and a really smart guy.  He is a good teacher who is helpful in office hours.  He also curves the class...by a lot.
he curves... intelligent man, but sometimes too intelligent to teach clearly

As a person, Shami's helpful, cares about his students, and is a funny, cool guy. As a professor, his English is hardly intelligible, his teaching methods don't make the most sense, but he makes the quizzes really easy on you.  He may be worth taking if you already understand the material completely and you want to get away with not doing a lot
No Comments

He's in good nature but can't speak the language.  He tries to be clear but it's just impossible.  Try picking an english sounding name for this class- it will help a ton. Im getting a much better grade this semester because I'm retaking it and I have a better teacher.
Shami is by far the worst teacher on the face of the earth. He's a real funny dude though, but he can't teach to save his life.

Nice guy but can no longer teach. He frequently gets lost during lectures and provides little meaningful explanation of the material. Expect to teach yourself entirely from the textbook. Insane that I paid tuition to take this class.

Webb is good at teaching differential equations and has been working in his field for over 50 years. That said, he is old and past his prime. Very difficult to hear speak, even when sitting in front row, it was basically useless to go to class. Had to teach myself differential equation, I would recommend someone else for this course.Also Exam Heavy

No tests. 1/3 weekly HWs, 1/3 midterm paper, 1/3 final paper. Interesting exploration of mathematical biology. Webb cares a lot and doesn't seem to have strict grading criteria as long as you put in some effort.

He is a nice guy but the lectures were extremely dry and uninformative. You will have to teach yourself everything but the textbook doesn't pretty good job. The exams don't look anything like the homework but he tells you everything to put on your formula sheet and is a very lenient grader.

Nicest guy you'll ever meet, but also probably one of the worst professors in the department. Trick to this class is just don't go. He'll tell you what you need to know for the exams. Just learn the methods from the textbook, copy them onto your cheat sheet, and then take the exam. Beware that tests are very fast-paced.

HW is chill but tedious and he doesn't really do examples in class so you have to figure it out yourself. Tests are fast-paced but should be fine if you have a cheatsheet. Don't go to class just read the textbook and you'll be fine

Chill math elective- some HW and 2 projects, no exams. Webb is kind, but you definitely do not need to go to class (most people did not). His lectures are a bit dry and difficult to stay engaged with, but reading the textbook (for the 1st half) and reviewing the slides (for the 2nd half) is sufficient to be able to do the HW. The projects were cool

Lectures are dry and not terribly helpful, but the class is structured very nicely so that you can basically just read the textbook outside of class to keep up. The textbook is actually quite decent. Midterms are pretty straightforward, and the homework isn't too bad.
Yes, his differential equation class have the A- grade (which is not mentioned in the syllabus). Don't need to go to class. Read the textbook, grind through the problems and you'll be fine.

Professor Webb is very nice. His lectures are interesting and informative, although he sometimes gets confused by his notes during his lectures. If you take his class definitely make a point to talk with him after class. He is more than willing to explain things to you  that you don't understand or even show what he is working on.

Webb is nice, but honestly I think he's past his prime. He doesn't really do any prep for lectures-- shows up, reads off his slides (which are photos, not just screenshots, but photos of the textbook and his paper notes), and confuses himself. Lectures then are worthless and you learn reading the textbook. Super long psets (5-7 hrs weekly).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The Professor is nice and caring, but the material of the class is becoming more and more difficult throughout time. The last few chapters are very difficult and I felt they are not very thoroughly explained.

Very accommodating, genuinely nice and sweet professor. Lectures are mainly reading textbook notes (useless). Homework is worth the same as a midterm, and his midterms and final are difficult if you do not study a lot. You have to put in very solid work throughout the semester to earn a good grade in his class. Def one of the easier diff eq profs
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tests are straightforward but sometimes there are some tricky questions. Homework is too much, expect to spend more than 6 hours per week on homework.
Very nice professor, but he gives much harder tests and assignments

Not the best prof but def very nice on grading. Allows formula sheets, tests straightforward. Extremely abundant office hours - all I hope if long live Glenn Webb (guy taught at Vandy for over half a century, makes him almost in the 80s). Regularly pushes due dates & exams back but DOES NOT USE BRIGHTSPACE WHAT???

While Webb isn't amazing, he's the best you can really ask for in Vandy's math department. He cares about his students and want them to succeed. Tests are very straightforward, and you get to bring a formula sheet making them pretty simple in terms of how to succeed in the class. He helps a lot with HW in office hours. Lectures can be confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Glenn is overall pretty good, but this course is truly harder than I expected. You literally need to do well on every single one of the test as well as the homework to get an A. Be prepared to the tests and even you prepared, the results may still disappoint you.

Nice and caring professor, but a difficult class. Tests were manageable since,they were heavily based off the textbook. He is also a quiet professor and does get off on math tangents every now and then.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Kind professor who cares about understanding rather than tripping us up. Super helpful in office hours. You see in him qualities that make a great mathematican.

Webb is an adorably soft-spoken professor. Super knowledgable and super passionate about ODEs. Sometimes a bit spacey in lecture but super helpful in office hours. Homework due for every class, but it's short and fairly easy.

Sweet, thoughtful, and soft-spoken professor. Class is 1/3 HW, 1/3 15 page midterm paper, 1/3 20 page final paper. Class material is mostly concerned with analysis of biologically-related systems of ODEs (e.g. HIV, populations, SIR models). Great time to learn Mathematica. Start early on papers. Webb often gives solutions & extensions for HW.
He keeps things very simple and he's one of the kindest and helpful professors I know.

Alright professor. Class isn't too difficult, just make sure you pay attention to the definitions. Has to redo his notes a lot during class but worth going to as he gives shortcuts for how to do many of the problems on his tests.

Professor Webb is one of the professors I respect the most. He is very knowledgeable in his subject and he is always very patient and willing to help students outside of the class and he wants to give as much what he knows to his students as possible. And as a person, he's a very neat and nice old man. I love this man.

A professor who is extremely knowledgeable with his field, loves his students, and loves teaching.  He is more concerned about students learning (without sacrificing too much of their grades). He is never reluctant for a side talk. This is what distinguishes him to be a good educator from a person merely knowledgeable about his or her fields.

Tests are very easy because he allows equation sheets and problems are nothing else but plugging in the equations. Lectures can be a little unclear sometimes as he suddenly starts talking about materials not relevant to the class. Great prof in general.

Nice old man. Although his voice is low, you got used to it after the first few lectures. Allows formula sheets. Assigns a reasonable amount of homework for every lecture so that you get familiar with the lecture material with minimal workload.

He is sometimes very hard to hear and goes on random tangents and doesn't end up explaining he material very well. Compounded with the book being terrible, it can be hard to understand what's going on. However, he is helpful outside of class and his tests are straight from the homework. "medium difficulty problems".

Sometimes he'll go off on crazy tangents or ridiculously long problems, but you don't really need to worry about most of that. As long as you write lots of examples of the formula sheets your should do fine as almost, if not all, of the questions on tests are from the book. Also on tests he sometimes puts definitions so put those on the sheet also.

Knows the stuff well and is pretty good at teaching you what you need to know. Work the homeworks and then work similar problems before tests and you should have no problem. Tests Qs are mostly striaght out of the book so nothing too difficult. Being allowed to use a formula sheet on each test was a huge plus and made it all about just practicing.
Very nice guy but also very boring.  Class wasn't hard.  Simple homework assignments and tests were pretty straight forward.  Still, be prepared for a very boring lecture.

Stop giving the Webbmaster bad ratings because you are not smart.  He is a very bright man, extremely helpful office hours and teaches a course which is necessary for all forms of mathematical modeling/computational math.  His course is easier than the other section also.  He is also experienced in modeling in biology (think DE Shaw).
awful..u can barely hear him, and even you do, is not helpful at all. if u choose his class, just do to the class. ur TA will be much helpful than him

A genuinely nice old man.  He gets forgetful sometimes while doing math on the board, but all in all if you ask him a question he will do it, no questions.  Assignments everyday, but they are short and easy, and he'll do the problems for you in his office hours if you go.  Tests are a mix of definitions and problems, not a hard class, take him.

Had Prof. Glembocki for both 1500 and 2500, and while his lectures might be boring and content heavy, he is very flexible with grading. 2500 is more focused on electromagnetism, and exams are mostly application type questions. Final project instead of exam. A lot of self-studying required!

Glembocki is relatively new to Vanderbilt, and I think he has trouble with Brightspace and TopHat. Having said that, he is very aware that he's scattered and he doesn't expect to be taken seriously all the time. He has a very relaxed class structure, which I appreciate in contrast to other stuffy engineering professors. He's also really empathetic.

Glembocki is just sooo boring. Seems like a really nice guy but wow lectures taught me nothing. Not a terribly hard class or impossible to pass. But, I really feel like I did not get anything out of it.

I was skeptical to take MSE 1500 with Professor Glembocki after seeing a lot of the other reviews, but he is one of my favorite professors. His class is at 9 am so it's hard to make it some days but he's super sweet and explains all of the concepts in ways we can understand. He gives you equations for exams and grades fairly with partial credit.

I hate being this harsh, but here goes. Glembocki was a mess for 1500 last year. Test formats changed constantly and were always annoying. Questions didn't make sense. Lectures were often redundant/wrong; Glembocki couldn't answer a lot of questions I had in class. Might get better in person, but I wouldn't take the chance. Hard sell.

Honestly after dropping out of Chem 1601 I was expecting MSE to be easier, but this section is definitely not. There is little guidance and help given to solve the homework problems, the lectures are horrendously boring, and you actually have to attend because he uses TopHat to log participation in class. It's hard to take notes without an iPad too
Professor Globetti is a great professor! I'm taking Intro to American Democracy at UNC-CH and her lectures are always engaging. I am not a poli major, but would definitely take again!

I'm not sure that I've ever liked a professor as much as Globetti. She gives extremely in-depth feedback on weekly assignments, is a great lecturer, and is just generally likable. Grading and exams were reasonable, but you definitely need to demonstrate knowledge of content to do well. Put in a little effort, and you can do well. Highly recommend.

Professor Globetti is probably the nicest professor you will ever have. She is unbelievably caring, intelligent, and engaging. Class is enjoyable and she incorporates current events to make the material more interesting. She truly cares about you inside and outside of class and wants you to succeed.

Globetti is incredible. She's leaving next year to UNC and Vanderbilt will suffer... one of the most caring and sweetest people you'll ever meet in college. Her class was very fair  if you studied, you did well. The group project was also fun. Take her if you can, even if you aren't into the subject. She's a gem.

I would highly recommend taking any class with Professor Globetti. She makes her lectures interactive and interesting, and this class was really not hard to do well in. Projects are not too bad and pretty fun, and you can definitely get an A just by attending and participating.
Great teacher, super caring, and awesome person in general. Her lectures are informative and fun. Pay attention and take notes in class because it shows up on the tests.

Globetti is awesome and you should definitely take her if you're interested in political science at all. She gives great lectures and has very clear requirements for papers and assignments. Tests and assignments aren't hard if you pay attention and take good notes. She's always willing to help outside of class as well.

One of the best professors at Vandy hands down. Class isn't an easy A, but if you show up to class, study for tests, and do your work, you'll be fine. Lots of optional textbook reading, but it is highly recommended, as it definitely pays off on tests. Dr. Globetti is such a sweet lady who really cares about her students. Highly recommend.

Globetti is the best! Very helpful, even on weekends, and genuinely cares that her students do well. Slightly harder than I thought it would be, but still very manageable and fun. Welcomes all viewpoints. Some readings can be long, but don't fret about them because if you study the lecture slides and study guide, you will do well. Take her ASAP!

Professor Globetti made my freshman year not so tough. Don't get me wrong, this class is not an easy A. She answers her emails ASAP, she welcomes discussion in class, and she drops the lowest quiz grade. She is also hilarious. The lecture is interesting and she makes fantastic notes. One down side, SO MUCH reading (it helps though). Take Globetti!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the kindest human beings. Definitely a "no wrong answer" kind of teacher and cares so much about her individual students. She herself is an easy grader, but her TAs grade the tests and can be very difficult graders. The readings aren't necessary to participate in class, but are important to do well on the quizzes and tests.

One of the nicest and best professors I have had. As usual, hard to get an A but A- is very achievable (in her Political Campaigns class). Particularly interesting. I did not dread going to her class and she made learning enjoyable.

Professor Globetti is one the best Professors at Vanderbilt. She is incredibly knowledgeable. Her lectures are clear and very easy to take notes from. She presents very complicated information in a comprehendible manner. She isn't an easy grade but she's very clear about what she expects. Go to class, take notes, you'll be fine.
Prof Globetti is really nice. She is easily available, always reply my email immediately. She is good at the lectures and is respected by students. Great professor. Good class, worth taking

Professor Globetti brings a ton of energy and her passion to every single lecture. This makes the class extremely refreshing. i decided to take this course again after taking it in high school and I'm glad I did. She is an awesome teacher and offers a lot of extra-credit opportunities. The grading is also fairly easy. I strongly recommend her.

Prof. Globetti is great. Most classes are very interesting and her lectures are always clear. Her tests are easy if you pay attention in class and take notes. She is also one of the nicest people I've ever met. Taking this class has  made me contemplate becoming a PSCI major and I would recommend it to everybody.

Prof. Globetti is amazing.  She is probably my favorite professor that I have had so far.  She is very clear about what she expects and makes the material interactive with current events.  If you put the work in, you will get a good grade.  Definitely take this class whether or not you are interested in politics.

This class with Globetti is sooo easy. The only issue I found with the class was that is obviously politically conservative and it was far too prominent in how she directed and responded to class discussion. It didn't help that the textbook was a conservative manifesto to 'Merica: The Best Country Ever.
Fantastic professor! She can make anyone interested in American politics! Fun and exciting, she comes highly recommended.

Prof. Globetti is one of the nicest teachers I have ever had. She gets to know all of her students throughout the semester, giving the 200 person lecture hall a more personal feel. If you go to class and type/write down the notes from her daily power points, you should a very good grade. I highly recommend this class!

Professor Globetti is so helpful and genuinely interested in seeing everyone succede. In my class of over 200 kids she seems to know almost everyone by name and engages the class in meaningful discussion. Exams are easy and cover the information on her slides in class. Textbook reading is minimal and not necessary if you take notes. Easy A.

Professor Globetti is extremely nice and seems genuinely interested in the subject and in the success of the students. The tests are very reasonable and follow closely to the powerpoints and textbook reading. I would definitely recommend taking Professor Globetti and PSCI100 to fulfill an AXLE requirement and get a pretty decent grade.
She's very nice and helpful-go to class and take notes and you can get an A
Take this class! She is one of the nicest, most unpretentious professors I've ever had, and she really works hard to make the class interesting. Not too much work outside of class, 3 major tests.
Really nice teacher. Class is easy, test are easy. Just go to class (which is required) and take notes. You'll get at least a B.
Very passionate and skilled lecturer. Offers a clear picture of the subject matter and is great both inside and outside of class in handling individual questions. Great professor to have.

Great Professor. Very clear in class and always willing to help outside of class. Classes are directly tied to the textbook readings so its really easy to follow along. Tests are fair and not too hard.
awesome professor.  tests are fair and if you go to class you will feel well prepared.  very nice and cares for his students. HIGHLY recommend

Highlights: Great Lecturer - enthusiastic;  Tests are fair - he goes over what will be on it all you need to do is study; Projects/Homework - can be difficult but can be conquered with a group. Negatives: homework is a little out of place when compared to his lectures. Overall: Great professor, great quality - learn a lot
New professor, still figuring things out.  Problems sets, 1 midterm, 1 group project and a final.  Easy to make a good grade with decent notes.
Great great lecturer. Extremely helpful and supportive. Open to different suggestions.

He is a new teacher; just got his phd over the summer. He's really nice, but is still figuring out his teaching methods, so he isn't all too clear during lectures. The tests and problems sets aren't hard, and he is really helpful if you go to office hours.
Ghandi's lectures are decent; he's not super engaging, but he's also nothing terrible. Exams were worth 90% total so be careful.

The entire class comes down to your grade on three non-cumulative tests. While they are not terribly hard, you have to go out of your way to study and practice for them, as he rarely gives adequate homework or practice problems. It hurts that his lectures are super boring and hard to follow.

Prof. Ghandi's lectures can be a little dry, but also very helpful as he is incredibly thorough when explaining concepts and going over examples. He also held review sessions before each exam, which I appreciated. Exams are very fair. Really no reason you shouldn't get an A if you put in a reasonable amount of time.
Professor Ghandi is an excellent lecturer, albeit a bit boring at times, who ensures you understand all of the content. The tests are fine so long as you do the practice tests a few times.

Ghandi is a good professor. He's kind, and his lectures are relatively easy to follow. He doesn't use slides, so you need to attend class to take good notes. But good notes and his problem sets are all you need to do well on exams. He holds office hours, but don't think about emailing him, because he won't respond. Overall, though, he's solid.

Professor Ghandi's lectures are sometimes dry but typically relevant and interesting. He goes through examples very clearly. 90% of the class grade consisted of 3 exams and they were graded without error carried forward. The class integrated calculus into microeconomic concepts well. Professor Ghandi is inconsistently accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures but a bit too technical.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: very smart guy, concepts are clear enough if you go to class. slightly all over the place. You will not know your grade until the end end of the semester.

Ghandi was great, made the class super easy but only lecturing on the things he would test you on and made that clear. Also made material for exams clear so you knew what to study. Very accessible outside class and helpful. Very smart man too.

Ghandi is a very understanding and knowledgeable professor. Didn't really need the textbook. The first test was the hardest for me, but once I learned how to study for the course, I was able to really improve my grade. Study the homework to prepare for the exams and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good lectures. The only issue is that it is difficult to pinpoint the same material taught in class to a chapter in the book. Good notes are a must.

Ghandi is a friendly and approachable professor. While his lectures could be more engaging, the material isn't too difficult. Just attend class, take notes, and study the homework - you'll do well. Also, try using unstuck ai for extra study prep.

Ghandi is awesome. You never need to read the textbook because he lectures on everything you need to know for the tests. He is super clear in his lectures and the tests are just variations of homework problems. Ghandi is also incredibly smart and you can tell that he has such an amazing grasp of economics which caries over into his lectures.

Prof. Ghandi is an energetic lecturer with substantial understanding of the course material. You can enjoy either ready-to-go formulas as well as clear, understandable derivations of them. No attendance, homework and quizzes. Be aware of exams though: they take up the major proportion of grades, and they require thorough understandings of concepts.
Sorry for this good man but honestly speaking, he exactly should improve something to make his lecture striking
Good man who will always stand by your side when y need help, but what he taught in class is totally irrelevant to what we had in exams
Absolutely terrible, nothing you can learn from his lecture

Prof Ghandi is very nice but has very little class structure. The lack of a textbook makes understanding the material difficult especially if you have never taken a stats class. Make sure to visit him during office hours for extra support. Very little homework which makes it difficult to gauge how well you are understanding the material.

Prof Ghandi is such a nice guy and pretty helpful in office hours. Outside of that, he is rlly hard to follow in class and your only source of notes is his handwritten white board notes. I had no knowledge of stats and 1500 was hard to follow. He curves at the end of the semester but it is just hard to understand the content from his lectures.

I took Ghandi for 1010 and would leave him at that... 1500 with him was no fun. It was not necessarily hard, just extremely scattered and boring. I took ap stats and that was all I needed to do well. It was simple enough, especially understanding his style from 1010, but would not recommend for any higher level econ class.

For principle macro, Ghandi was fine. Take good notes, make a friend or two in the class, and pay attention enough to know what he is talking about. If you pay attention to his notes and study before the test appropriately, then you will be completely fine. His notes and practice problems are all that matter for the tests. He has a few good jokes.

The content itself isn't hard. Attendance isn't necessary and perhaps even not recommended. As long as you adapt to the way he writes questions and the way he wants the answer, you should be fine. Make sure to also contact the TAs as they are major decision makers to your final grade.

Just show up, take notes, + study the cold tests & homeworks. I had never taken any econ before & would start studying the night before exams, and I did pretty well. You don't need textbooks and he curves. He has gotten better abt returning grades in a timely manner. Ghandi is a nice funny guy willing to help students and wants them to succeed!

Gandhi is a sweet and humorous professor who is very knowledgeable and helpful -- super approachable & friendly & a great professor. Maybe some concepts could be taught better and the lectures could use a little more "fun", but overall I would say he is a good professor. Lots of conceptual understanding & grade is based on a few exams & HW.

Ghandi is a great guy, but if you have never taken econ before, its tough. His lectures are hard to follow, and can only explain things one way. The actual concepts are not hard once you study them and understand the trends. Almost no homework, and the class is almost entirely based on 2 exams and a final.

Ghandi is the goat. The material is so easy, and he's honestly not the best lecturer, but it kind of even out where it still ends up being a pretty light class. Just go to class and actively take notes, do the homework (and learn from the homework), and you'll do just fine. Exams are very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Moderate amount of homework that's generally just for practice. If you go to lecture, you'll get all the information you need for tests. Personally didn't have trouble following his explanations but the presentations can be somewhat dull, the content isn't the most riveting after all. He seems like a great guy but his teaching is just alright.

Ghandi is a nice guy. Agree with the last review; his tests are somewhat intuition-based, so you might struggle regardless of how much you study. Hardest part about the class was the grading structure--the final exam (uncurved) is worth 40%. He rarely posted material online so going to class was a must despite how unorganized lectures were

Ghandi is a very funny guy. He clearly knows a lot about the content matter, and his style of teaching works well for me. I will say it's very intuition based, and either you understand the key concepts or you don't. You don't have to study that much in the class, but if you're struggling, you probably cant just study harder to get the material.
Ghandi is a nice guy but not the best teacher. It is difficult to study for the exams because there is not much practice available to prepare. The final was 40% of the overall class grade.
Biggest mistake was buying the textbook because I didn't use it once. All the info you need is in the lectures, just literally write down everything he puts on the board and you'll be fine.
He's very popular because he's a bit of a meme, not necessarily because he's the best teacher. He's pretty good though.

Ghandi gets a lot of hate for no reason. There's literally  three things you need to do to get an A in his class: (1) Attend lectures (2) Take Notes (3) Study the practice test. As long as you do those three things, literally ANYONE can get an A. Ghandi may not be the best educator, but he makes it quite easy to get an A if you do those 3 things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly love Ghandi. He is the sweetest man ever and a great lecturer. He is organized, consistent, and tells you exactly what to expect on the exams -- down to the exact number of questions that will be on each topic. Homework is graded on completion and he curves all the tests. Super low-stress class that was a helpful intro to econ.
Great guy, and lecturers are very clear. Very manageable class if you put in some work.

Not the most engaging lecturer but great guy. His class is a great time to do other work and half pay attention. Prepares you well for tests and they are weighted heavily. Put in about 5 hours per exam and you'll be good. 15 hours studying a semester for a class is awesome and his class is super chill. Really light intro to econ.

Ghandi is very nice, but he can't teach well. I took macro in hs so I already knew content, but those who didn't generally struggled bc his lectures were unclear. 2 midterms+final are 90% of your grade, but these were basically mirrors of the hw questions he posted. Not too hard but be ready to learn on your own if you're a first time econ student.

Prof. Ghandi is a GOAT. Tells us exactly what to expect for exams (down to how many Q's will be on each topic). Homework is light, lectures are interesting (can be dry but clear), and he's a witty, nice guy. Be sure to review HW/lecture notes for each test since the class is 90% exams. Go to class since he doesn't always use lecture slides.

There are a few in class quizzes and homework to boost your grade. They are based on completion. Ghandi is very kind about curving and helpful in his office hours. The exams are worth a lot, but they are based heavily on homework.
Does anyone know the grading scale?

Ghandi is a great guy, lectures are very boring. This class isn't hard, especially if you have taken an econ class before. His "cold tests" and homeworks are very similar to the tests so you aren't gonna be thrown any curveballs on exams. Study what is presented in the lecture, and you will be just fine. 3 exams make up 90% of ur grade. Rest is HW.

Ghandi is ok. Nothing wrong with him as a person, but he is a bit disorganized. The course itself is not crazy challenging, and the TAs are somewhat helpful. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you don't show up to class you won't get all the info you need. Overall, if you show up to class and study a little bit, you'll be fine.

Ghandi is the best. His lectures are straight forward and he is very helpful at office hours. His tests are pretty much copies of the practice tests he gives as study material. If you go to lecture, keep up with homework, and do the cold tests you will be golden.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Huge lecture classroom. Didn't rlly teach much real info and was rlly scatterbrained. Just crammed the week of each exam and was fine. Needed some notes From class tho
Very nice professor that has issues getting grades in. Did not receive grade for second midterm until day I received grade for final.

I had Ghandi for Econ1010 and I really liked him. However, learning math with no practice problems and no structure to the class except proved to be difficult. He is a nice guy tho. I got a 75% on the first midterm (pre-curve), 80% on second midterm (pre-curve), and a 90% on the final (pre-curve), and somehow ended the class with an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i thought he would be worse, but just consistently attend lectures and review content and you should be fine. dont skip out on lectures or youll miss a bulk of the information that you wont be able to find or learn online

I don't know why there are so many bad reviews. Ghandi's amazing; his lectures and tests are pretty straightforward. As long as you show up to every class, pay attention, and write everything down, there's no problems. Very small workload, but only 2 midterms and the final make up your grade. I never took macro before this class and had no issues.

People have mixed reviews of Ghandi on IntroMacro. I will say that all of these people are mostly on the good or bad side of dealing with his low-question count exams. The exams are around 24 questions, and because they are worth almost entirely of the grade, if you mess up a few questions, the scaling on your grade can drop fast. Just be good ig
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ghandi is the homie. If you go to class you will learn the material but the lectures are a bit boring. His exams are easy and he's super chill

Ghandi is super sweet, he is just extremely unorganized and never on top of things. He takes ages to grade exams and never graded any of our homeworks or other assignments. Lectures can get super boring and confusing. Tests are 90% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ghandi is a really nice guy, and I liked him in macro, but cannot teach a stats class to save his life. Always really big curves on tests and curves your final grade so it is fs doable. Make sure to go to class though because the content is very theoretical a lot of the time. This was my third stats class (AP and psy-pc) and I still struggled a bit
