Seriously, y'all think Ghandi is hard? This is the first time I've taken an economics course and everything is crystal clear. Success in this class is highly dependent on attending every lecture and giving your undivided attention. As long as you can do that, you're golden. Maybe some of these reviewers need to start showing up to class...
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First two midterms were fine, but I always did a bit worse than expected (and doesn't release answers probably bc the class would argue every question they got wrong and he wouldn't be able to explain). Very downhill after 2nd midterm because boy canNOT explain game theory. A cute man but simply horrible at teaching and makes you feel a lil dumb :(
Ghandi the goat
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taking this class was a huge mistake. His lectures were horrible: so unclear and inconsistent. He literally presented using an unsaved word document. He seemed so unprepared. We never even got our 2nd midterm grade until after the semester ended. I'm convinced he made up grades for all the tests. At least there was little work other than studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ghandi was fine. He was nothing special but not terrible. The entire course is graded on 2 midterms and a final which is not ideal, but if you study you can do well. He took obnoxiously long to grade tests and was pretty boring, but the class was bearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 2 Midterms  50% of your grade, Quizzes  10% of your grade, and the Final  40% of your grade. Ghandi rambles during lectures and makes simple concepts too complicated. Takes way too long to grade; I only had one graded assignment for the entire semester until everything was graded. Don't ask Ghandi for help  go to tutoring. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am telling you the way to succeed in this class is to attend class and take detailed notes. If you do that, you will most likely do well. Make sure to get notes from someone if you miss a class because there is no textbook or really feedback in general. Ghandi is a very nice person and curves tests and final grades very generously.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Everyone always gives Ghandi a hard time, but he was honestly not too bad. I was satisfied with his lectures and the provided homework was helpful and very similar to exams. However, he takes forever to post exam scores. He posted 75 percent of the grade all at once. I love Ghandi lowkey.

Ghandi is a nice guy but his class is pretty repetitive and monotonous. Its also frustrating to not know what you got on the midterm that constitutes your final exam. Exams are lowkey hard but if you go to class and take good notes you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Never gave feedback on exams, didn't even show us our results even up to report card was out. Zoom sessions were the only things that helped you clear up confusion. While Ghandi is a nice person, he is not good at teaching. Take notes for everything otherwise this class is terrible for someone who has no previous econ knowledge! Lowest grade I got.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ghandi really isnt that bad. Hes a good person. Frankly, lectures were boring but the BEST way to learn the content - go to ALL of them and TAKE NOTES. Theres basically no textbook use at all. Tbh, youre not prepared well for the problem sets, but just go to a TAs office hours b/c youll have a week to complete them. Not very email responsive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ghandi is a mediocre lecturer but a funny guy. There are only a few homework assignments and three big tests, so make sure to study for them. The class wasnt hard really, but the expectations for the class werent clear at all. If you want a chill class, take Ghandi, but expect to be a bit bored.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Hilarious--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The most unorganized class I've ever taken in my college career. The only class I got B (every other I got A, even the most weed-outed classes),Prof is almost inaccessible outside of lectures - you probably will have to talk with the TAs for questions. He NEVER GRADES, you'll never know your mistakes nor your grade (even after the deadline he has).
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Ghandi is nice and a great lecturer. There're no mandatory textbooks, but the lectures make more sense if you read the related chapters in advance. However, it's a pain that he doesn't grade the exams until the very last moment (so you'll have no idea of your grade until end of semester). Attend class and prep for exams, and you'll be fine.

Our grade was determined based on 2 midterms and a final. He ignored our questions during zoom reviews, he never responded to emails, and did not return our exam 2 grades (the exam that our final was based on) until after the final grades were returned. I'm sure he is a nice guy, but he is the worst teacher I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you show up to lectures, pay attention, take notes, study for the exams, and care about the class, YOU WILL GET AN A.

Dr. Ghandi is an extremely kind teacher! However, the course felt really disorganized. There were two midterms and one final that are worth a total of 90% of your grade, and only grades for the first midterm were ever returned to students. Besides studying for the three major exams, this course has very little work as long as you show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Three test comprise the majority of your grade, and we only received one grade back this whole semester. The professor is incredibly unresponsive, and even the syllabus is unclear. His lectures are hard to follow and not helpful; this is a self taught course. Expect to have no idea where you stand if you take this course. Nice man, awful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ghandi is one of the nicest professors on campus, but his lectures are very boring. He makes things clear in terms of what you will be tested on, but don't expect to get those tests back for a very long time. I would say you need to show up to class for notes or get them from a friend or expect to be lost. Annoying but bearable. No textbook used.

Ghandi is very caring and clearly knows his stuff. His lectures are quite disorganized. Sometimes he overcomplicates very basic concepts. Three exams are worth 90% of your grade. He's clear on what to expect for exams. If you have background knowledge in Econ this class shouldn't be bad, but if not, it can feel difficult at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ghandi is so nice and an awesome guy. People are hard on him for no reason. His tests are simple and are exact replicas of the homework assignments. Before each test, he outlines nearly every question so that we know what to expect.

Lectures are bare minimum fine. If you attend class and listen, you should be fine. The tests are straight from the hw and slides. But I've never had a professor be so bad with communication. He responded to 1 of my 10 emails this entire semester. He doesn't return any grades and expectations are unclear. Grading policies are not even in syllabus.
HORRIBLE! takes forever to grade large tests and this results in you not knowing your grade. If you don't have a background in econ please find a different prof

Professor Ghandi explained the concepts of economics relatively well in my opinion, and used graphs and logic effectively to explain cause and effect. He needs to explain the direction of his class more effectively. For example, explain when tests will be and which textbook to use. This made the class confusing and overwhelming at first.

Ghandi gets a lot of bad rep from people who have never taken an economics course before and I suppose I can understand that. If you've never taken econ before, his explanations are pretty lackluster and you may need outside help. Regardless, the workload is easily manageable and realistically only a couple of concepts are discussed overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ghandi is a pretty solid professor in that his lectures are interesting enough, and he always posts the powerpoints he uses to brightspace. There isn't much homework, and attendance isn't mandatory, but it does help to go to class. The major problem is that he takes forever to grade things, so you never really know your grade in the class.

This man makes no sense. He's a nice guy but never grades anything, lectures are unclear and easy to zone out. Exams are difficult and little guidance is given throughout the course. It's basically self taught.

If you have no econ background, Ghandi's lectures might be hard to follow since he steer off of his powerpoints to draw graphics and give examples. Reasonable amount of HW, gives cold tests before each test, but 2 tests are 50% and final is 40%. He is really caring and offers additional office hours before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ghandi seems like such a nice guy and wants best for us and is super accessible outside of class. Lectures can be VERY monotonous sometimes. Rambles a LOT about irrelevant things that has nothing to do with the class. EXTREMELY unorganized.. an iPad or notebook is a MUST because he draws so much and diverges form the powerpoints. The accent is fine
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I genuinely do not understand how anyone could dislike Ghandi. As long as you go to class and pay attention, he makes everything as easy as he possibly can. He gives cold tests for every exam and everything on the exam is almost word for word what he says in class or what was on the cold test. If you give him your full attention, you will be fine.

He really is one of the sweetest professors I've had but he cannot teach very well. Class is not structured very clearly. Homeworks for completion and each test and the final grade is curved. Test questions often not super similar to how material is presented in class

Ghandi doesn't get enough credit. His classes are tough but he really cares about his students, gives many examples and is accessible outside of class. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He is so willing to help, take advantage of it. The exams are hard but put in the work and you'll survive.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Let's start with the good. He is one of the nicest professors you will ever meet. This class also requires 0 work. However, he takes too long to post assignments and test scores; he postpones every single assignment/test because he moves too slowly. His lectures are boring and confusing. There are almost no practice problems and the tests are hard

If you don't have any background of economic studies, don't take this professor. This is an introductory class, but he still assumes you know everything. Calculus also wasn't a prerequisite for this class, but he assumes you are an expert in calculus!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Ghandi is a bad lecturer and is even worse at giving assessments. He expects everyone to have a deep understanding of topics but only teaches things at the surface level. He is bad at explaining topics and is unorganized. Assessments are extremely difficult and do not allow students to demonstrate knowledge. Doing homework does not help. RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A great professor and a really nice man. Lectures are usually focused on easier content, but the homework delves into the type of problems you need to know for exams. The reviews that he posts are really helpful for exams since most of the questions are similar. Very accessible, but it takes him awhile to post grades. Homework was for completion

A nice guy but should not be teaching a class online. His lectures are relatively pointless because he only goes over review concepts from Econ 1020 and doesn't really teach you what you are tested on. Textbook is somewhat helpful but you can't learn everything from it.

Ghandi really dumbed down this course and I discourage anyone interested in pursuing a graduate degree in econ from taking his non-intro classes. He also has taken zero measures to improve test security, which is probably why the average on the first exam was "unusually high." His teaching is a 3, but his understanding of online instruction is a 1.

Ghandi really is a gem. He has the ability to explain things really well and puts in the effort to help you understand concept rather than the formula. His tests are curved and more or less forward as long as you take notes during class b/c he doesn't use a book. He's really accessible and you can go to his office or set up zoom almost immediately.

Tests are difficult and his lectures can be kind of mind-numbing in person. I really wish he had been more specific as to where in the textbook we were throughout. Honestly, this class could be so much better if he used the textbook at all. I probably would have gotten a C, but I switched to P/F.
Gives good lectures, but no exactly easy tests.

NOPE. If you've never taken econ before, do not take Ghandi's class. He cannot explain concepts for the life of him. He's a nice and smart guy but just can't teach--this class was incredibly boring and you had to teach yourself all of the material.

Lectures are quite boring but material is straight-forward and attendance is not mandatory. Grade is based off of 2 exams and the final so you must learn the material on your own and be ready for them. HW counts for completion and follows the lecture material.

Having not taken stat before, this class is tough. I bombed the first test, but Ghandi really helped me get it together and was willing to work with me consistently in office hours to make sure it didn't happen again. A great guy, cares about his students, and knows the material very, very well. Listen in class, and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: i actually really liked him class is very straightfoward and he gives you practice tests make sure you know how to do them
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gandhi is a very nice guy, but not a very good professor. I took him for Econ 1010, and he was incredibly boring. Econ is already a dry topic, but he made it even dryer. His lectures were hard to understand. His tests are difficult, but they are curved and he curves the class at the end as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors in Vandy! He is always enthusiastic and patient in explaining the concept. Show up to lectures and you will probably get an A. He curves as well!
Interesting lectures. Show up to class and do some sort of studying and you will get at least a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Intro econ classes are probably very hard to teach, but Ghandi is not good at it. Students do not truly understand the concepts after leaving lecture, so most learning is done outside the classroom. Most test questions do not test for an understanding of the material. Those that do (short answer) are worth fewer points. Not an easy A & didn't learn
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ghandi is a really nice guy who really wants to help you understand, & he's happy to answer any question you might have. The info. in the lectures isn't always the most exciting (but he is always upbeat!), but it's very helpful in understanding the big concepts & doing well on tests. Read the book, take good notes, & you'll do great.
He is a very nice guy. His class is very boring and you really have to go to the lectures to succeed. The tests are alright if you study but I wouldn't say its an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ghandi is a good guy and enjoys teaching the class, but his class has little organization. He never references the textbook, and often doesn't define economic terms we have never heard of. The tests are not that bad if you figure out the material, but that's not always easy. Kind of just throws out random concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: his teaching is quite firm

He really wants to be a good professor; he explains things as best he can, and he's very available during office hours. However, he doesn't give enough practice problems, and every question on every exam is 1 point of your final grade, so there's little room for error. Also, this class doesn't follow a book, so you absolutely should go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ghandi is your best choice for ECON 1500, and I'm sure he will be just fine teaching macro/micro next semester (for the class of 2023). For 1500, expect a few homework problem sets that are graded for completion, an easy project, and three exams which are all straightforward and curved. There is a textbook, but it's not necessary. GO TO LECTURES.

Professor Ghandi gives the driest most boring lectures. His exams are similar to the cold test but there will always be one problem that is random (only 4 or 5 questions per exam). His final is SO HARD THOUGH. he will give you a cold test for the final but its not helpful. overall his exams are hard but he does curve the first 2

Ghandi is an amazing professor. Class is lecture heavy and much easier to understand if you've already taken AP Stats, so my lvl of difficulty may be biased. He is very willing to help explain misunderstood topics in class, though. Grade is takehome homework and heavily exam based, and grade is based on bell curve of class rather than traditional %
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ghandi is a really nice guy and is very helpful during office hours. But, his class is entirely him writing on the board so if you do not go to class and do not have friends send you the notes, you will NOT succeed in this class. He is also too smart for his own good so he has trouble explaining concepts to you that are easy for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a really laid back and nice guy, but is not great at explaining concepts. His class is also really tough if you haven't done AP Stats or have a background in it. 85% of your grade comes from tests and the MC has a lot of trick questions. Will let you make up any quizzes you skip but going to class helps since the tests only cover lectures.

Ghandi is a rare prof in the Econ department. The content is really easy, if you took AP Stats before this should be review. But make sure you really brush it up before exams - it is 85% of your grade. Have no normal homework load, extremely lecture heavy. Find other questions to do, his exams are harder than his in-class examples. Lenient grading

Ghandi is an average lecturer. However he is a friendly person, and willing to let people make up quizzes if class is missed. As other people stated though, the class is graded by a few tests, and homework and quizzes are hardly given any weight. Even you have taken stats before, it is still possible to screw up because of the tiny margins.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Ghandi is an incredibly nice person. He helps on quizzes and makes sures we get 100's on homeworks. The problem is homework assignments and quizzes are only worth 10%. There are two midterms worth 25% each and a final that's 35%. The tests are mostly open ended except there is no partial credit. Each test question is worth 1 final point.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Ghandis a good professor, but the margin of error is so small on tests and exams. One question missed on a test is 1 point off your final grade. He also intentionally tries to trick students on questions which is incredibly annoying. There isnt much hw so you have to study your notes outside of class.

Ghandi may be a nice guy and a decent lecturer but his class is not worth taking. It's significantly more difficult than other intermediate classes and tests make up the vast majority of your grade and are pretty tough. There's simply no point in taking a class with him if you can take it with somebody else. its a useless class anyway so get the A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Unless this class is required for your major, I would advise taking another stats class. This class was very difficult for me as there were only two tests and a final that made up 80% of the grade. The tests had a large margin of error, so missing a few questions could hurt your grade alot.

Ghandi is super helpful if you go to office hours with anything you aren't understanding. Always has a smile during lecture and is very understanding about student life. Lectures mainly consist of example problems that illustrate concepts, and if you learn those problems + HW + practice tests, you'll ace the exams. Allows formula sheets on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Intermediate Micro by its nature is not a super interesting course. Prof. Ghandi gives clear lectures and highlights his expectations in HW and cold tests. Most problems on the exams are similar to those on cold tests. Still, he makes you think by adding some "twists". So be sure you understand reasoning behind the material, not the solution itself

Overall a great professor with straightforward lectures and exams. If you show up to lectures it shouldn't be very hard to do well. He offered helpful review sessions to make sure we understood the material.

Professor Ghandi is easily one of the best professors in the economics department. Lectures are easy to follow. Tests consist of 80% of the grade but an A is achievable. Be aware of the final, which would be much harder than the two midterms

Really accessible and clear lectures that relate the concepts to applicable examples and explain the math behind them well. Very nice professor too, always willing to help out students by holding review sessions and making expectations for the tests and assignments very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ghandi gives good lectures and covers the material well-he teaches the class more mathematically than the other professors of 3010, so I'd recommend him especially if you have taken or are taking calculus. He really focuses on finding real world applications of the sometimes dense theory, and is really engaging about the material.
Solid choice for ECON 1500
Dr. Ghandi's lectures are clear, and his expectation is straightforward in the test. Go to the class, take good notes, and study every homework carefully, and then you'll be fine.

He knows pretty clear about the content of the class and he answers students questions very well both during and after class. His homework may require you to use excel so be careful when he explains about the functions of excel during the class. Not so much homework, usually once a week, which takes about an hour.
Excellent professor. Easy to follow. Exams are not straight forward but there is always a curve. You can get an A if your math background is not horrible.
Enthusiastic about teaching some very dry material, always helpful and accessible outside of class. Tests, homework, and quizzes are all pretty easy and focus more on conceptual things.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Pretty easy professor. With little background in statistics he explains the material well from the ground up. The class was at 8am, so it dragged quite a bit, but he did a good job explaining the material and was more than willing to answer questions.

Prof Ghandi is really nice and a great lecturer. Classes can sometimes be boring, but he explains things really well and slowly. He gives quizzes sometimes, but he checks them at the end of class, so everyone gets a 100. There is a final project, fairly easy, and he helps you out a lot. A's are achievable if you put in the work.
Pretty disorganized. Lectures aren't great. Class isn't too bad if you have a strong math background. Probably half of the work involves finding max/min - so basic differentiation.

This class was very hard for me- Sometimes I felt as though I was trying to do anything in my power to improve my grade but I never really quite can. His lectures really drag on especially at 8 am, and the material can be really challenging especially since I have never had previous experience with statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gandhi is the way to go.  Nice, helpful in class and especially during office hours.  Easy homework every 2 weeks; periodic quizzes, everyone gets 100%. Exams are a bit difficult and count pretty heavily.  That being said, most of the exam material comes from homework, practice tests, textbook, etc.  A's aren't easy but they are achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are dull, there are homework assigned every two weeks or so that are graded for credit and a few in class quizzes. 3 midterms that are all middle of the road if you study, but all fair. Ghandi loves stats, but he can sometimes drag on.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hojat is an excellent professor - one of the clearest lecturers I've ever had. Sometimes skips over steps in problems, and is a math whiz, which can be problematic - just ask him to slow down or repeat himself. Creates test questions from real world events (OPEC production, negative interest rates), which is interesting, but can be tough on tests.

Really nice guy that makes up for being a bad teacher by giving easy tests. You get to make a formula sheet for tests, so you don't really have to memorize anything. Lecture is painfully boring, but if you pay attention once every 20 minutes, you won't miss much because he moves very very slowly. Just do the homework and study the hw for the tests.

Prof Ghandi is nice, but his class is boring and the way he lectures can be confusing. The material seems easy as he's teaching, but the tests can be difficult. He curves the grades on tests and gives easy homeworks and quizzes as grade boosters. Overall the class is average.

Good teacher.  Very clear and slow in lectures, he goes over the important concepts a lot and stresses them to the class.  There are only a few homework assignments over the semester and he uses them as a chance to boost your grade.  Tests are pretty average with a curve.
Statistics is tough. He is clear cut on concepts. Exams are hard but he curves them.
If you go to class you will learn everything really well, that said the tests are hard

His teaching methods are pretty good; he lays it all the definitions and theory out there and then does a few clear examples. However, the tests are just a crapshoot. He puts questions on there that he admits he hasn't yet taught. If you've taken stats before you might be fine, but if you only learn what he teaches, a 90 is impressive.

Don't need to go to class but should since lecture notes are helpful. Tests are brutal even if you study. He doesn't go over test material really. Even if you study you will still have trouble with the test if you never have had previous experience in Micro but he's the nicest teacher I have had at Vanderbilt.

Was his first semester teaching at Vanderbilt. Difficult to understand through accent, and the lectures would get very boring, but are clear-cut. Very chill, nice guy. Helpful in office hours, but tests were difficult (avg of B-/B with no curve). Homework is purely helpful, yet difficult, but he goes over problems in class afterward. Read the book.
Some lectures were excellent, some boring. Very helpful. Exams are hard.

Perhaps the most average teacher I've ever had. Lectures are boring, but he teaches the material well enough. Homework is easy and graded for completion; very lenient on deadlines as well. Tests are fairly challenging but really aren't much harder than the textbook or homework problems. Seems like a nice enough guy outside of the classroom too.
His office hours are so helpful. If you have to take Micro, take Ghandi. Would also recommend getting the book, even though it's optional.
Very unclear in class, he does not prepare you well for the tests which are very difficult
does not assign a lot of work but the tests are much harder than the few homework assignments he offers and involve more critical thinking than knowledge of the class

Is somewhat unorganized in his lectures but for the most part teaches the material well. However, if the lectures don't help, the textbook is very easy to understand and helps tremendously on tests. Overall not too bad of a teacher and is fairly easy.

Lectures are boring and attendance is not mandatory, but all of the information you'll need is in the lectures. Textbooks aren't used, and there is very little homework. He is extremely chill teaches the topics well. However, the information won't really stick, so tests may be a little hard. Would definitely take classes with him again though.

Notoriously hard class but he was a chill prof! Lots of homework but very useful prep for exams. Homework weighted heavily so that helped. Exams were hard but he tried to calibrate. Nice guy, very accessible. Puts the work in to make sure concepts are understood. Class will be hard no matter how you slice but would recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is very hard to understand him. He first don't have clear voice and second he confuses when he teach. Avoid him at all cost.
a better option for TA than the professor. He at least gave examples and solve textbook questions and try his best to help students understand.

MATH 1300 is an overall difficult no matter who you take it with. The lectures focused mostly on proofs so doing practice questions outside of class was necessary to pass the class. Quizzes were generally easy and tests were curved by a few points.

1300 was simply not an easy class for me in general. The material seemed unnecessarily complicated sometimes and he will not slow down to make sure that youre understanding the material. Its hard to guess exactly what is going to be on exams, but he does usually tell us what is on the quizzes

I took calc 1 and 2 last year, so I thought I would be fine. I was wrong. Julio puts more time into proofs during class than examples, and he likes to introduce new material on his tests. He also almost never curves. I would avoid taking him as a professor if possible, but it you're stuck in the class--show up to office hours with him and his TA.

1300 is already a hard class, but Julio doesn't make it easier. He leans hard into "weed out" culture. He knows the material, but lectures are very fast and focused far more on covering material than on ensuring that students understand anything. Tests are very difficult and hard to predict/study for from homework and assignments. Good luck...

Julio is very patient in explaining concepts and re-explaining steps to ensure that everyone understands. He has straightforward exams and a sense of humor too. He responds well to the class and will accommodate based on performance on the exams. I think he is amazing and definitely your best bet for any math class. Very helpful in office hours
He cares about his students, but grades very harshly. 1301 sucks in general, but he really doesn't teach well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Let's be honest -- MATH 1301 is a nightmare of a class in general. You're not going to have an easy experience with this class; it's just the way the math department has structured it. That being said, Julio did his best to be understanding of our struggles and did provide extra credit and curve opportunities on exams with poor class averages.

1301 is a hard class, dont listen to people bashing the prof. Its just frustration over poor performance. Julio is a clear lecturer and gives lots of resources to succeed in exams. Exams and hws are graded pretty hard, but theyre graded by the TA, not the professor. Yes, averages were low but some tests were curved generously to compensate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE! WORST CLASS EVER TAKEN. WORST PROFESSOR EVER! DO NOT TAKE! HORRIBLE AT EXPLAINING, HARD GRADER! DOES NOT CURVE. SECOND TEST AVERAGE WAS A 55. WOULDNT U THINK THAT SAYS SOMETHING ABOUT THE WAY HE TEACHES????!! WELL HE DOESNT, HE SUCKS! to be fair, 1301 will always suck, not all of it is his fault but most of it is
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing prof! Highly recommend. I think his tests were easier than the other 1301 professors. He was always accessible outside of class and explained things clearly. 1301 is a beast but Julio will get you through.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took him for Core 1010. He is a really nice professor and class discussions are always interesting and thought-provoking. He genuinely cares about his students and provides encouragement and support.

Genuinely the kindest professor I've met. Flexible, accessible, and will always put student well-being above deadlines. His class is so fun and interesting, you get to do group literary analysis as a class. Readings are short stories and poems, very manageable. Papers are short and graded fairly. Easy final project/presentation, no exams.

LFLG is the best professor ever. While he isn't a hard grader, he gives very good feedback on essays on how to improve. He also just cares, and it shows. Every class started with him checking in on how we were. I will say three essays in Spanish are a bit of writing, but he is available for advice. He is actually like the best professor I have had.

I loved my time with Prof Lopez. He is a very kind grader and gives his students a lot of grace. He knows and loves what he's talking about. Not the best at technology (refused to have a Brightspace) but maybe that will change in future semesters, hopefully. Really caring, and always looking out for his students.

One of the nicest professors I've ever had! Cares a ton about his students/their viewpoints and is obviously passionate about the material he teaches. An interesting course, and if you enjoy smaller classes, one I'd 100% recommend as a literature credit. Discussion-based, and he always made sure we understood the material. Easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Lopez is the sweetest professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He is caring, accessible outside class, and selects a great assortment of literature for this FYWS. Three papers, oral presentation, midterm/finals, and 30% participation grade means it WILL take more time than your average FYWS, but Dr. Lopez is incredible so I definitely recommend!

Prof is the kindest professor I've had here at Vandy, he starts every class asking each individual student how their weekend was or what their plans are for the upcoming weekend and he loves to crack jokes. The class has very short readings and the tests are very easy as long as you've been semi concious in class

One of the best professors I have had at Vandy. I am genuinely shocked he has even one bad rating because of how kind he is. He truly cares about his students and is incredibly smart. The readings are also actually interesting and never long. Grading is clear and always very easy. Tests are also super straight forward and easy as well. 10/10

Professor Lopez Gonzalez is a really kind, caring, knowledgeable, and inspirational professor. I have learned so much in his class, reading the interesting and inspiring books and texts that he provides. Also, he really cares a lot about students, and gives good feedback for homework assignments and papers. Great professor!!

Professor Lopez Gonzalez is a fantastic and kind teacher. He lays out his expectations and is completely fair in grading and during class. He clearly wants his students to succeed and is open to accommodations. You have to read a lot, but the selection of literature is some of the best I have ever read in or out of school. Fantastic seminar.

Honestly? I went into this class not expecting much. To my surprise, I actually enjoyed the mandatory in-class readings and books we delve over in class. I don't take myself as someone who particularly enjoys literature, but I never got bored with this class. You do have to write papers that are bit open-ended, but he gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: im a mess right now, and am quite literally in his class right now. we're online so he likes us to turn on our cameras. i was um.. simply put, having a mental and physical breakdown and so i asked him if i could turn off my camera (i said was in pain). he only responded "please turn on your camera" where is that caring side to the professor? :')
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: LUIS! What a man. I love this professor. He is caring, knows about his subject and wants his students to succeed and love his content too. There is a lot of reading in all his classes, and most people don't do it. So if you do, and participate... you will get an A. He is the sweetest and will care about you all and ask about your lives. Take him

Professor Lopez Gonzalez is amazing. He cares so much about his students and the material he teaches. He gives great feedback on papers and is really committed to his student's improvement. I loved taking him and recommend him to everyone looking to take a Spanish class.
Great professor that cares about his students.

He grades very fairly and gives good feedback on papers. There are two presentations throughout the year, and speaking in class/answering his questions is pretty important. There are also tests that are very easy if you've even glanced at the assigned readings, which are never that long. Highly recommend.

For an intro science course, oceanography is challenging. However, if you attend most lectures (some for extra credit), log into office hours for homework, and take in the information from the presentations, you will be fine. The textbook is not necessary at all, and plus, there are only three midterm exams (no final).
Awesome guy, kept lectures light. Found it to be more difficult than average but still doable. lot of lectures, many people didn't go to class but still did well i thinl.

Such a sweet professor. He is so passionate about what he does and goes off on tangents about his work a lot. He's funny! The content isnt the easiest to understand but the tests are short and specific. There are 3 exams. The worst part was the sporadic homework but the help sessions are helpful! He hosts reviews before exams and gives study guides

Dr. Goodbred is so cute and passionate about oceanography. However, his class is pretty boring and confusing as it is all lecture. Grade is based on weekly quizzes and homework + 3 exams. The hw and quizzes aren't bad, but you kind of need to go to class to do well on the exams. Material is difficult, but easier than many of the other sciences here

Amazing professor. So passionate about the subject & makes lectures easier to pay attention to. He explains things super well and is willing to help you however he can. Attendance is not mandatory but I definitely recommend going because it'll help you on the tests (and he's just a fun guy)!
Very easy science course with interesting content. Good for non-stem majors to get natural science requirements out of the way without taking pre-med weeders.

Amazing prof! But you want to make sure you put in the time to study (use the study guide wisely, so helpful) and I promise you'll get a 90+ (the exams are easy!!!) You would want to show up to class because the lectures are really important (do post slides but I suggest to listen to the lectures). Office hours are also super useful when you need.

Goodbred is actually my favorite professor i've had. He is so sweet and so accommodating toward anything you need at all. He is so informed about eveything he lectures on and always has such a positive attitude. Even though it was pretty easy to skip, I rarely did because I genuinely enjoyed listening to his lectures.

Prof. Goodbred is so knowledgeable about all of the material. Highly recommend taking this class, especially if you need a lecture+lab credit. While attendance isn't mandatory, his lectures are very heavy so I would recommend going as much as possible. His review sessions are so helpful for the tests. My one piece of advice would be to go to those!
Prof. Goodbred is hands down one of the kindest professors at Vandy. He cares a lot about the material and it shows. Take this class he is such a gem.

Professor Goodbred is such a gem! He is sweet, caring, and easygoing. Oceanography is a great class to fulfill the AXLE M&S requirement as it's relatively easy but also engaging. He deserves all the hype!

Professor Goodbred is an amazing teacher. I learned so much about oceanography and the course is very manageable for those people who put in the time. Straightforward and a fair grader, this is the best AXLE class you can take for your LAB requirement! Professor Goodbred is the best!!

I've never done oceanography before this class, and Prof. Goodbred made this topic incredibly engaging. Some quiz questions may sometimes trip you up, but overall an excellent class. I definitely learned a lot, and it's not difficult to do well in this class if you put in the time and effort. Definitely take EES1030 if you need to satisfy AXLE.

Dr. Goodbred is a king through and through. Lectures aren't mandatory, but he brings so much energy to his 8am. He understands a lot of students are there for AXLE so the class is focused on general skills like Excel. Homework was annoying sometimes but overall nbd.

The lectures can feel very dense if you are not very interested in oceanography, but Professor Goodbred is so passionate about oceanography to where it isn't as boring as it could be. His grading criteria is crystal clear and there's absolutely no surprises. He's also very sweet; Please take him for oceanography!

Professor Goodbred is an absolute gem. By far the kindest professor I've ever had, and was incredibly understanding of the difficulties of fall 2020. Interesting material and very easy to do well -- grade is based off weekly open-note quizzes, easy homeworks, and 2 short essays that almost everyone got 100 on. Best choice for AXLE science credit.

I took this class online, so the class format differed from other years. We had weekly quizzes and assignments, but it wasn't overbearing. The only drawback is that the class is an 8am, but professor Goodbred is passionate about oceanography and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Goodbred is so pure and precious. He cares and loves his content, loves his students and wants you to succeed. He is by FAR the best online class I have taken during COVID because he ACTUALLY made adjustments to his course. What an angel. Take his class for SURE. His lectures are accessible, the homework actually helps. A+++ on professor

I love his class! My favorite this semester. Prof. G is so supportive and caring, and his passion about oceanography makes the class an enjoyable journey. You'll fall in love with oceans after taking his class. Very stress-free haha.

This was easily my favorite class this semester. I did lectures asynchronously because 8 AM is impossible for me but they are so worth watching. Prof G is a great professor, so enthusiastic, caring, and his class was very well organized, interesting, and worked great online. Wish we could have gone on the fieldtrips but oh well! Love oceans now!

Prof G is easily the most chill professor at Vanderbilt that I have had so far. We had no exams this semester and 2 relatively short papers, with weekly homework assignments and short quizzes. A lot of material that is covered and going to lecture helps you understand the material. Def an easy A class
Great professor who genuinely cares about the success of his students! His passion about topics shines through and keeps the course interesting.

It's hard to get to at 8am but don't give up! I wasn't expecting to enjoy this class as much as I did! He's super excited about oceanography and knows a lot. Can sometimes be disorganized and tangent-y but you get used to it. PPs posted but you really need to be in class to understand. Don't buy the textbook.

Goodbred is clearly very passionate about what he teaches, so it's a shame that a lot of people take the class just for AXLE or science req (like I did). He uploads all of the slides but you need to be in class to really understand the information. Don't buy the textbook, it's optional. Overall, would recommend taking the class.

Don't take this class unless you really care about oceanography! It's a powerpoint information dump, with no application whatsoever. Brutal at 8am. Professor Goodbred is nice enough but sheeeeeesh the material is dense and dry as it gets.

Goodbred is such a sweet professor who really cares about his students! At times his lectures can be a bit disorganized, but he holds review sessions before every test to clear up any questions. Homeworks help to balance out the overall grade and the tests are pretty straightforward, although you do have to study to do well on them.

Awesome man! truly cares about the subject material and his students. Easy A if you actually show up and pay attention to lectures. Suuupper nice guy. Take this class to fulfill MNS if you're not a stem major.
Goodbred is a good man. Really enjoyed this class as a non EES major.

Dr. Goodbred is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about his subject. However, the lectures are very much him dumping all of this knowledge on students with little interaction. Labs count a huge portion of grade and their grading criteria is very unclear. He is super nice and helpful about science stuff, but his assignments are super confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Goodbred is one of my favorite teachers ever. He is very enthusiastic about class & the material, its seriously infectious. He cares about his students and will work with you extensively about material you don't understand. Accessible outside of class. Very lecture heavy so be prepared but its not hard to pay attention w/ his good looks

Prof Goodbred is the most caring professor I've had so far. He cares so much about his students and wants everyone to do well. His slides don't have a lot of information on them, so its best to go to lecture because he explains everything really well. If you show up to class, go to the review sessions, and study a little bit, its easy to get an A!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR AN EASY A. Tests are hard. I'm not used to having to memorize such large, large, quantities of information. I usually study for about 7 hours for a test and I still get a B. If you're a bio/chem major, this shouldn't be that hard. I'm CS and we don't ever have to memorize a lot of info.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Goodbred really cares about what he is teaching which makes lectures more exciting. However, most students in his class don't really care about science which makes it hard for him to get the students engaged. The first test isn't as easy as you think it will be, so study!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Goodbred is easily the most enthusiastic professor I have ever had. He clearly loves what he teaches and that gives some of the class motivation to show up at 8:00am. There aren't many assignments and the tests are easy. Great way to get MNS AXLE credit.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I was not expecting to enjoy this class as much as I did. His enthusiasm for the subject is infectious! Very engaging yet laid-back teaching style; super approachable. No textbook, so be sure to go to class or get notes from someone -- you'll need them for the open-note exam. Ask questions often!

Great, passionate, kind, genuine teacher. Definitely knows his material. Is so kind and willing to help out during office hours. Never looks down on you for not understanding the material, really tries to help you understand the concepts and not just focus on the grade. Fairly hard exams, but I am speaking as a non-science person. Go to class!!!

Professor Goodbred rules! Like everyone said, do not underestimate the fist test, you should study and go over all the topics he sends out as the study guide. If you do that, you'll be fine. Great guy, super helpful during office hours. GO TO CLASS!

You can easily get an A in this class if you take the first test very seriously.Most people improve over the semester so start well! Print out the notes and annotate them in class well. Please dont both with the text
Don't get me wrong... he's a really nice guy and all. But this class is by no means, easy. Try botany for your lab requirement instead

Don't underestimate this class.  It's not terribly difficult, but it's definitely not easy. DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE THE FIRST TEST.  Professor Goodbred is a really nice guy who cares about his students and is willing to help if you're confused about concepts in lecture.
Great teacher and easy class. Go to lectures and study the night before the test and you will be fine.

He is not helpful in review session, hard to follow. In this intro class he almost knows too much. His tests are not terrible but they DO require that you study. Go to class and take notes it makes the biggest difference. But DO NOT waste your time on the textbook it does not help.

Prof. Goodbred is an extremely nice guy. However, do not under estimate his class.  Test questions can sometimes be very tricky and you may think all the answers are correct. I would suggest going to class even though class is not mandatory. Don't under estimate the first test, I know people who did horrible on the 1st and it was hard to recover.

Dont take this class if you're looking for an easy grade. He loves the topic and knows his stuff but he fails to realize that no one in the class wants to be a EES major. He doesn't drop test grades. Make sure you go to class and read the text. I ended up with a B+ but it was definitely a waste of time.

Professor Goodbred is such a nice guy and extremely helpful outside of class, however, his lectures are not always clear and even he admits that the textbook is pretty useless.  Though it has the reputation of being an easy A, I know many students that were struggling to get above a C

Professor Goodbred is the nicest guy in the world and really seems to care about Oceanography. He is always willing to help if you have questions. Tests can be tricky, so study lecture notes and the text. Take this class w/ the lab to fulfill the AXLE requirement!

I love Professor Goodbred! He is so excited about oceanography that you can't help but care too. It's an easy class if you show up and actually study, but don't underestimate the tests. If you study and listen in class, you'll be fine, though. I would definitely recommend the class and the professor in general!

This is a great professor/class for those looking to fulfill a science requirement. I am not at all interested in science, and I still found the class interesting. He is not a tough grader, and he seems to care more that students learn concepts rather than being grade-focused. This is a great professor/class to take.

Class was great, and he's great. Take it if you just need requirement. Lab is really easy. You never have to go to class. He's so interested and he tries so hard and it is actually kind of interesting. take the class.
Goodbred is a badass.  Class is pretty easy.  Watched a lot of movies.  Goodbred was helpful and realistic about the class being a core req. that kids arent that pumped up about.  A five star guy.
A great professor. Very energetic about Oceanography!  Three exams, one dropped.  A final and two papers.  Great course!
Easy class if you study the powerpoints and read the text.  Pretty good teacher, tries to keep the class interesting.
I heart Professor Goodbred, he is eager to help you and loves his job.  He thinks everyone else is as excited as he is.
He's a great professor who is VERY excited about oceanography.  Class ins't that hard as long as you put the effort in.  And hes a stud!
hottie with a body! beware of the groupie TAs!
Good professor, I like his energy. Lectures are relevant and applicable. Projects are difficult but is graded leniently. There are weekly quizzes that are not too hard.
I really do enjoy his teaching, and have taken multiple classes with him. He is understanding when it comes to extensions. Super easy to talk to and work load is not bad.
Very caring. Will answer your questions in the best way possible.
This course can be taught by Professor Vikash Singh so that Professor Gokhale can rather teach Computer Networks and Distributed Systems.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He was very nice and funny in class. He was more understanding about extenuating circumstances compared to many other professors. Sometimes, he seemed a ensure about specific quesitons about assingments and exams, but I think that is because he was not the one who created them. He drew a lot of diagrams in lecture so going to class is heplful.

Professor went over class time by 15+ minutes every week, while barely covering the content. CS6381 content was great, but was mostly covered in async videos, not in class. Programming assignments had huge scope, few specifications, and the worst-written starter code I've ever seen. He is unorganized and has no sense of time/level-of-effort.

class was made up of easy quizzes, a final project that you choose, and very difficult PAs (that were pretty lightly graded). Andy is a very reasonable and fun guy, and enjoyable to have as a professor. just wish he would preemptively make the PAs easier, rather than cutting them down after the assignment was released because of technical problems
Confusing class and a bit disorganized but Andy is a G. PAs were team-based and it was a bit confusing, but grading was chill. Weekly quizzes which were very reasonable, no tests.

It would be better if PA1, PA2, PA3, PA4 are not all given as a continuous project. I think, for instance, PA3 and PA4 should be given as a new project.

I think the PA assignments should incorporate the use of Python FastAPI.

This class does what I think every CS class should do: teach concepts that are important to understand, but difficult to pick up through projects on your own. The assignments in this class are no joke, but they're graded pretty easily. There's also a quiz every week, but you don't have to do that well on them to still get a good overall grade.

Prof Gokhale had so much to offer and was very caring. The material itself is interesting and very applicable to the 'real world'. It does require a decent amount of work to set things up & get assignments running. Pick a good partner since everything is done in groups of two. You'll learn an incredible amount & you don't have to worry about grades

Cloud Computing is a really poorly set up course, the programming assignments are long and don't teach you anything, and you can waste a lot of time trying to configure VMs. The quizzes aren't too hard, and Gokhale is a really nice prof and easy grader, even if his lectures are dry.

Professor Gokhale is really caring and kind overall, but the lectures are too dry and the assignments are not covered in lectures. Many students submit their assignments and homework half-complete, and it requires LONG time to self-study for the projects. Definitely requires a lot of work and time, but easy to get A because he is a lenient grader.

Very easy class for the first half if you took digital logic before as it is essentially just a digital logic review. Once you get to assembly it gets harder but still isn't too bad. He's a good lecturer and wants you to do well. Everything was graded extremely, extremely leniently though. There also isn't a lot of work given out. Good class

Andy is a good guy and a good teacher. The class is all quizzes (graded normally, but ranging in difficulty from pretty easy to very hard; the hard ones aren't graded too harshly), assignments (graded VERY leniently), and the final, which is basically structured as a longer quiz. Andy has a bit of an accent but he does a good job teaching

Homework is hard, but you got most solution online; Quiz is very hard, but TA graded them extremely leniently; Final is almost like the rehash of all the quiz. In a nutshell, next time you saw his name on the course list do not hesitate to take it.

This was his first time teaching this class. Grades are not very difficult to obtain. However, his teaching standards are not that high. Perhaps, he needed more experience in teaching this particular class.
His course is kinda like a CGPA booster. He is helpful and nice guy. Not so well on explaining part.
Andy is a great guy.  Incredibly nice, but not great at explaining.  He is very understanding and wants you to do well.

Prof. Gokhale's class is not difficult, but he expects hard work. Start early on assignments, go to class, put forth some hard work, get help (as early as possible) if you have trouble and you will do well.

Bi-weekly quizzes, 4-5 programming assignments, 1 presentation, no final. Lectures can be dry but are informative and he clearly knows his stuff. You can still do fine if you don't want to go to class by reading the book. Programming assignments are NOT explained well at all, so you spend hours just figuring out what to do. Otherwise a good class.
I took a different class from Bus 1600, but she is really excellent!

Prof Goldsmith is awesome!! She is hilarious and her lectures are genuinely engaging. I find the other review on here extremely dramatic. Boohoo! You have to attend class! How dare she. But seriously class is fair. There is actual work its not an automatic A but as long as you put in effort, attend class, and take notes during lectures ur fine.

Get one question wrong in the quiz? No problem, just one point get deducted from your final grade! Hey, guess what? You not only need to attend every single class, but also try to answer every question asked and email the professor after every single class! Don't wanna do it? You will get an email telling you how bad you are doing! Just dont takeit

Super interesting lectures, no exams, group and individual cases, presentation/ product pitch at end of semester. you know exactly what you are getting into. she is hilarious and her lectures are super interesting. Would totally take again!

An incredible lecturer, extremely knowledgeable, can go on a tangent, but they are always relevant and interesting. Not many assignments, just a few 2 pagers and one longer paper. While there is lots of reading, Professor Goodman goes over what he thinks is important about them during class. He is also incredibly nice! Definitely take his courses!
The worse teacher I ever had!
I couldn't ask for a better introduction to philosophy than the one I was provided with by Dr. Goodman. Great lectures, interesting papers, and helpful grading.
Theres just one 10-15 page paper at the end of the term and a final on the material. Goes off on tangents during class. Tough grader on the paper. Lots of reading for each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Genius but horrible teacher. Rambles and talks about what he wants instead of helping students understand concepts. Lectures aren't structured in any way and everything is confusing. Attendance was low and class was boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No clarity or structure to his class. If you like being in the dark and having your papers torn apart, then by all means, take his class.   Goodman's lectures were all over the place and self-serving. I've never quite met such a pompous faux intellectual. This is coming from someone who's entire circle of friends graduated from uchicago. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Wow. Only Lenny could make justice boring.  The lectures are impossible to get through, the papers are long and convoluted (at the end of an assignment, I knew less than I did before). The reading is interesting if you're into super esoteric, long-winded explanations of everyday things.

I had to take a writing seminar and ended up in Goodman's "Theories of Justice" and the lecture is just so long and boring and no one pays attention in that class and we all fall asleep. Unless you are extremely passionate about Plato and the Republic, or are a supernaturally awake person, don't take this class, no amount of caffeine can save you.

This guy is the worst. no organization. the lectures have nothing to do with anything. Reading is 100 pages between classes (hard stuff too), and he is a terrible grader. We read (and had to buy!!) 4 books by him. 4 books? way to pad your wallet at the expense of the students. keep away. i am a phil major he is the worst (cept' for wienstien)

I am assuming this page is for Lenn Goodman because he is by far the most frustrating professor I've had at Vandy (this seems to be an overwhelming consensus). His lectures make no sense, have no organization, and he doesn't even have a grading system in place. STAY AWAY. I just wished I knew this was Lenn's page before enrolling...

Miserable professor, miserable lectures, miserable class discussions. His lectures HAVE NO ORGANIZATION whatsoever, not to mention his extreme arrogance. I made an A but only after days of preparing for his essay tests. Term paper: "Does evolution threaten human dignity?" Extremely hard class-not worth taking.

This class was mind-numbingly boring.  I took it for CPLE credit and wish there'd been other options.  Professor Goodman tells you not to ridicule other points of view in your essays and then does the very same thing in every one of his lectures.  There is a lot of reading, and the lectures are extremely tedious.

He is definitely the smartest professor I have ever studied under. He expects a lot, but then, I do not find his demands unreasonable. If you stick with him, I guarantee you that you will be an erudite, well-rounded person. Very much a thumbs up!

Miserable professor, miserable grader, miserable class. It takes so much just to stay awake. He rambles on and on and doesn't answer questions directly, instead, he answers with more questions and incorporates philosophers no one but him has heard of. Apparently he doesn't understand people take his class who aren't philosophers. Steer clear!

I got an A and never read a single book for this class.  The readings are cumbersome and if you get behind at the beginning of the semester you'll never catch up.  The most important thing for the tests is to study your notes and be able to regurgitate what he said.  A brilliant man but somewhat scatterbrained with his lectures.  Take good notes.
By far, he's one of the most intelligent profs out there. He is a tough grader and expects a lot, but if you do the work there's no reason you can't get above a B in his class.
Tough grader, but very smart, very knowledgeable.  Clear in what he wants and friendly outside of class.

Yes, lectures were tedious, but you can gather quite a wealth of info- All it takes is a little time to sit down and think about what you've read, I didn't just regurgitate what the prof said since I rarely attended class! So it's not that hard- I ended up with a B, and I only read 1/3 books!
One of the worst philosophy classes I've taken, I would recommend that you not take this class....there are many other professors in the philosophy department who are MUCH better.

If you dont agree with his views,dont take any debate class from him.  He hated all my papers no matter how many times i went to office hours.  Just to tell you how much he sucks, I had 4 As in my other classes, and a C+ from him.

A very boring and uninspiring class.  A very lecture oriented class where he feeds you the information and expects you to regurgitate back on the test, if you can find a better CPLE class, I would take that instead.
Lenn's a good prof.  I took him for Jewish Philosophy and while I wouldn't call him easy by any stretch, he was very clear and straightforward.
Avoid. Just avoid.

His communication regarding exams is incredibly vague. Since the lecture focus is unclear, preparing for quizzes and tests feels like guesswork. When asked for guidance, he simply suggests "reading the book" to cover the nuances of heat transfer, offering no specific direction on what he considers essential for the actual assessment.

Absolute GPA killer. Zero practice for exams and the homework never relates to the tests. You never know his expectations. He "changed strategies" after the midterm, but it's still a mess. Grading on projects is a black hole—vague feedback and random points off. If you have a choice, AVOID THIS SECTION.

He is the worst professor I've taken at Vanderbilt. He fails to teach the material well, going off on tangents during lectures that rarely related to the subject matter. He waited until the last day of class to finally grade all the homework assignments, which he graded quite harshly with little to no feedback. Avoid him and take another professor!

Dr. Walker was a wonderful teacher and very accommodating. We got very minimal homework and classes were mostly just lectures. The final was a brief paper and presentation which was very manageable considering how busy I was with other finals.

I'm not sure why everyone dislikes professor walker. While it is true that he speaks off topic a lot it's very applicable (most of the time) and are interesting stories - I thoroughly enjoyed almost all of them. Unfortunately, this does take away from teaching. It would be nice if he did a few more in-class questions. Super nice guy!
Spent many of the lectures speaking of topic. Then when it came to actually teaching, he did not appear to understand the material well. Would not recommend.

Spends too much time speaking off topic and is terrible at actually covering the material relevant to the homework. He typically goes over the most basic examples and leaves you floundering through the textbook for everything else (essentially everything he will test you on and give you hw for).
This class (Heat Transfer)is miserable. Walker does a poor job of making it exciting. Go to class and pay attention.
No Comments
Great sense of humor. Wonderful material and reading assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment:
Sanjiv's mentorship inside and outside the classroom was invaluable to me. I was struggling with my career choice. Today I am happy in my chosen path. 

Sanjiv is just one of the nicest most genuine individuals I have met.

It does not mean he will not call you out 😀 and that may make some uncomfortable. It comes from a caring heart.

Thank you.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The material is not difficult and the assignments aren't either, but most of the class is just him and an 85 page ppt. Worse, some of them are back to back zooms. I appreciate finding speakers but it's hard to engage with. Grading requirements are not clear, and he often hid them within the ppt. He's not supportive, even mocking a student's accent.
I had little understanding of the construction process. I come away with deep appreciation. The "Safety Moments" to start each class will stay with me through my professional career.

CE 4150 was an AWESOME class if you're interested in energy/renewables there's nothing better Chill/easy class that is definitely more research/writing based than engineering but the goal is just to learn about how the energy transition could happen which is so cool One of the most interesting classes in ENG, but definitely not an ENG class

CE 4150 Energy Systems Engineering - Not quite a Religious Experience, but enjoyable. Learned a lot about energy systems in the US and around the world with a focus on renewables. More of a liberal arts class than an engineering class. Not that large of a time commitment. Dr. Gokhale grades electives much more leniently than major-required classes.
outstanding professor and very helpful.

Worst professor I had. He is extremely rude, condescending and will make remarks about you in front of the entire class. He is a tough grader, with no clear grading criteria, and will not allow you to retake an in-person quiz at all (even if your computer freezes while taking it). Regarding teaching style, lectures are dull and he reads off slides.

Can one class be a life changing, even life affirming experience? I would have said "no". That is until I had Dr. Gokhale as my instructor for CE4400 class during fall 2016. The class was nothing less than a Religious Experience. I am going to seriously miss not having him again as my teacher next semester.
Lectures are long but amazing. Truly an inspirational professor. Thank you Dr. Gokhale. I will miss you.
Most amazing class. Prepares students for career. Most amazing professor. And YES, funny!

The program is construction management which prepares the student for field life and has nothing related to the field. The student attitude is forced out in this program and the prfessor is treating the program as freshman level courses. The program and the courses are below the vandy reputation.

This is a 1 credit hour class in which I put in more time than two 3 credit hour classes! He expects a lot. He is the most organized professor and his directions are clear. He is preparing the students (seniors in this case) for the Real World. Having real world experiences he is one of the rare professors who stradles both theory and practice.
Absolutely without a doubt, a most amazing, caring, funny, and smart professor at Vanderbilt.
Great professor. One of the best in engineering. Knows everyone in the field. Attendance is not mandatory but quiz in every class...you learn a lot so dont miss a class unless you absolutely must!
Awesome.......great speakers, interesting materials...knowledgeable...he knows all the industry leaders and they know him. If you need a job...go talk to him!
Nice teacher !!

Absoultely outstanding. I took the CE286 class in 2007. No idea what the previous comment is all about. Best class I took in the school of engineering..and I did not even make an "A" in the class.  Keep it up - Dr.G.
Top notch.

Dr. Gokhale is a hard professor, there's no way around this. (He gives a lot of bonus points though.)  But you're going to come away from the class with a deep understanding of the material.  I took an 8am class this past semester to have him again.
Great professor and really nice guy all in one! Very helpful and loves teaching. Take his class if you get a chance!

One of the BEST professors at Vandy!! Once you get over the accent, this man is brilliant and also an excellent teacher. He really wanted us to do well. Gave us many extra-credit opportunities! And he loved teaching and loved the subject, it showed everyday! Very good!!

He makes Statics much easier, and he really likes the subject-- thats why he teaches it so well.  He gives tons of bonus point/extra credit opportunities, but many of his homeworks are down right hard.

Don't let his accent fool you, Dr. Gokhale is one of the best in the department.  He'll go out of his way to help you, and his lectures are both informative and useful.  Additionally, if you aren't doing so well in the course, he makes it easy to improve.
Way to go Dr. G, you are the MAN!
Awesome.
Tough tests..But Sanjiv still rules. I love this class.
Great Universities have great professors - like Dr. Gokhale. Keep up the good work.
He's one of the best professors in the Civil Engineering department, no doubt about it.  Concise, engaging, and never forgets that he's training professionals.

seriously one of the worst teachers imaginable. I hate this man, with a passion. And I was not alone. Combined with the rest of my class, efforts to remove this man sent him crying home. (or so we hear from the new class :) ) glorious.
THE BEST!!!!  I love Prof. Gokhale.
No Comments
very nice and understanding...not a gimme class but he makes the class easy enough to understand everything.  i'd take the class over again if they would have let me.

To me, the course was a little difficult, but Prof. did a good job teaching what we needed to know and why things mattered. I found the programming to be a little distracting from the understanding I wanted to gain from a math perspective, though the need to program through some of the concepts is at times needed.

Alright teacher, kind of unprepared for class. He has lecture notes but they don't seem well rehearsed, half the time we stall in class bcu he is figuring things out on the fly. Content is pretty easy though , but that makes tests weird because it's hard to know what he is testing. None of the lectures are posted anywhere either.
His handwriting was kind of hard to read and sometimes the lectures were confusing but hes very accessible outside of class.
Lectures are unorganized and tests are hard and time is always the problem. I would avoid taking him mainly because he sets really long exams and doesn't lecture well at all.

Griffin is a really nice and caring professor. Multi has a lot of confusing/hard to conceptualize topics and while griffin explained most topics well, I sometimes struggled to understand some of his lectures. Also the Psets and web works are difficult but the tests with griffin aren't terrible compared to what I've heard from other professors.

Lectures were boring and mildly unclear but could be worse. Don't know how bad the lectures were versus just the difficulty of multivariable calc. Asking him questions was unhelpful for the same reasons. Very caring and nice person though and he always tries to be helpful, and the exams were very fair.

Professor Griffin's lectures can be hard to understand at times since he likes to write proofs for everything and they can be hard to understand. The homework really clears up everything though. The tests are fair but time is always an issue. He's really caring and is always willing to help if you reach out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: professor is a nice person, but the course is terrible, the homework and resource are same for all 2300 student, but the test is different. The test is so hard and the time is just 50 minutes. You need learn many things by yourself.

Great person, alright professor, HORRIBLE tests (time wise). The exams are extremely long and I could never finish them in time for all my exams. You could know the material very well but you could get horrible scores on the exams because of time constraints. The questions are fair though. Lectures are unorganized and it was a lot of self learning.

Griffin is a kind and caring professor who truly wants students to succeed. One of the nicest professors I've ever taken at Vandy. His lectures are a little disorganized, but he was passionate about the material and gave us plenty of examples and opportunities to learn.
Lectures were all over the place and most of the material had to be self-taught. Terrible class and the grading on exams and assignments were ridiculously inconsistent.
Awesome professor. Really cares about his students and clearly enjoys teaching.

A little scattered but clearly cares about his students' success more than many other profs I've had. Available outside of class and generally a very kind person. Homework was reasonably short and tests felt fair; he also makes opportunities to earn back points if the whole class does badly on a particular section of an exam. Would take again.

A bit unorganized and all over the place, but he cares a lot about students and responds well to feedback. Not the best lecturer I've had, but is available and will help you if you ask. Also is a native English speaker, which is a first at my time at Vandy math and does help.

Prof. Griffin is the best math professor I've had at Vanderbilt. Makes linear very achievable. Goes over HW questions at beginning of class, assigns a mostly reasonable amount of HW, doesn't create tests with the intention of tripping students up. Really cares about student success, which is unusual for Vandy math...

I think it was his first year teaching this semester but he seemed a little all over the place and his lectures were a bit confusing and unorganized sometimes. But if you email or go to his office hours he's super helpful and does his best to explain and answer your questions. All exams were take home which made cryptography much more approachable.
