extremely nice professor!! he has a way of making students feel heard and respected. his lectures and group assignments are well designed, and he's overall very knowledgeable about PM with industry experience

Prof. McClain is a great professor of systems engineering. He is very knowledgeable and has lots of industry experience and clearly understands the material. The class consisted of 3 exams, homework assignments (all group work), pop quizzes, and 2 presentations. Overall it's a decent amount of work but not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor McClain is obviously a professional in the field and has countless real world examples to complement the material he teaches in class. His lectures are extremely engaging, and he explains everything in applicable ways. The class is project-based and groups rotate often. Highly recommend him as a professor.

This is a very easy class -- do exactly what the homework says (it's weekly writing, but it's not hard), and you'll do well. This isn't the class for you if you're a real startup founder, but if you're just looking for exposure to the world of entrepreneurship, it's probably a fine intro. No programming or technical work (for non-tech founders).

Prof. McClain is a great teacher who has a ton of knowledge in the area of project management. Also, he is very nice and super helpful during office hours. This class consists of weekly group assignments, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams. Unlike other engineering management classes, this class requires studying before exams and preparing for the quizzes

McClain was a great professor. Took digital his 1st semester at Vandy. Found his lectures to be very helpful with many relevant examples of problems to solve. This class is tough & covers a ton of content. He holds office hours everyday M-Th and is very responsive by email. He's a really nice guy who cares about students. Highly recommend for EECE.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: SO many unnecessary assignments that are never graded. Didn't upload syllabus until 3 weeks into semester. Said the only assignments we would have is four essays, but the syllabus shows more than four and a presentation. She requires 500-750 reading journals for every reading or video and they are so unhelpful. So many stupid in class assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Graves is a really caring and helpful professor. Unfortunately for personal reasons she wasn't in class too much which created a lot of confusion with both attendance and assignments not being graded until the last day grades were due. If I was given the opportunity I would take her class again, she's very engaging!
Great professor in Vanderbilt

She is a very understanding and caring professor! She understands that everyone have a rough life to balance and will give you an extension if you asked. Overall, I am very grateful to have taken her.

Overall, Graves is a very nice, approachable person who loves to help students. The class isn't very difficult as she recognizes that it's a required class and isn't particularly interesting. Grading is very lenient and assignments are quite simple. I didn't learn much but still enjoyed the class. Take Graves if possible, you won't regret it.
I feel like I didnt learn a lot in this class. While Graves is an incredible person and one of the most understanding teachers I had at Vanderbilt, I felt like she never liked being in class.

Professor Graves was not able to have class a lot this semester, and it created a lot of ambiguity around deadlines. The syllabus was always changing and it was very stressful to be a student in the class. That being said, the assignments were graded leniently and she made the content interesting with movies and tv added to doable readings.

Prof is sweet & personable! She picked interesting & fun texts. We even got to watch some in class. My review of her is limited bc she had a difficult semester so we did not have class a ton, thus class was altered quite a bit. But, she is a great person and caring. Her class is centered around learning and I liked the structure. I would recommend!
cheat sheet allowed for exams, pretty easy to get A even if you dont pay attention

Professor Gupta is the kindest professor I have come across at this school. She is incredibly caring about her students and the class matter is somewhat entertaining for a required HOD class. Had friends in other 2100 class and I can confirm that Gupta is definitely the best professor for the course.

One of the tougher HOD courses (50% of grade is 2 term tests) but passionate about material. Outside of the material, Dr. Gupta is one of the most caring and thoughtful people not just professors I've met. Highly recommend everyone to take her section for 2100 or HOD elective.

Professor Gupta is the GOAT! Best professor I've ever had in college. She is so caring about her students, so passionate about her work, and she makes class enjoyable. She's not just a great professor, but a great person -- if I am anything like Professor Gupta in the future, I will know that I am successful.

GUPTA IS GENUINELY IN THE GOAT CONVERSATION. I have had this wonderful professor for 2 straight years and she has taught so much valuable info (2100 for orgs, health/politics for higher level). Please take her class.

I had Professor Gupta for Capstone HOD 4950-53 but could only select HOD 2100 for this idk why so just know that. She was incredibly kind and attentive to all of our different projects across our sites, you can really feel she cares about each of her students. Tons of fun in-class exercises and brought us snacks, such a joy to have her as a teacher
So kind and caring of her students. Lectures can get a little boring but she does her best to keep the class fun and engaging. Amazing professor and human, and a great option for 2100!

The kindest and most compassionate professor; understanding of student's circumstances; two free absences; get to choose one assignment to submit a week late; two exams; one group project; one 5-page final paper. Class time was interactive and fun; she provided a safe environment! My favorite professor I have had yet! What a queen.
May her kind soul rest in peace. She will be remembered as the sweetest, most attentive, talented, and inspiring professor.
rip guo laoshi she was the sweetest prof ever i am taking chinese in her honor she was genuinely one of the nicest teachers i ever had

Guo Laoshi is the cutest, sweetest, most caring professor I've had at Vandy. She was super supportive and helpful, and I never felt embarrassed when I answered questions incorrectly. Chin 1101 requires a lot of studying outside of class, but it's not difficult to do well. TAKE HER! It's the most fun class and you'll learn so much!
very nice and awesome teacher. u can tell she cares a lot and is very friendly. nothing much else too say but take her classes!

Guo LaoShi is really great. My class with her was pretty small so she got to know all of her students. She joked with us and asked about our families, hobbies, etc. and related the course content to our lives. I would highly recommend taking her section.

Guo laoshi is the SWEETEST ever. Class was completely online but she did really good at keeping everyone engaged. She genuinely cares and is so sweet. Pretty easy A if you read the textbook, but the tests can be hard (they aren't worth too much compared to the whole grading scheme though)

I had Guo Laoshi my first semester at Vanderbilt for Chinese 2201. She is so funny and you can tell she has a passion for teaching chinese. I only had her for the lecture portion of the class, not the drill, but she was very excited to help us advance our chinese. She was also accommodating while online, which is great. Tests can be tricky though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers in the Vanderbilt Chinese department. As long as you show up and put in the work, you'll learn a ton of Chinese and get an A.

I loved these past two semesters with Guo laoshi. She actually succeeds at getting us to use tones properly and enunciate well--her lectures are quite clear and interesting, too. She's a hilarious professor and is evidently an expert in all things related to China. My Chinese has improved sizably with her help (but get ready for a lot of homework).

(Only had her for drill class) Guo Laoshi is very cute and bubbly. She works really hard to encourage all of her students with fun and relatable topics. I'm not a morning person, yet her lectures actually kept me awake because she was that engaging and funny. HW and dictations can get really heavy, but that's really a norm.
Clear and concise, a good professor. Personally was not a huge fan as a person, but she teaches well. I only had her for the grammar class, not drill.
Very funny and sweet, really makes an effort to engage with students while teaching. Definitely keeps everyone engaged and active with the material, even in a 25 person class.

Guo laoshi is an absolute sweetheart. As difficult as Mandarin is to learn, she works really hard to ensure her students succeed and will make sure in office hours they understand concepts. Homework can be heavy at times, but this is true and equal across the department's policies. She is incredibly funny and will get to know you as a person.
Makes class interesting and introduces topics that makes Chinese easy to learn. Assignments get boring but class with her is great.

Undisputed best teacher I have ever had and will ever have. He doesn't go too fast or too slow. Lectures are engaging. He breaks down difficult concepts into followable derivations. He avoids math beyond calc II and guides conceptually. You have the entire semester to turn in homework for full points. Exams are all take home. Hard to reach though.

As long as you're trying in this class, you should end up with an A. Professor Gurrola tries his best to make advanced concepts accessible to everyone and cares more about your learning than your grade. You can resubmit homework for full credit, and exams were take-home. 

Great lecturer and amazing in office hours, hard to reach by email though.
Awesome professor, hard to reach but the class is a free 100.
Love this big guy even though the content in class is hard to understand

Loved Dr. Gurrola so much. He is very kind, super understanding, lets you redo assignments as many times as you need, and throws food parties! It's rare that a STEM teacher is this caring. Only critique is that he doesn't respond to emails promptly. But other than that, Gurrola is a gem!

This class is hard content-wise but extremely easy to get an A. You can redo all the homework and he was very helpful if you asked for help. Favorite physics professor I've had as a physics major. He can be tough to reach sometimes outside of class. Would recommend to anyone that enjoys physics but doesn't want their GPA to plummet.

The material in the class is hard, but he always gives hints and helps with the HW (just start early and ask him your questions at the end of class). You can collaborate in all exams and assignments, and resubmit HW.  This all makes it really easy to get an A as long as you work hard enough for it.

His lectures are hard to follow since he derives everything quite quickly. However, not understanding the material at all would not prevent you from getting an A since all the homework are resubmittable and tests are take home. So although I got an A, I didn't take away much from the class.

Gives clear lectures and answers questions very readily but often goes on long tangents and detailed derivations which can be done much quicker; the class moves at a slower pace than I would like. He's genuinely very caring and if you put in the effort, you're pretty much getting an A: graded homeworks are resubmittable and tests aren't too bad.

Really easy classes, homeworks are "infinitely resubmit-able," and the exams are take home & collaborative. He's pretty decent at teaching special relativity and quantum mechanics but class would drag almost every day; he goes on long tangents and derives everything which can take a while. Felt like we were behind and didn't finish the content.

Really great at teaching the equations of quantum mechanics and the theory behind it. He encourages creative thinking. He encourages collaboration on homework and tests. Homework can be resubmitted so easy A if you work for it. Highly recommend this class to anyone who is eligible to take it as you will learn a lot and it will boost your GPA.

Professor Gurrola gives out notes for the lectures and is always super supportive and caring for his students. You can resubmit the homework and all the midterm+final are take home - an easy A if you do the work. I really enjoyed this class and would recommend taking it.
Hard work but not hard to do well since you can resubmit homework

Dr. Gurrola is a really amazing lecturer. He hands out notes for each class that are really detailed and accessible, and then explains them in class as he fields questions. All the homework is open for resubmission and he's really accessible - it's an easy A. If you study with friends and go to office hours it'll be the easiest class you take.

Professor Gurrola is a really nice guy who is very well versed in physics and does a pretty good job in explaining concepts. In addition, he is very engaged in helping students outside of class. His tests were all take home, including the final. Very manageable to get an A. However, I didn't really learn much due to very few hw and practice given.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Any assignment you hand in you will receive a 100. However, Dr. Gurrola is incredibly disorganized. He allows you to resubmit homeworks but doesn't even give them back on time. In office hours, he didn't even know which ones I had handed in and then blamed me. He doesn't accept responsibility or teach well. If you want to learn, go elsewhere.

Many students think he is great. Yes, he is a good person and encourages group work in EXAMS. However, he officially and unofficially canceled more than 10 classes and does not know how to teach. I am serious about Physics and Quantum Mechanics so I didn't learn so much from this class.

Amazing Professor. Greatest physics professor I have had, and ever will have, at Vanderbilt. He genuinely cares for his students and ensures every student is taken care of. He motivates students to perform there best without the stress and pressure that goes along with it. Truly a top class individual and professor.

Fantastic professor if you want to focus on learning the material rather than arbitrary testing standards. Homeworks are the major portion of the grade, and you can repeat them to fix what you got wrong. Super accessible, great lectures, and an all around awesome class. If you get a chance, take this class with gurrola.

Smart guy who loves this subject. Clear slides that have all the info you need. Review sessions on the night before the exam are helpful - he'll tell you to focus on certain concepts. Exams are difficult, usually applying the concepts onto hypothetical experiments, but they're fair and good partial credit. The problem is Zwiebel's second half...

love my boy graham cracker. exams are straightforward and exactly like his practice/previous exams, questions never try to trick you. lectures are a bit dull, but its always clear what material you need to learn. he's seriously the nicest guy one-on-one. definitely take him for intro bio/cell bio.

Insanely smart & knowledgeable prof. Amazing lectures that cover a lot of material. Tons of memorization, but if you record the lectures & re-listen before exams you should do just fine. MCQs are straightforward and don't try to trick you. Make sure to study every detail for his free responses. Great prof.
Great guy, tests were extremely difficult and is your full grade. LA sessions aren't mandatory but can be helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Graham is very good, but you have to know what you're getting into before his class. Don't underestimate it or prioritize other classes, you need to give this class a lot of time and focus to succeed. Use the notes in his presentation slides. They are very, very helpful and he frequently draws exam questions from them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Graham is knowledgeable and a great lecturer. The class is challenging if you've never taken chem or bio before. However, it's completely possible to do well (no matter your background) as long as you attend all the review sessions you can and study Graham's lecture slides and notes. Try not to put off studying until the last minute.

Dr. Graham is the best!! He is incredibly knowledgeable and funny during lecture. He pulls his exam questions from the speaker notes in his presentations so no need to read the textbook. The class is a high volume of material, which makes it challenging, but if you memorize the speaker notes in his presentations, you will do well in the course.

If you know every single thing on the slides including the speaker notes you will get a good grade. Because he had these slides and notes I never attended lectures. The quizzes also boost your grades and you can drop 3 of them. Very smart man. It's a lot of notes to memorize so studying took a decent amount of my time.

I learned a LOT from his lectures, and he is one of the best professors I've ever had. His slides are filled with plenty of notes, which will be the study guides for the entire semester. That being said, his exams are extremely difficult, especially his long answer questions required critical approaches of the entire materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Dr. Graham's class is rigorous and challenging, he is likely one of the best lecturers I have ever had. He is passionate, answers questions in a clear and coherent manner, and his class material is well-thought-out. He is a super solid option as a professor. I would take his section of the class again in a heart beat.

Dr. Graham's half-semester is definitely the best section of Bio 1510. His lecture slides are highly detailed with great notes that have all of the information for the exams. Exams are difficult, but his posted slides prepare you well. Don't use the textbook though, they don't follow it.

I LOVE DR.GRAHAM! You can tell that he knows what he is talking about from lecture to lecture and the quality of his slides reflect this. While it is memorization-heavy, Graham provides clear instructions and helpful office hours to answer any questions you have. Honestly my favorite Vandy professor!! Live, Laugh, LOVE Graham!!

Just the GOAT doing GOAT things. Dr. Graham is maybe the best prof at Vandy. It's so clear that whenever he steps into a room, he is the smartest one there. Super great lectures and powerpoints. Tells you exactly what you do and no not need to know. Makes you think a bit on tests so that you pull together all the info. Can't recommend enough!

Professor Graham teaches everything that he expects you to know, posts his COVID lectures and optional quizzes for each module, and holds review sessions every week to answer questions. He is a wonderful lecturer and always uses real-world examples to help solidify the concepts he's teaching. Skip the textbook readings! Highly recommend.

This class consists of lectures and tests and nothing else. Essentially if you can't memorize everything the professor says during a lecture you will not do well on the exams. There is no homework or any sort of practice for this course. Either memorize everything and do well or memorize nothing and fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite prof at Vandy! Absolutely loved the guy and his sheer level of intelligence. He goes out of his way each week to hold a help session (highly recommend going). Ya, his exams are hard but he gives you absolutely everything you need to do well. Put your time in (a lot of it) and you will be fine. Great Great Great prof.

Professor Graham is the first half of the Graham, Patton Duo and definitely the worser half. His tests are very detail oriented with small facts from his lecture instead of general concepts. To get a good grade on exams you really need to write down every single thing that Graham says in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's smart but he makes things so complicated and hard to understand in class. You will have to do a lot of independent studying to get a good grade in this class. Don't slack off , the daily quizzes can be a good help to your grade. Your lowest exam grade will be dropped, but don't depend on it too much. Just prepare to take a lot of notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes a really nice guy that is super knowledgeable in Biology. His lectures are always clear to understand. However, his exams always have some unexpected questions that require students to extend beyond what they already know; but its a good challenge. Overall, great Professor!

Dr. Graham is the best! Such a great prof that really cares about his students. It's a tough class but I can honestly say he gave us all the help we needed. Can not recommend him more. I truly respected Dr. Graham and found his class to be very informative! Definitely take him if you can!!

Graham is clearly a very intelligent and passionate teacher; however, the flipped format of his class made going to lectures feel redundant. I never skipped class and studied for all of his exams, but still felt wildly unprepared. Tests are extremely difficult and focus on obscure material that seems otherwise unimportant.

Graham is a good and knowledgeable teacher - he knows what he's talking about and is able to explain clearly. But get ready to memorize every. single. little. detail of his slides because he WILL ask the most random and specific questions on tests. Incredibly difficult to succeed on his exams and one of the hardest classes I've taken here.

Graham is horrible. Worst Professor Ive had at Vanderbilt. Test questions are super specific and mostly just random science facts that arent applicable to a bigger picture. He assumes you already have good chem and ochem knowledge This should not be an intro level class. Patton saves the day hes great and actually cares about students
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Graham is a pretty good choice for intro Biology. He explains everything very clearly although it can sometimes be a little boring. As long as you memorize everything on the slides and in the slide notes the exams are relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: -Does not care about the students. -Very full of himself. -Exams are very heavy on details. -Takes points off if the answer is correct but lacks something from the key.

Dr. Graham was a great teacher and so helpful! Despite the online-format because of COVID-19, his lectures were still very thorough. Most of the info covered on the tests were pulled from his lectures and Powerpoint slides. A lot of studying needed for a good grade, but tests were not *terrible*. Would definitely recommend a course w/ Dr. Graham!

Graham/Patton is probably the best choice for Biology at Vanderbilt, but honestly the nature of the online tests makes it so you could probably not study and still get above an 80%. Seeing as how the class is graded on a curve, this makes it pretty hard to get a A. With that being said, reasonable work load and a good class overall.
Good lecturer, genuinely a nice guy. Tests are a little specific, but straight from the powerpoints.

I really enjoyed Dr. Graham's section. He provided most of the notes needed on his slides in full detail with small amounts of textbook reading needed to succeed in his class. His exams were fair and the practice exams prepared me well. He is very responsible to emails.

Prof Graham was a great professor, definitely one of the best I've had in the Bio department. He teaches the first half of cell bio, and he has very clear, focused lectures. His exams are fair, and he prepares you well. Definitely would recommend taking him.

Graham's section has a TON of material, but the tests are fairly straightforward if (it's a big if) you can actually remember everything. Patton's section had less material but the tests were more confusing. Take Graham/Patton for gen bio 1, but don't underestimate it. Takes a lot of studying to do well.

Fantastic professor! Clear expectations for students, excellent lectures that stimulate your interest in biology. While Intro Bio at Vanderbilt is hard regardless, Dr. Graham's section is definitely the best option.

Graham is a great professor! I highly recommend Graham/Patton over the other bio professors. I hesitated waiting to take bio for a year because I thought I would be behind, but I'm so glad with my choice! Graham has literally everything you need in his slides. Textbook use is options (unless it mentions it in the slides, then you MUST read it)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The material is challenging and extensive, but Dr. Graham does a good job explaining things. Hosts weekly review sessions, and tests will not have any tricks if you've read through the class slides and lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Everything you need to know for the tests is included in his powerpoints and the notes he gives you with them-- everything. You need to know EVERY slide and all notes like the back of your hand in order to do well on the test. Not all memorization like some reviews say... You do need to understand the material.

He is very friendly and seems like he wants his students to do well. The difficulty of his class is not due to him, but just due to the difficulty of the content in general - it is really dense and there is a lot to memorize. As a professor, he is always willing to help and explains concepts clearly. I would recommend him for intro to bio

Graham is the best bet for Intro Bio. His tests are super easy if you memorize the slides. They're very detailed, but if you put in the time to memorize his detailed notes (he takes the notes for you at the bottom of his slides), you will definitely get an A. He was very helpful for explaining concepts at office hours and review sessions. Take him!

Dr. Graham is the most amazing professor I have had so far at Vanderbilt. He's extremely clear and organized, and is very helpful and nice during help sessions. His tests are hard, but you'll definitely learn a lot from his lectures. Highly recommend!

Biology is horrifically hard at Vanderbilt, but Graham's your best chance of getting through it. He's relatively clear, and all you really need to do is memorize every single detail of his slides. Although he says to read the book, it's not mandatory except for when he tells you specific pages. Hard but doable.

Graham is a really, really great professor. Explains things so clearly I could cry. Puts a lot of care into his powerpoints, is very organized and strategic during lectures, and is always willing to help students. That said his tests are hard but I'd take his section again in a heartbeat.

I made the mistake of studying exclusively out of the book for the first test. Got a D. For the second test, I skimmed the book, read the sections he specifically told us to read in class, but mainly studied out of the powerpoints/lecture notes. Lots of detail but it focused my studying. Did exponentially better.

All notes are in power points so you could skip if you wanted to but lectures really help and are very clear.  Tests are incredibly challenging.  Read the book, study the notes, and GO TO REVIEW SESSIONS! The only reason I passed the second test is because I attended every one (after failing the first). Overall a great guy with impossible tests.

Graham was a great professor. However, the class is very dense. I've never had to learn so much information in my life. None of it is difficult, there is just SO MUCH OF IT. Unless you are a savant, which may be the case, you need to start studying sooner than the day before and you'll be fine.

His tests are all memorization but only test on 10% of the material. Memorize EVERYTHING on his powerpoints. His voice is monotone and his lectures dry and boring, but if you attend and pay attention you will understand the material much better.

A really, really nice guy if you go to talk to him. Tests are all memorization; literally. Memorize EVERY single detail and you'll do well. Stay on top of your work and don't wait till the last minute. He's really helpful both in office hours and in help sessions.

Straight up memorization, to a ridiculous degree. Possible to get an A if you put in the work. Very helpful in office hours and help sessions, so make sure you go. Very little stress on critical thinking, whether for better or for worse.

He's a good teacher with pretty easy tests if you've read over the powerpoints many times. Goes over a ton of information so space out studying instead of cramming for too much the night before. I would recommend this section for Bio.

This was definitely a hard class.  Graham's tests are almost all memorization and he always seemed to ask the most difficult detailed questions.  Not studying enough in advance will result in very very low test grades.

Professor Graham was a great teacher.  Bio is a lot of memorization, but he is very clear on what he wants you to know for his exams.  Just memorize his notes in the slideshows and be sure you're able to discuss main processes in detail on his tests and you shoudl be fine.  PREPARE IN ADVANCE!  Don't wait till the last minute and you'll be golden.

AHHHH his class killed my gpa. his HALF of the semester killed my gpa... This class is hard. No joke. Make sure you look over your tests and check with the answer key. Almost everyone regrades their exams. I made the stupid mistake of never submitting for regrades. Seriously, bio in general is just hard. Mad studying is required to succeed.
Very difficult. Memorize EVERYTHING. It takes a couple of days to study for this, make sure you give yourself enough time.

Very clear about what you need to memorize (A LOT) and what will be on the test. Study far in advance because there is a lot of detailed material on his tests. But he gets higher averages than the other sections, so you'll feel pretty prepared.
This professor was HARD HARD HARD. But Graham and Patton are the best out of the other sections so take them if you want the best grade possible.
First time teaching 110a. Not bad, one hard exam and one easy exam. Just memorize everything.
Go through the mounds of notes he puts on his powerpoint slides and memorize. He's clear about what you are responsible for on the tests (structures, etc.)
He is a very clear teacher. The best way to study for his class is to look at the slides and his notes on the powerpoint slides. However, he does pronounce fructose incorrectly.

This class was really great, it was really interesting to learn biology in a way other than straight-up lecture. The last few weeks of the semester he had us read a series of papers from the Brown and Goldstein lab, and it was really cool to read the progression of someone's work like that, because that's not how papers are normally taught. Great.

Prof. Graham was very helpful in answering questions... he's obviously very intelligent, and gave very concise, practical lectures on molecular biology. Unfortunately the class was early in the morning, so I only made it to about half the lectures - but the ones I did attend were interesting as well as educational. I'd say this class is an easy B.

professor graham was very unhelpful and cooperative. his tests were not hard which is a bad thing because he did not challenge the class, which is shown by the very high averages. I submitted a test in for regrade and he has never returned it nor contacted me about it. Not very clear on his lectures

Excellent professor. He explains everything very clearly, and it's apparent by what he emphasizes what it is you will be required to write an essay about. Tests, while specific, are very straightforward. He won't try to write trick questions. Great experience.
Very nice and helpful guy. Easy tests. Very helpful outside class too.

I liked his section. They were power point based and focused on some interesting topics and experimental techniques. He is a very nice man and always eager to help you out. The exams weren't too bad, either. But the class usually does well, so do better.

This was by far the hardest course I have taken at Vanderbilt, but the most rewarding. Guil and Morgan truly care about the subject and are very accessible in and out of class. The grading is harsh, but hw/labs can be redone as many times as you want. Also, the subject matter was awesome! I looked forward to every lecture. 10/10 would take again

GUIL THE GOAT 🐐 this class is really hard but also so awesome. Guil and Morgan really want you to succeed- they put a ton of time into helping out students. The class is designed to be very difficult but very attainable to pass. Strongly recommend taking gen chem first, but it's not the end of the world if you don't.

Guil is a super nice guy and very smart, but not a good professor. He lectures as though we are PHD students, and though it is nice he expects the best, I did not understand much of anything. I learned more from the TA in lab. Redo hw and lab as many times as you can to get a better grade. Passable, but not enjoyable in the slightest.

In addition to being slow at responding to emails and grading tests, Prof. Guil will at times explain topics in a way that is hard to understand. Without a book to rely on for this class, you will have to search for another resource to clear up any areas of confusion. Luckily, the tests (which are insanely difficult) are only 1/3 of your grade.

This is one of the hardest classes I've taken, but one in which I've learned the most. Guil is incredibly bright and cares about you learning and understanding the material. He is super friendly and accessible for help outside class and though he is a tough grader, he will explain things so you really learn them. Lab is tough, but interesting.

This class was really difficult, but Guil was great in terms of teaching to the level that we could understand, and I thoroughly enjoyed the material. Be prepared to put in effort, but if you work hard, study for all of the exams, and take the time to redo the homeworks, it should be ok!

Guil gets a bad rep but I loved this class! It is definitely possible to get an A, but you have to work for it. You can redo all homeworks and labs so its best to try and get high grades in those to make up for test grades because the tests are VERY hard and graded weirdly. His lectures are super interesting and informative, you learn so much!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Guil is very intelligent, but this class is really tough and his expectations for you aren't really clear. Also, the grading system is very strange because he wants students to focus on learning more than grades, which would be fine if it wasn't such a tough class.

Has really cleaned up the expectations clarity since the previous review. Still no defined text, though. It's a hard class, the hardest I've had at Vandy, but if you put in the effort he expects and are able to think critically on tests then you'll do fine.
I was very interested in the material... but there is no textbook and Guil is very, VERY unclear about expectations. Take it for geo major, but expect to not understand anything.
LOVE HER! Really cared about her students. Definitely take her for 2100, however the content itself can be pretty dry.

Her exams were overly difficult and didn't seem to reflect what we learned in class. She often didn't respect students' time, and the course felt more confusing than it needed to be. Overall, the material could have been presented in a clearer and more organized way.
Professor Gupta is fantastic. I have taken two classes with her. Defo not an 'easy A' but interesting. She loves conversation with depth, and I appreciated that so much.
very nice and caring but lectures are sometimes not helpful in this type of course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Gupta cares about her students in class. She listens to the needs of the students and adjusts her syllabus accordingly. The tests she gives though are pretty tough and I know some people did not do well on them. She wants her students to succeed though and will work with you if you ask. Make sure you do well on the reading assignments.
She enjoys talking about literature. Awesome, makes the class easy when it is difficult.

She is the sweetest, kindest lady, and she works hard to make sure everyone feels included and participates in the lectures. She will give you extensions if you just ask. She's lovely and truly cares about the students. I had a class when my kids were going to bed and she would say good night to them during the lectures even. She is awesome. 10/10

I absolutely love Dr. Sevin. I took three classes with her and learned so much each time. She is very understanding to any situation. All she wants is for her students to succeed.
This semester I had a bad time mentally and didn't do ANY homework. She let me make it all up before finals.
100000/10 RECOMMEND 
if i could give her more stars, i would.
I took this class online. It was very easy. Do your homework assignments and do well on tests and you will ace this class.

do not take her. she is not helpful at all and always says class time is too short to teach/go over everything so you need to learn/teach yourself through homework. she skips/cancels classes a lot so you are responsible for your own learning.

I think I had Prof Sevin during a bad semester. At first she was great, but as the semester went on class became stressful for everyone. I wish I had switched to Hendrix. However, she can be very helpful. I think under normal circumstances it would have been a good semester. If you take her class, talk, but not too much.
This is a great professor.
Great professor. Attendance is mandatory, but super enjoyable every day. Class is very progressive if that is an issue for you. If you take with a good group, will be best class
super nice teacher, easy material, no exams!

This is my second class with Professor Gutman and I absolutely love her. You can tell she is passionate about what she is teaching and genuinely cares about her students doing well and succeeding. Just show up to class, participate at least somewhat, and put effort into the 3 pretty easy papers she assigns (that you can also revise).

Overall really interesting class (if you are interested in gender and sex education). Participation matters but don't have to participate a ton. Three major writing assignments that are pretty easy. None are very formal and if you go to office hours to discuss your ideas and ask for help the papers should be pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Incredibly nice and caring professor, 100% take if you can. Not too much work for the class- especially for a writing credit only three papers (one 750 words, two 1000 words)- and gives great feedback with opportunities to revise on everything. The topic is out of the box but I really enjoyed it.
AMAZING prof! Loved her so much, not too much writing required, lots of readings though. Would def take again!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: 2 papers, 1 final project, and two presentations. Very strict grader and feedback was clear but hard to understand and revise. The final project was ok but interestingly weird. I would not really recommend her if you are not a good writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Gutman was a great professor in my semester with her. There were 2-3 papers during the semester (depending on if you decided to write a research paper or creative media for the final project). She graded fairly and gave GREAT feedback on our papers (which you can revise). There is not too much work, just read or at least read summaries.

Dr. Gutman really cares about her students. All she expects is that you do the readings and participate in class. Easy grader and offers rewrites for each paper. Being late 3 times is an absence; 3 absences are a grade deduction. It is a W class, so not surprisingly you have to write 3 papers. Overall, very kind and clear on expectations.
He clearly cares about his students, just so disorganized that the class seems harder than it should be. Go to lectures so you know what to expect exams.
He genuinely would fail his own class. He does not know what is going on and the class is very disorganized.

Guelcher is just so boring. Unfathomably boring. They recently changed the curriculum so the class was kind of all over the place and it didn't feel like he knew what he was talking about. Tests don't really have any coding on them, mostly just multiple choice and short answer about the concepts. Not hard, just gruelingly boring.

Relatively easy class. Show up and write down what he does on the board and you can do the homework. Showing up is half your grade, literally. Guelcher is boring and not very helpful outside of class though, so attendance is pretty important.

Worst engineering class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Very unhelpful outside of class. Would only read excerpts from the textbook when you ask him questions at office hours. Rude when he's not in the mood. Left five minutes after starting the final exam. Inconsistent grader -- some students will get more points on certain questions than others.

As far as ChemE goes, this one is fairly easy. Guelcher is clear on what you need to know. Midterms are straightforward. Two midterms; one was a take-home MATLAB based test. Final was not comprehensive, but he threw us a curbeball. All were open book. Guelcher overall is just a goof, in a good way. He's really nice, laid back, and accommodating.

Good guy, and this course is pretty easy. Simple hw from textbook. All quizzes and tests are free response about textbook concepts-- just read the textbook beforehand and understand the material. All he does in lecture is summarize the textbook, occasionally adding engineering concepts. So much easier than general bio. Good

Easiest ES 140 chemical professor. Basically does entire problem for you and you just go home and print it. Extremely boring, but doesn't care if you sit on your phone or laptop all class. Miss class and you may miss a problem, but he doesn't take attendance.
Teaches Chem E decently, but really generated no interest for the subject. Basically wandered through incomprehensible equations all class, then expected a homework done on the subject
I love professor Mazalit. She is great. The class is very engaging and the way she teaches is the best with a lot of cultural exposure. I feel i learn so much Hebrew! You should take this class!
Mazalit's class is a wild ride. You never know what to expect when you walk into it. You will learn a lot more Hebrew than you think.
She is the most caring professor I have ever had. She really cares about my success as her student. You will definitely laugh while in her class, she is so so funny. I LOVE HER>

I have taken 3 classes with professor Haim and cannot rave about her enough! By far the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. She genuinely cares about all of her students, and has very fun, engaging classes. If you are putting effort into the class, you will get a good grade, regardless of how good your Hebrew skills are. Love her!!!
Mazalit is extremely caring and genuinely wants each student to succeed. She is hilarious and offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. She is phenomenal and you will learn a lot!
super fun class and she is very funny and easy grader - wants students to do well

I took modern Israeli culture last semester. Amazing professor! I enjoyed this class and miss it so much! One of my most profound experience at Vanderbilt. Prof. Haim cares deeply about her students. You need to show efforts though.

Mazalit is pretty chill. The class is pretty easy and she's very nice. She genuinely wants to see you succeed and offers a ton of interesting extra credit. It is a somewhat interesting and pertinent class. Some of the feedback on essays is very unclear which is challenging. But overall decent.

Professor Haim is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt! I've learned so much Hebrew and so much about Israeli culture. She cares deeply about her students and always makes herself available if you need help with the material. She values effort, so be sure to class prepared, participate, and complete extra credit assignments.

Mazalit is the best professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt and very creative. I took with her Modern Israeli Culture class and it was so inspiring! She shared with us her own research on the politics of emotions in Israeli culture and it was very interesting. Classes were great with a lot of visual arts and documentaries that are very relevant.

This is a great class! Entering Hebrew as a non-heritage learner, it was very eye opening. Mazalit encouraged me in office hours and class to keep trying until I gained confidence reading and speaking the language. She is an excellent professor for seeing students' needs, meeting them, and caring to do so until each individual student succeeds!

I needed a writing credit, so I took this course at the last minute. It turned out to be super cool with helpful writing workshops. There was a photography workshop one day and well-structured lectures with discussion time a lot of other days. The class always felt really relevant.

Mazalit is an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students. Her classes are very interesting and she always draws interesting connections to other areas of interests. I feel grateful to take Hebrew with her as it enriches my college experience and also will help me in the future as someone who is interested in international relations.

Mazalit is great, super nice and cares a lot about her students. The class is not the most organized, but if you participate a bit, she'll like you. She makes it easy for people to ultimately do well in her class regardless of how they do on their quizzes because she offers lots of random extra credit.
Very nice, but confusing lectures and unclear expectations in assignments

Professor Mazalit is an amazing professor! I took a class with her in the spring and was fortunate to receive her assistance when preparing for my internship this summer. She has a strong interest in the success of her students and always shares her knowledge on Israel with the class. Definitely take a course with her, as she is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I found the class to be very interesting. As someone who is a Jewish Studies major, it was beneficial to take a course related to Israeli culture. Professor Haim explained each lesson clearly, allowed for class participation, and encouraged students to meet during office hours. If you listen and do the work, then you will do well in the class.

Studying Hebrew with Professor Mazalit has been the best decision I've made at Vanderbilt! TAKE HER CLASS! She is super knowledgeable and has a deep passion for seeing her students succeed. She does teaching the way it is supposed to be done. Other professors should learn from her. Highly recommended!

Amazing professor, truly cares about each of her students. Made all of us feel welcome & comfortable, even though there were students with varying levels of Hebrew skill in the class. Daily homework, but manageable & doesn't take long. A couple quizzes, a few group projects, some individual video assignments. Grades by effort, so just do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing professor really cares about her students.

super accessible outside of class and on emails. takes "pulse checks" during class to see what students are struggling with/need more help on. exams were fair and very doable, but outside studying is needed. sometimes the class slides didn't include important info that he would verbally say, so go to class though attendance isnt required.

Super helpful professor, he always really approachable in OH and happy to work through problems or explain difficult concepts together. Group homework was annoying and some problems were tricky. Exams were somewhat difficult but still very fair. If you study the practice exams you'll do fine. Lets you use a cheat sheet which is really helpful.

Professor Haslag is a great finance teacher and I would highly recommend taking a course or with him. He is very patient and has engaging lectures. He is also very accessible outside of class and is helpful with any questions you might have.

Grade relies on midterm and final with some cushions like weekly quizzes (3-4 questions) w unlimited tries and problem sets in a group you pick that he helps with in office hours. Super nice guy. Tests are fair and similar to practice problems and tests he gives. Not hard if you use those materials and review ppts before tests. Curves tests!!

People that complained in this class also didn't make any effort to ask questions, do extra credit, or go to office hours. He wants you to do well, so if you study you'll be fine. Group problem sets cushion the grade, and there's a midterm/final re-weight if you do better on the latter. Lectures did move quickly. Nice guy who wants you to succeed.
Very accessible and straightforward; he went above and beyond to help his students. Most people that did not do well wouldn't pay attention in class and did not keep up with the material

he's so nice and it's clear that he wants everyone to succeed and genuinely understand the content. some hw problems are fine but others extend the concepts further than what we actually learned in class, so those can be time-consuming and tough. put in the work and use his resources and you will be fine.

Haslag is good and gives students lots of resources to do well. He can be a bit boring but his grading system is very fair for the students. The final exam was pretty hard but just make sure you make a good and complete formula sheet

Haslag was a very mediocre prof who did a very subpar job lecturing the class and explaining concepts. His lectures were extremely boring and I've never been in a class where every single person was so unengaged in what the prof was saying. This was easily the hardest business module course with the most difficult concepts and Haslag didn't help.

He is very nice and he is better than many teachers. However, he is not the best teacher in terms of teaching the material that he tests us on. He is definitely better than many other teachers, but he can improve by posting step-by-step solutions, better explaining concepts and their corresponding variables, and having organized in-class notes.

Prof Haslag is very caring. However, he was just very poorly adapted for the online format. He made learning as a remote student even more difficult than it already was and I hated this class for that. I'm rating him based on this online experience, but I'm sure he'd be a better prof in person, but I just personally can't attest to that.

Prof Haslag is awesome - the content is tough just because there's so much to fit in a short time (classic business minor module) but he goes out of his way to help his students. Wants students to succeed - as long as you put in some effort you'll do fine.

Even though finance was a lot of work at times, Professor Haslag was the best! He made the class really interesting, and it was clear that he cared about all of his students. I would love to take more classes with him if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: The class has great material and Professor Haslag does a really good teaching it. It's definitely a hard class, but there are plenty of opportunities to get help if you need it and he goes over and emphasizes difficult concepts. He's also well-organized and provides a super helpful outline of the whole course at the beginning. Very fair midterm.

Professor Haslag is brilliant and an excellent teacher. The class seems a little overwhelming at the beginning as the material is tough and the class moves pretty fast but Haslag is a really easy grader and an A is definitely attainable. This is probably the most helpful module in the business minor and provides a good foundation for future classes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: The structure of the business minor is poor, as Haslag has to teach a semester-long class in 8 weeks. However, despite this, he did a great job of explaining the material and tailoring to students' needs. He is the only prof I've had who asked for feedback and then actually changed accordingly. If you use his office hours & read, you'll be fine.

The class is hard -- previous exposure to accounting & finance would help -- but he is nice. Didn't have time to go to his office hours but I believe he'd be helpful from brief chats with him. I would recommend asking for his help directly when in trouble with group projects. Stay on top of the materials as they build up quickly.

Professor Haslag truly cares that his students understand the material. A lot of people rate him poorly because the class is pretty hard, but that is just the nature of Finance. If you pay attention and do the work assigned, you should be fine. He also provides a lot of extra credit opportunities, which is a good grade booster. Great guy.

Haslag teaches a class that is MBA-level yet a requirement for undergraduates who are simply trying to fulfill a minor. It is obvious that he cares about his students being interested, but the pace of the class is too fast and focused for his lecturing to be inspirational or special. However, he is very receptive to feedback and is always improving
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took him for finance class for the business minor. The class is hard, but that is pretty indicative of how finance is. He is very willing to help, gives out good study guides, and gives back points on tests. Also very receptive to feedback and willing to help outside of class whenever you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: While BUS2300 has its flaws, Professor Haslag is a very good professor. He knows his stuff and cares deeply about whether or not his students grasp the material. While difficult, this course is essential for anyone interested in the financial services.

Ah, the beauty of the flawed new business minor. This was a tough class. He does not have a grading criteria, grades extremely harshly, and does not want to give A's. He is unlike the other FNEC professors in that he did not work in the industry much. Class does not help with IB/fin interviews. Math/equation based. Have to learn everything on own
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Contrary to popular belief History of Rock isn't just an easy class grade-wise. There is barely any work, however the three main tests are pure memorization (album names, artist names, producer names, band member names) from a list of 40 songs per test. Luckily she provides a study guide otherwise everyone in the class would get Bs.
Easily one of the easiest classes at Vanderbilt. Only two midterms, two papers, and a final, and her lectures are pretty interesting.

This class was super fun, and the professor is just so cool in general! This class is super easy only if you are willing to memorize EVERYTHING! Papers are easy, and the exams are very straight forward (no multiple choice only short answer).

This class is great if you love learning about music and want an essay class to take. Lecture slides are not posted online, and it's worth attending the lecture. Exams are almost identical to the study guide. Reading the textbook(s) gives insight into writing the essay part of the exam. Graded on 2 papers, 2 exams, and a final and they're not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome class and awesome professor. Lecture slides are not posted but not difficult to get from a classmate. 2 papers that are graded sort of lightly and 2 tests that are very easy to prepare for by using prior exams that she gives free access to.
Prof Gunderman was absolutely amazing. She prioritizes her students learning about rock music over grades. Tests are easy and papers are interesting. She is so so amazing and I LOVED this class.

Prof Gunderman offered so much insight into the music industry in addition to course content. She did a great job of adapting lectures to her working schedule, and I genuinely looked forward to this class each week. There are two textbooks for the course, but they aren't necessary. Essays are memorization heavy, so make sure to study!

AMAZING professor and super awesome class! Three tests of the same format (one of which counts as the final) and two pretty straightforward papers. She is so kind and caring, take this class if you can!

Every Vanderbilt student needs to take a class with Prof. Gunderman. Most knowledgable professor I have ever had, she is very well known and active within the rock music industry. Doesn't post slides, but her lectures are so interesting that I made sure to be at every class. Her tests are pure memorization, and only other assignments were 2 papers.

Genuinely such an interesting class! The Professor is so cool and keeps us updated on her music career outside of class. The tests are purely memory based so make sure you study a few hours the days prior. She gives access to test banks which are incredibly helpful. Class is very low maintenance, show up to class since she doesn't post the slides!
She is so cool. Every class is interesting, and more often than not, she has a personal connection to whatever is being discussed. Just awesome.

Professor Gunderman is just the coolest. If you have the chance to take a class with her, do it! I took Women and Rock, which was pretty low-stress aside from a big research paper/project at the end of the year. It was a super chill and laid back class overall and she shares so many cool stories.

This is a really interesting class that teaches more than just the history of rock music, and allows you to learn a lot about general history. Gunderman is great and lets you take it at your own pace. The tests are hard and memorization of random stuff is key so be willing to learn some of those random facts bc those will cost you. Great class tho

Best class Vandy has to offer. I walked away learning so much interesting material. She knows so much about everything it is incredible. tests can be tricky if you don't grind the notes a few days in advance. Super cool class and even better professor!

Lectures are basically required b/c she doesn't post slides. 2 fairly straightforward papers, 2 exams & a final which rly only require a few hours of memorization shortly before. She posted past exams which was super helpful. Very interesting lectures and her stories are fun to listen to! If you need an easy/low-stress HCA class, def take this one!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Gunderman is so COOL. Honestly wish I was her friend to hear more about her awesome stories meeting/working with all of these famous artists. If you need an HCA class and don't take this, idk what you're doing.

Favorite class I've taken so far. Very easy 2 papers, super interesting lectures, 2 tests + final. Only really need to spend a couple hours studying before a test for memorization and recommend going to class bc she doesn't post the slides and it's fun. I wish I could take this class over again. Prof Gunderman is the coolest person on this campus.

Professor Gunderman is one of the most interesting individuals on campus. She missed about 1/4 of the year due to various touring commitments, but that didn't negatively affect my experience in the class. Two, papers, two tests, and a final. The lecturers are somewhat mandatory though since she doesn't post slides online. Take her class if you can!

Great class, super interesting, not a lot of work. I honestly tried way too hard on the papers, she is not a tough grader. Definitely, a good class if you need an easy and interesting A with a super sweet and awesome professor (she is SO COOL).

Prof. Gunderman is a solid choice. History of rock is a really cool class, but I wouldn't recommend taking it unless you enjoy rock music and/or have a strong working knowledge about rock music. The class was asynchronous because of covid, but prof Gunderman was still very accessible and responsive to emails. She also has a lot of cool stories!

Gunderman is great and Rock is an easy A. 2 tests, 2 papers, and a final. Papers are graded easily, tests are mostly memorization but not bad at all. The class is only lectures but they're interesting and you get to listen to music so it's fun. She checks attendance almost every class so show up but you can go on your computer so it's not boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she takes attendance at every class, you should show up because the material is genuinely interesting  she has so many cool stories from her own personal life that she shares through lecture i just took notes on my computer and did a lot of memorizing before each test (not hard, just tedious) two papers, one long one short, both graded easily
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Basically all lecture, few anecdotes if they relate to a specific theme/artist or about her travels. Occasionally shell open up class time for discussion. The reading is required, but you can get away with not reading if you understand the big ideas for possible essay questions on exams. You can tell shes very passionate about her teaching.

Gunderman is arguably one of the coolest professors at Vanderbilt. Her life experience in the rock music industry makes her lectures engaging and more personal. Take this class because you will discover and appreciate new music, and you will likely actually remember some of the material years from now (and because it's an easy A).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I can honestly say that I looked forward to going to History of Rock every week. Prof Gunderman is great; she shares really cool stories about the history of music and her personal experience touring as a musician. If you put the work in, it's an easy A. Anything on the slides could be on the exams so definitely go to class and take notes.

Class is fun. Listen to some great music and hear cool stories. Gunderman's a sweetheart who's clearly passionate about the topic. Lots of memorization for tests though. Get ready to buckle down the night or two before to learn names, albums, instruments, etc. It's music though so not bad at all compared to other classes. Harder than country music

Professor Gunderman is a true gem of a teacher at Vanderbilt. As a touring musician for Sheryl Crow, she gives really great insight into the life of music. Not an easy A show up whenever class. 1 Long paper, 1 short paper, 2 tests and a final. Any small detail on the PPs can be on the test and she doesn't send them online. But, great class anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty interesting - notes are necessary to study for/pass tests. Anything on the slides is fair game and she doesn't give them out. Tests are based on trivia basically (what instrument was used, what album X song is from, who wrote/produced Y song, etc) Understanding of social context/history not really important or covered, sadly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: History of Rock Music is my favorite class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. Prof. Gunderman is so knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, and will make you fall in love with rock and roll. Tests require a ton of memorization but if you spend time studying and especially using flash cards you will do well. Two papers, a few tests.

I dont know how everyone thinks this class was so easy. Its a lot of straight memorization. Personally, I would not retake this class - unless you love memorizing peoples names, obscure members and albums. Taught me very little about the history - not a blow off class as it was before.

Class was ****ing awesome.  Learn some cool rock history and watch some great footage. Anyone would be an idiot not to take it. Notes are same year after year.  Tests are cake. One of the easiest As at Vandy
Her class is awesome. TAKE IT. it doesnt hurt that its an easy A.
Her class is awesome. TAKE IT. it doesnt hurt that its an easy A.
Easy and very interesting. Seriously you could go to just the reviews if you wanted to and make an A...but the class is way too interesting to skip more than you have to! Best class ever.
Make sure you put time in on the papers and you'll do fine. Tests are cake, although the essays are graded a little rough. Great professor and the most interesting class I've had at Vanderbilt.

If you go to class and the review sessions or you know someone else who will, then the exams will not be a problem.  There were two papers, one on an artist of choice and one on a concert review.  Most people received a B on these papers. Random attendence checks were always when we got exams back and were easy to walk into late without a problem.

Wonderful professor. Professor Gunderman is always interesting, informative, and fair. If you attend class and put some time into the papers, an A is very attainable. Highly recommend this class to anybody, regardless if they like rock or not.

I really enjoyed her History of Rock class. She has a personality that makes it really interesting! She's fairly strict about grading papers. The tests are off of powerpoint slides she shows during class, so you have to go to class and take notes to do well. That all said, it isn't too difficult to get an A. I would definitely recommend her.

This class is easy. I knew nothing about rock and roll and I learned a lot of cool stuff in this class. Her stories are really funny and the class does not require a lot of work. Just take good notes and go to the review sessions. Study for the exams and you will do very well. TAKE THIS COURSE BEFORE YOU GRADUATE!

This class is a joke, and she takes it way too seriously. That said, it's an easy A. She is a huge liberal who injects a lot of accusations of racism into her lectures, which is really annoying. And for someone who acts so socially sensitive, she refused to grant extensions on the papers she made due on the holiest Jewish holiday of the year.
AMAZING PROFESSOR! Class is so interesting and she switches between powerpoints, documentaries, and general lecture. Studying is a must but it is relatively easy to get a A-range grade

Professor Gunderman is hilarious, intelligent, and knowledgeable about the subject matter. The class itself is a blast already thanks to the subject matter (History of Rock), but Gunderman makes it even better. She's a great professor, TAKE THIS CLASS. Favorite so far at Vandy.

If you're really into this stuff, it's probably a really good class and Gunderman is very into the stuff she teaches. But if you're just trying to get an A, this class has changed. TAs cannot any longer narrow down essays for the test, and the don't tell you the test questions during review sessions anymore. This class is not the joke it used to be

It's history of rock music. Why wouldn't you take it? Basically, like everyone else said, it's a great class and not too difficult, and she makes lectures entertaining. Basically you just need to memorize her powerpoint notes for tests. Papers require research, but topics of your choice made them kind of fun to write.

Definitely take this class to fufill your history credit for axle.  Professor Gunderman has a vast knowledge of this subject, and she has many funny anecdotes to go along with it. The test are really easy, but the papers are harder.  However, the class is still really easy with class averages normally around 88ish.
She's awesome.

class code may be wrong, but it's American Pop Music and it's fantastic.  she's fantastic, so talented, and very funny.  hope that the TA is good b/c she grades the papers.  Tests are DIRECTLY from lecture slides, so  just go to class and copy them verbatum and you'll ace the tests.

great prof! very helpful, easy going. subject is very interesting, although the lectures can get boring. tests are easy as long as you take notes from pwrpt and study them, and listen to the songs. def take for axle.

Jen Gunderman is awesome. Where else will you learn the history of rock by someone who played in the rock band the Jayhawks? Tests are easy, lectures are extremely interesting, and cool guest speakers. She gets frustrated because people take advantage of her, and this causes a somewhat harsh attendance policy. STRICT ON PAPERS THOUGH!!!

Class can be kind of boring, but it is definitely a nice change from other courses. Just memorize the info on the powerpoints and you're golden for a great grade in the class. The papers are long and unfairly graded, but its not bad enough to detract from the class.
An awesome class, and one of the coolest professors at Vandy.

She takes attendence randomly about 5 times, but other than that you'll probably be fine skipping some classes. If you copy exactly what's on the powerpoint slides, then that's all you need to study with. I used my textbook once to help me with a paper, but you don't even really need it. It's a pretty easy class & she knows her stuff, so take it.
Despite the BS paper and test grading, I enjoy this class. Everything's graded by grad. students, so it's obviously going to have BS grading.

What a great professor!  Her rock and pop classes are both so much fun.  The tests can be difficult and detailed, but just MEMORIZE the facts on her powerpoints and you will be golden.  Other than that, if you are a music fanatic like me, you will not only love the class but also love getting to know gunderman because she is very knowledgeable.

Best class I have taken at Vandy.  Extremely interesting.  Take notes during class and make sure to attend the review sessions held by the TA before the exams. She tells you EVERYTHING you need to know.  As long as you memorize that, you're garenteed an A.
By far the best professor at Vanderbilt.  Class is great.

Go to class, take the notes, and cram for tests.  Pop music (149) is not as fun as rock (153), but a nice break from typical Vanderbilt courses.  It's all memorization, and if you have a good TA they will help you cut out a lot of the fluff before tests.  Random attendance is taken and can hurt your grade.  3 tests 3 papers (two 3 page, one 10 page

History of Rock is an awesome course. Take it. All you do is listen to good music and watch video clips. She's a good lecturer and the class is wayyy low key. Two papers, but they're not hard...neither are the tests (plus review sessions are offered). TAKE THIS CLASS but don't bother to buy the book
Awesome class. I would honestly go to it for no credit. You watch tons of video footage and listen to a lot of songs in class. It is by far the best class I've ever taken.

I really love this class. I actually enjoy going to class, and it is sorta a break from my other classes. You don't have to know a lot about music. There is some work involved though, so be prepared, but I highly recommend this course.

She is a wonderful teacher of the history of ROCK because she is a musician herself, and so she teaches from the perspective of a professional musician -- which is intriguing and enlightening!  My only wish for the class is that she would choose for the listening assignments songs that we haven't already heard to death.

Didn't learn a single thing about rock music, or any music for that matter.  Class consists of memorizing large amounts of completely trivial facts.  if you enjoy music, know anything about music, or play any instruments, then please don't take this class, it insults your musical intellegence, reduces music to a list of artists.  not worth the time
Really awesome class, especially if you are a music geek like me.  Gunderman is really cool and very knowledgable.  Nothing bad to say, except that our person musical tastes sometimes conflicted...

Such an interesting class.  I never dreaded going, and you watch lots of fun video clips and learn things about music you've always wanted to know.  Tests aren't bad, but papers are graded more strickly than you'd think.
Paper grades are BS.  Don't take class.  You will have sooooo much work, for nothing.
very cool and interesting class.  tests need to be studied for but other than that not too difficult.  As far as hotness, good from far, far from good.
Grading on the papers was ****, but that hot ass makes up for it.  I wanna become friends with that.
great teacher, fun class

She is a very knowledgeable professor who knows a lot about the Rock and Roll business. Her tests are much like High School History tests (fill in the blank, essays) and they are fairly easy if you can memorize a great volume of info. She is surprisingly tough on grammer on her papers, but its NBD.
Great class, lectures were always enjoyable.
Doesn't deliver the best lectures. Super kind and available professor however. Attendance is mandatory but only worth 3% of grade. Exams incredibly similar to practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's awesome! I missed two assignments, and understanding it would dent my grade - he gave me an extension for both!  Also, grading is really really easy on exams. Classes are fun too. highly recommend.

Super super nice professor, he tries his best in class but the content is just boring so lecture is pretty boring, but overall the class is graded very easily. Averages always in the 90s, gives extra credit when you participate in class, and exams allow cheat sheet and are short and usually similar to practice exam.

Really easy on grading, you make a major mistake and you'll prob only lose like half a point. Can get extra credit if you participate in pair-share questions. Lectures are extremely boring tho, lowkey learned more from the textbook than the lecture. Also he's not the best at keeping a good flow, sometimes improvise too much on the spot.

Nice guy, just awkward. Will shift office hours and answer emails at 1am. However, class is too easy for what it should be. Too much time is spent on basic topics (logic gates, data representations). Exams have 90+ averages. Would have liked to see more focus on trimming performance
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: spams tophat attendance questions, spams quizzes, spams hw. class is mind numbingly easy but the sheer amount of busy work is incredibly annoying. complete waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class was extremely boring and unengaging. The professor showed little empathy or understanding toward students, often coming across as cold and indifferent. If you are looking for a professor who is approachable and cares about students' learning experience, this is not the right choice.

Hajiamini does try to teach OS well. The slides are honestly not too bad, but his delivery isn't great. Class itself is very easy. Easy homework with lots of extra credit. Exams were short and trivially easy. Unfortunate because you would expect such a core course to be emphasized a bit more in terms of rigor. Oh well. Operated some systems ig.

Hajiamini is a super sweet professor who goes the extra mile to help his students. He's super responsive over Piazza, email, and during office hours. The only reason why people don't like him is because computer architecture is objectively boring. Pretty easy and straightforward class all around.
Nice teacher but a boring class, where barely anyone ever participated. Class wasn't hard but inconsistent grading with the TA's and didn't really get much feedback on assignments.

Content before first two exams is pretty easy, lectures are useless and super boring but attendance is mandatory (TopHat), lots of busy work (zybooks, take-home quizzes), homeworks are graded inconsistently, final exam is not cumulative

I selected hilarious because it's hilarious that Hajiamini is even a professor. He is the worst professor I have ever had the misfortunate of taking. He cannot lecture in the slightest, grades attendance/participation, and throws a pissy-fit if you ignore him in lecture. I lost braincells listening to this man speak. You must self-study this class.
He's a really nice guy and seems to care about his students, but the class is incredibly boring and graders aren't very lenient with the grading.

Solid professor, I think he gets a lot of hate cuz the class is so boring. In general he is decent at explaining things and his slides and zybooks are pretty similar to what is on exams, quizzes, and homeworks.
Had Shervin for 1101 and now 2281. Most improved player award goes to him. Puts in a big effort into his class and explains concepts well. This is my guy

OS is a boring, but relatively easy class at Vandy. There are weekly homework assignments that can range from very easy to very frustrating. Definitely go to office hours for those. Hajiamini's tests were a lot more straightforward than I expected. He gives lectures on slides and takes attendance every day. Readings can be helpful.

Having only him teach cs 2281 comp arch is an absolutely joke.
