He is indeed super accessible, not strict at all when he grades anything, easy first half of the semester, but i didn't understand any material after the 2nd midterm until the final. A lot of office hour visits required and heavily time consuming class especially towards the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Though he's a nice guy, two big reasons why he shouldn't be a teacher: 1) HORRIBLE lecturer and 2) baffling, robotic administrative decisions. It is immensely hard to pay attention, even when he's teaching easier stuff. The second point refers to how he has weird, dumb rules about stuff like HW that he does for *literally* no reason.
The school teaches this class a bit too easy...Hajiamini really tried to teach this class well. Slides were mostly copied from CMU. Who would attend his section if CMU online videos has it all?

I will start off by saying that Professor Hajiamini is a great guy. He will go out of his way to help if you are struggling. He is willing to help out in any way that he can. His lectures can be quite dry and boring, but that may also just be operating systems as a class. The class gives a lot of hw, but it's easy to get a good grade in the class.

Overall, 2201 is a tough class, and Hajiamini is overall a nice guy.  He is pretty easily accesible outside of class.  The lectures are pretty boring, but I find most CS lectures boring so....  Not a bad choice as a professor.
operated some systems, wasn't too bad

Sorta timid/quiet, and lectures can drag. However, very accessible outside of class; helpful in office hours with assignments and test material. If possible, avoid for OS because Balasub writes/explains material better. If taken, visit office hours for all assignments. Tests not too bad; no serious complaints and was kind about absences, etc.

Not a bad choice for 2201 so if you don't get Roth it's not a huge deal, but he's just an average lecturer and I found it hard to pay a lot of attention during most lectures (though I have ADHD). 2201 is annoying and hard, but it's not his fault, that's just how the class is. I found the TAs to be more accessible and helpful than he was though.

He's not a bad lecturer, he can explain things & answers questions well. He's just so dry, monotone, & quiet that paying attention is impossible. 

I agree that a lot of ppl r just projecting their hatred for 2201 towards him. He himself isn't a bad choice, the course itself is just difficult.

That being said he's not very understanding :(
The lecture was dry, but if you followed along and you'd discover that he went straight to the important point. Not the best lecturer but definitely not as bad as the other negative reviews had said.

Underrated. Pay attention in class and ask about what you don't know, because he is always willing to help. Super nice, people project their hatred of 2201 in general onto him, when in fact he is not a bad prof at all.

I expected 2201 to be a tough class, but honestly it was not that bad. However, what was taught was absolutely boring and Hajiamini didn't make it any better. Roth once came in to sub for him and that lecture was the only one I actually paid attention to because of his energy and enthusiasm. Don't expect to learn much and don't stress too hard.

Prof. Hajiamini is a really clear and good lecturer. I suspect many of the negative feedback comes from starting PAs too late; start them early and they're a piece of cake I promise. Hajiamini was always accessible to me outside and inside the class. Would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Awful class. Java for people with no experience is tough but he made it even tougher. Comparatively speaking you learn 1+1 on lectures he will give you integrals on tests. He has no idea how to make his test reflect the info/examples in the slides. DO NOT RECOMMEND HIM. Can't teach, just reads and he will take out points even for a single comma. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you are taking this class choose another professor. He is difficult to talk to even though he tries. You will not find welcoming environment in his classroom. Does not not know how to teach - reads the slides. Why did we need a professor when he did not really contribute at all, except for creating the slides. You WON'T learn much from this guy.

Hard course, but Hajiamini really knows his stuff. I don't understand all of these bad reviews; even though he's not the best lecturer, all of the important information is on the slides, and if you're diligent and asking questions about things you don't understand, he's patient and always able to answer questions well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hajjamini is nice but not a great lecturer and has no control over this class. Roth is a good lecturer but in Hajjamini's class you get the worst of both worlds bc you deal with bad lectures and really mean grading. I don't even want to give the class credit by calling it hard, it's just the most stupidly structured class I have ever taken.
Really boring professor. Though the actual things you learn are very powerful. TAs a very picky with assignments.

If you have no prior coding experience, this will be a very hard class. There is a lot of homework, but the TAs are super helpful and make it possible to get good grades on each assignment. The tests are easier than the homework but are worth very little. Hajiamini isn't the best teacher and is super monotone but the lecture slides have good detail

Hajiamini knows the material well, although his lectures can be dry. Given that this was his first semester teaching at Vandy, he did a great job. Always happy to answer questions, overall genuinely nice and dedicated. Uses the same lecture slides as Roth, so doesn't make too much of a difference which professor. Make sure to start projects early.

Did great for his first semester teaching at Vanderbilt. Dr. Roth determines the curriculum and the grading criteria, but taking the class with Dr. Roth won't give you any advantage, since Dr. Hajiamini does a good job delivering the lectures. CS 2201 is a lot of work. Be sure to start projects early.

Dr. Hajiamini is a kind professor that explains topics decently well. Lectures can feel long and dry, but they give a good introduction to programming in Java. Not a difficult class in terms of getting a good grade, but there is a decent amount of work in the form of programming assignments and zyBook activities.

Prof. Hajiamini's lectures can be dry, but he knows the concept and is willing to explain it. CS2201 is a weed out class for CS majors, so that's why we have projects nearly every week that can take 4 hours to forever. Also TAs are quite random graders. You could learn a lot, but don't take it as a course filler if you don't want to do CS related.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Even tho Hajiamini's lectures can be a bit dry, he's pretty good at explaining things clearly. Good at answering questions and is very accommodating of students' needs. Considering that this was his first year teaching, he'll definitely get even better in the future. Solid option for CS2201.

A great choice for 2201 and is really awesome. Very knowledgeable will either answer questions on the spot or find the answer and let you know. Really committed to teaching. The content is not easy and is dry, but that's the nature of every section of this class. He's especially great considering it was his first year teaching here. Def recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 2201 is so hard, but so rewarding in what it teaches you - the foundations of data structures. easily the most valuable in my time at Vandy. Shervin was okay, understood the topics and taught fine, but not really a memorable teacher since it's his first year teaching. skipping class and just following the lectures was just as helpful as attending.

Hajiamini is a great option for 2201. He is knowledgable about the material and a decent lecturer, and he is also willing to thoroughly address any questions you have, both inside and outside class. The course itself is quite a bit of work, and some of the projects are long, but for his first semester being at Vandy, I think he did great.
His lectures are pretty dry. Would not recommend him for people new to cs.

Hanusa is the worst option for teachers for CHEM 1602. His lectures tend to ramble and are very hard to follow along with. His slides are crowded with information, and he goes too fast. Overall, try your best to avoid his class. There are a lot of better teachers for this out there, and there is no reason to make a hard class harder by taking him.

Poor lecturer, always gets distracted and doesn't explain concepts well. Didn't feel necessary to attend most lectures. Uses graded tophat bonus questions in class for bonus points (all profs give 3% bonus but do so in different ways).

I'm p sure Hanusa was my best bet for chem1602. If you wanna win, sit in the front, ask questions, and go to every office hour you can with your questions ready. He is so willing to explain and help, his lectures just feel really disjointed---that's the reason I rated him as a difficult prof.
I am 90% sure my grade would be lower if not for him.

Hanusa is a sweet man who cares, but he is not the best lecturer. It is SO easy to doze off in his classes, since his lectures are full of unnecessary info such as history lessons and he over-confuses topics. He seems to assume most students just get topics, even though 1602 is harder than 1601. Doesn't explain very well, wish I took Tainter.

Sweet guy, not the best lecturer. Originally took him for his high rating, but it seems he's fallen off this sem. If you take him, be ready to REALLY read the textbook, as he speeds through any important piece of info on his slides. Tophat is basically free, especially with help from the LAs. Probably would opt for Todd/Tainter if I could go back.

Hanusa is a nice guy but not a great lecturer, so you'll need to self-study more than other sections. Slides are very text-heavy and difficult to extract meaningful info. 1602 is definitely harder than 1601 but doable. My advice: read the textbook. DO NOT slack on discussion quizzes as they will tank your lecture grade. Go to class for bonus.

Hanusa is a nice guy but his slides aren't as clear imo. 1602 is definitely a large step up in difficulty from 1601 and is probably hard regardless of professor, but I did have a much easier time following along in Tainter's lecture during first sem. Hanusa does have much easier Tophat though, basically guaranteed extra credit.
Hanusa is a nice guy and very willing to answer questions. His slides are informative though sometimes stray away from main points. His lectures are somewhat drawsy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hanusa is a nice guy and he's pretty funny. Not v engaging. Make sure you're actively learning/paying attention during class, Hanusa doesn't do a fantastic job of making the application of certain concepts immediately clear. Go to class for the extra credit, and you can secure an A with a fair amount effort. Wants his students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Though I originally took him because of the high rating, I quickly found out that it wasn't at all accurate. You will find yourself forcing yourself to pay attention most classes, if not on the verge of falling asleep. Also only take him if being a history major was your second choice after being pre-med cause every third slide is a history lesson.

Hanusa is the sweetest professor ever but he's not the best teacher. His slides aren't very helpful and he gets off topic. If you do take him, read the textbook before class and the lecture will make much more sense.
Although he hadn't taught the second semester of gen chem in a while, I fell well prepared for each of the tests. The discussion quizzes are impossible, but that applies for any chem1602 professor

Dr. Hanusa is probably the best Chem 1602 professor. His slides contain much more information that the other professors, he's always friendly when the class is working on example problems, and he ensures that we know which topics are most important for the test. The exams are the same as the other sections, but he always prepares you well.

Hanusa is an awesome guy, 100% the nicest out of all the Chem 1602 Profs. His classes follow the same idea - lecture on a concept, do in class kahoot style questions with LAs, go over the right answer, repeat. This works great. The class is hard, but he wants to help. (After one exam, I finished early and he walked out to ask how it was, so nice)
Genuinely the best chem prof. Funny, kind, and willing to help.
Extremely helpful, he is available for office hours whenever you have time.

Hanusa is pretty good professor, took him in the fall and he was helpful. The only problem is that class is at 8AM and not required, so many times I didn't end up going. But honestly, the tests are all the same regardless of which prof you have, so don't stress too much over who you get, worry more about getting someone later in the day.
Really good professor, probably the best of the intro chemistry professors. However, they use unified tests and exams so there isn't a lot of difference.

Hanusa is pretty awesome. Like any chemistry professor, he is pretty quirky, but fun to listen  to, even though I had him at 8 in the morning. Doesn't do the best job of preparing students for the test (he saves a ton of trick questions for the tests). Do your best on clickers, & remember clicker questions for the tests. Class supplements help.

Dr. Hanusa tries very hard to make Chemistry fun for all of his students. However, it's hard to do this at 8 AM. If you have taken more than a year of chemistry in high school, you'll sleep during lectures, but if you haven't, you may feel a bit overwhelmed because of his speed. All tests are standardized. Pick whichever teacher fits your schedule.

Hanusa did his best at trying to cover the material of a very difficult subject. He went way too quickly through his lectures, but was always very helpful in his office hours. He seemed like the most personable Gen Chem professor. Nonetheless, the tests are going to be difficult no matter which professor you take.

Hanusa does his best for an 8am class. His lectures are dry, but occasionally he'll try to make a joke to liven things up. Still, he moves quickly which can make class hard to follow if you didn't take AP chem. Not super accessible or affable outside of class; seemed like a guy that felt like he had better things to do. Still, better than List.

Dr. Hanusa is a great chemistry professor - he is so passionate about his teaching and is a great lecturer.  The chemistry concepts are really difficult and he sometimes speeds through them, but he is very approachable in his office hours.  My favorite professor this semester.

Hanusa is an all right person, but he expects you to grasp extremely difficult concepts as though they are common sense, which is just not going to happen for the average student. Difficult to stay awake during his class, recommend taking someone else if at all possible.

Good professor. His lecture are interesting and he brings in a lot of extra material (not relevant to tests or textbook). He makes chemistry interesting to learn - however, you are graded 100% based on a department test so this makes it slightly more difficult. Great professor if you want to learn something useful with chemistry

Great professor. Going to lecture is not necessary because posts the lecture powerpoints on OAK. But with Chem 102 in general, if you didn't take AP Chemistry, the textbook is the real professor. If you have taken AP Chem, skim through the book and go over stuff not covered in AP.

A really great guy. He wants everyone to like chemistry, even though no one takes it unless they have to. He tries to make a few jokes and the powerpoints are a really handy tool to have. From hearing friends' comments about other profs, probably the best choice for 102A
He is about as good of a huge lecture professor as you can get. He is engaging and funny in a nerdy kind of way.

Really nice guy and you can tell he really cares about what he's teaching (sometimes a little too much because he tends to ramble). Honestly, you don't really need to go to gen chem lecture, especially with Hanusa, because he basically just reads from his very comprehensive ppts in class. Very boring at 8:10 am but does his best.

Hanusa was hard to follow in lectures sometimes.  I had him for first semester chemistry, and struggled to pull off a C+.  I switched to another professor for second semester and felt much better (Phillips).  He definitely doesn't work enough problems in class to help you out for the exams.

I love Professor Hanusa! He truly cares about his students' successes and is the only professor to hold review sessions and post review sheets for exams. He is the best professor for CHEM 102 and offers the best preparation for the standardized exams.

Hanusa is very interested, and therefore knowledgeable about chem. He really wants everyone to understand. but it's CHEM! you can't blame the man for maybe being boring, the subject matter is also! the tests are departmentalized, the quizzes are taken elsewhere. you really don't have to attend class. read the book, do practice problems will suffice

Hanusa definitely tries his best to explain everything so that anyone can understand.If you have trouble waking up in the morning or have had AP chem, you might do well to try another professor.If this is one of your first experiences with chem, I think hes probably your best choice.
Unless you have to take this class.....dont!
He's very clear in what you need to know for the tests and is a very clear teacher.  If you go to class and study hard, its a very passable class

this guys is so tall. anyways, class is useless, he usually teaches T/R at 8am which is when i had him and he was so boring it was painful.  nearly never went to class and i got a B+. if you've taken AP chem, you'll do fine, i didnt.  dont go to class, read the text and find old tests.  it's almost useless anyways b/c the class definitely weeds out
He wasn't as good as Philips. I felt less prepared for the exams and always lost points on his specific professor's page. He tires but just is not as effective as other teachers.

He's great. His lectures were actually clear enough so that I could actually stay awake for the 8 o clock class. He jokes in class and does a lot of examples, so you feel like you know what's going on.

ahh, chem. I might be biased because I despise science with a passion, but I thought this class was hard. I mean, numbers don't lie either. The average for my semester was like in the 70's or high 60's. Anyway, Hanusa is pretty cool. Much better than List and a little faster than Philips which I liked.
really thorough- has good review sessions and goes over all topics in detail- very clear as to what is on tests- prof pages on tests are pretty tough but one of the better teachers for intro chem

Dr. Hanusa wants you to do well.  He tries very hard to convey the lessons well and listens to class concerns. He will hold study sessions, gives out helpful handouts, and is alwasy willing to answer questions. He also adds some humor occasionally. Lectures consist of a lot of board work and lecture with some powerpoint and many demos.

A really nice guy. Can be boring at times, but he also has a really good sense of humor about messing things up. Definitely the best teacher for this class because you get the most preparation for exams.
damn, this guy can definitely put you to sleep!
Probably the best chem teacher during my semester. He prepares you pretty well for the dept. exams, and he's also the only chem teacher from this semester that gives extensive reviews.
Chem can be hard but he was the best professor out of all of them I thought.
Not the most entertaining, but goes over material that the other profs don't and in more detail.  Take him and you'll be the best prepared when the departmental exams hit.
great professor.tests are easy
First, the tests are departmental.  For a morning class, he puts you to sleep, he's a very dry lecturer and explains things vaguely.  Take Rosenthal if you can.

SUCH A SWEETHEART!!  He is the nicest chemistry professor alive, and for an 8 am class, he makes it SO much fun.  Ask him what they used to do with liquid nitrogen and frogs, you will be in for a good hardy laugh!

Dr. Hanusa is the best teacher I've ever had. He brings in tons of demos and tries really hard to get students interested, even for early morning chemistry classes. He is very helpful outside of class.
This guy is really not a good teacher...he contradicts the book and everything else, and then when you miss it on a quiz or test, its your fault not his.  not a good teacher.
No Comments
He's very personable and approachable, usually explains things clearly.
Professor Hanusa is an engaging teacher.  He makes even 8 o'clock classes interesting.
this my queen right here
mind numbing at times but still liked. clear criteria to get an A

Very nice professor. The class is very easy, as she grades assignments on completion. However I do not feel like I learned anything in this class. Lectures were unorganized, she would show up late, and the class would often get off track. If you are want an easy class, take 2400, if you are looking for a class that is worth your time, then don't.

The class is very unstructured and goes off of a grading contract where there are 4 short response papers and a final portfolio. Grading wise, just show up to class and do the HW and it should be an easy A. Prof Lefkowitz clearly has a passion for her job and the course centers a lot around changing the culture on post-career stress.
One of the kindest professors you will ever meet, but the class is very disorganized. Lots of important lessons but not a lot of structure.

Everyone knows Prof L is the GOAT. If you have an opportunity to take this (or any) class with her, DO IT! Not challenging, engaging, and with real world relevance. I looked forward to this class every week. TAKE TAKE TAKE!

Prof L definitely cares a lot about her students. Class seems like a waste of time sometimes, but attendance is mandatory and sometimes the discussions in class can provide valuable opportunities to hear from other students in class about the various topics the class covers.
Professor L is the nicest person I have ever met. She gives great advice. I really enjoyed this class and would recommend it to anyone.
BEST PROFESSOR! She makes class enjoyable, she is flexible, she is a little disorganized but she will work with you and teach you so well. TAKE IT!
Take her! Amazing person. You can always count on her!
She is the best professor ever. I loved going to her class. Make sure to listen to the lecture and participate. This is actually the best class.
HOD2400 is the easiest class you will ever take, just make sure to do your annotations and try to go to office hours as Prof. L is one of the kindest people I know.
Easy class but lectures were usually not very engaging. Overall, I don't feel like I learned much, there's a reason this class got taken out of the HOD core.

Definitely not a typical class but still useful for thinking about your career, especially for sophomores. Assignments are very light and grading is extremely easy as long as you complete them. Prof Lefkowitz is very caring and wants to help students however she can, very accessible outside of class.

She is the best! Contrary to other reviews, I learned a lot about the workplace and myself. I used the material from the class to help me in interviews and I got an internship! If you are someone who does not like inner work, talking about your feelings, etc., you will likely find this class "stupid". I challenge you to see the value of this class.

Easy A. On her assignments, she likes to see quantity over quality (there's no way she actually reads all of her students' assessments) and if you write a lot you'll get an A. Tbh her assessments are more busy work than anything else. Can't say I learned anything in the class but given the low workload and easy A I can't complain.

Just a true gem. This class is not meant to test you in any way. It is meant to help you figure out where you belong, what your plan might be, and how to accomplish your goals. I would recommend this to someone unsure of a life path and probably sophomores. She exposes you to important know-hows of a workplace and prepares you for your Capstone.

Absolutely loved Professor L! She is literally a queen and I want her to officiate my wedding! Really works with you and makes lectures enjoyable to go to, even if the content may be a little repetitive. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
Truly fabulous. Super easy to talk with, super warm, and a great person overall. TAKE HER CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not like this class, extremely boring to sit through. However, I loved Professor Lefkowitz. She was super fun and tried to make the content engaging. Also, she will meet with you outside of class to talk about anything and everything. Helped me find an internship, so she is very very helpful with career-oriented work.

You need to have severe cognitive dysfunction to not get an A in this class. She WANTS you to get an A. Literally let us re-submit 2 old papers if we "didn't get above a 95 in them." Btw there's 3 total papers in the class.

Very nice, teaches some cool applicable things to your professional life.
Hilarious, caring, insightful professor. What you get out of HOD 2400 is what you put into it. She's someone who is extremely helpful w/ academic, career, and life advising, too.

Prof L is the BEST!! Nicest woman alive. She is so kind and willing to meet with everyone about anything. The class is absurdly easy but still has useful things. I looked forward to going to class everyday and it was so fun. I don't know if it is possible to not get an A in this class if you do all of the assignments. They take a while but not bad.

Stereotypical kindergarten HOD course, but the class itself was easy and Prof L is super chill. Kind of boring to sit through but it is what it is. Assignments took an awfully long time to do (probably to make the class "harder") and she always switched up expectations, assignments, and grading extremely last minute. Hopefully that can be changed.

Learning the professional skills was good but then every assignment was more related to "critical reflexivity" or whatever and it overall began to rot my brain/make me feel dumber. It can feel impossible to sit through class and the "fun" stuff she does gets old really fast. You pretty much have to take this for HOD but it still isn't great

I don't even know where to begin. The easiest HOD core course but also the least enjoyable. You will feel like you're losing brain cells with every class you sit through. Assignments are easy but feel like busy work. Prof. Lefkowitz is one of those teachers where you will either love her or hate her. My rating reflects which side I fall on...

This class was basically LinkedIn101. Take this class being "easy" with a grain of salt. You still have to put a good amount of effort into the bigger assignments... they aren't hard, but don't wait until the last minute to start. The meditation and class activities may seem silly, but at the end of the day the class is what you make of it.

This class is entirely based on changing your 'thinking' and is less graded on content. But, class is a waste of time. You meditate and draw for half the class. The attendance policy is unclear and grades are seemingly random. Assignments change on the fly. It's difficult to really learn anything in this class or know your grade until the last week

Great professor. Loved every lecture and class activity she had. Class has large but few assignments. To succeed, just attend class, participate in-class, do the journal entries, and work on the case study assignments in advance :)

This is both the easiest and worst class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. You will never be stressed out by the work from this class, but you will also never actively enjoy sitting through her lectures. Every time she tells you to "close your eyes/look at your feet" it just leaves you thinking "geez, I am paying thousands of dollars for this."

The reviews are spot-on this is a class a 5th grader could pass. She's cool but the content just makes my brain fog 50x worse, it can be so rudimentary and nearly confirms the HOD coloring book jokes. I show up 20 mins late to every lecture and she's still typically doing the announcements, you can walk out during most class activities/games.

If you don't get an A in this class you might actually be mentally disabled. Pretty much nothing of substance in the class, put in any amount of effort and you'll get a 95+. Dr. L is super chill too, pretty funny and doesn't care if you turn in homework late. Attendance is in theory mandatory but you can just fill out the exit ticket remotely.

THE easiest class you could ever take but you also learn valuable skills (networking, mainly). Dr. Lefkowitz is very approachable and willing to help you with outside of class things like looking for internships, prepping for interviews, etc. She's super nice and super accommodating. God's gift to Vandy tbh.

Easiest class at Vandy. She cares so much about students and I can't imagine not getting an A. A total waste of time but you only need to go once every week or two. She really is a kind soul just a joke of a class.

Don't listen to the people saying HOD2400 with Lefkowitz is useless or boring - the stuff she does teach you is very applicable and you actually learn vital life skills. Yes, the class is a little unstructured and it's honestly stupidly easy, but the passion and care she puts into teaching literally brightens my day every time I come to class.

Could not tell you a single thing about her lecturing cus I never paid attention, but she's super sweet and has a ton of personality. Class is boring as hell and pretty sure I could've passed it in fifth grade, but she injects a lot of fun and quirkiness into it.

Professor Lefkowitz is an angel, so caring about students and invested in their success. Reads papers personally and loves to talk about them in office hours. If youre confused about what your life purpose is, this course is for you. Some of the class activities can seem a bit trivial, but I had fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a gem. This course focuses on intangibles that are invaluable in the real world. There is minimal work. Take her class if possible.

Very easy class. Although its very useless too - made me question why I decided to major in HOD. All we did was making lists of random companies and alumni names, making posters of kinds of lives we wanted to live, etc. I almost thought I was still in middle school. This class shouldnt exist. She never responds to email or slack either.

Prof. L is very sweet, but so boring. She talks about the same really simple concepts every lecture for hours (when they could be explained in 10 minutes). The class is easy, but all I really got out of it was how to contact people on Linked In. Be prepared to count down the minutes in this class.

Professor Lefkowitz is incredibly sweet and very quirky in the best way. She loves her students so much and will always be available outside of office hours. I will say the class was very boring (and very skippable) and could have been condensed into a 2-week crash course. I'm not sure if I learned anything but her energy was phenomenal.

Prof L is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She cares about her students and wants you to do well. During the year I would leave class and be confused why we spent class doing what seemed to be random things but it ended up being a very impactful and useful class for me to prepare and improve my professional self.

I had Professor Lefkowitz for one of my capstone internship classes. I absolutely loved her!! She is so funny, caring, and relatable. She is also super aware of how busy students are (e.g., each module included instructions for those "short on time"). An easy A. She was definitely born to teach! Like a friendly, fun mom.
Awesome and very caring professor. I would definitely recommend to anyone at Vanderbilt. Took it online but the Prof L was still engaging and kind
Professor L is the sweetest! Her voice is so peaceful and calming and she offers a lot of wisdom. Some assignments are tedious but all is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: LOVE PROFESSOR L! Highly recommend taking 2400 with her. She's super easy and makes class enjoyable even during covid. One of the best HOD professors imo

You have an extreme amount meaningless homework assignments every single week that includes an essay's worth of writing. Then you go to class and listen to her talk about how meaningless work negatively impacts people? In general, the class is completely unrelated to the title and nothing more than a glorified therapy session.
She is the kindest professor I've ever had. The class is really easy, and she genuinely wants to get to know every student. She gives off mom-vibes, and she is so much fun.
Absolutely take this class. Possibly the best professor and easiest class I've had at Vanderbilt. Everybody needs to experience Lefkowitz.
Fantastic teacher. She is hilarious, kind, and truly cares about the success of her students. Take this class if you can.

She's kind of a goofy woman, but so nice and so eager to help you out. Her grading criteria is pretty easy. You just need to finish the work on time. Her quizzes and journals are all about getting a lot of material down so more quantity than quality.

Class is kind of quirky but Lefkowitz is a great prof. Highly recommend going to her office hours, if you put effort into engaging with her she will give it right back. She is also a great career planning resource
My favorite professor at Vandy. So nice and cares about her students so much. Highly recommend taking any of her classes.

Such a great professor. Class is super easy, but there is weekly assignments and a couple projects that are time consuming. If you do the work with some effort, you will get an A. As a person, she is so funny, caring, and loves to help students. Take her for 2400.

Her class is the most helpful and meaningful class I've ever taken, ever. You learn so much about the working world, life after school, and skills you need to get to those places. Grades are based on things that you will need and use in the future. I recommend this class for anyone!

Professor Lefkowitz is fantastic! She makes this class very applicable to real life. I think that everyone at Vandy should have to take this course as it has changed the way I go about internships and interviews.

Lefkowitz is the nicest, most caring professor I've ever had at Vandy. She really wants her students to do well and understand the working world, even though the class is super easy and at times, tedious. HOwever, I learned a ton about internships, cover letters, and networking and found the class extremely helpful. Lefkowitz is simply the best
Papers are slightly long but the class is overall not difficult. She is one of the nicest and most accessible professors I've had.
Great teacher and great to go to for advice!!

Every math major should take a class with Chan before they graduate. He's such a sweet man and really cares about students enjoying his class and being successful. Even took us to take grad photos one day for class. Numeric itself is pretty straightforward- HW (flexible w/ extensions), 2 midterm, and a final (which could replace lowest midterm).

Professor Chan is an incredible teacher and is at his best in this class. He obviously enjoys the problem-solving techniques you learn and does a great job making lectures fun. You will need to do a decent amount of work, but grading is pretty easy and tests are fine as long as you have done the work leading up. One of the best Vandy math classes.
Dr. Chan is an amazing professor and in my opinion the best in the department! He was organized and invested and made the class really interesting. I would take any class with him!
Dr. Chan is AWESOME! Best class I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. I hope Dr. Chan gets tucked into bed by fairies every night.

Chan really redeemed statistics for me after a bad experience at my old school. Really nice professor who cares about students, will remember your name if you answer questions and go to office hours. Weekly problem sets and small Brightspace quizzes after every lecture, but overall a manageable workload. Fair exams with equation sheet allowed.

I took MATH 3010 with Professor Chan (that wasn't one of the class options on here so just putting under 2810). I can't recommend this class and professor enough. He is the best professor I've had at Vandy, and he made the class so fun.

Most poorly designed math class at Vanderbilt. I would accuse Dr. Chan for such a poor designed class. The whole class feels like a huge plug and chug. I have learned absolutely nothing from class except memorizing crazy excel formulas.

In this course, I had excused medical emergencies documented by the dean. However, this professor slyly referred me to the Math department, leading to the unnecessary involvement of university officials. Sadly, the Math department lacks empathy for medical issues. Steer clear of Vanderbilt's shady Math department.

Professor Chan is all you can ask for in a great math professor. He is highly accessible outside of class, gives great lectures, and really wants you to succeed. In addition, he is a brilliant and very nice guy. Beware of the large workload with problem sets and quizzes, but they will keep you on your game for exams. Could not recommend him enough.

Professor Chan is an excellent statistics professor, and I would 100% recommend you take his courses. His lectures are well-planned and easy to understand. The workload is fair and not overwhelming. His notes and homework assigments are posted online if you don't want to go to lecture, but lecture is lowkey and helps prepare you for exam material.

One of the best math professors I've ever had! He's a super cool and smart prof and really wants to help the students do well. Lectures are great and organized (even though the topic material isn't too interesting). Tests aren't that easy, but you'll likely be prepared if you do your homework. 
Definitely take his class if you have the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Chan is the best math teacher I ever had. He helped us understand concepts by explaining each step and color coding it. There's no curve, but one test is dropped. Prof Chan's class grade average was much higher compared to the other professors' averages, so if you decide to take calc, choose him as ur teacher--he's really good at what he does!

By far the best math professor I've ever had. He color coats the lectures and is incredibly organized. He also posts all of the lecture notes which can be very helpful if you miss a class. Only downside is there's a short quiz due every class. Tests are very fair - questions can be tricky but no dumb questions out of left field. Highly recommend.

Sweet guy! Very organized lectures, posts notes online. Tests are on the difficult side, but fair - let us replace the lowest midterm with the final. The class itself is annoyingly structured, though, with a short quiz 3 times a week on Brightspace. I would definitely recommend Prof. Chan regardless!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Beware of the Vanderbilt Math department. The math department lacks empathy and basic understanding skills (I am kinda convinced they are robots). If you have any AP credit please use it! If you can avoid taking Math 1200 I would highly suggest it. The professor does not show any empathy or caring. Would not recommend 0/10.

Dr. Chan is amazing! His lectures are color coordinated, and he moves slowly. His tests are the most fair tests I have taken in college. You are never really thrown curve balls, so preparing is straight forward. This class was so manageable and easy to do well in. TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!
really clear instruction, gives you lots of opportunities to succeed, nice and if you took calc ab in high school this is easier than that

Dr. Chan is incredible. He goes out of his way to color-code concepts and is super organized with his lectures, homework, assignments, and practice materials. He truly wants all of his students to succeed and is always willing to help. He's great at breaking down and simplifying the material. Though not required, he does appreciate participation.

Absolutely love Prof Chan! Notes on the board are color-coded and clear. If you copy everything down and make sense of it, you are well on your way to ace-ing the test. If you took HS calc, you barely have to spend time on this course. Unit tests don't trick you, but the final exam threw us off guard. Short & easy HW that can be done after class.

LOVE this man!!! Lectures are clear and color-coded. HW is due every day, but it's short and easy. No calculators. Prof Chan is exceptionally kind and caring, plus he holds multiple office hours per week. If you did not take calc in high school, you might need to go to office hours, TA, or Khan Academy for help. Otherwise an easy A and fun class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Caught people off guard by giving a super hard final. Can't believe he didn't curve it given the C- average.

If you have never taken calculus before, do not take his class. You do not actively learn from the course! He does problems on the board without explaining where things came from. Assisted office hours multiple times; however, it was not helpful. Do not expect this class to be easy, even more, when he teaches it.

All of the great reviews are true: Professor Chan is one of the best professors I have ever had at Vanderbilt. Whereas many professors don't know how to teach, Dr. Chan seems to have a real talent. He's accessible and understanding. Color codes chalkboard very well and is receptive to your input. Cannot recommend enough.
Genuinely wants to make sure you understand the material. Super helpful for visual learners: color codes everything on the chalkboard.

Dr. Chan is the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt, let alone in the Math department. Class is hard and I hate stats, but I have never had such a good lecturer. Incredible organization, 7 hours of office hours a week, and a friendly disposition with clear and consistent grading criteria. An absolute gem and I could not recommend more!

Dr. Chan's lectures are well organized and easy to follow, even if the concepts are not. Participation is expected, he will know your name and call on you if no one volunteers. Tests are tough but fair, lots of partial credit. The weekly problem sets can be time consuming, but if you keep up with them, you will be well prepared for the tests.

This man is the best professor I've ever had. He's really good at teaching difficult concepts, always available to students (replies to emails within minutes every time), and is willing to adjust grades to help students out (within reason). After we went online, he was so considerate about students' needs and made exams fair for everyone.

Professor Chan is a really nice guy and he has some of the most organized, easy to follow lectures of any math professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He does lots of examples and he makes the content really easy to understand. Homeworks are usually really long and time consuming, but nothing is really too hard.

This was a pretty hard class but he does a great job teaching the material and cares a lot about the students. The problem sets can take awhile and the exams are tough, but if you go to class, do the homework, and occasionally go to office hours you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Chan really cares about his students His lectures make hard concepts understandable and gives notes covering all the lecture material after class The problem sets and tests are reasonable and reflect what is taught on lectures I hope all Math professors I'm going to meet will be like Dr Chan

His lectures were super clear and the material was presented well. The tests are very doable and so are the homework assignments. There is a problem set due every week but it's usually not too bad. Definitely one of the better professors to take for stats

Professor Chan provides optional HW for every section, but there are mandatory weekly quizzes and problem sets that aren't too bad and honestly cushion your grade. His lectures are very clear and he uses different color chalk that makes difficult concepts easier to understand. Solid office hours, nit-picky grader, gives lots of partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Chan is a great professor. He was very helpful in office hours, and during lectures. He taught the material well and the tests weren't the most difficult, but you still need to do the homework (from textbook) to do well. The final exam was not harder than a regular test. Overall I really like Dr. Chan and I think that he was very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Chan works really hard to help students understand what is going on and is very organized in class. The tests are pretty fair honestly and he is generous with partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CHAN IS THE BEST! Lectures are super easy to follow and color-coded to make graphs and proofs more understandable. Examples given in class and through homework are very similar to those on the exams. He is also a super funny and approachable professor, definitely visited his office hours to explain certain problems. You will love him!

Chan is a decent choice for MATH1300. His lectures are not great but the tests are really not that awful compared to the other profs. Not difficult to get a decent grade if taken some effort. Overall would recommend as 1300 prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: God Awful Lecturess.

Incredibly nice guy and, although new, arguably the best MATH1300 prof. He actually cares about us doing well rather than making the tests impossible, like some other professors do. Always does his best to make class interesting

Consistently kind, eager to get to know students, clear in the grading system of Core (which can be quite confusing) and incredibly lenient on late assignments. Not a tough grader at all. Core professors can kind of be a lottery, but Makhdoumian is an absolute gem.

Dr. Makhdoumian is awesome. Discussion-based class with weekly lectures on topics that enhanced understanding of the readings. Her knowledge and passion for Native American Literature shine through in every class. Less writing-based than most English courses, but be ready for fun, interesting projects and class presentations. Take her for sure!

Professor Makhdoumian is brilliant, energetic, and very accessible. Her teaching also regularly incorporates contemporary issues. Take her class if you're looking for something meaningful without too much stress!
Great guest speakers, fun field trip at the end, and I truly learned a lot in class.

Professor Hiskey goes above and beyond to make sure that his students do well on tests (there is 1 mid-term and 1 final for testing), including holding review sessions before exams which will cover everything you need to know. The lectures may be a little tedious and boring, but he is a genuinely sweet guy who cares about his students.

Great professor made me want to go class and hear what he said. However the course material was very boring and made me not want to go. overall It was a good class and relatively easy if you just half paid attention.

Very nice guy, but the lectures are incredibly boring. He basically repeats the same information for the entire class. You will not learn anything, so there is no point in attending lectures. It's a short class, and he will spend the first 20 minutes talking about random stuff. If you go to the review session before a test, you will be perfect.

Hiskey is a fun professor, and his teaching made it an extremely easy class. He offered review sessions for both tests that covered all of the answers. The only other grade was a 3-part research assignment graded by TAs. Follow the instructions, don't have horrid grammar, and you should get full pts. There's also extra credit offered on everything.
hiskey goes on tangents during lecture and it makes them kinda boring. hes a really nice guy and project is easy points, tests arent too hard but very lecture based.

Goes on tangents during lecture and walks around answers; no point in attending class. Generally unresponsive over email and grades very arbitrarily. Clearly knowledgable at what he does but not good at teaching. If you're genuinely interested in political science do not take this class–you will come away having learned nothing.

Project points should be easy 100s, but they can take a lot of time if done correctly. Tests are tough, and lectures often feel like a waste since he rambles. Writing sections are graded very strictly under heavy time pressure. Hiskey is a very nice professor.

Really easy class, and it's really easy to get an A if you want it (just go to the review sessions). Lectures can get boring at times, but Hiskey is great and one of the more down-to-earth and understanding professors that I've taken.

Hiskey is nice, but he yaps too much. Seems to have ADHD because he will go on loooong tangents and regurgitate the same information. This makes for a boring class. Assignments were easy. Tests were alright, but they depend on how much you pay attention to his boring lectures.

Hiskey is the GOAT. This class is an automatic A if you show interest and some effort. Weekly readings were technically "required" but often not talked about/in-class discussions were flexible. Engaging guests. Only 3-4 writing assignments. Highlight was the field trips outside of class to meet immigrants and experience different cultures.

Prof. Hiskey is a very down-to-earth guy that really cares about his students. He makes the course material interesting and slideshows are available if you miss class – although you can't really skip two classes in a row without missing something big. Only one major assignment besides the exams but its separated into four parts. Would take again

I was constantly bullied by Hiskey. He has absolutely zero sympathy for people with ADHD and other learning disabilities. He constantly called me a liar and acted insulted when I asked clarifying questions. Do your mental health a favor and about Hiskey at all costs.

Despite what some reviews say, I found his lectures very engaging/interesting. He truly cares about the subject matter and his students. A 94 is an A but it is very doable. Assignments were graded fairly and the midterm + final was very doable. He provided 2-3 review sessions for both tests + offered many extra credit points throughout the semester

Dr. Hiskey is very nice and wants you to succeed. He gives engaging lectures that he also puts on Brightspace. He gives a 5-day grace period on assignments and also hands out a review sheet and hosts review sessions for both the midterm and the final. Lots of readings but I got an A after I quit reading after the midterm. Cool guy who knows a lot!

His lectures are boring and he often goes on tangents. Super nice guy and wants you to succeed but cannot(refuses) to answer questions directly. Long study guides, half of which will not be on the test. Grades kindly, offers extra credit for everything, even turning things in on time or meeting with him. I could have done better tbh

Hiskey is awesome. He is a passionate and funny lecturer, and his work/research on migration is impressive. PSCI 2252 isn't hard per se, but a 94% A is a high bar. However, Hiskey always says that you can do "as well as you want to do" in this class, which is 100% true--he is very accessible, and your grade is reflective of your effort.

Caring prof, very passionate and funny in lecture. Encourages you to think deeply about migration, rewards participation and thinking outside the box. Midterm, project, final exam. Easy grading on the exams, WANTS to give you as much credit possible. Goes out of his way to offer study sessions outside of class even on weekends. One of Vandy's best.

One of the best professors Poli Sci. He is incredibly caring and passionate about the material. Expectations are extremely clear and if you put in some work you will get an A. There are readings, but you never need to do them until the tests. He does many review sessions as well and grades easily on tests. Typically only 1 paper, midterm, + final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the nicest guys I've ever met, and it shows in his teaching style. Somewhat rigorous, reading- and lecture-heavy class, but he sets it out in a way that's manageable and rewarding. He's incredibly accessible and helpful, providing study guides, several review sessions for his exams, and even planning events where you can get EC.

Professor Hiskey is a great teacher. I am confused why his ratings are not higher. Only a midterm and a final and two papers. Not a harsh grader and gives very clear criteria. Tests come from a list of questions given before and he does review sessions. If you go to office hours it is easy to get an A on the papers. He is very passionate and kind.

3 big papers and a few readings every week, grades easily though and if you go to office hours he will like you. Sometimes he gets a little off topic in the lectures but nothing ridiculous. I am taking his class again next sem

Funny and great professor that does his best to make the material interesting and show its real world applications. His stories are interesting and serve to supplement the course material, and the material itself isn't too difficult. He often goes on tangents, but these are some of the best parts of class and are always fun to listen to.

Hiskey is very sweet and cares about his students a lot. He is really accessible to students despite being the department chair, which I appreciated a lot, and held many review sessions to ensure our mastery of the material. However, lectures were generally boring & a lot of the material was extremely dry. Grades are based on 2 tests and 1 project.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The Politics of Mexico lectures were wildly boring. Like so boring. He would repeat the same main ideas, in the same words, every single class. I'm not sure what other people found funny about him because that certainly was not the impression I got. INCREDIBLY hard exams, grades project really harshly as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hiskey is one of the coolest professors in the department. He genuinely cares about his students and their success and is always happy to help in office hours. I took his Latin American Politics class this semester and am taking another class with him next semester because I had so much fun!

Professor Hiskey is hilarious. He's warm, friendly, and sees his students as more than just bodies in seats. He tends to go on tangents. Some might feel like this is a negative thing, but I felt like I learned just as much through these "off-topic" discussions as I did through the organized lecture component. He's one of my favorite professors.

I am fascinated by Latin American politics as someone who has studied abroad there and taken multiple classes on the region. However, this class makes me lose all interest with his mindnumbing lectures where rambles for an hour and fifteen minutes and covers literally 2 slides. Everything I learned was by myself and outside of class.

This was a class on refugees and Professor Hiskey helped make it extremely interesting and inspirational. He is a super nice person and was available to meet outside of class, even on short notice outside office hours, and really cared about his students.

Hiskey ROCKS. His class is tough, don't get me wrong, but he makes the material interesting and accessible. Study hard for the midterms and final, and if you aren't satisfied with your grades, go in and see him--he will help you out. Overall, he is an amazing, funny lecturer, and his class singlehandedly changed my academic trajectory.

Hiskey rocks. Took Latin American Politics- lectures were pretty detailed, but he did an amazing job of bringing the material to life and made it all very tangible. It also helps that he's hilarious. Big group project and research paper, plus midterm and final. Grades based on understanding of content showing that you've read. but awesome prof!
Not an easy course.
His key is the reason I pursued my current career! 10 years later his politics of Mexico class was by far my most useful later in life.  Pay attention and approach him if you have any questions!
Hiskey is the man. He's funny and makes mexican politics not too bad. State Project is hard, but if you go to office hours he will help. I recommend taking him.

Such a good guy! Has a serious sense of humor.  I didn't find his grading hard and he'll always give partial credit. Go to class and ask questions but DON'T DO THE READINGS. The answers to all his test prep questions are in the powerpoints, you just have to read them!
The class has a pretty intense reading list. Hiskey's a nice guy though and he's really helpful outside of class. He's a hard paper grader, but his tests weren't that bad.

He's a nice guy but you're going to have to deal with his occasionally passive aggressive humor, overly-detailed and extremely dry powerpoint slides, insanely long reading assignments, and his difficult exams which often run over class time. Do the reading because he's going to expect you to write in a detail about it on the tests. Not an easy A!
Very nice guy.  Very unspecific in what he wants on the paper and grades it tough.  Midterm and final are not too bad if you study.  He doesn't care if you go to class or not.

Very knowledgeable, rambles a bit in lectures, a bit unclear about expectations, very helpful and sincere outside of class. If you do most of the readings, ask for help on the projects, and try to remember key concepts, you can make a high B to an A. In general, the class is informative and somewhat interesting.
GO TO CLASS...do more than a superficial reading...take notes...visit office hours...make sure he KNOWS who you are...

Professor Hiskey is personally a great guy, but somewhat of a rambler in lectures.  He will take 30 minutes to make a point he could make in 5.  His homework/reading list is the most demanding I've ever seen.  Still, you can study his outlines and sail through his exams if you're careful.

SUCH a nice guy! Pretty laid back as far as work and reading goes... assigns the bare minimum. Gives review questions and sessions before exams. Definately try to start a little early for the project. He is fair and wants to get to know the students. A+ for Hiskey :)
No Comments

Prof. Lomeli refuses to take into account that the world is not dictated by his own belief system. There is a right and wrong answer in this class to subjective material. For example, a student specified her opinion over a topic and he went on to imply her opinion is wrong. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Lomeli is an amazing professor, who genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Though his class has a lot of reading, we do discussions to make sure everything is digestible. He's available outside of class to talk about assignments, or to give advice on grad school/next steps. He's really an amazing guy.

He's a nice guy but needs improvement as a professor. Vague feedback and a tough grader. I believe a class that that is introductory should be introducing students to the topic, however, it felt as though you were expected to already know material.
Very vague, unorganized, and not structured. His feedback did not help my writing at all and he seemed to never improve on that.

Professor Lomeli tries his best but just needs to improve the structure of the class and clear grading rubrics as well as schedules. This class is more concentrated on academic writing and sometimes reading heavy. Although, he is open to suggestions from students needs more structure overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I was excited to come into this class, but Lomeli quickly changed that. The combination of his constant interruption of students, vague feedback, slow grading time, insane amount of reading and responses (for a 1000 level course), and tendency to have dull readings made this course unlikeable. He is a newer prof, but needs a LOT of improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: No structure to the class, and way too much reading/writing for a first-year writing seminar. He does not provide rubrics but grades very specifically and in particular of what he wants. He is a nice person but needs improvement as a professor.

Hilario is very passionate about the subject and cares about his students! However, there were many instances when feedback was unclear, the class was somewhat unstructured, and there was a lot of reading. He is always available to meet and wants you to succeed. Overall, great guy but needs improvement and time as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved how she lead class discussions, super engaging and sharp. Also approachable. I liked the class more than I thought I would (it's a requirement). Highly recommend!

Not a very smart professor. She gave me some of the worst advice on essay writing I've ever received. She can go on really interesting tangents and also puts people on the spot. Sometimes class is entertaining (mostly because of the interesting debates she has with students), and sometimes it is the most boring class I've ever taken. Easy class.
She is lovely!!!!!! Must take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Hill is so sweet & shines in seminar-style classes. Be ready to read multiple novels per week. Major downside is the complete lack of grading. Heading into finals week, not a single grade was posted, leaving students uncertain of their standing. Also, course content doesn't align w/ description; review syllabus before registering if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hill can go off on tangents, but she is passionate and knowledgeable. You can get by on skimming readings and participating once a class. Most of the readings are interesting and easy to understand/available in English. She also grades the tests easily if you mention a few specifics from the reading. By far the best lit class/professor.

There was lots of homework for this writing seminar, but most of it was reading books, which I actually enjoyed. The in class discussions were compelling, she does a very good job of letting the students steer discussion while maintaining a focus each day. One of my favorite professors thus far at Vandy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Hill is an amazing professor. The readings she chooses really make you think about the world around you, and her in-class lectures and discussions are both entertaining and fascinating. The class was graded by 6 pop in-class essays plus participation and a final paper, but she grades generously and makes sure everyone always speaks in class.
Nice lady but super boring lectures, exams start easy but get very hard, even with studying, I would only take in the future if the class is necessary, homework is really easy though

Repeatedly stressed that all notes were available on Brightspace only for her to provide a few bullet points. For the final she gave us 10 practice problems with no answer key. I learned all of the content with YouTube videos in a fraction of the time it took to decipher a few of her slideshows.

Annoying trap assignments posted at random times with no flexablity or extra chances to do them. No curve/ extra credit is offered and her or the TA's are extremely nitpicky on the tests. Yes the class is easy conceptually but I got messed up by her grading and class organization.

Very nice professor. Grading is a little weird, though, because each question is worth a lot of points, and you have to get everything right to get points for it (all or nothing for points). She also took off points on the project which made me get a B+ even though I was at an A- after the final. Very frustrating.
Best class for 1st semester, challenging midterms but remote final. worth it.

Who the heck said this is an easy class? I got cooked. If you're not interested in econ, you will be bored out of your mind, and exams won't come easily. Workload is a piece of cake, but exams suck. Don't take this if you aren't actually interested in econ. Not really her fault, though, so I would still take her for econ if I had to take the class.
Pretty easy class if you study for tests. The final was completely remote. Engaging lectures and explains things clearly. Moves a little fast sometimes.
Good lectures, could sometimes get boring due to easy content. Will get an A if you go to class and do assignments. Most of grade comes from exams, but they are similar to homework.
Great lecturer, most kids won't get an A but it is very feasible. Tests are easy if you understand the material, no tricks.
Luea is a good professor. Margin for error in ECON 1010 is not big because the exams are often graded harshly, but it is not very hard to get an A if you put in the work.

Dr. Luea was by far my favorite professor this semester. Her lectures are clear and engaging. She makes it very clear what will be on the 2 midterms and cumulative final. Though attendance isn't required, she sometimes gives attendance extra credit points. Please take!

do not underestimate this class! tests are pretty difficult, but not impossible! luea is amazing and such a nice professor. there was a +1 point extra cred for attendance for a random class in november! the final exam is a take home online test. YOU NEED TO DO GOOD ON THE MIDTERM TO GET AN A.

Luea is a very sweet lady, but if you didn't take econ in high school, you might be cooked. Your grade is almost entirely based on exams, so bombing one test can kill an A. Lectures are packed and the study material often differs from exams. Take detailed notes, go to office hours for points back, The class average is a B+, so don't expect an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Subject material is relatively easy and Dr. Luea is a very sweet person and teacher. However, her grading is very strict. You cannot afford to make any small mistakes as partial credit is basically non-existent. Make sure to go to office hours after an exam as you will probably end up getting a good amount of points back.
don't believe the ratings here the average grade is b+ intentionally. don't do it for requirements

Huge lectures, but a very easy class with a very relaxed professor. You don't really need to go to class because all the material is on the slideshows and the textbook, but it will help your grade if you do.

Such a wonderful professor. Intro-level huge econ lecture should be horrible, but it wasn't because she's so awesome! She engages with her students during the lecture, is incredibly skilled at explaining complex topics, and is obviously very passionate and knowledgeable.  You can't find a better Econ 1010 class in the country.
Would reccomend for intro micro. Is also an easy class for SBS AXLE

My favorite proffessor!!! This semester she had a family emergency/personal matter and remained accessible for all students. Wants her students to succeed. Looked at my notes after the first exam and helped me make a plan to do better. Keeps lectures interesting with real life examples and she has a great sense of humor.

A lot of her grade really revolves around simple stuff. The class is pretty test heavy, like there's 3 exams and it counts for a lot of your grade. You have a project and homework grade which are fodder and should be 100s. She is just restating what is in her lectures and she expands on the lectures whenever there is a graph.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sweet person but her lectures just didn't help at all. Make sure to attend office hours after a test otherwise you're gonna get points off despite having the correct answers. You cannot afford to miss any homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not many grade opportunities. Also special treatment to some students who she has a relationship with (unfair test corrections for extra credit). Nice person just not a good professor.

Do not take. She does not have any respect for her students. She cancels class and office hours often. 90% of your grade comes from tests, and the short response can be tricky and often graded harshly. Office hours are packed - and she will not let you meet with her one on one. Also, the athletes get points back and are able to do test corrections

DOES NOT help students. The homework and exam review questions are NOTHING like the exams. She canceled class too many times this semester and does not give enough time to work on the final exam. She is also unfair and gives extra credit opportunities to her "favorite" students. Ask her about her letting athletes do test corrections.

Professor Luea is very knowledgeable and clearly passionate about economics. The class is a little more difficult if you don't have a background taking ECON in high school but it's manageable if you keep yourself on track. She is very caring and makes sure her students succeed.
Super easy course, and super easy teacher. Classes were really boring, though; I hardly ever went. You only really need to study the day before an exam.
Hoarah Loux is my favorite econ professor shes honestly really great.

Decent class. Lectures skim over material, but that's to be expected from large classes. Highly recommend to at least skim over textbook for tests. Gives extra credit opportunities, and tests are almost entirely MCQ.
Very sweet, the material is easy enough, attendance is optional but I'd recommend attending because she often went over the homeworks or projects in class.
few tests, not too bad, zero attendence, and relatively simply material

Dr. Luea really tries but she is not a very engaging lecturer. She makes expectations very clear. Go to class and take advantage of the attendance points. It is not that difficult to do well in her class but you do need to study for exams, especially for content later on. Her office hours are helpful and she's super sweet if you do everything.

Professor Luea is straightforward with her expectations, this can make it easy to follow but also can be a little inflexible. Her tests are clear and she is knowledgeable. But her lectures are not engaging and she is not the best in terms of teaching in a way that helps students grasp concepts. She offers no extra credit besides maybe one point.

This course has a light workload, and exams are not crazy difficult. On average, I put in 1.5 hours of work a week, which is why I received an A- and not an A. However, Luea's lectures are unbelievably boring and hard to follow, so you should be prepared to teach yourself much of the material. I wouldn't actively avoid her if you need 1010 or 1500.

No prior econ experience but lightest class ever. 4 tests, 6 hws, and no final. Occasionally gave attendance extra credit points. Never met w/ her outside of class but didn't need to - study the slides and you'll be fine. Attendance not required by sometimes will slip in info not on slides that will be on tests. Easy A and highly recommend.

Luea is kind, but it is such a big lecture class so it can be very boring. The textbook is helpful for some content but also covers stuff we don't learn. The homeworks and the project are free points. The four exams are all on paper. You would be fine if you took econ in high school, but you have to put more effort in if you didn't. Nothing amazing

Very sweet prof but lectures can be so boring that they're hard to follow. The textbook can be really helpful for concepts, but include things we don't talk about all in class. She gives barely any practice problems, which makes it difficult to prepare for tests even though the tests are pretty easy. If you're familiar with econ, you should be fine

Definitely take her if you can! One of the highlights of the econ department! Class is pretty easy especially with a background in stats. Small part of grade was attendance. Tests were pretty easy, and she tries to help your grade out as much as possible.
Professor Luea is very nice and a great teacher. She engages with the class and loves participation.
Luea loves her alcohol. Margarita stands as her favorite economic example. The class is fine overall, though, and not hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Luea is easy to follow along and the course is easy to pick up because of it. There is little homework and it is not bad when there is.

Good lecturer and she is super nice and easy to get a hold of. Also very reasonable with grading. Class is structured slightly difficult so make sure that you put effort into all of your homework assignments, labs, and project, and definitely go to class.
Very organized, expectations and materials are made very accessible. Not a ton of work, but you will learn and have to study.

Luea does not explain the concepts clearly in lectures, and I often left class more confused than when I came in. The exams are really unclear and don't reflect what's taught. There are barely any practice problems, so you're mostly left to teach yourself. If you're someone who needs structure or clear instruction, I would not recommend this class.

Very nice woman, but tends to talk in circles occasionally. 4 exams which aren't extremely difficult. Generally a pretty simple, enjoyable class so long as you are interested in the subject. Overall, not bad.

Professor Luea is a kind professor, but due to the large nature of lecture-type classes, it's a little harder to understand what's going on if you don't already have a background in Macro. However, she is easily accessible and will always stay behind after class to answer questions or walk you through a concept.

If you know macro this is a piece of cake. Lectures are long and hard to understand, not the environment for questions, but a fair amount of the grade is a guarantee via take home work and a group project. Lots of learning on your own.

Luea is a really kind professor. She gives extra credit throughout the semester. She also prepares you sufficiently and has very reasonable tests; all the questions are based on topics in class. Midterms typically have 20-25 mcq for 75 points, so each question is worth a lot. If you do well on midterms, you'll be fine. The final project is easy.

Prof. L was terrific. Her lectures were always clear and posted for download, her tests were fair, and she made econ engaging! Her office hours were frequent and helpful (though TA's were unreliable). She assigns textbook reading, but it's TOTALLY unnecessary. The tests are all based on what she says in class, so GO TO CLASS. All in all, great!

Don't take this course unless it's literally required for you. Not worth it. She is not good at 300 person lectures, and she and the course are genuinely so boring and content is not remotely related to anything that someone who wants to major in econ is thinking about unless you care about tax policy. she's a nice person and prob best for 1010 tho

This is a VERY easy class. Because this is a principles class, most of the material is intuitive. The exams are the only thing you even have to remotely worry about and even those were easy. The quizzes were take-home and asynchronous, and the final project only took an hour or two to complete. She is also just a very nice and approachable person.

Dr. Luea is very nice and accommodating. She wants everyone in her class to succeed and does everything she can to ensure this. There is an easy homework assignment once or twice a week, a group project for the final and 3-4 midterm tests. If you study a little bit for the tests you should be good.

Dr. Luea is very nice and a decent lecturer. Each class is a lecture (which are sometimes too fast) and there is an easy homework assignment once or twice a week. If you study a little bit for the tests you should be fine.

It's hard to keep a room of 300 students engaged during lectures, but Professor Luea tries her best. In my experience, she's also been very kind to all her students and is always willing to help. As long as you go to class or even just review the slides she posts, the class is an easy A.

Take Luea if at all possible. Her lecturing was very strong, and exams were very easy and she offered plenty of easy points. Super nice and relates to students pretty well. Exams were graded reasonably quickly and she was extremely reliable.

Boring lectures but thats true for any big class. Attendance def not mandatory as she posts all slides but simply going to class should give you an A. She has EC, HW, and a project to boost your grade. She almost always ends class early for questions. 3/4 midterm exams were online with very little monitoring... overall solid intro course

Luea's lectures were sometimes boring but in all fairness, it was difficult to project to a room of 300 people. Overall she was pretty good at explaining concepts.
