She assigns a project that boosts your grade and despite exams being 60% of your grade, the tests are often online and unfortunately academic dishonesty is rampant with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While her lectures may be boring, she was very caring toward her students and made the class do-able. Her exams were hard if you dont study but the homeworks and quizzes were a breeze. Theres also a group project that boosts your grade a ton and she does extra credit.
If you show up to class, it's an easy A. For those who show up and are attentive, she is great and willing to help.
Professor Luea was a solid teacher, not really above or below average, but was good enough to convey the material effectively.
A great person, not a great professor. Overcomplicates easy topics and goes over the easy things too much while overlooking the harder topics.
She got injured my semester and was all Zoom lectures. Just a few exams that are not too bad if you study the material and lectures. She is fun and class isn't bad for macro.

Dr. L is a sweet lady, however her lectures are drawn out and she has trouble making them interesting and connecting to students. Just info - dumps a bunch of info on you for an hour and a half. She does understand what she's talking about and is knowledgeable. I wish she was clearer & better at exam-prep. She's also very strict about the syllabus.
Professor Luea is a caring instructor who makes macro easy to understand. Lectures are informative, and the textbook is optional if you attend class. Unstuck AI was a lifesaver for exam prep.
boooooooooo

Dr. Luea is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had at vandy. She truly cares about supporting her students. I found her class to be enjoyable but to be fair she broke her foot so we were remote a bunch and had two open note exams. Definitely study but I'd def recommend taking her!

Class should be an easy A... if you commit the time and energy. She doesn't give enough practice problems, which is detrimental when it comes to the exams. Very boring lecturer, can't help that she was out for 1/4 of the semester. Is a really sweet person, and very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ok so I messed up pretty bad in this class. Luea is really nice, but she's not super easy per se. I took this for AXLE credit and I am not Econ or math minded at all and it shows. I didn't always go to class and I really struggled on the tests even after studying. If youre not a math person, you really need to go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Luea is genuinely such a sweet and down-to-earth woman--the type of professor who makes you fall in love with econ. As a STEM major, econ is often counterintuitive, but Luea does a great job breaking down content into digestible pieces. Class is pretty easy--4 in-class (non-cumulative) exams and one final project (super easy). Office hours = good.

Professor Luea really cares about her students, makes her office hours available and wants her students to succeed. Not that you need office hours, the class is really easy. Lectures drag on a bit, but you can zone out and still do just fine as long as you study for tests, which are the majority of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Luea is a sweet, funny, and passionate teacher. I was lucky to take macro with her. She gave clear lectures which make topics understandable. There's a textbook but you only have to read it if you don't go to class. Just go to ever class and take notes and it's an A. She's very available and clearly cares about the sucess of her students.

She is the sweetest professors, and I loved the way that she explains things, she talks through things very well. If you do the work, you can easily get an A in this class, I just didn't put in the work,

Prof. Luea is super caring but her lectures are long and boring. Her slides are easy to understand, but the textbook is way too complicated and wordy. Graded based on three exams - every question on the exam is worth a lot so you can only get very few wrong to get an A. Harder than expected.

Professor Luea was a great professor. Her lecture slides were posted beforehand, and she followed the textbook in a way that made the class easy to progress. Absolutely zero complaints, macroeconomics is a worthwhile class and easy A.

While seemingly a very sweet and compassionate person, I did not enjoy her class. The lectures were non-engaging and held little value in my understanding.
I thought I knew the material super well, but did extremely poorly on my first exam of the year (there are ONLY three) which completely killed my grade, despite acing the next two exams.

Professor Luea is a very good lecturer who clearly explains challenging concepts from the textbook. She is incredibly caring and wants her students to succeed. Attendance is not mandatory but crucial to succeeding on the midterms (she mentions what will be on exams in class). Office hours are helpful but not necessary to success.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Luea is the best! She is super approachable and presents material in a way that makes sense. The content is not difficult if you do the readings and can stay awake in class. The exams are all 25 question multiple choice with no partial credit, so make sure you know what is going on. If you try in this class, you will do well.

Dr. Luea is super kind and caring. Content is easy, but every question you get off on a test is ~1% off your total grade. Do the HW. Participating in lecture means extra credit. Dr. Luea is always available, and office hours are beyond helpful. Lectures feel lengthy because content isn't engaging, but Dr. Luea presents it quite well.

She's very nice and passionate about stats, but the class itself is so boring, especially when it's a TH class. Her exams are online and pretty fair. Your grade gets boosted by short homework assignments and labs, but you can only get a few questions wrong and still get an A, which is a 94. She's also pretty strict on grading short answer questions

Would definitely recommend taking classes with Luea if possible. She makes lecture very engaging and understands what it is like to be a student. Most of the grades in the class are comprised of tests, but the tests are not too challenging and there are occasional extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.

ECON 1010 was a pretty boring class, but Dr. Luea did as much as she could to make it entertaining. The class itself is mainly graded on three exams. The first two are pretty hard and taken in class. The last test (final) was a take home which I think saved everyones grades. I would recommend this class if it is needed to fill a requirement.

Prof. Luea is one of the best lecturers in the Econ department at Vanderbilt. She makes the lectures fun by referencing real events (like the Barbie movie), is a good speaker, and cares about her students. Offered extra credit when the class tanked the 2nd exam. However, the grading is only based on 3 exams (HWs don't count for much).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 1010 is a dreadful class. Nevertheless, Luea does not make it any better. Her lectures are fine. They get the job done and the material is clear. However, the tests are quite short for the content covered and each question is weighted extremely heavily. If you have to take her for 1010 I wouldn't be worried, but certainly not excited.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not good at giving lectures. Gets off topic often
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super chill class, I skipped tons of lectures and still able to succeed despite 0 prior econ knowledge. All you have to do to do well on exams is do the readings & practice questions. final was online, open book, open note.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Luea is super caring and easily accessible. Always has office hours for students and made our final online and open note.

Prof Luea is one of the best Econ profs at Vandy. She is a great lecturer and super helpful. The class moves pretty fast and is hard to make up points for if you do badly on one midterm (everything is multiple choice). Really intelligent and cares about her students.

insanely difficult to reach outside of class; she is condescending towards you if you do not quickly understand the topic. I have emailed her multiple times to discuss content, but she never goes over it. in addition, the condescending attitude she portrays make me not want to engage outside of the class; virtually impossible to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'll be honest and say that I struggled a bit more than I expected to in this class. The content is easy, but I hated using Tophat with a passion. Luea is super friendly and kind, decent lecturer. But Tophat made me struggle. Some might disagree with me and that's totally ok, the content really wasn't that hard. I would suggest Luea as a teacher.

Luea is a good professor and tries to make the lectures interesting, but the class is just so boring. Test 1 was easy, but there's a massive jump between then and Test 2, so it's really easy to fall behind and stop caring until it's too late. It seems like every other ECON 1010 professor sucks though, so Luea's your best bet.

She was a great prof overall. Her lectures are funny and relatable. When studying, definitely focus on lecture material as there is a lot of unnecessary extra stuff covered in the textbook, but the textbook is a good review. Homework is minimal and manageable and she usually goes over it in class before it's even due.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a lecturer she's very helpful, and has a lot of open office hours, but I didn't appreciate her grading scale. You have to get a 95 to get an A, which turns out to be 5 questions wrong for the entire semester. While her tests aren't the hardest, you quite literally can't afford to miss a question here or there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Disclaimer: Class taken online over the summer, possibly done differently during regular semesters

Professor Luea is an excellent professor and did exceptionally well at being clear in her class requirements in an online workspace. She made herself very available outside of class and was fair in her testing of textbook, lecture and "lab" material.

Probably one of the best professors in the econ department. She has very simple lectures that are easy to follow. She gives you more than enough practice for her exams. Her exams were very straightforward and repetitive. To prep, sometimes she gave out test problems from previous years. Doing those was the most helpful for me.

Professor Luea is great! I truly enjoyed this course. Even though it was a summer course for me, only 4 weeks, I did so well in this class. She sends clear objectives and goals weekly and ensures that the assignment list is clear. The class time is very engaging and Professor Luea talks to you instead of at you.

Show up to class, take notes, and do the practice questions on TopHat for an A (which is a 95). Also gives 1% extra credit 2x per semester if you show up to class -- and given that an A is a 95, it's a big deal. Not a difficult course.
Super nice teacher. She was actually personable and enjoyed having her as a professor. Take her if she's an option for a professor. One annoying thing is that you need a 95 for an A.
Dr. Luea is a great intro professor.  Definitley worth a class. Easy grades, just put in the work outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Your entire grade is three exams and homeworks. Homeworks are super easy, and she does a good job of making things easy to understand. Tests are not bad at all, but the material is pretty boring. I would recommend her if you need to take this class, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, but terribly boring. My lecture was at 9am so I didn't go, I just did the tophat readings and homeworks. The exams are straightforward, but you'll still need to study. The reality of 1020 is that the material isn't real in the reality of the way our economy actually works, but you'll need to treat it as truth to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Luea is super good. Definitely take her if you can. 95 for an A and the tests can be a little hard, but she really cares. She made the final open note. Gave extra credit. If you show up and pay attention, she's actually a really good teacher who really cares.
Made final open note; easy quick hw; read textbook or attend lectures; go to office hours in person; caring; cancelled class a couple times; some of material is difficult; love her
Great teacher. Super nice. Trick questions on exams. And 95 % being a A is ridiculous.

Dr.Luea really does her best to keep students engaged in the material. She's very good at explaining the concepts and also very caring about student wellbeing. Content is pretty straightforward, if you have any AP Stats or intro stats experience you'll know at least half the material. Unlimited tries for homework and all the tests are predictable.

Prof Luea is very nice and teaches well. The tests are practically impossible if you don't have accomodations though. The questions are made to trick you and the tests take up practically your whole class grade so be prepared

Prof. L, is an exciting and knowledgable professor. If you attend lectures and pay attention you will do fine. Extra credit helps a lot and as long as you get high A grades on everything else, you should do well. Exams are difficult, but that's just because the final is open-note take-home and the other two make up like 30% of your grade. Take her.

if you have to take econ stat, take luea. easiest by a mile (other profs don't let you use reference tables of any kind, so you have to memorize the long formulas) and she gives extra credit for attendance sometimes. an A is a 95 w/ her but i'm not even an econ major and it took minimal work. also, her final is non-cumulative :)

Best professor for Econ Stats by a mile. Class itself is very straightforward and you will always know what is expected of you. Work outside of class is minimal. Tests can be challenging but if you understand the equations you will be fine. Very good lecturer as well.

As she said, her first-year writing seminar is the "chillest" you can find at Vandy. Very caring prof. As long as you (for most of the time) attend her lectures and participate in discussions, you are almost impossible to get below A. Three papers and several journal entries throughout the semester, very manageable.

Not sure why her rating is only a 3.5. This class was very straightforward and she gave all the tools necessary to succeed. Exams were surprisingly tough but the rest of the class was very manageable. Also gives out lots of extra credit for attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Luea was a great professor and truly cared a lot about her students' success in this class. If you need to take Econ Stat, you need to take it with Luea. There was only 3 exams, all not cumulative, and the final exam was open-notebook and remote. I suggest going to class since she sometimes gave extra credit when many kids didn't show up.

Professor Luea is one of the best professors I have had. Do the labs and quizzes ON TIME & you will get tons of 100s in the grade book. Her lectures are easy to understand & I recommend taking notes... she tells you everything you need to know. Also, the textbook is helpful. Tests are difficult but if you study & pay attention you will be fine.
Homework and lab are easy points since she goes over them in class. Tests arent hard especially if u took ap stats. Overall, fairly simple class. Didnt attend class ever and did fine

Professor Luea's FYWS was a class that I always looked forward to attending. She is extremely layed back in this class and makes it almost impossible to not get an A assuming you show up and turn in your assignments. Essentially, you work on one big paper all year that you gradually add to over time. Would highly reccomend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Luea is easily my favorite professor at Vandy. She is such a caring, sweet person and genuinely cares about the success of every student. The grade is based on only a few things, but they are quite doable if you pay attention and study. She is great. I wish she taught more classes.

Our class was very large and online, and she was still very accessible in and outside of class. Her expectations are clear and she's very straightforward about what you do and do not need to know. Didn't develop any sort of relationship with her and her voice was a little monotone, but I got through the class easily enough and got an A.

Very helpful in answering all questions, communicates course material effectively. There are 3 tests with questions just like the homework, and the homework assignments and lab activities are basically free points

Overall a pretty easy class, Luea is very straightforward and is clear on how things will be graded. Going to class is not mandatory but I would then read the textbook. Grade cutoff for an A is high but it is not a difficult class. Lectures can get dry but are helpful

Professor Luea is really clear with her grading and expectations. I think she's the best professor to take ECON 1500 with, but I do think the textbook was definitely a lot more helpful than her lectures. Keep in mind there are only three tests, so one test grade can dramatically change your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Luea is the best! I had her for macro and econ stat and the classes were structured the exact same. Very straightforward and the math is pretty simple with a bit of practice. Very clear and structured lectures. Beware the cutoff for an A is a 95% so be careful to double check exams before turning them in. Otherwise very nice class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super easy class and a super nice prof. She responds quickly and is really accessible and helpful even outside of class. Very understanding. Lectures are clear and easy to follow and the textbook is also helpful. Tests and quizzes are decently easy if you study a bit or just have common sense. Recommend as an easy class.

No, the tests and homeworks arent hard if you read the book and do practice. But macro isnt the easy A everyone promises- you actually have to try. She is not understanding for extra credit or work, and your grade is totally based on 3 exams with no wiggle room. Shes friendly but the class requires outside work and is extremely dry.

Just as with ECON1020 and ECON1010, Prof. Luea is hands down the most organized professor I've had at Vanderbilt. Her syllabus is clear, and you know precisely how you must perform on all the assignments to achieve a desired grade. If you pay attention and revise before exams, you should be fine. Fair warning: the cutoff for an A is a 95 w/ Luea.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her class was straightforward and not too hard if you read the textbook and pay attention to lectures. The tests are high stakes, but if you put in effort you should be fine.

Good professor. Not sure how she is in person, but asynch econ 1010/1020/1500 were all manageable, not too difficult, and her recorded lectures are helpful. Considering how many students she had, she did a good job overall.
She's a really solid professor. I have no clue how she managed to have 100s of kids and still respond to emails pretty quickly.

Professor Luea definitely cares about students. 16 assignments throughout the semester (she drops 2) and 3 tests (no cumulative final). 95% cutoff for an A makes it a little bit tough, especially since tests only have 25 questions each, but Luea is a great choice for ECON 1010.

Pr. Luea gives us the information we need to succeed and was willing to help outside of class whenever I needed clarification on the course material. She did a good job with Econ stats in getting us ready for Econometrics

Assignments were pretty easy, multiple attempts on homework and labs so getting 100% on them is very attainable. Only three tests so an A is tough to get, definitely requires studying for each test. Accessible through emails, office hours, or asking questions at the end of class. Understanding and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this in the fall of '20 after taking AP Macro in HS so this class was pretty easy, especially with open-note tests. Got an A by watching lectures, reading chapters, and doing review problems before the 3 exams. The class can be mostly self-paced since lectures are recorded but I tried going to live ones often. Would recommend Luea to anyone.

Professor Luea has really improved. I've taken several classes with her and she is much more engaged and willing to help now than a few years ago. Her tests are only 25 multiple choice questions which is tough because you need a 95 for an A, but they are pretty easy. She sticks to the basics and teaches clearly w/o tricking you on tests and hw.
I love everything about her classes!!!!!
As long as you follow up with the course content and do all the homework an A is very easy to get.

If you've taken AP stats before, you can practically sleep through this class and still get an A. Homework takes max 10 minutes, Luea basically does the labs for you, and the tests are almost exactly like the hw questions. Lectures can be dry, but she does care for her students and is very accessible outside of class.

If you've taken AP Stats, this class is basically the same thing with Excel instead of a TI-84 (the downside being you won't take much away from the class). Professor Luea is caring and makes learning Excel doable. The workload is very manageable. Grades are based on quizzes and labs, which can be attempted multiple times, and 3 tests.
Prof Luea is the cool mom prof, in a good way. Tough grading scale, but assignments and labs are a boost.
Very organized.

Easy content (basically AP stats with like two more concepts and learning excel basics) that's made uncreainably difficult by the cutoff being 95% for an A. That means out of the 25-point tests, you can get two questions wrong each as a maximum, which is easy to do in MCQs. Bland teaching style too, I just watched recorded lectures at 2x speed

Idk why Prof. Luea's rating is so low, she is such an amazing teacher! Econ1010 was such an easy class in terms of homework and tests, but I also felt that I learned a lot through the textbook and lectures. A real win-win. She also is great with the online format! 100% am trying to take more classes with her.

As long as you read the textbook and listen to lectures, class is relatively easy. There were three tests with 25 multiple choice questions each, two mini projects, and hw assignments that Luea allowed 3 tries to complete. The only downside is that an A is a 95%, but other than that, Luea was super kind in answering questions and helping students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Take her for an easy A! She is the sweetest professor and gives minimal homework. The "homework" is 5 Multiple choice questions that you get 3 chances to take. Tests were also pretty straightforward as long as you're up to date on the material. Luea is an angel.

Pretty simple and easy class. Prof Luea genuinely cares about the students and accommodates them. Show up to class, finish the readings, do the homework that requires minimum hard work, and you are set for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super nice professor and made really helpful adjustments to the class in light of COVID. I really appreciated how organized the course was and how clear her expectations were.

Prof Luea is a genuinely nice person, but oftentimes made the course content more confusing. Just read the textbook and you'll be fine. Grade is made up of tests, homework, and two mini-projects which take 5 min to do. Homework is super easy and you get three attempts per homework. Tests are not too bad if you read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Luea did a good job explaining concepts, but read the textbook for extra background that will help. Not too much hw, but the 3 exams basically determine your grade. If you go to lectures, do the hw, and read the textbook you should be good. She is always available to answer questions too. Good class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Luea was a great professor that explained things well. Not too much of a hw load, but make sure you read the textbook if you don't go to lectures. If you took AP stats in high school, this class should be pretty easy.
You'll do alright unless you procrastinate a lot. Dr. Luea's class is not that hard, but the reason I didn't get an A was that I postponed reading and listening to the recorded lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was only graded based on three exams so if you mess up on one, youll have a hard time reaching the cut off for an A. Regardless the class is very do at your own pace and Professor Luea is very accessible outside of class to answer even homework questions, recommend over the other Econ professors at Vandy for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Luea is amazing! I absolutely loved this class and she is exceptionally friendly, accessible, and supportive. Additionally, all of her TA's are super helpful. If you pay attention and do the readings, you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Great class for the freshmen. She does not require a ton of things, but make sure you catch up everything you covered during class. Otherwise, you're gonna have too many things to do before exam
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Despite having hundreds of students in most of her classes last semester, she was very accessible outside of class and responded to emails quickly. She mainly goes over the textbook chapter in class and does a few practice problems. Overall a good class but the 95 for an A makes itf stressful at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Luea gives you everything you need to succeed. Very organized!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She makes Econ so easy and understandable its incredible. If you have to take an Econ class you should take one of hers. A real gem.

Her class is an easy A if you do the work/reading, but an A is a 95% which is kinda frightening especially because most people take this class their first semester of college. However, the material is quite easy and the tests are very similar to the homework problems which is nice.

Professor Luea is extremely understanding and very straight-forward. Either attend the lectures or read the textbook, do one or the other, and you're set. The cutoff for an A is a 95 and the 3 exams are the majority of your grade. I would definitely take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took econstats online during COVID, 3 attempts for multiple choice hw and 10 attempts for multiple choice labs, test averages were all As, was a breeze.

She is super sweet, and her lectures are very direct and clear! The tests are tricky, and it is easy to get a bad grade in her class because there are only 25 questions on the tests. You have to be very careful on tests!

Professor Luea is amazing. She explains the content in a way that makes it easy for everyone to understand, she's very accessible and clearly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. The material is based on the textbook but she goes over all of it in class so there's really no reason to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Doctor Luea is amazing. She is clear about what she is teaching and willing to go the extra mile to explain difficult chapters. She is by far better than all other available professors that teach Micro and Macro. She gives off the vibe of the cool aunt. Tests are not difficult if you study and do the practice problems as well as listen to lectures.

Prof Luea's class is a fun intro to econ. It's pretty by the book and attendance is optional, which is extremely nice for those of us with busy schedules but an interest in the subject. The class is generally easy but is unfortunately skewed towards the three exams you will have, with an extremely high requirement for an A. But otherwise, solid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Useful and accessible intro to econ. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Luea is so chill yet also really good at explaining Econ. You don't need to do the readings because Luea just reiterates them during lecture. The HWs are the easiest thing in the world (take 5 minutes to do and you have to try to not get all 100%s). Tests are 25 questions and same difficulty as HWs. She is so nice and this class is so easy!

Need a 95 to get an A in the class but Luea explains the concepts really really well and is always ready to help outside of class. Grade is mainly based on three mcq exams and during covid the class was asynchronous
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Nice, lenient and understanding of students. Friends who took her for ECON 1500 loved her as well. 100% would recommend

This class is a very good foundational class. If you have any knowledge of macroecon you won't need to go to lectures at all. Just read the textbook and do the mini quizzes and you'll be fine. The one annoying thing is that you need a 95 to get an A.

Lecture was clear and never took the full time. Always really explicit about what to know, w/ easy HW and a project. Only reason a 4 instead of a 3 difficulty is the 95 cutoff for an A - HW and project are essentially completion grades, but you can only miss 5 questions across 3 25Q tests. An A- is easy but A is hard b/c of the high stakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Luea is probably your best bet for 1500. Tests are high stakes due to the low number of questions but an A is definitely achievable.

Professor Luea can teach you so much is so little time. I usually attend her lectures synchronously but you don't have to. The way she teaches the material almost makes the textbook unnecessary. She is amazing at what she does. Can't wait to take more classes with her in the future!

Prof Luea has made Econ 1010 a very straightforward and understandable class. She is really friendly and is clear in her expectations for the class. Def recommend to anyone wanting to take Macroeconomics.

Prof Luea was a fine professor for ECON1010. The textbook is not needed and everything on the test is taken straight from what she said in lecture. Exams are high stakes (3 25 question exams) but super easy mini projects and multiple choice homework questions help. Her lectures are pretty boring, but she's straightforward with the info

Prof. Luea is a great professor. If you listen to her well-prepared lectures & read the textbook, you'll be more than set for the class. We have 1-2 quizzes every week over the chapters covered, which are more than easy to get an A on, two straight-forward mini projects and three exams. If you learn the material, easy A. Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: class is hella easy. I will say though, the requirement for an A is higher than normal so even though the content is super basic you need to be careful not to make a simple mistake or two on an exam as that could well cost you an A

Professor Luea is one of my favorite professors ever! She truly cares about her students, and she is very accessible outside of class. Make sure to really study for the exams since this class weighed heavily by your performance on those two exams. Otherwise, I would definitely take Luea if you have the chance!

Great prof. Class is relatively easy but A is a 95. Project, homework, and labs make up half the grade and are easy points if you follow directions. Lecture is very clear and makes understanding concepts easy. Would recommend.

Best professor I've had at vandy so far. I had taken AP stats so that definitely made it easier for me, but honestly a great class even for non-econ majors. Not hard at all if you just do the work and study for tests, such an amazing organized prof. Would recommend.
A great professor who really cares about her students! I took two of her classes and she was understanding/flexible with deadlines. An easy class but I learned a lot.

Luea is a really nice and easy prof. She takes things pretty chill with her students and her class is really dialed back. Honestly wish it was more challenging or engaging, but if you've taken AP stats her econ stats class is a breeze.

If you've taken AP Stat, this class won't be difficult. Homework, Lab, and Project part of grade are easy to get As if you pay attention to what she says in class. Two multiple choice tests (midterm and final) can be made a lot easier if you know how to use distribution and stat calculator functions.

Prof Luea is amazing! She's extremely nice and caring, and is always available for help. If you haven't taken a stats class, it'll be smart to show up to lectures. Labs are relatively easy since she walks you through what you need to do and how you analyze output. Relatively hard to get an A (95 cutoff), but if you practice problems it's not bad.

3.5/5. It's unclear what you need to know, but by omitting a lot of formulas the content is made a lot easier. You have to pay a lot of attention for the rare occasions she does do problems in class. 95 for an A is intimidating. Learn DIST and STAT on your TI-84. Sometimes gives EC. Two MC tests (25Q, 50Q) and a project comprise most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a very interesting first-year writing seminar, even for a non-economics major. Prof Luea was very nice and if the deadline for a paper was the same week as a test, she would move it to the next week. She provided great feedback on papers, and structured the class as a transition to college writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You really have to be interested and pay attention to lectures which are boring and redundant/repetitive/thorough but the textbook we used was ridiculously unhelpful and the practice questions are nothing like the 3 multiple choice exams. She seems really nice though and I did learn a lot. 2 group projects are piece of cake/grade boosters.
Extremely through (sometimes slow) lectures; would definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: had her for stats/micro (1020) and both classes all you needed to do was go to lecture and take notes  I barely read outside of class . Lectures are still very boring, she tries to make jokes but overall it's very dry. Stats has grades padded by a project and homework, making tests less important compared to micro (all are 25 MC questions).

Pro: easy, doesn't cram a lot of information into single lectures, small amount of material to learn, straightforward tests Con: 95 is an A, doesn't care about her students, hard to reach by e-mail, skips office hours, sometimes writes test questions poorly, leaves students to fend for themselves

Her lectures are unhelpful, she's unsympathetic to any emergency situations that go on in your life, and she blows off your questions in office hours. Not the easiest class either if you've never dealt with stats before. Go to class or she gets salty.

By far the worst teacher I've had so far. Teaches maybe one topic a week, and spends 50 minutes each class to explain one example. Tests have no study guide and you have to read a ton to feel prepared. The examples she gives in class are much simpler than the test. Finally, I feel like I learned nothing

I have no doubt on Luea as being a caring and nice person. She is very accessible outside class, addresses every problems you bring up. Drawback is, the weekly workload is extremely low. That says, you might end up procrastinating instead of keeping up your study outside class conscientiously.

I think it is absurd that we pay for someone who has no interest in doing her job. Professor Luea cancels class and skips office hours. We had one TA for over 100 students which made exams awful since she didnt come. She doesnt answer emails either. I expect to get an A but it was a complete waste of my time.

Incredibly boring. Expects averages in the high 70s to mid 80s on exams, yet is the only professor I've ever had who sets an A at 95%. The project is easy, but that's really the one thing that is half doable without a lot of hard work. Avoid this class if possible.

you dont have to go to class but you should bc it's easier than reading the textbook and you only have to do one. Theres online HW 2 tests 1 final and a project. The tests and final are all multiple choice and if you miss more than 2 you get a B so be careful, not an easy A, but it does have an extremely light workload, betterthanthe othereconprofs

I really liked this class. It is basically 3 tests that are 25 MC questions only. She makes it hard to get an A because the tests are really high stakes. Also, a 95 is an A. But if you are able to great really good grades on the tests, it is an easy class and you don't have to go. She doesn't take attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do poorly on one test, say goodbye to your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Luea is a very nice and supportive professor. She wants you to do well, and will help you out if you do not understand things. I took her for microeconomics and economic statistics. Technically you do not have to attend, but I suggest that you try to. You may get an A, but does not mean that you understand material well enough.

This class is pretty darn easy. The HW load is extremely low - usually have to spend no more than 2-3 hrs a week on it outside of lecture. She tests you exactly on what she teaches. Go to class, because a lot of stuff is covered in lecture that will be on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class and material made somewhat difficult due to high stakes exams (20-25 questions) and a 95 cutoff for an A. Luea is nice and easily accessible with plenty of office hours. It isn't necessary to go to class but she does offer extra credit to those who attend once or twice. Most material comes from the book.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: easy if you put in some work. really nice and caring

She is so lazy that it's ridiculous. Her "lectures" were pulling up a digital copy of the textbook and reading it to us. I learned everything from the textbook only. She doesn't respond to email unless you email her 3 times. She often late to class and office hours. She expects her students to be professional when she is not professional herself.

She bops around class acting like she's so ditsy and funny, but when I came to office hours she was a cold-hearted woman. It seemed like she didn't want me to do well in class. Even when I presented her with a documented note from the emergency room, she wouldn't let me make up an assignment. Any other prof would've helped me, but she didn't care.

She isn't a bad teacher, but she just doesn't seem to care. In addition, I kid you not, without fail, every time I asked her a question in office hours, she told me something wrong and I would realize it while studying with the book. In addition, it seems that she is constantly inputting grades wrong and putting mistakes. She's pretty disorganized.

While the class is easy to do well in, even if you don't show up to class, I felt like I learned a very minimal amount and she was extremely disorganized. I found myself having to check every inch of an assessment and my online grade book for mistakes in grading. If I'm going to put in the effort for a class - please at least get my grade right.

The tests and projects are super easy, but the lectures are painful to sit through. Attendance isn't mandatory but she does give extra credit to kids that are present on low-attendance classes (usually Fridays). You don't need the textbook but it is helpful to read before the test if you haven't paid attention in lectures.
The lecture is very light... Most cases a lecture of stuff can be taught in about 5-10 minutes. Most likely because micro and macro econ are simple stuff.

Heather is a very caring and nice professor. Her expectations are clear and the test difficulty is comparable to AP calc, or easier even. She used to give out class notes , but she doesn't do that anymore. While the class is really easy, the tests are really high-stake so you NEED a mid-high 90s in every test to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I can't imagine a better prof or a clearer lecturer. She illustrates concepts incredibly clearly and makes it easy to figure out what her expectations are. Tests are pretty high stakes, but manageable. My one comment is that I never once needed the Excel Stat download that we were required to purchase. Don't waste your money on that.
Easiest class ever!!!

Luea is one of the easiest macro professors at Vandy. Most people don't go to class and still do well on the tests. If you go to lectures you don't have to read, but if you don't go then just do the reading and you're fine. 3 tests, 2 easy group projects, and 3 homework assignments with unlimited submissions, so you can submit until you get a 100.
Just be ware that sometimes there are important stuff during lecture that won't be in the text book... And tests would include those important materials.

this class is crazy easy but also a little frustrating because there are only a few grades, and exams are 25 point multiple choice tests so if you miss a few questions you're already at a B. Also, it's one point higher to get an A (so you need a 93.5 instead of a 92.5) but overall she's decently interesting and the workload is remarkably manageable

would definitely reccomend-the class is graded by relatively easy assignments and you don't really need to do the reading if you show up to class/you don't really need to show up to class if you did the reading. i did both, and the material wasn't bad, but you do you. she's decently interesting and seems like she'd be accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I did not learn anything in this course and it was insultingly easy. I really don't think this woman cared about teaching as every other week she cancelled class and  regularly came unprepared in terms oft teaching material (letting us out 20-30 minutes early (even on the day before the final)). Easy A but only take if you don't care about your edu

Grades projects really easily. Nice and funny woman. Going to class isn't necessary but helps. If you actually do all the readings, pay attention and take notes in class everyday, you should get an A. Not an overly amazing teacher but is accessible and fair. Will give you the benefit of the doubt.

Probably the most frustrating course I've taken. Homework was minimal and easy. Reading was suggested, definitely not required. Lectures were basic and anything but challenging. The midterms seemed so incredibly easy; however, the scores that I received indicated the exact opposite. Luea is a solid professor, but the grading in this class is odd.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Her midterms are much harder than the (very little) homework she gives. She's nice when asking her questions after class, but she goes extremely slow in lecture, so it's hard to pay attention.

Please disregard the rating below. This person clearly didn't go to class or studiy. Luea is great. 1midterm, 1final. Her notes are extremely helpful, but you MUST go to class. Go over the textbook to get the basic concept of material, but use it for practice problems. If you go to class, she will give u EC. Took my grade up a whole letter!

Exams are either entirely too long or cover information in a way that is completely different from anything she does in class or in the textbook.  Also refuses to curve exams even when class averages are very low.  She's nice and funny, but very confusing in lecture, and the impossibility of doing well on exams makes the class a GPA killer.
1 midterm, 1 final. MC straight from textbook. Gives out EC. Overall very easy - take her over anyone else

Very reasonable class.  Will say though that you absolutely MUST read the textbook if you are going to do well on the exams, since her lectures leave out significant detail that you'll need to know.  That said, she only gives full letter grades, and usually half the class gets A's and the other half B's.  Definitely recommend.

Her class is easy as long as you do a little reading outside of class. 25 multiple choice questions per test. Most are easy and obvious, but there are usually a few tricky ones. Little bs homework assignments due here and there. Pretty easy B+/A- if you just do a little studying before the test.
she is super nice, and her tests are very straight forward. She throws no tricks at you and there is no attendance.
Great Teacher, would highly recommend

Dr. Leich-Hilbun is an amazing lab professor and this course was so chill. Definitely learned but fun environment. 2 quizzes throughout the semester and very manageable lab reports, plus a "photo contest" after each lab. 10/10 great lab to take and a great professor.

One of the nicest and most caring profs at Vanderbilt. She lets class out 30 min early each day and is super responsive on email. Textbook is also a free pdf she wrote. Online exams were not too challenging, especially since they were take home. But if you have no background in stats, I would advise you to stay away from this class.
She didn't lecture at all and expected you to be able to answer MD level questions on the exams. Extremely difficult and I felt like I learned nothing,
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is enthusiastic about anatomy, but her online plan was really lacking. There were no lectures and all class material was application (how would you cure xyz diseasewhich scientists haven't done yet) so background knowledge was expected. Her half was not nearly as difficult as Hillyer's but overall I feel like I learned very little.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She did not teach the section at all - there were no lectures - synchronous or asynchronous. Her exam questions cannot be answered with the online textbook and were super difficult . I learned nothing in her section of the course while Hillyer actually taught material. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Leich-Hilbun is super nice and not a harsh grader at all! She cares most that you try to understand the material, so she won't take off a lot of points even if you get the answer wrong. Grade is based on weekly powerpoint slides (completion grade), 3 midterms, 1 video project, and a final exam. The textbook is a free PDF that she made herself.

I've taken several courses with Dr. Hilbun, and biostatistics has proven to be one of the most useful. While the course was disorganized (but so are all her other courses), I learned a lot (e.g. Matlab). The lecture is quite difficult to follow, but if you take good notes and find a good study buddy, you'll do just fine. Quizzes/tests are fair.

Spent days after days studying for anatomy exam and managed to do horribly. I currently have A on all other courses including orgo and I spent all my time and work into this course. No lectures and all we were given was an optional textbook, which she barely used for the exam. What the hell are we supposed to study off of?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's a sweetheart but taking this course while online is a horrible idea. Though she wants you to learn and be excited, she did not teach. No synchronous or recorded lectures, no discussion - all of your learning comes from reading hundreds of pages in a poorly written textbook. Wait to take this until classes are in person.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS REMOTE. There are no lectures and you have to teach yourself everything from the textbook. Probably one of my least favorite classes ever taken at this school. I've learned zilch and the weekly modules are super annoying.

Dr. Leich-Hilbun is very clear about what material you're responsible for knowing for assessments. The class consists of a quiz each Friday, 2 tests, and a group project. Class time is spent doing lectures, thinking through case studies, and doing activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Clear grading criteria. She is a passionate lecturer and very approachable outside classes. She is actually invested in her students and she will help you if you ask for it. You can tell she cares because she tries to make the class more than just memorization. Most of class is pre-med, but its easier than most premed core classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's a pretty leich-able professor overall. Her enthusiasm for the class is really strong but can become disorganized. Lecture material does not always match material your tested on. Very clear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Most of my class was premed (except me), making the weekly quizzes pretty difficult. Allison is super nice though and a very lenient grader. Solid choice if you're trying to get your liberal arts lab credit filled.
Very respectable teacher who cares a lot about the subject and her students. Tries to make anatomy more than just straight memorization. Weekly quizzes are a little annoying though.
Dr. Leich Hilbun is extremely clear about the material tested on exams/quizzes. She covers additional interesting material outside of what is tested. Highly reccommend 10/10

Dr. Leich cares a lot about her students and it is easy to get an A in the class. However, I hate the way that it is taught and organized. She does not teach any of the content you will need to know for weekly quizzes or exams. All your learning will be done out of class. Class is spent on irrelevant topics and you still have to go for attendance.

Dr Leich is very kind and very clear with her quizzes. Studying for this class can be very direct and if you study, you will get a good grades. I wish she would not have her lectures be so far ahead of the quizzes.

Leich Hilbun should not be an instructor for anatomy and physiology. She does not cover all the necessary information, and always sidetracks and talks about irrelevant details and diseases. Terrible. AVOID HER.

Her lab is amazing! I learned so much, and there was always fair grading. She just wanted you to learn, think critically, and enjoy doing fun lab work. It was such a nice lab, I mean seriously. Her quizzes made me think about the lab work from different perspectives, and her goal was always us learning. She's really nice and sweet, too.

Professor Leich Hilbun is hands down one of the best lab professors I have ever had. She cares about each student's learning and makes the class fun and applicable to real-world research. The work is incredibly manageable, the quizzes help with understanding each step of the experiment, and her grading is very fair. Best class (:

Shimizu-sensei is a kind person, but not an effective teacher. I started the class with some prior Japanese knowledge, but by the end, I felt like I had learned very little. The first few tests are online, but the rest are taken in person. Overall, I do not recommend taking this course.

Shimizu sensei is a very nice and fun professor. She is so sweet and really wants to help you do your best. Lots of homework and tests, I mean LOTS. It got pretty hard for me to keep up but she isn't a tough grader, so it's very hard to do badly or fail this class.
Shimizu sense is a very kind professor, helpful and always encourage student to learn in the class. Participate and you will get an A.

Shimizu sensei is a super fun professor to take and I would highly recommend anyone interested in learning language to take her class. She isn't a tough grader and the homework is more than manageable. The tests also aren't super challenging as long as you pay some attention and you will definitely feel like you are learning a lot. Super awesome.

Japanese Calligraphy was a short but sweet class I looked forward to every week. No knowledge of Japanese is needed whatsoever. Shimizu Sensei was always available to help during class and help us perfect our techniques. Graded on a final work at the end of each class, attendance, and a final piece. I'd reccomend if you need an hour or are curious!
a

There is a lot of homework but it is genuinely so easy and she does not care if you turn it in weeks late and you still get credit for them. There are a few quizzes here and there but she tells you exactly what words to study and the study guides for tests are exactly what show up on the test. Super sweet lady.

If you are confused at all, this class covers half of the content in the elementary class, which is 5 days a week. Shimizu Sensei's class was a great start to Japanese. She was very funny, and the class wasn't too bad. I would recommend coming to class. There were a lot of short hw assignments, but if you stay on top of it you'll be ok. Slow pacing
Super great class and professor. Very skilled at teaching the basics of a foreign language, which is not an easy task.
Do not take her class.
She's caring, but her lecture's too disorganized
I highly recommend you avoid her class, not because her class is difficult, but her teaching style is just too confusing. Never too late to switch with a different section/class.

Dr. Shimizu is so caring & adorable (in the best of ways). Her teaching can get a little confusing, but I genuinely only think it is because of language barriers, not because she's bad at it or because she wants to mak your lives harder on purpose. If you have time to just be patient with her, you can really get what you're looking for out of her.

Dr. Shimizu clearly cares a lot about her students, but as a professor she's a little all over the place. Constantly changing quiz and test dates, random homework assignments, etc. If you don't mind feeling a little disorganized, you will gain a good basic knowledge of Japanese and earn an easy A--she's a very easy grader.

Dr. Shimizu is a kind and knowledgable woman, but not a qualified language instructor to say the least. The class time cannot be used more inefficiently, and I learn almost all new content by myself. You cannot make up any quiz even if there are a ton. She has trouble getting what her students are doing, or thinking. nonetheless she's very kind.

A really easy-going professor who treats her students like her children. She explains the grammar quite well for an entry class. As for JPAN 1011-1012, the pace is very slow and easy A. Recommended as classes for fun but don't expect to speak a lot of Japanese after just two semesters.

She rarely responded to emails, which made it tough to get help or clarification when needed. The grading was also pretty confusing and hard to follow, so it wasn't always clear what was expected or how things were being evaluated.

SOO NICE If you haven't taken any stats/don't know R there is a lot to learn but Dr. Baroud/TA are very available. 70% of your grade is 2 exams and a final which are not super easy but HW assignments and review sessions prepare you pretty well. Assignments are long but useful. Dr. Baroud is awesome idk if anyone else teaches this class but PICK HER

Dr. Baroud is very acommadating during lecture. Always feel free to ask questions if you don't understand a concept. If you have experience with a statistics course, you'll do fine. Coding in R is required so take some time to get used to it beforehand. Practice problems from the textbook are very helpful before exams. Pace yourself, they're long.

A great professor at Vanderbilt with a lot of knowledge and excited to teach. The class itself can get a bit challenging and homework assignments are tedious but Professor Baroud is helpful and makes lectures very clear. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was challenging, but Prof. Baroud made it very manageable (I still had to put in a lot of work). She does a good job of having engaging lectures and is very concise. The homework assignments are long but there's max 1 per week, and as long as you try you'll do well. I learned a lot in this class.

Dr. Hiba Baroud is a gem among stones at Vanderbilt. She is by far one of the best professors I have had. Effectively teaches high-level material, is incredibly accommodating, offers valuable feedback, and will take time to make sure each student is doing alright personally. Tough class, but her persona makes you work hard and try your best.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Hilles was amazing. I took his FYWS in poetry. He made it a welcoming area for discussions and it was mostly class led, and he spoke the least. He was really helpful outside of class, and could meet with him outside of class to rewrite essays or look over drafts. Just participate a lot and convince him ur interested in his class for an A!

Professor Hilles is a very caring and considerate professor. He gives good feedback in workshop, and creates a positive atmosphere in class. I have no idea what the grading criteria is (it was never stated), but I got an A. I think as long as you do the assignments on time, you'll be fine. You write 11 poems and read a couple poetry collections

Simply the best professor at Vanderbilt. I have never had a more thoughtful, engaging, and overall delightful professor. You are MISSING OUT if you don't take a class with him. If you are engaged, your grade will reflect that.

Such a great class! The professor just expects you to care about english, however, that being said, you got to perform well when the time comes and give really good, well edited and thought out, work when it comes to your papers. He expects that, I think, knowing class is chill and most of his students are English majors. Great, great guy. Take it!

Great poet, but taught freshman writing like it was a grad seminar. Makes checks next to your name on the attendance sheet based on if you speak, which means everyone is competing to just say something and no one is listening to each other. Was surprised 18 yo students weren't inspired by a syllabus filled with old poets writing about old age.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Hilles really cares about poetry and his students. The class really isn't hard, and most of the grading is based off of participation. As long as you show up to class and make 1-2 comments a class you should be fine.

Hilles is hilarious and extremely genuine. However, he is an incredibly slow grader and only assigns two papers and a final, so you won't know how you're doing until it's all said and done. He's hard to reach outside of class, and he often ignores emails. Grading is average. He's a wonderful guy and an okay professor.

Prof. Hilles shows up to every class happy to discuss poetry for 3 hours straight. He has a very sly, wry sense of humor that only a few people seem to catch, but if you do, he's rather funny. He's very flexible with paper topics to allow his students to follow the creative or analytical drive that will lead each of them to the most understanding.
Such a wonderful poet and professor

Rick is wonderful. He is super approachable, and he really does just want to talk about poems. He is open to all ideas and opinions, and he just loves to talk. He brought our class oranges and chocolate every week. He is a great teacher and friend.
The dude loves poetry and just wants to talk to you about it. He's very helpful and cares about his students. Show up, put in some effort, and you'll be fine.
Boring class and mandatory attendance. No actual grades except on two papers. Not a hard class, but difficult to tell exactly how you're doing.

The class seems like a waste of time, but if you are into writing poetry, by the end of the semester, you will probably feel like you've progressed at least a little bit.  Not very much work involved except a portfolio due at the end of the semester.  The class is 3 hours long, but only once a week, so it is easy to get restless.

This was overall an easy class, just long to sit through. While it only met once a week, three hours is a long time to sit in one class (3-6 PM). As long as you write your weekly poems, this class is pretty easy.
Amazing teacher. Very enthusiastic and genuinely wants all of his students to appreciate poetry and do well in his class. Everyone should take this class.
Very cool guy...never gives you any problems when it comes to deadlines or attendance...take this man
i love this guy.  typical college poetry professor, he rocks a black turtle neck  with a black sports coat at all times.
Class was extremely easy and laid back. Professor Hilles was really friendly, lax on deadlines, and very passionate about poetry.

If you need an easy cple credit, take intro to poetry with this profesor. It's an easy A. Class can be unbearably boring at times but it requires hardly any preparation. We wrote alot of poems which I thought would be hard but it's really easy and actually fun. Prof. Hilles is a very kind teacher who loves poetry and cares alot about his students.
Awwww Michael is the best!!

Professor Hime is very enthusiastic about music and this class will teach a lot about music. However, as someone with 0 previous music experience, this class was HARD. It was a struggle to be able to effectively learn and apply the concepts, especially in the beginning. By the end of the semester, I got much better, attesting Michael's ability.

The worst and most boring class I have ever taken by far. Hime is nice enough, but I struggled to stay awake every single class and I never paid attention in class. Still got an A, but only because I had previous music experience, so if you don't you will struggle. He expects a lot of work and memorization from you. Would not recommend. STAY AWAY.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Michael is the best! His classes are the rare trifecta of easy, well-taught, & extremely interesting to anyone with the slightest curiosity about the subject matter. He makes sure that his students are prepared for papers and exams, and really makes an effort to get to know everyone individually. Funny, kind, & has a tangible love for his subject.

So passionate about music and so knowledgable. Makes it easy to understand and gets you excited to learn about music. Paper assignments are pretty easy and the tests, if you study using his study guide, are quite manageable. Stay on top of the listening lists and you'll do well. He's also accessible if you ever want to chat about music out of class

Professor Hime is amazing! He passionately lectures about the music and inspires the class to appreciate it. He is very knowldgeable about the material and explains it really well. To do well, do all your posts and spend time listening to the music. If you get the chance to take this class or any other class by him, go for it; You won't regret it.

Michael is the best lecturer you will ever have. It's impossible not to leave his class feeling fired up about what he's covered that day. He's engaging, accessible, and hilarious. This class will literally permanently change the way you listen to music.
Being specific I would take it again great commraderie and in charge persona thorough lecturer

I''m an engineer taking this class for liberals arts credit and have been blown away by the effort that Hime puts into his lectures. He goes to great lengths kindle an interest in music in his students. I wish more liberal arts classes were like his. Take this class if you get the chance. it is completely worth it.
Great teacher.  There is a lot of memorization, but studying really isn't required until the day before test.  Just pay attention to the format of the concert reviews and you'll be fine!

I took this course because I already had pretty good knowledge on music theory, and I am an ardent life fan of symphonies and other classical music. For me, this was easy. By the end of the course, you will be expected to recognize the masterpiece just by listening to the melodies.

Hime is an awesome teacher! He has been teaching this course for about 20 years! Amazingly, he is still full of passion on every class! I am not a music person, but I still do well in the class by just reviewing notes and listening to playlists. I recommend this class to anyone who wants take a break from all other stressful classes!
Cool!
His expectations for memorizing music are ridiculous. Don't take this class if you don't want to memorize 104 mp3's for a single quiz.

Hime is one of Vanderbilt's best teachers. He is enthusiastic and interesting; he tells jokes, and some of them are even funny. The first test (on music theory) will be difficult if you have no background in music. The rest of the class is easy as long as you listen to the music and focus on it--don't try to multitask.
Hime is the best ever.  If you can take one of his classes, do it.  He cares so much about what he teaches.

In four years at VU, Hime is the first professor to inspire me enough to rate here. He is an engaging teacher who truly cares about his students, and his class is fun. If you have any interest in music, take this class! Caution: May be a bit harder if you have no music background, but not impossible. And don't fall behind on listening to the music!

Professor Hime is a very fun and interesting lecturer, although his grading is subjective, masked by the supposed objectivity of musical analysis. Unless you are VERY interested in memorizing the vast number of exceptions to the vague rules that govern Music Lit, avoid this class. Great guy, but very difficult for a 100 level course.

I enjoy classical music.  I did not enjoy MUSL 140.  Hard to appreciate music when you have to memorize every movement of 20 different pieces to the point where you can pick out a 20 second snippet with no context.  Also, concert reviews are absurd as he asks you to review styles he has not covered in class.

The Hime clearly cares about both his students and the subject matter. Not a class that is too hard for students who do not read music/play instruments? I don't, and I had no trouble getting an A in the course with average/minimal work. A funny guy who likes to make class fun. I'd recommend him and this course to anyone.

Ok, the class is easy (especially if you're actually interested in music), but Hime gets VERY OLD after a while.  He'll give a speech in the first class in which he talks about how he doesn't like those  people who just like to spout off their trivial knowledge about music...then you realize he IS one of those people...

Unless you are a music major AVOID THIS CLASS! He gets along great with people who want to be musicians, but if you have other interests you will not get along. Admittedly, many people take this class thinking it will be a joke, but he makes it a point to be a particularly picky grader if you don't make this class your life.

I think he is one of the best profs I have had at Vandy, but since I don't know anything about music, the class was actually really hard for me. I had to work to do well, and I feel like he thinks that you don't need to know anything about music, but since there are so many people that do know a lot about music...you are REALLY behind if you don't.

definitely the best class i've ever taken in my life, and the most enthusiastic, inspiring professor i've had at vanderbilt.  i get so nostalgic every time i pass by the classroom and hear hime's booming voice...i'd probably take this class for no credit, it's that amazing.

I missed class one day and was really distraught, not because I missed something important but because I never wanted to miss a moment of this fantastic class.  Music experience is not at all necessary, even though it makes the class pretty much cake.

Take music from the Hime!  He knows his stuff and is possibly the BEST professor at Vanderbilt.  He keeps the students interested in the materials.  One word of caution: his listing lists are sometimes hard. Ask any former student: memorizing the music requires concentration.  You HAVE to JUST listen to music and can't do anything else.  Fun class.

This man loves his job, and he loves his students. I would take the class again for no credit in a heartbeat. If you have a musical background, there's nothing to worry about at all. If you don't, you'll be challenged, but you'll never regret taking his class for one second. The first day of class had me hooked.
Worked harder in it than some classes. Michael is inspiring. Politicians and diplomats the world over could learn a thing or two from Michael --- music has the power to bring us all together.

AWFUL!!!!!!!!!!!!  His bouncing and bopping around made me motion sick...ADHD?  Not to mention the fact that was unfair in his grading.  It seems that many people love his classes, but the one I took was one of my least favorite at Vandy.

i was fortunate enough to have michael for 141 (normally just teaches 140, for non-blair), and us blair majors loved him so much we wrote him an opera at the end of his time with us -- no joke. he is eccentric and silly and passionate and intelligent and wonderful. you must take his class. he should be allowed to branch out on his classes!
The BEST class I've taken at Vanderbilt.  Dr. Hime is an excellent teacher, and really helped me to fall in love with music.  Definitely take this class if you like music.

take this class- this class will teach you the ins and outs of music. end of story. take this for CPLE/elective credit/whatever. professor hime is the man. go to the review sessions on monday nights- the TA (jeff) knows the deal.

Best teacher at Vanderbilt, period.  Inspiring, engaging, funny, accurate, fair, kind, and many other good things.  The material is also fascinating, and he does a great job of getting you to love music.

Very inspiring teacher.  His classes are still vivid for me and I had them in '91.  I did have an easier time as I had a music-intense background (as compared to most taking the class with me), yet I still had much to absorb from him.

one of the greatest classes ive taken at vanderbilt.  As long as you go to class you are fine.  Attending the review sessions are also extremely helpful, especially before one of the tests.  Listening examples can be difficult if you haventbeen to class.

This is a great class- go to class, attend some of the review sessions- they ARE helpful! Really learn the listening lists, and plan out the 3 different types of concerts for the reviews EARLY-- at the end of the semester, there aren't many concerts.
He makes his classes interesting by being excited!!
Michael is fun and dynamic.  Class is good and well structured.  Beware of listening examples...they can be hard.

Professor Hoch is awesome. She is a great lecturer whose content and exams really seem focused on your learning of developmental psych, not just being good at memorization. Exams are easy if you study, very straightforward. TAKE PROFESSOR HOCH FOR PSYCH CREDIT, you will absolutely not regret it

I love her so much. I wish she taught more classes because this was one of the best classes I've taken so far. I went to lecture every day and barely had to study for exams. She makes lectures really fun and she's so sweet.

Take this class over gen psych for credit! Prof Hoch is the sweetest. Highly recommend. Class is optional, but you don't need to study for midterms if you go to class. No homework at all, and lots of opportunities for extra credit. Grade based on 3 midterms, 1 paper (revision option to replace), and an optional final (that can replace a midterm)

this woman deserves all good things in the world. I beg you to take this class. expectations are clear. there are four exams (including final), you can drop one. 1 paper. you get an opportunity to revise the paper, and you keep the best grade for the paper. the class was interesting and genuinely paid attention, so studying for exams was easy!!
Great professor and easy class! I did not go for the last two months of class and managed to teach myself everything needed before exam 2 and exam 3 in the 2-3 days before the exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the kindest professor I've had here. Attendance was not mandatory, and i used lecture slides to make quizlets for exams and did well. 3 exams, a 4th optional final, and one paper. TAs graded the papers harshly, but you get a revision and they only take the highest of the 2 grades. I had a dean's notif and she happily gave me an extension
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is amazing! She really wants to help people learn, and I did, but I was not stressed out by this class. AMAZING!! I wish she taught more classes.
My queen. 3 tests (+ one optional final). One 2-page essay. No homework. Option for extra credit. Take this class.

professor hoch was by far my favorite professor this semester. her lectures were so interesting and she always kept us engaged. the only grades come from exams (final is optional), a paper, and extra credit. this is the only class where i was genuinely interested in learning more about the topics and connecting it to my real life. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I LOVE DR. HOCH! She is such a kind and caring person who seems to genuinely care about her students. Her lectures are engaging and I learned so much in this class. The tests were straight-forward and aligned with the study guide and what she talked about in class. Would love to take another class with her!

Justine is truly one of the kindest professors I've had. Her teaching style is calm, clear, and easy to follow, and she creates a low-pressure environment where students can learn comfortably. Even though attendance isn't required, I always felt like going because the space she creates is so welcoming.
Go with her if you can.
easiest class ever have not gone to a single class

Take Hoch for dev psych! There is no hw or outside reading apart from one, short paper. Hoch is very soft-spoken so I sat up front. Study guides are super clear and help you do succeed on exams. Class is very well structured. Lecture slides are skeletal so I attended class because she is knowledgeable and caring about field.

Genuinely one of the sweetest profs I've had! She wants you to succeed, and is more than willing to help each and every student. 4 exams, one is dropped. There is one paper and one revision. Such a refreshing class and experience!!

This is the easiest class I've taken at Vanderbilt. I didn't even have to take the final exam because I was already easily at an A. Other than that there is literally nothing to do outside of class and you get to do psychology studies (which I got $140 for) in addition to 10 points of bonus credit. Hoch is very nice and knowledgeable.

Really simple class. Only homework assignment all year was a 2 page paper. Really fun and interesting content. Graded on 3 exams + final, 1 dropped. Extra credit is a whole 2.5% of the grade. Generally fantastic human being, super sweet, fascinating research/field. If you want 3 credit hours to go alongside a hard load, take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Content was clear and tests were simple. Very caring towards students.
Amazing.

Sweetest, most caring prof I've ever had. You can tell she loves what she does and knows a lot about it. Tests and paper are straightforward, and she did her best to make the lectures interesting. Such a refresher in a world where students often feel like so many profs want them to fail. Take her class!

Professor Hoch is incredible! Her lectures are engaging and the way she explains things makes for minimal studying later. Participation is not mandatory but definitely a class worth going to. She cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants everyone to succeed.

Take developmental psychology with her!!
