amazing class! the only note is that she moves really fast in her lectures, but the slides are posted so it is not hard to get all the material. three exams and final: drop the lowest, paper and revision: also drop lower grade, overall my favorite class this semester

Dr. Hoch is a very sweet and caring professor with super clear lectures. She gives out study guides before each exam and everything on that study guide is all that will be on the exam. If you go to class, review her powerpoints, and do the studyguide, you'll be fine!

The lectures are straightforward and easy to understand. There are three exams and a final (but you get to drop the lowest exam, so the final is basically optional). She provides a study guide for each exam, and the exams are very reflective of the study guide. There is one paper that you get to resubmit after getting feedback for a new grade.

Professor Hoch is kind, approachable and super knowledgeable/passionate about developmental psychology. The material is conveyed in a way that is interesting and easy to understand. Work outside class is very minimal and you only have 3 exams and 1 paper. I highly recommend this course with Professor Hoch. She is amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Course has 3 exams (not cumulative) and 1 final exam (lowest of the 4 dropped so basically optional final). Exams are based entirely on lectures. Attendance is optional but if you go to class and take notes the exams are straightforward. There is 1 paper (weird format) but you get a chance to resubmit it for a new grade after you get feedback.

She is such an amazing professor. Her lectures are so clear and easy to understand while still being so fun to listen to and participate during. It is clear she is very focused on the success of her students, and it really does feel like she is always there to help. I enjoyed this class more than I can express!

Dr. Hoch is very kind and it shows through her interactions with students. The 3 tests are based on the study guide, a condensed version of her lectures. For the paper, you submit it, get a score and feedback, revision, and then resubmit and score. The better score is taken. Extra credit if you participate in a study or write about doing research

Amazing professor to take Dev Psych with. Clearly knows what she's teaching and cares about the subject matter. Exams are multiple-choice and straightforward, she's very accessible outside of office hours. Her slides are a bit bare so take notes but her study guides are great! Did not love her TA but what can you do. Overall, highly recommend!

Professor Hoch is clearly very passionate about developmental psychology and a really good lecturer. There was no homework, so the grade depends on 3 unit tests and a cumulative final (lowest grade dropped) and a paper that you can resubmit for a better grade.

Very kind and humorous professor. Lecture attendance is not required and lecture slides are posted on brightspace however the lecture goes significantly more in-depth than the slides so attendance is encouraged. Tests are reasonable in length and difficulty and grades are returned quickly. Great professor and class, highly recommended!

Very easy class, highly recommended. Prof Hoch is caring and accessible. 2 papers with the lowest grade dropped, 4 exams and a final with lowest grade dropped. Exams are 50 multiple choice questions. She posts the slide deck but it's best if you attend lecture. No required readings, extra credit is offered. Take this class, you won't regret it!

Hoch's new to Vanderbilt this year. Very sweet, spends extra time outside class to answer questions fully. Grade based on four tests and two 2-page papers. Lowest test grade dropped, 1st paper is rewritten and resubmitted for a better grade. If you like your first 3 tests you don't have to take final. Never any hw, but attendance necessary.

Probably my favorite honors seminar I've ever taken! She is so down-to-earth, and you can tell she is very passionate about fostering discussion in the classroom. You are mainly graded off of a bunch of short essays and a final project, but she grades very fairly and gives good feedback. I highly recommend taking her if you have a chance.
Fun seminar. There were lots of shorter writing assignments, but you were given plenty on time to work on them. Be prepared to contribute during every lecture.

Professor Rouiller is really engaging, nice, and cares about her students. Attendance is mandatory and make sure to arrive on time. There are VHL assignments before every class, which can be time-consuming, but they are very helpful for preparing for class.

She is absolutely incredible. Took her for three semesters straight. My favorite professor at this school by far. Super fun, can talk to her about anything, and she loves being involved. Will continue going to her office every week even after being done with her classes. Be involved, do the work on time and you'll easily get an A.

Madame Rouiller is awesome for French. She clearly cares about her students and is always accessible. Offers extra credit and genuinely wants her students to not only succeed in French, but love it as well. 2 big exams, otherwise small weekly quizzes.

French 2501W: Professor Rouiller is so funny and engaging. She makes her class extremely enjoyable, and we are always laughing or having a good time. When it comes to grading, her main concern is effort and improvement. If you put in the effort, you will do well in her class. She also gives very useful feedback and is very caring and helpful.

Professor Rouiller is the best educator I have ever had. She made this class much more than just a class and taught the students a lot about the French language. She gave us ample opportunity to experience French Culture and became much more than a professor. If you get a chance to take her, do it. Especially if it is the travel embedded course!

Prof Honorine is amazing! I could not recommend her more for beginner-level French. She cares about all her students, and I learned a lot from her class. There is online homework most days, but the work isn't that difficult and we practice a lot during the class. Take her class!!

Take her class! Prof Rouiller is so passionate about French and she is super sweet and approachable. Classes are interactive and getting an A was very obtainable and easy if you just complete the assignments. Extra credit was also available. Cannot recommend her enough.

She's pretty nice and makes a few nice jokes every now and then. I would definitely take her again. She's very open to questions and tries to make sure everyone understands. This class isn't as easy as I thought, though. Had to fight for my grade. Everyone on here is just a genius except for me, I guess.

Although I took it with her, this is really the shout-out to all 2810 profs! They are all amazing and cared a lot about! But Professor Housden is also amazing! Office hours were super helpful (she even had them during finals week), and going there could really answer a lot of your questions! Three midterms + one final. Somewhat pretty average.

Super nice prof, and very easy to navigate course structure. Expectations and deadlines are very clear. Weekly webworks and problem sets. The class content is a little boring, but prof is very knowledgeable and time efficient in class.

Dr. Housden is awesome, she always had extremely organized and productive lectures. Exams are pretty fair and there is one problem set + one webwork due every week. No extra credit opportunities so lock in for the exams and go to office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love her! Total Icon and great lecturer

Math 2810 is a very easy class, but it does have a lot of material. I found Housen's lecture very clear and concise. It's obvious she knows what she is talking about, and she is always helpful. To be honest, this class is so easy that the professor you take doesn't matter too much, but taking Housden, I essentially never studied outside of class.

This is for MATH 2810. Housden was an amazing professor, she made the class seem very fair and actually made sure we understood the concepts. Tests were fairly straightforward with a cheat sheet, 2 homeworks each week which were similar to test material. No complaints about anything here.

Professor Housden not only made point-set topology approachable but also was fairly generous when it came to grading and exam policies. The midterm was not hard, though the final was more difficult. Homeworks are fair and straightforward, and you are encouraged to work in groups. There are also video group projects.

Professor Tucker creates a hostile and discouraging classroom environment. She is unprepared for lectures, dismissive of questions, and provides little meaningful feedback on student work. Expectations are vague, grading feels arbitrary, and communication is often last-minute or contradictory. Would give 0 if possible

Professor Tucker is consistently rude and impatient with students. She appears disengaged and unresponsive to student concerns, which creates an unwelcoming learning environment. Her explanations are often unclear, and she does not encourage alternative viewpoints. Overall, the course felt poorly supported

She plays nice until the add/drop period ends. Borderline narcissistic and asks questions during 1-1 meetings that are way too personal. Super unorganized and unclear on assignment directions (makes changes last-minute) and refuses to make any exceptions for valid, documented, and pre-notified reasons because it "wouldn't be fair to other students"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Tucker's class is like living high school drama all over again, but somehow, with a professor. No other way to explain it. Prepare for being viewed in an inferior way; not like being treated like a student who is paying to be in her classroom.

Don't take this class with her. There are so many better options for a professor, it's not worth it. Even though the syllabus for each section is supposed to be the same, she gives her section way more work than any of the others. The class is just about meeting expectations on each assignment, but she makes you redo a lot and gives a lot to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Tucker is awful. She does not care about her students, she will not make time to help you, and she is overall extremely rude during class. She does not allow you to miss more than 2 classes regardless of if you have an excuse or not. She clearly has favorites and if you are not her favorite shill will make you do extra work.

She only allows two missed classes and does not care if you have a medical exemption or emergency and need more. She is rude to her students and treated us like we're inferior. She also constantly gave us unsolicited personal advice instead of actually teaching the content. There was so much content that we rarely even covered in class.

Professor Tucker extremely egotistical. Her class time is spent gloating about her achievements and how she is superior to you. Despite this, she is rarely prepared for class or meetings. She has been late to every MANDATORY 1-1 meeting we have had. She modifies the standard class syllabus to give the class extra homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: this professor did not care about her students but only about herself. 10/10 would not recommend. the class could have been great if the professor actually cared about what she was teaching and the students, but no she was just mean and unreasonable.

Prof Tucker is amazing!!!! She genuinely cares about her students and getting to know them. This class was fulfilling and a great creative outlet! Attendance is mandatory, but for a class at 2 in the afternoon on Tues and Thurs that isn't so much to ask. SO easy to get an A if u try at all. I am not the best at staying on top of things but got an A

Dr.Tucker is my favorite professor. Her class was engaging, fun, and teaches essential life skills like confidence in public speaking. It's only 300-word paper/week, and if you get 10 pass papers it's an A (you can write more). She can be a bit unorganized but will change grades. The ppl being harsh were lazy as this is the easiest 2000+W.

This class was challenging at times but also very fulfilling. You will be expected to participate heavily at times and engage at a very high level with course content. However, papers are only 300 words weekly and your "roles" as French characters are variable based on the level of effort/major you have. It is a guaranteed A if you do the work.

Dr.Tucker is one of the best professors that you can create a relationship with at Vanderbilt. Hers is def one of the easiest 2000+ W courses out there. SUCH AN EASY GRADER like as long as you do it you will get an A. IDK why people are so hard on her lol she was amazing and this was one of my fave classes

Was disorganized with very sudden deadlines and lots of work early on. After that it's just one 300-word writing a week and 4 speeches throughout. Complaints are from people looking for an easy class in general, no 2000W class is gonna be as easy as this. Attend class, write within the easy grading criteria, use footnotes. Big time commitment tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
She was rarely on time for student meetings. She's unnecessarily strict&mean to her students, justifying it with "You are a Vanderbilt student" 
If a student has speech difficulties or doesn't speak English as their first language and needs reasonable accommodation and support, she'll say, "I had many students like you(who I've ignored equally)"

Not even arguably my least favorite class taken at Vanderbilt. It's a role playing class that requires in character participation every class and a ridiculously unproportional amount of work for 3 credit hours. The work is distributed evenly throughout the semester, so there is no break from pretending you are a French historical figure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Revolutions - followed Reacting to the Past. Class idea was fun but Prof. Tucker was disorganized and expected a lot. Used slack, no boundary between class and personal time. Assignments posted inconsistently each week. Writing and final grade almost entirely peer graded. Wanted to challenge myself and have fun - would have been better off not.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
I do not recommend anyone take revolutions unless they enjoy chaos and uncertainty. 
For example, rather than writing a paper on your own time, you will be told on Tuesday afternoon you have a paper due that evening. 
Expect many required out-of-class meetings. The class can be funny, but you do not learn much.
Revolutions was so much fun, I'd never had a class like that before. She's a little goofy but is really approachable and makes everything engaging. Please take her RPW Revolutions class if you can.

Prof. Tucker is a very brilliant professor with a strong passion for the French Revolution. I liked how she and Prof. Ramey integrated a French Revolution simulation in 3101  however, there was a lot of work associated with it but it was definitely a new type of engaging activity that you won't get in other courses. Not much French in this class.

Professor Tucker is funny, kind, and caring. She is somewhat inconsistent in her lectures, but she is good at keeping the class engaged. She implemented a French Revolution simulation (entirely in English) for the last month of the course with heavy writing and in-class participation. It was a great experience for me, but not for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Tucker is great! Class made up of 3 open note but closed book quizzes, 4 2 page papers, a 15 minute presentation, and a 5 page essay as the final exam. She expects you to speak French the entire class, but Prof Tucker is very nice and I found her to be a pretty easy grader. Would definitely recommend taking FREN 3101 with her!

only lets you skip 2 classes a semester (with excuses or not!!!) before she starts lowering your grade (even if you were sick or in the hospital or whatever). that's just the start of her weird grading standards. accessible outside class and wants to help but mainly (in my opinion) because the material isn't taught efficiently enough in class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: can be very disorganized and stresses out many students when she doesn't post hw on time/ever. also, in class she can be mean and calls students stupid without helping them fix their errors and likes to make students sing and clap. feels like preschool. for some reason though shes a completely different, more helpful, and nicer prof in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's a pretty good Professor, but she can be quite unorganized and she won't get back to you quickly. But the feedback she gives is good. She brings a lot of fun cultural things into the class along with the French grammar.
One of the best.  She's a rock star in academia yet still so dedicated to outstanding teaching.  Expects a lot but is very empathetic
Professor Tucker rocks!  She really is excited about her subject.

Absolutely fantastic professor! If you can take her class, do it. She's passionate about both the subject matter and her students, which is clear in her teaching, and the coursework is not difficult. This was my favorite class this semester!
Doesn't get any better than Tucker.  Interesting, fun. Challenging.respectful. Knowledgeable.  Take one of her classes NOW.

Don't get me wrong....Prof Tucker really expects you to spend a lot of time on your papers. But you won't believe the amount of cool stuff you learn about in her classes.  You can see the excitement in her eyes when she teaches.  It's sort of contagious.

Awesome prof.  She's hard and knows what she's talking about, that's for sure.  But if you put the work into it, she's there to help.  And it's been nearly a year since I took her class--and I can still email her with questions about courses and for advice!

She comes off as a really nice and helpful, for the students professor. But as the semester progressed people started to realize her true ways. REDICULOUSLY tough grader, looking for absolute perfection for a good grade. She is a  good teacher, and knows her stuff, but in all her grading and false persona make her as a prof someone u should avoid.

An amazing teacher! Sure, she sets the bar high, but she does everything she can to help you reach it. 4 essays (she'll review the drafts - so helpful) and 2 grammar tests. HW is almost optional, but do it. She has a great sense of humor, and introduced us to all sorts of random French stuff (news, music, etc). Take her classes!

Prof. Tucker is amazing. She really tries to make class fun and engaging. She tells you exactly what is going to be on the test with a study sheet. Homework every night but it's not too bad. She really wants everyone to succeed. She responds to emails and is helpful during office hours. 4 papers and she takes drafts & tells you exactly what to fix!

Prof Tucker expects a lot out of her students, but she has a contagious sense of humor that makes what she teaches a lot of fun.  and the breakfast thing--it's true.  Very cool. You have to work hard, but if you do she's really fair.

Prof Tucker is awesome!  She really knows her stuff and expects her students to be VERY involved in the class.  Grades papers on the harder side and is a stickler for grammar but overall very very fair.  Her class was really interesting tho, the one class that I actually looked forward going to most days!!  very approachable too.
Prof. Tucker knows her stuff.  You'll have to work your butt off...but she is really cool and one of the nicest people I've ever met

She is fantastic! She makes even long classes fun with her passion for French and teaching- you will not regret taking her class, so long as you are willing to participate and put in the work that is expected of you. She is a very fair grader too and ALWAYS there to help. Could not be a better professor- I give her my highest recommendations!
She is wonderful. Very clear, really wants to help students understand. Class isn't too hard if you study and see her in office hours. And... we got to eat brunch at her house!
No Comments

Made circuits about as bearable as it could be for a non-ECE. Daily homework, turned in physically, becomes a chore but is good for exam practice. Great lecturer lectures themselves are fairly interesting, and his YouTube videos from COVID help for review. Exams were mixed, I got a 96 on one and a 55 on the next. Final helped a lot of people out.

Holman is great. He really drills the concepts down so that exams are a breeze. If you go to every class, actually do each homework, and spend some time practicing and learning the material, this class is easy. If you fail to do any of those things, you will do poorly. Circuits is not hard, just requires time and effort.
Id love to see the grading scale for this.

If you're lucky enough to have Holman as an option for Electronics, TAKE HIM. His lectures are amazing, and he tells you EXACTLY what he wants you to know. He provides a decade worth of practice tests that ensure you will get an A if you prepare effectively. Beware 90% of your grade is tests, but that's just how this major is. Always accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took it last semester. He IS the guy to take circuit with. He really drills everything into your head and if you are continuing as an ECE, he is the best person to build your fundamental circuit analysis skills. Very lenient in final grading. You can deadass fail the first test but still end with an A. Do well on the final!

Dr. Holman is probably one of the best lecturers in the engineering school. That being said, his classes are incredibly difficult. Be prepared to go to office hours and have difficult exams that are worth a large portion of your grade. Make sure you do well on the final.

Holman is an amazing lecturer and truly has mastered the art of teaching Circuits I. The class is very easy to follow. The homework can be difficult, but if you do it as well as the provided practice exams, and actually attempt to UNDERSTAND the material, you're sure to get an A. It takes work, but it's very doable if you try to be interested :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No doubt worst class at Vandy. They'll talk a lot about Gen Chem but Circuits is a hundred times worse, especially if you're not an EE major. Exams are the hardest I've ever seen, homework is absurdly time-consuming and half the class hopes for a curve to get better than a D.

Dr. Holman is one of the best teachers I've ever had. Go to his lectures, because he will teach you everything you need to know for tests and in general. Great public speaker. There is some homework due at the start of every class, but it helps you master the material. You also get 6-7 old exams to look over before each test, which is great!

Amazing lecturer and genuinely loves teaching. He introduces concepts in class and expects students to master the skills individually. Very fair. He gives you all the resources to do well including all past exams and is available for office hours almost every day, but you need to work for it. He has high expectations and he'll help you reach them.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class a year ago and still wake up in a cold sweat every other night thinking I failed the final. This class has truly affected me in psychological ways I do not understand. Honestly Tim Holman was a nice guy though and tried his best. Maybe try and do a transfer credit situation.

The hardest prelab of the year was assigned for the week after Thanksgiving break (Monday). Then we had the longest homework of the year (by far) due on Tuesday. Then we had an exam on Wednesday. I actually think Dr. Holman is nice and a great lecturer but I'm still salty about that week of work. Still the best option for the classes he teaches.

By far the best prof I've ever had. Went into this class dreading it, but it ended up being my favorite class I've taken so far. Prof Holman is a great lecturer and also has youtube videos posted. He holds office hours everyday except Saturday and genuinely wants his students to succeed. I love this man

Easily, the best professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. Holman has office hours every single day except for Saturdays, so he is extremely accessible. Class is very organized and he goes over many examples in class. Holman knows how to simplify and explain complicated circuits topics. If all my professors taught like Holman, I would have a 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, one of the best here. First day seems scary with talk of grades being relative to others but it ends up a normal grading scale. He posts 11 practice tests per exam so do them all spaced out leading up to a test and you WILL do well. Go to ALL lectures and turn in ALL HW. Do this and you'll get an A. Intimidating prof. but great.

Attendance is mandatory if you want to do well, and homework is due in person. That said, Dr. Holman can turn even a drawing of wires into the most compelling thing you'll hear. He grades you relative to everyone else but will weigh the final more heavily if you do well. Homework takes a couple hours per assignment but helps a lot with mastery.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Holman was absolutely amazing for circuits. Lectures were very clear and engaging. Very test heavy but he emphasized that the final grade is not solely calculated mathematically. All his lectures are on YT in case you miss class. Too much homework (x3/week) for being only 10% of the grade, and must be handed in in person. Do all the practice exams.

Lectures are very detailed and helpful. Lots of office hours; very available outside of classroom. Homework is a lot considering it's worth only 10 percent of the grade. He gives lots of practice exams from previous years before each test and if you do those you should be fine. Tests may be a bit hard but still the practice exams are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Holman has office hours every day except on Saturday. There are only 8 homework assignments, and two midterm exams. Class has useful content and you will have to work for an A, but Holman is great at lecturing so if you do the past exams he uploads you should be fine. He really seems to love teaching and it shows in his lectures each day.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Holman has clear and diligently planned lessons. The organization of every course he teaches allows for students to concern themselves only with understanding the material. He replies to emails effectively and efficiently in a surprisingly fast manor, and is always willing to dedicate his time (even outside of office hours) to help a student.

This guy is a complete jerk. He sets the curve in a way that ensures students must fail, even if they try hard and go to office hours etc. He is way worse when you do independent study with him. He ignores your emails. I do not get good vibes from this professor.

Holman is a phenomenal lecturer; clear, engaging, material is second-nature to him. Tests are crucial, and I think most ppl got pretty stressed about them. What worked for me was starting on old exams (Holman posts them) a week before the exam. 1 a day for 4 days, then 2 a day for 2-3 days before exams. Makes actual exams feel like practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class: math heavy (nothing more than calculus), homework due every class (except for 2-3 reading days), exams are quite a time crunch (except for final). Concepts are nothing way out of the ordinary. Standard 2xxx class. The professor: Appears intimidating but is a very nice guy, wants you to succeed. Super accommodating and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Freshman gen chem was a breeze comparatively. Graded on a curve so you're constantly hoping everyone else did bad. Tests were brutal even as open notes. Homework every day, due in person at 9 AM with no option for online submission. Most grueling class I've taken. Tim himself is an okay guy but the class is just brutal, no mercy with grading
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is setup like a gen chem or freshman weedout course, large class size, 3 tests + final and homework due every class. Material can be tricky but if you attend all lectures and put in the work you should be fine. Holman has been teaching the course for years.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really good lectures. Expectations were clear and he definitely wants his students to succeed. Decent bit of homework but its manageable (more annoying than overwhelming). Not the hardest class if you pay attention in class and do a couple practice problems before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easily the best lecturer I've had in a while. Was genuinely interested in a 9 am class. Got a C on the first test, a B on the next, and an A on the final. Pretty generous curve at the end of the class, you can still get an A if you get a Cs/Bs on the exams.

He was pretty cool. I found that sometimes I struggled with timing on the exam (60 min for 4 ques.). It wasn't horrible and grades were determined more as to how you did compared to everyone else. He's taught this class a lot so he has it pretty much down!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Holman is the reason why I decided to add an EE minor because he made circuits so interesting! Lectures are extremely organized, and the tests are really not that hard. Once you understand the concepts and are able to tackle problems, nothing is unexpected. Really made you work for it though :( and I'm pretty sure he curved my grade in the end
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are impossible. He is also just has a weird attitude and is just a very "haha I got you!" type guy. Bad energy. Unreasonable. Dresses straight out of the 1950s. His lectures did not work for me and I ended up teaching myself from the book. Attendance is not mandatory but you're required to turn in homework every day so it basically is.

While passing out 3rd midterm: "Remember, I have mercy. It's your classmates that don't. They're who you're competing against for your grade. Good luck!" Only cutthroat class I've taken @ Vandy. Clear expectations, but tests are brutal. Don't copy the solutions manual, or you'll fail. 40% of the class got a D/F. He's why I'm CS now instead of CmpE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Holman is a great lecturer. He is clear and tells you everything you need to know for the tests. The material is difficult, but he explains it well. The tests are hard. There is homework every day, but it only counts for 10% of the final grade. Dr. Holman is accessible but is not approachable. He is somewhat condescending in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Holman is a solid choice for circuits. His lectures are very to the point, he doesn't waste time. The tests are the same for all sections and you are given tons of practice tests. He is a very harsh grader. If you mess up, you'll get punished. Make sure you go to lecture or get lecture notes from someone.

Not an easy class at all, but lecture-wise he's about as good as it gets. Great at explaining the material thoroughly and about as clearly as possible. When it comes to engineering classes, he's one of the best teachers of material I've had.
Class is not easy, but fortunately, Holman is extremely organized in lecture, clear in expectation, and explanatory in technicalities. I'd recommend him over other lecturers for circuit I and II.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Holman is very clear in what he expects you to know and makes sure his lectures are very to the point and focused on material that is relevant to the class and more importantly, the exams. The exams are very straightforward and he provides 6+ past exams for practice which is very helpful. The HW is very time consuming but very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Solid professor. Grading guidlines are clear, lectures are clear; if you do the homework and the optional practice tests you will learn the material. He is also very helpful and accessible outside class. Grading for this class is based on ranking the students and giving A's to the top few students, B's for the next few etc.

Daily homeworks make some parts of this class tedious, but Holman makes the material very concise and straightforward. Also has a good knack for alerting you to common student mistakes and helping out in general if you ask. Great professor for the introductory circuits class.

Holman is a phenomenal professor and lecturer. I thought I hated everything electrical and now I'm a changed man, I LOVED his circuits course. Don't get me wrong, it was extremely difficult, but so rewarding to learn such fascinating material.

Professor Holman is one of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. He is an amazing lecturer as his lectures are very detailed and clear and he is very helpful and enthusiastic about the material and teaching. There is homework due every lecture but that helps you stay on track. The class was not difficult at all. Highly recommend Holman.
Tests are too easy. You only need the textbook for hw problems. Learn mathematica too.
This class is so boring that I would never go to class if I do not have to turn in my HW at the beginning of each lecture
Holman is the best Engineering professor I've ever had. He is motivated, enthusiastic, helpful and approachable. His lectures are very clear, and the exams are easy. An overall great class.

He's a great lecturer. Packs a lot of material into lectures but manages to explain things very well. Very available and helpful outside of class. Overall great prof. for entry level EE courses. Make sure to do the homeworks and actually understand them. Tiny mistakes will cost you huge on tests but they can be avoided with practice.

Holman is a great lecturer.  He is very enthusiastic and wants you to learn.  If you have problems, be sure to identify them early, and see him quickly, because the material builds on itself continually.  The material isn't inherently difficult, but it is easy to make dumb mistakes if you haven't had enough practice.

Holman's very organized and a great lecturer. Take him over anyone else - if you can't get in, go to his lectures over your lecturer. Make sure you do multiple practice problems before tests because time issues are big

He is so excited about teaching every day. How to get an A: 1.Go to class. 2.Do NOT COPY SOLUTIONS MANUAL-> or you will fail. 3.Get help from the TA's or email the professor. 4.Dont fall behind on hw.  Homework is everyday only 4 problems. On exams, he gives TONS of partial credit. He was easy to pay attention to also.

Great teacher who really explains the material well. Puts complicated stuff into very simple terms and makes it easy to apply. Working the (long and tough) homeworks and understanding them is a necessity. Tests are difficult, long, and really test the limits of your understanding. Grade distribution makes an A possible if you put in a ton of work.

He explains the processes for solving every problem, but not really the meaning behind each equation. If you do  your HW, go to class, and are a good memorizer, you will be OK. Just don't expect an easy A

Dr. Holman explains the material perfectly. If you actually come to class, pay attention, and don't use the solutions manual to do your homework, you will do fine. I studied no more than 3 hours for an exam and never got below a 92. The people who do badly in this course don't practice the material enough and copy the solutions manual.

Now a senior, it has been circuits that has prevented me from achieving my desired career goals.  I have never recovered from my C in circuits and it will haunt me forever.  I'm not a big believer, but I would bet that purgatory probably consists of sitting in this class.

I'm not sure why people think 112 is a hard class.  If you go to lecture and pay attention instead of playing games on your computer he explains everything.  People make this class out to be worse than it really is.  I studied for maybe 2-3 hours for every test and never got below a 90.  Learn nodal, it applies to nearly everything in the class.
He is a terrible test maker, also he just expects you to understand stuff without question.
This class ruined my GPA and has significantly affected my career, and my future.  Abandon all hope ye who enter.

While it's a difficult class, his lectures are very clear and everything you need to know will be shown to you. For that reason, you need to go to class. Homework is due every lecture except before reviews for exams and the exams themselves, which is not great but they're not terribly long.  The downside is that homework is not graded very quickly

He knows the material, but it's pretty difficult. Homework has to be turned in before class because the TA runs to collect it then bolts out of the room.  Holman follows the same tactic when collecting tests, for he will count down from 120 seconds and then run out of the room forcing you to chase him to turn in the test

The homework (which is due every class period) takes forever and is SO much harder than anything you will see from lectures or on a test.  Also, there really isn't any partial credit and in the end your hw grade counts as much as a test grade.  The tests take forever and are almost impossible to complete in the 50 minutes given.

He is very hard. Exams are extremely difficult and don't have much time to complete them. No partial credit on homework. Luckily the material is not that difficult but you start to get it a week after he teaches it.

Holman is an O.K. teacher.  Going to class is necessary, but the homework is SO MUCH HARDER than anything he explains in class.  Oh, also your average homework grade is worh a test grade in weight so you need to spend alot of time getting it right and 3-4 problems are due EVERY class period.  Tests are reasonable if you understand the material.
Professor McCammon is a very interesting and engaging lecturer. Also, if you follow her assignments and include what she's looking for, her grading is pretty easy.
This is my favorite class of the semester. Professor McCammon is a very engaging lecturer. She is a fair grader on the module projects (very helpful if you meet with her about it).

I'm a freshman at Vanderbilt and decided to take the women and the law class this fall semester. I did not understand the writing technique classes were looking for so I did not do the best on the first two projects. However, she met with me and discussed weighing later projects heavier as I show improvement over the semester. Helpful and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof McCammon is extremely welcoming and works to create a comfortable environment so that everyone can participate. 6 module projects that you sometimes get to choose the topic, and a few discussion-based/group projects. Easy grader as long as you fulfill the criteria of what she's asking for. Super nice and a great person.

McCammon is unaccessible and not caring. There are no rubrics for papers, and she grades completely arbitrarily (and she will fail you with no remorse). There are only 6 papers, so failing one makes it impossible to do well. The content is interesting, but you're better off taking LITERALLY anything else if you care about GPA. DO NOT RECOMMEND.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor McCammon created a welcoming environment in her class, she facilitated important discussions and always included marginalized perspectives in every conversation. You're only graded on six projects so if you do badly on one it's hard to get your grade back up, but she teaches important content. The discussions alone make it worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Class consist of 6 modules and a paper for each module that makes up your grade. Grading criteria is very clear and the content is very interesting Would 100% recommend taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor McCammon is the best professor I have had at Vandy. I'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews. She seems very open to chatting with students and cares about the material. She puts a lot of thought into what she teaches and cares about her students. Six projects in the course and two or three discussion-based projects.

Would fail my papers and give no reason why I received a terrible grade. Boring lecturer. If you want to take a class on women and/or law, there is a history class Sex Law that is actually interesting!

Professor McCammon is super sweet and shows that she cares about her students. Her class is not hard to get a good grade and the course material is very interesting. She was always in a good mood and made sure that everyone had the opportunity to succeed. The projects aren't too difficult and the discussions are engaging.

Professor McCammon is very intelligent, very kind, and clearly passionate about a subject that I found invigorating. She seems like she would be cool outside of class. However, her grading is inconsistent and her expectations unclear. The course seems easy at first but you HAVE to stay on top of the readings and put a large effort into exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Strangely harsh grading. Content wasn't difficult--I feel like I learned a lot--but I don't think my final grade reflected that. Seems like many people had this issue. Classroom discussions were always interesting and students were always engaged.

Learned a lot about women and law, interesting topics and prof is nice, but take-home essay exam prompts were either completely vague or extremely detailed and then graded harshly. Go to office hours before each exam if you want a chance at an A. Small projects throughout were fun, can choose your topic. Don't regret taking, but grading was harsh.

Professor McCammon is great! There's a lot of readings due every class, but they're interesting. Participation matters, and she takes attendance. There are 4 essays for the entire semester, but as a first year writing seminar, they're not that long in length. She gives great feedback on drafts, so it's very easy to improve your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Take her class! I had her for my writing seminar, and it was both quite easy and very interesting. She assigns interesting readings, and class is all discussion. She is open to all ideas and opinions, so everyone felt comfortable speaking their minds. Essay topics are easy, and she gives good feedback. One of my favorites

Such a great teacher. Her lectures were easy to understand. The material was easily accessible and organized. There were 4 papers that were on subjects that you choose, based on class discussions. There was a variety of material to learn from. (P.S. didn't read a single book and wrote papers the night before...B+ as the overall grade in class.

She is nice, but very slow speaker and lecturer. Tests include several long essay questions, which you see for the first time on the day of the exam. Very theory and concept based class. Did way worse than I should have, felt grading was unfair.
exams are the worst- all essay, so basically leaving so much room for her to count off on every little thing

Class itself was awesome and really interesting. I loved professor McCammon during the class, but the final grade is completely arbitrary. I got A's on all of the papers and somehow ended up with a B.

Loved this class! Professor McCammon loves discussion and is very interested in hearing what you think. Daily reading and occasional one page response papers. 4 longer papers throughout the semester. She made our exams take home but that made them basically 15-20 page papers, so be prepared to write. Grades fairly easy if you put effort into it.
Great prof and class.

Good discussions.   You need to read and think, and it pays off in class.   She went over a draft of my paper before it was due and helped me a lot.     Great class.   Explains a lot about what I see going on in the world.

If you read the material, attend class, and occasionally contribute to the discussion, this Professor gives generous grades. McCammon definitely favors the more eager students in her class. For those who don't fall into that category the grades will seem arbitrary. In short, great teacher, but expect to put in the work.
Awful teacher. Boring. Seems like she is helpful if you meet one on one, but is not at all. grades arbitrarily. Do not take her if you want an A.

Worst teacher I've had at Vandy.  My GPA in the department is a 4.0...except for her, because she's rediculously biased and ruthlessly grades anyone who disagrees with her.  Like other reviews said, talks to you like you're a 2 year old, then makes up a grade based on how she feels about you.

not as bad as some of the other ratings say, shes very nice and was very willing to give extra credit and help students out with grades, the class, however, was pretty boring and the subject sometimes was too. tests are fair as long as you take good class notes and peruse the readings, but overall are pretty tough.Not a horrible course,but not easy

DON'T TAKE HER CLASSES!! She is extremly biased, intellectually dishonest, and grades based only on her close-minded views. I disagreed with her grading and she told me to write notes on the dissenting points. I did and she NEVER looked at it, even a semester later, claiming that she didn't have time.  I graduated 4 years ago and am still angry.
I loved McCammon.  She can be a harsh grader sometimes but overall, the lectures are very clear and the reading is mostly pretty easy
worst teacher at Vandy.  very vague about both tests and assignments.  obnoxious out of class.  grading is both harsh and illogical.
Fairly easy professor.  Tests are usually straight from notes so if you go to class and study the notes and at least skim the readings, you'll do okay

Worst career Vandy grade. Grades essays like you're a professional in the field. Deducts points for writing style. Must not be frusterated by a liberal feminist. Would not give me ability to review term paper due at end of semester.

She is a great professor.  Her class was always interesting and she lectures extremely clearly and thoughtfully, and always makes times for questions and discussion.  The assignment schedule was not at all rigorous either.

Worst class and grade I've had here at Vandy.  Class lectures/discussions are boring.  She talks to you like a kindergartener, but then grades you like a grad student.  My politics are even similar to hers, but I would still avoid her at all costs.
not very nice person, a man basher
Feminist?  Whatever...she is a great teacher.  Especially when compared to her peers in her dept.  Highly recommended over Jrade!

she is very helpful outside of class, and pretty clear on what she has to say.  Not exactly an easy grader.  And definately has the liberal/feminist bias, so if you are ultra conservative, she may not be for you.

Not a good professor, you gain nothing from attending class. Exams are insanely dense based on the most minute details from lectures and will include things that were never mentioned in class. DO NOT TAKE

This is the worst class I've ever taken at Vanderbilt. The professor is EXTREMELY unaccessible outside of class and is the COMPLETE OPPOSITE OF WORLD KIND. Very unclear grading, tons of unnecessary staff to memorize, no practice exam, and test on things that are not mentioned in class. DO NOT take his class. RUN RUN RUN.

There was too much material, and the class content did not always match the exam well. However, all of the key points were on the slides. It is an easy class if you are willing to memorize everything. Prof. Huang is caring and super-super knowledgable.

The exams are completely different from the material he teaches, and he teaches from PowerPoints a decade old. Destroyed my 4.0 and I know so many other students in the same boat. I have a friend already signed for S&T (the career path this class is supposed to prepare you for) who STILL struggled in there. That should say enough about Prof. Huang.

His exams aren't fair and I don't understand why he tests students stuff that he doesn't teach in class. He's not helpful outside of class and frankly not accessible at all as he's too busy with his own research. Classroom environment isn't welcoming

this is the most boring class and the prof doesn't know how to teach undergraduate students. please avoid his class if you can. His exams are totally different from what he teaches in class and the practice problems we do. he's just a bad teacher overall.
Got an A. Lots of review material but not hard. Prof. Huang and the TAs are super nice and helpful with problems.

If you're the type of person who can self-study the entire semester and is fine with getting nothing out of attending lectures, then this might be the class for you. After this semester, I can confidently say that Professor Huang was the worst professor I've had in my 3 years at Vanderbilt. Avoid.
AVOID THIS CLASS
This class was so bad I withdrew from it, DO NOT EVER TAKE THIS CLASS

This was easily the worst professor I have had at Vanderbilt. I strongly recommend not taking this class. The professor and TAs were consistently unhelpful, exams were poorly designed, and grading was extremely rigid. What was advertised as an easy elective became unnecessarily stressful. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. TERRIBLE TERRIBLE TERRIBLE.

Class was incredibly annoying — lectures boring and unhelpful, professor isn't helpful outside of class, and final exam was just plain unfair. Do NOT take. There are much easier and more organized level-2000s. Some of the questions on the final were not similar to HW/previous exam questions, although he said they would be. Again, unfair and boring.
Exams are NOT easy and there is way too much content to learn for them which is often useless, harder than many upper-level Econ classes. Take another 2000 level. SAVE YOURSELF.
Just don't go to class and self study. His tests are pretty much the same as the written homeworks so just lock in on the homeworks and its a free a.

Tons of assignments, crazy dense amount of information you have to basically memorize for each test. Professor just drones on all class and no one attends after the first month because you can just read the slides and learn the same thing. Would not take, there are easier 2000 level econ electives.
Professor Huang's course content is relatively difficult, but the exams are easier. He is quite strict with requirements, and late homework is not allowed.

Avoid for Money & Banking at all costs. Very disorganized lectures and slides, and his accent makes him difficult to understand. Problem sets due 1-2 times per weeks, significantly more hw than the upper level econ electives I have taken.

I can't say that some of these criticisms are wrong. Class is very difficult, solutions do require very advanced mathematics (at least Calc 3) and I relied very heavily on the TA. That said, I feel like the underlying economic knowledge was very good in this class and both the professor and the TA will help you if you ask.

Pr. Huang is intelligent and is willing to help. However, as others have said, he uses advanced mathematics and did not supply us with technical solutions for most of the semester. I wish we had more clear solutions and spent class time preparing for the next assignment. This course is difficult for those without the necessary math skills.

Prof Huang is a good guy but the lectures aren't that helpful for the assignments. Homework every week that are pretty math heavy, and the math isn't really taught during lectures. Lectures are usually spent going over past homework instead of teaching actual content.

He gives a lot of homework (one hw each week) and in every class he is explaining the last assignment instead of teaching the knowledge we need for the next one. He also plays tons of unhelpful videos in class. As a result, his class has only a few participants, yet the TA's office hour is usually full of confused students.

Professor Huang is the kind of professor that when you are giving him a comment on this website you literally cannot find any tags out of all those can be applicable to him. Beyond Buddhist sutras dry lecture. Literally the easiest test I have taken in my entire life since he just gave you the answer key to 99% of the problem beforehand.

Boring lectures, like many peope say here, and 2/3 of the class did not come to class. He does not take attendance. Textbook was not useful as well because all the homework answer can be found from his lecture notes. He is pretty clear on what will be tested by showing you a sample test, but be aware that he might change similarity for the final.

Lectures are some of the most boring I've encountered including math, philosophy, and econ courses. He explains things very poorly and in rather bad English. He does, however, go through exactly what will be on the test (almost word for word) so things are rather easy. Cannot emphasize how little I learned from or enjoyed my time.

This class has extremely dry lectures with notes posted online.  Most homework and tests can be done using the lecture notes as a reference.  I definitely learned a lot about finance and banking in this class, but mostly through studying for the tests, not because of the professor.

Prof Huang gave the most boring lectures of any college class I have taken. The first exam was straight from the practice exam and the second one and final were not. He told us if we studied the practice exam, we would be fine for the final (not true). There was a ton of memorization for this class because some test questions were very specific.

Huang is a pretty rambling lecturer but makes up for it by creating the most thorough and clear PowerPoints I've ever seen. Gives practice tests with answer keys, which is extremely helpful. Both midterms were extremely easy; final exam was significantly harder. The 8 homework assignments are graded for correctness.

Professor Huang is hard to understand. Lectures are complete rants. He will stay on one slide for a long time talking about irrelevant economic things. The first test was about 95% exactly like the first sample test which is cool. The second test is harder. Very boring.

He makes everything perfectly clear. You don't have to go to class, but if you do there is really no need for the book as he gives you slides and completed worksheets to help you understand everything you need to know. 2 tests, ~6 assignments. Sample tests to help you get a feel for what he's asking. Loves helping students! Phenomenal teacher.

Great class. Never have to go. Tests are straight from the powerpoints and practice tests. Dont be fulled by your first two test grades though. the final will be tricky. But take the class. At worst youll get a B+.

his tests were composed of questions straight out of the powerpoint notes that he gives you.  also, the sample tests he gave were very close to the real things.  plus you don't have to go to class and a book is not needed whatsoever.  and i still learned a lot, despite not going to class.  pretty much perfect situation here.
Huang is awesome.  Always more than willing to help students, and he provides a great guide to the test beforehand.  t-bond!

Such a sweet woman and truly cares about her students. Read one book a week alongside writing many poems, one pagers, and other mini-assignments, which was really overwhelming when done last minute so definitely budget your time well. Only meets once a week so the three hours got pretty long, but class was overall interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Read 1 middle-school book a week and discuss it with a group. 3 hours once a week, not very difficult. Lots of higher ed students in the class, but super chill

Harry potter class! easy ahh A but it's really type B/creative so if that's not your thing don't take. participation was super important and late points are taken off (i think, because I submitted everything late). no exams/quizzes of any kind but you did need to read your books/known enough to discuss them. love hundley so so much

Professor Hundley is one of the most caring professors ive ever had! Class was mainly discussion based, and assignments were very manageable! Be prepared to read a book per week and have many writing assignments, but this class utilized a lot of AI which lightened the load!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Hundley is a wonderful professor that will push you to do your very best. She is a kind hearted woman who gives one to sometimes three books a week that new all really interesting and there are lots of mini projects in this class.
Lots of reading, but made class fun and engaging

Easy A class but lots of reading and many mini assignemnts- poems, reflections and projects! I love reading (1-2 books per week) and discussions so this was a perfect fit! She's a GEM of a human being so kind and respectful. The class could be overweheming because there are lots of small, mini (not difficult) assignments so stay organized friends!

I loved this class! Although it was a heavy amount of reading (1-2 books a week), I would definitely take this class again. Professor Hundley is very caring and respecting of her students. No papers, quizzes, or tests. Overall, if you like to read, this class is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: lots of work but nice lady and easy A
TOO MUCH work. But overall an easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 100% recommend this class regardless of your major. Prof. He's classes are welcoming, engaging, and thought-provoking. I felt much more comfortable sharing input or thoughts on the readings than I have in any other lit class. It's pretty reading-heavy, but that's the nature of the course. The texts are super interesting, though. Highly recommend.

Huan He is an extremely caring and charismatic professor. I enjoyed his teaching approaches; he knows how to facilitate interesting discussions by asking thought-provoking questions. This class required a lot of reading, and some of the texts were harder to get through than others, but he does a great job of attempting to answer any questions.

considerate, kind, attentive, responsive. seminar style class discussion emphasis on small groups. if you try your best to participate in class, he will work with you to get the score you want out of the course. you get what you put in with the readings, the more ideas you bring to discussion, the more you learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love Huan He!! He has a really special skill of pulling loose threads from discussions and making them into cemented ideas. Really cares about what you write and gives incredible feedback too. This class is reading-heavy and some texts are more digestible than others, but I definitely grew a lot as a reader and writer.
Prof. He is so kind! His classes are amazing for students who are interested in critical theory. He uses critical theories to frame his classes/ discussions.

Prof. He is a joy to learn from; he is incredibly educated, a great discussion moderator, and a passionate educator. The class is reading-heavy, but not without warning. The content of the class was very resonant, and Prof. He makes very complex concepts relatively accessible.

Huston is truly a caring teacher that wants his students to succeed. He always showed up to class enthusiastic about teaching and made an effort to get to know the students. Overall, the class was not overly difficult but brushing up on the course notes is crucial.

75% of course is exams. No extra credit, heavy reliance on textbook. Mirroring the previous comments, there are no threads of clear connection between concepts and no clear examples during class that reflect test questions. Close monitoring of notes sheets, lack of balance between breaking subjects down and challenging conceptual topics. Avoid.

Professor Huston is a great guy who really tries to help his students. However, his lecture style is not always helpful. Additionally, he often seems unaware of what's on the homework assignments and tests and doesn't cover all the topics that we need to know. Overall, he's not a bad professor, but you have to go during office hours to do well.

Huston is honestly the worst professor I've had yet which is saying something because I've had some bad professors. Lectures are horrible and hard to follow. He cannot keep a train of thought and he does no in class examples so the homework is really hard. He tells you that all of the hw problems won't even help you on the test. Avoid this class!

calculus sucks with anyone, but Huston was actually enthusiastic about the content. exams/quizzes almost always mirrored the recommended hws, he would help you out significantly with homeworks in office hours. this class is a weed out but huston did a good job with what he could

Ok look, this class was by far the hardest class I have taken in my life. I took the final today, and although I don't know if I did well, I trust that this class actually taught me things; not just about math, but how to be resilient in the face of academic adversity. It will be a challenge, but just one step in front of the other.

This professor epitomizes incompetence. Lectures are a chaotic mix of irrelevant tangents and unclear explanations. Assignments lack clarity, and feedback is nonexistent. Avoid this class if you value your time and education.

He doesn't teach us things that are on exams but rather spends class doing one confusing, overly complex problem. He doesn't answer questions adequately and doesn't answer emails. I did better on exams when I didn't go to class and simply learned from YouTube. Assigns graded homeworks that are irrelevant to exams and extremely difficult.

The lectures are pointless in regards to doing well on exams. Instead of practicing questions similar to the ones we will be tested on, spends class time doing one extremely complex question. Doesn't effectively answer questions/respond to emails. It is a very difficult class but he makes it worse by teaching us things that are irrelevant to exams.

Prof Huston focused on more difficult problems in lectures and never covered problems that we would encounter in quizzes, exams, or homeworks. His lectures are very boring, but are helpful when you ask questions. He is good at explaining concepts only if you ask the right questions. Exams are hard. Quizzes are okay. Do the textbook homework

You can tell Dr. Huston likes teaching but his lectures just don't cut it. Grade is determined from 2 midterms, weekly homeworks, and a final worth 40%. You'll end up with a fine grade in the class but if you intend on actually learning anything stay away. Going to class was a massive waste of time - I would recommend teaching yourself at home.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very entertaining lecturer and super nice, but honestly isn't a very good lecturer. To get the most out of him, ask questions, be an active participant, READ THE TEXTBOOK. The weekly homeworks are very difficult, I recommend you do them with other people in your class. The exams varied in difficulty quite a bit so prepare for anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super nice professor, definitely cared about teaching us as well as the subject matter. A bit new though, and made exams difficult early and rather disorganized during lectures, but he got better over the semester. He listens to student feedback and made strides to improve his teaching style, so I would think he is worth taking.

Dr. Huston curved every midterm and also offered exam corrections for up to 75% (?) back on each problem you wanted to do corrections for.  He is an entertaining lecturer but I would prepare to spend some time in the textbook reviewing what he teaches in class.  Because of how he grades the midterms, it is very easy to get an A in the class.

He makes the grading criteria easy for a good final grade, despite all the struggles you're gonna encounter along the way. I like this structure for a math class as it optimized both my learning and gpa. He's not really good at teaching though and I sought out tutoring and other means to help me learn. Stick with it and be surprised at how you do.

He's fairly new to the school, and seemed to be working out the kinks in his methods. Exams were hard, but he was generous with curves and corrections. Tough grader overall. His lectures are good, but a little disorganized sometimes. Nice guy tho.

Professor Huston was a great introduction to multivariable. Their testing policy is generous, prioritizing learning over everything else. Their office hours are effective keys to learning an otherwise difficult to visualize subject. I highly recommend taking this course if you want to start learning in higher dimensional mathematics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: inspiring way to teach but too hard for multi-cal. first midterm was too difficult and he change the difficulty of the midterm and the second one become friendly with extra credit. relatively tough grader for homework.

Very kind prof, very knowledgeable about Deep Learning. I think some of the lecture slides were tough to understand, especially without an ML background, and some topics were explained confusingly. Overall very informative course and if you have trouble understanding, Dr. Huo will happily re-explain it. The midterm is easy and the course is chill.

Professor Huo is extremely caring, respectful, gives great lectures, and overall just a great person. I learned a lot from the deep learning class; it's probably the most useful class I have taken at Vandy. Definitely would recommend taking this class!

The structure of this course provided by Dr. Huo is very well-organized. And the homework is enjoyable, which let me know both fundamental implementations and multiple applications in Deep Learning. The grading criterion is clear. Recommend to take it if you want to open the door of Deep learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class changed my career path. Prof Huo extremely complex topics in a very clear way, and made Deep Learning feel easy. He is very young and just getting started, so he is only getting better! Somehow the class was never difficult or overwhelming, yet I feel I learned more than I do in most other classes. I cannot recommend him enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. The workload is relatively light. Since the course is research-oriented, you'll need to complete a proposal and give multiple presentations.

The guest lecture could be replaced by adding an another midterm exam to enhance the course difficulty. It could be better if the programming assignments are more in C++ and Java than Python to make it more difficult. I think the length of the NSF research proposal assignment should be longer than six pages, similar to the exemplar proposals given.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I can tell that she tries her best to make the class interesting, but that does not change the fact that the course material is quite boring. The assignment is generally easy, but there are several being quite annoying. The test might look daunting at first, but in the end, it's open-book.

Professor Huang was pretty solid for this class. That being said, lectures can be a bit dry, especially if you are not as interested in the human factors of SWE (which is focused on heavily). The 2 tests are difficult but barely worth anything and the coding assignments are long but quite doable and easy to score 100% (except maybe assignment #3).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Huang was decent. The first half of this course was very light and feel like an overview of basic software development; the second half of the course was more interesting. The course grade was mostly made up of easy projects; quizzes were not difficult (skim the reading would do); guest lectures were cool. Would recommend.
Very generous curve. I love this professor.
The expectations are almost ridiculously straightforward. You have 5 problem sets that are your quizzes that are the same problems. He gives very similar exams beforehand.

Though he is not the most exciting lecturer, I really like Prof Oh. Macro is a pretty boring subject, but Oh tries to connect content learned with interesting events from history (ex: Greece's debt). I highly suggest concentrating during lecture bcs the material is so much more rewarding that way. Very clear expectations and lectures!

Lectures were amazing and clear. Grading very is lenient and he gives a lot of partial credits. Weekly quizzes are given before hand so you can study them the night before. These quizzes literally are free points and a big portion of your grade. He also gives a similar midterm for you to study. Very willing to help in office hour. Best prof I had.

A decent class. Professor Oh is very helpful during office hours - going will significantly increase your grade. The whole class is based on very few test/quiz grades, so you must do well on them. Very mathematically based.

Lectures have a lot of derivations, but quiz questions are taken directly from the problem sets. You can go to office hours before the quiz and check all your answers. He gave practice tests for the midterm, and the average was high.

Tough class but he has gotten more reasonable. 5 of 6 graded quizzes that come straight from HW are 30% of your grade, the rest are the 1 midterm and 1 final. Good lecturer that posts the notes online.

Not the best macro professor to take. Prof. Oh is very monotone and makes attending class difficult. The final weighted so heavily (45%) and he ends up having to curve the class a lot at the end, but the agony throughout the semester just wasn't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Oh's class is definitely math-focused. If you are the type that does well with equations, etc. you should be fine in this class. Also, going to class helps because watching him derive the equations helped me understand them a bit more.

He is a good professor overall. If you are somewhat mathematically inclined, you will definitely get an A- or higher. People complaining about him too much definitely ruined the mood of the class at times. Try hard and he will help in office hours!

Prof Oh's lectures focus heavily on math, and then the implications of economic theory in data analysis. His explanations are clear, just be prepared to learn a lot of material. There are a few homeworks, one midterm and the final. The material is difficult but he curves the class so you end up with a reasonable grade.

There was only one midterm, constituting 35% of the grade total. The final was 50%. Teaching quality started okay, but fell off the rails halfway through the semester. The class wasn't that hard to get a decent grade it, but only because no one had any idea what was going on which lead to a sick curve. There are much better econ profs at Vandy.
Lots of mathematics, but that makes you understand the material better. I actually understand the concepts now because the math shows a more concrete way and proves them.

It's not the easiest class, as he does focus a lot more on the mathematics than any other economics course I've been in. However, he literally tells you on the first day that the slides are the most important for his exam, and as long as you study based off of those and pay attention when he goes through the calculations, you'll survive.

Even if he is a new teacher, his lecture is very clear and logical. He indeed uses lots of mathematics. However, using equations helps you understand the lecture further. Also, lots of questions from homework are quite similar with exams.

I love this guy. He's hilarious, which kept lectures somewhat interesting. He did focus a little too much on equations and derivations that we didn't need to know, but overall his lectures were clear. Helpful during office hours. Tests weren't bad at all, and I rarely went to class.

He's a new teacher, so he's just getting used to the position. His lectures are difficult to understand and attendance doesn't really help much, but the material can be learned well enough from reading the textbook. Tests are difficult but not impossible.

Things taught in class are not generally helpful on exams and it is very difficult to anticipate what sort of questions will appear on exams. TAs are not very helpful and the professor is unaware of the prerequisite knowledge for students in the course.
The best professor I have ever had, absolutely amazing.

I thought he was humorous in class and I could definitely understand him despite what others have been saying about the language barrier. Homework sets take literally forever (easy 2 hours a pop), so go to the TA for questions/help on that. I did fairly well but didn't feel like I learned much. Went to class about 75% of the time.
The absolute worst professor I have had.  Language barrier is awful and I don't feel bad saying that because he doesn't care.  He is obviously here just for research.

Not a good professor. The language barrier is difficult to get past and actually led to some bad misunderstandings, one of which almost had a huge effect on my grade. Much of the material in class is worthless and the book and the TAs are your only keys to success in the class. I got an A- but I felt I learned nothing.

An absolutely miserable person. Language barrier is huge & though the TAs are nice & willing to help its worse w/ them. Cares nothing about student's opinions, laughed at me when I went to discuss a problem w/ the hw. Never says class is mandatory but gave random deficiency reports for poor attendence. Got an B+/A- but learned it all from the book.
He's not very helpful. Problem sets take 6-10 hours, but the tests aren't terrible. Become friends with the TA as he or she will be the difference between a C and a B or B to A.

The homework assignments are massive and have nothing to do with the readings. You'll be asked to remember obscure information and know how to do things that aren't in the textbook. He'll get excited if averages are in the 70s.
Class was ok. Hard to understand when both the prof and TA refuse to use articles when the speak/write. You think you are failing the class but you really aren't

She is friendly, helpful, and wants you to succeed in her class. However, if you're taking this class just to satisfy an AXLE requirement, you might be frustrated by the amount of time consuming work it requires.
She is very interested in helping you succeed in her class. Her writing seminar was amazing, everyone in the class loved it.

Very interesting class, one of the unexpectedly better freshman writing seminars.  Grades go up during the semester (easy A-/B+). Prof Hylen made the class very fair and engaging. Many students go on to take other RLST classes because of her
I took her class for 109 and 231, and both were very interesting.  She is one of the best teachers in the department.  If you do the work you should have no problem getting an A- at least!

She's very clear and assignments aren't unreasonable at all.  She was so good at teaching a sometimes tricky subject that I couldn't tell what her personal religious beliefs were.  Tough on papers, but listen to comments, and grades tend to go up during the semester.
Professor Hylen is extremely knowledgeable in the subject area. Her lectures are clear and informative, and she is very up front about her expectations for assignments. Great class.

Professor Hylen ia the greatest!  Her class is intriguing and exciting.  Papers can be very time consuming, so I recommend starting atleast 5 days in advance to get it right.  Also, use her office hours.  She's great at listening and helping you understand what you are trying to convery in your paper.  I'll really miss her next semester!

I think she's a great professor! Very knowledgeable, answers your questions during class, and is very nice during office hours. Isn't an easy A, but she tells you what the tests will be like and what she expects for the papers. Reading is manageable, and you'll learn a lot.

This is the worst class I have taken. I dread going to class: she teaches her opinions as truth, ignores students who disagree with her and plays favorites.
