She has told us our answers are "dumb" and blames us for poor test performance. Homework is "busy work": tedious and boring. I don't feel I am learning anything.
This is the worst class I've ever taken.  If you don't agree with her, you're screwed.  It's a ridiculous amount of work for a 100 level class.  Really really really bad

Good class, lots of work, but you really learn a lot. She really knows her stuff, and she grades really hard on papers. It's really hard to earn an A in her class...but you'll learn a lot about how to analyze the Bible.

Absolutely terrible, the old teacher for this class was easy but it's not anymore.  Get ready to spend countless hours on a ridiculous "portfolio" to recieve mediocre grades in addition to memorizing sections of the New Testament for quotes on the test and essays.  DO NOT TAKE!

had runnels for both 2300 and 2410 and would probably take them for every math class if i could. really caring prof whos not even a bad lecturer or anything like that either. Overall just super solid professor, made getting through hard classes like 2300 and 2410 much less hard.

Dr. Runnels might not be the best lecturer but he cares for you genuinely and wants you to succeed all you need to do is to put in the work, and show you understood the material. I would take him any day over the other professors because he loves helping people, and he actually cares for you.
really cares ab students, do the work and put in effort and ur good
great professor who genuinely cares about students. if you go to lecture and do all the work for this class you will succeed
Really cares about students
It's not a difficult class in general, but each HWs/tests consists of 20 points in total so you are prone to getting a lower grade given that he deduct points very arbitrarily and randomly.

He doesn't include the grading scale in the syllabus so you never know it until the very end of the semester (after the final grades are posted), and he takes a lot of points off on HWs for very stupid and unclear reasons (e.g you didn't copy every word of the definition from the textbook/notes).
A much lower grade than I expected. His lectures are dry and definition-based. He teaches computation but not what the content really means. Textbook is much more useful than the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Does NOT tell students how well they need to do on HWs and tests. Takes points off for confusing reasons and does not listen to args. Not recommended.
DON'T take him unless you want ambiguous/unclear feedback on EVERY test/HW. Does not tell students how well you need to do to get the grade you wanted.

All tests are open-book and open-note, and you can submit corrections to get partial credits back for every test & HW. Test questions are pretty straightforward. However, he doesn't explain things clearly and the lectures are pretty dry. Although attendance is not mandatory, be sure you refer to the notes & examples he posts online prior to tests.

Dr. Runnels is a nice teacher that goes easy on his students. All tests were open book/notes, and you could always submit test corrections if you missed anything on the tests or homework. He explains things alright, but he often focuses on computation and not what things mean. He also gives ambiguous feedback on homeworks and tests.

One of the best math classes I have taken. The first two exams were a bit difficult, but they were curved. The professor was receptive to feedback we had about the length of the exams. The final was well written. You could tell how good the professor was when he had another professor sub in for him for lecture one day. Night and day difference.

Ian is awesome. Has a clear passion for math and wants to share it, and it rubs off on the class. Really made me enjoy math again after 1301 and 2300. Homework was 3/4 hrs weekly. Tests are the most challenging possible without feeling slighted by dumb/bs q's; I've thought "cool question" a few times while taking tests. Really chill, funny guy

Ian is by far my favorite math professor I've ever had at vandy. He is a diamond in the rough in the math department. Lectures are very helpful so I didn't need the textbook, very organized, and great at dumbing hard concepts down to an explainable level.
Ian was great- obviously enjoyed teaching the course and always tried to lighten the mood a bit. Would HIGHLY recommend <3

Simply put, I love Ian to death. Gives great lectures and is clearly very passionate about both number theory and teaching it. If I were to teach a class myself, I would do my best to lecture the way he does. The only knock on him is that the first two exams were overly difficult, however he curved them and the 3rd exam was very well written.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ian is hands down the best math professor I've had here at Vandy. He's very natural at explaining things in a pragmatic easy to see manner. one HW a week, 2 tests a semester, no surprises. Even reviews what he will put on test. In other math classes I received C's. With Ian, I am getting A's and B's. Really made me like math again
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dawn wrote the best marketing book available and understands all the concepts. If you ask her for help, she will go out of her way, even years after taking her class. Her way to do a marketing plan is the best way I've seen.
Great course. And Dawn is brilliant.
Useless
Literally wrote the book on the topic, but the book is the only value you should expect to receive. She is very condescending, a little crazy, and disorganized.

I wrote this comment to Professor Iacobucci's University of Pennsylvania profile where I guess she was before. Their gain is now Vanderbilt's loss. Literally wrote the book on the topic, but the book is the only value you should expect to receive. She is very condescending, a little crazy, and disorganized.

Thought-provoking content. An abysmal, insulting, and tone-deaf person. Those that befriended her outside of class fared better - maybe try that? My personal gripe: gave me 0 for semester attendance because I was in the hospital for testing. She said I didn't tell her in advance, but I didn't know I was going to have a medical emergency in advance.

She is one of the best profs I have had so far at Vanderbilt (top 2). One of the smartest people I've ever met, and so demanding in a really positive and constructive way. Extremely opinionated, but I genuinely think she does a good job listening and understanding students. Really gave me a passion for philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The main problem is that she refuses to take questions during class, so if you're confused by anything you won't be able to get a clarification.

If the philosophy department was a mountain range, she would be one of its peaks in terms of the amount of legwork required to fully appreciate her brilliance. Studying under her requires a fundamental understanding of both ancient and medieval philosophy as well as precise conceptual understanding of many terms within critical theory.
Brilliant woman who just wasn't cut out to be a professor.

Really awful undergrad professor.  Even for a senior PHIL major, her lectures are extremely confusing full of jargon and obscure references. Makes a point to make anyone who comments or asks a question feel really stupid.  Toughest paper grader in the department. Unless you're a grad student, AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Wanted to add something just b/c I was shocked to find she had been rated so low. She is brilliant and you're missing out if you fail to take her. She is opinionated but is open to hearing contrasting opinions as well - if you are just being ignorant (****/****) she won't let it fly but she is very open as long as you remain respectful! GREAT!

painfully boring class. she essentially turned "prison and exile writing" into "persecuted jews and females in history". she's really smart but is super vague and goes over peoples' heads. i guess i got lucky because she liked my papers and gave me A's, but she graded very harshly for others.
This class was painfully boring to sit through every time. She is hard to understand and phrases her questions in the most round-about, vague way. Don't take her...

She's clearly intelligent, but has difficulty teaching. Although structured as a discussion class, most of the time it was painfully silent while she asked impossible questions and went off on irrelevant tangents that had little or nothing to do with the text. Her "strong personality" means she disregards even valid opinions that clash with her own

Do not take her class!! She is super biased of her own opinions and will not accept critiques of them.  Papers you write for her must be exactly in line with her ideals or you lose points. She's also demeaning to you if you believe in democracy or conservative ideals. If you like senile, stubborn, old women choose her.

I like that the comments on Idit are so polarized; that's just the kind of person she is. Strong personalities are always polarizing and she certainly has that. She takes time to get used to, but I think she's one of the most brilliant people at Vanderbilt. She can be intimidating but in fact she's always willing to address dissenting views.

She's a little bit crazy, but she is one of the most gifted teachers I've ever had. As the saying goes, "she's forgotten more than I'll ever know." Truly brilliant. She might go over your head a lot, but she'll do her best to help you understand. Take her class just to see that not all professors don't care.
No Comments
Weirdo.  Couldn't understand much of what she said.  Passionate and brilliant, but not in any way that adds to her ability to educate.  Should stick to research, writing papers.
Intelligent professor. Difficulty in communicating assignments to students. Strict grader. Willing to work with student to make him/her understand.

Will go off on tangents, hard to understand, will successfully make 5 out of 10 people in class fall asleep while the other third of the class never shows up (attendence is mandatory). Not very opened minded to the idea of freshmen.

Dr. Dobbs-Weinstein is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt.  She really wants her students to understand and appreciate the material that she presents and outside of class she is extremely helpful.  She is also a really great person to get to know.
terrible...just terrible
She is one of the most intelligent people I've ever met.  Very helpful outside of class--get to know her!
Had her for my first year writing seminar and overall wouldnt recommend. Very unclear on what she expects and she was also disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Taking her class made me want to transfer out of Vandy. Even though the class is not actually that hard, prof. Nwankwo is so unlikeable and careless. Made no effort during COVID to make people's lives better. Do not take her class, whatever you do.

Prof Nwankwo gave us a thoughtful selection of African American literature to study and was wonderful at moderating our class discussions. She cares about her students and the subject so deeply, which made all of the reading and writing more than worth it. Added bonus: she wasn't a tough grader.

Professor Nwankwo really cares about her students' opinions and insights and gives ample opportunity to share. She has high expectations for her students but isn't unreasonable about them. She is also highly knowledgeable about her content, and I can't recommend her enough!

Professor Nwankwo is a great professor and person in general. She covered a large range of material written by Caribbean authors and taught it very well. I highly recommend taking this English class or any taught by her.

Great scholar in her own right, but incorporated a lot of non-literary materials like documentaries in class without being clear about what you were supposed to do with them. Didn't really feedback on your ideas for papers when you went to office hours. Expected you to keep a learning journal without instructions; it was mostly just more writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Immigration and US Identity is an extraordinarily interesting class. Heavy reading and papers are long and require work, but pretty sure every student in the class who showed up and completed the work got an A. Although the readings and papers are long, the material is interesting so it's not too bad to do the work.

Prof Nwankwo is very sweet and understanding. If you complete assignments, she is a very fair and even easy grader. She really wants her students to learn the subject matter at hand, though she can be unclear about what her expectations are. Overall, she is understanding, willing to work with students, wants you to do well, and is a lenient grader

I took her Freshman writing seminar and it was an extremely easy class. Attendance is mandatory, but it was relatively late in the morning so that was fine. She is very knowledgeable about the subject but is EXTREMELY vague on what she wants, especially in papers. However, she grades easy so as long as you can get the general gist you'll be fine.

Wonderful Prof and lots of personality.Highly proficient in what she does and very schlolarly. You will surely enjoy her thoughtful and insightful approach to text and content.She does know her onions!

Professor Nwankwo is intimidating at first, but was ultimately one of the most understanding professors I have ever had at Vandy. She truly cares about her students, though it may not be obvious at all times, and she is incredibly knowledgeable in her field. The amount of work she expects is appropriate, and she grades fairly- overall, great prof.

Very easy class. She is not clear about her assignments usually causing class wide confusion. However, the course load is manageable, and she is very flexible especially when there's confusion. allowed to miss 3 classes without  the absences being counted against you. Take the class for your GPA!
Mostly busy work. But if you're willing to put in the time and effort, it's an easy A. She can be a bit unclear sometimes about what she expects.
It is entirely unclear what she expects from you in her classes.
No Comments
Does not explain expectations properly. Other than that, it's like a high school English class. She treats you like a five year old and assigns unreasonable amounts of work. Avoid.
vague. avoid.

Dr. Cortez is a fantastic professor, and he is clearly very passionate about the subject matter. I appreciate how he always incorporates the perspectives of intersectional identities in film. I feel that I improved exponentially as a writer in this class, and Dr. Cortez encouraged me to push deeper in my analyses of film.
Iggy is the man. Incredibly knowledgable and respected. Highly recommend the class if you're interested in cinema. One of the smarter people I've conversed with.

Prof Cortez is awesome! His cinema class was one of my favorite I've taken at Vanderbilt. The movies he chooses have real modern applications in discussions and Cortez always promotes amazing conversation in class. He is funny and caring. Great class! Would take him again 100%

Iggy has the best screening requirements out of all CMA classes. However, he's also one of the least accessible professors, and can also be shallow in terms of human-to-human relationships. He's super subjective and is not really excited to see you at office hours unless you're there to be friendly, so to get an A, you should get ready to kiss up!

This is a great elective. The work is very manageable: weekly discussion posts, 1-2 papers, a midterm and a final, but you learn a lot and the material is super engaging. Iggy is one of the most intelligent people Ive ever interacted with and he is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject. Hes super personable and always willing to help!

He does not respect accommodations granted by the university. The material is naturally interesting; he makes it uninteresting by talking about himself incessantly. He equates being rigorous with failing students. There are better professors in the department.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ikard will push you to read in ways that you have never done. Quizzes and tests will be extremely specific, get ready for quote ID's- but your mind, knowledge, and wisdom will grow from his class. If you do not like reading THOROUGHLY- don't take. Participate, try your hardest, and read- and you will be fine. One of my favorite professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very tough grader - also the minimum to get an A was a 96. He gives pop quizzes on the readings with questions so specific that you may only get a 50% even if you did the readings. He cares about his students though and will let you revise the first paper if you get less than a 90.

Dr. Ikard is an incredibly engaging speaker with numerous fresh thoughts. He will expand your perspective on the world. He has very high expectations in terms of doing the readings and comprehensive writing, but as long as you do what he assigns as he asks you'll be fine. He just doesn't tolerate laziness, and I have a lot of respect for him.

His classes are not difficult, but challenging. Reads are 30-50 pgs maximum but you'll have ample time. The essays are not graded on a strict rubric, make your work cogent. Non readers and procrastinators, don't take the class. If critical race and academia interest you, take the class. He's passionate and I wish I could take more of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His immense knowledge is clouded by his massive ego. Talks about himself for most of class, inconsistent grader, returns assignments weeks after they are submitted, feedback is vague, if you miss more than 3 lectures he drops your final grade by an entire letter. Constantly makes errors that his ego will not allow him to acknowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This review is actually for AADS 3556. Professor Ikard genuinely inspired my career path and illuminated the way that I think about race. His class pushed me to be a more critical thinker and better writer to degrees that I didn't think I was capable of. His class is tough, don't take this for an easy A. Take this if you love to push yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved this course. Definitely be ready to read a decent amount and do so pretty thoroughly (he gives quizzes on the reading randomly so reading is mandatory!!). We had 4 short (~650 words) analytical essays, one cumulative test, an analytical bibliography, and a research paper. All the assignments take time but are not bad if you do the reading.

He gives minimal feedback, is busy with his "art" and grades whenever he feels like it, has a HUGE ego (which he admits), has favorites (he also admits this), and his grading is EXTREMELY unclear. Your writing grades will be determined on his view of "good" or "interesting". I would advise staying away from his courses.

All of the negative reviews are true, but I have never learned more from a class. His class is extremely challenging, but I came out of it having grown exponentially as a writer. Even is tangents in class are really educational, and taught me a lot about life. His lectures are full of energy. An A is achievable as long as you go to class and read

I took one of his freshman yr writing seminars. The class content was intriguing, but I didn't enjoy coming to class because I found that he spent a lot of time talking about how poorly we were doing. He was a very hard grader and I had no idea what differentiated my good papers from my bad ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible attitude.

Dr. Ikard is my favorite Vanderbilt professor so far. He can be a harsh grader but is super accessible and willing to help with anything you ask for. The readings are super interesting and always worth it because the discussions offer so much insight and perspective. If you put in the work, you can definitely do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very intellectual class. Most course reading I've ever had: three full books and two partially. Came in with the mindset that I'd be prepared incredibly well as a writer and critical analyzer; it wasn't worth the extra sweat, blood and tears. Essay feedback was often "lot of room for improvement;" none for papers. Other FYWS's offer better balance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am a little on the fence about Prof Ikard. I took him for Intro to AADS and now I'm taking him for Black Comparative Writers. Cons: harsh grader, very cocky, spends a LOT of class time talking about himself. Pros: very helpful outside of class, makes it known that he wants you to succeed. Also, there's a lot of work and reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Clearly intelligent and very sharp, but has one of the biggest egos Ive ever encountered. Im in his freshman writing seminar on race, sport, and american culture and he makes it clear in our lectures that he doesnt care for the baby class too much and has much better things to do. Hard to reach outside of class. Harsh grading, little feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Ikard is hands down my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He gets slack for being a tough grader, but he makes his expectations super clear and as long as you follow those and DO THE READINGS you'll be fine. He is super provocative and not afraid to call out racism and white supremacy for what it is. He honestly changed my whole perspective.

Although attendance is mandatory, class time is rarely used productively. Ikard will literally spend a whole class period talking about himself. Tough and random grading. Unclear why he marks points off and even if you talk to him, it still seems unreasonable. Takes pride in making things harder than they need to be for no good reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ikard is a phenomenal professor. Black Masculinity is a fantastic class, and if you have the chance, TAKE IT! Its fascinating and SO relevant. He will really push you & sometimes youll feel like its unnecessary, but by the end you will see how many valuable things you learned. He can be cocky but hes very accomplished, so its not unwarranted!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Best language teacher I have had and probably will ever have. You don't have to be especially talented to do well in this class. As long as you show up, do assignments and study for quizzes (neither of which are difficult), you will get an A. Nozomi-san actually wants students to learn and due to the small class size, she can connect with everyone.

She is an expert in creating immersive learning environments. This will be a great chance to actually learn the language instead of just knowing how to solve test problems. Very caring and supportive, so don't worry about making mistakes. Definitely will take again.

great n caring professor, but the class itself is very difficult. there is new content almost everyday. stay on top of homework. many graded assignments so be prepared for the vocab, kanji, and chapter quizzes beforehand. try not to get behind as many grammar structures are necessary for the next one. imai is understanding and super funny too!

I highly recommend Imai sensei if you have any interest in Japanese. This was my favorite class of the semester. Lots of skits, presentations, etc. but Dr. Imai creates a safe environment to practice. It's a 5 hour credit class, so be prepared to put in work every day. If you show up, study, and turn things in on time an A is totally doable.

Fantastic professor. Makes learning the language fun with lots of skits and conversational practice during class. Your speaking abilities will improve. There's daily HW, but it's not difficult, and she gives clear feedback and allows you to make up for points missed. Being active in class and reviewing notes will get you an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: SHE IS A GREAT PROFESSOR. DONT HESITATE TO TAKE HER LESSON

I took Imai-sensei's class last year, and I really wasn't sure what to expect going in. She made my first year of Japanese really fun, and motivated me to keep learning Japanese. It's a 5 credit hour course, so expect to do a bit of work- after all, learning a language is pretty difficult. You also get to practice the vocab and grammar in class.

Great sensei for anyone interested in Japanese. Makes class a lot of fun with mini-skits and role playing. Gives lots of constructive feedback, but make sure to stay on top of work, since Japanese as a language is hard--great sensei or not.

Learning a foreign language in itself is a very challenging matter. I would only suggest you take it if you like japanese culture. That said, she does do her best in teaching the class. The classes are very inclusive, in which she will call on you to speak up and role play. She will try her best to correct you and keep you on the right track.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I sincerely don't know where those bad comments came from. She's the most caring and patient teacher I've met at Vandy. Yes there is homework everyday, but most of the time you can finish them in half an hour or less. It's a five-credit class and learning a new language takes efforts. I would recommend her to everyone who wants to learn Japanese!

Imai is a quite good teacher. She explains gramma points clearly and always responds to students' questions. There would be a lot of interactions during the lecture, which practises your speaking very much. Homework everyday, some quizes every weeks, several unit tests and two oral tests one semester. Caring person and willing to provide supports.

I love Imai-sensei! She is a very sweet and caring professor. She expects a lot from her students, but she supports them unlike anyone else! All Japanese courses have daily homework and approximately 2-3 quizzes per week, so only take the language if are willing to work hard and put in the effort!

The participation grade is a pain in the ass. No matter how much effort you put into it, if you can't speak Japanese super fluently without many accents, you will get 85%. If you don't try at all, you will get 80%. Students' effort is hardly noticed, and it's just not worth the time and energy.

Imai is an extremely lovely person. She's super nice and enthusiastic is class. She cares about her students a lot. You will be able to improve a lot during the drills if you pay attention. But if you are not into Japanese and just want to take a random language course and get an easy A, think twice about taking Japanese.

She's new here, so she's very strict. The class is a lot of work, you get 2 to 3 quizzes every week, mandatory homework every night, a ton of vocab to memorize. Her instructions are very unclear, she can't speak English very well, and she gets salty and become passive-aggressive quite often. Very hard to get A/B. Avoid at all cost and take Spanish.
For the quizzes READ THE BOOK. Everything else is straight forward, show up and do work, and you should do well.
He is alright, I mean he makes everyone watch Old Greg in class so what more could you ask for?
Bob is the best discussion group leader you could have! He knows what he is talking about and likes his students. I highly suggest getting him as your lab leader!

Perhaps the most overrated professor at Vandy.  He's a nice guy, but is really unclear on what he wants and always goes off-topic, then slams you with hard tests and essay questions that are graded by TERRIBLE TAs.  Take someone else instead - Cannon is supposed to be a lot clearer.

There is a lot of work (papers), but if you get the work completed, you will get a good grade.  Very helpful inside and outside of class.  Very flexible, humorous, and social.  He is helpful in stirring up topics outside of class that relate to the subject being discussed.  Overall an amazing person and teacher.

I asked for an extension of two hours on my paper due in class, which he rudely refuesed (I had a legit reason, but I respect that he won't let us), but he sent an e-mail to our whole class insulting me for asking.  Then at classtime when it was due, he gave extensions to all the people who weren't finished. Expect nothing from him and you'll get i

Strict & unsympathetic deadlines despite the fact that I had two unpredictable & unfortunate events happen in the same week.  Learned nothing from him, all from the text book & projects.  He was vague, as was his syllabus.  his class was very unstructured, & he was very unhelpful & hard to reach outside of class.  Thinks very highly of himself.
bob is the man!!

Easiest course ever, if you read.  Interesting lectures & material, corny jokes.  Not necessary to show up for group discussion until last 15 min. to take the quiz because he always goes off topic anyway.  Easy to approach.
not only is he a great teacher but his sister is Carol on ER!
Take 1200 with Bob!  He created HOD so he really knows what he's teaching and applies the material to real companies well.  One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt!
I LOVE BOB!
No Comments
Bob was a great professor.  His lectures were interesting, complete with music videos and interesting anecdotes.
No Comments
Do not be intimidated at first, you will like him more as the semester goes on.

he's really a funny, sweet guy. SUPER smart, hard to understand at first from the accent but you adjust fast. your grade is 3 exams, hw, quizzes, and a final. go to class, do the hw, and go to review sessions, you'll be fine. he will curve exams, despite what he says in the beginning - tests are very hard. it's not impossible, but by no means easy.
Do your homework and you will get an A. However, his accent makes the class hard to understand. Not as hard as people may think

You wanna love him, but the class is just so miserable. He will remember your name and if you're always in class he will like you and will definitely help you after hours. But seriously, he just falls behind. And its really hard.

Chifan is an incredibly nice guy, and he genuinely cares about his students' success. Unfortunately, he is a miserable lecturer, and when he gets behind (which happens often), he gets even worse. Quizzes and tests are incredibly hard, and the way he curves things is absolutely absurd. Great man though. Easy to get a B or C, but very hard for an A.

Chifan's heart is definitely in the right place, but I'm just not sold on him as a teacher. We kept falling more and more behind where we should have been, we never went over the last chapter (even though we only did chap 13-17). The final was then largely based on the last chapter. :( You need natural ability and hard work to get by here.

He's such a sweetheart...his accent is hard to get used to at first but he always wants to help and does everything he can to help his students learn. As long as you do your work and study, you'll do fine. If you ever go to his office hours be prepared to be there for awhile though...he likes to rant about politics. but SUPER NICE. love him.

average teacher when reaches the information however when he finds himself behind he rushes through it and offers a very poor explanation. most people in my class had already taken the class scewing the curve immensely. Hes incredibly self righteous and very hypocritical. he expects u to know things he doesnt!
He's Romanian so the accent takes some getting used to, but he's a pretty fair teacher. Assigns homework like once a week, test problems come from the homework. Very easy if you do your work

I read what everyone else wrote on here and I think it's very misleading. He is a FANTASTIC teacher, his accent just makes it somewhat hard to understand him. He is 100% willing to help you understand the material outside of class. One time, I was sick and missed class and he went out of his way to help me understand what I missed and make up work.

Just awful.  Seems great at the start of the course, and I think he genuinely wants to help students, but he just can't teach effectively to people who aren't on the same level as him, mathematically.

Ionut did a great job with this class. He's a really nice guy and cares about his students. Go to office hours, he's quite helpful. Complex analysis is very difficult but this class was, overall, doable.
Horrible professor. Horrible at teaching and reviewing. Bad class organization. Problems were far too difficult and expected far too much information for the course.

The projects class is a kinda underwhelming course. No lecturing, half the time you just work on your own team's project and the other you present your progress with very limited constructive feedback from the professor. She also speaks like XQC, the way she mumbles makes it more difficult to understand than the professor with the heaviest accent.

Projects in Machine Learning fulfills a senior graduation requirement, so the difficulty was not high. You make an ML project and have presentations every 2 weeks showcasing your work. There's also a mandatory participation grade, so you have to raise your hand. It's repetitive, but very easy, and Dr. Oguz is super nice and chill in class.

She's fine. Her project course is presentations every day, which wasn't fun or informative at all. Just feels like an endless stream of busy work and makes the project of completing a senior project less entertaining than it should be. Offered little to no constructive advice or feedback, as well. Attendance mandatory. Just mid; don't recommend.
Class was pretty easy (very little homework), lectures are very engaging, and the subject matter is interesting even if you're nowhere near the field like me.
Nice professor, pretty easy class. I never payed attention and still came away with a B, but I was taking the class pass/fail so didn't put a ton of effort in. She's an excellent choice for Discrete.

Oguz is one of my favorite professors I've had. She's extremely kind and accessible outside of class. She's also one of the easiest lecturers to follow- she makes in engaging with games/examples. Discrete was challenging, but would absolutely take a class with her again.

Great professor and educator. She presents material well and is friendly and engaging with the class. Compared to other sections, Prof. Oguz's section seemed to have a better grasp so arguably the best professor to take for discrete.
Professor Oguz is one of the nicest professors at Vandy. She cares about her students and makes class materials easier to understand.
Be prepared to put extra extra extra effort!

Lectures were disorganized but not much worse than the rest of the professors in the math department I have taken. A mix of an accent, handwriting, and the organization makes the class hard to follow. Tests are pretty fair though, if you can manage to do the homework given the suboptimal textbook, lecture, and grading.

Surprised by the decent overall score on RMP, in reality lectures were confusing and felt disorganized. Maybe its a matter of personal preference but the lectures were hard to follow and the textbook was pretty bare bones. Tests are reasonable though.

Great lectures. If you attend every lesson, then you'll find that everything is connected in a systematic way and you are guaranteed to learn a lot. Grading is easy. If you demonstrate your understanding of the content you'll get the mark regardless having minor mistakes. Homework is a little too much, but they're good practice of exams.

The class is pretty hard, but that's just the course itself. Overall, the class could be improved, as she doesn't do the best job at breaking down the concepts. However, she truly cares about your progress in the class and even curves at the end of the semester. I thought I had a B until the end of the semester, where I found out she curved to A-!
Prof. Suvaina is well-intentioned and cares about her students but is simply a confusing lecturer. The exams aren't too bad but the textbook is more clear than her lectures.

While she cares a lot, class is so confusing and she gets very wrapped up in topics that end up being insignificant, or at least they are not connected back to the core concepts. Reading the textbook was way less confusing than going to lecture. She is very kind and wants everyone to succeed, just not a great lecturer.

Very nice and definitely willing to help outside of class. Just isn't always the best at explaining concepts and is not good at answering questions. Tests are crazy time crunch and super hard to actually finish. Overall, she cares but she is not great at breaking down complicated concepts

Even though she cares a lot about her students, she is probably the most confusing professor ever. Don't take this class unless you are ok with teaching yourself every lesson. In class instruction is useless. Don't even bother going to class.

My rating is solely based on the fact that Professor Suvaina cannot teach--her lectures were line by line repetitions of the textbook delivered in a fashion that was more confusing than the textbook. I quite literally read the textbook multiple times during lecture instead of listening as it was more helpful. High test averages. Unclear grading.

Even though she has a heavy accent and her handwriting can be hard to read, her lectures are overall pretty good because her logic is not hard to follow. Tests are really standard and if you pay attention in class and review the homework problems, you will succeed!

Her European accent is heavy and makes students hard to understand her initially. She is very nice and accessible after class, but she cannot explain the concepts and teach clearly. However, she does know a lot about the subject and she enjoys teaching it. Office hours help, tests are about homework questions and not super hard. Take the class
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are fair, lectures are a must. The class doesn't get too challenging until the last couple sections of material. Her final felt impossible, but it was likely due to lack of understanding of the last couple sections. Still, great professor with good intentions

Loved it. Dr. Suvaina is really enthusiastic about what she teaches and wants her students to feel the same way. Her lectures go a bit overboard with theory and not many examples, but the weekly homework is manageable, and tests, though not easy by any means, are consistently based on the homework. Read the textbook and do the homework.

Tests were long and not horrible until the last section. There were no curves. Weekly quizzes were also usually hard to finish on time. Homework was graded fairly easily. Suvaina is helpful and wants you to succeed, but the course is very difficult.

Professor Suvaina is extremely nice and truly wants you to succeed in her class. Tests are a little bit challenging but doable and she gives partial credits. Weekly homework and quiz mainly from the textbook.
Suvaina was extremely nice and cared about our success. The class is pretty manageable until the last section, where it gets really hard. The tests were tough.

It can be hard to get past Suvaina's accent in the beginning and she really tends to be confusing in lectures. She's not too helpful in office hours either, and the tests and quizzes are much harder versions of the homework problems. The tests are also really long, with not enough time given. There's a fairly decent curve at the end though.

She is a helpful teacher, however she has trouble explaining concepts. You need to read the textbook and do textbook problems. 3 Tests, 1 final, a quiz every week. My test grades got better as the semester went on. Content is kind of hard at first but then gets very manageable, until about the last month which is extremely hard material.
I like this professor! She is very easy.

She's very nice and offers good geometric and algebraic explanations for most concepts. The material is basically cal1 and 2 just with a third dimension (until the end when it gets 10x harder). She gives partial credit on quizzes and tests and holds review sessions before each test and the final. Homework graded for accuracy, but it's helpful.

Ioana expects all of her students to be math majors, so be careful. Helpful in office hours, but far from it in the classroom. A huge final curve can save your grade, though. Tests are difficult, quizzes are fine. She's a very nice woman, but your grade may be in danger.

Very helpful outside class; answers any questions and will work over homework problems. Very flexible about turning in homework; you just have to turn it in the day of. Has weekly/bi-weekly quizzes. Tests are very difficult though and she doesn't give points easily. Not very flexible with grades or curving. Definitely not an easy A class

Her class is not easy, but she is without a doubt the best Math professor I have had at Vanderbilt.  Her notes are well organized, and she goes out of her way to help her students out - she'll work through any homework problem with you in office hours, and she even hosts review sessions for each of her tests. Definitely take her.
A difficult teacher. She's helpful during office hours, but not so much in the classroom. It's a hard subject, and reading the book is mandatory if you want to do well.

She is very knowledgeable and a very good teacher. Is hard to understand once in a while but for the most part is pretty accessible. It's hard to understand some of the concepts because her explanations aren't always perfectly accessible, but she's pretty good. Definitely do the homework the same day as class to let it sink in

Being a mechanical engineer I thought I would be able to get by in this class by just doing the homework and studying. Not the case here for me. She is really helpful but goes too fast sometimes, especially at the end of the class. Math majors may have an easy time, but I got an 800 on the SAT and I squeaked by after studying a week for the final

Ioana is one the of the best professors I ever had. Her lectures are decent, and she's extremely patient when we seek help during her office hours. She gives moderate amount of homework and the exams are doable.

Prof. Suvinia is extremely knowledgeable about Linear Algebra, and really tried hard to make us understand the material. In doing so, a lot of difficult proofs were required, which take a lot of time and thought. That being said, work is fairly heavy but you really come out feeling like you learned the material. Office hours are bomb too..

Ioana was a great multivariable professor. Assigned a good chunk of homework due every week, but that way we were forced to do the problems and that helped a lot on the tests. She has an accent but is definitely understandable and a really nice woman. Office hours helped a ton and she's very accessible. Liked her and her class a lot.

RUSS1111 is one of my favorite classes taken at Vanderbilt. 3 papers a semester, you each get 1 draft and 1 final. All the drafts and finals count toward grades but she grades your paper in a way that you understand you do have issues at some point. She makes you convinced about her gradings, as all points taken off are given a reason. Solid choice
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Russian Fairy Tales was, for the most part, an easy A. Material was interesting, but class discussion could be a little boring. I barely read and got an A. No tests or quizzes, just reading responses (which can be finessed) and two papers. Take this if you need an International culture AXLE course/ lighter class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Russian Fairy Tales is really interesting but it is harder than it used to be - especially the second half of the course where she expects you to read novels pretty quickly. Weekly responses aren't too difficult and she grades pretty easy. Would recommend overall. Only negative is her occasional tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great teacher, and very accommodating to her students. The class is graded easily and I definitely would recommend taking her for 150. Final was cumulative but TAKE HOME (however, was not easy). The midterm as OPEN BOOK. Lectures are boring but the grading of this class makes up for that. Definitely easy to get a good grade if you try.

Foster is awesome! She tries her best to make the class interesting and you do learn. The tests were open note, which was nice, but meant they were really long. There are several days where she takes your attendance for a grade. Overall, I would definitely recommend this class!

Foster pretends to be easy, but ends up giving out much lower grades than expected. Her problem sets are not hard but her final project will take you over 30 hours to do. She doesn't hand back project grades quickly at all. She is just very vague with all homework and tests and what she expects.

Ease of the class varies on prior stat knowledge, but is very easy if you've taken stat before. She is very helpful, clear in her lectures, and a very nice person in general. The workload is not tough at all, but the final project requires a lot of work. Definitely recommended if you need 150.
Weekly problem sets are simple.  If you've had any stats class before, this class is a breeze.  Four projects, three tests (which are open book), partner on the final.  Very clear and helpful.
good teacher, clear, good class. Take her

Pretty amazing professor. At first, she seems boring, but by the end you will love her! There is a fair amount of homework, but it is pretty easy and she makes tests all open book and open notes. She really wants you to do well, and will help you anytime you need it. I would definitely definitely take another class with her!
Great teacher. Fair Grader, not hard assignments, and very clear in class.

Dr Reinhardt is great! This class was a great intro to myth and genuinely very interesting. Lots of reading but wasn't necessary to succeed if you read spark notes. Class lectures and discussions were great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved taking Greek Myths with Prof. Reinhardt. She is clearly very passionate about the topic, so lectures were surprisingly interesting for me. Exams (2) are straightforward and fair. Attendance and hard-copy of the books were required (5 books, but I don't think she ever checked if you had it). Would take again!

She's incredibly passionate about this class, which makes it very enjoyable. The weekly readings are manageable and there are weekly 1-question quizzes, but the lowest one gets dropped. The class feels easy until midterm and finals week because the midterm, final, and one major paper determine most of your grade, but She's a lenient grader
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading that's pretty difficult if you haven't read straight philosophy before. Tbh, you don't need to do the reading to participate in class. Participation is huge and there's no tests or quizzes, so just go to class, raise your hand a couple times, and do the final assignment (the first and only writing assignment) and you'll get an A.

Dr. Reinhardt is a fantastic professor. Very accessible outside of class and always does a great job of making difficult concepts understandable. I highly recommend her Plato course to anyone interested in ancient philosophy.

Professor Reinhardt is a great Latin teacher. She explains concepts clearly and is always willing to work with you to help you understand. Expect homework every night, but nothing extreme and it's not graded at all. She lays out exactly whats on every test, and as long as you pay attention its easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is the best. This class was engaging, there are readings you need to do before each class and a 1-question weekly reading quiz that's easy if you do the reading. Readings are also interesting if you like greek mythology and the prof is so nice!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: LOVE professor Reinhardt. She is super sweet and her lectures are fun and engaging. If you are interested in greek myth, definitely take this course! The midterms are not too hard and the quizzes can be done correctly as long as you review spark notes.
I LOVE professor Reinhardt. Her lectures are amazing, despite the reading heavy course. Her passion for the subjects makes all the work worth it. One of my favorite classes.

Far and away the best professor I have ever had.  Took her for CLAS 1120 as well and she is so much fun.  She takes what could be boring content and makes it so interesting.  She's super caring about students (to the point that she will give u an extension the day a paper is due if you ask for it) and if u contribute in class she will grade u easy.

Dr. Reinhardt is young and experienced at the same time. She is more than willing to answer any and all questions and she makes sure to pick the best mythology books for us to read. Her class discussions are intuitive and her lectures are fun. Her exams (2) make your hand cramp and the typed essays are loooong and the quizzes are kind of annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor. Engaging and passionate during lectures. Tests are straightforward and primarily about knowing characters/terms/passages. I haven't found her essay grading too harsh -- as long as you make a clear and forceful argument. Weekly reading quizzes are easy to predict, even if you just read the Sparknotes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Reinhardt's Greek Myths course, I always looked forward to coming to class every day because her lectures were so engaging and student driven. As a humanities major, the readings were very manageable and I appreciated the variety of myths. She is very accessible outside of class and cares a lot about her students.

Professor Reinhardt is a great professor for an introduction to the classics. She also is a great professor for freshman or anyone trying to get AXLE requirements done. This class is graded by a midterm/final and two papers. The second paper is fun and the midterms just require a day or two of studying. Pay attention every class and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Reinhardt is a very nice person who knows a lot about the subject she teaches. However, this class ended up being significantly more of a pain than many of my STEM major classes due to her harsh grading, limited number of assignments, and 30-50 pages of reading almost every night. Not the easy HCA credit people will tell you it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading, but to get an A on the tests you only need to know the big ideas. The reading quiz every week is easy if you read the text, you can't just look up the summary online. Reinhardt is caring, makes the class super compelling, and great at getting big ideas across. Plus the papers are short and fun, even for a stem major.

Professor Reinhardt is a wonderful professor. She truly cares about her students and she will always help you out if you need anything. She understands that sometimes life gets in the way and will give you an extension if you need one. She is relatable and makes the class fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Reinhardt not only makes you read over fifty pages a night but there are also weekly quizzes with only one question on them that has nothing to do with the plot. I received an F on quiz grades because I got two quizzes wrong. Also she is an extremely difficult grader and is not lenient at all. Her lectures are fine, but she is no help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Reinhardt is very passionate about what she teaches. The entire class is a discussion-style seminar about the readings done outside of class. There are reading quizzes every week, two major papers (graded very harshly), a final/midterm, and the rest of the grade is participation and attendance. Be warned, 5+ books are required.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When explaining more complicated parts of lecture notes she often confuses herself, and once even skipped over a part because she couldn't figure it out. Because of this tendency, she often now just does not explain the hardest bits and breezes over them, only covering the intuitive parts that we could interpret ourselves from the lecture slides.
She's awesome

Extremely nice and always there to offer help if you need it. She genuinely wants her students to do well, and she is very knowledgeable and makes the class interesting. I highly, highly recommend her.

Although her lectures tend to be a little bit boring, the class is pretty easy overall. There are 7 homework assignments, of which you must turn in 5. The homeworks are pretty accurate representations of what you will find on the test. Tests are clear-cut and straight from her personal notes, which she uploads online.
Very smart lady. High level concepts, high level thinker.
Would not recommend. Very boring lectures and tests are ambiguous and difficult to prepare for.

She's a nice lady but is extremely unclear and ambiguous on tests. Questions are very difficult to understand because of language barrier and her tests are written in ineffectively. The class is interesting but definitely difficult for the wrong reasons and there certainly needs to be a restructuring. The other teacher is much better.

Her English is really not that bad if you pay attention. The class is super interesting if you like macroeconomics. I learned a LOT about various macroeconomic theories and how they applied to Latin America. It's definitely a good class to talk about in interviews. HW graded on completion, but the tests are pretty hard. My favorite class at vandy!

She is a nice lady and cares about the students. However, she has a very strong Brazilian accent and limited English skills which makes it difficult to understand here. Lectures are very boring. Tests are not the easiest, but you can drop the 1st if the 2nd is higher or the 2nd if 3rd is higher. Keep up with the reading. Would not recommend.

Would not recommend taking this class. The lectures are incredibly unclear and the tests are confusing and not easy. I could barely comprehend multiple questions on the final. Prof. Zissimos' intentions are good, but since the class is neither easy nor enjoyable, I wouldn't take it.

Lectures are not great but material is interesting. Really enjoyed the lecture on the econ of drug trade. Tests are not too hard if you study on your own from her notes and skim the readings. Homework is graded on completion. Easy class but I didn't learn as much as I wanted lot to be honest. Prof is really nice and helpful though.

Do not take this class. She can barely speak english which makes understanding what she is saying next to impossible. Furthermore, the tests are extremely confusing because she uses google translate to write the questions. The TA was more helpful than her

This class is structured a bit different than it was before. There are 3 exams, however, she let you have the highest of either the first or second exam. This is not normal, she decided this mid semester. She is a bit unclear on what you need to know so some answers on the test are impossible to prepare for. However, it wasn't that hard

Easiest econ course I've taken.  Tests are 3 1-page essays, graded generously, and there are 3 exams, of which the highest 2 are counted to your grade (thus, the final is optional). Homeworks are time consuming though, so work in groups.  Lectures can be unclear because of the language barrier, but as easy as the class is I highly recommend it.

Class can be painfully boring, and her accent makes her difficult to understand, but it is easy enough if you go to class and take notes to complement the slides.  She is very nice and does genuinely seem to care about her students.
Hard but rewarding. You have to show up to class and  need to take pretty extensive notes but class can be interesting. Not bad if you study and pay attention

Isaac is SO nice, knowledgable, and has great stories.  But he makes interesting topics SO BORING.  He lectures the entire class off slides.  You also have to buy $200 worth of books.  Final exam is easy.  I think covid really threw him for a loop.  I hate to say it, but I think Isaac is past his teaching prime.  Pretty easy grader.
I really don't know what these kids are talking about. Fooled me into taking his class. More boring class I've ever taken--including high school. And I can't tell you what I've learned.

By far my favorite class this semester. Professor Isaac is incredibly caring, super sweet and funny, and insanely knowledgeable about everything related to the 60s. Papers and midterms aren't difficult if you put effort into them, and I loved our synchronous classes and discussions. Reading the material will help you a lot. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I'm a senior now, but I remember this guy from when I was a freshman. I'll be honest. I hate school and have always hated school, but this was one of the few classes at Vandy I actually liked and is probably the only "A" I've made at Vandy, too. He's a great professor who pushed me to pursue my dreams. After I graduate, I plan to join a commune.

WONDERFUL professor. I got my behind out of bed to be at his 8am class, and never missed a lecture. He knows and loves what he's teaching. It takes a few weeks to know what's important to him enough to quiz you on it, but after that the quizzes are a breeze. And he'll do everything he can to help you.

BEST professor I have had at Vanderbilt. So knowledgeable, SO helpful, clearly a brilliant man. Professor Isaac went out of his way to be helpful to all of his students, and is clearly passionate about his subject matter. I cannot recommend him enough.

He is definitely enthusiastic about this course, but it should be called Social Movements of the 1960s instead. Expect a semester mostly on the Civil Rights Movement. Many topics I thought would be included were  ignored. Reading seems pointless because you rarely write on it and the professor guides you to say what he wants in discussion.

Wonderful professor! I was nervous to be in a class called 'American Social Movements', however, Professor Isaac made the class very interesting. I learned a lot from him and would recommend this class for anyone looking to satisfy a CPLE requirement or interested in affecting social change.

Really nice guy! He's extremely helpful and accessible outside of class. He's really into this subject and enthusiastic about it. When I would go into his office hours consulting paper topics, he seemed to have knew EVERYTHING about the Sixties. Issac is a very qualified professor, and I highly recommend taking this writing seminar!
Great class!  Isaac loves the material and is very available to help if needed.  His enthusiasm ensures that class is never boring
The class was interesting and he really dedicated himself to the subject.  Easily accessible outside of class, always willing to help with any questions or proofreading.  Take this class!

very enthusiastic about the subject matter, he gets really into it, and you can tell he loves the material..  he's extremely helpful and is willing to read drafts of papers, etc.  i would recommend taking his class!

I had Dr Isaac at FSU, and he was a great professor. His classes are interesting, even if the subject matter isn't (i.e. Research Methods). You'll learn alot with him. He's great to talk to outside of class. He makes the learning personal, so you'll grow as a student and a person. His classes on social movements were the best I took as an undergrad (and I had 160 credits when I graduated). Take a class with him, you'll be happy you did. FSU is worse off without him. Vanderbilt students lucked out.
Great, goofy guy!  I would definitely take this class for a freshman seminar.  He really knows his stuff and his expectations aren't unreasonable.
funny little man...really enjoyed his class. very interesting topic and teaching. expects a lot from tests, but only midterm and final...really wants students to do well and is willing to help.
Ishan is so amazing, take him take him take him. I can't stress enough what an absolute goat he is. He was my TA for 1300 and I learned more from him than I did the professor!!!!!

Teaches the concepts very well, he emphasizes proofs and methods behind specific concepts heavily. His homework is very easy. The tests are difficult, but are very preferable to the other calculus professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 1301 is a hard class in general. Professor Ishan makes the material much easier to understand and is very helpful outside of class. He truly wants his students to do well in his class.

Dr. Medri's class is *difficult*.  The issue during class is that you will do next-to-zero problems, so you'll walk into exams not knowing what to expect.  Four exams plus a final, but you know when they are; feedback is sparse, all you'll know is that you got it wrong basically.  Tests are somewhat predictable but very hard to finish.  Tough class

Honestly, this class was one of the most traumatizing math classes I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. Half of our class withdrew. I'm pretty sure the last few positive reviews were written by mr. medri himself.

Professor Medri is super accessible outside of class and cares about the success of students. He is very approachable, funny, and great at math (sometimes to the detriment of an introductory understanding). His tests are very difficult but he awards substantial partial credit. The PSETs are also tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You really have to go to his office hours. He's not the best lecturer but he does care that his students do well. The course material is really difficult, and exam questions will almost always ask new questions or in ways you haven't seen. If you ask questions, go to office hours, email him, etc you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ivan is great overall, but his class can be hard. He is very accessible outside class, and you should definitely go to his office hour.

This class is really hard. Medri is a decent but not great lecturer. However, most of the math faculty are not great lecturers, and some are far worse than decent. He is also available for many, many hours outside of class for office hours. He is extremely dedicated to students' success--if you ask questions you will get help. Stop complaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ivan truly cares about his students. He is very accessible outside class, and his office hour is always the busiest. He wants to make sure you understand MATH rather than just formulas, so his lectures and tests can be hard sometimes. If you attend classes, read his notes, go to office hours, you will have a great experience.

Ivan Medri is a mess. Thinks student shouldn't understand everything he teaches. Tests fluctuate in difficulty level but are always stressful and nearly impossible to finish in 50 mins. Problem sets are hard as hell too; sometimes he doesn't even know how to do them. Lots of mistakes in lecture. Turns an intro stats class into a GPA nightmare.

Taking his numerical analysis this semester. At the beginning of the semester he said on the syllabus there's gonna be 10-12 assignments. He has in fact given out two assignments and three tests and by now (final's week) only graded ONE. I have no idea how I'm going to do in this class. God bless all those who takes his numerical analysis...

Has trouble explaining concepts clearly, lectures are hard to follow. I typically had to go back and carefully read the textbook after lecture just to understand what we covered. Exams can be difficult however he curves rather heavily.

Prof. Medri was definitely not the best, but he does care that his students succeed and understand the material, even if explaining the material is not his greatest strength. He tries to instill understanding more than test-taking methods or memorization, which I credit him for. His exams and weekly quizzes were difficult, but 1301 is a hard class.

Medri knows his stuff. Maybe too well, as lectures can be quite fast since, in addition to regular material, he focuses on understanding. My best advice is to preread all the material so you are ready.

I was told 2300 would be a lot easier than 1301. With the 1301 tests, you could expect to be able to answer most of the questions still. This dude has to put 30 pt curves on his exams because they simply don't reflect the example problems and notes he gives us. His 2300 section makes his 1301 section seem like a cakewalk.

I had to read the book before every class to have a clear idea of what we would be learning. In a class that's so visually heavy, he did not do a great job of helping us understand the concepts we were learning, instead just giving us the name of the concept and the formula. Office hours were unhelpful. This class shouldn't be as hard as it is

Honestly, one of the smartest math professors at Vanderbilt. His classes are in depth from the derivation and the proof of concepts and very accessible during office hours. I understand why others may not resonate with his teaching style because it is more geared towards learning the concept than passing tests. Take the class if you love calc!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Struggles explaining things at times, has very sloppy hand writing. Pace and workload more fair than other 2300 imo. Doesnt say much about vandys math department tho
Lectures have nothing to do with homework, quizzes, assignments, or tests. Tests are really hard, but he curves them sometimes. A little rude in office hours, but what math professor at vandy isn't.

Professor Medri is very condescending towards his students when they do not understand a concept even though during lectures he fails to cover important information or speeds through material. He's somewhat more helpful in office hours. Exams are extremely difficult, and he did not handle the transition to online class well at all.
Definitely knows his math but glosses over the exam concepts in class. Very good if you want to learn Maths but other than that, very difficult to get an A in the course.

HOD 1300 with Professor Payne was not enjoyable. Yes, I did learn many applicable and relevant aspects to group development, but his unclear grading criteria and interesting lecture style were two dealbreakers. Grading can vary widely by TA, and it is recommended to skim readings.
Not a hard class and your grade mostly depends on the TA but Payne oozes hubris and his gimmicky teaching style makes this class more difficult then it should be
god awful teaching style

Never again. Not a horrible professor but the hubris oozing off of this man made me fight demons the entire semester. Lectures were boring at best, off-topic and unhelpful at worst.  Payne is approachable and relatively understanding but he made my eye twitch.

Funny guy, great human being, alright as a professor. He's widely respected but his teaching style can be rather nebulous and in the air. People who really need structure will likely dislike him and this class, but also stand to gain the most from taking this class with him.
fine? interesting enough lecuturer, kinda condescending

Payne was a super engaging lecturer who clearly cares a lot about the topic and HOD. Most of the assignments were short little papers graded by the TA, and 2 group presentations. There were no tests and the quizzes were homework assignments.

Payne was sick! Definitely one of my most interesting and favorite classes. I really got to know the kids in my class through this course which made a huge difference. I didn't even want to skip this class because it was so interesting

if you want to fail hod, just take it!! worst professor in hod, tough grader, doesn't listen to students and doesn't offer help. Doesn't care about your academics, only thing he talks about is his career path, and how he got different jobs in investment banking and finance.
Such a great professor for HOD 1250. Your experience definitely depends on your TA but Dr. Payne cares so much about his students and is a really engaging lecturer.

Dr. Payne is fantastic! I've had him for HOD 1250, 1300, and 3262. While 1250 and 1300 are straightforward intros, his Social Entrepreneurship and Design Thinking classes are must-takes. He brings valuable industry insights, genuinely cares about his students, and is refreshingly real & unafraid to be honest. Workload is manageable and engaging!

Dr. Payne is one of my favorite professors. Yes, he's a staunch liberal. No, he doesn't provide great guidance on assignments (though that's the nature and point of this entrepreneurship class). However, he cares deeply about the subject matter and his students. Class time is used wisely; if you're productive, you'll finish most work during class.

All he does is talk about how people that look like him (white men) gentrify and ruin modern society. Have to double-check everything he says because he'll use fake stats to prove that point. Other than that though super easy class with no real work and test were not a concern. Really just depends who your TA is for lab cause that can ruin grades.

HOD 3262 is the best HOD class I've taken at Vandy. Low stress yet we learned so much. Prof Payne took all the anxiety away from this course and just let us explore and have fun. He's the G.O.A.T.. Couldn't recommend this class enough. Also, nearly everything is group work so just be prepared for that, though there's not much work in the class.
Great guy, great content. Can get boring at times but the group work is make or break. If you have a good group, the class is great.
Dr. Payne is awesome and his lectures are great however the class can be relatively hard.

This class had no content, its basically just developmental psychology but ultra liberal. Nothing against Dr. Payne personally, this class was just absolutely useless, and made me seriously consider switching majors. The exams were take home and if you have the online textbook, theres literally no reason to do any readings or pay attention in class

This class was SO boring. He tries to make mundane topics interesting but does it in all the wrong ways. The class feels like a more meaningless version of psych. You can definitely tell he cares so much and he is a great guy, but the class sucked. It's a good amount of work but nothing crazy or hard. It's all a waste of time.

Dr Payne is so incredibly passionate about the HOD program, and I could listen to his lectures all day. TAs do all the grading for the many papers due in the class. Tests are open note, book, and online. BUY AN ONLINE TEXTBOOK! Take the time to talk to him outside the class he's pretty cool and has access to many real-world opportunities!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Payne is super passionate about the content, always available to make HOD the best it can be. Content is horribly boring, lectures are hit or miss. Become friends with your TA, take away the highlights from lectures & readings. Your TA & lab group are what make the class what it is. Tests are open note, open book, online.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Payne is super engaging and really works to make the lectures interactive. You can tell he truly cares about the content and HOD as a whole. A great transition class into college. I met most of my closest friends in HOD 1250 :)

He's a very engaging professor but this class is oddly technical with lots of points deducted for APA formatting. It feels semi disorganized with all grading done by TAs. Basically an intro to psych class with so many papers (a paper a week). Open note test (make friends to collab on study guides it helps) and points for engaging in class.

Good prof. Seems to care about his students, but not the most engaging lectures. TAs do almost all grading, so it can be fairly subjective. Fairly easy class overall, tests are open note. Workload outside of class is pretty light, but the readings at the beginning of the semester are dense.

Dr. Payne is nice and passionate about HOD. The class can be a little overwhelming especially because he cold calls from a stack of note cards with names on them. The lectures can be boring, but labs are pretty good depending on the TA. Not a terribly difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most grading is done by TA's with too much variability in grading. No clear feedback was given. Did not even get grades back for the huge final group project!

Enjoyed Dr. Payne's lectures and I've learned a lot from 2 semesters. Papers are graded very easily and group projects are a little more harsh it kinda depends on your group. But I like that there are enough individual grades to balance out. Assignments can be vague so ask clarifying questions to TAs and Dr. Payne so that you do what they want.

Payne is a good lecturer, he knows how to keep his students engaged for 75 minutes. Even though it felt weird at times, I think I learned a lot about small group behavior. I do not think showing up to lecture matters.

For 1300, not content-heavy and the workload is also fine. But Jeremy Payne is boring and inconsiderate, and you can barely understand his lectures. I don't enjoy his lecture style at all. I feel that he doesn't really care about his students.

Unclear on the grading of group projects and nitpicky. He gave the option of not having to attend lectures but deletes does not include some slides online from lectures. Most of the grading is done by TA except for big projects. He is also unclear sometimes on what he wants for group projects and automatically enrolled 1250 students in his class.

I enjoyed the content and Payne is a nice guy, but his assignments were very annoying. Weekly reading assignments and quizzes based on the readings. Lots of essay's toward the end of the year. However, exams are open note, which was nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Payne cares about his students if you show that you care about the course. Going to office hours with some solid questions will help you out with the two group presentations. He tries to make the class enjoyable and the assignments are easy As as long as you follow the format to a T. just turn in the assignments on time lol.
Payne is a nice guy and is helpful but I did not find the course content to be interesting or useful. Easy A- but getting an A (94%) takes more work.

Do the readings and you will be just fine. Dr. Payne's lectures are disorganized and grading criteria can be vague/confusing, but I would never discourage you from taking his class. Listen to his directions and take notes as he will mention his expectations for assignments during class. Buy the e-textbook. Search bar is crucial for open note exams.

Dr. Payne is funny, cares about his students, and knowledgeable in his fields; lectures were always very interesting. 1250 as a course is a bit disorganized so course/grading expectations were sometimes unclear. The five essays and two big exams aren't too difficult to do well on if you put in the effort AND recognize patterns in his expectations.

I honestly feel pretty mixed about Professor Payne. He's an extremely talented lecturer -- the way he manages to grab everyone's attention (and sustain it for over an hour) is pretty impressive. The class is designed pretty poorly, but I guess that's not his fault. He's also the opposite of understanding -- so don't even try to get an extension.

Nice guy, cares about the students. Gives very few expectations for grading papers. The lectures can sometimes be confusing and it isn't always clear how they relate to the reading. Overall not a bad class if you put in effort and listen to feedback.

Payne was better in 1300 than in 1250; he implemented class feedback really well! I actually learned a lot about myself from the activities/lectures. VERY strict grading + unclear criteria + basically a paper due every week, but many opportunities for help + flexible time management. Grade heavily depends on TA. You'll be fine if you put in effort.

Do not take this class. Grading very difficult and unfair. The amount of work you do and effort you put in is not reflective of your final grade. This class has made me reconsider even majoring in HOD. Super disappointed in the TAs and Payne for how this class went.

Lots of psych stuff. Prof Payne is an okay lecturer. He tries to make concepts interesting, which I appreciate. The textbook info was interesting, but the exams, with super detailed questions, made the learning experience not as enjoyable. It's okay for a core requirement, but I probably wouldn't take it as an elective.

I really like Payne. His class is pretty easy to do well in because he makes sure there is a clear path to success. Wasn't that interesting of a class but the exams were super easy and the papers weren't too bad.
