Lectures were boring and useless if you did the required readings for the week. Grading was done by the TA's, and the writing is very formulaic, but the instructions were not clear. The pacing for the writing assignments was not the best and led to a bit of burnout. As a professor, I did not care for Payne: hypocritical and honestly a bit lazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not sure why so many reviews harp on Prof Payne. Yeah, your TA grades your assignments which kinda sucks but many classes are like that. 1250 isnt a great class in general but its required and Prof Payne makes it more fun and enjoyable than other professors do. Re: mental health, just communicate throughout the semester instead of the day before.
Not necessarily an easy A but Professor Payne is funny, kind, and always tries to help. He makes lectures as enjoyable as they can be.

Besides exams, all your papers (5 papers in total) are graded by your TA (who also grades your participation).Open-note exams, but you can only do well on exams if you copy 100% of the textbook (don't slack on readings!!!). He accepts 1% of all extension requests, so plan ahead (ironic since we study stress' impact). Lots of interesting content!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Useless lectures, everything is in the textbook. Asked exam questions about content that was not even taught in class nor in the textbook. Unclear instructions and criteria for papers that not even the TAs could answer questions about. TAs grade most work. Bright side: fun discussions and TAs, open-note format, cool projects, not super stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As others have said, grading comes to down to your TA mainly. Hard to get above a B+ on exams unless you really study when thats unlikely given the open note format. Control F will get you Bs on exams. Nice professor though. I like his lectures but honestly sat in the back and went on laptop. Dont really need to take notes.

1. ur TA  ur grade. if u get an extension & payne grades ur work, ur screwed cuz he's insanely tough 2. acts like he cares (mental health, etc), but doesn't. very cold & short over email & not understanding 3. lectures r useless but required, 100% of stuff is in textbook 4. exams r hard af 5. crazy on formatting. missed a comma once n lost 5 pts
TA grades everything so it really depends on whether your TA is a harsh grader or not. The lectures are boring and this class makes me want to drop this major.

there's a disconnect between what is preached and what his done. jeremy will place an immense focus on mental health, clinical disorders, and how the stress of life -- can impede on our academic productivity. but then he won't grant you a day extension on a quiz bc you were getting psychiatric help, instead sending a "good for you" email. he's fake
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You can tell Professor Payne genuinely cares about his students. Be prepared to be called on in class. Grading of all papers is done by TAs. Criteria can be unclear, but once you learn what they want, it gets easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Payne is a fine professor-- the tests and writing assignments are pretty formulaic, and not overly difficult. Reading is long and dense some weekends and nonexistent others. Overall, the class doesn't cover a lot of content.

Dr. Payne is very sweet and is great at making online lectures engaging. I learned a lot in HOD1250, but I did find the weekly quizzes and same prompt for all 3 AWPs to be annoying. Also the final exam was much harder than expected. Dr. Payne is very nice but also can be unclear about expectations. Annoying that you need a 94 for an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: A funny and positive person. Payne always makes class enjoyable and engaging and has been very accommodating for different time zones during the pandemic. His music taste is impeccable as well. Would highly recommend.

Professor Payne's class was engaging and fun overall. Some of the guidelines for assignments were unclear, but if you put effort into your papers you should be good. The material isn't difficult to understand, but there are a lot of readings. You need to do the readings to do well on the exams and quizzes. Participation is also graded.

Relatable, funny, caring. Finds ways to keep students engaged, even over Zoom. Weekly assignments were due Sunday, and we could complete them on our own time. 1 exam, 5 essays in APA, 1 final exam. Do the readings and you'll be fine for the exams, and make sure you understand the expectations for the essays. Overall, great professor.

You don't get to chose your 1250 professor, so if you got Payne, congrats, you got a good one!!! He's a solid professor, explains his lecture material well, and is just an overall solid dude. If he teaches anything other than 1250, take it. He's good at what he does and he cares about his students.

He is a fantastic teacher. He is hysterical, chill, and easily accessible. Professor Payne created a unique class environment that really allowed you to tailor it to your own needs. Take this class if you can.
Prof Payne made me want to go to class. This class is very interesting and easy to understand. TAs do the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Makes class a fun time and you can tell he cares a lot about his students. Assignments are at a reasonable workload and graded reasonably. For some reason there were never any clear guidelines on the frame analysis papers, and in the beginning it was hard to understand what he was looking for without a guideline. Be sure to know others in the class
He's super unclear and it gets really frustrating. But you do a lot of fun things in the class.

Payne was an awesome professor and always gave very engaging lectures. The assignments were difficult and often really unclear, but thats more the structure and nature of the class than his teaching. Pay attention to details about assignments on his slides and follow demo versions he gives you. Listen to all his advice/directions for presentations

Gives unclear directions for literally every assignment (be prepared to be forever confused). This class is all about group projects so it's manageable. Lots of quizzes. There are better professors for this class. But nice dude outside of class.

Nitpicky on assignments, not helpful with revisions. Seems like a nice guy at first, but is a mediocre professor. Grades participation and the final paper unnecessarily harshly which, as it is combined worth 35% of your grade, is a reason to look elsewhere.

Nice guy, but sometimes somewhat unclear in his answers to questions. That's my only complaint, though; solid professor otherwise. No tests. 4 3-5 page papers and one 14-17 page paper (the final) for individual work; for group work, it's 2 pretty easy presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Fair warning, there's a LOT of reading for this class. That being said, Jeremy is a super chill guy and makes class a lot less painful than it could be. Extremely funny too. Definitely worth taking.
The best, took two classes with her and would take as many more as possible. If you can get in any of her classes, DO IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Larson was an amazing professor that made the complex topics that we were learning easy and straight forward. She inspired me to look into getting my own PhD, purely because of how great of a teacher she was. As long as you don't skip class, Prof. Larson makes the course fun and tests decently simple. Take her if you have the chance!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Larson is awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
I was nervous when Dr. Larson didn't have any reviews here, but she turned out to be my favorite professor at VU. PSCI 3273 isn't free, but it's among the easier Poli Sci classes here. Larson is notably good at answering questions too. The only downside is she's a little monotone.
Highly recommend if you care at all about political science.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are pretty engaging, and the negotiations are honestly a lot of fun. I feel like I actually learned a lot of good stuff in this class, and it wasn't hard. Sometimes it feels like a lot of busy work, but it's easy to get an A. There are also these daily quizzes from articles, but honestly, they are pretty intuitive without reading.

Professor Leddin sometimes made comments that felt uncomfortable. She also has a dismissive and condescending tone asking questions one on one, which is why I often avoided asking questions about assignments, etc. She spends lots of time advertising her husband's books which is irrelevant to class. However, the class itself is easy and very fair.
Dr. Leddin is amazing, and her class is very engaging. I learned a lot- definitely recommend!
Dr. Leddin is the best Professor I have ever had. She is incredibly smart and kind. She does cold call so do the readings, but I cannot recommend you take this class enough.

Dr. Leddin is kind, funny, and extremely smart. The class was easy as long as you show up and skim the readings. She genuinely wants you to learn and succeed. I learned so much and will fs take a class with her again. She is tough if you don't follow her like 3 guidelines, but if you're respectful it should be an easy A.
Dr. Leddin is incredible! She cares so much about her students, and the class is informative and straightforward. Be sure to come on time and participate. If you put in the work you will get an A.

Dr. Leddin is one of the most engaging and impactful instructors I've had at Vanderbilt. Her energetic, humorous, and welcoming teaching style created a classroom environment where students felt comfortable, connected, and genuinely excited to learn.

Professor Leddin was easily one of the best professors I have ever had. She is extremely caring and is super informative. Class attendance is mandatory but not a chore. Leddin is super engaging and you really do learn a lot in her class.

Professor Leddin is an amazing teacher - very fair and passionate about her students' success. Her number one goal is always her students' learning, and it shows in every class. She makes the material practical, engaging, and easy to follow. Great experience - highly recommend!

Prof. Leddin is one of the best teachers at Vanderbilt. She cares deeply about her students and as long as you involve yourself in the class, which is easy -- read, do the homework, ask questions -- you'll really enjoy this course. She makes it easy to know what's expected of you and is honestly so great in office hours and has such good insights!

Dr. Leddin is the best professor on Vandy's campus. She is emotionally intelligent, kind and extremely funny. It is hard to be bored during a lecture with her. Her grading criteria is clear, and I wish other professors were like her. Taking Negotiation with her is the best decision I have made as an undergraduate student. She is simply the best!

Literally best professor ever! She is absolutely hilarious and brings so much energy to every class. There's kind of a lot of work but it's more tedious than difficult. She really cares about her students and wants to get to know you outside of class. You can learn so much (real-world-applicable!) information from this woman

Ok so shes kinda crazy but you kinda love it. She is SO GOOD at negotiation and business and she knows it. It's a class that requires some effort but I learned so much and it was my favorite class this semester. Also DO NOT BE LATE or she will call you out in front of the whole class and then murder you with a knife probably. Definitely take.

Prof. Leddin is the best professor I've ever had! She is incredibly supportive, and her lectures are always engaging. Negotiation simulations are interactive and fun. She provides great insights while being readily available for questions. Expectations are clear, and the coursework is manageable and fair. 100% recommend taking this class with her!

Dr. Leddin was one of the best professors I had at Vanderbilt. She is incredibly thoughtful, caring, and intelligent. She makes a significant effort to accelerate your career—especially if you are in business. The class itself is fun and engaging. There is a decent amount of work, but you get into the flow pretty quickly and she grades leniently.

Great professor! Utilizes engaging questions to manifest class discussion, making keeping up with material, and application in weekly negotiations easy and accessible. Go to class, you will love it, and when you do you will get an A!

pretty easy and solid class but there was a good bit of assignments so I wouldn't recommend it if you have problems with organization. Most(or all) grading is done by the TA, which is usually a good thing. She's really nice and knows what she's talking about and I could totally see myself and others going to her for career/life advice.

If you are a business minor or HOD, make sure to take Negotiation with Professor Leddin. She is easily one of my favorite professors from the business department. The material is very digestible and applicable, and I find myself using much of what I learned in interviews, other classes, and even outside of school.

Professor Leddin values participation and attendance more than other professors. This is to the benefit of the student and greatly enhanced my classroom experience. She is very engaging and is more than willing to provide help outside of class. This is not a hard class, but be prepared to participate and be engaged in class negotiations.

Professor Leddin utilizes interesting lessons, lectures, and negotiation simulations to teach us. This has been the most informative and useful class I have taken so far this semester. Highly recommend prof Leddin and BUSA 3105.

Dr. Leddin is a gem! She is supportive, caring, and sweet and goes the extra mile for her students outside the classroom. I have never encountered a professor who engages with her students like she does, and I would 100% recommend Dr. Leddin to anyone looking for a Business class.

Prof. Leddin is one of my favorite professors at Vandy! Took Org Behavior with her. Not sure where these other comments are coming from, but her expectations are honestly very clear and it's not hard to do well. If you're looking for a professor who actually cares, and if you want a mentor in business, take her class, you won't regret it.

Professor Leddin is a gem of a professor. I could not recommend her enough. She is extremely engaging and is truly invested in her students. As long as you go to class prepared every day and do all of the assignments, you will have no problem securing a good grade. Undoubtedly the best option for Negotiation.
Jamie was one of the best, if not the best prof I had during my MBA. Would take any course she offered just to be in the classroom with her.
Professor Leddin is awesome, I strongly encourage taking her class.
You can get a 98% cumulative grade on all coursework and not get an "A".

Grading for this class is usually homework (paper) + participation + group presentation. However, she would give 100% homework grades for everyone, and then intentionally "distinguish" some students with low grades for minor issues (and minimum feedback). Unfair and unprofessional.
I think these are a little harsh but I would say that the class was inconsistent
Leddin is a nice lady, but her class is not structured well. There is almost no rubric on how you will be graded so there's no much to go off of. Overall, I was confused the entire time.
I am sure she means well, but gee golly make sure you pay attention in class. She will absolutely roast you if she catches you staring off in to space. Whew!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I am so sorry, I have never written one of these but this was such a poor experience. I am very disappointed in how little I learned given the amount of work required.
Really confuzled by the structure and grading. No clear direction ever given
Take Professor Park instead

This was simply the worst college course I have ever taken. She is very defensive and abrasive if you ask for feedback or question her grading. There is little to no effort given on her part in structuring the course. There is essentially no content taught. The entire class is a popularity contest, with most of your grade coming from peers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible organization

Prof. Leddin is caring and passionate, and it's a pleasure to listen to her lecture. The course is easy and the HW consists of easy short essays. With that being said, the participation requirement makes students ask questions indefinitely and sometimes interrupts the class progress

I love Prof Leddin! She genuinely made me want to go to class and kept the class extremely straightforward to get an A. Wish she taught other courses, would love to learn more from her. Side note, lots of assignments but grades were easy and based on the rubric. 10/10 class and prof

Prof leddin is passionate about content and very clear in her expectations. OB really is an easy A. But the participation should be graded differently - everyone just did it through unneeded annoying zoom chats rather than ask in class.

Participation is annoying, considering she basically forces you to ask questions. Rest of the class was doable - HWs are fair, final project & exam both were not impossible to complete. She is clearly passionate about her job and brings that enthusiasm to her teaching style. Super positive, friendly, great teacher.

While there is a group project in this class, the professor makes it very easy to maintain a good grade even if left with a few interesting group members. Prof. Leddin is very caring and obviously knows her stuff. Definitely would take this class again!
Prof. Leddin is easily the kindest, most caring professor out there at Vanderbilt. I still regularly use most things I learned in this class!
I love this women. Everyone needs to take her class!
I learned so much in this class. Prof. Leddin goes above and beyond for her students and I am so lucky to have had her as a Business professor!

I have no idea what all the negative reviews are about. Prof. Leddin is one of the kindest, sweetest, and most caring professor at Vanderbilt. Her class is the reason why I am pursuing a business minor. Please do yourself a favor and take her class.
Prof. Leddin makes zoom lectures fun! I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to get a better feel for business regardless if you plan on declaring a Business minor. Best intro class ever!

Go to office hours! Prof. Leddin has helped me so much in my ability to network and get connections within the Business Minor program. I love this women like she is my mother. Do everything you can to take this class!
The best class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Do whatever you can do to take this class.
Prof. Leddin takes care of all her students. Everyone who takes BUS 2400 at Vandy should take it with Prof. Leddin.

Content is so easy to understand but the quizzes were unnecessarily specific/detailed. Group project is major part of your grade but largely scored on individual contribution. Participation requirement is disruptive because people ask useless questions. Straightforward final exam. Class would've been pretty boring without Prof. Leddin's liveliness!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Get ready for your life to be changed. Group projects are a necessity but you can make it work. I loved this class and am beyond grateful for Prof. Leddin's teachings. 10/10 would take again.

Prof. Leddin's class takes a subject I didn't think I would care about and made it apart of my every day life. Her wit and wisdom made going to class a pleasure. She deserves the world and don't believe a single negative review of her that you might read. One of the cartoons she showed in class makes me laugh to this day.

One of the best professors that I have ever had. Prof. Leddin is caring, compassionate, and a star of the Vanderbilt business minor program. She is readily accessible via office hours and will continue to advocate for you long after you have taken her class. Do yourself a favor and take this class!

In hindsight this class was fine. The content is common sense, but the online quizzes are overly complicated and confusing. You need to participate every class, which means people write the ridiculous comments in the Zoom chat. Group project is HUGE part of the grade, but your grade is not dependent on other group members.

Prof. Leddin brings incredible energy to every lecture and makes the material very engaging. The reading quizzes can be pretty annoying, but overall the workload is very manageable and the class is an easy A. (p.s. if you take this class, PLEASE only ask ONE question per lecture, that's all u need for participation).

The class is easy and an easy A, but most of class is unfortunately filled with students asking random questions to fulfill the participation requirement (10% of your grade). The material was interesting and I wish Prof Leddin spent more class time on material rather than questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Leddin is not caring nor sincere. The material is fine and mandatory for the business minor, so I'd advise seeking a different OB professor. She portrays herself as caring and understanding of students, but she's the polar opposite. She does not listen to students' concerns, show any empathy toward students, nor accommodate any student problems.

Professor Leddin is the easiest, most caring, and sincere professor I have had at Vanderbilt. Like some of the other reviews have said, I have no clue why she has anyone complaining. She is the greatest!!

Prof. Leddin was one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt! Shes extremely personable and provides really engaging lectures. Shes accessible outside of class and seems to really want her students to do well. Would definitely recommend!
Every time I enter Professor Leddin's classroom, I'm reminded why I decided to go to Vandy. She is encouraging and smart. Thankful for her!

Jamie is the absolute best. I do not understand why she has a 3.4 on here. Every class she teaches is a joy and could not be easier. She is by far my favorite professor at Vandy and I'd highly recommend her to anyone.

I did not enjoy this class. A 3rd grader could understand the content, yet Leddin chooses to make the assessments needlessly difficult and the quiz questions hyperspecific. I think she means well but something about her seems disingenuous, and I felt like she was trying to trip students up. Her participation policy leads to mindless questions.

Awful class experience and not a good professor. Materials she covered in class almost not show up on quiz. You need to read lots of textbook for quiz. Online homework is an alternative name for quiz, which can be done only once with no chance for revision. Participation is a mess. Avoid at any cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Class is obvious/common sense most of the time. Didn't feel like she handled online super well, was not super receptive to technical issues. Because of participation half the class is people asking obvious questions.

Relatively an easy A. There are small quizzes every session that go over last session's main points, but pretty straightforward. Participation matters, so a lot of people ask pointless questions. Material is also common-sense, so lectures can get boring. Group paper can be tedious if no one does work, but the TA grades really easily.

In-class participation is very important. Group project isn't too bad. Decent lecturer which is helped by interesting material. Really nice and caring person. Knows what she is talking about. You need to talk a lot in class to get participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I think this class would have been more difficult on campus, but online it was very easy. The lectures turned into a relative waste of time because of all the random questions asked just for participation. However, Dr. Leddin cared about her students and really believes the material that she teaches is important.

Easy class and great lecturer. The material is very simple/common sense, but she teaches it in an engaging way that makes the information seem very relevant. One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. Easy quizzes, final, and project. Would highly recommend.

You don't learn anything because it is just mumbo jumbo common sense topics that everyone knows. As another review said, it is just people raising their hands asking dumb questions to get participation points. There are also easy quizzes a group project, and a final. It is very easy but also a waste of time, unfortunately.

She uses every anecdote as an opportunity to flex her illustrious business experience. The material is incredibly dry and shouldn't merit being its own class, so she makes participation a big deal to make sure someone still shows up. Not a mean lady, just thinks a lot of herself and wants you to know it so you don't judge her for teaching OB.

One of the most excruciatingly boring classes at Vanderbilt. Prof Leddin is cringeworthy at best, thinks extremely highly of herself, and is fake to the point of making everyone in the room uncomfortable. Participation policy is a joke and means the entire class is just people raising hands to ask a stupid question for credit. Joke class, AVOID.

Very educated and experienced in the subject. In the classroom she's energetic and participation matters in your grade. Daily quizzes but if you took notes and reviewed them they are not bad. Group project and final exam. Easily accessible to talk to in office hours and learn more about the business world.

Great professor! Definitely cares about what she teaches. Lecture heavy but not hard info, everyday there's a quiz over the last lecture. Textbook is kind of useful if you use it to review, but if she doesn't cover things in class it won't be on the quizzes or final. Group project is worth a lot. Participation matters, but not a huge deal.
do well on final and group paper, besides that not a lot of work

She's a good teacher with tons of relevant work experience. Class is an easy A if you take notes in class and participate every now and then. Group project seems daunting but she grades easily. She was available outside of class and gives good career advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Leddin has a eccentric personality that she tries to bring into her lectures because it's a lot at one time and she tries to make it easily digestible. Overall, the class wasn't too bad.
nice lady, very energetic, easy A

Jamie is really well-versed in her field and has a lot of career experience, therefore her lectures are very applicable to real life. You need to take notes in class and study those for the quizzes/exam, and there is a group project but definitely a fairly easy A.

Materials are boring and she tried to make jokes in the class. Tough during office sometimes. Weekly quizzes plus a group paper plus a final. Must participate in class to receive credits. Take it for credit, if not, not worth the time.

Pretty easy material and not a hard A if you play it right. If you participate once per class, study for the daily quizzes (they cover notes from the previous class), and do the homework on time, then that's 45% of your grade. The other 55% is the final exam and final project, so just don't underestimate them, and you'll be fine. An A isn't hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: jamie leddin is an angel  she tries so hard to make a really boring class interesting, but the material is so mind-numbing that even with a really enthusiastic professor, it was a real struggle to pay attention. class really isn't hard if you show up and raise your hand once a lecture to participate  also one big group project
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I understand that some might like her, but if you are used to either STEM or reading intensive classes, she might not be for you -- but please be respectful to others. In her class, listening to stories of success, benefits of team work, and "powerful words to use," I constantly wondered why I even existed in this world.
Class topics are pretty simple, but Professor Leddin keeps the course very engaging. She is a great lecturer, but could be more specific on assignment expectations. Overall would recommend her class.
Great class - very engaging material, and the topics are really accessible. If you participate in class and pay attention to the lectures, you'll do really well on the quizzes and final.

Professor Ruiz is engaging, funny, and clearly cares about teaching. His class is easy to manage, with 6–7 assignments and discussion-based attendance. Readings are assigned each lecture, but the workload stays reasonable. I'd highly recommend him and the class to anyone interested in Caribbean studies!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you see a class with professor Jesus Ruiz in it, just take it. The lectures are engaging, work is easy, and professor Ruiz is hands down one the funniest professors at Vandy.

Superstar individual. Understands students' needs more than any other professor here, values your time. Fascinating course content, in a field in which he truly seems to be an expert, and brings in a lot of personal experiences to ground his lectures in reality. Also, a hilarious man. Generous grader too.
GOAT. THE GOAT.

Professor Ruiz is absolutely amazing! He's really passionate about the topics of this class and brings a unique sense of humor to every class. He makes the class very engaging, and there are only four small papers and a final project. Highly recommend!
he was awesome and very funny, cared a lot about his students, would def recommend his class
A really nice guy who knows a lot about what he teaches. He is a hall-of-fame professor.

Professor Ruiz is the best!!!!!!! He always includes funny yet deeply personal anecdotes that keep the class engaging. He truly cares about each student and makes himself accessible outside of the classroom. He is definitely pretty woke in his lectures but still makes the classroom a comfortable place to share any opinions. Lenient with extensions!

Professor Ruiz has been such an amazing introduction to the quality of instruction at Vanderbilt. He has amazing lectures, is incredibly understanding, and makes this class actually very engaging. I cannot recommend his classes more.

Professor Ruiz has been one of the kindest and most understanding professors I've ever had. He makes sure that we are not overstressed or overworked and is very open to making accommodations if you communicate with him. I cannot recommend prof Ruiz enough. He is also very passionate about his other classes. Take him if you can for sure.
Prof. Ruiz gives the vibes of the teacher from Dead Poets Society. Very passionate. Very relaxed and flexible for students. Be prepared for a new personal anecdote to support each class.
Prof Ruiz is the best and so awesome!!!!

Dr. Ruiz is one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He's thoughtful, passionate, and makes the class feel both engaging and approachable. He explains topics clearly, is always open to questions, and is very understanding with deadlines. The class is interesting, manageable, and genuinely enjoyable. Can't recommend Dr. Ruiz enough.

Prof Ruiz is one of the nicest, most understanding profs I have ever come in contact with. The content is extremely engaging and he actively talks about current events to bring historical and modern events together. Also lenient w/ deadlines, which has saved me several times. Can't think of one negative thing / downside to taking his class!

TAKE THIS CLASS! I can not stress this enough but this is generally one of the most insightful, most amazing professors that I have had the pleasure of being in contact with. His class is so engaging and you learn so much from it. He is also very understandable if you have any issues during the semester.

Professor Ruiz was great! Great lectures, you'll learn a lot about Caribbean history and how it connects to the current global political and economic landscape. Lots of creative freedom for final project, and always had meaningful conversations about the material.

Amazing professor, very lenient when it comes to deadlines and whatnot. Interesting lectures that are really engaging. One of the hidden gems of Vandy, take his class even if you're not an LAS or American Studies type of person. Truly just a "chill guy"

Jesus Ruiz is a great professor; his classes meet axle requirements. The only "work" you do is read the reading, discuss if you like in class, and at the end of each unit, you do a short reflection. He is also a very understanding professor if you need an extended deadline or your sick. Attendance is flexible as long as you let him know prior.

I strongly recommend to take this class. This class is a very easy A but you also learn so many things about the course. It won't let me input his course but it is CAL 2800. There are only 3 short papers and they were so interesting to write on. He also gives many extensions if you need it. He is so kind and passionate about his teaching.

Dr. Ruiz is one of my favorite professors here. He's very caring and accommodating, which was greatly appreciated. He's a wonderful lecturer and also just a really great person in general. His class encourages you to think critically about the material, and I've honestly never had a class quite like this one (in the best way). I learned so much!!!

Attendance is mandatory but you don't really need to do the readings to get through the class. Lectures are sometimes a bit unfocused but they're still interesting. There are short papers and one final project where you do a mock asylum interview. Grading isn't too harsh. Good guy, interesting perspectives.

Amazing professor, probably my favorite to date. He's incredibly passionate and incredibly kind. He makes you want to learn and makes it super easy to participate. Attendance is mandatory but I've never regretted attending class. Speaks to you like you're human and his peer.

Dr. Ruiz is an amazing professor! It was a fun semester full of amazing content about asylum and migration across the US/Mexico Borderlands and across the globe! It is always a fun time coming to class as it is always something new! You definitely need to take a class with him throughout your time at Vanderbilt!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: this professor is great. Very clear vision for his class, rather than a Professor that goes on random tangents in different directions, causing the class to be illogical. Professor Ruiz cares a great deal about his students, and any issue you have in the class you can undoubtedly go and talk to him about your problems.  THE GOAT 🐐🐐🐐🐐🐐🐐🐐
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Ruiz is one of the best professors, if not the best professor, I've had in my time at Vanderbilt. He is genuinely caring, and wants to see you succeed. The class has a relatively chill syllabus, and the workload is not bad. The discussions are really chill, and the readings are do-able. I'd definitely take any of his class again!

Professor Ruiz is a good professor! He's very relaxed when it comes to grading but also makes sure you actually learn things in his class. I learned a lot this semester and the workload was light. To me this is how a college class should be
Cool dude, cool dude
Best professor EVER!!

Professor Ruiz is an incredibly fun and smart guy. He has a relaxed approach to his courses while still providing very valuable enlightening lectures. He's super understanding, and I can't wait to take another course from him.

Dr. Ruiz is your typical hip-and-chill millennial. If you complete the assignments, you're basically guaranteed an A. He can be a bit too intense and personal, but they make for interesting lectures. There was never a dull moment with Dr. Ruiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is very relaxed and basically zero effort.  There are ~20 page readings for class that you dont need to do.  He expects consistent attendance, but all you have to do is show up.  He is very super nice and flexible with extensions. Take the class for an easy A and to get to know a nice guy.  Avoid if you're looking for something challenging.

Professor Ruiz is great! He's very knowledgeable on his subject and always makes class interesting and engaging. He really cares about his students and their success, doesn't grade too harshly, and is super reasonable and understanding. I would definitely recommend taking one of his classes, they are very eye-opening!

Dr. Mohammed is a very caring professor and wants students to think about sociological concepts in a way they never have thought of before. We had two social experiments to conduct and a podcast to produce. They were not difficult assignments and were rather interesting. If you put in some work, you should get an A.
Just 3 papers and homework was grad. Heard it changed tho and participation is part of grade but as long as you showed up to class and turned in stuff u got an A

I absolutely loved this class! Prof. Jihan allows you to pick the topics of your research papers, so you never have to write about a topic that does not truly interest you. She is also willing to provide feedback on any assignment before the due date. You will learn about interesting topics without having to stress about your grade.
I absolutely loved Professor Mohammed. Very caring.
Very sweet!!!!!!! She is extremely caring and organized with her lectures. TA is also awesome.
She truly cares about you and wants the best for her students. The class is graded on 3 short papers and a research project. She is a lenient and nice grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Mohammed is so caring and always checks up on our mental health. Each class is half lecture and half discussion. There are a couple response papers to films, 3 short papers, and a final paper, but they were all spaced out nicely. As long as you put some effort into them, you will get an A on each. Highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Mohammed seemed strict at first but she ended up being nice+caring. Get ready to read and write a lot of papers though, I was annoyed because we already have 4 papers assigned throughout the semester but then we ended up having to write a couple more as well without much advanced notice because she considered them "in-class assignments."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: For SOC-1010 Spring Semester, she actually quizzes you on the readings, making them mandatory! I took this class in the fall (her first semester) and never once were we quizzed on the readings. For the final, super specific material that did not have any actual relevance was quizzed on. No study guide and no hints. It ended up tanking my grade.
literally gave 100s on every assignment. no tests/quizzes except the final

Prof was kind and made sure to engage the class. However, this was one of the most disorganized classes I have taken at Vanderbilt. Lack of an encompassing syllabus made keeping on track difficult (final exam content was changed day of). The prof was extremely opinionated and rarely gave context to opposing opinions making class painfully one sided

Professor Mohammed is kind and great overall. This was her first semester teaching so the class was a bit rough around the edges at first, but by the end of the semester it came to be one of my favorite classes. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jihan Mohammed is a nice lady. I love her as a person but not so much as a professor. The class was easy but her grading sometimes did not make sense to me.

Super Great guy. I thought he was a phenomenal professor who prepared us aptly for the exams. Everything I missed throughout the course was my own fault. Phenomenal for Linear, and I assume everything else too.
This class was fine, but in order to understand everything it was really important to have gone in with background in calculus. Office hours and discussion sections were super super helpful.

This class is very easy if you do what is asked of you. There is a lot of opportunity for extra credit and automatic 100s. Prof Jimoh struggles with student understanding. When he is teaching what he has planned, he is straight-forward and easy to follow. However, if you are confused, he often cannot understand your question and really help.

Although Prof Jimoh was knowledgeable and funny, the atmosphere in his class felt off. We had a lot of material to cover, so missing a class wasn't an option. His lectures were often rushed and barely delved into the material because there was so much to get through, which meant lots of studying. However, he offers many extra credit opportunities.

Good professor but sometimes hard to understand. Lecture notes are clear and I learn a lot from them. There are three midterms, one final and then an exam taken multiple times until you get a good grade. Overall, I'd say the class is okay but the teaching is sometimes very confusing. He will make you go to OH so he can meet everyone which is nice.

Lectures are generally understandable, and he writes notes online and posts them so it's easy to use them for review. Really nice guy and cares about his students, but the fact that the course was coordinated meant that the exams were insanely hard and it was easy to lose 10-15% from arithmetic mistakes alone. Some of that wasn't his fault though

He's fine but the curriculum is coordinated and so the other profs are the ones that's awful. Grades super strange, very strict on definitions (you can't miss a single word). He's good at calc but not Lin Alg….
Great guy and takes time to get to interact and know a little bit about everyone in the class. Teaches complicated concepts well and in an intuitive manner.

Fawaz is SO sweet. My first impression of him was when he required each person in the class to schedule a 10 minute block to meet him in his office so he could get to know everyone. Really not a lot of professors would do that. He necessarily the best lecturer ever and the class was undeniably difficult, but he curves and always wants to help.

Fawaz is amazing at teaching this course! Although this course is hard (it's 1301), he made the course easy understanding! Due to the fact that 1301 is standardized test and one of the prof is Rafter, the tests were awful but we had curves (still bad but ok). Take his class (he's pretty good)!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Difficult class but Dr. Fawaz's whimsical personality makes it much better. Weekly quizzes are really easy but be sure to do the recommended textbook exercises for each chapter. The exams are hard but based on the exercises and you can replace your lowest exam score with the final exam. Utilize office hours and work with other students.

Math 1301 is one of the hardest math classes at Vanderbilt, but Professor Jimoh does a great job teaching the content and is a nice person. Make sure to complete each and every recommended textbook problem and you will be on a path for success.

Prof Fawaz is great. I actually did not mind this course, and at some points it also got interesting. My best suggestion would be to actually put in the work and do the exercises given. It will do you a world of good on the tests. Usually the test problems have some similar content to the exercises. He's a great prof and can make it manageable!

Took his Precalc (1005) class and then 1300, where he was the assistant prof or sum—dropped it since it was too hard for me so idek. great, kind instructor who clearly cares about ur success, showed me a lot of grace personally, wants to help. Prefers writing on the board over slides, smart, knowledgeable, and funny. Take him fs, u won't regret it!

Professor Fawaz is really great. if you put in the work by completing the recommended textbook problems, an A is almost certain. He does take attendance. He tries to remember names and is really caring. He uses an Ipad and the notes are posted on brightspace. Quizzes are really easy except for maybe 1 or 2 quizzes which you can drop.
Loved his class. I hope he stays at Vanderbilt because he seems to genuinely care about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bro is a chiller.

By far the best professor for Math 1300. Take him if you can. He cares a lot about his students and his office hours are super helpful . 4 midterms (drops lowest), 4 hws, weekly quizzes, and ca group.

Professor Jimoh is the kindest professor with such a great spirit. He is always smiling and making jokes. He cares about the students and wants us to succeed, stopping to ask us if we understand what he is teaching us frequently. The class overall is very very difficult, but our class compared to others has higher exam averages. He is the best!

Professor Jimoh clearly cares about his students, though can be disorganized at times. He's an entertaining lecturer (though perhaps not always intentionally). No graded homework and exams can be difficult to complete on time, but keep up with the suggested textbook exercises and you'll do okay.

Fawaz Jimoh cares a lot about his students, will learn everyone's name, and we did better than other classes on tests. The class itself is hard but he teaches it well and clearly. He is also funny and a cool guy in general. The tests are hard to finish in time but there are corrections so it is ok.
Professor Chung is so caring and nice! I really enjoyed her drill section. Take if you can.

This professor was one of the most hardworking professors that I have ever met at Vanderbilt. She puts time in effort to plan her courses, and her work ethic is incredible. Her lectures were very well prepared and comprehensible, and she holds herself to high standards. She is compassionate and friendly. I recommend this professor.

She really challenged my progress with Korean beyond textbook conversations. I feel like I am ready for my study abroad experience next year thanks to her. The readings are tough but that's to be expected for a language you're learning. Also, she is very accessible to help if you are having difficulty with the course material and very kind.
Honestly I don't quite get some of the comments here. Ms. Jihye is quite helpful in her office hours. Idt she is a bad person judging from my experiences.

Jihye is a TA in the econ department not a prof, and while I understand students complaints about her grading, she was literally just going off of what Prof Wooders made her do at least in 2160. Like I saw one student on here complain about getting a 33% on a quiz but if it's 3 questions and u get 1 right idk what u can expect to get...
Hardly cordial towards students and an unfair grader. Whether you are looking for a future instructor or a future colleague, Professor Heo is not a good choice.
Would give students really rubbish grades even though most of the questions are attempted rightly. Perhaps ridiculous is a better word than hilarious

She has no love and no mercy for her students. She doesn't deserve what she does, because as an educator in a good university, it doesn't matter about your skill. It matters about love. Just like what the Beatles say, all you need is love, love is all you need.
Yo bro she just refuse to give back any score on the quizzes even though I'm CORRECT! That's freaking lit like what the frack.
OMG like literally her grading is just so cruel. Sniff sniff I literally wanna cry
She's actually good at teaching, but not very kind in grading.
ji ni tai mei

What sort of disappointment lies ahead when one senses a 33.3333% on some certain quiz? For the world, under the reign of Ms. Jihye, is a huge blackhole doomed to suck away the soul and spirit of all her students, to the extent that all of them would be convinced that they would soon fail school, join gangs, and end up in delinquency centers.

Liu laoshi is an excellent professor who helps you sharpen your language skills beyond belief. From taking my first course with her nearly two years ago to finishing 3302W now, my Chinese has improved immensely and Liu laoshi has played a large role in my progress. I recommend her courses to anyone who cares about the language. I will miss her!

I've already taken two classes with Liu laoshi, and I'm about to take my third! She is amazing and will certainly help you improve your Chinese. Fair warning, though--3301 isn't easy at all, but if you put in enough hard work, you can certainly get the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is very nice and as long as you do the work and study, you will be fine.

Liu Laoshi is the absolute best! Best professor on campus by far. She seems to be super strict at first, but she's so easy to warm up to and you can tell that she actually cares about your success in Chinese. She always went out of her way to make sure our classes were fun and enjoyable and even brought us food multiple times! Love her so much!

Liu laoshi is one of my favorite chinese teachers and I had her for 2201 too. She is so caring and understanding, and she really wants students to succeed. Although she gives a lot of homework, it is manageable and not graded too harshly. If you meet with her, she always helps you improve. Class is mandatory, but its not too hard to do well.

Liu laoshi is the sweetest lady on earth. On a surface level she seems to be pretty strict. That in mind, she genuinely wants to help you improve your Chinese. She's really helpful out of class and is one of those people that just makes you smile when you have a conversation with her. Great teacher, loved her methods, and super caring person.

Such a sweet lady, cares a lot about her students. She brought our drill class candy on Halloween, for god's sake. It's Chinese, so there's a lot of work, but she is a very sweet lady and definitely makes it worth it. Grading is reasonable and she wants to work with you.

Professor Liu is honestly a gift to Vanderbilt and academia. She is understanding and cares about each of her students like they are her children. She assigns a lot of work but it is all manageable and if you put a reasonable amount of time into her class you will do fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Liu is great. She's really caring, sweet, and a pretty easy grader. Just come to class and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She's an absolute sweetheart. Most students came into this intro Mandarin class with years of instruction, even up to 7 years... But she understands those who haven't and appreciates hard work. She'll help you so just work hard! I worked really really hard for the A, but mainly bc the other Liu (lecture) professor was tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I've studied Chinese for a long time and Liu Laoshi's class improved my Chinese more than in my 3 years of Chinese in high school. This was the first time I'd ever peer-edited in a Chinese class. Her assignments are definitely long for a foreign language class but are totally doable. She gives you clear guidelines and examples/vocab you can use.

Prof. Liu is awesome- she is genuinely so caring and really just wants everyone in her class to do well and improve their Chinese. She gives small everyday assignments so they're easy to keep up with and really helpful. If you do the work (studying for small quizzes and short writing assignments) you will make an A.
Liu Jing Lao Shi is a wonderful teacher! She really care about her students' progress and will make class fun. Chinese is hard but Liu Lao Shi will be there for you.

Dr. Joseph truly embodies what it means to care about his students. Readings can be dense, but his lectures help clarify concepts and are always followed by a good discussion. The course is not difficult, and I appreciate how he challenged our thinking throughout the semester, which enhanced our learning. 10/10 recommend taking a course with him!

*for AADS 2148. Prof Joseph truly cared for his students, is funny, and enjoys teaching. Lectures followed by discussion every class can be monotonous, but a great class for AXLE credit. Worth while to skim all readings (~70pg/wk), but there are no reading quizzes. 50% of your grade is based on a midterm and final combined, so exhaust effort there
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Props to Vandy for hiring such an amazing professor. He is very understanding and truly cares about his students. He is also very funny and enthusiastic during every class, getting you to think about AADS in a way you both learn and find interesting. He is very lenient when it comes to grading and gives back amazing feedback. Highly recommend

GREAT PROFESSOR. Professor Joseph is very passionate and knowledgeable. His class is very engaging and mostly discussion-based. He is also very understanding and willing to accommodate his students. Highly recommend! My favorite class this semester. The topics and readings are interesting (you do not have to do all of them or read the whole thing).

Professor Joseph is not only an engaging lecturer, but is also one of the most caring people I have ever met. He truly wants his students to do well, not only in his class, but also within their mental health and beyond. Take him!!
Moreso concerned with teaching and getting you to think about AADS in a way you have not before than making students work for grades. Take any class with him!!

Professor Joseph is a kind and incredible professor who cares about his students. If you come to class engaged and ready to take notes, you will not have a difficult time. His discussion questions (which come after the lecture) also do a great job of challenging you to think in ways you've never thought of previously. 10/10 class and lecturer :)

Professor Joseph is by far one of the best professors I've met at Vanderbilt. He's enthusiastic during every class, and facilitates very engaging discussions. He's a new professor, but is doing an absolutely incredible job. An A is easy as long as you keep up with relatively simple readings and study your lecture notes. Wholeheartedly recommend.

She is the best professor I had at Vandy. Amazing lectures. Quiz every other week, which helps a lot with keeping up with content. Super interesting classes and included AI use as part of the course. Take algo with her!!!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. She has redone the course and it is impossible now. You will not do well everyone failed the first quizzes and she did nothing to fix the averages. She does not care about her students.

Dr. Julie is a passionate professor with perhaps the best delivery in the CS department. Her lecture slides are poorly designed and not good for referencing later. The class focuses more on easy parts and less on more important content. Although you feel like you're learning a lot, the class is not rigorous enough to prepare you for real life.

Very passionate professor for 3250. Class is overall pretty easy, but it does get harder towards the end. Homework is long and has multiple parts, but if you go to office hours it isn't that bad. Lots of extra credit opportunities at the end of the semester. Overall a great professor for 3250.
Going to Julie's algo class (especially after exam 2) is important. The class is a bit slow-paced and the exams are hard but graded nicely. Useful content though.

Great lecturer, you can tell she's rally passionate about the subject. Hw's are a bit time consuming but still doable. Tests make you think but are graded very leniently, and curves it at the end too. Take algorithms with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think a lot of the complaints about Dr.Johnson are about the courses itself and not her teaching style. Throughout my time at Vanderbilt she has by far made the most effort to get to know her students if you make yourself willing. While her slides aren't the greatest if you pay attention in class you should be fine

Possibly one of the worst classes I've taken at Vandy. Lectures are incredibly convoluted and she is unable to explain topics clearly. Many students end up having to get lecture materials from other professors that are teaching the course in different sections. 

Does not care for students either. Not reachable outside of class, and can be rude.

She skips hard stuff and overly emphasizes the easy stuff. The course is not hard if you know proofs. The difficulty between exams varies greatly. Exam 2 >> exam 3 > exam 1. Homeworks can be tough, and are graded also unreasonably tough. She is energetic and can be helpful. At times she uses slang from the South.

I thought Dr. Johnson was great for 2212. She taught the material very well, emphasizing topics that will be used in future courses (3250). Looking at other reviews here for 2212, many have general complaints about 2212 and not Johnson. As a professor, she's very helpful and really cares about students learning. Lectures are fun and engaging!

Pretty good, a lot of the reviews that are hating on her don't realize that for 2212 in general, your professor doesn't matter as much as how much you take out of things like ZyBooks, office hours, etc. Would recommend and would take again.

She's average at best. Has weird pet peeves - like no hash tables? The course itself focuses more on following specific types of proofs than problem-solving, which isn't a great way to learn algorithms in my opinion. Her lecture slides are quite terrible if you go back and review them. She's sort of passive aggressive too? Knows her algorithms tho.

Lecture and exam experience was alright, homework for this course in general though is not really like lecture or textbook examples (and this is intentional apparently). Besides doing the zybooks and attending class, you don't have to do much else to get the material--the way discrete is structured is just to make it unnecessarily hard sometimes.

Organized and clear lecture. The homework can be somewhat annoyed since you will write small essay and proof for each question. Moreover, there would be portion of homework that you need to read and grade others' writing. However, the content covered and exams are not difficult, and she with TAs are always there for help.

Dr. Johnson's course is incredibly fascinating and organized. I took this class online asynchronously and every day of every week was clearly laid out and labeled with estimated time to complete. They say 90% of success is organization, and Dr. Johnson makes success very attainable in that sense. She is also incredibly accessible outside of class.

Johnson's class is extremely organized. She will tell you exactly how to get from step A to step B, even laying out what homework to do every day of the week. She can go a bit fast so ask questions before you get left behind. If I followed it I would have gotten a better grade in the class. The homework is not as scary as it looks. No final.

I was lucky to have Dr. Johnson for several classes at Vandy and she is just awesome. Though they are not easy classes by any means, she is willing to offer lots of points for participation, encourages participation during lecture, and cares about students learning the material. Be ready for lots of work and intense lectures but Johnson is great

Dr. Johnson explains the concepts really well and includes lots of examples to help students understand and apply to concepts. Lots of "try this with your neighbor." Assignments can be difficult, but have straight-forward grading standards. She's also intentional about making her classroom welcoming.

She gives hard assignments & almost no help. You have to figure everything out on your own and going to her office hours is a waste of time because she doesn't even give a hint when you're stuck. Class time is not the conventional lecture but a bunch of group exercises and most learning happens by pre-recorded videos on your own outside of class.

I don't know why people are so hard on Dr. Johnson. Her grading is very clear, and she prepares you well for assignments as long as you pay attention in class and do her practice worksheets and activities. Not easy because you have to do the work, but certainly not hard to get an A. Also she is very helpful in office hours.

Professor Johnson always taught with an upbeat attitude and enthusiasm. This made the albeit boring material much more exciting. She does have a habit of going too fast in class, though, so you could get lost in the material if you don't get help. Best advice I can give you is to form a study group to help one another. Did wonders.

Algorithms with Julie Johnson was the best CS class I took at Vanderbilt. She makes the material accessible and assignments aren't too hard as long as you don't wait until the last minute. She posts slides online but you won't get the full picture if you skip class. I would take her over Arena any day.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Johnson is a solid choice for 2212. She teaches the material super well, and her CS experience is clearly there. The grade is based on quizzes every other week that aren't that tough if you go to lectures and some homeworks that are tricky. Super helpful in office hours. Overall a fine class, but take Johnson if you want to understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson will not hesitate to belittle and degrade you for asking clarification on her obfuscated teaching process. Get ready to sort through an overcrowded Brightspace and terribly formatted slides that she has not updated since '09. While she might teach you to prove if algorithms have optimal substructure, her course certainly does not.

Terrible alg professor. The homework is tough, filled with typos and ambiguities, and is very inefficient in teaching the material- it's graded harshly if your answer doesn't follow her exact template. Lectures are practically worthless. She comes off nice but can be very patronizing outside of class. Unfortunate given how important the subject is.

Don't take algorithms with her it's not worth it. She makes you do meaningless in-class activities and reads off lecture slides that have no relation to the incredibly difficult homework. Not to mention her lack of empathy, go to her office hours and ask questions and she's patronizing and unhelpful. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's definitely nice and wants you to do well. However, she takes an interesting subject and makes it absolutely unbearable to sit through. Algo is a difficult class, but she teaches it like a middle school class with partner activities, out of class required activities, and reiterating the same thing for 20 minutes. Not great at explaining also
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson cares a lot about teaching and is very willing to talk with you and help you out during office hours. She gets a little disorganized sometimes, but overall she's really nice.

Julie Johnson was a great professor. Her lecture slides were confusing at times, so the best thing to do is go to class and pay attention. It's not easy playing catch up with just the powerpoints. Focus in class and do the particpation activities, and you should do fine. The homework can be decently tough, but there's only 4 of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All sections in CS 2212 are set up to be consistent. Dr. Johnson's lectures are usually clear, though sometimes she moves too rapidly. However, you'll always be able to get what you need from lecture ppt and textbook. Quizzes, which are easy, make up to a large proportion to your grades. Homework is not easy, but doable. Overall, not a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can get all the information you will ever need on google and bright space, so lectures are optional. Fun class, but kind of work intensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Overall not a hard class, but sometimes the lectures weren't the most informative, but since it was an app inventor based class it isn't too hard to figure stuff out yourself, and professor Johnson was really helpful if I ever needed anything. If you actually do your work for the class it shouldn't be hard to get a good grade.
Johnson can be confusing when she tries to explain proofs or algorithms, but she gives you a lot of material to help with HW so, props.

Professor Johnson is a very sweet lady and her module was pretty enjoyable. You only have a couple of assignments so you have to show up to class to get the information to do them but they're pretty easy. Don't slack though, cause though she's nice, she'll fail you if you don't show up and take the class seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I thought the material was really boring and a little tough, but Johnson knows her stuff and tries to make it relatable. I honestly don't know how people didn't show up to class, i recommend going. Quizzes weren't bad if you studied old ones and she's a pretty generous grader.

Professor Johnson is the bomb. I started off the semester intimidated by her and terrified of this class (I'm a liberal arts major), but she was incredibly helpful. She really wants to get to know you and how you think so that she can give you the best advice, and she gives you all the help you need to be successful. TAs were wonderful as well.

CS101 is one of the best courses I have taken. Johnson is very helpful during office hour and after lectures. The tests are tough, but you'll do fine if you go through points in the lecture slides and read the questions in the textbook. Go to TAs when you're struggling with the homework.

The class is kinda boring. If you're a cs major, don't take the CS seminar. It's slow and doesn't provide any skills that'll help you in the future. If you're not a CS major, it's decent. Does provide some basic learning. Teacher is great though, i love julie johnson. She is a great teacher. Also easy A.

Fantastic teacher. Exceptionally easy class, I'd recommend cs 1101 to anyone. Vanderbilt doesn't make the material hard until 2201, 1101 is almost too easy. Most of the class is project-based homework, was pretty fun to do. You can skip lecture, but Julie Johnson is good at teaching the material. Go to class, work on the projects.

Loved this class! Dr. Johnson is the best professor I've had so far at Vanderbilt and she does a great job explaining things. The class isn't too difficult as long as you put in the effort outside of class. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her!

Never takes CS before so I thought the class was difficult. That being said, Johnson was incredibly unhelpful. Lectures are OK, but I went to her office hours for help on projects several times and got little help, so go to the TAs instead. Also, she made an error in my final grade and I only got it changed after arguing with her for days via email

I took CS103 before this class so take my review with a grain of salt. Still, Johnson knows what shes doing. I paid a lot of attention in ALL her lectures, and did all the hw myself. If you do that, you'll get an A no prob, even if you dont read much of the textbook. there's a LOT of hw, but if you do it you don't have to study much. Take her class

Dr. Johnson is an excellent professor. She teaches the material clearly and posts notes and other helpful material online for you to peruse. If you EVER have any questions she is easy to reach and gets back quickly with good help. Homework and quizzes are graded fairly, material is clear, there are never surprises. Great class, great professor.
Really clear, overall good teacher. Sells CS really well, made me change my major.  Ton of homework, lectures are really helpful and power points are online

Passionate about the subject, encouraging and wants you to succeed, great for people new to CS. Homework assignments are, for the most part, pretty easy but very time-consuming. Tests are easy B's if you don't study, so long as you do the homework, and the homework grades pull your average up. Lectures useful but often slower than need be.
She is really nice and personable. One of the better CS1101 professors.

Dr. Johnson is so helpful and clear on everything, but she tends to repeat things so lectures could get a little boring. Homeworks are challenging but they help you learn. I started with No experience in programming yet still found this class to be very manageable until the very last part (which is still okay but not as easily).
Yes

CS 231 with Johnson isn't that hard. If you get a jump on the HW before the quiz you can do well on both. She is enthusiastic and wants you to learn but has many downsides: her lectures are often convoluted and don't cover assessment material well. She teaches too many classes and is often too flustered to help during office hours

Julie tries, but her powerpoints and activities are really confusing. I learned everything through homeworks and quizzes. She is really nice though and wants you to do well. And she's better than Tarias.
Although enthusiastic, the lectures are unclear. Nicety may cover some of the downsides up to some extent.
She's charismatic so her lectures are interesting. She's great at explaining tough concepts. Cares a lot about students and wants to interest them and help them succeed.
Good teacher. Class is easy if you do all the homework. Just go to class and do the required homeworks and the A will come. She is good at explaining tough concepts.

Great teacher, she has so much interest in the subject and is great for students just starting to learn CS. Definitely take her if you have the option. You should read the textbook though because her lectures can be a little more general than what you should know for the tests.
Nice, Friendly, CS teacher. Helpful if you have problems with either your app or the software. Definitely recommend taking this module as it is interesting and easy.
Great professor and very enthusiastic about the subject. She is really nice and helpful.

This CS module is basically about programming in MATLAB, and when I took this class the programs were about cryptography algorithms. Lectures are kind of tangent to your assignments, but the slides do contain a bunch of codes that you may find extremely useful. Overall, it is an easy class and she grades generously.

Nicest and most helpful teacher ever. I went into the class asking myself why I chose CS for my ES140 module, finished the class wondering how hard it would be to become a CS major. She is an awesome professor

Pretty easy tests and homework, although the average was much lower than previous semesters. Class can be slow, but the book isn't completely in sync with how she teaches the material, so if you go and do you homework you should get an A no problem. She's also listens if you think you deserved more points on a test or exam, so be friendly.
Teacher was helpful, seemed to enjoy algorithms. Will have difficulty with your work if you do real code. Modestly fast grading, not very difficult.

Class is pretty boring and just a bunch of examples (and not really necessary, as you can generally reason everything out yourself), but she does give extra-credit quizzes for just about every homework (which is nice, as they are doable, but can be a little difficult).  Tests and the final were a joke, with the class avg somewhere around a 90.
Hard homeworks but you can always talk to her and she will help you through it. Test are very easy and straightforward.
No Comments
she sucks
She's not great - doesn't always know what she's talking about.

Not very smart.  She shows up to class unprepared and has to figure things out as she goes, often times making mistakes and correcting them later.  Her TA is one of the worst ones I have ever had.  Faily straightforward material, but she finds a way to screw you on your grade.  Do not take.

cs150, cs212, cs250 - she explains things as if we have never had cs before, which although sometimes it is boring, it is very helpful overall.  just show up for class and don't fall asleep cause i think her lectures end up being really informative.
No Comments

Dr. Lovensheimer is a very entertaining and engaging lecture who brings in a lot of his own experiences and stories about musical theatre. His lectures are interspersed with video clips of shows, and the class is graded based on 4 reflection papers that are each 4-5 pages. He will be missed at Vanderbilt!

Professor Love is very passionate and this class is not stressful or hard at all. He genuinely wants to share his love for musical theater with his students and he definitely knows what he is talking about. He doesn't give much feedback on the papers but he's also not a tough grader. I enjoyed this class and it fulfills HCA.

His lectures are very boring, unless you're into musicals. However, he grades the papers easily, which are only grades for this class. Should be an easy A if you attend his class and put in decent effort in the papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Such a fun class if you like musical theater. Lots of videos and relatively entertaining lectures. This class had very little work too, easy A if you show up and write a few short papers!

The overall class topic and lectures are kind of boring if you aren't into musicals. However, the professor is super nice and accomodating. There were only a couple of papers to write and the grades very high. Take this class for AXLE
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: MUSL 2600 is Vandy's most hidden gem, if you need AXLE credit for US History and want an easy A, take this class! Dr. L's lectures are clear and interesting, his tests follow the study guide exactly, and there is almost no HW. Despite what the description says in YES, you do NOT need to have previous music experience for this class.
He is an incredible professor. The lectures were interesting and the test material was easy. Just follow along with the slides and you will be fine.
One of the worst professors at the school. Lovensheimer is sassy, unhelpful, and unresponsive.

Pretty easy class but he was extremely unhelpful. He is a very weird lecturer. Also, he makes you read his own book and then has you write an essay on it. Basically if you just present the same arguments that he uses in the book you will get an A on it.

Pretty easy class. The professor is very funny and shows you a lot of clips in class. Lecture based class so you don't have to know anything before going in, even though it helps to know about musicals. He's a lenient grader even though he returns papers really late.

Absolutely the easiest class ive ever taken. Two take home (but not open book?) essays, a final paper, and one review of a show. You can not do a second of work other than writing the papers and still get an A. Also so funny, entertaining, and overall a great guy. DEFINITELY take this class if you get the chance

Went into this class thinking it was a joke.  Not a complete joke, but very easy. 2 take home midterms (they're essays though), a performance review of a show that you go see on your own time, and a final paper.  If you like musical theater, you'll love the class. If you don't, have a friend in the class sign you in.

Frustrating. Does not teach facts, assigns articles about abstract concepts that go way over most students' heads, talks about overly complex topics without covering the basics. Assigns a reading, then sits on his stool and talks about the reading for the entire class. Some class discussion, otherwise little engagement. VERY nice guy, accessible.
Very easy class definitely take.  Tests are easy, i never paid attention and got A+'s on everything.  Outlines he gives before tests literally tell u everything u need to know.  EASY A
This class seems to be getting slightly harder each semester. My friend took this last semester and told me the tests this semester are a little harder.

Dr. Lovensheimer is amazing! Makes lectures as interesting as American music can be (which honestly isn't interesting at all). But he gives reviews that make tests easy, but you do have to know the material before the test. If you are looking for an easy A I would definitely recommend this class, but you do have to do some reading and studying.

Had an overall great experience in the class.  The textbook reading is not always engaging, but he finds GREAT supplemental readings to augment the text.  Does have a liberal bias, but working hard on reading and writing assignments earns his respect.  Very laid back and passionate about the subject.  Reasonable in terms of homework assignments.
Take class
