Dr. Lovensheimer is THE BOMB!  I loved his class.  He's such an interesting lecturer, a very vibrant teacher and all around just great. I think I ended up with a B+ but he gave A-!!
Dr. L is AWESOME!!!!! He really enjoys what he's teaching and is there for the students. This class was my absolute favorite and I HIGHLY recommend it.

Absolutely awesome class. The tests are really easy, but that definitely does not mean the class is a joke. Dr. Love knows how to make an very interesting lecture. The early stuff in the course (Native Americans, Puritans) is a little slow, but the rest of the material is really good. Go to class, get the attendance points.

I really liked his class a lot. He makes it incredibly fun and interesting. Gives really helpful review guides to the tests, study from them and you can ace the tests! Realizes it's an elective, so doesn't give a heavy workload. Really seems to understand the students. I would recommend him to everyone!! he really made music fun.

Wonderful prof, hilarious too. Lots of cool documentaries watched in class. He takes attendance on Fridays when he thinks people will skip/be out of town. Three exams, two papers. He makes the tests from his notes on OAK so don't bother taking your own notes in class, just show up and enjoy.

The best guy! Take him if you can. he is fun, intelligent, interesting & wants all to do well. returns email immediately (unlike prior comments). Made me excited & passionate about subject I never was before. He's a must!

Really great guy. Cares about students and wants them to do well. Pop music lectures were almost always interesting and sometimes funny as well. Not difficult to get a good grade as long as you memorize and study from his review sheet.

AWESOME PROFESSOR! Knows more about musical theatre history than most people in the world. You can tell he really knows his stuff and although his lectures aren't mandatory you want to go because it's interesting. Pretty soon you'll be reading the textbook he's writing. Awesome guy

Loves American music and shows his enthusiasm every day in class. Know details he says are important. Read about the songs' musical characteristics from the book for quizzes, know everything said in review sessios for the tests, and you can get the A. Best way to fill the American history requirement.

Funny, engaging, incredibly passionate about musicals, however he is AWFUL about returning emails, and incredibly inefficient about grading. Decided a few days before our last midterm that we were not going to have one anymore because he simply didn't have time to grade them all. Incredibly unfair to those who needed the grade.
Funny, engaging, knowledgeable. You'll have to do a good bit of memorizing for this class, which is both boring and stupid, but it's not difficult.
He loves musicals and he's very funny. It's a fun class and I like that he explains the musicals in the context of the history.

Very interesting guy and has a lot to share.  You can skip the class once a week and still do well by going to the review sessions and studying what the TA tells you will be on the exams.  If you are looking for a 3 credit course with not too much work, this is the course and the prof for you.
EASY! goto class for attendance points and dont pay attention. I never read and I got an A. Just memorize all the crap he tells you to and make sure you know the songs!
Intersting class and interesting guy.  Tests are straightforward and grading isn't too harsh.

Ok this class appears easy and many upper class people will tell you it is. Well guess what? HE CHANGED THE WHOLE CURRICULUM. this class is no longer that easy, BE CAREFUL. getting an A in this class would require lots of studying and hard work.

The jazz class was easy for the most part, except for having to read an arduous book and write a paper on it.  The material is also interesting and the class is most bearable when he's not throwing a mini tantrum or cracking jokes about drinking, drugs,a nd partying.  He is overly verbose, and has a tendency to pretend to be humble.  He buggged me.
Country Music is easy and very interesting-- he realizes people take the class because they want to
Great professor

Take this class! It fulfills american component of CPLE and it's an easy A. The material isn't that boring, and Dr.L is really an interesting guy. He's a really funny guy and REALLY wants his students to do well. Everyone should take this class
Easiest Class Ever...I went to class only for the listening quizzes and exams...he called me out on it when I handed in my final, but I still got a flat A...this class is purely for GPA Boosting
He's a great one.  Knows wayyy too much... in a good way
The class is harder than it sounds, but there is always a review and review sheet before tests.  I loved the class.  The man is hilarious on top of everything else.
Maybe I watch too much tv, but am I the only one who thinks this guy looks like Mr Garrison from South Park?

Dr. L is great, funny and full of knowledge.  his smaller classes at blair are a lot of work, but worth it.  he really does care about his students and works hard to get everyone in office hours at least once or twice.

This class is a great. I never went, except for the quizzes and tests and will get an A-. He emails you review sheets that tell you what you need to know. HONESTLY, THIS CLASS IS AN EASY A. I never read, never went to class, or studied except the night before a quiz or test. He's also a really nice guy. He called me out for not going to class.

Very interesting class but terrible in terms of grades and papers.  It's just really weird how he teaches and wants the papers done.  Don't take it.  I would have dropped out if I had known about that class.

Dr. L is absolutely adorable and his favorite Beatle was John.  Definitely take this class, but keep in mind that sororities get the tests and will always do well without having to take notes or pay attention.  Tests are fill in the blank, so if you blank out you're screwed, but lectures are AWESOME.

this dude is AMAZING.  he is hilarious.  His course sort of blows.  His tests are very very easy AND you get to see engineers do poorly.  it is priceless.  I still talk to him when i see him around.  He is a great musical mind.  He will make you think about music in a new way.  VERY EASY TESTS.  no homework.  great teacher.
the best teach at vanderbilt

Perhaps not the easiest class in the book--the fact that there's only 3 listening quizzes (instead of 7) makes the class a bit more difficult.  Learned an incredible amount, however.  He no longer hands out review sheets, so attend the review sessions, read your notes and you'll be fine.
Wonderfully fun and very into his subject.  It's always good to have someone like that teaching.  Glad to see he's accepted baldness, unlike my current boyfriend!
I hope the school continues to support the country music class.  JL has excellent lectures.  I highly recommend the class and the professor.

Now I'm a big Fan of Love but let me tell you his attitude has been pretty pissy lately. He has not returned our last exams  or papers and we are days away from the final and have no idea what our final grades are. Like I said I like the guy a lot but he needs to stop being so pissy in his emails.
wonderful cple requirement. easy A if you can take notes and study...listening quizzes are kinda hard, though. interesting professor.
Every single person at Vanderbilt should take this class to fulfill the American Component.  It's incredibly easy and Jimbo is an understanding teacher.

Lovensheimer is a badass.  He's funny, interesting and not difficult.  Just come to class and read and you'll be fine, easy A if you do the work.   He's also a really cool guy and worth getting to know outside of the class.
He is awesome! Everyone should take a class from him. You just have to memorize the notes he gives in class and go to review sessions. He's also really helpful outside of class too. Highly recommend
Amazing teacher! this class is insanely easy! it's all memorization! the quizzes are uber easy! i loved this class! any class you can take with him do it!
HE'S AMAZING!!!!
Very interesting.  Very clear lectures.  He always lets you know how everything fits together.  Pretty much the only history credit I've ever enjoyed.
No Comments

Intro to Jazz is one of the best courses I have taken here.  He is an amazing lecturer and really cares about the students.  Not difficult either... just read or come to class and you'll do fine.  I wish more professors were like him.  He rocks!
Very funny and intereting lectures. Would recommend this class to anyone.
Will make you learn to love jazz, even if you don't know what it is.
What a joke, but how much fun. American Popular Music rocks.
very easy
I'm an A/S student, and I get his jokes.
Witty and urbane (not that the A&S kids actually listened closely enough to get the jokes)... this man gives AMAZING lectures. A jewel of a prof.

He is the most adorable and wonderful teacher I have ever had! He makes my every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday! He's funny, sarcastic, and has a wonderful sense of humor! 2 thumbs up (if I had more thumbs, they'd be up to)! He is the epitomy of hotness!
One of the best teachers at this school!  Very interesting class, fun, and easy to study for.
Best teacher at Vanderbilt
The hardest thing about American Music is staying awake.
He is awesome!  His lectures are interesting and still follow the reading, so you feel like your homework is worthwhile.  ALso, his quizzes are very predictable and fair...no tricks here!
What a stud!
He'll tell you everything you never knew about popular music- while also telling you about his quite interesting life!
Fabulous!!!! I can't say enough good things about this prof!
One sweet piece of eye candy.  This hunk of man meat really knows how to teach. Very funny and interesting.
Lovensheimer is AWESOME.  This class was ridiculously easy, and I feel like I'm able to appreciate music on a whole new level.  I'd highly recommend this class and professor...he's very funny, too.
He was an amazing professor.  I learned so much and didn't have to try hard at all.  He wants to make sure that you learn and do well in his class.
Lovensheimer knows his music history and theater. He has a genuine passion for teaching, and really cares about his students. He's a great professor, and keeps you interested and engaged.
Easy grader, and relatively interesting.

Awesome Class..awesome professor!!  Sings, Acts, and plays the piano.  He rocked my world.  Loves the theater and it shows with his class.  And, when I took him, the class was only 2 papers.  Favorite professor I've had at Vandy.
Fabulous, I considered switching to Blair just to take more of his classes
Has a tendency to ramble, but a good teacher.
Great guy, really nice, isn't out to get you at all.
No Comments

Prof. Ward was overall one of the best professors at Vandy. She made me feel comfortable when speaking out in class and did her best to support each and every student in the class. She was extremely accessible outside of class. Her grading was pretty fair overall. Pro tip: MAKE SURE TO STUDY FOR ALL QUIZZES!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ward is a super engaging lecturer with so many creative activities and real-life examples!! Participation is a large portion of your grade but it never feels like a burden. Rated this class a 3 instead of a 2 because the first quiz was unexpectedly difficult (make sure to study) but the other assignments were easy enough to make an A feasible.

I LOVE JULIE WARD! She is SO sweet and kind, always asking us what music we'd like to play while working and getting our feedback about assignments and workload. Interesting population health content too. One of my favorite classes at Vanderbilt!

Dr. Ward is a great professor. She works really hard to make class engaging through in class activities and gives time in class to complete all group assignments. She is clear in what she expects so as long as you pay attention, participate, and do the work you will do well.

Super kind, caring professor. 2 exams, 1 final paper, a few group worksheets. If you are interested in public health, TAKE THIS CLASS. She is very straightforward, compassionate, and accessible outside of class. Very low workload most of the time but study for the exams. Most people I know love her and the class.

- super passionate and engaged lecturer
- 2 "quizzes" (i think now there is 3) but treat them more like mini midterms. you can't just know the definitions, you should actually know whats going on. 
- few other reading assignments (if i remember correctly) 
- final paper 
- didn't do the readings, mainly just skimmed 
- attainable A, love her!!

If you're interested in Public Health, you NEED to take this class. Dr. Ward is extremely knowledgable, with experience as an ER Nurse, and passionate. She's also genuinely kind. Everything you learn is significant and applicable. 100% recommend.

Like another review stated, Dr. Ward is truly a gem at Vanderbilt! She is an incredible educator and a wonderful person. Her Population Health class was incredibly informative and she was very passionate about the subject. 

Her exams were not difficult, although some of the questions may be challenging. Her other assignments were great.

Vanderbilt is extremely lucky to have Professor Ward. She is truly one of the best professors I have ever had that obviously cares a lot about the topic and also knows a lot. She makes the lectures interactive, clear, and easy to understand. One of the gems at Vandy. Population Health is also something that applies in a lot of different fields.

Prof. Klass is incredibly knowledgeable/into the material, and it shows. She is not a harsh grader and provides ample opportunities for revision. Sometimes there is a lot to read, but 95% of the time it's pretty interesting. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Heavy on the reading, but graded homework is light with only a few assignments (3-4 essays) given all semester. Professor Klass gives extremely detailed feedback on essays, making it very easy to use the feedback to revise and improve your own work in order to get a better grade on second attempts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Passionate teacher, class is easy to follow and fun. Not too heavy content wise, but a good amount of reading.

Getting an A is possible, but not without Herculean effort. Expect to read 300+ pages weekly and watch a few movies too. Do not think you can skim, you simply cannot. Unless you are super passionate about the formation of major Hollywood studios, I would recommend a different W course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: For anyone looking to take an easy course, this was not one. There are tons of readings due every class (3-4 readings, 100+ pages total). 3 real papers, one small paper, along with a film quiz at the end of the semester. Participation grade is weighted heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking an Honors Seminar with Professor Klass. The amount of reading was reasonable, especially if you organize your time wisely. She gives constructive feedback on your short stories, and you can rewrite any of them to improve your grade. Participation matters in the class, but all the discussions were open-ended and engaging.

Take this class if you want to challenge yourself (good for improving writing, not as a grade booster if you are stem). She has changed her grading scale to match what you would normally expect for an A- and A. Speaking up in class is easier than sending notes, so I'd recommend doing that. It's not exactly a funny class, but an A is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I honestly don't get the hate for this class. There was a lot of reading to do in class but at the end of the day it is a writing class so I expected it. The grading is not too harsh and although getting an A might be difficult, it is totally not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is a little boring and reading-heavy, but after a little feedback she lowered the amount of readings per class (from 4-5 to 2-3). If you like fiction and writing your own, you'll like this class, but if not, keep it pushing (Cute little short story due every 1-2 weeks). Class was Hons-1810W-85, not ENG
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ppl seem to be complaining that there is too much reading but this is a W class so I'm not sure what they expected. My other W class had even more readings. Professor Klass is very responsive, grades quick, and allows for rewrites on all writing assignments. If your a decent writer and raise your hand once in a while, you'll get an A.

literally so much work for no reason: between 30-60 pages of reading per class plus papers and movies. she rambles for the whole time and i cannot pay attention in that class. think scary grandma vibes. she gives u option to rewrite papers and doesnt grade too harshly but an A is 95+. likely to get A- or B+
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Klass' first year writing seminar is definitely not interesting. While she assigns a lot of boring homework, you really only have to do one homework every month or so to do well on the papers and she gives unlimited rewrites. The class is an easy A but you have to be willing to sit around bored for 2.5 hours a week :)

Overall a really great professor who has a-lot of knowledge! Allows revisions for papers, and really helps to explain how to become a better writer. Super reading heavy and participation in class matters. Does ramble pretty often but thats her charm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The premise of this class sounded extremely intriguing and was a great respite from my stem course load. It did not disappoint. Jewish Humor was so funny and I learned so much about the culture I did not previously know. I would recommend taking this course if you know a little about the religion already, but it felt very accessible. Many readings

You can really tell Dr. Klass is passionate about the things she teaches! There are a lot of readings, and if she notices that people aren't caught up, she will start giving pop quizzes, so please at least know the plot. There are 4 writing assignments and one Final Term paper. Overall, she gives good feedback, and an A or A- is totally achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's a little quirky but funny and pretty nice. Class is easy enough if you do the readings although they can be lengthy. PLEASE participate once a class so she doesn't start doing reading quizzes. Otherwise, there's no tests and essays have infinite rewrites. Essay grading is slightly harsh, but fair especially considering the rewrites.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She gives a crazy amount of reading - be prepared to read for several hours a night and have close to 100 pages of reading per class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are no exams in Jewish Humor, plus unlimited rewrites on papers, but the class is brutal. Klass is very strange, and often off topic. You have to like the humor she likes, or else you will not do well in this very niche class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Barely any writing assignments despite it being a writing class which is nice, but a lot of reading. Participation matters, so you actually have to do the readings. An A is a 95, but if you do the bare minimum you'll finish with an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the tougher englishW classes. Good for people who like reading but not writing. You read 3-4 full length plays a week which you discuss during class which was difficult to keep up with at times. However, she is super understanding and I learned a ton. Pretty hard to get an A, but do the bare minimum and you get an A-

My favorite professors at this school. She was super accessible even when online and super nice. She rewards people that participate and are genuinely interested in the class. Very helpful during office hours and always willing to help a student improve their writing. I am a STEM major at this school and hate writing but this class was still great!

This class was essentially just a science fiction book club. It may seem like a lot of reading at first, but it doesn't feel like that much because the stories are all pretty interesting and different. You can redo all your papers too, so getting at least an A- is very do-able. Prof. Klass talks a lot but keeps things engaging.

Professor Klass's lectures were very interesting and the material was engaging yet very dense at times. Normally only 1-2 A's per semester as she requires a 95 for an A. However, she gives rewrites for all three papers so getting an A- is a breeze. If you are looking to get an A, you will also need to make sure to participate daily in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Take her class! She is so quirky, funny, and amusing. A 95 is an A which is annoying but it is doable and the A- is pretty easy to get. Actually interesting material/readings and the papers are short and to the point. No reading quizzes either. Great prof and class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you want an A, be prepared to put a lot of effort into your papers (which will be the entire grade). If you want an A-, do the absolute bare minimum. You can't get a B. Klass acts like a crackhead but she's entertaining and understanding. Strong recommend

I've taken a few classes with her. Her classes are extremely easy but are also easy to get lulled to sleep in. A's are 95s and its pretty hard to get above a 96 on any paper and easy to get below 95. Depending on class, reading can be a lot or average. Try not to get on her bad side as the majority of grading is subjective - and this should be an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor who really knows her stuff and is passionate about it - I went in not caring about Drama and left really enjoying the readings. She grades papers very easily, if you read the plays and put some effort into them you will get an A.

Take her. you'll be glad. Just make sure you read and attend class. She'll give pop quizzes because she knows people aren't reading. Sparknotes will help half of the time. Easy essays with regrade. Occasional extra credit if you write something on your own. Definite easy A-. You'll have to slightly work for the A, but getting the A is pretty easy

Interesting lecturer. Lots of reading but it's generally pretty good stuff (if you like fiction). There were 20-25 pages of essays to write but she's not a harsh grader and allows rewrites. If you do good work, show up to every class, participate, and take advantage of rewrites you'll get an A.

Klass is a very interesting, funny and intelligent woman, and this was the easiest class I have had at Vandy. Participation is important, and the more you talk, the easier she will grade you. You get to rewrite every paper, and she is very helpful. It helps to be interested in plays/drama to be engaged in discussions and not get bored sometimes.

According to students who have taken her before, she has gotten harder. There's a crazy lot of reading and she expects you to participate in discussions. She let's you do rewrites for papers (three 5 pagers) where your final grade is the average. I recommend that you get it checked before you have to turn it in. She is very helpful and funny.

Professor Klass is probably one of the easiest teachers I have ever had. Mostly because the course I took was a lower level class. Make sure you do the reading because class participation is big. She's a very easy grader and lets you do as many re-writes as you want to get a better grade. Take her if you can!

Really interesting teacher.  She assigned a lot of reading in my Jewish Science Fiction class, but it was all really interesting so I enjoyed doing it.  She started assigning pop quizzes halfway through the semester because everyone else wasn't doing the reading/participating in class. If you actually do the work then you'll get an A no problem
ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She grades based on if she likes you or not. She was so boring. The readings are useless

Class is easy. A few 4-5 page papers. A 7-9 page final paper that can be on any topic. Gives out a ton of reading assignments, which you can pretty much ignore. Attendance is required. Class couldn't be any more boring. Requires kids to watch 4 movies. Some of the movies are actually good. If you're even a remotely decent writer, you're good.

Easy class, but she is CRAZY. You don't have to read the thousands of optional articles she gives. She doesn't know how to use a computer. Only take home quizzes and papers. Movies on Thursday nights are a pain in my ass.

Terrible. I legitimately question how/if she has an English degree. She seems like a nice enough lady, but as a professor she's quite awful. An easy course but not one to take if you value the money and time you spend on your education at Vandy. Worst class I've had so far. English majors should AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS

She will find the longest possible movie to take up your Thursday nights, but you can write about how horrid the movie was in your paper. Do rewrites. Following her suggestions boosts your grade every time. Tries to make class interesting. Don't worry about the myriad of extra papers she suggests you read, not necessary. Overall enjoyable class.

Extremely nice. Very knowledgeable but scatterbrained and half the time you're just wondering, "Why do I, or you, care?" Lecture has little to do with any graded assignment but counts off final grade for too many absences. Horrible selection of readings, but overall not a bad choice if you need to get a 100-W out of the way. A or B for sure.

Really chill class. Just show up and do what she asks you to do, and you should do fine.  Also, she allows re-writes -- which everybody loves.  Her reading selections are also pretty awesome.  Lots of relatively modern and interesting stuff.  TAKE  the class. You won't regret it!

Dr. Shepard is a great professor and it's very simple and straightforward to get an A. Everything is graded as either satisfactory or not yet, and you can revise any not yet until you receive a satisfactory. Attendance is optional (except for peer teaching/exam days) and all exams are open note. Great professor and easy option for a science credit!

This professor is very kind. She is eccentric/quirky, but exactly what you would hope for when learning Astro or physics. People are mad because they don't try or show up and end with an A-. This will be the easiest MNS credit you can find, and the classes are relatively interesting.

Very easy class that you only have to attend like 7 times in the semester. All of the assignments teach you nothing and are just busy work. Shephard is super condescending and rude though which makes it unbearable to attend class.

This class is extremely easy. Attendance isn't mandatory and people rarely go. 4 in-person multiple choice tests were somewhat hard but you could revise all for full credit. The rest of the assignments were meaningless and so easy. My problem was her attitude in class. She crashed out on us a lot for nothing, and didn't create a strong environment.

Dr. Shepard is very knowledgeable and passionate about the content, and she truly cares about the mental health and well-being of her students. A few assignments and open-book tests that can all be revised until they are "satisfactory". It's an easy A as long as you do the work. Very open to feedback and strives to improve.

So sweet. Never have to go to class. Genuinely got a 100. It's all completion-based. If you want to learn astronomy, great, take the class, and if you don't, that's fine, you can coast by and get an A. No in-class tests (just 2 out-of-class one-page papers with 5 days' notice). Lightwork.

Her lectures are a little convoluted at times, but overall she is a great lecturer. You can revise assignments for full credit, and she does fun activities in class. It's a very easy but informative class.

Take this class if you're trying to get you're lab credit for A&S. She's the goat, 2 take-home tests, and some homework assignments every week that's relatively easy to knock-out. When taken with the lab is really when I learned, but the class was not stressful at all, and she's intentional in making sure it's not stressful. Great intro class.

Relatively new professor which shows through changes in the syllabus throughout the semester (she dropped a few assessment this semester). She is perceptive to feedback given to her and is open to conversation if you have questions or concerns. Her lectures and demonstrations are fun if you actually pay attention.

Tries to make class fun and interactive, and is accessible during office hours for help. Be sure to read the textbook, since much of exam content is not covered in lectures. Tests aren't too hard otherwise, and have test corrections and opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't know why everyone seems to hate her. This was one of the easiest classes ever. Extremely forgiving grading and material is, well, introductory. I read/took notes on the textbook, and classes helped reinforce learned ideas with practice. She's somewhat "millennial cringe" but not absolutely insufferable.

Hardest class I've ever taken at Vanderbilt. Tests were SO unnecessarily hard for an intro-level class. She doesn't teach, and makes so many mistakes and then argues when you try to say she's wrong. Very hostile classroom environment. Everyone was worried for their grades all semester. DO NOT take her class!

She made this class unnecessarily difficult. Seems like she liked teaching she just wasn't good at it. Don't buy lecture tutorials most unnecessary thing ever. READ TEXTBOOK she doesn't teach any of the material.

While this course was by no means perfect, a majority of these ratings are overly harsh. Dr. Shepard was occasionally difficult during lecture, but she does seem to genuinely encourage and appreciate constructive feedback about her teaching. Be prepared to read the textbook, as only some concepts are addressed during lecture. Overall easy A.

The course was very disorganized, and expectations were never clear. A large portion of the exam material was never actually taught in class. Grading was inconsistent across TAs, and there was zero accountability. She refuses to answer emails on weekends. The overall tone of the class was condescending
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. Doesn't lecture, which makes us study ourselves outside of class. Condescending to students. Seems passionate in Astro -- I found myself growing to hate astronomy cause of her class. Can confidently say that she is the single worst professor I had during my four years here.

Goes off on some weird tangents that are interesting if you like physics but also sometimes difficult to follow. Didn't think that intro-level physics would cover some quantum mechanics material but overall the class was structured so that it was basically impossible not to get an A (at least in fall of 2024)

Crashed out because we corrected a practice test question and she refused to believe that she was wrong. Put that question on the test and marked the opposite of what was deemed correct in lecture to be right on the test. Overall, very condescending and will try to make you feel inferior. Would not take again.
Do not take her classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible. She's always in a bad mood and is extremely passive aggressive to her students. Acts like she's some special, great teacher for not doing lecture-based classes, which in reality just leads to awkward class activities and unorganized slides. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the least favorite teacher I've ever had. She's simply just mean. Gets visibly angry during class, is condescending to students when they don't understand a concept, and almost yells at the class when someone doesn't raise their hand. Also made the quizzes unnecessarily hard, even when this class is literally just an intro science credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Shepard. She was helpful, accessible and kind. As a student, I could tell she wants us to all to do well in her classroom. There are many opportunities to do better and improve. She is very kind and approachable, and is really willing to make time to help you be successful.

Super easy class, possibly no way you couldn't get an A if you're somewhat competent. 4 Quizzes with 1 drop, with up to 20% test corrections, and the 3 quizzes could average out for your final exam grade. 

She also wasn't the nicest teacher and I thought she was joking at times but was actually being kinda mean to a student.
lots of textbook reading but interesting class
Very easy A, but get ready to read because she doesn't teach very much. Definitely take if you need AXLE credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is her first year teaching, and I expected issues and kinks in her teaching style over the semester. However, she never improved. She was constantly disorganized, and never actually used class time. She expected US to learn the material through the textbook, then we would come to lectures and "talk about it". It went as well as you would guess
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is very disorganized, isn't engaging, and feels like a total waste of time most days. No lecture as we read the textbook ahead of time, and she relies on students to ask questions about the text, which goes exactly how you'd expect. The expectations for quizzes are unclear. Very unprofessional and all over the place. Avoid if you can.

It is her first year teaching so I think she would improve as time goes on. For physics 1010 it was all conceptual (no math) and she offered 100% corrections on tests, so the class is an easy A. As a teacher, she is a little disorganized, but you can tell she cares about her students and tries her best to keep people engaged.

Too emotional and inexperienced to teach properly. Devolves into tangents on random stuff. Don't take in an election year, because if her preferred candidate loses then she will lash out at the entire class like she the day after election day. She needs a better grasp on her emotions and experience before she can teach properly.

She's gotten better throughout the semester, but she's alright. Still really disorganized and unclear expectations, wouldn't take again. Also goes on long rants on stuff. She's ok though, will probably be better next semester since its her first semester ever teaching a class, so I hope her ratings increase in the future.

People need to stop hating. Unless you have a room temperature IQ or no motivation to study for a few hours for a test and go to office hours, this is an easy A. There are rebates and extra credit to help you, and Dr. Shepard is very caring and wants her students to succeed.  Just pay attention and do lecture tutorials!

The class itself is easy, but the only reason it's hard is because she isn't clear about what content will appear on the exam and her study guides don't help either. Her class has no organization and she's too passionate about astronomy with a tendency to enter into long tangents about random stuff that has nothing to do with our content.

She's really nice and caring for her students, and is (occasionally) funny, but her teaching style is disorganized and the exams are not reflective of the study guides or class content. Only relies on students reading textbook and her answering questions about the textbook, but she veers off into rants on unrelated stuff.  Very easy class though.
She gets it, shes funny as hell and doesn't ask too much of you. Grades very easy but at the same time you actually learn something because she makes class enjoyable.

This is Dr. Shepard's first year as a professor so take the other reviews with a grain of salt. I would agree that her tests are not fair/representative of the class & the study guides suck. She has lately been connected with students more, acting relatable, and actually becoming funny. She needs to relax and find her structure and fix the grading.

Dr. Shephard seems like a good person and the class was interesting at first, but she quickly became uninteresting and unfunny. She doesn't seem motivated to actually do the work of teaching, so she instead assigns us long readings that she barely explains and answers in class as she goes on long tangents on unrelated stuff. Really disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is entirely based on textbook readings that we just ask her questions about. No lectures, just question and answer stuff about the textbook. Even then, she doesn't go over stuff about the textbook and tends to go on rants. Really confusing and disorganized class, and exams aren't reflective of the study guides. Easy, yet misleading content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Shephard is genuinely a great person and evidently passionate about her field. However, the class and her teaching style is super disorganized. Our grades are determined by four tests, some questions of which have things we didn't go over in class. Great person, but tedious, disorganized, and annoying class structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Shepard is a nice person, but she clearly lacks organisation and experience as an educator. She relies heavily on students reading the book and understanding the content on their own. It is never clear what she will test you on. The grading is very chill, you can get points back for every test. Overall a manageable A.

She is incredibly disorganized. Doesn't teach students, relys on us to read textbook then spends all of class going over questions. She is very unfunny - everytime she makes a joke nobody laughs. Matter of fact, everytime she makes a joke I consider never coming to class and transferring schools. She is genuinely the least funny person of all time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class isn't as bad as some of the other reviews make it. The content is easy but the tests are somewhat difficult since it's really easy to get answers wrong. But it's nothing too hard and it's easy to get an A. Her teaching style is pretty hectic though and it's hard to follow her, but she's alright as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is insanely disorganized. No lectures, only "Q&A" sessions which sometimes veers into rants about stuff we haven't covered. Study guides don't really reflect how hard the quizzes actually are, concerning since our grades are from quizzes. Also doesn't make it clear on what content will be on the quiz. Wouldn't recommend taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Shephard is probably the worst professor that I have ever taken at Vanderbilt. Completely oblivious to student's needs, incredibly disorganized in teaching style, she breaks her promises to students, and is the study guides do not reflect the difficulty of the exams, which constitute almost all of your grade. If you take astronomy, avoid her.
He is the best professor! This class isn't easy but he explains concepts better than anybody else. He's a funny and passionate dude who wants his students to succeed.

This is just a hard class. I didn't know what was going on most of the time, but Nchare is an incredibly caring, funny professor that wants his students to succeed. Tests are doable, and he is accessible. Econometrics will inevitably be difficult but Nchare is the man and the prof to take it w.

Offers a wide range of office hours outside of class. Exams are not that bad. However the 4 problem sets throughout the semester take such a long time. There is also a group project with unclear guidelines but he grades pretty leniently on it so as long as you complete it you should be fine. Very fun in lecture, he engages the class in the examples

if you took AP stats, you'll be fine. if not, study from the textbook, skim the notes for excel commands. he's a nice and funny guy, but his voice puts me to sleep during lecture. do practice problems and practice exam, usually at least one Q will be word for word from practice sets/exams. nothing too difficult, but sometimes felt disorganized

I wasn't sure about Nchare in Econ Stats, but after taking Econometric Methods with him, I have a newfound respect for him. The content is tough, but he is great at explaining things. He'd happily explain something 3 different times if you asked him. He tells you what's on the exams. He has a very unserious side to him which can make class fun

This is the toughest Econ class for the major and I would recommend doing it with Nchare. He's a very nice guy that will literally give you the answers for problem sets if you go to office hours. The content and lecture slides are difficult, but the exams are doable and he grades leniently. He will tell you what types of questions are on each exam.
Super great guy. Slides can be difficult to understand and exam difficulty varies, but he is generous with the grading. Good professor to take for what is known to be a hard class.

The nicest guy ever but lectures are boring and basically useless. Nchare will tell you the answers to the problem set if you go to office hours and he'll tell you exactly what's going to be on the exam.

Prof. Nchare is an awesome guy. His teaching is above average, but it's nothing to write home about. The class is straightforward; tests mirror the textbook and problem sets, and sometimes he even repeats questions. He's very accessible outside of class and is always willing to help. He might not be why you get an A, but he won't hurt your chances.

Nchare was interesting and fun to be in class with. From what I've heard, this is probably your best bet for 3035 even though he's not outstanding. Exam difficulty is reasonable. Project expectations were unclear.

Very nice guy and was very accessible outside of class. Teaches how to use Excel instead of stats sometimes which is somewhat annoying. Really cares about his students. There are weekly quizzes and 5 problem sets, but exams make up a bulk of the grade so there is not much room for error. Great prof if you have experience w/ stats, good prof if not

He assumed students had taken AP Stats before when half the class did not. Be prepared to teach yourself all of the material. It is not difficult at all, but definitely requires you to put in the work. Exams are very similar to practice questions given in class. He is the sweetest man ever!!

Nchare is a really nice guy and he definitely cares about his students. However, his lectures are pretty unorganized and he is a bit difficult to work with. The class isn't that hard, but an A is a 94, so you can't make too many mistakes.
The goat
super light lowkey the easiest class ever taken, if you've ever taken ap stats the class will be a breeze

Professor was very nice and very helpful in office hours, but a bit unclear in class. I think the disorganization was his main fault, but other than that a very decent professor. If you have taken AP stat, then this class will come very easy to you. Midterms were very easy, quizzes were honestly harder but not worth as much.

He is a really nice guy who cares about his students, but the lectures are really hard to follow along. If you took AP stats you'll be fine. But beware you'll mostly be teaching yourself as he glosses over a lot of important concepts, and spends a lot of time proving irrelevant formulas.
He is a nice guy, I enjoy talking with him. The class makes sense if you pay attention at least 60% of the time. If you show up, you don't need to do the readings. Grading is very reasonable.
Nice big guy with energy everyday, even sometimes his lectures are confused but he will teach u that point for 1000times!
Class is very easy, but a waste of time. Class time isn't used very productively, so it's smarter to just skip class and take notes off the Powerpoints.

Dr. Nchare wants students to succeed in his class even if the way his class is structured may not reflect this. Sometimes during lectures he would skip over the challenging concepts and even after studying exams were kind of challenging but grades were very curved at the end of the semester especially if you attend class/stop at office hours.

Great guy but not a great professor. Has trouble explaining concepts in a digestible manner and kids who took AP Stats in high school end up teaching their peers more than the prof. He will attempt to explain things to you until you understand though and in general is interested in student well-being but is highly inflexible with deadlines.
Super chill and a great choice for econometrics. He is super clear with what he expects of us/ what he will put on the tests. Class is very flexible and will extend deadlines reasonably.

I actually enjoyed Dr. Nchare's econometrics class. He is super kind and genuinely cares about each of his students. There is a ton of work (5-6 problem sets, 3-4 coding assignments, 1 final project, 2 midterms and a final) but the tests are really simple and he'll help you through the problem sets and coding assignments
Bro is a legend. Take him.

am I the only person who find the Professor's class impossible to get a good grade? As someone who have never taken stats before, doing his hw assignments is such a horrible and frustrating thing. He often put concepts that he haven't taught in class into the hw sets. (also, there could be minor errors in the slides regarding various concepts)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Karim is a nice guy but his class is disorganized. Lectures are dry and vague (class is usually only half full), so you will end up self studying for each exam. Exams/homework is usually pretty straightforward/easy but can be oddly tough sometimes. He can be hard to understand - both when he's lecturing and about his own grading criteria
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: average but gets the job done. Sometimes he'll rush and you have to learn it all my yourself.

Lectures were regurgitations of the textbook but less in-depth. Very vague about when lecturing and telling you which content his tests will cover. Makes you memorize tons of formulas. P-sets are straightforward (except one); he drops your lowest grade. Tests are somewhat tough, esp. if you're bad at probability. Each exam is 25-35% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: bro kinda garbage at lecturing, but his content is very easy. Just review his powerpoint slides to truly understand material. Homeworks are alright (drops lowest), tests are pretty reasonable. Not the worst, but far from the best.
This class is not that hard, and as long as you review the slides and do homework you'll be fine. Karim himself is a little bit hard to understand sometimes but he's a nice guy overall.

Attending lectures is not mandatory and honestly doesn't make much of a difference in what you learn. When I went to class, I either did work for other classes or just fell asleep because Karim is so dry. BASICALLY, as long as you review the slides and play with his review problems before a test, you will be fine.
OKAY professor. Nice in office hours, but very odd lectures -- there would be times he'd just go silent for absolutely no reason. Easy enough class.

The class itself was very easy.  He was very clear about what he wanted us to know as the lectures were always posted online.  His lectures were almost word for word the textbook, and he graded on the slower end.  All in all, good class.

Karim was great. Not sure why so many people disliked him. Go to lectures and do the homeworks and you're sure to do well on exams. Everything he tests on is directly from the lecture slides. He's a little dry and unclear when lecturing, but the material on the powerpoints is always good.

Not the best at teaching. Kind of just lectures and you have to figure it out on your own. It's pretty much on the student to do well. Nice guy though. He doesn't always show it but he definitely cares.

If you go to every class/ really grind before the tests you will be fine. Def not as easy as Lurea, but is a good option for econ stats. Using the textbook helps. He truly does care, but may not explain things in the best way. If you put in the work you will be fine

In my opinion, Professor Nchare is truly inconsistent. Very often, aspects of his lectures are statistically inaccurate. In order to succeed in this course, I had to look elsewhere for concrete teaching. He is very reluctant to help his students at all, claiming that he doesn't want to give away the answer, thus, hindering academic growth.

He's a nice guy, but not really suited for teaching. His lectures are boring and wildly difficult to focus on. He also always dodges questions and his heavy accent makes things to understand at times. He likes to go off on irrelevant tangents on calculus. Your grade is mostly determined by the midterms and a final, but the exams are very easy.
Three Exams plus homework determines your grade. Lectures are boring and generally unhelpful, but his exams are very regular. Easy to get a good grade.
Interesting lectures.
solid but not the best
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: was a first time professor as a graduate student. has a good understanding of the information but took the class way too seriously considering it was just a 2000 level elective. no participation grade, everything is graded on correctness. no buffer for you grade so the tests may screw you over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you take his class you will KNOW circuits. However, that is because everything is so much more difficult than the other sections. Cool guy, big fan of his.
Great foundational class for engineers. Difficult compared to all other offerings. Cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would highly recommend against the attending classes, since the professor just read off slides he makes it seem like certain things are correlated when they aren't and vice versa. Very confusing to listen to. Also doesn't really seem to understand the things he's talking about himself, yet expects us too
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kang is a fantastic professor. I learned a ton about circuits and feel like the class was well worth the effort. He gives you everything you need to succeed in the course, and I would recommend asking questions if anything is unclear. Work hard, and you will enjoy the semester!
Random NPC. He does not belong here
Every lecture has homework, the exams are extremely difficult to finish all questions. You have to learn everything on your own.

If you have the option between Kang and Holman, take Holman. However if you have the option between Kang and someone else, take Kang. He's a great guy, always loves to help students if you approach him after class or in office hours. Truly just a wonderful professor to form a relationship with. Highly recommend his class.

Love Kang, a lot of reviews say he's an awesome guy but bad lecturer. He must have read some of these ratings cause he was a great lecturer for me, wanted to get to know the people who came to talk to him. Maybe Holman is the better lecturer -  but exams + hw are the same so take Kang - makes you excited to learn circuits.

I found Dr. Kang to be a wonderful professor. His presentations were great, he provided explanations on how to do the hw due the next class, and was overall a really nice man. Kang is not a bad choice, do not let his ratings scare you away from him. I went to every class and ended up with my ideal grade, you got this!
If you are comparing Prof. Kang to Prof. Holman, Prof. Holman is the better teacher but Prof. Kang is the better guy.

While Kang is a very bad lecturer and you have to watch Holman's videos to learn the content, one pro of this class is that the exams are relatively more straightforward than Holman's. Kang is a nice guy but definitely avoid this class if you can.

This was one of the worst professors I've taken at this school. The content on the final exam was very unclear and misleading, not ideal for something worth a third of your grade. The TAs for this semester were terrible, one of them was an international and gave zero partial credit. If you have the chance, avoid Kang.

He reads word by word off lecture slides and rarely answers questions. However, the lecture slides are not bad so you will learn if you pay attention or read them yourself. Exam and homework are normal difficulty but he dropped 2 out of the 4 exams which made the class absolutely free.
Poor lecturer which is amplified with a thick accent, soft voice, and mask. You have to teach yourself and the exams are a grind. On the bright side, he is very kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Kang demonstrated absolutely no interest in the course or the students. Every class he read directly off the PowerPoints, contributing no new or helpful information. He is generally not friendly and does not like to answer questions. His English skills are extremely poor. This course was essentially a self-study

Had Prof Kang for circuits online, his lectures were just monotonally reading off the slides. You mainly have to teach yourself, but the posted material is very in depth and useful. Doesn't accept late homework, but dropped a test and you could use the final to replace another lower test grade.

Prof Kang really cares about his students. He gives u every chance to improve your grade in the tests, and if the tests aren't fair and the whole class agrees, he'll listen. Sets up lots of help sessions and will walk thru hw with u if needed Sadly, he's not great at teaching, at least online. Reads off slides, u often gotta teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's not a good lecturer, but he is kind. He read straight from the lecture slides, didn't really answer student questions, and had a lot of Zoom difficulties. His tests were not bad at all, he dropped our lowest test grade, and he offered several review sessions before each exam, so he definitely tries his best to help students however he can.
Loved Professor Poo. Pretty easy going class, just do your work. Also don't make fun of his name.
He is very good professor and very kindly to all class..His exams are very related with his old exams, so you are not getting any problem with his class..
Awesome professor, awesome person.
He's fairly funny, and teaches the course well, but sometimes he throws you a curve ball on the tests and you strike out hard core.  The lab sucks donkey balls.

Very nice person, lectures are hard to understand because talks softly into the board with a pretty heavy accent. His tests are very fair, but the homework assigned is in left field as far as how well it applies to what is being learned and to what will be on the tests. Help sessions for tests are good, he does old exams, which are close to new one

This guy will talk for hours on the most random topics, often deviating from course content on his own will. Gives sparse feedback and thinks he is always right. Overall, weird guy, doesn't teach very well, and can grade harshly purely based on whether he likes you or not.

One of the nicest professor you will ever have cares so much about his students and will go the extra mile for you. Also if a fantastic lecture who loves group discussion so expect to have to do the readings.

He's really passionate about students and class material. Mandatory attendance and office hours, but he is committed to your learning and enjoyment. I loved loved the course, participation goes a really long way with him, and he is much more chill than the syllabus makes him out to be. Interactive class with games and food as well.

Professor Kelner is an amazing professor who is clearly very passionate. He has great insight about the Jewish American experience. If you are engaged and willing to learn, you will takeaway a lot from him and this course. Participation matters, and go to office hours for any help.
One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. He truly cares about his students and the material he is teaching. Cannot recommend him enough.

You could tell that he was clearly passionate about the subject. There were short assignment/module work to complete before every class, which was quite heavy on the workload compared to other writing seminars. Some of the writing assignments required draft meetings with him, but to obtain good grade, writing studio sessions are recommended.

Professor Kelner is an amazing teacher and an awesome person as well. I went into the course not knowing that much about Jewish Diaspora however, I came out with an entirely new understanding. He will work and meet with you on your papers and gives amazing feedback. A perfect AXLE class or if you just want to know more about Jewish history!!

Prof. Kelner is an all-around great guy. I wasn't too fascinated by the subject material, but his passion for it clearly shows. If you want an easy writing seminar with a really nice professor, take his class.

Amazing, caring, compassionate professor. I was in his writing seminar on the Soviet Jewry movement, and it was obvious how passionate he was about the subject. He put so much effort into making sure we felt welcome, going the extra mile especially during COVID. He held draft review meetings in person, and he was very understanding and kind.

Prof Kelner is an awesome guy. This class is more of a creative writing class than a history class, but he is generally an easy grader. The readings are not needed for the writing assignments (stopped doing them after 3 weeks). Take home midterm and easy final. I'm not Jewish but still found the class to be very interesting!

Professor Kelner is a real cool guy. He brings a lot of energy to class and it's contagious. He knows a lot about research methods and integrates his own research into the class which is pretty interesting. Available for office hours. He loves participation, its a MUST. Do the homeworks & readings, the final is cumulative. Strict attendance policy

Professor Kelner is very passionate about the subject matter, and that rubs off on his students. His office is always open for help with papers, and oftentimes going there turns into an hourlong conversation with him about life. The reading is very optional, and he is a lenient paper grader.

Really helpful!!! Once I went to his office hours and could not find him. I sent him an e-mail. Although he was at New York and my paper was due the next day, he asked for my cell number, called me in the afternoon and discussed the subject matter! One of the best and interesting professors I ever had!

he's passionate about his work and very fair. if you are engaged, the class is very interesting and will give you many new perspectives. overall, he's a nice and knowledgeable individual who tries to make class fun
You won't find a more knowledgeable or considerate professor in the entire Jewish Studies department.

This is a really awesome class taught by an even better professor.  I have had the pleasure of having Prof. Kelner in 2 other classes, and I must say that taking SOC101 with him my freshman year made me become a SOC major.  He's passionate, engaging and incredibly fair.  TAKE THIS CLASS!

Good teacher, those it isnt very fun material you learn alot. Get to actually do a research project with your class. Not a lot of work, only the final and a couple easy writing assignments. Recommended
Really passionate about his class. Not extremely fascinating material but you will learn a lot with his teaching methods. Recommended

He is so enthusiastic about what he teaches and very engaging. He makes it such a pleasure to learn and his delight in what he does is evident. He definitely challenges you, but you are certainly rewarded in what you take away from the course.
Good prof, interesting class.  Do the readings.

Not what I expected. We read excerpts from books but we never get to read/discuss enough of it to retain information and interest. We only have 2 papers and a final but I dont believe I've been able to retain any of the information I have learned this semester. NOT a memorable class

Very interesting professor! If possible don't take this at 8am, even though attendance is not mandatory, the quizzes test on material covered in lecture. Lot of reading, but its interesting and if you do the work its an easy A.
Prof. Kelner is absolutley amazing. His enthusiasm for the subject is Contagious. Easy class if you do your part.

Kelner is a great professor!!! Extremely engaging, and tries to include the students in class. Uses discussion instead of lectures, which makes the class a lot more interesting. Very helpful... go to his office hours with questions! He is flexible and a very fair grader. Take this class!

Soc. 101 is an interesting class and Professor Kelner is a very good professor. He lectures well and tries to involve the students in class discussion. He's also very fair. Just do the readings, come to class, and you'll get a very good grade. I highly recommend this class and Professor Kelner.

Very nice, engaging, interesting teacher. Class can be somewhat uncomfortable at times because the students are abashed by his enthusiasm, no one answers his questions, etc. Very fair grader and an easy A with any amount of motivation and a class time other than early in the morning. Really a worthwhile professor to take a class from.
You'll love him!  Friendly guy, very interested in subject matter which rubs off on the students. Very fair.

Professor Carroll is super serious, but willing to help and work through things with her students. Her grading is slightly hard, but she gives concrete, quantitative feedback to improve the next time. Her Introduction to National Security class had great lectures, bringing in experts and high-level executives from top fields.

20 years embarrassingly behind on her knowledge of the Middle East. Course is graded by few and postures surrounding Middle Easy knowledge but unable to answer basic questions about special forces, civilian casualties, and military malpractice. Wish more students would question her obvious bias given she's a translator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Carroll genuinely has no idea what idea what's going on in the Middle-East. She ignores every historical event of Christian prosecution. When someone mentioned the Assyrian genocide after she claimed the Ottoman Empire was kind to all religious groups, she said “oh yea, besides that.” Difficult class already but she makes it worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had her for CORE1010, and she was great. She follows the curriculum, but she pushes deadlines and lightens the reading load when it is excessive. She lets us out early and is a very fair grader for assignments and papers. She doesn't expect more than the bare minimum, so if you show up and participate every once and a while, you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This course was mainly graded on four papers. However, the prompt for all of those papers was essentially "write about something and keep it around 1000 words." The open-endedness of the essays allows students to write about topics that genuinely interest them and succeed as a result. Also made me realize how great Chicago footnotes are
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: KBC knows more about the Middle East than anyone. Her lectures, filled with personal stories, were engaging. However, this class was hard. There is an insane amount of reading, exams, and a very long paper. The class is not the most structured. You won't understand a thing from her slides if you miss class. She's not an overly picky grader, though.

This class is what convinced me to add a psci minor as a STEM major- what was expected from you throughout the course was very clear, and Prof Carroll's lectures were interesting. Pop quizzes on important general concepts of readings (no specific details, and two are dropped), 4 papers, and one group project. Overall great class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is super knowledgeable, passionate, and caring, but I found this class to be quite difficult. The entire grade is comprised of one 20-page paper and two tests, but she is very transparent about this on the syllabus. Attendance isn't required, but it's important to show up, go to office hours, and commit yourself to the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her course Introduction to Comparative Politics course in the fall of 2023. She is not only an amazing professor with an interesting background, who gives good feedback, and who encourages participation. She has also helped me solidify my career plans, and gave me some steps on how to accomplish these things. Thank you so much!

Very interesting class with a lot of great guest lectures, which keeps it fresh. Attendance is important, but exams aren't too hard. Carroll is a great professor to get to know, you can tell that she values connecting with her students. Can't wait to take more classes with her.

Dr. Carroll is great and it's clear she wants to interact with her students. This is a class you have to show up to (40% of grade is attendance). But also ask her for feedback and take. She will be very honest with you during office hours and following her recommendations will get you a good grade! Tests are graded solely by TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: liked Carroll, but her feedback on papers could be unclear. TA and Carroll could give contradictory feedback, which made it difficult to improve. Paper topics could be on anything political, which was both nice and difficult. If you want to skip, do so early in the semester; she stacks up on quizzes and attendance to give out near the end

Super caring professor, and is very knowledgable. If you actually pay attention to her lectures, you will realize she covers so much material, but breaks it down in an efficient way. One of the best in the poli sci dept, and would recommend even if you aren't a poli sci major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Carroll is amazing, her lectures (although all over the place) are very interesting and offer a great start to comparative politics, you get to learn a lot about different countries. Quizzes are easy if you even skim the readings. There are pop quizzes but 2 are dropped. Attendance matters a lot and is taken randomly, can miss 3 classes.

Prof Carroll is the nicest, most caring prof. Lectures can be hard to follow (not great organization), but content is interesting, and no exams (just 1 paper/month), group proj. & pop quizzes from pre-readings. Skim reading, but be ready for pop quizzes. Best advice: USE OFFICE HOURS for feedback. Class is SO enjoyable once you get to know her.
boring lectures but overall very chill class, 4 papers that were low stakes and interesting to write, simple group project, pop quizzes & attendance but some are dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: boring lectures that don't even pertain to what you're graded on; you're graded on a few pop quizzes, a few attendances taken at random points, one paper per month of the semester, and absolutely no exams; very easy to get an A

Carroll is so knowledgeable and a great lecturer. The whole class was a 3-4 page paper on a reading per month, but random attendance and quizzes on readings which are rough (two get dropped). As long as you show up to class and put in effort for papers you can get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Carroll was really chill this semester for us. No midterms-- just pop quizzes, occasional attendance, and some short writing assignments. As long as you ask her for feedback on your essays and take her advice, writing assignments are super easy. She can be disorganized, but a lot of her topics are super interesting. Would recommend fs.

Prof Carroll is a really engaging lecturer and she's super funny. She says at the beginning of the course that if you show up you'll do well, which is 100% true. Her slides are helpful but she does add more during her lectures so I recommend showing up to class even though attendance is not counted.

Carroll is good lecturer; funny and passionate about subject. Classes are only lectures; can be boring on Tu/Th. Main issue is unclear grading criteria. Papers and short answers were arbitrarily nitpicked. If you take her class, ALWAYS ask her for advice on a rough draft and ALWAYS make an effort to follow that advice. It will help noticeably.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Carroll is incredibly disorganized and her ability to teach is not good. She is more of a high school teacher than she is a college professor at a high caliber school like Vanderbilt. She grades inconsistently and is unclear in her expectations for getting a good grade on exams. Overall, she is a nice lady but quite a poor performing prof

Dr. Carroll is overall a great lady, she feels like a mom. She will push you to do your best but is also always willing to help. That being said, she is also a little intimidating and her lectures are VERY disorganized. The lectures being disorganized wasn't a big deal for this course, but it may be if you're in a test-heavy class with her.

Carroll's connections & experience lend well to her class. We had cool guest speakers come in, and she really cares. Easy grader. Some lectures were dry, but I learned a lot. Midterm/final formatted where she sent a question after each class and you could work on them gradually. Wish more things contributed to our grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She gives weekly readings, but nothing in this class is required honestly. Your whole grade is based on a midterm and final, easy to do well on and a big group project. She's really nice and interesting to talk to. Has a lot of experience and knowledge -- I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Had her for U.S. Military and it was a really cool class. She brought in really interesting guest speakers and shared personal experiences. Small introductory assignment, big group assignment (writing a textbook chapter), and a midterm and final where she released one question at the end of each class and you could work gradually.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is comprised of the midterm, final, and a group research paper that you write with two partners. Professor Carroll gives good feedback on assignments. Lots of guest speakers in class. 92% minimum is nice for an A considering other Vanderbilt professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Alright, basically if you wanted to be treated like a toddler and literally called "children" or "kids" as a college student fully funding your own degree, then take her- she's great at devaluing anything you do. Additionally, near every lecture was a guest lecture, so why even pay her as a university...? Some of the guests did not even have slides

Professor Carroll makes class so enjoyable. It is the only class I've taken at Vandy where I can genuinely say I was excited to go to class everyday - she has so many stories about her time in the Middle East that make lectures enjoyable. Tests are TOUGH though, and you will have to rely on your lecture notes to study for it. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really mixed feelings about Prof Carroll. She is incredibly knowledgeable and interesting, but her teaching/testing style involves a lot of random details w/ no clear order and you MUST go to class (& the Freedom House report was unclear & awful). Still, she was generous with grading, & I learned SO much--would recommend the class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Highly recommended if you want to learn about the Middle East.

Really enjoyed this Middle East Politics class. 2 exams, freedom house report and final. Exams are short answer and essay, pretty straightforward if you go to class and you can definitely get by without doing the readings. Really interesting survey of different countries' history and current politics. Dry humor and fun stories. A must-take!

Carroll is a great lecturer with an infectious passion for the Middle East. Unfortunately, she can be dismissive if you try to go to office hours. Lots of material to study for the test, and she throws out names and terms quickly without putting them on the powerpoint. Get ready to write fast! No laptops allowed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teaching style and even worse testing style. Powerpoints contain no real notes, so be very careful to pay attention to what she says--only problem is, what she teaches is not logically order, uses a lot of unfamiliar Middle Eastern terms exclusively verbally, tests you on 4 random terms out of 100s of possible ones (terms can be Anything)

Great class on the US Military. Variety of topics, discussion of current events, awesome guest speakers. Dr. Carroll is just a cool human, especially knowledgable on Middle East politics and contributes a unique perspective from her time in Iraq. Whole class was pretty chill, focused on strengthening civil-military relations in gov't and society.

Not an easy A and assigns an insane amount of reading (300+ pages a week and it's not a novel). But she's reasonable with grades and clearly knows what she's talking about. I truly learned a lot. She says a lot of things that are on the text during lecture, so definitely go.

Prof. Carroll is hands one of the best polisci professors at Vandy. She has been to the places she teaches about and has a lot of good stories. She doesn't put up with the BS, and she appreciates when you contribute to class and put forth an effort

Dr. Carroll taught this class with much more flexibility than the other classes I have taken with her. She was flexible on due dates and readings, which made for a fun class. While she may seem cold and harsh, she does care about the students who put forth the effort. All around, would recommend as a prof but maybe not as a friend.

Prof Carroll is the best professor I have ever had. Her class has been really challenging, but I have never learned so much in one course. She doesn't put up with any B.S., but she really cares about her students. Go to office hours, talk in class, and do the readings!

Prof Carroll is absolutely brilliant and is hands down the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. I've taken two classes with her and loved both of them. I would take a class by her if it were on paint drying because she makes literally everything interesting. She's an incredible lecturer-- she exudes information. Take notes on every word she says.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: War in Iraq is the best class I've taken at Vanderbilt thus far. Professor Carroll is an amazing lecturer and she's very knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches. She's very accessible outside of class and cares about her students' success. The class is very easy IF you show up to lecture and take good notes- exams are simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Middle East Politics and War in Iraq were the two best classes I took at Vanderbilt. Carroll is one of those professors who can lecture for the whole class every class and you never get bored. Make sure to take good notes

Everyone kept telling me Professor Carroll was intimidating, but I didn't think this was the case at all. I enjoyed discussing the course material with her. She seems to know a lot about certain aspects of the course, but seemed a little flustered in terms of structure and grading. TA graded the assignments.

Katherine Carroll is my idol. She's brilliant, and she is an EXPERT in her field. She can take some getting used to--you're never sure how she feels about you and can seem mean at first--but if you work hard, she values that and will always help you in your endeavors. Her classes are excellent, and you will learn so much. Take all of her classes.

Professor Carroll demands alot from her students. You will have to work very hard throughout the semester.
