However, she is an extremely fair grader and you will learn more about the middle east than you ever expected. She is one of the best professors at sending out emails and truly cares about students despite her seemingly cold exterior.

Carroll is sort of cold at first, but she warms up as the semester goes on. She really is amazing individual and a true expert in her field. There is quite a bit of reading but as long as you read the articles and go to class the test are not too bad.

Carroll was very forthright with her disinterest in the comfort of her students from the beginning. It was difficult to get help from her, but the TA was great so that was not quite an issue. Her class is interesting, but the reading is long and boring.  Also, if you take this class, expect many references to the Middle East for examples.
A wonderful perspective on current issues
Learned a lot from her class. She is very intimidating at first and you definitely have to work for a good grade, but it's a very interesting class and worth sticking with it.

Many people say that Katherine Carroll is intimidating. However, as one of her public policy advisees, I think this is completely false. She is one of the most helpful professors on campus. Her office is always open and she is very proactive with sending emails. Additionally, she is the most FAIR grader i've had at Vandy.

Yes, there is reading but I didn't find it too bad, 1 article for each class. Yes, you have to pay attention because the PowerPoints don't have all the info, but lectures are interesting. I never found her to be condescending to people's ideas questions, she often encouraged students to share their thoughts in class! A's are DEFINITELY attainable.

Carroll is far and away the WORST teacher I've had at Vanderbilt. I was interested in pursuing a CP specialization when I enrolled, and she turned me off to the idea so much that I am considering a new major. Grading is arbitrary, she is unhelpful, even rude in office hours, and the TA was pretentious & unqualified. Do. Not. Take. This. Class.

Lets you know when she doesn't like you and is not helpful in office hours. She covers many topics in class on the surface and expects you to know in-depth for the test. She's very haughty and will call you out if she thinks your question is stupid. There is a lot of reading and it's difficult if you're not well-versed in political science writing.

Professor Carroll is easily the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt.  She has an unbelievable amount of knowledge, and is very clear in how she presents it.  Tests are pretty easy if you keep up with the coursework, and definitely attend class: it is interesting and you get many answers to exams from class time.  Definitely take this class!

Prof. Carroll is a great lady with lots of experience/knowledge. But the coursework is dense, so you really need to do your part to keep pace. Readings are crucial - don't get behind or else chance doing poorly on exams.

This was the most interesting PSCI class I've taken.  Prof Carroll is absolutely brilliant, and makes the material fascinating.  Her exams can be challenging, and you do need to do the readings, but with a good effort you can certainly make a solid grade.  She definitely has one of the coldest personalities I've ever encountered, however.

Fantastic professor! She has a ton of experience and knows what she is talking about. Her lectures and interesting and relevant. You will learn so much. If you do the reading and go to class the tests will be pretty easy. There is one paper, but the topic is your choice. I loved her class.

Definitely snobbish, which I personally believe is her way of showing tough love, but an undeniably brilliant woman and excellent educator. If you are not working hard she will push you until you do. She grades fairly.

She is not easy. You will work quite hard in this class. However, she is beyond fascinating and is brilliant. I feel like I have learned more in this class than in any other class and I am thrilled that I took it, even though I might not get an A. One note of caution: there is a long and important term paper in this class, but topics are open

Take her courses if you want to learn a ton of information from a professor who knows what she's teaching. Avoid if what you care about most is an easy A. Lots and lots of reading but the readings and lectures are all fascinating.  Professor Carroll can be intimidating because she's so knowledgeable but is also eager to help and answer questions.

I got placed in her class not by choice, she is awful! every class she has a powerpoint, but they only have pictures so you really have to listen and write down EVERYTHING. There are 2 articles a night that are long and tedious that are on the test so you MUST read everything. I asked for help and she wouldnt,she told me to ask the kids in my class

Brilliant yet mildly condescending, which I guess she's earned: incredible experience in the field, she's dynamite when she talks about it. V. helpful if you approach her. (On that note, if you're snooping about a test, forget it!!) Smart, intimidating. Good teacher but won't make it easy for you. Reading is rough, don't fall behind!

This website fooled me into taking her class. I found her to be hypocritical (stresses that you must be there on test days...only to change the test days and not be there herself). Her tests are 5 short answer (1-2 paragraphs) each question is worth 20 points. The subject material wasn't too hard, the reading was arduous but manageable.
Too much reading, otherwise a good class.
Stone cold fox

More reading than is humanly possible.  If you at least try and keep up with it and come to class you'll be fine.  Not to bad to get a B in, to get an A you really have to work hard.  She's really knowledgeable on the subject and you will definitely learn a ton.

Class is hard with lots of reading, but you'll learn a lot.  She expects you to do the reading and know what you're talking about, because she DEFINITELY does.  Don't ****, work hard, you'll get a B+ or A-.  Slack off or don't come to class, expect a C or D.

Prof. Rilling is THE goat. I was really behind in the class because I didn't have the background knowledge most of my peers did from hs and as a required class for my major I needed to take it. Prof. Rilling has helped me catch up so much and taught me so many tricks to get better at music. He cares so much about all of his students and music. GOAT

Truly one of the best teachers I've ever had in my life. Prof. Rilling is incredibly passionate for what he does and cares a lot for his students. I also felt he makes music theory so clear and easy to learn for people like me with little to no formal music education background. Highly recommend to any incoming freshman!
literally the best

Nothing I can say can fully describe how incredible Professor Rilling is. Coming in, I had little to no experience with formal music theory education. This man not only does it efficiently (pacing of class time), but he also makes all the information well packaged and distilled. Consistently felt class ended short because of his engaging teaching!
See comments below. Kevin Rilling is outstanding, both as a theory professor and person.

Prof. Rilling is one of the easier aural skills professors. His class consists of a few performance assignments (which you can resubmit for a higher grade) and some quizzes (which he prepares you for well). If you put in some effort, this class should be easy A. Plus, his cat, Eevee, is the cutest little thing!
I have not one negative thing to say about this incredible professor.
Great professor for theory, very enthusiastic during lecture and clear when teaching concepts. Not too much homework, and Professor Rilling is very clear about what will be tested on the quizzes.
Dr. Rilling is AMAZING, take his classes! Theory 2 can be tough, but don't hesitate to ask for help, he's very caring and supportive, and wants the best for you!
awesome guy

i've absolutely loved having rilling for aural skills this semester, you can tell that he really wants all his students to succeed, no matter how little or how much prior knowledge they're coming in with. one of my favorite professors i've had here so far.

Prof. Rilling is one of the most talented teachers I have ever had. I never even had to study for this class- not because it was overly easy, but because the organization of the class ensures that you leave each lecture completely understanding the material. He is also super understanding of  circumstances you might have out of class.

Prof. Rilling is everything you dream of when it comes to music theory professors. He's just a natural teacher that delivers silk-smooth lectures at a comfortable pace, and is always there to support his students whether it's about class material or other stuff. Super relatable partly because he was a recent Blair graduate himself. Take him!
amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Rilling is one of the best professors I've had at vandy. Gives straightforward assignments and teaches in a clear and concise manner that is very easy to follow. Also so compassionate and understanding of his students needs, and will never hesitate to accommodate you if you are going through any sort of rough patch. I would marry this man.

Professor Rilling was one of the best professors I have ever had. He is genuinely caring and very knowledgable on music theory. 2-3 homework assignments a week for class, but all really relevant to the course material and fair to the lectures. Provides really great help in office hours. I honestly can't say enough nice things about his courses.

So so amazing and makes theory actually understandable for people who struggle in the subject. He genuinely wants you to learn and understand and will break it down for you if you need. He is the only reason I actually like and understand music theory so definitely take Prof. Rilling, he is a king.

Professor Rilling is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He is extremely kind and always goes over things in class until everyone understands. He is very organized and assigns the perfect amount of work!

Prof. Rilling is amazing!!! He was my favorite teacher this semester. His lectures and expectations are very clear. He really cares about his students and will help you outside of class. If you have the chance, take Rilling!

Professor Rilling is easily my favorite professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He is very enthusiastic about what he is teaching and has the best energy. Music Theory is stereotypically a difficult/dreaded class, but Rilling makes it very understandable and I genuinely look forward to going to class.

Professor Rilling is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt University. He makes something as difficult as theory easy to understand and genuinely cares about his students and how they are understanding the material. He is easy to access outside of class and wants you to succeed. 10/10 would recommend. He is the best!
He is THE BEST theory teacher.

RIlling is the goat. I never took theory before taking the class but he is very straightforward and clear in his teaching that it makes it very easy to follow. I did not know I would be enjoying music theory as much!

Honestly Professor Rilling is the best professor Ive taken at Vanderbilt. I had no music theory background before taking his class, but he was really easy to follow. He gives really good feedback on the homework and tests as well. There is homework due basically every class, but thats standard for music theory here and it is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Probably my favorite professor and class I've ever taken. Dr. Leach is absolutely amazing. He is very receptive to feedback; he seems like he genuinely cares and wants to hear from his students. I learned a lot from this class, and the topics felt really interesting. Projects took a bit of time, though.

Dr. Leach is highly knowledgeable in web programming and maintains an engaging, student-centered classroom environment. He is exceptionally patient and attentive to student feedback, always encouraging real-time discussions. Whether you have questions during the lecture or need to stay late for a quick chat, he is always approachable and helpful.

Dr. Leach is very passionate about the class, very nice, and very knowledgeable. We read a research paper before every class, then recap and re-explain the paper in class, often making lectures repetitive and disincentivizing the readings. The papers are very interesting and informative, and Leach provides advanced cybersecurity info when asked.

PAs tough but will be the most rewarding assignments during Vanderbilt CS. The course itself is enough info to start with intro web security/compiler roles. I'm really lazy with school and needed this class just for graduation credit but ended up loving it the most during my time @ vandy. Exams are easy, start assignments early and ask questions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As others have said, 3276 is tough, but you'll learn more than in almost any other CS course, and you'll have a working compiler by the end of it. Leach has also made efforts to make the course easier, which includes late days and a lot of leniency. When half the class didn't even try PA4 by the deadline, he extended the due date. Take the course!

It's a good course and you'll learn a lot but very difficult. Assignments take a long time and you can only submit to the autograder 5 times per day. Exams are hard but have extra credit. Attendance is counted. Each class consists of a lecture + slide deck + occasional drawings on the whiteboard. Leach is nice, but can be a little uppity sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It would have been better if the exams are easier and the programming assignments are more difficult (use more difficult and faster language than Python but easier language than C/C++ like Java). For instance, the extra credit questions could be easier than the current ones. Currently, it is not easy to get full scores in extra credit questions.

This is one of the best CS classes I've taken here. It's quite hard, mostly due to the lack of prerequisite knowledge from other CS classes -- but Dr. Leach manages it pretty well! Overall, I learned a lot (far more than I could say about any other CS course here), the homework assignments were very interesting, and the exams were manageable.

The professor was enthusiastic and good at teaching, and the course material was also interesting. However, if you do not have experience with LARGE scale group projects, be prepared to commit a lot of time or lose points (or both). It was a difficult class but also a good learning experience. (harder than the current 3251 and way harder than 3270)

Professor Leach is amazing, and I thoroughly enjoyed Topics of Cybersecurity. I'm sure that any class you take with him will be awesome. He's a great professor and lecture is always enjoyable. His expectations are extremely clear and if you have any issues just communicate with him and you will be fine. Take his classes if you have a chance.
Great professor! I had him for two courses freshman year. Very willing to get to know students and very knowledgeable!
very unclear grading and tough lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes and professors I've had. Was genuinely interested in the subject before the class but his boring lectures and cold calling on made the class miserable. Graded papers harshly with little feedback. Scolded students for leaving to use the restroom. Do NOT recommend, I lost all the passion I had for Impressionism art

Loved this class, was truly enlightening! Prof Murphy is famous in his field and since I love architecture, was excited to take his class. Not sure what reviewer below expected but Art History exams always have slide Id's! Was a great semester experience.

Professor Murphy is without a doubt, the worst teacher I have had throughout my career as a student. Worst of all, the two exams that make up 60% of the final grade require memorization of buildings names, their architects, and details simply by seeing a picture of them. I learned nothing, and the course can be boiled down to a memorization game.

Western Arch is a solid choice-heavy amount of textbook reading, but he only grades based on the overlap between the book and class, so there's no point in reading. He does take graded attendance. The few papers and 2 tests (non cumulative) were pretty easy if you paid any attention. The one flaw is that you can't use your computer for notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nice guy and interesting class. The workload and grading is pretty standard for art history classes.

I took this class because I had heard that it was an interesting but relatively easy class.  I took more notes for this class than any pre-med class I've taken.  His lectures are difficult to follow (not helped by his dry and boring voice) and he moves from slide to slide before you finish writing and he grades his examinations very strictly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Interesting class, really nice guy. Assignments aren't to hard and he is not a tough grader. Attendance and participation are necessary.

Professor Murphy is very knowledgeable and passionate about his subject. His lectures are clear and logical, and he's quite helpful if you go to office hours. There is a bit of writing, but it isn't bad because the subject matter is very interesting.

Dr. Khabibulina is so kind and caring, and I would recommend this class to anyone who still needs an AXLE credit. As long as you do the readings and come to class, you'll be fine. There are daily quizzes, but if you read the fairy tales you will get all the questions.

This is for RUSS 1874, Fairy Tales. Everything is great about the class, minus the reality that you will be doing (easy) reading-check quizzes at the beginning of each class for the majority of the semester. It is almost as if the hardest part of the class is a mental toughness test when the class is at 8AM. Entertaining class!

Professor Khabibulina is the best if you're nervous about taking Russian! She is patient, a VERY easy grader, and believes in second chances. Attendance matters if you actually want to learn the language since every class covers a good amount of content. There is usually nightly homework but it shouldn't take you more than 15-30 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's one of the kindest professors at Vanderbilt. She explains concepts well and provides us with vocabulary that we need to know and example questions/sentences. In class we have conversations with each other using new vocab and grammar. Tests are tough but fair, and HW is not bad! She's also hilarious and shows us cute pics of her cat

She was so wonderful to have and helped me fall in love with Russian. She was always so caring and I have enrolled to take her again. If you're intimidated to start Russian, absolutely take her class! She's so sweet and understanding.

I had so much going on when I took this class and couldn't read the assigned readings.  Classes were very flexible. She often pushed the dates back on papers if we seemed too overwhelmed. Overall I love this lady. The best professor ever. Our final was writing our fairytale, which was SOOOO fun. 10/10 would recommend.
Very good, getting a good grade is easy but you learn a lot in the class.

Professor Khabibulina was so kind and understanding throughout the whole course. The class consisted of originally 4 papers and extensions were easy to obtain. Class discussions were always fun and interesting. I highly recommend her class!!

I love Professor Khabibulina. I've taken Russian with her for three semesters straight and would take a fourth if I were not leaving. She is the best language teacher I've ever had, not only because she is extremely personable and understanding, but also because the format of the class is engaging and immersive. I highly recommend her classes.

Professor Khabibulia is one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. You learn so much without even realizing it. The class consists of many presentations, short readings, nightly homework, and class discussion and collaboration. She truly cares about students and cares that students learn. Easy A if you put in the work and participate.

The class is very easy to do and she goes relatively easy on the students. However, her grading for the final project was quite unclear. She tries to help by assigning her grad students to help with projects, but our grad student and other faculty said that we were perfect for our project yet we ended up having a B- on the project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: K. Pace is so nice and caring. She is really experienced and passionate about her work. Her class is hard b/c there is only weekly reflections and a course project that's 50% of your final grade and not graded easily. While the project is difficult, she is extremely accessable, knowledgable, and wants her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get her out of here.
cold-hearted beach

K-Pace was great with lectures and engaging with students. Required readings were more optional than required. But, the final presentation, bibliography, and report are collectively 40% of the grade, but there is no feedback during course, so hard to know if you met her standards. You need to do very well on that to keep the A.

Famous American Trials was pretty easy-- If you do well with blue book exams and remembering major concepts from lectures/points and authors from readings, you will do well. She doesn't take attendance, but she doesn't post lectures online so you definitely need to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer assigned a lot of course readings, but is understanding. Doesn't personally grade, which can get tricky when trying to provide corrective feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Way more work than the other capstone seminar classes. Caring, but will completely change your topic if it doesn't align with her expectations. Spent most of my senior year worrying/stressing about this class, don't take if you want to enjoy it.

Professor Welch is a gem of a professor who goes above and beyond for her students. She knows what a good historian looks like and will give it her all to help her students get there. You should only be in this class if you love history. Pick a topic you're interested in and it'll be a great experience.

The last review is mid. Welch's lectures were always entertaining, and if you are someone who can handle your grade being dependent on blue book exams, this class is for you. Obviously, this class is not about the law of trials...because it's a history class...not a law class; so don't go in expecting you are going to learn legal principles.

Her lectures rarely even mentioned the trials we were tested on but rather basic contextual information we have all learned countless times in American history courses. Tests focus on themes rather than the development of law. Your grade completely depends on your ta. Lectures weren't mandatory, discussion is. You can get by with skimming reading.

I really admire Dr. Welch. She's super understanding of student wellbeing and her lectures are some of the most informative ones I've ever taken. She's super engaging and gives clear feedback on your writing. Her powerpoints are super informative and if you pay attention you will get a good grade. I have taken two classes with her and hope for more
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Your grade in Famous American Trials will be completely dependent on your TA, and there is no consistency between TA's. Some will be quite harsh and other will be really easy, so it's based on luck what grade you get. Welch lectures on things that are not important for the tests or papers. M/W lectures are non-mandatory but discussion is.

Dr. Welch is an incredible addition to Vanderbilt's history department. She is so knowledgeable in the field and her lectures are extremely engaging. Her tests had 2 essays on each of them, and she gave us the prompts before to prepare. One essay that she graded easily, and 25% participation, but if you do any of the reading it's easy to do well.

Dr. Welch was a great choice for the major capstone; her feedback was really informative and her passion for the subject made the class exciting even when I was exhausted. Definitely recommend her for any of the paper-intensive History classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Welch is awesome. Her lectures are straightforward but super comprehensive at the same time. She cared so much about the subject matter (US Slavery) and she was incredibly knowledgeable. Grading is pretty much 100% dependent on your TA. The TA's were not easy graders at all, but were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very inspiring lectures on history and overall great class atmosphere. Mandatory discussions on Thursdays which is kinda painful because the grading criteria is fairly harsh. I speak 5+ times during each discussion but still failed to impress her. Tons of readings, but no tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Welch is very knowledgeable in the subject and presented it in a way that was easy to understand and fascinating. She also cared a lot about allowing students to share opinions, and connected the history with current events, making class engaging and challenging perspectives. She also graded very easy on all our essays. Best professor I've had.

Dr. Welch is a knowledgeable professor and respected in her field. She is a great professor who cares more about student participation and our own thoughts than memorizing history. No tests, only three papers plus one final paper. Take the class!
SHE IS THE GOAT!!!! Love her and she is genuinely the most kind/loving prof I have ever had. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!

Dr. Klyce is amazing! She is knowledgeable in her subject and is so kind and caring towards her students. Makes an effort to know everyone's names by the first couple of weeks. Her lectures are amazing and she makes an active effort to engage her students. Show up, pay attention in lectures, and you'll easily get an A.

Dr. Klyce is such a kind and understanding professor. It would be difficult to not get an A in this class. You're graded on daily quizzes (easy, if you get ~70% right over semester you get 100%), easy summative tests, and very interesting exploratory assignments. Lectures are very interesting, and she makes very clear what will be on the tests.

She is definitely strict in her own way but is very nice and caring. Her grading can be picky but she explains why she took off points on certain things which usually makes sense. I enjoyed the class but getting an A is something you need to put effort towards with how she grades. She's still a great person and professor tho!

Everyone saying Dr. Marble is difficult contradicts my experience. This was my second class with her, and she's incredibly fair. Her grading is consistent (and pretty easy), and if you semi pay attention, you'll do well. I loved the structure—we spent the whole semester on one research proposal.

Dr. Marble cares about her students and incorporates student's feedback into her teaching style. We had length(ish) writing assignments every two weeks but they were definitely manageable. I am not quite sure why she has such harsh ratings because my experience with her was not that bad, however only con is class material isn't that engaging.

At first, I did not think that I would enjoy this class. Dr. Marble comes off as a little strict at first, and the course seems dry. However, if you participate, the course discussions can be very enjoyable. I did not see myself enjoying this course, but I have thoroughly. Dr. Marble is accommodating and a very fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Marble is always trying to be better and inclusive to everyone. Her course has around 6 quizzes, 6 mini essays and 3 projects. The workload is not bad at all. Her lectures are somewhat boring, she is a very slow talker and can be a picky grader. Overall though, the course was interesting and I'd take another one of her classes.

Dr. Marble was an overall good professor. Her and her TA's grading can be a tad niche and picky, but you'll still be able to get an A. The class has no tests, only 6 quizzes, making the workload super doable. I am not entirely sure why her rating is so low, but I would definitely take another class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Marble took the feedback of the previous reviews saying there was too much workload and completely got rid of exams this semester.  Every assignment we had there was choice in what topic we explored. She's also a knowledgable and engaging lecturer, so this class was fun even for someone who's not super interested in developmental psychology.
The passive aggressive things needs to stop. So immature. Assignments are doable if you don't procrastinate. Also she looks at laptop screens so watch out.

Marble is actually the worst professor I've had in undergrad. She is inaccessible and can be very passive-aggressive. I highly recommend taking this class with any alternate professor. I've taken more than one class with Marble and I can confirm that the class itself is absolutely doable, but having a good experience with her is not.

overall a good professor, biggest downside: that she WILL walk around the room and WATCH YOUR COMPUTER SCREENS to make sure you are on task like ALL the time. overall not a bad class but as someone who gets distracted a lot i needed to always pay attention to where she was in the room, but otherwise she tries to help you do well in the class!

Overall, solid class. The lectures at times were dry but Marble wanted all students to do well in the class. The grading criteria for each assignment was confusing at times, however the final grade calculations that Marble implemented made the class feel a lot less stressful at the end of the semester. Energetic about the topic.

I honestly had no issues with Professor Marble. Her lectures were dry but she tried her best. There were 2 projects, 3 tests, 3 shorter essays, and participation. Marble is kind and a fairly easy grader for most things. She gives study guides and possible free-response questions in advance for the test.

Marble is so very kind, but she expects a lot from her students. Maybe too much. Her tests are hard to complete in time, and she grades very harshly. I honestly never fully understood what I got wrong on tests. Though her class will encourage you to think critically about psychology topics, I do think I learned less in this class than others.

I honestly do not understand why there is so much hate for her. There are 3 exams (everything can be found on the slides and gives you short answer questions beforehand), 3 papers, and 2 projects. It may seem like a lot of work but honestly it is not too bad and pretty easy. Would def recommend her and her class!

She relies heavily on her slides but they are pretty organized and she presents her material clearly. Very nice and responsive in her class and office hours. Her grading is not as harsh as you might expect from reading so many negative comments. Not hard to get an A if you carefully do your work.

Never have I ever enjoyed a class at Vanderbilt less than PSY-PC 2400 with Marble. Take any other class ever and you will be grateful for it. If the Vanderbilt administration continues to allow this woman to teach classes how she currently does in the next couple years, I will worry for the mental health and sanity of the student body. Run!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exam questions are extremely specific, and, even if you're a good writer, she grades the Article Reflection papers harshly. Lectures weren't super boring, and she's definitely an expert in the field. I would only take her class if you are seriously devoted to the subject matter, otherwise, the time necessary to earn an A isn't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The amount of effort needed to get a good grade in this class far exceeds what should be necessary. Even f you go to lecture and type everything on the slides, you still need to do readings, memorize/create answers for short answer prompts, and study those 25 pages of notes to do well on the tests. Not to mention essays/projects. Hard to do good
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Marble reads off of the slides entirely. The class was much more difficult than I thought. And, even if you have an emergency and can't make an exam, you still will not be able to make up a test. The only reason you can end with a decent grade is because of her final grade calculations, but it isn't worth everything the class puts you through.

For an intro level psychology class, the professor was too difficult. She did not give enough time on exams for the amount of content she expected and did not make that clear either. She was also not accommodating as I know someone who had a medical emergency and could not retake a test. Grades on the first exam were on average incredibly low.

when you read the syllabus you might think that the class will be easy because she gives out 3 grading options and drops; however, each exam/project/essay is worth so much of your grade and shes grades very harshly. She does not do curves and roundups and you need a 94 instead of 93 for an A. The lectures are very boring as she just reads slides.

In the review session, if students ask a question that they do not understand, Dr. Marble will not explain their questions and said the question will be tested so I cannot explain it to you. The review session is meaningless and cannot help students to solve any problems that they don't understand.

Hard grader and not helpful outside of class.  Actual class time is boring, and she expects you to answer questions with her opinion only and not your own if it is different from hers.  She takes away participation points for missing class, even your first free 3 unexcused absences.  Mean. Would not take another class with her.

Very dry. Honest grader. Make sure to respect her and you'll get her respect. Do everything that is expected of you and she will support you. Comments in class are a must. No surprises. Attendance is crucial.

She's very good at leading discussion and assigns a short story project (very easy) at the end of the semester where you get to lead a class discussion. Always get to redraft papers (2nd draft worth more than 1st). Class participation is important and possible only if you do the readings. She's a bit dry at times, but I enjoyed the class overall

From someone who hated english going into the class, she was a great professor to have. She was extremely helpful and really helped me refine my writing skills. Most classes were discussions based on the reading because participation plays a big role in grading. Very helpful, would recommend.

The content of the course was very hard for me, but Colin was definitely there to help out when you needed it. He explained the background of concepts and gave many example problems. He was also very relaxed in class and very approachable because he's a grad student. I would definitely want him as a teacher again.

Overall, a pretty good, knowledgeable professor. Obviously an intelligent guy, who often gets off on tangents relating to some interesting and complex topics. Relates well to students. Lenient with deadlines and grading. Though the tests were somewhat difficult, he offered extra credit when he realized a question was unreasonably difficult.

Colin is an absolutely amazing professor. I took calculus before, but even so some of the basic fundamentl theory that they get into at the very beginning can be somewhat difficult. Colin makes the material easy to follow, and is a very fair test maker and grader. He has been known to give back points if he thinks that one question was graded harsh

amazing prof. readings are easy and honestly really interesting (long readings are skim-able as long as you know the essence). class is very discussion based. assignments have lots of writing but its really reasonable, usually just summaries and takeaways.

attendance is mandatory. skim the readings. mainly in class writing assignments and 1-2 outside assignments but they were not difficult. enjoyable even. and as the semester gets busy she cancels a couple. final project was just a long document of writing what we learned and answering questions. very passionate lecturer, stay engaged and participate

Dr. Koleyni is so sweet! Yes, there's an expectation of weekly assignments & participation MATTTERS, but other than that you get to hear a breadth of different perspectives from really great classmates and it's a safe space to really dig deeper into racial and ethnic health disparities that don't get talked about enough in modern healthcare.

This class was a pretty easy A tbh. Prof is very strict about attendance, so you HAVE to go to class otherwise she'll email you with work to make-up for class. Didn't do any readings. Weekly assignments but she cancelled like 3-4 of them as semester got busier. On the heavier writing side but she grades easy, would def recommend for easy MHS core.
Won't attend your performances for general chamber/recitals. Not super engaged with students but you will pass if you show up
amazing amazing amazing
He's the beeeeeest!

Prof. Alexander is great. he has a good sense of humor and makes class interesting. Only a Midterm and a Final that are worth 85% along with 15% attendanceparticipation. If you don't know a lot about current eventshistory tests can be a little tough, but he is a very lenient grader. Definitely would take again.

Prof. Alexander is leaving after this semester, but he is a great guy with a ton of knowledge and experience on int'l politics.  His lectures are engaging and the material is fascinating.  Tests are very difficult and their material seems random.  Attendance is mandatory, and beware: the midterm is 35% of the grade, and the final is 50%.
Very knowledgable man, but tests are nearly impossible.  Some material on exams was never mentioned in class.  Assigns a ton of reading that isn't necessary.  Would not take him again.

Had never taken PoliSci before taking 223 with Alexander on the London Maymester (I'm an engineer).  All of the learning was hands-on and interesting and Alexander is easily the most interesting in knowledgeable professor I have had at Vandy.  Know the PowerPoints and take good notes and you'll do great. 100% recommend this course and professor!
Tough class, but a great political science course. Tests are tough, but study and they are doable. Alexander is an extremely knowledgeable man.

Interesting class. Attendance not mandatory, but w/ his serious grade curving, it'll guarantee you an A. Midterm, final, 15% participation, which can be boosted w/ a 5-6 page extra credit paper on any topic. Great guy, a little dry, but veryyyy knowledgeable able intl politics and law. Pre-law advisor. Pre-law, this is your guy, get to know him.
Lecture-based with only a midterm, final, and participation grades. Lots of Powerpoint, but only take if you have at least some interest in the subject.

This was a special topics class about Globalization and Development - Professor Alexander provided very interesting insights and incorporated events in a way that made even the theories seem relevant. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him! Very knowledgeable and not a very hard grader.
Incorporates interesting discussions of current events in with international politics

Class attendance not mandatory, but tests based largely from lecture and there is a participation grade. Must study to do well, only a midterm, participation, and a final. Good grade is well within reach if one tries. Class is engaging, good lecturer who frequently asks for input from class.

Awful professor. His exams are nothing like he says and have more current events on there than actual information you learn in class. So unless you read about everything going on in the news and are well informed about it, I would steer clear of this professor for this class. Also, the final is worth 50% of your grade which is an awful idea.

Alexander is a very interesting and informative lecturer, and does a great job tying in the concepts with current events.  He also has extensive knowledge and experience with law, international law, and the UN, so if you are pre-law or want to deal with international politics, get to know this guy and meet with him to discuss it.
Had him for international politics. Never used the textbooks, just took notes on lectures and slides. Pretty easy class if you study, show up, and do the extra credit. Also a very interesting man

Whoever said Alexander is easy is lying. I've never struggled through a political science class this much. He's very clear in what he wants, but the questions are always curveballs. He's a nice guy. If you put effort into studying, you'll get a B+/A-, but don't be fooled into thinking that you'll definitely get an A.

Klint's a great guy, but be forewarned that his exams are much more difficult than they used to be, albeit not impossible.  I took IPE (225) with him two years back and secured a relatively easy A, yet in this class I had to fight for a B+.  IDs are easy, but the true/false can be rough.  Interesting material though, despite his boring lectures.

Alexander is a great guy, but his class is boring.  So much reading is assigned, while only a small percentage of that is needed for the tests.  His class is becoming more rigorous I hear, but I think he should assign a more realistic amount of reading and test on it, rather than making his class a measure of how well you can memorize slides.

Alexander is a fantastic professor! He is a great lecturer, always making everything relevant to current events and breaking things up with videos and discussion. His tests are straightforward and he is a very fair grader.

Only "mandatory" to go to class for first half of semester. Really lenient grader with partial credit on tests. As the previous poster indicated there was a "curveball" on the midterm, but overall was one of the most straightforward classes I have taken in my career at Vandy. Study the notes (which he posts online) and you will be fine.

I was not a fan of this class, although I ended up with an A. The class is almost entirely based on two tests, both of which occur in incredibly terrible times (aka midterms week, and finals week) so you can't even fully study. You should read/go to class, too - our essay question on a midterm included a case only mentioned in the book.

Klint is the bomb! His class is pretty interesting and not too hard. As long as you study for the midterm and final, and do the participation paper, it should be a pretty easy A. You don't really have to do much of the reading, and he breaks up classes by showing documentaries every now and then. Definitely one of the best profs I've had!

Prof. Alexander is the man: completely approachable and extremely helpful if you need it.  I will say though that his 2 tests (MT 30%, Final 50%) are definitely NOT a joke, and he does like to put several curveball questions on them.  Lenient grader though, and I did manage to pull an A, but not without hours and hours of studying before each exam.

Alexander is a great professor.  He assigns a good amount of reading, but lets people know that only the Genest reading will be on the test.  He gives out slides to memorize for the exams.  He only had one midterm and one final in addition to a participation paper.  His class is definitely worth it!

This professor was known for being straightforward and easy.  He used to give straightforward tests based on slide shows.  The final (50%) in this class was way too hard.  I learned 100 slides and 5 hours of movies.  I was confident on about half the exam.  It'll probably get curved, but cruel exam.

Alexander's class is the best I've taken at Vanderbilt thus far. I wasn't really interested in politics before his class, but I've decided to add on a double major in PSCI. He's accomplished so much, so you can't help but admire his expertise. The lecture slides are important, but pretty straight forward. The info is current and interesting. Take!
Lectures are painfully boring, but class discussions can get interesting.  A final (50%), midterm (30%), and participation (20%) which includes a paper.  Not a very hard grader.

He is a nice guy who is involved in the everyday effects of what he's teaching. His slides are the most important piece of information, they are your guide to doing well on the exams. His optional paper is great too because it can be hard to comment and maintain a high participation level, easily erased by the paper!

Really knows his stuff and is very knowledgeable (he's a corporate lawyer). There's only a midterm, final and an optional paper. Neither going to class nor the reading is required, but I would highly recommend going to class because the lectures are very interesting. Studying the slides is really all that is needed for the tests.

Prof Klint is awsome. He's a hotshot lawyer who teaches as a hobby. The class is extremely easy - one short presentation on one of the readings, a midterm, and a final. No need to read... just MEMORIZE the slides. There are a few questions (esp. on the midterm) that come from the Genest readings, but you can scrape by. Go to class.
Don't bother reading, all his test questions are from the lectures. His focus is on economics, so don't take it unless you have some understanding and interest in econ.
I loved this class...not sure of my grade yet, but positive I did well. Only test are midterm and final...GO TO CLASS AND PARTICIPATE...very interesting
Class was extremely boring. I hated going to it. But you only need to know the notes. Don't need to read. Only a midterm and a final. Not a hard class just study notes, which are on power points.

Alexander is the man! He's one of the coolest professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He doesn't like to do a lot of grading so there aren't many assignments, only a midterm and final. If you memorize the slides from class you know everything you need. I want to take every class he offers.

Class is entirely based on his powerpoint presentations, so if you go to class and take notes, you'll do fine.  He doesn't take attendance, but he knows your names and knows who comes to class.  He is extremely helpful and good-natured.  He is a lawyer in Nashville and will make time to field questions with anyone interested in attending law school

Very clear lectures and everything is on powerpoint slides.  Seems very knowledgable on the subject.  Very few assignments, basically just a midterm/final and a paper.  Grades papers easy as long as you cite sources correctly.  Tests are almost entirely based off the lectures/slides so you don't have to read.  Doesn't take attendance.

I loved this class. Everything is on powerpoint, and he explains really well. He also knows how to keep the class focused on what actually happens in the world. He's very open to class suggestions. The tests aren't difficult as long as you study the notes well. Fairly easy grader as long as you put effort into it. HOT.
This class is worth taking.  If you are worried about your grade, don't be.  If you go to class and take notes, you should end up with no less than a B+.
Awesome class...not very hard, especially if you come to class and take notes.  The paper is kinda a big project, but he doesn't seem to grade too hard.
Open to opinions of students. Good lecturing skills. However, you need to keep in mind of the midterms, final, and paper. The midterms and final are straightforward. The paper is around 8-12 pages.
Pretty easy if you study the notes.  Very few grades so you gotta do well on all the assignments.  Interesting letures though, and extremely helpful outside of class.

Excellent professor- the class is extremely interesting and he does a great job explaining all the information. As long as you study all the class notes you'll have no problem doing well in the class.
The class was pretty good, all the lectures are done on powerpoint.  The tests are a bit hard - id, short answers, and 2 essays all in class.  But if you study the notes, you should be good to go.

The most dense class I've taken, need very strong calc, lin alg, and stats fundamentals to understand. Lectures moved fast, covered lots of content, were proof/derivation based, and just generally difficult. Exams were mostly fair and homeworks were doable with GenAI. still, no formal teaching of any python but expected to use it at a high level.
Exams are difficult and homework is heavy. Lectures are very mid.
Brilliant guy but his class had even the international students confused. Homework and exam heavy, so not a lot of room for mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kolouri is a brilliant guy and a great professor. He does well answering questions and boiling down tough material into manageable chunks. A good math understanding is needed to stay afloat in class and definitely expect to put in many hours (>= 8) into the homeworks. But, this class is doable with good effort and is incredibly informative.

Easily the best professor in the CS department. Very mathematically dense lectures, but incredible at answering questions. Homeworks and tests are reasonable. Attendance is not required but you will get a ton out of going to class. Difficult course but very informational and 100% recommend.

Dr Kolouri by far gives the best math lectures in the CS department. That being said, there is a lot of math. The class is difficult, but Dr Kolouri cares a lot about your success and is very accessible. Additionally not all of the homeworks are graded very harshly and if you put in effort you should do well (expect at least one really tough exam).

Dr. Kolouri is a great professor. The slides can be very math heavy at times but he explains it well. I did not have any ML background so I found this class very challenging. Assignments can take 10+ hours but he grades very fairly. It is straightforward to get an A in this class as long as you put in the effort.

He is absolutely amazing! Best person to take Machine Learning with if you want to understand what's happening in the back end. His slides are easy to understand and he explains difficult concepts extremely well.

Two exams, some programming homework, and a final project. Dr. Kolouri indeed cares about students and want them to be successful. He is always available for talking about the course work and can provide a lot of help. He also gives clear lectures, covering plenty of topics about and math behind ML. Need to have good math skill to succeed.

While this wasn't my favorite class, professor Koch was a good professor. Much of the work is just practicing and writing your speeches. Basically like stripped back research papers, but Dr. Koch gives good feedback and is willing to work with students. He's very clear in his expectations, so just pay close attention to rubrics!

He's not the easiest grader, but also not super challenging. I'd say if you are not a naturally decent public speaker, not a good idea to take it as he'll grade accordingly. Biggest advice is you need to stay within the time limit for speeches (he'll take off SO MANY points if you're over/under) and make sure you practice speeches (he can tell).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Koch is a really nice guy and makes it very clear what he is expecting in his speeches. The amount of work for this class is so light except for when you have to actually write the speeches, but even that does not take long. Make sure to practice them a lot beforehand. He is not the easiest grader, but he is also not unreasonable. Great class

This class was very easy, but the expectations were unclear. We didn't get rubrics or grading criteria until the very last minute (and we had to ask for them). They graded very easily, but it was tricky to figure out what you needed to focus on. There was also a mandatory all day Saturday debate tournament that didn't have an alternative option.

Less of a cake walk than I assumed when I first saw these ratings, but it still isn't bad--you do have to put in some effort for an A though. Koch grades the first two speeches a lot easier than he does later on, so be careful. I do feel like my public speaking somewhat improved from this course. Videos of old speeches & impromptu speeches are fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Koch is very straightforward. You know exactly what you need to do to secure an A, and he creates fun class exercises and projects/assignments for his students. If you demonstrate that you are trying and you improve, you will do well. I would recommend this class to anyone who wants to become a better speaker.

One of my favorite classes at Vanderbilt. Classes were interactive and fun. While classes were 3 hours long (once a week), Professor Koch brought a great balance between lectures and various fun debate exercises. I think my public speaking has dramatically improved and helped me overcome this fear.

Dr. Koch is a great professor, and Argumentation and Debate is an easy class to take if you are interested in a communications major or minor. I felt that I was able to learn a lot without immense amounts of stress, which was a great change from my other classes. He gives good feedback, and is highly knowledgeable. I would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is straightforward and isn't too much work. If you meet the requirements you'll get the grade that you want.
Just a few speeches & fairly easy final. do have to work to get a solid A, but nothing too bad. just don't wait till last minute
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was a chill teacher that would give you the grade you wanted as long as you put in the effort.

Has gotta be one of the best classes I've taken at Vandy! He has such great taste in film and is so knowledgeable about everything around it. If you really watch all the films and do the reading, you'll learn so much about film. He's also very understanding about absences.

Professor Lutz was fantastic, deeply passionate about soccer. The course is rich in reading and learning, both in lectures and discussions. Active engagement is key for a good grade. There are two tests, with the option of a final project. Expect a weekly writing prompt. Great course for AXLE!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing! Very approachable and excellent lecturer. The class content was extremely interesting as well. In this class, you just have to show up and do what's asked and you'll be fine!

Terrific professor. Class was super easy but also super cool, loved his perspective on soccer. The course is pretty much showing up to class, doing some readings and writing 250 word responses each week, a midterm, and two presentations. None are graded harshly. The subject of the course is awesome to learn about too and Lutz is a super nice guy.

Professor Lutz is an extremely compassionate professor. Although there is a good amount of reading, it's nothing unmanageable. He is extremely accommodating if you have any illness, injuries, family problems, etc. His lectures are also very informative and engaging.

This was one of the new online classes Vanderbilt put together and it was pretty well-organized. Dr. Koepnick assigned a lot of outside work but graded assignments very generously. Grading was based on participation in discussion threads, assignment reviews, groupwork, a midterm and a final project. Would take again!

Professor Koepnick was probably the only professor who said I know this is a difficult time, and actually meant it. The entire class was practically graded by completion and while it can be a blow off class, if you pay attention most of the content is really interesting. I find myself referencing things I learned in this class a lot and enjoy it.

Professor Koepnick is amazing and this is a really easy class to take for AXLE (HCA). The work is not terrible and if you complete the assignments, you'll receive an A. The TA's were really helpful as well and you can get a lot out of this class if you want to! Highly recommend
Super nice prof. New class and he quickly created some really interesting content. Great guest lectures. Work is pretty easy if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Koepnick is sick at film study. He has great insights and really interesting lectures if you're into it. His selection of screenings is really solid, and he always has something interesting to say. papers are not hard, and assessments are very doable. he has a great dry sense of humor and just knows a lot of stuff. definitely listen in lecture.

A very interesting and good professor with cutting edge ideas, a little hard to follow or stay awake in class unless you're on top of the reading (which isn't easy) and are really motivated to get it all. He's great in conversation and helpful too.

Dr. Rose's class is 100% the best elective I've taken at Vanderbilt. She's so sweet and kind, and the class discussions are very interesting and relevant to daily life. There are weekly reading checks (but they aren't difficult), 3 short reflections, and 2 podcast assignments. She deserves tenure!!!!

Best professor ever, 100% recommend. Half of the grade is two podcast assignments, though those are not intensive and very enjoyable. Reading checks most weeks, but they're not difficult so long as you have a brain and skimmed the readings. Fun class discussions, especially if you're already into this topic but even if you're not they're enjoyable.
she can make a class both enjoyable and meaningful!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She puts in a lot of effort in making her class engaging and meaningful. Dr.Rose truly cares about her students and goes above and beyond that we learn! There are readings before class, podcast midterm and final (group project), and 4 - 5 reflections to write. As long as you participate in class and stay engaged, it's not a challenging A.

She is an incredibly caring and supportive educator. She consistently goes above and beyond to ensure every student feels valued and understood, creating an inclusive and welcoming learning environment. Just take her class—you won't regret it!

I didn't take this class for a grade, but I enjoyed it thoroughly. The content was super interesting, and the classroom discussions were a great experience. We engaged with all sorts of media, not just written literature. Seems like for graded students, making sure you regularly participate in the discussions is very important! But it's worth it :)
Mostly spent time reading slides and let students discuss during class, grading is vague
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There were midterm & final group podcast projects on any topic u want. Lots of reading assignments but she is an easy grader. Expectations are clear & she gives great feedback. She puts a lot of effort into making class fun & gives a lot of creative freedom. She is one of the nicest profs I've had. Mix of lectures, class activities, & discussions.

Dr. Rose is my favorite professor I have taken in my life. She is so incredibly caring about her students and teaches the most interesting and inspirational content that makes her class absolutely stellar. She is extremely understanding and kind but her class also is challenging in every perfect way. Get ready to think and share! 10/10 recommend.

Dr. Rose is new to Vanderbilt, but she is already such a strong professor who understands her students. Literary Lesbians was a class I always looked forward to because the readings were interesting, the discussions were educational, and Dr. Rose always had such great energy. One of the best prof-student relationships I've had. 10/10

Dr. Rose is great, just wants you to learn something. HW readings that you provide thoughts on, not too difficult. 4 reflections for completion and midterm and final are group podcasts. Easy A for an AXEL perspectives class, definitely recommend!

Wow. Where do I even start. Yiorgos changed my life in just one semester of teaching. Even that might be an understatement. I doubt I am the only one. I simply can't sribe my thoughts about Prof Kostoulas in 350 characters. Despite the immense knowledge his class gave me, I plan to dedicate the rest of my life to creating a religion for YK.

Yiorgos is my personal hero. He led me through my darkest time; he's very, very inspirational. He talks all the time about his little Achilleas, an academic weapon in high school. Anyways, back to Yiorgos, he is a total G. If I never met him, I would've dropped out and became a druggie, but he inspired me to change the world with my awesomeness.
I am a child in south america. Master Yiorgos taught me very well. I recomend him for all my brothers overseas
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Yiorgy is da best!
This professor was amazing. he has an extensive knowledge of all topics and is the only reason I graduated.

GREAT lecturer. This class has some really intensive material and he still kept me engaged. He is clearly very smart and successful in his field. Tests are hard, final group presentation at the end isn't too bad. Material is pretty interesting!

We would always talk about the material after class one-on-one, which is something no other prof. has done for me. The class itself is not very good, but Professor Kostoulas gives good lectures and is very caring.

I don't usually use RMP, but I have to come on here to talk about how great Yiorgos Kostoulas is. Would recommend taking this class if you have no friends who want to take it with you, as the entire class is a group project. Despite this, the class is still spectacular.

WOW


class is 10/10 :)

While the year long group prodject was not ideal, Yiorgos still impressed me. I always showed up to his lectures (even though he puts material online) because he is just that good. I recomend him for people who want to learn, and work with friends
He's the best if you actually take a chance to talk to him and don't just sit through class. If you engage even a little bit you'll enjoy this class more than any other. Tedious but not hard.
The class was tough, but Yiorgos showed that he cared. He is the best prof I have had at Vandy so far. I would recommend this class to everyone except if you are struggling in your classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He cares, which matters more than everything. 10/10

Yiorgos is great and so chill. The entire class is one big group project but you get to do some pretty cool research on a technology of your group's choice. Homework is weekly submissions where you split up the writing among your group for a couple paragraphs each, not too bad. One or two major presentations as well but overall chill and fun!

Engaging and insightful course! Prof. Yiorgos was an excellent instructor, providing valuable insights and flexibility in his approach. We had the chance to select a modern technology and study its potential from a business perspective. The project involved market research and strategic planning, which was very instructive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Highly rewarding class! It involved exploring cutting-edge technologies and their commercial viability. We worked in teams to investigate market trends and create a viable commercialization strategy. This course bridged the gap between technical understanding and business. Professor Yiorgos was very approachable and always encouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Incredible learning opportunity! The course focused on the real-world application of advanced technologies. We selected a unique technology, analyzed its industry impact, and created a comprehensive market entry strategy. The hands-on approach was enlightening. Dr. Yiorgos was an outstanding mentor, always available to guide us.

Fantastic experience! This course allowed us to dive deep into emerging technologies and their market potential. We conducted thorough research and developed detailed business models. It was an eye-opener to the practical aspects of tech innovation. Professor Yiorgos was exceptionally knowledgeable and supportive throughout the semester.

Great class! We got to work on commercializing a cool technology of our choice. Did some research and put our findings in the commercialization plan. It was great to see the business side of technology firsthand.
Yiorgos was a great professor and quite understanding and flexible.

Yiorgos is so incredible. He is a great professor and an even better father. He cares about everything he does. Plus, his son helped the Tactful Taos win the Wordmasters competition. Yiorgos similarly has a strong vocabulary.

Hard class, but very interesting. Got kinda crazy. You learn to pattent in Julia, but it gets confusing because you don't know if your patent is wrong because of your syntax or because you implemented logic wrong. Would recommend this class, but it is quite mathematically dense. My teammates in the group project really had my back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was a really fun class! We got to work on cool projects, like making a phone case and then a syringe pump at the end. It's amazing how many skills we covered, like 3D printing, soldering, and programming LEDs with microcontrollers. Overall there isn't much homework but Prof. Kostoulas is a harsh grader.

Best prof ever!! Yiorgos is so kind and genuinely cares about his students. Everything we learned in class was very helpful/applicable to the outside world. The year-long group project really helped me understand the material better.

Very useful class to take for every engineer. Some of the assignments and presentations can be tedious but it is all necessary. Yiorgos Kostoulas is very kind and conveys the material clearly. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Work in this class fluctuates -- there are periods where there is little to do and some periods where there is a good bit of work. Grading is pretty lenient. It is evident that he is more interested in your development as a communicator than just evaluation. I highly recommend his office hours, he's very accommodating and is willing to help.

Professor Yiorgos was great, Very relaxed, and approachable. Grading is not tough and he often brought his significant industrial experience into the classroom. He was always approachable and provided valuable feedback. I highly recommend this class to anyone who wants a great class at vandy. Vandy's best teacher ever!

Every day was a joy when I attended his class. Yiorgos cares about every student in his class, even when you leave his class he still goes out of his way to support you. His class was quite boring but he made up for it with his great group projects.

Tech Strategy was a great class! I learned a lot about technology commercialization. Most fun was the article Professor Yiorgos shared with us in class, which showed how the course topics are playing out in the real world. Every day was a joy when I attended his class.

In brightest day, in blackest night, No evil shall escape my sight. Let those who worship evil's might. Beware my power. -Mr. Kostoulas. He told and was very inspirational. Takes attention of the room immediately. I remember his class so vividly (In a good way)
He is so inspirational I really can't believe he great he is. Yiorgos does have his flaws, but they are minimal. My favorite teacher this year.
Let me start by saying that Yiorgos taught me more in two semesters than I learned in every one of my high school classes. What a great teacher! I wish the best for him!
Inspired me is a dark place. Illuminated my world 10/10
Excellent professor he is one of the best I have ever had.

entire class is based on group project with weekly deliverables. drop immediately if you don't get a good group bc this class is a ton of research/homework! also don't take this class if your semester load is already heavy. valuable content though, and the final product is a good testament for interviews/networking/impressing recruiters.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Tech Strategy was a great class! I learned a lot about technology commercialization. Most fun were the article professor Yiorgos shared with us in the class, which showed how the course topics are playing out in the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Yiorgos was great, Very relaxed, and approachable. Grading is not tough and he often brought his significant industrial experience into the classroom. He was always approachable and provided valuable feedback. I highly recommend this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Kostoulas is an exceptional professor who made a significant impact on my academic experience. What stood out to me the most was his passion for teaching and his ability to connect with students on a personal level. He was always approachable and available to provide guidance and support whenever needed.
He's the boy if you actually take a chance to talk to him and don't just sit through class. If you engage even a little bit you'll enjoy this class. Tedious but not hard.
He has the best teachings. he is the top g i love him he a legend
Great professor I recommend taking this class
In brightest day, in blackest night, No evil shall escape my sight. Let those who worship evil's might. Beware my power. -Mr. Kostoulas. He told and was very inspirational.
He's awesome at teaching!!
This professor is very good. He has long, boring lectures but they are worth it because they give a lot of information. He has one big group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself is not hard. It is A TON of work though. It's basically a group project the entire semester. I could not tell you one thing I learned. You research a single product in one industry but nothing is actually usable. You only have two absences you can use throughout the semester which sucked because the class were SO boring.

This was less work than other engineering classes, it was def more than I expected. Most of your grade is from one big group project, and he makes it v difficult to get an A. He also gave participation grades based on guidelines that were NEVER mentioned in the syllabus. Mine was a 70 and I went to all but 1 class and did all in class activities.
This class is one big group project. There is way too much assigned work and it all feels like one big repetition. Definitely wish I could go back in time and never enrolled.

The lectures were very boring. I did not learn much so the suggested textbook was more helpful than the slides when it came to the assignments. There wasn't too much work, but there is also a presentation with a partner. Participation is apart of your grade.

Professor Kostoulas isn't the most energetic professor when it comes to lectures, but he really knows his stuff. This class is best if you talk with him one-on-one about the assignments because the lectures aren't the most interesting.

Yiorgos is a fine professor, definitely knows what he is talking about, but makes his lectures boring. you could never go to class and still do well, but he takes attendance everyday so attendance is mandatory. I would neither recommend or dissuade someone from taking a class with him. He's fine.

More than 50% of our classes were cancelled. She is very kind, but she never came to class. And cancelled at 9:57 when class starts at 10:10 it was so annoying. And I don't mind no class, obviously, but it gets to a point... Her lectures were good and interesting. The assignments were a coloring sheet once a week, and an easy final project

Easiest class/professor you'll take at Vandy. Cancels class all the time, especially at the end of the semester. A couple of one-paragraph reading responses and a final group podcast project. Super sweet. Even though it was easy, you can actually learn quite a bit if you pay attention in class. Definitely a great low-stress class.

I have mixed emotions. She's so smart, an easy grader and caring professional. However, she tended to treat a class of seniors and juniors with too much babying. We had colorful worksheets and mini activities for a course I felt would benefit more from serious discussion and debate. I LOVED The course material and she is a great woman though.
She is the best.
Very chill class. I'd recommend any class they teach. They frequently cancel class and homework isn't bad.

Prof. Navarro is a caring and enthusiastic. Class was cancelled just about every other week. She had interesting lectures and encourage good class discussion. No tests, quizes or exams. Only big assignment was a group podcast which was very easy. Final was again a podcast or a one-page paper.

Navarro is so great. Frequently cancels class. You get to learn about a new discipline without being super about grades because they are very lenient with them. On the other hand, if you actually want solid feedback on how you are doing and you're actually interested in learning the subject on a deep level, Navarro is not the professor for you.

One of the most incredible profs! She is genuinely so interested in students' learning and is exceedingly responsive to students' input during class discussions. She puts so much effort into her lectures which makes the class really engaging. The assignments were very easy/manageable. She also just has a super cool personality! 100/10 professor!

Absolutely loved having her. Helped me further develop Critical thinking skills and provided new perspective on works I was already familiar with. She genuinely cares about her students and wants you to succeed, bot just in her class but in life. She helped me gain confidence in my writing.. Taking a class with her is a privilege/treat.

Navarro rocks. She is easygoing and understanding, and really tries to engage the whole class in discussion. Almost no homework; your grade is mostly participation in terms of talking to a few people around you. Good class for making friends!

Kristen is absurdly nice and so supportive. Her class is probably a little too easy, but she is super helpful and considerate for her students' experience. I loved her choice in readings, and she always had great discussions. She's very sympathetic about deadlines, and grades very generously.

Professor Navarro is great. She is such a kind and caring person. She makes herself super accessible to students and is always willing to talk about an assignment with you. As long as you skim the readings, do the assignments, and show up to most classes, you will get a good grade.

Professor Navarro truly cares about her students. She is flexible with deadlines, appreciates everyone's comments, and truly just wants people to learn. She is very informed on her subject matter. I learned a lot and did minimal work.

This is the best class I've taken at Vandy so far, Professor Navarro is obviously very passionate about what she does, tries to make everyone comfortable when discussing difficult topics and wants all her student to do excellently well. The coursework is a lot but super interesting so it doesn't feel like a bore. Would recommend this to everyone!
She is so nice and pretty easy class. Very Discussion based and you watch a lot of movies. If you write the essay well, you will get an A in the class.

Professor Navarro is honestly the sweetest teacher I've ever had! Her class is so chill, it's very hard to get anything lower than an A. If I could take all my english classes with her- I 100% would! Awesome teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof Navarro is one of the sweetest people I've ever met. Graded based on 3 papers where you get lots of insight as to what she's looking for, an extremely easy presentation, and participation. Discussion is very laid back, she encourages you to share whatever you're thinking, even if it's just "I liked that scene", in order to give you points.

This was a great course that is very interesting and relevant to learning what history is about. Kramer himself cares about the subject and is really happy to talk about it, though he is a little disorganized and the grading is really slow. But if the subject is interesting to you, I would recommend you take it.

Very disorganized and slow turnaround time for exams. Grading criteria for exams is very vague and you kind of have to guess what information he is looking for since they are entirely free response. Had several students including myself type out our exams because he couldn't read them. Impossible to read his chicken scratch handwriting on the board
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy
