reviews.comment: Kramer is awesome. Super fair grader, great review sessions, and interesting topic. You can tell he really loves his job and genuinely cares about his students. Lot of reading and the lectures are a little disorganized, but aside from that I loved the class. Highly recommend taking this class and I plan on taking more with Kramer in the future.

Professor Kramer may have an unorthodox way of lecturing (very free range), however, it is very effective at giving you a working knowledge of the material that you will remember after the course ends.  He is a very fair grader and gave students the option for extra credit as well as a sort of corrections opportunity. Taking him again!

Pros: I have never learned more important material than during this class. I could reflect on our societal structures, and I retained a lot of interesting lessons! 

Cons: Prof. K is unorganized, slow to respond via email, takes weeks to grade, and assigns a TON of work. Tests are DIFFICULT. This is not the class for those who don't LOVE history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kramer was a nice guy, but extremely unorganized. Would throw up his chicken scratch randomly on the chalkboard, late grades, and always late to class. Lots of assigned readings you don't really have to do. Discussions in class could sometimes be interesting, but it felt like an APUSH retake.

Prof. Kramer is passionate and well-read.  Makes it hard to be frustrated with his other antics, but he's always late and hard to get a hold of. Took forever to get my exam grades back. Reading is dense (200+ pages a class, multiple texts) and often excluded from discussion without warning. Very nice guy, but his disorganization is painful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was perhaps the most unorganized guy at Vanderbilt. He's a very nice guy outside of the class, but the lectures were extremely tedious and the exams were brutally tough as there was so much information to review. Wouldn't exactly recommend to anyone.

Nice guy who is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. What is expected on the tests is very clear and it is not difficult to get an A. He assigns long readings that are unnecessary. Showed up late to every class. Very unorganized with teaching styles and what was being taught during lectures. Lectures tended to be rather boring.

The previous post is cap ngl. Kramer is an amazing professor who will actually (matter of fact) give feedback on papers if you attend his office hours and let him know in advance that you are seeking feedback.Readings are heavy but who said  every page is important to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No idea how good of a lecturer he is cus I never showed up to class, but I completely forgot to submit one of the essays on time or do the weekly discussion posts, and he let me submit everything for full credit 2 days before final grades were due, saving me from failing. When you look up "g" in the encyclopedia, it's a picture of this man.

If you are a student who is only interested in content and not your grades, Paul Kramer is the guy for you. He never provides feedback and grades on paper in time. As such, to do well you must have very good writing skills. His reading assignments are ridiculously long and sometimes triggering, especially on the ones about race and slavery.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very, very reading heavy. Like, 200 pages per class. The lectures are mostly just going over reading but I found all of the content genuinely interesting. Prof. Kramer is incredibly intelligent, and the best part of this class was his responses to questions. They were always very thoughtful and taught me things I didn't even know to ask about.

Professor Kramer is very passionate about what he does, so I will give him that. However, there is usually around 200 pages of reading per week, and sometimes even 2 hour movies thrown in here and there. There is supposed to be 4 papers in the class, but he is so disorganized that one of the papers was cut this year. Overall very disorganized prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kramer is a decent lecturer, but the readings for each class are incredibly long and often irrelevant to the things you actually do for big grades. He does give good feedback on papers, but he is TERRIBLY slow with returning them back to you, so you will be 3 months into the semester with no idea how you are actually doing in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kramer is an okay professor. The setup of this course is to read 70-100 pages of reading before each class and spend the whole time discussing it. The overall content is interesting I suppose, but the readings are dense/boring. There are 4 papers which is your grade plus participation. He doesn't seem like a harsh grader but he is very slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Kramer is very kind, and gives amazing feedback (and easier grades) on papers, but his class can sometimes be a bit boring. There will be hundreds of pages of reading each week (most of which you can safely skip), and each class is basically a discussion on the readings.
Doesnt give attention to students on any level. Seems bothered to have teaching obligations.

Great lectures that I learned loads from. But like other reviews, I did not know my standing in the class going Into finals week. Really nice Professor and hes clearly very passionate about his field, but the grading was his real downfall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really love Kramer's lectures. Regardless of what other reviews say, he really is something special, I promise. The man is really intelligent, and really knows his way around history. He opened my mind in multiple important ways, and changed a lot about my politics. Be prepared to buy and read an ungodly amount of books though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Kramer provides a bunch of really awesome content through this class. You'll end up with a good grasp on the history of social change writing and what makes effective writing today. You get the chance to speak with a variety of cool journalists and writers. If you have a passion for a social issue, this class lets you explore it

Prof Kramer is a very nice man and clearly knowledgeable about history, but I would not take another class with him. We had to buy 10+ books and only read about 2 chapters out of each of them. Also, he takes a month to grade papers. Going into the last week of class, we'd only received back 1 paper and he does not respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He literally makes us buy like $200 worth of books and we read like 1 page per book??? Insanity. also he does take like a billion years to grade our papers lol

DO NOT take this man... I agree with the other rating. he's awful. he's suuuuuper lazy and takes literally forever to grade paper and rarely answers to emails. Literally do not take him. There are so many good profs in the history department and kramer is arguably the worst

This man is a disgrace to Vanderbilt. By far the WORST professor I've ever had. Doesn't ever respond to emails, is completely unorganized, and literally takes 30-40+ days to grade your papers. Last week of class, no one knew their standing in the class. DO NOT!!!! take this man. He seems nice but is lazy and honestly not deserving of this job.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Kramer is gentle in style and speech, but in regards to grading papers, he holds nothing back. He also takes at least 30-40 days to grade a paper. Going into the final week, no one in the class knew what their grade was. I would highly recommend NOT taking any of his higher level courses. He is not the hardest, but he is SO frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Intense class with a moderate-heavy reading requirement and be prepared to show up and participate. Responsive to requests for help. Learned a lot, thought provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Easy A but will never take again. Gave back almost no work the entire semester so you never know your grade for sure, never responded to emails, liberally biased to the point you can't take anything he says seriously, and a ridiculous attendance policy even though you don't need to be there to do well at all. Made us buy tons of textbooks for 1 ch.
Animated, great facilitator.  Excellent resource if you're looking for help.
If you put in the time, you get a lot out and he'll meet with you to iron out your papers.
Well thought out reading assignments for the most part - but you'll read more than your other classes.

Lectures are straighforward, but there is loads of reading and attendance is mandatory (although there is extra credit). You can skim the readings for discussion, and if you go to class its not hard to do well. This is by no means an easy class, but it is neither unfair, nor impossible. Participation 15%, 3 Essays (5 pages) 60%, Final 25%

Interesting material. He got better at lecturing as the semester wore on. Would've been a great class if he hadn't assigned absolutely absurd amounts of (dull) reading. The whole class thought his workload was unfair. His liberal bias bothered some people (not me). If he wasn't so demanding and was more approachable, he'd be a pretty good prof.
He's a nice guy and it's not a bad class. He's a pretty good lecturer too. The major complaints are that it's very reading intensive and the attendance policy is absolutely ridiculous.
An excellent professor, and an easy course to get AXLE requirements out of the way. Grading is based on 3 essays, a final, and mandatory discussions once a week. Fun, engaging, and interesting.
Was a dry class with dry material.  Nice guy but had a dry style.

Dr. Preacher only lectures, and in terms of work you will have about seven homework assignments. Those a pretty long and tough, but luckily, a lot of the key information is outlined in the PowerPoints. He can be a tad passive-aggressive when you meet one-on-one with him, but in class, he seems engaged. Additionally, his TAs can be hard to reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Preacher is awesome. His lectures are clear and extremely helpful, and he is very clearly a kind person. I haven't been able to attend his office hours yet, but I can confidently say that he would try everything to help his students. Even for a Friday class, he is funny and engaging, especially for a class where most people are filling a req.

Kris is a super caring and responsive professor, however, I can't say I learned much in this class. He flew threw lectures so fast I barely took notes, and I found myself clueless on most of the homeworks. Factor Analysis is a guaranteed A though, even if you don't know what's going on.

Preacher is a nice guy and knows the material extremely well. Classes are not mandatory at all. He reads the slides word for word and then posts the slides online. 4 homework assignments all semester that you can do the night before. Not an awful class, just a very boring one. Other introductory stats teachers are easier

Kris is a really nice guy with reasonable expectations. Only four homework assignments and three tests. Final is not cumulative. Gives easy extra credit on most assignments. Attendance is the opposite of mandatory. Lectures tend to be boring, but his  PowerPoints are VERY helpful. Just do the homework, look over the slides, and you'll be fine

Class is way too easy. He gives you all the formulas, so you just have to know how to apply them. He also gives lots of extra credit, so that a large number of people made over a 100% on the second test. If you need to take statistics, take it with Preacher. He's also very nice and his powerpoints have everything you need to know.

His multilevel modeling graduate course is a baptism by statistical fire for any undergraduate capable of sticking with it. However, taking his course will ensure that you understand everything you need to know. Take his class if you're in it for the content, not the grade.

Stats isn't interesting, and he knows it. He also knows pretty much everyone is taking that class because they have to. However, you really don't need to show up to any lecture, just the discussion sections, because he posts powerpoints that he reads directly from online. Quizzes are super easy and just test attendance to discussion.
Dr. Preacher is just really boring, because stats is really boring. However, an A is easy (even if you hate math!)

Class is dull. It is statistics though, so I didn't expect much. He gives three exams. four homework problem sets. This class doesn't require much time and attendance is anything but mandatory. Look over his slides, practice with his test review sheets, and an A/A- is attainable. Take his section if you're just fulfilling a requirement.
Very good lecturer, very kind and helpful. Responds to emails quickly. Would definitely take a course with her again.
I love her! She really cares about your understanding and isn't a very hard grader for exams. Still not an easy class but office hours are very helpful.
Class has quizzes, homeworks, and exams. Grading is very lenient. Very helpful in office hours. Definitely recommend for multivariable calc

Teaches clearly. You are always welcome 2 ask after class or in office hour. She even prepared online office hours n another big room for answering. Sometime, she would stay more than 1 hour after class for questions. Scores are very fair  (there are some kind of huge curves). Most of all!! she's humorous, one joke in class often make my day!
Took this class Fall 2022, and she is the best math professor I have had at Vanderbilt. Super nice, caring, nice grader, and always was positive.

Prof Kryvonos is such a great professor. She works hard to make the lectures easy to follow and engaging. She is also very accommodating when it comes to making up tests or late weekly homework. Tests aren't too difficult either.

Professor Liudmyla is super caring to her students and is always responsive to emails and during office hours. Don't rely on her online notes, go to lecture because she goes through extra problems that can be helpful. Calc is hard but she tries her best to help us understand it. Would definitely recommend!

Best Vandy math professor. Although I am not done with this course yet, I have learned more in math with Kryvonos than in all my other math courses combined. She is incredibly caring and accessible. Her lectures can be dry, but if you get lost she is great at reexplaining in office hours. Tests are every doable if you put effort into the homework.

Professor Kryvonos has been the best math professor I have had at Vanderbilt. Homework can be tough, however, if you take time to complete every homework to the best of your ability and actually make an effort to understand the concepts exams will not be difficult. She really cares about her students and makes herself available to all students.

Prof. Kryvonos is one of the best multi professors at Vandy! She makes the material approachable and the practice problems correlate directly with the homework. Tests are hard, but on par with all other professors. She is super accessible through office hours and zoom and email. Would 100% recommend her for MATH 2300
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are fairly boring and she can waste a lot of time on tangents but she def cares about her students. Accessible before class and on zoom at night. Homework is disproportionally time intensive compared to weekly quizzes. Exams are difficult but not unfair by any means. Prof Kryvonos is not bad but be ready to start a study group and read

Worst professor I have ever had. I was told this class was perfect for people who were taking their final math class and was not worried about this course. The homework and tests were nearly impossible, being 7+ pages long for a 50 minute time period. The homework was significantly more difficult than the examples in class and was graded harshly.

Professor Kryvonos was incredibly kind and was consistently available outside of class for extra help. The homework was generally harder than the exams and we were always informed of what we would be tested on. Her lectures were often boring and overly complicated but she is definitely still one of the best math professors at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kryvonos is an amazing addition to the Vanderbilt Math Department. While her lectures for diff eq can be dry at times, she is an effective communicator for any questions. She cares deeply about understanding and encourages students to work out solutions on chalkboards in office hours. Tests are tough, but she gives ample extra credit.

Her class was awesome! The lectures were always super interesting and the tests were fair (if you read the textbook). 

The only thing that I didn't love was the research group project at the end. It was a little frustrating and I wish it would've been done a little differently. 

She is an awesome person and very open to feedback (which is great)!

She's the sweetest professor I've had here. Lectures are mainly discussion based, so make sure to actually read the textbook outside of class if you wanna pass the tests. But she also gives the most useful study guides ever.
Dr. Mehari is a great professor! Her class is my favorite. I recommend her for developmental psychology. Her class is organized and her lectures are helpful. She is also very considerate and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such an awesome professor, it is clear that she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. There was a lot of reading, but she gave ample time to do it and there were not many assignments, just three longer papers and a few smaller reflections on what we read. TAKE HER CLASS, you won't regret it.
TAKE HER CLASS. I cannot overstate how much I enjoyed this class and its content. Get ready to read but also engage with the text!
Very helpful and cares about students. She will give ample opportunities to succeed and will make your writing much better.

Prof K is one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Though opinions vary between past and current students, I found this upper-level W course extremely manageable, with weekly journals and two essays (+ revision for the 2nd one). She prioritizes understanding the material and fostering great class discussions over stressing about grades.

I feel like there is some disconnect between the older comments and the current student opinion on this professor. Kutzinski will expect you to work and provide valuable insights, but she really looks to accommodate students and allow for revisions. She once gave me two chances for revision and is very open to extensions/cancelling assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor K is great and cares a lot about her students. She gives really good feedback on your papers and doesn't overwhelm you with assignments. She's super willing to meet with you outside of class and is very respectful of your time and schedules. Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kutzinski is one of the kindest and most personable professors I've had here at Vandy. Her classes were always engaging, she encourages other students to share their thoughts on assignments and class topics, and she is available for help outside of class. Lots of writing assignments, but she is lenient on due dates and very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Someone 8 years ago was clearly upset looking at these reviews... But Dr. Kutzinski is easily one of the best professors I've had here at Vanderbilt. Great lectures, always brought her adorable dog to class, had AMAZING book selections, and initiated thoughtful discussions about them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Vera is super smart, but the class can be a bit boring if you are not invested in the subject matter. She makes you work for your grade but gives you every opportunity to be successful. She also brings her dog to class which is awesome. I recommend taking her if you don't mind working decently hard and like deep discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Kutzinski leads great discussions in class and leaves good feedback on papers. There's a lot of reading (which is honestly good), but enter knowing you'll read a new book every week and a half or so.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Vera is a believer in tough-love, but she has improved my writing more than any other teacher or professor I have ever had. Her classes are difficult but not impossible. Participation, attendance, and effort are crucial. Her science fiction class is not easy but it is interesting.

One of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. Pushes you with harsh comments and midterm grading to participate and improve your writing. Papers are easy as long as your argument is clear and adheres to her notion of a "good" argument. Readings are sometimes boring but help you learn to think critically.

Kutzinski is the professor I believe has taught me the most about writing in my time at Vanderbilt. She is not afraid to give you a C- if you deserve it, but she also rewards you when you put in the work. She is incredibly intelligent and the discussions are engaging, but be prepared for some tough love. Take her class if you can!

I have never had a professor that was as hard to please as Professor Kutzinski. Her assignments are unclear so you do not know exactly what to do, and yet her grading is ridiculous and at times and unfair. Often times her grading seems nothing more than a matter of opinion, and yet she counts off. Do not take her class.

She is actually the worst. I have never had a more condescending, inconsiderate professor in my time at Vanderbilt. She deliberately makes her assignments difficult to understand so that she can rip you apart during grading. Papers are assigned frequently, and lectures are incredibly long and boring. Do not, under any circumstances, take her class.

She is intelligent, but grades incredibly hard and is often not clear on her expectations of students when completing her assignments. I have gone to the writing studio seeking help, they helped me, and then she counted me off for making the corrections that they told me to make. Unless you are one of 2-3 people she likes, very low chance at an A.

She is a very cold person. Emails and comments often come across as very rude. Gives very bad grades on papers simply because she "didn't like the argument." I was never clear on how to get a good grade on a paper. Unclear, and class is extremely boring.
Great professor, stimulating in class and gives great feedback with weekly papers so you have no excuse for continuing to turn in bad writing.
Extremely intelligent and stimulating.  Will challenge you and you'll like it.  Take a class with her if you can.
I love Dr. Kushan. She was the best professor I've ever had. Highly recommend taking her class. I miss her.
Dr. Kushan is AMAZE.
Dr. Kushan was incredibly helpful, kind, and intelligent. Would definitely recommend taking her for calc 1200. Thanks for a great semester Dr. Kushan!

Does not explain requirements for assignments and wants us to improve upon feedback from previous assignments. Returns feedback for the first assignment after all other assignments are due. Does not explain requirements regardless. Proceeds to grade harshly. Did not even come to class for a third of the semester.

I think the reason why she is so negatively rated is that many people did not listen to the lectures at all. The avg of first midterm was insanely low, while the midterm itself is totally normal no matter in which school. You could compare it with the CS188 of UCB. CS4260 has nothing harder than its counterparts in the other schools.
Never give back our test grade in 1 month, even before the final retake window. Changed syllabus for 14 versions. Extremely unorganized lecture and unreasonable grading rubrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Kunda is never available outside of class and often cancels/delay the class with a sorry message. I think I have received over 20 sorry messages from her this semester. It's so disappointed to see her efforts into our class and there are also lots of things to do if you need to do to get a A- in the class.

A very nice person, but the most unorganized professor i've ever seen. would cancel class all the time and then give out tests on material not taught. TAs didn't even know what was going on. do not take this class with her, you will not learn anything (unless you teach yourself).

She's not a bad person. But boy was she disorganized. Had it together for like 1 lecture, then started completely rambling in class and everything you learn is from the Berkeley lectures. Cancelled 4 of 28 classes minutes before start. Didn't even submit final grades on time. We should all be inspired that she became a professor at an elite college

Professor Kunda cancelled two weeks of class 5 min before each class session. It's a week before the final exam and she hasn't gotten any grades back to us and the course goals have changed about 6 times. Her classes consist of useless exercises and the only time I learned anything was when we were given material from the Berkley CS class.

Class was regularly canceled or delayed for weeks straight and class time was spent doing activities that were largely irrelevant to student's learning. Almost no grades have been released, and the professor did not respond to emails regarding exams or class content. If you want to learn AI, I would strongly encourage you to do it elsewhere.

I am just surprised that she's actually not fired. I was excited to have an innovator 35 Under 35 professor to teach us but she only gives us video lectures from CS188 UCB. Respect for her for not getting fired.

THE worst CS class at Vanderbilt. Teaches by making students watch YouTube videos and then having meaningless, disorganized class discussion. A total waste of time and tuition money. If you are really into AI then tough luck, you should've applied for Berkeley instead.
Kunda is the second most ridiculous person Ive ever seen  the most ridiculous one is the guy who gave her a good rating on this website (if they are not the same guy).

She regularly cancels class with little warning, and the exams don't get graded for months. Due to COVID19, I can't exactly just knock on her door to ask for help during office hours, but she almost never responds to emails either. Where exactly is our tuition going? Paying for youtube videos that we can google ourselves?
Can we please get someone else to teach this class?

She claimed that you would learn more in this class than just take a free youtube AI course and went on making this class consist entirely of Berkeley's CS188 lecture recordings and other random youtube videos and giving no feedbacks on homework and exams whatsoever, let alone randomly canceling classes 5 minutes before.
Asks you to describe algorithms in class but never goes through them herself and then wants you to code them in homework that takes multiple days and that aren't for that much credit

Her class is extremely discussion-heavy, which in my opinion is the only proper way to conduct a special topics graduate class. The papers she assigned for reading significantly helped shape my perspective of AI systems. Even though the course will make you work hard, every bit is absolutely worth it!

Professor Kusner is a really nice professor. From my perspective, he was one of those professors that knew the content, he just didn't know how to simply and explain content in an easier manner. It's a flipped classroom so make sure not to fall behind. I had a tutor for this class (and I usually don't need them for math). Best of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite math professor by far. I really hope he doesn't leave UGA in case he decides to teach further courses in the future, but if you're thinking about taking him... I 100% vouch for him. Not only is he a great prof but also a great person (and a soon to be dad). Very easy to talk to and extremely knowledgable. Could not have had a better one

Flipped classroom, homework daily before class which was videos and worksheets to go along with them. Explanations from him weren't the best but he was easy to follow along in class and very willing to help if you ask him. He gives credit for problems as long as you have a general idea of what you are doing and gives credit back on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: (He taught at UGA this year) Professor Woden is a very nice professor and is always willing to give help. The format for all the calc classes this year was watch the online videos and ask questions in class. He goes over the practice but it was kind of meh explanations. Not a hard grader-put some work that makes sense down and he'll give you points
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I took him for Calc I and am taking him for Calc II right now and his class is very easy in my opinion. He doesn't assign that much work and the quizzes/ tests are not hard at all. Pretty easy grader so long as you make an attempt on the problem and show all of your work. 10/10 would take again
Lectures can be a little dry/not extremely helpful, but homework is pretty short and he is really good when you ask for help on problems in office hour. Tests/quizzes were reasonable

Homework is short problem sets due on Mondays, so you have to do extra work outside of class to fully understand the material. He's a conceptual teacher, so just knowing how to do computations will not be sufficient, and this is what makes multi hard. The lectures are fairly engaging, albeit scattered at times. Overall, a safe bet. I liked him.

He is not a very clear lecturer. Homework can be time consumingcollaborate with each other on it since he allows. Tests are nothing like the homework, or textbook problems. However, interesting and fun. He's a nice guy and cares about his students but class is tough. Abstractness makes class challenging, but also interesting for those into math.

His lectures are really hard to follow, so resort to youtube videos. Even after the lectures are understood, his homework is impossible and graded on correctness. He makes up his own tests which have problems much harder than the homework. Overall, he makes the material unnecessarily difficult.

He's definitely one of the newer professors, but he tries his best and will answer any questions you have. There is usually weekly homework as well as weekly quizzes, the discussion class is a crucial component of this class, but a lot of people seemed ok even if they skipped the lectures. Pretty easy tests.

Professor Kusner is a somewhat new professor, and the inexperience shows somewhat. His lectures are overall good, but there are sometimes slides or points he attempts to make that are a bit unclear. He is a nice person and is easily accessible outside of class. The tests were very easy, especially for a mathematics course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Most math classes at Vanderbilt are test heavy and are taught from the textbook: this class is not an exception. However, there is something incredibly endearing about Kun Wang and how unintentionally/intentionally funny and caring he is. He scales tests, understands students, and the homework load is reasonable. Be warned, he does have an accent!
It's a hard class at times, but the lectures are very helpful and go over things a lot better than the book does.
I had him for 2300 and did fine but 2810 was hell. pick a prof with less proofs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not much HW compared to other profs for 2300. okay tests. final is no joke. review problems he does in class and HW for the tests. hes adorable. wears the same reeboks and ripped jeans to class every day. owns like 3 shirts

Kun is a good prof. However, he's got a thick accent and lecture can be really dull. Not to mention his 3 exams throughout the semester are really difficult. If you wanna pass the class, you'll have to spend a lot of time with practice problems. Fortunately, Kun is great during office hours. If you're backed up against a wall, then you can try Kun.

Kun Wang was pretty hard to understand, and focused too much on the derivations of formulas in class. However, he was very helpful and patient during office hours. He only had two midterms, which was rough. His first midterm was ridiculously hard, the second midterm was manageable, and the final was in between in difficulty.

Kun is a very average teacher. He gets the material across but only focuses on computation and not the actual mathematical concepts which can be confusing. His lectures are always the same, but very boring and hard to stay awake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Wang was an incredibly good math professor with a slight language barrier from time to time. His explanations focused on understanding a concept as a whole instead of how to just solve a problem. If someone ever had a question, he would go out of his way to give a good explanation. His homework load and tests are manageable as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is a little hard to understand, but he tries his best to liven up his lectures. He seems to really care about his students and their performance. His tests  are largely based on understanding concepts rather than difficult calculations, and he gives generous partial credit on problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is extremely nice and even funny; however, a language barrier holds him back a bit. His lectures consist of writing definitions, doing proofs, and going through example problems. His accent can make it hard to focus, depending on the person. Homework is graded closely but fairly. Tests are "okay," but don't follow the homework much.

I would definitely take this professor again! The course material is challenging but office hours are incredibly helpful and quizzes and homework help to make up for low test grades. By far my favorite professor this semester.

Wang has a thick accent, so it can hard to understand him, but at office hours he is very clear and explains the concepts well. He assigns mandatory homework which is a bit annoying, but it's good practice. He is a tough grader on the tests. Overall, if you want an A, you're going to have to really work for it.

Kun is a great professor who is always ready to help when you need him.  His test can be tough, but they are def manageable if you pay attention and do the work. He's always helpful and clear even though it is sometimes difficult to understand him. Also expect weekly quizzes and weekly mandatory homework. He will also curve the scores up  sometimes

There is a small language barrier, but he is good about writing everything on the board so that you can understand. Quizzes every week but you can drop two, graded homeworks every week but you can drop three (and they are easy and answers available online), and three tests that aren't too hard. Take him!!!

Kun is pretty hard to understand but mathematically it doesn't have any real impact because he can explain those concepts. Only graded problem sets once a week (other homework is optional). Class is boring but he goes over important problems.  Tests are similar to in class problems but were inconsistently hard.

Good teacher overall, though some things he says will not make sense to a normal English-speaking audience. Fun teacher and if you do the homework (of which there can be a lot), you'll generally be prepared for the weekly quizzes. Don't expect to be able to ace this class solely because you took Calculus in high school and did well.

Professor Kun is very caring and helpful if you are willing to put in the work for the class. As long as you attend lectures, complete ALL homework, and go to office hours, you will learn a lot. However, the tests are difficult and are often much harder than the homework and quizzes, and he doesn't provide many test review resources.

Awesome professor. The tests were pretty challenging, but definitely fair, and he was generous with partial credit. Although it seems hard to build a relationship with him, he does genuinely care for his students. Office hours are helpful. He's patient and willing to spend time. Encouraging, funny dude. Hope to take again.

Loved this guy! He was an exceptional lecturer, and his tests, though slightly challenging, were always fair. Attendance is not mandatory, but questions on the tests are always very similar to examples he does in class and homework questions.

Professor Wang is a super nice guy and really wants his students to succeed. On occasion he is hard to understand and goes very fast during lecture, but he is extremely helpful and clear in office hours. Grade is based almost entirely on tests and attendance does not matter.

There were only three levels of Russian language courses when I attended VU, but Dr. Kustanovich nearly made me fluent in the language. He may seem stern, but he's got a delightful, maybe eccentric, sense of humor, that one will come to see over many courses with him. Fabulous teacher. I can't remember another teacher so great.

Easy teacher. This class can be taken two ways - one you can come to class and do nothing cram before quizes and take notes off other students for exams and get an A - or two you can study and learn something and study and get an A. He seems like the kind of professor who does not care, and lets the class sort itself. Overall he's a good professor.
Very interesting class.  Meets once a week for a long time, but the work is not bad and requires no prior knowledge on the subject.

20th-cent. Russ. culture is the worst class I've taken at Vandy. You don't cover anything besides books, movies, and art. No sports, music, theatre, etc. 2nd, he is the most subjective and unfair grader. I gave the same test answers as a friend and scored a whole letter grade higher. He is unclear and sinfully boring. Don't take this class.

He's the nicest guy you'll meet at Vandy with a great sense of humor and really fun anecdotes. That said, he makes the Russian language much more incomprehensible than it really should be. He's an easy grader, but if you really want to learn the language, he can be really trying. He also gives about half a billion quizzes, sometimes one per day.

Once you get past the accent, he is easy to understand. He is pretty easy on grading, so as long as you get the general concepts, you will do fine. If you try in the class, you will pass, and if you show legitimate interest, you will probably get an A. Definitely take his class.

Let me start by saying that he's a great guy. That being said, he is a pretty inept professor. Obviously he knows Russian but that doesn't mean he can teach it. Basically a grammar course. 3 months in he still hasn't taught days of the week or how to say bathroom, but at least I can use the genitive case? Unless you're a native speaker think twice.

Some weeks there is nearly a quiz everyday.4 tests after each unit. No final, can miss up to 5 days. Vagueness over what the quiz will cover is a problem which sometimes occurs. Further,sometimes it seems he expects you to know things which have not yet been formally taught, which is frustrating. Class is marginally bearable.

Best professor ever. May seem intimidating at first, but he is SO kind. If you are enthusiastic about learning Russian, you will do well. The class is filled with lots of discussion in order to help you master topics. Class meets everyday, allowed to miss 5 classes. If you study and pay attention in class you will do great! Favorite class at Vandy!

Konstantin at first appeared intimidating, but he really is a great professor and wants his students to succeed. At the end of the semester he had us all over for dinner at his house. I learned a lot and I highly recommend this class.
She is overall helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Korsnack is the best english professor I've had. She goes above and beyond. She allows unlimited revisions, so there is no reason to not get an A. When going over papers, she provides amazing feedback. The readings are not only interesting, but short and sweet. You are graded on participation, but it's not hard to show up. Take her if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Korsnack is a great professor. She taught and implemented essential formal skills, while exposing us to more informal types of writing. There are unlimited revisions for each paper, and she is easily accessible outside of class to discuss what went wrong in prior drafts. In other words, if you try, there is no reason to not get an A.

Professor Stacey doesn't establish a formal attendance policy. He still takes attendance on some days. Exams are a little tough, but nothing unmanageable. Make sure to study the details of his slides. He gives engaging lectures, as he is very passionate about what he teaches. He is also very caring and understanding towards his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's a nice professor. His exams are a worded kinda poorly, so tougher than they need to, but still fair and not difficult. The course's content is easy, and he's happy to help. Just make sure to pay attention to some niche details in the slides, and you'll be fine.

Prof Stacey is super nice and is 100% willing to work with you outside of class for help. My only complaint is that assignment due dates (labs and homework) change all the time so you never know when you need to have it ready.

Dr. Stacey gave incredible, engaging lectures. Lots of required reading, three fairly challenging exams, and one paper, but tons of extra credit opportunities and support outside of class (including zoom exam review sessions the night before).

I loved SOC 1020, so I took this class and realized just how harsh the grading actually is. The exams are difficult with very tricky MCQ; Both times I went to office hours to discuss my scores, I had points added back due to improper grading. The exam format is not a great way to test our understanding. Glad this is my last Stacey class.

While the course is an introductory SOC class, his exams are much more difficult than necessary; multiple choice questions are very nitpicky and harsh grader in general. That being said, he is a nice person. I know a lot of students that were looking to take the class for an easy A, but ended up getting their GPA knocked down bc of this class.

Professor Stacey is an amazing professor who is very passionate about the class. His lectures are engaging and insightful. The class is part lecture, part student-led discussion which is where a lot of participation comes from, so make sure to talk. Overall great class!!

Professor Stacey is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had. I was in his sexuality section of SOC 1020 and I couldn't have loved it more. He's super engaging and really cares about his students enjoyment of and success in the class. He's also easily reachable outside class. Highly, highly recommend taking a class with him if you can!

This class was indeed challenging, Professor Stacey emphasizes it being a 3000-level course. With that being said, he is a thoughtful professor who is deeply invested in his field. Please note that this class includes a cumulative final. I would say an A is hard to achieve in this course, but if you work hard it's possible.
I have nothing but great things to say about Professor Stacey! Take a class with him if you can.

Professor Stacey is awesome. He's young so he really cares about his students and is willing to adjust parts of the class to make it easier for us. This class had two exams and one non-cumulative final, one paper, and four discussion posts. Lectures were very interesting. I was in the sexuality section so I highly recommend that one!

Plate is fantastic. He gives 4 representative practice exams per midterm and goes over great worksheets in class (don't skip). Office hours and review sessions are also super helpful. His videos are organized well. I supplemented with the textbook for a better understanding. Be aware of long midterms (~11 pages for 50 mins), so know the stuff well.

Dr. Plate is amazing! Flipped classroom style, but the videos are divided into subtopics, so theyre rly short. Exams are difficult, but with enough studying theyre not too bad. He provides lots of practice exams! Took this with Orgo 2 and it was not that bad. While his part is more chemistry, there wasnt any overlap with orgo 2. Wonderful dude :)
PLATE IS MY GOAT. Biochem is hard, but he has great videos and explains everything very well in office hours.

very kind, lecture videos were great for covering content and I liked that I could return to them if I needed to, really focused on the applications of content which is always very interesting but can make assignments challenging

Plate is so so inspiring and knowledgeable. He goes above and beyond. His lectures are flipped, which can be annoying but he uses class to go deeper into concepts/do practice problems which is very helpful. His tests are very very difficult but doable if you do the practice tests well in advance. Go to his office hours they are really helpful.

I absolutely hated the flipped classroom from the intro stem courses and was hesitent to hear that Dr. Plate was using it for class. Unlike those previous classes, Dr. Plate made great use of students time in and out of class and was always more than willing to give feedback and help. Biochem has lots of content, but he does his best to prepare you
The lectures are decent, but I found him to be very condescending. I was counting down the days when the class flipped to a different professor.

Plate is an amazing professor and wants his students to succeed. The course has a lot of material but it's super interesting and as long as you put the work in, it will be fine. To help with this, Plate has many practice problems and exams to make you comfortable with the topics. Exams are fair, and project rubrics are clear. Overall, a great class

This is an extremely information dense class, but Plate does a good job breaking it down and showing how different topics are interconnected. To be successful, you MUST practice every day. Even if you start studying a week before the exam, that probably won't be enough time to cover all the material. Solid curve at the end of the semester though.

Awesome and down to Earth.  Always available to help answer any questions.  Class was challenging due to the high volume of material, but the concepts themselves were fine.  Make sure to practice the mechanisms every day.  Practice problem sets and practice exams were reflective of the actual exams.  Focus heavily on the slides for studying.

Biochem is hard- there's no way around that, but Plate is an exceptional teacher and I found the class to be very manageable (comparable to 1510). That aside, Plate is extraordinarily caring, and really want his students to succeed. He goes out of his way to learn every name in a 100+ person lecture. You will need to study, but exams are reasonable
Really solid professor and he cares a lot about his students

By far my FAV prof here. Very caring, smart, and great at explaining, if a lil awk. Stays after every class to answer any q's. His content is super organized and in a flipped classroom style: short videos to learn then do problems in class. A lot of content but I really enjoyed learning bc he made it very clear and included ties to current studies.

Plate teaches difficult classes (biochem and other advanced chemistry) but is amazing. Class is not easy because of content itself but Plate is super accessible, doesn't talk down to you, and makes everyone comfortable asking questions in class. Honestly one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Tests are based on his lectures not the book

Love him. A little awkward, but is a great person and is extremely helpful. Attendance is not taken, but you will do so much better in the class if you go. He recommends the textbook but honestly just go to class. Only a hard class because of the amount of information covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer, is very good at describing complex mechanisms clearly and at highlighting what is important. Tests are tough (it's biochem), but he does a good job of preparing you for them in lecture and with all the practice tests he gives. One of the better biochemistry professors. Really nice and approachable guy too.

I had Dr. Plate for the first part of Biochemistry and really got the feeling that he cares about his students and their learning. Biochem isn't easy, but he always emphasized exactly what parts of the book to refer to and what to focus on. I also immensely appreciated that he gave us 4 practice exams from previous years. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Really interesting class that covers both fundamental concepts in chemistry/biology and cutting-edge research/lab techniques. Dr. Plate is clearly an expert in the area, and he provides practice tests and ungraded hw that make studying for tests pretty straightforward. Highly recommend!

Very hard class if you havent taken biochemistry. Be sure attend class for participation points. Lectures are very dry and truly not that important. The practice problems and tests are helpful. Office hours and review sessions are fairly helpful but not crucial

Dr. Plate's course is great! Tests are kinda hard, but definitely managable if you study beforehand. He holds a review session before every test, and his slides are super helpful for learning the material.

The course material is so fascinating and applicable to actual lab experiments. Really heavy on memorization, but he posts his very detailed slides so its easy. You have to do a flash talk on a paper at the end of the semester, which brings the course material to life. He also does test review sessions which were so helpful!

Dr. Plate is smart and communicates pretty well. Lectures are super dry, and 8 in the morning makes it worse. However, he draws mechanisms out well so they are easy to review on your own. Likes to ask some straightforward and some critical thinking questions on exams. Super cool material.

Dr. Plate is highly knowledgable about his research field and breaks down difficult concepts into digestable bits. His tests are similar to the practice tests, but definitely not easy if you don't understand the lecture materials at their core. He's a great human being and loves talking about his research to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Plate for bioorganic chemistry. It was his first time teaching but Dr. Plate did an amazing job. His lectures were pretty clear and he was always super helpful in office hours and willing to meet outside of them. He's also extremely nice and knowledgeable about the subject. Overall, I highly recommend his class for the science-inclined.

Dr. Rolen is very engaged with the material and students. He'll always have a fun fact or related concept to throw in. Did you know that the Boy Surface sculpture at the Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach is the background to several famous mathematicians' Wikipedia pages?!? I didn't! Anyways, lecutures are great and tests are fair.
Just a good professor who really cared about his students
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Although number theory will always have a special place in my brain's trauma center, Rolen is my favorite math professor. The class is all proofs, but he's good at teaching. He's willing to meet with students and help them succeed. The tests were really hard but there was a curve. Don't take NT if you want an easy class (it's hard, even for math)

Linear algebra is a tough class, and Dr. Rolen is shows signs of being a young teacher occasionally. however, he is very open to feedback and improvement. Tests are tough but he curves the class very nicely. show up to class, his lectures reflect what he wants you to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is very bright. He gave good lectures. The first test is hard as hell. The rest of the tests will be fine. Work hard and grind ur ass through this course. It's hard in Vanderbilt. Get used to high level Math courses. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: In Larry's class, I keep telling myself it's the material, not the professor. I struggled tremendously in the class, with every word of Larry brings me new questions. However, from his intellectual high ground, he could do nothing but repeat his lightning thinking process with tones of pity.

Prof Woods is AWESOME! Taking an 8am can be daunting, but I genuinely looked forward to going to class because of how awesome she is. Almost always ends class early, does fun activities in class (like watching movies related to soc). Her exams do reference the readings, so make sure to glance over those a bit before.

This woman is a GEM. The class is pretty straightforward and she makes the lectures pretty engaging. She sets an expectation for her students, but she is very caring and will acknowledge you outside class and have her door open if you are having any issues that will impact your performance in the class. She also tells great stories from her career.

Prof. Woods is one of the easiest professors at Vanderbilt. As long as you show up for class, you're set to pass with an A. Her slides are pretty vague, though, so you'll have to review the textbook for exams but everything else is lightweight.

Prof. Woods is so kind and caring, and has cool personal stories as a former cop. There are a few papers, plus a midterm and a final, all of which is cake & you can skate by without doing the readings. You DO have to go to class/be punctual every day. Overall, I learned a lot, she was super chill and I'd highly recommend this class to anyone.

Professor Woods was so so chill and she responds to emails quickly! If you want to do well, just put some effort in and getting a good grade won't be difficult. At least skim the readings since their content comes up on exams, but she also discusses those concepts in class. Participation is mostly personal-experience based, so speak up!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Woods is amazing! Her deviance class was one of my favorites at Vanderbilt because the topics covered are important and interesting. Dr. Woods isn't here to harshly grade anything, she wants to see her students succeed so they can use the content in class and apply it (or at least understand it) in the real world. Will be taking her again!

highly recommend for easy A. you do have to show up for class because of in class assignments but she lets you out early almost every class. don't buy the textbook or any of the books I never read them and did very well with little studying.

Super chill professor who you can tell really just wants to make this class as manageable as she can for students. Fun stories, pretty interesting guest lectures, will tell you everything you'll need to review for exams. Super lenient as well. Just make sure you show up! It would be pretty difficult not to do well in this class otherwise.

Attendance is really the only thing that matters. If you show up on time, you will do well. This is by far most important. You don't have to do any readings to be successful. Essays and assignments are graded very leniently. Midterm and final are also graded very easily. Lectures are interesting and she has cool stories to tell. Highly recommend!

Attendance is required. That's about the only way I think you don't get a good grade in this class (if you skip class or are late). She's the sweetest woman ever, has great stories, and the class content is relatively interesting. Paper are super easy. Readings are also not really required. Could not recommend taking her enough. Truly a gem.
My favorite professor at Vandy. She is so nice and caring. Pay attention in class and study a few days before the exams and you will do well!
EXCEPTIONAL
Amazing professor. She made her expectations for exams very clear. She gave amazing insights on the topics. I learned so much. Take this class if you can get in (it gets filled up quick).

Be ready to do ALOT of reading for this class, but the content isn't too hard to get (and Prof Woods is a SUPER fair grader). There are a lot of little essays throughout, but they're short and relatively easy. Overall, Prof Woods experience as a former officer offers really interesting insight into the content and makes the class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Fav prof at Vandy. She is just awesome. I try to take one of her classes every sem. She brings so many personal stories from experience which is super cool. Doesn't accept late work, but the assignments are straight forward, shouldn't give you trouble. This class didn't even feel like school, TAKE TAKE TAKE!!

Dr. Woods' intro to sociology class was great. As a premed, I couldn't be happier that I chose her as my professor. She has some incredible personal stories, and I felt engaged throughout the entire course. The papers were pretty short and there was no cumulative final exam. I even almost changed my major to sociology while taking this course!

SOC 3333: Professor Woods is amazing. Your initial impression of her might not be the best because she comes off as strict and unforgiving, but that is not the case if you are an active participant and care about the class. Homework is kinda light, consistent amount of short readings and writing responses. About four essays total. Very fair grader.

Can Laurie Woods be my grandma? She is a gem; I recommend her to any Vandy student. Extremely easy coursework with minimal work outside of class (just short summaries of each reading prior to class). Values the process of learning rather than the grade -- and I can say, with confidence, I've learned so much. Don't let her demeanor deter you! :)

Really easy class if you need your liberal arts credit. The tests were just based on the ppts and lectures and definitions from the book. The presentation was just a speech and the paper was easy once you did research for the speech. Woods was a great teacher and the lectures were really interesting. The class was even better if you participated.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super easy class, just a couple of writing assignments, a debate presentation, and 3 exams total. The exams were a little open ended but leniently grades. Topics were interesting and overall some terms have been  pretty helpful for MCAT so far. Take sociology with her if you can

Professor Woods is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. She really cares about students and he classes are very discussion-based which makes them exciting. You'll never be bored in her class and she has a flexible attendance policy. Definitely recommend taking all of her courses!

Has interesting guest lecturers, sometimes talks about her own experiences in policing, is a chill grader, and tests are just what's covered in class. Only reason to not take her class is if you need to have your phone out during class. Many small group discussions/regularly encourages class participation, in a good way.

Very easy professor! She can be a dry lecturer at times, but as a prior police officer, she brings a unique perspective to her field of work. For our class, she wanted to bring in more relevant news, so she allowed us to present individual topics in class that would drop a grade or final. Sweet and very cool.

Dr. Woods is a wonderful professor. Her goal is for students to learn, not stress about excessive workloads and meticulous grades. Everyone in class is engaged with the material, and she encourages everyone to think critically about the topics and their application to the world surrounding us.

Amount of work definitely fluctuates but decreases throughout the semester. Graded on 3 short response papers, a shortish paper on an outside event, a group debate, 3 exams, and participation. Exams are easy if you go to class, pay attention, take good notes and study textbook terms for a bit before. Learned a ton and highly recommend this course!!

You really have to show up, and read but great if you can. Unfortunately due to personal reasons missed many classes and was not able to make up everything, which lead to a grade poorer than my ability. If you can do everything I would recommend her.

This review is actually for SOC 3333 Policing in America. Woods is an incredible professor. I gave the course an average score because the last month or so up to our final presentations seemed a bit repetitive/boring, reiterating what we already learned. But we still learned a LOT, without needing an insane amount of work.

The lectures for Juvenile Justice got boring and redundant after a while. I would even suggest to not read the book because a lot of the material is the exact same but the exams are very straightforward. That being said, it is easy A and the topic itself still interesting.

I absolutely loved Professor Woods! Her Intro to Sociology course was easy, fun, and interesting. I actually looked forward to her class every day, and it was one of my favorite courses at Vanderbilt. Dr. Woods is genuinely caring, too; I feel like she really cares about all of her students. A true gem!!!

Woods is the coolest professor ever. Criminology was easy while still engaging. Participating helps your grade and also makes the course more fun. If you have a persona interest in this, you'll want to do the assignments anyways. She also brings in real experience from working in Narcotics which is awesome.

Intro to Sociology with Woods is literally a must-take. As long as you show up, it's probably the easiest A at Vanderbilt. Very little homework, outside of three small papers. Readings assigned for most classes, but I never did them and was fine. Study guides for every test that pretty much ensured you knew what to expect.

She is super sweet and quite the interesting lady. Criminology was a great course- easy tests and a few creative papers- just make sure you show up to class on time and don't use your phone (she gets pissed). Really dry textbook though, and you have to read at least some of it. Her experience in the field adds a lot to the class. Highly recommend!!
Only inconvenience is that participation/attendance are graded. Material is interesting, tests are easy, gives some extra credit, and professor has a great story. Zero complaints
Great faculty VUceptor for my Visions group. Looked forward to seeing her, very approachable and caring.

Took soc just because I heard it was a great class taught by a great professor. Not wrong, and I'm very glad I took her class on crime and media. You definitely learn a lot, and it's a pretty easy class if you are attentive to lectures and show up to class.

She's pretty nice and grades essays really easily. Memorize the study guides and review the slides for tests and you'll be fine on those too. A pretty easy A as long as you do all the work. The only problem I had was getting to class on time and she will get mad at you if you skip a lot or are late (skipping hurts your grade a lot).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She gives three tests, one debate/paper, and one outside paper. Class is only mandatory for certain days. She's so nice and has super engaging lectures.
amazing class and teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Woods is a great professor with an interesting background. Her classes are as engaging as you want to make them, and she highly values attendance and participation. She's an easy grader, and you only need the book to study terms for the exams. Super accessible outside of class, and genuinely cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Woods is a very knowledgeable and experienced professor, so her class was very enjoyable. Tests are easy as long as you take notes in class and read the book. She really hates cell phones and will call you out for it!

Would definitely recommend to get this pre-med requirement/recommendation out of the way with her. Extremely easy class, very hard not to get an A if you put in marginal effort. You do basically have to go to class to get the participation points, though.

Woods is such a nice lady and her class is very interesting. I just took it as a class for premed reqs, but I found it a lot more interesting than I thought I would. Tests are very fair, but you have to at least skim the readings (which can be lengthy) and come to class for extra credit and completion assignments for attendance. 1 midterm, 1 final.

I love her and this class. She's very experienced, intelligent, and caring. Plus, she's super chill and reasonable. There's one group project and some short papers. She's a lenient grader but participation and attendance are really important, as is note-taking because the slides aren't posted. I highly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is an interesting lecturer. Very down to earth and conversational. This is an easy class but it requires a lot of work- easy work. Attendance is VERY VERY important because the in class assignments count towards your grade. Plus its an 8AM which makes it hard to always be there. Tests are easy and she tells you how to study for them with guides

We watched a lot of videos, which is to be expected with a Commons seminar. I feel like I didn't learn much, though, and she never put grades into the grade book, which left you in limbo whether the class was really easy or you weren't doing the work correctly.

You have a chapter each week for but for the tests you just have to know basic concpets vocab. she covers some material only in class, but gives STUDY GUIDES so you can ask if you missed class. Papers are 3 pages max and she's a lenient grader (i've gotten all A's so far). really just a great class and worth the 8am- interesting life story too!

This class is easy, only for students who know American culture well. As an international student, I struggled a lot. The grading for paper and debate is very lenient. However I often felt the lectures boring since I did not understand much about what she was talking about. Exams are impossible for me even after thoroughly reading.

Dr. Woods is very nice, but a confusing professor. Her lessons are very vague and her exams are the same. Even when we study for hours, the questions are usually irrelevant to the course and textbook material.

I LOVE Professor Woods! She is so invested in the material and the class is so interesting! I didn't mind waking up at 8am for her class! Also, it is very easy! She grades the papers pretty easily as well. She gives study guides which help a ton with the tests. TAKE HER CLASS.
Love her so much! She is super nice and the class is super interesting. She is the one that makes you get up at 8 a.m. for the class.
Great, helpful, and easy

Woods is a great teacher! She really cares for the students and wants students to learn. She puts emphasis on life applications and not just theories so more interesting. Easy, interesting class that everyone should take.
Best teacher ever loves athletes and is so chill ad relaxed

Lauri Woods is incredible.I learned so much from her class!Her class is set up for you to thrive and learn an incredible amount.She engages you and makes you excited about assignments. Her lectures offer a real-world appeal to it, which most classes lack. Take her and prepare for a magical experience.
One of the best professor's I have had at Vandy. She is very helpful and nice, and her lectures and stories are actually fun to hear. I promise that you will love this class and Professor Woods!
fantastic professor and person! Highly recommend

Also took SOC 231 with her, and will take SOC 270 with her next semester. She's so great. I love her teaching style and she makes it so interesting. She's helpful and incredibly fair. One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt by far.

Great teacher; lectures are fun, grading is easy, and she really makes it possible for you to enjoy the class. I've had 2 classes with her, and both were great. You learn a lot without having to cram, and she adds real life experience to the textbook material.

Absolutely AMAZING! I could not imagine going to Vandy and NOT taking a class with her. Have had her twice just because she was that great...I seriously recommend that everyone take at least one class with her!
Fantastic teacher. Friendly, fun, and exciting. Great class.
Great professor. not too much work, but you still learn a lot. lots a quizzes, but you'll get an A as long as you do the reading. take the course!

In the Jackson Moore pairing, this is definitely the perhaps easier half but the weaker professor. Dr. Jackson's lectures are rather boring and her tests have focus on niche application questions. I wouldn't describe her as forgiving in terms of grading/expectations but do think she's a good teacher and would recommend her+moore over any others.

Dr. Jackson is super student-focused and clarifies her expectations for what to know. She explains the material really well and obviously wants to see you succeed. Exams were fair - super similar to the practice exams she gives. I didn't do as well as I was hoping in this class but - her co-prof is much harder.

Dr. Jackson gets a lot of hate but honestly she is not that bad. She is super clear about what her expectations are and teaches the material really well. A lot of people don't like her because she tests on application and won't just give you points for complaining. She also has 8 points of extra credit. Beware of her co-prof though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: all science classes here are gonna be a nightmare. but i feel like jackson made it a lil bearable. no need to read the textbook. use class notes, suggested hw problems, and practice exams to study. and u gonna get 80+ on her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Loved her. Class is definitely a time commitment, but definitely manageable with effort. Be prepared to ask her questions after class, that was probably the most useful thing for me.

Pre-recorded lecture videos are not very helpful so you have to read the textbook. She's passive aggressive in her announcements and her answers on the discussion board were largely unhelpful (if you have questions ask her in-person after class). MCQs on exams were mostly fair but nothing can prepare you for the FRQs. Exam 2 easier than exam 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
She is very passionate about biochemistry. However, she is evil.

Read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible. Grading criteria not clear. She is rude. Take the other section.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not responsive over email and takes months to get around to regrade requests. Exam grading criteria is arbitrary and unfair, especially free response. Prepare to lose 10 pts on exam 2 if you don't perfectly estimate the y intercept of a graph. One of my favorite classes in terms of the actual material, but still had a horrible experience overall.

She's a decent professor for this class. If you come to lectures (VERY important) and watch the video for the lecture right after lecture and take good notes, youll be fine. By far the best study material is the prev exams, sometimes exact questions. Its a hard class so prepare to spend at least 6hrs a week studying content.

She is mother. Only reason why you should take her and BADgandi together. She genuinely cares for students, explains concepts very clearly, and doesn't throw any curve balls at her students during exams. She wants her students to succeed. Don't listen to other ratings. They are just mad that they actually have to work for a grade!!
Run for your life, if you want to save your gpa

Smarter than Bagandi from what I can tell, but equally stubborn and useless when you have questions. This class is out to get you; you will be cheated out of points on exams, homeworks, and quizzes. Hope you are good at estimating x and y intercepts visually from a graph printout -- perfect guess required for 6% of exam 2 grade.
I hate this class so much, very not clear.

Dr. Jackson is one of the funniest, kindest professor's I've had at Vandy. This class was taught "journal club style", and it was by far the easiest BCB class I've taken. You have 2 group presentations, 2 take home exams, and a short final paper. You do have to talk at least once per class (she tracks this), but you could also get extra credit.

Keep in mind that the only people who rate on this site either did very well or very poor in her class. The low rating likely comes from the latter. I didn't do as well as I wanted, but I much preferred Dr. Jackson's teaching to Dr. Plant's. My only complaint would be her smug attitude at times and answering questions with "what do you think?"

Her portion was just pre-recorded lectures where she just repeated whatever was in the notes, and she covered a couple topics in class just repeating what she said again. Inconvenient times for office hours, was rude/unhelpful in discussion board, and overall super difficult tests. Would not take again.

Dr. Jackson for Biochem II was great. She's super nice and much more relaxed with this class than 2520. The biggest thing is participate, that's where you can lose the most. Besides that only 2 exams, averages were in the 90s for both exams, and an in-depth ppt on a scientific paper. Final is a short 1000 word article on a paper of your choice.
Flipped classroom and reused all old Covid lectures. Coming to class is usually a waste of time. Very condescending and doesn't seem to care at all. Horrible experience
One of the worst lecturers I've ever encountered. She is very unapproachable, condescending, and belittling.
Both Dr. Jackson and Badgandi are worthless professors.

Dr. Jackson is smart prof. but her open ended questions are nowhere from any book or class handouts and graded inconsistently. Dr. Badgandi is a crazy guy, he should not be teaching at Vanderbilt. Do NOT take Jackson/Badgandi for 2520. Take the other section.

She seems like a good professor at first, but she can be very moody. Also, her online exams were absurd compared to her in-person ones and the free response grading was very arbitrary. You have to have certain phrases word for word to get credit. Expressing the same idea in a different way gets no credit.

Dr. Jackson made her online tests unnecessarily hard and they did not reflect the material covered in lectures or class. I got an A in organic and am barely passing this class, it's a toss up of if you can correctly guess the answer to material you've never seen. She had so many people needing to discuss grades she sent out a google form instead.

A third of the class has either dropped or in the process of dropping. Tests are a disaster. I get the difficulties with the online class format, but if a third of your class is bombing your tests this badly, halfway into the semester, then the problem lies with YOU, not them.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She does not care about students. I had to withdraw and am completely devastated.

I am a senior with premed and I had to drop this course. I am completely devastated. I never received anything below A- at Vandy but this course was a killer with unreal expectations. My career is ruined. I don't even know where to restart.

I had a lot of expectation about this course but I may have to withdraw. The email she sent to the class was outrageous. Insufficient lecture objectives. Exams did not reflect the lectured material. Dr. Badgandi does not teach or explain anything. I feel like I'm going to have a mental breakdown.

She will never respond to emails. Arbitrary grading of free response questions. I am a senior and am totally devastated. She sent a pretty insulting email to the whole class and practically asked students to drop BSCI2520. The other section under Dr. Brame is doing perfectly fine and this section's class average in 60's. Are we all stupids?

Dr. Jackson is a very good lecturer and you will learn a lot from her class. The multiple-choice on tests were very fair for the most part, but the free-response sections were graded almost arbitrarily. This keeps the test averages around 75.
