As others have said, she is pretty unresponsive to emails, although she probably receives quite a few.
class was a mess, not designed for the online format. would not recommend

Actually a decent lecturer, but it doesn't matter because the grading on the tests is so arbitrary. She's completely unreachable by email, so not only can you bomb exam questions for no real reason, there's absolutely no accountability for whether the answer was ever even wrong or right. You couldnt pay me to take her class again.

I am getting As in Organic Chem and all other Neurosci courses but this course is a killer. The instructor is smart but she can't teach. Moreover, she does not care about undergraduate students. TAs are not helpful at all. Can you imagine a trimodal distribution of scores in this class ?
This is the worst teacher at Vanderbilt. Open ended questions are clueless.
Terrible teacher.
The average is now below C- the class has no connection with exams. I had no clue about the open ended questions.
She does not respond to emails. The class average for the last test was 61%. Her free response questions were brutal. She looks for some terms, didn't give credits if I wrote in my own words.

Honestly, the hardest class I've ever taken. However, she makes the journey easier by being accessible. Sometimes, she can seem pretentious (always mentions Cambridge) but her teaching skills are absolutely amazing. Go to office hours even if you don't have any questions because other people will, and that kind of functions as a reality check.

Phenomenal professor. Biochem is undoubtedly hard as a subject, but Dr. Jackson takes great care to ensure her students truly understand the material she teaches. Her lecture slides are clear and concise, and she asks very probing questions in class that sometimes work their way onto exams in some form, so don't skip lectures.

Dr. Jackson is a great professor. She makes it very clear as to what she expects from her students. The book is very helpful, if you want to understand the material better. However, it is not necessary to do well on the midterms. For the fist midterm I memorized a lot of details, while I spent half the time on the second one, to get the same grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was definitely the hardest I've taken so far at Vandy. There is a lot of memorization and we are sometimes tested on stuff from the book that was not in the lecture. Would recommend Eichmann if you're looking for an easier class. Dr. Jackson really cares about her students and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Jackson is the best professor I've had at Vandy. She's brilliant, kind, and she cares deeply for her students. Her lectures are clear and precise, and she always answers questions with clarity and ease. Yes, her exams are challenging, but her teaching gives you every opportunity to succeed. If you truly want to learn biochem, take her course.

She told us we didn't need to know anything that wasn't on the slides but tested us on information from the textbook. She is a tough grader who takes points off for the slightest mistakes. Class averages for her portion last semester were around 60% while Brame's was around 70-80%.

This professor is really rude to his PhD's and undergraduate researchers. I foolishly wasted time acing his course to try to do independent study with him. He ignored most of my emails and was a jerk overall. Definitely would not recommend (I am now at JHU for a PhD in the ECE department).

Dr. Massengill treats his undergraduate students like they are complete professionals. Extremely useful approach to the material. Dont be late to class. I really appreciate how he treated this course. Not easy material

Very interesting class. A lot better than Electronics 1. Just a note, never show up late to his class or take out your phone. He gets really pissed and after a few times will lower your grade. However, I learned a lot more because of this and still highly recommend taking this class. The design project is fun too

Probably the best prof I've ever had. He made the class super interesting. He's super passionate about the subject and engaged us as much as possible (giving out candy for holidays). I loved attending his class even though he doesn't really take attendance. Class is super easy A. Would totally recommend!

Professor Candelaria's lectures are super interesting and engaging, and he is very passionate about the subject. You get to watch several musicals in class and share your thoughts through discussions and a few short essays (which he reads himself to get to know his students). No formal tests. It's an easy A as long as you produce good work.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class to fulfill HCA, professor is very passionate about the subject, class is overall a very easy A, would recommend

Professor Candelaria teaches with passion and is clearly excited about teaching his students. He grades very leniently and the only real work we had to do outside of class was four short essays. I learned a lot about opera from his lectures, and that's really what matters. You can do very little work and get an A, but I enjoyed attending anyways.

Amazing professor, his love for opera makes the lectures fun and interesting, even for someone that doesn't listen to opera. Grade is 5 light reflection papers, and half attendance (show up as much as possible, talk sometimes). Would love to take class with him again.

Doctor Candelaria is an extremely fun and kind professor--he points out aspects of musicals that may otherwise be overlooked by audiences. Cass was graded by five papers (500 or 750 words ea.) and "attendance." He doesn't take attendance, but go to class; he works hard to make it engaging, so please respect his time and effort.

Well, he honestly grew on me a lot as the semester went on. You'll get the A if you just go to class. Started talking about random stuff that was kinda funny as time went on. You could really tell he truly cared about his students and does try his best, even if his best is not being an incredible professor. Take him and you will be fine in the end.
Very vague on assignment guidelines and harsh grader. Also picks on students if they do not participate or skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he just rambles about his personal life rather than actually teaching sociology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this guy. He goes off topic and rambles forever, makes uncomfortable remarks and blurts out whatever thought crosses his mind. Didn't learn much at all from him.

I'm not going to lie he is an acquired taste. He graded our paper exams himself though and he did not give absurd grades. We have reflections every week about the assigned readings and discussion of the week which he didn't grade, the TA did. He doesn't stick to the assigned syllabus and he does not have a standard/formal grading rubric.

Do not take with Lloyd. I think l had a particularly bad semester but he is a nutjob. Don't know if he graded a single assignment it was always our TA, which was honestly better because he would've written an essay. I've never hated a professor more and my class bonded over our mutual hatred. Not super difficult to do well, but not worth the effort
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Insanely rude & heartless. I missed 1 week of classes bc I was hospitalized. TAs were very understanding but Richard could not tolerate my absences and gave me a 0 for missing the assignment due that week. TAs gave us assignment break after a midterm, but he told me "wasn't my idea," gave me a 0 for that assignment too. Something's wrong with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very interesting guy, but he loves what he does and his energy makes you want to learn.

Dr. Lloyd is a funny guy with a love for anything bollywood but his lectures were so disorganized that I do not think I learned anything from them. Discussions were not engaging and readings were long and boring. You are graded on 3 midterms (or so he said but he just cancelled the last one because “we worked so hard”). Gives extensions if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Lloyd is extraordinarily passionate, well-versed in the subject matter, and willing to work with you on an individual basis to make a project of your choosing work. He's super funny, very kind, and appreciates effort above all. Course structure is subject to change, but no surprises. You learn a lot from him and it's easy to get a good grade.

Professor Lloyd clearly wants his students to understand the course material. His lectures are fun and engaging. However reading through his lengthy and frequent emails was sometimes hard, especially during the exam periods. Overall I do recommend him, he is a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: easy grader with few assignments. clearly passionate about the materials but his lectures are very disorganized. he doesn't manage class time well. he sends you a few emails every week with thoughts and reminders that range from encouraging/thought-provoking to lowkey kind of rude or concerning.

Overall, Dr. Llyod was a decent professor. He cares about the material he presents; however, his lectures are pretty boring. There was about a total of 13 papers all equally weighted. Three were graded harshly, as they were seen as "exams." However, the other 10-ish papers were three-page reflections that would automatically get a 100.
Did not give clear instructions, and lectures were hectic
Good! Lots of personal experience sharing in the lectures!

Professor Lloyd is a very engaging and hilarious lecturer. He assigns a good amount of reading, but the class is only graded on weekly current events (auto 100% if u hand in on time), two midterms, and one final (can be optional if satisfied by current grade). Very entertaining class, but you must take good notes to do well on the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lloyd is extremely funny and nice. His lectures are pretty entertaining and the class is pretty chill . Just 2 midterm exams, current events and the final exam are the bulk of the grades. Overall a great class.

Professor Lloyd is a solid teacher. Some of these other reviews don't do him the justice he deserves. He is dedicated to his students' success, and will always be willing to help at office hours. If he is aware you are putting forth effort, you will do well in his class. Just try your best and pay attention during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Lloyd is not teaching this course anymore to my knowledge. It is clear he wants students to critically think, and I enjoyed the lax attendance policy/ completion-grading on the reflections. However, I have never been more confused in a class. Lecture slides are convoluted, get ready to teach yourself (YouTube videos/ using SparkNotes)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the first class at Vanderbilt where I genuinely felt challenged (but not discouraged). You need to read to be successful in this course. Despite the lack of structure, his lectures contain important details you need for exams. Class is graded on two 30% exams, a 25% final, and 15% reflections. The prof cares about you; ask for help!

His class lacks structure which complicated my understanding of some topics. He is a tough grader and he looks for specific things in his papers, so utilize office hours if you want to make an A in this class. Lots of readings. To his credit, he is easy to talk to and genuinely cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I disagree with a lot of Professor Lloyd's negative reviews. This class ended up being one of my favorites to attend. The class definitely starts off more difficult, but once the material gets more relevant, the readings are actually pretty interesting. While Professor Lloyd did sometimes talk about some random things, his lectures were great!

I have no idea what to think of Lloyd. At the end of the day, he is an intelligent and knowledgable professor who clearly cares about his students learning and future. That is not to say that sometimes he can say some out of pocket stuff under the license of his know-all. And be a harder grader. But he will talk to you and make you feel seen.

Not 4 everyone. Lecture is entertaining but personal. And goes overtime. 2 much uncovered reading. He's also into ppl's backgrounds. Whether he cares abt his students, wants 2 b accessible, or is just being intrusive depends on perspective. (personally not for me). But some ppl seem 2 like it. Best description for him overall is Chaotic Neutral.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: A really quirky, funny, and provocative professor who deeply cares about the wellbeing of his students. His lectures are relaxed yet engaging and informative, given he doesn't go on the occasional tangent. If you show up to class and ask a question or two in office hours, you will be able to answer the exam questions and succeed in the class.

Lloyd's classes require you to pay attention and engage in more than just what's on the board. His papers are extremely open ended and require creative engagement with the topics of the class in other areas of art in society. This is very much a class for which you'll get out what you put in, so don't just look for a grade or you wont get it.

Really awful professor. Lectures are incredibly disorganized and very unclear grading criteria. Most of class will be him talking about his own opinion/life. You're better off not going to class. Do not recommend.

I've taken Lloyd's class over the course of two years, got some good grades and some bad grades. Nevertheless, he is the best professors I've ever had. He's passionate and genuinely cares about his students. Strongly recommended. Some ppl personally attack Lloyd bc they didn't get an A, and it's disheartening to see all the groundless accusations.

Lloyd is the worst professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He made a lot of personal remarks that were wildly uncomfortable to hear in class, he assigned a ton of readings and then barely addressed them, and papers were graded with little commentary on actual writing ability. I don't think I learned literally anything at all or grew as a writer.

Prof Lloyd is a really fun and engaging lecturer. He makes a huge effort to make the lectures interesting and to apply the material to topical issues (including Lil Nas X & BLM). Lectures are definitely disorganized/sometimes hard to follow, but you will NEVER be bored. His class always puts a smile on my face. Class material is very difficult tho.

Professor Lloyd is very unfocused and did not adjust well to Zoom at all. He often goes off topic to things that do not connect to course material and his comments hinders class discussions when students are actually trying to engage in in-depth discourse. I regret wasting my time in his class.

Professor Lloyd is very knowledgeable about the content of this course but struggles to present it in a digestible manner for first-time readers of these foundational texts to the Sociology discipline. There are 3 10-page papers- each worth 30% of your grade. He likes engaging with students but lectures can become unfocused.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There were two 10 page papers and I tried my hardest on both of them. I spent hours on each. He gave me a 7 on the first one and a 12 on the second one. And when I say 7 I mean 7 percent. (7/100) Terrible teacher! Would not recommend him. I went to office hours and he told me I had the two worst papers he had ever graded in his entire life..... oof
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Lloyd is the best professor I've had so far at Vanderbilt. I felt I had stagnated for a while in my writing ability and professor Lloyd really helped me overcome that plateau. He gives honest and unbiased feedback and is an overall stand up guy. Take his writing seminar.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is good at some topics but not able to clarify some other topics. Lectures are boring and not very intellectually inspiring. He often spends class time discussing pop culture tv shows/movies/celebrities, which is useless and waste of my tuition. I will try to avoid him.

Really interesting class that focuses on societies accent to modernity through readings of Kant, Smith, Marx, Weber, Durkheim, Simmel, Freud, Du Bois, and Rubin. The main grades are two 10 page take home midterms and a final. Lloyd is an interesting lecturer who clearly explains the material. Descent amount of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lloyd is a fantastic professor; I'm shocked how many people have rated him poorly. Lectures are incredibly engaging and feature a great mix of humor and clearly presented information. Class has two 10-page midterm essays and an in-class final exam; the test subject matter is high-level, but he explains each prompt multiple times. Would recommend!

He was a good professor, really interesting and knowledgeable. He told my class some good stories like the time he went to Drew Barrymore's birthday party and his research in rough areas of Chicago. If you're on his good side and contribute to class discussions, you're good.

I don't understand all the hate for a great professor. The reading is mostly New York Times bestsellers, and the syllabus is front-loaded so you do most of the "tough" reading in the beginning. The papers just have to show genuine engagement and ability to make connections between the readings. An easy and interesting class taught by a great guy.

The toughest A I've ever worked for, this class was possibly the most satisfying college course I've ever taken, because I knew I earned every inch that I got. Prof. Lloyd is knowledgeable about his subject and determined to knock it into his student's heads. He assigns as LOT of work. He's tough, but FAIR. He will go the extra mile to teach.

Overall a decent professor, Lloyd is the kind of teacher that knows a lot about his subject, but does not always know how to relay that knowledge to students. At times he can be pretentious and occasionally that gets in the way of teaching. However, he rewards hard work and effort where it is deserved, and has some pretty awesome stories to tell.

He is very articulate and knowledgeable, but tends to go off on tangents in his relatively unclear and disjointed lectures. Despite this, discussions are interesting and the class readings (warning, there are a LOT) are interesting and I learned a lot. He expects a lot of writing and reading from students - beware. But if you try, you will do well.

Lloyd expects absolutely unreasonable things from his students.  From the unnecessarily long reading assignments that generally have nothing to do with globalization (the supposed theme of the class) to the daily 1000+ word "emails" as if he were a middleschooler sending texts to his crush, his class is comprised solely of disorienting tangents.

This class is entertaining and interesting if you enjoy art and music. Prof. Lloyd can come off incredibly narcissistic at times, especially when talking about his books, and the class can drag on. It's the type of class that you question why you signed up for it, but in the end it's really not that bad. The work is manageable.

If you're looking for an easy class, this isn't it, especially in the beginning. However, if you do what's assigned and make an effort to contribute to discussion, you will be rewarded. His frequent emails to clarify things are extremely helpful as is recording lecture to listen to again. Overall I really enjoyed this class and would take him again

The two previous posts are completely inaccurate. Yes there's some writing, but to be honest if these students can't handle what Lloyd assigns, then they shouldn't go to a school like Vanderbilt. Lloyd is an amazing, helpful professor. He is constantly engaging students through emails and is always open to talk during office hours.

If you are looking for classes do not take them with this professor.  if you a are already in a class with him drop immediately.  this class involves 8 2-3 page papers, 2 6-10 page mid terms a final exam 6-10 pages and an extreme amount of reading, not to mention Lloyd is the worst professor on the campus

exactly the opposite of what you would expect of a vanderbilt professor.  If you are a freshman and get stuck in his class DROP ASAP! He lacks the ability to communicate with students and is very self centered.  He lectures a class of 17 because no one wants to take the class.  Avoid this professor at all costs!
He's fabulous!  And just wanted to give him his deserved chili pepper.

While the material isn't challenging, he tends to get off topic very often. His main research focus is the artists of Nashville so he goes off into that all the time. The classroom discussions were interesting, however. My biggest problem was that he was never really available to help at all.

ridiculous grader. he says he is politically unbiased but it's painfully obvious he's a staunch liberal (and if you try to be conservative on the midterm he will shoot you down flat). he's into himself because he writes a bunch for the nashville scene, and he likes to think he's pretty hip. class is extremely boring at 8am. do not take this class!

His class, while challenging, forces you to look at the world in new and unique ways. He draws comparisons that don't seem to make a lot of sense in the moment but ultimately become clear on the midterm. Class is never boring and he is really approachable and fun.
Tons of reading. Participate on his class and you'll get on his good side, which makes his grading much easier.

Lengthy readings. Syllabus is Attendance/Participation: 5% Current Events: 10% Midterms: 30% each (2) Final: 25%. midterms and essay are easy if you basically copy what he says in class or in the readings. 8 current events which are easy to get a 5 on.
This class can be very ambiguous, and reading can be pretty big chunk. Intense reading for sure.

Awesome professor! Lloyd is funny and is a great lecturer. Though many people often sit silently, he definitely likes the people who talk. All of his tests are take home and are pretty straight forward (i.e. synthesize the material). The final is a 2 hour in class essay. Definitely recommended!

immense amount of reading but interesting.  Lectures are not very organized. Not much work besides reading except weekly current event analysis (not hard; graded easily). Participate in class but if you arent liberal, he won't like u as much as the vocal DEMs in class. Tests are toughly graded out of class essays. Crazy final. 3 in class essays.

Interesting material, current event due almost every week, he is helpful, tests are pretty straightforward essays if you do the reading and attend class. He likes if you use his office hours and speak up in class
I had zero interest in this material before I entered the class - I only took it because it's required.  However, I really enjoyed this class and found Prof. Lloyd to be very helpful.
I'm not a SOC major, but i still found the topics interesting. Some of my classmates found the reading very difficult. Prof Lloyd is very candid in his comments and language.
good! its a fun class

The test structure is particularly difficult, since it extends over the weekend and he expects your responses to be eloquent and encompass all of the points covered in class. However, he gives you the information that you need. If you read the books and go to class, you'll do well.
not recommended
not good
RDL is fantastic

Lloyd is the reason I became a soc major.  Contemp Amer Soc was sooo interesting!  He seems kind of disinterested in his students but we had an amazing TA who was always VERY helpful.  Lots of awesome class discussion.  He keeps the class interesting.  Not an easy course, but the best class I've taken at Vandy.  I would retake it if I could!

I've taken numerous classes with Professor Lloyd. He may come off as a jerk or aloof, but if you engage the material and go to class you should be fine. He is the reason I decided to major in sociology. I almost never read anything and never made less than an A-  in any of his classes. Very brilliant man and rewarding classes.

The Urban Community class is very interesting, yet, I do not recommend this class to anyone who is not a sociology major.  I took this class to fulfill axle and I had a really hard time with it.  He gives take home tests, but is an extremely critical grader. Nice guy but HARD class to get an A in.

Great professor, hard paper grader but makes up for it on the final. wants to meet every student and is always willing to discuss papers or any problems you have with the class. i highly recommend taking his class

The topics are SO interesting!  He is pretty unintersted in his students though.  Most of the contact you'll ever have with him outside of class will be thru his TA.  If you want help on an essay, Lloyd is not really interested in talking to you, but the TA is available and cool.  REALLY REALLY interesting class though!  Lots of reading.

I have taken two of Professor Lloyd's classes. Professor Lloyd is the reason I declared Sociology as one of my majors. He is absolutely fascinating and has wonderful insight into society. Lloyd is pretty demanding but if you keep up with the reading, you should be completely fine! If you want to be in a life changing class, take his!

Did not like this professor. He always seemed annoyed with the students and acted like all of their comments in class were stupid. He is pompous and a jerk. Treats students like they are annoying and not intelligent unless you are one of the few in class who is a favorite.  Expects way too much reading. Semi-difficult grader.
This is the kind of class you think is the worst thing that ever happened to you while you are taking it, but you look back on it with the fondest of memories.

Great class. Really fun professor. You get to read NYT Bestseller books instead of a boring text. He gives you the essay questions for the tests in advance. As long as you prepare answers to the five possible questions, there is no reason not to do well in the class. He also requires eight 2-page reports on current events.
There were interesting parts of this class but I hated going.  He isn't helpful to the class and discussions are pressed.  Not what a freshman seminar should be...
No Comments

Hard class, but an excellent professor. I am sure that he wasn't trying to impress the previous reviewer, because Lloyd is just brilliant. He loves the material and is truly passionate about ti. One of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt!

this urban community class was a TON of work.. he spoke very properly/eloquently and used a lot of big words as if he was trying to impress us. the class isnt too bad as long as you know what hes looking for. he gives you a study guide that pretty much covers what you need on the tests.
hes so funny. hist 1000 was my hardest class but my favorite. dude is hilarious, kind, and incredibly smart. NOT an easy A, but no busy work either. just a lot of memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: His class was genuinely a gem, and he makes every lecture seem like a stand-up routine. The tests were very memorization-based (you have to know a ton of dates and proper nouns), but it is still possible to consistently do well. He does rush through the slides at the end of class, but ultimately, it is definitely worth taking the class.

Probably shouldn't have taken him for my semester ever in college, but I think it was worth it in the end. The tests are insane amounts of memorization of very loose details, often not specified by him. And the lectures can be disjointed yeah, but he's still really funny. I would take him again for the giggles

Look, yes he will go on tangents, yes he will rush through slides, is the class going to be straight forward yes, will you have to memorize some dates yes, but its not that hard just memorize and show up for the tests super easy.

I loved the class content and the professor but oh my gosh the nature of the tests were near impossible. A TON of memorization of the tiniest details, which I thought would be no problem but I was fighting for me life to get good grades. Great course, not an easy A.

Professor Lorge is simultaneously an extremely entertaining lecturer and the hardest professor I have ever had(and I am a stem major). His tests require you to know many details like dates original language vocab and events. In retrospect, his tests were fair but most people got caught off guard and screw up the first test, making an A impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Lorge is very funny. However, he gets kind of distracted during his lectures which sometimes makes them hard to follow. Attendance isn't mandatory so a lot of people just didn't go to his class. Tests are a lot of memorization of minuscule details, but the papers were easy (basically like an APUSH essay). Really understanding and caring guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is all lectures. Prof Lorge is a funny guy and is generally generous on grading, but be prepared to memorize crazy small details like dates and names for the tests which makes it kind of impossible.  3 tests and 4 2-page papers

I really enjoyed his lectures.  He was very engaging in class.  You can tell that he knows what he is talking about.  I think that he could teach many other classes because of his thirst for knowledge.  Additionally, he was very clear on his grading criteria on both essays and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This prof is the worst I've ever heard of. He is so bad I am writing it on behalf of my roommate. The amount they complained about him and the absurdity of his class inspired this. Whatever you do, don't take a class with him, tell your friend not to take a class, and overall just avoid him at all costs (but recommend it to somebody you hate)!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although Lorge is a great guy who is quite funny, taking Western Military History was a large mistake. As a 1000 level course, I wasn't expecting tons of reading along with the bombardment of material each lecture. This class was based on tests based off memorization, making it impossible to balance with other (more important) classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Prof. Lorge for his Western Military History class, which was one of my biggest mistakes ever. It is anything but an attainable A. He expects you to read hundreds of pages of reading and be able to remember tiny details from them for the tests. During lecture, he will go on long tangents then speed through the material he tests you on. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely hilarious.
Solid choice, very nice and straightforward
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Veers off during class and then summarizes the material in 10 min. Tries to be funny but then everyone gets screwed on the test. Do not take him, you will regret it. So much memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: To sum it up, Dr. Lorge is an entertaining lecturer. He also veers off topic quiet a lot. Tests were somewhat reasonably specific as long as you watch/read everything assigned and come to class. His final paper expectations were vague. His paper grading is not too harsh, but few things contribute to the final grade, so every point counts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very concise and clear grading outlines. Took him for History of Tea (Amazing Class). With out a doubt one of the funniest profs I've had at Vandy and he is asking you to do work, but it is VERY manageable. If you stay on top of your work and don't leave studying till the last minute it's very easy to do well. Great guy in lecture and out of class.

At first I worried Dr. Lorge was jaded or cynical or something, but it's actually just his sense of humor, which comes up quite often. I studied by writing down major events and dates 3-4 hours before the tests, reviewing the powerpoints, and rereading my notes, and it wasn't hard to get an A. Readings are interesting but not totally necessary.

Lorge is actually one of the funniest guys and made everyone laugh multiple times every lecture. Class was on topic maybe 40% of the time. No work or reading necessary. Essays are free points and take 20 min, tests are extremely easy (just have to know dates and significance) if you study for an hour or two. TAKE THIS CLASS.

Dr. Lorge was my professor for Chinese Thought. His is an excellent teacher who makes class worth going to. He always makes class fun and teaches in such a way to make you think. The class was based on 6 papers, which if you apply yourself, were not too much work and were not graded harshly at all. I will definitely take another class with him.

Lectures- boring. Homework: 4 easy paper with 5 paragraph form; grading not that hard. Just remember to do your readings and prepare for the exams. He uploaded everything so u do not even need to go to class.

Professor Lorge is a really fun lecturer. He's super animated and knowledgeable and he jokes around a lot, especially with the kids he's taught before. Crisis Sim is a must-take class: super fun, really unique, and extremely easy. I started each assignment within two hours of the deadline and never got lower than a 90.
Interesting and uniquely structured course. Very enjoyable. Minimal work except for the simulation recaps. Great class and professor. Co-taught with Professor Benson in the PSCI department.

Very hard tests with no leeway on grading. Interesting class though. He's funny but gets off topic a LOT so I always have something else to do in class when he starts to ramble. The readings aren't really necessary. All the info is on his powerpoints which he puts online

If you have a head for names and dates, you can do well in this course. He does not provide study guides, so you have to sift through 8-10 chapters per test to find the names and dates worth memorizing. Studying for the tests is very time consuming. Lectures are generally interesting, though.
Huge amount of memorization.

Probably my favorite professor ever. Professor Lorge manages to make almost anything interesting, and every lecture is worth going to. Only assignments are tests, for which the only difficult parts are memorizing dates. He is very fair in returning points that his TA's take off of the tests, and it is easy enough to get at least a high B.

I typically don't write on these things but had to correct his rating. DO NOT take his class unless you have a STRONG interest in specifically Chinese history. I have an impeccable memory and worked my butt off for a B+. He makes you memorize who wrote random irrelevant passages that you read once. I love history, but even this was too much for me.

Professor Lorge's class was really great.  The large historical time period did make it feel like we didn't learn as much, but that's because his lectures are very topical.  The textbooks have all the fine details.  His lectures also had themes that could be applied very widely, such as historiography and concept development.

He's a good teacher who spends a lot of class trying to make jokes. The humongous time period covered means you feel like you learned nothing about Chinese history. Tests are very hard to do well on and depend on memorization. HW really isn't very necessary to do though. You can squeak out a B without doing many HW readings and if your lucky a B+.

Bar none my favorite professor at Vanderbilt.  Is his class challenging?  Yes, but he makes the material so interesting that you want to do it.  He's excellent at putting things into everyday terms.  Not an easy A, but he is outstanding.

Favorite professor ever! For real! I Western Military History with him was amazing, and he always made his class interactive and hilarious. Tests were hard, but that is really just because you must memoize dates. Other than that, they are not bad.

Prof. Lorge is so funny in class...I always looked forward to his lectures because I knew no matter how bad my day was he'd make me laugh.  His exams, however, were not as funny.  He was also helpful outside of class for explanations, etc.

the hardest teacher EVER EVER i had to drop this class when he told us that only TWO students of his have ever received A's in his years of teaching, and that sometimes he accidentally writes in Chinese characters. RIDICULOUS.
Lorge knows everything there is to know about his specialties. He's funny, but he might offend you. His tests are tough so you absolutely must cram for them.

Lorge is quite self-centered and very dedicated to China.  He often tries to be funny in class and, succeeded in making it entertaining and informative, though his schtick can get old.  He has a tendency to wander off topic, particularly in dishing out dirt on the administration.  To do well, attend class, copy the slides and memorize your notes.

If you are going to take a Lorge class, take 130. The subject matter is interesting and Lorge definitely knows how to teach it. Memorization of dates is required for the tests but the 130 is (apparently) way easier than his other classes... 4 hours max of cramming dates = easy A's

This was his first semester teaching the class, but he really knew his stuff. You're likely to be insulted by something he jokes about, but everything else is funny. His tests are hard hard hard, but if you study enough, you'll be fine.

Definitely not a great professor by any stretch of the imagination.  Most of the class consists of Peter Lorge's personal comedy hour in which he makes mean and unoriginal jokes at the expense of other people, social groups, professions, etc...
Hilarious. looked forward to his class everyday, but  his class is difficult. You'll learn, you'll laugh, and you'll cry a little each time he hands out grades.
Lorge is awesome. His class is not easy and he grades fairly tough, but for history 200 you should take him. Most importantly, he is funny as hell.

Good guy, His grading varies from class to class.  Hist 200 is pretty fun with him and I actually learned a ton.  He really understands the historical method and knows how to teach it.  Plus his rants make class go by quick.  all in all, a good prof.
Very funny, good lecturer, very helpful, not terribly easy

Had him fall 03. Hard grader (we had no tests, only papers). Other people think he's funny, but his jokes are repetitive - spent about 25 mins per class whining about the administration, which got old very quickly. I'd give him a 3 overall - not horrific but nothing special.

Unless you want to spend hours memorizing trivial dates and regurgitating them onto exams, don't take this class.  It is the bane of my existence, and I wish someone had let me know this before I enrolled

This guys classes are WAY fun. BUT you'd better copy down every detail from lecture AND you'd better spend about  8 hours or so cramming every detail from class for the tests.  The readings aren't a huge source of test material necessary for an A.

Lorge's class is entertaining because he's a pretty funny guy.  But beware, his tests, though very straightforeward, require endless hours of preparation.  In his own words, usually only one student earns an A.

Hard. Very Hard.  Wants small details (ie dates and people's names).  Lots of memorization. However, the class was very entertaining.  He's quircky but has great jokes.  Easy to get him off topic.  Knows his Chinese History inside and out though.

This is your standard Spanish teacher. Nothing special, but she is also really sweet. The class average for our class was an A-, but if you try just a little bit, you can end with an A. There are short readings and homework between each class that take around 20-30 minutes total.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Lorenzo Garcia is very sweet and her class was a lot of fun. She did grade the writing harshly and the class focuses on a lot of grammar. Overall was a lot of fun and she created an enjoyable classroom environment.

Professor Lorenzo is a very sweet woman, and her class was run well and had good classroom banter. It feels as though most of the learning was done outside of class through the assigned readings and homework. Very little lecturing took place during class, and explanations were hard to come by. She was very accessible and understanding, though.

I didn't appreciate Dr. Lorenzo-Garcia. She was very emotionally driven rather than professional when you would not meet her standards. She also singles out students, making them feel  small in front of their peers. She does not have clear answers to in and outside of class. She also puts grades at the last minute. I do not recommend her.

I absolutely loved class with Professor Lorenzo-Garcia! Class was so entertaining and she is so kind and funny and supportive. There are definitely a lot of assessments (oral exams, written tests, and essays), but it is super manageable if you show up to class and participate. There is also extra credit to get a percentage up in your final grade.

She's really funny and nice. the class was hard for me, but spanish in general is. I think if you j want the class for the credit maybe take an easier prof. The tests are fairly hard and she doesn't always explain things the best. Once I got used to her style of teaching it was better though.

I absolutely LOVED her and looked forward to going to class. She truly cares about her students' understanding of Spanish. She made class so fun to the point that our entire class would erupt in laughter. Of course Spanish is gonna be difficult, but that has nothing to do with her teaching. She's great.

Senora Lorenzo-Garcia was a great Spanish teacher.  As someone who came in less experienced, I felt like she cared about my success in the class.  It is a difficult class, but she was very helpful and accessible outside of class.  I originally took this class for credit, but I am going to take 2202 with her next semester.
Homework is very easy, but she does not give any expectations for what she wants on written assignments or tests.

Professor Garcia is perhaps the single best teacher in the Spanish department. She cares very deeply for her students, is constantly bringing her all to the classroom, and does everything to promote learning and success. There is lot of self-learning due to the standardized curriculum, but she does her best to navigate through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is averagly difficult cause its Spanish. Since classes are standardized, this is due to the class and not the specific teacher. Alicia is literally wonderful. She is super nice and really values in-class participation. One way to get on her bad side is to consistently be late to class. If you get on her good side, it is the best feeling

Alicia is a great teacher. She is super energetic and makes class fun. The spanish classes are standardized so there's not much difference between teachers. She is a fair in her grading and as long as you get on her good side, getting an A shouldn't be too difficult if u put in some work

Profesor Garcia structures her classes completely irrationally. You are forced to teach yourself all of the concepts and material as homework the night before the lecture. Following this, she solely uses all of the questions asked on homework to teach in class and has you pair up to answer the questions. Professor Garcia cannot teach or grade.

Prof Lorenzo is a decent class to take. She is a tough grader on essays and tests a little above average in difficulty. Class is mediocrely engaging if not completely unorganized. She really doesn't do a lot of teaching and you are responsible for a lot of material that will be tested on. She is not very clear in her expectations in anything.

Prof Lorenzo has been awesome. She's high energy which makes her class fun, and she makes it easy to participate. She also speaks a lot of English in class. There is VHL homework every night and a few papers and oral quizzes to supplement the tests, but none of it is particularly difficult or time consuming.

I loved her and her teaching style, but the workload was pretty crazy. I know it's a W, but every week we would have daily homework and papers, along with MindTap. It was super interesting and I loved the class overall, but I wish this class had been less about nit-picky grammar and more about the art of writing in Spanish.

Sweetest Spanish prof I've had so far. She really cares about your learning. A few big papers with revisions and three unit quizzes which are easy to pass if you pay attention. She makes grammar really simple through lectures. Solid choice for 3301W.

Shes so sweet. She loves teaching and cares about her students and helping us succeed. She keeps class fun and interesting, but is also insanely knowledgeable about Spanish grammar. Shes definitely tough, but supportive. Class was very hard and seemed harder at the end, but is manageable. Be prepared to write, and study the grammar  2 quizzes.

Prof. Lorenzo is the most caring person I've ever met. She makes the class as fun as possible every day and her attempt at English is honestly adorable. While the class is fairly difficult and there is a lot of daily homework, she is great at explaining tough concepts, and she is even more helpful in office hours. 100% would recommend.

Prof. Lorenzo is a very nice person and can explain many aspects of the Spanish language quite well. The only downside of the class SPAN 3301W is that sometimes there might be too much homework to do in a very short period of time.

The homework in the class was unbearable. The professor means well, but it's simply too much for a 3 hour class. I talked to other students in SPAN3301 with different professors, and their classes are much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Alicia is such a sweet lady. She completely cares about you, and really pushes you to learn Spanish. So she gives you a lot (and by this I seriously mean a lot) of HW. But, you really improve a lot. Be aware that many students who take this class have Spanish as their mother tongue, or have been speaking it forever.

Alicia is an amazing professor and she is so funny. She is super sweet, and I think she genuinely wants students to learn. She is a tough grader, and gives out A LOT of homework. Too much. Staying actively engaged in class is the key to survival and success. Again, tough grader if you aren't "amazing" but mediocre at Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Even though this class was pretty difficult, I really learned a lot. At times I was frustrated because it felt like she was grading us as if we were native speakers but she was only trying to make us better at writing in Spanish. Definitely not an easy A, but definitely worth taking for anyone interested in furthering their Spanish education.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Profesora Lorenzo was overall a solid professor, but she's a really tough grader. Getting an A- is relatively easy, but an A is almost impossible. She's funny and sweet, and she cares a lot about her students, but sometimes it seems like she really does pick favorites. A lot of pointless homework and not a lot of communication. Iffy choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She really grew on me as the semester went on. Such a sweet lady, especially during office hours. She grades about as hard as the other Spanish teachers. If you take your time with the essays you'll do great in the class. The daily homework, though, is excessive. I guess it has to be for a language class, but it's not fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is really funny and sweet. She genuinely wants her students to do well. Participation is a big part of the lecture but it is not hard to participate at all, and if you get something wrong it's not a huge deal. The class was set up very much like a high school Spanish class w/ small, easy nightly assignments and infrequent bigger assignments.

I actually love her. She made class 4 days a week bearable with her humor and love for music videos at the beginning of class. The tests are super hard though, and you've got to know the grammar in order to do well on the them.

Great professor--very approachable and helpful during office hours. Tests are difficult but she has a lot of assignments to balance out low test grades. Keep up with the online homework; it will save your grade! Also, this class is a lot of work for a 100 level language class, but most of it is doable. Overall, a great experience.

One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. She is the sweetest lady you'll ever meet, and she really cares about her students. I've had her for three classes, so I owe a big portion of my Spanish knowledge to her. Reviews saying she is mean are wrong. If you respect her and care about learning, she is wonderful!

god this woman is horrible, my entire class hated her. try your best to not take her class. she makes it hard for people to get anywhere in the A range (she personally told us this on the first day of class)

AMAZING professor. Will bend over backwards to help her students. Fair amount of English allowed in class, and workload is reasonable. Wants all her students to do well and makes class fun. Must have for Spanish!!

This lady is the sweetest lady you will ever have teach you spanish. She loves her students and wants them to succeed. Tests and standardized and not hard. Homework load is resonable. She allows a good amount of english spoken in class. She is always willing to help outside of class. There were 2 pop quizzes (easy) during semester. Great teacher!

Makes learning Spanish as fun as it can be.  Exceptionally nice person, and very helpful if you make an effort.  Homework is graded kindly, but you'd better know your stuff for her tests.  Beware: This Spanish class is taught exclusively in the language.

Lovely woman and clearly passionate, but class is dry at times. HW is a lot of work and tests cover a LOT of material, but she's very kind and understanding. Wasn't my most interesting class, but really appreciated the effort she put in so that it wasn't always lectures. Super cool prof, though!
Rude and unprofessional. Talks poorly of students to their peers behind their backs.

Homeworks take forever & lectures are not engaging. She might call on you to answer a question in class so stay alert. Semester long group project that has to be submitted to a national competition. Quizzes are extremely specific and address obscure things from lecture slides or activities that no one remembers. Textbook chapters are long & dense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Troxel is a very understanding professor. I think the class was pretty boring and a lot of math which sucked but I think that's out of her control. She really cared about her students and what they had to say.
Way too much work for a module, somewhat disorganized in her lectures and thoughts. Nice lady though.

One of the nicest professors on campus. However, TA Gourab needs to go. Does not read the assignments students submit, gives random grades, and identical feedback to different students. If the TA is changed, I would highly recommend this class.

Very disorganized. Does not really care about the students. I am sad that I have to take this class. I felt like it was a waste of money. Vanderbilt charges thirty thousands dollars for tuition, yet has teachers won't really don't care about you.
Love her but this module was a lot more work than the others. Really interesting though!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Troxel was a really nice professor. Her class was very structured, which I honestly liked, and not especially exhilarating, but I had a nice time. Going along with the structure, she really cares about formatting and presentation of assignments. It is easy, but I do feel that she gave more assignments and work than my other modules.

Really wonderful professor. She cares a whole lot about her students, and really loves to get to know you if you reach out. She does a really great job of making complex material easy to understand, and has very reasonable expectations of students. Learned a lot in her class. She wants you to succeed, so reach out!
Troxel is very nice to talk to, but the module was kind of boring. Not completely her fault, more so the subject matter. Concrete dam stuff went smoothly, class was easy as expected.

I took three freshman engineering modules and this class was by far my favorite of the three. Troxel is very well respected and really cares about her students. We had a few homework assignments and a final  which consisted of a group project where we built and tested a dam. It was low stress , yet a lot was learned about civil engineering.
Class was pretty easy. Show up and get an A. A few easy homework assignments were done, but they only took 15 minutes max. Would recommend as a good intro into civil engineering.

She was incredibly helpful in office hours. There are "projects" every week or so that are like homework assignments, but much more intensive. If you do poorly on something, talk to her, and she'll more than likely allow you to re-work part of it for partial credit.

Troxel is undoubtedly the best option for statics. Annoying group projects but they aren't hard to get good grades on and help boost your overall grade a lot. Tests and final are very straightforward.

Possibly the best professor I've had in college. She is crazy nice and really cares about how her students do. The material in the class is not easy but if you do all the assignments and homework you'll get an A. Grades easily but there is a lot of work.
One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt.  If you have the option to take statics with troxel, take it.

Troxel is probably my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. She really cares about you doing well. Surveying is not interesting, and she makes the material exciting and fun. Follow the format carefully for labs and you will do very well.

A lot of group works and projects. She's helpful, and most often her door is open if you need any help. But she's not that good in explaining the material in class. However, she's very clear of what her expectations are, so listen carefully and you should have a good idea of what's going to be on the tests.

Crazy about being on time- would give pop quizzes at 9:10 and if you got there at 9:11 you got a zero. She gives lots of stupid projects and homework is do every single day. Overall, she's ok- nothing special.
seems really awkward at times but overall a pretty good teacher, homework is due pretty much everyday and the tests are similar to the homework problems and she's good about giving partial credit

She's a decent teacher at best. I don;t understand what everyone likes about her so much. She's a nice person but not particularly good at teaching this subject. She also has a TERRIBLE grading scale. PS. to the person below...nobody asked what your grade is so spare us from you solipsistic bragging. thanks!
The homework is what you'll spend time on, but it's not worth much. Study for the tests and you should be fine. She's really fun and nice.

I loved her class! she teaches like a mom (i.e. she babies her class)... we listened to music sometimes in class and watched monty python one day. i have a 97 in this class right now. if you do the homework and take notes, you'll get an A. she's really really clear about the material too
No Comments

Overall a GREAT teacher. If I had a choice between a teacher at 11am or her class at 8am, I would probably take hers. Tries to make things fun (but usually fails but still gets a laugh out of the class) and seems to be nervous teaching the class but still does a great job of doing it. If you ever need help, just go to her after class of her office.

Probably one of the best teachers I have ever had.  It is not an easy class, but if you attend and do the homework it can be.  She is not only a great teacher, but funny and cool too.  You almost have to make an effort to do badly in this class.

One of my favorite classes and teachers in my 4 years at Vandy. She is unbelievably nice and even good to talk to casually outside of class. She is very clear, concise and fair. I wish she taught more of my classes
She's the nicest and most flexible professors you'll ever run into.
Troxel is definitely the best for this class, shes clear and grades pretty fair.
The course sucks but she is a very fair  teacher.  Her tests are easier than the other sections.  Easy B, but somewhat hard to get an A.

Troxel has a smart, clear, and logical teaching style that any engineer would appreciate.  She has a genuine concern for her students and is uber cool.  Do the homework, participate and you'll excell.
if you don't like to participate in class, stay away.  otherwise, she's great.
Dr. Troxel is very clear and a very straightforward teacher. If you do the work, you should be able to get an A
This class was very well taught, if you show up to class and did the homework, then you should not have trouble doing well.  She broke down everything pretty well.

Surveying just sucks sucks sucks.  But CE's have to take the class and she's the one who teaches it.  Its incredibly boring and is only offered at 8am.. she gives daily quizzes/in-class assingments just to make sure kids show up to class.
Sucks, just sucks.
Lots of fun, just a down to earth person!  Her class can be hard, but she's a great teacher and very cool!

Despite the small size of the class, the professor never made it clear what we needed to be prepared for the numerous core assignments we had to complete. He was also rarely accessible to discuss it, and never updated grades until the end of the semester, meaning negligible feedback.

Despite the small class size the instructor failed to provide consistent or constructive feedback. Expectations were unclear, with little guidance on improvement. Grading was excessively delayed and incomplete, and several assignments were never graded. This neglect compromised the academic value of the course and demonstrated poor professionalism.

If you are going into the Arts and Sciences and are looking for a professor who teaches the mandatory CORE class, Being Human, this professor is one of the worst cases. He grades things late and never helps anyone with assignments. If you end up with him, expect to have the most anxiety inducing class you will ever take. Avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid. I got sick and told him I wouldn't be able to make it in for my presentation, but I still did the work/recorded it. He told me I'd have to redo it on a completely new topic and said he was doing me a “favor” not giving me a 0. If you don't have the same left-wing opinions as him, you're wrong. Just a classic bad spanish professor.

AVOID!!! I have NEVER felt more self conscious about my Spanish abilities! I asked for help on my first paper, he was not helpful and the prompts are very vague. When I turned it in he made me redo it bc he said that my interpretation was wrong (not the same as his). I asked how I could improve and he literally called me illiterate to my face.

Just don't do it. He made people rewrite essays if they had the wrong poem interpretation. If you don't interpret a poem the same way as him, you're wrong. I have never felt so self conscious about my Spanish. He made me teach class for 30 minutes without warning or preparation. AVOID

Dude Prof. Luis is so brilliant! He is incredibly smart and you will learn a lot. Yea, his essay assignments are vague, but it gives you more wiggle room and you can always ask him if you feel something is unclear. He's easy going and will help you in anyway he can. If you get a bad grade it's because you didn't seek help. Take his class!!

Prof. Luis is a great professor. He is very passionate about what he teaches and class is very engaging. It can be tough at first because you must speak during discussion, but it truly helps you improve your Spanish so much. Read and participate!

Such a sweet guy! His class is very discussion heavy, but I have gotten so much better at speaking and understanding Spanish. The workload is very reasonable and he is a very engaging professor. You definitely have to do the readings for each class if you want to do well, but as long as you actually try and participate you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: An authority in his field, with his own unique take on the texts under discussion but open to interpretation and discussion, elicits the best from each student. He is funny and makes the class entertaining. Sometimes hard to follow, but this is because of the brilliant connections he makes.

Professor Luis obviously knows what he's talking about, but his class basically just consists of him trying to get specific answers out of students instead of an organic discussion on the reading. His essay guidelines are non-existent, and he grades harshly if you do not give him exactly what he wants. Smart guy, unnecessarily stressful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is so engaging and passionate. Yes, he doesn't give super clear guidelines on essays but I've gotten As so far just by writing specifically about each line of the poem, essentially replicating class discussion - which is what he asks for. He's an expert in the field and pushes his students to do their best. I would take a class with him again.

The topic -classic Spanish lit-is obviously dull.  Prof. Luis makes this stuff interesting.  He's a REALLY smart guy, charismatic & engaging in class.  The downfall actual grades part -his expectations are not only unclearnon-existent (no rubricassignment sheets), & he expects interpretations that are way diff than what we learn in APIB in HS.

This class was awful. We spent the entire semester doing poetry. He expects you to have a strong background of Christian knowledge. If you do not have this background, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS you will have a very difficult time knowing what is going on
Very disorganized. I had the feeling that he did not prepare. Seems like a nice guy but the class was boring to levels I did not know before!

Energetic and passionate about his work. He challenges you to interpret stories outside the box, so if you are an English major, you will especially love him. Class is structured so you interpret poems first, then longer stories (VERY helpful!). Exams are essay-based. Challenging but never dull, this class was one of my favorites.

He is great! Almost everybody who was in his class this semester tried to get into his class for next semester. You have to get used to him, because he seems kind of grumpy at first, but the discussion in the class is really good.
No Comments

Dr. Lupu is very smart and highly accessible in office hours. While the lectures and readings can be a bit boring, the content itself is interesting. The TAs randomly deduct points on the assignments without much justification but it is not difficult to get an A. Class structure is very stress-free, and there are extra credit opportunities.

I think some of the reviews of Lupu on this site are a little harsh. His lectures are slightly boring but they are interesting if you do the readings beforehand. The TAs do grade harshly but if you follow the rubrics it isn't too bad. Helpful office hours. Overall, I would give him a 3.5 out of 5.

Your grade consists of 6 one page responses; 2 one page responses; annotations on readings; 2 midterms and participation. The assignments are very easy but the TAs just took points off for the fun of it. Lupu is funny and down to earth; I looked forward to class. Rarely spent any time on work outside of class. Content was interesting .
lecture boring. all work graded by tas. tough grading for midterms. highly not recommend.

Professor Lupu has to miss class a lot due to travel. There is a reading done outside of class. He does none of the gradings, so he will tell you how something is going to be graded, and then the TA'S will grade it differently, which is frustrating. Overall a very mid professor and I would not want to take another class with him.

Professor Lupu is a super nice guy and you can tell how much he cares about the subject. Unfortunately, his lectures were extremely boring and hard to get through. There was a ton of reading outside class, and pop "news quizzes" every once in a while. Also, his slides are really unhelpful if you don't actually pay attention to what he said.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really loved this class, but it definitely wasn't everyone's cup of tea. Lupu is a gem, very kind and intelligent. I thought the subject matter was really interesting so I was engaged in the class and therefore got more out of it than the people who tuned out. Lots of readings, not all of them are necessary. Relatively easy midterm papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lupu is a great guy but his lectures are extremely boring due to the excessive length. There are pop quizzes on recent world news events, weekly-ish assignments on your assigned country, and a couple of exams. Perusall reading assignments aren't necessary since the material is explained in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I liked this class! I think everyone gets an A. Not the most exciting class I've ever taken but I don't know how much you can expect from an intro to comparative politics class. Definitely geared towards freshmen. if you need to take an intro poli sci class this is a good choice. Also Lupu seemed like a very nice guy!

Noam is pretty cool guy who really knows his stuff, but the way this class works is not my favorite. The course material is interesting but lectures can be boring sometimes. The readings are SUPER long and boring and aren't necessary to do well. Noam also grades nothing and leaves it all to the TA so they have a way bigger impact on your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Lupu is a very nice guy and has a good personality, but his lectures are not very engaging. The topic material is interesting, but the lectures can be quite boring. All of the assignments are graded by the TA and the grading structure is very unclear when it comes to earning points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but not the most engaging speaker. Not sure if the class was boring because it was online or if it always like this...
This man does not care about teaching, and as such, is terrible at it.

Takes advantage of your free labor (data entry). Socially awkward guy. Seemed like he didnt really care about teaching. Gives no feedback. Delegated entire role of professor to the TA. No teaching in his class, just assigned reading. Weekly assignments with ambiguous instructions. Dont know your grade until very end. Need I say more? Nice guy tho

Absolutely terrible at providing any sort of feedback. The class is very open-ended, and you will never get a single grade back on your assignments. His lectures feel like a middle-schooler half-assing a presentation, and they'll put you to bed. 65% of your grade based on your final report, which is arbitrarily graded and seemed to tank everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Lowe is a great. She is understanding and accommodating. Her grading system is very simple. Readings are required and be prepared to participate in class about the readings. Heavily discussion based. No final-- presentation only. One writing assignment in the semester.

Class was super free, great if you want an easy A. Lowe's approach to teaching was definitely strange... I wish she had approached the music content from a more academic standpoint, instead of ~vibes~ and her political convictions. I think I learned more about what Lowe thinks of the music than any substantial music history education.

Dr. Lowe is the sort of professor who makes you question why RMP only has 5 stars because she clearly deserves 10 of them. The only thing she wants is your genuine interest and engagement with the material, and all her lectures and assignments are crafted in a way that makes sure you develop them. Beyond excellent in every imaginable respect.
Amazing professor

She is the nicest human being on Earth. She focuses on feeling Bach and made me WANT to do her readings. I submitted one homework nearly a week late and still receives good grade. She is also knowledgable about Bach and encourages discussion outside class. Literally a perfect professor.
Best professor I have had at Vandy. Learned so much. Take any class that she teaches you won't regret it.

I took Music, Gender, and Sexuality with Dr. Lowe and it was hands down my favorite class Ive taken at vandy. Weekly reading and reading response questions assignment. Interesting class discussions. One essay.
Amazing, so welcoming and enthusiastic. Everyone feels appreciated!

Professor Lowe is one of my favorite professors! She is really engaging and passionate about the content, and she uses class time very efficiently. The question sets can be a lot of work, but definitely manageable and clear. I learned so much from her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Lowe is honestly one of my favorite professors I have had at Vanderbilt so far. She is always positive and energetic, and is genuinely excited about what she teaches. She does give out a lot of readings, but you'll get a good grade as long as you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Lowe has so much positive energy that she spreads in her classes. She creates an environment that encourages a lot of discussion and allows you to always feel free to express yourself. I would 100% recommend her as a teacher. Theres a good bit of reading but as long as you show a knowledge of the reading, youre good to go.

It's a writing class so there are weekly questions sets that require good chunks of reading and about 2 hours of writing; gives really inspirational lectures; very passionate and knowledgeable about what she's teaching; probably easier than A&S writing classes; very caring and energetic; encourages opinions from students

Melanie Lowe is an amazing teachers and her lectures are interesting and really set you up well for the readings. A three page paper or question set is due every week based off of an article, and she really gives great feedback
She is amazing! This was a wonderful class. She is such an intelligent, articulate, and energetic professor that you can't help but be engaged and learn something

This is my second class with Prof. Lowe.  If she teaches something, TAKE IT.  This class, "Music Gender & Sexuality" was fascinating and I highly recommend it!  Prof. Lowe is always beautifully organized, her assignments are interesting, and each challenge your critical thinking skills to the T.  You'll never want her classes to end.

My entire class loved Prof. Lowe.  She is an articulate professor, came into class with so much vibrant energy and emphasized how we were all adults and she expected us to behave as such.  We always had very engaging conversations and the assignments were extremely interesting as well.  If you can take one of her classes, then DO IT!

Amazing professor! I looked forward to her class every week. She doesn't make crazy demands, but you definitely learn a lot from her. She is very understanding of students and really wants all of them to succeed. I'm pretty sure I'll be taking all of her classes. Oh, and no finals! She doesn't believe in them! :)

Great professor! I had her for MAR and it was extremely enjoyable, even though I was apprehensive about studying early music. Finds the most interesting topics to lecture, so class is very engaging. Fairly easy grader. Just make sure you go to class-she does take attendance.
I love Dr Lowe. She is a great lecturer and class discussion facilitator. Her enthusiasm is infectious. I could not recommend her more highly.

Energetic, very positive.  At times a bit opinionated, but not oppressively so.  Mind carefully the secret rules of musicology (no such thing as progress in the arts!  no such thing as objectivism!) as she is a stickler for them.

Dr. Lowe is one of my favorite teachers that I've had at Vanderbilt.  However, I didn't to that well in her class because the midterm was way harder than I expected.  But I loved the class and I got a lot out of it, which I figure is more important.
MAR is not an easy class to make interesting.  But she's pretty durn cool; and I'm just a little bit in love with her.
Dr. Lowe is great, she made MAR fun and interesting, something few music history professors are capapble of doing.

I loved this class!  The time went quickly; Dr. Lowe tries to keep her students engaged through out the lecture.  The midterm and final are easy; she isn't too hard of a grader on the paper, either.  She is great.

Really, really energetic. She definitely relates with her students better than the vast majority of professors, and really knows how to relate the material to modern times. She's not as bad as some with her grading standards; just beware the midterm and minor details, which she's all about.

dr. lowe knows her stuff but likes to boil music history down to the lowest common denominator, which is usually (for her) sex.  yes, memorable, but i have a feeling i'm missing some good details at times.  she's very vibrant and charismatic, tests aren't too bad as long as you study.

Does a great job of preparation for each class.  Most profs struggle with audio/visual materials (the tape's in the wrong place, they brought the wrong CD, etc).  Not her.  Very interesting class and she does a great job of presenting the material.
Great teacher, relaxing class, and minimal work.  Three quizzes, 1 paper, and a final.  Tests are pretty straight forward. Don't miss out on this one- easy and interesting!
This was an AWESOME class and she is wonderful at engaging the class in the lectures each day. One class I actually looked forward to everyday. Tests aren't too bad, but require some studying.
I didn't like this class, and I didn't like her approach to the material.  Sure, she's engaging and young, but it does little to make the material she teaches come to life.

She grades rather hard sometimes, but the class is very interesting.  This was one of those few classes I was excited about going to, and actually spent time outside of class doing further research on topics covered in class.

She loves her music.  Her class is interesting, but it can get a little monotonous at times.  Her tests only have a few questions, so study hard...if you miss one part of a question, your grade definitely suffers! She's super nice though

I think Dr. Lowe is a great teacher and a very intelligent woman.  However she spends alot of time with "how does this make you feel?" kinds of exercises which seem to waste time.  Just do the listening and the exams are fine.
Very fun class and a great first class of the day, especially on Fridays. The tests were fairly easy but the random attendence policy hurt some friends of mine.

I've had Dr. Lubinksi for 2 classes (PSY-GS 8876 and 8350). They ARE NOT easy. To do well in the class, you have to spend at least 6 hr/week doing the readings. Also, exams are 5 hour sit-down tests, or ~25 page final/midterm you have 2 weeks to write. However, I'm a better student and person because of it. I've learned more than ever before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: For a class that is important and topical, Psychometrics with Lubinski may be best described as a waste of time. The best part of the course was that it incentivized me to do outside readings. Topics he explained that I had learned in other classes were sometimes not even correct. Insistent that IQ tests are best thing since sliced bread.

Dr. Lubinski is a genuinely kind and caring professor. He is accommodating (he gave us his personal phone number to ask questions) and very experienced in the field. However, this class is very, very dry. If you're looking for a relatively easy A, this is the professor. If you want an interesting statistics class, look elsewhere.

Although he's kind and thoughtful, you'll quickly become lost in an ocean of seemingly unrelated topics through which he relentlessly marches to the sound of your 9:00am-just-out-of-bed heartbeat. Note: his blackboard drawings are pertinent for your survival and learning them will mark the difference between your A- and your B+. Good luck.

Nice person, but very unhelpful. His lectures are painstakingly boring, no engagement whatsoever, and you basically just sit and pretend to understand what he's saying.
