He doesn't answer questions with a straightforward answer, but prefers to provide countless examples without clarifying the definition. Not a great class.
Really is a nice guy, but does not stimulate students. If you want a class where you don't do anything and learn nothing, this is for you.
Nice guy, but super boring! Luckily, the class doesn't require much info so the tests aren't too bad, but it's a really boring and unnecessary class.
No Comments

Very boring class. I could've learned so much more it's all very surface level. Every class felt so long and the lectures were just looking at graphs. Assignments aren't hard as long and there are no tests. You don't need to do half the readings either.

One of my favorite professors! She is passionate about the subject area. I feel like she really cares about students and gives many opportunities to do well in the class. The class helps you understand social and health inequalities through a data-centered approach. The professor is analytical and provides good feedback and answers to questions.

The professor was not accommodating. Attendance was mandatory, but if you had an emergency or sickness, you had to write at least a two-page essay to earn back the attendance points. For some students, especially me, writing a thoughtful two-page essay takes twice the amount of time being in class. Also, the lecture style could be more engaging.

She is amazing. Lectures are super interesting and you really learn a lot. If you want to be a doctor, this class is going to be one of the most important ones you take at Vandy. Grading is pretty easy and straightforward. Just show up to class and get the assignments done and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really have enjoyed all of my MHS classes up until this point, but this class made me feel hopeless. You're graded on whether you know enough buzz words/talking points, and if she doesn't like you then she makes that very clear. Would 100% recommend another teacher for MHS 1930.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself was pretty interesting but Prof. Kalousova really dislikes when students share viewpoints that don't align directly with hers. Participation is a huge portion of the grade, but I found myself scared to speak up most days in case she snapped at me. Would definitely recommend a different teacher if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked this class and Dr Kalousava was a great professor. I feel like I learned a lot and it was pretty low-stress overall; grading criteria was very clear. Show up to class and follow the rubrics and you will be fine. She doesn't appreciate differing opinions too much, but I enjoyed the class. I recommend this class as a good MHS core course!

Prof. K is no joke in terms of class difficulty, especially in recent semesters. Her Sociology courses are notoriously more hard than the MHS ones based on personal experience. I found myself feeling nauseous after every exam in this class. She is very sweet though and insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Really interesting content that gives students a different perspective. Only complaint is she doesnt seem to appreciate differing opinions too much. That being said, as long as you do the work, you can get an A. Grade based on a course journal for completion, 2 easily graded presentations, and participation.

Dr. Soares is a really kind professor. We watched a documentary one time and she even brought snacks and tissues for us as she said it could be an emotional film. There is a Persuall assignment for each class, but it's not very time-consuming and the readings are interesting. Participating in class discussions is also not mandatory. TAKE HER!

Dr. Soares is a great professor. You are graded on 2 papers, daily readings, and 2 "discussion lead" days. The readings are sometimes long but you can get by with just skimming them. Class is discussion-based (can be awk when no one speaks) but participation is not mandatory. Dr. Soares is very understanding and knowledgeable. Interesting class!

Dr. Soares was possibly the best professor I have had so far here at Vandy. She is very caring and it is very clear that she cares for what she teaches and for her students. She grades essays very fairly and as long as you follow her directions and read the readings, you will get a good grade. I cannot recommend her enough!

He is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. His classes are a waste, he doesn't know how to teach. I would beware of taking this class as it is a waste of everyone's time. Please retire Froeb.

You will learn almost anything from his classes; everything you need to know is in his Cengage course, which you have to pay for and is a must if you want to do well on the quizzes and assignments. Also, he always cold calls and can make you feel dumb in front of everyone. Some people think he is funny and, overall, is not a challenging class.
Ten years later, I still read his blog.  That tells you what you need to know!

For whatever reason, they refuse to post lecture slides to Brightspace, even though there aren't any downsides to doing so. You're definitely left on your own in most regards, so make sure you have a clear plan
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Average lecturer and obviously knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. Regardless, I had a poor experience. Went through slides super quickly and refused to post them. Not accommodating. Treated questions outside of lecture like an inconvenience. This course felt like high school again. Take something else for CORE/AXLE.

Okay. Took for Intro to Astr. Only bad thing is professor does not post the lecture slides but everything is taken from the readings. Lots of homework and take home quizzes, tests can be hard if you don't have a clear study plan as there is no study guide explicitly given.

Professor Molina is great. They provide a lot of great content in class and are extremely reasonable with grading and giving partial credit on tests and giving extra credit whenever possible. They go really fast during the lectures, so you have to get everything down quick, and you can't get the slides later (as of this sem). Go to OH before tests!

Dr. Plant taught my section after a few semesters off, and seemed a bit rusty. Overall, I did learn a lot but sometimes questions on the exam were worded poorly (not just tricky, confusing) and graded somewhat harshly on them. Nevertheless, Dr. Plant placed a heavy emphasis on medical cases, which is important for those who will take the MCAT.

while she was clearly passionate about metabolism and I enjoyed the case studies, overall I found her slides to be really dense and she covered way too much material in each lecture. Also was not lenient at all in giving partial credit

Anyone who gives Dr. Plant a bad rate is not putting in the time and energy necessary to understand Biochemistry. It is a hard subject with lots of material to be covered, so people get mad if they do not get it instantly and then blame Plant. She is the sweetest woman ever! And she is from Brazil, which gives a super cool international perspective

I always have a great pleasure in attending Dr. Plant's classes. Indeed, it is always exciting to hear her explain the metabolism, insist on the most difficult parts, illustrate her point with the corresponding diseases. And it is always reassuring to be able to count on her for additional information whenever needed. A must choose!

Dr. Plant is a remarkable teacher: not only does she have a thorough knowledge of her subject, but she also has a keen sense of pedagogy, which makes the complex metabolism of the human body almost easy. In addition, she is very close to her students, ready to answer all questions, even after class. I recommend her course very warmly.

She is a new professor who clearly has no interest in her students actually learning the material. Following the exam, she called us all idiots after all but 3 people missed a multiple choice question (in a class of 100). She doesn't teach the material you need to know, and just assumes students know things. Do not take this professor

Professor Hayes is awesome. She is an amazing ASL teacher, but the class is definitely a lot of work. Make sure to watch the videos because there are lots of pop quizzes on the vocab. Overall, you will learn a lot and the class is super fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Hayes was really engaging which helped me learn ASL. This class is definitely not an easy A because you have to keep up with so much vocab and study for pop quizzes. She makes videos on each day's vocab which is super useful for tests, so make sure you don't take those for granted.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took this class because I wanted to learn ASL and get an A, mistake. It was my lowest grade and it may have been because I suck at learning languages. Hayes was a great teacher and she's super understanding & a kind person. It just moves very fast and tests are your whole grade. Not an easy class but great if you want to be fluent in ASL.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I was intimidated to take this class because I knew absolutely nothing about ASL, but Professor Hayes made it super accessible and fun. She posts videos of the vocab you go through each class which makes it easy to study for exams and do well. Tons of expressive and receptive practice to help you gain confidence and truly learn! Loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: ASL I Dr. Hayes is a great instructor for this course. As a hearing person deeply involved in the Deaf community, She is extremely knowledgeable on the subject and open-minded towards different perspectives. You do have to memorize lots of vocab tho., so not an easy A. Take it if you want to learn ASL. A great pleasure to learn from her.

Tests questions were kinda vague, and he looks for specifics. Lecture notes he posts online don't really cover what is tests; you really have to come to class and take notes. All in all though a good class to take.

Attend class and take notes; the notes he posts online (and the example questions) hardly cover even the bare bones of testable material. Likes to hear himself talk a lot, but that makes for some interesting 1-on-1 conversations. All that said, this class belongs in the Bio dept. Though he makes claims to the contrary, name memorization is key.

One of my favorite classes at Vanderbilt! Dr. Lybrand is not the friendliest or most flexible of professors, but he is extremely entertaining and interesting, and he really pushes you to think through chemical processes instead of memorizing facts for the tests. I learned so much from him, and I would encourage any Pre-med to take his class!

Med Chem is great! No textbook, and all the notes are posted on OAK. His notes aren't complete online so you need to go to class to fill them in. The material is extremely interesting, and it's all stuff you won't get in any other course. Very practical for the aspiring physician! There's a lot of material, but you'll be fine if you study.

one of the best chem elective classes you can take.  there is no text book, so you either have to go to class to fill in the lecture notes or get them from someone else, but no outside of class work except for a little drug topic project which isn't bad it all; knows a lot about med chem .  TAKE this class if you need an elective
Solid MedChem class.  Wants everyone to do well, but does require students to actually understand the material.  Great class for pre-meds and advanced chem students.

He teaches a very interesting medchem course.  I didn't think I would get so into it, but it really sucks you in.  Very informative.  You can tell he knows what he's talking about.  Tests aren't bad at all.  You can make an A pretty easily.

Pretty straightforward lecture class. She gives you topics that will be on the test a head of time and most of the information comes straight from the textbook readings. She also takes attendance everyday

Lecture style is rather disorganized, but she is very helpful over emails/in office hours. Takes attendance each class. A lot of the material is Psych 101 review, but the second half of the class is more political. Papers are pretty easily graded, and the midterm isn't bad at all.
The tests are based completely off the textbook, she gives you a list of topics you should know for the tests and if you read them from the book you will be fine.  Class can be somewhat boring.

She knows her stuff but......there seems to be a disconnect between what she teaches in class (straightforward health policy history) and what she expects on the exam (phd-level critical thinking). She does a good job answering questions in class but I did not find class or lectures stimulating. I would not recommend.
Monique is a really great instructor. She takes some time to get papers back, but she is amazing otherwise. Encourages class discussion. Is not a difficult professor. Highly recommend.

This class is useless- a waste of time. Way too much reading and a useless lecture that, if it weren't for mandatory attendance, no one would go to. Prof. Lyle takes MONTHS to get papers back and is completely dull and unprepared. STAY AWAY
Genuinely was the best prof at Vanderbilt, just now remember to leave her a review but wishing her all the best

One of my easier courses w/ a lot of downtime between papers. Grading felt harsh but office hours helped A TON. Went up a letter grade on my papers after rewriting. Lose points if you skip and participation matters a lot. Took it for AXLE and I am glad; beware vague rubrics though. And always go in person for questions. Radke was pretty funny too
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at vanderbilt. So sad she's leaving. Not good at responding to emails BUT very good with office hours. If you do all the work in time and participate in class you will be fine. Fairly reasonable when it comes to grade changes/rewrites and such an intelligent, genuine, cool person

Not that much work, but the class was absolutely dreadful. Dr. Radke was not accessible at all throughout the entire year and was completely unclear about her grading criteria. While she has good reviews, do not take her class if you ever want to receive any sort of response on the first email you send, as she won't respond until you send 3 more.

She's a very knowledgeable professor. Also, the class content was very interesting (probably cause it's an ethics class). However, if writing is not your strong suit (like me/uhm uhm pre-med people) then be very careful because she's very unresponsive and lazy with her emails. She will only respond on the days she holds class and no other day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Radke did a great job of making me interested in the content through discussions and short, digestable readings about each topic. The midterm was difficult, with having to write a lot in only a couple days, but the final paper was easy. Participation in discussion is key. Overall would recommend to fulfill distribution credits.
Great class - I took it as a senior and I learned alot. Incredinly thankful to learn about this subject. Two papers and participation - not graded on a lot, so make sure you do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sort of slow at responding to emails. Class is almost all discussion, which is interesting and made it go by quickly. Graded on participation, reading, and two papers. Overall, I learned a lot, and she grades pretty easily.

Readings contain unique content and points of views rarely encountered in other settings. Encourages class discussion and students in the class is very passionate about the topic. That being said, lectures are really boring and some aspects of the class seem irrelevant and overly ideological. Chill grading for a 3000 level Philosophy class.
Nice and enjoyable class. Wrote about something she presumably disagreed with and received good grade. Very good experience.

Dr. Radke was an amazing lecturer! I really enjoyed the content of the class. However, the way the class is structured with discussion means you spend a lot more time with your TA rather than her. I wish I got to interact with her more, since my TA was not the best. I definitely recommend the class though!

Lectures were very interesting, especially when we were able to debate and discuss issues as a class. TAs sometimes didn't give feedback on exam or final paper so it was kind of difficult to know how to improve writing for a field many people might not have experience in. Not my fav class I took this semester, but it was ok and not too difficult.

Radke's super chill. Lectures and discussions were fun and thought-provoking. If you're not good with writing or debating, good luck because this class requires a LOT of that to do well. Otherwise, the content and grading was super straightforward. The only thing is that the midterm was basically a 4000-word paper, but prepare and you'll be fine.

I loved this class! At least half of pretty much every class is a full-class discussion about a philosophical text. Grading is not harsh at all. If you participate and engage with the content, you'll do great.

Professor Radke was awesome! She caters the class towards the students and had really great lectures. She's not accessible ALL THE TIME but during reasonable hours she'll respond. She offers clear guidelines of what she wants for the papers. We used perusall, which was pretty easy to keep up with. Highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really loved taking Dr. Radke's class. She brings great energy to the class, and it's just a fun time with not too much work.
Radke is a great professor and makes ethics very enjoyable. Grading is clear and doesn't appear harsh at all. Would definitely recommend taking her for credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Lyn Radke for Intro to Ethics and she is really a gem. She is such a cool human being and one of the most understanding professors I have ever had. She knows so much about her field of study and you can tell how passionate she is about it. Take her class!!

Professor Radke is sweet, caring, and a wonderful teacher. She makes the class very discussion-oriented and facilitates our discussions really well. Her class is fun to participate in and her papers aren't bad because she allows infinite rewrites and meetings with her to go through them. no tests, just a few pop quizzes. highly reccommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I like philosophy. I did not enjoy her class. She is tunnel visioned and under-the-table rude. This is usually fine. BUT I was totally in the dark about her grading criteria and what she wanted. I got so lucky and I am SO happy to being done with her.

Professor Radke is great at deconstructing dense philosophical principals and explaining them clearly. Her handouts on the assigned readings are very well written. She gives helpful feedback and is helpful during office hours if you visit her with specific objectives. If you read the class material and write succinctly, A is attainable.

Solid professor that understands the course material. In class lectures were fun and interesting but you have to be there to understand the paper topics as well as reading quizzes sprinkled throughout the semester. Daily readings is required. There are 3 papers total throughout the semester but she grades really hard with no specific criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was intro level class and I have never had to work harder. She is an extremely harsh grader and her office hours are no help. She has unclear grading criteria. Whatever you do do not take her class. Nice person but not my favorite professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Radke is THE BEST!!! My most favorite professor this semester. I loved every aspect of this class. Readings were interesting, quizzes weren't hard at all, and she gives detailed feedback on your essays so that you have an easier time correcting them. If you're lucky enough to have the chance, Lyn Radke is the way to go.

Would recommend as a W class for AXLE. Class involves 3 papers which are graded kinda hard but you can rewrite 2 of the 3 to improve your grade. Professor hands out lots of little extra credit for papers to improve grades as well. Rest of the grade consists of an easy presentation, easy reading quizzes, and some short-assignments. Not too hard an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Super nice professor.  2 papers during the semester (5-6p) but you can re-write them.  Final paper is 8ish.  Really understanding with reading and deadlines; we had both our papers pushed back.  Participation is graded, but very loosely.  Highly recommend.  Also no real textbook, all of it is online.
A great TA!

Overall, McKay's class was okay. Her lectures could be pretty boring at times. She didn't submit feedback until the very end of the semester, on the day grades were due. Since the essays build on one another, timely feedback is essential for doing well, so this was frustrating. She's also not very responsive over email. Can be nitpicky with essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: McKay is interesting. My main issues with this class were the amount of reading/assignments and confusing brightspace page. She also took forever (1-2 months) to give back grades and feedback. That being said, she was an extremely light grader and cared more about participation than anything. Only read the readings when I had to do an assignment.

Prof McKay is great, very engaging and makes class interesting. About 1-2 hours of reading per week, 3 short papers and a final group project. Genuinely cares about your wellbeing outside of the classroom. I learned a lot from the class

Professor McKay is one of the most passionate and enthusiastic professors I've ever had! She restructured the class because it was online but made an effort to get to know all her students. Lots of reading and the class was graded based on 3 essays, participation, and a final group project worth 40% of the final grade. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. McKay is a very cool professor, but her lectures are a bit boring. Workload was easy throughout the semester but there is a final project and 10 page final paper due less than a week apart at the end. No exams for this class, pop quizzes on readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easiest class I've taken at Vanderbilt. "Reading" quizzes every week... But I never read and was able to pass them just by paying attention in class (no notes). You can just go back and look at the readings she asks you to include in the papers. I would put time into these and not class-to-class reading.

Dr. McKay is a lovely professor. She knows her global health jargon, and does a good job of covering it. The structure of her class gets monotonous by the end (similar types of powerpoints every class), but if you pay attention you'll do fine.

Really interesting class, but lectures can get long.  Weekly reading quizzes get hard if you don't read/know material.  Tons of reading for every class, think 3-5 readings 20+ pgs each.  No exams, but there are 3 smaller papers and a big final group project and paper.  She wants you to do well and is helpful, but does grade pretty harsh.

This class (Responses to Global Health Crises) was eye-opening, engaging, and well taught.  Lectures and assignments were very thought-provoking.  Three 5-7 page papers and a final 10-15 page paper.  McKay wants her students to do well, so it's not too tough.

Truly a gem, a superstar. Such a positive person, willing to work with you, actually treats you like an adult, and has a richer and more insightful perspective than any other professor I've spoken with -- on both the content feedback and the life advice sides.

Professor Mcllroy is the best! She genuinely cares about her students and makes the class as interactive and interesting as possible. HOD 1300 is a lot of group work, but if you put in the work there is no reason why you shouldn't get an A.

Prof Mac is honestly one of the best professors I've had here at Vandy. She is attentive, shows that she cares about her students and truly is an awesome person. Labs were interactive, but beware, there is a LOT of emphasis on group work in this class, so just be prepared for that. In all, I'd take her every semester if I could.

Dr. McIlroy was a great professor because of her enthusiasm and excitement to be in class. The class was split between lecture on Tuesday and lab on Thursday. I would recommend taking this class if you want to learn about how small groups work. If you give effort in to the class you will get a good grade.
Lecture is highkey useless, but professor is fine and makes it bearable.

Dr. Mcilroy makes anyone feel comfortable in her class. She can be a therapist because she really listens to her student and genuinely cares. Honestly look forward for the lab days because the different tasks are fun and get me to participate. The assignments are not too difficult, very straight-forward, sometimes graded harshly. Fav professor!

Absolutely phenomenal lecturer and amazing person. My complaints are with the HOD 1300 structure, which she makes the best of. Always available, always friendly, and is as lenient as the course allows her to be. Only thing to bear in mind is that she is very anti "easy A" grading, so if grades mean more than learning to you, maybe stay away.

Dr. McIlroy is one of the nicest professors that I have met at Vanderbilt. As long as you attend class, participate, and pay attention, you will do well. Thankfully there are no quizzes or exams. The GOs start early and the first one is graded very harshly. Group work is very important. She is a great professor and is very friendly and helpful.

Note: the aspects I disliked about the class were not from prof, but 1300 structure. My group was meh, making the class unenjoyable. But, this is why I loved prof. McIlroy. She was extremely caring and respectful when receiving feedback about the class and frustrations about the group. Kind professor. If you have to take 1300, she's a good option.

Probably the best professor I've had at Vandy so far. Extremely caring for her students and passionate about the subject matter, overall a class act. Engaging with her at office hours and outside/after class is one of the most beneficial things you can do not just for course understanding but for life/school in general. Highly recommend taking her.

Professor McIlroy is fantastic! She is enthusiastic and engaging. The course material is interesting! 1300 seems to vary in structure among different 1300 sections. For McIlroy, you start doing bigger assignments like the GO quite early. Some assignments could do with a little more clarification since there are no rubrics for them. Overall great!

Echoing the performative empathy reviews so that you don't get fooled by her. The only thing she cares about is her public perception and keeping up illusions. She's utterly devoid of actual care for her students. Actually practicing what she preaches is apparently too difficult for her to do. The TAs do most of the work.

HOD 1250 is an average class. Professor Mundy is not the most communicative, but depending on your TA, they can be more helpful and supportive, like with grading criteria. For quizzes, skim readings with AI and pay attention to lecture slides. A couple of interesting yet mundane guest speakers and the review sessions are jeopardy.

Professor Mundy's class was okay overall. The lectures were not very engaging, and the course structure didn't feel very impactful. A lot of the workload is TA-dependent, and grading can vary depending on your section. In my experience, it required some effort to clarify grading decisions on assignments

I loved professor Mundy! She genuinely cares about her students and the course was interesting and not difficult. Pretty much everything you need to know for the tests can be found in the lecture slides, although the readings were interesting. There are a lot of written assignments but they were not bad and the TAs were very accessible

Emailed her bc I got counted off for attendance when I was there, I received no response leaving me with a subpar grade. Didn't learn much in this class, was pretty light, if you put in the work your grade will reflect.
TAs carried this class tbh

Mundy is super sweet, but the class is massive so she doesn't really know students individually. All grading is done by TAs, so getting tight with them is crucial—set up time before every project to learn what they want. Also, don't waste hours on the endless readings as quizzes and midterms are lecture-based so extra reading will just confuse you.
Completely agree with others, fake is the perfect word to describe Professor Mundy. Performative empathy.

I personally found Mundy very fake and repulsive. She loves saying she looks out for students, but you don't feel any of that in how she acts. Luckily, you barely deal with her; almost all communication and grading is through the TA, so the class depends on how nice your TA is. One Front and back page of notes is allowed for the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is a life-changer, no joke. If you live w doubts, fear, comparison to others, overstretching yourself, and you want to break free, this class will do it. Only time I've left a class with a new direction and worldview (course fmrly taught by founder of HOD). And Dr. Mundy is a sweetheart. Never have I so clearly seen the good in someone.

easy class but professor is a condesneing jerk, very disorgainzed and claims shes cares about students wellbeing but that's not true in the slighest. Only good thing is she allows a 2 sided paper for notes on midterm and final.

AMAZING class. It's a tad more work than the typical HOD class (4x 4-page papers, 1x 6 page paper, short final presentation, and weekly 250-500 word discussion posts), but Dr. Mundy is a VERY generous grader. Recommend: use APA sub-headers for papers, put phone/computer away ALWAYS, participate regularly. Readings not required.

Dr. Mundy is a precious soul. Her Self & Human Development seminar is 100% the most inspiring class I've taken at Vanderbilt. Very few lectures; time in class is often spent in reflective activities and group discussion, so be ready to participate. Very manageable workload and fair grading. You get out what you put in here.

Very kind and energetic professor. TA's do most of the grading in this class so you don't engage with her much unless you want to. Pretty good lecturer. Does mindfulness activities at the beginning of every class.

Professors are kinda useless in the course, since TAs lead discussion and grade everything, but Mundy seemed like a nice woman. Lectures are typically full of nothing, a big chunk of time gets taken up by mindfulness activities and Peabody advertising at the start of most lectures. Not useless stuff, just felt like a very inefficient use of time.

Dr. Mundy is an amazing person and truly caring professor. I haven't met another professor who cares nearly as much as her. She is easy to access through email, and replies quickly. Lectures can sometimes be boring, but she spices it up with guest speakers and little mindfulness exercises. 1250 isn't too difficult either.
I feel like some people would definitely roll their eyes at what she says, but she's a nice lady overall. grading is TA dependent I'm pretty sure but the bar is low because this is an HOD intro

Dr. Mundy was one of my 1250 teachers, and I found that she came across nice in class yet refused to answer emails throughout the semester. All of her lectures were kind of the same content put in different words, and she is not involved in grading at all. She's a pretty easy going person, but I found her to be a little off-putting.
Great professor and nice guy! One of my favorite professors that I've ever had

Super nice guy. Accessible outside of class, gives very clear and engaging lectures. Exams will be difficult if you are new to calculus, but doable if you work at it. Homework is a little long, but unlimited attempts to get it right (comes in clutch). Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll miss a LOT if you don't show up.
such a good prof. so funny in lectures. showing up to class really makes a difference when it comes to exams. super easy class

CORE 2500 is the easiest course I've taken (and probably will ever take) but I think Sean is aware of this and is teaching 2500 to have fun and make math accessible for everyone, which is really cool. No exams, graded off of quizzes, homework, and participation. And Sean is funny, a clear lecturer, and cares about his students. Great guy.
Very nice and explains well. Every lecture is a new topic and keeps class flowing smoothly.

Amazing professor. Love this guy. The homework for this class felt like it wasn't wasting my time. Tests weren't overly difficult, and I never felt like it was unfair. Always kind and willing to help. He's extremely clear and easy to understand. Probably one of the best, if not the best, math professors I've had at Vanderbilt.

AMAZING PROFESSOR. i actually love him so much. he was extremely accessible outside of class and his lecture for the most part are very clear and understandable. the tests weren't too bad. definitely focus on the homeworks to study for the test. 100% reccomend taking any class with him

Decent prof, lectures felt like a whole lotta nothing sometimes but he wasn't afraid to pull specific applications from lecture and put them on tests, so show up. Really bad at explaining literally anything, worked out test answers and review sessions are confusing and skip steps, so just spam practice problems from ChatGPT lowk.

The positive reviews here confuse me, he's terrible. I have to take math classes as core requisites for my major. Out of all the math classes I have taken in my life he hands down gives the most useless and unimportant lectures imaginable. Inaccessible outside of class so good luck. Linear is pretty easy he just sucks, choose anyone else.
He is an awesome guy and professor. He has a lot of energy and is always willing to help you outside of his set office hours.

Great lecturer, I actually really enjoyed his class. However something is def off with his personality. Is overly nice sometimes and suddenly cold. Not sure what's up with that. Other than that, hes definitely a great professor and explains concepts well enough

Prof. McAfee was a good Calculus teacher---the lectures were average but he does a good job keeping class engaged and covers pretty much everything on tests in class. Weekly homeworks can be a decent amount but not bad if you stay on top of it. He reccomends textbook but you 100% don't need it. Would take again.
Bad lecture but highly accessible after class. He is a good professor but has bad lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McAfee was nice, a lot of opportunities for extra credit/ test corrections were given. If you work hard you'll be able to get the grade you want. Decent amount of homework. Lectures can get boring, but he does a good job at keeping the class engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Class taken for formality (hence the difficulty rating) but Sean is super accessible in and out of class, he is always open to questions. He is friendly and efficient, and this was one of my favorite classes throughout my time at vandy. 10/10 would recommend.

McAfee was great. His lectures were decent and his notes were usually helpful. He is always at office hours and I highly suggest going. Also, working with others from the class is good. His tests are pretty quick, so be proficient. Linear is hard and McAfee does a good job breaking it down, but if you hate fast pace tests, just be careful.

Professor McAfee is really caring, however, his lectures for this class specifically were really confusing and he did not follow his own lecture templates at all. I had to learn the entire class from outside sources. He is still probably the best option for the class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy. Is great at teaching material given the book is horrible. Explains hard to grasp concepts very well.

taken as formality, so class was easy (so take this with a grain of salt). regardless, prof sean makes an effort to ensure everyone understands concepts. takes questions in class, super helpful in office hours, really nice and encouraging. overall amazing person teaching in a horrible department. would recommend if you can get him.
big chillin!
A really respectful professor.
GOAT professor, talks about extended topics in last classes which are really inspiring. exams are well designed and not difficult at all, just make sure you can do calculation fast.

Great lectures, provides lecture notes so you can focus in class instead of trying to copy everything down. Explains everything clearly and makes sure that everyone is following along. Very accessible during office hours. Has weekly homework but is manageable.

Sean is seriously an amazing professor. He really cares about his students and he makes a genuine effort to get to know everyone. He is really good at explaining complicated topics.There are weekly homeworks and the exams are hard but definitely doable.

Professor McAfee is one of the few professors I have had that make it clear that he wants you to do well in his class and he gives you the opportunities inside and outside of class to make that happen. There are no quizzes and he offers review sessions before each exam. He also posts lecture templates online and is very accessible outside of class.

Not get me wrong, Sean is amazing. Despite that, I had no calculus prior experience, still due to my track I had to take this class 1st semester. It was simply too hard. For 1201 I got another prof. and it was a whole different experience. Still, if you have experience in calc maybe AP BC or IB AA get Sean, he is 10/10 as a human and professor.
Best professor I have ever had. Super interesting guy who clearly cares about his students. He's very passionate about math and he's a great communicator. Don't hesitate to take any of his classes.

Easily my favorite prof at Vanderbilt. After MATH 1300, McAfee made me realize I could really understand concepts again. Always friendly and understanding, great attitude. Very accessible outside class and was willing to meet with me alone the week of every test since I couldn't make it to office hours. Tests were very fair and graded generously.
Best teacher in the Vanderbilt math department. Basically a human golden retriever. Fun lectures, tons of office hours and review sessions. Really cares about teaching and cares about students
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a fantastic prof! I was worried about taking calc 1301, but McAfee made it such an enjoyable experience. He is such a pleasant and motivating person, is super accessible outside class (he even thanks you for visiting him during office hours), and ensures that you understand difficult concepts whilst encouraging you to persist.

Best professor I've ever had! I usually hate math, but he made what is considered a weed-out class to be manageable. He has an infectious smile/personality that makes you love math! He genuinely cares about your success and is soooo helpful and patient in office hours. He explains math so simply and beautifully. If you have to take 1301, TAKE HIM!

McAfee is such an awesome professor. Super helpful and approachable, caring & friendly, great at explaining. Office hours highly recommended. Textbook is very helpful and recommended as well. Very grateful to have had McAfee, hands down wonderful prof.

Best math professor I've had. 1301 is supposed to be the hardest class at Vandy but I never felt this way with McAfee. Lectures are lighthearted and he cares about his students. Additionally, he covers content with many examples which made complex topics easier. Attending class is essential to doing well on tests and there was weekly homework.

Best MATH 1200 professor! Lectures were very clear and he was a lively presence in class. He's also very helpful in office hours. There is extra credit outside of class with discussion, etc. so the grading structure helps those who are not the best test takers. While there was quite a bit of homework, McAfee made it worthwhile. Highly recommend!
Best math professor all around. Great presence in class and very engaging lectures and attitude. 100/10 recommend!

they recently changed the math department grading and tests. sean was very straightforward and understandable with his lectures. the tests now are standardized so the material is more consistent with every other section. there is homework for every lecture day but there is plenty of extra credit for any bad days
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor McAfee and the other Math 1200 professors were very helpful this semester. I would caution that this course is very hard if you have no prior calculus experience, but McAfee tried his best to slow down and explain everything. He has good availability for extra help too.

McAfee is a good professor. Explains things easily and have extensive amount of office hours every week. He seems to spend more time forming a basis of understanding concepts rather than giving lots of examples. The class is sort of difficult though. Be prepared to do daily homeworks 3x a week for the whole semester. This was definitely annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is so much content in this class, wouldn't recommend for a non-STEM major just looking for a science credit unless you are seeking a challenge.The quizzes and drawings are a lot! But, she cares about her students and their success, (go to office hours!) and she is an engaging lecturer who wants us to talk as we learn things, which is helpful.

Dr. Wegener was a good lecturer who did a great job outlining clear requirements for assignments and had a forgiving grading system. Generally a pleasant person to interact with and very accessible outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you think her class is hard or that she is mean, you must have really thin skin and don't actually use your tuition for learning. By far the most intentionally structured and organized class I have taken. Dr. Wegener wants you to succeed and she gives you so many fair opportunities to do so. Easy, fruitful, great class.

NSC 1400 is definitely geared toward MHS, Neuroscience, or pre-med majors, but it is possible to get an A if you try. There are 6 quizzes, and everything is take-home except the in-person final. Take time with the drawings; it's a great grade booster. We had over 30 points of extra credit throughout the semester, which really helped. Not too bad.

I believe anyone who considers Dr. Wegener only strict, mean, or tough never took much time to go to her office hours or talk to her personally. She has a strict teaching style and grading, but is also an excellent teacher, clearly knows what she is talking about, makes her expectations VERY clear, and gives a lot of cushion grade-wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great teacher, learned so much and my fav class this semester. Checkpoints are challenging, not so much memorization but applying it and critical thinking. I liked that part as it meant less prep outside of class. Classes are fun and engaging. Easy A if you just try and show up in my opinion.

Psychoparhamcology is a great class! Dr W records lectures, and rewatching them is a godsend for studying, as there is a lot of material/nuance. Attendance is required but can skip up to ~5 classes. Tests are tricky but fair, and one (including final) drop. Case studies are dense but great practice for med school or clinical work. Love her!

Wegener was quite good when I took her! I didn't really have a heavy background in neuroscience until I took her and felt it was very approachable content. The quizzes were confusing at times, but were very reasonable. You just have to study and that's about it. Wegener might seem intense sometimes, but she's very accessible and accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dont take!

Lots of extra credit available. Take home tests besides final(all are open-note), but wording is so confusing chat won't help. Half of grade is quizzes, half is drawing assignments whose guidelines weren't clear at all. Slideshows are confusing and pretty bare so must attend lectures. Tophat required to get the extra credit

Don't take this class unless you must. She makes it feel like she does not want you to succeed in her class. Accuses many of cheating (correct) but punishes everyone. Don't be like me and struggle by trying to take the take-home quizzes by yourself. I found out everyone uses chat to get A's BECAUSE THERE IS TOO MUCH MATERIAL/MEAN TRICK QUESTIONS.

Her class is easy to get an A if you attend every lecture (insane amount of extra credit), but she flies through content that's very difficult to understand unless you've taken BSCI 1511. Online take-home MCQ, in-class open-note final, and 5-6 drawings. LA's are good, her office hours are also helpful, but she is pretty scary and intense.

Wegener records all of her lectures & I recommend watching them even if you attend class. The class is a lot of work, but doable & I learned a lot. She does punish the whole class if she suspects cheating on her take-home quizzes. The drawing assignments are difficult, but useful SO DO THEM ALL! She is super intense, so YOUR LA IS YOUR BEST FRIEND!

Dr. W is clearly very knowledgeable about neuroscience, but doesn't seem to care about her students. She claims to care abt mental health, but then proceeds to be the least accommodating, hostile, and just out-of-touch professor. She gave us an online quiz during spring break and made our incredibly time-consuming final drawing due on reading day.

Prof Wegener was extremely hostile during class; she would give us take-home quizzes, but after every single one, she would accuse the entire class of cheating. The drawings were often extremely confusing, and grading was very nitpicky. She very clearly cares more about herself and her mental health than students.

Passive-aggressive. Class seems easy at first, but she's a terrible teacher. Thinks she's better than everyone. Cares about her mental health but not yours. I used to want to study neuroscience, but she completely ruined it for me. Quizzes are at home, but the final is in person and includes a super picky drawing assignments. SAVE YOUR GPA TRUST

Wegener is a rude and passive-aggressive professor who thought she was better than everyone else. I took the class interested in neuroscience came out of it hating neuroscience. The assignments were take-home quizzes, drawings, and an in-person final. She was very unclear on what would be on quizzes and the final. DO NOT TAKE this class

The quizzes are take home, so they seem easy but are very difficult. She talks very fast in lectures, and the material is dense so if you want to actually get all of the content you need to rewatch every lecture afterwards. This was a very difficult class.

Dr. Wegener is the breathe of fresh air of a highly intelligent, relatable, down to earth boss woman that I can without a doubt say I look up to. She is so knowledgeable, humble, and accessible to meet you throughout the semester. Her lectures are very engaging and she is the first professor to use TopHat well. Take her class if able!!!!

I spent so much time reading the Chapter material that the majority wouldn't end up on the quiz most of the time. Wegener's slides simply went through content too quickly for me. I wish Wegener spent more time lecturing/teaching us instead of having class periods to work on drawings and case studies. Provides lots of cushioning for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Literally the HOD of stem classes. You do have to draw pictures, which took longer than expected and were just annoying. Everything is open note so why pay attention? She is so condescending though and thinks she is the best thing since sliced bread... and contrary to how she tries to frame it as, these comments are not an anti-feminist rant

Narcissistic, self-absorbed, and egotistical. She is very full of herself and thinks she has the best pedagogy but comes across as very disengaging. The grading is generous and barely kept me sane in the class, but she is insufferable to deal with as a professor. Lots of class time goes to waste with her rants about the class. Shoutout Reed, the TA

Dr. Wegener's Neuroscience class was a mediocre experience. Although she cares deeply about her subject matter, her teaching style could be better. The slides are dense, and she moves through them quickly. She can come off as irritated at students for not meeting her expectations, but she also takes the time to give feedback on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wegener is an amazing professor and I would 100% recommend her to anyone. Her lectures were very engaging, and she made an effort to create community in the class. I never felt overwhelmed by the amount of work in this class, and if you show up and do the work you'll do well. She's also just really cool and funny

BEST PROFESSOR I'VE HAD AT VANDERBILT. Dr. Wegener is intelligent, passionate, and caring. She continuously checks in to make sure absent students are okay. LOTS of extra credit offered if you attend enough classes. Lectures are interesting and organized. Quizzes are challenging but take home and you are well-prepared. COULDN'T RECOMMEND ENOUGH!

Very clear how much she cares for her students. The lectures, the UCs, and cases were cool. She gives you time in class to work and is flexible with deadlines. she gets behind on grading which means you don't end up getting any good feedback on assignments. be proactive and meet with her/TA throughout, especially for the final paper annotations.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wegener was really approahable and helpful with feedback. A lot of class time is spent working on case studies or reflections and she walks around answering questions. Grading is based on reflection ability and communication skills not rote memorization. Good taste in music.

She puts a lot of time into making the class and content interesting. I enjoy the way she structures her class and I think her pedagogy is great for upper levels. Sometimes I feel though she tries to structure things too much and proposes how we should think too much, but I understand shes trying to teach us more than content. Easy A with effort

Decent professor, horrible person. Extremely passive-aggressive in emails and very rude to students in one-on-one communication. Would not recommend. There are better classes with more accommodating professors you can take. Not worth the mental stress.

You learn a lot in a low-pressure class, and I'm really grateful that it was never a source of stress or had high workloads. That being said, it sometimes felt a little disorganized or without clear expectations for some assignments, but the professor is SO incredibly accommodating and patient and happy to help you through any questions you have.

Dr. W was the best prof I've ever had!! take her class! She is the nicest person ever, her pedagogy is freaking awesome, she always gives you a chance to make up points, and she has almost no hard deadlines. She's a fair grader who wants you to succeed and understands that life can get hard. I've never had a professor just genuinely care so much!

Neurophys was definitely harder than I expected, but she made the class as fair as possible with balanced grading (groupwork, problem sets, concept checks). Also very accomodating and a very strong teacher. I highly recommend taking Dr. Wegener for any class if you are a neuro major.

This class was confusing this semester. THere was little feedback because she was behind on grading, and expectations and assignments were not clearly explained. Given the circumstances, I learned a lot of a variety of neuro diseases and enjoyed the concepts. Pro Wegener is a cool person and knows her stuff. Her class structure is unique.

I took both drugs and behavior and neuro diseases with Professor Wegener. I can 100% say that her classes were some of my favorite neuro courses. The classes are by no means easy, but if you come in ready to put the work in and come in with a genuine interest, you'll leave with so much appreciation for neuroscience and for her teaching. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I wasn't sure what to expect at first, since she is a relatively new professor at Vandy, but I was not disappointed! Her lecture style is full of helpful examples (problem-solving, real-life) that kept the class engaged. She was super considerate and relatable to students; she even let our class skip the final in light of COVID-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took both diseases & drugs&behav. Conclusion: She's probably the only prof I've had that knows how to push you out of your comfort zone without breaking you. She cares. She keeps several HOURS of her pre-exam days free for anyone to pop in and ask q's. She knows how to make info stick bc it's interesting. Her classes made me keep my neuro major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Wegeners class has been my favorite class at Vanderbilt. All of the homework is based on case studies and papers which makes the information so much more interesting. Tests were difficult enough to make you think but there were so many participation points that you could do mediocre and do well overall. Far more accessible than any other prof.

Very clear about grading and what's expected. Approx. 60% of the class is graded on completion of homeworks and answering tophat questions. She put a lot of thought into her lectures and teaching style, extends office hours, and cares about your understanding. If you love to learn and do the work, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do not take her class. She punished the class for doing well on tests and getting As. She had an annotated paper assignment that was very unclear and gave students bad grades on probably to limit the number of As. I definitely would not recommend. I learned nothing and came out more confused about neuroscience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Minarich is super sweet and brought Crumbl cookies on the final lecture! No exams/quizzes but 70% of your grade is based on 2 group video projects and 3 essays. Her feedback on the essays is helpful and she is very accessible outside of class. Take this class if you're interested in film or need liberal arts HCA requirement fulfilled.
While Professor Minarich is passionate about film, I found the lectures somewhat boring. I personally have an interest in film but this class did not support my passion.

For CMA 1600. Professor Minarich clearly cares about students and the material. She is very passionate. You will write a few papers and have weekly discussion posts, but they're not crazy overwhelming. Clear extra credit opportunities. Clearly overworked and underpaid.

This course was incredibly engaging and informative. Prof. Minarich is probably the best professor I have had and probably one of the best people I have ever met. She is very flexible, creative, understanding, and super intelligent. I developed as a writer way more in this course than any previous courses at Vanderbilt.

Dr. Minarich is amazing! She's funny and engaging with the class. Her course is pretty liberal (which I'm okay with), just as a warning; however, she is very open minded and will present multiple viewpoints on an issue. We watched a film from 2014, which is pretty awesome.

This class was as interesting as an 8am feminist literature class can be, but beware: she expects ridiculous time commitments from students. Movies, novels, and extra readings plus assignments due each class period. Very strict, DO NOT TAKE if looking for an easy A English credit.
Dr. Minarich is a great professor, but is not an easy grader at all. Beware of papers, it is nearly impossible to get an A. Knows her subject inside and out.

I seriously do not believe that she is so new to teaching--she seems like she's been doing it for YEARS. She's an awesome professor and really engaging and enthusiastic. Really interesting class as well. If you need a 118w, highly recommend something with her.

Dr. Minarich is awesome! She is super fun and spunky in class and she really makes you interested in the material. Her choices of readings are usually really interesting; make sure you read before class otherwise you'll be lost and participation is a decent part of your grade. 3 major papers and a bunch of one page responses that are really easy.

A TON OF GROUP WORK!! If you do not like group work do not take her. She is very helpful, but she has this sarcastic tone and it really just rubbed me the wrong way. A lot of reading and a lot of responses. She is nice, do not get me wrong, but just the amount of group work really turned me away from her.

New to teaching, but she is fantastic. Fair, clear, genuinely engaged in subject matter. Carries a big stick when it comes to syllabus, exams, and paper expectations, but she is very straight-shooting (i.e., no crazy curve balls) and totally willing to help you get there. You would think she had been doing this for longer.

Good teacher...very laid back, nice and ALWAYS willing to meet with you if you need help. Young-- She's currently a grad student here and she grades sort of hard for your rough drafts but she replaces that grade with whatever you get on your final draft and its always better.
not to bad just do the work and you should be fine.

It is clear that Professor Meadows cares a lot about her students' mental health and success. She was easy to talk to and very helpful outside of class, she even helped me with some personal things. She is obviously very knowledgable and cares that her students comprehend the content and participate consistently.

Professor Meadows cares about the students in class. Passionate about class topics but did little to change the structure of the class. Although, it was an English course, everyday was 50 minutes of student conversations and 5 minutes of Meadows rephrasing what was said - this got extremely repetitive. This class utilized two professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Good class, good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
hands-down worst prof I've ever had. Didn't release grades until after the semester was over, so we weren't able to revise our work- she told us that we would be able to. Just rephrase what students are saying & isnt a fair grader. I would 100% not recommend her. Could've learned more if this class was student lead.

HORRIBLE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fair amount of reading but fun and interesting class. Meadows and Rowe are a great duo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Meadows is an understanding professor. For example, she would give us a window to turn in assignments instead of just one day. Classtime is just a discussion of the readings, and the books are actually interesting. She does take a while to grade papers and such.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Meadows seems like a very nice woman but seems to like some students more than others. All she does in class is rephrase and repeat what the students say in class and doesn't actually teach anything. Besides, a uselessly harsh grader.

This instructor was genuinely caring and understood what students were going through at specific times of the year, or with a personal issue. The comments received on essays were helpful, and is good at telling people her expectations. Late grading, hard to get feedback to be used for improvements. Wants you to do well, but also make learning fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my all-time favorite professors at Vanderbilt. She has a strict attendance policy, but I'd never skip because her classes are so enjoyable. Expects you to do the reading because it's an English class, but understands that it isn't your only priority. Very discussion-based. GREAT personality. love her.

Very intelligent woman with little personality.  The class is great if you enjoy "deep thinking" nonsense.  She is incredibly cold to her students and makes class excruciatingly painful to attend.  Try to get Tichi instead.

Prof. Meadows is a great teacher. Our class was called Death and Taxes, but it has been incredibly interesting and insightful. Meadows is great at asking deep questions and creating a new understanding of the texts. The work load was tough at some points, but the quality of discussion made up for it! She is an absolutely wonderful professor!
Professor Marcus is fantastic. I think the old reviews are too harsh. She has changed a lot. Exams are fair. Her slides have all you need to succeed.
Her class is the best especially if you like applied econometrics. She is super nice and patient and provides very helpful study guide ahead of time. Topics are interesting and relevant too.

Cares about students and the material, but is a tough grader. Exams are very conceptual and she's extremely particular—small wording mistakes can cost points. Lectures are heavy and slides sometimes contain errors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly a solid professor. I think a lot of these ratings are either outdated, exaggerated, or flat out inaccurate. You can work with a partner on the problem sets and the grading is not that bad (class average on the midterm was a 93).

This class is a statistics heavy course advertised as an health economics course. Attendance is mandatory and you have no way of catching up as her posted powerpoints are very barebones and not comprehensible without narration. There are several 40+ papers you must read with unnecessarily hard problem sets not covered in class. Avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly unreasonable. Clearly prioritizes her own reputation as a professor over students' learning by depressing grades. Save yourself and don't take this course!!!

Easily one of the worst professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Information for the class is completely up to her discretion (and 99% of it contains her own research studies). Problem sets and exams are near-impossible. She doesn't seem to like to teach, or give her students decent grades. Beware of this class. Never again.

Attendance is mandatory, but most of the test content is from the slides, which she posts online. Pretty straightforward class; it seems like she's adjusted the difficulty since she started teaching this course to be more reasonable. Definitely recommend this as a higher-level Econ, especially if you like/are good at stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This had to be one of the most mind-numbing courses I have ever taken. It is essential an advanced statistics class and the variables just happen to be somewhat related to health. Professor Marcus cares about the students, but she is not engaging when she teaches in the slightest.

Class is lecture based but Marcus isn't the greatest lecturer. Class can be boring and many students zone off. Only 1 midterm and 1 finale (avg. of midterm was 80% but final much easier with avg. in 90s). 3 problem sets that aren't too bad if go to the TA and read the slides. One 5 minute presentation. No textbook. Overall, very avg. class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I feel lucky to have taken her after having taught a semester. She gave us her fall exams, which were VERY similar to ours (and easier). She uses Brame's videos, which are not helpful. Brame emphasized a LOT of things that Moore didn't care abt. Moore has less helpful wksts, and classtime is not productive. Not sure if shes teaching it again tho

Dr. Moore is very energetic and her lectures are both engaging and informative. Her tests are very similar to worksheets/slide content. Kind and cares about the well-being of her students. Pevious exams are very similar to actual exam. Accessible outside of class and she's more than happy to share about med school as someone a VUSM adcom. Take her!

Very sweet professor! She's caring and will take the time to answer whatever questions you have. She explains metabolism and all the pathways really well. One issue is that she does not have her own take-home videos and uses Dr. Brame's, which are good but don't cleanly align with our content. However, her exams were reasonable! Great prof!
Honestly one of the best professors I had at Vandy. Always there for the students and is very clear about her expectations during lectures regarding the exams.

She does use Dr. Brame's online lectures... BUT if you come to class, she'll specify what she wants you to know to succeed. Honestly, both the online lectures and her slides help you understand the concept more, while it may seem annoying/pointless at first. She is so sweet. I would take her + Plate to succeed. You just need to put in the work!
This was my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. I feel so lucky I had her for this class.

VERY nice and clearly cares about her students, but exams had typos and she would test on things that she said "not to worry about". Extra credit was a big bonus though. Lectures are fine, but it's clear she's just reading off her speaker notes.

Caring professor but flipped classroom did not work imo . Recorded lectures were from a different professor and tests often had different focuses and expectations. Exams tend to have several tables and focus on memorization of details, but there was partial credit. limited practice exams offered

The best professor I have ever had. Biochemistry is going to be difficult and the exams are hard, but you can tell that she cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She gave extra credit as needed. If you are willing to put in the work and genuinely want to learn and remember the material, take Dr. Moore. I can't recommend her enough.
One of the nicest professors at Vandy but her exams are absolutely diabolical. She tests on the most niche details that shouldn't matter. Her mini-lectures every class are pretty good though.
shes nice but she pmos so bad cuz classes r big fat waste of time and her exams are just a bunch of confusing tables abt the nichest details ever

You will essentially be taking 2 classes. She gives easy extra credit which saved my grade. Lectures were useless and honestly just more confusing but you have to go because she corrects the videos. Exams are tight time wise so just memorize everything so you can recall rapidly. No curve lots of time on quizzes. 2 homework assignments.

Dr. Moore is super caring and accessible. She uses another professors videos for a flipped classroom format so expectations get really confusing. It honestly felt like studying for 2 different professors. She tests on memorization so if that is a strength then you will be ok. Beware Jackson tests on understanding/application so you can't memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: gives million things. then only little things.

She's one of the nicest profs I've met. She didn't have much time to lecture per class bc the class is a flipped class but her lectures do contain everything you need to know. 5 points ec on a hw and 10 points ec across both exams. She gives a lot of partial credit when grading and made sure that basically everyone got full points on the tophat.

Very interesting course and Merryman does a great job teaching it. He just writes on a whiteboard with no posted notes so you'll have to pay close attention. Tests are pretty hard but homeworks are helpful for application.

I enjoyed his lectures and the content, but his exams were unnecessarily difficult. Studying was impossible, as questions were unpredictable, unrelated to homework or classwork, and focused more on deciphering his wording rather than mastering the material. The timing was tight, the grading was harsh, and it failed to reflect your understanding.

He's not a bad lecturer but his tests are ridiculous and, in my opinion, don't reflect students' understanding of the material. The tests contain long, unclear questions that are often more of a test of students' reading comprehension and ability to make the same assumptions he does than of their understanding of biomechanics.

My favorite professor here at Vanderbilt. I took the class last semester but forgot to review. He is very good at teaching and explained the materials + their applications well. The class is not as difficult as what people say. Lots of physics concepts do come back here though. You will be fine if you just keep practicing doing the problems.

Basically an extension of PHYS 1601. Material can be hard, but you can definitely find youtube videos on the content to help you understand it better. Merryman honestly has me stumped. Sometimes he was very friendly, other times he would express his lack of care for students. Overall, just work hard, grind it out, & you can get through this class.

Dr. Merryman is a great lecturer, but the class is basically physics 1601 on steroids. homework (20%), 4 exams (15%, 10%, 15%, 10%), and final (20%). Each exam is difficult because there is a "special" case that you need to solve and he takes off a lot of points for any mistakes. Make sure of to go to office hours to get 100% on homework category.

One of the smartest, coolest professors ever. Gives homework after every lecture except Friday. Understanding lectures and hw was super important for doing well on exams. TA's help you immensely with HW. Exams I thought were very difficult but the HW pulls your grade up. You just have to be flat out smart for this class and pray you understand it.

Dr. Merryman has been my favorite prof at Vandy! I thought this class was really hard, but he also made it really enjoyable and engaging. He makes his own tests and the questions can be kind of frustrating because they're vague. The TA is super helpful for homework assignments. Overall even though it's so hard I learned so much in this class.

Dr. Merryman is a grown-up Frat Boy who wants to haze you with physics. He claims his class is super hard, but you're good if you can do the homework TA's help. He's super engaging, good with questions. His homemade questions can be annoying (he expects you to ballistics expert) but are VERY ENTERTAINING. Take this if you want to break some bones.

One of my favorite profs at Vandy! I took biomechanics with him last year and really enjoyed it, so I signed up for this class. Didn't have a course description, but I saw he was teaching it so I figured it would be good and I was right. It was essentially an ethics for BME class. Discussion-based, easy A (not his usual tho), but still worth it

Attendance is not required, but definitely still go to class. There's no textbook, but you don't need one anyways, because his lectures are super helpful. There's a small amount of homework that is helpful for learning and is a nice grade boost. Exams are challenging, but fair. Loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Merryman is a really good lecturer. There is no textbook use and he teaches straight from the whiteboard, so you really need to go to class. His tests are difficult because his questions can be kind of vague and tricky. Homework twice a week, but it's usually not super difficult or time consuming. Overall, a solid professor for Biomechanics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I think he was overall a very solid professor. Attendance isn't technically required, but there is no textbook and he doesn't post lectures online so you really need to go to class to know the material. Homework is also very important for understanding. I liked the course overall, and think that Merryman was a good professor

Homework twice a week, usually require some sort of "trick" or deep understanding so you should DEFINITELY make time to go to TA office hours or find friends who do go. TESTS ARE HARD, and he does it on purpose to test your critical thinking. Do the practice tests, and rework the homework problems. Definitely learned a lot, though. Very thorough.

He's my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. His lectures are extremely engaging, and he loves to answer questions and really cares about his students learning. His homework and tests are tough, but if you go to class and pay attention, it shouldn't be too hard. If you are struggling, he is very accessible in office hours.

My favorite professor so far at Vandy. He doesn't use a textbook so attendance is extremely necessary, homework assigned twice a week that is always difficult but is the only way to learn the material. Learned everyone's name before the second class, really cares about the students.
He's very helpful in office hours! Also gives good lectures. His research is amazing, and he's a nice guy. He does make you work for your grade, though.
My favorite teacher at Vanderbilt. The tests are pretty hard but the HWs are most helpful he is an interesting guy and makes the class great

Easily my favorite teacher at vanderbilt.  He has changed the class completely and if you study and do the hws on your own you'll do great.  He sets up so many chances for you to ask questions and get help but you don't always need it.  take him!!
Getting better. Interesting class. Respects students' weekends and/or lazy days (first day back from thanksgiving, ect..)
Teaching isn't his strongsuit, but he can relate a lot of material in class to his research which is really interesting. Class average is lower than Miga's class but that just means a bigger curve!

take Miga's section. If you take Merryman, you'll have to teach yourself. slides are useless, homework is useless, and he overcomplicates things. avoid. I'm sure he is good at what he does in terms of research, but there is no way he was recruited for his teaching abilities.

Professor Merryman is a great person, but had some trouble teaching this course. I understand that this was his first year teaching it, and he had to follow Professor Miga's section. There is a lot of self-teaching in this course, but next year I bet Merryman will much better. Talk to him because his research is amazing.
Great teacher. Very helpful and available for EI at any time. I had him at the Naval Academy and he was interesting and a great teacher to have for Calc III

If you are taking him for a low level course, he is easy. If you take him for anything above calculus, he will go as absolutely hard on you as he can. He is EXTREMELY DIFFICULT. I have a 4.0 and he was by far the most difficult professor I have ever had. You must go to all office hours, read the textbook thoroughly and fall in love with the subject

This class is a joke. It is really easy - you will feel so bored most of the time. I read the posted notes before the test and got 95's. Attendance is mandatory and can be your downfall - grades clicker questions. Recitation is a joke with easy quizzes. Easy premed boost - take if you have the time.
Amazing! Besides weekly quizzes, there is practically no work. He gives you practice exams before the test so you know exactly what to expect.
Dude is a total boss. The class is a joke.

GPA booster.  There is homework, but it is rarely turned in.  Weekly quizzes are directly out of the text book.  Exams are long, but he tells you what are on the exams in the review session.  The take home tests can be long, but easy to ace.
So easy! As long as you go to recitation and read the textbook the day before the quizzes, attend midterm review sessions, and do practice tests, you'll get an A. Don't need to attend class.

Best teacher I have had at Vanderbilt. He really knows his stuff and explains things extremely well. Very funny and interesting guy. The homework isn't overbearing but really helps you learn the material. Awesome Teacher!

Good teacher who really helps you understand the material.  Curves tests if needed, including the final.  Do the Homework assignments and attend his test reviews and you should do great.  He also tends to digress  in class every now and then which gets pretty interesting.  Very nice guy
