This is for 1250W (Introduction to Poetry). Dr. Moore is probably my favorite professor I've had in my entire time at Vanderbilt. He is caring, kind, makes lectures engaging, and is overall just a good person to talk to. If you need a W course, I cannot recommend this class enough. If I could take another class with him, I absolutely would.

Took Moore's Bible in Literature class last fall and really enjoyed it! Every English major should take, even if not a Christian; he makes it accessible to people of all backgrounds. The works studied are also very diverse, not just old English. There is something for everyone.

One 5 pg. paper, one 10-12 pg. final paper, and a few short write-ups and discussion posts. Very engaging class discussion over Biblically-inspired English works. Fair but not easy grader. Would def recommend for anyone interested in Biblical poetry and not afraid to read a decent amount. Prof. Moore is very engaging and knowledgeable.

Dean Moore has some of the most interesting lectures of any English class I have ever taken, but he also allows for a significant (most) of class time to be focused on discussion. He is a tough grader and there is a lot of reading some nights, but his class is very rewarding in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dean Moore is a great professor. He cares about students, cares about success and knows about his content. The class is interesting and he tailors it to the time, which is so nice. There is little work outside of 2 papers and he wants you to succeed on them. Take his class. It's structured, interesting and will prepare you for other English classes

Simply phenomenal teacher and class. Take him if you ever get the chance. He truly loves what he teaches, and you will benefit from the knowledge of older literature. He is very helpful, very funny, and very professional. 10/10 recommend.

Dear Moore is an excellent lecturer and a true scholar of English literature. He can be very funny, he is wholly himself, and his knowledge of literary history is frankly astounding. I took his Bible in Literature course, which required no background in Christianity but it did make it more interesting for me to analyze the Biblical allusions.

Dean Moore is the best professor I've ever had. He gives engaging lectures, assigns reasonable amounts of work, and grades fairly. His passion for English and history makes even the most dry subjects fascinating. He also truly cares about his students and their well-being. Do yourself a favor and take ANYTHING he teaches!

Professor Moore is a great teacher and can make any subject interesting! The one drawback to his class was his very specific reading quizzes, but they are tolerable once you learn how to study for them (hint: memorize the footnotes!). I would definitely recommend taking a class with him.

I LOVE THIS MAN! I would take any course taught by him. At first I had minimal interest in poetry, but I became more interested as the course went on. He always engages his students in discussion with his charisma, humor and extensive knowledge on each poem and poet discussed. He is also very willing to help you with assignments. He is excellent!

Roger Moore is the best professor at Vanderbilt! He is everything you could ever want in a professor and more: understanding, entertaining, genuine, incredibly nice, interesting, and amazingly knowledgeable. I have also taken 208A with him and have worked with him for an independent study. Amazing.

Moore is wonderful. Don't leave Vanderbilt as an English major without taking a class from him. He is super interested and excited about what he teaches, and he is very understanding--he postponed a paper because of Rites weekend. Do the required work and you'll get a B.

Prof Moore is excellent. He has a ton of energy that makes his lectures fun and the reading interesting. He's also really fair with work and allowed paper rewrites in our class because he wants you to do well. He's willing to work with you outside of class. One of my favorite Vandy professors.

Extraordinarily talented lecturer. Engages you, encourages you, welcomes any and all comments. His grading is hard, but in a way that ensures you will put every ounce of energy and focus into your work to produce the best writing you have yet. Great for those both interested and not-so-interested in english. love that man!!!
Moore is the man. Definatly tough if you don't show up be he cares about what he is doing and will help you if you make an effort.

Professor Moore is an awesome professor and is one of the best at Vandy. HOWEVER. His classes are incredibly difficult; he assigns lots of reading, there are many quizzes, and he generally has a nasty tendency to behave as though his is the only class you're taking. Don't take him unless you can handle a heavy workload. If you can, it's worth it.
I love Prof. Moore. He's so enthusiastic about the subject and nice to his students. He's not the easiest grader, but he's fair.

You HAVE to take Moore!  He is by far the most enthusiastic professor I have ever had and he makes every class interesting.  Never looked at my watch once!  Also, the tests and papers are not graded too hard.  Love him!
He's a nice enough guy, but doesn't prioritize you if you're not a super suck up. Definitely picks his favorites and expects way too much on exams. Papers are okay, but the class is a bit ridiculous.

incredibly energetic, your hand hurts after lecture from scribbling down what he says, but tests arent hard if you go 2 class, really helpful, funny.  If he can make anglo-saxon literature entertaining at 10AM, you know hes awesome.
best english professor in the dept.  cute and entertaining too.
Difficult but amusing.
Great Professor. Very Enegetic and Positive
I hate this subject but this professor's sheer excitement everyday made me eager to come to class and deal with the boring material.
How can you not love this man? He truly cares about the material and his students.  The best professor I've had at Vandy.
Difficult class, but Moore is great.  He is very knowledgable and engages students during class.  The quizzes are hard, so be sure to study and especially look at the footnotes.

Great professor and makes poetry interesting.  Not an easy class though.  Tough quizes weekly, 4 papers and an exam. Unless you are an English major and like poetry it's not the best class to take just to fulfill a writing requirement.
One of the best teachers I have had at Vanderbilt.  He is energetic and really seems to care about his students.

Poetry is really not my thing and homosexual poetry is even more not my thing.  Difficult to relate to the subject matter and uninteresting subject matter.  Moore's an insightful guy, but poor job picking poems to read and tough grader.
I LOVE THIS MAN!!! He totally makes my Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays!  The class isn't difficult at all, and he really makes it fun.  The project at the end is a lot of work, though
He's no James Bond. However, he is incredibly interesting.  Difficult quizzes, but Moore is engaging and does make an effort to get to know his students.
He is uninteresting, doesn't give any background and has an overall skewed view of literature.  He is also very in touch with his feminine side.
Very femenine, and extremely entertaining. You will learn a lot in this class. It's difficult, but great for people who love English.

A lot of people do random crap on their laptop the entire class but they're born smart enough to spontaneously answer a question she asks. So even if you're super attentive and interested every day and just can't give a good answer to anything, you end up with a lower grade than them. Might as well not pay attention and just try to talk once a day.

Counts participation every day based on if you speak or participate in class. If you miss more than 3 classes your grade drops a letter grade and even more letter grades for further absences, so be careful. Most of the time everyone is goofin off on their computer. Even if YOU never do this, if you don't talk, you'll get a lower grade than them.

Very chill professor that has a unique "meets/doesn't meet expectations" grading scheme so you'll do good as long as you try. However, class discussions were VERY seminar based, one of the most student-discussion oriented classes I've taken even though I've taken many seminar classes. You will have to talk every day even if you are tired.

Every time many students are absent or emailed her that they're sick. She starts class by saying "looks like I'll definitely have to ask about [today's topic] on the Midterm because people are just magically absent!" And I don't know if this is supposed to be a joke but it's kinda toxic and not in good taste. Maybe she's not joking.

Prof Murray is sweet and approachable. The class covers interesting topics thru a range of media and readings. You will learn a lot. The readings get easier over the course. She wants everyone to succeed and if you do the work, it's a very manageable course. She is a fair grader. She has a strict attendance policy. I highly recommend her!

She is such a gem. Very reasonable workload- reading every night (but different formats like plays/ movies/ songs/ graphic novels to keep it interesting), seven 2-page reflections and a 5-page-paper for the midterm and final. The 3 exams were easy and required minimal studying as long as you showed up to class and did the work. Highly recommend!!!!
best prof ever. sweetest lady ever. she made me fall in love with spanish and made it clear that i wanted to double major in the subject. forever grateful to her.

Professor Murray is incredibly passionate and encourages students to lead discussion. Class consists of readings for homework and open, engaging discussions that can go anywhere, making it fascinating. He truly cares about his students. Finals were a group podcast and debate, which were enjoyable and low stress. Highly recommend.

Genuinely interested in hearing student opinions and having engaging class discussions. The topics weren't super interesting, but he tried to make it fun and approachable for the class. Wants everyone to get an A and grades very leniently. We have weekly reading assignments which are completion based, one group podcast, and one AI debate. Simple.

The best CORE teacher at Vanderbilt. He leads discussion so well, makes talking about different deep topics interesting, and uses analogies to make stuff understandable. If you participate, you will get a lot out of the class in terms of developing your thinking. He cares about his students and also loves a good sports discussion.

Professor Murray is genuinely one of the best professors I've had here, taken him twice now. The guy is so caring and knows what he's talking about when it comes to political sociology. If you have a chance to take him, do it. He doesn't care about punishing students with grades and aims to give everyone A's if you put in the work.

He is very kind and reasonable. If you try, you will get a good grade. He loves discussing topics as a class, so definitely take his section of CORE if you enjoy a back-and-forth debate structure. From what I've gathered, he is one of the best CORE teachers.

Very relaxed and effective lecturer. The discussions could get a little dry sometimes but that was more on other students than him. Timely with grading, responding to emails, etc. Overall, very good choice for CORE 1010 as he doesn't use the textbook and prefers to have broader philosophic discussions. Take him if you can, you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind and smart professor. It is a really easy class so most people never paid attention but it was actually really interesting material. He's very knowledgable and gives little homework with lenient grading. Instructions are extremely vague but it's because he wants to be flexible so just put in effort and you'll be fine.

Professor Murray delivers the most engaging "lectures," which are essentially discussions that actively involve students in the conversation. His projects are intellectually stimulating and thought-provoking. Overall, Professor Murray is an outstanding teacher, and I look forward to enrolling in another of his classes if I get the chance!

Super chill professor, just slightly reading heavy but it's manageable and it's covered in class with discussions. Very chill grader, we were graded on participation, 3 writing assignments, and biweekly discussion posts and reflections which weren't hard to do. Super understanding, and the class overall was very interesting!

Professor Murray is a great choice in the SOC department. 3 major assignments in the semester plus weekly short essays make up your grade. He was great with the online format. Lots of reading, but you can get by with skimming.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Took Sociology of Baseball. Extremely easy class. Turn in the assignments with some form of effort and you'll get an A. You get to work with other students to make a mock draft. Material is interesting. Take the class if you are passionate about baseball or just want an A.

Class was a few of two-week-long units. One/ two lectures per unit (60 mins of material per unit) and a few readings each unit. Three projects total and had to write discussion posts on Brightspace (i.e., non-intensive grading). Material was SUPER interesting, and the work wasn't too hard. Prof Murray is awesome!

I'm not a humanities person, but took Murray and was amazed at how enthusiastic he can be about every part of political sociology. He made every topic into something relevant towards our lives today and supported student discussion more than most other professors. Very lenient grader and gives you many opportunities for feedback  highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Love Murray. Lectures are quite a lot of him talking at you, but he's a really smart guys so a lot of it is really interesting and I didn't mind. Very clear about expectations, places bigger emphasis on you getting something out of the class rather than on grading tough. Complete the assignments and you'll get an A. You'll learn a lot too.

Any class about baseball is going to be fun for people who already enjoy the sport. Murray is a nice guy and sets up a really cool final project. Papers are about interesting topics and are more than manageable at 5 pages each. In class discussions ended up being fairly boring, especially on days where we focused on sociological theory.

Great professor. Sociology through baseball was an awesome class. Professor Murray really knows his stuff. No tests, only three short papers and a group project. You don't have to do any of the readings. Just make sure to skim the sociology journals for stuff to put in your papers.

This class section is specifically about business action in politics, so if you like both of those this class will interest you. The lectures can be long and boring but prof knows his stuff and loves to talk about it. Readings are long and esoteric, not necessary if you take notes in class. Final is tough but graded easily like three other papers

Murray is a great guy and has the potential to be a good professor but for now is kind of boring. There are no tests, just 3 short papers and a take home final. You won't need to read a single book he assigns until the final, but then you'll need to know the information for that paper. He basically repeats the readings aloud in class. Worth taking.
Good professor! Recommend!

Professor Murray knows his stuff. He is very laid-back and super flexible. There were no tests, only weekly reflections that took all of 10 minutes, 3 short papers, and one final paper. He gives GREAT feedback and truly wants everyone to do well. Lectures could drag on, don't HAVE to read the books, but it really helps.

He is very clear on what his requirements are, so there should never really be any confusion on what various assignments entail. If it isn't clear, he is very approachable. Overall, he is a very easy grader but assigns a great deal of reading. If you want an easy course you should take this class.

The class was interesting on most days, however some days the hour and 15 minute lecture seemed to drag on.  The first book is the worst part of the class as its pretty much an econ text book, but proves to be essential for discussion later on.  Overall the class was pretty good and from what I've heard better than most other first year seminars

He is a really easy grader and his class is set up so you don't have to do a lot of work outside of reading, just short papers. If you don't like business or politics, I wouldn't take the class. His lectures can get pretty boring and the reading is very dry and sometimes confusing. He's a really friendly, nice guy who knows what he's talking about.

Awesome professor. Graduate level reading, but going to class helps to clarify the material and make writing the papers much easier. Insightful lectures on interesting material (if you like business and politics). Would take more of classes in the future.

Professor Murray is extremely accessible, is a very easy grader, and leads interesting discussions. However, the course material is very specific and thus readings and classes are often repetitive andor boring. Enjoyable class and excellent professor!

(Had for core 1010 but not an option). shes a nice lady and very caring. you can get away with not reading the material as long as you participate a few times in discussion each day. she grades papers easy and is lenient with participation/absences. she stresses learning and improving rather than success/failure. highly recommend.

Professor Murray was wonderful! So sweet, caring, and interesting, and clearly very invested in the subject matter. Going to class and participating was very important, and she graded mostly based on grammar for papers. There were homeworks due for every class, which was annoying at times, but they were 1 page write ups, so not too bad.

Professor Murray is so sweet and helpful and an easy grader. Span 3365 Film/Cultural Trends is easy but soooo time consuming (the homework is watching 2 movies per week and writing papers about them). No tests though.

In the several classes that I've taken with her, Professor Murray has consistently been an excellent and insightful Spanish professor. She does a great job of connecting literature with social movements and realities. There is a good deal of reading and homework required, but she is a fair grader and very helpful outside of class. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Murray made me love Spanish. Coming into this class, I knew I would not enjoy it but it ended up being my favorite class of the semester. Class is made up of 4 essays and regular homework and participation. She's very helpful during office hours and revised your papers.

Professor Murray has the best-organized section of SPAN 203. There are no tests, just papers, and poetry comes at the beginning rather than the end of the section. She expects a lot, but is very helpful and encouraging.

Shabbir is a great teacher if you go to class and pay attention, which is what makes him gain respect for you as a student. If you show some interest and ask/answer questions, he will make the effort to put your needs above other students'. Very accessible outside of class, and you are prone to getting extra credit points if he likes you.

Hes a new prof but a fine choice for algo. Lectures can be confusing at times but he is great at slowing and and explaining if you ask questions. Homeworks are standardized across all profs and take a while, his tests are very fair. Attend class bc there will be random extra credit opportunities.

Came back to edit because he is so bad. Things he did: 
-cold calls
-assignment based on grading your other assignment correctly (no rubric or clarification)
-told me I was "wasting his time" in front of the class
-drops assignments and extra credit with under 24 hrs notice
-last minute quiz on reading day about material not covered in class
AVOID.

Dr. Shabbir is an amazing teacher and incredibility knowledgeable about algorithms, and theory. He always makes the class interactive and elaborates on every concept very nicely. The grading is very fair, and you have a solid understanding of algorithms after taking his course. Would strongly recommend.

There's not enough room here for me to go on about Dr. Mullane. Easily one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. She genuinely cares for her students, and if you take the time to get to know her, she can also serve as your best friend. Never been around a more authentic, bright, understanding professor like her. You will NOT regret taking her.

Best professor I have had in my Vanderbilt career. So passionate about this subject and really shows students how much she invests. Course content is engaging already, but Mullane goes out of her way to bring in guest speakers regularly and go on service learning trips. Work is so minimal and enjoyable. 100/10 recommend. DO take.

Most of this class is discussion based - many of the class periods involve watching and discussing a video, bringing in a guest lecturer, etc. She is a good teacher, and cares more about having a good discussion than just memorizing information. Field trips are fun, and the only really tough part is one big group project and two big papers.

Courtney is one of the best professors I've had! She's so sweet and genuine and it's very easy to talk with her about anything. Participation and attendance are very important, but because of the subject it's really easy to participate. Lots of guest speakers coming to talk about barriers people may face when accessing healthcare. Very informative!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof Muse (now Peterson) is very knowledgable about the subject matter, and she is helpful outside of class. She also tries to apply class to real life. She takes attendance, so you have to go to class because it meets once a week. Lots of reading with one novel due each month and a major group presentation. Participation is also important.

3 exams, a group project and attendance make up your grade. First 2 exams are pretty easy. She grades the group project based mostly on how you present more than content (ie. make eye contact!) The final (3rd exam) is tough so definitely study for that. Easy A-, a bit harder for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She's Dr. Peterson now. Class was a waste of time. She often reads directly off slides and shows videos so attendance is pointless (but part of your grade). Often tests on random info/facts that don't matter. Also cold at times. For me, her structure and style ruined interesting content. Hardly learned a thing but it's a pretty easy class.
This is the definition of an average class. Muse is a fairly boring teacher, but the class is an easy A-.

Muse is an amazing professor and the class was very interesting and well-taught. It is not hard to do well in the class, especially if you come prepared and study well before the exams. I loved this class because she really wanted to emphasize the social implications of different diseases and our health care system, and I was genuinely interested.

The class consists of two tests, a final, a paper, and attendance/participation. She really likes when you get involved in class and answer questions. Readings aren't necessary to do well just study the review and listen in class. Very nice and approachable. A lot of the information is taught through films and guest lectures which is nice.
best professor i've had at vanderbilt so far. she cares about student wellbeing and has very interesting lectures and readings. tests are fair and i learned a lot.

Super easy class, interesting too for the most part.  Only one exam, a short final essay (5pgs), a couple 2pg evaluations, and 2 in-class activities.  If you show up and take some notes, it's an easy A.  Be sure to skim the readings and participate, and show up because she takes attendance.  She's super helpful and will clarify anything you need.

Really easy class, except tests are much more involved than info in lecture.  Expect test questions to be hard and unclear and you need to know way more than just the study guide.  Dr Muse is very understanding and easy to talk to if you get on her good side by participating a lot in discussion (easy if you read), and her office hours are helpful.

Professor Muse is a very nice professor who seems to care about her students. She makes efforts to be helpful and office hours can be helpful. The tests are generally straightforward but grading can be annoyingly picky. Also, expectations on projects are not always clear. Overall a pretty good class/professor.

The easiest class I've ever taken. Learned nothing and felt like we were just feeding her ego. She's a nice lady, but is awful at communicating. I got a 100 on the midterm, and there's one small final paper. Expected to go to a middle school for the "movement". If you can deal with the feeling that you're wasting tuition then go for it, it's easy.

The class is easy, but is the most boring and useless class I've taken. She is a terrible teacher. The readings for the class are often irrelevant and non-academic. She has no business teaching at this school. Take 201 for an easy A, but if you have any intellectual curiosity whatsoever stay away.

This class is pretty easy but somewhat boring. 3 tests, a group project, and a 5 page final paper. Professor Muse is somewhat spacey and unorganized but very sweet and easy to talk to. It's a core class for MHS so I would definitely take it.

Muse is probably one of the most understanding professors I've come across. She is so approachable and really easy going. If you explain your reasoning on tests and it's valid, she'll give you credit. DO THE READING. She gets really frustrated when you don't and makes you do in-class assignments. GREAT professor, take her classes.

Easier class for those used to hard science classes. Reading the book not needed at all, but I do suggest taking *very* detailed notes in class to answer the more specific test questions. No biggie if you have a laptop, but she goes fast so handwriting can be hard. Tests moderate, and a 20 pg final paper that is a huge pain. She's helpful though.

Professor Muse's class is by far the easiest I have taken at Vanderbilt.  However, it is also extremely one sided. I can not remember another time at Vanderbilt where I have been so disappointed in the lack of discussion and debate on policy issues.  If you are conservative---watch out!

Good teacher, Good class.  Very Biased professor.  I have no problem with her teaching, but I do have issue with what she doesn't teach.  There are two sides to every argument and she isn't concerned with views not congruent with her own.  But still a good teacher
Awesome professor!  Very interested in the material and in students really learning.  Always helpful outside of class.  Not too tough either!  Just do the work and you'll get a good grade.

Amazing teacher! Professor Muse will go out of her way to help you in her class. Her tests are pretty easy as long as you read the material and take good notes in class. She is very understanding and very interesting. Very easy grader on papers. Also, she's probably the best-dressed professor I've ever had.

One of the kindest, most approachable, and most understanding instructors at Vanderbilt. Extremely fair grader - if you don't get an A, it's your own fault. 4 response papers, 2 tests, final exam. Class participation important. Highly recommended. Also, she's hot.

She's great! truly interested in teaching the material in an applicable way and gives many opportunities to make good grades. grades fairly. class is not hard if you just put in some effort. definitely take her!

great teacher... very nice and helpful during office hours.. made transition to college great... enjoyed class, would take class with her again if i could. I definitely recommend to anyone... and class material is very interested and open to all view points...  But all together, had a great time in class, and go to office hours she's a very helpful

Dr. Myers is a very sweet and approachable professor. He is very knowledgable and will answer any questions. Do the study guide for the tests - they help a lot. Keep up with readings and pay attention to how he words things in class. I would recommend emailing the TA if you have any questions outside of class, because he is a bit slow responding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Myers does not do well in the virtual environment. Unclear test guidelines and wants things worded in his exact way. Not the best teaching style and I haven't really learned anything. Maybe hes better in person but the class is structured kind of weird. He needs answers in his exact wording or else he'll mark you wrong.

Prof. Myers requires you to write word-for-word what he says in lecture in order to get A's on his exams. The class is graded on a 100 point scale and the exams are 25%. His lectures are hard to follow and very boring, but attendance is mandatory (and taken every class). I would not take this class with himas I've heard the other teacher is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am currently enrolled in MHS 1940 as a freshman and I thoroughly enjoy the class. The class is lecture heavy and there are not too many grades (2 tests, 3 brief 2-page papers and one final paper), but I truly feel as if I learned a lot. The expectations for the class are clear and Dr. Myers is very accessible to meet outside of class as well.

Community Health Research Myers is extremely picky and biased. If you don't use the exact wording he has in his head then you will not do well. Grading is extremely variable and unpredictable. I studied the exact same amount for both exams and received an A on one and a C on the other.

Very nice guy, but would not recommend as a professor. Lectures are long and boring, and grading is very picky. He wants things exactly a certain way (usually in his words) and if you deviate from that he penalizes you point-wise.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best Professors I have had at Vanderbilt University. Warm, kind, and empathetic! I learned a lot from his class, and I hope to take more classes with him.
Prof. Myers seems like a nice guy. But he is unwilling to meet outside of class to help. Very biased and unclear.

Class changing to MHS 235 next year, but will be same. BORING. Repeated so many topics. 2 written midterms, 12 page final paper. Nice guy but never gave rubrics so grading was subjective. Lets class out late every time. Not a difficult class, but very dull.

This class is a gem! Professor Wooders has a great course on coalition theory, cooperative games, and advanced game theory applications. Relatively little specific math is required; Prof. Wooders made me comfortable with intermediate probability theory, light calculus,and matrix algebra. Her lecture PSETs compliment the topics in the course greatly

ECON 4260 with Professor Wooders is one of the best classes I've taken. Working through problems on the board made it super engaging, and even when I messed up, I learned so much from talking it through. She's open to talking about life and whatever's on your mind. I can't recommend it enough if you're looking for a meaningful learning experience!

"Go listen to your teachers old and contrary

Without believing a word."

-- John Crowe Ransom, Class of 1909, Vanderbilt University

Wooders is completely lost and is certainly not in the right shape to teach a class. She is not representative of what a Vanderbilt professor should be and I am certain she would be terminated if the Econ department paid attention to its professors. Between the messy lectures, unclear subject, and lack of structure, do not take her. It is wasteful.

Her methodology of teaching is confusing, inconsistent, and unreasonable. Does not reply to emails almost all the times. Extremely condescending and has little respect to students. Her class is the biggest joke ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't give many practice problems or homework so you'll have to do a lot of out of class studying to get practice. You won't be able to complete problems on quizzes and tests (primary chunk of your grade) unless you've gotten practice. Her lecturing is the worst I've seen at Vanderbilt. It takes her 100 sentences to explain a concept worth 5.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I fail almost everything in this class lol - I gave it a good shot but it truly is impossible to do well. Sure you can self study and understand game theory concepts but you will not do well since the quizzes are extremely random and exams are crazy. Touted as "one of the best game theorists in the world" but can't teach an undergrad course...

Could go on forever regarding the reasons I dislike her and her teaching style. Would be far better off not going to class and just reading the textbook, but that still wouldn't prepare me for her exams. Horrible about providing any sort of feedback, and depends on the ta to actually clarify anything for us.
badbadbad

She is the worst professor I have ever had during my years at Vanderbilt. She barely knows what she's teaching (she couldn't solve the problems she give out). Even if you are 120% focusing on what she's teaching, you're getting 50% on your midterm because she doesn't even teach what will be on the midterm. PURE EVIL

You know how sometimes when you go to sleep and you're worried you might be sick? The fever dream that confirms this illness is Professor Wooders' class, filled with some of the most random anecdotes and a distinct lack of relevant content. It would be harder to eat a seed and poop out plants than to get an A

The worst professor I've seen at Vandy by far. She doesn't seem like she even knows what is happening half of the time and provides 0 context of what you are going to be tested on. She covers certain topics in class then tests you on things that have never been covered. Avoid at ALL costs!!

Easily the worst professor or instructor I've had for any class at any level. Impossible to learn from her confusing and disorganized lectures, and takes pride in not telling you what to study before the exams, which would be frustrating if there were any resources to study from in the first place. Do not take her
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wooders is terrible, she can't teach and does not even rely on the textbook, so it is impossible to teach yourself the material. Her grading criteria is arcane, all the tests are cumulative but she refuses to release answer keys to past tests, so you can't know what you did wrong. Worst professor at Vanderbilt hands down.

unfortunately, this class is basically a computer lab. the professor doesn't interact well with the class, and seems to be in her own little world (sometimes she randomly laughs, its confusing). no one (or the TA) has a clue what is going on. quizzes/tests are impossible but she let's you redo for partial credit - still ends up a bad grade tho.

So literally hurt when I do Professor Wooders's questions. Like literally, she's just the naughty child in her questions. Like OMG, I think I really need some help from consoling center. Like she's literally just awful and I literally just wanna cry... sniff sniff
I go to class and leave more confused than when I arrived. In the second week, she accidentally started lecturing on endangered species of the midwest. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An old snobbish lady who loves to pretend that she is no.1 in everything.
Absolutely awful, confusing and frustrating! Poor homework! Cheat students in disguising her homework!
Her homework sometimes is like the emperor's new clothes. Only "clever students" can see them, because they don't even exist!
The worst. Does not teach AT ALL in class.
Literally plays coursera videos in class. Are my parents paying money for this?
Awful! Awful! So frustrating!
Myrinina Wooding was the first person I ever met. I'm sorry, I way too tired to write. God Bless.
Do not take Professor Wooders. Bad lectures. Hard homework.
Her problem sets are horrible and frustrating. They are destined to send students into counseling centers, if they don't kill themselves. She is committing crimes against humanity!
Simply the most awful professor in Vanderbilt - boring lectures, anger-inspiring class slides. Not worth the money the university pays her.

Don't take her class. She is a funny person but you don't know what she is talking about. She sometimes denies herself and her handwriting is so bad that you can not recognize what she is writing. She is always absent from the course and never follow the textbook.

If you have the chance to take one of her classes, you should. She is very intelligent and funny. The class is structured differently than the usual but if you ask for clarification on assignments and homework, she will help you. Also, Professor Wooders really cares about you and wants you to do well in her class.

The most unorganized professor I have ever had. She is unclear about expectations for the class and the few lectures she gave were poorly structured. Lots of class time wasted. The class was 3 quizzes and a final paper, but we didn't get most of our assignments back. Not that hard, but you won't learn much at all.

She is one of the best professors I've had. I think that she has great knowledge of the topics in this class. All questions were answered and she provides real world examples of how things work. Sometimes things can be unorganized but she is understanding and asking questions about the assignments etc. is advised.

Knows more about networks than anyone else at Vandy or elsewhere. Very knowledgeable, relatively easy teacher. Lots of group projects makes the class pretty interesting. Has tons of interesting stories.

Nice professor, but very unorganized. Cares about what students learn. Definitely better for smaller classesgo to her office hours or email her. Not as bad as her ratings say, class is really easy if you just show up and listen. Frequently makes math errors when she does problemswatch for that on the board.

I honestly think she cares about her students deep down, but she is incredibly unorganized and unpredictable. Decided not to give the second midterm and instead give weekly quizzes, but we hardly had any. Will assign homework and then forget about it. The content isn't that hard though and she's kind of a pushover. Still a frustrating class/prof
This professor is not fair in grading. She has prefers. Avoid her class, she does not care about teaching. You will learn nothing from her course.
Worse ever. She agrees with everyone even if their answers contradict with each other. Definitely no preparation for the classes.

Woooders is very difficult. Lectures are useless - she can't teach. Never around during her office hrs and really unhelpful in general. Lots of hw and the tests never seem to reflect whats done in class (tons of suprises). Wooders views the low grades as the failure of students alone, and is not sympathetic when 2/3 of the class fails. Avoid her!
Avoid at all costs. if you haven't figured that out yet.
SHE IS MESERABLE
Convinced she's very nice, she just needs to make things more clear and to tell the class what to study for tests.

She was one of the most unclear and misleading professors I have ever been under.  She is completely useless as a lecturer and provides no reasonable explanation as to what will be on tests.  Hard only becasue figuring out what to study on her test is like guessing the lottery.

Teaches above the level of the student.  Makes material hard to understand.  Handouts and in class practice problems have a lot of mistakes so after you have studied them, you later find out the information was incorrect.
terrible

Tough class but be ready to teach yourself all the content from slides because he is one of the least engaging professors I have ever had. Lots of linear algebra. Go to the TA for your homework and start early. Some of them take very long but you only need to do five. Quizzes were take-home and you get to look at the problems before.

Class was super difficult, but good curve in the end. Very clear he cares about the students, would hold additional office hours at 9 pm. One of the only classes where it the professor worked harder than I did. Also, make friends in the class and grind the HW together, otherwise it'll take multiple days of work. The HW is great prep for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This guy CANNOT teach

First impression was that teaching us annoyed him. BUT, at one point I got very ill and he allowed me more time to finish something. He realized I cared a lot about the class. When I was finally well enough to finish the project, he'd said it was one of the best he'd ever seen. I know he is not the friendliest, but he DOES care. It meant a lot. Thx
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He was extremely and unnecessarily rude to the TA's and to the students, for what seemed like no apparent reason. It was as if he made the effort to be a miserable and mean person. Extremely prideful. Think twice before doing or saying something if you dont want to get berated publically. Horrible experience but the material is easy enough

One of the worst professors I've had by far. He's a tough grader and expects near perfect application of the material though he provides little guidance towards that standard. Provides poor in class lectures, and is open to questions but often gives rude and misleading answers where he does the work himself teaching you nothing.

This professor is one of our best in our department. He has master understanding on robotics and he really cares for the students. I learnt a lot and I love Nabil. He deserves a much better score than this.

has very inconsistent policies. classes: fast paced/ boring/not mandatory. however,  He can arbitrarily take Up to 10pts off semester GradE. Berated the tA for handing out noteS at the wrong timeS.  homework takes awhile.  what He tOLd us wouldn't be on the Exams was on the exams for a lot of points. for what its worth, he is really good at creo
Very unclear lecturer. Actually just a plain bad lecturer. Very standoffish and unhelpful. was kind of bitter and mean when you come to office hours. Class wasn't too bad, Nabil was.

Although he's has an accent and can be hard to understand, this professor is extremely good at what he does and knows what he's talking about. If you put in the time and effort you can learn a lot. He has high standards and a dry sense of humor but really does care about his students learning the material as long as they care.

I took this class as a technical elective (not a MechE) thinking it would be a normal intro class, but it functioned almost as a weed-out class for MechEs.  There was no clear grading standard making it difficult to perform well on the assignments/final project. Final grade was higher than I expected and I learned a lot (by teaching myself), though
Workload is absurd and he offers little to no help

He obviously knows a lot about the subject, but that translated to him pouring way too much material into an intro class. It made the class very work-heavy and at times overwhelming. He was also not very clear about what he wanted for each assignment. Even the TAs had to work hard to keep up with his expectations. Also terrible with communication

Yikes. This guy was bad. He's a smart guy who knows what he's talking about but his teaching skills just aren't there.  Due to this he has huge expectations for tests and assignments, yet doesn't provide students with the tools to be successful, and with a subject like this it's really hard to learn anything form the textbook or online. Good luck.

Easily the worst professor I have ever had. Gives no expectations when it comes to grading yet even the TA's say he is way too strict. Grades aren't given back for weeks and he will double assign problems without giving you feedback on the first time you did it. Sorry you have to take this class, but try to pick another professor.

Mike Myers' class was a lot of fun, but a lot of work and understanding is required in this course. Read and work problems out of the book and online as much as possible. Professor Mike will support you 100%.  I let my career get in the way of my studies and I feel short performing where I should have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof Myers is nice, funny, and caring. Wish I could have him for a class that was more interesting in CS because I feel like he is limited with discrete being a pretty boring/hard topic. Told us to do the study guide/work on discrete a  little daily & I should have listened to from the start so is my fault I did so poorly. Fun activities in class!

Dr. Myers is a great teacher. Discrete Structures is a difficult subject to teach and he does a good job of explaining it. My only critique would be that he uses powerpoint too much sometimes. Overall: great guy, hard class, but he makes it fun and doable.

Mike Myers is a solid professor. His lectures are slow and he assigns small, busy writing assignments every week, but he grades leniently. There are only two, very manageable, long paper assignments (1000-3000 words), and two tests that are taken on the computer. Overall, Myers is a good pick and an A is easily attainable if you put in some effort.

Easy class but difficult to get an A, most students end up in the A- range. TONS AND TONS OF WRITING. They need to make this a W course. I have written in this class more than any other. But Professor Myers is a super chill guy, definitely take him.

He made the class interesting with the long current event discussions at the beginning of class, but a lot of the work felt irrelevant and annoying to complete. Not a bad professor, the work was just a lot.

This class involve a lot of short assignments. The material was very dry and abstract. However, the professor was very good making the class as interesting as possible. Class involved going over powerpoints and an occasional activity. An A is attainable, but it there is a lot of written work.
Lot of busy work, didn't really learn anything, teacher just reads off the slides, very useless class, A is attainable

Professor Myers makes the class pretty interesting. He always maintains a jolly atmosphere in the classroom. The class consists of various assignments and also has one final project. The class in itself isn't too rigorous, however, assignments could take a while to complete.

Very helpful when students are struggling with assignments  and has open office hours. The course material was pretty dry, but if you put solid effort into the assignments and reports you can do well. The project is a big component of your grade, and he lets you do basically whatever you want.

Always helpful during office hour. Grade your assignment based on your report, not the model itself. The assignment are easy enough if you know how to Google about Simulink. Spend most of my time for assignment in googling stuffs.
Professor Myers was fun and enthusiastic. He enjoyed to incorporate movies with his lectures.I would love to take another class with Big Mike!
Homework can be tricky, but forgiving grades if reports are well thought out. Most of your grade in the class is based on a final project, which is very open ended and can be fun.
Very nice guy. He's always helpful whenever I go to his office. The class, however, is not that interesting.
He seems to be a professor reading straight out of powerpoint. No point taking the lecture. Easy quiz

It's a good thing the textbook (Hibbeler) is helpful because Dr. Myers is not able to explain further than what you can learn from the book, which I guess is understandable since this is not his field. Lectures are not very important. Expect a LOT of busywork. Fair though somewhat unclear grading and a harsher grading scale than other professors.
Dr. Myers is an amazing professor. He made the class very interesting and a lot of fun. There is quite a bit homework assigned for the class though.

Class was really easy. You have to go to class because the class size is small so he will know if you're not there.  However, you do not learn much in class, just discuss scenarios that relate to what we are reading in the textbook.  A lot of busy work, but  it is easy. If you go to class and do the work, the worst grade you can get it a B.
Great Teacher

Be ready to know all possible assumptions in the most specific form. And don't rely on the the assumptions he tells you in class, he'll change his mind when it get to the exam. A lot of busy work for the course, but the content isn't too hard.  Lectures are pointless since he just has you work example problems that are in the book already.

Class was very challenging, homework due every day as well as projects, online quizzes, and difficult tests. Almost no easy points. Mike cares about his students and communicates with the class well but will make you work for a good grade. You will learn a lot, though.
You did not learn much in the class and literally need to study by yourself in order to survive the course but he is a really kind and fun professor.

Very nice professor; extremely helpful and understanding. The homework is directly related to exam material and is graded relatively easily. The exams are graded more rigorously, but are still very fair. If you need this class for a requirement, I highly recommend taking it with Professor Myers.

Expect a lot of homework, though solutions manual is online and it is graded based on accuracy. There is usually at least two to three homework assignments due every class. On top of this, there are weekly online quizzes that cover chapter reading however they are fairly easy. The tests are fairly vague in what he is looking for in answers.
The course material is not that challenging, but Myers assigns too much work for how little material there is. His grading is strict but pretty fair.
Good guy, tough grader on tests.
The class overall is not hard but tests ask you assumptions and stuff that you cannot really get right. Good guy and wants you to do well.
White old woman who comes from the old world and it shows. Will give unclear instructions and then give you a bad grade.

You can't go wrong taking a fiction workshop with Reisman. She has mastered the ability to teach this class, wants the best for her students and their stories, and creates an awesome classroom environment. Plus she often brings chocolate covered almonds to class.

I really like Professor Reisman. She gives solid, constructive feedback on your stories, but she doesn't take them over with her own ideas. She'll talk with you and help you realize your vision for your own work. She is a really sweet woman and I appreciated having her as a professor this semester.

Nancy is the best honestly.  If you're into creative writing you should take her class.  She's very good at working with individuals rather than groups and because of that always takes an interest in each student's work in a unique way

Professor Reisman is kind and encouraged me in my writing. She's concerned about each of her students as writers and people, and that really stuck with me. The class is great because you basically read short stories and novels and discuss them, then write your own short fiction based on what you see in the readings. She gives great feedback too!

Prof. Reisman is passionate about creative writing. This class is a great opportunity to get inspired and explore the way you write. I do think Prof. Reisman could do a better job facilitating interesting class discussions. Paper prompts are too vague but can be interesting. Write a good paper and you'll get a good grade, prepare to work for it.

This class is ok, not a lot of work and she honestly does most of the talking in class you can kind of just sit there. A good amount of reading but they are all short stories. If you don't enjoy creative writing it's not for you.

She's really passionate about creative writing and about teaching. Her face lights up when she sees her students and she's really a joy to work with one-on-one. That said, she's a much better writer than lecturer--she gets to her points in a roundabout way.

Professor Reisman is great - she has a deep appreciation of fiction and her class discussions were always very productive and enlightening.  She exposed us to great works and authors and her comments on papers were always constructive and helped you earn a better grade.  Only 2 absences but class was fun and not hard to go to.
Great Professor, probably the best I've had at Vanderbilt, and an awesome writer, read The First Desire.

Prof. Reisman is one of few professors I've had whose interest in the field and enjoyment of teaching is apparent everyday in class, and this made a difference in a creative writing class based upon quality of professor feedback and the general interest level displayed in students' work.
She really enjoys creative writing and imparting the craft. Her knowledge of the department and where to get help is great.
No Comments

Dr. Schley is one of the best lecturers I've had. He does an amazing job at explaining concepts, using just the right amount of real world examples to get points across. I thought the exams were designed very well and sufficiently tested our progress. Office hours were super helpful.
Goat status

Pros: straightforward tests, no textbook, all info presented in class, kind prof who cares about students, easily accessible, class average was high, presentation/paper was pretty easy Cons: sometimes goes fast, no slides (he writes all the notes on the chalkboard and you have to copy it down fast)

Dr. Schley is great - definitely one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. The class isn't too hard at all if you take good notes and study from them. Test questions generally came directly from the notes he wrote on the board. Final project instead of a final, which is nice. Great guy and engaging lectures. Would recommend taking his class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers you can get at Vanderbilt. Never gave an uninteresting lecture, and is truly a genius. Wish I could take him for every chem class.

Dr. Schley does an excellent job teaching an interesting and complex course on organometallics. He does an incredible job of setting the foundational knowledge up firmly, which makes learning the theories and intricacies of catalysis much more manageable. You also won't find a more understanding and kind professor. I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This man knows how to teach what can I say

Prof Schley is one of the new additions to the Chemistry Department and he really takes interest in undergraduate teaching. He delivers straightforward lectures and write clear and organized notes. The tests are reasonable and manageable. Class materials are interesting and his research is even cooler!
She is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. She really improved my French, and the class discussions were excellent and enjoyable.

For someone who seems like such a nice and caring person on the surface, It's incredibly disappointing to see that the act isn't genuine. Keys to success in the class are either befriending her or raising your hand and responding to everything. It's a double-edged sword, but it inherently puts more timid people at a disadvantage.

Nathalie is AMAZING. She really cares about her students and helping be comfortable in the class. She speaks really fast, and it is a bit hard to understand her at times, but it definitely gets easier. There is lots of homework for every class session, but we do get to all of it at some point. Weekly partner presentations on movies and tv shows.

I love NDM! She's such a sweet and caring professor and her lectures are incredibly interesting. The homework is really heavy but the discussions are super interesting so it's worth it. Probably my favorite professor at Vanderbilt.

NDM is a great professor, and her lectures are wonderful if you can keep up with her French (she rarely speaks English). She does assign quite a lot to read and watch, but most of the material is wonderful. Assignments are clear and straightforward if you study and write well. Not too hard to get an A but you have to put the work in. Overall, great

I learned more in Madame Miller's class than in most other courses at Vanderbilt. Her level of energy is infectious and you will never, ever fall alseep in her class or get bored. She teaches at a fast pace but her expectations are clear concerning papers and quizzes/exams. If you read the texts and take notes, you can get an A for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Debrauwere-Miller is absolutely wonderful. I took two of her classes (French Lit. and French Feminism) and loved them both. Her energy and enthusiasm are infectious. She also explains things really well and won't hesitate to help you if you're having trouble understanding something. One of my all-time favorite professors!

I had her for the French feminist class. She was so great! She was energetic and passionate even when met with blank stares (the readings can be challenging at times). Fair grader and very approachable. Tip: keep up with the homework even though she doesn't collect it. When you have to write your essay you'll be glad you did.

She is the BEST. contagious passion for french lit and is excellent at teaching it. Lectures give enormous amounts of info but are very conversational, engaging, and useful for tests. Quizzes often but so helpful. Pretty easy grader, just put the work in. Really really cares about students. Every other french class pales in comparison to this one.

This is a French major/minor requirement so regardless you have to take it and Professor Debrauwere-Miller is so great. She's so positive and enthusiastic about the topic. She assigns extensive homework but doesn't collect it. Can seem overwhelming but just going to class, taking good notes, and studying for class will get you a good grade.

I was miserable in this class. It was inefficiently taught, and I don't feel like I learned much about French lit. We studied lots of little excerpts and only 2 major texts, and the analysis of them was painful. Any comment you make is never quite right, and she makes you feel like you aren't good enough to be in the class.

Loved this class and loved this professor.  Graduated in 2005 and had this professor several times.  This "French Feminist Thought" class was really interesting and thought provoking.  Would certainly recommend it.

I took Intro to French Lit. She was an easy grader, although I sometimes had a hard time keeping up with her in French. I loved the fact that we had to memorize a poem, and that the whole class was taught in French. It really improved my French.

I loved her! She was always organized and taught the material clearly making sure everyone understood it. She seems strict at first, but really isn't. She's an average grader, not too hard. I'm so sad she's leaving for the Vandy program in France thisyear
It's really annoying that she won't change or settle for the sake of the class, even though the work is too much and doesn't have much of a useful use.

Professor Neely is AMAZING!! This class is so much fun, you learn a lot about different types of children's literature and isn't just for education majors. Keep on top of assignments-there's lots of little assignments that can be challenging if you get behind. Midterms are the most difficult thing in the class, but easily passable.
So passionate about diverse books! Take this class if you love to read!!!
This class is just frustrating--the workload is overwhelming, the practical application is next to nothing, and she is not willing to compromise or change for needs of the class.

Fantastic. Those who don't like her are in Education to get the Mrs. degree or an easy A. She expects a lot of her students but keeps it very interesting, is extremely helpful and concerned about her students outside of class. She is very knowledgeable, fair, organised and has very clear expectation
Very excited about children's lit, inspiring. You learn a lot in this class, although there are a lot of assignments. Grading isn't overly easy, but fair.
She knows the subject very well and keeps class very interesting.  There is a lot of work (assignments), but her grading scale and expectations are very fair.
wonderful professor! lots of fun books and interesting information.  good ideas about how to use literature in the classroom, one of the best courses i've take at peabody
extremely knowledgable, very prepared, loves teaching!
No Comments
One of the worst teachers ever
No Comments
Course is structured poorly, he goes over a million things and expects you to memorize every formula with no cheat sheet on exams. He also teaches like he is displeased with life :/

This class should be titled "probability theory." While I was hoping to get into more applied concepts, mostly was spent generalizing and proving already-understood concepts from 2810/2820. Neamtu isn't the hardest math prof but still def not an easy A. Sometimes idk if he knew what he was teaching. 30% HW, 2 midterms and final.

He somehow cannot fully understand of what he want to teach. HW twice a week but only grade one or two questions. Grading is super-unclear, in which students cannot understand why they get points off. For each midterm, there is always one question out of the test curriculum. No notes sharing, two textbook being used and meaning useless.

Cool dude, pretty easy for a Vandy math class. Starts out a bit challenging and gets easier after the first midterm. Wish we went a bit faster through the content, sometimes felt like we were doing the same things over and over again, then didn't get a chance to learn the things I was interested in.

Decent lecturer (funny), great in office hours. Overall a good dude, but Neamtu can be a bit condescending with calling often-difficult equations/concepts "simple," "easy," or "obvious." Learn the practice problems in and out, because luckily test questions are pretty similar. HW worth 40% so don't lose hope if a midterm goes poorly. Go to class.

Neamtu is amazing! Clear lectures, not many homeworks, easy exams as long as you pay attention in class. Practice problems are really useful and similar to test problems. Would recommend his classes to everyone. Also, definitely take his class if you are into dry math jokes.

Great  funny and engaging lecturer. Easy homework , quizzes. Tests are very manageable if you make sure you understand how concepts work. Very helpful! I learned a lot of real-life applicable things! Great course!

Mike is a decent teacher but it's best just not to go to lecture except to take quizzes; the book is enough. HW is optional but quizzes either parallel hw problems or ARE hw problems so you should definitely do the homework. Tests range from easy to hard. Very manageable class. Mike structures it well, but isn't easy to contact or work with

Lectures are hit-or-miss. Half the time you can understand him, half the time you can't. Test questions similar to in-class examples and practice problems, so there shouldn't be too many surprises on his exams.

Neamtu has a sense of humor drier than the Sahara. That said, he's a pretty straight forward guy, the tests aren't easy but if you put in the work you can do fine. Go to class as much as you can tolerate multivariable calculus.
one of the best teacher I have ever had. Super funny and great lecturer! highly recommended!
He was very dry, but clear and he put a lot of test questions into his lecturers.

No curve, but generous partial credit, tests have only a few problems, but parts a-f, you have to work fast to finish them. Derivations given but a little circuitous and hard to follow. Homework is absolutely necessary to getting a good grade. Classmates have said they got better test scores where they just wrote illegible gibberish than did work.

I thought that he was rather entertaining.  He did a good job of teaching the class.  The book was good for a complement though.  It wasn't much work at all and the tests were extremely similar to the homework.  It was interesting though and I do think that I actually learned something.

Mike has a bit of an Eastern European Accent but not hard to understand. Explains techniques pretty clearly; teaches you how to do everything for all tests. Not super helpful outside of class but class is so not demanding, you wont need help. Easy, occassional HW asignments. easy tests. Hard final but he'll curve. easiest 175 teacher for sure.
One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt.

Sometimes a little confusing in the way he explains things, but he is an interesting and funny guy.  The tests were easy until the final, which was extremely hard.  He gives a lot of partial credit though and tries to help you make a decent grade.  Overall, good professor.

crazy hard class.  his style of teaching is very strange, because sometimes he seems to be going through the motions, and other times he tries very hard to get you to understand the material.  somewhat boring and unhelpful lecturer.  not very approachable in my opinion, but i know someone who is constantly at his office hours, so could just be me.

He is by far the worst math professor I've encountered at Vanderbilt so far.   He is not fair in his grading, nor is he consistent.  He is completely rude and unhelpful outside of class.  Do NOT take him under any circumstances!!

The man's accent is puzzling at times, and he sometimes explains things in a roundabout, confusing manner, but he bases his class around real life applications and a charming humor that is lacking in so many other math classes at Vandy.  Mike keeps it real.  Plus, you can always tell how he's doing on the stock market by how good of a mood he's in.

The class was hard, but Neamtu is not too bad of a teacher.  He sometimes goes on tangents, but for the most part stays on task.  His tests are hard, but he goes over most of what you need to know for it in class.

He expects you to work but he is a fair grader and will always help you when you need it.  He is a little sarcastic and full of himself but if you don't take it personally and can joke around with him, you should do fine in the class. Just don't let him intimidate you too much. I think he's great.
fun teacher, accent very odd at times.  rambles incoherently about google a lot, but overall a funny guy... it's a shame the class material is such a waste of time.
Tests are very reasonable but he has an odd grading system.
No Comments
An amusing guy who likes his math jokes.  Lectures are fast-paced, but understandable.  Definitely not an easy or simple class, but he's a fair grader.
Accused me of plagiarizing and greatly hurt my grade though I actually wrote it all.
She's very knowledgeable and an amazing lecturer but can be unnecessarily harsh at grading and following guidelines or codes.

Prof. Hemmer is amazing! Her lectures are super engaging and she posts lectures online which makes them really easy to reference for papers. 3 papers, no exams, which I personally loved. Make sure to attend and participate in discussion. She gives great feedback and is a pretty kind grader. One of the best professors I've had here!!

My favorite professor I've had at Vandy! Her lectures were super engaging and I actually enjoyed going to them. Lots of papers (I don't like writing) but she was a fair grader and gave pretty good feedback. Overall super wonderful person and professor. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her!
Dr. Hemmer is a great professor and a great choice for the Majors Seminar. She is always willing to read students' drafts and to give thorough feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Labs are boring but the TAs always let you out early and they should only take a few hours outside the class. They are graded very lightly (hard to get below a 90 on a lab). The midterm is the only hard thing in the class and I got a 70 on it so actually study for it but still ended with an A-. Easy way to get your lab credit over with.

As a non-stem major, this class is pretty dueable. Grades are based off Tophat, homeworks, take home quizzes and test. I got Cs on all of my tests but still managed a B+ in the class. Prof. Kelley also offers a zoom every class so you do not even have to go in person everytime which is pretty nixe. Actual lectures are boring but he tries!

EES1030 was pretty hard for me and my friends (non-STEM kids). The lab is like 10 pgs worth of confusing questions that take hours every week. The HW assignments in lecture are same long vibe. Tests were fair, but he covers a lot of content. Glad I got my AXLE lab done but be prepared to sweat if you want an A and aren't used to college science.

Professor Kellet is kind, understanding, and energetic even during 9am lecture. Participation is through Top Hat and textbook is not required, just suggested. He made lecture available through Zoom and had weekly small quizzes based on that weeks lectures. A few homework assignments throughout the semester.

Kelley had engaging lectures that appealed to both the STEM and non-STEM students in the class. Make sure and pay attention in class, and you should get a decent grade. Not too much homework and easy to reach when you need help, but he can be a bit disorganized at times. Overall, really enjoyed the class!

Professor Kelley has some of the most engaging lectures. He is very funny and can make anybody (including non-STEM students) interested in oceanography. This is a great MNS class to take if you are looking for something interesting with a light workload. He also lets you drop one of the 3 exams, which is clutch. Take Oceanography with Kelley.

This was for EES 2510, not EES 1510. He's a chill professor that is enthusiastic about the content. He is disorganized, but he just removes assignments that become delayed rather than punishing the students for it. Grading is not strict, but it is extremely helpful to take EES 1510 before this class.

I love Neil and highly recommend his Life Thru Time class! His lectures are engaging and his passion shines through the material. His main problem is with being disorganized, but this was never a problem for me because he is self aware about it and doesn't make it the students' problem. He often brings his dog to class which is a joy.

Prof. Kelley is caring, and one of the best professors I have had during my time at Vanderbilt. As long as you listen to lectures and fill out the study guides, I think you should be good for the class. Definitely recommend for anyone looking for a not-too-difficult science credit.

Definitely my favorite class so far! He is an enthusiastic teacher who gives interesting lectures and uses TopHat (which is pretty fun & interactive) to help keep attendance (not graded for accuracy). There is a final and 2 midterms & 1 gets dropped. Just study your lecture notes and slides, and you will do well!

Awesome professor that made a boring topic really interesting. Does not take attendance and gives awesome practice exams and study guides. Easy weekly homework assignment. Great class to take for a lab requirement also. I recommend this class to all my friends.

I was a little disappointed as he was super highly rated before. Nice guy but boring class with exams unrelated to lecture content. Exams are awful but study a ton and youll be fine. Honestly only 20 of 100 people even went to lecture, so if you want a cram class and chill otherwise take it. If you like incremental learning, do not take it.
Makes grading way too harsh. I studied my butt off for the class and I still haven't done too well.
this guy is a mess. he makes your tests worth your entire grade basically and won't really help outside of class. try accessing him, you won't be able to.

Heres the thing, the whole point of AXLE is to allow students to explore different areas of studies. All prof. Kelly managed to do this semester was make this content as boring as possible. Sure we talked about interesting stuff here and there, but it is massively outweighed by the boring memorization we have to do. AVOID THIS CLASS

Solid choice for professor. As long as you put in the bare minimum effort and not slack off you'll do well. Tests and quizzes are mostly memorization. Lectures are a bit dry at some times, but homework is overall very easy and straightforward. Records lectures, super helpful if you can't make it to class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR AXLE CREDIT! All the exams are just random memorization. I took this class expecting it to be an easy A, but it ended up having a heavier workload than my major classes. The lab itself was easy, but damn this class sucked. Prof Kelly is nice, but if you dont care much for oceanography stay away from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bad professor. bad class. doesn't care to respond to emails. grading is stupid.

Grading is stupid. He takes forever to grade things and it is based such a small sample size. Tests are weighed very heavily and it is just a bunch of dumb memorization. He doesn't respond to emails if you have questions. He makes it much harder to do well in his class than it should be.

Labs are run by the TAs, but I have only heard of them being easy graders. Expectations are very clear. Just show up to lab and don't miss. Hard to get below a 95 on a lab. Make sure you put in effort for the one test though. Just follow labs and ask questions in class. Super easy lab science for requirement. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory. You can teach yourself from the textbook. It is optional but buy it. Super nice professor and easily accessible. As long as you put in effort to the homeworks and tests you will get an A. Tests are not hard, but you have to study for at least three days. Great MNS class for non stem people.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He never gets grades back and lectures are all over the place. The tests are basically questions from his study guides but the study guides and tests don't clearly connect to the course content. It's the kind of course where you think you can slack off early but you lowkey can't. Super boring but nice guy.
Professor Kelley was awesome and my EES 1030 lab couldn't have been better. Clear instructions and a fair grader. If you have the chance, be sure to take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Kelley was my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He cares a lot about the material and creating a welcoming environment for students. Also he's very funny and I love the memes he puts in his lectures. Would take any class of his just because he makes everything so interesting.

Dr. Kelley's enthusiasm promotes enthusiasm in his students. One of the nicest Professors I've had at Vanderbilt University. This is probably my favourite class I've taken in two years. If you take detailed notes and stay on top of the lectures (which move pretty quickly and in depth), you'll do great.

I took this for a Chem Ed requirementdefinitely glad I did. Dr. Kelley is truly kind, caring, and fair. He listens to student feedback and is incredibly supportive. Glad I took his class, especially during Covid-19, b/c his teaching brightened up my semester. My advice: take good notes during lecture & use his study guides!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I knew nothing about oceanography prior to this class, but Prof. Kelly made it enjoyable and engaging. His lectures can be dry at times, but he cares a lot about his students and you can tell how much he enjoys teaching. Despite the large nature of the class, he's very accessible, and always willing to provide help if you need it.

Dr. Kelley is an awesome professor. He cares so much about the class. If you are only taking this class for AXLE, you still need to pay attention - the class is harder than you would think. A lot of my classmates didn't do as well as they wanted because they thought it was an easy A.

Both Kelley and EES1030 are solid choices for AXLE lab credit. My friend took the same class in the fall with a different professor, and she had one more midterm than me, and I got to drop my lowest midterm. Homework and participation grades are easy too. Don't bother with the textbook, but you should go to lectures and take good notes.

he's a really good, enthusiastic, energetic professor but having a 9 am class made it so hard to pay attention (much less show up). you don't really need lectures to do well   just learn everything on the study guide and practice tests before midterms by studying the textbook. grades are inflated by test revisions, a easy project, and homework
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's so nice and loves the lesson he teaches. The lectures are interesting and the materials are not too hard to follow up. He gave us clear review guides and materials, which were truly helpful for midterms and final. He's always willing to help you outside class. Enjoy this course and thank you professor!

Kelley is very nice and approachable and will make time to meet with you. He goes through topics pretty fast though and tests can be difficult because there's a lot of material but also a lot of chances to bring your grade up through homework. Glad I chose this class for a science credit over something else!

One of the best lecturers you will ever have. Class is interesting and tests are straightforward. You drop your lower midterm of the 2. The final project, worth 10% of your grade, takes maybe 10 minutes. This becomes a class where you willingly choose to learn and care about the material simply due to how awesome your professor is.
