Awesome dude. Super caring and fun in lecture. His tests aren't too bad if you study. The course has TONS of work for an Oceanography class, but he's a fair grader and office hours are flexible. Go to lecture if you can because of participation activities that are randomly given. One of the coolest professors at Vandy, just be ready to work.

Dr. Kelley rocks (no pun intended). He's so passionate, and it definitely comes across and makes class more interesting. Further, there are very clear expectations in the class, so an A is manageable if you put in a reasonable amount of work. Warning though: if you are taking this for AXLE, I highly recommend staying away from the accompanying lab.

Dr. Kelley is a great professor, and you should definitely take his class if you have the chance. He is the reason I am majoring in Earth Science. His lectures are interesting and funny, and although there is quite a bit of homework at times, it is all very easy and it is not hard to get an A+ in this class.

kelley is the most passionate person you will ever find to talk about rocks, plate tectonics, etc. his lectures and the weekly mc HWs are interesting and easy. the one problem with dynamic earth though is the weekly discussion hws which can be difficult to perfect. but, overall relatively easy class and i would definitely reccomend taking dr kelley
Have him for Oceanography. I'm not a science person but he really makes it interesting. Generous with grades but you still have to know the material.  Overall I would recommend him for sure!

Show up, do the non-taxing assignments, you'll get 100% in the class. Dr. Martin is the best teacher I've had at VU. Gets to know everyone, jokes all the time, and a lot more intangible pieces.

Separately, the skills of this course are so helpful for yourself and in any friendships/relationships. You'll take something real away from this class.
She's so incredible, easy and fun assignments that she grades super leniently. I absolutely love her.

Most lovely lady I ever did meet. Absolute ray of sunshine and has a great balance of independent learning and lecture content. Extremely accessible, cares about students, and has clear grading criteria that makes assignments easy to understand. Would take her class a thousand times again!

The best class I've taken at Vanderbilt! Professor Martin is incredibly kind, compassionate, and engaging. This course is a must-take if you're interested in therapy, counseling, or just improving your listening skills. The material is genuinely interesting; if you're passionate and participate, you'll get an A. Could not recommend more!!

Prof Martin is literally the best. She is super accommodating and kind. Extremely easy class but I actually do think I learned a lot. The only class I looked forward to going to. Shelbi our TA was amazing as well. Couldn't recommend her more for 1300

Dr. Martin is the sweetest professor I have had in my four years at Vandy. She TRULY cares about each of her students. Though the class is REALLY easy (completion = A), the content is interesting and relevant for anyone, no matter if you want to go into counseling or not. You will have fun, learn so much, and do so in a low stress environment.

Nina is the G.O.A.T.! She is hilarious, kind, and forms a personal relationship with each of her students. This course is different: you're put in situations to share vulnerably with classmates, and Nina creates a space where that is welcome and comfortable. Content is helpful to EVERYONE, not just aspiring counselors. Minimal HW; easy grader.

Nina is an awesome professor who really cares and forms a connection with all of her students. Very accommodating of student's needs. Assignments are pretty straightforward. Lectures are also generally really fun, as she usually has some sort of engaging activity for the class to do. Highly recommend.

I cannot speak highly enough about Professor Martin's Counseling class. All of the major assignments are rather unconventional (but in a good way), and she is always very accommodating to student needs. She makes an effort to form a personal relationship with every student in the class, investing in them as people outside the classroom. Amazing!

Professor Martin is the most genuine and kind-hearted professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. She gets to know every student, she is super accommodating, and her few assignments are extremely straightforward/short
Nina slays so hard. Intro to counseling is a chill and easy class in the traditional sense, but does make you think about things in a way other classes don't. Would take again and again!

This was definitely the chillest class I've taken at Vandy. Although we didn't do much to be honest, I feel like I've learned things in this class applicable to real life by working in small groups. Prof Martin is so caring about her students, keeps tabs on everyone's lives, and actually gets to know you.

Nina is an absolute g. Chillest and most fun prof I've had at Vandy, and you can tell she cares about the subject. A fair amount of group and partner work so you'll get to know the other kids in the class well, and generally the atmosphere is great. Ending at 5:30 was tough but if you show up and put in even a little effort you'll do great.
Great professor who breaks the math down so it becomes much more understandable than on first glance. No need to read the textbook if you attend lecture and pay attention.

Noah is an outstanding lecturer with a deep understanding of the subject matter. His lectures are well-structured and clear. The weekly homework, consisting of 10 questions, are directly from the textbook. Moreover, he is very accessible and approachable outside of class. I would highly recommend taking a class with him.

2 exams and a final made up 75% of grade. He's a good lecturer (and native speaker) but doesn't engage the class at all so can be pretty boring and easy to stop paying attention. Tests were difficult but nothing too eggregious. I'd recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not teach a thing but was very strict and boring

If you don't need to take this class, then don't take it.  No tests, but a lot of homework that has a heavy weight on the grade, mandatory attendance, and harsh grading on the projects. Her in-person classes are also unengaging and heavily relies on video-lectures (which is given to you as homework).

Most of what I learned in this class came from looking over slides without needing to pay attention to Dr. Novick. Lectures were  incredibly non-engaging, so much so that I couldn't get myself to tune into class. Tests are graded semi-harshly; she's very specific about random things. She also tends to go on random tangents and over-explain things.

I think a lot of the reviews for Dr. Novick are unnecessarily harsh. She sets her expectations very clear via the syllabus and rubrics, and grades pretty fairly. She plays by the rules for sure but this isn't a bad thing because you know what to expect this way. She is also really kind when you speak to her individually.

Psych of Thinking with Dr. Novick isn't terrible, but it definitely isn't great. The lectures are assigned asynchronously as online homework, and they're not at all helpful. Granted, it's not hard to get an A in this class if you put in some effort, but if you want a solid understanding of the subject, I'd recommend taking Cognitive Psych instead.

Takes off lots of points for minor mistakes that most other professors would overlook. She's extremely nitpicky about how you format answers and if it deviates from her approach in any way, even if your answer is still correct, she will mark the entire question wrong. Very rigid and inflexible, do NOT take her if you can avoid it!

We got a grade report for April 1st where my grade was an A in the class. We only had one assignment left and one exam left. My final grade ended up as a B. My grade dropped because she decided to restructure the grading and not let me make up an assignment I missed from a family medical emergency. Instead she yelled at me about it.

Prof. Novick is not only a dry lecturer, but she is condescending. It is one thing to be a bad teacher, but another to be a rude person. Avoid her classes at all costs. She struggles to explain concepts and has extremely confusing expectations.

here is a perfect example of how her class is: she marks me down and criticizes me for not citing the visuals I had for my application assignment - visuals I myself took hours and hours to make... would rather take all the effort, energy, and time I exerted here to Organic Chemistry. at least there, effort is recognized and not just insulted

I think these reviews are unnecessarily harsh. PSY-PC 2200 with Novick was an interesting class and was not a lot of work. Application assignments do determine the bulk of your grade and grading can be harsh, but listen in class and note how she frames things and youll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Listen to your upperclassmen peers who warn you against taking her course. You'll regret not listening. While Dr. Novick may be smart, she is not a good teacher. She is an extremely tough grader with extremely specific needs that are not relevant to actually understanding the material. If you don't do things her way, you get penalized for it.

Literally the WORST teacher I've ever had. Prepare to be barraged with unnecessarily harsh comments on application assignments that assume you are a PhD student doing psychology for a living and not just a curious undergrad. Grading is illogical and inconsistent. Instead of encouraging, she discourages you. You deserve better - AVOID this class :)

avoid this class! Grade is based on 3 application assignments with unclear grading criteria. If you try to ask clarifying questions, she tells you Im not going to do your project for you. Finally, Prof Novick has a generally unkind and rude disposition and way she speaks to students can be humiliating and disparaging.

Most days in class are just a waste of time with nothing productive happening. The application assignments are harshly graded and have a really bad rubric that is unclear. She also is just kinda rude and shoots down mosts ideas in and outside of class.
Grading criteria was extremely unclear. Most of the total grade was made up of three application assignments, and it was a complete mystery how to do well on them. Avoid this class if possible!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid her classes that have project. She does not have a clear standard of grading.

One of the worse professors I have ever taken at vandy. Bulk of our grade were 3 application assignments and would give extremely vague ideas and rubrics about what she was looking for. She wouldn't even grade according to her own rubric. Has an extremely picky style of grading where she takes off an insane amount of points unreasonable

Unclear about what she wants on the few assignments she gives... Then takes off a crazy amount of points if its not up to her unclear standards. Seems nice at first but is pretty rude outside class, too. Did not learn a thing or have a good time. Word of advice: dont take her class.

Professor Novick made an intro psychology class way more complicated than it needed to be. We had to spend two full class periods explaining the syllabus if that says anything. The class is graded off of 3 assignments and attendance. The assignments seem easy enough, but big points were taken off if they didn't fit her exact expectations.
Professor Novick is really nice and you can tell she genuinely cares about the students. The lectures and tests are really EASY if you read the textbook. 10/10 would recommend.

I think she is a good person and is knowledgeable about statistics, but she is just not a good professor. I felt the written part of the exams were more important than the stats part. Her lectures are very boring. Nonetheless, the thing that bothered me the most is that she makes you follow instructions and not think critically.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Novick is just hard to understand. This class really isn't that bad because you get your grade based on how everyone else does, so if you all do poorly, you all do well. She is weirdly picky about responses and wants you to answer with specific language but she does a good job teaching the material and cares that you do well.

Really knowledgeable professor, boring lectures, easy material AND you get to bring 'cheat sheets'. The problem I have with her is her incredibly pedantic grading. You can get all of the answers correct, but if it's not presented in her specific way, then you'll lose an unnecessary amount of points.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Stats are stats. She gives you what you need to excel in the class but also grades pretty harshly -- granted, she also applies a nice curve. Class isn't mandatory and if you do go, she'll pick on something from what you say. "the answer is 3.183" "well, actually, the answer is 3.18 because according to the syllabus you round to 2 decimals"...

She is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. Point blank. Don't take her class. Stats was one of my favorite classes before her class. She is the most boring professor and is not kind. She kind of makes you feel bad about yourself. And it's not like I am doing badly in the class..? Only perk is the cheat sheet you get to have for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not the most engaging lecturer. You can do well if you pay close attention and take good notes in class in addition to knowing how to do the homework. Graded on an actual curve, so only around a fourth of the class gets a solid A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer - must pay attention and take good notes. Not many examples to study from which is difficult. Can get a good grade if pay close attention. Allows a sheet of notes on test which is really helpful.

People here are wusses. Have y'all never had a good teacher before? Prof. Novick simply has expectations of her students to be thoughtful scholars who put effort into their work. Sure, she's boring in class, but she teaches you the skills to conduct statistical analyses and produce the written work for research articles. Highly recommend.

The professor is a very boring teacher. She is also extremely picky about stuff you write in your exams and all the sorts. This is one of those classes that is supposed to be straightforward and an easy A but she tries to make it extremely demanding. One can finish the class being an expert on statistical analysis and still get a terrible grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she is so freaking boring. She is not helpful in or outside of class. Is extremely picky about tests. All written and super long. Does not explain content well and she is not very nice when you ask a question. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Exactly like other reviews have stated: cold, condescending, and occasionally outright mean. Verbally berated the TA in front of the class a few times. C averages on tests bc of ridiculous grading criteria (although she grades on a curve so top half of class gets A-/A), but lets you have a cheat sheet so you don't need to actually learn . EASY A-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Novick is terrible. She teaches the most boring class in the history of the world, and she is MEAN - like really mean. Don't bother asking her questions because she will just respond with condescending sass. Peabody stats is supposed to be easy, but she curves the class so she makes sure someone fails every semester. Just horrible.

Professor Novick is not warm and bubbly but, she is clear in her teaching and class examples. The class material is incredible dull and dry, Professor Novick's teaching style does not change that. However, the class is graded on a curve and it is possible to do well. Take advantage of her office hours with homework questions. Hard tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very difficult and incredibly boring lectures. Highly recommend taking anyone else for Peabody stats.

Prof. Novick is one of the worst professors I've had at this School. Her lectures are boring, her grading can be arbitrary, and she is not very helpful/accommodating either. I would not recommend taking a course with her...

Even though Professor Novick lives in the statistical dinosaur age and does not convey an appreciation for modern statistical techniques to intro. students, her teaching material cuts to the heart of ordinary psychological research practice and is highly relevant. Dull but informative, her lectures are usually worth attending.

WARNING: this is the worst professor of my whole life. She encourages class participation, but is SO rude and patronizing if you say something wrong. her exams are very specific, and her lectures are very unorganized. She is boring, dry, unhelpful, and frankly should not be teaching. If you think you can take her class, DONT. no matter what.

Extremely dry and unhelpful. I did not learn anything in the class. This is an intro to stat class that primarily covered material I had previously learned in my AP class- and thank God it did. I would not have been able to do well in the class without this previous background in the material. Boring lectures and confusing teacher.

PAINFULLY BORING. literally the worst class ever. its pretty easy, just read the book, take the practice test, and study the studies she has on her slides. but i am literally falling asleep every day in class. it is MISERABLE. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

This class isn't easy, but if you go to class and do the homework, you will do fine. She grades on a curve so no worries.  The tests are pretty hard, but I'm sure there is some secret to doing better than I did. I think you'd be fine in her class.  She's not cuddly or friendly, but she does know statistics very well.

Professor Novick is one of those brilliant minds whose thinks logically. She is a scientist, not an artist, therefore, her classes are not imaginative, rather they are structured and get straight to the point. She is actually very helpful and approachable though she seems intimidating at first. She goes out of her way to assist interested students

I wish I had nicer things t say about the class because Novick is actually a pretty nice person. The class is boring, needlessly difficult, aggravating, uninspiring, etc...and Novick certainly does nothing to make it any better. Would have skipped it if I could.

If I weren't a cog studies major I would have dropped this class ages ago. It's one of those classes that you want to skip every time but you can't. She does some ridiculous grading policy on participation/attendance (she says even if you ask her to repeat something it counts as participation) Learn nothing in lecture, could've just read the book.

Professor Novick is actually quite friendly and helpful in person. She concentrates on statistics and impercial evidence as one must!! After all, the courses she teaches are psychology courses. Psychological courses are science based courses and therefore call for some maths and statistics. With hard one you will definitely excel in her class.

very cut and dry material, and her teaching style doesn't lend itself making the material more than that. her presentation of the material is automatic. one thing she REALLY stresses is class participation, she doesn't care about the merit of your comments only that you make them. avoid if you have a choice, but your grade will resolve itself.
Really difficult class...but its difficult material. so much hmwk, takes me hours! really hard tests, dont take this if you want a good grade!

OK. Prof Novick may not be the warmest woman teaching at Vanderbilt, but you have to understand that she is a numbers person not a people person. With that said, she does know her numbers and you will learn if you pay attention and do your homework. I think she is a good teacher even though she lacks some social skills.

She's not warm and cuddly, but she isn't mean and she can explain statistics like no one else.  I dreaded taking this class because I did so badly in 2101, but so far I have an A.  The homework is reasonable and tests are open book/note.
Avoid her like the plague.  That's all I can say.  Never have I ever felt so discouraged by a teacher.  She's awful, condescending, uninspiring, and rude.

Boring and cold but the class material is crystal clear and presented in an easy to understand way.  If you do the homework (easy) and takes notes, you WILL get an A in the class.  Just ignore her snips and subtle insults - they aren't personal.
She is mean.  She hates you if you don't understand what is going on.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.  Change majors to avoid taking it.

(Creativity seminar): Is it possible to fall asleep in a seminar of 5 students? In a class on creativity? Unfortunately, yes. The readings were tortuous and the discussions (as well as her voice)- monotonous. Not the fairest of graders, either. Nice lady and assigned interesting projects, on a positive note.

I would strongly advise avoiding this class at all costs. Prof. Novick is mean, condescending, answers questions by insulting you, doesn't want you to do well, and is so boring I occasionally wanted to cry. The homework takes an insane amount of time too. This class was not even worth having friday

Okay whatever you do, do NOT take the 2100 seminar titled "creativity" if she is still teaching it. it seems interesting, but she definitely sucks the life out of it and its almost painful. shes not a good teacher and she is VERY VERY dull. i dont recommend her in general..

This woman is the definition of an ineffective teacher. It's impossible to learn anything from such a condesending, boring, mean, uninspiring woman. She's horrible. I'd rather change majors than have a class with her again.
She is just mean

Dr. Novick is a brilliant woman.  While the material taught is not the most exciting, the class was informative and helpful for those who want to take the GRE-psychology test.  I for one, like Dr. Novick and think she is very interesting and intelligent.
No Comments
No Comments

I would go into class after reading the mandatory textbook and would leave the lecture more confused. She would often go into people's faces and roleplay infants' parents research etc. SHE SHOULD RETIRE. I would talk to students who had the other professor and they seemed to both learn more and have less assignments.

Dr. Noland was not a good lecturer. She tended to be pretty confusing and hard to follow. Most of what you need to know is in the textbook and she posts her lecture slides on Brightspace which is helpful. I did not find the tests to be hard and you can earn up to 10 extra credit points.
She's nice, but not a fan of her teaching (Mellow + unhelpful explanations). I learned outside of class, and it was WORK. Hardest 1250 profesor. ended with an A but it's A LOT of homework

Class is super easy, the exam questions are worded kinda weirdly but you get tons of extra credit so your grade's gonna be fine. Her voice is super boring, and her lectures will make you doze off, but she does try to be better and you gotta give her credit for that.

Dr. Noland is a kind professor who cares about you succeeding in the class. However her lectures are slow and sometimes boring. A lot of the learning for developmental psychology will be through the textbook. This class is really easy to get a good grade if you do the homework you can get up to 10 bonus points. I got 200/200 points in this class.

Definitely a very sweet, passionate person, but she structured the class like she didn't trust us to learn on our own. Dry lectures, interesting content. Very clear on assignment/grading criteria. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Exams are also really easy. Attendance is mandatory with discussion posts if you miss to make it excused :P.
boring lectures so I did not learn much, she is hard to understand but the class is super easy and everyone gets an A

This class is an easy A, as the material is relatively straightforward and there's plenty of extra credit offered. However, attendance is mandatory, and the lectures are boring. Also laptops aren't allowed during class. If you skip classes or have trouble staying focused, then don't take this class.

Agree with other reviews for the most part. Super easy class, cares a lot about students, but lectures are definitely boring/not engaging. Also not the most organized or tech savvy which got annoying at times. Would definitely take the course again, just not with her. However, if she is your only option she isn't really that bad.

Dr. Noland's class wasn't particularly difficult, but it was tedious. There was more homework in this class than any of my other classes, and I found her lectures to be boring and dry. She would also seem to lose her train of though during lectures a lot, and she does randomly call on people for answering questions and makes a big deal about it.

Overall Dr. Noland was a decent professor. Her lectures were dense and a tad boring, but her tests were relatively easy and straight forward as long as you studied and took notes. The best part of her class is that she builds in easy extra credit opportunities to buffer your grade, so it is challenging to do poorly in her class.

This class was literally only lectures. The second class starts to the minute it ends, it is a lecture that is somewhat confusing. The content is easy to understand but there is a lot of it. The extra credit system makes this class easy to get a good grade in. Dr. Noland and the TAs are very accessible outside of class for office hours.

Dr. Noland is confusing in her explanation or course material and for a small-ish class size I was hoping for more discussion based classes. There's three exams (and optional final) that aren't too difficult if you study the lecture slides especially with bonus points. She wants her students to succeed but tends to be a little off putting.

While Noland may not be the most interesting or engaging, this class was seriously very easy. Tests are a direct reflection of information on the slides and TAs are very accommodating and make attaining an A very easy. Overall easy class to get credit and get an A in. I would highly recommend.

I took this class to fulfill one of my peabody credits and it was not bad at all. A lot of busy work assignments but as long as you get your work done you will be fine. Lectures are long and often hard to sit through but this is defintely an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never stays on topic and very hard to follow. Attendance is mandatory for points but it should not be considering it is more beneficial to study the textbook- she will only confuse you.

Dr. Noland is not the most engaging professor, but her class is super easy. Prepared to be bored a lot during the lectures, but pay attention enough and do the little assignments and you'll get tons of bonus points, making it  super easy to get an A

I took PSYPC2550: Infancy with Noland, and she is a very sweet professor. I can tell she cares about her students' wellbeing and their lives outside of the classroom. But she is a dry lecturer, and the in class assignments are easy but so arbitrary. You need to study the lecture slides and do the practice exam to do well. She drops a test grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Probably not the smartest professor, but the class is super easy. If you go to all the lectures and pay attention it's a lay up A. Pretty boring because she talks so slow, but tons of opportunity for bonus points. No papers either which is nice.
She is just very strange! Class was decently easy but I did not learn anything

Noland is a caring lady that enjoys what she is teaching about. She gives lots of extra credit and the class is not extremely difficult. With that being said, the lectures are extremely confusing and it is very unclear what will be on the test. The exams are also super confusing. Not a hard class but frustrating for a type A student.

Very clear grading criteria. Overall very sweet professor who offers a ton of extra credit, wants you to get an A. I found it tough but everyone else in the class thought it was pretty easy. I didn't study at first so i fell behind. 3 exams, one group project, a few short quizzes, lots of homework and reading assignments, but pretty manageable.
Dr. Noland is very very very kind and cares about her students. There is lots of extra credit and she takes the time to make sure we understand the material that she lectures. Great class overall.

Dr. Noland is a very sweet woman who obviously cares about her students, which I really appreciated. She gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit to fill in the gap if you are struggling. Put in the effort in you should have no problem. However, her lectures are not the best. Slides are confusing and she often loses her train of thought.

Dr. Noland is a very kind person, but not the greatest professor. Her lectures are often confusing. She jumps around slides and sometimes loses her train of thought. Her slides have minimal bullets making going back and studying the slides pretty much useless. Tests are fairly difficult but plenty of extra credit to balance it out. Overall easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: you will definitely pass. getting an A or B is easily doable. exams are okay. homeworks are easy. group project isnt bad. optional take-home final can definitely help you out!!!

Dr. Noland is sweet and gives many opportunities to boost your grade. However, the lectures are a bit boring and you do need to study for the exams. Pretty easy class otherwise, the essays on the exam are the LRQ's

Very boring lectures but overall was able to teach everything we needed. Attendance is mandatory but you get a good amount a personal days & can make up absences. Do the homework and take notes in class & the exams are easy, & there are lots of opportunities for extra credit. Textbook required but she's fine with us using the pirated one online.
Dr. Noland is a good-natured, kind professor, but her lectures can be boring. Class content isn't difficult, but it's definitely slow. Go to class, it's an easy A if you don't wanna be challenged.

Course is interesting and based all on group discussions and from book readings. Noland is caring and wants students to do well, however, grading and criteria for assignments can get convoluted and unclear.
A good amount of short answer writing for homework and tests are medium difficulty. Extra credit and teacher support is beneficial.

This was an easy class. Professor Noland really cares about all her students doing well. If you show up to class (or complete the online make up work) and do the assignments, you should get an A in this class. The lectures were sometimes boring, but Professor Noland tries to keep students engaged with questions and videos.

Dev Psych is an easier A because Noland is understanding and wants everyone to do well. I really enjoyed having her so much I will be taking another one of her classes. However, lectures are not super engaging and interesting. I self taught some of the information too. And tests are hard so extra credit is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Going to class is part of your grade. Lots of little homework assignments outside of class but theres extra credit with them. Dry lecturer. Review sessions are helpful before test. Final is optional which is great. Overall recommend as a easy psych course
Dr. Noland was ok - I felt the class was quite superficial and vocab heavy, but an easy choice.

Dev Psych is definitely a step up from Gen Psych, but I can't say that it was amazing by any means. Doctor Noland is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject; however, the class itself was often rather boring with her often giving students what felt like busy work to kill time. Still, easy to do well if you apply a little effort.

Professor Noland is very caring and really is passionate about the material. There is a homework assignment before most classes but they're super short(only take about 30 mins to complete). The homework is also super helpful to study for exams, and exams are always straightforward. Lots of extra credit. Highly recommend this very interesting class!
Loved this class! Dr. Noland is really nice and is very accommodating. Lots of hw, but the hw assignments are short. Take her Dev Psych if you want a chill class on your schedule!

Dr. Nolan is a good professor, but nothing super special. Dev Psych was an easy course, but somewhat confusing in structure in terms of assignments and expectations. The material was very interesting, though, and I would recommend it over Gen Psych if you are looking for a PreMed filler, or if you just want to learn about babies.

Dr. Noland is a solid choice for Developmental Psych. Although not the most engaging lecturer, you do not need to take detailed notes to do well on the tests. The study guides and LRQs/LPs are all you really need. One big group project, final is optional to replace a low test grade, and decent extra credit opportunities. Would recommend.
Loved this class. Dr. Noland was also understanding. Just do all the work and you should do well on the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: It's hard not to make an A in the class with all the extra credit that is offered. Dr. Noland is nice. Take notes during lectures. Do your work. I slacked off the second unit and I did not do as well on that test. Stay committed. Don't get lazy. You'll get an A. Has been very accommodating during pandemic.

Super caring and catered to students needs. Tons of extra credit and final exam was optional (to drop lowest exam grade if wanted). Super clear about expectations and grading criteria. Couldnt recommend more highly!
so much extra credit it's insane. clearly loves her job/field but sometimes the lectures are a little disorganized. textbook pdf can be found online for free so don't purchase it

Noland can be a bit confusing at times but she is a great professor who truly cares about her students' learning. The class was very interesting, and the assignments and projects/papers were in-line with the course goals. Highly recommend if you want to earn an easy A and to learn some interesting content!

Prof. Noland is super passionate about teaching developmental psych, and her enthusiasm is reflected in the fun way she teaches and encourages discussions among students. She's a very kind and understanding, and it makes her really happy when students participate in the class and mini-group discussions.

Dr. Noland cares so much about the material and is very smart. She gives so much opportunity for extra credit, so it's an easy A. Not a lot of hw. Lectures can be boring but it's interesting material. She's very accessible and nice.

Dr. Noland is a very knowledgeable and a kind professor. I thoroughly enjoyed Developmental Psychology. She made it very attainable to get an A. We had many opportunities for extra credit and made tests very clear. She helps in anyway possible and cares about the wellbeing of her students. Just make sure to keep up with the assignments.

Dr. Noland is so kind and helpful. She cares a lot about the subject and if you work AT ALL you will get an A. If you do all the homework you can get bonus points on the tests, and you will be well prepared to take the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a generally interesting professor and her developmental psych class is extremely easy. There is a ton of extra credit and the material is very interesting so it makes some of the tedious work not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Noland strikes me as the kind of person who secretly doesn't actually like people. Luckily she knows it and overcompensates by being nice and understanding. From what I've heard from other students, her class is much more comprehensible now than it was when she started teaching. I enjoy the in-class conversation.

She is a great professor, just a little disorganized but she does not penalise you for her disorganization. She will let you re write all the important things to make up your grade. Likes it if you participate and ask questions. She is very accessible and will  try and help you understand material and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Class was an Easy A. If you do the few homework assignment and study for the tests its a very easy class. Lectures are kind of boring but definitely GPA booster. Recommend this class

Super easy class and friendly teacher. There are lots of group projects but they are very easy and so are the papers. You will have weekly lecture preps and an occasional quiz but the class is very easy overall. If you are looking for an easy A definitely take this class.

Noland is a very nice lady. Her class is very organized and you always know what to expect, but I might argue that it is too structured. She gives lots of extra credit so if you come to class and do the work you will get an A.

You will do a lot of work in this class, however its not particularly difficult. The lectures are always interesting and look at issues from many different perspectives. There final was optional too, which was awesome!

Easy A, but she's really annoying. Always goes off on unrelated and nonsensical tangents, and when someone suggests a correction or legitimate alternate viewpoint on something she says, she has too much pride to admit they're right. Only good part was when she messed up the basics of mitosis. Lots of extra credit and tests are MC and short answer.

Prof Noland is really sweet. She just seems very frazzled all the time and she is sometimes difficult to follow. There's plenty of extra credit so you don't need to worry about your grade too much. Pay attention to the examples she does in class, especially the videos of research experiments. We did a lot of group discussion, which was fun.

Pretty easy class once you get her routine down. She can be very confusing and ambiguous, both in talking and the design of her power points. However, her class is pretty easy and definitely A-able. The final was optional which was really nice. I would recommend her over some of the other 1630 professors, based on what I've heard from friends.

She was very interested in her material, and really wanted you to succeed but seemed ditzy. Her tests were confusing and over specific, she never had good explanations even for her own questions, and going to office hours was a huge waste of time. Gives lots of extra credit, but the classes and confusion isn't worth it.

Lectures were incredibly confusing. She assigned readings that had little to do with what she actually talked about. The group project and other assignments were incredibly easy, but exams were difficult because the information was often very specific. I know there are plenty of other professors that teach this class that are much much better.

I had an awful experience in this class. Dr. Noland is incredibly confusing and not helpful at all. Her lectures are boring and frazzled. It takes a lot of effort to sit through her class. I would NOT recommend taking a class with her. There are plenty of other professors who know what they're talking about and are much more helpful.
Very confusing teacher, but most material could be found in the book; her class was VERY boring, and her slides were pretty terrible, but she was lenient when it came to grading

This class is really interesting, and she wants students to do well. She curved two tests to the point that 1/3 of the class had over 100%. The quizzes are difficult, but together are worth less than 5% of your grade. I definitely recommend taking this class with Julia Noland. She's really sweet and willing to help you out.
Honestly, I could not tell you what I learned in this class.  Take it from someone else.  You will be bored out of your mind and do pointless assignments.  Save yourself the boredom.

This class is a joke. She doesn't really seem to understand what she is even talking about. Her "textbooks" are books that parents buy before they are about to have a child. However, super easy class. I did minimal work and got an A. Though she is confusing, she is super nice.
I had her first semester she ever taught. She gave lots of extra credit opportunities. Maybe slightly boring and sometimes slightly confusing, but she's nice.

Good lecturer, but lots of content. Memorize the stories and key points of readings and you'll be fine. However was a tougher grader on one essay and had to give more leeway on next. Not clear at all on grading rubrics.
Storytelling class, memorize the stories

You can usually rely on the slides to get you through the tests, but I suggest going to her lectures because she is always excited and interested in what she is teaching. I personally loved learning the information and while the class is not an easy A, it is easily manageable if you put in the effort for the tests.

Amy Non is a wonderful professor who care about  her students. Lectures are typically interesting but can get a bit dry after a while. Grading is overall pretty easy, but you need to keep up with all the material to be ready for the midterm and final. Workload isn't bad at all.

Dr.Whitman was a very good prof, goes through everything that is going to be on the tests and does so in an entertaining and engaging way. Funny and light-hearted guy, gives great feedback on tests. A lot of EC and I think you would have to try really hard to fail that class.

Really took his class because it sounded interesting. Also because I needed to fill credits before getting into my major. But, I'm extremely glad I took him. He's funny, creative and extremely knowledgable. He is also very understanding when it comes to assignments, absences, etc. He will work with his students and frankly, acts like his students.

Professor Whitman is the man! His lectures are hilarious, and the class would be laughing out loud almost every one. Weekly quizzes, which can be annoying, but he drops your two lowest scores and gives lots of extra credit. His exams are difficult, but you can do well if you study. GO TO CLASS. There will be rewards if you do.  Amazing guy.

Very easy class but you learn a lot. Gives out EC so come to class. Material can get a little dry but he does his best to keep  the class entertaining. Goes over lots of problems during class time, so if you come, studying will be at a minimum. 2 tests, 1 final, and short quizzes almost every week (can drop 2) . Would recommend.

Amazing professor. Attendance is not mandatory but there's no reason not to show up because Whitman is incredible. Usually has some pretty wild stuff to say. Chances are you probably won't understand what's going on in class but he's incredibly helpful during help sessions. All that's important is the class before the test. He breaks it ALL down.

You must take this class! AMAZING PROFESSOR and gives lots of extra credit if you come to class. I did all the problems after each chapter, which helps for practice before any quiz/exam . If answer questions during class, it will make your grade go up higher. Loved it.

Best professor at Vanderbilt! The semester starts a little hard, but it gets easier towards the end. To get an A, attend class (sometimes for EC) everyday and do the problems after each section for practice (it is not graded). He has a great personality and gives a lot of extra credit. Very easy class and interesting material. Love it!

Excellent class despite what I thought would be a dry subject. I especially enjoyed his examples of logical fallacies. I had some trouble but finally, with Professor Whitman's help I was able to grasp the distinction between "pickle they" and "not pickle they".
great class for an MNS credit. if you try, no problem to get an A. quizzes can be challenging, but with XC and easier tests, it is fine. he's an awesome guy too.

Whitman is the absolute man. From day 1 he kept the class interesting even with somewhat boring subject matter. Quizzes can be difficult at times, but he's more than willing to give you extra credit for showing interest and improving. 3 tests 25% each, quiz average last 25%
Good teacher, has a gift for teaching philosophy, even if it's just an intro logic class. Take his class, you won't regret it.
Don't need to go to class, and still a fairly easy A

Carlos is kind and supportive, intelligent and incisive in leading discussion, and a wonderful resource in and out of the classroom. Lots of reading but you can totally skim and he'll be happy with your participation if you talk once a class. Good feedback - very positive, helpful with rewrites
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Nugent is very kind and accessible. There was a lot of reading for this class so if you are not an English major it might be slightly difficult. He can ask long, convoluted questions and participation is very important to him so come to class having done the readings. The papers weren't difficult, he helps a lot during the process.

Professor Nugent is a really nice guy. However, the class is very reading-heavy (some readings were 100+ pages) and he uses pretty academic language which can be hard to follow at times. Classtime was mostly used for discussion of the readings with very little lecture, so you won't get a whole lot of context for said readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Nugent is a nice enough guy but prepare for an insane amount of homework and reading. Discussions are usually disappointing and filled with a lot of silence because we're given a bunch of readings without pretty much any lectures for context. I did fine in the class, but I wouldn't recommend it if you already have a full schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Nugent is such an amazing professor and always makes sure that students are confident in their work. He leads discussions in a way that never makes students feel like they said something wrong, and he has really helped me gain confidence in writing. He is absolutely amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is the best physics teacher I've met in Vandy. Clear organized and articulated.
Best physics professor at Vanderbilt.  He is MUCH better than the other options for the 2nd semester of physics.  Definitely recommend him.
Dr. Oberacker is by far the best professor I've had at Vandy. His classes are very clear and manageable, and he actually makes learning interesting.
Excellent teacher, great at presenting things clearly, really knows his stuff, can usually answer any question asked right away.  One of the best profs I've had.
Excellent Prof.  The best I've had at Vanderbilt.

This is the worst class I took at Vanderbilt. He gives zero grading criteria or clarity around expectations and fosters a highly uncomfortable classroom environment. Words cannot describe how happy I was for this class to end. He takes out his frustration on students in a completely inappropriate manner. I can't think of a single pro of this class.

You will get a good grade in his classes if you are willing to show up to class and participate. Sometimes his expectations for an assignment are incredibly unclear, but what he truly cares about is a willingness to put effort into his courses. FREN3234 was fun and full of unique content, you just must willing to put up with his Quebec French.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Impossible expectations, constantly changing requirements and boring content. If any other professor is teaching, take their section. You will walk out of class crying in frustration with this professor. The entire semester is reading, HW question, and discussing in class, with 2 papers and a presentation.

Prof. Nzabatsinda is an excellent professor. His reading assignments are relevant, engaging, and substantial but not overwhelming. He spends adequate time on each subject, ensuring that each student has a full grasp of the material before moving on. The course is not difficult as long as long as you come prepared.

I really appreciate the care Professor Nzabatsinda takes with the material--he's meticulous for this reason.  I feel like he's passionate about the material and he wants his students to also share that.  I would take his class again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took AP French before this so this class was a breeze for me, but if you don't have a strong foundation of French, this class will be hard and you won't learn anything. Lectures are all over the place and mostly him talking at us. we go over exercises in the textbook so you'd need to buy that. About 5 2-page papers but easy topics.

Professor Nzabatsinda provided little to no support and guidance during such a challenging semester and didnt take the time to teach us how to analyze literature. This class can be summarized into constant confusion about the paper expectations, endless blog posts, and no interesting conversations that would help everyone learn the material.
Easily the worst taught class of the semester. Directions and expectations are incredibly difficult to understand. Maybe would've been better in-person, but the online class was incredibly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I can't even describe how bad this was. He talks in a very confusing and circular way then gets mad when students don't understand. Every time he asked a question someone would have to ask him to repeat the question. Do not take this class under any circumstances because you will be sad, mad, and/or confused for an entire semester.

Awful class. He never ever explains anything clearly, and even the clarifying emails he sends out are incomprehensible. You have to figure out everything out yourself, and he still takes points off for ridiculous things that you weren't even aware were relevant. Miserable experience only made worse by the fact that this class is so boring. Avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the worst professor I've ever had. Explains papers and assignments in a horribly unclear manner, and then takes off points because the students misinterpreted his extremely unclear instructions. Calls you out in class too. And to make matters worse, the class is so, so, so boring, and I can not emphasize that enough. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Nzabatsinda is a genuinely kind and caring man. However, this is easily the worst class I have ever taken. The professor is exceptionally disorganized and has some of the poorest communication skills imaginable. At no point in the class will you understand what is going on since every assignment is explained in an obscure, cryptic manner.
Loved Prof. Nzabatsinda. He really wants you to participate so you can learn and get better at the language.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lots of reading but that's what you should expect from a class on texts and contexts. He also shows films and videos which is nice too since they go alongside history. He assigns lots of papers but he likes them on the shorter side which is good. The best part is that he's a native french speaker so his feedback is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nzabatsinda is a good, caring professor who is very detail-oriented and thorough with his assignments and handouts. He loves to lecture, but there is time for discussion as well. He does occasionally put people on the spot if you haven't contributed anything yet. Homework is very manageable and he's an easy grader if you do what he asks. Recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great French professor! The texts he chooses for the course are super interesting and captivating, but be prepared to discuss. For him the class is Texts first, then history which is better for writing papers and presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He has a very straightforward teaching & grading style. Cares more about quality of your papers more than the length. He lets you revise for credit w occasional extra credit opportunities. It's ok to miss reading a bit, but he does like to go over homework in class, so be prepared. Take if him you prefer lecture-based classes over discussion-based.

His accent is pretty hard to understand at first but gets better as you get used to him. He is a consistent grader on the 5 papers you have to write, and he wants you to keep them relatively short. You get to rewrite 3 of them. There are also 2 grammar tests that are semi-challenging. There is nightly homework from grammar books. Not easy, not hard

I honestly had the worst experience in this class. I am a straight A student, especially in French. However, I have received lower grades on my papers in his class than ever before. I did not learn much in this class, which is very disappointing, because the African diaspora is something that interests me greatly. I do NOT recommend this course.

He alternates between being chill and being an absolute nightmare. He speaks rather quickly and doesn't like to repeat himself, but I wouldn't let him know if you're intimidated; he'll go out of his way to single you out and embarass you. His grading is fairly leniant, though, and in 201W writing scores are really all that count.
I had a really hard time understanding him, but I felt like he got frustrated with me easily when I asked him to repeat himself. I had to work really hard in this class just to get by...
No Comments

Accent is hard to understand.  He drones on and on and on in class and it is impossible to stay awake.  There is little class participation, unfortunately.  However, he is a very very nice man and very helpful outside of class.
He's a fair grader, but his accent takes a little while to get used to, and he can be snappy if he's in a bad mood.  Sometimes he's not very clear on what the assignments are, so you have to ask.

hard to understand at times, sometimes gives unclear directions, impossible to argue with. he tends to think his opinion is the only right one, but all the same hes a nice guy. on the days when hes in a bad mood, watch out though...
I really like this prof!  He is super challenging, but very understanding and helpful outside of class.
Dr. Nzabatsinda is a really good teacher.  I found his accent a little hard to follow, but he is always well-prepared and cares a lot for his students.  He is extremely helpful and not too hard.
I loved Anthere's class. He is a little hard to understand because he was raised in Belgium after leaving Africa, but the class on African literature is incredibly interesting.
No Comments

This is an extremely easy course to take - there are no final exams and two papers (counts for 50% of overall grade)are unrelated to contents taught in class. You have a few quizzes that are easy as well.
Trust me on this one: just take the class. You will thank me later. It counts for AXLE as a United States Culture and History credit!
Prof. Blackmon is great. The class was not too difficult, and the projects were really interesting. I would for sure take one of his classes again.

He is an incredible professor that creates a safe space for everyone to share their songs. He is very accomplished, and I learned a lot from him. Our class became very close by the end of the semester thanks to him and, we all looked forward to his Wednesday night class. This is a good class for all levels of songwriters.

Great professor to take a class from. Took lyrics class online and the class was still engaging and fun, even over zoom. It's very clear he cares about music and encourages his students to be passionate about it as well. If you show up and participate, you'll have a good time. Also highly recommend if you are looking to improve songwriting skills!

Professor Blackmon is one of my absolute favorite professors! He fostered a comfortable classroom environment that allowed for everyone to really get to know each other and be vulnerable in our songwriting/exercises (even over Zoom)! All the assignments and feedback were very useful, and I feel like I grew a lot over the course!

One of the best professors I had at Vandy. Took his lyricwriting seminar my 5th year. All we did was listen to music, vibe, and write songs. It was super fun. Odie (hes a first name professor) cares a lot about us and was always cracking jokes - and gave pretty helpful feedback about my music as well. Pretty sure everyone got As

Really weird grading. Met with him to discuss it, and he didn't answer my question at all and just repeated his criticism, which was vague (one criticism, but got a C- on the essay). Great guy though, and he helped me out quite a bit on two of the four assignments (20% each, 20% for attendance).

I wouldn't recommend Dr. Ochonu to anyone I liked. I found his lectures to be dry and uninspiring. He was extremely vague on the expectations for our papers, and graded them harshly with poor explanations for how he evaluated our work. It's not that he is an overtly lazy or antagonist professor, but I was disappointed in how unreceptive he was.

April 3rd, 2025 review was hating for no reason. You only have to do 3 3-page papers and then a 5 or 6-page final. As you can see, I am not a writer, and I still did well in this class. He's a great communicator I do not know what April 3rd was talking about. He always responds within a few hours, even on weekends and breaks. Trust twin it's chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His teaching is ineffective. He provides contradictory feedback on essays, demonstrates poor communication with students, and appears disengaged. His lack of communication skills is a significant issue. PLEASE DON'T TAKE HIM FOR AXLE OR ANYTHING.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very nice and funny and chill class overall. While lectures could be dry at times, the light homework (only 3 papers and a presentation total) made up for it. Also very flexible and willing to help in office hours. As long as you show interest and participate once in a while in class, you'll be fine (and it's a pretty easy A)

Do not take. Lectures are BORING (reading off bare slides) and don't relate to the assignments at all. His syllabus has at most 2 sentences of detail for each assignment and he won't talk about the essays until the week they are due. He also cold calls. He's a really nice guy and an easy grader but it's not worth it.

His grading criteria and expectations are unclear for all of his assignments but he is overly harsh when it comes to grading. Although he is kind and is willing to help you explore writing more, he keeps repeating the same generic, lazy feedback that practically gets you nowhere. Lectures are VERY boring and are not needed for the papers.

As a first-year writing seminar, this class had less writing than others but probably more reading. Moses is more of a historian than a teacher, as he knows a lot about the subject but doesn't do as good education students. He gives really good feedback on essays and will help you with any part of the process, but can be hard to reach by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is clearly knowledgeable and it shows in the daily class discussions that he leads. There is a lot of reading but you can skim most and the rest is unneeded for success in class. For papers he grades them moderately hard, but one conversation with him and he will guide you in the right direction. One of my favorite professors I've had thus far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Ochonu is a really awesome guy- his lectures were interesting and I learned a ton from his class. Some of the assignment instructions were a little unclear: he isn't a fan of unconventional essay-writing. After the first essay, I made sure I stuck closely to the few instructions in the syllabus and avoided going off-topic and I was fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class could've been so cool, given the topic, but it was a massive disappointment. Professor Ochonu's lectures were irrelevant and boring, his grading was extremely hard, and he seemed to give up halfway through (after which he only showed movies in class). All of these issues were exacerbated by the fact that he refused to answer any emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Only grades are 3 papers and one end of year group project with literally no guidelines. Pretty impossible to do well even if you go to office hours. Allows rewrites but doesn't announce that to the class. Only way to get a rewrite is to ask after a specific paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Total chiller. Great guy and passionate. He's very straightforward and makes himself accessible. He allows you to get the grade you want if you're willing to work for it. Papers were interesting and graded appropriately. Will take his classes in the future
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Unsatisfying. The class had an interesting premise--Commodities and Conflicts in Africa--but the lectures were just okay and the reading was irrelevant to class discussion and the graded components. We watched a ton of movies in class. It was interesting at first. Had to write a group paper, which was a strange assignment.
I loved the class! I learned so much and there was a great dynamic! Also amazing style. I was worried coming in but i really enjoyed it-African Nationalism

I've taken three courses with him. If you are interested in Africa and are ready for a challenge he's a must have. There are movie days,his office hours are helpful and his lectures are engaging. He is a tough paper grader and there will be one group project. Do the reading, engage in class, and go to the writing studio and you'll do fine!

Pointless power-point based lectures on African facts. Never used class notes.  10% participate, and 70% papers x3, 1 group project. Broad paper topics arguing which factor ie: trade or farming better. Unclear criteria, don't use facts, subjective grader. Senior bio major taking course for AXLE, grade lowered my cumulative GPA.

Professor Ochonu is an intelligent man who is very interested in the subject he teaches. I only took the class because I needed to fill a spot, but I enjoyed it so much that I took the second half the next semester. His grading is a little tough, but he is very helpful during office hours if you are not getting the grade you want.

This is without a doubt the worst class I've had at Vandy. I dreaded going to every single one of his classes. People would fall asleep while sitting up. He's a very tough grader; my entire class would cry together the night before a paper was due because we would stay up all night to meet his ridiculous expectations.

Great professor!  He is so clear in his teaching, he is as nice as could be, and he is intellectually engaging!  He focuses on the most interesting parts of African history.  He assigned a buttload of reading, but most of it was worthwhile.  I absolutely recommend.

Poor lectures and grading.  Generally presents facts without context and in no particular order, which makes them hard to follow or prioritize.  Nice guy, but don't take this class from him if you want to learn a lot and have your grade reflect that.

Very knowledgeable and helpful professor.  He is an excellent student of Africa and therefore is a good prof.  Could stand to jazz up his teaching style, but over all, you will learn a lot and have no regrets.
nice guy. awful grader. i wouldn't take another class with him because he's really impossible to please...which sucks, because i love africa, and i kind of love ochonu too.
Prof Ochonu is, in fact, a tough grader. He is, however, very kind and approachable.
Unspeakably boring. Not particularly helpful or reasonable. I'd advise finding something else for that int'l cultures requirement.

He is really boring. You don't have to do the reading though because he never checks. We got one quiz because he suspected everyone of not reading-which they werent. Only 3 papers but besides that no other assignements. pretty tough grader though

I think he's a nice guy and I was interested in the class; however, we only had three 5 page papers graded the entire semester.  Since he only assigned three papers, you'd think he'd be lenient..not the case. It's an easy class because you don't have to do the readings but be prepared because he's a really tough grader.

decent professor. was really interested in the subject before i took the class, but now im not interested in continuing at all. good class because you dont always have to do the reading, but he grades harder than i would have expected.

Great professor.  Lectures a little boring, and there's a ton of reading, but if you don't do it, there's really no consequences besides his disappointment.  Only three writing assignments throughout class, all of which are graded fairly easily.

In the context of Vandy's math department, Alex is one of the best options.  He goes over all of the material found on exams in class, and always does a few examples.  Weekly hw's are of similar difficulty to exams.  Outside practice is needed to ensure a good grade and subject understanding.  Alex is hilarious and try's to make every class fun!

His lectures were difficult to follow and I learned more from reading the textbook/online. However, he was available for office hours and was caring. His tests and quizzes were difficult but he was a lenient grader. There is homework every week which was good practice for tests.

He's a really nice guy, but did not enjoy having him as a professor. Tests are so different from the lecture content, quizzes, and homework. He says quizzes and homework are harder than the exam so we are more prepared, but that is a lie. He doesn't curve. But whenever I doodled on exam questions I didn't know, he gave me a point.

In terms of the Vanderbilt math department, Alex was a pretty good professor. He actually taught the material in a way you can understand it. His exams are hard and fast-paced but pretty reasonable. There are weekly quizzes that are problems taken directly out of the textbook. There are also weekly homeworks that take a while but aren't bad.

Alex is such a kind professor and I enjoyed having him this year for 2410. The quizzes and homework focus a lot on proofs/abstract topics and he does not follow the book closely enough to make the book worth it. The midterms were easier but overall the topics were difficult. He tries his best and the class is what you make of it.

this is the last semester he will be in Vanderbilt
good prof in vandy math dept
good teacher at conceptual linear algebra. some homework are hard. midterm are fairly easy. recommend if you'd like math.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All of his sections are harder than others but you can learn a lot. If you want a meaningful experience, choose his class!

Professor Vlasiuk's teaching is either hit or miss for most people, you'll either get it or you will spend the entire semester trying to understand it. Definitely use the office hours to your advantage, he's a fair grader but his quiz and test questions can be confusing when it comes to the abstract topics. Overall, it's an ok class.

I don't understand the hate - Alex is SO funny and genuinely cares so much. When our first midterm had a low average, instead of getting angry, he spent the rest of the week reviewing the material, let us do corrections for points back, and then asked us what he could do better as a prof. Exams are fast paced but fair. Favorite prof this semester.

Alex is a funny guy, but not the best teacher. His lectures were very difficult to follow. He focuses heavily on theory, and often goes on tangents about proofs, despite this being an applied math course for engineers. He doesn't give very many example problems, which made it hard to study for exams. Felt like his section was much harder than other

He's a very likable professor, but his content is very difficult and hard to study for. His class, at least for linear seems much harder than other sections. He's pretty funny, but his lectures are hard to understand and his exams are really difficult.

I had Professor Vlasiuk as a Freshman in 2300. He was a pretty meh lecturer because he spends half of class doing proofs and the other half doing the actual problems. If you are willing to use the textbook as a resource and stay on top of your work, you can do well. He doesn't curve, but usually puts on problems that are covered in class or on hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Vlasiuk is really passionate about teaching. He would spend a lot of time in class doing proofs rather than doing examples. However, he is a tough grader, with no curve, little correction grades, and a lot of homework. He will always be available after class and during office hour. Be prepared to make a lot of effort. Not an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best the math dept has to offer. His lectures are incredibly clear, his feedback on homework is helpful and he's such a nice prof in general. Highly recommend if you want to take abstract or modern algebra.
This man is the GOAT. These others reviews are just salty they can't do math. He gives great feedback and the exams are totally reasonable.

Was a little worried due to other reviews below, but turned out to be completely fine. He's an older professor and English isn't his first language, so it takes a bit more effort to communicate clearly, but honestly not as bad as everyone makes it out to be. Lectures were solid, never had any issues with grading, and he was helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I asked him for help on a specific homework question and his response was "go to casa tutoring. You expect me to help you with homework?"

This class was super hard and I did not understand 80% of what the professor was saying. If you aren't obsessed with abstract math, then do NOT take this class. I was very unpleasantly surprised, and it was probably the worst semester of my college career so far. The material put me to sleep every week and I used the textbook as my pillow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nice guy, and helpful enough the few times I went to his office hours.  Go to class or you?re screwed--The flimsy ?textbook? from campus copy is better served as a snot rag for all the sense its abbreviated explanations make.  One of the more difficult math classes I've taken at Vandy, but an easy B and obtainable A if you put in the time.

Not exactly a thrilling teacher, and the textbook is horrible, but his lectures are clear and easy to follow enough that if you write down everything he says and know the homework backwards and forwards, it's an easy A.  And his accent is not bad at all.

If you don't speak Russian and aren't obsessed with math, get out of Dodge.  His lectures are horrendous and he uses a terrible study guide.  He misgraded one of my questions for 20 points, and I had to get my other chinese math teacher to argue with him for me.  The sheer comedy of it almost forgave his pathetic teaching from the semester.

Amazing teacher, especially if you enjoy math. Lectures are very clear and easy to follow. The homeworks are short, but they make sure you understand the material, and the quizzes/tests are significantly easier than the homeworks. He grades harshly, but he provides lots of extra credit on homeworks.

Highly recommend. Professor Oliver has wakened my interest in psychoanalysis. She encourages class discussion and respects every student's opinion whether it is fair or not. Incredibly knowledgeable and encouraging. Very generous: gives away TONS OF free philosophy books.

Worst class I've taken thus far. Oliver is a boring lecturer who takes an interesting topic and kills it. Reads from a script. She doesn't encourage discussion. It's easy, but the class is mindnumbing, especially since it's so long. Everything has a contrived feminist or anti-feminist spin. I wrote the final paper the day it was due & made an A-.

Interesting class. Reading not necessary on a daily basis. There are two papers worth forty percent each and participation is worth twenty percent, but the grading is all done by the TA, though she is willing to review papers beforehand and help. She's open to suggestions for class and gave lots of extra credit opportunities/ could re-write papers

AVOID!! I took this class looking for an easy A given the last 2 ratings. It's clear her policy changed in the past 3 years. Grading is all subjective-20% participation, 80% divided into 2 papers. Schedules the 1st paper to be graded/returned the week AFTER the deadline to withdraw. You don't know your grade in the class until it's too late.
Very easy teacher, just three essays and no final exam.  Grading is easy and essays can be resubmitted for a better grade.

TAKE HER CLASS! i know it sounds wack because its feminism and film BUT there are only two papers and one presentation NO QUIZZES NO TESTS. you watch movies like knocked up and baby mama and talk about them. BEST CLASS AT VANDY. There is a lot of reading, but i didnt read one article all semester and i got an a-. As long as you say one or two thing

Professor de Oliveira is so calm and collected. He is always prepared. Most of the classes were discussion based, which I personally really enjoyed being more outspoken. He's very open to hearing new ideas and really pushes students to think about what they are reading. The main book we read I really liked and definitely recommend the course.
Great professor, up there with the best of the best!
Very knowledgeable

He has very high standards for writing assignments, but ultimately has a point in his criticisms. What was frustrating was he would tell me that my papers were excellently argued but as criticism introduce potential complicating factors that he thinks I should have discussed that would have lengthened the papers far past the page cap to prove them.

He really knows his stuff and is super engaging if you demonstrate your interest. Expects you to read a hell of a lot, but the readings are great, he picks really fun stories so it's not really a drag. If you put the work in you can definitely get an A, he's not an unfair grader.

My class was a FYWS and it was pretty easy. The only issue was daily reading assignments, but other than that the grading scale was very easy, and Cassio is a really nice guy. A little shy because it's his first year, but overall a good professor.

Good professor, it's his first year teaching at Vanderbilt so there were some things that he could have done better in terms of conveying the material. Homework every day, tests every couple of weeks, and quizzes almost weekly. Offers test/quiz corrections. Expects a lot of participation in class!

Stay away from Ali Sina Onder.  Other teachers will integrate econ 150 as an econ and stat class.  Did not discuss econ the entire semester.  He's terribly boring, mildly difficult to understand, and the exams are difficult (on subjects he simply forgot to teach) and uncurved.  He manages to confuses you on trivial stat concepts.  Run
Make sure you do well on the group assignments because they will make or break your grade.  Allows cheat sheets on tests.  Test are difficult but not killer

one of the worst teachers i have ever had. he barely speaks any English and can not explain the topics at all. I have a good background in stats, and he would completely confuse me talking about basic topics. In fact he would get many examples wrong, and even graded one of our four midterm questions incorrectly. Avoid this guy if at all possible

Does a number of practice problems in class but doesn't assign enough homework problems to give you a firm grip on the material or a good idea of what will be on the test. Tests were 4 questions and difficult with no curve, but group homework and projects are easily graded and a substantial portion of  grade. Not a fun class but an A is obtainable.

Class is a discussion about a play a week. Discussions are interesting, but participation matters so read the plays. Your grade is 3 essays and you are allowed rewrites. She is a very fair grader and gives good feedback. Professor Orr is such a sweet person and while this class is a decent amount of work, I recommend taking it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Orr is amazing at driving discussion. She'll make topics really engaging, and she promotes a welcoming atmosphere among students. Sometimes the reading was heavy, but other weeks they weren't that bad. I loved hearing her insights too!

Prof. Orr is very knowledgeable and helps drive class discussion while orienting us in the right direction. I'm really glad I took her class--I learned a lot with a reasonable workload and a caring professor.

You read a book every 1.5 weeks. There's 3 papers and 2 presentations; not bad at all.
