You have essentially 3 chances to get an A per paper because you submit a draft and she gives you up to two rewrites. The novels are interesting, good reads. Professor Orr really tries to simulate discussion; come ready to discuss
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Orr is a huge sweetheart. Her lectures are great (not that you have to go to them) and she is so fun and eloquent. She's happy to meet with students outside of class and provide feedback on papers, and is super helpful and caring. I absolutely recommend her to anyone regardless of their interest in the subject!

Relatively easy class. I showed up about half the time and did very well. Reading isn't necessary but she will ask hard-hitting questions to trick you, so skim the readings. Gives good feedback on essays. 2 presentations that you can do in groups or by yourself. If you need to fulfill AXLE or Peabody Core, take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Her class was EXTREMELY boring. Most of the lectures were pointless because you only have to write about maybe 5 plays total. But the lectures that deal with the play you're writing about are quite helpful. She is pretty helpful outside of class/very available. Take this class if there isn't a better option. It's bearable because its easy.

Orr is a smart and sweet woman, and made the subject material interesting when I had known nothing about it. She really values participation in class, so while attendance is not mandatory, participating a lot WILL help your grade. Very helpful in conferences and gives useful feedback, and wants you to succeed! Also allows rewrites
Professor Orr was extremely knowledgeable on the subject area, and allowed the class to engage in discussion while not straying from the topic being discussed.

Very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic.  She required three short papers and one long paper and would allow rewrites on the short papers as long as you discussed the papers with her. She also required an oral presentation in which she graded easily.
Wonderful professor. A bit absent-minded at times, but I truly enjoyed her class and the Pacific lit we studied.  I think she's choice and a brilliant scholar.

Prof. Orr is very nice, she has a cool accent and is from New Zealand (which is the basis of class). The 1st of the sem. was reading about 3 poems a day (not to exceed a page) and discussing thm in class. There are 3 papers due throughout the sem. about 4-5 pages and she doesnt grade that hard (if youre not satisfied rewrites/regrades are allowed.

Without question, the worst instructor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. Everything in the class, from quiz dates to material to office hours to grading criteria is subject to change at a moment's notice. Quizzes were extremely difficult and you had to seek them out to get them back; the assignments were not graded until the last few weeks. Huge curve

Otte definetely fits more to the role of a great teaching assistance, he just cannot take the responsibility as a professor. However, you got the trade-off: he is a way-easier grader than doug schmidts and gives out final letter grade very generously, which could save your  GPA.
If you take CS 251 with Otte, you will learn nothing, or little.
Otte is the most irresponsible professor I've ever seen in Vanderbilt. The other day he let us go 15 minutes early because he was not prepared for the next ppt.
Take otte's class if you are suicidal and want to have more reason to end things.

All he cares about is his wife.  Otte is the worst professor I have ever seen in Vanderbilt, he decides whether or not to hold office hours in the weekend depending on his wife's travel plan. And his lecture was so boring that most of the students fall asleep. And he would not tell you anything about android and then let you do an app from scratch.

I learned a ton taking CS 251 from Otte but the class was one of the hardest things I've done in my life. Probably spent 20+ hours per week on his assignments for mediocre grades. That being said I really felt like I was a better programmer by the end of it all. Occasionally places too much emphasis on C++ features as oppose to design idioms
Knows his stuff.  Perhaps not the very best lecturer, he is very helpful in office hours.

Would have enjoyed the class more if he wasn't so lecture heavy. He just talks for hours on end. Yes, he has experience in Congress, but I would definitely not recommend this class to anyone who is actually interested in learning about the political system. Unbearably B-O-R-I-N-G. Good riddance!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Oppenheimer is one of the best professors I've ever had. He can be dry at times, but that's the nature of the material. His lectures are typically entertaining and he has a lot of experience in the legislative branch. He provided stories as examples for tough concepts, threw in some jokes, and was more than willing to help on exams and papers.

Professor Oppenheimer was pretty good once you got to know him. He is very kind at office hours and gives good advice. His lectures were a bit dry at times (cant blame him), but he tries to incorporate humor and make it fun. I had a good time taking notes while he spoke because much of his lecture material was useful for the exams and paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bruce is doable. Lectures can by dry at times but he's a funny guy. All grading is done by the TAs, who are nice enough. One paper, two tests, a final, and participation.

Prof. O is a nice guy, class is boring if you don't pay attention (and its easy not to) but if you pay attention he make sit interesting. The grading is all on 2 tests, a paper and the final, and all are pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Oppenheimer is a homie. He cares about his students understanding and learning, not about how well you do on tests. He's super nice if you come to office hours. Lectures can be very boring and hard to pay attention to if you're tired but if you do listen you learn a lot.

ou can really read your textbook and get the same level of excitement and the same exact information as you can being in his lectures. He's uninspired and doesn't encourage students to really ask questions or do anything. Maybe it's because it's an intro course. It's not an easy A for sure. I know most kids did really badly on the first test.

Oppenheimer is a hilarious guy and is extremely clear and intelligent, so anyone can understanding him. The grading criteria and workload were a lot. Grades were based on 2 tests, an essay, and a final. These were graded difficulty for the allotted time and required hours of reading for only a small amount of content to be included on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof O is the best! He's so knowledgable about Congress. This class was 50% participation and 50% final paper. His lectures are so interesting but the class is really discussion based so you have to do the reading (lots of reading). Would take again

Professor Oppenheimer is a very kind, old man. That said, he's not a very good professor. He easily goes off topic and you're never quite sure what the topic was supposed to be. He does not use a powerpoint and just gets up and lectures. He's also quiet and it is hard to take notes when you can barely hear him. Take him in a smaller class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really a good dude

The class is a 20 page paper (lots of work but graded easier than average), a midterm, and a final (worth 40% of your final grade). But don't let that stop you from taking this class. He is always willing to meet and his lecture aren't boring! Would take him again!!!

He allows you to skip a few classes, but honestly his lectures were so entertaining I never wanted to. The guy is hilarious if you pay enough attention, and he knows anything and everything about Congress. You know exactly what to expect out of tests, and it had a pretty manageable workload. Get ready to take notes though, you'll need them.

Attendance and reading the textbook is absolutely necessary to get a good grade in the class. The tests are all essays written in class and are way too strictly graded for something written in so little time.

Awesome professor, I've had him for 3 classes. He knows more than anyone else about Congress, is very kind, and assigns more interesting papers than other classes I've taken. He's kind of quirky and can be a dull lecturer, but if you can get past that, his classes are well worth it.

Amazing prof, expert in his field, knows everything about Congress. Very helpful in office hours and genuinely nice guy who cares about his students. Vague prompts and grading criteria, but he will clarify a bit if you go to office hours. Hardest course I've taken in college-do NOT take this if you're not prepared for a ton of work-but worth it.

Oppenheimer is extremely knowledgeable about congressional politics and has great anecdotes that he tells to illustrate concepts. Biggest drawback is the amount of work that goes into his courses. He's also rambles a lot, but he's a very caring individual and a great professor, if you can do well in his classes. One of my favorites in Poli Sci.

I took a small seminar with Prof O and it was my favorite class this semester. He is engaging and very knowledgeable, and he has a genuine desire for his students to be interested in his subjects. A great guy  all around. He likes baseball too, which is a plus.

At first, he's pretty intimidating, but after you get used to his sense of humor (which can sometimes be sharp), his class is pretty enjoyable. Gives good feedback once assignments have been graded, but has unclear grading criteria. Sometimes lectures can be dry, but other times incorporates storiesjokes. Is very nice to talk to outside of class.

One of the WORST teachers I've ever had. His lectures put me to sleep every time despite my best intentions. Tests are hard, reading assignments are long and cover way too much material but you need to do them to do well. Nice guy, but his lectures were horrible and boring would be an understatement. Take another professor if you can!
Great professor. Makes you work for good grades and doesn't curve, but an A or B is definitely doable. Really interested in the content and cares about his students.

This is the first review I've written and I just have to say that Oppenheimer is a really great professor. I took this class P/F my 2nd semester senior year for AXLE credit and it turned out to be the class I've learned the most in and actually wanted to put the most effort into. He makes you WANT to work hard and do well, which is very rare.

Professor Oppenheimer was a great professor and knows everything about Congress. I am so glad I took this class and do not regret it whatsoever. However, if you are looking for an easy A, do not take this. It is extremely difficult and takes a lot of commitment and hard work. Plus, he is a really tough grader. But he is really kind and helpful.

Clearly cares about the material he's teaching. I love his anecdotes about when he was a Congressional Fellow; he has lived the material he presents. He is a pretty tough grader, always wanting you to do better. The research paper prompt we had was rather vague, but if you go to office hours/ask questions in class, he'll answer them.

Definitely not an easy class, but not an impossible class either. Professor Oppenheimer makes you work for your grade, and he rewards participation and  perceived effort. The class could get dull at points, but Professor Oppenheimer definitely cares about his students. I would take this if you have a real passion for American politics.

Oppenheimer is an expert in his field, but his grading expectations are slightly ridiculous for a 100 Intro course, especially when compared to other PoliSci 100 classes taught by other professors. I completely agree with the poster below who said that seemingly perfect papers will often receive an 86 or an 89. If anything, it's very frustrating.
Oppenheimer is great. He's goofy...he brought his dog when he came to hand out our final exam. He's tough, but he's brilliant.

Professor Oppenheimer was by my favorite professor this semester. He is goofy; hilarious; entertaining; and always able to blow you away with his knowledge. From what I've heard, he is definitely a "must take before you graduate" type professor. A+. HOWEVER, he grades very hard, and a seemingly perfect paper will often be returned with an 86 or 89.

I found his lectures to be less organized and interesting than Geer's. Seems like he's reading off a list all the time, which makes it hard to take notes. Otherwise, he is a knowledgeable guy who knows a lot about congressional elections especially.
Overall pretty nice guy.  Will make you laugh out of pure goofiness.  He does his best to make his lectures interesting.

He expects a lot and grades rigorously. Don't take him if you're looking for something easy. He assigns a lot of reading and want you to know it well. Lectures are long but he knows everything. Seriously, everything. He is helpful but wants you to work.
If you are serious about politics you have to take a class with Oppenheimer. You learn a lot and don't get stuck with busy work. no question my favorite professor at Vanderbilt

I have taken 11 PSCI classes and taken as many of prof. o's courses as possible. He is an endless source of information on government and his stories and jokes make lectures more fun. He is very helpful and supportive when you come to him for help.. He treats us more like peers than other professors. He has high expectations and you learn a lot.

He's the best lecturer I've ever heard a really interesting character to watch.  He's extremely helpful and cares a lot about his students. He grades fairly, but he'll make you do the necessary amount to learn the material.   Extremely knowledgeable...I actually found a recent interview with him in a political magazine during the class.

Professor Oppenheimer is a terrific professor and leading scholar amongst the Vanderbilt faculty. His expectations for his class are high, and he grades rigorously. Above all, he is always willing to help and work on tests and papers...meet with him and he will tell you exactly what you need to do...I liked him so much that I made him my advisor.

I ADORE this man. He's my favorite teacher in the department. Sure he can be kind of boring sometimes- but he has good intentions and wants to see everyone do well. I would love to take many more classes with him!
Oppenheimer looks like a Founding Father, but his teaching is boring boring boring.  His class was one of the least riveting classes I took at Vandy and was the reason I did not major in Poly Sci.

Tall. Somewhat manic also; he will speak softly for a bit, then just as your lulled to sleep, raise his voice or slam his hand on the table to make a point about roll call voting, or some other worthless aspect of american politics. Goes to NCAA tournament though, so is at least somewhat normal.
I LOVE THIS GUY! He's an excellent teacher who doesn't get boring after about 10 minutes. 2 thumbs up!

The Bruce is Looooose.  Best professor at Vanderbilt, and likely in the country.  Entertaining and knowledgeable.  Political Biographies class is by far the best, but great in big lectures, too.  Too bad he can't win the Birkby award every year (though it's kind of a scam)

Great teacher and a very smart professor! Grades fairly and has helpful TA's. Not as intimidating as he looks. Seems politically libral but does not let it show inside class. Very well versed on the Legislative area of American politics.

Prof. O is knows a lot about Congress reps. and at first I thought this course would be very interesting, but I was wrong.  The second half of the course is very boring.  Hard grader on both tests and paper.  Has too high of expectations on work.
Oppenheimer knows so much about every aspect of American politics. And even though he says he is a huge democrat, his grading is surprisingly fair. He has great stories, too!
Very good and smart, test are not easy! Lays a good framework for political science classes in the future!

Prof. Oppenheimer is one of the main reasons I ultimately decided on a PSCI major.  If you're into American politics, particularly the legislative side, he's the one to go to.  He's obviously a brilliant man, and his sense of humor is great.

One of the smartest guys around.  He made the topics interesting with his personal stories about Congress and its members.  He's a big help if he knows you're doing hte work and I learned so much by putting forth the effort for him.
Bruce is a funny and remarkably smart man.  He lectures pretty well, but his tests can be pretty hard.

He gives great lectures and adds his unique humor to make the world of politics a little more interesting.  The tests were decent, a little on the difficult side.  He also takes attendance and allows 3 absences.

He is one of the smartest men I have ever been taught by.  Literally, he knows everything about every person who ever served in the US Congress.  Very challenging classes, but he is not that hard of a grader on papers.  Nice guy, great advisor.
Best prof. I've had at Vandy, and a fine advisor.  Has a great baseball seminar for Maymester, too.  Not easy with grades, but helpful if you'll do the work.
Great, very helpful teacher with a surprising dry whit masked by a dull delivery.  Is the world's tallest Jewish political scientist

Professor Osin is a very clear lecturer. The expectations are very clear from the get-go. Graded homework every class, with two tests and a final paper. Although the first test was harder, Osin eased up the difficulty on the final test and paper. I think this was mostly because of Corona, so I don't know how a regular semester would go.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took linear for the second time with Osin. Previously took linear with another prof and understood nothing and got a D-. Got a B+ with Osin and actually understood the material and liked going to class. Of the many math professors I've had, Osin is by far my fave. Super nice, wants you to succeed. Def a genius and easy to understand

I learned how to study mathematics from him.  Actually, I took MATH 204 taught by another professor in 2013. In the end, I dropped the class because I did not know how to study mathematics rigorously. However, In this time, prof. Oshin taught us how to do so indirectly through quiz and lectures.  I would like to recommend this course to all !!

The most recent rating is ridiculous. Dr. Osin is extremely helpful and fair and this class with him is probably one of the easiest classes in the math department. His tests are not hard AT ALL, and though the final is weighted heavily, it is also extremely easy. Any negative rating about Dr. Osin for Math 204 simply shows the student didn't try.
Tough enough class as is, but the tests were horrible. He's a good teacher, but understanding him is difficult, especially with his accent.

This class is VERY proof based. He randomly collects homework. 3 tests, one is dropped, 5 questions that are harder than the homework, but he gives tons of partial credit.  There is an extra-credit paper opportunity at the end of the semester that can raise your grade a letter.He is very helpful and always takes homework questions. Great teacher!
Incredibly rude, would not recommend.

Absolutely do not take the writing seminar. Especially as a freshman, this is not the one to take. His discussions are confusing and create an environment that is super stressful because he will question everything you say. I can't speak for his other classes but this is the worst writing seminar you could take.

Outlaw is undoubtedly the best professor I've ever had. After taking his FYWS, I took Critical Theory second semester and plan to take more classes from him in the future. He is a genius and one of the kindest people I have ever met. Grading is tough but fair and rewarding. If you put in the effort you will succeed. Learning from him is an honor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't take if you want a normal Vandy class where you game your way into an A. This class is about more than just learning how to do school well. Outlaw challenges big ideas, holds intense conversation, and is a reminder of the real learning that can happen at university. He has the coolest bio/story and truly loves students and the art of teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had. Rude, snarky, and condescending. Extremely unclear in his assignments and has no problem giving everyone crappy grades and then blaming it on them. Half the grade an arbitrary "participation" grade, which he decides based on how much he likes you (expect your grade to drop a whole letter grade on the last day).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The first day of class, I was frightened and almost dropped. I'm glad I stayed. The class was usually interesting due to his jokes and explanations. In order to do well, you must participate and do well on the continuous paper. He is very accessible (even outside of his office hours) and willing to go over paper edits. Very genuine & caring person!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The class is basically him rambling on about philosophical ideas and making students read multiple books at a time. Discussions are hard to follow if this is your first experience with philosophy. Also, gives vague instructions for papers, which are all the course requires. The submission of multiple papers with vague prompts determine your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although he knows a lot about philosophy the professor is completely misogynistic and will not consider a female's opinion on matters regarding philosophy and the equality of males and females. There were occasions when the professor just would not let females defend their position on topics. The classroom environment is completely patriarchal.
I heard such great things about Dr. Outlaw and was excited until I actually ended up in the class

The worst experience I ever had. Boring class, learned very little. It was a chore to attend his class and listen to him ramble about the same topics everyday or allow students to spout off poorly thought out ideas.

Hard on the outside but soft on the outside. Actually a sweet old man. Very knowledgeable and has high expectations. Definitely not the easiest of writing seminars but very interesting. Picked some good texts for the course too. He is accessible and gives feedback-- grade is based on the final paper. All other submissions are just drafts really.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: content was difficult to understand and he expected a lot of students. difficult content made it hard to write decent papers. however, there is one paper that is added onto throughout the semester, and the last submission  final grade. he is willing to talk to you and help you out

The readings are very dense and heavy. If you are not really interested in the topic, don't choose. Even though I am not extremely interested, I learned a lot, by here I mean, A LOT, its like a big deal, you look at things differently now because of the philosophy you learned. Professor Outlaw is really knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Outlaw is a grizzly bear on the outside, but a total softie on the inside. Yes, the class will challenge you in many ways and force you to think about democracy in America in a different way. However, if you do the reading and listen in class- it's extremely manageable. You work on just one paper throughout the semester.

Professor Outlaw is both a genius and a lunatic. The class was very challenging but in a great way. There is essentially one essay written over the 5-6 submissions, each submission is graded and returned he doesn't tell you the grade unless you ask, at the end the highest grade is taken. I highly recommend you take his course.

This class is tough but well worth your time. Be prepared to read, as the assigned texts are crucial to writing your final paper. The only assignment is a twenty page paper, but every two weeks you turn in a draft with a few pages, and each edition you add a couple of more. You /must/ participate in class, and don't be afraid to ask him for help.

One of the most frustrating classes I've ever taken. Expect to read about a lot of which you care little about and participate on. It's very hard and confusing course, he seems like he knows his stuff but isn't very clear in getting it across. One paper that he won't even tell you a final grade till like 2 weeks left ... got a C+... thanks

Lots of reading, be prepared to read and PARTICIPATE (50% of grade). The other 50% comes from a long-ass paper you write throughout the entire course, he won't tell you your grade though... until the end. And that kids is how I met a B- in this course. Tough and confusing. Pick something else for an easy first year seminar.

Prof. Outlaw is a genius. He's a philosophical mastermind, which is why his class is so difficult. His grading is relatively harsh,  but he does teach you how to read and write. Reading is huge for this class. Basically, the structure of the class is that you read the books and discuss in class. Sometimes class feels like it just drags on forever.

Sweetest professor ever, she cares a lot about her students and her material. She was sick for a week but still persisted to come to class because she said she didn't want to waster her student's time. She grades very fairly and responds very fast to emails! take her class!

Professor Osina is one of the nicest people I have ever met. She cares so much about her students and seeing them learn. The class has no exams and is based on homework and one long paper. The content isn't riveting, but Osina works hard to make it interactive and fun. Highly recommend.

Dr. Osina is very nice and cares a lot about the subject matter. If you have to take a methods class, she is probably the best option out there since her class has no exams. There are a lot of assignments, but they are manageable if you read the textbook and pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Osina is very sweet and cares about her students. The lectures can be boring at times, but the class is an easy A. No exams, just homework assignments, and one semester-long group project.

Dr.Osina is a very straight forward professor. She explains all required material in class, and while she gives a lot of homework they are never very long and she gives great feedback that is helpful for exams. She is clear about what she expects and as long as you do the homework and pay attention in class you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Osina deserves a better rating. I took this class with little to no statistical knowledge and a subpar math ability, and it was easier than I expected. The class is structured in a way that sets you up for success, and if you put in a minimum amount of effort, you'll do well. She is so kind and caring!

I love Dr. Osina. I don't know why other RMP reviews are so harsh on her! She was very sweet and funny in class and truly cared about her students (she even came to my ballet performance). Assignments were also straightforward and not difficult. Class was a little boring at times, but that's just the subject material.

Professor Osina is nice but this class is pretty tough and she doesn't always do a great job explaining things. If you're a Psych major needing to fulfill the methods requirement, I would advise taking a different class or professor. Lots of hours spent working late into the night just to get an okay grade. I'd def avoid if I could go back now.

I love Professor Osina! Her way of teaching works very well for me personally. Basically, every unit we would have lecture, class practice, homework that is very similar to the class practice, a study guide/practice test, and a test. Definitely try to make it to most classes though (especially if you don't have previous stats experience).

Although Osina is accessible outside of class and seems to be caring, she can come off as harsh and will make you feel dumb if you do not understand a concept, she is a very tough grader and will put questions on the test that do not relate to lecture problems.. she also does not teach the information well in lecture, so be prepared to study
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a sweet professor! Lectures and in-class discussions helped the textbook make a lot more sense than it would have otherwise.

Professor Osina is so funny without trying, also beyond caring about her students. Will stay after class for hours to help students understand concepts. Her lectures mostly get the point across, but it takes a good amount of outside studying.
She is wonderful! So kind and helpful!

Prof Osina is a very sweet person. However, as a lecturer, she is slow. I've reviewed the slides on my own pretty much after every class and have used Youtube to help me learn concepts. However, she is very accessible outside of class and is a great help then.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really nice professor but her lecture slides especially after the second midterm are awful. sometimes she doesn't know what she's teaching but is very accessible by email and office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Osina is really sweet and understanding with extensions or extra help. However, her grading style is intense and she takes off lots of points. If you do not have a background in stats, I would be wary of this class. Yet, the semester does get better and she offers extra credit as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you have not taken stats before, this class is not for you (unless you plan on putting alot of work into it). This class seems to be harder than the other stats classes. She is beyond sweet, I failed the first test and she told me she will change my grade if she sees me putting in the effort (I am). Her lectures can be confusing go to the TA.

Professor Osina is super super sweet and genuinely cares about her students!! She always wants best for us, but sometimes has trouble explaining concepts if you havent taken stats before. Usually HW before class that is graded for accuracy, that is what will get you, but exams are very very easy. Gives practice tests that are identical to the tests

Sweetest lady! Super understanding if you need extensions or extra help due to personal reason. The material itself is straightforward though her lectures can be confusing sometimes. Do the homework and study her practice exams and youll get an A

I enjoyed Experimental Research Methods in Child Development with Dr. Osina. She was a little all over the place with the online format, and the class is pretty much word-for-word what you read in the textbook (she uses slides provided by the textbook company). However, she is super accommodating and really wants you to succeed. Easy class.

This was Osina's first year teaching this class so it was a little rocky at some points. With that being said, she was incredibly helpful and took a ton of time to meet with us individually if we needed help, respond quickly to emails, and was super understanding the whole year. I would really recommend taking her class.

Osina is the sweetest lady ever and genuinely cares about her students. She tends to make things very confusing in her lectures, but is helpful when asked one-on-one questions. Fairly easy class if you pay attention and especially if you have any previous experience in stats. No need to get the textbook.

Professor Osina's lectures are very confusing. It seems that she does not know the material she is teaching, and she often wastes a lot of time asking questions and waiting for responses. Her lectures are very boring.

Professor Osina is a very nice and sweet lady. She clearly cares about her students a lot, and is always available to help with concepts outside of class. However, her actual lectures are confusing-- sometimes it seems like she doesn't know herself what she is teaching. Wastes time reviewing and asking questions.

She is such a BAD lecturer. She does not know how to explain statistical terminology clearly, reading powerpoint all the time. She tries to make some jokes in the class, which are not funny at all, yet expect students to laugh. Her lectures are very dry and boring. I had to teach myself for the tests.

Professor Osina's lectures are very confusing. She just does not explain things very clearly. She either asks easy questions, which wastes a lot of class time, or she asks very hard ones; nobody knows what she is talking about. I do not recommend her class for her bad lectures. She may be a good person, but she does not know how to teach.

Professor Osina is really sweet. I barely used the textbook; her lectures, homework, and classwork (ask your questions during classwork day) are enough to understand the material. Homework is usually mandatory. The first exam is kinda hard compared to the other two, so don't stress out if you don't do so well then. She gave our class extra credit.
Osina is very kind and a very great professor! You definitely have to work for your grade though.

Pretty easy class if you thoroughly go over the Powerpoints she usually posts before class. Read them once before going to class and read them again after class. Read them before quizzes and tests. A+ guarantee. Professor Osina is a decent professor. She tries to make jokes; her accent's understandable. Ask questions if confused.

Osina is such a nice lady who really wants everyone to do well. Her English is very clear compared to other professors from abroad. This class is run exactly like a high school class--regular homework, in class worksheets, and quizzes. If you just do the assignments, you don't have to study for the exams. Her review sessions are also helpful.

There's homework after basically every lecture, but it is helpful in solidifying the material. Tests are easy if you complete the review packet she gives beforehand which covers just about everything you should need to know. Attendance is only required on days homework is due.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Osina is hands down one of the best professors I have had in my entire life. She is kind, dedicated to her students success, and a great teacher. I hate statistics and am very bad at math, but she has constantly supported and encouraged me throughout the entire course. Her tests and quizzes are fairly straightforward. She is very understanding!
Her lectures may not be as clear, but she gives good in-class worksheets for practice. Posts all the material and slides online and gives a review packet before every exam. She is a very sweet lady!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Osina is the best!! She is so sweet and really wants you to do well. I had never taken Stats before and she was so willing to meet with me once a week to make sure I was understanding the material. Not a lot of extra credit, but easy homework assignments if you pay attention. 4 non-cumulative exams. Barely use the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Osina is a terrible teacher & is sometimes confused by the material herself. Puts INCORRECT material on lecture slides and gives extra credit if you "catch mistakes," but then doesn't correct the mistakes on the slides or explain them well, so if material on slides is confusing there's a good chance it's plain wrong. DAILY hw. Lots of pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Maria likes to use jokes and will talk with you before class starts. Because English isn't her 1st language, she could sometimes struggle to answer questions. If you've taken stats before, this class should be easy. If not, a little more attention is required to understand. Homework is completely manageable, and the textbook is completely useless.
Maria is so nice and patient. She's always there to help you and save you. Also, she gives practice exams before exams, so fairly easy class.

Professor Osina was not in her element for this class. Many lectures were slide after slide of cognitive development experiments that she had to review during lecture to make sure she knew. Sometimes we had to correct her on them. She is a very nice person, but I wasn't happy with having her for this class. It felt wasted.
Maria is very helpful and this is a fairly easy class.

Homework counts for around 50% of your grade, but homework is easy and really helps you understand the material. Everything you need to know and should study is posted online. She give you the best opportunity she can to succeed.

Professor Osina is wonderful! It is clear that she absolutely loves her job, and she is very helpful. Lectures are super straightforward, and the powerpoint slides are all posted online. Homeworks are not difficult, but be sure to keep up with them because they count for a lot of your grade. Overall a great class!
Tough material, but she is helpful. Don't be afraid to ask her for help or to go to office hours. Homework load is not bad, just make sure you do it.

Professor Osina is one of the sweetest professors you'll ever have. She truly cares about her students. She says all the time how she hates to see us struggle. Very approachable and helpful. Material is definitely challenging at times, but if you show her you care you can definitely succeed.
Not helpful, is not interested in helping students succeed - to the contrary, seems she is more interested in seeing them fail.

She is not a tough grader, but she held high expectations, sometimes even didn't bother to ask students how they felt. She assumed you'd understand and never gave clear instructions and useful feedback. Her feedback only made me look worse.

Professor Peter is incredible! I was shocked on Day 1 of this class of how much I learned. 3212 includes tutoring, (lots of) readings, a couple papers, a presentation, and two exams. She is a warm demander— she has very high expectations for every student which means you'll be challenged to think and participate and you won't lose motivation!

Dr. Peter is an amazing professor! Her workload is tough but you can get it done, and you are motivated to get it done because she pushes you to be better. She holds her students to a very high standard which can feel harsh at time, but she is very understanding and will help you succeed in her class (revisions, paticipation, and growth matter).

Peter criticized my teaching during one-on-one conversation. She never provided constructive feedback, but solely how I messed up (and she literally said "messed up"). And I felt offended and insulted.

First, so much work. Second, every time I received her feedback, every time I didn't even want to be a teacher anymore. What she provided literally discouraged me. She was very condescending and always thought she was right, which made conversing with her even worse.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at Vandy! I learned so much, and she gives amazing feedback. The class had a lot of work, but it was so worth it with how much I grew. She truly cares about every single student, and this class gave me the confidence to become a teacher!

Overall, this class was a lot of hard work. However, it is soooo rewarding. You get to work with kids and put what you are learning into practice. Dr. Peter is so sweet and truly cares about her students. She takes time to get to know you and makes personal conversations with everyone. Lots of in class participation, but it really isn't bad.

High workload, high expectations, seldom listen, self-centered. And make judgments quickly, make comments quickly. Always criticize, even strangers can tell. Avoid her if you can. Or just follow until the semester ends. And be aware of your mental health: be prepared to suffer from mental exhaustion with her.

I love Jeanne! She is one of my favorite professors on campus. She supports and cares for her students. It is a lot of work, and she is a hard grader, but overall, it was such a meaningful and impactful class. PLEASE take her classes!!!
Clear instruction, but high expectations, and she doesn't listen. Very tough.

Absolutely AMAZING. One of the best professors at Vanderbilt. Explicit with her expectations even if they are HIGH. Always willing to help and will go out of her way to make sure you reach your full potential. Models how one should teach, from having a vested interest in eaach student to "scaffolding" haha Favorite professor at Vanderbilt!
Wonderful teacher, clear about her expectations and is a fair grader.

Even though this class was an insane workload (12 + hours lesson planning, reading/studying for weekly quizzes) it was such a good experience and i learned sooo much that will help once entering the teaching field. prof. peter is so helpful/knowledgable and so incredibly sweet (even if she or her class is overwhelming at times).
AMAZING!!! Love her so much! Takes a genuine interest in each student and you will learn so much!
Jeanne was amazing and I felt that she was taking an honest interest in me as a developing teacher. We still keep in touch 3 semesters later.

I loved Dr. Pfalzer's class! We got to hear about rare neurodegenerative disorders from clinicians, patients, etc. and it really put everything into perspective. Graded on four open note quizzes, participation, two presentations, and a final paper. This was definitely one of my favorite Vandy classes and I could not recommend it more.

I'm a senior, and this is easily one of my favorite classes I've taken at Vanderbilt! Dr. Pfalzer is the BEST. She's hilarious and makes class entertaining. She's also so smart and you will learn about rare/interesting neurodegenerative disorders. She brings in scientists, caregivers, and patients to guest lecture. So cool. 10/10 recommend.
She is great! Woo hoo!

Rasico is a good dude. He tends to get behind the syllabus schedule, but grades easily. Absolutely must show up to class and participate. HW is mindtap heavy but you can chat it. Some people fall asleep every class. He's good at replying to emails. There's one quiz and one graded assignment per unit. One oral and one written exam and final project

Like all of the 1101 courses this class was just busy work. There's no exams so it's very easy to do well if you put in the work. Rasico is very particular about attendance and people being on their phones for some reason. This felt more like a high school class than a college course.

Class was sometimes boring, and he would go on tangents but he was very kind and understanding. Lots of daily homework, but that's the department's call so not really his fault. He often extended deadlines if we missed an assignment. Lots of cold-calling, but you'll be fine as long as you're halfway listening and he will help you respond correctly.
Dr. Rasico is a kind professor who is interested in helping students succeed. The phonology textbook is free, and lectures often follow what is in the textbook. He is accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For a class with only 9 people, it was too lecture-heavy and repetitive. Prof isn't very clear in lectures and would go on unhelpful tangents if someone asked a question. Tests were graded harsh and attendance is a part of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't trust any of the negative reviews, this guy's class is maximum /comfy/. Just ungraded reading assignments and easy exams.  The readings are hard to parse through, but in lectures he goes over the material clearly and succinctly. 4/5 considering lectures are mostly in English (due to the (free ;)))) ) e-textbook being in English, to be fair).

Definitely felt like I struggled in this class without a phonology background. Dr. Rasico is super nice but is so passionate about the material he often went on tangents and left the students behind on what he actually wanted us to get out of the lecture. He's great but this course could use better-defined boundaries and grading was tough

For a 16 person class, this one was way too much lecturing.  It was not engaging and Prof. Rasico was very repetitive with what he taught.  That is not to say it was easy, in fact a lot of the material was confusing.  This is definitely a linguistics course and I think a background in phonology would have been helpful.

I took this class as a requirement for the major. Although I didn't like the material at all, Dr. Rasico is great! He actually cares about his students and is really sweet. If you actually attend class and take good notes, you'll do well. I would definitely recommend him.
Awesome guy who cares about his students. I would take any class he taught. He is very clear on what will be put on tests and is an engaging teacher

I took this class to improve my Spanish accent, and it definitely helped. Most everything you learn in the class is practical and can immediately be put to use to improve your accent. He is very helpful in and out of class. Tests are pretty easy if you pay attention in class. Attendance is mandatory! Don´t miss a class.

I was not very interested in this class at first, but the professor made me like it more. He is such a good professor and is genuinely interested in what he teaches and the students as well. He pretty much tells you what will be on the test by his incessant repeating of certain terms, so the tests aren´t too difficult if you pay attention in class.

Really nice guy. Phonology was pretty easy...I'm not sure what the previous reviewer was saying. Class expectations were clear, always. Don't think this is a language/lit class. The material is very scientific and there are clear right and wrong answers. Highly recommend.
Terrible professor. Very unclear about what he wants from students and not helpful outside of class. Don't take it unless you have to.

Definitely an intelligent guy. Seems to know everything about linguistics. Manageable, fairly predictable tests. Follows the text books pretty closely. Has a tendency to go off on tangents and/or repeat things he has already beat to death. Good class to fulfill the major requirement but otherwise don't bother.

Catalan is his passion, so this class is a lot of fun.  Very laid back, and manages to cover a lot of material without being boring.  Rasico definitely cares about his students.  Very approachable and helpful.
love this professor, explains everything very clearly, tells you exactly what he wants on the test, very easy going, sometimes funny, pretty easy class overall
Nice guy, knows his stuff. He has some discrepencies with the text book, so its hard to study. Very nit-picky course in general. Not very helpful/encourging if you are having trouble in the class.
Grat class. Amazing! Nice professor.

He does tend to spend the first half of class repeating the latter half of the previous class.  Nevertheless, the topic is fascinating and he is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic, not to mention an easy grader.
his class is boring and he repeats the same class after class
He is boring and unfair
i hated this class... linguistics is so boring and he does not make it interesting.  the tests are really hard.
It's an easy class if you show up and do your reading.  There isn't too much course work, no papers or anything.  He's genuinely interested in linguistics, so if you are he'll love you.

Rasico is AMAZING!!  Show up to class and definitely take notes because his tests are almost entirely from class notes.  But, if you do those two things, you´re good to go.  ´We had no papers, but the tests were not too easy, not too hard.  If you show interest, he loves you. Definitely an easy A if you do the basics.

I loved PJ! Great teacher, style, relatable, friendly, and sweet. He made class so much fun by genuinely engaging with the students and creating a respectful environment. He is by far the best teacher I have had!

Prof. PJ is genuinely the kindest and most welcoming professor at MSU. He cares about all of his students and makes class enjoyable. He is also very personable and funny. I enjoyed his class mostly because he goes out of his way to just be kind all the time. He does require a lot of reading and writing, but he makes it fun and easy to understand.
He is so welcoming and is an amazing teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Pettis was amazing. He really cared about the wellbeing of his students. The lectures were also very engaging and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: literally one of the nicest professors, so flexible, genuinely cares- do not be afraid of him. genuinely passionate about what he does. I cannot emphasize how kind he is. The only reason why he gets a 4 instead of a 5 is because, since he actually works in theater and all that, he kind of assumes you naturally know things sometimes, but again- NICE
Great teacher, cares about his students. Be ready to do some work for this class, but it'll be worth it

Prof Franck is great. He cares about his students and really made class good despite COVID If people complain about his grading, or their inability to get into groups and work on their own, just ignore them. If you read the book, pay attention to the ppts and give the class a fair shot, you'll do well and have a great time too

Interesting class! Prof Franck puts in a lot of effort to help you learn. He's really nice and caring. I would suggest this class if you want to learn a lot about the basics of theatre, have a chance to be creative, and have a low-stress time. Only complaint is the "go figure out every group assignment you have" & some mistakes on quizzes.

Phillip Franck really cares about his students. His lectures are fun, engaging, and he tells great stories. In every class I've taken with him, he's pushed back assignment due dates because his students were stressed. He's also very accessible outside of class and has great career advice. As long as you put in the work, you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Funny guy. Very knowledgeable about plays and movies. Workload was low for a writing seminar, but I learned a lot. Lots of assigned reading, but some people don't do it all. Required to read a play or watch a movie pretty much every week. In-class discussions are awesome. Gives great feedback on essays. Fair grader. 3 short essays and 1 revision.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: FAVORITE CLASS EVER. SUPER EASY. EXTREMELY INTERESTING. highly highly highly recommend

Super nice guy who is passionate, knowledgeable, and eager to answer questions. This 1st year seminar focused on visual aspects in theatre and film- 3 essays critiquing plays/films (no outside research- just opinion/analysis) and 2 group projects. Class discussions are engaging and fun. I learned a lot and gained a deeper appreciation for design.

Professor Franck is simply the best. His classes are extremely interesting, and made me look at plays and movies from a different perspective. The class is not hard, although you should pay attention in the class in order to write good papers.

Never done theatre and I enjoyed the class and learned a lot. He's really funny and class was very entertaining but could feel pretty long. Bombed the first essay but he is willing to help you out if you put in the effort. Ended up with an A-, he definitely rewarded me for improvement.
Philip is incredible. Take any negative criticisms of him with a serious grain of salt. People who say Philip is "pompous" and complain that he grades too harshly are simply morons.

Phillip is flexible, engaging, and his first priority is for his students to learn.  He is accessible in person and online to consult about papers before they are finalized. will modify deadlines, assignments, and the use of class time to best suit students.  Take this class if you like talking about the theatre and improving your writing skills.

Fun, flexible Trekkie who teaches with enthusiasm. Teaches subjects that are stimulating and have clips from famous productions. Tough grader, but in a fair way-all essays can be rewritten for credit within a week of its return. Reading is not needed but helpful. Few essays, but not always clear in what he wants from a revised essay. Great teacher!

He was really fun and the class was sorta interesting. However, you had to pay for ticktes to see 2 plays (about $50). There were only papers and participation for your grades. The grading was pretty lax and he would help you out if you ask for it. Overall easy class for non-theater majors!

First let me say, I LOVE theatre, so I assumed I would love his class (I was in his intro class.)  I was very very wrong.  He is condescending, unhelpful, unsympathetic to any problem you are having, obsessed with theatrical lighting (and never stops talking about it, which kinda gets in the way of, well, more interesting topics.)

ridiculously hard grader.pompous,cusses a lot.if you deserve an A, he'll give you a B+.class is a/b tech theatre, not analysis of plays.don't take it if you think the themes and literary significance of the plays are more important. than the lighting techniques and position of the scenery in them.my least favorite course of the year.

Great Professor! A fun class that he always gives a good atmosphere, it felt like time flew by in class everyday. There's a lot of reading and papers, but Phillip always gives the opportunity to help. Some people think he grades harsh, but I got As on most of my papers. He likes papers that have 'pizazz.' Don't be shocked if he drops F-Bombs.

I thought he was a really great teacher; always managed to keep my interest in class.  His tests weren't bad at all either, as long as you paid attention when he lectured.  A little tough on papers, but I didn't put forth that much effort on them, and he is very willing to give advice and help if you ask him for it.

Very nice guy, but grades WAY too hard for an into, freshman-level course.  You might get a good grade on quizzes and tests, but he'll kill you on the essays.  Knocked me down a WHOLE LETTER GRADE just b/c he thought i should have switched the order of two paragraphs.

This class is a good choice for someone who needs any English credit. Just like a typical English class, there are outside readings and short essays for homework. Grade is mostly based on three essays, which you can score better through unlimited rewrites. Should not be a hard class with decent effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Phelan is by far the best English teacher Ive ever had. He gives really helpful feedback and is willing to hear other prospectives about the readings both in class and while grading. Hes really helped me improve my writing, but it is not a chill class. The readings are pretty interesting and hes really open to feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Phelan is such a sweetheart. He truly cares about his students and is accommodating about deadlines. The material was very interesting, but the papers can be extensive sometimes. However, he gives good feedback, time to workshop with the peers, and UNLIMITED rewrites.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Phelan truly cares about his students inside/outside the classroom. He's easily accessible, very knowledgeable and gives unlimited re-writes on papers. But, he is also very demanding of his students through strict attendance/participation policies and grades papers quite tough. Overall he provides an interesting class with low-ish grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unclear and have you read really hard books. Just give you general comments and does not tell you how to improve at all. Does not delve into the issue you are facing, but just brushes it over. I am positive that I learned nothing. In another similar class, I got an A and my paper got published, but in this class, I feel no motivation at all.

Professor Phelan is caring, super smart about the stuff he teaches, and really knows how to lead a classroom discussion. He's not the easiest grader, but gives you UNLIMITED rewrites to get the grade you want and he's very accessible outside of class. He does give extensions. Only complaint is strict attendance policy.

Nice guy out of class, but he simply is not a good professor.  He's an unreasonably  tough grader and unclear with what he expects from his students. I managed to pull off a B only because I constantly pestered him for help. Highest grade was a B+. Do not take this class if you're looking for a relaxed writing course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: really great teacher. fostered a great classroom environment. everyone got close with both him and each other. definitely my favorite  class of the semester. he was able to joke around enough to get us engaged but was serious when it was necessary and we followed his lead. we had really great discussions. also absolutely loved the stories we read
Good guy, good class. Not the easiest grader but gives good feedback and lets you do unlimited rewrites. Will work with you to get the grade you want.

Professor Phelan is a genuinely nice guy, but such an unreasonable grader. His guidelines are so vague you never know what's expected. Tends to speak in lengthy riddles so that you're never really sure what he's even saying. Gives weekly 2-3 pg papers, plus three 5-6 page papers, all graded harshly. If you're not super into writing, stay far away

Professor Phelan is a nice guy, but he is an extremely unreasonable grader, does not explain what he wants from his students, and does not know how to teach the class in writing. Only take his class if you are really interested in the subject matter, if not stay away and take any other professor, especially if you don't want your GPA to tank.

You come to class with a lot of respect for him off-the-bat; this dude has made it in life (sits on the boards of some BIG companies, sold his own company for a lot, etc.). He is very knowledgeable in financial accounting, and you will get an easy A if you study EXACTLY what he tells you to study and do the online homework on time. Take this class!

Homework is questions taken directly from textbook and he gives you practice exams that are almost identical to the real things. Almost never had to pay attention in lecture  just learn a couple concepts before the test with the practice exams. Best part is you can earn up to 7% EC if you do some easy assignments outside class.
Really nice guy and you can tell he really enjoys teaching the subject. I recommend taking this class with him, as long as you do the work and study enough for exams you will be able to do well.

I enjoyed the hands on experience and the opportunity to work with equipment that I never thought I would be capable of using. It is evident that he wants students to be safe and learn. I am looking forward to working more with him on future projects.
He's fun, but very monotone and puts you to sleep when you need to be paying attention for the lab. Very dry wit. Co taught machining elective with Withrow (main teacher)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The welding class is the best! Be prepared to spend a lot of time in the shop !!!

His door is always open and he enjoys helping people. I had a question he did not know the answer to so he says, "I don't know let's figure it out"....that is cool! He gets frustrated with people that complain about limited time and says,"you can sleep when you are dead!" My advice, take the classes and join the FSAE team. You won't regret it.
Great hands on class for learning practical application, basic material properties,heat transfer, and machining. He also teaches a welding class and is adviser for the FSAE car project. Cool!

First and foremost, you can learn from Phil,he builds airplanes!!! He has got to be one of the most patient and tolerant people on earth. The down side to taking one of his classes is getting in. There is usually a long waiting list. I wish there were more teachers like him!

Great class: I actually graduated several years ago and just wanted to let everyone know the importance of taking these classes.  The classes he teaches will help prepare you for a job. I learned a lot from Phil and wish I could have learned more. His experience is invaluable and I still call him with questions from time to time.

This guy rocks! I took the course because I heard it was easy. Well I found out it was not! It is a lot of work for a one hour course. I had no interest in this at all before the class but now I do. Phil has such enthusiasm in the subject matter you can't help but get interested.
Simply put Phil is the man. If you don't take his class you should still go to the shop and hang out because you will learn more practical engineering stuff from Phil than in any other class.
he dated uma thurman bottom line, can you say that about your teacher
Phil is the greatest!  Just watch out for your fingers when welding... they do actually burn
No Comments
Great Teacher...he makes sure that everyone learns what he is teaching. He works hard and it shows!!!!

Lectures could be a little disorganized, but Platt was clearly so passionate about classical music that I actually enjoyed hearing from him. Tests were super easy if you have any background in music at all. Definitely go to the review sessions he hosts, which basically cover the tests.

Platt is extremely passionate and knowledgeable. Although sometimes the lectures were dull, I did take a lot out of the class. Without a music background I believe this class would be more difficult. Just pay attention, take notes, read the textbook and you'll be fine

Platt is an... interesting guy. He is pretty passionate about music, but to be honest, it was a pretty dull class (and this is coming from someone who thought they would like this class since they had a classical background). Tests are not too bad. Just attend class and act happy.

Good class to take for AXLE or Peabody req's if you have a classical music background. Around half the class is on listening tests where you identify classical pieces but it generally isn't too hard. Platt is very passionate about the subject matter and will cover historical contexts. Don't use the restroom too much or else he might get a bit sad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Platt is very very knowledgeable when it comes to introductory classical music content. I realized at the end of the semester that I learned so much in this class. It is really very interesting and Platt's enthusiasm is encouraging. You will be bombarded with much information that you can mostly take or leave based on your level of interest.

The class overall was not that challenging. If you don't have any experience with music be prepared to memorize a lot of general music terminology for the first exam and the rest of the course is manageable. My problem with the class was the unorganized and sometimes boring lectures that would be easier to review if they were made into PowerPoint.

I really loved this class, but I know it's not for everybody. Don't take this if you can't enjoy heavy lectures or fall asleep easily. If you could be interested in any topic as long as the speaker is passionate about the subject, Platt certainly delivers there. I wouldn't say you need too much music experience to do well as long as you study.

So grateful I took MUSL1220, one of the few classes that prepared me for grad school. Dr. Platt covers an impressively broad range of repertoire in limited time. He is professional, knowledgeable, passionate, and connected (he brought in two Pulitzer and Grammy winners in one year), and he is kind and generous with his time and advice, too.

Platt is very knowledge and passionate about what he does but I found the lectures were sometimes off topic and not always relevant to the course material. If you have a little musical background and are interested in the subject, this is not a difficult class. Most of the work was listening to music or writing an occasional essay.

The other people have a point, but they are also exaggerating a lot. Professor Platt's lectures aren't the most exciting, but you'll learn a lot if you pay attention and you're interested. He usually posts his lecture notes and optional textbook reading, so you will be fine on tests if you read those. Great class overall - I learned a lot!

Very hard class if you have no background in music. These tests were very difficult and no study guide was given. The test material comes from lectures so make sure you go to every class. Really nice guy just very hard for non-blair students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Platt is passionate about the material he teaches. Despite this, his lectures are the driest, least engaging, and most disorganized that I've ever had to sit through--barely worth paying attention to. I wish he played more of the music discussed. Graded by 2 midterm exams, 1 short paper, brightspace discussions, final (4 short essays).

Platt is elegant and talkative. The class is an easy A if you reviewed the materials from TA closely. The content of the course is too broad, and he might not know what to focus on at some point during the lecture, but generally, he is nice. BTW, it is easy to fall asleep in his class! Also, the review session is very helpful!

Platt is an interesting professor. He is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable on music history, yet he sometimes boring especially when he has time to kill. Not a bad class, but I wish I would have taken other classes instead. He is also comically bad with technology.
I have no idea what the other guy is saying. Professor Platt is both an excellent professor and great professor.

Worse professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He was so pretentious and condescending. Avoid this professor like the plague. If you do end up in his class, learn everything you can from the readings and then try to gather what you can from his disorganized lectures. Your gonna loose some points on the writing, so just get all the multiple choice right.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super understanding when it comes to attendance, but disappointed in the lack of clear feedback. Very difficult to follow feedback, making it challenging to improve. I always want to do better but it's hard when you don't know what you did wrong. Also the class structure is the same everyday which can get repetitive.

The most understanding professor I have had. He gives a detailed class agenda in the syllabus and tends to stick to it. He sometimes struggled to keep the attention of some students but overall his lessons were informative and very discussion heavy (which I view as a great thing). Definitely would recommend and take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I ADORED this professor!! I had him for my first-year writing seminar on environmental justice in Latin America. He was very knowledgable and I learned so much in the course. The class was graded based on essays, which he gave sufficient time to write and great feedback on. His passion for the topic was evident. One of the best profs I've had!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor sets a new standard for incompetence. Grading seems to be a game of roulette. The lectures are a marathon of monotony, and his awkwardness could make even the most enthusiastic student lose interest. Given the choice, enduring the SAT daily for the next half-decade would be a preferable fate to enduring another semester of his class.

Dr. Plummer was great at facilitating discussion and fostering an interest in poetry, even though none of the people in the class were English majors. For a writing class the work was minimal; only 4 3-4 page papers, and you didn't even need to read the poetry before class. As long as you talk and show an interest in the poems you will be fine.
Lectures can be boring, he expects participation and often calls on people so be prepared/pay attention. This can sometimes be difficult due to the nature of the content.

It's really hard to write five pages on a twelve-line poem, but that's a general problem. Plummer is definitely very knowledgeable, and helps you through it. He calls on people during class, but has a weird habit of only picking the ones sitting near him. Every class is discussing a single poem, so it can drag on a while. Papers aren't too hard.
Nice sweet professor but his grades are arbitrary. He plays favoritism a lot and only picks on a few students he likes during class discussions. Attendance is mandatory.

I took him for Chaucer, so the reading was in Middle English, but Plummer teaches you how to read it and focuses very closely on the language so you become a pro by the end. Very articulate and thoughtful, and approaches the material from a level you can understand.  The midterm and final were easily graded.  Learned a lot. Definitely recommend.

Great Professor! He leads great discussions and always encourages students to contribute. He assigns lots of reading, but if you keep up with it then the class really isn't bad. He's a pretty easy grader and a really nice guy.

Fantastic professor, very well articulated and knowledgeable. Attendance is a must as a quarter of your final grade is determined by class participation, but as a bio major I would highly recommend taking this class to fulfill AXLE requirements.

Awesome professor and class. Really knows his Chaucer and makes it interesting. Enjoyed discussions. You do have to do the readings (most of which aren't too long) and attend lectures for quizzes and the midterm, but they neither will require intense additional studying if you keep up with both of those. Fair paper grader. Recommended.

Not too difficult, although I wouldn't recommend it if you have absolutely zero background in poetry. Plummer is very articulate, an excellent discussion leader, helpful, and non-judgmental of students' opinions. Look over the poems before class, go to class, participate in discussion, and spend some time forming your paper.
Don't be put off by the first class. Plummer is a great lecturer and discussion leader.  The class is very relaxed and not difficult or time-consuming.
He did what I thought was impossible: make a Chaucer class interesting. Not an easy essay grader and occasionally a little intimidating, but he enjoys what he does and his enjoyment is infectious
Slightly intimidating and not warm and fuzzy, but he'll occasionally relax and be fun.  Very understanding.  All around nice guy, but kind of a tough grader.
Plummer is awesome.  He really loves his research and knows what he's talking about.  His tests aren't too hard and he's always helpful.  The best professor in the English department!!!
decent class
He obviously enjoys what he does, and his class is fun.  He can play favorites sometimes, though, and he's such an expert in his field that it can be a little intimidating for new people.
No Comments

He was very excited by the topic, and just knew alot about it.  His requirements weren't too difficult, and he was really helpful outside of class.  His class was enjoyable to go to, though some days he could be boring.

I love Pintane; she is quite literally my favorite Spanish professor in the entire department. She truly does care about you. If you have a solid speaking level of Spanish, this should be fairly easy. There are grammar quizzes, but it's just basic grammar. This is your sign to take this class!

She is quite literally the best professor I have ever taken. She assigns homework but never checks it, except for the online grammar work but other than that, its fine. She truly cares about improving your Spanish and will meet with you.
super kind. not a tough grader, will meet with you to try to get grade up if you want. clear schedule of all homeworks and projects on brightspace
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Pintané does a great job with meeting students where they are at with their Spanish ability. This class had several projects, and she was very quick to respond to emails and helped us as needed. A lot of the class assignments and the two tests were tough, but she gave us opportunities to improve. Very genuinely caring. Would recommend

Prof. P is my favorite Spanish teacher ever. While class was really challenging, I have improved SO MUCH, and I'm so grateful for her pushing me to do well. She inspired me to do a Spanish minor! Get ready to memorize a ton of vocab, work in groups, and have oral exams. Not a ton of tests but great feedback from a caring, passionate professor.

Dr. Pintane is a gem of the Spanish department. You can tell she is passionate about her teaching and wants her students to do well. That being said this class was a LOT of work with online homework, readings, and various projects/exams. She will let you retake an exam if you don't do well, go to Spanish convo tables for extra credit! Loved her!

Professor Pintane was incredibly helpful. She would answer questions in depth and made the class very comfortable asking questions. I enjoyed class discussions and thought the professor did a very good job making students participate and share ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pintane was disorganized and an unreasonably hard grader. My Spanish actually got worse in this class.

The professor is incredibly sweet and caring. She genuinely wants to make sure you are learning and understanding content. The class is very heavy on assignments, with grammar homework ~3 times per week plus 1-2 projects per week, but all very doable. Multiple extra credit opportunities and very accessible outside of class. 100% recommend her class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pintane is an excellent Spanish teacher and a wonderful person. There was no schedule on the syllabus past the first few weeks of class, and her assigning schedule was rough (multiple papers/projects assigned the day before breaks and due the day after), which often made the class very stressful. Overall a clear and fairly kind grader.

the best prof I had my freshman first semester; very caring, kind, funny, and knowledgeable; she helps you with your speaking and writing skills immensely and it's not a terribly difficult class; 1000% recommend taking any of her classes

Must read carefully and participate regularly to do well! Grade is mostly determined by essays. Definitely go to office hours/ask her to look at drafts. She gives good feedback, but it was discouraging when my grades didn't improve after using it. Super nice, funny, and cares about you, so definitely a strong choice but a bit tougher grading-wise.

I enjoyed going to class, and the prof is so nice. Hw is pretty light, a few exercises online after each class and some writing assignments spaced out throughout the semester. She's a tough grader, and the grammar covered gets difficult (I struggled and I got a 5 on AP Span Lang). An A is doable if you practice a lot outside of class+extra credit.

Very caring professor, but incredibly tough grader and seems to just put arbitrary numbers down as grades. I met with her outside of class and used her feedback, but she just kept giving the same grades. Made the class harder than it needed to be. Interrupts often while you are speaking, including in presentations. Made me reconsider Spanish minor.

Definitely a great choice for SPAN 2204. Pintane is a tough grader but significantly improves your Spanish. Offered an extra credit assignment that was SO fun. Always welcomes students to her apartment because she is a faculty head of house. Tough at first, but is one of the most caring professors I've ever had.
Incredible lecturer. Difficulty in this class really depends on how comfortable you are with Spanish. Writing assignments are short, feedback is clear and detailed.

Prof. Pintane is amazing and an excellent choice for Spanish 3303! She is always very caring and gives really detailed feedback to help you improve. She makes the class engaging by incorporating discussion into every lecture, and you really learn how to analyze literature in more depth throughout the semester. You will love her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lots of work for this class, but it is manageable. Class is all discussion and presentations, so do the readings so you can participate. She gives great feedback on essays, and an A is attainable as long as you take her feedback. Midterm was just an essay and majority of the grade is essays. A very caring professor and made class engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Profesora Pintane is extremely knowledgeable. She's a little intimidating at first but grows on you a lot over the semester. The readings for every class are very manageable and are a requirement before each class.
