reviews.comment: This class specifically with Piot is horrendous. Assignment is given each week which is due on Thursday of all days. Expect to spend anywhere from 12-16 hours a week on the programming assignments themselves plus another couple on the readings. Instructions are often left unclear, and is unhelpful. He always with "read the instructions." STAY AWAY
His lecture is not perfect, but he's a nice and caring professor overall. He's pretty helpful during his office hours, and he always encourages students.

If you're not a CS major or minor, avoid taking CS 1101 with Piot at ALL COSTS. Easily the most time-consuming class I've ever taken, especially if you don't have coding experience. Solid 15 hours of homework a week and very few opportunities for help (office hours only offered 3 times a week for a 100 person class). Do not take this class.

He just doesn't teach well. The coding assignments are much harder than what he teaches in class and CS hw takes a solid 13-15 hours a week. Your grade really depends on which TA grades your work; some are nice and some grade harshly. The midterms are hard because of the time crunch. If you take this class, get ready to do a lot of work.

This class was a mixed bag. I enjoyed the assignments though they took more time than any class ever should. It gets difficult quickly, especially for an intro class. Tests are hard since they are timed and require coding multiple mini-projects. I spend a good 2-3 hours a day on this class. Grading criteria are all over the place and TA dependant.

He has an extremely heavy accent so I can never understand anything he is saying. I spend more time trying to figure out what he's saying then the actual content he's attempting (very poorly) to teach. On the rare occasion I understand what he is saying, he explains the material terribly.

Truthfully, I feel as though Prof. Piot would an excellent mentor for more advanced students. However, the pace of his introductory CS1101 course is way too fast for most beginners, and many students fell behind to some extent after the first four weeks of classes. Take Piot only if you're 100% confident you want to major in Computer Science!

Professor Piot is very humorous and caring! He is the cutest professor I've met at Vandy! Some people told me he is awful, but that is not the truth for 1101. School asks him to teach some classes which do not fit his professional area - that is why he probably did awful in those classes. HOWEVER, he is great for 1101!

Piot is a mediocre teacher -- he's not as bad as everyone says but he barley is there to teach in the first place. Most course content was taught through online youtube videos so going to class is basically a waste of time. Most of the grade is determined by programming assignments but overall if you spend the time on this class you can do well
Ok this one's tough bc he's usually the only 1101 professor but avoid if you can. Best of luck kids

He is super nice and he tries to be a good professor, but he is not the best teacher. The programming assignments are ridiculously difficult and they have super strict grading criteria. I did not really know how to code before this class, and I do not suggest students to take his class if they are new to coding.

Some background about me : It was my first CS class ever at an educational institute. Before this class I only knew some basic programming in Python. He teaches passionately but there is some kind of difficulty gap between the lectures in class, and the problem assignments we need to do. The class suddenly gets harder after the first few weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: nice guy but absolutely horrible teacher especially during covid. this class is not easy if you don't know any CS coming into this class and his lectures are extremely confusing. the PAs start off easy but get really difficult towards the end. the only good part of this class are the TAs.

His lectures tended to be unhelpful, especially since he asked that everyone watch the pre-recorded lectures he posted. They were basically a repeat of one another. However, the class itself wasn't terrible, and the amount of work is fair. I saw other reviews say don't do Piot no matter what, but I would say do it if you have to.

I think Professor Piot has done his job. He replied to the questions on Piazza within one hour most of the time. Participation is not mandatory, and you can just watch the recordings from the summer (which explains thing super clearly) and read the slides to learn the stuff. The programming assignments are hard, but what else do you expect?

Class was easy first few weeks, but the difficulty spiked way up around the halfway mark. Programming assignments are long, and some of them are really hard. Had to watch lectures before every class on top of textbook work. Not super accommodating considering the current circumstances. Choose another prof, or better yet, don't take this class.

Especially during COVID, not accommodating at all. I promise you will learn nothing in lecture and need to get all info from other lectures or learn from other students. Do not take 1101 if he is the only professor available. You will not learn anything and the expectations are ridiculous. TAs are also extremely inaccessible.

I am a freshman in Piot's CS 1101 class. While he may explain things a little weirdly at first, I actually think he is a good teacher. The best part is, though, the dude is hilarious. I don't even know if he is trying to be funny sometimes, but his humor always makes for a good class. Class isn't too hard either and I had 0 CS experience.

He is never clear in what he assigns students. When you ask him a question, he contradicts what he has previously said. He is not prepared for live lectures as things always seem to go wrong from what he anticipates. Not a good instructor and you can not learn from him. Been forced to take two of his classes and it's the same. Avoid at all costs.
piot gave a couple rude quizzes but thats about it, good luck taking his class i had a good time idk about other people tho

Worst prof Ive ever had. Confusing teaching, impossible to understand. Can't make sentences, bad English. Responses to questions incomprehensible, just writes on board, says a bit, and doesn't teach, literally expecting you to learn from textbook before class instead. Kids sleep in class or don't go. Everyone knows hes bad. Have to teach yourself

Tries hard. I've taken him for discrete and comp org. Definitely improving as a prof. Asks for feedback from his students consistently and tries to tailor his class around it, but college kids rarely give good feedback other than make me do less work. Not a guaranteed A as people look for unfortunately, but not a notoriously difficult prof either.

After having had Piot two semesters in a row, my biggest takeaway is that he cares intensely about being a good professor. That being said, his lectures are difficult to follow, which he has said he is looking to improve on. Outside of class he is wonderful. I recommend that you go through lecture slides on your own time and frequent office hours.

I checked this page before the sem but still took it because there's no choice. Lectures are incredibly unclear. You learn more reading Zybooks than going to lectures. The participation grading is the harshest of all sections. Quizzes are notoriously difficultall in all, a terrible choice even for a traditionally easy class like 2212. MUST AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Piot was very helpful and tried very hard to engage students in class. I've never coded before and this class was definitely time consuming, but worth it. I'm not a CS major and won't be taking CS again. DONT take this class if you're not exploring a CS major.
Professor Piot is a very nice man, tasked with teaching very dry subject matter. His lectures are not very engaging, so you need to be self motivated and force yourself to listen and take notes.

Piot is a difficult professor but he does care about his students. If you are self motivated and seek him out for help and to clarify any questions, then this class is very doable. Quizzes can be quite challenging so make sure to ask him questions outside of class.

This is the worst professor I've ever had in my college career. Examples provided on lecture slides will not match up with the ones given on the quiz. If you really would like to do well in this class make sure you memorize everything on the slides, then forget it all because you'll get a bad grade anyway!
He knows he does not explain things well, so he is very easy on grading.
He is always willing to answer any question from his students. If you have questions in class, don't be afraid to ask in class.

Lectures are extremely dry so no one pays attention. To make it worse, you can never understand the slides. HWs are not bad, and not intensive at all. (Though more intensive than those of other sections) Dr Piot is a nice person though, and willing to help you outside class.

Just avoid taking his class. Even I could get an A with just a 63-point final, I still think taking his class makes my semester so bad. His homework is super difficult because he gives very complicated coding problems every time. Sometimes he got wrong himself and the students have to correct him.
Heavy French accent, incredibly uninspiring. His lecture of Comp Org was so much harder, with more work, and worse grades than Ghosh. Never would recommend him to any student.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Least favorite professor at Vanderbilt! Terrible lecture with one of the least engaging classes of all time. Lectures the entire time by saying random things about the slides. Do not take this class. You will learn nothing. The assignments are time-consuming and the quizzes are terribly structured.
Really nice and caring professor. Quizzes are hard sometimes but you would get a good grade if you study and do the homework. Overall an interesting class.
For the love of god, do not take his class. Awful lecturer. Unreasonably hard homework. Don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Try to take literally anybody else for Computer Organization. He is not a very good teacher and he makes this class substantially more difficult than the other sections of comp org. People fail the quizzes, and he assigns an incredibly difficult makeup assignment to get 2-3 points back on the quiz. AVOID THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Piot is a very nice guy, but he is a really bad professor. His lectures are boring and cannot hold anyone's attention, and there are many points throughout the day where he will write incorrect information on the board. His quizzes do not match the lectures of the textbook, leaving many to not do well on the quizzes. Take a different prof

A nice, funny guy but abysmal at teaching. If you have to take discrete with him, go to office hours and he will be very dedicated to making sure you understand the concepts. I would highly recommend taking this class with another professor, however.

HW is mostly programming in assembly which is time consuming and isn't even the focus of the class or exams. Lectures are super boring and his slides are literally incomprehensible. Really nice guy though and does care a lot about his students. Probably not the best choice of prof for this particular class though.

He is very caring, he wants you to learn. If you have questions, he makes all the effort for you to understand. Sometimes the lecture gets boring, but it is simply because there are a lot of materials, if you listen carefully, it is very easy to understand.

Taking this class with Dr. Piot is essentially teaching yourself a class. He flies through all of the lectures and does not explain any of the concepts well. Going to lecture actually provides negative value to your learning experience. He posts all of hislecture PowerPoints online, which is helpful because you will be teaching yourself them.

Professor Piot is a nice guy, not a great teacher. His lectures are oftentimes very boring and most of the material can be learned on your own. He is a very nice guy overall though, and he definitely cares about his students l. Not a hard class, just make sure to study for the quizzes.

Piot is a funny, caring prof. He is super helpful during office hours. Going to lecture helps a lot. He is good at explaining the content (which is harder to decipher by just looking at the slides without going to class). There are 7 homeworks, one midterm, and a final. Great prof. Definitely recommend him over other professors for this class.

Dr. Piot is a really nice guy. His lecture can be sometimes confusing but his slides are very useful for quizzes. He cares about students and is super helpful during office hours. Around 7 quizzes and 5 problem sets. He's a funny guy and gets more and more adorable over the semester.

Dr. Piot is a really nice professor. He really cares about students and is very helpful during office hours. Although sometimes his lectures are little unclear, his lecture slides are very useful. Quizzes are not that hard if you study the slides. He also holds extra review sessions for quizzes which are very helpful.
Class and material is REALLY dry. Prof has a thick French accent, but also has that old-timey, gaudy French humor. Just study the slides

His powerpoint-based lectures are very dry and he appears unprepared or somewhat confused during them. He has difficulty communicating with and understanding students. This makes an easier course much, much more difficult than it needs to be. While Piot is learning as a teacher, I strongly recommend you take this class with another teacher.

Though sometimes I have trouble understanding what he's talking about, Prof. Piot is really nice and helpful, especially outside the class. Homeworks are hard but doable if  you seek help from Piot. Overall 7 midterm-like quizes (no pop quizes) but not too bad as long as you study the PPT. Materials are dry and abstract so be prepared.

While he is a very amiable and humorous person, he is very disorganized in lecturing; and his messy lecture slides did little to help. Assignments were often unrelated to contents taught in class. He would often pose a question to the class without giving a clear answer in the end; therefore the lectures are not informative at all.

Dr. Picard is a gem!! She truly cares about students and made an effort to make online learning as accessible & interesting as possible. There is a lot of readings and Perusall annotations for this class but as long as you keep up with it, it's manageable! The quizzes are not super hard but you need to be very specific and work hard to get an A.

Dr. Picard is an amazing professor with a clear passion for the class's content. She is caring, knowledgeable, and open-minded and really wants to hear student perspectives on topics. This class is not an easy A, and she makes you work hard for it, but she is very supportive and accessible to students. Highly recommend, but get ready to work!
She is very passionate about the subject and gives great lectures. Definitely recommend!

Prof. Pint is an incredible teacher. He puts complex problems into concise and relevant contexts in an understandable setting. Dynamics is a difficult course with a lot of content, but Prof. Pint makes it enjoyable. He goes over homework problems and covers extra examples helping with understanding the material.

Cary Pint is a very good professor. He teaches fairly well and always goes through the very tough homework problems and tries to help the class understand everything. He does make mistakes often, but admits when he's made one. Good prof
Loved Dr. Pint even though dynamics isn't the most interesting material all the time. He makes class fun and consistently reminds you why dynamics is useful in the real world.

Cary Pint is hands down the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. The guy clearly understands the big picture of what school should be about, and what it's like to be a student. He actually wants you to be a successful person, not just get a good grade. Therefore he's very reasonable, and great to get to know outside of class. Take this professor.
Class isn't easy and tests make you think, but an incredible guy to be around.  Inspirational and excited about the content.  Very helpful too.

This class was hard but the book was pretty good and Pint is really helpful in and out of class. He was reasonable and will work with you, I turned in a couple homeworks late after talking to him. He is also very friendly and energetic and cracks (often bad) jokes in lecture

Semester project was mad annoying. Would've taken the other experimental professor instead of this one if I had known that this semester project was this long and annoying. Take the other professor instead if you can just because of the project

Polyn is a really cool guy, and it shows that he cares a lot about his students. His lectures are pretty straightforward, but definitely helpful when it comes to the 3 tests. Good amount of assignments throughout the semester, mix of independent and group. The whole semester you're creating and running your own experiment. No final, just a paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Had him for Computational Neuro. Easily one of the most caring professors I've had. Always willing to spend time with you to work through any of the program assignments. The class itself isn't too bad if you have experience with Python. My only criticism is that his lectures can be a bit long-winded and too theoretical for what's expected in PAs.

I absolutely loved this class. However, caution should be granted because you should only take this class if you are interested in memory models and how math can be used in such models. The information is not difficult at all to comprehend, but I can see how it could be dense. Make sure to write out all details in exams or you will lose points.

Professor Polyn has no concern for students' personal matters. I asked for accommodations multiple times that were never granted. I went above in beyond on exams where in turn he would take off points for arbitrary things that he would not do on other students' exams. Avoid this class if you want a caring professor.

This man rocks. He was very flexible during covid and ended up allowing homework to be submitted for no late penalty at any time during the semester. He gave study guides as well as old exams and tests were open book. The study guides took a while to complete but were valuable and made the exams simpler. Very good teacher.

This class was very boring and hard to sit through. While the class itself is not that much work, the tests are incredibly difficult and his grading criteria is very specific. We also did not get our tests back until 2 days before the next exam. If you are a good test taker without paying attention in class, you should be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seemed monotone at first, but the classof grew on me. V caring, nice, & accessible for qs, Top Hat quizzes at the beginning of each lecture, so must at least skim readings (can feel like a lot sometimes) b4 each class. Lecture material was p interesting, based off the readings; exams are ez IF YOU STUDY- they're all frqs about stuff in class.

Polyn doesn't let you drop a test anymore. I didn't really like the material, so it was a lot of studying for tests. He does give a ton of extra credit, and he grades pretty leniently, so it's not terribly hard to do well on tests. Lecture was kind of boring but he's a nice guy and office hours are super helpful if you don't understand something.

Prof. Polyn is really caring and gives great lectures. He gives extra credits that really helps. Have to do the readings before class because there will be Tophat questions on the readings, so do the readings and go to class if you want an A! Tests are not hard as long as you go over the study guide he gives and look at the slides.

This class was awesome. Very easy to get an A if you go to class. He drops your lowest test score so if you do well on the first 3 tests you don't have to take the final. He makes the class interesting and is so helpful, and is really big in his field so he knows his stuff. The only negative is it was hard to pay attention because he's so hot.

I was lucky to have Dr. Polyn - he is brilliant and funny. The people who said this class is boring were probably failing by their own fault. This isn't a middle school class it's a college course, it's not supposed to be constantly entertaining. Dr. Polyn does a great job.

Professor Polyn is a really funny guy. He has an awkward sense of humor, which my whole class really enjoyed. Though it's models rather than biology, Polyn applies it to daily situations.Frankly, you have to try not to get a good grade. Attend class, do the readings (25min max per week), participate, and you're  golden for an A. Great class overall

Most boring class offered at Vandy hands down. He's a nice guy though. The book is boring. The tests aren't too hard bc he usually gives a study guide before tests which clear up any concepts you might not understand. Homework assgns are very helpful! Clicker ?s have some leanway.

Polyn's a really nice guy but his lectures were very boring. He tended to spend the first half of each class going over what we discussed last class, which made it feel like we moved so slow. Class was a really easy way to fulfill an AXLE MNS requirement. Just study the study guide/practice test before each test (4 but you get to drop 1).
Polyn has a different teaching style where the grades are based on clicker quizes and making multiple choice questions weekly. If you put in the effort, your grade should reflect it.

This class is pretty dumb but it's a requirement for psych majors. There's easy reading once a week and an in class clicker quiz based on the reading. There's also a weekly question that's very easy. Other than that there are no tests and your grades are based on your group project of creating an experiment. Polyn is boring and awkward but bearable

Worst teacher I have ever had.  A worthless class where you learn nothing and grading is beyond arbitrary.  Everything is on a scale of 5 so if you lose 1 pt you are looking at an 80.  The class can be truly defined by who shows up on Monday (attendance is mandatory).  No one goes because everything you need to know is in the book and he is boring.

I enjoyed Professor Powell's class overall as his lectures were mostly clear and engaging. The entire class is graded on four exams so your performance on those determines your grade. Assigned homework problems are optional but completing them will allow you to do well in the class. Dr. Powell was clear in office hours as well. I would recommend.

Decent + accessible outside of class but lectures unengaging and so fast paced. Only uses chalk board +no technology. Downside - Entire grade based on 3 exams + final but did let the final replace lowest exam grade. No attendance, but def need to go to class + do the optional hw to keep up. Good guy though and seems to care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found the lectures to be very disengaging and boring. The class is different from every other section of the class for the worse and has no other grades to support you besides the final and midterms. Most of the content I found myself learning through the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fav prof! He doesn't take attendance and assignments are optional. Attending class is important to understand the material and exam questions come from the textbook. He is very helpful during office hours. Grades are based on three midterms and a final. Multivariable calculus is a challenging course, so expect to study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Lectures on the chalkboard so you need to attend class (but he doesn't track attendance) or get notes from someone. His content doesn't align w the other multi profs but I think his tests are more straightforward and very true to what he teaches. Grade is all based on exams but exams are very true to the content
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Powell is amazing, caring, and a fun guy. The content of the course was difficult, but Dr Powell was very understanding. His lectures are clear and while there was a suggested textbook, it was not necessary.

Great lecturer; writes in great detail on the board. Tests are easy for a 3000 level math class; nothing outside of the scope. There is a textbook for the class but you don't really need to read it; just the notes from class should be sufficient. Homework is closely related to lectures and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Powell is without doubt one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He is an incredibly fair grader and a splendid lecturer. Beware that your whole grade is based on exams, but he will not throw any curveballs at you. Attend class, do the optional homework and you'll do fine.

Professor Powell is a wonderful teacher. He is clear in his teaching, explains problems well, and gives a conceptual and sometimes a proof-based explanation afterwards. Pros: Clear lecturer Examples in class are similar to tests Optional Hmwrk Cons: Grade made up of 3 tests and a final Must attend in class(Doesn't record lectures) Average was B-
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great lectures. Very approachable during his office hours. Homework is not a lot but captures the important parts of the lecture and helps with learning. Amazing experience.

Linear Algebra is not an easy subject but Powell did a really good job of providing a comprehensive overview of the material. Tests are hard simply by the nature of the course and were very proof heavy. However, Powell was incredibly fair in his questions. Definitely take him if you get the chance. Homework is 20% and tests are 80%.

His lectures can get pretty dry and boring really quickly, so you'll probably need to use the book to help you grasp concepts for the first time.  The only grades come from 3 tests and a final. Attendance and homework are optional. Office hours helped a lot, especially when I came with specific questions. Would take his class again.

Dr. Powell is the BEST math teacher I've ever had. He gives geometric bases for the concepts in math 175 (2300 now), which is extremely helpful in 2/3 variables. Great lecturer, incredibly helpful/patient in office hours. Doesn't grade hw, but DO IT, because your grade is only based on 3 exams and the final (learn from my mistakes lol). 10/10!

Good teacher but very difficult class. You only have three tests and a final and so if you get a bad grade on one of the tests your grade is messed up. He's really nice and helpful in office hours but still a hard teacher just because the material is difficult.

One of the best teachers at Vandy, probably the best in the department. Go to class and study the night before and you will be fine for the tests. Really helpful in office hours. Lectures are so clear, the difficult material is much easier to understand with Powell. If you skip class the course will be 10x harder.

Excellent Excellent professors. Multivariable is not an easy subject to learn or teach, but Prof Powell is extremely clear and concise, giving explanations and great examples. The tests are challenging (lots of problems in limited time) but doable. The class does requires you to do the hw problems he assigns (he does not collect/check/grade them).

3 tests and a final. Homework is optional and not for a grade but I highly recommend doing it. No curve for tests. He's very clear and wants you to understand the material. Not as easy as other raters have been saying, however.

Like others have said, lectures are typically clear but the pace is fast. Tests are fair in that he won't throw any true curve balls at you as long as you've attended lecture and done the homework. They are long though, so if you don't know the material like the back of your hand, you won't finish. Somewhat harder than expected.

Haven't loved this class. I know lots that like Powell, but I haven't found a rapport with him. He has lots of office hours but isn't good at finding alternate ways to explain things if you don't understand the first way. Lectures are "clear" but only cover easy examples. You have to memorize a process to do well on tests, which are long.
He's pretty hard, I think the reviews make him seem easy. He's definitely clear but lectures are very fast paced and in depth. Office hours havent helped mostly because they're clogged.

Powell is a great professor, but know that this isn't an easy class. He doesn't take attendance or collect HW, but to do well, you need to go to class and keep up on HW. The final grade is based only on exams, which are long and semi-difficult, and the curve is pretty small. However, he's nice, a clear lecturer and very helpful. I'd recommend him!

If you are a student who is going to be going to office hours all the time and is fine with doing homework on your own that isn't required to turn in, go ahead and take Professor Powell. But for a lot of you soon to be Freshman, you aren't going to want to do those things when they aren't required and if you don't you will get a bad grade.

This class is ok but the teacher will require you to do a lot of the learning on your own. He cares more about proofs for things than actual computation. The tests are much more conceptual than actual math. I took the same class in highschool and got a B+ but am struggling to get a C, even though I already know the material being taught.

Incredibly clear, lectures make any otherwise incomprehensible concept simple and easy. Is incredibly nice and very helpful during office hours. Tests are reasonable with computations, one or two proofs, and a few true/false questions. From what I hear from others, this is by far the best 175 class!

He goes rather fast and can be a tad boring, but he is extremely clear.  Tests are based on in-class examples and homework problems (which are optional).  Very few if any proofs.  He is also ridiculously helpful and thorough in office hours.  If you are in his class, attend office hours, they can make a difference.  My favorite math teacher so far!

Don't get me wrong, he is a good teacher. However, the class is no where as easy as the reviews imply. The average for my class was a 78/79. He explains things well, but tests are hard and very few curves. Don't take it expecting a high grade

Professor Powell is the best teacher ever! His lectures are extremely clear, he lets you know exactly what to expect for each test and quiz and he's very helpful. Even though class was at 8 am, I am SO glad I had him as my calc prof - it was worth it!
Very fair and easy. His tests are predictable, and he is very clear in lectures.
Professor Powell is great for math.  His tests are not hard, all the homework is optional, and he is willing to help all the time.  I agree with all the other ratings about Dr. Powell.
Hes an awesome teacher.  I completely agree with what everyone else has said.  Hes an awesome guy too.  I showed up an hour and a half late to an exam and he let me come up to his office to take it.

He's an amazing, no bs teacher. He teaches you what you need to know and doesn't try to trick you. Very clear and helpful. I only studied my notes and read the textbook and I still rocked his tests and quizzes. Take him if you want an A in 175.

He's very clear and explains everything very well.  Tests and quizzes come straight from the homework (which isn't even that excessive) so it makes it very possible to get an easy A if you just do the hw.  Overall, a great class with a really nice guy and he still gives out a dollar everytime he makes a mistake on the board!

If you're a math major, stay away. I wish would have. Prof. Powell is a really nice guy, but you won't learn anything. Class is a breeze. He tends to give examples straight out of the book instead of real applications and isn't interactive with the class...if you ARE NOT a math major, definitely take him, you'll pass and get credit for the class.

By far the best math professor I've ever had! He makes things easy to understand, and his teaches you everything you need to know for the tests. If you go to class and pay attention, you'll make an A!
Great professor. Makes material easy to understand, and if you still don't, he'll be happy to help you out...no questions asked. I'm taking him next semester for Diff Eq!

This guy is hands down the best math professor I've EVER had.  He's basically the nicest guy in the world, and teaches you in such a way so that you have no trouble keeping up.  His examples and homework problems are almost replicas of his test and quiz problems.  I had a 100% average in the class...pretty amazing.
He's the best. Cares for his students. The tests and quizzes are extremely fair. You can ask him questions during exam. And everytime you correct him in lecture, you'll make a dollar.
He makes this class amazing - his tests are fair, quizzes easy and he's a great guy.

If you're a junior, I'd strongly consider taking Quantum as a senior instead even if it means a heavier fall schedule.

He assigns HW on Friday and makes it due on Monday. Then, he holds office hours on weekdays so there is no way to ask him questions about the homework until after it's due.

In a class of 15 students, there were two A's.
Long shaft daddy

Wish he was teaching 1602 this semester; his lectures are detailed and a good supplement to the textbook, and he handled the asynchronous structure really well with pre-recorded lectures and office hours during normal class time. Super knowledgeable and helpful for questions, his accent wasn't an issue. You have to put in the work, but he's great
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Given that I took this class online asynchronously, it was hard. His accent was never an issue, it was just the material that was tough. I did horribly on the first exam (hence why my overall grade was so bad), but it was because I didn't know how to study quite yet. The lectures are lengthy but they seem to help. He isn't the best professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: gen chem is general is just a hard course, especially this semester when they made tests where you could not go back on questions. However, polavarapu was a very good teacher. his lectures were clear, and his accent was never an issue, unlike what some people say. he also genuinely cares a lot about his students, and it really warmed my heart

Dr. Polavarapu was excellent! He makes in-depth powerpoints, presents the information in understandable ways, and is very helpful in office hours. I really wish I would have taken him first semester too! People on here say his accent is confusing, but I had no issue understanding him at all. Great choice for gen chem

His accent is so thick that it takes active effort to understand what he is saying. The class is not that hard, but his teaching is so mediocre that you'll be better off just reading the book instead of going to class. Nice guy, but horrible teacher.

Gen chem's always super hard regardless of the professor. His slides are very detailed, and he does an excellent job of explaining the material at hand. He often rushes through example calculations in class, so be sure to review the slides again after class. Very generous with TopHat extra credit relative to the other professors.

PChem is tough, esp. with Prasad. Go to class or miss context in the slides otherwise. Math heavy for sure, but if you understand and apply basic concepts (normalization, finding average, etc.) you will be OK. Lookout for special problems from the lectures. Nice curve, and a nicer guy. Easy to talk to after class and got our $45 WebAssign refunded.

He's a nice guy that genuinely seems to care about how you do in the class, but his teaching and grading style were terrible. He flew threw powerpoints too fast to keep up with notes, and because he rarely took questions or did examples, lecture was useless. He also takes a ton of credit off if you don't have exactly what he has in his solution.

I was warned of Dr. Polavarapu prior to taking this class and I must say this was unfounded.  Make no mistake, the class is hard.  The material sucks and you will struggle, but he knows his stuff.  He held office hours everyday and was very clear in class if you pay attention.  He cares a lot about your success if you show him that you care.

I've heard some negative comments about Dr. Polavarapu prior to taking his class, but I must say that all the comments were unfounded. Dr. He wants his students to understand the material & has office hours EVERYDAY for that.  Pay attention class, ask questions if you don't understand. His lectures are dry, but he explains well if you pay attention

This dude flies through extremely dense material and even though its a science class the tests involve mostly derivations and calculations. So much so that the students taking it joke that its really an undercover calculus class.

Seems like a decent professor, but PChem with him is miserable. He essentially just reads from his power-points which are posted online, no quizzes or homework, so attendance is not necessary. The content of the course is just terrible. You will leave with a vague and useless understanding of quantum mechanics. Too bad, b\c quantum is so important.

Dr. Polavarapu is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt so far. He doesn't just throw information at you, expecting you to know how to apply it immediately. He walks you through the material and shows you why things are the way they are.

Such a sweet and helpful prof-definitely your best bet for gen chem. his accent is hard to understand but hes great at explaining hard concepts. His slides are very helpful and detailed. The slides alone will help you enough for the tests but he explains everything very well in class. also VERY helpful and sweet if you go to office hours

Very underrated professor for gen chem. He is overly helpful and kind to work with for those who reach out to him. His lecture slides are not very clean and artistic but packed with info and practice problems. He is difficult to understand at first but this quickly goes away though I did sit towards the front. Overall very kind and helpful.

Not a difficult class if you make use of office hours. Most people didn't and often complained about the difficulty of this class. The material can be learned from the book entirely though. He is willing to change test dates around to accommodate the needs of the students. He wants to see students do well.

P Chem is hard as nuts. Prasad just puts up his powerpoints and goes verbatim through them in class, however he is accommodating as far as moving tests and wanting the students to do well. Class isn't very helpful since it is so boring.

really helpful outside of class, but his accent can be hard to get used to at first. extremely detailed slides, can be a good thing or a bad thing. he also gives hints to hard mastering chem problems, which is nice. OVERALL A GOOD CHOICE

Difficult to understand.  Not a fair grader.  Does not test concepts, but, rather, ability to not make stupid mistakes.  Late night tests (for all chem classes) don't help.  He's a bit defensive if you ask him why something is graded a certain way.

Overall, good professor- cares about student success. Pretty poorly attended lectures, probably because it's 8 am chemistry, and all of his notes are online. Sometimes spends too much time on simple concepts while forgoing more challenging applications. Lecture based more on problem solving than conceptual understanding. Helpful emails.

Polavarapu is very fair and puts a fair amount of effort into the class. PCHEM, however, remains a miserable class for most participants due to the sheer difficulty. Seems to be easier for ChemEs than for Chem majors- the derivations aren't kind to us Scientists.

i think he's very overrated. a lot of ppl said that he's the best professor for general chemistry. however, i think his accent is a big problem. moreover, his slides are nice and include a lot of useful information, BUT it's very unorganized. he does not emphasize enough on important points, which makes it really hard for test preparation.
Going to this class is pointless. The notes are posted online. Prasad is a nice guy with a funny accent if you attend lectures. The departamentalized tests suck and they make this class hard.

If you really want to succeed in the class, you must read the book! The lectures are pretty much pointless; however, the lecture notes posted on OAK are excellent. The tests are departamentalized, so there is no point debating profs. The accent is a wee annoying and hard to understand, and may be repetitive.

Well, like it's been said earlier, most of the work is done out of the book so that's really the only chem teacher. But I would recommend Polavarapu over most others because a)very helpful outside of class, b)even though he has an accent he's still understandable enough to make sense, and c)he posts all of his lecture notes online
O.K. teacher but can be very boring. Learning chem is more done out of the book than in class. His powerpoints are helpful though and he always puts them online. Not a bad choice but not the best.

Polavarapu is a great teacher, but the chem class in general is very tough. Polavarapu's powerpoints are awesome and he actually teaches 100% of the time instead of rambling off on random things about his life. Take him! If you miss class, you always have his powerpoints!

Polavarapu is an excellent professor. He is kind and always readily available to help if anyone has any questions about the material. Also, the lecture notes really help because one is able to listen to him and focus in on learning instead of attempting to merely write down all of the material without having time to absorb it. I RECOMMEND HIM!

DEFINITELY, HE IS THE BEST. If I were to take this course over and over again, I would take it with him. He is so so helpful. He answers my emails sooner than I would think. Usually, he does not take more than six hours to answer a long email. TAKE HIM. He's the best.
Prasad is awesome. His powerpoints are ballin': they help out tremendously.  The tests are pretty much straight from the book. Be prepared to work, but chem 102 is very manageable.
Better than the other chemistry professors, but still a tough class. You won't have any fun with this course, but it isn't Prasad's fault.
Best general chemistry professor!  Powerpoints are extremely helpful and he works very hard to make sure students understand the material!

He is one of the better chem professors. Way better than Wright. Also, His lecture notes are amazing and are extremely helpful. He really cares about your grade and your understanding of the class. I would most definitely recommend him for anyone taking Chem 102.

Great teacher!!! our class always had the highest averages and he is always willing to help if you go into his office hours!! its a tough course but he is a great teacher!! his clicker quizes count for extra credit which is nice and if you do the work you'll be fine!

DONT HAVE TO COME TO CLASS BECAUSE HIS NOTES ARE FROM THE POWERPOINTS AND THEY ARE ONLINE. BUT THE IN CLASS CLICKER QUIZZES ARE HELPFUL. THE QUESTIONS ON THE TEST ARE SOMETIMES FROM THE CLICKER QUIZZES. HE'S WILLING TO HELP IF U ARE STRUGGLING. OFFICE HOURS ARE GREAT. PREPARES STUDENTS FOR EXAM PRETTY WELL. THE ONLY DOWN SIDE IS HIS WIERD ACCENT!

He puts all the lectures online, and follows them completely in class, so you really don't have to go except for clicker quizzes, which do actually help your grade. A great professor for those who don't want to attend class or don't want to pay complete attention

Such a nice guy and more than willing to do anything to help you out. his power point notes are really helpful. he is good at preparing you for the tests and pay attention to clicker quiz questions bc those were usually on tests.

Great professor, one of the best that i've had.  Smart and willing to help students all the time, he holds very good office hours. extremely intelligent and helpful, cares a lot about his students.  powerpoint slides are most helpful, they give all the info. that he lectures in class. he explains the material thoroughly, highly recommended.

Great professor. I am not even a premed or engineering student. I decided to take chemistry because of my interest in it during high school. At first i dreaded the class's difficulty, but his lectures are very engaging and he presents the material very well.
Great Professor! I was dreading gen-chem, but seriously guys, I got a 95%... he made everything clear, and once in a while would even be, ALMOST funny.

Great professor who is very helpful and dedicated. Coming to class isn't necessary because he posts his notes online. Tests are pretty difficult, but Dr. Polvarapu does a good job in preparing his students for them.

Contrary to popular belief, his accent really isn't that bad and he's easy to understand. If you're expecting the be excited about the subject you're crazy. Difficult pre-med weed-out class, but Dr. Polavarapu is the professor most devoted to helping you. Do suggested problems. Puts all his slides online and gives review sessions. HIGHLY recommende
his lectures are his powerpoint slides. very straightforward. do the practice problems because they will be on the exams.

He's a very nice professor. He's somewhat easy to talk to; however, I feel that he doesn't prepare us well for the exams. The exams are too difficult and the material isn't covered in class. His powerpoints are great, but he should be more interactive with the class and step away from his slides.

This class is ridiculous. The tests all have bad averages, yet nothing is done to correct that on the part of the department! Dr. Polavarapu is mildly interesting, and once he gets away from his powerpoint slides, starts barrelling through the lecture. Not a horrible teacher, but he's not the best, either.
he's extremely boring, he just reads off his slides and spends ages on stupid calculations thats we dont need to cover in class (concepts are more helpful)   there are better 102 teachers out there
reads verbatim off his powerpoint slides, and his accent is difficult to understand. tests are hard regardless of which teacher you get.
i loved his power point slides..helped so much on the tests last semester
You can't understand him and he seems like he could care less if you get the info or not.  He's just there to read the powerpoints.  There is no point in going to his class.

he can seem sort of monotone and honestly it was hard for me to pay attention but if you are prepared you can follow along; he is willing to help; but i did most of my learning with the book but he gives great slides online
well, I mean he just reads off powerpoints.  you either like it or you don't.  chem 102 is self-taught, and tests are departmental so professors don't matter too much.

Teacher knows his stuff! His powerpoint slides are amazing and help more that you'll ever think. He holds office hours everyday; use them. Don't be afraid to approach him. General Chem is not an easy class, but he makes you understand the material.

Extremely brilliant and very good teacher! Very enthusiastic. Tests are hard but if you work hard, he will work with you. Very understanding guy and don't let the accent fool you. He knows his stuff!! :)
No Comments

He is very nice and the lectures are problem focused, which is good. Going to class isn't vital because the power points are provided online. General Chemistry isn't so difficult anyways. Doesn't matter who you take.
No Comments

Didn't enjoy the fact that all he did was read verbatim off of power point. Never felt as prepared as other sections. Never went to class because there was no point. LOVE phillips this semester, though.
Uses PowerPoint to present lectures and posts note on Prometheus.  The class is difficult as ****, though.  Be sure you know what you are getting yourself into before you are taking the class.
Puts all his notes on Power Point so coming to class is optional. Explained things very clearly and succintly. Earned an easy A
I got a B+ in the class i think my lab TA screwed it over. He is a really good teacher. His studdy sessions help a hell of a lot.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
sick guy, awesome stories, easy tests. Only uses about half the total class time, though I've heard that's changed since I took him. Either way, great guy and class.

A must-take if you are at all interested in the music industry. Tests are easier than other comments make them out to be, just require some memorization. Lectures can be dry but are usually only an hour. Worth the effort of memorization for the shot classes and no homework + Porter's knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the rudest professors at the University. The lectures were not very representative of the exams. This class is not easy and only gets harder each year.

Porter's class is an honest nightmare. Grading is annoying, exams are tedious memorization of random facts (mostly provisions of industry contracts), and the TA is clueless. Testbank was helpful in past but he doesn't seem to recycle exams anymore. Also, lectures are super boring, but class never actually goes until 9pm (some til 8, some til 7).

Porter is really knowledgeable about the music industry, which makes his stories interesting. The class only meets for like an hour each week, which is pretty cool, but most of the lecture is just copying his notes. The tests aren't hard, but they require a lot of memorization of random facts and he changes them each semester. Still a solid prof.

Everyone said this class was easy. It wasn't, in fact it was a living nightmare. Prof. Porter is the worst lecturer I've ever had, the material on exams was arbitrary, and the exams were overly weighted. Grading is messed up, so is this class. Avoid at all costs.

Pretty easy class overall. His tests are similar versions of themselves so you can find them online and pretty much coast thru class. He's not the best lecturer, very old and boring but its an easy class if you're looking for 3 free credits and an A.
The coolest guy. His lecture style is kinda boring but the class is light and content interesting. Super light and lecture is maybe an hour.

I genuinely don't know how Vanderbilt hasn't fired him. He's an AWFUL lecturer and has designed the class poorly. The class isn't particularly hard, but it's gotten tougher than in years past. People used to have a test bank but he's caught on to that and is changing up his exams. One good thing is you get out early.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor, and is so knowledgable about the music industry. Also, his class is probably the easiest class I've taken in all my schooling years, including high school, which is crazy! Attendance - 10%, 1 Quiz - 20%, 1 Midterm - 30%, 1 Final - 40%. His tests are just rinse and repeats of previous tests so just memorize those and go.

Please do NOT take him. I had heard great things about how easy he was (bc he reused the same exams), but he changed the course this year. Graded only by attendance & 3 exams- all memorization of random facts that don't connect together. It's hard to memorize like 20 pages of lists of 5s for the final. Marks you off in full for minor details too.

Anybody who's complaining about this class has a maximum IQ of 80. By far the easiest and most fun class I've taken here. Graded on literally 3 exams, but they're super easy if you go to class and listen passively - no notes needed. Tons of quizlets out there for this class that have the questions, too.

GOAT

If you want a class for easy credit take this, its basically 1 hr a week for 3 credits. If you dont have a test bank you will not pass this class and if you do have one you will need to spend lots of time memorizing the questions before the test. He does give +/- grades so if you get an 89 its a straight B im still salty
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, especially if you know the test questions. Went in excited to learn about the music industry, but the content was dated and irrelevant, so didn't learn much.

This class sucked honestly. The lectures were extremely boring and disorganized and Porter was very difficult to listen to. If you don't have the past tests they are very hard to do well on as it requires memorization of a lot of random facts. Good part about this class was that we met for only about an hour each week for a full 3 credit class.
Professor Porter was great. Interesting lectures and very fair all the way around. You will get an A if you go to class and put in the time. Highly recommended!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Manages to turn an interesting topic into something incredibly boring with lectures that drone on and don't really have a purpose. Low-stress class and not hard to do well, but felt pretty disorganized overall, especially considering our midterm kept being pushed back for like five weeks for no apparent reason.
you're on your own for this class - easy if you memorize. but that's all. super boring lectures. attendance not mandatory

Porter's not amazing but he's not horrible either. The test questions can be a bit random (it could ask you small details he very briefly mentioned in lectures), so it really benefits the Greek life folks with plenty of past exams.. Other than that, the course itself teaches you a lot (if you're interested).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty much as easy as a class at Vandy gets. Porter is such a G, rounds up final grades. The only thing is that the tests are basically based on anything given in list format in any of the lectures, and if you don't have a test from a previous year to study from, the questions can seem kind of random/ you just have to comb through the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class consists of once a week 2 hour lectures, only 3 tests (including the final), and is an easy A. If you really care about the material you will enjoy this class. If not, then it could be a boring class that you cram for the night before the tests. Porter is an easy grader and if you try you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is easy but only because of all of the test banks. If you don't care about the material and don't listen/attend, you are definitely going to have to try and cram for the tests. Not an engaging lecturer and the class is boring - but you will get an A if you try. Grade only based off of 3 things though

The class is pretty easy (and has become even easier), so this isn't a huge issue, but there is hardly any structure. Assignments are getting canceled left and right, and we may only have a quiz, midterm, and final making up our grades. Take Porter if you want an easy class and do not care about ambiguity or if things get switched up regularly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A very simple class with a teacher who is passionate about the material. Lots of test and quiz questions are reused, so try to use your resources. Relatively interesting material but 3 hours is just very long and it gets boring, even though class gets out early most days. I
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy A; grade is based on two easy tests, easy quiz, paper graded on completion, and attendance; wants students to succeed, accessible by e-mail, interesting topic, lets you get out an hour early every week, re-uses questions from test to test, re-uses same tests from year to year so look for test bank help
You know what this is! So low stress and I honestly learned a lot.
Take it if you need an A. All tests can be found in a test bank. I went half the time and got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: You only need to ask yourself one question: Do you want an A? If yes, take this class. Just know that lectures are boring af and are at night (6-9)
You probably know what you are getting into here. Professor is a nice guy. As easy as it gets at Vanderbilt. Definitely boring though, try to take with friends...
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great sense of humor. Loves the Dodgers. Highly recommend taking this class!!!!!

Super knowledgable guy  when it comes to the industry, but incredibly long, boring class.  Mainly used it to do other work.  Take a few notes, pay attention to his test reviews and it's an easy A.  Only grades are a quiz, midterm, short guest speaker write-up, and final.  Spent almost no time on this class all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 89.5 and above is an A. He actually says on the first day of class that you are an idiot if you don't get an A. Show up once a week and spend two hours on your computer. Once in a while you might learn something interesting.

Overall, the class is entertaining, but the three hour time-slot makes it feel very long. He always lets class go 30-45 minutes early which is nice. He clearly knows the industry very well, and has very interesting anecdotes. Theres is one quiz, a midterm, and  final, each of which do not change much from year to year. Good blow-off class

He definitely knows the material and has tons of stories from years of experience. The lecture itself can drag sometimes because it's so long, but he tries to keep you engaged. Quizzestests barely change, and he goes over them in class essentially.  Interesting material, easy A.

Prof. Porter is a really cool guy. He knows a ton about the business of music. I'm sure I'd have a great time with him outside of class. But 2.5 hours of straight lecture makes this the most boring class ever. Avoid it if you can.

Really boring lectures that honestly don't help at all. The weekly problem set you have to do with a randomly assigned group is annoying and she does break some things down in class, but self-study is where you'll learn the most. Wish she would be more efficient with lecture time but it was so so dry.

These reviews are all slander. Professor Pool is extremely nice and makes Finance extremely digestible. This class is extremely easy if you show up and do the work. Any bad reviews are from people who clearly never showed up. Take this class with Pool for an easy A.

Most boring class I have ever taken in my life. She made me want to fall asleep. Nonetheless, she gave us 10 extra credit points for the final and was heavily available outside of class. The class does teach you the basics of financial concepts needed for IB interviews, but you could honestly just avoid this class and teach it yourself.

People are too tough on her. She clearly gives you everything you need to succeed. If you don't do the group projects, extra credit, or come to lecture, of course you will struggle. Compared to the other BUS professors she dedicates WAY more time to OH and takes feedback seriously. The people with the low ratings don't take the time to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful lectures. Her slides don't make sense, and neither does her teaching style. It's all self-taught: you either survive or you don't and that's how it goes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Pool is a kind woman who is very willing to help in OH. However, the class is very difficult, lecture slides can be unclear and you will have to dedicate a lot of time to independent studying. Tests can be confusing and group problem sets are even harder.
She's alright but the material is kind of frustrating at times
If you want to go to class and not learning anything, and then ruin your exam, this is the class to take.
Can't understand anything in class. simply can't concentrate in her dry teaching style. Had to teach myself instead
awful! just awful! so awful that the classroom is always at 1/2 of its capacity
A very bad professor who doesn't seem to understand the material very well.

Professor Pool is super dry and could not make the topic less interesting. Class wasn't mandatory, and you can do well on the tests by doing practice tests and looking at slides. The problem sets were done in a group which was a huge headache and were way harder than tests. Even though you can put 0 effort in and get a good grade, it's not worth it

Professor Pool is a nice woman, but her lectures are super dry. Didn't show up to class half the time and just studied the slides on my own, and the class was bearable that way. Homework heavy, but it's done in groups. Study the homework and practice exams and you'll probably be prepped for the midterm and final.

The best professor to take the finance module with. She breaks down finance into the need-to-know instead of overcomplicating things. Sometimes can be difficult to follow in class, but I got an A by doing all of the homework problems and studying the slides. the midterm and final are ridiculously easy if you do the practice tests, hw's and slides

Stupid class. Made me not want to continue with the Business minor. Lectures are useless and so is the text book. Don't buy it. If you want to take the class, just study the practice problems and the formula sheets the day before the exams. Group practice problems (45%), 2 tests (55%). Curved to a high A-. Waste of time.

She was very disorganized. Conceptually, finance isn't that difficult, but I would often find myself lost in lectures only to understand the concept on my own later and think, "this isn't hard, but she taught it in a way that complicated it for no reason." She gives practice tests like the real thing. Group HWs are hard but fine with a good group.

Great professor. She cares about her students and tries her best to make our lives easier. Lectures and homework are taken from the textbook. Easy quizzes. Tests are also not very difficult compared to the homework. Definitely take her if you have the chance.

Pohland was a great professor. She is super nice and VERY accessible outside of class. Pohland cares a lot about how well you understand things conceptually so make sure before quizzes and homeworks you are very familiar / comfortable with the material. Overall she is great but definitely use the textbook and utilize office hours!!!

Honestly a great option for 2300. Lectures were pretty much straight from the text book but go to class for weekly quizzes on the homework. If you put in the work you will do well and she really cares about her students.

Made tests pointlessly hard. Didn't help in conceptual understanding in any way, just copied notes onto board. Zero communication between her and the TA, so the TA became useless as he didn't know any of the grading criteria. Wasnt present for office hours. Made me think I was trash at math until I took upper-division courses and did decent. Avoid

Do not this class with professor pigg unless you have a solid background in calc. She speeds through the lectures, is unnecessarily strict about her guidelines and is not very understanding of others situations. Additionally, she is highly uncommunicative and can be difficult to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 12 quizzes (you drop two), four tests, and a final. Pigg is a solid choice, IF you understand calculus prior to Vandy. She definitely expects a decent background in algebra so if you're going to need a lot of support in that regard I would advise against that. Generous with partial credit and isn't an actual professor so pretty laid back overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is SO BORING. Each class she just stands at the board, works through her packet, while we stay completely silent and many people are confused. She's not very caring about her students and is very unapproachable. She does drop our lowest quiz grade and gives a bit of extra credit opportunity at the end of the year which is nice though.

Professor Pigg definitely brightens up 1200 with her sass/humor. Pay attention in class, keep up with homework (it's never turned in, but it's good practice), & review for quizzes & tests, & you'll do just fine. Drops your lowest 2 quizzes, averages your final with your lowest test, & gives extra credit for each week you go to your discussion.

Prof Pigg made calculus both enjoyable and unnecessarily stressful at the same time. If you follow what she's saying you're in a great place, but if you stop to ask her a question, she will get annoyed and has trouble explaining things in a different way. Tests and quizzes are difficult, do not expect much partial credit or explanation of points.

Pigg's class covers a lot of material very quickly and therefore moves very quickly in class. She's somewhat brisk, but she really wants you to succeed. She distributes a list of topics and practice problems before each exam, then works through it in class. She's also very funny with her southern colloquialisms. You'll have to work, but she's fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SHE WASN'T VERY UNDERSTANDING OF PERSONAL CIRCUMSTANCES AFFECTING MY GRADES OR THE FACT THAT HER CLASS WAS ONLY MANAGEABLE IF YOU'VE PREVIOUSLY TAKEN A CALCULUS CLASS BEFORE.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pigg is extremely organized and detailed. She does move quickly in class so be prepared and don't be afraid to stop and ask her questions! 1200 is a weedout class so you will have to work through every single problem on the homework to really be prepared for the exams. The final is especially tough!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Like many others this semester I was retaking calculus. Prof Pigg was great. She knows how to break difficult concepts down so they are easier to understand. Go to class, do the homework and go to office hours for help. My grade is so much better this time.

Great professor. Great handouts. Very helpful and kind during office hours. I was retaking calculus this semester and found the experience very good. You have to study. Im no math brain but made it through. Do the homework and go to office hours to get help.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pamela Pigg ignored most student requests for simple things like "could you give a 5 min warning for the end of quizzes". She sped through class lessons and did not care to slow down and explain clearly. She also was very harsh with grades and took off for anything, in office hours, she would always try to rush through all students and questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Save yourself the trouble. DON'T TAKE PIGG, I failed so you don't have to.

4 tests and a final. Weedout class. You have to go to class, do all the homework, and study in order to do well, but it's possible. This class requires commitment to do well. Great teacher and lots of help resources. If you do pass/fail, you have to put in effort to pass. Would recommend 1100 for peabody or no background in math.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I found Prof Pigg to be very organized and knowledgeable . Math at Vandy is a weed out course. I was taking for the second time. Piggs class is so much better than the last time. I always go to office hours for help. Its a lot of work but she is very helpful. Her handouts are very helpful. She seems to enjoy teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Pigg is one of the worst professors at Vanderbilt. Be ready to learn how to do the math exactly how she does it. Use X instead of Y but get the same answer? You get a 0. She takes her lack of understanding out on you. Genuinely enjoying failing kids and with a pass rate of roughly 50%, this class is not for you. Take ANY other 1200 Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is the worst professor I have ever had. If you have not taken calc before, DON'T take this class. She is unhelpful, rude, and does not care about her students in any way. Her teaching style is simply doing problems on the board very quickly with little explanation.

I was retaking calculus this semester. Prof. Pigg was amazing. Her lectures were so easy to follow and she was able to break things down so that I could understand. I definitely recommend her if you want to understand. My grade is so much better this time. Her tests and quizzes are very thorough but do-able.

The class was difficult but I did not have calculus in high school. Class was very organized and I had to get extra help during office hours. She was very helpful and answered all my questions. Some were taking the class pass/fail and were ticked that they had to do something. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is pretty stubborn and when asked for clarification or to slow down, she does not receive feedback well. However, she does really want people to succeed. Quizzes and tests are pretty hard to do well in, a lot of people took it pass fail which was manageable. Learn her handouts well and you should be fine although her tests are always harder

Her class is difficult, but calculus is a weed-out class so it's really what you'd expect. She's nice, and you can do decently if you've been exposed to Calculus before and do ALL the homework. However, if you didn't have rigorous exposure to calculus in high school, I would consider taking an easy math first to get used to math at Vandy.

I came into this class having taken AP Calc in high school thinking it was going to be easy, but it was incredibly difficult. Definitely my biggest time commitment, and I personally wasn't a fan of her teaching style. The tests and a lot of the quizzes are incredibly hard and you will have to grind for a good grade. Extra credit helps though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Pigg is absolutely the greatest. I really liked her handouts and she was very helpful during office hours. Lots of quizzes and tests but you get to drop a couple of quizzes. Do the homework go to class and you should do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, the class is tough. I took calc in HS and still felt like I was learning entirely new things because they were so much more difficult and in depth than before. But she really does want the class to succeed, despite the difficulty. She allots class time for questions and is always willing to go over quiz/exam questions. Lots of EC too.

Second time I took this class; even though I already knew the material and studied more and even felt like I performed better on the tests, she has absolutely insane grading policies. Instructs TA's to cut points for handwriting/less work/shoddiness, even though there is no space to actually write the answers down.
Prof. Pigg gives great handouts. Shes always available during Ofc hours but theyre in the early morning. Go to class and study the handouts and youll be ok. Im not a math person but did ok.
Thought calc was easy in high and figured MATH 1100 wouldn't be too hard? Yea, me too. Prof Pigg teaches very fast and is pretty negative when it comes to answering questions. Sweet lady though :)

The worst professor I had at Vanderbilt. Period. I took MATH 1100 as someone who has already taken math courses level above it just to fulfill a requirement and I despised the class. Terrible grading methods and she doesn't understand how to teach. She gets mad at students who question her speed or don't understand. She caused everyone to hate math

Sweet lady, likes to help, but is pretty stubborn when it comes to grading/her TAs usually grade really tough. She's pretty funny and openly embraces her southerness which is nice, but she is just a really hard teacher to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Pigg is not the best option for Calc 1201. She gives incredibly difficult quizzes which should be buffers to your tests, but instead they are extremely hard. She doesn't teach effectively and just simply solves problems on the board without teaching how to do them. I had to teach myself through the textbook for each quiz and test.

Clear when teaching concepts, but goes super fast on the board. Takes the time to further explain if asked to make sure you get it. Has a sense of humor. Quizzes and tests cover exactly what was taught in class, but are made harder because of time constraint.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great at conveying material but be sure to pay attention as she moves fast. Quizzes and tests are very difficult but that may just be the entire math department.

Pigg is the best option for 1200. Her quizzes are hard. Youll have one weekly (worth 15 pts each) pretty much. But exams will be easier because youre way better prepared. I actually learned a lot and am good at calc now. She gives a lot of opportunities to raise your grade at the end of the semester. Take her if you can.
Races through problems in lecture, not super eager to get to know students on a personal basis. The most high school-like class you'll take in college.

This class is the most format heavy math class I have ever taken. You literally get points taken off you get the right answer, but don't get there the way she wants. Blames everything on the Math Department. Seems happy-go-lucky but couldn't care less about you outside the class. Honestly would have been better to take 1300 than 1200 with Pigg.

Prof Pigg is very caring and an excellent teacher.  Her handouts are very helpful. Do your homework and study the handouts.  Very helpful during office hours.  Don't try to con her, she will call you out.  She's tough but if you work she will help you.

The class is ridiculous and is based so much on format rather than mathematics. The professor has office hits at such short time brackets and refused to answer questions when I asked her. She would say that we didn't go over it in class so it wouldn't be on the test and yelled. She had two sides to her which was really annoying and she didn't care.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Absolutely wonderful prof who is invested in her students' success. Works hard to ensure that you understand the material and feel prepared for exams.

RIP GPA. She is super fake about being bubbly. Very snappish when you ask her questions and the tests are more about formatting than math. Very frustrating. She is not a nice person and despite what she says about wanting to help you, nothing about this class really helps you learn. If you're doing good, it'll stay that way if not, she won't help
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She teaches a difficult subject. Sometimes points will be taken off for little things. Overall though, she cares a lot about her students and teaches very clearly.

Really nice and sweet lady who cares a lot about her students. Despite this, extremely hard class. 12 quizzes but get to drop 2. Usually hard and really necessary to do well on tests, but the tests are extremely difficult as well. If you aren't a math person this isn't the course for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Pigg is an amazing lecturer. Tests are hard but everything on the tests are similar to the problems that she taught us how to solve in class. Go to every lecture and study her handouts before tests and you'll be fine. Calculus is a subject that requires a lot of hard work. A is hard to get but not impossible.

The weekly quizzes are deliberately challenging (as are the tests tbh) but are doable if you complete the homework and packet she gives you beforehand. She is helpful in office hours (come with a question in mind) and gives a good extra credit boost at the end. Despite not being particularly good at math,  I managed to pull a B+ in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is really helpful during office hours, but you must come in with specific questions. She will not reteach material during office hours. It is easy to boost your grade with dropped quizzes and bonus points for attending weekly discussion classes. Tests are very difficult if you do not fully understand material and know how to combine all topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Pigg is an amazing teacher and helps students learn the material very well. However, this is a hard class and was by far my most time consuming class. This is not the class for you if you just want an easy A

I took AP Calc AB in HS so I figured this class would be a breeze - WRONG! Prof. Pigg gives you all the material you need to succeed (review packets & office hours) but this class requires a lot of effort. You have to carry out each problem in exactly the right way so partial credit can be more of a curse than a blessing. Extra credit opportunities
