Professor Pigg's class is not extremely easy. She offers so much extra credit including three extra credit quizzes and she averages your lowest test grade with your final if you want her to. She also lets you drop two quiz grades. For sure take her for an easy A or B.
She goes really fast and won't own up to her mistakes. Also, you get a lot of points off if you do your work differently than her, even by a margin and even if you get the correct answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. She really cares about her students and their success. She is willing to help outside of class , especially when preparing for tests. Her handouts are very helpful. Do the homework and go to office hours if you need help.

Hardest class I ever took. Pop quizzes, which are normally grade boosters, were really hard. Tests were near impossible. Partial credit is more of a curse than a blessing because points are taken off left and right. This is more a reflection of the difficulty of the course than Professor Pigg. She's very nice, but the class is just too tough.

Pigg is an amazing professor. She clearly wants her students to succeed, but Calc is a course that requires a lot of personal effort. Quizzes and tests are very detail oriented. Making little mistakes adds up and can be frustrating. Do the homework, it really helps. Go to office hours.

This is my second time taking Pigg, and I'd say the second semester is definitely easier than the first semester. Still a lot of room to bump up your grade through recitation and test corrections. Her handouts are a godsend and she's always there to help you. Overall, not impossible, but not easy by any means.

Class is fast paced but Pigg stops often for questions. She tries to make class entertaining.  She's a tough grader   If you study handouts and do homework you should do ok.  Go to office hours, she's a great help there.  She's hard but she's fair.  I would take her again, if I had to take another math class. Don't skip class.

She's a good teacher. Classes are very fast paced. She  gets annoyed when you ask questions in class. Office hours are very helpful. Do EVERY homework problem and use the supplement before the tests. They are very harshly graded. If you can skip using credit from high school, please do.I took Calc 1200 and am currently doing poorly in the class.

Avoid Calc 1200 if you already have credit for the class. I did well in AP and expected this class to be easy. I was wrong. This is the hardest class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Only B. Although the actual content was easier than math and physics courses I took in high school, the grading is so meticulous that it makes it very difficult to succeed.

Prof Pigg's class is tough but fair. She doesn't take up homework but it's a good idea to do it anyways. She wants all her students to understand what's going on. She goes a little fast sometimes but she asks for questions. Go to office hours if you need help.

This class is hard no matter who you take it with. You may know the concepts but you'll mess up if you don't pay attention to detail. There's a lot of wiggle room for your grade though. She drops 2/12 quizzes and averages your final with your lowest test grade. Test averages are in the 70's. If you have to to take this class, take it with Pigg!!
she's so funny and i love her southern accents! her extra credit assignment was not hard at all, just correction on exam papers and oh, no homework too! i love her she's so cute hahaaha

She is kind and very helpful. Study her class notes and you won't even need the text book. If you are thorough with the questions she does in class, you can easily make a good grade. Our section had the highest averages even though the tests are standardized. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. Take her if you want a good grade in calculus.

Really cares about her students and is very helpful. Classes are very problem driven so you get practices and she keeps class entertaining. Tests are difficult but doable if you do all the homework she assigns.

Love this professor. She is funny, caring, and a great teacher.  Really cares about her students and their success. She is willing to help outside of class , especially when preparing for tests. Would definitely take her again.

Took this class, advertised as precalculus math, because I wanted a good background for a real calc class. It was geared towards the international engineering students, who made up 95% of the class and were taking upper level calculus. Prof taught this class like everyone should have already known the material and didn't even follow the book.

Really difficult class, and I took BC in HS (and got a 4!). Quizzes are either really easy or really hard, and most of your grade is made up by the 5 tests (which are also hit or miss). Be prepared to fail at first. She is marginally helpful during office hours, but prepare to do a lot of learning on your own. Not an easy A by any measure!
Way too hard
Her lectures, while quick, are clear and problem-focused. She definitely cares
This was my second time to take this class.  Wish she had taught it the first time.  Explains things so well.  Makes class enjoyable.  Great prof.
She helpful, funny, nice and caring- enough said.

Take this prof for 150/155. Period. Don't chance it with anyone else. She is a charming southern woman with a simply hilarious sense of humor and an even greater prowess concerning mathematics. Super, Super helpful. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, she WILL help you. The class is hard not because of Prof. Pigg, but because of departmental restrictions...

I absolutely loved Professor Pigg as a teacher. She is an unbelievable professor who truly cares about her students and their success. She will work to explain key concepts to you until you understand, and she is always willing to meet outside of class as well. She made me actually enjoy calculus class.

Best teacher for Math 150 by far, our class scored better than all of the others. You do need to attend class, and it's helpful if you keep up, but otherwise it's all quizzes and tests. She wants you to do well.

Even though you may not want to, do the homework. Reinforcement is necessary since the lectures are often fast paced and difficult to follow (beware if you haven't taken calculus in high school). That being said Professor Pigg is probably the best possible choice. She's really nice, but the tests are, of course, really tough.
She is such a nice professor. She helped a lot if you don't understand. Spend time to go to her Office Hour and she'll surely helped you.

Love her! She is very helpful. The quizzes are hard, so be sure to study for them. However, they really help you prepare for the tests. Go to office hours for help. Study and do the homeowrk and you should do fine.

Probably the best math teacher I have ever had.  Very fair and helpful.  Tests are long and thorough. Gives great handouts and explains calculus where you can understand it.  I owuld definitely recommend her.

Pigg is great! Calculus 150B at Vandy is the worst, but she does the best she can with the ridiculous department rules. She gives great handouts but this class isn't one you can skip a lot. She wants students to do well and is very clear with material in class. Definitely go to office hours, she is intimidating 1:1 at first, but will warm up to you

Pigg is a great teacher and teaches the material clearly. However, the homework isn't necessarily helpful for tests, and even if you feel like you know the material, the tests usually include some ridiculously hard problems. Also, don't try to negotiate scores with Pigg, she can be pretty sassy and ruthless.

She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her lectures are clear and she gives out concise handouts for each (very helpful!). Draconian department standards get in the way of everything though. People who previously enjoyed math begin to dislike it because of ridiculous time restraints placed on tests.
great teacher, handouts are very helpful. very helpful during office hours. if you have to take the standardized calculus try to get her.
good teacher, handouts are helpful (must go to class!!).  tests are hard- not nearly enough time and graded extremely nit-picky. would retake this class with another professor if possible.

She is the best professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. This class is hard because it is so standardized, but she makes it okay. He classes always do far better than the other classes in terms of average on tests, and she's extremely helpful and wants her students to succeed. Avoid all other 150 professors and take her.

Professor Pigg is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. Math 133 is EXTREMELY difficult (I can barely add/subtract without a calculator) but she was there to help me through. The tests are hard but if you do the homework and meet with her during office hours you'll do fine.

She is absolutely the best teacher I have. She very concerned that all her students do good.  The test are long and thhorough but if you do your homework and go to her office hours for help it's ok. She is very kind and willing to help.  Her handouts are great.

She was the worst teacher that I've had at Vanderbilt. She refused to discuss questions that I had about course material and questions that I about tests (after she had graded/returned them). She took off points on a test when I did not put a "2" superscript on a square root sign (yeah, that happened) and then refused to discuss it. DONT TAKE HER!!

Great teacher. I like math so I was willing to put in the work, but she is pretty tough. Very helpful if you go to her outside of class. Tests are long, but if you learn to move quickly, they're fine.

Great teacher, very helpful, and explains everything well. Her quizzes are hard, but get you ready for the standardized tests. One of the best math teachers I've ever had and tries to make the class interesting.

Good teacher, explains concepts well, has great handouts and is very helpful during office hours but the tests long and thorough. You will need to do all the homework and study hard to do well in this class. An A is very difficult to get.  She expects a lot but you learn a lot.

Not a bad teacher, but the tests are far too long. Did not finish any test. Having a question contain 10 complex parts and take up a whole page, and to cram it in as one question on an 8 page, 14 quest test is ludicrous. If you can't do math at her speed, avoid her at all costs. Your grade will not be indicative of your level of understanding.
The only distraction I experienced during this class was her hotness.
I had her last semester and I wish she taught this semester.  She's tough but I could understand her and her handouts were the greatest.  Miss you Mrs. Pigg!

I had not taken a calc class prior to 155a, and got a C+. The fact that I was proud of this grade shows the level of difficulty she brings to the course. She teaches at a quick pace and has a fondness for hard problems, so you have to have a mastery of calc to receive an A from her. But because of this rigor, I have come out with a strong calc base

Professor Pigg is pretty funny and her handouts are very helpful, but the tests were pretty hard. She cares so much about her students though, that she let us replace our lowest test grade with the final exam.

She was my favorite prof last semester. I went to office hours and review sessions. She was very helpful and explained things really well. Her handouts were the best. The tests were difficult but I managed to get an A

Good class as far as calculus classes go.  Pigg actually seems to like teaching and like calculus.  Required a lot of work.  Tests were long and hard but I studied and got an A. Do the homework and go to review sessions and youll  be ok

Great prof!  She is so nice and really concerned about her students progress.  Her handouts are terrific and her lecture is so clear- she makes is sound so easy.  I went to her office for help and the help session before each test.  I totally recommend her.

A terrible woman.  I'm not trying to sound ****, but she should be teaching at the highschool level.  Memorize stuff and you'll do fine.  Ask why you should memorize it and she just ignores you.  I would not recommend this teacher.  Plus the test had nothing to do with the hours I spent on homework.  I feel like I was cheated.

Amazing teacher! She can go very fast, but she is clear and easy to understand. She truly wants every student to do well. There is a high time commitment for any calc, but do all the homework and you will be fine. If needed, go to office hours. Also, this semester she had the highest grades out of all other 155B professors. B averages on tests!

She's great, has great handouts, and is very helpful out of class.  Her test are long and thorough.  The first test is not until about the third week of class, I don't know what the previous person is talking about.  She tough but fair.  Those who try to cry their way to a better grade get treated the same as everyone else.

I dropped her class after a week because her test were impossible, she was an awful teacher and just a generally unhappy person.  She still holds it against me every time she sees me she makes an offhand comment in the hallway.

Dont let her kind grandmotherly ways fool u. Her test are hard. But she's a pretty good teacher.  I did not really learn new in this class due to APcal. But the tests are difficult. Also be careful in making sure you don't make silly errors on the test in showing work. Even taking off for missing parenthesis in work shown when the answer is right.

Pamela Pigg is an example of the profligate teaching practices that leave America devoid of math enthusiasts. The useless woman doesn't even have a Ph.D. She is insuffrable in her use of the expression "Did I boo-boo?" She will single-handedly kill my GPA and raise my blood pressure. That being said, she is pleasant enough as a conversationalist.

She makes things simple and easy to understand. She takes attendance most days so you should go to class but she won't waste your time. She gives amazing handouts to follow along in lectures. She doesn't take up homework. Her tests are hard and I had to rush through them to finish in time. Overall she's great if you identify with her teaching style

Pigg is an AMAZING TEACHER. She breaks things down to where anyone can understand her.  UNFORTUNATELY, this is where the good things end.  She makes her test and quizzes too long for the time she gives. She's the only 133 teacher, so be prepared to get a grade much lower than you expect. Half my class dropped or is retaking it. She has no sympathy.

she s a nice teacher. although sometimes she expects you to be ready for accelerated learning. but it is an accelerated class. so review before class unless you take calc before. she grades hard on test n half of the class may fail. but she drops the worst grade n give ten credits more for overall if you do test corrections. so she s good though.
Absolutely the best handouts, great teacher but strict.  If you want an easy grade don't take this class.

I took this class first semester and failed miserably. Our first test average was a 46. I'm retaking it with another teacher this semester and have a 94. Her tests were ridiculously long and much more in depth than other sections. Take her if you want to be a math major. If not, go to another section.

Prof. Pigg was extremely helpful, I was only auditing her class but she still allowed me to come to her for office hours and made things very clear.  She's strict, but she wants to prepare you for going into calculus.  She also has very informative handouts.  Take notes and do the homework and you'll be fine.
Great teacher, great handouts, tough tests.  She assumes you know your first semester stuff and goes on.  Sticks to the schedule and knows her stuff.  Very helpful if yu have questions.

Calc 150B is normally a hard class because it is a weed out class. However, if you have to take this math class, Prof. Pigg is the ONLY professor you should take it from. Her quizzes are pretty difficult, but if you go to class and to the recommended problems, you will be fine.  Her classes averages are consistently higher than any other class.

Great prof, great handout, explanations very clear.  I found her very helpful but I really worked hard.  I had not taken calculuc in high school so i had to study.  I recommend her if you want to understand what your doing
Avoid if you are in math 155.  her tests are rediculous and most students ended up spending more time on this class than all their others combined.  Supposedly she is not that bad for 150

prof pigg is the best. i took her math 150A course as a freshman without having taken calculus or even precalc in high school. go to class every day. do the homework. she is a great teacher and explains everything clearly - i did better on the department tests than my friends who had gotten 4's on the AP. if you have to take the class, take pigg.

Prof Pigg is the least helpful math prof you could possibly find at this school.  If someone asks a question she may either respond by looking at you like you're suffering from Downs or tell you that you should already have learned it.  If it wasn't for the TA I probably would've failed this course.

Great teacher.  I found her handouts very helpful.  She was available for help during her office hours.  Our class was expected to learn.  The other sections got curved and group work.  If you want to actually learn the subject, she great.  If you expect to have the grade given to you take someone else.

Fantastic calculus professor.  Although 155 kids seem to not like her, she is great for 150.  Clear explanations with good handouts and her humor keeps the class interesting.  The class moves a little fast so make sure you keep up with homework and lessons and you should be fine!  Make sure you get her for 150.

She's by far the toughest teacher up to date. Not only does she make everything way too complicated for it's own good, she also makes her section extremely difficult compared to the other 155b sections. Do not take her if you want to get an A. I have heard that 150b students like her though. Her handouts are nice since you teach yourself.

Hardest/worst teacher ever. Just writes examples on board, too fast to follow, and then makes you basically teach yourself. Impossible to get an A, unlike the other sections, where A's are common. Math was my best subject in high school. I will never take another math class because of her.

Terrible teacher. Goes extremely fast in class, although it makes sense when she does it on the board, it gets a lot harder when you try and do it alone. Her tests are near impossible, although there is always one kid who gets a 95, they mostly likely should have been placed in a higher class. EXTREMELY hard grader, very picky. STUDY, and avoid.

One of the best math profs I've ever had. I will say that while 150B loved her, 155B hated her. Handouts are very helpful; she does go a little fast in class, so make sure to keep up. Always willing to help outside of class. Take her if you get the chance, you won't regret it.

While her handouts are good, she is an impossible teacher and her tests are even more impossible.  Unless you want are willing to let all of your other grades slide to put all of your work into calculus DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
This one's a tough cookie.
good professor, but tests are challenging and you really have to know your calculus to do well.

I think she represents the material in an easy way. She got her awesome hand-outs. She is nice. However, her tests are not easy. You need to be WELL-PREPARED for them. Her tests are pretty long and got some degree of difficutly.
Absolutely the greatest.  Very clear presentation, really knows her stuff.  Tests are challenging but if you do your homework you'll be ok.
Good teacher. Just be prepared to have her teach the class with a tone suited for first graders. "Am I right? Come on! Am I right?"
BADD

dont listen to all of the comments that say "the tests are hard". ITS NOT HER FAULT people! math 150 A and B have departmentalized tests, so it's not pigg's fault. She is an incredible profesor, really explains everything well and is helpful and friendly. if you can take it from her. she is the best math professor you could get.

Ms. Pigg is definitely the best 150a teacher at vanderbilt. if you have to take 150a then take it with her.  The class is impossible but she is as helpful as a professor possibly could be in this impossible class!

Class was slightly difficult but, second semester calc is going to be.  Pigg is very helpful and wants everyone to do well.  Goes out of her way to give review sessions and help students.  overall decent class great teacher

Watch out!  The kids in my class who were naturally great at math did fine - but if you're one of those who needs a teacher who can explain the material, then Pigg is not for you.  The tests are impossible, as are the quizzes.
Very clear explanations, does a good job explaining everything.   Available for help and offers reveiws prior to tests.  Kind and encouraging.
She's been around and definitely knows how to prepare her students. She's always around for study sessions and really helps her students.

Prof. Hutchison is an incredible teacher, one of the best I had freshman year. If you must take calc. make sure you take it with her!!! Her class average is consistently better than the departmental average and it's definately not better students, she's just that good of a teacher.
go to class and take notes...do the homework...get an A

Mrs. Pigg is without a doubt my favorite math professor at Vandy so far. Her teaching style is very clear and she's unbelievably patient with those who have questions. She tells you far in advance that her tests will be hard, but as long as you keep up with the homework assignments and actually understand the material, you'll do fine.

Ok, she may be tough, but she really is the best professor to take for this class. I'm pretty sure she's the head of the dept. and prepares you very well for the final. Her class always gets the highest grades on the tests. Take her.

i thought that taking a math professor who spoke english would make it easier for me, but her quizzes and tests are TOO hard. even though she makes the final exam, i'd rather have an A, take the exam, and finish with a C/B, than have an F and still not do well enough of the final exam to raise the grade. Avoid Pigg, TAKE HUTCHINSON!!

Pamela Pigg is a great teacher. She always makessure you understand the material before you move on and she is readily available to reach outside of class. I took 150B from her twice (so I could replace my first****ty grade). She is tough on her quizzes and tests but all of her students do the best on the final and end up with the best grades.

She is one of the worst professors to take if you are a guy. She moves way too fast and her test are unfairly hard. She says that she makes all the tests hard so that we are not suprised when the final comes. Thanks alot ****! I really enjoyed getting C's all semester. She made me feel like a huge idiot. I am embarassed that she is also from MS.
Ms. Pigg is a very swift person. She goes over 30 pages of your textbook in one lesson. Please do noe take her, you will fail.

Shes the nicest professor I ever met, along with one of the hardest.  If you work hard, she'll work hard with you.  Always there when you need help.  Helped me like math.  She also reminded my of my grandma so thats a plus
GREAT TEACHEER.  DO THE HOMEWORK AND YOU'LL BE OK - BUT YOU HAVE TO PRACTICE.  VERY HELPFUL OUTSIDE OF CLASS.  HAS REVIEWS BEFORE EACH TEST.

Great Professor! Very helpful and encouraging. Test are not too bad if you do all your work and study and I do mean do your homework.  She has lots of office hours and review sessions before each test.

Simply put--the best professor I've ever had.  I've specifically tried to get her for every math class I have.  It's my 3rd semester with her... wouldn't trade her for another teacher.  Her tests are easily manageable if you do ALL the homework that's assigned.  They're long though, so make sure you know your stuff!  Most caring professor I've met!

Great teacher - she really works hard to make sure we understand.  Very encouraging and has lots of office hours.  Do your homework and ask questions and you'll do fine.  I also know she's from Tennessee.

She is horrible. As a fellow Mississippian, I am ashamed to be from the same state as her. She is nasty towards guys, very unhelpful, and moves way too quickly. Her tests are ridiculous and unfair. She makes anyone who has a question in class feel like they are an idiot and that they are an inconvience to her. Worst class ever. never take her
One of the best professors at Vandy. Hard, but very clear in class and helpful during office hours.  Get on her good side.

She is the best math professor at Vandy. She provides clear explanations and tries to make sure that the entire class understands the concepts. the class is tough, but if you stay on task you will do well. She's very easy to talk to and she has multiple office hours.

She is probably the best professor I had during my whole time at Vandy.  Her explanations are clear and she's very willing to explain anything, even if you no longer have her as a prof.  Yes, the course does require a lot of work, but it's calculus what do you expect?
Very good teacher.  Very helpful.  Test are difficult but stay with it.  She will prepare you for the final.

Although she is good at teaching, her class is miserable.  I can honestly say it is the worst I have ever taken.  She has a theory that she will prepare you for the final, which is true, but in the process you are given very unfair tests which give you little to no chance to demonstrate competency. Take another teacher or don't take calc.

She is a great great teacher. I had a horrible teacher for calculus and she has made the material very clear to unserstand. I highly recommend taking her if you can.  The tests are next to impossible but it helps in the end on the final

She tries to be really nice and helpful but it feels like she is talking down to you the whole time. Also she expects you to do the homework before she teaches the lecture, which is not much help. I personally did not like her at all, but if you get on her good side, she can be a favorite I guess if you work.

Very good teacher who explains everything thouroughly. I really disliked math before but because of her clear instruction (and my good grade on the final) I am now really excited about math. Warning: Be prepared to work hard for your grade.
Made a hard calss interesting and as enjoyable as possible.  Always available for help.  Seems to really enjoy teaching.
She makes this course much more difficult than it needed to be. Her tests were near impossible.
She has clear notes during each class but is unwilling to help outside of class and her tests are impossible and much harder than other sections.
I took her for two semesters. Her tests are over the notes and homework. Write everything that she writes on the board. I cannot stress that enough.  An A is hard to get. However, a B- is average.

It is possible to make an A here if you work extremely hard, go to office hours, and show up to class.  Extremely nice woman who can create quite possibly the hardest tests ever.  The benefit is the final is easy in comparison.  I finished in 1.5 hrs when we were given 2.5 by the department!
That class is no joke, but she tries to help as much as possible.  Her exams are really hard, but then the Final seems slightly easier.

She is a very good teacher, straight and to the point.  Her tests are very hard but it made the departmental final so much easier.  Her classes usually do the best on the final which means they get curved up the most.  Pay attention, do the problems and your golden.
Extremely unhelpful, very difficult.
boring
Nice lady and tries to make class fun.  She expects you to do your homework.
She's cool and very helpful. Math usually sucks but she tries to make it as clear as possible and helps you out on your grades as much as possible.

A hard class, but she does offer extra credit and is extremely helpful about scheduling help sessions.  She moves quickly in class, so unless you are good at independent study this isn't the class for you.  She is  very sweet unless she thinks you aren't doing your part, in which case watch out!
Went way too fast, very hard tests.  Nice lady.

Helpful and nice person. She's definitely harder than most of the other 150b teachers, but her class is manageable. Make sure to do hw and attend class, she gives extra credit based on this. Tests are rather intense.
Need to listen very carefully to what she is saying. It is up to the student to do homework. If you had a hard high school calculus teacher, then this class may be easy.
Very nice lady, terrible class
Miserable.  Very hard.
She's hard, very hard, but go see her and get to know her, it will really show up on your grade.  Keep up with homework and always do it, she unexpectedly takes it up a lot.
She is hard and goes fast. make sure you don't ****her off because she isn't very nice if she knows you don't try. her quizzes are easy though.
I have to admit she's really nice and cordial outside of the classroom, but I absolutely hated her class.  I can't stand her as a professor.
Fair, helpful and kind.  I'm not good in math but I made a B.  She has office hours and gives reviews for each tesst.

Made disparaging remarks about my math skills every time I went in for extra help.  Considering the fact that I was there because I didn't understand the material and was making an effort to succeed it was completely uncalled for. Not a nice woman.
Absolutely the greatest.  She's hard but she really cares.  She tries to make class fun.  Has very flexible ofice  hours.
The material covered is difficult, but she does her best to make sure you get it.  Very helpful in office hours, as well as in class.  One of the better teachers in the math department.
Class is ok for a math class.  Prof tries to make it fun.  She is very helpful outside class and the review sessions for tests are very helpful.
Do not take calc with ****g.  I took it in high school and I still got a bad grade because she tries to fool you on the tests.
Very helpful.  Very fair -  treats everyone the same and grades everyone the same.  One of the best.
Great teacher, makes class fun, very fair.
Great if you keep up.  Hard if you don't.
No Comments
Stay away.  Her tests are difficult and she can make rude comments to the students as mentioned before.  And another thing is she makes no effort to help her students outside of class.

I wish she'd teach the 170 series so that I could have had her again.  She still says hi to me in the hallway after 2 years!  I learned so much key calculus from her.  Take her, especially if you'll use math in your major classes.  Super helpful!
No Comments

The tests are very difficult, but that doesn't change the fact that she doesn't do a good job of teaching.  Office hours, graduate tutoring, etc. are encouraged, even if you've already taken calculus.

As long as you keep up with the (optional) homework, and pay attention in class, you should be fine. Her tests are hard, but she always gives extra credit and a big curve. I really liked her, but I think I would have been lost if I didn't have calc in HS
Granted, she is not the easiest professor in the math department, but do the homework, go to her office hours, and actually go to class and you'll do fine.  She'll make sure you know the material.

Tests are incredibly difficult. I took AP Calc and got a 5 on the exam but I'm retaking it for med school and I got a 64 on her first test. But if you do halfway decent on some of the tests- don't drop because she gives extra credit and a HUGE curve.
Extremely difficult, the only tests I passed were by a very little amount.
She is a very strict lady and doesn't put up with crap but a very good professor.  Gotta do your work and pay attention if you want to pass.
Stay away...her tests are hard regardless of whether or not you have had calculus before.   I think a TA does a much better job

Professor Price's History of the Bible course has been my favorite class at Vanderbilt. He is a tough grader on essays but is very accessible outside of class and will gives great feedback on writing. He was very understanding about mental health and granted extensions. Price is an inspirational teacher who cares greatly about his students!

As many other ratings say, it is very obvious that he is passionate about what he is teaching. That being said, he often teaches on the basis that his students have prior knowledge on the topics and uses a lot of advanced terms without explaining them. There is also a lot more work in this writing seminar than a majority of others, so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I would definitely recommend taking a course with Dr. Price. His courses can be hard work with lots of reading and papers, but Dr. Price is a genuinely great guy and you can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches and he cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: very nice guy, if you answer his questions he will like you, a bit of reading and writing though. not easy peasy but totally doable and reasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Price is a good professor, but this is definitely one of the harder first year writing seminars. Price is an engaging lecturer, and he is obviously very passionate about his field, but you absolutely have to put in the work outside of class if you want to do well.

Dr. P is a great fit for this course.
Prior reviews are either biased or MUCH improvement has occurred in her teaching.
Excellent for the subject & doctoral level writing (English background)
Optional turn-ins helped the process w/ significant feedback.
Dr. Preston was notably responsive to emails and learning logs.
Very engaging in class & comms.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had a great experience in Dr. Preston's class. Though it's not related to the course, I appreciated how inclusive and respectful she is with language. I also benefited greatly from her feedback on drafts and projects, via email, and outside of class in office hours. I overall found Dr. Preston to be very responsive, thoughtful, and supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not the best teaching style. I am a teacher myself so I was disappointed in the lack of how she taught this course. The content was great but the professor did not make it feel that way. I felt lack of structure and lack of inclusion. I thought I would take more out of this class to add to develop my capstone but it fell short of that
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not accessible/ not responsive to emails. I was not sure about reviews but they are definitely correct. Waste of tuition fee on this class. Rude professor. Just continuous lecture off of slides. Does not answer questions. Assignments make no sense just busy work. Adult class but treats you like a child. Do not take!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Grades are not clear. She gives a ridiculous exam that makes you feel stupid. I feel like the heavy material for a final that has few questions. The assignments were not beneficial in my learning experience. I can see the relevancy of this course in the classes we need to take but the Professor's way of teaching is not in a learning manner.

Did not feel like a doctoral level course She just read the slides No passion for teaching Long delay in email response Makes you feel stupid Not inclusive. Did not hold class which was not in her updated syllabus Made course more complicated than it seemed on the syllabus Many students had same issue. Needs more experience
This professor is so rude and condescending. He shows attitude towards his students, he does NOT deserve to be a professor. Never take him.

Prenosil is a great teacher, who tries to make it easier to understand the concepts. He stresses understanding why something works and asks about proofs. Tests were difficult but curved well; I recommend studying hard. Homework is pretty easy at least compared to multi.

Adam (he asked us to call him Adam!) is a little bit shy and seems kind of young/inexperienced. Lectures were a little stale but not confusing, always clear enough to take notes. Pace in class pretty quick. I found tests in this class to be challenging, but not in an unfair way; recommend heavy studying. He also curved grades pretty hard. Not bad

Prof Prenosil is a great man! He explains everything very clearly and is open to help if you don't understand. He is very caring. His tests are mostly based on homework and some of your understanding. Highly recommend taking him.

Linear is tough at Vanderbilt, but Prenosil teaches it well. If you fall behind, the textbook explains the concepts decently. This is not an applied math course, so be ready for abstract concepts. Expect to feel lost at times, but know that when you put in the work it will all click. Lots of homework, lenient grading, small curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Prenosil is a good choice in my opinion. His lectures can be a bit boring, but he is good at answering questions whether in class or office hours. There's also weekly homework, which is similar to the format of the tests. The tests were long, but he is lenient with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are kind of dry and confusing and can be hard to follow, but he usually teaches straight from the textbook, so it's easy to catch up on your own. Super nice and helpful in office hours!! He will go out of his way to make time for you. Tests are usually based on the homework problems. He curves a little, but not too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures are not the clearest, but he is really clear in office hours. He is always willing to go out of his way to help schedule office hours if your schedule doesn't work with his regular ones. Really lenient in grading and clearly want the students to do well!

Although he makes computational mistakes and his class is not very interactive, overall, he is an excellent professor. The homework is pretty light and homework boosts your grade a ton. He is very fair with his exams and is willing to adjust the grades if he feels that he is being unfair. He is helpful during office hours and is super chill.

Adam is an amazing professor. Lectures are to the point, homework is easy and light, tests are very fair. The course itself is a bit tough conceptually but Adam is your best option for sure. He curves everything and is willing to help a lot during office hours with homework and your grade. Highly recommend in a department riddled with bad profs
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is such a caring and nice lecturer! He really goes way and beyond to help his students. He held extra office hours which were so so helpful. His tests were definitely doable. Quizzes every now and then, but its just to test your understanding. Theyre not that bad.

Adam is really nice, but his lectures weren't great. Most people just read the textbook instead. Attendance was only mandated by short quizzes at the beginning of class, which weren't too hard. He assigned optional homework after every class, but the tests always seemed harder than the homework.
Adam is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. He's very helpful during office hours. The tests can be quite long and difficult, but he's a lenient grader.

Adam is a pretty nice guy, but hes not a great teacher. He mostly does examples from the book in class, and he makes a couple of mistakes while doing almost every one. There were a lot of quizzes, but most of them were pretty easy. The tests were always long and pretty difficult. Most people would just read the book in class instead of listen.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. Easy tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Principles of ELL Education. Lectures and discussion - can drag a bit but she is very kind and considerate. Definitely learned a lot. Not much homework each week but two big papers (midterm and final) and a presentation. Overall an easy A if you do the papers well. Definitely use the textbook.
Wrote this review because the ones below were way off base. Definitely a great professor that you will be lucky to learn from if in one of her programs.
She may be knowledgeable, but her instruction is the worst. The terribly quick pace and the unbelievable amount of contents would drive you crazy. She read the powerpoint all the time.
Learned a lot, and the is also a lot. Grading is good tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's awesome, made me want to major in child dev. Funny and interesting. You can do well if you put in the work! He pretty much teaches to the 3 noncumulative tests which is super helpful. Highly highly recommend

You come for the developmental psych. and stay for the English-accented humor that spins a pleasant web around the sometimes dry material. His course requirements are standard: paper, 2 or 3 tests, and some homeworks.
Inconsiderate grader. Needs to learn American grading system.

Dr.Price is friendly and helpful ad adds a bit of humor at times, but each class consists of an hour of powerpoint-presentation-lecturing. 3 exams, 2 essays, 1 group presentation, and research participation. Not an extremely difficult course, very manageable workload, just difficult to keep awake during some lectures.
She said she grades hard, but i made an A. she's super nice and always strikes up great conversations during discussion!
Wow! what a nice professor! one of the best professors at vandy hands down. she knows so much and is so helpful. really understands students. take her!

I think it is impossible to dislike Prof. Pruitt. SWEETEST women I have encountered at Vandy. The content of this course is not particular challenging, but it is not an easy A. If you work hard you will be rewarded. Prof. Pruitt was so nice, and was always very helpful in office hours. I definitely hope to take a class with her again! TAKE PRUITT

Pruitt is awesome! She is extremely knowledgable at poetry and is a poet herself. She's awesome to listen to and she starts up some great conversations. She's more than willing to meet with you outside of class about papers and gives you constructive criticism throughout the entire process. Great class, great professor. Highly recommend her!
Very nice woman who helps whenever needed. Little to no homework but some readings are quizzed in little quizzes that you can use the book on. She can be funny at times and class always seems short.

Probably the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt.  Incredibly nice and helpful. Got an A easily in her class and I hate English.  Changes up the types of readings and assignments so you aren't stuck reading novel after novel all semester.  Definitely take any class by her

Has to be one of the nicest professors on campus. scheduled some cool activities that kept interest in class up.  grades papers hard but as long as you're on her good side and come to class everyday you'll be fine.
Very funny.  She made class interesting even though it was in the morning and was 75 minutes long.
Professor Pressley was a great teacher who brought a lot of energy into the classroom and made math class extremely interesting! She's always willing to help. I would definitely recommend her

Professor Pressley made this class fun and the material bearable. She brought energy vs. another dude mumbling into the board. I stink at math but she was always willing to spend extra time with me to help me understand. She clearly knows the material. Pretty fair grader, tests weren't too bad.

She was a good prof. The class was easy to understand and tests were just like examples from the class or homework.  She always made time for me outside of office hours when I needed help. I also liked how we did problems in class instead of just having to listen to a lecture for 75 minutes straight. She did seem sort of new to teaching but overall it was a good class.
Pressley was great for math!  I loved this class, super clear and useful.  If you do the homework, you will do fine.

She was the worst professor I've ever had at Vanderbilt. Her teaching style was very unorganized, and she was very bad at explaining topics. She often made mistakes while teaching that she wouldn't correct until days later. The final was completely impossible too.

I totally agree with the first rater.  She is a terrible teacher and an unfair grader.  She always seemed very self conscious and unsure of herself.  None of the tests were very hard but the final exam was outrageously difficult.  You have to teach yourself the material in this class because Pressley is so incomprehensible.

Pressley's an awful professor. Her countless mistakes in class, terrible teaching abilities and lack of social grace all amount to a horrible experience. Do everything possible to avoid her. Tests are poorly written but easy. However she is a ridiculous and unfair grader, often taking off more points for incorrect algebra than for the actual concep

He was an easy enough grader, comparable to other Spanish professors. On a personal level, he is pompous and has an inflated opinion of his own intelligence. However, I recommend not challenging him no matter how wrong he is. Just smile, regurgitate his opinion in your essays, and wash your hands. That's how I got my A.

A very smart and knowledgeable man; however, this does not translate into good teaching ability. Although we're supposed to read the texts, this is impossible unless you already have extensive knowledge of Latin culture, making each session a monologue by Prieto. Also absent week before first test--which was special.

Prieto is INCREDIBLE. As long as you're a Spanish major and/or have a good command of the language, you will love this class. I learned more from him than any other Spanish professor I've had at Vandy. He is intelligent, engaging, and wants you to learn, as well as improve your Spanish. Hard grader, but worth it!

DO NOT TAKE. unless you are a spanish major that is a junior or senior and you absolutely have to take this class. he grades your papers and tests based on everything he says in class and you can't express your own ideas whatsoever. he will rip your spanish apart whether through papers, your accent, or your ideas. just a warning
Great professor. He is tough, but if he knows you are trying, he will give you a good grade. Just let him know you are making an effort.

At first, I was really intimidated by Prof. Prieto. He's really intense and passionate about literature and he's also supremely knowledgable and intelligent. I grew to really like the class however because he really wants to make his students passionate about literature and makes the class entertaining.

if you can't do an intense literary analysis, you seriously better not take this class. prieto's really intelligent & wants students to learn a lot--his emphasis on pronunciation is helpful too...but i couldnt even succeed in this class if it were in english

This class was very engaging and usually entertaining! Prieto does not just teach short stories, he teaches proper pronunciation, grammar and vocabulary. He wants all his students to become better at Spanish in all aspects. You must work to get good grades in his class, which is easier to do if you agree with his story interpretations.
Very boring! Easy grader

Prieto is the best Spanish teacher I've had at Vanderbilt. He actually teaches, which is unusual for a spanish professor and there is not a lot of busy work. First time I've had a spanish professor that emphasized quality rather than quantity. Must take.
No Comments

This is the 2nd class that I have taken with Prieto. He is absolutely inspirational, & a brilliant professor who engages you in the subject matter. His tests are rather straightforward, but you must work on the papers to produce something insightful & original. Take this and you will learn something. He's hot for an older guy too. (P.S. He's Cuban)

Attending classes is very important. The second half of this class is much harder than the first half. The quizzes and homework helped for the exams, but they were not easy. Many correction opportunities were given, which is good. He also curved the finals.

The class starts off easy, and escalates very fast after the halfway point. Lots of small homework assignments, and the last two exams and the final were insanely hard compared to the beginning. He told us he spent three hours creating one of our exam questions. No one answered it correctly. He gives 1100 a lot of the same work as his 1201 class.

Calc 1201 is a pretty standardized course, but Dr Pu seems to really care about his students' success. He was extremely accessible and answered emails unbelievably fast. Sometimes a bit difficult to understand and his lectures are really fast-paced but you'll survive

Dr Pu is a great professor and he clearly understands the class materials. His class is more than just math, and he always inspires us to think about why certain things hold. Corrections to exams are sweet.

Professor Pu cares about our success. You will find his exams closely following the outlines. Don't miss any review classes. His class is on a fast pace but he is really considerable in going through details during office hours. Very good structure of lectures. Will definitely take his class again!

This class is a little bit tough for me given my math background. Professor Pu is very patient in explaining things. He is always accessible after class. A good portion of points will be possible if you attended most classes. Plenty chances for extra credits.

Dr. Pu is exceptional in the math department! He really cares about his students and he is always ready to help us. He offered many opportunities for extra credit and curved the final grade. Best choice for cal class!
Fantastic teacher, if you are taking calc take it with professor pu.

Professor Pu was really supportive and encouraging throughout the semester. He taught the classes with a great structure of teaching the content and doing sample questions. I would definitely take another class with this professor. He genuinely cares about his students and wants his students to succeed.

Highly suggest taking Math 1201 with Dr. Pu. To be honest, it is a hard course and there are too many exams. Dr. Pu offers outlines for exams, which is extremely helpful. A lot of practice is needed after class, but this should be true for all Math 1201 classes.

Math 1201 is hard in general but Dr. Pu made it comprehensible. He offers numerous practice examples in class. Dr. Pu cares about his students and he is always accessiable after class. If you attend most classes and practice with outlines for each exam, you will be able to do almost all problems in the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Math 1201 is a standardized class, so the material is essentially the same in each section, but I would highly suggest taking it with Dr. Pu. Professor Pu genuinely cares about his students and wants them to do well, which is refreshing within the math department. He offered a lot of partial credit and correction opportunities that boost your grade

Calc 1201 is going to be difficult at Vandy no matter which professor you have, but definitely try to take it with Professor Pu. I felt like he genuinely wanted us to do well, and if you did the homework and showed up to class, it was clear what would be on the test. He is also pretty funny so class was enjoyable. Would take his class again.
tough, incomprehensible but kind and good

Dr Pu is one of the best Math professors that I've ever met. He offers plenty of in-class exercises to makes sure all the students are doing well and understand the material. There is a lot of homework but it is straight forward. Would definitely take his class again and recommend him to anyone that is looking for a math (or stats) class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall, Dr Pu is very considerable to students. He offered many opportunities to work in class and walk through these examples. He showed his care to the class and offered several extensions at the end of this semester. He gave us lists for materials in exams but the final exam is hard.

Dr. Pu had a very guideline to succeed in this class, in which all you need to do is follow it. His tests will be fine as long as you understand his ppt and the homework problem. The lectures are bit dry though, but he is pretty productive during it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shusen was a good professor and wanted to help students. His lectures were rough though... he'll read you the definition of all the words and then hope you work through a problem along with him, but makes it more confusing than need be. That being said, he gives you lots of opportunities to practice and wants you to do well. Never learned my name.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was majority education majors and we all did pretty well. Sometimes the lectures got a little off track/confusing, but overall, pretty simple. He is super patient and if you do the homework and review it before the test you will get an A. He also occasionally gives test corrections which is really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Loved 1010 & Dr. Heath! Class can be awkward with multiple discussion moments without much positive reinforcement for participating, but Dr. Heath gives great feedback on written assignments and responds well to effort if you're showing up with some enthusiasm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super sick prof, helped me out a ton, and the material was interesting. Take her for this if you can, really nice intro class.
Professor always seemed disappointed in student responses. She is not a positive motivator.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Heath is an incredible professor who genuinely cares about her students and their success. She is incredibly knowledgeable, and that shows in her lectures and the diverse readings she provides. Graded on two papers, campus engagement event reflections, and a couple of reading responses. Highly recommend RLST 1010 for HCA credit!
I am not sure if Professor Heath is actually a professor but I loved her class and would definitely recommend taking Women and Religion with her if you have the chance
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class. She didn't need to teach much since the class is based on the textbook completely, but was helpful when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sahai is the best. As kind and helpful as can be.
The class is entirely based on the SolidWorks textbook and a partner project at the end. Sahai is very available for help.

Professor Sahai is great. Super nice and really helpful. If there is a choice between Sahai and Mitchell, they follow the same course structure, so it's not a very consequential choice. I've had her a few times now and can definitely recommend her.

This professor was fairly nice and passionate about the subject; however, she was not very organized. I felt that the class was not structured well, as we wasted most of the time and rushed to finish the project week of. It was an easy A and very low-key project.

We were her first engineering module. Homework was a little confusing at times, I recommend to start learning about AutoCAD before the module starts. Also, final project felt a little rushed due to time constrains. She is a very nice person and I'm pretty sure she will learn and improve the module over time.

Rares is amazing. I took MATH3300 with him, and even though it is a really hard abstract algebra course, he made it make sense way more than my teacher for 2600. Gives a lot of weight to homework, making the grades softer. 2 exams, no final, but there is a final paper. Rares is a very knowledgeable and respected man in his field.

Absolute amazing professor! You can tell inside and outside of class that he not only cares about his students but is very much invested in your success. Super helpful during office hours and his lectures were usually helpful and example packed. HW and tests were standardized across sections. HW was hard but he was willing to help! Tests were fair.

2300 changed this year, so this is based on 2024 Fall Sem:
1) Use cheat sheets on exams to full advantage
2) Yes he has an accent, but you will get used to it
3) The tests are a LOT easier than hw
4) Prof. R is a chill guy, so pop in during office hours if you need anything
5) Pretty nice grader
6) Pay attention to midterms: it will help your final

idk what chat is on about his english is poor... for an old Romanian intellect his english is pretty good. He can certainly accurately deliver what's needed for this class. Very structured lectures and doesn't hesitate to stop and re-explain material. One of the best math profs here

An incredible professor who cares about his students (gave us HW extensions all the time and even pushed back our midterm) and thoroughly lectures on the material. HWs and tests can be long (no cheat sheets) so this class will take more work than other professors, but Rares is a very fair grader. He has math professor humor which our class loved!

Awesome guy but not great as a professor. He speaks very poor english and his lectures are pretty horrendous. His class structure is great and his tests are fair. Wouldn't recommend if you have better options, but he's a safe bet for a decently fair class.

Rares is a very nice professor who is willing to push midterms back to get in an extra week of review for the students. He makes what he is testing on clear and if you do well on the quizzes then the tests aren't bad. You will have to memorize a few things because there is no note sheet.

Professor is a nice, funny guy who cares about your learning. I only had two midterms and a final, which have been very straightforward so far. There is homework after each lecture, however, it reinforces the concepts and prepares you for online quizzes and the midterms. Definitely take him!

Sometimes he's a little tough to understand, but rares is the nicest guy and he really loves teaching. The homework is heavy and graded on correctness, but the graders are very generous. The class gets progressively harder, but he will make sure you have the opportunity to do well and is an extremely fair grader.

Took his class first semester freshman year, and let me tell you it was hard. Weekly quizzes on top of weekly homework make sure that you are staying on track with the class. He was pretty flexible with grading and ended up giving us two quiz/homework drops after some persuasion. Office hours are great for HW help. He's also occasionally funny!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy. I had trouble staying on top of homework at the start of the semester and Rares would always grant extensions and let me know if I missed an assignment. He made multi very enjoyable and engaging. Definitely take him if you can.

Professor Rasdeaconu always goes out of his way to help his students. Insanely helpful during office hours and he hosts review sessions before exams. Also willing to adjust the pace of his class for his students (pushes deadline during midterm weeks). Tests and quizzes are fair as long as you do your homework. Weekly quizzes, 3 exams, 1 final.

His lectures are amazing; he goes over time every class but he covers each concept thoroughly and works through many examples. Homework can be challenging but quizzes and tests are fair and you'll be fine if you can do the homework. Really cares about his students -- one of the best profs at Vandy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Rares is a very caring and nice professor -- he'll always go out of his way to help you if you're struggling and offers review sessions before each exam. Tests are rather long, but they were fine as long as you studied.

Professor Rares is a ~good~ professor. He explains things very clearly, has fair exams, and is very experienced. He's super helpful during office hours and will spend hours with you if it helps you understand. He does teach  5-10 minutes past class time EVERY SINGLE CLASS so if you have a class straight after that's far away don't take him.

I loved Rares. He was so accessible and caring, would always give out extensions and was willing to meet at ungodly hours to work through problems. Content can be a bit dense but reach out to him and you will be fine. Definitely take 2300 with him.
Good professor, great person. Super helpful and really tries to get everyone to understand the material.

Rasdeaconu is pretty nice and very clear about the material that will be tested on the quizzes and exams. Material can be a bit dry, but overall very doable. Grading tends to be very specific, and gets a bit frustrating when marked off for forgetting one of the dozens of formulas you have to memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rares lectures are always clear. Some quizzes, manageable if you work on it a little beforehand. Exams are straightforward and similar to quizzes. He is extremely caring and accessible outside of class. He gives you very genuine advice and guidance. Take his classes!

Rares doesn't speak the best English and he wears a mask so it's hard to understand him. His handwriting is average and can be hard to read. He doesn't explain concepts very well. I find that I learned most of the material from completing the homework and learning while I did problems. He's a nice guy but is a little too smart for this course.

Rares is an extremely nice guy who is always available in office hours or by appointment. That being said, he does a horrible job of conceptually explaining many of the topics in Linear Algebra. Majority of the topics I learned were from the textbook or the homework. The class is a lot harder than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures aren't always the clearest, but he really cares about his students and is willing to adjust the course's pace to make sure everyone is on the same page. Plus, he's actually pretty funny. Lots of homework, a short quiz every week, and 3 tests. Homework can be tough, but the tests/quizzes are straightforward and relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The amount of homework is insane.

Differential topolgy is a highly dense subject, which requires you some abstract and clever thinking, and prof. Rares was there from beginning all the way to the end. You'll have to think a lot and go to his office hours for homework sets. While in-class exams are mainly conceptual, the take-home exams will make you pull your hair out for days.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He cares about his student and remembers every person's name. His office's door is always open and it is easy to find him after class. His lecture is abstract but easy to understand through his explanation. There are quizs once a week and three exams including the final. They are relatively easy. The only "problem" is that the homework is a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Really easy tests especially compared to others in the math department. He might give quite a bit of hw but it helps in the long run and he he doesn't try to play any tricks on the tests they are usually straightforward. Also he's pretty funny which is a plus in a math class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Easiest math class have ever taken as a math major. 9 quizzes and 3 midterms (including final). No homework, no textbook, no attendance needed. If you want an easy A, go for it.

He cares a lot about his students, strongly recommend going to office hours especially to get points back on tests, He mostly deals with proofs, and book examples and struggles to explain the reasoning behind problem-solving step-by-step. Easy to get lost, lectures very fast, his accent didn't really bother me at all, doesn't tell class average
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Accent is hard to get used to at first and voice is somewhat monotone but he cares about students, learned everyone's name in a fairly large class. Fair tests, doesn't curve but lets you average lowest grade with your final. Takes attendance some days to get idea of who shows up. Homework mandatory/graded for correctness, check in solutions guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Rares was a great professor. I would always see him after tests and he would clearly explain what I missed, and if he felt like I deserved mor points for my thinking he would add them. Overall comapred to what tests Ive seen from other calc professors I truly believe his are the most doable. There is a TON of homework though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you have to take a higher math, TAKE. RARES. Clear lectures, very low pressure/down to earth classroom environment. Graded homework. He's endlessly helpful in office hours. He holds review sessions for tests (which are straightforward if you get the hw/quizzes). Also very understanding (gives extensions on quizzes and hw if you ask). Take Rares!
I love this man. Although he might not be the best presenter, he cares about his students. That's what makes him a great educator. Plus, he is really easy to get along with. Very amicable professor.
I love Rares so much! His tests and quizzes weren't difficult and his lectures are pretty easy to follow. He's just all around a great professor. Would recommend for anyone taking 175.

He is a very good professor. His teaching in class is very clear and helpful. He's good in answering questions during OH too. Having review sessions and  practice tests are very helpful for the exams.

It's strange how a lot of the homework problems are from subtopics that are not covered in class, or are not in the syllabus. Trying to understand what problems are in the homework and which sections I need to study have been tougher than the material itself. He's a nice guy, but the disorganization is disorienting.
Incoherent and illogical, for a mathematician or logician.

Had a genuine interest in every student and tried to do everything he could to help. He has a little bit of an accent which made him a little hard to understand at times, but it is normally not an issue. Mandatory graded homework (easy but takes time) and weekly quizzes. Tests are fair, easy if you pay attention in class and do the homework
Although he mainly lectures in class, he is excellent at answering questions during office hours.
awesome!!

Awesome!! Quizzes are easy. His test quite challenging, but mostly he will ask about the basic concept and definition of theorem that we learned in class. The ratio of difficulty of his test is 1:5, which mean every 1 difficult question relative to 5 easy questions...
Not very knowledgeable and biased despite trying to act so awkwardly 'cautious'!

Actually PHIL 9020 - Contemporary Metaethics (but open to undergrads)

She is very kind and picks good readings. Lots of class discussion.

I loved this class! Super interesting reading and discussions and some fun group work activities, which she graded just a bit harshly. The tests were easy and the prof gave us extra credit opportunities to make up for the lost grades on the in-class assignment.

Tests are very straightforward and basic lecture recall, super easy to do really well. Writing assignments, though only a few, are a little tricky to know what she wants and more harshly graded. Class overall was really engaging with interesting topics. One of my favorites!

Dr. Raskoff is a newer professor, but I think she has a lot of knowledge about the topic and I was exposed to many diverse perspectives. My criticisms of her course is that for some of the assignments it was unclear why I got the grade I did. I also feel like she was biased during the abortion section. Make sure to participate during class.
Terrible professor. It should've been an easy A course, but she grades harshly and unfairly. Avoid at all costs. She hands out arbitrary grades that make no sense whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Raskoff is a harsh grader on all assignments aside from tests, making it almost impossible to get an A. She doesn't give rubrics or clear expectations on anything. Also, if you don't frequently speak in class, even if you attend, she'll give you a 70 on participation...

The class should be pretty easy, but Prof. Raskoff has no sense of how to grade fairly. She provides no rubric for most assignments and then proceeds to grade the assignments incredibly hard. It makes absolutely no sense. At least her tests are pretty easy...

Incredible, chill professor. Teaches the content quite well and makes it intuitive. Lots of life lessons. Didn't love the structure of Consumer Finance. Much busy work papers and a weird group essay final. Very logical, but the work is so straightforward that graders nitpick pointless things relentlessly. The course will be great down the road.

Love Professor Rando and this class. Super valuable personal finance class, seriously, some of the most real-life important stuff I've learned here. This class is easy and doesn't require much work outside of class at all, besides 2 group projects (which are easy and each like a week of the semester).

Overall he is a good guy. However, I often hear of students say he puts a 9 in front of the grade and then role a die to figure out if it will be a 91, 92, 93, so on. He is not a difficult grader, it just feels random, hence the die example. Classes are enjoyable and he makes his own comments about the slides that make the class entertaining.

He is chill, nice, caring, respected, well-connected, and ready to meet/help - true, but I felt like this is too much for a business minor class. An absurd amount of attention to detail is needed in assignments, harsh grading - you need to be perfect to get a good grade. Spent 2-3x more time than on any BUS class and still nowhere near an A
He brings lots of guest speakers which is very inspiring.
Taught me so much. Always available too if you have personal or academic questions. Super smart guy.

Random is super chill, understanding and well-connected. He brings in former students who work at various companies to talk to us about recruitment, job offers and shares business-related opportunities on campus. Group work is a big part of your grade, which can be frustrating if your team doesn't contribute. Still, he's a solid professor overall.

Rando's a great guy and really cares. Class was fine but some assignments definitely felt like busy work. I often found the lectures to be pretty simplistic and that I wasn't really taking a way a ton. I think it's a great class for a freshman / sophomore, but if you've already had an internship in the business world, it might be a bit boring.

A hard class but I have learned a lot about Excel and PowerPoint and making presentations. Super helpful for future consulting careers. Rando was good about being accessible via email or office hours and lectures were interesting.

Do beware - policies are more "real world" like no extensions, no skips, and limited directions on assignments.

If you want to learn real skills, Rando is for you. I learned more in this class than in all others this year, combined. Truly helped me understand concepts to nail interviews. This class is group-dependent, and is all group work. Luck of the draw is a real factor. But, if you are willing to work hard, this will be the best class you've taken at VU

If you want an easy class to learn about the basics of entrepreneurship, THIS CLASS IS NOT FOR YOU! 65% of the grade is group work and you are stuck in one group that whole time, and if you get randomly placed in a bad group, which is all randomly assigned you're done for...

Rando is a super engaging lecturer and has a ton of experience that he'll tell great stories about. Most of your grade is comprised of different assignments for a group project that is worked on throughout the semester. Definitely not a hard class but some of the assignments require a lot of time consuming work outside of class with your group.

Entrepreneurship is a fun class, and as a stem major who's taking it for the AXLE credit, I feel like I've learned a lot of valuable information. Like other people have said though, your grade is mostly group projects (and he picks the groups), which can be unfortunate but I made it work. Great guy, some cool guest speakers.

Your grade is pretty much determined by the group you are assigned. Unfortunately, I got paired with two very lazy people. However, my individual grades made up for it. Not an easy A and very work heavy, but got something out of it.

Professor Rando makes the classes fun and sometimes very funny. He is quite inspirational. But I wouldn't take this class for an easy A. The group projects can be difficult but a lot of leadership skills are gained in the process as you steer through them.
A must-take prof at Vandy. Truly incredible, with no busy work and really valuable assignments.

The assignments were challenging but not difficult (if that makes any sense). You'll learn a lot about Excel & how you can use it to do actual corporate work. The powerpoint part can be a bit slow though it's a tiny portion of this class. Highly recommend it to sophomores and juniors before they start their (finance) internship!

LOVE this professor. If you take his class, make sure to go visit him during office hours. He genuinely cares about his students and he's got some awesome experience. You'll learn a lot about the topics he covers in class & life advice in general. Lots of group work & papers/presentations. Not a difficult class but you need to put in effort & time
His assignments are so ambiguous...

Prof. Rando is not knowledgable about anything related to data analytics and I felt like I could have gotten this same information by looking it up online. The assignments were difficult in an unnecessary way -- like they were challenging mainly because he gives you none of the info in class. This class would have been great if i were in 9th grade

Rando is a terrific professor, he likes to bring in guest speakers and tell us about his entrepreneurial past, which is all super cool and worth listening to. Great speaker and cool guy to talk to. Quizzes and cases are super easy. He puts you in groups early on and your grade is pretty much determined by how good your group is.

Not goin to lie, one of the best classes Ive taken at Vanderbilt. Regardless of whether you want to be an entrepreneur, Professor Rando gives so much valuable real-life lessons and stories from his career. Would recommend to anyone looking to go into business after graduation.

Rando is great. He has a ton of experience and clearly knows what he's talking about. You can tell he wants to help his students succeed in the class but also outside of the class. He will definitely go the extra mile for his students and he has a lot of interesting stories that relate to what you're learning. Definitely take his class.

Professor Rando might be the best professor I have in my time at Vanderbilt. He is inspirational, he is successful, and he is extremely knowledgeable in the area of entrepreneurship. This class by Prof. Rando is a must for anyone going near the business world. Rando has experience as an entrepreneur; his stories will stick with you for life.

The grading felt arbitrary, and the assignment guidelines were sometimes ambiguous. I worked very hard, and I was able to pull off a B+. The assignments were surprisingly time consuming, and one you had to completely learn yourself. I like him as a person, and he is an impressive business man, but I would not recommend this class.
not as ez as reviews advertised...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thé class isnt too hard to pass, but grading is rather arbitrary- felt like he just goes with what he likes best. And when people made mistakes in a presentation, he would call them out in front of the whole class which felt unnecessary.
the man. If you are interested in startups at all take this class

The whole semester is based on a group project. Its a decent amount of work but easy to do well because he grades the presentations easily. You have to read and prepare for the quizzes but the reading is easy and worth it.

Professor Rando is helpful and kind, but this class has a group project that determines the majority of your grade. Ended up being MUCH more work than I had imagined, and Rando gives too many assignments that take a lot of time. I did learn a fair bit about entrepreneurship, but this class isn't easy. Grading was a little unfair and arbitrary IMHO.

Rando is a nice enough guy but this class was structured in an annoying way. The semester-long group project ends up being a ton of work and is graded leniently, which makes all the effort seem somewhat pointless. Lectures are fairly boring and the class is less interactive than he makes it out to be.
