It is an easy class. The class is all based on creating a start-up company. Each group assignment builds off one another for this business plan. Just be aware that the group projects are work and take up time. Everyone gets A's. Quizzes every Tuesday/Attendance/case studies boosts your grade.

Rando is a great professor! I think he really shines in the Entrepreneurship course, more than Management. He's very fair and straightforward about his expectations. He really appreciates students who put in effort and make it clear they care. He was very communicative and helpful when group project drama arose. He has a lot of experience too.

Prof Rando was one of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. He truly is an inspirational guy, and speaks from tons of prior experience (He was the COO of a company and then ran his own franchise). You have to attend classes and there's a really easy quiz before every class. Group project is intense, so make sure you get a good start on it.

Professor Rando is unparalleled. I enjoyed everything I learned in this class and definitely feel more prepared to enter the workforce at the end of my year. The projects are fun, creative & educational--he is AWESOME!! TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CAN!! We are lucky to have him here at Vanderbilt. Managerial Studies Program, keep him as long as you can!

Rando's class isn't tough... at all. There's no chance you're going to finish the semester with anything lower than a B. With that said, the grading is so subjective that it can be challenging to do well on his simple assignments. The grades he gives on papers are so random. Good writing is not rewarded at all. Not great at responding to emails.

Great class. You know what is expected from you. He is really interested in seeing his students succeed and will meet with you outside of class if you need help. If you do what is asked, it is an easy A.
Great professor, great class. Not difficult at all and lectures are interesting. He cares about getting to know his students, and brings in lots of great guest speakers.
I love RANDO

I think there were some flaws to his understanding of basic business principles. Some students thought that it was an easy class, but personally the class was not helpful. All the assignments are busy work and do not prepare you for anything useful.

This class is not as easy as advertised! I put in a good amount of work, and made a B. In my opinion, papers were graded very strictly. Attendance is mandatory, as there is an easy quiz at the beginning of every class. I know a lot of people made easy A's, but beware! Especially if you are not the greatest at paper writing.

Take this class, even if your major/minor doesn't require it. Rando is literally great- so helpful, interesting, and engaged in the material and his students. This class was easy but fun. Can't recommend it enough!!!
Relatively easy class, but his grading is pretty arbitrary and inconsistent.
It is the easiest class you will take at Vanderbilt but you do learn a lot. I would highly recommend it to anyone interested in business or management because he's a great teacher.

Probably the easiest teacher I have had at Vanderbilt. Class is not boring, but very engaging. Attendance is mandatory, however, it is the easiest A you will ever get. Open book/notes/laptop/any resource on the weekly quizzes and even on final, so its almost guaranteed you get a 100 on both those.

Fun class if you like the idea of business or starting a business. Attendance is mandatory, because Rando gives easy quizzes that are open book. Taking notes not critical, but it helps on the cumulative "big quiz" at the end of the year. Definitely recommended the professor and the class.

Very fun class and definitely a good one to take for the corporate strategy minor. Classes were fun, no textbook, and there is a guest speaker every week. All tests and quizzes are open note. No final, only a project but make sure you allot enough time to do it well.
Awesome professor. He's very realistic about the interest level in the class and tries to make it interesting. Funny, relaxed, very helpful. Take this class!

Two bits of advice: participate regularly and be SURE to get a good group for your project.  If you speak in class regularly and have a hard-working group this class is an easy A.  I, however had a terrible group and mediocre participation, and I made an A by the skin of my teeth.  Fantastic professor and an interesting class, highly recommend.

Very good professor/speaker. The class is not challenging, but you do learn something. Project is the focus of the class, textbook is barely used, and guest lecturers are engaging. Only homework is reading a case study, several papers throughout semester. Take this class, it's not hard at all. If you want an 'A', participate in class.

Rando's real-world experience as an entrepreneur makes this class fascinating. Guest speakers every week, open note/book quizzes that are a breeze. NO TESTS! There are 3 papers and a final business plan that you should put some decent effort into. He wants you to do well and he is always available. Make sure you get a good group 4 your project!

GREAT teacher. Understands that class can be tedious and tries to make it entertaining. Always has guest speakers. Quizzes are easy--open book, open note. He really wants you to get a good grade and clearly spells out all assignments. Class is fun and definitely worth it. Rarely do reading. HW is easy. If you do some work, you should get an A.

Dr. Donnelly was a really kind professor. Lectures were fine and her content is easy. 2 Exams, 1 Group Project, 1 Paper. Attendance mandatory. You get 5 unexcused absences before she takes points away from you. The content was interesting and our prof was great.

I loved taking this course. Professor Donnelly is so kind and knowledgeable about sociology and health issues. I loved her lectures, and her slides were super clear to understand. You get five free absences: one midterm, one final, one paper, and one group project. It sounds like a lot, but they were well spaced out.

Calls out the attendance roster and checks for absences at the start of every class, probably because otherwise no one would come to her class. You could skip every class and just look over the posted slides to get 100 on every exam. Unfortunately, if you skip classes, she takes points off your grade. Otherwise, this is a super easy class

I loved Dr. Donnelly's class! I never had a bored moment with her teaching style. There are plenty of group discussions where everyone has the opportunity to share their opinions in a judgement-free environment. Overall, this class was very doable and extremely insightful. She is without a doubt the best professor I've had so far.

She's so sweet!! Midterms are easy to prepare for and class content was interesting. i liked the way she structured the assignments (1 group project, 2 exams, 1 final paper, daily readings). a lot of group discussions and opportunity to contribute insights based on personal experiences.

Unstructured and posts 10+ readings a week even though the exams have no relation to the content readings. She will still fail you despite the B+ Econ department average. Found the math portion of her class to be kind of obscure. Tests are tricky and the questions will have underlying nuances she never discusses.

No clear criteria for grading projects. Will give grades to make sure you are falling in the B average grade required by the Econ department. Says she doesn't take attendance but will make sure to use it against you in grading exams. Make sure to stay on her good side.

I really enjoyed this course. Professor Zaiour has very straight forward lectures and problem sets. The exams in the class mimic the exam review problem sets and the homework. She is very accessible outside of class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Reem keeps lectures relevant and clear. Her problems sets are very similar to exams, which are not very hard. She does not really assign homework and all you need to do is pay attention in class and do the study guide, and you will do fine on exams. She is a super nice person who wants students to succeed. Amazing prof and not too difficult.

New prof to the department... straightforward lectures. Provides problem sets that are similar to exams. No HW except for 3 problem sets: one for each exam. Super helpful in office hours and just overall an interesting class about migration. Take her class!

Previously took her ANTH 1101 class and decided to take this as well. Really interesting class and lecture-heavy. She's willing to accommodate for people, really understandable and lenient to all her students. Perusall is taken as participation for the class and she kept changing the standards but that's minor. Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Gamez is super sweet and caring. She's very approachable and willing to help you whenever you need it. She also provides great feedback on essays.

Professor Gamez is great. I took her ANTH 1101 class. lecture heavy, although she explains the concepts very well in these lectures. it will be easy if you pay attention and do the readings, which are not too much and all scannable. 4 fieldnote observation around 1000 words, 2 inclass writing exams, 1 final reflection paper around 2-3000 words.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gamez is a great professor. She's super kind, accommodating to student needs, and passionate. I had her for ANTH 1101, and I recommend this class to everyone. She is a strong lecturer and keeps lessons interesting with videos and discussions. Readings are short and easy to understand. Exams are timed short essays, doable if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Gamez really cares about her students and their learning about the material. This class was super interesting and we had such insightful discussions. If you care about social justice issues and history, this class is awesome. She is very caring and respected by her students, overall would take her again for sure.

I found that the professor teaching CORE 1020 seemed unfamiliar with the subject matter. The lectures lacked clarity, structure, and depth, which made it difficult to follow the material or gain a solid understanding of the course concepts. When questions were asked, the responses were often vague or unrelated, further contributing to confusion.

Amazing teacher for CORE. She is very caring and is quick to answer emails when it comes to questions regarding class. Also very understanding. I believe she is a chemistry teacher, and I plan to take her again once I reach higher-level chemistry! She makes science so fun and insightful!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: My heart goes out to Professor Robinson as she was charged with teaching a recently created class that had no point in even existing and lacked any substantial material. However, she falls prey to picking favorites and will hand out unfair grades solely based on whether she likes you or not. If you want to do well, stroke her ego.
Professor Robinson is wonderful! I would highly recommend taking one of her courses. She cares for her students and will work with you if you are willing to work with her.

I think everyone ended up getting an A in this class. She is not a great lecturer and I didn't learn a lot of things in this class, but the quizzes (in covid times) are incredibly easy and there're so many extra credits. As long as you put in minimum effort you will get an A. If you want to actually learn something though, go take the other prof's.

Disclaimer: online. Lots of weekly assignments but made material more digestible. Focuses on several real world applications so its helpful to see where analytical chem fits into the big picture. Some assignments were harder/more time consuming than others but she gives "applied" credit to help out. Overall, solid choice for analytical chem

Dr. Robinson is a great professor. The course content can be challenging at times but she does her best to make it an engaging experience by incorporating recent research that contains relevant analytical methods. Definitely a manageable class if you put in the effort. Also extra credit to help you along the way

Worst teacher I've had at Vandy. Completely disorganized and how no clue on how to effectively convey even basic information to the students. Complete misuse of examples that only further confused the class. Neglected basic principles in favor of discussing overly complex research articles. Little to no actual teaching. Extra credit available, tho.

Dr. Robinson is super nice and genuinely cares about Analytical Chemistry. However, her explanations of many topics were unclear, as well as what she expected us to know on the tests. The tests were unnecessarily tricky. She does give extra credit if you do extra assignments, which is what saved me a few letter grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pro: easiest chem class, straightforward tests, she's not trying to trick you, little & easy homework, extra credit opps, wants students to succeed, first semester teaching so room for growth Con: sometimes disorganized, lots of journal articles to read, sometimes doesn't do a good job connecting the foundational concepts to the higher level ones

Dr. Robinson was certainly a fair grader, and she offered a myriad of opportunities to earn "applied credit." She sometimes seem unprepared for lectures and occasionally struggled to explain things clearly, but overall taught the subject of analytical chemistry well. Problem sets were usually challenging, but they were done in groups.

Dr. Robinson is an extremely caring and sweet professor. She laughs a lot, her lectures are not boring as she keeps students engaged (although practically nobody responds initially). The class grade is comprised of a majority 4 exams, which are graded fairly, and four problem sets (20% of grade) which are group projects. Also, 5 pts of extra credit

While Dr. Robinson's class was no walk in the park, she made a point to encourage independent thinking and connect what we were learning to practical applications. Just memorizing the information is not enough to succeed in this class, you have to be able to actually understand it, but because of that you get a lot out of this class if you try.

Don't bother with Dr. Robinson. She does not teach the basics of any material, instead using "real-world" applications no one understands. Her problem sets and lectures have lots of errors, and she ignores emails. The textbook is mediocre at best, which isn't really a big help. Overall, a not a good professor. Beware!

Professor Rena (pronounced Renee) Robinson is a distinguished researcher in her field. That said, she should not be teaching. She has a very poor grasp of the material she teaches and fails to engage the class as students are quickly lost amidst her disorganized powerpoints. She doesn't answer emails and is not very helpful in office hours.

Definition of disorganized. The ppts she gives us don't always match the lectures, and her grading is very arbitrary. For some Qs, if you make a small error she'll give no credit. She also has several guest lecturers that are completely confusing, but she just told us to put that in the course evaluation when we complained. Worst prof I've had .

It's mid-semester semester so u know this is urgent. She is disorganized, unfamiliar with the material, and gives no clear explanations. Lectures are disorienting. I think it's very hard to make an intro level class this bad, but somehow she manages. Of all the chemistry courses i have taken this is the worst, and i took a lot of chemistry courses.

I love Dr. Williams. I took her Black Power class. I learned a lot, and assignments were not overbearing. If you plan accordingly, readings and papers should not be a problem. She is a fair grader. If I did not procrastinate, I would have gotten an A.

I know this was a pilot course, but there was so much uncertainty around grading all semester and the constant changes to the syllabus were frustrating. Clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic, also a very quirky professor. If you're just looking for an easy A, I wouldn't recommend but you'll definitely learn a lot

Best professor Ive ever had. It can be hard sometimes when we dont receive the grades we had hoped, to see the value of what was gained from class. But somehow I believe this is the most important class of my college career. It was both an honor and a privilege to study with this professor. If you dont want to learn, dont take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The professor rarely taught the class, making students talk all the time. The professor demonstrates a concerning lack of coordination, changing assignments for the group project nearly every class. Moreover, did not follow dead week policy, making assignments due during this time. Additionally, course work is too much compared to level 2000 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: PSY-PC 3650. Best professor I've taken at Vandy! She gives really elaborate and great feedback to all my assignments, I could see she really cares for her students. Learned so much in her class. don't know why ppl say she is a harsh grader.

Tests are basically all about the research she presents in class. I don't know why these people are saying she is a harsh grader, I literally got so many points from BS. She's a nice person and her section has less work. Honestly pretty easy, I studied maybe 2-3 hours for exams and got As. Just pay attention in class

Professor Rittle-Johnson was fine. Her lectures were the usual and she incorporates a lot of research (she loves research). No offense to her, but do not take her section. Take the large lecture section. That class has higher test averages, no papers, and easier tests. That is the one that has all the athletes. They basically aren't the same class.

Incredibly competent, knowledgeable, and respected professor. Her experience conducting research in the field is evident as her course involves lots of work reading & engaging with research studies. She is incredibly thorough & makes sure this isn't considered an 'easy A' class. Provides very helpful study guide outlines that mirror exam content.

I've taken multiple classes with her. Wonderful professor who really cares about her students. Very knowledgeable and passionate about her work and it shows in course content. Workload is more than manageable and as long as you do reading, attend class, and do some studying an A is easily attainable.
Such a harsh grader! Always takes your point off for no reason.

what to say...pretty kool teacher. likes to talk about children. knows her stuff. really likes examples, so read the book! tests over the material she says she will, tries to help as best as possible. grading can be a little difficult, but she's just being a little picky. must to readings!

She is really nice and really clear in class explaining every concept with concrete examples. She narrows textbook readings to a minimum, gives reading quizzes that are usually predictable, tries to vary class activities as much as possible. TA sucks at teaching and she tries to scare you for her tests but they are much easier then she makes it see
This class is pretty easy as long as you pay attention to her slides and videos.  She's also a very nice person but likes to talk about her kids a lot.
No Comments

Awful, awful, AWFUL! This could have been a very interesting class, but she made it horribly boring. I felt like the class had nothing to do with course title. She focused on math and science and those of us not teaching those subjects left feeling like we had totally wasted our time.

This class was incredibly boring. She could have made it much more interesting given the topics, but she chose to rely on research journal articles(not a research class)that bored the class to tears. Lots to read, huge lit review. Grading was fair, though

interesting topic, but boring class. . . you learn a moderate amount, but lectures are boring and tests cover a large amount of material. . . she's a nice person, but i wouldn't recommend taking her class
Her class is tortuous and shes a really picky grader. Most of the info for tests comes from her mouth and videos watched in class. if you dont write everything she says down, you're screwed

By far the easiest business course I've taken. All exams are online and take-home, and there are only two assignments for the entire semester, each taking about 1–2 hours to complete. The professor grades very leniently, making it a low-stress class overall. Attendance is mandatory and lectures can be quite boring, but it's an easy A.
Lacks professionalism, poor communication, harsh grader.

Unprofessional and plays favorites. If she has a bad day she'll take it out on you… better hope you don't have a presentation otherwise you'll be insulted and interrogated. Multiple people apologized to me afterward for how rude she was. No rubric, yet an extremely picky grader. I am always so grateful for my educators, but this is a first.

Easiest mod I've taken so far - she is engaging and really encourages participation, and all tests/quizzes are online and open book/open note. She also offers lots of opportunities for extra credit if you need it and does a good job of relating concepts to real world things. Really good at explaining concepts too.

So much extra credit, but mandatory lectures that are just a regurgitation of the textbook. 120 pages of reading a night & poorly worded exams. Lecture is content heavy and boring & it feels very intense. Prof Riley is kind, and it's a difficult class to teach, but content structure needs a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easiest business elective by far with Prof Riley. 3 quizzes, 1 midterm, 1 final are all online take-home assessments. 2 assignments that are pretty easy to do with relatively clear instructions (kinda long tho). That's all that makes your grade, plus participation which she really emphasizes in class but ends up grading leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Professor Riley, but just wish the class wasn't half a semester. We zoom through the material SO quickly which makes it very difficult to absorb the information and truly learn (we go through at least two chapters a day in class). Tests and quizzes are fairly difficult as well.

Prof. Riley is amazing. She is very dedicated and passionate about what she does. As a subject matter expert in marketing and sales, whether you're taking this class out of interest or to fulfill minor requirements, you will end up loving marketing. Her lectures are super engaging and dynamic as participation is graded. Attendance is mandatory.

Literally easiest class ever. All exams and quizzes are take-home. Only 2 homework assignments that only took me like an hour. Participation is required, but you don't have to pay attention because she posts the lecture slides.
Riley was great. Great lectures and engaging with students. Just be ready to read the textbook a lot because everything is based on the textbook. Not many study questions, just memorize the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teaching style is largely lecture-based, with frequent "checks on learning" by random calling on and questioning people about the reading. Heavy course load with chapter readings, case study readings, discussion question posts, concept journal writing assignments, group case reports, and final group project with presentation and 15-page paper.

This professor is actually really lenient and cares about helping students succeed. He's understanding when things are tough and makes sure no one gets left behind. The curriculum is hard, but his teaching style makes it way more bearable. Would definitely recommend if you want a professor who has your back.

he is really nice and just wants you to show up and has a lot of leniency with late work. the class is just midterms which he gives the terms before class and you just have to memorize which is not hard. and then two papers which he does not grade harsh either. i love this prof and will def take a future class again.
Awesome Guy! One of the best professors at Vanderbilt by far.

I LOVE dr. rife. He is very passionate about his field, which kept me engaged in lectures. He understands college students and is lenient and caring with necessary absences. 2 papers, 2 exams and usually gives lots of options for paper topics to find one you're interested in. All info for exams is given beforehand and he's accessible out of class

Rife is genuinely amazing. His passion is very evident for archaeology. This class is pretty easy, 2 exams and 2 papers, not too hard. He gives very detailed criteria that makes writing the papers really easy. Even if you just need an axle/core credit, I highly recommend Rife. He is funny and cares about all of his students as well.
Amazing guy and professor, loved learning from him. His passion is evident.

Professor Rife is caring, understanding, and makes his expectations clear. You are given everything on the test in advance and just have to prepare the information. He is very helpful during office hours, willing to review entire essay outlines and provide correct answers for an upcoming test. He really tries to make the content interesting.

Rife is a super intelligent, nice man and a very caring professor, but he is very disorganized. Most lectures are 90% repeating ideas he's mentioned before and 10% introducing new topics. It gets boring and repetitive quickly. Quizzes super easy, the midterm/final are straightforward with the right preparation, and the 2 papers are flexible enough.

Rife is very nice and genuinely cares about his students. However, he is also very disorganized and generally wastes a lot of class time. This course was supposed to cover the Crusades; we made it through 10 minutes on Muhammad. Easy class, nice guy, and good TAs, but if you really want to learn as much as possible, take with someone else
Nice guy but his lectures were boring. He just sat at the front of the class and talked the entire time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rife is a bit unorganized, but caring and a lenient grader.

Do yourself a favor and take a class with Joe Rife. He is one of the most caring professors at Vanderbilt about both his class and field. Even if you are in a STEM major, Classics 3200 is a perfect AXLE class. Even today in class he, unprompted, gave an extension on an essay because he heard students were struggling from his colleagues.

Professor Rife is nice, but it feels like he wants the class to be harder than it is. Two papers, two midterms, but the expectations are not clear at all. I asked him for feedback and he responded with one sentence. When I asked to explain my grade, he said my descriptive writing didn't suit the material. Not my kind of professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: LOVED Professor Rife! His class was super interesting and I loved his lectures and how he engaged with students and asked questions. Super, super caring, he will give you extensions if needed and completely understands everything going on with COVID. Graded on 3-4 short quizzes, two tests, and a paper- if you prepare for them well, you'll do great

Prof. Rife showed up unprepared & late to every class period, which was extremely frustrating. He did not seem to have a plan & he did not provide us the support necessary for us to succeed. The tests in this course did not assess our learning at all and he did not take out concerns seriously. He is a nice guy, but I did not like the class.

Pretty average class in my opinion. Prof Rife is nice but is really not an engaging lecturer. Easy A- ... anything better than that requires a decent amount of effort. Midterm and final requires you to have good lecture notes -- if the lectures weren't recorded I would not have done so well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you are interested in the topic, it is a class worth taking, but maybe not if you aren't willing to put in the work or pay attention. Tests were easy to prepare for. There were four papers, most pretty short and simple, but little feedback was given so be prepared to go ask in office hours if you need clarification. Little class participation.
Not helpful or considerate of others. Lectures are boring. One of those people who think he knows everything.
Not helpful. Rude to people when things do not go as planned. Not considerate. Thinks his way is always right.
Rife is an energetic and passionate lecturer, though his content is very boring. Grading is easy, and the readings are not at all necessary to complete. Content is uncomplicated and common sense.

Very alright. Classes are just hour and half lectures of this guy talking non stop. Knows his stuff but class is so boring. Sometimes gets very specific on certain things that arent that relevant/interesting. Everything graded by TAs but its not hard. Easy A-. Attendance everyday

The reviews below are incredibly incorrect. I've taken 4 classes with Joe Rife and I can attest that he is incredibly helpful. I've learned so much from taking classes with him over the span of 2 years, and I would wholeheartedly recommend his classes. Grading is certainly easy (I've gotten A- or A grades in all of the classes I've taken with him).

this class was so boring. all of the grading for the essays was so subjective. there was no feedback on the essays, so there was no way i could improve my grade, even after going to office hours weekly. the midterm was even worse. even after writing down everything he said in class, i did not receive a very high grade. an easy A-/B+ but not an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Rife is knowledgeable about what he teaches. I give him that. However, the grading is very arbitrary and the work does not coincide with the grade. Unless you plan on getting a Ph.D. in archaeology or anthropology, I would not suggest this class. Not an easy A, but an easy A-.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Perfect AXLE international cultures class. 2 tests+2 papers+term quizzes. The tests and quizzes are incredibly easy, and the papers are graded very leniently. Attendance is required for participation points, but the readings are not necessary whatsoever. I honestly wouldn't even recommend buying the textbook

Dr. Rife is great. It can be hard to follow sometimes because he talks so fast and covers so much information without any slides. He basically just talks for an hour and fifteen minutes, but the material is interesting and he has very clear grading criteria. I also find him nice to look at, which makes the lecture go by faster.

The most interesting class I have taken at Vanderbilt. Professor Rife is very straightforward with his requirements and expectations. He is truly interested in his subject and makes the class interesting as well. There is however a lot of reading for the class. Requirements: 1 short essay, 1 research paper, 3 memorization quizzes, 2 exams

LOVE HIM!!!  I went on his Maymester last summer and had the best time.  He is so passionate about what he teaches and researches and he really knows his stuff.  The whole program was fantastic..if you're looking at a maymester THIS IS THE ONE!!!

great, just absolutely wonderful. engaging, funny, and extremely knowledgable. homework is all reading, two papers, i.d./essay midterm & final. do your work, go to class, and an A is easily achieved. so worth going to class though! he will just randomly pull ancient coins and pottery pieces out of his pockets. the best!
Take technical writing if you can. One of the most easiest W courses and a kind human.

Food Science: what a class. Little out of class work, but still felt like I was learning such meaningful stuff about food science and policy, and stuff I could apply in my life. We got to hear from a campus dining exec, and the perspectives of that were fascinating. An easy A, no doubt, but one that feels fun and meaningful. Snacks in class!

Easiest, most chill W class you could take. We did 5 assignments the whole semester which were all relatively easy and interesting. She gives good feedback on papers and you can revise for more points also. Easy A, would recommend to anyone. She's very involved in the CSET program which is helpful if you're interested in majoring/minoring.

Though Shellie is very sweet, I felt her class was a waste of time. I didn't learn anything that I didn't already know, and I'm not even in CSET. Her lectures were not much content and a lot of fluff. If you want a super chill class, this is definitely for you. If you want to learn something, look elsewhere.

By far the best axle and W combo. For a writing class, it felt like I never had to write. there was like 1-2 assignments that exceeded one page. She gave incredible feedback and focuses more on the scientific communication aspect rather than hammering down on punctuation or anything else you may expect a writing professor to pick out.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shellie is one of the kindest and funniest profs I've had at vandy. She is serious about preparing you to be an excellent scientist, but she understands that writing can be difficult and goes above and beyond to make the class approachable. We baked cakes and played with legos for assignments. Allows for revisions for 50% back. Superb axle class

Shellie is an absolute gem! She truly cares about students and formats her class so that larger papers/projects are earlier in the semester and you don't have to worry about this class during finals week at all! Tech writing itself is pretty boring/easy too so don't expect to learn much but it's definitely an easy A and fulfills AXLE/CSET credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The take-home midterms and homework in this class can be challenging, but Haglund wants you to do well. He has plenty of office hours and allows you to resubmit exams and homework for full credit. The final is flexible based on your strengths and interests. If you work for the A, you'll earn one. (he does low key assume that already know python)
Take a class with Professor Haglund, he is absolutely incredible and this class is very much worth it.

Prof. Haglund is a gem. He assigns lots of homework, but he sends out answer keys to all the HWs after you submit them, and you can resubmit for full credit. Achievable A if you put in the work. Cannot stress enough how passionate he is about physics and teaching. History buff, too, and a great storyteller.

Truly a great professor and human being, highly recommend taking any course with him. This course specifically was a tremendous learning experience but definitely tough. He's a great teacher that genuinely wants to help his students excel and learn.

Hands down the kindest and most intelligent professor I've met. For a FYS, though, his lectures are really niche and don't have much to do with graded assignments. You can tell that learning is his main priority and he is very accessible outside the classroom. A lovely man but not a class you can skate through. Don't think he gave anyone an A.

Professor Haglund is a great professor. Unfortunately, his lectures can be pretty tedious and the amount of papers and reading assignments he hands out are a lot to keep up with. Kind, understanding guy that will work with you and help you pass but you have to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Haglund is very devoted to his subject and is very kind. He does not mind helping people outside of class. Also, my favorite part about him is his policy on grading. Hes more about the learning aspect, so there is always a way to get a 100 on homework and your grades up on tests. The homework took a while but easy A for them in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: he grades papers harshly and doesn't give many A's. This may be skewed since this was a FYWS instead of an actual physics class, but he made it too hard for an A. Too much reading assigned and classes were long and boring.
My favorite professor at Vanderbilt. Genuinely such a nice and caring guy. Any chance you get at taking his class I would take advantage of it and enroll in it.

he is nice and his classes are just like lectures which you have to do discussion posts before hand. LIke three a week which isnt bad but just gets tedious honestly. there are a few small papers and an in class midterm but the class is interesting. easy class and also he is nice.
Dr. McGregor is the man. Simple as that. If you have the opportunity to take his course, please do. You'll thank yourself later.

Graded on discussion posts for (almost) every daily reading, midterm exam (with corrections), five film responses, one site visit. Attendance & participation really matter. Kind prof and clearly very knowledgeable, but lectures were mostly just long rambles & class almost always went over.
Best professor at vandy! Definitely take him!

Had McGregor for the CORE 1010 track and thought he was decent. He does tend to go off on long tangents that take up a lot of the class time and usually results in class running a little late. McGregor did write all our names in Arabic once, which I thought was pretty cool. The class isn't too difficult and I enjoyed the readings/discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof McGregor is a super nice guy and the class isn't a lot of work but DO NOT take it if you're a non-RLST major and actually want to learn. I took this class because I wanted to learn about the Qur'an and the description said I didn't need prior knowledge, but his lectures were so rambling and made no sense to me that I barely learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class that consisted of discussion posts that were graded on completion, a final paper, and 4 three page responses to movies that were graded easily by the TA. Don't really need to pay attention in class because there are no tests or quizzes, material is interesting and Dr. McGregor is a funny guy

Professor McGregor was my favorite teacher my first semester at Vanderbilt. A midterm, a final, and two papers--all lenient on grading and very clear with guidelines. Moreover, the content in the class is interesting, and the professor gives great lectures. A definite must take for an AXLE requirement.

I want to like McGregor so much. He's such a nice, intelligent guy, but his lectures are so insufferably dry and theoretical. That may just be me--I don't love religious studies--but I wish there were more discussions or at least engaging lectures. The grad students loved him, but after day one, I stopped paying attention in lectures completely.

This class should be in the history department because that's basically all that it focuses on. McGregor doesn't cover much theology at all, and his lectures seem to have a lot of fluff and little substance. Grading was pretty easy - just go to class once a week and attend recitation to get all the necessary info. His answers to questions are vague

The material is very interesting and the class itself is enjoyable, but I personally think the format of the class sucks. I wish he offered the chance for more grades. If you mess up on a single thing, it can ruin your grade in the entire class. Grading is not lenient either, to make up for it.

not necessary to go to class. one research paper. one project, one quiz, 2 test. test cover much material. research paper is long and boring. project is incredibly burdensome!! aside from that its easy
Dr. McGregor has been my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He's quite an excellent professor, willing to work with you, funny, and an overall cool guy. Really makes lectures worth going to.
No easy, not tough.  You can do reasonably well if you either go to class or do the reading.  Both gets a little repetitive.
His lectures are very repetitive. The key to do well on exams is to attend class. The presentation and final paper are graded pretty loosely.
very nice guy. very boring lectures. it is all about early islam not any contemporary issues, which i was unclear about when enrolling.
He's great. He's very knowledgable and he is super easy.  I like going to class!

Dr. McGregor is my cousin, and I'll tell you, he is one kick@ss guy.  He was a real rabble rouser back in the day.  He's totally cool, and he knows a lot, especially how to teach (which a lot of profs don't konw jack about).  So take any class he teaches.  Period.
contrary to what others say, he is an easy grader.  also, the class requires very little work until the end of the semester.  overall, i was satisfied.

Took intro to Islam.  He's a good teacher and a great guy.  Very funny.  You'll be intimidated for sure at first but by the end, you'll love him. Oh, and make sure to attend any halloween events that he organizes...trust me...

I love Professor McGregor.  He has an incredibly witty and dry sense of humor, is incredibly educated in his subject material, and is the MOST helpful teacher I have ever had.  He is so easy to talk to and helps his students do well, and LEARN, must take!
Intro to Islam  Very knowledgable in Islam.  Presents material fairly well.  Helpful when needed.  Harsh grader though.

Lectures were meh, but not bad.
The professor obviously cares and even added more office hours when we asked for them.
Final project wasn't too hard, but the instructions were murky.
The class could use better organization, it was often difficult to tell what info on the slides was important and what was extra.

The class consisted of weekly homework, online reading quizzes, 3 exams, and a final project. Prof. Rubinov doesn't make the class extremely difficult which is appreciated but he is a very boring lecturer. Paying attention was the hardest part of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are extremely boring. There was just one homework assignment a week, but it always took a very long time to do. Because everything was online, we had open book group tests which made getting a good grade pretty easy as long as you put some effort in. The final project was worth a lot, but it was more annoying than difficult. Average.

Dr. Rubinov is super nice and accessible outside of class! His lecture style is relatively dry, but the material is interesting enough. It was his first time teaching the class so wasn't the smoothest but got much better as time went on. Tests are similar to the homeworks. Kind of a hard grader. Group final project wasn't bad and final is optional.
Solid history professor. Knows a ton about the topic so gives really detailed lectures. Grading is ambiguous so you won't know your grade till the end really but generous with points and lenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super engaging and detailed lectures, class projects are open ended and are easy A's if you put in the work. Quizzes can be tricky but it's mostly memorization-based. She really cares about her students and knows everyone's names in class, which is a huge plus.

The course was manageable if you just put effort into projects and tests, as Professor Rogaski has a study guide that covers exactly what she'll test you on. The projects are slightly ambiguous in grading, but it's straightforward as long as you make sure she knows you've learned the content when you write the reflection.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes super sweet and understanding about needing more time to complete something! Readings are abstract and participation is crucial!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Rogaski was easily my best professor this year. Her grading is pretty lenient. She generates great discussion in class by urging everyone to participate, giving you the themes you write about in the essays. She gives amazing feedback and allows revisions! (FYI: she grades on your improvement, not the quality of writing). Take this class!
Class had quite a bit of reading but was very manageable. Loved the content of the class and she's pretty engaging with her students. Really smart and would take again!

Very sweet lady and very accessible outside of class and helpful during office hours. This class is a little difficult since it is a completely different way of viewing medicine. Also, your entire grade is based on participation, two exams, and a final, so be sure to do well on those assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rogaski really cares about her students. Even though she assigns a lot of work, if she knows you are putting in effort, she will reward you for it. She is really compassionate and wants you to learn, and her down-to-earth attitude fosters a great learning environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Rogaski is knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. She's also funny and the class was so entertaining. The projects and quizzes were not conventional at all. For quizzes we had to identify images and draw our own maps. There was no final but there were lots of projects.

Rogaski has an impressive knowledge about her subject, but I think that is what makes the class slightly difficult. She doesn't give much direction on assignments, but expects a high level of detail when grading. The same thing happens on the cumulative final, which she requires the memorization of exact dates and names of people and events.

I love Professor Rogaski as a person. She's extremely knowledgeable and helps foster meaningful discussion in the classroom. She also promotes an environment of equality (between student and professor), which is one reason I like her so much. When there are reading assignments, they're quite long, and the course material is hardly riveting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Love this prof!! Take her if you can. She's super understanding and absolutely brilliant. Her class isn't easy by any means, but she makes it as manageable as possible and is amenable to extensions. Only one actual in class exam, plus two papers and weekly short assignments. Not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Rogaski knows her stuff and is passionate about it. Don't have to read the textbook but you will get so much more out of the class if you do. She expects you to work but the class isn't difficult, expect an A- with a little effort. No tests, just projects. Take a class with her if you can, I regret not readingnot always paying attention.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Unhelpful during office hours' meetings, unfair and unclear in her grading criteria and standards, and uninteresting in terms of course content. Discussions focused on semantics and philosophy rather than actual substance; she prefers a regurgitation of powerpoints to original thinking.

Good teacher, passionate about the subject, but rambles often and is sometimes unclear.  Quizzes aren't that hard if you study powerpoints- you must know dates! She doesn't give many As though. A typical B+ class

She is a fine lecturer, but the class structure was awful.  Your TA determines your entire grade. But yet she never lets them give any input at all in class.  Also, the memorizing of pictures from slides was the basis of half the test and this was not helpful to learning. She is also very inflexible.  I would not recommend taking this class.

Professor Rogaski is a great lecturer and definitely knows the material, but your grade is determined solely by the TAs.  If there was a "ratemyTAs.com," I'd be on it writing a terrible review for them.  I don't think classes should be structured this way--her TAs try to look smart by giving her students hell.  Watch out.

Interesting class. 3 papers and 2 tests, Rogaski is easy to talk to and definitely knows her stuff, but gives very few As.  She is fair though, and her tests are not too bad if you study her powerpoints.
Memorizing pics, quotes, years, etc. is crucial. Not too hard but grade depends on TA. Try not to get Marjorie cuz she sucks!!!!!!

Rogaski is very enthusiastic about HIST 152. All assignments are weighted the same, so you can do well on the papers if you don't like her tests. Her lectures sometimes ramble, but she stays fairly clear.
No Comments

She was so great in this class everyone should take it - learned tons about China and really kept my interest.  Extremely intelligent lady who is modest about how knowledgeable she is in the area.  Always in her office and grades relatively easily on her papers - hands down my favorite class ever
No Comments

This class could not be stuctured more poorly. On the second day, she just decided to add another paper to the syllibus. Tests are tough with little notice of essay questions. Lectures are very interesting, but almost not worth the trouble of this class. Take it for CPLE, then run.
Great teacher, very helpful, and interested in her students.  If you read the assignments, and can get interested into the material, an A is pretty easy.

A very intellectual professor. Rogaski is really a great professor to have for a discussion class. She is very understanding and the important thing for her is not the due date, but that everyone understands and learns the history.
Great teacher. She's really intelligent and knows her Chinese history. A great elective class, and a rare history class without a massive amount of reading.

Expect weekly homework, but it's usually light. Extremely fair grader and the material is relatively interesting. The main downside is the heavy end-of-semester weighting—I had a midterm, project, presentation, and final all within about 9 days for this class alone.
Professor explains concepts quite clearly and concisely. Tests are somewhat very comprehensive but extremely doable. LeGoat

The class content is very manageable. Saggi is a great professor, but she does explain some concepts in a convoluted manner. If you study for your exams and go to office hours to review the homeworks, you'll be fine.
Good class and teacher, really likes the content but the tests are super comprehensive.

Not sure if Prof Rupi will teach core1010 again, but truly a wonderful teacher. Sets each student up to do their best and helps whenever anyone asks. She managed to make this writing seminar engaging and even fun.

For this writing seminar, Professor Saggi was really helpful. Although I don't know if she'll teach this class ever again, I can attest to her character as a professor. She was always accessible, willing to answer questions, and just genuinely a nice person. Do your work well and reach out to her if you need help!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Saggi was one of the best Econ professors I've had and was pretty interesting and engaging for a boring topic. The biggest issue was that I had the class MWF at 8am, but it was still well worth it to take Macro with Saggi instead of another professor. She took attendance every class, but still gave me full credit even though I missed over 3 classes
Great Econ Professor. If there's one word I would use to describe her, it would be fair. If you work hard you can get an A in her class. Plus she's super interesting.

Dr. Saggi is fantastic! Her lectures were super clear and informative and exams/quizzes were very fair. Going to class is key (you cover so much more in lectures than just the slides she posts). Study for exams and you will do well! Definitely recommend!!!

Professor Saggi was great, and I heavily recommend taking her class. Whenever I had a question, she didn't hesitate to answer in a clear manner that helped me gain a deeper understanding of the learning material. Take the quizzes seriously as they count for a good portion of your grade, and don't fall behind.

She is a very clear lecturer who cares a lot about students. Attendance is mandatory. Her tests were a bit difficult and had vague questions although she seemed to grade somewhat leniently. Probably your best option for Macro.

Prof. Saggi is def one of the best profs all around! Great lectures, accessible and helpful during office hours, and really appreciates it when you put in the work. The grading scale is also not too difficult to handle. If you can wake up for the 8am, then she's def the one!

Best Econ professor at Vanderbilt. Her course is very manageable and you will ACTUALLY learn something: it is designed so you are spending a lot of time with the material. Could not recommend her enough. She also made it so you did not have to take the final if your average was high enough which was awesome. Seriously though - shes the best.
Prof Saggi is one of the best professors I've taken. Her class is clear and as long as you attend, take notes, and ask questions/consult the textbook or the professor, you will be able to pass.
Her tests are a little hard, but still reasonable. Her lectures are very clear and informational, I did learn a lot in her class.
Really great econ Professor. Must have been a curve. She was always around to help if you need. Take her if you can.

Dr. Saggi is a gem of the econ department. Intermediate macro can be a tough class but Dr. Saggi is an amazing prof. All you have to do is pay careful attention in class and she will give you everything you need. There are ZERO surprises! Not doing well in this class simply comes down to a lack of effort because Saggi does it all! Great great prof!

Really cares about student learning and will give your grade a boost if you participated in class and otherwise demonstrated that you understand the concepts being discussed. Exams are straightforward and she allowed us to replace our final grade with test 1/2 average, which reduced a lot of the COVID-19 stress

Professor Saggi explains things very well and always brings interesting discussions on current econ topics, although the discussions are usually beyond the requirement of the class. Read the slides and you'll be fine for the tests. The textbook wasn't used AT ALL so don't buy it. This class is easy A. Solid choice!

Excellent lecturer, Class is tough - but made me actually enjoy the subject and my major as a whole. Gives excellent feedback, and is very willing to meet with students. Whoever disagrees probably didn't pay attention.

Pointless class. Truly you learn so little that is applicable, I don't understand why this class is required for the major. Saggi recommends you don't use the textbook, but herself is horrible at explaining concepts and just isn't a good lecturer. Unresponsive to emails, and just sub par. I definitely wouldn't take again.

The material isn't too hard if you can follow it as she explains it, but if you get behind, nothing will make sense. Take the quizzes seriously, since each question is half a point of your final grade. Class got curved at the end of the semester. Almost no homework, except studying.

Professor Saggi gives very good lectures- you don't need to read the textbook as her lectures cover everything on the test. Her tests are difficult but follow the lectures pretty clearly, and if you attend class it is not difficult to do well. She is very accessible and focuses on concepts instead of blind math.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Saggi's lecture are pretty top-tier - they're clear, they're concise, and they relate to the readings (which is honestly kinda supplementary). While the class is a tough, Saggi is incredibly understanding and really accessible outside of class.

ECON 3020 is definitely not an easy class. There're a lot of materials to cover. However, Prof. Saggi's lectures are so clear that you'll never get confused if you pay attention. Her exams consist of straightforward questions with difficulties ranging from medium to slightly hard. (I.e. no super easy problems) 100% the best professor for 3020.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class isn't hard, and you really need to work for your grade. Although Prof Saggi is a tough grader, she's a fair one. Bi-weekly quizzes make up a fair portion of your grade, so I would recommend taking them very seriously (do the practice questions ahead of time). Her lectures are very clear and detailed, very great professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Intermediate Macro Theory was such a great class with Prof. Saggi.  The way she lectures is so clear, explaining every piece and how it fits into the bigger picture.  Also she's engaging - lots of chances for your participation by answering and asking questions in class.  Very approachable and intelligent professor.

Professor Ruppi is the best of the worst when it comes to Intermediate Macro. Her lecture style is fairly clear, albeit a little mundane, and if you take good notes, you should be good.   Quizzes are worth a decent amount (4%), so between that and the exams, there's definitely a lot of studying going on. DO THE PRACTICE PROBLEMS!!!

Like all upper level econ classes, this class is tough, but I learned so much about the foreign exchange market, exchange rate crises, and the IS-LM-FX model. If you go to class and understand the homework (which you should spend a lot of time on), you should do fine on the tests. Exams are very straightforward. Don't procrastinate on the papers.

No matter who you take for Maco at Vandy, it's going to be difficult, but I'd say Saggi is your best bet. Quizzes, despite being only 4-8 questions, are heavily weighted towards your final grade, so take those seriously! Missing lectures will set you back. There's always a couple questions on her test that challenge you, but she's a fair grader.

The key source of information in this class are Prof. Saggi's lectures, so if you miss even one occasionally, you'll fall behind significantly.  Tests were mostly straightforward and fair, quizzes can be tough.  Attendance counts.  Nice woman.  Sometimes her method feels a little too mechanical for me.  Do practice problems! Solid option for macro.

Very organized professor. Just three non-cumulative tests, which are generally straightforward. Quizzes are fine too. Some questions can be tricky, so make sure you do *every* practice question posted on Blackboard. Helpful during office hours. Take her!

I thought this class was difficult. Tests were not extremely difficult, but there is no scale in the class. Saggi writes a lot on the board which is good, but she doesn't go over the most difficult scenarios that she puts on the tests, nor are they in the book. Not a huge fan, but she is better than other Vandy econ professors. Attendance is taken.

Saggi has been my favorite professor so far. Her lectures are very interesting, and she is more than willing to stop and explain something if you need her to. Her grading is straight forward , and she gives lots of partial credit. Depending on how good of a note taker you are, you may need to supplement her lectures with the test book. Awesome prof

Really clear lectures, and puts everything on the board. Incredibly helpful during office hours. That being said, the material in this course was pretty difficult, and not something you can easily cram for in a night. No final exam, though; had a group project/presentation instead. Curved the class at the end.
She's really really helpful and if you put even a little bit of effort, you'll get a lot out of the class

Econ 232 will be hard no matter who you take it with. However, Saggi is definitely the easiest of all the options. She is also incredibly clear and teaches straight from the textbook. I highly recommend that Econ major take her. Great lady too!

Great lecturer. Fair grader on tests, which will be of medium to hard difficulty. Tests are similar to problem sets and in-class lectures, as well as the textbook. Probably should read the textbook before you going to class for best results! Overall, definitely a great teacher.

Best econ professor I've had; also learned more in this class than any other. Exceptionally clear in lecture, goes over everything multiple times, and very helpful in office hours. Material is difficult, but she teaches it well. Key to class is doing practice problems and going to her office hours to ask about questions that you're unsure about.

Not as bad as intermediate macro can get. Even though Saggi is not the most interesting lecturer, she is crystal and will go over concepts multiple times before moving on. However, test are still hard and I found them more lecture driven than textbook driven. Make sure you go to class!

Tough class. As are possible but extremely difficult to obtain, Bs more common, Cs possible if you don't do the practice problems/don't study/don't show up to class (which is mandatory btw). Overall, decent professor.
Not hard, quizzes arent bad. Attendance is mandatory unfortunately.
The final is ridiculously hard! It can totally change your grade in this class. She is helpful if you go ask her question.
I thought this was supposed to be an easier lower level elective. Definitely NOT!

Class is mostly composed of two tests- the midterm and the final, worth 36% of your total grade. She is clear, and her class really stick to the book which helps for studying and makes attendance less necessary

Funny, caring professor. This is a good course if you are willing to put in the work. There is homework after every class, which is pretty easy and really just for participation. Quizzes every week or two but Saliba is very straightforward with his expectations. If you do the work and pay attention in class, you will get an A

I do not recommend taking this class. Lots of reading which is every single day. The rough drafts are the same weight as the final draft, and the guidelines for each paper consist of about 3 sentences, then proceeds to grill you on his feedback. Even when you listen to the edits your grade will barely change. Lectures are also quite slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great teacher for 1101 or 1102. Very clear cut expectations. Fun to talk to. There's some busy work, but that is uniform throughout the department and does help your German. No reason you shouldn't get an A if you want it.

Saliba is very academic. Had to read lots of books and stories. Usually I BS my way through these kind of classes by not reading the books but that came back and bit me in the end. Had to write a 4 papers (5 pages, 8 pages, 12 pages, and 14 pages). The last two papers were due like 1 week apart (during finals week). Lectures were not stimulating.

Professor Saliba is awesome. The course content is super interesting and he presents it in a way that doesn't make it seem like droning on about facts and numbers. The course revolves a lot around comparing the content to the modern day and while there is a lot of writing, it's not overbearing. He's a tough grader, but my German is better from it.
A great professor for GER1101. Really invested in student's growth and learning, and class was easy but with lots of busy work for HW. Enjoyable as a professor and as a person!

PostDoc lacking pedagogical experience. Class is insane amount of work for an introductory writing class.  4 major PhD level research papers and homework. "Rough drafts" are graded like the final paper. Super tough grading. Comments on papers are highly offensive and grading seems totally subjective. If you don't agree with him, good luck. Run ...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment:
For 2610
-Amount of HW is ridiculous
-Exams are 1.5x longer than any but a genius could finish; he grades harshly w/ little to no curve
-Take ANY other prof because altho he's a nice guy in class / solid lecturer, he WILL tank your gpa
-Only got B- bc he procrastinated grading and threw in stuff as 100s bc he didn't have time to grade at the end!!
He struggled to lecture. Focused only on profs and was not accessible as a teacher.

Very friendly, very nice, willing to slow down lecture to answer clarification questions.Tough on grading hw but he gives decent feedback and is willing to reteach class materials during office hours. The downside is that he doesn't always respond to emails

Other reviews said too critically about him. This is his first time so the guy is trying to learn how to better teach. The tests and homework are long and cover more than most other sections, and he grade harshly but give extra credits for take again. Wouldn't have gotten an A if not for those Test Agains

The hws did take time to do but there were only 4 in total for each midterm. Strict with grading but there are given reasons for each deduction. Participation was not required but TA does keep track of it. You can tell he likes teaching and he adjusted to more problem-based lectures after students asked. OH and review sessions helped a bunch.

BS grader, taking half the point of a question even if it is correct with adequate work shown. Doesn't answer question about textbook exercise outside of petty suggested exercises. Lecture are proof only and some homework problems is completely irrelevant to the test(which he introduces new questions that you never seen before).

Hardest and worst class ever taken, he focus on proof that is not on the exams and all of his midterms contains more content than other professors. Unwise time management in class so students have to learn all on their own after class. He always try to say "put on your thinking cap for every mid-terms" that only helps to screw you over.

He is trying his best to fix his way of teaching since he is new here, but like all other poorly rated professor, he focus too much on proof and not many example in class. Even when he does example, he demands a lot in response so he can find any reasons to take point off from your exam. HW is also graded harshly and can be pretty long.

Honestly, I survived the class just reading the textbook, taking notes around the chapter guides he uploads, and memorizing those notes. Some things on the test are minimally mentioned on his slides but covered in the textbook notes, which were helpful. Interesting topics but boring approach to lecturing. I liked the market simulation though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pro: concepts are easy to grasp, slides and chapter guides are uploaded online and there isn't really anything else you need to review but those, kind to students (the type of prof who learns everyone's name in a big class) Con: boring, marketing simulation game is annoying, tricky multiple choice on tests, must do marketing studies

Terrible prof. Doesn't know material well and stutters and monotone. Tests are unrelated to what is taught in class. Unclear grading criteria. Required to do a market simulation but doesn't talk about it (grade based on performance). Office hours are unhelpful.
I was uber excited to take a marketing class as it is the most creative course of the Business Minor. However, I was bored out of my mind the entire class due to the dry, monotone lectures given
Very unclear about grading criteria, but does try to help students out and wants the best for them. Not an engaging lecturer at all, you will be bored throughout class.
Amazing Professor! He really cares that you do well in the class.
Amazing guy, great teacher.
Ryan is an amazing teacher. He's a funny guy and knows his math. Take his class.

Attendance for lecture was about 10 of 55 students, except on quiz days when everyone would show up at the start of class and then promptly leave thereafter. Extraordinary difficulty in understanding English; questions need to be repeated ten times but often to no avail. Once asked a student "Are you paying attention?" in the middle of class.
I genuinally believe that this man tries and wants to be a good teacher. However, just as I can want to get a 100 % on my orgo exam but fail miserably with a 32 %, so can professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dude sucks. His English is hard to understand, but worse than that, he's just a terrible teacher. Went to office hours thinking one on one would be more helpful. It wasn't. He was condescending, and couldn't understand why I didn't understand the problems, telling me it was, "trivial." Lectures are useless, HW heavy. Read the book.

Schaefer thinks he's so much better than other people. His lectures are really confusing and disorganized and he doesn't seem to respond to feedback when students complain because they're confused. take this class from someone else

Took this class electively, for a psych class it was hard because the slide decks were a little disorganized. Best bet is to cram for the first 2 exams 2-3 days before. The final was also harder then the first 2 exams, so for that one I would study unit 3 earlier. The 25 cumulative are hardest of the semester, so ask him their structure early.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Schaefer is very knowledgable, which came across during his lectures. Abnormal covers a lot of material, since it is an introductory course to this subfield, so tests were quite dense. The group project was a little confusing as well. Still, this has been my favorite class, as it challenged me as a learner. Also, Dr. S is very kind but fair.

Dr. Schaefer is a knowledgeable and kind professor. I found that attending class regularly was helpful for understanding the material. Exams were challenging due to dense material, but manageable. There was a group project with multiple components that was introduced late in the semester, making the workload heavier alongside the final exam.

This guy is so self obsessed! He doesn't seem very knowledgeable on the topic but is so confident. I should have taken the class from the other professor. huge mistake. I went into this class thinking it would be my favorite but I didn't learn as much as I thought I would

Type of guy I would grab a beer with and discuss the Lieber Code for hours (and would enjoy). Complete flexibility to write on a topic of your choice (making the research process all the more fun). I will say, he rarely gives over a 93.

EUS 2204 --> Prof Schmidt is certainly a passionate professor for the topic but fell short of expectations in this course. The class is based on four assignments (3 of which are papers) and participation. Grading feedback is sparse and does not give much direction or instruction at all in his assignments. Homework consist of long & dense readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schmidt was unfortunately disappointing. His standards for writing assignments are pretty vague, and he intentionally does not give a lot of helpful feedback during the paper-writing process, which is definitely frustrating when I get a disappointing grade back. Additionally, homework is super long and difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are great, super engaging prof and really cares about the subject matter. If you do the readings, class will be awesome. Graded on 4 papers and a presentation, kinda tough grader but if you pay attention and do the readings its not hard to get an a
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schmidt was honestly a great professor—very knowledgeable, interesting, and humorous. Nonetheless, the lectures can be a little boring sometimes. If you participate and write like those history reviews online, you will do just fine.
Professor Schmidt was funny and the class was not difficult at all. At times the lecture did not follow the topic of reading and was a bit disorganized, but was overall a great class!

The class was fairly interesting. Grade is def on me I used this class as a study hall lol. Although I do think the paper grading was a little demanding. Also this guy does not answer his emails??? Ever? Has a strict attendance policy but minimal communication back when you have to miss, never answered my questions abt the final... but overall fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've taken multiple classes with Schmidt and he is great - so knowledgable and passionate about European history, and provides really great feedback. Grade is made up of 4 short papers and weekly discussion posts, and his lectures are informative and interesting. Great prof and really caring, witty guy! He has some good stories too!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Schmidt has an incredible depth of knowledge about an wide range of topics in European history and philosophy. In HIST 2760 he does an excellent job of tying these concepts together to give you an excellent understanding of the evolution of the Western legal system. He also has a good sense of humor and is very helpful outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Schmidt is a knowledgeable, understanding, and kind professor. His class centers around a lecture, but he also encourages student participation and comments throughout. The readings are interesting, and his lectures thoroughly add to them. I have taken two of his classes and I would take more.

Professor Schmidt is an absolute gem! I took Idea of Europe with him and he is SO incredibly knowledgeable and excited about all of the topics. He is accessible outside of class and wants to see students succeed - really interesting course material and thought provoking assignments. Lectures were really great, loved the class. Schmidt is a must!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Schmidt is a very nice guy and clearly loves history. The class is relatively easy: 2 short papers, one long paper, and a weekly discussion post. He lectures for basically all of class and it's not the most engaging, but it's fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Schmidt is incredibly knowledgable; however, that knowledge doesn't translate to particularly helpful classes. He often regurgitates prior readings and doesn't allow for any student involvement, making it very hard to stay interested in an otherwise compelling topic.

Schmidt is the best; he's a visiting professor from Germany and is the epitome of an intellectual. Class is all lectures, where it's clear he is passionate about what he studies, I also took EUS2220, and grades are based on weekly discussion posts, 2 short essays, and a final essay; He is a very fair grader and so compassionate. Highly recommend!!!

I am a humanities student who avoids science courses due to disinterest, but Professor Scherrer made physics one of my favorite courses taken at Vandy. He's a kind and hilarious man who takes a variety of complicated topics and makes them easily understandable. Simple, straightforward exams that are based entirely on the content of the homework.
easiest class i have ever taken.

What you put into 1020 is what you get out of it. It is an easy class, but you will actually learn a lot of interesting and important things if you go to class. Scherrer is very funny and it is easy to see that he really cares about the material he covers. 100% take this class.
Only went to class for the 2 midterms and final. Class is super easy and professor is adorable older man.

PHYS 2290: One of the best lecturers I have had in the physics department by far. Homeworks are difficult but he is responds to emails very quickly and has  frequent office hours. Exams make up 80% of your grade but were pretty simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PHYS 1020 is a phenomenal choice for non STEM people needing to get AXLE/Liberal Arts credits out of the way. 80% of your grade is based on in-class exams, but they weren't too challenging if you took decent notes. Dr. Scherrer really knows his stuff and comes across as very nice (if not a little eccentric). Definitely recommend!

I absolutely loved Dr. Scherrer and could not recommend this class enough. I am not a STEM person, but this class was incredibly interesting. The tests were easy if you paid attention in class, and the homework was graded Pass/Fail (you get 100% if you get 60% of the Qs correct). He is so sweet and funny; I think everyone should take his class!

"Physics for Future Leaders" is one of the easiest science courses at Vandy, but it's still pretty enjoyable. Dr. Scherrer is super quirky but also incredibly knowledgeable about the subject. Test questions are entirely from lectures/homework. The final being 40% of the grade was a little annoying, but it was still manageable. Take him if you can!

Professor Scherrer is a phenomenal lecturer. No one really went to class, but they really should have! There are three exams that are closed-note and then 8 HWs that are open-note. The lab portion is a lot harder than the lecture, but they're still experimenting with how the lab should be. I think it's the easiest MNS+Lab to take for AXLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is easy, but mind-numbing. He expects nothing out of his students, which sounds great but actually feels like a waste of time. Would not retake.
