1020 was such a fun class! All of Scherrer's lectures were really interesting and engaging. All tests (including final) were multiple choice and open-note and there were a few homework assignments that were open-note as well. Attendance was optional and Scherrer doesn't expect much at all out of students. Super easy MNS class with no lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you go to class and take good notes this class is easy. Make sure you take notes because everything he talks about is in the exams.
Professor Scherrer gives amazing lectures and is very knowledgeable on the topic he teaches! As long as you pay attention in class you would have no problem on the homework and tests.

His lectures were pretty much copy and paste from the textbook so most of the class stopped coming by the end of the semester because we they probably got more out of reading it themselves. I know he wasn't the lead for this class so he was limited on what he could do, but printing out notes or giving us more examples would've helped so much more.

Dr. Sehayek is an amazing Calc 2 professor. His lectures are very well structured, and he post all his notes at the end of each week. The class is pretty difficult, and your class grade comes mostly from the exams. Dr. Sehayek prepares his students well for the exams and in his office hours he gives good hints of what will be in the exam.
Great professor. Lectures well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture is important, but he uploads his own notes. Good about taking questions and answering them well. Sometimes exam questions are a little out of left field. He's a nice guy, he really wants his students to like him. Hard to go wrong for a math class.
One of the best math professors I've ever had. Go to office hours.

It is quite astounding to think that this is only his second year as a professor, but Sehayek did a great job teaching 1200. He elucidates concepts well, his notes are organized and accessible, and he is a good lecturer too. He will improve even more throughout his career, I'm certain.
Great lecturer, highly recommend

Professor Sehayek's lectures were extremely detailed and organized (uploaded notes after class), and he did a great job explaining confusing concepts. The content of the class can be difficult, but he does a good job preparing you for the exams and is very accessible during office hours. He cares about his students and wants to see them succeed.

He is a good professor and tries his best to help as much as he can but it sometimes does feel that he makes relatively easy concepts a lot harder with his explanations. He is certainly better at office hours and I would 100% recommend going to them especially since he gives you hints of what will be on the exam.

Great teacher all around, super smart guy. Lectures are his own notes, very useful and guided by the students. Very reachable through office hours and is very clear at explaining expectations and concepts, go to them! Also gives so much help and wants to see his students do well in class, honestly one of the big reasons why i scored well.

He explains things so clearly and is a math genius who can explain any concept at whatever level you need. Although the difficulty of the content of this class is debatable, it's irrefutable that Sahayek makes it as easy as possible. He will reveal multiple test questions during class and office hours, and is very accessible and caring.
Good at explaining things. Found class very easy and, if anything, he would spend too much time explaining things. However, I have done similar content before.

No way I could have succeeded in this class without Dr. Sehayek. Love that he uploads his course notes and they are actually useful. Exams were tough but fair. Go to his office hours. Clearly cares about his students.

Really like his teaching style. He made the topics in class very accessible and his office hours were extremely useful. He is always willing to help if you need it and give you tips and tricks, just ask!

there was literally no reason for me to do poorly in this class other than i stopped going to class mid way through semester and my 2nd test grade reflected it. tests were not hard. if u went to class. allowed to bring a flash card into every exam and a full sheet of paper into final. i just hate math but he was pretty easy tbh

I took Sehayek's Calc I class in his first semester teaching at Vanderbilt. In my opinion, his lectures overcomplicated the concepts, but he made up for it by being available outside of class. He genuinely is a good guy and cares about his students. I think he will become a stronger teacher as he becomes a more seasoned professor.
Very good lecturer and also a nice guy
His lectures are as interesting as they can be for 1301, and he does a good job teaching the topics. The homeworks are 'optional' but if you dont do them you will struggle.

Best math teacher I've ever had. Anyone saying anything negative is saying something negative about the department criteria which he has to follow. He genuinely wants you to do well. SUPER smart guy too. Great teacher.
Amazing teacher. Works really well with what the department gives him. He's also super available outside of class. Nothing bad to say. One of the best math teacher's I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I thought Professor Sehayek was a great teacher and got unnecessary hate from some students. Most people just love Jacob Haley so they take any other professor as not good enough but he is actually a great teacher.

Sam overall did a good job of teaching the calculus content in an easy-to-understand manner. Completing all the homework problems and asking him questions in office hours is key to reinforcing the content, but his lectures were strong too. He is chill as well so it never felt stressful. The content is inherently tough but doing well is possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The cirriculum in this class is distributed in an overcomplicated manner that makes simple calculus topics much more difficult than needed. The professor seemed to dislike when repeat questions or clarification questions were asked but nonetheless often encouraged office hours. He is much better at teaching in a one-on-one, office hour environment.

Very caring and supportive professor. Lots of "optional" ungraded homework but is essential to complete if you want a good grade in the class. An A is definitely possible, I just dropped the ball on some of the homework. Professor Sam is a good lecturer and encourages everyone to go to office hours. Prepares you well for exams, just work hard
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had Professor Schade for CORE-1010 and she was extremely helpful. she facilitated class discussions limiting any awkwardness. Her comments are very useful and she is always very flexible with meeting times. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Schade very much encourages participation and cares about attendence and tardiness. As long as you are timely and engaged, you are set for a good grade.

Dr. Schade is amazing. German is a difficult language to learn but she makes it easy. The class itself is not hard -- she's an easy grader, which means you basically get out what you put in and the more you practice German, the more you'll learn.
She is truly the kindest person and makes learning a language so much more fun and attainable

Dr. Schade is a fantastic professor to take! She understands the challenging nature of German and puts a lot of effort into ensuring students understand the material. On grading she is very accommodating and allows resubmits for improvements. The class is focused a lot on media productions (good if you like the arts) but the work was manageable.

Although this class consists of plenty of homework everyday, overall grading is quite easygoing. Students can learn German language without worrying about their grades. She is caring and accommodating, and it will be a breeze if you do the homework. Highly recommended!

She's such a nice professor and even though German is a difficult language for English speakers, she makes the grammar pretty easy to understand and it's easy to ask questions in class. Would highly recommend.

Schade is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. Extremely kind, prioritizes learning over teaching you a lesson with your grade. If you show up to every class and submit every assignment on time you're basically guaranteed an A

Dr. Schade is amazing. I have been in her class for two semesters now and I could not recommend her any more highly. She understands the difficulty of learning a new language and thus is very understanding of students' struggles and mistakes. She is also very flexible when it comes to students turning in work late.

I have had Professor Schade for two semesters, and have really enjoyed her classes. She is very understanding of other obligations and lenient on late work / missing class on occasion. Grades are based off of attendance / participation, a few presentations, homework, and exams. Overall an easy and enjoyable class!

Dr. Schade is fabulous and truly is an amazing choice for learning a second language. She will never make you feel embarrassed or judged for making mistakes, and is very helpful with noticing common errors of each student and helping to work through them. This course is very fun, and you read a full-length drama at the end of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Schade is a wonderful professor! This class isn't really about learning vocab or grammar so I'd caution you to take a lower level if you aren't as comfortable with the language in context. The class is really interesting, as you'll learn about pieces of German history in German. There is definitely a decent amount of homework but an easy A.

Dr. Schade cares a lot about helping students learn German. At the start of the semester there was a lot of homework assigned, but after some feedback the load was lessened. Engaging with the homework is key to contributing to the discussions, even if they are on Zoom. Maybe two hours of homework between sessions. Overall, very helpful.

Doc. Schade is a very nice and caring professor, and was amazing for GER 1101. Highly recommended. There is daily homework, but it isn't hard to keep up with. As long as you pay attention you can easily succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: German Fairy Tales is such a fun, interesting class you should take if you get the chance! Prof Schade is sweet, cares about students and you get to read fairy tales and watch Disney movies for homework. Definitely try to enroll in her discussion section because she's an easy grader. Read the fairy tales, show up to discussion and you'll get an A

I loved taking German Fairy Tales! Professor Schade was so sweet and welcoming I am now considering a German minor just so I can take more classes with her. I loved that we got to write our own fairy tales as a final project. There is a midterm and final exam. Both are written but very straight-forward. If you do the readings, you will get an A!

You learn a lot about fairy tales, and lectures are pretty interesting. Reading tales for homework is honestly stress-relieving. Attendance is mandatory, but not a lot of people pay attention. All assignments are easy and the final project is fun, but your grade will be decided by the TA.

Dr. Schade is an amazing professor and woman. She is the reason I am continuing German next year. I would highly suggest taking her if you are searching for an understanding, respected, and interesting professor.

Great Prof. Had her for ger1102, taking her again for intermediate. super caring woman, will check on you if you start missing class. offers lots of extra credit, and will forgive you if you miss a hw or two. tests are super straightforward, and she'll review everything before. theres hw every class, but its all completion based. love her!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is easy to pass! Most of the fairy tales you can look up online, so no books are essential. Everything on the two midterms are discussed in class and were open note. Those and a final project are the only grades. Definitely take this class for an easy International Cultures credit. Who wouldn't want to read fairy tales for homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Schwarz was my favorite professor of the semester!! She is absolutely brilliant and her lectures reflect her intelligence, passion, and love for her work. She is so excited about the topic and she makes students feel excited. She is incredibly kind and invested in student learning, writing pages of kind and helpful feedback for each student.

Took Schwarz's semester version of Shakespeare last fall and cannot recommend enough! Part of the reason I chose to become an English major. There was a lot of reading (10 plays), but the interesting and entertaining class discussions made it all worth it. Also, her essay feedback was out of this world. Incredibly thorough and helpful. Must take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I came into Shakespeare dreading it, and left loving it. Dr. Schwarz helped me understand Shakespeare in an engaging way, and through her extremely detailed feedback I grew as a writer and presenter. Be engaged in her class and you will leave with so much knowledge and a grasp on how to read Shakespeare. I highly recommend taking her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very interesting lectures and discussion. Overall, a really great class.

I had Dr. Schwarz for Women Who Kill. There was a lot of reading, but she mostly split it up to where we only had to read parts for each class. Her lectures, which are more like conversations, were absolutely phenomenal. She was incredibly considerate for sickness and interview related absences, and she gives AMAZING feedback. I would take her 100x
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Schwarz is one of the most intelligent professors I've ever had. Her expertise in Renaissance drama is clear, and she welcomes and values all students' opinions. Her essay feedback is also incredibly detailed and helpful. She's such a caring person, has a great sense of humor, and is helpful outside of class. Manageable expectations too!

Best English Prof I've had at Vanderbilt - she's so chill and wise - very comforting. I'm bad at literature analysis - but it gets much easier once I talk to her. Def take her - fair work load, fair grading, and she's super accessible whenever you need. Class is super interesting! Makes Shakespeare a fun read.

Prof. Schwarz practically radiates knowledge and expertise on the topics that she teaches. Sometimes that can be an issue with professors, but with Schwarz, it just makes class cool, interesting, and fun - she never talks over your head. She assigns a fair amount of work and is also just a really nice person.

One of the best profs at Vandy! Her lectures are amazing and the discussion in her class was always really thought-provoking. Totally changed my thinking on Shakespeare and theater. Would definitely take again.

Schwarz is the BEST! So kind, intelligent and comforting - she really makes you feel comfortable and confident participating. She's super knowledgeable and approachable, which is rare for someone as articulate and brilliant as she is. Assigns a lot of reading which is followed by reading quizzes, but they're doable! LOVE HER! Def take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Schwarz is hands down my favorite professor in the Vanderbilt English department. Not only is she brilliant and more eloquent than you thought a person could be, but she is warm and charming and always has something interesting to say. Her class discussions are always amazing and she really helps you develop as a write and thinker. MUST TAKE!

She is extremely knowledgeable and nice.  One of the only classes I learned something in.  Her lectures are filled with depth and understanding.  Very nice.  The only thing is that you have to speak up or else just be allowed to be quiet all semester.

(Shakespeare in Culture) The class was very interesting to me. If you have an interest in Shakespeare you won't be bored.  3 papers, attendance, and a few assignments along the way.  She is very helpful and knowledgable!

(Shakespeare Sexuality).  Very nice, but would really be much more interesting if she spoke up.  She obviously has a passion for what she teaches, she just doesn't convey it very well.  Lots of reading, but other than that nothing insanely difficult.  You have to go to class!

she is a really nice lady, and a great help if you go to her in office hours. she is very, very intelligent and expects a lot from students' papers. reading quizzes every time reading is assigned (a lot), but she'll drop the lowest one. i'd recommend her; she's really passionate about renaissance drama. :)

(Renaissance Revenge Tragedy): Brilliant lectures, interactive discussions, great class design, great readings. If you don't like Renaissance-era readings, stay away, but otherwise, a surprising must-take teacher.
Extraordinary! Brilliant! Certainly the most eloquent, and perhaps most intelligent, literature professor I've encountered at Vanderbilt. She's the best!!!
No Comments
She's brilliant.  Wonderful class discussions in normally small classes (around 15 people).  You'll learn more than you thought possible.  Her topics are fun - she makes the Reniassance interesing!

Such an amazing professor! Prof Sergio creates a warm and welcoming environment in class. She's super funny and cares for everyone. There is daily homework, but it shouldn't take longer than 30 minutes. Quizzes and exams are very doable, as she gives you a study guide that prepares you. Had so much fun and made new friends in this class- 10/10!

Elena Sergio was hands down the best teacher I've had at Vanderbilt. I don't ever leave reviews on Rate My Professor, but I felt I had to after taking her class. Can't recommend her enough to any student who has to fulfill the language requirements or is interested in Italian. I can't imagine taking a different language with a different professor.

great prof who wants you to do well. 2 or 3 exams. some quizzes. lots of VHL homework but its relatively easy. the entire language department really cares about you doing well. dont worry. better than spanish
Dr. Sergio is so sweet and she cares a lot about her students. Make sure you stay on top of VHL homework because it's an easy grade booster - quizzes and exams aren't horrible if you study.
She is awesome. Take her class. Show up on time with a good attitude and study and you will get an A.
This was an easy class and Sergio is very nice

I only took Italian because the Spanish classes were full and I needed a foreign language, but I'm so glad I took this course with Dr. Sergio. This is the most fun I've had in a college course while still learning and appreciating the material.

I LOVE professor Sergio. She made learning a new language so easy and fun! Lots of quizzes but that provides more wiggle room for mess ups/learning. She's incredibly caring, put together, helpful, and so efficient with class time. Loved the way the class was taught. Take her!!!
Great class and great professor!
One of the kindest and most helpful professors ever. Just show up and do the work and its a guaranteed A.
Easy to get a good grade if you put in a little bit of work each day! She is kind and cares about Italian.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Elena is truly a gem. If you have the chance to take her for Italian, definitely do! She's super clear about her expectations for assignments and grades extremely generously. She's an extremely talented educator as well -- really good at what she does. Highly recommend her.

I took her as my second language class here at Vanderbilt, French was my first language course at this school, and of all the professors I have met, even the ones outside of the language department, Sergio is the best professor. It is an easy class if you are willing to learn because Sergio supports you so well, even on an individual level. 100/10

An incredible Italian professor!!! Really takes the time to hone in on each concept - I leave class each day feeling like I learned a lot. Quizzes and tests have been easy because she prepares us so well for them. The class is well-balanced, with good focus on both grammatical and conversational aspects. She is understanding and a speedy grader!

Core 1010. Professor Selcke is one of the most caring professors I have ever met and her personal anecdotes are very entertaining. Some of the readings for this course were long and dense but nothing unmanageable. Grades take a while to get back but has good feedback. Wants everyone to succeed.

SELCKE IS THE GOAT! SHE IS SO FUNNY. TAKE HER CLASS PLEASE IT WAS SO GOOD. She's also really smart and knowledgeable. she always responds to emails and encourages us to send her rough drafts for feedback.
Excellent choice for first-year writing seminar. Gives excellent feedback on writing, and is super helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Selke is ICONIC! I took her class as an 8 A.M, but honestly getting up for the class was not difficult because I knew the material would be engaging and she is a great lecturer. Be prepared for heavier reading (that is very interesting) and somewhat longer exams (not that bad if you study). I recommend to anyone- no matter what you're major is!

Professor Selcke wants all of her students to succeed. She is very understanding and funny. The course consists of reading assignments and questions before each class (these can be time-consuming), 3 quizzes, a midterm, a presentation, and a final. If you do the study guides before quizzes/tests you should be fine! Definitely not a punitive class

There is a lot of reading but they are easy and interesting reads, totally worth it for the insightful discussions. Prof. selcke truly cares about her students and Wants to see them succeed. * super funny

I absolutely loved Professor Selcke! She is super supportive and wants her students to succeed. There were a lot of reading and reading questions, but most of the readings are interesting. There were also 3 quizzes, midterm, final, and final presentation (just 5 slides). Highly recommend if you are, or even aren't, interested in Latinx studies!

I absolutely LOVED this class. Professor Selcke inspired an interest in Latin Studies that I never knew I had. Reading questions are due every class but they're easy to get full credit, 3 papers and a final paper. You will read such great books, and she is so helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taking this class was such an amazing experience. You get to read some awesome books and engage in really interesting discussions, and Dr. Selcke brings so much insight to the table. There's usually a good amount of reading per class, so make sure to carve out some time for reading since you have to answer some questions before every class. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Learned so much and she's so down to earth and helpful. I'm minoring in Latino/a studies in large part because of how much I love this class. You have reading journals due every class but as long as you do the readings, the journals are an easy 100%. She really just wants you to learn from and enjoy her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Selcke is super funny and sweet. She may seem intimidating at first but if you talk to her, she's always willing to help and support you in any way possible. (ex. essay extensions!) The class has a LOT of reading but if you're interested in latinx studies or you like reading memoirs, it shouldn't be too bad. Overall good class for FYS credit!

I took professor Selcke's first year writing seminar and it wasn't too shabby. Readings and questions before every class and three papers plus a research paper final. Tough grader on papers but great lecturer. Don't hesitate to ask any questions as she seems scary at first but you learn she is very helpful and understanding.

Professor is very unclear about expectations in this class and the class content. When I registered for the class, it was called: "Feminist Fictions." 1 month into the class, the title has been changed to "Feminist Fictions: Politics and Fabrication in the Work of Toni Morrison." None of the authors listed in course description are covered.

As someone taking bio and orgo together, this class made me less stressed about fitting in my W course requirement. She's so chill. If you want to learn something interesting about society and improve your writing simultaneously... she's good. Everything is run in a writing workshop manner, so you gain better writing skills; guaranteed an A.

I really enjoyed this class and professor Threadcraft really engages with her students. I didn't do the readings and barely participated but I liked listening to the discussions during class. She's super nice and encouraging but there was a lot of trial and error throughout the class, which I didn't mind. Not a super structured class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: - assigns lots of reading that nobody does - whole grade was based on 2 assignments: 1 group proj, 1 lit review - lit review had two sentences of instruction - does not answer emails - did not learn anything - easy A - nice person but doesn't seem like she actually cares about teaching / doesn't want to put much effort into grading

There were two to three readings for each class, and she went through the lectures very very quickly. Very heavy topics discussed in class, and she is a little judge about your answers, but listens to all opinions. Only two grades all semester: midterm lit review and final project. She is compassionate and often did what was best for us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Threadcraft is super nice and does not grade harshly. Papers are a big chunk of your grade, but you'll be fine with fairly minimal effort. Attendance is part of your grade; classes are always discussions of readings so the reading is kinda "mandatory" if you don't wanna look like a dumbass. Take for credit but don't expect anything too exciting.

I had her this semester and she really went out of her way to help me. When I was dealing with some stuff, she didn't just ignore it—she took the time to talk with me and helped me find campus support. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Would definitely recommend.

Compared to other CORE 1010 professors, she held boring classes, and she tended to lead the class discussion in a specific way, and treated other thoughts outside of it as "wrong". She was also very unclear about her expectations. She approved my thesis statement for my paper then later printed it out for the whole class to revise. Not a fan.
She doesn't care about the class or students, and will form quick judgments on you based on how much she likes you. Do not take her core class.

Took her class with Professor Greble and it was one of the best classes I've taken at Vanderbilt. Their dynamic is great and class discussions were always a blast, especially since the content/readings were always super interesting. Gives great feedback on assignments and grades pretty easily as long as you put effort into it. Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Schachter is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. I went from casually attending class to genuinely caring about the subject because of her passion. She grades fairly and genuinely wants you to succeed. JS 2260 was one of my favorite classes I've taken at Vanderbilt, easy.

I really enjoyed reading the various coming of age stories in the class, especially the novels and short stories. The final project opened up my understanding of my own family history and my Jewish identity. Great class!
Just don't take her class. She will give you much unnecessary stress.

Allison is not a BAD professor, but she is definitely not the nicest or most welcoming person. She wasn't a harsh grader, and the readings were actually quite interesting, but she did not interact well with class participation and discussion rarely went beyond surface level. I never felt inspired or eager to engage in further research after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Revolutionary Awakenings is a life-changing class thanks to Professor Schachter. You'll spend many long nights doing the readings and writing response papers, but it's all worth the super interesting class discussions that really change the way you think. She's a really tough grader on papers but is super passionate about her students' success.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was an awesome class and awesome professor!

Not sure if she was so awful because she was dealing with a newborn baby at home... but literally most disinterested, disengaged, unhelpful professor ever. Would look around the room as students talked. Office hours felt pointless. I regret taking this course.
A great course! Professor Schachter really cares about  students. She actually wants you to do well.

A really great professor. You can't get away with not reading the material so don't even try. However, the assigned readings are interesting and you learn a lot from the discussions. She's obviously passionate about English and is just a nice person in general. Her classes seem to go by quickly even though they're over an hour.
One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Extremely helpful outside of class. Good in facilitating discussion.

There's no question that Dr. Schachter's classes are challenging, but that's why I took them. This class was so interesting, really well thought out and brought so up so much. Students who come unprepared are sure to be put off by the demands of the course, but I loved it!

I was excited to take this class but was horribly disappointed. It was one of the worst I have taken at Vanderbilt. She is a harsh grader, often changed the syllabus, treated students like middle schoolers, and never really came to a conclusion about anything we discussed in class. The incorporation of media in the class was interesting, though.

Was really excited to take Jewish Storytelling until I experienced Schacter's teaching style--truly regret taking it. She picks favorites, has vague prompts, grades unfairly if does not like your writing style. Seldom clear in communication, changes syllabus often. The worst professor I have had at Vanderbilt. If you brown-nose exceedingly tolerabl
Dr. Schachter, was a exceptional professor.
This was a great class. Professor Schachter was really excited about the material and helped me to improve my writing. I really loved the popular culture material.

The first 1/3 of the class is insufferable with an in depth analysis of Genesis. Little writing improvement study, and more focused on the topic than learning to write argumentatively. Last 1/3 of the class was fun. Fair grader. Sometimes no work at all, sometimes a TON of work. A paper and 250 page book in 1 weekend was the worst/miserable.

I was struck by the work and preparation she put into the class.  The syllabus is crafted tightly, providing coherence throughout the semester.  Assignments and grading were clear and graded fairly.  Really knowledgable and made extra effort to help with me with my writing.  Also has cool fashion sense.  Highly recommended.

Sometimes vague on writing assignments but if you go to office hours and get her suggestions on how to make your paper good, you can definately get the A. Some hilarious material in this Desire in Jewish literature course. Lots of videos, lively discussions, group presentation at the end. Take it if you can.
Very interesting lecturer, expects the students to read carefully and participate. Not too much work involved, fairly short assignments and only two papers.
An amazing professor for FYBE, please take her, and you will learn so much!

She was actually quite awesome and very easy to talk to, and she takes great interest in what YOU think about a subject. If you communicate that to her clearly and intelligently with class participation and in the essays, you'll probably be satisfied with your grade. The class is really easy to be what you make of it.

I can't believe some of these reviews. Sharma (which is her last name btw) speaks better English than I do. If you pay attention in class and really follow her train of thought, you can learn a lot and get an A. She is one of the most brilliant people I have ever met, and it has been a sincere, eye-opening privilege taking three of her classes.

Pay attention to what she says is important to know and you can definately get the A. Notes are more important than the texts.  Toughest grading is on the 3 page papers because it's subjective. Participate in class. She loves it. Not a big work load, movies clips at the end of the semester. Some really interesting material. Take her.

I don't know what you guys are talking about!  She doesn't understand basic english sometimes and doesn't even teach the right course.  She teaches globalization/anthro NOT WGS.  Yes, it is an easy A but she is redic and rude.  Asks questions that don't have answers and then waits during long periods of silence.
This class is pretty easy, and you'd be surprised by how much it will actually help you in other non-WGS related classes. Plus, Sharma clearly likes teaching, and she can be pretty funny sometimes.
She's great. Very bright, knows how to stimulate good discussions. Wants everyone to learn a lot.
EASY class, dont expect to do a lot of work. The quizzes are a joke all you have to do is go to class (not to take notes just go).

Dr. Daniel is such an enthusiastic and kind professor. You can tell she really cares about what she teaches and that she works really hard at staying up to date in the field. She is very lenient, often offering an option to submit revisions for each project after the initial grade came out. I will 100% be taking another one of her courses!

Very sweet human being and professor. Genuinely cares and takes the time to get to know you. Makes sure course content aligns with your post-grad goals. Syllabus looks like a lot of papers (4 total), but can be done in any format (ex. podcasts) and is easy grading with good feedback. Challenges you to think deeply.
A very fast pace course.

Dr. Daniel is by far the sweetest and most understanding professor I've had at Vanderbilt! She is extremely passionate and inspires all of her students to think about their futures in education. She is so knowledgeable and easy to get in contact with outside of class. There are a few papers but she is not a harsh grader and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Shannon Daniel is one of the best professors I've taken. She is extremely knowledgable about her field, consistently sighting sources and sharing experiences. She caters class to us and always keeps our future plans in mind. You do need to write, but they are simple papers that she desires to be applicable to our future teaching! HIGHLY recommend.
So many papers. Not a harsh grader though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took Prof. Karim's intermediate fiction workshop this past spring and really enjoyed it! Workshop was productive yet fun, and the short stories we read were fantastic.

Really great person. Unfortunately, many people lowkey hated the core series but I kind of liked it. She's super chill and nice but her actual teaching and the way she runs the class is pretty boring. Interesting topics though. Easy A just show up.

Prof Sheba is literally a ray of sunshine. Leads meaningful class discussions, replies super fast to emails, and gives detailed feedback on my essays. This class was also wayyy easier than I thought it'd be because all essays are meet/not expectations. A lil disappointed bc wanted to improve my writing skills a lil more.

Definitely the best professor I have ever met at Vanderbilt. She is very caring and genuinely wishes her students to do well in the course and succeed in college. She made clear grading policies and gave good feedbacks for the papers throughout the semester. 100% recommend her.

I really enjoyed CORE with her! She is a reasonable person, and as long as you put in effort, she will reward you with Meets Expectations. CORE is also a unique class where your assignments are essentially Pass/Fail, and she truly grades you based on this. Great professor!
Nicest person ever and gives very good feedback. I can imagine in a different class she is a harder grader but she made me a better writer and is super funny and cares for her students a lot!!

She is one of the most professors that has the best patience with her students. Her advices really show that she truly cares about her students, especially writing skills. Dont be afraid to ask her questions and schedule office hours!

Great professor and I really don't have any complaints. Reading the books given are a must because that's what you go over during class. Essays are graded on time and are graded fairly. She's genuinely caring and she really wants you to do the best in the class. Loved her, just get ready for the essays which aren't super hard if you just do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Karim is a great professor for a first year writing seminar. There are three papers that constitute your grade, but you have plenty of time to finish them. There are weekly readings and responses, but those are very simple. The use of the writing studio is emphasized, SO USE IT! No revisions after the first paper, but a lot of help given.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Sheba is amazing. She genuinely cares about her students and makes you want to do well. There is a lot of reading that seems daunting but is actually entirely manageable. There is also a reading response due before each class that is open-ended and three essays over the course of the semester, but the books you read are all interesting.

Professor Karim is amazing!! She is the sweetest person and would just come to class earlier every day to talk to us about college life. She is also super accessible outside of class- if you go to her with a draft, she'll 100% be very willing to help you! The books we read for class are also super interesting, and she leads great discussions.

She is absolutely amazing!!! Definitely one of my favorite teachers at Vanderbilt! She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I enjoyed coming to class everyday for lively discussion about interesting topics. Although there is a lot of reading, the books were so good and she made it worth it. Take this class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Karim was absolutely incredible. She dove into the intricate details of the novel and took time to hear each of her student's interpretations. She helped the 15 of us in class bond as a group, and genuinely cared about how we did on our essays and our impressions about the books we read. I HIGHLY recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This was my favorite course this semester! I loved coming to class the discussions were always good and the books assigned were all really interesting. Professor Karim is also really clear about expectations, is very understanding, and created a comfortable atmosphere for her students.

One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt! She is such a joy to be around, a credible author, and gets to know her students. Our class had an emphasis on diverse young adult literature. Expect a few papers, daily reading responses (to amazing books), and a fun presentation. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Charles Sissom was a great TA for BSCI 1510L. Although he is a tough grader, he is passionate about biology and about helping you understand the material.
James Pask's sentient fleshlight.
Vanderbilt Johnny Sins. Bald and sexy

Lab was awfully boring and was tedious at some points throughout the semester. I genuinely hated reading so much information that doesn't correlate to bio lecture because I prefer to be explained to; however, Charles makes lab bearable. He's super funny and cares that you understand, and he takes the time to assist when its needed.

Intro biology lab is a nightmare with Dr. Pask, but having Charles as your TA prevents you from giving up on your future dreams and aspirations. Charles is entertaining and is a reasonable grader. He works very hard as he has to run the lab, and he really is the "father who stepped up" as Dr. Pask is absent during night laboratories. Nice emails.

He sent an email that included an extremely long P.S. that said "BEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEP" for a few hundred lines and then followed it up with a P.P.S that said "BEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEP" for another few hundred lines. I was scrolling on my phone trying to get to the end of that email laughing so hard. Grades VERY EASILY.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Love Charles! He genuinely cares for and wants his lab students to become better researchers. At times there can be a lot of work but he gives you ample time to get it done. I could not recommend him more to anyone contemplating different 1512L groups. Plus, he was very big on letting us decide what we wanted our project to be which was great!

He's really funny and accessible outside of lab. Cares about students and making a bond. I did not really feel super close with him until it came time to need a recommendation letter, and he wrote a stunning one for me. If he really likes you he will make effort to say hi when he sees you randomly and that is always nice to feel noticed

Charles singlehandedly saved my Intro Bio experience. He genuinely cared about every person in our lab group and made sure we had fun learning what we needed to. Sends the funniest emails and sometimes hides extra credit point opportunities in them. He still says hi to me 2 years later and helped our group deliver a great presentation in the end.
The most caring TA and human being I've ever encountered! Take him if possible! You'll learn AND enjoy lab a little more.
Charles is the best. His emails are hilarious and he's very nice. I wish I could have him as a TA in all my labs because he's that helpful.
Charles is cool.

Your success in bio lab really depends in part on your TA, and Charles is super helpful and friendly. Very enthusiastic about bio lab. Get ready for some whacky emails. Even though he's not my TA for 111C, he taught our group some techniques we used in our project.
he's the cutest ta ever! so sweet and helpful!!!
Can be very helpful, but is condescending at times.

Articulate, caring teacher who loves to teach and is willing to help anyone who wants to learn. Very intelligent. Thanks to his help in lab, my memory of this otherwise dreadful class will be a Sweet One.

Compared to other professors for the course, she seemed to be a more forgiving grader, and it's clear that she genuinely cares for her students. The only downside is her rubric for evaluating whether you used AI seems extremely subjective/just has indicators of a good essay, but if you do your work and participate in class, it won't be a problem.
She was very helpful and understanding. She really cares for her students!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Simplican is a vision of what I wish all professors could be. She works to establish accessible networks for students to engage and succeed in her courses outside traditional "listen to lecture, take a test" frameworks. She works with students to absorb content and find meaning in any way we are able. She is smart, kind, empathetic, and flexible.

Participation really matters. Assignments aren't too difficult grading wise (since she's a kind grader), but they do require you to do a high degree of reflection. She really cares a lot about you learning and reflecting on the material. Though she says textbook is mandatory, she provides copies on BrightSpace. Also, A=90, so that's so sick.

She is one of the sweetest professors I have had to pleasure to be in class with. This class is a good amount of work, but she makes sure everything is very clear and everyone feels comfortable in their ability to complete in the amount of time given. I can't recommend her enough!!
amazing professor, so caring and sweet and genuine, i absolutely loved this class :)
she is an icon. so chaotic, but fun. shes the reason im minoring in GSS now. take her class- its easy and interesting.

Very disorganized; often assigned readings which were irrelevant to lectures (which were more so redundant small group conversations than actual lectures). Perusall requirement was overwhelming. Does not listen to the feedback she's given even though she keeps asking for it. However, the subject itself was really interesting. Somewhat easy A.

Professor Simplican is awesome! Her class is really fun and she forms a great community of students in just one semester. You will get to know everyone and probably make a few friends along the way. She forms a safe space to share your thoughts. Four papers with good feedback. She focuses more on improvement of writing rather than grades :)

She cares a lot about disability studies, and that passion comes through to students - I learned so much in this class! She also cares a lot about students and is flexible with all deadlines. She is a bit disorganized though and there is a lot of busywork style homework that you never discuss in class.
Great, caring professor. Extremely laid back. Loves her students. Just overall awesome. Just be prepared to do readings and assignments for every class and to do 3-6 projects/essays for the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is absolutely amazing. Clear, direct, will direct you with your assignments during office hours, genuinely cares about your opinions and if you are learning. Great if you want to learn more about academic writing.

Professor Simplican is an extremely kind professor and you can tell that she genuinely cares about her students. Class was disorganized at times and there was a lack of explanation for the research paper, perhaps because this is the first time she taught this class post online school era.

Love her and would absolutely take another class with her. She is so passionate about the subject area while also helping her students make the class what they want it to be. The research paper was pretty difficult and new to me but she completely enables you to research whatever you want and makes herself super accessible during the assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is my favorite professor and has changed my view on academia. She's definitely quirky and on the outside might seem disorganized but it really is just that she's bursting with excitement and a passion for learning and teaching. I've never had someone care so much about her students, adapts to her students, and is so understanding.
Professor Simplican was amazing! Couldn't have had a better experience in a W-level class. Highly recommended and a fair amount of work and reasonable grading. Interesting lectures too!

She cares enough that every student in her class will pass. Not a lot of reading, and I enjoyed reading every single of them. She gets a little unclear with her instructions on papers, but she's nice enough to modify whatever if you reach out. Speak up in class bc she loves kids who participate. Highly recommend for the 1000-w level req.

The description for FYWS hasn't been updated. NOT A LIT COURSE! That said, the prof is great. She is sweet, understanding, insightful, and cares more about each student learning something than being a harsh grader. Lenient deadlines and great feedback. She is really helpful whenever you're stuck with essay topics! Graded on 23 research papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Sex and Society is a great class if you're looking to fulfill AXLE or are interested in the subject! Dr. Simplican can be disorganized at times, but she is super sweet and will you lots of feedback on how to improve papers and projects. There can be a lot of readings to do for homework, but the workload is very manageable and its an easy A!

I had a commons seminar with her called Gendered Lives that she likely won't teach again. Dr. Simplican is a wonderful woman and professor, I would love to take this class again. She is very caring, flexible with paper submission, and immensely interested in the course material.

Dr. Simplican is one of the most caring professors I've met at Vanderbilt. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and easily conveys that passion in class. The material can be difficult and esoteric, but she is accessible and more than willing to help her students understand things better.

I took Prof Simplican's first year writing seminar. We have journals, lit review research proposal and one 15 pages research paper to write. I am an international student. I can say that she values more on your ideas instead of language. The concepts sometimes are hard to understand. But the after-class interaction with her is very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's an amazing person and professor

This class is so doable. She gives you reading every time that you definitely have to keep up with, but facilitates really good discussion-you can tell she's listening to everyone and really thinking about what they have to say. There's only three 5-7 page papers which for a W course is really great. Prof Simplican will also help you if you need it
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This is a pretty easy class. There are no exams or a final, just a few papers that she grades leniently. She's really enthusiastic about these topics and also pretty funny. I would recommend it for an axle requirement class

She is a great creative mind and really wants to listen to what students have to say. She presents amazing perspective for students of all view points and is an all around nice lady. You must take her class!

Simplican is a great professor-she's clearly very passionate about what she teaches and assigns interesting readings and assignments. There is a reading and journal due for each class and she isn't exactly the most lenient grader on essays, so expect to put some work into this course, but if you put in the effort you'll do well and learn a lot.

Best Professor ever. Lectures are extremely engaging and so funny. She tells you exactly what she expects and as long as you follow rubric, do readings, you will get a 100 in the class. Absolutely recommend for anyone.
Worst professor ever. grades horribly as he wants specific words and events in the reading. If you do not write that specific word down your whole grade goes down. Never again!

Fav professor, take him if you can. Attendance not mandatory but 2 question quizzes every other class (easy if you pay attention and he drops lowest 2). Funny and accessible, study for tests bc entire grade is based on 3. Don't need to really read textbook, skim before quizzes. Gives study guides and hosts study review sessions. Beware of the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sides is seriously amazing! If you can take his class, do it. Taking good notes is key, and make sure you prep for the exams because they essentially make up your entire grade (guides given). Reading the textbook is not necessary but helpful, he only puts content from class on exams. Only note is beware the TAs who take off points recreationally...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is probably the best professor I have had and I loved his class, but he is a very tough grader and so are the TAs but if you do go to office hours that helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Outstanding at lecturing, very approachable!

The most unfair exam grading I have ever seen. I answered multiple questions correctly, but got points taken off because I didn't include a specific buzzword the TAs were looking for. Unless you read the TAs' minds, they'll find super petty reasons to dock points. It's even worse when you realize this is the main pre-req for all PoliSci classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Looooved him. Big lecture class so I didn't talk one on one with him often, but when I needed to, he was very kind and helpful. So funny too!! However I pray to God that he gets better TA's next semester. They were overly rigid graders that didn't fully reflect him I (and multiple others) felt.

Sides is funny and caring. Textbook is actually used in this class. The 2 question quizzes are from the readings and they're easy 100s if you read or get a summary. His TA's are evil graders. Lowkey if you don't use a key buzzword, you will be wrong. Overall grade is based off the 2 midterms and final. Bomb one, and your grade is cooked.

Professor Sides has set the bar extremely high for professors. He is charismatic, which makes class all the more enjoyable. He gives tips for doing well in his class if you attend office hours. If taking the class, be sure to attend all lectures and take extensive in-class notes. For the most part, test content is derived from lecture.

Best professor I've had. Always references current events that puts the class into a unique perspective instead of a boring history lesson. Lots of reading that isn't necessary as long as you stay engaged during lectures. TAs can be a bit nitpicky on grading exam stuff but everyone complaining about this class being hard is definitely an HOD major

If you are ever given the opportunity to take this class, TAKE IT! Professor Sides is amazing, and his passion for the content is evident in his lectures. He takes what might seem like boring content and makes it interesting and engaging. The only downside is that your grade is dependent on your performance on the two midterms and the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absurdly hard intro level class, only graded on 4 things. Tests are graded insanely brutally
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor John Sides is my favorite lecturer ever! He is extremely engaging and knowledgeable about Political Science. He truly cares about his students success and I highly reccomend attending his office hours. My only critique are his TAs. They grade harshly and the class itself is test heavy. Overall, I would take his class again.

Professor is great. Easy to meet and communicate with and happy to help. However, the TAs are crazy harsh with gradings. If taking the class, make sure to be super present in lectures. Readings are long and not necessary, but make sure to know the summary of the non-textbook readings. Definitely one of the harder 1000 level courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sides is the MAN. Best professor at Vanderbilt, he is a very engaging lecturer. Awesome office hours, go anytime you can.
My favorite professor so far! Pop quizzes were fairly difficult/annoying, but also made sense from a learning perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, available to meet with and he's a good lecturer. That's everything good about it. You're only graded on 4 things, so if you mess one up, say goodbye to ur chances of a good grade. The TAs are the most brutal graders I think I've ever encountered. If you don't keep up with the hours of reading a day, you won't do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is focused on analyzing quantitative trends in Public Opinion and not so much on theory. Content is not hard and heavily relies on reading. Quizzes are worth a large portion of your grade but is manageable if you do the work. He is very clear about what he expects on the final and generally wants his students to succeed in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you LOVE public opinion surveys. The class is not about the cultural contexts which shape societal consensus or an individual's opinion, it is very narrowly focussed on survey response. Sides is nice but the content is so dry, I'm a PSCI major and genuinely like learning, but this class was the worst part of my T/TR

Engaging lectures, he clearly cares about the subject. Most of the grade comes from daily reading quizzes, but theyre easy if you actually do the reading. Readings can sometimes be time consuming but if you do them then the class is interesting and easy
Although Sides knows what he is talking about and can keep the class on topic, grading policies ultimately lower my ability to recommend this class.

3 exams, readings due every class, lecture heavy. You don't really need to read the textbook but I would get summaries of the other readings for the exams. If you go to every lecture and take good notes, you'll be fine. Just don't fall off haha. His lectures are great and he's a great professor overall. Classes do get a little long tho sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sides is extremely caring and makes lectures engaging and interesting. Main gripe is grading: final grade is mainly 3 exams so messing up on one of them means you're toast. TAs were also hit or miss. Last names in the second half of the alphabet got more nitpicky TA. Sides also goes over everything you need to know for tests, so attendance matters
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a freshman my expectations for what a professor should be were greatly impacted in observing Professor Sides' enthusiasm for the course/lectures. His distinct manner of teaching made the class extremely enjoyable and a class I found myself look forward to despite politics not being something I'm particularly interested in. Strongly recommend!
Great lecturer and very engaging, however, the final grade in the class is determined by very few exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sides is a kind, funny lecturer but this course is graded by only a few exams and he doesn't seem to care about the stressed students. I went to almost all of the lectures and took good notes but don't do well on the exams because the TAs and Sides are nitpicky. Unfair! You rarely even get partial points on anything. I regret taking this course!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sides himself is a super sweet guy and engaging during lecture. The lectures cover a lot of material so dont skip. But TA's are BRUTAL with the grading and impossible to do well. They are nit-picky with answers and need to study countless hours to do mediocre. You can have the right answers but TA's still find something wrong with your answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer who is very knowledgable. Go to class, take good notes, and make sure to understand logical links rather than relying on pure memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sides is a cool professor and he tries to make the lectures as engaging as possible, but a majority of the grade comes from three tests. If you do badly in one of them, good game! One short answer problem is worth 12 points yet you can't even get partial credits. You either get 6 points taken off or all 12 points. This is an "intro-level" course...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures - he covers everything you need to know for tests so pay close attention to what he says. Some of the things he says might not be in the textbook, and the grading is very specific to how he explained certain concepts in class. Grading lowkey depends on which TA you get. Sides grades pretty easily, the TAs are a little bit harsher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Sides is an amazing lecturer. I could sit and listen to him talk for hours - he is so entertaining. The exams are pretty specific but always on stuff covered in lecture (you don't have to read the textbook, just take good notes in class). Not bad if you make a good study guide/take good notes. But he is an amazing guy, definitely recommend.

Sides is an amazing lecturer who was always very informative yet engaging. The class can be difficult since 80% of the grade is made up of 3 tests, but everything on the exams comes straight from the lectures. Definitely my favorite class and best professor this semester; I highly recommend if you are even slightly interested in politics.

Only 3 exams (2 midterms and 1 final), but the exams are not difficult at all as long as you pay attention in class. He does assign tons of reading (50-60 pages per night), but getting behind is okay, as he covers the important topics of the reading in the next lecture. Overall, very good professor and would take him again

Sides is such a charismatic guy! Genuinely such a nice dude. He only grades by three tests, which REALLY screws you over if you stumble on one of them; Tophat questions each class buff your grade tho, so it's not impossible to bounce back. The tests only focus on the lecture material, so you gotta attend class. If you do that, it's an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Sides is a great lecturer- keeps you engaged, makes the learning more bearable, and is so knowledgeable.  Gotta work for an A though, only 2 midterms & 3 quizzes + final.  One midterm can drop you a letter grade.TAs grade everything.  Learned useful content that helps me guide discussions with peers/friends about politics, overall would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor and class content was interesting and simple to learn. Graded based off of a couple of quizzes, two midterms, and a final. Have to work a little harder for an A as grading past a 90 gets a little harsh but pretty effortless overall.
Sides is super good at lecturing and is very funny. I liked the material presented in class. There are 3 tests and 2 exams which are graded very strictly by the TA's.

Sides is an engaging lecturer, which helps because you definitely have to pay attention to do well. A good bit of reading outside of class will appear on the exams. Review your comments from TAs on midterms ASAP and talk to him about getting points back if you feel you deserved credit. Accessible through office hours or email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Got absolutely hammered with the TA grading. I never got a single question wrong but the grading was insane. Unlucky for us people with last names in the back half of the alphabet. Sides himself is not bad and if you like PSCI then go for it but if I am being honest this was my GPA killer even though it was supposed to be my easy A lol

Professor Sides is amazing! His lectures are REALLY long but he is engaging and has interesting stories/lots of experience. Depending on the TA that you get your grade can be extremely variable. Not an easy A for our section, or at least for those with last names N-Z.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: good lecturer, tests tend to focus on very niche subjects and are graded fairly harshly

Just because it's an intro course doesn't mean it's an easy a. If you mess up on any of the three exams, it's difficult to get your grade back up. But Professor Sides is incredibly knowledgeable in his field, and he tries to make the lectures as interesting as possible. The TAs handle grading so that's a big hit or miss depending on who you get.

Professor Sides is highly organized and cares a lot about the subject matter. If anything I'd say his knowledge is a bit pigeonholed in the American political system, and he grades kind of harshly with little clarity at the beginning of the semester about how grading will work. Not as easy of an A as some people think.

I had John Sides in his first year teaching Intro to American Politics during COVID! He was extremely entertaining and engaging, and was super accommodating to me when I was sick from Covid (he let me finish my final at a later date). I agree with the previous comment that Sides quizzes and tests let me turn in work I was proud of. I recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a very efficient lecturer. You definitely need to take notes during lecture b/c the slides don't have all the info you need. 3 exams and 3 quizzes which had no time limit so even though the questions were ambiguous, you had the time to work on it. He has a great personality and teaches from examples so you can understand the concepts better.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really liked his lectures! Overall, he's a great professor who cares about his students. I heavily recommend PSCI 1101 and would take it again with Sides. The tests and quizzes were basically mini essays and there was no time limit; this lifted a lot of the stress from my work and allowed me to turn in work I was proud of.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Sides is great, would recommend to anyone. TAs graded pretty harshly but you could get points back pretty easily. Very clear about what is on exams. Overall great option.

Sides is extremely knowledgable about politics, and his lectures are always pretty interesting and funny with relevant current events and stories from his life. He's super sweet and thoughtful and really tries to connect w his students despite the large class size. Tests can be tricky if you don't read, and he takes a participation quiz each class.

Prof. Asides is a fantastic lecturer and a fair grader. He is approachable outside of class and genuinely tries to get know students, even in a huge lecture class such as this one, Intro to American Gov and Politics. The TAs grades much more harshly than Sides did, though.
The professor is nice and helpful. Take home exam. The quiz is a little difficult. If you study hard, you will be fine!

Simon is super knowledgeable and you have a lot to learn from him. His quizzes can be a bit tough, but the midterm and final are take home and open note. Simon is a little all over the place and doesn't stick to the syllabus, but if you can look past that, he's a really great professor. Also, he takes you on really cool field trips.

Class is usually very interesting. I definitely learned a lot. He's funny and really smart. Probably way to smart to be teaching honestly. Quizzes are very specific and pretty challenging. Midterm was take home / open note but very difficult. Possible to do well on, but takes a ton of time.

Simon is a legend! Very funny and charming, and a great lecturer. Definitely go on his field trips, as they're super fun. He can be disorganized, so don't be afraid to ask questions or track him down in his office.

He's really chill, great lecturer, but occasionally disorganized. Students love him. He teaches EES 2510 so well, it really broadened my perspective on the relationship between the geosphere and biosphere over time, and how millions of years of history shapes the world today. Sometimes students expect to be friends with him, though.

Simon is a great professor, and his class was really entertaining. We went on two different field trips, which were super fun, and he's a lot funnier than I thought he was going to be. The class itself wasn't too difficult, but the quizzes were oddly specific sometimes, so if you study it shouldn't be too bad. Overall, would recommend

Simon is a great guy! Super manageable class, creates a great community and his labs aren't too hard. Quizzes can get pretty specific but not unreasonable. Super passionate and does as well as possible with the material. Overall super funny guy and would definitely take him again if I get the chance.

Simon is a great professor. He is obviously passionate about his work, and it makes his class that much more interesting. He's funny, and he builds a good relationship with his students. The quizzes are a bit specific, but not unmanageable. All tests were take home as well. Overall, I would recommend.
Professor Darroch is an amazing professor that not only is super engaging but also is very fair and gives really great lectures. Furthermore, the labs aren't that hard.

A very fair class, Simon does the best with the material that he can. He is funny and great during lectures, if he doesn't know the answer to a question he'll ask someone else in the department instead of BSing an answer. Midterms and final exams were take-home, which took a while to do but I felt helped me learn the material better.

Prof Sandy was new at CU and had a lot of difficulties at the beginning of the semester with Canvas which made the rest of the semester cake. I don't think it would be the same now that they most likely got the hang of it. Overall, good professor hard to hear at times and very caring and accommodating to students. Def recommend

Firstly, Dr. Skene is incredible. She is such a sweet professor who you can tell is really passionate about her work. Her love of philosophy probably only comes second to her love of helping her students understand it. Secondly, the class itself is great. Skene picks a great collection of works and is always available to discuss them.

Great teacher that cares about her students and is passionate about her field of study. The class setup, especially towards the end of the semester, is more open discussion-based, where everyone can chip in about the readings. I like how she draws connections/relates the readings to real life. Really sweet and understanding; not lecture-heavy.

Wow. easily one of my favorite teachers. The class is actually pretty difficult because i think philosophy and analyzing difficult paper is in essence difficult. She is super nice though and very caring. Go to her office hours if you don't understand anything. The class has three papers. and she goes over readings in class, but be prepared!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Skene is excellent. She cares deeply about our learning and provides great feedback on all assessments. Good balance of lecture and discussion, as she covers the fundamentals of the topic and then leads meaningful and interesting conversations. Very interested in applying theory to practical examples. Highly recommended.

Easily the best prof I've had at Vanderbilt. She really cares about her students, and about what she teaches.  The course material could have been really boring, but Dr. Sandy always related it back to "real life" in surprising ways that really made me think. It ended up being my favorite class, by far.
Crazy easy class. If you study a little for each quiz and show up, you should do very well in the class
Skene is a wonderful professor. Quizzes were very easy, and final was a take home essay. She's engaging, and values the opinions of her students. Highly recommend as a professor.

Class was interesting and Slobogin is very knowledgeable. Makes you buy a textbook at the beginning of the year that you don't need. About 50% of your final grade is determined by tests and quizzes that are pretty challenging and which I felt like he didn't give adequate preparation for. Not a bad class if criminal law is your jam!

Professor Slobogin was phenomenal. He brought in guest lectures which made the topics that much more engaging and informative. He was super funny even when he didn't mean to be, and very caring about students and their lives. He was understanding about late work as long as it wasn't often, and he wasn't too difficult of a grader.

There are lots of homework before class to do, but the material is not insanely difficult and I found it very interesting. Class time usually starts off with a lecture that goes over concepts introduced in the homework, before the Professor opens up the class for discussion. The discussion portion was my favorite part. Overall, worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Highly recommend to anyone remotely interested in law. Slobogin is very knowledgable and clearly excited to share his knowledge with students. Also a kind & understanding professor. Really enjoyed this class. Graded on quizzes (which can be challenging, but he curves), participation, pre-class assignments & the final. A is very doable!

I was nervous to take Slobogin's undergrad Criminal Law course and am so glad I did! His lectures are so engaging; genuinely looked forward to class, which is saying something since it was an 8am. Graded based on 2 curved quizzes (10% each), final written exam, (30%), and completion of modules (30%)/participation (20%). Very manageable. Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Slayton teaches the MUTH 2100 (Accelerated I) course very well. He is very easy to follow, encourages participation, and values working together, whether that be in groups/pairs or as a whole class. He makes each class fun, with his humor and silly anecdotes. He provides available office hours, both in-person and online, to all students.

Dr. Slayton has a very specific teaching style that does not work for most. While his lectures are captivating, he has a condescending tone and borderline degrading attitude towards his students. He will cold call in class, and doesn't give great guidance if we are lost. He is not approachable, and doesn't give clear grading criteria. Judgemental

Professor Slayton opened our a-tonal theory class with a statement I paraphrase to "we're here to study all music, not just the music we like." His non-biased approach to music was very inspiring, especially in the field where there are so many options for what "music" you do later in life. He was a tough grader, but 100% fair in his assessment.

This was by far my favorite class this semester, but also the one I had to work towards the most—lots of emphasis on group work, which creates a tight-knit class environment. Dr. Slayton is incredibly knowledgeable, but he assumes that you will grasp concepts very quickly. Expect to spend time outside of class grasping these concepts.

Dr. Slayton is very inspirational, motivational, and we often have deep discussions in class. Composition projects were unnecessarily hard and took a lot of time. It's hard to know what he's looking for in the projects and essays. Hard to get an A in the class

Although Slayton is widely respected among a great deal of students at Blair, I think he could benefit from learning some patience for teaching students who don't catch on to concepts as quickly as he would like. If you aren't someone who picks up on esoteric, high-art modernist theory concepts quickly, good luck.

syntax with slayton has been my favorite class this semester, not just because of slayton's incredible teaching style and him constantly pushing us, but because of the loving and playful classroom environment he's cultivated this sem. he often has us working in pairs with people we don't know, which encourages us to get to know our peers better.

I've had Prof. Slayton for this class, MUTH 2100, and MUTH 2200, and he is the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He is such an intelligent and thoughtful person, and it really shows in all of his lectures. He doesn't assign much homework, but with an expectation of you having a solid understanding of the concepts discussed in class.

Professor Slayton is the type of person who you want to respect, not because he demands it, but merely because he is incredibly inspirational and kind. His class was not very easy, but he is very accessible outside of class, and is very helpful.

I've had him for all four semesters of music theory now and he is probably the best professor I've had yet. He is incredibly intelligent and inspires people to learn as well. He's also a great person and cares a ton about students--so care about school and demonstrate that you really want to learn and are trying your hardest. Don't disrespect him.
