Expects you to put in a ton of time. If you are trying and struggling, he does not help you, but expects you to work more on your own. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you don't go you won't pass. He's a nice guy, put not the clearest or most helpful professor.

Absolutely the best professor ever. He's a bit intimidating at first, just because he's so brilliant. He's not condescending (although sometimes he assumes you know more than you do), even though his IQ is probably in the 180s. Learn for the material, not for the grade, because he's not the easiest grader ever. But seriously, take him.

Dr. Slayton is great at providing varied ways of looking at curriculum. If you stay on top of the assignments and take it upon yourself to ask when you don't understand something, you'll do well in the class as well as have a good understanding of the material.

Prof. Slayton will definitely teach you theory in roundabout ways that really challenge you to learn for yourself.  Don't expect an easy class, but if you put the work in and make the extra effort you'll do very well.  Prof. Slayton has a good sense of humor and honestly cares about his students' success in his class. Love him.

Great professor. Teaches the material, but talks about things not necessarily tested as well. You have to study, but not too much if you have a basic grasp of theory. Very nice guy, makes jokes, and is practically the definition of a talent crush. The other theory professors are probably easier, but the "venerable master" is the best!

He's a great professor, expects effort and intelligence, but doesn't make you feel stupid or inferior when you make a mistake. Somewhat distant at first, but really a kind and helpful professor. Extremely knowledgeable in his field and a fantastic teacher

slayton is a funny guy and a decent teacher.  i liked the other theory professors better, but he's still a good teacher.  some of his grading seems pretty subjective, argue with him and you might get some points back.
he's the hottest man alive. TAKE HIS CLASS LADIES!

Slayton does know his stuff, good sense of humor.  The long hair is gone, but he still looks good without.  Great sense of style for a music theory prof, he also acts in indie theater and long-distance running.  He can be subjective in his test grading, so if you don't agree, be prepared to fight -- i found that true especially with the final exam.

Slayton is brilliant in every way, plain and simple.  His delivery and personality is best quality.  Plus, he is a genius when it comes to theory, and likely when it comes to everything else too.  I took his classes four years ago, and I hope he still has long hair today.  Someday I hope to bump into him running a marthon.  Take his classes, period
Slayton is a really great teacher.  Here clears up everything you didn't understand from Theory 2 in one class.  He is jokes around and is interesting.  He's also hot.

Professor Sloop is my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He is funny and engaging and although his public speaking class is the most difficult of the 1500s, I have truly improved as a speaker. He provides ample feedback and is very understanding. Take his class if you have the opportunity, you truly will learn something.

Really great guy. 3 papers, one "teaching presentation," and the rest of your grade is participation (25%). Participation means PARTICIPATION, not just piping in every once in a while. Send him emails about the readings before class. He gives a midterm update for participation and gives everyone a C. Don't be scared and  just keep participating.
Run! Grades super strict, no clear grading rubric. Participation matters a lot!!!

(Soccer: Media, Art, & Society) Wonderful professor!!! Very entertaining lectures, even tough they tended to drag. Him and Lutz have a great partnership with teaching this class.
The class itself is extremely easy. Just show up, do the readings at least occasionally (I recommend doing them all its very interesting!), and actually do the work.

Solid professor. Grades somewhat harshly on speeches, but once you get feedback, it's not too bad. Participation definitely matters. Not the best lecturer but I definitely improved at public speaking. Doesn't really help if you are scared of speaking, but definitely refines your skills and makes you focus on the important aspects of speaking.
one of my favorite profs! learned so much about public speaking and barely any work. so funny and great class atmosphere.

Professor Sloop was a fun professor to have. The class has a light workload but you have to make sure you participate because that has a huge impact on your grade. Can be a tough grader if you don't know how to formulate your speeches but once it's clear you should be fine getting A's on the speeches.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why Sloop has a good bit of tough reviews on here. He grades generously and also allows for re-writes for a higher grade (you cannot get a lower grade). He answers questions quickly and doesn't assign any homework or tests-only three papers and a podcast for the whole course. I really liked him and found it engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, his class was engaging and interesting.  The workload was manageable, however, he grades his papers much harder than you would expect him to.
Not a fan of Sloop as a professor nor as a person.
My favorite communications professor! Challenges you but I learned so much and he is a fair grader. Wish he would teach more classes. Take any class of his that you can
There's a reason even his colleagues don't like him
LOVE him! such a great professor and person. Take any class you can with him!

With unnervingly energy and a flair for shouting through lectures while jumping around the room, Professor Sloop holds your focus.  He is completely ridiculous and I loved it.  There was never a dull day in class, and never a time when I wasn't challenged.  An A is possible, but only for the hardest workers.

This guy is a total weirdo.  Thinks he's a gift to God's green earth of rhetorical analysis...if you have a problem at all with going to class or if you hate putting up with stupid everyday tasks, then stay away.

My favorite teacher. Engaging class discussions, thought provoking subject...basically you will be writing papers for any of his classes, and he is a hard grader, but totally worth it for all you will learn. Very helpful, humorous, and just a great class! He takes attendence and participation is a HUGE part (20%) of your final grade. Hard A

Well at first Sloop seemed to be grading easy but as the semester goes on he expects the speeches to be better and grade accordingly...BUILD A GOOD POLICY...overall, I enjoyed Sloop as a teacher and this has been the only class that I never missed/never wanted to miss.
All I can say is policy, policy, policy, and research!
He is AMAZING -- funny, great class, knows his stuff, keeps attention, class structured well, fair grader.  I'll be coming back for more!
Sloop is an extremely funny and engaging lecturer. His class format and assignments are unconventional, but this just adds to how fun and unique his courses are. Highly recommended.
I like him.
Rock on Sloop Dog!

had this guy back in the day @Drake.  haters don't get it and don't wanna.  Sloop kicks butt. going to college is about growing as a person, not about jumping through hoops-- if Sloop seems vague or random than you are too narrow in your expectation of edu-ma-cation.

Dont get me wrong the guy is funny and entertaining in class but he is also borderline cocky. It's kind of annoying when you go in for help and he basically says he cant helpt you because he is busy writing a book essentially implying that he is more important that you. Other than that class is ok

Sloop was a favorite professor of mine.  He is funny, intelligent, insightful, and always willing to meet with students.  I enjoyed the many classes of his I took and wish I had the opportunity to take more.  I highly recommend Sloop.
not helpful outside of class, even though he trys... nice person, not the best professor. he enjoys what he teaches, but doesnt realize that not everyone understand what he's talking about
boring in class.  has short attention span.  didnt learn anything in the class.  almost fell asleep many times.  his assignments are unclear and his grades are random.
I loved his classes so much I asked him to be my advisor and he wrote my grad school recommendation letters.  Learn in a non-traditional way.
Sloop Rocks
He is rude and cocky. His classes lack academic value of any kind. I think he is an unhappy man.
Good overall, exams were straightforward, but lectures could be boring, so it was easy to get lost before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Vandy! Super engaging lectures, not too many assignments, and overall just passionate and wants you to do well. I also really did learn a lot.

Professor Smith is without a doubt, the best Professor I have had at Vanderbilt. The tests are exactly what he prepares you for and review sessions happen prior to testing days, and he gives you everything you need to be successful. He is also just an awesome guy that wants everyone to succeed and he doesn't overcomplicate things at all.

Easiest game theory/polisci class. He is very friendly and the epitome of nerdy charming prof who cares about students. The WWI angle is cool, you'll learn a lot if you read and go to class. Changes how you look at the world. Dr. Smith is a delight, just wish there was more course content, only because I enjoyed it so much.

Super nice, easy class! You can choose which questions to answer on tests, and he lets you drop an assignment. Overall, very understanding, responds to emails quickly, and nice. I think he is a little bit nervous when teaching but he shouldn't be.

Smith is literally so so nice. You can tell he genuinely wants everyone to do well and understand the content. All the content was very easily understandable and I was never worried about not getting a good grade. Definitely recommend!

Really cool material and a super easy class taught by a really caring professor. Sometimes a bit too easy (slow) so that class kind of felt like a waste of time. But if you love strategy/history like me you'll still be entertained. The book is great but it's definitely not necessary to read to do well. Guaranteed A with a modicum of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class was very straightforward and can be taken without any prior knowledge of game theory. The lectures come almost straight from the book, so if you miss a class, it's easy to just read the chapter you missed. It got boring doing both, so I stopped reading and focused on the lectures only. Homeworks and tests were straightforward and easy.

Awesome professor, first 3000- poli sci class I've done (I'm a freshman), and the assignments and tests are an easy A if u pay attention in class and make notes. Highly recommended! He's super nice and wants you to get the best grade possible

Dr Smith knows a lot about international relations and game theory, but his approach to teaching it feels a bit like a high school course. He is a good lecturer, very friendly, and understanding - but he couldn't gotten through more of the exciting material he had if every class wasn;t 60% review of the last class. Still, he is easy and focused.
Another great class from Dr. Smith. Great guy and really enjoys teaching. Two papers and two exams, not hard at all if you actually do the reading and attend class. Would recommend.

The outlines handed out before class were a godsend for studying.  Professor Smith is funny and gives engaging lectures, but sometimes I'm reviewing my notes and feel like he didn't deliver enough information on a certain ID that we would be assessed on. Meetings with the TA helped. Liked the class, but it could have some improvements in clarity.

Only graded by 2 papers, 2 tests and discussion participation. A ton of material to review for test and only like 5 things are on it. Tests seem super easy but he grades them brutally. TAs are good though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a truly wonderful instructor and a great man. He truly enjoys teaching and puts his all into it. I found our seminars to be truly gratifying and helpful in understanding the weight of the class's subject matter. He is incredibly gracious with assignments and is always willing to help. I would 1000% recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Smith gives great lectures and cares deeply about the material he teaches. Lectures are dense, but if you take notes of his exact words, you will do fine on the midterm and final. Lots of readings, but all are interesting and not very lengthy. He's a very kind and understanding professor, and I would definitely take another class with him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an amazing history teacher and a great human being. He's incredible! I recommend taking him once at Vandy.

Professor Smith was an incredibly nice professor, always excited to engage with the class. Lectures could be very disorganized & dense, but material was very easy to understand. Class was only graded by four things: two papers and two exams. However, as long as you put in the bare minimum and stay on top of your notes & readings, this is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy but lectures are disorganized and theres too much content to really say much about any of one them. Perhaps difficult with the span of time covered, but I've seen it done better. Completely fine class, but there's enough actively interesting classes here that it feels like a waste to take ones which fall short of that
Very cool guy with a very gorgeous wife who is the department chair for German studies.

He is knowledgable and this is objectively a good class, however he lectures with this slow singsong-y cadence that feels almost like a caricature of what an academic would sound like. I'm not sure if these are his true mannerisms or if it's more of a persona, but I find it inordinately hard to sit through, I wish I chose a different class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Helmut is the embodiment of everything I like about Vandy history profs. Cares about his students and the content he teaches. Lectures are a little all over the place but I literally typed word-for-word what he said and did fine on tests. You have to take him in your 4 years here!

One of the nicest professors I've had! He's super down to earth and really cares about the students and the subject he is teaching. Attendance isn't taken but it might as well be mandatory to get an A. Still, as long as you attend, you should be able to get an A. Take a class with him if you the chance. 

His lectures are also so chaotic.

super nice guy. also took 1111 w him. he's extremely unorganized and chaotic in lectures but straightforward with papers and tells you exactly what will be on the exams. class is just 2 papers and 2 exams. he's very accessible outside of class and loves to help. there's a lot of reading but its not totally necessary. would recommend the class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory, but just attend and take notes and you are good. Lots of reading, but very little coursework. Exam format is given ahead of time. Great professor, interesting lectures. Definitely would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sometimes he can assign a lot of reading, but he is truly such a good teacher. He is so clear with his expectations and although he can be disorganized, he finds a way to make history interesting. If you attend class you are bound to get an A.

Professor Smith is very kind and is clearly incredibly knowledgeable about the subject. His lectures were very interesting and I don't think there is a single thing he didn't know about the subject. That being said, he was extremely disorganized and the grading criteria did not really make a lot of sense. It was an enjoyable class.

I absolutely love how passionate Professor Smith is about what he teaches. It inspires the students to want to attend the lecture and take interest in the subject. His lectures aren't always easy, but they are worth it. He is always accessible and his passion for the subject easily makes him one of the best professors at Vandy for me

Dr. Smith is a pretty average professor and definitely enjoys history. His lectures are fine, but he can't pace them very well. Way too much reading for an 1000-level class IMO. Might be fine for a class that isn't global history, but I wouldn't recommend anybody to this class with him. He did try but it was very euro-centric :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super nice! Giving amazing lectures in organized outlines and giving good grades! Also, he made the final test optional so that the lowest grade throughout the semester would be dropped:)

Professor Smith is an inspirational professor. You can tell how passionate about the subject he is, how much he cares about his students, and how much he wants us all to succeed. I wish I could take this class again and again, just for his lectures. His grading isn't too tough and he's super accessiblehe even spoke to me on the phone a bunch!

I've taken two classes with Professor Smith, and he has inspired me as a historian. I hold him in the highest regard, as he is an incredible, passionate scholar and a caring professor. I will never forget the knowledge he has given me and I am extremely grateful for my time with him.

Professor Smith is very passionate about the history of the Holocaust and I truly learned a lot by taking this class. The readings and lectures were interesting. He is a somewhat tough grader on essays, and especially on the midterm and final exam. I did well on both essays, and was prepared for the exams, but still received lower grades on them.
Boring...I love history but he made me not want to go to class. No textbook assigned. Very disorganized in lecture.
He is a great lecturer. Theres no way you would ever want to skip his class

Once again, the history department at Vandy astounds me with how good its professors are. Smith is awesome, knows what he's talking about. Papers are long and there is a lot of reading, but its possible to manage and his "2 grace days" a semester for handing things in late is a blessing. One of the best.

very energetic professor. lectures are really helpful and make up most of the tests. really nice guy, kind of disorganized but not in an annoying way. a lot of reading but no other homework but writing 2 of 3 five page essays.  i would definitely take his class again.

Absolutely unbelievable teacher.  Inspiring and engaging, he is the first person I mention when people ask me about Vanderbilt.  I've taken two of his courses and wish he taught more! Slightly difficult, but he makes you want to do the work and I would recommend him to anyone.
Awesome teacher. I wasn't looking forward to history 200, but he made it fun. He will challenge what you have to say and keep class interesting. Disorganized in an endearing, not frustrating way.
Very interesting class, he writes the main points of each lecture on the board, knows his stuff. Also a very nice guy - he still stops to say hello  every time he sees me on campus.
he is very interested in the subject and his lectures were very interesting. class was always fun but sometimes there was a lot of reading
Very nice, interesting professor - why I became a history major. He always talks to you when he sees you on campus and remembers your name.

He's a good teacher, very knowledgeable but he's very disorganized and his lectures many times are the same way. Theirs alot of boring readings and an ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE 9 HOUR MOVIE you HAVE to watch (in and outside of class). If you like the topic its not that bad but the readings and movies are.
No Comments
very smart, endearing and helpful.  I would definitely recommend him!
Nice guy. Smart.
No Comments
very fun professor - he makes everything interesting

Reaffirmed my decision to be a history major.  He was flexible about due dates for assignments.  Will give you the attention you want without calling you out in class or making you feel akward.  Still talk to him on campus.
The reason I became a history major.
Great teacher who benefits from a very interesting era to teach. Knows his stuff really well, I will probably take another class from him.
Enjoyed the class...very powerful...VERY knowledgeable...his book that we had to read for the class was pretty bad, but the class was good on the whole.  He's a pretty good lecturer, too.
He isn't very friendly, but his class is entertaining.
Great lecturer, nice guy, funny, very smart

One of the best professors I've ever had in my life. Without exaggerating, he completely changed how I thought about music, art, history, literature, and the movement of line. An extraordinary person, a gifted lecturer, a brilliant thinker, a passionate educator, and an inspired musician.
Hilarious. Expect to be roasted regularly. DO NOT get on his bad side.

great teacher, great guy. very fair in every way, (so dont turn in papers late, he wont take them), but you know exactly what to expect from him. very difficult, but i learned a ton. very tough grader, but prepares you very well for the next levels of theory. his class is a tough workout, but if you pass, its a good experience.

Great professor, with a great understanding of music theory. The class (theory 1) is very difficult, but a little easier once you get the basics down--lots of quizzes at the beginning of the semester. You will have learned a lot in the end though. His sense of humor makes class a little more fun.
Really opinionated.  If he disagrees with you, you will probably want to switch out.

Professor Smith is an amazing teacher. He is not concerned so much with rules as with simply making the music sound good. Expect to spend a good bit of class time reviewing the homework. Proponent of having students put their homework exercises on the board to be evaluated by other students. Once you've settled in, it's quite an enjoyable class.

Smith is cool. Its hard right from the start, but once you get the basics drilled into your head, everything else will go well. If you don't get something - GO TO HIM AFTER CLASS! He will explain it until you get it. He's got a funny sense of humor. If you are on the end of a joke, don't take it personal. He is an amazing prof. Hard, but excellent.

This guy is simply amazing.  His knowledge of music theory is incredible, and he does a great job of getting the info drilled into your brain.  My favorite class and my hardest class (except for possibly calculus).  Definitely take his classes.

smith is great, if you can follow him.  if you have a hard time following teachers when they get a little mixed up, you probly wont like his class.  i think his teaching methods are the best of the theory department.  lots of work, and you better do it if you want to be on his good side.  i wish he taught more thoery classes.

He's interesting and nice, but a bad teacher because he's not very intelligent and can't explain concepts well.  I mean, if you have a valid point, don't try logical reasoning with him - cause it will just get you on his bad side.  it's better to do what he wants than what is right.
doesn't teach everything

The hardest theory teacher at Vanderbilt but the best. You must be prepared to work your butt off, you will thank yourself later. Study in groups, and make friends with theory whizzes to help tutor you if you're not doing well. Block out significant time for homework. He doesn't appreciate slackers. His 'for the longest time' rendition is fantastic

Amazing teacher and person in general. Lots of homework, but it's well worth it just to be in class with a professor who has such a wonderful sense of humor and irony about everything.  Be prepared to work and make visible effort at grappling the material actively or he will tear you apart.
This class will kick your ass--but Carl Smith is an amazing teacher and you will be greatful for your time in his class when you get to uper level theroy.

class is IMPOSSIBLE and the grading is screwy (though there's a curve in the end. smith does give an excellent basis for future theory and is willing to help as long as you're obviously trying. DON'T GET ON HIS BAD SIDE! SHOW you're making an effort!!!!!!
No Comments

Picks favorites, not understanding, not helpful, very hard, moves ahead when only 1/2 the class understands.  the way in which he collects and grades homework has you turning in 2 assignments before the concept is even discussed in class!!
Starts out hard but you'll be thankful you had him for theory
Learned so much in her class. Takes her a little long to grade assignments. Fair grader
Claire ROCKS!  Love, love, love her

Professor Smrekar gives a great survey of contemporary  issues in education policy with a social justice focus. She grades at a leisurely pace, which is pretty frustrating, but she's always willing to talk with you about the assignment beforehand and/or talk about life and career advice. Great teacher/class for anyone who cares about education.
Very smart, not flexible, no feedback, great researcher - terrible teacher! Avoid her if possible.

Doesn't give feedback on written work in a timely manner, struggles with differing viewpoints (even when hers lack research), and gives grades that tell you more about her than the quality of your work. I was told on multiple occasions about the the high quality of my work but this never matched the grades posted. A serious disconnect.

I really enjoyed this class, which I took around 2001 or so.  Lots of reading, but relevant and focused.  When I met with the professor to discuss some topics with which I was struggling, she offered some suggestions for supplemental reading that were very helpful.  The rigor was what I hoped to find in grad school.
Still in her pattern of making students feel worthless...avoid this prof at all costs--she doesn't teach, she intimidates...big difference.
Very arrogant.  The worst class I took in college.  Her demeanor added to making it dreadful.  She is condescending.  Get another class if you can.

Very intelligent, highly informed, very well prepared.  Very hard grader.  Unrealistic expectations.  Very liberal.  Not a positive experience.  Learning shouldn't feel like surgery without anesthesia!!

The subject matter was great.  The course was well organized, and it could have been a great experience.  Unfortunately, the teacher was closed-minded, opinionated, critical, and impossible to please.  If I had to guess, I'd say that her goal for the class is to let you know that she knows and always will know more than you.

What a horrible experience. She is highly disrespectful to people's opinions and will simply dismiss you if disagree with her opinion. The assignments are ridiculous and she seems to grade based on her opinion of you, not your work. Avoid this professor if at all possible.

Overall a good class. Enjoyed the readings and the history.  Prof was knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. One complaint: for a graduate class the assignments felt very much geared toward "information regurgitation".

This was the most awful experience I have had at Vanderbilt.  If you can take another class instead of this one that she teaches every semester, do it.  She is snide and hateful and it is absolutely impossible to please her.

Participation and Attendance matters in her class. Besides that, she's a phenomenal teacher and you can tell she loves what she is teaching. Had her for a first year writing seminar and it was quite enjoyable. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a great professor, really wants to help you succeed, also grades pretty easily. Put in some effort and easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a great professor. She's really nice and gives great constructive criticism without being too harsh. She's very clear about what is due when and what she expects from you in your work. Always available to help you. You have to work for your grade but she's always willing to help you improve and she's a very fair grader.

She is an amazing person. I love how she cares so much about her students. I took her for CORE 1010 and I will never forget her kindness. She made the class not stressful and our class discussions were very engaging. Definitely take her class but, make sure you participate and keep an open mind.
I admire her sincerely.

Dr. Park is so smart and cares about her students so much. I really enjoyed her class and while lectures can be a little dry at times, I thought she was super funny. Grade is a book report and short presentation about a memoir, some article summaries (1/week), attendance, and a research paper/presentation. Loved this class and Dr. Park!
found the lectures really disorganised and very hard to focus as it was so boring. but as people have said, grading is generous

Professor Park is to psychology professorship what care bears are to clouds: absolutely essential. Her caring, loving demeanor will see you through the hardest of days; and her excellent teaching skills will make climbing Mount Education an elevator ride. You just have to press the button.

Dr. Park is crazy intelligent and passionate about her research. Her lectures are interesting but can get a bit long, especially since it's 8:00. She is nice, helpful, and straightforward. No tests, just a couple of presentations and papers. Sometimes she has a bit of trouble with PCs, but nothing too bad. Great prof, good class.

Professor Park knows her stuff and isn't afraid of drawing you into the fold of her ideas. She's at the cutting edge of schizophrenia research; and if this area is interesting to you, be ready for one wild and fun ride.

nice professor, but completely useless. she's disorganized, doesnt respond to emails and doesnt show up for her office hours half the time. easy class but not worth taking because you'll die of boredom.
you'd think this class would be interesting because its on schizophrenia, but trust me its not. the class is boring and she decides whatever grade she wants to give you in the end.
didnt go to class, didnt do good on the test at all but still made an A. boring professor but no work and easy A.

This class requires absolutely no work- only a few assignments the entire semester. However, half of your grade(50%) is based on a presentation and brochure that are completely subjective.  No amount of work can guarantee a good grade on the presentation and brochure.
boring class but theres absolutely no hard work required. test wasnt that straightforward but she's a really easy grader.

Professor Park is such a sweet person but she is the most disorganized professor Ive ever had. class wasnt difficult but entire grade is based on a final project. theres one MC test and two film reviews but they hardly count towards your grade so they're not a big deal. No textbook or any organization in class whatsoever and pretty boring lectures
Prof Park is intellegent, kind and fair. She is upfront with requirements - a low stress class; quite interesting. I would definately recommend.

She is more interested in having you learn the material than in giving you an actual score. She tells you up front that this will be an easy grade as long as you do the work. She's a very nice woman. I highly reccommend her class.
She is a little hard to understand and she isn't that proficient with Vanderbilt technology (i.e. OAK, ect.) but she is very willing to help and the class is super easy!
She's adorable and really really intellent!
Wonderful woman- she's got a cute 3 yr old son too! Classes are always tough, but she's intelligent, interesting, and always willing to discuss anything!

He's super nice and wants to help you succeed and improve as a writer. He definitely seems intimidating at first (because he is such an expert in his field), but he doesn't look down on you and does help you grow; his lectures are also always very interesting and engaging. Getting a good grade isn't hard, but you definitely need to put in effort

Very nice prof who is clearly knowledgable on all things Latin. Posts PPTs after each class explaining translations. Had to translate ~20 lines before each class, go over it in class. Had 5 quizzes, 3 review exams, and 1 final w/ vocab and grammar from assigned passages. Def doable A if you study, but not a breeze + translating took a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment:
Dr. Goaterman is truly inspirational in his passion for the subjects he teaches, and quite frankly, with how nice he is. He is kind beyond comparison. 

I really miss taking classes with him even though I have graduated. I would truly recommend his classes to anyone.

Dr. Solomon is the goatest of all goats. He is an amazing professor, and I took all of his classes that I could. I would recommend that you do the same. 

I cannot express how grateful I was to have this man as my professor. He really inspired me to better myself and I could never thank him enough for the impact he had on my life. 

Goatrating 10/1

Awesome, passionate lecturer.  The content is interesting and he does a fantastic job pulling you in with his enthusiasm.  Tough but reasonable grader.  Was a difficult course me because in-class essays are not my strength, but he gives you the prompts ahead of time, so that definitely allowed me to do much better than I would have going in blind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is an awesome professor! Super passionate about his areas of knowledge and connecting with his students! Two review essays, a midterm, and a final are the bigger grades, and he also does daily participation quizzes based on the readings which are pretty straightforward :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Dr. Solomon is the best professor I've ever had. You need to take at least one class by him before you leave this school, I don't care what your major is.

No BSing your way to an A, but I don't mind that. Participation is key everywhere, do the readings, go to class, study & prep for the essays and you can do well. His grading is tough but fair.

easy readings, interesting topic, fun lectures! daily quizzes to check for reading but they're multiple choice and not worth much of the final grade. otherwise, midterms and final are in-class essays + short answer questions. pay attention in class and you'll be fine

Professor Solomon has a really great presence in the classroom and his lectures stay consistently engaging. He  is obviously very passionate about the subject matter and is always happy to answer questions. I found the daily quizzes to be slightly difficult, but manageable. Writing tasks are a learning process, but he gives extensive feedback.

Good lecturer, very knowledgeable on the subject. Gives out essay questions ahead of time so preparation is needed. Daily quizzes on the reading for attendance are taken, but are fairly easy as the questions are on brightspace. Great elective class.

Dr. Solomon is entertaining and also gives good feedback. You don't want to skip class too much because although attendance isn't mandatory, there is a short quiz every class. Also, you will miss material and the powerpoints are not helpful on their own. It is feasible and probably easy to get an A, but I did miss class a lot/didn't read lol

Professor Solomon is amazing! He's by far the best humanities professor I've ever had. Very clear on what he values in essays, gives extensive feedback and his course material is very enjoyable. Only warning is that you should learn how to write quickly, since the review quizzes can get pretty intense. Highly recommend!
Absolute KING
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Solomon is incredible! His refresher courses are great if you need to polish your grammar skills, and he makes sure you understand all the fundamentals before moving into the more advanced material. The tests can be difficult at first, but if you study hard, you will be fine. He is also super responsive to emails!

Greek Civ is probably my favorite class I've taken here so far. The material is interesting, and Dr. Solomon is a great lecturer who always has interesting insights into the course readings. He is a pretty tough grader though; knows exactly what he's looking for and always notices any fluff, inconsistencies, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Latin1101 and 1102 with Professor Solomon. 10/10 would recommend. He's an amazing professor, but Latin is a difficult language. So be prepared to study outside of class and put in the work. Willing to answer any questions and help. Very gracious grader! He cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Literally love Dr. Solomon and Roman Civilization. You can tell he's really passionate about the subject, and lectures are interesting. This is a reading heavy class though, and short reading quizzes are at the beginning of every class. It's not an easy A, but if you're interesting the Classics, definitely take Solomon.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DO NOT take a class with Professor Solomon. His feedback is not great, he assigns tons of homework, and he is a nitpicky grader. For a beginner level class, he treats it like you are studying Latin as your major... His teaching style also makes the class tough to sit through

Bro this guy only lectures at you the wholeee time. It's unbearable. Don't take this class, learn Roman history the way its meant to be learnt. With discussion and fervor and interest. He's a respected scholar but not all scholars are great teachers
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Although Latin has never been my favorite subject, Professor Solomon was an incredible professor who managed to make a large amount of difficult information understandable. He is very articulate and an incredibly fair grader. Exactly what I expected from a Vanderbilt professor and made me feel as if my tuition was going to good use.

Dr. Solomon is amazing. He puts a lot of time into his slides/lessons and it's really helpful. He's also just a genuinely nice guy. The class is difficult if you've never had latin before since it's so much material, but he does everything he can to help you succeed. Definitely doable if you put in the effort,  he wants you to do well.

Awesome lecturer, really knows everything about roman and greek history. He let's you use computers in class, which makes it easy to stop paying attention.  However, if you stay in task his lectures are amazing and always interesting.  As long as you listen, a B/B+ is easy, but you have to work for the A. Daily quizzes make reading important.
Superb lecturer - you will learn a ton. If you go to class it's easy to get a B+ but if you want the A you will need to work hard.

Professor Solomon is easily my favorite professor at Vandy so far. He obviously loves the subject, teaches well and clearly, and is willing to help his students. It's easy to get a B/B+, but be prepared to put in a lot of extra effort if you want to get that A.

He's an expert teacher and really understands how to present material in a clear way. Lots of reading and tests are tough, but if you do the homework and pay attention in class you can do well. There's a homework quiz every day but he gives you the questions in advance, so it's not that hard.

His lectures are usually very interesting since they give you the foundation of knowledge and the connections needed to draw large and significant conclusions about the literature and history you read. He is always willing to answer questions and talk about assignments, but his tests and essays require a lot of work and critical thinking.

I am glad I had him for my first semester here. Great lecturer, knows a lot about his field, and best professor accent in Vanderbilt. It is an accelerated class so it is recommended taking if you had 2-3 years of Latin experience, but I had none and still got an A.

Dr. Solomon is a dynamic, helpful professor that literally helps you throughout the course. He is reassuring and adds additional clarity during office hours, and participation goes A LONG WAY with him. There are no surprises on the tests, and you can definitely tell he loves Classics. Also, his responds to emails usually within 10 minutes.

Solomon is, objectively, the best professor I've ever had. He's an absolutely phenomenal teacher. His methodology makes learning Latin fun and accessible. I learned more about Latin in one semester than I did in 3 years of French. You really can't go wrong by taking his class. He's a great guy, too, and very willing to help you succeed.

Dr. Solomon is hands down the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt.  Latin can of course get kind of boring but he really makes the class as enjoyable as possible while drilling the material into you.  If you go to class and do the homework then you should be fine.  Latin 100 moves at a very rapid pace though, so be careful.  I loved Dr. S!!
Solomon is just awesome. This man somehow made introductory Latin four days a week not boring. Very helpful, great lecturer, and the best professor accent at Vandy. If you can take him, do!

This class is extremely interesting however very difficult- not an easy A but still very much a class worth taking if you are interested in classics or Greek civ. Prof Solomon is probably one of the most knowledgeable and passionate professors at Vanderbilt- but he expects a lot out of his students.

Excellent lecturer, by far one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. However, do not expect an 'A' in this class, worked my butt off and consistently received 'B+' scores. It's completely worth it regardless.
Must pay attention in class, midterm and final are graded very specifically

participation is 10% of your final grade, and the class is small enough to notice. daily 3 question quizzes are 5% of your final grade. he assigns a lot of daily reading, but many of the questions he assigns for the reading direct you to specific lines (so much reading can be skipped). he gives you an outline of the tests. work hard, and do well.

This class is very tough.  You have daily quizzes that are 5% of your grade, along with a 10% participation grade.  You have well over an hr of reading for every class that you have to do in order to do well.  The test are very difficult, with a lot of information and vague essays that require class attendance and clear understanding of readings

Daniel Solomon might just be my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He is the nicest, most helpful man, and I would definitely take another of his classes. LAT100 does move very quickly, so it helps if you have a little background in Latin, but he is always there to help.

Solomon is easily one of the best professor's at Vanderbilt. He is genuinely dedicated to making sure his students understand the material and succeed. I am notoriously bad at foreign language and only took this class to fulfill the annoying AXLE foreign language requirement, but Solomon's teaching made this class a breeze. I highly recommend him.

Dr. Solomon is an amazing professor. He is brilliant, charismatic, interesting, hilarious, and above all, willing to help. You must WORK to understand the depth of the material covered, but he gives good grades easily because he is overly nice.

Took him both semesters of Latin.  amazing professor.  willing to clarify anything.  great explanations.  grades easily.  can turn in late homework.  if you're anything decent at languages (or english even) then this class will be a breeze.  best professor yet!

Awesome!!! Don't take the intensive class though unless you have had previous Latin experience because you do move fast. 3 exams, cumulative final, weekly quizzes, and daily homework. It is a lot of work, but Solomon is an awesome teacher maybe the best at Vandy!!! He tells you exactly what to know for quizzes and exams.

Ok, everyone who has posted thus far is completely ridiculous. Either his grading has changed over the years, or I am developmentally challenged. Although a good prof., grades with exceedingly difficult standards over a thousand year timeline. I am about to get lumber strunked by this class. Don't take if you think it is going to be easy.

Awesome professor. Hilarious, smart, and just an amazing teacher. Took the intensive class reluctantly, but the extra work and classes were completely worth it because he is definitely the best professor I've had here. Take his classes!!
interesting!!!! but not too easy. must work with him to get material down pat!...takes some work and you must read and really understand material for tests. daily quizzes and attendance mandatory
daily quizzes so you have to keep up with the reading.  grading standards aren't terrible, but you MUST be well prepared for all tests. lectures are long, but he is extremely well-versed
Solomon is amazing! He is the best professor I've had.  He really knows his stuff and doesn't hesitate to help you in and out of class.  He's also easy on the eyes.
Really interesting teacher, makes lot of corrections on exams, but grades nicely...very cool class!!!
Always cheerful in class and extremely helpful if you just ask.
Fun and nice guy. Passionate.

Best prof at Vandy. Incredibly witty, smart, & articulate. Knows everything about Classics. Daily MC quizzes, but questions are verbatim from the syllabus! Keep up with the reading and go to class and you'll get an A. Material is interesting and he makes class enjoyable. Usually won't feel the 75 minutes. Gives review sheets, very helpful!

Prof. Solomon is a very clear and helpful teacher, and really know what he is talking about. The class though went very fast and was somewhat diffcult for me, but he is really willing to help if you have problems, this class has hw everyday and is time consuming, but he is a great teacher and you actually learn the subject matter.

Professor Solomon is a great teacher.  There's a lot of material in this course, but he covers it very clearly and is willing to help outside of class.  He's also flexible, and quirky enough to keep the class entertaining.  It's a lot of material at a fast pace, but he makes the class worth it.

Professor Solomon was my mentor in Latin and he is the most understanding and clear professor that I have ever taken at Vanderbilt.  I loved all of his classes.  He was more than a professor, he became one of my close friends and I will always appreciate h

Awesome. Understanding, flexible, helpful, and funny. You can miss some classes but not too many. He's always willing to help you out. Homeowkr's not bad, and he tells you what's on the tests and quizzes. One of my favorite professors. Take this class.
Awesome professor. Very understanding if you have conflicts with things and might need an extesion. Also very helpful if you need advice on papers.  You learn so much from his classes.
Solomon is my favorite professor. I have never had someone so willing to work with me and answer any of my questions. He is always available.

One of the best at Vandy. Explains everything thoroughly so everyone understands while keeping it fun. Will help you out of class as much as you want. Very flexible. Great guy. Would recommend to anyone without hesitation.
Absorbing latin teacher.

Solomon was a demanding and serious, yet entertaining, teacher.  He is one of those people who truly amazes you with how much he knows.  His Latin 103 class was the most interesting language class I've ever taken.
Great prof, I've enjoyed Roman Civ. thoroughly.  Lectures last 75 minutes, but amazingly, I haven't been bored yet.
Dr. Solomon is the absolute best ever!  Take all his classes (if you can get in)!

Great professor - I'm always amazed at lecturers who can go 75 minutes with no notes whatsoever and convey a LOT of information.  Be prepared to extrapolate a lot on the information he gives you - Solomon doesn't just want facts, he wants ANALYSIS.
No Comments
One of the best professors I have ever had.  Made Latin simple and easy to learn, made Greek civilazation fascinating.  More than willing to work with his students.

The best professor to take for Peabody stats! Her grading system is so clear & it's very manageable to get an A. Although the only 'required' thing is the in-person tests, you should aim to complete as many of the additional assignments as possible so you can have a cushion if you have to miss class or do poorly on a test. So kind and approachable!

AMAZING take this professor if you can! She uses an incredibly convenient point system where the only required assignments are four in-person tests and everything else is optional and you choose what assignments to do for points. Exams are open note/book/internet just no ai. Shes helpful and caring in class. I wish all classes were set up like this

The statistics class content is manageable, but the instructor's grading system feels unnecessarily strict and unclear. Exams often focus on obscure details rather than the main concepts, making it difficult to demonstrate understanding. While the material itself isn't challenging, the instructor's rigid approach can be discouraging.

This professor and her class are amazing! Would definitely recommend it to students who need their stat credit fulfilled. Like others said, she uses a really convenient grading system that allows the students to clearly see where they are. Will need to read the textbook before every lecture, which is easy to read through. Tests open book/notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She uses a point system, and if you do everything you will get a good grade. She was very supportive and helpful during office hours. Class is typically a short lecture and an assignment you do with the classmates at your table. The only required thing is in person tests. Overall very nice teacher!!

Professor Vinci-Booher is one of the kindest professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Her class grading criteria is very clear, and she makes it easy to accumulate points throughout the semester. She makes the content easy to understand and helps out a lot during the in-class assignments. Great professor; easy class; highly recommend!!

Professor Vinci-Booher is a great professor. She really cares about her students and the needs of the class - during the semester, she switched some aspects of the course due to mid-semester feedback. The grading system is great and makes it easy to get a good grade with some effort. The content itself is not difficult. Great professor overall.

If this is your first introduction to Prof Song, get ready for a very hard MHS class. Class size was about 6 which was nice to get participation points and we got to go to a off campus coffee shop for class one time. However because this is Prof Song's research area she is super nitpicky about details. Assignment instructions are VERY unclear.

Prof. Song is a great lecturer. Topics are really engaging and you learn a lot and it was cool to have a real traditional chinese medicine practitioner come in to class. HOWEVER...this is on the more challenging side for a MHS class. Usually her assignments are not worded very clearly and if you don't participate 80% of the time, you lose 3 points.

She is a very caring lady. We usually talk after the class about many other health topics. Her criteria are indeed confusing but this problem can be resolved by going to her office hour. Also, attendance and participation is very important so stay active in the class. A is completely doable if you are active in the class!

Don't structure your paper according to the rubric, because it doesn't matter anyway. Dr. Song doesn't say what she wants on your paper until the day before it's due. One mistake costs you ten points. The best thing about this class is the mini meditation. Don't take her for an easy A. She's a caring lady, but a flaky professor.

Not accessible outside of class. I agree with another rating that pushes a political agenda in class. I would say what makes the class not great is that the TA, Jasmine is an incredibly unfair grader and this view is shared by all students. Participation is a huge part of the grade which is kind of hard when the class isn't the most interesting.

Where do I even start...this class had the potential to be interesting, but Prof Song used outdated materials and made it boring and irrelevant. Also, we were graded on such few assignments and had essays graded out of FIVE points, her TA Jasmine was the worst and graded so hard. I highly recommend avoiding taking this class with Prof Song.

Class is dull and boring. Just look at the slides online. She has a very clear political agenda that she pushes on the class. Very inconsiderate and rude professor- she removed points she already gave me on a test SHE made us submit to regrade. She does not follow her rubric on grading essays and takes off so many points for such small things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Song is awesome and I loved this class! She's really passionate in her lectures and really wants her students to do well. 6 quizzes (lowest one dropped), 3 short papers and a 10 page final paper. She grades very fairly and with minimal studying for the quizzes you can do well. Highly recommend, she truly is a great prof

Class is an easy A, but is extremely disorganized and feels like a waste of time. If you want to learn sociological concepts in health & society, this is NOT the class to take. The prof is very specific on the quizzes (everything on the quizzes is on the powerpoint slides.)

She puts everything you need to know from the reading on the powerpoints, which she posts. She announces quizzes, but they can be specific. There were 3 papers throughout the year that counted for a lot, and a fourth for the final. The last paper was killer. 10 pg book report on the worst book in America. Also, the cutoff for an A is crazy high.

Dr. Song is a fantastic lecturer and a very sweet person, but this was dullest course I've ever taken at Vanderbilt. Strange quizzes,  3 essays, a final paper, no tests/finals, and a relatively light workload. Should be an easy A (even though I didn't get one). Class might've been interesting to some, but it felt like a waste of time to me.

Don't bother doing the reading because she recites the text word for word & posts slides online. Study the slides for quizzes especially bolded & underlined terms and you'll get a 90 or 100. 3 papers - 1st has weird criteria, 2nd is easy, final paper is obnoxious b/c based on a dry health care book. Barely any work, but also pretty boring.

Professor Song makes an effort to create relatable lectures, including current events in addition to literally outlining the textbook on her slides. If you want a better understanding, you'll need the text. Lots of outside readings but only necessary for credit for participation in class discussion. Can sometimes be confusing b/c she's from China.

Prof. Song is amazingly dedicated to her work and students. Readings are mostly optional, but showing you read by participating in class and adding citations into papers gets you significantly higher grades than non-reading.  All assignments have exact criteria so it's easy to get an A if you follow the directions.  Weekly quizzes are on lectures.

Professor Song is my absolute favorite! She is very friendly and enthusiastic. Her office hours are really laid back, but very helpful. I am taking another class with her next semester just because she was that great, and her class was enjoyable.

Dr. Song is a great person and is good at what she does. The problem is communication - even with a detailed syllabus, there was always confusion with course expectations, and we ended up behind when she ran out of time during lectures. The quizzes weren't difficult but do make up a large portion of the final grade - study up!

Song is a down-to-earth, easily likable professor. She is very knowledgeable about the topic and her lectures are easy to follow. Quizzes are announced and there are a few short (1-2 page) reviews and papers. She encourages participation. She's often led off-topic, but she is a genuinely sweet lady who is always happy to help and answer questions.

Prof. Song assigns a decent amount of quizzes and papers, but if you study the class ppt lectures and use them as a reference when writing the papers expect an A or A-. This is not a class that you can skipnot participate in as these two are worth 20% total of grade.

Dr. Song is extremely difficult to understand at first however after a few classes you will not have any trouble. I found the class to be interesting and relatively easy. Nightly reading isn't really necessary for class however make sure you participate and nail the short papers by bringing in information to support your arguments from the readings

I can't believe there was a negative comment on here. Song rules. Her class teaches you a ton and if you pay attention her accent isn't an issue. She keeps the class interesting and the work load is light if can write a 2 pg paper a couple times in the semester and include what she asks for. I loved her - I'd def take again. She's knowledgeable!

Very nice professor, tough to understand until you get used to her thick accent. Fair grader, assigns lots of readings. Pay attention in class and participate (she loves participation) and you will be fine on the reading quizzes which are very easy. Her TA does most of the essay grading.

She is a nice professor.  However, she is extremely difficult to understand and is not very helpful when it comes to giving clarification.  Additionally, she makes up her own grading scale and does not really clarify it (a major issue in her class) and then makes it really difficult at the end to get a good a grade.  A lot of work for little pay of

Song is so nice and funny. There is a pretty heavy reading load and ten 1-2 page papers are assigned throughout the semester, but if you do them, you'll get an A. 60% of the grade is the 1-2 page papers and class participation (show up, relate your life experience to the lesson).  The final paper is pretty difficult, but she's really helpful.
Super nice lady.  So easy, light work load, and material is interesting.

Prof Song is an extremely nice woman and some people judge her because her accent is difficult, but that doesn't mean she's a bad teacher. She thoroughly knows her material and provides a wide range of readings that feed to the central topic of the class. It's true that there is A LOT of reading, BUT she's reasonable, and will cut down if asked.

Professor Song is brand new and has no idea what she's doing. She barely speaks english, assigns so much reading and never tests on any of it, and the lectures are so boring. I regret wasting this class with her because the topics are interesting.
Very knowledgeable and helpful. Appreciated the course and the feedback he gave us.

Really mean professor with his "standard of good slides". He really doesn't know much about what the students are talking about, and he doesn't show any interest about it, either. He chats with the students when he's giving the talk, but expect the students to give perfect talk afterwards. Just avoid him if you have a choice.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really good prof. Enthusiastic about physics and share that investment with students. My favorite VU class so far.
More interested in girls in the class than teaching...

Many puzzling thoughts. One is how VU allows to teach the only course in condensed matter theory in 8(!) weeks by a professor who lacks basic teaching skills. 20% of time was spent on topics that belong to general phsyscs courses - basics of Stat Mech, Optics etc. Also, he should had read about Standard Model before trying to enlighten his students

Not the best class considering the hw, textbook, lectures, and tests rarely line up the way they need to. He's an alright lecturer, but isn't always clear. I didn't really enjoy it but it's still a great easy way to fulfill axle

Good prof, great class for fulfilling axle lab science requirement, especially if you are somewhat familiar with physics.  Lectures can be boring but it's not too hard to learn the information (from the book or lecture).
THIS.  GUY.  SUCKS.

rips on America every class.  tests are impossible.  you find yourself rolling your eyes at least 4 times during the readings due to his "fun" style of writing.  oh yeah an he can't teach to save his life.  WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! for some ridiculous reason, people told me this would be easy for a CPLE requirement. hhhaaaaaaa- actual torture. the class is possibly the most boring thing i have ever sat through. he has NO idea what hes talking about- and he wrote the test book. hes kidding being a teacher. the tests are too hard... STAY AWAY.

This class is totally unfair and I would advise anyone who is thinking about taking it for CPLE to NOT DO IT.  The book is awful, the tests are hard, and the class overall just sucks! Heed my warning.
awful class, don't take it for CPLE
Sokrates has no business in the classroom...take this class if you hate life and want to suffer the entire semester.  WORST PROFESSOR EVER.

Sokrates makes physics fun! The tests are a little hard and ambiguous and he scares you with the whole "You can get an 84 and get a C" spiel but our curve wasn't bad 85-100 was an A and 82-84 was an A-. You'll be fine if you do ur hw and show up to class for quizzes. He's really not a bad guy!

ABSOLUTELY THE WORST CLASS THAT EVER EXISTED. half the stuff is made up and the terms and explanations don't make any sense. my knowledge of physics actually declined after this class. dave's hot thought but other than that it was the most torturous class i've ever taken.
The class is easy.  Study old tests and youll do fine.  Socrates is a terrible teacher.  You will learn some things that are wrong, but its easy.

Talk about an ego getting in the way of teaching. There are numerous errors on his exams and instead of rectifying the problem he has  huge fits in front of the class and turns it around blaming the students when he write amgious questions. Be ware of PHYSICS 105 Take Geo with Miller for CPLE.

this guy sucks.  tests are harder than they should be and ask questions about miniscuel details in the far corners of his own textbook.  if you think you are getting an easy class to fill your science requirement think again because the lab is an even bigger pain in the butt.
I thought that this class was going to be easy, but it isn't! It starts out easy and then gets much harder as the semester progresses! The only good thing about the class is DAVE!!

Sokrates is NOT a cool dude.  Class should be easy, but it's not.  You can have an 84 yet be making a C- due to his stupid bell curve.  Dave is by far the saving grace of the course, but I def. would NOT recommend Physics for Poets, go ahead and take real physics instead.  NOT AN EASY CLASS.
awful teacher and not understanding

Grades on a true curve. Easy class --> C= 85. You can do well but still get a C or D in this course.  PHYS 105 is much harder than it should be. Dave is awesome, though.  Overall, I don't recommend this class, I wish I'd taken REAL Physics, anyway. I might have learned something.
WORST CLASS/TEACHER EVER

This class is really not that bad. I thought it was pretty interesting, and although the book has some error, overall it was really readable.  If you have to take a science class, I would definitely recommend this one. And Dave is awesome!

His text, which he wrote, is aimed at a three year old, and full of errors.  His teaching is designed at penalizing rather than teaching.  The best thing about this class was his assistant, Dave.  Class way too hard for 'Physics for Everyone'.
He's rude, mean, and unhelpful, but I did learn quite a bit, and it's not a hard class.
Conceptual Physics is the worst class I've ever taken at Vanderbilt and Sokrates is the worst lecturer I've ever come across.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES.

This class was supposed to be easy, or at least easier.  "Physics for Poets."  Despite the omitted math, the class was difficult,  The book (which he wrote) was unclear and full of errors.  The tests were all multiple choice, but tricky.
Lots of reading, but its college, get used to it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great professor would take again.

Dr. Smith is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. She has hilarious lectures and is very caring for her students. She tries to develop close relationships with her students while also ensuring that they do very well in her class. The Ta's are useless though. Overall, I love Dr. Smith and her class is why I fell in love with neuroscience.

at home quizzes were easy, extra credit at the end really helped. exams are long and hard, but if you study hard throughout the semester, youll be fine. dont recommend unless youre into the subject or field. dont take it if you dont have to

Dr. Smith is a very caring person, but she's an absolutely terrible professor. She very easily gets sidetracked during lectures, and I personally felt that attending class was a waste of time. All she did was read the information from her slides and go off on the occasional side tangent. Her tests were very difficult, each with 75 questions.

I am majoring in Neuro but let me tell you, she is not representative of the Neuro track at Vandy. Her lectures are quite dry and boring and you don't even have to pay attention because the TAs makes the test and hold review sessions. TAs were mid; they were unresponsive to their emails and didn't really care. There is a lot of extra credit though.

While the class content was enjoyable, the TA continually stated that less people should be receiving A's, which was demoralizing and felt as though she was working against you, cemented by intense attendance policies and not permitting late assignments-- primarily enforced by the TA. One mistake or bad day and your entire grade is jeopardized.

Prof. Smith has a draconian and unbelievably old-fashioned attendance policy for Bio Basis. It is 2% off your final grade for missing lecture, and 4% off your final grade for missing student presentations. Attendance is taken via Tophat at the beginning of class and left up for ~5 minutes, so good luck if you are late.

Very chill class, probably one of the easiest neuro electives. Attendance is mandatory and unexcused absences are pretty harshly penalized but the guest lectures are interesting so it is worth going to class. Very easily graded and TAs are great. Highly recommend!

BioBasis is interesting because it is taught completely by guest lecturers. Sometimes dense, making exams tough, but graded extremely leniently. Pretty light workload- studied for exams the hour before. Would highly recommend for senior neuro students. Presentations are easy. Dr. Smith is still problematic, opinionated, and out of touch

NSC 2201 is quite manageable even if you aren't strong in STEM mostly because the class relies almost entirely on memorization and because there are so many opportunities to improve your grade (Extra credit, dropping lowest exam score, etc.). Prof. Smith is probably a little past her teaching primer; however, she is incredibly sweet and passionate.

I think Dr. Smith is a great professor, and I thoroughly enjoyed her class. The class is not hard if you just memorize the material, all four exams (no final!) are 70-75 multiple choice questions. ***Go to the review sessions!!! All exam content is discussed there!!!!

Class was one of the easiest workloads you will find. Due to it being guest lecturers all the time, the schedule is sometimes up in the air when work is due. Since Dr. Smith takes a sideline approach to this class, one doesnt have to deal with her off beat remarks too much if that kind of stuff bothers you

Horrible lectures. Make things unclear. Ask students to read textbook ahead of class instead of teaching them in class. What's the point to attend class if I have already read the textbook and the professor just go over them again in a shallow and confusing way? Definitely stay away from this class if not for credit. Read the textbook by yourself.

So much extra credit given. A lot of free points and the TA's tell you exactly what to do study during review sessions. Lectures are disorganized and not completely necessary. Easy A. Tests are easy and just pure memorization.
Read the textbook although its dense material and go to review sessions. Lectures are pretty dry for the most part. Gives extra credit so do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is easy to get an A in if you make sure to have basic understandings. Attendance is not mandatory nor necessary if you're willing to do minimal effort to catch up. 6 points on your overall grade are added through extra credit, so it's quite easy to coast on exams, do well on quizzes, and still get an A. DEFINITELY! GO TO THE TA REVIEWS!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is very sweet, but rambles in lecture and often makes content more confusing. I learned the material from the Exam review sessions run by the TAs. This class is very much still a STEM class, so the material is hard, but she also piles on extra credit. Before the final, I had over a 100 because of extra credit. Take at your own risk

Professor Smith pretty much teaches by the book. She has you read each chapter before class, and that's honestly all you have to do to perform well in addition to attending test reviews. The material is interesting, but there's no point in going to lecture if you can read the book and understand it. She offers extra credit that adds 5 grade points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Here is the thing about this professor. She has never published any research, and she is teaching at an elite research university. The way she teaches about gender and sex is outdated and she refuses to change the way she talks about these subjects. The class isn't terrible, but if you're looking for a good professor, look elsewhere.

Professor Smith is very knowledgeable on the material, provides mostly clear lectures with a lot of info that is on the tests, and genuinely cares about her students (she even gives us her phone number). The class material is definitely hard, but she is available outside of class. The tests are pretty straightforward, and there is extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Quizzes and tests are made by different people so it was hard to accurately prepare. Never really knew what you were going into. Test protocols changed frequently. Pretty much needed to watch the recorded lectures repeatedly and go to the TA review session to do mediocre in class
The workload is heavy and test is hard to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This may be the easiest class I ever took at Vandy. It's all guest lectures, and all you have to do is write a short summary on an assigned reading to prep you for each guest lecture. Tests are graded generously and you get the questions in advance (all short answer and written by students). Attendance is mandatory, but the lectures are worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Definitely NOT AN EASY intro class. Be ready to spend a lot of time reading and studying. Prof Smith and TAs are super nice, and they are all accommodating and open to different ideas. However, I wouldn't recommend to take this class unless it's your major requirement. Quizzes are graded on accuracy and exams are hard
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Currently a few weeks into class and it seems to be different than how she used to run class. READ THE TEXTBOOK. Her quizzes are no longer completion-based, and her suggestion of "doing a once-over" of the chapters is not reflected in the specificity of some of her quiz questions. Lectures are sporadic, but she is a nice professor and TAs are nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Readings are long, but TAs were helpful. Biology & anatomy background is useful but not necessary. Prof Smith is intelligent and tries to reduce her students' stress.
Easy class, as long as you do the readings/go to the review sessions, you'll be fine on the exams. There's also a decent amount of extra credit so don't worry if you did bad on one of the exams.

Leslie's class was interesting and I LOVED the people in my class, but I definitely think the material has progressed past her time ... at many times she said insensitive, homophobic, sexist, and/or otherwise discriminatory remarks. She seemed to always mean well but she isn't that educated on today's culture.

Very lecture-heavy and imo, you can get by without taking notes during lectures. Definitely go to the review sessions held by the TA's and pay close attention to what they say (often tell you exactly what's on the exam). Quizzes before every class (completion grade). She dropped our lowest exam of the first three. The extra credit is helpful too.

Professor smith seemed nice enough, and I could tell she was really trying. But her lectures are scattered and her attitude is at times outdated. The class is easy enough since it was graded on three exams (all open note), and some of the material was very interesting. Youll have to teach it to yourself though, make sure to go to review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Some students had issues with Prof. Smith but overall: great class, interesting stuff, easy to follow (download the slides beforehand). I rarely had to take notes as a result. If the class is online and its still open note: GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS and watch/read the supplements, dont read textbook (search textbook PDF as needed during exams)

She's goodhearted & wants you to succeed, but she's not a clear lecturer and rambles a lot, especially for molecular processes. Content is heavy and not that easy to grasp. I usually left lectures confused and relied on the textbook to learn content. Online at least, it wasn't the best experience. TA review sessions + extra credit help though
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't mind the recent negative reviews. Dr. Smith is a real gem, really cares for her students, tries to make the class fun and interesting. As long as you show up to class, review sessions (very important) and briefly skim the book, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Content is pretty interesting, but she is honestly a terrible lecturer and frequently doesn't know how to answer questions asked by students. There is a decent amount of material so you'll definitely have to study for the exams. Overall class is interesting but don't expect a free A you'll have to study hard for that

I just wanted to call attention to the fact that there is something suspect with this hire. She has no CV online. She has no publications on Scholar or Research Gate. For referencing her rich and powerful husband... I'm a bit suspect of how she worked her way up? This is an elite research institution -- and she has no publications available online?

Don't bother listening during lecture. Or reading ( a waste of time). DO GO TO REVIEW SESSIONS & RECORD/TAKE CAREFUL NOTES ON EVERYTHING THEY SAY. You can easily get an A without taking a single page of notes on lecture if you memorize and understand everything on review slides. Smith can't teach though, and she never meets deadlines for recs.

Dr. Smith is great! She makes the lectures very interesting and always keeps class exciting. The TAs host helpful review sessions before the tests and are very fair with grading. There was also extra credit offered at the end of the course!

Loved, loved, loved this class! Professor Smith always kept the class enjoyable and fun, and took time to explain things thoroughly. She also was very accessible outside of class, and was very encouraging. The class is mostly reading quizzes, lectures, and a few tests, and as long as you pay attention, you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super fun professor. Very fun to talk to and hear all about medical school and neuroscience. Only thing is she goes off on tangents easily and the TAs will have to bail her out during review sessions

Leslie Smith is a gem. Her lectures are engaging and she makes herself very available to answer questions. The material is NOT easy to understand and a lot of memorization is required, but TA review sessions help. If you are willing to work, a high grade is very attainable and you will learn a lot of information relevant to science and medicine.

This class is a gem for all the neuroscience majors because Dr. Smith brings in so many guest lecturers who are leading experts in their field. You will learn things that you won't in other classes. The biggest challenge is getting in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Leslie is the best! Human Sexuality is a very interesting class and NEVER boring.
