Exams are more material than I expected & not an easy A but if you put more than a night into studying and go to the review sessions before the test you should be good. Weekly assignments that are graded on completion and always entertaining. Fun class and prof

Leslie Smith is a RIOT. Brings a lot of energy and fun to the classroom, and clearly puts a lot of effort into engaging students and making content interesting. However, her lectures are confusing, especially to non-STEM students, and I would def recommend a tutor or Kahn Academy vids. With the extra credit, you will be fine though. Worth taking.
not an easy class but you just need to take good notes and literally memorize and understand EVERYTHING she talked about. dont worry about reading the book she tells u all u need to know

Leslie Smith is an absolute gem- best professor I have had at Vanderbilt. She is an incredible lecturer and is a subject matter expert. She is also hilarious- which is really a bonus. I had her for Human Sexuality, and it was in an incredible class. Her tests are quite challenging, though, but she offers extra credit.

From a pre-med student background (junior), this class was extremely doable and easy, received essentially an A+, didn't read textbook towards 3/4 of the sem, just pay and record review sessions and memorize to get A's on the test. Def recommend this course as a science gpa boost for pre meds.

Prof is amazing, and I say this as one of few who got < A-. In terms of organization, 2201 has intuitive grading criteria & coverage of course material. TAs are 10/10. 2201 focused on learning & not grades; so even if u fail exams 1&2, sleep in lecture, & have chem/bio lab every review like me, dive into the material and you'll make it out ok (:

For a class with such interesting subject material, Professor Smith somehow makes it pretty boring. A lot of her information is outdated. The multiple choice format for tests makes them harder than necessary. You definitely need to pay attention in lecture and do the textbook readings if you want to do well.

Leslie Smith is a very intriguing personality, but her lectures are difficult to learn from unless you are very invested in neuroscience. Besides looking for answers for the reading quizzes, there is no need to read the textbook. Don't really need to pay attention in class, all info you need to know is given during the review session.

This class is relatively easy compared to other intro to science classes but you still have to work a lot if you want to get an A. The review sessions for the tests are really helpful if you have good TAs and the tests are 75q mc. You need to really pay attention during lecture and understand what she is saying so taking the tests is easy

I had Professor Smith for Human Sex. Though her lectures are funny and the content isn't particularly difficult, do not take the class if you are looking for an easy A. Her test questions are based mostly on lecture, yet her lectures have a lot of irrelevant facts/statistics that she'll end up mentioning on her exams for no reason.

I love Dr. Smith! She is so nice and caring. Human sex began getting harder with most people getting A- and many stuff pulled from the textbook, but the material is interesting and she is always willing to help.

Professor Smith clearly cares about her students; she will repeat slides if need be, and she is ALWAYS available for questions. Although her lectures can sometimes be boring, I learned a lot in this class and would definitely take it again. It might not be your favorite class, but it is beneficial, especially if you want to go into healthcare.
Great class. Probably the easiest molecular neuro one. Most interesting neuro class by far though. Each class is a guest lecturer, and you learn so much cool stuff. Take it if you can get in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Intro to Neuro with Leslie. Lets be honest, a class with this much material will always be somewhat hard to teach in a big lecture hall. If you go to lecture, stay awake and take notes (I highly recommend sitting close), the class isnt a terrible amount of work and you can learn A LOT. I dont recommend relying much on the textbook at all.

Leslie Smith is a gem. She cares about her students, is very accessible outside of class and has many funny stories. Her lectures are a bit disorganized and the material is challenging at times but if you print slides for class and study for tests (lecture + book) it's manageable. Definitely do the extra credit (bumps you half a grade)!!

The tests are not easy; you need to pay attention in lectures and review all of the slides thoroughly before the exams. That being said, all of the test questions come from lectures, there aren't random things from the book in there, so as long as you study, you should be fine. Leslie is super accessible in office hours too if you ever need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Some reviews here aren't very accurate. Smith is super knowledgable and is a phenomenal STEM professor. There's SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT. I got a B+ test average and still got an A. She explains concepts so well during lecture, you just need to put in time to understand them. Tests are not random questions, they're straight from lecture.

Smith is very nice and knowledgable, but not the best teacher. Class is definitely not an Easy A, you have to work hard even just for a B. Tests on a random detail she mentions in passing during class. Lectures are hard to follow, I recommend printing out the slides beforehand. Tests are pretty hard. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT ASSIGNMENT NO MATTER WHAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Most people will tell you this is an easy A class but it's really not. She will continue to tell you it's an easy class or the tests are easy but a lot of effort is necessary for a good grade.

Lectures are very difficult to follow and usually don't reflect the random material on the test, so read the textbook and memorize as many details as you can to be best prepared. The tests and class are curved heavily, and this class is an easy A if you are willing to put in the work to memorize. Recommend this class for Pre-Meds to boost GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Abysmal. Test random details in the textbook. Do not take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Smith wasn't the greatest professor in my opinion. She was really nice, but she didn't seem too knowledgeable about the material and usually read heavily from the slides/her notes. The class material was nice to learn, but Dr Smith just wasn't the best at teaching it. Tests are harder than you would expect. Extra credit was helpful though!

This is by far one of the worst class I have taken in Vandy. Class pace is slow and always goes off topic meanwhile the three midterms are ridiculous. Basically tons of content focused out of no where. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. just don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst class ever, just don't take it and you'll thank me later
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She doesn't know how to teach and she loves testing random details in her test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't know why people are so in love with her. She has an entertaining personality, but her lectures are extremely difficult to follow and not that helpful. If you memorize the slides you'll be fine. This isn't a difficult class, but her tests are worded terribly so it can be easy to get confused if you aren't careful. Lovely human poor professor

Absolutely fantastic professor with really great lectures. She is hilarious, explains material in super dynamic and captivating ways (including some wild demonstrations), and truly cares about all her students. Her tests can sometimes try to include tricky answer choices , but this is still one of the easiest and most fun STEM classes out there.

This class definitely isn't super easy. You have to work hard. Her lectures are very important since her tests are mostly from the lectures. She offers 3% points of extra credit and 1% for consistent attendance. She makes the class very interesting! I have learned so much from her class. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is so easy. No reason to show up for lectures other than to enter the attendance code. There is real opportunity to learn though. Dr. Smith went out of her way to be accessible, going as far to give us her cell phone number. There was opportunity for 4% extra credit in the class. Take to boost science gpa and learn some cool stuff.

Leslie smith is a real gem. Teaching a subject like neuroscience would definitely be easy to make boring, but she makes it extremely interesting and fun. Taking another class with her next semester and am greatly looking forward to it.

Leslie is a very sweet and funny person. She clearly is very knowledgeable and passionate about neuro, and she is always willing to help her students. I highly recommend going to her office hours. She is kind of disorganized and would waste a lot of class time, however. The TAs were pretty useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is a great professor. She is very passionate and experienced in neuroscience. HW are just reading textbooks and tests are all MC, non-cumulative. Lectures sometimes get long, but she is very willing to help you learn and explain difficult concepts. Definitely take it if you have any sort of interest in neuro, and you'll learn a lot.

Dr. Smith is absolutely amazing, and if you have the chance to take her class you definitely should. Her lectures are so interesting, and though the class is hard, she knows that and helps by being available and giving extra credit. Tests are completely from lecture, so you should only have to read the textbook to supplement your notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: It is hard, but once you kind of get what's going on in class, you'll do fine. It is hard to get an A in this class, but B+A- is doable, especially with the extra credit. Be prepared to read and put a lot of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I love Leslie. Her class is hard but it's worth it in my opinion. She's very accessible and is always willing to help. Sometimes, she can be confusing in class and not explain things super well, but you can always go to her office hours and get help. Also she offers great extra credit!
Dr. Smith is a really good professor. She tries her best to make this heavy class funny and easier to understand for everyone. Though tests are hard, she curves a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Human Sexuality is a must-take! The content is always very interesting (though some of the videos shown in class are not) and the TopHat questions are easily my favorite part of the school week

I would definitely recommend taking human sex for an AXLE credit. Only three (non cumulative) and all multiple choice. Readings can be between 200-230 pages per test, but start reading early and you'll be fine. Review notes and TA slides very well and A- is easy. I got an A without extra credit but she has very generous extra credit too
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class isn't an easy A as it might seem, but it definitely is achievable. Tests can be super specific and lowkey hard. Lots of extra credit and completion grades to boost you up though. Very interesting material, and definitely show up to class, even if you have to sleep through it. Textbook helped me a good amount, although it was a lot.

It's clear that Leslie is passionate about neuroscience and her students.  She is always available to help and gives lots of opportunity for extra credit.  The tests can be difficult but they are based directly off of things mentioned in lecture.  The book has a lot of extra info you don't need so if you have good lecture notes you should be fine.

Human Sexuality was interesting and Leslie's lectures were usually funny (unless they got too science-heavy).  Tests were hard but fair, and the TAs put review slides on Blackboard that were super helpful and gave my studying a direction (reading the textbook takes FOREVER).  Attendance, (easy) assignments, and extra cred helped boost the grade.

I expected a pretty easy A out of human sex but I really had to work for it. The multiple choice exams have random statistics questions (like what % of women have had sex with other women?) that are pretty impossible to answer unless you memorized the textbook. Extra credit at the end will boost you up half a letter grade.

Take this class. Leslie is amazing and I learned so much useful information. The lectures and reading are both important for tests, but extra credit is offered in case you need it. Go to the test reviews, they are very helpful. Definitely one of my favorite classes at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are only 3 tests and everything else is just super easy assignments graded for completion with tons of extra credit given for attendance

I also witnessed Dr. Smith's amazing dab today for the final class. She's a fun teacher and  very knowledgeable, and does a great job of teaching potentially awkward subjects. The tests are painfully specific so it's a good idea to study through lecture ppts and by reading the textbook, but the work load is minimal and lectures are fun.

Dr. Smith closed out the semester today with a dab. What more can you ask for? The class was not an easy A by any means, but if you actually read the assigned chapters and do the extra credit, an A- shouldn't be hard at all. She  made the lectures really engaging, even if they did seem to drag on at times. I'd definitely take Dr. Smith again.

Leslie is easily one of the best professors at Vanderbilt, but that does not make the class an easy A. There is lots of dry reading, but she does her best to make the lectures interesting for the students. Keep up with the reading and a good grade is manageable. She gives lots of extra credit as well. I cannot recommend her more.

Leslie Smith has been my favorite teacher at Vanderbilt so far. She is absolutely hilarious, so you'll always stay entertained. The tests can be tricky, but you could only go to the review sessions before each test and still make a good grade. A major part of your grade is showing up and doing weekly assignments which are completion grades. So easy

The tests are unnecessarily difficult since students are expected to remember the smallest of details from the textbook. The phrasing of questions could also be simpler or the multiple choice options direct instead of confusing and tricky. In order to do well, be ready to cram the book and pray to remember every little detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is amazing and she inspired me to major in neuro. She is very willing to help all of her students and she is so passionate about the material. By no means an easy class, but if you keep up with the reading and work you will be fine. TA study sessions before every test helped a lot.  If you are considering neuro as a major, take her!
Really interesting content, her lectures can be a little dry but they aren't horrible.  Average professor. Although she is mysterious.
Inspirational person, decent lecturer. Tests aren't easy but aren't impossible either - people generally do fine after reading the textbook and going over powerpoints. Interesting content.

She's great! Fun to talk with and easy to understand, though the lightening in Wilson 103 is dim enough to induce sleep (I say this because she keeps the lights low). Her test require you to apply knowledge to made-up situations. People usually  do well on them. She's eccentric, but very strong. She's had a hard life, but she always stays positive!

Apparently 5 means simply showing up and passing so it's not that easy, but in comparison to the other premed intro courses (gen chem, intro bio, intro physics), this is probably the easiest.  It requires a little outside work/memorization though.  For helpfulness, she's pretty available if you have questions but sometimes she ignores your emails..

Intro Neuro with Leslie has been my favorite class taken at Vandy so far. It's not an easy class by any means but her expectations are clear and her testing is fair. Also she is both brilliant and hilarious. Just know that some of her info, particularly her stuff on the male v female brain is a little dated and very problematic.

Great class and great professor. I learned so much from this class. Reading the textbook is pretty essential for understanding the material, but her lectures clear things up when it's difficult to understand. Tests are hard but fair, and she gives huge extra credit assignment and added a few points to our 2nd test
Took neuro and human sex with her. She is always there for her students. Use her office hours because she will hook you up with whatever advice you need. Love her so much.

If you come to class (they track if you show up), pay attention/take decent notes, do all the weekly homeworks (participation grades, take about 10 minutes to do), and do the extra credit option at the end of the semester, you should be able to get an A- or A no problem. Tests can be hard, need good class notes to get an A. MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR!!

Anything Dr. Smith says in lectures is fair game for the test. I recommend reading the assigned text before hand so that her lecture is a clarification of that (the info is confusing, so it's good to read then listen to her explain it). Posts lecture notes online - review them before the test. TA's hold review sessions as well, which are helpful.

Dr. Smith is excellent, and she is very knowledgable. I took Human Sexuality this semester, and I am taking her neuroscience class next semester. If you have heard that this class is an Easy A, DO NOT assume you can get by without reading material or paying attention in lecture. Also, 10% of the grade is attendance, so show up! Awesome professor.

I loved neuroscience! This is not an "easy A" class - a lot of work I put in to get an A. The tests *MOSTLY* come from the lecture notes, but when you are studying difficult topics, the book helps. 2 chapters of reading per week, but she gave a lot of extra credit in the end. Dr. Smith is so nice!

For a class that is deemed an "easy A", you do have to put a considerable amount of effort. However, the material is interesting and relevant to college students so paying attention is not an issue. Make sure and read the textbook as the purposely pull material from it that wasn't studied in class. Also, make sure and attend review sessions.

Dr. Smith is a joy to listen to and material was interesting. She goes on tangents about info not on the tests, so just make sure to study the Powerpoints and you will be fine. Tests can be tricky, but attending class, doing the quizzes, and completeing the extra credit ensures a good grade in the class. She truly cares about all of her students.

She is very passionate about what she talks about and makes it interesting and engaging. However, she often goes on tangents and talks about things that she finds interesting rather than what is going to be on the test. Very nice and easy to communicate with.

Smith's Neuroscience class was challenging but so worth it. There are quizzes every night before lecture but there are always Quizlets with the answers so it's usually just easy points. The textbook is excellent (she actually wrote part of it!) but way too detailed. Look at her PowerPoints beforehand and only read the sections she covers.

Smith's human sexuality is hard for exams. Usually 3 exams. The first review session is useless. The last two review sessions are super helpful. TAs directly told u what to test instead of answering some questions. I won't complain about this but I think it is unfair somehow. Exams are usually about super detailed in readings.

Smith's neuroscience isn't easy, but it's a valuable class to take. She's very helpful during office hours, and responds to texted questions (!). Her tests are strenuous, but she understands this and gives out a ridiculous amount of extra credit.   She's also kind of quirky, and makes sex jokes during class. Take that how you will, I guess.
The tests are much harder than I would have expected.  Neuroscience and memorization of charts/diagrams are heavily involved.  Fascinating and engaging lectures.  I love Leslie!!

I LOVE Leslie Smith. I took her for Neuro, and then took Human Sexuality just because I wanted to have her again. Trying to get into another class with her. If you pay attention in class, the tests are super easy. Keep up with the minimal assignments (fun essays for Human Sex and pre-class quizzes for Neuro). Absolutely amazing professor. 10/10.

This class is very detailed and the tests will be over all of these details. Pay attention in class and do the readings. If you're still struggling she is incredibly excited to offer help in office hours. Very engaged and excited professor! Clearly loves what she's doing.

Her Powerpoints are really not useful at all, so you have to read the book carefully. Her tests are all multiple choice, and there's lots of minutiae that you need to remember. Make sure you keep up with reading and quizzes; it's almost impossible to pass otherwise. Classes are kind of boring, though, but she's a really nice person who tries hard.

She is awesome! She wants everybody to do well, so go to her office hours if you need help! 2 readings a week is pretty tough, but doable if you prioritize it. Very interesting material, and there is extra credit Ted talks you can watch. She's hilarious and fun, but the tests involve applying the material learned and are therefore tough.

Dr. Smith is an amazing lecturer and a really accomplished person! The lectures count more on the tests than the actual reading, but doing the reading is still important. There are also really helpful review sessions before the tests, and when asked, she is likely to give a lot of extra credit! This is a really hard, but really great class to take.

The class was pretty difficult and textbook intensive. She does a good job of lecturing on the reading and clarifying difficult subjects. She definitely knows what she is talking about. She ended up giving a lot of extra credit, so it would be helpful to ask for it if you're struggling. Its a hard class just by topic alone, but she's exceptional.

Dr. Smith is a really good lecturer, but the class is very difficult. Despite having no prerequisites, I REALLY recommend having a strong background in chemistry and some biology if you want to do well or understand the material.

Leslie is great. 10% of your grade is attendance so you have to go to class. There are online quizzes before every class but you can work with your friends on them so again, not too bad. Tests are manageable and the TAs do a super helpful review session the night before each test. There was also a huge extra credit assignment offered.

Professor Smith was nice enough, the class was absolutely huge though so you don't really get to know her. If you show up to every class for the clicker questions, do the assignments, and do the readingstudygo to the review sessions, it's a decently easy class. It is more science-related and biology driven than I expected though.

She doesn't really know you because the classes are so large, but Human Sexuality is a great class. However, it isn't an easy A, there are only 3 tests, each count for 25% and they are big and really hard. Must study. and the review sessions are a waste of time. TAs are usually unhelpful and just want to get out of there.

Tests are weirdly specific. They don't even read the assignments or extra credit. Always make sure to bring your clicker or if you forget it, don't even bother going to class. They won't give you credit if you're there.

Human Sex is that must have class at Vanderbilt. The tests are HARD, I repeat the tests are HARD, some of the hardest tests that I've taken at Vandy yet I learned a lot in the class. You have to read in order to do well as although Leslie can be dry at times, she tries to be funny

Prof Smith really cares about her students, she is passionate about neuroscience even if some of her lectures are confusing and slow.  Took this class to satisfy a science requirement and while not a scientific person, it was definitely doable.  Prof. Smith even tells students that they can call her cell if they have questions.   Interesting class!
Leslie is a great professor, and Human Sexuality is a great class. Definitely would recommend it, but it is NOT an easy A. In fact, the tests are some of the hardest I've taken while at Vanderbilt.

she's an awesome professor. definitely a lot of reading. online quizzes before every class (twice a week). she is really engaging and the TAs are pretty good as well. would definitely recommend it but it is a bit intense.
She's a great lecturer and gets you excited about neurons. Tests will be a challenge, and I recommend studying at least a few days in advance.

Not a blowoff class.  You need to attend lecture (entertaining but focused), take good notes, read the textbook, and go to the TA review sessions.  She curves and gives extra credit, and 25% of your grade is attendancehw completion.  Average difficulty overall.   Smith and TAs want to help you succeed, if you're willing to put in basic effort.

Great Class. The material isn't that challenging. You need to study, but the tests are relatively straight forward. Smith is one of the best lecturers I've had so far, and she personally wrote me a recommendation to a lab I wanted to work at. Definitely consider taking it with BSCI 110B, as a lot of the material coincide.

Harder class than I anticipated. Thought a class like human sex would be a joke, but it is kind of like biology. Her tests are just multiple choice on random stupid questions, so if you're not good at memorizing everything a teacher says don't take class. No real critical thinking, just memorization.

Smith is great, and she is a wiz when it comes to Neuro. She is one of the leading neuroscientists in America--she is obsessed with the brain in the best way possible. She is very passionate about the subject, and is always willing to answer questions that students have. She really helps clear up the reading. You better take one of her classes.

Prof.Smith is great and very helpful. She tries really hard to make sure her lectures are clear and everyone understands. There is a lot of reading though. The class is pretty straightforward on grading, the tests are based on the textbook. Definitely go to lectures, put in effort and getting an A is definitely possible.

Engaging, helpful, and informative.  Very fair and clear grading. She gives reading quizzes that help  boost your grade, as well as lots of extra credit opportunities (class attendance=extra credit). TAs are helpful, and they offer comprehensive pre-test review sessions. Tests require a decent amount of studying, but are very doable.

This class is one of the easier sciences at vanderbiltcompared to chemistry or physics it was much more enjoyable.would recommend taking biology first though so that her sections on molecules are not overwhelming.she moves fast but is super clear.her tests are long but getting a good grade is easy if you study.she is super helpful andloves students

Not as easy and the comments make it out to be. Much more biology than anatomy. Although the time commitment isn't much, the tests cover a lot of material and her lectures move quickly. Large grade bumps though with extra credit from attendance and curves. She is awesome. Recommend if youre willing to put in the effort.
Professor Smith is a good person who enjoys giving boring lectures with funny clicker questions. She gives tests that have nothing to do with class and are very difficult to do well on. NOT WORTH IT.

She is a wonderful prof who knows what she's doing! I ended up being a neuro major thanks to this class. The tests aren't very hard if you take the time to read the book and get a general idea of her focus in lecture.

I'm a bio major who took this class on a whim. The material is very interesting and the tests remarkably easy. Her daily quizzes are a bit high school but they keep you on top of the reading. Her lectures are disorganized, but entertaining. Go to the TA review sessions because they pretty much tell you what's going to be on the test.
Dr. Smith is an awesome teacher and I enjoyed attending her lectures. Neuro 201 requires about the same effort as a general science class at Vandy but test grades are more rewarding.

Dr. Smith is the best! She is extremely passionate and it definitely rubs off, after all its thanks to her that I'm now on the Neurosci track myself! Read the textbook and go to lecture and you'll love the class too.
Class was EXTREMELY interesting, but you MUST ATTEND CLASS and MUST READ THE BOOK to do well on the very hard tests. TAs super helpful and good ec opportunities.

One of the best lecturers at Vandy, especially for a science professor. Neuro is her thing. Lots of people take it to fill  reqs, but unless you take a genuine interest, it's not an easy class. Curve is generous but it's still somewhat of a weed-out course. Only a handful of tests(80+ q's) are nearly your entire grade. Study & take good notes.

NOT an easy A. Tests are very tricky and some of the questions are just based on her opinions. You must read the book AND attend lectures to do well. You will absolutely need the extra credit for attendance. Her powerpoints are posted, but not informative. GO TO CLASS. READ. But in general it was a pretty interesting class and I would recommend it!

Leslie said on the first day of class it was an easy A if you attended and paid attention. This is not true. Memorize the slides and read the text for the tests. Some questions completely come out of nowhere. That aside, the class is extremely interesting and she is hilarious. Some units are better than others.

Best professor at Vanderbillt.  She takes a personal interest in students and actually wants you to succeed.  Tests are generously curved.  This class covers a lot of material - but the material is interesting and will provide a strong foundation for any future bio/neuroscience/BME classes.  Best class I've taken at Vanderbilt.
Best class I've had here.  Dr. Smith is entertaining and makes the material interesting.  You'll want to go to class everyday.  The tests can be a little tricky, but totally worth taking her class.

The class is harder than people expect. I got an A in the class and most people received B's and A-'s. I read all of the chapters because the tests are detailed and not in the lecture and there are usually a couple questions just from the book. The test grades tend to get lower overtime. Class was fun. TA's were great. She is a little out there.
Great teacher, does a very good job explaining topics and is receptive to student's questions and concerns. I found some of her comments on abortion and research techniques to be disturbing.

Not too hard, requires some work but it's a science class. easy compared to bio classes. if you do the hw (you have your book for these and they are easy) and go to class that is 20% of your grade. Exams may be confusing at times but if you know material, you'll still get an A. Gives extra credit (DO IT) and TAs (Braden) are helpful and so is she.

okay.  so basically I am a neuro major, and the class was a great way to start into the major, but the class was pretty difficult, yet manageable.  I dont recommend to take it as a 1st semester freshman, but definitely 2nd semester.  I learned a lot, and she keeps the class extremely interesting!  However, dont to extra credit. only 1.5 pts each
Go to class to get the extra credit. Study the night before tests by reading the chapters. Always participate in her extra bonus opportunities. Almost no work = easy A

Dr. Smith is lost half of the time. During lecture she says somthing and then is like oh that was wrong or thats not what I meant. Her exams are very challenging. 50% fo the questions are not from the book, they are just random questions she makes up and the answer choices are very confusing. NOT easy A. Is not an easy A for perspectives.

I have taken both neuro and human sexuality with Leslie and really enjoyed both of her classes.  Her tests are reasonably tough, but an A is definitely attainable in neuro and while sex is not an "easy A" it's still not a very hard class.  I would definitely recommend Leslie, and she gives very helpful advice to neuro majors.
Love her. I want to take all of her classes. She is extremely intelligent, a tad crazy, and super passionate. very VERY willing to help anyone. It's not difficult to do well in this class at all.

she expects a lot from students. the class is not hard, but takes up a lot of time to study. prof smith is very funny, and makes the lecture very relaxing while making the point clearly. however, it is NOT easy to get an A in the class coz a lot of smart ppl are in it. if you're not premed or just wanna take it for fun, DON'T if want a good grade.

It is a very interesting class. The material up to the first test is really interesting, and then it gets a little cumbersome. However, she is hilarious and is very kind. It is helpful to read the book, but most of her test questions come from her lecture material that is not mentioned in the book.
GREAT PROF! Very knowledgeable and entertaining. And open to questions. Not an automatic A but definitely worth the work.
No Comments

So sweet - cares about her students. Don't be intimidated by the subject-you'll get over the awkwardness pretty quickly, and Dr. Smith's maintains a good sense of humor about it all. Sometimes her lectures were unclear (she would confuse words when she was talking), but reading the text helped. Exam questions were sometimes annoyingly confusing.

I would say she is a good teacher. She's a little odd at times, but her passion for the subject is quite obvious, which makes the class at least slightly more exciting. She is very fair with the grading of the class, and if you put in the effort, it really isn't too hard to get an A. I don't recommend this class for anyone who doesn't like science.

Smith is pretty quirky, but incredibly fair. She continually cuts us slack when she messes up, like giving us a few free 100s on quizzes if the wrong assignment was put up or something of the sort. She is very helpful, and I have no problems understanding her. She is very willing to help her students. She is also very passionate about the subject.

Dr. Smith is a great teacher she can explain hard material well and she is funny. I definitely recommend taking her classes. Her tests are mostly multiple choice and can be hard sometimes, but she's very fair and curves or throws out bad questions.

Leslie really know what she is talking about, but if you are taking the class because you think it is interesting I would not recommend it. The text is mandatory to read, as well as going to class. leslie is not very helpful outside of class and she runs through the material VERY fast. For beginners, Neuroscience is not a good choice.

If you are in the humanities and you are just taking this class because you think it would be interesting, DON'T. It's not worth it. Unless you like memorizing paths of the brain or happen to really like bio  and chem, because they are both incorporated somewhat. My advice would be to take psychology 101 instead.
Make sure and attend and study off of the review slides.

Leslie is a great professor!  This class should not be hard for science and engineering majors.  Going to class, taking go notes, doing the reading, and studying like you should for any science class will get you an easy A.  It's not that hard.  I don't see why ppl are complaining. Nothing quantitative. Mostly memorization, some harder concepts.

The best professor I have had in college!  I will go out of my way to take another class she teaches.  She makes lectures interesting with videos, demostrations, and examples.  She is always willing to answer any question will go over challenging material repeatedly.  She was very available, open to student input, and wants you to succeed.

AMAZING CLASS!  You must take it.  Study hard for the tests or you won't get an A, but there is extra credit and the tests are curved most of the time.  Don't miss a chance to take this class...it will change your life.

Human Sexuality...  She plays the song "lets talk about sex" on the very first class. This class is and easy advanced course. There are three tests, no homeworks, no finals. But you need to go to class to take the extra credit.          I think it worths. You learn a lot.. (about sexx :)

This class was really hard, averages on all of our tests were in the 'D' range. Must be able to command a lot of material, take this if you are good at science. Go to class/do homework to get 4 points added to your average.. you're going to need those.

Great prof!  She is able to explain hard material well and really has an interest in seeing her students succeed.  She gives extra points for attending class and is helpful during office hours.  The tests aren't easy but if you read the text and go to class you'll do fine. If you have questions about other psych classes or profs go to her ofc hrs

Interesting class and she goes out of her way to help you succeed. Go to class and do the homeworks for 4 points on your grade. Lectures are boring but cover all you need to know. Follows the book too, as well as hands out lecture outlines.
No Comments

also called nsc 252, attendance is not "mandatory" but you get 4 points on your average for just showing up to class plus class is interesting and fun (she plays music and is quite the character in class).  Exams are not easy but are straight forward - mostly from notes but must read the text.  All multiple choice exams and a non-cumulative final.

4 extra points for attendance and homework, no excuse for not getting those.  She's a morning person and it annoyed me, I like a teacher to just teach the material, no cheesy stories/jokes necessary.  But she's nice, very helpful, and wants the class to do well (hence the 4 pts).  Just study the book, and you'll get an A

This class is amazing, fun, and pretty easy! I thought this class was great, I learned alot of useful information and had fun in the class. You do need to read the chapters for the test but their not that bad and they give review sessions which are helpful. I really liked this class and i think EVERYONE should take it because it applies to everyone

Smith was a good teacher. Very nice, and hard not to like her.  Class is interesting but boring in the middle. Doesn't like to write new tests, so she recycles from previous exams.  Check your test files and she posts them online.
she tries hard to make her class interesting, and while her efforts are laudable, it was boring as hell.  it helps to pay attention during lecture, but reading the book is enough for getting an A.

Having developed the depts both @ Brown and here, she is a very knowledgable person. Obviously, she tries to relate through stories, which are sometimes made awkward or silly by the age gap. You might sometimes pick up on a little air of superiority on her, but that is a characteristic of most geniuses. All neuro/psych majors should take her class.

Hard first test, but then completely made up for it with basically two take home tests.  Could be hard, but she takes great care to make sure most people get quite good grades.  Another quality Smith class, take it for NSC or PSY majors.

very interesting class, not as easy as it may seem but with a little effort its not a hard class. she makes it fun, class is enjoyable, although the tests are more specific than the class lectures are. lots of extra credit.

this class is BORING.  dont be mislead into thinking this class will teach you much. she seems to be stuck in the olden times because the focus of this class is anatomy and stds.i thought it would cover more than just that kind of stuff and be a little more out there.  plus her tests are tricky and class average usually super low B. dont take it!
took 2 classes with her. She IS crazy! picks favorites and gives them the best grades.

Leslie Smith cares and is an awesome teacher that will make sure you don't lose interest in her class if you do poorly on the first test.  her subject is hard and her tests are not easy but she will personally see that you do well if you show her that you care and that you make an effort.  she rocks my academic world.
No Comments

I took both neuroscience and human sex with her. She a nice woman - qwerky and fun, will make you laugh (often at not with). 201 is easy compared to bsci classes, moderately difficult compared to psy/non-bio classes. She grades much easier for 252 than 201. Lots of extra credit; to do well keep up with your work; moderately helpful in office hours.

Good teacher and rather easy class. You do have to study and know the material, but the tests are completely straight forward, and if needed, she gives curves. Gives LOTS of extra credit opportunities. She's a little ditzy and digresses a lot (mostly talking about Brown U), but it's a fairly manageable A.
Tests are hard.  She cares about everyone learning it though.
Easy compared to bsci 110.  Very outgoing teacher, cool material.
Don't believe the other reviews, her class is easy but interesting.  Lectures can get repetitive with text reading, but good, pretty easy class all the same.
Great Class, very interesting, quite easy if you get the class-attendance bonus points

good lectures. gets sidetracked and likes to talk about who she knows and about Brown. tests are fair, although sometimes she throws in some bad questions (the TAs do most of the work for you) sit close to the front and ask/answer questions. Homework is helpful, makes you read and gives background.
Insensitive, plays favorites, tests are super hard, not helpful during office hours. She has made me cry and smiled as she did it.Loves the fact she went to Brown and is intellectually pretentious.
She's alot of fun!
she is a wonderful neuroscience teacher !!
a fun, easy class... I would recommend it for any psych major (or otherwise) who wants to boost their gpa!
she is the best lady when she likes you.
Hard tests & makes you do homework on chapter before she lectures so that when she lectures it's ridiculously boring

Her tests are really difficult and often ask obscure questions.  In class, she spends too much time on material that will not even be mentioned in exams.  She is fairly entertaining, though, and answers questions well.
No Comments
She rocks! The class I took with her was EASY!!
No Comments

She has the capacity to deliver very good lectures. However, her opinions frequently get in the way of the facts. She is very anti-cognitive, and she treats her TAs like crap. Please, no lectures based on poorly designed gender studies.
No Comments

Dr. Spicer is an awesome professor who truly cares about all her students. There are always opportunities to get points back so this class is a guaranteed A if you try. She created a great classroom environment and I really appreciate her!
Great class! You will learn a lot about R with zero experience necessary and she has a lot of patience.

Dr. Spicer is one of those insanely enthusiastic professors who forces you to engage with the material, which was great. The readings aren't very important at all (and she knows most don't do them). She grades speeches harshly but lets you write a reflection to get 75% of missed points back so you have to really slack to not get an A.

I LOVED Dr. Spicer's class! She's fresh out of her Ph.D., so she can definitely relate better to her students than other professors. Super approachable outside of class and always willing to help. Also gives a lot of opportunities to earn points back on assignments. Good amount of reading outside of class, but nothing too horrible.

Dr. Spicer is a great option for CSET 1500! She really cares about her students and how to best deliver the material in the most engaging manner. As someone who is still relatively new to teaching, she is doing a fantastic job with the class. Speeches are generally chill, and the focus is less on the grade and more on the learning, which is nice.

Jared Speck is the BEST 2600 math teacher you could have! His hilarious jokes and amazing lectures made me want to come back every day! If you are looking for an amazing math teacher Jared Speck is the ONE!

Super solid prof who clearly knows a lot about linear algebra. Very accessible by email if you have questions and willing to meet outside class if you can't make it to office hours. Wants students to succeed, and HW is 40% of grade. 1 midterm and the final are the only exams. One of the best profs I've had yet.
Great without talking too much

Professor Speck is a solid professor for linear algebra. He explains topics pretty clearly and takes questions from students, engaging frequently. Exams are curved, and your grade has buffer with homework, presentations, and reading taking up more than half. However, there were lots of topics I didn't end up understanding, and I'm not sure why.

A very knowledgeable professor who prioritizes the learning/abilities of his students over their ability to merely solve problems and pass. His lectures are extremely professional and well-explained, and the structure of his class is very organized in terms of lectures, textbook readings, problem sets, and exams.
You cannot find a better professor for MATH2600.

Prof Speck's class is fair and enjoyable and he makes learning the material easy. He loves teaching linear algebra and cares about his students. He teaches proof basics and focuses on core concepts rather than regurgitation. He is one of the few profs who teaches as if he is explaining the material to a friend he respects than a student he doesn't.

Professor Speck truly cared about his students and wanted everyone to do well especially within the covid craziness! His tests accurately represented the difficulty of homeworks and practice tests. The course consisted of weekly problem sets, class presentation, a midterm and a final. Professor Speck was awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jared is probably your best option for MATH 2600. He knows this is the first course where many students are dealing with proofs, and definitely eases you into it. The first half of the course is a lot easier than the 2nd, but it's the nature of the course. PSets/Participation weighted heavy! We love Jared

Prof. Speck might be one of the most caring professors I've ever had about getting kids to learn the material. Prepares well on his own time for stuff, and facilitates a really good environment. Even if you don't keep up on the readings, he makes it easy to fall back in.

Prof. Speck is an awesome choice for Lin Alg, or probably any other math class too. He's a sweet guy, doesn't assign too much work, and his tests are very doable. One PSet a week, daily readings before class, tests aren't a large portion of grade. Definitely recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He gives very clear lectures, helpfully mixing some motivation in between proofs. The content is exceptionally well presented, leaving little need to consult the book. Nonetheless, the bookwell chosen in its on rightis closely followed, making it easy to reference theorem for homeworks and review for tests. Exactly what you want for advanced math
Not recommend

Course and prof were extremely disorganized. I think the other good reviews are just because everyone gets in the A range at the end of the class, so long as you do your work. If you want an easy grade (which is a good thing), take this class. Also a tough guy to contact. He is nice, if you catch him in-person he will do everything he can to help.

Great professor. I think the content is not that easy. Although attendance is not mandatory, attending class greatly helps with assignments and group project. There is no final exam, just four individual assignments and a group project.

He's a nice professor, very chill. Around 6 individual assignments, a group project, and 2 exams. Grading was pretty lenient overall, but the PA's were pretty annoying. One thing that annoyed me was that his notes are written by hand (no CTRL-F), but you can definitely study effectively using them. Great class overall.
Nice and fun guy - really cares about students

Ignore people that say Sprinkle is a bad professor. They're just bad at math. He is a great guy, cares a lot about his students. Most of his classes are graded lightly as long as you show up and learn. Plays jazz before lectures. He's the best
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting and Sprinkle is pretty funny. Office hours are FAR (east of campus). Assignments for this class are a pain and will wipe you if you aren't prepared to work on them early. Tests are also super hard but smaller portion of grade. Final exam replaced by term project, which wasn't bad (splitting up work was tricky). TAs NOT GOOD

Professor Sprinkle was alright! Definitely one of the better professors in our ML department. Assignment grading is very clear -- there are rubrics given for every assignment, and the assignments are all in Python. Exams are tough, but you get a cheat sheet, so as long as you prepare well they really aren't any trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Moreover, after feeding material into students in an overwhelming way, he will be using a whole month for final presentation. Very bad at pacing and good at adding stress to student. Machine learning doesn't necessarily need to be hard in this way. He's so boring and inconsiderate.

His wording is so ambiguous that the tests and homework are hard to understand and therefore time-consuming. Good at arranging deadlines that the due date of a big assignment is followed by a big grueling test the next day. This is very inconsiderate considering the number of classes each student is taking at the same time.

Solid professor. While taking this class, I feel the lecture notes and homework assignments give me the confidence to do complex maths and implement complicated models by myself. Very helpful preparation for the future.

The class itself is fairly straightforward and easy. Mostly depends on who ends up in your group project since you work together all semester. Sprinkle himself is a great professor- very engaging, makes funny jokes, and knows his stuff from industry. He's kind and open to helping outside of class. Would definitely take him again
With the difficult circumstances, he still made space for all students and was excited to talk about the topic. Grading is a bit harsh, but only a couple of papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really passionate and adorable professor. Only went to like 5 classes but got an A. Graded on 4 essays. He knew I hadn't been going to class, but when I asked him for clarification on an essay (because the details were discussed in class) he wrote me a full essay guide just for me. He is so gentle but also very caring. Definitely recommend.

Very passionate and knowledgeable about his subject. Gives really interesting lectures and the class flows together in a really cohesive ways. readings are good too. assessments are not bad at all as long as you do the readings and pay attention in class. the guy loves Darwin and by the end, so will you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was so chill. Sponsel used time wisely but allowed for discussion and deviance from lecture plan. Show up, take notes, and do the reading and you'll get an A. Very easy AXLE requirement and nice break from intense classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great professor. Brilliant and very passionate about the subject. He grades pretty slowly, but his grades are always fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Took this class because it was just 3 take home exams... ended up being tough. He has some sort of speech impediment which make his lectures kinda hard to understand at first. He isn't really inspiring. Very knowledgeable but also his lectures are soooo boring. Thankfully you can use your laptop. But the take home exams are graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Incredibly knowledgable about all things Darwin and the history of Evolution. His lectures are long but interesting and funny to keep you involved. If you give the bare minimum of attention during lectures and readings you should do fine on the 3 take-home tests, but if you actually want an A you might have to do a little bit more.

This class is amazing and funny! It looks at how theories are influenced by their social contexts & the ways the relationship between sci and religion has changed He is a very tough grader & you MUST go to lecture to pass the readings are primary source docs so lectures are the only way to answer an exam Its all submitted online. Hard to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Coolest. Guy. Ever. His lectures are super engaging and informative. He's so passionate about what he teaches. His exams are take home and there's no final. Still, the exams require a great deal of critical thinking and can be very tricky. Participation is 10% of the grade, so show up and say something once in awhile.

Professor Sponsel is great. He really knows what he's talking about and loves the subject. The tests are all take home tests with three essay questions. Even with open book and open notes, they are kind of difficult especially if you haven't been doing the reading. Definitely go and participate in class. I didn't and my grade reflects it.

Prof. Dowdall is a very caring professor who really wants you to do well. The homework is mostly an online component, with questions that you can attempt for as many times as you need to get full credit. He's allowed test corrections and his office hours are extremely helpful. His exams are reasonable and he is very passionate about what he does.

Professor Dowdall was a very kind professor who genuinely cared about students and tried his best to accommodate to students' needs. The lectures moved very fast though because of how much needed to be covered. Each section had a 5-10 question homework, so you could fall behind very easily.

Concept was not easy while Professor Dowdall did great in weekly lectures explaining everything clear.
Weekly homework was a lot but did provided sufficient practice for understanding the concepts of the course.
Professor is great guy and office hours are crowded for most of the times.

Lectures are great as they cover exactly what you need to know. The homework assignments are more challenging than the actual exams and demand a significant time investment each week. However, he is accessible during office hours. Mastering the concepts covered in both lectures and homework is key to achieving success in the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was fine. The homework assignments took forever and there was usually one assignment per chapter due 3 times a week. The questions were nothing like the exam questions which was the hardest part for me. Nice guy, really approachable, but the lectures are basically the exact same as the textbook. Also you only get one side of a cheat sheet

Solid professor. Although he is fast-paced, Dowdall gets through a lot of important content and makes you enjoy the proof-based nature of pure math. Definitely normal to feel confused at times. Tests are fair and easier than the toughest (or most theoretical) homework problems and in-class proofs. Fun class; very approachable in office hours.

He is definitely underrated to get a 2.9 rating. His lectures are clear and his office hours are so welcoming. He cares and gives a great selection of homework. A great lecturer and even a great friend.

Professor Dowdall is a good professor. Generally, he explains stuff well, but he goes very fast which can make him hard to follow. Definitely go to office hours. He doesn't do pop quizzes; he'll tell you about quizzes the class before. Homework takes a lot of time and can be difficult. Calculations are ok, proofs are very hard. Tests are hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dowdall's class is very fast-paced. He goes over concepts quickly, so you need to be very attentive during class. The difficulty of exams is acceptable as they are similar to homework questions. If you blew one of them, don't worry, he might give you a rewrite. There is also a curve after the final.

Prof. Dowdall gets way too much hate on here. His tests are extremely fair - the average on the last two has been about an 80. He talks fast and rarely repeats himself so you will have to be diligent about taking notes, but if you show up, pay attention, and ask any questions that you have, you will do well in this class. Video projects are free As
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know how these negative reviews come about. Indeed, the class is hard, and Prof. Dowdall sometimes overestimates the ability of his students (HW average sits around 75, midterms around 70). However, if you are willing to put in the effort to learn the materials and get to know Prof. Dowdall, you will find him interesting and very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolute not. Avoid at all costs. The exams are incredibly hard. Does not seem to teach very well at all. Exams are nothing like lectures, homework, etc.

Good professor, cute professor. Clear, thorough lectures. Good at answering questions, often answers much more than you need (which is good). Cares about students. Reasonable grader. Reasonable exams. Homework can be hard, but that's all math classes. Each exam has a couple challenging questions but the other ones you should get if you study well.

He gives clear lectures without constantly looking at notes. He's interested in and engaged with topics and available to help during office hours. He's able to clear up questions in a useful and concise manner. Homeworks can be quite difficult, but he's a fair grader. Similarly for tests.

Calc 3 is already difficult, Dowdall doesn't make it easier for you. Lectures are pretty dry with tons of definitions and examples that are usually tough to follow. Homework is from the textbook and due every two weeks, but it's a lot. Quizzes are easy because they're similar to the easiest homework questions. Midterms are a whole other monster.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You need to meet with him outside of class. You also must be prepared to answer any given textbook questions as they are fair game for examinations. Pay attention in the lecture and I suggest skimming sections prior to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He can not tell us how to prepare for the exams. He is a brilliant guy but can not explain in class. Practically spoiled my career!
Very dry and difficult tests and a extremely challenging final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Smart person who is abysmal at teaching. Speeds through lectures without explanations or clarifcations and makes multi unnecessarily hard for absolutely no reason. Take with a different prof.
Dr. Dowdall could be a very smart guy but he can NOT explain the topics at all. His exams are not representative of what he covers in class. He does not care about his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Spencer's lectures are clear and at a good pace. He is willing to provide help outside of class. His exams are somewhat difficult but not curves will be given.

He is too smart, so he may skip some steps when explaining proof and his class may be a little bit confusing, but he is accessible outside the class and always passionate answering questions. The tests are hard, but if you prepare well, you can get good grade and he curves at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Spencer is smart but not very good at teaching. His lectures are heavy and sometimes hard to follow because he teaches so quickly and there are a lot of notes. It is extremely hard to follow his thoughts while copy what he writes on the board. I will never take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The hardest math class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Spillers is very knowledgeable, and is well versed in all matters concerning literature. The class topics are interesting, but the 10 page papers get tiring, the class itself is not engaging, and discussions quickly turn into 20-minute monologues and awkward silences. If you are passionate about literature and culture, take this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Spillers is incredibly knowledgeable and guides in-class discussions well. The novels we covered were super interesting, split up into manageable sections to be read before each class. The only grades came from three 6-7 page essays and three essay revisions. Lectures were great as long as you showed interest in the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Spillers is nice and very knowledgeable, but she's not a good teacher. The books we read were interesting, but we would only cover 10-20 pages a day for 4-5 days, and then try to rush through the last 100-300 pages in a single day, usually skipping the majority of the book. Lectures are boring and ramble-y, and class is not engaging.

Very intelligent and loves literature. However, she's consistently late, doesn't give good grading criteria, doesn't return work in a timely manner, and really doesn't follow the syllabus. 2 page paper per week, 3-4 novels (long and boring), 3 ten page papers per semester. Would not recommend.

Great race and feminist scholar underrated by students at Vandy. An easy grader as long as you show genuine engagement with the texts and say something original. Felt bad for her for having to teach such an apathetic class of kids taking a survey class. Grading basis still stands. Fantastic lecturer with a great deep voice. Would recommend!

This class has so much potential, and  Professor Spillers does as well.  But this class fell short of my expectations day after day.  Spillers is unclear, uninspiring, and dry to the extreme.  Did not get helpful feedback and learned next to nothing.  Do not recommend.

Doesn't respond to email. Missed class without prior notice, was late almost every day. Didn't have the syllabus on the first day, didn't stick to it the rest of the semester, and didn't provide rubrics or even expected word count for assignments. Took weeks discussing chapters 1-3 of each book and had to rush through the rest. Would not recommend.

Great selection of books you'll read. Grade comes from three 8-10 page papers and weekly one-pagers where you're supposed to present a new thesis on what you've read. Very knowledgeable and helpful outside of class (if you manage to get her)

We did not keep up with the syllabus at all, and she canceled class often and without sending e-mails. I enjoyed the discussions when we did have class, and she knows the subject very well--African American lit. She is a somewhat tough grader, but it is possible to make an A for sure. She is not my favorite ENGL prof, but she is not awful either.

"three 8-10 page papers, weekly one page papers. you have to keep up with readings." Still true. She didn't even take attendance half the time. Nice enough lady, helpful to me when I went into office hours. Knowledgeable, made up for classes she couldn't attend. I've learned more in other ENGL class I've taken, but still a fun/worthwhile class.

If you are interested in learning about how history and english work together, I would recommend this class. The professor knows her stuff, and is filled with knowledge. Her comments on my papers always improved my writing. A lot of reading and writing, but it's an english class, people! What would you be expecting?

I would not recommend her class. Pretty dry lecturer, little class discussion, and a very tough grader. There's also a ton of reading that you have to keep up with, and she takes days to reply to emails.

three 8-10 page papers, weekly one page papers.  you have to keep up with readings, attendance is mandatory.  she travels a lot, so not very helpful when you're stuck on a paper and she won't conduct office hour type topics via e-mail.  overall not a bad experience, but i'm not sure i'd take another of her classes

Professor Spinrad is one of the kindest, most genuine professors I've had. His lectures are super entertaining and he has so many awesome stories to share. The homeworks are very hard and often take a long time to make any progress on. Make sure to take good notes in class so the homework isn't as bad, because the notes aren't online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If possible, try to attend both lecture sessions, the first time to get the high level ideas (and pin down what questions you have), the second time to pay attention to those areas that confuse you. Then go home and write down every detail you remember that day. If you look at your notes, you'll be surprised how much you learned.

If you're a CS student and you don't take Spinrad, you are really missing out. Put genuine effort into this class, and you will learn a ton. His lectures are so interesting, and his stories are hilarious. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Vandy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is possibly the hardest good class (as in Spinrad is a good teacher). You'll have an easier time if you've taken his undergrad Algo course. I had taken mine elsewhere in undergrad and am currently sacrificing my grad research for this class. I felt like I needed it though and it's helping me reviewing algorithms.
If you don't come to class, you're not going to pass. The homework requires a good understanding of the topics discussed in the lecture as well as a higher-level analysis of those topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The most frustrating thing about Spinrad's class is, you can't take coherent notes in his class. That's fine, but he also moves very quickly during class, so you can easily get lost in almost every lecture. Don't take his class if you don't consider yourself a brilliant student. You'll get brutally left behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class was rarely boring due to Spinrad's great stories and jokes. Homeworks could be difficult and make you feel pretty lost, although the tests were fair for the most part. I would definitely recommend Spinrad for this course.

Prof Spinrad is very kind and friendly and jokes in lectures a lot. His lectures sometimes are confusing, so go to office hours if you're lost. Don't miss lectures, he doesn't use a book. Tests/homework are challenging, but if you like solving puzzles, this is the class for you. Put effort into learning and you'll get a lot out of this class.

Jerry's the man. Dope stories. No exams - just homeworks all semester (we had 8 total). As long as you put an honest effort in them you'll be fine. No regrets tbqh. Get ready to get schooled on algorithms, brother. :)

Dr. Spinrad is an amazing lecturer. His class is very difficult although the challenge is reasonable. His one fault is that he is not really helpful outside of class. Despite this, I do believe that if you work hard and spend time with a textbook or an online resource, you can learn a ton. Whether you'll get a good grade is another question...

Unavailable, inconsistent, and lacking in transparency, Jeremy Spinrad is one of the smartest people but worst professors at Vanderbilt. He puts no effort into his job as an educator. Do not expect feedback on assignments or help in general if you don't understand a concept. You will be left wondering your grade since he doesn't use Blackboard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a genius first of all. Second, he is a great, funny lecturer. He keeps his lectures entertaining with funny stories. He knows what he's talking about. The homeworks are hard as are the tests. Don't expect to pass by memorization. You can't. You can only pass via understanding how to think. He is one of my favorite professors I have ever had.

Take if you want to be good at CS. Tests are easier than homework cause you have less time. Can't explain your work in math? Write words. If you're right, you get full points. If you're clever and wrong, you get 7/10 and a counterpoint.  Paying full attention is more important than perfect notes. He loves effort, destroys smugness.  Dope 'stache.

Spinrad is brilliant and hilariousnot a combination you see frequently, especially not in a university setting. He keeps class engaging with funny (depending on your preferred style of humor) jokes despite the material sometimes being dry. Homeworks are hard and I recommend finding other students to discuss the problems with. Tests are also hard

Yes, lots of people say that professor Spinrad is unclear. I thought so the same way when I first entered the class. But algorithm is hard to grasp and it requires a lot of work. After I spent a great amount of time I get better and better at it and when I looked back I think that professor Spinrad actually does a good job in covering the material.

In my 4 years at Vanderbilt I haven't had a worse professor than Spinrad. His lectures are extremely unclear and he doesn't use a textbook so it's really easy to get lost. He won't help in office hours beyond giving vague confusing hints. He's clearly brilliant, but is a horribly incompetent teacher.

Professor Spinrad is quirky. He doesn't use a textbook so attendance is mandatory (if you skip more than one class, you're hopelessly lost). He doesn't answer HW questions unless you have a C in the course. Lectures are entertaining, ask questions if you're lost. Spinrad's class weeds out the amateurs from the hardcore Comp. Sci or Math majors.

Very unclear professor. Assumes prior knowledge. He uses no textbook, so there's nothing to look at for help. There's a curve, but you still need to work your ass off to do alright. Very difficult class, especially with Spinrad. Avoid him.

Spinrad should be dismissed from teaching CS 212. He spent half of the precious lecture time talking about jokes completely unrelated to the course material. When he does teach, he assumes students have prior knowledge of the concepts to be taught constantly asks open questions only to leave students new to the field confused and uninspired.

DO NOT TAKE CS 212 WITH SPINRAD. Instead, take it with Johnson. The difference: with Spinrad you will try very hard and not get a good grade. With Johnson you won't try hard and will get a very good grade. Spinrad is not an effective lecturer and the work is extremely difficult.

Dr. Spinrad is awsome and very funny, but if you don't like thinking or working then don't take this class. TAKE NOTES ON ALL THE PROOFS HE DOES ON THE BOARD HE ASKS SIMILAR OR IDENTICAL ONES ON HOMEWORKS AND EXAMS

Great professor. Crystal clear teaching style with minimal use of the book. Encourages you to THINK and solve creatively using the material taught in class, rather than to just regurgitate or calculate mindlessly. Hilarious guy.

dont let my numbers discourage you dr spinrad is a great professor he is very difficult and will not help you on homework assignments but will always go back over the lecture material with you if you dont understand something in lecture say so IMMEDIATELY and he will explain it again the material is childs play for him so he makes difficult exams

Don't expect A's or answers to be handed out to you - you have to work for them. This is good, because what he teaches delineates a code monkey from an actual computer scientist. He's a funny guy, he cares about his students, and tries to be fair. Come to class ready to learn, and you'll enjoy your semester.

Prof. Spinrad is extremely intellingent. He generally assumes the same of his students. If there is something you don't understand get help IMMEDIATELY. Be prepared for some heavy problem solving: not so much calculations but more heavy thinking.

Hard tests and homeworks but not impossible. Go to class, everything on the tests/homeworks is from class. Zero use of the book, you don't even really have to buy it unless you want to. Don't bother asking him questions about homework before you turn it in, he'll just answer with some sort of riddle, causing you more distress. HILARIOUS prof though
Awful professor.  Very unclear in his lectures, requiring that you learn everything yourself.  Then he gives you painful tests and homeworks.
This guys is far and away the worst professor I have had at Vandy. I have done development work for several fortune 50 companies, and I can tell you that this guy DOESN'T KNOW WHAT HE IS DOING.
One of the best professors I had at Vanderbilt -- very intelligent, very challenging.  He expects you to work to do well in his class, however.  Slackers beware.

Spinrad is a classic example of the arrogant apathy displayed by the computer science department at VU.  He almost purposefully lectures over everyone's head, thus requiring them to attend further study sessions.  A true timewaster.
A dreadful professor.  Jerry Spinrad was unclear, unhelpful, and un-insightful.  Avoid anything this man teaches at all costs and you'll be a lot happier.
Try as hard as you can! You might get a "B". He has a good personality but slackers beware he teaches with very intellectual style.

He was my adviser before I switched majors.  His advice?  "You're an adult.  I don't care what you pick.  Figure your own schedule out."  Needless to say, I wasn't impressed; he didn't seem to care at all.
It's like murder trying to figure out what he wants...it's a passable class, but don't expect an A unless you're a problem-solving nut.
No Comments
guy is a freaking genius.... just can't teach on the level of his own intelligence.... his test are a comparison between your brain and his, beware, but you learn quite a bit
She's super kind and I love her lectures. Sulprizio is very entertaining and our class discussions were always very engaging. Participation was mandatory, so it's important to communicate. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor for core! Really helped our class stay engaged and led us to have great conversations. The class itself is a lot of work but she's really easy to contact and get help if needed.

Sulprizio is bordering on goat status. Very passionate and knowledgeable lecturer, and enjoys teaching. This class is interesting but a lot of work. 2 7-8 page papers, 1 open mic creative project, weekly pop quizzes and readings, and midterm + final. Picky with essay length (must be >7 pages). Grades ~ in line with effort. Loved her here and 1130.

She's an engaging lecturer, and is really funny. Lots of reading and pop quizzes once a week. I've had her before, and in both courses, assignments can be very vague. This allows for creative freedom but makes it difficult to know what she's grading on and has cost me points. Final comedy project was fun. Prob best for people who rlly like classics
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is the worst worst worst professor I have ever had in my whole life,she made 1 credit hour class hard as if her life depends on it.I worked super hard for this useless class just to get a B.This is one of my biggest regrets at Vanderbilt.

Sulprizio is a gem. Her passion is contagious and she's super knowledgeable. Gets to know names w/o asking. ~15 pages/class of reading for weekly pop quizzes, but they're all interesting stories. 3 500-word papers (easy) + some extra credit. Midterm and final exam are easy if you read. Final is 5-page paper/project of your choice. Def participate.

Very laidback, cool prof but the class wasn't easy. 5 quizzes, 1 midterm, 1 final, 5 pg paper, 1 presentation added up to a lot of work + translating HW before each class. All the quizzes and exams weren't too hard tho bc the passages you had to translate were the same ones we did in class before (randomly selected). More work than I expected tbh.

I had Prof Sulprizio on my Maymester and she was just amazing. So kind and super knowledgeable about all things Roman history. Would definitely recommend!! Her grading is fair, all grades received were in line with the effort put in.

Professor Sulprizio is one of the best professors I've had the pleasure of interacting with during my time at Vanderbilt so far! The class I took with her was a maymester, so I am sure it is different than her normal term classes, but I still could not recommend taking anything with her more. She is understanding, flexible, and just lovely.

Had her for Greek Myths, readings before every class (about 20 pages) and 1 pop quiz a week.
