Attendance was mandatory and is not very lenient with unexcused absences despite her syllabus only saying "5 allowed absences, use them wisely" for the policy. Papers graded oddly tough and she does not always specify why points were deducted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Had her for 1130 Greek Myths. Def one of the better profs for this class, but lots of reading for HW, weekly pop quizzes, 4 papers (3 short, 1 long), and 2 exams. Caring, interesting lecturer, and a very fair grader. Seemed like a lot of work for what is often taken as an elective, but I guess that's expected in classics.

She knows her stuff very well but to a level where if you can't match it, you will not be able to get an A. She can be rude and condescending if you need help understanding a concept. Lots of small details are needed on tests. Seems like she needs to like you in class to get an A on a written assessment. Very very picky with written work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Sulprizio is super caring and passionate. She genuinely wants every student to succeed and will provide extra resources and time outside of class to do so. There is "cold calling," but it is honestly beneficial to learning the language and I think it helps to discuss perspectives on translation or interpretations.

Straightforward tests and quizzes with everything on them (passages and grammar) gone over in class. There is a participation element with you translating in class, but its not too daunting and Prof. Sulprizio does not expect perfection especially with more vague Latin. Super interesting content and a super caring prof who wants you to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Constant cold-calling in class which can be anxiety inducing. Class should have been a low-stress elective, but I had more work in this class than any other.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: People are just mad that this course wasn't an easy A, but ofc it's not it's a 3000 lvl course. You have to do the readings (which aren't tedious/unnecessary), show up to class, and write the papers. Prof. Sulprizio did a great job at listening to student feedback for the first-time class, and it really wasn't that hard if you made an effort

Book is same as 1102, creates her own worksheets sometimes which is really helpful. Attendance is expected but you have a few days allowed that you can skip. Honestly the most fun class I've had and the most amazing experience getting to spend a whole year in Latin with Professor Sulprizio and my classmates. Long live 1102 and our trivia night!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had at Vanderbilt. Her classes are disorganized and boring and her entire course for 'Classical World on Film' is lifted from a book chapter by chapter. Should have been a fun, low-intensity class but she made it miserable. Lazy and doesn't care, she gives the classics department a bad rep. Avoid at all costs!!!
She's obnoxious and a hardo about piffle subjects.
Her tests and quizzes are sometimes hard, but she grades fairly and leniently. This class is not an easy A, but if you put in the effort, you will be able to get an high score.

One of my favorite professors in the classics department. Class time is used to discuss readings, of which there's a pop quiz over every week or so. The exams were super easy if you went to class and took notes, but she is a little tougher on the papers. All in all, she wants to see your effort but also roots for your success!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Sulprizio is a great choice for intro Latin. She is very clear about expectations in class, but expects participation out of everyone to help us learn. She was very lenient this year because of covid, but if you showed up to class, did the homework, and put in some work memorizing the vocab it was an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sulprizio is amazing! Class is always interesting, she's so chill and supportive of whatever answers you say to her questions. There's around an hour of reading for every class, and usually a pop quiz every 1 or 2 weeks. Just stay on top of the readings, and it's an easy A. Definitely take her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. The material is very interesting, and the professor does a good job of reviewing concepts from the readings in class. Class time was mostly used to discuss the material (give your opinions about it, relate it back to life, etc.). A midterm, a final exam, a final paper, few responses, and a few reading quizzes.

Prof. Sulprizio is a shining example of what a Classics professor should be like. Doing well in the class requires doing rather lengthy readings often, but the details are explained well in lecture. She gives great feedback on all assignments and is very fair with her grading. Keep up with the content, and engage in discussion with your peers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Papers in the class were graded a little harshly, with some confusion. Allowed paper rewrites for B's and lower. There was a few extra credit opportunities. The reading was essential for the course/papers and made the pop reading quizzes easy. I found the exams to be easier than the papers. Dr. Sulprizio is also nice and a hoot in class. No final!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Extremely harsh grader. Very hard to get an A. Stay away if you are not a classics major and want an easy A/A-. Cannot stress enough how much I disliked this useless class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: hard grader, all essay tests, horrible study guides
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had! Very understanding and unlike a lot of other professors I've had, seems genuinely excited to teach the subject. She's very clear about what she expects and as long as you take good notes during the lecture and pay attention during lectures you'll be fine. Would take any of her classes. Good sense of humor!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Always provided clear instructions for the hw. Participation isn't hard. Subject material isn't hard as well, just make sure you know the vocabulary and she drills all you need to know effectively so there are no surprises on quizzes. 10/10 would take again.

Dr. Sutton is a nice professor but has clear favorites and inconsistent grading. Lectures and exams are disorganized, with no study guides or practice tests. Quizzes and homework are easy 100s. However exams can be confusing, hard to interpret, and heavily impact your grade. Take this course only if required.
Highly recommend taking this if you are a chem major and/or need a W. Very relaxed class with a few pages of writing a week. Not graded difficultly at all.

Dr. Sutton is a great teacher. She genuinely cares about her students, and wants them all to do well in her class. At times the class' material is a little disorganized, but she is always clear about what she will put on the exams. The exams are not difficult and it is not necessary to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sutton is so sweet and caring. A lot of the stuff she focuses on during office hours shows up on the exams. The first midterm and the first few quizzes were pretty intimidating. However, it gets a lot easier once you get used to the format of the class/content. Also, highly recommend taking the lab; it helped solidify the concepts really well.

Professor Sutton is very caring and receptive to feedback during office hours. The class itself was honestly quite easy. 1/3 of the grade is basically automatic 100s (take-home quizzes and online homework) and the tests are not very difficult either, although they require a bit of studying. Overall you learn a lot and the grading is very generous.

Random weekly quizzes in class that you work on with the people around you. Tests are easy, and you get basically free points in the homework and quizzes as long as you put in a good effort and go to class. Dr. Sutton is super nice and really encouraging to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Sutton is one of the most caring professors at Vanderbilt. She cares so much about her students, and she also cares about continuously making her class better as well. The class isn't easy by any means, but once you get to know her style, it gets way better. Make a connection with her, go to office hours, and take the lab (CHEM 2100L) as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sutton is a caring teacher, but this class is not an easy A like other reviews have said. Her lectures are very disorganized and she often goes on tangents, especially during office hours. I can not recommend going to office hours enough. Making a personal relationship with her during office hours will be important. Be aware of pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: sutton is insanely kind and funny, but pretty disorganized. she goes off on tangents a lot and her exams feel super unpredictable, but lots of grade buffer in the hw/quizzes. once you understand her test and teaching style, its pretty easy. but dont underestimate the class. its def more challenging than people say.

Dr. Sutton is a great professor who genuinely cares about the success of her students and wants them all to do well. The class itself is challenging, but if you put in the work, you will succeed. Definitely go to her office hours. Highly recommend taking her class.

Lectures are all over the place, but since the class is so easy you can laugh it off. Homework is negligible. She really does care about the students, and if you show interest in the material she'll beg to talk to you about it, which is sweet. Not the best at writing test questions, but you really don't have to worry because she'll give you an A.

Sutton's a good person but that shouldn't be confused with being a good professor. Class is disorganized, and exam questions are confusing, convoluted, or vague. This was especially true on the final. Not a hard class but a miserable one to get through tbh.
I love Dr. Sutton! One of the most caring and nice professors ever. The course this year was a bit sporadic, but none of its really her fault.

Dr. Sutton genuinely cares about you, she's sweet and inspirational, but doesn't really go that in-depth during lectures, which bothers people who actually want to learn stuff. At least half of the material overlaps with gen chem or high school chem. Would definitely recommend taking for a good grade.
Sutton's teaching style isn't about grades but about learning the material. Her exams are fair and she wont let you fail. Highly reccomend

Dr. Sutton was extremely passionate and always available to help. Her analytical class did an excellent job explaining the importance of lab based chemistry and should be taken by anyone hoping to get involved in research or interested in the field. Highly recommend taking a class with her.
Dr. Sutton's labs were excellent. Many of the experiments she has you do are very similar (calibration curves and such). Once you get that down, you are set for the semester.

Easy A.

Dr. Sutton did a great job at teaching this course despite seeming more disorganized than us at some points. The exams are straight to the point, and she relates all topics to something any person can recognize. She somehow takes a topic like analytical chemistry and makes you not hate going to the class. 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Sutton is an amazing prof. and it is very clear that she cares about her students. Lots of pop quizzes during class but they are open note and collaborative. Lectures can get disorganized since she goes off on a tangent a lot but going to her OH helps clear concepts up. Textbooks practice problems aren't very useful when it comes to exam prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a girlboss. Really cares about her student's and strongly encourages problem solving, critical thinking, and colaboration. Almost every class had an open note, group, pop quiz, which were really helpful for understanding the material and preparing for exams. That said lectures were pretty disorganized and textbook was useless. Hilarious prof

Easy A. No quizzes, no exam, no prelab, no BS. Just show up, follow the procedure, and write a basic lab report. TAs were excellent. Some cool experiments with CBD/THC, pregnancy/covid tests, etc. Much less work that orgo/gen chem lab and emphasized collaboration.

AChem lab was pretty solid. V casual compared to orgo. Labs were designed to be highly applicable (drug tests, pregnancy tests, cosmetics safety, etc.) None of the experiments took more than ~2.5 hours, and most were less than 1.5 hours. Reports were pretty straightforward, and on multiple occasions she waived the report/made it a group report.

WOW. Dr. Sutton is such a great person, and she really changed my view on Vandy STEM professors. She made a really challenging class very doable. I would take any class of hers in a heartbeat. She is more than willing to accommodate test dates due to stress. You will have to work for a good grade, but she is a great resource.

Dr. Sutton was the lab instructor for CHEM 2100L this semester, and she and the TA's did an amazing job at making this lab informative, enjoyable, and applicable to research and other scientific applications! I truly enjoyed this lab and feel that I have gained many valuable skills this semester! A great choice for a chemistry lab course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Sutton is an amazing professor! She truly cares about her students and pushes us to succeed. She does a great job at demonstrating how the concepts we learn can be applied to research as well as other real-world applications and is very accessible in office hours. Highly recommend!! One of Vanderbilt's best!

Sutton for 2100 is a solid choice. She's vry lenient on grading and will give you a lot of points back. Group quizzes sum up to a 100 on a midterm at the end of the year and final replaces worst test. Very sweet and caring professor who is very accessible and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She was extremely flexible during covid and overall just a lot of fun. Forensics is a great, chill elective for the chem major/minor. The structure is very unique compared to other chem courses. You'll get a lot better at finding the important parts of scientific articles, presenting, and synthesizing information.

Literally my favorite professor! Super sweet and cares a lot about her students. The course is challenging and the material is definitely detailed, but Dr. Sutton does a great job of making students feel prepared in capable. She also brings in lots of real world applications so that you really feel like you're learning something useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you have to take A Chem, definitely take with Sutton over the other professor. Gives good clear lectures, and provides lots of opportunities to practice problem solving for tests with in class group quizzes and Sapling homework. She really wants her students to succeed, so if you put the effort in you will do well. Made lectures fun and engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Sutton is incredibly caring, and she definitely wants every one of her students to succeed. She is very accessible outside of class for any questions. You'll probably have to learn a lot of the material on your own, so the only real reason to attend lecture is to get the clicker bonus points she offers. A great choice for Gen Chem students.
She relies on class a lot on only practice problems and doesnt walk you through much. Her classes werent that helpful if you dont already have an idea of what youre doing.

Take Sutton if you don't mind learning from the text book and want review questions in class. She cares about the class and wants everyone to do well, but can be a little all over the place. Definitely not a bad intro chem professor, especially for those with a decent chem background (the class is still insanely hard though).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This review is tainted by the unnecessarily difficult and confusing curriculum she had to teach. She clearly cared about how her students performed and even added extra office hours the week of her due date (heavily pregnant by the end of the semester). Her class average was higher than the other three professors.

Dr. Sutton is kind, dedicated, and an amazing lab professor. She made this lab much more applicable than it was in past years, and wants students to learn valuable lab skills, rather than regurgitating procedures. If you take CHEM2100, take this lab with it.

Pro: easy grader, cares about students, very sympathetic to missing lab for valid excuses, everyone either got an A or A-, cares more about your understanding of major concepts than tiny details, lots of points for completion & lab safety, lots of labs in groups so you aren't going through it alone Con: weekly quizzes, long lab reports

Not a good intro level prof. Uses clicker questions as a crutch. Doesnt teach. Hugely hormonal this semester as well on account of her pregnancy. More and more disorganized as the semester went on. Very caring prof though, and not the worst out of the gen chem pool.

She is super nice! always holding extra office hours to make sure students understand. Plus, she is humorous and very caring to her students in and outside of the classroom, like showing up for class several days before giving baby birth lol
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Sutton was my lab instructor for Analytical Chem lab. She made a considerable effort to make the labs meaningful and representative of what is actually done in the chemistry world. She sometimes tried to put on the persona of a tough grader, but she does not. She appreciates effort, and there were many easy points to gain towards your grade.

Sutton was a really interesting lecturer that was generally easy to follow and gave you all the tools you needed to do well, even if this sometimes meant a lot of reading. She was a little disorganized at times, but she was always super helpful during office hours and is super passionate about the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Sutton is truly an amazing person. She endlessly cares about her students and will do anything to help you succeed both in and out of the classroom. She may be a little unorganized at times, but I really think that's just because she's so excited about the material. If you have a chance to take forensics or analytical, do it

Professor Sutton is completely incompetent. Her course expectations are vague, there's no consistency in her teaching style, and her "student-involved" classroom is an excuse to do nothing while we struggle through problems on the board. Tests are just ridiculous. She picks questions beyond the scope of the material, and is surprised when we fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer, really caring person. Very helpful in office hours. 2 tests, a final, homework, and 11 quizzes, of which the best 10 are graded. While they are pop quizzes, they are open-notes and collaborative, which means that you should aim to get 100s on all of them. She really wants you to succeed.

Here's what I remember from Sutton (took her last year). She always wanted her class to have the best average on the exams, so she was willing to do whatever it took to help you. She worked a ton of problems in class (occasionally her math was off, but the logic was there). If you want to learn, sit near the front.

I agreed to write one for her last year (long story) but didn't see her name; however, I like to keep my word so here's my rating.  She's super helpful in office hours, but was a little hard to follow in class (it was her first year last year).  The tests are standardized but I didn't find general chemistry terribly difficult.  Just go to class.

When it comes to Gen chem, regardless of the professor (I had Todd and Sutton), you MUST READ THE TEXTBOOK. I would often bring my book to class and read instead of listening to Sutton lecture. She is a sweet lady and can be helpful in explaining some concepts but at the end of the day, read the textbook and work the problems in the chapter review.

Gen chem is going to be tough no matter what professor you have. That being said, Sutton really wants you to succeed.  Go to office hours--she's so nice and loves working with you.  However, in class she can be disorganized and often makes mistakes.  Read the book before lecture and you'll be fine.

I switched to her lecture for my second semester of chemistry. BIG MISTAKE! She constantly made mistakes, and I felt like she did not take our education seriously. She relies way too much on the book and homework to teach us. Even when begged to work problems out in class, she outright refused! This has been my worst experience at Vanderbilt so far

Dr. Sutton is by far the best chem prof. Her lectures are good, but I think what sets her apart is she is SO willing to help during office hours & she clearly cares a lot about the success of all 150+ students. I don't like chem, but I want to do well just because of her energy in class. Also, she brings snacks for everyone 3-4 times per semester!
Best 102 professor. Wants you to succeed and is 100% willing to talk to you outside of class. Helpful as any in class. Work outside the lectures is necessary.
She's engaging and helps understand the concepts.

While I can't speak for other courses she teaches, this has been my favorite so far at Vanderbilt. Difficult content, but the course is so reasonable in workload/design/extra credit allowing for actual enjoyment/internalizing of the material without stressful cramming or rote memorization. Great lecturer and accessible + understanding I loved her!

We used the Oxford Animal Behavior textbook for this course. I found it to be extremely enjoyable and fun to attend. Maybe the other students had a different experience with the other courses, but PSY 3715 was far from difficult, and I had actually learned a lot. Exams were free-response and covered the same material as in class. Will take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this class! Quizzes 2x a week, very few resources given. Often told us to "google it" instead of teaching her content (which is not google-able) or giving resources. Exams: hit or miss. Either decently okay or terrible. Even though I got an A, I didn't learn anything. Useless lecture. Respectfully, she is just VERY bad at explaining things.

Don't take this class. Her online textbook is confusing & unfinished. We NEEDED the textbook for tests and homework. When the average was an F on a test she sent an email blaming us for it. After the final, she changed her grading scale causing many grades to drop. She takes feedback poorly. Her syllabus is not accessible or clear. Avoid the class.

A massive issue with this course was that no grading scale was provided in the syllabus. After the semester ended was when she decided where to draw the grade boundaries based on everyone's final grade. Many issues arose and she handled it very unprofessionally based on the extremely petty responses she gave us. Does not handle feedback well.
The worst worst worst Professor that I ever had.

Taking Dr. Herculano's NSC2201 course was one of the most rewarding decisions I've made in my college career. It was a lot more work than I expected, but this information stuck. She is a passionate lecturer and cares about her students.

 Last comment: GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS! Her brain is a trove of information you can't find elsewhere!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Herculano is clearly knowledgable and deserves the respect she has earned, but she does not structure or teach an intro level class well. Her lectures jump around too much, she expects students to cover way too much on their own, and she can be very unclear with instructions. I would trust the neuroanatomy reviews, but avoid intro with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her grading criteria was so unclear. Spent forever making her diagram, just for her to say that people didn't follow directions on it, when there were none. She expects you to read her mind. On the final, it might seem easy because it's prompt formed, but somehow she managed to take points off seemingly arbitrarily. Avoid at all costs.

I really respect her as a researcher in her field, but she should not teach this class. Her expectations were super unclear with so much left open for interpretation. The homework was more frustrating than it should be, and the midterms were not intuitive. The final was easier, but the class was not good at making people interested in neuroscience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class if you love word searches. Take this class if you love spending HOURS scavenging through a self-designed uncompleted textbook and graduate level lecture slides. Grade is based on daily fill in the blank exams without a word bank, two exams (fill in the blanks), one final (free response) + diagram. Fails to five clear directions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the definition of the worst class ever. she is the worst lecturer ever and expects you to read her mind on any of the so-called "fill-in-the-blank" assignments.  the grading scale is so unclear that no one knows how they're even doing in the class until the last exam. all exams also had an average of failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I've ever taken. She is disorganized, condescending, and unapproachable. Neither the "textbook" nor lectures coincide at all with exam content, and the exam averages have both been Fs. She then blamed the class for not doing readings, even though the poor exam scores were clearly a result of her flawed teaching. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not only is she the worst teacher I have ever had, she provides the class with the worst supplemental materials I have ever seen. Somehow it turned into advanced neuroanatomy for the entire last half of the semester, and with her teaching and resources, it's just impossible. Take this class if you enjoy pain.

Please do not attempt to take this class. The professor is a genius, but may be the worst teacher I've ever had. She wants you to know "EVERYTHING" about the brain, yet she teaches NOTHING. How is that even possible?This is the biggest waste of a semester. Textbook is awful. Most unorganized website I've ever seen. Save yourself.

Genuinely has no place being a professor. Everything was made unnecessarily difficult and half the stuff she emphasized was never tested while random details about obscure things were. Taking this class was an absolute nightmare and is making me want to drop neuro major as a whole. The curve on this class better be crazy.
This class is so poorly put together that it almost feels like she wants her students to fail. Major props to her TAs for being literally the only good thing in the gigantic mess

HORRIBLE CLASS. I am a Neuroscience major, but after this class, I'm highly considering dropping. As several reviews have stated, the textbook is just a website with hundreds of incomplete links containing irrelevant information and tests are impossible. Lecture time is spent repeating the same words over and over. DO NOT TAKE with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The 'textbook' is confusing and disjointed, and the lectures are nearly impossible to decipher for the daily FIB quizzes that only test your ability to scour her website for the correct word. We all struggle because we don't "read everything", and she only goes over about 20% of the content in class. A nightmare, do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has the potential to be a interesting and good class. However at the moment it is very difficult, as the textbook is a work in progress, especially during the later sections. The class is curved heavily though. The class will most likely be better later on. Also, going to office hours for both the TAs and her makes the class much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class could be good, but right now it's just not. The answers to homework are not found in the lectures and her "textbook" is absolutely horrendous (it's half-finished and difficult to connect to individual lectures). When >50% of the class failed the midterm she blamed us for not reading her awful textbook. Do not take.

All the quizzes and exams in her class are fill in the blank and if you don't write the word that makes sense in her brain, you get it wrong. It doesn't matter how much you study, you will fail her exams. After everybody failed her second exam, she told the class that it was our fault and to study harder. The "textbook" is very confusing too!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class because I thought I would want to major or minor in Neuroscience, but I will never take a neuroscience course again. And all of the tests are fill in the blank which are so hard and the average was failing. She also made her own online textbook which is itself extremely confusing to navigate. Do not take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Herculano is clearly very smart. She is also a terrible teacher. She suggested that students learn via google as she failed to give a textbook and her self-written "online textbook" was only finished with about 2/3 of the content for exam 2. She teaches how she learns and fails to teach in other style. She should stick to research.

Professor Herculano is very well acclaimed in the neuro field but has questionable teaching strategies. She uses an incomplete textbook and her lecture slides are barren. Your grade depends fully on fill in the blank quizzes and exams which are phrased in a confusing and misleading way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class as a psych distribution, and Herculano made it really interesting. Despite my lack of interest in neuro as a topic, I really enjoyed her lectures. She's a great teacher and is super passionate about what she teaches. She's so fun, sweet, and positive!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is very respected in the field, but I think she struggles explaining her knowledge at a level for undergrads to understand. She assigns hours of reading before each class in a flipped classroom style. Tests are fill in the blank and is tough! However, if you're willing to work, you can learn so much. She emphasizes function and connectivity

I took the graduate version of the "mezzanine" course neuroanatomy. This course focus on the central nervous system components other than the cortex, which really gives you a lot of "a-hah" moments even if you have been study neuroscience for a long time, because a lot of "hows" and "whys" would have never been covered by some ordinary lecturers.

If you are a neuroscience major, you really must take this class. You cannot know your neuroscience without the neuroanatomy. This class will definitely be a lot of work. You will need to read research papers and brace yourself to be challenged. Still, you will learn a lot as long as you put in the work. Exams are doable if you study and go to OHs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Herculano is the best professor I have ever had at Vanderbilt. While I originally went in expecting to be required to memorize brain parts, her emphasis was systems/networks. Her teaching really gave me a broad overview, rather than particular and tedious details. If you really want to understand the brain on a whole, take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had at Vandy. The course is difficult because of the content of it, but Dr. Herculano makes an extra effort to ensure that everyone in the course understands the material. If you put in the work, show up to class to take the quizzes (before each lecture), and take good notes it easy to learn a lot and succeed.

Dr. Cho is a great prof who clearly loves what she does. The class itself isn't too difficult -- there are 6 homework and a final research paper (70% of grade), but luckily she's not a tough grader. Lectures are very confusing though... I usually left class feeling very overwhelmed by the content (probably because the class is 3 hours long though)

Lectures are straightforward and to-the-point. Highly recommend for people planning to do research in psychology; the class covers the basics of psychometrics and its application well. The instructor is very positive and always willing to help.

Professor Cho is one of the nicest professors at this school. She has been the most accommodating professor I've had given the circumstances of this semester. She is always willing to talk outside of class, and will spend however long it takes to make sure you understand a given concept. Very reasonable workload too. Highly recommend.

I love Dr. Cho so much. She is incredibly sweet and clearly cares for her students. Although Psychometrics has a lot of abstract concepts, she tries really hard to accommodate and make sure everyone understands. There are 6 homeworks for the semester and 3 exams, all are open note and not difficult with a little review. I'd definitely recommend her

I'd disagree with the severity of the other comments here. Took her F25, and while she wasn't a great professor, she cared and tried, though that often fell indequate of student expectations. While the 2212 content isn't exactly easy (lectures are boring + students are unengaged), the exams are pretty easy for how hard the homwork sets are

dont take her. even if u have to dont. make sure u dont. she doesn't know how to teach. never ever take her class if you want to pass. you will have to do all learning on your own. she does not know how to articulate words to make people understand. never take her class if you want to survive.
The lectures are useless. I do not recommend her section.
An outstanding human being. We need more people like her in this world.
Thank you for being a true conservative. The greatest professor I've ever had!
Good professor but can be a little dry.

She is conservative and doesn't pretend to be anything else. She listens to students' views though. She is a pretty easy grader on papers. May be Vanderbilt's most prestigious professor (appears on Fox News regularly). Before Vandy, she was a professor at Princeton. Definitely a good PoliSci class to take.

Not a hard teacher or class at all. Her class is definitely different than other PSCI classes, and it is discussion based. She is VERY conservative and has no reservations about it in class, which some find irritable. But, she offers a unique and very interesting perspective on things, I definitely recommend taking it, regardless of your politics.
horrible teacher, tests are easy if you study on your own.
She is amazingly boring.

Good teacher- pretty cool background; you definately want to read the textbook, but her lectures outline the main points of the book.  She's definately open about her political views, but it's OK to disagree with her.

Odd course, odd teacher.  As long as you agree with her views, it is an easy A.  But if you question her or challenge her opinions, she becomes unpleasant to deal with.  Some in the class complain about her right wing views.  I dislike all her new hairdos

Professor Swope is a must take for philosophy. I've never loved the philosophy subject but he makes it bearable and interesting! Read the readings and participate and you'll be golden. He's always accessible outside class and is a very reasonable grader. I'm so glad I took him for this class.

Professor Swope was one of the best professors I've ever had at Vanderbilt. Even though logic may seem like a boring topic, he really made class engaging and was so helpful. Would definitely take him again!

Prof Swope is very caring for his students, and obviously cares more about the content of the course than the grades. I found the lectures interesting and engaging, and his expectations were very clear and easy to meet.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great choice of a professor for PHIL 1002W. Half of the final grade was weekly discussion posts graded on completion. The other half was 2 essays. He's a reasonable grader, and is always available outside of class to meet during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Tairas gets a lot of hate he shouldn't. His class is fair. He's not a great lecturer, so most people tend to zone out and not pay attention to his lectures (which I did as well). But the homework are very fair and exams/quizzes are all doable, with only the MCQs being hyper-specific (think ISD but worse). Impossible to 100% this course, but easy A.

assignments are easy, but quizes and exams focus a lot on details and require deep understanding. personally recommend using ai to generate mcqs to test your understanding to prepare for the exams.( works for me.
the class's test is not that hard if you pay attention to during lecture and spend some time reviewing. do not mislead others if you do not pay attention during lectures....

Tairas is an extremely sweet man. He really cares about his students. The homeworks are very easy albeit tedious. The quizzes and exams are quite hard and require extensive studying of the slides. He includes some absurdly obscure details in the exams.
Too much homework. Never take his class again
Shameless prof never recommend, but nice to his students
Lots of assignments that aren't that hard, but exams are brutal and pretty much requires a ton of memorization or true deep understanding. Good teacher, decent lectures, though.

By numbers there are a lot of homeworks, theyre pretty easy, most of them are tedious, but none of them are super difficult. Reads off of the slides for the most part which is boring. Tests are 45% of your grade and insanely difficult. Tests tend to lose focus on conceptual content and focus on specifics from lecture slides and obscure details.

This man is the worst lecturer I have ever had. Couple that with the dry course content that is CS 3270 and you're in for a bad time. Homeworks were easy and helpful but exams were absolutely brutal. He asks the most obscure multiple-choice questions that are barely explained in lectures and expects perfection. Worst CS class at Vanderbilt
Prof. Tairas is a nice person in class and is willing to answer questions. The lecture is a bit easy compared with the homework and exams, but it's the way they expect you to learn in CS.

Lectures are good, but almost all of your learning is gonna happen on PA's. Assignments can be hard at times if you don't have coding experience, but they're usually very time consuming. Exams are pretty reasonable if you're doing ok with PAs. As a work of advice, it's better to submit PA's on time with some bugs than take late penalties.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: PL is a watered down class with a lot of unnecessary content, but it has some useful things. The assignments are very straightforward and easy, but the exams require some review. While lectures are dry and attendance isn't taken, you basically have go everyday for random TopHat. The book isn't that important but is a good reference.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Robert is a nice guy but is not understanding at all. His lectures are long and monotonous, and he isn't very helpful outside of class time. He knows a lot about python but his homework assignments are extremely difficult and I never felt prepared for them after attending lecture. Exams were very hard and nothing like the practice exams given.

Lectures are fascinatingly boring. He's a fine instructor but doesn't really do a good job at explaining already mind-numbing content in an accessible or interesting way. Course itself is okay. Tairas is very cold sometimes - gives off the impression that he cares only about his students' grades, and not about the students themselves.

Professor Tairas is a great CS professor. The course is easy in itself and his lectures make it even easier. The programming assignments can be a little challenging sometimes, so it's important to start early. Definitely recommend taking his CS 1101.

As someone who has had no CS experience before, I spent a lot of time outside of class to teach myself. It was definitely a time-consuming class if you have had no experience with CS because there are programming assignments every week, and they can be much more challenging than the information learned from lectures. Definitely go to office hours.

An average lecturer, but definitely take him over Hajiamini, the other CS1101 lecturer. The Programming Assignments are very time-consuming, and even with a 5 on AP CSa, I still find the course very challenging. The slides is very helpful if you misheard him. Do all the works he assigned ahead!
Very strict on deadlines.

Tairas is deeply average. He lectures with his slide deck every class for 50 minutes. You really don't have to pay attention. He's a fine teacher, frankly. You won't have any problems taking him. The programming assignments are pretty fun, at least!

PL is pretty easy, but it's more of a prolog+racket programming class than a programming languages class. The projects are rather straightforward and I'd estimate maybe a 2 hr workload a week outside of class. That being said, we had full access to compilers and notes on exams so I'm sure the class would be harder without that.

I mean overall I enjoyed the course but the professor was nothing special. I think that the deadlines were strict because of the high expectations in the school of engineering but I didn't have too many issues. IMO you should take this professor over the other one because the class is simple and intuitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably the most organized professor I've ever had. The class involves a lot of assignments and will take a lot of your time. However, if you are willing to devote a good amount of hours each week to the class and you do all the assignments, it should not be a difficult class (I had never coded before).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures on Zoom are pointless. You can ace the class without them, just skim thru ZyBooks activities. EXCEPT when he adds a question/weird syntax thing ONLY mentioned in lectures. That isn't even standard practice. He shows examples in the lectures, but they're hard to follow/unhelpful. Also doesn't budge on grades. Seems nice, but lame prof.

While his lectures weren't the most interesting over zoom, you can tell he really loves teaching and knows what he's talking about. If you pay attention to the lectures, you should have a pretty easy time passing the class but it's definitely a solid amount of work (not overwhelming though). Him and the TAs are also really responsive on piazza.

The class is alright. It's a pretty generic introduction to programming course. I wasn't a fan of the textbook being used, but otherwise it was a solid class for those that don't have much programming experience. If you do, however, you may find yourself bored and the class a bit annoying.

I have little programming experience and I think Tairas created a good introduction to all the fundamental concepts. Starts out really easy but gets more difficult by the last few weeks of the semester. He was very organized even in all this COVID-19 mess. The TAs are very helpful and Tairas is very accessible (and answers questions super fast).
Tairas is great. He and all of the TAs are easily accessible out of class and they do their best to help you succeed in the class. I highly recommend.
The lectures aren't super exciting, but Prof. Tairas is very accommodating and does his best to make sure everyone succeeds. This is a great class if you don't have a lot of programming experience.

Really great class that's not bad at all even if you have no prior coding experience. Lectures were kind of boring but he makes good power points and always posts them. Programing assignments were easy at first but got much harder and more time consuming as the semester went on. If you like problem solving, a lot of the work can be pretty fun.

Professor Tairas is a super nice guy who is really passionate about what he does. His lectures are very well organized and helpful, and he's a really approachable guy. The homeworks are pretty easy because the specs are really descriptive, but the tests are harder than you might expect.

An amazing CS professor. Super nice guy and is truly caring, has a slightly unique lecture style but it really works. Also probably the most organized guy I ever met, when classes went online with COVID he was still incredibly clear and organized.

Tairas is a really great lecturer and clearly cares a lot about his students. He's super helpful and accessible in office hours too, I would highly recommend taking him. At first in lecture it seemed like he was babying us and I found his style of lecturing a little odd, but once the class content got harder I came to appreciate it.

Graded by entirely TAs, and grades can vary heavily depending on which TA you have. The professor doesn't care to review TAs' grades and gives unhelpful feedback. Smart guy, but would learn just as much by reading material yourself. Lectures are informative but drawn out unnecessarily. Unclear grading and refuses to round.

Bane of my existence. Lecture was 75 minutes long, but we would only get through 3-5 slides/week. The worst part was the 3 essays (worth 30% each), graded by TAs, no rubric. Even after going to office hours and never missing a class, it felt impossible to grasp their expectations. In hindsight, I learned, but not enough to justify losing my sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Talisse is not real, I swear. Lowkey an easy class. Grade is based off 3 10 question quizzes and 3 papers. His TA's are nice graders. His lectures are based off of the powerpoint, so you don't HAVE to go, but he will scare you with "pop quizzes." He is very interested in you putting your own original philosophies into your work. Cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall you could tell that he cares a lot about his students.If you take the time to meet with him he will ensure you do well in his class.However he also is prone to long off topic tangents ranging from his ex-fiancé to how he thinks having kids are immoral and has said in class he does not care about 90% of students.Class is interesting though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Contrary to popular opinion, I thoroughly enjoyed Prof. Talisse's class. His lectures are very intense. Grading is done entirely by TA's. If you aren't into philosophy do NOT take this class. Honestly, it was super disappointing to see others not take this class seriously. Have an open mind, try to keep up with the readings, and go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are dull, and the only reading assigned is from two books he wrote that you must purchase at the beginning of the semester. Three exams are take-home essays of about 2,500 words each, and the TAs entirely do the grading. There are much better classes for Poly Sci, Philosophy, and LHS credit.

This is a class where you get out what you put into it.The first half is definitely more conceptual than practical but it seems some people enrolled in a philosophy class expecting not to engage with philosophy. I learned a lot and its always fun to be able to quote Aristotle. As a political science major - take it!!

Everything tagged in his rating is the opposite of what he's actually like. Somewhat of a funny guy if you get to know him, but besides that, the lectures are a snooze before the last couple of months. The worst thing is you actually have to listen to the lectures to do well. He does love philosophy but as a political science major - don't take it

Very eccentric but also pretty funny guy. Readings are never very long and his comments on different subjects can be interesting. Tends to talk in circles when discussing certain topics which puts a damper enjoyment. Has two midterm exams worth 30% each and a term paper worth 35% which are graded by TAs and can make or break your grade.

I genuinely believe that the people rating him poorly just aren't putting in effort to actually understand the material. His examples only sound like "crazy tangents" when one hasn't bothered to do the readings for which his ideas engage with. You can "get by without opening the textbook", but perhaps engage earnestly consider learning something...

Talisse really likes to hear himself talk. His lectures are intense. He yells about the topic for an hour going on tangents with examples that don't really make sense. You are graded with only 3 papers graded by TAs. Honestly, you will probably just learn more just reading the texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's the opposite of all the things I tagged. When people say his lectures are insane, they mean it--and not in a good way. The grading criteria for the papers he gives says one thing when he actually wants the opposite. Clarify everything with the TA and if you do poorly, go to him. There were only 5 papers--2 midterms w/ 2 papers & a final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: This guy seems like he took drugs before every class, he talks in circles and then starts talking about clubbing babies to death. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Talisse is intelligent and a very typical "philosophy guy". Attendance not mandatory, but if you go to class and listen carefully to what he said, you'll get lots of insights into political theory. Two midterms are two 1200-1500 words papers each and final paper is 1800-3000 words. Grading criteria a bit unclear and doesn't use slides though

literally love the man so much. not cuz the class was easy cuz it WASN'T but man this guy's iconic. Don't come into his classes cocky; the purpose of his courses is to entertain theories and dig deep. You don't have the answers! There aren't clear answers to philosophical questions and if you pretend you know what your doing you will look dumb.

Perhaps it was due to the online format and the larger class size than he normally has but this class was honestly awful, the volume of reading was far too massive and unless you have a prior interest or knowledge of political science many of the readings are hard to follow thus making engagement with the general course difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He tends to be too slow. Definitely recommend him more for in person class than online classes! He's brilliant and accessible!

I took Dr. Talisse for Intro to Ethics and 3620, and he was amazing for both of them. He is one of the best professors in the philosophy department. However, both classes were graded on just two exams and a final paper, and the exams only had about eight questions a piece, so each question significantly impacted your grade. Very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Literally never opened the textbooks once I realized that all of the exam content was covered in lecture. He is so interesting - class is easy, just two exams and a final paper. Grading is based on these few assignments but if you pay attention you'll be fine. He is super accessible and interesting, which makes studying for the class enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Talisse is opinionated and goes on tangents, but the class is not difficult. There is a standard amount of reading for a philosophy class, two straightforward tests, and a final paper. Go to class and do the readings and you'll be fine. He loves when students participate and debate with him in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really like him. He's interesting and will turn your perspective on how our society functions upside down. However, some of the material can get a bit dry. You have to go to class or get the notes from a friend - the exams are based on the lectures only, pretty much.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: This guy single-handedly fed my heretofore non-existent interest in philosophy and, even though it was quite a few years ago, I STILL discuss some of the things he taught me. Arrogant? Perhaps. Brilliant? Absolutely. Definitely recommend his class. Prepare to have your mind thoroughly blown.

Honestly, I like the guy. Pretty big ego though. His way, or the high way. It's like he uses philosophy to protect himself (prob childhood trauma). He then debates students until to show them they are wrong. TONS of reading, but thats expected. Exams are fair. Attend class. Do reading. You'll be fine. 2 exams, 1 6-8pg essay.

I loved the material of this class a lot. I hated the way Talisse presented it. He was incredibly unhelpful. He never communicated with his students beyond spending the entire class hour taking about the text. If you miss class you're pretty much screwed for that material unless you get notes from someone else. He also seems to be quite egotistical
Fun prof. The class is kindof hard but he makes it interesting and fun. I'd take him again.

By far the best professor I have had at Vanderbilt!  Incredibly passionate about his subject.  Takes an interest in his students and truly cares if they master the material.  Creates a great classroom atmosphere with his willingness to answer questions.  If you get the chance to take a class with him, do it!  Your perspective will never be the same

Philosopher in every sense of the word.  If you're insecure in your beliefs, don't take a class with him.  Otherwise, definitely take his classes.  It will open your mind up.  Don't let his confrontational approach get to you.  It's nothing personal...he just questions things for a living.  I love the class.
Easy CPLE math class.  Dry sense of humor.  Have to go to class because of pop quizzes.

this class all depends on your TA.  I got an aweful one and my section suffered.  The TA grading is not well regulated, so some grade really hard while others are very easy.  It is not a very fair or ETHICAL setup.
Professor Talisse was the worst philosophy professor that I have ever had.

i almost got scared away the first day, but i am glad i stayed. tests are not too difficult but a lot of grading depends on TA. talisse has good lectures...he is bitingly sarcastic and doesn't seem like a very nice person, but gets his point across well
Gets a bad rep for his in your face approach. Some can't handle the Socrates treatment, but you'll learn more from this guy than almost anybody else.  Normal guy outisde of class.

He puts up a front that he is a jerk. But he knows his stuff, teaches well, and does truly care about his students. That may not come across in the lecture, but if you have a conversation with him it does. As far as 105, alot depended on the TAs.
great class.  he picked some great books for an intro class and presented them in an interesting manner.  i learned a great deal every day.  he's a bit intimidating though and is very opinionated.
in terms of easyness it all depends on your TA, he doesn't grade and I got screwed with a hard TA.  Other people I know who are halfway retarted did better than me because they had an easy TA.
How "clear" can Formal Logic be?  He's fun and energetic, a bit of an ****, but it's an enjoyable kind of feistyness.  Easiest grades since 9th grade Algebra.
Grading was fair.  You decide what grade you want.  He does curve.  Was not too fond of him using the F-word.  I can't ever imagine Logic being so compelling/exciting/emotional to justify the F-bomb.
Very bright and energetic. Knows his stuff. Cares about students.  Personable.
Brilliant man and very friendly.  Learned a lot.  Would highly recommend his class.
Talisse is a brilliant professor overall.  He may try to shock the class the first day so that some people drop.  His tests are, literally, the easiest tests I've had since middle school.
Egotistical and demanding without clear grading criteria.  If you worship her as a cult leader, you'll get an A.
Ape her opinions and tell her how brilliant she is and you'll get a great grade.  Those who can't do, teach.

Assigns long critiques on plays that you have to go to. Do the reading so you can participate in class discussion which is a part of your grade. Terryl gives great feedback on your papers and allows (requires) you to rewrite them to get a better grade. Take this class if, and only if, you are interested in theater.

There's a reason Terryl's higher-level courses are called the "B-hive". If you choose a play she doesn't like, it'll be very hard to impress her. She's unclear about her requirements for paperwork, and seems to find email impossible. But she's a likable person and really loves theatre. Don't get hung up on grades, and you'll learn a lot from her.

She was one of the best directors, mentors and colleagues I could have ever hoped to know and work with.  She was Hermia to my Lysander, taught me how to audition, encouraged me to leave the University of Michigan and attend The Juilliard School.  She and Jon were vital to my success as a working actor today.  Greg Jbara

A really great FYS. Terryl always comes to class excited and makes the material fun. She's definitely my favorite professor this semester. The show critiques are not difficult as long as you put in effort, nor is the reading. I'd recommend the class to theatre majors and nonmajors alike, but it's very helpful to have as your theatre prerequisite.

I highly recommend Terryl's Seminar.  Yes, she can be strict, but this is to weed out the flakes so those who are genuinely interested and show a little effort can prosper.  She is very understanding and sympathetic and a great person to know your first year at Vandy.
Take this class!  Terryl is fun and really sweet, and the critiques are opinion based - so a lot easier than the other seminars.  A great overview of Theatre in a casual, intimate setting!

I highly recommend her freshman theatre seminar, "Trash or Treasure."  I had no experience with theatre before this class, but I really enjoyed it and got to see a lot of great plays.  There are only 5 critiques the whole semester, and the final is a one-act play.  Terryl is always funny and interesting.

Pretty easy A. 3 papers worth 60%. Participation is 25% and short reflection papers are 15%. Participation matters a lot and she will cold call but very low stakes cold calling. Papers are worth a lot but u can rewrite 2/3 and she gives u really good feedback so the rewrites are guaranteed A. Overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: super chill, easy grader. attendance is mandatory but shes super chill about it and lets you make up missed classes with short papers

Prof T is not an easy A, but she gives great feedback on your essays that are fair and helped improve my writing. She takes engagement seriously, so I recommend closing your laptop during discussions or leaving it in your bag. Participate in discussions, and she will really appreciate it too (be prepared for some low-stakes cold calling).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far one of the most interesting classes that I have taken and Prof. Teukolsky was amazing. Fair grader, gives great feedback on papers, and clearly wants her students to do well and enjoy the class. Participation is important but lectures were engaging so that wasn't really an issue
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Teukolsky is so kind and passionate about what she teaches. She really encourages you to think critically and be open-minded, which is especially appreciated when it comes to answering paper prompts and participating in-class. She's also a really nice grader—I don't know where thoughts otherwise come from. She allows for re-grades, too.

She brings a lot of energy to the class. Some of the readings are kind of tough, but worth it. We get to revise the papers if we want to. I needed a couple of extensions on due dates. Loving the class so far!
so strict
She is awesome, especially in class discussions. Gives a lot of feedback on papers, with a revision option. We read some amazing science fiction & watched 'Jaws.' Take her if you can!

Teukolsky seems sweet but she has unreasonably high expectations. Class discussions are interesting, but her grading is vague + harsh. Her essay prompts are often vague. Most importantly, the class did not really discuss what it promises to discuss, which is the question of word vs. image. It was an aight class to take, but certainly not the best.

A very caring professor. Course wasn't the most interesting, but she gives great feedback on essays and lets you rewrite them to improve your grade. Always encourages students to participate and encourages students to meet with her outside of class to discuss essays (which I recommend) Easy to make an A if you take her feedback and meet with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Shes very very nice. I am not the best writer, but the feedback she gave me (and what she taught in class) allowed me to get my grade up by resubmitting them. The class itself on 19th century criminals was actually rather interesting, contrary to my original belief. I am predisposed to hate English class, but she made this one enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a sweet and thoughtful professor. Lectures and discussion are so interesting and she puts so much attention to detail in assignments and lessons. Best professor. If you get the chance to take a class with her, count yourself so lucky.

Professor Teukolsky is the BEST prof. She made me love Victorian literature and did such a fantastic job weaving historical context into the discussions of literature. She was really understanding about COVID. She's so organized. She mixes modern media with old novel. She allows students to revise for a better grade, and is tough but fair. So fun!!

I'm only halfway through the class, but I love Professor Teukolsky. She hosts engaging lectures and encourages original thought. She never makes you feel stupid, but is always willing to work with you to improve your writing and understanding. She is accessible, kind, flexible, and incredibly passionate and supportive. One of my favorites so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Teukolsky facilitates excellent and thought-provoking discussion in class. Professor Teukolsky values the input of all her students and makes an effort to encourage all students to participate and share their opinion. She allows you to rewrite any of your essays for a better grade, and you can make up attendance points for days you missed

Class was held entirely online. Attendance was mandatory and class was mostly discussion about assigned readings. The grade is mainly based on three papers, and the feedback given is fair. Follow the prompts, don't procrastinate, and you'll get As. Prof. Teukolsky is very kind and gives informative lectures as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Teukolsky really stimulates class discussion. She is very involved in students' learning and holds you accountable rather than letting you slip.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She was my favorite prof last semester. The class covered a lot of different topics, like South African history and the Vietnam War. I ended up talking more in class than I usually do. Recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She definitely helped me improve as a writer. Some of the books were kind of tough but class discussions helped. The class was actually fun at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Love the class & the prof. Recommend if you like talking about books and movies together! Good class discussions, not too many books.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of the worst profs I've had. She graded harshly, gave vague essay prompts & unhelpful feedback, assigned an insane amount of reading (even for an English class), gave us a ridiculous take home essay to do over Thanksgiving break & acted like we were all idiots. I didn't learn anything in this class other than to avoid Professor Teukolsky.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this prof ain't it. prof teukolsky comes off sweet, but over the semester, you see how unreasonable she can be. she has an innate disrespect for students, refuses to consider anything other than the literary canon, and grades papers on very inconsistent criteria that differ greatly from class discussion (i.e. she once asked us to define simile).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Teukolsky's classes are discussion heavy but are confined to rote thematic analysis and characterization. Prompts, grading criteria, and feedback for essays are vague both before and after they are assigned. This class is intended to be an introductory course that can be skipped by students who wish to pursue literary studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As a first year English major this class genuinely made me consider switching to STEM. It is evident she does not know movies, she thinks you can't understand English unless you have a PHD, and she is extremely classist. She spent a full ten minutes explaining what a similie is. This semester  an academic lobotomy. Save your soul and avoid.

Worst professor I've had at Vanderbilt. She is extremely cold and rude to students she doesn't like. She'll snap at you for asking what she believes to be a stupid question. Harsh grader with no solid criteria and blanket grades papers if you don't go to office hours. Avoid her if you care about good class discussion or valuable insight.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class content is so interesting and fun to read. She definitely grades papers a lot harsher than expected and your grade is only based on a few things. It's pretty hard to make an A but if you're ok with getting a solid B, I'd recommend taking the class because you'll learn so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Teukolsky is an awesome professor. She is clearly super knowledgable about the course content, and she fosters engaging discussions that always leave me feeling like I've gained a new perspective. Her grading is very fair -- go to office hours and make sure your paper's argument makes sense, and you will be fine. I would definitely recommend!

Great at leading discussions and makes everyone's comments feel valued. Open to fun tangents and often relates course material to pop culture. Paper topics can sometimes make you feel like you just need to re-package material directly from the lectures.

Professor Teukolsky is oddly specific about how her class is run. She asks to speak to you after class if you're late and cares a little too much about attendance. She also writes paper topics that are literally a paragraph, so it is obvious she wants you to write her way. Overall, she is super sweet and if you do it her way you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Don't let her scare you- she has high expectations but she is really sweet. So much knowledge on Victorian Britain. Gives great feedback and is very helpful during office hours. She has clear expectations so meet them and make friends with her and you will be fine. Lectures are all discussion based but can get kinda boring. Expect A- if you try.

Before a paper is due, go to her office hours, listen carefully to her ideas and incorporate them in your paper. I did not have much writing experience, but following this strategy paid off. Only 3 papers, not too much work. She makes the class interesting and I learnt a lot about crime in Victorian Britain. This class is worth taking!

She pretends to be tough, but she's really sweet. Reading quizzes are really easy and announced, which is nice. Tough on papers, so you can't BS your way to an A. Likes to have the class break into groups for short discussion and likes to make big lists on the board. Good prof if you're into Victorian lit.

She's nice and will be happy to answer any emails you send, but takes tardiness VERY SERIOUSLY. If you are late, she will stop what she's doing, look at you, and ask to speak to you after class. Otherwise, quite boring but harmless.
Easy grader, knowledgeable about Victorian literature, and class discussions are nearly always interesting.

I took Teukolsky for a class on the poetry of the Victorian Period.  So the readings for each class were pretty short.  She is very helpful in class discussion and office hours.  Her grading isn't too hard, and she gives the option to revise and extra credit to get a higher grade.  I learned a lot in this class and I definitely recommend Teukolsky.

She's great, she really knows a lot about the Victorian period and really wants her students to do well. Class discussions are interesting, not a difficult grader, always willing to help. All in all, an awesome professor here.

Professor Goddu was very condescending at times. Her grading was extremely unclear which made it very hard to get an A on papers. I showed her a paper outline and she advised that I change it then gave me feedback on the paper by describing the outline I should have used...which was the original outline that she told me to change.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You will learn from this class, but not because of the assignments. (all same essay, pretty dry) Value is from discussion and because Morrison is a legendary writer. Prof wants work done a VERY SPECIFIC way and doesn't really equip you to do it. So if you want to succeed, be ready to make this class one of your top priorities.

Very kind and helpful. She is very understanding about assignments and accessible outside of class. Take her Toni Morrison class - one of THE best classes at Vandy. Really eye-opening class that introduces new perspectives and if you love literature like I do, her class is for you. Great and I highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Goddu thinks she is god's gift to teaching, so she comes across very patronizing. You get one grade at the end of the semester as she believes in 'ungrading'. Confusing expectations and she doesn't take responsibility for her own ineptitude. Overall rude and condescending. Would expect more nuanced interpretations from an English Prof.

I love Professor Goddu. I took her Toni Morrison FYWS. Lots of reading, lots of writing, and great feedback but tough grading. She will really make you work for your grade. An "A+" paper in another class is an "A-" for her. An "A" paper in another class is at most a "B+" for her. To get an "A," you are going to need to give it everything you got
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Goddu is a wonderful, caring person and a great professor. This class teaches you a ton about the environmental humanities and you read some great works. Not too difficult to keep up with the readings, but she does expect a lot on writing assignments and grades toughly. She also expects constant participation. Overall, a fantastic class.

Professor Goddu is honestly the sweetest Professor I've had at Vandy yet. She really understood and took into account the pressures of this "unique" semester. She actually focuses on helping her students become better writers rather than grading their work. That being said, 2 am Redbull driven essays don't cut it in this class, she expects effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Got one grade all semester and ended with a B+, wack!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Goddu is one of my absolute favorite English professors at Vanderbilt, and the Toni Morrison class I took with her was a transformational experience. Professor Goddu is incredibly intelligent, kind, and accessible outside of class. She also gave detailed and thorough essay feedback that really helped me grow immensely as a writer.

Toughest grader. If you think you will improve as a WRITER in her class, you will improve to be a writer that she wants you to be (meaning there are incredibly specific expectations from her and if you fail to meet them you will not get a grade that reflects your efforts). She does offer lots of office hours, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Goddu is easily the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt so far. She is INCREDIBLY intelligent and knowledgeable about her subject and she moderates/drives discussions so well. She's thoughtful and thorough with her feedback on papers and is also extremely helpful during office hours. Very challenging, but SO intellectually stimulating.

Dr. Goddu is AMAZING. Toni Morrison is my favorite class I've ever taken and everyone in my class is obsessed with her. She'll make you work hard on your papers, but gives helpful feedback and went out of her way to do writing workshops. You'll become a better writer and English student. If you are passionate about literature, TAKE HER!

Professor Goddu was one of the best teachers I have ever had. She will push you to work the absolute hardest you can, but is extremely fair and wants you to succeed. Her classes are always lively and will force you to think in new and exciting ways.

Prof. Goddu's Lit & the Environment course is probably the most relevant course you can take at Vanderbilt. It was a challenging class, but the work load was manageable and consistent. Her aim is to make you a better writer and to make you care about climate change. She has spent years crafting her pedagogy and it shows. You MUST take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Goddu is an incredible teacher. She does expect a lot from students, but also gives incredible, honest, and constructive feedback on papers in return. She is always willing to meet outside of class, and only assigns readings with a purpose. I never felt like I had "busy work." I am a better writer because of her. Highly recommend!
Amazing. high expectations but so caring. Invested in your development as a student. Good sense of humor. Great books. Her climate fiction class has great recent books!

Professor Goddu is a fantastic teacher, mentor, and intellectual. Her Climate Fiction course (Literature and the Environment) is one the the best courses I have taken. It opens your eyes to the realities of our changing world in an engaging and imaginative way. Professor Goddu creates a welcoming and fun atmosphere in class.

Professor Goddu is an amazing professor. She has high expectations but puts in the time and effort to help you meet them. She is super understanding when life interferes with class assignments/meetings. She will make you a great writer. Highly recommend
