Professor Goddu is a gem of a professor. She has high expectations but she will push you to create a real argument and argue it flawlessly. She doesn't ask you to do too much reading and she is very accessible outside of class. She worked with me when my writing wasn't up to par and I'm finishing the semester a much better writer with a good grade.

A great professor. She will teach you how to write an airtight argument. While her standards are higher than the average english professor, she makes herself extremely accessible outside class and gives your writing a ton of attention to help you rise to the challenge. Teaches contemporary texts and shows you why the english major is still valuable

One of the best professors I have had at Vanderbilt. Take her!! She is always fair, caring and thoughtful. She is extremely dedicated to students - although she is challenging she wants nothing but everyone to succeed. Her class is fun and interesting you will learn A TON. Highly recommend.

Professor Goddu has extremely high expectations, but she does everything she can to help you to meet them. I've never had a teacher who provoked as deep a level of thought and analysis as she did. Definitely good for you in the long run.

Professor Goddu's class was interesting but her expectations for paper's were incredibly unfair. We were forced to read really dense books in a week and then write a paper the following week and she would rip it apart. Nice lady and interesting class/material but a hard grader.

One of my favorite teachers I've ever had - interesting, engaging, helpful - but she was unfair in grading. All semester she gave constructive criticism, but on the final she ripped everyone to shreds. Be careful in her class. You can never be sure what grade you'll get.
Horrible professor - highly critical of students, played favorites, and seemed more interested in tangents about herself or her own research than teaching the material

Prof. Goddu is one of the best professors I've had. She was always very well-prepared for classes, made sure that everyone contributed, and available to students outside of class. She does have high expectations though; she grades pretty hard (but fairly) and expects you to participate in discussions.

I had this professor for the WS major capstone class-our only assignment for the semester was to write a (mini) thesis.  class was disorganized, to try to make up for the lack of content she would assign trivial light books like "The Writing Life" -no academic value.  She also often projected her own insecurities on to her students..not admirable.
A very brilliant professor, but very demanding in class.  She's so organized it can be frustrating.  Probably not a class you'd enjoy, but one that would be good for you in the end.

A wonderful professor who really makes you think about your statement.  She is big on making sure one has proof from the text to back up a statement. Her quizzes keeps students in line and also helps with discussion.

Professor Goddu makes you feel like you are doing well in the class, and then smacks with you a lower grade than you deserve after the course evals are filled out.  Other than that, she's a very engaging teacher.
No Comments

Nate Tenpas cares about students actually learning. The tests are quite difficult because of timing especially, as there are a lot of problems in the 75 min given. However, he gives a lot of partial credit, so don't leave anything blank. Also, make sure to understand "why" you are learning what you are learning, as he tests that.

Nate is simply the best. No other way to put it. He explained everything so well that I walked away with a truly deep understanding of calculus. Super fun and energetic guy, which is nice in a class like this. Can not recommend Nate enough! He actually made my first semester so much better. Love the guy, total chiller but somehow also the best prof

A fantastic professor. He is charismatic and funny in class, and he made it a point to get to know each of his students by name. While the tests and graded problem sets were on the harder side, he definitely made it worth your while to come to office hours. Lecture was very dynamic- rarely did it feeling he was just teaching at us. A good class!

If you have the option to take Nate, do it. He's definitely one of the better math professors at Vanderbilt, even being a grad student. He makes it a priority to know all of his students and is extremely accessible outside of class. Tests are somewhat hard, but not unreasonable. He also curves pretty generously when the average is too low.

Tenpas is an amazing professor. His lectures give you a clear gasp of calculus and he makes it very fun and intuitive. The tests and homework's are a little bit difficult but very fair. You will come out having a strong foundation in calculus and understand it for what it is and not how to just apply it. He's an absolute gem in Vanderbilt.
Most grad students get a bad rap but this one is the mold breaker. Great teacher and lecturer. Hard tests but he gives a good idea of what to expect.

Class goes asynchronous during COVID. There are a lot of lecture videos to watch every class, but she grades everything fairly with plenty of extra credits. The grade is mostly determined by seven quizzes and three exams, and she drops the lowest 2 quizzes, which is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is pretty straightforward. I had taken formal logic first, so that helped a lot. I can see how Henning may not be the best lecturer, but I think it is worth coming to class for sure. Do the practice/homework and take it seriously and you should be fine. Don't expect an easy A in any college course.

Professor Henning didn't always understand people's questions in class. But, she doesn't grade the homework: just 3 tests (the third is the final but not cumulative) and 7 quizzes (lowest two dropped.) Not good about giving you extra practice problems, but the ones she gives are similar to the tests/quizzes. Also gives study guides for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I have ever had at Vanderbilt. She somehow found a way to make an easy class difficult. Her teaching is extremely unclear, and she was unable to answer questions in class in an understandable way. If you ask her a question, she basically just repeats the question to you while staring at you. Take this class with anyone else.
Don't take this class. lecture is boring and she just weaves her political opinions into everything. grade is one paper and her grading doesn't make sense. definitely don't recommend

If you want to take Prof. Walden's class, be ready to only write 1 paper that your whole grade is dependent on. A few other assignments such as summaries but your main grade, for this writing intensive course, is decided by 1 paper that is both the midterm and final. Students left class crying; she told one of them to drop out during office hours.

The lectures were a mess, clearly copied and pasted from other sources and just thrown together, she filled every slide with a huge block of text. Exams were WAY too long, many students stayed 30-45 mins after. Didn't get grades back for months, didn't get to see feedback. No guidance for exams. Went on personal rants and told stories too often.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Thinks telling hundreds of long stories about her adult children, with lots of gestures in a really loud voice, is teaching. Her powerpoints have ZERO organization. Two papers - gave no concrete guidelines on how to write them, then graded each completely differently. Refuses to help anyone study for tests in any way, even weeks in advance.

She is very vague about how to prepare for tests, giving te impression that it will be easy if you know the concepts. The test did not cover concepts, and the questions were so difficult to understand/comprehend. idk where the heck she gets those questions from either. EPIC FAIL as a teacher. Don't take her. p.s. She is an airhead
Tedra has a *lot* of energy which made the class fun for me.  I recommend her freshman seminars!

she is such a sweet teacher, but doesnt really give much direction in terms of what she wants out of her assignments, which makes her deceivingly hard.  she really likes what she teaches though, which makes the class interesting and she really values her students' opinions and what they have to say

very unclear explanations of notes in classes... you basically have to read the entire book to do well on tests her multiple choice is really difficult.  very ambiguous directions for projects but if u go to her she helps.
Don't get stuck with her, especially if you are a guy. She automatically thinks you won't do well if you are one and grades that way. Not helpful at all and the tests are pretty hard.

Avoid her at all costs. The class is very hard to sit through. She talks as if you were a child and tests you on material you never cover.  The test questions are based on minute details that do not relate to the overall topics. Very annoying.

Talks to students like they are 5 and then tests like you are grad students.  She requires group projects and does not give clear directions.  During these presentations she likes to interrupt and is often rude to students.  I do NOT reccomend her at all.
Not to impressed with her as a professor. Nice person, but not a very good teacher.  Class was hard to sit through.

Well respected in the classroom but is likely tenured. Perhaps no longer has a deep interest in advancing the program (Blair) as a whole, and just wants students to have fun and enjoy music. Very good conductor, kind, and patient.

Professor Verrier is a deeply caring conductor, he loves you, even if you frustrate him. He's so inspiring on the podium and wants to see you succeed. Notably great with latin American music, he gets the wind symphony moving and grooving.
He is the kindest and most passionate person you'll ever meet. It is an honor to have been able to be in his ensembles. 100/10
Staying in the Blair orchestra is so fun and literally made my day. He is an experienced conductor and gets sentimental at times...so great!
Very Funny, great conductor!

Prof Beckers is great at lecturing and knowledgable on contents. He is energetic and really cares about if you get the concepts. Grading is very lenient and not a lot of work. Highly recommend taking his class!

The concepts of this course are incredibly difficult: lot's of linear algebra, stats, multi, diff-eq, etc. That being said, the homeworks allow you to use AI, and are graded leniently. The midterm short answers are quite tough, but MCs are from the in class Top-Hat for the most part. Final was all MC, but this time mostly not from the Top-Hat.

Beckers is a fine person, but he teaches at a level that isn't very friendly to those not familiar with machine learning concepts, so be prepared for a lot of self-learning. The grading in the course is also incredibly lenient, with most of the homework's being given a 100 if you just did the bare minimum. Overall easy class, but didn't learn a lot
FIRST!!!!!

I was majoring in Neuroscience without a clear idea of what I wanted to do in the future, but his class on Brain-Computer Interfacing completely changed my perspective. Now, I'm inspired and eager to learn more in this field.

Professor Womelsdorf is great, the class was super early in the morning so that made it hard to pay attention to lectures. Get ready to write a weekly 2 page paper plus 2 long 10 page papers for the semester. The course is very interesting though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Womelsdorf was definitely one of better professors I've had at Vanderbilt. There are weekly essay reflections (which he gave full credit for just doing), participation, then 2 larger essays (for feedback he would tell you what exactly to fix), as long as you put in the work its an easy A.

I took Professor Womelsdorfs BCI class, and it was honestly a great experience. Lectures were interesting and well planned, class work made sense and actually expanded on the topic, and the class was actually enjoyable. He was a good professor to talk with and cares about his students. Very professional, and I would take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Womelsdorf is an amazing professor, the topics are super interesting, there are no actual grades (you won't receive a number or letter on individual assignments, if you do them and do them like you care then you will get an A), and discussions are super interesting. I really wish I could take this class for another semester.

This class is absolutely amazing with Professor Womelsdorf. I encourage anyone interested or not interested in the subject to take this class. You will not regret it. He is so informed and a pioneer in this field. So knowledgeable and intriguing.

Prof. Womelsdorf was one of my favorite professors this semester! He really cares about his students and is really passionate about the topic of BCIs. I would absolutely recommend this class to anyone. It's not difficult to get an A as long as you pay attention in class. Super interesting subject, great professor, highly recommend :)

Amazing prof, class on BCI's was very interesting. Work involved mostly writing topics papers along with 2 more intensive essays, however that was simply the nature of the course as a First Year Writing Seminar. Overall great choice, definitely would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a pretty good professor. She does read off the slides (that are published on Brightspace anyways) but I would still encourage going to class. She grades mainly on 3 response papers, the midterm, and the final, all of which I would say are graded fairly. Overall, the class was okay, but I feel like I could have learned more.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only grades for the class are the three response papers, the midterm, and the final. There are extensive readings for each class, and you should do them because you need them for the papers and exams. She grades fairly. The class is not very interesting or engaging because Professor Thrower just reads off of slides. She does not offer much help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Thrower is an average professor. She reads directly off slides, assigns three response papers that you can do well as long as you follow the rubric, and a midterm and a final that are graded somewhat arbitrary. She gives extra credit. If I had to take her again I would, but I would not be excited.

Professor Thrower is kind and somewhat approachable, but she only teaches class by lecturing off of slides. There are readings assigned for every class that have major relevance to the response papers and exams. The response papers are easy to do well on if you just follow the rubric. However, the exams can be difficult to study for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Basic polisci course. There were 3 response papers that had easy to understand instructions and rubrics, hard to not do well on. Two exams. They are only writing, so you need to have all the info memorized. There was at least 1 reading a day, and actually read them since they are discussed in class and they are important for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind and smart professor, but she didn't seem to care that her TA's grading was so arbitrary. Vague instructions caused students to be unaware of what Prof wanted. She admitted fault and compensated us by dropping the lowest scored essay, but I still felt like it was unfair. Lectures are fine but she just reads off the slides. Study hard for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting class, just not the best execution. Thrower is super kind but lectures were rushed at times and in-class activities were a bit disorganized. Grading was also heavily dependent on TA and was quite nitpicky (e.g. thesis, grammar), particularly with the 5 reflection papers worth 30% total. But great class if you're thinking abt a psci PhD

The class is 5 3-4 page essays and 2 large writing style tests. Participation is 10% . The grades you get on most things depends on the TA. Thrower is very nice. Most classes are slideshow lectures and some classes are activities like a debate or something else. A lot of readings if you choose to do them. A is doable.

Dr. Thrower is really reasonable with grading and gives opportunity for extra credit. I definitely learned in this class. You must read and participate. The class consisted of 4 mini papers, 2 larger papers, and a final paper before the coronavirus hit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class material was much more interesting than the class itself. Prof Thrower is not the most engaging lecturer and basically reads off the PowerPoint. That being said, the class is not hard or a lot of work.

A lot of "uninspiring" material but she is not a boring lecturer and she often had us work together in groups. There are only a few grades and they are all papers so the grading can be tricky. Reading for every day, and it can be difficult to participate without doing it. She is very approachable and I would definitely take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Thrower was obviously very excited about the content she was teaching, but she expected us to read A LOT of material for each class and remember very specific theories. Also, she graded on participation based upon how much you raised your hand during lecture. This was very intimidating for an introvert like myself. Not an easy A.

She was hands down one of my favorite professors this semester. She's very accessible and kind to her students, and she's great about answering questions (or, if she doesn't know, looking up the answer). She assigns a lot of reading, but she goes over all of it in class. She emphasizes participation. Would definitely recommend.

This review is for PHIL 3891 - Ethics of AI. As a freshman, I was pretty nervous taking this class filled mostly with seniors and grad students but Prof. T made it the best class I've ever taken at Vanderbilt so far. Discussions were amazing, I learned so much about AI and its implications in society. All around amazing teacher, pretty easy grader!
This is actually for PHIL 3891 but he is amazing in a seminar setting. Values quality over quantity in terms of work, so not horrible on long essays etc. Take him!

8 weekly response papers (1 page) but you can drop two of them. 2 three-page papers and one 4 page paper and TAs graded really generously. Feedback and grading criteria is unclear, but as long as you do the bare minimum you get an A. Ppl stopped coming to class cuz the lectures aren't super inspirational or anything, a bit abstract for my liking.

Grading done by TAs but this was his first year and he adapted when students were feeling overwhelmed with reading. Lecture is optional and supplementary and he now records them which is nice. Very reading heavy. TAs know what they are talking about and writing is very technical and clear. Don't write with fluff. Thorstad does care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Thorstad is a feedback oriented professor who genuinely cares about his class and how his students are handing the workload. He changed his entire syllabus halfway through the course and cut readings by nearly 50% because students (including myself) were having a hard time balancing all the readings. Overall really passionate and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Thorstad is a nice guy and very understanding. The class is a difficult introduction class. The readings are tough and there are weekly writing assignments plus essays. If you are interested in philosophy, it is good. Also, each TA is different from what I hear.

I am in PHIL 1002 and Thorstad is a great teacher. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches and goes out of his way to help students understand course material. the class is more writing heavy than I was expecting but not overly harsh grading considering the tough material. Its a hard intro class but is very interesting and Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Taking PHIL 1002 with Thorstad in his first year here.

Was a relatively good experience, and the topics were super interesting! Some readings/lectures are definitely tough though.

He is responsive to student feedback, and when students shared a concern/complaint/etc, he adjusted accordingly.

Experience may be better or worse depending on TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Totally disagree with the recent ratings. As a current student, I think her class is fantastic. Great lecturer. While challenging, the exams are reasonable for it being an upper-level class (curved heavily). They're focused on application rather than memorizing. Blame the Econ department for the tough exams since grades are forced to be B+ average.
Fun to listen to and teaches content well. Unfortunately, content and practice exams does not prepare you well enough for the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exam does not align with the actual practice test and study guide. Don't even study because non of that actually matters at all.
No one finishes any of the exams in the time alloted. Exams are so hard don't even bother studying. None of the practice she gives will compare to the actual test.

The tests have been ridiculously hard, and I have left discouraged each time. I study so long for both for both, only for nothing I've studied to appear. The curve does no one justice. "easiest class in the department" she may say on the first day-- DO NOT believe her.

Beware. This class is not the same 4230 that used to be free play. No more essay-writing about model theory. Both tests so far have been impossible, even though they didn't seem like they would have been based on the lectures. I would NOT take this class.
tests are pretty unfair
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives extremely challenging exams without providing sufficient practice beforehand. Although there is a curve, it does not adequately compensate for the level of difficulty.

The best professor I've taken at Vanderbilt. Her lectures and explanations are super clear & good sense of humor. tests are pretty difficult but if you actually pay attention to the lectures its not impossible to get a good grade, and she curves quite a bit

Worst professor in the econ department. Tells us exams will be like problem sets but gives exams that are unlike anything we've practiced. This is a stand alone econ elective and none of us have enough game theory experience to comprehend her lectures and honestly even the exams. Unfair professor and unfair grading, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

She is a great professor and clearly a genius. There are essentially only four grades in the class: two midterms, a final, and a group presentation. The tests are straightforward for the most part, but she will always add a slight twist to what you have seen before. It is not hard to figure but you have to be pretty spot on with everything you do.

She was nice and a good, understandable lecturer. Overall, the material was pretty simple and the exams straightforward. My one major complaint was that the group project grading was arbitrary and ridiculously stringent, to the point where I almost got knocked down to an A- after getting As on every other assignment

Surprised this is a 4000-level class. You barely learn anything besides basic game theory. A lot of class time was wasted on exam review sessions and group presentations. Overall pretty easy but boring

EASIEST CLASS EVER, should be an intro class; it requires 0 prereq knowledge and could be taught in 2 weeks instead of 14. That said, great teacher and pretty chill with accommodating any issues. Free A, no assignments, attendance thru post-class form. Nice and funny person too.
She grades harshly on exams and group presentations. Provides very little feedback which is annoying.

1. i dont like how 75% of your grade is tests
2. she grades too harshly on the group presentation
3. the grading is pretty messed up. don't make any small mistakes. i made a small subtraction error and that cost me 2% of my final grade since they mark points off for each subproblem after based on your mistake

Pretty mid class. Workload was manageable because she doesn't teach a lot of content. Felt like the TA covered way more lectures compared to other classes. Not a lot of components graded and her grading criteria is very unclear, so try not to make any mistakes on exams.
the best. Take her.
Masha is the best. Lectures are super clear and midterms are easy as long as you do your work. Final can be more challenging than midterms but is not impossible

Masha was great. Her lectures were easy to understand and she always was open to answer questions from students. The exams in this class were probably too fair (averages of 80s-90s, but the final hasn't happened yet so that might change). I definitely recommend this class to any Econ majors.

Maybe the single best professor I have had at Vandy. She just has a way of taking what can be really tough material and distilling it down into a way that makes so much sense. I simply cannot explain how great she is at teaching. I often walked away from a tough lecture talking with my classmates about how great of a teacher she is. 10000% take her
Masha a real one
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you can take her, ABSOLUTELY do it. Lectures were straightforward and easy to follow. Her tests were super fair and if you studied (which you should, ECON 3012 is an intermediate class after all), you got a good grade - never any tricks or things she hadn't shown you. She is super nice and clearly cared about her students doing well.
Masha is the BEST professor I ever had at Vanderbilt. She is so accessible and one of the fairest exam makers I have met. Not to mention her sense of humor making a difficult subject fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Masha is simply the best. Probably my best prof this semester! This class can be super difficult but she is a ridiculously great teacher! Like an amazing prof. If you can take her, DO IT! I simply cannot recommend her enough. She is the best!!!

HIST 1735W (US Intelligence Community) - Very well-respected professor and extremely knowledgeable about subject. Grading is very reasonable, but could be more transparent. Accessible during office hours for paper suggestions or just casual conversation. Lectures are interesting and very enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Schwartz is the best! He had great classes and also advised multiple research projects I did throughout college. He is passionate about his work and very encouraging. He helped open doors for me when it came to research and professional experiences. I definitely recommend taking a course with Professor Schwartz!

Schwartz knows a lot about Vietnam. You'll learn a ton from his class. Attendance for lectures isn't mandatory, but it is for discussions. Know that Schwartz grades a bit harsher than his TAs, but you'll likely get more from the class if you take his discussion section too. Regardless, the class isn't bad. Two tests and a paper or so. Take him!

Schwartz is an amazing professor. His IC course is new, so he's still ironing out some details, but the subject matter is great, and he often brings in distinguished guests. He gives great feedback on drafts of papers before the final versions are due. The course isn't overly intensive either. Must take if interested in intel/national security.

Incredible professor, one of the best ever taken at Vanderbilt. Very kind and had a deep knowledge of his subject. Makes high quality relationships with students. Feel blessed to have learned from him.

Wonderful professor and wonderful class. Definitely a high-level writing class that has hard grading, but he cares a lot about his students and is always accessible to talk to outside of class. I had a wonderful time hearing about his experiences and learning about the topic. Would highly recommend, but not the easiest class!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's a disservice to Professor Schwartz and his expertise to read a negative review on any course of his. As a junior, this is by far the best course I've taken. The material is highly applicable to current events. He is so well versed in history that you will leave the class share what you learned with friends. Do yourself a favor, enroll!

Prof Schwartz is a super genuine guy and this class was really interesting. Your readings give you a more detailed timeline, but his lectures were filled with cool stories and foreign policy background. He recognized where his expertise was lacking and brought in great guest lecturers like the former head of the NSA and authors of books we read

Schwarttz knows his stuff. He is kind and understanding, yet still blunt with feedback. He handles sensitive subject matter with class, and he knows what he's talking about. Prepare for quite a bit of reading, but very interesting material nonetheless. He assigns a cool documentary that helps a lot, as well as cool extra credit opportunities.
Take his class.

Schwartz is an amazing prof with SO much knowledge and excitement to teach. His lectures are super interested and you can tell how much he both cares about his students and the material. The tests are very memorization heavy, but I just spent 12 hours cramming and got an A. He is truly such a caring and intelligent man, definitely take his class!
Such a great professor! Take him you won't regret it!

Professor Schwartz is the best professor I have had. He is a great, thought-provoking professor and  truly wants the best for every one of his students. He made time to really get to know everyone in this small class, and is exactly what a Vanderbilt Professor should aspire to be like.
this is NOT a 1000 level W. he grades based on nothing but vibes and is sooooo hard to please. I beg you to take any other W. this class has tanked my gpa like no other
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For 1735W. Quite literally the most difficult 1000 course I've taken. Grades way too hard for a 1000 course. Feedback is minimal and unhelpful. Graded on 3 papers with no grading criteria; he says he just knows good writing when he sees it. If you're taking just to take a W, find a different one. Content is interesting but not worth the hassle.

Professor Schwartz is truly amazing! His class is not the easiest, but I honestly learned so much it was worth it. Also, gives great feedback on papers and really motivates you to do the work. He is a good lecturer who kept me engaged the whole time, and his knowledge of history is fantastic. I think you have to take it purely for the experience.

Professor Schwartz is one of the best professors I've ever taken. He cares a lot about students, offers extra credit, and has options for test-takers and paper writers on the final exam. He is extremely knowledgable and will help you out if you go to office hours. Take his class if you have the chance even if you're not a history major.

Prof Schwartz is a nice guy but I would not recommend taking this class if you're not a history major because the lectures droned on, the weekly mandatory discussions added a lot of extra work + stress, and exams were insanely stressful to prepare for because they count for so much of our grade and we're expected to memorize 100+ terms for each.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schwartz is super nice and clearly cares about his content area a lot. This class, however, is structured harder than it should be. There are only a few graded assignments and it is very memorization heavy. He does offer several extra credit opportunities which is nice.

Schwartz is really nice and wants his students to succeed! I agree with the previous review about HIST 2700; the midterm and final are a lot of work bc of heavy memorization (about 110 terms on the final) and the take-home essay. But, if you manage your time well and attend his office hours/TA review sessions, the midterm and final are doable.

Professor Schwartz cares about his students and gives many extra credit opportunities. That said, Im a 3.9 student and still got a C+ on the midterm (B- with extra credit) because its very memorization heavy (the date memorization section tanked me). The final was likely harder but he gives students a research paper option if preferred.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Schwartz is a great pick if you want a deep dive into the Vietnam War. Class lectures are engaging and assignments are very straightforward. Do the work and show up to discussion sections and itll be an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Schwartz is an amazing lecturer and an absolute wealth of knowledge when it comes to just about every topic in US History. There is 1 short paper, a midterm, a final, and a few very short assignments, but you can get out of the final and paper if you write a research paper. Graded easily but likely depends on your TA
Incredibly intelligent, interesting, and respects his students. Several extra credit opportunities and the class is only graded on four items, so if you want an A it is yours to earn.
The best. Great professor, engaging class. Take this man.

Professor Schwartz is one of the greatest figures of historical pedagogy that I have ever seen. His lectures are great and during section meetings, he connects historical events with contemporary events to make the class more interesting. Gives good feedback, multiple extra credit opportunities that are not hard. Very passionate about history.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Schwartz is a great lecturer. You can tell he is very successful and passionate about the lecture material. I really enjoyed his class. That being said, the tests are a LOT of work. He gives you many terms (125 for the final) and essay prompts 48 hours before that are due when you take the exams. The final is a ridiculous amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Schwartz is my favorite professor that I've had so far, and I'll be taking him again. He is so passionate about history and really wants to see every student at Vanderbilt engaged with the department. And, of course, he's brilliant and had many experiences that make his lectures interesting.

Schwartz is an extremely nice and helpful guy and I learned a lot from his writing seminar. He's accessible in office hours and wants to help every student succeed. But, you have to work for an A and I felt like I was often writing towards his opinion just to make him happy. If you write with different views, be ready to do a lot of research.

He cares a ton about all of his students and loves seeing them get excited by his class. He understands that most of his students aren't going to be majoring in history and tries to relate lots of his class to modern day events so it's useful for everyone. His tests are a lot of memorization and a paper. He is a great professor!

Professor Schwartz is easily the most amazing professor/ teacher I have ever had. I took him for a history of the Cold War writing seminar that was so engaging and interesting, I really enjoyed it. I can't wait to take him again next semester- everything he knows is up in his head and he makes everything so fun to learn about! Be sure to take him

Professor Schwartz is a good lecturer by all means. However, his paper grading is very tough, and you must read a decent amount to write the papers. He is easily accessible in office hours, but be prepared to put in work on the 3 papers if you want to do well. Fortunately there is some extra credit. The workload is easy but the grade is hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Schwartz is a very knowledgeable and caring professor, but the golden reviews about him are misleading. You have to work hard for an A and I felt that I needed to write what he wanted to hear in order to do well. Nevertheless, he brought up perspectives of history I never would have considered and I did enjoy his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Schwartz is probably the best one out there. I learned so much in his first year seminar on the Cold War. He gives a lot of extra credit. He also gives wonderful advice on essays. He truly cares about his students. He definitely wants us to learn and do the best that we can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Incredibly nice and accommodating--it's very apparent he cares about leaving an impression with his course rather than cramming a bunch of info that will be soon forgotten after the semester. Gives out lots of extra credit opportunities to allow students to get more involved. Few assignments so don't muck up the graded stuff.

Professor Schwartz is great. He is an awesome professor, and he really cares about his students' learning. 3 papers for this class, and he gives good feedback. He makes you work hard for your grade, and I really benefitted from this. One of the best professors at Vandy. Take him if you can, and go to office hours if you need help with anything
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Schwartz went to Columbia undergrad, Oxford masters, Harvard Ph.D. He's an unbelievably smart guy and he will push you to learn the material and deliver quality work. He is extremely responsive outside of class and actively encourages students to meet with him to discuss papers and material. A real gem.
One of those gems of a professor where he is extremely intelligent, gives great lectures, fair assignments, and truly cares about his students.

Professor Schwartz is a genius. The guy got his PhD from Harvard, but is humble and loves to hear students' opinions. I took this class for AXLE, and you could definitely tell the history majors/history buffs apart from the non-history majors. Grades were given accordingly. But if you work very hard, you'll be rewarded, and Schwartz is a great guy.
Awesome lecturer. Your grade is based off of section, one paper, a midterm and a final, which makes it difficult if you mess up on one assignment, but Schwartz is worth it.

Honestly a really good Professor. You definitely need to pay attention during lectures, but he also offers lots of extra credit to encourage students to get involved more. He also seems like a genuinely nice guy who cares about his students.
Best professor I've ever had at Vandy. He's super smart, gives entertaining lectures, and is extremely nice outside of class.

Schwartz is Vandy's best professor, in my opinion. Complete expert in his field and really passes on his love of history to his students. Absurdly nice guy who goes out of his way to help you however he can. The class does have a lot of reading, but it's manageable, and the workload isn't too bad. Midterm, final, paper, section participation.
Schwartz is pretty engaging and super knowledgable, I liked him a lot as a person. Grading really depends on your TA.

Dr. Schwartz was a brilliant lecturer and so understanding of my busy schedule and busy other pre-med classes. He was very reasonable about other deadlines and activities and gave me several extensions on my papers. He expects good work and effort, and gives so much helpful feedback. TAKE HIS COURSES, your life will be changed. He's amazing.

Professor Schwartz's passion for  teaching made me look forward to class each week, even though it was a 2 and 12  hr seminar.  He makes sure students are actively involved  (rather than just lecturing the whole time), and brings interesting and immersive resources to the class. He expects quality work, and provides excellent feedback.

Simply the best. Schwartz puts a ton of effort into making every lecture as engaging and informative as possible, and as a result he'll make you want to go to class even though attendance isn't required. Be forewarned though: he assigns a ton of reading and expects a lot out of you for papers. Take his class regardless; he's truly inspirational.

My favorite professor at Vanderbilt! Professor Schwartz is wonderful: he has interesting lectures, gives very useful feedback on papers, understands his students and is an all-around great guy. This class was difficult, but if you work hard (especially revising drafts) you will do well. He is very approachable and great during office hours as well!

Schwartz is a brilliant professor who gives tons of constructive feedback and makes an effort to connect with his students. He is a tough grader, but he does offer some extra credit opportunities and if you seek out his help during office hours he will definitely point you in the right direction on a paper. Loved his class. Hope to have him again.

Professor Schwartz is amazing. Brilliant and effective lecturer. uses a lot of multimedia to support his points which is great for stimulating discussion and holding your attention. fair bit of reading but manageable if you keep up with it.

Professor Schwartz is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt.  Incredibly helpful and accessible to everyone.  His class will be difficult and you will have to work, but you will enjoy it and learn a lot.  Highly recommend him.

He's a tough, but very fair grader. I definitely improved as a writer because of him. His essay topics are challenging and really make you consider the material. He always had great comments which pushed me in the right direction though. Very interested in students' opinions. He talked as much as he listened in class.

Professor Schwartz is terrific. His writing seminar was by far my favorite class of my first semester. He was well versed on the subject matter and did a good job at leading discussion of the books we were using without dominating the class. He wasn't great with paper turnaround, but his feedback on rough drafts is always clear and concise.
While Schwartz was a very smart and engaging man to listen to during lecture, his TA ruined my experience. If you can get him one-on-one, I'm sure he is great.

Awesome professor! Extremely helpful outside of class. As for assignments, lots of reading and short papers from time to time. The hardest task was the final project which was 15-page research paper. In the end, you really learn something. I loved it!

Honors seminar for US and the Vietnam War. Take this class. Take any class with Prof. Schwartz. He assigns a TON of reading, but it's well worth it to put in the effort. Extremely humble, extremely engaging. I didn't care too much about the Vietnam War (or history) before the class - just needed it for AXLE. I'm now fascinated by the subject.

The best professor I've ever had. You will find no one more knowledgeable in their field. The class (Cold War) was by no means a GPA booster, but Schwartz is whip-smart, funny, and a spellbinding lecturer. Big class; forgive him if his office hours are somewhat packed. Lots of reading and critical thinking needed to keep up with discussion groups.

There's no better professor at Vanderbilt. I would sign up for whatever class he teaches without question - he's a fascinating lecturer and knows more about the history of American foreign policy than anyone else on campus. Also just a great guy to go talk to at office hours.

He's a very humble guy though he has no reason to be.  He's helpful, presents the material well, and makes you think really hard about the material.  He's not the easiest grader, but he's fair and reasonable.  Definitely would recommend, especially if you like American History.

Great - he's interesting, engaging, great to talk to outside of class, very interested about his students, and he knows so much about the history of American foreign relations that it's actually scary (but in a good way).  If you're interested at all in the history of politics, you have to take him!

Schwartz is very passionate about U.S. History.  Class attendance is not neccesary and the grading is easy as long as you follow guidelines set by the TAs.  Study sheets are emailed out before exams detailing pretty much everything on them.
really passionate about his subject. not really necessary to do the readings as long as you go to class and study for the tests.

A genuine person. Not insanely egotistical like most of my professors. Knows his stuff better than anyone i have ever had at Vanderbilt. Wish we had more like him here. Makes me pay attention to world events...scary.
Schwartz is my favorite professor. I've taken 4 classes with him and I periodically go to his office hours just to talk. He's a great friend to have in the History department.

Professor Schwartz's class on the Cold War was difficult and challenging, yet he orates with such knowledge and great enthusiasm that you almost forget you are being crippled by a lack of grades. Almost.
He is simply the best and most supportive! Excellent coverage of material. He makes you work, but you can be assured you know the stuff when you are done!

Schwartz was my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. He tries to scare the living bejesus out of you on the midterm, but you will learn a lot if you study like hell. You may never work harder for a C in your life, but he is brilliant and knows his stuff more than any other professor I've ever had. He is also very personable and helpful out of class.

Lectures aren't exactly on-the-edge-of-your-seat events, but as far as History lectures go, not too bad.  Falls behind lecture schedule, ie, your paper on the Cold War will be due 2 weeks before he gets around to talking about it.  Overall, okay class, but then again, I'm no history buff. :P

He's such a smart guy and a great lecturer. Breck Walker was an awesome awesome TA. Class was not hard for me but I'm very into history. Didnt do many of the readings but the TA explained them well enough that I could BS my way through.
Great lectures.  LOTS of reading but it all tied into what was going on in class.
Massive amounts of reading. You really ought to know about history and current events before taking the class, even though it's an introductory course.

He's the man when it comes to Vietnam-era U.S. and world history.  Took his class (U.S. and the Cold War) to try my hand at a history class, and was amazed.  He keeps it interesting, and is full of all sorts of information.  Be prepared to read a lot.
Schwartz loves to hear himself talk, but he's interesting to listen to.  His class is not at all boring to sit through.  He's a tough grader, though, and his paper topics are pretty challenging.

Professor Darrah was clearly knowledgeable in data science! Classes consisted mainly of lectures explaining concepts / R, easy pop quizzes just to make sure you attend class, HW assignments, and 2 exams. He loves to answer questions / class engagement so please participate! Overall Prof. Darrah was a great professor

CS1100 with Professor Darrah wasn't bad albeit somewhat disorganized near the end when he strayed off the standard curriculum. The class itself is pretty standardized and easy to get an A. He gave the most extra points opportunities out of the other sections. He's really accessible and willing to help out students who are struggling.

I found this class pretty hard. Darrah clearly tried his best but sometimes it felt like he couldn't communicate some concepts. Overall, pretty good guy but sometimes the class feels hard for no reason. The midterms and final were okay, but I would suggest keeping track on the time esp for first time coders. I did end up learning a lot though.

Darrah is very kind and listens to his students and you can see his passion for computer science. The workload (weekly ZyBooks assignments and Programming Assignments every other week) is manageable. We had two midterms and 1 final. He goes above and beyond for us to make sure we understand the material and always answers our questions.

Professor Darrah does a good job of conveying foreign concepts, especially for first-time coders. He takes his time to explain whatever concept is at hand and is eager to work with his students if they need help. He won't leave you hanging and has a very reasonable course workload.

Avoid this class at all costs. Its not entirely Darrah's fault, but he clearly hates the syllabus and is not good at teaching it. He changes the formats of the exams on whim to 'try something new' and often tests you on things you were given very little practice on. Tons of kids cheat in this class, and if you dont you feel behind. Just dont.

Darrah is phenomenal. Unlike other CS profs, he actually interacts with students and listens to feedback in live time and changes exams based on them. He pushed back an exam when there was clearly not enough coverage, yet still gets criticism from students. Darrah doesn't give himself have the credit he deserves. Take him if you have the chance.

Tim Darrah isn't a professor, he is a way of life. There is no reason not to take Tim Darrah. The homework is chill, the exams are chill, HE is chill. Darrah 4 eva. If you don't get an A in Darrah's class, you wouldn't have gotten an A in the other sections either. Darrah 4 life.

Darrah is a really chill dude, but class was kind of a disorganized mess. He was absent a ton and would tell us a test was moved when we showed up to take said test. However if you're interested in learning python it's a pretty good and relatively simple intro class.

Honestly cool dude, it's clear it was first time teaching, and didn't give 2nd exam grades back until after the final, but he addressed it and will probably be better when you take his class. Would definitely recommend, not a stressful class at all.

Could definitely tell it was Professor Darrah's first semester teaching, but I think he did his best. Lectures sometimes felt a little unplanned and all over the place, but the homework and textbook were fairly self-explanatory and made the problem sets easy to complete. Exams were fair and grading was very simple and lenient.

He doesn't explain things super well but if you ask clarifying questions he answered them until you fully understand the material. Super accessible and a super nice professor. Grading is slow but it's the TA's fault. If you take this class you should take it with Darrah

GREAT. HELPFUL. I wish everyone could have this professor. She truly cares and while the work may get difficult you are never alone and she is extremely kind and forgiving which makes for an excellent environment to succeed and LEARN. This is a high level class with a lot of content but it is interesting and she makes it very doable and fun. TAKE!

Dr.Fracchia is a great professor! Her classes are heavily discussion based but are super engaging. We only had 2 big assignments, a final paper and group presentation, throughout the semester and lots of feedback was provided in advance on your ideas. As long as you show up to class. participate, and complete your assignments you will be good!

Dr. Fracchia (used to be Dr. Saul) is a really great prof. Her class is easy (basically one group project and one longer paper), and she's super understanding and kind. She is very knowledgeable about her field (forensic anthropology) and has really cool guest speakers come to lecture. Overall, manageable class and interesting content.

I took HI120I at Colby. Prof Chavez is really passionate about what he gives lectures on. Pretty lenient on deadlines, assigned readings and essays are interesting (2 opinion pieces where you choose your own topic), participation matters - make sure you do class reading. Overall a nice guy who wants to share some of his knowledge about history.

Professor Chavez is great! I would recommend him for anyone needing PSCI or AXLE credit. His tests are mostly based on his lectures, so as long as you show up and take notes you'll do well. He also gives great feedback on essays.
Lectures and powerpoint are most lessons and he does them exceptionally well. Great character, very nice, and great teacher.

Professor Chavez is a fantastic professor. He's insightful, gives great lectures, and makes even the most mundane topics hilarious and interesting. Skipping class is possible but not recommended: his outlines and powerpoints are much easier to understand if you hear his lectures. Overall, great guy and increased my love for IR exponentially!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Chavez is a gem, honestly. His lectures are engaging, but are significantly more fun if you already have prior knowledge on the topics. My favorite thing, though, was his feedback on the op-eds; paragraphs of praise and extra questions to provoke deeper thought. Definitely the best IR class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Grades consist of two tests (midterm & final), three short op-eds, and a final 5-page paper. Tests are easy if you study (he gives specific study guides) and he is a very lenient grader. I'm an engineering student with a limited background in Poli Sci only taking this for AXLE and it's been a pretty easy class, but I've definitely learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Chavez is a fantastic professor. He really cares about the topics he's teaching, and it comes through in his lectures. His exams are difficult, but the papers you write for the class are graded rather leniently. All around would absolutely recommend Chavez for any PoliSci class

Professor Chavez is by far my favorite professor I've had so far. His lectures are very interesting and easy to understand. He gives very clear outlines for the papers and grades fairly easily. He is very willing to help students and is accessible both by email and his office hours. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy class with not amazing lectures, but he is really nice and is super knowledgeable about international relations! Readings don't matter so much
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Chavez its great and nice, but his class is lecture heavy. He assigns a lot of readings and does not reference them in class at all. I would take him again because he grades very fairly and knows a lot. Super nice but not super inspiring

He's a great professor. He's very clear on what he expects from students and really cares about the topics. He's super friendly and accessible and makes everything interesting. Currently taking another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Solid PSCI class to take, mostly test based. Very flexible with his schedule, a fair grader, and an overall really good prof. Office hours weren't necessary to attend, he read all of my assignment drafts if I sent them 1+ week in advance
For a new professor, Chavez is great. i very much enjoyed his class, he clearly cares about his students, he's funny. and he's pretty chill about individual needs and requirements.

His first year as a professor and it shows in that he's very clear with his lectures and assignments, understanding of students, and approachable and easy to talk to. The class is a little boring but it's also a survey so it's to be expected. Very clear grading criteria and a solid PSCI class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Had him as my TA--super awesome guy. He understands students, is caring, clear, entertaining, and extremely smart. Wouldn't call him super easy but his grading is totally manageable--He gives clear guidelines of his expectations that are totally reasonable. Definitely would recommend taking anything he teaches.

I learned A LOT in this class. Dr. Patterson is a genius with many amazing historical stories, experiences, and insights (although you might hear the same ones a bunch). Homework isn't hard, but sometimes can be time consuming (watching films). Only one test which was easy, and take home final. Highly recommend!

Lots of readings, but they are all GOOD readings that everyone should read in their lifetime. Sometimes Professor Patterson accidentally tells the same stories or asks the same questions over multiple class periods, but that is because she clearly overworks herself. She is incredibly caring, inspirational, receptive, and brilliant. Would recommend

MY FAV CLASS. Prof Patterson is hilarious. Each class someone presents on a reading; few reading responses; one group project; 8 page final paper. She cancelled our midterm cause she realized we were stressed out and gave us two week off of class. She keeps discussions open to the class and entertaining. I got 100s on almost every assignment.

This course was completely disorganized, but she's a good professor and our course load was not as difficult as some of these comments made it seem. I think this was just a difficult semester for her because she's generally very accessible and open to critical engagement. I highly doubt that she's going to give anyone lower than a B-.

I really wanted to like her, but this entire class was a mess. She constantly brought up the exact same topics over and over again without actually teaching us anything. No one knew what to read 99% of the time. She's a great person with amazing stories and life experiences that are definitely interesting, but there was just so much wasted time.
Incredibly unorganized. Hard to access via email. Very repetitive. Unwilling to consider alternative perspectives. Unaccommodating and uninspired. Waste of time.
HORRIBLE! My mental health was been withered by her impossible quizzes. Please stay away

Patterson, and AADS, epitomize dysfunction. She chronically misses her own office hours, and she doesn't follow her own syllabus. Her grading style is random. She's VERY forgetful and she comes to class unorganized, demonstrating the sheer depth and scale of her incompetence. She needs to do everyone, including herself, a service by retiring ASAP.

There are a lot of papers in this course, but they're relatively short (250-750 words) and aren't graded harshly at all. The readings and films that she assigns are generally very interesting. Patterson herself is honestly a sweetheart and is really interested in learning more about her students and their perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Patterson is amazing. She was dealing with a lot this year and class was online but regardless I really enjoyed her lectures. She is passionate about the topic and very interested in hearing what her students have to say. I will def be taking another class of hers in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: T Patt is a wonderful teacher! She is a very tough grader, but makes up for it in her knowledge and helpfulness. She is not afraid to speak her mind on topics, and loves to foster open discussion in class. You will learn a lot from her, and I personally plan to take more of her classes!

Professor Pattersons class is definitely tough but worth it. We have like 3-4 short 5 question-quizzes throughout the semester that ask very specific questions and are almost impossible to pass if you dont pay attention to the films and readings. Shes very real though when it comes to discussing racism at Vanderbilt and isnt shy about her views

The best professor I have ever had the privilege of taking classes with on any level. I took multiple classes with her years ago at Binghamton University. I learned more from her classes about AAS--and about myself personally---than I did in all my other classes combined. Her challenging classes made me an infinitely better student and person.

She is brilliant but an extremely tough grader. She assigns dense readings and her reading quizzes require that you really delve into the material; however, it is possible to do well in this class as long as you read and ask questions when the readings seem a little too complex. Sometimes she rambles in class, but her stories usually relate.

As a student of color on campus, a T-Pat class before graduation is essential. I've taken two. Her classrooms foster not only a wonderful learning environment but a real sense of community. Her class is a lot of work, she is a tough grader and her paper prompts can be unclear, but her office hours, knowledge, and teaching style make it worth it.

Prof. Patterson is a professor who has a load of knowledge to share and she loves to share it.  Most people hate that she lectures a lot and leaves no room for discussion but I use it as a platform to write her extremely tough papers.  Keys: Go to class & office hours, listen & discuss, and use texts in papers.  She recognizes effort.

Tiffany Patterson is a beautiful soul and cares deeply about what she is teaching. However, Prof. Patterson should never be a professor. She's a ridiculously tough grader and her midterm is literally impossible. She does give extra credit. It's very, very, very hard to get an A in her class, but you will learn an immense amount about AADS.

I thought this would be an overview of African American History and it was not. She was gone half of the semester because she wanted to travel and seemed like she got her grades from thin air. I would not recommend this class to anyone. I had friends take her other class and they had the same experience.

Dr. McNamara is amazing. He is very conscious of our time, does not expect too much. The class is interesting, engaging, and fulfilling. I really respect Dr. McNamara. He balances research, teaching, and being the Dean, but always has time for students and responds quickly to email. We frequently ended class early, but read the homeworks!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof McNamara was great! He was really nice and kept lectures pretty interesting. Mostly graded off of exams, a few small(1 page) papers, and easy daily reading quizzes. He is a professor who actually cares about making sure his students understand the material and his exam questions were actually in line with what we learned. Highly recommend him!
The class was harder than I thought it would be, but we learned a lot. Super nice person. You definitely have to study and keep up with readings.
literally THE class I learned the most. Put in effort and then there you go. Not a tough grader and he is super clear about class content, no confusion. I would definitely recommend him!!!!

Professor McNamara is easily one of my favorite professors at Vandy. Even though spatial cognition sounds like a dry subject, he made it so interesting! He gave really detailed feedbacks on papers and was always willing to help. Definitely try to attend classes and participate in the discussions because he does deduct points if you don't.

Genuinely one of the best professors Ive ever had. I intentionally took him twice because he is so amazing. He gives a "pop" quiz on the reading every class but he tells you this. They're easy and usually one question. He loves when you participate and if you just talk to him he is super accommodating. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I'd definitely recommend Dr. McNamara to anyone! He is the sweetest guy and his classes are not difficult. Spatial cognition is graded by 3 papers (1500-3000 words) plus class participation and daily reading quizzes. As long as you keep up with the reading you'll have no trouble.

I loved Spatial Cognition with Dr. McNamara! You need to show up and do the reading but if you do the quizzes are easy (but you can't really miss more than 2 for a good grade). Essays are a bit tricky but he is such a sweet guy and I loved his energy and his lectures , also class was very low stress and you don't have to always pay attention.

Tim was an amazing professor. Very passionate and knowledgeable. And if you discuss with him you can convince him to let two answers be right for the pop quizzes. I enjoyed his class so much. He is not tough but also not easy easy grader. Beware of those darn quizzes every class. They are really tricky. But still got an A so. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really great professor. Really cares about his students and the course material. There are quizzes every class but if you read the book, you should be fine! Highly would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor McNamara really cares about his students and will answer any and all questions during lecture. Mini quizzes are given almost every class, so you have to read the book. There are 2 exams and a final. There are also a few thought papers (clear guidelines and less than 500 words). I really enjoyed the class and highly recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PSY 3730 with Professor McNamara was a great class. He is very clear with his grading criteria and you can do well as long as you do the textbook readings and come to class ready to take notes. He is a caring professor and very passionate about the field. Overall, I feel as if I learned a lot from this class. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures are pretty interesting and clear with what you have to know for the tests. Definitely have to read the chapters to do well, but the textbook is pretty interesting and straightforward. Does pop quizzes based on readings, but they are pretty easy. He is very helpful and wants everyone to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Knowledgable but little difficult.
Professor McNamara is very knowledgeable and very helpful indeed, uh huh

I thought this class was difficult, not because of the material but because of the amount of stuff you have to learn.  I wouldn't discourage you from taking this class because if you work, you can easily get an A.  It'll at least teach you discipline.
Too much material covered for tests.
boring class, boring teacher, hard tests.  get someone else for psych 101

GO TO CLASS!  If you go to class and know the bold terms from each chapter you will ace this class.  Also keep up with the reading and read over class notes from the lecture before b/c usually once a week he gives pop quizzes that could help you.
Good teacher, I could understand everything he said, but the class was pretty difficult and he makes the tests so that you better make sure you go to class!!!
bad
Topics covered in class are very broad and sometimes irrelevant.  He also needs to liven up his lectures and examples during class.

Very interesting class.  Tests were difficult, but if you put in the time studying and you go to class, you will do well.  People that say its hard just don't make the effort.  Text is interesting; class is engaging and fun.  Would recommend.
A great class!  Pretty good teachers, but the TAs grade very hard.  Sucks because he doesn't curve.
Not bad for an introductory class.  The tests were a little harder than I expected, but you can get a good grade.  McNamara is a little self-involved, but it isn't distracting.

This guy is very into himself and his work.  If it wasn't for his incredible TA's, I would have done poorly in the class.  He made introductory psych very difficult and tricky.  HOwever, his TA's were very helpful and available.
McNamara is awesome!!! I do not get why people think he is difficult or bad. They're dumb!
He is so boring and makes an introductory course unnecessarily hard.
Tough tests (for an intro course), but entertaining professor. His comments are hilarious and makes class worthwhile.
Awesome class. McNamara is fun, interesting, and looks like Niles Crane from Fraiser. Lots of people do badly on the tests, but if you study you certainly can get an A.
No Comments
I thought that Prof. McNamara was good.  The tests were difficult, but if you studied, especially the words, they weren't that bad.
Totally boring class.  Tough grader.
Not a bad teacher for intro psych, which is about the easiest class offered at college.  Pop quizzes count for extra credit at the end, which can really help out.
Really difficult, you think you did well on tests and get the grades and almost no one gets above a 70.

You only have to go to 2/3 of the classes, theres 3 ~6 page papers where you can just ramble about something and get a good grade and you keep a journal that needs to have 25 entries about literally anything and you get full credit simply for doing.  Easy class and also interesting although he has a tendency to talk in circles

He definitely has a tendency to go off on tangents, but he's a super intelligent guy and really knows his stuff. He allows 10 absences, which is insanely generous, and if you pay attention in class you'll get an A.

Not as good of a teacher as or as he'd like to think. Blathers on and on about information you can already ascertain from the papers at first glance, but his insights offer nothing deeper into the topic at hand. Nevertheless, he is overly critical and expects you to know things/concepts for the paper that you couldn't possibly, with his teaching.
just don't take it. he's an interesting guy, but his lectures don't present the knowledge he expects you to know for papers and the midterm/final. take it with lachs.

I absolutely hated this class. I'm sure Tlumack is great in small settings, but in a large lecture no one had any idea what the heck was going on. I left everday befuddled because this man is hard to follow. Granted I'm not a philosophy major, so if this is just for AXLE, I'd go with another teacher.

This guy is extremely intelligent (and not just in philosophy): bring up quantum physics, electronics, computers, etc. and he's always on top of the discussion. Hilarious examples (like his own hypnosis experiments, Orgasmotrons, etc.) Class can be a little dry at times, but only if you let him talk and talk (cause he will if nobody participates).
The best in the department by far!! Take Tlumack if at all possible.
Professor Tlumack is a sexy man which makes his class very interesting. His sense of humor can not be matched on the Vandy campus.

Tlumack is very intelligent and his class is interesting if people show up and discuss, but this was a rare occurance in my class. He is a little different, but interesting. There were only 3 papers and a final exam; and readings before every class, but they weren't that bad.
A nice and brilliant man.  I highly recommend any of his classes for the serious philosopher.
Tlumak is a fantastic professor.  He speaks with a very academic tone that can be difficult to grasp at first, but once you're familiar with it, you'll love him.
horrible horrible experience most students sleep or don't show up

She's very nice, but honestly, made CORE more intense than it needed to be. CORE is usually just an easy A where everyone meets expectations if they do the work, but she liked to make people do corrections, which was a little unnecessary. Overall, she's very nice though, and wants to see students succeed.
Overall was ok. Wasn't very clear with expectations on assignments, which is a bit frustrating. Isn't the quickest at responding to emails. Liked to harp on attendance often.

While she had interesting topics in her lectures, she had considerably a lot more work than other writing seminar professors. Four big papers and lots of writing and reading assignments in class. Graded harshly for a writing seminar that's supposed to be light. She also doesn't respond quickly to emails, so it's hard to communicate with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her lectures are overall interesting and knowledgable. I liked going to class. However, she is not very good at responding to email which can be difficult when you are trying to makeup work since attendance is mandatory. Additionally, rough drafts are graded harsher than usual, making them unnecessarily stressful. She tends to post readings late.

Professor Benn is a really nice person and is pretty accessible outside of class! Our TA was also super accessible. However, DO NOT take this class if you are not proficient in genetics. If you are pre-med, I heard it was generally quite easy, but if you are NOT biology focused, it will be difficult. Please don't make the same mistake as me...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class material was quite interesting, but because I'm not a science person, I had some difficulty in understanding some information. If you are not really familiar with biology like me, then it might be a little difficult, but if you try harder it wouldn't be too bad. Article review is not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Benn Torres is incredibly knowledgeable about her subject. That being said, having taken some stem classes in the past this intro anth class is noticeably tougher than necessary. Unclear "article review" grading expecs, exams easy tho just memorize slides, annoyed I had to buy overpriced online hw code for useless assignments/book. Meh class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lectures are all over the place and very dry. She is incredibly knowledgeable and it is clear that she does enjoy the subject, but I think the material does not lend itself to an exciting lecture. There is a lot of memorization. Overall, it's a fine class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Benn is one of the best professors that I have had at Vanderbilt. I took her first year writing seminar, and while it was a difficult and sometimes confusing subject, her lectures and teaching made it easier. There is a lot of reading and pop quizzes, but she wants you to succeed. Try your best and form a relationship with her, she's awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Benn's Intro to Bio. Anth class is amazing and inspired me to become an anthropology major. Her lectures are super clear and organized and the article reviews actually make you think and analyze current research. Exams are based solely on lecture material, don't read the textbook. Memorize everything on the PPTs and you'll get an A+.

Unfair expectations for an intro class. Very difficult class even for an anthro major. Disorganized, unclear, and impossible to predict what is on tests. She is very comfortable with some people doing fine and others floundering in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about the topic, which makes it even more interesting. While there were readings for every class, they were not that heavy and were mainly needed for class activities to enforce the lessons and main ideas. Her tests are not that hard and are largely big picture or important facts. She really sticks to the class objectives
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Benn has been one of my favorite professors so far! Her class is very straightforward and had the least amount of overall work of all my classes this semester. She knows a lot about her field and tries to tie in interesting examples to concepts. Primary literature is a lot of the reading, but she doesn't expect you to completely understand it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very enthusiastic about the topic and made class engaging by making us do activities in class based on readings to further enforce our learning. She really does care about students outside of class and is willing to meet with you to help you. She does require reading but will go over the confusing aspects in class. ratings here are harsh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. I really could have taken it P/F because it was an elective. She is enthusiastic, but she expects way too much even though it's an intro class. You need to literally memorize everything, no review.  Who got time to do that??? It was the worst idea to take this class.

Unless you have serious interest in the topic, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Dr. Benn is sweet, but it is way too much material for an intro class. Lectures are very boring and she flies through material. Tests don't represent material covered in class, the article reviews are tedious and expectations are unclear. Unorganized class overall. Hated it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super easy class mostly based on the three tests. If you create a good cheat sheet then you're all set. There is a participation grade but if you miss a few points it doesn't affect your grade that much.

Prof. Tung was super knowledgeable and her lectures were engaging and informational. Tests were a lot - but you get a notecard for each exam and the final.
