Going to class is definitely beneficial and a lot of information is presented in class. Overall, great class and a great way to earn a science gen. ed. requirement.

Dr. Tung is a very inspiring and entertaining lecturer. The course content is interesting but has a lot of information, and she very clearly does her best to keep it engaging. She is very lenient with deadlines and extra credit. Would recommend going to as many classes as possible but she provides detailed study guides and posts lectures.

Dr. Tung was so great! Her lectures were packed with fascinating information, and her exams are fairly easy to do well on. Reading is pretty heavy for this course, especially because several assigned articles were never discussed in lecture or on exams. Easy way to knock out an MNS credit and learn about an interesting subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Tung is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. She not only taught us evolution over the past several million years but she also mentioned topics such as health disparities, racism in anthropology, her work in Peru with Wari Trophy Heads and uncovering the past of the remains of past slaves found at the Nashville Zoo. Amazing woman!

Professor Tung is a very engaging lecturer! I took Biological Anthropology because it looked like the least painful for my science requirement as a Peabody kid and actually really enjoyed the content because of Professor Tung. She is also very understanding and the tests are not too difficult.

Truly one of the best lecturers and courses I have ever taken. She cares about the material and her students. Plus, the TAs are wonderful, and she gives study guides -- only caveat is a 94 is an A. Do not let this dissuade you though because the material is so fascinating!

Overall great class! I was not particularly invested in the subject material, but the professor made the class very approachable and easy to go through while still learning a lot about bio anthropology. Homework and studying for tests was very manageable as an engineering student. Professor and TAs are all very invested in the class which was great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I've never taken anthropology, but Dr. Tung made the subject both accessible and fun. I didn't find the exams or homework particularly difficult, but to each their own--some students say she is very hard. Took this class on a whim and had a wonderful time, Dr. Tung packed a lot of content into a semester and I learned a lot. Highly recommend!

Professor Tung is one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt! I loved going into lecture every day and this was definitely my favorite MNS class that I took. Her lectures were very clear and even though my major has nothing to do with biological anthropology, she made me want to learn more than any other class. DEFINITELY take her class!!

While I may not have personal interest in fossils, monkeys rafting to South America, or the human phylogeny, Dr. Tung was super caring and responsive to emails. Exams aren't simple, but even as a filler class I was super happy with my time in her class. There are so many funny, out of pocket things that happen, especially if you like bone marrow!

Prof. Tung is by far the greatest lecturer I've had. She took a subject almost completely foreign to me, biological anthropology, and she made me so interested and invested in it. Show up to class b/c the reading is dense and she covers the important points in class. Take her study guides seriously and you'll do fine on tests. 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Tung is one of the most caring kind professors you will have. She loves her job, AS A TEACHER, and as a researcher. She cares about people's knowledge and their grades, offers extra credit and bonus points, and is willing to talk to you for hours even in a 160 person class. She makes the class interesting even if you don't love bones!
Amazing professor. She makes her lectures very interesting and made me care about a subject I did not care about before.

Tiffany Tung is the most amazing professor I've had here at Vanderbilt. She inspires with her teaching and is super helpful outside of class. She actually teaches as a "hobby" while her real work is found in Peru as a bioarcheologist studying genocides of indigenous people. She is absolutely amazing! 10/10 would take again.

Tiffiny Tung is actually brilliant. You can tell she's passionate about the subject and she actually cares about her students. We watch a lot of NOVA videos in this class, which are pretty entertaining. You do have to go to class because there are a lot of participation sheets but they're easy. Whoever writes her tests could use some help.
I'm a bio major. I asked questions about the biology that she talked about but she couldnt answer my questions.

Aside from being a pleasure to look at, Professor Tung legitimately and deeply understands human evolution and is capable of conveying its mysteries with finesse and interest. Be prepared to read a small library worth of research articles.

Professor Tung is an awesome lecturer and takes a boring topic and makes it as interesting as possible.  There are random attendance checks to make sure you are there and they are worth a good amount of your final grade.  Tests are straight forward.

Don't actually remember any of the info we supposedly learned but really good for a requirement-fulfilling lecture class. You can definitely see why she received a teaching award; she is constantly aware of the zero knowledge level of the students and adjusts to that. Reading the textbook is semi-necessary. Attendance requirement was annoying.

Amazing class. Went into it not interested at all in biological anthropology just to fulfill a MNS requirement however came out of it loving the material. Amazing teacher, really makes you passionate about the subject. Work is not too hard either just have to study hard for tests, not bad at all.

Professor Tung is by far the best professor I've had at Vandy. I loved the class and actually learned a lot. The tests aren't horrible, but study! The lab was super easy, and be sure to go to class because of the random participation. I won't say it was an easy A, but it was far from a hard class. She helps whenever you need it. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Amazing professor. Made the class so interesting, I actually looked forward to coming to class. She is very clear about what is expected of her students on the exams and other assignments. I would love to take more classes with her.

Tung is an amazing professor. Tests aren't easy but if you follow the study guide you'll be fine. She's very understanding. Two tests, a lab, a problem set, and a final. Fairly straight forward. Just make sure you do all the readings and go to class!! She has random participation exercises. Overall a great class.

Tung has been my best prof at Vandy! Fascinating class that could have been a boring one on human origins. Her lecturing is funny, engaging and very clear. Tests are hard but very fair and there is a study guide. Good bit of reading. Only complaint is that she had a lot of conferences which prevented her from lecturing and the movies were bad.

Biological Anthropology did not spark my interest at all - until I took professor Tung's class. She made each lecture interesting and I felt like I really knew the material. Tests aren't very difficult - she gives you study guides to help! Grade consists of two tests and a research paper. Great Class
Tung is absolutely the most fascinating professor I've had at Vandy.  The class is definitely not easy, but her excitement for the subject matter makes it enjoyable.

What a wonderful teacher! Everything she says is interesting and clear. Only two tests, two papers and a final. This is a great option to get a science credit out of the way - and learn about evolution and primates (and even forensic science) in the process!

Honestly one of the best teachers here! had a lot of reading but the quizzes were easy if you at least tried to skim the articles or paid attention during class in discussions. She enthusiasm for her class and research is so infectious that you don't even realize you are enjoying learning about dead people. a must take class here

This class was ridiculous. Quiz every Tuesday, which even if you study for, are hard to do well on since they are either super ambiguous or have something on them you can not study for. Tung is a good teacher and all, but this class is not worth it.

I loved Professor Tung. She was a great and engaging lecturer. You can tell she really cares about her students. The class was really easy if you had a good memory for the tons and tons of reading she assigned. If not, though, it would be very difficult. I think it's worth it though, because Tung is an example of first-rate teaching.

Very passionate about the subject, which makes you excited to be there. a TON of reading though. make sure you do it, and pay attention in class, because pretty much everything will appear on the test. make sure you know times/geography/features. the 2 papers are fairly basic.

Ug! This class was my hardest class this semester. There is a ton of reading from the textbook, book, articles on line, and articles out of a reader. Tests are hard, but if you she does give you a study guide beforehand which is helpful. But on a positive note, she is one of the best lecturers I've ever had!
she was awesome and made the class extremely interesting.  it was not an easy A, but manageable and worth it for tung - one of the best professors ive had at vandy.

Awesome teacher, class was extremely easy, seriously, pay attention, take notes, even though the powerpoints are online, I took notes every class and tore each test to pieces. Papers were graded kinda tough though, but put some extra effort in, you'll be fine. She is very cute too, I honestly loved this class. Would take her again.
She was a good teacher with interesting lectures, but it was a big class without very much support for students. I didn't like my TA.
She's fabulous both in and out of the classroom, and completely dedicated to her subject and students!  She'll make you want to be a bioarcheaologist...I promise!

Prof. Tung makes a possibly boring subject very interesting. She is very helpful at times and depending on your TA, you will have even more success in the course. The only bad thing is that you may understand the information, but you have to interpret it on the tests as she does during lectures. Make sure that you go to (at least) every lecture!

She's great.  Her tests are straightforward and she is really into what she teaches which makes her classes extremely interesting.  She's also very helpful, probably the most helpful and enthusiastic teacher I've had at Vanderbilt.  Take one of her classes if you get a chance.

Tiffiny Tung is my hero. honestly, her class was one of my favorite ever at vandy. she makes talking about hominid skulls interesting. she is a fair grader always willing to take time out to help you even after you're not in her class anymore. and i guess it helps that she isn't as gross and poorly dressed as most other vandy teachers.
She really is great

LOVE HER!!!! She's incredible. Plans on going to Peru in summer of 06'. Was on the discovery channel for researching mummies. Class is uber interesting! Also teaches Human Osteology and Medicine. Take her if you have the opportunity!!!!!

Professor Tung is INCREDIBLE! She is so excited about what she teaches and it makes you become interested in the subject enough to wake up at 9AM and go to class. Don't miss out on taking ANY class with her, she is nothing short of amazing!!
Professor Tung is awesome. She is knowledgeable and fun. Classes are incredibly clear and everything is online. Great for cple. But be careful, you may get a crush on the teacher.

Not an easy A but definitely doable if you just memorize the answers to the study guide questions before exams. Weekly assignments are graded pretty harsh so take your time with them. Sneaky funny guy, super nice, but not very flexible with things like missed exams. Don't let the class scare you and you'll be fine.

It would be best to take Intro to Neuro before taking this class. The lectures are fascinating, and Dr. Tong is very knowledgeable and passionate about his field. Although he does seem to have negative reviews, I wouldn't let that decide whether to take the class. He's very kind and willing to answer questions/concerns. The TA, Keely, is the best.

Dr. Tong is very knowledgable and clearly cares about what he teaches in his course. The lectures can be heavy at times but most of the information is very interesting if you are curious of how the mind and brain work. Tests are not hard as long as you study. However, even though it is not required, I highly recommend taking intro to neuro before.

I really enjoyed this course, and Dr. Tong is extremely knowledgable. He does move fast, and this course is not easy. The tests are pretty rough, but the homework is not bad, and the expectations are clear. If you're interested in cognitive neuroscience, this course covers basically every relevant topic in a fair amount of detail.

DO NOT take this class! Lectures are long and confusing and the readings are incredibly dense and hard to understand. The "study guide" is full of content he never taught and the review session was completely pointless. Can't even teach yourself because his slides SUCK! Also not understanding about missing class at ALL!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tong is nice and smart but teaches a demanding class. Lecture slides are difficult to follow, and has a boring tone, making understanding the material hard. He doesn't answer questions clearly and isn't lenient on missing class or assignments, even when sick. The review session and study guide also weren't helpful. Be prepared to teach yourself!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tong has his humorous moments that help increase understanding, but this is outweighed by the denseness of the lectures and unengaging nature of the lectures. The impression Tong lectures remind me of an undergraduate that sounds like they know what they talk about but don't actually know - except, he does know but it still comes off this way.

Professor Tong seemed very knowledgable about the material, but the lectures were very boring as he just rambled the whole time. The 3 tests are pure memorization of the lecture material and account for 75% of your grade. The weekly homework is also graded differently each week by the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There were weekly assignments that weren't graded the same each week. TAs graded assignments differently. Prof Tong's lectures are boring and long, and all the exams expect you to memorize the information.

Very nice professor but extremely hard to follow during lecture. Lectures are not engaging whatsoever. There were weekly assignments that didn't necessarily go along with the lectures and just felt like busy work/waste of time. Exams weren't too hard as long as you study the slides. Overall just disappointed by how boring the class was taught.

while his course material is dense, his lectures are very interesting and the tests are very doable if you put in the time to study the lecture slides. there are several reading assignments with grading that can be pretty dependent on the TA.

A solid class! There is homework every week that consists of reading a scientific journal and writing short answers -- they grade for accuracy, but it's not hard to get a 100. There are three exams, all of which were moderately challenging. If you study, you should be good to get a 90 or above. Professor Tong is super brilliant and respected!

Professor Tong does not care about his students. He is obviously knowledgeable but no matter why you miss an assignment (illness, death etc) he will not let you make it up and his excuse is that if he were your boss you "would've had to tell him before not showing up to work". Meanwhile, I don't get paid and I pay a lot of money to take his class.

The course content overall is interesting but definitely not worth it to take if you love your GPA. There are only three exams and they account for 75% of your grade. The exams are very TOUGH even with proper prep. The average for his class was always low too, but he would send out mass emails saying it's our fault for not studying enough...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tong is one of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. He's very likable and clearly passionate about what he teaches. NSC 2201 isn't a prereq, but it definitely helped that I had taken it (but 3 semesters before I took this class, so it wasn't super fresh in my mind). The tests are not hard but homework is NOT graded leniently.
Professor does not care about his students. He is a very harsh grader and does not give any good feedback.
Great class! It was fun and I learned a ton. Professor Tong was respectful and will give you feedback on every one of your homework. He really knows his stuff and 100% will recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed this class. No tests, but a consistent amount of homework before every class in the form of a 250 word response to assigned reading. He gives feedback on every one of these, so it's easy to improve in this course. Overall, Prof Tong is highly knowledgeable and leads lighthearted but thought-provoking discussions.

My experience in this class was very pleasant and counted towards the neuro major. Assignments are clear and thoroughly explained. The structure is simple: he assigns 1-2 articles for each class, we read it and write a short response to submit before class. Dr. Tong overall is a funny, lighthearted, and genuine person. 10/10 class, highly recommend

I loved the material and the way that he taught it. I definitely had to put some effort in to get good grades, but this is the type of class where your efforts are actually met with results. Additionally, he's great with helping you understand concepts you don't get either after class or in office hours. He can also occasionally be funny lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class is hard but rewarding. The readings are mostly research articles instead of textbooks. There are a few questions based on the readings every week as homework so make sure to do the readings. Lectures are fun and inspirational. Tests are quite hard and detailed but manageable if you study for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For an elective class, this is not an easy class at all. Tests consist of MC and free response and require thorough knowledge of the lecture material. Tong is not a bad professor, but this class is unnecessarily challenging for an elective course. Free response on tests require full detail, and lots of points are taken off.

He is not lenient at all. One of my friends actually had a life threatening disease and he made it so hard for her to keep up with the work that she had to drop the class. Do not be fooled by neuroscience not being a prerequisite. Everyone is a neuroscience major. This was the only class at Vanderbilt I have ever struggled in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tong's lectures are clear, interesting, and easy to follow. He answers all questions in lecture or in office hours, and his readings (which are of reviews and articles rather than the book) are challenging but rewarding. His tests are very fair.  He is, as a person, somehow quiet and fun at the same time.   Take his class if you can.

Professor Tong is a really funny guy. He makes the more difficult concepts easy to learn with humor. Tests are difficult, but if you follow the study questions he gives you and thoroughly understand them, an A is doable. Get to know the TAs, as they will do most of the grading, and can give you "flex points" on tests if you explain your reasoning.

Tests are hard. Consist of 20 Multiple Choice, 5 definitions, and 4/ 5 mandatory free response. The free response/ essay- like questions are the hardest parts of the test. No textbook used. Readings every week with simple questions is a plus.

Awesome class blending psychology and neuroscience. Really enjoyed the material, but the tests are a true test of information packing. 20 MC, 7 short answer, 5 long answer - quite a feat. It can be done, but slacking will cost you here. Really worked for my A-. He is really full of himself though - presents his curriculum vitae on the first day.

He is a great teacher!  Basically no assigned reading and even those you dont really need to do unless you dont get the material.  Go to class and pay attention and you'll be fine (3 tests 1 term paper).
Very knowledgeable... fun class topics, lots of reading but I learned lots from this course.

Dr. Tong is amazing!  His lectures are entertaining and they have cool demonstrations.  The material is usually clear, if not he clarifys at review sessions in class before tests.  There is VERY little req. reading - tests come from notes and are fair.  Attendance is mandatory, but you want to be there.  My favorite class so far.
No Comments
Prof. Tong is a really great lecturer, and i really enjoyed learning from him!

Overall, a great professor that really cares about his students. Really tries to teach, which is rare among college professors. Even if you don't like stats, Tomarken makes it fun and enjoyable. He's basically the cool high school teacher that somehow is a college professor.

I didn't take stats or AP stats in high school so this class required more effort from me than it did for my peers. Dr. Tomarken is a really kind professor. The material is dry because it's stats but some lectures are really funny. He's an all-around amazing person and I recommend taking stats with him!

This guy is amazing. Puts the well-being of his students before any of his work. He's not the type to make his work hard for the sake of being hard. He actually cares that you learn and understand what he teaches. I cannot recommend him enough. He also has a great sense of humor.

Professor Tomarken was great, but this was the hardest course I have taken at Vanderbilt. The tests are very long, and I ran out of time on one, which plummeted my grade despite strong performance on other assignments. I wasn't a fan of the R computer software, it felt confusing and unnecessary. Nice lectures and accessible professor.

This is a must-take! Highly recommended for an easy A, especially for premed students satisfying the statistics requirement. He really cares about stats and will do anything to make it really fun and interesting, and homework assignments help you really master the material. Tests are cake but may include info emphasized in lecture so don't skip!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Great guy, can tell he cares about his students. Also funny. Makes lectures interesting even though stats can be pretty dry at times. Not a difficult class just look at the slides

He makes PP presentations that cover everything you need to know and study guides for each exam. Lectures can be a little dry, but from the PPs you learn everything you need to know. HW is similar to exams and a big part of the grade. You can tell he tries to make the lectures fun and throws in dad jokes.

I look him for quantitative methods last spring and I highly recommend him! Wait to take the class until the spring if you want. He is very nice and clear on what to expect for the exam. He is also very helpful during office hours. Stats is pretty easy and chill with him.

Very clear. Textbook optional; he makes thorough PP presentations that cover everything you need to know. A good combination of openness about what will be on the test and tests that require understanding. Doing well on the homework is important (large % of grade), and homework is well-reflected on tests. Fun lecturer, lots of dad jokes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Took PSY 2100 last spring semester. Professor Tomarken is super chill. Lectures are straightforward. Problem sets are easy if you follow his PowerPoints. Office hours are super accessible and he helps you out if you need. Tests are fair. Group projects are easy. Def recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I had him last spring semester for Quantitative Methods. He is helpful during office hours , and I enjoy stats with him. Everything you need is on the Powerpoint. He also hosts review sessions which are helpful. He's a nice person and willing to help you out!

I can confidently say that Professor Tompkins has been my favorite professor at Vanderbilt and is one of the most impactful educators I have had the privilege of learning from. She provides insightful advice, an engaging teaching style, and genuine care for all of her students' success. It is refreshing to have a professor who truly supports you.

Prof Tompkins is by far the most non classical professor in a university. She teaches in a way that is student first. You will feel comfortable in her class all times. She will work with you in every way. I specifically, had many hardships in my own life while I took her class and she was willing to work with me in every aspect. She's truly amazing

Too many reviews on here complaining about "busy work" -- its only busy work if you dont care, and if you dont care, thats ur loss. Also, ppl dont realize she is in charge of 200+ students every semester, and most of the answers to ur emailed questions can be found on her thorough resources. Prof Tompkins is the absolute best.

Prof. Tompkins is by far my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. She is one of the most caring, genuine, and kind profs @ vandy. I did my Ind. study with her and could sing her praises forever. I highly recommend getting to know Prof T before you leave Vanderbilt! She always has her students best interests in mind, and I am really going to miss her!

I asked Professor Tompkins for advice several times this semester and it was neither helpful nor progressive. For a course that preaches the value of quality communication, I guess it didn't apply in my case.

Professor Tompkins had such a positive impact on my Vanderbilt experience both as a professor and academic advisor. She genuinely cares about the success and development of her students. Not to mention, she's very approachable and easy to talk to. I would highly recommend her as a professor and mentor!

Prof Tompkins is one of the most human and accessible professors I've ever had. The class wasn't easy, but it was doable & challenging in a way that promoted growth. I learned a lot! She was always understanding when it came to accommodating for emergencies or other external things that made the semester difficult, & I am forever thankful for that.

Tompkins was my professor for the capstone internship class. I absolutely loved her! She is so nice, caring, and helpful. The weekly modules were very organized, and the assignment guidelines were great. Definitely an easy A as long as you do the work. One of my favorite professors at Vandy! On a side note, I loved her weekly chats w/ HOD grads.
Literally the like best teacher I have ever like had. So great!!!

The online "lectures" are full of busywork. I gained virtually nothing from the lectures and attendance is mandatory. Professor Tompkins does care a lot about the coursework, but sometimes to a fault. She is not open to feedback about the coursework or the HOD major at all. The homework is also busy-work.

Prof. Tompkins embodies what it means to teach at the college level. She holds her students to a high standard but also makes their wellbeing a priority. In her class, students get as much as they put in. If students go in with an open mind and embrace the design thinking process, they'll grow as academics and as people. She's the best HOD teacher!

Prof. Tompkins made a 3-hour Monday morning lecture surprisingly enjoyable. She is very nice and approachable and has very clear assignments, schedules, expectations (and very user-friendly guides/rubrics). She is flexible and understanding of complications and accommodates as much as possible. Fun/interesting class activities - interactive, too.

She's so nice and just wants everyone to do well in the course. For its numbering, this course is shockingly easy - usually have to spend no more than 1-2 hours a week on it outside of class. Take this course - it will be super helpful for you as you look for internships or full-time work.

Had her for my internship class and oh my gawd, so much meaningless work. The materials are not challenging at all, and she takes point off very random details. Extremely micromanaged. Be prepared for 5 pages of instructions for a 2-page project.

Professor Tompkins knows what she is doing, but there is way too much busy work in this class. Really frustrating how much extra work this class requires, and while some of the work is useful, you don't learn anything academic. It's pretty much Networking 101/how to get a job. Sounds useful, but too much extra work. Grading is subjective.

Professor Tompkins was one of the worst professors I have had in the HOD program.  Her assignments are unclear and she takes off points for very random things on projects. Be prepared to spend ridiculous amounts of money printing out assignments and readings for this class. She is a huge fan of killing trees and is known for her long projects.
Professor Tompkins is sweet and straightforward but will give you tedious, usually pointless, assignments to complete EVERY CLASS. she's aight

Although it might seem a little tedious at times, this class is super helpful! Lots of projects, but Professor Tompkins makes her expectations very clear and makes the class engaging. In the end, you will end up very prepared for the real world job search process!

I think I'm in love with Professor Tompkins. She's so cute and Southern and she's really helpful outside of class.  1400 basically teaches you how to get a job, and Tompkins makes it interesting.  There's a decent amount of busy work but the class is definitely helpful.  Take it with Tompkins if you can.
I knew very little about this subject before taking this class, but I think Prof. Tompkins helped me to develop my own management ability and market myself to the type of industry I was pursuing.

She is pretty easy and the course load is not difficult. She tends to make a relatively big deal out of projects that take less than an hour to do. However, she can grade some projects pretty subjectively. (like she didn't like the format of your resume)

This class is super helpful for entering the real world.  I was successful at getting an internship this summer due to the information that I learned in this class.  Professor Tompkins is extremely helpful and very open to meeting with students outside of class.  I highly recommend taking this class.

This class teaches you so much about yourself and the working world. Assignments are practical, and helpful for later on when you apply for internships and jobs. Professor Tompkins is extremely engaging, and does not hesitate to take the time out of her schedule to help students with anything they need. I highly recommend this class!

This class is super useful in preparing you for the work world. There are a ton of projects that aren't hard just take up time. Expect more assignments than your typical class. Tompkins is great. So sweet, fair, and explains everything very clearly.

I think that this class should be a requirement for all college students. Professor Tompkins is extremely helpful, organized, and approachable. An amazing class that really prepares you for a successful career path. definitely take this class!!

Prof Tompkins is an AWESOME professor. She genuinely cares about her students and is willing to go above and beyond to help out her students. She wrote my letters of recommendation for summer internships as well as edited some of my cover letters. She is great. I HIGHLY recommend her class.

SUPER organized, a very engaging professor, very fair in grading and policies. An understanding, sweet, adorable lady. She knows her stuff! Definitely take her for 1400, it's a great class and she's so knowledgeable. She's also very approachable and easy to reach outside of class.

I really disliked her at first but completely turned around by mid-semester. She's really knowledgable, helpful and nice. Uploads tons of .doc/.ppt files to OAK with different bits of info in each, so sometimes locating the right info for an assignment is a pain. The class is extremely practical. It caters to HOD majors pretty strongly.
Very helpful and reachable outside the class. Great professor!

I really think all the negative reviews may have been written by the same person.  Such a sweet professor, really cares about her students.  Fair grader and very organized.  She makes sure you know exactly what is expected in an assignment.  Makes the subject interesting and keeps class from feeling boring.  Definitely take 1400 with Tompkins.
Tompkins is a fantastic teacher. The class is very easy but you learn a LOT. Take it with Tompkins!
Take this class with Tompkins! She is a great professor and cares about her students. Make sure you follow directions and go to class!

The subject matter of this class isn't really that interesting but it's an easy class. Most HOD major have to take it so DEFINITELY take it with Tompkins. She created the course and is way more switched on than other professors. She's really nice and interested in helping her students.
I had Kristen for the HOD Internship class. She was one of the best Instructors I have had in my four years at Vanderbilt. She listened to the students and cared about our learning.
She's very nice. Clear exceptions of what is wanted. However there is a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller was very knowledgeable and invested in the content and open to questions and clarifications. My issue with this course were the readings/precis. The readings were time consuming as many words are not in English and need to be looked up and the summaries are graded very nit picky. Overall, nice professor but a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's very nice to be around. If you do your work, you will succeed. Clear exceptions of what is wanted. However there is a lot of work.

She's a really nice and understanding professor. However, your grades are literally just the exams which are solely memorization so I didn't feel like I was there to learn. She shows you some pictures and you have to know all the little details about them. I wouldn't take this class just for AXLE if you're not like trying to major or minor in art.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is very knowledgeable in her field but an incredibly boring lecturer. In addition, the class is based around memorizing 60 pieces of art for the test, so it's not even worth your time to learn the interesting parts of the class. Would have been a fine class online, but with closed book exams this is not worth it.
Not a good professor. Grade harshly on paper. Not recommended.

Dr. Miller is okay. The class isn't too bad because of the online format this semester, but there is no way I would do well if this course was in-person. Exams are pretty rough without notes, and as nice as Dr. Miller is, the class is super boring. I feel bad because she is really passionate about Japanese art, but I couldn't care less frankly.
An easy professor! Lectures can be boring, but the class itself is easy since she is not a hard grader!

Professor Miller is extremely knowledgeable and I really enjoyed the format of her lectures. This class had a lot of required reading for article summaries, but they were reasonable and helpful for studying. Professor Miller is also lowkey very funny and has a dry sense of humor.  I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable in her field, which is great. I agree that the language part of her class can be very demanding, but the learning process is very rewarding. She makes the concept clear, and the exams logical and predictable.

IF YOU DO NOT SPEAK CHINESE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! All of the names for things are in Chinese and are extremely difficult to memorize if you do not speak the language!! And you think you're good at memorizing things until you have to memorize them in a language that has little correlate with English.

Very nice and will help you over email and during office hours. Class is easy only if you go to every lecture, take notes, and memorize well. If you can't memorize, don't take it. For the two tests and non-cumulative final exam, just memorize the images she gives you (40-60) and the key terms. She will clarify any questions you have. Quirky humor.

East Asian architecture is difficult if you don't spend time memorizing. She's great at clarifying things when asked, and she expects discussion and participation.  Really, just practice the architectural names and dates and you'll be fine.

She's pretty much obsessed with Asian art and architecture... so much that she kind of expects that everyone else is too. If you're an art/architectural history person with good memorization skills, this class will be pretty easy; names are the only challenge. If not - especially if you can't keep up with notes - think about taking something else.

Prof Miller is incredibly nice  and very helpful outside of class. Lectures are  dry.  Lots of history and Asian vocab, so if you aren't familiar with it, you have to read the textbook. Final not cumulative, two tests, one paper- pretty picky, but good for an international credit.

This class was really hard. Her lectures are hard to understand and tests are hard. Don't take this class unless you are extremely interested in Japanese art. She is helpful and nice outside of class. The hardest art history class I have ever taken though.

Arts of Japan is impossible and pretty miserable! Professor Miller's lectures are incomprehensible and the book is quite difficult to read. Unless you are proficent in Japanese I would NOT recommend this class to anyone!

Not an easy course, but if you study and put effort into it, you'll walk away with a decent grade.  Learned an incredible amount of info about Japanese/Asian art.  Three tests a semester, final's not cumm. which makes the class much more managable.    Any interest in Asian art and you have to take these classes with Prof. Miller!
I had her twice and she is a great teacher. She tries to make it interesting and if you just study its easy to get an A.

It is almost physically impossible to stay awake in this class.  I really do not like her teaching style, which at times can be very confusing.  She is, however, a very nice person and will help you if you need it.
Very enjoyable class. Miller is nice and funny.  Laughs a lot. She can be unclear at times, but very helpful outside of class. You will learn a lot.
Good teacher but teaches in a complex manner, expects a great deal of reading.

This class is hard, but if you are willing to put in the time you can get an A.  Miller can be disoriented at times.  Says "uhm" A LOT.  Sometimes hard to follow.  Doesn't understand that most students don't speak Japanese and can't learn the names very fast.  Can be a snob because she's so smart

I knew nothing about Asian art, but after her class I felt I was a semi-expert.  She is so nice and SO SMART.  Vandy got lucky that she decided to teach here.  She's Ivy League level.  Work hard and you'll earn an A.  Loved her!

An example of her tyranny:  "Gosh class, it looks like I can't get the projector working.  Today's test cancelled!"   People start packing up their stuff.  Then, suddenly, "Ooops!  Projector fixed!  Now, on with the testing fun!"

Very brilliant...definitely knows her stuff. Kind and smiles a lot :) Class lectures interesting, relevant, and easy to follow. Environment relaxed, but I really felt that I learned a lot. Highly recommended.
No Comments
Class you look forward to
clear, easy to understand, funny, slides on the internet

Professor Tran is  brilliant and inspirational. He really cares about students and our learning. This class changed how I think about about food, culture, and gender. I recommend this class to anyone who is able to take it!
Best teacher so far.
Professor Tran will force you to be curious about the world in new ways. This is a good thing! Just prepare yourself to work hard and his courses will be very, very rewarding.

graded by three papers; very intelligent prof and clearly passionate; very interesting lectures and very funny, but the way he grades can be irritating because he is very specific with the way he wants things graded; get ready for pop quizzes and daily heavy reading; overall, not a terrible choice for a writing seminar
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Man is so smart and has good humor. Go to class and ask for feedback on papers.
Super engaging professor who cares about his students and what he's teaching. He is a fair grader. Would absolutely take another course with Professor Tran!

I feel genuinely inspired from engaging in Professor Tran's lectures. He's a tough grader and whose high expectation on student's paper works. Yet, he's always accessible after class. Make sure you spend the time to discuss with him regarding your paper assignments before the deadline. Procastination does not work for this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very hilarious and great professor who really wants you to learn. I learned more from his class than all of my other classes this semester. You learn how to think critically in ways never done before and apply it to writing. Highly recommend taking one of his classes.

Professor Tran is incredible. He comes off as just a regular guy, but you will quickly learn how smart of a person he is. I always enjoyed going to his class. He grades papers pretty tough, but as a result I had to think in ways I hadn't thought before, and isn't that what college is about? Take this man's class.

Professor Tran is a great guy who cares a lot about his students and actually understands their point of view. Hilarious lecturer and super interesting class. Not an easy A but it changed my perspective on things.

really caring, funny and chill professor who really wants you to learn, think, and use your mind. good amount of readings in course but definitely doable, not difficult to attain good grade since focus is on learning and thinking and discussing rather than grades, really interesting course that expands your mind. Prof is just a chill and cool dude

Professor Tran is probably the smartest person I have ever met. He's really in touch with what matters to his students, is down to earth, and pushes everyone in his class to question their beliefs and learn as much as possible. I can't imagine not having taken a class with Professor Tran. He's a must at Vandy.

Professor Tran is the most demanding professor I've ever had, but he does it because he genuinely wants his students to learn and improve. I feel like I have become a much better writer because of him, and also feel like I have learned so much about the world and how to listen to and learn from other peoples' opinions.

Professor Tran is the coolest. Very laidback and very interested in helping his kids succeed. Go to office hours to talk about your papers and do all of the required readings. Class discussions are a good intellectual diversion. Pay attention and go!

Professor Tran is a super cool guy who really wants his students to succeed. He's really laid back, but don't let that mean he doesn't grade essays hard. I hear he gives more work than other writing seminars but its an awesome subject so whatever. Papers and quizzes, as expected, and make sure to show up!
HE ROCKS

Prof. Tran is awesome. His classes are so relaxed and I actually look forward to going. His grading on papers isn't easy, but if you go to office hours and ask questions about how you can improve he's extremely helpful.
He is an amazing teacher who keeps it interesting. A pretty hard grader when it comes to papers, but it's not out of spite. One of the best professors I've met here and is an easy going guy.
Best professor I've had at Vandy.  He can be demanding, but it made me a better writer and more aware of the world around me.  Amazing!!
hardest prof ever. needs to tone down expectations and stop expecting too much.

Very intelligent and introspective professor who takes a genuine interest in getting to know his students and obviously loves teaching the material. Not shy about expressing strong opinions or pushing the class to do the same.
He's a little bit tough, but he's extremely helpful and is a cool guy. He's awesome.
He's very intelligent and know his material really well. He likes his class small so attendance is mandatory. Very helpful and easy to approach. Overall, a good professor.
Extremely Helpful. He would try his best to make you catch up with the courses and very instructive when you have problems.

his philosophy class is amazing, you have to do 6 papers, which are not long and they usually are on movies that you have to watch and make a connection with whatever philosophy we are talking about the has 2 test but if in the midterm you get a 100 he will exempts the final, he is very nice and you have a lot of opportunities for extra credit

Boomer is such a caring and engaging professor! He breaks things down well and makes his class fun with little brainteaser activities in between lecture topics. Also gives lots of extra credit opportunities, although it's not hard to do well on the tests if you study from the book activities.

Taking this as a non-philosophy major, it turned out to be more interesting than I thought. SUPER easy A the way the class is set up, and extra credit for showing up to class. He actually cares about the students too and says you can go talk to him about anything. Book is helpful to have to study from. Would recommend this to fulfill a requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really solid guy. Took the class just to get MNS credit but ended up actually enjoying it. He's nice, entertaining, and a clear grader. Definitely would recommend.

10% of grade is  quizzes, which are really just showing up to class. The other 90% is either 3 tests or the final. The tests are super easy and there was always about 10 points of extra credit (out of 100 possible points). Besides extra credit on tests there is plenty of extra credit in general.

Professor Tschantz is the man!! He is a BRILLIANT guy who really wants to see you grow in your mathematical approach to problems and symbolic programming ability. His class is not difficult and is made up solely of weekly Math/Coding assignments (no tests or quizzes). Biggest advice is to attend lectures, this man's ability will blow your mind.

Math 3660 uses Wolfram Mathematica for all assignments. There are 12 homework's which increase in difficulty and require substancial studying to fully understand the content. Lectures are dull but the Professor is easily assessable outside of class. Final project is very flexible and can be done in groups. No tests but still a difficult class.

Definitely one of the more "chill" upper-level math courses. 50% of your grade is weekly HW and the complete answers are posted ahead of time. 2 midterms and a final, each of which are straight forward. Lectures can be a bit boring but not mandatory to attend. A is very realistic.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Only math class I've taken at Vanderbilt where I wasn't fighting for my life lol. Grade is 50% weekly homework, graded super easily; midterms were very straightforward as well. Definitely take Number Theory with him.

Take Number Theory with Tschantz.  I took it with another prof and dropped the class within the adddrop period because I could already tell he was awful at this subject.  Tschantz makes it easy and interesting and the tests are very straightforward.  If you keep up with the HW and the review sheets for the tests you'll get an A.
You learn a good amount, and the class is pretty easy.  Attendance is not mandatory, and he is very helpful.

I am taking my third class with him now. Easily the most helpful professor I have had and his classes are always easy. Take him if you need to take multivariable. If you're a math major, take Math Modeling of Econ and Theory of Numbers with him.
I agree with the last two comments.  The only grades are homework and a project, so you have every opportunity to do well.  Tschantz is a great lecturer and is extremely helpful if you need the help.

Professor Tschantz is a freaking genius.  Anybody who thinks otherwise is an idiot.  This was my greatest opportunity at Vanderbilt for learning highly technical stuff that actually applies to real life.

I can't believe that people skip class when you have an ex  hedge fund quant guy teaching you econ modeling.  A lot of what is taught is highly applicable / the final project is open ended.  The class is what you make of it.  Skipping class and do an easy project is easy.  Go to class, ask questions and challenge yourself with the project.

very nice and intelligent guy. however hes a little boring doesnt connect with the class too well. he just moves from one thing to anotehr without really explaining why he did it. but the class is good and easy to pass. he will help you whenever and however you need it.

Professor Tschantz's course on economic modelling was my favorite at Vanderbilt.  He ended up being my favorite professor as he was very straightforward and obviously extremely intelligent.  If you expect to be spoon fed then don't take his courses as he expects you to have somewhat of an ability at original thought.

Probably one of the worst math professors I've ever met; he was completely in able to connect with the class, despite his jolly Santa Clause looks. His expectations weren't too high though and you could teach yourself everything you needed for the exam. But, don't expect to learn anything from class.
Professor Tzchantz is Santa Claus!!!! His tests are very fair, instead of weekly quizzes, he gave take home quizzes.  Not very organized--no syllabus, no OAK, but the class was very easy.

8 pages of writing per week = bad... assigning 4-5 pages of writing per week during the period students are supposed to be writing their termpaper = worse.... never learning a thing about writing during a writing class = priceless... some things money can't buy, for everything else theres part of a 40 000$ tuition wasted on this crappy class.
Really great, but I was one of the very few people who consistently went to class... they missed out.

Great Prof.  Very intelligent yet not at all condescending.  Very knowledgeable and his lectures are interesting.  Not your traditional math class; the 'puzzle' sets often offer no clear starting place and essentially force you to discover the mathematics on your own.  Excellent choice for the first-year writing seminar.

This professors teaching style is not really teaching. She felt more like watching a YouTube video of and organizational talk than an academic teaching the class. This course is very out of sync. The lecturer should be more academically trained then hiring someone from an outside organization to teach. Have someone with  expertise teach course.

The professors grading is vague. The items in class from Syllabus vary. Not very helpful to students. When she feels like one person knows the items in class she will repeatedly call on them and not give others a chance. This course should be evaluated for better professor to teach it or take out from the line up

Did not understand why this course is part of the course requirement line up for the program. Vanderbilt does not show student reviews for professors if the reviews don't hit a certain percentage. Professor had long lectures did not hear student opinion much. It did not feel like she properly taught the class and grading was off.

Two major group projects. Didn't follow syllabus. Never discussed assigned readings. Asked for feedback that made you feel pressured to say something positive. Felt like an excel class not a data analytics class. When students asked then she looked at async stuff. Her grading varied from syllabus. Irrelevant class didn't takeaway anything.

For a 3000 level class, mathematical logic was surprisingly easy. Professor Tsinakis is a very caring professor and wants his students to do well. Test problems were directly from either notes or homework.

Thought he was very cold and weird. Class was awkward. On tests, he takes off a lot for little mistakes. Homework wasn't too bad, but studying for tests was brutal - and, each test is cumulative. By the test before the final, you basically have to memorize 60 long proofs and understand them backwards and forwards. Only plus: optional final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: very caring and intelligent, wants you to succeed and to be inspired by the interesting math. However, not organized, he's a very chill and nonchalant guy so lectures aren't always the most productive and don't move quickly enough. doesn't explain difficult concepts that well. still a good solid prof and class not overly difficult, doable tests

Horrible at explaining things.  Lots of homework and very difficult. Way too harsh in grading in my opinion. its a proof class so its hard to make it 100% the answer he desired. Not recommended unless you are a math person.
Doesn't give the clearest explanations if you don't already have a very good grasp on the material but fair grader, lots of partial credit. He's a genuinely nice dude

Hes a good guy, and wants you to do well in the course. I took this as an ENG Math elective and found this course difficult. Math majors sitting around me seemed to do much better (As). Hw nearly every class and four tests throughout the year. A lot of memorization. Pretty tough
He attempts to be funny, and he can be pretty witty.  His teaching style is somewhat dry, but then again it's the math department.  Go to class or you're screwed.
He's amazing! Good teacher and he's funny! I enjoyed this class a lot!

Dr. Troseth was an amazing professor through and through. I had her for Dev Psych and my FYWS, and she was so compassionate and accommodated whatever situation came up. She made both of the classes super fun and you could tell she knew the material!

She's knows a lot about cog psych, but I don't feel like she knows how to connect with students who find it difficult. I wish it were easier to ask questions without feeling badly about not understanding lecture or doing badly on tests. Seems like other lower-level profs understand more that we're still figuring it out and finding our strengths

Idk about all of these reviews that say she really cares about her students. The class isn't ridiculously difficult, but she's not actually that nice. Her teaching isn't great, but she posts her powerpoint so you can learn on your own time after class. Kinda treats it like a high school class as if students don't know how to be students. annoying.

Lectures are fine, small quizzes/activities aren't hard, but essay-based tests require detailed, specific answers and ability to understand/apply material. She seems nice but does not actually make an effort to work with or help students facing serious personal challenges that interfere with school. Clearly lacks compassion when you need it most.

The "Harry Potter" part of the title is generous. This is an extremely intense child psych/dev class and should be labeled as such. Yes, we talked about Harry Potter, but the class was much more about writing about psych and really detailed studies than anything else. She was also slightly problematic on a regular basis.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Troseth is super understandable and really cares about her students, and she made the class schedule super flexible online. There were lots of small assignments but they're just graded on completion, so you can build your grade up pretty easily. She's awesome and relatable, this is my second class with her, and I would take her again.

Dr. Troseth is a great lecturer who cares about the success of her students. Tests are not easy, require deep understanding and application, but are manageable. Beyond the class content, she teaches strategies for evaluating experimental data that are helpful for future studies in psychology. Definitely a worthwhile class if you put in the effort.

I love Dr. Troseth! Dev Psych can be good or bad depending on who you have. Definitely recommend her! Three tests (mc and short answer but you get a study guide), one group project, one final group paper, and small assignments here and there. Her lectures are great - very information-heavy, but you watch lots of videos and do some activities.

I love Dr. Troseth! I have now taken two classes with her and she really cares about her students. Dev psych can get a little tough, but the final was optional with her. She really cares about her students and has clear grading criteria. So nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Take any class with Professor Troseth! She is a great professor, loves helping you during office hours, and genuinely cares about not only your grade but more important what you have learned. If I could take a class with her every semester for the rest of my time at Vandy I would. Beware that some of her quizzes have very specific questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is pretty engaging, but her tests are not easy. You will have to be pretty detail oriented to pass dev psych
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great personality but really specific grading and not the clearest directions, especially for the group project. Keep up, go to office hours, ask questions, and participate in class (she loves it). Go to the writing studio (and start your paper early)!! Easy to pass, but you might have to work for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: My main complaint was the lack of guidance on papers, but other than that, this was a great class. She is a phenomenal professor who really knows her subject. She does move fast but is willing to answer questions if you didn't get everything.
She is so nice and you can go to her and argue your points back easily. Gives a lot of opportunity for extra credit and no final if you are satisfied with your grade!!!

The class is deceivingly difficult. The material is very straight forward and easy, but Troseth's grading style is ridiculously strict considering the simplicity of most of the stuff you learn. There are quizzes at least once a week on readings, so if you dont go to class you'll miss out on a bunch of points.

An absolutely wonderful person. LOVES when you come into office hours. Class is an easy A if you work hard and study for the exams. She's a bit picky and some of her writing rules make little to no sense, but you learn a lot and hopefully create a meaningful relationship with this amazing person. She also seems quite well known in her field.

Prof. Troseth is a wonderful person in and outside of the classroom. She makes class engaging for ALL of her students! Powerpoints, lots of videos, and easy in class assignments just for showing up. Her syllabus and expectations are crystal clear, and she always is willing to help you if you ask.
VERY hard class and not taught well. Only lectures and then very hard tests which try to trick you. Also 2 very long papers. Do not take this class with Troseth

Easy Class- Just follow the study guides. Exams make up a very large majority of the grade plus two an easy paper that's not worth much. Four exams, if you do very well on the first three, she may let you skip the last exam.
class is borning. not hard but alot of work. lots of boring lectures. not impossible to get an a but not easy either. lots of notes to study and a few papers

Incredible human being, wonderful professor. The class is great, but if you get the chance, talk to her outside of class, too. She'll actually want to form a relationship with you; nothing wrong with getting to know a professor who truly cares about you, right?

Completely amazing class-where else can you discuss Harry Potter for a grade? Wonderful professor-kind, caring, intelligent, flexible, and funny. Would take a class with Dr. Troseth every semester if I could.

So ridiculously easy - felt like a middle school/high school level class in terms of difficulty. Troseth is an incredibly nice lady and it shined through in all of her lectures. Can't stress that enough. Just put in the amount of work you'd put in for an  A&S class and you'll have an easy A.

Dr. Troseth is great! She is caring, kind, motherly.  She really wants her students to do well.  Tries really hard not to stress her students out.  Great class, learned alot.  If you are taking psych 1630, take it  with her.

Great professor. Very understanding and wants you to do well. Material is pretty easy, as long as you read the textbook before the test, you will do well.  Only one big paper and it's not graded too hard.  I highly recommend this class, it's interesting.
Amazing professor. I plan to take as many classes as I can with her. Extremely understanding of situations that may arise outside of her class. LOVE HER!!!

TAKE THIS CLASS! Just READ and go to class and you will be fine! It's pretty simple material. The tests are part multiple choice which can be tricky at times. She wants you to do well so she grades the group projects easier. The only time consuming thing is your last paper- just talk w/her about it and you'll do well!

Nice lady, but SO much material on the tests.  It's borderline ridiculous, but at least the topics are interesting.  We had a few minor papers and one major paper which she handed out guidelines for.  She's pretty touchy about grammar so watch yourself there.  Also had one group presentation that takes some time.  Class is all note taking.

She's a nice lady. Lots of material on the tests, all in the form of articles. two mini-tests and 2 tests, only two of which count (she drops the lowest of a test, or the average of the 2 mini tests). you really need to EARN the grade you get, but the material is all very straight-forward. she'll work with you to the best of her ability.

This class was painful. The reading quizzes were so hard--I read every single article and got 50-70% on every quiz that wasn't multiple choice. You have to basically go to ever class; no textbook so much take immaculate notes; she is not very helpful. I got help on a paper and she said it was a definite A...I got a B on it. Definitely easier classe

Pretty easy class.  Not as easy as 1150, but still a manageable class.  Two mini-tests, two large tests, and a project.  Reading quizzes though are tough.  Overall, easy class if you put in the effort.

Please take this class! It is pretty interesting, even if you don't care about Harry Potter. She's a little tough on writing, but in a helpful way. She even helped me with advising outside of class (though she's not my advisor). She really cares about her students and their success, and it's easy to do well if you try
This is a really easy class.  There is a lot of writing, but she grades easy and wants you to get an A.
Difficult and confusing.

She is so nice, I definitely recommend this class, she made it really fun and we got out early most of the time. She's also a really easy grader and tells you exactly what to do on the major papers to get an A.

Most amazing woman.  Easiest class, learned a lot, did ZERO work, no tests, no quizzes.  She's the nicest teacher I've ever had.  Lots of papers but she grades them very fairly.  Just show up, smile, and she'll love you.  Easy A, go for it.

Complete airhead. She is so scatterbrained and makes everything seem more difficult than it really is. She is inconsistent with grades and really I think it all depends on her mood and/or if you are one of her favorites.
nicest teacher ever.  sooooo easy to get an A..she does everything she can to make u get a good grade. never looked at the text book once and still did very well.
Very nice if you get to know her. I barely went to class and still managed to get an A after a little grade-grubbing. Be careful with whom you choose to work with in groups.

She is really one of the nicest teachers I have ever had, she made the final optional, she let our class bring a double sided "cheat sheet" to the tests which most people brought typed in size 4 font with no margins

This teacher is the sweetest most caring teacher I've had. She wants everyone to do well and will go out of her way to make sure you are happy and that you get a good grade. Although the lectures were not the most interesting, she is very cute and I reccomend taking this class for an easy A.
Such a nice woman, very helpful and understanding. Makes the class much less boring.
she is so nice & wants all of her students to do well. come to class and you are almost guaranteed an A
she is so nice and a explains everything really well.  Her class is easy and tests arent so bad especially if you go to class.  She wants you to do well.  I recommend her.
She took her class way too seriously. Lectures are boring and nonengaging. Cutoff for a B/B+ is a sharp 89. Tests are difficult given the time crunch. Didn't enjoy her class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A very knowledgeable professor. Inspirational to me as a female, but I take issue with the way many of the assignments are graded on a 3 point scale (so you can only a get a 0, 66, or 100 on them). A lot of readings/asynchronous lectures. Class is def doable if you take it with friends and have study buddies, but wouldn't recommend taking alone.

Prof Turner is a fine teacher, but assigns some of the hardest tests I've ever taken in college. Besides that your grade is based on policy memos graded out of 3. This means you can get a 66.7% on an assignment worth 8% of your grade (with no curve). She expects you to know every research experiment way too in depth. Do not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Turner was one of the most intelligent professors I've had at Vanderbilt, and it is clear she is very knowledgeable about the subject matter: Econ of Education. At times, the reading could be a lot, but it was always manageable. Class may have been easier than in the past due to open resources for tests (COVID).
My literal favorite person in the world. Good luck with retirement!

There were a few tests, a presentation, and a paper. You HAVE to show up to every class, but if you do that and take good notes, a B or better should be no problem. I think she does a wonderful job of being engaging. One of my favorite classes.

As a HART major, this was my first CLAS class, but she really focused on the art vs. the history. She lectures the entire time and knows everything on the topic, but she can be boring. Midterm, final, and paper. Not easy for sure but making an A is possible! She also offers extra credit, which was great.
Do NOT take if you are and athlete.  She plays favorites.

Decent writing seminar, you can get by skimming most of the readings. essays are graded strictly and grades are based much more on organization and grammar than on content. Be prepared to diligently proofread papers until they are spotless before turning in. definitely not an easy A but worth taking if you are already a very competent writer.

Decent writing seminar, you can get by skimming most of the readings. essays are graded strictly and grades are based much more on organization and grammar than on content. Be prepared to diligently proofread papers until they are spotless before turning in. definitely not an easy A but worth taking if you are already a very competent writer.

Dull lecture class that consists of looking at slides all day.  Two tests are half the grade, a 15 page paper on a sculptor the other half.  There's no need to read/buy the book; just stay awake and you're guaranteed a "B."  An "A" is out of the question though as she's by far the pickiest grader I've encountered at Vandy.
Prof T was very helpful outside of class. Although attendance isnt mandatory, missing even one lecture will put you behind. She's a difficult grader but is an expert in her field so it makes sense.
No Comments
Good class not too hard and almost fun

Professor Tsak is demanding and she requires alot but she is an expert in her field.  Her grading is particular but we are of course at one of the top schools in the country, who isn't a picky grader.  I have been in three of her classes and I loved them a

Sweet Lord! VERY picky grader. Grade consists of two exams, a paper, and the final. Mess one up and your GPA is shot. She lectures for 75 minutes straight. She is kind and courteous, though. Knows anything and everything about Roman art. Don't take this class unless you're really interested in it.
boring, dry, memorizing slides and dates, smart lady, early morning class, picky grader
hard to follow in lectures, expects a LOT of reading, isnt veyr helpful outside class, very friendly tho ... slides are online, which is a plus

Loved this class and the teacher.  She's so nice and a very good speaker.  Lectures without any notes.  The class was easier then any other ahst classes that I've had at Vandy, so I don't know what these people are talking about.  Easy grader, not that picky.  Has extra credit.
i found this class to be boring and difficult. so many of the images look the same and she is so picky about the dates

A wonderful teacher.  Some students say that she is too hard and not flexible, yet they were simply not willing to put in the work.  Very clear about what she will test you on, lectures were intriguing, one of the nicest ladies you will ever meet.

This was my first Art History course, and I LOVED IT.  She is among the best teachers I have ever had.  She is extremely nice, and always willing to help.  Tests aren't as bad these people say, if you pay attn., you know what she is looking for. A+++++!
One of the smartest profs I've had.  Knows her subject backwards and forwards, lectures always interesting.  Lots of memorizing, but that's nothing new to art majors.  Take her, you'll learn a lot!

Had her a few years ago for about four classes.  One of my best profs at Vanderbilt. Knows her stuff. You have to work, but that's what college is about, isn't it? Take her--you'll definitely know a lot more about ancient art in the end.
It's a lot of work, but it is worth it.  I learned more in her class than I have in any of my others combined.  She's without question the best professor that I have had.

lots of memorizing, a research paper, but the stuff is interesting, class discussion raised to a high level.  you'll know a lot of interesting stuff about an ancient civilization by the end.  available for extra help and very friendly.
only if you want to memorize useless facts.  otherwise stay clear
need to understand that engineers dont really care about how stairs are used in ancient times!  its the same way they are used today, you step on them.
She knows this stuff backwards and forwards.  Very impressive.  She lectures without any notes at all.  The class is HARD and you have to roughly 80-100 images, dates, etc for each exam.
Will not waiver on grading, even when she admits she is wrong.  Not worth it unless it's your major.
Super nice, super helpful, super interesting class, VERY hard/critical grader
Great class!

Professor Turpeinen is very nice. She is a nice grader and ultimately cares for her students. She answers all questions and warmly welcomes class participation. She is accepting of multiple world views, which I respect. Congratulations on your new baby. Thank you for your accommodations.

Professor Turpeinen is fantastic. She has very productive lectures and stimulating class discussions. There are a decent amount of readings but it is nothing too overwhelming. I would highly recommend taking one of her classes. She is very understanding and works well with her students to create a friendly, open classroom environment.

Prof. Turpeinen cares a lot about the subjects she teaches. She is very open with students and encourages us to fully share our opinions and criticisms. She does assign a lot of reading and lecture a solid amount, but a lot of it is really interesting. She really focuses on overarching concepts rather than memorization, which I really appreciate.
Rebecca was an awesome teacher. Really nice and helpful. Very passionate as a teacher, which kept the class engaged. Also very fair as a grader. Everyone in our class loved her.

Wonderful teacher, very engaging throughout the 1.5 hour class period. Assigns a lot of readings, which are absolutely vital to earning a decent grade. Kind and always willing to help. The class was largely discussion based, which made it much more interesting. I definitely recommend taking one of her classes.

She is a wonderful instructor - knows her material, engages great discussions to the students, very approachable. I am no philosophy major, but she made the material so interesting and clear to any of us.

Excellent professor! I'd recommend her by far. The class is beyond stimulating; Professor Tuvel holds wonderful discussions allowing the students to speak a great deal and clarifying along the way in order to make a wonderful class environment. She is also extremely thoughtful in her feedback on papers & more than willing to help a student improve!

Great course. Rebecca is a very helpful instructor and makes boring material really interesting. Her willingness to help her students impressed me. Doesn't hesitate to help you with papers any other questions you may have. Would recommend taking a course with Rebecca!
Prof Tyson gave a series of stigmatizing lectures on the topic of CFS. She talked about planned future work which seemed outdated from modern methods of scientific standards.
Sarah is awesome. She's pretty clear and the class is easy.  I got really interested in the material because of her!

Adore her. Actually enjoyed the class and became interested in the material solely due to her teaching expertise. One of the few professors I've ever had where I've honestly wanted to give her a raise, no matter how much she's making. Take a class with her. You won't regret it.

Sarah is a fantastic professor - quite possibly the best I've had at Vanderbilt. She is passionate about her subject, invested in her students' success, always hilarious, and fosters incredibly meaningful and thought-provoking discussions. Take. This. Class.

Sarah is by far the greatest professor I have ever had. She isn't the easiest grader, but she grades very fairly. She is one of the funniest professors I have ever encountered. I highly recommend her. If you're interested in learning about philosophy and you enjoy meaningful conversations, take a class with her.

Possibly the best teacher I have had at Vanderbilt.  Her class makes me want to take more philosophy.  Such a nice teacher who is always willing to help you out on papers.  Incredibly interesting class and she keeps the discussion going when people run out of ideas. Sarah Tyson is the best!
Sarah is a great teacher who is always willing to help you.  I definitely recommend taking her!

My favorite class last semester. Really good at guiding discussion and keeping things interesting and relevant. Very passionate about her subject. Good survey of classic names in philosophy. No textbook required.
She's an authority of intellect.  Tyson soothes the air like new question. Her Amazonian height and bounce of step at each new day paints the very myth of the good life lived.
She's a really great and fun teacher.  I like the class, and it's not even my area.

Sarah is an amazing teacher. Class consists completely of discussion(with a few, no sweat quizes). An easy class if you do the readings and put critical thought into the papers(which are basically the whole grade). She'll meet with you anytime you need it too. A good AXLE class.

Sarah is a great teacher. She is VERY helpful outside of class. She will go way out of her way to make sure you are understanding the material. She is truly there to help you succeed and she is a very fair grader.

This was definitely one of the best classes to take and Professor Tyler was one of the best people to take it with. You get a full immersive experience and as long as you do all the work that is due, you will be able to make it out with an A!
Great teacher and class! She really cares about our feedback and does a lot to give us the information from multiple perspectives.   The work is not hard, though it is sometimes time consuming.

Quite possibly the wrong instructor for the course. The instructor struggles to provide effective feedback or provide guidance for doing well on assignments. Grading is non-constructively strict. The instructor gets very testy when challenged on an assignment.   -If this instructor is teaching the course, you may want to try another one or wait

Professor Brown is interested in his students really understanding the material. There were actually 3 tests, group presentation, and a final. The in-class assignments were like once a week. None of the work was too bad.

This class was pretty much mandatory. Every class was a group presentation of the reading and maybe videos, and he basically did not teach. The two tests are reasonable, but he doesn't post the powerpoints until a few days before each test. Also, there's a final paper.

Tyson Brown is a young professor who really wants his intro to social research students to grasp the material and do well in class. Grading is based on two midterms, a group (2-3person) presentation, the final exam, and class activities once every 1-2 weeks.
