He uses repetition of the assigned textbook reading to make sure students really "get it"

Dr. Guenst is very nice and cares about her student's mental health a lot. However, on exams, she is a very harsh grader and you essentially do not get any partial credit, which is ridiculous for an engineering class. Also, she is not great with technology, her Zoom office hours were mainly just her trying to figure out how to share her screen.

She's so sweet and cares for every one of her students. The class is not hard, and she wants everyone to get an A. Incredible prof.

Also, her outfits are awesome.
The class is an easy A. Dr. Guenst is one of the best professors at Vanderbilt. She cares for her students and teaches you exactly what you need to know for the exams.

Dr. Guenst is one of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of having at Vanderbilt. She teaches you exactly what you need to know for the exams and she actually cares about her students. She drove and paid for our class to go skating at Brentwood Skate Center and provided food and drink. And she is a FASHION ICON! Truly an inspiration.

A truly nice lady who is very passionate about what she teaches, sadly its all powerpoints, no electronics, fell asleep, eventually stopped going. Daily assignments but usually easy to complete. Would recommend only if there's not a better option for your engineering module and you don't want to have to do actual difficult work like some of them

Super super nice! Really easy and interesting module, but can drag a lot at first if you already understand the information. Attendance is definitely not mandatory as long as there isn't any homework due when you skip. LOTS of personal stories but if you're into that you'll like the class.

She was amazingly sweet and nice. Some work was required, mostly writing a paragraph before class about what we learned last time, though every assignment was ridiculously easy. Very great for a module. I'd choose to take it over again if I had to choose modules again.

Take this class! Professor Zee is great. If you show up and participate, which a lot of people do not, you will do great. Tests and all other assignments are doable and she is flexible if you need extra time.

reviews.comment: Prof Z is the best! She's incredibly knowledgeable in her field and encourages out-of-the-box thinking. The Brightspace is a bit disorganized, she's definitely a Type B professor, so just be ready to have to ask many clarifying questions and for deadlines/assignments to move around a lot.

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Z, however she was very unorganized in her Brightspace which led to tons of confusion. If it she was more organized, I would definitely take her class again, but I couldn't stand the inorganization that led to me doing assignments that weren't actually due.

Professor Tzankova is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about climate studies and does a great job inspiring her students to engage with sustainability. We had a lot of readings (studies and current events - very interesting) and other assignments, but all of it was graded lightly. Very friendly and chatty professor; highly recommend to all!
The best! Take her. Super interesting science class that's more social sciences heavy. Very fun, engaging lecturer.

Easy A as long as you do the work, she focuses more on learning than actually grades which I appreciate. The final project is a group research paper but it is very doable and she grades it very nicely.  Overall, you should def take this class for perspectives credit or if you are interested in climate studies

This was my second class with Dr. Z, theres a reason so many of her students return! One of the best professors I've had at Vanderbilt, truly such a joyful person whose laugh is infectious. There are daily article readings and responses but the TA's always grade them lightly, her group projects are fun and everyone gets an A if they do the work!
Very good and caring professor! Lectures were a bit tough to keep up with sometimes because prof. Zdravka has kind of monotonous voice, but she explains course material very well

Prof. Z is a fantastic professor. The only thing I didn't like about this class was the number of readings we had to do. Otherwise, the class was relatively easy, although the group project was kind of stressful.

reviews.comment: Amazing professor!! Genuinely cares for students and is passionate when teaching. Readings were simple (only 0.5-1 page reflections) about twice a week and no quizzes, tests, or exams. Interesting topics and actually learned a lot.
Really chill professor, you learn so much in the class. Make sure to complete all of the assignments.

This was my favorite class this semester! The material was so interesting and engaging. There was a 1~ page reading response due before every class, but it really wasn't that difficult to knock out. Professor Z was so nice and understanding and the class was pretty chill. There are 2 take-home tests and a group presentation + paper. Would recommend

reviews.comment: Professor Tzankova was a good professor and very lenient grader. My only complaint was that there was a lot of reading that had to be done before each class.

reviews.comment: Professor Z is an endless source of information. She lectures a lot, always brings new information to the table, and knows what she's talking about. Sometimes her slides become less engaging, but she is great to listen to. You can get as much or as little from her classes as you'd like. She won't force you to care, but she'll make you want to.

Super nice & a guaranteed A if you complete the assignments. There's a lot of readings, but you only have to skim through them enough to make each reading response. This was my chillest class of the semester

Super amazing professor and very easy grader. There's lots of reading and writing assigned every class, but you don't have to put in a ton of effort to get 100 on every assignment. Take if you liked her for ENVS 1101. This class follows the exact same format.

Professor Zdravka is exceptional; she genuinely prioritizes her students and the learning environment. Her focus is on fostering active participation and ensuring comprehension of the content rather than solely emphasizing final grades is phenomenal. If you put effort into her class, you are likely to do well.

Professor Z was amazing! It is evident that she is passionate about her field of study and cares about the success of each of her students. This course was enjoyable, and I am happy to have learned a lot about the subject. Though tedious at times, understanding the gist of the content is enough to do well. Highly recommend!

Professor Z was fantastic. She's down-to-earth and deeply passionate about the subject. The class is intensive but straightforward, with fair grading. Expect to write 6-8 pages weekly and a 12-page group research paper. Two short response tests along the way. Overall, a great AXLE course & professor.

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is very respectful and engaging. The class is tedious with busy work, which was not super fun. But, an easy A at Vanderbilt. If you go to class, do minimal work on assignments, and talk in class every so often, you will do fine. Yet limited interesting aspects about the class.

Super chill class, and you learn a lot. There is a decent amount of reading, but you can get away with skimming, since you will cover the important stuff during class discussion. Class is mostly spent doing group discussion. Super lenient and just expects a good faith effort from her students.

Everyone loves Professor Z. She's goofy and a very lenient grader. The workload was more this semester, but she's reducing it for future years. If you need an AXLE course or are interested in Climate Studies, any of her classes are the way to go

Dr. Z is a super chill professor who really cares about what she teaches. ENVS 1101 is a really great introduction to climate justice and the current state of the climate crisis for both people coming from humanities or STEM backgrounds. There's a lot of reading, but everything is graded super leniently. Lots of emphasis on active learning.

Z is the best. There is definitely a bit of homework, but it is all super easy. Just takes some time. Light grading. Easy tests. Genuinely interesting stuff. She just really cares about you. Couldn't recommend it more. Take her.

There are so much reading and writing for this introductory class. There is no structure and every class, you have a new topic to read (20-60pages) and then a paper to write. That paper is 3 times a week for the whole semester. Dr. Tzankova is great, the class, not so much.

reviews.comment:
Dr. Z was one of my favorites! She is very kind and understanding regarding coursework. She cares a lot more about learning than grades, which is amazing. 
The class had lots of outside reading, but if you have a chance to take her class, do it.

Dr. Z is such a passionate, intelligent, and kind professor. ENVS 1101 was a fascinating class and made me want to study Climate Studies/Enviro. and Sustainability Studies. The readings are long at times but skim and you'll be fine. Be prepared for group work, including a 12-page final group paper and a 15-minute presentation. Highly recommend!

reviews.comment: prof z was very nice and an easy grader when it came to assignments. the class did feel a bit unstructured at times, and the readings for each class seemed like a lot sometimes, but overall, the class is an easy AXLE if you need the credit.

reviews.comment: Prof.Z is an expert in environmental policy. Lots of readings and you don't necessarily need to complete them, but those materials definitely help you learn a lot. There are several required reading reflections, discussion board posts, a book review and a final group research paper, but definitely manageable (and she's really a nice grader)

Extremely knowledgeable and brimming with kindness. First time teaching this class so it was a little unstructured. Several discussion posts on readings. She tries to break up lectures with short neighbor discussions. Small groups are assigned at the beginning of the year, with a few smaller assignments and a final research paper/pres with them.
Professor Z is really nice, her exams are really straightforward and there are extra credits on the exam. The lectures are interesting too.
incredibly easy but also a very interesting professor

Professor Z is phenomenal at making sure students succeed. Highly recommend this class for the business minor, especially if you are interested in the environment and sustainability. If you put in the effort to understand the material and regurgitate it in class conversations, you are on track to do well in the class.

Dr Zee is by far the best and most remarkable professor here at Vandy. She is super sweet,caring & flexible with assignments. She is an expert in her field & wants her students to succeed. I would strongly recommend her. Her lectures & engaging and interesting and you will do so well in class, minimally but also because her readings are interesting

Prof Zee is a remarkable person and pretty solid teacher too. Her SOC 1030 class is definitely one of the easiest courses I have taken here, but it was still very interesting. There is so much extra credit that I'm not sure how anyone wouldn't get an A if they put in the bare minimum amount of effort. Take her class!

Professor Tzankova was one of my favorite professors. She gave her students lots of freedom and flexibility in assignments. Tests had lots of extra credit and the grading had lots of cushion. If you do the readings and engage in material you will do fine. During the lectures there is lots of peer discussion.

Prof. Z is a gem! She is kind, understanding, and passionate. Her class is super easy and expectations are manageable while also allowing u to learn about social issues u may have never been exposed to. Lectures can get a bit boring but only because she is so smart that some material may go over your head. So easy to make a deeper connection w her!

Prof. Z is incredible! I loved this course. I wish more courses were like this one so you could focus more on learning than on struggling to reach a certain performance threshold. Throughout the course, I learned about the history and character of different NGOs, their operations, and fundraising/grantmaking--great for public-minded people!

Prof Z is nice, understanding, and an expert in her field. This class was very interesting and heavy on the readings. The group project is a big thing but it's manageable. Not much homework and no tests/quizzes is a plus.

I absolutely loved Professor Z and this class! She made all of her content very interesting; there were almost always readings assigned, but they were relatively short and were always insightful. Classes were usually based off of a lecture but group discussions were common. Tests were very easy and open ended, overall an amazing class and prof!

I am a biology major who took her class to get AXLE credit. I ended up learning much more. Dr. Zee is a kickass lecturer who is really passionate about her area of expertise. You will learn a great deal if you do the readings, which you can get away with skimming. manageable amounts of reading and you will get a good grade if you show effort.

reviews.comment: Words cannot express how much I love Prof Z! She's so smart and so caring. Exams are super straightforward - as long as you show up to class and do the readings (which are short and always interesting) you're guaranteed an A. I learned so much from this class. She's so open and willing to talk about anything in office hours.

Amazing Professor! She really wants everyone to succeed in this class. Plenty of extra credit opportunities throughout the semester that can definitely help you boost your grade. Lectures are inspiring and fun.

Zee is super intelligent and gives pretty interesting lectures. As long as you show up to class and do the daily readings and responses (annoying, but help your grade a lot and can be done fairly quickly), you will get an excellent grade. She teaches super meaningful, applicable content.

reviews.comment: Professor Z is truly one of the best. She knows so much about environmental sociology and does a great job in transmitting that information. Easy A, but still a great opportunity to learn about really important issues in our world!

reviews.comment: Professor Zee is amazing. I took her for Environment and Society 1030. Beware that each homework assignment is worth 1% of your final grade, and they're assigned for every class, but as long as you hand it in on time you get full credit. Exam grading is very generous, and if you study it's actually hard to get any points off. Great GPA booster.

reviews.comment: Great professor to take if you're interested in the concepts of sociology. Her class is graded through reading notes for passages, three easy exams, and a final paper. Definitely take this class for an easy A.

reviews.comment: Tzankova is super knowledgeable and assigns a good amount of readings as homework. The class material was dense and hard to grasp for someone not majoring in Sociology, but I learned a lot and she makes it a smooth class. Took this for ENVS minor; no finals or tests, just big group project.

She cares SO much about the topics we go over in class and it is clear she is an expert at what she does. Her class is engaging and interesting and if you skim the readings you will be fine. Her tests are easy, if you go to class and have a basic understanding you will get an A. She genuinely cares wants you to succeed.

Prof Z is awesome! She is an expert in her field, but also cares deeply about teaching undergraduate students. Her grading is rather lenient and the workload is manageable. Weekly reading reflections and a handful of projects. No exams in this class! Be aware of pop quizzes and regular attendance checks, though.

reviews.comment: Very easy, simple tests with short answers that you can just put what you know, long and dense readings for homework but only need to skim

reviews.comment: Prof Z is amazing! She is very energetic & knows her stuff! Be ready to read quite a bit for homework because you need to participate in class. reviews.comment: Extremely laid back when it comes to grading. As long as you take decent notes and review the material before the exams you will probably do well. reviews.comment: She is AMAZING!!!Lenient grader, really tries hard to help you out in the class and super considerate. Couldn't ask for a better professor!

reviews.comment: I did the readings because they were really interesting and made lectures more engaging, but you can definitely skip some if you're having a rough week. Tests were easy as long as you pay attention in class and review your notes a couple times.
Best professor I've had in college. Listens to students and changes class material based on what works and what does not. Tests are easy if you study. Gives you many opportunities for extra points.

Absolutely the best--take every class you can with her! Super knowledgable and caring. Great group discussions, choose your topic on two 9 pg papers w/ flexible due dates. Midterm and final a little tough but not bad. Helps to have a basic background in US history and CMST. Dean Beasley is truly a gem. Super inspiring and sure to brighten your day!

Dean Beasley is a must-take professor if you can. She's extremely kind, caring, and knowledgeable. Classes were part-lecture, part-discussion, and she welcomed diversity of thought. Despite her busy schedule as a dean, she made herself very available and welcomed us to submit papers for review before the due date. Awesome professor!

reviews.comment: she is my advisor and i absolutely love her. her class was very interesting and she really tries to push her students to think outside the box. she is incredibly intelligent and clearly an expert in her field. her passion for her work is obvious. tests are very hard but i learned a lot in her class...worth the hard work.

Beasley has great lectures that are interesting in their own right, but her tests are very difficult and not always based upon these lectures. She is intentionally vague in her guidance to stimulate creativity, but in the end your success will come from your ability to memorize facts from the textbook.

Love her! I've taken 3 classes with professor Beasley and she is extremely engaging and cares about her students. Tests are difficult but as long as you attend class you'll get all the information you need to succeed.

You will adore Professor Beasley. She is funny, accessible, engaging, and tries to make every class enjoyable. I rarely miss her class just because it's so much fun. Watch out because her tests are harder than you expect, but making an A isn't difficult.

The best Intro to Engineering module I took. Prof. Vernon makes lectures fun and relevant, I really liked her “Engineering Job of the Day” slides showing what Vandy engineering grads do now. Super approachable and fun projects. Had 3 group projects total, all pretty chill but interesting.

Highly recommend taking a module with Dr. Vernon. She knows what she is talking about and is very knowledgeable about internships and careers post-graduation. She was very helpful and genuinely wants to help set you up for success in the best way that she can.
Vernon is a good professor but her class was pretty boring and the projects were sometimes confusing.
Dr. Vernon is a very chill and easy going professor. The module was an easy A overall but sometimes projects were a little bit confusing. Homework was short and extremely easy.

attendance is mandatory even for such a boring class. this is truly the most boring class i've evr had to take and i wish i had never chosen this module in the first place. on top of that, the prof is rude and she doesn't teach anything the whole 10/14 days since she cancelled sm days in the first place and we are forced to teach ourselves

Most boring engineering module ever. Powerpoint slides every day, many grammar issues. Stresses about attendance but also cancels classes whenever she feels like it and assigns group projects. reviews.comment: She is very kind and caring. She helped me a lot when I was struggling with everything around me. Definitely take her, Amazing lectures too.

Dr. Vernon is a very kind professor. Her module wasnt my favorite, but I appreciate her dedication to immersing us in the real world of chemical engineering. I enjoyed learning how to 3D model in Fusion360, and the skills she taught were very useful! With that said, theres not very much flexibility in the course, so its less creativity-oriented.

Dr. Vernon is such a caring professor. Was the module where I felt like I go the most exposure to what a career in the major could look like, she gave chemE careers of the day to show us what we could do w a chemE degree. Easy A like most of the modules, but I feel like I got the most exposure to different types of work in this module. So nice/good

Took a special topics class with Dr. Vernon, and although I'm not sure if it'll be offered again, take a class with her if you get the chance! Super caring, minimal work, and very accommodating if something comes up! Have to put in a couple hours of work when something is due (about 5 times for my class) but that was about it.

I absolutely loved Professor VanDiver! She's super knowledgeable about Black art, and connects past to present in an interesting way. There was only one test, and a few papers but she really walks you through how to get through them, even if you have no prior art experience. She truly cares about her students and let's it show. Highly recommend!

reviews.comment: Professor Vandiver is amazing. She is knowledgeable and considerate. She really cares about students. But she has high expectations for your papers. There is NO EXAMs for this class, but you have to write several papers as material reflections. Those papers are creative but the grading is somewhat tough.

I loved art history before but was not a fan of this class. It introduces too many works of art and it feels like she just reads off her notes the entire class while making attendance mandatory. Wasn't the biggest fan of this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Totally loved this class! It sparked my interest in art history. Prof. VanDiver is an eloquent speaker and easy to understand and talk with. Each lecture was so engaging that I always lost track of time. Assignments tested more of the analyzing abilities with a lot of creative freedom. As long as you take a lot of notes in class, you will do great!

Professor Vandiver can be a tough grader, but she's amazing. She expects a lot from her students and her expectations can be a little unclear, but she's always willing to meet outside of class. She's also super knowledgable about art history, and if you're passionate about the subject, I would recommend taking at least one class with her.

Professor Vandiver cares about the subject and the students! She can be a tough grader, but her expectations are clear and she's available to help with anything. She's so sweet and sincerely values the well-being of her students; I'd absolutely take a class with her again and my major isn't remotely close to art history.
Prof. VanDiver is very passionate about her subject and cares about her students. She made History of Western Art interesting and engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. VanDiver is very knowledgeable and respected in her discipline. She is kind, but her class is a lot of work for a first-year writing seminar, and she can be a harsh grader. Take this class if you are very interested in Art History, but if not, it can be kind of dry.

Prof VanDiver is someone who's extremely passionate about her subject, but you're going to have to read quite a bit. She's great to have as a professor if you're interested in the subject--I was lucky to have classmates who were also interested. If you do take her, be ready to work though! You'll learn a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Honestly, I was not interested in art history at all before this class, but Professor VanDiver makes a real effort to engage her student in the course work with discussion and interesting lectures. There are a lot of readings, but the assignments are really straightforward forward and she even gives a rubric for each one.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor VanDiver did a very good job in this intro art history class. She gave us all the tools we need to look at and appreciate art, and made me consider adding it as a minor. I already knew a lot about art coming in, but this class can be an easy A if you just memorize all the works for the three exams. I found that part fun and not that hard

Attendance is mandatory (double penalization). Class is pretty boring and do not get caught on your phone. She walks around looking for reflections of screens in people's glasses (no joke). Tests can be rough but overall not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Attendance and participation are MANDATORY in this course! Readings are assigned most nights, but they are not very long. Professor VanDiver is a tough grader on the essays, but her feedback is very helpful. If you go to her office hours for help, your grade will improve, but you definitely have to put in the work for an A on an essay.

Dr. Vandiver makes her lectures very interesting and easy to keep up with. There's not a ton of reading or homework, and the tests and writing assignments are very manageable if you put work into it, but there is a lot of memorization.

I enjoyed this writing seminar a lot because the subject matter was interesting and Dr. VanDiver is good at pulling readings. The workload isn't too intense. However, this is definitely not a high school writing class and you have to expend a solid bit of time and effort to get a good grade. Very helpful in office hours! Get to know her a little.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Attendance is MANDATORY. Exams are graded harshly and homework is not very helpful in terms of prep. Professor Vandiver does make an attempt at humor during lectures which is nice but if you are not interested in the material, do not even bother taking this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I was in Professor VanDiver's first year writing seminar. I felt that she really helped improve my writing and always gave clear, useful feedback on my papers and revisions. With that being said, her lectures can get dull at times and her grading did feel a little harsh sometimes. Overall though a good class, especially if you're into the subject.
Harsh grader

Incredibly boring lectures, and very difficult tests to study for. Pure memorization. Art history can be interesting, but her lectures made you want to fall asleep. She seems nice but can be intimidating. Once got mad at a student for looking at the clock...

Tough because of memorization and tests where you don't have enough time, although she then made concessions in grading. Asks basic questions to engage the class. 3 exams and pop quizzes. Clearly struggling with teaching three sections of the same class and sometime confuses the sections. Really pretty and inflects sentences like a sorority girl.

Professor VanDiver is one of the most passionate professors I have had at Vanderbilt. Her interest and zeal about the material really makes her class engaging and interesting. Be sure to make notecards as you learn the art b/c it will pay off for the test. Also, make a list of key topics she discusses. One of them will be an essay on the test

Dr. VanDiver doesn't mess around but she is so smart and passionate! If you go to office hours and display interest she'll like you. The class is tough but so worth it if you're interested. You need to read the textbook before class because she does ask questions and call on people randomly

Doc V was so helpful to me during Statics. He co-taught the class and truly helped me break down the class into the basic concepts. Definitely go to office hours, he lives in FGH so he will stay with you until you understand everything 100%. Definitely take Statics with Mazita Tahir bc Doc V comes with her.

Doc V was an amazing help for statics and giving life advice in general. He thoroughly cares about teaching his students the basic concepts, which has transformed my study methods for statics and all other engineering classes. He will stay in office hours until you really understand the material or just to share some of his crazy stories.

Great prof. He would always meet with us whenever we needed him. So so helpful in all aspects of statics and even other classes! He gives great advice and is so funny. Makes sure you really understand what is going on, and shows you how simple everything really is. Best prof I've had at this school.

Doc V is the man. Very comfortable with the subject matter he is teaching and stresses the basic concepts in a way that students can understand thoroughly. His class is the only one I've been able to look back on a year later and still feel comfortable with the material.
He tests on the basic concept. He cares more about you learning than he cares about grilling kids on info they dont know. He expects his students to do well
Doc V is the man and he will go out of his way to help you succeed. If you show that you are interested in succeeding he will help you get there.
This is a teacher that really cares about what you are learning. He makes PAVE fun and kept it interesting. Really good guy.
Perfect. He is the man.
Vanderbilt could do a lot worse
he's SUPER kind and caring!
Reverse psychology always worked.
He's an awesome guy. The class isn't too bad, he's interesting to listen to. One cool cat
Definitely you want to be in his class. He is very funny, energetic, easy to get along with.  The best class you’ll ever have.

He is very supportive & helpful. His lectures are well organized and easy to understand.  I liked the way he tied in calculus and physics.  The best teacher and class you’ll ever have!  He is so good that I even enjoyed the class as an EE major!
Talks a lot and exaggerates things. Likes to manipulate people. Friendly though.
No Comments
No Comments
Professor Bell is one of the most inspirational people I have ever met. He is easily one of Vanderbilt's best professors. If you have the chance to take one of his classes, do it.

old guy who has extremely boring classes. Its difficult to understand what he says but the material we learned was actually interesting. grades pretty easily and you can get away with not doing the work.

Professor Bell is a fairly hard grader, but really does push you to be a better writer and a better student. We read way more books than any other freshman writing seminar, but his seminar was really relevant to current events, and class conversations were really enlightening and engaging. Bell is also readily available outside of class for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Bell is one of the most interesting people I have talked to on campus. He knows the material backwards and forwards and the class content can be extremely interesting. Can be a tough grader on papers and tons of reading and videos assigned but you can get by without reading all of it. Would definitely recommend One of my favorite teachers
He is awesome. Very difficult grader, but go in for help before the essay is due and he will be very helpful

Do not miss a chance to take a class with Professor Bell. If you participate in class discussions and take the time to get to know him, you will greatly benefit from his knowledge and experience. He has been like a mentor to me in my time at Vanderbilt. English majors especially-- take his class!!

Prof Bell is an absolute legend. The dude knows his stuff and is intensely interesting. I took him for my freshman writing seminar and loved every minute of it - I wish I could take it again. He's sharp as a tack for his age, loves his students, loves English, and is personable to boot. He's a little tough  on grades but it's doable. Take him now.

Professor Bell was my favorite and most helpful professor my first semester at Vandy. He is not an easy grader and demands a lot, but at the same time you will learn a lot. He is always willing to help with any paper and really cares about his students. Highly recommend. Also, his class can be extremely funny. Great Professor

Professor Bell is my favorite professor at Vandy. And he's the hardest professor I've had. He pushes you; you know you'll have to read a lot, write a lot, think a lot--but it's well worth it. You'll definitely learn in his class. He's also pretty hilarious.

Bell is not just a great professor; he's a mentor. He cares about and remembers his students, and his mind is as sharp as any in the department. He tries his hardest to be helpful and engaging and personal. Don't let yourself graduate without taking at least one of his classes.

Bell is great. He knows his stuff. If he thinks he's being unclear, he'll try to say something in a million different ways, and he is always helpful to meet with after class. He learns about students on a personal basis, and he remembers student long after class is over. He is what every professor should try to be like on campus.
I LOVE PROFESSOR BELL. He's amazing, and if you're an English major you cannot leave Vanderbilt without taking one of his classes.

It's been a while since I had Prof. Bell, but when I did, he changed my life.  He taught me to think, to pay attention to myself, & to merge the two.  To accept both my limitations & abilities, & to understand the possibilities of both.  He SEES.  He was my best intellectual companion, ever, and I miss him.  (And he's totally, totally hot.)

i loooooove  professor bell! he is seriously my favorite professor at vandy. Class discussions are always interesting and the assigned novels are amazing reads, asks a lot of you but if you do the reading and attend class you will do well. not an easy grader but by no means impossible - i HIGHLY recommend him!

I love Prof Bell! He is the most caring and understanding prof I have had; he takes the time to get to know each student. He is a very difficult grader but he is very flexible - there are no real due dates and you are able to write as many papers as you want. If you get a bad grade you can rewrite every paper until you get the grade that you want.

Oh, Vereen, whose name he shares with actor Ben Vereen... the class was interesting at first, but then the topic of film became a philosophical effigy, a discussion of symbols and themes that may or may not exist. And then the papers... it is a film class, but Professor Bell insists on grading as an English professor. Funny and dry, but not great.
This guy is the quintessential college professor, down to the patched elbow blazers.

Prof. Bell is a nice little old man who thinks about the books we read is very abstract terms.  He's always relating something or other to Sarte and it gets hard to follow his train of thought in lecture.  He's also a fairly hard grader, but if you read the novels and understand them, you'll do well
A challenging, interesting, caring prof.  Very helpful and available outside of class.
Bell was a really nice, funny, cute old man, but he can be cynical and also a really hard grader.  he also had everyone asleep in lectures and he went off on phisophical tangents all the time.
Did not like Bell one bit, too into his own opinions to grade others' fairly.  I was bored to tears every day in class.

This class isn't set up like a normal english class- you take a test on a book BEFORE you ever discuss the book in class.  Didn't really make sense to me, and the class was kinda pointless- I can read books on my own, thanks.
i am in love with prof. bell, he is the funniest cuttest guy ever.  but not the most consistent grader
No Comments
She doesn't even teach she just talks about herself
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Prof Shaw is awesome. Her content is always super interesting and lets the class discussion be lead what the students are interested in. She def wants her students to do well. She has credit no credit assignments that help you rack up points so that your final paper isn't as scary. I 100 appreciated this. Her attendance policy is also pretty chill

Loved Prof. Shaw! Her class was laid back and had a lot of class and group discussions about readings. While the conversation could veer off-topic, I feel like it made the space more comfortable and less uptight. Generally not stressful and she works to make the final paper less intense by listening to her students and their struggles/commitments

Overall, Prof Shaw is a good choice. She is fun & brings good energy. She understands the difficulties of being a student. The class material is interesting & our class had group work. She is kind of scattered & does not use class time efficiently. She is a tougher grader, but half the assignments are for credit so it's very realistic to get an A.

Dr. Harris is very kind and caring... BUT the grading criteria are unclear, especially for exams. The presentation is easier to follow since the TA walks you through exactly what she wants and grades it. Participation: I made sure to speak in every class, and still did not get full points. Not a bad class, but I would not take it again.

Could be better. Her lectures are great, you can learn a lot but the exams are not nice (it's very heavy writing and grades weirdly). There's a lot of writings and the requirements are not clear and so points would be certainly removed…

The ONLY thing we were graded on was a policy brief presentation/paper at the end of the semester. As long as you put in time and work into this, you will get an A (I BS-ed this assignment and got an A-). There are weekly readings but honestly, you don't have to do them or participate. Very low-stress class. A few guest speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is so funny and welcoming; I am always excited to come to class. Her lectures truly are discussion-based, you have to read to participate but it's interesting and not overwhelming. In class, she's easy to follow and preparing for exams is straightforward. She is so caring and is always asking "how she can help set you up for success".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Harris is a QUEEN. She cares deeply about students and will dedicate time to make sure you're successful and get you connected with opportunities/people that relate to your interests and goals. Class is interesting with many chances to engage. Grading is fair and she's accessible for feedback. If you're a child psych person, connect with her!!!

Adolescent development with Dr. Harris is my favorite class I've taken at Vandy. Dr. Harris knows her material and her lectures are fascinating and filled with real-life applications. She genuinely wanted us to succeed- she went over exactly what was on the exams ahead of time and gives you countless opportunities to participate in class.

Prof Harris was my favorite professor Ive had at Vanderbilt, if you get the chance to take one of her classes DO IT! Its really clear that she is passionate about what she is teaching and that she actually cares about her students. Most of the grade in her class was determined by a few big exams and papers but she grades very fairly, no daily hw

I took this class as an elective and it was a welcome change of pace from heavy STEM coursework. The lectures are friendly and easily digestible, and the assignments few and far between, with deadlines you can set on your own. A decent amount of reading before each class, but it is the only textbook I really enjoyed. I recommend it as an elective
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Harris lectures a lot but has so much experience in her field. She doesn't have the most accessible tests and you really have to read the textbook to know the content in my opinion but she tries to make things interactive and interesting. Nothing is hard other than the tests.

The class had no direction. Prof Harris just rambled in class and never got anywhere - boring lectures. She made students read a dense chapter of the textbook before every class and then we basically had to regurgitate what we read. If you skim the textbook every once in a while and follow directions you'll come out with a pretty solid A.

Vicki is AMAZING and so is her Hospitalized Child class. She's invested in her students' success and wants everyone to get something out of her class. The work isn't bad - reading and posting discussion questions for every class and one final project. Every class has a guest speaker in children's healthcare so it's relaxed and easy to learn a lot.

The subject matter is taught well and easy to understand. Vicki is kind, engaging and is always willing to answer questions/help students understand class topics. She starts every class asking what you found interesting in the reading, so participation is important. Overall not too much work and a very sweet prof.

Super interesting and engaging lectures. An A should not be hard as long as you actually listen in class & she gives you study guides that clearly outline what you need to know for the test. Participation is important, but she gives you plenty of opportunities to talk in class.

I would recommend her class because she is nice and the class was very easy. However, she takes a really long time to give grades back (almost all given in the last week of class). Her class is so discussion based that you will just learn about the lives of everyone in the class. I unfortunately learned almost nothing content-wise from her class.

Harris is super nice and helpful. KNOWS HOW TO LECTURE AND GRADES FAIR- you don't see this a lot at Vandy. Get ready to talk. Many writing assignments, make sure to keep up. Readings not most important. She cares more about class engagement than reading stuff. Also, if you're reading this, swing back and comment when you're done. Pass the baton!

Dr. Harris is awesome. Adolescent development is super discussion based and she really cares about hearing what everyone has to say and the material is interesting. There's a moderate amount of work but all the assignments are straightforward and she puts a lot of resources on Brightspace to help with each one

Dr. Harris is my favorite professor I've had at my time at Vandy. She really cares about her students and if you care about her class, you're set. She values hard workers, but is always a resource for those who might be struggling- is really accommodating with issues that come up. I'd highly recommend taking her class.

Dr. Harris rocks. I loved her class and felt like I learned a lot. Easily one of my favorite professors from my undergrad experience. Form a good relationship with her and you're set. She can tell if you care or not. Would recommend.

Dr. Harris always offers helpful hints and is fun to learn from. The class was interesting and provided me with the skills I need to take on the rest of my Vanderbilt experience. I know she's always wanted a chili pepper, too.

Hospitalized child is the BEST class at Vandy. Vicki sets up interesting speakers and visits for each class like to the Ronald McDonald House and Pediatric Nurses from the cancer center. Your grade depends on participation, one presentation and a project but if you like the topic it is very easy to get an A,
Harris is tricky. Her lectures are wonderful, but watch your grades. She grades on a whim and DOESN'T ROUND UP. It's a huge heartbreaker to have an 89.7 and not get an A- for the class.

Vicki Harris is a really good teacher. She is so helpful... She tells you exactly what to write in the papers if you ask her. She's very sweet and the class is very easy to relate to. There are guest speakers and fun stuff like that.

I really enjoyed this class. It is fun because everyone can relate to at least some of the stuff that you read from the textbook. Professor Harris was relaxed and pretty cool. She is also helpful if you have questions.

This class is a really good one to take. It's adolescent development, so it's interesting and related to real life in high school. She's really nice and approachable. It's not a lot of work. You don't even need to read the book to do well. An easy A.

Really good teacher.  Very interested in the subject and is good a relating it.  Also relatively easy grader and not too picky about structure and style of stuff.  Have to study for the tests but they aren't too hard (and she gives you a study guide for them) and the questions are pretty fair
Relatively easy grader and rather genial and perky, but taking notes for her class is a bit of a joke because she sprinkles in a lot of anecdotes.

Dr. Greene is a very nice person and a fair grader, but she lectures straight from the textbook. Her lectures werent very interesting because it was just her copying problems onto the board. Take her class if you already know physics well, youll do well and youll be bored with the content, but if you really want to learn physics, Id avoid her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Caring--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Hwis a free 25% to your grade because she posts corrections she allows us to use as reference. Project is a free 15%. Tests are straightforward if you made an earnest attempt to do the hw. I didn't do physics in highschool, and I really liked Dr. Greene's metod of teaching it. Learning other QM and relativity concepts earlier than normal was nice

Dr. Greene teaches several of the required course in the physics major, so she is not someone you can just not have, but she is an extremely kind professor and distinguished scientist. She is very willing to help if you ask. Tests are straightforward. Lectures are not amazing but familiar from most HS physics.

Professor Greene simply does not explain anything she writes down. Copies directly from the textbook and the final was a disaster. Homeworks are 25% of your grade so do them correctly. I did not know that for the first 4 homeworks because I transferred into the class and my grade suffered for it.

Class on "presenting physics research" w/ Dr. Greene, and I felt like she taught it well. She genuinely cared about our learning. She graded very leniently, based upon participation during presentations. She gave good feedback, but was never overly critical. She's a friendly person and very willing to work with students.

PHYS1911 is an absolute joke if you've already taken AP Physics C. About 70% of the course is straight highschool physics. Greene is a pretty boring lecturer - she just copies her notes onto the board whilst reading them aloud. Exams are 20%, so make sure to study, but they're otherwise pretty straightforward. Great GPA booster for first sem @Vandy
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Greene is a poor lecturer, as she copies numbers directly from her notes to the board the entire class, making it difficult to keep up with what's being taught. It's much easier to teach yourself from the book. She is an incredibly lenient grader, and having a thorough note sheet is enough for an A on an exam.

Professor Greene is well-accomplished and she goes out of her way for her students. The class is a bit deceiving in difficulty; I wouldn't call it particularly hard or easy. Don't try to judge it from the first few lectures. An advantage about 1911 is that you gain exposure to advanced content that most general physics sequences don't deal with.

I didnt have the best physics experience in high school and I struggled in this class. I ended up having to teach myself most of the content but the book is somewhat helpful. Professor Greene is a great person, very understanding but she assumes we know certain things and its easy to get lost. Very generous grader though, saved my grade.

Lectures are pretty understandable, if you take notes. She assigns weekly homework, but it's all manageable. Doesn't take longer than 2 or 3 hours. Prior programming knowledge is helpful. The tests are not too difficult--just like the homework--and she is an extremely generous grader. I know someone who got a problem wrong and still received 8/10.

Professor Greene is one of the sweetest people I've ever met. Lectures can be confusing because she does a lot of proofs so it isn't always clear which bits of information you actually need to know, but she is extremely helpful if you go to her office hours and is very understanding if you need extra time for homework.

She is pretty clear with her lectures, however, they were a little fast and seemed straight out of the book at times.  Definitely a recommended course if you are a physics major, it is very informative on the workings and applications of Maxwell's Equations.
Good Prof. Brings in cool demos. Willing to accomodate to the classes requests. Lots of overhead and powerpoint.
good communication, interesting demos in class. engineers take this section as opposed to the others its much easier

She is a nice lady, but extremely scatterbrained. She teaches completely off the overhead and her tests never seem to be over all the stuff that has been covered. She does try, but when she says, I made everything straight forward  know that is crap.

She is infuriating. Up until this class, I have thoroughly enjoyed my Spanish classes. It's not even because its a writing class that I don't enjoy it. She makes class anxiety-inducing. She changes her homework expectations last minute, accuses you of CHEATING, makes you redo papers, the list goes on. Idk how she has good ratings.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: worst teacher ever. Doesn't give good feedback and accuses you of cheating if you use words not from the class.

Professor Gardner is THE BEST! She is so incredibly sweet. Your attendance is mandatory, and she is strict on phones. She grades fairly, and there is usually many grades in the grade book that a couple low quiz grades will not hurt you. There is weekly homework, but it is easy. Expect to be doing partner work almost every class.

I loved my time in her class so much that I'm taking her again next semester. As others have said, strict with various things (phone usage, attendance, etc.), but generally very caring. Clearly wants her students to learn and improve their Spanish throughout the class. HW for every class, but I often completed it in under an hour. Would recommend!

Professor Gardner was a highlight of my semester! She is so kind and always had treats for us (like chocolate!). Strict on some things, like attending class and no phones. Very easy class, expect around 20 minutes of homework between each class. No tests!

Prof. Gardner was a fun and engaging professor. I took her for my AXLE language requirement, and she did a great job making class fun, though no one was a spanish major. Felt similar to high school spanish, but more engaging and she did a good job facilitating. For basic AXLE requirements, especially if you have spanish experience, I reccomend.
Great woman who cares about her students. Class is extremely easy and if you do the homework (10 min or less a night) and show up she'll like you.
the class itself was pretty easy but gets super accelerated at the end. however, she clearly picks favorites (go to office hours)

Gardner is very funny if not sometimes passive aggressive, but a great professor. You have to talk in class and give presentations. There is also regular homework due every time the class meets. Occasionally expresses conservative political views so don't take if that's a deal breaker, but I learned a lot and she cares a lot about her students.

Attendance is big for this class. Also study for the two tests. If you follow her requirements, you can do well. Print out every worksheet for class as well. Hard class for most students, but doable. You have to work for an A- it is a 94. She is so passionate though and I would absolutely take her class again. Easier than 3301W. Homework heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The instructions for assignments can be very vague but she grades fairly. She is also hilarious and makes everyone excited to come to her class. She really cares about her students.

Dr. Gardner was very nice and funny, which made class enjoyable. However, her assignments were extremely vague and class seemed disorganized. A lot of times I'd go into class without knowing what was due. She didn't give much feedback on assignments either. I'd only take this class if you really like creative writing.

Profesora Gardner is such a sweetheart who seemed genuinely interested in her students and was always bright and cheery. She is clearly passionate about literature and knows her stuff. The class is difficult, as most language classes, so do not get lazy and be sure to keep up with the daily assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Don't take Gardner unless you love Spanish. She assigns a LOT of homework, but all of it helps you understand the material. You have to work hard for an A for sure. Try to connect w her in some way because she loves to see students invested. I was nervous for this class, but I learned so much and because of her I want to major in Spanish.

I loved Gardner. The class was definitely hard, but she was very supportive and I think communicating with her about any confusion or hesitations really help you get the advice and confidence you need. She is an absolute expert at teaching difficult Spanish literature and grammar concepts, but she teaches material in a very approachable way.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This is the 2nd time I have had Professor Gardner for a Spanish class. She is very well-versed in Golden Age Spanish history and literature, and you will leave her class with a wealth of knowledge few people have about the time period and its works. Despite the high work volume, I am sad to never be able to have her for a class again. Love her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I'm just giving her a 2 because I think her average should be a bit lower (I'd otherwise give her a 4). She's just kind of disorganized, and her expectations are sometimes unclear and restrict your creativity. She's still incredibly nice, and I'd highly recommend her class, but be prepared for some frustration with confusing assignment guidelines.

Profe Gardner is an invaluable part of Vanderbilt. Her class was essential in my decision to declare a major in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese, particularly because my writing skills improved so much throughout the course. She always cared to teach us to the best of her ability and I am extremely excited to take another class with her.

She is an amazing lecturer and really cares for her students. The class requires a lot of reading and analysis with three big essays (3-4 page each) and several "mini's"(1 page each). However, you learn a ton and she is one of the best professors on campus.

Profesora Gardner is INCREDIBLE. She is so passionate about Spanish, and her enthusiasm makes class everyday something to look forward to. I cannot speak more highly about her--take her class if you have the chance!

Very sweet, and a good choice for 3303. Loves students who come to office hours and gives them better grades on assignments, so try to go at least a few times to ask questions. Overall, grades fairly and understands that students make mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Apparently SPAN4405 (upper-level lit) is difficult with anyone, but with Prof. Gardner it seems extra demanding -- prepare to read a ton. Easily assigns 35pp./class (in medieval Spanish!), and essays are frequent, lengthy, and not graded particularly leniently. Still, you learn a lot - she's a good lecturer.  You'll need to budget a lot of time...

Knows her stuff and gives good feedback on helping improve your essays. Most assigned work is not long(5 big essays 2 pages each) but expect small daily hw as well. Good balance of learning about grammar and writing practice. Some times kinda repetitive with grammar lessons, but overall fun class.

Profesora Gardner is the greatest person I have met at Vanderbilt. She would do anything for her students, but isn't a pushover when it comes to grades. She explains all topics well and is never unable to answer a question. She grades essays reasonably, and tests weren't too hard. Getting a B+/A- in the class was a breeze; an A would be hard.

Professor Gardner is a very good teacher! She's really clear in explaining everything and clarifies stuff well even if you don't get it. She's really nice and sometimes fairly funny. Expects you to talk and participate in class- it's part of the grade! Lots of peer work too, i.e. going over your homework, essays, etc with a peer and reviewing it.

Prof. Gardner is an absolute gem.  Nobody cares about their students more than her, and she inspires a passion for literature even in students who otherwise wouldn't care for it (myself).  Grading isn't easy, but is reasonable.  In all, she's super knowledgeable and caring. I have taken all her classes, and would do it all over if given the chance.

I loved Gardner! She was helpful, interested in her students, kind, and funny. Only problem: her assignments are sometimes very unclear, but she is not a super hard grader, especially out of all the 201W teachers I think she is one of the easier ones.

Profesora Gardner is a gem.  She knows the material she teaches inside-and-out and is also personable, empathetic, engaging, and concerned for her students.  Prof. Gardner returns papers and tests reasonably quickly, and gives clear-cut feedback.  Grading is moderate  it's quite hard to fall below the B range, yet not easy to get an A. Excellent.

Gardner was by far the best Spanish teacher I've ever had. Lectures were engaging and time seemed to fly by during class. She always has thoughtful feedback on essays and is willing to put in the time to help her students improve. Tests were grammar-based and difficult, but not impossible. Easy to earn a B, but getting an A requires a lot of work.

I absolutely loved this class. She is very passionate in what she is teaching and actively engages the class. By far the most entertaining class of my first semester at Vanderbilt. Be ready to work, though, since the homework is fairly demanding. Keep up, however, and it will be hard to get anything worse than a B.

Professor Gardner is a fun and engaging lecturer who loves her job! Nobody falls asleep in her classes. Be ready to work, though. 203 material is difficult and her tests require in-depth knowledge of the textbook and of class discussions. Study. And go over your mistakes with her. Also, she starts class early and ends it on-time.

Plays favorites and grades very hard. Unless this is going to be the class that you put most of your effort into this semester I would try to take 203 with a different teacher. She is nice but expects a lot, our tests were a lot harder than other sections.
She is a terrible teacher and the class is pointless. If you get her, change teachers.

Profesora Gardner was great! She really understands college kids, and how on a Friday afternoon we may not participate in class discussions as much as usual. My writing also really improved from this class. It definitely takes effort but this class is very helpful and pretty interesting.

One of the most invested and caring professors at Vanderbilt.  Truly cares about her students.  Not that easy of a class and she is not an easy grader, but you learn a lot.  She is a great professor to learn from.

She is absolutely fantastic. Anyone who gets a chance to learn from her is truly blessed. She really wants her students to be successful. Plus- she LOVES what she is teaching, so you will grow to love it too.

Hard.  The tests are kinda rigged. They are subjective questions looking for exact answers. I really like the teacher, but if you are not very interested in the subject area its hard to succeed. I ace most classes, this class will be my lowest grade by far.

Great professor who keeps class fun and interesting.  She explains things clearly and is very willing to help.  The class itself is pretty easy, especially if you have taken some spanish before.  Also, the assginments and tests are pretty easy.

This class wasn't easy, but not too demanding. Gardner's a fun, energetic teacher who kindly deviates from the departmentalized syllabus from time to time. She really likes to teach and cares about her students. Get her for your section of 201W, which isnt a very demanding course in the first place.

She's a great teacher and really cares about her students. She's a pretty lenient grader, but always tries to make sure that you understand the material. The office hours are the best time to get to know her! She's awesome.

She is enthusiastic, helpful, and nice. She grades fairly easily, but it is necessary to put a decent effort into the compositions. Go to office hours if you aren't sure how to express something. She is very helpful in giving advice and explaining things. Some of the course busy work can get annoying, but that's not her fault. Take her if possible.

Sort of a demanding course because of the 5-day-a-week thing. Prof. Gardner is fun to learn from and always willing to help. Much better than most other intermediate spanish teachers, from what i've heard. She's a very sweet lady and not TOO hard of a grader ? not an easy A if you are not GREAT at Span. I took AP in hs and still ended up with a B+.

She is fair, and she wants you to succeed. Sometimes it can be frustrating because she insists on talking in Spanish all the time, but now that I am in upper level Spanish classes, I cannot thank her enough. Try not to get frustrated if you are not used to her Spanish accent or use of vosotros; they both come in handy later.

Incredibly nice, and very understanding. Shes not too hard of a grader either...the work load is decent, three 1-2 page papers, three 2-3 page papers, usual hw assignments and daily grades, and 3 tests...with a small amount of work, an A is easy to get...she also makes the class fun and interesting constantly...if available, take her.
She is extremely nice and is always willing to help. It seems like she really wants her students to succeed. Even better, she is an easy grader. Definietly take her!
No Comments

such a great prof! has a really high energy, and demands that students participate but she breaks down the grammar stuff really well so its easy to learn.  easy grader on the composiciones. you will come out of this class with amazing spanish listening comprehension!

I LOVE HER!!!  She's so fun and sweet, and her class is not hard at all.  She has a lot of energy and really wants you to do well.  Easy grader.  I wish she would teach higher level sections so I could have her again.  She's so sweet.  I don't know anyone in my class who doesn't like her.  TAKE THIS CLASS!

As long as you establish some sort of interesting personality you should be successful in this class, speak up in class, read your textbook, and just connect things to your everyday life to understand it better, tests are pretty straightforward and she is a very understanding professor.

Class content was fun and interesting but the assignments and project can be a bit unclear. She is a tough grader when it comes to essays. There is a final project at the end of the semester that is 55 points of the entire grade.

I love Dr. Scheer. She brightened up my morning and you could tell she cared about all of us. Scheer actually wants to make sure the course work and her teachings can apply to your future career. The textbook she chose is awful though and I feel like you can get away without reading it

Dr. Scheer is a great option for Psy-Pc 2550! She definitely cares about both her students and the material a lot. Her papers are more enjoyable than the exams. However, I feel like the class was just a regurgitation of the textbook, which made the class discussions less meaningful than they could've been.

Professor Scheer truly cares about her students, and it is so clear. Both herself and the TA make themselves very available in this class, expectations for the entire semester are made clear early on, and she is flexible when you are communicative with her. This class is also incredibly interesting, and the workload is very manageable!

A lot of people love Prof Scheer, but I personally didn't vibe with her teaching style. She was condescending at times and does not have regular office hours. Her grading criteria is pretty unclear and she tested us several times on material that we did not learn in class. Not a bad class but she is just very set in her ways.

probably my favorite professor ive taken class with! so fun to talk to, makes an effort to get to know each student, gives study guides and periods before each exam, all application projects are open ended and can be tailored to your interests

Dr. Sheer is the kindest and funniest professor I know! She really gets to know her students and truly cares. This class was my easiest class of the semester; I never felt stressed by assignments. She provided study guides and even took time in class to help us study for upcoming exams. Exams were also super straightforward and not difficult.

She is awesome! The exams are mainly short answer, but graded fairly. Two application papers that are easy. The final is a project that takes a decent amount of time. No homework, reading isn't necessary. She cares about her students and makes class fun and engaging.

Favorite prof of this semester, I loved her teaching style. If you read the book, complete the study guide, and participate in class, you'll be fine; unfortunately, I had a busy semester so I fell off on reading/studying and my grades dropped. I def could've pulled off an A if I'd read the textbook. DON'T PROCRASTINATE ON THE INTERVIEW PROJECT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Leigh Scheer is my favorite professor ever. Take this class if you can. 3 tests, 2 essays, and a project. I really enjoyed going to class each day.

Professor Scheer is such an incredible person. Her lectures are engaging, she cares about her students, and this has definitely been my favorite class at Vandy so far. I wish I could take so many more classes with her.

Not a fan of teaching style. 3 exams - pure memorization. 2 papers - one very long and comprehensive. Must attend class for participation credit. Other teacher is easier, so avoid this professor unless you need this class to graduate. Be prepared to read the book. Gives study guides which are just the headers of the textbook, so not very helpful.

Professor Scheer is awesome, super approachable, & always willing to answer questions! Not a lot of readings (& you'll survive even if you don't do them). 3 exams (none cumulative), no final, 2 application papers, & final project. Exams = application based & rely heavily on content from class, but attendance isn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class very rarely deviates from the textbook except for when it comes to the group projects and papers, which has felt like a good balance to me. The textbook is a fairly good textbook imo. Professor Scheer is huge on relating class/textbook concepts to personal examples, which is a really efficient way to learn. This class has been fantastic!

Hearing about the activities that other professors did for this class made me annoyed that we had to teach ourselves by reading the textbook. Rubrics were unclear for papers but I felt like our TA was pretty generous with grading for tests. This style didn't really work for me but Scheer is nice enough, would not take a class with her again though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is such a sweet and approachable person; I love chatting with her. Be prepared to read the textbook; the exams are specific and answers come from the text. No lecture slides. Learning is done via group projects, application assignments, 2 papers, & a term project. This class did not fit my personal style of learning but to each their own.
I loved Dr. Scheer (previously Wadsworth). She truly cares about her students and her class was interesting and fun. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She explains the materials nicely and gives engaging class activities and helpful assignments. Manageable workload. Highly recommend.
By far one of the best professors I've ever taken here at Vanderbilt. Her class is amazing, just be sure you stick to the guidelines 100%. Tough grader, but amazing and caring professor.
Professor Wadsworth is the most arrogant teacher I have ever encountered. The complete lack of humility displayed by someone in her position is disappointing. This is highly toxic behavior.

Love her and definitely recommend. Show up and participate in discussion. Do the study guides and only study that for the exams, which are easy so long as you actually study. Nightly reading of the text isn't necessary, just skim if that but still not necessary, especially if you've taken other psych classes.

The majority of your time will be spent reading the TEXTBOOK. The textbook is your teacher not her. In class, she will put key ideas on the board and ask you if you can comprehend what you read along with pointless groupwork. Papers are easy but vague. Don't memorize what you read? You won't pass exams which are mostly easy, but will ask specifics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She does not teach. She relies heavily on the textbook and group assignments. She does not give lectures, she just makes us do pointless textbook activities. You will have to teach yourself, and her tests cover information in the textbook instead of the actual focus of the lectures. The group projects are pointless and a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor. Always has clear expectations and explains concepts very well in class. Also re-exposes you to material so much that it is easy to remember and studying for tests takes little time.

Dr. Scheer is so helpful and accessible outside of class. I met with her and she helped me figure out my whole life plan! She is knowledgeable both about what she teaches and about different career paths/majors/things on campus. Her class so interesting even though it's online! Highly recommend anything she teaches!

Professor Scheer is one of those teachers who makes learning enjoyable. Despite the fact that this class was at 8 a.m., she never failed to keep the class engaged. Her grading was straightforward, and she was beyond understanding. Hands-down, I would recommend this class to absolutely anyone and would love to take a class with her again.
Adolescent Development was just an amazing class, and Professor Wadsworth really approached it well (especially considering it was fully online -- I've heard it's even better in person).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Scheer is a a great professor; she is super clear and her workload is definitely enough that you will learn a lot, but not be overwhelmed. Make sure to read every chapter and you should be well prepared for assignments and tests.

Professor Scheer is the best! She is super personable, intelligent, and cares about teaching. She teaches in such an engaging way (not lecture style, changes it up) and invites students to participate heavily in course. Definitely my favorite professor I've had at Vanderbilt so far :)

Amazing prof. One of the best Vandy has to offer. Knows her stuff so well you wonder if she was born with a PhD(she'll say no). Very clear on what's on and what's not on the test; tests straightforward. Grades harsh early but lets you go at end. If you put in the work, you'll be fine. Relatable to both ed and non-ed students. Would highly recommend

The class was easy, but things were graded a little too hard sometimes. Dr. Scheer definitely cares a lot about her students and wants to see them use her material in a real-life setting. She does a good job of making sure that all ideas are applicable to professions outside of teaching so that her non-education students feel welcome as well.

Wadsworth has been one of my favorite profs yet. Very reasonable, interesting, and funny. Really wants you to do well and cares about her students- memorized all of our names on the first day of class. Would definitely take her again

Wadsworth is an AMAZING professor, very kind-hearted and super willing to work with her students. The class is not super easy, but if you follow instructions and stay on top of things you will do well. Her tests are pretty easy, as long as you study and review everything on the study guide. She is SO helpful outside of class if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Wadsworth is amazing! Her lectures are engaging, she doesn't care if you take notes on your computer, and she gives a study guide and class time to study before every exam. There's also no final exam. I had her first semester and HAD to take her again. She also totally understands that sometimes life happens and is really flexible about it.

Dr. Wadsworth is a homie! She is honestly one of the best lecturers I've ever had because she doesn't use powerpoints, it's all in her head. I really appreciated her willingness to try different things in class, constantly breaking out into pairs, small groups, large groups, and having class discussions on the topics. I would take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A really great professor who outlines all her expectations for assignments. Do the study guides for the test and you will do really well. Participate in class and add to lecture notes. I love her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easily my favorite professor and class I've taken so far at Vanderbilt. She is very clear with her expectations and as long as you follow them, you will do well on the three projects/essays. Tests are very fair and you will do well if you study the material (she provides study guides). Participation also matters a fair amount.

One of my favorite professors at Vanderbilt. Explains concepts very well. Tests are fair. Course itself is a little difficult but if you put in effort you will get an A. I think most people got an A or a high B. Very nice and interesting professor. Super helpful and easy to contact. Hope to take another of her classes.

I took this class bc the rate my professor reviews were glowing. However, while she is clearly an expert on the subject and class sessions are relaxed and easy to get through...I  would stay away. Her grading is arbitrary plain and simple

Very good class. Wadsworth is extremely helpful and understanding. Reading the book is not crucial. Attending class is important because all the test info comes from the class. Tough grader on the research paper.
Easily my favorite professor at Vanderbilt. Super helpful with awesome study guides for the 3 noncumulative tests. The final project is big but doable, and her grading is not difficult or ambiguous.

Professor Wadsworth is a great teacher. She is so friendly and her lectures are always interesting. The tests are not too bad. There is no final. Instead, she requires a final research paper. Although the paper is difficult, she gives plenty of time and is always willing to help out. One of the best professors I had tis year.

the class is interesting, and relatively easy but be prepared to do lots of group discussion in class. much more of a middle school type class than a college lecture. Wadsworth clearly knows her stuff but most of the time it is your classmates doing the talking/teaching... which can be problematic and extremely annoying

Wadsworth is one of the best professors peabody has. She's sweet, funny, and passionate about her work in the class. This is a super easy class to get an A in cause she's a really simple grader. She's entertaining and really makes the information applicable to your future career.

grades are highly subjective, gave me a poor grade on final paper despite having her critique it. tests are mostly short answer, but I never receive partial credit for any answers, attended classes almost everyday, and raise my hand everyday, but she does not call on me. participation is a part of the grade. Would highly advise not taking her.

Wadsworth is a great professor. Her lectures are very clear and concise and you can tell that she knows what she is talking about. Your grade is based on three non-cumulative exams, two 5 page papers and one large project. The project takes up a lot of time so start working on it early.  Enjoy!

Best professor I've had at Vandy so far.  Really knows her stuff, great at explaining and giving examples.  Fair and reasonable grader.  Always available to help, incredibly approachable.  Very good-natured, really wants all of her students to succeed.  It's professors like her that give Vanderbilt such a good name.

Mrs. Wadsworth is an exceptional professor. She makes her expectations very clear and she is a fair and reasonable grader. She prepares you for the test, and if you do your part you will be successful in her class. Don't underestimate the research paper. She gives you plenty of time for it though and she is available to offer advice. Great Class!!

Wadsworth is literally the best teacher I have ever had. The material is interesting and you have to stay on top of the reading but her lectures are so thorough and clear that you learn so much in her class. She knew all of our names by the second day of class (without assigned seating) and is always very personable. great teacher great class.

Dr. Wadsworth is an amazing teacher. Skim the textbook, be able to participate in class, but mostly use class notes for studying.
