Tests are pretty easy- she tests understanding of concepts, not just rote memorization- use her examples from class. One 10 page paper on topic of your choice- fair, comprehensive rubric
She is wonderful. She grades a bit too difficult, but you'll learn so much from her class. She's really knowledgeable about the topic.
Sweet lady, but not very clear. Gets off track easily and blabs about her kids. I would recommend taking psych 1630, but not with her.

An amazing intro to my child development major. She makes everything crystal clear to understand, and there is basically no excuse not to get a good grade. Study guides are posted online and include everything on the test. She also goes over them in class. Participate; she likes this. She's pregnant enough to pop and is actually due soon! Love her.

An amazing intro to my child development major. She makes everything crystal clear to understand, and there is basically no excuse not to get a good grade. Study guides are posted online and include everything on the test. She also goes over them in class. Participate; she likes this. She's pregnant enough to pop and is actually due soon! Love her.

Educational Psych was the second class I've taken with Leigh and I absolutely loved it. Leigh is extremely helpful. She keeps class interesting and engaging, and makes sure you leave knowing your stuff. Tests can be kind of tough, but there are no surprises so as long as you pay attention and study, you'll be fine. Great class.
Class was extremely easy, but she taught a lot.  The class was always interesting and tests were very straightforward.
She has no idea what is going on and is not afraid to admit it.
she's amazing. i love the way she teaches

She is sooo nice. You really dont have to be an education major to take this class....it is more about the politics of education. There aren't tests or quizzes, just a really easy 2, 5, 7, and 10 page paper. She is a pretty easy grader i dont know how someone couldn't get an A..and she even says on the first day that she wants you to get an A
Follow the sylabus and you will do fine...look over the handouts because you will discuss them in class
No Comments
No Comments

She is not only a teacher but a very personable and understanding human being as well, quite the feat for a professor with an "Welcome to Education, Boys and Girls!" class. What could have been dull and monotonous (and if you had only read the textbook, that is what it would have been) was actually enjoyable. The highlight of my first semester.

I love Leigh!! She is a great professor...she really cares for her students! There is some work involved, but it isn't hard. She is a very fair grader!! She makes the class very interesting, she gets to know her students, and she's the BEST!
Prof. Wadsworth is awesome. She knows that EDUC 1020 material can get tedious and makes the best out of it. She's also super helpful and easy to talk to!
Very nice, but seems a little loopy sometimes. Knows what she is talking about and is very passionate about her work.

No homework and one fun term paper at the end of class. The class is also interesting. Tests are straightforward and not hard. He literally tells you the questions beforehand. Vrooman is a little weird, but this is 100% the move for an upper level econ elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Vrooman does a much better job teaching the upper level Sports Econ than the intro. The smaller class size allows him to make the class way more interactive and his casual approach to teaching makes for a fun environment. Tests are not hard; essentially just regurgitating the graphs and stories he goes over in class.

The upper-level sports econ seminar with Prof. Vrooman is a good option for the upper-level econ major elective. He goes into greater depth on some of the sports econ theory, which is fascinating, yet the class is not, by any means, difficult. A good class to take senior year. Three reasonable exams + semester paper. Fun professor, solid choice.

Vrooman is the man. Cares a lot about the material and if you are a sports fan, you should 100% take this class. By far the most interesting class I've taken at Vanderiblt. 3 tests that are all multiple choice and he tells you nearly every question.

No homework, just studying and reviewing. The class is solely multiple choice tests. Approx. 1/3 of the questions are ambiguous so there is a luck factor, but if you take notes and study, you'll likely land in the A range. If you are a sports fan, this is a must! It'll change the way you view pro sports, and class will be the highlight of your day.

Attendance and good note-taking are essential.  Vrooman's lectures are great, and he's an authority in sports econ - he can also be kind of headstrong and intimidating, and I'm not sure he's a nice guy at all.  Still, fascinating subject matter if you like sports.  A caveat: tests are somewhat ambiguous and super-valuable to your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Let's dispel with this fiction that the tests are hard. Seriously, though, they aren't. At all. It's completely *multiple choice*, and easy multiple choice at that. There's no homework, lectures are hilarious, and Vrooman literally, specifically tells you what's going to be on the test. How is anyone going to complain about a multiple choice exam?

Really interesting class, even if you're not into sports! Vrooman is so funny and nice. No homework. Attendance is a must to get notes but be warned the tests are NOT easy. 3 tests x 36 multiple choice that are pretty tricky; it's easy to miss a few or a lot each time and tank your grade.

At first, this class seemed really interesting and cool. Then the test rolls around. The test questions are arbitrary and the answers are difficult. I went to every class and still didn't do that well.

If you're taking 280, you should know what you're getting with Vrooman. He's all over the place during class, but the tests won't be that tough, and it'll be an easy A- or B+ with an A possible. 2 exams and 1 paper with pretty much no work throughout and you don't have to go. Downside is the exams take close to 4 hours.
Nice guy, go to glass and a B is easily obtainable.

Only 3 exams. No readings or hw. You only have to know the material in the lectures. Only complaint is that his class is 50 minutes, but he expects you to take 2 hours on the exam. So, you will either miss your next class or go it it and come back after. Very nice guy and helpful

Vrooman is a fun an entertaining teacher. He doesn't assign homework and the class has no textbook so the course is very easy as long as you attend class. The tests are simple multiple choice questions and you get to drop one of them. He's a nice guy, very smart, and loves sports. I'd absolutely recommend his class.

Great class, you'll learn a lot and I like his teaching style as he repeats the most important things several times and really emphasizes them so that I've left this class actually remembering the material. Don't skip class, although it's interesting enough that you should want to go. It'll help you better understand both sports and econ in general

If you go to every class and study the old tests, this class is very easy. That said, Vrooman isn't a very good professor at all. He's completely unavailable outside of class, and his lectures can be unclear and confusing. Don't expect to learn a lot. You learn way more in AP Econ than this class.

Professor Vrooman was a huge disappointment. He showed up to class late every day and was unavailable outside of class.  The examples he used were often a force, and more confusing than helpful. He should spend less time trying to make his students think he's cool and more time actually teaching economic principles.  I feel like I learned nothing.

Great class and made me look at sports in a whole new way. A bonus is that you don't have to buy a textbook. A drawback is that the tests take forever (I averaged 3-4 hrs./test) and there are three of them.

This class is great if you're happy with a B and have no desire to take any future economics classes. Vrooman mispeaks frequently in lectures, tries to use two entirely different examples at the same time, and only teaches new material in the last 10 minutes.  The only way to do well is to get old tests and memorize Vrooman's cryptic answers.

This professor greatly disappointed me.  His class is easy for those who normally average Cs and below, but it's quite hard for people who usually get As to get As in this class.  Also, I learned basically nothing compared to AP Macroeconomics in high school
The best!
AWESOME CLASS. VROOMAN ROCKS. He is so good at explaining the material, and his tests are pretty straightforward. Not difficult to do well if you go to class. ALL ECON MAJORS SHOULD TAKE THIS CLASS.

Loved the class.  Wasn't too hard - you're given a very good idea about what will be on the test, but you have to write a LOT on the exams in order to do well.  I averaged 2 blue books full.  Very reasonable for a Econ 250+ course.

Take this course no matter what.  You'll have to study to get an A (or A-) but Vrooman's the man and will explain everything well.  You have to go to class, but that's not a big deal since Vrooman keeps the class interesting and fun.

His lectures are really interesting. No textbook required, which means you need to actually show up. Taking good notes will help a lot, since every question is based on what he said in class. If you are good with graphs, his class will be super easy. He will relate everything to sports and politics. Analyze how he asks questions and you'll be fine

This class isn't easy by any means. However, the level of difficulty is tolerable because the subject matter is extremely interesting. Although there isn't attendance, you really have to go or you will struggle on the tests. He will also call you out if you skip

This class is great. Go to class because you can't do well on the tests otherwise. It was harder than I thought it would be, but still one of my favorite classes. He is very willing to help if you have questions. Go to lab at Sam's...it's the best part of the class.
No Comments

The curve makes this class hard to fail but also hard to get an A- usually you can only miss 2 questions on the test out of 36. He will ask the questions he says he may ask on graphs. Old tests are key. Know why every right answer is right, and every wrong, wrong. If you don't understand, go to office hours. He will explain them all if you ask him.
You must go to class!

absolutely terrible, if you go to class you might do well, and if you dont, then you will have problems... i love sports and beer and while i appreciate the analogies, they get old quick and make him sound like an idiot... his test questions arent very straightforward either

There's no book for this class so although attendance isnt mandatory, to study you have to be there. And interpret confusing graphs that he throws in there. He favors the football players and the only real thing ilearned is that beer and football are what college is about. Which is fun but a test rolls around and you have no clue what's on it.
Vrooman is, hands down, the best econ professor at Vandy.  Sports Econ is a great class and the amount you learn is unreal.

very arrogant and unhelpful...if you are a girl (or guy) who isnt very much into sports DO NOT take this class, i attended every single class and studied my non-existent textbook FOREVER and felt like I knew the stuff but then would get Cs on all the tests....take buckles

There is no textbook, no powerpoints or lecture notes aside from confusing graphs. You're supposed to write down whatever bull comes out of his mouth and be tested on it later. There was no homework, but I didn't learn anything except that all college students are supposed to care about is beer and football. Worst class I've ever taken at Vanderbil

Go to class or you will fail, guaranteed. There is no book, only class notes. He will give you some old tests to review and they help, study them. He grades compared to everyone else so A's change depending how dumb the rest of the class is. He's funny as hell so listen.
do. not. take. this. class. seriously... buckles is the better option for those without econ experience. the little extra work is soooo worth it
Awesome professor. Fun class. GO TO CLASS OR YOU WILL FAIL.
An Angry and soft southerner
GREAT

vrooman rocks.  If you can take 280 - take it.  It was the best class ive had at vanderbilt by far.  Its challenging but vrooman explains things very clearly.  Gotta make it to class though, however i found myself never ever wanting to miss it.  Take 280 and go to the friday "lab" at Sam's and get to know the guy -hes awesome
If you have a limited econ background..take Buckles.
awesome class, awesome guy "rodger, are you stoned again?"
Vrooman uses tons of sports analogies for his entry level econ classes, so if you're not up on sports, don't take it -- wait for buckles or someone else.

Vrooman is the reason I am now an Econ major.  He uses no text so if you go to class and review sessions you have to be a retard not to earn an A.  He is extremely clear if you pay attention and go to class.  His class is logical and he doesn't require you to think like he does to get an A.
Vrooman's the reason I never got an econ major.  Unclear, never helpful, goofy in manner.  Very nice guy - curves his classes too much.  Take someone else.
Great class
Hard teacher but a good class. No homework, No text.
if you don't miss too many classes, and study your notes, this is a pretty easy class.  He's pretty entertaining.
Do yourself a huge favor and take very good notes. If you do this without missing more than two or three classes you've got an A.

For me Vrooman's class went by really quickly each day.  I took AP Econ. in high school and his class is ten times more interesting.  He's funny, laid back, and there's no homework.  Tests are hard but there is only four tests and most of the questions are taken straight from old tests.

No Hmwk in this class. You just have to study for three tests and go to class, which isnt bad b/c his lectures are entertaining.  IF YOU ARE ONE OF THOSE PEOPLE THAT STUDIES BY MEMORIZING YOUR NOTES THEN TAKE BUCKELS because Vrooman doesn't use a textbook - he tests you on what he says in class.

Don't listen to all of the bashing from the Econ 100 people- they're just upset that the old tests they had didn't match up to the tests he gave. Sports Econ is a great class that any Econ major should take and he is actually very helpful in office hours- if you can actually get in (long lines).

Vrooman is the kind of professor you would want to hang out with. He is such a cool guy and gives great, funny lectures. His tests are challenging but you will do fine if you prepared by actually thinking and not by memorizing the old notes and tests.
No book...not helpful in office hours....tests are way too hard...curve will screw you over....avoid, avoid, avoid
Great class and teacher. Can't beat 2 for 1 beers at lab.

If you are already familiar with Macro, his class is not that bad and he has a unique a fun way of dealing with Macro topics. Can be intimidating and an ass, but if you can get over that, his class is a good experience.

This class is really hard. No book, no powerpoint, only notes that you can get down from his lectures. Must attend class regularly to pass. Lectures are really interesting, but I question the application of some material beyond this class. Doesn't build good foundation in econ-take Buckles for that.

He has favorites with students and if you are not his favorite, don't bother going to office hours. He won't help you at all! To be his favorite, you have to be a hot chick! Also, tests are hard and graded on some weird curve that nobody understands.
getting to the point isn't a strength of his

Fun/interesting lectures. Tests can be hard and multiple choice can be tricky. I got all A's and A-'s for all the exams. But I ended up with a B+ for the semester because of some weird curve. So you never know what your grade in that class will be until the very end. I didn't like his curve system.
this man is the wort teacher i have ever had. he is gross, sleazy and ****. do not take his class.

Tests are unreasonably hard.  Vrooman is a smart guy; you feel as though you're learning a lot in class until the test comes along and you make C's.  Also, picks favorites and rarely receptive to students during office hours.
Great teacher, especially if you like sports, if you go to class, easy A or B.  No homework or textbooks, or papers.

Vrooman gives funny and relatively interesting lectures, and he keeps macroecon pretty simple, though the tests are kind of scary at first, you learn how to take a vrooman test and the course turns out OK. His lectures include profanity, which I see as a bonus.
hysterical but a really hard class! no book and few grades.
Vrooman's a great guy but the class really blows.  Didn't learn anything and the tests are ridiculously abstract.

i love vrooman!  the tests are hard, but he makes econ entertaining (i actually considered an econ minor until i took another econ course and realized i hated it) little known fact: he's one of the top 5 sports economists in the nation!
Okay, so the guy was hilarious and everything, but I didn't learn a darn thing in that class. Not having a book really sucked.
He makes economics far more interesting than it was in most of my econ classes...
hard but interesting in class.  curve is tough but he's still worth taking.  very helpful outside of class.
Thinks he is a football player...still.  Won't prepare you for anything.  Doesn't actually teach econmics.
Vroom is da BOMBASTIC.  How can you NOT like the man who has lab at Sam's?
I don't know why anyone would still take this class from this professor, he doesn't prepare you at all for any econ classes following it.
Prof. Vrooman is a great teacher, but he needs to get a book. Also, he needs to get rid of his grading curve.
Vrooman is TOUGH and won't help outside of class.  Refused to answer question about previous tests that he had given us.  Tests are hard unless you get it completely.
He's hilarious and puts things in a simple way that makes learning them a lot easier.
Takes getting used to his sports analogies.  Grades on curve...20% A's, 20% B's, 20% C's, etc..
his class is interesting, just be sure to prepare for tests by looking over the old ones.

Great lecturer...makes the material really interesting but makes the tests hard. Make sure you really know all of the material before going into the test. But definately one of the bests teachers I have had at Vandy!

Some knowledge of sports required.* Vrooman is fun and there's no HW, but the tests are tricky. You can memorize your notes and get a C. If you have trouble with multiplechoice tests, don't take this class. Vrooman's one of the best profs I've had @vandy.
Great lecturer - tests are hard but fair and intelligent for multiple choice tests.
No Comments
You gotta study, and sometimes he can throw you a curve ball, but why **** about studying when you don't have any regular homework?  One of the more memorable classes I've taken here.
Great prof.  Knows material and challenges the student.  Very fair.
Great class, esp. if you like sports and beer
No homework, just make sure you go to class. Tests can be a little tricky, but he always gives you an old one so you can practice.

Vrooman is one of the best profs at Vandy...he knows how to teach, unlike some boring rich guys who fly in every day just to teach one class (ie Buckles)...if you're a Peabody person who likes Coloring 101, then don't take Vrooman...otherwise, he rules
Awesome teacher, he knows his ****, you have to goto class, but he teaches in a way guys can totally understand

Vrooman spends too much time joking, and too little time showering and teaching.  Take Buckles instead if at all possible.  The cost/benefit of studying for Vrooman's absurd-no study's a B-, 14 or 15 hours for an A-.
No Comments
No Comments
No homework, just show up for lectures. Tests can be tricky though. People who get As on them usually overstudy big time.

Judging by the previous responses, either you like or you dislike Vrooman (spelled correctly with an A, not an I).  I hated economics until I had Vrooman.  He relates the subject to matters I understand -- sports and beer.

There are many things that could have taught this class better than Vroomin. A retarded, ****en, cracked-out monkey comes to mind. Vroomin thinks that by coming to class in sandals and relating economic concepts to beer makes him a good teacher. HE BLOWS

I was an econ major up until Buckles and his 101 class.  If I thought that class was hard, that must mean I've very bad at econ.  Bearing that in mind, I thought Vrooman was extremely easy.  The guy gives some of the best lectures I've had here at Vandy.
No Comments
This man should be fired.
Class is way overrated
I HATED THIS CLASS. He tought nothing important, and was very rude in OH
He's one of the most fun teachers Ive ever had.  Just make sure you go to class.
No Comments
He's unhelpful and his tests are based on his lecture notes, not on theory

This is the best class I took this year. Professor Waters is brilliant, caring and gives brilliant feedback. If your goal is to learn and be a better filmmaker, Prof. Waters is the best professor to work with. If your goal is to whine about the class load, then give up filmmaking altogether. Would take this class again without a doubt.

Waters is kind and passionate
Expect to make 4-5 short films w guidance on working with a camera, lights, sound
He grades fairly based on the execution of your films
Dont take if you are looking for an easy course
The quality of your projects will be directly tied to your effort
It took a lot of practice to learn premiere, lighting, sound design

Professor Waters is truly a sweet man outside of class, but when it comes to grading and critiquing, he is very rude, and he rarely gives feedback that will help you improve. Honestly, he turned me off of studying film at all at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Waters is by far the worst professor I've had at Vanderbilt. At first, he comes off as caring as helpful to beginners, and will take into account that they have no experience when grading. But, he then relentlessly tears them down for not being up to par with other students with experience, and leaves no constructive criticism. Just a mean guy.

This class is definitely a lot more work than it seems, just due to the nature of how much time it takes to brainstorm/shoot/edit projects. Waters is a great and caring professor who wants to see you succeed, but he also needs to see you put in the effort. Excellent choice of professor for a film fundamentals class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Waters is passionate about what he teaches, so he pays attention to who's putting in  effort. In-class participation or stopping by office hours to ask about projects go a long way with him. He's got a great sense of humor, as well, and he's probably the most friendly professor I've had at Vanderbilt.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed class with Professor Waters and I looked forward to class each week. If you participate in class and do your work, you will do well. Waters is a funny and likable professor, and he really knows what he's talking about.

Waters just wants people to participate and be visited in office hours. You do the homework, see him outside of class, and take his criticisms into consideration and you'll do well. Skip class or don't come prepared and his mean side comes out. He is helpful with writing comments and editing work.

Took this to fulfill a W requirement thinking I could get by my creativity and wit, I was wrong. Challenges you to turn ideas into material. Adheres to the txtbook little too strictly. Taking this during maymester expecting a lesser load but he giving us no slack. Overall good dude, just gotta do the work and be open to his insightful criticism.

Waters is awesome. He cares about his students, wants their work to look professional, and by all accounts knows what he's talking about. You'll get out what you put in, and for some students that won't be much. For me it was off the charts. Without his help I couldn't have excelled so much in so little time.

Dr. Watkins is amazing!! She is extremely caring and makes class engaging. Class assignments included field notes, interviews, and reflections all writing based. She is very flexible and wants to help all that she can. Take her classes!
Took prof watkins for a mandatory pedagogy class. she was great, class was pretty boring though. super understanding and kind professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Watkins is amazing!!! Science Ed major or not, you should take a class taught by her, and Science Modeling (SCED 3400) is a fantastic class to take. Experimentation and investigation with freedom like I've never seen before. Truly does make you think about what science education can be. Her discussions and conversations are incredibly engaging!
She's one of the best professors at Vanderbilt, and MUSO1240 is one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. Strongly recommend!
Really interesting class and she is a really fun teacher to have. The music theory can be aggravating, but she really tried to make it as easily digestible as possible.

Great class to take for communications requirements for students with some background in music. Graded off of songwriting assignments and musical theory and there are 3 in-person song performances where you sing in front of the whole class. She's passionate about what she teaches and if you do the work, should be an A course.

Professor Walker is a great professor, I just wish the course description had been a little more accurate as to what the course would actually be like. Had I known it would be more music theory and singing in front of the class than actual songwriting I probably wouldn't have taken it. Nonetheless it was a fine class and I learned a bit.
Daily homework, probably about an hour.5 per week. A couple tests that if you practiced music theory was very very manageable. Homeworks were chill just take notes on theory in class

Deanna is incredible. Grades fairly leniently but still provides helpful feedback. Very encouraging and welcoming classroom environment. Sometimes certain days can feel boring or repetitive but my favorite days were the song performances! Definitely learned a lot of lyrical techniques and refreshed my basic understanding of music theory
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Songwriting II is fun, and the overall class is structured very loosely - songs due each week are based on simple pre-defined themes (like love song, story song, no chorus songs etc.) and Prof. Walker is the sweetest. Gives terrific feedback, and is an equally great musician herself.

One of my favorite classes that I've taken at Vanderbilt. Prof Walker is one of the most caring, passionate, and knowledgeable teachers ive ever meet. Definitely can be a difficult class if you dont have prior music background, but if you do its an easy class that you will learn a ton of new interesting material in. highly recommend either way.

Super nice professor. Easy class but I would have liked more structure, organization, and proven songwriting techniques. Critique is just opinion and everyone gets complimented. If you are serious about songwriting, there are a lot of classes in Nashville with songwriters that have written hits and aren't just teaching theory.
Professor Walker is such an amazing professor. She is super kind and caring to her students and just an overall heartwarming person to be around. Was my first music class, and I really enjoyed it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Can't say enough good things about her. She genuinely cares about each student and their development as a songwriter and constantly works to put you in contact with fantastic resources in the songwriting industry. Even if you don't wanna be a professional songwriter, this class is a lot of fun and absolutely worth the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best choice you could make would be to take a class with her. She's really passionate about helping you get your thoughts out onto the page and knows how to be encouraging while also offering valuable constructive feedback.

I just finished Songwriting 2 with Deanna and it was the only class this semester that I was devastated to leave. Deanna is so amazing and I have grown significantly as a songwriter since studying with her. She provides a really open and constructive classroom environment. I am truly heartbroken the course doesn't fit in my schedule next semester.

I LOVE DEANNA. She is so amazing. She is so kind and caring. She's solid at teaching theory. She'll make time outside of class to help and give you advice and support however she can. I can't wait to take Songwriting 2!!!

Really chill, creative! Can be a little disorganized, but I love the comfy atmosphere and her adult sessions (inspirational! Guest speakers like Shelly Peiken). If anything, I wish she'd explained more about creating melodies/chord progressions for songs (we covered a lot of theory and writing/lyric techniques), although we improvised a lot.

If you are a super creative and talented musician, this class is not for you. Take a higher level songwriting or composing class, or you will be bored.  Otherwise: have fun, be musical, and boost your GPA!

Such a fun class! The actual song writing part is easy. As long as it shows that you put in a little effort, she'll give you a good grade for it. Music theory, however, is a little more tricky. If you are someone who has never taken theory before, make sure you pay attention and do the hw (easy). Very fun class!

Prof. Walker was pretty much useless. I got the feeling that she was much more involved in her own music career than teaching---a year later, I'm still getting emails on her list serv asking if I know people in the music industry who can help her, or to come pay and watch her show. She was a fine professor, but I got tired of being means to an end.

Deanna was my favorite teacher and is one of the sweetest people that will go out of her way to be as helpful as possible!  She's a genuinely talented songwriter herself, yet is very down-to-earth and friendly.  She also sings/plays piano.  Attending the night class was great too!  I'm hoping on taking some more of her classes if at all possible.

I took D's class 3 times. I absolutely loved it and looked forward to it. The classes are SUPER EASY. Don't bother buying or reading the textbooks. Attendance is mandatory though, and you're required to go to D's adult night class 3 times a semester. You don't have to know how to play an instrument, either. The assignments are lyric-based.

I've taken Songwriting 1 and 2. 1 is a lot harder than 2 because of the music theory. 2 is much easier and funner. Make sure you keep up with your journal so you don't end up rushing it at the end of the semester. Songs are critiqued by classmates. If you have stagefright, you're going to have to get over it because the final exam is at the Commons

Great, fun, and informative class. Don't let the comments below fool you. It's not 100% easy. Half the class is writing songs, and the other half is music theory. It's basic music theory but still difficult for someone unfamiliar with it. I recommend this class if you have a genuine interest in songwriting, but I would not recommend it as a blowoff

Deanna is pretty much perfect. There's really nothing at all challenging about this class if you pay attention to the theory lessons. It's an easy A but totally not a class to just blow off Deanna puts all of herself into teaching and loves when you do the same with your songs. you HAVE to take this class.

hardest thing about this class is just being brave enough to perform a song in front of the class. Homework isn't too bad but can feel sort of like rote drilling in order to create memorization but maybe that's just how to learn music. She sounds like she is from California (she's from New Mexico).

Best class! D is so helpful and so interesting. Theory work can be tedious, but she is willing to help you if you need it! If you are shy, you better get over it because you are required to perform your songs in class..so fun!!

She's really laid back and cool but does expect you to do the assignments on time. She wants everyone to do well and grades assignments based on effort (except for theory stuff). Take the class its really fun!

Such a fun class!! D is super helpful and willing to work with you to make sure you have a good grasp on the material! If you are shy about performing your songs in class...you're going to have to get over it :) Loved the class!!

D is one of the most chill professors at Vandy. She seems to know everything about the music industry (both lyrics and music) and getting into the business. No prior knowledge of either music theory of songwriting is required, but any would be helpful. Eager to help and answer any questions. Very open, chill, and encouraging.

She's awesome! Totally recommend her class to anyone who is interested in learning more about music and then applying that knowledge to making original songs. She's very open-minded and supportive; no one is "bad at music." Very nice- her class rocks.

be careful taking this class.  unless you are an experienced musician, both in theory and in songwriting, you will find yourself far behind the rest of the class and this teacher.  she cares but can be a huggggggeeee ****h.

very cool - she expects you to do the work (which it seems like there's too much of for a beginning music class) but as long as you attempt it, you'll get a good grade.  and it's not hard, just repetitive.

One of the coolest women I've ever met.  Easy grader, but be cool and don't take advantage of her!  Very very kind person and so eager to help.  Has given me so many opportunities in the music industry.
Had her for songwriting and theory.  She is cool as hell and the assignments are fun.  If you are any way musical and creative, then you will do well in this class and work well with her.
The best classes I've taken at Vanderbilt.  D is supportive and teaches a great class.  If you're interested in songwriting at all, talk to her and take the course, it will help you.
awesome prof and great person. a fun class regardless of your musical background.
Learned a great deal from her.  She is an amazing piano player.
Spacey but fun, fairly lenient but expects you to do the work.
Sometimes a little spacy but very nice and supportive
Good professor overall. He cares a lot about his students and is very knowledgeable about Russian history.

Such a nice guy. Professor Wcislo encourages students to "form their own narrative" on the history and encourages intellectual risk-taking. Loves talking to students, especially in office hours. Grades came from participation, one four-page paper, and three six-page papers.

Prof. Wcislo clearly knows a lot about Russian history but he is not great at coherently expressing it with students. Lectures are often longwinded and confusing. 3 essays worth 60%, take home final worth 20%, and participation worth 20%. Pretty tough grader but not that hard to get a B

I would highly recommend this class to anyone with any interest in the subject. Wcislo is a very engaging and erudite professor, makes the lectures very lucid, and is very understanding. He will generally grant extensions for legitimate reasons and offers proof reading of essays. Reading intensive but interesting material. TA was helpful as well.

Tried  hard on the first paper, got a B. Tried VERY hard on the second paper, got a B. Tried VERY hard on the midterm, got a B minus. Didn't try on the last paper, got a B. Still not sure what he was looking for.

Fantastic professor. Very engaging, knowledgable, thought-provoking and helpful. Class is mostly lecture based with some discussion, but he is always willing to continue the conversation with you privately. No tests, only papers, but DO come to class. You will not do well if you skip. Not an easy A by any stretch, but still very possible.
A very nice man. Is more than willing to help you out and wants to hear your opinions and thoughts. Lectures are interesting (even though he always goes over). Would definately recommend him.

Great professor, took him two years ago and still ask for advice for my hist classes.  One of the best people I've met that teaches at Vandy...and as for those who rated him harshly, yes he will give you bad grades if you blow off his class.  And he's extremely smart, so he will know, and your grade will reflect it.  So get over it.

Very passionate about history, but definitely a lot of reading. Papers can be difficult but if you go to him he'll read rough drafts and tell you exactly what to do to help you. Not the easiest A but it's very possible.
Smart. Kind. Good. Best class ever with Damon and Lachs.
No Comments

By far the worst teacher I've ever had.  I took him as a senior, and he couldn't care less about his students. He makes no effort to understand where you're coming from if you discuss any grading problems, and his lectures are boring to say the LEAST. I am dumber for having taken his class. I award him no points, and may God have mercy on his soul.

Very pretentious.  Class is boring and he lectures without regard to the course.  He does help outside of class, but when grading he doesn't seem to have any basis for his critique.  Avoid him, espeically if you don't like teachers with a chip on their shoulder.

Awesome teacher, he's really funny. He makes the subject pretty interesting for you so his lectures go by in a flash. For West. Civ., post 1700, he doesn't require much, but the midterm and take home final were a ****. If you put some effort into the class, you'll do well

Long-winded and at sometimes doesn't quite connect up with what he started off with.  He lost me at the beginning of the semester but had me really learning though I didnt think so.  Lots of texts and readings, hard grader, almost always runs over on time, but GREAT person.

I am a senior and have gone to see a professor outside of class maybe 8 times in my academic career, but Wcislo is a guy to see outside of class.  Pretty much will tell you what he wants.  Great guy too.
His class structure is very weird and not helpful.  His papers require much reading with no direction, and his grading is a level to hard for this course.  I hate him.
Man, I really liked the previous classes, but this one is a drag. It's not very difficult, but it is not engaging at all. I find it laboring sitting through the class and taking notes is impossible.

I have to say, Wcislo is the worst history teacher I've had, and I'm a history major. This class is impenetrable, owing to his long, unclear, tangential sentences. He is very smart, but this class is uninteresting and not much of a history class at all. More like sociology, with harder grading.

Prof. Wcislo is an extremely engaging professor, with a vast knowledge of his areas of expertise. Grading can be a bit harsh, he challanges you but is not unfair in his grading. You better be prepared to think in his class. Which I think is a good thing.
So far so good - the semester just started!  He makes you want to research the past, beyond the 8 texts we are using!
He is hard yet very interesting and engages well with the students.
Never lets you out on time, ALWAYS runs over
AMAZING professor, inspired me to go beyond the classroom.
Simply one of the best professors I've had at Vandy.  Very helpful, really interesting, and knows what he's talking about.  I like him a lot.
A good professor.  His lectures are engaging.  Enjoyed going to his class.  No tests, only papers.
great lecturer, no tests, likes to pound the table for emphasis
Great lecturer; respectful fellow.
Great guy, very helpful, good prof

Professor is truly not good. She gave me a grade of a Pass in her course when she was the one who had a misleading course overall. I think that she gave me that grade because I didn't attend her class, when I couldn't because I was looking for a job. She also in her previous class did not give me a 4.0 because of a petty reason. Terrible teacher

The course isn't bad overall. It's very lecture-heavy, and Wendy rarely makes eye contact during class. That said, she's helpful in office hours and has strong industry connections. Practice quizzes closely mirror real ones. Exams are tough—you need to know everything, including non-mandatory readings.

Easy class, do not listen to reviews whining about how hard this class is. I showed up to the first class, mid term, and final and ended with a 98. Do the movie extra credit, study each practice test / exam, and make sure your cheat sheet is packed. If you do all of those things are just aren't careless you'll get an A.
Worst lecturer at the school. Leave class more confused than you come in and have to teach yourself. Avoid at all costs.
Take her class only if you want to show off your business talents!

If you've ever had a professor who makes hard content feel easy, she does the opposite. She is very talented at taking normal ideas and making them feel novel, confusing and complex. If I pay attention in class I leave more confused. Tests are the majority of the grade. 0/10
Lecture slides often move at the speed of light, and there's way too much content in the slides. The material isn't terrible, but you basically have to teach yourself all of it

The class is not hard, but there are quite a few things to memorize and keep track of, and she isn't very good at explaining things. Her lectures aren't all that clear either. She does speak a lot about finance as a field though which I think is worth hearing.

Course is easy to do well, 90 for an A- and then lots of extra credit available through the research lab. That being said, I don't think I learned a lot about finance just because the lectures were typically not easy to understand sometimes and it was right before lunch. But she is nice and helpful in office hours.

She is a very kind person but I cannot understand her when she explains topics and does not go very in depth and answer questions. I struggled a lot in this class and had to teach myself all the material. She has very long slides that do not really make sense. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

1 quiz per week (really similar to the practice quiz) Two exams. Two group problem set. She had way too many slides per class which made it impossible to understand anything. You can tell she loves finance but it is so hard to follow her lectures. Rly sweet lady but this class was insanely frustrating. By the end of the semester no one came
boring lectures but he is super smart. also very slow grader so you wont know where you stand in the class

My least favorite class I have taken in my four years. Dr. Wehby, while highly knowledgeable, was the least engaging professor I've ever had. His lectures are dry and unorganized. The exam content is significantly harder than what is gone over in class (but very crammable). No opportunities to participate in class, and an incredibly slow grader.
Wehby's class is extremely boring and he is extremely disorganized. He is a very dry lecturer and I'd zone out frequently. Content is interesting enough, but he makes it dreadful

Dr. Wehby is clearly very passionate about his work and class content. However, he has a lot on his plate, making it very challenging for him to stay up on grading. You can zone out in class, taking the bare minimum notes, and cram before the test, and be fine. It took him about 55 days to grade the first test, so do not expect fast grading.

Dr. Wehby is very passionate about what he teaches. In my class, we were graded on only maybe 4 or 5 things, being 2 midterms, a final, a presentation and participation/attendance, even though he never takes attendance. The downside is that his lectures are pretty boring and being at 8 am they are quite easy to fall asleep in or skip entirely.

Dr. Wehby is a very sweet and knowledgeable professor. His lectures drag on and become boring quickly though, especially at 8 in the morning. Tests are not very hard; he gives out great study guides but we are unable to see any feedback for what we got incorrect. Overall, not a bad or difficult class!

Dr. Wehby is very knowledgeable about this topic. He cares deeply about what he is teaching and it shows. He is an amazing guy and good to his class. He is sweet and humorous. However, this class was very boring, lessons droned on. Exams were online and pretty easy. There is little outside work.

Professor Wehby is knowledgeable about the subject material. However, the disorganized nature of the class and almost non-existent feedback from projects and exams makes the class rough and a slog. Tests ask about the implementation of teaching procedures for special education children, yet, this was barely taught in class. The TA was much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wehby was inaccessible even when most of the class had complaints about him not grading our tests. It was hard to know what you were doing wrong when he didn't post grades or feedback until last minute, and I received no meaningful feedback from him or the TA the entire semester. Knowledgeable and a cool guy, just not a reasonable professor for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wehby is very knowledgable about the disability community and always brings up new and interesting ideas. Really challenges your thinking. He takes forever to grade exams, so you shouldn't count on feedback in between exams.

I loved, loved, loved taking his class. He was such a sweet guy, and though the lectures were dry and sometimes boring, I learned so much. If you talk through the study guide with someone and memorize it, you can get an easy A and learn so much. In retrospect, one of my favorite professors in Peabody.

Professor Wehby is a gem. He knows SO much about his subject area and does the best to make an intro class interesting and useful. Such a good and interesting class. He is sweet and cares about us all. Get close to the TA!! They end up doing a lot of the work and are more accessible since Wehby is so busy.

Dr. Wehby is so knowledgable and experienced in the field, but his lectures are not the most engaging, besides his stories. The class is a little disorganized, lots of assignments at the backend of the semester and pretty much no work at the front - so be prepared for that. Tests are hard, but generally he curves! Alyssa, his normal TA, is great!

Prof Wehby is an expert in his field but he reads off his slides. Any question you ask he is happy to answer and his class is laid out nicely but the tests didn't usually reflect the amount of studying I did. Some of the material is interesting and easy to learn but sometimes I dreaded going to class. For an intro class, the tests are tough
Dr. Wehby is a very knowledgable professor and his class is required for all education majors. Lectures are pretty plain, but if you actually are interested in being a teacher they are not boring.

Prof. Wehby's class was rough because it consisted of him reading off powerpoints for an hour and 20 minutes. As long as you get the notes from class, you can study those for the tests and do well. Go to class before tests because he covers what will be on it, and pay attention to how he wants essays because if you follow his outline it's easy.

Grade based on exams, final, and project. The MC are based off the textbook while the short answer and essay are based off his lecture notes. Wehby shares some inspiring personal stories but the rest of the information he presents are boring and dry. Attendance not mandatory, just review the PPTs he posts after class.

Professor Wehby is super nice and super caring. He really knows his stuff when it comes to special education and he understands that not everyone is going to be a special education teacher, but it is important that all people have some knowledge of persons with disabilities. However, I agree with the other comments, he is very disorganized.

Wehby is the dad. A bit disorganized lectures/notes, but he is the Chair of the #1 department in the country, so understood. Drastically different from McTam. Simply cram for tests and you'll be fine. Lectures bit boring, get fun when tells a personal stories. PLUS, if you're reading this, you should also review when you're done. Pass the baton!

Professor Wehby is the epitome of unorganized. The lectures are painful to sit through, note-taking is a drag. The tests are ridiculously specific to class material, so you better study up. He is a really caring guy though, he's not all bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wehby is a really nice person and he genuinely tries to get to know his students. However, he is extremely disorganized and didn't stick to the syllabus at all, pushing everything back and assigning readingsprojects last minute. He was near impossible to get in contact with (doesn't answer any emails and went out of town a lot) and somewhat vague.

Seems nice and funny, but is super unorganized and unhelpful. Usually doesn't assign readings until the night before, and they're generally pretty long (30-40 pgs). Leaves town often and rarely responds to emails. Doesn't stick to syllabus. Everything got pushed back so far that we had a project, test, and final exam within the same week.

Prof. Wehby is super nice, helpful, available, whatever you want a professor to be. The lectures can get boring if only because the material gets repetitive after a while, but he can be funny too, so it's not too bad. Tests are easy if you do his study guides and don't blow it off. For SPED 1010, you need time for 15 (or more) volunteer hours.
GREAT PROFESSOR. Attend class and put in effort and you will be fine. He is very interested in the subject and caring. Nice overall.

Professor Wehby is an amazing, nice, funny, cool teacher. He has a lot of experience in this subject and is super eager and genuine in delivering the material.  The lectures can be a little boring and his notes are scattered, but he's open to helping outside the class. Complete his study guides and ask him questions and you'll do well on tests.

Professor Wehby is passionate, but he just has this manner of speaking that makes you want to not pay attention. He also makes you print fillintheblank notes and doesn't allow computers.  Also, the material is more hands-on...and you are tested on it as if it is quantitative data.

Wehby is such a nice guy, and super helpful during office hours. Although he does not cover everything that is on the tests in class, other assignments like volunteering and movie reviews can make up for poor test grades. He just wants you to get an idea of special education since most of those in his classes will be general ed teachers.

It was a lot of reading and his style of teaching detracts from learning the material.  Interesting stuff that I would rather just learn and know than be tested on (considering the way that he presented it).
Awesome.
most boring class of my life i couldn't make myself go...and he grades very hard
Not a difficult class, but he the information and resources are very outdated and he presents a very biased view of SPED.
Definitely Ray Ramano. Loved his class...very helpful and very good at recruiting students to the field. His enthusiasm is contagious.
No Comments
He is awesome.  He really appreciates hard workers and makes an effort to get to know his students.
Awsome class and teacher.  You can tell he's really interested in the subject and really cares about his students.  Tests are easy as long as you read the notes.

best teacher by far! very entertaining, interested in the subject, schedules lunches and dinners with his students just to get to know them better. great guy. very easy. made the final exam optional. tests are easy. great class. best teacher ever! i'm not even sped major
If you've seen "Welcome to Mooseport" then you already know Dr. Wehby.  His dad owns a big plumbing business here in Nashville.
Its all been said. He's a cool guy. He's also a good guy to know in the SPED department along the way. Can be very helpful, so make an impression and make a friend
He's the man
He IS Ray Romano.  Besides that, cool guy, kinda a boring class, but you'll learn a lot and it's a good experience.
REALLY CARES BOUT HIS STUDENTS
Wehby is such a caring professor!  He really wants everyone to do well, so it is very very possible to make an A in the class.
BORING. wehby is a nice guy and he definitely knows his stuff, he's just so boring. his tests suck: tons of material and only 30 questions on it
Looks EXACTLY like Ray Romano, and is an interesting person. Easy tests, but boring class. Ends up fun at the end if you stick it out.

Good Guy, Pretty Easy Class.  But, he's a bit boring.  Class drags on.  My girlfriend said he's hot, so that's why I put that.  However, if you are a guy...I was 1 of 7 guys in the class of 120.  Talk about good odds.
Professor Johns is very easy to get along with, and his relaxed approach to lab aids applied learning.
Love this guy who will always be there when u need help. Although the text mentioned in class sometimes will be too hard to understand, he will be patient to explain everything for u!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: The exams are not difficult if you have a decent understanding of the content, which most students don't, because the way he teaches the content is confusing and over complicated. I didn't go to class for the second half of the semester, looked up the homework on Chegg, but thanks to exam curves (and dropping one exam) got a halfway decent grade

His class material was difficult, but the exam questions weren't as hard. If you could actually study his lecture notes you would find better derivations of equations than those given in the book. His homework problems were hard, but if you could re-do his derivations in lectures you would conquer all of them.

Johns is hilarious, he is very helpful outside of class but his lectures tend to be entirely derivation-base, a stark contrast to a textbook with almost none. Don't expect an easy A from him, but he's probably your only option anyway.

Good class. Material is difficult but the grading is easy, since hw is 30% and the lab is 25%. Tests are also quite easy compared to the material covered in lectures. He is very helpful, willing to answer your questions for 30 minutes after the lecture.

The material is VERY DIFFICULT but absolutely fascinating. If you are not interested in quantum physics, you should avoid this class. He is knowledgeable and very helpful in or outside class. Tests are impossibly tough but he curves them. Also HW's are 40% of the grade.

He's a great guy and one of the most helpful professors you'll probably ever get, but his homework is hard and it's very difficult to follow along with him in class.  None of us would had survived if he hadn't passed out his lecture notes each day before class.  225 is just naturally impossible though, so it's best to get a helpful prof like him.

Very tough class. The material is very difficult, you will only understand if you really try. Most people had no clue what was going on in his lectures. His homework assignments and takehome tests were very difficult, but you can do well if you spend a lot of time on it. Most students had an A or a C/D.
Doc Johns is funny and engaging, but his lectures sometimes are only derivations of equations given in the textbook. He really knows his stuff and is really helpful.

He posts sample exams online, which proved the most helpful for studying. MP assigments are time consuming and may not even apply to the lectures or the tests. He is very very stingy with partial credit. Lectures sometimes are also completely useless.

this guy is bill nye, hilarious in class... actually kept me awake during a 9 am class. talked about being stoned and is kind of strange at times. his tests are much easier if you go to his review sessions so go! masteringphysics sucks, but he'll give you the answers if you go to his sunday night reviews. overall, a good choice fro the class

all right professor. a little too blind to what goes on in class and how much cheating happens.  Sometimes the tests come out of left field and you have no idea what is going on.  a genuinely nice guy, though.
Love this guy. Great teacher.
Big Willy is the first professor, and the only, to address the class in Klingon
Very unaccomadating, and somewhat spiteful.

Dr. Johns is nerdy, and quirky, but I switched into his 8am lecture with the 7pm lab just to get out of another more "well known" professor and never once regreted it.  He ended up being a pretty alright guy, and I dont even like physics.

This is a good guy grade A. Compared to what i hear about other teachers, this guy is fun and quirky. He is kinda a nerd and isn't clear in lecture, so i skipped about 1/3 of lectures, but get him nonetheless. he gives you candy after you hand in your test.
Weirdest guy ever.
great prof.  he is so weird that you don't ever fall asleep.  good thing to have for a morning class. help sessions are key, use them!
wonderfully nice man, very helpful, very interesting.. one of the most enjoyable classes I've had!
No Comments
class doesn't help much, but he is great at explaining problems in help sessions/ office hours.

Professor Williams is a kind person who will tell you exactly what he quizzes over and always gives time to his students. It's an easy A, however his lectures are often redundant and I don't learn much from his class. You have to know some of the subject beforehand to understand the material (he's not clear). Strict on how he wants things done.

Professor Williams is the best professor for musicianship/aural skills at Blair. He would literally meet with you as many times a week as you want. He lays out what you're graded on very clearly and you can re-take any of the performance assessments. Loved his class and his personality. I'm taking musicianship with him again next semester.

Depending on your aural/theory background, Williams' class is either a breeze or takes effort. There isn't much work outside class, but it's expected that you consistently review concepts. Strict about attendance-you definitely need to show up to know what's going on. Seems a bit intense at first, but he is approachable and cares about helping you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Williams is great until he hands you a pop quiz over a topic you barely learned in class. He expects his students to have known difficult topics beforehand and doesn't go back to them after he has explained them once. He expects aural skills to already be developed and doesn't ever explain how to develop them. Would not take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Williams is an amazing teacher. He cares about his students and is passionate about the material he teaches. He will give you a great foundation to build off of during your time at Blair. You need to pay attention and work hard in class, but there is essentially no work outside of class. Be sure to show up on time with all the necessary materials.
Great professor, learned a lot, great to go to for office hours. Participate and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Williams was, by far, my worst teacher at Blair. His knowledge on the subject is very limited, and he can only teach it one way (Theoretical learners beware). When I asked him for help (multiple times), the only advice he could give me was to just practice more. If you have little to no experience with musicianship, I would not take him.

Prof. Williams was a good professor, he's very type-a.  This class is unusual, it looks like it isn't much work, but if you don't keep practicing the concepts steadily, you'll find you're way behind.  Go easy, but definitely practice.  This makes the exams and hearings he has relatively easy.

Good prof, comes off a little tough at first.  light grader in general, especially for hearings/exams.  Lenient about attendance.  Easy to understand, get extra help from, etc.  I'm no expert at this stuff, but I got an A, so I think he's a good deal lol
You only have to go to class when there's a quiz - rare for Blair classes.  There's very little homework, but the quizzes and tests are hard, so you'll need to prepare/teach yourself the material.

Although you must attend class to pass, he doesn't take attendance and it's very easy to slack off in this class- until the exam. I feel like I've had to teach myself a bit, as he doesn't walk you through everything. It's an odd combination of babying and throwing things at you that you haven't really been taught.

Williams is extremely nice and approachable. He doesn't make the class any harder than it needs to be, so how well you do depends on your own ear training/sight singing skills, not his teaching skills. He doesn't assign a lot of homework, but make sure you're prepared for the sight singing quizzes in his office.

Intro to GenAI was taught by several people including Dr. White, but they don't seem to care about this class at all. It was basically a tutorial of how to use ChatGPT. Super boring, half the class doesn't come. Several instructors were also unresponsive to emails, including about incorrect grades.
Great professor.

All the actual content comes from prerecorded lectures that are very digestible and easy to understand. Class can get a bit repetitive with about biweekly class presentations but they are usually easy. Grades pretty chill. Good class to take.

The workload never really lets up with this class -- there's tons of lecture content and weekly quizzes -- but I thought the material was really interesting, and the assignments were really creative and actually taught a ton of useful skills. Prof White is clearly very smart, and is a good teacher because of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a decent prof, the programming assignments can get a little tricky at times. My biggest complaint is that his grading isn't very transparent and I didn't know what grade I had in the class until they were published. The group project was really interesting and actually taught me a lot.

No tests, quizzes are take-home, relaxed professor. A true blessing for the Computer Science department.  The first half of CS 278 is spent learning about software development by doing in-class exercises and small projects in groups. The second half is spent in a larger group project which needs to work by the end of the class.
Very good addition to the CS professors. Great professor, would really recommend any of his classes
Professor Wiseman is the best professor I have met at Vanderbilt. The content is challenging, but he is so available to meet in terms of office hour appointments. He is a great instructor as well.

Professor Wiseman is the best professor I have met at Vanderbilt University. The content is challenging, but he is so available to meet in terms of office hour meetings. He is such a great instructor as well.

I'm pre-med and this is the hardest class I have ever taken. Be warned, this class is a simulation of the office and you will walk out more confused than you were walking in. I'm convinced Professor Wiseman has never stuttered in his life and he is incredibly funny. PROBLEM SETS TAKE 10+ HOURS! Get ready to hear: "Is that a question or statement?"

Professor Wiseman is the best polsci professor I had so far. Lecture is worth listening; He genuinely knows so much about the topic; Very engaging materials. Though quizzes and exams might be a little challenging when you don't have a big brain to memorize a lot of things, he curves. A very nice curve in the end.

Professor Wiseman is the best professor at Vanderbilt by a long shot! Attendance is technically not mandatory, but you will be lost if you miss lectures. However, it just goes to show that the lectures actually have substance. That being said, you won't want to miss lectures anyway since Wiseman is genuinely so funny and entertaining!
Thats my Uncle!!!!! :D

Attendance isn't tracked, but you're not going to pass the class if you don't go. The material is very difficult and grading can be tough: this is not a blowoff class. But  Wiseman genuinely takes a lot of time for students and is very patient with questions. Class is about 85% Game theory and 15% politics, so be warned if you only want polisci.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for game theory, and it was the hardest class I've ever taken but I loved it. You have to go to class (nothing is posted online), but classes are super interesting-- he's a great lecturer, caring, and funny. Tests and problem sets are really hard but he curved the final grades. Take if you're willing to put in the work, it's worth it!

Prof. Wiseman is intelligent, caring, and inspirational. Very fun and engaging lectures, and easy to connect after classes. Problem sets and exams could be really challenging (the mean of 2nd midterm is 62%), but if you're willing to work hard, you'll get a lot out of it. Definitely recommend if interested in game theory (and political applications

Prof. Wiseman is a great professor and gives such detailed lectures and slides that you really do not need to do the readings, even though he jokes that it hurts him when students don't read. He is very thorough and professional and happy to help if needed. One policy memo, midterm, final, group presentation. Use the TA for assignments, too!

Prof Wiseman is fantastic. Some of the best lectures I've ever heard. He knows everything about the public sector and can be great as a life/ career coach too. Class was pretty easy: a few assignments, all mostly easy. Readings aren't strictly necessary. Definitely take Prof Wiseman if you can; you'll be glad you did! He's awesome.

Take this class. Professor Wiseman genuinely wants students to learn and is dedicated to being accessible outside of class. If youre willing to dedicate a lot of time to problem sets, youll get a lot out of this class (and do better in the class overall). 100% recommend this class and Professor Wiseman.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Wiseman is one of the smartest people at Vanderbilt. His lectures are artful. That said, game theory is exceptionally tough. The problem sets are difficult (and are 50% of the final grade), but the exams are more straightforward. You will have to work your ass off, but it is very rewarding and he genuinely wants you to succeed.

Prof Wiseman is a very caring and brilliant professor. Problem sets are more difficult than the actual exams, but he is always available to help outside of class. He's responded to emails at 2am, and while it is not an easy A, he genuinely wants to see you succeed.

Prof Wiseman is extremely intelligent, and his lectures will show that. He's extremely organized and has taught this class so many times that lectures are clear and interesting. He brings in relevant policy issues for discussion that makes it interesting. By no means an easy A, but not extremely tough either. Great guy

Incredible professor. Genuinely really wants to get to know students, and he strikes a good balance between seriousness and approachability. His lectures are planned down to the second, and he explains everything very clearly. He has high expectations, so you need to work for an A, but it's manageable if you plan ahead.

Difficult subject material, but Wiseman is good at teaching it. He is likable and makes the class enjoyable. Homework and tests are difficult, but are graded fairly and not unbearable given you attend lectures and keep up on the readings.

Difficult class but knowledgable and funny professor. Important to go to the lectures and take notes. The tests are open-note so not that bad. Homeworks are harder than midterms. Took me 10 hours to do some problem sets and he won't answer many questions on them. 5 problem sets all semester and 10% of grade for each one. Nice curve at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Homework is a significant portion of the grade, which you think would be an excellent thing, but the homework is significantly harder than material covered in class or in the textbook and is graded tough. He is a good lecturer and takes care to provide individual attention; however, he will not help students with homework problems whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wiseman makes class enjoyable through his humor. When he asks a question to the class, however, be prepared to defend the reasoning behind your answer. He also always made himself available outside of class. With the policy memo, there was some lack of clarity as to what he was expecting, but it was ironed out through meeting with him.

He had a sense of humor that made the 8am class bearable for me. He is overall a nice and smart man but can seem condescending if you are not used to his style. The class is undeniably difficult. Specifically, one is expected to be very knowledgable about the readings and the lectures for the exams.

I cannot say enough great things about Alan Wiseman. Yes, the class is hard and the material is boring. BUT he makes class entertaining. He really teaches and cares about your learning- somewhat of a rarity. He is so funny and so accessible. He will do anything to help you truly understand and really develop an interest. An AMAZING teacher and man
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Wiseman is incredibly smart and his lectures leave you thinking about policy in a whole new way. Grading can be a little tough but he's fair and at the end of the day you'll learn a ton in this class

Wiseman is an alright professor but be prepared to have no idea what level of detail is expected on the homework and tests. You're basically left to fend for yourself and that leads to the homeworks taking forever to complete. He does curve though which is nice.

Great, great professor. Best lecturer I've had in the PSCI department. Game theory is hard but he makes it as accessible as possible and gives every student the tools to succeed. Only problem with the class is that grading can be kind of contrived, but if you pay attention in lectures you'll know what he is looking for. Tough, rewarding class

Professor Wiseman gives excellent lectures and offers appropriate though difficult assignments and exams. Class time is spent either learning about theory through Wiseman's case and text study or engaging in discussion about politics. His readings are enlightening but optional and his assignments are unfamiliar but build new skills.

Professor Wiseman has been my favorite professor so far. His intelligence and experience completely rub off and make lectures genuinely enjoyable and incredibly informative. A tad finicky with grading but he is more than willing to explain potential improvement. Amazing policy analyst, professor, and person. Great sense of humor too.

Professor Wiseman is an amazing professor. He is extremely helpful in office hours, an excellent lecturer, and very smart. That being said (as he always says), PSCI 2259 is incredible hard and not for the faint of heart. Don't take it unless you love game theory. Tests are difficult and if you don't go to class, you will be completely lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Wiseman is an excellent lecturer who really knows his stuff. Outside of class and with feedback, though, he's less helpful. Nitpicks with grading. Barely any nightly homework, but problem sets were MONSTROUS. I hear from other people who have taken his other classes that he's easier. Game Theory is just different. Way more math than politics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Wiseman is one of my favorite professors at the school. He challenges his students, but I have never learned more than I did in his class, not to mention it is relevant and interesting material. I appreciate that he has high expectations for us, but that he also does whatever he can to help us achieve them. Also HILARIOUS sense of humor. fantastic.
Extremely well versed in game theory. Explains difficult concepts clearly, though tends to speak in complicated verbiage.

Absolutely terrible. He only talks in buss words so it's impossible to understand what he is saying. Has very easy problems in class and then puts very challenging ones on the midterms (which are way too long) and problem sets. Questions are useless since he is extremely condescending and doesn't actually answer the question in normal english.

Great prof. Knows his stuff and is really helpful and available to students. Not many assignments, but need to put in a lot of work on them. Crystal clear grading criteria. Class participation and preparation are really important. Witty and picks interesting discussion topics, so class is always interesting. Transformed how I think about policy.
Great professor. A paper, a big presentation, midterm, and final. Made me love policy,

I would definitely recommend Prof. Wiseman - his grading can be a little tough, but the course material is incredibly interesting and the class was very enjoyable.  I also learned more than I do from the average class and there wasn't a whole lot of day-to-day work.

Professor Wiseman is a nice guy and I learned more in this class than a lot of other classes. While the grading isn't easy by any means, it is reasonable and there isn't a ton of work. Prof. Wiseman can be sarcastic, but if you're not super sensitive then you'll be fine. Would recommend!
intimidating at first but really nice guy and helpful outside of class. dont need to read the book if you go to class

STAY AWAY!! this man is awful and will kill your gpa. he expects you to have a graduate level understanding of economics for an undergraduate political science course. Don't take any of his classes. it will kill your gpa. he's also really mean and thinks he's the man which gets annoying.

this class was exactly what i wanted as a second semester senior. it let me practice what i wanted for my future in software engineering and let me choose what i wanted to do.

there really is no class, barely any work, no tests, and Jules grades very generously. as long as you make reasonable progress on your project, it is an easy A.

You definitely have to work independently in this class, much more so than other classes -- but the material was interesting enough, and I definitely learned something! Class could've used more structure, but it was the first time it was offered, so hopefully it'll get better.

Professor White is an outstanding teacher with a clear passion for the subject matter. His teaching style clearly conveys his interest in both the material and the outcome of his students. He's always available for office hours and will go out of his way to help with difficult concepts. Excellent teacher.

Loved this class! Dr. White is a cool prof and the class was a fun and easy A. Reading quizzes, participation, midterm and final, one paper; if you show up and do the reading, it's pretty easy. Her writing criteria were decently clear and she told us most of what could be on the exams ahead of time. I would totally take one of her classes again!

One of my favorite professors. Dr. White is a phenomenal teacher, very clear in her "lectures" and expectations, and she really cares about her students! I enjoyed every class, and this is coming from someone who took the course on a whim to satisfy AXLE. Never knew I'd end up enjoying it as much as I did, and it's all thanks to her.

Dr. White is really sweet and a good teacher. There's weekly reading quizzes, so make sure you actually do the reading. The lectures are interesting and she encourages class participation and discussion. There's 3 exams and 1 term paper besides the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is very energetic, a decent to good lecturer, and makes class and the subject exciting. Tough to contact outside of class.

Dan is a great guy and fun to have in class. Gets passionate and nerds out about AV stuff; makes class much more engaging even when it's all theory. Rocking with him very much and would take for another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Work is easily the best professor I've had at Vanderbilt. He's funny, engaging, and it's clear he really cares about his job and his students. The class is super interesting, and overall not too hard either. Highly recommend Prof. Work.

Work was my favorite professor ever! This was my favorite engineering class I've ever taken. Work is so cool and really involved in the field. He had so much real world experience and told great stories. I would retake this class a million times if I could. The class was not a ton of work but still so interesting and informative.
Talk too fastm
Dan Work is an all around awesome guy. Super nice and super passionate about transportation. He knows a ton and can talk for hours- class was also a pretty easy .

Prof. is an amazing guy and knows a lot about british lit. Fun class overall and readings were generally interesting. 7 reading quizzes (drop one), a paper, a final and a final project. He is nitpicky and a little harsh about grading the essay so make sure to edit closely. Gave us the option of writing 3 papers and he takes the highest grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You know that initial sense of wonder when you hit a great book? Prof. Wollaeger can sustain and enhance it, without sacrificing intellectual rigor. (Analytical interpretation has never been the same.) He'll also direct you to new books which become your favorites of all time. Definitely a homie!
