Wolly's writing seminar was a great way to start freshman year! He's a caring and helpful professor who will take time to answer your questions. He gives extensive feedback on most essays which is helpful for improving your future writing assignments. He tried to pick readings that we would all find valuable and interesting. A funny guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Wollaeger is a great professor and I would undoubtedly take his class again.

Mark Wollaeger is a great lecturer. Hes one of the more traditional professors in the department in some aspects, but hes still quite liberal and even a little hipster with regard to playing newer games. He isnt as much of a carebear as some, but hes very academic, often hilarious, and a little more authentic than most.

Mark is so amazing because he is caring and intelligent. He is very understanding, but it is sad to see that some students abuse his flexibility. However, if you go to class, his office hours, and show genuine interest in improvement, a good grade is absolutely possible. Also, do read all the books because they are not only required but fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: MW is the absolute homie! This guy so clearly cares about his students and their ultimate development as writers. He gives a few creative assignments that can really help your grade. Always accessible in office hours, before/after class, over email, and around campus. Do the reasonable readings, show up to class, participate, and you're good!

Prof Wollaeger is a super fun guy! I can't emphasize how much you won't regret taking this particular class. The topics are really thought-provoking. Make sure you buy the books ahead of time, and talk to him if you have questions (he's very nice)! Don't be intimidated by the syllabus, the workload is very manageable. Once more, amazing class!

Dr. Wollaeger is truly devoted to inspiring creative thought in his students, and it is clear that he works hard to plan texts and discussions that will benefit students. There is a significant amount of writing, but he generally gives you freedom to cater assignments towards personal interests and thought. Definitely cares about student success.

Wollaeger is a great professor! Though this is an intro class, the class was made up of a few freshmen, a few sophomores, some juniors, and a senior. Still, Wollaeger made sure everyone understood the concepts being covered, regardless of previous exposure to English, and asking questions was perfectly fine.

Professor Wollaeger seemed to have structured the class in a very thoughtful way that I think contributed well to learning the concepts we discussed throughout the semester. Everything felt very related and past discussions and readings would come up throughout the course, even months later which I really like and I think helped me takeaway more.

This is by far my favorite class I have taken at Vanderbilt both because of the material I have learned and the environment created by our wonderful professor. He encouraged us to share our thoughts and ideas while also guiding us to make connections and providing his expertise. I left every class so happy and sure of myself as a student.

Foundations was an incredible course. I had Prof. W in a course previously, and it was one of the main reasons I chose to pursue an English major. The interconnected nature of the themes presented to us, the question process, and ability to form our own conclusions rather be told a 'right ' or 'wrong' meaning was indispensable. I loved this class.

It is hard to imagine a course with a better match of syllabus and professor. The structure and progression of thecourse was cohesive and logical in a way none of my other classes were, and Professor Wollaeger did a fantastic job of getting the most out of the material in the course.

Required class for major, but the discussions we had in class were wonderful, both for understanding the material and understanding the world around us. Discussions about a chapter we'd read would turn existential, or enlighten me to a new idea or aspect of being a citizen and a human. It was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Our lectures were actually very instructive and often helped unpack what initially would seem dry or opaque. Dr. Wollaeger was brilliant at conducting class conversations and following the trail of students' thoughts to a satisfying conclusion for the day. Also, Wollaeger's unending enthusiasm contributed to my learning
I have always had a passion for the subject matter but Professor Wollaeger brought it to new levels. A really enjoyable class overall, makes me want to continue to pursue an English major!
the level of teaching ability witnessed here was world-class. Don't let this guy retire.
I really enjoyed the creative aspect of the class. Instead of just doing analytical work, Professor Wollaeger also encouraged us to do creative assignments. Professor Wollaeger was amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wollaeger selected great works for us to read. I think the reflection papers are effective and productive. This capstone as a mandatory part of the English major is great because I feel like I have been challenged in so many different ways. This is one of my favorite English classes and I would strongly recommend Wollaeger.
Great course. By far the best last lecture I've ever had the privilege of witnessing. Wollaeger loves what he does, and it shows. Highest praises!
Best professor I have had at Vanderbilt!! He is personal, hilarious, and keeps your attention in every lecture/discussion.  I highly recommend!

Professor Wollaeger is very engaging and makes the classes interesting, but his grading criteria is extremely subjective. No one could meet his standards. While I enjoyed the class, it was much too difficult for a survey course.

I learned so much from Prof. Wollaeger. He is funny and engaging and created a community where the open forum facilitated passionate discussion and provoked more critical thinking. The only thing I wish I had was more clarity in regards to assignments and grading criteria. The final knocked down grade because I feel he wasn't clear enough.

Such a great prof!  If you get the chance to take him, do it! I absolutely hated the thought of taking British War Writing, but he made it fun and interesting.  Fairly easy grader, not unreasonable. Easy to talk to and really wants to help you out.

amazing lecturer, makes class interesting and fun. very interested in his students and in improving their writing. high expectations, but not unreasonable. very approachable and helpful. extremely smart. any chance you have to take a course with him, TAKE IT.

LOVED this class!!! He's really into the subject and so smart!  My writing improved greatly, partly because of the writing conferences he schedules with you.  He works with you no matter what your writing level to improve your skills.  HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

He was the only english professor I have ever had that actually took the time to read and proof my papers and really work with me to improve my writing, not just for a better grade, but for personal improvement. He was a great teacher and I recommend to take his class.
Fantastic. My favoriate professor. He really knows poetry and seems like he loves teaching. Tough comments on papers but grading not that hard.
Intelligent and insightful professor. Quizzes aren't a problem as long as you actually do the reading. I recommend this class highly.
You read a novel a week, but the books are great and class is always interesting. There's a quiz almost every week too, but if you read the books you'll be fine. Pretty tough grader on essays.
Took same class as unhappy miss. Classic headcase. He teased her in class for sleeping; she freaked. Good class, honrs, not as organized as might be. Smart guy.
Hey, he was a good guy.  Admittedly, he wasn't my favourite professor at first.  But I really appreciate having had him.  Good bloke.  Good novels.  Good times - especially his final lecture!
No Comments

One of my classmates _hated_ this class and Wollaeger but that's only because she didn't get the grades she wanted. (thought she might have already been here). Great class, though, really smart and funny professor.

Pretty frustrating because everyone just has a test bank and cheats on the exams. Haven't taken bio since freshman yr of hs and it ended up being more challenging than I thought it would be. Lab is basically a free A if you show up and always ends early.
Terrible. Claims they curve grade depending on various labs, but will not if you are on the cusp of a grade. He obviously does not care.

People get mad about this class but even without the test bank this class is manageable. Yes there is a lot of information but overall class is okay, assignments are easy, just focus on the exams. Prof is a nice and funny dude although the vibes are intimidating, but I would take this class again.

Dr Woelfle is a great professor, clear lecturer, and his class is very interesting. Attendance is recommended, and he provides study guides for exams. If you are a non-stem major looking to fulfill AXLE, I would recommend this class, especially if you have some prior biology knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NEVER TAKE THIS COURSE IF YOU CARE ABOUT YOUR GRADE. Cover tons of materials that are not covered in other sessions. You need to reach 93.5 to get an A. Tests take up 2/3 of your final grade, with an average of 75. No extra credits, no curve, no replacement. The professor is just reading the slides. JUST DON'T TAKE IT.

This class was NOT baby bio. There are three exams and all covered a ton of content. Class lecture is not mandatory but exams are harder if you dont go. The textbook is 100 dollars but you need it to complete homework assignments. The lectures are monotone and boring.
The tests are very difficult and relatively few questions. He seems harsh and doesn't tolerate nonsense.

Dr. Woelfle is an interesting personality. He comes across as quite stoic and even passive aggressive which can honestly be a stressful thing to experience although I don't think that he actually means. So if you keep this in mind you should be fine. It's worth it to be patient with him and try to understand his meaning.
Half of your grade in lab is based on 4 quizzes. It's not hard to do well but it's frustrating if you mess up a quiz. The professor also just yells at kids for the smallest things. Beware

Do not take this class unless you have access to a test bank for this class. It is hard to do well without it. The professor is incredibly dry and it is hard to stay focused. He also doesn't care about his students

Easy class because tests are same across semesters. Without that you're probably screwed. No point in attending lecture really because he posts all the slides online but easy A. Lab is super easy too. He's kind of a strange dude and a boring lecturer.

this man does not care if you pass this class or not. test questions are worth a lot, so if you don't understand bio (which most people who take this class do not), then you can basically kiss an A goodbye. the only people who genuinely do well in this class are the people who somehow got the answers before hand- really screws the rest of us over.

This man could care less about if you pass something that isn't even relevant to your major. I attend every lecture and try so hard, but to be honest, if you don't have access to a test bank, you are screwed. He doesn't want to be there, he doesn't care about you, and honestly seems like he hates everything in general. Take astrology. Save yourself

He gives no partial credit either you get the whole question right or none at all and he is so incredibly mean he is not receptive to questions and he could honestly care less about you doing well in the genetics course OR the lab. Cannot emphasize enough how much to stay away from this terrible TERRIBLE person. Take genetics in the spring.

Woelfle is a genius, but his teaching style is unfavorable. The lectures were confusing, and he intimidated students who approached him (whenever I went to him, he would act like I was stupid for asking questions). The only reason I got the grade I did was because of the TA, which changes every class. 100% don't take unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would avoid at all costs. Does not award partial credit fairly - entire exam pages would be 0/15, taking off almost two letter grades, no matter how much work you put on the page demonstrating your knowledge. A curve at the end helps, but when multiple students are getting below a 30 on the final, you have to start asking yourself what's going on

Although Dr. Woelfle is quite knowledgeable, his exceptionally strict grading policies and cold demeanor make him unapproachable and virtually impossible to get an A for any of the courses he teaches, including BSCI 3860. Would highly recommend to not take any of his courses and to find alternate professors for courses like BSCI 2210 or BSCI 3860.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are pre-med, do not take this class unless you are a senior and have already submitted your apps. There is really no way to prepare for the exams. The questions are so far out of left field that even if you spent every minute of every day studying, you still won't know how to begin them. This class was so unenjoyable

Avoid at all costs!! Dr. Woelfle does not teach. He is an extremely accomplished and intelligent individual, however he does not translate this knowledge to students. It's possible to do better but as a whole my class did very poorly, especially on the final. I am a straight A student, so take that as you will.

The professor is ok but the lectures are boring in general. Posts slides online but they don't cover all the exam materials, so reviewing based on the slides is not quite a good idea. The class might not be friendly to students without previous backgrounds in bio, so it's not exactly "baby". Recommend astrology over this class as an AXLE req.

The material itself isn't that difficult, but there is way too much information to memorize.  Tests are average but make up an overwhelming majority of the grade.  If you have good experience with bio, the class should be fine.  However, the last time I took bio was my freshman year of high school, so I thought the class was a little difficult.

This class is ridiculous. All of the people in greek life have the answer keys in their test banks and it makes it unfair for everyone else because the class is curved to a B- average (which makes this class a GPA killer for most). Lectures are boring and labs are painfully long. Overall, there are much better AXLE lab science options.

Don't bother reading the textbook unless the lecture material is unclear, but the suggested problems are helpful for understanding the material - but are not at all like the test questions. The problem sets and old sample tests are best for test prep. Very hard, but doable if you put in a lot of studying hours.

This class was way harder than biochemistry. Tests were very difficult and I wouldn't have passed if not for the curve. Woelfle is cool, if not intimidating, but the tests are pretty ridiculous even if you spend a lot of time working on practice problems, going to office hours, and reading the textbook. My grade did not reflect my effort at all.
Class is cake, lab is hard. Not because the labs are hard in themselves, but because the lab quizzes are worth 50% of the grade, and there is only 4 of them.
Pretty clear that woelfle doesn't care that much about this class, which isn't really an issue since it's not that difficult. Just read the slides, you don't need to go to class

I went to every lecture, did the textbook practice problems, and still barely passed. Tests are fairly difficult, and his grading is extremely inconsistent and borderline unfair. He takes off all points on wrong answers despite saying he'll give partial credit -- spoiler, he won't. Avoid if you want to keep a decent GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would argue that this class is almost as difficult as biochemistry (which is canonically considered the most challenging one in the BSCI dept). Lecture material is more important than the textbook. Professor is intimidating but funny (sometimes). He is incredibly awkward, but will always answer your questions if you ask them. Use office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Woelfe is a great lecturer, utilizing several pedagogical techniques in his classroom. That being said, his tests are REALLY HARD. Genetics is one of the hardest classes I have taken at Vanderbilt. You HAVE to go to class, do the readings, go to office hours and do recc. problems, and even then you might not pass. Good Luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a horrible teacher. Extremely rude, does not care about his students, and is prideful. I'd stay away from him as much as possible. One of the worst professors I've had in my entire time here at Vanderbilt.

Pretty easy class since everything was online, but I have a lot of problems with Woelfle himself. His lectures are absolutely riddled with incorrect information and inconsistencies--the same goes for his answers to lab work. The lectures aren't worth watching and you get more just out of reading the textbook.
Very passive-aggressive when you ask questions and he is not interested in student's learning.

Genetics is hard but Woelfle is solid. Friedman is certainly more energetic and maybe less intimidating but Woelfle has a sarcastic personality and means well, don't mistake humor for intimidation. Tests are pretty difficult. Textbook reading isn't necessarily required but the textbook problems are essential for learning the material. Graded HW.

Hardest class I've taken (for reference, I did better in orgo, gen chem, & bio). Many people cheat on the take-home tests & use test banks (ruining the curve), so if you have academic integrity, it'll be an uphill battle. Prof isn't good at answering Qs, but he is accessible. My advice: read, go to lecture, memorize practice tests, & do hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mediocre at best. He puts little to no effort into teaching and is rude whenever someone asks for clarification. The class isn't too difficult, so don't bother coming to class. Simply read the annotated slides he posts on Brightspace and you should receive an A...A- at the lowest. Best class to take if you're doing it for AXLE.

The class is pretty easy (not SUPER easy but easy). The prof absolutely does not care whatsoever. Did not even visibly attempt to make online lectures of any form making it a glorified textbook reading. Lab is annoying because of stupid quizzes that are worth half of your grade.

Woelfle is one of my favorite professors I have had at Vandy. Failed the first test, went to class 1/3 of the time, and didn't do the best on some pop quizzes and still came out with a B. He's so funny and makes 9 AM lectures not bad at all. Understands majority non-science people are taking this class and has clear expectations for grades
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dont like this course. I knew little about biology before and this course is a huge challenge to me. There are too much stuff to memorize. This is the only course I receive a B EVER. The professor has no passion towards his teaching. I didnt receive my test paper from him and asked him about this. He just told me I dont know. Not friendly at all!

I loved Woelfle's genetics class, but it's definitely tough. He's a great teacher and is very willing to help, but you have to come to lectures since he focuses on very specific things from the book. This has been the hardest class I've taken at Vanderbilt, but it's very worth it if you like the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Genetics with Dr. Woelfle was one of the best experiences I have had as an undergrad at Vandy. He was always available to help, and if you can see through the deadpan and sometimes sarcasm he is one of the best at teaching and communicating the material.

Bio with Prof. Woelfle has its pros and cons.  He's got a big personality and seems unapproachable but is friendly when you reach out to him.  A warning: tests can be more difficult than you expect, even if you study a good amount.  Overall, the class is more difficult than some other "easy" sciences but still not very difficult.

Take this class for AXLE credit. Easy class, even if your bio knowledge is rusty. No need to attend lectures, except for 5 unannounced quizzes. Tests are mostly multiple choice. Only thing I didn't like was the cumulative final. The final grade was generously curved. Lab is also quite easy.
Easy class, very enjoyable, study for the tests, class not mandatory (posts all lecture notes)

Genetics is really tough. Dr. Woelfle explains everything well, but he can come across as unapproachable and grouchy. Ignore this and ASK FOR HELP if you need it. Go to TA help sessions and do as many practice problems/previous exams as you can in preparation for tests. He often uses super similar questions. Grading can be brutal.

Genetics is hard. There is no way around that. It is a new way of thinking and you probably won't do well, at least on the first test. Good news is, there is a curve at the end. And Dr. Woelfle is hilarious. I understand he comes off condescending. He's not. It's an 8AM class and he hates mornings. If you go to him for help, he will help you!

I did ok in intro to bio, so i thought i would be fine in genetics. Boy was i wrong. A very difficult class, very difficult tests and assignments. Don't take it unless you absolutely have to. I usually finish tests first in the class, but for his tests i just did not have enough time to finish every time (so did most of the class).

I love Dr. Woelfle! He's sarcastic and has dry humor so I thought he was absolutely hilarious. I always went in for help and he always was willing to helpvery helpful. Ppl saying he's condescending, he's joking and I think its pretty obvious he is! The subject of genetics is hard though. He's a great teacher but genetics is hard as hell.

Woelfle is condescending and makes you feel stupid when you ask questions. He's bitingly sarcastic for no good reason, and he just feels completely unapproachable. His tests are 5 long answers that each take 20 minutes to do, but you only get 50 minutes to take them. However, he puts his powerpoints online and is pretty clear in lecture.
Dr. Woelfle was scary and condescending when I asked questions.
He was not helpful and in many instances non-responsive. He is also arrogant and pompous. Makes the course even more difficult.  STAY AWAY!!!!!!
He knows that you aren't taking this class because you like bio. He tries. Tests seem to have gotten harder this year.

Very easy lab science. Online homework about every other week. 5 question quizzes are hinted at but technically pop, so sometimes looking over the chapter or posted powerpoints is helpful, but they're easy. 3 tests, all based off of the powerpoints. Lab that accompanies the class is also very basic and usually only lasts 1.5 hours.

I love Dr. Woelfle! He is very clear in explaining concepts in class, helpful outside of class, and really sarcastically funny. Everyone seems to think his class is super hard, but if you just keep up with the readings and practice problems, you'll be fine. Genetics lab with him is also very informative, not too time consuming, and fun!

He is very clear and extremely helpful outside of class. Attend his review sessions because he often covers problems similar to those on the test. Also, the final is just repeats of the problems from the tests during the year. That being said, this class is the hardest I've had at Vanderbilt. But if you do practice problems, you will get an A.

Woelfle is a great professor! He's extremely clear and always willing to help. He even puts his notes and past tests online. You don't really need the textbook except for practice problems. Tests are extremely difficult. The questions are clear but require A LOT of thought.

This class was super difficult, but Woelfle did a good job with clear ppts.  He would go out of his way to explain and go through problems outside of class.  I would recommend the class with him, but expect to put in tons of work. I learned a lot and it was frustratingly hard, but worth it in the end. Oh and get used to his sense of humor

Everyone warned me about Woelfle, but he's not bad at all. He's very clear, incredibly organized with his lecture slides, helpfully posts everything online, and is generous with regrades. You just need to be willing to work for your grade.
Don't have to go to class, test average around B+/A- range, slideshows and practice tests are posted online. Definitely take for MNS requirement or lab requirement

Professor Woefle realizes that most of the people in the class are non-majors just taking this class for an AXLE credit and teaches accordingly.  You don't have to go to class, as he posts annotated lecture slides online.  His tests are straight forward and he posts helpful practice tests on OAK.

I am so glad I took this class.  I had a hard time paying attention because he was so precious. The material was good and he is very helpful.  His test could be tricky but if you attend class take notes and review you will do just fine.  Speaking of fine did I mention how precious he is.
This professor may be old, but he is mighty fine.  But overall he is a good teacher, but his sarcasm is a pain in the rear, but u need to take this class

Definitely take this class to fulfill AXLE or to get an easy A. This class was probably easier than my high school biology class. He is very clear on what he expects. He also provides accurate practice tests, so there are no surprises. Don't waste money on the book. Going to class is enough.

Perfect class to fulfill AXLE. Lectures exactly what is in the book, so if you completely understand the book, class isn't really necessary. No trick questions on tests. Take advantage of review sessions to clarify any questions you have. 4 writing assignments are pretty subjective in grading. Exceed word limit, only docked for not writing enough.

VERY easy class, very approachable guy. the lectures are posted online which makes it easy to see whats expected of you, and what information will be on the test. Other than that, he has quick assignments mostly in the form of summary.
I took it just for AXLE, and it was fine. Not difficult material, easy tests, posts everything online.

His grading is SUPER stringent. I'm in his lab also and he grades the report like a paper published on Science. Tests are also difficult becuase you have to be really really comprehensive. Recommended for the scientists out there only.
SO so so hard tests. Problem sets are easy and material seeems easy, but then the tests seem okay but the grading is so hard! this will definitely ruin my gpa, science gpa, pre med chances, etc...
Difficult class! the professor is cool, but that doesnt change the fact that this is a hard class. I tried it just to fulfill AXLE and hurt my GPA. advice: take it in the fall with  Ava d. Due

My adviser said this was a good class. I think what he meant was it was unbelievably difficult, but kind of fun. Woelfe does a reasonable job at presenting the material, but it's usually so complicated you'll find yourself reading things over and over and still not grasping the entire concept. I found it very intellectually stimulating.

Hard class but excellent professor! He's funny, keeps it interesting most of the time and is great in lab.  Very dry sense of humor.  SO helpful outside of class...he would stay an hour after lab to help me understand the upcoming test material. Tests are difficult...really have to know everything forwards and backwards.

Man, this class is HARD. I am a Molecular Bio major and I've made all A's in my Bio classes prior to now, but I had to scrape my butt off just for an A-. Don't take this class unless you REALLY understand Biology. His tests are very well written, but require A LOT of thinking and putting together fragmented pieces of information. Good luck.
class is really tough, he goes over most material but not all for exams. You have to do more work outside of class.

I went into this class as a non-major. It's a pretty easy class as long as you attend lecture and/or read. Woefle is a cool guy, but he occasionally got on my nerves when I felt like he was teaching down to the class.

friendly guy...great for your grades too.  genetics lab with woelfe was the most relaxed lab i've ever had.  class is pretty easy too, he doesn't go over stuff too fast and a lot of it's review from bsci 110b.

I hate biology. But did well in this class. Attendance is NOT required (except on quiz days) and he puts all his powerpoints on Blackboard...as long as you keep up with the notes (by either going to class or on bb) then you should do fine...and lab is important that 25% can really help your grade.
Cool dude
He's pretty cool and doesn't mind assisting you. The course material is harder than you would expect though.
If you actually go to class (most people don't) you'll be way ahead of the curve and do well in this ridiculously easy class.  Great way to fulfill CPLE requirements.

Woelfe is great.  He makes class easy for those with little interest in science, his tests are fair and straight from the book, and he curves grades at the end of the semester.  The lab portion of the class was largely painless.  You'll have to study for the tests and work hard on the papers, but an A is definately within reach.
Good thing he's teaching my 9 am class, otherwise I probably wouldn't go!  He's very nice and helpful.  Cute too.
What a waste of good oxygen.  Totally moronic individual.  Stay clear.
Very easy for a non-science major.  Attendance is not necessary.  Just make sure you get the notes from someone and skim the textbook before the exam.  Tests are all scantron.  Lab was very easy.
Great class, except for the grading.
Genetics lab was practical and pretty cool. He is a good teacher. He's funny and not too hard. The presentations aren't such a bad thing because by the end, you'll be pretty prepared.
Woelfle is great! He's funny and really helpful. The class was pretty interesting and if you have to take a lab science I highly recommend one with him.

As a non-science major I found some of the test difficult, but Woefle realizes that most of his students are just in the class to fufill CPLE and he is really chill. He's a Cubs fan, but other than that rather cool and the labs are really easy.

As a non-science major taking this class to fulfill a requirement, I found it relatively difficult (admittedly because I did not keep up with the awful readings) and EXTREMELY BORING.  I once counted him saying "essentially" more than 50x in one
Straight forward class. Do reading and attend lectures. He made morning lab bearable.
the tests can suck if you don't keep up with the notes and readings, but take the class just because he's funny.  also -- the labs are really easy.
The lectures are easy enough to follow, but look out for the tests, they can be a bit tricky, you'll need to study for them.
The class consisted of power point presentations and scantron exams.  Fairly straight-forward if you keep up with the reading.  He's a good guy with a Norm Mac Donald sense of humor.
This class is so easy, and Woefle is a really cool guy.

This class is called Science for athletes for a reason. It's not nearly as bad as other reviews, but it's heavily dependent on your student TA, who does the grading. If you follow the directions on the busywork (while it is sometimes unclear) you will do well. The group project is annoying but just get organized early.

This class is FULL of busywork. There were multiple assignments a week, barely any that actually mattered, and most grades you could tell were assigned based on the random whims of some student grader, never seen by the professors. You might as well take a real science and at least learn something instead of whatever this was.

Grading is really strict in this class and he takes off points unnecessarily on small assignments. 6-week long self-experiemt in a group is very annoying. You get 5 absences (good), but any more and you get 10 points off. Overall easy science elective (likely an A), but more difficult than you might think.

This class was fairly easy and mostly busy work, but grading was very strict. Small mistakes could lead to big point deductions, and I had to email the professors about grading errors. Overall, it's not too hard to get an A if you show up and do the work, especially with the amount of extra credit available.

I really hate to have to do this, but this has been one of the most unprofessionally-run courses I've ever taken. The criteria for assignments was constantly changing, and whoever grades assignments (AI??) is horrible at it. The lectures are a massive waste of time. Do not take. You will randomly get C's on your busy-work assignments. Junk.
DO NOT take this class. The instructions are completely unclear, and the grading is so inconsistent. DON'T TAKE IT.

Terrible. Instructions are unclear on every assignment and you will receive a 60% if your work isn't perfect, and then if you try to clarify or resubmit you'll be met with a passive-aggressive message about how that won't be allowed.He may or may not even grade papers, the comments seem to be AI or teacher aid and they always lead to a D grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Food Science: what a class. Little out of class work, but still felt like I was learning such meaningful stuff about food science and policy, and stuff I could apply in my life. We got to hear from a campus dining exec, and the perspectives of that were fascinating. An easy A, no doubt, but one that feels fun and meaningful. Snacks in class!
Very unclear grading criteria. Annoying amount of busywork. Lectures were middle- and high-school-level content.

The nature of this class is that it's supposed to be easier than other science college courses, and while there were some interesting and engaging lectures, a lot of the class depended on lectures you could find in a general high school science class with busy work & harsh/inaccessible/inconsistent grading criteria.

Doesn't care about this class and it shows. His grading criteria is ambiguous and unpredictable. Inaccessible outside of class and doesn't answer emails. I learned absolutely nothing, and completed assignments that were irrelevant to the "lessons" that were taught. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

I would sooner put a crowbar through my prefrontal cortex than take a class with this man. He will never respond outside of class, gives random attendance on Fridays despite it not being a factor in your grade on the syllabus, and enjoys randomly embarrassing students. So much busywork and so little learning, even for AXLE. avoid. or not who cares

Incredibly frustrating class for no reason at all. He changed his attendance policy without warning halfway through the semester when his ego was hurt. There are no rubrics or grading instructions, and your fate in this class seems VERY subjective and dependent on his explicit biases (he seems to have something against women).

I hate this man. SO rude, especially to girls. Literally 2 months to get grades back on assignments worth 30% of grade. He has some weird chip on his shoulder and wants to see his students fail. Also said he would fix grades and then never did. Biggest waste of time and could have found an easier axle with a much nicer prof.
Entertaining lecturer and a fun class!! Emphasizing talking about science in real life and had fun assignments.

Really annoying and nitpicky. Grades harshly on assignments and gives no grading criteria. Topics are useless, and he makes cold calls in class. It is not an impossible class, but it a huge inconvenience. He randomly takes attendance in class when his ego gets hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was easy but grading is up to their judgement and lectures get weird when he just stares at you until you answer.

This class is super easy and made up of only a few assignments and NO TESTS. However, both Prof Wright and Prof Durst teach the class and they both just make everyone so incredibly uncomfortable. They will cold call you and stare at any female untill they answer. They are both really creepy and especially to women.

Honestly he makes me so uncomfortable. He is misogynistic and only cold calls on girls or the baseball team. I have learned nothing, and his assignments are useless busywork. This class was an easy A, but I would never take a class with Professor Wright again.

Very unclear grading criteria/instructions. Shows no kindness or empathy towards his students and does not care about them at all. There was no attendance policy, but he got his ego hurt that not many people showed up to class one day and decided to doc 20% off of everyone's grade who was not in class on that ONE day. 10/10 do NOT recommend!
Take this class if you would like to have concepts you learned in second grade mansplained to you for 50 minutes three times a week.

Do not take this class if you are a woman! Wright is extremely misogynistic and allows this bias to affect how he treats his class. He only "cold calls" on girls and has mentioned multiple times that women are "less" than men in various aspects. His grading/instructions are also extremely unclear and his ego is VERY high. Good luck!

Dr. Wright was very funny and carried the discussions. Although this class didn't have any real assignments and you could've skipped every class and pretended this wasn't on your schedule and still get credit for it. I guess my review is biased. But it was a very fun iSeminar.
Class was graded on 4 projects that we did throughout the semester, along with a weekly assignment that took around 20 minutes to complete. Would take again

Easiest class of all time. Don't need to go to class. Just follow directions on mini assignments, which take no more than 10 minutes to do. He does say some stuff on the assignments only to those who go to class, so try to have someone you know tell you about the specifics of what he wants.
Quite simply an incredible human being.
Literally the easiest class ever. Just follow the instructions and u will get an A. Never went to class this semester and ended with an A.

take this class. super chill. He has a couple of assignments that requires you to come to class but otherwise attendance is not mandatory. He's funny and a good lecturer if you do decide to come to class. You get graded on a couple of mini assignments and a couple other projects. No tests

Do not take CSET with this professor. He tanked my GPA by grading something incorrectly last semester and he has failed to respond to my repeated emails asking him to fix it, which he still has not done even though he said he would.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super chill class, no readings, one short hw assignment each week, no mandatory attendance, and lenient grader. Funny guy. I went to class and took no notes (there are no tests, just open-ended writing assignments) and that worked great. Would def recommend, but he said he's restructuring the class and adding more hw for when he teaches it again.

This was his first time teaching this class so things might change! No readings ever, hardly any assignments, slightly unstructured. Large lecture class where he reviews the basics of science (think creation to climate change). 2-5 sentence review every week, fact-checking assignments every other, two group projects. He was very kind and available.

There are only 5 grades in this class which are 3 tests and 2 projects. He wants to give everyone an A if they at least turn something in. He was an interesting and funny professor and the class was very laid back. He explained concepts well, while also having fun! He doesn't respond to emails that well, and he cancels class quite often though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This guy is fairly entertaining, but he's a horrible teacher. The slides he posts make zero sense, even after he explains them, and it is difficult to tell what is and is not required for the test. Also, he failed to return a single assignment before the drop period, and then joked about it. Avoid at all costs.
He was by far the worst professor I had at Vanderbilt. He spent way too much time trying to act cool and was horrible at explaining concepts.
He has his days

no textbook so write everything down. 3 tests (including the final) all equally weighted. everything on the tests is from lectures so DON'T SKIP (esp after the first test)!! he's a nice, funny guy and makes class interesting. the grad students are graded differently. take home part of tests def. help bring your test grade up (spend time on them!)

THIS IS THE WORSE PROFESSOR EVER! He rarely writes anything on the board and expects you to know how to do everything. He thinks it is hilarious that no one ever comes to his class, but doesn't realize it is because he is AWFUL. His test averages are ALWAYS lower than every other classes. I had to basically teach myself chem. SWITCH OUT

Professor Wright is funny, and nice outside of class... but is a terrible professor. Out of the four General Chem sections, ours had the lowest average on every test, and overall. I always had to borrow notes from another section, and they were much better than anything Wright did. If you get him, don't bother going to class, just teach yourself.

Wright was at best confusing.  I had no idea what he was talking about most of the time and I always went to class.  Does not inform students about OWL or help session.  Be prepared to teach yourself.  Says ok all the time.

Don't expect to learn much if you go to class, he is usually not very prepared and tends to get things wrong in examples. He doesnt respond to emails unless you write him 5 or 6 times and doesnt seem to care if his students are learning anything in his class or not. He wont tell you about OWL homework, or anything else like help sessions.

Wright could not care less about his students or how much they learn in his class.  After not responding to my emails I asked him if he had been getting them; his response was "Uhh send me 6 or 7 more, maybe I'll pick one and respond."  After taking his class I can re-tell 10-12 different stories about his ****en fun at Tulane, that's about it.
One of the best and funniest science teachers I've ever had.  Hands down.

wright is arguably one of the worst teachers at the school.  He seems like he would be fun to talk to outside of class, but he expresses no interest in what his students learn.  Please do not take Wright unless you plan on skipping class every day.
No Comments
No Comments
Very unorganized. Does not prepare students for tests. Going to class is entertaining, but a waste of time.

Stories are entertaining, but not helpful outside of class whatsoever. Does not respond to emails and really does not care about the individual student.  Desperately tries to reclaim his youth by frequently going off topic and talking about ****en stories at tulane.

Very easy class, material can easily be mastered without going to class and just doing OWL and suggested problems. Professor is extremely animated and interested in getting students to learn. Very helpful if you do attend class though.
awesome teacher, so funny and made class bearable but at the same time didn't really cover any of the material on the tests. it wasn't necessary to go to class at all but it was entertaining at least
Excellent professor. Knows what he is talking about. Makes a lecture exciting. If you want to learn take him.

If chemistry isn't your strong point, Wright is defn NOT for you...switch into List's class! Wright speeds thru ALL the material at breakneck pace & skips a lot of material. He also goes ahead to other chapters that aren't even on the test. He's funny, but that's not going to help your GPA out any.
Goes off on too many tangents.  He doesn't quite cover the test material as clear as the other professors.
Did not like him as a professor-- he's a funny guy, but not very organized or clear.  His has some funny stories, though...
Good prof, he makes chemistry interesting.  He is very clear and answers any questions you might have, highly recommended.

I had to drop in to this guy's lecture one day...it was AMAZING. he has such a love for the subject and explains it in really down to earth terms. he's funny as anything too (he's a former frat at Tulane = LOTS of stories)
Tough class that takes lots of work, wright is an average teacher but going to class is not really necessary, just read the book and do homework
Entertaining in class (esp for 8am!), nice guy, helpful...not as clear as other teachers, esp when the material gets harder (but maybe nothing's clear at 8am?)
Well spoken and easy to understand.  Generous curve at end of year but class is still hard.  He is king of arrogant but he is better than the rest of the professors.
No Comments
Well spoken and intelligent.  He teaches material that is on the test, and is helpful outside of class.  However beware, he is a smart ass.
get to know him, it will help you!

You're graded pretty specifically and inconsistently. Some of the more conceptual questions on exams are worded confusingly which was frustrating. I didn't find the exams very hard (but I've been through quite a few math classes :p). I didn't really like that my friends with other professors seemed to have much lighter expectations

If you are generally poor at math, I would not recommend this class. Lectures were hard to follow and I ended up teaching myself with an optional textbook that I only found helpful on occasion. Studying for exams was difficult because the questions were much more conceptual and abstract than the calculation-heavy homework.

This professor made stats unbearable. Lectures are complete gibberish, impossible to follow, and teach nothing. Grading takes forever. Exams are horribly worded and confusing. He's the only stats prof with a final, which is insane. You would think intro to stats would be easy, he made it a living nightmare. I relied on the TA to teach me. Drop it.

He's alright, definitely not the best lecturer and very nit picky with grading. Taught myself but just basic statistics at the end of the day. Better professor options but only option to fit in my schedule so didn't have much of a choice

Hao Wu is such a bad teacher. He doesnt explain anything and will give you an awful grade even if you get the problems correct. This is supposed to be an easier class at vanderbilt but he grades this class like it is the hardest class at vanderbilt. if you want to take a hit to your gpa for no reason take him.

The class is really great for those that want to learn about multivariate stats. Hao really cares about students and will sit down with you to answer questions/is very accessible. His approach is more math-heavy, but it's a great complement to other courses that are more applied. You gain an in-depth understanding and he really wants you to learn!

Dr. Wu's Multivariate stats class shouldn't be taken if you don't have an understanding of linear algebra first. His class is derivation heavy, and there is a lot of hand calculation involved. Weekly quizzes and homework assignments were helpful in figuring out what you actually needed to know for the exams, but they were very time consuming.

Hao is the best statistics professor I've had. He explains concepts with insightful interpretations that help me think more deeply about math and stats. His notes are clear and highlight key ideas. He sets clear expectations, offers helpful exam guidance. He takes time to answer questions, which gives me deeper insights. He cares students a lot.

The first part of the course was not bad but the final was horrendous. I studied 50+ hours and still did terrible. Hardest exam I have taken at Vandy. My grade dropped from an A to a B+. If you have to take this class, try to max points on HW, quizzes, attendance and midterms(which are graded fairly)in order to create a cushion for the final.

Overall, Dr. Wu was a decent professor. He/TAs were always accessible outside of class numerous times a week, and going with questions is vital. The topics build on one another, so once you get confused you will begin to do poorly on the following topics. He puts a high emphasis on understanding conceptual ideas, which makes the tests challenging.

Learned a lot, but a tough class. He tries really hard to incorporate student feedback which is appreciated. Has recorded video lectures which are extreme useful. 3 exams total which are manageable, but lectures themselves are very dull.

I like that he's trying his best to make changes based on student feedback. I'm sure this course can only get better (previous years seemed much worse). He's a nice guy that goes over content in great detail even though slightly too talkative. Final exam was insane, prob to lower the class grades but I def went from an A to a B just from this exam.

I was going to give 5 stars because he was a very nice and humorous with straightforward, reasonable exams. However, after seeing other's thoughts on today's final, I think it is strange that he would take an experimental approach to the heaviest-weighted part of our grade. I felt very betrayed and my day was unfortunately ruined. He's cool though.

Wu's teaching style is incredibly unclear, and his lectures contain confusing information. That being said, the first two exams were reasonable and very similar to previous homework and participation quizzes. I would rate him higher if it weren't for the final, which contained unfamiliar content that seemed out of left field.

I was going to give this class a more positive rating until the final exam. While Wu tends to overcomplicate the material the homework, discussions problems, quizzes and first too exams weren't too difficult if you studied. HOWEVER, the final exam had content that was never covered, it seemed as though he was trying to lower the average grade.
This was probably the worst class I have taken at Vanderbilt. He was incredibly unclear while teaching and overcomplicated everything. Take the class if you need to but have a different section
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's kinda cute ngl..

Pretty cool guy he has occasional humor out of nowhere while staying 100% serious and it makes everyone laugh and then after everyone laughs he stares at us like he doesn't know he said something funny and then continues teaching.
Try not to fall asleep challenge

Hao deeply cares about learning for the sake of learning. Flipped classroom style, which some love and others don't. Lots of partial & extra credit, half the class gets an A/A- which is 89%+. Heavy emphasis on theoretical points, you'll learn a lot from discussion keys and doing the HW. Participation points are easy, don't need many to get a 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu was a very caring and knowledgeable professor who cares a lot about student feedback. He has made good changes to his class. He is very hard working and has spent a lot of time working on his notes and videos to make sure they are of high quality. His class also focuses more on conceptual material. I highly recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Weekly homework and quizzes that aren't too bad if you use the key he posts online to guide you. Class is boring and you are expected to come in already knowing the content (he posts videos online) and be able to do the homework. Exams aren't too bad if you study and know the content. Not a terrible class, but would not recommend.

Dr. Wu has given the most in-depth feedback from any professor I've had freshman year. He seriously puts effort into making changes based on student opinion and makes you feel like he really cares. The videos and notes he provides are high quality and a good study resource, very organized and structured.

Overall, Professor Wu is very kind and helpful. He was always happy to meet with me to answer my questions. There were two exams and a cumulative final. The exams were long with some difficult questions. However, I felt well-prepared for the exams. Participation, 10 homeworks, and 10 quizzes also contributed to the final course grade.

Makes the class way harder than it needs to be; nit-picky grader; expects students to understand everything at a deep level; 3 tests (cumulative final); 10 HW assignments; 10 take home quizzes; have to put in a lot of effort to do well; helpful in office hours; he wants students to do well but also has too high of expectations of non-STEM students

Flipped classroom videos that are very hard to understand. TA graded everything and would take off points for things prof said was fine. Prof wouldnt check until it was brought up by student in office hours. Awful class overall, very confusing and would not recommend. Able to pass but have to put a lot of work in for something that should be easy

I guess class is easy since it's Peabody. However, assignments almost every day, he doesn't teach very clearly and complicates concepts further than he needs to. If you take this class, I would recommend watching Youtube videos. Exams are hard, but probably easier than A&S. Might not be the best stats professor but is not horrible.

Professor Wu seems like a decent enough guy, and to his credit, he does try to help his students. However, in every other area, he falls abysmally short of what is expected. Woefully disorganized, baffling exam grading criteria, and lectures with all the value and vivacity of a mildly interesting piece of driftwood. Overall, pretty meh.

The class itself is not super work heavy. The homework is based on the discussions. The discussion (class) is so boring and very unproductive. He is a harsh, VERY SPECIFIC grader on exams. They are unnecesarily hard. Oh and he will curve DOWN so that only 30% of class gets an A. AVOID HIM IF POSSIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most boring lecturers I've ever had. Makes an intro stats class unnecessarily hard, grades for things that are minuscule and unclear. No flexibility whatsoever on homework/at home quizzes. Can be rude to students.
Professor Wu seems to care about his students, but his class is incredibly boring and Ive learned almost nothing.

Bro this class was not good. Wu Hao is a pretty good teacher who cares about what he teaches but he's really challenging for literally an intro stats class. The classes are really boring, the exams are pretty hard, and overall it's just an unnecessarily hard class for intro stats. He's very logistics-oriented too. Idk man not my favorite

I've taken 4 Peabody stat classes with 4 different professors and Hao Wu is by far THE WORST. His homework uses a software not available to students and that most professors don't use so you have to go to a special computer lab to do work. Also the most boring lecturer. You will fall asleep. Avoid at all costs.

Very accessible outside of class; quizzes, homework, and review sessions are very helpful for midterms; truly cares about his students; knows what he's talking about and gives clear explanations; emphasizes on concepts rather than pure calculations

Hes straightforward in his lecturing, and gives a few homework assignments and quizzes. Other than that, there are two midterms and a final... he is very kind and wants the best for his students, so if you give your best itll all go well!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is incredibly disorganized. His homeworks are due at completely random times during the semester. He tests on mathematical concepts that he cannot adequately explain in English for the majority of the class to understand. The only reason anyone would do well in this class is if they've already taken AP stats. He also cut half the req. topics.

Super willing to meet with you and really cares about your conceptual understanding of statistics. Lecture can be slightly hard to follow at times but if you take good notes and ask questions you will be fine.

Hao Wu teaches largely without giving clear instructions, lectures, or tests. The homeworks are manageable and possible to get an A but the tests (50% of grade) however diverge completely from the material discussed in homeworks and reaches tangentially into lectures. In the cumulative final, he had to explain the short answers >five times. Tough.

Professor Hao emphasizes on concepts more than calculation and explores meaning behind statistical methods. Take him if you are genuinely interested in statistics; avoid if you are just trying to get requirements out of the way by memorizing some equations and getting an A. He has a little bit of an accent, but it's definitely understandable.
Very, very boring lectures that are extremely hard to follow. Makes stats WAY more complicated than it needs to be. Tough grader
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: peabody stats has never been more boring. just lectures on a board with no slides. tough TA grader. cares about attendance. BORINGGGGGG
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: As CORE teachers go, he was valid. No extra work outside the basic curriculum, he didnt really check for annotations and if he did he was chill if you didnt have any. Doesnt really cold call so dont worry if you didnt read the HW. Truly caring professor that wants you to think about the world and leave the classroom smarter.

Prof. Wuerth was a good lecturer. The content was ok, not the most interesting for me personally. The papers were fine, lots of regurgitation and less creative thinking. Your TA will be more important than the professor, which makes the class harder to recommend or not depending on who you get. I think he was an good lecturer to listen to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TA-dependent. An A is almost guaranteed if you can write clearly and have time to go to TA office hours. TA-led lectures occur every Friday, and attendance is only mandatory then. The first and last few readings do not matter, but the rest are necessary. The papers can be written last minute, but it's better to be done sooner and work with the TA.

By far the worst professor I have taken. Grades depend on the TAs idea of fair grading. The professor's lectures are so torturous, you find yourself looking at the clock and begging to be released from the boring, monotone ramblings of a man who confuses even his own self. Avoid this professor if you can, especially if it is for a TR class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class really depends on who your TA is. TA does all the grading for the class- 3 papers worth 25% and quizzes/ participation make up the other 25%. Lectures are often behind in comparison to the readings, but the class does cover interesting content. He is very knowledgeable on the subject, just often presents it in a confusing way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Wuerth is a good speaker and makes his lectures entertaining. But those lectures tend to be convoluted and developed from a framework of his own thinking (not designed for students). He also struggles to ask questions that don't jumble terms. Overall you may leave his class more confused than when you entered. Show up, comment once, don't listen.
This class is supposed to be easy but he made it difficult. 25% participation with a weekly quiz. Three papers with 25% each. TA is not helpful. Extremely boring lectures and mandatory attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Three papers and participation. TA's do all the grading. Hes super knowledgeable and is just a genius. Quotes page numbers from memory. A solid choice, I dig julian. Suit game was unmatched
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives extremely boring and long-winded lectures that often go off-topic. The essays are not too long, but the prompts do not make any sense and are hard to write about. Tough grader even on assignments that are supposed to be rough drafts. Also, we can't use technology in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the papers are hard and he's not very good at responding to emails. also there's no TA for this class anymore
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very funny and nice. You have to read a lot but it is worth it. Attendance is 25%, and there are 3 papers for 25% each. They are not easy but as long as you do the work and go to office hours for help, you should be fine. He cold calls on people so be prepared. Participation matters

Professor Wuerth is a solid choice for a professor. His course involves a lot of reading, but the in class discussions and his witty humor about the topics he covers makes the dense course material fun and comprehensible. He is incredibly knowledgeable, and helpful outside of class. The grade is based on three short, hard papers and participation.

Pretty straight forward class. not the most exciting professor ever but he does what he can to make the information interesting and relevant. Couple of short papers and easy weekly quizzes. If you go to class and talk to the TA an A is super attainable.
Really funny, nice guy, but the material was way over my head and lectures tended to be confusing and unhelpful.  Expect weekly reading quizzes and a few papers.

A great teacher! A super nice guy who is always willing to help during his office hours. The reading is hard, but he explains it well in class. The paper prompts are hard but as long as you answer the questions he's asking and use proper grammar you'll get an A. Go to class because attendance counts and he gives hints for the papers.

Pretty interesting guy, very much an expert on Kant. That being said it is difficult to get him to admit that their are any other viewpoints than his own/Kant's and he paces literally nonstop. Felt like I was getting motion sickness
Also took 105, 220 was even better. I can't tell if Wuerth works better with smaller classes or has worked on improving his teaching skills. Grading is straightforward and class is relaxed.
Julian is the best teacher ever! I LOVE coming to his classes. It is so fun learning with him. He is awesome!!!!!!!
He is awesome!! My fav!!
Great Teacher, but the TA really makes a difference more. But if you do the reading and go to class you will have no problem getting an A
Dull. Attendance was mandatory but really, the class was easy: a few papers, and the final exam questions were given to us in advance. Be careful, he paces nonstop: made me sleepy.

Professor Wuerth is a very, very nice professor. He is brilliant, and will do anything he can to keep his students interested. He is also very reasonable and understanding of the fact that many of his students are taking other classes. Really nice guy

He's a brilliant professor- Witty and articulate. He tends to read from the book, which is useful if you get behind in the reading, or if you have difficulty understanding the txt. His specialty is Kant. Your TA plays a big role in solidify your understanding. Lectures can be a bit dry at times. I'm a big fan of his.
He tends to read from the book, which acts as a good review if you read it. How well you understand the material really depends on your TA.
I think he is an enthusiatic professor, the class is easy and fast paced but pretty boring. You will ge an A but sitting through the lectures sometimes sucks

Professor Wu is a kind guy. He does his best to make the class engaging and the assignments aren't too difficult if you read the textbook and take the time to understand the material. I don't like that the final grade is so heavily based on the midterm and final but if the class doesn't do too well on the midterm he might let you reweigh the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely the worst business module everything is on Quizlet though

Class is manageable as long as you read the TB after every class and study slides. You have 2 unexcused absences but try to go to every class since it helps. For reading TB, study the key terms and summaries. Midterm and final were like weekly quizzes. No surprises. If you put in minimum effort you'll get an A + Dr. Wu is a great professor.

weekly quizzes that are usually pretty easy and case studies that he grades a bit tougher. participation and attendance matter. he moves REALLY fast sometimes you can barely understand him. all quizzes and exams are multiple choice on brightspace. ended up with an A- instead of an A b/c of the midterm but he lets you reweight the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Freeman was a great professor and I learned a lot. It was also one of the easiest business modules for me because there isn't any math involved. I wish he had provided more criteria for the midterm and final tests. I enjoyed the case studies we were assigned and overall the workload wasn't too bad.
Professor Wu seems like a nice professor, but tests were difficult, and the lectures cover only the surface level of topics that he grades on.

Pro: Professor Wu is an amazing lecturer. He gives some great examples to illustrate terms and concepts. Participation matters. Con: Very fast-paced class. Case study homework can be confusing. The midterm and final are challenging.
Super easy and mostly interesting. Exams matter though so study but if you study this class is a super easy A. Nice guy

I loved Professor Wu! His lectures were great and his slides were excellent (great examples, interesting videos, etc.). He is also very responsive and quick with email. The tests are easy as long as you read the textbook and study. Wonderful class!

About as easy as As come at Vandy. Show up, pay attention, participate once per class, and review the PowerPoints and textbook terms, and you'll get an A for sure. Case studies (20% of your grade) are kind of tedious, but the exams and quizzes aren't hard. Interesting material, and he's very knowledgeable about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pretty easy A if you put some effort on the homework and participate in class. You can just study for the midterm and final for a couple hours the night before because a lot of it is just basic examples from his powerpoints or book vocab. He's also a really nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Even though class can be dry, Dr. Wu really cares about his students. The material was simple and it's not hard to get an A. There is 1 midterm and final (not cumulative) worth 20% each. The other 60% is from homework, attendance, and participation. Homework is an easy A and the average for the midterm was an 89%. Just study the notes and vocab.

Attendance was mandatory (2 skips), material was easy and not hard to grasp. Going to lecture and reviewing slides is all you need, and HW does not take long. However, the final was 35% of the grade and tests are all MC and despite with easy-ish material, it is VERY easy to mess things up as the questions can be confusing.

You think it is an easy class but then the final exam comes and kills you. Don't be fooled. Study hard for the final. Class is easy (try to get a 97+), because the final exam may drop you 10% or more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is absolutely terrible at explaining things. Class average on first exam was a 59, that should say something. There are only two exams in his class at the moment, and he gives so much homework to the point where you feel like you are drowning and have no other time for other courses. Thinks his class is the only class you have. Regret taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pro: accessible in office hours, this class had one take-home test and an easy project, have a week to do homework and it's not a lot, don't have to memorize/learn a lot from class if you take good notes Con: doesn't explain things well (make sure you copy the notes down well), Mathematica can be frustrating

Tough class (for me) but nice professor. Cares about his students, clear lectures, seems approachable. 3 tests plus final, and homework is 25% of grade, which is a nice cushion. Occasionally curves tests but generally expects students to perform without much help from his grading. Grading seemed tad easier than other profs in 2300. Solid professor.
Professor Wu has a very good understanding of the material and how to teach it. Grades all finished homework as at least a 90. Pretty easy to get a B in this class if you put in average effort.

Good: let's you bring a cheat sheet (front and back, 8.5x11) for each test, great teacher compared to rest of math department, tests are straightforward & based off homework/class Bad: hard to figure out problems without Chegg, lectures aren't always clear ***for the cheat sheet alone, take Wu. DiffEQ is very formulaic/rigid so your sheet saves you
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is one of the best Vandy math professors. He is very straightforward and clearly communicates the all the important concepts in differential equations. His tests are pretty to-the-point and manageable. Averages are usually in the 70's. Wu is caring and wants you to succeed. Would take him again.

As a professor Wu is straightforward. His lectures are very to-the-point without being too dry, but at times he does show great passion and understanding of the subject. Weekly homework, 3 fair exams and a final. The class is fair and not too terribly hard, but he smoothed out the experience.

He is really good at Mathematics and he explains things pretty clear and easy during the class. His homework is a little bit too much and is compulsory. Exams are hard, with a class average of 72.25 for the first test. He is accessible outside the class and if you are Chinese, you can even talk to him in your mother language lol.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wu is probably the best 1301 professor there is. He's definitely not easy but his tests are fair and he is very generous with curves. He truly wants his students to succeed and do well in the course. If you have to take 1301, take it with Wu.

Professor Wu is a okay lecturer, but he is not very good at answering students' questions in class or simplifying difficult concepts. I learned much more from the textbook. His tests are difficult, but not impossible. He does curve tests if the average is below a 70 (usually a 5 to 10 point curve). Weekly quizzes can be grade boosters.

He basically just speaks the textbook out loud for his lectures. But his tests are actually representative of what you learn, like what's on the optional homework instead of theory. He also gave curves when the averages were too low. He is the definition of an okay 1301 professor. Which is very good.
He is not that good in explaining concept but his tests are very considerate and he sometimes get a curve

The class isn't bad; Xu is really querky which keeps it relatively entertaining.  The homework and tests are extremely easy, so there's no real need to pay attention.  That said, the final is 45% of your grade and is much more difficult, so be prepared.

Okay teacher, explains fairly well,Very easy in class tests.  But the final IS HARD, VERY VERY HARD, and to make it worse, it is 45% of your grade (at least in my time), It is impossible to finish, and he combines concepts from different chapters into one question.  If you can reason thru each concept, you'll be fine (but you still wont finish)

Sneaky man.  Homework is essentially a completion grade, and his two tests are a complete joke, over half the class got 100 on each.  But, no matter how much you study, his final exam is one of the hardest tests you will ever take.  Luckily he grades on a curve, so just study more than everyone else and you'll get out with a decent grade.

extremely paranoid that someone was going to attack the class at any moment, relatively easy though, gives you homework "hints" and both tests are take home with an average of about 100% but the final is awful so he curves tremendously in the end

A fairly easy class. Didn't pay much attention in class, and most of the class didn't show up. He can be fairly funny, but reading the book can get you through most of the class. He's a fair prof, but not all that great at explaining things.

This guy is a HORRIBLE teacher. You won't learn a thing from him. He makes some funny jokes in class but it takes 10 minutes to translate what he said. If you take it with him you can do well (or average for the class) but you may still not learn a thing. Is there for his students but his language barrier is so bad that he can't teach the students.

Class is tough and very conceptual.  He is a brilliant professor, and he lets you know that constantly.  He brags about himself incessantly, but it's kind of funny if you take it light heartedly.  The tests are difficult, the final is impossible, but he is fair and curves the class accordingly.  Overall worth it if you have to take it.
Easiest class on earth.  Bring your comp, surf the net, sit back, chomp on some chips, and get an A+.
nice guy.  loves teaching this class.  always looks sad that no one shows up (probably because the class is so easy and his english is so bad).

run away! or just dont come to class - it's optional. time is better spent reading the book. his lectures are broken english and tests are broken english on paper. However, VERY nice and fair - just you're left wondering 'does he know we're laughing at his chinese pronunciation of words?'

This class would be soooo much easier with an English speaker. All he does is read slides and has never given a straight answer to any legitimate question. As always, nice guy, but fairly hard to understand.
there is no worse professor than him
No Comments

She is nice but I truly think CSET as a department at Vandy should be dismantled. I am surprised that people major in this. I feel confident I could sum up this class in one sentence "be truthful and don't try to fool people with your communication". That's it. Homework every class and assignments which truly feel useless and super repetitive
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Misti has been by far one of my best professors to date. She engaged us really well with interesting topics and always gave us a voice in class discussions. Super knowledgable and caring, she gives thoughtful and helpful feedback for everything you turn in. While a bit of reading, they are worthwhile and easy to skim if you have a late night.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Yang is a wonderful person. She genuinely cares about the well-being of her students. She will learn your name, she will make sure you are included, and she will amaze you with her intellect. She is a great person and a great teacher.

Highly recommend taking either a first year seminar or commons seminar with her! Fantastic teacher who you can easily connect with on a personal level. First year seminars are tough, but commons seminars are a lot of fun and fairly easy.

Awesome prof. I'm an anthropology major now because of her. She's tough, but discussions are very engaging. She's an understanding person, knows what she's talking about, and makes class fun. Attendance is crucial & be prepared to write.

This class is a commons seminar and meant to be relatively easy. Professor Yant is a very direct, to the point person. She is funny and kind, but also expects respect and participation. She is concerned with understanding and learning more than grades, and if you show effort you will do well. She is also very helpful and cares about  students.
Professor Yant is one of my favorite teachers I have had at Vanderbilt.  Very helpful and has amazing lectures.  Take any class you can with her

The class isn't the easiest, but Yago is clear about what will be covered in class and on the tests. These tests are hard though to complete in the time limit.  You don't get graded on everyday homework, but you really should do it for the practice problems. His accent is strong but understandable.

Yago is the man. The class wasn't easy but I ended up with a B-. He has a sense of dry humor that makes you pay attention better in class. Although the material is hard, he wants his students to do well and I definitely did not deserve the grade he gave me at the end of the class.

Yago is a great and nice Professor, and my classmates this year complemented his sense of humor so class was usually interesting. If you have any problems, go to office hours or set up appointments. Do all the graded and textbook homework, take all extra credit opportunities and understand the material well. Exams are hard but definitely passable.
Not so clear during the class. There are two quizzes every week so it makes attendance fairly important. If you do not show up, you will not get any credits.

Yago is a nice guy but his tests are impossible. If you have the opportunity make sure you take 1200. His accent definitely makes it harder to understand.
