If you do end up in this class make sure you do the homework every night. Your grades on the HW and the quizzes are not accurate to what you will receive on the actual tests.

Yago is a nice guy but his tests are impossible.  If you have the opportunity make sure you take 1200.  His accident definitely makes it harder to understand.  If you do end up in this class make sure you do the homework every night. Your grades on the HW and the tests are not accurate to what you will receive on the actual tests.

Although you can barely understand a word he says sometimes, he is a very nice person who will explain everything again during office hours, which are necessary to understanding the material. He basically gives you free 100pts out of 550 of your grade. He has a grader who this year was very generous. Watch out for the first test.
Yago is adorable, his accent is totally fine, and he knows his stuff despite sometimes being careless with his algebra. He's a cool dude and I'd definitely take him again.

Yago was a great professor - his lectures could be dry, but he has a wry sense of humor that keeps the class interesting.  His tests are difficult, but do not present any material that wasn't covered in class or on the homework.  As long as you study, you should be fine.  No surprises, very straightforward kind of guy.
Besides thick accent, other things are perfect

Dr. Antolin was very willing to help.  Tests were pretty straightforward, plentiful practice problems (which need to be done) were provided, and  (easy) daily quizzes and homework assignments counted for over an exam's worth of points.  However, English is not his first language, it and shows, though he is normally pretty understandable.

Yago is an average professor. The grading is clear, he'll help when asked, and his lectures aren't terrible. Attendance and daily homework aren't mandatory, but there are 2 quizzes a week and 4 graded homeworks (one before each test) which cannot be made up. Tests are not too difficult, but they are long. Yago is funny and relaxed.

Yago's grading is clear, there are no surprises, and he'll help when asked. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are 2 quizzes a week which cannot be made up. Homework isn't picked up. There are 4 tests and one exam. The problems are not too difficult, but sometimes there is not enough time to finish the tests. Overall an average professor.
Yago is the man!
The best. Grade easily. Very nice, gentle instructor. Very friendly. Flexible.
I absolutely loved Shiomi-sensei's class! She always has a great attitude in the class and is always flexible if you are having any problems. She is definitely one of Vanderbilt's best professors.

Shiomi-sensei is an amazing professor. She always makes sure that the students understand everything and is always willing to meet with students at a later time to help them. I definitely recommend taking a class with her.

FASCINATING class made even better by a professor who loves the subject!  She admits it's her favorite class to teach!  Be prepared for some great discussions and readings (read enough to get the gist of it, and then go with class flow).  2 assignments, one of which is completion, make up class content.
Great teacher! I loved Dr Yagel's class. Very lenient with deadlines and truly cares for her students. That being said, it's a lot of work. Not for the lazy or fainthearted

There are 200-300 page reading assignments for each class and she often will cancel class an hour before, which is VERY frustrating when assignments are due. She never grades the 1-page assignments you turn in, so by the time she gets them back to you, you have made the same mistake multiple times. I feel like my writing did not improve at all.

Dr. Yagel is incredibly smart and nice. You're assigned to read a book a week for Medicine, Religion, and Spirituality, however its not really necessary. Just make sure you're able to participate in class. The final research paper makes up most of your grade. Write a good paper, go for help on it, and you'll get a good grade in the class.

We read 12 books throughout the semester and had to write 8 1-page papers about a few of them, but they are easy to write. There are two big papers that require research, but she is really good with telling you how to do them. Overall, Yagel is really nice. Just follow her instructions, participate in discussions, and this class is an easy A.

Best professor I've had at Vandy. Really cares about what she's teaching. Really cares about her students and their writing. Extremely fair with grading and expectations. If she's teaching a class, take it! Be ready for lots of reading though.

Great professor. Classes have a lot of reading, but the books are interesting so it's not too bad. She gives a lot of freedom with paper topics so you get to research material that you're intereted in. She's also really understanding.
Wonderful, wonderful professor!  Engaging, desiring her class to comprehend what the material implies about the world today.  Would highly recommend :)

You read 11 full length books over the course of the semester, she is a very tough grader.  Papers are on extremely difficult topics and you don't get to do rewrites on every paper unlike the other poster said.  She is very unorganized and although the lectures are interesting, the work outside of class is ridiculous. Do not take her writing semina
Easiest class at vandy. She allows rewrites on all papers and comments on necessary changes to afford an A.
Fadlon is a decent teacher. Overall happy with the class, very helpful. Goes through lectures pretty quick though.
Prof Fadlon was great! Very helpful
Professor Fadlon was great!
Fadlon reads off of his notes in class which makes for some of the most mundane lectures I've sat in.

He gives two midterms and a final. The exams are hard, but he cures so that the average is somewhere in B. I actually learned a lot in this class, something that I can't say about many other classes. Very interesting and smiley professor. Would recommend

Very straightforward teacher. Teaches directly from a set of notes that he provides online, making attendance optional and textbook use minimal. Few homework assignments that aren't particularly difficult, and two midterms that can be tricky but are easily manageable with a small amount of prior studying. Would recommend.
A great professor. I wish he will teach upper level classes.

He reads straight from his notes in order to teach, which are difficult to follow. He doesn't do a good job of answering questions, and he is impatient when you do. He gives 2 midterms and a final. The midterms are very very difficult but he curves them.

I literally could not understand anything she was talking about in class ever.  The book is helpful especially if you Google more examples before tests.  Make sure you go to class, as she has a decent number of pop quizzes including the occasional take-home quiz.  Quizzes are easier, but the tests often have proofs or problems not learned in class.
She is terrible.  Could not understand a word of what she said, she never helped when students asked questions, and she has a grudge against students.  Avoid her.  Take Mike Neamtu instead.

Completely terrible. Lectures are based on PowerPoints but she does a terrible job explaining them. Don't try to ask question because she can't understand them. Tests are impossible and not at all related to the study materials she gives you.  If you can avoid this professor, do it.

I rarely rate professors but this one I had to. This professor is terrible. Can barely understand her, not very helpful after the grading, very slow to return emails, frequently evades questions. Lectures are useless. Doesn't address questions in class, flies through material, mumbles. It's REALLY BAD. I had As in all classes except this one.

STAY AWAY! She's easy (if you're not a complete moron), but God is she awful. Doesn't speak a lick of English (the fact that she has her lectures  memorized throws you off, but just try asking a question), and she's completely useless as a teacher. If you can deal with it, learning out of the textbook is the best idea.
Absolutely brutal. Completely out of touch w/ students
Not hard. She tells you what's on the tests and they're very similar to homework questions.
You might not want to take her if you don't like reading many articles.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: For all the people that gave her a bad rating, you must be a frat bro majoring in HOD lmao

Prof Yi was a super difficult grader. We had to watch a TV show and then take super in-depth quizzes analyzing it. Sometimes you got the answers correct but weren't up to her standards of detail so she would take points off. I'm sure it would have been easier with more understanding of Korean language/history. I ended up withdrawing from the course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's a really unfair and tough grader. Her feedback is rude and doesn't help, and she is extremely nitpicky. There is also a lot of homework, and the tests are pretty hard if you don't dedicate all the films to memory and watch them more than once. Wouldn't ever recommend it unless you are familiar with Korean films already.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really respect Prof Yi. She might seem like a tough grader, but I genuinely think she's a FAIR grader. Everyone who says she's a tough grader only say that because they came into the class expecting to do no work (asian studies has a rep for being "insanely easy As"). The reading isn't a lot and it's very interesting material. Recommend her!

This class is extremely hard for no reason. I would strongly recommend not taking this class with this professor. Attendance is mandatory. It is very hard to get an A in this class. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR
A ton of required reading and a tough grader. Very strict attendance policy as well.

Fantastic instructor who really listens to her students and adapts her teaching style to her classroom. While there is a fair amount of reading/material, they are usually quite niche and interesting and relate to the subject matter in a unique way. Her passion in the subject material really shows through her lectures and engagement with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The professor treats class as if this is your only class and assigns unnecessary amounts of work that isn't hard but extremely time consuming. On top of all of this her lectures constantly go off topic and her tests and quizzes test you on unnecessarily specific details.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best courses I've taken at Vanderbilt. Prof. Yi is so knowledgeable in her field and wants to help students learn through many avenues (lectures, small groups, short papers, etc.) Prepare for every class because it's heavily discussion-based when she's not lecturing. It's very interesting though, so you'll want to put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Took this class Spring of 2020, Prof Yi was great with the switch to online. Weekly discussion postings. Discussion based class so be prepared to talk in class. There was only one test, but it was difficult. Multiple Papers. P.S: She makes you use Chicago Style citations.

She definitely knows what she's talking about and sets clear grading criteria but that also means she expects a lot from you. Grades really tough but also provides a lot of grades. I would not recommend her classes for an easy A or a class to take for fun. You have to be prepared for class because she chooses random people to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While she may be a tough grader on some assignments and assign a lot of reading, she teaches history in a very unique way which makes the class engaging. She also provides many opportunities for extra credit so there's no excuse to fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really passionate lecturer who knows a lot about her subject area. She incorporates a multimedia approach (e.g., movies) into her classes that is really special. She notices if you're engaged in class, and she genuinely wants everyone to succeed, even if she doesn't always show it. Don't lie to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While she is a tough grader, there are a number of drops/freebies that she gives near the tail-end of the class to bump up your grade significantly. Grades aside, the content and material of this class are very interesting - covering a plethora of contemporary topics through a multitude of perspectives and their implications in a modern society.
Professor Yi gave great lectures, however there was a lot of reading before class. There were weekly 300 word discussions. She graded very hard on worksheets. Be prepared to speak in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She penalizes students for everything, even if ill or dealing with serious extenuating circumstances. Most assignments are large essays or huge worksheets that are only worth 2.5% or lower, and she grades extremely harshly. You can work as hard as you possibly can in her classes, she will not care or treat you fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Yi assigns hundreds of pages of reading each week in addition to films outside of class. Most assignments are only worth 2% of your grade but are lengthy essays. Not worth it for the amount of tedium involved. Also, skipping class, even if you are excused/sick, doesn't fly with her at all. The material would otherwise be interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took the class during COVID so not sure how things have changed, but it was a challenging course that she made a lot easier. The posted notes are great but I still would recommend reading the book to understand the complexities of linear and diff eq. Discussion was not required but helpful for practice. Relatively easier course than 2300 imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is comprised of 2 tests and the final (25% of your grade each) and the last 25% are quizzes and homework. The class isn't difficult to pass, but it is difficult to get an A. Prof Wang is super sweet but sometimes overcomplicates the material and is hard to understand. I definitely had to teach myself sometimes during the course.
Shes very nice, but the class was comprised of 3 exams, each 25% of your grade, so it was hard to get an A unless you do really well on the tests. They werent terrible, but As were hard to get.

Dr. Wang was so helpful with everything. She was understanding and accommodating of personal circumstances. She posts notes of everything with examples which are great if you skip class or missed something. One short problem set per week and a timed homework after each chapter. 3 Midterms that are very similar to the homework. Straightforward exams

Really good lectures that are easy to follow, which is good because there is a lot of stuff covered in the class. The quizzes and homeworks are plenty and not always easy; they definitely force you to learn the material. She dropped 2 quizzes and one homework, as well as gave out some small extra credit assignments (usually proofs for +0.2%).

Dr. Wang is a very dedicated professor. She puts a lot of work into making lesson notes and creating practice problems. Timed "quizzes" (1 or 2 problems based on the suggested problems) due every midnight of class day and one more exam-like homework per chapter. Lots of work but pays off. Midterms are fair, but small errors can cost a lot of points
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ill admit I rarely went to class in person. But the reason that Wang is such an amazing teacher is because of her notes. I could stare at the textbook all day long and not understand a concept but take one look at the her notes that she uploads and instantly get it. Shes the best math professor Ive had here at Vanderbilt.

Math1301 is hard. You have to practice. Do every optional and non optional hw assignment and make sure you understand. Trust me. Studying for tests will be easy if you do this. Yi wang is about as good as gets for 1301 profs. She doesnt over complicate things, she wants to help, and she knows what shes doing. Test avg 65-70, but not bad for 1301.
Fair professor who made expectations clear, and really nice guy. Course was useful and of average difficulty.

Professor Chen is nice and easy to reach, but the lectures are extremely dry and both the outline of the course and the final project is unclear. Attendance is not required, so a lot of students stopped showing up after a few lectures. Your grade only consists of a paper presentation and the final group project, so it  adds more to the confusion.

Professor Chen is a nice guy who is accessible and wants you to succeed. However, the lectures for Network Analysis can be quite dry and many students stopped showing up, so the class itself was quite boring. It is a very easy class and if you work with him on your project ideas you will do well. Just don't expect to learn a ton or be super engaged

Dr. Chen's Network Analysis class was probably the easiest A I have gotten in a CS class. While his lectures can be overly complex, as long as you complete all of the reading summaries and group project, you'll be fine. If you have a background in network building or analysis that's great but if not you'll have to reach out to him to get help.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Content is kind of hit or miss, some of it was very cool, some of it meh. Daily reading checks and participation is a chunk of your grade as well as 30 min essays and a final project. So you never really have to memorize anything or know anything off the top of your head except for the reading checks. Prof. Young is very knowledgeable in the field.

Professor Young encourages students to think critically and creatively about the subject matter. She is always open to discussion, and I really enjoyed her class! There are three papers throughout the course: a phenomenological analysis, a response paper, and a research paper.

Prof. Young is very knowledgeable about her subjects. There were 6 in-class essays which could be stressful, but I found she graded semi-easy considering each was only a few points towards total grade. The final project was very fun and creative rather than stressful. If you talk to her outside of class, she is very understanding and helpful!

she is such a sweetheart and the class was super interesting. might seem irrelevant but she is so passionate she makes it worth it. super understanding about personal issues and just cares about her students a lot. highly recommend.

She is really nice but is a tough grader - not an easy A. This is a very niche subject matter. You have to come to class and be willing to put time into this, or you won't do well. She also is super rigid about what she expects in essays: topic sentences, leading concluding sentences, etc. Make sure you are interested in the subject matter!

Barve made what should be an easy class into a total drag. Lectures begin at a snails pace, but pop quizzes make attendance all but mandatory. Second half of course is poorly explained and exams quickly become out of the lectures' depth. Lots of typos/errors on homework, exams. Barve is generally understanding but class was endlessly frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: There were many difficult concepts in this class, but his exams were not nearly as bad as they could've been. However it felt like many times during class he had little idea what he was talking about, and would often make mistakes when doing problems in class. Overall a very nice guy though, and hopefully he will get better the more he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Barve is a good professor. His lectures can be dry and often slow, but he's usually very clear when he explains things. He will tell you what to expect on exams and doesn't try to play tricks on you. The class has some difficult concepts regardless, but Barve makes it manageable. Cares about his students for sure and very fair in grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a good professor. One of the best. He makes the course so much easier. You just have to do your homework and the exams are also easy bc of cheat sheets.

Hes a really nice guy, but you can tell its his first semester teaching. He also definitely cares about his students he brought us all snacks for our final in case we had forgotten to eat breakfast. My issues with the class has a lot more to do with the curriculum being all over the place and confusing.

Pretty sure he's new to teaching. Overall a really nice guy, but lectures can be a bit dry. Exams are on the easier side compared to other profs who teach this class. This class overall has a lot of homework, regardless of the professor. This class is tough, but honestly Barve probably is the easiest option.

Loved this class by the end of the semester. You get used to his style of chalkboard (not slides) lecture with questions/occasional discussions with the class. I learned a lot that extends beyond just film to other forms of media but even just life in general, product vs art, what it means to be truly objective. Inconsistent grading sometimes.

Seth Kim is by far my favorite professor that I've had at Vanderbilt. He has a passion for critical thinking and wants his students to leave the classroom with a more developed perspective on life. If you appreciate teachers who care more about expanding your knowledge rather than grades and tests, then Seth is the man for you.

Seth is straightforward when it comes to what to expect and how he grades the few assignments hell give throughout the semester. Hes attentive, so although participation is a big part of your final grade, you dont have to give a speech every class as long as he can tell youre paying attention. Expect meaningful discussions in and out of class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Clearly a very smart guy but made me scared to talk in class because if you say something he considers stupid, he makes that very clear. It is embarrassing. Is more interested in showing off his knowledge than teaching us about the subject. Very unclear grading practices - tries to trip you up. Not the most difficult class, but just not enjoyable.

This man has 2 pages because all these reviewers couldn't spell his name right. If you're on here because you are considering a class he teaches, just show up. He tells you what he's all about in the first class; if you're smart you'll take him at his word. If you're not, you'll start a ratemyprofessor witch hunt because you're a "problem-solver."
Dr. Kim is the single greatest professor I have ever had the pleasure of studying with.

Seth consistently encouraged rigorous thought processes and close inspection of difficult concepts while creating a positive and productive environment. This class deals with heavy topics and if requires a lot of attention and thought, however this class is not about catching you in things you dont know, he cares about his students and the subject.

Overall, really enjoyed Seth as a professor-he's passionate about teaching. There are times where he could be dismissive, approaching condescending, which hinders engagement and discussion. I hope he continues, along with the other profs in this program, to commit to working against structural disparities and not perpetuate them. Glad he's at Vandy

Seth is an extremely intelligent and inspirational teacher. His lectures will change how you think about culture, cinema, and pedagogy. He's not for everyone, don't take his class for AXLE or to watch movies, take it if you want a class that will make you think critically. With that being said, the workload is manageable b/c participation is key.

I completely understand the hate for Seth, but I think my classmates need to relax a little. All the hate stems from grade anxiety. If you really get invested in the material, and you really try, YOU WILL GET A GOOD GRADE. You may not like him as a person, but Seth is extremely knowledgeable and, most importantly, he cares.

I will never take a class with Seth again. I don't think I came out learning a single thing. Could never follow any lectures, and had constant anxiety because of the workload. Avoid at all costs. If I didn't have to take this course for credit, I would have dropped as soon as I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He'd be a better philosophy professor rather than being teaching Intro to Film and Media Studies. He has very unclear grading expectations, and it's impossible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. There are required screenings and readings that we rarely mention in class. He thinks he has discovered this brilliant new way of teaching, yet he teaches you nothing about film. Assignments are basically "write an essay" or "take this test," then you find out he wants things in a specific way AFTER he's done grading.

I understand that film studies in general tends to be a little haughty, but Seth's class takes this to a whole new level. He stresses critical thinking but to the degree where no progress is made in understanding. Also, he talks with his eyes closed like he's making the most important point the world has ever heard. The guy is so full of himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Every week his class was the worst part,  I dread coming to his class. Get ready to have conversations about how to have conversations, do NOT expect to discuss anything film related. Answers questions with questions. I often wonder if he knows what he's talking about as he doesn't seems to have plan or original thoughts. Literally the worst.

Seth is undoubtedly one of the worst professors I've had in Vanderbilt, and perhaps one of the worst teachers I've ever had at all. He will fill lectures with his pseudo-intellectual ramblings which he only vaguely and often times never connects back to the core of the class. There is no grading criteria or understanding presented of how to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I HATE this class. All he does is lecture us on critical thinking. You need the textbook but he will never reference it. He won't tell you what's on the midterm. He talks about how his opinion doesn't matter and his papers don't matter, but your grade is still based on them, so enjoy the class.
She is fantastic. She took us on a field tour of the power plant, which was an incredible experience.
Great professor, keeps saying turban instead of turbine

Dr. Y is super awesome and has created custom notes for the class that are way more readable than a textbook. She is super fun and probably the exact opposite of Anilkumar. Quizzes were open notes but not always straightforward. Sometimes I wished things had more structure. Quizzes can be grade replaced, so easy A if you do the necessary work

Dr Yraguen is the best person in the entire world. She was super accommodating when I needed it, letting me turn in work as late as I needed, and do alternative testing options. She is brilliant and really encourages you to understand the content. She is generous with partial credit on quizzes and offers grade replacement opportunities. 100/10.

She believes your grade should reflect your content knowledge at the end of the semester. You can grade replace by showing that you have mastered the topic on subsequent tests (which include optional questions on previous topics). Homework is optional. Tests did take a while to be graded. TAKE HER IF YOU CAN she is awesome and feels like a friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely my favorite professor at college so far. The class and material may be difficult, and she does not hand out free grades, but she will put in all the effort to make sure you understand it. She graded on a mastery grading scale which allowed me to go from a C+ before the final exam, to an A+ when receiving a 100 on all my mastery topics.

Her teaching style stands out from the rest. She genuinely cares about ensuring everyone gets the hang of thermo and is there to guide you through every bit of it. Plus, she's super easy to reach outside of class, and her lecture notes cover everything you need. Just keep up with the homework for each chapter, and you should do fine on the exams.
The content was very enjoyable. I work in a research lab, and it was nice to learn about techniques that I could use in my research.
Lectures are straight forward. She provides supplemental material to point students in the right direction. She is also available and responds quickly over email.

She curves. It will be a lot of work. I personally love reading research articles. In this class, material is based on primary literature. But in her attempt to simplify things for the class, she often ends up confusing the students by ignoring nuanced conclusions and even contradicting authors statements. Take at your own risk.

Grades based off two exams (midterm/final). Study guides and old exams are posted online. Homework assignments lead up to preparation for the final presentation. Plenty of chances to make up grades if you do poorly on an assignment or exam. Got a better grade than I was expecting.
The group projects was the best part about the entire class - it helped to prep for medical school interviews. The content was rather straightforward and easy to understand.
Really interesting material covered in class. Defiantly enjoyed the second half more than the first! But it was neat to see everything come together.
Posts old exam material to help study. Multiple choice questions are recycled from last material. Lenient grader on exams and assignments.

This is an extremely difficult and niche neuro class that is completely based off of scientific articles and random facts from the articles that don't seem to contribute much to your learning. Be prepared to put in a LOT of effort bc an absurd amount of info is covered in this class. Unless you're really interested in research, I wouldn't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Has extensive knowledge of the class material, but not accurate in her presentation. Probably the least lenient teacher I've had; her test questions are often contradict the lecture slides, and what's worse, she never addresses these mistakes when students bring them up. Overall, spent more time decoding her words than learning the material.

We have a review session tonight for the final exam. She also posted all of the old quizzes and last years exam. As long as you are willing to put effort in, you will do well. Her grading criteria is straight forward.

Prof. Yohn gave good feedback and helped us with our final presentation. We met with her several times to review the layout. It was a very beneficial experience and I enjoyed presenting and reading in depth about the material.

Avoid! Rude and not understanding of her students Worst lecture slides ever! During Covid, she ADDED hours of work on top of the original syllabus Her feedback for group project is incomplete, sets you up for failure Exams (2) are difficult, rely on memorization of things you will immediately forget Extra credit exists, so that's nice
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Yohn always seemed irritated at her students, which was discouraging. If someone asks a question and no one answers, she often refused to answer the question. Emails sent to class were often downright rude; even if her points were valid, there was no reason for her to be so harsh. I liked the content and grading was nice, but I dreaded class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Having moved to a remote classroom - there are a lot of opportunities to complete extra credit. The discussion boards are helpful to see where other students have questions on the lectures. We are preparing our final presentations now; she has given us chances to re-do assignments.

Not even half way through the semester yet, and I am enjoying this course! Plenty of extra credit opportunities and she makes sure everyone is on the same page before moving onto another topic in the lecture.

I really enjoyed this class. The group project was a lot of fun and was an easy A. There are online quizzes which are open notes, you can complete these with other students in the class. Exams and quizzes are straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You need to come to class to do well. But all of the material is easy to grasp as long as you are willing to invest the time into reviewing material before hand. She was a great professor and the TA was great! Defiantly would recommend this course for Neuro majors !

Great class! One of my favorite at Vanderbilt, I have recommended this course to several of my friends. You will do fine as long as you are willing to work for your grade. If you are looking for an easy A, probably not the best class to take.

Weird class. Content was all relatively straightforward, but the course was structured bizarrely. There were open-note quizzes that asked questions no one - not even people who recorded lectures - could answer. Exam problems that blatantly contradicted lecture slides. Still, lots of extra credit, fairly easy project at the end. Not the worst pick.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Doable class if you're looking for an A, but not necessarily an "easy A," and the class dynamic or professor were not that enjoyable. She tries way too hard to come off as scary and strict and doesn't really like when you ask questions, which just makes things all the more stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Plenty of chances to do well - many extra credit options offered during the course. Attendance to class is needed to understand the material. At the beginning of each class, we review key concepts. It is a fair class if you study and come to class.

Disorganized slides, doesn't explain the material well. You have to superficially read many papers &understand the slides/papers in the way she wants (she will sometimes say things that directly contradict the papers in lecture) to do good on the tests/quizzes. Even then online quiz q's can be unclear& test on things she doesn't cover well in class
Great lectures, interesting content, easy exams, and Dr. Yohn really cares about her students. Must take for any neuro majors.
textbook is required for class but should be listed as optional. she is very assessable outside of class and responds quickly to emails.

Dr. Tao is one of the funniest most approachable professors I have had at Vanderbilt. He is exceptionally lenient with due dates but his homework assignments are very challenging and time consuming, so I would not wait until the last minute to start them. Lecture attendance is essential to do well but Dr. Tao makes them engaging and humorous.

Avoid D. Tao for Quantatative Methods!! He is a terrible lecturer, which really doesn't matter since the homeowrk comes from the textbook and not what he teaches. The class is weighted very heavily towards a final project, which is incredibly difficult and a rubric is not provided until after he grades. Much better off with a different professor!

Dr. Two is great! The content for QM 2 sucks and he knows it. Class is totally optional and I honestly wouldn't even recommend going to lectures. Homework can be completed with the textbook and is graded by the TA. Exams are ok, and final project worth 30% of overall grade is pretty manageable.

Definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken but Tao made it more bearable. He cares a lot about the students and is always willing to push back due dates to reduce stress. Truly the nicest guy and there's never a dull moment in class.

Probably the hardest class I've ever taken but you should take it with Kenny. Funny and engaging lecturer despite his terrible handwriting. Do your best to adjust to his handwriting. At the beginning of the semester, couldn't read but learned over time. Very intelligent and he skips steps sometimes in lecture but is always willing to answer questio

Dr. Tao is extremely vague and nondescript with homework, exams, and the final project. He can never answer my question with a straightforward answer. Also, his notes are all handwritten and barely readable. He is very responsive to emails however his responses never make sense or answer the question I asked. Never again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Final group project instead of final exam. Never used the textbook, learned everything from lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory but IDK how you would learn anything without going to class. Overall great guy. Responds quickly to slack.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: You grade reflects your effort. The two tests are worth about 20% each (provides previous tests and are difficult if you do not put above-average effort into class. He's a genius, will offer as much help as you need, and is very accessible outside of class (will respond to Slack messages at 9:00 PM). Work hard, try your best, and you'll earn an A
Great guy, super sarcastic and witty

Prof Z is a great professor to take for Core 1020. He is a little picky on the main assignments, but there are always chances to revise it so you can still get a good grade. Every class is just discussions on the readings so it's very chill. And he provides amazing feedback.
This professor is awesome. If I was a girl id flirt with him

Great class! Some readings were a bit hard but prof z explained things well. couple quizzes and smaller assignments but the assignments were honestly fun cause they weren't a typical essay or something. Term paper on any topic pertaining to class, which made it better as someone who's not a big writer. Prof z was super super nice and helpful

Prof. Zainaldin is the perfect combo of an effective professor and a kind person. I learned a lot without being stressed over the little things like with a strict prof. Attend lectures and participate, you'll do a lot better. The 2 exams are open-note, and the paper is not too long. This is an amazing prof, take a class with him if you can!!

The most engaging and fun professor. He is so passionate about what he teaches and has plenty of fun stories that make class discussions always engaging. He grades very kindly and is a very helpful resource for becoming a better writer and thinker. Definitely take a class with him!
Great guy. This class is an Easy A. He is so lenient with grading and attendance.
He is awesome definitely take him. Very engaging and teaches well. Top notch.

Andres is the GOAT. Not only was Core 1010 an easy A to get thanks to his kindness and cooperation, but he geuinely made the class enjoyable. He is such a funny person, and he always made sure everyone was included in discussions. Also, we would get to watch movies or listen to songs. He was my favorite professor from my first semester.

Core1010 fulfilled it's easy A reputation, but Andres made it so fun. Genuinely a great guy who cared about his students and got to know everyone. Encouraged creativity and was absolutely hilarious. This class which could have been super dull became my favorite of the semester. TAKE HIM.

andrés was easily the best teacher i had during the beginning of freshman year. he was hilarious and kept us engaged in what is basically a normal writing seminar with some philosophy mixed in. he made sure everyone was included in discussions and took into account our opinions about what we were learning. if you take CORE 1010, take it with him!!
Really interesting guy. He swears a lot during class but uses cuss words wisely in a way that promotes his lecture. Definitely non-standard for a professor, but I really liked his class!

Prof. Zamora was the best professor I've had so far! For an honors writing seminar, the writing was definitely manageable and lectures were super engaging! He was clear on what he wanted but if you showed that you cared and were putting in effort, it was easy to achieve a desirable grade.

Dr. Zamora is hands-down the best professor I've taken at Vanderbilt. His passion for what he teaches is contagious. I learned so much in his class, and I am so glad I took his seminar. It is clear he is genuinely cares about his students. He is always there to help and give constructive feedback on assignments and presentations. Take Zamora!!!

This man deserves a 5/5. Spanish film is an incredibly interesting class and a different angle to explore spanish culture than the tons of lit classes at Vandy. Professor Zamora really helps you understand the nuance of the genre, and class discussions help improve your speaking skills, especially with describing complex topics. Great instructor.

I took HONS1860W which was Women in Spanish Film and lemme tell you...by far my favorite class this semester. Professor Zamora is funny, smart, witty, and NEVER boring. He cares about our understanding +  processing of material, and at times though the content is awkward he makes it very easy to talk and learn. Absolutely recommend this professor.

Class is based off reaction papers, a presentation, participation, and essay exams. No rubrics, but hes clear with what he wants and you have freedom to take assignments in whatever direction you like. Great class to develop your understanding of films overall. Interesting professor who brings unique life experience from Spain. 100% recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take. This. Class. Professor Zamora does a great job familiarizing students with Spanish texts and encouraging them to think deeper. He's hilarious and I genuinely enjoyed going to his class. Grades are primarily based off of 4 papers where you choose the topic. There's a good bit of reading, but he's understanding if you fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Zamora is extremely insightful and obviously loves what he does. Very interesting class, and definitely a great choice for a first year writing seminar. Most of the grade was off of the 4 papers we wrote, but grading was fair.

Professor Zamora is hilarious and a very kind teacher. He is engaging and not a super hard grader, but definitely go to class and participate. I took him for a freshman writing seminar and he is very knowledgable about writing. We had to buy books to read for the class, but no textbooks. We had no tests only essays.

I took Zamora's FYS "Travel Matters" and loved the class. Because it's only a 15 person class, attendance is necessary but the lectures are lighthearted. While participation is "graded," some kids in my class never talked so it's not a big deal. He's not a super tough grader so don't expect to have trouble passing, but getting above a 90 isn't easy
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The books we read in this class were engaging and challenging, and my Spanish reading comprehension increased dramatically in the course of the semester.  Zamora is a genuinely likable, interesting guy, but mandatory lectures didn't help much with the class.  He is a generous grader on take-home exams.  Overall, this is a good class and professor.

Spanish Realism. Zamora is such a laid back professor. He isn't afraid to get off topic to really get students engaged in his lectures. This usually drives me nuts, but somehow he finds a way to relate it back to the class. Readings (skimmings) are required(ish) and he's really lax about attendance. Probably my favorite Spanish professor yet.

Zamora is a pretty cool guy, but the Travel Matters Seminar is pretty dry at times. There's lots of reading and journals every week. Usually doesn't give A's on papers unless they're genius, so a B would be the average. Zamora is a great professor and really loves this topic, but you have to read all the text to truly comprehend his seminar.
The class is mostly discussion. There are 3 papers and 1 final paper. There are weekly journals and participation is graded. There are very few A's on papers.
It was kind of funny to have a professor for a writing seminar whose first language is not English, but he is awesome!  Absolutely take a class from him.
Zamora's the man.
He is the best teacher i have ever had at Vanderbilt and he is damn sexy.
Cool guy, funny and definetley spits game

MZW is a fascinating guy with interesting thoughts and explanations of economics concepts. His class consisted of challenging daily readings and calculus-heavy in-class problems. There were 4 midterms and a final. Exams tend to be much more difficult than class, but with curves and the lowest dropped. I skipped the final and he dropped it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was revamped for Spring 2023 to a class with only exams. I normally prefer this except for the fact that the exams were significantly more difficult (technically and conceptually) than any material covered in class or on the "study guides" he provides. If your math skills are not amazing you will suffer tremendously. Avoid this class!!!

Awful teacher. Even after the absolute disaster that was the first test, he did nothing to adjust his approach. The tests are all math, but he barely shows you how to solve the problems and just somehow expects you to know how to do it on the spot. Its honestly ridiculous, I've never seen anything like it in my four years of college.

He's not gonna be everyone's cup of tea, but I enjoy this class. He does his best to make the class as discussion-based as possible and is an engaging lecturer. He also expects a ton from his students though so be prepared to know the class concepts inside and out. Only gripe is that he assigns economic essays from the 50s for HW that are on exams.

His lectures don't follow any structure and are disorganized. He doesn't give any practice or examples and the test material doesn't cover half the things he teaches. He prides himself on putting "twists" to questions and expects you to apply class concepts, but never teaches you them. The average scores on exams have never been higher than an 80.

Prof does not seem to care about the class. The course is graded by 5 tests that are primarily math focused. Curriculum is reading and lecture based, no problem sets. Only practice problems are on the review sheets, which are posted as late as a single day before the test, and sometimes contain errors on the answer key (if one is provided at all).

If I had to look back on things I regret doing at Vandy, choosing this professor would have to be #1 on that list. Tests are hard af and not like review sheet at all and he can't teach for shii. I aint never rated a professor but I feel like I gotta so noone gotta go through what Spring 23 went through.

Everyone thought we would be writing papers this semester. Unfortunately he changed the class to 5 tests that are wildly harder then anything seen in class. To sum the class up he will put questions on the test, he literally can not solve (ask any person from this semester about the circle question).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading is totally mess. He gives no feedback and can postpone grade release for months. He just randomly assigns grades based on personal preference and you can do nothing about it. The lectures are useless and you can learn nothing meaningful from his course. Definitely take other electives! Half of the course drops after the first meeting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was most definitely unconventional but has a unique lecturing style that will be appealing if you like to talk about Economic concepts in a more abstract setting. The workload is moderate but I would never say that I was ever stressed out about the class which is always a good thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: MZW the goat, definitely recommend if you really like econ. That said, if you're just trying to get a major with the past of least resistance, this probably isn't the class. Not that it's so hard, just the readings are intimidating and the material is hard.

The reading reflections are intimidating. You can either get A-, B+, or B on this, so it feels unfair that you worked hard and can only get an A-. However, the papers (which make up a bulk of the grades) are graded very fairly to a point of leniency. 1 out of the 3 classes were always cancelled every week, which was nice. Recommend as an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: The reading is really hard but the prof is super knowledgeable and lectures are very clear.

this is the first time I rate a professor because of an awful learning experience. U need to do pre-class readings and write weekly responses. The articles often contain ridiculously complicated formulas and information. The maximum grade you can get on this 30% part is A-. No PowerPoint/board note. Be ready to spend time on it and get B/lower.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not a traditional class. No real syllabus or clear expectations. Never knew what your grade was in the class. Had to write a reflection paper every week that he claimed he read but was clear he didn't. Didn't receive a single grade/feedback throughout the semester but I think he just gave everyone an A in the end. Don't take if you want structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're interested in econ research, TAKE HIM for 4050. You literally just read academic papers on environmental economics, so it's the perfect way to find out if econ research is your cup of tea. Grades are three 3-5 page critiques of papers, and weekly reflections on the rest of the papers. The more you put into this class the more you get out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: 4050 is awesome if you're interested in econ research in any capacity. Class is reading 2 papers a week and then discussing it. MZW knows students are coming from different places and tries to balance teaching to the top and bottom. If you're writing an econ honors thesis this is the best class to take, MZW wants you to learn and grading reflects.

Avoid for ECON 4050. The class is advertised as an econometrics class where you learn statistical techniques/applications in environmental econ, but really its MZW assigning 50 - 100 pages of reading per week and not teaching econometrics. Low effort by the prof.

Assigned us both standard SW metrics textbook, but also a 2nd-year PhD textbook we never ended up using. Only 1 lecture a week & slow pace meant we didn't cover things in much depth. Reading never assigned. It wasn't too difficult to get a good grade but I feel like I didn't learn a lot about metrics. I'd take a non-metrics course with him though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: lots of room for improvement lol. graduating next sem so i just wanted to take this class and get out but he's so vague and only holds class once a week. assignments are PhD level and no communication at all.

Two complaints: didn't go into enough depth in the material (very little in terms of proofs, etc.), and only held class once a week. It's possible that MZW just didn't want to make things difficult on kids during COVID (curved tests to an 87 average). The TA is amazing, and the professor is very kind as well as good at explaining things.

Took MZW for ECON 3035 & 4050. Different type of professor but a real gem in the department. His off the cuff style is unique and his lectures are engaging and practical rather than straight from the textbook stuff. He's not for you if you love structure and simply doing work and getting out. Class was about evaluating/discussing academic papers

He constantly made errors on the board during his lectures and would have to begin practically every class with 'corrections' on the last class's lecture. Wasted lots of lecture time on tangents and irrelevant material. Without a textbook was confusing what we were even supposed to know. Was confused all year and feel like I learned nothing.

Hard class. His explanations were often circular and hard to understand, but once you understood them, you really understood the material. However, understanding concepts was often quite difficult. Curve was fairly generous, pop quizzes were for completion, and understanding problem sets was by far the best way to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is not a good teacher, that's for sure. Nice dude though.

He managed to convey a lot of material in a single semester, for which I give him credit, and he was often useful in office hours. My praise ends there. It was clear more than once that, as he is tenure-track, teaching is not his priority. He could get snappy when frustrated and often offered no understanding when life conflicted with the course.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is boring and the slides are exactly copied from the textbook. He sometimes confuses everyone and even himself about the concepts. The HW is somehow irrelevant to the course notes and hard. Midterm is find, but the final is sooooo hard. Curve? Possibly does not exist this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: he is super clear about what will be on the exam, and he is also willing to answer your questions. Overall a great teacher(It's his first year of teaching) and I would recommend taking econometrics with him. Class meets at 8 am but that is not what he can control.

Material was initially over a lot of students heads, so the professor worked to dumb it down for us. Prof has a great sense of humor. Problem sets are easy and as long as you do them, you should get A's. The two exams are harder and involve a lot of writing (midterm - 30%, final - 40%). Attend class, because there are pop quizzes. Curved to an 86.

He really cares about his students' learning. Clear disconnect at the beginning between what he expected us to know and what we actually knew. He is extremely helpful during office hours through. Really mild-mannered guy that relates to college students.

Really funny. It was very apparent that a lot of the class was not up to par on the pre-reqs for Econometrics. If you have a strong math/stats background, you will definitely be ahead. Grading isn't too bad and he is pretty understanding about extensions. A half-dozen or so problem sets, a few quizzes, one midterm, and a final.

She now teaches at Pitt, I had her for Sex and Sexualities. Mary is Kind and Loving, creates an Excellent and Accepting class atmosphere. Classes are mandatory, but she is very liberal with absences and extensions. It's a boon to go to class, and you can get away without reading - but you definitely need to know all the material before the midterm
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Z is amazing! She really makes you think about contemporary issues as well as past issues related to sex. She's open to all perspectives and never makes you feel bad for anything you say in class. Absolutely loved her

Dr. Z actually is amazing! She's young and really enjoys using pop culture and media to help guide the class. The class does assign readings before each class (anywhere from 2-30pgs) but as long as you participate in the in-class discussions you'll be fine. Only "homework" is two one-page papers a month. Overall, it's an easy, educational class

The class itself was good, but beware of getting involved with professor's lab. He refused to let a student in his lab publish their honor's thesis, then later stole parts of that student's honors thesis and published it without giving them credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Interesting material taught by an interesting professor. Super nice guy, and he tries to keep lectures entertaining by telling jokes. Over 80% of your grade is made up of tests, but easy extra credit opportunities. Definitely recommend for a psych or MHS elective.

Dr. Zald is a nice professor, and he keeps his lectures entertaining. The tests are mostly lecture heavy material, and he gives you study guides. Overall a pretty interesting and fun class - there is some group work and weekly homework assignments.

Dr. Zald was my favorite teacher in my time at Vanderbilt. He cares deeply about his students' learning, has a fantastic deadpan sense of humor that makes the class so much more fun and interesting, and is clear and descriptive of topics. 10/10 would take again.

Great class. Dr. Zald is one of the best profs I've ever had and a hilarious man. Gives amazing lectures and really cares about his students. Puts questions on the tests from the book so you have to read, but tests are pretty easy. 5 min group presentation, no attendance, and gives extra credit. Must take for any psych/neuro major.

Professor Zald was fundamentally a nice man, but his class was less than impressive to me.  He could be unintentionally offensive, and oftentimes made his class less useful by trying to make it more "fun." He was not always always tactful during sensitive topics. However, after being told he had offended someone, he apologized to the entire class.

Zald transforms the study of personality from a dull and speculative stamp collection of theories into a cutting-edge science grounded in neuro-cognitive and advanced psychometric research, which he conveys with wit and charm. If you like a few laughs interspersed with fascinating lectures and a few tests, he'll appeal to you.

This class was ridiculously easy. Dr. Zald is a fun lecturer and going to his classes is entertaining. The information he teaches is pretty intuitive and his tests are straight-forward. I didn't take the pre-req (PSY 101) before taking this class and had no difficulty getting an A.

This class was very hard.  A lot of memorization from the textbook was required, much of it material he had not gone over in class. Questions were tricky on exams. Grade is completely dependent on a couple of exams. No curve.
Excellent class. Engaging Lectures, and only graded material is multiple choice exams (which will be only a little tricky). Take this class!

Loved this class.  Zald is funny and can teach well.  He's pretty engaging and uses lots of examples from movies and such.  Tests are not difficult if you use the study guide and he does curve them somewhat.

Absolutely loved this man and this class. Gives out outlines/powerpoints for every lecture, covers all important material in class, tests are multiple choice and fairly straightforward. Makes class fun and interesting by bringing in examples from pop culture and has a great sense of humor. Plus, the subject matter is very interesting/pertinent.

Zald is an entertaining professor, class is worth going to, albeit it's early and attendance isn't mandatory. The tests cover a lot of material, though are fair, so if you read the textbook thoroughly and study, you'll be fine.

Class is worth going to - he is rather entertaining.  Zald has a great sense of humor and brings in creative examples.  Moves at a good pace and is easily understood.  Tests aren't that bad, they're straightforward and generally curved.  Definitely recommended to take his class.

Forget what everyone else says -- his tests are HARD, long, and he does not curve them like he says he will.  His extra credit is a joke, and I don't mean that in a good way, I mean he does not really give it to you in the end.  I should have gotten a higher grade in his class (I calculated it myself) and he gave me lower than I earned.  BEWARE!!!!
Tests are just about as challenging as other psych courses, but he is very easy to listen to, funny (he even dressed in drag to teach one of our classes).

Really a great professor.  The note outlines for every lecture are great, and the tests are totally fair.  I recommend his class for every psych major, or even everyone just interested in the aspects of personality!

This guy is great.  His lectures are funny and entertaining and very to the point.  Also, there is an outline for every lecture, so note taking is easy, and the quizzes and tests should follow a similar format.  Love this man
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Kourosh is a great professor, and I definitely enjoyed being in his Math 345 class at UMB. This is a very hard class, as the concepts of probability and statistics can be difficult. I  learned that the way to pass is to come to class, read the material again at home, do lots of practice problems, and commit at least 5 hours a week for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: great man
if u wanna be good in math .... take his class !

Only take Kouroush if you really enjoy math and want to be challenged A LOT. Tests are extremely hard and he expects too much out of the class. Offers difficult extra credit projects on complicated math topics. Kinda funny in class if you get over him being a little obnoxious sometimes. He will call on people and know when you miss class.
Do not take this class with this teacher. Expects way too much is unclear and hard to understand. Material on tests comes out of no where.
His tests are way too hard, and he is rude in class.
Has a badass accent and will bend over backwards in order to make sure you understand the material...in short Kourosh is the man!

Jone is a great person, but I think she is a little too out of touch to be a good calculus professor. She often spends a lot of lectures on topics that aren't super important to the course and the tests are difficult. Definitely do the "optional" homework, virtually all of the tests and quizzes come from there. She is a fun prof, but not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WORST MATH PROF, DO NOT TAKE. Although Jone is a nice person, she can not teach. To give some perspective, she came on the first day of the lecture and straight up said that she did not understand calculus. I warn anyone about taking her to make sure you have a very good foundation on clac 1 or whatever class she is teaching.

Professor Jone is a very kind/funny person but she is not that good of a math professor. This is her first semester teaching and she definitely improved. Although her lectures are boring, she is good with preparing you for the tests. Most of her content is based on the test and sometimes she tells you exactly what topic are going to be on the test.

She does everything in her power to see to it that you understand(and enjoy) the material. One time, instead of doing an ordinary lecture, we played a little game of math; it was quite fun and a twist to good old lecture-based learning. 1300 is not "beginner-friendly" so most of the hate should go to how accelerated it is, not Jone. She's amazing.

She may not be a really good math professor, but you will definitely learn the content and get a good grade. Once she was out for a conference and we had another instructor. I thought that the instructor did a much better lecture than Prof. Jone, but when it came to the test, I found out that Prof. Jone did much much better on test prep for us.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is great! Even though there are a lot of readings, Dr. Z always tries to make those in an interesting way. She cares about every students and always makes her class fun! Definitely will take again.

Cannot say enough good things about Prof. Z! She's super friendly and so caring for her students, always willing to push assignments back if we were stressed or had a lot going on. Class material wasn't difficult at all, and most of the time was interesting. Readings could be dry sometimes, but some of them are interesting studies. Highly recommend
Great class however, the tests are very difficult which lowers the overall enjoyment of the course. I will still take this class again however, the tests are tricky!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best classes Ive taken at Vanderbilt and Dr. Z was great. There were aspects that were surprisingly difficult, but overall a manageable class. Really interesting course material. Attendance isnt mandatory, but going to class makes it exponentially easier. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is a great professor! She is super knowledgeable and makes sure that everyone ends up doing well in the class. I learned so much! Her study guides help so much for studying for the exams. Take her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is so knowledgeable on elections and voters around the world. She made the readings more understandable and made class very enjoyable. She was a flexible and fair grader, often changing the weighting assignments to however it best benefited the student. She also included choice assignments (ex. choose 3/5). Learned a lot with little pressure
Professor Zechmeister is caring and gives clear lectures in class. Her grading criteria is sometimes unclear but she is willing to help outside the class. Take her if you can.

Professor Zechmeister was an absolutely amazing professor this semester! She's very understanding and is always willing to go out of her way to help you out. Her grading criteria are sometimes complicated but she's not a very tough grader when it comes to projects. Her tests were difficult but doable. I'd definitely recommend taking her!

Prof Zechmeister is great! Really straightforward lectures without it being boring, and both tests and papers are graded clearly and fairly. If you are interested in survey research, she is also open to students doing research in the Latin American Public Opinion Project lab.

The class was interesting. It was lecture and powerpoint format, but you need to pay attention to the lectures. There are three papers, a midterm, and a final. She was helpful and two good movies were shown. You also have to present a group project at the end.

Zechmeister is a great professor whose lectures are very interesting and clear, with each one building upon prior ones.  Very nice that all readings are posted online so no textbooks.  If you put in the effort you will do well.  Great class!

She is really interested in the subject matter, so she makes it more interesting to learn about Latin American politics.  3 papers, midterm, final, presentation on a country (none of which are difficult).  Great professor

Great class! She is very clear in lecture and gives a detailed outline for the midterm/final. One research paper on a mexican current event.Kind of a tough paper grader, but easy tests if you take EXCELLENT notes and attend class.She is very caring and will help you in anyway,including reading your papers for feedback before you turn it in.

I LOVED THIS CLASS! three 2-3 page essays, midterm, final, inclass presentation on a latin american country. powerpoints and readings key for tests, but not too many readings assigned. she hands out a study guide with all you need to know. attendence not mandatory, put there is a participation grade. She is great! in fact, I made her my advisor!!

Zelik was very nice and the most understanding prof I had during Covid. The course is mostly self led, but Zelik is always there for assistance and feedback. Creo was the worst part of the course, but if you've used CAD in the past you'll be fine. Do not put the project off to the last minute and make sure you work with someone reliable
Solid option for ME 2160. Very nice guy, reasonable grading criteria, gives good feedback. Get ready to grind the homework though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: The final can be up to 60% of your final grade, not including the final project. The CAD software can be painful but you just have to grind through it, and Zelik is a good professor to have, he cares about helping you learn the material. The midterm/final are v stressful, but it's right out of the class tutorials and homework.

Creo kinda sucks, but you will get good at it if you actually do the tutorials. Do NOT start homework the night before because it takes forever. The group project is super cool and will be useful to show employers but its not weighted heavily enough. Final was hard. Awesome class, but its extremely time intensive and not an easy A by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The project for this class was very time intensive. You definitely learn the ins and out or Creo parametric, but you don't know enough in the early stages to make much progress on your project, leaving a lot of work at the end. The TA's were super-helpful, and Zelik was almost always on top of responding to emails answering any questions.

Professor Somer-Topcu actually teaches at UT Austin now. She is an amazing lecturer and made the subject interesting. We did have three 3-6 page research papers, two midterms, and a final, so I found myself studying a lot for her class. However, she had reviews before each test, and I never felt like I was unprepared. Coming to class is imperative.

I had heard from friends that Professor Somer-Topcu is an extremely hard grader and signed up for 210 reluctantly. After taking a couple tests now though, I can confidently say that her test formats are extremely easy (longest portion is 1-page essays). She also tries to make class interesting through relevant videos, Daily Show clips, etc.
Really knowledgeable, but tough at times. Very in-depth course. Midterm, final, and a debate. Definitely recommend for anyone interested in Europe.

Best teacher I've had at Vanderbilt. Didn't have much of an interest in the subject beforehand, now taking all of her classes and majoring in political science. Very clear on what she expects and makes herself available for help. Keep up with the readings and participate and tests/papers will come easy to you.
Are you kidding me? She is one of the best profs I've had. She is funny, approachable and knows her stuff. Not the easiest class (too many facts on the EU) but I am having a very good experience

Her difficulty is vastly overrated here.  Her debate grades are very high and her tests averages were somewhere in the 80s.  Her class is not that hard, as she gives you a study guide with topics to know.  It is memorization, but that's what most PSCI classes are.  She expects people to read and walked out on her class when they did not.

Most biased grader Ive ever had.  Seems to decide after the first exam what grades everyone will make, and nothing you do will change this.  Gave me an A- on everything, yet thanks to participation and quizzes I only needed a B on my final paper to make an A, yet still got an A- despite thorough research and intense proofreading. Such a headache.

Her lectures can be interesting but difficult to understand. Also, she is big on participation and once walked out of a class because she felt no one had done the reading. Not an easy A, and almost seems as if you need prior knowledge of the topic to do well. Class is mostly about memorization and trying to get on her good side.

Agree with the comment below.  Although granted test 2 was significantly easier than test 1, and the debate grades (20%) are usually fairly high, she is INCREDIBLY nit-picky with exam grading, and realistically exams are nothing more than exercises in memorization of ridiculous amounts of facts.  Not impossible, but def a tougher poli sci course.

her lectures are pretty boring and her tests are difficult. there is a sign in sheet for class everyday and she marks down when you speak in class. this is more of a history class than anything else. memorize a ton of facts and you can probably end up with a B+

This was one of my favorite classes this semester! She is originally from Turkey (but her English is very easy to understand) so she is very informed on the subject. Two midterms, a project, a final, and an attendance/participation grade. A must take professor at Vandy!
This is the best class I am taking this semester

Clear lecturer and intelligent about the subject matter.  You have to go to class and read the textbook because she has genuine surprise pop quizzes about once a week.  There's an in-class debate, a midterm and final, and the pop quiz grades and a participation grade.  The tests are pretty tough, but I did well because there was a friendly curve.

Very interesting class yet time consuming (reading and film screenings). Class discussions elucidate the innate connection between film and philosophy. Zeman is very understanding and will give you the time to craft a paper worth writing.  It is a writing class, so of course grading is subjective.

NEVER take anything from this man. He acts like he, too, is learning the material because he's one of those profs who tries way too hard to be "nice" to students. He ends up treating you like you're 5, but his grading is deceptively hard. We read way too much Freud in this class, which would be fine except he took all Freudian theories seriously.

Do NOT take this class! Although the material is remotely interesting, he is a terrible grader. His class is really boring and his grading is so arbitrary. I learned absolutely nothing and if you want to hate philosophy, take the class!

Class was interesting, definitely learned a LOT. He himself ia a likeable, extremely smart guy. He grades papers based on strength of ideas rather than stylistic details so as long as you can create a strong, arguable thesis, you don't have to be the best writer in the world to make an A.
terrible! completely arbitrary grading! i was interested in the subject and he managed to make me dislike it

So it was an interesting class but the whole content could be waay better taught. I really like him as a person a lot, but I feel like you are on your own on this one for projects and hw. You also really have to put more time, in addition to the 1 hr 45 min class, to meet with him to further discuss any concerns (there will be a lot) from lecture
intellectually challenging, but such a fun course
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The materials are super interesting. Learned a lot about encryptions and hacking. This is a challenging topic, but Zhenkai is such an easy grader which makes this class manageable. He's also very approachable, which makes the class almost like a peer-to-peer discussion, except he's super smart and incredibly knowledgable about he's saying.

Zhenkai really cares about how students like the class, and does his best to make lectures interesting. My only criticism is that he can get a bit excited and starts writing vertically on the board, which is a bit hard to follow. If you ask him to slow down and be more thorough in his explanation he is happy to oblige.
The textbook online program basically teaches you step by step to solve all the problems. Very homework heavy, but he is caring and tells you what he is looking for. He was a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No Comments

cracks jokes in class to keep the mood light. doesn't do unnecessary proofs. does a lot of examples to help students understand the material. tests are straightforward. makes sure that students understand. great professor!
He has a thick Chinese accent and is difficult to understand.  However, he is very helpful and enthusiastic about the subject.

Knows the content perfectly well. Organized but very old school - weekly homework submitted and graded on paper. Thick accent, but after 2 weeks it's fine. Lectures are fast-paced but easy to understand. Funny and tries hard to make it engaging. Took after 1301 with Rafter - exams are way easier, although no cheat sheet at all. Good prof.

Analysis is hard. Zheng makes it worse. 11+ weekly HWs that take hours to do, but are only worth 30% of your grade. 70% is in terribly graded exams. Forget one step? -5 points. Barely curves. Later, he deviates from the textbook, so he can use his own, nearly incomprehensible proofs instead. Nice guy though, which is the only good thing I can say.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zheng does nothing online. If you aren't in class, you'll miss the homework handouts, when tests will be, etc. He teaches this class very homework heavy. Quizzes are reasonable based on the homework, but exams are hard. He also routinely does examples wrong in class and expects you to know where/how to fix them, but he's nice.
Horrible. If you're taking diff eq DON'T TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is kind and tries to be funny in class coming up with jokes that most people don't catch. Heavy accent which takes time to get used to.
