Lectures come with examples but are fast paced, and he throws a ton of homework at you every single weekend, which is good for multi but I'd say far too much. Tests are hard especially WITHOUT CHEAT SHEETS.

This class wasn't all that hard. It was hard to understand him because of his thick accent, but you get used to it. He's sweet and care, but I mostly understood the concepts through doing the HW. There is about 3-6 hrs of graded HW every week. The weekly quizzes are fairly easy, but most exams aren't.
I really enjoyed his class. He is very kind, funny, and cares about our learning. There is a lot of homework but if you do it, the tests aren't bad.

This was a bad professor. All notes are on the chalkboard so don't expect online notes if you miss class. There were questions on the final exam that required a problem-solving method we were not exposed to in class. The thick accent makes it worse. He gives you a higher grade if you are Chinese, kind of discriminatory. Avoid this professor.

Dechao is a really caring guy that clearly knows a lot about what he is teaching. He truly really wants students to do well. However, his accent is extremely strong, he gives a large amount of hw, and his tests are tough. He doesn't allow cheat sheets unlike other professors. He's okay to take but look elsewhere if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His class is tough, but a lot of that is the class and not the professor. If you do not like math, do not take this class. It is very proof heavy, and the lectures can get math dense at times, but Professor Zheng is very helpful and makes the class much more enjoyable. Over 60 percent our grade was the midterm and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy. Has a pretty thick accent but you get used to it as the semester goes. A little bit unorganized lecture wise, but they're not too hard to follow. He does a LOT of example problems during class. Exams are a breeze if you do the homework. He definitely tries to make the class as easy as possible. Plus, hes a funny dude. Take him.

His accent can be a bit difficult to understand, but it's easy to get used to it after the first few classes. His lectures can be a bit hard to follow. However, the tests are exactly like the homework, so as long as you can figure out how to do the homework problems, you'll do fine on the tests. He's also really helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty good, a little bit unclear at times but usually not much of a problem. A good amount of homework, but it's graded which was nice. The tests were just like homework problems and easy compared to other sections of diffeqs. I would recommend taking him, and he definitely rounded my grade up at the end.

Dr. Zheng can be a little hard to understand sometimes but he is always very helpful and available outside class. He gives weekly homework which can be a lot at times but his tests are easy and usually repeat questions from notes/homeworks. Good with classes that are computational based, might be a bit hard to follow if analysis based.
I tried my best but I just cannot understand his accent. The test average is about 80 every time and he gives TONS of homework.

His accent is a bit difficult to understand. Weekly quizzes and homework, he will literally squeeze them in for each week. He doesn't use Brightspace at all. He prides himself on tricking students on tests. If HW and quizzes weren't 1/3 of grade, my final grade would be significantly lower.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: May the lord have mercy on anyone who takes Professor Zhengs class. He is obviously very smart and passionate about MV, but that doesnt matter if you have no idea what he is saying- I had to teach myself every single topic. Tests are based off homework and arent horrible but the final was genuinely horrible and tanked my grade. Very funny though

This class was fairly easy until the end of the semester. He has a strong accent and lectures were hard to follow. Homework takes forever. Tests and quizzes were relatively straightforward until the final, which was worth a third of our grade and was absolutely ridiculous and impossible. It was probably harder than most of the other multi classes.

Professor Zhang is bad. I pretty much relied on the book to teach myself because I would get so lost in his lectures. He's also frustratingly unaccommodating if you miss class for an excused reason, and doesn't let you make up quizzes. He grades really hard and his tests are probably the most difficult of any of the other professors. Avoid him

Unbelievably confusing lectures towards the end. Dechao is clearly very smart but just was not great at conveying much of the material. If you love math and are talented you might find this class alright. Dechao wants everyone to do well but this class was unbelievably difficult. I would not take this class again.
So hard to understand what he's saying because of his accent. Lectures were way too confusing to even try following. Consider yourself lucky if you pass.

Professor Zheng is very difficult to understand, but he definitely is passionate about multivariable calculus. If you go to his office hours, he will devote all of his attention to helping you understand a problem. The tests for this class were extremely difficult, and the final was even worse; however, he tends to grade on a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Multivariable is a fun class. He tries to make it easy. If you attend class, he is clear about when quizzes are and will tell you the topic each week. Homework is due every Wednesday. Tests are based on the homework although he takes off a lot of points for arithmetic errors. Overall, entertaining class and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS MAN. Super funny, very clear on what will be on midterms, and extraordinarily helpful during office hours. Just hilarious and cannot recommend enough. Great, GREAT professor even if his accent is hard to understand, you get used to it after a week so long as you focus. This guy is great, TAKE HIS CLASS

hardest class ive ever taken. he has a very thick accent and cant explain things. people would ask questions and he would say "you dont need to know that just go with it" office hours arent helpful either. thought i was gonna fail but he must have bumped my grade a ton. hes pretty funny. not sure theres anyone better though theyre all bad
funny as hell but can be hard af to understand his lectures cuz his explanations are just absurd sometimes, he's chill tho

After I failed the 1st test, I went to Dr Zheng for help. He was very interested in helping me understand the content and told me not to worry about the 1st test as long as I improved. He does care about his students, but you have to reach out to him. His accent was hard to understand, but he was fine if you interrupt to ask a clarifying question.

Pretty straightforward teacher. Lectures for the entire class period, but half the lectures are example problems. Makes occasional jokes and real-life comparisons. Bit of an accent, but still understandable. Gives weekly homework and quizzes based on the homework on Fridays. The tests are exactly what he teaches in class and assigns in homework.

Very hard to understand at first but his tests and quizzes (at the end of every week) are very fair if you ACTUALLY do the homework, very likable personality and a fun guy to listen to once you overcome the language barrier.

He's not a very good lecturer but if you do the homework you'll be ok. Tests and quizzes are entirely based off hw. Vanderbilt offers a lot of resources for math help so if you utilize those this class shouldn't be a problem. Just don't rely on Dr. Zheng to explain stuff.

Zheng is  probably the easiest professor in Math department. Weekly quiz comes directly from homework. Midterms are easy if you do the homework. However, the final could be a little bit challenging because he changes his policy that if anyone get A in final, then get A in the entire course. Also, he lowers down A's threshold to 90 instead of 93.
Quite confusing sometimes even if you try hard to listen. You must spend a lot of time learning materials by yourself to get a decent grade.

This class is pretty simple. If you do AND understand the homework, you can probably pull an A. That said, the lectures can sometimes be hard to follow and I highly suggest flipping through the section on which he is lecturing the day before class.  Can be a bit hard to understand but a good class overall.

Don't take him for Analysis. He is extremely confusing. He provides 0 feedback on homework and doesn't give you solutions. And you need to know all of the homework problems for the exams. He also lets you out of class late every day.

In addition to other comments-- Weekly homework assignments. Weekly quizzes that are quick and easy if you did the homework. Pretty lenient grader. You'll love the guy even if you only get a B-. Does plenty of sample problems but the homework is the best way to really learn the material. Textbook required

Thick accent but you get used to it. Really smart guy and wants his students to do well. Tests are challenging but fair, no curveballs, tends to be enough time to finish. Writes everything on the . Pretty funny too. "What, you no take highschool? You no take middle school?" Cracks me up.

It took me a while to get used to Dr. Zheng's accent. But he's very good about writing stuff on the board, and he constantly cracks jokes. He makes things fairly clear, and the tests aren't too bad (no proofs!) Also the homework is pretty easy.

I HIGHLY suggest taking this class from Zheng. He is friendly and easier than other teachers. His accent is a hard to understand, but you get used to it. Homework/quizzes, exams, and  final each count for 1/3. If the test average is not high enough, he allows you to redo the problems to make up the points, because he wants his students to learn.

sometimes hard to understand but he writes everything on the board so you can figure out what he means, quizzes once a week are usually easier than the homework which is also due once a week and only a few problems on the homework are graded so if you skip the hard ones you'll still probably do ok, overall would highly recommend

Took for sculpture 1 and had a great time. Mel is very accomplished, but I don't think he ever mentioned his own work in class, so idk why other ppl said he was condescending. His feedback (if you ask for it) is great direction, and the two semester projects are really effective for developing as an artist.

Like the person below said, Mel is a very accomplished artist. However, he's also very into himself & these accomplishments. Can be somewhat condescending, mostly because he seems to believe that his way of doing things is the best way. Definitely show up to class, esp. on crit days. As with any art class, put in the effort & you should do fine.

Mel is an interesting guy and a highly accomplished artist himself. He is very interesting and if you participate in discussions, you are assured an A. He's not very understanding of absence or tardiness, so be in class and be there early if you can.
I thought she suck at first because the grading system is 50% exam 20% Labs 20% Final 10%HW than i notice she gave us like a bunch of points on the exam lol

Zoorob reads straight through her powerpoint with little added information. It doesn't seem as if she knows the information very well, based on her constant mistakes. She's a very nice lady but the only reason you should go to class is for the clicker questions. Reading the book is a definite must to fill in the gaps.

Zoorob tries to be engaging but she's constantly making mistakes and does not fully explain a lot of content so the tests become really difficult. She doesn't always directly answer student questions. However, she gives clicker questions which is a bonus

Zoorob is obviously a nice woman but she was not a very good teacher. She did not explain the material a lot of the time and could not fully answer questions. Her class was frustrating and not helpful. I do not recommend it.

Zoorob is fairly helpful but moves quickly and does not spend ample time explaining tricky topics in class. Much of the class depends on reading the section BEFORE class and printing off notes beforehand to make following the lecture easier.

If you aren't a humanities person, this is a great W class to take. It doesn't really require that much writing (mostly lab reports), and the writing is graded more for scientific content than style. Dr. Zoorob is a good professor, although she can be disorganized and sometimes it's difficult to know what she expects.

Grace is very funny and engaging for a 200 person lecture class at 8 am in the morning. She isn't absolutely phenomenal when it comes to expalaining complicated processes, but she seems to know her stuff and is fairly helpful. She's a little silly but her class had a pretty high average on most exams.

Prof Zoorob is nice and tries to liven up class, but she makes so many mistakes. People are constantly correcting her in class. She also doesn't usually understand people correctly when they ask a question.

Her accent is not hard to understand. She is not always willing to rework clicker questions when a bunch of students get them wrong, but will sometimes let the class redo them. She had no idea what ch. 8 was talking about, but knew the rest. The online homework is really how you learn. Pick Gen Chem class based on time of day not teacher.
No Comments
she is a REALLY nice lady, always tries to help as much as possible, lectures are really important bc the book was completely useless...
The tests are pretty hard.  He finds a way to make some interesting lectures out of difficult topics. Definitely take this class if you are an Econ major.

Definitely cares about his students and is passionate about subject matter, but tests are very difficult--his final was literally a book that he self admittingly makes too long to weed out 'those who do/don't know the material.' not an easy course but take him if your an econ major.
Perhaps he's better than some,but it'd be nice if the exam review questions somewhat resembled the actual exam questions, rather than leading you to study all the wrong things...

Zissimos is a very good professor.  He goes over the material in great detail so that you have a clear understanding, and he definitely knows what he's talking about. He's extremely approachable. His tests are difficult -the questions really test your knowledge- but I learned a lot from his class.

I like Ben, but he definitely favors students that are good at math on his tests. His tests consist of ridiculous applications of the in class material. His grading is pretty lenient, do all the problem sets. However, sometimes I felt he didn't know what he was talking about
he is VERY nice and CARES a lot about students and how he teaches!!  he's also VERY smart and sometimes, his tests are ridiculous, but overall great teacher.

Zissimos is very nice but not easy since it is hard to apply the subject like he wants you to on the exams. I don't think there is an easy 232 teacher at Vandy though, so Zissimos is your best bet. 2 exams and a cumulative final (which is hard). Weekly problem sets (not graded) and if you do all but 2, you get +5 to your final grade.

pro. zissimos is a good teacher, really helpful.  All the class slides are posted except for the examples you do in class.  The problem sets are not graded. recommend it if you are taking intermediate macro

Really good teacher. Very nice and accommodating (gave us friday off once, moved a test for some, etc), but the material is still tough. While he speaks clearly and you know what to generally expect for the tests, they are still difficult.
